480353.title: Tubular adenoma
480353.description: The most common type of adenomatous colonic polyp (about 80% of adenomatous polyps). They can be found anywhere within the colon and has a low risk of malignant transformation (<5%).

Vf0GO2.description: The symbol for the female sex.

ef0xO2.description: The symbol for the male sex.

Uf0bl2.title: Angiotensin-converting enzyme
Uf0bl2.description:
An enzyme that converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II and degrades bradykinin. 
ACE inhibitors are used to treat hypertension and chronic kidney disease. 

A deficiency or dysfunction of ACE can cause a dry cough and/or angioedema. ACE levels are used diagnostically to assess disease activity in patients with sarcoidosis.

2f0Tl2.title: Achlorhydria
2f0Tl2.description: A deficiency in production of hydrochloric acid in the stomach. Etiologies include chronic atrophic gastritis, stomach cancer, VIPoma, and long-term proton pump inhibitor use.

ff0kl2.title: Pneumobilia
ff0kl2.description: The accumulation of gas in the biliary system. Common causes include sphincterotomy of the sphincter of Oddi, biliary-enteric anastomosis, and gallstone ileus.

Tf06l2.title: Agraphia
Tf06l2.description: An acquired writing deficit that is the result of a defect in central language processing.

gf0Fl2.title: Acalculia
gf0Fl2.description: The inability to perform mathematical tasks (e.g., difficulty counting, adding, and subtracting). Caused by lesions to the parietal lobe.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

hf0cN2.title: Allodynia
hf0cN2.description: A sensation of pain triggered by a stimulus that is not ordinarily considered painful.

if0JN2.title: Anabolism
if0JN2.description: The type of metabolism in which energy is consumed, resulting in the formation of more complex molecules (the opposite of catabolism).

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Glycolysis versus gluconeogenesis

Qf0uN2.title: Anasarca
Qf0uN2.description: A condition characterized by extreme generalized peripheral edema. Common causes include liver failure, nephrotic syndrome, heart failure, and severe malnutrition.

jf0_N2.title: Anisakis
jf0_N2.description: A genus of parasitic round worms (e.g., Anisakis simplex) found in fish. The disease anisakiasis is caused by consuming raw fish infected with the parasite.

Pf0Wm2.title: Anisocoria
Pf0Wm2.description: A condition of having pupils of unequal diameter.

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Anisocoria

kf0mm2.title: Anosmia
kf0mm2.description: The complete loss of the ability to smell.

lf0vm2.title: Antithrombin
lf0vm2.description: An anticoagulant protein produced by the liver that inhibits the activity of thrombin and other coagulation factors (e.g., factors IXa and Xa).

mf0V52.title: Anuria
mf0V52.description: Complete absence of urine production, typically as a result of acute or chronic renal failure. Defined in adults as a urine output < 50 mL/24 hours.

Mf0M52.title: Aphagia
Mf0M52.description: The complete loss of the ability to swallow (complete dysphagia). Can occur as a result of complete obstruction of the esophagus by esophageal cancer.

nf0752.title: Apophysis
nf0752.description: A bony protuberance that arises from an ossification center other than an epiphysis and serves as the point of attachment for ligaments and tendons (e.g., tibial tuberosity).

of00M2.title: Ataxia
of00M2.description: A lack of coordination of voluntary movements. Common causes include impaired cerebellar function (cerebellar ataxia), impaired vestibular function, and/or loss of proprioceptive sensation (sensory ataxia).

6f0jM2.title: Bääm
6f0jM2.description: The term AMBOSS editors shout out after having reached their weekly goals.

pf0LM2.title: Bacteriuria
pf0LM2.description: The presence of bacteria in the urine. Thresholds for bacteriuria on urine culture (reported as colony-forming units/mL) differ based on the method of urine collection used. Thresholds also differ across guidelines.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

Jf0sM2.title: Basal ganglia
Jf0sM2.description: An essential part of the extrapyramidal motor system. The basal ganglia is anatomically formed by the caudate nucleus and the lentiform nucleus (putamen and globus pallidus). Functionally, the substantia nigra, subthalamic nuclei, and red nucleus also form part of the basal ganglia.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

If0Yn2.title: Water bottle heart
If0Yn2.description: A radiographic sign of a very large pericardial effusion. A large, bottle-shaped cardiac silhouette is seen on chest x-ray.

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Diagnosis

media.title: Pericardial effusion with water bottle configuration

rf0fn2.title: Bowman's capsule
rf0fn2.description: The cup-shaped part of the nephron that surrounds the glomerular capillaries. Consists of an outer (parietal) surface and an inner (endothelial) surface. The inner surface, which is in contact with the endothelium of glomerular capillaries, is formed by podocytes.

7f04n2.title: Brachydactyly
7f04n2.description: A congenital shortness of one or more fingers or toes. Associated with many congenital syndromes, including Down syndrome.

Hf0Kn2.title: Bruch membrane
Hf0Kn2.description: The innermost layer of the choroid. Bruch's membrane lies adjacent to the pigmented epithelium of the retina.

sf0tn2.title: Café au lait macule
sf0tn2.description: A benign type of hyperpigmentation that predominantly affects children and manifests as a pigmented macule or patch commonly located on the trunk. An isolated lesion is usually idiopathic, whereas ≥ 6 lesions suggest a genetic etiology (e.g., neurofibromatosis type 1, McCune-Albright syndrome).

destinations.label: Hyperpigmentation disorders → Café au lait macules

Gf0Bn2.title: Hepatobiliary triangle
Gf0Bn2.description: An anatomical space formed by the common hepatic duct, the cystic duct, and the lower border of the liver. Contains the cystic artery and the cystic lymph node (Lund node). During cholecystectomy, the hepatobiliary triangle must be carefully identified to prevent damage to the cystic artery and extrahepatic biliary system.

tf0XL2.title: Chelating agent
tf0XL2.description: A substance that binds to metal ions in the body, facilitating their excretion. Used to treat metal poisoning. Examples include dimercaprol, deferoxamine, and succimer.

Ff0gL2.title: Chemosis
Ff0gL2.description: Swelling of the conjunctiva caused by conjunctival vein vasodilatation and increased blood flow.

8f0OL2.title: Cheyne-Stokes breathing
8f0OL2.description: An abnormal breathing pattern characterized by crescendo-decrescendo pattern of tidal volumes followed by a period of apnea. Common causes include heart failure, damage to respiratory centers (e.g., stroke, traumatic brain injuries, metabolic encephalopathies), and central sleep apnea.

uf0pL2.title: Citrated blood
uf0pL2.description: A blood product that has been made incoagulable by the addition of sodium citrate. Citrated blood is used to determine coagulation parameters (e.g., INR).

Ef08L2.title: Claudication
Ef08L2.description: Pain of vascular origin that is reliably induced by exercise and relieved or reduced by rest. The pain is typically cramping in nature and is most commonly described in the lower extremities (in lower limb peripheral arterial disease). Claudication is caused by tissue ischemia secondary to arterial insufficiency.

vf0AL2.title: Clipping
vf0AL2.description: The surgical clamping of an intracranial aneurysm with the help of metal clips.

Df01o2.title: Coil embolization
Df01o2.description: The endovascular embolization of an aneurysm or injured vessel with the help of a fine, spiral-shaped platinum coil.

wf0ho2.title: Cotton wool spots
wf0ho2.description: An ophthalmologic finding characterized by yellow-white deposits on the retina. Caused by swelling of retinal nerve fibers (e.g., due to ischemia as a result of diabetes and/or hypertension).

destinations.label: Retinal vessel occlusion → Retinal vein occlusion

Bf0zo2.title: DIP
Bf0zo2.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Distal interphalangeal joint
2. Desquamative interstitial pneumonia

yf0dK2.title: Diplopia
yf0dK2.description: A condition of double vision that can be monocular (e.g., due to disorders of the crystalline lens) or binocular (e.g., due to strabismus).

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Paralytic strabismus

Af0RK2.title: Dysarthria
Af0RK2.description: A condition of impaired articulation resulting from motor dysfunction of the tongue, lips, or vocal cords. Typical pathologic speech patterns include slurring, mumbling, staccato pronunciation, and changes in speed and pitch.

_f05K2.title: Dysdiadochokinesia
_f05K2.description: An inability to perform rapid antagonistic movements (e.g., supination/pronation). Movements are often slow, hesitant, or incomplete.

zf0rK2.title: Dysmetria
zf0rK2.description: An inability to accurately coordinate voluntary movements, typically resulting in overshoot (hypermetria) or undershoot (hypometria). Dysmetria is usually caused by lesions of the cerebellar hemispheres.

-f0DK2.title: Body dysmorphic disorder
-f0DK2.description: A psychiatric disorder characterized by persistent preoccupation with a perceived flaw in one's physical appearance that is mild or not observable by others. Other symptoms include repetitive behaviors (e.g., skin scratching) or thoughts (e.g., comparing oneself to others), impairment in functioning, and significant distress. Diagnosis requires ruling out an eating disorder.

ZT0Z62.title: Dystrophy
ZT0Z62.description: A degeneration of tissue (e.g., due to malnutrition or hereditary disease).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cellular adaptation

0T0e62.title: Dystrophin
0T0e62.description: A structural protein in muscle cells. Certain muscular dystrophies (e.g., Duchenne's muscular dystrophy) are associated with mutations in the gene that codes for dystrophin.

media.title: Anti-dystrophin antibody staining of muscle tissue

aT0Q62.title: Dysuria
aT0Q62.description: Pain or discomfort that occurs during urination. Most commonly caused by infections, such as urinary tract infections or STI-related lower genital tract infections.

YT0n62.title: Echolalia
YT0n62.description: Involuntary repetition of another person's speech. Common pathological causes include schizophrenia and autism. Echolalia may occur physiologically as a part of normal childhood development between 1 and 2 years of age.

XT0962.title: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
XT0962.description: A diagnostic test that uses an antibody coupled with an enzyme as a marker to detect a specific antigen (e.g., tumor markers, viruses, drug, other antibodies). The coupled enzyme catalyzes a reaction involving a chromogenic or fluorogenic substrate. The antigen level in the test sample can then be quantified based on the degree of color change or fluorescence.

cT0ap2.title: Elschnig spots
cT0ap2.description: Multiple, round, brown-black spots with a bright ring that are scattered throughout the retina of patients with malignant hypertension.

1T02p2.title: Embolia cutis medicamentosa
1T02p2.description: An iatrogenic skin lesion caused by accidental injection of a drug (e.g., local anesthetic) into an artery. This mishap, which occurs most often with intramuscular injections, causes necrosis of tissue surrounding the injection site.

destinations.label: Collection of dermatological disorders → Embolia cutis medicamentosa

WT0Pp2.title: Empty sella syndrome
WT0Pp2.description: Invagination of the cerebrospinal filled subarachnoid space into the sella turcica.

destinations.label: Rare neurological diseases → Empty sella syndrome

dT0op2.title: Endemic disease
dT0op2.description: An endemic disease is a condition that is regularly found in a specific geographical area. Malaria, for example, is endemic to large parts of Africa.

destinations.label: Population health → Elements describing population health

VT0Gp2.title: Endotoxin
VT0Gp2.description: A lipopolysaccharide found in the outer cell membrane of several gram-negative bacteria. Consists of O antigen, a core polysaccharide, and lipid A. Released by living bacteria through membrane blebbing and upon bacterial cell death, inducing host release of IL-1, IL-6, and TNF-α, which cause fever and hypotension leading to septic shock. Can also trigger the coagulation cascade, leading to disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC).

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

eT0xp2.title: Enhancement
eT0xp2.description: A term in radiology used to describe increased contrast uptake (hyperdense appearance in relation to surrounding structures on CT and MRI scans) as a result of increased perfusion.

UT0bJ2.title: Epidemic
UT0bJ2.description: A disease that spreads quickly within a specific population or region. Limited to a specific area and time period (e.g., seasonal influenza).

destinations.label: Population health → Elements describing population health

2T0TJ2.title: Epiphora
2T0TJ2.description: Excessive watering of the eye due to increased tear production or impaired drainage. Often caused by irritation or a blockage in the tear duct.

fT0kJ2.title: Epulis
fT0kJ2.description: Benign gingival hypertrophy. A common cause is mechanical irritation.

TT06J2.title: Erethism
TT06J2.description: A syndrome caused by chronic mercury poisoning. Clinical features include shyness, anxiety, irritability, emotional lability, insomnia, delirium, and anorexia.

ST0yJ2.title: Hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction
ST0yJ2.description: A physiologic response to alveolar hypoxia in which local mediators induce vasoconstriction of alveolar pulmonary capillaries. Results in decreased blood flow through poorly ventilated regions of the lung, thereby reducing right-to-left pulmonary shunting.

3T0Sq2.title: Imprinting
3T0Sq2.description: An epigenetic phenomenon that results in silencing of one of the alleles of a gene depending on whether the allele was paternally or maternally inherited.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Epigenetic regulation of gene expression

iT0Jq2.title: Glial cell
iT0Jq2.description: A cell of the nervous system that serves a homeostatic role (e.g., structural and nutritional support, insulation of neurons, phagocytosis of pathogens). Glial cells in the CNS include astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, ependymal cells, and microglia. Glial cells in the PNS include satellite cells and Schwann cells.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

jT0_q2.title: Glucosuria
jT0_q2.description: The presence of glucose in urine. Occurs when blood glucose levels exceed 180 mg/dL (the renal threshold for reabsorption of glucose), as in patients with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus. In pregnancy, glucosuria can occur at normal blood glucose levels due to increased GFR.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

PT0WI2.title: Gunn sign
PT0WI2.description: A tapering of a retinal venule at the point where a retinal arteriole crosses the retinal venule; creates an hourglass shape. Associated with advanced hypertensive retinopathy.

kT0mI2.title: Hemagglutination
kT0mI2.description: A clumping of erythrocytes induced by certain compounds (e.g., antibodies, viral molecules). Hemagglutination assays are used in blood typing and evaluation of viral infection (e.g., influenza).

OT0II2.title: Hematemesis
OT0II2.description: Vomiting blood. Color can vary from bright red to brown, and appearance may resemble coffee grounds. Causes include esophageal variceal bleeding, peptic ulcers, gastritis, and stomach cancer.

lT0vI2.title: Hematochezia
lT0vI2.description: Passage of bright red or maroon blood per rectum, with or without stool. Most commonly caused by lower gastrointestinal bleeding (e.g., from diverticulosis, hemorrhoids, ulcerative colitis, or colorectal cancer). Less commonly caused by severe upper gastrointestinal bleeding.

NT0-I2.title: Hematuria
NT0-I2.description: The presence of ≥ 3 red blood cells per high-power field in the urine. May be microscopic (not visible to the naked eye) or macroscopic (visible discoloration of the urine).

mT0Vr2.title: Hemoglobinuria
mT0Vr2.description: Presence of free hemoglobin in urine. A common cause is intravascular hemolysis (e.g., transfusion mismatch).

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

5T0ir2.title: Hemoptysis
5T0ir2.description: A symptom of coughing up of blood from the lungs or airways. Considered massive if the bleeding is life-threatening (> 100–600 mL of blood within 24 hours).

MT0Mr2.title: Hemianopsia
MT0Mr2.description: Loss of vision in one half of the visual field. In homonymous hemianopsia visual fields on the same side are affected (e.g., the nasal field of the right eye and temporal field of the left eye). In heteronymous hemianopia the same visual fields of both eyes are affected (e.g., temporal fields of both eyes as a result of damage to the optic chiasma).

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Scotoma and anopia

LT0wr2.title: Hirsutism
LT0wr2.description: A condition of excessive male pattern hair growth in women (e.g., on the chin, above the upper lip, and around the umbilicus) that is most commonly idiopathic but associated with excess androgen in 10% of cases.

KT0U72.title: Holocephalic
KT0U72.description: A descriptor for involvement of the entire head. Commonly used when describing headaches that affect the entire head.

pT0L72.title: Hydrops fetalis
pT0L72.description: A fetal condition characterized by generalized edema and accumulation of fluid in serous cavities (e.g., pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, ascites). Diagnosed via ultrasound. Etiologies include severe fetal anemia (e.g., hemolytic disease of the newborn, hemorrhage), congenital infections (e.g., parvovirus B19), chromosomal abnormalities, and congenital heart defects. Associated with a high rate of perinatal mortality.

JT0s72.title: Hyperekplexia
JT0s72.description: A rare, hereditary, neurological disease that presents at birth and is characterized by an increased startle response and hypertonia (predominantly truncal).

qT0C72.title: Hyperkeratosis
qT0C72.description: An abnormal thickening of the skin visible on histopathological examination as hyperplasia of the stratum corneum.

sT0tH2.title: Hyposmia
sT0tH2.description: Partial loss of the ability to smell.

GT0BH2.title: Hypoxia
GT0BH2.description: An inadequate supply of oxygen to tissue, which can result in altered mental status, respiratory distress, cyanosis, and tachycardia. Etiologies include decreased partial pressure of oxygen, dysfunctional breathing, impaired oxygen transfer in the lungs, anemia and resulting lack of hemoglobin, and compromised perfusion.

tT0Xs2.title: Egodystonic
tT0Xs2.description: A descriptor used in psychoanalysis for thoughts and behavior patterns that are not in agreement with an individual's ego (self-image). Many personality disorders and conditions have egodystonic features (e.g., patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder whose behaviors do not reflect their values).

FT0gs2.title: Egosyntonic
FT0gs2.description: A descriptor used in psychoanalysis for thoughts and behavior patterns that are in agreement with an individual's ego (self-image). Many personality disorders and conditions have egosyntonic features (e.g., patients with anorexia nervosa who view their behaviors as congruent with their values).

8T0Os2.title: Implantation metastasis
8T0Os2.description: Seeding of a tumor along the needle tract (e.g., after FNAC or a needle biopsy).

uT0ps2.title: Intermediate filament
uT0ps2.description: A type of cytoskeletal filament that maintains cellular structure. Examples include vimentin, desmin, cytokeratin, and neurofilaments.

ET08s2.title: Interpolation
ET08s2.description: A term used in regression analysis to describe the process of finding the value of the dependent variable (y) for a value of the independent variable (x) that lies within the range of the data set.

vT0As2.title: Intertriginous
vT0As2.description: A descriptor for a region in which two areas of skin come into contact with one another. Examples of intertriginous regions include the genital area, the axilla, the inframammary region, the web spaces of fingers and toes, and skin folds resulting from obesity.

DT01G2.title: Incision
DT01G2.description: A surgical cut or a wound that results in a neat separation of body tissue.

9T0NG2.title: Isosthenuria
9T0NG2.description: An inability of the kidneys to concentrate or dilute urine, which results in the excretion of urine that is isotonic with plasma.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

CT0qG2.title: Karyogamy
CT0qG2.description: The fusion of the nuclei of two gametes during fertilization, which gives rise to a diploid zygote.

xT0EG2.title: Catabolic
xT0EG2.description: A type of metabolism in which complex molecules are broken down into simpler ones, resulting in the release of energy. The opposite of catabolic is anabolic.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Glycolysis versus gluconeogenesis

yT0dt2.title: Clinodactyly
yT0dt2.description: An abnormal curvature of a finger. Typically refers to inward curvature of the 5th finger. Associated with several genetic syndromes, including Down syndrome and Turner syndrome.

AT0Rt2.title: Coke oven gas
AT0Rt2.description: A mixture of volatile substances that are formed by the destructive distillation of coal. Chronic exposure to coke oven gas can result in bronchial carcinoma.

_T05t2.title: Concave
_T05t2.description: A descriptor for something that is hollowed or curved inward.

zT0rt2.title: Concordance
zT0rt2.description:
1. Genetics: The similarity between two related individuals (e.g., twins, first-degree relatives) with respect to a particular attribute (e.g., incidence of a particular disease).
2. ECG: T-wave concordance means that the T-wave is oriented in the same direction as the QRS complex. T-wave concordance is a normal feature of all ECGs. However in a patient with a left bundle branch block, the presence of T-wave concordance signifies ischemia.

-T0Dt2.title: Pupillary near reflex
-T0Dt2.description: A reflex action that allows the eyes to focus on suddenly closer objects by changing the way the light is projected onto the retina. Consists of contraction of the medial recti (convergence/abduction), contraction of the pupillary sphincter (miosis), and contraction of the ciliary muscles (accommodation).

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Accommodation and convergence

Zg0ZF2.title: Convex
Zg0ZF2.description: A descriptor for something that is rounded or curved outward.

ag0QF2.title: Cryoglobulins
ag0QF2.description: A group of immunoglobulins (IgM, IgG, IgA) that precipitate in vitro at temperatures < 37°C. May be associated with cryoglobulinemic vasculitis and hyperviscosity syndrome.

Yg0nF2.title: Lenticonus
Yg0nF2.description: A congenital conical elevation at the anterior pole (anterior lenticonus) or posterior pole (posterior lenticonus) of the crystalline lens in the eye. Anterior lenticonus may be seen in Alport's syndrome, and a posterior lenticonus may be seen in Lowe's syndrome (oculocerebral renal syndrome). A lenticonus appears as an oil globule in the center of the red reflex on direct ophthalmoscopy.

bg0HF2.title: Leukocyturia
bg0HF2.description: The presence of white blood cells (WBCs) in the urine. Typically detected via microscopic examination of the urine sediment. Considered clinically significant if > 5 WBCs are visible per high power field on urine microscopy. Severe leukocyturia can cause visible cloudiness.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

Xg09F2.title: Lisch nodule
Xg09F2.description: A hamartomatous, pigmented lesions of the iris comprised of melanocytes characteristically found in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1.

1g0282.title: Macroscopic hematuria
1g0282.description: Frank blood in the urine resulting in visible bright red or red-brown discoloration of the urine.

Wg0P82.title: Marsupialization
Wg0P82.description: The surgical procedure of incising a closed cavity (e.g., cyst) and suturing its walls to adjacent tissue in order to convert the closed cavity into an open one.

destinations.label: Bartholin gland cyst and abscess → Bartholin gland abscess

Vg0G82.title: Meconium
Vg0G82.description: The first stool that a newborn passes (typically within 24 hours of birth), which is typically green and composed of concentrated bile, mucus, hair, and desquamated cells.

destinations.label: The newborn infant → Assessment of the newborn

Ug0bu2.title: Metamorphopsia
Ug0bu2.description: A type of visual distortion in which straight lines appear wavy, which can be tested for using an Amsler grid. It is associated with certain ocular conditions, most notably macular degeneration.

2g0Tu2.title: Metaplasia
2g0Tu2.description: A reversible transformation of a mature cell type into another cell type that is not native to that specific region in response to chronic irritation or cell injury (e.g., transformation of squamous epithelium into columnar epithelium in the case of Barrett esophagus).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cellular adaptation

fg0ku2.title: Microscopic hematuria
fg0ku2.description: The presence of red blood cells (RBCs) in urine on microscopic examination of the urine sediment (in contrast to gross hematuria, which is evident on visual inspection of urine). Considered clinically significant if ≥ 3 RBCs are visible per high-power field on urine microscopy.

Tg06u2.title: Microsatellites
Tg06u2.description: A sequence of repetitive, short (2-6 base pairs), noncoding DNA sequences used as a genetic marker.

gg0Fu2.title: Miosis
gg0Fu2.description: Constriction of the pupil. Can be physiological (e.g., pupillary response to light) or nonphysiological (e.g., due to nerve compression in Horner syndrome or drug effects).

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Pupillary response

hg0cE2.title: Mucolysis
hg0cE2.description: Dissolution of thick mucus secretions in the respiratory tract.

3g0SE2.title: Mucocele
3g0SE2.description: Collection of mucus in a pre-existing hollow space (e.g., paranasal sinus, lacrimal sac, appendix). Trauma, chronic infections, and surgical procedures can obstruct the ostium of a paranasal sinus, leading to retention of secretions and pressure atrophy of the paranasal sinus.

Rg0lE2.title: Müllerian ducts
Rg0lE2.description: A pair of embryonal ducts that give rise to the fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, and upper one-third of the vagina in a female fetus. In a male fetus, the production of Müllerian inhibiting factor by the Sertoli cells of the testes causes degeneration of the Müllerian (or paramesonephric) ducts.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Ductal sex differentiation

ig0JE2.title: Mydriasis
ig0JE2.description: A dilation of the pupil. Either due to physiological pupillary response (dark surroundings) or nonphysiological causes such as trauma (e.g., head injury), oculomotor nerve injury (e.g., autonomic neuropathy), and drug intoxication (e.g., amphetamines, cocaine).

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Pupillary response

Qg0uE2.title: Myoglobinuria
Qg0uE2.description: The presence of myoglobin in the urine. Etiologies include extensive muscle injury (e.g., rhabdomyolysis from crush injury) and McArdle disease (GSD type V). Can result in acute tubular necrosis.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

jg0_E2.title: Myoclonus
jg0_E2.description: A brief, shock-like, involuntary twitch of a muscle or groups of muscles caused by muscular contraction or inhibition. Pathological causes include encephalitis, trauma to the head and/or spinal cord, hypoxia, toxic or metabolic encephalopathies, degenerative diseases (e.g., Creutzfeld-Jakob disease), and certain epilepsy syndromes (e.g., juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome).

Pg0Wv2.title: Na+-K+-ATPase
Pg0Wv2.description: A transmembrane protein pump that actively transports three Na+ ions out of the cell for every two K+ ions that it moves into the cell. Uses ATP for energy. The ATP binding site is on the cytosolic side. Na+-K+-ATPase maintains the concentration gradients of Na+ and K+ and is thus responsible for the resting membrane potential of all cells. The pump is phosporylated when it transports sodium and dephosphorylated when it transports potassium.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Resting potential

4g03v2.title: Afterload
4g03v2.description: The force against which the ventricle contracts to eject blood during systole. Afterload is primarily determined by the blood pressure in the aorta, which is influenced by total peripheral resistance.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Factors that affect cardiac output

Og0Iv2.title: Nephrocalcinosis
Og0Iv2.description: The generalized interstitial deposition of calcium oxalate or calcium phosphate in the kidney (usually in the renal medulla). Occurs as a result of increased urinary excretion of calcium, phosphate, and/or oxalate. Usually asymptomatic and diagnosed incidentally on abdominal x-ray, CT, or ultrasound (macroscopic nephrocalcinosis) or by renal biopsy (microscopic nephrocalcinosis).

Ng0-v2.title: Neurotropic
Ng0-v2.description: A descriptor for any agent (e.g., a drug, pathogen, or toxin) that selectively affects nerve tissue.

mg0VD2.title: Noncaseating granuloma
mg0VD2.description: A nodular collection of macrophages that forms as a result of inflammation without central necrosis. Associated with sarcoidosis, berylliosis, and Crohn disease.

5g0iD2.title: Nocturia
5g0iD2.description: The need to wake one or more times at night to urinate. Quantitatively, nocturnal polyuria is defined as the passage of > 33% of 24-hour urine output at night.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

Mg0MD2.title: Nystagmus
Mg0MD2.description: A series of involuntary, rhythmic, oscillatory eye movements.

Lg0wD2.title: Oligodendrocyte
Lg0wD2.description: A glial cell of the central nervous system that myelinates nerves.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

og00w2.title: Oliguria
og00w2.description: Reduced urine production. Causes include prerenal and intrinsic acute kidney injury. Defined as urine output of < 0.5 mL/kg/h or < 400 mL/24 hours in adults.

Kg0Uw2.title: Osmolality
Kg0Uw2.description: The number of solute particles (or osmoles) per unit mass of solvent (mOsm/kg). Distinct from osmolarity (mOsm/L) but used interchangeably in clinical practice, as 1 L and 1 kg of biological solutions are often equivalent. Used preferentially to describe the osmotic pressure of biological fluids, as it does not vary with temperature and can be measured by an osmometer.

6g0jw2.title: Osmotic fragility
6g0jw2.description: The measure of a cell's structural integrity in response to osmotic stress: E.g., in the case of normal erythrocytes, hemolysis begins when the erythrocytes are placed in a 0.5% NaCl solution, whereas in a 0.25% NaCl solution, all erythrocytes are hemolyzed.

pg0Lw2.title: Pallesthesia
pg0Lw2.description: The ability to perceive vibration. Mediated by sensory receptors such as Pacinian corpuscles, Meissner corpuscles, and Merkel disc receptors and carried by the dorsal columns.

Jg0sw2.title: Pandemic
Jg0sw2.description: A disease that spreads quickly worldwide and is limited to a specific time period (e.g., Spanish influenza in 1918-1919).

destinations.label: Population health → Elements describing population health

qg0Cw2.title: Pancytopenia
qg0Cw2.description: A decrease in all blood cell lineages, leading to anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukopenia. Causes are divided into impaired blood cell production and increased cell destruction.

Ig0Y92.title: Parulis
Ig0Y92.description: Inflammation of the periodontium that eventually leads to the formation of a gum abscess.

rg0f92.title: Pathognomonic
rg0f92.description: A symptom, clinical sign, or diagnostic finding that is characteristic of a particular disease.

Hg0K92.title: Photophobia
Hg0K92.description: A symptom of eye pain associated with exposure to bright light. Associated with migraine headaches and meningitis.

Gg0B92.title: Pityriasis alba
Gg0B92.description: Dry, scaly, hypopigmented skin lesions that are self-limited and harmless. Most commonly occur in children.

tg0XC2.title: White thrombus
tg0XC2.description: A thrombus that is composed predominantly of platelets and has very few erythrocytes. White thrombi usually occur in arteries.

Fg0gC2.title: Pleural fibrosis
Fg0gC2.description: A condition that is characterized by fibrous adhesions between the visceral and parietal pleura. Usually develops following pleuritis and/or pleural effusions and can result in restrictive lung disease. Appears on chest X-rays as diffuse pleural thickening or localized plaques.

8g0OC2.title: Pneumonectomy
8g0OC2.description: The surgical resection of an entire lung.

ug0pC2.title: Podocyte
ug0pC2.description: A specialized cell of the inner layer of the Bowman capsule. Has foot processes that form narrow filtration slits, through which plasma filters into the lumen of the Bowman capsule.

Eg08C2.title: Poikilocytosis
Eg08C2.description: A hematologic finding of abnormally-shaped erythrocytes (e.g., acanthocytes, echinocytes).

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

Dg01x2.title: Polydactyly
Dg01x2.description: The presence of > 5 digits on a hand or foot. Can occur as an isolated mutation and have no pathological value (often unilateral) or be a symptom of an underlying condition (usually bilateral), e.g., trisomy 13.

wg0hx2.title: Polyuria
wg0hx2.description: The production of an abnormally large amount of urine. Quantitative thresholds vary by age. Adults: > 3L/day; neonates: > 150 mL/kg/day; children ≤ 2 years of age: > 100–110 mL/kg/day; older children: > 40–50 mL/kg/day.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

9g0Nx2.title: Postictal
9g0Nx2.description: The phase immediately after the end of a seizure. Notable for typical neurological findings such as confusion, drowsiness, headache, speech impairment, and weakness. Can last for minutes to hours.

Cg0qx2.title: Nonmaleficence
Cg0qx2.description: An ethical concept that is based on the statement "do no harm" from the Hippocratic Oath. May be outweighed in certain situations by the benefits of 'harming' the patient, e.g., as in most surgeries.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Medical ethics

Bg0zx2.title: Pupillary block
Bg0zx2.description: The apposition of the lens and the iris, which hinders the flow of aqueous humor from the posterior chamber into the anterior chamber and increases pressure in the posterior chamber. This causes the iris to bulge forward (iris bombe). In patients with a shallow anterior chamber, the bulging iris can block the iridocorneal angle and result in increased intraocular pressure.

Ag0RB2.title: Rathke pouch
Ag0RB2.description: An embryonal, ectodermal outpouching of the pharyngeal roof, which develops into the anterior pituitary gland (adenohypophysis). Like the CNS, the anterior pituitary arises from the ectoderm. However, while the CNS arises from the neural tube, the anterior pituitary is derived from the stomatodeum, which develops into Rathke's pouch.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

_g05B2.title: Renal function test
_g05B2.description: A set of laboratory tests, including serum creatinine, urea, uric acid, and cystatin C, that serve as parameters to assess kidney function. An increase in the value of any one of these parameters may indicate impaired kidney function.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Renal function test

zg0rB2.title: Reciprocal translocation
zg0rB2.description: A chromosomal mutation in which genetic material is exchanged between nonhomologous chromosomes.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

0S0ey2.title: Rostral
0S0ey2.description: An anatomical direction indicating a structure situated toward the mouth or nasal cavity. When used to describe the brain, indicates a structure situated toward the tip of the frontal lobe.

media.title: Cranial anatomical terms of location and direction

aS0Qy2.title: Rumpel-Leede test
aS0Qy2.description: Appearance of petechiae on the forearm when a tourniquet is applied to the ipsilateral arm and inflated to a point between diastolic and systolic blood pressure for 2 minutes. Positive if 10 or more petechiae per square inch appear on the forearm. Most commonly used to assess for dengue fever.

YS0ny2.title: Winged scapula
YS0ny2.description: An abnormally prominent medial or lateral border of the scapula. Common causes include paralysis of the trapezius muscle (supplied by cranial nerve XI) and paralysis of the serratus anterior muscle (supplied by the long thoracic nerve).

destinations.label: Peripheral nerve injuries → Nerve injuries in the upper body

XS09y2.title: Gravitation abscess
XS09y2.description: An abscess that extends caudally through tissue planes or structures as a result of gravity.

1S02A2.title: Sclerosis
1S02A2.description: A pathological hardening of tissue as a result of an inflammatory or a degenerative process. Characterized histologically by an increase in the level of collagen and/or reticulin.

WS0PA2.title: Southern blot
WS0PA2.description: A laboratory method that involves gel electrophoresis and blotting and is used to detect DNA sequences.

VS0GA2.title: Soluble transferrin receptor
VS0GA2.description: A part of the transferrin 1 receptor that regulates endocytosis of transferrin-bound iron by erythroid cells of the bone marrow. Soluble transferrin receptor levels increase in conditions associated with erythroid hyperplasia (e.g., iron deficiency anemia, chronic hemolytic anemia) and decrease in conditions associated with erythroid hypoplasia (e.g., aplastic anemia, chronic renal failure).

2S0T_2.title: Vocal fremitus
2S0T_2.description: A part of the pulmonary examination used to evaluate the conduction of vibrations to the chest wall produced during speech. Palpate the posterior chest wall with the ulnar aspects of both hands while the patient says a phrase such as "toy boat". Fremitus becomes more pronounced in the presence of consolidation and less pronounced in the presence of effusion or pneumothorax. The examiner can also assess fremitus with a stethoscope on the chest wall (vocal fremitus).

fS0k_2.title: Strangury
fS0k_2.description: Painful, interrupted, drop-by-drop urination as a result of spasmodic contraction of the bladder and urethra. Common causes include cystitis, urethral calculus, and bladder cancer.

TS06_2.title: Striatum
TS06_2.description: A part of the basal ganglia that is composed of the caudate nucleus and putamen. The striatum receives most of the input from the motor cortex.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

gS0F_2.title: Stupor
gS0F_2.description: An altered mental state of decreased responsiveness to the environment and responsiveness only to intense or painful stimuli (e.g., during a medical examination). It can be a manifestation of catatonia or result from medical conditions like traumatic brain injury (TBI) or critical illness, indicating significant dysfunction of the brain or metabolic processes.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

SS0y_2.title: Superantigen
SS0y_2.description: Viral or bacterial antigens that cause nonspecific activation of multiple clones of T cells, resulting in massive cytokine release. Unlike normal antigens, superantigens do not have to be processed and presented by macrophages for recognition by specific T cells. Superantigens bind directly to the MHC II complexes of T cells, resulting in widespread polyclonal T-cell activation. Exotoxins produced by certain bacteria are important examples of superantigens (e.g., TSST-1 toxin produced by S. aureus can result in toxic shock syndrome).

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

hS0cz2.title: Symblepharon
hS0cz2.description: Adhesion(s) between the palpebral conjunctiva and the bulbar conjunctiva. Common causes include burns, inadequately treated conjunctivitis, eye surgery, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, pemphigoid, and trachoma.

3S0Sz2.title: Synesthesia
3S0Sz2.description: A perception of a sense other than the sense that is stimulated (e.g., auditory stimulus also produces olfactory sensation).

iS0Jz2.title: Tenesmus
iS0Jz2.description: A distressing and persistent but ineffectual urge to empty the rectum or bladder.

QS0uz2.title: Tortuosity
QS0uz2.description: Characterized by many twists and/or turns (e.g., retinal vessels, conjunctival vessels).

jS0_z2.title: Trocar
jS0_z2.description: An instrument with a sharp conical end that is used in minimally invasive surgery (e.g., laparoscopy) to establish a portal of entry into a body cavity (e.g., abdomen, thorax).

kS0m-2.title: Virilization
kS0m-2.description: The appearance of male secondary sexual characteristics (e.g., voice deepening, hirsutism, male-pattern hair loss, increased muscle mass, clitoromegaly) in a female individual. Can develop in any condition that causes hyperandrogenism.

lS0v-2.title: Preload
lS0v-2.description: The extent to which heart muscle fibers are stretched before the onset of systole. Preload is directly related to end-diastolic pressure and end-diastolic volume.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Factors that affect cardiac output

NS0--2.title: Western blot
NS0--2.description: A form of gel electrophoresis which is used to detect specific proteins in blood, cerebrospinal fluid, and tissue samples.

mS0VZf.title: Xanthochromia
mS0VZf.description: The presence of bilirubin in the cerebrospinal fluid, resulting in yellow discoloration that can be assessed by direct visualization or, if available, via spectrophotometry. Typically, xanthochromia is a result of hemoglobin breakdown that occurs within 12 hours after bleeding into the CSF (most commonly due to a subarachnoid hemorrhage). Rarely, xanthochromia can occur because of significant hyperbilirubinemia.

5S0iZf.title: Circumduction
5S0iZf.description: The movement of a limb in which the proximal end remains fixed while the distal end traces a circle. Circumduction is a combination of isolated movements such as flexion, extension, abduction, and adduction.

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

MS0MZf.title: Intermediate host
MS0MZf.description: An organism in which a parasite undergoes asexual development. Forms an essential part of the life cycle of a parasite. Can be human, and the affected individual develops symptoms of the parasitic infection. The parasite is eventually transmitted actively or passively to another intermediate host or a definitive host.

nS07Zf.title: Cytoplasm
nS07Zf.description: The substance that is enclosed by the cell membrane but not by the nuclear membrane, including all the organelles, structures, and compounds within that substance.

LS0wZf.title: ß-lactamase
LS0wZf.description: A bacterial enzyme that hydrolyzes the beta-lactam ring of beta-lactam antibiotics, rendering the bacteria resistant to these antibiotics.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanisms of drug resistance

oS000f.title: Cordocentesis
oS000f.description:
A prenatal diagnostic procedure in which fetal blood is withdrawn via ultrasound-guided transabdominal needle insertion into the umbilical cord. Cordocentesis can be performed after 18 weeks of gestation for the following indications:
1. To identify the type of fetal hemoglobin and to assess the severity of fetal anemia
2. To diagnose genetic defects in the fetus if amniocentesis, chorionic villus sampling, and/or fetal ultrasound are inconclusive
3. To diagnose fetal infections if amniocentesis is inconclusive

6S0j0f.title: Orthopnea
6S0j0f.description: A sensation of shortness of breath that occurs upon lying down and is relieved by sitting up. Left ventricular failure is a common cause.

JS0s0f.title: Poliosis
JS0s0f.description: A decrease or absence of melanin in hair bulbs. Usually manifests as patches of white or grey hair on the scalp, eyelashes, or eyebrows.

qS0C0f.title: Flu-like symptoms
qS0C0f.description: A combination of nonspecific symptoms typically associated with influenza. Includes headache, body ache, fever, and malaise.

IS0Yaf.title: Epicanthus
IS0Yaf.description: A sickle-shaped fold of skin which covers the canthus and caruncle of the inner corner of the eye. It is a normal finding in certain races (e.g., Asians) and is associated with some genetic syndromes (e.g., Down syndrome).

rS0faf.title: Hypertelorism
rS0faf.description: An increased distance between two paired organs or parts of the body. However, the word hypertelorism is often used to refer to ocular hypertelorism, which is defined as a distance between the eyes that is greater than the 95th percentile. It is commonly idiopathic or caused by congenital disorders (e.g., Down syndrome, Noonan syndrome).

7S04af.title: Micrognathia
7S04af.description: A condition of congenital mandibular hypoplasia. Can be hereditary with no pathological association or occur as a symptom of numerous syndromes (e.g., trisomies). Can lead to feeding difficulties and abnormal tooth alignment.

destinations.label: Rare inherited syndromes → Pierre Robin sequence (Pierre Robin syndrome)
Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital T-cell immunodeficiencies

media.title: Surgical treatment of Pierre Robin sequence (2/3)

HS0Kaf.title: Trident hand
HS0Kaf.description: A deformity of the hand that is typically associated with achondroplasia and characterized by short stubby fingers of equal size and an increased separation between the middle finger and ring finger, which gives the hand the three-pronged appearance of a trident.

tS0XYf.title: Terminal disinfection
tS0XYf.description: Disinfection of an area that was previously occupied by a patient aimed at eliminating all sources of infection for any individual who later enters the same area. Terminal disinfection is an important measure in reducing the number of nosocomial infections.

8S0OYf.title: Akinetic mutism
8S0OYf.description: A condition characterized by decreased motor responses and paucity of speech. Caused by injury to the mesial frontal region of the brain (e.g., from traumatic brain injury, hydrocephalus, Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease).

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Appearance and behavior

uS0pYf.title: Sex chromosome
uS0pYf.description: The chromosomes that determine the sex of an individual are called sex chromosomes, while all other chromosomes are called autosomes. A normal individual has 22 pairs of homologous chromosomes and 2 sex chromosomes. The female karyotype is 46XX and the male karyotype is 46XY.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

ES08Yf.title: Autosome
ES08Yf.description: All chromosomes with the exception of the gender-specific chromosomes (X and Y) are called autosomes. A normal individual has 22 pairs of homologous autosomes and 2 sex chromosomes. The female karyotype is 46XX and the male karyotype is 46XY.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

vS0AYf.title: Heterozygote
vS0AYf.description: Two genetically different alleles are present at the same loci in a pair of homologous chromosomes.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

DS01bf.title: Homozygote
DS01bf.description: Two genetically identical alleles are present at the same loci in a pair of homologous chromosomes.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

wS0hbf.title: Penetrance
wS0hbf.description: The probability that individuals with a disease-specific genotype will manifest with the disease's corresponding phenotype. Can be complete penetrance (e.g., 100% of individuals with the mutation for autosomal dominant Huntington disease develop the disease) or incomplete penetrance (e.g., BRCA1 gene mutations lead to breast cancer in about half of cases).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

9S0Nbf.title: Expressivity
9S0Nbf.description: The extent to which a phenotype is manifested in an individual carrying a particular genotype. In the case of genes with variable expressivity, the severity of the disease varies even among individuals with the same disease-specific genotype.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

xS0Ebf.title: Hysteroscopy
xS0Ebf.description: A procedure to view the uterine cavity and the tubal ostia using a fiberoptic endoscope that is passed transcervically. Diagnostic indications include evaluation of abnormal uterine bleeding and diagnostics of infertility. Therapeutic indications include resection of polyps and submucosal myomas, endometrial ablation and/or resection, and resection of uterine septa (metroplasty) and/or adhesions.

BS0zbf.title: Hypochromia
BS0zbf.description: A descriptor for decreased pigmentation of cells (e.g., due to decreased hemoglobin concentration).

yS0dXf.title: Hyperchromia
yS0dXf.description: A descriptor for increased pigmentation of cells (e.g., due to increased hemoglobin concentration).

AS0RXf.title: Microcytic
AS0RXf.description: A descriptor for cells of abnormally small size (e.g., erythrocytes in patients with iron deficiency anemia).

zS0rXf.title: Azotemia
zS0rXf.description: An increase in the level of nitrogenous waste (both urea and creatinine) due to renal insufficiency.

-S0DXf.title: Aerophagia
-S0DXf.description: Swallowing of air. Aerophagia may occur physiologically during swallowing. It can also be a symptom of autonomic disorders, anxiety, and/or disorders of the stomach.

0h0ecf.title: Fovea centralis
0h0ecf.description: A pit in the center of the macula that is composed of cone cells. Has the highest visual acuity of any region in the retina.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

Yh0ncf.title: Dislocation
Yh0ncf.description: A complete displacement of the bones at a joint such that the articular surfaces of the bones are no longer in contact.

Xh09cf.title: Cervical incompetence
Xh09cf.description: Painless cervical dilation, in the absence of uterine contractions and/or labor, in the second trimester of pregnancy. Can lead to second-trimester pregnancy loss and preterm birth.

destinations.label: Maternal complications during pregnancy → Cervical insufficiency

ch0a1f.title: Bronchophony
ch0a1f.description: An abnormal increase in the clarity and pitch of the spoken voice heard over the lung. Bronchophony can indicate the solidification of lung tissue.

Wh0P1f.title: Interposition graft
Wh0P1f.description: A graft that is used to surgically bridge a tissue defect (e.g., following resection of blood vessels, ureters, or segments of the stomach or intestine).

dh0o1f.title: External urethral meatus
dh0o1f.description: The distal, external opening of the urethra. Serves as the terminal portion of the spongy (penile) urethra.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Urethra

Vh0G1f.title: Locomotor system
Vh0G1f.description: A collective term for structures such as muscles, joints, bones, tendons, and ligaments that permit movement.

eh0x1f.title: Tonometry
eh0x1f.description: The measurement of intraocular pressure. Methods include Goldmann applanation tonometry (gold standard) and handheld applanation tonometry (e.g., Tono-Pen).

Uh0bWf.title: Urinoma
Uh0bWf.description: A cyst containing urine that forms outside the urinary tract following trauma or a surgical procedure involving the kidneys and/or the urinary tract.

2h0TWf.title: Renal capsule
2h0TWf.description: A layer of connective tissue that forms a capsule around the kidney and adrenal gland.

fh0kWf.title: Intrinsic activity
fh0kWf.description: The extent to which a drug activates a receptor after binding to it. The intrinsic activity of a drug is expressed as a fraction of the maximum possible receptor activation in the corresponding tissue. A pure agonist has an intrinsic activity of 1, while a pure antagonist has an intrinsic activity of 0.

Th06Wf.title: Bradyphrenia
Th06Wf.description: A slowing down of information and thought processing. Common causes include Parkinson disease, schizophrenia, antipsychotics (where it can occur as an adverse effect), and certain forms of dementia.

gh0FWf.title: Micrographia
gh0FWf.description: An acquired defect of writing in which an individual's handwriting becomes smaller and cramped. A common cause is Parkinson disease.

Sh0yWf.title: Hypomimia
Sh0yWf.description: A reduced degree of facial expression. Can be caused by neurologic conditions (e.g., facial nerve paralysis, Parkinson disease, myasthenia gravis), psychiatric conditions (e.g., depression), and connective tissue diseases (e.g., scleroderma).

hh0cdf.title: Telangiectasia
hh0cdf.description: A small, dilated, intradermal blood vessel, red to dark blue in color, with a diameter of < 1 mm. Etiologies include venous insufficiency (spider veins), acquired conditions (e.g., cirrhosis, rosacea, connective tissue diseases), inherited conditions (e.g., ataxia telangiectasia), and neoplastic conditions (e.g., basal cell carcinoma).

media.title: Telangiectasias, reticular veins, and corona phlebectatica

3h0Sdf.title: AMPK
3h0Sdf.description: An enzyme which protects cells from a lack of ATP (energy deficiency) by increasing cellular uptake of glucose and fatty acid oxidation. AMP-activated protein kinase is a unique enzyme that should not be confused with cAMP-activated protein kinase (protein kinase A).

Rh0ldf.title: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor
Rh0ldf.description: A family of transcription factors that regulate metabolism. There are three subtypes: PPAR-α (decrease triglyceride levels), PPAR-β/δ (increase fatty acid breakdown), and PPAR-γ (increase insulin sensitivity). PPAR-α receptors are targets of fibrates, a class of antilipidemic drugs. PPAR-γ receptors are targets of glitazones (thiazolidinediones), a class of antidiabetic drugs.

destinations.label: Second-line lipid-lowering agents → Fibrates (fibric acid derivatives)

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications
Overview of lipid metabolism and lipid-lowering agents

Qh0udf.title: Iatrogenic
Qh0udf.description: A descriptor for any harm resulting from a medical treatment or procedure.

Ph0WVf.title: Pannus
Ph0WVf.description:
1. Rheumatology: A granulation tissue growth in the inflamed synovium that causes it to become thickened and edematous in patients with chronic rheumatoid arthritis. It can cause fibrous ankylosis and/or joint deformities and the destruction of other intraarticular structures, such as cartilage.
2. Ophthalmology: Superficial vascularization of the cornea with cellular infiltration; a complication of a variety of inflammatory and infectious conditions such as HSV keratitis, chemical injury, or keratoconjunctivitis (e.g., trachoma conjunctivitis).

mh0Vef.title: Detumescence
mh0Vef.description: The subsidence of an erection or a swelling in general.

destinations.label: Male reproductive organs → Male sexual response

nh07ef.title: Uvea
nh07ef.description: The vascular middle layer of the eyeball that lies between the retina and the sclera. It consists of three parts: the iris, the ciliary body, and the choroid.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

oh00Uf.title: Microfold cells
oh00Uf.description: A type of specialized epithelial cell of gut-associated lymphoid tissue and component of the immune system.  Endocytoses antigens for delivery to antigen-presenting.

Kh0UUf.title: Antipyretic
Kh0UUf.description: A drug that reduces fever (e.g., acetaminophen, ibuprofen).

6h0jUf.title: Linea terminalis
6h0jUf.description: A line that forms the boundary of the pelvic inlet and consists of the pubic symphysis, the pubic crest, the pectineal line (pubis), the arcuate line (ileum), the sacral ala, and the sacral promontory.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

ph0LUf.title: Widal test
ph0LUf.description: A serological test for typhoid fever in which a patient's serum is diluted and mixed with H and O antigens of Salmonella. If antibodies against the pathogen are present in the serum, antigen-antibody complex formation causes agglutination.

Jh0sUf.title: Off-label use
Jh0sUf.description: The use of an FDA-approved drug for an unapproved clinical indication, with an unapproved dosage, through an unapproved route of administration, and/or for an unapproved subpopulation.

rh0f2f.title: Intercostal space
rh0f2f.description: The anatomic space between two adjacent ribs. Contains intercostal muscle, arteries, veins, lymph nodes, and nerves. The vessels and nerves take their course near the superior portions of the intercostal spaces.

7h042f.title: Focused assessment with sonography for trauma
7h042f.description: A rapid, standardized, bedside ultrasonographic test used to screen for free fluid (e.g., blood) in the right upper quadrant, left upper quadrant, pericardial space, and pelvis. An extended version (eFAST) adds an evaluation of the chest for signs of pneumothorax. Most commonly used in unstable patients with trauma.

media.title: Free fluid in hepatorenal space (Morison pouch)
Free fluid in the splenorenal recess

Hh0K2f.title: Hemarthrosis
Hh0K2f.description: A condition of blood within a joint. Etiologies include a tear in a ligament, meniscus, or joint capsule; osteochondral fracture; coagulation defects (e.g., hemophilia); surgery involving the joint (e.g., arthroscopy).

destinations.label: Hemostasis and bleeding disorders → Clinical features

sh0t2f.title: Hemolytic crisis
sh0t2f.description: An acute life-threatening complication that occurs as a result of a sudden, massive breakdown of erythrocytes at a rate that exceeds the ability of bone marrow to replace them. A hemolytic crisis is usually caused by an acute trigger and presents with fever, chills, icterus, severe pallor, tachycardia. and/or symptoms of shock.

th0Xff.title: Gibbus
th0Xff.description: A hump or kyphotic deformity in the spine (usually thoracolumbar spine). Common causes include spinal fracture and spondylodiscitis (especially Pott's disease).

media.title: Tuberculous spondylitis (Pott disease) with gibbus deformity

Fh0gff.title: Bradycardia
Fh0gff.description: A heart rate of less than 60 beats/min in adults. Children have their own age-specific values for the minimum heart frequency.

8h0Off.title: Phlebotomy
8h0Off.description: The removal of blood from the body primarily via venipuncture to use for diagnostic laboratory studies. May be performed therapeutically for patients with iron overload in hereditary hemochromatosis or viscosity symptoms in polycythemia vera.

uh0pff.title: Molecular mimicry
uh0pff.description: The antigenic resemblance between molecules on some pathogens and those of normal cells in the body. Can cause autoimmune disease if the immune response against pathogens also attacks normal cells (e.g., in acute rheumatic fever).

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → Immune tolerance and autoimmunity

Eh08ff.title: Panniculitis
Eh08ff.description: An inflammation of subcutaneous fat that typically manifests as tender, erythematous nodules, most commonly on the extremities. Causes include infections, allergic reactions, external injury, and malignancy. Types include erythema nodosum and lipodermatosclerosis.

vh0Aff.title: Arthrodesis
vh0Aff.description: A surgical fusion of two bones in a functional position (e.g., in severe, therapy-resistant osteoarthritis or in severe deformities).

Dh01Tf.title: PTHrP
Dh01Tf.description: A protein produced by malignant cells that has the same function as parathyroid hormone. Production of PTHrP is the most common cause of hypercalcemia of malignancy.

wh0hTf.title: Synovectomy
wh0hTf.description: Open or arthroscopic removal of damaged synovial tissue. Possible indications include rheumatoid arthritis and bacterial arthritis.

9h0NTf.title: Arthrography
9h0NTf.description: Radiographic visualization of a synovial joint (e.g., shoulder, hip) after injection of a contrast medium (air and/or a radiopaque dye) into the joint. Arthrography was previously used to visualize cartilage, ligaments, and/or the joint capsule, but has now been replaced by MRI.

xh0ETf.title: Infectivity
xh0ETf.description: The ability of a pathogen to grow and multiply in a host and spread to other hosts.

destinations.label: Population health → Elements describing population health

Bh0zTf.title: Sniffing position
Bh0zTf.description: The position of the head during intubation. The patient's head is elevated to a height of 10 cm using a neck cushion, and the neck is extended at the atlanto-occipital joint so that the region between the incisors and the epiglottis is aligned in a straight line. This position makes endotracheal intubation using direct laryngoscopy possible. However, this position may worsen cervical injury.

media.title: Sniffing position: three axis alignment theory

yh0dgf.title: Cyanosis
yh0dgf.description: A physical examination finding in which the skin appears dusky blue due to the presence of deoxygenated hemoglobin, which is dark red in color. This is in comparison to the normal pink color of skin caused by the bright red of oxygenated hemoglobin. Peripheral cyanosis can be seen in the limbs; central cyanosis can be seen on the tongue and lips.

zh0rgf.title: Six Ps of acute limb ischemia
zh0rgf.description: The 6 Ps summarize the main clinical features of acute limb ischemia: pain, pallor, pulselessness, paralysis, paresthesia, and poikilothermia.

-h0Dgf.title: Steatorrhea
-h0Dgf.description: A condition of foul-smelling, bulky, oily, floating stool caused by a pathological increase in stool fat content. Etiologies include processes that disrupt exocrine pancreatic function (e.g., cystic fibrosis, chronic pancreatitis), bile salt availability (e.g., gallstone disease, hypolipidemic drugs), and small intestine malabsorption (e.g., celiac disease).

Z30ZSf.title: Binocular diplopia
Z30ZSf.description: Double vision that occurs when both eyes are open.

030eSf.title: Monocular diplopia
030eSf.description: Double vision that disappears when the eye with the pathology is covered or shut.

a30QSf.title: Coloboma
a30QSf.description: A unilateral or bilateral developmental disorder of the eye in which the choroid fissure fails to close, resulting in a defect in one of the structures of the eye (e.g., retina, optic disc, iris). The most common manifestation is a keyhole-shaped defect of the iris.

Y30nSf.title: Halitosis
Y30nSf.description: A condition of having unpleasant odor to the breath. Etiologies include oral infections, consumption of certain foods, gastroesophageal reflux disease, Zenker diverticulum, and fetor hepaticus.

b30HSf.title: Pterygium
b30HSf.description: A triangular, fleshy thickening of the bulbar conjunctiva that usually extends from the inner corner of the eye to the corneal surface.

X309Sf.title: Gonadal dysgenesis
X309Sf.description: A developmental disorder in which germ cells are not present in the rudimentary gonads (testes, ovaries). Examples of gonadal dysgenesis include Turner syndrome and pure gonadal syndrome (e.g., Swyer syndrome).

destinations.label: Differences (disorders) of sex development → Gonadal dysgenesis

c30ahf.title: Singultus
c30ahf.description: A quick, involuntary contraction of the diaphragm, which leads to inspiration and a loud, reflexive closure of the vocal cords (commonly called a hiccup). Psychogenic hiccups are continuous hiccups that are not explained by any organic disease and disappear during sleep.

1302hf.title: Pancreatitis
1302hf.description: An inflammation of the pancreas that typically causes epigastric pain that radiates to the back. Further categorized as acute or chronic. Etiologies include alcohol use disorder and pancreatic ductal obstruction.

W30Phf.title: Polydipsia
W30Phf.description: A condition of excessive thirst. Can be caused by organic (e.g., dehydration, hypovolemia, hyperglycemia, diabetes insipidus) or non-organic conditions (e.g., psychogenic polydipsia).

d30ohf.title: Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
d30ohf.description: A condition of insufficient sex steroid production in the gonads that leads to low serum concentrations of sex hormones (e.g., estrogen, testosterone) with a compensatory increase in the concentrations of pituitary gonadotropins (e.g., FSH, LH). Causes include gonadal dysgenesis (e.g., Turner Syndrome), gonadal tumors, or other gonadal injury (e.g., infiltrative disease, radiation, infection).

e30xhf.title: Natriuresis
e30xhf.description: Increased renal excretion of sodium. Natriuresis also results in an increase in urine output (diuresis) because of the osmotic effect of sodium.

U30b3f.title: Facial flush
U30b3f.description: A transient reddening of the face and neck caused by vasodilation of small arteries and arterioles. Triggers include certain diseases (e.g., carcinoid syndrome), ingestion of certain drugs (e.g., niacin), heat, emotional factors, or physical exertion.

f30k3f.title: Conjunctival injection
f30k3f.description: A redness of the conjunctivae of the eye due to vasodilatation and increased blood flow through conjunctival vessels.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → External eye examination

T3063f.title: Ciliary injection
T3063f.description: A red or rose-colored, ringlike pattern of vasodilation around the cornea. Ciliary injection is seen in diseases of the cornea, ciliary body, and iris.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → External eye examination

g30F3f.title: Mixed injection
g30F3f.description: A combination of ciliary and conjunctival injection.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → External eye examination

S30y3f.title: Index case
S30y3f.description: The first patient recorded as having a previously unknown infectious or hereditary disease.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Other types of inheritance

h30cRf.title: Left anterior descending artery
h30cRf.description: A branch of the left coronary artery that runs between the right and left ventricles on the anterior surface of the heart toward the cardiac apex. Supplies > 50% of the left ventricle (mainly the anterior portion), the anterior wall of the right ventricle, the anterior region of the interventricular septum, and the papillary muscles.

R30lRf.title: Cesarean delivery
R30lRf.description: An obstetric procedure in which a baby is delivered via an incision over the lower abdomen. Conducted when vaginal delivery is not possible or is risky for the mother and/or fetus.

i30JRf.title: Episiotomy
i30JRf.description: An obstetric procedure in which the perineum is incised at the end of the second stage of labor in order to facilitate delivery (by enlarging the vulval orifice) and to prevent spontaneous perineal or vaginal tears. Based on the axis of the incision, an episiotomy may be median, lateral, or mediolateral.

4303if.title: Dual antiplatelet therapy
4303if.description: A combination treatment with aspirin and a platelet P2Y12 receptor blocker (e.g., clopidogrel) used to reduce the risk of thrombosis after arterial stenting (e.g., PCI) and for secondary prevention of stroke.

k30mif.title: Xerostomia
k30mif.description: A condition of dryness of the mouth. Common causes include drugs (e.g., diuretics, anticholinergics), dehydration, Sjögren syndrome, and ionizing radiation.

O30Iif.title: Erythropoietin
O30Iif.description: A hormone endogenously released by the interstitial cells of the kidney that stimulates the production of erythrocytes in the bone marrow. It can be administered exogenously to patients with chronic kidney disease to stimulate erythropoiesis, which can prevent and treat anemia of chronic kidney disease.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Bone marrow and hematopoiesis
Physiology of the kidney → Hormone synthesis

m30VQf.title: Nondisjunction
m30VQf.description: The failure of a pair of homologous chromosomes to separate during meiosis I or the failure of a pair of sister chromatids to separate during meiosis II or mitosis. Results in an increase or decrease in the number of chromosomes in the daughter cells.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

530iQf.title: Leukostasis
530iQf.description: Increased viscosity of blood caused by an excessive number of leukocytes (usually >100,000/μL). The very high number of immature leukocytes in patients with acute leukemia increases the risk of cerebral and pulmonary complications caused by vessel obstruction.

M30MQf.title: Pancreatogenic diabetes mellitus
M30MQf.description: A type of secondary diabetes mellitus that develops because of injury to the exocrine pancreatic tissue (e.g., chronic pancreatitis, pancreatic cancer, cystic fibrosis). Can develop after pancreatic surgery (e.g., partial or total pancreatectomy).

n307Qf.title: Myelophthisis
n307Qf.description: The replacement of hemopoietic bone marrow tissue by elements that do not form blood cells (e.g., fibrosis, tumor), which can result in severe anemia.

L30wQf.title: Defecography
L30wQf.description: A diagnostic test in which a contrast material (barium paste) is instilled into the rectum and a video recording is made of the anorectal region during the process of defecation using a fluoroscope. Defecography is used to analyze patients with anal sphincter dysfunction, fecal incontinence, and/or symptoms of pelvic floor weakness.

o300jf.title: Fallen fragment sign
o300jf.description: A radiological finding in which a bone fracture fragment appears within the cavity of a bone cyst, which is a characteristic sign of a simple (unicameral) bone cyst.

destinations.label: Benign bone tumors → Overview of benign bone tumors

K30Ujf.title: Soft tissue rheumatism
K30Ujf.description: A general term for painful, inflammatory disorders of the muscle, tendon, ligament, fascia, bursa, and subcutaneous tissues (e.g., fibromyalgia syndrome).

630jjf.title: Athetosis
630jjf.description: A symptom of involuntary writhing movements of the fingers, hand, toes, and/or extremities caused by damage to the thalamus, striatum of the basal ganglia, and/or regions within this network.

p30Ljf.title: Oneirism
p30Ljf.description: A condition characterized by visual hallucinations, typically experienced during a waking state, that are dreamlike and rich in detail. Associated with delirium tremens and narcolepsy.

J30sjf.title: Esophoria
J30sjf.description: A type of heterophoria in which one eye has a tendency to converge toward the nose when the other eye is shut; the opposite of exophoria.

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Basic terms

q30Cjf.title: Exophoria
q30Cjf.description: A type of heterophoria in which one eye has a tendency to deviate away from the nose when the other eye is shut; the opposite of esophoria.

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Basic terms

I30YPf.title: Exotropia
I30YPf.description: A type of manifest squint (heterotropia) in which the eye deviates away from the nose; the opposite of esotropia.

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Basic terms

r30fPf.title: Esotropia
r30fPf.description: Medial (inward) deviation of one or both eyes at primary gaze, usually due to CN VI damage. Can be congenital (e.g., accommodative esotropia) or acquired (e.g., diabetic CN VI palsy).

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Basic terms

s30tPf.title: Duane syndrome
s30tPf.description: A congenital, unilateral or bilateral, abduction paralysis of the eyeball. Retraction of the eyeball and narrowing of the palpebral fissure during adduction are characteristic features.

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Abducens nerve palsy (VI)

t30X4f.title: Base excess
t30X4f.description: Excess value of base in the blood. Used to identify whether an acid-base imbalance is predominantly a respiratory, metabolic, or a mixed acid-base disorder. The normal range is -2 to +3 mmol/L.

destinations.label: Arterial blood gas analysis → Arterial blood gas analysis

830O4f.title: Protease
830O4f.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the breakdown of proteins.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Digestion and absorption of dietary proteins

u30p4f.title: Dermographism
u30p4f.description: The formation of urticaria (wheals) after minor pressure is applied to the skin, likely mediated by local histamine release. Increased incidence may be observed during pregnancy (especially in the second half), at the onset of menopause, in atopic children, and in patients with Behçet disease.

E3084f.title: Monoamine oxidases
E3084f.description: A family of enzymes that break down the neurotransmitters noradrenaline, dopamine, and serotonin.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla

v30A4f.title: Plica syndrome
v30A4f.description: An inflammatory hypertrophy of the synovial plicae (synovial folds) in the knee joint. Patients present with patellar pain as well as clicking and/or locking of the knee joint.

D301kf.title: VEGF
D301kf.description: A signaling molecule that stimulates vasculogenesis (de novo formation of blood vessels) and angiogenesis (formation of blood vessels from preexisting vasculature).

w30hkf.title: Ectrodactyly
w30hkf.description: A typically bilateral, congenital deformity in which the middle finger and occasionally other digits are partially or completely missing.

930Nkf.title: Paroxysmal
930Nkf.description: A descriptor for a symptom, sign, or condition that has a sudden onset, recurs suddenly, and/or worsens suddenly, often without a clear inciting trigger. Examples include paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and paroxysmal pain (a feature of some pain with neuropathic etiology).

C30qkf.title: Cysticerci
C30qkf.description: The larval form of Taenia species, which can accumulate in body tissues after ingestion of Taenia eggs in contaminated food to cause cysticercosis.

x30Ekf.title: Chondromalacia
x30Ekf.description: A softening and breakdown of articular cartilage (e.g., from trauma, overuse, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis).

B30zkf.title: Ragocyte
B30zkf.description: A granulocyte with cytoplasmic inclusion bodies (phagolysosomes) that may be seen in the synovial fluid of patients with rheumatoid arthritis and/or systemic lupus erythematosus.

y30dOf.title: Splenorenal recess
y30dOf.description: A space between the left kidney and the spleen. A potential site of accumulation of intra-abdominal fluid in a recumbent patient and is, therefore, examined as a part of a FAST scan (focused assessment with sonography for trauma).

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

A30ROf.title: Morison pouch
A30ROf.description: A space between the right kidney and the right lobe of the liver. Morison's pouch is a potential site for the accumulation of intra-abdominal fluid in a recumbent patient and is therefore examined as part of a FAST scan (focused assessment with sonography for trauma).

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

z30rOf.title: Fencer attitude
z30rOf.description: A characteristic body posture in the fields of pediatrics that involves extension of the ipsilateral extremities and flexion of the contralateral extremities. Passively turning an infant's head to one side induces an asymmetrical tonic neck reflex, which causes the infant to assume a fencer's attitude.

-30DOf.title: Mastectomy
-30DOf.description: The surgical removal of varying amounts of breast tissue. Typically performed in breast cancer for tumor removal and occasionally for prophylaxis. Mastectomy is also a gender-affirming procedure.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Surgical resection of tumor and breast reconstruction

aR0Qlf.title: Drop attack
aR0Qlf.description: A sudden collapse without loss of consciousness. May occur in transient ischemic attacks or stroke, syncope, certain types of seizures (e.g., atonic seizures), and vestibular dysfunction (Tumarkin otolithic crisis).

XR09lf.title: Glabella
XR09lf.description: The region of the face above the root of the nose and between the eyebrows.

1R02Nf.title: Pleocytosis
1R02Nf.description: An increase in the number of cells in body fluids. Often used specifically to refer to an increased leukocyte count in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

VR0GNf.title: Hypertrichosis
VR0GNf.description: A condition of generalized or localized excessive hair growth that does not follow a pattern of male distribution (in contrast to hirsutism). Common causes of generalized hypertrichosis include hereditary or ethnic predisposition and certain medications (e.g., phenytoin, cyclosporine, glucocorticoids, minoxidil).

eR0xNf.title: Single photon emission computed tomography
eR0xNf.description: A diagnostic technique in nuclear medicine that is used to produce a three-dimensional image of a structure by analyzing gamma waves that are released from an injectable radionuclide tracer. SPECT has a lower resolution than positron emission tomography.

UR0bmf.title: Scurvy
UR0bmf.description: The clinical manifestation of vitamin C deficiency, which leads to abnormal collagen production. Symptoms include swollen gums, poor wound healing, mucosal bleeding, curly body hair, follicular hyperkeratosis, and generalized weakness/fatigue.

2R0Tmf.title: Saber shin
2R0Tmf.description: An anterior bowing of the tibia, causing it to resemble a saber. Common causes include rickets, congenital syphilis, and Paget disease of bone.

fR0kmf.title: Ankylosis
fR0kmf.description: A bony or fibrous fusion of the articular surfaces of a joint that results in joint immobility.

TR06mf.title: Sex hormone-binding globulin
TR06mf.description: A protein that binds to and transports androgens and estrogen. Determining the concentration of SHBG when measuring testosterone and/or estrogen helps determine the proportion of the hormone that is unbound and, therefore, biologically active. SHBG production in the liver is suppressed by androgen and insulin and stimulated by estrogen and hyperthyroidism.

gR0Fmf.title: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography
