Jo0s1S.description: The protrusion of the bladder, rectum, intestines, uterus, cervix, and/or vaginal apex into the vaginal vault due to decreased pelvic floor support. Risk factors include multiparity, older age, and obesity.

qo0C1S.title: Bacterial gastroenteritis
qo0C1S.description: An infection of the gastrointestinal tract by bacteria such as Campylobacter, Salmonella, Shigella, Yersinia, Vibrio cholerae, Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Clostridioides difficile, Clostridium perfringens, and non-cholera Vibrio species.

ro0fWS.title: Diarrhea
ro0fWS.description: A condition defined either as the presence of ≥ 3 bowel movements per day, water content exceeding 75%, or a stool quantity of at least 200–250 g per day. Acute diarrhea lasts for no longer than 14 days and is typically caused by viral or bacterial infection or food poisoning. Chronic diarrhea is often caused by underlying gastrointestinal or endocrinologic conditions.

Ho0KWS.title: Autoimmune hepatitis
Ho0KWS.description: Rare form of chronic hepatitis which predominantly affects women. It is commonly associated with other autoimmune conditions such as diabetes mellitus type 1 and celiac disease.

media.title: Overview of PSC, PBC, and autoimmune hepatitis

so0tWS.title: Immunosuppressants
so0tWS.description: A broad group of drugs that suppress the immune response. Used to treat various conditions (e.g., autoimmune and inflammatory disorders) and help prevent organ transplant rejection. Examples include glucocorticoids, alkylating agents, antimetabolites, and biologics. Adverse effects include an increased risk of infection and malignancy.

Go0BWS.title: Sexually transmitted infections
Go0BWS.description: A group of infections that are primarily transmitted via sexual intercourse. Often (initially) asymptomatic, and therefore easily spread. If symptoms are present, they commonly include pain in the suprapubic and genital area, urethral or vaginal discharge, and genital lesions, which may or may not be painful.

media.title: Chancre of the glans penis in primary syphilis

uo0pdS.title: Atelectasis
uo0pdS.description: A loss of lung volume caused by deflation of alveoli and subsequent collapse of part of the lung. May be categorized according to etiology as obstructive (e.g., tumor), nonobstructive (e.g., pleural effusion, pneumothorax, and surfactant deficiency), postoperative (within 72 hours of surgery), or rounded (e.g., asbestosis).

Eo08dS.title: Peritonitis
Eo08dS.description: Inflammation of the peritoneum (the inner lining of the abdominal wall that also covers most internal organs), usually of infectious origin.

xo0EVS.title: Spasticity
xo0EVS.description: A physical finding of increased, involuntary, velocity-dependent muscle tone, which causes stiffness, and/or tightness of the muscles and manifests as resistance to movement. Occurs following damage to the primary motor cortex or the corticospinal tract (e.g., stroke, neurodegenerative disease, cerebral palsy).

yo0deS.title: Electroconvulsive therapy
yo0deS.description: A procedure in which electric currents are applied externally to the skull to initiate a seizure under anesthesia. This procedure can be used as first-line treatment for psychotic depression, severe depression associated with suicidality or refusal of food, and catatonia.

Ao0ReS.title: Obstipation
Ao0ReS.description: A complete inability to pass stool or gas, usually secondary to bowel obstruction. Other causes include severe hypothyroidism, diabetes, fecal impaction, or volvulus.

1K022S.title: Transplantation
1K022S.description: The process of transferring an organ or a tissue graft. This may be an autologous transplantation, in which the graft originates from the patient him/herself, allogenous transplantation, in which the graft originates from a genetically different person, or xenotransplanation, in which the graft originates from another species.

dK0o2S.title: Palliative care
dK0o2S.description: An approach to managing the care of patients with serious or life-threatening conditions. Focuses on alleviating symptoms and improving quality of life, with or without simultaneous life-prolonging therapy.

eK0x2S.title: X-ray
eK0x2S.description: An imaging modality that uses x-rays, i.e. electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength of 0.01–10 nm, to create two-dimensional images of internal body structures. Depending on their density and composition, different types of tissue absorb different amounts of radiation. To create an image, a generator projects x-rays at the structure to be visualized and a detector captures the radiation that passes through the body, either digitally or on photographic film.

fK0kfS.title: Ultrasound
fK0kfS.description: A noninvasive imaging method that uses high-frequency sound waves to create images of internal organs and structures based on the density of tissues.

6K0jhS.title: Tinnitus
6K0jhS.description: A symptom characterized by hearing sound (e.g., whistling, hissing, buzzing, ringing, pulsating) in the absence of an external source. Can be unilateral or bilateral, acute or chronic, and intermittent or constant. Commonly associated with hearing loss.

GK0B3S.title: Viral hemorrhagic fever
GK0B3S.description: A potentially life-threatening syndrome involving severe multiorgan failure, usually accompanied by hemorrhage. It is caused by the Ebola, Marburg, Lassa, dengue and yellow fever viruses.

tK0XRS.title: Headache
tK0XRS.description: Pain related to irritation and/or inflammation of intracranial or extracranial structures with pain receptors (e.g., meninges, cranial nerves, blood vessels). Further subdivided into primary headache (e.g., tension-type headaches, migraine) and secondary headache (e.g., following head trauma or infection).

media.title: Differential diagnoses of primary headaches fact sheet

c60aPS.title: Pontiac fever
c60aPS.description: A mild, self-limiting disease caused by Legionella infection. Symptoms are difficult to distinguish from the flu and include fever, headache, and muscle aches. Pneumonia is absent.

1602PS.title: Legionnaires' disease
1602PS.description: A type of pneumonia caused by Legionella spp. (most commonly Legionella pneumophila in the US). In addition to symptoms of atypical pneumonia, patients may develop diarrhea, neurologic manifestations (e.g., confusion, agitation), and hyponatremia.

W60PPS.title: Opisthotonus
W60PPS.description: A spastic contracture of the axial muscles along the spinal column, which causes the head and lower limbs to hyperextend backward and the trunk to arch forward. Classically associated with tetanus.

d60oPS.title: Risus sardonicus
d60oPS.description: An abnormal facial expression of raised eyebrows and grinning distortion of the face caused by sustained spasm of the facial muscles. Characteristically associated with tetanus.

V60GPS.title: Trismus
V60GPS.description: A limited ability to open the jaw due to tonic spasms of the jaw musculature. Most commonly associated with tetanus. Can also arise secondary to peritonsillar abscess, infection in the jaw muscles, and trigeminal nerve pathology.

U60b4S.title: Tetanus vaccination
U60b4S.description: A vaccine that consists of denatured tetanus toxin. Typically given as 5 doses of DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, and acellular pertussis) before 7 years of age, followed by boosters of Tdap (tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis) at 11-12 years of age and 19-64 years of age and Td (tetanus, diphtheria) every 10 years in adulthood.

260T4S.title: Tetanus prophylaxis
260T4S.description: Administration of active and/or passive tetanus immunization during acute wound management, depending on patient immunization status and the extent and cleanliness of the wound. Wounds with an increased risk of tetanus include bite and puncture wounds, injuries contaminated with dirt or feces, burns, and frostbite.

f60k4S.title: Rose-colored spots
f60k4S.description: A description for the characteristic erythematous papules that can develop on the trunk of individuals with typhoid fever or paratyphoid fever.

destinations.label: Typhoid and paratyphoid fever → Clinical features

g60F4S.title: Erythema migrans
g60F4S.description: A rash characterized by a circular, slowly-expanding red ring with central clearing. Pathognomonic of early Lyme disease and appears around the site of the tick bite.

360SkS.title: Early neuroborreliosis
360SkS.description: A manifestation of disseminated Lyme disease that can affect the peripheral and/or central nervous system. Manifests within the first few months of infection. May include Bell's palsy, meningitis, polyneuropathy, and/or encephalomyelitis.

Q60ukS.title: Borrelial lymphocytoma
Q60ukS.description: A rare, cutaneous manifestation of European Lyme disease characterized by a bluish-red nodular swelling typically located on the earlobe or near the nipple. Often occurs near a previous or concurrent lesion of erythema migrans.

j60_kS.title: Late neuroborreliosis
j60_kS.description: A manifestation of disseminated Lyme disease that can affect the peripheral and/or central nervous system. Can include Bell palsy, meningitis, polyneuropathy, and/or encephalomyelitis. Occurs months to years after infection.

P60WOS.title: Lyme arthritis
P60WOS.description: A manifestation of late Lyme disease that typically affects large joints (e.g., knees, elbows). Can manifest as intermittent or persistent monoarthritis or oligoarthritis.

4603OS.title: Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans
4603OS.description: A late cutaneous manifestation of European and Asian Lyme disease caused by infection with Borrelia afzelii. Characterized by chronic progressive atrophic dermatitis affecting the extensor surfaces of the extremities.

k60mOS.title: Post‑treatment Lyme disease syndrome
k60mOS.description: A controversial syndrome (the medical community does not agree on its existence) characterized by fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and other nonspecific symptoms that can last up to 6 months after successful treatment of Lyme disease.

l60vOS.title: Cutaneous anthrax
l60vOS.description: A condition caused by Bacillus anthracis infection. Characterized by the formation of a painless papule surrounded by vesicles that progresses into a painless, necrotic ulcer with black eschar. Can progress to bacteremia and death.

N60-OS.title: Inhalation anthrax
N60-OS.description: An acute, often fatal illness caused by inhalation of Bacillus anthracis spores. After an incubation period of typically < 3 days, the disease manifests with fever, myalgia, and cough that can rapidly progress to acute respiratory distress, hemorrhagic mediastinitis, and shock.

m60VlS.title: Intestinal anthrax
m60VlS.description: A potentially fatal illness caused by ingestion of Bacillus anthracis spores from undercooked meat. After an incubation period of 2-5 days, the disease manifests with abdominal pain, hematemesis, and severe bloody diarrhea. May lead to hemorrhagic lymphadenitis and ascites.

q60CNS.title: HIV testing
q60CNS.description: A group of tests indicated in all patients with clinical features of acute or chronic HIV infection and possible past exposure. Also recommended early in every pregnancy. Screening tests can detect both HIV antigen (p24) and anti-HIV antibodies. Confirmatory tests include HIV-1/HIV-2 antibody differentiation and Western blot. Additional laboratory studies include flow cytometry for CD4 count and PCR for viral load.

7604mS.title: Combined antiretroviral therapy
7604mS.description: A medication regimen that targets retroviruses. Primarily refers to therapy for HIV infection (e.g., NRTIs that can be combined with either a non-nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitor, protease inhibitor, or integrase inhibitor).

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

H60KmS.title: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors
H60KmS.description: A group of drugs comprised of nucleoside analogs (pentose sugar + nitrogenous base) that inhibit reverse transcription of RNA to DNA. Used for the treatment of HIV (e.g., zidovudine, lamivudine, emtricitabine, abacavir) and hepatitis B (e.g., entecavir).

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

G60BmS.title: HIV-associated lipodystrophy
G60BmS.description: A Cushing-like syndrome (disproportionate fat deposition, dorsocervical fat lump “Buffalo hump,” peripheral wasting, breast enlargement, dyslipidemia) that can develop after use of certain HIV antiretroviral drugs (i.e., zidovudine, stavudine, protease inhibitors) or as a result of the HIV infection itself.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

F60g5S.title: Nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors
F60g5S.description: A class of antiretroviral drugs used as part of a multi-drug regimen for the treatment of HIV (e.g., efavirenz, nevirapine). They are non-competitive inhibitors of viral reverse transcriptase. Adverse effects include hypersensitivity reactions, hepatotoxicity (nevirapine), and CNS toxicity (efavirenz).

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

u60p5S.title: Protease inhibitors
u60p5S.description:
1. A class of antiretroviral drugs that inhibit viral protease. Used to treat HIV infection.
2. A group of proteins that antagonize the activity of various serine proteases.

E6085S.title: Integrase inhibitors
E6085S.description: A drug that reversibly inhibits HIV integrase, which prevents the HIV genome from integrating into host DNA. Generally well-tolerated, but adverse effects insomnia, dizziness, and increases in serum creatine kinase. Examples include dolutegravir, elvitegravir, and raltegravir.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

w60hMS.title: AIDS
w60hMS.description: The advanced disease stage of an HIV infection characterized by a CD4+ T cell count <200/μL or the presence of AIDS-defining illnesses (e.g., esophageal or bronchial candidiasis, pneumocystis pneumonia, wasting syndrome, Kaposi's sarcoma).

960NMS.title: Cachexia
960NMS.description: A form of secondary protein-energy malnutrition caused by chronic conditions associated with inflammation (e.g., chronic infections, cancer, chronic kidney disease). Characterized by weight loss of > 5% within 12 months. Pathophysiology is complex and involves cytokine-mediated increased muscle catabolism and reduced protein synthesis.

destinations.label: Unintentional weight loss and malnutrition in adults → Etiology

C60qMS.title: Toxoplasmic encephalitis
C60qMS.description: An infection of the brain caused by reactivation of Toxoplasma gondii in immunocompromised individuals. The most common neurological AIDS-defining illness.

z60rnS.title: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
z60rnS.description: A fatal disease characterized by multifocal demyelination in the brain. Caused by reactivation of a latent JC virus in patients who are immunosuppressed (e.g., due to AIDS, hematologic malignancies, posttransplant).

Zp0ZLS.title: Kaposi sarcoma
Zp0ZLS.description: An endothelial soft tissue cancer that is caused by human herpesvirus 8 and typically affects individuals with HIV infection. Most commonly develops in the skin but can also occur in other areas (e.g., lymph nodes, lungs, or gastrointestinal tract). The lesions are characteristically painless plaques and/or nodules with variable discoloration (e.g., brown or blue-violet).

media.title: HIV patient with Kaposi sarcoma and candidiasis

ap0QLS.title: Owl-eye appearance
ap0QLS.description: A description of microscopic intranuclear inclusions of cells in CMV infection or Reed-Sternberg cells in Hodgkin lymphoma.

Xp09LS.title: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
Xp09LS.description: A life-threatening syndrome of immune activation that results in widespread inflammation and tissue destruction. Manifestations include fever, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and neurologic dysfunction (e.g., altered mental status, seizures). Can occur either as primary syndrome due to genetic mutation with onset in infancy or as secondary syndrome (e.g., after infection or malignancy).

dp0ooS.title: Tertian malaria
dp0ooS.description: A form of malaria caused by the protozoa Plasmodium vivax or P. ovale that are transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito, which is endemic in many tropical and subtropical regions. Characterized by febrile paroxysms that occur every 48 hours due to the release of merozoites and their invasion of new red blood cells. More benign than falciparum malaria, but relapses are common. Treated with chloroquine.

Vp0GoS.title: Falciparum malaria
Vp0GoS.description: The most severe type of malaria, which is caused by the parasite Plasmodium falciparum that is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito and endemic in many tropical and subtropical regions. Falciparum malaria is associated with high parasitemia and a high risk of complications and death. P. falciparum invades and destroys RBCs, which leads to microinfarctions in the CNS, liver, adrenal gland, and other organs.

ep0xoS.title: Severe malaria
ep0xoS.description: A potentially fatal subset of malaria characterized by the presence of any vital organ dysfunction, e.g., impaired consciousness, severe anemia, acute kidney injury, ARDS, DIC, and/or metabolic acidosis.

ip0J6S.title: Atovaquone-proguanil
ip0J6S.description: An antimalarial drug used for the treatment of chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum infection and for malaria prophylaxis. Can cause gastrointestinal discomfort.

Pp0WpS.title: Primaquine
Pp0WpS.description: An antimalarial that is also used to treat Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Can cause hemolysis in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency.

lp0vpS.title: Mefloquine
lp0vpS.description: An antimalarial drug used for both prophylaxis and treatment of malaria. Adverse effects include dizziness, fatigue, and gastrointestinal discomfort.

np07JS.title: Giardiasis
np07JS.description: A protozoan infection caused by Giardia duodenalis (formerly Giardia lamblia), which is usually transmitted through contaminated water. Most common in the tropics, subtropics, and North American mountain regions and typically manifests with foul-smelling, fatty diarrhea.

Lp0wJS.title: Ocular toxoplasmosis
Lp0wJS.description: A condition of retinal and choroid inflammation caused by infection with Toxoplasmosis. Manifests with yellow-white lesions, marked vitreous reaction, concomitant vasculitis, and visual field defects. Forms white, atrophic scars with surrounding hyperpigmentation. Recurrent infection can develop at old scar sites.

6p0jqS.title: Cutaneous leishmaniasis
6p0jqS.description: A form of leishmaniasis characterized by reddish, often granulomatous macules and papules that progress to ulcerations. It typically resolves without intervention and is the most common form of leishmaniasis among immunocompetent individuals.

qp0CqS.title: Mucosal leishmaniasis
qp0CqS.description: A form of leishmaniasis characterized by the destruction of the nasal and nasopharyngeal mucosae. Typically caused by Leishmania species that are endemic to South America (e.g., L. braziliensis, L. guyanensis, L. panamensis).

Ip0YIS.title: Visceral leishmaniasis
Ip0YIS.description: A disseminated form of leishmaniasis, typically caused by L. donovani or L. infantum. Manifestations include insidious onset fever, weight loss, lymphadenopathy, and hepatosplenomegaly.

7p04IS.title: Kala-azar
7p04IS.description: A severe form of visceral leishmaniasis. From the Hindi term for "black fever," describing the darkening of the skin (especially of the palms and soles) that is sometimes observed among affected patients in south Asia.

sp0tIS.title: Candida esophagitis
sp0tIS.description: An opportunistic infection of the esophagus caused by Candida albicans infection. Most commonly occurs in patients who are immunocompromised or using inhaled steroids. Can develop concomitantly with oral thrush and odynophagia. Endoscopy shows white mucosal plaques.

tp0XrS.title: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis
tp0XrS.description: A respiratory hypersensitivity reaction caused by exposure to Aspergillus fumigatus antigens. Manifestations include asthmatic symptoms and sinusitis. Most commonly seen in patients with preexisting lung disease. Primarily treated with systemic glucocorticoids and antifungals.

8p0OrS.title: Aspergilloma
8p0OrS.description: An Aspergillus fungus ball in a preexisting pulmonary cavitary lesion (e.g., from tuberculosis).

media.title: Aspergilloma (fungus ball) within right upper lobe cavity

up0prS.title: Invasive aspergillosis
up0prS.description: A severe infection caused by the fungus Aspergillus. Immunocompromised patients are at risk of invasive aspergillosis, which manifests as severe pneumonia and septicemia with potential involvement of other organs (e.g., in skeletal, cutaneous, or neurological tissue).

xp0E7S.title: Rotavirus infection
xp0E7S.description: An acute viral gastroenteritis that is transmitted via the fecal-oral route and occurs most commonly in infants and young children. After an incubation period of 1-3 days, patients typically present with vomiting, watery diarrhea, fever, and malaise. Symptoms usually resolve within 1 week. Universal rotavirus vaccination of infants is recommended to prevent infection.

yp0dHS.title: Cercarial dermatitis
yp0dHS.description: An acute, cutaneous hypersensitivity reaction to infection with schistosome cercariae, usually from contaminated fresh water. Typically manifests as a pruritic, maculopapular rash within 24 hours.

ZJ0ZsS.title: Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis
ZJ0ZsS.description: A form of chronic schistosomiasis characterized by chronic granulomatous inflammation in response to the deposition of Schistosoma eggs around the liver and/or spleen. Can cause periportal fibrosis resulting in hepatosplenomegaly and ascites (if portal hypertension develops) and sometimes portosystemic shunting that can lead to or exacerbate pulmonary involvement. Often associated with intestinal schistosomiasis.

bJ0HsS.title: Neuroschistosomiasis
bJ0HsS.description: A form of chronic schistosomiasis characterized by chronic granulomatous inflammation in response to the deposition of Schistosoma eggs in the central nervous system. Manifestations include headache, encephalopathy, sensory and motor deficits, myelopathy, and seizures.

XJ09sS.title: Rheumatoid nodules
XJ09sS.description: Nontender, firm, subcutaneous lumps often seen in rheumatoid arthritis. Primarily found in areas exposed to higher pressure such as the extensor side of the forearm (in about 25% of patients) or other bony prominences.

1J02GS.title: Felty's syndrome
1J02GS.description: A rare subtype of rheumatoid arthritis (< 1% of cases) characterized by arthritis, splenomegaly, and neutropenia. Usually occurs in the late stage of severe rheumatoid arthritis. The exact pathophysiology is not understood.

WJ0PGS.title: Adult-onset Still disease
WJ0PGS.description: A rare condition characterized by intermittent fever, salmon-pink rash, arthralgia, and/or arthritis. Adult-onset Still disease and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis are increasingly viewed as the same condition with different ages of onset. Serious complications include macrophage activation syndrome and associated interstitial lung disease.

VJ0GGS.title: Compression test
VJ0GGS.description: A test used to assess for rheumatoid arthritis. Considered positive if pain is elicited upon compression of the metacarpophalangeal or metatarsophalangeal joints

eJ0xGS.title: Anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies
eJ0xGS.description: A set of autoantibodies against citrullinated peptides. Peptide citrullination is increased in patients with inflammatory conditions. While ACPAs can be present in other diseases, they are highly specific for and enable early diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis, especially in patients who are negative for rheumatoid factor.

TJ06tS.title: Rheumatoid factor
TJ06tS.description: A group of autoantibodies (mostly IgM) that bind to the Fc region of IgG antibodies. RF is characteristically elevated in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, however, it is nonspecific. RF elevations can be found in other autoimmune (e.g., Sjögren disease, SLE) and infectious diseases (e.g., HCV infection). It may also be physiologically elevated in older patients.

hJ0cFS.title: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs
hJ0cFS.description: A group of unrelated medications with immunosuppressive and antiinflammatory properties that improve symptoms and prevent further disease progression. They are commonly used to treat rheumatoid arthritis, but may also be indicated in other diseases (e.g., malignancies, psoriatic arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus). DMARDs can be classed as either synthetic agents, which are further divided into conventional (e.g., methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, cyclophosphamide) and targeted DMARDs (e.g., JAK inhibitors), or biologic agents (e.g., TNF inhibitors, anti-CD20).

iJ0JFS.title: Swan neck deformity
iJ0JFS.description: A finger deformity caused by hyperextension of the proximal interphalangeal joint and flexion of the distal interphalangeal joint. Commonly seen in patients with rheumatoid arthritis that affects the fingers. Can also occur after flexor digitorum superficialis laceration or surgical repair of finger flexor tendon injuries (tight repair of the flexor digitorum profundus).

QJ0uFS.title: Boutonniere deformity
QJ0uFS.description: Finger deformity caused by hyperextension of the distal interphalangeal joint with flexion of the proximal interphalangeal joint due to slipping or disruption of the central band of the extensor digitorum (ED) tendon. Can be caused by sharp or blunt trauma (e.g., jamming a finger in a door) or by rheumatoid arthritis (inflammation of the joint space pushes the central band of the ED out of its normal anatomical position).

jJ0_FS.title: Hitchhiker thumb deformity
jJ0_FS.description: A thumb deformity seen in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. Characterized by flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint and extension of the distal interphalangeal joint.

PJ0W8S.title: Mennell sign
PJ0W8S.description: A physical examination technique that is used to evaluate for inflammation and/or degeneration in the sacroiliac joints. Pain in the sacroiliac joint elicited on passive extension of the hip with the patient in prone or lateral position is suggestive of sacroiliitis.

kJ0m8S.title: Schober's test
kJ0m8S.description: A technique to assess spine mobility. With the patient standing, the examiner marks two points on the back at L5 and 10 cm above L5. The patient touches their toes without bending their knees. An increase in the distance between the points < 4 cm suggests impaired spine mobility.

nJ07uS.title: Syndesmophytes
nJ07uS.description: A collection of bony growths or calcifications that can form in the annulus fibrosus or the spinal ligament. Etiologies include ankylosing spondylitis, reactive arthritis, and psoriatic arthritis.

pJ0LES.title: Acute gouty arthritis
pJ0LES.description: An inflammatory arthropathy caused by urate crystal deposition within a joint. Typically manifests with a severely painful and swollen joint, and peripheral small joints in the lower extremities are especially affected. Synovial fluid analysis shows needle-shaped, negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals.

qJ0CES.title: Podagra
qJ0CES.description: A condition characterized by pain and swelling of the first metatarsal-phalangeal joint of the foot. Usually caused by deposition of uric acid crystals in the setting of hyperuricemia (gout).

7J04vS.title: Chronic gouty arthritis
7J04vS.description: A condition characterized by progressive joint degeneration due to recurring gout attacks and deposition of urate crystals next to joints. Typically develops several years after the onset of disease in patients with undertreated gout. Can cause formation of tophi and renal manifestations such as uric acid nephrolithiasis and uric acid nephropathy.

media.title: Gouty tophi due to urate crystal deposition in bones and soft tissues

sJ0tvS.title: Soft tissue tophi
sJ0tvS.description: A characteristic feature of chronic gout caused by deposition of urate crystals in cartilage, tendon sheaths, and soft tissue (subcutis), particularly surrounding joints. Manifests as hard, painless nodules that may appear yellow and chalky if close to the surface of the skin, especially on toes and fingers and possibly also larger joints (e.g., elbows). Can cause joint destruction. Requires several years of inadequately treated gout to develop and rarely seen nowadays.

GJ0BvS.title: Bone tophi
GJ0BvS.description: A characteristic feature of chronic gout caused by deposition of urate crystals in bones, particularly the hallux, elbows, knees, and extensor surfaces of the forearms. Manifests as hard, painless nodules that may appear yellow and chalky if close to the surface and can lead to bone erosion and joint destruction. Tophi develop over several years of inadequately treated gout and are rarely seen nowadays.

tJ0XDS.title: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease
tJ0XDS.description:
A form of inflammatory arthritis in which calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystals deposit in hyaline or fibrocartilage. The acute form (often called "pseudogout") is characterized by episodic acute attacks of synovitis in a large joint. Several chronic forms also exist, the most common of which presents similarly to severe osteoarthritis.
Synovial fluid analysis yields rhomboid-shaped, positively birefringent crystals.

8J0ODS.title: Colchicine
8J0ODS.description: An anti-inflammatory agent that inhibits microtubule polymerization. Primarily used in the treatment of acute gouty arthritis.

destinations.label: Gout and hyperuricemia → Acute gout flare

uJ0pDS.title: Allopurinol
uJ0pDS.description: A xanthine oxidase inhibitor that prevents conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine into uric acid. Standard medication for chronic gout and/or hyperuricemia.

EJ08DS.title: Uricosuric medications
EJ08DS.description: A group of drugs that inhibits uric acid reabsorption along the renal tubules, which increases renal elimination of uric acid. Used as an alternative to or in combination with allopurinol for the treatment of chronic gout. Examples include benzbromarone, probenecid, and lesinurad.

DJ01wS.title: Probenecid
DJ01wS.description: A drug that inhibits reabsorption of uric acid along the renal tubules, which leads to increased elimination of uric acid. Used to treat chronic gout.

wJ0hwS.title: Rasburicase
wJ0hwS.description: A recombinant uricase that catalyzes the conversion of uric acid to water-soluble allantoin. Used to prevent and treat tumor lysis syndrome. Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency.

9J0NwS.title: Uric acid nephropathy
9J0NwS.description: A condition of renal dysfunction caused by hyperuricemia, which leads to monosodium urate crystal deposition in the stroma of the kidney and subsequent inflammation. Can cause hypertension or progress to chronic renal failure.

xJ0EwS.title: Acute uric acid nephropathy
xJ0EwS.description: A condition of acute kidney failure due to precipitation of uric acid in the renal tubules secondary to acute hyperuricemia (e.g., tumor lysis syndrome). Manifests as anuric/oliguric renal failure.

-J0D9S.title: Rhizarthrosis
-J0D9S.description: A degenerative joint disease caused by overuse and instability of the first carpometacarpal joint.

bq0HCS.title: Radiological signs of osteoarthritis
bq0HCS.description: The signs include irregular joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, osteophytes, and subchondral cysts.

Wq0PxS.title: Subchondral sclerosis
Wq0PxS.description: A dense area of bone just below the cartilage zone of a joint. Typically formed in response to a compressive load on the joint. Can be visualized on x-ray.

media.title: Advanced degenerative arthritis of the great toe metatarsophalangeal joint (2/2)

dq0oxS.title: Osteophyte
dq0oxS.description: A bony outgrowth that can occur in inflamed or degenerating joints (e.g., from osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, joint ligament injury, ankylosing spondylitis). Can be asymptomatic or cause pain, joint deformity, tendinitis, restriction of joint movement, or compression of adjacent nerves. Visible on imaging as bony projections or spurs along the joint line.

media.title: Advanced degenerative arthritis of the great toe metatarsophalangeal joint (2/2)

Vq0GxS.title: Subchondral cyst
Vq0GxS.description: A fluid-filled cyst that develops at the surface of a joint due to local bone necrosis induced by joint stress. It is a sign of osteoarthritis.

media.title: Illustration of right hip radiograph in osteoarthritis

Uq0bBS.title: Harrison's groove
Uq0bBS.description: A groove that extends symmetrically along the subcostal margins, where the diaphragm attaches to the ribs. Occurs in infants or children with weak bones (e.g., rickets) due to the diaphragmatic pull on the weakened ribs, or those with chronic respiratory disease (e.g., childhood asthma) due to the excessive diaphragmatic pull on normal ribs.

2q0TBS.title: Craniotabes
2q0TBS.description: A softening of the skull bones. Typically seen in children with rickets. Considered normal in infants up to 6 months of age.

fq0kBS.title: Marfan sign
fq0kBS.description: Distention of the epiphyseal plate of the distal tibia with widening and cupping of the metaphysis gives the impression of a double medial malleolus on inspection and palpation of the ankle.

Tq06BS.title: Rachitic rosary
Tq06BS.description: A radiologic sign characterized by distension of the bone-cartilage junctions of the ribs. Classically seen in children with rickets.

gq0FBS.title: Looser's zones
gq0FBS.description: 0.1- to 1-cm wide, radiolucent lesions that are perpendicular to the bone cortex and often surrounded by a thin, irregular, sclerotic margin. Typically seen with osteomalacia or rickets, and caused by erosion of the softened bone cortex by blood vessels overlying the bone. A callus develops at the site of blood vessel infraction but fails to mineralize completely. Looser zones occur symmetrically. Most common sites are the ribs, radius, ulna, axillary border of the scapula, pubic rami, ilium, and medial border of the femoral neck.

hq0cyS.title: Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia
hq0cyS.description: A congenital condition usually associated with neurofibromatosis type I. Characterized by unilateral anterolateral bowing of the lower third of the tibia and, in some cases, the fibula.

iq0JyS.title: Osteopenia
iq0JyS.description: A reduction of bone mineral density with a T-score of -1 to -2.5. Etiologies include lack of estrogen or testosterone, lack of exercise, alcohol and cigarette consumption, and use of glucocorticoids. Can develop into osteoporosis.

Qq0uyS.title: T-score
Qq0uyS.description: The difference in standard deviations between a patient's bone mineral density (BMD) and the BMD of a young adult female reference mean. A T-score ≤ -2.5 SD indicates osteoporosis. A T-score of -1 to -2.5 SD indicates osteopenia.

Oq0IAS.title: Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry
Oq0IAS.description: A noninvasive technique that measures bone mineral density and body tissue composition using two x-ray beams with different energy levels. Uses include osteoporosis screening (commonly measured in lumbar spine and hips) and assessment for sarcopenia. Recommended every 10 years for postmenopausal women > 65 years of age and younger postmenopausal women with a pathological fracture or risk factors for osteoporosis (e.g., family history).

nq07_S.title: Raloxifene
nq07_S.description: A selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that acts as an estrogen antagonist on receptors in breast and endometrium (prevents growth stimulation of estrogen-receptor positive cells) and as an agonist on receptors in bone (inhibits bone resorption). Indicated in the treatment of osteoporosis in patients with contraindications to bisphosphonates or postmenopausal women who also benefit from breast cancer prophylaxis. The most severe adverse effect is an increased risk of thromboembolism.

Lq0w_S.title: Teriparatide
Lq0w_S.description: A recombinant parathyroid hormone analogue that increases bone growth by upregulating osteoblastic activity. Can be used in the treatment of severe osteoporosis (T-score ≤ -3.5) and in patients with contraindications to bisphosphonates.

oq00zS.title: Denosumab
oq00zS.description: A monoclonal antibody against the RANK ligand. Used to treat osteoporosis and hypercalcemia of malignancy that is refractory to bisphosphonates. Also used as a systemic therapy to treat certain bone tumors (e.g., bone metastases, osteoclastoma).

Kq0UzS.title: Jaw claudication
Kq0UzS.description: A symptom of jaw pain that occurs with chewing. Classically associated with giant cell arteritis.

6q0jzS.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus
6q0jzS.description: A multisystem autoimmune disease that particularly affects women of childbearing age and leads to chronic inflammatory reactions in a variety of organs, including the skin, kidney, and joints. Typical findings include fever and fatigue, a malar rash (facial "butterfly rash"), myalgia, and arthritis.

Iq0Y-S.title: Discoid lupus erythematosus
Iq0Y-S.description: A chronic autoimmune skin condition characterized by erythematous scaly plaques that often result in inflammation, scarring, and atrophy on the face, ears, and scalp. Serologic abnormalities are uncommon. It may occur with or without concurrent systemic lupus erythematosus.

destinations.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus → Specific clinical manifestations

sq0t-S.title: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
sq0t-S.description: An uncommon subtype of cutaneous lupus erythematosus characterized by extreme photosensitivity and annular plaques or psoriasiform lesions that heal without scarring. May be associated with systemic lupus erythematosus.

destinations.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus → Specific clinical manifestations

tq0XZh.title: Drug-induced lupus erythematosus
tq0XZh.description: A syndrome with SLE-like symptoms (e.g., fever, malaise, myalgia, arthralgia, and/or a photodistributed rash) seen during therapy with certain medications (e.g., isoniazid, hydralazine, procainamide). Patients are typically ANA positive, anti-histone antibody positive, and anti-dsDNA negative.

8q0OZh.title: Anti-histone antibodies
8q0OZh.description: A group of autoantibodies and subset of anti-nuclear antibodies that are seen in 70% of patients with SLE and over 95% of patients with drug-induced lupus.

uq0pZh.title: Anti-dsDNA antibody
uq0pZh.description: An autoantibody against double-stranded DNA (dsDNA). Highly specific for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); found in 70% of patients with SLE. Levels of anti-dsDNA antibodies correlate with disease activity and are associated with lupus nephritis.

Dq010h.title: Anti-Sm antibody
Dq010h.description: An autoantibody against Smith antigens (nonhistone nuclear proteins) which are highly specific (but only 30% sensitive) for systemic lupus erythematosus.

Bq0z0h.title: Lupus nephritis
Bq0z0h.description: A condition of renal involvement of systemic lupus erythematosus. Typically caused by autoantibodies against renal nuclear antigens, immune complex deposition within the glomeruli, and intrarenal complement activation. Has several forms, including focal and diffuse types. Can manifest with nephrotic syndrome or nephritic syndrome.

destinations.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus → Specific clinical manifestations

ZI0ZYh.title: Gottron papules
ZI0ZYh.description: Erythematous papules on the extensor surfaces of the hands, typically over the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and interphalangeal joints. A characteristic dermatological finding in dermatomyositis.

aI0QYh.title: Limited systemic sclerosis
aI0QYh.description: A subtype of systemic sclerosis characterized by cutaneous sclerosis of the neck, face, and distal limbs with sparing of the trunk. Typically preceded by Raynaud phenomenon. Associated with anticentromere autoantibodies, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and severe gastrointestinal involvement.

YI0nYh.title: Sclerodactyly
YI0nYh.description: A tightening of the skin over the fingers that manifests in red-blue discoloration of the skin, edema, fibrosis with a waxy appearance, and limited range of motion. Associated with systemic sclerosis.

media.title: Digital pitting scars in systemic sclerosis

bI0HYh.title: Diffuse systemic sclerosis
bI0HYh.description: A subtype of systemic sclerosis characterized by skin sclerosis of proximal limbs and trunk. Associated with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) autoantibodies, interstitial lung disease, cardiac involvement, and scleroderma renal crisis.

XI09Yh.title: CREST syndrome
XI09Yh.description: A constellation of cutaneous and extracutaneous features that are commonly observed in patients with limited systemic sclerosis (SSc). CREST stands for Calcinosis cutis, Raynaud phenomenon, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, and Telangiectasia. The term is outdated since these findings can also manifest in diffuse SSc.

WI0Pbh.title: Morphea
WI0Pbh.description: A rare, idiopathic inflammatory skin condition that causes localized, painless, discolored patches that can evolve into firm plaques.

2I0TXh.title: Ringed sideroblast
2I0TXh.description: An immature red blood cell in which abnormal mitochondrial iron deposition forms a ring around the nucleus. Seen in bone marrow of patients with heme synthesis disorders (e.g., from myelodysplastic syndromes, alcohol use, lead poisoning, sideroblastic anemia).

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

TI06Xh.title: Leukemic meningitis
TI06Xh.description: The infiltration of leukemic cells into the central nervous system, predominantly in the meninges. It can also occur in the subarachnoid space and perivascular tissue. Leukemic meningitis is most commonly seen in childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

SI0yXh.title: Auer rods
SI0yXh.description: The cytoplasmic inclusions of eosinophilic rods and granules that can be seen in immature myeloid cells (e.g., myeloblasts or promyelocytes) on a peripheral blood smear. Their presence most often suggests acute myelogenous leukemia, but they can also be seen in individuals with chronic myelomonocytic leukemia and myelodysplastic syndrome.

media.title: Auer rods in acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL)

hI0cch.title: Tumor lysis syndrome
hI0cch.description: A constellation of electrolyte disturbances that can occur as a result of cancer treatment. Widespread lysis of tumor cells can release significant quantities of potassium, phosphate, uric acid, and lactate dehydrogenase. Clinical features are variable, although acute kidney injury and cardiac arrhythmias are two of the most common and concerning manifestations.

PI0W1h.title: Smudge cells
PI0W1h.description: A finding on peripheral blood smear characterized by the remnants of abnormally fragile lymphocytes that have ruptured. Although not exclusive to chronic lymphocytic leukemia, smudge cells are often present and considered pathognomonic for this condition.

media.title: Gumprecht shadows in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)
Smudge cells in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)

NI0-1h.title: Philadelphia chromosome
NI0-1h.description: An abnormal chromosome 22 that results from the Philadelphia translocation, a chromosomal translocation in which chromosomes 9 and 22 exchange a portion of their q arms. The Philadelphia chromosome produces the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein, which elevates tyrosine kinase enzyme activity. It is also referred to as t(9;22)(q34;q11.2). The translocation is implicated in the pathogenesis of several leukemias, most notably chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML).

LI0wWh.title: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors
LI0wWh.description: A class of antineoplastic agents that inhibits tyrosine kinase cell surface signaling proteins. Examples of targeted receptors include epidermal growth factor receptor (e.g., blocked by erlotinib and osimertinib) and BCR-ABL (e.g., blocked by imatinib and dasatinib).

oI00dh.title: Imatinib
oI00dh.description: A biologic anti-neoplastic agent used in the treatment of Philadelphia chromosome (t(9:22) translocation) positive neoplasms, chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML), and acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL). It functions by competitively inhibiting the tyrosine kinase that results from the abnormal BCR-ABL gene.

KI0Udh.title: Plethora
KI0Udh.description: A physical examination finding characterized by cutaneous flushing/erythema as a result of increased red blood cell mass. Can also affect large vessels and result in venous dilation (e.g., inferior vena cava plethora).

6I0jdh.title: Secondary polycythemia
6I0jdh.description: An increase in total red blood cell (RBC) mass (typically correlating with elevations in the RBC count, hematocrit concentration, and hemoglobin concentration) secondary to a factor that stimulates erythropoiesis. Increased total RBC cell mass causes hyperviscosity, increasing the risk of thrombosis and poor oxygenation. Secondary polycythemia is typically caused by erythropoietin (EPO) production by the kidneys secondary to chronic hypoxemia (e.g., from heavy smoking, chronic pulmonary or cardiac disease, high altitude). Other etiologies include doping with EPO and EPO-secreting tumors (e.g., renal cell carcinoma).

JI0sdh.title: Budd-Chiari syndrome
JI0sdh.description: A rare condition characterized by hepatic vein obstruction that manifests with hepatomegaly, ascites, and abdominal discomfort. Most commonly caused by thrombotic occlusion secondary to a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm (e.g., polycythemia vera). Blood flow obstruction causes liver congestion and subsequent liver cell damage, which may result in liver failure.

qI0Cdh.title: Mantle cell lymphoma
qI0Cdh.description: An aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma of B-cell origin that presents at a median age of 65–70 years and mainly affects men. The majority of patients present with advanced disease. Clinical features include lymphadenopathy, B symptoms, and intestinal polyposis of any part of the gastrointestinal tract. Mantle cell lymphomas are typically CD5-positive and have the translocation t(11;14).

rI0fVh.title: Hairy cell leukemia
rI0fVh.description: A low-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by cells with irregular cytoplasmic projections and a "hairy" appearance on peripheral blood smear. Most common in middle-aged men.

7I04Vh.title: Burkitt lymphoma
7I04Vh.description: An aggressive (high-grade) B-cell lymphoma that is most common in children. Associated with translocation t(8;14) in 75% of cases, and commonly with EBV infection. In adults, it occurs in association with HIV infection.

HI0KVh.title: CHOP
HI0KVh.description: A combination of cyclophosphamide, hydroxydaunorubicin (adriamycin), Oncovin® (vincristine), and prednisone that is used in the treatment of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. An antibody against CD20 (rituximab) is added if the non-Hodgkin lymphoma is of B-cell lineage (R-CHOP regimen).

GI0BVh.title: Necrotizing lymphadenitis
GI0BVh.description: A rare condition characterized by painful cervical lymphadenopathy and fever. Most commonly occurs in Asian populations. The exact cause is not fully understood, but there is an association with infections and autoimmune conditions. Typically resolves spontaneously within 1–4 months of onset.

tI0Xeh.title: B symptoms
tI0Xeh.description: The presence of fever, night sweats, and weight loss, which together are classically associated with lymphomas. Sometimes used to refer to the same symptoms in patients with other conditions (e.g., tuberculosis, inflammatory conditions, rheumatologic conditions).

uI0peh.title: Pel-Ebstein fever
uI0peh.description: Intermittent fever with periods of high temperature for 1–2 weeks, followed by afebrile periods for 1–2 weeks. Relatively rare but very specific for Hodgkin lymphoma.

destinations.label: Fever → Differential diagnoses by fever characteristics

vI0Aeh.title: Ann Arbor staging system
vI0Aeh.description: A staging classification system for Hodgkin lymphoma and non-Hodgkin lymphoma that has been replaced by the modified Ann Arbor classification (Cotswold staging system). Components include the extent of lymphatic tissue involvement, the presence of constitutional symptoms, and the presence of splenic involvement.

wI0hUh.title: Reed-Sternberg cells
wI0hUh.description: A type of large, multinucleated cell primarily derived from B lymphocytes. Typically has a bilobed nucleus with dark centers of chromatin and pale halos, which results in an owl eye appearance on histopathologic examination. Classically associated with Hodgkin lymphoma.

yI0d2h.title: ABVD
yI0d2h.description: A chemotherapy regimen used for the treatment of Hodgkin lymphoma. Consists of adriamycin (doxorubicin), bleomycin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine.

zI0r2h.title: β2-microglobulin
zI0r2h.description: A low molecular weight structural component of major histocompatibility complex type 1 (MHC I). Clinically relevant as a tumor marker in certain hematologic malignancies, and as the major constituent protein of dialysis-related amyloidosis.

ar0Qfh.title: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
ar0Qfh.description: A type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma associated with abnormal production of monoclonal IgM antibodies. It mostly occurs in old age and has a good prognosis, as it is a type of indolent lymphoma. The clinical presentation includes hyperviscosity syndrome, platelet dysfunction, and Raynaud's phenomenon.

Xr09fh.title: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
Xr09fh.description: Characterized by complete or incomplete monoclonal immunoglobulins, detectable in patient serum without accompanying clinical symptoms.

fr0kgh.title: Anemia of chronic disease
fr0kgh.description: A condition of anemia that develops in patients with a chronic disease process such as inflammation (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus), malignancy (e.g., lung cancer, breast cancer, lymphoma), or infection (e.g., tuberculosis). Mediated through hepcidin and cytokines and is characterized by normocytic or microcytic anemia with elevated ferritin levels.

gr0Fgh.title: Megaloblastic anemia
gr0Fgh.description: A type of macrocytic anemia characterized by large, nucleated red blood cell precursors that contain uncondensed chromatin. Caused by inhibition of DNA synthesis (e.g., from vitamin B12 or folic acid deficiency) that results in G2 cell cycle arrest, which leads to relatively immature nuclei compared to the cytoplasm. Associated with hypersegmented neutrophils.

Sr0ygh.title: Aplastic anemia
Sr0ygh.description: A condition characterized by pancytopenia due to bone marrow failure with reduced bone marrow cellularity. Typically acquired and idiopathic but can occur secondary to other causes (e.g., medications or viral infections) or as part of an inherited bone marrow failure syndrome (e.g., Fanconi anemia).

hr0cSh.title: Fanconi anemia
hr0cSh.description: A hereditary form of aplastic anemia caused by an autosomal recessive defect in interstrand cross-link repair (e.g., by homologous end joining). Associated with short stature, café-au-lait spots, thumb and forearm malformations, and an increased incidence of acute myeloid leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes.

media.title: Short thumb and café au lait spots

Rr0lSh.title: Hemorrhagic diathesis
Rr0lSh.description: An abnormal and increased susceptibility to bleeding, often due to hypocoagulability.

Qr0uSh.title: Hemostasis
Qr0uSh.description: The physiological process by which bleeding is stopped. Includes blood vessel constriction, formation of a platelet plug, and blood coagulation through the formation of a fibrin clot.

jr0_Sh.title: Primary hemostasis
jr0_Sh.description: Platelet plug formation. Complex cascade triggered by endothelial damage, which results in in platelet linking and temporary hemostasis.

lr0vhh.title: Secondary hemostasis
lr0vhh.description: The process of achieving hemostasis via the interaction of plasma coagulation factors (the coagulation cascade).

nr073h.title: Intrinsic pathway (hemostasis)
nr073h.description: A part of the coagulation cascade that is initiated when collagen is exposed. Primarily consists of factors VIII, IX, XI, and XII. Activated mainly by thrombin. Impairment of this pathway results in bleeding disorders (e.g., hemophilia A and B).

pr0LRh.title: Protein S
pr0LRh.description: A cofactor of protein C. Protein C and S complex together to inhibit factors Va and VIIIa, resulting in inhibition of the coagulation cascade.

Jr0sRh.title: Protein C
Jr0sRh.description: A protein that inhibits factors Va and VIIIa, resulting in inhibition of the coagulation cascade and, subsequently, clotting. Requires protein S as a cofactor.

qr0CRh.title: Fibrinolysis
qr0CRh.description: The breakdown of fibrin in blood clots by the enzyme plasmin.

8r0OQh.title: Vitamin K deficiency
8r0OQh.description: A vitamin deficiency that leads to deficiency of the coagulation factors II, VII, IX, and X, which impairs the coagulation cascade and leads to pathological bleeding. Symptoms include ecchymosis, hematomas, and hemarthroses.

Dr01jh.title: Bleeding time
Dr01jh.description: A laboratory examination that tests the function of platelets and their ability to aggregate (i.e., form a clot). It is performed by making a small puncture to the skin and measuring the time it takes for the bleeding to stop.

9r0Njh.title: Coagulation studies
9r0Njh.description: A series of serum tests that evaluate for abnormal blood clotting. A typical panel includes the prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT); it can also include an international normalized ratio (INR), serum fibrinogen concentration, and serum D-dimer concentration.

Cr0qjh.title: INR
Cr0qjh.description: The ratio of an individual's prothrombin time (PT) relative to the PT of a control sample. Common causes of elevation include vitamin K deficiency and warfarin therapy. Used to monitor the effectiveness of the latter.

yr0dPh.title: Prothrombin time
yr0dPh.description: An assay that evaluates the extrinsic and common pathways of the coagulation cascade (measures activity of factors I, II, V, VII, and X). Used to evaluate coagulation disorders and to monitor the effect of warfarin. Normal range is 11–15 seconds.

e70xkh.title: Platelet count
e70xkh.description: A laboratory parameter that indicates the number of platelets detected per unit volume of blood. It is a standard component of the complete blood count. A normal platelet count is between 150,000/mm³ and 400,000/mm³.

f70kOh.title: Immune thrombocytopenia
f70kOh.description: An acquired form of a low platelet count secondary to antibody formation against GpIIb/IIIa on platelets, without any perturbation of the structure or function of WBCs, RBCs, or coagulation factors (i.e., isolated thrombocytopenia). It is a diagnosis of exclusion without specific clinical or laboratory parameters.

S70yOh.title: Thrombopoietin receptor agonists
S70yOh.description: A class of platelet growth factors used to treat thrombocytopenia. Thrombopoetin receptor agonists mimic the effect of endogenous thrombopoietin on megakaryocytes, thereby leading to increased platelet production. Examples include eltrombopag, avatrombopag, and romiplostim.

370Slh.title: Hemolytic uremic syndrome
370Slh.description: A thrombotic microangiopathy characterized by the HUS triad: thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and acute kidney injury. Shiga toxin-associated HUS is the most common form and predominantly affects children; it is caused by Shiga toxin-producing bacteria (most commonly Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli O157:H7). Non-Shiga toxin-associated HUS is caused by complement pathway dysregulation (in complement-mediated HUS), infection, medication, transplant, or autoimmune disease.

media.title: Hemolytic uremic syndrome and thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura

j70_lh.title: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
j70_lh.description: A thrombotic microangiopathy in which microthrombi, consisting primarily of platelets, form and occlude the microvasculature. Caused by reduced activity of the protease ADAMTS13. Associated with a pentad of symptoms: thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, neurologic abnormalities, acute kidney injury, and fever.

media.title: Hemolytic uremic syndrome and thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura

O70INh.title: Primary polydipsia
O70INh.description: The excessive intake of fluids in the absence of thirst. Can cause euvolemic hyponatremia. Patients with severe disease typically have an underlying mental health disorder (e.g., acute psychosis due to schizophrenia).

l70vNh.title: Desmopressin
l70vNh.description: A synthetic vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone) analog used for a number of conditions, including central diabetes insipidus, nocturnal enuresis, von Willebrand disease types 1 and 2, and mild hemophilia A.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

M70Mmh.title: Pituitary adenoma
M70Mmh.description: A benign tumor that often arises sporadically from the anterior pituitary gland. Classified based on their size as either microadenomas or macroadenomas. Also classified by whether they produce hormones as secretory (functional) or nonsecretory (nonfunctioning) adenomas.

n707mh.title: Sheehan syndrome
n707mh.description: A condition of hypopituitarism caused by ischemia and necrosis of the pituitary gland due to severe postpartum hemorrhage.

I70YMh.title: Thyroid storm
I70YMh.description: An acute exacerbation of hyperthyroidism or thyrotoxicosis, resulting in a life-threatening hypermetabolic state. Features include hyperpyrexia with profuse sweating, severe cardiovascular symptoms (e.g., arrhythmia, heart failure), gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g., abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea), and neuropsychiatric symptoms (e.g., severe agitation, psychoses, seizures).

7704Mh.title: Congenital hypothyroidism
7704Mh.description: A condition that is generally asymptomatic at birth but can eventually cause symptoms such as lethargy, constipation, feeding problems, macroglossia, umbilical hernia, dry skin, as well as prolonged jaundice. In developing countries, iodine deficiency is most common; thyroid dysgenesis is more common in developed countries.

s70tMh.title: Myxedema
s70tMh.description: A collection of fluid caused by deposition of glycosaminoglycans (mucopolysaccharides) in various tissues. Most commonly occurs in the lower legs (pretibial myxedema), behind the eyes (exophthalmos), and in the heart (myxedematous heart disease). Etiologies include hypothyroidism and Graves disease.

G70BMh.title: Subclinical hypothyroidism
G70BMh.description: A form of hypothyroidism characterized by increased TSH, but normal T3 and T4 levels.

t70Xnh.title: Euthyroid sick syndrome
t70Xnh.description: A syndrome that causes abnormal findings on thyroid function tests in patients with severe, nonthyroidal illness (e.g., a critically ill intensive care patient). Believed to be caused by cytokines. The most common pattern is a decrease in T3 levels, while levels of T4 and TSH are normal or low (low T3 syndrome).

F70gnh.title: Low T3 syndrome
F70gnh.description: A subtype of euthyroid sick syndrome characterized by a normal serum free T4 concentration and TSH concentration and a decreased serum free T3 concentration. Typically asymptomatic.

E708nh.title: Levothyroxine
E708nh.description: A synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4) used to treat hypothyroidism or to suppress TSH release.

v70Anh.title: Myxedema coma
v70Anh.description: A condition of severe hypothyroidism characterized by altered mental status, hypothermia, myxedema, hypoventilation, hypotension, and bradycardia. Etiologies include nonadherence to thyroid replacement therapy, infections, surgery, and/or trauma that result in decompensation of an existing thyroid hormone deficiency.

D701Lh.title: Hashitoxicosis
D701Lh.description: Transient thyrotoxicosis in patients with early Hashimoto disease resulting from the initial destruction of the thyroid gland and subsequent release of thyroid hormones. Typically lasts for 1 to 5 months but sometimes as long as 2 years.

970NLh.title: Riedel's thyroiditis
970NLh.description: A rare form of chronic thyroiditis characterized by extensive fibrosis of the thyroid gland and surrounding tissues, leading to a firm, immobile, enlarged thyroid and symptoms of compression, e.g., dysphagia, dyspnea, dysphonia. It is considered part of the spectrum of IgG4-related disease.

C70qLh.title: Acute suppurative thyroiditis
C70qLh.description: A rare, potentially life-threatening bacterial infection of the thyroid gland that manifests with thyroid pain and fever. Treatment includes broad spectrum antibiotics and abscess drainage.

x70ELh.title: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
x70ELh.description: A poorly differentiated malignant neoplasm of the thyroid, characterized by aggressive local growth and rapid lymphatic and hematogenous metastasis.

y70doh.title: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
y70doh.description: A well-differentiated malignant neoplasia of the follicular cells of the thyroid gland characterized by predominantly hematogenous metastasis.

_705oh.title: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
_705oh.description: A well-differentiated malignant neoplasia of the thyroid gland and the most common type of thyroid cancer, characterized by early lymphatic metastasis.

z70roh.title: Thyroglobulin
z70roh.description: A protein made in the thyroid gland that is a precursor to thyroid hormone.

ZH0ZKh.title: Psammoma body
ZH0ZKh.description: A group of concentric, intracellular calcium collections seen in certain neoplasms such as papillary carcinoma of thyroid, papillary serous endometrial carcinoma, mesothelioma, meningioma, and serous papillary cystadenocarcinoma of ovary and endometrium. Can also appear in chronically inflamed tissue.

0H0eKh.title: Papillary microcarcinoma
0H0eKh.description: A subtype of papillary carcinoma of the thyroid characterized by a tumor less than 10 mm in diameter. Typically not detectable on clinical examination.

aH0QKh.title: Primary adrenal insufficiency
aH0QKh.description: A state of decreased adrenal production of adrenocortical hormones (glucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids, and adrenal androgens) caused by a disorder of the adrenal glands. The most frequent cause of primary adrenal insufficiency is autoimmune adrenalitis. Less commonly, it is due to infection (tuberculosis, CMV) or adrenal hemorrhage.

dH0o6h.title: Secondary adrenal insufficiency
dH0o6h.description: A state of decreased adrenal production of glucocorticoids and adrenal androgens as a result of decreased production of ACTH in the pituitary gland. Can be caused by a sudden discontinuation of glucocorticoids after prolonged glucocorticoid therapy and hypopituitarism.

TH06ph.title: Polyglandular autoimmune syndrome
TH06ph.description: A group of conditions characterized by autoimmune disease that causes multiple endocrine deficiencies. Includes polyglandular autoimmune syndrome type I (Whitaker syndrome) and polyglandular autoimmune syndrome type 2 (Schmidt syndrome).

SH0yph.title: ACTH stimulation test
SH0yph.description: A test in which serum cortisol levels are measured before and 30 or 60 minutes after the administration of exogenous ACTH, usually given as a 250 μg bolus of corticotropin. In a healthy patient, serum cortisol levels should increase in response. A low response (e.g., < 18 μg/dL at 30 or 60 minutes) confirms adrenal gland dysfunction and is the gold standard for diagnosing primary adrenal insufficiency. However, results may also be abnormally low in cases of secondary and tertiary adrenal insufficiency (due to chronic ACTH deficiency and resultant adrenal atrophy), so it is important to interpret within the clinical context.

hH0cJh.title: Addisonian crisis
hH0cJh.description: An acute, severe glucocorticoid deficiency caused either by stress in a patient with underlying adrenal insufficiency or sudden discontinuation of glucocorticoids after prolonged glucocorticoid therapy. Causes fever, abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, impaired consciousness, and life-threatening shock.

RH0lJh.title: Saline infusion test
RH0lJh.description: A diagnostic test used to confirm primary hyperaldosteronism. Plasma aldosterone and renin activity levels are drawn at baseline and after 4 hours of a normal saline infusion (salt loading). Patients with primary hyperaldosteronism have elevated plasma aldosterone (> 6 ng/dL if seated and > 10 ng/dL if recumbent) because of a failure to suppress aldosterone secretion.

iH0JJh.title: Fludrocortisone suppression test
iH0JJh.description: A diagnostic confirmatory test for primary hyperaldosteronism. Plasma aldosterone and renin activity levels are drawn at baseline and after 4 days of oral fludrocortisone. Patients with primary hyperaldosteronism have elevated plasma aldosterone (> 6 ng/dL) because of a failure to suppress aldosterone secretion.

QH0uJh.title: Pseudohyperaldosteronism
QH0uJh.description: A clinical presentation characterized by hypertension and hypokalemia but with normal aldosterone release. Etiologies include congenital adrenal hyperplasia, exogenous mineralocorticoid use, and Cushing syndrome.

PH0Wqh.title: Cushing disease
PH0Wqh.description: A condition of increased ACTH production by a pituitary tumor leading to classic Cushing symptomatology, including fatigue, recurrent infections, glucose intolerance, lower extremity swelling, proximal muscle weakness, depression, central and neck obesity, easy bruising, striae.

4H03qh.title: Dexamethasone suppression test
4H03qh.description: A diagnostic test for Cushing syndrome (hypercortisolism). Dexamethasone, a powerful glucocorticoid, suppresses ACTH secretion (and thereby cortisol levels) without interfering with serum cortisol measurement. While low doses of dexamethasone would decrease serum cortisol levels in healthy individuals, cortisol levels will remain elevated in patients with hypercortisolism. Higher doses of dexamethasone, however, decrease cortisol levels even in patients with hypercortisolism, with the notable exception being hypercortisolism caused by ectopic ACTH production (e.g., paraneoplastic syndromes)

kH0mqh.title: Phenoxybenzamine
kH0mqh.description: A nonselective, noncompetetive alpha blocker that blocks both alpha-1 and alpha-2 adrenoceptors irreversibly and equally. Used for preoperative blood pressure management before pheochromocytoma excision to induce alpha blockade and thereby prevent hypertensive crisis. Also used in long-term management of inoperable pheochromocytoma.

OH0Iqh.title: Primary hyperparathyroidism
OH0Iqh.description: A condition caused by excessive excretion of parathyroid hormone (e.g., from parathyroid gland adenomas and hyperplasia of the parathyroid glands). Manifestations include hypercalcemia, nephrolithiasis, bone and joint pain, lack of appetite, nausea, and constipation.

mH0VIh.title: Secondary hyperparathyroidism
mH0VIh.description: Excessive excretion of parathyroid hormone and hyperplasia of the parathyroid glands in response to low serum calcium levels. Causes include hypovitaminosis D and chronic kidney disease.

KH0Urh.title: LADA
KH0Urh.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Latent autoimmune diabetes in adults
2. Left anterior descending artery

6H0jrh.title: Maturity onset diabetes of the young
6H0jrh.description: An autosomal dominant form of noninsulin-dependent diabetes mellitus characterized by early onset (< 25 years of age) and lack of autoantibodies.

JH0srh.title: Hemoglobin A1C
JH0srh.description: The concentration of glycated hemoglobin A1 in red blood cells. In an nonenzymatic reaction (glycation), glucose in the blood binds to hemoglobin and forms HbA1c. The higher the blood glucose levels, the more HbA1c is detectable. Therefore, the percentage of HbA1c in the blood serves as a surrogate parameter for the average blood glucose level over the life span of red blood cells (~ 3 months) and can be used to diagnose diabetes mellitus and monitor response to treatment.

qH0Crh.title: Glucose intolerance
qH0Crh.description: A metabolic condition associated with insulin resistance that results in hyperglycemia. One of the criteria for prediabetes. Defined as a serum glucose concentration 140-199 mg/dL two hours after the administration of 75 g oral glucose.

IH0Y7h.title: Oral glucose tolerance test
IH0Y7h.description: An oral glucose challenge used to diagnose diabetes. Performed as a one-step or two-step test. Also used to confirm the diagnosis of gestational diabetes or assess for growth hormone hypersecretion (e.g., to evaluate for acromegaly).

sH0t7h.title: Conventional insulin therapy
sH0t7h.description: A type of insulin regimen that usually involves twice-daily injections of intermediate insulin mixed with either short-acting insulin or rapid-acting insulin. Can be self-mixed or premixed.

GH0B7h.title: Intensive insulin therapy
GH0B7h.description: A type of treatment regimen for diabetes mellitus that uses ≥ 3 insulin injections per day or continuous infusions, i.e., full basal-bolus regimen and insulin pump therapy. Indicated in all patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus and some patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The goal is to simulate physiological glucose metabolism.

FH0gHh.title: Insulin pump
FH0gHh.description: A medical device that infuses insulin (usually a rapid-acting insulin analog) subcutaneously. The basal rate of infusion and boluses of insulin can be tailored to the patient's glucose needs.

8H0OHh.title: Dawn phenomenon
8H0OHh.description: Hyperglycemia in diabetic patients (especially type 1) that results from inadequate insulin production in response to a physiological surge of catecholamines, somatotropin, and cortisol production during the early morning hours.

vH0AHh.title: Monckeberg arteriosclerosis
vH0AHh.description: A form of arteriosclerosis characterized by calcification of the media and internal elastic lamina that do not cause arterial stenosis. It is associated with diabetes mellitus and/or progressive kidney disease and usually affects arteries in the extremities.

9H0Nsh.title: Diabetic kidney disease
9H0Nsh.description: A form of chronic kidney disease that occurs in 20–40% of patients with diabetes mellitus. Caused by glomerular damage induced by glycosylation of the basement membrane and plasma hyperfiltration. Patients are usually asymptomatic, and diagnosis is based on the presence of albuminuria and/or reduced eGFR.

CH0qsh.title: Nodular glomerulosclerosis
CH0qsh.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by eosinophilic, hypocellular nodules of mesangial matrix in renal glomeruli. Referred to as Kimmelstiel–Wilson nodules when caused by diabetes.

xH0Esh.title: Diabetic retinopathy
xH0Esh.description: A vascular disease of the retina that can develop in individuals with chronic, undercontrolled diabetes mellitus. Classified into nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy, proliferative diabetic retinopathy, and macular edema. Loss of vision is typically insidious, but acute loss of vision can occur as a result of retinal detachment, vitreous hemorrhage, or macular edema.

BH0zsh.title: Nonproliferative retinopathy
BH0zsh.description: A vascular disease of the retina affecting individuals with diabetes mellitus in which weakening of the vessel walls results in retinal microaneurysm and leaking of fluid and blood.

destinations.label: Diabetic retinopathy → Overview of diabetic retinopathy

yH0dGh.title: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy
yH0dGh.description: A vascular disease of the retina affecting individuals with diabetes mellitus in which neovascularization arises from the disc and/or retinal vessels.

destinations.label: Diabetic retinopathy → Overview of diabetic retinopathy

AH0RGh.title: Macular edema
AH0RGh.description: An ophthalmologic finding characterized by retinal thickening and swelling of the macula, typically in the context of macular ischemia. Commonly occurs in the setting of diabetic retinopathy. Often leads to vision loss.

_H05Gh.title: Diabetic neuropathy
_H05Gh.description: A complication of diabetes mellitus characterized by damage to nerve fibers. Most commonly manifests as distal symmetrical sensory loss of the lower extremities. May also manifest with mononeuropathy, autonomic neuropathy, or a mixed motor and sensory neuropathy.

0s0eth.title: Malum perforans
0s0eth.description: A painless ulcer that is usually located on a plantar pressure point of the foot (e.g., over the head of the metatarsal bones or the heel). Occurs as a complication of diabetes due to neuropathic, microvascular, and macrovascular changes.

as0Qth.title: Diabetic neuropathic arthropathy
as0Qth.description: A complication of chronic diabetes characterized by bone destruction due to progressive loss of sensation from peripheral neuropathy and changes in circulation.

bs0Hth.title: Limited joint mobility syndrome
bs0Hth.description: A stiffness of the small joints of the hand characterized by flexion contractures of the fingers. Associated with tight waxy skin, particularly on the dorsal surface of the fingers. Commonly seen in patients with diabetes mellitus.

cs0aFh.title: Necrobiosis lipoidica
cs0aFh.description: A rare, chronic granulomatous disease of the skin commonly associated with diabetes mellitus; starts as a reddish brown papule and progresses to a yellow-brown papule or plaque with visible telangiectasias. Ulceration of the lesion may also occur following minor trauma.

destinations.label: Collection of dermatological disorders → Cutaneous granulomas

Ws0PFh.title: Gestational diabetes mellitus
Ws0PFh.description: A condition of impaired glucose tolerance during pregnancy. Associated with an increased risk of maternal morbidity (e.g., preeclampsia, type 2 diabetes) and fetal morbidity (e.g., macrosomia, shoulder dystocia). Most cases can be controlled with lifestyle changes. Divided into class A1GDM (no medication required) and class A2GDM (medication, usually insulin, required).

Ts068h.title: Kussmaul breathing
Ts068h.description: A type of hyperventilation characterized by a deep, labored, breathing pattern, which serves as a respiratory compensation mechanism for severe metabolic acidosis to exhale more CO₂. Most commonly associated with diabetic ketoacidosis.

Rs0luh.title: Obesity
Rs0luh.description: A chronic metabolic-nutritional condition characterized by the accumulation of excess body fat. In adults, typically defined by a body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m². A lower threshold (25 kg/m² or 27.5 kg/m²) is recommended for adults of Asian descent. In children, defined as a BMI ≥ 95th percentile for age and sex. Associated with a moderate to very severe risk of weight-related health problems.

Qs0uuh.title: Body mass index
Qs0uuh.description: An estimate of overall body fat determined by the ratio of a person's body mass (in kilograms) by the square of the body height (in meters). A BMI of 18.5–24.9 kg/m² in adults or in the 5th–84th percentile in children is considered healthy. Lower cutoffs are recommended for adults of Asian descent. BMI may underestimate body fat in older adults and individuals with low muscle mass and overestimate body fat in muscular individuals.

destinations.label: Principles of nutrition → Diagnostic tools for assessing healthy weight and body mass

Ps0WEh.title: Acute tubular necrosis
Ps0WEh.description: A form of acute kidney injury that is caused by severe damage to the renal tubules. Accounts for approximately 85% of intrinsic acute kidney injuries. May be due to ischemic/hypoxic (e.g., thromboembolism, prolonged hypotension) or toxic (e.g., contrast-induced nephropathy) damage.

destinations.label: Acute kidney injury → Subtypes and variants

4s03Eh.title: Pigment nephropathy
4s03Eh.description: An acute kidney injury that occurs as a result of the toxic effects of heme-containing pigments (e.g., hemoglobin, myoglobin) on proximal renal tubular cells (toxin-induced acute tubular necrosis). Can occur in patients with severe intravascular hemolysis or rhabdomyolysis.

destinations.label: Acute kidney injury → Subtypes and variants

ks0mEh.title: Contrast-induced nephropathy
ks0mEh.description: A form of acute kidney injury characterized by > 25% increase in serum creatinine within 3 days of administration of IV contrast. Risk factors include underlying renal insufficiency, age > 60 years, diabetes mellitus, and prior kidney disorders.

destinations.label: Acute kidney injury → Subtypes and variants

Os0IEh.title: FENa
Os0IEh.description: The percentage of glomerular filtered sodium (Na) that is excreted in the urine in relation to filtered creatinine (Cr). FENa (%) = (serum Cr × urine Na)/(serum Na × urine Cr) × 100. Used to help determine the cause of acute kidney injury (AKI) and to differentiate between causes of hyponatremia. Low FENa suggests prerenal AKI or extrarenal sodium loss; high FENa indicates intrinsic renal causes or renal sodium loss.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Renal function test

Ns0-Eh.title: Uremia
Ns0-Eh.description: A symptom complex that is characterized by anorexia, nausea, vomiting, pruritus, pericarditis, pleuritis, peripheral neuropathy, and CNS abnormalities (confusion, lethargy, seizures, somnolence, coma), and an increased risk of infection and bleeding; occurs secondary to elevated levels of nitrogenous waste products (e.g., urea) in the blood due to kidney failure.

5s0ivh.title: Chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder
5s0ivh.description: A term for the heterogeneous group of metabolic bone diseases that can occur with severe (stage IV, V) chronic kidney disease. Manifestations include 1) abnormalities of calcium, phosphorus, parathyroid hormone, and/or vitamin D metabolism, 2) abnormalities in bone growth and turnover, and 3) soft tissue calcification.

media.title: Pathophysiology of chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD)

Ms0Mvh.title: Glomerular filtration rate
Ms0Mvh.description: The rate at which fluid is filtered through the kidneys (specifically, from glomerular capillaries into the Bowman capsule). In clinical practice, creatinine clearance is a useful surrogate measure for GFR (but typically overestimates actual GFR). Can be approximated with various formulas as estimated GFR (eGFR).

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function
Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Renal function test

ps0LDh.title: Dysmorphic red blood cells
ps0LDh.description: A morphologic descriptor for red blood cells with an irregular cell surface due to osmotic stress inside the renal tubules. Visible on urine sediment analysis, where they resemble "Mickey Mouse ears."

Js0sDh.title: Red blood cell casts
Js0sDh.description: A collection of abnormal red blood cells that form in the renal tubule visible on urine microscopy in patients with glomerular damage (e.g., glomerulonephritis).

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

media.title: Red blood cell (RBC) casts in urine sediment

qs0CDh.title: Nephritic sediment
