_MY5rp.title: Motor evoked potential
_MY5rp.description: The electrical response of the brain, as measured by electroencephalography, in response to transcranial magnetic stimulation of the motor cortex.

ZnYZ7p.title: Evoked potentials
ZnYZ7p.description: Electrical events generated in the CNS following peripheral stimulation of sensory organs (e.g., skin, eyes), typically measured by electroencephalography (EEG). Used to detect subclinical central nervous system lesions, especially visual (VEP), somatosensory (SSEP), or brainstem auditory potentials (BAEP).

0nYe7p.title: Computed tomography angiography
0nYe7p.description: A noninvasive diagnostic imaging technique that uses computerized tomography, intravenous administration of a radiocontrast agent, and specific timing to visualize blood vessels of interest. Also allows imaging of surrounding anatomic structures.

cnYaHp.title: Magnetic resonance angiography
cnYaHp.description: A diagnostic imaging technique that combines a regular MRI with the injection of a contrast agent. Used to visualize blood vessels and perfusion of anatomic structures.

media.title: Multilevel peripheral arterial disease of the lower limbs

TnY6sp.title: Jobe test
TnY6sp.description: A physical examination maneuver used to assess the supraspinatus. The patient outstretches and internally rotates their arm so that the thumb faces downward, which minimizes the effect of the deltoid muscle on abduction. Considered positive if the patient cannot maintain their arm abducted against resistance or if it is painful to do so, which suggests injury to the supraspinatus tendon or muscle or injury to the suprascapular nerve.

destinations.label: Orthopedic shoulder examination → Examination of the rotator cuff

gnYFsp.title: Lift-off test
gnYFsp.description: A physical examination maneuver used to assess the subscapularis muscle. The patient places their hand on the lower back with the palm facing outward and lifts the arm posteriorly off the back against resistance. Considered positive if the patient cannot lift the arm posteriorly, which indicates injury to the subscapularis muscle or tendon.

destinations.label: Orthopedic shoulder examination → Examination of the rotator cuff

3nYSGp.title: Infraspinatus test
3nYSGp.description: A physical examination maneuver to assess infraspinatus muscle function. The patient stands with the elbow flexed at 90º. The examiner applies force to the patient's lateral underarm, which creates an internal rotation movement in the shoulder. The patient is asked to maintain the position and resist the force. The test is considered positive if pain or weakness develop during the maneuver.

destinations.label: Orthopedic shoulder examination → Examination of the rotator cuff

inYJGp.title: Painful arc
inYJGp.description: Pain-related restriction of movement and strength with abduction of the arm between 60–120°. Seen in patients with subacromial impingement syndrome.

destinations.label: Orthopedic shoulder examination → Shoulder impingement tests

4nY3tp.title: Neer test
4nY3tp.description: A physical examination maneuver used to assess the presence and degree of rotator cuff impingement. Elevate the patient's internally rotated and outstretched arm with simultaneous stabilization of the scapula. Pain upon eliciting this maneuver indicates narrowed subacromial space and impingement, particularly of the supraspinatus muscle and tendon.

destinations.label: Orthopedic shoulder examination → Shoulder impingement tests

knYmtp.title: Hawkins Kennedy test
knYmtp.description: A test for subacromial impingement syndrome. The examiner places the patient's arm in 90° anteversion and flexes the elbow to 90°. In this position, pain during internal rotation is a nonspecific indication of impingement syndrome.

destinations.label: Orthopedic shoulder examination → Shoulder impingement tests

qnYC8p.title: Glenohumeral joint
qnYC8p.description: A ball and socket joint formed by the glenoid cavity of the scapula and the head of the humerus.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

media.title: Range of motion of the shoulder
Lateral view of the shoulder joint

GnYBup.title: Coracoacromial arch
GnYBup.description: A structure that consists of the coracoid process, the acromion, and the coracoacromial ligament. Prevents superior displacement of the humeral head from the glenoid cavity.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

tnYXEp.title: Acromion process
tnYXEp.description: The lateral continuation of the scapular spine, which curves anteriorly over the superior aspect of the shoulder and articulates with the clavicle to form the acromioclavicular joint.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

8nYOEp.title: Coracoid process
8nYOEp.description: An anterolateral pointed hook-like process that arises from the superior border of the scapula and lies below the lateral end of the clavicle. Provides attachment to pectoralis minor, coracobrachialis, and short head of the biceps brachii muscles. Lies in close proximity to the brachial plexus and the axillary vessels.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

unYpEp.title: Coracoacromial ligament
unYpEp.description: A ligament that extends from the coracoid process to the acromion. Together with the coracoid process and the acromion, it forms the coracoacromial arch.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

EnY8Ep.title: Rotator cuff
EnY8Ep.description: A group of muscles and tendons that stabilize and assist in movements of the glenohumeral joint (shoulder joint). Includes the supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor, and subscapularis muscles and their associated tendons.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Muscles of the shoulder girdle

vnYAEp.title: Supraspinatus muscle
vnYAEp.description: A rotator cuff muscle that originates from the supraspinatus fossa of the scapula and inserts into the greater tubercle of the humerus. Responsible for abduction of the arm between 0-15°.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Muscles of the shoulder girdle

DnY1vp.title: Subscapularis muscle
DnY1vp.description: A muscle that originates from the subscapular fossa (ventral scapular surface) and inserts into the lesser tubercle of the humerus. Innervated by the upper and lower subscapular nerves. Internally rotates and adducts the humerus.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Muscles of the shoulder girdle

wnYhvp.title: Teres minor muscle
wnYhvp.description: A rotator cuff muscle that originates from the lateral border of the scapula and inserts onto the medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus. Adducts and externally rotates of the arm. Innervated by the axillary nerve.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Muscles of the shoulder girdle

CnYqvp.title: Glenohumeral ligaments
CnYqvp.description: A group of three ligaments (superior, middle, and inferior) that lie on the internal aspect of the glenohumeral joint capsule and strengthen the joint capsule anteriorly. They originate from the glenoid labrum and merge with the fibrous layer of the capsule distally before inserting onto the anatomical neck of the humerus.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

xnYEvp.title: Coracohumeral ligament
xnYEvp.description: A ligament that extends from the coracoid process of the scapula to the greater tubercle of the humerus. Strengthens the anterior part of the glenohumeral joint capsule.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

BnYzvp.title: Long head of the biceps
BnYzvp.description: The lateral head of the biceps brachii muscle. Originates from the supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula and continues as a tendon through the bicipital groove of the humeral head before joining the muscle body. Injury can result in biceps tendinopathy and/or subacromial impingement syndrome.

ynYdDp.title: Subacromial bursa
ynYdDp.description: A synovial, fluid-filled sac that lies between the deltoid muscle and the head of the humerus and extends under the acromion. Minimizes friction between the head of the humerus and the acromion, especially during overhead abduction of the shoulder joint.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

-nYDDp.title: Speed's test
-nYDDp.description: A physical examination test to evaluate the biceps tendon in the bicipital groove. Also known as the palm-up test. The patient's arm is fully extended with their palm facing up, and they are asked to flex the shoulder forward against resistance. Pain and/or tenderness in the bicipital groove indicates a positive test. A different variant of the Speed test involves abduction of the patient's arm with the elbow flexed at 90° and the forearm supinated followed by bending of the elbow against resistance.

destinations.label: Orthopedic shoulder examination → Examination of the long head of the biceps tendon

ZLYZwp.title: SLAP lesion
ZLYZwp.description: A superior glenoid labrum lesion. Commonly occurs after a fall onto the extended arm.

destinations.label: Soft tissue lesions of the shoulder → Glenoid labrum injuries

bLYHwp.title: Inspection of the shoulder region
bLYHwp.description: A part of the musculoskeletal examination. The clinician notes the height of both acromions and inspects the shoulders, the outline of the trapezius muscle, neck, scapular outline, pectoralis, and deltoids. The clinician identifies signs of asymmetry, atrophy, hypertrophy, protrusions (e.g., as in winged scapula), swelling, hematoma, or visible bruising.

destinations.label: Orthopedic shoulder examination → Inspection of the shoulder region

1LY29p.title: Digital rectal examination
1LY29p.description: A test used to evaluate the prostate and rectum. Insert a gloved and lubricated finger into the patient's rectum. If the patient is a male, palpate the prostate gland and assess size, consistency, and nodularity. Can also aid in the detection of ovarian or uterine masses. Note any palpable masses or palpable protrusions. Always check the glove after a digital rectal examination, as visible blood may indicate underlying gastrointestinal bleeding.

eLYx9p.title: Nutritional status
eLYx9p.description: An individual's physiological state in relation to protein, energy, and micronutrients. Influenced by consumption (e.g., excess or insufficiency) and the ability to absorb and utilize nutrients (e.g., the impact of malabsorption syndromes).

2LYTCp.title: Vital signs
2LYTCp.description: The signs that indicate the basic functions of the body. Usually includes temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and blood oxygen saturation. Normal ranges vary depending on age and sex.

destinations.label: Physical examination → Vital signs and measurements

SLYyCp.title: Supravesical urinary tract obstruction
SLYyCp.description: A mechanical or functional blockage of the outflow of urine proximal to the bladder. Examples include ureteral calculi, ureteropelvic junction obstruction, and ureteral strictures.

hLYcxp.title: Ureteropelvic junction obstruction
hLYcxp.description: A congenital or acquired condition in which the junction between the ureter and renal pelvis is narrowed. Patients generally present with a palpable abdominal mass secondary to hydronephrosis (in neonates) or episodic abdominal pain following large amounts of diuresis (in older children and young adults).

destinations.label: Urinary tract obstruction → Subtypes and variants

QLYuxp.title: Hydronephrosis
QLYuxp.description: Dilatation and distension of the renal collecting system due to distal obstruction.

PLYWBp.title: Hydroureter
PLYWBp.description: Dilatation of the ureter due to a distal obstruction.

OLYIBp.title: Obstructive nephropathy
OLYIBp.description: A type of renal insufficiency caused by urinary tract obstruction.

mLYVyp.title: Infravesical outlet obstruction
mLYVyp.description: A mechanical or functional blockage of the outflow of urine distal to the bladder. Examples include benign prostatic hyperplasia, urethral strictures, and posterior urethral valves.

5LYiyp.title: Urethral stricture
5LYiyp.description: The narrowing of the urethra secondary to the formation of scar tissue usually resulting from trauma, instrumentation, or infection.

destinations.label: Urinary tract obstruction → Subtypes and variants

JLYsAp.title: Urinary bladder tamponade
JLYsAp.description: An acute bladder outlet obstruction due to a blood clot in the internal urethral orifice. Secondary to bleeding caused by bladder cancer, bladder trauma, surgery (e.g., TURP), hemorrhagic cystitis, or anticoagulant-induced bleeding.

wLYh-p.title: P wave
wLYh-p.description: A waveform seen on an ECG that represents atrial depolarization. The right atrium depolarizes slightly earlier than the left atrium.

media.title: P wave morphology in the limb leads
Morphology of the normal P wave in leads II and V₁
P wave morphology in the precordial leads

9LYN-p.title: P pulmonale
9LYN-p.description: An ECG finding characterized by narrow-peaked P waves with an amplitude > 2.5 mm in the inferior leads II, III, and/or aVF. It is a result of right atrial enlargement and, therefore, may indicate pulmonary diseases (e.g., pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary embolism, COPD).

media.title: Morphology of P pulmonale in leads II and V₁

yLYdZJ.title: P mitrale
yLYdZJ.description: An electrocardiographic sign of left atrial enlargement (e.g., due to mitral stenosis). Characterized by a biphasic (i.e., "double-humped") P wave and/or prolongation of the P > 0.10 s (i.e., a wide P wave).

ZoYZ0J.title: PR interval
ZoYZ0J.description: The time between the beginning of the P wave and the beginning of the QRS complex (Q wave or R wave) on an ECG. Represents atrioventricular transmission of the electrical impulse generated by the SA node. Normally ≤ 0.2 seconds.

aoYQ0J.title: QRS complex
aoYQ0J.description: A component of the ECG waveform that represents the electrical conduction in the ventricles and corresponds approximately to ventricular systole.

YoYn0J.title: Incomplete bundle branch block
YoYn0J.description: A bundle branch block with a QRS duration between 0.1 and 0.12 seconds.

boYH0J.title: Complete bundle branch block
boYH0J.description: A bundle branch block with a QRS duration ≥ 0.12 seconds.

XoY90J.title: Right bundle branch block
XoY90J.description: An electrocardiographic finding that suggests dysfunction of the right bundle of His in the cardiac conduction system. Classically manifests as a prolonged (widened) QRS complex and a characteristic "M" or "rabbit ear" appearance due to rSR' waves in the right precordial leads (V1, V2).

media.title: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia and right bundle branch block

1oY2aJ.title: Left bundle branch block
1oY2aJ.description: Cardiac conduction alteration in which there is delay or obstruction of impulses sent through the left bundle branch pathway, leading to delayed left ventricle contraction. ECG signs include a QRS duration ≥ 120 ms, a rS or QS complex in lead V1, and a notched (M-shaped) R wave in V6.

media.title: Sinus tachycardia with a left bundle-branch block

UoYbYJ.title: Poor R wave progression
UoYbYJ.description: The absence of the normal increase in the size of R waves from lead V1 to V6 on an ECG. Possible causes include anterior wall myocardial infarction and left anterior fascicular block.

media.title: Comparison of normal and poor R-wave progression
ECG with right ventricular load in pulmonary embolism (2/2)

2oYTYJ.title: Persistent S wave
2oYTYJ.description: The presence of an S wave in all of the precordial leads (V₁-V₆) on an ECG. Normally, the S wave amplitude decreases from V₁ to V₆ and is often not visible in V₅ and V₆. Causes of a persistent S wave include right heart strain (e.g., due to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and left anterior fascicular blocks.

ToY6YJ.title: QT interval
ToY6YJ.description: The duration between the beginning of the Q wave and the end of the T wave on an ECG that normally lasts < 350–440 ms. Represents ventricular depolarization and repolarization.

goYFYJ.title: Prolonged QT interval
goYFYJ.description: An ECG finding in which the QT interval corrected for heart rate (QTc) is > 440 ms in men and > 460 ms in women. (QTc = QT interval/√RR interval in seconds). Causes include congenital defects in the membrane ion channels of the heart, electrolyte imbalances (e.g., hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia), and medication toxicity. It increases the risk of torsades de pointes.

hoYcbJ.title: Shortening of the QT interval
hoYcbJ.description: A shortened duration of intraventricular depolarization or repolarization. Etiologies include hypercalcemia, hyperkalemia, digoxin, and increased sympathetic tone (e.g., due to hyperthyroidism or fever).

QoYubJ.title: Sokolow-Lyon criteria
QoYubJ.description:
Criteria used to diagnose myocardial hypertrophy based on certain amplitude changes of the ECG:
Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH): SV1 or 2 + RV5 or 6 ≥ 3.5 mV
Right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH): RV1 or 2 + SV5 or 6 ≥ 1.05 mV

OoYIXJ.title: Patent foramen ovale
OoYIXJ.description: A variant of cardiac anatomy in which the foramen ovale remains patent beyond 1 year of age. Estimated to be present (but undiagnosed) in 25-30% of the population. Usually asymptomatic and does not require treatment. Can cause paradoxical embolism, in which case antiplatelet or anticoagulation therapy, and/or surgical closure may be considered.

destinations.label: Acyanotic congenital heart defects → Patent foramen ovale (PFO)

loYvXJ.title: Cough reflex
loYvXJ.description: A brainstem reflex elicited by irritation of the larynx or respiratory epithelium. In a positive test, the patient coughs. The reflex is mediated by the afferent sensory and efferent motor pathways of CN X.

NoY-XJ.title: Thoracic duct
NoY-XJ.description: The largest lymphatic channel in the body. Drains the lower limbs, pelvis, abdomen, left side of the thorax, left upper limb, and left side of the head and neck. Originates from the cysterna chyli (below the diaphragm), passes through the aortic hiatus, lies in the posterior mediastinum, and terminates by draining into the junction of the left subclavian and internal jugular veins.

qoYC1J.title: Metformin
qoYC1J.description: An antidiabetic biguanide drug used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus. It reduces liver production of glucose, increases insulin sensitivity, and induces weight loss.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

IoYYWJ.title: Sulfonylureas
IoYYWJ.description: A class of oral antidiabetic drugs that inhibits ATP-sensitive potassium channels in the pancreatic β-cell membrane, which leads to depolarization and increased insulin release. Adverse effects include weight gain, disulfiram-like effects (particularly in first-generation drugs), hypoglycemia (particularly in second-generation drugs), and nephrotoxicity. Examples include glyburide, glipizide, and glimepiride.

roYfWJ.title: Glyburide
roYfWJ.description: A sulfonylurea that is used for glycemic control in patients with diabetes mellitus. More strongly associated with hypoglycemia than other sulfonylureas.

7oY4WJ.title: Glimepiride
7oY4WJ.description: A sulfonylurea drug that stimulates insulin release from pancreatic beta cells. It is used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

soYtWJ.title: Glitazone
soYtWJ.description: A group of medications used for glycemic control in diabetic patients (e.g., pioglitazone, rosiglitazone). They reduce insulin resistance in peripheral tissues by stimulating the gamma subtype of peroxisome proliferator activated receptors (PPAR). Adverse effects include weight gain, peripheral edema, heart failure, and osteoporosis.

GoYBWJ.title: Pioglitazone
GoYBWJ.description: A PPAR-γ agonist used for glycemic control in patients with diabetes.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

toYXdJ.title: Rosiglitazone
toYXdJ.description: A PPAR-γ agonist used for glycemic control in patients with diabetes.

8oYOdJ.title: Meglitinides
8oYOdJ.description: A class of oral antidiabetic drugs with the same mechanism of action and adverse effects as sulfonylureas. They inhibit ATP-sensitive potassium channels in the beta cell membrane, leading to depolarization and increased insulin release. Adverse effects consists of weight gain and hypoglycemia, as well as renal failure. Examples include mitiglinide and repaglinide.

uoYpdJ.title: Repaglinide
uoYpdJ.description: An oral antidiabetic drug of the meglitinide class. Causes closure of ATP-sensitive potassium channels in the beta cell membrane, which leads to depolarization, increases calcium concentration in the cell, and release of insulin. Adverse effects include hypoglycemia, weight gain, and renal failure.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

EoY8dJ.title: Incretin mimetic drugs
EoY8dJ.description: A class of medications that stimulate glucagon-like-peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors, resulting in insulin secretion from beta cells of the pancreas, decreased glucagon levels, and slowed gastric emptying in response to food intake. Includes semaglutide, liraglutide, exenatide, and dulaglutide. Used to treat type 2 diabetes, obesity, and overweight with weight-related complications.

destinations.label: Diabetes medications → Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (incretin mimetics)

DoY1VJ.title: GLP-1
DoY1VJ.description: An incretin secreted by intestinal cells and certain solitary tract neurons that promotes glucose-dependent insulin secretion. Degraded by DPP-4.

destinations.label: Diabetes medications → Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (incretin mimetics)

9oYNVJ.title: Exenatide
9oYNVJ.description: A glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist used in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

destinations.label: Diabetes medications → Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (incretin mimetics)

CoYqVJ.title: Dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors
CoYqVJ.description: A class of antidiabetic medications that inhibit dipeptidyl peptidase-4, which breaks down glucagon-like peptide 1 (incretin). DPP-4 inhibitors (e.g., sitagliptin, saxagliptin) are not associated with increased risk of hypoglycemia but can cause gastrointestinal adverse effects.

xoYEVJ.title: Sitagliptin
xoYEVJ.description: A DPP-4 inhibitor used for glycemic control in patients with diabetes.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

BoYzVJ.title: Vildagliptin
BoYzVJ.description: A dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus. Not commercially available in the United States.

AoYReJ.title: Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors
AoYReJ.description: A class of medications (e.g., acarbose, miglitol, voglibose) that decrease intestinal glucose absorption by inhibiting alpha-glucosidase, an enzyme that breaks down starch and disaccharides into monosaccharides. Used to control postprandial hyperglycemia in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Adverse effects include flatulence, abdominal discomfort, and diarrhea.

_oY5eJ.title: Acarbose
_oY5eJ.description: An alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, which is used for glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

zoYreJ.title: SGLT-2 inhibitors
zoYreJ.description: A class of drugs that cause reversible inhibition of the sodium-dependent glucose transporter (SGLT-2) in the proximal convoluted tubule of the nephron, which results in polyuria and glycosuria. Examples include dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and canagliflozin.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

-oYDeJ.title: Dapagliflozin
-oYDeJ.description: A sodium-dependent glucose transporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT-2 inhibitors; gliflozin), which acts at the proximal tubule of the nephron to reduce glucose reabsorption. Dapagliflozin is used for glycemic control in diabetic patients.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

aKYQUJ.title: Doxazosin
aKYQUJ.description: A peripheral alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist used in the treatment of urinary retention due to overactive  sphincter and/or benign prostatic hyperplasia.

bKYHUJ.title: Prazosin
bKYHUJ.description: A selective α-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist that causes smooth muscle relaxation (vasodilation, prostatic urethral relaxation). Used to treat hypertension, Raynaud phenomenon, and benign prostatic hyperplasia with urinary obstruction. Some guidelines also recommend prazosin for sleeping disorders associated with PTSD. Adverse effects include orthostatic hypotension, fainting, and priapism.

XKY9UJ.title: Terazosin
XKY9UJ.description: α-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist that causes smooth muscle relaxation (vasodilation, prostatic urethral relaxation). Used to treat hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia with urinary obstruction.

1KY22J.title: Tamsulosin
1KY22J.description: An antagonist on adrenergic alpha-1 receptors, mainly used in the treatment of benign prostatic hyperplasia.

WKYP2J.title: Alfuzosin
WKYP2J.description: An α1-receptor antagonist used to treat benign prostatic hyperplasia. Blockage of the α1-receptor leads to relaxation of prostate and bladder neck muscles, which facilitates urination. Common adverse effects include postural hypotension, urinary tract infections, headache, and fatigue.

hKYcTJ.title: Uroflowmetry
hKYcTJ.description: An objective, noninvasive test used in the evaluation of patients with suspected bladder outlet obstruction (i.e., hesitancy, frequency, poor stream, terminal dribbling, straining to micturate) or detrusor overactivity (urinary frequency). It records urinary voiding time, average and maximum flow rate, time to maximum flow rate, and the total voided volume of urine. A continuous, single bell-shaped curve with urine volume >200 mL (over 15–30 seconds) and at a rate >15 mL/sec is normal.

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Urodynamic studies

RKYlTJ.title: Sunburn
RKYlTJ.description: An acute, self-limited inflammatory skin reaction caused by excessive exposure to ultraviolet radiation. Both UVA and UVB radiation affect the dermis, but erythema is predominantly caused by UVB radiation.

kKYmgJ.title: Ovarian torsion
kKYmgJ.description: A gynecologic emergency caused by partial or complete twisting of the ovary and the fallopian tube around their supporting ligaments. Can result in compression of the ovarian vessels and lymphatics, edema of the fallopian tube and ovary, and subsequent ischemia and necrosis. Manifestations include sudden-onset, unilateral pelvic pain, nausea, and vomiting.

NKY-gJ.title: Bifascicular block
NKY-gJ.description: An umbrella term for the blockade of two fascicles (intraventricular conduction pathways) of the heart. There are three fascicles: the right bundle branch and the left anterior and left posterior fascicles (the latter two of which comprise the left bundle branch.

MKYMSJ.title: ST elevation
MKYMSJ.description: An elevation of the ST segment above the isoelectric line. Considered significant if it is ≥ 0.1 mV in a limb lead or ≥ 0.2 mV in a precordial lead. Myocardial ischemia causes significant elevations in anatomically localized leads. Pericarditis causes diffuse ST elevations.

nKY7SJ.title: ST depression
nKY7SJ.description: A depression of the ST segment below the isoelectric line. Significant depressions in anatomically localized leads suggest myocardial ischemia without progression to full thickness infarction. Seen in unstable angina and non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI).

6KYjhJ.title: T-wave inversion
6KYjhJ.description: A deflection of the T wave in the opposite direction of the QRS complex that precedes it. Differential diagnosis is broad and ranges from normal to life-threatening (e.g., cardiac ischemia). TWI in lead III is a normal variant. A new T-wave inversion (compared to prior ECGs) is always abnormal. Pathological TWIs are usually symmetric and > 3 mm in amplitude.

rKYf3J.title: Precordial leads
rKYf3J.description: The ECG leads placed directly over the heart, encircling the precordium. On a 12-lead ECG, these are leads V1–V6.

7KY43J.title: Brugada syndrome
7KY43J.description: An inherited arrhythmia syndrome characterized by a repolarization abnormality in cardiac myocytes that can lead to sudden cardiac death. Characteristic ECG findings include persisting ST-segment elevations and T wave changes in leads V₁–V₂ (Brugada pattern) and an rSr' complex in leads V₁–V₂ (pseudo right bundle branch block).

destinations.label: Management of tachycardia → Stable wide-complex tachycardia

HKYK3J.title: Applanation tonometry
HKYK3J.description: A test that can be used to infer the intraocular pressure by measuring the amount of force needed to temporarily flatten part of the cornea.

tKYXRJ.title: Pemphigoid gestationis
tKYXRJ.description: A vesiculobullous disorder that most commonly occurs during the third trimester of pregnancy or in the postpartum period. Manifests with pruritic, urticarial, vesiculating papules and plaques and commonly involves the periumbilical skin. Associated with autoantibodies against BP180. Can affect newborns via placental transfer of autoantibodies.

destinations.label: Maternal complications during pregnancy → Pregnancy dermatoses

8KYORJ.title: Nonclassic CAH
8KYORJ.description: A form of CAH that is milder than classic CAH and may only involve decreased cortisol levels. Usually unidentified on infant blood screening; often becomes evident in late childhood or early adulthood. Symptoms in females include irregular or absent menses, masculine characteristics, and severe acne. In both men and women, symptoms include early appearance of pubic hair and rapid growth during childhood.

uKYpRJ.title: Jaw-thrust maneuver
uKYpRJ.description: A maneuver used to facilitate bag-mask ventilation in patients with suspected spinal injury. Involves opening the upper airway without extending the neck. With the patient supine, the person performing the maneuver places their fingers behind the angles of the lower jaw and moves the jaw upward while using the thumbs to open the mouth slightly.

destinations.label: Airway management → Initial airway opening maneuvers

EKY8RJ.title: EC-clamp technique
EKY8RJ.description: A technique used to create a tight seal between the mask and the patient's face during bag-mask ventilation. With the patient supine, the person performing the technique uses the little, ring, and middle finger of one hand (the "E") to lift the jaw toward the mask while using the thumb and index finger to squeeze the mask onto the face (the "C").

vKYARJ.title: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
vKYARJ.description: Heart failure with reduced stroke volume and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF ≤ 40%)

DKY1iJ.title: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
DKY1iJ.description: Heart failure with reduced stroke volume and preserved LVEF (≥ 50%), plus evidence of increased LV filling pressures, e.g., increased natriuretic peptides and hemodynamic measurements.

media.title: Pressure-volume loop in diastolic heart failure

wKYhiJ.title: Recovery position
wKYhiJ.description: A position used to protect the airway of an unconscious patient without suspected spinal injury. Patients are placed in a lateral decubitus position with slight neck extension and their extremities are arranged to stabilize them and prevent rolling into a supine or prone position.

destinations.label: Airway management → Initial airway opening maneuvers

xKYEiJ.title: Nonseminoma
xKYEiJ.description: A group of aggressive, radioresistant germ cell tumors that includes the following histological variants: embryonal carcinoma, teratoma, choriocarcinoma, yolk sac tumors, and mixed germ cell tumors. Commonly found in the testes but can occur in almost any location.

zKYrQJ.title: Peptic ulcer perforation
zKYrQJ.description: The erosion of a peptic ulcer through the full thickness of the bowel wall. Anterior duodenal ulcers are most likely to perforate. Manifests with acute peritonitis seen as pneumoperitoneum on imaging and requires surgical intervention.

U6Yb4J.title: Livedo reticularis
U6Yb4J.description: A reddish-blue discoloration of the skin in a reticular (net-like) pattern. Thought to be due to blood vessel spasm. Can be a normal finding, drug reaction (e.g., amantadine), or indication of underlying systemic disease (e.g., polyarteritis nodosa, SLE).

destinations.label: Collection of dermatological disorders → Livedo reticularis

T6Y64J.title: Malignant hypertension
T6Y64J.description: Terms traditionally used to describe hypertension with concomitant retinopathy and later expanded to include damage to other target organs (e.g., kidney, heart, and brain). The term hypertensive emergency is currently preferred.

36YSkJ.title: Oligoclonal bands
36YSkJ.description: Characteristic bands representing IgG subfractions on electrophoresis or isoelectric focusing of CSF. They signify increased production of multiple, nonspecific clones of IgG within the CNS due to intrathecal inflammation. Detectable in most patients with multiple sclerosis but also seen in other inflammatory, infectious, and neurodegenerative conditions.

K6YUNJ.title: McMurray test
K6YUNJ.description: A physical examination maneuver used to assess for meniscal tear. With the patient supine, the examiner holds the knee in one hand and the ankle in the other hand and brings the knee to full flexion. The examiner extends the knee while applying external rotation (to test for medial meniscal tear) or internal rotation (to test for lateral meniscal tear). The test is positive if pain, popping, and/or clicking occur.

v6YA5J.title: Medial meniscus
v6YA5J.description: A crescent-shaped pad of fibrocartilage in the medial knee between the tibial plateau and the medial femoral condyle. Aids in dissipating loading forces, stabilizing during rotation, and lubricating the knee joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The knee joint

media.title: Microscopic anatomy and biomechanics of the knee menisci
Macroscopic anatomy of the knee menisci

D6Y1MJ.title: Lateral meniscus
D6Y1MJ.description: A circular pad of fibrocartilage in the lateral knee between the tibial plateau and the lateral femoral condyle. Aids in dissipating loading forces, stabilizing during rotation, and lubricating the knee joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The knee joint

x6YEMJ.title: Genu recurvatum
x6YEMJ.description: A knee joint deformity characterized by hyperextension of the tibiofemoral joint. Can be congenital (e.g., due to connective tissue disorders, muscular dystrophy) or acquired (e.g., as a complication of poliomyelitis, osteomyelitis, Osgood-Schlatter disease). Complications include knee pain and gait disturbances.

A6YRnJ.title: Central scotoma
A6YRnJ.description: A loss of vision in the center of an eye's visual field. Typically caused by lesions that affect the macula (e.g., macular degeneration, macular edema).

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Scotoma and anopia

bpYHLJ.title: BEP
bpYHLJ.description: A chemotherapy regimen used to treat malignant ovarian and testicular germ cell tumors. Consists of bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin (platinum).

cpYaoJ.title: Maceration

1pY2oJ.title: Phenotype
1pY2oJ.description: The observable morphological, physical, biochemical, and/or behavioral characteristics of an organism that are determined by the genotype (genetic makeup). Often influenced by environmental factors.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

WpYPoJ.title: Genotype
WpYPoJ.description: The genetic composition of an individual. Manifests in a specific environment as certain observable traits (phenotype).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

epYxoJ.title: Nullipara
epYxoJ.description: A woman who has never carried a pregnancy beyond the point of viability (i.e., 20 weeks of gestation).

UpYbKJ.title: Primipara
UpYbKJ.description: A woman who has carried one pregnancy beyond the point of viability (i.e., 20 weeks of gestation), regardless of whether the fetus was alive at birth.

2pYTKJ.title: Freckles
2pYTKJ.description: A form of hyperpigmentation that typically occurs during childhood after UV exposure. Manifests as small red, brown, or tan macules with equal distribution in sun-exposed areas.

TpY6KJ.title: Left shift
TpY6KJ.description:
1. An increase in the number of immature neutrophils (banded neutrophils, metamyelocytes). Commonly occurs as a reaction to infection and/or inflammation because polymorphonuclear leukocytes are released into the circulation before they are fully mature in order to meet the increased demand.
2. A shift in a 2-D plot to the left side. For example, a shift of the hemoglobin dissociation curve to the left (due to ↓ temperature, ↓ 2,3-diphosphoglycerate, ↓ pCO₂ and/or ↑ pH), resulting in an increased affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen.

QpYu6J.title: Imbibierung
QpYu6J.description: The absorption of fluid by a colloid or a gel, which results in swelling of the colloidal medium.

OpYIpJ.title: Amitriptyline
OpYIpJ.description: A tricyclic antidepressant used for psychiatric illnesses such as depression, anxiety disorder, and bipolar disorder, as well as for the prophylaxis of tension headaches and migraines. While the exact mechanism of action remains unclear, it is assumed that the agent works through nonselective presynaptic reuptake inhibition of monoamines.

lpYvpJ.title: Trimipramine
lpYvpJ.description: A tricyclic antidepressant primarily used to treat depression but also used to treat insomnia and anxiety disorders.

NpY-pJ.title: Doxepin
NpY-pJ.description: A tricyclic antidepressant used in the treatment of many conditions, including major depressive disorder, diabetic neuropathy, chronic pain, insomnia, and anxiety. Has the strongest antihistaminic effect among tricyclic antidepressants and thus is useful (in topical formulation) for the treatment of pruritus.

mpYVJJ.title: Desipramine
mpYVJJ.description: A tricyclic antidepressant primarily used to treat major depressive disorder. Adverse effects include orthostatic hypotension, anticholinergic effects, and sedation.

5pYiJJ.title: Nortriptyline
5pYiJJ.description: A tricyclic antidepressant used to treat depression, anxiety, neuropathy (e.g., diabetic neuropathy), and chronic pain (e.g., fibromyalgia) as well as for the prophylaxis of migraines. Inhibits the reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine in the synaptic cleft.

MpYMJJ.title: Imipramine
MpYMJJ.description: A tertiary amine tricyclic antidepressant that is thought to increase synaptic concentrations of serotonin and norepinephrine in the central nervous system. Used to treat childhood enuresis, major depressive disorder, neuropathic pain, and panic disorders.

npY7JJ.title: Clomipramine
npY7JJ.description: A tricyclic antidepressant that is used to treat obsessive compulsive disorder and major depressive disorder. Clomipramine has more selective serotonergic activity than other tricyclic antidepressants.

6pYjqJ.title: Enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma
6pYjqJ.description: A rare lymphoma derived from aberrant enteral T lymphocytes that most commonly manifests in the proximal jejunum. Initially asymptomatic then causes B symptoms and gastrointestinal symptoms. Associated with celiac disease in about 80% of patients.

JpYsqJ.title: 5-alpha-reductase deficiency
JpYsqJ.description: A rare, autosomal recessive disease caused by a loss-of-function mutation of the SRD5A2 gene on chromosome 2, which results in an inability to convert testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Karyotypically male individuals (46, XY) usually manifest with ambiguous or female genitalia at birth due to a lack of DHT-dependent genital tubercle virilization. Karyotypically female individuals are asymptomatic.

GpYBIJ.title: Pyonephrosis
GpYBIJ.description: A pyogenic urinary tract infection that develops proximal to an obstructed and dilated urinary tract. Most commonly involves the renal pelvis and collecting ducts.

ypYdHJ.title: Giant hypertrophic gastritis
ypYdHJ.description: A type of gastritis characterized by enlargement of the mucosal folds (rugae) due to hyperplasia of the gastric mucosa. Causes excess mucus production, protein loss, and parietal cell atrophy with decreased acid production. Manifestations include epigastric pain, anorexia, weight loss, vomiting, and edema secondary to protein loss.

_pY5HJ.title: Acrophobia
_pY5HJ.description: A persistent and intense fear of heights.

-pYDHJ.title: Arachnophobia
-pYDHJ.description: A persistent and intense fear of spiders. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

ZJYZsJ.title: Hematophobia
ZJYZsJ.description: A persistent and intense fear of blood. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

2JYTtJ.title: Influenza vaccine
2JYTtJ.description: A vaccine against the influenza virus that in its injectable form contains two strains of inactivated influenza A virus (H1N1 and H3N2), and one or two lineages of the influenza B virus, depending on whether the vaccine is quadrivalent or trivalent. A live, attenuated, nasal spray vaccine is also available. Recommended during the flu season, typically between October and April (in the northern hemisphere), for all individuals older than 6 months.

TJY6tJ.title: Cutaneous horn
TJY6tJ.description: A benign skin growth composed of keratin that resembles a horn and may develop from preexisting actinic and seborrheic keratoses or warts. Rarely, cutaneous horns progress to squamous cell carcinoma.

QJYuFJ.title: Antiphospholipid antibodies
QJYuFJ.description: A group of antibodies (e.g., lupus anticoagulant, anti-cardiolipin, anti-β2-glycoprotein) that bind to plasma proteins with an affinity for phospholipid surfaces. Their presence may be associated with an increased risk of arterial and venous thrombosis, although they are also seen in asymptomatic patients.

jJY_FJ.title: Cephalexin
jJY_FJ.description: First-generation cephalosporin that is administered orally and is effective against many gram-positive bacteria, as well as a few gram-negative bacteria such as Proteus, E. coli, and Klebsiella.

4JY38J.title: Fourth generation cephalosporins
4JY38J.description: A class of the antibiotic cephalosporin that includes cefepime. They are active against gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas, but ineffective against Enterococcus, Listeria, MRSA, and atypical bacteria.

kJYm8J.title: Fifth generation cephalosporins
kJYm8J.description: A class of the antibiotic cephalosporin that includes ceftaroline. They are active against gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, including Enterococcus faecalis, Listeria, and MRSA, but ineffective against Pseudomonas and atypical bacteria.

OJYI8J.title: Cefepime
OJYI8J.description: A fourth-generation cephalosporin with a broad spectrum of activity against both gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas.

lJYv8J.title: Ceftaroline
lJYv8J.description: A fifth-generation cephalosporin that is active against organisms such as Listeria, MRSA, and Enterococcus faecalis (which are not covered by first to fourth-generation cephalosporins). Lacks antipseudomonal activity.

KJYUEJ.title: Pyostomatitis vegetans
KJYUEJ.description: A rare oral condition strongly associated with inflammatory bowel disease (especially ulcerative colitis). Manifests with slightly elevated, yellow-white, round mucosal lesions with a characteristic snail-track appearance. Most commonly affects the labial and buccal mucosae, gingivae, and palate.

6JYjEJ.title: Magnetic resonance enterography
6JYjEJ.description: An imaging technique that evaluates the small bowel with high contrast resolution. An MRI abdomen is performed following the ingestion of osmotic contrast material. The distention of the small bowel by the contrast facilitates a detailed evaluation of the intestinal wall. Commonly used in the evaluation of Crohn disease.

JJYsEJ.title: Ulcerative jejunitis
JJYsEJ.description: A rare complication of celiac disease characterized by multiple chronic ulcers in the jejunum. Can cause malabsorption, anorexia, weight loss, and abdominal pain. Typically associated with a poor prognosis and often does not improve with a gluten-free diet.

9JYNwJ.title: Chondrocyte
9JYNwJ.description: A cell that produces and maintains cartilage.

CJYqwJ.title: Chondroblast
CJYqwJ.description: Mesenchymal progenitor cells found in cartilage that secrete the extracellular matrix. Can form chondrocytes when trapped in the matrix.

xJYEwJ.title: Perichondrium
xJYEwJ.description: A fibrous layer of connective tissue the surrounds, nourishes, and regenerates cartilage (with the exceptions of articular cartilage and fibrocartilage).

AJYR9J.title: Osteoblasts
AJYR9J.description: The cells of the bone that promote the development of new bone matrix during the bone remodeling process.

0qYeCJ.title: Diabetic cardiomyopathy
0qYeCJ.description: A disorder of the myocardium seen in diabetic patients. Chronic hyperglycemia results in altered metabolism of glucose and fatty acids, microangiopathy with endothelial dysfunction, and autonomic neuropathy, which collectively results in cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, myocardial fibrosis, ventricular dilation, and ultimately in systolic and/or diastolic heart failure. This disorder may or may not be accompanied by CVD and hypertension.

aqYQCJ.title: Hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism
aqYQCJ.description: Hypoaldosteronism that is caused by decreased renin activity. Most commonly caused by diabetic nephropathy or chronic interstitial nephritis, but may also occur due to drugs that directly or indirectly inhibit renin synthesis in the juxtaglomerular apparatus (e.g., NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, heparin, cyclosporin). Patients present with features of hypoaldosteronism, i.e., hypotension, hyponatremia, and type 4 renal tubular acidosis.

YqYnCJ.title: Epiphyseal plate
YqYnCJ.description: The cartilage at the end of long bones where new bone growth takes place. Closes at the end of puberty.

KqYUzJ.title: Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
KqYUzJ.description: Segmental or generalized infarction of the anterior part of the optic nerve. Most cases are idiopathic but can also be caused by giant cell arteritis. Typically manifests with abrupt-onset progressive monocular vision loss and edema of the optic disc.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (AION)

media.title: Papilledema in non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION)

pqYLzJ.title: Hypocalcemia
pqYLzJ.description: A serum calcium concentration < 8.5 mg/dL (< 2.12 mmol/L) or ionized/free calcium concentration < 4.65 mg/dL (< 1.16 mmol/L). Etiologies include hypoparathyroidism, parathyroid hormone resistance, vitamin D deficiency, and loop diuretic use. Manifestations include tetany, paresthesias, muscle spasms, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias, and gastrointestinal symptoms.

JqYszJ.title: Hypercalcemia
JqYszJ.description: A serum calcium concentration > 10.5 mg/dL (> 2.62 mmol/L) or ionized (free) calcium concentration > 5.25 mg/dL (> 1.31 mmol/L). Etiologies include excess parathyroid hormone, granulomatous disorders (e.g., sarcoidosis), thiazide diuretic use, and bone remodeling/demineralization. Manifestations include nephrolithiasis, bone pain, constipation, neuropsychiatric symptoms (e.g., anxiety), cardiac arrhythmias, and muscle weakness.

rqYf-J.title: Radius (bone)
rqYf-J.description: A long bone of the forearm located parallel to the ulna and found laterally when in anatomical position. The proximal end articulates with the distal humerus to form the elbow joint. The distal end articulates with the scaphoid and lunate carpal bones.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

GqYB-J.title: Tunica intima
GqYB-J.description: The innermost layer of an artery or vein. Consists of a layer of endothelial cells supported by an elastic lamina.

tqYXZq.title: Tunica media
tqYXZq.description: The middle layer of a blood vessel that is composed predominantly of concentrically arranged smooth muscles with variable amounts of collagen and elastin fibers. The tunica media is prominent in arteries and relatively thin in veins.

FqYgZq.title: Tunica adventitia
FqYgZq.description: The outermost layer of a blood vessel, composed predominantly of connective tissue.

EqY8Zq.title: Biceps brachii muscle
EqY8Zq.description: A muscle in the ventral compartment of the arm. Originates from the coracoid process and supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula. Inserts into the radial tuberosity of the radius and bicipital aponeurosis in the forearm. Innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve. Flexes the arm and forearm; supinates of the forearm.

DqY10q.title: Triceps brachii muscle
DqY10q.description: A muscle in the posterior compartment of the arm that is made up of a long head originating from the infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula, a lateral head originating from the proximal humerus, and a medial head originating from the distal humerus. All three heads insert into the olecranon. The triceps is innervated by the radial nerve and is responsible for extension of the forearm.

cIYabq.title: Spine of scapula
cIYabq.description: A horizontal bony ridge located on the posterior surface of the scapula. Divides the scapular surface into the small supraspinous and larger infraspinous fossae. The spine forms the acromion process laterally.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

1IY2bq.title: Interclavicular ligament
1IY2bq.description: A ligament that unites the sternal ends of the clavicles and attaches to the superior border of the manubrium. Strengthens the sternoclavicular joint capsule superiorly.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

media.title: Bones and ligaments of the sternoclavicular and sternocostal joints

WIYPbq.title: Costoclavicular ligament
WIYPbq.description: A ligament that connects the first rib to the sternal end of the clavicle. Limits elevation of the shoulder (pectoral) girdle.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

media.title: Bones and ligaments of the sternoclavicular and sternocostal joints

VIYGbq.title: Glutathione
VIYGbq.description: An antioxidant that cycles between a reduced (GSH) and an oxidized form (GSSG). The reduced form serves as a protective agent against hydrogen peroxide and organic peroxides, which is especially important in erythrocytes (see glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency). The enzyme glutathione reductase uses NADPH as an electron source to regenerate reduced glutathione from its oxidized form.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Pentose phosphate pathway

UIYbXq.title: Ankyrin
UIYbXq.description: A membrane protein that connects the lipid bilayer and the membrane cytoskeleton. Defects in ankyrin are implicated in the pathogenesis of hereditary spherocytosis.

TIY6Xq.title: Differential time to positivity
TIY6Xq.description: Differential time to positivity = [Time taken for a blood culture from a peripheral vein to become positive] - [Time taken for a blood culture from an intravascular catheter to become positive]. Growth of organisms from the catheter sample at least 120 minutes before growth of organisms from the peripheral vein sample indicates a positive DTP and suggests a catheter-related bloodstream infection.

MIYMWq.title: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
MIYMWq.description: A spinal deformity characterized by lateral deflection and rotation of the vertebral bodies. Manifests between 10-18 years of age and is more common in girls. Usually asymptomatic in early stages, but more advanced disease may cause pain, functional impairment, and in severe cases, pulmonary disorders.

LIYwWq.title: Nontunneled catheter
LIYwWq.description: A type of central venous catheter in which the catheter passes directly through the skin into a vessel. They can be placed rapidly and therefore are the preferred modality if urgent access is required. Compared to tunneled catheters, they have a higher infection risk and use is typically limited to < 2–4 weeks.

oIY0dq.title: Venous catheter for renal replacement therapy
oIY0dq.description: A large-bore central line with multiple lumens used for short-term renal replacement therapy (e.g., hemodialysis, hemofiltration). May be tunneled or nontunneled.

destinations.label: Renal replacement therapy → Hemodialysis and hemofiltration

uIYpeq.title: Tranexamic acid
uIYpeq.description: A synthetic lysine analog and inhibitor of plasminogen with antifibrinolytic action. Indicated in the treatment of excessive blood loss from major trauma, menorrhagia, acute AUB, postpartum bleeding, surgery, dental procedures, and epistaxis. Adverse effects include changes in color vision, thromboembolic events, and anaphylaxis.

vIYAeq.title: Pus
vIYAeq.description: A whitish-yellow exudate that contains proteins, leukocytes (esp. neutrophils), bacteria, and cellular debris. Pus formation (suppuration) is usually the result of infection by pyogenic bacteria such as streptococci, staphylococci, or gonococci. Certain noninfectious conditions can also result in pus formation (e.g., pustular psoriasis).

destinations.label: Skin and soft tissue infections → Purulent SSTIs

DIY1Uq.title: Air embolism
DIY1Uq.description: The obstruction of a blood vessel by an air bubble. Etiologies include surgical procedures that involve the head, neck, and/or thorax (e.g., cardiopulmonary bypass), intravenous injections, penetrating lung injuries, and decompression sickness.

9IYNUq.title: Sex determining region of Y
9IYNUq.description: A region of the Y chromosome gene that encodes for the SRY protein (also known as testis-determining factor, or TDF), which is a transcription factor that suppresses ovarian development and regulates male sex determination at around 6 weeks of gestation.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Gonadal sex differentiation

BIYzUq.title: Ejection click
BIYzUq.description: A crisp, high-frequency, early-systolic sound that is caused either by the stretching of the aortic root or the pulmonary artery or by the opening of a stiff aortic or pulmonary valve. An ejection click can be heard on auscultation in patients with aortic stenosis, pulmonary stenosis, and/or pulmonary hypertension.

media.title: Heart murmur in aortic and pulmonary stenosis

crYaTq.title: lusitropic
crYaTq.description: The ability to influence the rate of relaxation of cardiac muscle (lusitropy). Positively lusitropic substances (e.g., catecholamines) increase the rate of relaxation of cardiac muscle.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Regulation of cardiac activity

1rY2Tq.title: Anastomosis
1rY2Tq.description: A connection between two luminal structures. Can be physiologic (e.g., in the Circle of Willis in the brain), pathologic (e.g., fistulas), or introduced surgically to restore continuity (e.g., to reconnect bowel after surgical resection).

WrYPTq.title: Gyrus
WrYPTq.description: A convolution or rounded ridge on the surface of a cerebral hemisphere. The grooves between gyri are called sulci.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

drYoTq.title: β-lactamase inhibitor
drYoTq.description: A class of antibiotics that inhibit the bacterial enzyme beta-lactamase and therefore prevent the inactivation of β-lactam antibiotics (e.g., penicillins, carbapenems, cephalosporins). Have insignificant antibacterial activity when used alone. Examples include tazobactam, clavulanic acid, and sulbactam.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Beta-lactam antibiotics

VrYGTq.title: Vestibular migraine
VrYGTq.description: A condition characterized by spontaneous episodic vertigo in a patient with migraines. The vertigo is often accompanied by nystagmus and aural symptoms (e.g., tinnitus, phonophobia). Headaches may be absent during the vertigo attacks. Hearing is preserved, which differentiates vestibular migraine from Ménière disease.

hrYcSq.title: Thyroid cyst
hrYcSq.description: A thyroid nodule caused by cystic degeneration of thyroid tissue, involution of a follicular adenoma, or thyroid cancer. Further classified into simple (fluid-filled, benign) and complex (partly solid, 5–10% risk of malignancy). Hemorrhage into a cyst can cause pain and rapid enlargement of the nodule that causes compression symptoms (e.g., hoarseness, dysphagia). Management includes ultrasonography, fine needle aspiration, surgery, and potential treatment for thyroid cancer.

MrYM3q.title: Hashimoto encephalopathy
MrYM3q.description: A rare neurological syndrome associated with high anti-TPO or anti-Tg antibody titers. Symptoms vary widely and may include impairment of cognitive function and vigilance, myoclonus, seizures, or psychosis. Patients usually respond to glucocorticoid therapy.

yrYdPq.title: Arterial blood gas analysis
yrYdPq.description: A laboratory test of arterial blood that measures oxygen saturation (saO₂), bicarbonate blood levels (HCO₃⁻), and partial pressure of both oxygen (paO₂) and carbon dioxide (paCO₂). Can be used to assess the gas-exchange process and acid-base balance.

media.title: Arterial blood for arterial blood gas analysis
Radial artery puncture with arterial blood gas (ABG) sampling

zrYrPq.title: Retained placenta
zrYrPq.description: The lack of expulsion of the placenta within 30 minutes of delivery. Can be caused by the improper separation of the placenta from the uterine wall (placenta accreta spectrum) or trapping of a separated placenta within the uterus.  Complications include postpartum hemorrhage, postpartum endometritis, and uterine inversion.

Y7Yn4q.title: Biliary pancreatitis
Y7Yn4q.description: The most common type of acute pancreatitis in adults and children. Caused by a gallstone and/or biliary sludge that passes through the common bile duct and becomes impacted directly after the pancreatic duct, obstructing outflow of pancreatic enzymes and leading to inflammation.

b7YH4q.title: Endogenous
b7YH4q.description: A descriptor for a factor that originates from or is produced within an organ/organism (e.g., endogenous cortisol production).

X7Y94q.title: Exogenous
X7Y94q.description: A descriptor for a factor that originates from or is produced outside of an organ/organism (e.g., exogenous cortisol, exogenous risk factors).

T7Y6Oq.title: Corpora cavernosa
T7Y6Oq.description: Anatomic compartment located on each side of the dorsal penis. Originates at the base of the penis and terminates at the head of the glans penis. Contains spongy tissue with trabeculae, which fills with blood to form an erection.

media.title: Urethra, corpora cavernosa, and corpus spongiosus of the penis
Median section of the male pelvis with detail of a testicle

O7YINq.title: Acute alcohol intoxication
O7YINq.description: A condition caused by ethanol ingestion, which typically causes altered mental status, slurred speech, unsteady gait, and disinhibition. Ingestion of large amounts of alcohol can lead to coma, respiratory depression, and death.

m7YVmq.title: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes
m7YVmq.description: A global nonprofit organization that develops and implements evidence-based guidelines for the management of kidney disease.

57Yimq.title: RIFLE criteria for AKI
57Yimq.description: A classification system for acute kidney injury. The acronym stands for Risk, Injury, Failure, Loss, and End-stage kidney disease. For the first three categories, patients are classified according to the level of kidney injury (i.e., degree of increase in serum creatinine and/or decrease in GFR and urine output) and for the last two categories, according to the duration of complete loss of kidney function.

M7YMmq.title: Acute Kidney Injury Network stages
M7YMmq.description: A classification of acute kidney injury (AKI) severity used for clinical and epidemiologic studies. In the AKIN classification, AKI is defined as an increase in serum creatinine of ≥ 0.3 mg/dL or ≥ 50% within 48 hours. Stages are determined based on serum creatinine concentration, urine output, and need to initiate renal replacement therapy.

K7YU5q.title: Vertebroplasty
K7YU5q.description: A minimally invasive procedure used to stabilize and relieve pain from a vertebral body fracture. Involves percutaneous injection of bone cement into the vertebral body.

q7YC5q.title: Strongyloides stercoralis
q7YC5q.description: A nematode (roundworm) that causes strongyloidiasis. Larvae penetrate the host via the skin (most commonly the feet), migrate to the lungs and intestines, and are excreted in the feces.

I7YYMq.title: Strongyloidiasis
I7YYMq.description: A parasitic infection caused by the nematode (roundworm) Strongyloides stercoralis, which is endemic to warm, moist regions. Larvae penetrate the host via the skin (most commonly the feet) and migrate to the lungs and intestines via various routes. Symptoms may be absent, mild, or severe and include a pruritic serpiginous rash, cough, abdominal pain, and diarrhea.

t7YXnq.title: Allergic asthma
t7YXnq.description: A type of asthma triggered by allergens (e.g., pollen, dust mites, mold spores, pet allergens).

u7Ypnq.title: Nonallergic asthma
u7Ypnq.description: A phenotype of asthma that is not triggered by allergens. Common triggers include viral upper respiratory tract infections, cold air, medication (e.g., aspirin, NSAIDs, beta blockers), physical exertion, and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

97YNLq.title: Corpus luteum
97YNLq.description: A yellow structure within the ovary that is formed from the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation. The corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone and inhibin A, degenerates 8–12 days after ovulation in non-pregnant women. If fertilization occurs, the corpus luteum persists for at least 2 more months due to the effect of placental human chorionic gonadotropin. Hemorrhage within the corpus luteum can result in a luteal cyst.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Oogenesis and folliculogenesis

_7Y5oq.title: Starling equation
_7Y5oq.description:
A formula used to calculate the net flow of fluid over a semipermeable (capillary) membrane: 
J = K [(Pc-Pi) - σ(πc - πi)] 
(J = net fluid flow, K = capillary fluid permeability constant, Pc = capillary pressure, Pi = interstitial pressure, σ = capillary protein permeability constant, πc = capillary oncotic pressure, and πi = interstitial oncotic pressure)

cHYa6q.title: Mosaic
cHYa6q.description: A phenotype in which different cell populations have different karyotypes as a result of mitotic chromosomal translocation defects or genetic mutations that occur early in the germinal stage of embryogenesis. For example, if there is an error in one cell of the zygote after the first mitotic division, about half of the subsequent cells will also carry the mutation, while the other half will not. Unlike chimerism, in which different cell populations arise from different zygotes, all the cell populations in mosaicism emerge from the same zygote.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

mHYVIq.title: Triangular interval
mHYVIq.description: A triangular space that contains the radial nerve and the deep brachial artery. Bounded superiorly by the teres major, medially by the long head of the triceps, and laterally by the humeral shaft. The apex faces caudally.

media.title: Visual mnemonic: Axillary spaces and their borders

xHYEsq.title: Proteoglycans
xHYEsq.description: Proteins with numerous covalently linked GAG side chains. Proteoglycans have multiple functions, e.g., shock absorption and supportive function for cartilage.

_HY5Gq.title: Glycosaminoglycan
_HY5Gq.description: A polysaccharide formed by repeated disaccharides (e.g., amino sugars, uronic sugars, galactose). Associated with mucopolysaccharidoses, a group of metabolic disorders caused by excessive accumulation of polysaccharides.

asYQtq.title: Lactobacillus acidophilus
asYQtq.description: A gram-positive bacillus that is part of the normal flora of the gastrointestinal tract and vagina. Used in some probiotic preparations.

destinations.label: Diagnostic procedures in gynecology → Genital swabs

bsYHtq.title: Ovarian vein thrombosis
bsYHtq.description: A postpartum complication that typically occurs 3–5 days after birth. Often associated with endometritis. Caused by hypercoagulability during pregnancy, endothelial microlesions during labor, and slowed blood flow in the ovarian veins. Typically presents with right-sided abdominal pain with fever and headache. Management includes ultrasonography to confirm the diagnosis and administration of heparin.

dsYoFq.title: Splitting of the second heart sound
dsYoFq.description: An auscultatory finding in which the second heart sound, which normally consists of sounds created from the near-simultaneous closure of the aortic valve (A₂) and pulmonary valve (P₂), becomes distinctly split. Can by physiologic (e.g., during inspiration due to decreased intrathoracic pressure) or pathologic.

VsYGFq.title: S4 heart sound
VsYGFq.description: An extra heart sound (gallop) caused by a late diastolic contraction of the atria (an “atrial kick”) against a noncompliant ventricle. Compliance is reduced in old age or from any cause of ventricular hypertrophy (hypertension, aortic stenosis, HCM). Also occurs in acute MI. An S4 is heard immediately before S1, initiating a cadence that resembles that of the word “Ten-nes-see," with the syllables corresponding to the heart sounds S4-S1-S2.

media.title: S4 Heart Sound (S4 Gallop) - Heart Auscultation - Episode 10

jsY_uq.title: Oscillopsia
jsY_uq.description: A visual disturbance in which stationary objects appear to oscillate. Usually associated with nystagmus and/or impaired vestibulo-ocular reflex. Bilateral vestibular lesions result in oscillopsia with head movement; unilateral vestibular lesions usually result in oscillopsia when attempting to fixate on an object. Central lesions typically result in vertical oscillopsia.

ksYmEq.title: Osmotic myelinolysis
ksYmEq.description: Damage to the myelin sheath of nerves in the CNS caused by a sudden rise in the osmolarity of blood. Most commonly caused by rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia. The most common type of osmotic myelinolysis is central pontine myelinolysis. Clinical symptoms appear 2–6 days after correction of hyponatremia and include an altered level of consciousness, coma, locked-in syndrome, dysarthria, dysphagia, diplopia, and/or worsening quadriparesis.

OsYIEq.title: Central pontine myelinolysis
OsYIEq.description: The most common type of osmotic myelinolysis, in which a sudden rise in blood osmolarity (e.g., rapidly increasing serum Na) disrupts the blood brain barrier and causes efflux of water from the brain, resulting in dehydration of and damage to the myelin sheath of nerves in the central region of the pons.

psYLDq.title: Gracile nucleus
psYLDq.description: A nucleus located in the medulla that receives afferent fibers from the dorsal column and carries fine touch and proprioceptive impulses from the lower body.

JsYsDq.title: Cuneate nucleus
JsYsDq.description: A nucleus located in the medulla that carries fine touch and proprioceptive impulses from the upper body above the level of the T6 vertebra but not the face and ear.

media.title: Ascending sensory tracts of the spinal cord

7sY4wq.title: Substantia nigra
7sY4wq.description: A section of the midbrain that is part of the basal ganglia. The substantia nigra contains dopaminergic neurons that transmit signals involved in movement. Degeneration of the substantia nigra pars compacta is the pathologic hallmark of Parkinson disease.

-sYDxq.title: Clue cells
-sYDxq.description: A collection of vaginal epithelial cells covered with bacteria (particularly Gardnerella vaginalis) identified on wet mount preparation.

ZGYZBq.title: ERBB2
ZGYZBq.description: A tyrosine kinase receptor that controls cellular growth and differentiation. It is encoded by a proto-oncogene that when mutated can contribute to certain cancers (e.g., breast cancer, gastric cancer).

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Staging and receptor testing

bGYHBq.title: Syndesmosis
bGYHBq.description: A type of fixed joint (synarthrosis) in which bones are joined together by connective tissue. Examples include the fontanelles of the skull, the inferior tibiofibular joint, vertebral body connections (ligamenta flava, interspinous ligament, supraspinous ligament), and interosseous membranes.

VGYGyq.title: Differential cyanosis
VGYGyq.description: A condition in which the upper body appears pink and the legs appear cyanotic. It can occur when deoxygenated blood flows across a patent ductus arteriosus into the postductal systemic circulation, e.g., in patients with preductal coarctation of the aorta or pulmonary hypertension.

destinations.label: Acyanotic congenital heart defects → Eisenmenger syndrome

eGYxyq.title: Chlamydia pneumoniae
eGYxyq.description: An obligate intracellular gram-negative bacterium that causes upper and lower respiratory tract infections, including atypical pneumonia.

SGYyAq.title: Keratin
SGYyAq.description: A family of structural proteins. Found in abundance in keratinocytes of the epidermis. Also expressed in cancers of epithelial origin.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Structure of the skin

iGYJ_q.title: Anagen phase
iGYJ_q.description: The phase of the hair growth cycle in which the hair actively grows.

jGY__q.title: Telogen phase
jGY__q.description: The phase of the hair growth cycle in which the hair has stopped growing, commonly called the resting phase.

5GYi-q.title: Eccrine sweat gland
5GYi-q.description: A skin appendage found in the dermis of most parts of the body. Aids in thermoregulation via secretion of sweat. Areas of high concentration of eccrine sweat glands include the palms, soles, and head. The cells of eccrine glands release content via exocytosis (i.e., using secretory vesicles).

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Skin appendage

rGYf0I.title: Giant cell arteritis
rGYf0I.description: A type of vasculitis that causes chronic inflammation of the large and medium-sized arteries. It is most common in women over the age of 50. Classic localizations include the carotid artery and its major branches, as well as the aorta. Patients usually present with constitutional symptoms (e.g., fever, weight loss, night sweats, fatigue, and malaise) and new headaches.

media.title: Polymyalgia rheumatica and giant cell arteritis fact sheet

uGYpaI.title: Charcot neurological triad
uGYpaI.description: The combination of scanning speech, nystagmus, and intention tremors. Often used to describe cerebellar involvement in multiple sclerosis but can occur with any cerebellar lesion.

wGYhYI.title: Elbow
wGYhYI.description: A complex synovial hinge joint between the distal end of the humerus and the proximal ends of the radius (humeroradial joint) and ulna (humeroulnar joint), as well as between the radius and ulna (radioulnar joint); connects upper arm and forearm.

destinations.label: Upper arm and elbow → Elbow joint

media.title: Range of motion of the elbow and distal radioulnar joints

KtYUeI.title: Tibialis anterior
KtYUeI.description: A muscle in the anterior compartment of the leg innervated by the deep peroneal nerve. Primary actions are dorsiflexion and inversion of the foot.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

6tYjeI.title: Extensor digitorum longus
6tYjeI.description: A muscle of the anterior compartment of the leg that functions primarily to extend toes 2-4 and secondarily in ankle dorsiflexion. Innervated by the deep peroneal nerve and receives blood supply from the anterior tibial artery.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

media.title: Muscles of the extensor compartment of the leg

ptYLeI.title: Fibularis tertius
ptYLeI.description: A muscle of the anterior compartment of the leg that functions primarily to evert the foot at the ankle joint and secondarily to dorsiflex the ankle. Innervated by the deep peroneal nerve and receives arterial supply from the anterior tibial artery.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

media.title: Muscles of the extensor compartment of the leg

JtYseI.title: Extensor hallucis longus
JtYseI.description: A thin muscle of the anterior compartment of the leg that primarily extends the hallux. Secondary functions include ankle dorsiflexion, inversion, and eversion. Innervated by the deep peroneal nerve and receives blood from the anterior tibial artery.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

media.title: Actions of the extensor muscles of the leg
Muscles of the extensor compartment of the leg

FtYg2I.title: Gastrocnemius
FtYg2I.description: A muscle of the superficial posterior compartment of the leg that functions as a powerful plantarflexor of the foot. Innervated by the tibial nerve and receives blood supply from branches of the sural artery.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

media.title: Anatomical overview of superficial flexors (lower leg)
Schematic overview of superficial flexors (lower leg)

8tYO2I.title: Triceps surae muscle
8tYO2I.description: A superficial flexor of the leg that consists of the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles. Their tendons fuse to form the calcaneal tendon (Achilles tendon). Innervated by the tibial nerve (L4-S3). Flexes and inverts the ankle.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

utYp2I.title: Soleus muscle
utYp2I.description: A muscle of the superficial posterior compartment of the leg that functions as a powerful ankle plantarflexor. Innervated by the tibial nerve and receives blood supply from the posterior tibial, peroneal, and sural arteries.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

media.title: Anatomical overview of superficial flexors (lower leg)

AtYRTI.title: M. tibialis posterior
AtYRTI.description: A muscle in the deep posterior compartment of the leg innervated by the tibial nerve. Main actions are foot inversion and plantar flexion.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

media.title: Deep flexor group of muscles of the leg

1FY2SI.title: Perilymphatic fistula
1FY2SI.description: A congenital or acquired abnormal connection between the inner ear and middle ear. Can cause sensorineural hearing loss, dizziness, and vertigo.

dFYoSI.title: Spondylosis
dFYoSI.description: A broad term used to describe degenerative changes of the spine that may result in irritation and/or damage of the adjacent nerve roots; symptoms may include pain, paresthesia, and weakness.

2FYThI.title: Cyclooxygenase
2FYThI.description: A family of cytosolic isozymes involved in the synthesis of prostaglandins and thromboxane from arachidonic acid.

TFY6hI.title: African trypanosomiasis
TFY6hI.description: A disease caused by infection with Trypanosoma brucei, which is transmitted by the Tsetse fly. It is characterized by recurrent fever, lymphadenopathy, somnolence, and coma. Treatment options include suramin for blood-borne disease and melarsoprol for CNS involvement.

media.title: African trypanosomiasis fact sheet and incidence map

RFYl3I.title: Right coronary artery
RFYl3I.description: A coronary artery that branches into the right marginal artery and (usually) the posterior descending artery. Supplies right ventricle, inferior wall of left ventricle, and (usually) the posterior wall (via the posterior descending artery).

qFYCQI.title: Vascular compliance
qFYCQI.description: The ability of a vessel to expand in response to changes in pressure. Compliance is equal to change in volume divided by change in pressure (i.e., C = ΔV/ΔP)

7FY4jI.title: Oropharynx
7FY4jI.description: A continuation of the nasopharynx that extends from the inferior border of the soft palate to the superior aspect of the epiglottis. Prevents food from entering the larynx.

uFYpPI.title: Transcellular compartment
uFYpPI.description: A small part (approx. 5%) of the extracellular fluid compartment, which consists of fluid that is secreted by epithelial cells and/or fluid that is contained within epithelium-lined cavities: e.g., cerebrospinal fluid, aqueous humor, synovial fluid, pleural fluid, peritoneal fluid, tracheobronchial and gastrointestinal secretions

EFY8PI.title: Transcellular fluid
EFY8PI.description: Fluid that is secreted by epithelial cells: e.g., cerebrospinal fluid, aqueous humor, gall, synovial fluid, pleural fluid, tracheobronchial and gastrointestinal secretions

9FYN4I.title: Intravascular
9FYN4I.description: A descriptor for being situated within blood vessels (e.g., intravascular access).

xFYE4I.title: Extracellular fluid
xFYE4I.description: The fluid outside cells. Makes up 40% of an individual's total body water (or 25% of their total weight). It is further divided into the interstitial fluid compartment (75%) and intravascular fluid compartment (25%). Sodium is the main extracellular cation and chloride is the main extracellular anion.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function

yFYdkI.title: Pulse examination
yFYdkI.description: A part of the cardiovascular examination that assesses characteristics of the pulse, which include: rate, rhythm, amplitude, and contour (i.e., rate of upstroke). Pulses can be assessed at the carotid, radial, femoral, posterior tibial, and dorsalis pedis arteries.

zFYrkI.title: Thumb sign (Marfan disease)
zFYrkI.description: A sign seen in patients with Marfan disease. Patients are asked to place their thumbs in the palms of the same hand and then clench to form a fist. A positive thumb sign is present when the thumb protrudes beyond the ulnar border of the hand (the thumb is longer than the width of the palm).

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Clinical features

d8YolI.title: Apolipoprotein E
d8YolI.description: A protein encoded by the APOE gene located on chromosome 19, which exists in three alleles: ε2, ε3, and ε4. The ε4 allele is a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

q8YCnI.title: β-oxidation
q8YCnI.description: A catabolic process in which a fatty acid chain is cleaved at the β carbon (every 2nd carbon) by dehydrogenase enzymes. Breaks down odd-chain fatty acids into acetyl-CoA and propionyl CoA and even-chain fatty acids into acetyl-CoA only. Typically occurs in the mitochondria; β-oxidation of very long-chain fatty acids occurs in peroxisomes.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

s8YtLI.title: Adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction
s8YtLI.description: An adenocarcinoma located within 5 cm of the esophageal gastric junction. This location makes both thoracic and abdominal lymphatic spread possible, which complicates surgical treatment. The prognosis of these carcinomas has been historically poor.

media.title: Adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction: Siewert classification

98YNKI.title: Phospholipase A2
