98YNKI.description: An enzyme that converts membrane phospholipids into arachidonic acid. Inhibited by corticosteroids.

x8YEKI.title: Phosphodiesterase
x8YEKI.description: An enzyme that can break phosphodiester bonds. A subgroup of these enzymes can degrade and inactivate the second messengers cGMP and cAMP.

-8YD6I.title: HMG-CoA synthase
-8YD6I.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the condensation of acetoacetyl-CoA with acetyl-CoA to form 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA (HMG-CoA). Exists as two distinct isozymes: a mitochondrial form (HMGCS2) that is the rate-limiting enzyme for ketogenesis, and a cytosolic form (HMGCS1) that initiates the mevalonate pathway for cholesterol and other isoprenoid synthesis.

PuYWrI.title: Glasgow-Blatchford bleeding score
PuYWrI.description: A risk stratification score used to triage management in hemodynamically stable patients with upper gastrointestinal bleeding.

4uY3rI.title: Postthrombotic syndrome
4uY3rI.description: A syndrome characterized by features of chronic venous insufficiency (e.g., pain, edema, venous dilation, ulceration, abnormal skin pigmentation) that develop following a deep vein thrombosis.

wuYhtI.title: Autoimmune pancreatitis
wuYhtI.description: A rare chronic inflammatory condition of the pancreas that typically manifests with obstructive jaundice and mild epigastric pain, and responds well to glucocorticoid therapy. Classified as type 1 (the pancreatic manifestation of IgG4-related disease with frequent multi-organ involvement) or type 2 (a pancreas-limited form often associated with inflammatory bowel disease).

xuYEtI.title: Red thrombus
xuYEtI.description: A type of thrombus primarily formed in vessels in which blood is in stasis or travels at a slower velocity (e.g., veins). Traps large amounts of red blood cells, which lend the thrombus a dark red color. Most common in deep veins of the lower extremities (e.g., popliteal and femoral veins).

1EY2uI.title: Cholecystokinin-secretin pancreatic function test
1EY2uI.description: A diagnostic test that can differentiate gastrinoma from other causes of hypergastrinemia. If the administration of secretin causes a fasting serum gastrin level of > 120 pg/mL, the test is positive for gastrinoma.

WEYPuI.title: Fertilization
WEYPuI.description: The process of sperm and egg fusion, which consists of the acrosome reaction and impregnation.

2EYTEI.title: Pronuclear fusion
2EYTEI.description: A process in which the female and male pronuclei lose their respective nuclear envelopes and fuse to form a zygote nucleus with a diploid set of chromosomes.

fEYkEI.title: Timolol
fEYkEI.description: A nonselective beta-blocker commonly used topically in the treatment of both open- and closed-angle glaucoma.

JEYs9I.title: Hypothermia
JEYs9I.description: A core body temperature that is less than 35°C (95.0°F).

GEYBCI.title: Decompensated cirrhosis
GEYBCI.description: The development of complications of portal hypertension (e.g., overt ascites, variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy) in a patient with cirrhosis. Often triggered by an acute event (e.g., infection, alcohol intake, certain medications) but can also develop gradually (e.g., accumulation of fluid in ascites).

1vY2_I.title: Herpetic whitlow
1vY2_I.description: An infection of the dermal and subcutaneous tissue of the fingers caused by HSV-1 (and less commonly HSV-2). Often secondary to primary oral lesions. Manifests with painful, grouped, nonpurulent vesicles and axillary and/or epitrochlear lymphadenopathy proximal to the infection.

destinations.label: Herpes simplex virus infections → Cutaneous herpes

VvYG_I.title: Acidified glycerol lysis test
VvYG_I.description: A screening test for hereditary spherocytosis in which red blood cells are placed in hypotonic solution with added glycerol.  In a patient with hereditary spherocytosis, spherocytes will lyse more quickly than normal cells due to a decreased surface area to volume ratio.

evYx_I.title: Eosin-5-maleimide binding test
evYx_I.description: A flow cytometric test used to confirm the diagnosis of hereditary spherocytosis. EMA binds to several membrane proteins (e.g., band 3, Rh polypeptides, Cd 47) of RBCs and a reduction of these proteins in hereditary spherocytosis leads to decreased binding of EMA.

UvYbzI.title: Salicylate
UvYbzI.description: The active metabolite of aspirin. The pharmacology compound is a topical keratolytic agent used in the management of common dermatologic conditions (e.g., warts, corns, acne, seborrheic dermatitis).

2vYTzI.title: Phencyclidine
2vYTzI.description: A stimulant drug that activates glutamate receptors and antagonizes NMDA receptors, causing dissociative hallucinations. The most common symptoms of intoxication are nystagmus and violent, abnormal behavior, although hypertension, tachycardia, and hyperthermia may also be present.

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Phencyclidine use disorder

TvY6zI.title: Pralidoxime
TvY6zI.description: An oxime drug that reactivates acetylcholinesterase that has been inactivated by phosphorylation (e.g., in patients with organophosphate poisoning).

gvYFzI.title: Acetaminophen
gvYFzI.description: A nonopioid drug that is used as an analgesic and antipyretic.

SvYyzI.title: Caustic liquid
SvYyzI.description: A liquid that causes chemical damage to tissue. Typically highly acidic or alkaline relative to physiologic pH. Alkaline liquids cause liquefactive necrosis (saponification of fats). Acidic liquids cause coagulation necrosis (denaturation of tissue proteins).

hvYc-I.title: Autoimmune connective tissue diseases
hvYc-I.description: A collection of autoimmune diseases that target collagen or elastin, affecting multiple systems throughout the body. Diseases include systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, systemic sclerosis, Sjogren syndrome, and mixed and undifferentiated connective tissue disease.

destinations.label: Connective tissue diseases → Autoimmune connective tissue diseases

ivYJ-I.title: Head thrust test
ivYJ-I.description: A maneuver to examine the vestibuloocular reflex and clinically differentiate between peripheral and central causes of acute vestibular syndrome. Considered abnormal if the patient is unable to maintain central visual fixation, in which case a corrective saccade (quick eye movement) occurs to fixate on the target again. This indicates a deficient vestibuloocular reflex on the side of the head turn.

PvYWZr.title: Mixed connective tissue disease
PvYWZr.description: An autoimmune disease characterized by concurrent features of at least two connective tissue diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, idiopathic inflammatory myopathies). Early features are typically nonspecific (e.g., fatigue, low-grade fever); later stage features include Raynaud phenomenon, interstitial lung disease, myositis, and acrosclerosis. Anti-U1 RNP antibodies are present in all individuals with mixed connective tissue disease.

kvYmZr.title: Persistent postural-perceptual dizziness
kvYmZr.description: An idiopathic disorder in which patients experience recurring episodes of non-rotational dizziness (not true vertigo, as it does not have a rotational component, or sensation of self/environment "spinning") and hypersensitivity to motion. These symptoms follow an inciting episode of vertigo or dizziness, such as vestibular neuritis or a panic attack. Patients often have associated depressive or anxiety disorders.

NvY-Zr.title: LH
NvY-Zr.description: A hormone that is synthesized and secreted by the anterior pituitary gland. In women, LH surge triggers ovulation. In men, LH stimulates testicular Leydig cells to synthesize testosterone.

mvYV0r.title: Bone formation by endochondral ossification
mvYV0r.description: The replacement of growing cartilage with bone from osteoclast and osteoblast activity. Responsible for growth of the axial skeleton, appendicular skeleton, and base of skull.

destinations.label: Virtual histology slide box →  Connective tissue

7vY4Yr.title: Graves disease
7vY4Yr.description: An autoimmune condition of the thyroid gland in which circulating TSH receptor autoantibodies lead to overstimulation of the thyroid gland and excess thyroid hormone production. Classic clinical signs include diffuse goiter, ophthalmopathy, and pretibial myxedema.

FvYgbr.title: Ciguatera fish poisoning
FvYgbr.description: A condition caused by the consumption of fish contaminated with toxins formed by Gambierdiscus dinoflagellates (e.g.,  ciguatoxin, saitotoxin, scaritoxin). Most commonly occurs after ingestion of large, predatory reef fish (e.g., grouper, barracuda). Manifestations include gastrointestinal symptoms, paresthesias, and cardiovascular symptoms (e.g., bradycardia, heart block).

vvYAbr.title: Congenital iodine deficiency syndrome
vvYAbr.description: A syndrome of congenital hypothyroidism caused by iodine deficiency. Features of congenital hypothyroidism are usually apparent at birth because of concomitant maternal hypothyroidism from iodine deficiency.

wvYhXr.title: Vestibular rehabilitation therapy
wvYhXr.description: A type of physical therapy used in the management of patients with peripheral vertigo. Components include repositioning maneuvers (e.g., Brandt-Daroff exercises), habituation exercises (e.g., Cawthorne-Cooksey exercises), adaptation exercises for gaze stabilization, postural control exercises, and fall prevention training.

9vYNXr.title: Subclinical hyperthyroidism
9vYNXr.description: The combination of low serum TSH levels and normal serum free T4 and T3 levels. Patients usually do not exhibit symptoms of thyrotoxicosis. Subclinical hyperthyroidism is often transient but may progress to overt hyperthyroidism.

CvYqXr.title: Subacute thyroiditis
CvYqXr.description: A transient, self-limited, patchy inflammation of the thyroid gland that causes a triphasic pattern from thyrotoxicosis to hypothyroidism, before returning to a euthyroid state. One of two histological subtypes may develop: subacute granulomatous thyroiditis (de Quervain thyroiditis), which follows viral infection, or subacute lymphocytic thyroiditis (silent or painless thyroiditis), which is caused by autoimmune disease, adverse effects of medications, and postpartum changes.

xvYEXr.title: Antisynthetase syndrome
xvYEXr.description: A common form of overlap myositis characterized by muscle weakness, Raynaud syndrome, nonerosive arthritis, interstitial lung disease, and skin changes to the palms (mechanic's hands). Affected patients are positive for antisynthetase antibodies.

yvYdcr.title: Hypersensitivity reactions
yvYdcr.description: An exaggerated and/or pathological immune response to foreign or self-antigens. Type I hypersensitivity reactions are immediate allergic reactions (e.g., food, pollen, asthma), type II are cytotoxic, type III are immune complex-mediated, and type IV are delayed and cell-mediated.

AvYRcr.title: Serum sickness
AvYRcr.description: A type III hypersensitivity reaction in which antibodies to foreign proteins are produced. These antibodies deposit in tissues as antibody-antigen complexes 1–2 weeks later, which causes inflammation and tissue damage. Manifests with fever, rash, arthralgias, and lymphadenopathy.

zvYrcr.title: Tamm-Horsfall protein
zvYrcr.description: The most abundant protein excreted in ordinary urine. Produced by renal tubular cells of the loop of Henle. Physiological function is not well understood. Contributes to the mucoprotein matrix of hyaline casts.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

-vYDcr.title: Granular casts
-vYDcr.description: A finding on urine microscopy. Granular casts are an amalgamation of plasma proteins and dead or injured tubular epithelial cells that slough into the tubular lumen. A notable example of granular casts are the "muddy brown casts" of acute tubular necrosis, which are caused by spilled cellular contents of infarcted tubular epithelial cells.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

XDY91r.title: Complicated diverticulitis
XDY91r.description: A condition of colonic diverticular inflammation associated with complications, such as perforation, abscess, fecal peritonitis, bowel obstruction, and/or fistula formation.

WDYPWr.title: Somatic symptom disorder
WDYPWr.description:
A psychiatric disorder in which a patient has persistent (≥ 6 months) somatic symptoms that disrupt daily life and ≥ 2 of the following: high levels of anxiety about health; disproportionate and persistent thoughts about the seriousness of one's symptoms; excessive time and energy devoted to these symptoms and health concerns.
Specifiers for somatic symptom disorder are the predominance of pain (formerly pain disorder), the persistence of severe symptoms (marked impairment for over 6 months), and severity of the disease (mild, moderate, or severe).

destinations.label: Somatic symptom and related disorders → Somatic symptom disorder

dDYoWr.title: Stroke
dDYoWr.description: An acute neurological condition in which arterial blood supply to brain tissue is impaired due to a focal vascular cause. The ultimate cause of neuronal cell death is always ischemia due to insufficient perfusion. However, the insufficient perfusion itself can be caused by both occlusion (ischemic stroke) or rupture (hemorrhagic stroke) of an upstream artery. Typical presenting symptoms include acute unilateral weakness and/or numbness of the limbs and/or face.

2DYTdr.title: Nodular basal cell carcinoma
2DYTdr.description: The most common subtype of basal cell carcinoma. Typically manifests as a pearl-like papule or nodule with rolled borders and central ulceration (rodent ulcer) on the face, especially the nose. Grows gradually, rarely metastasizes, and has a low likelihood of recurrence after excision.

destinations.label: Basal cell carcinoma → Subtypes and variants

hDYcVr.title: Vocal fold nodules
hDYcVr.description: Benign lesions that are caused by frequent microtrauma (e.g., voice overuse by teachers or professional singers) to the vocal cords, which leads to edematous swelling and development of fibrotic scars in the superficial lamina propria.

destinations.label: Benign laryngeal lesions → Vocal fold nodule

3DYSVr.title: Vocal fold polyp
3DYSVr.description: A benign lesion that develops in response to vocal fold irritation (e.g., from smoking, GERD, vocal overuse). Typically located on the anterior one-third of the vocal fold and manifests with hoarseness, throat discomfort, loss of vocal range, and a breathy voice.

destinations.label: Benign laryngeal lesions → Vocal fold polyp

5DYiUr.title: Abdominal hernias
5DYiUr.description: The protrusion of intraabdominal contents through congenital or acquired areas of weakness in the abdominal wall. Classified into four categories: ventral hernias (epigastric, umbilical hernia, incisional hernias), groin hernias (inguinal and femoral hernias), pelvic hernias (obturator, sciatic, and perineal hernias), and flank or lumbar hernias.

nDY7Ur.title: Cholangiocarcinoma
nDY7Ur.description: A malignancy in the bile duct that originates more frequently in extrahepatic than intrahepatic ducts. Risk factors include primary sclerosing cholangitis and liver fluke infection. Clinical features may include cholestasis, Courvoisier sign, and abdominal discomfort.

media.title: Centrally located right hepatic lobe mass
Extrahepatic bile duct thickening in cholangiocarcinoma

sDYtfr.title: Actinic keratosis
sDYtfr.description: A skin lesion caused by exposure to UV rays that manifests as rough, scaly skin plaques with the potential to progress to squamous cell carcinoma.

8DYOTr.title: Pharyngeal cancer
8DYOTr.description: A collection of cancers (most commonly squamous cell carcinomas) including malignant tumors in the nasopharynx, oropharynx, and hypopharyx. Risk factors include alcohol and tobacco use.

9DYNgr.title: Constipation
9DYNgr.description: A condition of infrequent, difficult passage of stool that may be accompanied by the sensation of incomplete bowel emptying. Common in all age groups and often occurs without a pathological cause as a result of a low-fiber diet, poor hydration, and/or lack of exercise. Can be associated with anatomical or physiological colorectal abnormalities (e.g., colorectal carcinoma, motility disorder in diabetic neuropathy).

CDYqgr.title: Arteriosclerosis
CDYqgr.description: Thickening, hardening, and loss of elasticity of the arterial vessel wall. The three types of arteriosclerosis are atherosclerosis, Monckenberg's medial calcification, and arteriolosclerosis, of which atherosclerosis is the most common.

BDYzgr.title: Multiple sclerosis
BDYzgr.description: A chronic, demyelinating disease of the CNS caused by an immune-mediated inflammatory process. The clinical course is usually characterized by exacerbations with periods of remission in between. Initial manifestations include internuclear ophthalmoplegia and retrobulbar neuritis, followed by loss of vibration and touch, upper motor neuron weakness, Charcot's neurological triad, cranial nerve palsies, and autonomic dysfunction.

media.title: White matter lesions in multiple sclerosis

yDYdSr.title: Lichen planus
yDYdSr.description: A chronic, inflammatory disease characterized by papules and plaques, possibly with Wickham striae and erosions, on the skin, mucosa (e.g., oral, genital), hair, and/or nails. Multiple sites can be affected simultaneously. Cutaneous lichen planus is usually self-limited, but hypertrophic cutaneous disease and mucosal lichen planus are typically chronic and have the potential for malignant transformation.

_DY5Sr.title: Whipple's triad
_DY5Sr.description: A triad that consists of 1) hypoglycemic symptoms (e.g., sweating, palpitations) that typically follow exertion or fasting; 2) documented hypoglycemia during an episode, and 3) relief of symptoms upon administration of glucose. Characteristically seen in patients with insulinoma.

zDYrSr.title: Infantile hemangioma
zDYrSr.description: A benign, vascular tumor caused by abnormal development of vascular endothelial cells. Typically presents as a red-blue papule or macule. Occurs in up to 10% of infants and typically involutes slowly within a few years.

destinations.label: Overview of neonatal conditions → Neonatal skin lesions

-DYDSr.title: Cherry hemangioma
-DYDSr.description: The most common acquired cutaneous vascular anomaly. Present as bright cherry-red, dome-shaped papules or macules (generally 1–5 mm in diameter). Caused by proliferation of dilated mature capillaries. Most commonly located on the trunk and upper extremities, but can occur anywhere on the body. Do not regress spontaneously and have no malignant potential.

destinations.label: Benign skin tumors → Vascular skin tumors

media.title: Capillary hemangioma of the skin (cherry angioma)
Capillary hemangioma of the skin (cherry angioma)

0wYehr.title: Plaque
0wYehr.description: A term that can refer to atherosclerotic lesions within an artery wall (atheroma), elevated skin lesions > 1 cm (skin plaque), depositions of amyloid in tissue (amyloid plaque), depositions of Aβ protein in the brain (senile plaque), and pleural changes associated with asbestosis (pleural plaque).

cwYa3r.title: Ulcer (dermatology)
cwYa3r.description: A skin lesion that results from loss of the epidermis and some portion of the dermis.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Secondary skin lesions

dwYo3r.title: Atrophy
dwYo3r.description: A decrease in tissue mass. Can be caused by decreases in cell size (due to cytoskeleton degradation or decreases in protein synthesis) or decreases in cell number (due to apoptosis). Etiologies include lack of use (e.g., in muscle), denervation, loss of blood supply, loss of hormonal stimulation, poor nutrition, and drug adverse effects (e.g., skin thinning from chronic topical steroid use).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cellular adaptation

3wYSir.title: Erythema
3wYSir.description: A superficial redness secondary to the dilation of capillaries. On darker skin tones, capillary dilation may appear as a deeper shade of purple or brown.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Complex skin lesions

RwYlir.title: Lichenification
RwYlir.description: A leathery thickening of the skin due to epidermal hypertrophy. Commonly occurs in association with eczema or other pruritic skin diseases as a result of repeated manipulation of lesions.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Complex skin lesions

jwY_ir.title: Benzodiazepine dependence
jwY_ir.description: The physical adaptation to prolonged benzodiazepine use, which is characterized by the development of tolerance (diminished response) and withdrawal symptoms with decreased drug intake. Dependence may develop even if medication is taken as prescribed.

4wY3Qr.title: Keratosis pilaris
4wY3Qr.description: A benign skin condition caused by increased keratinization and the formation of keratin plugs in hair follicles. Manifests as dry, rough skin with small follicular papules and perifollicular erythema, typically on facial cheeks and the extensor surfaces of the proximal arms and thighs. Associated with atopic dermatitis and ichthyosis vulgaris.

lwYvQr.title: Dilated cardiomyopathy
lwYvQr.description: A disorder leading to dilatation and impaired contraction of one or both ventricles, typically resulting in heart failure. Idiopathic in up to 50% of cases and may be hereditary. Other important causes include myocarditis, ischemic heart disease, hypertension, pregnancy, and heavy, long-term alcohol consumption.

MwYMjr.title: Leukemia cutis
MwYMjr.description: A condition caused by infiltration of the skin by neoplastic leukocytes (e.g., from leukemia, myelodysplastic syndrome). Typically manifests with violaceous nodules.

JwYsPr.title: CASPAR
JwYsPr.description: The ClASsification criteria for Psoriatic ARthritis (CASPAR) requires that ≥ 3 of the following 5 criteria are fulfilled: evidence of psoriasis, psoriatic nail dystrophy, negative rheumatoid factor, dactylitis, and radiologic signs.

IwYY4r.title: Lentigo maligna
IwYY4r.description: A precancerous skin lesion characterized by intraepithelial proliferation of dysplastic melanocytes. Caused by prolonged exposure to UV light and typically develops in older individuals (> 70 years old) on sun-exposed areas (e.g., face, neck) as a darkly pigmented macule with irregular borders and "island-like" speckling.

media.title: Intraepithelial precancerous skin lesion: lentigo maligna

rwYf4r.title: Aortic valve stenosis
rwYf4r.description: A valvular disease characterized by narrowing of the aortic valve, resulting in obstruction of the outflow of blood from the left ventricle into the aorta during systole.

media.title: Continuous wave (CW) Doppler in aortic valvular stenosis
Heart murmur in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, aortic stenosis, and pulmonary stenosis

7wY44r.title: Asystole
7wY44r.description: A cardiac arrest rhythm in which there is no electrical activity on ECG.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Advanced cardiac life support (ACLS)

HwYK4r.title: Sedative-hypnotic toxidrome
HwYK4r.description: Signs and symptoms resulting from the toxic effects of sedative-hypnotic agents that increase the activity of GABA receptors (e.g., barbiturates, benzodiazepines, and benzodiazepine-like drugs). Features include reduced level of consciousness (e.g., coma), hypothermia, bradycardia, respiratory depression, hypotension, hypotonia, hyporeflexia, and slurred speech.

swYt4r.title: Benzodiazepine overdose
swYt4r.description: An overdose that typically manifests with sedative‑hypnotic toxidrome (e.g., altered consciousness, mild respiratory depression, ataxia, slurred speech). Rarely life-threatening unless associated with the coingestion of alcohol or other respiratory depressants.

GwYB4r.title: Macule
GwYB4r.description: A nonpalpable skin lesion ≤ 1 cm in size that differs in color from surrounding skin.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Primary skin lesions

xwYEOr.title: Polycystic kidney disease
xwYEOr.description: An inherited disorder characterized by the development of multiple cysts in the kidneys. There are two distinct types: autosomal recessive PKD (ARPKD), which typically manifests in infancy or early childhood, and autosomal dominant PKD (ADPKD), which typically manifests in adulthood.

T9Y65r.title: Chronic respiratory failure
T9Y65r.description: The inability of the respiratory system to maintain adequate gas exchange as a result of chronic illness (e.g., chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, interstitial lung disease, obesity hypoventilation syndrome).

g9YF5r.title: Uremic pericarditis
g9YF5r.description: A complication of chronic kidney disease that causes fibrinous pericarditis. Typically presents with a friction rub on auscultation. Unlike other forms of pericarditis, this condition does not typically cause ECG changes because there is a lack of inflammatory cells invading the myocardium.

S9Yy5r.title: Phototoxic reaction
S9Yy5r.description: A non-allergic photosensitive reaction caused by the direct, toxic action of UV-activated drug metabolites on the skin. Common offenders include tetracyclines (especially doxycycline), thiazides, sulfonamides, fluoroquinolones, retinoids, and NSAIDs. Presents with sunburn-like rash within minutes to hours of sun exposure.

39YSMr.title: Global malabsorption
39YSMr.description: A condition of impaired intestinal absorption of carbohydrates, fats, protein, vitamins, nutrients, and minerals. Caused due to a diffuse reduction in the absorptive capacity of the intestine (e.g., in celiac disease due to diffuse intestinal villus atrophy; after extensive small bowel resection). Manifestations include diarrhea, steatorrhea, weight loss, and signs of vitamin and nutrient deficiency (e.g., anemia, cheilitis, glossitis).

Q9YuMr.title: Photoallergic reaction
Q9YuMr.description: A delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction that occurs due to UV-induced changes in drug antigenicity (formation of a photoallergen). Typically occurs due to topical drug exposure, including sunscreens, NSAIDs, topical antihistamines. Manifests as erythema and eczema on sun-exposed skin.

j9Y_Mr.title: Angiodysplasia
j9Y_Mr.description: A degenerative disorder of gastrointestinal blood vessels that consists of abnormal, dilated, and tortuous communications between veins and capillaries. May be asymptomatic or lead to upper or lower gastrointestinal bleeding.

P9YWnr.title: Myofascial pain syndrome
P9YWnr.description: A chronic pain disorder caused by muscle tension or repetitive motion and characterized by the presence of trigger points in muscles and/or fascia. The pain can occur anywhere but is mostly confined to one anatomical region, leading to weakness and limited range of motion.

49Y3nr.title: Hashimoto thyroiditis
49Y3nr.description: The most common type of autoimmune thyroiditis and the leading cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas. Caused by autoantibody-mediated destruction of thyroid tissue, which usually leads to hypothyroidism. Diagnosis is confirmed by positive thyroid antibodies.

l9Yvnr.title: Portal vein thrombosis
l9Yvnr.description: A thrombus in the portal vein, which can cause complete or partial closure of the vein. Most commonly occurs as a complication of liver cirrhosis. Can lead to portal hypertension.

media.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein thrombosis 2/2

m9YVLr.title: Hepatic encephalopathy
m9YVLr.description: A deterioration in mental status and cognitive function caused by severe liver disease. Hepatic dysfunction results in the inadequate elimination of metabolic products with subsequent accumulation of neurotoxic metabolites (like ammonia).

59YiLr.title: Adenoid hypertrophy
59YiLr.description: Enlargement of the pharyngeal tonsils (often reffered to as adenoids). Common among children, who present with mouth breathing, mucopurulent nasal discharge, snoring, and/or impaired hearing.

n9Y7Lr.title: Monteggia fracture
n9Y7Lr.description: A fracture of the ulna (usually the proximal third) with concomitant dislocation of the radial head. Typically caused by either a fall on an outstretched and pronated forearm or a direct, forceful blow to the forearm.

L9YwLr.title: Rome IV criteria for irritable bowel syndrome
L9YwLr.description: A set of criteria used to diagnose irritable bowel syndrome. Diagnosis requires symptom onset to be at least 6 months ago, recurrent abdominal pain for ≥ 1 day per week during the previous 3 months, and ≥ 2 of the following: pain related to defecation, a change in stool frequency, and/or a change in stool appearance.

p9YLor.title: Ott test
p9YLor.description: A test for assessing thoracic spine mobility. With the patient standing, the examiner marks the spinous process of the C7 vertebra. A second mark is made 30 cm inferior to the first mark. The patient flexes forward as far as possible while keeping the knees straight, and the distance between the two marks is remeasured. An increase in the distance between the marks of < 2 cm indicates impaired thoracic spine mobility.

q9YCor.title: Milkman syndrome
q9YCor.description: A condition characterized by pseudofractures in the cortex of multiple bones. Visible as radiolucent bands with decreased density on x-ray. The ribs, pubic rami, iliac bones, neck of the femur, radius, ulna, and scapula are predominantly affected.

79Y4Kr.title: Ergocalciferol
79Y4Kr.description: An inactive intermediate in the vitamin D biosynthesis pathway found in plant dietary sources. After ingestion, it is converted to its active form (1,25-dihydroxyergocalciferol) in the kidney and liver. Commonly used as a supplement for the prevention and treatment of vitamin D deficiency.

u9Yp6r.title: Nateglinide
u9Yp6r.description: An oral antidiabetic drug of the meglitinide class. Causes closure of ATP-sensitive potassium channels in the beta cell membrane, which leads to depolarization, increases calcium concentration in the cell, and release of insulin. Adverse effects include hypoglycemia, weight gain, and renal failure.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

v9YA6r.title: Liraglutide
v9YA6r.description: A glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist used in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

destinations.label: Diabetes medications → Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (incretin mimetics)

D9Y1pr.title: Albiglutide
D9Y1pr.description: A glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist used in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

destinations.label: Diabetes medications → Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (incretin mimetics)

w9Yhpr.title: Dulaglutide
w9Yhpr.description: A glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist used in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus. Adverse effects include nausea, diarrhea, and vomiting.

destinations.label: Diabetes medications → Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (incretin mimetics)

99YNpr.title: Saxagliptin
99YNpr.description: A DPP-4 inhibitor used for glycemic control in patients with diabetes.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

C9Yqpr.title: Urinary retention
C9Yqpr.description: An inability to voluntarily empty the bladder. Etiologies include mechanical obstruction (e.g., benign prostatic hyperplasia, urethral strictures) and neurologic dysfunction (e.g., from anticholinergic drugs, peripheral neuropathy).

x9YEpr.title: Empagliflozin
x9YEpr.description: An antidiabetic drug that reversibly inhibits the sodium-dependent glucose transporter (SGLT-2) in the proximal tubule of the kidneys, which results in polyuria and glycosuria.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

0CYeqr.title: Retroperitoneal fibrosis
0CYeqr.description: A rare condition of inflammation and fibrosis of the retroperitoneum. Most frequently results in fibrosis of the ureters and can also affect blood and lymphatic vessels.

YCYnqr.title: Gardner syndrome
YCYnqr.description: The constellation of extracolonic manifestations of familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), which includes hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium, endocrine tumors (e.g., thyroid cancer, adrenal adenomas), osteomas, desmoid tumors, and cutaneous lesions.

media.title: Atypical congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium in familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP)

VCYGIr.title: Kerley B lines
VCYGIr.description: A radiographic finding observed in the periphery of the lungs characterized by linear opacities perpendicular to the pleural surface. This finding represents thickening of the interlobular septa due to pulmonary edema.

2CYTrr.title: Kawasaki disease
2CYTrr.description: An acute, necrotizing vasculitis that primarily affects children < 5 years of age. Characterized by high fever, conjunctivitis, mucositis, cervical lymphadenopathy, polymorphous rash, and erythema and edema of the distal extremities. Can cause coronary artery aneurysms.

gCYFrr.title: Bacillus
gCYFrr.description: A genus of Gram-positive, rod-shaped bacteria. Can be aerobic or facultative anaerobes. The two most clinically-relevant species are B. anthracis (which causes anthrax) and B. cereus (which causes food poisoning). The term "bacillus" is also used to describe other bacteria with a similar rod shape.

3CYS7r.title: Parvovirus B19-associated arthritis
3CYS7r.description: A complication of parvovirus B19 infection that more commonly affects adults. Typically manifests as self-limited arthralgia with symmetrical, nondestructive polyarthritis, particularly in the joints of the fingers, hands, knees, and ankles.

destinations.label: Parvovirus B19 infections → Subtypes and variants

RCYl7r.title: Croup
RCYl7r.description: An inflammation of the larynx and trachea, usually due to parainfluenza virus. Typically affects small children six months to three years of age during winter months. Characterized by hoarseness, barking cough, and inspiratory stridor. Radiographs are not routinely required, but if performed they typically show subglottic narrowing (steeple sign).

iCYJ7r.title: End-stage renal disease
iCYJ7r.description: A terminal stage of renal failure characterized by irreversible kidney dysfunction with by a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) < 15 mL/min/1.73 m² and manifestations of uremia requiring renal replacement therapy.

OCYIHr.title: Lymphadenopathy
OCYIHr.description: An enlargement and/or change in consistency of one or more lymph nodes. Common causes infection, autoimmune disease, medications, and malignancy.

5CYisr.title: Quinine
5CYisr.description: An alkaloid obtained from bark of the cinchona tree that is toxic to Plasmodium falciparum (the protozoan parasite that causes malaria). Used to treat uncomplicated malaria.

nCY7sr.title: Pseudopodia
nCY7sr.description: A temporary extension of cell cytoplasm used for motility and ingestion of nutrients or foreign material.

KCYUGr.title: International Prognostic Score
KCYUGr.description: A scoring system used to predict 5-year freedom from progression for patients with advanced Hodgkin lymphoma. Unfavorable prognostic factors include male sex, age ≥ 45 years, stage IV disease, serum albumin concentration < 4 g/dL, hemoglobin concentration < 10.5 g/dL, leucocytosis (> 15,000/μL), and lymphopenia (< 8% of white blood cell count and/or absolute lymphocyte count < 600 cells/μL).

pCYLGr.title: Karyotype
pCYLGr.description: The chromosome pattern in eukaryotes that can be observed by light microscopy during metaphase. Used to detect chromosomal aberrations.

JCYsGr.title: Germline mutation
JCYsGr.description: A mutation that arises in the gametes or sex cells of an individual. Can be passed on to offspring.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

qCYCGr.title: Somatic mutation
qCYCGr.description: A mutation of somatic cells that typically affects only one allele of a gene. Does not occur in germline cells and, therefore, cannot be passed on to offspring. A common mechanism of carcinogenesis.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

HCYKtr.title: Chromosomal translocation
HCYKtr.description: The relocation of one chromosome segment onto another nonhomologous chromosome during cell division. If nonreciprocal exchange happens during translocation, deletions or duplications can lead to inherited (e.g., Down Syndrome) or acquired disease (e.g., AML, CML).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

GCYBtr.title: Point mutation
GCYBtr.description: The ateration of a single DNA base pair via deletion, exchange, or insertion of a single nucleotide in the genetic code.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

tCYXFr.title: Trinucleotide repeat expansion
tCYXFr.description: The mechanism behind trinucleotide repeat disorders in which errors in DNA replication lead to increasing numbers of repeated sequences of three nucleotides. In general, the greater the number of trinucleotide repeats, the greater the chance of exhibiting symptoms and the worse the clinical manifestations.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

FCYgFr.title: Frameshift mutation
FCYgFr.description: A mutation of a gene with the insertion or deletion of a number of nucleotides not divisible by 3, which leads to modified amino acid coding in the gene segments downstream. Often, this will introduce several pathological stop codons, leading to a prematurely truncated peptide composed of an abnormal amino acid sequence. Mutations of this type tend to be very severe.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

8CYOFr.title: Silent mutation
8CYOFr.description: A gene mutation resulting in an altered codon which codes for the identical amino acid as the non-mutated codon. This type of mutation is possible due to redundancy in the genetic code; several trinucleotide sequences can produce the same amino acid. These mutations are usually clinically inconsequential.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

uCYpFr.title: Nonsense mutation
uCYpFr.description: A mutation that causes the formation of an abnormal stop codon, which leads to alterations in the splicing process and early termination of translation.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

ECY8Fr.title: Missense mutation
ECY8Fr.description: A mutation in a gene leading to an altered codon, which codes for a different amino acid. Mutations of this sort can have variable phenotypic consequences, ranging from minimal (the new amino acid is very similar to the correct one) to severe (the altered protein cannot function). Sickle cell disease is caused by a missense mutation.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

vCYAFr.title: Carter effect
vCYAFr.description: An effect observed in multifactorial inheritance disorders in which individuals of the less commonly affected sex are more likely to pass on the condition if they are affected compared to individuals of the opposite sex who more commonly develop the disorder. Hypothesized to occur because less commonly affected individuals possess a higher number of susceptibility genes, and the condition will, therefore, manifest less frequently, requiring more genetic loci to be affected. The numerical increase in susceptibility genes leads to an increased probability of passing on mutated alleles to offspring.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Other types of inheritance

DCY18r.title: Autosomal dominant inheritance
DCY18r.description: A mode of inheritance that causes disease even if only one allele is altered. Usually caused by mutations in structural genes. Examples include achondroplasia and Huntington disease.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Autosomal dominant inheritance

wCYh8r.title: Mallory-Weiss syndrome
wCYh8r.description: A condition characterized by a longitudinal mucous membrane tear (limited to the mucosa and submucosa) at the gastroesophageal junction that can lead to bleeding. Usually precipitated by forceful vomiting.

9CYN8r.title: Autosomal recessive inheritance
9CYN8r.description: A mode of inheritance that causes disease when both alleles are altered. Heterozygotes are carriers and show no phenotypic evidence of disease. Examples include cystic fibrosis and phenylketonuria.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Autosomal recessive inheritance

CCYq8r.title: X-linked recessive inheritance
CCYq8r.description: An inheritance pattern seen in conditions caused by mutated genes found on the X chromosome. Male individuals are virtually always affected (owing to the presence of only one X chromosome) whereas female carriers are unaffected (owing to the presence of two X chromosomes), unless they inherit two mutated X chromosomes.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → X-linked recessive inheritance

ACYRur.title: Nagayama spots
ACYRur.description: A papular enanthem on the uvula and soft palate that may be seen in patients with exanthema subitum.

-CYDur.title: Vitamin D deficiency
-CYDur.description: A vitamin deficiency that manifests in children as rickets and in adults as osteomalacia. Causes include insufficient sunlight exposure, low intake through food, and poor intestinal absorption of fat soluble vitamins (D, E, A, and K).

axYQEr.title: Wells criteria for pulmonary embolism
axYQEr.description: A diagnostic algorithm in stable patients for assessing the probability of pulmonary embolism (PE). A score is assigned based on risk factors for deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and PE (e.g., signs of DVT, tachycardia, history of recent malignancy, etc.). A score of < 1 indicates low risk, while a score > 6 indicates high risk.

destinations.label: Pulmonary embolism → Pretest probability of pulmonary embolism

YxYnEr.title: Splenic rupture
YxYnEr.description: A potentially life-threatening injury that compromises the structural integrity of the splenic capsule, parenchyma, or vasculature. Mostly secondary to blunt abdominal trauma (e.g. a motor vehicle accident) but can be atraumatic/spontaneous (e.g. infectious mononucleosis, leukemia, malaria). Can cause massive intra-abdominal hemorrhage.

1xY2vr.title: Exophthalmos
1xY2vr.description: An anterior protrusion of the eyeball due to an increase in the intraorbital pressure in patients with endocrine disorders (e.g., Graves disease, Cushing syndrome). In Graves disease, exophthalmos is usually bilateral and associated with other eye signs of Graves ophthalmopathy (e.g., lid lag, diplopia). Often used interchangeably with the term "proptosis," which indicates anterior protrusion of the eye due to a nonendocrine cause.

exYxvr.title: Levodopa test
exYxvr.description: A diagnostic and therapeutic test for Parkinson disease in which a patient is given a dose of levodopa. If symptoms improve after levodopa administration, a diagnosis of Parkinson disease is supported.

UxYbDr.title: Steeple sign
UxYbDr.description: A radiologic sign on a frontal chest x-ray most commonly found in patients with croup. Characterized by subglottic narrowing, giving the upper trachea a conical shape reminiscent of a church steeple or a wine bottle.

QxYuwr.title: Zika virus infection
QxYuwr.description: A mosquito-borne infection that is usually asymptomatic or causes mild fever, joint pain, rash, and conjunctivitis. Endemic to South America, Africa, and Southeast Asia. Can also be transmitted sexually and transplacentally. The most feared complication is fetal microcephaly, which occurs after mothers contract the virus.

PxYW9r.title: Pastia's lines
PxYW9r.description: Linear petechiae in the groin, underarm, and elbow creases that may be seen in patients with scarlet fever.

4xY39r.title: Tender point
4xY39r.description: In osteopathic medicine, tender points are small, hypersensitive areas located in tendons, ligaments, or muscles that typically do not radiate pain when pressed. Tender points are associated with somatic dysfunction treated with counterstrain.

kxYm9r.title: Essential thrombocythemia
kxYm9r.description: A myeloproliferative neoplasm marked by a massive elevation of thrombocytes (≥ 450,000/μL) that cannot be explained by reactive thrombocytosis. It may cause thromboembolic events, petechial bleeding, and vasomotor symptoms such as headache, visual disturbances, or acral paresthesias. In 50% of patients, JAK2 is mutated.

OxYI9r.title: Mucormycosis
OxYI9r.description: A rare, life-threatening fungal infection caused by molds of the order Mucorales, most commonly Rhizopus oryzae. It affects immunocompromised patients and patients with diabetes, particularly those with DKA or poorly controlled blood glucose. It may present as sinusitis with extensive local tissue necrosis and invasion, or as pulmonary infection with extension into the mediastinum.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Opportunistic fungal infections

lxYv9r.title: Glucagonoma
lxYv9r.description: A rare neuroendocrine tumor of the pancreas that secretes glucagon. In >50% of cases, metastasis is present at diagnosis. Clinical findings include impaired glucose tolerance or diabetes mellitus, weight loss, necrolytic migratory erythema, chronic diarrhea, deep vein thrombosis, and depression.  May be associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1.

NxY-9r.title: Antistreptolysin O antibody
NxY-9r.description: An antibody against the hemolytic enzyme streptolysin O, which is produced by group A Streptococci (GAS). Can be measured in the serum to assess for recent GAS infections (e.g., pharyngitis, tonsillitis) in patients with complications of GAS infection (e.g., rheumatic fever, poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis). Serum concentrations increase ~ 1 week after GAS infection, peak between 3 and 6 weeks, and decline after 8 weeks.

wxYhAr.title: Breast engorgement
wxYhAr.description: The painful swelling of breast tissue due to the accumulation of breast milk. Physiological engorgement affects both breasts and typically occurs 3-5 days postpartum, when milk production increases as colostrum transitions to mature milk. Engorgement can also result from insufficient removal of breast milk (e.g., due to decreased breastfeeding or pumping frequency, poor latch), which manifests with tenderness, firmness, and fullness of one or both breasts.

destinations.label: Infant nutrition and breastfeeding → Breastfeeding complications

9xYNAr.title: Pelvic instability
9xYNAr.description: A lack of mechanical stability of the pelvic ring that suggests pelvic fractures or pubic symphysis diastasis. Clinical findings include rotational laxity, asymmetry of the anterior superior iliac spines, and limb length discrepancy.

CxYqAr.title: Rai staging
CxYqAr.description: A classification system used to assess the prognosis in patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Based on clinical features: isolated lymphocytosis, lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly and/or splenomegaly, anemia, and thrombocytopenia (< 100,000/mcL). Defines 5 stages of disease: Rai stages 0-IV.

BxYzAr.title: Hand elevation test
BxYzAr.description: A clinical test used in the diagnosis of carpal tunnel syndrome. The patient holds both hands above the head for one minute. The test is considered positive if the symptoms of CTS (paresthesia and numbness) are reproduced in the affected hand.

destinations.label: Orthopedic examination → Arm and hand examination

yxYd_r.title: Carpal compression test
yxYd_r.description: A clinical test used in the diagnosis of carpal tunnel syndrome. The examiner applies pressure over the carpal tunnel for 30 seconds. The test is considered positive if pain or paresthesia occurs.

AxYR_r.title: Bereavement
AxYR_r.description: The event of losing a loved one. Grief is the natural response to bereavement.

bBYHzr.title: Albuminocytologic dissociation
bBYHzr.description: A diagnostic finding of elevated protein levels and normal cell counts in the cerebral spinal fluid seen in patients with Guillain-Barré syndrome or chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.

XBY9zr.title: Forchheimer sign
XBY9zr.description: A petechial enanthem on the soft palate that may be seen in patients with rubella infection.

cBYa-r.title: String sign
cBYa-r.description: A contrast-filled bowel segment that resembles a string on x-ray. Caused by marked narrowing of the bowel lumen, which may be caused by Crohn disease (usually stenotic terminal ileum), hypertrophic pyloric stenosis (elongated and narrowed pylorus), colon cancer, carcinoid tumor, or gastrointestinal tuberculosis.

WBYP-r.title: Cyclical vomiting syndrome
WBYP-r.description: An idiopathic condition characterized by recurrent episodes of severe vomiting with normal health between episodes. Affects adults and children; most common in children and women. The Rome IV diagnostic criteria for CVS include a history of ≥ 3 distinct episodes of vomiting in the past year, each lasting < 1 week, with at least two episodes in the past six months.

dBYo-r.title: Methacholine
dBYo-r.description: A synthetic choline ester that acts as a non-selective muscarinic agonist. Used in the bronchoprovocation test to diagnose bronchial asthma.

fBYkZ7.title: Myasthenic crisis
fBYkZ7.description: Acute, life-threatening exacerbation of myasthenic symptoms that leads to respiratory failure. Potential triggers include infection, surgery, anesthesia, and pregnancy.

TBY6Z7.title: Atrial tachycardia
TBY6Z7.description: An elevated rhythm (>100 bpm) originating from an ectopic atrial focus instead of the sinoatrial node.

SBYyZ7.title: Tropical sprue
SBYyZ7.description: A disease characterized by chronic diarrhea with subsequent malabsorption in association with a stay in the tropics or subtropics.

hBYc07.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation
hBYc07.description: A procedure used to treat recurrent C. difficile infections in patients who have not responded to at least two appropriate antibiotic regimens. The stool of a healthy donor is combined with normal saline solution and transferred to the gastrointestinal tract of the patient.

lBYva7.title: Pick bodies
lBYva7.description: A neuronal cytoplasmic inclusion of aggregated tau proteins. Occurs in ~40% of patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration and is also found in patients with other neurodegenerative diseases. Positive on silver stain.

NBY-a7.title: Weil's disease
NBY-a7.description: A severe form of leptospirosis characterized by multiorgan involvement (e.g., hemorrhagic diathesis, hepatic dysfunction, renal dysfunction).

mBYVY7.title: Cytomegalovirus mononucleosis
mBYVY7.description: A condition similar to mononucleosis caused by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). Often asymptomatic but can manifest with nonspecific symptoms, such as fever and malaise. Splenomegaly, cervical lymphadenopathy, and tonsillopharyngitis may also occur but is less common than in EBV mononucleosis. A heterophile antibody/monospot test is always negative.

5BYiY7.title: Iron studies
5BYiY7.description: A set of laboratory tests, including total iron-binding capacity, transferrin, and ferritin levels, used to diagnose abnormalities in iron stores (e.g., deficiency or overload) and anemia of chronic disease.

LBYwY7.title: Panic attack
LBYwY7.description: A sudden-onset episode of intense fear associated with ≥ 4 of the following: palpitations, tachycardia, diaphoresis,  trembling, shortness of breath, sensation of choking, chest pain, abdominal distress, dizziness or feeling faint, sensation of chills or heat, paresthesias, derealization or depersonalization, fear of losing control or dying. Can occur due to several conditions, including acute stress disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, anxiety disorders, and panic disorder.

oBY0b7.title: Cytomegalovirus infection
oBY0b7.description: A common infection that is typically asymptomatic in immunocompetent individuals. Can cause a mononucleosis-like syndrome but results in a negative heterophile antibody test. In immunocompromised individuals, CMV infection can cause localized disease (e.g., retinitis, colitis, encephalitis) and severe systemic disease.

JBYsb7.title: Herpes simplex virus infections
JBYsb7.description: An infection caused by herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) or herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2). Most common infections are labial and genital herpes, which manifest with painful ulcerations. Also includes herpetic gingivostomatitis (painful lesions of oropharynx), herpetic whitlow (lesions on fingers), and eczema herpeticum (diffuse lesions, particularly in patients with underlying eczema).

HBYKX7.title: Homer Wright rosettes
HBYKX7.description: A collection of halo-like clusters of cells that surround a central pale area that contains neuropil. Associated with tumors of neuronal origin (e.g., medulloblastoma, primitive neuroectodermal tumors, neuroblastoma, pineoblastoma).

tBYXc7.title: Measles
tBYXc7.description: A highly infectious disease caused by a paramyxovirus that commonly affects nonvaccinated children. Symptoms typically include conjunctivitis, coryza, cough, and pathognomonic Koplik spots on the buccal mucosa, followed by sudden development of a high fever, malaise, and an erythematous, maculopapular rash that originates behind the ears and spreads to the rest of the body toward the feet.

FBYgc7.title: Histoplasmosis
FBYgc7.description: A systemic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum. Manifestations include subacute pneumonia, hilar lymphadenopathy, chronic fibrotic apical infiltrates with cavitation, mucosal ulcers, and splenomegaly.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

8BYOc7.title: Heliotrope rash
8BYOc7.description: An erythematous to violaceous rash on the upper eyelids, sometimes accompanied by edema. Classically associated with dermatomyositis.

uBYpc7.title: Shawl sign
uBYpc7.description: An erythematous or violaceous rash of the upper back, posterior neck, and shoulders that typically develops after sun exposure. Classically associated with dermatomyositis.

EBY8c7.title: X-linked ichthyosis
EBY8c7.description: A hereditary form of ichthyosis caused by recessive mutations in the STS gene on the X-chromosome, which encodes for steroid sulphatase.

vBYAc7.title: Ichthyosis vulgaris
vBYAc7.description: A autosomal dominant disorder of skin cornification caused by a mutation of filaggrin. Patients present with fine, light gray scales that primarily involve the limbs and trunk and spare the intertriginous regions. The lesions begin in infancy, are typically worse during winter, and often disappear spontaneously during adolescence. Ichthyosis vulgaris is the most common type of hereditary ichthyosis.

9BYN17.title: Meyerding classification
9BYN17.description: A radiographic classification that measures the degree of vertebral displacement of the body of the cranial vertebra over the caudal vertebra. There are five grades of displacement: I (0-25%), II (25-50%), III (50-75%), IV (75-100%), and V (greater than 100%, complete anterior displacement or spondyloptosis). Meyerding classification helps in treatment decision-making, as grades III and above often require surgery.

CBYq17.title: CMV retinitis
CBYq17.description: An inflammation of the retina due to infection with cytomegalovirus (CMV). Typically only occurs among patients who are immunocompromised. Typically presents with blurred vision, visual field defects, and eye floaters. Fundoscopy shows a “pizza-pie” appearance caused by retinal hemorrhages, fluffy and granular white opacities around retinal vessels resembling cotton-wool spots, and retinal detachment.

xBYE17.title: Cytomegalovirus esophagitis
xBYE17.description:
A cytomegalovirus infection of the esophagus that mostly affects patients who are immunocompromised. 
Manifestations include odynophagia, fever, and substernal burning pain. Endoscopy shows linear esophageal ulcerations.

BBYz17.title: CMV colitis
BBYz17.description: An infiltration of the large intestine by acute systemic CMV infection, which most commonly occurs in patients who are immunocompromised. Patients present with acute abdominal pain, fever, and watery diarrhea that can progress to bloody diarrhea.

yBYdW7.title: CMV encephalitis
yBYdW7.description: A complication of cytomegalovirus infection that mostly affects patients who are immunocompromised. Typically causes impaired cognitive function and neurological deficits.

ABYRW7.title: Atlantoaxial subluxation
ABYRW7.description: A loss of ligamentous stability between the atlas (C1) and axis (C2), which can result in compression of the spinal cord, medulla, and/or vertebral arteries by the odontoid process, especially upon neck flexion. Most commonly caused by Down syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, and trauma.

zBYrW7.title: ABO incompatibility
zBYrW7.description: A cause of hemolytic disease in the fetus or newborn in which maternal antibodies against antigens of the ABO system enter fetal circulation. Can also refer to an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction that occurs when a patient receives blood against which they have antibodies (e.g. a person with type O blood has anti-A and anti-B antibodies and will react against type A, type B, and type AB blood).

destinations.label: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn → Pathophysiology

ZyYZd7.title: Acute rheumatic fever
ZyYZd7.description: A complication of untreated or subclinical infection with group A streptococcus (GAS), particularly tonsillopharyngitis. Causes nonspecific symptoms (e.g., fever, malaise, and fatigue), pancarditis, migratory polyarthritis, skin findings (e.g., subcutaneous nodules, erythema marginatum), and Sydenham chorea.

YyYnd7.title: Plaque psoriasis
YyYnd7.description: The most common form of psoriasis. It is characterized by symmetrically distributed, thick, scaly, erythematous plaques.

XyY9d7.title: Retinoids
XyY9d7.description: Vitamin A derivatives used in the treatment of mild to moderate acne vulgaris (topical retinoids) or severe acne vulgaris (oral retinoids). Retinoids work to treat acne by reducing keratin production, which blocks skin pores and promotes formation of acne vulgaris. Some retinoids have also been used systemically to treat cancer.

cyYaV7.title: Cutaneous lichen planus
cyYaV7.description: An inflammatory disease characterized by pruritic, polygonal, planar (flat-topped), purple plaques or papules (referred to as the 6 Ps of lichen planus) on the extremities (e.g., wrists and ankles) and trunk, with white lines (Wickham striae) on the surface of the lesions. The course is typically self-limited, with lesions resolving within 1 year.

UyYbe7.title: Bronchopneumonia
UyYbe7.description: A pulmonary infection that affects the bronchioles and adjacent alveoli (patchy distribution). Usually involves the lower lobes and/or the right middle lobe. Primarily caused by pneumococci.

2yYTe7.title: Interstitial pneumonia
2yYTe7.description: A category of lung diseases characterized by inflammation with possible fibrosis of the interstitium of the lung (i.e., the parenchyma between alveoli). Includes secondary interstitial pneumonia caused by exposure to pathogens (e.g., Mycoplasma) and environmental factors (e.g., asbestos, radiation) as well as idiopathic interstitial pneumonias (e.g., acute interstitial pneumonia, usual interstitial pneumonia).

4yY327.title: Excessive daytime sleepiness
4yY327.description: A symptom characterized by an inability to maintain daytime wakefulness, often resulting in drowsiness or sleep in inappropriate situations. Causes include inadequate or poor quality nighttime sleep (e.g., due to obstructive sleep apnea or insomnia), diseases affecting the brain (e.g., tumors, metabolic encephalopathies), major depressive disorder, and certain sleep disorders (e.g., narcolepsy, hypersomnolence disorder).

kyYm27.title: Major depressive disorder with peripartum onset
kyYm27.description: A psychiatric condition with depressive symptoms meeting the criteria for a major depressive episode, with symptoms starting during pregnancy or within 4 weeks of delivery. In the DSM-5, antepartum and postpartum depression are referred to as major depressive disorder with peripartum onset.

destinations.label: Major depressive disorder → Depression in the peripartum period

NyY-27.title: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
NyY-27.description: A non-neoplastic, glandular and stromal hyperplasia of the transition zone of the prostate. It is a common disorder that affects ∼ 40% of the male population by 50 years of age.

MyYMf7.title: Dapsone
MyYMf7.description: An antifolate antibiotic used in the treatment of dermatitis herpetiformis, leprosy, toxoplasmosis, and chloroquine-resistant malaria. Also used for Pneumocystis jiroveci prophylaxis.

nyY7f7.title: Pentamidine
nyY7f7.description: An antimicrobial agent with a poorly understood mechanism that is used to treat African trypanosomiasis, babesiosis, leishmaniasis, and to prevent or treat Pneumocystis pneumonia (especially in patients unable to take TMP-SMX).

LyYwf7.title: Thumbprint sign
LyYwf7.description:
A radiologic sign that describes two phenomena: 
1. An enlarged epiglottis (supraglottic narrowing), which has an appearance similar to a thumb on a lateral neck x-ray
2. An indentation in the bowel wall caused by haustral edema (e.g., from ischemic colitis, inflammatory bowel disease, infection), which has an appearance similar to a thumb on CT scan or abdominal x-ray

media.title: Thumb and vallecula signs in acute infectious epiglottitis

KyYUT7.title: Ethylene glycol
KyYUT7.description: An alcohol found in various chemical products (e.g., antifreeze). Ingestion (e.g., as a substitute for ethanol) causes sweet-smelling breath, altered mental status, hallucinations, seizures, dyspnea, anion gap metabolic acidosis, and signs of acute kidney injury.

destinations.label: Toxic alcohol poisoning → Ethylene glycol poisoning

6yYjT7.title: Palivizumab
6yYjT7.description: A short-acting monoclonal antibody against respiratory syncytial virus fusion protein (RSV F protein). Used for RSV prophylaxis.

JyYsT7.title: Anti-Ro/SSA antibody
JyYsT7.description: An antibody against ribonucleoprotein antigens (Ro proteins) of epithelial cells, especially of the salivary glands. Classically associated with Sjögren syndrome and systemic lupus erythematosus when found with anti-La antibodies.

qyYCT7.title: Anti-La/SSB antibody
qyYCT7.description: An antibody against ribonucleoprotein antigens (La proteins) of epithelial cells, especially of the salivary glands. Usually found with anti-Ro antibodies. The presence of anti-Ro and anti-La antibodies is associated with Sjögren syndrome and systemic lupus erythematosus.

7yY4g7.title: Bismuth-Corlette classification
7yY4g7.description: A classification system for hilar cholangiocarcinoma that includes preoperative assessment of local tumor spread and extent of resection. Type I tumors are distal to the hepatic duct confluence; type IV tumors extend into the bilateral proximal hepatic ducts.

HyYKg7.title: Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization
HyYKg7.description: A minimally invasive procedure used for the treatment of liver tumors and cholangiocarcinoma. Involves either the sequential injection of a chemotherapeutic and an embolic agent or the injection of drug-eluting beads, which reduce the blood supply to the tumor and induce local cytotoxicity.

syYtg7.title: Microvascular decompression
syYtg7.description: A neurosurgical procedure used to treat trigeminal neuralgia. Following craniotomy, a blood vessel that compresses the trigeminal nerve root is identified and separated from the nerve.

tyYXS7.title: Vulvovaginitis
tyYXS7.description: An inflammation of vulvar and/or vaginal tissue. Further subdivided into infectious etiologies (e.g., bacterial, fungal) and noninfectious etiologies (e.g., allergic, mechanical). Manifestations include pruritus, irritation, discharge, odor, and dysuria.

FyYgS7.title: Neuhauser sign
FyYgS7.description: A radiographic finding of a mottled ("soap bubble") appearance in the distal ileum and/or caecum as a result of meconium mixing with swallowed air, often caused by meconium ileus. Can also occur in other conditions, including necrotizing enterocolitis and ileal atresia.

EyY8S7.title: Bronchial challenge test
EyY8S7.description: A group of pulmonary tests used to identify airway hyperresponsiveness and bronchoconstriction in response to direct, nonallergic stimuli (e.g., methacholine, histamine) or indirect stimuli (e.g., exercise, hyperventilation). Can help distinguish bronchial asthma from other obstructive lung diseases.

destinations.label: Pulmonary function testing → Specialized testing in obstructive lung disease

DyY1h7.title: Leukorrhea
DyY1h7.description: A yellow-white vaginal discharge with >10 WBCs/HPF on microscopy. Can be physiological, but pathological discharge should be suspected if the discharge is malodorous, the vagina is pruritic or erythematous, or the cervix is tender. Leukorrhea in newborns can result from transient in utero exposure to maternal estrogen and requires no treatment.

yyYd37.title: Light-chain amyloidosis
yyYd37.description: The most common type of systemic amyloidosis. Caused by a clonal plasma cell proliferative disorder that results in tissue deposition of amyloid fibrils composed of abnormally folded immunoglobulin light chain proteins. Often affects multiple organ systems (e.g., manifesting as nephrotic syndrome, restrictive cardiomyopathy, peripheral neuropathy, chronic diarrhea,  fatigue, and/or weight loss).

AyYR37.title: Reactive amyloidosis
AyYR37.description: A subtype of amyloidosis characterized by systemic deposition of serum amyloid A protein (AA protein) in multiple organs. Associated with chronic inflammatory conditions (e.g., inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis) and chronic infections.

ZAYZR7.title: Irritant diaper dermatitis
ZAYZR7.description: The most common cause of diaper dermatitis (diaper rash), a cutaneous reaction localized to the diaper area. Typically occurs in infants 9–12 months of age. Caused by persistent moisture (e.g., from urine and feces) in the diaper area, often due to infrequent diaper changes.

aAYQR7.title: Specific developmental disorders of scholastic skills
aAYQR7.description: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by a combination of genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors that affect an individual's ability to acquire and use academic skills despite having average or above average intelligence and adequate educational opportunities.

dAYoi7.title: Sunset sign
dAYoi7.description: A clinical finding that is characterized by the downward deviation of the eyes. Associated with increased intracranial pressure (e.g., due to hydrocephalus) in infants or young children.

eAYxi7.title: Oral thrush
eAYxi7.description: A localized, mucocutaneous Candida infection. It is characterized by white plaques in the oral cavity that can typically be scraped off, exposing red, inflamed patches, and/or areas of bleeding. Other manifestations include a cottony feeling in the mouth, loss of taste, and, in some cases, pain while eating.

UAYbQ7.title: Barrel chest
UAYbQ7.description: An increased anteroposterior diameter of the thorax caused by hyperinflation of the lungs due to air trapping. Associated with advanced stage chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

fAYkQ7.title: Flat wart
fAYkQ7.description: A yellow-brown cutaneous papule with a smooth surface caused by infection with the cutaneous serotypes of HPV. Typically affects the face or shins. Sometimes manifests with a linear pattern secondary to autoinoculation.

SAYyQ7.title: Common wart
SAYyQ7.description: A rough, scaly papule or plaque (sometimes with a cauliflower-like appearance) caused by infection with the cutaneous serotypes of HPV. Affects the elbows, knees, fingers, and/or palms and is usually painless.

3AYSj7.title: Type I hypersensitivity reaction
3AYSj7.description: An IgE antibody-mediated reaction in which antigens bind to preformed IgE on the surface of mast cells and basophils, causing the release of histamine and other inflammatory mediators and the synthesis of leukotrienes and prostaglandins. These mediators induce vasodilation, increased capillary permeability, smooth muscle contraction, and inflammatory cell chemotaxis.

destinations.label: Hypersensitivity reactions → Type I hypersensitivity reaction

RAYlj7.title: Type II hypersensitivity reaction
RAYlj7.description: An IgG or IgM antibody-mediated hypersensitivity reaction. Antibodies bound to their targets induce antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (e.g., immune thrombocytopenia, acute hemolytic transfusion reactions), complement-mediated inflammation (e.g., Goodpasture syndrome), or cell surface receptor interactions (e.g., myasthenia gravis, Graves disease).

destinations.label: Hypersensitivity reactions → Type II hypersensitivity reaction

iAYJj7.title: Type III hypersensitivity reaction
iAYJj7.description: An overreaction of the immune system that accounts for many glomerulonephritides and vasculitides, serum sickness, and the Arthus reaction. It is caused by immune complex deposition, which leads to complement activation and release of lysosomal enzymes from neutrophils, which subsequently results in cell death and inflammation. Clinical features strongly depend on the underlying etiology but tend to be generalized (immune complexes are distributed throughout the body).

destinations.label: Hypersensitivity reactions → Type III hypersensitivity reaction

media.title: Animation: Immune Complex-Mediated Hypersensitivity - Type III Hypersensitivity Reaction

QAYuj7.title: Type IV hypersensitivity reaction
QAYuj7.description: A T-cell mediated delayed hypersensitivity reaction involved in contact dermatitis and type IV drug reactions (e.g., ampicillin rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis). Presensitized CD4+ T cells recognize antigens on antigen-presenting cells, leading to the release of inflammatory cytokines, while presensitized CD8+ T cells recognize antigens on somatic cells, leading to cell-mediated cytotoxicity.

destinations.label: Hypersensitivity reactions → Type IV hypersensitivity reaction

PAYWP7.title: Carcinoma of the penis
PAYWP7.description: A rare cancer that typically manifests with a lump or ulcerative lesion on the penis. Mainly occurs in older men. Risk factors include untreated phimosis, infection with human papillomavirus, and smoking. Overall prognosis is determined by the presence and extent of regional lymph node involvement.

OAYIP7.title: Zinc deficiency
OAYIP7.description: The classic triad of symptoms includes acral or periorificial dermatitis, alopecia, and diarrhea. Also causes impaired wound healing, hypogonadism, and altered taste and smell. Acrodermatitis enteropathica is an inherited form; acquired causes include insufficient dietary intake, liver/renal disease, and Crohn disease.

5AYi47.title: Portosystemic shunt
5AYi47.description: A connection between the portal vein and either the inferior or superior vena cava that allows portal venous blood to bypass the liver and enter systemic circulation directly. Can be created for therapeutic purposes, e.g., transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunts and surgical portosystemic shunts, or can be a pathological response in patients with portal hypertension.

MAYM47.title: Caffeine halothane contracture test
MAYM47.description: A test for malignant hyperthermia susceptibility that is performed by exposing a skeletal muscle biopsy sample to ryanodine receptor 1 agonists such as caffeine or halothane. High levels of contractility indicate susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia.

KAYUk7.title: Abdominal compartment syndrome
KAYUk7.description: A sustained intraabdominal pressure > 20 mm Hg that is associated with organ dysfunction or failure (e.g. acute kidney failure, respiratory failure, shock).

JAYsk7.title: KOH test
JAYsk7.description: A quick, inexpensive test to identify fungal infections (e.g., dermatophytoses, Candidiasis) or bacterial vaginosis. May be used to examine skin cells or vaginal fluid. A sample of skin scraping or vaginal fluid is evaluated under a microscope after the addition of potassium hydroxide (KOH). KOH is a strong alkali that dissolves cells and protein debris in specimens but leaves fungal elements (e.g., budding yeasts, hyphae, spores, and pseudohyphae). The addition of KOH also leads to the production of amines in patients with bacterial vaginosis, giving a characteristic odor (positive whiff test).

rAYfO7.title: Streptococcus gallolyticus
rAYfO7.description: A gram-positive bacterium, formerly known as Streptococcus bovis biotype I, that causes infective endocarditis. It is strongly associated with the development of colorectal cancer.

HAYKO7.title: Vanishing bile duct syndrome
HAYKO7.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by paucity or absence of bile ducts. Caused by congenital disorders that impair intrahepatic bile duct formation (e.g., congenital hepatic fibrosis, Alagille syndrome, cystic fibrosis, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency) and disorders that damage the biliary tree (e.g., primary biliary cholangitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis, chronic graft-versus-host disease, transplant rejection).

GAYBO7.title: Cerebral venous thrombosis
GAYBO7.description: A thrombotic obstruction of the cerebral veins and/or related anatomical structures (dural sinuses) which drain blood from the brain. Women are affected more often than men. Predisposing factors include prothrombotic states, pregnancy, oral contraceptive use, malignancy, and infection.

DAY1N7.title: Fundoplication
DAY1N7.description: A surgical procedure in which the gastric fundus is wrapped around the lower esophagus to form a cuff, effectively narrowing the distal esophagus and the gastroesophageal junction to prevent reflux of stomach contents. Used to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and hiatal hernia.

_AY5m7.title: Beck triad
_AY5m7.description: A clinical triad of hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and distended neck veins that is seen in cardiac tamponade.

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Clinical features

zAYrm7.title: Drug-induced esophagitis
zAYrm7.description: A condition characterized by esophageal mucosal irritation (e.g., from increased acidity, alkalinity, or osmolality) caused by oral medications. Common causes include antibiotics, anti-inflammatory drugs (e.g., aspirin) and bisphosphonates.

media.title: Esophagitis in the mid- to upper esophagus

0_Ye57.title: Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure
0_Ye57.description: An indirect measure of left atrial pressure and, therefore, an estimation for preload. Measured by advancing a balloon catheter into a small pulmonary artery and then inflating the catheter. The PCWP is then measured distal to the inflated balloon. Normal: 4–12 mm Hg.

b_YH57.title: Cerebral shunt
b_YH57.description: A long-term treatment for hydrocephalus intended to return excess cerebrospinal fluid from the ventricle to systemic circulation, most commonly through the peritoneum. Frequently complicated by obstruction and infection.

X_Y957.title: Ergotamine
X_Y957.description: A drug in the group of ergot alkaloids (produced by certain fungi) that works by constricting blood vessels around the brain. Indicated in the treatment of migraine headaches.

c_YaM7.title: Dandy-Walker malformation
c_YaM7.description: A congenital malformation caused by failure of the fourth ventricle to close. Leads to persistence of Blake's pouch (cyst in the 4th ventricle) and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia. May present with a variety of neurologic abnormalities (e.g., ataxia) and hydrocephalus. In its syndromic form, it may also be associated with a variety of extracranial abnormalities (e.g., craniofacial abnormalities, cardiac defects).

1_Y2M7.title: Macrocephaly
1_Y2M7.description: A head circumference that is > 2 standard deviations above the mean size for a given age and sex (e.g., > 97th percentile on the WHO growth charts). May be seen in individuals with hydrocephalus, neurofibromatosis, tuberous sclerosis, skeletal dysplasia, acromegaly, intracranial hemorrhage, and cerebral metabolic diseases (e.g., Tay-Sachs disease, maple syrup urine disease).

media.title: Facial features of Fragile X syndrome

V_YGM7.title: Water deprivation test
V_YGM7.description: A study that indirectly assesses antidiuretic hormone activity to determine the cause of hypotonic polyuria (i.e., primary polydipsia or central or nephrogenic diabetes insipidus). Urine concentrating capacity (based on plasma and urine osmolality, urine volume, and serum sodium) is evaluated at baseline, then every 1–2 hours during prolonged water deprivation. This test is often followed by a desmopressin challenge test.

U_Ybn7.title: Serum-ascites albumin gradient
U_Ybn7.description: The difference between albumin concentration in ascitic fluid and albumin concentration in the serum. A SAAG >1.1 g/dL indicates that portal hypertension is the likely underlying cause of ascites.

2_YTn7.title: Fluid wave test
2_YTn7.description: A physical examination maneuver performed to evaluate for the presence of ascites. With the patient supine and a second examiner's hand on the midline (to stop transmission through fat), place one hand on the patient's lateral abdominal wall and tap the opposite lateral abdominal wall with the other hand. A palpable wave impulse suggests the presence of ascites.

f_Ykn7.title: Shifting dullness
f_Ykn7.description: A physical finding characterized by a change of resonance from dull to tympanic when the patient changes from supine to lateral decubitus position. Suggests the presence of free fluid in the abdomen, which migrates as the patient changes position.

T_Y6n7.title: Mobitz II second-degree AV block
T_Y6n7.description: A type of second-degree atrioventricular block characterized by a constant PR interval with P waves that intermittently are not followed by a QRS complex (i.e., a dropped beat). Conduction of the atrial impulses to the ventricles follows a regular pattern (e.g., 2:1 block). Can progress to third-degree atrioventricular block.

media.title: Mobitz type II second-degree atrioventricular block and bifascicular block

k_Ymo7.title: Beriberi
k_Ymo7.description: A collection of symptoms attributed to Vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency that manifest in "dry" or "wet" forms. Dry beriberi occurs due to damage to peripheral nerves, and is characterized by numbness in the hands and feet, loss of tendon reflexes, paralysis, nystagmus, pain, and vomiting. Wet beriberi is characterized by edematous cardiac tissues, leading to high output cardiac failure, dyspnea on exertion, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and tachycardia.

m_YVK7.title: First-degree atrioventricular block
m_YVK7.description: A type of atrioventricular block characterized by a PR interval > 200 ms with normal atrial to ventricular conduction (SA node rate = heart rate). Usually asymptomatic.

5_YiK7.title: Second-degree atrioventricular block
5_YiK7.description: A type of atrioventricular block further subdivided into Mobitz type I block (Wenckebach) and Mobitz type II block. Characterized by P waves that are not always followed by a QRS complex.

M_YMK7.title: Third-degree atrioventricular block
