M_YMK7.description: A complete dissociation of conduction between the atria and ventricles. ECG shows P waves and QRS complexes that occur at regular intervals, but independently of each other. Ventricular contraction is stimulated by impulses that are generated close to the AV node or bundle of His (ventricular escape). Manifestations include pronounced bradycardia (< 40 bpm), cerebral hypoperfusion, heart failure, Stokes-Adams attacks, and cardiac arrest.

destinations.label: Atrioventricular block → Third-degree AV block (complete heart block)

n_Y7K7.title: Hyponatremia
n_Y7K7.description: A serum sodium concentration of < 135 mEq/L (some sources may use a cutoff of < 136 mEq/L). Etiologies include thiazide diuretic use, adrenal insufficiency, and syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion. Manifestations include altered mental status, nausea, vomiting, muscle weakness, and hyporeflexia. If severe, can cause seizures, coma, and death.

L_YwK7.title: Hypernatremia
L_YwK7.description: A serum sodium concentration > 145 mEq/L (some sources may use a cutoff of > 146 mEq/L). Etiologies include insufficient free water intake, often in combination with excess water loss. Manifestations include altered mental status, thirst, ataxia, and hyperreflexia. If severe, can cause seizures, coma, and death.

K_YU67.title: Beer potomania
K_YU67.description: A condition of dilutional hyponatremia secondary to limited renal free water excretion as a result of extremely low levels of dietary solute intake. Typically seen in patients with chronic alcohol use (especially beer drinkers) and a concomitant poor diet because alcohol does not contain significant protein (needed to form urea), sodium, or potassium but contains enough calories to prevent catabolism of the body's protein stores to urea. Can also occur in patients with severe dietary restriction (e.g., elderly patients on a tea-and-toast diet).

6_Yj67.title: Laparoscopic Heller myotomy
6_Yj67.description: Surgical procedure used to treat achalasia, in which the lower esophageal sphincter is incised longitudinally to re-enable passage of food or liquids to the stomach.

p_YL67.title: Central venous access
p_YL67.description: A catheter terminating in a central vein, such as the subclavian, internal jugular, or femoral vein, that can be used for hemodynamic monitoring and to administer medication and fluids.

media.title: Insertion of a central venous catheter (CVC)

I_YYp7.title: Angle of His
I_YYp7.description: The angle that is formed between the esophagus and the gastric fundus. Normally measures 50-60°.

r_Yfp7.title: Inclusion-body myositis
r_Yfp7.description: An inflammatory myopathy characterized by slowly progressive weakness of both the proximal and distal muscle groups. Typically seen in men over the age of 50. Muscle biopsy shows endomysial inflammation and characteristic intramuscular vacuoles that resemble inclusion bodies of aggregated proteins.

s_Ytp7.title: Jaffe-Lichtenstein syndrome
s_Ytp7.description: A rare congenital condition caused by sporadic mutation of the GNAS1 gene. Results in the replacement of bone with fibrous tissue that appears radiolucent on x-rays. Manifestations include bone deformities (especially of the long bones) with associated pain, uneven growth, and/or pathologic fractures.

G_YBp7.title: Bartholin gland carcinoma
G_YBp7.description: A rare type of vulvar carcinoma that arises from a Bartholin gland. Primarily occurs among postmenopausal women and typically presents with gradual, painless enlargement of the gland. Diagnosis is made via histologic examination of a biopsy specimen. Treatment involves surgical resection.

destinations.label: Bartholin gland cyst and abscess → Differential diagnoses

t_YXJ7.title: Lewy bodies
t_YXJ7.description: α-Synuclein-positive intracytoplasmatic inclusions in neurons, especially in cortical and subcortical regions. Cause neuronal degradation. Characteristic of Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies.

destinations.label: Parkinson-plus syndromes → Dementia with Lewy bodies

F_YgJ7.title: Spinal epidural hematoma
F_YgJ7.description: A hemorrhage into the epidural space of the spinal canal. Commonly caused by venous bleeds (e.g., due to coagulopathy or overanticoagulation). Typically manifests with acute, severe back pain and signs of spinal cord compression (e.g., motor and sensory dysfunction distal to the site of compression).

destinations.label: Back pain → Urgent spinal causes of acute back pain

8_YOJ7.title: Neoplastic meningitis
8_YOJ7.description: A neurologic complication of cancer in which a primary tumor metastasizes to the meninges. Most commonly caused by melanoma, lung, breast, and gastrointestinal cancers. Manifestations include signs of increased intracranial pressure, cranial nerve deficits, encephalopathy, radiculopathy, cauda equina syndrome.

u_YpJ7.title: Fractional urine examination
u_YpJ7.description: A collection of urine of a specified quantity or duration (in contrast to the entire amount voided during a full day). Can be used to diagnose conditions affecting the kidneys or prostate.

E_Y8J7.title: Two-glass test
E_Y8J7.description: A fractional urine examination to diagnose chronic bacterial prostatitis. Urine cultures are obtained before and after prostatic massage. The prostate is confirmed as the source of infection if bacteria are only found in the second sample or if the bacterial count of the second sample is 10-fold higher than that of the first sample.

C_Yqq7.title: Uncal herniation
C_Yqq7.description: Displacement of the medial temporal lobe (the uncus), from the middle fossa, across the tentorial opening and into the posterior fossa due to elevated ICP (usually secondary to intracranial hemorrhage or cerebral edema). This causes compression of the ipsilateral CN III, the ipsilateral posterior cerebral artery, as well as the contralateral cerebral peduncle, and presents as abducted/depressed ipsilateral eyes with fixed, dilated pupils, occipital infarction, and ipsilateral paralysis.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Subtypes and variants

x_YEq7.title: Foramen magnum herniation
x_YEq7.description: Structures of the posterior fossa (e.g., cerebellar tonsils, medulla) herniate at the foramen magnum, causing impaired consciousness, decerebrate posturing, apnea, impaired circulation, and death.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Subtypes and variants

B_Yzq7.title: Hemoglobin H disease
B_Yzq7.description: A type of alpha thalassemia in which there is a defect in 3 of the 4 alleles responsible for coding of the α-globin chains, which results in excessive production of pathologically altered hemoglobin H (HbH). The features of HbH disease usually appear in the neonatal period and are characterized by mild to moderate anemia, hepatosplenomegaly, and yellowing of the eyes and skin (jaundice).

y_YdI7.title: Hemoglobin Bart's disease
y_YdI7.description: A form of thalassemia in which 4 defective α-chain coding alleles result in excessive production of pathologically altered Hb Bart consisting of 4 γ-chains. The condition is incompatible with life (resulting in death in utero or shortly after birth) and is characterized by intrauterine ascites and hydrops fetalis, severe hepatosplenomegaly, and often cardiac and skeletal anomalies

A_YRI7.title: Mitral regurgitation
A_YRI7.description: A valvular disease characterized by leakage of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium due to incomplete closure of the mitral valve during systole.

media.title: Heart murmur in ventricular septal defect, mitral regurgitation, and tricuspid regurgitation

z_YrI7.title: Culdocentesis
z_YrI7.description: A diagnostic procedure in which a spinal needle is introduced through the posterior vaginal fornix to aspirate intraperitoneal fluid from the pouch of Douglas. Historically used to diagnose hemoperitoneum due to a ruptured ectopic pregnancy; now largely replaced by ultrasonography.

ZzYZr7.title: Subacute combined degeneration of spinal cord
ZzYZr7.description: A progressive and symmetric demyelinating disease that involves the spinocerebellar tracts, lateral corticospinal tract, and dorsal columns of the spinal cord. Manifestations include spasticity, ataxia, and decreased proprioception and vibratory sensation. The most common etiology is vitamin B₁₂ deficiency.

0zYer7.title: HLA-B27 associations
0zYer7.description: A specific allele of the class I major histocompatibility complex that is strongly associated with seronegative arthropathies (e.g., ankylosing spondylitis). This allele is present in 6% of the general population but in ~ 90% of patients with seronegative arthropathies.

azYQr7.title: Intrinsic factor
azYQr7.description: A protein produced by the parietal cells of the stomach that facilitates vitamin B12 absorption in the ileum. Deficiency of intrinsic factor (e.g., due to atrophic gastritis, or following gastrectomy) leads to vitamin B12 deficiency.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

YzYnr7.title: Tachycardia-bradycardia syndrome
YzYnr7.description: A subtype of sinus node dysfunction in which there are alternating periods of bradyarrhythmia (e.g., sinus bradycardia, sinus pauses, sinoatrial exit block) with supraventricular tachyarrhythmia (e.g., atrial tachycardia, atrial flutter, atrial fibrillation).

destinations.label: Sinus node dysfunction → Subtypes and variants

bzYHr7.title: Arthus reaction
bzYHr7.description: A rare, localized, type III hypersensitivity reaction characterized by immune complex deposition in the walls of dermal blood vessels. Caused by an immune response via complement activation after intradermal injection of antigens (e.g., tetanus or diphtheria toxoid). Manifests with pain, swelling, erythema, and occasionally necrosis at the injection site.

czYa77.title: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome
czYa77.description: A syndrome characterized by inflammation of the liver capsule that occurs in women as a complication of pelvic inflammatory disease. Clinical features include fever, nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain, and/or pleuritic chest pain.

1zY277.title: Tertiary hyperparathyroidism
1zY277.description: High levels of parathyroid hormone caused by persistent secondary hyperparathyroidism (sHPT), usually as a result of chronic kidney disease. tHPT causes reactive hypercalcemia in response to the long-term elevation of PTH.

WzYP77.title: Carcinomatous meningitis
WzYP77.description: A type of neoplastic meningitis caused by metastatic solid tumors (e.g., lung or breast cancer), though sometimes used to describe all types of neoplastic meningitis. Manifestations include radicular pain, mental status change, focal neurologic deficits, and headache. Typically a sign of advanced disease with systemic spread and poor prognosis.

dzYo77.title: Lymphomatous meningitis
dzYo77.description: A type of neoplastic meningitis caused by metastatic lymphoma. Manifestations include radicular pain, mental status change, focal neurologic deficits, and headache. Typically a sign of advanced disease with systemic spread and poor prognosis.

fzYkH7.title: Hiatal hernia
fzYkH7.description: The protrusion of an abdominal structure (most commonly the stomach) through the esophageal hiatus into the thoracic cavity. Further classified into sliding, paraesophageal, mixed, and complex types.

TzY6H7.title: Mixing study
TzY6H7.description: A test used in the workup of prolonged PTT in which the patient's plasma is mixed with normal plasma in vitro. If the prolonged aPTT is caused by a lack of clotting factors, the factors contained in the normal plasma will normalize the aPTT. In the presence of a clotting inhibitor such as lupus anticoagulant, the clotting time (aPTT) remains increased.

gzYFH7.title: Hyperpituitarism
gzYFH7.description: A condition caused by overactivity of the pituitary gland, typically due to a pituitary adenoma. Results in hypersecretion of a pituitary hormone via hyperproduction.

3zYSs7.title: Ischemic colitis
3zYSs7.description: A condition characterized by hypoperfusion injury of the large bowel from hypotension, vasoconstriction, thrombosis, or other conditions that may reduce blood flow. Mostly transient and self-limited (nongangrenous form), but can also lead to severe acute ischemia with bowel infarction (gangrenous form).

media.title: Infarction of small intestine with ischemia

RzYls7.title: Romana sign
RzYls7.description: A unilateral, painless edema of the eyelids and periocular tissue seen in patients with Chagas disease when the portal of entry of T. cruzi is the conjunctiva.

QzYus7.title: Loeffler syndrome
QzYus7.description: An eosinophilic pulmonary disease caused by the passage of parasites (e.g., Ascaris lumbricoides, hookworms, Strongyloides stercoralis) through the lungs. Characterized by transient migratory pulmonary opacities and peripheral blood eosinophilia, sometimes with mild respiratory symptoms (most commonly a dry cough).

destinations.label: Eosinophilic lung diseases → Simple pulmonary eosinophilia (Loeffler syndrome)

jzY_s7.title: Necator americanus
jzY_s7.description: A common hookworm. Like other hookworms, it is transmitted through cutaneous penetration by larvae. Causes cutaneous larva migrans (a pruritic, serpiginous rash). Can also cause anemia by consuming blood from the gastrointestinal tract.

4zY3G7.title: Prolactinoma
4zY3G7.description: A usually benign, prolactin-producing tumor of the anterior pituitary gland. Symptoms are due to hyperprolactinemia (e.g., galactorrhea, amenorrhea, gynecomastia, and loss of libido) and/or due to mass effect (headaches, bitemporal hemianopia because of compression of the optic chiasm).

kzYmG7.title: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause
kzYmG7.description: A set of signs and symptoms that result from hypoestrogenism and affect the genitourinary tract. Causes vulvovaginal atrophy (which may lead to vaginal dryness and irritation, dyspareunia, loss of labial fat pads, and bleeding after sex) and lower urinary tract atrophy (which may lead to urinary incontinence, dysuria, and frequent urinary tract infections).

lzYvG7.title: Pupillary light reflex
lzYvG7.description: A brainstem reflex elicited by shining a light into each eye. Normally, the pupil constricts. The reflex is mediated by the afferent sensory pathway of CN II and the efferent motor pathway of CN III.

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Pupillary response

NzY-G7.title: Transsphenoidal hypophysectomy
NzY-G7.description: The surgical resection of a part of or the complete pituitary gland by introducing an endoscope to the anterior wall of the sphenoid sinus either through the nostrils or through an incision in the buccal mucosa under the upper lip. The pituitary fossa can then be accessed via the sphenoid sinus.

mzYVt7.title: Primary hypothyroidism
mzYVt7.description: Hypothyroidism that is primarily a result of a thyroid gland disorder. Common causes include Hashimoto's thyroiditis, postpartum thyroiditis, subacute granulomatous thyroiditis, status post thyroidectomy, radioiodine therapy, certain medications (e.g., amiodarone, methimazole, propylthiouracil), or an iodine deficiency. Patients have decreased T3/T4 levels and increased TSH levels.

5zYit7.title: Secondary hypothyroidism
5zYit7.description: A condition of hypothyroidism that results from a pituitary disorder. Characterized by decreased TSH and T3/T4 concentrations.

ozY0F7.title: Disulfiram-like reaction
ozY0F7.description: A hangover-like reaction characterized by nausea, severe flushing, tachycardia, and hypotension that is caused by the accumulation of acetaldehyde as a result of combined intake of alcohol and certain drugs (e.g., sulfonylureas, some cephalosporins). The name derives from the drug disulfiram, which is used in the treatment of chronic alcoholism and induces the same symptoms when a patient consumes alcohol.

6zYjF7.title: Pyruvate kinase deficiency
6zYjF7.description: An autosomal recessive defect of erythrocyte pyruvate kinase, which is necessary for glycolysis in RBCs. Causes chronic hemolytic anemia of variable severity.

pzYLF7.title: Polychromasia
pzYLF7.description: Ability to stain erythrocytes with both acidic and alkaline substances. The alkaline substances bind to ribosomal RNA that is only present in very early stages of erythrocyte maturation. The physiological percentage of polychromatic erythrocytes is < 0.1%, but can be increased in any disease affecting erythropoiesis

7zY487.title: Pathergy skin testing
7zY487.description: A test used to assess for a nonspecific, exaggerated skin reaction to minor trauma. Usually consists of a 5-mm skin prick in the forearm or oral prick in the mucous membrane of the lower lip with a 20-gauge needle. Considered positive if a papule, pustule, or oral ulcer appears at the site after 48 hours.

GzYB87.title: Succussion splash
GzYB87.description: A splashing sound created by the movement of gastric contents. To elicit the succussion splash, place the stethoscope over the epigastrium of a supine patient. Hold the hips of the patient and gently shake the abdomen. The succussion splash is physiologic immediately after a meal. If present after ≥ 3 hours of fasting, it suggests a gastric outlet obstruction.

tzYXu7.title: Sister Mary Joseph's nodule
tzYXu7.description: An enlarged periumbilical lymph node. Classically associated with metastatic gastric cancer but can develop in other abdominopelvic malignancies (e.g., gallbladder, pancreas, kidneys, testicles, prostate, ovaries).

8zYOu7.title: Cutaneous larva migrans
8zYOu7.description: The cutaneous manifestation of a nematode infection, most often with a zoonotic hookworm (i.e., Ancylostoma braziliense and Ancylostoma caninum). Characterized by pruritic, serpiginous marks (cutaneous lesions with progressive, creeping, snake-like borders) that represent an allergic reaction to the cutaneous migration of larvae.

vzYAu7.title: Rapid plasma reagin test
vzYAu7.description: A common serologic (nontreponemal) test for syphilis that detects nonspecific anticardiolipin antibodies. Most commonly used for screening purposes but can also be used to track disease activity and treatment response. Highly sensitive but nonspecific.

wzYhE7.title: Cholinergic poisoning
wzYhE7.description: A syndrome caused by substance-mediated overstimulation of the postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors (AChRs). Features of muscarinic AChR hyperactivity include diarrhea, urination, miosis, bradycardia, bronchospasm, bronchorrhea, emesis, lacrimation, lethargy, sweating, and salivation (DUMBBBELLSS). Features of nicotinic AChR hyperactivity include tachycardia, hypertension, and skeletal muscle weakness.

xzYEE7.title: Edrophonium
xzYEE7.description: A rapid-onset and short-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that was historically used in the evaluation of myasthenia gravis (edrophonium test). This test has now been replaced by more sensitive and specific autoantibody tests.

yzYdv7.title: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth
yzYdv7.description: A condition characterized by the pathological increase of bacteria in the small intestine, which can lead to bloating, flatulence, abdominal discomfort, and, in severe cases, diarrhea, malabsorption, and poor oral intake.

-zYDv7.title: Nephrotoxicity
-zYDv7.description: A property of a substance to impair renal function. Nephrotoxic substances include certain metals (e.g., lead, mercury, and cadmium salts), radiocontrast agents, and organic solvents (e.g., hydrocarbons). Many drugs also have nephrotoxic properties at high doses and/or after long-term use (e.g., aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, vancomycin, lithium, cyclophosphamide, cyclosporine, NSAIDs).

Z-YZD7.title: Overt hypothyroidism
Z-YZD7.description: A state of low circulating thyroid hormones accompanied by clinical signs and symptoms, including dry skin, cold intolerance, fatigue, muscle cramps, voice changes, and constipation.

0-YeD7.title: Mixed dementia
0-YeD7.description: Dementia that has features of both Alzheimer dementia and vascular dementia.

b-YHD7.title: Fibroadenoma
b-YHD7.description: A benign tumor of the breast that is composed of fibrous and glandular tissue. It is the most common breast tumor in women < 35 years of age.

X-Y9D7.title: Phyllodes tumor
X-Y9D7.description: A rare fibroepithelial breast tumor that typically manifests in individuals between 40–50 years of age as a large, painless, multinodular breast mass. Most commonly benign but can be malignant.

c-Yaw7.title: Intraductal papilloma
c-Yaw7.description: Benign, solitary or multiple polypoidal breast masses that arise from the epithelium of the lactiferous breast duct, typically palpable as a tumor close to or behind the nipple. Most common cause of bloody nipple discharge.

1-Y2w7.title: Vasomotor rhinitis
1-Y2w7.description: A type of nonallergic rhinitis characterized by increased blood flow to the nasal mucosa in response to triggers (e.g., changes in temperature or humidity, emotional stimuli, exercise, strong odors), leading to congestion, rhinorrhea, and postnasal drip.

W-YPw7.title: Gustatory rhinitis
W-YPw7.description: A type of nonallergic rhinitis that typically manifests with diffuse watery rhinorrhea after intake of spicy food and/or alcohol.

d-Yow7.title: Rhinitis medicamentosa
d-Yow7.description: An increase in nasal vasodilation and congestion caused by an overuse or discontinuation of topical nasal decongestants (e.g., sympathomimetics like phenylephrine, oxymetazoline, xylometazoline). The exact cause is unknown but thought to be secondary to adrenergic receptors becoming refractory to the drug (i.e., tachyphylaxis).

V-YGw7.title: Drug-induced rhinitis
V-YGw7.description: A type of nonallergic rhinitis induced by certain medications. Examples of causative medications include antihypertensives, aspirin, NSAIDs, phosphodiesterase inhibitors, oral contraceptives, and some antipsychotic drugs.

e-Yxw7.title: Ugly duckling sign
e-Yxw7.description: A nevus that deviates in appearance from the general nevus pattern in the same individual. The presence of this sign should raise suspicion of melanoma.

2-YT97.title: Common acquired melanocytic nevi
2-YT97.description: An acquired melanocytic nevus (junctional, compound, or dermal) that arises from clusters of melanocytic nevus cells in the epidermis and dermis and manifests as a uniformly pigmented lesion, most commonly on sun-exposed areas.

f-Yk97.title: Traumatic brain injury
f-Yk97.description: An injury caused by mechanical forces transmitted to the brain. Can be divided into primary and secondary brain injury. Primary brain injury includes axonal damage, bleeding, and contusions of brain matter. Secondary brain injury includes cerebral edema, cytotoxicity from free radical release, electrolyte imbalance, mitochondrial damage, and ischemia from vasospasm.

h-YcC7.title: Schema therapy
h-YcC7.description: A treatment approach in psychotherapy based on the theory that people acquire certain basic schemas throughout their lives and thereby establish certain behavioral patterns. Combines various psychotherapeutic concepts and aims to diffuse the harmful potential of maladaptive schemas. Indications include borderline personality disorder, posttraumatic stress disorder, and eating disorders.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Schema therapy

3-YSC7.title: Anemia of chronic kidney disease
3-YSC7.description: Normocytic, normochromic anemia due to reduced renal production or erythropoietin in patients with chronic kidney disease.

Q-YuC7.title: Obturator sign
Q-YuC7.description: A physical finding characterized by right lower quadrant pain caused by flexion and internal rotation of the right leg. Associated with appendicitis.

j-Y_C7.title: Heatstroke
j-Y_C7.description: A life-threatening heat-related illness characterized by significantly elevated body temperature (typically defined as > 40°C) and severe CNS dysfunction.

4-Y3x7.title: Glipizide
4-Y3x7.description: A short-acting sulfonylurea antidiabetic agent commonly used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

M-YMB7.title: Ancylostoma braziliense
M-YMB7.description: A zoonotic hookworm that is an intestinal parasite in cats and dogs. Endemic to tropical areas such as the southwestern US, the Caribbean region, Central and South America, and Southeast Asia. Can infect humans by directly penetrating the skin. Causes cutaneous larva migrans.

n-Y7B7.title: Ancylostoma caninum
n-Y7B7.description: A zoonotic hookworm that is an intestinal parasite in dogs. Endemic to tropical and subtropical areas. Can infect humans by directly penetrating the skin. Causes cutaneous larva migrans.

o-Y0y7.title: Taeniasis
o-Y0y7.description: A collection of diseases caused by Taenia species. Includes intestinal taeniasis (which can be caused by T. solium and T. saginata) and cysticercosis (which can be caused by T. solium).

6-Yjy7.title: Halo sign
6-Yjy7.description:
1. A clinical finding used to detect CSF in blood-tinged rhinorrhea or otorrhea, commonly after trauma. Several drops of the leaking fluid are put on gauze or paper. A rapidly-expanding clear ring of fluid surrounding blood suggests the presence of CSF.
2. A radiologic finding of hemorrhagic ground glass opacities around nodules in the lungs on CT or X-ray. Most frequently seen in patients with invasive aspergillosis but can be seen in other angioinvasive pulmonary infections.
3. An ultrasonographic finding characterized by a hyperechoic liver lesion. It is a concerning feature for malignancy.
4. An ultrasonographic finding characterized by a periluminal hypoechoic halo caused by edema of the temporal artery wall. Can be caused by temporal arteritis.

p-YLy7.title: Acute viral hepatitis
p-YLy7.description: Acute inflammation of the liver due to hepatitis virus infection. Usually presents in three stages: 1) Prodromal stage: fever, malaise, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain and tender hepatomegaly. 2) Icteric phase: jaundice, dark urine, pruritus. 3) Resolution of symptoms: usually within 4 weeks in HAV and HEV infection; can become chronic in HBV and HCV infection.

J-Ysy7.title: Crystalline nephropathy
J-Ysy7.description: A group of kidney injuries involving crystal deposition that results in obstruction and inflammation. Can be caused by precipitation of intrinsic minerals, extrinsic dietary components, drugs with low urine solubility (e.g., acyclovir, indinavir, ciprofloxacin, methotrexate), metabolites, and proteins. May lead to acute kidney injury, progressive chronic kidney disease, or nephrolithiasis, depending on the location of crystal deposition.

q-YCy7.title: Acanthosis nigricans
q-YCy7.description: A skin disorder characterized by patches of velvety hyperpigmentation in the axilla, groin, and/or neck. Skin tags can also develop in affected areas. Classified as benign (e.g., from endocrine or drug adverse effects) or malignant (e.g., as a paraneoplastic syndrome).

r-YfA7.title: Water hammer pulse
r-YfA7.description: A physical exam finding in which palpation of a distal arterial pulse (such as the radial pulse) shows a rapid upstroke followed by prompt collapse of the vessel, (e.g., "bounding pulse"). Occurs due to rapid and large stroke volume ejection into the arterial system and is most commonly associated with aortic regurgitation. Referred to as Corrigan's pulse in the carotid artery and water hammer pulse in the limbs.

7-Y4A7.title: Pregestational diabetes mellitus
7-Y4A7.description: Diabetes mellitus (type 1 or type 2) that is diagnosed before pregnancy. Associated with a significantly increased risk for congenital abnormalities and maternal complications during pregnancy and delivery.

H-YKA7.title: Macrosomia
H-YKA7.description: A significantly larger-than-average fetus, defined as birth weight > 90th percentile or > 4,000 g (8 lbs 13 oz). Risk factors include maternal diabetes and obesity, advanced maternal age, and excessive gestational weight gain. Increases the risk of birth complications, including dystocia, clavicle fracture, and postpartum hemorrhage.

F-Yg_7.title: Renal cysts
F-Yg_7.description: A fluid-filled sac that develops in the kidneys. Cysts may be single or multiple and develop in healthy individuals or as a manifestation of various conditions, e.g., polycystic kidney disease, von Hippel-Lindau syndrome, cystic renal carcinoma.

8-YO_7.title: Renal papillary necrosis
8-YO_7.description: Injury to the kidney that is caused by coagulative necrosis of the renal medullary pyramids and papillae. The etiology is often multifactorial but possible precipitating factors include pyelonephritis, obstruction of the urinary tract, sickle cell disease, and analgesic abuse.

v-YA_7.title: Pericardial friction rub
v-YA_7.description: A high-pitched scratching sound best heard on auscultation during expiration while the patient is sitting upright. The rub is heard in atrial and ventricular systole as well as early diastole. It indicates friction between the visceral and parietal pericardial tissue. Seen most commonly in pericarditis.

C-Yqz7.title: Pericardial knock
C-Yqz7.description: A high-pitched, early-diastolic sound that sounds like a premature S3 and is often present in patients with constrictive pericarditis. Caused by the sudden slowing of blood flowing into the ventricle during diastole because relaxation of the ventricle is impaired by the rigid pericardial sac. The knock is best heard between the apex of the heart and the left sternal border.

A-YR-7.title: Acid-base disorders
A-YR-7.description: A group of conditions characterized by imbalances in the concentrations of hydrogen ions (H⁺) and bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻), which lead to changes in arterial blood pH. Can be categorized as acidoses or alkaloses and have a metabolic or respiratory origin.

_-Y5-7.title: Aldosterone-to-renin ratio
_-Y5-7.description: The ratio of plasma aldosterone concentration (PAC) to plasma renin activity (PRA), which is used as a screening test  for primary hyperaldosteronism. An elevated ratio suggests primary hyperaldosteronism and is an indication for confirmatory testing.

z-Yr-7.title: Adrenal venous sampling
z-Yr-7.description: A specialized diagnostic test used to differentiate between unilateral and bilateral adrenal hypersecretion of aldosterone. The aldosterone/cortisol ratio is measured in the right and left adrenal veins, as well as in a peripheral vein (usually the inferior vena cava), using catheterization. Adrenal venous sampling may be part of the diagnostic workup of hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, and, rarely, Cushing disease.

ZZbZZH.title: Aldosterone escape
ZZbZZH.description: A physiological phenomenon that describes a lack of edema formation and frank hypernatremia in patients with primary hyperaldosteronism. The most likely mechanism is secretion of atrial natriuretic peptide and pressure natriuresis that results in compensatory diuresis.

0ZbeZH.title: Roth spots
0ZbeZH.description: Retinal hemorrhages that can occur in infective endocarditis. Roth spots are most likely caused by septic microemboli that lead to vascular occlusion and localized immune-mediated vasculitis. Examination usually shows exudative, hemorrhagic lesions with pale centers.

bZbHZH.title: Fat necrosis
bZbHZH.description: A death of adipose tissue caused by acute inflammation. Etiologies include enzymatic fat necrosis (due to release of lipases and amylases from pancreatic cells) and trauma (e.g., direct trauma to the breast).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Necrosis

1Zb20H.title: Lyme carditis
1Zb20H.description: A complication of early disseminated Lyme disease. Typically occurs 1–2 months after infection and manifests as AV conduction dysfunction and/or decreased cardiac contractility due to myopericarditis. Associated signs and symptoms include chest pain, dyspnea, edema, palpitations, and syncope.

media.title: Complete heart block related to Lyme disease

WZbP0H.title: Tick paralysis
WZbP0H.description: A rare syndrome caused by the salivary neurotoxin of certain ticks (e.g., Rocky Mountain wood tick). Typically manifests with weakness in the lower extremities that progresses as an ascending paralysis that can lead to respiratory failure.

dZbo0H.title: Thoracic aortic aneurysm
dZbo0H.description: A focal dilatation of the thoracic aorta to more than 1.5 times its normal diameter. Classified by location as either ascending or descending aneurysms.

VZbG0H.title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
VZbG0H.description: A focal dilatation of the abdominal aorta to > 3 cm. Most commonly infrarenal. Frequently asymptomatic and detected incidentally.

media.title: Saccular and fusiform abdominal aortic aneurysms

eZbx0H.title: Japanese encephalitis
eZbx0H.description: A condition caused by Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV). Most JEV infections cause subclinical disease; however, patients can develop acute encephalitis, manifesting with prodromal fever, vomiting, headaches, and weakness followed by altered mental status that can progress to focal neurological deficits, psychosis, and/or seizures. Most common in patients < 15 years of age.

UZbbaH.title: Oral sodium loading test
UZbbaH.description: A confirmatory diagnostic test for primary hyperaldosteronism. Patients adhere to a high-sodium diet for 3 days, followed by 24-hour urine measurements of aldosterone, sodium (urine sodium > 200 mEq demonstrates appropriate sodium loading), and creatinine (to assess adequate urine collection). Urine aldosterone levels are elevated (> 12 mcg/day) in patients with primary hyperaldosteronism because of a failure to suppress aldosterone secretion.

2ZbTaH.title: Laryngoscopy
2ZbTaH.description: A procedure used to visualize the larynx for diagnostic and/or therapeutic purposes. Includes both indirect (e.g., mirror laryngoscopy,video-assisted, or fiberoptic laryngoscopy) and direct methods of visualization (e.g., with a lighted blade). Common indications include endotracheal tube placement, evaluation of upper airway symptoms (e.g., stridor, hoarseness, chronic cough), and removal of laryngeal lesions or an upper airway foreign body.

TZb6aH.title: Rule of the 6 Fs
TZb6aH.description: A mnemonic for common risk factors for cholelithiasis, which include: female sex, fat (overweight or obesity), forty (age > 40 years), fertile (multiparity), fair-skinned (white populations), and family history.

gZbFaH.title: Captopril suppression test
gZbFaH.description: A diagnostic confirmatory test for primary hyperaldosteronism. Plasma aldosterone and renin activity levels are drawn at baseline and 2 hours after a single dose of oral captopril (25–50 mg). Patients with primary hyperaldosteronism have ≤ 30% decrease in aldosterone from baseline because of a failure to suppress aldosterone secretion.

RZblYH.title: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
RZblYH.description: A rare condition characterized by noninfectious thrombi on the heart valves (usually the aortic and/or mitral valve). Most commonly seen in association with rheumatologic conditions and advanced malignancy. When associated with systemic lupus erythematosus, the term Libman-Sacks endocarditis is used.

PZbWbH.title: SOFA score
PZbWbH.description: A scoring system used to assess the severity of organ dysfunction and the risk of mortality. Commonly used in intensive care units (ICUs). Considers partial arterial pressure of oxygen, platelet count, bilirubin, mean arterial pressure (or vasopressor requirement), Glasgow Coma scale score, creatinine, and urine output. A simplified version of the SOFA score (the qSOFA score) identifies patients at increased risk for in-hospital mortality with suspected infection outside the ICU.

destinations.label: Care of the critically ill patient → Predictive scoring systems

4Zb3bH.title: Quick SOFA score
4Zb3bH.description: A clinical evaluation tool used for risk stratification in adults with sepsis or infection. High in-hospital mortality or prolonged ICU stay is predicted if ≥ 2 of the following are present: altered mental status, tachypnea (≥ 22 breaths/min), and/or systolic hypotension (≤ 100 mm Hg).

kZbmbH.title: Acute pericarditis
kZbmbH.description: An inflammation of the pericardium most commonly caused by infection, myocardial infarction, or cardiac surgery. Manifestations include fever, a pericardial friction rub on auscultation, and retrosternal chest pain that may be exacerbated by lying supine or inspiration and relieved by sitting or leaning forward. ECG usually shows diffuse, concave ST-segment elevation and/or PR depression.

NZb-bH.title: Leprosy
NZb-bH.description: A chronic infection caused by Mycobacterium leprae that typically manifests with hypopigmented skin lesions, nerve thickening, and peripheral nerve palsies. Subtypes include lepromatous and tuberculoid leprosy.

mZbVXH.title: Follicular adenoma
mZbVXH.description: A benign encapsulated tumor of the thyroid gland that is surrounded by a thin fibrous capsule.

MZbMXH.title: Thyroid incidentaloma
MZbMXH.description: An asymptomatic thyroid nodule discovered incidentally during imaging of the neck that was carried out for an unrelated reason.

nZb7XH.title: Toxic adenoma
nZb7XH.description: A benign, solitary nodule in an otherwise nonpalpable thyroid gland. Caused by a gain-of-function mutation of the TSH receptor gene in a single precursor cell, which results in autonomous production of thyroid hormones.

LZbwXH.title: Toxic multinodular goiter
LZbwXH.description: A multinodular enlargement of the thyroid gland with TSH-independent functioning of some nodules. It is the second most common cause of hyperthyroidism.

6ZbjcH.title: Acute liver failure
6ZbjcH.description: Rapidly progressive and severe acute liver injury lasting ≤ 26 weeks in individuals without previous hepatic disease. Abnormal liver chemistries, coagulopathy, and hepatic encephalopathy are required to confirm the diagnosis. Acute liver failure is most commonly idiopathic or due to drug toxicity (especially acetaminophen) or acute viral hepatitis. Treatment consists of supportive therapy and liver transplantation.

qZbCcH.title: Xeroderma pigmentosum
qZbCcH.description: A rare hereditary disease caused by defective DNA nucleotide excision repair mechanisms. Manifests with severe photosensitivity that often leads to UV-induced skin and ocular damage and skin cancer. Some patients present with neurodegenerative disease.

IZbY1H.title: Laryngitis
IZbY1H.description: Inflammation of the larynx that typically manifests with an altered voice (e.g., hoarseness and/or dysphonia). Acute laryngitis (i.e., < 3 weeks) is typically caused by an upper respiratory tract infection or vocal strain and is self-limited. Causes of chronic laryngitis (i.e., ≥ 3 weeks) include gastrointestinal esophageal reflux disease, laryngopharyngeal reflux, prolonged exposure to airway irritants (e.g., smoking), adverse effects of medications (e.g., coughing from ACE inhibitors), chronic infection (e.g., tuberculosis), and, rarely, systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., granulomatosis with polyangiitis).

rZbf1H.title: Acute viral rhinosinusitis
rZbf1H.description: An inflammation of the paranasal sinuses and adjacent nasal cavities caused by a viral infection. Symptoms include purulent nasal drainage and nasal obstruction or facial tenderness for up to 4 weeks. Clinically differentiated from bacterial rhinosinusitis by a duration of < 10 days and no signs of worsening. Most common cause of acute rhinosinusitis.

7Zb41H.title: Acute bacterial rhinosinusitis
7Zb41H.description: An inflammation of paranasal sinuses and adjacent nasal cavities caused by a bacterial infection; most commonly S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, or M. catarrhalis. Symptoms include purulent nasal drainage and nasal obstruction or facial tenderness for up to 4 weeks. Clinically defined by a duration of > 10 days or worsening after initial improvement (double worsening).

HZbK1H.title: Sydenham chorea
HZbK1H.description: Involuntary, irregular, non-repetitive movements of the limbs, neck, head, and/or face. One of the major clinical manifestations of rheumatic fever following group A streptococcal infection. Movements are usually generalized but may be asymmetrical or confined to one side (hemichorea) and are not urge- or compulsion-driven.

tZbXWH.title: Recurrent acute sinusitis
tZbXWH.description: A condition with at least 4 episodes of acute bacterial rhinosinusitis per year. Each episode must meet the criteria for acute bacterial rhinosinusitis, with no symptoms between episodes.

FZbgWH.title: Kartagener syndrome
FZbgWH.description: A subset of primary ciliary dyskinesia characterized by the triad of situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis. Additional clinical features of primary ciliary dyskinesia can also be present, such as reduced fertility, chronic ear infections, and conductive hearing loss.

8ZbOWH.title: Purulent gonococcal arthritis
8ZbOWH.description: A manifestation of disseminated gonococcal infection that involves the rapid onset of purulent monoarticular or oligoarticular inflammation. Commonly affects the knees, ankles, elbows, and wrists.

uZbpWH.title: Arthritis-dermatitis syndrome
uZbpWH.description: A manifestation of disseminated gonococcal disease that is characterized by the triad of polyarthralgias (sometimes purulent), tenosynovitis, and dermatitis (vesicular, pustular, or maculopapular lesions, possibly with a necrotic or hemorrhagic center). Additional symptoms include fever and chills.

EZb8WH.title: Prosthetic joint infection
EZb8WH.description: An infection that involves a joint implant and its surrounding tissue. Most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis. Manifestations include fever, localized swelling, and erythema.

wZbhdH.title: Bacterial coxitis
wZbhdH.description: An acute infection of the hip joint most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Considered an orthopedic emergency due to the potential for rapid joint destruction. Manifestations include fever, malaise, severe hip pain, limited range of motion, and refusal to bear weight.

9ZbNdH.title: Critical illness myopathy
9ZbNdH.description: A syndrome of widespread, typically proximal, symmetric weakness in critically ill patients. Possible risk factors include immobility, prolonged duration of mechanical ventilation, severe hyperglycemia, sepsis, and use of certain drugs (e.g., glucocorticoids, neuromuscular junction blockers). Management includes minimizing sedation, early mobilization, physical and occupational therapy, and treatment of the underlying illness. Symptoms may last for months to years after discharge.

CZbqdH.title: Galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase
CZbqdH.description: An enzyme involved in the final step of galactose metabolism to glucose. Catalyzes the conversion of UDP-glucose + galactose-1-phosphate to glucose-1-phosphate + UDP-galactose. Deficiency results in classic galactosemia.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Galactosemia

xZbEdH.title: Uridine diphosphate galactose-4-epimerase
xZbEdH.description: An enzyme involved in the metabolism of galactose to glucose. Catalyzes the reversible conversion of UDP-galactose to UDP-glucose. Deficiency results in a rare form of galactosemia.

BZbzdH.title: Essential fructosuria
BZbzdH.description: A benign disorder of fructose metabolism caused by an autosomal recessive gene defect that results in fructokinase deficiency. Elevated fructose levels may be detected in urine.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Disorders of fructose metabolism

yZbdVH.title: Type 3 glycogen storage disease
yZbdVH.description: A type of glycogen storage disorder (type III) caused by deficiency of the glycogen debrancher enzyme (α-1,6-glucosidase). Typically manifests in infancy or childhood with generalized muscle weakness, cramps, hepatosplenomegaly, cirrhosis, fasting hypoglycemia, ketosis, and hyperlipidemia.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Glycogen storage disorders (GSD)

AZbRVH.title: Type 4 glycogen storage disease
AZbRVH.description: A type of glycogen storage disease that is caused by a deficiency of the glycogen branching enzyme. Patients present during infancy or childhood with hepatosplenomegaly, a failure to thrive, and proximal myopathy. Cirrhosis and liver failure develop rapidly, necessitating liver transplantation.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Glycogen storage disorders (GSD)

zZbrVH.title: Synovial fluid analysis
zZbrVH.description:
A group of tests used to examine joint fluid (synovial fluid) that help to diagnose specific types of arthritis.
Synovial fluid is obtained via arthrocentesis and examined for its appearance, white blood cell count, and glucose level, as well as for the presence of crystals and growth on bacterial culture.

00beeH.title: Herpetic gingivostomatitis
00beeH.description: A severe manifestation of an (often primary) HSV-1 infection characterized by painful lesions of the oral and pharyngeal mucosa.

destinations.label: Herpes simplex virus infections → Oral herpes

Y0bneH.title: Nuclear medicine thyroid scan
Y0bneH.description: A nuclear medicine test in which a radiotracer (usually radioactive iodine) is administered to a patient. The thyroid gland absorbs the tracer, and the radiation is measured with an imaging device to create pictures of the gland that provide information about its function. Often combined with radioactive iodine uptake measurement.

10b2UH.title: Community-acquired pneumonia
10b2UH.description: A condition of pneumonia acquired outside of a health care establishment (in contrast to nosocomial pneumonia). Common pathogens are Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, atypical bacteria (e.g., Chlamydia pneumoniae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Legionella spp.), and viruses. Symptoms include fever, cough, purulent sputum, and dyspnea.

V0bGUH.title: Mycobacteria
V0bGUH.description: A group of aerobic, acid-fast actinobacteria that can cause severe disease in humans, including tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis), leprosy (M. leprae), and HIV-associated diseases (M. avium complex/M. avium intracellulare).

f0bk2H.title: Hypercoagulable states
f0bk2H.description: An inherited or acquired state in which an individual is predisposed to forming blood clots. This most often manifests as recurrent deep vein thromboses or pulmonary emboli. Etiologies include conditions of inherited thrombophilia (e.g., factor V Leiden mutation), malignancy, pregnancy and the puerperium, various drugs (e.g., oral contraceptives, tamoxifen), and immobilization.

T0b62H.title: Hutchinson teeth
T0b62H.description: Widely-spaced, notched, hypoplastic teeth characteristic of congenital syphilis.

g0bF2H.title: Mulberry molars
g0bF2H.description: Abnormal development of the first molars, which take on the appearance of a mulberry. Characteristic finding in congenital syphilis.

media.title: Hutchinson's Teeth resulting from congenital syphilis

S0by2H.title: Jugular venous distention
S0by2H.description: A physical examination finding of a bulging jugular vein. Typically evaluated with the patient in supine position with the torso elevated to 45° and the head rotated away from the examiner. Tangential lighting can help elicit the finding. Indicates elevated jugular venous pressure. Conditions associated with jugular venous distention include right-sided heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and cardiac tamponade.

h0bcfH.title: Signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG
h0bcfH.description: A set of findings that includes: high R peak in left chest leads (I, aVL and V₄₋₆), deep S peak in right chest leads (iIII, aVR, V₁₋₃), widened QRS complex (> 100 ms), left axis deviation (often QRS axis ≥ -30° in frontal plane leads), changes in repolarization (e.g., ST depression and T-wave inversions in the precordial leads), ST elevation in V1₁₋₃ (discordant to deep S), and abnormalities in atrial depolarization (increased duration of P waves (≥ 120 ms) or biphasic P waves). Prominent U waves may also be seen.

30bSfH.title: Congenital herpes simplex virus infection
30bSfH.description: A congenital infection most commonly transmitted via perinatal transmission during birth and rarely via the placenta in utero. Intrauterine infection can cause fetal demise, preterm birth, very low birth weight, and microcephaly. Perinatal infection can cause vesicular mucocutaneous lesions.

destinations.label: Congenital TORCH infections → Congenital herpes simplex virus infection

P0bWTH.title: Obligate intracellular pathogen
P0bWTH.description: A pathogen that cannot replicate outside of a host cell. Examples include all viruses, certain bacteria (e.g., Chlamydia spp., Rickettsia spp.), certain protozoa (e.g., Trypanosoma spp., Plasmodium spp.,) and certain fungi (e.g., Pneumocystis jirovecii).

k0bmTH.title: Coccidioidomycosis
k0bmTH.description: A fungal infection caused by Coccidioides immitis that is usually subclinical but can manifest with symptoms of acute pneumonia (e.g., fever, cough, chest pain) and arthralgia. Dissemination to other organs is possible. Skin manifestations of erythema nodosum and erythema multiforme are also classical.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

media.title: Coccidioidomycosis (Valley fever) fact sheet and US endemicity map

O0bITH.title: Paracoccidioidomycosis
O0bITH.description: An infection caused by Paracoccidioides brasiliensis and Paracoccidioides lutzii. Acute infection is usually asymptomatic but can cause generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and aplastic anemia from bone marrow involvement. The chronic form causes lung fibrosis, adrenal insufficiency, and skin and mucosal ulcers.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

media.title: Paracoccidioidomycosis fact sheet and endemicity map

l0bvTH.title: Blastomycosis
l0bvTH.description: A fungal infection caused by Blastomyces dermatitis. Infection is often asymptomatic but can manifest with acute or chronic pneumonia and skin involvement with irregular verrucous lesions. Bone, joint, and genitourinary involvement can also occur.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

media.title: Blastomycosis fact sheet and US endemicity map

N0b-TH.title: Coccidioides immitis
N0b-TH.description: A dimorphic fungus endemic to the deserts of the southwestern United States, Mexico, and Central and South America. Causes coccidioidomycosis. Seen on microscopy as spherules containing endospores.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

n0b7gH.title: Histoplasma capsulatum
n0b7gH.description: A dimorphic fungus that causes histoplasmosis. The fungus is endemic to the Mississippi and Ohio river valleys where it is found in bird and bat droppings.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

L0bwgH.title: Pneumocystis jirovecii
L0bwgH.description: A yeast-like fungus originally classified as a protozoan that causes Pneumocystis pneumonia. Identified as disc-shaped yeast form on methenamine silver stain of lung tissue.

o0b0SH.title: Paracoccidioides brasiliensis
o0b0SH.description: A dimorphic fungus endemic to Latin America that causes paracoccidioidomycosis if its spores are inhaled. Forms large, budding yeast with a characteristic shape that resembles a captain's wheel.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

K0bUSH.title: Paracoccidioides lutzii
K0bUSH.description: A dimorphic fungus endemic to Latin America that causes paracoccidioidomycosis if its spores are inhaled. Forms large, budding yeast with a characteristic shape that resembles a captain's wheel.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

60bjSH.title: Aspergillus fumigatus
60bjSH.description: A fungus that appears as septate hyphae branching at acute angles with terminal conidiospores. Causes allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA), chronic aspergillosis (including aspergilloma), and invasive aspergillosis in immunocompromised hosts.

J0bsSH.title: Conjunctival follicles
J0bsSH.description: A lymphoid follicle on the palpebral or bulbar conjunctiva that is small, raised, and yellowish-white due to hyperplastic tissue. Vascularization is usually peripheral.

70b4hH.title: Dermatophyte infections
70b4hH.description: A group of infections of the skin, hair, and nails caused by keratinophilic fungi, most commonly from the Trichophyton, Microsporum, and Epidermophyton genera.

H0bKhH.title: Nocardia asteroides
H0bKhH.description: A weakly acid-fast, gram-positive, aerobic bacterium found in soil and water. Causes pulmonary infections in immunocompromised patients.

x0bERH.title: Congenital diaphragmatic hernias
x0bERH.description: A common developmental anomaly that is characterized by protrusion of intra-abdominal contents through an abnormal opening in the diaphragm. Patients present postnatally with respiratory distress and a characteristic absence of breath sounds over the ipsilateral (most frequently the left) chest.

B0bzRH.title: Collar sign
B0bzRH.description: A radiological sign seen on computer tomography that is associated with diaphragmatic hernia.

y0bdiH.title: Nocardia
y0bdiH.description: A genus of aerobic, gram-positive bacilli, weakly acid-fast with branching filamentous rods that is ubiquitous in soil worldwide. Transmitted through inhalation (most common), ingestion, and inoculation through a skin wound or injury. Causes nocardiosis, which manifests as either pulmonary, cutaneous, or disseminated disease. Nocardia species include Nocardia asteroides complex, which commonly causes pulmonary manifestations, and N. brasiliensis, which commonly causes skin manifestations.

A0bRiH.title: HIV postexposure prophylaxis
A0bRiH.description: A medication regimen given to a patient who has been exposed to HIV to prevent transmission. The recommended combination is tenofovir with emtricitabine, in addition to either raltegravir or dolutegravir. Should be administered within 72 hours of exposure.

z0briH.title: Opportunistic infection
z0briH.description: An infection caused by usually benign pathogens that have the ability to cause disease in an immunocompromised host (e.g., patients with AIDS). Examples include esophageal candidiasis, cytomegalovirus infection, cryptococcal meningitis, pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, and toxoplasmosis.

-0bDiH.title: Adhesive atelectasis
-0bDiH.description: A form of nonobstructive atelectasis that occurs due to surfactant deficiency or dysfunction. Causes include acute respiratory distress syndrome and neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.

ZabZQH.title: Rounded atelectasis
ZabZQH.description: An uncommon form of atelectasis that occurs when redundant pleural tissue folds inward and traps lung parenchyma. Causes include pneumoconioses (e.g., asbestosis), tuberculosis, and hemothorax.

0abeQH.title: Middle lobe syndrome
0abeQH.description: A pulmonary syndrome characterized by recurrent or fixed atelectasis of the right middle lobe and/or lingula. Can be caused by intraluminal or extraluminal obstruction or have no identifiable cause in some cases. Associated with childhood asthma and Sjogren syndrome.

aabQQH.title: Postoperative atelectasis
aabQQH.description: A common postoperative complication (especially after chest or abdominal surgery), which often occurs within 72 hours of surgery. Symptoms depend on the extent of atelectasis. Clinical findings include a dull percussion note, diminished breathing sounds, and decreased fremitus over the affected lung.

YabnQH.title: Replacement atelectasis
YabnQH.description: A form of nonobstructive atelectasis in which the alveoli in an entire lobe of the lung are replaced by neoplastic tissue (e.g., bronchioloalveolar cell carcinoma), resulting in loss of effective lung volume and subsequent lung collapse.

Xab9QH.title: Infantile seborrheic dermatitis
Xab9QH.description: A common, benign, inflammatory skin condition in infants. Symptoms include erythema and greasy, yellow, scaling patches. Most commonly affects the scalp but may also affect the face, ear, neck, and/or diaper area. Typically manifests within 3 months of birth and resolves by 1 year of age.

cabajH.title: Juvenile polyposis syndrome
cabajH.description: An autosomal dominant syndrome characterized by > 10 hamartomatous polyps throughout the gastrointestinal tract. Typically manifests within the first 2 decades of life with hematochezia. Patients have an increased risk of developing colorectal and/or gastric malignancies.

1ab2jH.title: Cowden syndrome
1ab2jH.description: An autosomal dominant condition that causes GI hamartomatous polyps, skin manifestations (e.g., papules and hyperkeratosis of the skin and mucous membranes), and changes in thyroid and mammary glands (e.g., multinodular goiter, adenomas, fibroadenomas, intraductal papillomas).

dabojH.title: Hamartoma
dabojH.description: A benign mass composed of mature cells that are native to the tissue of origin but have abnormal tissue organization. Has a low potential to undergo malignant transformation.

UabbPH.title: Hyperplastic polyps
UabbPH.description: The most common form of benign gastrointestinal polyp. Typically small and found in the distal colon (i.e., rectum and sigmoid). May evolve into serrated polyps and pose a risk of malignant transformation.

2abTPH.title: Sessile serrated polyps
2abTPH.description: A type of premalignant, dysplastic polyp found most often in the proximal colon. Like other serrated polyps, CpG islands, microsatellite instability, and BRAF mutations are classically associated with this lesion.

fabkPH.title: Traditional serrated adenoma
fabkPH.description: An uncommon gastrointestinal polyp that is inherently dysplastic and poses a risk for malginant transformation. The classic genetic abnormalities in these polyps are CpG islands, microsatellite instability due to DNA mismatch repair errors, or mutations in the oncogene BRAF.

SabyPH.title: Kerion
SabyPH.description: A severe form of tinea capitis characterized by a deep, boggy plaque with pustule formation. Treatment with griseofulvin should be initiated promptly to minimize the risk of permanent hair loss within the lesion.

habc4H.title: Tinea cruris
habc4H.description: A dermatophyte fungal infection affecting the groin region. Presents as itchy, erythematous scaly skin with a central clearing that characteristically spares the scrotum. Most common causes include Trichophyton rubrum and Epidermophyton floccosum.

3abS4H.title: Acute decompensated heart failure
3abS4H.description: An acute worsening of the clinical features of heart failure in a patient with preexisting cardiomyopathy. Typical manifestations include progressive dyspnea, edema, nocturia, and neurologic symptoms (e.g., confusion, headaches, altered mental status).

media.title: Heart failure cells in decompensated heart failure

Rabl4H.title: Cronkhite-Canada syndrome
Rabl4H.description: A rare, nonfamilial disorder that presents with hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyposis, alopecia, and cutaneous hyperpigmentation. The polyps are benign and do not increase the risk of malignant transformation.

iabJ4H.title: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema
iabJ4H.description: A form of pulmonary edema caused by increased pulmonary capillary hydrostatic pressure. Fluid is characteristically low in protein. Causes include acute decompensated heart failure (most common cause) and transfusion-associated circulatory overload.

Qabu4H.title: Desquamative erythroderma
Qabu4H.description: A rare, severe form of infantile seborrheic dermatitis that manifests with widespread erythroderma, recurrent diarrhea, infections, and failure to thrive. Associated with immunodeficiency (e.g., in complement disorders).

4ab3kH.title: Overt hyperthyroidism
4ab3kH.description: A condition in which the serum TSH level is low or undetectable and serum free T4 and/or T3 levels are elevated. The majority of patients experience symptoms of thyrotoxicosis, such as tachycardia and heat intolerance. Causes include Graves disease and toxic multinodular goiter.

kabmkH.title: Respiratory diphtheria
kabmkH.description: A type of pharyngitis caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae. Manifests with sore throat, cervical lymphadenopathy, low-grade fever, and characteristic gray-white coating of the pharynx and tonsils. The coating is composed of necrotic fibrin, white blood cells, erythrocytes, epithelial cells, and bacteria.

Nab-kH.title: Differences of sex development
Nab-kH.description: The congenital presence of chromosomal, gonadal, and/or phenotypical patterns that do not fit binary notions of male or female sex.

mabVOH.title: Thionamides
mabVOH.description: A group of drugs that impairs thyroid hormone synthesis by inhibiting thyroid peroxidase and thus preventing the oxidation of iodine. Examples include methimazole and propylthiouracil.

LabwOH.title: Periodic limb movements of sleep
LabwOH.description: Frequent motor stereotypies of the legs (typically flexion and extension of the toes, ankles, knees, and hips) and sometimes of the arms during sleep. Most commonly seen in restless legs syndrome but also occurs in other sleep disorders (e.g., narcolepsy). Cases that occur in isolation are rare and referred to as periodic limb movement disorder.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Periodic limb movement disorder

qabClH.title: Plantar wart
qabClH.description: A hyperkeratotic papule or plaque on the sole of the feet caused by infection with the cutaneous serotypes of HPV. Typically located on areas of friction or mechanical pressure and can be painful.

IabYNH.title: Miconazole
IabYNH.description: An imidazole antifungal that is used topically in the treatment of superficial fungal infections such as tinea.

rabfNH.title: Azoles
rabfNH.description: A group of antifungal agents that decreases fungal ergosterol synthesis by inhibiting cytochrome P450. Used in the treatment of both local and systemic fungal infections. Agents include ketoconazole, clotrimazole, itraconazole, and fluconazole. Typical adverse effects of systemic use include testosterone synthesis inhibition (especially in the case of ketoconazole) and liver dysfunction.

HabKNH.title: Griseofulvin
HabKNH.description: An oral antifungal drug commonly used for superficial skin infections (e.g., tinea, ringworm). Adverse effects include teratogenicity, carcinogenicity, disulfiram-like reactions (unpleasant hypersensitivity to alcohol), and induction of cytochrome P450.

sabtNH.title: Klebsiella granulomatis
sabtNH.description: A gram-negative bacillus that causes the sexually transmitted infection granuloma inguinale. The pathogen is endemic to tropical and subtropical regions.

GabBNH.title: Coagulation cascade
GabBNH.description: A series of reactions involving a system of three pathways that results in the coagulation of blood. Consists of the extrinsic pathway (tissue factor pathway), intrinsic pathway (contact activation pathway), and final common pathway.

tabXmH.title: Hyperfibrinolysis
tabXmH.description: A state of increased fibrinolytic activity, resulting in abnormal bleeding. Excessive plasmin activity causes increased fibrin degradation, resulting in unstable blood clots that dissolve shortly after forming. High plasmin concentrations also lead to platelet dysfunction and the degradation of fibrinogen, thus inhibiting the formation of the thrombus itself. Caused by various conditions, including congenital or metabolic causes, trauma, decreased hepatic clearance (due to liver dysfunction), sepsis.

uabpmH.title: Viscoelastic hemostatic assay
uabpmH.description: A group of assays that rapidly measure several parameters of clot formation and resolution (including coagulation, platelet function, and fibrinolysis) by applying shear stress to a blood sample and measuring its viscous and elastic properties over time. VHAs are frequently used as a point-of-care test to optimize the management of rapid bleeding in surgery, trauma, and postpartum hemorrhage. The available methods to perform VHAs are the thromboelastogram (TEG), rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM), and Sonoclot.

destinations.label: Hemostasis and bleeding disorders → Management of acute bleeding

Eab8mH.title: Schizoaffective disorder
Eab8mH.description: A psychiatric disorder characterized by the presence of psychotic symptoms that meet the criteria for schizophrenia in combination with features of a major mood episode (depressive, manic, or mixed). By definition, at some point during the span of the disorder, delusions or hallucinations must have been present for ≥ 2 weeks in the absence of mood disorder symptoms. However, the mood disorder symptoms must be present most of the time.

Cabq5H.title: Tetanolysin
Cabq5H.description: A toxin produced by Clostridium tetani that causes hemolytic effects. Its exact function is unknown.

xabE5H.title: Neonatal tetanus
xabE5H.description: A newborn infection with Clostridium tetani. Typically affects children of poorly-immunized mothers who had aseptic umbilical stump management. Symptoms include difficulty opening the mouth and feeding (due to trismus), risus sardonicus, and/or clenched hands. Symptoms are rapid-onset, most often occurring on days 5-7 of life.

Babz5H.title: Cardiorenal syndrome
Babz5H.description: A spectrum of conditions affecting the cardiac and renal systems that occur when dysfunction in one organ results in dysfunction of the other. It is divided into five types, according to the phenotype and underlying etiology.

AabRMH.title: Rickettsia rickettsii
AabRMH.description: A small, gram-negative, obligate, intracellular coccobacillus responsible for Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever. It infects Dermacentor ticks, which then pass on the pathogen to humans.

_ab5MH.title: Ehrlichiosis
_ab5MH.description: A tickborne bacterial infection endemic to the mid-Atlantic, southeastern, and south central regions of the US. Caused by the Ehrlichia genus and transmitted to humans via the lone star tick (Amblyomma americanum). Typically causes flu-like symptoms, but severe infection can lead to renal failure and GI bleeding.

zabrMH.title: Babesiosis
zabrMH.description: A parasitic infection endemic to the Northeast and upper Midwest regions of the United States that is caused by Babesia species. Transmitted to humans via the Ixodes tick and typically causes mild flu-like symptoms. Severe infection can cause hemolytic anemia, DIC, ARDS, and death.

-abDMH.title: Babesia
-abDMH.description: A genus of protozoal parasites that infect red blood cells and cause babesiosis. Typically transmitted via ticks (e.g., Ixodes).

ZYbZnH.title: AIDS-defining conditions
ZYbZnH.description: A group of conditions, including malignancies (e.g., primary lymphoma of the brain) and opportunistic infections (e.g., Pneumocystis pneumonia, cerebral toxoplasmosis), that occur in patients with HIV infection, indicating progression to AIDS.

0YbenH.title: Pretibial myxedema
0YbenH.description: A rare dermatological feature of Graves disease that manifests as nonpitting edema and skin thickening, typically in the pretibial areas. Circulating autoantibodies stimulate fibroblasts to produce excess glycosaminoglycans in affected tissues.

XYb9nH.title: HIV-associated dementia
XYb9nH.description: An AIDS-defining condition that typically affects untreated patients with advanced HIV infection (CD4 count < 200/mm3). Early stages are characterized by minor memory impairment; in later stages, severe neurologic deficits (impaired vigilance, aphasia, motor deficits) develop. Gait disturbance and depression are also frequently found.

media.title: Multinucleated giant cells in HIV-associated encephalopathy

cYbaLH.title: Catheter-associated urinary tract infection
cYbaLH.description: A health care-associated infection that occurs in patients with indwelling bladder catheters or up to 48 hours after urinary catheter removal. Duration of catheterization is a significant risk factor. Manifestations include fever, pyuria, suprapubic and/or flank pain, and catheter obstruction.

1Yb2LH.title: Anterior fat pad sign
1Yb2LH.description: A radiographic finding caused by an elbow joint effusion. Results in the presence of a convex lucent crescent in the coronoid fossa on a lateral x-ray view of the elbow.

media.title: Anterior and posterior fat pad signs in supracondylar humerus fracture

WYbPLH.title: Supracondylar fractures
WYbPLH.description: A fracture of the distal humerus, superior to the elbow joint. Typically a transverse fracture above the medial and lateral epicondyles. The most common type of elbow fractures in children.

VYbGLH.title: True aneurysm
VYbGLH.description: An abnormal dilation of an artery due to a weakened vessel wall. Involves all three layers of the vessel wall (i.e., tunica intima, tunica media, tunica adventitia).

eYbxLH.title: Pseudoaneurysm
eYbxLH.description: A collection of blood that forms due to a vessel wall defect. Can result in the accumulation of blood between the tunica media and the tunica adventitia or between the blood vessel and surrounding tissue. Can also refer to a complication of myocardial infarction in which a rupture of the heart wall becomes contained within surrounding pericardium.

UYbboH.title: Arterial dissection
UYbboH.description: A tear in the intima of an arterial wall (e.g., cervical artery, cerebral artery, aorta) that leads to blood entering between the intima and media or adventitia at high pressure and separation of these layers, which creates a false lumen. Leads to luminal occlusion due to thromboembolism and hypoperfusion.

2YbToH.title: Hand hygiene
2YbToH.description: The practice of cleaning the hands using an alcohol-based rub or antimicrobial soap to reduce the risk of transmission of infection. Performed before and after each patient encounter, before sterile procedures, after removing gloves, after touching medical equipment, and after coming in contact with infected secretions and/or blood.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Health care hygiene

fYbkoH.title: Penicillin-binding proteins
fYbkoH.description: A group of bacterial proteins that are essential for cell wall synthesis. They function as transpeptidases, permitting crosslinking of peptidoglycan within the cell wall. Virtually all beta-lactam antibiotics function by inhibiting penicillin-binding proteins.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Beta-lactam antibiotics

TYb6oH.title: Flucytosine
TYb6oH.description: An oral antifungal agent used to treat a wide variety of fungal infections. The drug enters fungal cells and is converted to fluorouracil, which competitively inhibits DNA and protein synthesis.

3YbSKH.title: High-output heart failure
3YbSKH.description: A state of heart failure characterized by increased cardiac output and lowered systemic vascular resistance. May be caused by arteriovenous fistulas, renal disease, anemia, beriberi, or Graves' disease.

RYblKH.title: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
RYblKH.description: A condition of decreased gonadal function due to a disease that primarily affects the pituitary gland and/or hypothalamus. Characterized by low concentrations of pituitary gonadotropins (FSH and LH) and low concentrations of sex hormones (e.g., estrogen, testosterone). Causes include isolated GnRH deficiency, functional hypothalamic amenorrhea, and brain tumors or other brain injury (e.g., infiltrative diseases, radiation, Sheehan syndrome).

iYbJKH.title: Circumflex branch of left coronary artery
iYbJKH.description: A branch of the left coronary artery that runs in the coronary sulcus toward the posterior surface of the heart. Supplies a large part of the left atrium and the left ventricle.

QYbuKH.title: Attenuated FAP
QYbuKH.description: A variant of familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) characterized by lesser polyps (> 10 but < 100) present mainly in the right colon, and a more advanced age at presentation compared to FAP (40 years for polyps, 60 years for colorectal cancer). Patients with attenuated FAP have a lower risk (∼ 80%) of developing colorectal cancer than with classic FAP.

jYb_KH.title: Turcot's syndrome
jYb_KH.description: A rare inherited disorder characterized by the combination of primary brain tumors and colorectal cancer or polyposis. Associated with familial adenomatous polyposis (mostly medulloblastomas) and Lynch syndrome (mostly gliomas).

PYbW6H.title: Myoclonic seizure
PYbW6H.description: A type of seizure characterized by nonrhythmic, brief (< 0.5 seconds) muscle jerking of the entire body (generalized) or only one part (focal). There may be a brief period of impaired consciousness during the seizure, but there is no postictal period.

4Yb36H.title: Atonic seizure
4Yb36H.description: A sudden decrease in muscle tone that is not preceded by myoclonic or tonic features and typically lasts < 2 seconds. It may occur focally in the head, trunk, or limb, or generalize and affect all muscles, resulting in a  "drop attack."

lYbv6H.title: Seasonal allergic conjunctivitis
lYbv6H.description: A type of allergic conjunctivitis caused by hypersensitivity to seasonal allergens (e.g., pollen) and characterized by intense itching. May be associated with allergic rhinitis.

NYb-6H.title: Giant papillary conjunctivitis
NYb-6H.description: A type of conjunctivitis caused by chronic exposure to an irritant (e.g., contact lenses or solution, ocular prosthesis, sutures). Characterized by papillary hypertrophy.

mYbVpH.title: Metastatic cancer of unknown primary
mYbVpH.description: Disseminated (metastatic) cancer for which the primary cancer is not known despite thorough investigation (including biochemical tests for serum markers, imaging, and histology). CUP accounts for 3-5% of all the patients who present with a tumor and has a very poor prognosis, with no form of evidence-based therapy available.

5YbipH.title: Antibiogram
5YbipH.description: A collation of the results of all antibiotic sensitivity tests in a region or institution, typically presented in a table. Used to predict the sensitivity of a pathogen to various antibiotics and to select empiric antibiotic therapy.

MYbMpH.title: Dry tap
MYbMpH.description: Failure to obtain bone marrow during bone marrow aspiration. Typically caused by bone marrow fibrosis (e.g., in myelofibrosis) or hypercellularity (e.g., in acute leukemia).

nYb7pH.title: Rimantadine
nYb7pH.description: An antiviral and antiparkinsonian drug (with dopaminergic properties) that is primarily used for treatment of Parkinson disease because it acts as a weak NMDA receptor antagonist. It was formerly used for treatment and prophylaxis of influenza A but is currently not recommended because of the risk of viral drug resistance.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against influenza viruses

LYbwpH.title: Zanamivir
LYbwpH.description: A neuraminidase inhibitor used for the prophylaxis and treatment of influenza A and B. Inhibits viral budding and prevents dissemination of the virus into the bloodstream. Not recommended for individuals with underlying respiratory disease (e.g., asthma, COPD).

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against influenza viruses

oYb0JH.title: Famciclovir
oYb0JH.description: A prodrug of penciclovir and guanosine analog used to treat herpes infections (especially herpes zoster). Requires phosphorylation by viral thymidine kinase to function.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against herpes viruses

KYbUJH.title: Valganciclovir
KYbUJH.description: A prodrug of ganciclovir with better oral bioavailability used to treat cytomegalovirus (CMV) infections.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against herpes viruses

6YbjJH.title: Sofosbuvir
6YbjJH.description: A nucleoside polymerase inhibitor (NS5B) used as an antiviral drug used in combination with velpatasvir or ledipasvir for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C infection. Adverse effects include headache and fatigue. It is contraindicated in severe renal insufficiency.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

pYbLJH.title: Simeprevir
pYbLJH.description: An HCV protease inhibitor (NS3/4A); it is used in the treatment of chronic hepatitis C infection as a part of a triple antiviral combination that also includes peginterferon-alfa and ribavirin. Adverse effects include photosensitivity reactions and skin rash.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

JYbsJH.title: Ledipasvir
JYbsJH.description: A non-nucleoside polymerase inhibitor (NS5A) used as an antiviral drug in combination with sofosbuvir for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C infection. Adverse effects include headache and fatigue.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

qYbCJH.title: Velpatasvir
qYbCJH.description: An inhibitor of nonstructural protein 5A, which plays a key role in RNA replication within hepatitis C viruses. Used in combination with sofosbuvir to treat hepatitis C infection.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

HYbKqH.title: Lobar pneumonia
HYbKqH.description: An infection localized to one pulmonary lobe, most commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, gram-negative bacilli, and Staphylococcus aureus.

sYbtqH.title: Oral hairy leukoplakia
sYbtqH.description: A benign condition characterized by painless, white plaques with a feathery or hairy appearance on the lateral tongue (or less commonly, the floor of the mouth, palate, or buccal mucosa) that cannot be scraped off. Caused by Epstein-Barr virus infection but typically only occurs in patients who are also immunocompromised.

media.title: HIV patient with oral hairy leukoplakia

GYbBqH.title: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea
GYbBqH.description: A symptom characterized by nocturnal bouts of coughing and acute shortness of breath resulting from the effect of lying in a supine position, which increases pulmonary venous congestion as well as reabsorption and redistribution of edema.

tYbXIH.title: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
tYbXIH.description: An opportunistic infection caused by nontuberculous mycobacteria species that typically affects immune compromised patients (e.g., due to AIDS or immunosuppressive therapy). Symptoms include night sweats, weight loss, lymphadenopathy, abdominal pain, anemia, and leukocytosis. It is usually treated with macrolides and ethambutol.

EYb8IH.title: Fetal growth restriction
EYb8IH.description: A condition in which estimated fetal weight or abdominal circumference is below the 10th percentile for gestational age. Causes may be maternal (e.g., substance use, systemic disease), uteroplacental (e.g., placental insufficiency), and/or fetal (e.g., genetic abnormalities).

yYbd7H.title: Atopic keratoconjunctivitis
yYbd7H.description: A type of allergic conjunctivitis caused by exposure to environmental allergens in individuals with atopy. Characterized by conjunctival injection and discharge as well as atopic dermatitis of the eyelid. Severe cases can lead to ulcers, scarring, cataract, and an increased risk of retinal detachment.

-YbD7H.title: Cryptococcal meningoencephalitis
