-YbD7H.description: An infection of the meninges and/or brain parenchyma by the yeast Cryptococcus neoformans. Typically only affects patients with severe immunodeficiency (e.g., AIDS). Typically has an indolent presentation that progresses over a period of weeks.

0bbeHH.title: Ticarcillin
0bbeHH.description: A carboxypenicillins antibiotic that was discontinued in the US in 2015.

YbbnHH.title: Monobactam
YbbnHH.description: A class of antibiotics with intrinsic β-lactamase resistance that is effective only against gram-negative bacteria. Can be used in individuals who are allergic to penicillins. Usually combined with aminoglycosides to widen antibacterial coverage. Aztreonam is currently the only approved monobactam.

bbbHHH.title: Aztreonam
bbbHHH.description: A monobactam antibiotic that is used predominantly to treat gram-negative infections. An alternative to penicillin in case of allergy, and to aminoglycosides for patients with renal insufficiency.

Xbb9HH.title: Sulfonamides
Xbb9HH.description: A broad category of drugs that have a sulfonamide group. Commonly used sulfa drugs include certain antibiotics (e.g., sulfadiazine, sulfamethoxazole, dapsone), sulfasalazine, celecoxib, sulfonylureas, probenecid, and certain diuretics (thiazides, furosemide, acetazolamide). These drugs are commonly implicated in drug-induced hypersensitivity reactions.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Sulfonamides and diaminopyrimidine

cbbasH.title: Trimethoprim
cbbasH.description: An antibacterial agent that inhibits bacterial dihydrofolate reductase. Most commonly, this drug is compounded with a sulfonamide (such as sulfamethoxazole). Adverse effects from folate antagonism include megaloblastic anemia, leukopenia, and granulocytopenia.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Sulfonamides and diaminopyrimidine

1bb2sH.title: Neomycin
1bb2sH.description: An aminoglycoside antibiotic that is only administered orally and is not absorbed systemically. Used for hepatic encephalopathy (decreases the burden of colonic ammonia-producing bacteria).

WbbPsH.title: Amikacin
WbbPsH.description: An aminoglycoside antibiotic that has potent activity against gram-negative infections (e.g., Pseudomonas aeruginosa). Also has activity against some gram-positive and atypical organisms. Inhibits protein synthesis by binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit. Adverse effects include nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.

dbbosH.title: Sulfamethoxazole
dbbosH.description: A sulfonamide that inhibits folate synthesis. Bacteriostatic. Effective against gram-positive and gram-negative organisms, Nocardia, and Chlamydia. Often used in combination with trimethoprim for sequential block of folate synthesis.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Sulfonamides and diaminopyrimidine

VbbGsH.title: Polymyxins
VbbGsH.description: A class of bactericidal antibiotics that disrupt the cell membranes of gram-negative organisms. Used to treat multidrug-resistant, gram-negative infections. Ineffective against gram-positive bacteria. Examples include polymyxin B and polymyxin E (colistin).

ebbxsH.title: Colistin
ebbxsH.description: A cationic detergent molecule the disrupts cellular membranes and causes cell death due to leakage of intracellular contents. Used to treat infections caused by gram-negative bacilli (particularly Pseudomonas aeruginosa) that are resistant to other antibacterial drugs.

UbbbGH.title: Clinical features of conjunctivitis
UbbbGH.description: A collection of signs and symptoms that suggest conjunctivitis. Features include foreign body sensation, itching, conjunctival injection (pink eye or red eye), swelling of the eye, and ocular discharge.

2bbTGH.title: Neurocysticercosis
2bbTGH.description: A parasitic infection typically acquired by ingesting T. solium eggs, which are excreted in human feces and then ingested (e.g., in contaminated food). The presence of larvae (cysticerci) in the brain can lead to neurological deficits and seizures.

fbbkGH.title: Splenic vein thrombosis
fbbkGH.description: A thrombotic obstruction of the splenic vein that most often occurs as a complication of pancreatitis. Chronic splenic vein thrombosis may result in overt upper gastrointestinal bleeding from gastric varices.

gbbFGH.title: Iliofemoral aneurysm
gbbFGH.description: An aneurysm that forms in the ileofemoral arterial system. May be asymptomatic or result in acute limb ischemia or compression of nearby nerves or veins. Often associated with other aneurysms, especially abdominal and thoracic aortic aneurysms.

3bbStH.title: Phenazopyridine
3bbStH.description: An orally administered local anesthetic that is used for symptomatic relief in patients with urinary tract infections because it is rapidly and completely eliminated in urine. Patients who are prescribed phenazopyridine should be warned that the drug can cause an orange discoloration of bodily fluids. The use of phenazopyridine is contraindicated in patients with renal insufficiency and/or severe liver dysfunction.

ibbJtH.title: Heberden nodes
ibbJtH.description: Nodules on the dorsal aspect of the distal interphalangeal joints (DIPs) caused by the formation of osteophytes/bony spurs. Can cause pain and functional impairment. Characteristically seen in patients with osteoarthritis.

media.title: Distribution pattern of osteoarthritis of the hand

QbbutH.title: Bouchard nodes
QbbutH.description: Nodules on the dorsal aspect of the proximal interphalangeal joints (PIPs) caused by the formation of osteophytes/bony spurs. Can cause pain and functional impairment. Characteristically seen in patients, mainly women, with osteoarthritis.

jbb_tH.title: Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysms
jbb_tH.description: An aneurysm that develops in small blood vessels in the brain (e.g., lenticulostriate arteries). Associated with chronic hypertension and diabetes. Not visible on angiogram. Their rupture can cause intracerebral hemorrhage.

PbbWFH.title: Intracranial aneurysm
PbbWFH.description: Abnormal dilation of a cerebral artery or vein, especially around the circle of Willis. Berry (saccular) aneurysms are the most common type, although fusiform, mycotic, traumatic, or Charcot-Bouchard aneurysms also occur.

Nbb-FH.title: Blaschko’s lines
Nbb-FH.description: A system of lines in skin that correspond to the route of migration of ectodermal cells during embryonic development. These lines, which are not related to dermatomes, lines of skin tension, or lines of lymphatic drainage, are linear over the limbs, V-shaped over back, and S-shaped over the abdomen. Blaschko's lines are normally not visible, but certain congenital skin lesions (e.g., epidermal nevi) occur along these lines.

mbbV8H.title: Rifabutin
mbbV8H.description: An antibiotic similar to rifampin that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by preventing transcription. Commonly used to treat tuberculosis and Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infection in patients with AIDS.

5bbi8H.title: Rifamycin
5bbi8H.description: A group of antibiotics that obstruct bacterial protein synthesis by inhibiting bacterial DNA-dependent RNA-polymerase. Includes rifampin and rifabutin. Effective against mycobacterial disease (e.g., tuberculosis) and certain invasive staphylococcal infections. Used as chemoprophylaxis for N. meningitidis and H. influenzae infection. Adverse effects include orange discoloration of body fluids (e.g., urine, tears) and CYP450 induction.

MbbM8H.title: Consumption coagulopathy
MbbM8H.description: A pathologic state characterized by hyperfibrinolysis and hypercoagulability, which results in the formation of thrombi in the organs and microcirculation. This process results in the consumption of clotting factors, platelets, and fibrinogen.

nbb78H.title: Extrinsic pathway (hemostasis)
nbb78H.description: A part of the coagulation cascade that is activated by injury to the endothelium. Consists of tissue factor (factor III) and factor VII. Impairment of this pathway results in bleeding disorders (e.g., factor VII deficiency).

obb0uH.title: Thessaly test
obb0uH.description: A physical examination maneuver that tests injury to the meniscus of the knee. The patient stands (with assistance) on the affected leg at 20° of knee flexion, then rotates their knee externally and internally. Joint line pain with rotation, a clicking noise, or a feeling that the knee is locking or catching suggest meniscal injury.

pbbLuH.title: Peau d'orange
pbbLuH.description: A skin appearance resembling the rind of an orange, characterized by skin thickening and areas of dimpling. Occurs secondary to lymphatic obstruction and lymphedema (e.g., underlying breast tumor) or to an infection of the soft tissue (e.g., erysipelas, cellulitis).

media.title: Inflammation of breast with peau d'orange change

7bb4EH.title: Extravascular hemolysis
7bb4EH.description: A form of hemolysis in which RBCs are phagocytosed by macrophages within the liver, spleen, and/or bone marrow. Distinct from intravascular hemolysis, in which RBCs are lysed within blood vessels, usually due to mechanical damage or complement fixation.

HbbKEH.title: Acetaminophen overdose
HbbKEH.description: The ingestion of a large dose of acetaminophen. Acute overdose is defined as ≥ 7.5 g for adults or ≥ 150 mg/kg for children < 24 hours before presentation. Chronic overdose is usually defined as ≥ 6 g/day or ≥ 150 mg/kg/day (whichever is less) if ingested over a period of 24–48 hours and ≥ 4 g/day or ≥ 100 mg/kg/day (whichever is less) if ingested over a period of > 48 hours. May cause nausea, vomiting, and, in severe cases, acute liver failure. Treatment involves administration of N-acetylcysteine; patients with acute liver failure may require liver transplantation.

GbbBEH.title: Barbiturate overdose
GbbBEH.description: An intoxication that presents with neurologic, psychiatric, respiratory, and/or cardiovascular changes. The classic barbiturate toxidrome includes a combination of: sedation/altered mental status, blurred vision (due to miosis or mydriasis), hypothermia, hypotension, bradypnea, and nystagmus. The pharmacotherapy of choice is sodium bicarbonate to increase excretion by urine alkalization.

FbbgvH.title: Percutaneous balloon valvuloplasty
FbbgvH.description: A procedure used to treat cardiac valvular stenosis. A balloon is advanced into the target valve (either percutaneously or transapically) and inflated, "stretching" open the stenotic valve in the process.

8bbOvH.title: Wood lamp examination
8bbOvH.description: A procedure in which ultraviolet light is used to examine skin lesions. Characteristic patterns of fluorescence under ultraviolet light can help in the diagnosis of pigmentation disorders (e.g., vitiligo, melasma) and superficial fungal infections of the skin (e.g., erythrasma).

CbbqDH.title: Physiologic tremor
CbbqDH.description: A type of postural tremor that is not caused by an underlying disorder and is considered normal. Typically manifests as a fine bilateral tremor when holding a position against gravity. Physiologic tremors may worsen as a result of sympathetic stimulation; causes include stress, exercise, fatigue, caffeine, alcohol, hypoglycemia, and certain drugs (e.g., SSRIs, beta-2 agonists) and medical conditions (hyperthyroidism, pheochromocytoma).

BbbzDH.title: Demeclocycline
BbbzDH.description: An antibiotic in the tetracycline class used to treat acne, bronchitis, and Lyme disease. It is also used as a treatment for hyponatremia caused by the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH), as the drug inhibits adenylyl cyclase activation in the kidney. Adverse effects are similar to other tetracyclines, but it is the only drug in the class that can cause nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

AbbRwH.title: Floxacillin
AbbRwH.description: A penicillinase-resistant penicillin used to treat infections caused by gram-positive organisms.

_bb5wH.title: Antimycobacterial drugs
_bb5wH.description: A group of drugs used to treat infections caused by Mycobacterium species. Examples include rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Antimycobacterial drugs

zbbrwH.title: Chloramphenicol
zbbrwH.description: A bacteriostatic antibiotic that inhibits peptidyltransferase at the 50S ribosomal subunit in bacteria. Used to treat bacterial meningitis and rickettsial infections (e.g., murine typhus). Adverse effects include gray baby syndrome and aplastic anemia.

-bbDwH.title: Beta-lactam antibiotics
-bbDwH.description: A class of bactericidal, broad-spectrum antibiotics that includes penicillins, carbapenems, aztreonam, and cephalosporins. Function by binding to penicillin-binding proteins, inhibiting peptidoglycan crosslinking (and thus cell wall synthesis). Eliminated primarily renally. Adverse effects include hypersensitivity reactions. Often used in conjunction with beta-lactamase inhibitors because many organisms produce beta-lactamase enzymes.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Beta-lactam antibiotics

ZXbZ9H.title: Homonymous hemianopia
ZXbZ9H.description: Bilateral impairment of a unilateral visual field in each eye. For example, left homonymous hemianopia involves the inability to see the left visual field in either eye, i.e. impairment of the temporal visual field in the left eye and the nasal visual field of the right eye. Starting at the optic chiasm, information from the left visual field in each eye is relayed by the right optic tract to the right visual cortex, where it is processed. Accordingly, homonymous hemianopia occurs as the result of lesions between the optic chiasm and visual cortex.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Scotoma and anopia

0Xbe9H.title: Short-acting insulin
0Xbe9H.description: A type of insulin with an onset of action ∼30 minutes after administration, early peak plasma levels (2-3 hours after administration), and duration of action of 4-6 hours. Regular insulin is an example of a short-acting insulin.

aXbQ9H.title: Intermediate-acting insulin
aXbQ9H.description: A type of insulin that has an onset of action 1-4 hours after administration, intermediate peak plasma levels (6-10 hours after administration), and typically last 10-16 hours. NPH insulin is an intermediate-acting insulin.

YXbn9H.title: Long-acting insulin
YXbn9H.description: A group of insulin analogs that have an onset of action 1-4 hours after administration, no defined peak, and typically last > 24 hours. Examples include insulin glargine and insulin detemir.

bXbH9H.title: Diffusion-weighted MRI
bXbH9H.description: A form of magnetic resonance imaging that is based on measuring the diffusion of water molecules in tissue. Used in the evaluation of acute ischemic stroke and transient ischemic attack.

XXb99H.title: Perfusion-weighted imaging
XXb99H.description: A neuroimaging technique used in patients with suspected acute ischemic stroke to detect areas of cerebral hypoperfusion. This can be done using CT or MRI. Areas of perfusion-diffusion mismatch suggest potentially salvageable brain tissue and can be an important factor in treatment decisions.

cXbaCH.title: Cystic echinococcosis
cXbaCH.description: A condition caused by E. graulosus infection. After a long incubation period, can manifest with a single hepatic cyst (hydatid cyst), hepatomegaly, and RUQ pain. Can involve the lungs.

1Xb2CH.title: Alveolar echinococcosis
1Xb2CH.description: A condition caused by E. multilocularis infection. After an incubation period of 5–10 years, typically manifests with malaise, weight loss, RUQ pain, and hepatomegaly. Primary disease outside of the liver is rare.

WXbPCH.title: Hemangioblastoma
WXbPCH.description: A rare, benign, primary CNS tumor of vascular origin that is almost always infratentorial and most commonly affects middle-aged adults.

VXbGCH.title: Medial collateral ligament injury
VXbGCH.description: The most common ligamentous knee injury. Typically causes by valgus stress (especially with external rotation). Manifestations include knee swelling, medial joint line tenderness, deformity, and instability. Often associated with medial meniscal tears.

destinations.label: Knee ligament injuries → Collateral ligament injury

UXbbxH.title: Posterior drawer test
UXbbxH.description: A physical examination maneuver that assesses for posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) injury. The patient lies in the supine position and flexes the knee to 90°. The foot of the knee being tested is fixed in place by the examiner and the patient is asked to relax. The proximal end of the tibia is then pushed posteriorly. A firm endpoint along with the absence of posterior tibial movement implies that the PCL is intact. If there is a lax endpoint or significant posterior displacement of the tibia (especially in comparison to the contralateral leg), the test is positive.

destinations.label: Knee ligament injuries → Posterior cruciate ligament injury

fXbkxH.title: Valgus stress test
fXbkxH.description: A test for medial collateral ligament injuries. Gentle valgus stress is applied across the knee while the patient is in the supine position with the hip slightly flexed (20–30° of flexion) and abducted and the knee slightly flexed. Medial joint laxity indicates medial collateral ligament tear.

destinations.label: Knee ligament injuries → Collateral ligament injury

TXb6xH.title: Varus stress test
TXb6xH.description: A test for lateral collateral ligament injury. Gentle varus stress is applied across the knee while the patient is in the supine posiotion with the hip slightly flexed (20–30° of flexion) and abducted and the knee slightly flexed. Lateral joint laxity indicates lateral collateral ligament tear.

destinations.label: Knee ligament injuries → Collateral ligament injury

hXbcBH.title: Percutaneous nephrostomy
hXbcBH.description: A urologic procedure that involves the insertion of a pigtail catheter into the dilated renal pelvis under ultrasound guidance using the Seldinger technique to rapidly drain urine and relieve pressure on the renal parenchyma. Indicated for complete urinary tract obstruction and a concomitant infection as a temporary solution until definitive treatment can be performed.

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Urinary drainage procedures

3XbSBH.title: Codeine
3XbSBH.description: An opioid that is most commonly used as an analgesic and to treat cough. Carries a high risk of addiction.

RXblBH.title: Chronic pulmonary aspergillosis
RXblBH.description: A chronic pulmonary infection caused by Aspergillus spp. that develops in individuals with preexisting lung disease and can manifest as an aspergilloma, aspergillus nodule, cavitary or fibrosing aspergillosis, or subacute invasive aspergillosis. Symptoms include shortness of breath, weight loss, and chronic fatigue.

media.title: Aspergilloma (fungus ball) within right upper lobe cavity

iXbJBH.title: Methadone
iXbJBH.description: A long-acting oral or parenteral opioid commonly used to treat opioid withdrawal and some forms of chronic/severe pain (e.g., malignancy).

QXbuBH.title: Butorphanol
QXbuBH.description: An opioid analgesic that has κ-receptor agonistic and μ-receptor partial agonistic properties. Associated with a lower risk of respiratory depression compared to other opioid agonists.

jXb_BH.title: Superior vena cava syndrome
jXb_BH.description: A condition caused by obstruction of blood flow in the superior vena cava (e.g., by a thrombus or external compression). This impairs venous backflow to the right atrium and results in upper venous congestion. Features include a feeling of fullness in the head, dyspnea, edema of the upper extremities, and distention of the superficial veins of the chest, face, and upper extremities.

destinations.label: Oncologic emergencies → Superior vena cava syndrome

4Xb3yH.title: Brainstem glioma
4Xb3yH.description: A tumor arising from glial cells in the brainstem. Common presenting symptoms include cranial nerve deficits, ataxia, and upper motor neuron signs. Treatment usually consists of radiation or chemotherapy, as surgical resection is often impossible. The prognosis is generally poor due to the tumor's aggressiveness and location.

kXbmyH.title: Claw sign
kXbmyH.description: A radiologic sign that refers to sharp angles on either side of a mass. It suggests that the mass has arisen from the parenchyma itself, rather than just being located adjacent to it.

NXb-yH.title: Telogen effluvium
NXb-yH.description: A type of alopecia caused by premature shedding of hair follicles that are in the resting phase (telogen) of hair growth. Results in diffuse, nonscarring hair loss but does not progress to complete baldness. Etiologies include hypothyroidism, drug adverse effects, malnutrition, severe psychological stress, and chronic illness. Hair pull test is typically positive.

oXb0_H.title: Nasogastric tube aspiration
oXb0_H.description: A procedure in which a nasogastric tube is passed into the stomach, a small amount of liquid is instilled, and the stomach contents are aspirated by suction. Although previously used to identify gastrointestinal bleeding, the procedure is now generally thought to have limited diagnostic value.

KXbU_H.title: Neonatal abstinence syndrome
KXbU_H.description: Withdrawal reaction in a newborn due to maternal opioid use (or sometimes other substances) during pregnancy. Usually presents during the first days of life with variable symptoms (e.g., irritability, seizures, gastrointestinal problems, sneezing, and sweating).

HXbKzH.title: Mixed insulin
HXbKzH.description: A mixture of intermediate-acting insulin (NPH insulin) and either regular insulin or a rapid-acting insulin (e.g., insulin aspart) used in conventional insulin therapy. Typical combinations include a 70/30 and 50/50 ratio of NPH insulin to rapid-acting or regular insulin.

sXbtzH.title: Amniotic fluid embolism
sXbtzH.description: A rare but life-threatening condition in the peripartum period caused by the entry of fetal cells and debris from the amniotic fluid into maternal circulation. These cells and debris are thromboplastin-rich and trigger disseminated intravascular coagulation. Risk factors include placental abruption, uterine rupture, grand multiparity, age > 35 years, and certain procedures such as amniocentesis.

GXbBzH.title: Fat embolism
GXbBzH.description: Entry of fat particles into the pulmonary vessels and/or into the vessels of the CNS resulting in embolisms. Most commonly associated with closed long bone fractures. Manifests with a classic triad of dyspnea, neurological deficits, and a petechial rash (50% of cases).

FXbg-H.title: Overflow incontinence
FXbg-H.description: An involuntary leakage of urine secondary to overfilling of the bladder. Etiologies include underactivity of the detrusor muscle and bladder outlet obstruction.

EXb8-H.title: Pad test
EXb8-H.description: A diagnostic test used in the evaluation of urinary incontinence. Patients wear a preweighed sanitary pad and drink a specified volume of liquid. The pad is then weighed again to measure urinary leakage.

vXbA-H.title: Sexual maturity rating
vXbA-H.description: A sexual maturity rating scale used to assess the development of secondary sexual characteristics. Includes stages for development of pubic hair in both boys and girls (stages Ph1–6), breast development in girls (stages B1–5), and genital development in boys (stages G1–5).

destinations.label: Puberty → Development of secondary sexual characteristics

9XbNZs.title: Deep sulcus sign
9XbNZs.description: Abnormal deepening and darkening of the costophrenic angle on supine chest x-ray that is caused by air gathering in the pleural cavity. Diagnostic finding in cases of pneumothorax.

AXbR0s.title: Mixed incontinence
AXbR0s.description: A condition with features of both stress and urge incontinence.

zXbr0s.title: West Nile virus
zXbr0s.description: A vector-borne flavivirus most often transmitted by Culex mosquitoes. Infection manifests with fever, headache, myalgias, rash, and, rarely, encephalitis.

-XbD0s.title: Meningococcal meningitis
-XbD0s.description: An inflammation of the protective membranes surrounding the brain and the spinal cord caused by infection with Neisseria meningitidis.

ZcbZas.title: Total incontinence
ZcbZas.description: Urinary incontinence characterized by continuous loss of urine that is not associated with preceding symptoms (e.g., urinary urgency) or triggered by a specific activity (e.g, sneezing). Caused by a complete loss of sphincter function that may be due to previous surgery, nerve damage, metastasis, or abnormal anatomy (e.g., fistula between urinary tract and skin).

Ycbnas.title: Opioid analgesics
Ycbnas.description: A group of endogenous and exogenous substances that act on μ-, κ-, and δ- (opioid-) receptors in the CNS and the gastrointestinal tract. Opioids provide effective analgesia and are used to treat severe acute or chronic pain. They also induce sedation and constipation; effects that can be used therapeutically. Additionally, opioids reduce coughing. Other effects include strong euphoria and respiratory depression.

bcbHas.title: Opioid withdrawal
bcbHas.description: A constellation of symptoms that manifest following the abrupt cessation or reduction of opioid use after a period of prolonged chronic use. Characterized by sympathetic hyperactivity (e.g., tachycardia, hypertension, mydriasis, hyperreflexia, irritability), gastrointestinal perturbations (e.g., excessive lacrimation, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea), and flu-like symptoms (e.g., rhinorrhea, chills, piloerection).

Xcb9as.title: Solitary pulmonary nodule
Xcb9as.description: A small (≤ 30 mm) lesion in the pulmonary parenchyma. Can be purely solid (dense and homogeneous on imaging) or subsolid (hypodense or ground-glass component on imaging, with or without a solid component).

media.title: Spiculated lung lesion with pleural tags

dcboYs.title: Type 4 renal tubular acidosis
dcboYs.description: A condition caused by impaired sodium reabsorption in the distal tubule, usually due to hypoaldosteronism. Manifests with a normal anion gap, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis as well as hyperkalemia and low urine pH.

destinations.label: Renal tubular disorders →  Hyperkalemic renal tubular acidosis (type 4)

VcbGYs.title: Carbonic anhydrase II deficiency
VcbGYs.description: An autosomal recessive disease that leads to renal tubular acidosis, osteopetrosis with recurring pathological fractures, and cerebral calcification that can cause intellectual disability.

destinations.label: Renal tubular disorders →  Mixed renal tubular acidosis (type 3)

ecbxYs.title: Type 2 renal tubular acidosis
ecbxYs.description: A condition caused by an inability of the proximal convoluted tubule cells to reabsorb bicarbonate. Associated with other defects of reabsorption. Manifests with a normal anion gap metabolic acidosis, hypophosphatemia, hypokalemia, stunted growth, polyuria, and polydipsia. Etiologies include inherited disorders (e.g., cystinosis, tyrosinemia), amyloidosis, and multiple myeloma.

destinations.label: Renal tubular disorders → Proximal renal tubular acidosis (type 2)

Ucbbbs.title: Type 1 renal tubular acidosis
Ucbbbs.description: A normal anion gap metabolic acidosis and hypokalemia caused by an inability of the distal convoluted tubule to excrete H+ due to decreased activity of the H+/K+ ATPase antiporter on the apical surface of intercalated cell, which reabsorbs K+ and secretes H+ into the lumen of the tubule. Common causes among adults include autoimmune diseases (e.g., Sjögren syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis), hypercalciuria, and drugs such as ifosfamide and lithium. The most common cause among children in a hereditary gene defect.

destinations.label: Renal tubular disorders →  Distal renal tubular acidosis (type 1)

fcbkbs.title: Liddle syndrome
fcbkbs.description: A rare, autosomal dominant disease caused by mutations in genes that encode the epithelial sodium channel in the collecting duct (ENaC), which is responsible for the active reabsorption of sodium and water. These mutations result in structural alterations in these channels, making them more resistant to degradation. Patients subsequently develop pseudohyperaldosteronism.

Tcb6bs.title: Gitelman syndrome
Tcb6bs.description: A renal tubular disorder with clinical features including fatigue, muscle weakness or cramps, polyuria, and chondrocalcinosis. Typically affects individuals in late childhood and adulthood. Caused by an autosomal recessive defect that results in impaired function of the thiazide-sensitive sodium-chloride cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule.

gcbFbs.title: Fludrocortisone
gcbFbs.description: A synthetic mineralocorticoid with strong aldosterone activity that is used to treat primary adrenal insufficiency, 21-hydroxylase deficiency of congenital adrenal hyperplasia, and orthostatic intolerance.

Scbybs.title: Beclomethasone
Scbybs.description: A synthetic glucocorticoid used as topically and in inhaled formulation (e.g., to treat asthma).

3cbSXs.title: Fasting plasma glucose
3cbSXs.description: The measurement of serum glucose concentration after > 8 hours of fasting. A value ≥ 126 mg/dL indicates diabetes mellitus. A value between 100 and 125 mg/dL indicates impaired fasting glucose (due to a prediabetic state).

icbJXs.title: Bronchoscopy
icbJXs.description: An endoscopic procedure for visualizing the airways. Can be performed as a diagnostic (e.g., bronchoalveolar lavage, biopsies, cytology, transbronchial needle aspiration, and endobronchial ultrasound) or therapeutic (e.g., balloon dilatation, ablation, brachytherapy, and stent placement) measure.

QcbuXs.title: Megaureter
QcbuXs.description: A pathologically enlarged ureter, either due to a primary disease of the ureter or distal obstruction causing dilation of the ureter.

media.title: Congenital anomalies of the kidneys and urinary tract (CAKUT)

jcb_Xs.title: Alpha-1 blocker
jcb_Xs.description: A group of drugs that act as antagonists on α-1 adrenoreceptors and induce relaxation of blood vessels as well as the smooth muscle cells of the bladder neck and the urethra. Used to treat hypertension (e.g., doxazosin) or benign prostatic hyperplasia (e.g., tamsulosin, alfuzosin).

OcbIcs.title: Carotid artery stenosis
OcbIcs.description: A narrowing of the carotid artery due to atherosclerosis. Usually most prominent within 2 cm of the carotid bifurcation.

lcbvcs.title: Bernard-Soulier syndrome
lcbvcs.description: A hereditary platelet disorder characterized by thrombocytopenia, platelet dysfunction, giant platelets, and bleeding diathesis. Caused by ↓ Gp Ib/IX/V complex on platelet surface (receptor for von Willebrand factor) and resulting impaired platelet adhesion.

Ncb-cs.title: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
Ncb-cs.description: A rare autosomal-recessive bleeding disorder caused by deficient fibrinogen receptor GpIIb/IIIa in platelets, leading to defective platelet aggregation and subsequent increased mucosal bleeding (e.g., epistaxis, gingival bleeding), petechiae, and ecchymoses.

McbM1s.title: Neurogenic shock
McbM1s.description: Systemic hypoperfusion caused by decreased vascular sympathetic tone after an insult to the central nervous system. Characterized by hypotension and often accompanied by bradycardia. Most commonly seen in acute spinal cord injury but can also occur after brain injury.

Lcbw1s.title: Germ cell tumors
Lcbw1s.description: A tumor that arises from reproductive cells. Examples include seminoma, dysgerminoma, teratoma, and yolk sac tumors. Can arise in extragonadal locations.

ocb0Ws.title: Non-germ cell cancer of the testis
ocb0Ws.description: A category of testicular tumors that arise from nongerm cells. Includes tumors derived from the hormone-producing stromal cells of the testes (Sertoli and Leydig cells) and testicular lymphoma.

KcbUWs.title: Extragonadal germ cell tumors
KcbUWs.description: A primary germ cell tumor that arises anywhere along the body's midline, from the pineal gland to the coccyx, except for the gonads. The most common site is the anterior mediastinum in adults and sacrococcygeal region in young children. Non-seminomatous EGCTs often have elevated tumor markers (AFP and β-hCG).

6cbjWs.title: Relative mineralocorticoid potency
6cbjWs.description: The potency of a steroid (in terms of its effect on sodium retention) compared with hydrocortisone. Hydrocortisone is the synthetic equivalent to physiologic cortisol and has, by definition, a mineralocorticoid potency of 1. The relative mineralocorticoid potency can be used to calculate dosages required for a substitution regimen and when switching from one steroid to another.

scbtds.title: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
scbtds.description: A type of cardiomyopathy characterized by fibro-fatty replacement of myocardium with ventricular dilation and thinning. Associated with arrhythmias.

tcbXVs.title: Arrhythmia-induced cardiomyopathy
tcbXVs.description: A reversible cardiomyopathy caused by long-standing tachycardia. Changes typically consist of LV dilatation and increased LV filling pressures and pulmonary artery pressures with a corresponding fall in systemic cardiac output. These changes usually resolve with treatment.

FcbgVs.title: Cardiac exercise stress test
FcbgVs.description: A diagnostic study used to test for coronary artery disease and myocardial ischemia. Graded exercise is used to induce an oxygen demand-supply mismatch. ECG, echocardiogram, MRI, PET, or SPECT is then obtained to evaluate for ischemia.

destinations.label: Coronary artery disease → Cardiac stress testing

8cbOVs.title: Cardiac pharmacological stress test
8cbOVs.description: A diagnostic study used to test for coronary artery disease and myocardial ischemia. Involves the administration of  pharmacological agents to induce (and detect) an oxygen demand-supply mismatch in the myocardium. This is achieved either via an agent that causes dilation of the coronary arteries, which results in a coronary steal phenomenon (adenosine, dipyridamole), or an increase in heart rate and contractility, similar to that seen in exercise (dobutamine).

destinations.label: Coronary artery disease → Cardiac stress testing

Ecb8Vs.title: Adson test
Ecb8Vs.description: A physical examination test to evaluate for thoracic outlet syndrome. The patient's radial pulse is monitored while their shoulder is abducted, externally rotated, and extended. Weakening or loss of pulse (a positive test) indicates compression of the subclavian artery by the scalene muscles or a cervical rib (rare). Asking the patient to extend their head and rotate it to the affected side while inhaling deeply may cause a more significant decrease in radial pulse.

vcbAVs.title: Wright test
vcbAVs.description: A physical examination test to assess for thoracic outlet syndrome. The patient's shoulder is passively abducted to a 90° angle, and then the elbow is externally rotated and flexed, followed by hyperabduction of the arms over the head. The test is positive if radial pulse is decreased and/or if paresthesia develops or intensifies.

Dcb1es.title: Roos stress test
Dcb1es.description: A provocation test used to reproduce symptoms of thoracic outlet syndrome. Both shoulders are positioned in abduction and are externally rotated at 90° angles, with elbows flexed at 90°, while the patient repeatedly makes a fist and then relaxes the hand. Considered positive if there is a sensation of heaviness or fatigue in affected limb.

wcbhes.title: Preseptal cellulitis
wcbhes.description: Infection of the soft tissues anterior to the orbital septum (a membrane that extends from the orbital rims to the eyelids and lies anterior to the orbital contents). Characterized by ocular pain and eyelid erythema and edema.

Ccbqes.title: Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction
Ccbqes.description: An adverse reaction to blood transfusion that occurs within the first 24 hours after transfusion. Causes include ABO incompatibility and the immune response to other blood group antigens (e.g., Kell, Duffy, Jk). Results in the destruction of donor red blood cells by recipient antibodies. Manifestations include fever, gastrointestinal symptoms, and allergic symptoms (e.g., flushing, itching, urticaria). Can cause disseminated intravascular coagulation, renal failure, and jaundice.

destinations.label: Transfusion reactions → Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction

xcbEes.title: Delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction
xcbEes.description: An adverse reaction to blood transfusion that occurs days to weeks after the transfusion. Occurs in patients who were previously sensitized to specific red blood cell antigens. Mediated by the immune response upon reexposure to minor blood group antigens or D (Rh) antigens. Manifestations include fever, jaundice, and anemia.

Bcbzes.title: Nonhemolytic febrile transfusion reaction
Bcbzes.description: A complication associated with blood transfusion that is characterized by a fever within 6 hours of receiving blood products due to leakage of cytokines from donor RBCs and/or host immune response to residual donor leukocytes. Complicates 3% of transfusions.

destinations.label: Transfusion reactions → Febrile nonhemolytic transfusion reaction

ycbdUs.title: Packed red blood cells
ycbdUs.description: A collection of red blood cells that have been prepared for blood transfusion by removing plasma from whole blood. Packed red blood cells may be further treated with leukoreduction to remove leukocytes (reducing the risk of non-hemolytic febrile transfusion reactions) and irradiation to inactivate lymphocytes for use in patients who are immunosuppressed (reducing the risk of graft-versus-host disease).

AcbRUs.title: Sideroblastic anemia
AcbRUs.description: A form of anemia caused by ineffective heme synthesis. Characterized by the presence of basophilic stippling and ringed sideroblasts in a peripheral blood smear and secondary iron overload. May be congenital or acquired. Usually causes microcytic anemia, although normocytic or even macrocytic variants are possible.

Y1bn2s.title: Prayer sign
Y1bn2s.description: A physical examination finding characterized by an inability to appose the hands due to contractures of the metacarpophalangeal, proximal interphalangeal, and/or distal interphalangeal joints. Used to diagnose limited joint mobility in patients with diabetes mellitus.

f1bkTs.title: Open fracture
f1bkTs.description: A fracture in which the bone and/or soft tissue are exposed to the external environment. Compared to closed fractures, open fractures are more prone to infection and neurovascular injury.

destinations.label: General principles of fractures → Subtypes and variants

media.title: Open fracture of the right ankle
Open fracture of the left ankle

T1b6Ts.title: Myocardial infarction
T1b6Ts.description: An acute myocardial injury caused by ischemia that results in tissue necrosis. Most commonly caused by atherothrombotic coronary artery disease (type 1 MI) or another cause of mismatch between oxygen supply and demand (type 2 MI). Further classified clinically into ST-elevation MI (STEMI) and non-ST-elevation MI (NSTEMI).

media.title: Acute inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)
Symptoms of an acute myocardial infarction

R1blgs.title: Intrauterine adhesions
R1blgs.description: A condition characterized by adhesions and/or fibrosis of the endometrium that can cause amenorrhea and infertility. Associated with intrauterine instrumentation (e.g., dilation and curettage), postpartum hemorrhage, or intrauterine infections.

destinations.label: Anomalies of the female genital tract → Anomalies of the uterus

i1bJgs.title: Mupirocin
i1bJgs.description: An antibiotic that is primarily effective against gram-positive bacteria. Used topically for treatment of skin infections (e.g., impetigo, folliculitis) and MRSA decolonization (when applied to the anterior nares).

Q1bugs.title: Scintigraphy
Q1bugs.description: An imaging procedure in which low doses of radioactive substances are injected into the bloodstream and then detected by a device (gamma camera), providing information about the metabolic activity of body structures. The selection of the radioactive agent depends on the structure to be scanned (e.g., thyroid gland, bowel, bones, heart, lungs).

media.title: Nuclear medicine bone scan in Paget disease of the bone
Mismatched perfusion defects from pulmonary emboli
Thyroid scan before and after radioiodine therapy in Graves disease

O1bISs.title: Subcutaneous emphysema
O1bISs.description: A condition that results from entrapment of air or gas into the subcutaneous tissues and typically presents with sudden, painless soft tissue swelling, often around the upper chest, neck, and face. Often identified by eliciting crepitus on examination. Etiologies include pulmonary barotrauma (as during mechanical ventilation), surgery, and infection (e.g., gas gangrene).

media.title: Traumatic pneumothorax and pneumomediastinum with subcutaneous emphysema

l1bvSs.title: Flail chest
l1bvSs.description: Paradoxical motion of part of the chest upon breathing, in which it visibly collapses inward on inspiration, leading to respiratory distress, tachypnea, and shallow breathing. Caused by detachment of a segment of the rib cage from the chest wall, which results from three or more adjacent ribs fractured in two or more places.

N1b-Ss.title: Doppler ultrasound
N1b-Ss.description: An imaging test that uses a probe emitting high-frequency sound waves to estimate blood flow within blood vessels via the doppler effect.

m1bVhs.title: Contrast-enhanced CT scan
m1bVhs.description: A computerized tomography scan in which a radiocontrast agent is used to better delineate internal structures. The contrast can be administered intravenously, orally, or rectally, depending on the indication.

51bihs.title: Middle segment pancreatectomy
51bihs.description: Resection of the pancreatic neck and proximal body with sparing of the head and tail. This procedure may be indicated for benign central pancreatic lesions (like cystadenomas), pancreatic trauma, and tumors in the neck of the pancreas. An advantage of this tissue-saving procedure is that it can preserve pancreatic exocrine and endocrine function.

destinations.label: Pancreatic and hepatic surgery → Pancreatic surgery

n1b7hs.title: Colonic diverticulosis
n1b7hs.description: A condition characterized by the presence of multiple outpouchings at weak points in the colonic wall (usually between the taenia coli). Likely caused by increased intraluminal pressure due to straining and reduced elasticity of the wall with age. Typically asymptomatic but can bleed and/or become inflamed (i.e., diverticulitis).

L1bwhs.title: Thromboembolism
L1bwhs.description: The obstruction of a blood vessel by a clot or its pieces that have dislodged from another site in circulation where the clot first formed. May be venous (e.g., DVT or pulmonary embolism) or arterial. Arterial thromboembolism is usually an acute event resulting in ischemic tissue damage (e.g., stroke, acute mesenteric ischemia, acute limb ischemia, acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary infarction).

o1b03s.title: Long-leg cast
o1b03s.description: A cast that extends from the middle of the thigh to the base of the toes, and immobilizes the knee at 5–20° of flexion and the ankle in the neutral position. Commonly used to treat fractures of the distal femur, patella, tibia, and/or fibula.

K1bU3s.title: Arthroscopy
K1bU3s.description: A minimally invasive surgical procedure in which the inside of a large joint (e.g., knee, shoulder) is directly visualized using an endoscope. Used to diagnose intra-articular pathologies that are not apparent on imaging. Instruments can also be inserted through the incision (arthroscopic port) into the joint space for therapeutic procedures (e.g., removal of bony and/or cartilaginous fragments, ligament and/or meniscal reconstruction).

p1bL3s.title: Levalbuterol
p1bL3s.description: A short-acting beta-agonist used for bronchodilation in patients with asthma or COPD. It is a pure R-albuterol enantiomer, such that it may have fewer systemic adverse effects (e.g., tachycardia) with similar efficacy as racemic albuterol (contains both R- and S-enantiomer).

q1bC3s.title: Proximal femoral osteotomy
q1bC3s.description: A reconstructive surgery in which the proximal femur is cut, following which the cut ends are realigned and refixed. Used to treat malunion or non-union of hip fractures, as well as certain acquired or congenital hip deformities. The exact site of the osteotomy (e.g., intertrochanteric region, greater trochanter) and the type of realignment vary depending on the indication.

71b4Rs.title: Foley catheter
71b4Rs.description: A thin, flexible, and sterile tube inserted through the urethra to continuously drain urine into a urine collection bag. The catheter is held in the bladder by a water-filled balloon.

H1bKRs.title: Pericardiocentesis
H1bKRs.description: A procedure used to drain pericardial fluid, usually guided by ultrasound. A large needle is introduced via a subxiphoid, parasternal, or apical approach. Pericardial fluid is drained by simple needle aspiration or placement of a pericardial drain.

s1btRs.title: Aspirin
s1btRs.description: An irreversible cyclooxygenase-1 inhibitor that is used as an analgesic, antipyretic, anti-inflammatory, and antiplatelet drug. Low-dose aspirin is used in the management of cardiovascular events (e.g., acute MI, angina) and for primary/secondary prophylaxis of cardiovascular disease. Adverse effects include peptic ulcers, hemorrhage, aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease, and Reye syndrome.

G1bBRs.title: Norepinephrine
G1bBRs.description: A catecholamine hormone and neurotransmitter produced in the adrenal medulla and in noradrenergic neurons by hydroxylation of dopamine. It is an agonist at alpha receptors with lower affinity for beta-1 receptors that has no effect on beta-2 receptors. Used to treat hypotension and shock by increasing systemic vascular resistance and inotropy.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

F1bgis.title: Pneumonitis
F1bgis.description: A condition of lung tissue inflammation. Etiologies include exposure to environmental allergens (e.g., hypersensitivity pneumonitis), radiation (e.g., radiation-induced lung injury), and aspiration (e.g., chemical pneumonitis). Can also be idiopathic (e.g., acute interstitial pneumonitis).

81bOis.title: Peritoneal lavage
81bOis.description: Irrigation of the peritoneal cavity with fluid. Peritoneal lavage may be performed in order to obtain a diagnostic sample for cytological studies, or therapeutically in order to remove blood, fecal matter, and/or purulent secretions from the peritoneal cavity.

u1bpis.title: Laparotomy
u1bpis.description: A surgical procedure in which a large incision is made through the abdominal wall to access the abdominal cavity. Used for major intra-abdominal surgeries that are difficult to perform laparoscopically, or for exploring the abdominal cavity in emergencies such as peritonitis, bowel gangrene, perforated abdominal viscus, or intra-abdominal hemorrhage.

E1b8is.title: Arthrocentesis
E1b8is.description: A diagnostic and/or therapeutic procedure in which synovial fluid from a joint is aspirated using a sterile needle to determine the etiology of joint effusions, as well as to relieve pain or pressure from a joint. Usually done as an office procedure or at the bedside of hospitalized patients.

D1b1Qs.title: Lactated Ringer's solution
D1b1Qs.description: An isotonic crystalloid fluid used for fluid resuscitation and maintenance fluid therapy. Increases extracellular volume with minimal increase in intracellular volume. Also has mild buffer action (due to lactate metabolism into bicarbonate) that counters acidosis. Risks of administration include lactic acidosis in patients with liver failure and lumping of red cells if given with blood products (due to citrate in blood products binding to calcium)

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

w1bhQs.title: 5% dextrose
w1bhQs.description: A crystalloid solution that contains 5 g/dL (278 mmol/L) of dextrose (a glucose isomer). Despite having an isoosmolar composition, D5W acts as a hypotonic solution in the body due to the rapid intracellular uptake of glucose. Administration of 100 mL of 5% dextrose increases extracellular fluid volume by 40 mL and intracellular fluid volume by 60 mL.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

91bNQs.title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement
91bNQs.description: A minimally-invasive, percutaneous procedure in which the aortic valve is replaced through an endovascular technique that wedges a replacement valve into the old valve.

C1bqQs.title: Vagal maneuvers
C1bqQs.description: A set of actions performed to decrease the heart rate through physical stimulation of the vagus nerve. Common maneuvers are the Valsalva maneuver and carotid massage. The stimulated vagus nerve then acts on the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes, which slows the heart rate and reduces conduction velocity.

x1bEQs.title: Procainamide
x1bEQs.description: A class IA antiarrhythmic drug that blocks fast sodium channels.

B1bzQs.title: Transrectal ultrasound
B1bzQs.description: An imaging test performed by inserting an ultrasound probe into the rectum to visualize the rectum and prostate. Commonly used to assess for prostatic hyperplasia, prostate cancer, and rectal cancer.

y1bdjs.title: Cardiac myxyoma
y1bdjs.description: A heterogeneous mass attached to the interatrial septum that is a common primary tumor of the heart in adults.

A1bRjs.title: Esophageal stenosis
A1bRjs.description: Narrowing or restriction of the lumen of the esophagus that leads to swallowing difficulties.

_1b5js.title: Nasal decongestants
_1b5js.description: A group of agents including α1-sympathomimetics that decrease production of nasal secretions by causing vasoconstriction of nasal blood vessels. Can be administered intranasally (e.g., phenylephrine, oxymetazoline, xylometazoline) or orally (e.g., phenylephrine and pseudoephedrine) to provide acute symptomatic relief.

z1brjs.title: Octreotide
z1brjs.description: A somatostatin analogue that inhibits growth hormone secretion and causes splanchnic vasoconstriction (via decreased secretion of vasodilatory peptides such as glucagon). Used to treat acromegaly, some neuroendocrine tumors, secretory diarrhea, and acute variceal bleeding. Radiolabelled octreotide can be used to localize neuroendocrine tumors with somatostatin receptors.

-1bDjs.title: Eculizumab
-1bDjs.description: A recombinant monoclonal antibody that inhibits the immune system by binding to and deactivating complement C5 (the terminal part of the complement cascade). Used to treat paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome. Increases the risk of infection with encapsulated bacteria (e.g., Neisseria spp.).

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

aWbQPs.title: Endoscopic variceal ligation
aWbQPs.description: An endoscopic procedure in which esophageal and/or gastric varices are ligated using rubber bands. Ligation causes occlusion and thrombosis of the bleeding vessel, which then sloughs off, leaving behind a superficial mucosal ulcer that heals rapidly. EVL is used to control acute variceal hemorrhage as well as for secondary prophylaxis of variceal hemorrhage.

YWbnPs.title: Endoscopic sclerotherapy
YWbnPs.description: An endoscopic procedure in which varices are injected with a sclerosing agent (e.g., ethanolamine oleate, sodium morrhuate, sodium tetradecyl sulfate). The sclerosing agent causes thrombosis and necrosis of varices. Used to control acute variceal hemorrhage.

destinations.label: Esophageal varices → Management of esophageal variceal hemorrhage

bWbHPs.title: Nifedipine
bWbHPs.description: A short-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker with a half-life of < 2 hours commonly used in the management of hypertension and supraventricular arrhythmias. Unlike other calcium channel blockers, this agent is not typically used in the management of angina. Adverse effects include headaches, peripheral edema, and reflex tachycardia (especially compared to other dihydropyridine agents).

XWb9Ps.title: Epoprostenol
XWb9Ps.description: A synthetic prostacyclin (PGI2) that has vasodilatory effects and inhibits platelet aggregation. Used as an intravenous infusion in the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension.

cWba4s.title: Hydralazine
cWba4s.description: A direct peripheral vasodilator that mainly affects arterial smooth muscle.

1Wb24s.title: Bone scan
1Wb24s.description: A radionuclide scan that uses technetium-99m to evaluate bone disorders. Used to evaluate metastatic fractures, traumatic fractures, neoplasms of the bone, and other disorders causing inflammation of the bone.

dWbo4s.title: Arteriography
dWbo4s.description: The imaging of blood vessels, which can be performed with or without a contrast medium. When a contrast medium is used, it is introduced either intravenously (e.g., CT angiography with iodine contrasts, MR angiography with gadolinium), or into a specific region (e.g., coronary vessels, cerebral vessels) using a catheter. Can only detect blood loss with rates > 0.5–1.0 mL/min.

VWbG4s.title: Clavicular plate
VWbG4s.description: A metal plate that is used for open reduction and internal fixation of a clavicular fracture.

eWbx4s.title: Shoulder spica cast
eWbx4s.description: A cast that immobilizes the shoulder in abduction as well as slight external rotation, and the elbow in a semiflexed position. While it is no longer commonly used, a few surviving indications include immobilization after shoulder arthrodesis and postoperative immobilization following internal fixation of a proximal humerus fracture.

UWbbks.title: Arm sling
UWbbks.description: A bandage or orthotic device used to treat proximal upper extremity injuries. The affected arm is positioned with the elbow flexed and the shoulder adducted and internally rotated, while a single bandage supports its weight on the contralateral shoulder by wrapping around the affected wrist, forearm, and elbow joint.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

media.title: Broad arm sling using triangular bandage

fWbkks.title: Ladd procedure
fWbkks.description: Surgical treatment for intestinal malrotation and midgut volvulus. Involves bowel detorsion (if volvulus is present), Ladd band division, mesenteric widening, appendectomy, and cecum and colon repositioning.

destinations.label: Intestinal malrotation, midgut volvulus, and gastric volvulus → Midgut volvulus

TWb6ks.title: Metronidazole
TWb6ks.description: A nitroimidazole antibiotic that is effective against a number of protozoa (e.g., Giardia, E. histolytica, Trichomonas) and anaerobic bacteria.

gWbFks.title: Sigmoidoscopy
gWbFks.description: An endoscopic evaluation of the lower gastrointestinal tract from the anus to the sigmoid colon. Can be performed using a flexible or rigid endoscope. Indications include screening for colorectal cancer, evaluation of suspected rectal or sigmoid colon pathology, and follow-up examination of a previously diagnosed lesion in the rectum or sigmoid colon.

SWbyks.title: Erysipeloid
SWbyks.description: A cutaneous infection caused by Erysipelothrix rhusiopathie, a gram-positive, capsulated bacilli that is found in a variety of animals including fish, shellfish, pigs, and birds. Infection is usually acquired occupationally by contact with infected meat.

destinations.label: Skin and soft tissue infections → Differential diagnoses

hWbcOs.title: Compression stockings
hWbcOs.description: A type of elastic hosiery that exert graduated pressure along the length of the stocking (i.e., higher pressure at the lower end of the limb), aiding anti-gravity venous return and minimizing venous distention and pain.

3WbSOs.title: Vasa previa
3WbSOs.description: The presence of fetal vessels directly over the internal cervical os and below the presenting part of the fetus. These vessels are typically unprotected by placental tissue or the umbilical cord and may bleed following rupture of membranes, resulting in fetal exsanguination. Risk factors for vasa previa include placental anomalies (e.g., bilobate or succenturiate placenta and velamentous insertion of the umbilical cord), placenta previa, multiparity, and in-vitro fertilization.

RWblOs.title: Chylous ascites
RWblOs.description: A rare form of ascites characterized by accumulation of milky lymphatic fluid within the peritoneal cavity as a result of leakage or exudation of lymph from intraabdominal lymphatic vessels. Diagnosed by a triglyceride concentration > 200 mg/dL in ascitic fluid. The two most common causes in developed countries are intraabdominal malignancy and cirrhosis.

iWbJOs.title: Cardiac myxoma
iWbJOs.description: The most common type of primary neoplasm of the heart. A noncancerous tumor composed of connective tissue, most commonly located in the left atrium, originating from the interatrial septum. May cause obstruction of cardiac blood flow.

QWbuOs.title: Gastrin
QWbuOs.description: A peptide hormone that stimulates gastric acid secretion and increases stomach motility. It is secreted by G cells in the  antrum of the stomach and the duodenum.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

jWb_Os.title: Fomepizole
jWb_Os.description: A competitive inhibitor of alcohol dehydrogenase used in the treatment of methanol or ethylene glycol poisoning to prevent the formation of toxic metabolites and the development of severe metabolic acidosis.

PWbWls.title: Nafcillin
PWbWls.description: An antistaphylococcal penicillin that is effective against methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus but not methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).

4Wb3ls.title: Pulmonary valve regurgitation
4Wb3ls.description: Valvular heart disease characterized by retrograde blood flow from the pulmonary artery into the right ventricle during diastole due to insufficient closure of the valve.

media.title: Heart murmur in aortic and pulmonary insufficiency

kWbmls.title: Tricuspid valve stenosis
kWbmls.description: A valvular disease characterized by obstruction of blood flow from the right atrium into the right ventricle during diastole due to impaired opening of the valve. Extremely rare and is most commonly caused by infective endocarditis (especially in IV drug users), carcinoid tumors, or rheumatic fever.

OWbIls.title: Tricuspid valve regurgitation
OWbIls.description: A valvular disease characterized by retrograde blood flow from the right ventricle into the right atrium during systole due to insufficient closure of the valve. Extremely rare and can be caused by infective endocarditis (especially IV drug users), rheumatic fever, or right ventricular heart failure.

lWbvls.title: Acid-fast bacteria
lWbvls.description: A group of bacteria with cell wall properties that prevent decolorization by acids after previous staining. Includes all mycobacteria and actinomycetes (e.g., Nocardia).

NWb-ls.title: Autoimmune adrenalitis
NWb-ls.description: An autoimmune-mediated destruction of the adrenal glands, which causes primary adrenocortical insufficiency.

5WbiNs.title: Adrenal infarction
5WbiNs.description: The acute loss of perfusion of the adrenal parenchyma, resulting in necrosis and loss of function.

nWb7Ns.title: Colonoscopy
nWb7Ns.description: A procedure in which a flexible fiberoptic endoscope is passed through the anus to visualize the mucosa of the rectum, colon, and, sometimes, the terminal ileum. Commonly used to diagnose and/or manage lower gastrointestinal disorders.

LWbwNs.title: Transurethral catheterization
LWbwNs.description: A procedure in which a catheter is inserted through the urethra into the bladder.

KWbUms.title: Secondary hemorrhage
KWbUms.description: A complication of bleeding within 24 hours of surgery that is caused by either a slipped ligature, a lysed or dislodged thrombus, and cessation of reflex vasospasm. Bleeding that occurs 7–14 days after surgery is due to a surgical site infection, which causes sloughing and erosion of blood vessels.

6Wbjms.title: Hemophilia A
6Wbjms.description: An X-linked recessive disease that results in the deficiency of factor VIII. Most often presents in boys with recurrent episodes of epistaxis, bruising, and/or hemarthrosis. Lab studies show normal platelet counts, BT, PT, but prolonged aPTT.

pWbLms.title: Hemophilia B
pWbLms.description: An X-linked recessive disease that results in the deficiency of factor IX. Manifests in boys with signs of bleeding, such as recurring epistaxis, bruising, and/or hemarthrosis. Lab values show normal platelet counts, BT, and PT, but prolonged aPTT.

JWbsms.title: Goiter
JWbsms.description: A general term for any abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland. Can be classified based on their morphology and function, as well as whether they are benign or malignant. Depending on the etiology, patients may be asymptomatic or present with hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism.

qWbCms.title: Factor VIII
qWbCms.description: A cofactor of factor IXa (activated factor IX). Factor VIII circulates in blood bound to von Willebrand factor (vWF).

IWbY5s.title: Factor IX
IWbY5s.description: A circulating serine protease that functions in the intrinsic coagulation pathway as an activator of factor X. The synthesis of factor IX takes place in the liver and involves vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation. Factor IX is activated by factor XIa (activated factor XI), calcium, and membrane phospholipids. Antithrombin III inactivates factor IX. Isolated factor IX deficiency is seen in patients with hemophilia B.

rWbf5s.title: Peripheral insulin resistance
rWbf5s.description: The inability of cells to respond adequately to insulin, which causes inhibited glucose uptake from the bloodstream and impaired anabolic metabolism.

7Wb45s.title: Insulin-like growth factor 1
7Wb45s.description: An anabolic polypeptide hormone produced primarily by the liver in response to growth hormone. Stimulates cell growth and proliferation.

HWbK5s.title: Guyon's canal syndrome
HWbK5s.description: Entrapment of the ulnar nerve within Guyon canal at the wrist. Causes include repeated pressure on the wrists (e.g., cyclists), trauma, ganglion cysts, fibrous bands, anomalous muscle insertions, and ulnar artery aneurysms. Symptoms include intrinsic hand muscle weakness and paresthesias or sensory loss of the ring and little finger.

destinations.label: Ulnar nerve entrapment → Overview of ulnar nerve entrapment

sWbt5s.title: Wartenberg sign
sWbt5s.description: A persistent abduction of the fifth finger due to weakness of the third palmar interosseous muscle. Can be caused by ulnar nerve lesions.

tWbXMs.title: Fluoroscopy
tWbXMs.description: An imaging technique that uses continuous x-rays to take a series of images that are particularly useful for the evaluation of moving structures (e.g., for swallow studies, catheter manipulation, lumbar puncture, angiograms).

FWbgMs.title: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery
FWbgMs.description: A minimally invasive procedure that can be used in the diagnosis and treatment of certain intrathoracic conditions.

8WbOMs.title: Diaphragmatic eventration
8WbOMs.description: A congenital or acquired disorder in which the diaphragmatic muscle is partly or completely replaced by fibroelastic tissue.

uWbpMs.title: Fasciotomy
uWbpMs.description: A procedure in which the skin, subcutaneous fat, and deep fascia are incised in order to decrease the intracompartmental pressure in a limb and restore blood flow.

EWb8Ms.title: Open reduction and internal fixation
EWb8Ms.description: A surgical procedure to repair bone fractures and/or dislocations through operative (open) repositioning (reduction), followed by fixation with rods, nails, plates, and/or screws.

destinations.label: Trauma and orthopedic surgery → Internal fixation

media.title: Internal fixation of a vertebral fracture

vWbAMs.title: Excisional biopsy
vWbAMs.description: A procedure in which an entire lesion or mass is surgically excised to obtain a tissue sample for analysis by a pathologist. In dermatology, an excisional biopsy obtains a sample that includes all layers of the skin (i.e., healthy and abnormal tissue) and is preferred over an incisional biopsy for lesions suspicious for melanoma. Methods include fusiform (elliptical) biopsy, deep shave biopsy, and, if the lesion is small enough for complete removal, punch biopsy.

DWb1ns.title: Balanced electrolyte solution
DWb1ns.description: A crystalloid solution with a concentration of electrolytes that closely resembles the concentration of electrolytes in plasma (e.g., lactated Ringer's solution, Hartmann solution).

wWbhns.title: 0.9% NaCl
wWbhns.description: An isotonic crystalloid fluid containing sodium and chloride, each with a concentration of 154 mEq/L (154 mmol/L). Administration of 100 mL of NS increases extracellular fluid volume by approximately 100 mL with little to no change in intracellular fluid volume.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

9WbNns.title: Ambulatory ECG monitoring
9WbNns.description: Procedure in which the patient's cardiac electrical activity is documented, generally over a 24-hour period; some devices allow monitoring for months or even years. Monitoring can be continuous (e.g., Holter monitor) or intermittent (e.g., event recorder, loop recorder). Allows better detection of cardiac arrhythmias or conduction abnormalities compared to a standard ECG.

CWbqns.title: Analgesia
CWbqns.description: The absence or relief of pain, often provided by medication. Analgesic medications are a heterogeneous group commonly divided into the nonopioid and opioid analgesics.

xWbEns.title: Liver biopsy
xWbEns.description: The removal of a small liver sample for study under a microscope, usually performed through the insertion of a needle through the skin and abdominal wall.

BWbzns.title: Obeticholic acid
BWbzns.description: An agonist of the farnesoid X receptor, a nuclear receptor that inhibits synthesis of cholesterol by promoting the transport of bile acids out of the hepatocytes. Used as a second-line treatment for primary biliary cholangitis.

yWbdLs.title: Low anterior resection
yWbdLs.description: A surgical procedure that includes the sphincter-preserving resection of the upper part of the rectum and the sigmoid colon. Indicated in the treatment of rectal adenocarcinoma in combination with total mesorectal excision, usually following neoadjuvant chemoradiation.

destinations.label: Colorectal cancer → Treatment of rectal cancer

AWbRLs.title: Total mesorectal excision
AWbRLs.description: A surgical procedure that involves the en bloc excision of the fold of the peritoneum covering the upper rectum (mesorectum), regional lymph nodes, and vasculature. Indicated in the treatment of rectal adenocarcinoma in combination with low anterior resection, usually following neoadjuvant chemoradiation.

destinations.label: Colorectal cancer → Treatment of rectal cancer

_Wb5Ls.title: Stricturoplasty
_Wb5Ls.description: A surgical procedure that opens up a bowel stricture without having to resect the bowel.

zWbrLs.title: Calcium carbonate
zWbrLs.description: A compound used as an oral antacid to neutralize acidic gastric contents. Has a fast onset of action (5 minutes) but the effect does not last longer than 30–60 minutes. Also used as an oral calcium supplement.

ZdbZos.title: Mechanical ventilation
ZdbZos.description: A form of artificial ventilation by various mechanical means. Positive pressure ventilation involves forcing air into the airways at a higher pressure. Negative pressure ventilation involves creating negative airway pressure that effectively sucks air into the lungs.

0dbeos.title: Bone age
0dbeos.description: The maturity of a child's bone development, expressed in years. Most commonly assessed using an x-ray of the nondominant hand and wrist. Used to determine a child's physiological maturity and growth potential, and to predict adult height. A difference between bone age and chronological age of more than 2 standard deviations suggests pathology. Current methods of bone age determination are mostly based on primarily White populations and may not be accurate in patients of other races.

adbQos.title: Esophageal manometry
adbQos.description: A diagnostic test that is used to evaluate the peristaltic function of the esophagus during swallowing. The propagation, speed, and vigor of the peristaltic wave is measured via an esophageal catheter fitted with pressure sensors every 3–6 cm. May be used to investigate dysphagia suspected to be due to esophageal motility disorders if high-resolution esophageal manometry (gold standard test) is unavailable.

Ydbnos.title: Antibiotic prophylaxis
Ydbnos.description: Treatment with antibiotics to prevent infection (e.g., perioperatively, for animal bite wounds, in patients at high risk of endocarditis undergoing invasive procedures)

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Additional considerations

bdbHos.title: Lung adenocarcinoma
bdbHos.description: A non-small cell lung cancer. The most common type of lung cancer in nonsmokers.

Xdb9os.title: Squamous cell lung carcinoma
Xdb9os.description: A non-small cell lung cancer. More common in men. The most common lung cancer among smokers.

cdbaKs.title: Conservative management
cdbaKs.description: A therapeutic strategy that seeks to avoid invasive and/or risky interventions. Examples include nonoperative management of classically surgical conditions and medical therapy focused on preventive measures, supportive care, symptom control, and watchful waiting.

1db2Ks.title: Dynamic renal scintigraphy
1db2Ks.description: A diagnostic test in which a radiotracer that is excreted by the kidney (e.g., Tc-99m MAG3 or Tc-99m DPTA) is used to assess renal perfusion as well as urine flow in the urinary tract. In children and patients with renal insufficiency, Tc-99m MAG3 (mercaptoacetyltriglycine), which is excreted primarily by tubular secretion, is preferred as a radiotracer over Tc-99m DPTA (diethylenetriamine pentaacetic acid), which is excreted primarily by glomerular filtration.

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Imaging techniques

WdbPKs.title: Dactylitis
WdbPKs.description: An inflammation of the fingers and/or toes seen in a variety of conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, sarcoidosis, and sickle-cell disease.

ddboKs.title: Tetanus immunoglobulin
ddboKs.description: A preparation of immunoglobulins against the tetanus toxin that is made from the pooled serum of screened donors. Used for postexposure prophylaxis against tetanus as well as its treatment. TIG provides passive immunity by neutralizing any unbound tetanus toxin, but it is not effective against tetanus toxin molecules that are already bound to nerve endings.

VdbGKs.title: Tetanus diphtheria acellular pertussis vaccine
VdbGKs.description: An inactivated vaccine that contains the tetanus toxoid, reduced diphtheric toxoid, and acellular pertussis. Used in individuals ≥ 7 years of age for routine Tdap boosters, postexposure tetanus prophylaxis, and catch-up immunization for those with incomplete DTaP vaccination.

edbxKs.title: Hemorrhoidectomy
edbxKs.description: The surgical removal of hemorrhoids. Classified either as an open procedure (e.g., Parks-Ferguson hemorrhoidectomy), or closed procedure (e.g., Milligan-Morgan hemorrhoidectomy) depending on whether the anal mucosa is sutured after the procedure or left open to heal by secondary intention.

2dbT6s.title: Rectal varices
2dbT6s.description: The dilation of the rectal venous plexus (hemorrhoidal plexus) in patients with portal hypertension. The rectal venous plexus consists of submucous collateral veins between the superior rectal vein, which drain into the portal venous system via the superior mesenteric vein, and the middle and inferior rectal veins, which drain into systemic venous circulation.

fdbk6s.title: Stool softener
fdbk6s.description: An orally or rectally administered surfactant that allows stools to absorb fat and water, making stools softer and easier to pass through the gastrointestinal tract. Used to treat or prevent constipation. Examples include docusate, glycerine, and mineral oil.

Tdb66s.title: Floating shoulder injury
Tdb66s.description: A combination of a clavicular fracture and a scapular neck fracture.

gdbF6s.title: Afferent pupillary defect
gdbF6s.description: A condition in which the eye cannot react to light but the accommodation reflex remains intact. Direct pupillary reflex is absent in the affected eye. Consensual pupillary reflex is absent in the normal eye. Most common etiology is severe damage to the retina or optic nerve.

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Afferent pupillary defect

Sdby6s.title: Direct pupillary light reflex
Sdby6s.description: The physiological constriction of a pupil in response to ipsilateral light stimulation. E.g., constriction of the left pupil in response to illumination of the left eye.

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Pupillary response

hdbcps.title: Indirect pupillary reflex
hdbcps.description: Physiological constriction of the pupil in response to illumination of the contralateral eye. E.g., constriction of the left pupil in response to illumination of the right eye (left consensual light reflex).

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Pupillary response

3dbSps.title: Intestinal adhesion
3dbSps.description: A collection of fibrous, intraperitoneal strands of connective tissue between organs and tissues that are not physiologically connected. Arise as a result of inflammation of the peritoneal lining (e.g., after abdominal surgery).

Rdblps.title: Pathological lead point
Rdblps.description: An intestinal lesion or abnormality of the intestinal wall that enables the proximal bowel to be pulled by peristalsis into the distal bowel, causing intussusception.

idbJps.title: Intestinal malrotation
idbJps.description: A congenital abnormality characterized by abnormal or incomplete coiling and/or fixation of the gastrointestinal tract during embryologic development. The most common types of malrotation are nonrotation and incomplete rotation.

destinations.label: Intestinal malrotation, midgut volvulus, and gastric volvulus → Intestinal malrotation

Qdbups.title: Ileocolectomy
Qdbups.description: The surgical removal of a diseased section of the ileum and the ascending colon with anastomosis between the remaining parts of the small bowel and the colon.

4db3Js.title: Optic neuritis
4db3Js.description: An inflammatory demyelination of the optic nerve. The most common identifiable cause is multiple sclerosis. Clinical presentation depends on whether inflammation involves the optic disc (papillitis) or the part of the optic nerve behind the eyeball (retrobulbar neuritis).

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Optic neuritis

kdbmJs.title: Central retinal vein occlusion
kdbmJs.description: An occlusion of the central retinal vein, usually by a thrombus. Can be either nonischemic or ischemic. Nonischemic CRVO manifests with mild to moderate loss of vision. Ischemic CRVO manifests with severe loss of vision, an afferent pupillary defect, and extensive retinal hemorrhage on ophthalmoscopy.

destinations.label: Retinal vessel occlusion → Retinal vein occlusion

OdbIJs.title: Central retinal artery occlusion
OdbIJs.description: An occlusion of the central retinal artery, usually by a thromboembolic phenomenon. Manifestations include sudden, painless loss of vision with a fundoscopic examination that shows a pale, edematous retina and a cherry-red spot near the fovea.

destinations.label: Retinal vessel occlusion → Retinal artery occlusion

ldbvJs.title: Acute dystonia
ldbvJs.description: An acute adverse reaction following the intake of antipsychotics caused by antagonism at D2 receptors. Characterized by sustained, painful muscle spasms, especially of the head, neck, and tongue (e.g., torticollis, facial grimacing, fixed or deviated stare).

Ndb-Js.title: Postoperative pneumonia
Ndb-Js.description: A form of hospital-acquired pneumonia that typically occurs 3 to 5 days following an operation. Increased risk following upper abdominal, thoracic, or long operations and in patients with older age, lowered functional status, long recovery times, or smoking history.

mdbVqs.title: Enteroscopy
mdbVqs.description: An endoscopic procedure by which the small bowel can be visualized and biopsies can be taken.

5dbiqs.title: Cystoscopy
5dbiqs.description: An endoscopic procedure in which a thin tube with a light and a camera is inserted through the urethra into the bladder, allowing for visualization of the urethra, bladder, and ureteral orifices. Certain diagnostic and/or therapeutic procedures such as the removal of bladder stones, collection of biopsy samples, resection of certain bladder tumors, and administration of intravesical medications (e.g., chemotherapy) can be performed during cystoscopy.

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Cystoscopy

Ldbwqs.title: Surgical repair of the mitral valve
Ldbwqs.description: A surgical procedure to correct severe mitral stenosis, mitral valve prolapse, or mitral regurgitation. It involves either ring annuloplasty (narrowing the valve by suturing a ring of metal or tissue circumferentially) or valve repair (rebuilding or shaping the valve leaflets).

KdbUIs.title: Spermatocele testis
KdbUIs.description: An abnormal cystic collection of sperm within the epididymal duct. Usually located on the upper testicular pole and is palpable as a mass distinct from the testis. Rarely causes symptoms but can be surgically removed if it causes pain.

6dbjIs.title: Orchitis
6dbjIs.description: Inflammation of one or both testes. Most commonly due to bacteria (especially sexually transmitted bacteria, e.g. gonorrhea or chlamydia) or a viral mumps infection. Bacterial orchitis often results from epididymitis, associated with an infection of the urinary tract, and is then called “epididymo-orchitis.”

pdbLIs.title: Pressure ulcer
pdbLIs.description: A condition of localized tissue damage due to pressure that obstructs blood flow to the skin and subcutaneous tissue. Most commonly develops over bony prominences, such as the sacrum, heel, hip, and back of the head.

media.title: Typical locations of pressure ulcers (decubitus ulcers)

JdbsIs.title: Buckle fracture
JdbsIs.description: A type of incomplete bone fracture characterized by a bulge in the cortex without a break in its continuity. Torus fractures are the result of bone impaction.

media.title: Metaphyseal torus fractures of the radius and ulna (2/2)
Metaphyseal torus fractures of the radius and ulna
Buckle fracture of the distal radius

qdbCIs.title: CT enterography
qdbCIs.description: A radiographic imaging technique for the evaluation of the small bowel. Following the ingestion of contrast, CT imaging of the abdomen with IV contrast is performed.
