Provides a high resolution and facilitates the evaluation of the small bowel wall, the surrounding mesentery, and the perienteric fat. Commonly used in the evaluation of Crohn disease and other small bowel disorders.

IdbYrs.title: Sporotrichosis
IdbYrs.description: A condition caused by Sporothrix schenckii spores that enter the skin via trauma. Manifestations include localized skin lesions (e.g., pustules, ulcers, nodules) and ascending lymphangitis. Can become disseminated in patients who are immunocompromised.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Other fungal infections

rdbfrs.title: Bone marrow biopsy
rdbfrs.description: A procedure in which a sample of bone marrow is collected either by aspiration or trephination and analyzed. Performed to diagnosis hematologic malignancies, myelodysplastic syndromes, or unexplained anemias.

7db4rs.title: Platelet dysfunction
7db4rs.description: A group of disorders of platelet adhesion or platelet aggregation.

HdbKrs.title: Sclerotherapy
HdbKrs.description: The injection of irritant chemicals (e.g., ethanol, sodium tetradecyl sulfate) into a vascular space or body cavity to cause inflammation, fibrosis, and obliteration of the said space. Used to treat varicose veins, hemorrhoids, esophageal varices, hydatid cysts, malignant pleural effusion, and intracranial aneurysms.

tdbX7s.title: Penetrating trauma
tdbX7s.description: An injury caused by a foreign object piercing the skin, which damages the underlying tissues and results in an open wound. The most common causes of such trauma are gunshots and stab wounds.

media.title: Tension pneumothorax with mediastinal and subcutaneous emphysema

Fdbg7s.title: Massive hemothorax
Fdbg7s.description: The presence of more than a third of the blood volume (i.e., > 1,500 mL in adults) within the pleural cavity or continuous bleeding ≥ 200 mL/hour for at least 4 hours. Usually the result of traumatic rupture of intrathoracic blood vessels. Clinical features include hypotension, decreased breath sounds and a dull percussion note over the lung fields.

8dbO7s.title: Diphtheria, tetanus, acellular pertussis vaccine
8dbO7s.description: An inactivated vaccine that contains the tetanus toxoid, diphtheria toxoid, and acellular pertussis. DTaP is used for active immunization as part of the primary immunization schedule and for postexposure tetanus prophylaxis in children between the ages of 6 weeks and 7 years.

udbp7s.title: Obscure gastrointestinal bleeding
udbp7s.description: A condition of gastrointestinal bleeding that persists or recurs after an initial negative evaluation to find the source of bleeding.

Edb87s.title: Aortorenal bypass surgery
Edb87s.description: A revascularization surgery in which an anastomosis is created between the aorta and the renal artery, using a vein graft or a vascular prosthesis in order to circumvent a stenotic lesion in the renal artery.

vdbA7s.title: Percutaneous transluminal angioplasty
vdbA7s.description: A revascularization procedure in which a catheter with a balloon at its tip is passed along a guide wire to the site of arterial stenosis. The balloon is then inflated to relieve the obstruction. In patients with CAD or PAD, angioplasty is the preferred revascularization procedure for focal arterial occlusion or if patients are not surgically fit to undergo a bypass procedure.

Ddb1Hs.title: Papillary carcinoma of the breast
Ddb1Hs.description: A rare type of invasive ductal carcinoma with a peak incidence between the ages of 60 and 70. More common among non-white women. The tumor has a very low frequency of lymph node metastasis. Nearly 90% of the tumors express estrogen receptors.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Types of breast cancer

wdbhHs.title: Viscus
wdbhHs.description: An internal organ, specifically an organ located within the abdomen or chest.

9dbNHs.title: Gastrografin swallow
9dbNHs.description: A diagnostic procedure in which gastrografin, a nontoxic, water-soluble contrast agent, is ingested and visualized on fluoroscopy to evaluate the integrity of the esophagus.

CdbqHs.title: Pellagra
CdbqHs.description: A deficiency of niacin (vitamin B3). Characterized by the presence of glossitis and "the three Ds": diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia, and possibly death (the four Ds). Typically caused by decreased intake of niacin or tryptophan but can also result from carcinoid syndrome and Hartnup disease.

xdbEHs.title: Alveolar-arterial gradient
xdbEHs.description: The difference between the partial pressure of oxygen in the alveoli (A) and the partial pressure of oxygen in the arteries (a). The normal range varies with age, altitude, and the concentration of inhaled oxygen. Normal range for a young person breathing room air at sea level is 5–10 mm Hg and increases with physical exercise. In diseased states, A-a gradient increases with a ventilation-perfusion mismatch and/or impaired gas diffusion across the alveoli but remains normal or low with alveolar hypoventilation.

BdbzHs.title: Alveolar partial pressure of oxygen
BdbzHs.description: The partial pressure of oxygen in the alveoli. If there is no airway obstruction, the partial pressure of oxygen in the alveoli is calculated using the alveolar gas equation: PAO₂ ≈ [FiO₂ × (Atmospheric pressure - 47)] - [0.8 × (PaCO₂)], where FiO₂ is the concentration of inhaled oxygen, PaCO₂ is the partial pressure of carbon dioxide in the artery, and atmospheric pressure is 760 mm Hg at sea level.

ydbdss.title: Ischemic stroke
ydbdss.description: Acute neurological dysfunction caused by brain, spinal cord, or retinal infarction. Involves neuronal cell death in the territory perfused by an artery that is stenosed or occluded by emboli, thrombi, or microangiopathic changes

media.title: Acute ischemic stroke with hyperdense middle cerebral artery sign
Evaluation and management of ischemic stroke

AdbRss.title: Zenker's diverticulum
AdbRss.description: Outpouching of the lower pharyngeal mucosa and submucosa caused by inadequate relaxation of the upper esophageal sphincter and increased intraluminal pressure.

zdbrss.title: Minute ventilation
zdbrss.description: The volume of air that a person breathes per minute (i.e., the product of tidal volume and respiratory rate).

-dbDss.title: Blood urea nitrogen test
-dbDss.description: A blood test that measures the amount of urea nitrogen, a waste product produced by the liver in the urea cycle after protein degradation. Urea nitrogen is physiologically filtered and excreted by the kidneys.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Renal function test

ZVbZGs.title: Fenoldopam
ZVbZGs.description: An antihypertensive drug that functions via partial agonism of the dopamine (D1) receptor in the renal vasculature, thereby leading to arterial vasodilation in the kidney.

0VbeGs.title: Isoproterenol
0VbeGs.description: A nonselective beta-adrenergic agonist used to treat bradycardia and heart block by increasing heart rate and contractility. Leads to dilation of the peripheral vasculature and is contraindicated in patients with angina, tachyarrhythmias, and ventricular arrhythmias.

aVbQGs.title: Midodrine
aVbQGs.description: A selective alpha-1 adrenergic agonist used in the management of postural hypotension and refractory ascites.

YVbnGs.title: Phenylephrine
YVbnGs.description: An α-adrenergic agonist (predominantly α1, α2 to a lesser degree) that is used primarily as a decongestant (e.g., for allergic rhinitis), mydriatic, and vasoconstrictor (e.g., topical hemorrhoid treatment). Also indicated as a vasopressor for second-line treatment of hypotension secondary to shock.

bVbHGs.title: Ephedrine
bVbHGs.description: An indirect sympathomimetic drug that causes α- and β-mediated adrenergic stimulation by promoting the release of norepinephrine. Used to treat anesthesia-induced hypotension.

XVb9Gs.title: Second-degree burn
XVb9Gs.description: A burn that involves both the epidermis and dermis and causes blisters (e.g., vesicles, bullae). Further subdivided into superficial and deep partial-thickness burns.

media.title: Second-degree scalding injury (2b; deep partial-thickness burn) after initial debridement

cVbats.title: Escharotomy
cVbats.description: Surgical procedure indicated for circumferential third-degree burns involving the limbs or the thorax with signs of impending vascular or respiratory compromise, respectively. Escharotomy is characterized by an incision of the burnt necrotic tissue to prevent constriction of the skin which may otherwise result in compartment syndrome and impaired movement of the thorax.

1Vb2ts.title: Third-degree burn
1Vb2ts.description: A burn that involves the skin and the subcutaneous tissue and results in tissue necrosis. Full-thickness burns are usually painless as a result of cutaneous nerve destruction and do not blanch on applying pressure.

WVbPts.title: Lactate dehydrogenase
WVbPts.description: An intracytoplasmic enzyme that catalyzes the reversible conversion of lactate to pyruvate. Five isoenzymes exist that are found in higher concentrations in specific organs: LDH 1 and 2 (heart, kidneys, erythrocytes), LDH 3 (lungs), LDH 4 and 5 (liver and skeletal muscle). LDH levels are elevated in patients with an injury to any of the aforementioned organs and in conditions with an increased cell turnover (e.g., cancer).

dVbots.title: Creatine kinase
dVbots.description: An intracytoplasmatic enzyme found predominantly in skeletal muscle and heart muscle, as well as the brain. Its serum concentration is a useful surrogate marker for myocardial or muscle injury.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Overview

eVbxts.title: Bone biopsy
eVbxts.description: Small sample of bone is extracted for histopathological analysis and/or gram-staining and culture. Commonly used in bone infections and malignancies.

2VbTFs.title: Mycoplasma genitalium
2VbTFs.description: A type of bacteria that can cause infections of the genitourinary tract. Because it lacks a cell wall, it is undetectable on a regular Gram stain.

fVbkFs.title: Shenton's line
fVbkFs.description: A continuous curved line drawn from the medial border of the femoral neck to the lower border of the superior pubic ramus in an AP view X-ray of the pelvis. An interruption of this line should raise suspicion for femoral neck fracture or hip dislocation.

TVb6Fs.title: Hilgenreiner line
TVb6Fs.description: A horizontal line that is drawn through the left and right triradiate cartilages in an AP view x-ray of the pelvis used to measure the acetabular angle. Use of this line with the other lines and angles (e.g., Perkin line) is used to diagnose developmental dysplasia of the hip.

gVbFFs.title: Perkin line
gVbFFs.description: A vertical line drawn perpendicular to Hilgenreiner line through the most lateral ossified point of the acetabulum in an AP view x-ray of the pelvis. Used to evaluate developmental dysplasia of the hip.

SVbyFs.title: Acetabular angle
SVbyFs.description: The angle between the Hilgenreiner line and a line drawn from the lateral triradiate cartilage to the most lateral ossified point of the acetabulum. Normal values in children: < 28° at birth, < 25° at 6 months, and < 22° at 1 year. In adults, the normal range is 33–38°. A high acetabular angle is a sign of acetabular dysplasia. A decreased acetabular angle can be seen in children with Down syndrome and achondroplasia.

3VbS8s.title: Center-edge angle
3VbS8s.description: The angle between a line drawn through the center of the femoral head and the lateral edge of the acetabulum and a vertical line through the center of the femoral head and the center of the acetabulum in an AP view x-ray of the pelvis. Normal range varies with age and is 25–39° in adults. A low angle is associated with acetabular dysplasia; a high angle is associated with acetabular protrusion.

lVbvus.title: Hurthle cell carcinoma
lVbvus.description: A well-differentiated malignant neoplasm of the thyroid gland that derives from Hürthle cells, a distinct type of thyroid cells. It is often classified as a subtype of follicular thyroid carcinoma.

NVb-us.title: Circumferential burn
NVb-us.description: Burns that encircle the chest, neck, abdomen, and/or an extremity. Burnt necrotic tissue is inelastic and circumferential burns can result in constriction when the limb or torso wall begins to swell up from necrosis. Subsequent compartment syndrome or impaired thoracic movement with respiratory dysfunction may result.

5VbiEs.title: Radiographic signs of a fracture
5VbiEs.description: The x-ray findings characteristic of a fracture. Includes disruption of the bony cortex and a radiolucent fracture line.

MVbMEs.title: Stress fracture
MVbMEs.description: A fracture of structurally normal bone due to the coalescence of microfractures from repetitive activity. The absence of a single inciting event and underlying bone disease differentiates stress fractures from acute fractures and pathologic fractures.

nVb7Es.title: Fascial dehiscence
nVb7Es.description: The separation of fascial closure after abdominal surgery. Can be partial or complete and may result in evisceration of intraabdominal contents, bowel obstruction, and/or strangulation. Causes include increased intraabdominal pressure, technical failure, local infection, and/or ischemia.

LVbwEs.title: Seromas
LVbwEs.description: A collection of serous fluid in a tissue, organ, or body cavity that typically accumulates several days after surgery.

pVbLvs.title: Organ evisceration
pVbLvs.description: A condition in which the viscera are present outside of the body, typically after penetrating abdominal trauma or complete dehiscence of an abdominal surgical incision.

JVbsvs.title: GI fistula
JVbsvs.description: An abnormal connection between the bowel and another epithelialized structure, such as the skin (enterocutaneous fistula), vagina (rectovaginal fistula), or the bladder (rectovesical fistula), through which fecal matter can discharge. Causes include bowel surgery, inflammatory bowel disease, malignancy, and certain infectious diseases (e.g., tuberculosis, chlamydia).

qVbCvs.title: Radioactive iodine ablation
qVbCvs.description: A nuclear medicine technique used to treat hyperthyroidism (e.g., due to Graves disease, toxic adenoma, multinodular goiter) and well-differentiated thyroid cancers. Uses iodine-131, a radioactive element that emits beta rays, to destroy thyroid tissue.

IVbYDs.title: External beam radiotherapy
IVbYDs.description: A treatment method where a machine delivers carefully targeted radiation beams from outside the body to destroy cancer cells, halt their growth, or offer palliative therapy of locally advanced unresectable or metastatic disease. Is the most commonly used form of radiation therapy.

rVbfDs.title: Thyroidectomy
rVbfDs.description: The surgical removal of all thyroid tissue including both lobes and isthmus.

sVbtDs.title: Phlegmasia alba dolens
sVbtDs.description: A rare condition in which a complete obstruction of venous drainage from the limb results in significant fluid sequestration, edema (due to increased capillary hydrostatic pressure), and white coloring ("alba"). The edema precipitates phlegmasia cerulea dolens and compartment syndrome, which in turn leads to arterial occlusion and impending critical limb ischemia.

GVbBDs.title: Transverse vaginal septum
GVbBDs.description: A transverse septum within the vagina that is formed due to failure of recanalization of the Mullerian duct. Patients are usually asymptomatic before puberty, but present at the time of puberty with primary amenorrhea and/or periodic lower abdominal pain.

destinations.label: Anomalies of the female genital tract → Anomalies of the vulva and vagina

tVbXws.title: Osteotomy
tVbXws.description: A surgical procedure in which a bone is cut in order to allow realignment, lengthening, or shortening of bones.

FVbgws.title: Hip spica
FVbgws.description: A type of cast that encloses the trunk and one or both lower legs. This cast immobilizes the pelvis, hip joint, and knee joint, and is used to facilitate healing of fractures or other injuries involving the hip joint and/or proximal femur.

8VbOws.title: Pavlik harness
8VbOws.description: A nonrigid orthotic device that may be used to treat infants less than 6 months of age with developmental dysplasia of the hip or femoral fractures. To achieve concentric reduction of the femoral head, the harness keeps the hips abducted by 50° and flexed by 90–100°.

destinations.label: Developmental dysplasia of the hip → Treatment

uVbpws.title: Von Rosen harness
uVbpws.description: A rigid harness that is used to treat infants with developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) below the age of 6 months. The harness keeps the hips abducted by 50° and flexed by 90–100° in order to achieve concentric reduction of the femoral head.

destinations.label: Developmental dysplasia of the hip → Treatment

EVb8ws.title: Closed reduction
EVb8ws.description: A nonsurgical, physical manipulation to realign a displaced fracture and/or dislocation into a proper anatomical position.

vVbAws.title: Open reduction
vVbAws.description: A procedure to repair a fracture and/or dislocation by surgically exposing and manipulating (i.e., reducing) the involved structure(s) back into their physiologic positions.

DVb19s.title: Ladd bands
DVb19s.description: A growth of abnormal fibrous tissue that classically attaches the cecum to peritoneum and liver, crossing the duodenum in its course. Associated with intestinal obstruction and malrotation.

destinations.label: Intestinal malrotation, midgut volvulus, and gastric volvulus → Intestinal malrotation

wVbh9s.title: Respiratory splinting
wVbh9s.description: A reduced inspiratory effort in conditions that are associated with pain during breathing (e.g., pleuritic chest pain, rib fractures). Pain causes reflex tightening of the chest wall muscles in an attempt to decrease excursion of the chest wall.

9VbN9s.title: Boxer's fracture
9VbN9s.description: A transverse fracture of the metacarpal neck, most commonly of the 4th or 5th metacarpal. Primarily occurs as a result of impaction injury (e.g., from punching). Typically angulated in the volar direction.

CVbq9s.title: Distal pancreatectomy
CVbq9s.description: A procedure in which the distal half of the pancreas is resected, most commonly to remove a tumor in the body or tail of the pancreas or to treat chronic pancreatitis.

destinations.label: Pancreatic and hepatic surgery → Pancreatic surgery

yVbdCs.title: Abscess
yVbdCs.description: An enclosed collection of pus within tissue. Usually caused by a bacterial infection.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Acute local inflammation

AVbRCs.title: Acute urinary retention
AVbRCs.description: A sudden, painful inability to void despite having a full bladder. Most commonly caused by benign prostatic hyperplasia. Can be caused by non-obstructive etiologies (e.g., after spinal anesthesia, pelvic surgery, spinal cord injury). Examination shows a palpable, tender, distended bladder. Urgent bladder catheterization (transurethral or suprapubic) should precede further diagnostics.

_Vb5Cs.title: Spontaneous breathing trial
_Vb5Cs.description: A test that is used to determine whether a mechanically ventilated patient is ready to breathe without a ventilator. In a patient on mechanical ventilation, SBT is performed once the patient has a stable/resolving lung disease, normal PaO₂ and O₂ saturation on FiO₂ < 0.4–0.5 and PEEP < 5–8 mm H₂O, a pH ≥ 7.35, hemodynamic stability with little or no vasopressor therapy, as well as an ability to spontaneously initiate an inspiratory effort (i.e., good neuromuscular function).

zVbrCs.title: Gastroenterostomy
zVbrCs.description: The surgical creation of an anastamosis between the stomach and the jejunum.

-VbDCs.title: Shock
-VbDCs.description: A life-threatening circulatory disorder that leads to tissue hypoxia, a disturbance in microcirculation, and end-organ damage. Further subdivided into categories that include hypovolemic, distributive, and cardiogenic shock.

ZebZxs.title: Band ligation
ZebZxs.description: The application of a rubber band around the base of an enlarged vessel (e.g., esophageal varix or hemorrhoid). Ligation causes occlusion and thrombosis of the vessel, which then sloughs off, leaving behind a superficial mucosal ulcer that heals rapidly.

0ebexs.title: Idiopathic flushing
0ebexs.description: A condition of episodic reddening of the skin with the sensation of warmth or burning of the face, neck, and, less commonly, the upper trunk and abdomen. Occurs as a physiologic response to emotional stress, such as embarrassment or anger, which causes increased blood flow to the skin and engorgement of the subpapillary venous plexus.

Yebnxs.title: Hematocrit
Yebnxs.description: The percentage of total blood volume that consists of red blood cells. Normal values are 41–53% for males and 36–46% for females.

bebHxs.title: Bilevel positive airway pressure
bebHxs.description: A noninvasive form of ventilation that maintains two different levels of positive pressure in the airway, such as a higher level (e.g., 10 mm Hg) during inspiration and a lower level (e.g., 4 mm Hg) during expiration. Commonly used to treat acute exacerbations of COPD and asthma. Maintaining a slightly positive pressure prevents airway collapse, decreases the work of breathing, improves alveolar ventilation, and increases the diffusion of oxygen from the alveoli into the blood.

Xeb9xs.title: Tracheostomy
Xeb9xs.description: A surgical opening in the anterior tracheal wall, typically held open with a tracheal tube. Most commonly performed when long-term mechanical ventilation is required.

WebPBs.title: Intracranial lesions with ring enhancement
WebPBs.description: A radiological finding of an intracranial lesion with a peripheral rim of increased radiodensity due to the concentration of enhancing contrast dye. Conditions that manifest with ring-enhancing lesions include glioblastoma, toxoplasmosis, and CNS lymphoma.

VebGBs.title: Hypoparathyroidism
VebGBs.description: A disorder characterized by inappropriately low levels of parathyroid hormone (PTH). Most commonly caused by damage to parathyroid glands after anterior neck surgery. Other causes include inflammatory or autoimmune injury to parathyroid glands and genetic conditions affecting PTH synthesis.

eebxBs.title: Lymphadenitis
eebxBs.description: The inflammation of a lymph node that causes it to become tender and enlarged. A common immune response to fighting infections and sometimes neoplasms.

Uebbys.title: Hypoxemia
Uebbys.description: A decreased oxygen content in arterial blood. Typically results in a partial pressure of oxygen (PaO₂) of < 80 mm Hg and/or an oxygen saturation of less than 95%.

2ebTys.title: Escherischia coli O157:H7
2ebTys.description: A serotype of enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC) that produces Shiga toxin. Infection with O157:H7 can cause bloody diarrhea and hemolytic uremic syndrome, most commonly in children.

febkys.title: Stack splint
febkys.description: A plastic mechanical device used to stabilize the distal interphalangeal joints in full extension following extensor tendon injuries.

Teb6ys.title: Dynamic splint
Teb6ys.description: An articulated splint with spring or elastic components that control the motion across a joint and/or place it under constant tension.

Sebyys.title: Thrombotic microangiopathy
Sebyys.description: A condition in which microthrombi, consisting primarily of platelets, form and occlude the microvasculature, leading to microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and end-organ damage. Most commonly caused by disseminated intravascular coagulation. Thrombotic microangiopathies include thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, hemolytic uremic syndrome, and HELLP syndrome.

3ebSAs.title: Pyogenic liver abscess
3ebSAs.description: A type of liver abscess caused by bacterial infection. Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Streptococci are among the most commonly isolated causative pathogens. Typically manifests with fever, which may be accompanied by right upper quadrant pain. Pyogenic liver abscess is the most common form of liver abscess in the US.

QebuAs.title: Acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
QebuAs.description: The most common subtype of Guillain-Barré syndrome in the United States and Europe, in which antibodies against the myelin sheath and Schwann-cell antigens are produced. Signs of demyelination on nerve conduction studies (e.g., prolonged F-wave latency, reduced nerve conduction velocity) are a characteristic feature.

jeb_As.title: Percutaneous aspiration, instillation, and reaspiration
jeb_As.description: A minimally-invasive procedure used to treat hydatid liver cysts. Consists of ultrasound- or CT-guided percutaneous puncture of a cyst, aspiration of its contents, injection of a scolicidal agent (e.g., hypertonic saline, ethanol), and subsequent reaspiration.

PebW_s.title: Amebic liver abscess
PebW_s.description: A liver abscess caused by the protozoan Entamoeba histolytica, which is transmitted feco-orally. Usually occurs following travel to an endemic region. E. histolytica colonizes the intestine, and can invade the liver via portal veins. The abscess contains a reddish-brown paste resembling anchovy paste.

4eb3_s.title: Cholecystectomy
4eb3_s.description: The surgical removal of the gallbladder. Indicated for symptomatic or complicated gallstone disease, for asymptomatic gallstone disease in patients with diabetes, immunosuppression, or gallbladder calcification, and for gallbladder carcinoma. Most often performed laparoscopically.

kebm_s.title: Epidermolysis bullosa
kebm_s.description: A rare, heterogeneous group of congenital and/or genetic blistering skin disorders that occur during infancy and childhood. The severity of the lesions, extent of mucosal involvement, and site of cleavage (intraepidermal/subepidermal) differ depending on the specific subtype. A common feature in all forms of epidermolysis bullosa is the induction of blisters by minor trauma and exacerbation in warm weather.

Neb-_s.title: Hemorrhagic stroke
Neb-_s.description: An acute neurological condition characterized by nontraumatic hemorrhage within the brain parenchyma (intracerebral hemorrhage) or the subarachnoid space (subarachnoid hemorrhage). Resulting tissue compression and reactive swelling cause clinical symptoms (e.g., neurologic deficits) and long-term tissue damage. Causes include hypertension, ruptured arteriovenous malformations, and cerebral amyloid angiopathy.

mebVzs.title: Alpha blockers
mebVzs.description: A class of drugs that inhibit alpha-1 and alpha-2 receptors. Nonselective alpha blockers include phenoxybenzamine and phentolamine. Commonly used alpha-1 blockers include prazosin, tamsulosin, and doxazosin, which are used to treat BPH and PTSD.

5ebizs.title: Marjolin ulcer
5ebizs.description: A cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma that arises from chronic, nonhealing wounds (e.g., burn injuries, pressure ulcers). Typically aggressive and associated with poor prognosis due to high risk of local recurrence.

destinations.label: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma → Subtypes and variants

neb7zs.title: Digital subtraction angiography
neb7zs.description: An imaging method that involves taking a series of x-rays at timed intervals while injecting intravascular contrast. The pre-contrast images are then digitally subtracted from the images taken with intravascular contrast to visualize the artery of interest. This test has the highest diagnostic accuracy in testing for peripheral arterial disease and allows real-time visualization of the patient's arteries.

media.title: Peripheral arterial disease with iliac occlusion

Lebwzs.title: Fibrillin
Lebwzs.description: A glycoprotein of connective tissues that forms a supportive sheath around elastin. It is an important component of elastic fibers. Mutation of the fibrillin-1 (FBN1) gene causes Marfan syndrome.

KebU-s.title: Temporal artery biopsy
KebU-s.description: The gold standard confirmatory test for diagnosing giant cell arteritis (GCA).

6ebj-s.title: Hemicolectomy
6ebj-s.description: The surgical resection of the right or left portions of the large bowel. When right-sided, it involves resection of the terminal ileum, cecum, ascending colon, hepatic flexure, and proximal third of the transverse colon. When left-sided, it includes resection of the distal third of the transverse colon, splenic flexure, descending colon, and sigmoid colon.

destinations.label: Colorectal cancer → Treatment of colon cancer

pebL-s.title: Third space volume loss
pebL-s.description: The leakage of intravascular fluid into interstitial spaces or spaces lined by epithelium, such as the peritoneal cavity, pleural cavity, or pericardial cavity, as a result of altered hydrostatic/oncotic pressure and/or inflammation/injury to the epithelium lining these cavities. Continuous third space fluid loss can result in hypovolemic shock.

Jebs-s.title: Partial hip replacement
Jebs-s.description: A surgical procedure that replaces the femoral head with a prosthesis. The patient's native acetabulum is not replaced. Commonly performed for femoral neck fractures in older adults without significant osteoarthritis.

qebC-s.title: Traction screws
qebC-s.description: Metal screws used to counteract the opposing pull of muscles on fracture bone fragments. This serves to both prevent displacement of the fracture and to decrease bleeding and pain. This treatment method, combined with other conservative treatments (stabilization using a splint, analgesia), would be appropriate in elderly patients with too many comorbidities to safely undergo surgery or in very young patients.

IebYZG.title: Terlipressin
IebYZG.description: A synthetic vasopressin analogue with a longer duration of action, less adverse effects, and a more selective action on V1 than V2 receptors (V1 receptor stimulation causes vasoconstriction, and release of ACTH, while V2 receptor stimulation causes antidiuresis). Used to treat acute variceal hemorrhage, hepatorenal syndrome, and severe septic shock.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

rebfZG.title: Cyproheptadine
rebfZG.description: A first-generation H1 antihistamine with nonselective antiserotonergic activity. It also has anticholinergic and antidopaminergic activity at higher concentrations. Common indications include carcinoid syndrome, serotonin syndrome, and cold-induced urticaria.

7eb4ZG.title: Marfan syndrome
7eb4ZG.description: An autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder that affects microfibrils and elastin in connective tissue throughout the body. Caused by fibrillin 1 deficiency due to FBN1 gene mutation. Can result in pathological manifestations in the cardiovascular system (e.g., mitral valve prolapse), the musculoskeletal system (e.g., joint hypermobility), and the eyes (e.g., lens subluxation).

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Summary

sebtZG.title: Biopsy
sebtZG.description: The removal of cells or tissue for laboratory examination or testing. Several methods exist to remove the target tissue (e.g., fine needle aspiration, punch biopsy).

GebBZG.title: Diffusion capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide
GebBZG.description: A measure of the ability of the lungs to transfer gas from inhaled air to red blood cells in the pulmonary capillaries. The main determinants for diffusing capacity include the area and thickness of the alveolar-capillary barrier and the diffusion constant of the measured gas. Results are used to further characterize obstructive and restrictive lung diseases. Abnormal DLCO despite normal lung volumes may be seen in patients with pulmonary vascular diseases (e.g., pulmonary hypertension), systemic disorders, (e.g., anemia), or early interstitial lung disease.

destinations.label: Pulmonary function testing → Single-breath diffusing capacity

tebX0G.title: Trousseau's sign of latent tetany
tebX0G.description: A sign that can be observed in patients with tetany due to hypocalcemia. After the inflation of a blood pressure cuff (pressures above the systolic blood pressure), an ipsilateral carpopedal spasm occurs, lasting for several minutes.

Deb1aG.title: Arterial ulcer
Deb1aG.description: An ulceration caused by decreased arterial blood flow (e.g., due to peripheral arterial disease), typically found on the lateral ankle or distal digits.

media.title: Features of arterial, venous, and neuropathic ulcers

webhaG.title: Mixed ulcer
webhaG.description: An ulcer caused by venous insufficiency, but the healing of which is compromised by concomitant arterial disease.

9ebNaG.title: Diabetic ulcer
9ebNaG.description: An open wound at the bottom of the foot or toes that manifests in patients with diabetes. Caused by impaired sensation of progressive damage, poor circulation, and foot deformity.

media.title: Infected ulcer on the ball of the foot
Features of arterial, venous, and neuropathic ulcers

CebqaG.title: LQTS
CebqaG.description: A congenital or acquired heart condition in which the QT interval (i.e. ventricular depolarization and repolarization) is prolonged. Most patients remain asymptomatic until they present with syncope, seizures, or life-threatening arrhythmias including torsades de pointes and ventricular fibrillation.

xebEaG.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia
xebEaG.description: A hospital-acquired infection that develops 48 hours after the initiation of mechanical ventilation via either tracheostomy or intubation. Approx. 5–10% of patients on mechanical ventilation develop VAP.

yebdYG.title: Central line-associated bloodstream infection
yebdYG.description: A standardized surveillance definition for an intravascular catheter-related infection that is used to monitor hospital nosocomial infection rates. Patients must have a nosocomial primary bloodstream infection that occurs > 48 hours after placement of a central line and within 48 hours of removal.

AebRYG.title: Ureterolithotomy
AebRYG.description: A surgical procedure in which urinary stones that are not amenable to endoscopic treatment are removed using an open or laparoscopic approach.

zebrYG.title: Surgical embolectomy
zebrYG.description: The removal of an embolus by opening up an artery with an incision.

-ebDYG.title: Acute traumatic coagulopathy
-ebDYG.description: An acute disorder of coagulation that occurs acutely following severe injuries. Diagnostic criteria: PT/PTT > 1.5x normal in an acute trauma patient without pre-existing coagulopathy. Sometimes associated with a drop in platelets, but this is not required for diagnosis. ATC is associated with greater transfusion requirements, longer ICU stays, and increased mortality.

ZUbZbG.title: Torus palatinus
ZUbZbG.description: A benign bony overgrowth that is typically located in the midline of the hard palate. Most frequently affects young adults. Usually asymptomatic but large tumors may interfere with speech or eating.

destinations.label: Benign bone tumors → Overview of benign bone tumors

0UbebG.title: Ureteral stent
0UbebG.description: A thin, hollow tube is inserted into the ureter to enable drainage of fluid from the renal pelvis into the bladder. Cystoscopy-guided transurethral placement is most common, although an antegrade approach via puncture of the renal pelvis is also possible. Usually, a double-J stent is used.

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Urinary drainage procedures

aUbQbG.title: Bariatric surgery
aUbQbG.description: A category of surgical procedures performed to help patients lose weight. Includes procedures that reduce the size of the stomach or reroute the small intestine.

YUbnbG.title: Herniotomy
YUbnbG.description: A surgical procedure in which a hernia sac is removed that is performed to treat different types of hernias, e.g. small bowel or hiatal hernias.

XUb9bG.title: Hamman's sign
XUb9bG.description: A crunching, rasping sound in sync with the heartbeat that is caused by the heart beating against air-filled tissues. Associated with pneumomediastinum, pneumopericardium, and tracheobronchial injury.

cUbaXG.title: Carney complex
cUbaXG.description: A rare, autosomal dominant syndrome caused by mutations in the PRKAR1A gene. Manifests with periorificial lentigines, endocrine tumors (e.g., adrenal, pituitary glands, testicular tumors), and some nonendocrine tumors (e.g., cardiac myxoma, schwannomas).

1Ub2XG.title: Cystolithiasis
1Ub2XG.description: The presence of one or more urinary calculi within the bladder. Bladder stones can form within the bladder itself, usually resulting from bladder outflow obstruction. They can also form in the kidneys and pass through the ureter.

WUbPXG.title: Neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction
WUbPXG.description: A condition characterized by disruption in the innervation of the detrusor and/or urethral sphincter due to lesions in the brain, spinal cord, or peripheral nerves. Can manifest with urinary retention and/or incontinence.

dUboXG.title: Radial styloidectomy
dUboXG.description: Surgical removal of the radial styloid process.

VUbGXG.title: Intravenous immunoglobulin
VUbGXG.description: A treatment that contains IgG antibodies derived from donor blood. Used to treat a variety of conditions, including immune deficiency, inflammatory disorders, and autoimmune conditions (e.g., ITP, AIHA, Kawasaki disease, Guillain-Barré syndrome).

UUbbcG.title: Needle thoracostomy
UUbbcG.description: A technique for emergency decompression of a tension pneumothorax. A long (5-8 cm), large-bore (14 to 16-gauge) needle catheter is inserted over the superior margin of the rib, after which a rush of air should be heard. For adults, the 2nd intercostal space at the midclavicular line or the 4th–5th intercostal space between the anterior and midaxillary line should be used. Tubing is then attached to the catheter to allow trapped air to exit the pleural cavity.

2UbTcG.title: Thoracotomy
2UbTcG.description: A surgical procedure in which an incision is performed on the anterior chest to gain access to the thoracic cavity. Can be performed in a planned or urgent basis in operating rooms or as an emergency thoracotomy at the bedside.

fUbkcG.title: Jersey finger
fUbkcG.description: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) due to hyperextension of a flexed distal interphalangeal joint. Commonly occurs while playing sports, e.g., when a player's finger gets caught in the jersey of another player who quickly pulls away.

TUb6cG.title: Mallet finger
TUb6cG.description: Rupture of the extensor digitorum (ED) tendon, which acts to extend the fingers of the hand. A common sports injury that occurs due to hyperflexion of the distal interphalangeal joint. The classic mechanism of injury is a ball hitting the tip of the finger.

gUbFcG.title: Obstructive shock
gUbFcG.description: A type of shock caused by physical obstruction of blood flow in central vessels of the systemic or pulmonary circulation that leads to reduced cardiac output. Etiologies include cardiac tamponade, tension pneumothorax, and massive pulmonary embolism.

SUbycG.title: Whirlpool sign
SUbycG.description: A radiologic sign characterized by a whorled appearance created by the twisting of one structure around another (e.g., from cecal volvulus, malrotation with midgut volvulus, ovarian torsion, testicular torsion). Can be seen on ultrasonography and CT scan.

hUbc1G.title: Pseudomembranous colitis
hUbc1G.description: A condition most commonly caused by Clostridioides difficile infection and sometimes caused by other microorganisms or chronic ischemia. Characterized by the formation of pseudomembranous plaques on the colonic mucosa due to necrosis and exudation of fibrin. Diagnosis is confirmed with colonoscopy or histopathologic examination. Indicates an increased risk for toxic megacolon, ileus, and sepsis.

iUbJ1G.title: Cilostazol
iUbJ1G.description: A phosphodiesterase inhibitor that inhibits platelet aggregation and acts as a direct arterial vasodilator. Used to alleviate the symptoms of intermittent claudication.

QUbu1G.title: Dipyridamole
QUbu1G.description: A phosphodiesterase type 3 inhibitor used for intermittent vascular claudication, as an antiplatelet (anti-angina, TIA/stroke prevention) agent, and in the prevention of coronary stent restenosis.

kUbmWG.title: Teardrop sign
kUbmWG.description: A radiological sign most commonly seen in orbital floor fractures. Characterized by the presence of prolapsed orbital tissue (e.g., fat, connective tissue septa, and occasionally the inferior rectus muscle) into the sinus.

OUbIWG.title: Central cord syndrome
OUbIWG.description: A syndrome caused by a lesion near the central canal of the spinal cord. Etiologies include hyperextension of the neck, syringomyelia, and intramedullary spinal cord tumors. Typically affects the cervical cord. Selective damage to the crossing spinothalamic fibers and to the medial fibers of the corticospinal tract result in motor weakness, loss of pain, and loss of temperature sensation predominantly in the upper limbs and trunk.

destinations.label: Incomplete spinal cord syndromes → Central cord syndrome

lUbvWG.title: Posterior cord syndrome
lUbvWG.description: An incomplete spinal cord lesion due to damage to the dorsal columns that results in isolated loss of proprioception, vibratory sensation, and tactile discrimination. Can be caused by interruption of the posterior spinal arteries, demyelination, tabes dorsalis, or subacute combined degeneration (B12 deficiency).

destinations.label: Incomplete spinal cord syndromes → Posterior cord syndrome

NUb-WG.title: Revised cardiac risk index
NUb-WG.description: A tool used to predict the risk of a major adverse cardiac event following surgery. Incorporates patient-related risk factors (e.g., cardiovascular disease, renal disease) and surgery-related risk factors (e.g., thoracic or major abdominal surgery).

mUbVdG.title: Lunate dislocation
mUbVdG.description: A form of carpal injury characterized by disruption of all perilunate ligaments, causing palmar dislocation of the lunate into the carpal tunnel. Typically caused by hyperextension (e.g., fall on an outstretched hand). Corresponds to stage IV of the Mayfield classification of perilunate ligament injuries. May lead to carpal instability. Imaging shows volar lunate rotation and proximal migration of the capitate, making contact with the radius.

MUbMdG.title: Gonioscopy
MUbMdG.description: An ophthalmologic examination technique that uses a special contact lens and a slit lamp microscope to illuminate and directly visualize the iridocorneal angle. It is the gold-standard test to diagnose angle-closure glaucoma.

nUb7dG.title: Informed consent
nUb7dG.description: The process of attaining the patient's authorization for a medical test, treatment, or procedure.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Informed consent

LUbwdG.title: Drop arm test
LUbwdG.description: A physical examination maneuver used to assess supraspinatus tendon integrity. From a starting position with the arm abducted at or beyond 90°, the patient slowly lowers the arm. A positive test occurs when a patient is unable to slowly lower their arm (i.e., the affected arm drops).

KUbUVG.title: Sevelamer
KUbUVG.description: A phosphate binding agent used in the treatment of hyperphosphatemia in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) on hemodialysis.

rUbfeG.title: Total parenteral nutrition
rUbfeG.description: The intravenous administration of all required nutrients, bypassing the gastrointestinal tract. May be considered if oral intake or enteral nutrition is not possible for a prolonged period of time (e.g., due to malignancy, chemotherapy-associated anorexia).

7Ub4eG.title: Specialized nutrition support
7Ub4eG.description: The administration of enteral nutrition and/or parenteral nutrition in situations in which oral feeding is not possible (e.g., during mechanical ventilation for critical illness). May also be used to enhance nutritional status in patients who are unable to meet metabolic needs with oral feeding (e.g., those with dysphagia secondary to stroke).

FUbgUG.title: Postcholecystectomy syndrome
FUbgUG.description: Persistent or new abdominal symptoms following gallbladder removal. The pathophysiology is not yet fully understood, but it is thought to be due to alterations in the enterohepatic circulation of bile secondary to remaining biliary stones, biliary injury, or sphincter of Oddi dysfunction. Symptoms may include RUQ or epigastric pain, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, flatulence, bloating, and diarrhea.

8UbOUG.title: Melanoma
8UbOUG.description: A highly malignant tumor arising from melanocytes. Risk factors include extensive sun exposure, light skin, and a family history of melanoma. Metastasis is common; risk of metastasis correlates with tumor depth.

uUbpUG.title: Light's criteria
uUbpUG.description: A validated measure that determines if pleural fluid is exudative. One of the following has to be present: pleural fluid protein/serum protein ratio greater than 0.5; pleural fluid LDH/serum LDH > 0.6; or pleural fluid LDH > 2/3 the upper limit of serum LDH reference range.

EUb8UG.title: Evans syndrome
EUb8UG.description: A condition in which two or more hematologic immune cytopenias are present at the same time, most commonly immune thrombocytopenic purpura and autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

vUbAUG.title: Parastomal hernia
vUbAUG.description: The protrusion of intraabdominal contents through the abdominal wall defect created during stoma placement (e.g., colostomy).

DUb12G.title: Epinephrine
DUb12G.description: A substance that is produced by the adrenal glands (and available for therapeutic administration, e.g., anaphylaxis) with both α and β adrenergic agonist activity. Causes bronchial smooth muscle relaxation, cardiac stimulation, peripheral vasodilation (small doses), and peripheral vasoconstriction (large doses).

wUbh2G.title: Posterior cruciate ligament
wUbh2G.description: The largest and strongest intra-articular ligament of the knee. It originates on the lateral border of the medial femoral condyle and inserts on the posterior tibia between the two tibial plateaus. The PCL's primary function is to prevent posterior translation of the tibia at the knee. PCL injuries are common in athletes (knee hyperflexion with a plantar-flexed foot) and persons involved in motor vehicle accidents (direct posterior force to the tibia from the dashboard).

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The knee joint

media.title: Attachments of menisci and cruciate ligaments of the knee

CUbq2G.title: Arteriovenous malformation
CUbq2G.description: An abnormal, congenital arteriovenous connection. Can result in venous hypertension, tissue ischemia, and/or hemorrhage. It is the most common cause of spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage in children.

xUbE2G.title: Lateral collateral ligament
xUbE2G.description: A ligament that connects the femur to the fibula. Does not merge with the knee capsule. Responsible for lateral knee stability.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The knee joint

BUbz2G.title: Medial collateral ligament
BUbz2G.description: A ligament that connects the medial femoral condyle to the anteromedial tibia. Provides restraint against valgus stress and tibial rotation.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The knee joint

yUbdfG.title: Anterior cruciate ligament
yUbdfG.description: A ligament that connects the posteromedial aspect of the lateral femoral condyle to the anteromedial tibia. Its primary function is to prevent anterior translation of the tibia, but it also helps prevent tibial rotation and valgus/varus displacement.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The knee joint

media.title: Attachments of menisci and cruciate ligaments of the knee

AUbRfG.title: Hemorrhagic choroidal detachment
AUbRfG.description: A separation of the choroid from its attachments throughout the eye through intraocular hemorrhage. Most commonly occurs following intraocular surgery but can be caused by eye trauma and inflammation.

_Ub5fG.title: Inferior vena cava filter
_Ub5fG.description: A filter (metal or other material) that is placed in the inferior vena cava (usually infrarenally) during a catheter intervention to prevent pulmonary embolism from DVT. Only indicated in patients who have absolute contraindications to anticoagulation or thrombolysis.

zUbrfG.title: Gastrografin enema
zUbrfG.description: A diagnostic test in which radiopaque, water-soluble gastrografin contrast is instilled in the rectum to visualize the lumen of the colon and the rectum on imaging. It can also be used to relieve constipation.

Z2bZTG.title: Esophagitis
Z2bZTG.description: An inflammation of the esophageal lining. Causes include GERD, infections, drugs, and allergic reactions.

02beTG.title: Blue toe syndrome
02beTG.description: Ischemia due to small vessel occlusion that manifests as toe discoloration. Typically caused by cholesterol embolization syndrome.

a2bQTG.title: Acetylcholine receptor antibodies
a2bQTG.description: An autoantibody directed against the acetylcholine receptor. This antibody is present in most patients with generalized and thymoma-induced myasthenia gravis and is highly specific for the diagnosis.

Y2bnTG.title: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
Y2bnTG.description: A disorder characterized by thickening and sclerosis of the skin and deeper structures from proliferation of dermal fibroblasts and dendritic cells. Most commonly attributed to administration of gadolinium-based contrast agents to patients with underlying renal failure, particularly those on dialysis.

b2bHTG.title: Aortography
b2bHTG.description: A catheter angiography of the aorta. The aorta and its branch vessels are visualized on x-ray following the injection of a contrast agent using a catheter. This modality has widely been replaced by CT angiography.

X2b9TG.title: Diagnostic laparoscopy
X2b9TG.description: A surgical diagnostic procedure used to visualize the abdominal cavity with a laparoscope inserted through an incision in the abdominal wall (minimally-invasive instrumentation). Facilitates biopsy of suspicious lesions and collection of peritoneal fluid. Indications include evaluation of acute abdominal pain and evaluation of cancer.

media.title: Peritoneal access with closed technique (using Veress needle)

12b2gG.title: S1Q3T3 pattern
12b2gG.description: A pattern of ECG findings classically associated with right ventricular strain due to pulmonary embolism. Characterized by a deep S wave in lead I, a pathological Q wave in lead III, and an inverted T wave in lead III.

media.title: S1Q3T3 pattern in acute pulmonary embolism

W2bPgG.title: Leukocyte esterase
W2bPgG.description: An enzyme produced by white blood cells. When found in body fluids (primarily the urine), it suggests infection. It is commonly tested as part of a urine dipstick analysis to evaluate for urinary tract infection.

d2bogG.title: Donovan bodies
d2bogG.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by intracytoplasmic cysts filled with deeply staining, safety-pin shaped bodies within macrophages on Giemsa or Wright stain (Pud cells). Diagnostic of granuloma inguinale (donovanosis).

V2bGgG.title: Primary wound closure
V2bGgG.description: The act of approximating the edges of a wound with materials such as sutures, staples, or adhesive or the physiologic healing process of naturally well-approximated wounds (e.g., paper cuts).

e2bxgG.title: Myelosuppression
e2bxgG.description: A condition in which bone marrow activity is decreased, causing anemia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia. It is commonly caused by infection of the bone marrow (Parvovirus B19) or by chemotherapeutic agents.

U2bbSG.title: Curettage
U2bbSG.description: The act of surgically removing tissue by scraping or scooping.

22bTSG.title: Coccygectomy
22bTSG.description: The surgical excision of the coccyx.

f2bkSG.title: Secondary wound closure
f2bkSG.description: The process by which skin wounds are left to heal without suturing. The tissue that constitutes the gap between skin edges is called granulation tissue. This tissue generally forms the scar after healing is complete.

T2b6SG.title: Tissue plasminogen activator
T2b6SG.description: A serine protease found on endothelial cells of the blood vessels. Catalyzes the conversion of plasminogen to plasmin, which is the main enzyme responsible for clot breakdown. Recombinant tissue plasminogen activators (e.g., alteplase, reteplase, tenecteplase) are used as thrombolytics in patients with acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, or ischemic stroke.

g2bFSG.title: Compression ultrasonography
g2bFSG.description: A diagnostic test to evaluate for deep vein thrombosis. It uses ultrasound to visualize a vein while the examiner applies external pressure over the vein using the ultrasound probe. Incompressibility of the obstructed vein is a sign of DVT.

media.title: POCUS protocol for detection of lower extremity DVT

S2bySG.title: Fungemia
S2bySG.description: The presence of a fungus in the bloodstream; rare, except in immunosuppressed patients.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Systemic fungal infections

R2blhG.title: Rectal suction biopsy
R2blhG.description: A technique in which a suction device draws in rectal mucosa and submucosa, which is then biopsied. Commonly used in the diagnostic evaluation of rectal abnormalities, including infection, neoplasia, amyloidosis, Crohn disease, and Hirschsprung disease.

i2bJhG.title: Small bowel enteroscopy
i2bJhG.description: Group of techniques used for the diagnosis and treatment of diseases located in the small bowel. These include push enteroscopy, balloon enteroscopy, and spiral enteroscopy.

Q2buhG.title: Fluorescein angiography
Q2buhG.description: An imaging procedure in which fluorescent dye (fluorescein) is injected intravenously in order to highlight retinal vessels, which are then photographed.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Retinal examination

media.title: Fluorescein angiography in dry age-related macular degeneration
Fluorescein angiography in ischemic branch retinal vein occlusion

j2b_hG.title: Reperfusion injury
j2b_hG.description: A condition characterized by endothelial damage caused by a returning blood supply after a period of ischemia (e.g., myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke). Causes increased capillary permeability, tissue swelling, and release of reactive oxygen species. Extensive reperfusion injury (reperfusion syndrome) is associated with systemic disturbances such as acidemia, hyperkalemia (which can cause cardiac arrhythmias), and edema (which can cause compartment syndrome).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Free radical injury

P2bW3G.title: Sitz bath
P2bW3G.description: A bath in which the perineal area is immersed for a period of time in warm water. Used primarily as a symptomatic therapy for painful anal conditions such as thrombosed external hemorrhoids and anal fissures.

42b33G.title: Anal fistula
42b33G.description: Abnormal connection between the epithelium surface of the anal canal and the perianal skin.

O2bI3G.title: Acute megacolon
O2bI3G.description: An acute dilation of the colon in the absence of a mechanical obstruction, characteristically seen in severely ill or postoperative patients. Clinical features include gradual abdominal distention, abdominal pain, and altered bowel movements (diarrhea or constipation).

destinations.label: Megacolon → Acute megacolon (Acute colonic pseudo-obstruction or Ogilvie's syndrome)

l2bv3G.title: Megacolon
l2bv3G.description: A dilation of the colon in the absence of a mechanical obstruction. Acute causes (e.g., C. difficile infection) are surgical emergencies. Chronic causes include Chagas disease and Hirschsprung disease.

N2b-3G.title: Chronic megacolon
N2b-3G.description: Permanent dilation of the colon caused by congenital/acquired colonic dysmotility in the absence of a mechanical obstruction.

M2bMRG.title: Strabismus
M2bMRG.description: Misalignment of an eye with regard to the normal visual axis, which results in the inability of images from the right and left eye to be fused together.

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Basic terms

n2b7RG.title: Leriche's syndrome
n2b7RG.description: Peripheral artery disease at the level of the aortic bifurcation or bilateral occlusion of the iliac arteries that leads to the classic triad of bilateral buttock, hip, or thigh claudication; erectile dysfunction; and absent/diminished femoral pulses.

media.title: Localization of arterial occlusion in PAD

L2bwRG.title: Subacromial bursitis
L2bwRG.description: An inflammation of the subacromial bursa (located between the scapula and the supraspinatus muscle) that is often caused by repetitive overhead motion. Associated with rotator cuff tears, impingement syndrome, and adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder).

o2b0iG.title: Pes anserine pain syndrome
o2b0iG.description: A condition characterized by pain and tenderness at the anteromedial aspect of the knee at the pes anserinus insertion. Thought to be caused by sartorius, gracilis, and/or semitendinosus tendinopathy.

destinations.label: Collection of orthopedic conditions → Pes anserinus pain syndrome

K2bUiG.title: Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex
K2bUiG.description: A group of atypical mycobacteria (e.g., Mycobacterium avium, Mycobacterium intracellulare) that cause opportunistic infections among AIDS patients with CD4 count < 50/μL.

62bjiG.title: HIV-associated enteropathy
62bjiG.description: Chronic diarrhea for which no etiological agent can be identified in patients with HIV. Thought to be due to direct or indirect effects of HIV infection on the enteric mucosa.

J2bsiG.title: Dental abscess
J2bsiG.description: A collection of pus in the pulp of a tooth that can spread to the local (gum, alveolar bone) or regional (oral, cervical, facial) structures.

q2bCiG.title: Orbital mucormycosis
q2bCiG.description: A fungal infection of the orbital contents posterior to the orbital septum, including the fat and extraocular muscles. Mucor and Rhizopus are the most common fungal pathogens.

I2bYQG.title: Open pneumothorax
I2bYQG.description: A pneumothorax due to a traumatic, open chest wall wound that allows air to enter the pleural cavity directly through the wound during inspiration, leading to a collapsed lung on the affected side. If untreated, can lead to tension pneumothorax and respiratory collapse.

r2bfQG.title: Leydig cells
r2bfQG.description: Endocrine cells in the testicular interstitium between the seminiferous tubules that secrete testosterone in the presence of luteinizing hormone.

H2bKQG.title: Mohs micrographic surgery
H2bKQG.description: Microscopically controlled surgery in which thin layers of skin are removed and examined for cancer cells. The result of the examination determines additional tissue removal. Best method for ensuring that both the tumor is completely removed and that uninvolved skin is spared.

G2bBQG.title: Pelvic binder
G2bBQG.description: A device (such as a sheet or wrap) that immobilizes and stabilizes the pelvis after injury. Tamponades bleeding and stabilizes fractures in the pelvis and perineum to reduce the risk of severe hemorrhage.

t2bXjG.title: Malignant tumors of the salivary glands
t2bXjG.description: An umbrella term for tumors of the parotid (most common), submandibular, sublingual, and minor salivary glands. Associated with ionizing radiation and some viral infections (e.g., HIV, HPV, EBV). Manifestations include submucosal swelling and mucosal ulceration.

destinations.label: Diseases of the salivary glands → Malignant tumors

82bOjG.title: Selective estrogen receptor modulator
82bOjG.description: A class of drugs that has competitive agonist effects on the estrogen receptor. Depending on the tissue, SERMs may produce either estrogenic or antiestrogenic effects. Common uses include ovulation induction, contraception, osteoporosis treatment, breast cancer treatment, and vaginal atrophy.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

v2bAjG.title: Pancreatic ascites
v2bAjG.description: An accumulation of pancreatic fluid in the peritoneal cavity. Etiologies include pancreatic duct disruption (e.g., due to acute pancreatitis, pancreatic surgery, or trauma) or pseudocyst leak/rupture.

D2b1PG.title: Rifaximin
D2b1PG.description: A non‑absorbable antibiotic that can be used in patients with hepatic encephalopathy, severe cases of relapsing pseudomembranous colitis, small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, and traveler's diarrhea.

w2bhPG.title: Hyperkalemic emergency
w2bhPG.description: A potentially life-threatening condition caused by a rapid increase in serum potassium concentrations (e.g., due to increased tissue breakdown, chronic kidney disease). ECG can show peaked T waves and cardiac arrhythmias. Requires acute treatment (e.g., calcium gluconate, insulin with glucose).

92bNPG.title: Saphenous varix
92bNPG.description: A dilated, saccular swelling of the great saphenous vein that lies just distal to the junction of the femoral vein and the great saphenous vein. May be associated with varicose veins of the lower limbs. Presents as a reducible groin swelling below the inguinal ligament with a palpable cough impulse, mimicking a femoral hernia.

C2bqPG.title: Gonadotroph adenoma
C2bqPG.description: A rare, typically benign tumor of the gonadotroph-secreting (FSH/LH) cells of the anterior pituitary gland. Usually asymptomatic, presenting only with mass effect, but causes detectable elevations in FSH or LH in 35% of cases. Very rarely they cause ovarian hyperstimulation symptoms (oligo/amenorrhea, menorrhagia) in premenopausal women or precocious puberty in boys.

x2bEPG.title: Amenorrhea
x2bEPG.description: The absence of menstruation. Classified as primary (no menarche by 15 years of age) or secondary (absence of menstruation for more than 3–6 months in an individual who previously menstruated).

B2bzPG.title: Contrast venography
B2bzPG.description: An invasive procedure in which a contrast agent is directly injected into the venous system under fluoroscopy to map veins and assess flow abnormalities.

y2bd4G.title: Polymyalgia rheumatica
y2bd4G.description: A chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease of unknown etiology that mainly affects women > 50 years of age. Typically manifests with acute pain and stiffness in the shoulder girdle, pelvic girdle, and/or neck, and constitutional symptoms (e.g., fatigue, malaise, and depressed mood). Approximately 20% of patients also have giant cell arteritis.

media.title: Polymyalgia rheumatica and giant cell arteritis fact sheet

A2bR4G.title: Hypogonadism
A2bR4G.description: A condition caused by reduced function of the testes or ovaries, leading to decreased production of sex hormones. Can result from diseases of the ovaries or testes (primary hypogonadism) or conditions affecting the pituitary gland or hypothalamus (secondary hypogonadism). In children, manifestations include impaired development of primary or secondary sex characteristics (e.g., ambiguous genitalia, delayed puberty) and, in adults, menstrual irregularities, gynecomastia, erectile dysfunction, loss of body hair, decreased libido, and/or infertility.

z2br4G.title: Silver sulfadiazine
z2br4G.description: A silver-containing topical antimicrobial agent with possible anti-inflammatory effects. Acts by binding bacterial cell membranes; exact mechanism is unclear.

-2bD4G.title: Chlorhexidine gluconate
-2bD4G.description: An antiseptic agent that is active against gram-positive bacteria, gram-negative bacteria, facultative anaerobes, aerobes, and yeast. Disrupts cell osmotic equilibrium and induces the precipitation of cytoplasmic contents.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

0fbekG.title: Primary hypercortisolism
0fbekG.description: A condition of hypercortisolism caused by excess secretion of cortisol from the adrenal glands (often an adrenal adenoma) or from chronic glucocorticoid therapy. High levels of cortisol cause negative feedback on the pituitary and suppress ACTH release.

afbQkG.title: Secondary hypercortisolism
afbQkG.description: A condition of hypercortisolism caused by excess production of ACTH either from a pituitary adenoma (Cushing disease) or from an ectopic focus.

bfbHkG.title: Cerebral falx
bfbHkG.description: A crescent-shaped fold of the dura mater that separates the two hemispheres of the brain.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

Xfb9kG.title: Supratentorial region
Xfb9kG.description: The area of the brain above the tentorium cerebelli (i.e., the upper region of the brain).

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

cfbaOG.title: Retroperitoneal hematoma
cfbaOG.description: Bleeding into the retroperitoneal space. May occur spontaneously (e.g., in patients on anticoagulants) or result from blunt or penetrating trauma, iatrogenic causes such as vascular access procedures (e.g., percutaneous coronary intervention), or surgery involving retroperitoneal access or manipulation of adjacent vascular structures.

media.title: Retroperitoneal hemorrhage from the left common iliac artery

WfbPOG.title: Jones criteria
WfbPOG.description: Criteria for the diagnosis of rheumatic fever: previous evidence of infection with streptococcal infection (required); major criteria: arthritis, carditis, subcutaneous nodules, erythema marginatum, and chorea; minor criteria: fever, elevated acute phase reactants, arthralgias, and prolonged PR interval.

dfboOG.title: Postoperative ileus
dfboOG.description: A usually transient condition of obstipation and intolerance of oral intake due to intestinal dysmotility following surgery in the absence of mechanical obstruction. This is thought to be due to a physiological inflammatory and neurohumoral response to surgery and usually passes spontaneously within 72 hours. Persistence beyond this time is called prolonged postoperative ileus.

VfbGOG.title: Cryotherapy
VfbGOG.description: The use of cold temperature as a medical therapy. Examples include the application of ice to injuries to reduce pain and swelling, scalp cooling to reduce hair loss during chemotherapy, and the use of liquid nitrogen to destroy abnormal tissue (e.g., cryoablation).

efbxOG.title: Dermoscopy
efbxOG.description: A technique wherein an instrument called a dermatoscope is used to visualize and magnify skin structures in the epidermis, dermoepidermal junction, and upper dermis, e.g., to diagnose skin lesions and triage skin cancers.

UfbblG.title: Wedge biopsy
UfbblG.description: A procedure in which a "V" or triangular-shaped area of skin is removed, usually reserved for large legions in which evaluating the length, breadth, and depth are all important; e.g., for squamous cell carcinoma margins.

ffbklG.title: Strangulated hernia
ffbklG.description: An irreducible hernia in which perfusion of the contents of the hernial sac becomes compromised as a result of the mechanical constriction of blood vessels. Intestinal necrosis, intestinal perforation, and peritonitis may rapidly follow the onset of strangulation.

Tfb6lG.title: Irreducible hernia
Tfb6lG.description: A type of hernia in which the contents of the hernial sac cannot return back through the abdominal wall defect into the peritoneal cavity with the application of gentle external pressure. Increases the risk of subsequent strangulation and bowel obstruction.

gfbFlG.title: Stool culture
gfbFlG.description: A test used to identify bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites in stool often in the context of a suspected gastrointestinal infection.

hfbcNG.title: Urinary frequency
hfbcNG.description: The need to void small quantities of urine frequently throughout the day and night. A common cause is benign prostatic hyperplasia.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

3fbSNG.title: Scotoma
3fbSNG.description: An area within the visual field where vision is temporarily or permanently reduced or absent.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Scotoma and anopia

RfblNG.title: Prostatic abscess
RfblNG.description: A complication of prostatitis that presents with genitourinary symptoms similar to acute bacterial prostatitis (e.g., fever, dysuria, pain) and a fluctuant prostate on rectal examination. Treatments involve antibiotic therapy and transrectal ultrasound-guided drainage.

ifbJNG.title: Antineoplastic agents
ifbJNG.description: A group of drugs with cytotoxic properties used to inhibit proliferation of rapidly growing cells (as in the treatment of cancer and other proliferative disorders). Classified according to mechanism of action, including alkylating agents, antimetabolites, topoisomerase inhibitors, and mitotic inhibitors. Associated with a range of adverse effects (e.g., nausea, vomiting, increased risk of infection, and impaired growth of healthy cells).

QfbuNG.title: Laser ablation
QfbuNG.description: A procedure that uses a laser of specific wavelength to heat and destroy abnormal tissue. Often used in ophthalmologic, surgical, and dermatologic procedures.

PfbWmG.title: Light chain
PfbWmG.description: A component of immunoglobulin, which consists of four different proteins. Two of these proteins are larger than the other two and are called heavy chains. The two smaller proteins are referred to as light chains, which themselves can be one of two types: kappa or lambda. Production of excess light chains (usually due to hematopoietic aberrations) occurs in diseases such as primary systemic amyloidosis and multiple myeloma.

4fb3mG.title: Breast abscess
4fb3mG.description: An encapsulated accumulation of pus within the breast tissue that presents as a fluctuant mass on exam, usually in the setting of mastitis. Typical in women who are breastfeeding or immunocompromised.

kfbmmG.title: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease
kfbmmG.description: A group of rare, genetic kidney disorders characterized by the presence of small medullary cysts, tubular damage, interstitial fibrosis, and progressive renal dysfunction.

OfbImG.title: Proctocolectomy
OfbImG.description: The surgical removal of the rectum and part or all of the colon. Indications include inflammatory bowel disease (particularly ulcerative colitis), malignancy, and disorders that cause colonic polyps (e.g., familial adenomatous polyposis).

lfbvmG.title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
lfbvmG.description: A chronic, progressive, fibrosing interstitial pneumonia of unknown cause characterized by progressive worsening of dyspnea and lung function. Respiratory failure typically occurs within 3-7 years of diagnosis. Usual interstitial pneumonia is the histological and radiographic correlate.

destinations.label: Interstitial lung diseases → Classification of idiopathic interstitial pneumonias

Nfb-mG.title: Postpericardiotomy syndrome
Nfb-mG.description: An autoimmune febrile pericarditis or pleuritis that typically manifests 1 to 6 weeks after cardiothoracic surgery with fever, malaise, chest pain, tachycardia, and pericardial friction rub.

mfbV5G.title: Cholangiography
mfbV5G.description: A diagnostic test performed by inserting a catheter into the biliary tree over a guidewire, followed by injection of contrast dye, enabling real-time visualization of the biliary tree. Can be performed percutaneously or intraoperatively.

5fbi5G.title: Cholescintigraphy
5fbi5G.description: A test used for the diagnosis of acute cholecystitis and cystic duct obstruction and evaluation of common bile duct patency. Technetium-99m is selectively secreted into the biliary tree and allows visualization of the biliary tract. This radiotracer is injected intravenously and visualized with a gamma camera. A lack of filling of the gallbladder (i.e., no gallbladder visualized by the gamma camera) suggests a stone in the cystic duct.

MfbM5G.title: Upper gastrointestinal series
MfbM5G.description: A diagnostic imaging test which can be used to diagnose anatomic and/or functional abnormalities (e.g., strictures, dilatation) in the esophagus, stomach, and small intestines. A radiopaque fluid (e.g., barium or gastrografin) is swallowed and radiographs are taken to visualize the lumen of the alimentary tract.

Lfbw5G.title: Signet ring cell carcinoma
Lfbw5G.description: A type of adenocarcinoma characterized by diffuse proliferation of multiple, round, mucin-filled cells with peripheral nuclei. Most often develops in the stomach. Can metastasize to the ovaries (Krukenberg tumor).

ofb0MG.title: Cerebral perfusion pressure
ofb0MG.description: The effective pressure that delivers blood to the cerebral tissue. Defined as the difference between mean arterial pressure (MAP) and intracranial pressure (ICP). Thus, as ICP rises (e.g., from space-occupying lesions or inflammation), cerebral perfusion pressure decreases.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Pathophysiology

KfbUMG.title: Endovenous thermal ablation
KfbUMG.description: A technique for the treatment of chronic venous disease from valve incompetence. Laser or high-frequency radio waves are applied to the affected vein to seal it off and prevent further blood flow through it. Blood can then be diverted to veins with proper valve functioning.

6fbjMG.title: GABA
6fbjMG.description: An inhibitory neurotransmitter that reduces neuronal excitability and muscle tone

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

qfbCMG.title: Cystic hygroma
qfbCMG.description: A rare, congenital malformation of the lymphatic system that is caused by obstruction or sequestration of the jugular lymph sac. Presents typically during infancy or early childhood as a lymph-filled swelling in the posterior triangle of the neck. Associated with Turner syndrome.

IfbYnG.title: Carotid body tumor
IfbYnG.description: A benign, slow-growing neck swelling in the carotid triangle of the neck that arises from the chemoreceptor cells of the carotid body. Typically seen after the age of 40 years. Carotid body tumors may be functional and secrete catecholamines.

rfbfnG.title: Laryngocele
rfbfnG.description: An air-filled, saccular dilatation of the laryngeal ventricle. May be confined within the larynx (internal laryngocele), and/or can herniate through the thyrohyoid membrane and appear as a lateral neck swelling (external laryngocele).

GfbBnG.title: Posterior triangle of the neck
GfbBnG.description: A triangular region of the neck bordered by the clavicle inferiorly, the sternocleidomastoid muscle anteriorly, and the trapezius muscle posteriorly. The region is subdivided by a belly of the omohyoid muscle into the occipital and the supraclavicular triangles.

tfbXLG.title: Edoxaban
tfbXLG.description: An oral factor Xa inhibitor that is used in the treatment of deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism as well as prophylaxis against stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation.

ufbpLG.title: Portal hypertensive gastropathy
ufbpLG.description: Venous and capillary ectasia resulting from clinically significant portal hypertension. Appears as a mosaic or "snakeskin" pattern on the gastric mucosa on endoscopy. Often asymptomatic but may manifest with chronic blood loss, leading to iron-deficiency anemia or, less commonly, acute bleeding.

Efb8LG.title: Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome
Efb8LG.description: A serious and potentially fatal complication most commonly seen after hematopoietic cell transplantation. Characterized by hepatic venule obstruction that causes sinusoidal congestion and hepatic ischemia, leading to hepatomegaly, right upper quadrant pain, jaundice, weight gain due to fluid retention, portal hypertension, and ascites. Thought to be related to hepatic venous endothelial damage.

vfbALG.title: Hepatic sinusoid
vfbALG.description: A blood vessel in the liver that is fenestrated, which allows oxygen-rich blood from the hepatic artery to mix with nutrient-rich blood of the portal vein. Separated from hepatocytes by a plasma-rich space called the perisinusoidal space (of Disse).

media.title: Hepatic microstructure: sinusoids, perisinusoidal space, and hepatocytes

Dfb1oG.title: Hepatic hydrothorax
Dfb1oG.description: A pleural effusion that develops in a patient with cirrhosis in whom other causes of pleural effusion have been ruled out. Although the exact pathophysiology of this condition is not fully understood, it most likely results from the transdiaphragmatic passage of ascitic fluid through small diaphragmatic defects. Manifestations include fatigue, dyspnea, nonproductive cough, and pleuritic chest pain.

CfbqoG.title: Poiseuille equation
CfbqoG.description: A physical law that describes flow through vessels. Defined as: R = 8Lη/(πr^4); where R: resistance to flow, L: length of the vessel, η: viscosity, and r: radius of the vessel. Because resistance is inversely proportional to the radius raised to the fourth power, small changes in vessel radius can have large effects on resistance.

xfbEoG.title: Intracranial pressure
xfbEoG.description: The pressure within the cranium, including its compartments (e.g., the subarachnoid space and the ventricles). It is determined by the volume of the components of the cranium, i.e., brain, cerebrospinal fluid, and blood. Normal pressures range from 7 to 15 mm Hg.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Summary

BfbzoG.title: Urinary nitrite
BfbzoG.description: A test used in the diagnosis of urinary tract infections (UTIs). Positive nitrites indicate the presence of bacteria (most commonly gram-negative), which convert endogenous nitrates to nitrites. A negative nitrite test does not rule out UTI, since several pathogens that cause UTIs (e.g., enterococci species) do not convert nitrates to nitrites.

yfbdKG.title: Schwann cell
yfbdKG.description: A type of glial cell that myelinates the axons of motor and sensory peripheral neurons. Disorders of these cells include neoplasms (e.g., schwannoma, acoustic neuroma) and demyelinating disorders (e.g., Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease, Guillain–Barré syndrome).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

_fb5KG.title: Transplant rejection
_fb5KG.description: A posttransplant disorder in which graft tissue is attacked by humoral and cell-mediated immune responses in the recipient. There are three types of graft rejection: hyperacute rejection (< 48 hours after transplantation), acute rejection (< 6 months after transplantation), and chronic rejection (> 6 months after transplantation). Characteristic signs include pain and swelling in the graft region and loss of organ function. HLA antigen matching of the donor and recipient reduce the possibility of graft rejection.

zfbrKG.title: Calamine lotion
zfbrKG.description: A topical skin moisturizer and protectant frequently used to treat superficial burns or to reduce symptoms of pruritus.

-fbDKG.title: Hematopoietic stem cell
