-fbDKG.description: A type of pluripotent stem cell that can differentiate into all types of blood cells. Located in the bone marrow.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Bone marrow and hematopoiesis

ZTbZ6G.title: First-degree burn
ZTbZ6G.description: A burn that involves only the superficial epidermis. Typically painful, erythematous, and blanchable, with quick capillary refill. Usually heals within 3–6 days without scarring.

0Tbe6G.title: Thyroid peroxidase
0Tbe6G.description: An enzyme in the thyroid gland which catalyzes the addition of iodine onto thyroglobulin to make thyroxine (T4) or triiodothyronine (T3).

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Function

aTbQ6G.title: Pseudoachalasia
aTbQ6G.description: A condition characterized by symptoms and diagnostic findings (e.g., impaired LES relaxation) that mimic achalasia but are caused by another condition, e.g., malignancy (most common), Chagas disease, amyloidosis, and sarcoidosis.

YTbn6G.title: 4th-degree burn
YTbn6G.description: A burn that involves structures deeper than the dermis (e.g., fat, muscle, tendon, fascia), resulting in charred tissue.

cTbapG.title: Prostaglandin E1
cTbapG.description: An eicosanoid that induces vascular smooth muscle relaxation, leading to vasodilation. Synthetic forms are used to treat erectile dysfunction and maintain a patent ductus arteriosus.

WTbPpG.title: Trazodone
WTbPpG.description: An atypical antidepressant that functions via serotonin reuptake inhibition and antagonism as well as H1-receptor and α1-receptor antagonism. Used for the treatment of depression, insomnia, and generalized anxiety disorder. May cause priapism.

destinations.label: Antidepressants → Serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitors

dTbopG.title: Isograft
dTbopG.description: A tissue or organ from a genetically identical individual (identical twin).

gTbFJG.title: Stem cell engraftment
gTbFJG.description: The anatomical and functional incorporation of transfused hematopoietic stem cells in the recipient's bone marrow. Most commonly defined as 3 consecutive days with an absolute neutrophil count > 500/µl. Usually occurs within 2-4 weeks after stem cell transplantation.

STbyJG.title: Anorectal manometry
STbyJG.description: A test used to evaluate anorectal physiology (e.g., anal pressure and anorectal reflexes). Usually performed in combination with rectal sensory and balloon expulsion tests. Indications include evaluation of chronic constipation, fecal incontinence, and Hirschsprung disease.

3TbSqG.title: Romiplostim
3TbSqG.description: A thrombopoietin agonist that increases platelet production by stimulating megakaryocytes in the bone marrow. Used in the treatment of ITP and in certain thrombocytopenias of other origins.

iTbJqG.title: Costochondritis
iTbJqG.description: Inflammation of the costochondral and/or sternocostal joints. Associated with excessive or repetitive exercise and with minor chest wall trauma. Manifests as sharp, well-localized chest wall tenderness that is reproducible with palpation. Typically self-limited; management is supportive.

QTbuqG.title: Nil per os
QTbuqG.description: A term used to indicate that nothing (e.g., medications, food) should be taken by mouth. Often used as a dietary restriction order in patients at risk of adverse events from oral intake (e.g., risk of aspiration, anticipated general anesthesia, recent GI tract surgery, conditions requiring bowel rest).

jTb_qG.title: Meatal stenosis
jTb_qG.description: A narrowing of the ventral meatus that causes a thin urinary stream and straining with urination. Most commonly caused by circumcision but may also occur as a congenital malformation.

destinations.label: Abnormalities of the male urethra and webbed penis → Hypospadias

kTbmIG.title: Intrathecal chemotherapy
kTbmIG.description: A procedure to introduce antineoplastic drugs directly into the subarachnoid space via lumbar puncture or a device placed under the scalp (Ommaya reservoir). Used to treat or prevent tumors that invade the central nervous system (e.g., lymphomas, leukemia, leptomeningeal metastases).

OTbIIG.title: Estrogen
OTbIIG.description: A steroid hormone produced in the ovaries and, to a lesser degree, in the adrenal glands and adipose tissue. Essential for development of the female reproductive system and secondary sexual characteristics. Also plays a role in bone metabolism and liver function.

lTbvIG.title: Primary CNS lymphoma
lTbvIG.description: A rare malignant tumor that arises from the lymphatic tissue of the central nervous system. Most often a non-Hodgkin lymphoma of B-cell type. Immunosuppression and EBV infections are important risk factors.

NTb-IG.title: Cardiomegaly
NTb-IG.description: An enlarged heart. Can be caused by a variety of conditions such as persistent high blood pressure.

media.title: Enlarged cardiac silhouette and left pleural effusion
Cardiomegaly and prominent thoracic aorta in aortic regurgitation

mTbVrG.title: Stereotactic radiosurgery
mTbVrG.description: The precise delivery of a single high dose of radiation to a small focused area, e.g., to treat brain tumors.

5TbirG.title: Stereotactic radiotherapy
5TbirG.description: The precise delivery of multiple doses of radiation to a targeted area. Originally developed for intracranial tumors but increasingly used for extracranial neoplasms. Can treat larger areas than stereotactic radiosurgery.

MTbMrG.title: Whole-brain radiotherapy
MTbMrG.description: A type of external beam radiation therapy in which the entire brain is irradiated over the course of a few weeks. Used as palliative therapy in patients with multiple brain metastases.

nTb7rG.title: Battle sign
nTb7rG.description: Ecchymosis overlying the mastoid process caused by basilar skull fracture that involves the petrous part of the temporal bone.

LTbwrG.title: Diagnostic peritoneal lavage
LTbwrG.description: A diagnostic test used to assess for bleeding or viscus perforation in abdominal trauma. Highly sensitive, but invasive. Performed by placing a catheter into the abdomen, aspirating, then instilling a liter of warm saline. If fecal matter or significant blood is detected, this constitutes a positive test and emergent laparotomy is indicated.

oTb07G.title: Imaging-guided percutaneous drainage
oTb07G.description: A minimally-invasive procedure in which imaging (usually CT) is used to guide a needle through the skin in order to drain the contents of a cyst, abscess, or other such structure while avoiding damage to surrounding organs.

KTbU7G.title: Labetalol
KTbU7G.description: An adrenergic blocker with nonselective β antagonism (both β1 and β2 receptors) and some α1 antagonism.

pTbL7G.title: Prostacyclin
pTbL7G.description: A lipid-derived compound that stimulates vasodilation by inducing smooth muscle relaxation. It also inhibits platelet aggregation.

JTbs7G.title: Ecthyma gangrenosum
JTbs7G.description: An ulcerated skin lesion that invades the epidermis and dermis into the arteries and veins. Most commonly seen in immunocompromised patients with Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia. Other causative pathogens include E. coli, Proteus, and methicillin-resistant S. epidermidis. Associated with life-threatening septic shock.

destinations.label: Skin and soft tissue infections → Differential diagnoses

ITbYHG.title: Oropharyngeal dysphagia
ITbYHG.description: Difficulty propelling a food bolus from the oral cavity into the pharynx, or from the pharynx into the upper esophagus. Common causes include Ludwig angina, cranial nerve IX and/or X palsy, oropharyngeal carcinoma, congenital webs, and Zenker diverticulum. Patients typically present with dysphagia early in the swallowing process, coughing, choking, and nasal regurgitation.

rTbfHG.title: Esophageal dysphagia
rTbfHG.description: Difficulty propelling a food bolus through the esophagus, either due to a disorder of peristalsis (e.g., diffuse esophageal spasm, achalasia) or an obstructive lesion (e.g., esophageal carcinoma).

HTbKHG.title: Nonobstructive atelectasis
HTbKHG.description: A subtype of atelectasis that is not caused by airway obstruction. Includes compression atelectasis, adhesive atelectasis, cicatrization atelectasis, relaxation atelectasis, and replacement atelectasis.

GTbBHG.title: Raccoon eyes
GTbBHG.description:
1) A term for bilateral bruising of the periorbital skin, which is a classic sign of basilar skull fracture. Unilateral raccoon eye is associated with orbital fracture (can also be bilateral).

2) An alternate term for the heliotrope rash seen in rheumatological diseases (e.g., dermatomyositis, polymyositis)

tTbXsG.title: Vitamin B₆
tTbXsG.description: A water soluble coenzyme whose roles include amino acid metabolism, glycogenolysis, heme synthesis, sphingolipid synthesis, conversion of tryptophan to niacin, and neurotransmitter synthesis.

8TbOsG.title: Frog-leg lateral view
8TbOsG.description: A lateral x-ray view of the hip taken with the hip flexed and abducted. Often used as an initial diagnostic study for slipped capital femoral epiphysis or avascular necrosis of the hip.

ETb8sG.title: Pharyngitis
ETb8sG.description: An inflammation of the pharynx. It can arise in combination with inflammation of the pharyngeal tonsils; for this reason, the terms tonsillitis and pharyngitis are often used interchangeably or in combination (tonsillopharyngitis). It is commonly caused by viruses and group A streptococci.

DTb1GG.title: Joint effusion
DTb1GG.description: The presence of an increased amount of fluid (e.g., pus, blood, inflammatory infiltrate) within the synovial compartment of a joint. Etiologies include inflammation, infection, and trauma. Diagnostic workup typically includes aspiration and analysis of fluid contents.

media.title: MRI image of suprapatellar joint effusion and intact posterior cruciate ligament of the knee

wTbhGG.title: White blood cell count
wTbhGG.description: A laboratory result that measures cells of the immune system. It helps to determine how or if the body is responding to a pathological state. For example, a high count may indicate an infection, inflammation, or hematogenous malignancy. A low count may indicate an autoimmune disease, an infection that targets immune cells, or immunosuppressive medication.

xTbEGG.title: Triple bubble sign
xTbEGG.description: A radiographic sign seen on abdominal ultrasound/x-ray in patients with jejunal atresia. The three bubbles correlate with the distended stomach, duodenum, and jejunum proximal to the obstruction.

destinations.label: Congenital visceral malformations → Jejunal atresia and ileal atresia

media.title: Triple bubble sign in jejunal atresia

BTbzGG.title: Jejunal atresia
BTbzGG.description: A malformation with complete occlusion or absence of the jejunal lumen. Manifests in neonates with a distended upper abdomen, delayed meconium passage, bilious vomiting, and a triple bubble sign on x-ray.

destinations.label: Congenital visceral malformations → Jejunal atresia and ileal atresia

media.title: Triple bubble sign in jejunal atresia
Triple bubble sign in jejunal atresia

ATbRtG.title: Cecostomy tube
ATbRtG.description: A device used to decompress the colon. The tube is inserted through the skin into the colon and allows air in the colon to escape through the abdominal wall. It can also be used to irrigate and flush the colon, promoting the passage of feces through the bowel.

_Tb5tG.title: Thalassemia
_Tb5tG.description: A group of hereditary diseases in which defective hemoglobin chain synthesis results in ineffective hematopoiesis.

zTbrtG.title: Myotome
zTbrtG.description: A group of muscles that are innervated by a single spinal nerve root

-TbDtG.title: Corkscrew sign
-TbDtG.description: A radiographic sign of midgut volvulus seen on upper gastrointestinal contrast series. Describes a spiral pattern of the distal duodenum and proximal jejunum at the site of the volvulus.

destinations.label: Intestinal malrotation, midgut volvulus, and gastric volvulus → Midgut volvulus
Intestinal malrotation, midgut volvulus, and gastric volvulus → Overview

0gbeFG.title: Decompressive craniectomy
0gbeFG.description: A neurosurgical procedure in which part of the skull (bone flap) is removed to manage refractory intracranial hypertension (e.g., due to posttraumatic cerebral edema). The excised bone flap is replaced (cranioplasty) once intracranial pressure normalizes.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Treatment

agbQFG.title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy
agbQFG.description: A treatment involving the inhalation of 100% oxygen in a pressurized room or chamber. Used to treat a number of conditions, including environmental injuries (e.g., burns, carbon monoxide poisoning, decompression illness, acute mountain sickness), complex wounds, and infections.

YgbnFG.title: Peritoneal carcinomatosis
YgbnFG.description: A terminal feature of abdominal cancers (commonly of the ovary, appendix, or the colon) characterized by seeding of the tumor to the peritoneum.

media.title: Peritoneal carcinomatosis in a patient with pancreatic cancer

bgbHFG.title: Hemoglobin F
bgbHFG.description: A hemoglobin protein variant made up of two alpha chains and two gamma chains that is the dominant type in fetal circulation and persists in newborn circulation for approximately 6 months. It has a higher affinity for oxygen than adult hemoglobin.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

Xgb9FG.title: Hemoglobin S
Xgb9FG.description: A hemoglobin protein variant present in sickle cell disease and individuals with sickle cell trait. Composed of two alpha subunits and two mutated beta subunits. The mutations result in proteins that have an increased tendency to polymerize into chains, which then deform red blood cells.

cgba8G.title: Red cell aplasia
cgba8G.description: A bone marrow disorder involving an isolated decline of red blood cells produced by the bone marrow; it is thought to be mediated by an autoimmune reaction that may be triggered by malignancy, drugs, or infection.

1gb28G.title: Transient aplastic crisis
1gb28G.description: A condition in which red blood cell production (erythropoiesis) is temporarily suppressed; this may be due to viral infection, especially with parvovirus B-19 in patients with hemolytic anemias (e.g., sickle cell disease, thalassemias).

WgbP8G.title: Bridging anticoagulation
WgbP8G.description: The temporary administration of a short-acting anticoagulant, typically a low molecular weight heparin (LMWH). Used when anticoagulants need to be discontinued transiently (e.g., periprocedural discontinuation of warfarin) and during the initiation of warfarin therapy, when LMWH is administered in parallel with warfarin therapy until adequate anticoagulation is achieved.

destinations.label: Periprocedural management of oral anticoagulant therapy → Periprocedural management of VKAs

dgbo8G.title: Prostaglandins
dgbo8G.description: A group of signaling molecules derived from arachidonic acid with a wide variety of functions, including inflammation and cervical ripening.

VgbG8G.title: Ductal-dependent congenital heart disease
VgbG8G.description: A group of congenital heart diseases that require a patent ductus arteriosus to sustain life. Depending on the underlying lesion, the ductus arteriosus functions to supply either pulmonary circulation (critical right heart obstruction), systemic circulation (critical left heart obstruction), or mixing of blood (parallel circulation). Many cyanotic heart diseases are ductus-dependent (e.g., hypoplastic left heart syndrome, transposition of the great arteries, tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia).

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Overview of cyanotic congenital heart defects

egbx8G.title: Ductus arteriosus
egbx8G.description: A fetal vascular connection between the main pulmonary artery and the aorta that functions to divert blood from the lungs in utero. Normally, the ductus constricts and involutes soon after birth (into the ligamentum arteriosum), but it may remain patent in some congenital heart diseases.

destinations.label: Prenatal and postnatal physiology →  Fetal circulation

UgbbuG.title: Subacromial lidocaine injection test
UgbbuG.description: A diagnostic and therapeutic procedure that can be used in the evaluation of patients with undifferentiated shoulder pain. Lidocaine is injected into the subacromial space in an attempt to distinguish subacromial impingement syndrome (e.g., subacromial bursitis, rotator cuff tendinopathy) from glenohumeral joint pathology. Pain relief from injection suggests subacromial impingement syndrome. Improves the specificity of Neer test but decreases the sensitivity.

destinations.label: Soft tissue lesions of the shoulder → Subacromial impingement syndrome

2gbTuG.title: Rotator cuff tendinopathy
2gbTuG.description: A chronic degeneration of one or more rotator cuff tendons. Potential causes include overuse (e.g., seen in manual laborers, athletes) and/or extrinsic trauma (e.g., friction from nearby bony structures).

destinations.label: Soft tissue lesions of the shoulder → Rotator cuff disease

fgbkuG.title: Hemophilia
fgbkuG.description: An inherited bleeding disorder caused by deficiency in coagulation factor VIII (hemophilia A), IX (hemophilia B), or XI (hemophilia C).

Tgb6uG.title: Hemophilia C
Tgb6uG.description: An autosomal recessive disorder causing clotting factor XI deficiency. Results in a bleeding diathesis. Especially common in Ashkenazi Jews.

ggbFuG.title: Schistocyte
ggbFuG.description: A sheared erythrocyte fragment seen on peripheral blood smear. Causes include DIC, TTP/HUS, HELLP syndrome, and mechanical heart valves.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

SgbyuG.title: Choledochal cyst
SgbyuG.description: A rare premalignant condition characterized by cystic dilatation of the biliary tree. Commonly manifests in early childhood with obstructive jaundice and a palpable mass in the right upper quadrant (RUQ). Older children and adults often present with RUQ pain or symptoms of associated complications, e.g., pancreatitis. The risk of progressing to cholangiocarcinoma is high and complete excision is advised.

hgbcEG.title: Danazol
hgbcEG.description: An androgen agonist that mainly works by lowering LH and FSH secretion from the pituitary gland. Used to treat conditions such as endometriosis, fibrocystic breast disease, hereditary angioedema, and immune thrombocytopenic purpura.

3gbSEG.title: Urine specific gravity
3gbSEG.description: The ratio of urine density to water density; normal range is 1.005-1.030. Typically correlates with urine osmolality and is routinely included in urinalysis. Large molecules such as glucose or radiocontrast media can increase urine specific gravity despite a normal urine osmolality. Conditions that can cause high urine specific gravity include volume loss and heart failure. Conditions that can cause low urine specific gravity include renal failure and diabetes insipidus.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

igbJEG.title: Saccular aneurysm
igbJEG.description: A berry- or sack-shaped protrusion of a cranial artery, typically where cerebral arteries exit the circle of Willis. Risk factors for development include hypertension, smoking, and genetic predisposition (e.g., connective tissue disorders). Can rupture, which is the most common cause of nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage.

QgbuEG.title: Senile osteoporosis
QgbuEG.description: A geriatric syndrome characterized by loss of both trabecular (spongy) and cortical (hard) bone, as well as calcium deficiency. Typically occurs after age 70. Thought to be linked to zinc deficiency, leading to an increase of endogenous heparin, causing mast cell degranulation and increase in bone resorption by prostaglandin E2. Dietary calcium deficiency and decreased Vitamin D metabolism are also thought to contribute to the pathogenesis.

jgb_EG.title: Postmenopausal osteoporosis
jgb_EG.description: A loss of estrogen after menopause increases osteoclast maturation, causing more bone resorption compared to bone formation. Bone loss mainly involves trabecular (spongy) bone rather than cortical (hard) bone.

PgbWvG.title: Secondary osteoporosis
PgbWvG.description: An increased bone loss as a result of medical conditions that cause increased bone remodeling. Medical causes may include kidney disease, cancer (e.g., multiple myeloma), malabsorption, corticosteroids, hyperthyroidism, and inflammatory arthritis.

4gb3vG.title: Osteoclasts
4gb3vG.description: The cells in bone tissue that break down bone matrix in the process of bone remodeling.

kgbmvG.title: Selective bowel decontamination
kgbmvG.description: The administration of antimicrobial agents to reduce the burden of aerobic gram-negative bacteria and yeast in the intestinal tract to prevent infections caused by these organisms. Used preoperatively for patients receiving liver transplants

lgbvvG.title: Septoplasty
lgbvvG.description: A surgical procedure that corrects a deviation of the bone or cartilage of the nasal septum.

Ngb-vG.title: Esophagoscopy
Ngb-vG.description: A diagnostic test in which a flexible endoscope is inserted through the mouth into the esophagus in order to visualize the esophageal mucosa down to the gastroesophageal junction.

5gbiDG.title: Axillary radiograph of the shoulder
5gbiDG.description: A lateral radiograph in which the x-ray is directed toward the patient's axilla. This view can reveal a posterior shoulder dislocation because it focuses on the relationship of the head of the humerus to the glenoid fossa of the scapula.

MgbMDG.title: Anisometropia
MgbMDG.description: A condition in which the eyes have unequal refractive power. Can be caused by astigmatism and asymmetric hyperopia and myopia.

ngb7DG.title: Glenoid fossa
ngb7DG.description: A shallow depression in a bone that another bone fits into: e.g., the head of the humerus fits into the glenoid fossa of the scapula.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

LgbwDG.title: Glenoid labrum
LgbwDG.description: Tissue that encircles the glenoid fossa of the scapula. It stabilizes the humerus within the glenoid fossa.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

media.title: Lateral view of the shoulder joint

ogb0wG.title: Y-view of the shoulder
ogb0wG.description: An x-ray in which the body of the scapula forms the letter "Y" with the coracoid process and the acromion. Most commonly used for diagnosing shoulder dislocations.

6gbjwG.title: Iron deficiency anemia
6gbjwG.description: A type of anemia caused by depleted iron stores, either due to chronic loss (e.g., GI bleeding, menorrhagia), inadequate intake, decreased absorption (e.g., atrophic gastritis, IBD), or increased demand (e.g., during pregnancy). Typically manifests as a microcytic anemia (MCV < 80 fL) but may also be normocytic. Other characteristic laboratory findings include decreased serum ferritin, iron levels, and reticulocyte count.

pgbLwG.title: Hirschberg's test
pgbLwG.description: A test used to evaluate the alignment of the eyes. Involves shining a light at the eyes and observing the location of the light reflex on the cornea in reference to the pupil. Asymmetrical corneal reflections indicate that the visual axes are not aligned (strabismus).

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Concomitant strabismus

JgbswG.title: Vitamin E
JgbswG.description: A fat-soluble vitamin and antioxidant. Deficiency may occur in patients with fat malabsorption (e.g., pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, cholestatic liver disease). Common findings include neuromuscular impairment (e.g., ataxia, hyporeflexia) and hemolytic anemia.

qgbCwG.title: Nerve root
qgbCwG.description: The proximal segment of a nerve as it leaves the brain stem or spinal cord. From the spinal cord, a motor ventral nerve root joins with a sensory dorsal root at each vertebral level to form the spinal nerve.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

IgbY9G.title: Spurling test
IgbY9G.description: A maneuver used to test for cervical spine radiculopathy. Performed by extending and rotating the neck to the side of the pain and applying downward pressure to the head. The test is positive if the limb pain/paresthesia can be reproduced.

rgbf9G.title: Interstitial pregnancy
rgbf9G.description: A pregnancy that occurs outside the uterine cavity in the portion of the fallopian tube that penetrates the muscular layer of the uterus. It has the potential to grow to larger sizes than standard tubal pregnancies and therefore has a higher risk of rupture. Typically associated with a bicornuate uterus.

7gb49G.title: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
7gb49G.description: A progressive, fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by upper and lower motor neuron damage. The initial presentation is highly variable and includes asymmetric limb weakness, fasciculations, and subtle vocal changes. Most patients develop respiratory muscle weakness and dysphagia.

media.title: Clinical features and pathophysiology of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis

HgbK9G.title: Ultrasound-guided thrombin injection
HgbK9G.description: A percutaneous procedure used to treat pseudoaneurysms. Ultrasound is used to guide the needle, through which thrombin is injected directly into the cavity of the pseudoaneurysm. Thrombin initiates rapid formation of blood clots, which stops the bleeding.

destinations.label: Aneurysm → Femoral artery aneurysm and pseudoaneurysm

sgbt9G.title: Ultrasound-guided compression
sgbt9G.description: A technique in which the examiner visualizes the pseudoaneurysm on ultrasound and uses the probe to compress the pseudoaneurysm, which stops the bleeding. Depending on the extent of the pseudoaneurysm, compression may have to be maintained for 30–60 minutes and require multiple sessions. It is therefore time consuming and often painful.

GgbB9G.title: Stent implantation
GgbB9G.description: An endovascular procedure in which a stent is inserted into an obstructed vessel, usually after dilating the occlusion with an angioplasty balloon.

ugbpCG.title: Spinal cord compression
ugbpCG.description: A condition caused by compression of the spinal cord from etiologies such as intervertebral disk prolapse or rupture, tumor, abscess, and hemorrhage. Symptoms include back pain; motor and sensory dysfunction distal to the site of compression (saddle anesthesia); and autonomic symptoms such as bladder and bowel dysfunction, orthostatic hypotension, and loss of sweating below the lesion.

Egb8CG.title: Vacuum dressing
Egb8CG.description: A method of wound care management in which subatmospheric pressures are applied to a wound, increasing blood flow to the area and promoting accelerated wound healing.

media.title: Negative pressure (vacuum-assisted) wound therapy: materials and application

vgbACG.title: Complex meniscus tear
vgbACG.description: A combination of horizontal, longitudinal, and radial meniscus tears.

Dgb1xG.title: Trabecular bone
Dgb1xG.description: A sponge-like bone matrix with numerous cavities, located within the medullary cavity of bones. Composed of bone processes that are arranged along the lines of stress.

wgbhxG.title: Aneurysmal bone cysts
wgbhxG.description: An expansile, well-defined osteolytic lesion with blood-filled cysts that is typically seen in patients 10–20 years of age. The most common sites are the distal ends of the long bones and the vertebrae.

destinations.label: Benign bone tumors → Aneurysmal bone cysts

CgbqxG.title: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
CgbqxG.description: A disease caused by clonal proliferation of Langerhans cells (dendritic cells that arise from bone marrow and migrate to skin and lymphoid tissue). Typically occurs in children. Can cause lytic bone lesions, skin rash, fever, hepatosplenomegaly, and lymphadenopathy.

destinations.label: Benign bone tumors → Langerhans cell histiocytosis

xgbExG.title: Endoscopic ablation
xgbExG.description: A treatment modality for dysplastic tissue that induces destruction of cells by either thermal, chemical, or mechanical energy. Performed during (predominantly upper) endoscopy. Most frequently used in the management of low-grade and high-grade dysplasia in patients with Barrett's esophagus.

BgbzxG.title: Anterior cord syndrome
BgbzxG.description: Damage to the anterior ⅔ of the spinal cord usually as a result of occlusion of the anterior spinal artery (a branch of the aorta). Presents with complete, bilateral paralysis, loss of pain, and loss of temperature sensation below the level of the lesion. Vibration and proprioception are spared (intact dorsal column). Common causes include aortic aneurysms, aortic surgery, hyperflexion injury, and severe disc herniation.

destinations.label: Incomplete spinal cord syndromes → Anterior cord syndrome

ygbdBG.title: Structured exercise therapy
ygbdBG.description: A structured exercise program for the treatment of symptomatic peripheral arterial disease. Patients repeatedly walk or exercise until the onset of claudication and then rest until the pain subsides. This cycle is repeated for 30-45 minutes, three times a week, for a minimum of 12 weeks. Structured exercise therapy has been shown to improve patients' functional status and quality of life.

_gb5BG.title: Esophagectomy
_gb5BG.description: A surgical procedure that removes a part of or the complete esophagus and subsequently creates an anastomosis between the proximal esophagus and the stomach either directly or by using a part of the colon as interposition. Used in the treatment of esophageal cancer.

zgbrBG.title: Potter sequence
zgbrBG.description: A collection of fetal abnormalities caused by oligohydramnios. The classic triad of Potter sequence is craniofacial abnormalities, clubbed feet, and pulmonary hypoplasia. The prognosis of patients born with Potter sequence depends on the root cause of oligohydramnios, but the condition is often deadly due to pulmonary hypoplasia.

-gbDBG.title: Enzyme immunoassay
-gbDBG.description: A diagnostic test that uses an enzyme labeled antibody/antigen to detect a specific antigen (e.g., tumor markers, viruses, drug, other antibodies). The coupled enzyme catalyzes a reaction involving a chromogenic or fluorogenic substrate. The antigen level in the test sample can then be quantified based on the degree of color change or fluorescence.

ZSbZyG.title: Stool acidity test
ZSbZyG.description: A test performed to assess the pH of a stool sample. Stool may be acidic if malabsorption (e.g., due to lactose intolerance or celiac disease) is present.

0SbeyG.title: Fecal lactoferrin concentration
0SbeyG.description: The measure of lactoferrin concentration in the stool, which can be used as a diagnostic tool for inflammatory bowel disease. Lactoferrin is expressed by activated neutrophils in response to acute inflammation; concentration positively correlates with the severity of inflammation.

aSbQyG.title: Ashkenazi Jewish descent
aSbQyG.description: A specific Jewish population associated with a higher frequency of certain conditions including Tay-Sachs disease, Niemann-Pick disease, Gaucher disease, Fanconi anemia, cystic fibrosis, and Crohn disease.

YSbnyG.title: Romano-Ward syndrome
YSbnyG.description: An autosomal dominant disorder of myocardial repolarization that causes congenital long QT syndrome. Causes a long QT interval and increased risk of ventricular tachyarrhythmias and sudden death. Not associated with deafness.

bSbHyG.title: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome
bSbHyG.description: An autosomal recessive form of congenital long QT syndrome. Caused by a mutation in genes KCNQ1 or KCNE1, which encode for potassium channels in the heart and inner ear. Cardiac manifestations include dizziness, syncope, torsade de pointes, and sudden cardiac death. Associated with sensorineural deafness.

XSb9yG.title: Thymoma
XSb9yG.description: A tumor of the thymus gland. An asymptomatic thymoma is usually detected as an incidental finding on a chest x-ray, where it appears as a mediastinal mass. Symptomatic thymomas typically present in individuals between 40–60 years of age with thoracic symptoms (e.g., chest pain, cough, dyspnea) or paraneoplastic syndromes, the most common of which is myasthenia gravis. Treatment options include surgery, chemotherapy, and/or radiotherapy.

1Sb2AG.title: Conversion disorder
1Sb2AG.description: A somatic symptom-related disorder characterized by neurological symptoms (e.g., paralysis, weakness, visual disturbances) that are not explained by a recognized neurological disease or other medical conditions, and are not intentionally produced.

destinations.label: Somatic symptom and related disorders → Functional neurological symptom disorder

WSbPAG.title: Pleural empyema
WSbPAG.description: Empyema is the accumulation of pus within a pre-existing cavity. A pleural empyema is the presence of pus in the pleural cavity, although the term is also used for any pleural effusion in which gram-positive bacteria are present.

dSboAG.title: Congenital glaucoma
dSboAG.description: A condition of glaucoma present at birth found in <1% of children born in the United States. Typically bilateral. Classified into primary (e.g., from sporadic occurrence or autosomal recessive inheritance) and secondary forms (e.g., from trauma, infection, or tumor). Typically presents with buphthalmos, enlarged corneal diameter with corneal clouding, photophobia, and excessive tearing. Treatment involves surgery.

eSbxAG.title: Sumatriptan
eSbxAG.description: A 5-HT receptor agonist that acts by vasoconstriction of (dilated) cranial and basilar arteries. Used for acute treatment of migraine and cluster headaches. Most effective if taken early after the onset of symptoms. Most important adverse effect is a temporary increase in blood pressure.

USbb_G.title: Psoas abscess
USbb_G.description: A collection of pus within the iliopsoas muscle, most commonly caused by S. aureus or E. coli infection. Manifestations include fever, antalgic gait, and lower abdominal/flank pain. Swelling may be palpable in the iliac or inguinal region.

2SbT_G.title: Dihydroergotamine
2SbT_G.description: An ergot alkaloid used for the treatment of migraine and cluster headaches.

fSbk_G.title: Aldosteronoma
fSbk_G.description: A usually benign tumor of the adrenal gland that produces aldosterone and causes signs of hyperaldosteronism.

TSb6_G.title: Abdominoperineal resection
TSb6_G.description: A radical surgical procedure that involves resection of the rectum, sigmoid, and anus, with total mesorectal excision and permanent colostomy. Used in certain patients with rectal carcinoma (if adequate distal resection margins cannot be achieved without compromising the sphincter), adenocarcinoma of the anal canal, and severe perianal Crohn disease.

destinations.label: Colorectal cancer → Treatment of rectal cancer

gSbF_G.title: Incentive spirometer
gSbF_G.description: A medical device that is used to maintain and/or improve lung function, typically during prolonged hospitalization or after surgery. The patient places their lips on the mouthpiece, inhales slowly and deeply to raise the indicator to a specific target, and then holds their breath for at least 5 seconds before exhaling. The indicator shows whether the patient's breathing is too fast, too slow, or within the normal range.

SSby_G.title: Mastalgia
SSby_G.description: Mastalgia is breast pain or discomfort that is often caused by physiological changes (e.g., hormonal effects, lactation) but can also be due to an underlying disease (e.g., benign inflammatory breast conditions).

hSbczG.title: Brain herniation
hSbczG.description: A shift of cerebral tissue from its normal location due to factors that cause mass effect and increased intracranial pressure (e.g., mass lesions, cerebral edema). Subtypes include subfalcine herniation, uncal herniation, and foramen magnum herniation. Clinical features include acutely worsening level of consciousness (e.g., coma), pupillary changes (e.g., ipsilateral mydriasis, fixed dilated pupils), new focal neurologic deficits (e.g., hemiparesis, decerebrate posturing), and cardiorespiratory compromise (e.g., bradycardia, apnea).

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Subtypes and variants

3SbSzG.title: Peritoneum
3SbSzG.description: A serous mesothelial membrane that forms the lining of the abdominopelvic cavity and the outermost layer of most intra-abdominal and pelvic organs. Consists of two layers: parietal peritoneum and visceral peritoneum.

media.title: Peritoneum and fascias of the abdomen

RSblzG.title: Enterotomy
RSblzG.description: A surgical incision into the small or large intestine. Can be part of a surgical procedure or occur as a complication (e.g., during exploratory laparotomy).

iSbJzG.title: Kernohan's syndrome
iSbJzG.description: A syndrome of uncal herniation characterized by paradoxically, ipsilateral weakness (due to contralateral cerebral peduncle compression). This is unusual because commonly, an ipsilateral brain lesion results in contralateral motor symptoms. It occurs in patients with increased ICP caused by intracranial hemorrhage or cerebral edema.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Subtypes and variants

QSbuzG.title: Upper motor neuron
QSbuzG.description: Nerve cells controlling movement, originating in the prefrontal gyrus of the cerebral cortex (primary motor cortex). Long axons sent from these cells form the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts. Most of their fibers cross over to the contralateral side at the pyramidal decussation. The tracts terminate in the anterior horn of the spinal cord or the cranial nerve nuclei of the brainstem, where they synapse with lower motor neurons.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

jSb_zG.title: Ureteropelvic junction
jSb_zG.description: The junction between the ureter and the renal pelvis

PSbW-G.title: Cricothyrotomy
PSbW-G.description: A procedure in which an incision is made in the cricothyroid membrane to allow for insertion of a tracheostomy tube into the airway. Used for emergency airway management after intubation fails or ventilation with a supraglottic airway device is unsuccessful.

OSbI-G.title: Decision-making capacity
OSbI-G.description: A patient's ability to make a specific health care-related decision, which must be evaluated by the physician in the process of obtaining informed consent. The patient must be capable of understanding (1) the information provided and (2) the relevance of the information to his/her specific situation. In addition, the patient must have the ability (3) to make and (4) to communicate a decision.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

NSb--G.title: Bladder cancer
NSb--G.description: A neoplasm of the bladder. The most common type is urothelial cancer, followed by squamous cell carcinomas and adenocarcinomas. More common in males > 65 years, esp. those who have a history of nicotine abuse or exposure to carcinogens (e.g., aniline dye, azo dye, heavy metals). Often presents with painless gross hematuria or irritative voiding symptoms.

KSbU0t.title: Enterocutaneous fistula
KSbU0t.description: An abnormal connection between the lumen of the intestine and the skin, presenting as leakage of intestinal contents through a cutaneous opening; most commonly arises as a complication of abdominal surgery.

JSbs0t.title: Gastric outlet obstruction
JSbs0t.description: A condition of obstruction of the pyloric channel or duodenum by intrinsic or extrinsic factors. Manifestations include postprandial, nonbilious vomiting, early satiety, progressive gastric dilation, weight loss, a succussion splash, and hypokalemic hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis.

qSbC0t.title: SMA syndrome
qSbC0t.description: Proximal small bowel obstruction following compression of the third portion of the duodenum in between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery. Results from a narrowing of the aorto-mesenteric angle which may occur congenitally, or may be acquired following sudden, extreme weight loss.

ISbYat.title: Bouveret syndrome
ISbYat.description: Gastric outlet obstruction secondary to impaction of a gallstone in the pylorus or proximal duodenum. It is considered a very proximal form of gallstone ileus.

rSbfat.title: Pseudokidney sign
rSbfat.description: An ultrasound finding characteristic of intussusception, made up of longitudinal layers of bowel wall resembling a kidney.

sSbtat.title: Core needle biopsy
sSbtat.description: A procedure in which a hollow needle is used to collect a sample of tissue (e.g., breast, prostate, lymph nodes) for evaluation of its histopathological features. It is commonly used to assess suspicious breast lumps, prostate nodules, or abnormal lymph nodes.

GSbBat.title: Breast-conserving surgery
GSbBat.description: An umbrella term used to describe the surgical removal of a portion of breast tissue. Breast-conserving surgery is often used in combination with adjuvant radiation therapy to treat breast cancer. Different terms for this procedure are used (e.g., lumpectomy, partial mastectomy, quadrantectomy), but they are often not stringently defined.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Surgical resection of tumor and breast reconstruction

tSbXYt.title: Gadolinium-based contrast agent
tSbXYt.description: An intravenous contrast agent that can be administered prior to obtaining an MRI to optimize the study. Most is excreted by the kidneys. Associated with a risk of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis.

FSbgYt.title: Implied consent
FSbgYt.description: An exception to the principle of informed consent. In the case of an emergency, physicians may assume the patient consents to a life-saving procedure if the patient is currently incompetent (e.g., unconscious) or if obtaining informed consent will delay the appropriate treatment, seriously harming the patient (e.g., causing death or disability). Does not apply if the patient has previously clearly communicated refusal of the procedure.

8SbOYt.title: Ectopic testis
8SbOYt.description: A congenital abnormality in which the testis is located outside the normal path of descent (e.g., superficial inguinal pouch, suprapubic region, perineum, femoral canal). Associated with increased risk of cancer and infertility. Patients require regular urological evaluation.

uSbpYt.title: Odontogenic infection
uSbpYt.description: An infection arising from either the teeth (most commonly dental caries) or their surrounding tissues (e.g., gingivitis or periodontitis). May lead to local complications, such as an odontogenic abscess and continuous/hematogenous spread.

vSbAYt.title: Nasopalatine duct cyst
vSbAYt.description: A benign cyst that arises from epithelial remnants of the nasopalatine duct, which usually undergoes progressive degeneration during embryologic development. Most patients are asymptomatic.

DSb1bt.title: Necrotizing sialometaplasia
DSb1bt.description: An inflammation of the salivary glands, which often clinically and histologically simulates squamous cell carcinoma or mucoepidermoid carcinoma. Most likely due to ischemia of salivary gland tissue.

wSbhbt.title: Alzheimer disease
wSbhbt.description: A chronic neurodegenerative disorder and the most common cause of dementia. Characterized by progressive behavioral and cognitive dysfunction (e.g., short-term memory loss, impaired attention control and reasoning). Associated with deposition of β-amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles composed of phosphorylated tau (p-tau) protein.

CSbqbt.title: Vibrio vulnificus
CSbqbt.description: A gram-negative, motile, curved bacillus found in salt and brackish water. Causes gastroenteritis, septicemia, and wound infections that can spread rapidly and lead to myositis and necrotizing fasciitis.

xSbEbt.title: Pasteurella multocida
xSbEbt.description: A small, gram-negative coccobacillus that most commonly causes infections in animal bite wounds, especially from cats.

zSbrXt.title: Acalculous cholecystitis
zSbrXt.description: Acute necroinflammatory disorder of the gallbladder without evidence of gallstones or cystic duct obstruction.  Secondary to conditions that result in reduced perfusion and biliary stasis (e.g., multiorgan failure, severe trauma, surgery, sepsis, total parenteral nutrition, prolonged fasting). Usually seen in critically ill patients. Possible symptoms are fever and RUQ tenderness.

-SbDXt.title: Emphysematous cholecystitis
-SbDXt.description: A rare, severe complication of acute cholecystitis caused either by primary or secondary infection of the gallbladder with gas-forming bacteria or necrosis of the gallbladder wall. Elderly, diabetic patients are at especially high risk. The classic diagnostic finding is air in the gallbladder wall on ultrasound or CT.

ZhbZct.title: Ostomy pouch
ZhbZct.description: A bag that is usually taped to the skin to collect bowel contents after an ostomy surgery (e.g., enterostomy or colostomy).

Yhbnct.title: Irrigation
Yhbnct.description: A procedure that involves cleaning a wound (or a body cavity) with a stream of fluid (e.g., normal saline).

chba1t.title: Biatrial enlargement
chba1t.description: Enlargement of both left and right cardiac atria. May be seen in dilated cardiomyopathy, valvular heart disease, restrictive cardiomyopathy, or constrictive pericarditis.

1hb21t.title: Synovial fluid
1hb21t.description: A viscous liquid high in hyaluronic acid produced by joint tissues. Functions include aiding the nutrition of articular cartilage by acting as a transport medium for substances such as glucose and lubricating articular surfaces between joints. Synovial fluid analysis is used in the diagnostic workup of joint infection and inflammation.

dhbo1t.title: Holter monitor
dhbo1t.description: A continuous, ambulatory, battery operated ECG worn by patients for 24-48 hours. Commonly used to diagnose suspected episodic arrhythmia (e.g., recurrent palpitations/syncope).

VhbG1t.title: Sistrunk procedure
VhbG1t.description: The definitive procedure for removal of thyroglossal duct cysts. Involves removal of the cyst, a portion of the hyoid bone, and excision of tissue comprising the path of descent from the foramen cecum.

destinations.label: Congenital neck masses → Thyroglossal duct cyst

ehbx1t.title: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return
ehbx1t.description: A congenital cardiac abnormality in which the pulmonary veins drain into the systemic venous circulation (e.g., the vena cava) rather than the left atrium. Without return of blood to the left heart, there is no systemic circulation. Survival after birth depends on the presence of a right-to-left shunt (usually an atrial septal defect)) to allow for blood to enter the left heart, then systemic circulation. Surgery is the definitive treatment.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Total anomalous pulmonary venous return (TAPVR)

UhbbWt.title: Truncus arteriosus
UhbbWt.description: A part of the developing heart that divides into the pulmonary trunk and aorta.

2hbTWt.title: Left ventricular hypertrophy
2hbTWt.description: An increase in mass of the left ventricle in response to myocardial wall stress. Most commonly seen in chronic hypertension or aortic stenosis (high afterload), but can also result from any condition where there is pressure or volume overload (e.g., aortic regurgitation).

fhbkWt.title: Right ventricular hypertrophy
fhbkWt.description: A thickening of the muscular wall of the right ventricle of the heart, usually due to chronic pumping against increased resistance (e.g., pulmonary stenosis, pulmonary hypertension, chronic lung disease).

media.title: Right ventricular hypertrophy with extreme right-axis deviation

Thb6Wt.title: Brugada pattern
Thb6Wt.description: An ECG pattern associated with Brugada syndrome. Characterized by ST-segment elevation and T wave changes in leads V1-V2. Three distinct subtypes include: 1) J wave ≥ 2 mm, negative T wave, coved type ST elevation with gradually descending terminal portion; 2) J wave ≥ 2 mm, positive or biphasic T wave, saddleback ST elevation with terminal portion elevated ≥ 1 mm; and 3) J wave ≥ 2 mm, positive T wave, saddleback ST elevation with terminal portion elevated < 1 mm.

ghbFWt.title: Peaked T wave
ghbFWt.description: A T wave that is > 5 mm in amplitude in the limb leads or > 10 mm in amplitude in the chest leads. In early myocardial ischemia, tall and broad T waves can be seen in the leads corresponding to the ischemic region. Tall, narrow T waves in all leads can be caused by hyperkalemia.

ShbyWt.title: Hyperacute T wave
ShbyWt.description: A broad-based, symmetric T wave that develops shortly after the onset of myocardial ischemia. Often precedes the appearance of ST-segment elevations.

3hbSdt.title: Balloon embolectomy
3hbSdt.description: A procedure in which a catheter with an inflatable balloon attached to the tip is inserted into an artery. The tip of the catheter is passed beyond the clot. The balloon is then inflated, which allows the clot to be removed when the catheter is withdrawn.

Rhbldt.title: Cardiac output
Rhbldt.description: A measure of the amount of blood volume ejected from the heart, usually measured in liters per minute. Calculated by multiplying the stroke volume (blood volume per heart beat) by the heart rate (beats per minute).

Qhbudt.title: Flexor digitorum profundus
Qhbudt.description: An extrinsic hand muscle that acts to flex the digits. The tendons run through the carpal tunnel and insert on the palmar side of the distal phalanges of each finger.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

jhb_dt.title: Extensor digitorum
jhb_dt.description: An extrinsic extensor muscle of the hand that acts to extend the digits. After the metacarpophalangeal joint, the ED tendons divide into a central band, which inserts on the middle phalanges, and two collateral bands, which insert on the distal phalanges. It is innervated by the posterior interosseus nerve, a branch of the radial nerve.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

media.title: Dorsal extensor aponeurosis and tendons of the hand

mhbVet.title: Basal insulin regimen
mhbVet.description: A type of treatment for type 2 diabetes mellitus that involves the injection of long-acting insulin (e.g., glargine) or intermediate-acting insulin combined with an antidiabetic drug. Indicated for patients with persistently elevated HbA1c levels despite noninsulin antidiabetic therapy.

5hbiet.title: Caudal regression syndrome
5hbiet.description: A congenital condition in which the caudal half of the spine and/or spinal cord do not develop or develop abnormally. The most common manifestations include absent sacrum and coccyx (i.e., sacral agenesis) but affected patients may also show abnormalities in the musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, nervous, and genitourinary systems depending on the anatomic location of the lesion. Could be an isolated condition, associated with pregestational diabetes mellitus, or manifest as part of a syndrome (e.g., VACTERL, OEIS).

destinations.label: Diabetes mellitus in pregnancy → Fetal and neonatal complications of diabetes mellitus in pregnancy

MhbMet.title: Chlorpheniramine
MhbMet.description: A first-generation H1-receptor antagonist. The preferred first-generation H1 blocker in pregnant women.

nhb7et.title: Famotidine
nhb7et.description: An H2 receptor inhibitor that suppresses gastric acid secretion. Used to treat various conditions that cause or are exacerbated by excess acid production (e.g., peptic ulcer disease, gastroesophageal reflux disease)

ohb0Ut.title: Split pleura sign
ohb0Ut.description: A CT scan finding of thickening of visceral and parietal pleura. Caused by fibrin that adheres to the surfaces and subsequent vascular proliferation

KhbUUt.title: TSH receptor
KhbUUt.description: A receptor that is stimulated by the hormone TSH; found on the surface of thyroid follicle cells, adipose cells, and orbital fibroblasts.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Microscopic anatomy

6hbjUt.title: Lipohyalinosis
6hbjUt.description: A narrowing of an artery due to hypertrophy of the media of the vessel wall combined with lipofibrous deposition within the vessel wall. Lipohyalinosis of the vessel walls leads to focal damage, the formation of microaneurysms, and an elevated risk of ruptures. Chronic hypertension is a risk factor.

phbLUt.title: Craniotomy
phbLUt.description: Surgical removal of a piece of the skull (bone flap) > 30 mm in size in order to gain access to the intracranial compartment. The bone flap is replaced before closure of the surgical wound.

JhbsUt.title: Anastomotic stricture
JhbsUt.description: The narrowing of a surgically created anastomotic suture line between two portions of the gastrointestinal tract.

qhbCUt.title: Wedge resection
qhbCUt.description: A form of organ-conserving surgery involving the removal of a triangular portion of tissue. Can be performed for diagnostic as well as therapeutic purposes (e.g., wedge resection of lung or breast cancer).

IhbY2t.title: Fasciculation
IhbY2t.description: A twitching of muscle caused by involuntary, asynchronous contraction of muscle fascicles within a single motor unit (i.e., all fascicles supplied by a single motor neuron). Usually benign but can signify a lower motor neuron lesion when accompanied by other motor deficits.

rhbf2t.title: Interleukin 6
rhbf2t.description: A cytokine produced by monocytes and macrophages that causes fever and production of several acute phase reactants. Due to its short half-life, can be used to monitor patients with severe inflammatory reactions and sepsis.

HhbK2t.title: Mulder sign
HhbK2t.description: A physical examination used to diagnose interdigital neuroma (Morton neuroma). Pain is elicited when medial-lateral pressure is applied to the plantar surface of the foot between the involved metatarsal heads. Displacement of the neuroma from the compressed intermetatarsal space may produce a click or snapping sensation.

shbt2t.title: First metatarsalphalangeal joint sprain
shbt2t.description: A sprain of the ligaments around the first toe. Commonly seen in athletes forced to hyperextend their toe, such as sprinters or football players.

thbXft.title: T wave
thbXft.description: An electrocardiogram waveform that corresponds to ventricular repolarization. Typically ~160 ms long. Concerning morphologic changes include peaked T waves (as seen in hyperkalemia), flattened T waves (as seen in hypokalemia), and inverted T waves (as seen with recent myocardial infarction or ischemia)

Dhb1Tt.title: Renal transplantation
Dhb1Tt.description: The transplantation of a kidney from a living or deceased donor. Indicated in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) as an alternative to hemodialysis. Complications include acute tubular necrosis, graft rejection, infection in the setting of immunosuppressive therapy, and vascular and urological complications.

whbhTt.title: Spinal shock
whbhTt.description: The acute transient loss or depression of all sensorimotor functions and reflexes below the level of a spinal cord injury.

ChbqTt.title: Urushiol-induced dermatitis
ChbqTt.description: Highly pruritic papulovesicular rash due to a type IV hypersensitivity reaction that occurs after skin exposure to urushiol-containing plants such as poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac.

yhbdgt.title: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
yhbdgt.description: A condition characterized by the development of intense pruritus, usually of the palms and soles, during the second and/or third trimesters of pregnancy.

destinations.label: Pregnancy-associated liver diseases → Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy

_hb5gt.title: Hyperparathyroidism
_hb5gt.description: A state of increased secretion of parathyroid hormone (PTH). Primary hyperparathyroidism is usually caused by parathyroid adenomas or hyperplasia, resulting in increased PTH secretion. Secondary hyperparathyroidism occurs in response to decreased serum calcium levels caused by an underlying condition (e.g., CKD). Tertiary hyperparathyroidism occurs as a result of parathyroid gland hyperplasia from untreated secondary hyperparathyroidism.

-hbDgt.title: Right-to-left shunt
-hbDgt.description:
A term that can refer to:
1) A phenomenon in which blood from the right side of the heart flows to the left side due to a cardiac defect.
2) A phenomenon in which blood from the right side of the heart flows through alveoli that are not well ventilated (e.g., in atelectasis), which results in decreased oxygenation to the left side of the heart.

Z3bZSt.title: Atrioventricular septal defect
Z3bZSt.description:
A defect of the atrioventricular valves (i.e., mitral and tricuspid valves) as well as the atrial septum and/or ventricular septum. Because of the left-to-right shunt (through the septal defects), 
pulmonary hypertension and heart failure may eventually develop. AVSD accounts for ~ 5% of all congenital heart defects and is the most common congenital heart defect in patients with Down syndrome.

destinations.label: Acyanotic congenital heart defects → Atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD)

Y3bnSt.title: Gray baby syndrome
Y3bnSt.description: A syndrome associated with chloramphenicol accumulation in newborn (particularly premature) infants (e.g., due to chloramphenicol administration to the mother during pregnancy). Symptoms include hypotension, cyanosis, hypothermia, hypotonia, ashen-gray coloration of the skin, and abdominal distension.

b3bHSt.title: Hunner lesions
b3bHSt.description: Patches of inflammatory bladder wall ulceration. Visible on cystoscopy. Occur in 5–10% of patients with interstitial cystitis.

X3b9St.title: Postoperative urinary retention
X3b9St.description: A failure to void for more than 4 hours after surgery. Risk factors include older age, male sex, use of spinal anesthesia, and lengthy procedures.

W3bPht.title: Genu valgum
W3bPht.description: A misalignment of the lower extremity characterized by inward curving of the leg at the knees, increasing the distance between the ankles. The degree of misalignment can be measured using the hip-knee-ankle angle on radiography. May be a physiological finding in children 3–7 years of age. Pathological causes include rickets, congenital conditions, and trauma.

destinations.label: Angular deformities of the lower extremities → Overview

d3boht.title: Prochlorperazine
d3boht.description: An antiemetic agent that blocks postsynaptic mesolimbic dopaminergic receptors, including the chemoreceptor trigger zone (responsible for vomiting). Also has strong α-antagonist and anticholinergic effects.

V3bGht.title: Doxylamine
V3bGht.description: An H1-receptor antagonist that diminishes vestibular stimulation and depresses labyrinthine function through its central anticholinergic activity. Used as a strong sedative in insomnia and in combination with vitamin B6 in hyperemesis gravidarum. Adverse effects include drowsiness, confusion, dry mouth, blurred vision, reduced bowel sounds, and urinary retention.

23bT3t.title: Fetal hydantoin syndrome
23bT3t.description: A collection of congenital defects including intrauterine growth restriction, microcephaly, craniofacial deformities, nail hypoplasia, and intellectual disability. Usually caused by maternal use of phenytoin or, less commonly, carbamazepine.

g3bF3t.title: Hemiepiphysiodesis
g3bF3t.description: Surgical fusing of the growth plate in children. Used to selectively interrupt growth of a long bone (usually of the leg) to treat angular deformities.

h3bcRt.title: Rheumatic heart disease
h3bcRt.description: Chronic cardiac damage that occurs as a complication of cardiac inflammation and scarring in acute rheumatic fever. Typically manifests with valvular regurgitation or stenosis, most commonly of the mitral valve. Most common in children and young adults in resource-limited areas with inadequate access to health care.

R3blRt.title: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy
R3blRt.description: A minimally-invasive procedure used for the treatment of renal stones > 20 mm. Involves puncturing the renal pelvis calyx under sonographic and radiologic guidance. A nephroscope is then inserted through the puncture, which allows for the introduction of instruments that can fragment and retrieve the stones.

i3bJRt.title: Monospot test
i3bJRt.description: A latex agglutination test that uses red blood cells from horses to detect heterophile antibodies. Typically used to support the diagnosis of Epstein-Barr virus infection. The test is nonspecific and may be false positive (e.g., in patients with previous infection, HIV, autoimmune disease, and viral hepatitis) and false negative (e.g., in patients tested within 1 week of symptom onset, in children < 5 years of age).

Q3buRt.title: Gastric parietal cell
Q3buRt.description: An epithelial cell of the stomach that produces acid (through activity of the H+/K+ ATPase enzyme abundant in the membrane of secretory vesicles) and intrinsic factor (required for vitamin B12 absorption).

j3b_Rt.title: Prerenal acute kidney injury
j3b_Rt.description: The most common form of acute kidney injury. Results from decreased renal blood flow (e.g., due to hypovolemia, hypotension, or renal vasoconstriction/stenosis). BUN:Creatine ratio is greater than 15-20 and fractional excretion of sodium [FENa] is below 1%.

P3bWit.title: Von Willebrand disease
P3bWit.description: A bleeding disorder characterized by deficient or dysfunctional von Willebrand factor (vWF), which is important for platelet adhesion and aggregation, and prevents degradation of Factor VIII. Most commonly caused by inherited mutations and has both autosomal dominant and recessive forms. Typically asymptomatic and associated with normal platelet count and coagulation tests, although prolonged bleeding is common. In severe vWD, PTT may be increased due to Factor VIII deficiency.

43b3it.title: CRAB criteria
43b3it.description: The CRAB criteria indicate organ damage related to multiple myeloma: Calcium increased > 11 mg/dL, Renal insufficiency (creatinine clearance < 40 mL/min or serum creatinine > 2 mg/dL), Anemia (Hb < 10 g/dL), and Bone lesions.

k3bmit.title: Pautrier microabscess
k3bmit.description: Aggregates of atypical CD4+ T-cells within the epidermis that are indicative of mycosis fungoides.

m3bVQt.title: Subhepatic abscess
m3bVQt.description: An abscess that is located directly beneath the liver. Commonly a complication of acute cholecystitis but can also result from perforated ulcers. Manifestations include fever and diffuse abdominal pain and rigidity.

53biQt.title: Peripheral nerve block
53biQt.description: A type of regional anesthesia involving the injection of local anesthetic agents around nerves in the peripheral nervous system to achieve reversible numbing of pain conduction in the corresponding innervated tissue.

M3bMQt.title: Autonomy
M3bMQt.description: A core principle of medical ethics. Refers to the right of patients to make informed decisions about accepting and refusing care, given they have decision-making capacity and legal competence.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Medical ethics

n3b7Qt.title: Beneficence
n3b7Qt.description: A core ethics principle. Refers to health providers taking actions that serve the patient's welfare.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Medical ethics

L3bwQt.title: Justice
L3bwQt.description: A core principle in medical ethics that states that patients should be treated fairly and equitably.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Medical ethics

o3b0jt.title: Endoscopic mucosal resection
o3b0jt.description: The endoscopic resection of a superficial mucosal lesion. Allows for diagnosis, staging, and in some cases treatment of gastrointestinal lesions (e.g., early gastric cancer, sessile colon polyps).

63bjjt.title: Ductogram
63bjjt.description: A mammogram with contrast injection to visualize the breast milk ducts. Provides better resolution of small lesions (compared to a regular mammogram) and helps to guide a core needle biopsy for nonpalpable lesions.

p3bLjt.title: Plantar fasciitis
p3bLjt.description: A common degenerative condition of the plantar fascia that is caused by mechanical overuse, usually related to prolonged standing, elevated BMI, and repetitive activities such as running or dancing. Typically presents with foot/heel pain that is worse in the morning, improves throughout the day, and worsens again in the evening.

media.title: Area of tenderness on palpation in plantar fasciitis

I3bYPt.title: Surrogate decision-maker
I3bYPt.description: A person who makes treatment decisions for a patient who lacks decision-making capacity or competence. Can be designated by the patient prior to loss of capacity (a power of attorney), by the government (a court-appointed guardian), or via default sequence in the absence of a patient- or court-appointed surrogate (sometimes called next-of-kin). Also includes parents or legal guardians of unemancipated minors.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

r3bfPt.title: Medical power of attorney
r3bfPt.description: A legal document in which a patient grants authority to a surrogate to make health care decisions on behalf of the patient in the event that he or she loses decision-making capacity or competence. A type of advance directive.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

73b4Pt.title: Next of kin
73b4Pt.description: A person's closest relative or relatives who, in the absence of a medical power of attorney or living will, serves as a patient's surrogate decision-maker if the patient lacks the capacity to make decisions. In the United States, the legal order of next of kin varies by state but is typically spouse, adult child, parent, adult sibling, close friend.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

H3bKPt.title: Oral advance directive
H3bKPt.description: An oral statement made with full decision-making capacity to a family member or friend stating acceptable interventions and who should act as a surrogate decision-maker in the event of decreased capacity. These statements are considered reliable oral advance directives if there is evidence that the patient (1) was informed about the risks and benefits of the decision, (2) was specific in stating preferences in particular clinical scenarios, and (3) held a steady preference over time, which was repeated to more than one person.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

s3btPt.title: Behavioral therapy
s3btPt.description: A type of psychotherapy focused on eliminating self-destructive or unwanted behaviors.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

G3bBPt.title: Liposuction
G3bBPt.description: A type of cosmetic surgery that involves aspiration of excessive adipose tissue.

t3bX4t.title: Phentermine
t3bX4t.description: A sympathomimetic amine that is used to induce weight loss.

u3bp4t.title: Condylar degeneration
u3bp4t.description: A type of temporomandibular joint disorder that can range from osteoarthritis of the temporomandibular joint condyle to severe condyle reabsorption.

E3b84t.title: Mastoid air cells
E3b84t.description: A group of air-filled spaces within the mastoid process of the temporal bone. Can become opacified on imaging due to fluid accumulation (e.g., from acute or chronic infections of the sinus or ear).

v3bA4t.title: Prostatectomy
v3bA4t.description: The removal of the entire/part of the prostate gland. Referred to as radical prostatectomy, if the capsule and the seminal vesicles are removed as well (e.g., indicated in patients with prostate cancer), or simple prostatectomy if only the obstructive part of the prostate is removed (e.g., performed in benign prostate hypertrophy).

D3b1kt.title: Aneurysm
D3b1kt.description: An abnormal dilation of an artery due to a weakened vessel wall.

media.title: Thrombus from an abdominal aortic aneurysm

93bNkt.title: Vitamin K
93bNkt.description: A fat-soluble vitamin that plays a major role in secondary hemostasis. Key proteins involved in the synthesis of vitamin K dependent factors (factors II, VII, IX, X) and proteins C and S require vitamin K as a cofactor to maintain proper function.

C3bqkt.title: Primary valve ablation
C3bqkt.description: An endoscopic procedure that involves the transurethral incision of posterior urethral valves in the membranous part of the urethra. Referred to as fulguration if a high-frequency electric current is used for incision.

destinations.label: Abnormalities of the male urethra and webbed penis → Posterior urethral valves

x3bEkt.title: Acid-fast bacilli smear microscopy
x3bEkt.description: A rapid test to identify active tuberculosis that involves microscopic examination of specially stained smears to detect acid-fast organisms such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

B3bzkt.title: Nucleic acid amplification test
B3bzkt.description: A test that detects a particular pathogen in a specimen of blood, tissue, or bodily fluid by amplifying the RNA or DNA of the pathogen. Examples include polymerase chain reaction and ligase chain reaction.

y3bdOt.title: Ureteroneocystostomy
y3bdOt.description: A surgical procedure involving the creation of a tunnel in the submucosal layer of the bladder, into which the ureter is reimplanted. Used to correct the retrograde flow of urine in patients with vesicoureteral reflux by improving the flap-valve mechanism of the vesicoureteral junction. The rate of success is nearly 100%.

A3bROt.title: Meatotomy
A3bROt.description: A surgical procedure in which the meatus of the urethra is ventrally incised. Indicated in patients with meatal stenosis.

destinations.label: Abnormalities of the male urethra and webbed penis → Hypospadias

_3b5Ot.title: Vesicostomy
_3b5Ot.description: A surgical procedure in which a connection is formed between the bladder and the outside of the lower abdominal wall to allow for the drainage of urine. Indicated in patients with anatomical (e.g., posterior urethral valves) or functional (e.g., neurogenic bladder) bladder outlet obstruction.

destinations.label: Abnormalities of the male urethra and webbed penis → Posterior urethral valves

z3brOt.title: Subureteric transurethral injection
z3brOt.description: A day-care procedure that involves a cystoscopy-guided injection of a bulking agent (usually dextranomer/hyaluronic acid) below the mucosa of the ureterovesical junction. Corrects vesicoureteral reflux by altering the angle of the intramural ureter.

-3bDOt.title: Urethral diverticulum
-3bDOt.description: A distinct outpouching of the urethral mucosa that most frequently leads to dribbling, dysuria, and dyspareunia. Usually presents in adult women but can also be congenital.

destinations.label: Abnormalities of the male urethra and webbed penis → Hypospadias

ZRbZlt.title: Congenital umbilical hernia
ZRbZlt.description: A congenital malformation that occurs when intra-abdominal contents (most commonly peritoneum) protrude through the umbilicus before complete closure of the umbilical orifice. It is a very common finding in infants, and most umbilical hernias close spontaneously by age 5.

media.title: Congenital malformations of the anterior abdominal wall

YRbnlt.title: BRCA testing
YRbnlt.description: Genetic test to detect mutations on breast cancer susceptibility genes (BRCA1 and BRCA2).

XRb9lt.title: Vitamin K antagonists
XRb9lt.description: A class of oral anticoagulants that inhibit the production of coagulation factors II, VII, IX, and X. The most commonly used medication in this class is warfarin. Use requires regular monitoring of the INR.

cRbaNt.title: Schatzki ring
cRbaNt.description: A narrowing of the lower esophagus caused by a ring of mucosal or muscular tissue resulting in dysphagia, especially to solids. Pathogenesis is unclear, mucosal rings may be peptic strictures occurring as a consequence of gastroesophageal reflux disease.

1Rb2Nt.title: Bougie dilator
1Rb2Nt.description: Tapering cylindrical instrument for introduction into a tubular passage of the body. Used to stretch an area of narrowing (e.g., urethral or esophageal stricture).

dRboNt.title: Esophageal webs
dRboNt.description: Thin membranes of normal esophageal tissue protruding into the esophagus causing symptoms such as dysphagia, odynophagia, and food impaction. Acquired esophageal webs are much more common than congenital webs and are mainly observed in Plummer–Vinson syndrome.

VRbGNt.title: Salicylate toxicity
VRbGNt.description: A state induced by aspirin (or other salicylate) overingestion that causes tinnitus, nausea, vomiting, tachypnea, and respiratory alkalosis (early) or increased anion gap metabolic acidosis (late). Can lead to nephrotoxicity because salicylates are excreted renally.

eRbxNt.title: Conflicts of interest
eRbxNt.description: A circumstance in which an individual's objectivity regarding a primary interest (e.g., patient welfare, objective research) is potentially affected by a secondary interest (e.g., personal financial gain).

destinations.label: Medical professionalism and codes of conduct → Conflicts of interest

URbbmt.title: Do-not-resuscitate orders
URbbmt.description: An order to withhold cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) or advanced cardiac life support (ACLS) for patients who are apneic or in cardiac arrest.

destinations.label: Goals of care → Limitation of life-sustaining treatment

SRbymt.title: Acute wound treatment
SRbymt.description: A process that includes evaluation (e.g., for acute bleeding, damage to neurovascular structures), cleaning, primary or secondary closure (for open wounds, depending on wound characteristics), and analgesia.

3RbS5t.title: Seat belt sign
3RbS5t.description: Typical injury after vehicle collision with ecchymoses on the neck or on the flank caused by the seat belt strap. Indication of possible intra-abdominal injury.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal perforation → Traumatic hollow viscus injury

RRbl5t.title: Cholecystostomy
RRbl5t.description: The placement of a tube into the gallbladder to drain fluid. Often used as a temporizing measure in patients that cannot undergo cholecystectomy (e.g. severely ill patients with acute cholecystitis).

iRbJ5t.title: Retrograde cystography
iRbJ5t.description: An imaging modality that uses x-rays to visualize the bladder after retrograde filling with contrast agent. Indications include evaluation of the bladder for lesions (e.g., diverticula), leakage, or rupture following trauma.

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Imaging techniques

QRbu5t.title: Suprapubic catheter
QRbu5t.description: A thin, flexible, sterile tube that is percutaneously inserted through the abdominal wall just above the pubic symphysis and into the bladder to relieve urinary retention. It may be used intermittently or left in place to continuously drain urine.

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Urinary drainage procedures

media.title: Schematic overview of a suprapubic catheter

PRbWMt.title: Androgen receptor antagonists
PRbWMt.description: A drug that blocks androgens from binding to their receptors, thereby reducing downstream androgenic effects. Used in the management of prostate cancer, hair loss, hirsutism (due to, e.g., polycystic ovary syndrome), and as part of gender-affirming hormone therapy for transgender women.

4Rb3Mt.title: Medical castration
4Rb3Mt.description: Medical suppression of testosterone secretion by preventing the release of gonadotropin hormones from the pituitary. Used in the management of androgen-sensitive localized high-grade or metastatic prostate cancer. Achieved using gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists (e.g., leuprolide, buserelin, goserelin) or antagonists (e.g., degarelix) and can be combined with an antiandrogen (e.g., flutamide) for complete androgen blockade.

ORbIMt.title: Cardiopulmonary death
ORbIMt.description: The irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions.

lRbvMt.title: Older adult abuse
lRbvMt.description: Any form of maltreatment (e.g., physical, psychological, or financial) of an older adult. Includes intentional harm and neglect that results in harm. Most commonly perpetrated by individuals with a longitudinal relationship and responsibility for the older adult (e.g., a caregiver or relative). Physicians are legally and ethically obligated to report suspected older adult abuse in most US states.

NRb-Mt.title: Gastritis
NRb-Mt.description: An acute or chronic inflammation of the lining of the stomach. Manifestations include upper abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, bloating, anorexia, and heartburn.

mRbVnt.title: H. pylori stool antigen test
mRbVnt.description: A test that detects the presence of H. pylori antigens in a stool sample. Can be used for diagnosis of H. pylori infection and proof of eradication post-treatment. Stool antigen testing is preferred over a urea breath test for the diagnosis of H. pylori infection in children.

MRbMnt.title: Heavy alcohol use
MRbMnt.description: A level of alcohol use that increases the risk of negative health consequences but does not meet diagnostic criteria for alcohol use disorder. Defined by the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism as the consumption of ≥ 5 standard drinks per day or ≥ 15 standard drinks per week for men and ≥ 4 standard drinks per day or ≥ 8 standard drinks per week for women.

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Classifications of alcohol use

nRb7nt.title: Sphincter of Oddi dysfunction
nRb7nt.description: Stenosis or dysfunctional motility at the sphincter of Oddi leading to pancreatic or biliary obstruction.

oRb0Lt.title: Intimate partner violence
oRb0Lt.description: A form of physical, sexual, and/or psychological abuse carried out by an intimate current or former partner. Partners may be cohabitants or noncohabitants.

media.title: Bruise on the left upper arm
Multiple bruises on the right lower arm

JRbsLt.title: Number connection test
JRbsLt.description: A test in which patients are timed while connecting numbers in order that are randomly distributed over a piece of paper. Used to test for hepatic encephalopathy (HE), in which increased test time relative to an age-normalized standard increases suspicion for HE.

qRbCLt.title: Paracentesis
qRbCLt.description: A procedure in which a needle or catheter is used to remove ascites fluid from the peritoneal cavity for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes.

media.title: Paracentesis materials, insertion site, and patient positioning

IRbYot.title: Percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography
IRbYot.description: A diagnostic procedure in which contrast material is injected into the bile ducts via transhepatic needle to visualize the entire biliary tree. It also allows for therapeutic interventions such as infected bile drainage and biliary tract stone extraction to be performed, e.g., in patients with acute cholangitis.

rRbfot.title: Superficial spreading melanoma
