rRbfot.description: A type of melanoma that displays relatively prolonged horizontal growth before growing into the deeper layers of skin. The most common type of melanoma (70% of cases). Tends to arise on sites of intermittent, intense sun exposure and appears as a flat, irregularly-bordered macule with variable pigmentation.

7Rb4ot.title: Closed globe contusion
7Rb4ot.description: A closed globe injury from blunt trauma that does not result in full-thickness ocular wall laceration or rupture. Can result in conjunctival and corneal abrasion, ecchymosis, retinal detachment, lens dislocation, and hyphema.

destinations.label: Traumatic eye injuries → Closed globe contusion

sRbtot.title: Reynolds pentad
sRbtot.description: A classic presentation of acute ascending cholangitis consisting of the Charcot triad (RUQ pain, fever, jaundice), hypotension, and altered mental status.

GRbBot.title: Arteriovenous fistula
GRbBot.description: A nonphysiologic connection between an artery and a vein. Can be congenital (e.g., brain arteriovenous malformation) or acquired (e.g., trauma, malignancy, or surgical construction for dialysis access).

tRbXKt.title: Hemofiltration
tRbXKt.description: A renal replacement therapy modality that uses convection and ultrafiltration to remove solutes and water from the patient's blood. Can be used for precise volume control and clearance of molecules of any size (e.g., TNF, interleukins, myoglobin).

destinations.label: Renal replacement therapy → Hemodialysis and hemofiltration

FRbgKt.title: Muscarinic antagonists
FRbgKt.description: A group of anticholinergic drugs that competitively inhibit postganglionic muscarinic receptors and thus have a variety of applications that involve the parasympathetic nervous system. Common indications include asthma, irritable bowel syndrome, and urinary incontinence. Numerous adverse effects are possible, the most common of which is dry mouth. Toxicity results in more severe reactions such as disorientation, hyperthermia, tachycardia, and coma.

8RbOKt.title: Factitious diarrhea
8RbOKt.description: A type of factitious disorder imposed on self in which individuals deliberately produce signs and symptoms (e.g., through laxative abuse) or falsify these (e.g., by adding substances such as water or urine to the stool) for the purpose of deception.

DRb16t.title: Chlorthalidone
DRb16t.description: A thiazide-like diuretic that inhibits sodium and chloride reabsorption in the loop of Henle. Adverse effects include hypokalemia, hypercalcemia, and hyperglycemia.

wRbh6t.title: Encephalitis
wRbh6t.description: An inflammation of the brain parenchyma, most often of viral origin and less frequently due to bacteria, fungi, or autoimmune disorders. Symptoms include headache, confusion, drowsiness, seizure, and focal neurological symptoms.

9RbN6t.title: Acute cerebellitis
9RbN6t.description: An acute inflammation of the cerebellum most commonly following a viral infection (coxsackievirus, echovirus, enteroviruses, EBV, HSV I, VZV, measles, rubella, mumps, parvovirus B19), characterized by a sudden onset of cerebellar dysfunction. Symptoms may include fever, tremor, nystagmus, truncal ataxia, dysarthria, headache, nausea, and vomiting.

CRbq6t.title: Stanford V
CRbq6t.description: A treatment plan for advanced Hodgkin lymphoma that involves combination chemotherapy with doxorubicin, vinblastine, mechlorethamine, vincristine, bleomycin, etoposide, and prednisone.

BRbz6t.title: Cotswolds-modified Ann Arbor system
BRbz6t.description: A modification of the Ann Arbor staging system used for Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The same stages (I-IV) are used with additional identifiers to describe the extent of disease, e.g., "X" is used for bulky disease and stage III is divided into two categories based on the location of intraabdominal disease. It has now largely been replaced by the Lugano staging system.

yRbdpt.title: Stellectomy
yRbdpt.description: Surgical excision of the stellate ganglion, which results in a reduction in the amount of norepinephrine released to the heart. Primarily used as a final treatment option in cases of refractory congenital Long QT syndrome.

-RbDpt.title: Hereditary multiple exostoses
-RbDpt.description: A genetic disorder characterized by the development of multiple osteochondromas. Most commonly caused by autosomal dominant inheritance of a germline mutation in the EXT tumor suppressor gene.

0ibeJt.title: Thyroglossal duct cyst
0ibeJt.description: A remnant of the thyroglossal duct that forms during the embryonic development of the thyroid gland. Typically presents as a painless midline neck mass that elevates with swallowing and tongue protrusion. Diagnosis is made with ultrasound imaging. Treatment involves surgical excision.

destinations.label: Congenital neck masses → Thyroglossal duct cyst

aibQJt.title: Liver hematoma
aibQJt.description: A collection of blood within the liver. Most frequently due to blunt abdominal trauma.

YibnJt.title: Small bowel perforation
YibnJt.description: A hole in the small bowel wall; most frequently caused by infection/inflammation, erosion, or (usually penetrating) trauma.

bibHJt.title: Duodenal hematoma
bibHJt.description: A collection of blood within the duodenal wall. Most common in pediatric patients who have sustained blunt abdominal trauma.

diboqt.title: Peripherally inserted central catheter
diboqt.description: A form of venous access that is inserted peripherally (e.g., in the brachial vein) and advanced until it reaches a larger, more central vein. Mostly used for temporary access, such as outpatient IV antibiotic administration. The placement has fewer procedural risks (e.g., hemothorax, pneumothorax) than other forms of central access. The catheter may remain in place for up to 12 months if long-term therapy is needed.

destinations.label: Vascular access → Long-term central venous access

VibGqt.title: Amsterdam II criteria
VibGqt.description: A clinical guideline used in the diagnosis of hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC). It takes into account a family history of at least 3 relatives with either colon, endometrial, gastric, ovarian, or urothelial cancer. One should be a first-degree relative of the other two. At least two consecutive generations must be affected, and at least one relative must have been diagnosed before 50 years of age. If a patient meets Amsterdam II criteria, genetic testing for mutations in DNA mismatch repair genes should be carried out to make a diagnosis of HNPCC.

eibxqt.title: Intravenous regional anesthesia
eibxqt.description: A type of regional anesthesia involving the intravenous injection of local anesthetic agents into an extremity that has been separated from the central circulation by tourniquets and exsanguinated by compression to achieve reversible numbing of pain conduction and a bloodless surgical field.

2ibTIt.title: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
2ibTIt.description: An acute worsening of the manifestations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (typically characterized by increased frequency or severity of cough, increased sputum volume or change in sputum consistency, and/or increased dyspnea). Caused by an underlying infection (e.g., viral or bacterial pneumonia) in ~ 80% of cases.

destinations.label: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

fibkIt.title: Long-term oxygen therapy
fibkIt.description: A treatment for chronic hypoxia (usually secondary to chronic lung disease). Patients are provided with a low flow (typically 1-2 L/minute) of oxygen for ≥ 15 hours a day to reduce symptoms and improve survival.

destinations.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease → Management of advanced disease

Tib6It.title: Metanephrine
Tib6It.description: A metabolite of catecholamines (e.g., epinephrine and norepinephrine).

gibFIt.title: 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid
gibFIt.description: A serotonin metabolite. Levels are elevated on a 24-hour urine collection in carcinoid syndrome.

3ibSrt.title: Nephrectomy
3ibSrt.description: A procedure that involves the partial or complete surgical removal of one kidney. Indications include benign (e.g., renal stone, pyelonephritis, neglected ureteropelvic junction obstruction, or renal tuberculosis) and malignant (e.g., renal cell carcinoma or Wilms tumor) conditions.

Riblrt.title: Ureteroscopy
Riblrt.description: An endoscopic procedure in which a thin tube with a light and a camera is inserted through the urethra, past the bladder, and into the ureters and renal pelvis. This allows for visualization of the urinary tract for diagnostic purposes. Procedures such as the removal of urinary calculi, treatment of strictures, and collection of biopsy samples can also be performed using ureteroscopy.

iibJrt.title: Hydromorphone
iibJrt.description: A potent synthetic opioid drug primarily used for pain control.

Qiburt.title: Breast-conserving therapy
Qiburt.description: Consists of lumpectomy (breast-conserving surgery) followed by whole-breast radiation therapy. BCT provides better cosmetic outcomes than radical mastectomy with equivalent overall survival rates.

jib_rt.title: Spinal epidural abscess
jib_rt.description: A localized infection in the epidural space surrounding the spine that can lead to spinal compression, thrombosis of nearby veins, and interruption of blood supply. Clinical symptoms include fever, malaise, and point tenderness. Neurologic deficits can also occur.

media.title: Spinal epidural abscess, osteomyelitis, and discitis

4ib37t.title: Urinary tract infections
4ib37t.description: An infection of the urinary system (urethra, bladder, ureters, renal pelvis). Most commonly caused by Enterobacteriaceae, especially Escherichia coli. Typically manifests with suprapubic pain, dysuria, and urinary urgency. Subdivided into uncomplicated and complicated presentations.

kibm7t.title: Multicystic dysplastic kidneys
kibm7t.description: A genetic condition in which the kidney is malformed during development, attributable to abnormal induction of the metanephric mesenchyme. In modern practice, this condition is virtually always diagnosed in utero during regular ultrasound examination; if missed, it may present in early childhood with recurrent urinary tract infections and hydronephrosis of the unaffected side. Bilateral involvement leads to Potter sequence and is incompatible with life.

media.title: Congenital anomalies of the kidneys and urinary tract (CAKUT)

OibI7t.title: Obstructive cystic dysplasia
OibI7t.description: A condition characterized by renal dysplasia and cystic dilatation due to fetal urinary obstruction. Can be asymptomatic in mild cases or cause acute renal failure in severe cases. Manifestations include oligohydramnios during pregnancy and renal cysts that can be seen on ultrasonography.

media.title: Congenital anomalies of the kidneys and urinary tract (CAKUT)

libv7t.title: Breast cyst
libv7t.description: A well-circumscribed collection of fluid within the breast that is influenced by hormonal changes. Usually manifest as single or multiple, sometimes painful, benign breast masses. Most common in premenopausal women.

Nib-7t.title: Gastroparesis
Nib-7t.description: Poor gastric emptying due to non-mechanical obstruction. Typically presents as postprandial fullness, nausea, vomiting, and bloating. Most cases are idiopathic; also associated with diabetes mellitus and upper GI surgery.

mibVHt.title: Tendon suturing
mibVHt.description: A surgical treatment used for tendon repair. Indicated once conservative methods have failed or when there are associated injuries present.

5ibiHt.title: Intraosseous suturing
5ibiHt.description: A suturing technique used to attach bone fragments in injuries such as avulsion fractures.

KibUst.title: CT urography
KibUst.description: An imaging study that uses CT with intravenous contrast to assess the anatomy and, to a certain degree, function of the urinary collecting system, renal calyces, ureters, and bladder. A first-line imaging test to assess for genitourinary abnormalities (e.g., malignancy, stricture).

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Imaging techniques

pibLst.title: Functional tremor
pibLst.description: A complex resting, postural, and/or action tremor with a sudden onset. Worsens under direct observation and diminishes with distraction. Commonly a feature of conversion disorder but may occur in other psychiatric disorders (e.g., anxiety disorders, depression).

Jibsst.title: Adam forward bend test
Jibsst.description: A physical examination maneuver used to screen for scoliosis. While standing with their back exposed, the patient bends forward and reaches for their toes, keeping their knees extended, arms straight, and palms touching. Abnormal findings include spinal curvatures (e.g., rib humps) and anatomical asymmetries (e.g., uneven shoulders, scapulae, hips, and/or skin folds).

qibCst.title: Chloroprocaine
qibCst.description: A short-acting ester-type local anesthetic. Functions by decreasing sodium permeability of neurons, leading to decreased transmission of action potentials.

IibYGt.title: Knee brace
IibYGt.description: Typically used to stabilize the knee after a ligamentous knee injury. Also used after initial treatment of acute patellar dislocation.

7ib4Gt.title: Dystonia
7ib4Gt.description: A movement disorder characterized by sustained or intermittent muscle contractions that can cause involuntary movements and/or fixed postures. Can be idiopathic, hereditary, or acquired. Acquired dystonia can be caused by drugs (especially antipsychotics), metabolic disorders, cerebrovascular disease, and traumatic brain injury.

HibKGt.title: Brain abscess
HibKGt.description: A focal, suppurative lesion in the brain. It may occur as a direct spread from sinus, ear, and/or dental infections; inoculation of pathogens following open skull fractures; brain surgery; and/or hematogenous spread from infective foci.

sibtGt.title: Facial nerve palsy
sibtGt.description: A neurological condition in which motor function of the face is partially or completely lost, depending on the location of the lesion (peripheral or central). Idiopathic in 50% of affected individuals. Specific causes include trauma, infections (e.g., Lyme disease, Herpes zoster, HIV infection), and metabolic disorders.

media.title: Examination findings in facial nerve palsy

GibBGt.title: Peripheral facial nerve palsy
GibBGt.description: Paralysis of the ipsilateral eyelid, forehead, and lower facial muscles caused by a unilateral lesion of the facial nerve between the nuclei and muscles.

media.title: Examination findings in facial nerve palsy

tibXtt.title: Bell's phenomenon
tibXtt.description: Bell's phenomenon is a physiologic, reflexive movement of the eye (upward and outward) that occurs when the eyelid is actively closed. The phenomenon can be observed if the lid is kept open by the examiner, while the patient attempts to actively close it. In cases of severe facial palsy, Bell's phenomenon is more evident (due to lagophthalmos).

vibAtt.title: Neuroma
vibAtt.description: A benign growth of neural tissue that can arise from different types of tissue, such as nerve fibers or their myelin sheath. Can also develop secondary to swelling of a nerve (without neural tissue proliferation) after trauma.

CibqFt.title: Intertrochanteric fracture
CibqFt.description: A type of extracapsular fracture of the femur. Manifestations include hip pain and swelling, a shortened and externally rotated leg, and significant ecchymosis.

xibEFt.title: Otosclerosis
xibEFt.description: The overgrowth of the footplate of the stapes bone in the middle ear leading to progressive fixation of the bone and decreased sound conduction. Usually initially unilateral but becomes bilateral in most cases.

yibd8t.title: Endoureterotomy
yibd8t.description: A surgical procedure that uses an endoscopic technique to open a ureteral stricture (e.g., with electrocautery or laser).

AibR8t.title: Transluminal balloon dilation
AibR8t.description: A method for treating stricture or stenosis of a lumen (e.g., coronary artery stenosis, peripheral vascular disease, ureteral strictures). A catheter with a balloon tip is advanced to the site of stricture or stenosis, and the balloon is then inflated to expand the lumen.

_ib58t.title: Ruptured ovarian cyst
_ib58t.description: A condition in which an ovarian cyst ruptures (e.g., during intense physical activity), which results in the sudden onset of lower abdominal pain. Can result in significant hemorrhage.

zibr8t.title: Cystolitholapaxy
zibr8t.description: The fragmentation of bladder stones into small pieces (e.g., with a stone punch, a small electric wave, or a pneumatic wave). Fragments can then be removed cystoscopically (transurethrally) or through a suprapubic skin incision.

-ibD8t.title: Elevated intracranial pressure
-ibD8t.description: An intracranial pressure > 20 mm Hg that can result in a decrease in cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) and/or herniation of cerebral structures. Manifestations include headache, vomiting, papilledema, diplopia, bradycardia, hypertension, irregular breathing, and altered mental status.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Summary

media.title: Manifestations of increased intracranial pressure in infants

ZQbZut.title: Sodium nitroprusside
ZQbZut.description: An intravenously administered, short-acting nitrate used to treat hypertensive crisis. Releases nitric oxide, which causes arterial and venous dilation. Cyanide and methemoglobin are also released, which can cause cyanide toxicity and methemoglobinemia respectively.

0Qbeut.title: Subfalcine herniation
0Qbeut.description: Herniation of the brain (usually the cingulate gyrus) under the free edge of the falx cerebri due to intracranial hypertension (e.g., from intracranial hemorrhage). Consequent compression of the foramen of Monro causes hydrocephalus and compression of the pericallosal arteries (branches of the anterior cerebral artery) causes ipsilateral stroke, which typically presents with contralateral leg weakness.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Subtypes and variants

aQbQut.title: UVA phototherapy
aQbQut.description: A type of phototherapy used to treat various skin conditions, including atopic dermatitis, using ultraviolet A (UVA; 315–380 nm wavelength), which has antiproliferative and antiinflammatory effects on the skin. Adverse effects include skin aging and increased risk of skin cancers.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Overview of treatment

YQbnut.title: UVB therapy
YQbnut.description: A type of phototherapy used to treat various skin conditions, including psoriasis, vitiligo, and atopic dermatitis, using ultraviolet B, which has antiproliferative and antiinflammatory effects on the skin. Broadband UVB therapy uses a 290–320 nm wavelength; narrowband UVB therapy uses a wavelength of 311–312 nm. Adverse effects include skin aging and increased risk of skin cancers and are less severe with narrowband UVB.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Overview of treatment

bQbHut.title: Pneumatosis intestinalis
bQbHut.description: A radiographic finding of gas within the wall of the intestine. The etiology varies from benign conditions to life-threatening gastrointestinal diseases. In newborns, the finding is considered diagnostic for necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), resulting from intramural gas-producing bacteria.

1Qb2Et.title: Acute abdomen
1Qb2Et.description: Severe abdominal pain lasting for hours to a few days. Causes include intra-abdominal, pelvic, thoracic, and systemic pathologies that may require urgent surgical interventions. Rapid diagnosis and management are crucial.

media.title: Differential diagnoses of acute abdomen by region

WQbPEt.title: Visual analog scale
WQbPEt.description: A tool used to assess the subjective severity of a symptom. Most commonly used to quantify an individual's level of pain, e.g., by indicating the severity on a continuous scale from "no pain" to "worst pain." Other uses include assessment of dyspnea, appetite, and mood.

dQboEt.title: Morphine
dQboEt.description: A potent opioid primarily used to provide effective analgesia for severe acute or chronic pain. Adverse effects include sedation, constipation, strong euphoria (which can quickly lead to addiction), and respiratory depression. Acute morphine intoxication is a potentially life-threatening condition that typically causes altered mental status, severe respiratory depression, and miosis.

VQbGEt.title: Pentazocine
VQbGEt.description: A synthetic opioid that functions as an agonist at the kappa opioid receptors and sigma receptors with weak antagonist action at the mu opioid receptors.

2QbTvt.title: Antiplatelet agents
2QbTvt.description: A group of drugs that inhibit enzymes or receptors required for platelet activation, platelet aggregation, and/or thrombus formation. Includes aspirin (an irreversible cyclooxygenase inhibitor), and P2Y12 receptor antagonists (e.g., clopidogrel, prasugrel, ticagrelor). Used for management of cardiovascular events and prophylaxis of cardiovascular disease.

fQbkvt.title: Bisphosphonates
fQbkvt.description: A family of drugs that inhibit osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. Used to treat hypercalcemia and bone metabolism disorders (e.g., osteoporosis, tumor-induced osteolysis). Examples include zoledronic acid, pamidronate, etidronate, and alendronate.

SQbyvt.title: CT retrograde cystography
SQbyvt.description: Imaging modality using computed tomography to visualize the bladder after retrograde filling with contrast agent. Indications include evaluation of the bladder for postoperative leakage or rupture following trauma.

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Imaging techniques

iQbJDt.title: Auriculotemporal syndrome
iQbJDt.description: A condition characterized by sweating and flushing of the cheek while eating. Can be caused by surgical injury and subsequent regeneration of parasympathetic nerve fibers that transmit gustatory stimuli. The newly developed fibers attach to the sympathetic fibers responsible for the innervation of the sweat glands and the cutaneous blood vessels.

destinations.label: Diseases of the salivary glands → Malignant tumors

QQbuDt.title: Sublingual gland
QQbuDt.description: A salivary gland located medial to the mandible above the mylohyoid muscle and below the sublingual fold. Its main salivary duct ends in the Wharton duct. Produces mainly mucous fluid.

media.title: Tubular secretory elements of the sublingual gland

jQb_Dt.title: Stokes-Adams attacks
jQb_Dt.description: A sudden loss of consciousness, usually without warning and lasting for a few seconds, due to an abnormal heart rhythm (especially complete atrioventricular block).

PQbWwt.title: Port-wine stain
PQbWwt.description: A congenital vascular malformation formed by dilated venules in the dermis. Typically manifests as a well-demarcated, red-purple macule or patch. Commonly located on the face and does not fade spontaneously. Can be seen in association with many vascular syndromes (e.g., Sturge-Weber syndrome, Klippel- Trenaunay syndrome).

destinations.label: Overview of neonatal conditions → Neonatal skin lesions

4Qb3wt.title: Infant
4Qb3wt.description: A child under 1 year of age.

OQbIwt.title: Initial hematuria
OQbIwt.description: Frank blood in the urine that occurs at the beginning of micturtion and clears by the end of micturtion. Usually caused by urethral damage.

lQbvwt.title: Terminal hematuria
lQbvwt.description: The passage of blood or clots in urine during the last part of micturition (when the bladder neck contracts). Suggests a lesion of the prostate or the trigone of the bladder.

NQb-wt.title: Conus medullaris
NQb-wt.description: The tapered, lower end of the spinal cord that is comprised of its sacral segments. The conus medullaris lies at the level of L1 and L2 vertebrae.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

mQbV9t.title: Sturge-Weber syndrome
mQbV9t.description: A rare congenital vascular disorder caused by somatic (and not inherited) mutations in the GNAQ gene that result in capillary-venous malformations. These affect the face, brain, and eyes, manifesting as the characteristic "port wine" stain on the forehead and upper eyelid, along with seizures, intellectual and behavioral problems, and visual defects, among other features.

5Qbi9t.title: von Hippel-Lindau syndrome
5Qbi9t.description: A disease resulting from the deletion of the VHL gene on chromosome 3, which encodes a tumor suppressor. Subsequently, activity of hypoxia inducible factor 1a is increased. VHL is associated with hemangioblastomas, bilateral renal cell carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and renal/pancreatic cysts.

LQbw9t.title: Trigone
LQbw9t.description: A smooth triangular portion of the bladder floor. Bordered ventrally by the bladder neck (and internal urethral opening), dorsolaterally by the ureteral meatuses, and superiorly by the interureteric ridge.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Urinary bladder

JQbsCt.title: Canagliflozin
JQbsCt.description: An antidiabetic drug that reversibly inhibits the sodium-dependent glucose transporter (SGLT-2) in the proximal tubule of the kidneys, which results in polyuria and glycosuria.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

IQbYxt.title: Pharmacogenetics
IQbYxt.description: The study of the effect of genetic variations on drug metabolism and drug action. For example, certain mutations in single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) or human leukocyte antigen (HLA) can alter drug potency (or even toxicity) for an individual compared to the average person.

rQbfxt.title: Necrotizing soft tissue infection
rQbfxt.description: A group of life-threatening infections characterized by soft tissue destruction and systemic toxicity. NSTI subtypes include necrotizing fasciitis, cellulitis, myositis, and clostridial myonecrosis, or gas gangrene.

destinations.label: Skin and soft tissue infections → Necrotizing soft tissue infections (NSTIs)

GQbBxt.title: Lovibond's angle
GQbBxt.description: A physical finding characterized by an angle ≥ 180° between the base of the nail and its surrounding skin, a clinical feature of nail clubbing.

FQbgBt.title: Egophony
FQbgBt.description: A physical examination finding elicited by asking the patient to say "E" while auscultating the lung fields. Characterized by changes on auscultation of an "E" sound to an "A" sound. Suggests the presence of pulmonary consolidation (e.g., from lobar pneumonia).

uQbpBt.title: Bronchovesicular breathing
uQbpBt.description: A normal physiologic breath sound heard on auscultation over the 1st and 2nd intercostal spaces. Characterized by intermediate intensity and pitch through both inspiration and expiration.

vQbABt.title: Crackles
vQbABt.description: A pathologic breath sound on auscultation characterized by discontinuous, intermittent rattling. Etiologies include pneumonia, atelectasis, pulmonary fibrosis, bronchiectasis, interstitial lung disease, and pulmonary edema.

DQb1yt.title: Wheezes
DQb1yt.description: A high-pitched, continuous respiratory sound due to narrowing of the airways below the thoracic inlet (e.g., due to bronchospasm, inflammation, or obstruction). Often heard during expiration in asthma, COPD, anaphylaxis, bronchitis, and foreign body aspiration. May also be heard during inspiration in severe cases.

wQbhyt.title: Rhonchi
wQbhyt.description: A physical examination finding of low-pitched breath sounds on lung auscultation. Caused by secretions and/or obstructions in the airway. Often heard in patients with pneumonia, cystic fibrosis, chronic bronchitis, or COPD.

9QbNyt.title: Pleural friction rub
9QbNyt.description: A pathological breath sound on auscultation finding characterized by scratchy, high-frequency breath sounds. Associated with pleurisy, pneumonia, and pulmonary embolism.

CQbqyt.title: Whispered pectoriloquy
CQbqyt.description: A physical finding elicited by asking the patient to whisper while the examiner auscultates over the lung fields. This is typically barely audible by the examiner but clearly audible in the presence of lung consolidation.

AQbRAt.title: Glycogen storage disease type V
AQbRAt.description: A glycogen storage disease characterized by deficiency of muscle phosphorylase (myophosphorylase), an enzyme necessary for glycogenolysis. Presents with generalized muscle weakness, rhabdomyolysis with myoglobinuria, and exercise intolerance with second wind phenomenon.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Glycogen storage disorders (GSD)

_Qb5At.title: Axillary artery
_Qb5At.description: An artery that is the continuation of the subclavian artery as it crosses the lateral border of the first rib. Supplies blood to the axilla, upper arm, and lateral thorax. The axillary artery then becomes the brachial artery after it passes the lower border of the teres major muscle.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage
Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

zQbrAt.title: Venous cutdown
zQbrAt.description: Emergency procedure that involves the surgical exposure of a vein, typically the saphenous vein, and subsequent insertion of a cannula into the vein under direct vision. The technique is rarely used today since safer techniques have become available (e.g., IO infusion, ultrasound guided central venous catheters).

-QbDAt.title: Intraosseous access
-QbDAt.description: A technique used in emergencies to establish safe access for administering fluids and medications. A needle is inserted through bone cortex into the marrow. A common site of insertion is the proximal anteromedial tibia, but other sites (e.g., femur, humerus) can also be used.

ZjbZ_t.title: Saturday night palsy
ZjbZ_t.description: A condition characterized by radial nerve damage after sitting or sleeping with the arm draped over a seat, especially in the setting of alcohol and/or drug intoxication, or after sleeping while holding another individual who is exerting pressure on the arm. Caused by pressure on the middle of the upper arm along the course of the radial nerve.

0jbe_t.title: Papilledema
0jbe_t.description: A swelling of the optic disc secondary to elevated intracranial pressure

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Papilledema

ajbQ_t.title: Winter formula
ajbQ_t.description: A formula used to determine the expected respiratory compensation in patients with metabolic acidosis. Defined as: Expected pCO₂ (in mm Hg) = (1.5 x HCO3-) + 8 (+/- 2). If the measured value is lower than the expected value, then there is concurrent respiratory alkalosis. If the measured value is higher than the expected value, then there is concurrent respiratory acidosis.

Yjbn_t.title: Leber hereditary optic neuropathy
Yjbn_t.description: An inherited form of optic neuropathy passed from mother to child by mitochondrial DNA (mitochondrial inheritance). Typically presents as subacute visual changes in one or both eyes, usually in young adults. Funduscopic exam typically shows circumpapillary telangectasia.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Mitochondrial myopathies

bjbH_t.title: Wrist drop
bjbH_t.description: Impaired ability to extend the wrist and hand due to high radial nerve palsy. This occurs due to damage or repeated/prolonged compression of the radial nerve at the level of the mid-humerus, where it travels in the spiral groove. Injury mechanisms include mid-humerus fractures, the use of crutches, and Saturday night palsy.

Xjb9_t.title: J point
Xjb9_t.description: The junction point between the end of the QRS complex and the beginning of the ST segment on an ECG. Used to measure ST elevations and ST depressions in reference to the onset of the Q wave.

1jb2zt.title: Peripheral interosseous nerve compression syndrome
1jb2zt.description: A low radial nerve palsy due to compression of the peripheral interosseous nerve, a branch of the radial nerve. Symptoms include paralysis of the finger extensors. Unlike high radial nerve palsies, wrist extensors and sensation are not affected.

WjbPzt.title: High anion gap metabolic acidosis
WjbPzt.description: A metabolic acidosis caused by an increase in the serum concentration of organic acids (normal: 10–16 mmol/L). These organic acids can be endogenous (e.g., lactic acid, ketoacids) or exogenous (e.g., glycolic acid in ethylene glycol poisoning, formic acid in methanol poisoning).

djbozt.title: Degenerative disk disease
djbozt.description: A group of conditions that lead to displacement of the spinal disc into the spinal canal and subsequent compression of either the spinal cord or a nerve root. Symptoms include radicular pain in the distribution of the affected nerve root, paresthesias, muscle weakness, and loss of deep tendon reflexes associated with the affected muscles.

ejbxzt.title: Guanfacine
ejbxzt.description: A selective alpha 2 agonist that acts by inhibiting sympathetic outflow from the central nervous system. It is used to treat attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and hypertensive crisis.

Ujbb-t.title: Dexmedetomidine
Ujbb-t.description: A central alpha 2 agonist used for sedation and anxiolysis. Often used in ICUs for light to moderate sedation with fewer cardiovascular adverse effects than other sedatives (e.g., barbiturates).

Tjb6-t.title: Foreign body in the nose
Tjb6-t.description: An object that has been inserted into the nose, usually by young children or adults with developmental or psychiatric disorders, and often without the caregiver's knowledge. Common foreign bodies include jewelry, food, pebbles, and toys. Animate objects, e.g., insects, are less common but are sometimes found in tropical climates.

hjbcZF.title: Medical errors
hjbcZF.description: An action or failure to act that exposes a patient to possible harm in the context of medical care, regardless of whether or not harm actually occurs.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Management of medical errors

RjblZF.title: Dicloxacillin
RjblZF.description: An antistaphylococcal penicillin that is effective against methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus but not methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).

QjbuZF.title: Nail clubbing
QjbuZF.description: Painless bulbous swelling of the distal phalanges. The nail bed becomes convex and may soften. Typically associated with chronic hypoxemia (e.g., due to cardiac shunts, interstitial lung disease, lung cancer, cystic fibrosis).

PjbW0F.title: Combined spinal and epidural anesthesia
PjbW0F.description: A form of neuraxial anesthesia in which a local anesthetic is injected into both the subarachnoid and epidural spaces, with the catheter remaining in the epidural space for administration of additional doses as needed. Allows for a more rapid onset of analgesia than epidural anesthesia alone. Frequently used during labor and orthopedic procedures. Poses an increased risk of fetal bradycardia.

kjbm0F.title: Jugular venous pressure
kjbm0F.description: A physical examination technique to estimate jugular venous pressure. The patient is placed in supine position with the torso elevated to 45 degrees and the head rotated away from the examiner. Tangential lighting can help elicit the finding. Determine the vertical distance between the upper limit of visible distention of the internal jugular vein and the sternal angle. A distance > 4 cm is considered elevated. Conditions associated with elevated JVP include right-sided heart failure, fluid overload, pulmonary hypertension, cardiac tamponade, and constrictive pericarditis.

media.title: Jugular venous pressure waveforms in common cardiac conditions

OjbI0F.title: Thomas test
OjbI0F.description: A physical examination procedure used to evaluate for hip flexion contracture and iliopsoas hypertonicity. The patient lies supine and brings one knee to their chest. The test is positive if the contralateral hip flexes and the thigh lifts off the table.

destinations.label: Osteoarthritis of the hip and knee → Clinical features

Njb-0F.title: BRCA mutation
Njb-0F.description: An autosomal-dominant inherited gene mutation (BRCA1 or BRCA2) of a tumor suppressor gene that codes for a DNA repair protein. Associated with an increased risk of breast cancer (∼ 70%) and ovarian cancer as well as, to a lesser extent, colon, pancreas, stomach and prostate cancer. BRCA is an abbreviation for BReast CAncer.

mjbVaF.title: Carvallo sign
mjbVaF.description: A phenomenon of changes in cardiac murmur intensity during inspiration. In general, murmurs that arise from the right side of the heart increase in intensity during inspiration. Murmurs that arise from the left side of the heart (except the murmur of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy) decrease in intensity during inspiration.

MjbMaF.title: Thrills
MjbMaF.description: A clinical finding in which a turbulent blood flow (e.g., from a cardiac murmur, aneurysm, or AV fistula) is palpable as a vibration. Cardiac thrills are usually felt over the region where the corresponding murmur is heard best, and their presence correlates positively with the loudness of the murmur.

6jbjYF.title: Percutaneous transhepatic biliary drain
6jbjYF.description: A therapeutic intervention in which infected bile is drained and/or a biliary tract stone is removed via the insertion of a transhepatic needle through the skin. The drain is placed into the biliary tree rather than the gallbladder itself.

pjbLYF.title: Type I collagen
pjbLYF.description: The most common form of collagen in the human body. Found in tendon, ligaments, bone, dermis, and dentin. Collagen is also present in healed scars; in the collagen remodeling phase of wound healing, type III collagen is replaced with type I collagen.

JjbsYF.title: Deviated nasal septum
JjbsYF.description: Displacement of the nasal septum from the midline. Significant deviation can lead to nasal airway obstruction, external nasal deformity, headache, and epistaxis.

qjbCYF.title: Nasal turbinate hypertrophy
qjbCYF.description: Enlargement of the nasal turbinates, which can cause difficulty breathing through the nose.

IjbYbF.title: Cerumen impaction
IjbYbF.description: A buildup of tightly packed cerumen in the external auditory canal that is either symptomatic or prevents visual evaluation of the auditory canal and/or tympanic membrane. Symptoms may be localized (fullness, pain, and/or itching in the ear), audiovestibular (conductive hearing loss, vertigo, tinnitus), and, in some individuals, can include speech delay and/or behavioral changes.

media.title: Cerumen impaction of the left external auditory canal

sjbtbF.title: Silodosin
sjbtbF.description: A selective alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist used to treat benign prostatic hyperplasia. Adverse effects include retrograde ejaculation, orthostatic hypotension, and nasopharyngitis

FjbgXF.title: Rhinoplasty
FjbgXF.description: A surgical procedure to alter the shape of the nose.

8jbOXF.title: Kussmaul sign
8jbOXF.description: A sign characterized by distention of the jugular veins during inspiration (due to elevation of jugular venous pressure). Can be seen in patients with constrictive pericarditis, restrictive cardiomyopathy, right ventricular infarction, and tricuspid stenosis.

Djb1cF.title: Rib notching
Djb1cF.description: A radiographic sign where internal thoracic and intercostal arteries dilate and develop to collaterals in patients with aortic narrowing (e.g., coarctation of the aorta). The increased perfusion leads to pressure atrophy and resorption of the neighboring ribs, which may visualize in chest x-rays as inferior rib notching.

destinations.label: Acyanotic congenital heart defects → Coarctation of the aorta

media.title: Rib notching in coarctation of the aorta

wjbhcF.title: Benazepril
wjbhcF.description: An ACE inhibitor that, like other agents in this class, prevents the conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II. Used to treat hypertension, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, myocardial infarction, and as a nephroprotective medication in patients with diabetes mellitus.

9jbNcF.title: Irbesartan
9jbNcF.description: An angiotensin-receptor blocker used as second-line treatment for the management of hypertension if angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors are not tolerated. Like other agents in this class, functions by inhibiting blocking AT1 receptors, decreasing the binding of angiotensin II. This decreases vasoconstriction, which lowers the blood pressure. Also leads to decreased secretion of aldosterone, causing decreased reabsorption of Na+ and water, which also lowers blood pressure.

xjbEcF.title: Triple-negative breast cancer
xjbEcF.description: A type of breast cancer that does not show overexpression of the following receptors on immunohistochemical staining: estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2). It is often difficult to treat, as many anticancer agents target these receptors.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Staging and receptor testing

yjbd1F.title: Plummer-Vinson syndrome
yjbd1F.description: A condition characterized by the triad of dysphagia, upper esophageal webs, and iron deficiency anemia. Associated with glossitis and increased risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Most commonly presents in white women 40-70 years of age.

AjbR1F.title: Everolimus
AjbR1F.description: An mTOR inhibitor commonly used as an immunosupressant for its suppression of T cell activation and B cell differentiation.

_jb51F.title: Teardrop cells
_jb51F.description: A type of dysmorphic red blood cell characterized by a teardrop shape. Associated with extramedullary hematopoiesis (e.g., from myelofibrosis, thalassemia, splenomegaly).

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

zjbr1F.title: Sickle cells
zjbr1F.description: A red blood cell with a sickle shape (e.g., as seen on blood smear of individuals with sickle cell anemia).

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

media.title: Sickle cell disease with drepanocytes and target cells

-jbD1F.title: Macrocytes
-jbD1F.description: A type of dysmorphic red blood cell characterized by increased size and spherical shape. Often seen in patients with megaloblastic anemia.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

ZPbZWF.title: Spherocytes
ZPbZWF.description: A type of dysmorphic erythrocyte that is sphere-shaped. Most commonly associated with immunologically-mediated hemolytic anemias and hereditary spherocytosis.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

0PbeWF.title: Echinocytes
0PbeWF.description: A type of dysmorphic red blood cell characterized by smooth and evenly spaced cytoplasmic projections. Associated with chronic kidney disease (uremia), liver disease, and pyruvate kinase deficiency.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

aPbQWF.title: Acanthocytes
aPbQWF.description: A type of dysmorphic red blood cell characterized by irregular, thorn-like cytoplasmic projections. The presence of acanthocytes in the blood is associated with hemolytic anemia, myelodysplastic syndromes, splenectomy, and hereditary abetalipoproteinemia. The presence of acanthocytes in the urine indicates glomerular damage.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

YPbnWF.title: Stomatocytes
YPbnWF.description: A type of dysmorphic red blood cell characterized by slit-like central pallor caused by changes in membrane permeability. Associated with hepatic disorders and hemolytic anemias. Also can be due to a hereditary structural defect of the erythrocyte membrane.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

bPbHWF.title: Hereditary abetalipoproteinemia
bPbHWF.description: A rare, autosomal recessive disorder characterized by deficiency of apolipoproteins, which results in low serum concentrations of chylomicrons, LDL, and VLDL. Manifests in early infancy with failure to thrive and fat malabsorption.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

XPb9WF.title: Heinz bodies
XPb9WF.description: A collection of red blood cell inclusions composed of damaged, denatured hemoglobin. This finding on blood smear is classically associated with G6PD deficiency and can coexist with bite cells (the result of splenic macrophages removing the precipitated hemoglobin).

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

cPbadF.title: Basophilic stippling
cPbadF.description: A collection of basophilic granules made of RNA that are seen in erythrocytes. Can develop in a variety of disorders that cause impaired cell division (e.g., lead poisoning, thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia, myelodysplastic syndromes).

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

1Pb2dF.title: Carboxyhemoglobin
1Pb2dF.description: A hemoglobin molecule whose binding site is occupied by carbon monoxide (which binds with much higher affinity than oxygen). Carboxyhemoglobinemia (i.e., carbon monoxide toxicity) causes fatigue, headache, nausea, chest pain, respiratory failure, seizures, and coma. Chronic smokers can have baseline carboxyhemoglobin levels of 10-15%.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen transport and conditions that affect oxygenation

WPbPdF.title: Methemoglobin
WPbPdF.description: A form of hemoglobin that contains iron in its oxidized (ferric, Fe3+) rather than its reduced state (ferrous, Fe2+), typically only 1% of total hemoglobin. Cannot bind oxygen. High levels result in tissue hypoxia.

dPbodF.title: Methemoglobinemia
dPbodF.description: The presence of a supraphysiologic concentration of methemoglobin in the blood. Most commonly caused by medications (e.g., local anesthetics, nitric oxide, or dapsone) or exposure to environmental nitrates or nitrites. Rarer causes include congenital enzyme deficiencies or hemoglobinopathy. Causes tissue hypoxia and brown-colored blood.

VPbGdF.title: Oxyhemoglobin
VPbGdF.description: A hemoglobin protein with oxygen bound to its heme component.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen and carbon dioxide transport

ePbxdF.title: Hyperhomocysteinemia
ePbxdF.description: An increased serum concentration of homocysteine, which increases the risk for developing atherosclerosis and thrombotic disease and thus predisposes to coronary artery disease and stroke.

UPbbVF.title: Sézary syndrome
UPbbVF.description: A condition of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with leukemic dissemination of mutated T cells. Can be an advanced form of mycosis fungoides or arise de novo. Characterized by systemic erythroderma accompanied by palmar and plantar hyperkeratosis, intense pruritus, and generalized lymphadenopathy. Atypical T cells (Sézary cells) can be detected on peripheral blood smear.

2PbTVF.title: Bacterial embolism
2PbTVF.description: An obstruction of a vessel in the systemic or pulmonary arterial circulation by an infectious (i.e., contains microorganisms) thrombus. Most frequently occurs secondary to infective endocarditis.

gPbFVF.title: BUN/creatinine ratio
gPbFVF.description: A ratio of the concentration of blood urea nitrogen to the serum creatinine concentration. Can be used to help identify the cause of acute kidney injury (AKI). A ratio ≥ 20:1 indicates renal hypoperfusion (e.g., hypovolemia, renal artery stenosis) which is referred to as prerenal AKI. A ratio < 15:1 indicates intrinsic renal damage (e.g., glomerulonephritis), which is referred to as intrarenal AKI. A ratio between 10:1 and 20:1 can also be seen in healthy individuals and patients with urinary tract obstruction that causes postrenal AKI.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Renal function test

SPbyVF.title: Waxy casts
SPbyVF.description: Nonspecific finding on urine microscopy that occurs in association with chronic kidney disease or end stage renal failure. Consists of degenerating granular casts of various cell types and indicates severe kidney injury with longstanding reduced urine flow.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

3PbSeF.title: Broad casts
3PbSeF.description: A urinary cast formed in dilated tubules with low flow. Most commonly seen in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease. Similar in appearance to hyaline casts, but wider in size.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

RPbleF.title: Urine dipstick
RPbleF.description: A diagnostic tool comprising a urine test strip with various parameters that change color when placed into urine. Used to rapidly assess for potentially pathological changes. It does not include a microscopic evaluation of the urine.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

kPbmUF.title: Peak flow meter
kPbmUF.description: A device used to measure peak expiratory flow as a marker of lung function. Widely used in ambulatory monitoring of chronic respiratory diseases (e.g., asthma, COPD) and emergency assessment of exacerbations. The reliability of measurements can vary (e.g., due to incorrect technique).

NPb-UF.title: Bevacizumab
NPb-UF.description: A humanized monoclonal antibody against vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) used in the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration and malignancies (e.g., colorectal cancer, renal cell carcinoma). Common adverse effects include gastrointestinal perforation or bleeding, venous thromboembolism, hypertension, and stroke.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

mPbV2F.title: Epispadia
mPbV2F.description: An embryonic malformation typically characterized by an exposed urethra on the dorsal penis (in males) or between the labia and the clitoris (in females). Typically also presents with urinary incontinence and is strongly associated with bladder exstrophy. An acquired form arises from chronic pressure (e.g., as a result of a transurethral indwelling catheter eroding the urethra).

destinations.label: Abnormalities of the male urethra and webbed penis → Epispadias

5Pbi2F.title: Pindolol
5Pbi2F.description: A nonselective beta-blocker (both β1 and β2 receptors) with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity.

nPb72F.title: Nadolol
nPb72F.description: A nonselective beta blocker (both β1 and β2 receptors) without intrinsic sympathomimetic activity.

LPbw2F.title: Esmolol
LPbw2F.description: A cardioselective beta blocker (β1 selective) without intrinsic sympathomimetic activity commonly used in surgery to treat tachycardia and in the acute treatment of supraventricular tachycardia.

oPb0fF.title: Betaxolol
oPb0fF.description: A cardioselective beta blocker (β1 selective) without intrinsic sympathomimetic activity.

IPbYTF.title: Oral rehydration solution
IPbYTF.description: Orally administered electrolyte solution that is used to treat mild-to-moderate dehydration in children. The WHO-recommended low osmolarity solution contains sodium (75 mmol/L), glucose (75 mmol/L), potassium (20 mmol/L), chloride (65 mmol/L), and citrate (10 mmol/L) and has a total osmolarity of 245 mOsm/L.

destinations.label: Dehydration and hypovolemia → Initial fluid therapy for dehydration and hypovolemia

rPbfTF.title: Oral rehydration therapy
rPbfTF.description: Oral fluid replacement with premixed or selfmixed oral rehydration solutions that contain specific amounts of sugar, salt, and water. Used to treat dehydration.

destinations.label: Dehydration and hypovolemia → Initial fluid therapy for dehydration and hypovolemia

HPbKTF.title: Carotid endarterectomy
HPbKTF.description: A surgical procedure in which the inner lining of a carotid artery is removed, along with any associated atherosclerotic deposits. Used to treat high-grade and/or symptomatic carotid stenosis.

sPbtTF.title: Pulmonary endarterectomy
sPbtTF.description: A surgical procedure in which the inner lining of a pulmonary artery is removed, along with any associated deposits. Used in treatment of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.

GPbBTF.title: CEA
GPbBTF.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Carcinoembryonic antigen 
2. Carotid endarterectomy

tPbXgF.title: Pericardiectomy
tPbXgF.description: The complete or partial removal of the pericardium. Used to treat severe or non-transient constrictive pericarditis.

FPbggF.title: Hypertropia
FPbggF.description: A position of the eyes in which one eye is deviated upward (hypertropic) relative to the other eye.

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Basic terms

8PbOgF.title: Superior oblique muscle
8PbOgF.description: An extraocular muscle innervated by the trochlear nerve (CN IV). Functions include intorsion (internal, or medial, rotation), abduction, and depression of an adducted eyeball. It is the only extraocular muscle that can depress an adducted eye.

uPbpgF.title: Radical mastectomy
uPbpgF.description: The surgical removal of breast tissue, pectoralis major, pectoralis minor, and axillary lymph nodes. Historically used to treat breast cancer but now has been largely replaced by less extensive procedures (e.g., modified radical mastectomy, breast-conserving surgery).

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Surgical resection of tumor and breast reconstruction

EPb8gF.title: Ligature marks
EPb8gF.description: Skin marks caused by the application of pressure, e.g., by a rope. They initially appear as a pale furrow with punctiform hematomas and progress to a darker color. If present on the neck, they suggest strangulation. When encountered on other body parts, they may indicate physical abuse.

DPb1SF.title: Phenelzine
DPb1SF.description: An irreversible, nonselective monoamine oxidase inhibitor that is used to treat depression.

wPbhSF.title: Tyramine
wPbhSF.description: A naturally-occurring amino acid that is derived from tyrosine. Acts as a catecholamine-releasing agent. Certain foods rich in tyramine (e.g., red wine, cheese, fava beans) can result in sympathetic overactivity and hypertensive crisis if combined with monoamine oxidase inhibitors.

9PbNSF.title: Dextroamphetamine
9PbNSF.description: An amphetamine derivate that acts as a central nervous stimulant. It can be used to treat attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and narcolepsy, but is also used recreationally.

CPbqSF.title: Kniest syndrome
CPbqSF.description: A rare autosomal dominant form of dwarfism caused by a mutation in the gene responsible for producing type 2 collagen. Patients present with short stature, ocular problems (myopia, cataracts), and hearing abnormalities (hearing loss, recurrent ear infections).

destinations.label: Connective tissue diseases → Inherited connective tissue diseases

xPbESF.title: Hypochrondogenesis
xPbESF.description: A rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in genes encoding type 2 collagen, resulting in severe malformations of bone formation and bone growth. Affected children usually die in utero or shortly after birth because of respiratory failure.

BPbzSF.title: Vertebral burst fracture
BPbzSF.description: A vertebral compression fracture involving displacement of a posterior segment of the vertebral body into the spinal canal. Results from high-energy trauma with axial loading force. Most commonly occurs at the thoracolumbar junction and often manifests with signs of spinal cord injury.

media.title: T12 burst fracture and L1 fracture

-PbDhF.title: Brompheniramine
-PbDhF.description: A first-generation H1-blocking antihistamine used to treat the symptoms of the common cold and allergic rhinitis.

Z4bZ3F.title: Hydroxyzine
Z4bZ3F.description: A first-generation H₁ receptor antagonist used to treat symptoms of allergic conditions and pruritus. Also used as an anxiolytic agent.

04be3F.title: Greater auricular nerve
04be3F.description: A cutaneous nerve that originates in the cervical plexus (mostly ventral rami of C2 and some from C3) and provides sensation to the skin overlying the parotid gland, ears, and mastoid process, as well as the parotid fascia.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

a4bQ3F.title: Hyperacusis
a4bQ3F.description: Increased sensitivity to environmental sounds (i.e., normal volume noises are painfully loud to the patient). Can result from facial nerve dysfunction, ear trauma, or middle/inner ear infection.

b4bH3F.title: Plasmapheresis
b4bH3F.description: An extracorporeal procedure that involves filtering plasma from whole blood. Therapeutically, it is used to remove harmful substances, e.g. autoantibodies or toxins, and treat a variety of autoimmune (e.g., Goodpasture syndrome, Guillain-Barré syndrome), hematologic (e.g., thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura), metabolic (e.g., severe Wilson diseases, and oncologic conditions (e.g., Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia) as well as intoxications (e.g., mushroom poisoning). ​The plasma is then replaced with another solution e.g., donor plasma or albumin solution.

c4baRF.title: Terminal sedation
c4baRF.description: Sedation of a terminally ill patient with otherwise intractable pain symptoms during the final days or hours of life to ease suffering. Terminal sedation is legally and procedurally distinct from euthanasia in so far as the intent of terminal sedation must always be to relieve pain and not to bring about death, even if it includes accelerating death as a secondary effect.

destinations.label: Overview of palliative medicine → Management of imminently dying patients

W4bPRF.title: Phentolamine
W4bPRF.description: A short-acting, nonselective α-adrenergic antagonist. Commonly used to briefly counteract the effects of excessive circulating sympathomimetics (e.g., epinephrine).

d4boRF.title: Activated charcoal
d4boRF.description: An adsorbent agent used to treat some types of enteral poisoning. Usually only effective for substances 100–1000 daltons in size that were ingested less than 1 hour prior to administration.

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Enhanced elimination
Approach to the poisoned patient → Decontamination

U4bbiF.title: Severe pancreatitis
U4bbiF.description: A subtype of pancreatitis (Atlanta grade) characterized by acute pancreatitis with persistent pancreatic failure (> 48 hours) and single or multiple organ failure.

destinations.label: Acute pancreatitis → Severity grading and prognostic scores

24bTiF.title: Antitachycardia pacing
24bTiF.description: A pacing algorithm delivered by an implantable cardioverter defibrillator that paces the heart faster than the native heart rate in order to terminate ventricular tachycardias without the use of a high-energy shock.

destinations.label: Cardiac implantable electronic devices → Automated implantable cardioverter defibrillators

f4bkiF.title: Lower motor neuron
f4bkiF.description: A nerve that originates at the synapse with an upper motor neuron in the anterior horn of the spinal cord or the cranial nerve nuclei within the brainstem.  Axons from lower motor neurons carry motor function within peripheral nerves. Tracts terminate at the neuromuscular junction, where they synapse with skeletal muscle fibers.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

T4b6iF.title: Antiganglioside antibody
T4b6iF.description: An autoantibody against ganglioside antigens. Associated with autoimmune demyelinating disorders (e.g., multiple sclerosis, Guillain–Barre syndrome, chronic inflammatory demyelinating neuropathies), autoimmune conditions (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjogren syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis), and neurodegenerative disorders (e.g., Alzheimer disease).

h4bcQF.title: Polycythemia
h4bcQF.description: An increase in erythrocyte count (including hematocrit, hemoglobin, and red blood cell mass), which may be primary (in polycythemia vera) or secondary to smoking, chronic pulmonary or cardiac disease, high altitude, or increased epoietin levels (e.g., in doping, renal cell carcinoma). The latter generally manifests as isolated erythrocytosis. The increased blood cell mass leads to hyperviscosity, increasing the risk of thrombosis and poor oxygenation.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen transport and conditions that affect oxygenation

i4bJQF.title: Colesevelam
i4bJQF.description: A bile acid sequestrant that promotes bile acid excretion and, subsequently, the conversion of cholesterol into bile acids, thus lowering the serum cholesterol concentration. It is a second-line lipid-lowering agent.

destinations.label: Second-line lipid-lowering agents → Bile acid resins

Q4buQF.title: Antiviral capsid antigen IgM antibody
Q4buQF.description: Antibodies against EBV viral capsid antigens (VCA). Elevated VCA IgM antibodies suggest acute EBV infection. Elevated VCA IgG or EBV nuclear antigen IgG antibodies suggest past infection.

P4bWjF.title: Dacryoadenitis
P4bWjF.description: An inflammation of the lacrimal gland. Most commonly caused by infection. Can be acute or chronic.

destinations.label: Diseases of the lacrimal apparatus → Dacryoadenitis

k4bmjF.title: Bronchodilators
k4bmjF.description: A group of drugs that dilate the bronchi and bronchioles by relaxing smooth muscle. Used to decrease respiratory airway resistance and increase airflow to the lungs (e.g., to treat asthma and COPD). Commonly used agents include beta agonists and anticholinergics that may be used individually or as combined therapy.

54biPF.title: Laminar flow
54biPF.description: A type of flow with smooth movement of molecules in the same direction as the pressure gradient. In normal physiology, blood in the circulatory system and air in the lungs demonstrate laminar flow.

M4bMPF.title: Turbulent flow
M4bMPF.description: A type of flow characterized by chaotic movement of molecules in directions different from the pressure gradient. Turbulent airflow (e.g., from bronchial obstruction) requires a higher pressure gradient to move air. Turbulent blood flow creates sound waves that can be auscultated as murmurs or bruits.

n4b7PF.title: Dacryostenosis
n4b7PF.description: Obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct (NLD). Presents with epiphora and predisposes to infection of the lacrimal sac (dacryocystitis).

destinations.label: Diseases of the lacrimal apparatus → Dacryostenosis

L4bwPF.title: Viral pneumonia
L4bwPF.description: A primary infection of the lung by a viral pathogen (most commonly influenza virus among adults and respiratory syncytial virus among children). Typical manifestations include fever, dyspnea, cough, and chest x-ray that shows bilateral reticular opacities.

o4b04F.title: Burton's line
o4b04F.description: A thin purple-bluish line on the gums that is a classic sign of chronic lead exposure.

K4bU4F.title: Mees lines
K4bU4F.description: White bands across the nails of fingers and toes that occur secondary to chronic arsenic poisoning or thallium exposure.

64bj4F.title: Currant jelly sputum
64bj4F.description: A thick, mucoid, blood-tinged sputum that resembles red currant jelly. Classically associated with Klebsiella pneumonia.

p4bL4F.title: Retinal photocoagulation
p4bL4F.description: A procedure that uses a laser to create retinal burns in order to seal leaking blood vessels and minimize the growth of new vessels. Types include focal and panretinal photocoagulation. Used in the treatment of ocular conditions involving neovascularization, e.g., diabetic retinopathy and central retinal vein occlusion.

J4bs4F.title: Deep brain stimulation
J4bs4F.description: A therapeutic procedure that involves the implantation of an electrode into the patient's brain to deliver electrical stimuli. The electrode is connected to a neurostimulator (battery-operated device) that is most commonly implanted under the skin near the collarbone of the patient and can be manually turned on and off by a magnet. Used in the treatment of neurologic and psychiatric disorders.

q4bC4F.title: Tissue flap
q4bC4F.description: Viable tissue that is transplanted with its vascular supply from one area of the body to another, usually to treat areas of extensive tissue loss following burns, necrotizing fasciitis, surgery, or trauma. Numerous types and combinations of tissue may be used for flaps, including skin, muscle, and bone.

I4bYkF.title: Blood pressure measurement
I4bYkF.description: Blood pressure can be measured with an automated device or manually (the auscultatory method) with a stethoscope and sphygmomanometer.

r4bfkF.title: Chorea
r4bfkF.description: A type of involuntary movement characteristic of a group of neurological disorders called dyskinesias. Chorea movements are continuous, involuntary, rapid, abrupt, irregular, nonstereotyped, and are not urge- or compulsion-driven. Most commonly involve the shoulders, hips, and face.

74b4kF.title: Femoroacetabular impingement
74b4kF.description: Abnormal contact between the acetabulum and proximal femur during terminal hip flexion, which leads to damage of the articular cartilage and acetabular labrum. Can result from global or focal acetabular overcoverage of the femoral head (pincer impingement), which is typically seen in middle-aged women, or from an abnormally shaped, non-spherical femoral head (cam impingement), which is seen in young men.

s4btkF.title: Shagreen patch
s4btkF.description: A cutaneous manifestation of tuberous sclerosis consisting of a raised plaque of rough, dimpled (orange peel-like) skin. Most commonly found on the lower back.

G4bBkF.title: Ash-leaf spot
G4bBkF.description: A dermatologic finding characterized by a hypopigmented macule, often in an ellipsoid shape, that fluoresces when illuminated under Wood lamp examination. The presence of three or more spots is one of the major diagnostic criteria for tuberous sclerosis.

t4bXOF.title: Neurofibroma
t4bXOF.description: A benign nerve sheath tumor that can arise anywhere on the body. Patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 typically develop multiple neurofibromas in childhood. Can also develop spontaneously in adulthood, typically as a solitary lesion.

u4bpOF.title: Hypertensive crisis
u4bpOF.description: An increase in systolic blood pressure above 180 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure above 120 mm Hg.

E4b8OF.title: Provisional tic disorder
E4b8OF.description: A tic disorder in which a patient has motor or phonic tics that occur over a period of less than one year before resolving. Particularly common during childhood and often does not require treatment.

v4bAOF.title: Hemiplegic migraine
v4bAOF.description: An uncommon subtype of migraine with aura that is distinguished by motor weakness as the manifestation of the migraine aura in at least some migraine episodes. May be sporadic or familial.

D4b1lF.title: Rapid strep test
D4b1lF.description: A rapid antigen detection test to diagnose group A strep (GAS) infections (e.g., tonsillitis, pharyngitis, perianal dermatitis) at the point of care using a swab. Tests for antigens specific to GAS with a specificity of > 95% and a sensitivity of 70–90%.

w4bhlF.title: Panendoscopy
w4bhlF.description: A procedure in which a camera-equipped blade or an endoscope (either flexible or rigid) is inserted via the mouth or nose in order to visualize the complete upper airway and digestive tract, including the pharynx, larynx, upper trachea, and esophagus. This is useful for evaluating pathologies of these structures, particularly in cases of suspected pharyngeal carcinoma.

94bNlF.title: Nasopharyngoscopy
94bNlF.description: A procedure in which a fiberoptic laryngoscope (either flexible or rigid) is inserted via the mouth or nose to visualize the larynx during intubation or diagnostic evaluation of the upper airway (e.g., in patients with suspected foreign body or patients with chronic hoarseness and/or dysphonia).

C4bqlF.title: Neuropsychological testing
C4bqlF.description: A series of standardized tests that evaluate patient performance in multiple cognitive and functional domains. Used by specialists in the diagnosis of neurocognitive disorders. Examples include the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status.

x4bElF.title: Alloimmunization
x4bElF.description: A process by which an immune response develops against foreign antigens following exposure to them.

B4bzlF.title: Palpitations
B4bzlF.description: The unpleasant awareness of one's own heartbeat. Can feel like a fluttering or pounding in the chest. Usually benign but can indicate a life-threatening cardiac condition (e.g., myocardial infarction).

destinations.label: Cardiovascular examination → History and general examination

y4bdNF.title: Melanocyte
y4bdNF.description: Pigment-containing cells that produce melanin and are primarily located in the epidermis. Melanin production is stimulated by melanocyte-stimulating hormone and ultraviolet radiation. Malignant transformation of melanocytes causes melanoma.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Cells of the skin

media.title: Layers of the epidermis and their characteristics

A4bRNF.title: Mineralocorticoid
A4bRNF.description: A class of steroid hormones that influence electrolyte and water balance and the body. Produced in the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex. The main mineralocorticoid is aldosterone.

_4b5NF.title: Gravidity
_4b5NF.description: The number of pregnancies a woman has had (regardless of the outcome or number of fetuses per pregnancy). Reported as the first number in the gravida/para notation (e.g., G2P2 indicates that a woman has had 2 pregnancies).

z4brNF.title: Parity
z4brNF.description: The number of pregnancies a woman has had that have reached at least 20 weeks of gestation (regardless of the number of fetuses per pregnancy). Reported as the second number in the gravida/para notation (e.g., G2P2 indicates that a woman has had 2 pregnancies that have reached at least 20 weeks of gestation).

-4bDNF.title: Gestational age
-4bDNF.description: The age of a fetus calculated from the first day of the last menstrual period.

0kbemF.title: Aquagenic urticaria
0kbemF.description: A rare form of urticaria that is caused by contact with water.

akbQmF.title: Flumazenil
akbQmF.description: A selective antagonist of the benzodiazepine site (found on GABAa-receptor) that is primarily used to treat benzodiazepine overdose.

YkbnmF.title: Hyperemesis gravidarum
YkbnmF.description: A condition of severe, persistent nausea and vomiting during pregnancy that is associated with > 5% loss of pre-pregnancy weight and severe dehydration. More common among young, primigravid women and women with multifetal gestation or molar pregnancy.

destinations.label: Maternal complications during pregnancy → Hyperemesis gravidarum

bkbHmF.title: Methylene blue
bkbHmF.description: A heterocyclic aromatic chemical compound that produces a deep blue solution when dissolved in water. Used to stain histological preparations as well as to treat methemoglobinemia by reducing methemoglobin back to hemoglobin.

Xkb9mF.title: Cholinergic urticaria
Xkb9mF.description: Urticaria that is triggered by a rise in ambient temperature (e.g., after exercise or a warm shower).

ckba5F.title: Physical urticaria
ckba5F.description: A subtype of chronic inducible urticaria. Hives and/or angioedema appear after exposure to an identifiable environmental stimulus such as pressure, heat, cold, or UV radiation.

1kb25F.title: Modafinil
1kb25F.description: A nonamphetamine CNS stimulant commonly used to treat excessive daytime sleepiness (e.g., in narcolepsy, shift work sleep disorder, or sleep apnea patients).

WkbP5F.title: Sleep hallucinations
WkbP5F.description: A symptom of narcolepsy (approx. half of cases) involving vivid, often frightening visual or auditory hallucinations that occur as the patient falls asleep (hypnagogic) or wakes up (hypnopompic). Hypnopompic hallucinations are less common.

dkbo5F.title: Menstrual recurrent hypersomnia
dkbo5F.description: A very rare variant of Klein-Levin syndrome. Characterized by recurrent episodes of excessive sleepiness just before or during menses. Associated with compulsive eating (65% of cases), depression (35% of cases), and sexual disinhibition (29% of cases). Symptoms sometimes respond to estrogen-containing contraceptives.

VkbG5F.title: Taxis
VkbG5F.description: Process of realigning displaced bone or reducing a hernia via manual pressure.

ekbx5F.title: Decussation
ekbx5F.description: The point at which axons cross from one side of the body to the other in the medulla oblongata.

UkbbMF.title: Oxime
UkbbMF.description: A class of drugs that reactivate plasma cholinesterase activity in patients with cholinergic toxicity (e.g., organophosphate poisoning) by removing the inactivating phosphoryl group from the enzyme's active site. The only class of drugs that can treat both the nicotinic (e.g., muscle weakness) and muscarinic (e.g., bronchospasm) symptoms of cholinergic toxicity. Examples include obidoxime and pralidoxime.

2kbTMF.title: Direct Coombs test
2kbTMF.description: A test used to determine if hemolysis is immune-mediated. Patient RBCs are washed and incubated with anti-human antibodies. A positive test (indicated by agglutination) means that there were already antibodies ("directly") bound to patient RBCs (from in vivo sensitization), which the test antibodies are then able to cross-link.

fkbkMF.title: Indirect Coombs test
fkbkMF.description: A test used to detect serum antibodies against RBCs. The patient's serum is incubated with test RBCs, which are then washed and incubated with anti-human antibodies, which will bind to any patient antibodies that reacted to the test RBCs and cause agglutination (a positive test result). This test is typically used to test for compatibility between a blood product donor and recipient (cross-matching) and to test for anti-Rh antibodies in Rh-negative pregnant women.

Tkb6MF.title: Transfusion-associated circulatory overload
Tkb6MF.description: A transfusion reaction in which patients develop pulmonary edema as a result of volume overload. Typically occurs when a large amount of blood products are transfused rapidly. Risk factors include a history of underlying cardiovascular or renal disease. Clinically presents with hypertension, respiratory distress, and hypoxia within six hours of transfusion, with signs of pulmonary edema on examination and imaging.

SkbyMF.title: Lipid disorders
SkbyMF.description: An abnormal concentration of one or more lipids in the blood, e.g., elevated levels of LDL and/or triglycerides. Causes can be genetic (e.g., familial hypercholesterolemia) or secondary (e.g., related to diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, or nephrotic syndrome).

hkbcnF.title: Incomplete fractures
hkbcnF.description: A fracture in which the fracture line is either absent or does not completely traverse the width of the bone (i.e., an intact periosteum and cortex are seen on at least one side of the bone). Examples include buckle fractures, greenstick fractures and bowing fractures.

3kbSnF.title: Hypertriglyceridemia
3kbSnF.description: A condition of elevated serum triglycerides (e.g., ≥ 150 mg/dL in adults). May be caused by primary genetic disorders or secondary acquired conditions (e.g., obesity, diabetes, medication-induced). Increases the risk of coronary artery disease. Severe hypertriglyceridemia (i.e., levels ≥ 500 mg/dL) increases the risk of acute pancreatitis.

RkblnF.title: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
RkblnF.description: A thrombotic obstruction of the venous system within the cavernous sinus, most commonly due to an infection  spreading from the sinuses, ears, or dentition. Clinical features include headache, cranial nerve palsies (III, IV, V1, V2, and/or VI), periorbital edema, and proptosis.

ikbJnF.title: Bence Jones protein
ikbJnF.description: Polypeptide consisting of one or two immunoglobulin light chains. Its detection in urine is suggestive of plasma cell disorders such as multiple myeloma or Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia.

QkbunF.title: Polymyositis
QkbunF.description: A rare inflammatory myopathy characterized by proximal skeletal muscle weakness, increased serum creatine kinase concentration, and evidence of myositis on EMG and biopsy, in the absence of any of the characteristic findings of the other inflammatory myopathies. Considered a diagnosis of exclusion.

jkb_nF.title: Xanthelasma
jkb_nF.description: A subtype of xanthoma characterized by a collection of lipid-filled deposits that develop on the medial aspect of the eyelids as soft, yellow plaques. Associated with underlying lipid disorders that can increase the risk for atherosclerosis and associated conditions (e.g., coronary artery disease, myocardial infarctions).

PkbWLF.title: Total hematuria
PkbWLF.description: The passage of blood or clots throughout micturition. Suggests an origin of the bleeding within the bladder, ureter, or kidneys.

4kb3LF.title: Dermatomyositis
4kb3LF.description: An inflammatory myopathy characterized by progressive symmetrical proximal muscle weakness and distinctive skin findings, including an erythematous rash on the extensor hand joints (Gottron sign), upper eyelids (heliotrope rash), upper anterior torso (V-sign), and upper posterior torso (shawl sign).

kkbmLF.title: Inferior petrosal sinus testing
kkbmLF.description: A diagnostic test to diagnose pituitary ACTH hypersecretion (Cushing disease) that involves insertion of a catheter via the jugular or femoral veins into the inferior petrosal sinus veins bilaterally to measure ACTH concentrations before and after CRH stimulation. Performed if Cushing disease is suspected, but neuroimaging is inconclusive.

OkbILF.title: Statin-induced myopathy
OkbILF.description: Myopathy triggered by statin use and characterized by muscle weakness (usually symmetrical and affecting the proximal rather than the distal muscles) and/or muscle myalgias (aches, pains, and soreness) with elevated CK and normal ESR. Associated with rhabdomyolysis in extreme cases.

lkbvLF.title: Paresthesia
lkbvLF.description: An abnormal sensation (e.g., tingling, prickling, or "pins and needles") caused by damage to peripheral nerves.

Nkb-LF.title: Caudate nucleus
Nkb-LF.description: A component of the dorsal striatum and the basal ganglia. Primary function is the coordination of movement; also involved in procedural learning, associative learning, and many other functions. Caudate nucleus atrophy is the hallmark of Huntington disease but can be seen in other neurodegenerative diseases (e.g., Parkinson disease).

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

mkbVoF.title: Putamen
mkbVoF.description: A part of the dorsal striatum and basal ganglia that is primarily involved in movement and learning.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

5kbioF.title: Uterine procidentia
5kbioF.description: A form of pelvic herniation. Protrusion of all vaginal walls or cervix beyond the vaginal introitus.

MkbMoF.title: Uterine prolapse
