MkbMoF.description: A type of pelvic organ prolapse characterized by the descent of the uterus toward or through the vaginal introitus. Symptoms include a sensation of vaginal fullness, pelvic pain, constipation, and urinary incontinence.

okb0KF.title: Tracheal stent
okb0KF.description: A tube used to maintain tracheal patency. May be used preventatively (e.g., in a patient with laryngeal stenosis/trauma or following tracheal surgery) or palliatively (e.g., inoperable tracheobronchial malignancy).

KkbUKF.title: Crystalline arthropathy
KkbUKF.description: A type of inflammatory arthropathy caused by crystal deposition within or around joints and characterized by pain and swelling of the affected joints. Gout, caused by articular deposition of monosodium urate crystals, is the most common type, followed by calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease and basic calcium phosphate crystal deposition disease.

6kbjKF.title: Osmolar gap
6kbjKF.description: The difference between the measured serum osmolarity and the calculated serum osmolarity. Normally, the calculated serum osmolarity is primarily determined by circulating levels of sodium salts (chloride and bicarbonate), glucose, and urea. An increased serum osmolar gap occurs when other solutes (e.g., ethanol, methanol, propylene glycol) are present in high enough concentrations to increase the measured osmolarity by more than 10 mOsmol/L.

pkbLKF.title: Foramen magnum
pkbLKF.description: A large oval-shaped opening in the occipital bone at the base of the skull in the posterior cranial fossa. The medulla oblongata passes through the foramen magnum, becoming the spinal cord running through the spinal canal. Other structures that pass through this foramen include the meninges, the tectorial membrane, the anterior and posterior spinal arteries, the vertebral arteries, and the spinal component of the spinal accessory nerve.

JkbsKF.title: Serologic studies
JkbsKF.description: A laboratory study of the serum. Most commonly refers to the detection of specific antibodies and/or antigens in the blood (e.g., ANA, Lyme IgM).

qkbCKF.title: Anti-aquaporin-4
qkbCKF.description: Autoimmune antibodies directed against aquaporin-4 (AQP4), a protein found in the membranes of astrocytes. The presence of anti-AQP4 antibodies is part of the diagnosis of neuromyelitis optica (present in ~ 75% of cases).

rkbf6F.title: Eschar
rkbf6F.description: A skin lesion characterized by dried, necrotic skin tissue. Etiologies include burns, infection, gangrene, and pressure ulcers.

FkbgpF.title: Cerebral salt wasting
FkbgpF.description: Causes hypovolemic, hypotonic hyponatremia, although the mechanism is poorly understood. Classically, its onset occurs within 10 days of an inciting event within the central nervous system (particularly subarachnoid hemorrhage) or neurosurgical procedure. Severe symptoms are treated with hypertonic saline and fludrocortisone.

8kbOpF.title: Abulia
8kbOpF.description: A milder form of akinetic mutism that is characterized by disinterest and a slowed mental state. When asked to perform certain motor or verbal tasks, patients display a delay in the motor and/or verbal response, or fail to continue the assigned task after initially complying. Usually results from damage to the frontal lobe and/or its connections.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Appearance and behavior

ukbppF.title: Alexia
ukbppF.description: An acquired inability to read that is the result of a defect in central language processing.

Ekb8pF.title: Posterior cerebral artery
Ekb8pF.description: A pair of blood vessels within the circle of Willis that originate from the basilar artery. The posterior cerebral artery supplies most parts of the occipital cortex, inferior and medial temporal cortices, thalamus, and rostral midbrain.

vkbApF.title: Common peroneal nerve
vkbApF.description: A nerve arising from the L4–S2 dorsal branches that innervates the lateral surface of the lower leg and the back of the feet and toes, as well as the foot and toe extensors and foot pronators. Because it descends along the lateral side of the popliteal fossa to the head of the fibula, it is susceptible to injury during fracture of the fibular head or compression, e.g., from tight casts or sitting cross-legged.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves
The leg, ankle, and foot → Innervation

media.title: Innervation of the lower extremity (dorsal view)

Dkb1JF.title: Malar rash
Dkb1JF.description: A flat or raised fixed erythema over both malar eminences and nasal bridge with characteristic sparing of the nasolabial folds. A true malar rash is caused by systemic lupus erythematosus. However, other rashes caused by rosacea, dermatomyositis, or seborrheic dermatitis are frequently mistaken for a malar rash.

media.title: Malar rash in systemic lupus erythematosus
Malar rash in systemic lupus erythematosus

wkbhJF.title: Middle cerebral artery
wkbhJF.description: A terminal branch of the internal carotid artery that supplies most of the cerebral cortex on the lateral surfaces of the frontal lobe, anterolateral surface of the parietal lobe, and the superolateral surface of temporal lobe, as well as large parts of the basal ganglia and internal capsule. The MCA is the most commonly occluded artery in ischemic strokes.

9kbNJF.title: Anterior cerebral artery
9kbNJF.description: A pair of blood vessels within the circle of Willis that arises as 1 of 2 pairs of terminal branches of the internal carotid arteries (the middle cerebral arteries being the other) and supplies the medial portions of the frontal and parietal lobes, much of the corpus callosum, the caudate nucleus, and the anterior portion of the internal capsule.

xkbEJF.title: Lumbosacral plexus injury
xkbEJF.description: An injury to the neural network formed by the ventral rami of spinal roots T12-S4 and their communications, which can result in a variety of symptoms, including pain in the lower back and leg and weakness in parts of the leg. Etiologies include trauma at the pelvic level, radiation therapy, diabetes, and vasculitis.

BkbzJF.title: Lumbosacral trunk
BkbzJF.description: The nervous tissue connecting the lumbar plexus with the sacral plexus. Comprised of nerve roots of L4-L5. Originates over the medial psoas major muscle and runs inferiorly over the pelvic brim to join S1 and contribute to the sacral plexus

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

ykbdqF.title: Lumbosacral radiculopathy
ykbdqF.description: A condition caused by injury to one or more nerve roots from L1 to S1, which results in pain in the lower back and hip that radiates down the back of the thigh. The pain may be described as tingling, numbing, and/or shooting and may be associated with paresthesias.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Complications of delivery

AkbRqF.title: Postpartum angiopathy
AkbRqF.description: Multifocal narrowing of the cerebral arteries in the absence of inflammation in the weeks after an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery. Diagnosed by cerebral angiography, which reveals segmental vasoconstriction that often resolves spontaneously.

_kb5qF.title: HLA-DR3
_kb5qF.description: A specific allele of class II major histocompatibility complex. This allele is associated with a variety of autoimmune disorders including Grave's disease, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, myasthenia gravis, Addison's disease, type 1 diabetes mellitus, and systemic lupus erythematosus.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → Immune tolerance and autoimmunity

zkbrqF.title: Supine hypotensive syndrome
zkbrqF.description: A pregnancy complication caused by compression of the inferior vena cava (less commonly also the abdominal aorta) by the enlarged uterus in women lying in a supine position. Can occur after approx. 20 weeks' gestation and presents with symptoms of reduced preload/hypovolemic shock and fetal bradycardia. Placing the mother in the left lateral position usually alleviates symptoms.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Common discomforts during pregnancy

-kbDqF.title: Nucleus ambiguus
-kbDqF.description: A branchial motor nucleus in the medulla that gives rise to fibers that supply the stylopharyngeal muscles via the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), as well as the muscles of the palate, pharynx, upper esophagus, and larynx via the vagus nerve (CN X). Disruption of function (as in patients with posterior inferior cerebellar artery stroke) is associated with dysphagia, hoarseness, decreased gag reflex, and hiccups.

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Origin and pathways of the cranial nerves

ZObZIF.title: Inferior oblique muscle
ZObZIF.description: An extraocular muscle innervated by the oculomotor nerve (CN III). Functions include: extorsion (external, or lateral, rotation), elevation, and abduction of the eye. It is the only extraocular muscle that can elevate an adducted eye.

0ObeIF.title: Bielschowsky test
0ObeIF.description: A test used to determine which extraocular muscle is impaired in patients with incomitant hypertropia (vertical gaze deviation in which the degree of deviation is not constant). The degree of hypertropia is evaluated in the following three positions: 1. primary gaze; 2. left and right lateral gaze; 3. left and right head tilt.

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Paralytic strabismus

YObnIF.title: Lateral rectus muscle
YObnIF.description: An extraocular muscle innervated by the abducens nerve (CN VI). Main function is abduction of the eye.

bObHIF.title: Ciliary muscle
bObHIF.description: A muscle that plays a role in eye accommodation. Contraction makes the lens more spherical, and increases the eye's power of accommodation to aid in viewing closer objects.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

XOb9IF.title: Pupillary sphincter
XOb9IF.description: A circular muscle in the iris responsible for pupillary constriction. Cranial nerve III carries parasympathetic fibers from the Edinger-Westphal nucleus to the ciliary ganglion. The short ciliary nerve (a branch of the ciliary ganglion) then carries the postganglionic fibers to innervate the pupillary sphincter and enable pupillary constriction.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

cObarF.title: Riluzole
cObarF.description: A sodium-channel blocker drug that inhibits glutamate release in the CNS, which is responsible for its anti-excitotoxic effect (although the exact mechanism by which it inhibits glutamate release is unknown). It is used in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis because of its neuroprotective and spasmolytic effects.

1Ob2rF.title: Hemin
1Ob2rF.description: An iron-containing porphyrin that inhibits heme synthesis. Used to treat acute intermittent porphyria by preventing the accumulation of the toxic heme synthesis intermediates.

WObPrF.title: Nusinersen
WObPrF.description: An intrathecally administered antisense drug that is used to treat spinal muscular atrophy, a motor neuron disease caused by a defective SMN1 gene. Nusinersen induces differential splicing in the SMN2 gene, which then essentially takes over the role of the SMN1 gene.

dOborF.title: Edetate calcium disodium
dOborF.description: A chelating agent used in the treatment of lead poisoning. It binds metal ions (e.g., lead) in the serum and is subsequently excreted renally. A sodium-only variant, disodium EDTA, is no longer used as it can cause life-threatening hypocalcemia. Other forms of EDTA have various industry applications.

UObb7F.title: Nitroglycerin
UObb7F.description: A peripheral vasodilator that decreases preload through venous dilation (venous pooling), which can reduce myocardial wall tension and improve myocardial perfusion. It is used to treat angina due to coronary syndrome. Off-label uses include esophageal spastic disorder, gastroesophageal variceal hemorrhage, and uterine relaxation.

2ObT7F.title: Isosorbide dinitrate
2ObT7F.description: A long-acting nitrate that causes smooth muscle relaxation through the increase of nitric oxide. Used to treat and prevent angina. Adverse effects include reflex tachycardia, hypotension, flushing, and headache.

fObk7F.title: Isosorbide mononitrate
fObk7F.description: A long-acting nitrate that causes smooth muscle relaxation through the increase of nitric oxide. Used to treat and prevent angina. Adverse effects include reflex tachycardia, hypotension, flushing, and headache.

SOby7F.title: Aortic endarterectomy
SOby7F.description: A surgical procedure that involves removal of part of the inner lining of the aorta in order to remove an adherent atherosclerotic plaque. Indicated in some cases of peripheral arterial disease with aortoiliac involvement.

3ObSHF.title: Medial longitudinal fasciculus
3ObSHF.description: A pair of myelinated tracts that runs ventrally through the midline of the brain stem and upper part of the spinal cord. The MLF connects the nuclei that control extraocular muscles (abducens, trochlear, and oculomotor nuclei) with one another and with the vestibular nuclei. The MLF controls conjugate horizontal movement (versions) of the eyeball and the adjustment of eye movement with a change in head position.

ROblHF.title: Cortical blindness
ROblHF.description: A loss of vision due to damage to the bilateral cerebral visual pathways of the occipital lobes. Most commonly caused by posterior cerebral artery stroke. Does not cause other abnormalities on ophthalmologic examination besides blindness.

iObJHF.title: Retrobulbar hemorrhage
iObJHF.description: Bleeding into the intraorbital space behind the globe of the eye. Increased intraorbital pressure causes anterior displacement of orbital contents, occlusion of the retinal artery, and stretching of the optic nerve and its blood supply. Symptoms include pain, vision impairment, and loss of pupillary reflexes. Causes include orbital trauma, eye/sinus/lid surgery, and ruptured arteriovenous malformations.

PObWsF.title: Diabetic embryopathy
PObWsF.description: Any anomaly in an embryo associated with diabetes in the mother. Anomalies typically develop during the main embryonic period and include neural tube defects, small left colon syndrome, caudal regression, and renal disorders (e.g., renal agenesis).

destinations.label: Diabetes mellitus in pregnancy → Fetal and neonatal complications of diabetes mellitus in pregnancy

4Ob3sF.title: Microcephaly
4Ob3sF.description: A head circumference that is > 2 standard deviations below the mean size for a given age and sex (e.g., < 3rd percentile on the WHO growth charts). May be seen in individuals with chromosomal trisomies, fetal alcohol syndrome, congenital TORCH infections, cranial anatomic abnormalities, and neural tube defects.

kObmsF.title: Holoprosencephaly
kObmsF.description: A failure of the prosencephalon (the anterior portion of the embryonic brain) to develop into two cerebral hemispheres. Associated with trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome).

destinations.label: Teratogenesis → Risks of substance use during pregnancy

lObvsF.title: Atrioventricular dissociation
lObvsF.description: A condition in which atrial and ventricular contractions occur independently. Occurs if a ventricular pacemaker is faster than the sinus node pacemaker (e.g., ventricular tachycardia or sinus bradycardia with a junctional rhythm) or if there is disruption of electrical transmission through the atrioventricular (AV) node (e.g., third-degree AV block). Electrocardiogram shows no relationship between P waves and QRS complexes (i.e., P-R dissociation).

NOb-sF.title: Stool microscopy
NOb-sF.description: A diagnostic stool test commonly obtained in patients with gastrointestinal disorders. Abnormal microscopic findings include the presence of leukocytes, erythrocytes, and/or abnormal flora including yeast, parasites, and ova.

5ObiGF.title: Laminectomy
5ObiGF.description: Removal of the dorsal part of the vertebra (lamina) to widen the spinal canal, thereby relieving pressure on the spinal cord and spinal nerves. Indications include spinal stenosis (most common), spinal epidural hematoma, and syringomyelia.

MObMGF.title: Pulsus bigeminus
MObMGF.description: An physical finding characterized by palpation of two heartbeats in rapid succession followed by a long gap until the next heartbeat in the setting of a regularly irregular cardiac rhythm. Indicates severe left heart failure or digoxin toxicity.

KObUtF.title: Tubal ring sign
KObUtF.description: An adnexal ultrasound finding that suggests, but does not confirm, a tubal ectopic pregnancy. Consists of an echogenic ring, representing trophoblastic tissue, surrounding a fluid-filled gestational sac in the fallopian tube without a yolk sac, indicating early pregnancy.

6ObjtF.title: Hypertensive encephalopathy
6ObjtF.description: Cerebral edema that occurs in patients with severe hypertension. Severe hypertension results in the failure of CNS to autoregulate blood flow, which leads to vasodilation and hyperperfusion, resulting in cerebral edema.

pObLtF.title: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery
pObLtF.description: An artery that arises from the vertebral artery at the level between the medulla and the pons and courses posteriorly wrapping around the medulla to supply the lateral part of the medulla, and the inferior part of the cerebellum.

JObstF.title: Vaginal pessary
JObstF.description: A device made of materials such as silicone or latex that is inserted into the vagina in order to provide more support for pelvic organs or deliver medication. It is most often used for prolapse of the uterus; can also be used in some patients with stress incontinence.

qObCtF.title: Methylmalonic acid
qObCtF.description: A dicarboxylic acid that combines with coenzyme A to form methylmalonyl-CoA. In a Vitamin B12 mediated reaction, methylmalonyl-CoA is converted into succinyl-CoA, which then enters the Kreb's cycle. Vitamin B12 deficiency results in a buildup of methylmalonic acid.

IObYFF.title: Hypoaldosteronism
IObYFF.description: A state of either decreased aldosterone production (e.g., adrenal insufficiency, hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism) or resistance to aldosterone (e.g., administration of K+ sparing diuretics). Since aldosterone normally increases the reabsorption of Na+ and water and decreases the reabsorption of K+ and the excretion of H+, patients manifest with hyperkalemia, hypovolemic hyponatremia, and mild hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis.

7Ob4FF.title: Thalidomide
7Ob4FF.description: An immune-modulating medication previously used to treat nausea in pregnant women but found to cause birth defects. It also is used in the treatment of certain cancers, including multiple myeloma.

GObBFF.title: Carbidopa-levodopa
GObBFF.description: A combination drug used for the symptomatic management of Parkinson disease. Levodopa crosses the blood-brain barrier and is converted into active dopamine in the CNS to improve motor symptoms. Carbidopa cannot cross the blood-brain barrier and prevents the conversion of levodopa in the periphery, which minimizes the peripheral adverse effects of dopamine (e.g., nausea, autonomic dysfunction) and increases the availability of levodopa that can enter the CNS.

destinations.label: Medication for Parkinson disease → Adverse effects

tObX8F.title: Deep tendon reflex
tObX8F.description: A reflex to test the integrity of a sensory and motor neuron circuit. Upon tapping of the reflex hammer, activation of the dorsal root ganglion causes firing of the lower motor neuron for the agonist muscle and relaxation of the antagonist muscle, resulting in automatic movement. An increased DTR indicates an upper motor neuron issue, whereas decreased DTR indicates a LMN, neuromuscular junction, or muscle issue.

8ObO8F.title: Uniparental disomy
8ObO8F.description: A genotypic anomaly in which an individual receives two copies of one chromosome from a single parent and no copies from the other. Can occur due to errors in meiosis I or meiosis II. Typically results in a normal phenotype. Cannot be detected by karyotyping because the number of chromosomes is normal.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

uObp8F.title: Retained products of conception
uObp8F.description: Tissue derived from a fertilized egg (e.g., fetus, placenta) that remains in the uterus after delivery, induced abortion, or pregnancy loss. Complications include maternal peripartum infection and postpartum hemorrhage.

EOb88F.title: Hepatitis B vaccine
EOb88F.description: An inactivated vaccine against hepatitis B that contains a subunit of the hepatitis B virus.

vObA8F.title: Varicella vaccine
vObA8F.description: A live-attenuated vaccine used to prevent chickenpox, a condition caused by the varicella-zoster virus (HHV-3). Available as a monovalent (Varivax) or polyvalent (ProQuad/MMRV against measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella) vaccine.

DOb1uF.title: Hib vaccine
DOb1uF.description: An inactivated vaccine that protects against pneumonia and meningitis caused by the encapsulated, gram-negative coccobacillus Haemophilus influenzae type b. Part of the normal immunization schedule in children younger than 5 years. Also recommended for patients with sickle cell disease, asplenia, or a history of bone marrow transplantation, and for patients ages 5-18 with HIV.

wObhuF.title: Ganglion cyst
wObhuF.description: Benign transilluminating liquid/gel-filled nodules that develop along tendons or joints (usually the dorsal wrists). May be asymptomatic or cause pain that may self-resolve or become chronic. Large cysts can cause numbness, weakness, or tingling if the nerve is being compressed. Of unknown etiology, but often occur in the presence of irritation or mechanical changes.

destinations.label: Collection of orthopedic conditions → Ganglion cyst

9ObNuF.title: Autolytic debridement
9ObNuF.description: The physiological breakdown of nonviable tissue by endogenous enzymes and moisture, promoted by moisture-retentive dressings. It is a painless form of selective debridement.

yObdEF.title: Bovine spongiform encephalopathy
yObdEF.description: A prion disease of cattle that results in progressive neurologic dysfunction. The same prion responsible for this disorder in cattle is thought to result in variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in humans.

AObREF.title: Junctional tachycardia
AObREF.description: A nonreentrant supraventricular tachycardia that arises from increased automaticity of myocytes in the atrioventricular node and/or bundle of His. Can cause a paroxysmal junctional tachycardia (heart rate > 100/minute) or an accelerated junctional rhythm (heart rate 60-100/minute). Etiologies include myocardial ischemia, digoxin toxicity, and congenital heart disease.

_Ob5EF.title: Scrotal hernia
_Ob5EF.description: A displacement of intra-abdominal contents into the scrotum. Results from a large, indirect inguinal hernia that descends through the inguinal canal into the scrotum.

zObrEF.title: Posterior spinal artery syndrome
zObrEF.description: Posterior spinal artery syndrome is a loss of function of the cord that is supplied by the posterior spinal arteries, namely the posterior (dorsal) columns, resulting in loss of proprioception and vibratory sensation at and below the level of the injury.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Clinical significance

ZlbZvF.title: Lipodermatosclerosis
ZlbZvF.description: Localized chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the skin and subcutaneous tissues of lower leg. Characterized by painful, indurated, and hardened skin. Can result in atrophie blanche. Corresponds to CEAP class C4 venous disease.

0lbevF.title: Chorda tympani
0lbevF.description: A branch of the facial nerve (CN VII) that runs through the middle ear and exits the base of the skull at the petrotympanic fissure, where it joins the lingual nerve. The chorda tympani carries preganglionic parasympathetic secretomotor fibers to the submandibular and sublingual glands, afferent taste fibers from the anterior 2/3 of the tongue, and sensation from the posterior wall of the external acoustic meatus.

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Origin and pathways of the cranial nerves

clbaDF.title: Thiamine
clbaDF.description: A water-soluble vitamin found in many foods such as yeast, cereal grains, beans, nuts, and meat. Its active form, thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP), is a cofactor for several dehydrogenase enzyme reactions involved in glucose and energy metabolism. Deficiency, which is most commonly seen with alcohol use disorder, can manifest as beriberi, Wernicke encephalopathy, or Korsakoff syndrome.

WlbPDF.title: Macrocytic anemia
WlbPDF.description: A type of anemia characterized by larger than normal red blood cells (with mean corpuscular volume > 100 fL). Etiologies include vitamin B12 deficiency, folate deficiency, liver disease, alcohol use, orotic aciduria, myelodysplastic syndrome, and hypothyroidism.

dlboDF.title: Alcohol withdrawal syndrome
dlboDF.description: A transient excitatory state caused by a sudden cessation or reduction in alcohol consumption after a prolonged period of heavy drinking. Symptoms include anxiety, tremors, sweating, and palpitations, which usually develop 6-24 hours after the last drink. In some cases, patients may present with complications such as seizures, hallucinations, and delirium.

media.title: Clinical institute withdrawal assessment for alcohol (CIWA-Ar)

VlbGDF.title: Coal workers' pneumoconiosis
VlbGDF.description: A severe form of anthracosis that occurs with prolonged exposure to coal and carbon dust. Characterized by nodular opacities (typically <1 cm) in the upper lobes of the lung and chronic bronchitis that can progress to pulmonary fibrosis.

destinations.label: Interstitial lung diseases → Overview of pneumoconioses

media.title: Anthracotic pigment in lung in coal worker's pneumoconiosis

elbxDF.title: Small left colon syndrome
elbxDF.description: A congenital defect in which there is an abrupt decrease in intestinal diameter (usually near the splenic flexure). It presents as delayed passage of meconium and can lead to intestinal obstruction. Associated with a maternal history of gestational diabetes.

destinations.label: Diabetes mellitus in pregnancy → Fetal and neonatal complications of diabetes mellitus in pregnancy

UlbbwF.title: First-trimester combined screening
UlbbwF.description: A noninvasive first-trimester screening consisting of measurement of sonographic nuchal translucency and beta-HCG and PAPP-A levels in maternal serum. Performed between 10-14 weeks' gestation and can detect trisomy 13,18, and 21, neural tube defects, as well as molar and ectopic pregnancies.

Tlb6wF.title: End-of-life care
Tlb6wF.description: The care and support provided to patients near the time of death. May include medical interventions for management of physical symptoms as well as psychological, emotional, and spiritual support.

SlbywF.title: Notifiable diseases
SlbywF.description: A group of diseases considered to be of great importance to public health and that must be reported to local, state, and national authorities in the US when diagnosed or strongly suspected by laboratories or doctors. Examples include HIV infection, tuberculosis, chlamydia, gonorrhea, and botulism.

destinations.label: Ethics of communicating medical information → Reporting

3lbS9F.title: Jugulotympanic paraganglioma
3lbS9F.description: A benign tumor that arises from autonomic paraganglia. Most common tumor of the middle ear. Highly vascular, therefore tumors typically present with a pulsatile tinnitus as the initial symptom.

destinations.label: Glomus tumors → Classification of the various types of glomus tumors

ilbJ9F.title: Modified Dandy criteria
ilbJ9F.description:
To diagnose idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH, or pseudotumor cerebri), each of the following has to apply:
1) Symptoms of increased ICP (e.g., headache, visual changes, pulsatile tinnitus, papilledema)
2) Absence of localizing neurologic findings on neurologic examination
3) Absence of deformity, displacement, or obstruction of the ventricular system with otherwise normal neurodiagnostic studies (except for cerebrospinal fluid pressure > 20 cm H2O and/or neuroimaging showing an empty sella turcica, an optic nerve sheath with filled out CSF spaces, and/or smooth-walled nonflow-related venous sinus stenosis or collapse)
4) Awake and alert
5) No other apparent cause of intracranial hypertension

Qlbu9F.title: Iridocyclitis
Qlbu9F.description: A form of anterior uveitis characterized by inflammation of the iris with involvement of the adjacent ciliary body. Presents with eye pain, redness, and photophobia. Most common etiologies include infection (e.g.; herpes, syphilis, CMV, etc.) and systemic inflammatory conditions (e.g., sarcoidosis, inflammatory bowel disease, ankylosing spondylitis, etc.).

jlb_9F.title: Ophthalmoplegia
jlb_9F.description: The paralysis of one or more extraocular muscles. Can be seen in a variety of neurologic and ophthalmologic conditions, such as orbital cellulitis, Graves' disease, myasthenia gravis, or multiple sclerosis.

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Paralytic strabismus

PlbWCF.title: Disease-modifying MS therapy
PlbWCF.description: Medications for long-term multiple sclerosis (MS) management to prevent relapses. Agents include glatiramer acetate, interferon beta, mitoxantrone, dimethyl fumarate.

4lb3CF.title: Cough variant asthma
4lb3CF.description: A type of asthma characterized by chronic dry cough without other typical symptoms of asthma.

klbmCF.title: Testicular choriocarcinoma
klbmCF.description: A rare germ cell tumor composed of trophoblastic cells. Manifests with a testicular mass and highly increased serum human chorionic gonadotropin concentrations, which can cause gynecomastia and symptoms of hyperthyroidism.

OlbICF.title: Corticosteroid-induced myopathy
OlbICF.description: An adverse effect triggered by corticosteroids that manifests with insidious-onset proximal muscle weakness of upper and lower limbs.

llbvCF.title: Severe combined immunodeficiency
llbvCF.description: A rare and severe form of primary immunodeficiency characterized by deficiencies in both B and T cells. Etiologies include defects of the IL-2R gamma chain (most common) and deficiencies of adenosine deaminase. Patients typically develop failure to thrive and severe (often fatal), recurrent infections in the first year of life.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital mixed immunodeficiencies

Nlb-CF.title: Albright hereditary osteodystrophy
Nlb-CF.description: A constellation of features comprising of short stature, a round face, and shortening of the fourth and fifth digits. It is the phenotype of pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1a.

destinations.label: Rare inherited syndromes → Albright hereditary osteodystrophy (Martin-Albright syndrome)

MlbMxF.title: Balanoposthitis
MlbMxF.description: An inflammation of both the glans penis and the foreskin. Typically presents with pruritus, erythema, pain, and edema. Etiologies include infections, inflammatory disorders, irritant and allergic reactions, and precancerous lesions.

destinations.label: Disorders of the glans penis and foreskin → Balanitis and balanoposthitis

nlb7xF.title: Balanitis
nlb7xF.description: An inflammation of the glans penis. Typically presents with pruritus, erythema, pain, and edema. Etiologies include infections, inflammatory disorders, irritant and allergic reactions, and precancerous lesions.

destinations.label: Disorders of the glans penis and foreskin → Balanitis and balanoposthitis

LlbwxF.title: Folinic acid
LlbwxF.description: A 5-formyl derivative of folic acid (vitamin B9). Does not require activation by dihydrofolate reductase to be biologically active. Used to treat folic acid deficiency, to prevent adverse effects from antifolate drugs such as methotrexate, trimethoprim, and pyrimethamine, and to increase the therapeutic efficacy of thymidylate synthase inhibitors such as 5-fluorouracil and capecitabine.

olb0BF.title: Etoposide
olb0BF.description: A chemotherapeutic agent that inhibits topoisomerase II, which leads to DNA degradation. Commonly used in the treatment of testicular and small cell lung cancer. Adverse effects include myelosuppression and alopecia.

KlbUBF.title: Adjustment disorder
KlbUBF.description: A psychiatric condition in which inappropriate or maladaptive emotional or behavioral changes occur in response to a psychosocial stressor. Symptoms resolve within 3–6 months following resolution of the stressor. The full criteria for other psychiatric conditions, such as major depressive episode or generalized anxiety disorder, are not met.

destinations.label: Trauma- and stressor-related disorders → Adjustment disorder

6lbjBF.title: Moraxella catarrhalis
6lbjBF.description: A gram-negative diplococcus that colonizes the upper respiratory tract. It commonly causes acute otitis media in children and COPD exacerbations in adults.

plbLBF.title: Congenital tracheoesophageal fistula
plbLBF.description: An abnormal connection between the trachea and esophagus caused by a defect in the lateral septation of the foregut. Commonly occurs with esophageal atresia. Postnatal manifestations include drooling and choking due to inability to swallow secretions.

media.title: Esophageal atresia and a distal tracheoesophageal fistula

JlbsBF.title: Laryngomalacia
JlbsBF.description: A collapse of supraglottic structures during inspiration due to anatomical and/or functional abnormalities. Manifestations include low-pitched inspiratory stridor, swallowing dysfunction, reflux, and, in severe cases, failure to thrive.

qlbCBF.title: Primary open-angle glaucoma
qlbCBF.description: A type of open-angle glaucoma that develops without an obvious ocular cause. Risk factors include age > 40 years, familial predisposition, and diabetes mellitus.

IlbYyF.title: Hurler syndrome
IlbYyF.description: A hereditary deficiency of alpha-L-iduronidase, resulting in the buildup of heparan and dermatan sulfate. Causes dysmorphic facial features, failure to thrive, hepatosplenomegaly, dysostosis, and corneal clouding.

rlbfyF.title: Hunter syndrome
rlbfyF.description: An X-linked recessive condition caused by a deficiency of iduronate-2-sulfatase. Results in the accumulation of heparan sulfate and dermatan sulfate. Typically manifests with dysmorphic facial features, hepatosplenomegaly, neurocognitive decline, and aggressive behavior.

HlbKyF.title: Postvoid residual volume
HlbKyF.description: The total volume of urine retained in the bladder after voluntary micturition. Can be assessed using ultrasonography or by catheterization. PVR < 100 mL is normal. High PVR is a sign of bladder outlet obstruction (e.g., due to BPH) or, uncommonly, due to detrusor underactivity.

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Urodynamic studies

slbtyF.title: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy
slbtyF.description: A condition of peripheral nerve damage due to chronic hyperglycemia. Commonly manifests with sensory polyneuropathy in a stocking-glove pattern and a burning sensation in the feet.

GlbByF.title: Optic nerve sheath fenestration
GlbByF.description: A surgical procedure in which small patches of dura surrounding the optic nerve are removed, allowing CSF to drain into the periorbital fat. This procedure is used in patients with idiopathic intracranial hypertension who have not adequately responded to medical therapy or who have rapid, severe vision loss.

tlbXAF.title: Gastroenteritis
tlbXAF.description: An inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract that usually manifests with diarrhea, vomiting, or abdominal pain. Most commonly caused by viruses but can be caused by bacteria, parasites, and fungi.

FlbgAF.title: Lithium-associated nephropathy
FlbgAF.description: A chronic interstitial nephritis that develops due to chronic lithium use. Causes interstitial fibrosis, focal nephron atrophy, and tubular cysts. Often manifests concurrently with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus but can occur independently.

vlbAAF.title: Myeloradiculitis
vlbAAF.description: Inflammation of the spinal cord and the spinal roots.

Dlb1_F.title: Eversion of the upper eyelid
Dlb1_F.description: A maneuver in which the upper eyelid is lifted, turned inside out (e.g., using a cotton-tipped applicator), and held in place to facilitate examination of the interior of the eyelid. Typically performed to evaluate for foreign bodies.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Upper eyelid eversion

9lbN_F.title: Pappenheimer bodies
9lbN_F.description: An abnormal finding in red blood cells characterized by small, blue or purple granules that contain iron. Etiologies include sideroblastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, and sickle cell disease.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

Clbq_F.title: Chordae tendineae
Clbq_F.description: Bands of fibrous tissue that connect the papillary muscles to the tricuspid valve and the mitral valve in the heart.

xlbE_F.title: Thyrotropic pituitary adenoma
xlbE_F.description: A pituitary adenoma that secretes TSH, resulting in secondary hyperthyroidism. Accounts for 1% of all pituitary adenomas.

Blbz_F.title: Ginkgo biloba
Blbz_F.description: An herbal supplement commonly used to treat several conditions (e.g., memory loss), though there is no robust clinical evidence to support its use. Generally well-tolerated but can cause disorders of hemostasis.

ylbdzF.title: Benztropine
ylbdzF.description: An anticholinergic agent that competitively antagonizes muscarinic acetylcholine receptors. About 1/2 as potent as atropine. Also has some antihistamine effects. Commonly used to treat extrapyramidal symptoms associated with antipsychotic drugs and as an adjunctive treatment for Parkinson disease.

AlbRzF.title: Pancreatic fistula
AlbRzF.description: An abnormal connection between the pancreatic ducts and surrounding organs or spaces (e.g., the peritoneal cavity, retroperitoneum). May be caused by trauma (e.g., surgery) or pancreatitis. The leakage of pancreatic secretions outside of the intestines may cause metabolic acidosis (due to bicarbonate loss) and malnutrition (due to impaired ingestion).

_lb5zF.title: Alcoholic ketoacidosis
_lb5zF.description: A complication of excessive alcohol intake presenting with elevated anion gap metabolic acidosis. Typically occurs following a period of binge drinking with little food intake and persistent vomiting.

zlbrzF.title: Thioridazine
zlbrzF.description: A first-generation antipsychotic used in the management of treatment-resistant schizophrenia.

-lbDzF.title: Complete blood count
-lbDzF.description: A laboratory test that measures red blood cell count, white blood cell count, hemoglobin, hematocrit, mean corpuscular volume, mean corpuscular hemoglobin, mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration, and platelet count. In a CBC with differential, the percentage of subtypes of white blood cells (e.g., neutrophils, lymphocytes, etc.) is also included.

ZNbZ-F.title: Aqueous humor
ZNbZ-F.description: The watery fluid secreted by the ciliary body that fills the anterior and posterior chambers of the eye. Overproduction or suppressed outflow of aqueous humor can cause glaucoma.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Segments and chambers of the eye

0Nbe-F.title: Trabecular meshwork
0Nbe-F.description: A mesh-like extracellular matrix that is primarily responsible for outflow of aqueous humor from the surface of the eye. It is closely linked to the ciliary muscle, and contraction of this muscle causes widening of the trabecular pores, while relaxation decreases the size of the pores.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Segments and chambers of the eye

aNbQ-F.title: Flunarizine
aNbQ-F.description: A nonspecific calcium channel blocker sometimes used for migraine prophylaxis.

YNbn-F.title: Apraclonidine
YNbn-F.description: An alpha-adrenergic receptor agonist (α2 > α1) used to acutely reduce intraocular pressure by decreasing aqueous humor production. Commonly used in the treatment of acute angle-closure glaucoma, after ophthalmologic procedures, and in the diagnostic workup of Horner syndrome.

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Anisocoria

XNb9-F.title: Open wound treatment
XNb9-F.description: A process that includes evaluating, cleaning, and closing a wound. Recent wounds that have a low risk of infection can directly be closed (primary closure). Infected wounds or wounds with foreign bodies should be treated openly (e.g., disinfection, drainage) before being closed (secondary closure).

1Nb2Z8.title: Dirty wound treatment
1Nb2Z8.description: The treatment of a wound containing foreign or infectious material. Foreign material can either be solid bodies (e.g., bullets, remaining suture material) or biological material (e.g., saliva from animal bites). Involves cleaning, disinfection, debridement, and drainage. Tetanus prophylaxis and antibiotic treatment are also necessary.

UNbb08.title: Rapid alternating movement test
UNbb08.description: A group of tests for dysdiadochokinesia characterized by performing rapidly alternating movements. One of these tests involves asking patients to tap their laps alternately with the palm and the back of their hand. Deficits in this task suggest a cerebellar lesion.

2NbT08.title: Guidelines for lipid-lowering therapy (ATP III guidelines)
2NbT08.description: A treatment used to improve serum lipid levels to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease. Includes general measures like dietary changes, weight management, and physical activity as well as medical therapy with statins or second-line agents.

gNbF08.title: Microcytic anemia
gNbF08.description: A type of anemia that is characterized by smaller than normal red blood cells (mean corpuscular volume < 80 fL), which are also often hypochromic. Causes include iron deficiency (most common), anemia of chronic disease, thalassemia, lead poisoning, vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) deficiency, and sideroblastic anemia.

hNbca8.title: Gag reflex
hNbca8.description: A brainstem reflex elicited by touching the back of the throat or roof of the mouth with a foreign object. In a positive test, the patient elevates his/her soft palate and pharyngeal muscles contract. The reflex is mediated by the afferent sensory pathways of CN IX and the efferent motor pathway of CN X.

3NbSa8.title: Sensory ataxia
3NbSa8.description: Ataxia that results from impaired proprioception. Most often caused by a peripheral neuropathy that affects large myelinated fibers or damage to the dorsal column. Patients typically have a positive Romberg's sign (ataxia worsens with the eyes closed).

RNbla8.title: Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis
RNbla8.description: A channelopathy caused by an autosomal dominant defect of voltage-gated sodium channels of the sarcolemmal membrane. Characterized by episodes of muscle weakness and/or myotonia precipitated by exposure to the cold, fasting, or after exercise. Named because hyperkalemia can also precipitate attacks, though patients are often normokalemic during episodes. Typical onset is in infancy or early childhood. Management includes preventive strategies (e.g., avoidance of potassium-rich foods) and supportive measures.

QNbua8.title: Preeclampsia with severe features
QNbua8.description: Preeclampsia with any of the following severe features: systolic blood pressure > 160 mm Hg or diastolic > 110 mm Hg, platelet count < 100,000, markedly elevated liver enzymes or RUQ pain, worsening renal insufficiency, pulmonary edema, severe persistent headache, or persistent/worsening visual symptoms.

jNb_a8.title: Focal seizure with impaired awareness
jNb_a8.description: Abnormal electrical activity that is localized to one hemisphere and impairs consciousness. Symptoms include behavioral arrest, automatisms (lip smacking, chewing), sensory hallucinations, and/or repetitive clonic movement.

destinations.label: Focal seizures and syndromes → Focal seizures with structural or metabolic cause

PNbWY8.title: Ictal
PNbWY8.description: The period of abnormal electrical brain activity when a seizure is occurring.

4Nb3Y8.title: Wing-beating tremor
4Nb3Y8.description: An upper extremity tremor that is exaggerated by holding the arms outstretched anteriorly or laterally with the elbows flexed and that becomes worse the longer the arms are held up. The patient resembles, very roughly, a bird flapping its wings, which gives the tremor its name. Classically associated with Wilson disease.

kNbmY8.title: Trihexyphenidyl
kNbmY8.description: A centrally-acting anticholinergic agent that inhibits excitatory cholinergic neurons, which decreases the concentration of acetylcholine. Used to treat Parkinson disease, parkinsonism, and drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms.

ONbIY8.title: Atrioventricular reciprocating tachycardia
ONbIY8.description: A supraventricular tachycardia that occurs as a result of a reentry circuit between an accessory pathway and the AV node. Two subtypes exist depending on the direction of reentry circuit: orthodromic AVRT and antidromic AVRT. Not to be confused with AVNRT where there is no accessory pathway and reentry occurs purely within the AV node.

lNbvY8.title: Tachycardia
lNbvY8.description: An increased heart rate. Defined as > 100 beats/min for adults and adolescents, > 140 beats/min for children 2-12 years of age, and > 160 beats/min for children < 2 years of age.

NNb-Y8.title: Deferoxamine
NNb-Y8.description: A trivalent metallic iron-chelating agent that binds free iron in plasma; the complex is then excreted in the urine. Used in the treatment of acute iron poisoning and hemochromatosis.

mNbVb8.title: Kyphoscoliosis
mNbVb8.description: A condition of excessive anterior (kyphosis) and lateral (scoliosis) misalignment of the spine (almost always the thoracic spine). If moderate to severe, kyphoscoliosis causes thoracic volume changes and may lead to restrictive breathing problems.

5Nbib8.title: Oculomotor apraxia
5Nbib8.description: The inability to coordinate head and eye movements, resulting in saccades (rapid eye movements).

LNbwb8.title: Apnea test
LNbwb8.description: An essential part of the evaluation of brain death, as it measures brainstem activity. After preoxygenation with 100% oxygen, the patient is disconnected from the ventilator and observed for evidence of respiratory drive (such as gasps or chest movement). After 8–10 minutes, an arterial blood gas reading is obtained. If the PCO2 is elevated above normal levels, this signifies an absence of respiratory drive, and the apnea test is considered positive.

oNb0X8.title: Oculocephalic maneuver
oNb0X8.description: A test of brainstem functioning primarily used to determine brain death. The patient's eyes are held open and the head is quickly rotated to one side. In a positive test, the patients eyes will move in the opposite direction as the head (i.e. if the patients head is rotated to the right, the eyes will look to the left). Though it is an important component of the neurological exam, it can only be performed if C-spine integrity is ensured.

KNbUX8.title: Latanoprost
KNbUX8.description: An analog of prostaglandin F2α used for the treatment of primary open-angle glaucoma. Reduces intraocular pressure by improving aqueous drainage.

6NbjX8.title: Trabeculectomy
6NbjX8.description: A surgical procedure for open angle glaucoma involving the creation of a tunnel (through excision of trabecular meshwork) from the anterior chamber to the subconjunctival space under a thin scleral flap. Facilitates drainage of aqueous humor, thereby lowering intraocular pressure.

pNbLX8.title: Breath-holding spell
pNbLX8.description: Episodes of prolonged expiratory apnea that occur among distressed, crying children. Typically seen in children aged 6 months to 6 years. May result in transient paroxysms of cyanosis or pallor, syncope, and/or anoxic seizures. Although these episodes may have a dramatic presentation, they are benign and usually require no treatment.

JNbsX8.title: Hypermagnesemia
JNbsX8.description: A serum magnesium concentration above 2.2-2.4 mg/dL (0.91-1.0 mmol/L). Often asymptomatic, but magnesium levels ≥ 4 mg/dL can cause neuromuscular symptoms (e.g., reduced deep tendon reflexes, lethargy, respiratory failure), cardiovascular symptoms (e.g., hypotension, bradycardia), and gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g., nausea, vomiting). The most common cause is renal insufficiency in combination with increased magnesium intake.

qNbCX8.title: Vasopressor
qNbCX8.description: A group of vasoconstrictive agents used to increase blood pressure in patients with impaired control of systemic vascular resistance (e.g., septic or neurogenic shock). Most vasopressors are either vasoconstrictive or ionotropic. Examples include epinephrine, norepinephrine, milrinone, phenylephrine, and vasopressin.

INbYc8.title: MDMA
INbYc8.description: A recreational drug related to amphetamines that produces feelings of euphoria and empathy in users 30 minutes to 1 hour after ingestion. Symptoms of intoxication are caused by sympathomimetic effects and include tachycardia, diaphoresis, hyperthermia, and dehydration.

rNbfc8.title: Bruxism
rNbfc8.description: Involuntary and repetitive teeth grinding and/or jaw clenching due to increased masticatory muscle activity. The cause of bruxism is not fully understood, but it is associated with psychological stressors and certain drugs (e.g., antidepressants, antipsychotics, stimulants).

7Nb4c8.title: Cortical laminar necrosis
7Nb4c8.description: A condition characterized by often irreversible tissue damage of the CNS. Caused by diseases leading to hyperthermia, hypoxia, hypoglycemia, or excitatory toxicity of the cerebral cortex (e.g., ischemic stroke, hypoglycemic encephalopathy, status epilepticus). Clinical features depend on the affected cortical areas.

HNbKc8.title: Grasp reflex
HNbKc8.description: A primitive reflex normally seen in infants up to 3–6 months of age. Consists of flexion of the fingers upon applying pressure on the palm of the hand (palmar grasp reflex) or flexion and adduction of the toes upon applying pressure to the sole of the feet (plantar grasp reflex). Can reappear in patients with damage to the frontal lobe.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

sNbtc8.title: Hypomania
sNbtc8.description: A mood state characterized by ≥ 4 consecutive days of persistently elevated, expansive, and/or irritable mood with ≥ 3 (or ≥ 4 if mood is only irritable) of the following: inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, flight of ideas, distractibility, increased goal-directed activity, and/or excessive involvement in risky activities. Unlike in mania, the episode is not severe enough to cause marked impairment in functioning or require hospitalization.

GNbBc8.title: Tiagabine
GNbBc8.description: An anticonvulsant that inhibits GABA reuptake. Used to treat focal seizures, with or without impairment of consciousness.

tNbX18.title: Cetuximab
tNbX18.description: A monoclonal antibody against the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) often used in the treatment of colorectal cancer and head and neck cancer. Adverse effects include elevated liver function tests, diarrhea, and an acneiform rash on the face, upper chest, and upper back.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

FNbg18.title: Maple syrup urine disease
FNbg18.description: An autosomal recessive disease caused by a deficiency of the branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex, which leads to the accumulation of valine, leucine, and isoleucine as well as their keto-acids. Manifests during the neonatal period with poor feeding, irritability or lethargy, vomiting, dystonia, hypoglycemia, and ketonuria with characteristic sweet-smelling urine.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Maple syrup urine disease

8NbO18.title: Organic acidemias
8NbO18.description: A collection of hereditary disorders characterized by the accumulation of organic acids. Typically caused by deficiencies and/or defects in enzymes required for the breakdown of the products of amino acid or fatty acid metabolism. Usually manifest in infancy with vomiting, lethargy, hypotonia, failure to thrive, seizures, anion gap metabolic acidosis, hyperammonemia, hypoglycemia, and urinary excretion of organic acids.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Organic acidemias

vNbA18.title: Lactose
vNbA18.description: A disaccharide made of glucose and galactose.

DNb1W8.title: Memory therapy
DNb1W8.description: A form of management for dementia that involves repeating tasks aimed at improving a specific area of cognitive function (e.g., memory, processing speed, reasoning). Tasks may be performed in individual or group settings. Example tasks include image recognition, problem solving, and reading and remembering.

yNbdd8.title: Bile acid resins
yNbdd8.description: Drugs designed to block bile acid resorption in the gut, leading to increased excretion in the stool. Used in the management of dyslipidemia (primarily by decreasing LDL levels) and bile acid diarrhea.

destinations.label: Second-line lipid-lowering agents → Bile acid resins

ANbRd8.title: SIGECAPS
ANbRd8.description:
A mnemonic for major depressive symptoms: Sleep (insomnia or hypersomnia), Interest loss (anhedonia), Guilt (low self-esteem), Energy (low energy or fatigue), Concentration (poor concentration or difficulty making decisions), Appetite (decreased appetite or overeating), Psychomotor agitation or retardation, and Suicidality.

The mnemonic refers to a prescription one might write for a depressed, anergic patient - SIG: Energy CAPSules.

_Nb5d8.title: Diabetic fetopathy
_Nb5d8.description: Any anomaly in a fetus associated with diabetes in the mother. Anomalies typically develop during the second and third trimesters and include macrosomia, postnatal hypoglycemia, and polycythemia due to fetal hyperinsulinemia during gestation.

destinations.label: Diabetes mellitus in pregnancy → Fetal and neonatal complications of diabetes mellitus in pregnancy

zNbrd8.title: Postpartum “blues”
zNbrd8.description: A mood disorder that occurs in up to 80% of women after delivery and is characterized by mild depressive symptoms, including tearfulness, sadness, or other mild forms of SIGECAPS symptoms except for suicidality. Symptoms for postpartum blues resolve within 2 weeks.

destinations.label: Major depressive disorder → Depression in the peripartum period

ZmbZV8.title: Phenobarbital
ZmbZV8.description: A barbiturate used to treat insomnia, anxiety disorders, alcohol withdrawal, and some seizure disorders. Second-line for status epilepticus.

0mbeV8.title: Schizophreniform disorder
0mbeV8.description: A psychiatric disorder characterized by symptoms of schizophrenia (e.g., delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, negative symptoms) that last for ≥ 1 month but < 6 months.

ambQV8.title: Brief psychotic disorder
ambQV8.description: A psychotic disorder that manifests with delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, and/or disorganized behavior. Symptoms last ≥ 1 day but < 1 month with a full return to the previous level of functioning.

YmbnV8.title: Delusional disorder
YmbnV8.description: A psychiatric disorder characterized by ≥ 1 delusion that lasts for ≥ 1 month but does not cause significant functional impairment. Common central themes of the delusions are grandiosity, jealousy, and persecution.

bmbHV8.title: Mood disorder with psychotic features
bmbHV8.description: A psychotic disorder that meets criteria for a mood disorder and shows psychotic features that appear exclusively during manic or depressive episodes. Mood symptoms may be present in the absence of psychosis.

Xmb9V8.title: Cerebrospinal fluid
Xmb9V8.description: The fluid that bathes the entire central nervous system. The fluid is produced by the choroid plexuses of the brain and flows through the ventricles and the subarachnoid space until it is reabsorbed by the arachnoid granulations. The primary function of CSF is to provide mechanical support to the CNS and transport biochemical compounds (e.g., neuromodulators).

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

cmbae8.title: Hypersomnolence disorder
cmbae8.description: A sleep disorder in which an individual feels unusually tired despite uninterrupted sleep for at least 7 hours. Hypersomnolence disorder is often accompanied by sleep inertia (difficulty waking up).

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Hypersomnolence disorder

1mb2e8.title: Delayed sleep phase disorder
1mb2e8.description: A circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder characterized by an antegrade shift of the sleep-wake cycle by > 2 hours, i.e., individuals go to bed very late in the evening and awake very late in the morning. If the individual attempts to go to bed early, they have sleep-onset insomnia; if the individual wakes up too early, they have daytime sleepiness.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders

embxe8.title: Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders
embxe8.description: A group of disorders characterized by persistent or recurrent pattern of excessive sleepiness, insomnia, and/or sleep disruption due to an alteration of the circadian system (e.g., alteration in exposure to sunlight with seasons, jet lag) or due to a misalignment between the endogenous circadian rhythm and the sleep-wake schedule required by an individual's environment (advanced or delayed sleep phase disorders).

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders

2mbTU8.title: Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder
2mbTU8.description: A mood disorder characterized by extreme irritability and severe recurrent outbursts of anger (verbal or physical). Outbursts are inappropriate for developmental age and occur > 3 times per week for > 12 months. Diagnosed between 6 and 18 years of age in individuals who do not meet the criteria for bipolar disorder.

destinations.label: Depressive disorders → Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder

fmbkU8.title: Laser trabeculoplasty
fmbkU8.description: A procedure for open-angle glaucoma in which a laser (e.g., argon laser or pulsed YAG laser) is used to stimulate the trabecular meshwork, facilitating drainage of aqueous humor and thereby lowering intraocular pressure.

Tmb6U8.title: Word salad
Tmb6U8.description: A feature of disorganized thought and speech characterized by speaking a sequence of words that have no logical connection (e.g., "Over the moon, ocean yellow a cabinet runs circle"). Typically associated with schizophrenia.

hmbc28.title: Jacksonian march
hmbc28.description: The spreading of paresthesia or uncontrolled motor activity during a simple partial seizure from a distal part of the body toward a more proximal part. Results from seizure activity that progresses to the motor cortex.

destinations.label: Focal seizures and syndromes → Focal seizures with structural or metabolic cause

imbJ28.title: Derailment
imbJ28.description: Incoherent and disorganized thought expressed verbally through rapid and dissociated switching from one topic to the next (e.g., "I took my mother shopping but the sun was so bright because the door was shut."). Common in schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders.

Qmbu28.title: Flight of ideas
Qmbu28.description: A stream of rapidly shifting and loosely connected ideas expressed verbally through fast, rambling speech and frequent jumps in topic. Associations are usually discernible and follow a unifying theme, but may appear incoherent due to digressions, distractions, and increased rate of speech. Commonly occurs in manic episodes, e.g., in bipolar disorder and schizophrenia.

jmb_28.title: Clang associations
jmb_28.description: A feature of disorganized thought and speech characterized by use of words based on rhyme patterns rather than meaning (e.g., "He fed the cat, bat, gnat with a hat, fat."). Typically associated with schizophrenia.

PmbWf8.title: Hallucinations
PmbWf8.description: A perception of something that is not present, i.e., a sensory perception that occurs in the absence of an adequate stimulus (perceptual disturbance). Most commonly auditory, but may also be visual, tactile, olfactory, or gustatory.

4mb3f8.title: Delusions
4mb3f8.description: A collection of fixed, false beliefs not attributable to a patient's culture or religion that are maintained despite being contradicted by reality or rational arguments. Can be bizarre or nonbizarre. Often occurs as a symptom of psychiatric conditions (e.g., schizophrenia).

kmbmf8.title: Holliday-Segar formula
kmbmf8.description: The most common method used to estimate maintenance fluid requirements in children. Calculated based on body weight (kg): (4 mL/kg/hr for first 10 kg of body weight) + (2 mL/kg/hr for second 10 kg) + (1 mL/kg/hr for each kg thereafter). E.g., a 25-kg child would require 65 mL/hr (40 mL for first 10 kg + 20 mL for second 10 kg + 5 mL for last 5 kg).

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Continued fluid needs

OmbIf8.title: Arnold-Chiari malformation
OmbIf8.description: A caudal displacement of the cerebellar tonsils, vermis, and fourth ventricle through the foramen magnum. Symptoms arise due to dysfunction of hindbrain cells and lower cranial nerves, as well as obstructed CSF outflow. Usually associated with hydrocephalus and spina bifida (myelomeningocele).

lmbvf8.title: Zileuton
lmbvf8.description: A leukotriene modifier that inhibits 5-lipooxygenase, reducing the production of leukotrienes. Decreases bronchoconstriction and inflammation. Used in the maintenance treatment of asthma (not for acute asthma attacks) and allergic rhinitis. Adverse effects include hepatotoxicity and excessive fatigue.

Nmb-f8.title: Cromolyn sodium
Nmb-f8.description: A mast cell stabilizer previously used to treat chronic asthma. Associated with minimal adverse effects, which include throat irritation and cough, but low treatment efficacy.

mmbVT8.title: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy
mmbVT8.description: A condition in which amyloid beta peptide deposits accumulate in the vessels of the CNS, increasing the risk for intracerebral hemorrhage. Most frequently associated with advanced age and Alzheimer disease.

MmbMT8.title: Subependymal giant cell astrocytoma
MmbMT8.description: Benign, slow-growing tumor of mixed glial cells that is associated with tuberous sclerosis. Typically arises in periventricular areas and, if symptomatic, presents subacutely with evidence of obstructive hydrocephalus (e.g., headache, papilledema).

omb0g8.title: Substance tolerance
omb0g8.description: The process of physical adaptation to the persistent use of a substance characterized by a diminished response to the substance and/or the need to steadily increase the dose for the same desired effect.

KmbUg8.title: Substance withdrawal
KmbUg8.description: A syndrome that occurs upon cessation or significant reduction of substance intake after prolonged use. Symptoms depend on the substance taken. Individuals often recommence taking the substance to avoid or relieve withdrawal symptoms. Substances associated with withdrawal are alcohol, amphetamines, cocaine, nicotine (tobacco), opioids, sedatives, hypnotics, anxiolytics, caffeine, and cannabis. Often the symptoms of withdrawal are opposite to those of intoxication (e.g., heroin intoxication causes sedation and constipation, while withdrawal causes anxiety, insomnia, and diarrhea).

6mbjg8.title: Congenital B-cell immunodeficiencies
6mbjg8.description: A group of immunodeficiencies caused by dysfunctions in B-cell maturation and/or function. Includes Bruton agammaglobulinemia, selective IgA deficiency, and common variable immunodeficiency.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital B-cell immunodeficiencies

pmbLg8.title: Congenital T-cell immunodeficiencies
pmbLg8.description: Hereditary partial or complete immunodeficiency of cell-mediated immunity caused by a lack and/or reduced function of T-cells. Common causes include SCID, DiGeorge syndrome, and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital T-cell immunodeficiencies

rmbfS8.title: Common variable immunodeficiency
rmbfS8.description: A primary immunodeficiency caused by B cells that are unable to differentiate into immunoglobulin-producing plasma cells, consequently leading to decreased serum immunoglobulins. Unlike most other primary immunodeficiencies, CVID is typically diagnosed after puberty, and patients usually have enlarged tonsils, lymph nodes, and/or splenomegaly.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital B-cell immunodeficiencies

HmbKS8.title: Hepatoblastoma
HmbKS8.description: A rare childhood tumor of liver precursor tissue that is usually diagnosed before the age of 3 years. Clinical features include a large, asymptomatic abdominal mass with increased liver size. The characteristic diagnostic finding is elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein levels. Treatment includes surgical resection, chemotherapy, or liver transplantation.

smbtS8.title: Mesoblastic nephroma
smbtS8.description: A congenital tumor of the kidney mesenchyma that is often diagnosed in utero or during the first 3 months of life. Usually unilateral. May lead to hematuria, hypercalcemia, and hypertension. Treatment involves nephrectomy soon after diagnosis.

GmbBS8.title: Pyrimethamine
GmbBS8.description: An antiparasitic agent that functions by inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase, thereby preventing tetrahydrofolate synthesis. It can also be used to treat malaria, pneumocystis pneumonia, and toxoplasmosis.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Sulfonamides and diaminopyrimidine

tmbXh8.title: Sulfadiazine
tmbXh8.description: A sulfonamide antibiotic that functions by antagonizing para-aminobenzoic acid, thereby inhibiting folate synthesis. It is used to treat Toxoplasma gondii encephalitis.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Sulfonamides and diaminopyrimidine

Fmbgh8.title: Hypokinesia
Fmbgh8.description: A decrease in muscle movement. Can manifest with rigidity and an inability to initiate or complete movements. Typically seen in patients with damage to the basal ganglia (e.g., from Parkinson disease).

destinations.label: Medication for Parkinson disease → Adverse effects

umbph8.title: Hypomagnesemia
umbph8.description: A serum magnesium concentration < 1.5 mg/dL (< 0.62 mmol/L). Associated with tetany, torsades de pointes, hypokalemia, and hypocalcemia.

Emb8h8.title: Low back pain red flags
Emb8h8.description: The presence of any of these symptoms in a patient with acute lower back pain indicates an increased risk of a more dangerous cause of symptoms and thus merit immediate workup (e.g., imaging): fecal/urinary retention/incontinence, saddle anesthesia, progressive weakness, significant weakness localizing to a single nerve root, history or high risk of malignancy, fever, immunosuppression, or osteoporosis.

vmbAh8.title: Gambling disorder
vmbAh8.description: A non-substance-related addictive disorder characterized by persistent and recurrent gambling that results in functional impairment.

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Gambling disorder

wmbh38.title: Dysautonomia
wmbh38.description: A dysfunction of processes that are regulated by the autonomic nervous system (e.g., urination, defecation, sweating, salivation, maintenance of blood pressure and heart rate). Etiologies include neurologic disease, age-related changes, and medication effects.

xmbE38.title: Vestibulocochlear nerve lesion
xmbE38.description: An injury to the vestibulocochlear nerve. Can be caused by infections (e.g., bacterial meningitis, Lyme disease) or tumors (e.g., acoustic neuroma).

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Vestibulocochlear nerve palsy (VIII)

Bmbz38.title: Pure motor stroke
Bmbz38.description: A clinical variant of a lacunar stroke, usually caused by lesions in the internal capsule. Patients manifest solely with contralateral hemiparesis of the face, arm, and leg.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

ymbdR8.title: Pure sensory stroke
ymbdR8.description: A clinical variant of a lacunar stroke, usually caused by lesions in the thalamus or posterior limb of the internal capsule. Patients present solely with contralateral numbness and paresthesia of the face, arm, and leg.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

AmbRR8.title: Dyssynergia
AmbRR8.description: A disturbance of muscular coordination that causes uncoordinated and abrupt movements. Seen in patients with neurodegenerative diseases including spinocerebellar ataxia.

_mb5R8.title: Varenicline
_mb5R8.description: A partial nicotine agonist used to aid smoking cessation. It reduces positive symptoms and prevents withdrawal symptoms. Adverse effects include headache, insomnia, depression, and suicidal ideation, so patient education and close monitoring for neuropsychiatric symptoms is recommended.

destinations.label: Tobacco product use and smoking cessation → Pharmacological treatment

Z5bZi8.title: Dihydrorhodamine test
Z5bZi8.description: A test in which a blood specimen is treated with dihydrorhodamine 123 and induced to make superoxide radicals. In normal cells, dihydrorhodamine 123 is oxidized to green fluorescent rhodamine 123, which can be measured by flow cytometry. In cells with defective NADPH oxidase (i.e., patients with chronic granulomatous disease), this reaction is impaired.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital neutrophil and phagocyte disorders

05bei8.title: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1
05bei8.description: A congenital immunodeficiency disorder caused by a defect in leukocytic chemotaxis. An autosomal-recessive mutation of the beta-2 integrin gene leads to defective expression of CD18, which prevents leukocyte migration into tissues. Classic features develop shortly after birth and include recurrent bacterial infections, impaired wound healing, delayed separation/infection of the umbilical cord, and leukocytosis (mainly due to neutrophilia).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital neutrophil and phagocyte disorders

Y5bni8.title: Job syndrome
Y5bni8.description: A condition caused by a mutation in STAT3 that results in Th17 cell deficiency and, thus, impaired neutrophil recruitment to sites of infection. Characterized by increased serum IgE concentrations. Manifestations include coarse facial features, recurrent abscesses, retained primary teeth, and eczema.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital T-cell immunodeficiencies

media.title: Autosomal dominant hyper-IgE syndrome fact sheet
Facial appearance of individuals with hyper IgE syndrome

15b2Q8.title: Terminal complement deficiency
15b2Q8.description: An autosomal recessive condition that causes deficiencies in terminal complement factors (C5–C9), and thus impaired formation of the membrane attack complex. Patients are at increased risk for Neisseria infections. Meningococcal vaccination and prophylactic antibiotics are recommended.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital complement deficiencies

W5bPQ8.title: Neurodegenerative brain diseases
W5bPQ8.description: A group of conditions that causes progressive impairment of memory, speech, reasoning, intellectual function, and/or spatial-temporal awareness. Examples include Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, and frontotemporal dementia.

d5boQ8.title: Marijuana
d5boQ8.description: A drug from the Cannabis plant that is used medically and recreationally. The main active component is tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), which influences the cannabinoid receptors CB1 and CB2. Intoxication can induce dysphoria, anxiety, and/or panic. Additional symptoms include conjunctival injection (red eyes), mydriasis, increased appetite (“munchies”), dry mouth, mild tachycardia, and impaired reaction time.

V5bGQ8.title: Cocaine
V5bGQ8.description: An addictive recreational stimulant that is either insufflated, smoked, or injected intravenously. Acts by inhibiting synaptic monoamine reuptake (serotonin, dopamine, norepinephrine, epinephrine), causing euphoria. Adverse effects arise from vasoconstriction causing nasal septal perforation (when insufflated); myocardial ischemia; CNS stimulation causing agitation, seizures, focal neurological deficits, hallucinations, and hyperthermia; and hemorrhagic alveolitis (crack lung) and rhabdomyolysis. Cocaine is also used therapeutically as a local anesthetic and vasoconstrictor, most commonly for ENT surgery.

e5bxQ8.title: Lysergic acid diethylamide
e5bxQ8.description: A hallucinogenic drug that acts by increasing serotonin and dopamine in the synaptic cleft. Common symptoms of intoxication include visual hallucinations and illusions, synesthesia, intensified perceptions, depersonalization, and confusion.

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Other hallucinogen use disorder

T5b6j8.title: Anticholinergic agents
T5b6j8.description: A group of agents that block acetylcholine at muscarinic or nicotinic receptors in the peripheral and central nervous system. Reduces activity of the parasympathetic nervous system in the gastrointestinal tract, urinary tract, and lungs. Can also be used as neuromuscular blockers.

g5bFj8.title: Lithium poisoning
g5bFj8.description: A condition caused by elevated serum lithium concentrations (e.g., due to overdose, decreased clearance from renal impairment, volume depletion). Features are highly variable but commonly include delirium, ataxia, fasciculations, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.

S5byj8.title: Biophysical profile
S5byj8.description: A noninvasive evaluation of fetal wellbeing. It consists of four parameters measured via ultrasound (fetal breathing, movement, tone, and amniotic fluid volume) and a nonstress test, which is optional if all ultrasound parameters are normal. Each parameter receives a score of either 0 (abnormal) or 2 (normal) points. The maximum score is 10. A score ≤ 4 indicates potential fetal compromise, which is often taken as an indication for delivery.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Antepartum fetal surveillance testing

35bSP8.title: Cerebral palsy
35bSP8.description: A heterogeneous group of disorders that affect muscle tone and the development of movement and posture. Results from nonprogressive damage to the brain in utero and/or during infantile development. Risk factors include prematurity, TORCH infections, intracerebral hemorrhage, and postnatal meningitis. Manifestations include spastic paresis, ataxia, involuntary movements (choreoathetosis, dystonia), dysarthria, and impaired intellectual development.

R5blP8.title: Cerebral aqueduct
R5blP8.description: A narrow channel in the midbrain which allows cerebrospinal fluid to flow between the 3rd and 4th ventricles. Stenosis of this structure causes non-communicating hydrocephalus due to obstruction of CSF flow from the 3rd to 4th ventricle.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

i5bJP8.title: Choroid plexus
i5bJP8.description: Specialized neuroepithelial tissue that is found in the walls of brain ventricles. The choroid plexus is responsible for CSF production.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Microscopic anatomy

Q5buP8.title: Choroid plexus papilloma
Q5buP8.description: A rare benign tumor of the choroid plexus. Typically presents with headache (and other symptoms of intracranial hypertension) due to hydrocephalus secondary to cerebrospinal fluid overproduction.

j5b_P8.title: Myositis-specific antibody
j5b_P8.description: A group of autoantibodies (with activity against various nuclear and cytoplasmic antigens) that are highly specific, but not sensitive, for several of the inflammatory myopathies.

O5bI48.title: Hypothyroid myopathy
O5bI48.description: A clinical feature of hypothyroidism that manifests as proximal muscle weakness with elevated creatine kinase levels.

l5bv48.title: Avolition
l5bv48.description: A reduced or absent ability to initiate purposeful activities. A negative symptom of schizophrenia.

m5bVk8.title: Illusions
m5bVk8.description: A perceptual disturbance in which a real external stimulus is misinterpreted (e.g., perceiving a stationary object as being in motion).

M5bMk8.title: Diabetic ketoacidosis
M5bMk8.description: A condition that is primarily seen in patients with type I diabetes and is caused by insufficient insulin levels (often secondary to acute infection). Manifests with hyperglycemia (usually 200-600 mg/dL), polyuria, polydipsia, nausea, vomiting, volume depletion (e.g., dry oral mucosa, decreased skin turgor), and eventually mental status changes and coma. Unlike in HHS, there is no insulin available to suppress fat breakdown; ketogenesis results. Treatment consists of IV insulin, electrolyte, and fluid replacement.

o5b0O8.title: Halothane
o5b0O8.description: An inhaled anesthetic agent. The mechanism of action is unknown, but it is thought to alter neuronal ion channels. Causes respiratory and myocardial depression. Adverse effects include hepatotoxicity and, rarely, malignant hyperthermia.

K5bUO8.title: Plantar flexion
K5bUO8.description: The anatomical movement of the foot in which the angle between the anterior surface of the leg and superior surface of the foot is increased (e.g., pressing down on a gas pedal, standing on tip toes). Facilitated by the  gastrocnemius and soleus muscles.

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion
The leg, ankle, and foot → Bones and joints

65bjO8.title: Dorsiflexion
65bjO8.description: The anatomical movement of the hand or foot in the dorsal direction. For the hand, this involves a decrease in the angle between the anterior surface of the forearm and superior surface of the hand (e.g. moving fingers closer to the forearm). For the foot, this involves a decrease of the angle between the anterior surface of the leg and superior surface of the foot (e.g. moving toes closer to the shin).

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Bones and joints
Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

p5bLO8.title: Peroneus longus
p5bLO8.description: A muscle located in the lateral compartment of the leg innervated by the superficial peroneal nerve. Primary actions are eversion of the foot and plantar flexion of the ankle.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

J5bsO8.title: Peroneus brevis
J5bsO8.description: A muscle located in the lateral compartment of the leg innervated by the superficial peroneal nerve. Primary actions are foot eversion and plantar flexion of the ankle.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

q5bCO8.title: Foot inversion
q5bCO8.description: The anatomical movement of tilting the sole of the foot toward the midline of the body.

I5bYl8.title: Foot eversion
I5bYl8.description: The anatomical movement of tilting the sole of the foot away from the midline.

r5bfl8.title: Chronic granulomatous disease
