r5bfl8.description: A congenital immunodeficiency syndrome caused by an X-linked or autosomal recessive defect in the phagocytic NADPH oxidase enzyme, which results in an inability of neutrophils and macrophages to produce superoxide radicals. Affected children typically present with recurrent, severe infections of the lungs, skin, bone, and lymph nodes by catalase-positive organisms (e.g., S. aureus, Serratia, Klebsiella, Aspergillus, Burkholderia).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital neutrophil and phagocyte disorders

75b4l8.title: Hyper-IgM syndrome
75b4l8.description:
A group of immunodeficiency syndromes characterized by a class-switching defect that results in decreased levels of IgG, IgA, and IgE with normal or elevated levels of IgM. The most frequent form is an x-linked recessive CD40 ligand deficiency. Patients are at increased risk for recurrent pyogenic infections and opportunistic
infection (e.g., pneumocystis, CMV).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital mixed immunodeficiencies

H5bKl8.title: IL-12 receptor deficiency
H5bKl8.description: An autosomal recessive T-cell immunodeficiency characterized by an impaired Th1 cell response due to a genetic lack of IL-12 receptors and subsequent reduction in IL-12 activity. Causes increased risk of disseminated mycobacterial and fungal infections. Can present after administration of the Bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) vaccine.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital T-cell immunodeficiencies

s5btl8.title: Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis
s5btl8.description: A group of congenital immunodeficiency syndromes characterized by impaired T-cell immunity against Candida species. Typically manifests with noninvasive Candida infections of the skin, mucous membranes, and nails.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital T-cell immunodeficiencies

G5bBl8.title: Chiari I malformation
G5bBl8.description: A caudal displacement of the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum. Symptoms include occipital headache, neck pain, radicular pain in the shoulders and arms, and lower cranial nerve palsies. Can be associated with syringomyelia and/or hydrocephalus.

F5bgN8.title: Depersonalization/derealization disorder
F5bgN8.description: Psychiatric condition defined by persistent or recurrent episodes of depersonalization, derealization, or both. Depersonalization symptoms include feeling detached with respect to one's own thoughts, feelings, body, and action. Derealization symptoms include detachment from surroundings (i.e. experiencing them as unreal, distorted, or dreamlike).

85bON8.title: Hemoglobin
85bON8.description: An iron-containing oxygen transport protein found in red blood cells. Reference ranges vary by source. Elevated in polycythemia vera and decreased in anemia.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

media.title: Oxygen dissociation curves for hemoglobin and myoglobin

u5bpN8.title: Glutamic acid decarboxylase
u5bpN8.description: An enzyme that decarboxylates glutamate to GABA and carbon dioxide. Isoforms of this enzyme may be targeted by autoantibodies in diseases such as diabetes, stiff person syndrome, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

v5bAN8.title: Braxton Hicks contractions
v5bAN8.description: Irregular, weak uterine contractions that do not increase in frequency, intensity or duration. These contractions may be noticed by the patient starting in the second trimester. They usually occur infrequently (typically ≤ 2/hour), last for up to 1 minute, and are not associated with cervical changes or descent of the presenting part. They typically stop with rest, walking, and/or a change in position.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Normal spontaneous labor

w5bhm8.title: Bloody show
w5bhm8.description: The detachment of the cervical mucus plug and subsequent passage of blood-tinged mucus through the vagina, suggesting the beginning of labor.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Normal spontaneous labor

95bNm8.title: Signs of placental separation
95bNm8.description: Clinical signs indicating separation of the placenta from the uterus during the third stage of labor include a sudden gush of blood, a firm, contracted uterine fundus, and lengthening of the umbilical cord.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Normal spontaneous labor

C5bqm8.title: Crowning
C5bqm8.description: The appearance of the fetal head at the vaginal opening during and between contractions. Seen during the second stage of labor.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Normal spontaneous labor

B5bzm8.title: Prolonged active phase of labor
B5bzm8.description: A condition diagnosed when cervical dilation during the active phase of labor (dilation ≥ 6 cm) does not accelerate further. The protraction is defined as a dilation < 1 cm per 2 hours.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormal stages of labor

A5bR58.title: Arrested active phase of labor
A5bR58.description: A condition diagnosed when cervical dilation is ≥ 6 cm in a patient with ruptured membranes and there is either no further cervical dilation for ≥ 4 hours despite adequate uterine contractions or no further cervical dilation for ≥ 6 hours in a patient with inadequate uterine contractions.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormal stages of labor

_5b558.title: Prolonged second stage of labor
_5b558.description: The failed delivery of the baby after 3 hours in a primiparous woman and after 2 hours in a multiparous woman (an extra hour can be added if an epidural was administered). Usually due to abnormalities of the 3 P's of labor (pelvis, passenger, power).

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormal stages of labor

-5bD58.title: Obstetric lacerations
-5bD58.description: A laceration of perineal skin and soft tissue that occurs during childbirth. Categorized as type 1 (laceration of vaginal mucosa and perineal skin only), type 2 (type 1 plus involvement of pelvic floor musculature and fascia), type 3 (type 2 plus involvement of the external anal sphincter), and type 4 (type 3 plus involvement of rectal mucosa).

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Complications of delivery

media.title: Surgical repair of second-degree perineal laceration

aMbQM8.title: Fern test
aMbQM8.description: A test used to diagnose ruptured membranes in pregnant patients. Vaginal fluid is placed on a glass slide and allowed to dry. Amniotic fluid creates a characteristic fern-like pattern under microscopy.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormal rupture of membranes

YMbnM8.title: Nitrazine test
YMbnM8.description: A test used for diagnosing premature rupture of membranes. Vaginal fluid is placed on a pH indicator strip. The strip turns blue (indicating pH >6.0) when the vaginal fluid is composed of amniotic fluid; can be falsely positive if there is semen, blood, or bacteria in the vaginal fluid.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormal rupture of membranes

bMbHM8.title: Granulopoiesis
bMbHM8.description: The process by which granulocytes develop from myeloid precursor cells in the bone marrow.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

XMb9M8.title: Brandt-Andrews maneuver
XMb9M8.description: An obstetric maneuver used to help to deliver the placenta after childbirth. Involves controlled downward traction on the umbilical cord while one hand is placed on the abdomen to secure the uterine fundus in place. If performed incorrectly, avulsion of the cord, pain, hemorrhage and inversion of the uterus can occur.

cMban8.title: Pathological myopia
cMban8.description: A type of myopia that begins during childhood and progressively worsens, which results in severe myopia by adulthood with a spherical equivalent refractive error that is > 6 diopters. Occurs as a result of increased axial growth of the eyeball (typically > 26.5 mm of axial length). Often accompanied by degenerative changes in the retina.

1Mb2n8.title: Rhabdomyoma
1Mb2n8.description: A benign tumor of striated muscle. May be either neoplastic or a hamartoma.

WMbPn8.title: Phenothiazines
WMbPn8.description: A group of drugs with antipsychotic and antiemetic properties that acts predominantly by dopamine receptor (D1 and D2) receptor antagonism but also has antimuscarinic, alpha blocker, and antihistaminergic effects. Agents include prochlorperazine and chlorpromazine.

dMbon8.title: Germinoma
dMbon8.description: A malignant tumor of undifferentiated germ cells that usually arises in the gonads, mediastinum, or pineal gland. It is histologically identical to dysgerminomas of the ovaries and seminomas of the testes.

VMbGn8.title: Bronchiolitis obliterans
VMbGn8.description: A chronic disease of the small airways, usually caused by repeated cycles of inflammation and scarring. Over time, scarring builds up and causes obstructive lung disease. Common etiologies include inhalation of toxic fumes and severe adenovirus pneumonia.

eMbxn8.title: Cortical signs
eMbxn8.description: Clinical features of damage to brain cortex, e.g. aphasia, hemianopsia, agnosia, and/or apraxia.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

UMbbL8.title: Interstitial emphysema
UMbbL8.description: A collection of gasses within the connective tissue of the lung that most commonly affects premature neonates. Air usually resides only within the bronchoalveolar tree but can escape if the alveoli become ruptured (e.g., due to barotrauma during mechanical ventilation, infection, respiratory distress syndrome).

2MbTL8.title: Internal capsule
2MbTL8.description: A deep subcortical structure that lies between the basal ganglia and is comprised of the anterior limb, genu, and posterior limb. Contains motor (corticospinal and corticobulbar) and somatosensory projection fibers, which form the corona radiata.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

fMbkL8.title: Dysarthria-clumsy hand syndrome
fMbkL8.description: A lacunar stroke syndrome that presents with dysarthria, dysphagia, facial weakness, and ipsilateral clumsiness (e.g., dysmetria, dysrhythmia, dysdiadochokinesia). Typically due to occlusion of penetrating arteries in the basal pons and internal capsule.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

gMbFL8.title: Partial-thickness biopsy
gMbFL8.description: An excisional biopsy procedure used to obtain a tissue sample of skin. Less invasive than a full-thickness biopsy, but more likely to miss important histological features. If a residual tumor is suspected, Mohs surgery can be used to resect it.

SMbyL8.title: Hyperglycemic crisis
SMbyL8.description: Complications of diabetes characterized by severe hyperglycemia and metabolic disturbances. Includes diabetic ketoacidosis (ketosis and metabolic acidosis) and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (extreme hyperglycemia, hyperosmolality, and dehydration without significant ketoacidosis).

hMbco8.title: Prosopagnosia
hMbco8.description: Inability to recognize familiar faces, but still able to name parts of the face (e.g., nose, mouth) or identify individuals by other cues (e.g., clothing, voices). Caused by bilateral lesions or large unilateral lesions of the ventral occipitotemporal cortex (fusiform gyrus).

3MbSo8.title: Peripheral artery bypass surgery
3MbSo8.description: An operative vascular reconstruction in which a vein (usually the great saphenous vein) or an artificial graft is used to bypass an arterial stenosis to improve blood flow to the distal extremities. Typically the preferred revascularization procedure in patients with long-segment arterial occlusion. Examples include femoro-popliteal, aorto-iliac, aorto-femoral, or femoro-femoral bypass for lower extremity peripheral arterial disease

media.title: Overview of peripheral artery bypass surgeries

RMblo8.title: Vincristine
RMblo8.description: A vinca alkaloid chemotherapeutic agent that inhibits microtubule formation in the mitotic spindle. Most commonly used to treat Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas, acute leukemia, rhabdomyosarcoma, neuroblastoma, and Wilms tumor. Adverse effects include mixed sensory and motor neuropathy and autonomic dysfunction.

iMbJo8.title: Primidone
iMbJo8.description: A barbiturate used for the treatment of epilepsy and essential tremor.

jMb_o8.title: Second wind phenomenon
jMb_o8.description: A characteristic finding in patients with McArdle's disease. Patients develop significant fatigue and myalgia soon after beginning exercise, but are able to resume exercise without significant symptoms after a short break. The phenomenon is believed to be due to recruitment of alternative energy sources (e.g., fatty acids) and increased blood flow to muscles.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Glycogen storage disorders (GSD)

PMbWK8.title: Pectus excavatum
PMbWK8.description: A sternal depression usually beginning at the manubrium and progressing down to the xiphoid process. The most common deformity of the anterior chest wall. Usually occurs sporadically, but is associated with connective tissue disorders (e.g., Marfan syndrome).

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Clinical features

4Mb3K8.title: Atypical antidepressant
4Mb3K8.description: A class of antidepressants that includes mirtazapine and bupropion. They are typically prescribed as second-line therapy for patients who fail initial SSRI therapy. However, they can sometimes be used as first-line drugs due to their favorable side-effect profile.

kMbmK8.title: Mycotic aneurysm
kMbmK8.description: An arterial aneurysm caused by infection of the vessel wall. Usually occurs due to bacteremia/fungemia or embolization from infective endocarditis.

OMbIK8.title: Frataxin
OMbIK8.description: A mitochondrial protein that normally interacts with iron transport and homeostasis in the cell. Loss of function due to a trinucleotide repeat in the frataxin gene causes the majority of cases of Friedreich ataxia.

lMbvK8.title: Major depressive disorder with mixed features
lMbvK8.description: "Mixed features" is a qualifying term added to either major depressive or bipolar disorder that describes a state of experiencing both depressive and manic symptoms simultaneously.

NMb-K8.title: Hummingbird sign
NMb-K8.description: A radiologic feature seen on midsagittal MRI of the brainstem in patients with progressive supranuclear palsy. Atrophy of the midbrain with relative sparing of the pons results in a pattern that resembles a bird.

mMbV68.title: DIG FAST
mMbV68.description: A mnemonic that summarizes the cardinal symptoms of a manic episode and thus provides a tool to screen for mania and, by extension, bipolar disorder: D-istractibility, I-mpulsive behavior, G-randiosity, F-light of ideas, A-ctivity increase, S-leep deficit, and T-alkativeness.

5Mbi68.title: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
5Mbi68.description: A congenital condition characterized by cutaneous capillary malformations (e.g., port-wine stain), varicose veins, and soft tissue or bony overgrowth, most commonly affecting the lower limbs.

MMbM68.title: Enuresis alarm
MMbM68.description: A treatment for enuresis that uses a moisture sensor embedded in the child's underwear or in a sleeping pad, which triggers an alarm and/or vibration, alerting the child and/or parent when involuntary urination begins.

nMb768.title: Type 1 diabetes
nMb768.description: A metabolic disease characterized by chronic hyperglycemia (elevated blood glucose levels) caused by autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. More commonly manifests in children.

LMbw68.title: Type 2 diabetes
LMbw68.description: A metabolic disease characterized by chronic hyperglycemia (elevated blood glucose levels) caused by peripheral insulin resistance and pancreatic beta cell dysfunction. More commonly appears in older adults.

oMb0p8.title: AUDIT-C
oMb0p8.description: A validated clinical tool used to identify alcohol misuse. It consists of 3 questions (scored from 0 to 4) that ask about frequency of alcohol consumption, number of alcoholic drinks in a typical day, and frequency of consuming ≥ 6 drinks on one occasion. Total scores range from 0 to 12: a score of ≥ 4 in men or ≥ 3 in women suggests alcohol misuse. Higher scores indicate higher risk.

6Mbjp8.title: Upper motor neuron damage
6Mbjp8.description: A lesion that affects the neural pathway above the anterior horn of the spinal cord or the motor nuclei of the cranial nerves. Etiologies include traumatic brain injury, stroke, and multiple sclerosis. Manifestations may include muscle weakness, spasticity, hyperreflexia, clonus, and a positive Babinski sign.

JMbsp8.title: Serotonin
JMbsp8.description: A monoamine neurotransmitter produced from tryptophan in the central nervous system (particularly the raphe nuclei), enterochromaffin cells of the enteric nervous system, and platelets. Signaling via serotonin receptors is involved in mood and cognition, gastrointestinal motility, and platelet aggregation.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

qMbCp8.title: Mononeuritis multiplex
qMbCp8.description: An asymmetrical sensory and/or motor peripheral neuropathy involving damage to ≥ 2 peripheral nerves in separate areas of the body. Common causes include diabetic microangiopathy, medium-vessel vasculitis, certain granulomatous diseases (e.g., sarcoidosis), amyloidosis, and certain infections (e.g., Lyme disease, leprosy, HIV).

IMbYJ8.title: Lenticulostriate arteries
IMbYJ8.description: The deep branches of the middle cerebral artery that supply the internal capsule, caudate nucleus, putamen, and globus pallidus. Common location for development of Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysms.

rMbfJ8.title: Buphthalmos
rMbfJ8.description: An enlargement of the eyeball due to increased intraocular pressure. Most commonly seen in infants and young children and is a sign of congenital glaucoma.

7Mb4J8.title: Isopropyl alcohol
7Mb4J8.description: An alcohol used as a disinfectant, antifreeze, and solvent. May be ingested accidentally or intentionally (e.g., as a substitute for ethanol). Typically causes CNS depression (sedation). Metabolized to acetone, a ketone, so serum and urine ketones are usually elevated.

destinations.label: Toxic alcohol poisoning → Isopropyl alcohol poisoning

HMbKJ8.title: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy
HMbKJ8.description: A disorder of the peripheral nervous system that primarily affects sensory nerves. Typically occurs within the first two months of chemotherapy, most commonly with cisplatin, docetaxel, and vincristine. May persist during and after treatment. Symptoms include numbness, pain, paresthesias, and dysesthesia in the hands and feet.

destinations.label: Complications of cancer therapy → Neurological complications

GMbBJ8.title: Primary gaze
GMbBJ8.description: The primary position of the eyes in binocular vision. The head is erect and the eyes are focused on a distant object that is lying at the intersection of the sagittal plane of the head and the horizontal line passing from the the center of rotation of each eye.

tMbXq8.title: Erythropoiesis
tMbXq8.description: The production of red blood cells (RBCs, erythrocytes) within the bone marrow.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Red cell line: erythrocytes

FMbgq8.title: Diamond-Blackfan anemia
FMbgq8.description: A genetic syndrome caused by an intrinsic defect of erythrocyte progenitor cells that leads to pure red cell aplasia. Other manifestations include short stature, webbed neck, low set ears, small jaw, and triphalangeal thumbs.

8MbOq8.title: Reticulocyte count
8MbOq8.description: A test that measures the concentration of reticulocytes in the blood. Typically reported as a fraction of all red blood cells. Normal range is 0.5-1.5%. Correlates with erythropoietic activity. Increased values can be caused by hemolysis and hemorrhage. Decreased values can be caused by aplastic anemia, chronic kidney disease, and bone marrow suppression.

uMbpq8.title: Reticulocyte production index
uMbpq8.description: A formula to calculate whether erythrocyte production in response to the degree of anemia is adequate. Calculated as reticulocyte percentage × (patient hematocrit/normal hematocrit)/reticulocyte maturation factor. Maturation factors for a given Hct: 20% = 2.5, 25% = 2, 35% = 1.5, 45% = 1. RPI ≥ 2 indicates adequate erythropoiesis; RPI < 2 indicates inadequate erythropoiesis (hypoproliferation).

EMb8q8.title: Red blood cell distribution width
EMb8q8.description: A measure of the range of RBC size or volume. A high RDW indicates a high degree of anisocytosis (unequal size of RBCs). Conditions associated with increased RDW include iron deficiency anemia, anemia due to vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, and conditions associated with reticulocytosis.

vMbAq8.title: Leukemia
vMbAq8.description: A group of conditions characterized by an increase in premature leukocytes that are subsequently released into the bloodstream. Consists of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL), chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), and chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL).

DMb1I8.title: Neutrophil granulocyte
DMb1I8.description: A type of white blood cell that accounts for approximately 40–60% of all granulocytes (besides eosinophils and basophils). Part of the innate immune system. Functions include antigen recognition, phagocytosis, and production of bactericides.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

wMbhI8.title: Neutropenia
wMbhI8.description: A decreased neutrophil count (mild: 1000–1499 cells/mcL; moderate: 500–999 cells/mcL; severe: < 500 cells/mcL). Most commonly caused by bone marrow damage, which can be drug-induced or due to malignancy or viral infection. Associated with an increased risk of infection.

9MbNI8.title: Eosinophilia
9MbNI8.description: An elevation in the number of eosinophils in the peripheral circulation, usually considered an absolute eosinophil count > 500/mm³. May be primary (hematologic etiology), secondary (reactive), or idiopathic.

CMbqI8.title: Eosinophil granulocyte
CMbqI8.description: A type of white blood cell, specifically a granulocyte, that mediates inflammatory/allergic reactions (via the secretion of proinflammatory cytokines), activates mast cells, and secretes antiviral, bactericide, and cytotoxic proteins (e.g., major basic protein). Accounts for approximately 3% of circulating granulocytes.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

xMbEI8.title: Basophil granulocyte
xMbEI8.description: A type of granulocyte that mediates immune reactions via the production of histamine and serotonin, prevents blood clotting by releasing heparin, and performs phagocytosis.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

BMbzI8.title: Monocyte
BMbzI8.description: A type of white blood cell that is part of the innate immune system. Monocytes differentiate into macrophages and act as antigen-presenting cells (via MHC-II), which activate the adaptive immune system.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

media.title: Normal monocyte in peripheral blood smear

yMbdr8.title: Mast cell
yMbdr8.description: A type of granulocyte cell found in interstitial connective tissue (e.g., around submucosa and surrounding blood vessels). Expresses receptors for the Fc portion of IgE antibodies. In response to allergen contact, IgE antibodies can trigger degranulation of mast cells, which causes histamine secretion, inflammation, and allergic symptoms.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

AMbRr8.title: Lymphocytosis
AMbRr8.description: An increase in the number of lymphocytes in the peripheral circulation. Can be absolute (i.e., elevated total lymphocyte count) or relative (i.e., elevation in the proportion of leukocytes that are lymphocytes). Etiologies include infections (especially viral), leukemia, and chronic inflammation (e.g., autoimmune diseases).

_Mb5r8.title: Lymphopenia
_Mb5r8.description: A decrease in the number of lymphocytes circulating in the blood to below the normal range (cutoff values vary). Etiologies include immunodeficiencies, autoimmune disorders (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis), infections (e.g., tuberculosis, viral infections), malignancies (e.g., lymphoma), and medication-induced reactions (e.g., immunosuppressive agents, chemotherapy).

zMbrr8.title: Natural killer cells
zMbrr8.description: A type of lymphocyte that can detect downregulation of MHC class I molecules (e.g., by tumor cells or virally-infected cells). In response, they activate and release cytotoxic granules (perforin and granzyme) that induce lysis of target cells.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Lymphoid cell line

-MbDr8.title: T lymphocytes
-MbDr8.description: A type of white blood cells that originate from hematopoietic stem cells and mature in the thymus. An important part of cell-mediated immunity, which is especially vital to viral and fungal immunity. Sometimes divided according to the CD4 subtype that they express. Subtypes include helper (CD4+), cytotoxic (CD8+), memory, effector, regulatory, and natural killer T-cells.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

media.title: Maturation of T cells in the thymus
Effects of T-helper cells in secondary lymphatic organs

ZnbZ78.title: Memory T cells
ZnbZ78.description: A type of T cell involved in memory formation as part of the acquired immune response. In response to re-exposure to a previously encountered antigen, memory T cells induce a faster and stronger immune response. Expresses CD4 and CD8 surface markers.

0nbe78.title: Regulatory T cells
0nbe78.description: A type of T cell that limits and downregulates the immune response, including the prevention of autoimmune disease by maintaining tolerance to self-antigens. Expresses CD4 surface marker.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

anbQ78.title: T-helper cells
anbQ78.description: A type of CD4-positive T cell that functions in augmenting and coordinating the immune response. Releases cytokines in response to recognition of antigens presented on MHC-II receptors. Subtypes include Th1, Th2 and Th17 cells. The specific subtype determines which cytokines are released and, consequently, the type of immune response.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

Ynbn78.title: Cytotoxic T cells
Ynbn78.description: A type of T cell that expresses the CD8 surface marker. Recognizes foreign antigens presented on MHC-I receptors and subsequently triggers apoptosis or cell lysis of the presenting (infected) cell.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

Xnb978.title: B lymphocytes
Xnb978.description: A type of white blood cells that develops from hematopoietic stem cells. A key to adaptive immunity, as B cells (by interacting with helper T cells) develop into pathogen-specific memory B cells and antibody-secreting plasma cells. The main subtypes of B cells include: plasma cells, memory B cells, follicular B cells, marginal zone B cells, and regulatory B cells.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

cnbaH8.title: Plasma cell
cnbaH8.description: A differentiated B lymphocyte that secretes immunoglobulins that target a specific antigen.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

1nb2H8.title: Toxoid vaccine
1nb2H8.description: A type of vaccination in which a bacterial toxin is used to induce an immune response. These toxins are modified to lose their toxicity while maintaining immunogenicity. Examples include the diphtheria and tetanus vaccines.

WnbPH8.title: Sleepwalking disorder
WnbPH8.description: A non-REM sleep arousal disorder characterized by episodes of sitting up, walking, or eating, as well as a blank stare (eyes open), in the first third of the sleep cycle. It is difficult to rouse the individual during an episode of sleepwalking and there is no recollection of the episode when he/she wakes up.

VnbGH8.title: Zafirlukast
VnbGH8.description: A leukotriene-receptor antagonist used in maintenance treatment of asthma and allergic rhinitis. Acts to decrease bronchoconstriction and inflammation. Not used for treatment of acute asthma attacks.

enbxH8.title: Leukotriene receptor antagonists
enbxH8.description: A class of drugs that blocks the leukotriene receptor. Acts to decrease bronchoconstriction and inflammation. Used in the maintenance treatment of asthma (not for acute asthma attacks) and allergic rhinitis.

Unbbs8.title: Asthma exacerbation
Unbbs8.description: A worsening of asthma symptoms that develops over a short period of time (may be acute or subacute). For some patients, this may be the first manifestation of asthma.

2nbTs8.title: Hereditary motor sensory neuropathy type I
2nbTs8.description: A hereditary motor sensory neuropathy caused by mutations of several genes that affect myelin structure, maintenance, and formation. Common features include distal leg weakness, foot deformities, and sensory deficits.

hnbcG8.title: Polyneuropathy
hnbcG8.description: A condition involves damage to multiple peripheral nerve fibers. Etiologies include diabetes mellitus, alcoholism, vitamin B12 deficiency, drug adverse effects, and certain inflammatory conditions (e.g., Guillain-Barre syndrome). Patients typically present with symmetric distal sensory loss or a burning sensation associated with motor weakness.

3nbSG8.title: Cimetidine
3nbSG8.description: An H2 receptor inhibitor that suppresses gastric acid secretion. Used to treat various conditions that cause or are exacerbated by excess acid production (e.g., peptic ulcer disease, gastroesophageal reflux disease)

RnblG8.title: Left axis deviation
RnblG8.description: An electrocardiographic finding in which the mean angle of ventricular depolarization (i.e., the QRS complex) is between -30º and -90º. LAD is present if the QRS complex is upright in lead I and down in lead II. Common causes for LAD include: left ventricular hypertrophy, left bundle branch block, and old inferior myocardial infarction.

destinations.label: ECG → Determination of the cardiac axis

media.title: Left bundle branch block with left axis deviation

inbJG8.title: Simple partial seizure
inbJG8.description: Abnormal electrical activity that is localized to one side of the brain in which consciousness is preserved. Symptoms can be motor (e.g., jerking arm movements), sensory (e.g., gustatory hallucination), autonomic (e.g., tachycardia), or psychic (e.g., déjà vu).

QnbuG8.title: Broca aphasia
QnbuG8.description: A form of aphasia caused by lesions in the inferior frontal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere. Language production is greatly limited, resulting in non-fluent, telegraphic, and grammatically incorrect speech. The patient is unable repeat after the examiner. Language comprehension, however, is intact.

jnb_G8.title: Wernicke aphasia
jnb_G8.description: A form of aphasia caused by lesions in the superior temporal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere characterized by impaired language comprehension and repetition. Affected patients can speak fluently, but usually produce nonsensical phrases. The patient is unaware of these deficits. Visual field defects (e.g. contralateral superior quadrantanopia) may be seen as well.

OnbIt8.title: Hyperactive delirium
OnbIt8.description: A type of delirium characterized by increased psychomotor activity (e.g., agitation). Most commonly occurs in cases of delirium due to substance use or substance withdrawal. Patients are at increased risk for falls and removal of intravenous lines and feeding tubes. Management strategies include standard delirium precautions (e.g., maintaining a regular schedule, keeping a clock and calendar in the room); restraints and antipsychotic medications are second-line therapy.

lnbvt8.title: Parkinsonian gait
lnbvt8.description: A shuffling gait with quick, shortened steps due to rigidity of the muscles. Classically seen in patients with Parkinson disorder.

Nnb-t8.title: Substance use disorders
Nnb-t8.description: A class of psychiatric disorders characterized by cognitive and behavioral changes and physical symptoms related to the continued use of one or more substances despite negative consequences.

mnbVF8.title: Tertiary wound closure
mnbVF8.description: A category of wound healing combining primary and secondary closure and used for potentially contaminated wounds. The wound is left open for several days of observation and then sutured if there are no signs of infection. Indications include animal bites and lacerations with foreign bodies.

5nbiF8.title: Chédiak-Higashi syndrome
5nbiF8.description: A rare congenital immunodeficiency syndrome that is caused by an autosomal recessive defect in the lysosomal trafficking regulator gene (LYST). This mutation results in a defect in neutrophil chemotaxis/microtubule polymerization. Clinical features include recurrent pyogenic infections, oculocutaneous albinism, mild bleeding diathesis, and progressive neuropathies. Patients eventually enter a fatal accelerated phase (hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital neutrophil and phagocyte disorders

MnbMF8.title: Diethylstilbestrol
MnbMF8.description: A synthetic nonsteroidal estrogen used in the US from 1938 to 1971 to prevent pregnancy complications (e.g., miscarriage) until it was banned by the FDA. Pregnant women who took DES have an increased risk of breast cancer. In utero DES exposure increases the risk for clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina and cervix and can lead to structural reproductive system anomalies in the unborn child that result in increased infertility rates and poor pregnancy outcomes.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

nnb7F8.title: Mitochondrial myopathies
nnb7F8.description: A group of rare disorders characterized by impaired energy production that mainly affects organs with a high energy requirement (e.g., brain, skeletal muscle). Muscle biopsy shows an accumulation of abnormal mitochondria that have a ragged red fiber appearance.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Mitochondrial myopathies

LnbwF8.title: Mucopolysaccharidoses
LnbwF8.description: A group of rare inherited metabolic disorders that result in impaired breakdown of glycosaminoglycans due to mutations in lysosomal enzymes. The most common disorders of this group are Hurler syndrome and Hunter syndrome.

onb088.title: Modified Bishop score
onb088.description: A scoring system used to evaluate the potential for successful elective labor induction. Components include cervical dilation (the extent of opening of the cervical os), cervical length (which replaces cervical effacement in the original Bishop score system), fetal station (position of the fetal head in relation to the ischial spines), cervical position (e.g., posterior, middle, or anterior), and cervical consistency (e.g., firm, medium, or soft).

KnbU88.title: Preterm prelabor rupture of membranes
KnbU88.description: A rupture of membranes that occurs before the onset of uterine contractions and before 37 weeks' gestation. Associated with a variety of complications, including preterm delivery, pulmonary hypoplasia, chorioamnionitis, umbilical cord prolapse, and placental abruption.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormal rupture of membranes

6nbj88.title: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy
6nbj88.description: A rare disease of pregnancy that is caused by dysfunction of fatty acid β-oxidation. It most commonly occurs in the third trimester, and is characterized by extensive fatty infiltration of the liver, which can result in acute liver failure. Symptoms include are jaundice, RUQ pain, nausea, and vomiting.

destinations.label: Pregnancy-associated liver diseases → Acute fatty liver of pregnancy

Jnbs88.title: Lysosomal acid maltase
Jnbs88.description: An enzyme encoded by the GAA gene that is responsible for degrading glycogen to glucose in the lysosome. Deficiency of the enzyme results in Pompe Disease (glycogen storage disease II).

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Glycogen storage disorders (GSD)

media.title: Glycogenolysis through splitting of α-1,4-glycosidic bond

qnbC88.title: Glucose-6-phosphatase
qnbC88.description:
An enzyme responsible for catalyzing the final step of glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, the conversion of glucose-6-phosphate to glucose. Deficiency results in von Gierke's Disease (glycogen storage disease I).
Should not be confused with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase.

InbYu8.title: Glycogen debranching enzyme
InbYu8.description: An enzyme that removes the final four glucose molecules from a branch of glycogen. In the process of glycogenolysis, glycogen phosphorylase removes glucose monomers (with α-1,4 linkages) until the last four remain. Because the type of bond then changes (α-1,6 linkages), glycogen debranching enzyme is required. Deficiency causes Cori disease.

media.title: Glycogenolysis through cleavage of α-1,6-glycosidic bond

rnbfu8.title: Glycogen phosphorylase
rnbfu8.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the release of glucose-1-phosphate from glycogen, the rate-limiting step in glycogenolysis. Deficiency of this enzyme results in McArdle Disease (glycogen storage disease type V).

media.title: Glycogenolysis through splitting of α-1,4-glycosidic bond

7nb4u8.title: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase
7nb4u8.description: The enzyme responsible for catalyzing the first step in beta-oxidation of fatty acids.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

snbtu8.title: Intraventricular hemorrhage
snbtu8.description: Bleeding into the ventricular system of the brain. In infants, prematurity is a very strong risk factor. In older children and adults, trauma and vascular anomalies are the most common causes. The prognosis for an adult is very poor.

GnbBu8.title: Superior rectus muscle
GnbBu8.description: An extraocular muscle innervated by the oculomotor nerve (CN III). Functions include: elevation, intorsion (internal, or medial, rotation), and adduction of the eye.

tnbXE8.title: Inferior rectus muscle
tnbXE8.description: An extraocular muscle innervated by the oculomotor nerve (CN III). Functions include: depression, extorsion (external, or lateral, rotation), and adduction of the eye.

media.title: Blowout fracture of the orbital floor

FnbgE8.title: Disconjugate movements
FnbgE8.description: Movement of the eyes in opposite directions: e.g., convergence (in which both eyes adduct) or divergence (in which both eyes abduct).

8nbOE8.title: Conjugate gaze palsy
8nbOE8.description: An impaired ability of the eyes to move in a single direction (e.g., horizontal or vertical). Typically caused by brainstem lesions (e.g., from stroke, tumor).

unbpE8.title: Class 3 obesity
unbpE8.description: An obesity category defined by BMI ≥ 40 kg/m² in adults and ≥ 140% of the 95th percentile for age and sex in children. A cutoff of ≥ 35 kg/m² is recommended for adults of Asian descent.

Enb8E8.title: Rathke cleft cyst
Enb8E8.description: A benign, intrasellar/suprasellar cysts that arise from the remnants of the Rathke pouch. Typically asymptomatic, but can manifest with headache, visual disturbances, and hypopituitarism.

vnbAE8.title: Mid-parental height
vnbAE8.description:
Estimated adult height of a child calculated on the basis of parental height using the following formulas:
♂: [(Paternal height + Maternal height)/2] + 2.5" (6.5 cm) 
♀: [(Paternal height + Maternal height)/2] - 2.5" (6.5 cm)

wnbhv8.title: Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1
wnbhv8.etymology: Abbreviations: APS-1, PGA syndrome type 1, APECED
wnbhv8.description: An autosomal recessive disease caused by a mutation on the AIRE gene on chromosome 21. Manifestations include hypoparathyroidism, chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, adrenal insufficiency, primary hypogonadism, and malabsorptive disorders.

xnbEv8.title: Amniotic fluid index (AFI)
xnbEv8.description: An ultrasound measurement of amniotic fluid volume. The gravid uterus is divided into four quadrants and the deepest fluid pocket of each (excluding fetal parts, placenta, and umbilical cord) is measured. The amniotic fluid index is the sum of these four measurements. A value < 5 cm indicates oligohydramnios and ≥ 24 cm is consistent with polyhydramnios.

ynbdD8.title: Hypercholesterolemia
ynbdD8.description: A condition of elevated cholesterol. May be caused by primary inherited conditions (e.g., familial hypercholesterolemia) or secondary acquired conditions (e.g., obesity, hypothyroidism, medication-induced). Diagnosed if the average of two fasting lipid panels confirms elevated cholesterol levels (most commonly measured with LDL) based on age and ASCVD risk factors.

AnbRD8.title: Paramedian midbrain syndrome
AnbRD8.description: A condition characterized by ipsilateral oculomotor nerve palsy, contralateral hemiataxia, and a contralateral tremor due to damage to the tegmentum of the midbrain (e.g., due to compression or infarction of branches of the posterior cerebral artery). Can also manifest with contralateral sensory loss.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

_nb5D8.title: Ductal ectasia
_nb5D8.description: A chronic inflammatory condition of the breast characterized by dilatation of the terminal (subareolar) lactiferous ducts. Typically manifests as unilateral green or bloody nipple discharge with or without a subareolar mass. Most commonly seen in perimenopausal women.

znbrD8.title: Vitamin C
znbrD8.description: A water-soluble vitamin and enzymatic cofactor for lysyl and prolyl hydroxlases, both of which are important enzymes in the synthesis of collagen. Vitamin C deficiency results in scurvy.

-nbDD8.title: Chondrodystrophy
-nbDD8.description: A general term referring to skeletal disorders arising from an abnormality in cartilage development.

ZLbZw8.title: Psychosis
ZLbZw8.description: An impaired perception of reality characterized by delusions, hallucinations, and/or disorganized thinking. Psychosis may be primary (caused by an underlying psychiatric disorder) or secondary (caused by a medical disorder or substance-induced).

0Lbew8.title: D2 receptor
0Lbew8.description: A Gi-coupled dopamine receptor that mediates motor function and is located mainly in the substantia nigra, striatum, area postrema, and pituitary gland. Loss of receptors (e.g., in multiple system atrophy) or stimulation (e.g., in Parkinson disease) results in impaired motor function while overstimulation can induce psychotic symptoms.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

aLbQw8.title: Absence status epilepticus
aLbQw8.description: A type of nonconvulsive status epilepticus characterized by absence seizures lasting longer than 10 minutes (usually hours or days).

YLbnw8.title: Epileptic spasm
YLbnw8.description: Sudden flexion and/or extension that predominantly affects truncal and proximal muscles, lasts for 1-2 seconds and occurs in clusters typically upon awakening. The most common cause is West syndrome (infantile spasms).

bLbHw8.title: Bimanual uterine massage
bLbHw8.description: Manual technique used in postpartum hemorrhage caused by uterine atony to promote uterine contractions and to tamponade the vascular sinuses in the uterus. Performed by placing one hand in the vagina and pushing against the body of the uterus while the other hand compresses the fundus from above through the abdominal wall. The posterior aspect of the uterus is massaged with the abdominal hand and the anterior aspect with the vaginal hand.

XLb9w8.title: Acute symptomatic seizures
XLb9w8.description: A seizure that occurs at the time or soon after acute conditions such as metabolic and electrolyte disturbances, brain tumors, alcohol withdrawal, toxicity, CNS infections, stroke, and traumatic brain injury. Can be focal or generalized.

cLba98.title: Lower motor neuron lesion
cLba98.description: A lesion located anywhere along the nerve fibers between the anterior horn of the spinal cord and relevant muscle tissue. Causes flaccid paresis with muscle weakness, atrophy, diminished reflexes, and an absent Babinski sign.

dLbo98.title: Cytarabine
dLbo98.description: A pyrimidine analog that inhibits DNA polymerase. Used in the treatment of leukemias, especially acute myelogenous leukemia in adults and lymphomas. Adverse effects include myelosuppression with megaloblastic anemia.

VLbG98.title: Cochlear aqueduct
VLbG98.description: A fine duct connecting the perilymphatic space of the cochlea with the subarachnoid space of the brain. The duct is one possible route by which an ear infection can cause meningitis. Meningitis can also cause delayed hearing loss if bacteria/viruses from the spinal fluid enter the inner ear through the cochlear aqueduct.

eLbx98.title: Eastern equine encephalitis
eLbx98.description: A mosquito-borne disease that causes a life-threatening inflammation of the CNS. Onset of symptoms occurs 4 to 10 days after infection, with typical initial symptoms including fever and headache. Rapid deterioration (e.g., seizures, coma, or death) follows shortly thereafter. There is no treatment, and approximately 30% of patients die within 5 days of diagnosis.

destinations.label: Miscellaneous mosquito-borne diseases → Mosquito-borne Togavirus diseases

ULbbC8.title: Neurogenic hyperthermia
ULbbC8.description: A noninfectious cause of fever, due to dysfunction of the anterior hypothalamus (usually after head trauma) that impairs the body's ability to dissipate heat.

2LbTC8.title: Pulse pressure
2LbTC8.description: The difference between systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure, which is normally 30–40 mm Hg in adults. Low (narrow) pulse pressure is usually due to a decrease in stroke volume (e.g., congestive heart failure, shock, cardiac tamponade, aortic stenosis). High (wide) pulse pressure is usually due to an increase in stroke volume (e.g., normal exercise, aortic regurgitation) or stiff arteries.

TLb6C8.title: Intra-abdominal pressure
TLb6C8.description: The pressure within the abdominal compartment. In adults, pressures < 12 mm Hg are normal, with an average typically ~ 5 mm Hg. In children, values are typically lower. Intra-abdominal hypertension occurs when IAP is ≥ 12 mm Hg. Compartment syndrome occurs when IAP is > 20 mm Hg.

gLbFC8.title: Naegleria fowleri
gLbFC8.description: A pathogenic amoeba found in bodies of warm, fresh water. Invades the CNS via the cribriform plate. Once there, it consumes glial cells, leading to the rapid development of fulminant meningoencephalitis. Mortality rates approach 100%.

destinations.label: General parasitology → Protozoa that cause ocular and neurological disease

SLbyC8.title: Epilepsy syndrome
SLbyC8.description: A condition characterized by a certain type of seizures that has a typical age of onset and is accompanied by characteristic EEG patterns and other clinical features, such as loss of motor skills and psychomotor retardation. Examples include juvenile absence epilepsy, Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, Dravet syndrome, Ohtahara syndrome, Doose syndrome, and West syndrome.

3LbSx8.title: Breastfeeding jaundice
3LbSx8.description: A type of neonatal jaundice caused by insufficient breastfeeding. The lack of calories and reduced bowel movements (normally stimulated by food intake) result in decreased bilirubin excretion and consequently increased bilirubin reabsorption, leading to hyperbilirubinemia.

RLblx8.title: Breast milk jaundice
RLblx8.description: A type of neonatal jaundice caused by increased levels of beta-glucuronidase in maternal breast milk. Beta-glucuronidase increases deconjugation and reabsorption of bilirubin, which leads to hyperbilirubinemia.

iLbJx8.title: Paranoia
iLbJx8.description: A thought pattern characterized by irrational suspicion or mistrust. Paranoia may be a manifestation of a psychiatric disorder such as schizophrenia and may involve paranoid delusions.

QLbux8.title: All-trans retinoic acid
QLbux8.description: A vitamin A-derivative that can be used topically for the treatment of mild to moderate acne vulgaris and systemically for acute promyelocytic leukemia.

jLb_x8.title: Lenalidomide
jLb_x8.description: An antineoplastic agent used to treat multiple myeloma and some myelodysplastic syndromes. The mechanism of action is complex, but the end result is induction of apoptosis. Adverse effects include venous thromboembolism and Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

PLbWB8.title: Cladribine
PLbWB8.description: A chemotherapeutic agent used to treat hairy cell leukemia. It is an adenosine analog that acts as an antimetabolite, effectively halting the reproductive capability of cells. The drug is preferentially activated in lymphocytes and monocytes, so adverse effects are limited.

OLbIB8.title: Centor score
OLbIB8.description: A set of criteria used to estimate the probability that pharyngitis is streptococcal (i.e., caused by group A Streptococcus).

media.title: Modified Centor score for group A streptococcal infection

lLbvB8.title: Vas deferens
lLbvB8.description: The duct that carries sperm from the testicles to the urethra.

destinations.label: Male reproductive organs → Epididymis, ductus deferens, and accessory glands

NLb-B8.title: Korotkoff sounds
NLb-B8.description: The sounds heard when auscultating over the brachial artery during sphygmomanometry. Korotkoff sounds are a result of turbulent blood flow through a brachial artery that is partially compressed by the inflated arm cuff of a sphygmomanometer. When deflating the cuff, the pressure at which Korotkoff sounds appear marks systolic BP, and the pressure at which Korotkoff sounds disappear marks diastolic BP.

mLbVy8.title: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
mLbVy8.description: An inability of the pancreas to produce enzymes necessary for digestion, such as trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, lipases, cholesterol esterase, and amylase. Results in malabsorption of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and fat-soluble compounds (notably vitamins A, D, E, K, B12, albumin, and calcium), which leads to steatorrhea and weight loss. Common causes include chronic pancreatitis and cystic fibrosis.

5Lbiy8.title: Tissue transglutaminase antibodies
5Lbiy8.description: A collection of IgG and IgA autoantibodies that are pathologically specific to tissue transglutaminase. Exposure to gluten sensitizes B cells to produce these antibodies. Present in over 90% of patients with celiac disease.

MLbMy8.title: Situs inversus
MLbMy8.description: A rare, genetic condition in which some or all major visceral organs are positioned opposite from their normal position. Can be seen in isolation or as a feature of primary ciliary dyskinesia.

media.title: Situs inversus due to Kartagener syndrome
Situs inversus with dextrocardia (situs inversus totalis)

nLb7y8.title: Automatism
nLb7y8.description: Brief episodes of unconscious behavior, such as lip smacking, chewing, finger rubbing. These are typically associated with focal seizures.

KLbUA8.title: Pediculosis ciliaris
KLbUA8.description: An infestation of Pthirus pubis, spread through direct head-to-head contact or shared bedding, clothing, or towels. Manifests with eye pruritus, crusted eyelashes, and lice and/or nits at the eyelash base.

destinations.label: Lice infestation → Pediculosis ciliaris (eyelash lice infestation)

6LbjA8.title: Hypercyanotic spells
6LbjA8.description: Episodes of severe cyanosis that develop due to worsening of right ventricular outflow tract obstruction in patients with tetralogy of Fallot. Episodes are typically triggered by agitation or exercise. Children often assume a squatting position, which increases systemic vascular resistance, thereby increasing blood flow through the pulmonary vasculature.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Tetralogy of Fallot

media.title: Tet spell in tetralogy of Fallot

pLbLA8.title: Primary ovarian insufficiency
pLbLA8.description: Impaired ovarian function in female individuals younger than 40 years of age due to a primary defect in the ovaries that decreases follicle numbers or results in an insufficient response to gonadotropin stimulation. Often idiopathic; identifiable causes can be genetic (e.g., Turner syndrome), autoimmune (e.g., thyroid disease), infectious (e.g., mumps infection), or iatrogenic (e.g., chemotherapy or radiation).

JLbsA8.title: Periodic paralysis
JLbsA8.description: An acute-onset weakness that most commonly affects the lower extremities and proximal muscles. Sensorium is typically intact, and hyporeflexia is present. Can be precipitated by diet or exercise. Further subdivided into primary periodic paralysis (e.g., caused by mutations in sodium, potassium, or calcium channels) and secondary periodic paralysis (e.g., due to renal tubular acidosis or thyrotoxicosis).

qLbCA8.title: Oppositional defiant disorder
qLbCA8.description: A disruptive, impulse-control, and conduct disorder characterized by anger, irritable mood, and defiance toward authority figures. Significantly impairs social and/or academic functioning. A diagnosis of exclusion (e.g., not attributable to substance use or disruptive mood dysregulation disorder).

destinations.label: Impulse and conduct disorders → Oppositional defiant disorder

ILbY_8.title: Enterococcus faecalis
ILbY_8.description: A gram-positive bacterium that is a normal component of the gastrointestinal tract flora. Can cause urinary tract infections, biliary tract infections, and endocarditis (especially after genitourinary or gastrointestinal interventions).

rLbf_8.title: Saint Louis University Mental Status Examination
rLbf_8.description: A cognitive screening tool to assess the degree of cognitive impairment in individuals with suspected dementia. Includes testing of orientation, learning and memory, language, complex attention, perceptual-motor, and executive function cognitive domains. Advantages include sensitivity for detecting early-onset dementia in individuals with mild cognitive impairment and that different levels of education are taken into consideration.

7Lb4_8.title: Acute bilirubin encephalopathy
7Lb4_8.description: A bilirubin encephalopathy in infants caused by increased levels of bilirubin and its neurotoxic effects. Clinical features include hypotonia, lethargy, apnea, and seizures. Can progress to chronic bilirubin encephalopathy (kernicterus).

sLbt_8.title: Holt-Oram syndrome
sLbt_8.description: An autosomal dominant disorder characterized by congenital cardiac septal defects (e.g., secundum atrial septal defect) and upper limb defects (e.g., deformity of the carpal bones). Associated with dysfunction of cardiac conduction. Most commonly caused by a mutation in the TBX5 gene.

destinations.label: Acyanotic congenital heart defects → Atrial septal defect (ASD)

GLbB_8.title: Hartnup disease
GLbB_8.description: An autosomal recessive metabolic disorder characterized by a defect transport protein required for the absorption of neutral amino acids (e.g., tryptophan) in the small intestine and proximal renal tubule. Since tryptophan is required for the synthesis of vitamin B3 (niacin), patients may become deficient and present with symptoms of pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia) and cerebellar ataxia.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Hartnup disease

tLbXz8.title: Myeloperoxidase
tLbXz8.description: An enzyme found in neutrophil granulocytes that is involved in the production of acids with antimicrobial activity. Antibodies against this enzyme can be found in patients with microscopic polyangiitis. Used as a marker for cells of myeloid lineage.

FLbgz8.title: Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase
FLbgz8.description: A specialized DNA polymerase expressed at high levels in immature T and B cells. It is helpful in the diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

8LbOz8.title: Splenic sequestration crisis
8LbOz8.description: A life-threatening complication of sickle cell disease that is caused by splenic vaso-occlusion. Predominantly affects infants and young children. Typically presents with acute-onset severe anemia (i.e., a decrease in the hemoglobin level by ≥ 2 g/dL with reticulocytosis), left upper quadrant pain, and signs of intravascular volume depletion (e.g., hypotension) due to the trapping of blood in the spleen.

uLbpz8.title: Hyperhemolysis
uLbpz8.description: A very rare complication of sickle cell disease. The condition is caused by hemolytic crises (both intravascular and extravascular hemolysis!), which are triggered by mild oxygen deficiency. Presents with acute onset, worsening anemia despite associated reticulocytosis due to increased RBC turnover.

ELb8z8.title: Myelopathy
ELb8z8.description: A neurologic disorder caused by injury to the spinal cord. Extrinsic compression of the spinal cord or cauda equina (e.g., due to degenerative disk diseases) is the most common cause of myelopathy. Other causes include trauma, infection, and autoimmune disorders. Clinical features vary depending on the level of the lesion and include pain, stiffness, impaired sensation, and manifestations of lower motor neuron lesions (at the level of the lesion) and upper motor neuron lesions (below the level of the lesion).

vLbAz8.title: Gastric ulcer
vLbAz8.description: An ulcerative lesion in the stomach lining. Typically manifests along the lesser curvature of the antrum. Less common than duodenal ulcers. Risk factors include Helicobacter pylori infection and chronic use of NSAIDs. Often asymptomatic but can present with upper abdominal discomfort (e.g., postprandial heaviness, early satiety, and gnawing, epigastric pain).

DLb1-8.title: Duodenal ulcer
DLb1-8.description: A peptic ulcer located in the duodenum, typically in the first part (i.e., the duodenal bulb). Most commonly caused by an infection with Helicobacter pylori or chronic use of NSAIDs.

wLbh-8.title: Base deficit
wLbh-8.description: A measure that quantifies the amount of bicarbonate that has been utilized to buffer an acid. A base deficit > 2 mmol/L suggests a metabolic acidosis.

xLbE-8.title: Acute hypertensive nephrosclerosis
xLbE-8.description: A condition of acute kidney damage secondary to hypertensive emergency. Manifestations include microscopic hematuria and an increased serum creatitine concentration. Histopathologic examination shows petechial subcapsular hemorrhages and/or visible infarction with necrosis of mesangial and endothelial cells, thrombosis of glomerular capillaries, luminal thrombosis of arterioles, and red blood cell extravasation and fragmentation.

BLbz-8.title: Fosphenytoin
BLbz-8.description: Intravenous pro-drug of phenytoin with a better safety profile. Although its mechanism of action is not fully clear, it likely works on ion channels. Indications include status epilepticus and short term (<5 days) treatment of epilepsy.

yLbdZu.title: Transcalvarial herniation
yLbdZu.description: Herniation of the brain parenchyma through a defect (either traumatic or surgical) in the calvarium.

ALbRZu.title: Upward brainstem herniation
ALbRZu.description: Increased pressure in the posterior fossa due to a space-occupying lesion that pushes the superior cerebellum through the tentorial notch. Presents with nonspecific symptoms of nausea and vomiting, which rapidly progress to coma and death.

_Lb5Zu.title: Cerebral aqueductoplasty
_Lb5Zu.description: A neurosurgical procedure in which a stenotic or closed cerebral aqueduct is opened to allow adequate passage of CSF between the third and fourth ventricles.

zLbrZu.title: Sleep latency
zLbrZu.description: The length of time required to fall asleep.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Sleep physiology

-LbDZu.title: Circadian rhythm
-LbDZu.description: A collection of physiologic changes that follow a 24-hour cycle and are primarily regulated by light. Mediated by the suprachiasmatic nucleus of the hypothalamus, which releases the norepinephrine that causes the pineal gland to release melatonin.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Sleep physiology

ZobZ0u.title: Flurazepam
ZobZ0u.description: A long-acting benzodiazepine derivate that binds to allosteric sites on GABA-A receptors to increase chloride flux. It is commonly used as a hypnotic for patients with increased sleep latency and difficulty maintaining sleep.

0obe0u.title: Beers Criteria Medication List
0obe0u.description: A guideline from the American Geriatrics Society that specifies medications that are potentially harmful to adults over 65 years of age.

aobQ0u.title: Sleep restriction
aobQ0u.description: A component of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia. Patients are advised to restrict their time in bed to the average number of hours they spend actually sleeping. This can reduce sleep latency but may also exacerbate some comorbidities (e.g., may precipitate manic episodes in bipolar patients) and create safety concerns related to daytime activities (e.g., drowsy driving).

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Insomnia disorder

Yobn0u.title: Paradoxical intention
Yobn0u.description: A cognitive behavior therapy for patients with chronic insomnia aimed at reducing the anxiety and stress surrounding being unable to sleep. In this technique, the patient is advised to remain awake as long as possible, but otherwise follow good sleep hygiene practices (e.g., avoiding stimulants close to bedtime, exercising, sunlight exposure during the day and darkness at night).

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Insomnia disorder

Xob90u.title: Pemphigus syphiliticus
Xob90u.description: A rare dermatologic condition characterized by bullous lesions predominantly on the palms and soles found in infants with congenital syphilis.

cobaau.title: PGE2
cobaau.description: A signaling molecule derived from arachidonic acid. Increases body temperature, mediates pain, induces uterine smooth muscle contraction, and causes vasodilatation via vascular smooth muscle relaxation. Exogenously administered in infants with cyanotic heart conditions who require temporary patency of ductus arteriosus. Also used for labor induction.

1ob2au.title: Congenital Zika virus infection
1ob2au.description: A congenital infection that characteristically causes microcephaly in affected infants. Other manifestations include joint contractures, hypertonia, and hyperreflexia. Most infants will also exhibit neuroradiological evidence of disease such as intracranial calcifications, reduced brain volume, and ventriculomegaly.

media.title: Congenital Zika syndrome TORCH fact sheet

WobPau.title: Choroid plexus carcinoma
WobPau.description: A rare malignant neoplasm of the choroid plexus (~ 1% of pediatric intracranial malignancies) that primarily occurs in children < 5 years. Typically associated with signs of hydrocephalus, which can be caused by both increased CSF production and CSF outflow obstruction.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Microscopic anatomy

doboau.title: Shiga-toxin-producing Escherischia coli
doboau.description: An Escherichia coli pathotype that produces Shiga toxin (i.e., verotoxin). Transmitted via the fecal-oral route. Includes the subset enterohemorrhagic E. coli (EHEC). Infection with EHEC (particularly serotype O157:H7) can cause bloody diarrhea and hemolytic uremic syndrome, most commonly in children.

VobGau.title: Diving reflex
VobGau.description: A reflex in mammals in which immersion of the head triggers peripheral vasoconstriction, redirection of blood to the heart and brain, and slowed pulse rate, which optimizes respiration. This reflex is especially pronounced in infants; placing an ice-cold wet towel on the face or immersion of the head in ice water, which causes the heart rate to slow, can be used to terminate supraventricular tachycardia.

eobxau.title: Squirt sign
eobxau.description: The explosive release of gas and stool with rectal examination, due to intestinal obstruction. The presence of this sign in a newborn who has failed to pass meconium for > 48 hours suggests Hirschsprung disease.

UobbYu.title: Trichophyton rubrum
UobbYu.description: A dermatophyte that causes fungal skin infections, or tinea, especially of the feet, hands, nails, and groin.

2obTYu.title: Antidepressant discontinuation syndrome
2obTYu.description: A syndrome characterized by headache, nausea, insomnia, hyperarousal, and sensory disturbances. Occurs in ~ 20% of patients after sudden discontinuation of an antidepressant that has been taken for ≥ 4 weeks. Symptoms typically persist for 1-2 weeks.

fobkYu.title: Blistering distal dactylitis
fobkYu.description: A bacterial infection of the palmar fat pad of the distal phalanx of the fingers, commonly manifesting with a single, purulent blister. Caused mainly by group A hemolytic streptococci.

destinations.label: Finger and toe infections → Blistering distal dactylitis

Tob6Yu.title: Tinea manuum
Tob6Yu.description: A dermatophyte infection of the hands that is typically associated with tinea unguium or tinea pedis.

gobFYu.title: Iodine deficiency
gobFYu.description: Severe iodine deficiency develops when iodide intake is chronically < 20 mcg/day. Iodine can be obtained through foods (e.g., seafood, vegetables) or iodized salt. Pregnant women require more iodine daily. Consequences of iodine deficiency are diffuse or nodular goiter, hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, cretinism, and higher neonatal mortality.

SobyYu.title: Shwachman-Diamond syndrome
SobyYu.description: Rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, bone marrow failure (particularly neutropenia), growth retardation, short stature, and recurrent infections. Second most common cause of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency in children (after cystic fibrosis).

hobcbu.title: Rotavirus vaccine
hobcbu.description: A live attenuated vaccine that protects against rotavirus infection – the leading cause of severe diarrhea in young children. Given as a 2-dose or 3-dose regimen, depending upon the vaccine used. The first dose is given at 2 months, second dose at 4 months, and third dose at 6 months (if needed).

3obSbu.title: Inactivated poliovirus vaccine
3obSbu.description: An inactivated vaccine that prevents infants and toddlers from developing poliomyelitic paralysis. Usually given as a 3-dose regimen at 2 months, 4 months, and 6–18 months. A booster dose should be given at 4–6 years of age.

Roblbu.title: 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine
Roblbu.description: A vaccine that protects against 23 serotypes of S. pneumoniae. The minimum age for the first dose is 2 years.

iobJbu.title: Pneumococcal vaccine
iobJbu.description: An inactivated vaccine that confers immunity against Streptococcus pneumoniae. Types include pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV15, PCV 20, PCV21) and the pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23).

Qobubu.title: Pathological neonatal jaundice
Qobubu.description: Jaundice appearing in an infant before the third day of life with serum bilirubin levels > 15 mg/dL or a daily increase of bilirubin levels > 5 mg/dL. Caused by an underlying condition (e.g., hepatitis, sepsis, metabolic diseases, immune-mediated hemolysis.)

job_bu.title: Tympanostomy
job_bu.description: A procedure in which small tubes are inserted into the eardrum (tympanic membrane) to allow air to enter the middle ear and fluid to drain. Indications include treatment of recurrent acute otitis media.

PobWXu.title: Central transtentorial herniation
PobWXu.description: A brain herniation syndrome characterized by symmetric, stepwise passage of the central brain tissue through the tentorium cerebelli. First, the diencephalon herniates (lethargy, miosis, abnormal respirations), then the midbrain herniates (fixed mid-dilated pupils, stupor/coma, extensor posturing). Once the midbrain herniates, damage is irreversible.

4ob3Xu.title: Tympanocentesis
4ob3Xu.description: A procedure in which the eardrum is punctured with a small gauge sterile needle to drain fluid from the middle ear. Indications include acute otitis media that does not respond to initial pharmacological therapy.

kobmXu.title: GABA receptor agonist
kobmXu.description: A class of agents that induce GABAergic effects through activation of GABA receptors. Used to reduce neuronal excitability and muscle tone.

OobIXu.title: Myelography
OobIXu.description: A fluoroscopic examination of the meninges, nerve roots, spinal canal and/or spinal cord by injecting a radiopaque dye into the spinal canal. Can be used to diagnose conditions such as disc herniation, spinal canal stenosis, tumors, and inflammation of the meninges. Can be used when MRI cannot be performed (e.g., in patients with incompatible pacemakers) or would be inconclusive (e.g., patients with metal implants after spinal cord surgery).

lobvXu.title: Heat exhaustion
lobvXu.description: A heat-related illness characterized by decreased blood volume and/or total body water, normal or slightly elevated core body temperature (typically defined as ≤ 40°C), and normal mental status.

Nob-Xu.title: X-linked dominant genetic disorder
Nob-Xu.description: An inheritance of a mutation located on the X chromosome that results in phenotypic expression of the mutation with only one abnormal gene. Because female individuals have two X chromosomes, the inheritance of an X-linked dominant disorder typically manifests in a less severe form than in male individuals.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → X-linked dominant inheritance

mobVcu.title: Microphthalmia
mobVcu.description: Small orbits, which may be unilateral or bilateral. Due to a developmental disorder of the eyes. Results in functional impairment. Often a finding in chromosomal disorders (e.g., trisomy 13).

5obicu.title: Osteoblastic metastasis
5obicu.description: A sclerotic bone tumor caused by metastasis from a primary extraosseous tumor in which the rate of new bone formation exceeds the rate of bone destruction. Most common causes include prostate cancer and small cell lung cancer.

MobMcu.title: Osteolytic metastasis
MobMcu.description: Radiolucent bone tumors caused by metastases from a primary extraosseous tumor in which the rate of bone destruction exceeds bone formation. Osteolytic metastases are the most common form of bone metastases.

nob7cu.title: Chondromalacia patellae
nob7cu.description: A softening, fragmentation, and/or erosion of the articular cartilage of the patella that is usually the result of overuse (e.g., repetitive knee flexion) or trauma. Demonstrable tissue damage differentiates chondromalacia patellae from patellofemoral pain syndrome.

Lobwcu.title: Anisocytosis
Lobwcu.description: The appearance of erythrocytes of different sizes on a peripheral blood smear. Considered a nonspecific finding of many different forms of anemia, including iron deficiency anemia and hereditary spherocytosis.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

oob01u.title: Antacid
oob01u.description: A drug that neutralizes gastric acid. Used to treat heartburn, though no clinical recommendation exists for their use in cases of reflux esophagitis or gastric ulcers. Examples include magnesium hydroxide and aluminum hydroxide.

pobL1u.title: Hyperviscosity syndrome
pobL1u.description: A constellation of symptoms caused by impaired microcirculation of blood as a result of increased blood viscosity (e.g., due to polycythemia vera, Waldenstrom macroglobinemia, acute lymphocytic leukemia). Symptoms include syncope, headache, impaired vision, paraesthesias, and numbness.

sobtWu.title: Meiosis
sobtWu.description: A type of cell division that halves the number of chromosomes and results in the formation of four haploid daughter cells. Meiosis is responsible for the production of gametes.

Fobgdu.title: Lumbar spine
Fobgdu.description: A portion of the spine located inferior to the thoracic spine and superior to the sacral spine. Consists of 5 vertebrae (L1–L5).

media.title: Range of motion of the spine

BobzVu.title: Hyperhidrosis
BobzVu.description: A condition of excessive sweating. Can be localized or generalized.

yobdeu.title: Prone position
yobdeu.description: An anatomical descriptor for horizontal positioning of the body with face and torso facing downward (i.e., lying on the abdomen).

AobReu.title: Supine position
AobReu.description: An anatomical descriptor for horizontal positioning of the body with face and torso facing upward (i.e., lying on the back).

zobreu.title: Block vertebra
zobreu.description: A block vertebra is characterized by complete or partial fusion of adjacent vertebrae. It may be a congenital (e.g., a neural tube defect due to hypoxia) or acquired vertebral anomaly

-obDeu.title: Lacrimation
-obDeu.description: The production of tears within the eyes.

0KbeUu.title: Lophotrichous
0KbeUu.description: Bacteria with two or more flagella located at one end of the cell

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

bKbHUu.title: Chemoprevention
bKbHUu.description: The use of pharmacologic agents to reduce the risk of developing carcinoma in high-risk individuals.

XKb9Uu.title: Apophysitis
XKb9Uu.description: Irritation or inflammation of the apophysis, which is the site on bone where a tendon inserts (e.g., tibial tubercle is the apophysis for the patellar tendon). Commonly caused by excessive strain (traction) due to exercise. May result in detachment of the apophysis (e.g., in Osgood-Schlatter disease), especially in adolescents whose apophysis is not fully ossified.

cKba2u.title: Patellar sleeve fracture
cKba2u.description: A patella fracture most often encountered in pediatric patients. It occurs when the outer cartilaginous “sleeve” of the patella separates from the ossified core of the bone due to incomplete ossification of the patella.

1Kb22u.title: Fatty cast
1Kb22u.description: A type of urinary cast formed when tubular epithelial cells become engorged with lipids and slough into the tubular lumen. Has a Maltese cross appearance under polarized light.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

WKbP2u.title: Right axis deviation
WKbP2u.description: An electrocardiographic abnormality in which the cardiac axis is between 90º–180º. It has a broad differential diagnosis, but common causes include right ventricular hypertrophy, lateral myocardial infarction, and COPD. It also may be a normal variant in children or particularly thin adults.

destinations.label: ECG → Determination of the cardiac axis

media.title: Right ventricular hypertrophy with extreme right-axis deviation

VKbG2u.title: Granulomatosis infantiseptica
VKbG2u.description: The clinical syndrome of early-onset neonatal listeriosis, which is characterized by disseminated visceral abscesses and/or granulomas, sometimes involving the skin.

eKbx2u.title: Orotic aciduria
eKbx2u.description: An autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by a defect of uridine monophosphate synthase. Manifests with failure to thrive, developmental delay, megaloblastic anemia, and excretion of orotic acid crystals in the urine (that can cause urethral and ureteral obstruction).

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Orotic aciduria

UKbbfu.title: La Crosse virus
UKbbfu.description: An arbovirus capable of causing mild meningoencephalitis, especially in younger children. Infection almost exclusively occurs in the summer months and 50% of patients first present with seizures. Lumbar puncture may demonstrate elevated red blood cells. The combination of seizures and elevated RBCs in CSF can lead to confusing the features with those of herpes simplex encephalitis.

2KbTfu.title: Foot abduction brace
2KbTfu.description: A foot brace consisting of a connecting bar between two footplates, which are adjustable and onto which shoes are attached. It helps obtain correction by connecting the feet horizontally, as they are held in place by the footplates and shoes at the desired angles to the sagittal plane. Used to treat and prevent relapses in cases of idiopathic clubfoot deformity which have been completely corrected by manipulation, serial casting, and heel cord tenotomy.

fKbkfu.title: Ivemark syndrome
fKbkfu.description: An exceptionally rare genetic laterality disorder that features congenital asplenia, bilateral trilobed lungs, and cardiac malformations

TKb6fu.title: CD40 ligand
TKb6fu.description: A cluster of a differentiation molecule that is encoded by a gene on chromosome Xq and upregulated on activated CD4 T-cells (T helper cells). CD40L on T-helper cells serves as a ligand for the CD40 molecule on B cells; binding of CD40L with CD40 causes immunoglobulin phenotype switching (i.e., the production of immunoglobulins other than IgM) by B cells.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

gKbFfu.title: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist
gKbFfu.description: A drug that activates the gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor in the pituitary gland. Continued stimulation of the receptor leads to desensitization of the pituitary gland, thereby reducing the secretion of gonadotropins (LH and FSH) and decreasing estrogen in females and testosterone in males. Used to treat hormonally-sensitive cancers, to delay puberty in patients with precocious puberty, and to induce a hypoestrogenic state in women with menorrhagia, endometriosis, or uterine fibroids.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

SKbyfu.title: Neonatal gonococcal conjunctivitis
SKbyfu.description: A neonatal eye infection contracted during delivery from mothers infected with Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Manifestations include profuse, purulent ocular drainage and pronounced eyelid swelling.

hKbcTu.title: WAS gene
hKbcTu.description: A gene on chromosome Xp that is responsible for the production of the WAS protein in cells of a hematopoietic lineage. WAS protein, which is found only in blood cells, is involved in relaying signals from the surface of the cell to the actin cytoskeleton within the cell. A defect in the WAS gene is classically seen in Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital mixed immunodeficiencies

3KbSTu.title: Natamycin
3KbSTu.description: An antifungal agent used to treat ocular fungal infections, particularly those caused by Aspergillus or Fusarium.

RKblTu.title: Lysosome trafficking regulator gene
RKblTu.description: A gene that is located on chromosome 1q. It codes for a protein that is responsible for regulating cellular vesicle transport and the transport of substances into lysosomes. Loss of function of this gene (as occurs in Chediak-Higashi syndrome) results in lysosomal fusion, which causes the formation of large granules within neutrophils, as well as poorly functioning thrombocytes and melanosomes.

iKbJTu.title: Absolute neutrophil count
