iKbJTu.description: The number of neutrophils per cubic millimeter of blood, calculated by multiplying the total white blood cell count with the percentage of neutrophils (mature forms + band forms). Normal values range between 1,500/mm³ and 8,000/mm³.

QKbuTu.title: Bruton tyrosine kinase gene
QKbuTu.description: A gene on chromosome Xq that is responsible for the production of a cytoplasmic tyrosine kinase called BTK, which enables B-cell maturation. Defects of this gene are responsible for Bruton's agammaglobulinemia and type III isolated growth hormone deficiency.

jKb_Tu.title: Primary autoimmune neutropenia
jKb_Tu.description: A condition in which autoantibodies destroy neutrophils. Typically causes mild neutropenia leading to recurrent otitis media, but profound immunodeficiency with severe infections is also possible. Treatment is usually supportive with antibiotics for infection. Immunomodulatory medications are reserved for severe cases.

PKbWgu.title: T-cell receptor excision circles
PKbWgu.description: Small circles of DNA created in T cells by passing through the thymus that indicate maturity of T cells. Reduced amount of TRECs suggests immunodeficiency and is present in severe combined immunodeficiency disease (SCID). In the United States, newborns are screened for SCID using PCR amplification of TRECs.

4Kb3gu.title: Interleukin-2 receptor subunit gamma gene
4Kb3gu.description: A gene on chromosome Xq that codes for a protein called the common gamma chain (γc), which forms a component of receptors for certain cytokines that are involved in the growth and maturation of T cells, B cells, and natural killer cells. A defect in this gene is the most common cause of severe combined immunodeficiency.

kKbmgu.title: Cardiac silhouette
kKbmgu.description: The outline of the heart on frontal (i.e., AP and PA) and lateral chest x-ray. On frontal views, the right border is primarily formed by the right atrium and the left border by the left ventricle and the left atrial appendage. On lateral views, the anterior border is formed by the right ventricle and the posterior border by the left atrium (superiorly) and the left ventricle (inferiorly).

OKbIgu.title: Leuprolide
OKbIgu.description: A gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor agonist that can either be used to stimulate LH and FSH secretion (via pulsatile administration) or suppress LH and FSH secretion (via continuous administration, which downregulates GnRH receptors). Used continuously to treat hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, precocious puberty, menorrhagia, and endometriosis. Used in pulsatile fashion to increase fertility.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

lKbvgu.title: Gardnerella vaginalis
lKbvgu.description: A gram-variable rod that causes infections of the genitourinary tract (predominantly vulvovaginitis).

NKb-gu.title: Cefoxitin
NKb-gu.description: A broad-spectrum, second-generation cephalosporin. Effective against many gram-positive and some gram-negative bacteria, including many β-lactam resistant bacteria.

mKbVSu.title: Amine test
mKbVSu.description: A test that is used in diagnosing bacterial vaginosis. Positive if adding 1–2 drops of 10% KOH to infected vaginal discharge (on the speculum after the pelvic examination/on a microscope slide) emits a characteristic amine odor.

5KbiSu.title: Wet mount preparation
5KbiSu.description: A diagnostic test in which a specimen (e.g., vaginal fluid, stool) is examined under a microscope without supravital staining.

MKbMSu.title: Pyrantel pamoate
MKbMSu.description: An anthelmintic agent that is used to treat certain worm infections (e.g., enterobiasis, ascariasis, and ancylostomiasis). Acts as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker, resulting in paralysis of the parasites, which are subsequently passed in the stool.

nKb7Su.title: Ivermectin
nKb7Su.description: A broad-spectrum antiparasitic used in the treatment of worm infections (e.g., enterobiasis, ascariasis, and strongyloidiasis), head lice infestations, and rosacea.

LKbwSu.title: Chondromyxoid fibroma
LKbwSu.description: A rare, benign cartilaginous neoplasm that typically occurs between the ages of 10 and 30 years. Most commonly seen in the upper third of the tibia. Appears on x-ray as an eccentrically located, well-defined osteolytic lesion within the cortex with sclerotic margins.

oKb0hu.title: California encephalitis
oKb0hu.description: A rare mosquito-borne cerebral infection caused by the California encephalitis virus, which typically affects school-aged children in the central and eastern United States (despite its name). The majority of infected individuals are asymptomatic. In symptomatic patients, encephalitis is characterized by seizures, coma, focal neurological findings (e.g., Babinski sign), and paralysis.

KKbUhu.title: Transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy
KKbUhu.description: A primary immunodeficiency that manifests in infants > 6 months (when the transplacentally transferred maternal IgG is no longer active) with decreased serum IgG levels despite normal B cell levels, which usually normalize between 2–6 years of age.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital B-cell immunodeficiencies

6Kbjhu.title: Preductal SpO₂
6Kbjhu.description: The oxygen saturation of hemoglobin (as measured by pulse oximetry) in the right limb. It represents the oxygen saturation of blood in the region of the aorta that is proximal to the ductus arteriosus. Preductal SpO₂ is therefore a more reliable measure of brain oxygenation than SpO₂ measured in other limbs.

pKbLhu.title: Rhizomelic shortening
pKbLhu.description: A disproportionately short length of the proximal limb (i.e., shoulder and humerus in the upper extremity; hip and femur in the lower extremity). Seen in certain syndromes, such as rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata and achondroplasia.

JKbshu.title: Interleukin-12
JKbshu.description: An interleukin that induces the maturation of naive T-cells into helper T (Th)-cells and the production of IFN-gamma and TNF-alpha by Th-cells. Reduction of IL-12 activity (e.g., IL-12 receptor deficiency) can cause immunodeficiency.

qKbChu.title: Distraction osteogenesis
qKbChu.description: A surgical procedure used to repair skeletal deformities. Involves cutting and progressively separating the bone, allowing new bone material to fill in the gap during the healing process. Leads to an increased linear length of the bone.

rKbf3u.title: Karyotyping
rKbf3u.description: A test used to identify and evaluate the size, shape, and number of chromosomes in a sample of cells. To accomplish this, the chromosomes are visualized by means of a light microscope and sorted and arranged by size (karyogram). This test can help identify the specific chromosomal pathology (e.g., aberration, translocation, or deletion) of a patient's genetic condition.

7Kb43u.title: Functional heart murmur
7Kb43u.description: Common, harmless heart sounds during infancy and childhood that often disappear by adulthood. Characteristics suggesting an innocent heart murmur are an intensity < 3/6, position-dependency, asymptomatic patient, early or midsystolic murmurs, and physiologic split of S2. Often an ECG or echocardiogram is performed to rule out an underlying heart disease that requires treatment.

HKbK3u.title: 17α-hydroxylase
HKbK3u.description: An adrenal enzyme that is involved in steroidogenesis. Adds a hydroxyl group to carbon atom 17 of the cholesterol moiety.

media.title: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia on steroid pathway and affecting drugs

sKbt3u.title: Paradoxical diarrhea
sKbt3u.description: The involuntary seepage of liquid feces in patients with fecal impaction. Caused by leakage of proximal semi-solid feces past hardened stools impacted within the rectum and decreased rectal sensation.

tKbXRu.title: Adenosine deaminase
tKbXRu.description: An enzyme involved in purine metabolism that is associated with lymphocyte activation. Conditions that trigger the immune system, such as tuberculosis, can cause increased amounts of ADA (e.g., in the pleural fluid). A deficiency of this enzyme causes the autosomal recessive form of severe combined immunodeficiency.

FKbgRu.title: Cystathionine synthase
FKbgRu.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of homocysteine and serine to cystathionine, using vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) as a cofactor. Deficiency of this enzyme causes homocystinuria.

8KbORu.title: Marfanoid habitus
8KbORu.description: A collection of clinical features including tall stature, long limbs (with an increased limb length to body height ratio), overcrowded dentition with a high-arched palate, arachnodactyly (long, slender fingers), and joint hypermobility. Marfanoid habitus can be seen in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2b, Marfan syndrome, and homocystinuria.

uKbpRu.title: Type V collagen
uKbpRu.description: One of the most important types of collagen, found predominantly in cell surfaces, hair, and the placenta. Encoded by the COL5A1 and COL5A2 genes, mutations of either can produce one of the classic forms of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

EKb8Ru.title: RET gene
EKb8Ru.description: A proto-oncogene that encodes a tyrosine kinase. Mutations that lead to gain of function are implicated in the pathophysiology of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2a and 2b.

vKbARu.title: Galactokinase deficiency
vKbARu.description: An inborn error in galactose metabolism due to absent or dysfunctional galactokinase. Inability to convert galactose to galactose-1-phosphate leads to pathologically increased conversion of galactose to galactitol by aldose reductase. Elevated blood galactose and early-onset cataracts (due to accumulation of galactitol) occur.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Galactosemia

DKb1iu.title: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase
DKb1iu.description: A purine salvage enzyme that converts hypoxanthine to inosine monophosphate (IMP) and guanine to guanine monophosphate (GMP). Deficiency causes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.

wKbhiu.title: α-L-iduronidase
wKbhiu.description: A lysosomal enzyme responsible for the hydrolysis of glycosaminoglycans such as dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate. Deficiency of this enzyme results in Hurler syndrome.

9KbNiu.title: Ectopia lentis
9KbNiu.description: A displacement or malposition of the eye's crystalline lens from its normal location. Can be a complete (i.e., luxation; lens lies completely outside of the hyaloid fossa) or partial dislocation (i.e., subluxation). Commonly associated with certain systemic diseases, including Marfan syndrome, and homocystinuria.

destinations.label: Diseases of the lens → Ectopia lentis

CKbqiu.title: Aromatase
CKbqiu.description: An enzyme of the cytochrome p450 family that is produced in the ovaries, adipose tissue, and placenta. Aromatase is responsible for conversion of testosterone to estradiol, and androstenedione to estrone.

xKbEiu.title: Aromatase deficiency
xKbEiu.description: A disease caused by autosomal recessive loss-of-function mutations in the CYP19A1 gene on chromosome 15q, which results in a deficiency of estrogen and increased levels of testosterone. Karyotypically male infants appear normal. Karyotypically females are born with ambiguous genitalia and usually have primary amenorrhea, impaired development of female secondary sexual characteristics, and virilization (e.g., hirsutism).

destinations.label: Differences (disorders) of sex development → Aromatase deficiency

BKbziu.title: 21β-hydroxylase
BKbziu.description: An enzyme that is produced predominantly in the adrenal cortex and involved in steroidogenesis. The enzyme is encoded by the CYP21A2 gene on chromosome 6p. Deficiency of this enzyme is the most common cause of congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

yKbdQu.title: Dihydrotestosterone
yKbdQu.description: An androgen with a potency that is 2–3 times greater than that of testosterone at the androgen receptor. Formed when testosterone is reduced by the enzyme 5α-reductase. Responsible for the differentiation of male external genitalia in utero, prostate growth, balding, and sebaceous gland activity in adults.

AKbRQu.title: Type III collagen
AKbRQu.description: A protein encoded by the COL3A1 gene that is found in extensible connective tissue (e.g., skin, lungs, vessels), bones, cartilage, dentin, and the lens of the eye. Mutations in the COL3A1 gene cause type III and IV Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (predominantly cardiovascular manifestations).

_Kb5Qu.title: Menkes disease
_Kb5Qu.description: An X-linked neurodegenerative disease caused by a defect in the Menkes P-type ATPase (ATP7A gene). It results in the inability to transport copper from enterocytes to the liver and other cells of the body, leading to decreased copper levels. Clinical features include failure to thrive, developmental retardation, epilepsy, connective tissue anomalies, and characteristic kinky, brittle hair.

destinations.label: Connective tissue diseases → Connective tissue disorders

zKbrQu.title: Elastin
zKbrQu.description: A highly elastic protein, encoded by the ELN gene, that is a component of elastic fibers. Allows tissues to reassume their original shape after exposure to mechanical strain, stretching, or contracting (e.g., skin smoothing out after being pinched).

-KbDQu.title: Arachnodactyly
-KbDQu.description: A condition in which the fingers and toes are abnormally long and thin in proportion to the palm of the hand/sole of the foot. May be an incidental finding without pathological significance or a symptom of an underlying condition, typically one that affects connective tissue (e.g., Marfan syndrome).

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Clinical features

Z6bZju.title: Cranial suspensory ligament
Z6bZju.description: A fibromuscular structure that anchors the embryonic gonad to the posterior abdominal wall. Regression of this ligament under the influence of testosterone is responsible for testicular descent in males. In females, this ligament persists as the suspensory ligament of the ovary and is responsible for the intra-abdominal location of the ovaries.

06beju.title: Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis
06beju.description: A transient, self-limited patchy inflammation of the thyroid gland, characterized by granuloma formation. Often follows viral infection and is more common in women. Inflammation typically causes a triphasic pattern from thyrotoxicosis to hypothyroidism, before returning to a euthyroid state. Most common cause of thyroid pain.

a6bQju.title: Exon
a6bQju.description: A gene segment that is translated into a peptide sequence after the splicing process has removed intron sequences.

Y6bnju.title: Intron
Y6bnju.description: A gene segment that is not translated into a peptide sequence. Typically interrupts coding sequences (exons). Although their functionality is not in providing code for the peptide sequence, introns play an important regulatory role.

b6bHju.title: Steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome
b6bHju.description: A condition characterized by two consecutive relapses of nephrotic syndrome during corticosteroid therapy or one relapse within 2 weeks of ceasing therapy. A relapse is defined as a urine protein-creatinine ratio ≥ 2 (or ≥ 200 mg/mmol/L) or a urine dipstick test of 3+ or greater on 3 consecutive days.

X6b9ju.title: Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome
X6b9ju.description: A failure to achieve at least partial remission within 4 weeks of corticosteroid therapy, or failure to achieve complete remission after 8 weeks of corticosteroid therapy. Complete remission is defined as a urine protein-creatinine ratio < 0.2 (or < 20 mg/mmol) or a urine protein dipstick test of 1+ or lower on 3 consecutive days. Partial remission is defined as proteinuria that is < 50% of the initial presenting value or a urine protein-creatine ratio between 0.2 and 2 (20–200 mg/mmol).

c6baPu.title: Visual training
c6baPu.description: Training to correct eye movements (e.g., in strabismus) and visual-motor deficiencies through the use of specialized computer and optical devices (e.g., lenses and prisms).

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Concomitant strabismus

16b2Pu.title: Diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis
16b2Pu.description: A histopathological pattern of glomerular injury characterized by increased cellularity in more than 50% of the glomeruli. Electron microscopy typically shows subendothelial deposits leading to thickened capillaries (resembling wire loops). The most common underlying causes are SLE and IgA nephropathy, but other inflammatory, autoimmune, or infectious diseases can also lead to DPGN.

W6bPPu.title: Neonatal hyperthyroidism
W6bPPu.description: A condition that is characterized by increased levels of thyroid hormones in the newborn period. Most often occurs in babies born to mothers with Graves' disease due to transplacental passage of stimulating maternal TRAbs. Presents with tachycardia, hyperphagia, poor weight gain, and a diffuse goiter.

destinations.label: Graves disease → Graves disease in neonates

d6boPu.title: Vitamin A
d6boPu.description: A fat-soluble vitamin that is involved in vision, cellular communication, the immune system, and reproduction. Can be administered as a supplement in vitamin A deficiency or to treat measles.

V6bGPu.title: Rule of 2s for Meckel's diverticulum
V6bGPu.description: Meckel's diverticulum occurs in 2% of the population, usually manifests in the first 2 years of life, has a length of 2 inches, is located 2 feet from the ileocecal valve, and often consists of 2 types of tissue (mostly gastric and pancreatic tissue).

e6bxPu.title: Pulsus parvus et tardus
e6bxPu.description: A physical examination finding in which a distal arterial pulse (e.g., the radial pulse) is weak and delayed. Classically associated with aortic stenosis.

U6bb4u.title: Hemorrhagic cystitis
U6bb4u.description: An inflammation of the bladder in which damage to the epithelium and blood vessels causes hematuria and symptoms of bladder irritation (e.g., frequency, urgency). Causes include infection, radiation and/or chemotherapy.

26bT4u.title: Tubo-ovarian abscess
26bT4u.description: An infectious inflammatory mass of the fallopian tube and/or ovary that is most commonly a complication of pelvic inflammatory disease. Symptoms include fever, lower abdominal pain, vaginal discharge, and leukocytosis.

destinations.label: Pelvic inflammatory disease → Subtypes and variants

f6bk4u.title: Enterovesical fistula
f6bk4u.description: An abnormal connection between the bladder and bowel (e.g., colon, rectum). Can be congenital (e.g., failure of the urorectal septum to develop) or acquired (e.g., due to inflammation, cancer, radiation, trauma). Results in direct spread of intestinal bacteria to the bladder.

T6b64u.title: Vesicovaginal fistula
T6b64u.description: An abnormal connection between the vagina and the bladder. Possible causes include early sexual intercourse, prolonged/obstructed labor, cancer, and pelvic surgery or irradiation. Typically presents with painless urine incontinence and frequent UTIs (due to direct spread of vaginal bacteria into the bladder).

g6bF4u.title: Gonadarche
g6bF4u.description: A phase of pubertal change characterized by activation of reproductive glands by the pituitary hormones FSH and LH. Causes growth of the ovaries and testes and increase in production of sex steroids.

S6by4u.title: Adrenarche
S6by4u.description: Maturation of the zona reticularis of the adrenal gland leading to the production of androgens and subsequent development of pubic and axillary hair (pubarche) and body odor. Usually begins at 6–10 years of age and precedes other pubertal changes.

h6bcku.title: Anovulatory cycle
h6bcku.description: A menstrual cycle characterized by the absence of ovulation and a luteal phase, resulting in menstrual irregularities. Common (and not pathological) in adolescents during the first few months to years after menarche.

destinations.label: The menstrual cycle → Abnormalities of the menstrual cycle

R6blku.title: Acute hemorrhagic conjunctivitis
R6blku.description: A highly contagious disease caused by coxsackie group A24 (CA24), enterovirus E70 (EV70), and adenovirus 11 (AV11) strains. Manifestations include acute conjunctivitis and massive subconjunctival hemorrhage.

i6bJku.title: Angular conjunctivitis
i6bJku.description: A chronic conjunctivitis caused by Morax-Axenfeld diplobacilli. Characterized by mild inflammation confined to the conjunctiva and lid margins near the angles and maceration of the surrounding skin. Patients present with itching, redness, conjunctival hyperemia, and foamy discharge at the angles of the eye.

Q6buku.title: Cubitus valgus
Q6buku.description: A deformity of the elbow resulting in an increased carrying angle > 15° (i.e., deviation of the forearm from the body when extended). A typical feature of Turner syndrome, but may also be due to fracture, trauma, or infection with involvement of the lateral epiphyseal growth plate.

P6bWOu.title: Petroleum jelly
P6bWOu.description: A water-repelling hydrocarbon mixture used as a moisturizer to treat or prevent dry, scaly, itchy, and irritated skin (e.g., diaper rash, atopic dermatitis).

46b3Ou.title: Rosenthal fibers
46b3Ou.description: A collection of astrocytic processes that appear as eosinophilic, corkscrew-like fibers on histopathologic examination of pilocytic astrocytomas.

destinations.label: Brain tumors → Primary brain tumors according to age

k6bmOu.title: Glial fibrillary acidic protein
k6bmOu.description: An intermediate filament protein found in glial cells that is involved in cell-cell communication, blood-brain barrier functioning, and mitosis. Used in immunohistochemical staining as a marker for cells of glial origin.

O6bIOu.title: Urease
O6bIOu.description: An enzyme that converts urea to ammonia and carbon dioxide, which results in an increase in pH.

l6bvOu.title: Breakthrough urinary tract infection
l6bvOu.description: The occurrence of a urinary tract infection while a patient is on continuous antibiotic prophylaxis. A breakthrough UTI raises the concern for renal injury

N6b-Ou.title: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
N6b-Ou.description: A histopathological pattern of glomerular injury with a wide variety of manifestations, including both nephritic syndrome and nephrotic syndrome. MPGN can be caused by immune complex deposition or anomalous complement activation. Characterized by splitting of the glomerular basement membrane (double contour or tram-track appearance) on light microscopy.

m6bVlu.title: Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies
m6bVlu.description: A group of antibodies directed at components of the cell wall of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Associated with chronic inflammatory bowel disease (particularly Crohn disease).

56bilu.title: Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
56bilu.description: A condition in which bronchoconstriction is triggered by physical exertion. Can occur in individuals with or without a history of asthma.

n6b7lu.title: Epididymo-orchitis
n6b7lu.description: A condition characterized by inflammation of the epididymis and testes. Most commonly caused by bacterial urinary tract infections and sexually transmitted infections. Manifestations include testicular pain, swelling, redness, and often systemic symptoms (e.g., fever).

L6bwlu.title: Scrotal hematoma
L6bwlu.description: Accumulation of blood within the scrotum. Common causes include trauma (saddle injury), surgery (e.g., inguinal herniorrhaphy), femoral artery catheterization, and hemophilia.

o6b0Nu.title: Wilms tumor 1 gene
o6b0Nu.description: A gene located on chromosome 11p that produces a transcription factor important for the growth and differentiation of the kidneys and the gonads. Conditions associated with mutations in this gene include Wilms tumor, Denys-Drash syndrome, Frasier syndrome, and WAGR syndrome.

K6bUNu.title: Growth hormone deficiency
K6bUNu.description: A failure of the pituitary to produce adequate amounts of growth hormone (GH). May present during childhood with proportionate short stature, or during adulthood, when it is usually asymptomatic or has only subtle findings (e.g., weight gain, weakness, and depression).

J6bsNu.title: Transient tachypnea of the newborn
J6bsNu.description: The most common cause of respiratory issues in neonates shortly after birth. Due to delayed reabsorption of lung fluid. It is typically seen in newborns >35 weeks' gestation who are delivered by cesarean section without labor. Respiratory issues usually self-resolve within 24–48 hours. Chest x-ray shows lung hyperinflation and fluid within the lung fissures. Treatment is supportive.

destinations.label: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome → Differential diagnoses

q6bCNu.title: Anastrozole
q6bCNu.description: An aromatase inhibitor that is most commonly used in the treatment of hormone-receptor positive breast cancer.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

media.title: Drugs influencing the function of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal-axis

I6bYmu.title: Cutis marmorata
I6bYmu.description: A rash characterized by reticulated or mottled erythema of the extremities and trunk. It is a common benign rash of infancy caused by vasoconstriction in response to cold temperatures. It can also develop as a cutaneous manifestation of decompression sickness.

r6bfmu.title: Infantile acropustulosis
r6bfmu.description: A dermatologic condition of infancy that manifests with episodic eruptions of pruritic vesicles and pustules on the palms and soles. Typically self-limited.

76b4mu.title: Milium
76b4mu.description: A benign, small (1–2 mm), white papule caused by the retention of keratin and sebaceous material. Frequently found on the nose and cheeks of neonates; lesions typically resolves within the first few weeks of life. Can also develop spontaneously in adulthood or as secondary lesions in healing skin.

H6bKmu.title: Glossoptosis
H6bKmu.description: Posterior displacement of the tongue into the pharynx.

destinations.label: Rare inherited syndromes → Pierre Robin sequence (Pierre Robin syndrome)

s6btmu.title: Transient neonatal pustular melanosis
s6btmu.description: A transient, self-limited skin condition of the neonatal period characterized by pustules on a nonerythematous base, collarettes of fine scale, and/or hyperpigmented macules. Can occur on any part of the body but most commonly affects the forehead, anterior neck, and lower back.

destinations.label: Overview of neonatal conditions → Neonatal skin lesions
Rare inherited syndromes → Pierre Robin sequence (Pierre Robin syndrome)

t6bX5u.title: Very long-chain fatty acid
t6bX5u.description: A fatty acid with a total carbon-chain length > 20. Broken down by β-oxidation in peroxisomes. Can accumulate in peroxisomal disorders such as adrenoleukodystrophy and Zellweger syndrome.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

F6bg5u.title: Granulocyte
F6bg5u.description: A type of cell that accounts for approx. 40–60% of all leukocytes and differentiates into neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils, of which neutrophils are the most common. Part of the innate immune system and of particular importance in the immediate immune reaction to infections or disease.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

86bO5u.title: Leukocyte
86bO5u.description: A type of blood cell found throughout the body that functions as part of the immune system. Subtypes include granulocytes from the myeloid cell line and lymphocytes from the lymphoid cell line.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → White cell line: leukocytes

u6bp5u.title: Lymphocyte
u6bp5u.description: A type of cell that accounts for approximately 20–45% of all white blood cells and forms part of both the acquired (B and T lymphocytes) and innate (NK cells) immune system

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Lymphoid cell line

v6bA5u.title: Thrombocytosis
v6bA5u.description: An increase in the number of platelets in the blood (> 400,000/μL). Etiologies include malignancy, chronic kidney disease, infection, and inflammatory conditions.

w6bhMu.title: Erythrocyte
w6bhMu.description: A blood cell involved in oxygen transport (via abundant levels of hemoglobin), CO2 transport, and acid-base buffering. Lacks a nucleus and organelles. In adults, cells are produced in the bone marrow and circulate for ~ 120 days. Disorders of red blood cells include anemia, polycythemia, and hemolysis.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Red cell line: erythrocytes

C6bqMu.title: High-risk pregnancies
C6bqMu.description: A pregnancy with risk factors for adverse outcomes. Examples of such risk factors include: maternal age ≥ 35 years, substance use, history of certain medical conditions (e.g., antiphospholipid syndrome, epilepsy, hypertension, diabetes mellitus), prior pregnancy complications (e.g., preterm delivery), and current pregnancy with placental abruption, multiple gestation, or Rhesus incompatibility.

B6bzMu.title: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
B6bzMu.description: A condition in which the pulmonary vascular resistance remains abnormally high after birth. This results in right-to-left shunting of blood via the fetal circulatory pathways.

destinations.label: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome → Differential diagnoses

y6bdnu.title: Neonatal polycythemia
y6bdnu.description: A hematocrit > 65% or hemoglobin > 22 g/dL in a neonate. Neonatal polycythemia is more commonly seen after delayed umbilical cord clamping, chronic fetal hypoxia, or placental insufficiency (e.g. in diabetic mothers). Most infants are asymptomatic, some show poor feeding, cyanosis, or neurological symptoms due to associated hyperviscosity of the blood.

destinations.label: Overview of neonatal conditions → Neonatal polycythemia

A6bRnu.title: Partial exchange transfusion
A6bRnu.description: A procedure in which part of the blood is replaced with an isotonic fluid to lower the hematocrit. Normally used in neonates with polycythemia.

destinations.label: Overview of neonatal conditions → Neonatal polycythemia

_6b5nu.title: CHARGE syndrome
_6b5nu.description: Syndrome of congenital anomalies: Coloboma, Heart defect, Atresia of the choanae, Retardation of growth, Genital abnormalities, and Ear anomalies.

z6brnu.title: Interleukin-2
z6brnu.description: A cytokine secreted by activated T helper cells that causes an autocrine stimulatory effect leading to T cell proliferation (especially regulatory T cells). Also involved in the activation and differentiation of B cells as well as the regulation of macrophage function.

-6bDnu.title: Interleukin-4
-6bDnu.description: A cytokine produced by Th2 cells that promotes differentiation of naive CD4+ T cells to produce additional Th2 cells (positive feedback). Also induces class switching of B-cells from IgM-producing to IgG- and IgE-producing subtypes.

0pbeLu.title: Cell membrane
0pbeLu.description: A semipermeable membrane that surrounds the cytoplasm of a cell and provides a barrier between the interior and exterior of the cell. Controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell.

apbQLu.title: Lipid bilayer
apbQLu.description: The two layers of phospholipids that form a universal component of all cell membranes.

YpbnLu.title: Flippases
YpbnLu.description: A group of transmembrane proteins that transport phospholipids from the outer to the inner surface of the membrane.

bpbHLu.title: Floppases
bpbHLu.description: A group of transmembrane proteins that transport phospholipids from the inner to the outer surface of the membrane.

Xpb9Lu.title: Scramblases
Xpb9Lu.description: A group of enzymes located in the cell membrane that transport phospholipids between the inner and outer membrane surfaces.

cpbaou.title: Membrane proteins
cpbaou.description: A collection of proteins that are embedded in the lipid bilayer of membranes. Includes integral membrane proteins, which are embedded within the lipid bilayer, and peripheral membrane proteins, which are attached to the outer lipid bilayer.

1pb2ou.title: Integral membrane proteins
1pb2ou.description: A type of membrane protein that is permanently embedded in the cell membrane.

WpbPou.title: Transmembrane proteins
WpbPou.description: A type of integral membrane protein that spans the phospholipid bilayer of the cell membrane.

dpboou.title: Peripheral membrane proteins
dpboou.description: A type of membrane protein that is temporarily attached to the external lipid bilayer.

epbxou.title: Glycocalyx
epbxou.description: A glycoprotein-polysaccharide layer that covers the cell membrane of some eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells.

Tpb6Ku.title: Nuclear envelope
Tpb6Ku.description: A lipid bilayer membrane that surrounds the nucleus and controls substance transport in and out of the nucleus. Consists of an inner and outer membrane connected by nuclear pores.

3pbS6u.title: Nuclear pores
3pbS6u.description: A group of structures in the nuclear envelope that regulate substance transport between the cytoplasm and nucleus.

Rpbl6u.title: Nucleolus
Rpbl6u.description: A region of the nucleus where rRNA synthesis and ribosomal subunit assembly occur.

ipbJ6u.title: Endoplasmic reticulum
ipbJ6u.description: A eukaryotic cell organelle (further divided into rough and smooth types, whose functions include synthesis of proteins and lipids synthesis and metabolism of carbohydrates.

Qpbu6u.title: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
Qpbu6u.description: A eukaryotic cell organelle whose functions include protein synthesis and packaging of synthesized products for the Golgi apparatus. Unlike the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, it has surface ribosomes.

media.title: Translocation of ribosomes to the endoplasmic reticulum during translation

jpb_6u.title: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
jpb_6u.description: A eukaryotic cell organelle whose functions include lipid synthesis and carbohydrate metabolism. Unlike the rough endoplasmic reticulum, it lacks surface ribosomes.

PpbWpu.title: Golgi apparatus
PpbWpu.description: An organelle of most eukaryotic cells that is involved in the modification and processing of proteins and lipids into vesicles for transportation out of the cell.

media.title: Structure and function of the Golgi apparatus

OpbIpu.title: Mitochondrion
OpbIpu.description: An organelle present in most eukaryotic cells whose primary function is to generate energy in the form of ATP.

KpbUqu.title: Lysosome
KpbUqu.description: A membrane-bound, eukaryotic organelle that contains hydrolytic enzymes used to degrade cellular debris.

qpbCqu.title: Autophagy
qpbCqu.description: The process by which cells degrade unnecessary and/or dysfunctional components via lysosomes.

rpbfIu.title: Peroxisome
rpbfIu.description: A eukaryotic, membrane-bound organelle involved in several anabolic and catabolic processes. Functions include β-oxidation of very long chain fatty acids, α-oxidation, and synthesis of cholesterol and bile acids.

7pb4Iu.title: Cytosol
7pb4Iu.description: The cytoplasmic matrix bound by the cell membrane. Does not include the cytoplasmic organelles.

spbtIu.title: Cytoskeleton
spbtIu.description: A network of microfilaments, intermediate filaments, and microtubules that extends throughout the cytoplasm of cells. These cellular components are usually anchored to the plasma membrane and determine cell shape and structure.

GpbBIu.title: Microfilament
GpbBIu.description: A cytoskeletal element found in actin and microvilli. Involved in muscle contraction and cytokinesis.

tpbXru.title: Plectin
tpbXru.description: A protein that links components of the cytoskeleton (e.g., intermediate filaments).

Fpbgru.title: Microtubule
Fpbgru.description: A cytoskeletal element found in cilia, flagella, the mitotic spindle, and centrioles. Involved in cell division, cell movement, and axonal trafficking in neurons. Consists of a cylindrical outer structure of helical, polymerized heterodimers of α- and β-tubulin. Grows slowly but collapses quickly. Motor proteins (e.g., dynein and kinesin) move cellular products on microtubule scaffolds.

Epb8ru.title: Kinesin
Epb8ru.description: A motor protein that transports cellular products anterograde to the microtubule (- → +) away from the nucleus, e.g., in axonal transport

vpbAru.title: Cytoplasmic dynein
vpbAru.description: A motor protein that transports cellular products retrograde to the microtubule (+ → -) toward the nucleus.

9pbN7u.title: Tight junction
9pbN7u.description: An epithelial cell junction that prevents the paracellular passage of ions and molecules between cells. Consists of claudins and occludins.

Cpbq7u.title: Claudins
Cpbq7u.description: A type of structural protein found in tight junctions that regulates paracellular transport.

xpbE7u.title: Occludins
xpbE7u.description: A type of structural protein found in tight junctions that regulates paracellular transport.

Bpbz7u.title: Anchoring junctions
Bpbz7u.description: A group of mechanical attachments between cells. Examples include desmosomes, hemidesmosomes, and adherens junctions.

ypbdHu.title: Desmosome
ypbdHu.description: A cell-to-cell connection that provides structural support with intermediate filaments, particularly in tissues that undergo mechanical stress (e.g., skin, gastric tissue, bladder). Connects keratinocytes in the stratum spinosum of the epidermis.

ApbRHu.title: Desmosomal plaque
ApbRHu.description: A subgroup of desmosomal proteins that are critical in maintaining the structural integrity of cardiac myocytes and epidermal cells. Mutations to the desmoplakin gene results in several cardiomyopathies and keratodermas, including skin fragility-woolly hair syndrome.

_pb5Hu.title: Desmoglein
_pb5Hu.description: A desmosomal cadherin that facilitates cell-to-cell adhesion.

zpbrHu.title: Desmocollin
zpbrHu.description: A desmosomal cadherin that facilitates cell-to-cell adhesion.

-pbDHu.title: Hemidesmosome
-pbDHu.description: An epithelial cell junction that connects basal cells to underlying basement membrane. IgG antibodies against hemidesmosomes form in patients with bullous pemphigoid.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Structure of the skin

ZJbZsu.title: Adherens junction
ZJbZsu.description: An epithelial cell junction that connects cells across a broader, belt-shaped area. Key proteins involved in adherens junction function include vinculin, catenin, and cadherins.

aJbQsu.title: Gap junction
aJbQsu.description: A cell junction that facilitates electrical and chemical signals between neighboring cells (e.g., to propagate the cardiac action potential). Consists of connexon channel proteins.

YJbnsu.title: Connexon
YJbnsu.description: An epithelial cell junction that consists of 6 connexin proteins with a central pore. Gap junctions form when the connexons of two neighboring cells join together.

bJbHsu.title: Connexins
bJbHsu.description: A transmembrane protein that aggregates to form a connexon. Connexons then form gap junctions.

1Jb2Gu.title: CRB-65 score
1Jb2Gu.description: A score used to decide whether patients with pneumonia require hospitalization. Confusion, respiratory rate ≥ 30/min, systolic blood pressure ≤ 90 mm Hg or diastolic BP ≤ 60 mm Hg, and age ≥ 65 years are each assigned 1 point. If the CRB-65 score is ≥ 1, hospitalization is indicated. (not to be confused with CURB-65 score in which blood urea is also considered and a score  ≥ 2 indicates hospitalization)

WJbPGu.title: DNA replication and repair
WJbPGu.description: The process of duplicating DNA using each strand of the original double helix as a template for the new complement strands. Results in two copies of the double helix, each composed of one of the original strands and one complement strand (semiconservative replication).

eJbxGu.title: Translation and protein synthesis
eJbxGu.description: The process by which ribosomes synthesizes polypeptides from a messenger RNA template. The polypeptides then fold into active protein.

TJb6tu.title: Cartilage
TJb6tu.description: A type of avascular, tough, fibrous, and elastic type of connective tissue primarily found in joints and at the end of long bones (around articular surfaces). Composed of chondrocytes, a type of cell that produces collagen, proteoglycans, and other components of extracellular matrix.

hJbcFu.title: The cell cycle
hJbcFu.description: The sequence of events through which cell growth, DNA replication, and cell division occur

RJblFu.title: Female pseudohermaphroditism
RJblFu.description: A condition in which a genotypically female individual with female internal genitalia (i.e., ovaries, fallopian tubes, and uterus) develops male external genitalia/clitoromegaly. The underlying mechanism is hyperandrogenism during embryogenesis. Possible causes include congenital adrenal hyperplasia (most frequently 21β-hydroxylase deficiency) and maternal androgen excess (e.g., due to androgen-producing ovarian tumor or drug intake).

iJbJFu.title: G1 phase
iJbJFu.description: A part of interphase in the cell cycle during which cell growth and synthesis of proteins, RNA, organelles, and cyclin D takes place. Occurs between the M and S phases. G1 checkpoint ensures that the cell is ready to enter S phase.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

media.title: Cell cycle regulation: cyclins and cyclin-dependent kinases

QJbuFu.title: G0 phase
QJbuFu.description: The resting period of a cell after exiting the cell cycle. At this stage, the cell is differentiated and has a specific function but is no longer undergoing cell division.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

jJb_Fu.title: S phase
jJb_Fu.description: A part of the cell cycle during which DNA and histones are synthesized. Occurs between the G1 and G2 phases.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

PJbW8u.title: G2 phase
PJbW8u.description: A part of the interphase of the cell cycle during which cell growth and synthesis of tubulin (required for mitosis) take place. Occurs between the S and M phases. G2 checkpoint ensures that the cell is ready to enter M phase.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

4Jb38u.title: Mitosis
4Jb38u.description: The final phase of the eukaryotic cell cycle that follows after replication of DNA. Results in the production of two genetically identical daughter cells. Begins during the early embryonic period and plays a significant role in growth and development, cell replacement, and regeneration of damaged tissues.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

kJbm8u.title: Prophase
kJbm8u.description: The first stage of mitosis, in which chromosomes condense, centrosomes separate, and the mitotic spindle forms.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

lJbv8u.title: Mitotic spindle
lJbv8u.description: A structure composed of multiple cytoskeletal proteins that forms perpendicular to the axis of cell division to condense chromosomes and facilitate chromosomal separation during mitotic cell division.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

mJbVuu.title: Metaphase
mJbVuu.description: A stage in eukaryotic cell division between prophase and anaphase in which the duplicated chromosomes line up along the equatorial plate. The most important process during metaphase is the spindle assembly checkpoint, which ensures that all chromosomes are attached to microtubules from both sides of the cell and are correctly aligned on the metaphase plate. This ensures the proper division of chromosomes.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

5Jbiuu.title: Anaphase
5Jbiuu.description: The fourth phase of mitosis, in which the sister chromatids separate.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

MJbMuu.title: Telophase
MJbMuu.description: The fifth phase of mitosis, in which cell bodies divide at the equatorial plane, the mitotic spindle disintegrates, and chromosome decondensation occurs.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

nJb7uu.title: Cyclin-dependent kinase
nJb7uu.description: A constitutively inactive enzyme that is activated by cyclin. Responsible for progression of the cell cycle.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

oJb0Eu.title: Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor
oJb0Eu.description: A group of molecules that prevent cell cycle progression by inhibiting cyclin-dependent kinases. Includes several endogenously produced molecules as well as antineoplastic medications (e.g., palbociclib)

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

KJbUEu.title: G1 checkpoint
KJbUEu.description: A cell division checkpoint that restricts entry into the synthesis (S) phase. Without growth signals that lift this checkpoint, cells will not divide. After this checkpoint, cells become committed to division. Loss of this checkpoint (e.g., from loss of p53 function) leads to unregulated cell division.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

media.title: Effects of ionizing radiation on the cell cycle

pJbLEu.title: p53
pJbLEu.description: A tumor suppressor that induces p21, which leads to inhibition of G1→S progression in the cell cycle. Loss of function of p53 results in unregulated cell division, which causes cancer.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

JJbsEu.title: G2 checkpoint
JJbsEu.description: A cell division checkpoint that occurs during the G2 phase. Checks for DNA damage and completeness of DNA replication. Facilitates the initiation of mitosis through phosphorylation of various proteins (e.g., histones). Regulates synchronized cell division. Mediated by mitosis promoting factor (i.e., cyclin B-CDK1 complex).

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

IJbYvu.title: Mitosis promoting factor
IJbYvu.description: A cyclin-CDK complex formed from cyclin B and cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1). Phosphorylates several target proteins that regulate transition of the cell cycle from G2 phase to M phase. Regulates the G2 checkpoint.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

7Jb4vu.title: Protein kinase B
7Jb4vu.description: A serine/threonine-specific protein kinase that regulates key cellular processes such as glucose metabolism, cell proliferation, transcription, apoptosis, and cell migration.

HJbKvu.title: Retinoblastoma protein
HJbKvu.description: A tumor suppressor protein encoded by the RB1 gene on chromosome 13q. It primarily inhibits progression of the cell cycle from the G1 to S phase by binding oncogenic E2F transcription factors. Loss of function of pRb is associated with several malignancies such as retinoblastoma, osteosarcoma, and cervical cancer.

sJbtvu.title: Caspases
sJbtvu.description: Cytosolic proteases that are involved in the pathways of programmed cell death (apoptosis).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Apoptosis

FJbgDu.title: Triphalangeal thumb
FJbgDu.description: A form of polydactyly in which the thumb has three phalanges, instead of the normal two. It is inherited in an autosomal dominant transmission, and is associated with many genetic conditions, including the commonly tested Diamond-Blackfan syndrome.

8JbODu.title: Blueberry muffin syndrome
8JbODu.description: A descriptive term for neonates born with multiple bluish, purple marks in the skin, which can be due to extramedullary erythropoiesis, purpura, or metastases. The differential includes various cancers (e.g., rhabdomyosarcoma), blood disorders (e.g., hemolytic disease of the newborn), and congenital viral infections (e.g., rubella).

destinations.label: Overview of neonatal conditions → Neonatal skin lesions

media.title: Blueberry muffin rash in congenital rubella

uJbpDu.title: Transient erythroblastopenia of childhood
uJbpDu.description: A temporary (1–2 month) pure red cell aplasia that occurs in otherwise healthy children, usually between the ages of 1–4 years old. Hb usually ranges from 6–8 g/dL with normal MVC and reticulocytopenia.

EJb8Du.title: Hypersegmented neutrophil
EJb8Du.description: A neutrophil with >5 lobes, as seen on peripheral blood smear. It is associated with megaloblastic anemias due to B12 or folate deficiency.

vJbADu.title: Germinal matrix
vJbADu.description: A region within the brain that lies between the caudate nucleus and the thalamus and is rich in neurons, glia, and small blood vessels. Cells migrate from it during brain development. Very fragile in preterm infants, which may result in germinal matrix hemorrhage.

DJb1wu.title: Roving eye movements
DJb1wu.description: Slow, conjugate back and forth movements of the eyes (ping-pong gaze).

wJbhwu.title: Superior gluteal nerve
wJbhwu.description: A nerve that arises from L4, L5, and S1. Innervates the gluteus medius and minimus muscles (responsible for abducting the hip) and the tensor fascia lata (hip flexion and medial rotation, knee abduction and lateral rotation). Impairment of this nerve leads to a positive Trendelenburg sign and a Trendelenburg gait.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

media.title: Innervation of the lower extremity (dorsal view)

9JbNwu.title: Inferior gluteal nerve
9JbNwu.description: A nerve that arises from L5, S1, S2. Innervates the ipsilateral gluteus maximus muscle (primary thigh extensor).

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves
Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region

media.title: Innervation of the lower extremity (dorsal view)

CJbqwu.title: Succimer
CJbqwu.description: A chelating agent used in the treatment of arsenic, lead, and mercury poisoning. After binding the toxin in the blood, it is filtered by the kidney and excreted in urine.

xJbEwu.title: Nucleotide
xJbEwu.description: The building block of RNA and DNA. Consists of a nucleoside base, sugar, and phosphate. Examples include guanine, adenine, cytosine, thymine, and uracil.

media.title: General structure of nucleosides and nucleotides

BJbzwu.title: Cytosine
BJbzwu.description: A pyrimidine derivative and one of the four main nitrogenous bases found in both DNA and RNA. Can spontaneously deaminate into a uracil residue.

yJbd9u.title: Thymine
yJbd9u.description: A pyrimidine derivative and one of the four main nitrogenous bases found in DNA. Pairs with adenine in DNA but is replaced by uracil in RNA.

AJbR9u.title: Uracil
AJbR9u.description: A pyrimidine derivative and one of the four main nitrogenous bases found in RNA. Can form from spontaneous deamination of a cytosine residue.

_Jb59u.title: Adenine
_Jb59u.description: A purine derivative and one of the four main nitrogenous bases found in both DNA and RNA. Can spontaneously deaminate into a hypoxanthine residue.

zJbr9u.title: Guanine
zJbr9u.description: A purine derivative and one of the four main nitrogenous bases found in both DNA and RNA. Can spontaneously deaminate into a xanthine residue.

0qbeCu.title: Guanosine
0qbeCu.description: A purine derivative and one of the four main nitrogenous bases found in both DNA and RNA.

Xqb9Cu.title: Deoxyribonucleic acid
Xqb9Cu.description: A nucleic acid that consists of two polynucleotide chains arranged in a double helix. Carries the hereditary information (collectively known as the genome) for the construction and function of an organism.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA → Overview of nucleic acids

cqbaxu.title: RNA
cqbaxu.description: A single stranded molecule composed of ribonucleotides.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA → Overview of nucleic acids

1qb2xu.title: Double helix
1qb2xu.description: A pair of parallel helices coiled around the same axis (e.g., the structure of DNA)

WqbPxu.title: Anti-Müllerian hormone
WqbPxu.description: A hormone produced during fetal development by Sertoli cells (within the testes) that suppresses the formation of the paramesonephric duct, which would otherwise become the fallopian tubes, uterus, and upper portion of the vagina.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Ductal sex differentiation

dqboxu.title: Supercoil
dqboxu.description: The overwinding (positive supercoils) or underwinding (negative supercoils) of a DNA strand. Plays a role in the compacting and packaging of DNA within cells and also regulates gene expression. Can be formed during DNA replication as helicase unwinds double-stranded DNA.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

VqbGxu.title: Palindromic sequence
VqbGxu.description: A series of nucleotides in which the sequence in the 5'→3' direction of one strand matches the sequence in the 5'→3' of the complementary strand (e.g., the sequence 5'-AGGATCCT-3'). Results in the formation of a cross-shaped structure in double-stranded DNA that can function as a specific binding site.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

eqbxxu.title: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery
eqbxxu.description: An artery that arises from the basilar artery at the level of the medulla. It courses posteriorly to supply the anteroinferior cerebellum, the middle cerebellar peduncle, and the inferolateral pons before it anastomoses with the posterior inferior cerebellar artery.

UqbbBu.title: Lateral pontine syndrome
UqbbBu.description: A neurological condition caused by infarction of the lateral pons that can involve nearby cranial nerve nuclei. Caused by occlusion of the anterior inferior cerebellar artery or branches of the basilar artery. Manifestations include Horner syndrome, facial paralysis and droop, decreased taste from the anterior ⅔ of the tongue, decreased facial sensation for pain and temperature vertigo, audiovestibular dysfunction, and ataxia.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

2qbTBu.title: 11β-hydroxylase
2qbTBu.description: An enzyme that is produced predominantly in the adrenal cortex and plays an important role in steroidogenesis. Deficiency of this enzyme is the second most common cause of congenital adrenal hyperplasia, which is characterized by ↑ 17-hydroxyprogesterone, ↑↑ DOC, and ↓ corticosterone.

fqbkBu.title: Splitting (psychiatry)
fqbkBu.description: A type I (pathological) defense mechanism that involves segregating experiences and people into extremes of all-good and all-bad because of an inability to integrate the good and bad images of both self and others into a cohesive whole. Very common in borderline personality disorder.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

Tqb6Bu.title: Sertoli cell tumor
Tqb6Bu.description: Rare non-germ cell testicular tumor that derives from normal Sertoli cells (which facilitate spermatogenesis). Can produce estrogen and lead to gynecomastia in affected men.

gqbFBu.title: Potassium iodide
gqbFBu.description: An antithyroid drug that inhibits the release of thyroid hormones by preventing the proteolytic cleavage of T3 and T4 from thyroglobulin. Potassium iodide also decreases the vascularity and size of the goiter. Used as an adjunctive therapy in hyperthyroidism, thyroid storm, and as a pre-treatment before thyroid surgery.

SqbyBu.title: Selective mutism
SqbyBu.description: A childhood anxiety disorder characterized by refusal to speak in certain situations (e.g., at school or at the doctor's office) while readily speaking with family or friends.

hqbcyu.title: Pregnancy-associated protein A
hqbcyu.description: A serum protein that is mainly synthesized by the placenta, which therefore increases in concentration during pregnancy. Since PAPP-A levels are decreased in conditions involving chromosomal aberrations such as Down syndrome, PAPP-A measurement is part of first-trimester screening.

3qbSyu.title: Middle East respiratory syndrome
3qbSyu.description: An infection caused by coronavirus, which presents with acute respiratory syndrome and acute kidney injury.

Rqblyu.title: Palifermin
Rqblyu.description: A recombinant keratinocyte growth factor used to prevent severe mucositis following combined radiochemotherapy.

iqbJyu.title: Disinhibited social engagement disorder
iqbJyu.description: A psychiatric disorder of childhood characterized by uninhibited interactions with nonfamiliar adults. Associated with emotional neglect during infancy.

destinations.label: Trauma- and stressor-related disorders → Disinhibited social engagement disorder

Qqbuyu.title: Dexrazoxane
Qqbuyu.description: An EDTA-derivative that is used to prevent cardiotoxicity associated with high-doses of anthracycline-based chemotherapeutic agents (e.g., doxorubicin, daunorubicin), and/or to treat extravasation of parenterally administered anthracyclines.

4qb3Au.title: Acrolein
4qb3Au.description: A urotoxic substance produced in the metabolism of oxazaphosphorines such as cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide. Acrolein causes damage to the bladder epithelium and can lead to hemorrhagic cystitis and, less commonly, bladder carcinoma. Prophylactic administration of mesna can prevent hemorrhagic cystitis by binding to acrolein, which is then excreted renally.

kqbmAu.title: Spoon nails
kqbmAu.description: An abnormality of the finger nails that is characterized by spoon-shaped concavity. Typically manifests as a feature of iron deficiency anemia. Less common reasons are high altitude, genetic predisposition, trauma, and exposure to petroleum products.

OqbIAu.title: Messenger RNA
OqbIAu.description: A type of RNA that carries the amino acid sequence for protein-coding genes from DNA to the ribosome. Typically modified with a 5' methylated guanine cap and 3' poly(A) tail to protect the transcript from ribonucleases and exonucleases, respectively.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

lqbvAu.title: tRNA
lqbvAu.description: A short, specialized RNA adapter molecule, typically 75-90 nucleotides long, that carries specific amino acids to the ribosome during protein translation. Charged with amino acids by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

Nqb-Au.title: rRNA
Nqb-Au.description: A specialized form of RNA that comprises the majority of the ribosome.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

Lqbw_u.title: MicroRNA
Lqbw_u.description: A small, noncoding RNA molecule (~ 22 nucleotides in length) that combines with ribonuclease enzymes to form the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC) to regulates gene expression. miRNAs decrease protein expression by binding to the 3' untranslated region of mRNA to prevent translation or induce degradation of the mRNA molecule.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

pqbLzu.title: Mitochondrial DNA
pqbLzu.description: A segment of the eukaryotic genome contained within mitochondria (as opposed to the nucleus). Represents a very small portion of the overall genome. Inherited entirely from the mother.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

qqbCzu.title: Hyperphagia
qqbCzu.description: An abnormally enhanced desire for food, resulting in overeating and obesity. Often seen as a feature of inherited disorders (e.g., Prader-Willi syndrome).

destinations.label: Rare inherited syndromes → Prader-Willi syndrome and Angelman syndrome

IqbY-u.title: Lead poisoning
IqbY-u.description: A condition caused by the accumulation of lead in the body. Clinical features vary based on blood lead level and can include cognitive impairment, encephalopathy, abdominal colic, and peripheral neuropathy. Management includes chelation therapy and removal of the source of exposure.

rqbf-u.title: Histones
rqbf-u.description: A group of proteins that bind to DNA in the nucleus of eukaryotes to support the structure of chromatin via coiling and uncoiling of DNA helices.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

7qb4-u.title: Cold agglutinin disease
7qb4-u.description: A primary (idiopathic) disease in which hemolysis is mediated by monoclonal cold-sensitive IgM autoantibodies produced by a low-grade clonal B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the bone marrow. Manifestations include acrocyanosis, Raynaud phenomenon, hemolytic anemia, and venous thromboembolism.

destinations.label: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia → Cold agglutinin hemolytic anemia

HqbK-u.title: Trophozoites
HqbK-u.description: The active, motile, feeding stage of a sporozoan parasite (e.g., Plasmodium falciparum, Giardia).

sqbt-u.title: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase
sqbt-u.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the first committed step of the pentose phosphate pathway: the oxidation of glucose-6-phosphate to 6-phosphogluconolactone with the concomitant reduction of NADP to NADPH.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Pentose phosphate pathway

media.title: Reduction and oxidation reactions of glutathione

GqbB-u.title: Branched-chain amino acid
GqbB-u.description: An amino acid with an aliphatic side chain. The three branched chain amino acids are valine, leucine, and isoleucine. A defect in the metabolism of branched chain amino acids causes maple syrup urine disease.

tqbXZE.title: Atrophic glossitis
tqbXZE.description: A condition characterized by a painful, erythematous, edematous tongue that appears smooth due to loss of papillae. Caused by underlying nutritional deficiencies (e.g., iron, vitamin B12, folic acid, riboflavin, or niacin).

FqbgZE.title: Total iron binding capacity
FqbgZE.description: A laboratory test that determines the capacity of the blood to bind iron. An indirect measure of transferrin, the iron transport protein. Useful to differentiate different types of microcytic anemias.

8qbOZE.title: Bite cells
8qbOZE.description: An RBC with one or more semicircular portions removed ("bitten off") from the cell margin. These "bites" occur due to the removal of denatured hemoglobin inclusions (Heinz bodies) by macrophages in the spleen and are seen in Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

Eqb8ZE.title: Milk-alkali syndrome
Eqb8ZE.description: A syndrome caused by excessive consumption of calcium and absorbable alkali (most commonly calcium carbonate). Manifests with hypercalcemia, metabolic alkalosis, and acute kidney injury.

vqbAZE.title: Growing pains
vqbAZE.description: A benign condition commonly seen in children between 3-12 years of age. Typically presents with episodes of nighttime pain in the lower extremities (calves, shins, thighs). Pain is not present during the day or with activity.

Dqb10E.title: Ornithine transcarbamylase
Dqb10E.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of carbamoyl phosphate and ornithine to citrulline and inorganic phosphate. OTC is located predominantly in the mitochondria of hepatocytes and is involved in the urea cycle, which generates urea from ammonia.

wqbh0E.title: Hair tourniquet syndrome
wqbh0E.description: Medical condition in which a fiber (hair, thread, etc.) becomes tightly wrapped around an appendage, putting it at risk of ischemic damage. Symptoms are a painful, swollen, reddened appendage with a deep groove proximal to it, in which the constricting fiber may be visible.

destinations.label: Acute limb ischemia → Subtypes and variants

9qbN0E.title: Amniotic band syndrome
9qbN0E.description: A congenital disorder caused by entrapment of fetal parts (usually a limb or digits) in fibrous amniotic bands while in-utero. Presentation is highly variable for each case, and includes absence of the distal portion of digits, syndactyly, abdominal wall defects, visceral protrusions, craniofacial anomalies, and/or constriction bands around various parts of the body.

media.title: Hand affected by amniotic band syndrome

Cqbq0E.title: QT dispersion
Cqbq0E.description: The variability in QT intervals between ECG leads (maximum QT interval minus minimum QT interval). In healthy Individuals there is no dispersion as ventricular electric function is synchronic.

xqbE0E.title: Acute chest syndrome
xqbE0E.description: A complication of sickle cell disease characterized by new chest infiltrate and respiratory symptoms. Typically presents with chest pain, dyspnea, and hypoxia. While the exact pathophysiology is unknown, symptoms occur due to vaso-occlusive crisis within the pulmonary vasculature. Carries a high risk of mortality.

media.title: Consolidation in the left lower lobe

Bqbz0E.title: Ingrown toe nail
Bqbz0E.description: A common nail pathology that develops when the corner or sides of the toenail grow into the surrounding paronychium or nail bed. Symptoms include pain along the margins of the nail, and features of secondary infection.

yqbdaE.title: Hydrocelectomy
yqbdaE.description: A surgical procedure performed to correct a hydrocele and prevent its recurrence. Indicated for the reduction of large or thick-walled hydroceles and involves incision and complete or partial resection of the hydrocele sac (tunica vaginalis).

AqbRaE.title: Developmental milestones
AqbRaE.description: The physical, cognitive, social, and/or emotional abilities that most children can perform by a given age.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Developmental milestones

_qb5aE.title: Varicocelectomy
_qb5aE.description: A surgical procedure performed to treat varicoceles by ligating dilated veins of the pampiniform plexus to relieve venous congestion and redirect blood flow.

zqbraE.title: Rhizopus
zqbraE.description: A genus of molds that are ubiquitous in decaying vegetation and soil. In immunocompromised and diabetic patients, they can cause mucormycosis, a fungal rhino-orbital-cerebral, pulmonary, or cutaneous infection.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Opportunistic fungal infections

-qbDaE.title: 21β-Hydroxylase deficiency
-qbDaE.description: The most common form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia caused by a deficiency of 21β-hydroxylase enzyme. It presents with hypotension, ambiguous genitalia, and virilization (in the female genotype), and/or precocious puberty (in both males and females). Patients may also have hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and metabolic acidosis. Diagnosis is confirmed by increased levels of 17-hydroxyprogesterone.

ZIbZYE.title: Mucor
ZIbZYE.description: A genus of molds that are ubiquitous in decaying vegetation and soil. In immunocompromised and diabetic patients, they can cause mucormycosis, a fungal rhino-orbital-cerebral, pulmonary, or cutaneous infection.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Opportunistic fungal infections

0IbeYE.title: Cardiobacterium hominis
0IbeYE.description: A fastidious, gram-negative coccobacilli that belongs to the HACEK group of organisms (Haemophilus species, Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans, Cardiobacterium hominis, Eikenella corrodens, Kingella kingae).

YIbnYE.title: Keyboard shortcuts for AMBOSS
YIbnYE.description:
A-G → select answers A-G
P → attending physicians commentary
Q → highlight relevant terms in question
R → study radar in learning card
S → show answer (= give up)
T → what we still need to consider (light bulb)
W → highlighting of high yield information in learning card
X → show difficulty of question
5 → show answer statistics
space → open all answers or learning card sections

bIbHYE.title: Fibroma
bIbHYE.description: A benign tumor composed of connective tissue. Can occur almost anywhere in the body; common locations include the ovaries, uterus, skin, and tendons.

XIb9YE.title: Riboflavin
XIb9YE.description: A water-soluble vitamin which is mainly found in milk, dairy products, meat, fish and green vegetables. Symptoms of riboflavin deficiency include cheilitis, glossitis, stomatitis, seborrheic dermatitis, corneal revascularization and a normochromic, normocytic anemia. Deficiency is usually caused by insufficient dietary intake or increased demand (e.g., during pregnancy, lactation).

cIbabE.title: Vitamin A deficiency
cIbabE.description: A deficiency in retinol and its derivatives, which are fat-soluble vitamins found predominantly in liver, meat, eggs, whole milk, carrots, and green leafy vegetables. Symptoms include xerophthalmia, xeroderma, and night blindness. Associated with fat malabsorption conditions (e.g., cystic fibrosis).

WIbPbE.title: Bilateral optic disc swelling
WIbPbE.description: An important clinical finding that indicates elevated intracranial pressure.

dIbobE.title: Clomiphene citrate
dIbobE.description: A nonsteroidal drug that acts as an estrogen receptor antagonist in the hypothalamus and thereby disrupts the normal feedback inhibition on gonadotropins (LH, FSH). This results in an increased secretion of gonadotropins from the pituitary, which stimulates ovulation. It is commonly used for oligoovulation or anovulation (e.g., polycystic ovary syndrome).

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

media.title: Drugs influencing the function of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal-axis

VIbGbE.title: Letrozole
VIbGbE.description: An aromatase inhibitor that decreases estrogen production by inhibiting the conversion of androgens to estrogens. Used to treat postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer and women with anovulatory cycles (e.g., due to polycystic ovary syndrome).

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

eIbxbE.title: Exchange transfusion
eIbxbE.description: The process of removing red blood cells (erythrocytapheresis) and serum from a patient and replacing them with allogeneic (donor) red blood cells and fluid (normal saline, serum, or albumin solution). Most commonly performed for management of sickle cell disease. Other less common indications include severe neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, ABO incompatibility, and severe intraerythrocytic parasetemia.

UIbbXE.title: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
UIbbXE.description: A severe hypersensitivity reaction that most commonly occurs 2–8 weeks after drug exposure. The most common causative agents are antiepileptics (e.g., lamotrigine, carbamazepine), allopurinol, sulfonamides, and vancomycin. Manifestations include fever, lymphadenopathy, a diffuse rash, facial edema, and eosinophilia.

destinations.label: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms

media.title: Facial edema in drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)

2IbTXE.title: Meningococcal septicemia
2IbTXE.description: The systemic dissemination of meningococci in the blood, which often occurs concomitantly with meningococcal meningitis but can also occur on its own. Causes high fever, organ failure, and typically a petechial or purpuric rash.

fIbkXE.title: Lactic acidosis
fIbkXE.description: A high anion gap metabolic acidosis caused by the elevation of serum lactate. Etiologies include severe tissue hypoxia, liver failure (due to decreased clearance), and metformin use. Elevated lactate is clinical serum marker for tissue hypoperfusion.

TIb6XE.title: Proptosis
TIb6XE.description: An anterior protrusion or bulging of the eye(s) caused by disease within the orbit, e.g., orbital cellulitis, malignancy, myopathy, or cavernous sinus thrombosis. Exophthalmos is a subset of proptosis that is typically bilateral and associated with endocrine disorders, e.g., Graves disease.

gIbFXE.title: Nonbullous impetigo
gIbFXE.description: A type of impetigo typically characterized by small papules and pustules on an erythematous base that rupture and form honey-colored crusts. Most commonly located on the face and extremities. Can be pruritic but is rarely painful. Most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus (~ 80% of cases) and Group A Streptococcus pyogenes (~ 10% of case). Typically managed with topical antibiotics (e.g., mupirocin).

SIbyXE.title: Bullous impetigo
SIbyXE.description: A type of impetigo typically characterized by flaccid vesicles and bullae that rupture and form thin, brown crusts. Typically located on the trunk and upper extremities. Most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus strains that produce exfoliative toxins A and B. Typically managed with systemic antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin, dicloxacillin).

3IbScE.title: 17-hydroxyprogesterone
3IbScE.description: A steroid hormone that is derived from progesterone and is a precursor in cortisol biosynthesis. Serum levels are measured to screen for congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Elevated levels are found in defects of the 21β-hydroxylase and 11β-hydroxylase enzyme. Decreased levels are found in defects of the 17α-hydroxylase enzyme.

RIblcE.title: Familial hypercholesterolemia
RIblcE.description: An autosomal-dominant condition associated with mutations in the LDL receptor that lead to elevated LDL levels with early atherosclerotic complications (cardiovascular disease).

iIbJcE.title: Pericardial effusion
iIbJcE.description: The acute or chronic accumulation of fluid in the pericardial space (between the parietal and the visceral pericardium). Can lead to compression of the heart and circulatory insufficiency (cardiac tamponade).

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Summary

media.title: Pericardial effusion with water bottle configuration

QIbucE.title: Cardiac tamponade
QIbucE.description: A compression of the heart (especially the right ventricle) caused by pericardial effusion, which leads to circulatory insufficiency.

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Summary

jIb_cE.title: Beta-thalassemia
jIb_cE.description: A hemoglobinopathy characterized by impaired production of one or both beta chains of hemoglobin.

PIbW1E.title: Parent training in behavioral management
PIbW1E.description: A training that teaches parents of children with ADHD how to understand and manage their child's condition, how to manage problematic situations, and how to support positive behavior using operant conditioning.

4Ib31E.title: Phagocyte
4Ib31E.description: A specialized cell that ingests and destroys dead cells and debris, foreign particles, and/or invading microorgansisms. White blood cells that can act as phagocytes include monocytes, differentiated monocytes (i.e., macrophages), and granulocytes (i.e., neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital neutrophil and phagocyte disorders

kIbm1E.title: Keratomalacia
kIbm1E.description: A softening of the cornea. Can be caused by vitamin A deficiency.

lIbv1E.title: Alpha thalassemia
lIbv1E.description: A hemoglobinopathy characterized by deficiency of any of the 4 alpha globin chains. There are four types according to the amount of deficient chains: minima (silent carrier), minor (alpha thalassemia trait), intermedia (Hb H disease), and major (Hb Bart disease).

NIb-1E.title: Bitot's spot
NIb-1E.description: An ophthalmologic finding of gray, triangular patches on the bulbar conjunctivae of patients with vitamin A deficiency.

mIbVWE.title: Leukemoid reaction
mIbVWE.description: An exaggerated reactive leukocytosis (WBC elevation 50,000–100,000/mm³) in response to often benign etiologies such as inflammation (e.g., organ rejection) or infection (e.g., sepsis) or, less commonly, solid malignant tumors.

5IbiWE.title: Primary dysmenorrhea
5IbiWE.description: Lower abdominal and pelvic pain that occurs shortly before and/or during menstruation in the absence of pelvic pathology. Caused by increased prostaglandin levels.

MIbMWE.title: Secondary dysmenorrhea
MIbMWE.description: Lower abdominal and pelvic pain that occurs shortly before and/or during menstruation and is due to an underlying pelvic condition.

nIb7WE.title: Calcineurin inhibitors
nIb7WE.description: A group of immunosuppressant drugs that act by inhibiting interleukin-2 production and IL-2 receptor expression, reducing T-cell activation. Examples include tacrolimus, cyclosporine, and pimecrolimus.

oIb0dE.title: Fluorescent spot test
oIb0dE.description: A screening test used for identifying enzyme defects (e.g., G6PD deficiency, galactosemia). In diagnosis of G6PD deficiency a blood sample is incubated with glucose-6-phosphate and NADP. Normal G6PD activity produces fluorescent NADPH out of NADP, while in G6PD deficiency a lack of fluorescence is seen.

KIbUdE.title: Pulmonary apoplexy
KIbUdE.description: Pulmonary hemorrhage and hemoptysis caused by rupture of bronchial veins from elevated pulmonary capillary pressure. May be associated with severe mitral stenosis or severe left-ventricular failure.

6IbjdE.title: Physiological neonatal jaundice
6IbjdE.description: Jaundice that is caused by the normal changes in neonatal bilirubin metabolism after birth (increased production and enterohepatic circulation; decreased clearance). Occurs in around half of term infants and almost all preterm infants. Manifests between the 2nd and 8th day of life in term infants (up to 2 weeks in preterm infants) and is usually most severe on the 5th day. Affected neonates are usually asymptomatic, except for transient icterus.

pIbLdE.title: Supraglottoplasty
pIbLdE.description: A microsurgical procedure to remove or alter obstructing tissue of the upper larynx in order to provide a more stable and patent airway in children with laryngomalacia.

JIbsdE.title: Uridine 5'-diphospho-glucuronosyltransferase
JIbsdE.description: An enzyme of the liver that catalyzes important glucuronidation reactions, such as the conjugation of bilirubin. The water-soluble, conjugated bilirubin can then be excreted via bile into the intestine or in urine.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Metabolism of erythrocytes

qIbCdE.title: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulation test
qIbCdE.description: A test used to evaluate the reactivity of the hypothalamic-pituitary-axis to GnRH stimulation. LH and FSH levels are measured after administration of GnRH. Can be used to distinguish between hypogonadism caused by dysfunction of the hypothalamus or the pituitary gland in patients with decreased basal gonadotropin concentrations. Indications for testing include suspected central precocious puberty or delayed puberty.

rIbfVE.title: Embryotoxon
rIbfVE.description: A thickening of Schwalbe's ring in the cornea. Schwalbe's ring is formed by the junction of the trabecular meshwork and Descemet's membrane. Posterior embryotoxon, which refers to an embryotoxon that is readily apparent without slit-lamp examination, can be inherited as a dominant trait or occur in diseases such as Alagille syndrome, familial aniridia, and X-linked ichthyosis.

7Ib4VE.title: Caroli disease
7Ib4VE.description: A condition characterized by abnormal widening of the intrahepatic bile ducts and renal cysts. Manifestations include recurrent cholestasis, choledocholithiasis, and cholangitis. Most often accompanied by renal cystic disease of varying severity.

HIbKVE.title: Hypotonia
HIbKVE.description: A physical examination finding of low or decreased muscle tone. Can occur as a symptom of congenital or acquired diseases (e.g., Down syndrome, lower motor neuron disease, Guillain-Barré syndrome, myasthenia gravis).

sIbtVE.title: Levonorgestrel
