sIbtVE.description: A progestin (i.e., progesterone analog) that can be used alone for emergency contraception within 120 hours of unprotected intercourse or in combination with estrogen for routine oral contraception.

GIbBVE.title: Mifepristone
GIbBVE.description: A progesterone antagonist that disrupts the effects of progesterone during pregnancy. Used in combination with a prostaglandin analog during medication abortions.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

tIbXeE.title: Ulipristal
tIbXeE.description: A selective progesterone receptor modulator used chiefly as an emergency contraceptive. It can also be used to treat the symptoms of uterine fibroids. It is metabolized by CYP 3A4, leading to serious drug-drug interactions if given with other CYP 3A4 substrates.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

FIbgeE.title: Combined oral contraceptive pill
FIbgeE.description: An oral medication that contains both estrogen and progesterone. In addition to working as a contraceptive, these medications are used to treat polycystic ovarian syndrome, endometriosis, amenorrhea, and other conditions. Adverse effects include an increased risk of venous thromboembolism, hypertension, and hepatic adenoma.

8IbOeE.title: HIV serology
8IbOeE.description: A group of tests that evaluate the antibody immune response to HIV infection. Does not directly test for the presence of HIV. Includes ELISA, simple and rapid tests, and Western blot.

uIbpeE.title: Hemoglobin electrophoresis
uIbpeE.description: A test that measures the different types of hemoglobin in the blood by using electrical current to separate them. Used to diagnose, e.g., sickle cell anemia and thalassemia.

vIbAeE.title: Ventricular preexcitation
vIbAeE.description: The premature electrical activation of the ventricles due to conduction through an accessory pathway. Typically accompanied by a preexcitation pattern on resting ECG, although this is variable and often masked by associated tachyarrhythmias, during which the only indications may be a heart rate > 200/min and a wide QRS complex.

DIb1UE.title: Splice site mutation
DIb1UE.description: A genetic mutation at the specific site in between exons and introns that may cause changes in splicing that result in the inclusion of introns or the loss of exons. Can have a variable effect on the phenotype, depending on the exact location of the mutation.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

xIbEUE.title: Nucleosome
xIbEUE.description: An organizational unit in the eukaryotic cell. Consists of a segment of DNA coiled twice around an octamer composed of histone proteins H2A, H2B, H3, H4 with one final histone (H1) as the linker protein.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

yIbd2E.title: Linker DNA
yIbd2E.description: A portion of DNA that binds to the linker histone H1 to stabilize chromatin fibers of the nucleosome.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

_Ib52E.title: Chromatin
_Ib52E.description: A complex of DNA and histone proteins that package DNA within the nucleus. The basic structural unit of chromatin is the nucleosome.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

zIbr2E.title: Heterochromatin
zIbr2E.description: A condensed form of chromatin that is sterically inaccessible and thus transcriptionally inactive. Typically has increased histone methylation and decreased acetylation.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

arbQfE.title: Sister chromatids
arbQfE.description: Two identical copies of the same chromosome joined together at the centromere before cell division. When joined together, sister chromatids are called dyads.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

media.title: Homologous chromosomes before and after replication

YrbnfE.title: Kinetochore
YrbnfE.description: A protein complex found at the centromere that allows for the attachment of mitotic spindle microtubules during mitosis. Sister chromatids are drawn to the opposing poles of the mitotic spindle by these structures.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

brbHfE.title: Centromere
brbHfE.description: A condensed region of the chromosome where sister chromatids join. Divides the chromatids into a short p arm and a long q arm. Mediates attachment of the chromosome to the meiotic or mitotic spindle.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

Xrb9fE.title: Well-child visits
Xrb9fE.description: A series of periodic preventive care examinations that are performed at the ages of 3-5 days (in-hospital examination), 1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 24, 30, and 36 months, and yearly thereafter until adulthood. Performed to screen for disorders of growth and development, among other medical and psychosocial conditions.

media.title: Length- and weight-for-age percentiles for age (girls 0–24 months)

crbaTE.title: Growth faltering
crbaTE.description: A pattern of slow growth in children compared to the predicted values for their age and sex. Often secondary to malnutrition, which can be due to a complex interplay between multiple biological, nutritional, and psychosocial factors. Growth faltering is classified according to growth charts from the WHO (for those < 2 years of age) and CDC (for those 2-20 years of age).

media.title: Stature- and weight-for-age percentiles (female individuals 2–20 years; 3ʳᵈ–97ᵗʰ percentiles)

WrbPTE.title: Immunoglobulin M
WrbPTE.description: A class of large, pentameric (5-sided) antibodies that is generally the first immunoglobulin produced by plasma cells in the spleen and lymph nodes in response to initial contact with a new antigen. IgM antibodies in a patient's serum indicates recent/acute infection.

drboTE.title: IgG
drboTE.description: The most abundant immunoglobulin in serum. Can be free-floating in serum or bound to the surface of lymphocytes. Production in response to an antigen is delayed. Important for long-term immunity; IgG antibodies have high affinity and specificity for their corresponding antigens. Crosses the placenta, facilitating conferral of passive immunity as well as hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn.

media.title: General structure of immunoglobulins exemplified by IgG

VrbGTE.title: IgA
VrbGTE.description: A class of antibody found on mucosal surfaces and in bodily fluids (e.g., tears, saliva, mucus, breast milk).  Important for mucosal immunity. Secreted in dimeric form but circulates in monomeric form.

erbxTE.title: IgE
erbxTE.description: An immunoglobulin that binds to mast cells, resulting in the release of histamine. Thought to function in the defense against parasites. Mediates immediate-type reactions (type I hypersensitivity).

UrbbgE.title: IgD
UrbbgE.description: A monomeric class of antibody located on the surface of mature B lymphocytes. Its function and clinical relevance are not yet fully understood.

2rbTgE.title: Autoantibodies
2rbTgE.description: A group of antibodies that react with self-antigens. Can be seen in healthy individuals and in several autoimmune disorders (e.g., antithyroid antibodies in Hashimoto thyroiditis and Graves disease).

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → Immune tolerance and autoimmunity

grbFgE.title: Factitious hypocalcemia
grbFgE.description: A condition characterized by decreased total calcium with a normal ionized (active) calcium. Since ionized calcium is within normal range, this condition is asymptomatic. Typically occurs due to hypoalbuminemia (total calcium levels appear low because of a decreased amount bound to albumin).

SrbygE.title: Iron poisoning
SrbygE.description: A condition caused by the acute accumulation of iron in the body after oral ingestion. Most common in toddlers (ingestion of red iron tablets mistaken for candy). Presents with hemorrhagic gastroenteritis, dark-colored stools (i.e., false melena), shock symptoms, and possibly renal or liver failure.

hrbcSE.title: Chronic iron toxicity
hrbcSE.description: A condition caused by the chronic accumulation of iron due to a variety of causes, including hereditary hemochromatosis, repeated blood transfusions, excessive iron therapy, or liver disease. Clinical features include cirrhosis and liver failure, heart failure, severe diabetes, and bronze skin discoloration.

3rbSSE.title: Speculum examination
3rbSSE.description: A part of the gynecological examination performed by inserting a speculum device into the vagina in order to visually inspect the vaginal wall and ectocervix and obtain cytological smears.

destinations.label: Diagnostic procedures in gynecology → Speculum examination

media.title: Medical speculum examination of the vagina

irbJSE.title: Transcription
irbJSE.description: A process in which DNA is used as a template for mRNA synthesis by RNA polymerase.

QrbuSE.title: Delta gap
QrbuSE.description: The delta gap = ∆ anion gap/∆ bicarbonate. ∆ Anion gap = measured anion gap - 12 (12 is the normal anion gap) and ∆ bicarbonate = 24 - measured serum bicarbonate (24 is the normal serum bicarbonate level). The delta gap is measured in patients with high anion gap metabolic acidosis (HAGMA) to determine if a mixed acid-base disorder is present. If the delta ratio is 1–2, then only HAGMA is present. If the delta ratio is < 1, an additional normal anion gap metabolic acidosis is present. If the ratio is > 2.0, an additional metabolic alkalosis is present.

4rb3hE.title: Sexual dysfunction
4rb3hE.description: A group of conditions that includes lack of sexual desire (libido), impaired arousal, inability to achieve orgasm, and pain with sexual activity. Etiologies are often multifactorial and include psychosocial, hormonal, neurologic, and vascular causes.

destinations.label: Sexual dysfunction and paraphilic disorders → Sexual dysfunction

krbmhE.title: Uterine aspiration
krbmhE.description: A procedure in which the contents of the uterine cavity are evacuated using suction, typically with a manual or electric vacuum. Commonly performed for procedural abortion, management of miscarriage, and diagnostic sampling of the endometrium.

OrbIhE.title: Zidovudine
OrbIhE.description: An antiretroviral nucleoside analog that inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase (nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor). Used for the treatment of HIV infection and post-exposure prophylaxis of perinatal HIV transmission in neonates. Potential adverse effects include bone marrow suppression, myopathy, hepatomegaly, and lactic acidosis.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

lrbvhE.title: Nevirapine
lrbvhE.description: An antiretroviral non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used for treatment of HIV infection. Adverse effects include hepatotoxicity and rash.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

mrbV3E.title: Mittelschmerz
mrbV3E.description: Unilateral, lower abdominal pain experienced by some individuals during ovulation. The etiology is unclear; potential causes include follicle rupture, spasms of the fallopian tube or uterus, and peritoneal irritation from follicular fluid.

5rbi3E.title: Xerosis
5rbi3E.description: A condition of dry skin that can result from environmental factors (e.g., low humidity, cold exposure, sun exposure), behavioral factors (e.g., excessive skin washing), vitamin deficiency (vitamins A and D), skin diseases (e.g., psoriasis, eczema), systemic conditions (e.g., Sjögren syndrome), or drug adverse effects (e.g., topical retinoids).

MrbM3E.title: Dystrophin gene
MrbM3E.description: The largest gene in the human body, which is located on chromosome Xp and codes for a protein called dystrophin in skeletal and cardiac muscle. Dystrophin forms a part of the cellular cytoskeleton that strengthens muscle fibers. Small amounts of dystrophin are also found in nerve cells. Mutations of the dystrophin gene are responsible for Duchenne's and Becker's muscular dystrophies as well as certain familial cardiomyopathies.

nrb73E.title: Physiologic leukorrhea
nrb73E.description: Vaginal discharge that is white or yellow and non-malodorous in a patient with no findings that would indicate pathology, such as  vaginal pruritus or tenderness. Even profuse discharge is, by itself, not a sign of pathology. The amount of vaginal discharge can vary based on a woman's menstrual stage and age.

destinations.label: Diagnostic procedures in gynecology → Speculum examination

Lrbw3E.title: Endometrial polyp
Lrbw3E.description: Overgrowth of localized endometrial tissue that may be pedunculated or sessile, single or multiple, and up to many centimeters in size. The lesions may contain blood vessels and cause irregular menstrual bleeding, spotting, menorrhagia, and postmenopausal bleeding. Risk factors include arterial hypertension, obesity, a history of cervical polyps, and/or tamoxifen or hormone replacement therapy.

destinations.label: Benign and premalignant lesions of the endometrium → Endometrial polyps

orb0RE.title: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia
orb0RE.description: A type of hemolytic anemia that is the result of mechanical damage to erythrocytes by microthrombi in small blood vessels. Characterized by schistocytes on the peripheral blood smear. Common causes include thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, hemolytic uremic syndrome, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and HELLP syndrome.

destinations.label: Hemolytic anemia → Mechanical destruction of RBCs

KrbURE.title: Kasabach-Merritt syndrome
KrbURE.description: A condition characterized by consumption coagulopathy and/or thrombocytopenia. Most commonly occurs in children and manifests with a large hemangioma (due to microthrombi formation within the hemangioma).

6rbjRE.title: Hemoglobin A2
6rbjRE.description: A form of adult hemoglobin that makes up less than 3% of total hemoglobin. Consists of 2 α-globin and 2 δ-globin subunits (α2δ2). Increased HbA2 levels can be seen in patients with beta thalassemia.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin variants

JrbsRE.title: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia
JrbsRE.description: A conjugated (direct) bilirubin concentration > 1 mg/dL if the total bilirubin is < 5 mg/dL, or more than 20% of the total bilirubin if the total bilirubin is > 5 mg/dL. Due to intrahepatic cholestasis (hepatocellular injury through infection, cirrhosis, inflammation, etc.) or extrahepatic outflow obstruction (biliary obstruction by calculi, malignancies, strictures, etc.).

qrbCRE.title: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia
qrbCRE.description: The presence of increased concentrations of the unconjugated (“indirect”) fraction of bilirubin in the serum. Etiologies include increased production (e.g., from hemolysis, hematoma resorption), impaired conjugation (e.g., from metabolic disorders), and impaired hepatic uptake of bilirubin.

rrbfiE.title: Abnormal uterine bleeding
rrbfiE.description: Menstruation that is abnormal in regularity, volume, frequency, and/or duration, intermenstrual bleeding, or unscheduled bleeding while on hormonal contraceptives. Usually applies to bleeding in nonpregnant individuals of reproductive age

7rb4iE.title: Genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder
7rb4iE.description: A DSM-5 sexual disorder that is characterized by ≥ 6 months of difficulty with sexual intercourse, vulvovaginal or pelvic pain during intercourse, fear or anxiety about pain related to sexual intercourse, and/or tightening of the pelvic floor muscles during attempted vaginal penetration; and that is not attributable to nonsexual mental disorders, severe stress (e.g., partner violence), medication or substance use, or another medical condition.

destinations.label: Sexual dysfunction and paraphilic disorders → Sexual dysfunction

HrbKiE.title: Bicuspid aortic valve
HrbKiE.description: A congenital abnormality in the aortic valve. In utero, two leaflets of the aortic valve fuse, resulting in only two leaflets instead of the usual three. A common occurrence in patients with Turner syndrome. Predisposes to both aortic stenosis and aortic regurgitation.

srbtiE.title: Misoprostol
srbtiE.description: A synthetic prostaglandin E1 analog that is used in the termination of intrauterine pregnancies, to induce cervical ripening or labor, to treat incomplete or missed abortions, and in the prevention of NSAID-induced gastric ulcers.

GrbBiE.title: Progestin
GrbBiE.description: A synthetic form of progesterone. Commonly used for contraception as well as in the treatment of abnormal uterine bleeding and endometriosis.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

trbXQE.title: Nadir
trbXQE.description: The lowest or minimum value of the parameter being referenced. Commonly used to refer to the lowest blood cell count on CBC (e.g., platelet nadir) or the lowest fetal heart rate reading on cardiotocography (i.e., deceleration nadir)

FrbgQE.title: Early deceleration
FrbgQE.description: A decrease in the fetal heart rate by ≥15 bpm (but generally not <100 bpm) with a gradual onset (≥30 sec to nadir) in which the nadir of the deceleration occurs during uterine contraction. The most common cause of an early deceleration is head compression.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

8rbOQE.title: Late deceleration
8rbOQE.description: A deceleration (decrease in the heart rate by ≥ 15 beats/minute) in which the onset to nadir is gradual ≥ 30 seconds and the nadir occuring after the contraction curve attains its peak. Late decelerations indicate uteroplacental insufficiency and/or fetal hypoxia. Common causes include placental pathology (e.g., abruption), pre-eclampsia, and excessive uterine contractions.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

urbpQE.title: Variable deceleration
urbpQE.description: A deceleration (decrease in the heart rate by ≥ 15 beats/minute lasting ≥ 15 seconds) that has an abrupt onset (with the nadir reached within 30 seconds) and abrupt recovery. Variable decelerations, which are the most common type of deceleration, may or may not be temporally related to uterine contractions. A few variable decelerations that disappear with changes in maternal position typically do not need any intervention but recurrent variable decelerations might indicate cord compression.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

Drb1jE.title: Intrauterine resuscitation
Drb1jE.description: Various interventions with the specific aim of increasing delivery of oxygen to the placenta and fetus. Examples include left lateral recumbent positioning of mother, maternal IV fluids, maternal oxygen, and/or intra-amniotic infusion.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Intrauterine resuscitation

wrbhjE.title: Ribonucleotide reductase
wrbhjE.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the reduction of ribonucleotides (ADP, GDP, UDP, CDP) to deoxyribonucleotides, which are precursors for DNA synthesis.

destinations.label: Purines and pyrimidines → Synthesis of deoxyribonucleotides

media.title: Redox chain for ribonucleotide reductase regeneration

CrbqjE.title: Adenine phosphoribosyltransferase
CrbqjE.description: An enzyme involved in the purine salvage pathway that converts adenine and PRPP to AMP. Deficiency causes excess adenine to be converted to 2,8-dihydroxyadenine (DHA), which is deposited as calculi in the kidneys.

xrbEjE.title: Xanthine oxidase
xrbEjE.description: An enzyme that plays a central role in the purine catabolism. It catalyzes the oxidation of hypoxanthine to xanthine and the oxidation of xanthine to uric acid.

BrbzjE.title: Gender dysphoria
BrbzjE.description: A state of emotional distress attributed to incongruence between a person's gender identity and assigned gender. Results in significant impairment in key areas of functioning (e.g., school, social life).

ArbRPE.title: Paraphilic disorders
ArbRPE.description: A group of disorders characterized by abnormally intense and persistent (> 6 months) sexual interests, which can manifest as urges, fantasies, and/or behaviors. Associated with significant distress and/or functional impairment of the affected individual or with (potential) harm to others (e.g., children, nonconsenting adults). Examples include exhibitionistic disorder, pedophilic disorder, and fetishistic disorder.

destinations.label: Sexual dysfunction and paraphilic disorders → Paraphilic disorders

_rb5PE.title: Latent phase of labor
_rb5PE.description: The initial phase of the first stage of labor, which is characterized by slow cervical dilation, usually between 0 and 6 cm. The active phase of more rapid dilation usually begins at 6 cm.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Normal spontaneous labor

Z7bZ4E.title: First stage of labor
Z7bZ4E.description: The period of time between the onset of true labor pains and complete dilation of the cervix (≥ 10 cm). Normal duration of the first stage of labor is < 20 hours in a primiparous woman and < 14 hours in a multiparous woman. The major events that occur during the first stage of labor are effacement and dilation of the cervix as well as formation of the lower uterine segment. The first stage of labor can be subdivided into a latent phase and active phase.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormal stages of labor
Normal labor and delivery → Normal spontaneous labor

07be4E.title: Endometrial stripe
07be4E.description: An ultrasonographic finding characterized by an echogenic layer in the long axis view of the uterus. Used to evaluate thickness of the endometrium.

a7bQ4E.title: Spontaneous abortion
a7bQ4E.description: The spontaneous loss of pregnancy before 20 weeks' gestation.

Y7bn4E.title: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea
Y7bn4E.description: Anovulation caused by dysfunctional hypothalamic GnRH secretion resulting from decreased energy availability (e.g., due to reduced calorie intake, excessive exercise) and/or stress. Commonly manifests with menstrual irregularities (e.g., amenorrhea) and infertility.

b7bH4E.title: Loop electrosurgical excision procedure
b7bH4E.description: A procedure used to diagnose and treat cervical cancer by using a thin electric wire loop to remove abnormal cervical tissue. Can be performed under local anesthesia as an office procedure. Used in the management of high-grade cervical abnormalities detected on screening and in early-stage cervical cancer.

destinations.label: Invasive cervical cancer → Surgical interventions for cervical cancer

c7bakE.title: Androgen
c7bakE.description: A steroid sex hormone that has an anabolic effect on muscles and bones in both sexes and stimulates sexual differentiation and spermatogenesis in male individuals. Includes dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, and dihydrotestosterone. Serves as a precursor to estrogen.

V7bGkE.title: Follicular hyperkeratosis
V7bGkE.description: A skin condition characterized by the blockage of hair follicles with plugs of keratin, resulting in rough, cone-shaped, elevated papules. The openings are often closed with a white plug of encrusted sebum. Seen in deficiencies of vitamins E, A, C, and B complex.

U7bbOE.title: Lutein
U7bbOE.description: A naturally occurring carotenoid and xanthophyll of plant origin. Found in high quantities in green leafy vegetables (spinach, kale) and yellow carrots. Acts as a photoprotectant for the retina from free radical-mediated damage, and as a dietary supplement. Used in conditions such as age-related macular degeneration and cataracts.

T7b6OE.title: Alkalosis
T7b6OE.description: A process that tends to make blood alkaline. Based on the underlying mechanism, alkaloses can be classified as respiratory alkaloses (conditions associated with hyperventilation) or metabolic alkaloses (e.g., renal or gastrointestinal loss of hydrogen ions).

g7bFOE.title: Acidosis
g7bFOE.description: A process that tends to make blood acidic. Based on the underlying mechanism, acidoses can be classified as respiratory acidoses (i.e., conditions associated with alveolar hypoventilation) or metabolic acidoses (e.g., due to gastrointestinal loss of bicarbonate, increased retention of H⁺ ions by the kidney, or increased concentration of organic acids).

S7byOE.title: Aplasia cutis congenita
S7byOE.description: A birth defect in which the fetus is missing a portion of skin. It is associated with trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome) and maternal use of methimazole, carbimazole, valproate, or certain ACE inhibitors. It most commonly occurs as a solitary skin defect on the scalp.

h7bclE.title: Benzoyl peroxide
h7bclE.description: A topical acne medication with comedolytic and bactericidal (Propionibacterium acnes) effects secondary to a release of oxygen free radicals. Adverse effects include skin irritation, erythema, increased photosensitivity.

37bSlE.title: Cutibacterium acnes
37bSlE.description: A gram-positive, anaerobic bacterium that is part of the normal skin flora. Found in hair follicles and is associated with acne formation. The bacteria can break down sebum. Excessive proliferation results in the release of pro-inflammatory fatty acids and pustule formation.

R7bllE.title: Antepartum hemorrhage
R7bllE.description: The occurrence of vaginal bleeding after the 20th week of gestation. Most commonly seen during the third trimester and is associated with significant fetal as well as maternal morbidity and mortality. Common causes are bloody show associated with labor, miscarriage, placental previa, and placental abruption.

media.title: Types of hemorrhage in placental abruption

i7bJlE.title: Simple mastectomy
i7bJlE.description: The surgical removal of the entire breast tissue and nipple-areolar complex with sparing of the pectoral muscles. Unlike a modified radical mastectomy, sentinel axillary lymph node biopsy is performed instead of level I & II node dissection.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Surgical resection of tumor and breast reconstruction

Q7bulE.title: Modified radical mastectomy
Q7bulE.description: The surgical removal of breast tissue, underlying pectoralis fascia, and axillary lymph nodes. Unlike a radical mastectomy, the pectoralis muscle is spared. Modified radical mastectomy is preferred over radical mastectomy due to equivalent survival outcomes but decreased morbidity.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Surgical resection of tumor and breast reconstruction

j7b_lE.title: Prozone effect
j7b_lE.description: A type of interference that occurs with competitive immunoassays as a result of a high concentration of the analyte (either antigen or antibody). The prozone effect results in a false negative result.

P7bWNE.title: Gestational breast cancer
P7bWNE.description: A breast cancer that develops during pregnancy, within 1 year of delivery, or during lactation.

k7bmNE.title: Nonstress test
k7bmNE.description: A form of antepartum fetal surveillance in which cardiotocography is performed for a period of 20–40 minutes along with a recording of fetal movements. Indicated in high-risk pregnancies involving maternal medical conditions (e.g., gestational diabetes, preeclampsia) or fetal conditions (e.g., fetal heart defects, fetal growth restriction). An NST tests the reactivity of fetal heart rate to fetal movements, unlike a contraction stress test, which tests fetal heart reactivity to hypoxia induced by uterine contractions.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Antepartum fetal surveillance testing

O7bINE.title: Contraction stress test
O7bINE.description: A test to assess the response of the fetal heart rate to contractions indicated in high-risk pregnancies. Stimulation occurs via nipple self-stimulation or oxytocin infusion (then called "oxytocin challenge test"). Uterine contractions should occur in a rate of three contractions within 10 minutes. Testing is considered positive if >50% of contractions are followed by late decelerations in FHR. Positive testing may indicate adverse outcomes of the fetus.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Antepartum fetal surveillance testing

l7bvNE.title: Heterophoria
l7bvNE.description: Latent ocular misalignment (strabismus) that only becomes apparent when binocular gaze is interrupted. Can be detected using the cover-uncover test.

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Basic terms

m7bVmE.title: Fordyce spots
m7bVmE.description: Enlarged sebaceous glands in the mucosa of the mouth or genitalia that appear as small yellow-white spots. Fordyce spots are asymptomatic and are seen in most individuals.

57bimE.title: Urethral caruncle
57bimE.description: A small, benign, pedunculated, vascular mass that arises from the posterior wall of the distal urethra and protrudes out of the urethral meatus. It is seen in postmenopausal women and results in dysuria, dyspareunia, irregular vaginal bleeding, and, occasionally, urinary retention. The pathogenesis of urethral caruncles is not understood.

M7bMmE.title: Paraurethral glands
M7bMmE.description: A pair of tubular paraurethral glands that open onto the posterior wall of the distal female urethra. Analogous to the openings of the prostatic glands into the prostatic sinus. Function is not well-established. Can become infected (i.e., paraurethral gland abscess)

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Vagina and vulva

n7b7mE.title: Greater vestibular glands
n7b7mE.description: A pair of glands located in the superficial perineal pouch and extend via 2-cm long ducts into the vestibule of the female genitalia. Bartholin glands, which develop as outgrowths from the caudal part of the urogenital sinus, are analogous to the bulbourethral glands in males.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Vagina and vulva

L7bwmE.title: External cephalic version
L7bwmE.description: A procedure in which the fetus is rotated from a breech presentation, or oblique/transverse lie to the cephalic presentation by external manipulation. Typically performed as an elective procedure in women who are not in active labor and are at or near term (usually at 37 weeks of gestation) to increase the likelihood of a vaginal cephalic delivery.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Mechanical obstruction of labor

67bj5E.title: Assisted vaginal breech delivery
67bj5E.description: The infant spontaneously delivers up to the umbilicus and then the remainder of the body is extracted manually.

p7bL5E.title: Obstructed labor
p7bL5E.description: The arrest of fetal progression through the pelvis as a result of a mechanical obstruction (e.g., cephalopelvic disproportion). Cesarean delivery or assisted vaginal delivery may be required.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Mechanical obstruction of labor

J7bs5E.title: Cell-free fetal DNA testing
J7bs5E.description: The evaluation of cell-free fetal DNA in the maternal circulation, which can be used to assess for various fetal characteristics (e.g., sex, paternity) and conditions (e.g., aneuploidy, hemolytic disease of the fetus).

q7bC5E.title: Nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers
q7bC5E.description: A class of calcium channel blockers that do not contain the dihydropyridine molecule. They include phenylalkylamines (e.g., verapamil), which are purely cardioselective, and benzothiazepines (e.g., diltiazem), which act on both heart and vascular smooth muscle.

r7bfME.title: Engagement (Obstetrics)
r7bfME.description: The entry of the widest transverse diameter of the presenting part (e.g., biparietal diameter in the case of cephalic presentation) through the plane of the pelvic inlet. Engagement usually occurs before the onset of labor in the case of a primigravida, and during the first stage of labor in the case of multiparous women. In the case of cephalic presentation, the station of an engaged skull is typically "0".

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Orientation in utero

77b4ME.title: Station (Obstetrics)
77b4ME.description: The distance between the fetal presenting part and the maternal ischial spines measured in centimeters. A negative (-) station indicates that the presenting part is above the ischial spines. A positive (+) station indicates that the fetal part has passed below the ischial spines.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Orientation in utero

G7bBME.title: Cephalic presentation
G7bBME.description: A fetal presentation in which the head lies closest to the cervix. Associated with an increased chance of successful vaginal delivery.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Orientation in utero

t7bXnE.title: Compound presentation
t7bXnE.description: A type of malpresentation in which the fetus presents with an extremity in addition to the part of the body in the pelvic inlet (e.g., hand presenting with the head).

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Orientation in utero

F7bgnE.title: Oblique lie
F7bgnE.description: A type of malpresentation in which the fetal long axis is diagonal to the uterine long axis.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Orientation in utero

u7bpnE.title: Shoulder presentation
u7bpnE.description: A type of malpresentation in which the fetus presents with a shoulder. Commonly associated with transverse and oblique lies.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Orientation in utero

E7b8nE.title: Vertex presentation
E7b8nE.description: The most common fetal presentation. A type of cephalic presentation in which the fetal head is maximally flexed such that the chin is in contact with the chest. The occiput is the presenting part (denominator) in vertex presentation.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Orientation in utero

v7bAnE.title: Head molding
v7bAnE.description: A transient deformation of the head into an elongated shape due to external compression of the fetal head as it passes through the birth canal during labor; typically resolves within a few days after the birth.

destinations.label: Birth traumas → Neonatal soft tissue injuries

D7b1LE.title: Simethicone
D7b1LE.description: Oral anti-foaming agent that decreases the surface tension of gas bubbles and thereby dissolves and prevents gas pockets and allows easier passage of gas in the GI system. Used in abdominal discomfort and pain due to excess gas and in cases of detergent intoxication.

w7bhLE.title: Preeclampsia without severe features
w7bhLE.description: Preeclampsia (gestational hypertension with proteinuria, renal insufficiency, elevated liver enzymes, headache, and/or visual symptoms) without any of the following severe features: systolic blood pressure > 160 mm Hg or diastolic > 110 mm Hg, platelet count < 100,000, markedly elevated liver enzymes or RUQ pain, worsening renal insufficiency, pulmonary edema, severe persistent headache, or persistent/worsening visual symptoms.

C7bqLE.title: Fertility awareness-based methods
C7bqLE.description: A range of family planning methods that estimate the peak fertility period in female individuals. During this fertile window, unprotected sex may be avoided if the method is being used for contraception or increased if conception is desired. Includes the calendar method (rhythm method), cervical mucus method, basal body temperature method, and symptothermal method.

x7bELE.title: Vaginal douche
x7bELE.description: A practice that involves flushing a water solution into the vagina for hygienic and/or contraceptive purposes despite lack of evidence for its effectiveness. Carries potential risk of increasing the rate of unintentional pregnancy by pushing semen into the cervical canal.

B7bzLE.title: Lactational amenorrhea
B7bzLE.description: A physiologic type of amenorrhea that occurs during the postpartum period due to a delay in the resumption of ovulation. Typically occurs among women who breastfeed exclusively within the first 6 months postpartum and lasts for ~ 10 months. Mediated by the suckling stimulus, which stimulates prolactin release, inhibits gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) release, and inhibits the preovulatory lutenizing hormone (LH) surge. Can be used as a nonhormonal method of contraception; failure rate is ~ 2%.

media.title: Stimulation of milk production and ejection

y7bdoE.title: Symptothermal method
y7bdoE.description: A fertility awareness-based contraceptive method in which the fertility period is estimated by evaluating the abundance and consistency of cervical mucus and measurement of the body temperature throughout the menstrual cycle.

A7bRoE.title: Condom
A7bRoE.description: A barrier device used to protect against undesired pregnancy and STIs, including HIV. Condoms are available for internal or external use. They can be made of a variety of materials, but latex is the most reliable.

_7b5oE.title: Contraceptive diaphragm
_7b5oE.description: A dome-shaped barrier device comprised of latex, silicone, or plastic that is placed into the vagina prior to sexual intercourse to block the cervix. The contraceptive diaphragm rests in the anterior and posterior fornix of the vagina.

z7broE.title: Cervical cap
z7broE.description: A barrier method of contraception in which a dome-shaped latex or plastic barrier device covers and blocks the cervix during intercourse. It is used with spermicide.

-7bDoE.title: Spermicide
-7bDoE.description: A nonhormonal contraceptive that inhibits sperm motility. It is inserted into the vagina before intercourse. Has low efficacy compared to other contraceptives.

0HbeKE.title: Oil cyst
0HbeKE.description: An imaging finding in which fat necrosis forms a pool of oil that is surrounded by fibrous tissue. Usually referred to in the context of breast imaging. Most commonly occurs after surgery or trauma, but may also form spontaneously.

destinations.label: Fat necrosis of the breast → Diagnosis

aHbQKE.title: Male pseudohermaphroditism
aHbQKE.description: A condition in which a genotypically male individual has female external genitalia. The underlying mechanism is hypoandrogenism during embryogenesis. Possible causes include androgen insensitivity syndrome, 5-α reductase deficiency, and Swyer syndrome.

YHbnKE.title: Mean sac diameter
YHbnKE.description: The average diameter of the gestational sac (length + width + height/3) as measured by ultrasonography during the first trimester. A rough estimate of the gestational age can be calculated from the mean sac diameter by the formula: GA (in days) = MSD + 30.

bHbHKE.title: Fetal femoral length
bHbHKE.description: The length of the fetal femur as measured on ultrasonography between 14 and 20 weeks of gestation. Accurate measurement of fetal femoral length requires that the beam of the transducer is parallel to the femoral shaft. Femoral length can be used to determine the gestational age during the early second trimester. A shortened femoral length may also be seen with genetic abnormalities such as Down syndrome

XHb9KE.title: Expected date of delivery
XHb9KE.description: The day on which the patient is expected to go into labor. Assuming that all cycles last 28 days, ovulation occurs during the midcycle, and the length of gestation is 280 days (10 lunar months), the EDD is calculated by Naegele's formula as 280 days after the first day of the last menstrual period (or  [LMP + 7 days] - 3 months). But this estimate can be erroneous and a first trimester ultrasound scan is used to provide a more reliable estimate based on crown-rump length.

cHba6E.title: Endometrial hyperplasia
cHba6E.description: Abnormal thickening of the uterine lining caused by the proliferation of endometrial glands due to increased estrogen exposure (e.g., polycystic ovarian syndrome, obesity, tamoxifen use). Manifests with abnormal uterine bleeding. Diagnosis is confirmed with endometrial biopsy showing endometrial hyperplasia without atypia (benign endometrial hyperplasia) or with atypia (endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia); the latter has a high risk of progressing to endometrial cancer.

destinations.label: Benign and premalignant lesions of the endometrium → Endometrial hyperplasia

WHbP6E.title: Pityrosporum folliculitis
WHbP6E.description: An infection of hair follicles by the fungus Malassezia furfur. Typically manifests with pruritic, papulopustular eruptions distributed primarily on the upper trunk. Most commonly affects young to middle-aged adults.

VHbG6E.title: Herpetic folliculitis
VHbG6E.description: A localized inflammation of the hair follicle or sebaceous glands primarily caused by herpes simplex (HSV-1 and -2) and varicella zoster viruses (VZV). Manifests in erythematous papules, pustules, papulovesicles, and plaques, which usually appear grouped or clustered.

UHbbpE.title: Urine anion gap
UHbbpE.description: The difference between the concentration of measured anions and the concentration of measured cations in the urine. Calculated as [Urine Na] + [Urine K+] - [Urine Cl-]. Normal range is -20 to -50 mEq/L. Positive urine anion gap is associated with decreased renal acid excretion (e.g., type 1 and type 4 renal tubular acidoses); negative urine anion gap is associated with loss of bicarbonate (e.g., diarrhea).

2HbTpE.title: Acquired torticollis
2HbTpE.description: A postural deformity of the neck (i.e., heat tilt and/or neck rotation) that develops after birth and has an identifiable cause. Muscular causes include cervical muscle spasms (e.g., due to neck sprain or drug-induced dystonic reactions); nonmuscular causes include skeletal involvement (e.g., atlantoaxial subluxation), infection, CNS involvement, ocular torticollis, GERD, and benign paroxysmal torticollis of infancy.

fHbkpE.title: Atopic triad
fHbkpE.description: A triad of asthma, allergic rhinitis (hay fever), and atopic dermatitis (eczema) that is linked by allergen-triggered IgE-mast cell activation.

THb6pE.title: Endometrial biopsy
THb6pE.description: An outpatient diagnostic procedure in which a long, narrow plastic cannula is inserted into the cervical os to aspirate a sample of the endometrium. Endometrial sampling is used in the work-up of patients with infertility or abnormal uterine bleeding and to screen periodically for endometrial carcinoma among patients on estrogen replacement therapy.

gHbFpE.title: Fecundity
gHbFpE.description: The ability to conceive and produce offspring. Decreased physiologically with age.

SHbypE.title: Aromatase inhibitors
SHbypE.description: Antiestrogen drugs (e.g., anastrozole, letrozole, exemestane) that inhibit the conversion of androstenedione to estrone and testosterone to estradiol. First-line treatment for estrogen-promoted (hormone receptor-positive) breast cancer in postmenopausal women. Adverse effects include arthralgia, myalgia, osteoporosis, hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

hHbcJE.title: Masturbation
hHbcJE.description: Stimulation of one's own genitals for sexual pleasure. Can involve the use of hands and fingers as well as sex toys or everyday objects. Physiological behavior that often starts in childhood and is exhibited by both sexes and all age groups.

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual activities

3HbSJE.title: Kleihauer-Betke test
3HbSJE.description: A quantitative test to evaluate fetal-maternal hemorrhage. A maternal blood smear is exposed to acid, then stained. Adult hemoglobin is removed by the acid, whereas fetal hemoglobin (HbF) is not. Pink cells indicate HbF on a positive test.

destinations.label: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn → Prevention

RHblJE.title: Serial ultrasounds
RHblJE.description: Obstetric ultrasounds done every 3–4 weeks to assess fetal anatomy and growth. They are not routinely performed but are indicated if infections are acquired during pregnancy that can adversely affect the fetus (e.g., parvovirus B19, Zika virus).

iHbJJE.title: Hematocolpos
iHbJJE.description: A condition in which the vagina fills with menstrual blood, usually due to an imperforate hymen that prevents the release of menstrual blood. Typically manifests with a bluish mass pushing the labia open on pelvic examination.

destinations.label: Anomalies of the female genital tract → Anomalies of the vulva and vagina

jHb_JE.title: Sonohysterosalpingography
jHb_JE.description: A procedure in which saline is instilled into the uterine cavity via the cervical canal and ultrasonography is performed to evaluate the uterine cavity and morphology/patency of the fallopian tubes.

PHbWqE.title: Post-ejaculatory urinalysis
PHbWqE.description: Centrifugation of a urine sample that is obtained following ejaculation and microscopic examination of the separated sediment for sperm cells. Post-ejaculatory urinalysis is performed to rule out retrograde ejaculation.

4Hb3qE.title: Male condom
4Hb3qE.description: A barrier method of contraception in which a thin sheath of material (e.g., latex) covers the penis during sexual intercourse. It also protects against STIs, including HIV.

kHbmqE.title: Female condom
kHbmqE.description: A barrier method of contraception in which a thin sheath of material (e.g., latex) is worn inside the vagina during intercourse. It also protects against STIs, including HIV.

OHbIqE.title: Contraceptive sponge
OHbIqE.description: A barrier method of contraception in which a foam disk containing spermicide is placed in the vagina against the cervix during intercourse.

NHb-qE.title: Stepping reflex
NHb-qE.description: A primitive reflex elicited by holding an infant upright and setting the feet onto a surface. In response, the infant places one foot in front of the other (stepping motion) with alternating flexion and extension of the legs. Typically persists until 2 months of age.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

mHbVIE.title: Asymmetrical tonic neck reflex
mHbVIE.description: A primitive reflex elicited by turning an infant's head to one side. In response, the infant extends the ipsilateral arm and leg while flexing the contralateral arm and leg. Aids in development of hand-eye coordination. Typically persists until 3-4 months of age. A persistent reflex has an association with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

5HbiIE.title: Plantar grasp
5HbiIE.description: A primitive reflex elicited by stroking an infant's foot from the toe to the heel. In response, the infant plantar flexes (curl in) the toes. Typically persists until ~ 3 months of age. The absence of a plantar reflex at birth can be a symptom of cerebral palsy.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

MHbMIE.title: Palmar grasp
MHbMIE.description: A primitive reflex elicited by stroking an infant's palm horizontally. In response, the infant flexes the fingers (closes the palm). Typically persists until 3-6 months of age. The absence of a palmar reflex at birth can be a symptom of cerebral palsy.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

nHb7IE.title: Rooting reflex
nHb7IE.description: A primitive reflex elicited by stroking an infant's cheek. In response, the infant will turn the head to the ipsilateral side and open the mouth. Typically persists until 4 months of age. Persistence or reappearance of this sign indicates central neurodegenerative or vascular disease, often affecting the frontal lobes (frontal release sign).

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

LHbwIE.title: Sucking reflex
LHbwIE.description: A primitive reflex elicited by touching the roof of an infant's mouth with a finger. In response, the baby sucks the finger. Typically persists until 4 months of age.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

oHb0rE.title: Galant reflex
oHb0rE.description: A primitive reflex elicited by placing an infant in the prone position and stroking the paravertebral region on one side. In response, the infant rotates the ipsilateral hip. Typically persists until 4-6 months of age. A persistent reflex has an association with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and bed-wetting.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

KHbUrE.title: Glabellar tap sign
KHbUrE.description: A primitive reflex that is elicited by tapping on the root of the nose (i.e., the glabella). Normal response is blinking to the first several taps. An abnormal response is persistent blinking and indicates frontal release (i.e., frontal lobe dysfunction).

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

6HbjrE.title: Landau reflex
6HbjrE.description: A primitive reflex elicited by placing an infant in the prone position. In response, the baby arches the back and raises the head. Typically persists until 24 months of age. Reflex is diminished in infants with hypotonia (floppy infant syndrome).

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

pHbLrE.title: Snout reflex
pHbLrE.description: A primitive reflex elicited by lightly tapping an infant's closed lips. In response, the baby puckers the lips with each tap. Typically persists until 4 months of age. Persistence or reappearance of this sign indicates central neurodegenerative or vascular disease, often affecting the frontal lobes (frontal release sign).

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

JHbsrE.title: Cervical leukoplakia
JHbsrE.description: A condition of atypical cells that form a white membrane on the cervix. This finding merits further evaluation via biopsy, which typically shows hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, or the presence of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia.

qHbCrE.title: Peripheral blood smear
qHbCrE.description: A diagnostic test in which peripheral blood is examined under the microscope. Can be used to diagnose conditions that cause abnormal counts or morphology of red blood cells, white blood cells, and/or platelets.

media.title: Peripheral blood smear of a healthy individual

IHbY7E.title: Glisson capsule
IHbY7E.description: A fibrous inner layer of the heptic capsule that covers the entire liver (including the bare area).

rHbf7E.title: Sex therapy
rHbf7E.description: A type of therapy for individuals or couples that addresses psychological and physical barriers to a healthy sexual relationship. Involves exercises to increase sexual sensory awareness and progressively heighten levels of sexual contact.

7Hb47E.title: Calcium gluconate
7Hb47E.description: A calcium salt used in the treatment of hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia, hypermagnesemia, beta-blocker poisoning, and calcium channel blocker poisoning.  Rapid intravenous administration may result in transient bradycardia and hypotension.

tHbXHE.title: Inhibin A
tHbXHE.description: A form of inhibin in females that is predominantly produced by the corpus luteum and placenta. Increased levels of inhibin are seen in 70% of sex cord stromal tumors of the ovary and 20% of epithelial ovarian tumors. During pregnancy, increased levels of maternal serum levels of inhibin A are typically associated with Down syndrome, molar pregnancy, and preterm delivery.

FHbgHE.title: Sacrococcygeal teratoma
FHbgHE.description: The most common germ cell tumor of infancy and early childhood. Manifests as a mass near the caudal end of the fetus near the rectum. Can cause obstruction, weakness, pain, and/or paralysis.

8HbOHE.title: Unconjugated estriol
8HbOHE.description: A weak form of estrogen. During pregnancy, estriol is the major estrogen because fetal dehydroepiandrosterone enters maternal serum and is converted by the placenta to unconjugated estriol, which is then rapidly conjugated by the liver to a water-soluble form that can be excreted in urine. Decreased levels of unconjugated estriol are associated with Down syndrome, Edward syndrome, molar pregnancy, and fetal demise.

uHbpHE.title: Unscheduled bleeding
uHbpHE.description: Endometrial bleeding that occurs on unexpected days during treatment with hormonal contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy. Most commonly occurs with oral contraceptive pills in the first 3 months of therapy or if a pill has been missed. Bleeding may be caused by too much estrogen (estrogen breakthrough), too little estrogen (estrogen withdrawal), or too much progesterone (progesterone breakthrough).

EHb8HE.title: Uterine artery ligation
EHb8HE.description: Bilateral suturing or clipping of uterine arteries during a laparotomy to stop bleeding in patients with postpartum hemorrhage or hemorrhage following gynecologic surgery to avoid hysterectomy. The procedure leaves the uterus intact and preserves fertility. Complications include pelvic infection, hematoma, and artery perforation.

vHbAHE.title: Cervicitis
vHbAHE.description: An infectious or noninfectious inflammation of the cervix. Most commonly caused by bacterial infection with Neisseria gonorrhoeae or Chlamydia trachomatis. Typically manifests with dyspareunia, postcoital and/or intermenstrual bleeding, a friable cervix, and vaginal discharge.

DHb1sE.title: Cervical motion tenderness
DHb1sE.description: A pelvic examination finding characterized by extreme pain with bimanual examination. Usually associated with pelvic inflammatory disease.

CHbqsE.title: Hyperandrogenism
CHbqsE.description: A state of excess androgen levels that causes symptoms such as growth of facial hair, deepening of the voice, and male-pattern baldness. Causes include PCOS, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, tumors (e.g., adrenocortical tumors), menopause, and certain drugs (e.g., some anticonvulsants).

xHbEsE.title: High grade squamous intraepithelial lesion
xHbEsE.description: A standardized term used to report cytological or histopathological examination findings of squamous lesions of the anogenital tract. Indicates that the lesion is most likely precancerous and associated with a persistent HPV infection. HSIL has a high likelihood of progressing to invasive cancer.

BHbzsE.title: Amnioinfusion
BHbzsE.description: The transabdominal or transcervical infusion of fluid into the amniotic cavity to restore normal amniotic fluid volume. Used in severe oligohydramnios to assist in fetal lung development and for better visualization during fetal anomaly scans. Can also be used to relieve cord compression and reduce associated complications if there are signs of distress during labor (e.g., meconium staining).

yHbdGE.title: Pseudocyesis
yHbdGE.description: A disorder in which the patient has physical signs of pregnancy (e.g., breast tenderness, weight gain, amenorrhea, morning sickness) and believes that they are pregnant, but is not in fact actually pregnant. Classified under "Other Specified Somatic Symptoms and Related Disorder" in the DSM-V.

destinations.label: Somatic symptom and related disorders → Pseudocyesis

AHbRGE.title: Delusion of pregnancy
AHbRGE.description: Fixed belief in being pregnant, despite evidence to the contrary (e.g., negative β-hCG). Patients lack physical signs suggestive of pregnancy (e.g., enlarged abdomen, morning sickness, breast tenderness) and may have a history of psychosis.

_Hb5GE.title: Malingering
_Hb5GE.description: The act by which a patient feigns symptoms or claims to have a disease to attain a secondary gain (e.g., compensation or time off from work). Symptoms are usually not specific to a certain condition.

destinations.label: Somatic symptom and related disorders → Malingering

zHbrGE.title: Couvade syndrome
zHbrGE.description: A condition in which an individual experiences pregnancy-related symptoms (e.g., nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain) despite not being pregnant. Typically manifests near the end of pregnancy (e.g., during labor and delivery).

-HbDGE.title: Prolonged deceleration
-HbDGE.description: A decrease in fetal heart decrease by ≥ 15 beats/minute from the baseline lasting ≥ 2 minutes but < 10 minutes. If the deceleration lasts longer than 10 minutes it must be considered as a baseline change (fetal bradycardia).

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

0sbetE.title: Recurrent variable decelerations
0sbetE.description: Potentially life-threatening decelerations in fetal heart beat occurring in more than 50% of contractions in a 20-minute period. Indicates umbilical cord compression/prolapse or stalled labor.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

asbQtE.title: Umbilical cord compression
asbQtE.description: Compression of the umbilical cord between the presenting part of the fetus (usually the head) and the pelvis. Typically causes recurrent variable decelerations on CTG due to a baroreceptor-mediated reflex decrease of the FHR.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Umbilical cord complications

bsbHtE.title: Anomalies of Müllerian duct fusion
bsbHtE.description: A group of congenital anomalies caused by defective fusion of the Müllerian ducts during embryonal development. The gonads (and secondary sexual characteristics) typically develop normally, but a variety of uterine abnormalities occur (e.g., unicornuate uterus, didelphic uterus, septate uterus).

destinations.label: Anomalies of the female genital tract → Anomalies of the uterus

Xsb9tE.title: Pudendal block
Xsb9tE.description: Injection of a local anesthetic into the pudendal canal to block transmission within the pudendal nerve. This procedure, which anesthetizes the perineum, is most commonly performed prior to an episiotomy.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Clinical significance

csbaFE.title: Postterm pregnancy
csbaFE.description: A pregnancy that has reached or exceeded 42 0/7 weeks' gestation.

1sb2FE.title: Non-reactive nonstress test
1sb2FE.description: A fetal heart tracing with < 2 accelerations within 20 minutes after 40 minutes of continuous fetal heart rate (FHR) monitoring. An acceleration is defined as an abrupt increase in FHR by >15 beats/minute lasting >15 seconds if the gestational age is >32 weeks, or by >10 beats/minute lasting >10 seconds if the gestational age is < 32 weeks. A non-reactive tracing indicates fetal sleep, the presence of acidemia, or CNS depression.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Antepartum fetal surveillance testing

esbxFE.title: Reactive nonstress test
esbxFE.description: A fetal heart tracing with ≥ 2 accelerations within 20 minutes period. An acceleration is defined as an abrupt increase in fetal heart rate by more than 15 beats/minute lasting more than 15 seconds if the gestational age is > 32 weeks, or by more than 10 beats/minute lasting more than 10 seconds if the gestational age is < 32 weeks. A reactive stress test indicates an awake fetus without acidemia or CNS depression.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Antepartum fetal surveillance testing

Usbb8E.title: Prolonged acceleration
Usbb8E.description: An acceleration on fetal heart tracing that lasts longer than 2 minutes but less than 10 minutes.

2sbT8E.title: Category II fetal heart rate tracing
2sbT8E.description: A fetal heart rate pattern that is neither normal nor definitively abnormal. Has varied potential for developing fetal acidosis and hypoxia and requires close monitoring.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

fsbk8E.title: Second stage of labor
fsbk8E.description: The period of time between complete cervical dilation to delivery of the infant. Normal duration of the second stage of labor is <3 hours in a primiparous woman and <2 hours in a multiparous woman. The second stage of labor is characterized by regular uterine contractions increasing in frequency and intensity as well as the appearance of the fetus' head at the vaginal opening as contractions progress.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Normal spontaneous labor

gsbF8E.title: Intermittent variable decelerations
gsbF8E.description: Variable decelerations in fetal heart beat tracings that occur with less than 50% of contractions in a 20-minute period. This finding does not require any intervention, and is not associated with adverse perinatal outcomes.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

Ssby8E.title: Vibroacoustic stimulation
Ssby8E.description: The application of vibratory sound waves to the abdomen of a pregnant women during a nonstress test to induce accelerations in the fetal heart rate tracing.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Antepartum fetal surveillance testing

hsbcuE.title: Discriminatory zone threshold
hsbcuE.description: The β-hCG serum concentration at which a gestational sac can be detected on ultrasound. The threshold for transvaginal ultrasound ranges from 1500-3500 mIU/mL. For abdominal ultrasound, the threshold is > 6500 mIU/mL. Multiple pregnancies may have higher β-hCG levels (i.e., high β-hCG levels before IUP can be visualized). A single β-hCG level should not be used to diagnose pregnancy viability or location.

3sbSuE.title: Pelvic congestion syndrome
3sbSuE.description: A diagnosis of exclusion in women with chronic, nonmenstrual pelvic pain lasting longer than 3–6 months and no other underlying gynecological condition. The pain is caused by varicose veins in the pelvis and reproductive organs (e.g., ovaries) that most likely arise secondary to multiple pregnancies.

RsbluE.title: Acceleration (CTG)
RsbluE.description: An abrupt increase in fetal heart rate by more than 15 beats/minute lasting more than 15 seconds if the gestational age is > 32 weeks, or by more than 10 beats/minute lasting more than 10 seconds if the gestational age is < 32 weeks.  The presence of > 2 accelerations within a span of 20 minutes indicates a reactive fetal heart rate tracing. If the acceleration lasts longer than 10 minutes, it should be considered a baseline change in the heart rate.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

media.title: Illustration of baseline rate, baseline variability, acceleration, and deceleration on CTG

isbJuE.title: Deceleration (CTG)
isbJuE.description: A decrease in the fetal heart rate that is ≥ 15 beats/minute and lasts ≥ 15 seconds. Decelerations may be classified as a early, late, or variable depending on their onset in relation to uterine contractions. Early decelerations indicate fetal head compression during uterine contractions and are not a cause for concern. Recurrent variable decelerations might indicate cord compression. Late decelerations usually occur with uteroplacental insufficiency.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

QsbuuE.title: Sense strand
QsbuuE.description: The DNA strand that runs from 5' to 3', from which the complementary RNA strand is produced.

jsb_uE.title: Antisense strand
jsb_uE.description: The DNA segment in double-stranded DNA that runs from 3' to 5', is complementary to the sense strand, and is used as a template for transcription to produce the complementary mRNA strand.

PsbWEE.title: Low grade squamous intraepithelial lesion
PsbWEE.description: A standardized term used to describe cytological or histopathological examination findings of squamous lesions of the anogenital tract. Indicates that the lesion is likely self-limited and associated with a transient HPV infection.

media.title: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) of the cervix

4sb3EE.title: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance
4sb3EE.description: A term used in the Bethesda system to describe abnormal cervical cytology (Pap smear) with reactive changes that cannot be categorized as low-grade intraepithelial lesions (LSIL). ASC-US is the most common abnormal finding on a Pap test and usually indicates an HPV infection.

media.title: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US)

ksbmEE.title: Atypical glandular cells
ksbmEE.description: A term used in the Bethesda system to describe abnormal cervical cytology (Pap smear) with atypical glandular cells that originate from the glandular epithelium of the endocervix, endometrium, or rarely, from other sites (e.g., ovaries). This finding is associated with premalignant or malignant disease.

OsbIEE.title: RNA polymerase
OsbIEE.description: An enzyme that synthesizes RNA from a DNA template.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  RNA polymerases and transcription factors

lsbvEE.title: Transcription factor
lsbvEE.description: A protein that binds to DNA and regulates the rate of transcription from DNA to mRNA.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  RNA polymerases and transcription factors

Nsb-EE.title: Zinc finger
Nsb-EE.description: A family of transcription factors that contain a zinc finger binding domain and an effector domain that can bind to a certain DNA sequence to regulate gene expression.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  RNA polymerases and transcription factors

MsbMvE.title: Left ventricular ejection fraction
MsbMvE.description:
The fraction of blood that is ejected by the left ventricle into the systemic circulation with every cardiac cycle. 
LVEF = (LV stroke volume/LV end-diastolic volume) × 100. Normal LVEF is 50–70%.

nsb7vE.title: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
nsb7vE.description: An idiopathic cardiomyopathy characterized by the development of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) in the months after or before delivery.

LsbwvE.title: Homeobox
LsbwvE.description: A group of genes responsible for morphogenesis, including craniocaudal organization of the embryo, positioning of limbs, and proper development of the skin and limbs.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  RNA polymerases and transcription factors

6sbjDE.title: Polyadenylate tail
6sbjDE.description: A post-transcriptional modification added to a messenger RNA molecule to facilitate export from the nucleus and protect the transcript from degradation. Typically around 200 adenines long and is added to the end of the 3' UTR by poly-A polymerase.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

psbLDE.title: Splicing
psbLDE.description: The process by which newly synthesized mRNA molecules undergo selective removal of introns with preservation of exons, resulting in mRNA that is ready for translation.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Post-transcriptional modification (RNA processing)

JsbsDE.title: Spliceosome
JsbsDE.description: A large complex that consists of small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPS) and other proteins. Removes introns from pre-mRNA.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Post-transcriptional modification (RNA processing)

qsbCDE.title: Idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
qsbCDE.description: A genetic disorder characterized by a defect in gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) production or action. Presents with signs and symptoms of hypogonadism (e.g., delayed puberty, infertility, decreased libido). Subdivided into a normosmic form and an anosmic form (called Kallmann syndrome).

rsbfwE.title: Alternative splicing
rsbfwE.description: The combination of different exons from a single hnRNA sequence to form different mature mRNA sequences. Allows a single hnRNA sequence to encode several different proteins.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Post-transcriptional modification (RNA processing)

HsbKwE.title: Pregnancy luteoma
HsbKwE.description: A rare, benign tumor of the ovary thought to be caused by the hormonal effects of pregnancy. Usually asymptomatic; can manifest with symptoms of virilization. They typically regress spontaneously postpartum.

ssbtwE.title: lac operon
ssbtwE.description: A collection of E. coli genes that are actively transcribed when glucose is absent and lactose is available. Includes a promoter region activated by catabolite activator protein, an operator region, and several genes that encode enzymes involved in lactose metabolism.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Regulation of transcription

media.title: Animation: Prokaryotic gene regulation - Lac operon

Fsbg9E.title: Theca lutein cyst
Fsbg9E.description: A type of functional ovarian cyst that is thought to originate from excessive amounts of circulating gonadotropins such as β-hCG. Typically multiple and seen bilaterally, with a high association with gestational trophoblastic disease and multiple gestations. USG shows bilateral enlarged, multilocular, cystic masses of the ovaries. Usually resolve spontaneously once the source of beta-hCG is removed.

vsbA9E.title: Nonreassuring fetal status
vsbA9E.description: A term used to describe the characteristic changes in the fetal heart rate (FHR) in response to fetal hypoxia and metabolic acidosis (usually secondary to placental insufficiency). Detected on cardiotocography as fetal tachycardia (FHR > 160-180/min), fetal bradycardia (FHR < 110/min), loss of baseline variability, recurrent variable decelerations, and late decelerations. Requires either intrauterine resuscitation or immediate delivery (cesarean or, if imminent, vaginal delivery).

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

Dsb1CE.title: Posterior pelvic pain provocation test
Dsb1CE.description: A provocation test for sacroiliac dysfunction to distinguish between pelvic girdle and low back pain. The patient lies supine with the hip and knee flexed at 90°, and axial pressure is applied along the length of the femur to push the ilium posteriorly. The test is positive if the maneuver reproduces the patient's pain. Most commonly used in a pregnant patient.

wsbhCE.title: Active straight leg raise
wsbhCE.description: A test to assess the stability of the lower spine and pelvic girdle. The patient lies supine and is asked to raise one of his/her legs 20 cm above the table without bending the knee. Difficulty in raising the leg is considered a positive response.

9sbNCE.title: Carboprost tromethamine
9sbNCE.description: A prostaglandin PGF-2a analog that is used in refractory postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony and pregnancy termination between 13–20 weeks' gestation. Should be used with caution in those with asthma.

CsbqCE.title: Uterine inversion
CsbqCE.description: An obstetric emergency that can follow vaginal delivery, in which the uterine fundus collapses into the endometrial cavity, which turns the uterus partially or completely inside out. Risk factors include nulliparity, cord traction, fundal pressure during the third stage of labor, and a retained placenta. Manifests with severe postpartum hemorrhage and a round, protruding mass from the cervix or vagina.

media.title: Manual reduction of uterine inversion (Johnson method)

xsbECE.title: Uterine tachysystole
xsbECE.description: The occurrence of either > 5 contractions within 10 minutes when averaged over a 30-minute period, contractions that occur for ≥ 2 minutes, normal duration contractions that occur within 1 minute of each other, or lack of resting tone between contractions.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Intrauterine resuscitation

BsbzCE.title: Dyschezia
BsbzCE.description: A condition of difficult or painful defecation (usually due to hard stools/constipation).

ysbdxE.title: Preterm labor
ysbdxE.description: The development of regular uterine contractions with cervical effacement, dilation, or both, before 37 weeks' gestation.

_sb5xE.title: Female sexual interest/arousal disorder
_sb5xE.description: A type of female sexual dysfunction characterized by symptoms such as reduced interest in sexual activity, sexual thoughts, initiation or participation in sexual activities, sexual excitement/pleasure in sexual encounters, sexual arousal, and genital or nongenital sexual sensations during sexual encounters.

destinations.label: Sexual dysfunction and paraphilic disorders → Sexual dysfunction

-sbDxE.title: Signaling cascade
-sbDxE.description: The interconnection of individual steps in a signaling pathway (e.g., during signal transduction).

ZGbZBE.title: Second messenger
ZGbZBE.description: A small molecule released by a cell in response to a first messenger, plays an important role in signal transduction. Examples include cAMP, cGMP, and inositol trisphosphate.

0GbeBE.title: Cell surface receptor
0GbeBE.description: Receptors that are located in the cell membrane and bind hydrophilic ligands, which cannot cross the membrane themselves. There are three types of cell surface receptors: G protein-coupled receptors, enzyme-linked receptors, and ligand-gated ion channels.

aGbQBE.title: Intracellular receptors
aGbQBE.description: A class of receptors that exist within the nucleus or cytoplasm. Examples include the nuclear receptor of steroid hormones and the IP3 receptor on the endoplasmic reticulum.

YGbnBE.title: B-Lynch uterine compression suture
YGbnBE.description: A suturing technique that mechanically compresses an atonic uterus with an open hysterotomy after cesarean section in the setting of postpartum hemorrhage.

bGbHBE.title: G protein-coupled receptor
bGbHBE.description: A class of transmembrane receptors that contain a G protein. With the extracellular binding of an agonist, the G-protein undergoes a conformational change that results in interaction with intracellular proteins, activating a signal transduction cascade (second messenger system; typically via the cAMP or phosphatidylinositol pathway), to regulate a variety of physiologic functions.

media.title: Signal transduction of G protein-coupled receptors

XGb9BE.title: G protein
XGb9BE.description: A group of cellular proteins that act as molecular switches in the presence of GTP/GDP. Play a role in signal transduction and other cellular processes such as cytoskeletal assembly, protein synthesis and cell growth.

media.title: Signal transduction of G protein-coupled receptors

cGbayE.title: KRAS gene
cGbayE.description: A proto-oncogene that encodes a GTPase (a ras protein) that regulates cellular growth. Mutation is associated with colon, lung, and pancreatic cancers.

1Gb2yE.title: Non-receptor tyrosine kinases
1Gb2yE.description: A type of membrane receptor that lacks intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity. The membrane-bound receptor activates an intracellular kinase that phosphorylates tyrosine residues. Examples of ligands that bind to these receptors include growth hormone, prolactin, erythropoietin, and interferons.

dGboyE.title: Ligand-gated ion channels
dGboyE.description: A group of cell-surface ion channels that increase ion flux in response to ligand or drug binding.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

VGbGyE.title: cAMP
VGbGyE.description: A second messenger synthesized from adenosine triphosphate (ATP) by adenylate cyclase. Has a wide variety of physiologic functions, including facilitating cellular responses to glucagon, insulin, and autonomic signaling. Pathologic overactivation (e.g., by bacterial toxins) causes several effects, including impaired electrolyte secretion and resorption.

eGbxyE.title: Cyclic guanosine monophosphate
eGbxyE.description: A nucleotide derived from guanosine triphosphate. Acts as a second messenger molecule and activates dependent protein kinases, as well as dependent ion channels in the photoreceptor cells of the retina. Has diverse downstream effects, e.g., vasodilation, long-term potentiation of neurons.

UGbbAE.title: Nitric oxide
UGbbAE.description:
A compound that activates guanylyl cyclase, thereby increasing cGMP synthesis, which causes smooth muscle relaxation and subsequent vasodilation via 3 effects:
- decreases intracellular Ca2+
- activates cGMP-dependent protein kinase → activates myosin light chain phosphatase → dephosphorylates myosin light chain
- activates K+ channels → cell hyperpolarization
Produced physiologically and also released by nitrate medications (e.g., sodium nitroprusside, nitroglycerin, isosorbide mononitrate, and isosorbide dinitrate).

2GbTAE.title: Guanylate cyclase
2GbTAE.description: An enzyme that synthesizes cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) from guanosine triphosphate (GTP). Overactivated by heat-stable toxin from enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC).

fGbkAE.title: Inositol trisphosphate
fGbkAE.description: A molecule involved in the Gq protein messenger system. Formed from the breakdown of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) by phospholipase C. Diffuses to the endoplasmatic reticulum and binds to ligand-gated ion channels, which leads to the release of calcium from the endoplasmatic reticulum into the cytosol.

TGb6AE.title: Diacylglyceride
TGb6AE.description: A molecule involved in Gq protein messenger system. Formed from the breakdown of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) by phospholipase C. Activates protein kinase C.

hGbc_E.title: Immune complex
hGbc_E.description: A large molecule formed by an antibody bound to an antigen. In normal immune physiology, immune complexes lead to complement deposition, opsonization, and/or phagocytosis. In cases of diseases caused by immune complexes (e.g., lupus or rheumatoid arthritis), these large molecules deposit in tissues (type III hypersensitivity reaction).

destinations.label: Hypersensitivity reactions → Type III hypersensitivity reaction

3GbS_E.title: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection
3GbS_E.description: A form of assisted reproductive technology in which a single sperm is injected into an oocyte during in vitro fertilization.

RGbl_E.title: Syrup of ipecac
RGbl_E.description: A drug formerly used as an expectorant or an emetic. Previously used to induce vomiting after accidental ingestions, but its use is no longer recommended, as studies have failed to prove its efficacy.

iGbJ_E.title: Trophoblast
iGbJ_E.description: Cells that form the outer layer of a blastocyst, which eventually become the placenta.

QGbu_E.title: Cefpodoxime
QGbu_E.description: A third-generation cephalosporin with high activity against gram-negative and less activity against gram-positive organisms. Typically used in the treatment of uncomplicated cystitis, upper respiratory tract infections, acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, and skin infections.

jGb__E.title: Obstetric forceps delivery
jGb__E.description: An assisted vaginal delivery in which forceps are used to extract the fetus (in vertex position, with head engaged) through the vagina by exerting gentle rotation and/or traction to the fetal head. Performed to expedite vaginal delivery in prolonged second stage of labor or signs of fetal distress in the 2nd stage of labor, as long as vaginal delivery is safe and feasible.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Assisted vaginal delivery

PGbWzE.title: Vacuum extractor delivery
PGbWzE.description: An assisted vaginal delivery in which a vacuum extractor (e.g., a metal or plastic cup) is attached to the fetal head with a suction device, which enables traction of the fetal head. Indicated in prolonged second stage of labor, fetal distress, and in cases where maternal pushing efforts are contraindicated (e.g., maternal fatigue or cardiopulmonary conditions). Complications include intracranial hemorrhage and cephalohematoma.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Assisted vaginal delivery

lGbvzE.title: Protein kinase A
