lGbvzE.description: A cAMP-dependent serine/threonine-specific protein kinase that regulates the activity of various enzymes (including glycogen phosphorylase kinase) via phosphorylation.

NGb-zE.title: Hyaline cartilage
NGb-zE.description: A type of cartilage that is especially resilient to compression and composed of groups of oval/round shaped chondrocytes with numerous glycogen deposits. Its extracellular matrix contains mainly collagen II fibrils and proteoglycans. Can be found in the cartilaginous rings of the trachea, the nasal septum, and in articular cartilage.

destinations.label: Cartilage → Overview and structure of cartilage types

mGbV-E.title: Articular cartilage
mGbV-E.description: A specialized type of hyaline cartilage that covers articular surfaces in synovial joints to reduce the contact area and, therefore, stress zones of bones. Does not possess perichondrium and is nourished from surrounding vessels and synovial fluid. Contains a network of collagen II fibrils.

destinations.label: Cartilage → Overview and structure of cartilage types

5Gbi-E.title: Fibrocartilage
5Gbi-E.description: A type of cartilage that is composed of both fibrous tissue and cartilaginous tissue. Unlike other types of cartilage, which only have type 2 collagen, fibrocartilage has both type 1 and type 2 collagen. Found in entheses, menisci, the pubic symphysis, the annulus fibrosus of intervertebral discs, the triangular fibrocartilaginous complex, and the temporomandibular joint.

destinations.label: Cartilage → Overview and structure of cartilage types

nGb7-E.title: Hypotension
nGb7-E.description: A systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg and/or diastolic blood pressure < 60 mm Hg. Can be asymptomatic or symptomatic (fainting, fatigue, dizziness, cool, clammy extremities). When accompanied with tachycardia, hypotension is a sign of shock and should be treated as an emergency.

LGbw-E.title: Internal cephalic version
LGbw-E.description: A procedure in which the fetus is rotated from a breech presentation or oblique/transverse lie to the cephalic presentation by internal manipulation. This technique is mainly used for delivery of a second twin who is breech, following a normal vaginal delivery of the first twin.

oGb0Zv.title: Hydrosalpinx
oGb0Zv.description: An accumulation of serous fluid in the fallopian tubes that results from distal blockage of the tubes. Most commonly occurs as a late-stage complication of pelvic inflammatory disease, following the development of salpingitis and pyosalpinx. May also occur in endometriosis and tubal pregnancy.

6GbjZv.title: Diminished ovarian reserve
6GbjZv.description: A decline in the number of functioning oocytes (either as a normal consequence of age or due to an underlying disorder such as endometriosis) that manifests as a reduced response to ovarian stimulation in individuals who can become pregnant and who have regular menstruation.

IGbY0v.title: Heliox
IGbY0v.description: An inhaled gas mixture composed of helium and oxygen. Since helium has a lower density than oxygen, it increases laminar flow and reduces turbulent flow. It can be used for the treatment of large airway obstructions (e.g., vocal cord dysfunction, foreign bodies) and medium/small airway obstructions (e.g., asthma/COPD exacerbations).

rGbf0v.title: Rosette test
rGbf0v.description: A qualitative test that assesses for fetal-maternal hemorrhage. Maternal Rh-negative blood is incubated with Rho(D) immunoglobulin, which binds to fetal Rh-positive erythrocytes. The addition of an indicator causes these erythrocytes to form a rosette pattern if present, which are visualized by light microscopy.

destinations.label: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn → Prevention

7Gb40v.title: Chorioretinitis
7Gb40v.description: A type of posterior uveitis characterized by inflammation of the choroid (vascular layer of the eye) and retina. Can be a symptom of congenital toxoplasmosis, syphilis, and cytomegalovirus infections. Presents with redness of the eye, light sensitivity, blurred vision, impaired night vision, and tearing; typically painless.

HGbK0v.title: Simplified Bishop score
HGbK0v.description: A scoring system used to evaluate the potential for successful elective labor induction. Components include cervical dilation (the extent of opening of the cervical os), cervical effacement (the degree of thinning of the cervix), and fetal station (position of the fetal head in relation to the ischial spines). In comparison to the original Bishop score system, the simplified Bishop score omits cervical position and cervical consistency.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Induction of labor

tGbXav.title: Nonhormonal contraception
tGbXav.description: A contraceptive option that does not contain hormones. Often used in individuals with contraindications to hormonal contraception. Options include the copper IUD, surgical sterilization, behavioral methods of contraception, and barrier methods of contraception

8GbOav.title: Vulvodynia
8GbOav.description: Vulvar pain lasting ≥ 3 months without a clearly identifiable underlying cause. May be associated with hormonal, genetic, inflammatory, psychogenic, and/or neurological factors.

destinations.label: Dyspareunia in women → Causes of superficial dyspareunia

uGbpav.title: Calendar method
uGbpav.description: A fertility awareness-based contraception method in which the fertility period is estimated by documenting menses and calculating the timing of ovulation.

EGb8av.title: Fetal-maternal hemorrhage
EGb8av.description: A bleed that introduces fetal erythrocytes into the maternal circulation, which can lead to alloimmunization. Large volume bleeds can result in hemodynamic instability.

destinations.label: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn → Pathophysiology

vGbAav.title: Ectopic ureter
vGbAav.description: A congenital anomaly in which the ureter terminates at an abnormal site (most commonly the urethra or vagina).

destinations.label: Congenital anomalies of the kidneys → Overview

DGb1Yv.title: Ureterocele
DGb1Yv.description: A congenital anomaly characterized by abnormal dilation of the terminal portion of the ureter. Can occur in the bladder or urethra.

destinations.label: Congenital anomalies of the kidneys → Overview

wGbhYv.title: Meyer-Weigert law
wGbhYv.description: The concept that in cases of double ureter (a congenital anomaly), the ureter from the upper pole of the kidney inserts medial and inferior to the insertion of the ureter from the inferior pole of the kidney.

9GbNYv.title: Fibroblast
9GbNYv.description: A type of cell present in connective tissue that produces collagen and other components of the extracellular matrix. Fibroblasts play an important role in the wound healing process.

destinations.label: Connective tissue → Cells of the connective tissue

CGbqYv.title: Asymptomatic bacteriuria
CGbqYv.description: The presence of ≥ 100,000 colony-forming units of bacteria per mL of urine in a voided urine sample in patients with no signs or symptoms of urinary tract infection (e.g., dysuria, frequency, urgency, or suprapubic pain). Treatment is generally not required, except in pregnant individuals because of the risk of pyelonephritis.

BGbzYv.title: Myofibroblast
BGbzYv.description: A cell that differentiates from fibroblasts in response to tissue injury. Synthesizes components of the extracellular matrix during wound healing. Can cause pathologic fibrosis.

destinations.label: Connective tissue → Cells of the connective tissue

yGbdbv.title: Collagen
yGbdbv.description: An abundant protein that organizes and strengthens the extracellular matrix. Undergoes extensive posttranslational modification. Includes several subtypes of collagen (e.g., type I collagen, the most common type that is found in bone, skin, and tendons).

_Gb5bv.title: Lysyl oxidase
_Gb5bv.description: A copper-containing enzyme that facilitates cross-linking of lysine and hydroxylysine between tropocollagen molecules to produce collagen fibrils. Decrease in activity is associated with Menkes disease and a form of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

zGbrbv.title: Collagen fibrils
zGbrbv.description: The most common quaternary structure of collagen. Consists of cross-linked tropocollagen molecules. Formation occurs spontaneously in the extracellular compartment.

0tbeXv.title: Reticular fibers
0tbeXv.description: A small-diameter fiber of the extracellular matrix that primarily consists of collagen molecules (especially type III collagen). Found in reticular connective tissue and the basement membrane and contributes to the tensile strength of tissues.

1tb2cv.title: Mucous connective tissue
1tb2cv.description: The extracellular matrix of the umbilical cord, which is formed by collagen fibers, hyaluronic acid, and water. It surrounds, protects, and insulates the umbilical cord vessels by providing a high degree of flexibility and turgor, which renders them resistant to compression.

dtbocv.title: Cephalopelvic disproportion
dtbocv.description: A condition in which the fetal head is too large for the maternal pelvis, which can lead to failure to progress during labor. Common causes include fetal macrosomia, multiparity, post-term pregnancy, and an abnormally shaped maternal pelvis.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormal stages of labor

VtbGcv.title: Two-step oral glucose tolerance test
VtbGcv.description: A screening test for gestational diabetes typically performed at 24-28 weeks' gestation. Consists of a 50-g oral glucose load followed by one-hour blood glucose measurement. Different thresholds for a positive screen (≥130 mg/dL, ≥135 mg/dL, or ≥140 mg/dL) have been proposed. A positive screen is followed by a diagnostic 100-g, three-hour oral glucose tolerance test.

Utbb1v.title: Subchorionic hematoma
Utbb1v.description: Bleeding between the gestational sac and uterine wall due to separation of the chorionic plate from the decidua. A common cause of vaginal bleeding during the first trimester of pregnancy. Depending on its size and location, the hematoma may reabsorb or expand, leading to complications including preterm labor, prelabor rupture of membranes, and pregnancy loss.

2tbT1v.title: Lupus anticoagulants
2tbT1v.description: A group of antibodies against phospholipids found in cell membranes. In vitro, they prevent blood clotting and prolong aPTT, but have a procoagulatory effect in vivo. In patients with antiphospholipid syndrome, the antibodies induce a hypercoagulable state and thrombosis formation.

ftbk1v.title: Anticardiolipin antibodies
ftbk1v.description: A group of antibodies (IgM, IgG, IgA) against cardiolipin, a phospholipid in cellular membranes. In addition to patients with antiphospholipid syndrome, these antibodies can be found in those taking certain medications (e.g., phenothiazines, hydralazine, TNF-a inhibitors), those with other autoimmune diseases, infections, neoplasms, and also in healthy individuals.

Ttb61v.title: Bismuth subsalicylate
Ttb61v.description: A drug that converts to bismuth and salicylic acid in the GI tract and exhibits antisecretory, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory action. Used in diarrhea, heartburn, nausea, traveler's diarrhea, and H. pylori quadruple eradication therapy (protects mucosa, promotes ulcer healing).

gtbF1v.title: Uterine leiomyosarcoma
gtbF1v.description: A rare malignant tumor arising from the smooth muscle cells of the myometrium. Usually presents with menstrual irregularities, postmenopausal bleeding, pelvic pain, and a rapidly enlarging uterus. Clinically difficult to distinguish from a benign fibroid; a definitive diagnosis can only be made on histology.

Stby1v.title: Biliary colic
Stby1v.description: A condition characterized by dull pain in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen that often radiates to the right shoulder or scapula. Can be associated with nausea and vomiting. Caused by impaction of a gallstone in the neck of the gallbladder. Often triggered after a meal and typically lasts < 6 hours with spontaneous resolution.

htbcWv.title: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder
htbcWv.description: Affective (e.g., mood swings, irritability) and somatic (e.g., bloating, lethargy) symptoms with an onset in the luteal phase and with resolution following menstruation. Impact on daily functioning is significant. DSM-5 criteria for PMDD include ≥ 5 symptoms in most menstrual cycles.

3tbSWv.title: Wobble hypothesis
3tbSWv.description: A property of the genetic code in which codons that differ in the third position (wobble position) can specify the same tRNA/amino acid.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

RtblWv.title: Peptidyl transferase
RtblWv.description: The catalytic center of the ribosome and the site of peptide bond formation during the second step of the elongation phase of protein synthesis. Peptidyl transferase activity is intrinsic to the rRNA (ribozyme) of the large ribosomal complex.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

itbJWv.title: Eukaryotic initiation factor 2
itbJWv.description: A GTP-dependent protein that mediates the binding of tRNA to ribosomes.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

OtbIdv.title: Protein folding
OtbIdv.description: The process by which a polypeptide chain acquires its functional three-dimensional structure. Determined by a protein's primary structure, post-translational modifications, interactions with solvent around the protein, and chaperone proteins.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Protein folding and misfolding

Ntb-dv.title: Protein glycosylation
Ntb-dv.description: The attachment of a carbohydrate to a protein, which forms a glycoprotein. Typically refers to enzymatic glycosylation (a type of post-translational modification) but can also refer to nonenzymatic glycosylation (e.g., glycation of hemoglobin to form HbA1c in patients with diabetes). Can affect protein function.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

mtbVVv.title: N-linked glycosylation
mtbVVv.description: A form of enzymatic glycosylation in which an oligosaccharide is added to the nitrogen atom of the side chain on an amino acid. N-glycosylation typically occurs on amino acids such as asparagine and arginine, which have nitrogen in the side chain. N-glycosylation plays a role in directing cellular protein trafficking.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

5tbiVv.title: O-linked glycosylation
5tbiVv.description: A form of enzymatic glycosylation in which an oligosaccharide is added to the oxygen atom of the side chain on an amino acid. O-glycosylation typically occurs on amino acids such as serine, threonine, tyrosine, hydroxylysine, and hydroxyproline. O-glycosylation plays a role in directing cellular protein trafficking.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

MtbMVv.title: ADP-ribosylation
MtbMVv.description: A posttranslational modification in which one or more ADP-ribose residues are added to a protein molecule by ADP-ribosyltransferase using NAD+ as a cofactor. Plays an important role in regulating gene expression (e.g., histone modification by poly-ADP-ribosylation). Certain exotoxins (e.g., exotoxin A of P. aeruginosa, diphtheria toxin) inhibit protein synthesis by mono-ADP-ribosylation of elongation factor-2.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

6tbjev.title: Vulvectomy
6tbjev.description: A procedure in which the vulva is removed (either partly or entirely). It is usually performed in cases of vulvar dysplasia or malignancy.

ptbLev.title: Placental site trophoblastic tumor
ptbLev.description: A rare type of potentially malignant gestational trophoblastic disease that is histologically characterized by the absence of villi, decreased syncytiotrophoblast cells, and proliferation of intermediate trophoblast cells. Patients have lower levels of beta-hCG when compared with other forms of GTD. Placental site trophoblastic tumors are resistant to chemotherapy. Up to 30% present with metastasis.

Jtbsev.title: Proctoscopy
Jtbsev.description: A procedure in which a camera is used to examine the anus, rectum, and/or sigmoid colon.

qtbCev.title: Progestin challenge test
qtbCev.description: A study used in the evaluation of patients with secondary amenorrhea. A progestin is administered for 5-10 days. If uterine bleeding occurs within 14 days after progestin cessation, amenorrhea is likely caused by anovulation. Absence of bleeding by 14 days suggests a low estrogen state or reproductive outflow tract abnormalities.

ItbYUv.title: Fecal fat test
ItbYUv.description: A test that quantitatively or qualitatively measures the amount of fat in stool. Increased stool fat indicates fat malabsorption.

rtbfUv.title: Cow's milk allergy
rtbfUv.description: A food allergy caused by an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction to proteins with cow milk (e.g., casein, alpha-lactalbumin, beta-lactoglobulin). Patients present with colicky abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, vomiting, hives, itching, and/or wheezing. The onset of symptoms typically occurs during late infancy or early childhood.

7tb4Uv.title: Montevideo unit
7tb4Uv.description: A measurement of uterine contraction during labor. Measurements are obtained via an intrauterine pressure catheter. Uterine resting pressure (~ 10-25 mm Hg) is subtracted from the peak contraction pressure, and the net pressure of all individual contractions over the course of 10 minutes is summed. 200–250 MVUs is considered adequate uterine contractions during the active phase of labor.

HtbKUv.title: Occiput transverse position
HtbKUv.description: A type of malposition in which the fetal sagittal suture and fontanels align with the transverse plane of the maternal pelvis.

media.title: Plane of the pelvic inlet: left occiput transverse position

stbtUv.title: Scrotal hematocele
stbtUv.description: A collection of blood between the tunica albuginea and the tunica vaginalis (i.e., outside the testis).

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Descent of gonads

ttbX2v.title: Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate
ttbX2v.description: An injectable, progestin-only contraceptive that provides relatively long (up to 3 months) but reversible protection. Typically used in women that have contraindications for estrogen-containing contraceptives or who do not want to take daily oral contraceptives.

Ftbg2v.title: Megesterol acetate
Ftbg2v.description: A progestin with anti-estrogenic properties. It is used in the palliative treatment of advanced breast or endometrial cancer and as an appetite stimulant in cachexia related to cancer or HIV.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

8tbO2v.title: Dronabinol
8tbO2v.description: The principal psychoactive cannabinoid in cannabis, which is also produced synthetically and used as an antiemetic for chemotherapy-induced nausea or an appetite stimulant in HIV-related anorexia.

utbp2v.title: Cancer anorexia-cachexia syndrome
utbp2v.description: A progressive wasting of skeletal muscle mass with or without the loss of body fat that occurs in patients with cancer. Results from decreased appetite and the hypercatabolic state that is generated by pro-inflammatory cytokines and tumor-derived factors.

destinations.label: Principles of cancer care → Cancer-related complications

Etb82v.title: Ketorolac
Etb82v.description: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug that is typically used for the short-term management of moderate to severe pain (e.g., postoperative pain relief). Ketorolac eye drops are also used to treat allergic conjunctivitis.

vtbA2v.title: Ketonuria
vtbA2v.description: A condition in which ketone bodies are present in the urine. A sign of excess ketone production, as seen during states of starvation and diabetic ketoacidosis.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

Dtb1fv.title: Lipoxygenase
Dtb1fv.description: A family of isozymes involved in the synthesis of leukotrienes from arachidonic acid.

wtbhfv.title: Supportive psychotherapy
wtbhfv.description: A treatment approach used especially for the management of anxiety disorders. Focuses on empathizing with the patient and providing encouragement and coping techniques to improve self-esteem and functioning.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Supportive psychotherapy

Ctbqfv.title: Motivational interviewing
Ctbqfv.description: A counseling technique that is used to create intrinsic motivation in an individual for behavioral change, based on the following 4 steps: engaging, focusing, evoking, and planning. Interview techniques used include: using open-ended questions, affirming, reflecting, and summarizing (OARS). Each of these steps and techniques is calibrated according to the specific stage of change that the individual is currently in (based on the transtheoretical model). Can be used for certain lifestyle changes (e.g., weight loss, tobacco cessation).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Motivational interviewing

xtbEfv.title: Group therapy
xtbEfv.description: A treatment approach in psychotherapy in which one or more therapists treat a group of patients, usually with the same mental disorder or behavioral problems. Provides a setting for patients to share similar experiences, difficulties, and coping strategies. Commonly indicated for management of substance use disorders or personality disorders, but also used for support groups (e.g., grief management).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Group therapy

ytbdTv.title: Apt test
ytbdTv.description: A hematologic test used to differentiate neonatal or fetal blood from maternal blood by exposing blood to sodium hydroxide. Fetal hemoglobin's resistance to alkali denaturation allows it to remain intact, and it appears pinkish under microscopy (indicating a positive test), while adult hemoglobin gives off a light-brownish color due to denaturation. Indications include newborn gastrointestinal (stool, vomiting) or pulmonary bleeding, as well as antepartum bleeding of unknown origin (e.g., vasa previa).

AtbRTv.title: Depression with atypical features
AtbRTv.description: A subtype of depression that is characterized by increased sleep, and/or leaden paralysis of the arms and legs, increased appetite and weight gain, and mood reactivity (brightening of mood in response to positive events).

destinations.label: Major depressive disorder → Subtypes and variants

ztbrTv.title: Aldosterone synthase deficiency
ztbrTv.description: A rare disease caused by a mutation of the CYP11B2 gene on chromosome 8q. Deficiency of aldosterone synthase (corticosterone methyloxidase) results in hypoaldosteronism.

-tbDTv.title: Type 1 pseudohypoaldosteronism
-tbDTv.description: A form of aldosterone resistance that is caused by an autosomal dominant loss-of-function mutation in the gene encoding for mineralocorticoid receptor protein or autosomal recessive loss-of-function mutations in the genes encoding the epithelial sodium channel.

destinations.label: Renal tubular disorders →  Hyperkalemic renal tubular acidosis (type 4)

0Fbegv.title: Familial glucocorticoid resistance
0Fbegv.description: A hereditary condition caused by loss-of-function of the glucocorticoid receptor in all tissues (including the pituitary and hypothalamus). The lack of negative feedback by cortisol causes increased ACTH production. As a result, patients have increased cortisol levels with features of mineralocorticoid excess and hyperandrogenism without clinical features of hypercortisolism.

aFbQgv.title: Primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease
aFbQgv.description: A distinct form of ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome that is characterized by small adrenal glands with multiple, small, black nodules and cortical atrophy between the nodules. This condition may occur sporadically or as a manifestation of the inherited condition known as the Carney complex.

YFbngv.title: Glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism
YFbngv.description: A rare, autosomal dominant disorder in which the activity of aldosterone synthase (corticosterone methyloxidase) is controlled by ACTH. Normally, the activity of this enzyme is not significantly influenced by ACTH stimulation. Suppression of ACTH secretion by glucocorticoids treats hyperaldosteronism caused by this condition.

bFbHgv.title: Pseudohypoaldosteronism type 2
bFbHgv.description: An autosomal dominant condition characterized by increased sodium reabsorption and decreased potassium secretion due to dysfunction of ion channels in the kidney. Manifestations include hypertension, hyperkalemia, hyperchloremia, and metabolic acidosis.

destinations.label: Renal tubular disorders →  Hyperkalemic renal tubular acidosis (type 4)

XFb9gv.title: Sarcolemma
XFb9gv.description: The cell membrane of a myocyte.

cFbaSv.title: Processus vaginalis
cFbaSv.description: An outpouching of the parietal peritoneum from the abdominal cavity to the scrotum created as the fetal testis descends into the scrotum from its intra-abdominal location.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Descent of gonads

1Fb2Sv.title: Communicating hydrocele
1Fb2Sv.description: A collection of peritoneal fluid around the testis caused by the failure of the processus vaginalis to obliterate after birth. The hydrocele communicates with the peritoneal cavity. Seen in infants and young children. Since the processus vaginalis closes spontaneously by 2 years of age, most communicating hydroceles spontaneously resolve. Persistence beyond 2 years or the presence of a coexistent inguinal hernia are indications for surgery.

WFbPSv.title: Narrow therapeutic index
WFbPSv.description: A term used to describe drugs in which the minimum dose for a therapeutic effect is quite close to the dose that is associated with adverse effects. A small decrease in the blood concentration of the drug from this therapeutic window results in therapeutic failure while a slight increase in blood concentration can have serious adverse effects. Examples include lithium and drugs used for chemotherapy.

dFboSv.title: Bladder stress test
dFboSv.description: A test that simulates involuntary release of urine in order to confirm stress incontinence. Leakage of urine occurs under increased abdominal pressure (e.g., Valsalva maneuver, forced coughing, sneezing, laughing, or exercising). Fluid loss that occurs only several seconds after coughing indicates urge incontinence.

eFbxSv.title: Central vertigo
eFbxSv.description: A type of vertigo caused by a lesion of the CNS. Typically causes gait imbalance and ataxia.

UFbbhv.title: Peripheral vertigo
UFbbhv.description: A subset of vertiginous conditions generally characterized by the following features: severe vertigo, absent or mild ataxia, mostly horizontal nystagmus, and potentially hearing loss. Examples include Ménière disease and benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.

2FbThv.title: Urethropexy
2FbThv.description: Surgical fixation of a displaced urethra and bladder neck to nearby tissue. Used to treat stress urinary incontinence. Less effective than midurethral sling and associated with more complications.

TFb6hv.title: Mid-urethral sling
TFb6hv.description: Most common type of surgery used to treat stress urinary incontinence resistant to conservative treatment. A synthetic sling is placed under the urethra and bladder neck to lift, support, and exert pressure on the urethra to aid urine retention. The end of the sling is attached to pelvic fascia or the abdominal wall.

gFbFhv.title: Dyscalculia
gFbFhv.description: A type of specific learning disorder characterized by difficulties in understanding numerical information and performing mathematical calculations.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

SFbyhv.title: Sarcoplasm
SFbyhv.description: The cytoplasm of a myocyte (muscle cell). Contains glycosomes (stored glycogen), myoglobin, calcium ions, and myofibrils.

hFbc3v.title: Sarcoplasmic reticulum
hFbc3v.description: A type of smooth endoplasmic reticulum in myocytes. It functions as a storehouse for calcium. Release of calcium from the sarcoplasmic reticulum results in muscle contraction.

RFbl3v.title: Actin myofilament
RFbl3v.description: A thin filament of muscle tissue that consists of actin molecules, regulatory proteins, and nebulin. Regulatory proteins limit interaction between myosin and actin, thereby preventing permanent muscle contraction. Nebulin is an actin-binding protein.

media.title: Actin filaments and actin-binding proteins in the contractile apparatus

iFbJ3v.title: Tropomyosin
iFbJ3v.description: A protein involved in the regulation of contraction of striated muscle. Blocks the myosin-binding site on the actin filament. During muscle contraction, tropomyosin is removed from the myosin-binding site, which allows myosin to bind to actin.

media.title: Actin filaments and actin-binding proteins in the contractile apparatus

QFbu3v.title: Calmodulin
QFbu3v.description: A multifunctional calcium-binding protein ubiquitously expressed in all eukaryotic cells. Involved in several cellular functions and processes such as muscle contraction, inflammation, metabolism, apoptosis, and intracellular signaling.

media.title: Electro- and pharmacomechanical coupling of smooth muscle cell contraction

jFb_3v.title: Myosin filament
jFb_3v.description: The thick filament of a muscle cell, which consists of a head and a tail that work together with actin to generate muscle contraction.

4Fb3Rv.title: Sarcomere
4Fb3Rv.description: The contractile unit of striated muscle cells, formed by actin and myosin myofilaments attached to the cytoskeleton.

media.title: Changes in sarcomere length during muscle contraction
Overview of the sarcomere and myofilaments

kFbmRv.title: I band
kFbmRv.description: The lighter of the two bands in sarcomeres, Regions composed only of actin filaments (with no superimposition by thick filaments (myosin)). Bisected by Zlines, upon which the actin filaments are anchored.

media.title: Changes in sarcomere length during muscle contraction

OFbIRv.title: A band
OFbIRv.description: The portion of the sarcomere containing myosin, which overlaps with actin except in the central H zone. The A band does not change size during contraction.

lFbvRv.title: Z lines
lFbvRv.description:
1. A line that separates one sarcomere from another (see Z band). Acts as an anchoring point for actin filaments through anchoring proteins such as α-actinin. Connected to the M line through the titin protein.
2. The physiologic transformation zone between squamous and columnar epithelium in the esophagus. Macroscopically visible during upper endoscopy.

NFb-Rv.title: H zone
NFb-Rv.description: A central segment within the A band of a myosin filament. Contains only myosin filaments and decreases in size during contraction.

media.title: Changes in sarcomere length during muscle contraction

mFbViv.title: M lines
mFbViv.description: The center of the H zone, where myosin filaments attach. Connected to the Z band through the titin protein.

MFbMiv.title: Sliding filament theory
MFbMiv.description: The cycle of muscular contraction on a molecular level. Myofilaments (protein fibers that consist of myosin and actin filaments) slide past each other to generate a contraction. The process involves crossbridge cycling, which is a repetitive cycle of connections (crossbridges) between myosin heads and actin filaments, and subsequent loosening of the crossbridges. Requires an initiating stimulus, calcium, and ATP.

oFb0Qv.title: Major depressive disorder with psychotic features
oFb0Qv.description: A subtype of major depressive disorder characterized by the presence of psychotic symptoms (e.g., delusions, hallucinations) that occur exclusively during depressive episodes.

destinations.label: Major depressive disorder → Subtypes and variants

KFbUQv.title: Adjustment disorder with depressed mood
KFbUQv.description: A psychiatric condition in which depressive symptoms occur within 3 months of a psychosocial stressor. Low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness are the predominant symptoms. Upon resolution of the stressor, the symptoms do not persist for more than 6 additional months. Full criteria for other psychiatric conditions, such as major depressive episode or generalized anxiety disorder, are not met.

destinations.label: Trauma- and stressor-related disorders → Adjustment disorder

6FbjQv.title: Adenylate kinase
6FbjQv.description: An enzyme of the mitochondrial intramembrane space that facilitates the transfer of a phosphate residue from one ADP to another to create ATP (adenylate kinase reaction).

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Overview

pFbLQv.title: Glucose-alanine cycle
pFbLQv.description: A metabolic cycle in which alanine from protein degradation is transported from skeletal muscle to the liver to form glutamate and pyruvate. Pyruvate is then used to create glucose via gluconeogenesis.

qFbCQv.title: Extracellular matrix
qFbCQv.description: An organized, mesh-like structure formed by glycosaminoglycans, proteoglycans, glycoproteins, amino sugars, laminin, fibronectin, and other molecules. Provides structure and supports cell growth and function.

rFbfjv.title: Persistent complex bereavement disorder
rFbfjv.description: An unusually prolonged and/or intense period of grief characterized by significant dysfunction that impairs daily life. Can manifest with hallucinations and somatic complaints. Associated with an increased risk of developing a psychiatric disorder (e.g., prolonged complex bereavement disorder, suicidal ideation and behavior, substance use disorder).

destinations.label: Grief and end-of-life counseling → Bereavement and grief

7Fb4jv.title: Hoarding disorder
7Fb4jv.description: A psychiatric disorder characterized by a persistent difficulty associated with discarding possessions. Results in the accumulation of these possessions and clinically significant distress and/or impairment.

tFbXPv.title: Family therapy
tFbXPv.description: A psychotherapeutic method that regards the whole family, rather than individuals, as the unit of treatment. Focuses on improving communication between family members. Can be used in the management of schizophrenia, eating disorders, and bereavement.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Family therapy

FFbgPv.title: Rubin's maneuver
FFbgPv.description: An obstetric maneuver used in the management of shoulder dystocia. Involves manual rotation of the fetal shoulder girdle by applying pressure to the posterior part of the anterior shoulder. When used with the McRoberts maneuver, involves application of suprapubic pressure (proximal to the symphysis pubis) to the posterior part of the impacted anterior shoulder.

media.title: McRoberts maneuver and suprapubic pressure (Rubin I maneuver) in shoulder dystocia

8FbOPv.title: Wood's maneuver
8FbOPv.description: An obstetric maneuver used in the management of shoulder dystocia. Involves manually rotating (abducting and extending) the shoulder girdle by applying pressure to the anterior part of the posterior shoulder.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Shoulder dystocia

uFbpPv.title: Zavanelli maneuver
uFbpPv.description: An obstetric maneuver used in the management of shoulder dystocia. Involves administration of a uterine relaxant, pushing the fetal head back into the pelvis, and then performing a cesarean delivery. Used as a measure of last resort due to high risk of perinatal hypoxia and injury.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Shoulder dystocia

EFb8Pv.title: Symphysiotomy
EFb8Pv.description: A procedure in which the symphysis pubis is divided in the midline in order to increase the space of the pelvic cavity and facilitate vaginal delivery. Indicated in the case of obstructed labor due to cephalopelvic disproportion, breech presentation, or shoulder dystocia. Mainly performed when caesarean section is unavailable.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Shoulder dystocia

vFbAPv.title: Urethral cotton swab test
vFbAPv.description: A test for urethral mobility used in the workup of stress urinary incontinence. A cotton swab is placed into the urethra and the patient performs the Valsalva maneuver. Movement of the cotton swab > 30° from the horizontal plane is considered positive for urethral mobility and is a predictor that surgery will be beneficial.

9FbN4v.title: Bedbugs
9FbN4v.description: Parasitic arthropods of the Cimicidae family, whose bite causes a painless papule on exposed skin (typically in bed while sleeping) that becomes itchy and resolves spontaneously within 1–2 weeks. Crowded living conditions are risk factors for bedbug infestations.

CFbq4v.title: Bamboo spine
CFbq4v.description: A radiographic sign of ankylosing spondylitis that occurs as a result of ossification of outer fibers of the annulus fibrosus, which results in ankylosis (fusion) of intervertebral joints.

media.title: Bamboo spine and dagger sign in ankylosing spondylitis
Cervical chalk stick fracture in ankylosing spondylitis

xFbE4v.title: Aquagenic pruritis
xFbE4v.description: Severe itching following skin contact with water. Aquagenic pruritus may be associated with hives in patients with aquagenic pruritus. Aquagenic pruritus without any skin lesions can be caused by myeloproliferative conditions such as polycythemia vera and chronic myeloid leukemia.

_Fb5kv.title: Ploidy
_Fb5kv.description: The number of sets of chromosomes in a cell. Normal human cells are diploid, carrying a maternal and a paternal set of chromosomes, while gametes are monoploid.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

zFbrkv.title: Aneuploidy
zFbrkv.description: An abnormal number of chromosomes in a cell.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

-FbDkv.title: Buspirone
-FbDkv.description: An anxiolytic drug used for long-term management of anxiety disorders and short-term relief of symptoms of anxiety. The mechanism of action is unknown but related to serotonin and dopamine receptors. Adverse effects include headaches, dizziness, nausea, and seizures in chronic users.

Z8bZOv.title: Performance-only social anxiety disorder
Z8bZOv.description: An anxiety disorder characterized by intense fear and/or anxiety related to speaking and/or performing in public. Typically accompanied by multiple physical symptoms, e.g., blushing, palpitations, and sweating.

a8bQOv.title: Radial nerve
a8bQOv.description: A peripheral nerve in the upper limb that arises as a continuation of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus (nerve roots: C5-8, T1). The radial nerve innervates the triceps, brachioradialis, supinator, and muscles in the extensor compartment of the forearm, as well as the skin on the dorsal surface of the arm, forearm, and hand.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

b8bHOv.title: Claustrophobia
b8bHOv.description: A persistent and intense fear of enclosed spaces. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

X8b9Ov.title: Aerophobia
X8b9Ov.description: A persistent and intense fear of flying. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

c8balv.title: Odontophobia
c8balv.description: A persistent and intense fear of dental procedures. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

18b2lv.title: Traumatophobia
18b2lv.description: A persistent and intense fear of injury. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

d8bolv.title: Entomophobia
d8bolv.description: A persistent and intense fears of insects. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

V8bGlv.title: Cynophobia
V8bGlv.description: A persistent and intense fear of dogs. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

e8bxlv.title: Astraphobia
e8bxlv.description: A persistent and intense fear of thunder and lightning. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

U8bbNv.title: Alprazolam
U8bbNv.description: A short-acting benzodiazepine that is used as an anxiolytic to treat generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorders, social anxiety disorders, night terrors, and insomnia. Also used as a muscle relaxant and to treat symptoms of alcohol withdrawal.

28bTNv.title: Coulrophobia
28bTNv.description: A persistent and intense fear of clowns. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

f8bkNv.title: Masklophobia
f8bkNv.description: A persistent and intense fear of costumed characters. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

T8b6Nv.title: Triskaidekaphobia
T8b6Nv.description: A persistent and intense fear of the number 13. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

g8bFNv.title: Emetophobia
g8bFNv.description: A persistent and intense fear of vomiting. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

S8byNv.title: Ideas of reference
S8byNv.description: The sense that the ordinary actions of others (e.g., whispering, smiling) have personal significance. Ideas of reference can be a manifestation of a psychiatric disorder (e.g., bipolar disorder or schizophrenia) and may develop into delusions of reference (e.g., an individual thinks that television broadcasts are addressing them directly).

38bSmv.title: Antisperm antibody
38bSmv.description: An antibody that causes agglutination, immobilization, and/or toxic effects on sperm, which can result in infertility. Can be detected in cervical fluid, semen, or blood (of men or women). May develop spontaneously or after testicular injury.

R8blmv.title: Pseudoparkinsonism
R8blmv.description: A condition of secondary parkinsonism (e.g., cogwheel rigidity, stiff gait, tremor) as an adverse effect of medications with antidopaminergic effects. including typical antipsychotics (e.g., haloperidol), some antiemetics (e.g., metoclopramide), some calcium channel blockers (e.g., flunarizine, amiodarone), valproate, and lithium.

i8bJmv.title: Psychoanalysis
i8bJmv.description: A type of psychotherapy. Indications include cluster B and C personality disorders, anxiety disorder, and major depressive disorder.

Q8bumv.title: Transference
Q8bumv.description: A phenomenon in which a patient projects feelings about important persons onto the clinician (e.g., by viewing the clinician as their significant other or parent).

j8b_mv.title: Counter-transference
j8b_mv.description: A phenomenon in which health providers subconsciously project their own feelings onto patients. Examples include a therapist projecting feelings toward their own child onto a patient and a physician projecting negative feelings stemming from past difficult patient encounters or life experiences onto a patient.

P8bW5v.title: Free association
P8bW5v.description: A technique in psychoanalytic therapy in which a patient is asked to freely share all thoughts and feelings that occur. The aim is to uncover unconscious emotions and thoughts.

48b35v.title: Therapeutic alliance
48b35v.description: A relationship through which a patient and clinician engage with one another to set and work toward a therapeutic goal.

k8bm5v.title: Dream interpretation
k8bm5v.description: A psychoanalytic technique in which a patient shares the content of their dreams with a therapist, who then interprets and explores how dream content reflects the patient's urges and fears.

O8bI5v.title: Interpersonal therapy
O8bI5v.description: A time-limited (12 to 16 weeks) treatment approach that aims to improve understanding of problematic interpersonal relationships and/or life situations and thereby help control a patient's moods and patterns of behavior. Used primarily to treat major depressive disorder.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Interpersonal therapy

m8bVMv.title: Token economy
m8bVMv.description: A system that positively reinforces desired behaviors by rewarding them. This technique is based on operant conditioning and commonly used in behavioral therapy.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

58biMv.title: Implosion
58biMv.description: A technique used in behavioral therapy to treat phobic disorders. The patient imagines an anxiety-provoking stimulus until the feeling of fear is replaced by a sense of calm and control.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

M8bMMv.title: Cognitive therapy
M8bMMv.description: A type of psychotherapy that relies on altering a person's perception of a particular situation (cognitive restructuring) to change or mitigate disruptive thought patterns. Used in the management of major depressive disorder, paranoid personality disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, anxiety disorders, and eating disorders.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Cognitive therapy

n8b7Mv.title: Dialectical behavioral therapy
n8b7Mv.description: A modified form of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for patients with severe problems regulating emotions and/or with suicidal and dangerous behavior. Most commonly used in patients with borderline personality disorder. Also used for eating disorders and mood disorders (e.g., bipolar disorder). Includes exercises for mindfulness, skills training (e.g., emotional regulation, distress tolerance), and crisis intervention.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Dialectical behavioral therapy

o8b0nv.title: Couples therapy
o8b0nv.description: A treatment approach in psychotherapy that focuses on solving conflicts, sexual problems, and/or communication problems within the context of an intimate relationship. Different forms of couples therapy include conjoint, concurrent, and four-way therapy.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Couples therapy

68bjnv.title: Altruism (psychiatry)
68bjnv.description: A mature ego defense in which the individual performs acts that benefit others in order to alleviate negative feelings.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

p8bLnv.title: Humor (psychiatry)
p8bLnv.description: A defense mechanism that is classified as mature and involves the channeling of unpleasant thoughts and feelings into a light-hearted story or joke, which reduces the intensity of a situation and thus of personal discomfort.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

J8bsnv.title: Sublimation (psychiatry)
J8bsnv.description: A mature defense mechanism in which an unacceptable behavior is replaced with a more socially-acceptable behavior (e.g., aggressive urges are channeled into sports).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

q8bCnv.title: Suppression (psychiatry)
q8bCnv.description: A defense mechanism that is classified as mature and involves the deliberate attempt to not think about something specific, e.g., trying not to think of smoking while trying to quit.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

78b4Lv.title: Displacement (psychiatry)
78b4Lv.description: An immature defense mechanism in which an individual redirects impulses and emotions in a destructive way from a target that is perceived as threatening or unacceptable to another that is perceived as less threatening or more acceptable.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

H8bKLv.title: Intellectualization (psychiatry)
H8bKLv.description: A neurotic defense mechanism that involves concentrating on the intellectual components of a situation in order to avoid dealing with the anxiety provoked by this situation.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

s8btLv.title: Isolation of affect (psychiatry)
s8btLv.description: A type III (neurotic) defense mechanism that involves objectifying and emotionally detaching oneself from strong thoughts and emotions to make these more tolerable; e.g., reporting a personal traumatic event in matter-of-fact, clinical terms.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

G8bBLv.title: Rationalization (psychiatry)
G8bBLv.description: A type III (neurotic) defense mechanism that is classified as neurotic and involves justifying ideas, actions, or emotions with fallacious reasoning.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

t8bXov.title: Reaction formation (psychiatry)
t8bXov.description: A neurotic ego defense mechanism in which an individual replaces an undesired idea or feeling by acting in a diametrically opposite manner.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

F8bgov.title: Repression (psychiatry)
F8bgov.description: A neurotic/anxiety defense mechanism in which an individual involuntarily prevents unpleasant thoughts from entering his/her consciousness.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

88bOov.title: Externalization (psychiatry)
88bOov.description: A type III (neurotic) defense mechanism in which an individual projects internal characteristics (e.g., moods, attitudes) onto the external world, (e.g., on objects and/or other people). For example, an aggressive man perceives others as aggressive and himself as peaceful.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

u8bpov.title: Dissociation (psychiatry)
u8bpov.description: A psychological defense mechanism that is a natural protective response to a traumatic or stressful experience. Dissociations are characterized by disruption and/or discontinuity of normal consciousness, memory, identity, and perception of oneself (e.g., derealization, depersonalization).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

E8b8ov.title: Sexualization (psychiatry)
E8b8ov.description: A neurotic defense mechanism that refers to an inappropriate imposition of sexual significance on a person

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

v8bAov.title: Inhibition (psychiatry)
v8bAov.description: The subconscious restriction of a behavioral or verbal response even though the stimulus for the response is present.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

D8b1Kv.title: Acting out (psychiatry)
D8b1Kv.description: An immature ego defense mechanism in which an individual expresses repressed or unconscious feelings and thoughts through impulsive and unrestrained actions (e.g., throwing tantrums, using drugs, committing crimes).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

w8bhKv.title: Denial (psychiatry)
w8bhKv.description: A defense mechanism that is classified as immature and involves refusing to accept the truth of a fact or situation, such that it is difficult to deal with. Allows the individual to avoid confronting uncomfortable or painful aspects of one's life. E.g., individuals with a substance use disorder may refuse to acknowledge their addiction and argue that they have full control of their use.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

C8bqKv.title: Distortion (psychiatry)
C8bqKv.description: A type 1 (pathological) ego defense mechanism in which individuals reshape perceived reality to be more acceptable. While typically a normal cognitive pattern in childhood, distortion is a common feature of psychotic disorders in adults.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

x8bEKv.title: Primitive idealization (psychiatry)
x8bEKv.description: An immature defense mechanism in which an individual assigns more positive qualities to an external object or person than they actually have.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

A8bR6v.title: Identification (psychiatry)
A8bR6v.description: A type II (immature) defense mechanism in which an individual internalizes or conforms to the qualities of another person.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

_8b56v.title: Passive aggression (psychiatry)
_8b56v.description: A type 2 (immature) ego defense mechanism in which an individual expresses negative emotions toward someone in an indirect, nonconfrontational way.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

-8bD6v.title: Somatization (psychiatry)
-8bD6v.description: A type 2 (immature) ego defense mechanism in which the psychological distress is transformed into physical symptoms.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

Yubnpv.title: Reactive hypoglycemia
Yubnpv.description: A type of recurrent, symptomatic hypoglycemia that occurs within 4 hours after a carbohydrate-heavy meal due to excessive insulin release.

bubHpv.title: Pseudobulbar affect
bubHpv.description: An affect that is out of proportion to a situation, not congruent with a situation or the individual's mood, or unstable; e.g., crying after knocking over a glass, laughing hysterically after hearing devastating news, crying one second and laughing hysterically the next. A labile affect may be seen with manic episodes or in patients with pseudobulbar palsy.

destinations.label: Bulbar palsy and pseudobulbar palsy → Subtypes and variants

Xub9pv.title: External attribution
Xub9pv.description: The act of attributing one's behavior or an event to a certain situation or environment. For example, a person who is angry while driving attributes his anger to being cut off on the road.

cubaJv.title: Hyperreflexia
cubaJv.description: A condition of exaggerated deep tendon reflexes. Common causes include upper motor neuron injury (e.g., due to stroke, spinal cord injury, multiple sclerosis), hyperthyroidism, drug reactions (e.g., heroin withdrawal, serotonin syndrome), and hypocalcemia.

1ub2Jv.title: Exposure and response prevention therapy
1ub2Jv.description: A cognitive behavioral therapy technique for patients with psychiatric conditions (e.g., anxiety disorders, OCD, PTSD). The patient is gradually exposed to a specific trigger (e.g., memories, feelings, situations) in a controlled environment; over time, their response to the trigger is lessened.

duboJv.title: Primase
duboJv.description: A DNA-dependent RNA polymerase that adds RNA primers on which DNA polymerase III can initiate replication.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

VubGJv.title: Topoisomerases
VubGJv.description: A group of prokaryotic and eukaryotic enzymes that relieve supercoils that develop during DNA elongation as parent DNA is separated by helicase. Targeted by chemotherapeutic and antibiotic agents.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

eubxJv.title: Topoisomerase I
eubxJv.description: An enzyme that cuts one of the two strands of double-stranded DNA to add or remove DNA supercoils during transcription and replication. The anti-Scl-70 antibody against topoisomerase I causes diffuse systemic scleroderma. Irinotecan and topotecan are antineoplastic drugs that target topoisomerase I.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

2ubTqv.title: Okazaki fragment
2ubTqv.description: A short, 1000-2000 nucleotide DNA fragment synthesized discontinuously on the lagging strand during DNA replication. Joined by DNA ligase.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

Tub6qv.title: Telomerase
Tub6qv.description: A eukaryotic reverse transcriptase that carries its own RNA template and adds DNA telomeres to 3′ ends of chromosomes. This function prevents loss of genetic material during DNA replication.

hubcIv.title: Base excision repair
hubcIv.description: A form of single-stranded DNA repair in which a glycosylase excises a damaged base and leaves an apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) site. An AP endonuclease cuts the 5' end of the DNA strand, and a lyase cuts the 3' end. DNA polymerase brings in a new base to fill the AP site, and DNA ligase seals the strand.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

3ubSIv.title: Nucleotide excision repair
3ubSIv.description: A mechanism of single-stranded DNA repair in which endonucleases excise DNA containing damaged bases (e.g., pyrimidine dimers). DNA polymerase and ligase then add and seal the gap. Used to repair helix-distorting lesions. Defective in patients with xeroderma pigmentosum.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

RublIv.title: Simple epithelium
RublIv.description: Epithelium formed by a single layer of cells with all cells attached to the basement membrane.

QubuIv.title: Squamous epithelium
QubuIv.description: A type of epithelium formed by flattened (squamous) cells. Examples include the epidermis, esophagus, cervix, and serous membrane (e.g., peritoneum).

jub_Iv.title: Cuboidal epithelium
jub_Iv.description: Epithelium formed by cuboidal cells (width = height). Found in the distal tubule of the kidneys, bile ducts, and the surface of the ovaries.

PubWrv.title: Columnar epithelium
PubWrv.description: A type of epithelium formed by cells that have a rectangular or cylindrical shape (height > width). Found in the inner lining of the intestinal tract and the respiratory tract (respiratory epithelium).

kubmrv.title: Microvilli
kubmrv.description: A collection of small, ~ 0.1 x 1-2 µm cell membrane protrusions composed of microfilaments that enlarge the surface of epithelial cells (e.g., in renal tubular cells, enterocytes) to aid in functions such as absorption and secretion.

OubIrv.title: Stereocilia
OubIrv.description: A group of organelles present in the auditory and vestibular canal that serve as mechanosensory receptors. Relative movement of stereocilia results in depolarization and transduction of the original stimulus into an electric impulse.

media.title: Mechanoelectrical transduction of sound waves by inner hair cells

lubvrv.title: Kinocilia
lubvrv.description: A type of cilia present in the auditory canal. Usually surrounded by several stereocilia. Movement of surrounding endolymph relative to kinocilia triggers depolarization and the transmission of a neurologic impulse.

MubM7v.title: Urothelium
MubM7v.description: A type of stratified epithelium that lines much of the urinary tract, including the renal pelvis, the ureters, and the bladder. Tissue composed of transitional epithelium can stretch in response to distension.

nub77v.title: Respiratory epithelium
nub77v.description: The epithelium of the respiratory tract, which is lined by ciliated, pseudostratified columnar cells with goblet cells in the bronchi, ciliated, simple columnar cells in the bronchioles, simple cuboidal cells in the terminal brionchioles, and simple cuboidal and squamous cells in the respiratory bronchioles.

media.title: Cells and structures of lungs and airways

KubUHv.title: Epithelial tissue
KubUHv.description: One of four basic types of tissues and is present in almost all organs of the human body as lining and glandular tissue. Classified as according to function as either surface epithelium and glandular epithelium. Surface epithelia is further divided into squamous, cuboidal, and columnar types.

6ubjHv.title: Glandular epithelium
6ubjHv.description: A single cell or group of cells that produce and secrete specific products (e.g., mucin). While glandular epithelium commonly invaginates from surface epithelium into other tissue (e.g., connective tissue), it is separated from other tissues by the basal lamina. Glandular epithelium can be endocrine (which secretes products in the bloodstream) or exocrine (which secretes products onto a surface).

IubYsv.title: Pulmonary acinus
IubYsv.description: A part of the airway distal to a terminal bronchiole. Each acinus contains multiple respiratory bronchioles, alveolar ducts, alveolar sacs, and alveoli.

vubAGv.title: Exocrine gland
vubAGv.description: Glands that secrete their product via a duct onto epithelial surface.

wubhtv.title: Merocrine secretion
wubhtv.description: A form of cellular secretion involving the exocytosis of vesicles. The most common form of cellular secretion in human cells.

9ubNtv.title: Apocrine secretion
9ubNtv.description: A type of secretion in which cells release contents by budding and pinching off a part of the cytoplasm. Examples of apocrine glands include mammary glands, ciliary glands of the eyelid, and apocrine sweat glands.

_ub5Fv.title: Basement membrane
_ub5Fv.description: A thin layer of extracellular matrix to which cells can anchor. Separates epithelium from underlying connective tissue. Composed of the basal lamina adherent to the epithelium and the reticular lamina, which is beneath the basal lamina and adheres to underlying connective tissue.

zubrFv.title: Basal lamina
zubrFv.description: A thin layer of extracellular matrix proteins located adjacent to the epithelium. With the lamina reticularis, it forms part of the basement membrane.

aEbQ8v.title: Narcissistic personality disorder
aEbQ8v.description: A cluster B personality disorder characterized by a pervasive pattern of grandiosity, an excessive need for admiration, and a lack of empathy.

bEbH8v.title: Ventilation-perfusion mismatch
bEbH8v.description: An imbalance between the total lung ventilation (airflow; V) and total lung perfusion (blood flow; Q). V/Q mismatch is an indicator of gas exchange and is the most common cause of hypoxemia. Normal V/Q ratio is 0.8 (since lung bases are better ventilated and perfused than the apices). Decreased ventilation (e.g., in pneumonia, atelectasis) decreases the V/Q ratio. Decreased perfusion (e.g., in pulmonary embolism) increases the V/Q ratio.

media.title: Effect of positioning on V/Q mismatch: ARDS
Effect of positioning on V/Q mismatch: Pneumonia

XEb98v.title: Myofilaments
XEb98v.description: A group of protein fibers that consists of thick (myosin) and thin (actin) filaments. Interactions between myofilaments are responsible for the contractile properties of muscle cells.

WEbPuv.title: Neurotic ego defense mechanism
WEbPuv.description: An ego defense mechanism that offers a short-term advantage in coping (through tension reduction) but causes long-term problems with relationships and work. Common neurotic defenses include controlling, displacement, intellectualization, isolation of affect, rationalization, dissociation, reaction formation, and repression. Seen in adults under stress, patients with obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD), and patients with certain anxiety disorders.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

dEbouv.title: Intrusion symptoms
dEbouv.description: Recurrent, unwanted, disturbing thoughts. May be frightening (e.g., sexual, violent, or contrary to moral norms). Commonly a normal psychological phenomenon but may also be associated with psychiatric disorders (e.g., acute stress disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder).

VEbGuv.title: Intermittent explosive disorder
VEbGuv.description: A disruptive, impulse-control, and conduct disorder characterized by recurrent impulsive outbursts of aggression. Aggression is disproportionate to the triggering event. Outbursts cause significant distress and impact interpersonal functioning and/or result in legal or financial consequences. Diagnosed over 6 years of age (or equivalent developmental age).

destinations.label: Impulse and conduct disorders → Intermittent explosive disorder

UEbbEv.title: Disruptive, impulse-control, and conduct disorders
UEbbEv.description: A group of psychiatric conditions that affect the self-regulation of emotions and behaviors and begin in childhood or adolescence. Behaviors impair social, academic, and/or occupational functioning. Includes conduct disorder, oppositional defiant disorder, and intermittent explosive disorder.

TEb6Ev.title: Somatic symptom and related disorders
TEb6Ev.description: A group of disorders characterized by prominent somatic symptoms that are not explained by a medical condition and are exacerbated by personal stress, depression, and interpersonal conflicts. In contrast with malingering, secondary gain (e.g., time off work, access to medications) is not a feature of this group of disorders.

gEbFEv.title: Excoriation disorder
gEbFEv.description: A psychiatric condition characterized by recurrent skin picking, resulting in lesions, significant distress, and impairment in daily functioning. Involves repeated attempts to decrease or stop picking. Usually begins in adolescence. The majority of affected individuals are female, and comorbidity with obsessive-compulsive disorder, trichotillomania, or major depressive disorder is common.

SEbyEv.title: Hot cross bun sign
SEbyEv.description: A radiological sign visible on MRI as a cross-shaped hyperintensity on T2-weighted axial images of the pons. Associated with multiple system atrophy but can also occur in other neurodegenerative conditions.

REblvv.title: Antimitochondrial antibodies
REblvv.description: A type of antibodies that target mitochondria, especially those of liver cells, and lead to progressive destruction of the liver parenchyma and bile ducts. Elevated antibody levels are detected in more than 95% of patients with primary biliary cholangitis. May also occur in other diseases such as autoimmune hepatitis, systemic sclerosis, SLE, and antiphospholipid syndrome.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → Immune tolerance and autoimmunity

iEbJvv.title: Posterior uveitis
iEbJvv.description: A painless intraocular inflammation that presents with floaters in the visual field and blurred vision. Inflammation can involve the vitreous body (vitritis), the choroid (choroiditis), and/or the retina (retinitis, chorioretinitis, retinochoroiditis). The etiology can be infectious (bacterial, viral) or occur in association with rheumatological or inflammatory conditions (vasculitis, inflammatory bowel disease).

QEbuvv.title: Adrenal adenoma
QEbuvv.description: A benign tumor of the adrenal gland that most commonly originates from the adrenal cortex. Most adrenal adenomas do not produce excess hormones and are therefore asymptomatic (nonfunctioning adenoma). In rare cases, the adenoma is hormonally active (functional adenoma), leading to conditions such as mild autonomous cortisol secretion, primary hyperaldosteronism, or Cushing syndrome.

jEb_vv.title: Direct immunofluorescence
jEb_vv.description: A technique involving antibodies coupled with a fluorescent compound to identify a specific protein or organism by targeting a surface antigen.

kEbmDv.title: Desmoid tumor
kEbmDv.description: A slow-growing, benign but locally aggressive tumor caused by the proliferation of fibroblasts. Is often associated with familial adenomatous polyposis (sporadic desmoid tumors are rare). Can arise from any part of the body, most commonly, the extremities, the abdominal wall, and abdominal cavity. May be asymptomatic until they grow large enough to compress adjacent structures (e.g., bowel/ureteric obstruction).

OEbIDv.title: Flutamide
OEbIDv.description: An androgen receptor blocker used to treat metastatic prostate cancer in combination with gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH/LHRH) analogs for medical castration. Previously used in women with excess androgen levels to control acne, seborrhea, hirsutism (in refractory cases), and androgenetic alopecia; now replaced by safer options.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

lEbvDv.title: Major depressive episode
lEbvDv.description: A major depressive episode is diagnosed when ≥ 5 of the following symptoms are present for a period ≥ 2 weeks: depressed mood most of the time, anhedonia, change in appetite, feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, insomnia or hypersomnia, diminished concentration, psychomotor agitation or retardation, fatigue, and suicidal ideation. In addition, at least one of the 5 symptoms should be anhedonia or a depressed mood.

NEb-Dv.title: Social communication disorder
NEb-Dv.description: A communication disorder characterized by consistent difficulties using verbal and nonverbal communication appropriately in social situations.

5Ebiwv.title: Pegylation
5Ebiwv.description: The process of attaching polyethylene glycol to a biomolecule to protect the biomolecule from the host's immune system, to decrease the biomolecule's renal clearance (by increasing the size of the molecule), and/or to increase the biomolecule's water solubility.

MEbMwv.title: Nasal septum perforation
MEbMwv.description: A defect in the nasal septum that results in a communication between the two nasal cavities. Etiologies include trauma (e.g., nasal fracture), surgical complications (e.g., from septoplasty or rhinoplasty), and systemic diseases (e.g., granulomatosis with polyangiitis).

destinations.label: Miscellaneous ear, nose, and throat disorders → Nasal septal ulceration and perforation

nEb7wv.title: Topographic Freudian model
nEb7wv.description: A model of the mind developed by Sigmund Freud in 1900. Divides the mental apparatus into three systems (unconscious, preconscious, and conscious), which differ in their level of conscious awareness.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

LEbwwv.title: Structural Freudian model
LEbwwv.description: A model of the human psyche developed by Sigmund Freud in 1923. Divides the mental apparatus into the id, ego, and super-ego. These three components each represent a certain part of one's personality structure and interact with one another. With this structural model, Freud revised some of the concepts he introduced in his previous topographic model of the mind.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

oEb09v.title: Type 4 collagen
oEb09v.description: A subtype of collagen that forms the basal lamina of basement membranes. Unlike other forms of collagen, type IV collagen does not have repetitive glycine residues, and the non-collagenous domain at one end of the amino acid chain is not removed during post-translational processing. These two characteristics cause side-by-side instead of end-to-end linkage and give type IV collagen a sheet-like structure. Conditions associated with damage to or a defect of type IV collagen include Goodpasture syndrome and Alport syndrome.

KEbU9v.title: SGA
KEbU9v.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Small for gestational age 
2. Second-generation antipsychotic
3. Supraglottic airway

6Ebj9v.title: Perichondritis
6Ebj9v.description: A condition characterized by inflammation, typically due to infection, of the perichondrium (connective tissue that envelops cartilage). Usually refers specifically to inflammation of the auricular cartilage.

destinations.label: Ear injuries → Perichondritis of the pinna

pEbL9v.title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation
pEbL9v.description: A noninvasive neuromodulation procedure in which magnetic pulses are administered over the skull, which stimulates nerve cells and activates regions of the brain. Used in the management of treatment-resistant major depressive disorder and treatment-resistant schizophrenia.

qEbC9v.title: Phospholipase A2 receptor
qEbC9v.description: A transmembrane protein that occurs in glomerular podocytes. Its exact function is not completely understood. Autoantibodies against this receptor are seen in idiopathic membranous nephropathy.

IEbYCv.title: Eosinophiluria
IEbYCv.description: Eosinophils in the urine. Eosinophiluria can be present in various conditions, including acute interstitial nephritis (AIN), rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN), and transplant rejection.

rEbfCv.title: ASD
rEbfCv.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Atrial septal defect
2. Acute stress disorder
3. Autism spectrum disorder
4. Antiseizure drug
5. Adult Still disease
6. Alzheimer senile dementia
7. Arthroscopic subacromial decompression
8. Aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase

7Eb4Cv.title: Hypercapnia
7Eb4Cv.description: An elevation of CO₂ > 45 mm Hg in arterial blood (normal pCO₂: 33–45 mm Hg). Can be acute (e.g., respiratory muscle paralysis, asthma, pneumonia) or chronic (e.g., COPD). Can be caused due to increased ventilation-perfusion mismatch (e.g., pneumonia, pulmonary embolism), decreased respiratory drive (e.g., sedative overdose, brainstem stroke), or decreased respiratory nerve/muscle function (e.g., poliomyelitis, Guillain-Barré syndrome).

HEbKCv.title: Blocking (psychiatry)
HEbKCv.description: A type 2 (immature) ego defense mechanism in which an individual unconsciously and transiently inhibits the thought process. It usually occurs when experiencing stress.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

sEbtCv.title: Mature defenses
sEbtCv.description: A group of defense mechanisms found in normal adults that help cope with psychological stress. These include altruism, anticipation, humor, suppression, and sublimation.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

GEbBCv.title: Immature ego defense mechanism
GEbBCv.description: An ego defense mechanism that is most commonly seen among adolescents, patients with depression, and/or those with personality disorders. Includes acting out, blocking, somatization, introjection (identification), passive aggression, and regression, among others.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

tEbXxv.title: Early-onset dementia
tEbXxv.description: The onset of dementia before the age of 65 years. Causes include Alzheimer disease, traumatic brain injury, chronic traumatic encephalopathy, heavy alcohol use, cerebrovascular disease, infection, frontotemporal lobar degeneration, Huntington disease, multiple sclerosis, and prion disease.

FEbgxv.title: Hypocapnia
FEbgxv.description: Decrease in pCO₂ < 33 mm Hg in arterial blood (normal pCO₂: 33-45 mm Hg). Hyperventilation (e.g., due to a panic attack, pulmonary embolism, pneumonia, aspirin overdose) increases CO₂ loss and can cause hypocapnia. Hypocapnia results in respiratory alkalosis. The ↑ in pH can lead to hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, and hypophosphatemia. Acute hypocapnia can also cause cerebral vasoconstriction, with cerebral hypoxia leading to dizziness and visual disturbances.

8EbOxv.title: Anti-smooth muscle antibodies
8EbOxv.description: A type of antibody that targets smooth muscle. ASMA can be found in ≥ 85% of individuals with autoimmune hepatitis Type 1.

uEbpxv.title: Anti-endomysial antibody
uEbpxv.description: An antibody that binds to the endomysium that overlies smooth muscle cells. Serum IgA endomysial antibodies have a high sensitivity of up to 98% and a high specificity of up to 100% for celiac disease.

EEb8xv.title: NREM-related parasomnia
EEb8xv.description: A group of sleep disorders characterized by repeated episodes of brief but incomplete awakenings that typically occur during the first third of sleep and are accompanied by sleepwalking and/or sleep terrors.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Classification of sleep disorders

wEbhBv.title: Anti-liver-kidney microsomal-1 antibody
wEbhBv.description: An antibody against the cytochrome P450 enzyme CYP2D6. Associated with autoimmune hepatitis type 2.

CEbqBv.title: Alveolar edema
CEbqBv.description: A type of pulmonary edema in which the majority of fluid collects in the alveoli. Presents on chest x-ray with a positive air bronchogram and bilateral opacities that extend outward from the hilum (bat wing pattern). Common causes include heart failure, acute myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, and pneumonia.

xEbEBv.title: Bacillary angiomatosis
xEbEBv.description: A  condition caused by Bartonella bacteria (e.g., Bartonella henselae) that most commonly develops in patients who are immunocompromised. Causes vascular proliferation, which leads to the development of solitary or multiple, red-purple papules that bleed easily.

AEbRyv.title: Post-nasal drip syndrome
AEbRyv.description: Abnormally increased nasal mucus secretion that drips down the back of the throat and can lead to coughing, a feeling of obstruction in the throat, and throat clearing. Causes include allergies, cold temperatures, viral or bacterial infections, dry air, and certain medications. First-line treatment includes first-generation antihistamines (e.g., diphenhydramine). UACS was previously referred to as post-nasal drip syndrome.

_Eb5yv.title: Temper tantrums
_Eb5yv.description: Angry outbursts characterized by, e.g., stomping and screaming, which typically occur from age 2–5 and are a normal part of a child's development. Warning signs that may indicate an underlying disorder include angry mood persisting throughout the entire day or the child causing physical harm to him/herself or others during tantrums.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Common developmental behaviors

avbQAv.title: Submetacentric chromosome
avbQAv.description: A chromosome wherein the centromere is positioned such that the p arm is shorter than the q arm.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

YvbnAv.title: Metacentric chromosome
YvbnAv.description: A chromosome wherein the centromere is positioned such that the p and q arms are equal in length.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

Xvb9Av.title: Projection (psychiatry)
Xvb9Av.description: A defense mechanism in which the individual attributes his/her undesired thoughts or emotions to another individual(s): e.g., a husband who has an affair believes that his wife is also cheating.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

cvba_v.title: Disulfiram-ethanol reaction
cvba_v.description: Cutaneous vasodilation and/or hypotension that occurs with simultaneous ingestion of alcohol and disulfiram. DER occurs as a result of acetaldehyde accumulation.

destinations.label: Alcohol use disorder → Initiation of pharmacotherapy

1vb2_v.title: Upper respiratory tract infection
1vb2_v.description: An infection involving structures at or above the vocal cords, e.g., the nasal cavity, sinuses, pharynx, and/or larynx.

WvbP_v.title: Dacryocystography
WvbP_v.description: Contrast imaging of the lacrimal sac and nasolacrimal duct to locate the site of NLD obstruction. Dye is instilled into the punctum of the eye and an x-ray or CT of the face is performed. Indicated in patients with chronic dacryocystitis and recurrent acute dacryocystitis. DCG should not be performed until after the treatment of infection.

destinations.label: Diseases of the lacrimal apparatus → Dacryocystitis

evbx_v.title: Nasolacrimal duct probing
evbx_v.description: A procedure in which the lacrimal punctum is dilated and a flexible metallic probe is inserted into the nasolacrimal duct (NLD). Used to diagnose NLD obstruction (dacryostenosis).
