Also used to treat refractory congenital dacryostenosis that does not respond to lacrimal sac massage. Ocular infection is a contraindication to probing.

destinations.label: Diseases of the lacrimal apparatus → Dacryostenosis

Uvbbzv.title: Anticentromere antibodies
Uvbbzv.description: An antinuclear antibody against centromere proteins that is associated with limited systemic sclerosis and an increased risk of developing pulmonary hypertension. Occasionally seen in patients with other autoimmune diseases (e.g., Sjogren syndrome).

2vbTzv.title: Anti-topoisomerase I antibody
2vbTzv.description: Autoantibodies directed at topoisomerase I that can be present in several conditions. Most commonly associated with diffuse systemic sclerosis and a poorer prognosis.

fvbkzv.title: Anti-RNA polymerase III antibodies
fvbkzv.description: Antibodies that may be present in individuals with diffuse systemic sclerosis. Associated with higher risk for scleroderma renal crisis.

Tvb6zv.title: Calcinosis cutis
Tvb6zv.description: Small white calcium deposits within the skin that may be idiopathic, secondary to systemic conditions (e.g., systemic sclerosis, dermatomyositis, chronic renal failure, metabolic disorders and infections), or secondary to tissue damage (e.g., trauma).

gvbFzv.title: Pseudo-Koebner phenomenon
gvbFzv.description: The development of certain infectious dermatoses (e.g., verrucae vulgaris, molluscum contagiosum, pyoderma gangrenosum) in traumatized skin that was previously normal due to inoculation of the pathogen into the damaged skin.

Svbyzv.title: Pathological defense mechanism
Svbyzv.description: A defense mechanism that offers a short-term advantage in allowing an individual to cope with problems (through tension reduction) but may cause long-term problems with relationships and work. Examples include splitting, projection, denial, and distortion.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

3vbS-v.title: Controlling (psychiatry)
3vbS-v.description: An immature defense mechanism in which an individual attempts to excessively manage or regulate the environment to minimize or avoid anxiety.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

ivbJ-v.title: Acquired dacryostenosis
ivbJ-v.description: Acquired obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct (NLD) secondary to NLD concretions, post-traumatic/post-inflammatory stenosis, or granulomatous diseases (e.g., sarcoidosis, tuberculosis). Presents with epiphora and predisposes to infection of the lacrimal sac (dacryocystitis). Treatment involves lacrimal duct probing or dacryocystorhinostomy, as well as management of the underlying condition.

destinations.label: Diseases of the lacrimal apparatus → Dacryostenosis

PvbWZD.title: Dextromethorphan
PvbWZD.description: An NMDA receptor antagonist that is widely available as an over-the-counter cough suppressant. It can also be used to treat a pseudobulbar affect.

4vb3ZD.title: Compound nevus
4vb3ZD.description: A type of common melanocytic nevus (common mole) with nevus cells found both in the dermis and epidermis. Typically presents with a central raised area surrounded by a flat area that is usually lighter in color than common moles.

OvbIZD.title: Case study
OvbIZD.description: A mode of qualitative research that involves the systematic investigation of a complex phenomenon within a specific context to gather insight into the individual experience of the phenomenon of interest. Often used synonymously, "case study" must be distinguished from "case report," which represents a type of observational, descriptive study that reports disease presentation, treatment, and outcome in a single subject or event.

Nvb-ZD.title: Case series report
Nvb-ZD.description: A type of observational, descriptive study that is an aggregation of several similar patient cases. Can describe the course of a disease or the response to treatment. Case series do not look for evidence of cause and effect.

5vbi0D.title: CD117
5vbi0D.description: A cytokine receptor with tyrosine kinase activity that is located on the surface of stem cells, mast cells, melanocytes, interstitial cells of Cajal, and germ cells. Increased levels of CD117 are seen in malignant cells of gastrointestinal stromal tumors, mastocytomas, seminomas, embryonal carcinomas, and leukemias of myeloid lineage.

MvbM0D.title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
MvbM0D.description: A heterogeneous group of high-grade B-cell lymphomas with variable clinical, histological, immunophenotypical, and cytogenetic features. It is the most common form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma among adults.

KvbUaD.title: Perinatal mortality rate
KvbUaD.description: The rate of deaths in the prenatal period (after 22 weeks of gestation) and in the early neonatal period (the first 7 days after a live birth).

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

JvbsaD.title: Mortality rate
JvbsaD.description: The frequency of deaths in a population within a specific time interval. Calculated by dividing the total number of deaths during a specified time period by the number of people in the population and multiplying by a conversion factor to express the figure as the number of deaths per 1,000 or 100,000 individuals/year.

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

IvbYYD.title: Maternal mortality rate
IvbYYD.description: The annual number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births. Includes the death of any person who is pregnant or any death within 42 days after birth or termination of a pregnancy.

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

7vb4YD.title: Proportionate mortality
7vb4YD.description: The number of deaths caused by a specific disease divided by the total number of deaths in a defined population over a certain time period.

HvbKYD.title: Methylxanthine
HvbKYD.description: A class of drugs derived from the purine base xanthine. These drugs nonselectively antagonize adenosine receptors and inhibit phosphodiesterase. Used to treat asthma but have a narrow therapeutic index. Includes aminophylline, theophylline, theobromine, and pentoxifylline.

svbtYD.title: Lacrimal syringing
svbtYD.description: Lacrimal syringing is mainly used as a diagnostic tool in infants with epiphora. The reflux of saline irrigated into the lacrimal punctum indicates a nasolacrimal duct obstruction.

destinations.label: Diseases of the lacrimal apparatus → Dacryostenosis

GvbBYD.title: 1-alpha hydroxylase
GvbBYD.description: An enzyme that converts 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol (calcidiol), an inactive form of vitamin D, into 1,25-dihydroxy cholecalciferol (calcitriol), the active form of vitamin D. The enzyme is located predominantly in the cells of the proximal convoluted tubule and to a lesser extent in keratinocytes.

media.title: Regulation of calcium and phosphate metabolism

tvbXbD.title: Senile cataract
tvbXbD.description: An acquired cataract that develops in patients as a result of the aging process. The incidence increases steadily after the age of 50 years and by the age of 70 years nearly 90% of the population has evidence of cataractous changes in the retina.

FvbgbD.title: Interventional studies
FvbgbD.description: A type of prospective analytical study where the investigator performs an intervention (e.g., administers a drug) to evaluate the outcome.

8vbObD.title: Monocytosis
8vbObD.description: An increase in the number of monocytes in the peripheral circulation. Can be absolute or relative. Most commonly caused by bacterial infections (e.g., tuberculosis, syphilis). Other causes include autoimmune disease (e.g., SLE) and malignancy (e.g., lymphoma).

uvbpbD.title: Polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy
uvbpbD.description: An ocular disease characterized by multiple aneurysmal protuberances from choroidal vessels into the retina.

Evb8bD.title: Drusen
Evb8bD.description: Extracellular lipid and/or protein deposits that are located between the retinal pigment epithelium and Bruch's membrane of the choroid. Drusen tend to occur near the macula. A few, well-demarcated drusen (hard drusen) may be a normal finding in individuals above the age of 40, but the presence of soft drusen (clusters of drusen that are larger and not as well-defined as hard drusen) is associated with age-related macular degeneration.

vvbAbD.title: Cystoid macular edema
vvbAbD.description: Accumulation of fluid at the macula in tiny cyst-like cavities within the outer plexiform layer (Henle's layer) and inner nuclear layers of the retina. Common causes include ocular surgery or laser therapy, retinal vascular disease, choroiditis, and retinal dystrophies.

Dvb1XD.title: Doyne's honeycomb macular dystrophy
Dvb1XD.description: A hereditary maculopathy caused by an autosomal dominant mutation in the EFEMP1 gene of chromosome 2p. Typically presents with slowly progressive loss of vision in the 2nd or 3rd decade of life and drusen arranged radially around the macula in a honeycomb pattern.

wvbhXD.title: Rouleaux formation
wvbhXD.description: An aggregation of erythrocytes with the appearance of a stack of coins on peripheral blood smear. This aggregation is caused by increased concentrations of plasma proteins (e.g., fibrinogen, immunoglobulins). Associated with multiple myeloma but is not specific to this condition.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

CvbqXD.title: Vitamin A toxicity
CvbqXD.description: A rare condition caused by excess intake of vitamin A (usually dietary supplements, possibly large amounts of animal liver). Acute toxicity presents with headache, fatigue, dizziness, nausea, loss of appetite, dry skin, alopecia, and possibly cerebral edema. Chronic intoxication may further present with osteoporosis, bone pain, and psychiatric changes.

xvbEXD.title: Hard exudate
xvbEXD.description: Accumulation of exudate from capillary leakage within the outer plexiform layer (Henle layer) and the inner nuclear layers of the retina.

BvbzXD.title: Kiesselbach plexus
BvbzXD.description: An anastomosis of arteries located in the anteroinferior portion of the nasal septum. Contains branches of the anterior ethmoidal artery, sphenopalatine artery, and superior labial branch of the facial artery. Origin of ~ 90% of episodes of anterior epistaxis.

media.title: Arterial supply of the nasal septum

yvbdcD.title: Xerophthalmia
yvbdcD.description: A pathologic dryness of the cornea and/or conjunctiva.

AvbRcD.title: Lung compliance
AvbRcD.description: The change in volume of the lungs per unit change in pressure. Decreased in conditions that are associated with increased lung stiffness (e.g., pulmonary fibrosis) and increased in conditions such as emphysema.

destinations.label: Respiratory physiology → Lung and chest wall compliance

_vb5cD.title: Chikungunya virus
_vb5cD.description: An RNA virus that belongs to the alphavirus genus of the family Togaviridae. Mainly occurs in Sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Indian subcontinent. Transmitted by mosquitoes most commonly from the species Aedes aegypti. Causes chikungunya with abrupt onset of fever and severe joint pain. The symptoms are similar to those of dengue and Zika.

zvbrcD.title: Zika virus
zvbrcD.description: A flavivirus typically transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes (esp. A. aegypti) that causes Zika virus infection. It is endemic to South America, Africa, and Southeast Asia.

-vbDcD.title: Pseudomonas keratitis
-vbDcD.description: A rapidly progressive type of bacterial keratitis most commonly seen in contact lens users. Manifestations include decreased visual acuity, eye pain and redness, photophobia, and foreign body sensation. Complications include corneal perforation and irreversible vision loss.

ZDbZ1D.title: Ocular rosacea
ZDbZ1D.description: A variant of rosacea involving the eyelids and the globe. Manifestations include sclerokeratitis, conjunctival injection, blepharitis, dry eyes, and foreign body sensation. Can occur with or without cutaneous features of rosacea. Previously classified as a subtype of rosacea.

0Dbe1D.title: Otomycosis
0Dbe1D.description: Fungal infection of the external auditory canal most commonly caused by aspergillus or candida. Predisposing factors include a humid climate, immunocompromised host (e.g., diabetics), hearing aids, and use of antibacterial or steroid ear drops. Common clinical findings are pruritus, pain, scaling, greyish-white malodorous discharge, and decreased hearing.

aDbQ1D.title: Bipolar II disorder
aDbQ1D.description: A mood disorder characterized by at least one episode of hypomania and one major depressive episode. In addition, no manic episode should ever have occurred (distinguishing feature from bipolar I disorder).

YDbn1D.title: Bipolar I disorder
YDbn1D.description: A mood disorder characterized by the occurrence of one or more manic episodes with or without depressive episodes.

1Db2WD.title: Blastomyces dermatitidis
1Db2WD.description: A dimorphic fungus that causes blastomycosis upon inhalation. Appears as a yeast with broad-based buds and thick cell walls on KOH stain. The fungus is endemic to Southeastern and Central US, the Midwest, and Canadian states near the Great Lakes where it is most commonly found in wet soil and decaying wood.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

WDbPWD.title: Epidemiology
WDbPWD.description: The study of the determinants and distribution of diseases.

media.title: Cutoff value of an optimal screening test

VDbGWD.title: Attributable risk
VDbGWD.description: The absolute risk attributable to exposure in the exposed group. Calculated as: incidence rate in the exposed group - incidence rate in unexposed group

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Estimates of population impact

eDbxWD.title: Chi-square test
eDbxWD.description: A statistical method used to compare the distributions of two categorical variables. Each variable (independent and dependent) can be composed of two or more categorical groups. Compares the proportions of numbers (trues) per group and evaluates whether there is a statistically significant difference in the distribution. Typically used for large sample sizes.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

TDb6dD.title: Metaphysis
TDb6dD.description: The portion of a long bone located between the epiphysis and the diaphysis. Contains the growth plate during childhood. Has a rich blood supply. Prone to hematogenous osteomyelitis.

gDbFdD.title: Diaphysis
gDbFdD.description: The shaft of a long bone. Comprised of compact cortical bone with overlying periosteum and a medullary canal containing marrow.

hDbcVD.title: Hydroxyapatite
hDbcVD.description: Hydroxylated calcium phosphate salts that adhere to collagen fibrils in a crystallized form and render them resistant to pressure. Component of bone matrix.

iDbJVD.title: Osteocyte
iDbJVD.description: An osteoblast that has become walled in by the mineralized matrix of bone. Involved in bone remodeling. Connected to surrounding osteoblasts and osteocytes through gap junctions in the bone canaliculi.

QDbuVD.title: Periosteum
QDbuVD.description: Dense, fibrous membrane that covers the outer surface of the bone. Consists of two layers: an outer fibrous layer that consists of primarily dense collagen and an inner layer that contains nociceptive nerve endings, vessels, and mesenchymal stem cells, from which osteoblasts originate.

NDb-eD.title: Woven bone
NDb-eD.description: An immature bone with a poorly organized, hypomineralized matrix. Woven bone is formed when a large amount of bone substance is formed in a short period of time (e.g., embryonic development, bone healing).

HDbKfD.title: Follicular lymphoma
HDbKfD.description: A low-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma of B-cell origin that is characterized by the histologic presence of densely packed lymphoid follicles (with minimal or no tingible body macrophages) containing small cleaved cells without nucleoli (centrocytes) and larger noncleaved cells with multiple nucleoli (centroblasts). Follicular lymphoma typically shows a t(14;18) chromosomal defect and is the most common low-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma in adults.

GDbBfD.title: Ruxolitinib
GDbBfD.description: A JAK 2 inhibitor approved for the treatment of polycythemia vera and primary myelofibrosis. Improves symptoms and quality of life in patients but does not reduce the risk of transformation to acute myeloid leukemia.

tDbXTD.title: Class I human leukocyte antigen
tDbXTD.description: A protein that is coded for by the MHC cluster 1 of genes. HLA class 1 proteins occurs on the surface of all nucleated cells and they display antigens derived from within the cell.

FDbgTD.title: Complement degradation product 4d
FDbgTD.description: A byproduct of the degradation of the human complement protein C4b, which is involved in the classical complement pathway. C4d inhibits the generation of C3 convertase. C4d also has a thioester moiety that enables strong covalent bonding with endothelial cells and the basement membrane; it is therefore used as a marker of antibody-mediated rejection following organ transplantation.

8DbOTD.title: Donor-specific antibodies
8DbOTD.description: Antibodies in the serum of an organ recipient that are directed against the HLA antigens of an allograft. These antibodies may be produced following exposure to non-self antigens during a blood transfusion in the past or may be synthesized denovo after allograft transplantation. The presence of preformed DSA against a given donor's HLA antigens (positive cross-match) increases the risk of organ rejection.

uDbpTD.title: Richter's transformation
uDbpTD.description: Transformation of CLL into an aggressive, high-grade NHL; occurs in ~5% of CLL cases.

EDb8TD.title: Tubulitis
EDb8TD.description: The presence of inflammatory infiltrate in the tubular epithelium. It is characteristically seen in tubulointerstitial nephritis and renal allograft rejection.

vDbATD.title: Leukemic hiatus
vDbATD.description: A gap in the differentiation of white blood cells in which there is a high number of blast cells and mature leukocytes but no intermediate forms in the peripheral blood. Common finding in individuals with acute myelogenous leukemia (AML).

DDb1gD.title: Acute cellular rejection
DDb1gD.description: Acute graft rejection that is the result of a cell-mediated immunity (i.e., T-cell mediated).

wDbhgD.title: Acute humoral rejection
wDbhgD.description: Acute graft rejection that is caused by circulating donor-specific antibodies.

CDbqgD.title: Polyomavirus-associated nephropathy
CDbqgD.description: A condition of renal dysfunction caused by reactivation of a BK polyomavirus infection in patients who are immunocompromised.

BDbzgD.title: Percentiles
BDbzgD.description: A statistical measure that quantifies the percentage of observations below a value of interest. Commonly used to evaluate growth in children (e.g., if a child's height is in the 25th percentile, then he is taller than 25% of children in the studied group).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Measures of dispersion

media.title: Stature- and weight-for-age percentiles (female individuals 2–20 years; 3ʳᵈ–97ᵗʰ percentiles)
Stature- and weight-for-age percentiles (male individuals 2–20 years; 3ʳᵈ–97ᵗʰ percentiles)

yDbdSD.title: Oocyst
yDbdSD.description: A thick-walled stage in the life cycle of certain protozoa (e.g., cryptosporidium, cyclospora) containing multiple sporozoites. The oocyst is shed in the feces of infected humans and animals. Oocysts remain viable for many months in the environment and once ingested, the oocyst releases sporozoites into the intestinal lumen of the new host.

ADbRSD.title: Cryptosporidiosis
ADbRSD.description: A disease caused by ingestion of food or water infected by the Cryptosporidium parasite. Causes mild, self-limited diarrhea about a week after infection in immunocompetent patients. The disease is more severe in immunocompromised individuals, causing potentially life-threatening protracted diarrhea and/or biliary tract infections (e.g., cholangitis, cholecystitis).

_Db5SD.title: P-value
_Db5SD.description: The probability that the result of a given statistical test will be at least as extreme as the result actually observed, assuming that the null hypothesis is correct. If the value is equal to or less than a predetermined cutoff (usually set at 0.05), the result is considered statistically significant and the null hypothesis is rejected.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

-DbDSD.title: Basophilia
-DbDSD.description: An increase in the number of basophils in the peripheral circulation. Can be absolute or relative. Most commonly caused by myeloproliferative disorders (e.g., chronic myelogenous leukemia). May also be caused by parasite infections and allergic reactions.

media.title: Chronic myeloid leukemia on blood smear

0wbehD.title: Giardia duodenalis
0wbehD.description: A flagellated protozoan commonly found in the tropics, subtropics, and North American mountain regions. Usually transmitted through ingestion of Giardia duodenalis cysts from contaminated water (e.g., ponds, water storage systems, mountain streams). Causes giardiasis, which typically manifests with foul-smelling, fatty diarrhea.

YwbnhD.title: Mixed cryoglobulinemia
YwbnhD.description: A collective term for type II and type III cryoglobulinemia. Type II cryoglobulins are monoclonal IgM and polyclonal IgG antibodies, while type III cryoglobulins are polyclonal IgM and polyclonal IgG antibodies. In vivo, these cryoglobulins form immune complexes, have rheumatoid-factor-like activity, and can activate the complement pathway. In vitro, these cryoglobulins precipitate slowly on cooling. Mixed cryoglobulinemia is associated with infections (especially hepatitis C), and autoimmune diseases (especially Sjogren's disease and SLE).

media.title: Diffuse purpura on the lower extremities

bwbHhD.title: Anti-U1 RNP antibodies
bwbHhD.description: The antibodies against U1 small ribonucleoprotein (an intracellular protein that forms a part of the spliceosome). Primarily seen in patients with mixed connective tissue disease.

destinations.label: Autoantibodies in rheumatic diseases → Antinuclear antibodies (ANAs)

Xwb9hD.title: Scleroderma renal crisis
Xwb9hD.description: A life-threatening complication of systemic sclerosis (SSc) that typically manifests with abrupt onset of hypertension, pulmonary edema, encephalopathy, and/or microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, progressing to oliguric renal failure. Occurs more often in individuals with diffuse SSc than in those with limited SSc. Additional risk factors include anti-RNA polymerase III positive serology and treatment with corticosteroids.

cwba3D.title: Cryoprecipitate
cwba3D.description: A substance that precipitates at cooler temperatures. Commonly used to refer to a product obtained from frozen blood plasma via centrifuge.

1wb23D.title: Allergic interstitial nephritis
1wb23D.description: An acute inflammation of the renal tubules and interstitium that leads to acute interstitial nephritis. Caused by a hypersensitivity reaction, most commonly to medication, e.g., penicillins, cephalosporins, NSAIDs, and rifampin.

WwbP3D.title: Diaphoresis
WwbP3D.description: The secretion of sweat from sweat glands. Sometimes used to refer to excessive sweating.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → The sympathetic vs. parasympathetic nervous system

dwbo3D.title: Joint hypermobility syndrome
dwbo3D.description: A common hereditary disorder of connective tissue. Major clinical features are musculoskeletal and dermatologic, including joint hypermobility that may result in recurrent dislocations, hyperelastic skin, easy bruising, and chronic pain.

VwbG3D.title: Granulocytopenia
VwbG3D.description: A condition in which the amount of granulocytes, especially neutrophils (the largest group of granulocytes), is reduced. Can be caused by hereditary conditions, bone marrow disease (e.g., tumor infiltration), autoimmune conditions, and adverse effects of medication. Severe granulocytopenia is called agranulocytosis and reduces immunity considerably.

ewbx3D.title: Tarsorrhaphy
ewbx3D.description: A surgical procedure in which the upper and lower eyelid margins are partially sewn together. This procedure is most often performed to protect the cornea from harmful exposure due to inadequate eyelid coverage (e.g., in Graves disease) and to enable healing of complicated corneal lesions (e.g., in neurotrophic keratopathy). The procedure may be total, partial, temporary, or permanent.

2wbTRD.title: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
2wbTRD.description: A malignant neoplastic disease that arises from lymphoid cell lines and is characterized by the proliferation of immature, nonfunctional cells in the bone marrow that are subsequently released into the bloodstream. The excessive proliferation of immature blasts in the bone marrow impairs all other cell lines, resulting in anemia, clotting disorders, and increased susceptibility to infections.

fwbkRD.title: Acute myeloid leukemia
fwbkRD.description: A malignant neoplastic disease that arises from myeloid cell lines. Characterized by the proliferation of immature, nonfunctional cells in the bone marrow that are subsequently released into the bloodstream. Excessive proliferation of immature blasts in the bone marrow impairs all other cell lines, resulting in anemia, clotting disorders, and increased susceptibility to infections.

Twb6RD.title: Severe dengue
Twb6RD.description: A manifestation of dengue characterized by greatly increased vascular permeability (e.g., pleural effusion, ascites, and severely increased or decreased hematocrit), hemorrhagic symptoms (e.g., petechiae, ecchymoses, purpura), and significant organ involvement (e.g., changes in mental status, liver failure, or cardiomyopathy).

gwbFRD.title: Rapid-acting insulin
gwbFRD.description: A subset of insulin analogs that have the following characteristics: onset of action 5-15 minutes after administration, peak plasma levels ∼1 hour after administration, and duration of action of 3-4 hours. Examples include lispro, glulisine, and aspart.

hwbciD.title: Locus
hwbciD.description: The specific location of a gene on a chromosome.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

3wbSiD.title: Allele
3wbSiD.description: A single copy of a gene, inherited from one parent. A person can be heterozygous (two different alleles) or homozygous (two identical alleles) for each gene.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

RwbliD.title: Genetic polymorphism
RwbliD.description: A frequently occurring variation in a gene (i.e., more than one allele occupies the same locus of that gene). A gene is considered polymorphic if each of its existing alleles is present in ≥ 1% of a population.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

iwbJiD.title: Hemizygote
iwbJiD.description: An organism that only has one copy of a genomic region (e.g., as a result of altered function or deletion of the corresponding region on the other chromosome).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

QwbuiD.title: Recessive allele
QwbuiD.description: The allele that is not revealed phenotypically in a heterozygous individual.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

jwb_iD.title: Codominance
jwb_iD.description: A type of dominance in which both alleles of a gene are expressed in a heterozygous individual. The ABO blood group system is an example of codominance.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

PwbWQD.title: Incomplete dominance
PwbWQD.description: A type of inheritance in which a dominant allele does not entirely mask the expression of a recessive allele, which results in a mixed phenotypic trait in a heterozygous individual.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

4wb3QD.title: Multiple alleles
4wb3QD.description: The occurrence of more than two different alleles in a population (e.g., due to the accumulation of several stable mutations over the course of evolution). In the ABO blood group system, for example, there are three such alleles (A, B, O) that encode the different blood groups depending on the combination.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

kwbmQD.title: Anticipation (genetics)
kwbmQD.description: The tendency of certain diseases to be more severe and have earlier ages of onset in subsequent generations. A common mechanism in trinucleotide repeat disorders such as Huntington disease and myotonic dystrophy.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

5wbijD.title: Mitochondrial inheritance
5wbijD.description: The inheritance of genetic information transmitted maternally through the mitochondrial genome. Genetic diseases with this mode of inheritance (e.g., mitochondrial myopathies, Leber hereditary optic neuropathy) can affect all offspring of affected females but have variable expression due to heteroplasmy.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Other types of inheritance

MwbMjD.title: Multifactorial inheritance disorders
MwbMjD.description: A group of conditions caused by multiple factors (e.g., lifestyle, environmental, and polygenic factors). Examples include metabolic syndrome and coronary heart disease. These disorders do not have a certain inheritance pattern but often cluster in families.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Other types of inheritance

LwbwjD.title: CpG island
LwbwjD.description: A region of DNA in which a cytosine nucleotide is followed by a guanine nucleotide. Often found in the promoter region of genes. Cytosine nucleotides can be methylated to regulate gene expression.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Epigenetic regulation of gene expression

KwbUPD.title: Chromatin remodeling
KwbUPD.description: The process of reorganizing chromatin structure (e.g., from a compact state to a more accessible arrangement). Facilitates access to specific genetic loci by transcription factors and RNA polymerase, which promotes gene activation and transcription. Involves various enzyme remodelers (e.g., SWI/SNF ATPases), histone posttranslational modifications (e.g., acetylation of histone lysine residues), and direct modification of DNA itself (e.g., DNA demethylation).

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

6wbjPD.title: X inactivation
6wbjPD.description: A process in which an X chromosome in a cell with multiple X chromosomes becomes inactivated via the action of regulatory RNAs, Xist RNA, and methylation of DNA and histones. Results in the formation of Barr bodies.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Epigenetic regulation of gene expression

pwbLPD.title: X-inactive specific transcript RNA
pwbLPD.description: A functional RNA product involved in X chromosome inactivation (lyonization). Coats the affected X chromosome and recruits various protein complexes that result in chromosomal inactivation.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Epigenetic regulation of gene expression

JwbsPD.title: Barr body
JwbsPD.description: The inactive X chromosome present in all female somatic cells. Appears as a small, dark-staining spot at the periphery of the nucleus. Consists of tightly-packed, transcriptionally-inactive, heterochromatin.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Epigenetic regulation of gene expression

media.title: Barr body and aberrant nuclear projection

qwbCPD.title: Gene frequency
qwbCPD.description: The relative frequency of an allele at a given genetic locus in a sample or population. Calculated by dividing the number of identified alleles of interest by the total number of all alleles in the population.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

IwbY4D.title: Two-hit hypothesis
IwbY4D.description: A hypothesis which posits that two mutation events are required to result in a phenotypic change. For example, a mutation in the allele of a tumor suppressor gene, followed by a second loss-of-function mutation, can lead to unregulated cell proliferation.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

7wb44D.title: Single nucleotide polymorphism
7wb44D.description: A DNA sequence variant in a population that differ by only a single base pair. They are usually caused by errors during DNA replication and are point mutations.

FwbgkD.title: Nitazoxanide
FwbgkD.description: An antiparasitic drug used to treat infectious diarrhea due to Cryptosporidium parvum or Giardia duodenalis.

8wbOkD.title: Nonsustained ventricular tachycardia
8wbOkD.description: An arrhythmia originating in the ventricles that is usually asymptomatic but may sometimes cause palpitations, chest pain, dyspnea, or syncope. Characterized by three or more consecutive broad QRS complexes (> 120 ms) and tachycardia (> 100/minute) on ECG lasting < 30 seconds.

uwbpkD.title: A disintegrin and metalloproteinase with a thrombospondin type 1 motif, member 13
uwbpkD.description: A zinc-containing metalloprotease that cleaves von Willebrand factor, a large protein involved in blood clotting, which results in decreased enzyme activity. Deficiency (e.g., in patients with thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura) causes small-vessel platelet-rich thrombus deposition with subsequent hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and possible organ damage.

Ewb8kD.title: Asbestos body
Ewb8kD.description: Asbestos fibers coated with ferritin or hemosiderin. Asbestos bodies, which are seen in the sputum and lung parenchyma of patients with a prolonged exposure to asbestos, are formed when macrophages attempt to phagocytose the indigestible asbestos fibers.

Dwb1OD.title: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia
Dwb1OD.description: A limb-threatening reduction in blood flow to the lower extremity characterized by rest pain, nonhealing lower extremity wounds, and/or gangrene for at least 2 weeks. Objective evidence of occlusive arterial disease is necessary to make the diagnosis.

xwbEOD.title: Flecainide
xwbEOD.description: A class IC antiarrhythmic drug (sodium channel blocker). Indicated for the prevention of ventricular arrhythmias, paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, and atrial fibrillation/flutter. Can also be used for pharmacological cardioversion of atrial fibrillation or flutter (off-label)

BwbzOD.title: Eosinopenia
BwbzOD.description: A decrease in the absolute eosinophil granulocyte count. Often associated with the stress-induced release of ACTH and glucocorticoids, which suppress the release of eosinophils from the bone marrow.

AwbRlD.title: PIGA
AwbRlD.description: A gene that causes paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) when mutated. Physiologically, a membrane-bound glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor protects RBCs against complement-mediated hemolysis. Patients with PNH have an acquired mutation in the PIGA gene (phosphatidylinositol glycan anchor biosynthesis, class A gene), which renders the GPI anchor ineffective, resulting in hemolysis.

_wb5lD.title: Renal papilla
_wb5lD.description: The junction between the renal pyramids and the minor calyx. Histologically, the site at which the medullary collecting ducts converge into the papillary duct and empty the urine into the minor calyx.

zwbrlD.title: PCSK9 inhibitors
zwbrlD.description: A lipid-lowering agent consisting of monoclonal antibodies against free PCSK9, the enzyme that is responsible for the degradation of hepatocyte LDL receptors. Increasing the number of LDL receptor increases the removal of serum LDL by hepatocytes. Examples of PCSK9 inhibitors are alirocumab and evolocumab.

-wbDlD.title: Cortical bone
-wbDlD.description: The dense, outer layer of bone surrounding the trabecular bone within. Its high resistance to rotational and compressive forces are fundamental to the main functions of bone: supporting soft tissue, maintaining body structure, protecting organs, bearing weight, and providing levers for movement.

09beND.title: Obstructive jaundice
09beND.description: A condition of conjugated hyperbilirubinemia secondary to obstructed biliary outflow or intrahepatic cholestasis. Obstruction can be intraluminal (e.g., gallstones, parasites), intramural (e.g., cholangiocarcinoma, biliary strictures), or extraluminal (e.g., pseudocyst compressing the common bile duct). Intrahepatic cholestasis can occur in hepatitis (e.g., viral, alcoholic, chronic), sepsis, pregnancy, and certain inherited syndromes (Dubin-Johnson syndrome, Rotor syndrome). Manifestations include jaundice, pruritus, pale stool, and dark urine.

a9bQND.title: Filaggrin
a9bQND.description: A protein that binds to keratin fibers in epithelial cells. Filaggrin is derived from profilaggrin, which is coded for by the FLG gene on chromosome 1q. Filaggrin helps the epidermis to form a barrier against water evaporation, and the processing of filaggrin releases amino-acids that help with water retention (natural moisturizing factors). Mutations in filaggrin can cause ichthyosis vulgaris and atopic dermatitis.

Y9bnND.title: Screening test
Y9bnND.description: A type of test used to identify disease in asymptomatic individuals. For this reason, screening tests typically favor high sensitivity over specificity.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

b9bHND.title: Confirmatory test
b9bHND.description: A test used to confirm disease in patients who are symptomatic or have tested positive on a screening test. Typically favors high specificity rather than sensitivity.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

X9b9ND.title: Positive likelihood ratio
X9b9ND.description: The likelihood that a person with a given disease will have a positive test result compared to a person without the disease having a positive test result. The higher the positive likelihood ratio, the greater the test's validity. The formula for calculating the LR⁺ is: sensitivity/(1 - specificity) or (true positive ratio/false positive ratio).

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

c9bamD.title: Negative likelihood ratio
c9bamD.description: The probability that a person with a disease will have a negative test result compared to the probability of a person without the disease having a negative test result. The lower the negative likelihood ratio, the higher the test's validity. The formula for calculating the -LR is: (1 - sensitivity)/specificity or (false negative ratio/true negative ratio).

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

19b2mD.title: Receiver operating characteristic curve
19b2mD.description: A type of graph that plots true positives (sensitivity) on the y-axis and false positives (1 - specificity) on the x-axis. Used to show the trade-off between clinical sensitivity and specificity for every possible cutoff to evaluate the ability of the test to adequately diagnose subjects (e.g., diseased vs. nondiseased).

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

W9bPmD.title: Friedewald formula
W9bPmD.description: An equation used to calculate the estimated LDL level using the cholesterol levels that are measured directly during laboratory testing: LDL (mg/dL) = total cholesterol – HDL – (triglycerides/5), where “triglycerides/5” represents the VLDL level.

U9bb5D.title: Anti-LKM antibody
U9bb5D.description: An autoantibody against components of the cytochrome P450 system found in patients with various types of liver disease (e.g., autoimmune hepatitis, drug-induced hepatitis, hepatitis D).

29bT5D.title: Anti-liver cytosolic antigen type 1 antibody
29bT5D.description: An antibody against a peptide found in the liver cytosol. Associated with type 2 autoimmune hepatitis.

f9bk5D.title: Sun protection factor
f9bk5D.description: A measure of the amount of UV radiation that causes sunburn on skin protected by sunscreen compared to unprotected skin. Recommended values typically range from 15 to 50, with higher values indicating greater protection.

g9bF5D.title: Right upper quadrant
g9bF5D.description: The right upper quadrant of the abdomen when it is divided into four quadrants by two imaginary lines, one horizontal and the other vertical, that intersect at the umbilicus.

h9bcMD.title: LUQ
h9bcMD.description: The abdomen is divided into four topographic quadrants (four-region scheme) by two imaginary lines, one horizontal and the other vertical, both intersecting at the umbilicus. The LUQ is the left upper quadrant of the abdomen.

39bSMD.title: Left lower quadrant
39bSMD.description: The abdomen is divided into 4 topographic quadrants (four-region scheme) by two imaginary lines, one horizontal and the other vertical, both intersecting at the umbilicus. LLQ is the left lower quadrant of the abdomen.

R9blMD.title: Ganglioneuroma
R9blMD.description: A rare, benign tumor of the autonomic nerve fibers most commonly associated with MEN 2B. Most commonly located in the abdomen (intestines), but also adrenal glands, mediastinum, head, and neck. Usually asymptomatic; possible symptoms are caused by compression of surrounding structures or secretion of hormones (e.g., VIP, norepinephrine) and their associated effects (e.g., diarrhea, hypertension).

i9bJMD.title: Birth rate
i9bJMD.description: The number of live births that occur during a specified time interval.

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

Q9buMD.title: Fertility rate
Q9buMD.description: The rate of live births among women of childbearing age (14-44 years) in a population during a specified time interval.

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

j9b_MD.title: Basal keratinocytes
j9b_MD.description: Keratinocytes that are located in the stratum basale of the epidermis. These keratinocytes proliferate, differentiate, and ascend through the layers of the epidermis, then finally undergo senescence to form the stratum corneum. This entire process lasts approximately 2-4 weeks.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Structure of the skin

P9bWnD.title: Copeptin
P9bWnD.description: The c-terminus of the antidiuretic hormone (ADH) precursor protein. Circulating plasma copeptin levels reflect circulating ADH levels. Plasma copeptin is more stable ex vivo than plasma ADH and therefore provides more reliable results.

49b3nD.title: Endocardial fibroelastosis
49b3nD.description: A disorder characterized by diffuse thickening of the left ventricular endocardium from proliferation of fibrous and elastic tissue. Occurs primarily in infants, often with comorbid congenital heart disease.

k9bmnD.title: Transcutaneous pacing
k9bmnD.description: The delivery of electrical current from outside the patient's chest in order to temporarily pace the heart. It is most commonly used for hemodynamically unstable patients with bradycardia.

destinations.label: Management of bradycardia → Temporary cardiac pacing

media.title: Placement of adhesive electrode pads for defibrillation, electrical cardioversion, or transcutaneous pacing

O9bInD.title: Transvenous pacing
O9bInD.description: Temporary pacing of the heart via an electrode that is placed through a venous access site into the right atrium and/or ventricle. It is most commonly used for hemodynamically unstable patients with bradycardia who do not respond to transcutaneous pacing.

destinations.label: Management of bradycardia → Temporary cardiac pacing

l9bvnD.title: Glucagon
l9bvnD.description: A catabolic hormone produced by pancreatic alpha-cells that opposes the effects of insulin and works to increase blood glucose through gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis. It can be used to treat severe hypoglycemia and beta blocker toxicity.

N9b-nD.title: EDS
N9b-nD.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to: 
1. Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
2. Excessive daytime sleepiness.

m9bVLD.title: Lactiferous ducts
m9bVLD.description: 15–20 ducts that drain the lobes of the mammary gland.

media.title: Fine structures of the mammary gland

59biLD.title: Tyrosinase
59biLD.description: A copper-containing, oxidative enzyme that is involved in the production of melanin from tyrosine. A deficiency of tyrosinase is responsible for type 1A oculocutaneous albinism.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Cells of the skin

M9bMLD.title: Oculocutaneous albinism
M9bMLD.description: A group of autosomal recessive disorders characterized by impaired melanin biosynthesis. Patients present at birth with hair, skin, iris, and choroid depigmentation.

n9b7LD.title: Hypomelanosis of Ito
n9b7LD.description: A rare neuroectodermal disorder characterized by the presence of multiple hypopigmented streaks or whorls along Blaschko's lines at birth. Hypomelanosis of Ito is caused by a sporadic mutation in a gene controlling skin pigmentation after fertilization, which results in a form of cutaneous mosaicism. In addition to cutaneous manifestations, patients can also develop mental retardation and seizures.

L9bwLD.title: Nevus depigmentosus
L9bwLD.description: A nevus (birth mark) characterized by the presence of a solitary, hypopigmented lesion with well-defined but serrated borders. Nevus depigmentosus is caused by a sporadic mutation in a clone of melanoblasts during embryonic development.

o9b0oD.title: Analytical studies
o9b0oD.description: A study designed to examine, understand, make inferences about the relationships between variables (e.g., risk factors, exposure, etc.) and outcomes (e.g., disease). Can be experimental (e.g., controlled trials, uncontrolled trials, etc.) or observational (e.g., cohort, case-control, cross-sectional).

K9bUoD.title: Twin concordance study
K9bUoD.description: A study comparing the frequency of a given disease in twins (monozygotic or dizygotic). Usually performed to determine the influence of genetic and environmental risk factors on the development of a disease.

p9bLoD.title: Mechanistic target of rapamycin
p9bLoD.description: An intracytosolic serine/threonine protein kinase that is translated from the mTOR gene on chromosome 1q. The mTOR protein kinase form a part of 2 functional complexes: TORC1, which is involved in cell growth, cell proliferation, and mRNA translation, and TORC2, which is involved in rearrangement of the actin cytoskeletal, cell survival, and cell cycle progression. mTOR inhibitors (e.g., rapamycin, sirolimus) have antineoplastic activity.

J9bsoD.title: Berkson bias
J9bsoD.description: A type of selection bias that results from taking a sample from a subpopulation rather than the general population. The paradigm for clinical studies is sampling a hospital inpatient population, e.g., for respiratory disease. Due to this population's greater exposure to risk factors, e.g., for respiratory disease, the study will show a higher rate of disease than in the general population.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

q9bCoD.title: Non-response bias
q9bCoD.description: A type of selection bias that may occur as a result of high nonresponse rates of participants in telephone or written surveys. This can cause a bias if the nonresponder's characteristics differ significantly from those of the responders.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

I9bYKD.title: Recall bias
I9bYKD.description: A type of information bias that occurs due to study subjects' inaccurate or incomplete recollection of past events/exposure. Can be intentional (e.g., person embarrassed to tell the truth about a sexually transmitted infection) or unintentional (incomplete memory recall). Recall bias is a major issue in retrospective studies that require self-reporting via interviews or questionnaires.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

r9bfKD.title: Malassezia globosa
r9bfKD.description: A yeast that is naturally present on human skin. Can cause tinea versicolor, folliculitis, or seborrheic dermatitis if overgrowth occurs in individuals with factors predisposing to infection (e.g., excessive sweating).

79b4KD.title: Observer bias
79b4KD.description: A type of bias in which the measurement of a variable or classification of subjects (e.g., as cases or noncases) is influenced by the experimenter's knowledge or expectations (e.g., regarding the subjects' exposure status).

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

H9bKKD.title: Confirmation bias
H9bKKD.description: The tendency of an investigator to favor results that support his or her hypothesis or preconceived notions, ignoring other results.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

s9btKD.title: Hawthorne effect
s9btKD.description: The phenomenon that study subjects alter their behavior when they know they are being observed. The effect can significantly affect the validity of a study. Researchers should be discrete with regards to their observations to avoid this effect. A further means of reducing the effect is to extend the timeline of observation to monitor long-term effects.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

t9bX6D.title: Crossover study
t9bX6D.description: A type of clinical study in which each patient switches from the control group to the experimental group during the trial period and serves as their own control. The goal is to obtain an efficient comparison of treatments with fewer patients than in noncrossover studies.

F9bg6D.title: Procedure bias
F9bg6D.description: A type of bias that occurs when the subjects in different study groups are treated unequally because of their affiliation with their respective groups (e.g., subjects who receive one drug are cared for in an intensive care unit while subjects who receive another drug are cared for on a general medicine ward).

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

u9bp6D.title: Type III iodothyronine deiodinase
u9bp6D.description: A type of iodothyronine deiodinase that deiodinates the inner ring of T4 and T3 thereby converting T4 to reverse T3 (rT3), and T3 to T2. Both rT3 and T2 are biologically inactive. Type 3 deiodinase is normally active only in the placenta and the brain.

E9b86D.title: Standard normal value
E9b86D.description: A statistical measure that allows for comparison of populations with different means and standard deviations. Calculated by subtracting the population mean from the value and dividing by the population's standard deviation. Used to express data in terms of units of standard deviation (i.e., how many standard deviations above or below the mean a value is). These values are known as Z-scores.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Distribution and graphical representation of data

v9bA6D.title: Standard error of the mean
v9bA6D.description: A statistical measure of the dispersion of a random sample of means selected from a population that measures the deviation of the sample mean from the population mean. Demonstrates how accurate the estimate of the mean is likely to be. Calculated as the standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size. Influenced by the standard deviation (e.g., a greater SD increases the chance of error) and the sample size (a smaller sample size will increase the chance of error). Used to calculate confidence intervals.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Measures of dispersion

D9b1pD.title: Positively skewed distribution
D9b1pD.description: Asymmetrical distribution of values in a curve that skew to the right, resulting in a longer right tail of the curve. This causes the mean to shift to the right of the peak.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Distribution and graphical representation of data

w9bhpD.title: Negatively skewed distribution
w9bhpD.description: An asymmetrical distribution of values in a curve that skew to the left (toward zero or negative values), resulting in a longer left tail of the curve. This causes the mean to shift to the left of the peak, where it becomes smaller than the median and the mode.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Distribution and graphical representation of data

99bNpD.title: Type II iodothyronine deiodinase
99bNpD.description: A type of iodothyronine deiodinase that deiodinates the outer ring of T4 to convert it to the more potent thyroid hormone T3. Type 2 deiodinase is present primarily within the pituitary gland, thyroid gland, and brown fat.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Function

C9bqpD.title: Pathological nipple discharge
C9bqpD.description: A persistent, unilateral discharge, typically from a single lactiferous duct, that is unrelated to nipple stimulation or expression. Most commonly caused by benign conditions (e.g., intraductal papilloma, mammary duct ectasia) but may also be caused by malignancy.

x9bEpD.title: Physiological nipple discharge
x9bEpD.description: Bilateral breast discharge that is typically milky and originates from multiple ducts. Often occurs after nipple stimulation or expression. Causes include lactation during pregnancy and breastfeeding and galactorrhea resulting from hyperprolactinemia (e.g., adverse effects of medication, repeated nipple stimulation, prolactinoma). Often, the cause cannot be identified (idiopathic galactorrhea).

A9bRJD.title: Statistical power
A9bRJD.description: The probability that a study will detect a true difference, i.e., rejecting the null hypothesis when the alternative hypothesis is true. It is the complement of the probability of making a type II error (Power = 1 - beta).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

_9b5JD.title: Parametric tests
_9b5JD.description: A class of statistical tests and measures used to evaluate statistically significant differences between groups when the study sample has a normal distribution and the sample size is large. Examples include the T test, analysis of variance (ANOVA), and calculation of the Pearson correlation coefficient (r).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

z9brJD.title: Non-parametric tests
z9brJD.description:
A class of statistical tests and measures that used to evaluate the statistically significant difference between groups when the sample has non-normal distribution and the sample size is small. Examples include the 
Mann-Whitney U test, the Wilcoxon test, and calculation of the Spearman correlation coefficient.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

-9bDJD.title: Type I iodothyronine deiodinase
-9bDJD.description: A type of iodothyronine deiodinase that converts non-sulfated T4 to T3 by outer ring deiodination (5'-deiodination) as well as removes rT3, sulfated T3, and sulfated T4 from serum by inner ring deiodination (5-deiodination). Present primarily within the thyroid gland, kidney, and liver.

YCbnqD.title: Hounsfield scale
YCbnqD.description: A scale used to quantify the radiodensity of substances imaged by computed tomography (CT) relative to water (0 Hounsfield units) and air (-1000 Hounsfield units). Clinical applications include evaluation of fat content of the liver and other masses.

eCbxID.title: Basic multicellular unit
eCbxID.description: A collection of osteoclasts that excavates a tunnel in cortical bone. Subsequent osteoblastic activity results in the formation of new bone matrix in the excavated tunnels.

destinations.label: Bone tissue → Bone remodeling and healing

fCbkrD.title: Necrotizing inflammation
fCbkrD.description: Inflammatory reaction that leads to cell necrosis. Seen in, e.g., tuberculosis and granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

SCbyrD.title: Near-total thyroidectomy
SCbyrD.description: A surgical procedure used to treat benign thyroid conditions that affect the entire gland (e.g., large goiter, toxic MNG, Graves' disease). Both lobes are removed; a small cuff of thyroid tissue is left behind to safeguard the recurrent laryngeal nerve and the parathyroid glands, which are in close proximity to the thyroid gland.

hCbc7D.title: Sodium bicarbonate
hCbc7D.description: A chemical compound with a variety of medical uses, including correcting metabolic acidosis, hyperkalemia, and tricyclic antidepressant and aspirin overdose, as well as an antacid (when administered orally). Parenteral formulations vary in concentration depending on the clinical application, e.g., 8.4% NaHCO3 ampules, 1.3% NaHCO3 infusions.

3CbS7D.title: Radiation thyroiditis
3CbS7D.description: A form of acute thyroiditis that occurs a few days after the thyroid gland is exposed to radiation. It is most commonly seen following radioiodine therapy in patients with Graves disease, or following external beam radiotherapy for head and neck cancers. Patients present with pain in the thyroid region and thyrotoxicosis (due to the release of T3 and T4 following rapid destruction of thyroid tissue).

RCbl7D.title: Epitope
RCbl7D.description: The part of an antigen to which an antibody attaches.

iCbJ7D.title: Serum sickness-like reaction
iCbJ7D.description: A reaction to drugs and infections that resembles serum sickness (e.g., fever, rash, arthralgia, lymphadenopathy). Typically occurs 1-2 weeks after exposure.

QCbu7D.title: Adenotonsillectomy
QCbu7D.description: The surgical excision of the adenoids and tonsils. Used to treat chronic or recurrent otitis media, sinusitis, and severe nasal obstruction (e.g., obstructive sleep apnea).

jCb_7D.title: Enflurane
jCb_7D.description: An inhalational anesthetic with medium speed of onset and recovery that is moderately potent. The exact mechanism of action is not known. Lowers the seizure threshold and may cause nausea, malignant hyperthermia, and postoperative shivering.

PCbWHD.title: Class Ic antiarrhythmic agent
PCbWHD.description: A group of antiarrhythmic drugs that act by blocking sodium channels, which inhibits phase 0 depolarization. They mildly increase action potential duration (due to their potassium channel blocking activity) and slow conduction velocity. Examples include flecainide and propafenone.

mCbVsD.title: Wolff-Chaikoff effect
mCbVsD.description: A transient decrease in the production of thyroid hormones following the ingestion of a large amount of iodine. The Wolff-Chaikoff effect lasts for 5–10 days after the ingestion of iodine and is followed by an increase in the synthesis of thyroid hormones.

5CbisD.title: Tetrabenazine
5CbisD.description: A reversible inhibitor of vesicular monamine transporter type 2 (VMAT-2) that decreases synaptic vesicle uptake of monoamines (e.g., dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, histamine), which results in the depletion of catecholamines. Used to treat tardive dyskinesia, Tourette syndrome, and chorea associated with Huntington disease

MCbMsD.title: Pentobarbital
MCbMsD.description: A barbiturate that has sedative, hypnotic, and anticonvulsant properties. Can be used to treat insomnia, as preanesthesia, and as an antiseizure medication.

nCb7sD.title: Secobarbital
nCb7sD.description: A barbiturate that depresses central nervous system activity by binding to GABA receptors. Previously used as a sedative-hypnotic. Now most commonly used as a lethal drug for physician-assisted dying.

LCbwsD.title: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force
LCbwsD.description: An independent, volunteer panel of national experts in prevention and evidence-based medicine. Founded in 1984, the aim of the USPSTF is "to improve the health of all Americans by making evidence-based recommendations about clinical preventive services such as screenings, counseling services, and preventive medications."

oCb0GD.title: Killian's triangle
oCb0GD.description: A triangular region in the muscular wall between the thyropharyngeal and cricopharyngeal parts of the inferior pharyngeal constrictor muscle. Potentially weak gap, through which Zenker's diverticula characteristically occur.

KCbUGD.title: Acid-fast
KCbUGD.description: The ability to resist decolorization by acids after prior staining. Notable acid-fast organisms include all Mycobacteria, Nocardia, and some Coccidia, such as Cryptosporidium parvum.

6CbjGD.title: Hemoglobin casts
6CbjGD.description:
A finding on urine microscopy. Results from degeneration of RBCs within the cast matrix. Cells are no
longer visible, but hemoglobin pigment remains, giving the casts an orange-yellow or red-brown color.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

pCbLGD.title: Plasma cell dyscrasia
pCbLGD.description: A group of conditions characterized by the abnormal proliferation of the same type of (monoclonal) plasma cell that may also secrete a monoclonal immunoglobulin and/or immunoglobulin fragment (e.g., light chain). Includes multiple myeloma, monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS), and Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia.

JCbsGD.title: Seidel test
JCbsGD.description: The topical application of fluorescein dye to the cornea during slit lamp examination to assess for leakage of aqueous humor from the anterior chamber. Displacement of dye by nonfluorescent fluid indicates an open globe injury.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Slit lamp biomicroscopy examination

sCbttD.title: Receptor activator of nuclear factor κB
sCbttD.description: A surface receptor found primarily on osteoclasts. When agonized by RANK ligand (RANKL), a signaling cascade is triggered that causes differentiation and subsequent activation of osteoclasts.

destinations.label: Bone tissue → Bone remodeling and healing

GCbBtD.title: Receptor activator of nuclear factor κB ligand
GCbBtD.description: A membrane protein ligand on osteoblasts that binds to RANK on osteoclasts. Induces differentiation and activation of osteoclasts.

destinations.label: Bone tissue → Bone remodeling and healing

tCbXFD.title: Osteoprotegerin
tCbXFD.description: A glycoprotein that is produced by osteoblasts. It inhibits osteoclast activity because it acts as a decoy receptor for RANK ligands (RANKL) and prevents the binding of RANKL to RANK receptors on osteoclasts.

destinations.label: Bone tissue → Bone remodeling and healing

FCbgFD.title: Macrophage colony-stimulating factor
FCbgFD.description: A  type of cytokine/growth factor that causes hematopoietic stem cells to differentiate into macrophages. Involved in differentiation, proliferation, activation, and maturation of macrophages and monocytic lineage. Also has a role in bone remodeling by activating precursor osteoclasts to undergo further differentiation.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Bone marrow and hematopoiesis

8CbOFD.title: Ergosterol
8CbOFD.description: A cell membrane component unique to fungal species. Key enzymes in its synthetic pathway include squalene epoxidase (inhibited by terbinafine) and 14–α–demethylase (inhibited by azoles), which converts lanosterol to ergosterol.

uCbpFD.title: 7-dehydrocholesterol
uCbpFD.description: A precursor molecule of cholecalciferol (vitamin D3). Converted to cholecalciferol within the epidermis after exposure to ultraviolet B (UVB) light, as with exposure to sunlight.

ECb8FD.title: M protein
ECb8FD.description:
A term that can refer to:
1. A monoclonal immunoglobulin (paraprotein) that is produced in plasma cell dyscrasias (e.g., multiple myeloma, Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance). Detected on serum or urine electrophoresis as a spike in the gamma-globulin zone (monoclonal spike, M spike).
2. A virulence factor of group A streptococci that prevents opsonization by complement factor C3.

CCbq8D.title: Germline
CCbq8D.description: The cells that develop into mature germ cells (gametes), which pass on DNA to progeny.

destinations.label: Basics of embryology → Germ cell development (gametogenesis)

xCbE8D.title: Gamete
xCbE8D.description: A mature germ cell. Fusion of gametes (fertilization) forms a zygote.

destinations.label: Basics of embryology → Germ cell development (gametogenesis)

BCbz8D.title: Oocyte
BCbz8D.description: An immature female germ cell that can undergo oogenesis to become an ovum.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Oogenesis and folliculogenesis

yCbduD.title: Meiosis I
yCbduD.description: The first stage of meiosis, in which cells segregate based on homologous pairs. This produces two haploid cells (i.e., with 23 chromosomes) with sister chromatids.

ACbRuD.title: Meiosis II
ACbRuD.description: The second stage of meiosis in which cells segregate by separation of sister chromatids, which produces haploid cells (i.e. 23 chromosomes in humans) that are genetically distinct from each other and from the parent cell.

_Cb5uD.title: Prophase I
_Cb5uD.description: First stage of meiosis I in which duplicated homologous chromosomes form pairs and crossing-over occurs (genetic recombination).

zCbruD.title: Metaphase I
zCbruD.description: The third phase of meiosis I, in which homologous chromosome pairs align at the equatorial plane.

-CbDuD.title: Anaphase I
-CbDuD.description: The third phase of meiosis I in which chiasmata disintegrate and homologous chromosome pairs separate. In this phase, nondisjunction may occur, leading to trisomy in the offspring.

ZxbZED.title: Telophase I
ZxbZED.description: The last step in meiosis I in which the homologous chromosome pairs complete their migration to the two cell poles and a nuclear membrane forms around each set, resulting in the division of the cell into two cells.

0xbeED.title: Prophase II
0xbeED.description: A step of meiosis II in which the chromosomes condense and the spindle apparatus forms.

axbQED.title: Metaphase II
axbQED.description: A step in meiosis II in which single chromosomes align at the equatorial plane.

YxbnED.title: Anaphase II
YxbnED.description: The third phase of meiosis II, in which the two chromatids of each chromosome are separated at the centromere. In this phase, nondisjunction can occur, which leads to aneuploidy in the offspring.

bxbHED.title: Telophase II
bxbHED.description: The fourth phase of meiosis II, in which the cell membrane pinches in at the equator and the parent cell divides into two haploid cells each with single chromatids.

cxbavD.title: Totipotent
cxbavD.description: The ability of a cell to differentiate into all cell types, including extraembryonic (placental) cells.

1xb2vD.title: Pluripotent
1xb2vD.description: The ability of a cell to differentiate into all cell types, with the exception of extraembryonic cells (e.g., the cells of the ectoderm, which can differentiate into nerve or skin cells but not into other germ layer cells).

2xbTDD.title: Alpha-tocopherol transfer protein
2xbTDD.description: A protein involved in the transport of vitamin E (α-tocopherol). Defects in genes that encode α-TTP result in severe vitamin E deficiency, which can result in ataxia, muscle weakness, and hemolytic anemia.

fxbkDD.title: Parathyroid adenoma
fxbkDD.description: A benign tumor of the parathyroid glands. Typically presents with primary hyperparathyroidism with elevated serum calcium and parathyroid hormone levels.

Txb6DD.title: Crossing over
Txb6DD.description: An exchange of DNA segments between homologous chromosomes, which results in genetic recombination. Occurs during the pachytene stage of prophase I of meiosis.

SxbyDD.title: Thiamine pyrophosphate
SxbyDD.description: A derivative of thiamine (vitamin B1) that serves as a cofactor for enzymes of carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism.

3xbSwD.title: Septo-optic dysplasia
3xbSwD.description: A heterogeneous disorder that can manifest with optic nerve hypoplasia, pituitary hypoplasia, and abnormal development of midline structures that separate the right and left halves of the brain (e.g., corpus callosum).

RxblwD.title: Flavin mononucleotide
RxblwD.description: A vitamin B2 derivative that serves as a cofactor for several enzymes that carry out redox reactions (e.g., L-amino acid oxidase, NADH reductase)

ixbJwD.title: Flavin adenine dinucleotide
ixbJwD.description: A derivative of riboflavin (vitamin B2) that serves as an electron carrier in redox reactions.

QxbuwD.title: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide
QxbuwD.description: A molecule that serves as an electron carrier in redox reactions, especially in catabolic cellular processes. The reduced form is NADH; the oxidized form is NAD⁺.

jxb_wD.title: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate
jxb_wD.description: A molecule that provides electrons for anabolic reactions and oxidation-reduction reactions. Also used in the respiratory burst, the cytochrome P450 system, and by glutathione reductase. Primarily produced via the hexose monophosphate pathway. Reduced form is NADPH; oxidized form is NADP⁺.

PxbW9D.title: Coenzyme A
PxbW9D.description: A coenzyme derived from Vitamin B5 (pantothenate) that serves as a cofactor for acyl transfers. Plays a key role in the metabolism of fatty acids.

4xb39D.title: Epigenetics
4xb39D.description: The study of the inheritable chemical alterations of DNA and histone proteins caused by environmental factors, which affect genetic activity.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Epigenetic regulation of gene expression

kxbm9D.title: Hemoconcentration
kxbm9D.description: An increase in red blood cell concentration and other constituents of the blood, such as electrolytes, as a result of plasma volume loss (e.g., from dehydration).

OxbI9D.title: Pyridoxal phosphate
OxbI9D.description: The active form of vitamin B6. Serves as a coenzyme in decarboxylation, deamination, and racemization reactions of amino acids.

lxbv9D.title: Polystyrene sulfonate
lxbv9D.description: A cation-exchange resin that binds potassium in the gut via the exchange of Na+ for K+. Effect takes several hours. A rare but severe adverse effect is intestinal necrosis.

Nxb-9D.title: 17,20-lyase
Nxb-9D.description: An enzyme that converts 17-OH pregnenolone into dehydroepiandrosterone and 17-OH progesterone into androstenedione. Encoded by the CYP17A1 gene on chromosome 10q and produced predominantly in the adrenal cortex and gonads. Inhibited by ketoconazole and spironolactone.

mxbVCD.title: 3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase
mxbVCD.description: An enzyme that converts pregnenolone into progesterone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone into 17- hydroxyprogesterone, dehydroepiandrosterone into androstenedione, and androstenedione into testosterone. There are two isoforms of the enzyme: type 1 is found in placental tissue; type 2 is found in the adrenal gland and gonads.

5xbiCD.title: 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase
5xbiCD.description: An enzyme that converts dihydroepiandrosterone into androstenediol, androstenedione into testosterone, and estrone into estradiol. 14 isoforms of this enzyme exist. Some have tissue specific expression: (e.g., isoform 1 in placenta, isoform 2 in the GI tract, isoform 3 in the testes) but most are found in all tissues.

destinations.label: Differences (disorders) of sex development → 17β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3 deficiency​

MxbMCD.title: Sickle cell trait
MxbMCD.description: A condition in which one allele of the β globin gene carries the sickle hemoglobin mutation while the other allele is normal, producing hemoglobin AS (HbAS). Most often asymptomatic but can cause painless hematuria. Symptoms of sickle cell disease may rarely occur as a result of severe oxygen deficiency.

nxb7CD.title: Infarction
nxb7CD.description: A condition of tissue necrosis that results from insufficient blood and oxygen supply to the affected region. Etiologies include thromboembolic occlusion, rupture, vasoconstriction, and vessel compression.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Necrosis

LxbwCD.title: Mirabegron
LxbwCD.description: A selective beta-3 agonist used in the treatment of overactive bladder, including urgency urinary incontinence. Stimulates beta-3 adrenergic receptors of the detrusor smooth muscle, relaxing the muscle and increasing bladder capacity for urine.

destinations.label: Overactive bladder and urgency urinary incontinence → Treatment

6xbjxD.title: Zygote
6xbjxD.description: A developmental stage that occurs after a fertilized oocyte completes meiosis. During this stage, maternal and paternal chromosomes align on the metaphase plate and embryonic development begins.

pxbLxD.title: Ulnar nerve
pxbLxD.description: An upper limb nerve that arises from the medial cord of the brachial plexus (nerve roots: C8, T1). Within the forearm, it innervates the flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial half of the flexor digitorum profundus. Within the hand, it innervates the  palmaris brevis, adductor pollicis, the interosseous muscles, the hypothenar muscles, and the skin on the medial side of the hand (including the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger).

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

qxbCxD.title: Carpal tunnel
qxbCxD.description: A narrow passage on the ventral portion of the wrist through which the median nerve and several tendons from the flexor group of forearm muscles pass (i.e., flexor pollicis longus, flexor digitorum superficialis, and flexor digitorum profundus). The tunnel is bounded by wrist bones, and the roof is formed by the flexor retinaculum. Further narrowing or compression of the carpal tunnel results in carpal tunnel syndrome.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

media.title: Cross-section of wrist showing the carpal tunnel and Guyon canal

IxbYBD.title: Median nerve
IxbYBD.description: An upper limb nerve that derives from the medial and lateral cords of the brachial plexus (nerve roots: C5/6–T1). Within the forearm, it innervates all the muscles of the flexor compartment except the flexor carpi ulnaris and medial half of the flexor digitorum profundus. Within the hand, it innervates the thenar muscles, the lateral two lumbricals, and the skin overlying the lateral portion of the palm.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

rxbfBD.title: Anterior interosseous nerve
rxbfBD.description: A pure motor branch of the median nerve in the forearm that innervates the pronator quadratus, flexor pollicis longus, and the lateral portion of the flexor digitorum profundus.

sxbtBD.title: Pronator teres syndrome
sxbtBD.description: A rare compression neuropathy caused by compression of the median nerve between the humeral and ulnar heads of the pronator teres. Archers, tennis players, and body builders are more commonly affected. Symptoms include pain in the ventral aspect of the proximal forearm and paresthesia in the median nerve territory of the hand (i.e., the thumb, index finger, middle finger, and radial aspect of the ring finger).

destinations.label: Peripheral nerve injuries → Nerve injuries in the upper body

txbXyD.title: Pronator teres
txbXyD.description: A muscle in the superficial anterior compartment of the forearm that pronates and flexes the forearm. It originates from the medial epicondyle of the humerus as well as coronoid process of the ulna, and inserts into the lateral side of the middle third of the radius. It is innervated by the anterior interosseus nerve, a branch of the median nerve.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

8xbOyD.title: Cervical rib
8xbOyD.description: An extra rib that arises from the 7th cervical vertebra. Usually asymptomatic but can compress the lower trunk of the brachial plexus (C8-T1) and/or subclavian vessels, which can lead to thoracic outlet syndrome.

Exb8yD.title: Quadrilateral space syndrome
Exb8yD.description: Compression of the axillary nerve and posterior humeral circumflex artery within the quadrangular space, which is located inferior and posterior to the glenohumeral joint. Typically occurs in young athletic males as a result of fibrous bands or degenerative paralabral cysts and presents with paresthesias over the lateral and posterior surface of the shoulder that are worsened by active abduction and external rotation of the arm against resistance.

vxbAyD.title: Quadrilateral space
vxbAyD.description: A quadrilateral anatomical space that contains the axillary nerve and the posterior humeral circumflex artery. Located posterior and inferior to the glenohumeral joint. Bounded superiorly by the teres minor, inferiorly by the teres major, medially by the long head of the triceps, and laterally by the humeral shaft.

media.title: Visual mnemonic: Axillary spaces and their borders

Dxb1AD.title: Musculospiral groove
Dxb1AD.description: A shallow, oblique depression that is located on the posterolateral surface of the humeral shaft in between the origins of the medial head of the triceps and the lateral head of the triceps. The radial nerve and deep brachial artery lie within this groove.

wxbhAD.title: Morula
wxbhAD.description: An embryo consisting of a ball of totipotent cells that are produced from a zygote (fertilized cell) after three days. Appearance resembles a mulberry.

media.title: Overview of the 1st week of pregnancy and embryogenesis

9xbNAD.title: Blastocyst
9xbNAD.description: A thin-walled, fluid-filled structure with a cluster of cells at one pole that is formed 5 days after fertilization. The cellular cluster (inner cell mass) gives rise to the embryo. The wall of the blastocyst (trophoblast) will form the placenta and fetal membranes.

CxbqAD.title: Posterior interosseous nerve
CxbqAD.description: A motor branch of the radial nerve that arises near the lateral epicondyle and innervates all muscles of the posterior compartment of the forearm except for the long head of the extensor carpi radialis (which is directly innervated by the radial nerve).

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

xxbEAD.title: Preimplantation genetic testing
xxbEAD.description: The use of genetic testing to assess an embryo for aneuploidy, sex, monogenic disorders, and/or structural chromosomal abnormalities. DNA is typically obtained from trophectoderm cells 5 or 6 days after fertilization and assessed with comparative genomic hybridization or next-generation sequencing.

BxbzAD.title: Supinator muscle
BxbzAD.description: A muscle of the deep posterior compartment of the forearm that originates from the posterolateral surface of the proximal ulna as well as the lateral epicondyle and inserts into the lateral surface of the proximal radius. It is innervated by the deep branch of the radial nerve (posterior interosseous nerve), and is responsible for supination of the forearm.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

yxbd_D.title: Radial tunnel
yxbd_D.description: An anatomical space in the lateral aspect of the elbow that extends from the radial head to the distal margin of supinator muscle. It is bounded laterally by the extensor carpi radialis longus, extensor carpi radialis brevis, and brachioradialis (mobile wad group of muscles), medially by the brachialis and biceps tendons. The roof is formed by the superficial head of the supinator muscle while the floor is formed by the radiocapitellar joint capsule and the deep head of the supinator.
