This space contains the posterior interosseous nerve.

_xb5_D.title: Syncytiotrophoblast
_xb5_D.description: The outer layer of cells that covers the chorionic villi of the placenta and actively invades the uterine endometrium. These cells are therefore in direct contact with maternal blood and uterine decidua. Syncytiotrophoblasts secrete human chorionic gonadotropin, human placental lactogen, progesterone, and leptin.

zxbr_D.title: Cytotrophoblast
zxbr_D.description: The fetal part of the placenta that forms the inner layer of chorionic villi. Located between the syncytiotrophoblast and embryoblast. Cytotrophoblasts are stem cells (which undergo mitosis, as opposed to syncytiotrophoblasts) and remain highly proliferative throughout pregnancy. Important component of the process of blastocyst implantation inside the uterine cavity.

-xbD_D.title: Tetrahydrofolic acid
-xbD_D.description: A folate derivative produced by the action of the dihydrofolate reductase on dihydrofolic acid. Serves as a cofactor in amino acid and nucleic acid synthesis.

ZBbZzD.title: Plantar flexor
ZBbZzD.description: A muscle that causes flexion of the ankle, pressing the foot down toward the sole (e.g., pressing down on a gas pedal or standing on tip toes). The strongest flexor of the ankle is the triceps surae muscle.

media.title: Anatomical overview of superficial flexors (lower leg)
Actions of the deep flexor muscles of the leg
Schematic overview of superficial flexors (lower leg)
Deep flexor group of muscles of the leg

0BbezD.title: Cauda equina
0BbezD.description: A bundle of lumbosacral nerve roots that originate in the conus medullaris at the distal end of the spinal cord, located around L1-L2. Compression results in cauda equina syndrome.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

media.title: Conus medullaris and cauda equina syndromes

aBbQzD.title: Adductor pollicis muscle
aBbQzD.description: A muscle of the thenar eminence that is typically innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve and responsible for adduction of the thumb. The muscle originates from the capitate as well as second and third metacarpals and inserts into the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

YBbnzD.title: Lumbrical
YBbnzD.description: A set of muscles that extend the digits. The lumbricals of the hand are innervated by the median and ulnar nerves are facilitate metacarpophalangeal joint flexion and interphalangeal joint extension. The lumbricals of the feet are innervated by the medial and lateral plantar nerves and facilitate metatarsophalangeal joint flexion and interphalangeal joint extension.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

bBbHzD.title: Nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio
bBbHzD.description: The ratio of the size of the nucleus to the size of the cytoplasm of a cell. Indicates relative maturity of a cell, with more mature cells typically having decreased ratios. An increased N:C ratio is typically associated with dysplastic changes and/or malignancy.

cBba-D.title: Mid-inguinal point
cBba-D.description: Mid-point of a line drawn from the anterior superior iliac spine to the top of the pubic symphysis.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Arteries
Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Vascular supply of the thigh

VBbG-D.title: Skin biopsy
VBbG-D.description: The removal of a sample of skin tissue for histopathological evaluation. A common diagnostic procedure in dermatology (e.g., to diagnose tumors or skin infections).

fBbkZw.title: Skin culture
fBbkZw.description: A laboratory test to identify pathogens that cause infection of the skin and to determine the treatment that will effectively treat the pathogen. Requires a sample of skin, which is usually obtained by skin swap, scraping, or biopsy. Culture of pathogens on special culture plates that promote growth may take up to several weeks.

gBbFZw.title: Epiphysis
gBbFZw.description: The end of a long bone. Functions as the secondary ossification center during bone growth.

SBbyZw.title: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
SBbyZw.description: Manifestations of unopposed osteoclast activation in patients with severe hyperparathyroidism. Features include bone pain, subperiosteal bone resorption, and/or bone cysts. Multiple bone cysts in the skull can cause a "pepper-pot" appearance on x-ray. In advanced OFC, large, cystic, vascular cavities with a tumor-like appearance on x-ray and a brown color due to hemosiderin deposition ("brown tumors") can form in long bones.

OBbIaw.title: Carbon tetrachloride
OBbIaw.description: A toxic halogenated hydrocarbon that causes neurotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and cardiotoxicity via free radical damage.

nBb7Yw.title: Gastric antral vascular ectasia
nBb7Yw.description: Dilation of small blood vessels in the antrum of the stomach that can lead to gastrointestinal bleeding. The dilated vessels appear on endoscopy as long stripes resembling those on the surface of a watermelon. Common causes include collagen vascular diseases and portal hypertension.

oBb0bw.title: Embryogenesis
oBb0bw.description: The process by which the embryo develops during the first eight weeks after fertilization. During this period, most of the major organ systems form.

KBbUbw.title: Gastrulation
KBbUbw.description: The formation of the trilaminar embryonic disc (endoderm, mesoderm, ectoderm) through the migration of epiblast cells.

6Bbjbw.title: Notochord
6Bbjbw.description: A dorsal midline structure derived from mesoderm that arises during the 3rd week of gestation (trilaminar disc). It secretes sonic hedgehog (SHH), a signaling protein that activates cellular differentiation and neurulation. It forms the nucleus pulposus of intervertebral discs.

pBbLbw.title: Neurulation
pBbLbw.description: The process by which the neural plate folds to form the neural tube. This process generally begins during the third week of embryonic development.

qBbCbw.title: Bladder catheterization
qBbCbw.description: The placement of a catheter into the bladder either through the urethra (transurethral) or suprapubically. The most common indication for bladder catheterization is drainage of urine (e.g., in urinary retention, for urinary output monitoring, and supportive management of immobilized patients). Can also be used for instillation of drugs into the bladder (e.g., BCG instillation in bladder cancer) or to irrigate the bladder with saline (e.g., in massive hematuria with clots).

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Urinary drainage procedures

IBbYXw.title: Bypass surgery
IBbYXw.description: A procedure in which an obstructed segment of an artery or vein is bypassed to restore circulation using either an autologous vein graft or a prosthetic, mostly polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) or polyester (Dacron), graft. Examples of bypass surgeries include femoro-popliteal, aorto-iliac, aorto-femoral, or femoro-femoral bypass for peripheral arterial disease; coronary artery bypass grafting for coronary artery disease.

media.title: Vessels commonly used in coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG)
Arterial and venous grafts used in coronary artery bypass grafting
Overview of peripheral artery bypass surgeries

rBbfXw.title: Epiblast
rBbfXw.description: A part of the bilaminar disc that consists of columnar cells adjacent to amnioblasts. Forms the embryo by undergoing gastrulation (3rd week of embryogenesis).

7Bb4Xw.title: Hypoblast
7Bb4Xw.description: A part of the bilaminar disc that consists of cuboidal cells adjacent to the blastocyst cavity. Forms the yolk sac.

HBbKXw.title: Yolk sac
HBbKXw.description: An extra-embryonic membranous sac derived from endoderm and lined by mesenchyme derived from mesoderm. Connects to the embryo via a yolk stalk. Involved in blood supply to the embryo.

GBbBXw.title: Extraembryonic coelom
GBbBXw.description: A precursor of the gestational sac formed between the somatopleuric and splanchnopleuric layers of extraembryonic mesoderm during embryonic development. Precursor of the gestational sac.

tBbXcw.title: Primitive streak
tBbXcw.description: An elongated accumulation of epiblast cells that are the origin of gastrulation.

8BbOcw.title: Postmyocardial infarction syndrome
8BbOcw.description: An acute pericarditis that occurs 2–10 weeks after myocardial infarction. Postmyocardial infarction syndrome likely occurs because neo-antigens released from the injured myocardium combine with antibodies to form immune complexes, which elicit an inflammatory response.

media.title: Timeline of most common post myocardial infarction complications

uBbpcw.title: Early infarct-associated pericarditis
uBbpcw.description: An acute pericarditis that occurs 1–3 days after a transmural myocardial infarction due to irritation of the pericardium by the underlying infarct.

media.title: Timeline of most common post myocardial infarction complications

EBb8cw.title: Ketotifen
EBb8cw.description: A second-generation H1-antihistamine that also blocks the release of histamine from mast cells. Used in the form of eye drops to treat allergic conjunctivitis.

DBb11w.title: Fluorometholone
DBb11w.description: A low-potency glucocorticoid that is used in the form of eye drops to treat inflammatory conditions of the eye (e.g., allergic conjunctivitis).

wBbh1w.title: Paromomycin
wBbh1w.description: A drug related to the aminoglycoside family of antibiotics. Because oral paromomycin is not significantly absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract, it is used as a luminal antibiotic in the treatment of hepatic encephalopathy and as a luminal amebicide (by eradicating intestinal cysts).

9BbN1w.title: Expansile cough impulse
9BbN1w.description: A clinical sign used in the evaluation of a hernia. Considered positive if the hernia expands upon coughing, which increases intra-abdominal pressure and pushes the hernial content through the hernial orifice.

xBbE1w.title: Primitive pit
xBbE1w.description: A thickened portion at the anterior end of the primitive streak that gives inductive signals during early development.

BBbz1w.title: Trilaminar embryonic disc
BBbz1w.description: A three-layered embryonic structure that develops in the 3rd-4th week of development. Consists of endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm. Formed via gastrulation through the migration of epiblast cells from the primitive streak.

yBbdWw.title: Neural plate
yBbdWw.description: A region of medial ectoderm that has differentiated into neural cells in response to signaling from the notochord.

_Bb5Ww.title: Primary thyroid lymphoma
_Bb5Ww.description: A group of rare, extranodal lymphomas that arise in the thyroid. Almost all primary thyroid lymphomas are non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphomas. Typically manifests as a rapidly growing goiter in patients with chronic Hashimoto thyroiditis.

zBbrWw.title: Drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia
zBbrWw.description: Destruction of platelets by antibodies produced against certain drugs. These drugs include heparin (type 2 heparin-induced thrombocytopenia), quinine, abciximab, carbamazepine, sulfonamide drugs, and certain antibiotics (e.g., vancomycin).

-BbDWw.title: Drug-induced pemphigus
-BbDWw.description: Separation of the epidermis from the dermis as a result of drug-induced damage to desmoglein. The damage is typically cause by a drug-induced type 2 hypersensitivity reaction but certain thiol-group-containing drugs (e.g., penicillamine, captopril, enalapril) can damage desmoglein directly. Drug-induced pemphigus caused by non-thiol drugs typically presents with features of pemphigus vulgaris (flaccid blisters with mucosal involvement) while thiol-drugs usually present with features of pemphigus foliaceus (red, scaly, skin crusts without mucosal involvement).

ZybZdw.title: Antihypertensive therapy
ZybZdw.description: A treatment used to control high blood pressure. Includes nonpharmacologic measures including smoking cessation, dietary changes, weight loss, and exercise, as well as pharmacologic treatment, including ACE inhibitors, angiotensin-receptor blockers, diuretics, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, alpha blockers, and vasodilators.

0ybedw.title: Platelet aggregation
0ybedw.description: A part of the hemostatic mechanism of platelets involved in repairing injuries to the vascular endothelium. After cross-linking with fibrinogen, platelets form large aggregates at the site of initial platelet activation and are ultimately stabilized by a cross-linked fibrin clot.

aybQdw.title: Pentoxifylline
aybQdw.description: A nonspecific phosphodiesterase inhibitor that increases blood flow to the microcirculation. Thought to lower blood viscosity and increase red blood cell flexibility. Used to treat Peyronie disease and calciphylaxis.

Yybndw.title: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
Yybndw.description: A severe cutaneous adverse reaction to a specific drug, believed to be caused by T-cell mediated hypersensitivity. Typically, this reaction is characterized by the appearance of hundreds of nonfollicular sterile pustules in the intertriginous areas within 2-5 days (rarely up to 12 days) of drug exposure. The most commonly implicated drugs are aminopenicillins, quinolones, sulfonamides, pristinamycin, terbinafine, quinine derivatives (e.g., hydroxychloroquine), oxicam NSAIDS (e.g., peroxicam), and diltiazem.

bybHdw.title: Bradykinin
bybHdw.description: An inflammatory mediator that causes increased vascular permeability, vascular dilation, bronchoconstriction, and pain.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Acute local inflammation

Xyb9dw.title: Ejection fraction
Xyb9dw.description: The percentage of blood pumped by the left ventricle during each contraction (i.e., stroke volume divided by end diastolic volume). Normally ∼ 55%. The term may also rarely be used to describe the blood pumped from the right ventricle.

cybaVw.title: Anti-GBM antibodies
cybaVw.description: Antibodies that are directed against a type IV collagen antigen intrinsic to the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), which result in acute or rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, often associated with pulmonary hemorrhage (Goodpasture syndrome).

WybPVw.title: Barton fracture
WybPVw.description: An intra-articular fracture of the distal radius with associated dorsal displacement.

dyboVw.title: Hutchinson fracture
dyboVw.description: A fracture of the radial styloid process. Typically caused by direct trauma to the back of the wrist or forced dorsiflexion and abduction.

VybGVw.title: Lung abscess
VybGVw.description: A localized collection of pus and necrotic tissue within lung parenchyma caused by microbial infection (e.g., with Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes). Common causes include aspiration of oropharyngeal contents, pneumonia, immunocompromise, or bronchial obstruction (e.g., lung cancer). Clinical features include fever and a cough productive of foul-smelling sputum.

eybxVw.title: Thrombosis
eybxVw.description: The formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel. Can dislodge and obstruct another site of circulation as an embolic thrombosis.

Uybbew.title: Effect modification
Uybbew.description: A phenomenon in which an internal factor modifies the effect of a risk factor on the outcome of interest. If the outcome (e.g., the incidence of a disease) is greater than expected, the interaction is synergistic (positive interaction). If the outcome is less than expected, the interaction is antagonistic (negative interaction). Effect modification is not a bias.

2ybTew.title: Generalizability
2ybTew.description: The applicability of study results to populations other than the target population from which the sample population is drawn.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Precision and validity

fybkew.title: Stratified sampling
fybkew.description: A method of study design in which the population of interest is divided into subpopulations before participants are enrolled in the study, and participants are recruited from each of the subpopulations rather than from the entire population of interest. This renders the study population more representative of the target population.

Sybyew.title: Neural tube
Sybyew.description: A hollow structure formed by invagination of the neuroectoderm (neurulation). Gives rise to neurons and glial cells of the brain, spinal cord, retina, and posterior pituitary.

hybcUw.title: Neuropore
hybcUw.description: The cranial and caudal openings of the neural tube, which communicate with the amniotic cavity. Closes around day 24-27 of embryological development.

3ybSUw.title: Surface ectoderm
3ybSUw.description: A germ layer derived from ectoderm. Gives rise to the epidermis, hair, nails, inner ear, external ear, enamel of teeth, lens of the eyes, anterior pituitary, parotid gland, and anal canal (below the pectinate line).

RyblUw.title: Neural crest cell
RyblUw.description: A type of cell derived from the neural plate, which itself derives from neuroectoderm. These cells give rise to the adrenal medulla, pigment cells, Schwann cells, meninges (pia and arachnoid mater), pharyngeal arch cartilage, odontoblast, aorticopulmonary septum, endocardial cushions, and cranial bones.

iybJUw.title: Bilaminar disc
iybJUw.description: An embryonic structure derived from the embryoblast around the 2nd week of embryogenesis. Consists of two layers: the epiblast and hypoblast, which lie between the amniotic cavity and the yolk sac.

QybuUw.title: Craniocaudal folding
QybuUw.description: A process that occurs during embryologic development in which the cranial and caudal embryonic poles curl, which leads to curving of the germinal disc.

PybW2w.title: Blastocoel
PybW2w.description: A fluid-filled cavity that forms in a blastula. Lined by cuboidal hypoblast cells. Forms the yolk sac and lining of the chorionic cavity.

4yb32w.title: Buccopharyngeal membrane
4yb32w.description: region without mesoderm at the cranial embryonic pole.

kybm2w.title: Cloacal membrane
kybm2w.description: region without mesoderm at the caudal embryonic pole.

OybI2w.title: Opening snap
OybI2w.description: A high-frequency, early-to-mid diastolic sound that can be heard in patients with mitral or tricuspid stenosis. An opening snap occurs because the mitral or tricuspid valve leaflets cannot open fully and blood that is attempting to flow into the ventricle collides with a partially opened valve.

lybv2w.title: Microstomia
lybv2w.description: A disproportionately small mouth. A finding in systemic sclerosis and several congenital syndromes with craniofacial abnormalities, including trisomy 18.

Nyb-2w.title: Dysphagia megalatriensis
Nyb-2w.description: A type of cardiac dysphagia which is caused by compression of the esophagus by a giant left atrium. The most common causes are mitral stenosis due to rheumatic heart disease and a left atrial myxoma.

mybVfw.title: Cardiac dysphagia
mybVfw.description: A group of cardiovascular anomalies that cause dysphagia due to compression of the esophagus. Includes vascular ring anomalies (e.g., double aortic arch), dysphagia lusoria (abnormal right subvlavian artery), severe atherosclerosis, and aneurysms.

MybMfw.title: Ranibizumab
MybMfw.description: Humanized monoclonal antibody fragment that inhibits vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) and thereby prevents the growth of new blood vessels. Used for treatment of wet age-related macular degeneration and proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

nyb7fw.title: Axial mesoderm
nyb7fw.description: The central region of the mesoderm, forms the notochord and the prechordal mesoderm.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

Lybwfw.title: Paraxial mesoderm
Lybwfw.description: An area of mesoderm located on the sides of the neural tube. Divides into somite pairs.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

oyb0Tw.title: Somite
oyb0Tw.description: A group of paired, segmented, round cell clusters of embryonic development that are involved in the segmentation of vertebrae.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

6ybjTw.title: Sclerotome
6ybjTw.description: The subdivision of a somite that develops into skeletal tissue within vertebrates.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

pybLTw.title: Dermomyotome
pybLTw.description: The subdivision of a somite that develops into the dermatomes and myotomes within vertebrates.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

JybsTw.title: Intermediate mesoderm
JybsTw.description: Located lateral to the paraxial mesoderm, is composed of the urogenital fold, consisting of the nephrogenic ridge and genital ridge.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

IybYgw.title: Lateral plate mesoderm
IybYgw.description: Located lateral to the intermediate mesoderm. Develops into the somatopleuric mesoderm and the splanchnopleuric mesoderm.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

7yb4gw.title: Ectoderm
7yb4gw.description: The outermost layer of the 3 primary germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm) formed during gastrulation on the 3rd week of embryonic development. Gives rise to surface ectoderm, neuroectoderm, and neural crest cell ectoderm.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

sybtgw.title: Endoderm
sybtgw.description: The innermost layer of the 3 primary germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm) formed during gastrulation on the 3rd week of embryonic development. Gives rise to the epithelial lining of the gastrointestinal tract, lower respiratory tract, genitourinary tract, and forms the parenchyma of the liver, pancreas, submandibular and sublingual gland, and follicles of the thyroid gland.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

GybBgw.title: Luteinizing hormone/choriogonadotropin receptor
GybBgw.description: A G protein-coupled receptor that is coded for by the LHCGR gene on chromosome 2p. The receptor, which is primarily expressed in the gonads, adipose tissue, adrenal glands, thyroid glands, and esophagus, binds to both luteinizing hormone and human chorionic gonadotropin. LHCGR gene mutations that intrinsically activate this protein cause testotoxicosis and Leydig cell adenomas, while mutations that deactivate this receptor cause hypogonadism and Leydig cell hypoplasia.

tybXSw.title: Human placental lactogen
tybXSw.description: A hormone synthesized by syncytiotrophoblasts of the placenta. It promotes growth and differentiation of the breast tissue, production of insulin-like growth factors and erythropoietin in the fetus, fetal angiogenesis, as well as maternal insulin resistance.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac →  Placental function

FybgSw.title: Inhibin
FybgSw.description: A protein that inhibits the production of FSH. In females, inhibin is produced predominantly by the granulosa cells of the ovaries, placenta, or corpus luteum; in males, it is produced by Sertoli cells. There are 2 isoforms of inhibin: inhibin A and inhibin B.

destinations.label: Cytokines and eicosanoids → Transforming growth factor family

8ybOSw.title: Sulfosalicylic acid test
8ybOSw.description: A test in which sulfosalicylic acid is added to urine to measure urine proteins. In contrast to a urine dipstick test, it is not specific for albumin.

uybpSw.title: Human chorionic gonadotropin
uybpSw.description: A hormone produced by the placenta after implantation. Its β subunit is measured to detect pregnancy. Also measured as a tumor marker in seminomas, choriocarcinomas, germ cell tumors, hydatidiform moles, and teratomas.

Eyb8Sw.title: C1 esterase inhibitor
Eyb8Sw.description: An enzyme that inactivates proteases involved in the complement cascade (C1r, C1s, and MASP), kallikrein, and coagulation factors XIa and XIIa. A deficiency of C1 esterase inhibitor results in hereditary angioedema.

vybASw.title: Stomodeum
vybASw.description: forms during embryonic development as a result of deep depression by the buccopharyngeal membrane due to expansion of the brain.

Dyb1hw.title: Proctodeum
Dyb1hw.description: Structure derived from ectodermal tissue that is located at the caudal end of the embryo and develops into the anal canal.

yybd3w.title: Inferential statistics
yybd3w.description: An analysis of a sample group that is performed to make inferences that go beyond the sample group (e.g., analysis of prevalence of a disease in a specific population to draw conclusions about the prevalence of the disease in the general population).

AybR3w.title: Vinorelbine
AybR3w.description: An antineoplastic drug that belongs to the class of vinca alkaloids. Used in the treatment of certain types of breast cancer and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It works by binding tubulin in microtubules, which causes inhibition of mitosis. Important adverse effects include neutropenia and neurotoxicity.

_yb53w.title: Lichen simplex chronicus
_yb53w.description: A benign skin condition characterized by lichenified plaques with excoriations and moderate to intense pruritus that leads to persistent rubbing and/or scratching to provide symptom relief. Results from habitual behavior (e.g., scratching in response to stress) or is a manifestation of chronic eczematous inflammation.

zybr3w.title: Phenacetin
zybr3w.description: An analgesic banned by the United States Food and Drug Administration in 1983 after studies showed that the use of this drug increased the risk of urothelial carcinoma, particularly of the renal pelvis.

0AbeRw.title: Data (epidemiology)
0AbeRw.description: The information collected during observation and/or experimentation (e.g., via questionnaires, medical records, medical devices, laboratory tests) that is used as a basis for analysis and discussion.

aAbQRw.title: Sample (epidemiology)
aAbQRw.description: A group of people that is representative of a larger population that is being studied. Sampling allows researchers to infer information about a population based on results from a subset of that population.

YAbnRw.title: Cumulative incidence
YAbnRw.description: The proportion of a population that newly develops a given outcome (e.g., a disease) over a specified period of time. Calculated by dividing the number of new cases in a given time period by the number of people at risk in that time period. In descriptive studies (e.g., of population health) the terms cumulative incidence or incidence proportion are used. In outbreak settings, the term attack rate is used. In analytical epidemiology, the term absolute risk (AR) is commonly used (e.g., AR in the control group, AR in the treatment group).

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency
Interpreting medical evidence → Measures of association

bAbHRw.title: Rate (epidemiology)
bAbHRw.description: A measure of the frequency of an event in a population over a specific period of time. The denominator includes a measure of time. Rates are usually reported as 1,000 or 100,000 cases per unit of time.

XAb9Rw.title: Ratios
XAb9Rw.description: A comparison of the magnitude of one value compared to the magnitude of another value.

cAbaiw.title: Proportion
cAbaiw.description: A ratio that compares one part of the population to the whole. Typically expressed as a percentage.

1Ab2iw.title: EGFR inhibitors
1Ab2iw.description: A group of chemotherapeutic drugs (e.g., cetuximab, gefitinib, erlotinib) that bind and block epidermal growth factor receptor. Inhibits cell growth in tumors that overexpress of EGFR (e.g., non-small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer). A common adverse effect is an acneiform rash.

WAbPiw.title: Gefitinib
WAbPiw.description: An antineoplastic drug that belongs to the class of EGFR inhibitors, which inhibit the activity of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Used to treat cases of advanced-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that are EGFR-positive.

dAboiw.title: Cardiac index
dAboiw.description: The measure of the volume of blood ejected from the heart (cardiac output, L/min) in relation to body surface area (m²). Normal range at rest is 2.8–4.2 L/min/m².

VAbGiw.title: Flexor carpi ulnaris
VAbGiw.description: A muscle in the superficial anterior compartment of the forearm that originates from the medial epicondyle as well as olecranon process, and inserts into the pisiform, hamate, and base of the fifth metacarpal. It is innervated by the ulnar nerve. The flexor carpi ulnaris primarily adducts the wrist, but in conjunction with the flexor carpi radialis, it causes wrist flexion.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

eAbxiw.title: Subtotal thyroidectomy
eAbxiw.description: A subtotal resection of the thyroid gland that preserves a posterior rim of thyroid tissue to minimize injury to the adjacent laryngeal nerves and parathyroid glands. The amount of thyroid tissue preserved is more than that of near-total thyroidectomy and ideally circumvents the need for lifelong thyroid hormone replacement postoperatively.

UAbbQw.title: ALK inhibitors
UAbbQw.description: A group of chemotherapeutic drugs (e.g, crizotinib, alectinib) that bind and block anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK). Used to treat ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancers.

2AbTQw.title: Crizotinib
2AbTQw.description: An antineoplastic drug that belongs to the class of tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Blocks the activity of the tyrosine kinases ALK, ROS1, and MET. Used to treat ALK-positive, advanced-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and ROS1-positive, metastatic NSCLC.

TAb6Qw.title: Attrition bias
TAb6Qw.description: A type of selection bias in which selective loss to follow-up of participants has a significant impact on the characteristics of a study population, which causes the association between variables to be overestimated or underestimated.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

gAbFQw.title: Axillary nerve
gAbFQw.description: An upper limb nerve that is a direct continuation of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus (nerve roots: C5 and C6). It innervates the deltoid muscles, teres minor, and skin overlying the deltoid muscle.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

SAbyQw.title: Respondent bias
SAbyQw.description: A type of information bias that occurs when exposure or outcomes are subjectively reported by individuals rather than measured by an objective test.

hAbcjw.title: Ectopic ACTH production
hAbcjw.description: A form of Cushing syndrome in which a tumor outside the pituitary gland produces excess ACTH. It is most often a paraneoplastic syndrome seen in small cell lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma, and pancreatic neuroendocrine (islet cell) tumors.

3AbSjw.title: Volunteer bias
3AbSjw.description: A type of selection bias that can occur when individuals who volunteer to participate in a study have different characteristics than the target population. In this case, study findings cannot be extrapolated to the target population.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

RAbljw.title: Endogenous hypercortisolism
RAbljw.description: The overproduction of cortisol either caused by benign or malignant adrenal tumors (primary hypercortisolism) or excess ACTH production from pituitary gland tumors or paraneoplastic syndrome (secondary hypercortisolism).

iAbJjw.title: Allocation bias
iAbJjw.description: A type of bias in which there is a systemic difference in the way that participants are assigned to treatment or intervention groups: e.g., assigning all older patients to one group and all younger patients to another group. Can be avoided by randomizing.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

QAbujw.title: Hazard ratio
QAbujw.description: A measurement of how often a particular event occurs in one group compared to how often it occurs in another group, over time. Hazard ratios originate from survival analysis studies that evaluate time-to-event data. A hazard ratio greater than 1 indicates increased risk and a hazard ratio less than 1 indicates decreased risk. If the hazard ratio is 1, the risk of the outcome over time is the same in the two groups being compared.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Estimates of association strength

jAb_jw.title: Ecological fallacy
jAb_jw.description: A problem that occurs when one ascribes characteristics of a group to a particular individual in the group. For example, if a study found that the greater a country's chocolate consumption, the more Nobel Prizes awarded to that country, it would be an ecological fallacy to deduce that the greater an individual's chocolate consumption, the more likely they are to win a Nobel Prize.

PAbWPw.title: Tolvaptan
PAbWPw.description: A competitive vasopressin 2 receptor antagonist that acts in the collecting ducts, causing selective water excretion by inhibiting arginine vasopressin. Mainly used to treat hyponatremia (e.g., due to syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion, congestive heart failure, cirrhosis) and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

4Ab3Pw.title: Random error
4Ab3Pw.description: An error that occurs due to chance and/or precision limitations of a test. In contrast to systematic errors, random error cannot be replicated by repeating an experiment. Random errors can be reduced by averaging over a large number of observations. If the p-value of a study is < 0.05, the chance that the data was obtained by chance or random error is smaller than 5%.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

kAbmPw.title: Clinical features of pleural effusion
kAbmPw.description: Symptoms, which are typically only present with large (> 300 mL) effusions, include dyspnea, symptoms of hypoxia, retrosternal pleuritic chest pain, and nonproductive cough. Physical examination findings include asymmetric chest expansion, decreased fremitus, faint or absent breath sounds, pleural friction rub, and dullness to percussion over the area of effusion.

OAbIPw.title: Baroreceptor
OAbIPw.description: A pressure-sensitive receptor that regulates arterial pressure. Found in the cardiac atria, aorta, and carotid sinuses. In response to low effective arterial volume, sends signals through the vagus and glossopharyngeal nerves that lead to ADH release by the posterior pituitary, relative vasoconstriction, and decreased signaling to the vagal parasympathetic center, which increases heart rate and inotropy.

lAbvPw.title: Megakaryocyte
lAbvPw.description: A hematopoietic cell of the bone marrow that produces platelets. Derived from myeloid precursor cells. Megakaryocyte proliferation is primarily regulated by thrombopoietin.

NAb-Pw.title: Spongiotic dermatitis
NAb-Pw.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by intraepidermal and intercellular edema (spongiosis), visualized as widened intercellular spaces between keratinocytes. Specific patterns occur in allergic and irritant contact dermatitis, atopic dermatitis, and other spongiotic diseases.

oAb0kw.title: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
oAb0kw.description: A muscle in the superficial compartment of the forearm that originates from the lateral epicondyle and inserts into the base of the second and third metacarpals. It is innervated by the radial nerve and causes wrist extension and abduction. The ECRB is the most commonly affected muscle in lateral epicondylitis.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

KAbUkw.title: Attributable risk percent
KAbUkw.description: The proportion of a disease that can be attributed to an exposure. Calculated as: (relative risk - 1)/relative risk.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Estimates of population impact

6Abjkw.title: Porphyrins
6Abjkw.description: A group of intermediates in the heme synthetic pathway, including porphobilinogen and uroporphyrinogen. Defects in heme synthesis cause porphyria due to accumulation in plasma and subsequent organ deposition. The photosensitivity of patients with cutaneous porphyrias results from activation of porphyrins in the skin by ultraviolet light.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

media.title: Heterocyclic backbone of the porphyrine structure

pAbLkw.title: Anti-HAV IgG antibody
pAbLkw.description: An antibody against hepatitis A antigens that typically develops in the early convalescent phase of disease and remains detectable for decades. Associated with lifelong protective immunity. Detection indicates either past infection or vaccination.

qAbCkw.title: mTOR inhibitors
qAbCkw.description: A class of drugs that inhibits mTOR (the mechanistic target of rapamycin), which decreases cell proliferation and lymphocyte differentiation. Used in some drug-eluting stents to reduce the rate of restenosis and as anticancer agents (e.g., for breast carcinoma, renal cell carcinoma, and neuroendocrine tumors). Examples include sirolimus and everolimus.

IAbYOw.title: Inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase inhibitors
IAbYOw.description: A group of agents, including mycophenolate mofetil, that block inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMDH/IMPDH) and selectively inhibit lymphocyte proliferation.

rAbfOw.title: Anti-NMDA encephalitis
rAbfOw.description: A type of encephalitis caused by autoantibodies against the NMDA receptor. Manifestations include prodromal malaise, headache, and fever followed by psychiatric and neurological symptoms (e.g., seizures, coma) and symptoms of autonomic dysfunction.

HAbKOw.title: CMV pneumonia
HAbKOw.description: A viral infection of the lungs caused by cytomegalovirus. Typically affects individuals with immunocompromise. Clinical features include fever, nonproductive cough, and dyspnea. Chest imaging characteristically shows diffuse bilateral infiltrates. Mortality is high, even with treatment.

sAbtOw.title: Alpha-1 adrenergic agonist
sAbtOw.description: A group of sympathomimetic agents (e.g., phenylephrine) used to treat (septic) shock, hypotension, open-angle glaucoma, congestion (e.g., rhinitis), and urinary incontinence. Adverse effects include hypertension, ischemia and necrosis of fingers and toes, and urinary retention.

GAbBOw.title: Beta blocker overdose
GAbBOw.description: An intoxication that can manifest with symptoms of cardiotoxicity (e.g., hypotension, bradycardia, bradyarrhythmia, cardiogenic shock), metabolic imbalance (e.g., hypoglycemia, hyperkalemia), wheezing (due to bronchoconstriction), and neurologic symptoms (e.g., seizure, delirium, coma).

destinations.label: Cardiovascular drug poisoning → Beta blocker poisoning

tAbXlw.title: Hydrostatic pressure
tAbXlw.description: A measure of the pressure exerted by any fluid on the wall of an enclosed space. Intravascular hydrostatic pressure, for example, is the force exerted by the blood confined within blood vessel walls (e.g., capillary hydrostatic pressure), driving fluid out of capillaries and into the interstitium. Increases in hydrostatic pressure (e.g., due to heart failure, dihydropyridine CCB use) lead to an increased movement of fluid into the interstitium, causing edema.

FAbglw.title: Reflex tachycardia
FAbglw.description: A condition of tachycardia secondary to a decrease in blood pressure, which stimulates baroreceptors of the sympathetic nervous system.

8AbOlw.title: Corticosteroid
8AbOlw.description: A class of steroid hormones produced by the adrenal cortex. Includes glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids.

uAbplw.title: Severe hypothermia
uAbplw.description: A stage of hypothermia in which the core body temperature is <28°C (82.4°F). Manifestations include paralysis, rigidity, areflexia, apnea, hypotension, ventricular fibrillation, and coma.

vAbAlw.title: Muscarinic receptor agonists
vAbAlw.description: A group of drugs that activate muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, which predominantly mediate parasympathomimetic effects. Used to treat several conditions such as glaucoma, urinary retention, and myasthenia gravis.

DAb1Nw.title: Panhypopituitarism
DAb1Nw.description: The inadequate production of all pituitary hormones as a result of damage to the pituitary gland and/or hypothalamus.

wAbhNw.title: Ecological study
wAbhNw.description: A type of observational, descriptive study that assesses the prevalence of exposure and/or outcome in a specific sample group using population-based data. Can help draw conclusions that relate to the population as a whole but not to individuals within the population. Can show association but not causality.

9AbNNw.title: Metaanalysis
9AbNNw.description: A method of statistical analysis that is often used in systematic reviews to pool quantitative data from multiple studies. Increases the statistical power and improves the generalizability of findings. The validity of meta-analyses is limited by bias in study selection and the quality of the studies included.

CAbqNw.title: Janus kinase
CAbqNw.description: A kinase that belongs to the group of intracellular tyrosine kinases involved in cytokine-mediated signaling. Mutations in the JAK2 gene are associated with certain myeloproliferative neoplasms, including polycythemia vera, primary myelofibrosis, and essential thrombocythemia.

xAbENw.title: Melanin
xAbENw.description: A pigmented polymer that is produced by melanocytes and stored in organelles called melanosomes, then transferred to keratinocytes. Provides protection against ultraviolet radiation and determines the color of the skin and iris.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Cells of the skin

BAbzNw.title: Albinism
BAbzNw.description: A group of congenital conditions caused by absent or reduced melanin synthesis in melanocytes, resulting in hypopigmentation. Further classified as ocular albinism, which primarily affects the eyes, or oculocutaneous albinism, which affects the hair, skin, and eyes.

yAbdmw.title: Patch (dermatology)
yAbdmw.description: A nonpalpable skin lesion > 1 cm in size that differs in color from surrounding skin.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Primary skin lesions

AAbRmw.title: Chemical leukoderma
AAbRmw.description: A condition characterized by depigmentation after exposure to chemicals (e.g., hydroquinone) that have a toxic effect on melanocytes. In areas of contact, depigmentation typically starts with small, "confetti-like" macules that then spread and coalesce. In some patients, depigmentation can also spread to distant sites. On skin biopsy, this condition is indistinguishable from vitiligo.

_Ab5mw.title: Melanoma-associated leukoderma
_Ab5mw.description: A condition that typically presents with extensive, patchy, and asymmetric hypopigmentation and depigmentation of the skin in patients with melanoma after treatment or development of metastases. The pathogenesis is unclear, but may involve a host immune response against melanoma also results in destruction of normal melanocytes.

a_bQ5w.title: Surveillance bias
a_bQ5w.description: A type of bias that can occur if an exposed sample that is subjected to increased testing and monitoring is compared with an unexposed sample from the general population. Can result in higher incidence and/or prevalence rates.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

b_bH5w.title: Internal elastic lamina
b_bH5w.description: A layer of elastin-containing connective tissue that is present between the tunica intima and tunica media of blood vessels. It is most prominent in muscular arteries. Duplication of this layer can occur as a result of aging. Calcification of this layer is seen in Monckenberg arterial sclerosis. The segmental absence of this layer is seen in fibromuscular dysplasia. Fragmentation of this membrane is seen in malignant hypertension and certain forms of vasculitis.

W_bPMw.title: Medication for opioid use disorder
W_bPMw.description: Pharmacotherapy treatment for individuals with opioid use disorder. Methadone or buprenorphine are most commonly used to stabilize cravings and minimize opioid withdrawal symptoms while reducing the risk of overdose and intoxication.

d_boMw.title: Pleurisy
d_boMw.description: A condition of inflammation of the pleura that lines the lungs. Most commonly caused by viral infection but can also occur secondary to pneumonia, lung cancer, autoimmune disease, and pulmonary embolism. Typically causes sharp chest pain that is worse with inhalation.

V_bGMw.title: Dobutamine stress test
V_bGMw.description:
An invasive diagnostic procedure that uses intravenous dobutamine to simulate the effect of exercise on the heart 
in combination with radiologic methods (e.g., echocardiogram, MRI) to assess cardiac structure and function.

e_bxMw.title: Splanchnic
e_bxMw.description: A term used to describe visceral organs of the abdominal cavity and their respective vascular structures (e.g., splanchnic circulation, i.e., referring to the gastrointestinal vessels) and sensory and autonomic nerves.

S_bynw.title: VO2
S_bynw.description: The total amount of oxygen taken up by the body per minute for aerobic respiration. VO₂ is dependent on the ability to extract oxygen from the air, the ability to ventilate the alveoli, the ability of the heart to pump blood, and the ability of tissues to extract oxygen. The value of VO₂ increases with activity and decreases with age but the range for a resting individual at sea level is 0.20–0.50 L/min among men and 0.15–0.40 L/min among women.

3_bSLw.title: Partial cystectomy
3_bSLw.description: A bladder-preserving surgical procedure that involves a full-thickness removal of part of the bladder.

R_blLw.title: Radical cystectomy
R_blLw.description: In men, the removal of the bladder, prostate, and seminal vesicles. In women, the removal of the bladder, uterus, cervix, ovaries, and anterior vaginal wall. In both men and women, regional lymph nodes are also removed.

i_bJLw.title: Capillary bed
i_bJLw.description: The smallest blood or lymph vessels in the body. They play an essential role in the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide, as well as the microcirculation of nutrients and waste products.

Q_buLw.title: Intraocular pressure
Q_buLw.description: The pressure inside the eye generated by the flow of aqueous humor against resistance. Normally 10-21 mm Hg. Typically elevated in patients with glaucoma.

P_bWow.title: Weiss ring
P_bWow.description: A ring-shaped opacity in the vitreous cavity that can be seen on ophthalmologic examination of individuals who have posterior vitreous detachment. Caused by glial tissue that has separated from the optic nerve head.

destinations.label: Diseases of the vitreous body → Posterior vitreous detachment

4_b3ow.title: Adipose tissue
4_b3ow.description: A type of tissue that consists of adipocytes (i.e., fat cells). Stores in the form of triacylglycerols that can be released when needed. Also serves as insulation and secretes endocrine mediators (e.g., leptin, estrogens).

l_bvow.title: Functional diarrheal disorders
l_bvow.description: A group of diarrheal disorders characterized by increased bowel motility and rapid transit of intestinal content, resulting in decreased reabsorption of water.

N_b-ow.title: Minimum alveolar concentration
N_b-ow.description: A measure of anesthetic potency. Defined as the fraction of an inhalational anesthetic that must be present in the inspired air to provide sufficient analgesia (defined as lack of response to an extremely painful stimulus) in 50% of patients. Lower MAC values correlate with higher fat solubility.

m_bVKw.title: Rare disease assumption
m_bVKw.description: A mathematical assumption in case-control studies. As case control studies do not track patients over time, relative risk cannot be calculated. However, if the disease is rare, the relative risk (RR) approximates the odds ratio (OR).

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Estimates of association strength

5_biKw.title: Amifostine
5_biKw.description: A drug that is used to prevent nephrotoxic adverse effects in patients receiving chemotherapy with platinum-based, alkylating agents (e.g., cisplatin, carboplatin, and oxaliplatin) by acting as a free radical scavenger.

M_bMKw.title: Neonatal hypoglycemia
M_bMKw.description: Low blood sugars in a newborn. While there is no consensus on exact serum glucose cutoffs, they are generally  defined as blood sugar levels <40 mg/dL or <50 mg/dL in the first 24 hours after birth. Can be caused by several conditions, including persistent hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia (e.g., due to gestational diabetes), prematurity, and sepsis. May be asymptomatic or manifest with autonomic (e.g., tachycardia, sweating, tremors) and neurological symptoms (e.g., hypotonia, lethargy, seizures).

destinations.label: Overview of neonatal conditions → Neonatal hypoglycemia

n_b7Kw.title: Atypical squamous cells (cannot exclude HSIL)
n_b7Kw.description: A term used in the Bethesda system to describe abnormal cervical cytology (Pap smear) in which high-grade lesions can neither be ruled out nor confirmed with certainty.

media.title: Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (ASC-H)

L_bwKw.title: Reflex HPV test
L_bwKw.description: A screening strategy for cervical cancer in which a test for high-risk human papillomavirus types (hrHPV genotyping) is performed when individuals have abnormal Pap smear results. Typically performed on the same specimen initially collected for cytology.

o_b06w.title: Myometrium
o_b06w.description: The smooth muscle layer of the wall of the uterus between the endometrium (inner uterine layer) and the serosa (outer uterine layer). The main function of the myometrium is to stretch during pregnancy and to induce contractions during labor and afterbirth.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Uterus and cervix

K_bU6w.title: Fibrosarcomas
K_bU6w.description: A group of malignant mesenchymal tumors that are derived from cells of the connective tissue.

6_bj6w.title: Peroxisomal membrane adrenoleukodystrophy protein
6_bj6w.description: A protein on the membrane of peroxisomes that is responsible for the transport of activated acyl-coenzyme A derivates from the cytoplasm into peroxisomes. This protein is coded for a gene on chromosome X. A deficiency or deactivating defect in this protein is responsible for adrenoleukodystrophy.

J_bs6w.title: Desmoplasia
J_bs6w.description: A histological pattern of increased growth of fibrous or connective tissue secondary to tissue damage (e.g., due to invasion of malignant tumors). Desmoplasia is often found in colorectal or pancreatic cancer.

q_bC6w.title: Leukopenia
q_bC6w.description: A reduction in the white blood cell count to below normal range.

I_bYpw.title: High endothelial venule
I_bYpw.description: A part of the paracortex of a lymph node through which T and B cells enter from the blood. Also found in Peyer patches.

H_bKpw.title: Latency period
H_bKpw.description: A period of apparent inactivity between stimulation (e.g., infection with a pathogen, exposure to a toxin, onset of a disease process, administration of a drug) and response (e.g., signs and symptoms, pharmacological effects). The duration of a latency period can vary greatly depending on the scenario, ranging from very short (e.g., in the case of certain infections or pharmaceuticals) to very long (e.g., in the case of malignancies).

t_bXJw.title: Diffusion-limited gas exchange
t_bXJw.description: A form of gas exchange in which the diffusion rate of gas across the blood-air barrier is the limiting factor. Diffusion can be limited by changes in the thickness or surface area of the alveolar-capillary membrane or in partial pressures of the gases being exchanged. Occurs during strenuous exercise and in certain pathological conditions that affect the blood-air barrier (e.g., emphysema).

F_bgJw.title: Outlier
F_bgJw.description: A data point or observation that is distant from other data points or observations in a data set.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Measures of central tendency and outliers

8_bOJw.title: Type II error
8_bOJw.description: A type of error that occurs when the null hypothesis is accepted despite it actually being false. Consequently, the alternative hypothesis is rejected even though an observed effect did not occur due to chance. The probability of a type II error is denoted by beta (β).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

u_bpJw.title: Type I error
u_bpJw.description: A type of error that occurs when the null hypothesis is rejected despite it actually being true. Consequently, the alternative hypothesis is accepted, although the observed effect is actually due to chance. The probability of a type I error is called the significance level and is denoted by alpha (α).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

E_b8Jw.title: Selection bias
E_b8Jw.description: A general term for different types of systematic errors that may occur if study subjects are inappropriately selected (e.g., sampling bias, Berkson bias, nonresponse bias) or a large number of subjects are lost to follow-up (attrition bias).

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

v_bAJw.title: Statistical significance
v_bAJw.description: A statistical determination that an observed result has likely not occurred by chance alone. For most epidemiological studies, the standard threshold for declaring statistical significance is 5%.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

D_b1qw.title: Sampling bias
D_b1qw.description: A type of selection bias that can occur when a study is conducted in a way that certain individuals are more likely to be selected for a study group, resulting in a nonrandomized sample of a population. This can lead to incorrect conclusions being drawn about the relationship between exposures and outcomes.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

w_bhqw.title: Stratification
w_bhqw.description: The division of a population into subpopulations based on a particular characteristic (e.g., gender, age, occupation) during the study design process, before randomization (i.e., assignment to experimental and control groups) occurs.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

9_bNqw.title: Scatter plot
9_bNqw.description: A diagram that displays data points in a two-coordinate system. Useful for interpreting trends in the data. The strength and direction of a linear relationship in a scatter plot can be quantified using the correlation coefficient (r).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Distribution and graphical representation of data

C_bqqw.title: Aggressive periosteal reaction
C_bqqw.description: A type of periosteal reaction that is associated with rapid subperiosteal deposition of woven bone. On x-ray, aggressive periosteal reactions appear as "disorganized," "lamellated" (onion-peel), "spiculated" (perpendicular hair-on-end or sunburst), and Codman triangle. Aggressive periosteal reactions are typically associated with malignant tumors (e.g., osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, chondrosarcoma) but can also occur with certain benign bone lesions that grow aggressively (e.g., acute osteomyelitis, eosinophilic granuloma).

x_bEqw.title: Matching (epidemiology)
x_bEqw.description: The grouping of individuals based on particular variables known or thought to be confounders (e.g., gender, age, occupation) during the design phase of a study. This method is frequently used in case-control studies to ensure study and control groups have similar baseline characteristics.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

B_bzqw.title: Plasmacytoma
B_bzqw.description: An early-stage plasma cell dyscrasia characterized by a single lesion that affect bones (solitary plasmacytoma of bone) or soft tissue (solitary extramedullary plasmacytoma), or, in rare cases, multiple solitary lesions in soft tissue, bone, or both (multiple solitary plasmacytoma). The most common site is the spine, followed by the pelvis and ribs.

y_bdIw.title: Dysgeusia
y_bdIw.description: An altered sense of taste, often characterized as a persistently sweet, sour, salty, bitter, or metallic taste that is incongruous with the actual stimulus.

A_bRIw.title: Standard normal distribution
A_bRIw.description: A normal (Gaussian) distribution with a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. Numerical data can be "standardized" into a standard normal distribution to facilitate data analysis by subtracting the population mean and dividing by the standard deviation.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Distribution and graphical representation of data

-_bDIw.title: Balloon tamponade
-_bDIw.description: The application of direct pressure to a site of internal bleeding via inflation of an internally inserted balloon to achieve short-term hemostasis. Common indications include esophageal variceal hemorrhage, acute uterine bleeding (e.g., postpartum hemorrhage), hemoptysis, and post-ERCP bleeding.

ZzbZrw.title: Postcardiac injury syndrome
ZzbZrw.description: Acute pericarditis that typically occurs 2–10 weeks after myocardial infarction (postmyocardial infarction syndrome, Dressler syndrome), cardiac surgery such as CABG or pericardiotomy (postpericardiotomy syndrome), or chest trauma. PCIS most likely occurs because neo-antigens released from the injured myocardium combine with antibodies to form immune-complexes, which elicit an inflammatory response. In addition to acute pericarditis, patients occasionally develop pleuritis and pneumonitis.

bzbHrw.title: Internal rotation
bzbHrw.description: A descriptor for rotational movement toward the midline.

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

Xzb9rw.title: External rotation
Xzb9rw.description: A descriptor for rotational movement away from the midline.

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

1zb27w.title: Continuous variable
1zb27w.description: A variable that can take on any numeric value in a range of values. E.g., measurements of blood pressure, temperature, IQ levels, or weight.

WzbP7w.title: Nominal variable
WzbP7w.description: A variable that has two or more categories without having any kind of order or numeric value. Examples include gender and eye color. There is no set distance (interval) between data.

dzbo7w.title: Transurethral resection of bladder tumor
dzbo7w.description: A diagnostic and therapeutic procedure that uses an electrocautery resectoscope to excise visible bladder tumors up to and including the muscularis propria. Allows for the determination of muscle involvement on histopathology.

VzbG7w.title: Linear regression
VzbG7w.description: A statistical method that models the relationship between a predictor x (categorical or continuous independent variable) and an outcome y (continuous dependent variables) on a scatter graph as a straight line by fitting a linear function to the data. Opposite of logistic regression in that the outcome variable is continuous rather than categorical. Considered multiple linear regression if >1 predictor variable is analyzed.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

ezbx7w.title: Vaso-occlusive crisis
ezbx7w.description: Acute recurrent episodes of severe pain, typically of the bones of the extremities, chest, and back. Most common acute complication in patients with sickle cell disease. Caused by vasoocclusion and subsequent tissue ischemia. May be accompanied by vasoocclusive phenomena (e.g., dactylitis, acute chest syndrome, stroke, splenic or hepatic sequestration).

destinations.label: Sickle cell disease → Vasoocclusive crisis (sickle cell pain crisis)

UzbbHw.title: Osmotic fragility test
UzbbHw.description: Measures the ability of RBCs to resist hemolysis when exposed to different degrees of salt dilution. E.g., RBCs swell and eventually lyse when incubated in hypotonic saline due to water influx. Whether RBCs lyse or not depends on their surface area to volume ratio. This ratio is decreased in patients with HS, making their RBCs more vulnerable to osmotic stress.

2zbTHw.title: Stratified analysis
2zbTHw.description: A method of statistical data analysis in which the data sample is grouped into separate strata (subgroups) to identify confounding variables and/or effect modifiers. This allows for the assessment of the effect between exposure and outcome in each of the subgroups.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

fzbkHw.title: Restriction (epidemiology)
fzbkHw.description: A method of study design in which admission into the study population is limited to patients that meet certain criteria (e.g., age > 55, or female sex) to control for confounding.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

Tzb6Hw.title: Descriptive statistics
Tzb6Hw.description: An analysis of a sample group that is performed to measure, describe, and summarize collected data but not to make assumptions beyond the scope of the sample group. Employs measures of central tendency (mode, median, and mean) and measures of dispersion measures (range, quartiles, variance, and deviation).

gzbFHw.title: Fistula
gzbFHw.description: An abnormal connection between two epithelium-lined surfaces. Examples include gastrocolic fistula, pancreaticoduodenal fistula, and arteriovenous fistula. Can be surgically created (e.g., an arteriovenous fistula created for hemodialysis access) or occur as a complication of trauma or a disease process.

SzbyHw.title: Conivaptan
SzbyHw.description: A vasopressin receptor antagonist that reduces renal reabsorption of water and is used to treat hyponatremia caused by syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH).

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

Rzblsw.title: Extracorporeal blood rewarming
Rzblsw.description: A rewarming method used to treat individuals with severe hypothermia (body temperature <28°C); most effective approach for swiftly increasing core body temperature. Possible methods include cardiopulmonary bypass, venovenous hemofiltration, and arteriovenous ECMO. Usually reserved for patients who have not responded adequately to other treatment, since it is associated with the highest risk of complications (e.g., stroke, hemorrhages).

izbJsw.title: Nutation
izbJsw.description: Anterior tilting of the sacroiliac joint (the top of the sacrum tilts forward).

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

Qzbusw.title: Counternutation
Qzbusw.description: Posterior tilting of the sacroiliac joint (the top of the sacrum tilts backward).

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

kzbmGw.title: Allergy
kzbmGw.description: An abnormal immunological response to an otherwise harmless environmental stimulus (e.g., food, pollen, animal dander). Manifestations include hives, edema, pruritus, and bronchospasm.

lzbvGw.title: Categorical tests
lzbvGw.description: A class of statistical tests used to evaluate differences between groups with categorical variables. Examples include the Chi-square test and Fisher exact test.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

Nzb-Gw.title: Fishers exact test
Nzb-Gw.description: A statistical method used to compare the distributions of two categorical variables. Each variable (independent and dependent) can be composed of two or more categorical groups. It is a nonparametric alternative to the Chi-square test that is usually used when sample sizes are small.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

mzbVtw.title: T-distribution
mzbVtw.description: A type of continuous probability distribution used when performing T-tests with data in which the population standard deviation is unknown or the sample size is small. This type of distribution approaches the normal distribution as the sample size increases.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

5zbitw.title: Logistic regression
5zbitw.description: A statistical method that models the relationship between a predictor x (categorical or continuous independent variable) and an outcome y (categorical dependent variables) on a scatter graph as a straight line by fitting a linear function to the data. Opposite of linear regression in that the outcome variable is categorical rather than continuous. Considered multiple logistic regression if >1 predictor variable is analyzed.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

nzb7tw.title: Kruskal-Wallis H test
nzb7tw.description: A type of statistical test that compares three or more groups by testing the null hypothesis that the medians of the groups are equal. An extension of the Mann-Whitney U test (used for two groups). Considered a non-parametric alternative to one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

Lzbwtw.title: Analysis of variance
Lzbwtw.description: A statistical method used to compare the means of an outcome (dependent variable, continuous data) of ≥ 2 groups (independent variable, categorical data). Used to determine whether an observed difference between the means is statistically significant. For example, ANOVA can be used to determine if there is a statistically significant difference in the mean reduction of blood pressure (continuous data, dependent variable) between different dose groups (e.g., 5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg; categorical groups) of a given antihypertensive therapy (independent variable).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

ozb0Fw.title: Carcinoid heart disease
ozb0Fw.description: A pathologic finding seen in patients with carcinoid syndrome that is characterized by plaque-like deposits of fibrous tissue on the endocardium. The deposits especially affect the right heart (tricuspid and/or pulmonary valve).

pzbLFw.title: Systematic review
pzbLFw.description: A systematic analysis of multiple, previously conducted studies using preformulated methods aimed at answering specific research questions. Quantitative systematic reviews use meta analysis to combine the results of individual studies.

JzbsFw.title: Myomectomy
JzbsFw.description: The excision of subserosal and/or intramural fibroids. Indicated to treat fibroids that are rapidly growing, causing severe pain, and/or have recurrent refractory bleeding. Typically performed for patients who are planning to conceive in the future. Can be performed via an abdominal or vaginal approach.

rzbf8w.title: Secondary peritonitis
rzbf8w.description: The development of peritonitis due to a pre-existing acute abdominal condition, such as perforation of an abdominal viscus, abdominal organ inflammation (e.g., appendicitis, diverticulitis, pancreatitis), or trauma (including surgery). More common than primary peritonitis. Typically caused by a mixed aerobic and anaerobic infection.

7zb48w.title: Ventricular free wall rupture
7zb48w.description: A complication of myocardial infarction in which the ventricular wall ruptures due to weakening of the infarcted region. A free wall rupture typically occurs within 2 weeks of an anterior or lateral wall infarct and presents with new-onset chest pain and cardiogenic shock due to cardiac tamponade.

HzbK8w.title: Dyspepsia
HzbK8w.description: A condition of epigastric pain that lasts ≥ 1 month. Often associated with early satiety and postprandial discomfort. Functional dyspepsia (with no identifiable organic cause) accounts for 60% of all cases. Organic causes of dyspepsia include gastritis, peptic ulcer disease (including H. pylori infection), gastroesophageal reflux disease, biliary colic, medications (e.g., NSAIDs, iron supplements), pancreatitis, and gastric malignancy.

szbt8w.title: Discrete variable
szbt8w.description: A statistical term for numerical variables that can only assume whole number values.

Fzbguw.title: Diabetic otopathy
Fzbguw.description: Sensorineural hearing loss, vertigo, and/or tinnitus that occur in patients with long-standing, poorly controlled diabetes mellitus as a result of a neuropathy of the vestibulocochlear nerve and/or microangiopathy of vessels supplying the inner ear.

Ezb8uw.title: Membranous ossification
Ezb8uw.description: The formation of bone from mesenchymal stem cells without cartilage. Responsible for growth of the skull, facial bones, and clavicles.

destinations.label: Virtual histology slide box →  Connective tissue

Dzb1Ew.title: Hypervitaminosis D
Dzb1Ew.description: An elevated serum concentrations of either 25-hydroxyvitamin D (calcidiol) or 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol), usually due to excess intake. This most often leads to hypercalcemia as well. Symptoms are similar to hypercalcemia and include abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, fatigue, weakness, and irritability.

wzbhEw.title: Gliadin
wzbhEw.description: A component of the wheat protein gluten. Triggers a T-cell mediated immune response in genetically susceptible individuals, which causes celiac disease.

CzbqEw.title: Verrucous vegetations
CzbqEw.description: A noninfectious valvular vegetation seen in patients with nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (especially Libman-Sacks endocarditis due to systemic lupus erythematosus). Caused by sterile platelet thrombus formation, typically on the aortic or mitral valves.

xzbEEw.title: Isolated systolic hypertension
xzbEEw.description: A form of hypertension that is characterized by elevated systolic BP and normal diastolic BP (and widened pulse pressure). It most commonly occurs in the elderly population because of a decrease in arterial compliance. It may also occur due to an increase in cardiac output (e.g., anemia, hyperthyroidism, aortic insufficiency, AV fistula). It is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events (MI, stroke, renal dysfunction).

AzbRvw.title: Ductus venosus
AzbRvw.description: A fetal blood vessel that connects the umbilical vein and hepatic segment of the inferior vena cava. Postnatally, the ductus venosus undergo fibrosis and forms the ligamentum venosum.

destinations.label: Prenatal and postnatal physiology →  Fetal circulation

_zb5vw.title: Foramen ovale (heart)
_zb5vw.description: A fetal foramen that connects the right atrium and the left atrium. Normally closes postnatally as a result of the increased left atrial pressure, which results in compression of the septum primum against the septum secundum and the subsequent fusion of these septa to form the interatrial septum. Failure of the septum primum to fuse with the septum secundum results in a patent foramen ovale.

destinations.label: Prenatal and postnatal physiology →  Fetal circulation

zzbrvw.title: Castration-resistant prostate cancer
zzbrvw.description: Progression of prostate cancer (e.g., elevated serum PSA levels, progression of pre-existing metastasis, or new metastases) despite androgen-deprivation therapy or bilateral orchiectomy.

X-b9Dw.title: Factorial study
X-b9Dw.description: A type of clinical study that aims to test the effect and interactions of two or more interventions. Individuals are randomly assigned to groups receiving different doses and combinations of drugs (i.e., ≥ 2 factors of treatment at various dosages).

c-baww.title: Arginine vasopressin resistance
c-baww.description: The inability of the kidneys to concentrate urine (reabsorb water) due to an impaired or absent renal response to arginine vasopressin (AVP). May be caused by a hereditary AVP receptor defect or drugs (e.g., lithium, demeclocycline) or conditions that disrupt AVP signaling within the kidney.

1-b2ww.title: Arginine vasopressin deficiency
1-b2ww.description: The inability of the kidneys to concentrate urine (reabsorb water) due to a deficiency of arginine vasopressin (AVP). May be caused by hypoxic encephalopathy, neurosurgery, tumors, or autoimmune disease.

d-boww.title: Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension
d-boww.description: A dietary pattern promoted by the United States Department of Health and Human Services to prevent and control hypertension. The plan focuses on a diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, low-fat dairy foods, but also includes meat, fish, poultry, nuts and beans. The intake of sugar-sweetened foods and beverages, red meat, and added fats (especially saturated fat and cholesterol) should be limited.

V-bGww.title: Regression (epidemiology)
V-bGww.description: A method of statistical analysis that involves developing a mathematical relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables. Examples include linear and logistic regression.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

e-bxww.title: Ampulla of Vater
e-bxww.description: The junction between the pancreatic duct and common bile duct. Pancreatic juice and bile mix in the ampulla and drain out of the major duodenal papilla (papilla Vateri) into the intestinal lumen.

U-bb9w.title: Incidence
U-bb9w.description: The number of new disease events or cases. Often expressed as the cumulative incidence (a proportion) or the incidence rate (a rate).

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

T-b69w.title: Reporting bias
T-b69w.description: A type of measurement bias that occurs in case of selective disclosure or suppression of information by subjects, resulting in underreporting or overreporting of exposure or outcome. There may be a number of reasons for reporting bias, including social desirability, resulting in, e.g., nondisclosure about past medical history, sex partners, and/or drug use.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

g-bF9w.title: Adrenalectomy
g-bF9w.description: A surgical procedure to remove one or both adrenal glands. Usually performed for patients with autonomous benign lesions (adenomas) or carcinomas.

S-by9w.title: Multifocal atrial tachycardia
S-by9w.description: A tachyarrhythmia (HR > 100) in which the atria respond to impulses from multiple atrial pacemakers outside of the SA node. Characterized by at least three different P wave morphologies. Precipitated by underlying lung disease or heart failure.

h-bcCw.title: Significance level
h-bcCw.description: The probability of a type I error is called significance level and denoted by alpha (α). The type 1 error occurs when the null hypothesis is rejected although it is actually true and, consequently, the alternative hypothesis is accepted although the observed effect is actually due to chance.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

3-bSCw.title: Pramlintide
3-bSCw.description: Injectable amylin analog that is used as adjunct to insulin therapy in patients with type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Can decrease the rate of gastric emptying, increase satiety, inhibit glucagon secretion, and reduce the dose of insulin needed for glycemic control.

R-blCw.title: Orlistat
R-blCw.description: A lipase inhibitor that reversibly inhibits gastric and pancreatic lipase, causing decreased fat breakdown and absorption. No longer recommended for general use, but may be prescribed for weight loss in some patients with obesity.

P-bWxw.title: Catheter ablation
P-bWxw.description: A procedure that uses heat generated by a radio frequency electric current to destroy pathologic tissue. Applications include cardiac catheter ablation to eliminate aberrant pathways or impulses for various tachyarrhythmias (e.g., AVNRT, AVRT, atrial fibrillation) and minimally invasive treatment of tumors, e.g., hepatocellular carcinoma or renal cell carcinoma.

4-b3xw.title: Decidual reaction
4-b3xw.description: The physiologic changes that occur in endometrial tissue in the postovulatory period and during pregnancy. This process is stimulated by increased levels of progesterone, promotes formation of the placenta, and prevents the immune system from attacking the developing embryo (since paternal DNA is foreign to the maternal immune system).

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

k-bmxw.title: Decidua
k-bmxw.description: A specialized, transformed layer of the endometrium that forms during pregnancy in the course of decidualization. Until the definitive placenta is formed, the decidua provides the conceptus with nutrition and immunologic protection and prepares the uterus for placental circulation. Consists of three parts distinguished by their relation to the site of implantation: the decidua basalis, decidua capsularis, and decidua parietalis.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

O-bIxw.title: Chorionic villi
O-bIxw.description: A collection of structures that arise from the chorionic plate (formed by cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts) and project into the intervillous space to establish the placental-maternal interface. During the second trimester, chorionic villi branch into intervillous trees.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

l-bvxw.title: Basal plate (placenta)
l-bvxw.description: The primarily maternal component of the placenta (decidua basalis), which abuts the uterine wall and receives vascular supply from the uterine spiral arteries. Also contains several ingrown embryonal cells.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

N-b-xw.title: Intervillous space
N-b-xw.description: The area between the chorionic plate and the basal plate of the placenta. Contains maternal blood and protruding villous trees. It is the site of fetomaternal gas and nutrient exchange.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

m-bVBw.title: Chorionic plate
m-bVBw.description: The fetal component of the placenta. Consists of syncytiotrophoblasts, cytotrophoblasts, and extraembryonic mesoderm. Further divided into two distinct layers: the chorion frondosum and chorion laeve.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

5-biBw.title: Placental barrier
5-biBw.description: The structures that separate the maternal and fetal circulation in the placenta and controls gas and nutrient exchange. Consists of several layers: syncytiotrophoblasts, cytotrophoblasts, basal lamina of trophoblasts, villous stroma, basal lamina of capillary endothelium, and capillary endothelium.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

M-bMBw.title: Decidua basalis
M-bMBw.description: The layer of endometrium that forms the maternal part of the placenta. Interacts with trophoblastic tissue (the fetal part of the placenta). Composed of 3 parts: stratum compactum, stratum spongiosum, and stratum basale.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

n-b7Bw.title: Decidua capsularis
n-b7Bw.description: The cap-like layer of decidua that covers the conceptus and its chorionic vesicle after implantation.
