destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

L-bwBw.title: Decidua parietalis
L-bwBw.description: The layer of decidualized endometrial tissue that lines the sides of the uterus that are not occupied by the embryo.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

o-b0yw.title: Histiotrophic nutrition
o-b0yw.description: The initial nutritional support system of an implanted embryo prior to perfusion of the placenta with maternal blood. The trophectoderm/trophoblast absorbs nutrients, derived from endometrial cells, by phagocytosis.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

K-bUyw.title: Hemotrophic nutrition
K-bUyw.description: The nutritional support system of the embryonic-placental circulation, which facilitates transplacental passage of nutrients, respiratory gases, and hormones from maternal blood vessels to the fetal circulation. The initial nutritional support system (histiotrophic nutrition) transitions to hemotrophic nutrition around week 8 of gestation

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

p-bLyw.title: Spearman correlation coefficient
p-bLyw.description: A nonparametric method to measure the correlation between two ranked variables (i.e., compares ordinal scale variables, not nominal scale variables). Due to this method, the Spearman correlation coefficient is less susceptible to the effect of outliers but is relatively imprecise, as it does not use all information from a data set.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

q-bCyw.title: Range (statistics)
q-bCyw.description: The difference between the largest and smallest value in a data set. For example, in the data set “3, 4, 9, 27,” the range is 24 (i.e., 27-3).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Measures of dispersion

I-bYAw.title: Mode (statistics)
I-bYAw.description: The value(s) that appear(s) most frequently in a data set.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Measures of central tendency and outliers

r-bfAw.title: 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase deficiency
r-bfAw.description: A rare form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia in which synthesis of all active steroid hormones is impaired. Most commonly presents at birth with ambiguous genitalia due to deficiency of sex hormones and adrenal insufficiency due to deficiency of both glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid

7-b4Aw.title: Papillary muscle rupture
7-b4Aw.description: A life-threatening complication of myocardial infarction (both STEMI and NSTEMI) that typically occurs 2 to 7 days after infarct. Clinical manifestations include acute onset hypotension, pulmonary edema, and a systolic murmur.

s-btAw.title: Heyde syndrome
s-btAw.description: A syndrome that consists of aortic stenosis, subsequent acquired von Willebrand disease, and gastrointestinal bleeding due to angiodysplasia. Altered blood flow through a stenotic valve accelerates the destruction of the procoagulant von Willebrand factor, resulting in the loss of platelet-mediated hemostasis.

G-bBAw.title: Primary villi
G-bBAw.description: A developmental stage of chorionic villi in the placenta (day 9-11 of gestation). Cytotrophoblast cells migrate into the syncytiotrophoblast trabeculae and form the inner layer of primary villi. The outer layer of the primary villi is composed of microvilli-lined syncytiotrophoblastic clefts and lacunae that are in direct contact with maternal blood.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

t-bX_w.title: Secondary villi
t-bX_w.description: A developmental stage of chorionic villi in the placenta (days 13-15 of gestation). Characterized by the migration of extraembryonic mesoderm cells into the center of primary villi.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

F-bg_w.title: Tertiary villi
F-bg_w.description: A developmental stage of chorionic villi in the placenta (week 3 of gestation). Characterized by the formation of capillaries within the mesenchymal core of secondary villi.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → Development of uteroplacental circulation

8-bO_w.title: Stapedectomy
8-bO_w.description: A procedure to remove the stapes and replace it with prosthesis. Typically performed for patients with otosclerosis.

D-b1zw.title: Placental septa
D-b1zw.description: A collection of structures of the placental basal plate (the maternal surface of the placenta) that project into the intervillous space and separate the placental cotyledons.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

w-bhzw.title: Stem villi
w-bhzw.description: The basal region of the villous trees. Connected to the chorionic plate of the placenta and provide mechanical support. They contain fetal blood vessels embedded in condensed fibrous stroma and are thought to regulate fetal blood flow to the site of fetomaternal nutrient and gas exchange.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

9-bNzw.title: Intermediate villi
9-bNzw.description: The continuations of stem villi of the placenta. They contain prominent vessels, serve as the principal sites of fetomaternal gas and nutrient exchange during the first and second trimesters, and mature into terminal villi.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

C-bqzw.title: Anchoring villi
C-bqzw.description: The portion of the villous trees that anchor to the decidua. The cytotrophoblast of anchoring villi expands and positions itself between the decidua and the syncytiotrophoblast.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

x-bEzw.title: Chorion frondosum
x-bEzw.description: The part of the chorionic plate that is involved in the formation of the placenta. Includes the chorionic villi.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

B-bzzw.title: Chorion laeve
B-bzzw.description: The smooth, outer layer of the chorionic plate. Not involved in the formation of the placenta.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

y-bd-w.title: Placental cotyledons
y-bd-w.description: A collection of 15-30 lobes of tissue of the placental basal plate (the maternal surface of the placenta), which are divided by placental septa.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

A-bR-w.title: Allantois
A-bR-w.description: A fluid-filled, sac-like structure that forms from the yolk sac in the 3rd week of gestation; one of the extraembryonic membranes (including amnion and chorion). It forms the urachus, which connects the fetal bladder and the umbilicus. Primarily involved in the exchange of liquid waste.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Embryology

_-b5-w.title: Umbilical artery
_-b5-w.description: A pair of fetal blood vessel that carry deoxygenated blood from the internal iliac arteries to the placenta, where oxygenation occurs. Postnatally, the umbilical arteries undergo fibrosis to form the medial umbilical ligaments.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The umbilical cord

z-br-w.title: Umbilical vein
z-br-w.description: A vein derived from the allantois that carries oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus. Drains into the inferior vena cava via the ductus venosus. Obliterates after birth and forms the round ligament of the liver. Often used as a source of intravenous access in neonates.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The umbilical cord

--bD-w.title: Vitelline duct
--bD-w.description: A long, narrow duct that connects the yolk sac with the midgut of the fetus. It gets obliterated during the 6th to 7th week of embryonic development.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The umbilical cord

0ZXeZ9.title: Schwartze sign
0ZXeZ9.description: A reddish-blue coloration of the tympanic promontory that can be seen on otoscopic examination. Indicates an active otosclerotic (otospongiotic) focus.

aZXQZ9.title: Connecting stalk
aZXQZ9.description: A precursor of the umbilical cord derived from extraembryonic mesoderm. Establishes a connection between the embryonic disc and the future chorionic plate. Contains the developing umbilical vessels and the allantois.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The umbilical cord

YZXnZ9.title: Chlorpropamide
YZXnZ9.description:
A first-generation sulfonylurea used as an oral hypoglycemic drug. Stimulates the release of
endogenous insulin in type 2 diabetes mellitus. Adverse effects include hypoglycemia, weight gain, SIADH, and disulfiram-like effects. Has no effect in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

cZXa09.title: Anxiolytic
cZXa09.description: A variety of substances grouped together based on their anxiety-reducing properties. Agents of several drug classes (e.g., opioids, antidepressants, benzodiazepines, sympatholytics, etc.) have anxiolytic effects.

1ZX209.title: Menin
1ZX209.description: A protein that functions as a tumor suppressor and is encoded by the MEN1 gene in humans. The protein is associated with pathophysiology of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN 1).

WZXP09.title: Neurofibromin 1 gene
WZXP09.description: A gene located on chromosome 17 that encodes neurofibromin protein, an inhibitor of cell growth and proliferation via inhibition of the Ras signal transduction pathway. Mutations in this gene are associated with neurofibromatosis I.

VZXG09.title: VHL gene
VZXG09.description: A tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 3 that is deleted in Von Hippel-Lindau disease and in some patients with renal cell carcinoma.

eZXx09.title: Merlin protein
eZXx09.description: A protein encoded by the neurofibromin 2 gene (NF2) gene. Responsible for regulation of cell growth and proliferation.

UZXba9.title: Neurofibromin protein
UZXba9.description: A protein encoded by the neurofibromin 1 gene (NF1). Responsible for regulation of cell growth and proliferation via inhibition of the Ras signal transduction pathway.

2ZXTa9.title: TSC1 gene
2ZXTa9.description: A tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 9 that encodes tuberous sclerosis complex 1 (TSC1, also called Hamartin protein). Mutations in this gene are associated with tuberous sclerosis.

fZXka9.title: TSC2 gene
fZXka9.description: A tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 16 that encodes tuberous sclerosis complex 2 (TSC2, also called Tuberin protein). Mutations in this gene are associated with tuberous sclerosis.

TZX6a9.title: Tuberin protein
TZX6a9.description: A tumor suppressor protein encoded by the TSC2 gene. This gene is located in chromosome 16 and, when mutated, is associated with tuberous sclerosis.

gZXFa9.title: Hamartin
gZXFa9.description: A tumor suppressor protein encoded by the TSC1 gene. This gene is located in chromosome 9 and, when mutated, is associated with tuberous sclerosis.

SZXya9.title: ATM gene
SZXya9.description: A gene located in chromosome 11 that produces a protein involved in the repair of double-stranded DNA breaks. Mutation in this gene are associated with ataxia-telangiectasia syndrome.

hZXcY9.title: GNAQ gene
hZXcY9.description: A gene located on chromosome 9 that codes for guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(q) subunit alpha (GNAQ protein). Mutations in this gene are associated with Sturge-Weber syndrome.

3ZXSY9.title: Electric alternans
3ZXSY9.description: An ECG pattern characterized by alternations in the appearance of the QRS complex between beats. Can be caused by pericardial effusion; thought to be caused by the swinging motion of the beating heart when it is surrounded by pericardial fluid.

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Diagnosis

RZXlY9.title: Myxomatous degeneration
RZXlY9.description: A pathologic increase in the deposition of glycosaminoglycans in tissue. Myxomatous degeneration of the mitral valve can weaken the valve and result in mitral valve prolapse.

iZXJY9.title: Lead time
iZXJY9.description: The length of time between the initial detection of a disease and the expected outcome (i.e., death or onset of clinical symptoms).

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

QZXuY9.title: Slit lamp examination
QZXuY9.description: A part of the eye examination conducted with a binocular microscope to evaluate for traumatic and nontraumatic disorders, including corneal abrasion, lens dislocation, ocular foreign bodies, and keratoconjunctivitis. Facilitates a three-dimensional view of the eye.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Slit lamp biomicroscopy examination

PZXWb9.title: Extracorporeal therapy
PZXWb9.description: A procedure in which blood or plasma is taken out the patient's circulation and purified before returning it to circulation. Examples of extracorporeal therapies include hemodialysis, hemofiltration, hemoperfusion, exchange transfusion, plasma exchange therapy (plasmapheresis), and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO).

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Enhanced elimination

4ZX3b9.title: Hemoperfusion
4ZX3b9.description: An extracorporeal therapy in which blood is circulated through a cartridge containing an adsorbent (e.g., activated charcoal, resin) to remove a toxin. Hemoperfusion is most commonly used to treat theophylline and/or barbiturate overdose.

kZXmb9.title: Response bias
kZXmb9.description: A type of bias in which study participants do not respond truthfully or accurately because of the manner in which questions are phrased (e.g., leading questions) and/or the possibility of more socially acceptable answer options. Especially common when using surveys.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

OZXIb9.title: Parallel-test reliability
OZXIb9.description: A type of statistical precision that refers to the reliability of a new test compared with an established test. If the new test produces similar statistical results as an older, established test, it implies a similar degree of reliability.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Precision and validity

lZXvb9.title: Cognitive bias
lZXvb9.description: A type of error that that occurs in research or clinical practice wherein the personal beliefs of the study participants, investigators, patients, and/or clinicians influence the study results and/or clinical outcome. Examples include response bias, observer bias, confirmation bias, framing bias, availability bias, anchoring bias, ascertainment bias, visceral bias, and hindsight bias.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors
Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

NZX-b9.title: Triple-blind study
NZX-b9.description: A type of blinding in a randomized controlled trial in which the researchers, study participants, and analysts do not know who is in the control group and who is in the treatment group.

5ZXiX9.title: Unpaired t-test
5ZXiX9.description: A type of statistical test in which two different populations are sampled at the same time in order to compare the difference between the means of a continuous outcome variable of the two groups. Tests the null hypothesis that the means of the two groups are equal.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

MZXMX9.title: Paired t-test
MZXMX9.description: A type of statistical test in which the same population is sampled at two different times in order to compare the difference between the means of a continuous outcome variable of this group. Tests the null hypothesis that the group mean is equal at these two different times.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Statistical tests

nZX7X9.title: Vasopressin receptor antagonist
nZX7X9.description: A drug that blocks vasopressin receptors in the blood vessels (V1 receptors) and renal collecting tubules (V2 receptors). Examples include tolvaptan and conivaptan. Used in the management of hyponatremia and refractory ascites.

LZXwX9.title: Internal validity
LZXwX9.description: The extent to which a study is free from systematic error (such as bias) and confounding. Results from studies with high internal validity are considered true for the sample of studied individuals.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Precision and validity

oZX0c9.title: Vertical transmission
oZX0c9.description: An infection acquired directly from the mother that is transmitted to the embryo, fetus, or newborn through the placenta, during exposure to bodily fluids during birth, or via breastmilk.

KZXUc9.title: Invasive candidiasis
KZXUc9.description: A Candida species infection of the blood (candidemia) and/or organs (e.g., endophthalmitis, endocarditis, meningitis, and osteomyelitis.)

JZXsc9.title: Echinocandin
JZXsc9.description: A group of antifungal agents that inhibits synthesis of β-glucan, a component of the fungal cell wall. Used to treat invasive aspergillosis and Candida infections. Agents include caspofungin, micafungin, and anidulafungin.

qZXCc9.title: Posaconazole
qZXCc9.description: A triazole antifungal that works by inhibiting the synthesis of ergosterol, a component of the fungal cell membrane. It is used in the treatment of aspergillosis and candidiasis.

IZXY19.title: Choriocapillaris
IZXY19.description: The internal layer of the choroidea of the eye, composed of capillaries, which supply nutrients to the outer retina. The choriocapillaris is adjacent to the Bruch's membrane.

rZXf19.title: Pygmalion effect
rZXf19.description: A psychological phenomenon in which the behavior of study subject is positively influenced by the experimenter's expectations, because the experimenter acts in a way that increases the likelihood that the expected behavior will occur. The Pygmalion effect is a type of self-fulfilling prophecy (along with the placebo and Golem effects).

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

7ZX419.title: Subacute invasive aspergillosis
7ZX419.description: A form of aspergillosis characterized by pulmonary cavitation, nodules, and consolidations that progress over 1–3 months.

HZXK19.title: Galactomannan antigen
HZXK19.description: A heteropolysaccharide component of the Aspergillus cell wall that is shed during the phase of hyphal growth. It can be detected in a serum or bronchoalveolar lavage sample in patients with invasive aspergillosis.

sZXt19.title: Salvage prostatectomy
sZXt19.description: A radical prostatectomy that is performed after unsuccessful primary radiation therapy. The procedure is challenging and is associated with a slightly higher risk of complications (e.g., urinary incontinence, impotence) due to scarred and damaged tissue caused by prior radiation.

GZXB19.title: Iloprost
GZXB19.description: A prostacyclin (PGI₂) analog that dilates systemic and pulmonary arteries. Iloprost can be used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension and to treat severe rest pain associated with critical limb ischemia.

tZXXW9.title: Icatibant
tZXXW9.description: A bradykinin B2-receptor antagonist used to treat acute attacks of hereditary angioedema (i.e., due to C1 inhibitor deficiency, which leads to excessive release of bradykinin). Adverse effects include injection site reactions, fever, rash, and dizziness.

FZXgW9.title: Physical therapy
FZXgW9.description: A program of specially designed exercises for preventive and therapeutic purposes (e.g., physical exercise, massage, electrotherapy, hydrotherapy, assistive devices) to help patients regain or improve physical abilities impaired or threatened by disease, injury, and/or disability.

8ZXOW9.title: Endovascular aneurysm repair
8ZXOW9.description: A minimally invasive technique used to repair aortic aneurysms (e.g., AAA). An expandable stent graft is placed intraluminally under fluoroscopic guidance via the femoral or iliac arteries at the site of the aneurysm, thus excluding the dilated aortic segment from circulation. Known as TEVAR (thoracic EVAR) when performed for a thoracic aortic aneurysm.

media.title: Arterial access for endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA)
Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA)

BZXzd9.title: Transverse plane
BZXzd9.description: The plane that divides the body into superior and inferior parts.

_ZX5V9.title: Thyroid-binding globulin
_ZX5V9.description: A transport protein to which most circulating thyroid hormone is bound and thus inactive.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Function

-ZXDV9.title: Intraarticular space
-ZXDV9.description: A space between articulating bones that is filled with synovial fluid (synovia) and is several millimeters in width. It enables bones to articulate with each other.

Z0XZe9.title: Joint capsule
Z0XZe9.description: The fibrous connective tissue that surrounds synovial joints. Composed of two layers: an outer fibrous layer and an inner synovial layer (synovial membrane).

media.title: Structure of ball and socket synovial joints

Y0Xne9.title: Synovial bursa
Y0Xne9.description: The fluid-filled sacs in the musculoskeletal system lined with synovial membrane. Serve to reduce friction when muscles and tendons pass over bones.

media.title: Structure of ball and socket synovial joints

b0XHe9.title: Ligament
b0XHe9.description: A poorly elastic strand of connective tissue composed of parallel arrays of dense collagen fibers, which insert into the joint body or joint capsule. It directs and limits joint motion and also strengthens the joint capsule. Ligaments are always present in synovial joints.

c0XaU9.title: Ball and socket joint
c0XaU9.description: A synovial joint in which the spherical head of one bone fits into a concavity of another bone. Can move in multiple axes and provide the maximum range of motion. Examples include the hip joint and the glenohumeral joint.

10X2U9.title: Condyloid joint
10X2U9.description: A type of synovial joint in which a bone with an ovoid convexity articulates with an ellipsoid-shaped cavity on another bone.

W0XPU9.title: Saddle joint
W0XPU9.description: A synovial joint in which one articular surface is concave (saddle-shaped) and the other is convex. Permits biaxial movement (flexion and extension, abduction and adduction) but not axial rotational movement. Examples include the sternoclavicular joint and the first carpometacarpal joint.

d0XoU9.title: Hinge joint
d0XoU9.description: A uniaxial synovial joint that only allows for flexion and extension. Examples include the humeroulnar, proximal interphalangeal, and distal interphalangeal joints.

V0XGU9.title: Pivot joint
V0XGU9.description: A type of synovial joint that allows only rotational movement around a single axis (uniaxial movement). Examples include the radioulnar joints (forearm pronation and supination) and the atlantoaxial joint (turning the neck from side-to-side).

U0Xb29.title: Plane joint
U0Xb29.description: A synovial joint in which the articulating surfaces of both bones are either flat or slightly curved. They permit only limited uni-axial gliding movement. Examples include the acromioclavicular joint, facet joints of the vertebrae, and intercarpal joints of the wrist.

20XT29.title: Amphiarthrosis
20XT29.description: A type of joint that permits only limited motion and is typically connected by ligaments or cartilage (e.g., intervertebral joints).

f0Xk29.title: Synarthrosis
f0Xk29.description: A type of immovable, fibrous joint. Depending on the type of tissue connecting the articular surfaces, synarthroses are further classified into syndesmoses, synchondroses, symphyses, and synostoses.

S0Xy29.title: Symphysis
S0Xy29.description: A type of fixed joint (synarthrosis) in which two bones are joined together by fibrocartilage. Examples include the pubic symphysis and intervertebral disc joints.

h0Xcf9.title: Synostosis
h0Xcf9.description: A type of fixed joint (synarthrosis) in which bones are fused together via ossification. Examples include the sacrum and ossified (closed) epiphyseal plates.

R0Xlf9.title: Nontreponemal tests
R0Xlf9.description: A group of tests that detect antibodies against cardiolipin, which are released from cells damaged by Treponema pallidum. Nontreponemal tests include the Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) slide test, rapid plasma reagin (RPR) card test, unheated serum reagin (USR) test, and the toluidine red unheated serum test (TRUST). These tests tend to be sensitive (but not very specific) for the diagnosis of syphilis.

i0XJf9.title: Filgrastim
i0XJf9.description: Recombinant human granulocyte colony stimulating factor (G-CSF). It is used to treat neutropenia (e.g., due to chemotherapy, chronic neutropenia, radiation exposure). It is also used following bone marrow transplantation to reduce the duration of neutropenia. Longer-acting than neupogen, another form of G-CSF.

Q0Xuf9.title: β-D-glucan assay
Q0Xuf9.description: A test used to diagnose certain invasive fungal infections; β-D-glucan is a carbohydrate component of cell walls common to many fungal species, including Candida spp., Aspergillus spp., and Pneumocystis jirovecii. Its presence suggests invasive infection.

P0XWT9.title: Myocardial oxygen demand
P0XWT9.description: The amount of oxygen required by the heart to perform optimally. The three determinants of myocardial oxygen demand are heart rate, contractility, and ventricular wall tension. Increase in any one these parameters increases myocardial oxygen demand.

40X3T9.title: Granuloma
40X3T9.description: A nodular collection of macrophages and giant cells that forms as a result of chronic inflammation. This structure is formed when the immune system is unable to completely eliminate a foreign substance. The resultant granulomatous inflammation attempts to wall off the foreign substance. Subdivided into caseating (necrotic) and noncaseating (nonnecrotic) types. Associated with hypercalcemia due to calcitriol production.

k0XmT9.title: Pitting edema
k0XmT9.description: A type of edema characterized by residual indentation following the application of pressure to the site of the swelling. Etiologies include fluid retention (e.g., in patients with heart failure or as an adverse effect of medications, such as calcium channel blockers), protein deficiency (e.g., hypoalbuminemia), venous insufficiency, and increased capillary permeability (e.g., from burns).

O0XIT9.title: Nonpitting edema
O0XIT9.description: A type of edema in which there is no residual indentation following the application of pressure to the site of swelling. Etiologies include lymphatic disorders (lymphedema due to lymphatic obstruction) and thyroid disorders (myxedema due to states of thyroid hormone imbalance).

l0XvT9.title: Tendons
l0XvT9.description: A band of dense connective tissue that attaches muscle to bone. Formed from fascicles of collagen fibers.

N0X-T9.title: Ototoxicity
N0X-T9.description: A property of having toxic effects on the cochlea, vestibulocochlear nerve, and/or vestibular system. Examples include drugs like aminoglycosides, furosemide, cisplatin, and aspirin and heavy metals such as lead and mercury. Clinical features include hearing loss, tinnitus, and dizziness.

m0XVg9.title: Tendon sheath
m0XVg9.description: A tubular connective tissue sheath that surrounds a long tendon. Facilitates the sliding of the tendon within surrounding structures.

50Xig9.title: Proctitis
50Xig9.description: An inflammation of the lining of the rectum caused by sexually transmitted infections (e.g., gonorrhea, genital herpes, candidiasis, chlamydia), radiation therapy, and inflammatory bowel disease.

M0XMg9.title: Immunization
M0XMg9.description: The process by which a person becomes protected from a disease. Active immunization (e.g. vaccination, recovery from some infections) stimulates the body's immune system to develop a sustained response to specific antigens that lasts for years (or even a lifetime); subsequent exposure to those antigens triggers an enhanced immune response. Passive immunization refers to the transfer of already-formed antibodies (e.g. placental transfer of maternal antibodies, rabies post-exposure prophylaxis), which confers temporary protection to disease.

n0X7g9.title: Fascia
n0X7g9.description: A thin layer of connective tissue that separates muscles and organs from other body structures. Reduces friction between muscles and is well-innervated to facilitate proprioception and nociception.

o0X0S9.title: Skeletal survey
o0X0S9.description: A series of x-rays that cover all bones in the body. Common indications for performing a skeletal survey include suspected child abuse, suspected bone metastases, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, multiple myeloma, Paget disease of the bone, osteogenesis imperfecta, and metabolic bone diseases (e.g., scurvy, rickets, hyperparathyroidism).

K0XUS9.title: Birbeck granules
K0XUS9.description: A collection of rod or racket-shaped organelles that are found in Langerhans cells. The exact function of these organelles is not known.

destinations.label: Benign bone tumors → Langerhans cell histiocytosis

p0XLS9.title: Ranolazine
p0XLS9.description: A metabolic modulator that targets late inward sodium channels within myocardial tissue decreasing intracellular calcium levels. It decreases myocardial oxygen demand without altering the heart rate, contractility, end-diastolic volume, or blood pressure. Used to treat chronic angina, in combination with other medications. Adverse effects include arrhythmias and QT prolongation.

destinations.label: Coronary artery disease → Pharmacodynamics of antianginal medications

J0XsS9.title: Langerhans cell
J0XsS9.description: A bone-marrow derived dendritic cell that migrates to skin and lymphoid tissue, where it functions similarly to a macrophage. Like other dendritic cells, Langerhans cells function as antigen presenting cells. Has characteristic rod- or racket-shaped granules (Birbeck granules) and stain positive for S100 and CD1a.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Cells of the skin

r0Xfh9.title: Plaque (dermatology)
r0Xfh9.description: A well-demarcated and elevated skin lesion greater than 1 cm in size.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Primary skin lesions

70X4h9.title: Shoulder girdle
70X4h9.description: A bony ring that connects the upper limb to the axial skeleton. Consists of the clavicle, scapula, acromioclavicular joint, sternoclavicular joint, glenohumeral joint, and scapulothoracic joint. Some sources also consider the proximal end of the humerus as a part of the shoulder girdle.

s0Xth9.title: Serositis
s0Xth9.description: An inflammation of any serous surface such as the pericardium, pleura, or peritoneum. Usually associated with autoimmune diseases, such as systemic lupus erythematosus and rheumatoid arthritis.

C0XqR9.title: Humeral trochlea
C0XqR9.description: A dumbbell-shaped bony projection on the distal end of the humerus that lies lateral to the medial supracondylar ridge on the ventral aspect. Articulates with the ulna.

x0XER9.title: Capitulum
x0XER9.description: A spherical bony prominence on the distal humerus that lies lateral to the trochlea process. Articulates with the head of radius.

_0X5i9.title: Proximal radioulnar joint
_0X5i9.description: A synovial pivot joint between the head of the radius and the radial notch on the proximal ulna. Supported by the annular ligament and the quadrate ligament. Along with the distal radioulnar joint, it is responsible for forearm pronation and supination.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints
Upper arm and elbow → Elbow joint

ZaXZQ9.title: Annular ligament of the radius
ZaXZQ9.description: The annular ligament of the radius is a circular ligament that wraps around the radial head. It holds the radial head in its position in close proximity to the ulna. It is often involved in a subluxation of the radial head in children, as their annular ligament is still immature.

destinations.label: Upper arm and elbow → Elbow joint

0aXeQ9.title: Brachialis muscle
0aXeQ9.description: A muscle in the ventral compartment of the arm. Originates from the anterior surface of the distal half of the humerus and inserts into the coronoid process and ulnar tuberosity. Innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve. Flexes the elbow joint.

XaX9Q9.title: Lown-Ganong-Levine syndrome
XaX9Q9.description: A pre-excitation syndrome of the heart that presents with paroxysmal tachycardia, palpitations, or collapse. ECG findings include very short PR intervals, sinus rhythm with ventricular extrasystoles, and normal QRS complexes.

1aX2j9.title: Plaque (cardiology)
1aX2j9.description: An atherosclerotic lesion comprised of lipids, connective tissue, leukocytes, and cellular debris that can develop within artery walls in the presence of certain risk factors (e.g., smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia). Complications include vessel obstruction and ischemia, coronary heart disease, peripheral artery disease, and thrombosis when plaque rupture occurs.

WaXPj9.title: Bronze diabetes
WaXPj9.description: Combination of diabetes mellitus and dark brown skin pigmentation due to iron deposition in patients with hemochromatosis.

daXoj9.title: Congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium
daXoj9.description: An ophthalmologic finding characterized by round or oval-shaped, darkly pigmented lesions on the retina on slit lamp examination. Single lesions have low diagnostic value; however, the presence of multiple, bilateral lesions is associated with familial adenomatous polyposis (Gardner syndrome).

media.title: Atypical congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium in familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP)

VaXGj9.title: Olecranon
VaXGj9.description: A hook-like bony projection of the proximal ulna. Fits into the olecranon fossa on the dorsal aspect of the distal humerus when the elbow is extended. Prevents elbow hyperextension (> 180°).

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

eaXxj9.title: Radial notch
eaXxj9.description: A lateral continuation of the trochlear notch in the ulna that accommodates the head of the radius, forming the proximal radioulnar joint.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

UaXbP9.title: Trochlear notch
UaXbP9.description: A concavity between the olecranon and the coronoid process that articulates with the trochlea of the humerus (humeroulnar joint).

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

2aXTP9.title: Tuberosity of the ulna
2aXTP9.description: A rough area of bone in the ulna, just distal to the coronoid process into which the brachialis muscle inserts.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

TaX6P9.title: Radial tuberosity
TaX6P9.description: An eminence distal to the medial aspect of the head of the radius that is the attachment point for the biceps brachii tendon.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

gaXFP9.title: Styloid process of radius
gaXFP9.description: A bone projection of the distal radius that serves as insertion site for the brachioradialis muscle and the radial collateral ligament.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

SaXyP9.title: Ulnar notch of the radius
SaXyP9.description: An articular surface of the distal and medial radius that articulates with the ulna, forming the distal radioulnar joint.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

3aXS49.title: Pleural plaques
3aXS49.description: Thickened pleural tissue caused by the collection of collagen fibers in the parietal pleura. Frequently associated with prior exposure to asbestos fibers, which are believed to trigger chronic inflammation. Plaques are typically asymptomatic and become visible on imaging studies (e.g., chest x-ray, CT) 20–30 years after initial exposure.

iaXJ49.title: Lymphangiosarcoma
iaXJ49.description: A rare cutaneous malignancy that can develop in patients with long-standing chronic lymphedema, classically as a complication of prior radical mastectomy or radiation therapy (Stewart-Treves syndrome). The tumor originates in vascular endothelial cells (hemangiosarcoma) or lymphatic endothelial cells (lymphangiosarcoma) and patients typically present with multiple purple-colored macules and/or papules.

jaX_49.title: Barium follow-through study
jaX_49.description: A radiographic study that uses an oral contrast agent to identify defects in the gastrointestinal tract (e.g., strictures, fistulae).

PaXWk9.title: Lipolysis
PaXWk9.description: A catabolic process involving the breakdown of lipids. Triglycerides are broken down into glycerol and free fatty acids and are later released into the circulation. It is stimulated by hormones such as glucagon, cortisol, epinephrine, norepinephrine, growth hormone, testosterone, and ghrelin.

4aX3k9.title: Cavo-tricuspid isthmus
4aX3k9.description: A region of fibrous tissue in the right atrium between the opening of the inferior vena cava and the tricuspid valve that is involved in the re-entrant pathway of a typical atrial flutter.

kaXmk9.title: Atrioventricular node ablation
kaXmk9.description: A procedure performed via cardiac catheterization in which the AV node is destroyed using high-frequency radio waves, resulting in permanent AV block. A permanent pacemaker is required for all patients undergoing this procedure. AV node ablation is typically used to treat patients with atrial fibrillation who are not candidates for, or have not responded to, pharmacological rate or rhythm control strategies.

OaXIk9.title: Alcohol septal ablation
OaXIk9.description: A cardiac catheterization procedure in which ethanol is injected into the most proximal septal perforator branch(es) of the left anterior descending artery in order to cause infarction of the basal interventricular septum. Used to treat left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy.

laXvk9.title: Bundle of Kent
laXvk9.description: An accessory pathway that conducts impulses from the atria to the ventricles. It occurs in < 0.3% of the population. Tachyarrhythmias caused by aberrant conduction through this accessory pathway are collectively referred to as Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

maXVO9.title: Senile plaques
maXVO9.description: An extracellular aggregation of amyloid beta (Aβ) peptides formed after the cleavage of amyloid precursor protein (APP). Associated with Alzheimer's disease, though they can also occur in normal aging. Includes two main Aβ isoforms, Aβ40 and Aβ42, of which Aβ42 has a far greater amyloidogenic potential. It is unknown whether the aggregations have a direct neurotoxic effect.

media.title: Senile plaques in presenile Alzheimer's disease

5aXiO9.title: Screening for hearing loss in children
5aXiO9.description: A screening procedure to detect pediatric hearing loss that is separate from the newborn hearing screening. Performed routinely at recommended ages and annually for children with risk factors for hearing loss. Pure tone audiometry is the preferred initial test.

MaXMO9.title: Assisted vaginal delivery
MaXMO9.description: The vaginal delivery of a baby performed with the help of forceps or a vacuum device to guide the baby out of the birth canal using gentle traction. Indications include prolonged second stage of labor, fetal distress, and maternal conditions that prohibit safe and effective pushing (e.g., cardiovascular disease).

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Assisted vaginal delivery

LaXwO9.title: Aortic unfolding
LaXwO9.description: A common radiological abnormality seen on chest x-rays of the elderly. Caused by the disproportionate increase in the length of the aorta compared to its diameter and the increasing laxity of tissues with age. Visible as a widened aortic knuckle. Can be mistaken for a thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) and vice versa. If a TAA is suspected, a thoracic CECT scan is indicated. Otherwise, no further investigations or treatment are required.

oaX0l9.title: Secondary sexual characteristics
oaX0l9.description: A collection of physical features that develop during puberty. Includes breast development in female individuals, testicular and penile enlargement and voice changes in male individuals, and development of pubic, axillary, and body hair.

destinations.label: Puberty → Development of secondary sexual characteristics

KaXUl9.title: Sentinel loop sign
KaXUl9.description: A radiologic finding describing the dilatation of a loop of small intestine due to a functional ileus near an inflamed process. In the upper abdomen, it can be an indication of pancreatitis. In the right lower quadrant, it can be an indication of appendicitis.

6aXjl9.title: Colon cut off sign
6aXjl9.description: A radiographic sign characterized by gaseous distention of the ascending and transverse colon that abruptly terminates at the splenic flexure. Caused by a spasm of the splenic flexure of the colon. Etiologies include acute pancreatitis, colon carcinoma, inflammatory bowel disease, and mesenteric ischemia. Can be mistaken for a true colonic obstruction.

paXLl9.title: Dutcher body
paXLl9.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by periodic acid-Schiff positive cytoplasmic immunoglobulin inclusions. Seen in Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, multiple myeloma, and MGUS.

JaXsl9.title: Modified barium swallow
JaXsl9.description: Real-time contrast-enhanced imaging of the mechanism of swallowing. It is performed during the evaluation of suspected oropharyngeal dysphagia and may help ascertain aspiration risk.

qaXCl9.title: Nasal endoscopy
qaXCl9.description: A diagnostic modality that facilitates visualization of the nasal cavity and sinuses using an endoscope. Indications include chronic sinusitis, epistaxis, nasal polyps, or suspected cerebrospinal fluid leak.

IaXYN9.title: Humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy
IaXYN9.description: A paraneoplastic syndrome in which parathyroid hormone-related peptide (PTHrP) is secreted by the tumor. Like PTH, PTHrP causes osteoclastic bone resorption, increases serum calcium levels, and decreases renal phosphate reabsorption. Hypercalcemia, in turn, suppresses the secretion of PTH from parathyroid glands (secondary hypoparathyroidism).

raXfN9.title: Hypophosphatasia
raXfN9.description: A metabolic bone disease caused by mutation(s) in the ALPL gene on chromosome 1p, which is responsible for producing alkaline phosphatase (ALP). Deficiency of the bone isoform of ALP results in accumulation of pyrophosphate, an inhibitor of bone mineralization. The age of symptom onset and the severity of clinical presentation varies based on the severity of ALP deficiency.

HaXKN9.title: Anthralin
HaXKN9.description: A topical preparation used in the treatment of psoriasis due to its antiinflammatory effects and ability to promote normal keratinocyte differentiation. Adverse effects include skin irritation and temporary staining of skin.

saXtN9.title: Coal tar
saXtN9.description: A topical medication used to treat psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis due to its keratolytic and anti-inflammatory properties. Adverse effects include allergic contact dermatitis, sun sensitivity, and discoloration of the skin and fabrics. Can be combined with UV light therapy.

GaXBN9.title: Pneumoconioses
GaXBN9.description: A group of restrictive interstitial lung diseases caused by the inhalation of certain dusts, often affecting miners and agricultural workers. Asbestosis and silicosis are the most common types.

taXXm9.title: Interosseous membrane of the forearm
taXXm9.description: A piece of fibrous connective tissue that connects the lateral ulna to the medial radius. It connects the radius and ulna without restricting movement, attaches muscles to the radius and ulna, and stabilizes the radioulnar joint by preventing proximal migration of the radius.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

FaXgm9.title: Flexor carpi radialis muscle
FaXgm9.description: A muscle in the superficial anterior compartment of the forearm that originates from the medial epicondyle and inserts into the base of second and third metacarpal bones. Innervated by the median nerve. Flexes the forearm. Flexes and abducts the wrist.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

8aXOm9.title: Palmaris longus muscle
8aXOm9.description: A muscle in the superficial anterior compartment of the forearm that originates from the medial epicondyle and inserts into the palmar aponeurosis. Innervated by the median nerve, C7, and C8. It is a weak flexor of the wrist.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

uaXpm9.title: Flexor digitorum superficialis muscle
uaXpm9.description: A muscle of the superficial anterior compartment of the forearm that originates from the medial epicondyle of the humerus and inserts into the base of the middle phalanges of the second to fifth digits. Innervated by the median nerve. Flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

EaX8m9.title: Tumor-induced osteomalacia
EaX8m9.description: A paraneoplastic syndrome caused by the secretion of fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF-23). Patients present with features of hypophosphatemic rickets/osteomalacia. TIO is typically associated with slow-growing mesenchymal tumors of the limbs, nasopharynx, and/or sinuses.

vaXAm9.title: Flexor pollicis longus
vaXAm9.description: A long muscle located in the deep flexor compartment of the forearm. Its main function is flexion of the thumb at the interphalangeal joint.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

waXh59.title: Brachioradialis muscle
waXh59.description: A muscle of the posterior compartment of the forearm that originates from the lateral epicondyle of the humerus and inserts into the styloid process of the radius. Flexes the forearm at the elbow. Innervated by the radial nerve.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

9aXN59.title: Extensor carpi radialis longus
9aXN59.description: An extensor muscle located in the superficial compartment of the forearm. Its main function is wrist extension and abduction.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

CaXq59.title: Extensor digiti minimi
CaXq59.description: An extensor muscle located in the superficial compartment of the posterior forearm. Its main function is to extend the fifth digit at the metacarpophalangeal joint.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

xaXE59.title: Extensor carpi ulnaris
xaXE59.description: An extensor muscle located in the superficial compartment of the posterior forearm. Its main function is wrist extension and adduction.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

BaXz59.title: Abductor pollicis longus
BaXz59.description: A muscle of the deep posterior compartment of the forearm that originates from the posterior surface of the ulna, interosseus membrane, and radius and inserts into the base of the first metacarpal. It is innervated by the deep branch of the radial nerve (posterior interosseous nerve) and is responsible for abduction and extension of the thumb.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

yaXdM9.title: Extensor pollicis brevis
yaXdM9.description: A short extensor muscle of the deep compartment of the posterior forearm. Its main function is to extend the proximal phalanx of the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

AaXRM9.title: Extensor pollicis longus
AaXRM9.description: An extensor muscle located in the deep compartment of the posterior forearm. Its main function to control the movements of the thumb by allowing extension at the MCP, CMC, and interphalangeal joints.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

media.title: Tendons of the extensor muscles of the right hand and forearm

_aX5M9.title: Extensor indicis
_aX5M9.description: An extensor muscle located in the deep compartment of the posterior forearm. Its main function is the extension of the index finger at the metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

zaXrM9.title: Head of radius
zaXrM9.description: A disk-shaped structure of the radius, the medial rim of which articulates with the radial notch of the ulna, forming the proximal radioulnar joint. The superior concave surface (articular fovea) articulates with the capitulum of the humerus (humeroradial joint of the elbow).

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

0YXen9.title: Head of ulna
0YXen9.description: An articular eminence in the ulna that articulates with the radius to form the distal radioulnar joint.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

cYXaL9.title: Trapezium
cYXaL9.description: A carpal bone that articulates with the thumb metacarpal bone to form the carpometacarpal joint of the thumb. It forms the lateral border of the carpal tunnel along with the scaphoid, serves as the insertion site for the flexor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis, abductor pollicis brevis, and distally articulates with the radial collateral ligament of the thumb.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

media.title: Bones of the hand and wrist

dYXoL9.title: Hamate
dYXoL9.description: A carpal bone on the ulnar edge of the distal carpal row. The hamate has a volar hook-shaped projection that forms the ulnar border of the carpal tunnel and the radial border of the Guyon canal.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

media.title: Normal x-ray of the carpal bones

VYXGL9.title: Wrong way eyes
VYXGL9.description: A gaze deviation in which the eyes turn away from the side of hemorrhage. Etiologies include thalamic hemorrhage and large lobar hemorrhage. In contrast, other sites of supratentorial hemorrhage typically cause a gaze deviation toward the side of hemorrhage.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

eYXxL9.title: Ocular bobbing
eYXxL9.description: An involuntary, irregular, usually conjugate, rapid downward eye movement. Ressembles down-beat nystagmus but is more pronounced. Speed is variable, but commonly there is a slower return to the primary gaze position. Typically caused by lesions of the pons or pontomedullary junction.

UYXbo9.title: Free radical
UYXbo9.description: A chemical species that is highly reactive due to its unpaired electrons. Causes cellular injury by reacting with and impairing the function of cellular molecules. Antioxidants scavenge free radicals, such as reactive oxygen species produced under states of hyperoxia (oxygen toxicity), and prevent oxidative damage.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Free radical injury

2YXTo9.title: Fiberoptic endoscopic examination of swallowing
2YXTo9.description: A form of transnasal laryngoscopy used to visualize the oropharynx and assess pharyngeal swallowing function. Can be used to assess possible aspiration and retention of food in the pharynx after swallowing.

fYXko9.title: Metacarpal bones
fYXko9.description: A set of five bones, each related to a digit, that articulate proximally with the carpal bones and distally with the proximal phalanges. Each bone is numbered 1-5 (radial to ulnar direction). Each metacarpal bone consists of a base, shaft, and head. The shaft is the point at which the interossei muscles attach.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

TYX6o9.title: Phalanges
TYX6o9.description: A group of small, long bones that make up the digits. In the hand, each finger has three phalanges (proximal, middle, and distal) and the thumb has two (proximal and distal). In the foot, the second to fifth toes have three phalanges (proximal, middle, and distal) and the great toe has only two (proximal and distal).

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

SYXyo9.title: Midcarpal joint
SYXyo9.description: A group of synovial joints between the proximal row of carpal bones and the distal row of carpal bones. This joint allows movements at the wrist (flexion, extension, abduction, adduction).

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

hYXcK9.title: Radiocarpal joint
hYXcK9.description: A synovial, biaxial, ellipsoid joint between the proximal row of carpal bones (except the pisiform) and the distal end of the radius.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

media.title: Range of motion of the wrist (radiocarpal) joint

RYXlK9.title: Carpometacarpal joint
RYXlK9.description: The articulations between a carpal bone and a metacarpal bone of the hand. There are 5 carpometacarpal joints in total.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

iYXJK9.title: Carpometacarpal joint of the thumb
iYXJK9.description: The proximal thumb joint that connects the trapezium to the first metacarpal bone. Commonly affected by osteoarthritis.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

jYX_K9.title: Metacarpophalangeal joint
jYX_K9.description: The joints between the metacarpal bones and the proximal phalanges of the hands. Arthritis of these joints is associated with rheumatoid arthritis.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

media.title: Range of motion of the 2nd–5th metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints

PYXW69.title: Proximal interphalangeal joints
PYXW69.description: The joints between the first (proximal) and second (intermediate) phalanges of the hand. Can be affected in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

media.title: Bones of the hand and wrist
Normal appearance of hands and wrists

kYXm69.title: Abductor pollicis brevis
kYXm69.description: A muscle of the thenar eminence that originates from the scaphoid and trapezium and inserts into the proximal phalanx of the thumb. It is typically innervated by the median nerve and is responsible for abduction of the thumb.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

OYXI69.title: Opponens pollicis
OYXI69.description: A muscle of the thenar eminence typically innervated by the median nerve. Responsible for thumb opposition.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

lYXv69.title: Flexor pollicis brevis
lYXv69.description: A muscle of the thenar eminence that is innervated by the median and ulnar nerves. Responsible for flexion of the thumb.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

NYX-69.title: Short-lasting unilateral neuralgiform headache with conjunctival injection and tearing
NYX-69.description: A condition of trigeminal autonomic cephalgia characterized by unilateral throbbing pain and autonomic symptoms (e.g., conjunctival injection and tearing). The pain attacks occur frequently and usually last from 5 seconds to 4 minutes.

mYXVp9.title: Thenar eminence
mYXVp9.description: The muscular prominence on the palmar aspect at the base of the thumb. Consists of the abductor pollicis brevis, flexor pollicis brevis, and the opponens pollicis. Damage to the median nerve can result in atrophy of the musculature here and cause ape hand deformity.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

5YXip9.title: Palmar interossei muscles
5YXip9.description: A set of muscles that adduct the digits toward the midline. The palmar interossei muscles of the hand are innervated by the ulnar nerve. The palmar interossei muscles of the feet are innervated by the lateral plantar nerve.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

MYXMp9.title: Dorsal interossei muscles
MYXMp9.description: A set of muscles that abduct the digits away from the midline. The dorsal interossei muscles of the hand are innervated by the ulnar nerve. The dorsal interossei muscles of the feet are innervated by the lateral plantar nerve.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia
The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

nYX7p9.title: Hypothenar eminence
nYX7p9.description: A group of muscles of the hand consisting of the opponens digiti minimi, the abductor digiti minimi, and the flexor digiti minimi.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

LYXwp9.title: Abductor digiti minimi
LYXwp9.description: A muscle responsible for abduction in the hand and foot. In the hand, it is part of the hypothenar eminence, which is typically innervated by the ulnar nerve and responsible for abduction of the 5th digit. In the foot, it is part of the lateral plantar region, which is innervated by the lateral plantar nerve and is responsible for abduction of the 5th toe and flexion and support of the longitudinal arch of the foot.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

oYX0J9.title: Flexor digiti minimi brevis
oYX0J9.description: A muscle responsible for flexion. In the hand, it is part of the hypothenar eminence, which is typically innervated by the ulnar nerve and responsible for flexion of the 5th digit. In the foot, it is found in the plantar region, which is typically innervated by the lateral plantar nerve and responsible for flexion of the 5th digit.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

KYXUJ9.title: Opponens digiti minimi
KYXUJ9.description: A muscular component of the hypothenar eminence in the hand and the lateral muscle group in the foot. In the hand, it is responsible for the opposition and flexion of the 5th digit and is innervated by the ulnar nerve. In the foot, it is responsible for the abduction and flexion of the 5th digit and innervated by the lateral plantar nerve.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

6YXjJ9.title: Palmaris brevis
6YXjJ9.description: A muscle of the hypothenar eminence that is typically innervated by the ulnar nerve and responsible for strengthening of the palmar grip by wrinkling skin on the ulnar side of the palm.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

JYXsJ9.title: Palmar aponeurosis
JYXsJ9.description: A flattened, tendinous insertion in the subcutaneous tissue of the palm that extends from the flexor retinaculum as a continuation of the palmaris longus and divides into four parts that insert into the fibrous flexor sheaths of the fingers.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

rYXfq9.title: Extensor retinaculum
rYXfq9.description: A fibrous thickening of the deep fascia. In the forearm, it is located on the dorsal aspect of the wrist and is responsible for holding the extensor tendons in place. In the ankle, it extends from the anterior surface of the tibia to the anterior surface of the fibula and extends from the medial malleolus and plantar aponeurosis medially to the lateral aspect of the calcaneus.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

7YX4q9.title: Anatomical snuffbox
7YX4q9.description: A triangular area located above the base of the thumb on the lateral surface of the hand bound by the tendons of the extensor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, and abductor pollicis longus. Scaphoid bone fractures often cause pain in this region.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

HYXKq9.title: Partial Horner syndrome
HYXKq9.description: A variant of Horner syndrome that manifests with ptosis and miosis but not anhidrosis. Associated with cluster headaches.

sYXtq9.title: Palmar erythema
sYXtq9.description: An asymptomatic redness of the palms, especially of the thenar and hypothenar eminences. Can occur in hyperestrogenic states (e.g., chronic liver disease due to impaired estrogen metabolism, pregnancy) or in conditions with hyperdynamic circulation (e.g., thyrotoxicosis, pregnancy).

GYXBq9.title: Hyperestrogenism
GYXBq9.description: A condition of increased circulating estrogen due to increased estrogen production (e.g., due to ovarian tumors), excess estrogen supplementation (e.g., due to hormone replacement therapy), or decreased metabolism and excretion of estrogens (e.g., due to chronic liver disease). Symptoms in women include menstrual irregularities, enlargement of the breasts, and infertility; symptoms in men include gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, and female distribution of pubic hair (feminization). Palmar erythema and spider telangiectasis occur in both sexes.

tYXXI9.title: Alveolar dead space
tYXXI9.description: The volume of air in alveoli that are ventilated but not perfused and therefore do not partake in oxygen-carbon dioxide exchange.

media.title: Anatomical vs. alveolar dead space (minute ventilation)

8YXOI9.title: Detrusor sphincter dyssynergia
8YXOI9.description: A pathophysiological finding of neurogenic bladder dysfunction in which involuntary contractions of the detrusor muscle press small amounts of urine against the contracted internal sphincter and detrusor muscle. Commonly seen in patients with traumatic injury to the spinal cord or multiple sclerosis.

uYXpI9.title: Jejunostomy tube
uYXpI9.description: A type of feeding tube inserted endoscopically, surgically, or fluoroscopically through a small incision in the abdominal wall into the lumen of the jejunum. Used for long-term enteral nutrition if gastrostomy tube placement is contraindicated (e.g., after esophageal surgery).

EYX8I9.title: Esophageal varices
EYX8I9.description: The presence of dilated, tortuous submucosal veins in the esophagus. Occurs in patients with portal hypertension due to increased blood flow within portosystemic anastomoses (between the left gastric vein and the esophageal vein in esophageal varices). Can rupture, causing hematemesis and/or melena.

DYX1r9.title: Tracheal deviation
DYX1r9.description: A clinical sign characterized by lateral shift of the trachea away from the midline. Usually caused by unequal pressure within the chest cavity but can also result from mass effect. Etiologies include atelectasis (ipsilateral deviation), tension pneumothorax (contralateral deviation), pleural effusion (contralateral deviation if lesion is large), and carcinoma (contralateral deviation if lesion is large).

xYXEr9.title: Septal myectomy
xYXEr9.description: A surgical procedure that consists of partial resection of the hypertrophic muscular intraventricular septum to widen the left ventricular outflow tract. It is the treatment of choice for patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who are refractory to maximal pharmacological therapy.

BYXzr9.title: Cyproterone acetate
BYXzr9.description: An antiandrogenic drug that inhibits binding of dihydrotestosterone to androgen receptors and inhibits luteinizing hormone secretion. Used for the treatment of prostate cancer, hypersexuality, precocious puberty, and hirsutism.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

yYXd79.title: Abiraterone
yYXd79.description: An androgen synthesis inhibitor used in the treatment of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Works by inhibiting products of the CYP17 gene (including 17α-hydroxylase and 17,20-lyase), blocking androgen synthesis in the adrenal glands, testis, and tumor tissue. Combined with glucocorticoids to avoid adrenal insufficiency.

bbXHH9.title: HIV retinopathy
bbXHH9.description: A noninfectious microvascular disorder found in about 60% of individuals with advanced HIV. Usually causes no pain and only mild or no changes in vision. Fundoscopic findings include small cotton wool spots, retinal hemorrhages, telangiectasia, microaneurysms, and areas of capillary nonperfusion. Tends to resolve spontaneously over weeks to months.

XbX9H9.title: Parapneumonic effusion
XbX9H9.description: A type of pleural effusion that typically arises as a result of pneumonia, lung abscess, or bronchiectasis. Further subdivided into uncomplicated parapneumonic effusions (sterile; pH ≥ 7.2), complicated parapneumonic effusions (infected; pH < 7.2, elevated LDH, glucose < 60 mg/dL), and empyemas.

cbXas9.title: Oncotic pressure
cbXas9.description: An intravascular osmotic pressure generated by proteins (especially albumin). This pressure keeps intravascular fluid within blood vessels and opposes intravascular hydrostatic pressure.

1bX2s9.title: Uremic fetor
1bX2s9.description: A characteristic ammonia- or urine-like odor to the breath found in patients with uremia (e.g., from chronic kidney disease).

WbXPs9.title: Counseling on safer sex practices
WbXPs9.description: A set of strategies for counseling patients on sexual practices. Includes a discussion of factors that increase the risk of contracting sexually transmitted infections (e.g., not using condoms, multiple sex partners) and the benefits, risks, and limitations of different contraceptive methods and testing (e.g., HIV testing).

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual health

dbXos9.title: Local osteolytic hypercalcemia
dbXos9.description: A type of hypercalcemia of malignancy in which skeletal metastases (most commonly from multiple myeloma or breast cancer) induce osteolytic activity, causing hypercalcemia.

VbXGs9.title: External hordeolum
VbXGs9.description: A warm, erythematous, tender swelling of the anterior eyelid margin caused by acute suppurative inflammation of the Zeis glands (unilobar sebaceous glands near the base of eyelashes) or Moll glands (apocrine sweat glands near the base of eyelashes).

ebXxs9.title: Hemotympanum
ebXxs9.description: A collection of blood in the tympanic cavity behind the tympanic membrane. Visible on otoscopy as a blue, intact eardrum. Occurs secondary to head trauma (e.g. basilar skull fracture) and/or ear barotrauma.

UbXbG9.title: Putamenal stroke
UbXbG9.description: A stroke involving the putamen. Typically presents with contralateral hemiplegia, hemisensory loss and gaze palsy, ipsilateral deviation of the eyes, stupor, and coma.

2bXTG9.title: Cerebellar stroke
2bXTG9.description: A stroke involving the cerebellum. Typically presents with cerebellar signs (e.g., ataxia, nystagmus, slurred speech), headache, vomiting, vertigo, neck stiffness, gaze palsy, and facial weakness. Hemiparesis is not a typical feature.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

fbXkG9.title: Thalamic stroke
fbXkG9.description: A type of stroke involving the thalamus. Typically manifests with contralateral hemiparesis and hemisensory loss, miotic and unreactive pupils, and upgaze palsy with gaze deviation away from the side of the lesion.

TbX6G9.title: Lobar stroke
TbX6G9.description: A type of stroke involving relatively superficial areas of the cerebral cortex. The clinical findings depend on the specific lobe affected. A stroke involving the frontal lobe typically presents with contralateral weakness or paralysis of the leg with relative sparing of the arm and ipsilateral gaze deviation. A stroke involving the parietal lobe typically presents with seizures and contralateral sensory loss. A stroke involving the occipital lobe typically presents with seizures and contralateral homonymous hemianopsia.

gbXFG9.title: Pontine stroke
gbXFG9.description: A type of stroke involving the pons. Typically presents with decreased level of consciousness (due to disruption of the reticular activating system), quadriplegia, ocular bobbing, facial palsy, and dysarthria.

SbXyG9.title: Decortication
SbXyG9.description: A surgical procedure in which the pleural lining of the lung is removed (pleurectomy) along with restrictive, fibrous lung tissue. Facilitates re-expansion of the lung by increasing lung compliance. Indications include the presence of fibrous thickening caused by chronic inflammation, infection, and malignancy.

3bXSt9.title: Counseling on smoking cessation
3bXSt9.description: A set of strategies to encourage smokers to quit. One approach is the "5 As," consisting of "Ask, Advise, Assess, Assist, Arrange." Clinicians should query and document use of tobacco ("Ask"), urge quitting with clear and personalized language ("Advise"), assess patient willingness to quit ("Assess"), provide resources to aid quitting ("Assist"), and schedule regular follow-ups ("Arrange").

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Counseling on smoking cessation

RbXlt9.title: Hyposthenuria
RbXlt9.description: The excretion of urine with a low specific gravity due to an impaired ability of the kidneys to concentrate urine.

ibXJt9.title: Anti-HAV IgM antibody
ibXJt9.description: An antibody against hepatitis A antigens whose titers rapidly increase 4-6 weeks after infection and decline to undetectable levels within 4–6 months. Their presence has a sensitivity of 99-100% and a positive predictive value of 88% for acute infection.

QbXut9.title: Counseling on illicit drugs
QbXut9.description: A set of strategies to encourage patients to stop using illicit/recreational drugs. Clinicians should provide feedback regarding the patient's drug consumption and engage the patient in a conversation using reflective or motivational listening (a technique in which the topic is broached by repeating or rephrasing the patient's own words). Clinicians should additionally assess the patient's readiness to change and schedule regular follow-ups.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Counseling on illicit drugs

jbX_t9.title: MELD score
jbX_t9.description: A model used to predict mortality in liver cirrhosis, to stratify patients awaiting liver transplantation, and to predict outcomes in alcohol-associated hepatitis. Considers renal function, bilirubin, INR, and plasma sodium.

lbXvF9.title: Renal medullary cancer
lbXvF9.description: A rare but aggressive type of non-clear cell renal cancer that almost exclusively occurs in young individuals with sickle cell trait.

mbXV89.title: CTAB
mbXV89.description: An abbreviation for "clear to auscultation bilaterally" (i.e., lung auscultation without pathologic findings).

5bXi89.title: Clevidipine
5bXi89.description: A short-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker with a half-life of < 2 hours commonly used as an intravenous agent in the acute management of hypertension. Adverse effects include headaches, peripheral edema, and reflex tachycardia.

MbXM89.title: Nicardipine
MbXM89.description: A medium-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker with a half-life of 8-12 hours commonly used in the management of hypertension, angina and supraventricular arrhythmias. Adverse effects include headaches, peripheral edema, and reflex tachycardia.

LbXw89.title: Head and neck examination
LbXw89.description: A part of the physical examination that evaluates the head, eyes, ears, neck, and throat. Inspect of the structures of the head and neck (including the ears, nose, and oropharynx), palpate of structures (e.g., sinuses, lymph nodes, thyroid gland), and perform special testing (e.g., of vision, audition, gustation, olfaction).

KbXUu9.title: Infection-induced urticaria
KbXUu9.description: A sequela of viral, parasitic, or bacterial infection that presents with urticaria. Thought to be mediated by mast cell activation and subsequent release of histamine. Typically self-limited; treatment options include symptomatic management of pruritus with antihistamines.

6bXju9.title: Lateral decubitus view
6bXju9.description: An x-ray projection that is made with the patient lying on the right or left lateral side. Very sensitive for small amounts of pleural effusions.

pbXLu9.title: Relative polycythemia
pbXLu9.description: A relative increase in hematocrit concentration, hemoglobin concentration, and red blood cell count secondary to a reduction in plasma volume. Does not reflect an increase in the total red blood cell mass. Caused by fluid loss (e.g., insensible losses, severe vomiting, diarrhea, excessive sweating, diuretic treatment).

qbXCu9.title: Counseling on support options for domestic violence
qbXCu9.description: A set of strategies to support patients that may be victims of intimate partner violence (IPV). Express empathy, validation, acknowledgment, and nonjudgmental support after a disclosure of IPV. Assess the patient's willingness to take action and evaluate whether the patient is presently safe. The patient should be referred to a social worker or domestic violence advocate/hotline to receive advice about preparing a safety plan. Clinicians should not encourage the patient to leave their relationship but should support them if they come to that decision on their own.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Counseling on support options for domestic violence

IbXYE9.title: Radioallergosorbent test
IbXYE9.description: An immunoassay that detects specific compounds using antibodies coupled to radioactive tags. Previously used to detect allergen-specific IgE but is no longer widely used.

rbXfE9.title: McConnell sign
rbXfE9.description: A constellation of echocardiogram findings consisting of hypokinesis or akinesis of the right ventricular free wall with normal apical movement. Suggestive of massive PE.

7bX4E9.title: Massive pulmonary embolism
7bX4E9.description: A pulmonary embolism that causes hypotension or hemodynamic instability. Also referred to as "high risk."

HbXKE9.title: Dyschromatopsia
HbXKE9.description: A congenital or acquired abnormality in the ability to perceive colors.

destinations.label: Diseases of the retina → Color perception disorders

sbXtE9.title: Snellen chart
sbXtE9.description: A chart used to evaluate visual acuity. Typically displays several rows of capital letters of different sizes. The patient, from a predetermined distance from the chart (in the US typically 20 feet or 6 meters), covers one eye and consecutively reads the rows of letters out loud beginning with the smallest row she/he can read. Patients who use glasses (exception: reading glasses) should wear them and the use should be noted. The visual acuity is determined by the smallest line of letters from which the patient can correctly identify more than half the letters and recorded as “distance of the patient from the chart/distance at which a healthy eye can read the line of letters as noted next to the line on the chart”. A recorded visual acuity of 20/40 thus means that the patient can see from 20 feet away what a healthy eye can see from 40 feet away.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Visual acuity

GbXBE9.title: Otoscopy
GbXBE9.description: A physical examination technique that uses an otoscope to visualize a patient's tympanic membrane. Pull the outer ear to straighten the ear canal, then insert an otoscope (with properly-sized speculum attached) into the ear. Bracing the hand with the otoscope can prevent injury to the ear canal. Can be combined with a pneumatic attachment to test tympanic membrane mobility.

destinations.label: Head and neck examination → Examination of the ears

media.title: Examination and surface anatomy of the tympanic membrane

tbXXv9.title: Direct ophthalmoscopy
tbXXv9.description: A type of fundoscopic examination that is performed using a direct ophthalmoscope, a handheld device with its own light source and lens. The examiner looks directly through the lens to obtain an upright (uninverted) view of the fundus. Direct ophthalmoscopy has a lower magnification and breadth than indirect ophthalmoscopy.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Fundoscopic exam

FbXgv9.title: Costovertebral angle tenderness
FbXgv9.description: Pain that is elicited upon percussion of the costovertebral angle (approx. 12th rib). When present, this finding should raise concern for pyelonephritis.

ubXpv9.title: Digitate dermatosis
ubXpv9.description: A distinct type of small plaque parapsoriasis that typically presents with finger-shaped, atrophic, erythematous plaques over skin cleavage lines, distributed symmetrically on the flanks. Typically asymptomatic but can be pruritic. Treatment options include topical steroids and phototherapy.

EbX8v9.title: Type I pneumocyte
EbX8v9.description: A thin squamous cell that lines the alveoli and comprises 97% of alveolar surfaces. Facilitates gas diffusion across the alveolar wall.

vbXAv9.title: Lacrimal gland
vbXAv9.description: A component of the lacrimal apparatus located on the upper lateral part of the orbit on the surface of the levator palpebrae superioris and the lateral rectus muscles. It is a serous gland with tubuloalveolar secretory elements that secretes the aqueous layer of the tear fluid. Innervated by parasympathetic fibers of the facial nerve.

media.title: Lacrimal apparatus and tear film layers

wbXhD9.title: Subclavian groove
wbXhD9.description: The groove on the inferior surface of the middle third of the clavicle, where the subclavius muscle attaches.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

9bXND9.title: Impression for costoclavicular ligament
9bXND9.description: A rough, depressed oval area on the medial third of the clavicle where the costoclavicular ligament attaches, thus binding the first rib to the clavicle and limiting shoulder elevation.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

CbXqD9.title: Tuberosity for coracoclavicular ligament
CbXqD9.description: A tuberosity on the lateral clavicle that consists of the trapezoid line and the conoid tubercle. The trapezoid ligament attaches to the trapezoid line; the conoid ligament attaches to the conoid tubercle.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

xbXED9.title: Conoid tubercle
xbXED9.description: A bony prominence on the lateral inferior surface of the clavicle. It is the insertion point of the conoid ligament.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

BbXzD9.title: Trapezoid line
BbXzD9.description: A ridge located near the acromial end of the clavicle upon which the trapezoid ligament attaches.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

zbXrw9.title: Supraspinous fossa
zbXrw9.description: A concave depression located superior to the scapular spine on the posterior aspect of the scapula. The supraspinatus muscle, which forms part of the rotator cuff, inserts here.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

ZXXZ99.title: Suprascapular notch
ZXXZ99.description: A deep groove located between the coracoid process and the superior scapular border. The superior transverse scapular ligament traverses this notch and attaches at the base of the coracoid process. Suprascapular nerve entrapment can occur at the suprascapular notch.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

bXXH99.title: Levator ani
bXXH99.description: The major muscle group that forms the pelvic floor. Consists of three major muscle components (pubococcygeus, iliococcygeus, and puborectalis muscle) that support the pelvic viscera, maintain continence, and aid in defecation and urination.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region
