cXXaC9.title: Triple sugar iron agar
cXXaC9.description: A culture medium that contains the fermentable sugars lactose, sucrose, glucose, as well as iron and further nutrients. Used to detect microorganisms on the basis of their ability to ferment sugar, which causes a color change within the medium. Predominantly used to differentiate between enteric bacteria such as Salmonella and Shigella.

WXXPC9.title: Palpation of the apical impulse
WXXPC9.description: A part of the cardiac examination. Palpate the point of maximum impulse (PMI), which is located on the anterior chest most inferolateral from the sternum where a beat can be felt (typically medial to the midclavicular line at the 5th intercostal space). Typical PMI is ~ 2 cm² in area, Lateral deviation of the point of maximum impulse and size > 2 cm² suggest left ventricular enlargement.

dXXoC9.title: Inspection of the conjunctivae
dXXoC9.description: A part of the eye examination to evaluate the conjunctivae. Expose the conjunctiva by applying gentle pressure while pulling down the skin below the lower lid. Red conjunctiva suggests conjunctivitis. Pale conjunctiva suggests anemia.

destinations.label: Head and neck examination → Focused examination of the eyes

VXXGC9.title: Palpation of the liver
VXXGC9.description: The assessment of the liver by placing a hand under the rib cage and pressing down parallel to the rectus muscle. As the patient inspires, the liver moves inferiorly onto the examiner's fingers. Can detect abnormal liver consistency (e.g., nodularity, hardness, irregularity, masses), size, and tenderness. Assessment is often unreliable. A hard or irregular liver edge is consistent with cirrhosis in the appropriate clinical context. A tender liver edge is consistent with acute hepatitis or heart failure in the appropriate clinical context.

eXXxC9.title: Examination for pitting edema
eXXxC9.description: A physical examination technique used to assess peripheral edema. Performed by applying pressure to the swollen area with a finger for a few seconds and then releasing it, observing if an indentation or "pit" remains.

UXXbx9.title: Inspection of the sclera
UXXbx9.description: A part of the eye examination to evaluate the sclerae. Expose the sclera by gently pulling open the eyelids. Normal sclerae are white. Presence of a yellow tinge throughout the sclera suggests jaundice.

destinations.label: Head and neck examination → Focused examination of the eyes

2XXTx9.title: Percussion of the abdomen
2XXTx9.description: A part of the abdominal examination. Hyperextend your nondominant middle finger and place the distal interphalangeal joint over the abdomen. Strike the joint with the other middle finger and evaluate the elicited sound over all four quadrants. Normal findings include tympanic sounds over air-filled or bowel-containing quadrants, with muffled sounds over solid organs (e.g., liver, spleen). Can be used to determine the size and location of intraabdominal organs.

fXXkx9.title: Palpation of the abdomen
fXXkx9.description: A part of the abdominal examination. With the patient lying supine, palpate superficially (light pressure) to assess the abdominal wall and then transition to deep (stronger pressure) to assess intraabdominal organs. Observe the patient's face during palpation to gauge intensity and location of pain. Tenderness during palpation has a broad differential that can be narrowed down based on the specific location (e.g., right lower quadrant pain as a sign of appendicitis).

TXX6x9.title: Auscultation of the abdomen
TXX6x9.description: The use of a stethoscope to examine the abdomen. Typically performed prior to percussion and palpation, as these techniques can induce a change in bowel sounds. With the patient lying supine, auscultate all four abdominal quadrants. The normal finding is gurgling bowel sounds every 5-10 seconds. Attenuated or absent bowel sounds suggest paralytic ileus. Increased bowel sounds suggest gastroenteritis.

gXXFx9.title: Examination of the pupils
gXXFx9.description: A part of the eye examination to evaluate the pupils. Evaluate pupil size (normally 2-6 mm), reaction to light, and accommodation. Assesses for afferent or efferent neural pathway defects.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Pupillary examination

hXXcB9.title: Palpation of the spleen
hXXcB9.description: A physical examination technique to assess for splenomegaly, texture of the splenic contour, and tenderness. The patient takes deep breaths; on expiration, palpate the right lower quadrant and gradually move toward the left costal margin. In the majority of patients, the spleen cannot be palpated.

QXXuB9.title: Acromioclavicular joint
QXXuB9.description: A gliding synovial joint between the tip of the acromion process of the scapula and the lateral end of the clavicle.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

jXX_B9.title: Coracoclavicular ligament
jXX_B9.description: A structure that consists of the conoid and trapezoid ligaments. The conoid ligament attaches to the clavicle on the conoid tubercle; the trapezoid ligament attaches to the trapezoid line on the clavicle. The two parts join to attach to the coronoid process of the scapula.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

PXXWy9.title: Acromioclavicular ligament
PXXWy9.description: A ligament that extends between the acromion and the clavicle. Strengthens the superior aspect of the acromioclavicular joint capsule.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

4XX3y9.title: Conoid ligament
4XX3y9.description: A component of the coracoclavicular ligament that connects the conoid tubercle of the clavicle with the coracoid process of the scapula.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

kXXmy9.title: Trapezoid ligament
kXXmy9.description: A component of the coracoclavicular ligament that connects the trapezoid line on the inferior surface of the clavicle with the coracoid process of the scapula.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

OXXIy9.title: Sternoclavicular joint
OXXIy9.description: A saddle joint located between the medial end of the clavicle and the manubrium of the sternum. It is the only true anatomical joint that connects the shoulder (pectoral) girdle to the torso.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

media.title: Bones and ligaments of the sternoclavicular and sternocostal joints

lXXvy9.title: Anterior sternoclavicular ligament
lXXvy9.description: A ligament that extends anteriorly between the manubrium of the sternum and the sternal end of the clavicle. Strengthens the sternoclavicular joint capsule and prevents anterior displacement of the clavicle.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

media.title: Bones and ligaments of the sternoclavicular and sternocostal joints

NXX-y9.title: Posterior sternoclavicular ligament
NXX-y9.description: A ligament that extends posteriorly between the manubrium of the sternum and the sternal end of the clavicle. Strengthens the sternoclavicular joint capsule and prevents posterior displacement of the clavicle.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

media.title: Bones and ligaments of the sternoclavicular and sternocostal joints

mXXVA9.title: Transverse humeral ligament
mXXVA9.description: A broad, fibrous band that extends from the greater tubercle of the humerus to the lesser tubercle of the humerus. Bridges the intertubercular sulcus and holds the biceps tendon in place during movement of the glenohumeral joint.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

5XXiA9.title: Rhomboid muscles
5XXiA9.description: The rhomboid major and rhomboid minor muscles. Innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve. They elevate, retract, and caudally rotate the scapula.

MXXMA9.title: Rhomboid minor muscle
MXXMA9.description: A muscle that originates from the spinous processes of C7–T1 and inserts onto the superomedial border of the scapula. Innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve. Elevates, retracts, and caudally rotates the lateral angle of the scapula.

nXX7A9.title: Rhomboid major muscle
nXX7A9.description: A muscle that originates from the spinous processes of T2-T5 (or T1-T4) vertebrae and inserts onto the inferomedial border of the scapula. Innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve. Retracts the scapula and fixes the scapula to the thoracic wall.

LXXwA9.title: Serratus anterior muscle
LXXwA9.description: A muscle that originates from the outer lateral surface of the first 8 or 9 ribs and inserts into medial border of the scapula. Innervated by the long thoracic nerve. Protracts the scapula, fixes the scapula to the thoracic wall, and assists in abduction of the shoulder above 90°.

KXXU_9.title: Palpation of head and neck lymph nodes
KXXU_9.description: A part of the head and neck examination. Palpate the anterior cervical (along the sternocleidomastoid muscles), posterior cervical (between the mastoid process and clavicle), tonsillar (below angle of mandible), submandibular (along the jawline), submental (below the chin), and supraclavicular lymph nodes. Swelling or tenderness suggests infection or malignancy.

6XXj_9.title: Focused examination of gait
6XXj_9.description: An assessment for gait abnormalities. Evaluate the patient's ability to stand still, walk naturally, heel walk, toe walk, and tandem walk (heel-to-toe). Abnormality in any of these suggests neurologic or musculoskeletal deficits.

pXXL_9.title: Examination of the thyroid gland
pXXL_9.description: A part of the head and neck examination. Inspect the thyroid gland area anteriorly and laterally and palpate the gland.Can be performed either in front of or behind the patient. Palpate between the cricoid cartilage and the suprasternal notch. Having the patient swallow a sip of water can facilitate both inspection and palpation, as the thyroid moves superiorly upon swallowing.

destinations.label: Head and neck examination → Examination of the neck

JXXs_9.title: Auscultation of the carotid arteries
JXXs_9.description: A part of the cardiovascular examination. With a stethoscope, auscultate along the course of the carotid artery (i.e., over the base of the neck, over the carotid bifurcation, and over the angle of the jaw). Presence of a carotid bruit suggests stenosis.

qXXC_9.title: Inspection of the ears
qXXC_9.description: A part of the HEENT examination. Visually assess the external ear for asymmetry, drainage, and skin abnormalities. While inserting an otoscope, pull the ear posteriorly and inferiorly to straighten the auditory canal, visualizing the middle ear and tympanic membrane. If the otoscope has a pneumatic attachment, assess tympanic membrane mobility. An inflamed ear canal with a bulging, immobile tympanic membrane suggests otitis media.

IXXYz9.title: Inspection of the oropharynx
IXXYz9.description: A part of the HEENT examination that evaluates the lips, mouth, teeth, and pharynx. Visualize the posterior pharynx, typically with an otoscope and tongue depressor, while the patients says "ah" to elevate the soft palate. Deviation of the uvula suggests glossopharyngeal nerve palsy. Evaluate the color of the pharynx, the presence of exudates or masses, dryness of the mucosa, oral lesions, and dentition.

rXXfz9.title: Inspection of the hands
rXXfz9.description: A part of the physical examination. Visually inspect the hands and note any skin abnormalities, masses, or evidence of trauma. Muscular atrophy suggests nerve compression or malnutrition. Joint deformity or swelling suggests arthritis. Note any nail findings, including changes in color (e.g., blue coloration that suggests cyanosis or clubbing that suggests pulmonary disease) or texture (e.g., Beau lines in patients receiving chemotherapy).

destinations.label: Orthopedic examination → Arm and hand examination

7XX4z9.title: Class IA antiarrhythmic drugs
7XX4z9.description: A group of antiarrhythmic drugs that preferentially blocks activated fast sodium channels (state-dependent blockade), which inhibits phase 0 depolarization. These drugs prolong action potential duration (due to their moderate potassium channel blocking activity) and slow conduction velocity. Examples include quinidine, procainamide, and disopyramide.

HXXKz9.title: Class IB antiarrhythmic drugs
HXXKz9.description: A class of antiarrhythmic drugs that inhibit sodium channel activity, which leads to a delay of phase 0 depolarization. Shortens the action potential duration and can slow conduction velocity in depolarized or ischemic tissues. Examples include lidocaine and mexiletine.

sXXtz9.title: Class II antiarrhythmic agent
sXXtz9.description: A group of antiarrhythmic drugs that work by blocking beta receptors, which results in the inhibition of sympathetic activity. They slow conduction velocity especially in the atrioventricular (AV) node. Examples include metoprolol and esmolol.

GXXBz9.title: Class III antiarrhythmic drugs
GXXBz9.description: A group of antiarrhythmic drugs that work by blocking potassium channels (delayed rectifier current), therefore prolonging repolarization, action potential duration, and the effective refractory period. Examples include amiodarone, ibutilide, dofetilide, and sotalol.

tXXX-9.title: Class IV antiarrhythmic drugs
tXXX-9.description: A group of antiarrhythmic drugs that work by blocking slow cardiac calcium channels, which slows conduction velocity in the sinoatrial (SA) and atrioventricular (AV) node. Examples include verapamil and diltiazem.

FXXg-9.title: Class V antiarrhythmic drugs
FXXg-9.description: A group of antiarrhythmic drugs that do not fit into the other antiarrhythmic categories (i.e., I through IV). They work through different mechanisms. Examples include adenosine, digoxin, and magnesium sulfate.

EXX8-9.title: Palpation of the chest
EXX8-9.description: A part of the pulmonary examination. To evaluate chest excursion, place palms on the posterior chest wall. As the patient takes a deep breath, the hands normally lift outward symmetrically. Asymmetric lung expansion suggests abnormality (air or fluid) in the pleural space. Also includes evaluation for fremitus and palpation of the anterior and posterior chest wall for tenderness (e.g., from musculoskeletal trauma) and crepitus (e.g., from pneumomediastinum).

vXXA-9.title: Inspection of the chest
vXXA-9.description: A part of the physical examination. Note the overall shape of the patient's chest and the rate, rhythm, and effort of breathing, including the anterior and posterior chest wall for deformity or asymmetry of motion. Inspiratory retraction of the supraclavicular areas and contraction of the sternocleidomastoid muscles suggest increased respiratory effort.

DXX1ZC.title: Inspection of the abdomen
DXX1ZC.description: A part of the physical examination. Identify any skin abnormalities (e.g., striae, scars, ecchymoses), protrusions or masses (e.g., hernia, distention), shape and symmetry of the abdomen (e.g., hepatomegaly, tumor), and pulsations (e.g., aortic aneurysm).

wXXhZC.title: Focused examination of hearing
wXXhZC.description: A part of the HEENT examination that assesses for asymmetry in auditory acuity. Rub fingers several centimeters away from the patient's ear, testing individually and noting differences between each ear. Alternatively, stand behind the patient on one side, whisper a phrase, and asks the patient to repeat the phrase. Can also include Weber and Rinne tests. Specialized equipment is required for quantitative measurement of hearing loss.

destinations.label: Head and neck examination → Examination of the ears

9XXNZC.title: Inspection of the nose
9XXNZC.description: A part of the HEENT examination. With the patient's head tilted back, insert an otoscope into each nare and assess the appearance of the mucosa, the turbinates, and the presence of any discharge.

destinations.label: Head and neck examination → Examination of the nose and throat

yXXd0C.title: Pectoralis minor muscle
yXXd0C.description: A muscle that originates from the third to fifth ribs near their costal cartilages and inserts onto the medial border and superior surface of the coracoid process of the scapula. Innervated by the medial pectoral nerve. Stabilizes the scapula by drawing it anteriorly and inferiorly against the thoracic wall.

-XXD0C.title: Inspection of the head
-XXD0C.description: A part of the physical examination. Visually inspect the head and evaluate the quantity, distribution, and texture of hair, the shape and contour of the skull, facial and eye asymmetry (e.g., cranial nerve palsies), and skin abnormalities.

destinations.label: Head and neck examination → Examination of the head

ZcXZaC.title: Patellofemoral pain syndrome
ZcXZaC.description: A common cause of anterior knee pain (classically around or behind the patella). Associated with overuse (e.g., frequent running). Worsens with activities that load the patellofemoral joint while flexing the knee (e.g., climbing stairs).

0cXeaC.title: Palpation of the head
0cXeaC.description: A part of the physical examination. Palpate structures of the head, noting any masses, deformity, crepitus, or skin lesions. Tenderness over the frontal and maxillary sinuses suggests sinusitis. In newborns, palpation of the head assesses fontanelle closure.

destinations.label: Head and neck examination → Examination of the head

YcXnaC.title: Pectoralis major muscle
YcXnaC.description: A chest muscle that originates from the external oblique aponeurosis, first six ribs, sternum, and medial clavicle and inserts into the lateral margin of the bicipital groove in the humerus. It is innervated by the lateral and medial pectoral nerves. It flexes, adducts, and internally rotates the humerus.

XcX9aC.title: Deltoid muscle
XcX9aC.description: A shoulder muscle that originates from the scapular spine, acromion, and lateral third of the clavicle and inserts onto the deltoid tuberosity on the anterolateral surface of the humeral shaft. Further divided into clavicular, acromial, and spinal portions. Primarilty abducts the arm but also aids in flexion and extension the arm. Innervated by the axillary nerve.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Muscles of the shoulder girdle

ccXaYC.title: Latissimus dorsi muscle
ccXaYC.description: A muscle that originates from the inferior angle of the scapula, 9th to 12th ribs, spinous processes of T7 to L5 vertebrae, dorsal surface of the sacrum, and iliac crest and inserts into the crest of the lesser tubercle on the humerus. It is the broadest muscle in the body. Innervated by the thoracodorsal nerve. Adducts, extends, and internally rotates the arm.

media.title: Lateral view of the right chest wall and abdominal wall

1cX2YC.title: Teres major muscle
1cX2YC.description: A muscle that originates from the dorsal surface of the inferior angle of the scapula and inserts into the medial border of the bicipital groove in the humerus. Innervated by the lower subscapular nerve and/or thoracodorsal nerve. Adducts, internally rotates, and extends the arm when the scapula is fixed by other muscles. Protracts the scapula when the humerus is in a fixed position.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Muscles of the shoulder girdle

WcXPYC.title: Subclavius muscle
WcXPYC.description: A muscle that originates from the first rib and inserts into the subclavian groove on the inferior surface of the middle-third of the clavicle. It is innervated by the subclavian nerve. It depresses the clavicle and elevates the first rib.

fcXkbC.title: Cornual pregnancy
fcXkbC.description: A rare type of ectopic pregnancy in which the gestational sac implants in the cornua of a bicornuate or septate uterus.

ScXybC.title: Thalamus
ScXybC.description: A brain structure responsible for relaying sensory information. Consists of multiple nuclei, including the ventral posterolateral nucleus (pain, temperature, pressure, touch, vibration, and proprioception), the ventral posteromedial nucleus (face sensation, taste), the lateral geniculate nucleus (vision), the medial geniculate nucleus (hearing), and the ventral lateral nucleus (motor information).

media.title: Anatomical illustration of the thalamus and hypothalamus

hcXcXC.title: Trapezius muscle
hcXcXC.description: A muscle that originates from the external occipital protuberance, nuchal ligament, and spinous processes of T1-T12 vertebrae. Inserts into the spine of the scapula, acromion process, and lateral third of the clavicle. Innervated by the spinal accessory nerve and C2-C4 branches. Fixes the scapula to the thoracic cage, retracts the scapula, and medially rotates the inferior scapular angle. Depending on which part of the trapezius contracts, it can also elevate or depress the scapula.

3cXSXC.title: Inspection of the neck
3cXSXC.description: A part of the physical examination. Visually inspect the neck and note the presence of any scars, masses, or deformities. Evaluate the position of the trachea and the thyroid gland for visible enlargement.

destinations.label: Head and neck examination → Examination of the neck

RcXlXC.title: Inspection of the lower extremities
RcXlXC.description: A part of the musculoskeletal examination.With the patient standing, inspect the alignment of the knees and the contour of the thighs (e.g., abnormal contour due to quadriceps atrophy). Inspects the tibiofemoral joint for deformities, irregularities, or swelling. Notes any skin abnormalities or edema. As the patient walks, inspect overall gait and extension and flexion of the hip and knee joints.

icXJXC.title: Inspection of the upper extremities
icXJXC.description: A part of the musculoskeletal examination. Inspect the contour of the shoulders anteriorly and posteriorly (e.g., atrophy, asymmetry). Note any swelling around the elbow, wrist, or hands and any skin abnormalities. Assess range of motion at each upper extremity joint.

jcX_XC.title: Steroid acne
jcX_XC.description: An acne-like dermatologic finding associated with elevated serum levels of glucocorticoids, e.g., in patients with Cushing syndrome or using anabolic steroids. Characteristic skin findings include uniform erythematous follicular papules distributed on the face, trunk, and extremities.

OcXIcC.title: Focused examination of sensation
OcXIcC.description: A type of neurological examination that is performed to assess sensation. Typically assesses the patient's perception of sharpness, dullness, temperature changes, light touch, vibration, and proprioception.

lcXvcC.title: Focused examination of deep tendon reflexes
lcXvcC.description: A part of the neurological examination. With a reflex hammer, strike a tendon briskly and note the muscle contraction response. For the Achilles tendon and patellar tendon, the patient sits with the feet hanging over the edge of the table. For the biceps tendon and brachioradialis tendon, position the patient with elbow joint in flexion. For the triceps tendon, position the patient with the arm forming a right angle at the shoulder.

NcX-cC.title: Focused examination of passive and active motion
NcX-cC.description: A part of the musculoskeletal examination. Assess active movement by having the patient flex and extend the joint of interest. Assess passive movement by having the patient relax at the joint of interest while manually testing range of motion at that joint. These maneuvers are typically performed for the knee, shoulder, wrist, and elbow.

mcXV1C.title: Montreal Cognitive Assessment
mcXV1C.description: A screening tool to assess the degree of cognitive impairment in individuals with suspected dementia. Includes testing of memory, visuospatial ability, executive function, attention, language, abstraction, recall, and orientation. Providers must have completed certified training.

LcXw1C.title: Amino acids
LcXw1C.description: A group of structural compounds of proteins that contain a functional carboxyl (-COOH) and amine (-NH₂) group. Each amino acid has an individual side chain that determines its unique properties. There are twenty proteinogenic amino acids, which can be further classified based on charge, polarity, and if they are essential or non-essential.

KcXUWC.title: Palpation of the radial pulse
KcXUWC.description: A part of the peripheral vascular examination. Place two fingertips on the flexor surface of the lateral wrist, 2-3 cm proximal to the base of the thumb, and notes the rate, rhythm, and strength of the radial pulse bilaterally.

6cXjWC.title: Carina
6cXjWC.description: A branchpoint in the tracheobronchial tree where the trachea bifurcates into the right and left mainstem bronchi.

pcXLWC.title: Counseling on avoidance of contact sports in suspected mononucleosis
pcXLWC.description: A set of strategies to counsel patients with mononucleosis to avoid strenuous physical activities for at least 21 days after initial symptoms develop because of the risk of splenic rupture. Counsel the patient to avoid high-contact sports (e.g., football, wrestling) for at least 4 weeks.

JcXsWC.title: Peritendinitis
JcXsWC.description: A condition characterized by inflammation of the sheath around a tendon (the paratenon). Often found in association with degeneration of the tendon and/or the bone-tendon junction.

qcXCWC.title: Hydroxycobalamin
qcXCWC.description: A precursor to vitamin B12 used to treat cyanide poisoning. Binds directly to cyanide to form cyanocobalamin (which is excreted by the kidneys). Also used to treat vitamin B12 deficiency.

IcXYdC.title: Sodium thiosulfate
IcXYdC.description: An agent used to treat cyanide poisoning by supplying sulfur donors to mitochondrial rhodanese, which converts cyanide to thiocyanate (which is then excreted by the kidneys).

rcXfdC.title: Amyl nitrite
rcXfdC.description: A nitrite agent that functions as an arteriolar dilator and induces methemoglobinemia (used to treat cyanide poisoning). Also used as a recreational inhalant.

7cX4dC.title: Sodium nitrite
7cX4dC.description: A nitrite agent and inducer of methemoglobinemia used to treat cyanide poisoning.

HcXKdC.title: 4-dimethylaminophenol
HcXKdC.description: A rapidly-acting inducer of methemoglobinemia used to treat cyanide poisoning.

GcXBdC.title: Dimercaprol
GcXBdC.description: A chelating agent used to treat metal toxicity (e.g., from lead, arsenic, gold, and mercury).

tcXXVC.title: Drop metastasis
tcXXVC.description: The metastasis of a primary central nervous system (CNS) neoplasm inferiorly, typically via cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Typically presents as nodules along the spine and cauda equina that can cause back pain with neurologic symptoms (e.g., limb weakness). Can be detected by lumbar puncture.

FcXgVC.title: Crepitus
FcXgVC.description: A physical finding characterized by crackling sounds upon palpation. Etiologies include gas trapping underneath the skin (e.g., from surgical intervention, pulmonary barotrauma, infection) and grinding of two surfaces against one another (e.g., from manipulation of the joints).

8cXOVC.title: Risk factors for HBV infection and groups at risk
8cXOVC.description: Risk factors include chronic liver disease, MSM, and elevated risk of percutaneous or mucosal exposure to HepB-positive blood as well as histories of injection drug use, sexually transmitted infection, incarceration, and travel to endemic areas.

ucXpVC.title: Haldane effect
ucXpVC.description: A process in which oxygenation of hemoglobin in the lungs displaces carbon dioxide. Oxygenation promotes dissociation of H+ from hemoglobin, which shifts the chemical equilibrium toward carbon dioxide formation, which is then released from RBCs and increases PaCO₂. The CO₂ can then be exhaled during ventilation.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen and carbon dioxide transport

wcXheC.title: Autonomic neuropathy
wcXheC.description: A type of small fiber neuropathy that affects autonomic nerves. Common in individuals with poorly controlled diabetes. May result in constipation, urinary retention, gastroparesis, erectile dysfunction, postural hypotension, and/or arrhythmias.

xcXEeC.title: Atrioventricular node
xcXEeC.description: A structure in the conduction system of the heart between the atria and the ventricles that creates a slow action potential mediated by calcium channels. Delays conduction of the action potential between the atria and ventricles, which allows for coordinated contraction of the atria followed by the ventricles.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Conduction system of the heart

BcXzeC.title: Wandering atrial pacemaker
BcXzeC.description: An arrhythmia defined by the presence of multiple atrial pacemakers. Characterized by at least 3 different P wave morphologies. If tachycardia is also present (HR > 100), it is referred to as multifocal atrial tachycardia.

ycXdUC.title: Hair pull test
ycXdUC.description: A test to evaluate alopecia. The examiner tugs ~ 50 strands of hair from the patient's scalp. If > 5 strands are pulled out, the test is positive (e.g., as in patients with telogen effluvium).

AcXRUC.title: Hemophilic arthropathy
AcXRUC.description: A common chronic joint disease caused by recurrent hemarthrosis (e.g., among patients with severe hemophilia). Typically develops by early adulthood. Most commonly involves the knees, ankles, and elbows.

_cX5UC.title: Ixodes scapularis
_cX5UC.description: A tick that is found in the northeastern and upper midwestern US. It transmits Lyme disease, ehrlichiosis, anaplasmosis, babesiosis, and Powassan disease. Closely related to the western black-legged tick (Ixodes pacificus).

zcXrUC.title: Amblyomma americanum
zcXrUC.description: A tick that is found in the southeastern and eastern US. It transmits ehrlichiosis, tularemia, and southern tick‑associated rash illness (STARI).

-cXDUC.title: Dermacentor variabilis
-cXDUC.description: A tick that is found east of the Rocky mountains and in limited areas along the Pacific coast. It transmits tularemia and Rocky Mountain spotted fever.

destinations.label: Tick-borne diseases → Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF)

Z1XZ2C.title: Rhipicephalus sanguineus
Z1XZ2C.description: A tick that is found worldwide. In the southwestern US and along the US-Mexico border, it has been reported to transmit Rocky Mountain spotted fever.

destinations.label: Tick-borne diseases → Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF)

01Xe2C.title: Ixodes cookei
01Xe2C.description: A tick that is found in the eastern half of the US and Canada. It transmits Powassan disease.

a1XQ2C.title: Amblyomma maculatum
a1XQ2C.description: A tick that is found along the Atlantic coast and the Gulf of Mexico. It transmits Rickettsia parkeri rickettsiosis, a type of spotted fever.

Y1Xn2C.title: Dermacentor andersoni
Y1Xn2C.description: A tick found in the Rocky mountain states (Montana, Wyoming, Idaho, Utah, Colorado, and Nevada) as well as southwestern Canada between elevations of 4,000 and 10,500 feet. Transmits Rocky Mountain spotted fever, Colorado tick fever, and tularemia.

destinations.label: Tick-borne diseases → Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF)

b1XH2C.title: Ornithodoros
b1XH2C.description: A gensus of soft-bodied ticks that can transmit tick-borne relapsing fever. In North America, they are found in the western half of the US and in southwestern Canada.

X1X92C.title: Ixodes pacificus
X1X92C.description: A tick that is found along the pacific coast of the US (especially northern California). It can transmit anaplasmosis and Lyme disease.

c1XafC.title: Orphan Annie eyes nuclei
c1XafC.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by enlarged, oval nuclei with central clearing, with most of the chromatin at the margin of the nuclear membrane. Associated with papillary carcinoma of the thyroid gland.

media.title: Nuclear grooves and Orphan-Annie eyes in papillary thyroid carcinoma

11X2fC.title: Nuclear grooves
11X2fC.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by longitudinal invaginations of the nuclear envelope. Associated with papillary thyroid carcinoma.

media.title: Nuclear grooves and Orphan-Annie eyes in papillary thyroid carcinoma

W1XPfC.title: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
W1XPfC.description: Widespread extravasation of blood from the pulmonary capillaries into the alveolar space, resulting in destruction of the capillary-alveolar basement membrane. Etiologies include vasculitis, ARDS, trauma, and coagulation disorders. Diagnosis usually requires bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage, and biopsy is often indicated to determine underlying etiology.

d1XofC.title: Lid lag
d1XofC.description: A sign of ophthalmopathy caused by spasm of the smooth muscle portion of the levator palpebrae superioris due to sympathetic overactivity (as in from Graves hyperthyroidism). Evaluated by instructing the patient to follow the examiner's finger as it moves downwards. Lid lag is present if the sclera can be seen above the iris as the patient looks down.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Examination of extraocular muscles

V1XGfC.title: Thymic shadow
V1XGfC.description: A triangular-shaped opacity representing the inferior margin of a normal thymus. Most commonly found to the right of the mediastinum but can also be bilateral or left-side prominent. Considered a normal finding on neonatal or pediatric chest x-rays. Absence of a thymic shadow is associated with thymic aplasia, as in DiGeorge syndrome.

U1XbTC.title: CSF otorrhea
U1XbTC.description: A leakage of CSF from the external auditory meatus found in patients following a fracture of the middle or posterior cranial fossa (posterior basilar skull fracture).

21XTTC.title: CSF rhinorrhea
21XTTC.description: A leakage of CSF from the anterior nares found in patients following a fracture of the anterior cranial fossa (anterior basilar skull fracture).

f1XkTC.title: Acholic stool
f1XkTC.description: Pale, clay-colored stool. Suggests biliary obstruction or decreased bile production.

T1X6TC.title: Heterochromia iridis
T1X6TC.description: A genetic or acquired asymmetry in the pigmentation of the irises. Either part or the entirety of one iris can be a different color than the other. Often occurs sporadically but can manifest as part of Sturge-Weber or Horner syndrome, in retinoblastoma, or as a sequelae of injury to the eye.

destinations.label: Diseases of the uvea → Rare conditions

g1XFTC.title: Delta-aminolevulinic acid synthase
g1XFTC.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the rate-limiting step in the synthesis of heme (the reaction of glycine with succinyl-CoA to delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA). An X-linked defect in the gene for ALA synthase causes sideroblastic anemia.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

S1XyTC.title: Thrombopoietin
S1XyTC.description: A hematopoietic growth factor that regulates production of megakaryocytes and promotes platelet production. It is primarily produced in the liver and kidneys.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Bone marrow and hematopoiesis

h1XcgC.title: Single-unit smooth muscle
h1XcgC.description: A type of smooth muscle that consists of multiple myocytes connected by gap junctions (connexins), which facilitate synchronized, coordinated contraction of the muscle tissue. This type of smooth muscle can be found in hollow organs, such as the uterus and the gastrointestinal tract.

31XSgC.title: Multi-unit smooth muscle
31XSgC.description: A type of smooth muscle that consists of multiple myocytes that are connected by gap junctions (connexins). Therefore, each cell must be individually stimulated for it to contract. Examples of this type of smooth muscle include the arrector pili muscle and the muscle that lines the trachea and blood vessels.

R1XlgC.title: Venous thromboembolism
R1XlgC.description: An umbrella term for the formation of a thrombus in the venous system. Manifests as deep vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism.

i1XJgC.title: Meniscus
i1XJgC.description: A fibrocartilaginous structure that absorbs forces in the joint and helps to prevent abnormal joint movement. Present in the knee, wrist, acromioclavicular, sternoclavicular, and temporomandibular joints.

destinations.label: Cartilage → Overview and structure of cartilage types

media.title: Attachments of menisci and cruciate ligaments of the knee

Q1XugC.title: Free water deficit
Q1XugC.description: The amount of free water loss responsible for causing a patient's hypernatremia and which must be replaced in order to restore a normal serum sodium concentration.

j1X_gC.title: Corrected reticulocyte count
j1X_gC.description: A formula used to correct the reported reticulocyte count in patients with anemia: percentage of reticulocytes × (patient hematocrit/normal hematocrit). The corrected reticulocyte count helps to avoid overestimating the degree of reticulocytosis.

P1XWSC.title: Anterior cutaneous nerve entrapment syndrome
P1XWSC.description: An entrapment of the cutaneous branches of the sensory nerves supplying the abdominal wall, either due to intra-abdominal or extra-abdominal compression of the nerves (e.g., from obesity, tight clothing, scarring). Common cause of chronic abdominal wall pain.

41X3SC.title: Counseling on sleep hygiene
41X3SC.description: A set of strategies to encourage healthier sleeping habits. Includes getting 7-8 hours of sleep per night, maintaining a regular sleep schedule, avoiding stimulants (e.g., caffeine, nicotine) in the evening, limiting exposure to electronic screens before bedtime, avoiding naps, and exercising regularly.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Counseling on sleep hygiene and lifestyle modifications to improve mood

k1XmSC.title: Counseling on sudden infant death syndrome
k1XmSC.description: A set of strategies for reducing the risk of sudden infant death syndrome while the baby is <1 year of age. Counsel patients to always place babies on their backs on a firm surface for sleep. There should be no pillows, loose bedding, or blankets in the crib. The baby should sleep in the same room as the parents but not on the same bed. Encourage mothers to breastfeed as long as possible and to avoid exposing the baby to cigarette smoke. Use of a pacifier can also reduce the risk of SIDS.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Counseling on sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS)

N1X-SC.title: Treatment-resistant hypertension
N1X-SC.description: A condition of having blood pressure measurements above goal despite use of at least three antihypertensive medications from different classes. Ideally, one medication should be a diuretic, and all three medications should be at optimal dosage (usually defined as at least 50% of maximal dose).

51XihC.title: HIV preexposure prophylaxis
51XihC.description: A medication regimen given to individuals who are HIV negative but at high risk of contracting HIV to prevent HIV transmission. The preferred combination is tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and emtricitabine.

J1Xs3C.title: Orientation to person, place, and time
J1Xs3C.description: A part of the mental status examination. Ask the patient to state their name, the current date, and current location. Disorientation in any of these suggests altered mental status.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

q1XC3C.title: Palpation of pedal pulses
q1XC3C.description: A part of the peripheral vascular system examination that assesses the pulses at the dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial arteries. With the tips of the second and third finger, palpate the dorsalis pedis artery at the dorsum of the foot lateral to the extensor hallucis longus tendon and the posterior tibial artery between the medial malleolus and the Achilles tendon. Confirm the presence of a pulse and any asymmetry between pulses in each extremity.

s1XtRC.title: Tetrahydrobiopterin
s1XtRC.description: A molecule used as a cofactor for reactions catalyzed by phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH), tyrosine hydroxylase (TH), and tryptophan hydroxylase. Deficiency can result from impaired synthesis or regeneration and can manifest with progressive neurological deterioration due to impaired neurotransmitter synthesis.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla

t1XXiC.title: Caudal
t1XXiC.description: An anatomical direction indicating a structure situated toward the inferior part of the body. When used to describe the brain, indicates a structure situated toward the posterior of the cranium.

v1XAiC.title: Urogenital sinus
v1XAiC.description: Arises from the cloaca during the 4ᵗʰ–6ᵗʰ week of embryonic development. Precursor of the bladder and urethra in both sexes; the prostate gland and bulbourethral glands in male embryos and the lower ⅔ of the vagina, vulval vestibule, greater vestibular glands (Bartholin glands), and urethral and paraurethral glands in female embryos.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → External genitalia and urogenital differentiation

D1X1QC.title: Genital tubercle
D1X1QC.description: The embryonic predecessor to the glans penis, corpus cavernosum, and corpus spongiosum in males and glans clitoris and vestibular bulbs in females.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → External genitalia and urogenital differentiation

w1XhQC.title: Gubernaculum
w1XhQC.description: An embryonic band of fibrous tissue that aids in the descent of the gonads. Postnatally, becomes the scrotal ligament in males (attaches the testes to the scrotum) and the ovarian ligament and round ligament of the uterus in females.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Descent of gonads

91XNQC.title: Patent processus vaginalis
91XNQC.description: An outpouching of the parietal peritoneum that extends through the inguinal canal. Normally obliterates spontaneously after the fetal testes have descended into the scrotum, within a few weeks to 2 years after birth; failure to obliterate can cause a communicating hydrocele and/or an infantile inguinal hernia.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Descent of gonads

C1XqQC.title: Mesonephric ducts
C1XqQC.description: An embryonic structure that develops into the male reproductive system during fetal development. Under the influence of testosterone, the Wolffian duct differentiates into the epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory duct, and seminal vesicle. In female embryos, the Wolffian duct degenerates without the influence of testosterone. A Gartner duct may remain as a remnant.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Ductal sex differentiation

_1X5jC.title: Calvaria
_1X5jC.description: The roof of the skull and part of the neurocranium. Composed of the upper parts of the frontal, parietal and occipital bones, which are connected via the coronal suture, sagittal suture, and lambdoid suture.

-1XDjC.title: Medial rectus muscle
-1XDjC.description: An extraocular muscle innervated by the oculomotor nerve (CN III). Main function is adduction of the eye.

0WXePC.title: Fontanelles
0WXePC.description: Connective tissue that holds together the bone plates of the incompletely ossified fetal and infant skull. Enables stretching and deformation of the skull to facilitate birth and accommodate the brain, which grows at a faster rate than the surrounding bone.

aWXQPC.title: Mastoid fontanelles
aWXQPC.description: The areas of connective tissue between the parietal, temporal, and occipital bones of the fetal and infant skull. Close between 6 and 18 months of age.

YWXnPC.title: Posterior fontanelle
YWXnPC.description: A triangular area of connective tissue at the junction of the lambdoid and sagittal sutures between the parietal and occipital bones of the fetal and infant skull. Closes between 2-3 months of age.

bWXHPC.title: Anterior fontanelle
bWXHPC.description: The diamond-shaped area of connective tissue at the junction of the coronal and sagittal sutures between the frontal and parietal bones of the fetal and infant skull. Closes between 12 and 18 months of age.

XWX9PC.title: Sphenoidal fontanelles
XWX9PC.description: A collection of areas of connective tissue located between the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones of the fetal and infant skull. Typical close between 6 and 18 months of age.

1WX24C.title: Inferior nasal conchae
1WX24C.description: A pair of facial bones that extend along the lateral wall of the nasal cavity.

WWXP4C.title: Vomer
WWXP4C.description: A facial bone that forms part of the bony nasal septum. It is bordered superiorly by the sphenoid bone, inferiorly by the maxilla, and anteriorly with the ethmoid bone and the nasal septal cartilage.

UWXbkC.title: Ethmoid bone
UWXbkC.description: A bone of the skull located in the roof of the nasal cavity, between the orbits. It separates the nose from the brain. It it divided into three parts: the cribriform plate (contains the olfactory bulb), the ethmoidal labyrinth, and the perpendicular plate (middle nasal concha, superior two-thirds of the nasal septum).

2WXTkC.title: Sphenoid bone
2WXTkC.description: A bone that comprises a portion of the skull base and the bony orbit. Contains the foramen rotundum (passage of V2), foramen ovale (passage of V3), and foramen spinosum (passage of middle meningeal artery).

TWX6kC.title: Temporal bones
TWX6kC.description: The bones on the side of the skull base. Comprised of squamous, mastoid, petrous, tympanic, and styloid parts.

hWXcOC.title: Foramina of the cribriform plate
hWXcOC.description: A fenestrated portion of the ethmoid bone through which the olfactory nerve traverses the cribriform plate. Damage to this structure is classically associated with cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea.

PWXWlC.title: Optic canal
PWXWlC.description: An opening in the sphenoid bone that permits the optic nerve to exit the cranium and enter the orbit.

media.title: Canals and foramina of base of skull

OWXIlC.title: Foramen rotundum
OWXIlC.description: An opening in the sphenoid bone of the skull that connects the middle cranial fossa with the pterygopalatine fossa. Serves as the passage for the maxillary branch of the trigeminal nerve.

media.title: Canals and foramina of base of skull

lWXvlC.title: Foramen ovale (skull)
lWXvlC.description: An oval opening in the skull base located in the sphenoid bone (middle cranial fossa). Structures passing through foramen ovale include the mandibular branch of the trigeminal nerve (V3), the accessory meningeal artery, the lesser petrosal nerve, and the emissary veins that connect the cavernous sinus with the pterygoid plexus

NWX-lC.title: Foramen spinosum
NWX-lC.description: An opening in the sphenoid bone of the skull that carries the meningeal branch of the mandibular nerve as well as the middle meningeal artery and vein.

media.title: Canals and foramina of base of skull

MWXMNC.title: Carotid canal
MWXMNC.description: A skull base foramen located in the petrous part of the temporal bone. Transmits the internal carotid artery and its sympathetic plexus.

oWX0mC.title: Internal acoustic meatus
oWX0mC.description: The opening of the internal auditory canal in the posterior cranial fossa within the petrous part of the temporal bone. Contains the facial nerve, vestibulocochlear nerve, and labyrinthine artery and vein.

KWXUmC.title: Jugular foramen
KWXUmC.description: An opening in the skull found in the posterior cranial fossa between the temporal and occipital bones. Transmits the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), vagus nerve (CN X), accessory nerve (CN XI), internal jugular vein, inferior petrosal sinus, occipital artery, and often the posterior meningeal artery.

media.title: Canals and foramina of base of skull

6WXjmC.title: Hypoglossal canal
6WXjmC.description: An opening in the skull base through which the hypoglossal nerve exits. Located in the occipital bone (posterior cranial fossa), anterolateral to the foramen magnum.

media.title: Canals and foramina of base of skull (inferior view)

rWXf5C.title: Inferior orbital fissure
rWXf5C.description: A fissure between the greater wing of the sphenoid bone superiorly and the palatine and maxillary bone inferiorly. Contains the zygomatic nerve, infraorbital nerve, infraorbital vein and artery, and inferior ophthalmic vein.

7WX45C.title: Petrotympanic fissure
7WX45C.description: A bony fissure in the temporal bone that runs from the temporomandibular joint to the tympanic cavity. Contains branches of the facial nerve.

HWXK5C.title: Stylomastoid foramen
HWXK5C.description: An opening in the skull base located between the styloid and mastoid processes of the temporal bone. Transmits the facial nerve (CN VII) and the stylomastoid artery.

8WXOMC.title: Cryptococcosis
8WXOMC.description: An invasive fungal infection with Cryptococcus yeast acquired by inhalation of the organism, typically from soil in the environment. Considered an AIDS-defining illness. Causes pulmonary infection that can spread to the central nervous system hematogenously.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Opportunistic fungal infections

wWXhnC.title: Maxilla
wWXhnC.description: A pair of bones that form the upper jaw, the floor of the nasal cavity and parts of its lateral wall and roof, and the walls of the orbits.

_WX5LC.title: Sphenomandibular ligament
_WX5LC.description: A band of connective tissue that spans from the sphenoid bone to the mandible. It functions to prevent inferior subluxation of the mandible from the temporomandibular joint. It is derived from the Meckel cartilage (1st branchial arch).

-WXDLC.title: Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz equation
-WXDLC.description: An equation that is used to calculate the membrane potential based on the permeability of the cell membrane to different ions and their respective concentration gradients. As an example for a membrane separating two monovalent positive ions A⁺ and B⁺, the membrane potential = 61 × log ((Pᴬ[Cᴬ]ₒ + Pᴮ[Cᴮ]ₒ) / (Pᴬ[Cᴬ]ᵢ + Pᴮ[Cᴮ]ᵢ)), where P is the permeability of the membrane to the ion, [C]ₒ is the extracellular concentration of the ion, and [C]ᵢ is the intracellular concentration of the ion.

ZdXZoC.title: Length constant
ZdXZoC.description: A numerical value that quantifies the length that an electrical signal can travel along an axon before decaying a specified amount. Larger values indicate further travel of the electrical signal.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Distribution of charge inside and outside the cell

0dXeoC.title: Membrane capacitance
0dXeoC.description: The property of a neuron to absorb a portion of electric charge. Thicker nerve fibers have higher membrane capacitance. High membrane capacitance impedes electrical conduction.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Distribution of charge inside and outside the cell

adXQoC.title: Blue sclera
adXQoC.description: A physical finding typically in patients with osteogenesis imperfecta. The sclerae appear blue because the connective tissue is thinner than usual and translucent, allowing the underlying choroidal veins to shine through.

destinations.label: Skeletal dysplasias → Osteogenesis imperfecta (brittle bone disease)

YdXnoC.title: Nodule (dermatology)
YdXnoC.description: An elevated cutaneous lesion > 1 cm in both diameter and depth.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Primary skin lesions

bdXHoC.title: Umbilicated
bdXHoC.description: A descriptor for lesions that have a small depression (resembling the umbilicus). Examples include lesions of molluscum contagiosum and Penicillium marneffei infection.

cdXaKC.title: Smooth muscle cell
cdXaKC.description: A nonstriated muscle cell with involuntary activity. Primarily found in hollow organs such as the bronchi of the lungs, gastrointestinal tract, urinary tract, reproductive system, and the cardiovascular system (e.g., arteries, veins).

media.title: Electro- and pharmacomechanical coupling of smooth muscle cell contraction

1dX2KC.title: Refractory period
1dX2KC.description: The recovery period immediately after stimulation of an excitable membrane in which a second stimuli cannot cause excitation until the membrane returns to its resting membrane potential.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Action potential

WdXPKC.title: Repolarization
WdXPKC.description: The process by which a membrane potential is returned to its resting state.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Action potential

ddXoKC.title: Afterhyperpolarization
ddXoKC.description: The repolarization of the membrane potential below the resting potential that occurs after an action potential. Limits the duration of an action potential and inhibits further action potential generation (raises the sensitivity threshold).

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Action potential

VdXGKC.title: Depolarization
VdXGKC.description: The process by which movement of ions across the cell membrane causes the voltage differential between intracellular and extracellular environments to dissipate. This change in voltage is used to trigger various cellular events such as muscle contraction and neurotransmitter release.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Action potential

edXxKC.title: Threshold potential
edXxKC.description: The electrical potential that must be reached by a stimulus in order to generate an action potential. Most excitable cells have a threshold potential of -50 mV.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Action potential

media.title: Action potentials of pacemaker cells in the sinus node

2dXT6C.title: Adrenal medulla
2dXT6C.description: The inner layer of the adrenal gland. Contains chromaffin cells and functions as a modified sympathetic ganglion that secretes epinephrine and norepinephrine. Activated by acetylcholine.

fdXk6C.title: NADPH oxidase
fdXk6C.description: An enzyme that converts oxygen into superoxide radicals, a reactive oxygen species important for the neutrophilic respiratory burst to fight pathogens. Defects in NADPH oxidase cause chronic granulomatous disease.

TdX66C.title: Th1 cell
TdX66C.description: A T cell subset that activates macrophages and cytotoxic T cells. Induced by interferon-gamma and IL-12; inhibited by IL-4 and IL-10. Decreased function (e.g., from IL-12 receptor deficiency) causes increased risk of developing disseminated mycobacterial, Salmonella species, and fungal infections.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

3dXSpC.title: Glomus body
3dXSpC.description: A specialized component of the dermis involved in body temperature regulation. Consists of an arteriovenous anastomosis (shunt) surrounded by a capsule of connective tissue. Found predominantly in the nail beds of the fingers and toes. When skin temperature is low, they shunt blood from the surface of the skin and thus prevent heat loss. When skin temperature is high, they increase blood flow to the skin surface and thus dissipate heat.

idXJpC.title: Respiratory viral panel
idXJpC.description: A polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay that can detect specific viral nucleic acids in patients with signs and symptoms of respiratory infection. Used to diagnose influenza, RSV, adenovirus, parainfluenza, and other common respiratory viruses. Results should be interpreted with caution as a positive result may indicate an asymptomatic infection or recently resolved past infection.

QdXupC.title: Abdominal guarding
QdXupC.description: An abdominal examination finding that refers to patient contraction of the abdominal wall muscles during palpation. Involuntary guarding (also referred to as "rigidity") refers to involuntary tightening of the muscles due to peritoneal inflammation and is often localized to a specific abdominal quadrant. Voluntary guarding refers to voluntary contraction in order to avoid pain during the examination and is often generalized over the entire abdomen.

jdX_pC.title: Aminocaproic acid
jdX_pC.description: A lysine derivative that inhibits the plasminogen-plasmin cascade. Used as an antifibrinolytic agent in patients with excessive bleeding and increased fibrinolysis.

PdXWJC.title: Muscarinic acetylcholine receptors
PdXWJC.description: A type of receptor stimulated by acetylcholine released from postganglionic fibers in the parasympathetic nervous system. Targets include the heart (decreases heart rate and atrial contractility), smooth muscle (increases bladder contraction, and eye (causes miosis).

5dXiqC.title: Hepatic angiosarcoma
5dXiqC.description: A rare, aggressive malignancy arising from the hepatic endothelial cells. Associated with environmental exposures such as vinyl chloride, arsenic, and thorium dioxide. Management is often limited by advanced disease at the time of diagnosis.

LdXwqC.title: Saltatory conduction
LdXwqC.description: A mode of transmitting action potentials along an axon that relies on the presence of gaps in the myelin sheath (i.e., nodes of Ranvier). Enhances the conduction velocity of action potentials.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Action potential

pdXLIC.title: Tissue transglutaminase
pdXLIC.description: An intracellular enzyme released from epithelial cells as a result of inflammation or mechanical irritation. It also functions as an antigen. The detection of tTG is central to the diagnosis of celiac disease.

JdXsIC.title: Loculation
JdXsIC.description: A small cavity or pocket within an organ or other part of the body. Often formed by the organization of scar tissue. Loculated pleural effusions can develop due to hemothorax, pyothorax, chylothorax, and tuberculous pleuritis.

qdXCIC.title: Costophrenic blunting
qdXCIC.description: The loss of clear, sharp margins of the angle between the diaphragm and the lateral chest wall on imaging. Due to the accumulation of fluid in the pleural space.

media.title: Costophrenic sulcus blunting from pleural effusion

IdXYrC.title: Keratoderma blennorrhagicum
IdXYrC.description: A skin lesion characterized by hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles. Can be yellow-brown in color and have a waxy texture. Often appears in conjunction with reactive arthritis.

7dX4rC.title: Catecholamine
7dX4rC.description: A group of biogenic amines that act as neurotransmitters (e.g., dopamine and norepinephrine) and/or hormones (e.g., epinephrine). They increase blood pressure and heart rate as part of the fight-or-flight response and are therefore often used in intensive care and emergency medicine in cases of circulatory instability.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla

HdXKrC.title: Sebaceous gland
HdXKrC.description: An exocrine gland found primarily in the dermis of the face and scalp. Secretes sebum to lubricate the skin. Stimulated by androgens (especially dihydrotestosterone) and inhibited by estrogens. It is a type of holocrine gland.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Skin appendage

media.title: Sebaceous gland and the arrector pili muscle

sdXtrC.title: Meloxicam
sdXtrC.description: A nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used as an analgesic and antipyretic. Inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX), which prevents the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandin H2. Possesses relative COX-2 selectivity.

media.title: Arachidonic acid metabolism and interfering drugs

GdXBrC.title: Hapten
GdXBrC.description: A small molecule that binds to bigger carriers and triggers a hypersensitivity reaction. Does not elicit an immune reaction on its own. Examples include NSAIDs, diuretics, allopurinol, phenytoin, and some antibiotics.

tdXX7C.title: Polycystin
tdXX7C.description: A group of transmembrane proteins involved in the development of renal tubular cells. Mutations are associated with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.

FdXg7C.title: PKD1 gene
FdXg7C.description: A gene located on chromosome 16 that codes for polycystin-1. Mutations in this gene are found in 85% of patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD).

8dXO7C.title: Topoisomerase II
8dXO7C.description: An enzyme that creates double-stranded breaks in the DNA helix to remove or add supercoils. Eukaryotic topoisomerase II is inhibited by several chemotherapeutic agents (e.g., doxorubicin, daunorubicin, etoposide, and teniposide). Prokaryotic topoisomerase II is inhibited by fluoroquinolone antibiotics.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

AdXRsC.title: Pancreas
AdXRsC.description: A retroperitoneal organ located behind the stomach, between the duodenal curvature and the hilum of the spleen. Has exocrine and endocrine functions. Exocrine functions include the production and secretion of proenzymes. Endocrine functions include the production and secretion of hormones such as insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin.

_dX5sC.title: Ionizing radiation
_dX5sC.description: A form of radiation that contains enough energy to liberate electrons from atomic orbit, which ionizes them. Light in the x-ray spectrum or higher has sufficient energy to ionize atoms, which can create damaging free radicals.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → Mechanisms of DNA damage

zdXrsC.title: Cowdry A inclusion
zdXrsC.description: An eosinophilic intranuclear inclusion found in cells infected with herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, and cytomegalovirus.

XVX9GC.title: Disorganized speech
XVX9GC.description: A type of speech characterized by loose associations (illogical, sudden, and frequent changes of topic), word salad (sequences of words without a logical connection), and/or flight of ideas (quick succession of thoughts). Usually due to an underlying disorganized thought process (e.g., schizophrenia).

dVXotC.title: Tick-borne diseases
dVXotC.description: A collection of diseases that are transmitted by ticks (e.g., Ixodes scapularis, Dermacentor variabilis) as the vector. Includes Lyme disease, tick paralysis, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, Babesiosis, Ehrlichiosis, Anaplasmosis, Tularemia, and tick-borne relapsing fever.

VVXGtC.title: Tularemia
VVXGtC.description: A bacterial infection caused by Francisella tularensis and transmitted via ticks, deer flies, and infected animals. General symptoms include high fever and a flu-like illness. Specific manifestations depend on the mode of transmission (e.g., a skin ulcer at the site of pathogen entry, pneumonia symptoms from inhalation).

2VXTFC.title: Musculocutaneous nerve
2VXTFC.description: An upper extremity nerve that originates from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus (spinal roots C5-7) and innervates the biceps brachii muscle, the brachialis muscle, and the coracobrachialis muscle in the anterior compartment of the arm as well as the skin overlying the lateral half of the forearm.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

fVXkFC.title: Keratinocyte
fVXkFC.description: A keratin-producing cell predominantly found in the stratified squamous epithelium of the skin (epidermis).

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Cells of the skin

TVX6FC.title: Merkel cell
TVX6FC.description: A cell that acts as a mechanoreceptor for light touch and sensation. Primarily found in sensitive areas of the skin such as finger pads.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Cells of the skin

media.title: Layers of the epidermis and their characteristics

iVXJ8C.title: Sacroiliitis
iVXJ8C.description: A condition of inflammation of the sacroiliac joint. Associated with several disease processes (e.g., ankylosing spondylitis, celiac disease, inflammatory bowel disease). Pain is typically located in the low back and buttock. Can cause symptoms that radiate into the leg, mimicking radiculopathy.

QVXu8C.title: Episcleritis
QVXu8C.description: A condition characterized by inflammation of the episclera, causing a local area of bright red or pink injection. Typically asymptomatic but can cause tenderness and photophobia. Usually self-limited.

jVX_8C.title: Birefringence
jVX_8C.description: A physical phenomenon in which a bundle of light is refracted into two polarized rays upon meeting an anisotropic material. Used in compensated polarized light microscopy of arthrocentesis aspirates. Allows gout (negative birefringence) to be differentiated from calcium pyrophosphate crystal deposition disease (positive birefringence).

PVXWuC.title: Goblet cells
PVXWuC.description: A type of simple columnar epithelial cell that secretes mucin. Primarily found in the respiratory, reproductive, and gastrointestinal tracts and have a basally-displaced nucleus due to the large number of mucin granules present in the cytoplasm.

media.title: Cells and structures of lungs and airways
Respiratory epithelium of the trachea with goblet cells

4VX3uC.title: Scleroderma esophageal dysmotility
4VX3uC.description: A complication of systemic sclerosis and CREST syndrome that manifests as heartburn, dysphagia, or odynophagia. Can cause reflux esophagitis and esophageal strictures due to impaired esophageal motility.

kVXmuC.title: Reid index
kVXmuC.description: The ratio between the thickness of mucus-secreting glands and the thickness of the wall between epithelium and cartilage in the bronchial tree. An increased ratio (> 0.5) is seen in patients with chronic bronchitis.

OVXIuC.title: Club cell
OVXIuC.description: A nonciliated, cuboidal cell located in the bronchioles that degrades toxins and maintains the integrity of the respiratory epithelium. Secretes surfactant, glycosaminoglycans, and lysozymes.

media.title: Cells and structures of lungs and airways

lVXvuC.title: Enterochromaffin cell
lVXvuC.description: A neuroendocrine cell associated with small cell lung carcinoma and neuroendocrine tumors. Found throughout the tracheobronchial epithelium and gastrointestinal tract as single cells with neurosecretory granules.

NVX-uC.title: Alpha cells
NVX-uC.description: A type of pancreatic cell responsible for synthesizing and secreting glucagon. Found in the peripheral parts of pancreatic islets.

media.title: Pancreatic acini and islets of Langerhans

mVXVEC.title: β cell
mVXVEC.description: A pancreatic cell that synthesizes and secretes insulin. Found in the central portions of pancreatic islets.

MVXMEC.title: Phospholipase C
MVXMEC.description: An enzyme that cleaves phospholipids. Functions as part of the IP3/DAG pathway to cleave PIP2 into IP3 and DAG (e.g., in autonomic signaling). Also a virulence factor produced by several bacteria (including Pseudomonas aeruginosa) that degrades cell membranes.

LVXwEC.title: Pyocyanin
LVXwEC.description: A virulence factor produced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa that generates reactive oxygen species that damage host cells. Contributes to the blue-green color of some Pseudomonas infections.

oVX0vC.title: Diphtheria toxin
oVX0vC.description: A bacterial AB toxin produced by Corynebacterium diphtheriae that inactivates elongation factor (EF-2) via ADP-ribosylation, thus impairing protein synthesis. Encoded by β-prophage.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

KVXUvC.title: AB toxin
KVXUvC.description: A multicomponent bacterial toxin that enables binding (B) and subsequent uptake via endocytosis of an active (A) component. Active components are typically adenosine diphosphate (ADP) ribosyltransferases but can have other enzymatic effects (e.g., activation of adenylate cyclase). AB toxins include diphtheria toxin, exotoxin A, Shiga toxin, Shiga-like toxin, heat-labile toxin, edema toxin, cholera toxin, pertussis toxin, tetanospasmin, and botulinum toxin.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

6VXjvC.title: Adenylate cyclase
6VXjvC.description: An enzyme that synthesizes the 2nd messenger cAMP (from ATP), which primarily activates PKA (among other targets). Overactivated by heat-labile toxin from enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC), cholera toxin from Vibrio cholerae, and pertussis toxin from Bordetella pertussis. Mimicked by edema toxin from Bacillus anthracis. In the Lac operon, its activity increases in response to low glucose. Also plays a role in glycogen regulation.

pVXLvC.title: Toxic shock syndrome toxin-1
pVXLvC.description: A bacterial virulence factor produced by Staphylococcus aureus that binds to MHC II and T-cell receptors outside of the antigen binding site. Causes large release of IL-1, IL-2, IFN-γ, and TNF-α, leading to toxic shock syndrome.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

JVXsvC.title: T-cell receptor
JVXsvC.description: A receptor present on T cells that recognize and bind antigen-MHC complexes. Also important in the positive and negative selection process of T cell differentiation.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

qVXCvC.title: Antigen-presenting cell
qVXCvC.description: A group of cells (B cells, Langerhans cells, macrophages, and dendritic cells) that present peptide fragments on their surface via MHC class II.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

IVXYDC.title: Alpha toxin
IVXYDC.description: A bacterial virulence factor produced by Clostridium perfringens and Staphylococcus aureus. C. perfringens alpha toxin acts as a phospholipase to degrade cell membranes and tissue. It is the causative agent of gas gangrene and is responsible for the double zone of hemolysis seen on blood agar cultures. S. aureus alpha toxin causes apoptosis through the formation of pores in the cell membrane.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

7VX4DC.title: Membrane blebbing
7VX4DC.description: A process by which protrusions of cell membrane separate from a cell. Part of the process of apoptosis. Also used by gram-negative bacteria to release endotoxin.

HVXKDC.title: Heat-stable toxin
HVXKDC.description: A virulence factor produced by Enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC) that overactivates guanylate cyclase, increasing production of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP). This causes decreased resorption of sodium, chloride, and water in the gastrointestinal tract.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease
Diarrheagenic E. coli → Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC)

sVXtDC.title: Electrosurgery
sVXtDC.description: The passage of high-frequency alternating electrical current through the skin via a probe, resulting in the generation of heat within the tissue. Can be used to cut tissue (electrosection), destroy tissue (electrodesiccation and fulguration), or stop bleeding (electrocoagulation) and is often used during excisional biopsies and the removal of benign or malignant lesions. Electrosurgery is distinct from electrocautery.

GVXBDC.title: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
GVXBDC.description: A form of pulmonary hypertension (WHO classification Group 4) that is characterized by chronic thromboembolic occlusion of pulmonary vessels. Causes increased resistance in the pulmonary arteries and can lead to right-sided heart failure.

destinations.label: Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale → Etiology

tVXXwC.title: Pronephros
tVXXwC.description: A precursor of the kidney that arises in the cervical region of the embryo during the 4th week of embryonic development and migrates caudally to connect with the pronephric duct (which eventually forms the mesonephric duct). Composed of nephrotomes and nephric tubules. Degenerates with the subsequent development of the mesonephros.

FVXgwC.title: Mesonephros
FVXgwC.description: A temporary kidney that functions as the excretory system during the first trimester and then degenerates before being replaced by the kidneys. Caudal parts of the mesonephros contribute to the mesonephric duct to form the epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal vesicle, and ejaculatory duct.

8VXOwC.title: Metanephros
8VXOwC.description: Appears during the 5th week of fetal development; consists of the ureteric bud (formed in the caudal end of the mesonephric duct) and the blastema (metanephric mesenchyme) and eventually differentiates into the collecting duct system and the excretory system.

uVXpwC.title: Tendinous xanthoma
uVXpwC.description: A firm, mobile, skin-colored, and nontender nodule comprised of extravasated lipoproteins that incorporate into tendons. Most commonly develop on the extensor tendons of the hands and the Achilles tendon. Associated with severe hypercholesterolemia.

EVX8wC.title: Eruptive xanthoma
EVX8wC.description: A small, yellow papule with an erythematous border formed from the deposition of triglycerides. Most commonly develop on the buttocks, back, and extensor surfaces of the extremities. Associated with hypertriglyceridemia and lipoprotein lipase deficiency.

vVXAwC.title: Gastric lymphoma
vVXAwC.description: An uncommon malignancy characterized by a primary lymphoma that develops in gastric tissue. Subtypes include mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) gastric lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the stomach.

DVX19C.title: Examination of the skin
DVX19C.description: A part of the physical examination to assess for dermatologic conditions. Examine the skin, hair, nails, and mucous membranes. Note the morphology of any lesions, including size, shape, color, primary and secondary morphology, configuration, and distribution. Assess skin turgor, moisture, and temperature.

wVXh9C.title: Teniposide
wVXh9C.description: A chemotherapeutic agent that inhibits topoisomerase II, which leads to DNA degradation. Commonly used in refractory acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Adverse effects include myelosuppression and mucositis.

9VXN9C.title: Purine analogues
9VXN9C.description: A class of antimetabolic drugs that mimic the structure of metabolic purine nucleosides. Mechanism of action varies (e.g., inhibition of DNA polymerase, leading to DNA breaks). Examples include chemotherapy agents (e.g., cladribine, fludarabine) and antiviral drugs (e.g., acyclovir, ganciclovir).

xVXE9C.title: Topoisomerase I inhibitors
xVXE9C.description: A class of chemotherapeutic agents that inhibit topoisomerase I and prevent DNA unwinding and replication. Drugs in this class include irinotecan and topotecan. Used to treat ovarian, colorectal, and small cell lung cancers. Adverse effects include severe myelosuppression and diarrhea.

BVXz9C.title: Topoisomerase II inhibitors
BVXz9C.description: A class of chemotherapeutic agents that inhibit topoisomerase II, which leads to DNA double-strand breaks and increased DNA degradation. Drugs in this class include etoposide and teniposide. Used to treat solid tumors (particularly testicular and small cell lung cancer), leukemias, and lymphomas. Adverse effects include myelosuppression and alopecia.

AVXRCC.title: Touton giant cell
AVXRCC.description: A multinucleated histiocyte formed by the fusion of lipid-laden macrophages. Appears on histopathologic examination (e.g., of fat necrosis and xanthomas) as a central ring of nuclei surrounded by abundant clear cytoplasm comprised mainly of accumulated lipids.

_VX5CC.title: Low-density lipoprotein
_VX5CC.description: A lipoprotein that transports cholesterol from the liver to extrahepatic tissue. Characterized by high contents of apolipoprotein B-100.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

zVXrCC.title: Distal interphalangeal joints
zVXrCC.description: The joints between the second (intermediate) and third (distal) phalanges of the hand.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

media.title: Bones of the hand and wrist
Normal appearance of hands and wrists

-VXDCC.title: Extramedullary hematopoiesis
-VXDCC.description: The production of RBCs outside of bone marrow (e.g., paravertebral areas, spleen, liver). Typically a pathologic response to bone marrow dysfunction (i.e., primary myelofibrosis) or metastatic neoplasia. Physiologic during fetal development.

ZeXZxC.title: Foregut
ZeXZxC.description: The proximal part of the gastrointestinal tract that includes the esophagus to the upper duodenum. Supplied by the celiac trunk.

0eXexC.title: Midgut
0eXexC.description: The middle part of the gastrointestinal tract that includes the distal duodenum to the proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon. Supplied by the superior mesenteric artery.

aeXQxC.title: Hindgut
aeXQxC.description: The distal part of the gastrointestinal tract that includes the distal third of the transverse colon to the anal canal (above the pectinate line). Supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery.

media.title: Arterial supply of the gastrointestinal tract

YeXnxC.title: Hepcidin
YeXnxC.description: An acute phase reactant released by the liver that decreases iron absorption by binding and degrading ferroportin on intestinal mucosal cells and macrophages, which inhibits iron transport. Levels are increased in patients with chronic inflammation, which causes anemia of chronic disease.

beXHxC.title: PKD2
beXHxC.description: A gene located on chromosome 4 that codes for polycystin-2. Mutations in this gene are found in 15% of cases of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.

XeX9xC.title: Left ventricular outflow tract
XeX9xC.description: The portion of the left ventricle through which blood flows out of the heart and into the aorta.

ceXaBC.title: DMPK gene
ceXaBC.description: A gene that encodes dystrophia myotonica protein kinase. CTG trinucleotide repeat expansion of this region results in myotonic dystrophy.

1eX2BC.title: Demargination
1eX2BC.description: The loss of neutrophil binding to adhesive endothelial integrin molecules, resulting in elevated circulating neutrophils. Generally induced by glucocorticoid administration or elevated catecholamine levels.

WeXPBC.title: Morbillivirus
WeXPBC.description: A virus of the family of Paramyxoviridae that causes measles (rubeola).

deXoBC.title: Ciliated columnar epithelium
deXoBC.description: A type of epithelium consisting of simple columnar cells with hair-like projections. Predominantly found in the respiratory tract (e.g., bronchioles) and oviducts (e.g., Fallopian tubes) of the female reproductive tract. In the respiratory tract, these cells propel mucus from the airway; in the female reproductive tract, they move the ovum toward the uterine cavity.

media.title: Alveoli and bronchioli of the lung

VeXGBC.title: Single-stranded DNA-binding protein
VeXGBC.description: A type of protein that binds to single-stranded DNA near the replication fork and prevents single strands from reannealing into double-stranded DNA.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

eeXxBC.title: Herpes esophagitis
eeXxBC.description: A complication of herpes simplex virus infection that typically occurs in patients who are immunocompromised. Causes odynophagia, dysphagia, and retrosternal chest pain. Endoscopy shows multiple vesicles and multiple small superficial ulcers that may coalesce to form diffuse superficial ulcers.

destinations.label: Herpes simplex virus infections → Herpes esophagitis

UeXbyC.title: Ovulation
UeXbyC.description: A process in which the mature oocyte is released from the Graffian follicle. Ovulation typically occurs in the middle of the menstrual cycle.

SeXyyC.title: Chest x-ray
