SeXyyC.description: An imaging study used to screen for and diagnose several conditions (e.g., respiratory disease, neoplasms, thoracic trauma) and to assist with various procedures (e.g., monitoring the position of tubes and devices). To minimize errors, interpretation should be performed using a systematic approach such as the ABCDEFGHI mnemonic: Airway, Bones and soft tissue, Cardiovascular, Diaphragm, Edges and effusions, Fields, Gastric bubble, Hardware, and Impression.

heXcAC.title: Clobetasol
heXcAC.description: A high-potency topical corticosteroid. Often used for treatment of eczema, psoriasis, and lichen sclerosus.

3eXSAC.title: Striae (dermatology)
3eXSAC.description: A scarring of the dermis that manifests with erythematous, violaceous, and/or hypopigmented linear patches that become progressively hypopigmented and atrophic. Typically asymptomatic. Primarily located on the abdomen and thighs. Etiologies include pregnancy, rapid weight gain, Cushing syndrome, and chronic topical corticosteroid use.

ReXlAC.title: DNA helicase
ReXlAC.description: An enzyme that initiates DNA replication by unwinding double-stranded DNA at the origin of replication.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

QeXuAC.title: Pedunculation
QeXuAC.description: A morphological descriptor for a lesion connected by an elongated stalk of tissue.

jeX_AC.title: Verrucous
jeX_AC.description: A morphological descriptor for a cutaneous lesion with an exophytic, rough, or cauliflower-like appearance.

PeXW_C.title: Suvorexant
PeXW_C.description: An orexin (also known as hypocretin) receptor antagonist used to treat insomnia. Adverse effects include abnormal dreams, night terrors, headache, and CNS depression.

4eX3_C.title: Vellus hair follicle
4eX3_C.description: A type of hair follicle that extends only into the reticular dermis and is shorter and thinner than terminal hair follicles. Found throughout the body. During puberty, vellus hairs in the axillae and the genital area become terminal hairs.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Skin appendage

keXm_C.title: Terminal hair follicle
keXm_C.description: A type of hair follicle that extends into subcutaneous fat and is taller and thicker than vellus hair follicles. Found on the scalp, eyebrows, and eyelashes. During puberty, vellus hairs in the axillae and the genital area become terminal hairs.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Skin appendage

OeXI_C.title: Superior orbital fissure
OeXI_C.description: An opening in the skull formed by the divergence of the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid bone. Several important structures traverse this cleft, including the oculomotor nerve (CN III), trochlear nerve (CN IV), branches of the ophthalmic nerve (CN V1), abducens nerve (CN VI), and the ophthalmic vein.

meXVzC.title: Pterygopalatine fossa
meXVzC.description: A depression on the pterygoid and palatine bones of the skull. Communicates to the nasal and oral cavities through the sphenopalatine foramen and greater palatine canal respectively.

destinations.label: Skull → Temporal, infratemporal, and pterygopalatine fossae

MeXMzC.title: Examination of the ankle
MeXMzC.description: A part of the musculoskeletal examination. Inspect the ankles and the feet and note any deformities or skin changes. Palpate the joints and joint ligaments to evaluate for tenderness (e.g., from arthritis or sprain). Assess range of motion by stabilizing the heel and inverting/everting the foot and dorsiflexing/plantarflexing the ankle.

LeXwzC.title: Casal necklace
LeXwzC.description: A physical finding characterized by an erythematous or hyperpigmented rash in the distribution of a broad collar (dermatomes C3 and C4). Associated with niacin deficiency.

KeXU-C.title: DNA polymerase I
KeXU-C.description: A prokaryotic enzyme with 5'→3' exonuclease activity that excises RNA primers on lagging strands during DNA synthesis and replaces them with DNA.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

6eXj-C.title: Leading strand
6eXj-C.description: A strand of DNA that is synthesized continuously (due to its free 3' end) in the same direction as the growing replication fork.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

peXL-C.title: Lagging strand
peXL-C.description: A strand of DNA that is synthesized discontinuously (in short segments called Okazaki fragments) in the opposite direction as the growing replication fork due to the 5′Ž→3′ action of DNA polymerases.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

JeXs-C.title: DNA polymerase III
JeXs-C.description: A prokaryotic enzyme that elongates both the leading and lagging strands during DNA replication by adding deoxynucleotides to 3′ ends. Also has 3′→5′ exonuclease activity that proofreads added nucleotides.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

qeXC-C.title: Elongation factor
qeXC-C.description: A protein that facilitates binding of the aminoacyl-tRNA to the A site of the ribosome, which facilitates elongation of the peptide chain during protein synthesis. Bacterial virulence factors (e.g., diphtheria toxin, exotoxin A) inactivate eukaryotic elongation factor 2 (EF-2).

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

IeXYZx.title: Pyrimidine dimer
IeXYZx.description: A DNA lesion in which two pyrimidines are covalently linked following ultraviolet radiation exposure. Usually repaired by nucleotide excision repair.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → Mechanisms of DNA damage

reXfZx.title: Tumor suppressor gene
reXfZx.description: A gene for which loss of function or inactivation leads to an increased risk of developing cancer. Examples include APC (associated with familial adenomatous polyposis), TP53 (associated with Li-Fraumeni syndrome), NF1 (associated with neurofibromatosis type 1), and DNA repair proteins (e.g., BRCA associated with breast cancer).

7eX4Zx.title: Vitelline fistula
7eX4Zx.description: A congenital anomaly caused by complete failure of the vitelline duct to obliterate. The patent duct enables direct communication between the intestine and the umbilicus, which causes discharge of meconium from the umbilicus.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The umbilical cord

HeXKZx.title: Patent urachus
HeXKZx.description: A congenital anomaly caused by failure of the urachus to completely obliterate, which results in communication between the bladder and the umbilicus.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Embryology

seXtZx.title: Acetylcholine
seXtZx.description: A neurotransmitter synthesized from choline and acetyl coenzyme A. Functions as a signal in the neuromuscular junction (motor endplate) to cause muscle contraction. Also functions as a neurotransmitter in the brain, in the internal synapses of the sympathetic nervous system (SNS), and the final synapse of the parasympathetic nervous system (PNS).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

GeXBZx.title: Ubiquitin-proteasome system
GeXBZx.description: A process by which proteins are targeted via ubiquitination for subsequent destruction by proteasomes. Defects in this system are implicated in some cases of Parkinson disease.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Protein degradation and associated diseases

teXX0x.title: Proteasome
teXX0x.description: A barrel-shaped protein complex that degrades damaged and ubiquitin-tagged proteins. Defects in the ubiquitin-proteasome system are associated with Parkinson disease.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Protein degradation and associated diseases

FeXg0x.title: Ubiquitination
FeXg0x.description: A post-translational modification in which ubiquitin protein is attached to a peptide (e.g., at the N-terminal end and/or lysine, cysteine, serine, and threonine residues). Can prevent interactions between proteins or mark a protein for proteasomal degradation.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Protein degradation and associated diseases

8eXO0x.title: Peptide
8eXO0x.description: An organic molecule composed of a linear chain of two or more amino acids.

ueXp0x.title: Peptide bond
ueXp0x.description: A covalent bond formed between the carboxyl group (COOH) of one amino acid and the amino group (NH2) of another amino acid within a protein chain.

EeX80x.title: Alpha helix
EeX80x.description: A common formation found in the secondary structure of proteins.

veXA0x.title: Beta sheets
veXA0x.description: A common formation found in the secondary structure of proteins.

weXhax.title: Zymogen
weXhax.description: A protease that is first secreted in an inactive form to avoid damage to the immediate surrounding tissue. Pancreatic zymogens include pepsinogen, trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, and procarboxypeptidase A.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Digestion and absorption of dietary proteins

9eXNax.title: Pepsin
9eXNax.description: A form of pepsinogen that becomes activated by the acidic pH of the stomach. It is secreted by chief cells in the stomach and breaks down proteins into smaller peptides.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Digestion and absorption of dietary proteins
Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

CeXqax.title: Trypsin
CeXqax.description: A pancreatic enzyme activated from trypsinogen by enteropeptidase. Activates pancreatic zymogens (e.g., chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases).

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Digestion and absorption of dietary proteins

BeXzax.title: Exopeptidase
BeXzax.description: An enzyme that hydrolyzes peptide bonds at the N- or C-terminal end of a protein. The different types of exopeptidases are aminopeptidases, carboxypeptidases (e.g., carboxypeptidase A), dipeptidyl-peptidases (e.g., cathepsin C), peptidyl-dipeptidases (e.g., angiotensin-converting enzyme), tripeptidyl-peptidases, and dipeptidases.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Digestion and absorption of dietary proteins

yeXdYx.title: Carboxypeptidase
yeXdYx.description: A pancreatic exopeptidase that cleaves peptide bonds at the carboxyterminal end of a protein. Carboxypeptidase A targets peptide bonds with aromatic amino acids; carboxypeptidase B primarily cleaves bonds involving basic amino acids.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Digestion and absorption of dietary proteins

_eX5Yx.title: Dipeptidase
_eX5Yx.description: A brush border enzyme of the intestinal mucosa that cleaves dipeptides.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Digestion and absorption of dietary proteins

zeXrYx.title: μ-opioid receptor
zeXrYx.description: A class of G-protein coupled receptors with a high affinity for beta-endorphin and exogenous opioid analgesics (e.g., morphine). Downstream effects of receptor activation include analgesia, euphoria, sedation, respiratory depression, and constipation.

-eXDYx.title: δ-opioid receptor
-eXDYx.description: A class of G-protein coupled receptors. Downstream effects of receptor activation include analgesia, respiratory depression, tolerance, and addiction.

ZUXZbx.title: κ-opioid receptor
ZUXZbx.description: A class of G-protein coupled receptors that bind to opioid compounds. Downstream effects of receptor activation include analgesia, sedation, dysphoria, and constipation.

0UXebx.title: Acetylcholine receptor
0UXebx.description: A transmembrane receptor that responds to acetylcholine. The two main types are nicotinic and muscarinic. Nicotinic receptors are ligand-gated and are found in the autonomic ganglia and at the neuromuscular junction.  Muscarinic receptors are G-protein coupled and are found in various organs, including the heart, brain, and smooth muscle cells.

aUXQbx.title: 5-HT3 receptor
aUXQbx.description: A ligand-gated ion channel receptor that plays a role in emesis, cognition, anxiety, gut motility, and peristalsis. Located both in the central and peripheral nervous systems. Receptor activation causes rapid depolarization of neurons. Antagonists of these receptors (e.g., ondansetron) are used as antinausea medications.

YUXnbx.title: Dextrocardia
YUXnbx.description: An abnormal orientation of the heart in which the apex is located to the right aspect of the mediastinum rather than the left. Often associated with situs inversus (e.g., due to Kartagener syndrome).

bUXHbx.title: Cilia
bUXHbx.description: A cellular structure composed of microtubules in a 9 doublet + 2 central singlet arrangement and a basal body composed of 9 triplets with no central microtubules. Moves via the action of axonemal dynein and gap junctions that coordinate movement. Dysfunctional cilia causes primary ciliary dyskinesia.

cUXaXx.title: Leser-Trélat sign
cUXaXx.description: A paraneoplastic syndrome that manifests as multiple, sudden-onset seborrheic keratoses. Associated with underlying visceral malignancy (especially gastrointestinal cancers).

1UX2Xx.title: Axonemal dynein
1UX2Xx.description: An ATPase that links peripheral doublets of microtubules and causes bending of cilia and flagella.

WUXPXx.title: Erlotinib
WUXPXx.description: A tyrosine kinase epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitor (EGFRi). Used to treat non-small cell lung and pancreatic cancer. Adverse effects include xerosis and an acneiform rash on the face, upper chest, and upper back.

dUXoXx.title: Bortezomib
dUXoXx.description: A proteasome inhibitor that arrests cell growth at the G2-M phase and causes apoptosis. Often used in the treatment of multiple myeloma and mantle cell lymphoma. Adverse effects include peripheral neuropathy and reactivation of herpes zoster (shingles).

VUXGXx.title: Carfilzomib
VUXGXx.description: A proteasome inhibitor that stops cell growth at the G2-M phase and causes apoptosis. Often used to treat multiple myeloma. Adverse effects include fatigue, peripheral neuropathy, and dyspnea.

eUXxXx.title: Vemurafenib
eUXxXx.description: A small molecule inhibitor used in the treatment of malignant melanoma and other cancers with a V600E mutation of the BRAF gene (i.e., valine (V) replaced with glutamic acid (E) at amino acid position 600).

UUXbcx.title: Hypergranulosis
UUXbcx.description: A histopathological finding characterized by thickening of the stratum granulosum of the epidermis. Often seen in patients with lichen planus.

2UXTcx.title: Pseudofolliculitis barbae
2UXTcx.description: An inflammatory skin condition characterized by firm, hyperpigmented, tender, pruritic papules and pustules on hair-growing areas on the lower face. Often caused by a reaction to ingrown hairs (e.g., after shaving). More common in Black males.

destinations.label: Dermatological conditions in skin of color → Pseudofolliculitis barbae

fUXkcx.title: Dermal papilla
fUXkcx.description: An extension of the papillary dermis into the epidermis.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Structure of the skin

TUX6cx.title: Red neuron
TUX6cx.description: A histopathologic finding of damaged neurons characterized by marked eosinophilic staining due to degradation of proteins within the cytoplasm. Seen within the first 12-24 hours after ischemia.

gUXFcx.title: Gangrenous necrosis
gUXFcx.description: A subtype of coagulative necrosis most commonly seen in the limbs and gastrointestinal tract (after chronic ischemia). Further divided into dry gangrene (caused by ischemia) and wet gangrene (caused by superinfection).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Necrosis

media.title: Dry gangrene in peripheral arterial disease

3UXS1x.title: Procarbazine
3UXS1x.description: An alkylating chemotherapeutic agent of the hydrazine class. Used to treat Hodgkin lymphoma. Its mechanism of action is not well understood. Adverse effects include myelosuppression, pulmonary toxicity, and increased risk of developing leukemia.

RUXl1x.title: Elliptocyte
RUXl1x.description: A pathologic red blood cell form characterized by elliptical shape. Seen in patients with hereditary elliptocytosis.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

iUXJ1x.title: Hereditary elliptocytosis
iUXJ1x.description: An asymptomatic condition characterized by the presence of elliptocytes in the blood. Caused by mutations in genes encoding RBC membrane proteins (e.g., spectrin, protein 4.1).

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Erythrocyte morphology

QUXu1x.title: Continuous murmur
QUXu1x.description: A heart murmur that is audible during diastole and systole. Occurs during hyperdynamic states, as well as in patent ductus arteriosus and arteriovenous fistulas.

destinations.label: Acyanotic congenital heart defects → Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)

jUX_1x.title: Corrosive esophagitis
jUX_1x.description: A condition caused by ingestion of caustic substances (e.g., bleach, detergent). Causes ulceration and fibrosis of the esophagus. Complications include strictures, perforation, and increased incidence of squamous cell carcinoma.

PUXWWx.title: Autonomic nervous system
PUXWWx.description: The division of the peripheral nervous system that controls muscles and glands, largely subconsciously. Composed of the sympathetic and parasympathetic domains.

media.title: Overview of somatic and autonomic motor pathways and neurotransmitters
Autonomic innervation of the gastrointestinal tract

4UX3Wx.title: Cholesterolosis
4UX3Wx.description: Mucosal changes within the gallbladder wall due to excess cholesterol in bile. Cholesterol deposits within macrophages, which causes a yellowish, speckled mucosal coloration. Mucosal changes can be localized or diffuse.

kUXmWx.title: Clear cell
kUXmWx.description: A cell with clear cytoplasm under hematoxylin and eosin staining due to glycogen- or lipid-filled cytoplasm. Associated with a subtype of renal cell carcinoma and malignancies of the female reproductive tract.

OUXIWx.title: Corpus spongiosum
OUXIWx.description: A sponge-like erectile vascular tissue on the ventral side of the penis. Surrounds the penile urethra and originates at the level of the urethral bulb. Prevents the urethra from collapsing during erection.

lUXvWx.title: AP site
lUXvWx.description: A site in a double-stranded DNA molecule that no longer has a base attached to the underlying phosphate backbone. Can be a result of direct DNA damage or through the action of base-specific glycosylases during normal base excision repair.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

NUX-Wx.title: Bloom syndrome
NUX-Wx.description: A rare, autosomal recessive disorder caused by chromosomal instability due to mutations in the BLM gene, a member of the DNA helicase family. Patients present with small stature (with normal body proportions), café au lait spots, photosensitivity, infertility in men, immunodeficiency, and an increased risk of developing cancers.

mUXVdx.title: Alpha-1 receptor
mUXVdx.description: A subset of G-protein coupled adrenergic receptors. Activation causes vascular smooth muscle contraction, sphincter muscle contraction (e.g., in the bladder and intestine), and pupillary dilation. Commonly used pharmacologic agonists include midodrine and phenylephrine, which are used to increase blood pressure.

5UXidx.title: Linea alba
5UXidx.description: A fibrous structure formed by the aponeuroses of the abdominal muscles. Runs from the xiphoid process to the pubic symphysis on the anterior abdomen.

media.title: Peritoneum and fascias of the abdomen

MUXMdx.title: Tuberoinfundibular pathway
MUXMdx.description: A major dopaminergic pathway within the CNS responsible for the regulation of prolactin secretion from the anterior pituitary gland; dopaminergic neurons originating in the arcuate nucleus in the tuberal region of the hypothalamus project to the median eminence, which is located directly above the pituitary stalk. The neurons release dopamine to inhibit the secretion of prolactin from the anterior pituitary gland.

nUX7dx.title: Endopeptidase
nUX7dx.description: An enzyme that hydrolyzes peptide bonds at a specific site within a polypeptide chain. Examples include chymotrypsin, trypsin, pepsin, elastase, collagenase, and matrix metalloproteinase.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Digestion and absorption of dietary proteins

LUXwdx.title: Immunoglobulin class switching
LUXwdx.description: A mechanism that changes the type of immunoglobulin produced by a mature B cell, usually from IgM to another isotype (e.g., IgE, IgA, and IgG). The heavy chain constant region (Fc region) is changed while the heavy chain variable region, which is specific to the antigen, remains the same.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

oUX0Vx.title: Lymphotoxin-alpha
oUX0Vx.description: A cytokine secreted by lymphocytes that plays an important role in the development of secondary lymphoid organs (e.g., Peyer's patches), regulation of innate immune response, and prevention of tumor growth by promoting cancer cell death.

destinations.label: Cytokines and eicosanoids → Interferons and tumor necrosis factor family

KUXUVx.title: Peyer's patches
KUXUVx.description: Aggregated lymphoid nodules that belong to the mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) throughout the ileum. They contain macrophages, dendritic cells, B lymphocytes, and T lymphocytes that monitor the intestinal lumen for pathogenic bacteria and generate an appropriate immune response within the ileal mucosa.

pUXLVx.title: Primary emotions
pUXLVx.description: Emotions that are innate and recognized universally across cultures. The exact list of core primary emotions varies across theorists but commonly includes joy, fear, anger, sadness, disgust, surprise, and contempt.

JUXsVx.title: Secondary emotions
JUXsVx.description: Emotions that are shaped by the interaction between acquired sociocultural norms and primary emotions. Examples include shame, guilt, pride, and embarrassment.

qUXCVx.title: Anticodon
qUXCVx.description: A sequence of three nucleotides in tRNA that is is complementary to the codon on mRNA.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

IUXYex.title: Start codon
IUXYex.description: A sequence of three nucleotides (AUG) that initiates peptide formation with methionine.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

rUXfex.title: Stop codon
rUXfex.description: A sequence of three nucleotides that terminates peptide formation. The three RNA stop codons are UAG, UAA, and UGA.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

7UX4ex.title: Cardinal ligament
7UX4ex.description: A paired ligament that connects the cervix and the lateral fornices of the vagina with the lateral pelvic wall. Contains the uterine artery and vein, which serve as the main blood supply of the uterus.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Ligaments of the female pelvis

sUXtex.title: Round ligament of uterus
sUXtex.description: A ligament that connects the uterine fundus to the labia majora and passes through the inguinal canal. Contains the Sampson artery.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Ligaments of the female pelvis

GUXBex.title: Inosine
GUXBex.description: A nucleoside formed by attachment of the base hypoxanthine to a ribose ring. Present in tRNA and permits wobble base pair formation.

FUXgUx.title: Preinitiation complex
FUXgUx.description: A 43S ribonucleoprotein preinitiation complex containing the small ribosomal subunit (40S) and the translation initiation complex (i.e., an initiator tRNA, GTP, and eIF1/2/3/4 complexes). It binds to a start codon (AUG and rarely GUG) on RNA, at which point the 60S ribosome joins (forming an 80S ribosome) and translation begins.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Stages of transcription
Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

8UXOUx.title: Ovarian follicle
8UXOUx.description: The basic unit of the female reproductive system. Contains the maturing oocyte. Each unit contains one ovum surrounded by a layer of granulosa cells. These cells are surrounded by the theca folliculi.

uUXpUx.title: Polyene
uUXpUx.description: A group of antifungal agents, that bind to ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane, which forms pores that disrupt electrolyte balance. Used to treat both minor fungal infections (e.g., nystatin for mucocutaneous candidiasis) and severe fungal infections (e.g., amphotericin B for systemic mycoses).

EUX8Ux.title: Benzofuran
EUX8Ux.description: A class of antifungal medications that bind to keratin, interfering with microtubule function and disrupting fungal mitosis, which inhibits fungal growth. Griseofulvin is a benzofuran.

vUXAUx.title: Chaperone protein
vUXAUx.description: A class of proteins that facilitate protein folding and assembly. Also prevent newly translated polypeptide chains from forming aggregates.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Protein folding and misfolding

wUXh2x.title: Acylation
wUXh2x.description: A form of post-translational modification in which acyl-groups (lipids) are added to proteins.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

CUXq2x.title: GPI anchor
CUXq2x.description: A glycolipid that anchors cell-surface proteins on the plasma membrane of hematopoietic cells. Deficiency or decreased activity of GPI causes paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria due to the absence of surface proteins like CD55 and CD59, which are inhibitors of complement activation.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

xUXE2x.title: Phosphorylation
xUXE2x.description: The attachment of a phosphoryl group to a molecule. Plays a role in several physiologic processes, including enzyme regulation, carbohydrate metabolism, and post-translational modification.

BUXz2x.title: Acetylation
BUXz2x.description: The linkage of an acetyl group by acetyltransferases.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

AUXRfx.title: Carboxylation
AUXRfx.description: A chemical reaction that inserts a carboxyl group (-COOH) into a compound, which creates a carboxylic acid. Enzymes catalyzing this reaction are called carboxylases (e.g., acetyl-CoA carboxylase).

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

Z2XZTx.title: Porta hepatis
Z2XZTx.description: A fissure that runs along the inferior surface of the liver. Contains the hepatic ducts, branches of the hepatic artery, and the portal vein.

02XeTx.title: Portal triad
02XeTx.description: A structure contained within the free border of the lesser omentum that contains the proper hepatic artery, portal vein, and common bile duct. Also contains lymphatics and branches of the vagus nerve.

a2XQTx.title: DNA clamp
a2XQTx.description: A subunit of DNA polymerase responsible for anchoring DNA polymerase by closing a clamp around DNA.

X2X9Tx.title: DNA polymerase
X2X9Tx.description: A group of enzymes that elongate DNA strands during DNA replication by adding nucleotides to an RNA primer.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

c2Xagx.title: Maculopapular rash
c2Xagx.description: A morphological descriptor for a rash with a mixture of palpable and nonpalpable lesions ≤ 1 cm in size. Individual lesions cannot be both macular and papular.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Complex skin lesions

V2XGgx.title: Keto-enol tautomerism
V2XGgx.description: A transient tautomeric shift of nucleotide bases from the usual keto-configuration to the enol-configuration that can occur during DNA replication and repair. The switch in base configuration results in mismatched base pairing (e.g., enol-thymine pairs with guanine instead of adenine), which can cause spontaneous mutations during DNA replication and repair.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → Mechanisms of DNA damage

e2Xxgx.title: Munro microabscess
e2Xxgx.description: A histopathological finding characterized by an accumulation of neutrophils in the stratum corneum surrounded by parakeratosis. Characteristic of psoriasis.

U2XbSx.title: DNA mismatch repair
U2XbSx.description: A form of single-stranded DNA repair in which replications errors in newly synthesized DNA (e.g., base-base mismatches and mispairings caused by erroneous base insertion or deletion) are recognized and removed. The gap is then filled and resealed. Occurs primarily during S phase. Defective in patients with hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (Lynch syndrome).

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

22XTSx.title: Nonhomologous end joining
22XTSx.description: A mechanism of double-stranded DNA repair in which DNA ligase connects two ends of the break without a homologous template (which can lead to lost DNA). Defective in patients with ataxia telangiectasia.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

S2XySx.title: Mucociliary clearance
S2XySx.description: A mechanism by which cilia in the respiratory tract and sinuses direct mucus and debris toward the pharynx. Defects in this mechanism increase the risk of developing upper respiratory tract infections and sinusitis.

h2Xchx.title: Caspofungin
h2Xchx.description: A group of antifungal agents that inhibits synthesis of β-glucan (a component of the fungal cell wall). Used to treat invasive aspergillosis and Candida infections. Agents include caspofungin, micafungin, and anidulafungin. Generally well-tolerated, but adverse effects include mild, asymptomatic elevations of aminotransferases and alkaline phosphatase, gastrointestinal upset, and flushing (due to histamine release).

32XShx.title: Anidulafungin
32XShx.description: An antifungal agent that inhibits synthesis of β-glucan, a component of the fungal cell wall. Used to treat invasive aspergillosis and Candida infections.

R2Xlhx.title: Micafungin
R2Xlhx.description: A group of antifungal agents that inhibits synthesis of β-glucan (a component of the fungal cell wall). Used to treat invasive aspergillosis and Candida infections. Agents include caspofungin, micafungin, and anidulafungin. Generally well-tolerated, but adverse effects include mild, asymptomatic elevations of aminotransferases and alkaline phosphatase, gastrointestinal upset, and flushing (due to histamine release).

i2XJhx.title: Iduronate 2-sulfatase
i2XJhx.description: A lysosomal enzyme responsible for the degradation of glycosaminoglycans such as dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate. Deficiency of this enzyme results in Hunter syndrome.

Q2Xuhx.title: β-glucocerebrosidase
Q2Xuhx.description: A lysosomal enzyme responsible for the degradation of sphingolipid glucocerebroside during glycolipid metabolism. Deficiency is associated with Gaucher disease. Mutation in the glucocerebrosidase gene is associated with increased risk of Parkinson disease.

j2X_hx.title: α-Galactosidase A
j2X_hx.description: A lysosomal enzyme responsible for the degradation of the glycolipid ceramide trihexoside (globotriaosylceramide). Deficiency of this enzyme causes Fabry disease.

l2Xv3x.title: Cervical effacement
l2Xv3x.description: Thinning of the cervix that occurs during labor. Usually reported in percentage and used as a component of the modified Bishop score that assesses the likelihood of successful induction.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Normal spontaneous labor

N2X-3x.title: Common gamma chain
N2X-3x.description: A cytokine receptor subunit of several interleukins, including IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, and IL-9. An X-linked recessive defect of this protein is the most common cause of severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital mixed immunodeficiencies

m2XVRx.title: Calcipotriene
m2XVRx.description: A synthetic, topical vitamin D analog used in the treatment of plaque psoriasis for its antiproliferative effects on keratinocytes.

M2XMRx.title: Minoxidil
M2XMRx.description: A direct arteriolar vasodilator used to treat androgenetic alopecia and severe refractory hypertension.

n2X7Rx.title: BBB
n2X7Rx.description: An abbreviation that primarily refers to bundle branch block or blood brain barrier.

L2XwRx.title: Kegel exercises
L2XwRx.description: Pelvic floor strengthening exercises used in the management of urinary and fecal incontinence and to prevent pelvic organ prolapse. While keeping the stomach, back, and gluteus muscles relaxed, the patient contracts their pelvic floor muscles (i.e., squeezes muscles that stop the flow of urine or prevent flatulence) for 3 seconds and then rests for 3 seconds. This is repeated 10 times, 3 times a day. Patients should gradually increase the contraction time to 10 seconds.

o2X0ix.title: Gartner duct cyst
o2X0ix.description: A type of vaginal cyst. Originates from a vestigial remnant of the mesonephric duct and is usually asymptomatic but can present with dysmenorrhea and  dyspareunia in rare cases.

p2XLix.title: James-Lange theory
p2XLix.description: A psychological theory developed by William James and Carl Lange, which states that the physiological response to a stimulus causes an emotional experience, and that self-perception of the response (rather than cognition) constitutes the emotion.

J2Xsix.title: Mass effect
J2Xsix.description: Signs and symptoms caused by compression and/or displacement of normal tissues by a tumor, aneurysm, hematoma, and/or abscess, e.g., elevated intracranial pressure caused by a brain tumor.

I2XYQx.title: Aortic aneurysm
I2XYQx.description: A pathological dilation of the aorta due to a weakened vessel wall. Symptoms depend on the location (e.g., ascending thoracic, descending thoracic, abdominal, thoracoabdominal) and size of the aneurysm.

72X4Qx.title: Glomerular basement membrane
72X4Qx.description: An extracellular matrix component that is part of the three-layered glomerular filtration barrier. Contains macromolecules such as collagen IV and laminin; and negatively-charged heparan sulfate proteoglycans, which make it impermeable to proteins with a negative charge (e.g., albumin).

G2XBQx.title: 5′ untranslated region
G2XBQx.description: The region of an mRNA that is directly upstream from the initiation codon.

F2Xgjx.title: Release factor
F2Xgjx.description: A protein that recognizes the stop codon on the mRNA, marking the final step of protein synthesis. Initiates the release of a completed polypeptide chain from the ribosomal complex via hydrolytic cleaving of peptidyl tRNA bonds.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

82XOjx.title: Counseling on lifestyle modifications to improve mood
82XOjx.description: A set of strategies for supporting patients undergoing treatment for mood disorders. Includes relaxation techniques, exercise, mindfulness, and meditation.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Counseling on sleep hygiene and lifestyle modifications to improve mood

u2Xpjx.title: Photosensitivity
u2Xpjx.description: An abnormal skin reaction to UV light. Often used synonymously with photosensitivity disorder, but may also be used to describe individuals who burn rapidly when exposed to UV light.

E2X8jx.title: Genetic code
E2X8jx.description: The relationship between the DNA (or mRNA) nucleotide sequence and the respective amino acid sequence of a protein.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

v2XAjx.title: Protein modification
v2XAjx.description: The modification of proteins following their synthesis by ribosomes. Includes cleavage of the polypeptide chain, modification of amino acid residues, formation of disulfide bridges, and covalent addition of functional groups (e.g., phosphate).

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

C2XqPx.title: Hydrogen bond
C2XqPx.description: A non-covalent bond that is formed between a hydrogen atom and a more electronegative species (e.g., oxygen, nitrogen). Hydrogen bonds are responsible for the secondary and tertiary structures of proteins as well as the double helical structure of DNA.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

x2XEPx.title: Allergic contact dermatitis
x2XEPx.description: A form of contact dermatitis caused by a type IV hypersensitivity reaction after skin exposure to contact allergens (e.g., chemicals, metals). Typically manifests with erythematous, pruritic papules and plaques and, in severe cases, vesicles with serous oozing.

_2X54x.title: Base-specific glycosylase
_2X54x.description: An enzyme that cleaves the bond between deoxyribose and a modified or mismatched DNA base, creating an abasic site (AP site). Initiates base excision repair.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

ZfXZkx.title: Somatotropinoma
ZfXZkx.description: A pituitary adenoma that secretes growth hormone. Accounts for 10–15% of pituitary adenomas and is the most common cause of acromegaly or gigantism. Can also result in a deficiency of other pituitary hormones due to the destruction of normal pituitary gland tissue and mass effects (e.g., headache, bitemporal hemianopsia, diplopia).

afXQkx.title: Gluconeogenesis
afXQkx.description: A metabolic pathway that produces glucose from noncarbohydrate, carbon-containing substances such as glucogenic amino acids, triglycerides, and glycerol. Primarily takes place in the liver.

YfXnkx.title: Polygenic inheritance
YfXnkx.description: A mode of inheritance characterized by multiple genetic loci whose allelic contributions determine the resulting phenotype. Several genotypes can cause the same phenotype. Examples include height, skin color, and eye color.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Other types of inheritance

bfXHkx.title: Fibrinous pericarditis
bfXHkx.description: Acute pericarditis caused by exudative inflammation, which results in fibrin and leukocytes extravasation into the pericardial space.

XfX9kx.title: Macrophage
XfX9kx.description: A white blood cell that is part of the mononuclear phagocytic system. Phagocytizes dead tissue, cellular debris, bacteria, cancer cells, and any substance that contains foreign proteins on its surface.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

media.title: How macrophages engulf and destroy pathogens

cfXaOx.title: Conotruncal cardiac abnormalities
cfXaOx.description:
A group of conditions characterized by defects in the cardiac outflow tract. Includes transposition of great vessels, tetralogy of Fallot, and persistent truncus arteriosus. Often associated with failure of neural crest cell migration.
ƒ

1fX2Ox.title: Aorticopulmonary septum
1fX2Ox.description: A structure that forms during heart morphogenesis. Normally rotates and fuses the ventricular septum to form the membranous interventricular septum, which closes the interventricular foramen. Failure to rotate causes transposition of the great vessels.

WfXPOx.title: Cardiac morphogenesis
WfXPOx.description: The embryological development of the heart. Involves cardiac looping to establish left-right polarity, septation of the chambers, outflow tract formation, and valve development.

dfXoOx.title: Zinc oxide
dfXoOx.description: The active ingredient in most inorganic sunscreens; absorbs UVA and UVB radiation to prevent skin damage. Also the active ingredient in barrier creams (e.g., to treat diaper dermatitis); prevents chemical irritants and moisture from contacting damaged skin.

VfXGOx.title: Para-aminobenzoic acid
VfXGOx.description: A component of organic suncreens that absorbs UVB radiation.

efXxOx.title: Achievement motivation
efXxOx.description: The desire to pursue success, excel at challenging tasks, and meet a high standard of excellence. Individuals differ in their need for achievement, which influences how they set goals, handle challenges, and respond to success or failure. Individuals with high achievement motivation are driven by intrinsic motivation and personal mastery, choose moderately challenging tasks, and have a high internal locus of control. Individuals with low achievement motivation are driven by the desire to avoid failure rather than to succeed, choose very easy or very hard tasks to avoid blame for failure, and have a high external locus of control.

UfXblx.title: Hierarchy of needs
UfXblx.description: A psychological theory developed by Abraham Maslow, which argues that motivation arises from the drive to fulfill a hierarchy of needs, commonly illustrated as a pyramid. Basic physiological and safety needs are the foundation of the pyramid, while higher-order needs, such as love and belonging, esteem, and self-actualization form its peak. Maslow proposed that lower-order needs must be satisfied before higher-order needs can be meaningfully pursued. A key criticism of this theory is that human behavior does not adhere to a hierarchy of needs; individuals may prioritize social connection or personal growth even when foundational needs remain unmet.

2fXTlx.title: Juxtaglomerular complex
2fXTlx.description: A specialized structure of the kidney that is located between the distal convoluted tubule and the afferent arteriole of the nephron. Involved in the regulation of NaCl excretion and the glomerular filtration rate (GFR).

ffXklx.title: Mononuclear phagocytic system
ffXklx.description: A collection of monocytes and monocyte-derived tissue macrophages that functions as part of the innate immune system. Responsible for phagocytosis of pathogens, subsequent antigen presentation, and secretion of proinflammatory cytokines.

TfX6lx.title: Serratia
TfX6lx.description: A catalase-positive, gram-negative bacillus in the family Enterobacteriaceae. Causes nosocomial pneumonia and urinary tract infections. Some strains produce a red pigment.

gfXFlx.title: Proto-oncogene
gfXFlx.description: A gene that, when mutated, increases the risk of developing cancer. These genes are typically involved in protein production for cell growth and differentiation. Examples include BRAF, JAK2, and KRAS.

SfXylx.title: MYCL1 gene
SfXylx.description: A proto-oncogene that encodes for the transcription factor L-myc-1 protein. Increased expression or amplification of the MYCL1 gene is associated with the development of small cell lung cancer.

hfXcNx.title: Glucogenic amino acid
hfXcNx.description: An amino acid that is metabolized to pyruvate and to metabolites of the citric acid cycle.

destinations.label: Amino acids →  Catabolism of the carbon skeleton of amino acids

3fXSNx.title: Ketogenic amino acid
3fXSNx.description: An amino acid that is metabolized into acetyl-CoA, which can then be used to synthesize ketone bodies. Two amino acids are exclusively ketogenic: leucine and lysine.

destinations.label: Amino acids →  Catabolism of the carbon skeleton of amino acids

media.title: Degradation of glucogenic and ketogenic amino acids via the citric acid cycle

ifXJNx.title: Counseling on contraception options
ifXJNx.description: A set of strategies for discussing contraception with patients. Discuss the patient's priorities regarding whether, when, and how to have children. If the patient wishes to know about contraceptive options, discuss their effectiveness and adverse effects. The most effective options are intrauterine devices and implants, followed by injectable contraceptives, oral contraceptives, and the transdermal patch. Less effective options include diaphragms and condoms.

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual health

QfXuNx.title: Antoni A region
QfXuNx.description: A histopathologic feature of schwannomas characterized by closely packed, highly cellular regions of tissue with nuclei stacked in palisades.

destinations.label: Brain tumors → Primary brain tumors according to age

PfXWmx.title: Endarteritis
PfXWmx.description: A condition of inflammation and proliferation of the intimal layer (inner layer) of an artery, which results in occlusion of the arterial lumen.

4fX3mx.title: Vasa vasorum
4fX3mx.description: A group of small blood vessels and/or capillaries that supply the wall of large blood vessels such as the aorta and vena cava.

kfXmmx.title: Stroke volume
kfXmmx.description: The volume of blood pumped by the left ventricle in a single heartbeat. Defined as end-diastolic volume (EDV) minus end-systolic volume (ESV). Increases with increased contractility, increased preload, and decreased afterload.

OfXImx.title: Ribonuclease H
OfXImx.description: A family of endonucleases found in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes that can hydrolyze the RNA segment of RNA/DNA duplexes that form during replication and repair, thus preventing DNA instability.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

lfXvmx.title: Ryanodine receptor channel
lfXvmx.description: A calcium channel in the membrane of sarcoplasmic reticulum. There are three isoforms: RYR1 primarily in skeletal myocytes, RYR2 primarily in cardiac myocytes, and RYR3 in various cells including neurons. Mutations in RYR1 increase susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia. Mutations in RYR2 increase the risk of arrhythmias. Dantrolene is an antagonist of this receptor.

NfX-mx.title: Urachus
NfX-mx.description: A structure in the fetus that connects the apex of the urinary bladder and the yolk sac. It arises between the 5th and 7th week of fetal development from the allantois, after the allantois invades the urogenital sinus (3rd week). The urachus eventually degenerates to form the median umbilical ligament. Failure of the urachal to degenerate can cause a urachal sinus, urachal diverticulum, urachal cyst, or urachal fistula.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Embryology

KfXUMx.title: Neovascularization
KfXUMx.description: The formation of new blood vessels in normal or abnormal tissue, as well as in abnormal locations (e.g., retinal neovascularization). Vessels are formed de novo, rather than arising from pre-existing blood vessels.

6fXjMx.title: Transforming growth factor-beta
6fXjMx.description: A multifunctional cytokine secreted by numerous types of immune cells. Its anti-inflammatory properties include inhibiting B lymphocytes and macrophages and activating regulatory T cells and Th17 cells. It also mediates wound healing by stimulating angiogenesis, granulation tissue formation, and collagen production.

destinations.label: Cytokines and eicosanoids → Transforming growth factor family

pfXLMx.title: Basal metabolic rate
pfXLMx.description: The amount of energy required to maintain basic life-sustaining function at rest in a temperate environment during digestive inactivity. Typically measured in the morning, after an overnight fast and 24 hours without exercise.

JfXsMx.title: AP lyase
JfXsMx.description: An enzyme responsible for cleaving the phosphodiester backbone on the 3' end of a damaged nucleotide during base excision repair.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

qfXCMx.title: AP endonuclease
qfXCMx.description: An enzyme responsible for cleaving the phosphodiester backbone on the 5' end of a damaged nucleotide during base excision repair.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

IfXYnx.title: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases
IfXYnx.description: A group of enzymes that each add a specific amino acid to the 3'-terminal end of a tRNA molecule. There is one version of this enzyme for every amino acid and corresponding tRNA pair.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → tRNA charging

rfXfnx.title: Tryptase
rfXfnx.description: A proteinase released during mast cell degranulation. Used as a marker of mast cell activation, and can help identify a type 1 hypersensitivity reaction if high levels are measured in the serum. Commonly used to differentiate anaphylaxis from mimics such as hereditary angioedema when the diagnosis is uncertain.

destinations.label: Hypersensitivity reactions → Type I hypersensitivity reaction

7fX4nx.title: Histamine
7fX4nx.description: A vasoactive amine and inflammatory mediator released during mast cell degranulation. Excess activity mediates symptoms of anaphylactic reactions, including hypotension, swelling, erythema, and bronchospasm.

destinations.label: Hypersensitivity reactions → Type I hypersensitivity reaction

HfXKnx.title: Cytokine
HfXKnx.description: A cell signaling protein. Includes chemokines, interferons, interleukins, and other proteins.

sfXtnx.title: Cathepsin
sfXtnx.description: A protease typically found in lysosomes that activates matrix metalloproteinases.

GfXBnx.title: Hereditary xanthinuria
GfXBnx.description: Hereditary xanthinuria is an autosomal recessive condition caused by a deficiency in xanthine dehydrogenase. This normally catalyzes the conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid. The enzyme's deficiency causes increased concentration and deposition of xanthine in the kidneys and skeletal muscle, leading to renal toxicity and myopathy by adolescence and early adulthood.

tfXXLx.title: Patient-centered care
tfXXLx.description: A clinical model of practice that focuses on open communication between the patient and the clinician, shared decision-making, and a shared goal of alleviating discomfort for the patient.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

8fXOLx.title: Urea cycle
8fXOLx.description: A series of biochemical reactions that produce urea from ammonia, a product of amino acid catabolism. Takes place primarily in the liver and to a lesser extent in the kidney.

ufXpLx.title: Nephron
ufXpLx.description: The functional unit of the kidney. Made up of a glomerulus (the major filtration structure) and the tubules (major absorbing and concentrating structure).

vfXALx.title: Proximal convoluted tubule
vfXALx.description: The portion of the nephron between the Bowman capsule and the loop of Henle. Reabsorbs solutes including electrolytes, glucose, amino acids, urea, phosphate, and citrate.

media.title: Overview of the proximal convoluted tubule

DfX1ox.title: Distal convoluted tubule
DfX1ox.description: The segment of the nephron located between the ascending loop of Henle and the connecting tubule and collecting duct. 10-15% of Na+ is resorbed in the DCT; Na+ resorption is regulated by aldosterone. ADH regulates the tubule's water permeability. The DCT is the site of PTH-regulated Ca2+ resorption.

wfXhox.title: Loop of Henle
wfXhox.description: A portion of the nephron comprised of a descending and an ascending loop. Modulating urine tonicity and electrolyte reabsorption. The descending part increases tonicity through free water reabsorption in contrast to the ascending part, which is impermeable to water and reabsorbs only electrolytes, which decreases tonicity.

xfXEox.title: Adenosine (drug)
xfXEox.description: A class V anti-arrhythmic drug that causes a short-term heart block by slowing down conduction in the atrioventricular node.

BfXzox.title: Total complement activity
BfXzox.description: The total complement activity test measures the capacity of serum to lyse sheep erythrocytes coated with anti-sheep antibodies (IgG). The term "CH50" refers to the dilution at which serum lyses 50% of the sheep erythrocytes. A decrease in total complement activity occurs in complement deficiencies (e.g., cirrhosis and hepatitis), while an increase is seen in proinflammatory conditions (e.g., cancer and ulcerative colitis).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital complement deficiencies

_fX5Kx.title: Interleukin-17
_fX5Kx.description: A pro-inflammatory cytokine produced by T helper 17 (Th17) cells in response to interleukin-23 signaling. Involved in chemokine induction that attracts monocytes, macrophages, and neutrophils to the site of inflammation. Associated with some autoimmune diseases. Deficiency of IL-17 causes chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis.

-fXDKx.title: Hypoxanthine
-fXDKx.description: A purine derivative formed from the deamination of adenosine.

0TXe6x.title: Histone acetylation
0TXe6x.description: A mechanism of gene regulation that involves the linkage of an acetyl group to the lysine residues of histone proteins by histone acetyltransferases. This process results in less positively charged histones that do not strongly bind to DNA. Thus, DNA can be easily transcribed.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

aTXQ6x.title: Histone methylation
aTXQ6x.description: The addition of methyl groups to histones. Typically results in suppression of transcription.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

WTXPpx.title: Microsatellite DNA
WTXPpx.description: A repetitive, 2-6 nucleotide sequence of DNA. Defects in mismatch repair genes can cause these DNA regions to expand (microsatellite instability).

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

dTXopx.title: Pre-mRNA
dTXopx.description: A type of heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA) that undergoes several modifications (e.g., splicing, addition of a polyadenylate tail and a 5' cap) to become messenger RNA (mRNA).

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

VTXGpx.title: Myocardial stunning
VTXGpx.description: A condition of transient cardiac dysfunction that occurs after acute coronary ischemia (even after timely, successful revascularization). Can also manifest as a cardiotoxic adverse effect of treatment with the monoclonal anti-HER2 antibody trastuzumab.

eTXxpx.title: Injectisome
eTXxpx.description: A needle-like protein appendage present on some gram-negative bacteria (including Pseudomonas, Salmonella, Shigella, certain strains of E.coli). Facilitates the direct delivery of toxins into the host cells.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

2TXTJx.title: IgA protease
2TXTJx.description: A bacterial enzyme that cleaves mucosal IgA and allows organisms to adhere to and colonize mucous membranes. Produced by Streptococcus, Haemophilus, and Neisseria species.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

fTXkJx.title: Lipopolysaccharide
fTXkJx.description: An endotoxin located in the outer membrane of gram-negative bacteria. Composed of a core polysaccharide, O antigen (immunogenic component), and lipid A (toxic component). Triggers macrophage, complement, and tissue factor activations. Associated with septic shock.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

STXyJx.title: Constitutional symptoms
STXyJx.description: A collection of nonspecific symptoms such as weight loss, fever, chills, night sweats, changes in appetite, changes in sleep, chronic pain, fatigue, and malaise. Typically evaluated on a review of systems with further evaluation based on pertinent positives and negatives.

3TXSqx.title: Greater sac
3TXSqx.description: A large portion of the peritoneal cavity that extends from the diaphragm to the floor of the pelvis. Connects to the lesser sac via the omental foramen.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

QTXuqx.title: Oogenesis
QTXuqx.description: The development of an immature oocyte into a mature egg cell.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Oogenesis and folliculogenesis

jTX_qx.title: Folliculogenesis
jTX_qx.description: The process of the maturation of ovarian follicles in females. Stimulated by follicle-stimulating hormone. Necessary for oogenesis to occur.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Oogenesis and folliculogenesis

NTX-Ix.title: GpIIb/IIIa receptor
NTX-Ix.description: A binding site for fibrinogen and von Willebrand factor on the surface of platelets. Involved in platelet aggregation and endothelial adherence.

5TXirx.title: Toxin A
5TXirx.description: An enterotoxin produced by Clostridioides difficile. Binds to the brush border of enterocytes and alters fluid secretion into the intestinal lumen, resulting in diarrhea.

MTXMrx.title: Toxin B
MTXMrx.description: A cytotoxin produced by Clostridioides difficile. Depolymerizes actin filaments and alters the cytoskeleton of enterocytes, resulting in diarrhea.

nTX7rx.title: Enterocyte
nTX7rx.description: A simple columnar epithelial cell found in the small intestine. Enterocytes contain microvilli, which form the brush border that enables absorption and transport of nutrients.

LTXwrx.title: Shiga toxin
LTXwrx.description: A toxin produced by Shigella spp. and enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC), which inhibits the 60S subunit of ribosomes by cleavage of adenine in ribosomal RNA (rRNA). Causes damage to enterocytes and endothelial cells, which can result in bloody diarrhea and hemolytic uremic syndrome.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease
Diarrheagenic E. coli → Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC)

oTX07x.title: DNA polymerase II
oTX07x.description: A DNA-dependent DNA polymerase that functions as a backup enzyme for DNA synthesis. It has 3' → 5' exonuclease activity and 5’ → 3’ polymerase activity.

KTXU7x.title: 5'→3' exonuclease activity
KTXU7x.description: The ability to remove nucleotides in the 5'→3' direction (as opposed to proofreading, which removes nucleotides in the 3'→5' direction). Unique to DNA polymerase I.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

6TXj7x.title: 5'→3' DNA polymerase activity
6TXj7x.description: The ability to add deoxynucleotides to the 3' end of DNA strands. Main function of DNA polymerases.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

qTXC7x.title: Biofilm
qTXC7x.description: A material produced by some bacteria that facilitates adhesion to surfaces (e.g., catheters and prosthetic devices). Biofilm-producing organisms include S. mutans, S. sanguinis, P. aeruginosa, Viridans group streptococci, and nontypable H. influenza.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

GTXBHx.title: Nitroblue tetrazolium dye reduction test
GTXBHx.description: A diagnostic test used to assess phagocyte function. Considered normal (positive) if incubated neutrophils are able to reduce the dye to a blue color. Considered abnormal (negative) if no blue color is produced, which indicates that there is a defect in the production of reactive oxygen species (e.g., due to NADPH oxidase deficiency in patients with chronic granulomatous disease).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital neutrophil and phagocyte disorders

uTXpsx.title: Charcoal yeast extract agar
uTXpsx.description: A medium used to culture and identify Legionella pneumophila. Activated charcoal neutralizes toxic metabolic products, while yeast extract supplies protein and other growth nutrients. Cysteine and iron enhance the growth of L. pneumophila and may also support the growth of Brucella, Francisella, and Pasteurella species.

ETX8sx.title: Chocolate agar
ETX8sx.description: A type of blood agar plate that contains V-factor (NAD) and X-factor (hematin). Used to culture fastidious bacteria (e.g., Haemophilus influenzae, Francisella tularensis).

vTXAsx.title: Eaton agar
vTXAsx.description: A growth medium containing cholesterol. Used to culture Mycoplasma pneumoniae.

DTX1Gx.title: MacConkey agar
DTX1Gx.description: A growth medium containing a neutral red pH indicator that turns pink when culturing bacteria that can ferment lactose (e.g., Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacter, Serratia), which results in the production of acid.

wTXhGx.title: Eosin methylene blue agar
wTXhGx.description: A growth medium used to culture and identify Escherichia coli. The medium turns dark purple when colonized by most lactose fermenters and is colorless for lactose nonfermenters. E. coli colonies cultured on the medium have a green metallic sheen.

9TXNGx.title: Mannitol salt agar
9TXNGx.description: A growth medium used to culture gram-positive bacteria, specifically Staphylococcus species. It has a high level of salt that inhibits the growth of most other bacteria. S. aureus produces golden yellow colonies (aureus is Latin for gold), while other Staphylococcus species grow without changing the color of the medium.

CTXqGx.title: Tricarboxylic acid cycle
CTXqGx.description: A sequence of intramitochondrial chemical reactions that releases energy via oxidation of acetyl-CoA derived from carbohydrates, fats, and proteins into CO2. Energy is saved in the form of FADH2, NADH+H, and GTP. Provides metabolites for several metabolic pathways.

yTXdtx.title: ICAM-1
yTXdtx.description: A protein found on the surfaces of endothelial cells and white blood cells. Functions as a ligand for LFA-1 (integrin) on leukocytes and is the site of attachment for rhinovirus to enter respiratory epithelial cells.

ATXRtx.title: CCR5
ATXRtx.description: An integral membrane protein predominantly found on the surface of white blood cells, dendritic cells, and microglia. It functions as a chemokine receptor that allows recruitment of leukocytes to areas of inflammation. It is used by many HIV strains (R5-tropic strains) as a coreceptor for entry into host cells.

_TX5tx.title: CD21
_TX5tx.description: A membrane protein that forms the B-cell coreceptor complex with CD19 and CD81. It binds to antigens via C3d and is the site of attachment for the Epstein-Barr virus.

zTXrtx.title: CXCR4
zTXrtx.description: Chemokine receptor found on the surface of lymphocytes. It binds stromal-derived-factor-1 (SDF-1), which is a strong chemotactic agent for lymphocytes. It is the site of attachment for some HIV genotypes (X4 viruses).

-TXDtx.title: Integrins
-TXDtx.description: A family of transmembrane receptor proteins that facilitate stable cellular adhesion to the basement membrane by binding to collagen, laminin, and fibronectin. Integrins also establish intercellular junctions in the immune system (e.g., for leukocyte extravasation).

ZgXZFx.title: P antigen
ZgXZFx.description: A glycosphingolipid found on human erythrocytes. Parvovirus B19 binds P antigen to infect erythroid progenitor cells.

0gXeFx.title: Chemokines
0gXeFx.description: A group of pro-inflammatory signaling proteins that induce chemotaxis of leukocytes. Includes interleukin-1, interleukin-8, TNF-α, and LPS.

bgXHFx.title: Doppler effect
bgXHFx.description: Change in frequency of a wave relative to an observer who is moving from the wave source. As the observer moves toward the source, the frequency increases; when moving away, the frequency decreases.

XgX9Fx.title: Morbilliform
XgX9Fx.description: A dermatologic descriptor for an erythematous, maculopapular rash that resembles measles.

cgXa8x.title: Type II pneumocyte
cgXa8x.description: A cuboidal alveolar cell that secretes surfactant from lamellar bodies. Proliferates in response to lung damage and serves as a precursor for both type I and type II pneumocytes.

1gX28x.title: Interleukin 10
1gX28x.description: A cytokine produced by Th2 helper T cells and regulatory T cells. Inhibits the immune response by downregulating the expression of MHC class II molecules, inhibiting the secretion of Th1 cytokines, and suppresses activated macrophages and dendritic cells.

VgXG8x.title: Phosphotransferase
VgXG8x.description: An enzyme that catalyzes a phosphorylation reaction. Kinases are a subtype of phosphotransferases.

UgXbux.title: LH surge
UgXbux.description: A rapid increase of LH triggered by increased levels of estrogen at the end of the follicular phase of the menstrual cycle. LH stimulates the primary follicle to release the egg (ovulation). Increased levels of progesterone inhibit the LH surge.

2gXTux.title: Progesterone
2gXTux.description: A sex hormone synthesized by the adrenal cortex, corpus luteum of the ovaries, and testes. It has multiple functions, including stimulating the endometrium during the menstrual cycle, maintaining pregnancy, and inhibiting lactation.

fgXkux.title: Graafian follicle
fgXkux.description: The final follicular stage of folliculogenesis. During every menstrual cycle, multiple ovarian follicles undergo maturation, but only one follicle matures to become the dominant follicle, which ultimately ruptures and releases the ovum (via ovulation). Following ovulation, it transforms into the corpus luteum.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Oogenesis and folliculogenesis

media.title: Secondary and tertiary follicles in the ovary

TgX6ux.title: Localized amyloidosis
TgX6ux.description: A condition in which abnormal protein aggregates (amyloid plaques) are deposited into single organs rather than systemically. Examples include Alzheimer disease, medullary thyroid cancer, and isolated atrial amyloidosis.

hgXcEx.title: DNA polymerase-beta
hgXcEx.description: A eukaryotic polymerase used during base excision repair to fill the gap left behind following removal of the AP site.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

3gXSEx.title: IκB
3gXSEx.description: A protein that inactivates NF-κB transcription factor, which normally activates COX-2 (a pro-inflammatory enzyme). IκB's action is enhanced by corticosteroids.

RgXlEx.title: NF-κB
RgXlEx.description: A transcription factor involved in the regulation of multiple inflammatory and immunologic processes. Activates COX-2. Glucocorticoid therapy inhibits NF-κB and results in immunosuppression.

igXJEx.title: D1 receptor
igXJEx.description: A class of dopamine receptor that is coupled to a Gs protein and activates adenylyl cyclase. Subsequent activation of protein kinase A causes smooth muscle relaxation.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

jgX_Ex.title: Vasopressin 1 receptor
jgX_Ex.description: A class of vasopressin receptors that are coupled to a Gq-protein. Activation mediates smooth muscle contraction (e.g., vasoconstriction and uterine contractions).

PgXWvx.title: S-adenosylmethionine
PgXWvx.description: An important cofactor (methyl donor) for the synthesis of epinephrine and the 7-methylguanine cap on eukaryotic mRNA. Synthesized from methionine. After donating a methyl group, it is converted to S-adenosylhomocysteine, which is remethylated back to methionine in the presence of vitamin B12 and N-methyl-THF.

destinations.label: Amino acids →  Catabolism of the carbon skeleton of amino acids

4gX3vx.title: Counseling on the use of prescription opioids
4gX3vx.description: A set of strategies to counsel patients on the risks of opioid therapy, including the possibility of overdose, addiction, and adverse effects. Stress that patients should not use someone else's opioids or take higher or more frequent doses than prescribed. One approach to patient counseling is the establishment of specific "SMART" goals (Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Relevant, Time-limited) for opioid therapy.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Counseling on the use of prescription opioids

OgXIvx.title: Sucralfate
OgXIvx.description: A sucrose sulfate-aluminium complex that reacts with HCl in an acidic environment to create a protective barrier over the gastric/duodenal mucosa. Also acts as an acid buffer and promotes HCO3 production. It is used to promote ulcer healing in peptic ulcer disease.

lgXvvx.title: Tophus
lgXvvx.description: A characteristic feature of chronic gout caused by deposition of urate crystals in tissue, including bone (bone tophus) and soft tissue (cartilage, tendon sheaths, subcutis; known as soft tissue tophus). Manifests as hard, painless nodules that may appear yellow and chalky if close to the surface of the skin.

media.title: Gout tophus with foreign body granulomas
Gouty tophi due to urate crystal deposition in bones and soft tissues

NgX-vx.title: Optochin
NgX-vx.description: A derivate of hydroquinine used in microbiology to distinguish between Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is optochin-sensitive, and other alpha-hemolytic streptococci (e.g., viridans streptococci).

mgXVDx.title: BRAF gene
mgXVDx.description: A proto-oncogene that encodes B-Raf, a serine/threonine kinase. Activating mutations in the BRAF gene are associated with melanoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, papillary thyroid carcinoma

5gXiDx.title: Infiltrative cardiomyopathy
5gXiDx.description: A type of restrictive cardiomyopathy commonly caused by infiltration of the myocardium that causes myocardial thickening and can lead to diastolic dysfunction. Conditions that can cause infiltrative cardiomyopathy include amyloidosis, sarcoidosis, hemochromatosis.

MgXMDx.title: Catalase-negative organisms
MgXMDx.description: A group of organisms that do not produce catalase, an enzyme that degrades hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen before neutrophils can convert it via myeloperoxidase into microbicidal products. This characteristic is used in microbiology to distinguish between catalase-positive pathogens (e.g., Staphylococci) and catalase-negative pathogens (e.g., Streptococci).

ngX7Dx.title: Neutrophilia
ngX7Dx.description: An increase in the number of neutrophils in the peripheral circulation. Causes include bacterial infections, inflammation, and stressors.

LgXwDx.title: Pleuroperitoneal membrane
LgXwDx.description: One of four embryonic structures that form the diaphragm. The pleuroperitoneal membranes form laterally toward the septum transversum (which forms the central tendon of the diaphragm) and fuse with the septum transversum and the mesentery of the esophagus to complete the diaphragm.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Embryology of the peritoneum

ogX0wx.title: Bronchogenic cysts
ogX0wx.description: A congenital malformation of the lungs that arises during embryonic development. Caused by abnormal budding of the foregut with subsequent dilation of large and small bronchi, which results in the development of typically unilocular, round, fluid-filled cysts. These may be intrapulmonary or located within the mediastinum.

6gXjwx.title: Annular pancreas
6gXjwx.description: A congenital pancreatic malformation caused by abnormal rotation of the ventral bud of the pancreas around the foregut during embryonic development. A ring of pancreatic tissue persists around the duodenum, causing constriction of it. Can manifest prenatally with polyhydramnios or postnatally with vomiting.

pgXLwx.title: Yolk sac tumor
pgXLwx.description: A malignant germ cell tumor composed of endodermal cells. Can arise in the testis or ovaries. More common among children.

qgXCwx.title: Embryonal carcinoma
qgXCwx.description: A malignant germ cell tumor composed of epithelial cells that resemble primitive embryonal cells. It can occur in the testis or ovary and typically occurs in young adults.

IgXY9x.title: Palpation of the ears
IgXY9x.description: A part of the head and neck examination. Gently pull and press on the tragus, earlobe, and upper ridge of the auricle in order to evaluate for tenderness, which can be a sign of ear infection. Press on the mastoid area and note any tenderness, nodules or swelling.

rgXf9x.title: Cyanocobalamin
rgXf9x.description: A synthetic form of vitamin B12 used to treat vitamin B12 deficiency. Also formed from the reaction of hydroxycobalamin and cyanide. Because cyanocobalamin is nontoxic and renally excreted, hydroxycobalamin is used as an antidote to cyanide poisoning.

7gX49x.title: Midbrain
7gX49x.description: An anatomical part of the brainstem located between the diencephalon (thalamus and hypothalamus) and the pons and cerebellum. Composed of a dorsally located tectum (with inferior and superior colliculi), a ventrally located tegmentum (with the cerebral peduncles), the substantia nigra, and the superior cerebellar peduncles.

HgXK9x.title: Superior laryngeal nerve
HgXK9x.description: A branch of the vagus nerve whose internal portion carries sensory innervation above the vocal cords and whose external portion carries motor function for the cricothyroid muscle.

sgXt9x.title: Thyroarytenoid muscle
sgXt9x.description: A muscle that aids in relaxation of the vocal cords to lower pitch of voice. Can also bring the vocal folds together (adduction). Innervated by the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

GgXB9x.title: Lateral cricoarytenoid muscles
GgXB9x.description: A pair of muscles that function as adductors of the vocal cords (closes the glottis). Innervated by the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

tgXXCx.title: Transverse arytenoid muscle
tgXXCx.description: An adductor of the vocal cords (closes the glottis). Innervated by the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

FgXgCx.title: Recurrent laryngeal nerve
FgXgCx.description: A pair of nerves that arise from the vagus nerves and carry sensory innervation below the vocal cords and motor function for all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid muscles bilaterally. Unilateral RLN palsy (e.g., compression from a thyroid or apical lung cancer) causes voice hoarseness. Bilateral RLN palsy (e.g., during thyroidectomy) causes stridor.

8gXOCx.title: Oblique arytenoid muscle
8gXOCx.description: An adductor of the vocal cords (closes the glottis). Innervated by the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

ugXpCx.title: Pretectal region
ugXpCx.description: A part of the subcortical visual system located on the dorsal side of the midbrain in close proximity to the tectum and the pineal gland. Involved in the direct and consensual pupillary light reflex, smooth eye movement, and the accommodation reflex.

EgX8Cx.title: Sella turcica
EgX8Cx.description: A saddle-shaped depression in the sphenoid bone that contains the pituitary gland.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamus and pituitary gland

media.title: Base of skull (superior view of internal surface)

vgXACx.title: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
vgXACx.description: A collection of laws and regulations by the U.S. Congress to protect the privacy and security of health information.

destinations.label: Ethics of communicating medical information → Confidentiality

DgX1xx.title: Secondary gain
DgX1xx.description: The external advantages obtained as a result of being ill (e.g., financial compensation, warm meals while hospitalized). The illness may be presumed to be unreal and can lead to transition into the sick role (e.g., using illness for personal advantage). Conscious falsification of evidence for secondary gain is known as malingering.

destinations.label: Somatic symptom and related disorders → Malingering

wgXhxx.title: Principal cell
wgXhxx.description:
A specialized cell in the collecting duct of the nephron that facilitates reabsorption of Na⁺ and secretion of K⁺. Aldosterone regulates the resorption of Na⁺ and secretion of K⁺ by stimulating the integration of eNaC channels 
and N⁺/K⁺-ATPase pumps in the cell membrane. Antidiuretic hormone regulates the resorption of water by integrating aquaporin channels in the cell membrane.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Physiology of the tubular system

media.title: Transport in the connecting tubule and collecting duct

9gXNxx.title: Aquaporin channels
9gXNxx.description: Water channels expressed on the cell surface of the distal convoluted tubules and collecting duct in response to antidiuretic hormone (ADH). They facilitate the resorption of water and thus the concentration of urine.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Urine production

CgXqxx.title: Descending loop of Henle
CgXqxx.description: The segment of the nephron between the proximal convoluted tubules and the ascending loop of Henle. The main function of this segment is to concentrate the ultrafiltrate, making the urine hypertonic. The segment is impermeable to Na+ and the medullary hypertonicity promotes passive reabsorption of H2O.

xgXExx.title: Supraoptic nucleus
xgXExx.description: A hypothalamic nucleus that, along with the paraventricular nucleus, regulates water balance via the effects of antidiuretic hormone and oxytocin. Damage to this region can result in diabetes insipidus.

BgXzxx.title: Phenotypic mixing (viral)
BgXzxx.description: A phenomenon in which the genome of one virus that has infected a cell is coated with the surface proteins of a second virus that has infected the same cell. The new protein coat determines the infectivity of the hybrid virus. No genetic information is exchanged; progeny viruses express a phenotype determined by the genotype of the first virus.

ygXdBx.title: Subacute lymphocytic thyroiditis
ygXdBx.description: A transient, self-limited, patchy inflammation of the thyroid gland, characterized by lymphocyte infiltration. Caused by autoimmune disease, certain medications, and postpartum changes. Inflammation typically causes a triphasic pattern from thyrotoxicosis to hypothyroidism, before returning to a euthyroid state.

AgXRBx.title: Keratin pearl
AgXRBx.description: An abnormal structure formed by concentric layers of epithelial cells surrounding a keratin matrix secreted by the cells. Associated with well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma.

media.title: Keratin pearls in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC)

_gX5Bx.title: Cerebellar vermis
_gX5Bx.description: An area located along the anteromedial aspect of the cerebellum. Connects the two cerebellar hemispheres and interacts with the cerebral cortex and the spinal cord. Involved in regulating bodily posture and motion.

zgXrBx.title: Indinavir
zgXrBx.description: A protease inhibitor used as part of an antiretroviral regimen for treatment of HIV. Adverse effects include nephrolithiasis, crystal-induced nephropathy, and HIV-associated lipodystrophy.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

-gXDBx.title: Tesamorelin
-gXDBx.description: A GHRH analog used as a treatment for HIV-associated lipodystrophy. Adverse effects include IgG antibody development, peripheral edema, and arthralgia.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

ZSXZyx.title: Growth hormone–releasing hormone analogs
ZSXZyx.description: Analogs of native human GHRH that have chemically modified amino acid sequences. Used to treat growth hormone deficiency as well as HIV-associated lipodystrophy (i.e., tesamorelin).

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

0SXeyx.title: Raltegravir
0SXeyx.description: A drug that reversibly inhibits HIV integrase, which prevents the HIV genome from integrating into host DNA. Generally well-tolerated, but adverse effects insomnia, dizziness, and increases in serum creatine kinase.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

aSXQyx.title: Enfuvirtide
aSXQyx.description: A fusion inhibitor used as part of antiretroviral therapy to treat HIV infection. Binds to gp41 and prevents entry of HIV into host cells. Adverse effects include injection site reactions and neutropenia.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

YSXnyx.title: Abacavir
YSXnyx.description: A nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor that can be used as part of a antiretroviral regimen for treatment of HIV.
