Adverse effects include bone marrow suppression and abacavir-related hypersensitivity syndrome (potentially life-threatening systemic reaction with fever and maculopapular rash).

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

bSXHyx.title: Aminolevulinic acid dehydratase
bSXHyx.description: The second enzyme in the pathway of heme biosynthesis. Converts aminolevulinic acid (ALA) to porphobilinogen. Lead poisoning inhibits ALAD, disrupting heme synthesis. ALAD deficiency causes ALAD porphyria.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

XSX9yx.title: Aminolevulinic acid dehydratase porphyria
XSX9yx.description: An autosomal recessive disorder resulting from a severe deficiency of aminolevulinic acid dehydratase. It is an incredibly rare disorder that presents in childhood with acute symptoms of abdominal pain, motor neuropathy, muscle weakness, and neuropsychiatric manifestations.

cSXaAx.title: Porphobilinogen deaminase
cSXaAx.description: A cytosolic enzyme that catalyzes the third step in heme biosynthesis, where four molecules of porphobilinogen are condensed to form hydroxymethylbilane. There are 300 different potential genetic defects in this enzyme that can lead to acute intermittent porphyria.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

1SX2Ax.title: Congenital erythropoietic porphyria
1SX2Ax.description: A rare, autosomal recessive porphyria that results from a deficiency of uroporphyrinogen III synthase. It presents in early childhood with hemolytic anemia and severe cutaneous photosensitivity, including brownish-red teeth, bones, and urine.

dSXoAx.title: Pseudounipolar neuron
dSXoAx.description: A sensory neuron in the peripheral nervous system that has an axon that splits into two branches. One branch carries sensory information to cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglia; the other branch carries information from the dorsal root ganglia to the spinal cord.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

VSXGAx.title: Mucositis
VSXGAx.description: A condition of painful inflammation and ulceration of the mucous membranes lining the digestive tract. Etiologies include Kawasaki disease and as an adverse effect of chemotherapeutic agents (e.g., taxanes, methotrexate).

destinations.label: Complications of cancer therapy → Gastrointestinal complications

eSXxAx.title: Kinase
eSXxAx.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate group onto another molecule. A type of phosphotransferase.

destinations.label: Enzymes and biocatalysis → Classes of enzymes

USXb_x.title: Systemic amyloidosis
USXb_x.description: A condition in which abnormal protein aggregates (amyloid plaques) are deposited into multiple organs. Examples include light chain amyloidosis, reactive amyloidosis, and dialysis-related amyloidosis.

2SXT_x.title: Cryoglobulinemia
2SXT_x.description: A condition characterized by elevated serum cryoglobulin concentration. Typically asymptomatic but can manifest as cryoglobulinemic vasculitis. Causes of cryoglobulinemia include multiple myeloma, HCV, SLE, and rheumatoid arthritis.

media.title: Diffuse purpura on the lower extremities

fSXk_x.title: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma
fSXk_x.description: A type of renal carcinoma that is derived from intercalated cells of collecting ducts. Identified in histology by large, polygonal cells with a prominent cell membrane and the presence of perinuclear halos.

TSX6_x.title: Angiomatosis
TSX6_x.description: A rare vascular lesion characterized by proliferation of vessels mixed with adipose tissue. May appear similar to hemangiomas or vascular malformations. It can be congenital or acquired. Congenital forms may be idiopathic or associated with syndromes such as Sneddon syndrome, Sturge Weber syndrome, Gorham disease, or Klippel Trenaunay syndrome. Acquired angiomatosis may be caused by infections such as Bartonellosis or HIV.

destinations.label: Benign skin tumors → Vascular skin tumors

gSXF_x.title: Hemoglobin C disease
gSXF_x.description: A hemolytic anemia caused by a homozygous mutation of the beta chain of hemoglobin, with glutamic acid being replaced by lysine at position 6.

SSXy_x.title: Anti-RNA-polymerase III autoantibodies
SSXy_x.description: Autoantibodies directed at Anti-RNA-polymerase III. A marker of diffuse systemic sclerosis and a poorer prognosis.

3SXSzx.title: Hormone sensitive lipase
3SXSzx.description: An enzyme produced primarily in adipocytes. Hydrolyzes stored triglycerides to free fatty acids. Enzyme activity is increased in response to glucagon, beta adrenergic stimulation, and ACTH signaling. Insulin inhibits its activity.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

RSXlzx.title: Tubulin
RSXlzx.description: A protein that serves as the main constituent of cell microtubules, which serve important roles in structural support, intracellular transport, DNA segregation, and cell motility.

iSXJzx.title: Celiac trunk
iSXJzx.description: The first branch of the abdominal aorta. Arises at the T12 vertebral level and supplies the foregut. Branches into the common hepatic, splenic, and left gastric arteries.

media.title: Arterial supply of the gastrointestinal tract

QSXuzx.title: Superior mesenteric artery
QSXuzx.description: A branch of the abdominal aorta that arises at the level of L1 and supplies the midgut. Branches include the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery, ileocolic artery, right colic artery, and middle colic artery.

media.title: Superior mesenteric artery in healthy subject

jSX_zx.title: Palatoglossus muscle
jSX_zx.description: A muscle that elevates the posterior tongue during swallowing. Innervated by the vagus nerve (CN X), unlike other muscles of the tongue (which are innervated by the hypoglossal nerve, CN XII).

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Cranial nerve types and functions

PSXW-x.title: Inferior mesenteric artery
PSXW-x.description: A branch of the abdominal aorta that originates at the level of L3 and supplies the hindgut. Divides into the left colic, sigmoid, and superior rectal arteries.

media.title: Arterial supply of the gastrointestinal tract

4SX3-x.title: Orbicularis oculi muscle
4SX3-x.description: A muscle that closes the eyelids. Innervated by branches of the facial nerve (CN VII).

kSXm-x.title: Detrusor
kSXm-x.description: A smooth muscle of the bladder wall. Its cells are arranged in longitudinal and spiral bundles. Contraction of this muscle is primarily controlled by the parasympathetic system via M3 muscarinic receptors.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Urinary bladder

lSXv-x.title: Stomach
lSXv-x.description: A hollow intraperitoneal organ that is located in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen between the esophagus and the duodenum in the gastrointestinal tract. Involved in the mechanical and chemical digestion of food.

NSX--x.title: Small intestine
NSX--x.description: A hollow, intraperitoneal organ that extends from the pylorus of the stomach to the ileocecal junction. Further divided into the duodenum, the jejunum, and ileum. Develops from the distal foregut and the midgut.

5SXiZB.title: Gallbladder
5SXiZB.description: A hollow intraperitoneal organ that stores and concentrates bile. Supplied by the cystic artery.

MSXMZB.title: Epiploic foramen
MSXMZB.description: A foramen that allows communication between the greater sac and lesser sac of the abdominal cavity. Bordered by the caudate lobe of the liver superiorly, the first part of the duodenum inferiorly, the hepatoduodenal ligament anteriorly, and the inferior vena cava posteriorly. Clamped during the Pringle maneuver to occlude vascular inflow to the liver.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

nSX7ZB.title: Hepatoduodenal ligament
nSX7ZB.description: A ligament within the lesser omentum that extends from the superior part of the duodenum to the porta hepatis of the liver. Contains the proper hepatic artery, portal vein, and common bile duct.

oSX00B.title: Brunner gland
oSX00B.description: A type of gland located within the proximal duodenal submucosa that produces alkaline secretions (e.g., bicarbonate), which neutralize stomach acid to activate enzymes required for the digestion and absorption of nutrients. Also secretes the amylase and maltase. Activated by secretin.

KSXU0B.title: Rugger-jersey spine sign
KSXU0B.description: An x-ray finding that is caused by subplate sclerosis combined with lytic regions in the vertebral body. The alternating sclerotic-lytic regions mimic the horizontal stripes of a rugby jersey. Typically seen in hyperparathyroidism.

6SXj0B.title: Central nervous system
6SXj0B.description: The portion of the nervous system that consists of the brain and spinal cord.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex
Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

pSXL0B.title: 3'→5' exonuclease activity
pSXL0B.description: The ability to remove nucleotides in the 3′→5′ direction. Used by DNA polymerases to proofread recently synthesized RNA and DNA.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

JSXs0B.title: RNA primer
JSXs0B.description: A short sequence of RNA nucleotides on which DNA polymerase initiates replication.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

qSXC0B.title: Eukaryotes
qSXC0B.description: A group of single-celled or multicellular organisms that have membrane-bound organelles (e.g., nucleus, mitochondria).

ISXYaB.title: 14-alpha-demethylase
ISXYaB.description: A cytochrome P450 enzyme responsible for the demethylation of lanosterol, an essential step in the biosynthesis of ergosterol. Azole antifungal agents target this enzyme to disturb fungal membrane function, resulting in growth inhibition and death of the fungal cells.

rSXfaB.title: Dysesthesia
rSXfaB.description: An abnormal sensation that can manifest with discomfort, irritation, itching, burning, and/or pain. Sometimes described as similar to an electric shock or pinprick pain.

7SX4aB.title: Parasympathetic nervous system
7SX4aB.description: A division of the autonomic nervous system responsible for stimulation of "rest-and-digest" activities, including salivation, lacrimation, urination, digestion, and defecation. The primary neurotransmitter involved in these processes is acetylcholine.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Parasympathetic nervous system

HSXKaB.title: Beta-2 receptor
HSXKaB.description: A G-protein linked adrenergic receptor. Activation causes vasodilation, bronchodilation, lipolysis, insulin release, aqueous humor production, and cellular potassium uptake.

sSXtaB.title: Beta-1 receptor
sSXtaB.description: A G-protein coupled adrenergic receptor. Activation leads to increased cardiac contractility, increased heart rate, increased lipolysis, and increased renin release.

GSXBaB.title: Ventricular pseudoaneurysm
GSXBaB.description: A false aneurysm in which myocardial rupture is contained in the pericardium or scar tissue. Most frequently occurs 3-14 days after myocardial infarction.

tSXXYB.title: Cartilaginous joint
tSXXYB.description: A joint connected by fibrous and/or hyaline cartilage (e.g., intervertebral discs between vertebrae, the pubic symphysis, manubriosternal joint). Further categorized into primary cartilaginous joints (composed of hyaline cartilage) and secondary cartilaginous joints (composed of fibrocartilage).

FSXgYB.title: Ligamentum flavum
FSXgYB.description: A group of paired ligaments of the vertebral column that originate on the surface of articular processes of vertebrae and attach to laminae of adjacent vertebrae. Contain elastic tissue that provides support in the upright position, aids in flexion of the vertebral column, and prevents separation of the vertebral laminae.

8SXOYB.title: Intervertebral disc
8SXOYB.description: The fibrocartilage between vertebrae in the spine that functions as a shock-absorber. Composed of a central nucleus pulposus, which is surrounded by an annulus fibrosus.

uSXpYB.title: Counseling for patients with memory loss and/or cognitive impairment
uSXpYB.description: A set of strategies to counsel patients and evaluate emotional stability (e.g., suicidality), safety risks, adequacy of supervision, and whether there is evidence of neglect. Clinicians should have contact information for the patient's caretaker or next of kin, who should be advised to determine whether the patient is adequately handling finances, medications, and other responsibilities.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Counseling for patients with memory loss and/or cognitive impairment

ESX8YB.title: M protein (virulence factor)
ESX8YB.description: A virulence factor expressed on the surface of group A streptococcus that blocks the alternative complement pathway. Shares similar epitopes to human myocardial and nerve proteins, which can lead to autoimmune attack, which causes acute rheumatic fever.

vSXAYB.title: Phagocytosis
vSXAYB.description: A process by which a phagocyte (e.g., a macrophage) engulfs a foreign particle, cellular debris, or microorganism and directs it toward the lysosome for inactivation and degradation.

DSX1bB.title: Superficial inguinal lymph nodes
DSX1bB.description: A cluster of lymph nodes that receive lymphatic drainage from the anal canal below the dentate line and skin below the umbilicus (except the popliteal area). In female individuals, they also receive lymphatic drainage from the lower third of the vagina and the round ligament. They drain into the deep inguinal and external iliac nodes.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Lymphatic drainage of the thigh

wSXhbB.title: Dentate line
wSXhbB.description: An anatomical line that divides the upper and lower anal canal. Above the dentate line, the anal canal is supplied by the superior rectal artery and innervated by the inferior hypogastric plexus. Below the dentate line, the anal canal is supplied by the middle and inferior rectal arteries and innervated by the inferior rectal nerves.

9SXNbB.title: Para-aortic lymph nodes
9SXNbB.description: A cluster of lymph nodes that lie on either side of the aorta, adjacent to the lumbar vertebrae. They receive lymphatic drainage from the testes, ovaries, uterus, fallopian tubes, kidneys, and adrenal glands and drain into the lumbar lymphatic trunks.

CSXqbB.title: Deep inguinal lymph nodes
CSXqbB.description: A cluster of lymph nodes located medial to the femoral vein. They receive lymphatic drainage from the superficial inguinal and popliteal lymph nodes. In male individuals, they also receive lymphatic drainage from the glans penis. In female individuals, they also receive lymphatic drainage from the clitoris. They drain into the external iliac lymph nodes.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Lymphatic drainage of the thigh

xSXEbB.title: Inferior mesenteric lymph nodes
xSXEbB.description: A cluster of lymph nodes that surround the inferior mesenteric artery. They receive lymphatic drainage of the large intestine from the splenic flexure of the colon up to the upper rectum and drain into the superior mesenteric lymph nodes. Lymphadenopathy of these nodes is associated with mesenteric lymphadenitis, typhoid fever, ulcerative colitis, celiac disease, and colonic malignancy.

BSXzbB.title: Internal iliac lymph nodes
BSXzbB.description: A cluster of lymph nodes located in the pelvis, adjacent to the internal iliac arteries. They receive lymphatic drainage from the lower rectum, anal canal above the dentate line, lower third of the ureter, and urethra. In male individuals, they also receive lymphatic drainage from the erectile tissue, prostate, seminal vesicles, and vas deferens. In female individuals, they also receive lymphatic drainage from the fallopian tubes, the body of the uterus, cervix, and upper and middle third of the vagina. They drain into the common iliac lymph nodes.

ySXdXB.title: Mediastinal lymph nodes
ySXdXB.description: A cluster of nodes that drains the trachea and esophagus. Lymphadenopathy of these nodes is associated with primary lung cancer and granulomatous disease.

ASXRXB.title: Hilar lymph nodes
ASXRXB.description: A cluster of nodes that drains the lungs. Lymphadenopathy of these nodes is associated with granulomatous disease (e.g., sarcoidosis).

_SX5XB.title: External iliac lymph nodes
_SX5XB.description: A cluster of lymph nodes located in the pelvis, adjacent to the external iliac vessels. They receive lymphatic drainage from the superficial and deep inguinal lymph nodes, lower third of the ureter, bladder, and urethra. In male individuals, they also receive lymphatic drainage from the seminal vesicles and vas deferens. In female individuals, they also receive lymphatic drainage from the upper third of the vagina, body of the uterus, and cervix. They drain into the common iliac lymph nodes.

zSXrXB.title: Bipedalism
zSXrXB.description: A form of movement that relies only on the use of an organism's two hind limbs (or legs in the case of humans).

bhXHcB.title: Muramic acid
bhXHcB.description: An amino sugar acid that occurs as N-acetylmuramic acid in peptidoglycan, a component of bacterial cell walls. Bacteria that lack muramic acid in their cell walls (e.g., chlamydiae) do not Gram stain well.

1hX21B.title: Body check
1hX21B.description: A part of the physical examination for patients with possible traumatic injury. After respectfully draping the patient, inspect the body systematically for bruises or open wounds. Palpate the joints, abdomen, head, and vertebrae for evidence of occult injury.

WhXP1B.title: Neoantigen
WhXP1B.description: An antigen to which the immune system has not previously been exposed. Refer to proteins that result from host cell alteration (e.g., neoplastic transformation) as well as host proteins that are typically not exposed to the immune system (e.g., in sympathetic ophthalmia).

dhXo1B.title: Stent thrombosis
dhXo1B.description: An acute occlusion of a coronary artery stent with a newly formed thrombus. Sufficient stent thrombosis can lead to signs and symptoms of acute coronary syndrome. To prevent stent thrombosis, dual antiplatelet therapy is recommended in patients who undergo coronary stenting.

VhXG1B.title: Sternal kyphosis
VhXG1B.description: A deformity of the anterior chest wall where the middle and lower portion of the sternum protrudes forward, which leads to concave and depressed adjacent costal cartilages. Associated with Marfan syndrome and osteogenesis imperfecta.

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Clinical features

ehXx1B.title: Activities of daily living
ehXx1B.description: A group of basic self-care tasks that include bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring (getting in or out of bed or standing up from a chair), continence, and eating. The ability to perform these tasks is assessed in older adults or patients with physical or cognitive impairment.

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Functional status assessment

UhXbWB.title: Instrumental activities of daily living
UhXbWB.description: A group of eight tasks required for maintaining a household independently: grocery shopping, managing transportation, using the telephone, preparing meals, housekeeping, managing finances, doing laundry, and managing medications. The ability to perform these activities is assessed in older adults or patients with physical or cognitive impairment.

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Functional status assessment

2hXTWB.title: Ventricular free wall
2hXTWB.description: The area of the left ventricular wall that is not part of the interventricular septum or the apex.

fhXkWB.title: Optic chiasm
fhXkWB.description: The area of the brain where the optic nerve fibers of the nasal side of the retina cross the midline. Located directly below the hypothalamus in close proximity to the pituitary gland.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Overview of the visual pathways

ThX6WB.title: Flap endonuclease-1
ThX6WB.description: A eukaryotic DNA replication enzyme that removes RNA primers during lagging strand synthesis.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

ghXFWB.title: Trichuris trichiura
ghXFWB.description: A type of whipworm that is contracted fecal-orally. Larvae migrate through the small intestine to the large intestine and develop into adult form. Patients can present with symptoms of iron deficiency anemia due to chronic GI blood loss (trichuriasis).

hhXcdB.title: B-Raf kinase
hhXcdB.description: A serine/threonine kinase encoded by the BRAF gene. Part of the RAS/MAPK pathway, which regulates cellular growth, differentiation, and apoptosis.

3hXSdB.title: Xanthine
3hXSdB.description: A purine derivative formed from the deamination of guanine.

RhXldB.title: Deamination
RhXldB.description: The removal of an amino group from a larger molecule (e.g., nucleotides). The deamination of cytosine, adenine, guanine, and 5-methylcytosine forms uracil, hypoxanthine, xanthine, and thymine, respectively. Deaminated nucleotides are replaced by base excision repair.

destinations.label: Amino acids →  Biochemical reactions of amino acid metabolism

media.title: Endogenous sources of DNA damage: spontaneous deamination of DNA bases

ihXJdB.title: Ciliary ganglion
ihXJdB.description: A parasympathetic ganglion located behind the orbit between the lateral rectus muscle and the optic nerve. Contains fibers of the oculomotor nerve.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Parasympathetic nervous system

QhXudB.title: Compliance (physiology)
QhXudB.description: The ability of a hollow organ or vessel to expand in response to changes in pressure. Defined as change in volume over change in pressure (i.e., ΔV/ΔP)

jhX_dB.title: Edinger-Westphal nucleus
jhX_dB.description: A preganglionic nucleus that contains parasympathetic fibers of the oculomotor nerve, which innervate the sphincter muscle and the ciliary muscle. Located in the midbrain at the level of the superior colliculus, posterior to the oculomotor nucleus.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Parasympathetic nervous system
Cranial nerve palsies → Origin and pathways of the cranial nerves

PhXWVB.title: Glycogenolysis
PhXWVB.description: The breakdown of glycogen by glycogen phosphorylase, which shortens the polysaccharide and releases glucose-6-phosphate. Increased by epinephrine, glucagon, and AMP. Decreased by glucose-6-phosphate, insulin, and ATP.

4hX3VB.title: Hypophosphatemia
4hX3VB.description: A serum phosphate concentration < 3.0 mg/dL. Etiologies include increased renal excretion of phosphorus, insufficient intestinal absorption, and transcellular shifts. Associated with rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

khXmVB.title: U wave
khXmVB.description: A small, often absent, electrocardiogram waveform that is more pronounced in the context of hypokalemia or bradycardia. Occurs after completion of the T wave.

media.title: Sinus arrhythmia and prominent U waves

lhXvVB.title: Thermogenesis
lhXvVB.description: A heat-generating mechanism that occurs as a result of muscular activity (shivering thermogenesis), mitochondrial activity in brown adipose tissue (nonshivering thermogenesis), or the digestion of food (diet-induced thermogenesis).

NhX-VB.title: 11β-hydroxylase deficiency
NhX-VB.description: Rare type of congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Manifests with hypertension, precocious puberty, and virilization in female individuals.

mhXVeB.title: 17α-hydroxylase deficiency
mhXVeB.description: A rare cause of congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Female individuals have normal external genitalia at birth but delayed puberty. Male individuals have female external genitalia with a blind-ending vagina and intra-abdominal testes at birth.

MhXMeB.title: Oxidase
MhXMeB.description: A test used to identify bacteria that produce cytochrome c oxidase, an enzyme that converts oxygen to H₂O₂ and H₂O to produce energy. Oxidase-positive bacteria include Pseudomonas, Campylobacter jejuni, Vibrio cholerae, and Helicobacter pylori. Oxidase-negative bacteria include E. coli, Salmonella, Shigella, and Klebsiella.

nhX7eB.title: Lipoteichoic acid
nhX7eB.description: A cell wall component present in all gram-positive bacteria. Lipoteichoic acid is anchored in the cytoplasmic membrane and extends to the outer cell wall and acts as an antigen that induces TNF-α and IL-1.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

LhXweB.title: Lecithinase
LhXweB.description: A phospholipase that degrades phospholipids within cell membranes. Component of alpha-toxin produced by Clostridium perfringens; causes gas gangrene (due to myonecrosis) and hemolysis.

ohX0UB.title: Dihydrofolate reductase
ohX0UB.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of folic acid to dihydrofolate, and dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate using NADPH. THF is the active form of folate in humans, and interference with this enzyme can cause folate deficiency. DHFR can be targeted in humans (methotrexate), bacteria (trimethoprim), and protozoa (pyrimethamine).

KhXUUB.title: Bacteriophage
KhXUUB.description: A DNA/RNA virus that infects bacteria and replicates within the cell, giving the bacteria the ability to produce certain virulence factors (e.g., exotoxins).

6hXjUB.title: White dermatographism
6hXjUB.description: A physical finding of transiently blanched skin after skin stroking. Caused by cutaneous vasoconstriction. Associated with atopic dermatitis.

phXLUB.title: Fibroatheroma
phXLUB.description: An atherosclerotic lesion characterized by a necrotic core encapsulated by surrounding fibrous tissue (fibromuscular cap). The core is formed by dead, lipid-laden macrophages (i.e., foam cells). Rupture results in thrombi that can cause acute coronary syndrome.

JhXsUB.title: Coronary steal syndrome
JhXsUB.description: A phenomenon in which long-standing coronary artery disease requires maximal coronary arterial dilation distal to the stenosis to maintain normal function. Administration of vasodilators (e.g., dipyridamole) causes dilation of normal vessels, thereby resulting in shunting of blood to well-perfused myocardium. Subsequent myocardial ischemia downstream of the pathologically dilated vessels manifests as angina.

qhXCUB.title: Exfoliative toxin A
qhXCUB.description: A protease toxin produced by some strains of Staphylococcus aureus that cleaves proteins responsible for interepidermal cell attachment. Causes bullous impetigo and staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

7hX42B.title: Rib contusion
7hX42B.description: A traumatic injury to the rib without fracture that causes pleuritic chest pain and tenderness.

GhXB2B.title: Palpation of the the feet and ankles
GhXB2B.description: A part of the musculoskeletal examination. Feel the temperature of the skin (e.g., overly cool in arterial insufficiency). Press on the skin for several seconds and note whether there is pitting (e.g., edema). Press on the fingernails and note the speed of capillary refill and pedal pulses. Palpate the malleoli and test range of motion. Note any obvious swelling, tenderness, or difficulty with movement.

8hXOfB.title: Peptidoglycan
8hXOfB.description: A polymer chain of sugars (N-acetylmuramic acid and N-acetylglucosamine) and amino acids that forms the cell wall of bacteria, providing protection from osmotic pressure damage.

uhXpfB.title: Haploid cell
uhXpfB.description: A cell that contains only one unpaired set of chromosomes. Ploidy is usually referred to by the haploid number (n=1, or 1n).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

vhXAfB.title: Palpation of the shoulder region
vhXAfB.description: A part of the musculoskeletal examination. Palpate the sternoclavicular joint and assesses range of motion while exerting pressure on the clavicle cranially and caudally. Continue palpating along the clavicle to the acromioclavicular joint. Note any tenderness or swelling (e.g., as in arthritis or subluxation). Palpate the coracoid process (pain in this area suggests tendonitis). Palpate the greater tubercle of the humerus while rotating the upper arm (pain in this area suggests rotator cuff tendinopathy). Finally, palpate the border of the scapula. Note any muscle asymmetry (suggestive of nerve damage) or tenderness.

destinations.label: Orthopedic shoulder examination → Palpation of the shoulder region

DhX1TB.title: Cholera toxin
DhX1TB.description: A toxin secreted by Vibrio cholera. It causes watery diarrhea by increasing intracellular levels of cAMP, which increases secretion of water, sodium, potassium and bicarbonate into the intestinal lumen.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

whXhTB.title: Lipid A
whXhTB.description: Antigenic component of LPS in endotoxins of gram negative bacteria. Stimulates release of TNF-alpha, IL-1, IL-6.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

9hXNTB.title: Protein A
9hXNTB.description: A virulence factor that binds to the to Fc region of IgG and prevents opsonization and phagocytosis. Produced by Staphylococcus aureus.

destinations.label: Staphylococcal diseases → Resistance and virulence of staphylococci
General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

ChXqTB.title: Siderophore
ChXqTB.description: A molecule secreted by bacteria and fungi that binds, chelates, and transports iron (ferric form, Fe3+) across the cell membrane.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

xhXETB.title: Factor XII
xhXETB.description: A coagulation cascade factor that activates the kallikrein system and leads to the production of bradykinin. Can be activated by bacterial endotoxins.

BhXzTB.title: Plasmid
BhXzTB.description: A small circular dsDNA strand in the cytoplasm of a bacteria or protozoa. Plasmid genetic material can replicate independently and can confer virulence factors to other bacteria.

yhXdgB.title: Lymph node
yhXdgB.description: A secondary lymphatic organ found along lymphatic vessels that filters particles (e.g., microorganisms, cancer cells) from lymph.

AhXRgB.title: Pyramidal decussation
AhXRgB.description: The crossing of the fibers of the corticospinal tract from one side to the contralateral side. Occurs at the most caudal part of the medulla.

media.title: Brainstem and origin of cranial nerves II-XII

_hX5gB.title: Corticospinal tract
_hX5gB.description: A descending white matter tract of the spinal cord that conveys voluntary motor input to anterior horn cells. Further divided into anterior and lateral portions.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

media.title: Overview of the ascending and descending pathways of the spinal cord

zhXrgB.title: Spinothalamic tract
zhXrgB.description: A set of sensory nerves that transmit pain and temperature (lateral tract) as well as crude touch and pressure (anterior tract). Neurons receive signals from primary neurons exiting the Lissauer tract and project axons that decussate in the anterior white commissure and ascend on the contralateral side of the body to the thalamus.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

media.title: Overview of the ascending and descending pathways of the spinal cord
Ascending sensory tracts of the spinal cord

-hXDgB.title: Dorsal column
-hXDgB.description: The white matter of the dorsal (posterior) aspect of the spinal cord. Consists of the fasciculus gracilis, which carries sensory impulses (including pressure, vibration, fine touch, and proprioception) from the lower limb and foot, and the fasciculus cuneatus, which carries sensory impulses from the upper limbs.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

Y3XnSB.title: Major basic protein
Y3XnSB.description: The predominant granule of eosinophils. Involved in host defense against helminths and parasites. In allergic asthma, it causes damage to epithelial cells in the lungs, which leads to bronchospasm.

b3XHSB.title: Dihydrouridine
b3XHSB.description: A modified form of uracil found in the D-arm of tRNA molecules. Facilitates recognition of tRNA by the correct aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

X3X9SB.title: Acceptor stem
X3X9SB.description: The 5'-CCA-3' terminal end of the tRNA molecule that covalently binds to an amino acid, which creates a charged tRNA molecule.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

c3XahB.title: D-arm
c3XahB.description: The dihydrouridine-containing region of a tRNA molecule needed for correct recognition by the proper aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

13X2hB.title: Poly-A polymerase
13X2hB.description: The enzyme responsible for the addition of the 3' poly-A tail (~200 adenines long) to the end of mRNA molecules before leaving the nucleus. It does not require a template.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Post-transcriptional modification (RNA processing)

W3XPhB.title: Aminoacyl-tRNA
W3XPhB.description: A tRNA molecule to which its specific amino acid has been covalently bound in an ATP-dependent manner by a specific aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → tRNA charging

d3XohB.title: Aminoacyl site
d3XohB.description: The area of the ribosome where a charged aminoacyl-tRNA molecule first binds to its anticodon during translation.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

V3XGhB.title: GTP
V3XGhB.description: A nucleoside triphosphate molecule commonly used as a source of energy for enzymatic reactions, including translation, gluconeogenesis, and signal transduction. Generated during the Krebs cycle.

e3XxhB.title: Peptidyl site
e3XxhB.description: The area of the ribosome that secures the tRNA molecule attached to the synthesizing polypeptide during translation.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

U3Xb3B.title: Peptidyl-tRNA
U3Xb3B.description: A peptide connected to a transfer RNA (tRNA). During translation, a peptidyl-tRNA initially binds to the A site of a ribosome, then transfers to the P site, where the tRNA is held as the peptide is added to the synthesizing polypeptide chain.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

23XT3B.title: Ribozyme
23XT3B.description: An RNA molecule that can catalyze a specific biochemical reaction (e.g., peptide bond formation during elongation in protein synthesis).

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

f3Xk3B.title: Virion
f3Xk3B.description: The infective form of a virus when present outside of cells, which consists of DNA or RNA, a protein capsid, and sometimes an envelope.

T3X63B.title: Capsid
T3X63B.description: A protein capsule that covers the genome of a virus. It is composed of capsomeres (aggregations of protomer subunits).

media.title: General structures of different virus particles

g3XF3B.title: Organ of Corti
g3XF3B.description: A cochlear organ that transduces sound waves into hearing potential, which is then converted to an action potential of the cochlear nerve.

S3Xy3B.title: Calretinin
S3Xy3B.description: A protein expressed in tissues of mesothelial origin (e.g., mesothelioma).

h3XcRB.title: Large cell carcinoma
h3XcRB.description: A poorly differentiated, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) characterized by large, pleomorphic cells. Typically develops in the lung periphery and has a poor prognosis.

33XSRB.title: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor antagonists
33XSRB.description: A group of agents that bind to anterior pituitary gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptors and decrease the secretion of luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone, which leads to a decrease in circulating androgens and estrogen. Used to prevent ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome and to treat prostate cancer. Also administered during infertility treatment to prevent premature ovulation.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

i3XJRB.title: Silicotic nodule
i3XJRB.description: A histopathologic finding of chronic silicosis characterized by weakly birefringent silica particles in a central hyalinized region surrounded by concentric collagen fibers (that resemble an onion skin).

j3X_RB.title: Reinke crystals
j3X_RB.description: A collection of rod-like, eosinophilic, cytoplasmic inclusions that can be found in Leydig cells of the testes in association with Leydig cell tumors.

P3XWiB.title: Hypotelorism
P3XWiB.description: An abnormally decreased distance between two organs or bodily parts, most commonly the eyes (orbital hypotelorism). Often a result of fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), but also associated with Patau syndrome (trisomy 13), fragile X syndrome, and Prader-Willi syndrome.

43X3iB.title: Palmoplantar erythrodysesthesia
43X3iB.description: A condition characterized by erythema and swelling of the palms and soles with associated pain, paresthesias, and desquamation of skin. It is typically an adverse effect of antineoplastic drugs, such as 5-fluorouracil, capecitabine, cytarabine, doxorubicin, and docetaxel.

destinations.label: Complications of cancer therapy → Dermatological complications

l3XviB.title: Ventral horn
l3XviB.description: The anterior subdivision of gray matter occurring longitudinally within the spinal cord that contains alpha motor neurons. Each horn is organized somatotopically, with the medial portions innervating the proximal muscles of the limbs, while the lateral portions innervate the distal muscles.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

N3X-iB.title: Dorsal horn
N3X-iB.description: The posterior subdivision of gray matter occurring longitudinally within the spinal cord that contains neurons entering ascending pathways carrying sensory information to the brain.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

media.title: Transverse sections of the spinal cord

m3XVQB.title: Lateral horn
m3XVQB.description: The lateral subdivision of gray matter found longitudinally within the spinal cord between the levels of T1 to L3. Seen in cross-sections of the spinal cord as a lateral projection located between the dorsal and ventral horns. Contains sympathetic neurons that control autonomic function.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

media.title: Cross section of the spinal cord

L3XwQB.title: Dorsal root ganglion
L3XwQB.description: A cluster of nerve cell bodies that emerges from each level of the spinal cord. Contains the cell bodies of sensory (afferent) neurons.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

media.title: Segment of the spinal cord with spinal roots, nerves, and fibers

o3X0jB.title: Filum terminale
o3X0jB.description: A fibrous extension of the meninges that extends from the conus medullaris to attach to the sacrum and coccyx.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

media.title: Important structures of the spinal cord

K3XUjB.title: Posterior thoracic nucleus
K3XUjB.description: A small group of interneurons found in the intermediate zone of the spinal cord. Relays unconscious proprioception to the cerebellum.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

63XjjB.title: Motor unit
63XjjB.description: A functional unit that consists of a motor neuron and the skeletal myocytes that it innervates.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

q3XCjB.title: Renshaw cells
q3XCjB.description: A type of inhibitory interneuron found in the spinal cord. Inhibits alpha motor neurons via the neurotransmitter glycine, which decreases the rate of action potentials fired.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

v3XA4B.title: Zinc salt
v3XA4B.description: Used to treat and prevent zinc deficiency. Also used as a medical therapy for Wilson disease by blocking intestinal copper absorption via the induction of intestinal cell metallothionein.

y3XdOB.title: Parkinson disease
y3XdOB.description: A neurodegenerative disease involving a progressive depletion of dopaminergic neurons in the basal ganglia, particularly the substantia nigra. The typical clinical picture seen in PD is called "parkinsonism" and features the classical cardinal symptom of bradykinesia along with resting tremor and/or rigidity. Postural instability is another frequent late finding. Neuropsychiatric and nonmotor manifestations include cognitive dysfunction, depression, and psychosis.

z3XrOB.title: Odontoid process
z3XrOB.description: A bony protuberance at the upper part of the second cervical vertebra (axis). It projects upward, fitting into the anterior arch of the first cervical vertebra (atlas). This articulation forms the pivotal joint around which the atlas and the skull rotate, crucial for head movement.

0RXelB.title: Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex
0RXelB.description: A complex of enzymes located in the mitochondrion that are required to link glycolysis to the citric acid cycle. Pyruvate and NAD+ are converted to acetyl-CoA and NADH. There are five essential cofactors: vitamins B1, B2, B3, B5, and lipoic acid.

aRXQlB.title: α-Ketoglutarate dehydrogenase
aRXQlB.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of α-ketoglutarate into succinyl-CoA and CO2 during the citric acid cycle in the presence of these cofactors: B1, B2, B3, B5, and lipoic acid. One NAD molecule is also reduced.

dRXoNB.title: Exteroception
dRXoNB.description: The sense of external stimuli applied to the body. Consists of tactile sense, thermoception, and nociception.

VRXGNB.title: Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3
VRXGNB.description: A receptor responsible for normal chondrocyte function and cartilage growth. Mutations in the gene that encodes this receptor cause growth abnormalities of connective tissue, including achondroplasia and craniosynostosis.

2RXTmB.title: Pancreatic duct
2RXTmB.description: A duct that extends from the tail of the pancreas to the head of the pancreas. Carries exocrine pancreatic enzymes. Joins with the common bile duct to form the hepatopancreatic ampulla. Obstruction of this duct (e.g., due to gallstones in the common bile duct) can result in acute pancreatitis.

fRXkmB.title: Hepatopancreatic sphincter
fRXkmB.description: A smooth muscle ring that surrounds the common bile duct and distal pancreatic duct as they enter the duodenum. Regulates flow of bile into the duodenum and prevents reflux of intestinal contents and bile into the ducts.

TRX6mB.title: Pancreatic islets
TRX6mB.description: A group of cells in the pancreas that arise from pancreatic buds. Contains α, β, and δ endocrine cells.

media.title: Exocrine acini and endocrine islets of Langerhans

SRXymB.title: Extraglomerular mesangial cells
SRXymB.description: A type of cell found in the juxtaglomerular complex between the macula densa and juxtaglomerular effector cells. Involved in autoregulation of blood flow to the kidney.

3RXS5B.title: Thyroglossal duct
3RXS5B.description: An embryological structure that forms when the thyroid diverticulum (thyroid gland precursor) located at the base of the tongue descends to the final location of the thyroid gland (anterior to the thyroid cartilage). The duct usually obliterates after the thyroid gland has descended; the foramen cecum of the tongue remains.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Embryology

PRXWMB.title: Pterygopalatine ganglion
PRXWMB.description: A parasympathetic ganglion found in the pterygopalatine fossa of the skull. Contains sensory branches (from the maxillary nerve), parasympathetic branches (from the facial nerve), and sympathetic branches (from the superior cervical ganglion).

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Parasympathetic nervous system

media.title: Parasympathetic innervation to the head and neck

MRXMnB.title: DNA crosslink
MRXMnB.description: A replication-halting lesion caused by covalent linkage of two nucleotides, either on the same strand (intrastrand) or on opposite strands (interstrand) of double-stranded DNA. Genetic defects in the pathway responsible for repairing these lesions results in Fanconi anemia.

LRXwnB.title: Inulin
LRXwnB.description: A polysaccharide that can be used to calculate the glomerular filtration rate. Because it is neither reabsorbed nor secreted in the nephron, the amount that is present in urine directly represents the amount that was filtered in the glomeruli.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function

oRX0LB.title: Renal blood flow
oRX0LB.description: The blood volume that flows through the kidney per unit time. Normally ~ 20% of cardiac output.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Renal blood flow

KRXULB.title: Renal plasma flow
KRXULB.description: The volume of plasma entering the kidney per unit time. RPF = (UPAH x Urine flow rate)/PPAH, where UPAH = urine concentration of para-aminohippuric acid (PAH) and PPAH = plasma concentration of PAH.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Renal blood flow

qRXCLB.title: Angiogenesis
qRXCLB.description: The normal physiological development of new blood vessels. Not to be confused with neovascularization, which refers to pathological formation of new blood vessels (e.g., in abnormal tissue or in abnormal locations).

IRXYoB.title: Macula densa
IRXYoB.description: A specialized group of tall cuboidal cells in the distal convoluted tubule of the kidney that are a part of the juxtaglomerular apparatus. Senses Na+ levels and controls renin release, glomerular filtration, and renal blood flow through signaling pathways that include COX-2 mediated prostaglandin secretion (tubuloglomerular feedback).

rRXfoB.title: Suspensory ligaments of the breast
rRXfoB.description: The suspensory ligaments of Cooper are fibrocollagenous connections between the dermis of the breast and the deep fascia over the pectoral muscles. They support and maintain the shape of the breast parenchyma.

7RX4oB.title: Lymphoma
7RX4oB.description: A hematologic cancer characterized by a discrete tumor mass in the lymph nodes. Further categorized into Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas.

tRXXKB.title: Myocyte
tRXXKB.description: The primary cell found in muscle tissue. Further subdivided into cardiac, skeletal, and smooth types.

FRXgKB.title: Skeletal muscle
FRXgKB.description: A type of striated muscle that consists of large, elongated, multinucleated cells organized into sarcomeres. Attaches to bones via tendons. Facilitates voluntary movement coordinated by the somatic nervous system.

8RXOKB.title: Striated muscle
8RXOKB.description: A type of muscle tissue formed by elongated, multinucleated fibers (myofilaments) arranged into sarcomeres. Includes cardiac muscle and skeletal muscle.

uRXpKB.title: Synovium
uRXpKB.description: A specialized type of connective tissue found in the inner surface of the capsule of synovial joints. Composed of 2 layers: the intima (inner layer, contains type A and type B cells) and the subintima (outer layer, contains fibrous, areolar, and adipose tissue). The synovium surrounds the synovial space.

ERX8KB.title: Pseudostratified epithelium
ERX8KB.description: A type of epithelium that consists of a single layer of cells but appears as if it was formed by multiple layers of cells because the nuclei are positioned at different levels.

DRX16B.title: Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium
DRX16B.description: A type of squamous epithelium protected by layers of dead, keratin-containing cells. Found in the epidermis of the skin and certain parts of the oral mucosa (e.g., gingiva, dorsal surface of the tongue, hard palate).

9RXN6B.title: Hexosaminidase A
9RXN6B.description: A lysosomal enzyme. Deficiency of this enzyme, which causes Tay-Sachs disease, leads to the accumulation of GM2 ganglioside.

CRXq6B.title: Uroporphyrinogen III decarboxylase
CRXq6B.description: The fifth enzyme in the pathway of heme biosynthesis. Converts uroporphyrinogen III to coproporphyrinogen III. Deficiency leads to accumulation of uroporphyrinogen and resulting porphyria cutanea tarda (especially after sun exposure).

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

xRXE6B.title: Glycoprotein120
xRXE6B.description: Docking envelope protein on the surface of HIV. Formed by cleavage of gp160 into gp120 and gp41. Essential for HIV attachment to host cells (e.g., CD4 T cells).

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

BRXz6B.title: Glycoprotein 41
BRXz6B.description: Transmembrane envelope protein on the surface of HIV. Formed by cleavage of gp160 into gp41 and gp120. Essential for fusion and entry of HIV into the host cells (e.g., CD4 T cells).

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

ARXRpB.title: Reverse transcriptase
ARXRpB.description: An enzyme produced by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) that converts viral RNA to DNA. Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors are used in the treatment of HIV.

_RX5pB.title: Macrophage-tropic human immunodeficiency virus
_RX5pB.description: A strain of HIV with tropism for macrophages (instead of T cells). Typically seen with CNS involvement of HIV infection.

zRXrpB.title: Integrase
zRXrpB.description: An enzyme produced by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) that incorporates the viral genome into the host cell DNA. Inhibitors of integrase (e.g., raltegravir and dolutegravir) are used in the treatment of HIV.

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

-RXDpB.title: Interoception
-RXDpB.description: A sense of stimuli applied to or arising in the internal organs and structures of the body.

0iXeJB.title: Mechanoreceptor
0iXeJB.description: A sensory neuron that responds to mechanical distortion or pressure. Functions to detect stimuli (e.g., touch, pressure, vibration, sound) from the environment. Examples include Ruffini, Meissner, and Pacinian corpuscles, Merkel discs, and cochlear hair cells.

media.title: Mechanoelectrical transduction of sound waves by inner hair cells

YiXnJB.title: Ruffini corpuscles
YiXnJB.description: A type of mechanoreceptor located in the fingertips and joints. They are slow-adapting mechanoreceptors sensitive to mechanical pressure, objects slipping along the skin surface, and joint-angle changes.

ciXaqB.title: Meissner corpuscles
ciXaqB.description: A type of mechanoreceptor located in superficial layers of hairless skin (e.g., the epidermis and upper dermis of the fingertips and eyelids). They are rapidly adapting mechanoreceptors sensitive to dynamic, fine, and light touch, position, and low-frequency vibrations (30–50 Hz).

diXoqB.title: Pacinian corpuscles
diXoqB.description: A type of mechanoreceptor located in the deep layers of the skin (e.g., dermis and subcutaneous layer), ligaments, and joints. They are very rapidly adapting and are sensitive to high-frequency (100–400 Hz) vibrations, deep touch, and mechanical pressure.

UiXbIB.title: Thermoreceptors
UiXbIB.description: The free nerve endings that detect hot and cold sensations on the skin. These sensations are transmitted via Aδ and C fibers.

QiXurB.title: Muscle spindle
QiXurB.description: A structure formed by intrafusal muscle fibers (modified skeletal muscle fibers), nerve fibers, and a surrounding perineural capsule. Involved in proprioception and is activated by alteration of muscle length.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord reflexes

jiX_rB.title: Golgi tendon organ
jiX_rB.description: A sensory organ for proprioception. Located at the junctions between tendon and muscle, they respond to tension and force within the muscle. Increased force and tension results in lengthening of muscle, which triggers relaxation of antagonist muscles and inhibition of agonist muscles to prevent excessive muscle tension that can damage the muscle.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord reflexes

4iX37B.title: Intrafusal muscle fibers
4iX37B.description: A type of muscle fiber located within the muscle spindle that serves as a proprioceptor (e.g., joint position, rate of muscle stretch). Consists of nuclear bag and nuclear chain fibers. Runs in parallel with skeletal muscle fibers.

kiXm7B.title: Extrafusal muscle fibers
kiXm7B.description: A type of skeletal muscle fiber that is located outside of the muscle spindle and contracts in response to stimulation by a motor neuron.

OiXI7B.title: Golgi tendon reflex
OiXI7B.description: An inhibitory muscle reflex that is triggered by Golgi tendon organs (sensory organs for proprioception) to prevent muscle damage. Increased force and tension result in muscle lengthening, which triggers the contraction of antagonist muscles and the inhibition of agonist muscles.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord reflexes

5iXiHB.title: Somatosensory cortex
5iXiHB.description: A part of the cerebral cortex located in the postcentral gyrus. Receives the bulk of the sensory input from the body.

destinations.label: The somatosensory system → Central processing of sensory information

MiXMHB.title: Primary somatosensory cortex
MiXMHB.description: The region of the parietal lobe cortex that is responsible for processing general somatic sensations such as touch, pressure, vibration, pain, and temperature.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex
The somatosensory system → Central processing of sensory information

niX7HB.title: Sensory homunculus
niX7HB.description: A somatotopic representation of the body. The human body is depicted according to the region of the brain that receives sensory input from a specific body part. The size of the cortical area for each body part is directly related to the degree of sensory input from that area (e.g., the face and the hands have larger areas of cortical representation than the lower extremities).

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

LiXwHB.title: Secondary somatosensory cortex
LiXwHB.description: A brain structure located at the parietal operculum on the ceiling of the lateral sulcus. Involved in the recognition and interpretation of stimuli. Receives afferent input from the primary somatosensory cortex. Gives efferent output to the amygdala (emotional response) and hippocampus (tactile learning and tactile memory).

destinations.label: The somatosensory system → Central processing of sensory information

KiXUsB.title: Pneumocystis choroiditis
KiXUsB.description: A rare condition that is most commonly seen in patients with disseminated Pneumocystis infections (usually from the lungs). Causes multiple, bilateral, yellow-white choroidal lesions that spare the retina. Visual changes are uncommon.

6iXjsB.title: Appendix
6iXjsB.description: A vestigial, blind-ended tube attached to the proximal cecum, close to the ileocecal valve.  Obstruction due to lymphatic hyperplasia or fecalith impaction can result in appendicitis.

CiXqFB.title: Enamel
CiXqFB.description: The highly mineralized, hard part of the tooth that covers the crown and acts as a protective barrier. Can be degraded by acids from food and drink.

media.title: Fine structure of the dental crown

xiXEFB.title: Ameloblast
xiXEFB.description: A type of cell derived from surface ectoderm involved in enamel formation of the teeth.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

XQX9uB.title: Koilocyte
XQX9uB.description: A dysplastic squamous cell characterized by a well-defined, clear, balloon-like, perinuclear halo and hyperchromasia. Pathognomonic of HPV infection.

cQXaEB.title: Preganglionic nerve fiber
cQXaEB.description: A parasympathetic or sympathetic neuron that releases acetylcholine to activate the postganglionic nerve fiber.

media.title: Overview of somatic and autonomic motor pathways and neurotransmitters

1QX2EB.title: Postganglionic nerve fiber
1QX2EB.description: A parasympathetic or sympathetic nerve fiber that is activated by acetylcholine release from preganglionic nerve fibers. Parasympathetic postganglionic neurons then release ACh. Sympathetic postganglionic neurons then release norepinephrine and/or epinephrine (with the exception of nerve fibers innervating the sweat glands and arrector pili muscles, which release acetylcholine).

media.title: Overview of somatic and autonomic motor pathways and neurotransmitters

WQXPEB.title: Chromaffin cells
WQXPEB.description: A group of neuroendocrine cells found in the adrenal medulla and other ganglia of the sympathetic nervous system. Release epinephrine and norepinephrine.

dQXoEB.title: Zona glomerulosa
dQXoEB.description: The outermost layer of the adrenal cortex. Produces mineralocorticoids (e.g., aldosterone). Activated by angiotensin II.

media.title: Location and microscopic anatomy of the adrenal gland

VQXGEB.title: Zona fasciculata
VQXGEB.description: The middle layer of the adrenal cortex. Produces glucocorticoids (e.g., cortisol). Activated by ACTH from the anterior pituitary.

media.title: Location and microscopic anatomy of the adrenal gland

eQXxEB.title: Zona reticularis
eQXxEB.description: The innermost layer of the adrenal cortex. Produces androgens (e.g., androstenedione). Activated by ACTH from the anterior pituitary.

media.title: Location and microscopic anatomy of the adrenal gland

UQXbvB.title: Sirenomelia
UQXbvB.description: A condition of sacral agenesis and fusion of the lower extremities. Thought to be caused by dysfunction of the vitelline artery.

2QXTvB.title: BCR-ABL
2QXTvB.description: A fusion protein and constitutively active tyrosine kinase produced by t(9;22) chromosomal translocation (Philadelphia chromosome) in patients with chronic myeloid leukemia.

fQXkvB.title: Plasmin
fQXkvB.description: A serine protease that degrades formed fibrin clots (fibrinolysis) and certain coagulation factors (e.g., factor IIa). Its inactive precursor is plasminogen.

TQX6vB.title: Supravalvular aortic stenosis
TQX6vB.description: A narrowing the of aorta immediately superior to the aortic valve. Classically associated with Williams Syndrome.

SQXyvB.title: Adipocyte
SQXyvB.description: A cell that stores energy as fat. Constitutes the major component of adipose tissue.

hQXcDB.title: Tunica albuginea
hQXcDB.description: The fibrous layer of connective tissue surrounding the corpora cavernosa of the penis and testes (in males), and the ovaries in females.

3QXSDB.title: Lateral geniculate nucleus
3QXSDB.description: A thalamic nucleus involved in the visual pathway. Receives visual information from the retina via the optic tract and transmits information via the ipsilateral optic radiation to the visual cortex.

RQXlDB.title: Circle of Willis
RQXlDB.description: An anastomosis of blood vessels that supplies the brain and consists of the following arteries: the anterior cerebral artery, anterior communicating arteries, internal carotid arteries, posterior cerebral arteries, and posterior communicating arteries.

iQXJDB.title: Neuroectoderm
iQXJDB.description: A part of the ectoderm that gives rise to the neural plate and differentiates into the central nervous system by the process of neurulation. Induced by the notochord.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

QQXuDB.title: Alternative pathway
QQXuDB.description: The activation of the complement system directly by pathogens (microbial surface molecules).

jQX_DB.title: Synaptophysin
jQX_DB.description: A protein found in synaptic vesicles in the central nervous system and neuroendocrine cells. Used as a biomarker for tumors of neuroendocrine origin.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

PQXWwB.title: Hyperdefecation
PQXWwB.description: An abnormally increased frequency of bowel movements (often defined as > 3 bowel movements per day) without the change in stool consistency associated with diarrhea. Most often occurs as a consequence of hyperthyroidism.

4QX3wB.title: Mucin
4QX3wB.description: A family of proteins that are composed of glycosylated polysaccharides, which allow them to absorb water and form gel-like secretions. Mucins are found in particular on mucosal surfaces and provide a protective barrier, e.g., preventing chemical injury from gastric acid.

kQXmwB.title: Napsin A
kQXmwB.description: An immunohistochemical marker for adenocarcinoma of the lung. Used in conjunction with TTF-1.

OQXIwB.title: Palpation of the inguinal lymph nodes
OQXIwB.description: A part of the physical examination. Adjust the patient's gown so that the medial aspect of the thigh is accessible while the genitals remain covered. With the tip of your fingers, palpate horizontally along the inguinal ligament and vertically along the femoral artery. Note any fixed nodularity, tenderness, or swelling.

lQXvwB.title: Erythrogenic exotoxin A
lQXvwB.description: A superantigen produced by group A streptococci that causes nonspecific cytokine release, which causes toxic shock–like syndrome.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

NQX-wB.title: Anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
NQX-wB.description: A rare congenital cardiac anomaly in which the left coronary artery arises from the pulmonary artery. Infants with this condition typically develop pallor, irritability, and diaphoresis after feeding. Can progress to congestive heart failure.

mQXV9B.title: International medical graduate
mQXV9B.description: A term referring to physicians (or aspiring physicians) who received their medical school education outside the United States. This can include both US citizens who studied abroad (US IMGs) and non-US citizens who studied abroad (non-US IMGs).

5QXi9B.title: Hyaluronidase
5QXi9B.description: An enzyme that degrades hyaluronic acid. Produced by some bacteria, including Streptococcus and Staphylococcus, as a virulence factor to facilitate invasion of host tissue.

MQXM9B.title: Hyaluronic acid capsule
MQXM9B.description: A virulence factor of Streptococcus pyogenes that inhibits phagocytosis.

nQX79B.title: Streptolysin O
nQX79B.description: A virulence factor produced by Streptococcus pyogenes that degrades cell membranes, which lyses RBCs and is responsible for β-hemolysis.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

LQXw9B.title: Assessing speech
LQXw9B.description: Note the quantity, rate, loudness, articulation, and fluency (e.g., monotone inflection, hesitancy in the flow of speech, malformed sentences, circumlocutions) of the patient's speech. Abnormalities are associated with conditions such as mood disorders and aphasias.

oQX0CB.title: Fibroblast growth factor receptor 1
oQX0CB.description: A receptor responsible for normal chondrocyte function and cartilage growth. Mutations in the gene that encodes this receptor is associated with Kallman syndrome.

KQXUCB.title: Aortic root dilation
KQXUCB.description: An aneurysm of the proximal thoracic aorta associated with connective tissue disorders such as Marfan syndrome and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Clinical features

6QXjCB.title: Gain-of-function mutation
6QXjCB.description: A mutation in a gene that results in increased function of that gene. Converts proto-oncogenes into oncogenes.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

pQXLCB.title: Superior cervical ganglion
pQXLCB.description: A sympathetic ganglion of the sympathetic trunk located adjacent to the 2nd and 3rd cervical vertebrae. Its fibers travel along the internal carotid artery and innervate the head and neck, including the internal carotid artery, cutaneous blood vessels, eye, thyroid gland, salivary glands, lacrimal gland, and pineal gland.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system

JQXsCB.title: High-density lipoprotein
JQXsCB.description: A lipoprotein that transports cholesterol from extrahepatic tissue to the liver.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

qQXCCB.title: Classical pathway
qQXCCB.description: The activation of the complement system by antigen-antibody complexes (IgG- or IgM-mediated).

media.title: Classical pathway of the complement system

IQXYxB.title: Pyelonephritis-associated pili
IQXYxB.description: A virulence factor of uropathogenic E. coli that promotes adherence to urothelial cells via cellular projections composed of glycoproteins. Involved in the pathogenesis of cystitis and pyelonephritis.

7QX4xB.title: Call-Exner bodies
7QX4xB.description: Granulosa cells arranged in clusters surrounding a central cavity with eosinophilic secretions, resembling primordial follicles. Characteristic of granulosa cell tumors, a type of malignant sex cord stromal tumors.

destinations.label: Overview of ovarian tumors →  Sex cord-stromal tumors of the ovary

sQXtxB.title: Epithelial ovarian tumors
sQXtxB.description: Most common ovarian neoplasms. Includes malignant types (serous cystadenocarcinoma, mucinous cystadenocarcinoma) and benign types (serous cystadenoma, mucinous cystadenoma, endometrioma).

destinations.label: Overview of ovarian tumors →  Epithelial ovarian tumors

GQXBxB.title: Schiller-Duval bodies
GQXBxB.description: A histopathologic structure that resembles glomeruli of the kidney. Pathognomonic of yolk sac tumors (found in approximately 50% of cases).

tQXXBB.title: Voltage-gated potassium channel
tQXXBB.description: Potassium-selective channels that are involved in repolarization of myocytes during the action potential. There are two types of voltage-gated potassium channels: delayed rectifier potassium channels and the rapidly activating A-type channels. They are sensitive to voltage changes across the cell membrane and open during phase 2 (delayed rectifier) and phase 3 (delayed and rapid rectifiers) of the myocyte action potential.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Action potential

FQXgBB.title: V600E mutation
FQXgBB.description: A substitution of glutamic acid (E) in place of valine (V) at amino acid position 600 caused by activating mutations in the BRAF gene. Cancers (e.g., certain melanomas) with this mutation can be treated with vemurafenib, a BRAF kinase inhibitor.

8QXOBB.title: Adrenocortical carcinoma
8QXOBB.description: A rare cancer of the adrenal gland. Most cases are sporadic, but some are associated with hereditary cancer syndromes (e.g., Li-Fraumeni syndrome, Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1). Can cause syndromes of hormone excess (e.g., Cushing syndrome, virilization).

uQXpBB.title: Sarcoma
uQXpBB.description: A cancer of connective tissue (e.g., muscle, nerve, or bone). Comprises soft tissue sarcomas (e.g., leiomyosarcoma and liposarcoma) and sarcomas of bone and cartilage (e.g., osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma).

EQX8BB.title: TTF-1
EQX8BB.description: An immunohistochemical marker for follicular, papillary, and medullary thyroid carcinomas as well as adenocarcinoma of the lung.

vQXABB.title: Prodrome
vQXABB.description: A collection of early signs and symptoms that precede other characteristic findings of a condition. For example, dizziness, a sense of warmth, and pallor are prodromal symptoms of syncope.

DQX1yB.title: Luteinization
DQX1yB.description: Process by which the corpus luteum forms in the ovaries. Occurs after the oocyte has been released from the follicle. Induced by increased levels of estrogen during the later stage of the follicular phase, which causes granulosa and theca cells to express LH receptors. The LH surge then transforms these cells into luteal cells.

wQXhyB.title: Endometrial desquamation
wQXhyB.description: Process by which the endometrium atrophies, becomes ischemic, and sloughs off as menses in the absence of implantation. Results from vasospasm of uterine spiral arteries, which deprives the endometrium from blood flow.

9QXNyB.title: Secretory phase
9QXNyB.description: The third (and final) phase of the uterine cycle, which corresponds to days 14–28 of the menstrual cycle. Characterized by endometrial differentiation, which is induced by progesterone in preparation for possible implantation and pregnancy. If pregnancy does not occur, subsequent decreases in progesterone levels induce necrosis of the functional endometrium, thereby resulting in menstruation.

CQXqyB.title: Luteal phase
CQXqyB.description: The second phase of the ovarian cycle, which corresponds with days 14-28 of the menstrual cycle. Characterized by transformation of granulosa and theca cells into luteal cells under the influence of progesterone.

xQXEyB.title: Follicular phase
xQXEyB.description: The first phase of the ovarian cycle, which corresponds with days 1-14 of the menstrual cycle. Characterized by maturation of a dominant follicle under the influence of estrogen, which then releases the oocyte during ovulation.

BQXzyB.title: Proliferative phase of the menstrual cycle
BQXzyB.description: The second phase of the uterine cycle, which corresponds with days 4-14 of the menstrual cycle. Characterized by regeneration of the functional layer of the endometrium before ovulation occurs.

yQXdAB.title: Pinworm test
yQXdAB.description: A simple test to detect Enterobius vermicularis eggs. A strip of cellophane tape is is attached to the anal region for a few seconds and then transferred to a glass slide. If present, the eggs can be detected through microscopy.

AQXRAB.title: Meteorism
AQXRAB.description: An excessive accumulation of gas in the gastrointestinal tract that results in abdominal distention. Causes include bowel obstruction, increased fermentation in the intestinal lumen due to bacterial overgrowth, and inflammatory bowel disease.

-QXDAB.title: Membrane attack complex
-QXDAB.description: End product of the complement system pathways (classical, lectin, alternative) composed of complement factors C5, C6, C7, C8, and C9. These factors bind to the surface of pathogens and form a transmembrane channel, leading to cytolysis and cell death. Plays a particularly important role in fighting gram-negative bacteria (e.g., Neisseria).

ZjXZ_B.title: Respiratory center
ZjXZ_B.description: A collection of neurons located in the medulla oblongata and pons that regulate respiratory rate and tidal volume. Receives signals from the cortex, hypothalamus, mechanoreceptors, and chemoreceptors.

ajXQ_B.title: True vocal cords
ajXQ_B.description: The thickened edges of the cricovocal membrane and ligament that form part of the glottis and facilitate air passage for phonation. Lined by stratified squamous epithelium.

YjXn_B.title: Enteric nervous system
YjXn_B.description: A component of the autonomic nervous system (ANS) that influences the function of the gastrointestinal tract. The nerve cell bodies of the enteric nervous system are located in two plexuses: the myenteric plexus (Auerbach plexus) and the submucous plexus (Meissner plexus).

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Enteric nervous system

media.title: Autonomic innervation of the gastrointestinal tract

XjX9_B.title: Gastrocolic ligament
XjX9_B.description: A part of the greater omentum that connects the greater curvature of the stomach to the transverse colon. Contains the right and left gastroepiploic vessels.

cjXazB.title: Gastrosplenic ligament
cjXazB.description: A fold of peritoneum that extends from the greater curvature of the stomach to the splenic hilum. Contains the left gastroepiploic artery and short gastric branches of the splenic artery.

1jX2zB.title: The arc of Riolan
1jX2zB.description: An anastomotic network between the branches of the middle colic artery (superior mesenteric artery) and the left colic artery (inferior mesenteric artery). Provides collateral blood supply to the splenic flexure.

media.title: Arterial blood supply of the colon

WjXPzB.title: Crypts of Lieberkuhn
WjXPzB.description: A series of invaginations in the lamina propria of the gastrointestinal tract (between two adjacent villi) that contain Paneth cells, goblet cells, and stem cells.

media.title: Intestinal villi and crypts of Lieberkuhn

djXozB.title: Proper hepatic artery
djXozB.description: A branch of the common hepatic artery and part of the portal triad. Bifurcates into the left and right hepatic arteries.

VjXGzB.title: Portal vein
VjXGzB.description: A large blood vessel that conveys nutrient-rich blood from the gastrointestinal tract to the liver. About 75% of hepatic blood flow is from this structure with the remainder largely coming from the hepatic artery.

ejXxzB.title: Hepatocyte
ejXxzB.description: The main cell that makes up the liver. Involved in protein synthesis and storage, carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, and detoxification.

UjXb-B.title: Kupffer cell
UjXb-B.description: A specialized macrophage that resides in the liver sinusoids. They function primarily to clear aged red blood cells and bacteria.

fjXk-B.title: Stellate cell (liver)
fjXk-B.description: A cell found in the perisinusoidal space of the liver that stores vitamin A and produces extracellular matrix in response to liver injury.

gjXF-B.title: Alcohol dehydrogenase
gjXF-B.description: Enzyme that converts ingested methanol to acetaldehyde, with the reduction of NAD+ to NADH. Found in the liver and the stomach, primarily.

3jXSZy.title: Round ligament of the liver
3jXSZy.description: A remnant of the fetal umbilical vein that lies within the free edge of the falciform ligament.

RjXlZy.title: Hepatomegaly
RjXlZy.description: An abnormal enlargement of the liver (e.g., liver span > 16 cm in the midclavicular line on ultrasound). Common causes are malignancy, infection, and venous congestion.

QjXuZy.title: Splenic artery
QjXuZy.description: A branch of the celiac trunk that supplies the spleen and parts of the stomach and pancreas. Further divides into the short gastric and left gastroepiploic arteries.

jjX_Zy.title: Splenic vein
jjX_Zy.description: A vein formed by the union of several small veins that return blood from the stomach, pancreas, spleen, and hindgut. It unites with the superior mesenteric vein to form the portal vein.

PjXW0y.title: Splenorenal ligament
PjXW0y.description: A fold of peritoneum (peritoneal ligament) that runs from the splenic hilum to the posterior abdominal wall. Contains the tail of the pancreas and a portion of the splenic artery and vein.

4jX30y.title: Red pulp
4jX30y.description: The portion of the spleen composed of splenic cords and sinuses (sinusoids). Populated predominantly by macrophages, which facilitate the filtrating functionality of the spleen.

media.title: Red and white pulp of the spleen

OjXI0y.title: Secretory initiation
OjXI0y.description: A stage of lactogenesis that occurs during the second half of pregnancy as the result of high levels of circulating progesterone. During this time, small amounts of milk can be secreted.

ljXv0y.title: Secretory activation
ljXv0y.description: The second stage of lactogenesis. Occurs after delivery of the infant and is triggered by the rapid decline in progesterone. Characterized by rapid production of breast milk.

NjX-0y.title: Carotid bruit
NjX-0y.description: A pathologic sound heard on auscultation over the carotid artery that is caused by turbulent blood flow. Associated with carotid artery stenosis.

mjXVay.title: Erb point (cardiology)
mjXVay.description: An area at the left third intercostal space, along the parasternal line, at which the murmur of aortic regurgitation is best auscultated, especially with the patient leaning forward.

5jXiay.title: CD1a
5jXiay.description: A protein that mediates antigen presentation. Expressed by Langerhans cells.

MjXMay.title: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscles
MjXMay.description: A pair of muscles that function as the only abductors of the vocal cords (open the glottis). Innervated by the recurrent laryngeal nerve. Paralysis of these muscles may lead to asphyxiation.

njX7ay.title: Cricothyroid muscle
njX7ay.description: A muscle that contracts (tenses) the vocal cords, which heightens pitch of voice. Unlike other laryngeal muscles, innervated by the superior laryngeal nerve.

LjXway.title: Nasopharyngeal cancer
LjXway.description: A cancer of the nasopharynx that can cause painless lymphadenopathy, obstruction of the Eustachian tube (which causes recurrent otitis media and conductive hearing loss), nasal discharge, nosebleeds, and/or impaired nasal breathing. Associated with Epstein-Barr virus infection.

ojX0Yy.title: Oropharyngeal cancer
ojX0Yy.description: A cancer of the oropharynx that can cause dysphagia, pain, obstructive sleep apnea or snoring, bleeding, and/or a neck mass. Often metastasizes early to nearby lymph nodes. Associated with human papillomavirus infection.

KjXUYy.title: Hypopharyngeal cancer
KjXUYy.description: A cancer of the hypopharynx that often remains asymptomatic for a long period before causing dysphagia, pain, weight loss, hemoptysis, dyspnea, and/or a neck mass. Often metastasizes early to nearby lymph nodes. Associated with human papillomavirus infection.

JjXsYy.title: Cryptomenorrhea
JjXsYy.description: A condition in which menstruation occurs but is not externally visible. Often caused by obstructed blood flow due to a congenital lower genital tract anomaly (e.g., transverse vaginal septum, imperforate hymen). Blood collects within the vaginal tract, which causes distension (hematocolpos) and cyclical pelvic pain.

destinations.label: Anomalies of the female genital tract → Anomalies of the vulva and vagina

qjXCYy.title: Alveolar macrophage
qjXCYy.description: A type of macrophage present in the alveoli, where they phagocytose foreign materials and initiate the immune response. Hemosiderin-laden alveolar macrophages are associated with pulmonary hemorrhage.

IjXYby.title: Hymenectomy
IjXYby.description: A surgical procedure to treat imperforate hymen. Involves incision of the hymen followed by evacuation of obstructed material.

destinations.label: Anomalies of the female genital tract → Anomalies of the vulva and vagina

rjXfby.title: Vaginal agenesis
rjXfby.description: A failure of the vagina to form. Most commonly occurs due to Müllerian agenesis. Examination shows normal external genitalia (as the lower 2/3 of vagina arises from the urogenital sinus), but the vagina will either be a dimple or a blind-ending pouch.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Ductal sex differentiation

HjXKby.title: Mesoderm
HjXKby.description: The middle layer of the 3 primary germ layers (endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm) formed during gastrulation on the 3rd week of embryonic development.
