Gives rise to muscle, bone, cartilage, connective tissue, serous membranes, adrenal cortex, vessels, spleen, dura mater, kidneys, and ureters.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

sjXtby.title: Opsonization
sjXtby.description: A process by which pathogens and immune complexes are marked with an opsonin (e.g., complement factor C3b) for phagocytosis, after which the pathogen can be eliminated by phagocytes that express opsonin receptors, e.g., Fc receptor and complement receptor 1.

GjXBby.title: Cidofovir
GjXBby.description: A nucleotide analog of cytosine that competitively inhibits viral DNA elongation by the viral DNA polymerase. Cidofovir does not require phosphorylation by viral kinase for activation. Primarily used for treating CMV retinitis in patients who are immunocompromised and acyclovir-resistant HSV. Adverse effects include nephrotoxicity.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against herpes viruses

tjXXXy.title: Hyperphosphatemia
tjXXXy.description: A serum phosphate concentration > 4.5 mg/dL. Etiologies include hypoparathyroidism and chronic kidney disease. High phosphate levels result in the formation of insoluble calcium phosphate, which can lead to nephrolithiasis, metastatic calcifications, and hypocalcemia.

media.title: Regulation of calcium and phosphate metabolism

FjXgXy.title: White pulp
FjXgXy.description: A collection of white blood cells (e.g., lymphocytes, macrophages, dendritic cells) and supporting parenchymal tissue in the spleen. Consists of periarteriolar lymphatic sheaths (PALs), follicles, and the marginal zones.

media.title: Red and white pulp of the spleen

EjX8Xy.title: Coelomic epithelium
EjX8Xy.description: An epithelial cell layer derived from mesoderm that lines the male and female gonads. Also contributed to the epithelium of the abdominal and peritoneal body cavities.

vjXAXy.title: Endometrium
vjXAXy.description: The innermost lining of the uterus. Composed of stroma (connective tissue) and simple columnar epithelium with glands.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Uterus and cervix

DjX1cy.title: Cervical transformation zone
DjX1cy.description: An area of transition from one type of epithelium to another. Associated with increased risk of metaplasia, dysplasia, and cancer. Examples include the area between the ectocervix and endocervix of the female reproductive tract and the gastroesophageal junction.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Uterus and cervix

wjXhcy.title: Fallopian tube
wjXhcy.description: A pair of structures between the fundus of uterus and ovaries. Suspended in the broad ligament and divided into the infundibulum (widest part near ovaries), ampulla (middle part, where fertilization typically occurs), isthmus (narrowest region), and intramural portion (opens into the uterine cavity). Lined with ciliated columnar epithelium.

9jXNcy.title: Fantasy (psychiatry)
9jXNcy.description: An immature defense mechanism in which an individual believes in fantastical or magical ideas in order to cope with a difficult or painful reality.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Defense mechanisms

xjXEcy.title: Mesentery
xjXEcy.description: A contiguous, double-layered fold of visceral peritoneum that contains intestinal vessels, lymphatics, and nerves, and anchors the bowel to the posterior abdominal wall.

BjXzcy.title: Labial adhesions
BjXzcy.description: A condition of partial or complete adhesion of the labia minora that typically affects young girls up to 4 years of age. These adhesions form as a result of superficial labial injuries caused by perineal inflammation (e.g., urinary tract infection, diaper dermatitis, diarrhea). Usually asymptomatic but can cause recurrent urinary tract infections if the external urethral opening is obstructed.

yjXd1y.title: Quadriceps femoris muscle
yjXd1y.description: The main extensor muscle of the knee, composed of 4 separate heads: the rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, and vastus intermedius. Inserts at the tibial tuberosity. Supplied by the femoral artery and innervated by the femoral nerve.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

media.title: Muscles of the anterior compartment of the thigh

AjXR1y.title: Patellar ligament
AjXR1y.description: A distal extension of the common quadriceps tendon (of the quadriceps muscle) that connects the patella to the tibial tuberosity and facilitates full extension of the knee.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The knee joint

media.title: Ligaments and retinacula of the patella

nPX72y.title: Zebra body
nPX72y.description: A characteristic appearence of abnormal lysosomes on electron microscopy caused by configuration of myelinoid membranes into parallel palisading lamellae within the lysosomal cytoplasm. Can be seen in a number of lysosomal storage disorders, including Niemann-Pick disease, Fabry disease, and Hurler syndrome.

LPXw2y.title: Protein kinase C
LPXw2y.description: A serine/threonine kinase that plays a role in intracellular signal transduction. Activated by diacylglycerol and IP3-mediated calcium release.

oPX0fy.title: Gaucher cell
oPX0fy.description: Lipid-rich macrophages that resemble crumpled tissue paper. Seen on light microscopy in patients with Gaucher disease.

6PXjfy.title: Protein kinase G
6PXjfy.description: A serine/threonine kinase that plays a role in intracellular signal transduction. Activated by cGMP.

pPXLfy.title: PPAR-α
pPXLfy.description: A nuclear receptor that is primarily expressed in hepatocytes and activated during fasting states. Activation of PPAR-α increases lipoprotein lipase production, fatty acid uptake and oxidation, and HDL synthesis. Drugs that increase PPAR-alpha activity (fibrates) are used to treat dyslipidemia.

JPXsfy.title: Lipoprotein lipase
JPXsfy.description: A membrane protein found on the surface of capillary endothelial cells. It hydrolyzes triglycerides into free fatty acids and glycerol molecules, using ApoC-II as a cofactor.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

qPXCfy.title: Inward rectifier potassium channels
qPXCfy.description: A voltage-gated potassium channel that is closed during depolarization of myocytes (phase 0–2 of the cardiac action potential), and opens during repolarization, reducing the net outward flow of potassium and thereby slowing repolarization and prolonging the cardiac action potential.

IPXYTy.title: L-type calcium channel
IPXYTy.description: A long-acting, high-voltage channel found in cardiac myocytes and skeletal and smooth muscle cells. Responsible for the coupling of excitation (depolarization) and contraction. Activation via depolarization triggers calcium influx into the cells, which in turn stimulates the release of calcium from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.

rPXfTy.title: Triglyceride
rPXfTy.description: A lipid composed of one glycerol linked to three fatty acids. Mainly stored in adipocytes and serves as an energy reserve.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

7PX4Ty.title: Sphingomyelinase
7PX4Ty.description: A lysosomal enzyme responsible for the degradation of sphingomyelin. Deficiency of this enzyme, which causes Niemann-Pick disease, leads to accumulation of sphingomyelin in the liver, spleen, bone marrow, and brain.

sPXtTy.title: Arylsulfatase A
sPXtTy.description: A lysosomal enzyme responsible for the degradation of sphingolipid (e.g., cerebroside sulfate). Deficiency of this enzyme, which causes metachromatic leukodystrophy, leads to accumulation of sphingolipid (cerebroside sulfate) in neural and non-neural tissue.

GPXBTy.title: Galactocerebrosidase
GPXBTy.description: A lysosomal enzyme responsible for the degradation of galactocerebroside. Deficiency of this enzyme causes Krabbe disease and leads to accumulation of toxic myelin degradation products (e.g., psychosine).

tPXXgy.title: Globoid cell
tPXXgy.description: A giant, multinucleated tissue macrophage that contains toxic myelin breakdown products. Found clustered in the brain tissue in patients with Krabbe disease (also called globoid cell leukodystrophy).

FPXggy.title: Glycine
FPXggy.description: A non-essential amino acid that is a precursor for porphyrins in the heme synthesis pathway and is involved in purine biosynthesis. It also functions as an inhibitory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system, especially in the spinal cord, brainstem, and retina.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

8PXOgy.title: Neuromuscular junction
8PXOgy.description: The chemical synapsis between a motor neuron and a muscle fiber. A neurotransmitter (e.g., acetylcholine) is released from the neuron into the synaptic cleft, where it binds to acetylcholine receptors at the motor endplate and triggers muscular contraction.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

uPXpgy.title: Tetrodotoxin
uPXpgy.description: A potentially-deadly neurotoxin present in pufferfish that blocks voltage-gated sodium channels, which inhibits action potential propagation. This causes muscle weakness, paralysis, hypotension, and paresthesias.

vPXAgy.title: Anti-β2-glycoprotein antibodies
vPXAgy.description: A group of antibodies directed against the cardiolipin ­binding factor β2­ glycoprotein I. Their presence is associated with prothrombotic effects, possibly due to the activation of platelets and endothelial and immune cells. May be associated with antiphospholipid syndrome.

DPX1Sy.title: Cardiac remodeling
DPX1Sy.description: A change in the size, structure, and/or function of cardiac muscles in response to pressure/volume overload, cardiac injury, and/or irregular electrical activation.

CPXqSy.title: Areola
CPXqSy.description: The hyperpigmented circular region on the breast that surrounds the nipple and contains the openings of sebaceous glands (Montgomery tubercles).

xPXESy.title: Montgomery tubercles
xPXESy.description: A collection of sebaceous glands of the areola, located circumferentially around the nipple. Secrete a lubricating fluid and protects the nipple-areola complex.

BPXzSy.title: Mammary papilla
BPXzSy.description: The central portion of the breast where the lactiferous (milk) ducts of the mammary glands join and open onto the skin.

Y4Xn3y.title: Mammary ridges
Y4Xn3y.description: The cutaneous crests from which multiple glandular buds originate. Located on both sides of the trunk and course from the axilla to the groin.

X4X93y.title: Hypoplastic thumb
X4X93y.description: A congenital anomaly caused by incomplete development of the thumb. The radius is typically small or absent. Associated with VACTERL anomalies and Fanconi anemia.

c4XaRy.title: Cytochrome complex IV
c4XaRy.description: A mitochondrial enzyme in the electron transport chain. Inhibited by cyanide, azide, and carbon monoxide.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Electron transport chain and ATP synthesis

media.title: Mechanism of action: respiratory chain inhibitors

14X2Ry.title: Rhodanese
14X2Ry.description: A mitochondrial enzyme that converts cyanide to thiocyanate, which is then excreted by the kidneys.

W4XPRy.title: Thiocyanate
W4XPRy.description: A compound formed from cyanide and sulfur donors by the mitochondrial enzyme rhodanese.

d4XoRy.title: Cyanomethemoglobin
d4XoRy.description: A compound formed by binding of cyanide and methemoglobin. Its presence reduces the amount of free cyanide availability to bind to cytochrome complex IV in cases of cyanide poisoning.

V4XGRy.title: Oxidative phosphorylation
V4XGRy.description: A metabolic process used to form ATP from the transfer of electrons by a series of electron carriers. Carried out inside the mitochondria of most eukaryotes.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Electron transport chain and ATP synthesis

e4XxRy.title: Truncation
e4XxRy.description: Shortening of a protein as a result of a gene defect, premature termination of protein elongation, or deletion of amino acid residues at the N-terminus and C-terminus by proteolysis. A truncated protein is usually non-functional.

U4Xbiy.title: Relaxin
U4Xbiy.description: A vasodilating hormone secreted by the corpus luteum, and later, by the placental and decidual membranes. Increases endothelial nitric oxide secretion, which causes vasodilation and decreases vascular resistance and mean arterial pressure, which increases the glomerular filtration rate during pregnancy.

24XTiy.title: Hypoplasia
24XTiy.description: A decrease in the amount of organic tissue due to a decrease in cell number.

f4Xkiy.title: Bulbous urethra
f4Xkiy.description: A part of the anterior urethra in males that lies proximal to the penoscrotal junction. Is covered by the corpus spongiosum but not by the corpora cavernosa. Bulbourethral glands open into it. Lies in close proximity to the pubic symphysis and is the most commonly injured structure in men with straddle injuries or direct blows to the perineum.

T4X6iy.title: Straddle injury
T4X6iy.description: An injury to the perineum caused by falling astride an object (e.g., a bicycle bar, bathtub/trampoline edge). Can damage soft tissue structures, especially the bulbar urethra in males, which are crushed between the object and the pubic symphysis.

g4XFiy.title: Pendulous urethra
g4XFiy.description: The longest and most distal part of the anterior urethra in males. Extends from the penoscrotal junction to the urethral meatus. Is encased by the corpus cavernosum and the corpora spongiosum.

S4Xyiy.title: Membranous urethra
S4Xyiy.description: The distal portion of the posterior urethra in males that lies within the urogenital diaphragm (external urethral sphincter). Lies between the prostatic urethra and the bulbous urethra and is the shortest and the least dilatable part of the male urethra.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Urethra

h4XcQy.title: Posterior urethra
h4XcQy.description: The proximal portion of the male urethra that extends from the neck of the bladder to the distal part of the urogenital diaphragm. Consists of the prostatic urethra proximally and the membranous urethra distally.

34XSQy.title: Anterior urethra
34XSQy.description: A portion of male urethra that lies within the corpus spongiosum. Consists of the bulbous and pendulous parts of the urethra.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Urethra

R4XlQy.title: Prostatic urethra
R4XlQy.description: A portion of the posterior urethra that traverses through the prostate gland. Extends from the bladder neck to the beginning of the membranous urethra. Is the widest and most dilatable portion of the urethra. A bulge in the posterior wall is called the verumontanum. The prostatic and ejaculatory ducts open into the prostatic urethra.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Urethra

i4XJQy.title: Hypesthesia
i4XJQy.description: A diminished ability to perceive sensation (e.g., pain, temperature, touch, vibration).

P4XWjy.title: Pyknosis
P4XWjy.description: An irreversible condensation of chromatin that results in a shrunken, deeply basophilic nucleus. Seen in cells undergoing necrosis or apoptosis.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cell injury

44X3jy.title: Karyorrhexis
44X3jy.description: A process of fragmentation of the nucleus into numerous, deeply basophilic particles. Seen in cells undergoing necrosis or apoptosis.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cell injury

k4Xmjy.title: Spiral arteries
k4Xmjy.description: A collection of small arteries that supply blood to the endometrium of the uterus. Develop during the proliferative and secretory phases of the uterine cycle (days 5-28 of the menstrual cycle).

O4XIjy.title: Functional layer of the endometrium
O4XIjy.description: The innermost layer of the uterus in which implantation can occur. Develops during the proliferative and secretory phases of the uterine cycle (days 5-28 of the menstrual cycle) before being sloughed off during menstruation (days 1-4 of the menstrual cycle).

l4Xvjy.title: Hemosiderin
l4Xvjy.description: An iron storage complex produced during the breakdown of ferritin and the breakdown of phagocytosed hemoglobin (e.g., after red blood cell destruction). May be found in various tissues (e.g., alveolar macrophages, liver parenchyma) or the urine depending on the underlying pathology (e.g., pulmonary hemorrhage, hemochromatosis, intravascular hemolysis).

N4X-jy.title: Protein kinase R
N4X-jy.description: A serine/threonine protein kinase that phosphorylates eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 subunit 1 and consequently inhibits protein synthesis.

m4XVPy.title: Sorbitol
m4XVPy.description: A sugar alcohol formed by the reduction of glucose by aldose reductase and converted to fructose by sorbitol dehydrogenase. Can accumulate in tissues that lack sorbitol dehydrogenase (lens, retina, kidney, Schwann cells), which results in osmotic damage.

54XiPy.title: Sorbitol dehydrogenase
54XiPy.description: An enzyme that converts sorbitol into fructose, which prevents the accumulation of sorbitol. Not found in the retina, kidney, or Schwann cells.

M4XMPy.title: Kallikrein
M4XMPy.description: A group of serine protease enzymes. Responsible for several physiological functions, including regulation of blood pressure through activation of bradykinin.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

media.title: Interaction between the kallikrein and secondary hemostasis pathways

n4X7Py.title: Ecallantide
n4X7Py.description: A kallikrein inhibitor that decreases activation of bradykinin. Used to treat acute hereditary angioedema attacks.

L4XwPy.title: Popliteal lymph node
L4XwPy.description: A cluster of lymph nodes located in the popliteal fossa that collect lymph from superficial lymphatic vessels of the skin over the dorsolateral aspect of the foot and the posterior calf, as well as from the deep lymphatic vessels running along the anterior and posterior tibial vessels.

p4XL4y.title: MUTYH gene
p4XL4y.description: A gene that encodes for the DNA glycosylase MUTYH glycosylase, which is involved in base excision repair. MUTYH glycosylase repairs oxidative DNA damage by excising inappropriately paired guanine bases from the DNA backbone. Inactivation of this gene results in MYH-associated polyposis.

J4Xs4y.title: Autosomal-recessive polyposis syndrome
J4Xs4y.description: An autosomal recessive adenomatous polyposis syndrome that is caused by a mutation in the MUTYH gene. Similar to other forms of adenomatous polyposis syndromes (e.g., FAP), it is associated with colonic polyposis and an increased risk of colorectal cancer. However, it can manifest at a later age and it is associated with a slightly lower risk of colorectal cancer compared to FAP.

q4XC4y.title: BLM gene
q4XC4y.description: A gene that encodes for DNA helicases. BLM gene mutations result in impaired DNA repair, UV sensitivity, and an increased risk of developing cancer (Bloom syndrome).

I4XYky.title: Reassortment (viral)
I4XYky.description: A process by which segmented genomic strands from different viral strains that have coinfected the same cell are sorted into progeny. Can cause antigenic shift.

r4Xfky.title: Complementation (viral)
r4Xfky.description: A phenomenon in which one virus that has infected a cell produces nonfunctional protein and a second virus that has coinfected the cell makes functional protein that serves both viruses.

74X4ky.title: Ribonuclease L
74X4ky.description: An enzyme that degrades cellular and viral mRNA and thus halts protein synthesis. Activated by type I interferons.

destinations.label: Cytokines and eicosanoids → Interferons and tumor necrosis factor family

H4XKky.title: Venturi effect
H4XKky.description: A reduction in fluid pressure that occurs when a fluid flows through a constricted section of a vessel. Accompanied by an increase in fluid velocity.

s4Xtky.title: Strawberry cervix
s4Xtky.description: A finding on pelvic examination of an erythematous cervical mucosa with papilliform and punctate hemorrhages, which resembles the surface of a strawberry. Associated with trichomoniasis.

G4XBky.title: Juxtaglomerular cell tumor
G4XBky.description: A rare malignancy of juxtaglomerular cells in the kidney that causes excess production of renin, which results in severe hypertension and headaches. Serum studies show hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis due to excess aldosterone.

t4XXOy.title: Vitamin K epoxide reductase
t4XXOy.description: An enzyme that is required to reduce and activate vitamin K, which is essential for γ‐glutamyl carboxylation of glutamic acid residues of procoagulant factors II, VII, IX, X and anticoagulant proteins C and S.

84XOOy.title: Dark-field microscopy
84XOOy.description: A microscopy technique that illuminates specimens against a dark background. Can be used to visualize spirochetes such as Treponema pallidum.

u4XpOy.title: Factor VII
u4XpOy.description: A vitamin K dependent clotting factor produced by the liver. Functions as a serine protease in conjunction with tissue factor and initiates the extrinsic pathway coagulation cascade. Of the procoagulant factors, it has the shortest half-life (approximately 6-8 hours).

E4X8Oy.title: T-type calcium channel
E4X8Oy.description: A voltage-gated calcium channel that is opened by low-voltage depolarization potentials and allows calcium influx. This channel is located on the surface of cardiac pacemaker cells, vascular smooth muscle cells, and thalamic neurons. T-type calcium channels of cardiac packermaker cells open in the middle of phase 4 (slow depolarization phase) and close at the start of phase 0 (rapid depolarization phase).

D4X1ly.title: Mass spectrometry
D4X1ly.description: Extremely sensitive and specific analytical tool for the detection and characterization of various biomolecules such as nucleic acids, proteins, and carbohydrates. Mass spectrometry relies on ionization, which is the process of transforming neutral chemical species (atoms or molecules) into ions. The sorting of ions by mass-to-charge ratio is used to determine the isotopic nature of the sample, the mass of the molecules, and their chemical structures.

w4Xhly.title: Recombination (viral)
w4Xhly.description: A process of genomic exchange between two homologous strands of DNA from similar or related viral strains that have coinfected a host cell. Increases genetic diversity in viral progeny.

94XNly.title: Bacterial transformation
94XNly.description: A process by which some bacteria and yeast take up exogenous genetic material and incorporate it into their genome.

C4Xqly.title: Granulysin
C4Xqly.description: A cytolytic protein that is produced and released by cytotoxic T cells. Mediates keratinocyte damage in patients with Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.

x4XEly.title: Carotid sinus
x4XEly.description: A vascular dilatation located at the base of the internal carotid artery, just after the common carotid artery bifurcates. Functions as a baroreceptor that helps maintain blood pressure homeostasis. Innervated by a branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve that is stimulated when the carotid sinus is stretched (e.g., by high blood pressure). The neural pathways result in decreased heart rate and vascular dilation that lower the blood pressure.

B4Xzly.title: Carotid sinus massage
B4Xzly.description: A vagal maneuver used to stimulate the carotid sinus. With the patient supine with chin extended, apply pressure to one carotid sinus (located between the angle of the mandible and the upper border of the thyroid cartilage) for 5–10 seconds. Results in ↓ heart rate, ↓ AV nodal conduction, and ↓ blood pressure due to vasodilation. Used to terminate paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardias (due to AVN re-entry) and to diagnose carotid sinus syndrome.

y4XdNy.title: Baroreceptor reflex
y4XdNy.description: A reflex that regulates blood pressure homeostasis. Stretch receptors (baroreceptors) in the carotid sinus, aortic arch, atria, and vena cavae sense changes in blood pressure and send afferent signals to the vasomotor center of the medulla (solitary nucleus). The solitary nucleus then sends efferent signals to modulate sympathetic and parasympathetic tone and maintain blood pressure homeostasis.

A4XRNy.title: CD40
A4XRNy.description: A surface membrane receptor on B cells that binds to CD40L on the surface of CD4+ T helper cells. CD40-CD40L serves as the second signal for B cell activation and induces Ig class switching.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

_4X5Ny.title: B cell activation
_4X5Ny.description: A process by which a naive mature B cell is activated and becomes capable of producing immunoglobulins other than IgM. Antigen-presenting MHC II of B cells binds to the T cell receptor (TCR) of CD4+ T helper cells (Th cell). Second signaling of B cell CD40 to CD40L on the Th cell triggers immunoglobulin class switching.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

z4XrNy.title: CD28
z4XrNy.description: A surface protein on naive T cells that binds B7 receptors on antigen presenting cells. Serves as a second signal for the activation, maturation, and proliferation of T cells.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

-4XDNy.title: B7 protein
-4XDNy.description: A surface receptor on antigen presenting cells that binds to CD28 on naive T cells. This interaction serves as the 2nd signaling for T cell activation, maturation, and proliferation.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

ZkXZmy.title: Aortitis
ZkXZmy.description: A condition of aortic wall inflammation. Etiologies include autoimmune disease (e.g., vasculitis, rheumatoid arthritis) and infection. Can lead to aneurysm formation.

akXQmy.title: Parietal pleura
akXQmy.description: A serous membrane that lines the thoracic wall (costal part), the thoracic part of the diaphragm (diaphragmatic part), and the mediastinum (mediastinal part). The inferior line of attachment is diagonal and extends to the 8th rib anteriorly, 10th rib laterally, and 12th rib posteriorly. Superiorly, it extends above the first rib and into the supraclavicular fossa. Sensitive to pain.

YkXnmy.title: Visceral pleura
YkXnmy.description: A serous membrane that closely invests the surface of the lungs. The inferior attachments are the same as the lower border of the lung: 6th rib anteriorly, the 8th rib laterally, and 10th rib posteriorly. Insensitive to pain.

bkXHmy.title: Pleural cavity
bkXHmy.description: A potential space between the visceral pleura and the parietal pleura. Contains a small quantity of pleural fluid that minimizes friction during the respiratory movements of the lungs. The pressure within the pleural cavity changes during respiration (negative during inspiration; positive during expiration), which aids in alveolar expansion and collapse.

XkX9my.title: Solifenacin
XkX9my.description: A competitive antagonist of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors that functions as an antispasmodic agent for the bladder. Used to treat overactive bladder, including urgency urinary incontinence.

destinations.label: Overactive bladder and urgency urinary incontinence → Treatment

ckXa5y.title: Dicyclomine
ckXa5y.description: A competitive antagonist of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors that functions as an anti-spasmodic agent for the bladder. Used to treat urge incontinence (overactive bladder).

1kX25y.title: Bundle of His
1kX25y.description: A part of the electrical conducting system of the heart that rapidly conducts electrical impulses from the proximal atrioventricular node to the ventricles. Consists of specialized fast-conducting myocytes surrounded by an insulating layer of connective tissue. Divides into the right and left bundle branches.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Conduction system of the heart

WkXP5y.title: Sinoatrial node
WkXP5y.description: The pacemaker of the heart. Located in the right atrium adjacent to the opening of the superior vena cava. Composed of specialized pacemaker cells that spontaneously generate action potentials, which are converted to electrical impulses that are conducted to the myocardium through a specialized pathway, which results in myocardial contraction. Generates impulses at the rate of ~ 60–100/min in adults.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Conduction system of the heart

dkXo5y.title: Purkinje fibers
dkXo5y.description: The most distal pathway of the electrical conducting system of the heart. Composed of specialized Purkinje cells that conduct electrical impulses from the proximal bundle branches to the ventricular myocytes, which results in ventricular contraction.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Conduction system of the heart

VkXG5y.title: Bachmann bundle
VkXG5y.description: A specialized bundle of myocytes that connects the right and left atria. Conducts electrical impulses from the sinoatrial node located in the right atrium to the left atrium and ensures nearly synchronized atrial contraction.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Conduction system of the heart

ekXx5y.title: Bundle branches
ekXx5y.description: A part of the electrical conducting system of the heart that transmits electrical impulses from the Bundle of His proximally to the right and left ventricles, which results in ventricular contraction.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Conduction system of the heart

UkXbMy.title: Dasatinib
UkXbMy.description: A biologic anti-neoplastic agent used in the treatment of Philadelphia chromosome (t(9:22) translocation) positive neoplasms, chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML), and acute lymphocytic leukemia (ALL). It functions by competitively inhibiting the tyrosine kinase that results from the abnormal BCR-ABL gene.

2kXTMy.title: Nilotinib
2kXTMy.description: A biologic anti-neoplastic agent used in the treatment of Philadelphia chromosome (t(9:22) translocation) positive neoplasms and chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML). Functions by competitively inhibiting the tyrosine kinase that results from the abnormal BCR-ABL gene. Approved for imatinib-resistant CML.

fkXkMy.title: Basilar membrane
fkXkMy.description: A structure contained within the cochlea of the inner ear that vibrates in response to sound waves.

media.title: Mechanoelectrical transduction of sound waves by hair cells

TkX6My.title: Cochlea
TkX6My.description: A spiral-shaped, fluid-filled structure of the inner ear that is involved in hearing. Contains the organ of Corti.

gkXFMy.title: Helicotrema
gkXFMy.description: A part of the cochlea near the apex of the basilar membrane, which responds to low frequency sounds.

SkXyMy.title: Tonotopy
SkXyMy.description: The spatial relationships between sounds of different frequencies and different locations on the basilar membrane. The apex (near the helicotrema) responds to low frequencies; the base of the cochlea responds to high frequencies.

hkXcny.title: Hyperventilation
hkXcny.description: A respiratory minute volume that exceeds metabolic needs and causes a respiratory alkalosis due to excess elimination of carbon dioxide.

3kXSny.title: Iliac artery
3kXSny.description: The right and left common iliac arteries originate at the aortic bifurcation (usually at the level of L4). Each common iliac artery in turn bifurcates at the sacroiliac joint to form an internal and an external iliac artery.

RkXlny.title: Sodium/glucose cotransporter 2
RkXlny.description: The major cotransporter involved in glucose reabsorption in the proximal convoluted tubules of the kidney.

ikXJny.title: p21
ikXJny.description: A phosphoprotein that prevents cell cycle progression by inhibiting cyclin/cyclin-dependent kinase complexes. Activated by the tumor suppressor protein p53.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

QkXuny.title: Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1B
QkXuny.description: A phosphoprotein that prevents cell cycle progression by inhibiting cyclin/cyclin-dependent kinase complexes.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

jkX_ny.title: E2F
jkX_ny.description: A family of transcription factors that are involved in the regulation of the cell cycle. Play an important role in regulating the G1 to S phase transition. Normally inhibited by retinoblastoma protein.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

PkXWLy.title: E7 protein
PkXWLy.description: An early (E) gene product induced by oncogenic strains of human papillomavirus. Inactivates tumor suppressors Rb, p21, and p27.

4kX3Ly.title: E6 protein
4kX3Ly.description: An early (E) gene product induced by oncogenic strains of human papillomavirus. Stimulates degradation of the tumor suppressor protein p53.

kkXmLy.title: Branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve to the carotid sinus
kkXmLy.description: A nerve that innervates the carotid sinus and is responsible for the bradycardic and hypotensive responses that occur as a result of carotid sinus stretch.

lkXvLy.title: Reverse triiodothyronine
lkXvLy.description: A tyrosine-based inactive thyroid hormone that contains iodine. Made in the bloodstream by deiodination of thyroxine (T4).

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Function

NkX-Ly.title: Cannabis withdrawal
NkX-Ly.description: A withdrawal syndrome that causes irritability, anxiety, depression, insomnia, restlessness, and/or decreased appetite.

mkXVoy.title: Barbiturate dependence
mkXVoy.description: The physical adaptation to prolonged barbiturate use, which is characterized by the development of tolerance (diminished response) and withdrawal symptoms with decreased drug intake. Dependence may develop even if medication is taken as prescribed.

5kXioy.title: GHB withdrawal
5kXioy.description: A withdrawal syndrome that causes CNS stimulation (e.g., irritability, insomnia, hallucinations, delirium), autonomic instability (e.g., tachycardia, hypertension), gastrointestinal complaints (e.g., diarrhea, abdominal pain), tremors, and increased muscle tone.

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Gamma-hydroxybutyric acid use

MkXMoy.title: Amphetamine withdrawal
MkXMoy.description: A withdrawal syndrome that causes dysphoria, anhedonia, fatigue, insomnia or hypersomnia, agitation, anxiety, appetite changes, and depressed mood.

nkX7oy.title: Cocaine withdrawal
nkX7oy.description: A withdrawal syndrome that causes depression, anxiety, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, anhedonia, appetite changes, and hypersomnia.

LkXwoy.title: Juxtaglomerular cell
LkXwoy.description: A specialized smooth muscle cell located at the juxtaglomerular apparatus of the kidney. Releases renin in response to decreased blood pressure, low serum sodium concentration, and beta-1 adrenergic stimulation.

okX0Ky.title: Cleft lip
okX0Ky.description: A facial abnormality caused by a failure of fusion of the maxillary prominence with the medial nasal prominence. Can be unilateral or bilateral and complete or incomplete.

destinations.label: Cleft lip and cleft palate → Summary

KkXUKy.title: Cleft palate
KkXUKy.description: A facial abnormality caused by a failure of fusion of the palatine prominences. Can be unilateral or bilateral and complete or incomplete. In addition to the facial deformity, infants often have feeding, hearing, speech difficulties and defects in dentition.

destinations.label: Cleft lip and cleft palate → Summary

media.title: Development of the face and palate

pkXLKy.title: Shared decision-making
pkXLKy.description: A process in which the patient and clinician work together to make a health care decision that strikes a balance between the patient's preferences and values, evidence-based information on the risks and expected outcomes, and the clinician's experience.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

JkXsKy.title: Round window
JkXsKy.description: A membrane-covered opening in the middle ear that lies below the stapes-covered oval window. Vibrations of the footplate of the stapes are transmitted to the round window through the perilymph, which causes it to vibrate in the opposite phase of the oval window. Injury to the round window (e.g., violent nose blowing, barotrauma while diving) causes sensorineural hearing loss.

qkXCKy.title: Perilymph
qkXCKy.description: The fluid contained within the bony cochlea that transmits sound vibrations from the stapes-covered oval window to the round window.

rkXf6y.title: Oval window
rkXf6y.description: An opening located in the middle ear at the base of the cochlea through which sound waves are transmitted to the inner ear. Covered by the foot plate of the stapes.

7kX46y.title: Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissues
7kX46y.description: A collection of secondary lymphatic organs that are scattered along the mucosal linings of various tissues, including the gastrointestinal tract, nasopharynx, eye, and skin. Examples include the Peyer patches and the tonsils.

HkXK6y.title: IgA anti-epidermal transglutaminase antibodies
HkXK6y.description: Autoantibodies against epidermal transglutaminase, a key autoantigen in dermatitis herpetiformis.

skXt6y.title: Uterine cornua
skXt6y.description: The points where the fallopian tubes enter the uterine cavity. Serves as an attachment for the round ligament of uterus.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Uterus and cervix

GkXB6y.title: Sertoli cells
GkXB6y.description: Somatic cells of the testis that play several structural and functional roles in the male reproductive system. They secrete inhibin B (inhibitor of FSH), and androgen-binding protein to maintain local levels of testosterone. Tight junctions between Sertoli cells form the blood-testis barrier, which serves to keep gametes separate from the circulation and protect them from autoimmune attacks.

tkXXpy.title: Seminiferous tubules
tkXXpy.description: The part of the testis responsible for spermatogenesis. Lined by columnar cells (Sertoli cells).

FkXgpy.title: Dynein
FkXgpy.description: A class of motor proteins that convert cellular energy to mechanical energy. They allow for migration, propagation, and movement of cells/organelles usually along the microtubules.

8kXOpy.title: Chlorine-based solutions
8kXOpy.description: A sterilization compound used as a bactericidal and sporicidal agent that is commonly referred to as bleach. This solution oxidizes and modifies protein structures of pathogens by inactivating sulfhydryl groups.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

ukXppy.title: Isopropanol-based solution
ukXppy.description: A type of sanitizing agent commonly used to disinfect surfaces and skin (antiseptic). It exerts a bactericidal effect by disrupting bacterial membranes and proteins but is not sporicidal.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

vkXApy.title: Iodine-based solution
vkXApy.description: A bactericidal agent with limited sporicidal activity that causes halogenation and denaturation of bacterial proteins and RNA/DNA.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

DkX1Jy.title: Bacteriostatic
DkX1Jy.description: A substance that stops bacteria from reproducing (does not directly kill bacteria). Includes some disinfectants, antiseptics, and antibiotics.

wkXhJy.title: Sensitivity
wkXhJy.description: The proportion of people with a condition who test positive. A test with high sensitivity (i.e., few false negatives) can be used for screening purposes. The formula for calculating sensitivity is: True Positives/(True Positives + False Negatives).

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

CkXqJy.title: Bactericidal
CkXqJy.description: A substance that directly kills bacteria. Includes some disinfectants, antiseptics, and antibiotics.

xkXEJy.title: Uterosacral ligaments
xkXEJy.description: A collection of avascular fibrous bands that connect the cervix to the sacrum, which provides mechanical support to the uterus.

media.title: Supporting ligaments of the uterus (dorsal view)

BkXzJy.title: Suspensory ligament of the ovary
BkXzJy.description: A ligament that attaches the ovary to the lateral pelvic wall. Contains the ovarian artery, vein, nerves, and lymphatic vessels.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Ligaments of the female pelvis

media.title: Supporting ligaments of the uterus (dorsal view)

ykXdqy.title: Ovarian ligament
ykXdqy.description: A ligament that connects the medial pole of the ovaries to the uterine cornua. Contains the ovarian branch of the uterine artery.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Ligaments of the female pelvis

media.title: Supporting ligaments of the uterus (dorsal view)

AkXRqy.title: Uterine artery
AkXRqy.description: A branch of the internal iliac artery. Serves as the major blood supply to the uterus and the upper part of the vagina. Travels in the cardinal ligament and anastomoses with the ovarian artery.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis
Female reproductive organs → Uterus and cervix

media.title: Blood supply of the female reproductive organs (dorsal view)
Supporting ligaments of the uterus (dorsal view)

-kXDqy.title: Vertebral arch
-kXDqy.description: The posterior part of a vertebra, consisting of two pedicles and two laminae, four articular processes, two transverse processes, and a single spinous process. Together with the vertebral body anteriorly, it encloses the vertebral foramen.

ZOXZIy.title: Vertebral body
ZOXZIy.description: The cylindrical, anterior part of the vertebra. Articulates with the vertebral bodies above and below via the intervertebral disc.

0OXeIy.title: Vertebral canal
0OXeIy.description: The space between the bodies and arches of adjacent vertebrae that extend from the foramen magnum to the sacral hiatus. Contains the spinal cord, nerve roots, meninges, and blood vessels.

bOXHIy.title: Broad ligament of the uterus
bOXHIy.description: A fold of peritoneum that serves as a mesentery and connects the uterus to the walls and floor of the pelvis. Contains the fallopian tubes, ovaries, ovarian and uterine vessels, and the uterine ligaments (e.g., suspensory ligament of the ovary).

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Ligaments of the female pelvis

media.title: Supporting ligaments of the uterus (dorsal view)

cOXary.title: Intervertebral foramina
cOXary.description: The lateral spaces between the pedicles of two adjacent vertebrae, through which spinal nerves and their vessels emerge.

WOXPry.title: Transverse processes
WOXPry.description: A series of bony projections on either side of the vertebral arch in the spinal column. They provide attachment points for muscles and ligaments of the spine and act as levers for muscular action, aiding in the movement and stability of the spine.

dOXory.title: Anterior longitudinal ligament
dOXory.description: A ligament that attaches to the anterior portion of the vertebral column and runs continuously from the occiput to the sacrum.

eOXxry.title: Nuchal ligament
eOXxry.description: A sheet of fibrous tissue that connects the external occipital protuberance and the tips of the spinous processes of C1 to C7 vertebrae. The upper and middle fibers of the trapezius muscle and the splenius capitis muscle originate from this ligament.

fOXk7y.title: Conduction pathway of the heart
fOXk7y.description: The sinoatrial node is the fastest spontaneous depolarizer and thus serves as the pacemaker of the heart. Conduction travels from the sinoatrial node → atrioventricular node → bundle of His → right and left bundle branches → Purkinje fibers → ventricles.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Conduction system of the heart

TOX67y.title: N-acetyl-p-benzoquinoneimine
TOX67y.description: A toxic breakdown product of acetaminophen that causes liver cell necrosis by binding to hepatic proteins. At therapeutic doses of acetaminophen, only small amounts of NAPQI are produced and rapidly inactivated by glutathione. In cases of acetaminophen overdose, increased formation of NAPQI depletes glutathione reserves and results in liver failure.

hOXcHy.title: Cystic duct
hOXcHy.description: A component of the biliary duct system that connects the gallbladder with the common hepatic duct to form the common bile duct. Bile stored in the gallbladder flows through the cystic duct to the common bile duct. Cystic duct obstruction (e.g., due to a gallstone) can cause acute cholecystitis.

3OXSHy.title: Common hepatic duct
3OXSHy.description: A part of the biliary duct system that is formed by the union of the right and left hepatic duct. Joins the cystic duct coming from the gallbladder to form the common bile duct.

ROXlHy.title: Cystic artery
ROXlHy.description: An artery that typically arises from the right hepatic artery (branch of the proper hepatic artery) and supplies the gallbladder, cystic duct, common hepatic duct, and proximal common bile duct. Forms a part of the Calot triangle, along with the cystic duct and the common hepatic duct.

QOXuHy.title: Bile acids
QOXuHy.description: A group of steroid end-products of cholesterol metabolism. Primary bile acids (cholic acid and chenodeoxycholic acid) are produced in the liver and secreted in bile into the intestine. Gut flora dehydroxylate primary bile acids into secondary bile acids (lithocholic acid, deoxycholic acid, and ursodeoxycholic acid), which are required for the absorption of fats and fat-soluble vitamins.

jOX_Hy.title: Cholic acid
jOX_Hy.description: A primary bile acid that is used to treat bile acid synthesis disorders and peroxisomal disorders (e.g., Zellweger spectrum disorders). Administered orally. Adverse effects include diarrhea, reflux esophagitis, and malaise.

4OX3sy.title: Pigment gallstones
4OX3sy.description: A type of gallstone composed primarily of calcium bilirubinate (unconjugated bilirubin and calcium). Second most common type of gallstone after cholesterol stones. Brown pigment stones are radiolucent and are mainly caused by biliary tract infection. Black pigment stones are radiopaque and are mainly caused by hemolysis.

media.title: Pathophysiology for different types of gallstones

kOXmsy.title: Cholesterol gallstones
kOXmsy.description: A type of gallstone that consists predominantly of cholesterol. Typically radiolucent but can have some calcification from calcium carbonate. Associated with obesity, pregnancy, Crohn disease, and diabetes mellitus.

media.title: Pathophysiology for different types of gallstones

lOXvsy.title: Glucuronidation
lOXvsy.description: The conjugation of a substance with glucuronic acid, which produces a glucuronide. Glucuronidation is the most common coupling reaction in phase II of the hepatic biotransformation reactions and converts substances (e.g., drugs) into hydrophilic metabolites that can be excreted by the kidneys or in bile.

NOX-sy.title: Uroporphyrins
NOX-sy.description: A group of heterocyclic compounds that accumulate in patients with porphyria cutanea tarda. Urinary excretion causes the classical finding of tea-colored urine.

mOXVGy.title: Interatrial block
mOXVGy.description: A block in the conduction pathway from the right atrium to the left atrium. Results in prolongation of the P wave on ECG and increases the risk of developing atrial fibrillation.

5OXiGy.title: Antidesmoglein antibodies
5OXiGy.description: Autoantibodies found in pemphigus vulgaris. Directed against desmoglein 1 or 3, which mediate keratinocyte adherence.

MOXMGy.title: Ectopic pacemaker
MOXMGy.description: A group of cells within the heart (other than the sinoatrial node) that has the potential to spontaneously depolarize and generate electrical potentials that are transmitted to the ventricles, resulting in ventricular contractions. Causes ectopic beats and arrhythmias.

nOX7Gy.title: Escape rhythm
nOX7Gy.description: A myocardial electrical rhythm generated by ectopic pacemaker cells. Atrial escape rhythms cause abnormal p waves that precede a normal QRS complex. Junctional rhythms are bradycardic (40–60/min) and have normal QRS complexes without a preceding p wave. Ventricular escape rhythms are bradycardic (25–40/min) and have wide QRS complexes without a preceding p wave.

media.title: Sinus bradycardia with sinus pause and junctional escape rhythm

LOXwGy.title: Translocation trisomy 21
LOXwGy.description: A genetic cause of Down syndrome in which the long arm of chromosome 21 is translocated to another chromosome (commonly chromosome 14). As a result, three copies of chromosome 21 are present in the affected individual (unbalanced translocation). Accounts for approx. 4% of cases of Down syndrome.

oOX0ty.title: Neuraminidase
oOX0ty.description: A viral enzyme that cleaves neuraminic acid residues from glycoprotein, which results in viral release from the host cell. Found in influenza virus.

KOXUty.title: Bird beak sign
KOXUty.description: Gradual tapering of the lumen of a hollow viscus, typically seen on contrast-enhanced imaging. Most commonly used to describe barium esophagogram findings in achalasia cardia and contrast enema findings in midgut and cecal volvulus.

media.title: Bird beak sign in cecal volvulus

6OXjty.title: Amyloid plaque
6OXjty.description: A collection of abnormal, extracellular, fibrous proteins that are deposited in tissues as part of conditions such as systemic amyloidosis.

media.title: Senile plaques in presenile Alzheimer's disease

JOXsty.title: Alpha-2 adrenergic receptor
JOXsty.description: A Gi G-protein coupled receptor present in the presynaptic sympathetic neurons of the central nervous system, pancreas, platelets, and vascular smooth muscle. Activation causes feedback inhibition of sympathetic neurons, decreased insulin secretion, increased platelet activation, and decreased vascular resistance.

qOXCty.title: Popcorn calcification
qOXCty.description: A type of calcification characterized by amorphous rings and arcs that resemble popcorn on imaging. Seen in several conditions, including chondrosarcoma, degenerating fibroadenomas, and pulmonary hamartomas.

IOXYFy.title: Renal interstitium
IOXYFy.description: The extraglomerular intertubular tissue found mainly in the renal medulla. Participates in fluid and electrolyte exchange.

rOXfFy.title: TNF inhibitors
rOXfFy.description: A group of biologic agents used to treat various inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, Crohn disease). Examples include etanercept, infliximab, and adalimumab.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

7OX4Fy.title: Unbalanced Robertsonian translocation
7OX4Fy.description: Extra chromosome (trisomy) or missing chromosome (monosomy) in an offspring of a carrier of balanced Robertsonian translocation. Inheritance of a Robertsonian chromosome involving chromosome 21 and a normal pair of chromosome 21 results in trisomy 21 (Down syndrome).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

HOXKFy.title: Urinary cast
HOXKFy.description: A cylindrical structure formed in the distal convoluted tubule and/or collecting ducts of the kidney that is visible on urine microscopy. Can be acellular (e.g., hyaline cast) or cellular (e.g., WBC casts, RBC casts, epithelial casts).

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

sOXtFy.title: Recombinant hCG
sOXtFy.description: A subcutaneously injected drug used in women undergoing assisted reproduction technology (e.g., IVF or ICSI). Causes an LH surge that stimulates final oocyte maturation and ovulation.

GOXBFy.title: Posterior descending artery
GOXBFy.description: A coronary artery that supplies the posterior wall of the heart. Most commonly originates from the right coronary artery but can originate from the circumflex coronary artery or both of these arteries.

FOXg8y.title: Left coronary artery
FOXg8y.description: A coronary artery that branches into the left anterior descending artery (LAD) and the left circumflex artery (LCX).

8OXO8y.title: Platelet activating factor
8OXO8y.description: A proinflammatory phospholipid mediator that is produced by platelets, inflammatory cells (e.g., neutrophils, monocytes, macrophages), and the endothelium. Involved in the local and systemic inflammatory response and platelet aggregation and activation.

uOXp8y.title: Complement component 5a
uOXp8y.description: A pro-inflammatory compound formed from the cleavage of C5. Acts as an anaphylatoxin, mediator of sepsis, and neutrophil chemotactic factor.

EOX88y.title: Leukotriene B4
EOX88y.description: A neutrophil chemotactic factor secreted by leukocytes during acute inflammation. An end product of arachidonic acid metabolism. Requires 5-lipoxygenase activity for its formation.

vOXA8y.title: N-formylmethionine
vOXA8y.description: An amino acid sequence that initiates bacterial proteins. Detected by receptors on host immune cells, which leads to phagocytosis.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

DOX1uy.title: Complement component 3a
DOX1uy.description: A proinflammatory compound formed from the cleavage of C3. Acts as an anaphylatoxin and is involved in T cell and macrophage activation, mast cell degranulation, vasodilatation, angiogenesis stimulation, and chemotaxis.

wOXhuy.title: Anaphylatoxins
wOXhuy.description: A group of fragments of complement proteins (e.g., C3a, C4a, C5A) that cause a pro-inflammatory response (e.g., neutrophil and macrophage activation, platelet activation, cytokine release).

9OXNuy.title: Control group
9OXNuy.description: A group in a trial or experiment that does not receive the intervention (e.g., a drug) or did not develop the outcome (e.g., a disease) that is being researched. It serves as a comparison to the case or treatment group.

xOXEuy.title: Chronic pyelonephritis
xOXEuy.description: A recurrent or persistent inflammation of the kidney (e.g., from recurrent or persistent infection, vesicoureteral reflux, or urinary tract obstruction) that results in fibrosis (corticomedullary scarring).

yOXdEy.title: Hyperphenylalaninemia
yOXdEy.description: An increased serum phenylalanine concentration. Among neonates, the threshold for hyperphenylalaninemia is 60 μmol/L. Mild phenylketonuria (PKU) typically occurs with a concentration 600-900 μmol/L; classic PKU typically results in a concentration > 1,200 μmol/L.

AOXREy.title: Hyperammonemia
AOXREy.description: The accumulation of excess ammonia in the blood. Can be acquired (e.g., from cirrhosis) or hereditary (e.g., from urea cycle disorders). Causes asterixis, slurred speech, somnolence, vomiting, cerebral edema, and blurred vision.

destinations.label: Amino acids → Conditions associated with amino acid metabolism

_OX5Ey.title: Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency
_OX5Ey.description: An X-linked recessive urea cycle disorder (the most common one) that typically causes hyperammonemia in the first few days of life. Laboratory studies characteristically show elevated orotic acid and decreased BUN.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Urea cycle disorders

zOXrEy.title: Transamination
zOXrEy.description: The transfer of an amino group from one molecule to another (e.g., by alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase).

destinations.label: Amino acids →  Biochemical reactions of amino acid metabolism

alXQvy.title: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1
alXQvy.description: A mitochondrial enzyme that transfers the ammonia group (released from glutamate or glutamine) to a phosphorylated bicarbonate molecule to form carbamate and then phosphorylates carbamate to form carbamoyl phosphate. The rate-limiting enzyme for urea synthesis. Activated by N-acetylglutamate.

YlXnvy.title: Argininosuccinate synthetase
YlXnvy.description: A cytoplasmic enzyme involved in the urea cycle. It synthesizes argininosuccinate from citrulline and aspartate.

blXHvy.title: Argininosuccinase
blXHvy.description: A cytoplasmic enzyme that is involved in the urea cycle. It converts argininosuccinic acid to arginine and fumarate.

XlX9vy.title: Arginase
XlX9vy.description: A manganese-containing cytoplasmic enzyme that is involved in the urea cycle. It converts arginine into urea and ornithine.

WlXPDy.title: PAX8-PPAR-γ rearrangement
WlXPDy.description: A common genetic alteration seen in follicular adenoma and follicular thyroid carcinoma. Involves the fusion between the PAX8 (thyroid-specific transcription factor) and PPAR-γ (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma) genes, which results in the production of an oncogene.

dlXoDy.title: β-sheet fibrils
dlXoDy.description: A collection of insoluble amyloid fibrils that are deposited extracellularly in various conditions (e.g., multiple myeloma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, rheumatoid arthritis).

VlXGDy.title: Physiologic dead space
VlXGDy.description: The sum of anatomic and alveolar deadspace; the volume of inspired air that does not participate in gas exchange.

media.title: Anatomical vs. alveolar dead space (minute ventilation)

elXxDy.title: Anatomic dead space
elXxDy.description: The part of the respiratory system that conducts air but does not participate in gas exchange. Includes the nose, pharynx, trachea, and bronchioles.

media.title: Anatomical vs. alveolar dead space (minute ventilation)

UlXbwy.title: Oxygen saturation
UlXbwy.description: The percentage of oxygen-saturated hemoglobin in the blood. Normal levels in postnatal systemic arterial circulation are 95-100%. Oxygen saturation in venous blood differs from site to site based on the metabolic activity of the tissue. Oxygen saturation of blood in the pulmonary artery (mixed oxygen venous saturation) is 60-80% in the resting state.

2lXTwy.title: Specialized transduction
2lXTwy.description: A type of transduction mediated by a lysogenic phage in which bacterial and viral DNA becomes excised and packaged into phage capsids, which can then infect other bacteria.

TlX6wy.title: Hypocortisolism
TlX6wy.description: A state of decreased production of glucocorticoids (e.g., due to adrenal insufficiency). Can cause weakness, fatigue, depression, decreased appetite, weight loss, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain.

glXFwy.title: Serpiginous
glXFwy.description: A descriptor for a cutaneous lesion with a progressive, creeping, snake-like border.

SlXywy.title: Schistosomiasis
SlXywy.description: An infection caused by Schistosoma species. Clinical manifestations vary depending on the species involved and can include dermatitis, hepatosplenomegaly, portal hypertension, genitourinary infection, and pulmonary hypertension.

media.title: Geographic distribution of schistosomiasis (risk of transmission)

hlXc9y.title: Thyroidization
hlXc9y.description: A descriptor for a histopathologic finding seen in patients with chronic pyelonephritis in which renal tubules that contain eosinophilic casts have an appearance that resembles thyroid tissue.

RlXl9y.title: True negative
RlXl9y.description: A negative test result in an individual who does not have the condition that is being tested.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

ilXJ9y.title: False negative
ilXJ9y.description: A negative test result in an individual who has the condition that is being tested.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

QlXu9y.title: False positive
QlXu9y.description: A positive test result in an individual who does not have the condition that is being tested.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

jlX_9y.title: True positive
jlX_9y.description: A positive test result in an individual who has the condition that is being tested.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

PlXWCy.title: Leflunomide
PlXWCy.description: A disease-modifying antirheumatic drug that is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis. Its antiproliferative and anti-inflammatory effects are due to the prevention of pyrimidine synthesis through inhibition of dihydroorotate dehydrogenase. Adverse effects include gastrointestinal symptoms, hepatotoxicity and teratogenicity.

4lX3Cy.title: Subacute necrotising encephalomyelopathy
4lX3Cy.description: A mitochondrial myopathy that typically manifests in infancy with psychomotor delay, lactic acidosis and manifestations of basal ganglia and/or brainstem dysfunction (e.g., ataxia, dystonia, cranial nerve palsies). Characterized by bilateral, symmetric necrosis of the central nervous system (especially the basal ganglia, thalamus, and brainstem).

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Mitochondrial myopathies

NlX-Cy.title: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
NlX-Cy.description: The leading national public health institute in the United States, which serves to protect public health and safety through control and prevention of communicable diseases and mitigation of environmental health hazards nationally and internationally.

mlXVxy.title: Ionized calcium
mlXVxy.description: A form of calcium that is not bound to any proteins and circulates in the blood as Ca2+. It is physiologically active. Serum ionized calcium concentration is used to estimate total calcium stores.

destinations.label: Hypocalcemia → Calcium homeostasis and calcium physiology

5lXixy.title: Total serum calcium
5lXixy.description: The total amount of calcium circulating in the serum. ~ 50% of total serum calcium is inactive and bound to proteins such as albumin. Measured total calcium can be corrected for a lower or higher serum albumin. Corrected calcium (mg/dL) = measured total calcium (mg/dL) + [0.8 x (4.0 - albumin concentration in g/dL)].

destinations.label: Hypocalcemia → Calcium homeostasis and calcium physiology

MlXMxy.title: Factor Va
MlXMxy.description: A coagulation factor of the common pathway that is activated by thrombin (factor IIa). Once activated, factors Va, Xa, and calcium form prothrombinase complex, which converts prothrombin (factor II) to thrombin.

nlX7xy.title: Factor Xa
nlX7xy.description: A coagulation factor of the common pathway that is either activated by factor VIIa together with tissue factor (factor III) in the extrinsic pathway or by factor IXa together with factor VIIIa in the intrinsic pathway. Both activation pathways take place in the presence of calcium. Once activated, factors Va, Xa, and calcium form prothrombinase complex, which converts prothrombin (factor II) to thrombin.

LlXwxy.title: Factor XIII
LlXwxy.description: A clotting factor of the common coagulation pathway that is activated by factor IIa (thrombin) in the presence of calcium. Once activated, it stabilizes the fibrin clot by introducing crosslinks.

olX0By.title: Ureteric bud
olX0By.description: Forms during the 5th week of fetal development as part of the metanephros. The ureteric bud originates from the caudal end of the mesonephric duct and fulfills two purposes: inducing further differentiation of the metanephric blastema and forming the collecting duct system (including the ureter, renal pelvis, major calyces, minor calyces, collecting ducts and tubules).

KlXUBy.title: Metanephric mesenchyme
KlXUBy.description: Part of the metanephros that eventually forms the excretory system, including the glomeruli, Bowman's capsule, proximal convoluted tubule, Loop of Henle, and distal convoluted tubule. Its differentiation is induced by the ureteric bud (the other part of the metanephros).

6lXjBy.title: Maintenance dose
6lXjBy.description: The maintenance dose refers to the amount of a certain drug needed to achieve a steady target plasma concentration. Formula: maintenance dose = (Cp ∗ Cl ∗ τ) / F (where Cp = target plasma concentration at steady state, Cl = clearance, τ = dosing interval, F = bioavailability)

JlXsBy.title: H2 receptor
JlXsBy.description: A G-protein coupled histamine receptor. Stimulation of H2 receptors in the gastric parietal cells leads to increased gastric acid secretion via ATPase activation.

rlXfyy.title: Vitamin B₅
rlXfyy.description: A water-soluble enzyme used in the synthesis of coenzyme A, which is important for energy metabolism and the synthesis of cholestrol, fatty acids, and acetyl choline. Deficiency of vitamin B5 is rare and manifests with adrenal insufficiency, enteritis, alopecia, dermatitis, distal paresthesias, and dysesthesias.

7lX4yy.title: Vitamin B₇
7lX4yy.description: A water-soluble vitamin that functions as a cofactor for carboxylation, transcarboxylation, and decarboxylation enzymes involved in gluconeogenesis, lipogenesis, fatty acid synthesis, and amino acid catabolism.

HlXKyy.title: Folate
HlXKyy.description: A water-soluble vitamin that acts as a coenzyme in DNA and RNA synthesis. Important for methylation reactions and the formation of nucleic acids. Dietary sources include leafy green vegetables and liver. Deficiency in early pregnancy can cause neural tube defects. 'Folate' typically encompasses all biologically active forms, while 'folic acid' refers to the synthetic preparation.

slXtyy.title: Micelle
slXtyy.description: A spherical-shaped aggregation of surfactant molecules in a colloid. Composed of an outer layer of hydrophilic (polar) heads and an inner hydrophobic (nonpolar) core. Allows absorption of lipids and fat-soluble vitamins.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Digestion and absorption of lipids

GlXByy.title: Elevated transaminases
GlXByy.description: An increased serum concentration of ALT and/or AST. The pattern of elevation provides additional information about the underlying etiology. For example, hepatocellular injury is marked by elevated AST and ALT disproportionate to ALP; isolated elevation of AST may indicate cardiac or muscle disease.

tlXXAy.title: Homocysteine
tlXXAy.description: An intermediate molecule that is derived from the amino acid methionine. Can be converted into cystathionine (requires vitamin B6), which is then converted into the amino acid cysteine, or it can be recycled back into methionine (requires folate and vitamin B12). High levels of homocysteine cause hyperhomocysteinemia.

destinations.label: Amino acids →  Catabolism of the carbon skeleton of amino acids

FlXgAy.title: Cystathionine
FlXgAy.description: A molecule derived from homocysteine. It is formed by the action of the cystathionine beta-synthase enzyme, which requires vitamin B6 as a cofactor. It is converted to the amino acid cysteine by the action of the cystathionine gamma-lyase enzyme.

destinations.label: Amino acids →  Catabolism of the carbon skeleton of amino acids

8lXOAy.title: Fibrinogen
8lXOAy.description: A soluble protein produced in the liver that acts as a clotting factor. It is activated by thrombin (factor IIa) to become fibrin (factor Ia).

ulXpAy.title: Thrombin
ulXpAy.description: An enzyme produced from prothrombin (factor II) in the common pathway of the coagulation cascade by the action of factor Va, factor Xa, and calcium ions. Catalyzes the conversion of fibrinogen (factor I) to fibrin (factor Ia) in the final step in the coagulation cascade.

ElX8Ay.title: Endothelium
ElX8Ay.description: A single layer of squamous cells lining the inner surface of blood and lymphatic vessels that plays an important role in filtration, vessel tone, hemostasis, and inflammation.

vlXAAy.title: Venous stasis
vlXAAy.description: A state of decreased velocity of blood flow through small veins, which can be caused by prolonged immobilization. Venous stasis increases the risk of deep venous thrombosis.

DlX1_y.title: DNA methylation
DlX1_y.description: A mechanism of regulation of gene activity that involves the linkage of CH3 groups with cytosine bases by DNA methyltransferases. Results in inhibition of transcription.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Epigenetic regulation of gene expression

wlXh_y.title: Chylomicron
wlXh_y.description: A lipoprotein that carries triglycerides and cholesterol from the small intestine to adipocytes, cardiac muscle, and skeletal muscle. Composed of an outer phospholipid bilayer with embedded apolipoproteins and a core containing triglycerides and cholesterol.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

9lXN_y.title: Soluble NSF attachment protein receptor
9lXN_y.description: A protein complex that mediates the fusion of intracellular vesicles with other membranes (e.g., exocytosis of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

zlXrzy.title: Pelvic splanchnic nerves
zlXrzy.description: Visceral nerves that arise from the S2 to S4 spinal levels. They provide parasympathetic innervation to the pelvic viscera, which includes the bladder, rectum, uterus, cervix, and erectile tissue.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity
Autonomic nervous system → Parasympathetic nervous system

-lXDzy.title: Femoral nerve
-lXDzy.description: A nerve that originates from the L2 to L4 lumbar levels. Innervates the skin of the anteromedial thigh and medial lower leg, as well as the quadriceps femoris, iliacus, sartorius, and pectineus muscles. Injury causes decreased extension of the knee and decreased flexion of the hip.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Innervation of the thigh
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

media.title: Innervation of the lower extremity (ventral view)

ZNXZ-y.title: Obturator nerve
ZNXZ-y.description: A nerve that arises from lumbar levels L2 to L4. Innervates the skin of the medial thigh and the gracilis, pectineus, obturator externus, adductor magnus, longus, and brevis muscles. Injury causes decreased adduction and decreased medial rotation of the leg.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves
Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Innervation of the thigh

0NXe-y.title: Genitofemoral nerve
0NXe-y.description: A nerve that arises from the L1 and L2 segments of the lumbar plexus. It provides sensory innervation to the skin of the anterior scrotum in males and mons pubis and labia majora in females. In males, it also provides motor innervation to the cremaster muscle. Injury results in a decreased cremasteric reflex.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

aNXQ-y.title: Ilioinguinal nerve
aNXQ-y.description: A nerve that originates from the anterior ramus of the L1 segment of the lumbar plexus. Provides cutaneous sensation to the mons pubis, the upper medial thigh, the root of the penis and the anterior scrotum in males, and the labia majora in females. The ilioinguinal nerve is the afferent limb of the cremasteric reflex.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

YNXn-y.title: Area postrema
YNXn-y.description: An area just outside the blood-brain barrier located on the floor of the 4th ventricle that contains the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ). Stimulation of this area causes vomiting. The area postrema can be inhibited by dopamine receptor antagonists (e.g., metoclopramide).

bNXH-y.title: Chemoreceptor trigger zone
bNXH-y.description: A region within the area postrema that is in direct contact with blood (due to lack of blood-brain barrier). It is part of the vomiting centers of the brain (in the medulla). This area is connected to the nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) of the vagus nerve. Stimulation of this region by circulating drugs or hormones causes vomiting.

XNX9-y.title: Adams-Oliver syndrome
XNX9-y.description: A rare congenital syndrome characterized by aplasia cutis and transverse limb defects.

cNXaZA.title: Cholesterol desmolase
cNXaZA.description: A mitochondrial enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone, which is the first step in steroid hormone synthesis. Activated by ACTH and inhibited by ketoconazole.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal cortex

eNXxZA.title: Myosin light-chain phosphatase
eNXxZA.description: An enzyme in smooth muscle cells that dephosphorylates the light chains of myosin, which results in smooth muscle relaxation. Activated by cGMP.

media.title: Electro- and pharmacomechanical coupling of smooth muscle cell contraction

2NXT0A.title: Citrate synthase
2NXT0A.description: A mitochondrial enzyme involved in the Krebs cycle that catalyzes the conversion of oxaloacetate and acetyl-CoA to citrate.

fNXk0A.title: Isocitrate dehydrogenase
fNXk0A.description: A mitochondrial enzyme involved in the Krebs cycle that catalyzes the conversion of isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate and carbon dioxide.

TNX60A.title: Pyruvate carboxylase
TNX60A.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the carboxylation of pyruvate into oxaloacetate in the presence of ATP and biotin during gluconeogenesis. Regulated by acetyl-CoA (positive allosteric modulator).

gNXF0A.title: Bacterial transposition
gNXF0A.description: A process by which genes can move from one position in the genome to another, or from a plasmid to bacterial DNA. A common way for bacteria to acquire antibiotic resistance.

SNXy0A.title: Adenosine triphosphate
SNXy0A.description: A nucleoside triphosphate that stores and transfers energy. Dephosphorylation of ATP produces ADP and releases energy.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Electron transport chain and ATP synthesis

hNXcaA.title: Pilus
hNXcaA.description: A bacterial appendage found on the surface of gram-negative bacteria. Facilitates adhesion of bacteria to specific surfaces. Sex pili are used to exchange genes with other bacteria during conjugation.

3NXSaA.title: Red marrow
3NXSaA.description: A type of bone marrow that contains hematopoeitic stem cells and stromal cells. In adults, it is mainly found in flat bones (e.g., pelvis, skull, sternum).

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Bone marrow and hematopoiesis

iNXJaA.title: Mesenchymal stem cells
iNXJaA.description: A population of multipotent stem cells in the bone marrow and mesenchymal tissue that can differentiate into various cell types, including osteoblasts, adipocytes, and chondrocytes. Not involved in hematopoiesis.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Bone marrow and hematopoiesis

QNXuaA.title: Yellow marrow
QNXuaA.description: A nonhematopoietic type of bone marrow that is found in the shafts and diaphyses of long bones in adults. Composed mainly of fatty tissue.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Bone marrow and hematopoiesis

PNXWYA.title: Granulocyte-monocyte colony-stimulating factor
PNXWYA.description: A cytokine that stimulates the production of all myeloid cell lines (granulocytes, monocytes, erythrocytes, thrombocytes). Recombinant GM-CSF can be used to treat bone marrow failure or neutropenia.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Bone marrow and hematopoiesis

kNXmYA.title: Pleiotropy
kNXmYA.description: The production of two or more seemingly unrelated phenotypical changes by a single gene.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

ONXIYA.title: Loss of heterozygosity
ONXIYA.description: An event in a cell in which a dysfunctional allele of a gene is inherited and the remaining allele is switched off via a mutation. If this single mutation takes place in a tumor suppressor gene, the loss of heterozygosity can lead to the development of cancer. For example, in Li-Fraumeni syndrome, one copy of the p53 tumor suppressor gene is damaged, so loss of heterozygosity can lead to cancer.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

lNXvYA.title: Pyogenic
lNXvYA.description: Causing the formation of pus, usually due to an infection with pyogenic bacteria. Enteric bacteria as well as staphylococcus and streptococcus species are the most common causative agents.

5NXibA.title: Lower esophageal sphincter
5NXibA.description: A circular muscle located at the junction between the stomach and esophagus. Prevents reflux of gastric contents into the esophagus. Dysfunction of this sphincter is seen in achalasia and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

MNXMbA.title: Coombs reagent
MNXMbA.description: A reagent containing antihuman globulin. It can bind to human antibodies and complement on the surface of red blood cells and may be polyspecific (i.e., contains both anti-IgG and anticomplement antibodies) or monospecific (i.e., targets either IgG or specific complement components). Used in both direct and indirect Coombs tests.

nNX7bA.title: Mycolic acid
nNX7bA.description: A type of fatty acid found in the cell walls of Mycobacteria species. Can be identified by Ziehl-Neelsen stain. Mycolic acid synthesis is inhibited by isoniazid.

LNXwbA.title: Orthoflavivirus louisense
LNXwbA.description: A single-stranded, positive-sense RNA virus of the Flaviviridae family that causes St. Louis encephalitis. Mainly found in the US. The virus cycles between mosquitos and birds and is transmitted to humans via mosquito bites.

oNX0XA.title: Cyclooxygenase-1
oNX0XA.description: An enzyme constitutively expressed in most cell lines. Converts arachidonic acid to cyclic endoperoxides, which serve as a precursor for thromboxane A2, prostaglandins, and prostacyclin. Therefore, COX-1 is involved in the regulation of many normal cellular processes (e.g., gastric mucosal protection, platelet aggregation, renal function). This enzyme is inhibited by NSAIDs.

6NXjXA.title: St. Louis encephalitis
6NXjXA.description: A vector-borne disease caused by the St. Louis encephalitis virus. Causes a prodrome of fever, malaise, sore throat, and cough. Progresses to aseptic meningitis and/or encephalitis and can cause headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, disorientation, irritability, tremors, and, occasionally, convulsions.

destinations.label: Miscellaneous mosquito-borne diseases → Mosquito-borne Flavivirus diseases

pNXLXA.title: Human T-cell lymphotropic virus
pNXLXA.description: An RNA virus that belongs to the family of retroviridae (meaning it expresses reverse transcriptase activity). Involved in the pathogenesis of adult T-cell lymphoma and HTLV-associated myelopathy. This virus is endemic to Japan and the Caribbean.

qNXCXA.title: Lymphocytic encephalitis
qNXCXA.description: A viral disease transmitted by rats. In immunocompetent individuals it causes nonspecific symptoms such as fever, malaise. In immunocompromised individuals it can cause encephalitis, seizures, respiratory failure, coagulopathy, renal failure, and liver failure.

INXYcA.title: Bronchiole
INXYcA.description: A branch of a bronchus. These divide into terminal bronchioles and finally into respiratory bronchioles.

rNXfcA.title: Terminal bronchiole
rNXfcA.description: A branch of a bronchiole. Though part of the conducting zone of the respiratory system, these are not lined with cartilage. This is the primary site of inflammation in asthma. Terminal bronchioles further branch into respiratory bronchioles.

7NX4cA.title: Respiratory bronchiole
