7NX4cA.description: The final branch of a terminal bronchiole from which alveoli evaginate. The respiratory bronchiole has less smooth muscle than the terminal bronchiole, and participates in gas exchange.

sNXtcA.title: Pleural fluid
sNXtcA.description: Fluid within the pleural space that minimizes friction during the respiratory movements of the lungs. When there is too much fluid in the pleural space, it is termed a pleural effusion.

GNXBcA.title: Monosomy
GNXBcA.description: A type of aneuploidy (numeric chromosomal abnormality) in which the resulting karyotype shows 45 instead of 46 chromosomes. One homologous chromosome from a pair is absent, typically due to mistakes during mitotic or meiotic cell division.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

tNXX1A.title: Homologous chromosomes
tNXX1A.description: One of the 23 pairs of chromosomes (one chromosome from each parent) present in the somatic cells of eukaryotic organisms. Although they are similar in size, genetic sequence, and centromere location, they do not necessarily carry the same alleles.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

media.title: Homologous chromosomes before and after replication

FNXg1A.title: Acrocentric chromosome
FNXg1A.description: A pair of sister chromatids in which the centromere is located near one end of the chromosome. As a result, they have a very short p arm and a very long q arm.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

8NXO1A.title: Electron transport chain
8NXO1A.description: A series of increasingly electronegative organic molecules that transfer electrons via redox reactions. It is coupled with transport of protons (H+) across the inner mitochondrial membrane, resulting in an electrochemical proton gradient. This gradient is used for ATP production.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Electron transport chain and ATP synthesis

ENX81A.title: Pimecrolimus
ENX81A.description: A calcineurin inhibitor with immunosuppressant effects that selectively inhibits calcineurin, which ultimately leads to a decrease in interleukin-2 transcription. As a result, activation of Th2, CD8, and NK cells is decreased.

vNXA1A.title: Acetyl-CoA
vNXA1A.description: An activated acetyl unit attached to coenzyme A by a high-energy thioester bond. A product of major catabolic pathways such as beta-oxidation of fatty acids, ketone body degradation, glycolysis, and pyruvate oxidation. Converted to acetoacetyl CoA (used in cholesterol synthesis and ketogenesis), malonyl CoA (used in fatty acid synthesis), and citrate (used in Krebs cycle).

DNX1WA.title: Oxaloacetate
DNX1WA.description: The conjugate of oxaloacetic acid that serves as an intermediate in several metabolic pathways (e.g., citric acid cycle, gluconeogenesis).

CNXqWA.title: Fumarate
CNXqWA.description: An unsaturated dicarboxylic acid that is involved in Krebs cycle. It is synthesized from succinic acid by the enzyme succinate dehydrogenase. It is also produced from aspartate and citrulline by the enzyme argininosuccinate as a byproduct of the urea cycle. Fumarate is converted to malate by the enzyme fumarate dehydratase.

BNXzWA.title: Succinyl-CoA
BNXzWA.description: An intermediate of the Krebs cycle that consists of succinic acid linked to coenzyme A by a high-energy thioester bond. Succinyl CoA synthetase can reversibly convert succinic acid to succinyl-CoA. Succinyl-CoA can also be synthesized from alpha-ketoglutarate by alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase and from methylmalonyl-CoA by methylmalonyl-CoA mutase. Succinyl-CoA is converted to aminolevulinic acid for heme synthesis by aminolevulinate synthase.

yNXddA.title: α-ketoglutarate
yNXddA.description: A substrate of the citric acid cycle. In muscle tissue, α-ketoglutarate combines with amino groups to form glutamate, which can then enter the glucose-alanine cycle.

_NX5dA.title: Calcineurin
_NX5dA.description: A calcium- and calmodulin-binding serine-threonine phosphatase that activates transcription factors (NFATS = nuclear factor of activated T cells) via dephosphorylation. NFATS induce the transcription of IL-2, which activates T cells. Can be targeted with calcineurin inhibitors.

zNXrdA.title: Myopathy
zNXrdA.description: A dysfunction of muscle fibers without the involvement of the neuromuscular junction or nerve supply. Symptoms include muscle pain, weakness, cramping, and tetany.

-NXDdA.title: Hyaline membrane
-NXDdA.description: Membranes composed of fibrin, cellular debris, and red blood cells that line the alveoli in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) or newborn respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS). Result in impaired gas exchange.

ZmXZVA.title: Carnitine-dependent shuttle
ZmXZVA.description: The biochemical process required for the transportation of long-chain fatty acids across the inner mitochondrial membrane. These fatty acids subsequently serve as a substrate for beta-oxidation and ketone body production.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

0mXeVA.title: Active immunity
0mXeVA.description: Immunity acquired as a result of exposure to an antigen. Fighting off an infection and immunization both confer active immunity. The initial immune response involves the formation of IgM antibodies, which class switch to IgG immunoglobulins after a period of 4 to 6 weeks.

YmXnVA.title: APC gene
YmXnVA.description: A tumor suppressor gene located on chromosome 5q22. Encodes a protein (Adenomatous Polyposis Coli) that is a negative regulator of the β-catenin/WNT pathway. Mutation is associated with familial adenomatous polyposis.

bmXHVA.title: MLH1 gene
bmXHVA.description: A DNA mismatch repair gene. Mutation in this gene is associated with hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (Lynch syndrome).

XmX9VA.title: TP53 gene
XmX9VA.description: A tumor suppressor gene that encodes the p53 protein that suppresses cell division and regulates DNA repair and apoptosis. Mutations in this gene result in uncontrolled cell proliferation and are hence associated with most cancers and Li-Fraumeni syndrome.

cmXaeA.title: DCC gene
cmXaeA.description: A tumor suppressor gene. Mutations in this gene are associated with colon cancer.

1mX2eA.title: DNA methyltransferase
1mX2eA.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a methyl group to DNA. Can change the expression of a DNA segment.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Epigenetic regulation of gene expression

dmXoeA.title: Methylation
dmXoeA.description: The process by which methyl groups are added a molecule. Methylation of DNA or histones usually results in gene suppression.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

emXxeA.title: Transposable element
emXxeA.description: A DNA sequence that can change its position within a genome or between genomes of distinct bacteria.

UmXbUA.title: 4-α-D-glucanotransferase
UmXbUA.description: A glycogen debranching enzyme that transfers 3 glucose residues (from a branch with 4 residues) onto the terminal glucose chain. The remaining single branching glucose is cleaved by α-1,6-glucosidase.

2mXTUA.title: HLA-B51
2mXTUA.description: A human leukocyte antigen that is best known for its association with Behcet disease.

fmXkUA.title: Hepatosplenomegaly
fmXkUA.description: An enlargement of the spleen (splenomegaly) and liver (hepatomegaly). Splenomegaly is defined as any of the following: palpable 8 cm below the costal arch, > 20 cm in diameter, or > 1000 g in weight. Hepatomegaly is defined as > 16 cm in the midclavicular line by ultrasound. Can be caused by various conditions, including malignancy, infection, or venous congestion.

gmXFUA.title: Bacterial outer membrane
gmXFUA.description: A secondary plasma membrane surrounding the thin cell wall of Gram-negative bacteria. This acts as both an additional protective barrier and a site of integral membrane proteins, which have a variety of functions including substrate-specific porins and adherence factors. Mutations of these proteins confer antibiotic resistances onto gram-negative bacteria.

4mX3fA.title: Commensals
4mX3fA.description: A group of microorganisms that normally live on or within humans without causing harm. When identified on laboratory testing, they are generally considered to be contaminants, but repeat testing can confirm if they represent true infection. Examples include Corynebacterium spp. (excluding C. diphtheria), Bacillus spp. (excluding B. anthracis), Propionibacterium spp., and viridans group streptococci.

kmXmfA.title: Aorto-ventricular pressure gradient
kmXmfA.description: The pressure gradient between the aortic root and the left ventricle during systole, which is usually minimal can become pathologically elevated (e.g., in patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy or aortic stenosis).

OmXIfA.title: Athletic heart syndrome
OmXIfA.description: A collection of cardiac changes seen in athletic individuals. Characterized by eccentric ventricular hypertrophy, which can mimic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Typically associated with sinus bradycardia.

lmXvfA.title: Eccentric hypertrophy
lmXvfA.description: A type of cardiac remodeling associated with dilated cardiomyopathy in which sarcomeres duplicate in series, causing muscle fibers to increase in length and width.

mmXVTA.title: Bacterial conjugation
mmXVTA.description: A process in which a bacterium directly transfers genetic material to another bacterium via a pilus.

5mXiTA.title: Cyanide-nitroprusside test
5mXiTA.description: A test that detects increased amounts of cysteine/cystine and homocysteine/homocystine in urine to screen for inborn diseases of amino acid transporters (e.g., cystinuria). Sodium cyanide and sodium nitroprusside are added to a urine sample; the test is positive if the sample turns red/purple.

MmXMTA.title: Exotoxin
MmXMTA.description: A polypeptide toxin produced and secreted by certain bacteria. In contrast to endotoxins, exotoxins induce high titers of antibodies or act as superantigens that can activate large numbers of T cells, which results in the massive release of cytokines. Examples include tetanus, botulism, and diphtheria exotoxins.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

nmX7TA.title: Urine alkalinization
nmX7TA.description: A treatment regimen to raise urinary pH to 6.5–7.5. Slow and prolonged alkalinization (e.g., by consuming a diet rich in fruits and vegetables or using supplemental potassium citrate) is used to prevent recurrence of calcium oxalate, uric acid, and cystine stones. Rapid alkalinization of urine is achieved by administering IV sodium bicarbonate to enhance toxin excretion in cases of poisoning (e.g., salicylate toxicity).

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Enhanced elimination

LmXwTA.title: Radiopacity
LmXwTA.description: The light areas on x-ray, fluoroscopy, and CT scans. Represents high-density areas (e.g., metal, bones), which absorb more x-rays than low-density areas, allowing fewer x-rays to reach the film. This results in a lighter appearance as x-rays appear black on radiographic images.

omX0gA.title: Pudendal nerve
omX0gA.description: A nerve that originates from the S2 to S4 sacral nerve roots. Provides sensory innervation to the skin of the perineum, external genitalia, and external urethral and anal sphincter muscles. Injury can cause urinary and fecal incontinence.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

6mXjgA.title: Urine acidification
6mXjgA.description: A treatment regimen to lower the urinary pH to ≤ 7. Slow and prolonged acidification of urine (e.g., by consuming cranberry juice dairy products, grains, meat) is used in to prevent recurrence of calcium phosphate and struvite stones. Rapid acidification of urine is achieved by administering oral methionine or IV ammonium chloride to prevent stone recurrence or to enhance elimination of weak bases such as cocaine, amphetamines, and strychnine.

pmXLgA.title: Gastric acid
pmXLgA.description: An acid composed of water, hydrogen, and chloride that is secreted by parietal cells in the stomach. Its main function is to maintaining the acidic environment of the stomach. It activates pepsinogen, which then becomes pepsin. It is a natural defense mechanism against microorganisms (except H. pylori).

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

JmXsgA.title: Bicarbonate
JmXsgA.description: An alkaline compound with multiple functions in the body. Secreted by mucosal cells of the small intestine and the pancreas to increase the pH of incoming acidic chyme from the stomach. Also plays a critical role in acid-base homeostasis of the blood; carbonic acid dissociates to form bicarbonate and a hydrogen ion.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

qmXCgA.title: Ghrelin
qmXCgA.description: A hormone secreted by the gastrointestinal tract (e.g., stomach) that stimulates appetite. Levels increase during fasting states and decrease after intake of food.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract
General endocrinology → Regulation of appetite and satiety

ImXYSA.title: Hypercalciuria
ImXYSA.description: The presence of elevated calcium levels in the urine. Associated with calcium oxalate stone formation, Bartter syndrome, primary hyperparathyroidism, and vitamin D excess.

rmXfSA.title: Sampson artery
rmXfSA.description: A small vessel that anastomoses with the uterine and ovarian arteries. Courses inferior to the round ligament of uterus.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Ligaments of the female pelvis

7mX4SA.title: Bifid scrotum
7mX4SA.description: A midline cleft in the scrotum caused by incomplete union of the labioscrotal swellings. Associated with hypospadias.​​​​​​​

destinations.label: Abnormalities of the male urethra and webbed penis → Hypospadias

HmXKSA.title: Lesser sac
HmXKSA.description: An intraperitoneal recess that lies posterior to the stomach and lesser omentum. Common site of free fluid collection patients with intra-abdominal bleeding or acute pancreatitis. Opening of the lesser sac allows surgical access to the pancreas and is also done in gastric resections.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

smXtSA.title: Hemoperitoneum
smXtSA.description: Collection of blood in the peritoneal cavity. Most common causes include blunt or penetrating trauma to a visceral organ (esp. the liver or spleen) or large vessels (e.g., ruptured aneurysms). Generally considered a surgical emergency.

tmXXhA.title: Pneumatocele
tmXXhA.description: A cystic air-filled space in the lung parenchyma. Associated with acute infections (e.g., Staphylococcal or Pneumocystis pneumonia), chest trauma, and barotrauma from mechanical ventilation.

FmXghA.title: Streptococcus anginosus
FmXghA.description: A subgroup of viridans streptococci (gram-positive, catalase-negative cocci) that are part of the normal oral and GI tract flora in humans. Can cause brain and liver abscesses and bacteremia.

8mXOhA.title: Androstenedione
8mXOhA.description: A weak androgen steroid hormone that is an intermediate in the biosynthesis of estrone and of testosterone. Released by the adrenal gland and converted by aromatase to estrone in postmenopausal women.

umXphA.title: Inhibin B
umXphA.description: A hormone produced by Sertoli cells in males and ovarian granulosa cells in females that suppresses the release of follicle stimulating hormone (FSH). Involved in regulating developing follicles in females. Can be used to measure ovarian reserve and as a marker for granulosa cell tumors.

vmXAhA.title: Window period
vmXAhA.description: The duration of time between the onset of infection and the point at which a laboratory test can detect the infection.

media.title: Serology time course of acute and resolved hepatitis B infection

9mXN3A.title: Posterior vermis syndrome
9mXN3A.description: A syndrome characterized by vomiting, morning headache, gait abnormality, falls, and oculomotor dysfunction. Caused by lesions of the flocculonodular cerebellar lobe (e.g., medulloblastoma).

xmXE3A.title: δ-aminolevulinic acid
xmXE3A.description: A nonproteinogenic amino acid and the first compound in the heme/porphyrin synthesis pathway.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

ymXdRA.title: Ferrochelatase
ymXdRA.description: An iron-dependent enzyme that catalyzes the eighth and final step of the heme synthesis pathway. It converts protoporphyrin to heme by catalyzing the insertion of iron into protoporphyrin IX. Inhibition of this enzyme (as seen in lead poisoning) can result in sideroblastic anemia.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

AmXRRA.title: 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate
AmXRRA.description: Regulatory molecule created from the glycolytic intermediate 1,3-BPG. Found in erythrocytes. Tightly binds to deoxyhemoglobin to promote oxygen release (e.g., in peripheral tissue). Loosely binds to oxygenated hemoglobin to keep oxygen bound to hemoglobin (e.g., in the lungs).

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Metabolism of erythrocytes

_mX5RA.title: Biliverdin
_mX5RA.description: A green-colored pigment that forms from the breakdown of hemoglobin. Heme is broken down into biliverdin by heme oxidase.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Metabolism of erythrocytes

zmXrRA.title: Heme oxidase
zmXrRA.description: Enzyme that oxidizes heme into biliverdin in the process of hemoglobin breakdown.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Metabolism of erythrocytes

-mXDRA.title: C3 deficiency
-mXDRA.description: Genetic immunodeficiency disorder characterized by deficiency of the complement factor C3, which results in impaired opsonization of encapsulated bacteria. Patients present with recurrent pyogenic infections in early childhood and are at an increased risk for autoimmune conditions.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital complement deficiencies

Z5XZiA.title: Myogenic autoregulation
Z5XZiA.description: A mechanism by which arterial smooth muscle contracts and relaxes in response to changes in blood pressure to keep blood flow constant.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Renal blood flow

05XeiA.title: Sodium-hydrogen antiporter
05XeiA.description: A membrane protein found in epithelial cells of the proximal convoluted tubule. Maintains pH balance. Upregulated by angiotensin II.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Urine production

a5XQiA.title: Bruit
a5XQiA.description: An abnormal swishing sound on auscultation over a blood vessel. Caused by turbulent blood flow through a stenosed arterial segment (e.g., carotid artery stenosis, renal artery stenosis, AAA) or increased flow through an unobstructed vessel (i.e., arteriovenous fistulae).

Y5XniA.title: Tubuloglomerular feedback
Y5XniA.description: A mechanism by which macula densa cells regulate glomerular filtration rate (GFR). In response to high sodium chloride concentration (which indicates high GFR), the macula densa releases ATP and adenosine, which act on the myogenic juxtaglomerular cells of the afferent arteriole to cause vasoconstriction and reduce GFR. In response to low sodium chloride concentration (which indicates low GFR), the macula densa releases PGE2, which acts on the juxtaglomerular cells and causes renin release to increase GFR.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Renal blood flow

b5XHiA.title: Aldose reductase
b5XHiA.description: An NADPH-dependent oxidoreductase that primarily converts glucose to sorbitol, a critical first step in the polyol pathway.

X5X9iA.title: Polyol pathway
X5X9iA.description: A molecular pathway in which glucose is converted to sorbitol and then fructose. Increased activity of this pathway is seen in patients with poor glycemic control, which results in sorbitol accumulation in the lens, retina, myelin sheaths, and kidney.

c5XaQA.title: Frank-Starling law
c5XaQA.description: A principle that describes the relationship between end-diastolic volume and cardiac stroke volume. Cardiac contractility is directly related to the wall tension of the myocardium; an increase in end-diastolic volume will cause the myocardium to stretch, which increases contractility and results in increased stroke volume.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Regulation of cardiac activity

15X2QA.title: Concentric hypertrophy
15X2QA.description: A type of cardiac remodeling that occurs due to pressure overload or, in case of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, because of genetic mutations. Results in increased left ventricular wall thickness and is characterized by sarcomeres duplicating in parallel.

W5XPQA.title: Diastole
W5XPQA.description: A phase of the cardiac cycle that follows systole and the S2 heart sound. Ventricular filling occurs during this phase due to atrial contraction and ventricular relaxation.

d5XoQA.title: Systole
d5XoQA.description: A phase of the cardiac cycle that follows the S1 heart sound. Ventricular contraction and atrial relaxation and filling occur during this phase.

e5XxQA.title: Saponification
e5XxQA.description: The formation of white chalky deposits from the precipitation of long-chain fatty acids bound to sodium, potassium, or calcium ions. Can result from acute pancreatitis-induced fat necrosis.

U5XbjA.title: Glucocerebroside
U5XbjA.description: A sphingolipid found in the cell membranes of many tissues. Can accumulate in the lysosomes of macrophages in patients with Gaucher disease due to deficiency of glucocerebrosidase, which causes multiorgan dysfunction.

25XTjA.title: Sphingolipid
25XTjA.description: A lipid molecule with a long-chain or sphingoid base that may be linked to a fatty acid via an amide bond. Functions are not well understood but likely include structural function and cell-to-cell communication. Can accumulate due to a deficiency of lysosomal enzymes, which causes sphingolipidoses such as Tay-Sachs disease.

f5XkjA.title: Galactose 1-phosphate
f5XkjA.description: A product formed from galactose by galactokinase. Converted to glucose-1-phosphate by galactose 1-phosphate uridylyltransferase.

destinations.label: General metabolism → Disorders affecting the carbohydrate metabolism

T5X6jA.title: Synaptic cleft
T5X6jA.description: The space between a presynaptic neuron and postsynaptic neuron (or motor endplate) where an impulse is relayed by neurotransmitters.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

g5XFjA.title: Coronary sinus
g5XFjA.description: The main coronary vein. Receives blood from smaller coronary veins that merge together to form it. Courses transversely along the posterior surface of the heart in the left atrioventricular groove and drains deoxygenated blood into the right atrium.

S5XyjA.title: Anaplasmosis
S5XyjA.description: Bacterial zoonosis caused by Anaplasma spp. Transmitted by the hematophagous Ixodes tick. Invades erythrocytes and causes anemia.

h5XcPA.title: Superoxide
h5XcPA.description: A reactive oxygen radical (O₂-) produced by NADPH oxidase. Present in phagocytes (neutrophils and macrophages), for example. Important for hydrolyzing pathogens following phagocytosis.

35XSPA.title: Ixodes
35XSPA.description: A genus of ticks that are important vectors of zoonotic diseases such as Lyme disease, ehrlichiosis, and anaplasmosis. Species include Ixodes scapularis (deer tick) and Ixodes pacificus (western black-legged tick).

R5XlPA.title: Partial thromboplastin time
R5XlPA.description: An assay that evaluates the intrinsic and common pathways of the coagulation cascade (measures activity of factors XII, XI, X, IX, VIII, V, II, and I). Used to evaluate coagulation disorders and to monitor the effect of heparin. Normal range is 25–40 seconds.

i5XJPA.title: Iliotibial band
i5XJPA.description: A fibrous band of the fascia lata that originates from the lateral iliac crest and inserts at the lateral condyle of the tibia. It helps extend, abduct, and laterally rotate the hip and stabilize the knee.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region

media.title: Knee (showing iliotibial band and part of quadriceps femoris)

Q5XuPA.title: Anserine bursa
Q5XuPA.description: A synovial fluid-filled sac located a few centimeters inferior to the medial knee joint line between the pes anserinus (the common tendon for the sartorius, gracilis, and semitendinosus muscles) and the medial tibial condyle.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The knee joint

media.title: Ligaments and retinacula of the patella

j5X_PA.title: Thymidine kinase
j5X_PA.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the reaction by which phosphorylate deoxythymidine is turned into deoxythymidine monophosphate. Activates guanosine analogs used in the treatment of herpes simplex and varicella zoster infection (e.g., acyclovir, famciclovir).

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against herpes viruses

P5XW4A.title: Arteriolosclerosis
P5XW4A.description: A thickening and loss of elasticity of arterioles. Associated with chronic diabetes, chronic hypertension, and normal aging.

45X34A.title: Hyaline arteriolosclerosis
45X34A.description: A thickening of arteriolar walls caused by deposition of proteins below the endothelium. Appears as pink, amorphous deposits (hyaline) within the arteriolar walls on H&E staining. Seen in patients with chronic essential hypertension, chronic diabetes, and as a part of normal aging.

k5Xm4A.title: Hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis
k5Xm4A.description: A thickening of arteriolar walls due to the proliferation of subendothelial smooth muscle cells, which gives a pathognomonic onion-skin appearance to the arteriole on H&E staining. Seen in patients with severe/malignant hypertension.

O5XI4A.title: Chemotaxis
O5XI4A.description: Directed cellular migration that is mediated by chemical stimuli. During an immune response, immune cells undergo chemotaxis toward an infectious or inflammatory focus.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

m5XVkA.title: Anaerobic glycolysis
m5XVkA.description: A metabolic process that involves the anaerobic enzymatic conversion of glucose to lactate. Occurs in the cytosol and yields 2 molecules of ATP per glucose molecule.

55XikA.title: Host tropism
55XikA.description: The ability or tendency of a pathogen to infect a specific cell or organism. Determined by factors such as cell surface receptors, transcription factors, and other signaling molecules.

M5XMkA.title: Macular sparing
M5XMkA.description: A phenomenon in which macular vision is preserved despite adjacent visual field defects (e.g., in homonymous hemianopia due to a posterior cerebral artery stroke). The mechanism of this phenomenon is not fully understood; suggested mechanisms include extensive representation of the macula in the primary visual cortex and overlap between vascular territories of the middle and posterior cerebral arteries.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Scotoma and anopia

n5X7kA.title: Frontal eye field
n5X7kA.description: An area in the frontal cortex partly responsible for visual perception, awareness, and movement. Damage or ischemic lesions in this region causes gaze deviation toward the side of the lesion.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

L5XwkA.title: Horn cyst
L5XwkA.description: A keratin-filled cyst seen on dermoscopic or histopathologic evaluation of seborrheic keratoses.

o5X0OA.title: ALK gene
o5X0OA.description: A proto-oncogene located on the short arm of chromosome 2 whose gene product is ALK receptor tyrosine kinase. Mutation is associated with lung adenocarcinoma.

K5XUOA.title: Epidermal growth factor receptor gene
K5XUOA.description: A gene located on chromosome 7 that encodes the epidermal growth factor receptor protein. Activating mutations are associated with lung adenocarcinoma.

65XjOA.title: Enterotoxin B
65XjOA.description: A type of heat-stable toxin produced by Staphylococcus aureus. Involved in the pathogenesis of Staphylococcal food poisoning.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

p5XLOA.title: Heat-labile toxin
p5XLOA.description: A virulence factor that is destroyed at high temperatures and produced by certain bacteria, including enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC), Clostridium perfringens, and Bacillus cereus. Heat-labile enterotoxin overactivates adenylate cyclase, increasing production of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP). This causes increased secretion of chloride and water efflux into the intestinal lumen, which results in watery diarrhea.

destinations.label: Diarrheagenic E. coli → Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC)
General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

q5XCOA.title: Antiglutamic acid decarboxylase antibody
q5XCOA.description: An antibody against the enzyme glutamic acid decarboxylase, which is responsible for the conversion of glutamic acid to GABA. Found in ~ 80% of patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

I5XYlA.title: 50S subunit
I5XYlA.description: The large subunit of the prokaryotic ribosome. The large subunit (50S) and small subunit (30S) form the 70S ribosome.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

r5XflA.title: 30S subunit
r5XflA.description: The small subunit of the prokaryotic ribosome. Combines with the large subunit (50S) to form the 70S ribosome.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

75X4lA.title: Ribosomal translocation
75X4lA.description: The movement of the ribosome one codon along mRNA in the 3' direction. Occurs during the elongation process of translation.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

H5XKlA.title: Topoisomerase IV
H5XKlA.description: A bacterial enzyme that relaxes positive supercoils and unlinks recently replicated DNA. Inhibited by fluoroquinolone antibiotics.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

s5XtlA.title: Initiation complex
s5XtlA.description: A complex that forms during translation from the assembly of ribosomal subunits and the initiator tRNA (Met-tRNA) at the start codon (AUG) on the mRNA.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

F5XgNA.title: Aural fullness
F5XgNA.description: A sensation of fullness or pressure in the ear, especially when yawning or swallowing. Seen in patients with Eustachian tube dysfunction and Meniere disease.

u5XpNA.title: Carbonic anhydrase
u5XpNA.description: An enzyme with a zinc active site that is responsible for converting carbon dioxide and water into bicarbonate and a free hydrogen ion.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen and carbon dioxide transport

E5X8NA.title: Target lesions
E5X8NA.description: A skin lesion with three distinct zones: an inner dark red/brown zone, a surrounding pale zone, and an outer erythematous ring. It is the classic lesion of erythema multiforme.

media.title: Target lesion in erythema with scaling

v5XANA.title: G cell
v5XANA.description: A gastrin-producing cell that can be found in the gastric antrum and the duodenum. Stimulation via stomach distention, vagal stimulation, amino acids, and peptides causes gastrin release, which increases gastric acid production in parietal cells.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

D5X1mA.title: Lichenoid hyperplasia
D5X1mA.description: A type of pigmented dermal purpura. Associated with several conditions that cause inflammation and keratosis of the skin, including eczema, secondary syphilis, and some granulomatous lesions.

w5XhmA.title: Myocardial contractility
w5XhmA.description: The inherent ability of the heart muscle to contract. An increase in the myocardial contractility (e.g., sympathetic activation) leads to an increase in the stroke volume and cardiac output.

95XNmA.title: Löffler endocarditis
95XNmA.description: Endocarditis with infiltration of eosinophilic material. Part of the infiltrative/restrictive cardiomyopathy group. Associated with an elevated eosinophil cell count and hypereosinophilic syndrome. Causes diastolic heart failure with edema and dyspnea.

C5XqmA.title: Glycogenesis
C5XqmA.description: The process of glycogen synthesis from glucose by glycogenin, glycogen synthase, and glycogen branching enzyme. Triggered by high serum insulin concentrations.

y5Xd5A.title: Ritonavir
y5Xd5A.description: A protease inhibitor that inhibits the packaging and assembly of viruses. Used as part of an antiretroviral regimen for the treatment of HIV and hepatitis C. Also inhibits cytochrome P-450 and thus increases the concentration of other antiretrovirals (e.g., lopinavir) that are metabolized by this enzyme.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

A5XR5A.title: Darunavir
A5XR5A.description: A protease inhibitor that inhibits packaging and assembly of viruses. Used as part of an antiretroviral regimen for treatment of HIV.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

_5X55A.title: Sciatica
_5X55A.description: A nonspecific term usually used to describe low back pain that may radiate down the leg to the foot, i.e., along the sciatic nerve pathway. Typically caused by nerve root dysfunction, e.g., from degenerative disk disease.

media.title: Innervation of the lower extremity (dorsal view)

z5Xr5A.title: Dihydropteroate synthase
z5Xr5A.description: An enzyme that produces dihydropteroate, an intermediate metabolite in the folate synthesis pathway of bacteria. Targeted by sulfa drugs such as sulfamethoxazole and dapsone.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Sulfonamides and diaminopyrimidine

-5XD5A.title: Sympathetic nervous system
-5XD5A.description: A division of the autonomic nervous system responsible for stimulation of fight-or-flight activities, including mydriasis, bronchodilation, urethral sphincter contraction, ↑ lipolysis, and ↑ heart rate. The primary neurotransmitters involved in these processes are acetylcholine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system

media.title: Overview of somatic and autonomic motor pathways and neurotransmitters

ZMXZMA.title: Reverse pulsus paradoxus
ZMXZMA.description: A physical finding characterized by a pathologic increase in systolic and diastolic blood pressures during inspiration. Seen in patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) and patients receiving intermittent positive pressure ventilation (IPPV).

0MXeMA.title: Cereulide
0MXeMA.description: An enterotoxin produced by Bacillus cereus that is resistant to heat, acid, and proteases. It is typically found in foods containing starch and causes emesis 1-5 hours after consumption.

aMXQMA.title: Partial arginine vasopressin deficiency
aMXQMA.description: A polyuria-polydipsia syndrome caused by partial arginine vasopressin deficiency. Characterized by low urine osmolality that increases by ≥ 10% after desmopressin administration.

YMXnMA.title: Complete arginine vasopressin deficiency
YMXnMA.description: A polyuria-polydipsia syndrome caused by complete deficiency of arginine vasopressin. Characterized by low urine osmolality that increases by > 50% after desmopressin administration.

bMXHMA.title: Proteasome inhibitor
bMXHMA.description: A class of chemotherapeutic drugs that inhibits the ubiquitin-proteasome system, which is responsible for degrading proteins. Commonly used to treat multiple myeloma. Drugs in this class include bortezomib, carfilzomib, and ixazomib.

XMX9MA.title: Pyrophosphate
XMX9MA.description: An anion formed during the hydrolysis of ATP.

cMXanA.title: Somatostatinoma
cMXanA.description: A rare neuroendocrine tumor of δ-cell origin that is typically located in the pancreas or gastrointestinal tract and secretes somatostatin. Usually manifests with abdominal pain and weight loss in addition to the triad of diabetes mellitus/glucose intolerance, gallstones, and diarrhea/steatorrhea.

1MX2nA.title: Hemagglutinin
1MX2nA.description: A glycoprotein on the surface of influenza virions that binds to sialic acid residues on the respiratory epithelium. Following endocytosis, hemagglutinin causes fusion of the viral envelope with the host endosomal membrane. This protein is also the target of neutralizing antibodies against influenza.

WMXPnA.title: Sciatic nerve
WMXPnA.description: Composed of L4–S3 fibers, the sciatic nerve travels through the posterior compartment of the thigh before branching into the tibial and common peroneal nerve at the popliteal fossa. It provides motor innervation to the hamstrings and most of the lower leg musculature as well as sensory innervation to most of the lower leg and foot.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Innervation of the thigh
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

media.title: Innervation of the lower extremity (dorsal view)

dMXonA.title: Blister
dMXonA.description: A collection of fluid (e.g., serum, blood, pus) in the skin. Further divided by size into vesicles (< 1 cm) and bullae (> 1 cm).

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Primary skin lesions

eMXxnA.title: Chronic uric acid nephropathy
eMXxnA.description: A condition of chronic kidney disease caused by deposition of uric acid in the renal medulla. Seen in patients with chronic hyperuricemia. Manifests as progressive chronic renal failure.

2MXTLA.title: Interleukin-3
2MXTLA.description: A cytokine that supports the growth and differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells.

fMXkLA.title: Toll-like receptors
fMXkLA.description: A type of pattern recognition receptor expressed on sentinel cells. They are components of the innate immune system and play a crucial role in host defense against pathogens by recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and activating a signaling cascade that induces an immune response.

TMX6LA.title: Interleukin-5
TMX6LA.description: A cytokine secreted by mast cells that stimulates eosinophil proliferation and activation. Also secreted by T cells to promote B cell differentiation and class switching to IgA.

SMXyLA.title: Body (stomach)
SMXyLA.description: The largest region of the stomach, which connects the cardia and fundus to the pylorus. It has a medial lesser curvature and a lateral greater curvature.

hMXcoA.title: Gastric antrum
hMXcoA.description: The region of the pylorus that connects the body of the stomach to the pyloric canal.

media.title: Regions of the upper gastrointestinal tract

3MXSoA.title: Pylorus
3MXSoA.description: The most distal aspect of the stomach. Contains glands that secrete gastrin and somatostatin. Further subdivided into the proximal antrum and the distal pyloric canal (which houses the pyloric sphincter).

RMXloA.title: Lesser curvature of the stomach
RMXloA.description: The medial concave border of the stomach. Contains the right and left gastric arteries. The lesser omentum extends from the lesser curvature to the liver.

iMXJoA.title: Greater curvature of the stomach
iMXJoA.description: The lateral convex border of the stomach. Contains the right and left gastroepiploic arteries. The greater omentum extends from the greater curvature to cover the intestines.

QMXuoA.title: Lesser omentum
QMXuoA.description: A fold of peritoneum that extends from the lesser curvature of the stomach to the liver. Contains the gastrohepatic and hepatoduodenal ligaments.

jMX_oA.title: Greater omentum
jMX_oA.description: A component of visceral peritoneum that extends from the greater curvature of the stomach to cover the intestines. Contains the gastrosplenic ligament, gastrophrenic ligament, and gastrocolic ligament.

PMXWKA.title: Cholecystokinin
PMXWKA.description: A hormone secreted by I cells in the small intestine after a meal. Stimulates gallbladder contraction and secretion of pancreatic enzymes, relaxes the sphincter of Oddi, and inhibits gastric emptying in order to digest fats and proteins.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

kMXmKA.title: Agonist
kMXmKA.description: A molecule that binds and activates an enzyme or receptor to produce the maximum response that a receptor can elicit.

lMXvKA.title: Antisynthetase antibody
lMXvKA.description: An antibody directed against tRNA synthetase enzymes, including anti-Jo-1 antibodies. Found in patients with antisynthetase syndrome.

NMX-KA.title: Myxoma
NMX-KA.description: A benign, noncancerous tumor composed of gelatinous or mucoid connective tissue. Most commonly found in the heart.

mMXV6A.title: Dipeptidyl peptidase-4
mMXV6A.description: An enzyme expressed on most cell surfaces. Has several metabolic functions, including breakdown of incretins (e.g., GLP-1).

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

5MXi6A.title: Lineweaver-Burk plot
5MXi6A.description: A representation of enzyme kinetics in a linear graph based on the double reciprocal of the Michaelis-Menten equation. Relates the inverse of the substrate concentration (i.e., 1/[S]) to the inverse response rate (i.e., 1/velocity).

MMXM6A.title: Noncompetitive antagonist
MMXM6A.description: A molecule that decreases the activity of an enzyme or receptor by binding to a site other than the active site (allosteric site), or irreversibly at the orthosteric site (less common). With respect to receptor effects, it causes a reduction of maximum effect (lowered efficacy) that cannot be overcome by increasing the dose of the agonist. With respect to enzyme kinetics, it decreases the maximum reaction rate (Vmax) but does not decrease the Michaelis-Menten constant (Km).

nMX76A.title: Aldolase B
nMX76A.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the breakdown of fructose-1-phosphate to glyceraldehyde and dihydroxyacetone phosphate, a necessary step in the glycolytic-gluconeogenesis pathway. Deficiency of the enzyme results in hereditary fructose intolerance.

LMXw6A.title: Primary motor cortex
LMXw6A.description: A region of the brain located in the frontal cortex, anterior to the central sulcus. Controls motor function of the contralateral side of the body, which is somatotopically arranged in an inverted fashion from toe (medial side) to mouth (lateral side). A lesion in this area causes contralateral motor weakness.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

media.title: Lateral view of important areas of the brain

oMX0pA.title: Premotor cortex
oMX0pA.description: An area of the motor cortex that lies anterior to the primary motor cortex. Involved in the intention and planning of movement. Lesions to this area can cause apraxia.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

6MXjpA.title: Broca area
6MXjpA.description: An area of the brain located in the inferior frontal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere. Involved in speech production. Lesions in this area cause expressive aphasia.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

pMXLpA.title: Primary visual cortex
pMXLpA.description: The primary processing site of visual information. Located on the medial aspect of the occipital lobe and receives visual information from the lateral geniculate nuclei, pretectal nuclei, and superior colliculi.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

qMXCpA.title: Secondary visual cortex
qMXCpA.description: A visual association area located in the occipital lobe. Receives input from the primary visual cortex and is responsible for the integration of visual properties, including color, position in space, and illusory contours. Damage to this region can result in visual hallucinations.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

IMXYJA.title: Somatosensory association cortex
IMXYJA.description: The region of the parietal lobe cortex that is responsible for the integration of palpatory sensory information. Enables pattern recognition.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

rMXfJA.title: Visual association cortex
rMXfJA.description: The region of the parietal lobe cortex that is responsible for the integration of visual sensory information. Enables pattern recognition.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

7MX4JA.title: Primary auditory cortex
7MX4JA.description: A region of the temporal lobe where contralateral auditory information is processed. Neurons are organized tonotopically based on the frequency of sound they respond to.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

media.title: Lateral view of important areas of the brain

HMXKJA.title: Wernicke area
HMXKJA.description: An area of the brain located in the posterior section of the superior temporal gyrus in the dominant hemisphere. Part of the auditory association cortex. Involved in written and spoken language comprehension. Lesion to this area causes receptive aphasia.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

sMXtJA.title: Functional antagonist
sMXtJA.description: A molecule that inhibits the effect of an agonist through a separate receptor. It has no effect on the receptor or enzyme that the agonist binds.

FMXgqA.title: Parietal lobe
FMXgqA.description: A major lobe of the human brain that is located posterior to the central sulcus. Involved in processing sensory information. Contains the primary somatosensory cortex, the somatosensory association cortex, and the visual association cortex.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

media.title: Lateral view of the cerebral lobes

uMXpqA.title: Partial agonist
uMXpqA.description: A molecule that binds an enzyme or receptor at the same site as a full agonist. It does not possess the same efficacy as the full agonist, but competes for the binding site and thus also has an antagonistic effect.

EMX8qA.title: Lentiform nucleus
EMX8qA.description: A structure in the brain that consists of the putamen and globus pallidus in the basal ganglia.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

vMXAqA.title: Subthalamic nucleus
vMXAqA.description: A small nucleus that is part of the basal ganglia. Damage to this part of the brain results in contralateral hemiballismus.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

DMX1IA.title: Lateral nucleus
DMX1IA.description: A region of the hypothalamus that regulates hunger. Damage to this area causes anorexia, starvation, and failure to thrive. Stimulated by ghrelin and inhibited by leptin.

wMXhIA.title: Ventromedial nucleus
wMXhIA.description: A hypothalamic nucleus that regulates satiety and is stimulated by leptin. Damage to this region can result in hyperphagia and obesity.

CMXqIA.title: Suprachiasmatic nucleus
CMXqIA.description: A hypothalamic nucleus that regulates circadian rhythm in response to light input from the retina. Damage to this region causes abnormalities of the sleep-wake cycle.

xMXEIA.title: Posterior nucleus
xMXEIA.description: A hypothalamic nucleus that regulates conservation of heat via the sympathetic nervous system. Damage to this region results in hypothermia.

BMXzIA.title: Paraventricular nucleus
BMXzIA.description: A hypothalamic nucleus that, along with the supraoptic nucleus, regulates water balance via the effects of antidiuretic hormone and oxytocin. Damage to this region can result in diabetes insipidus.

yMXdrA.title: Preoptic area
yMXdrA.description: A region of the anterior hypothalamus that is responsible for thermoregulation, secretion of GnRH, and generation of thirst sensation, and plays a significant role in sexual behavior.

_MX5rA.title: Ventral posterolateral nucleus
_MX5rA.description: The thalamic relay center for the spinothalamic tract, which conveys all sensory information from the contralateral side of the body. Efferent output projects to the primary somatosensory cortex.

zMXrrA.title: Ventral posteromedial nucleus
zMXrrA.description: The thalamic relay center for the trigeminal and gustatory pathway, which receives sensory information from the face and oral cavity. Receives afferent input from the trigeminal nucleus and projects to the somatosensory cortex.

-MXDrA.title: Medial geniculate nucleus
-MXDrA.description: The thalamic relay center of the auditory pathway. Receives afferent input from the inferior colliculus and projects to the primary auditory cortex.

ZnXZ7A.title: Ventral lateral nucleus
ZnXZ7A.description: A collection of neurons in the anterolateral region of the thalamus that receive afferent input from the basal ganglia and cerebellum and send efferent impulses to the motor cortex. Involved in movement planning and coordination as well as motor learning.

0nXe7A.title: Hippocampal formation
0nXe7A.description: A brain structure that consists of the hippocampus, dentate gyrus, and entorhinal cortex.

YnXn7A.title: Amygdala
YnXn7A.description: A structure of the limbic system located deep in the medial part of the temporal lobe, anterior to the hippocampus. Receives signals from the hypothalamus, cerebral cortex, and the olfactory cortex. Also relays emotional reactions and is involved in the recognition of emotional facial expressions.

bnXH7A.title: Cingulate gyrus
bnXH7A.description: A part of the limbic system located at the medial aspect of the cerebral hemisphere above the corpus callosum. Involved in emotion, behavior, learning, and memory.

XnX97A.title: Anterior thalamic nuclei
XnX97A.description: A collection of neuronal cell bodies in the anterior part of the thalamus that can be divided into the anteroventral, anteromedial, and anterodorsal nuclei. Receive input from the mammillary bodies as well as the hippocampus and project to the cingulate gyrus. Considered a part of the limbic system and is involved in the Papez circuit.

cnXaHA.title: Hippocampus
cnXaHA.description: A curved, seahorse-shaped collection of neurons located within the medial temporal lobe on the floor of the lateral ventricle. Part of the limbic system. Plays an important role in memory formation and emotional response.

1nX2HA.title: Dentate gyrus
1nX2HA.description: A part of the hippocampal formation located in the temporal lobe medial to the hippocampus. Involved in the generation of memories.

dnXoHA.title: Direct pathway of the basal ganglia
dnXoHA.description: A neuronal circuit involved in the coordination of movement. Dopamine release from the substantia nigra stimulates D1 receptors in the striatum, which leads to GABA release that inhibits the globus pallidus internus. Subsequent disinhibition of the thalamus leads to increased movement.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

VnXGHA.title: Indirect pathway of the basal ganglia
VnXGHA.description: A neuronal circuit involved in the coordination of movement. Dopamine release from the substantia nigra stimulates D2 receptors in the striatum, which inhibits GABA release. Subsequent disinhibition of the globus pallidus externus leads to GABA release, which in turn inhibits the subthalamic nucleus. This leads to decreased stimulation of the globus pallidus internus, which leads to disinhibition of the thalamus and increased movement.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

enXxHA.title: Dorsomedial nucleus
enXxHA.description: A thalamic nucleus that receives input from the temporal cortex, substantia nigra, and amygdaloid nucleus and projects to the prefrontal cortex and the intralaminar nuclei. Part of the limbic system.

UnXbsA.title: Intralaminar nuclei
UnXbsA.description: A group of neurons that can be subdivided into an anterior (rostral) and a posterior (caudal) portion. Thought to play a role in awareness and arousal.

2nXTsA.title: Familial hypertriglyceridemia
2nXTsA.description: An autosomal-dominant condition characterized by markedly increased triglyceride levels in the serum. Associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis.

TnX6sA.title: Intestinal schistosomiasis
TnX6sA.description: A form of chronic schistosomiasis characterized by chronic granulomatous inflammation in response to the deposition of Schistosoma eggs in the gastrointestinal tract. Can cause abdominal pain, diarrhea, and bleeding. Often associated with hepatosplenic schistosomiasis.

gnXFsA.title: Acute schistosomiasis syndrome
gnXFsA.description: A systemic condition caused by a hypersensitivity reaction to Schistosoma antigens. Typically develops 3-8 weeks after initial infection and is self-limited. Manifestations include a serum sickness-like reaction (e.g., fever, rash, myalgias), cough, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and eosinophilia.

SnXysA.title: Chronic schistosomiasis
SnXysA.description: A condition characterized by chronic granulomatous inflammation in response to the deposition of eggs of the trematode Schistosoma. Can affect the gastrointestinal, pulmonary, genitourinary, and central nervous systems.

hnXcGA.title: δ-cells
hnXcGA.description: A somatostatin-producing cell that can be found throughout the gastrointestinal tract (e.g., stomach, intestine, pancreas).

3nXSGA.title: Parafollicular cell
3nXSGA.description: A calcitonin-secreting cell found between thyroid follicles. Cell of origin of medullary thyroid carcinoma.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Microscopic anatomy

media.title: Microscopic anatomy of the thyroid gland

RnXlGA.title: Adiponectin
RnXlGA.description: A hormone produced by adipose tissue. Modulates insulin sensitivity, enhances fatty acid breakdown and has anti-inflammatory effects. Inversely related to adiposity.

QnXuGA.title: Fructokinase
QnXuGA.description: A phosphotransferase enzyme that catalyzes the first step in fructose metabolism, the conversion of fructose to fructose-1-phosphate. Deficiency leads to essential fructosuria.

jnX_GA.title: Hexokinase
jnX_GA.description: A phosphotransferase adds a phosphate group to a six carbon sugar, most notably glucose (to produce glucose-6-phosphate) or fructose (to produce fructose-6-phosphate). Unlike glucokinase, this enzyme phosphorylates glucose regardless of insulin or glucose levels and is inhibited by glucose-6-phosphate.

PnXWtA.title: Reducing substance
PnXWtA.description: A chemical element or compound that can donate electrons (i.e., become oxidized) in a reduction-oxidation reaction. Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism can result in the presence of reducing sugars in the urine.

4nX3tA.title: Glycolysis
4nX3tA.description: An oxygen-independent sequence of chemical reactions that converts glucose to pyruvate and produces ATP and NADH as byproducts.

knXmtA.title: Brachial plexus
knXmtA.description: A bundle of nerve fibers that arise from the spinal cord nerve roots C5-T1. Terminal branches include the musculocutaneous, axillary, radial, median, and ulnar nerves. Responsible for innervation of the shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

OnXItA.title: Classic galactosemia
OnXItA.description: An autosomal recessive, congenital defect caused by absence of galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase, the enzyme responsible for the final conversion of galactose to glucose. Classically manifests with jaundice, vomiting, hepatosplenomegaly, infantile cataracts, and failure to thrive. Affected patients are at increased risk for E. coli sepsis.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Galactosemia

lnXvtA.title: Long thoracic nerve
lnXvtA.description: A peripheral nerve in the upper limb that arises from the brachial plexus (nerve roots: C5–C7). The long thoracic nerve innervates the serratus anterior muscle, which is responsible for protraction of the scapula. Damage to this nerve results in a characteristic winged scapula.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

NnX-tA.title: Miglitol
NnX-tA.description: An alpha-glucosidase inhibitor that is used for glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

mnXVFA.title: Atrial natriuretic peptide
mnXVFA.description: A peptide hormone released from atrial myocytes in response to increased stretch on the atrium. Leads to vasodilation and decreased renal sodium reabsorption. Also promotes diuresis via afferent renal arteriole dilation and efferent renal arteriole constriction. Contributes to aldosterone escape in patients with primary hyperaldosteronism.

MnXMFA.title: Glycation
MnXMFA.description: The nonenzymatic attachment of a carbohydrate to a protein, which forms a glycoprotein (e.g., glycation of hemoglobin to form HbA1c in patients with diabetes). Can affect protein function.

nnX7FA.title: Ferroportin
nnX7FA.description: A transmembrane protein that transports intracellular iron out of the cell and into the bloodstream. Found primarily in duodenal enterocytes (specifically the basolateral membrane), hepatocytes, macrophages, and adipocytes. It is inhibited by hepcidin, which is secreted in response to sufficient iron levels.

LnXwFA.title: Degeneracy (genetic code)
LnXwFA.description: A property of the genetic code illustrated by the diversity of codons that specify a single amino acid during translation. Reduces the damage caused by point mutations at the third position of a base triplet (the wobble position)

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

onX08A.title: Universality (genetic code)
onX08A.description: A property of the genetic code illustrated by the near-universal correspondence of codons to the same amino acids among almost all living organisms.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

KnXU8A.title: Non-overlapping (genetic code)
KnXU8A.description: A property of the genetic code illustrated by the reading of genetic information from a fixed starting point as a continuous sequence of bases. Codons are non-overlapping; each nucleotide belongs to only one codon, and after the codon triplet is read, the reading frame shifts to the next codon.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

6nXj8A.title: Open reading frame
6nXj8A.description: A segment in the sequence of nucleotides of a single-stranded nucleic acid that can be translated into amino acids. Contains a start codon, a stretch of codons that encode a protein, and a stop codon.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

pnXL8A.title: Unambiguity (genetic code)
pnXL8A.description: A property of the genetic code illustrated by the specificity of each codon for one single amino acid.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Genetic code

JnXs8A.title: Complement component 1q
JnXs8A.description: A protein complex involved in both innate and adaptive immunity. Activates the complement system and aids in the clearance of cell debris. Levels of complement component 1q are typically low in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus. About ⅓ of lupus patients have anti-C1q antibodies.

qnXC8A.title: Phenylalanine hydroxylase
qnXC8A.description: An enzyme that hydroxylates the aromatic ring of phenylalanine, which is needed to produce tyrosine. Deficiency in this enzyme (or its cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin) results in phenylketonuria.

InXYuA.title: Germinal center
InXYuA.description: A site within a follicle of a secondary lymphoid organ (e.g., lymph nodes, spleen) where B cell proliferation and differentiation as well as immunoglobulin class switching occurs. The functioning of cells within the germinal center depends on interaction with T cells.

rnXfuA.title: Cytochrome P450 inhibitor
rnXfuA.description: A substance that inhibits the cytochrome P450 system, which leads to increased serum concentrations of any drug metabolized by the system (e.g., warfarin). Examples include sodium valproate, isoniazid, cimetidine, ketoconazole, acute alcohol use, and chloramphenicol.

destinations.label: Fundamentals of pharmacology → Drug interactions and the cytochrome P450 system

7nX4uA.title: Cytochrome P450 inducer
7nX4uA.description: A substance that induces the cytochrome P450 system, which leads to decreased serum concentrations of any drug metabolized by the system (e.g., warfarin). Examples include carbamazepine, rifampicin, chronic alcohol use, phenytoin, griseofulvin, and phenobarbital.

destinations.label: Fundamentals of pharmacology → Drug interactions and the cytochrome P450 system

HnXKuA.title: Contact precautions
HnXKuA.description: A set of measures used for the care of patients with suspected or confirmed infection with pathogens that spread via direct contact or fomites. Includes patient isolation or cohorting, usage of gloves and gowns upon entering the patient's room, frequent cleaning of surfaces, and single patient use medical equipment.  Always performed in addition to standard precautions.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Isolation precautions

snXtuA.title: Myeloperoxidase deficiency
snXtuA.description: An autosomal recessive condition in which deficient or absent myeloperoxidase predisposes to recurrent Candida infections; more severe immunocompromise is rare. Diagnosis can be made with a positive (normal) nitroblue tetrazolium test and/or immunohistochemical or genetic testing

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital neutrophil and phagocyte disorders

GnXBuA.title: Nidogen
GnXBuA.description: Ubiquitous glycoprotein that constitutes an intrinsic component of the basement membrane. Responsible for connecting networks of collagen and laminin.

tnXXEA.title: Secondary hyperaldosteronism
tnXXEA.description: A condition characterized by increased serum aldosterone concentrations secondary to increased activity of renin. Manifestations include hypertension and symptoms of hypokalemia (headaches, fatigue, muscle weakness).

FnXgEA.title: Loading dose
FnXgEA.description: An initial dose of a drug given before starting a longer treatment course. This is done to quickly get the serum concentration to therapeutic levels before beginning a maintenance dose. The formula for calculating loading dose is (Cp x Vd) / F, where Cp = peak plasma concentration in units/mL, Vd = volume of distribution, and F = bioavailability.

8nXOEA.title: Branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase
8nXOEA.description: An enzyme that metabolizes branched-chain amino acids (i.e., valine, leucine, isoleucine). Decreased activity of this enzyme causes maple syrup urine disease.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Maple syrup urine disease

unXpEA.title: Disulfiram
unXpEA.description: A drug that inhibits acetaldehyde dehydrogenase and leads to reduced metabolism of ethanol with increased accumulation of the unpleasant intermediate acetaldehyde, thereby amplifying negative symptoms of intoxication (e.g., nausea, vomiting) and  increasing sensitivity to alcohol.

destinations.label: Alcohol use disorder → Initiation of pharmacotherapy

EnX8EA.title: Lipoic acid
EnX8EA.description: An essential cofactor for enzymes and antioxidant involved in aerobic metabolism, most notably pyruvate dehydrogenase complex and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase. Inhibited by arsenic.

vnXAEA.title: Acid dissociation constant
vnXAEA.description: A measure of acid strength. The lower the pKa of a substance, the more easily a proton is lost and the more acidic it is.

DnX1vA.title: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase
DnX1vA.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the carboxylation of propionyl-CoA into methylmalonyl-CoA in the presence of ATP and biotin. Propionyl-CoA is a byproduct of odd-chain fatty acid and essential amino acids (valine, isoleucine, methionine, threonine) degradation.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

wnXhvA.title: Enterohepatic circulation
wnXhvA.description: The circulation of hepatic metabolites (e.g., bile acids, bilirubin, drugs), which are first excreted into the intestine, then reabsorbed by enterocytes, and then transported back to the liver. Increased enterohepatic circulation, which can occur in conditions associated with decreased stool passage (e.g., breast milk jaundice, cystic fibrosis, Hirschsprung disease), can result in unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia.

9nXNvA.title: Tectum
9nXNvA.description: A structure located posterior to the cerebral aqueduct that forms the roof of the midbrain. Contains the superior and inferior colliculi.

CnXqvA.title: Tegmentum
CnXqvA.description: A structure located between the tectum and the base of the midbrain. Contains the nuclei of cranial nerves III–V, the red nucleus, and the substantia nigra. Involved in the modulation of extrapyramidal motor function.

xnXEvA.title: Crus cerebri
xnXEvA.description: The anterior portion of the cerebral peduncle. Forms the base of the midbrain. Contains motor tracts that travel from the cerebral cortex to the pons and the spinal cord (corticospinal, corticopontine, and corticobulbar tracts).

ynXdDA.title: Periaqueductal gray matter
ynXdDA.description: A structure consisting of gray matter that surrounds the cerebral aqueduct in the midbrain. Part of the nociceptive system. Plays a major role in the perception and modulation of pain.

_nX5DA.title: Red nucleus
_nX5DA.description: A pair of oval-shaped structures located in the midbrain that, together with the cerebellum, function to maintain muscular tone, motor coordination, and gait. Appear red on gross inspection because of their high iron content. Afferents arise from the dentate and interposed cerebellar nuclei; efferents go to the spinal cord (rubrospinal tract) and the olivary bodies of the medulla (rubro-olivary tract).

znXrDA.title: Cochlear nuclei
znXrDA.description: The nuclei located in the pons that receive auditory input from the organ of Corti (first-order neurons) and are part of the auditory pathway. Further divided into a ventral and dorsal group. They project to the ipsilateral and contralateral lateral lemnisci.

-nXDDA.title: Trapezoid body
-nXDDA.description: A transverse pathway located in the ventral aspect of the pons, posterior to the pyramidal tracts. Formed by a decussation of the ventral cochlear fibers and part of the auditory pathway. Contains fibers from cranial nerve IV, the acoustic striae, and the medial lemniscus. Thought to play a role in sound localization.

ZLXZwA.title: Superior olivary nucleus
ZLXZwA.description: A group of brainstem nuclei located in the pons at the level of the trapezoid body. Part of the auditory pathway (third-order neuron). Relays auditory signals from the cochlear nuclei and forms the first major point of integration of auditory information from both ears.

0LXewA.title: Corticopontine tract
0LXewA.description: A nerve fiber tract that runs from the cerebral cortex to the pontine nuclei in the pons. Contains frontopontine, parietopontine, temporopontine, and occipitopontine fibers. Part of the corticopontocerebellar pathway.

aLXQwA.title: Pontine nuclei
aLXQwA.description: A collection of neurons in the pons that convey information from the motor cortex to the cerebellum regarding movement of the contralateral limbs.

YLXnwA.title: Locus coeruleus
YLXnwA.description: A set of two pontine nuclei located near the pontomesencephalic junction. Largest group of noradrenergic neurons in the central nervous system. An increase in norepinepherine production is associated with anxiety disorders while a decrease is linked to depression.

bLXHwA.title: Heart rate
bLXHwA.description: The number of heart contractions per minute (beats per minute). Normal heart rate at rest is 60–100/minute.

XLX9wA.title: Medial circumflex femoral artery
XLX9wA.description: An artery that arises from the profunda femoris artery (posteromedial side) and, along with lateral femoral circumflex artery, supplies the head and neck of the femur. Damage or trauma to this artery can result in avascular necrosis of the femoral head.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Hip joint

1LX29A.title: Enterochromaffin-like cell
1LX29A.description: A type of neuroendocrine cell in the gastric mucosa. In response to gastrin released by G-cells, enterochromaffin-like cells release histamine that stimulates release of gastric acid by parietal cells.

WLXP9A.title: Vitamin K dependent factors
WLXP9A.description: The coagulation factors II, VII, IX, and X, which are involved in secondary hemostasis. Require vitamin K for synthesis and activation via gamma-glutamyl carboxylation.

dLXo9A.title: Apolipoprotein B-100
dLXo9A.description: An apolipoprotein that mediates endocytosis of LDL by binding to the LDL receptor on hepatic and extrahepatic tissues. Defective apoB-100 causes type II familial hyperlipidemia.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

VLXG9A.title: Thyrotoxic myopathy
VLXG9A.description: A condition of muscle weakness, pain, and atrophy associated with hyperthyroidism (e.g., from Graves disease, thyroiditis). Typically affects proximal muscles (e.g., hip flexors, quadriceps) more than distal muscles. Can develop acutely or several weeks to months after the onset of hyperthyroidism.

eLXx9A.title: Anhidrosis
eLXx9A.description: A condition of diminished or absent sweating in one or more parts of the body. Associated with Horner syndrome, autoimmune diseases (Sjögren syndrome) and certain drugs (e.g., anticholinergics).

2LXTCA.title: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
2LXTCA.description: The most common type of dilated cardiomyopathy. Caused by myocardial ischemia due to a narrowing of the coronary arteries. (e.g., from atherosclerosis, vasospasm, and/or inflammation of the coronary arteries). Manifests with fatigue, dyspnea, dizziness, and palpitations. Can result in sudden cardiac death.

fLXkCA.title: Adrenergic receptor
fLXkCA.description: A G protein-coupled receptor class that binds catecholamines (norepinephrine, epinephrine). Responsible for general stimulation of the sympathetic nervous system.

TLX6CA.title: Effective refractory period
TLX6CA.description: An interval of time during which stimuli cannot generate a new action potential in a depolarized cardiac cell. The sodium channels are in an inactivated state until the cell fully repolarizes.

gLXFCA.title: Vulnerable child syndrome
gLXFCA.description: A condition characterized by excessive parental concern about the health of a child whom the parents view to be vulnerable. Can result in separation difficulties, sleep difficulties, and other psychosocial challenges. Children with extensive medical issues (e.g., long stays in a NICU) are at increased risk for this condition.

destinations.label: Somatic symptom and related disorders → Differential diagnoses

SLXyCA.title: Air crescent sign
SLXyCA.description: A chest x-ray or CT finding in which a crescent-shaped lucency surrounds a radiopaque mass. Most commonly associated with pulmonary aspergillosis.

hLXcxA.title: Thromboxane A2
hLXcxA.description: An arachidonic acid derivative and potent platelet aggregator and vasoconstrictor. Inhibition of thromboxane A2 synthesis in thrombocytes is responsible for aspirin's antiplatelet effect.

3LXSxA.title: Hyperoxaluria
3LXSxA.description: An elevated level of oxalic acid in the urine. Causes include increased intake of dietary oxalate (e.g., from beets, beans, energy drinks, soy, dark green vegetables) and/or vitamin C (which is metabolized to oxalate),  bile acid malabsorption and/or chronic diarrhea, ethylene glycol poisoning, and pyridoxine deficiency. Increases the risk of developing calcium oxalate stones.

RLXlxA.title: Idiopathic hypercalciuria
RLXlxA.description: A condition of elevated urinary calcium levels despite normal serum calcium levels. Caused by increased intestinal calcium absorption, bone resorption, and/or decreased renal tubular reabsorption. Predisposes to calcium stone formation.

iLXJxA.title: Hypocitraturia
iLXJxA.description: A decreased level of citrate in the urine. Usually caused by renal tubular acidosis; also caused by chronic diarrhea and chronic use of carbonic anhydrase inhibitors. Predisposes to calcium stone formation because citrate forms soluble complexes with calcium.

QLXuxA.title: Uterine hypoplasia
QLXuxA.description: A failure of the uterus to develop adequately in utero. Etiologies include hypogonadism and Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome.

jLX_xA.title: Linitis plastica
jLX_xA.description: A morphological feature of gastric cancer (mostly diffuse type of gastric adenocarcinoma) characterized by a thickened and leathery stomach wall. Histology classically reveals signet ring cells.

PLXWBA.title: High altitude illness
PLXWBA.description: A group of syndromes that can occur when ascending to high altitudes (typically over 8000 feet or 2500 m). Includes acute mountain sickness, high-altitude cerebral edema, and high-altitude pulmonary edema.

kLXmBA.title: Acclimatization
kLXmBA.description: A physiologic process that is triggered by hypoxemia and tissue hypoxia caused by a lack of oxygen at high altitudes. Oxygen deprivation triggers respiratory alkalosis (hyperventilation) to increase blood oxygen levels. Erythropoiesis is stimulated to increase hematocrit and oxygen-carrying capacity. 2,3-BPG levels increase to enhance Hb-O₂ disassociation in peripheral tissues, and renal excretion of HCO₃⁻ increases.

lLXvBA.title: Glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase
lLXvBA.description: An enzyme that reversibly converts dihydroxyacetone phosphate to glycerol-3-phosphate. It provides electrons for the mitochondrial electron transport chain and links carbohydrate metabolism to lipid metabolism. Inhibitors of this enzyme such as biguanides (metformin) are used for treatment of diabetes.

mLXVyA.title: Abetalipoproteinemia
mLXVyA.description: A rare, autosomal-recessive disorder characterized by deficiency of apolipoproteins, which results in low serum concentrations of chylomicrons, LDL, and VLDL. Manifests in early infancy with failure to thrive and fat malabsorption.

nLX7yA.title: RNA polymerase II
nLX7yA.description: A eukaryotic enzyme that transcribes mRNA from DNA after binding to the promoter region.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  RNA polymerases and transcription factors

LLXwyA.title: Methylmalonic acidemia
LLXwyA.description: An autosomal recessive condition caused by impaired metabolism of methylmalonic acid. Manifestations include metabolic acidosis, dehydration, lethargy, seizures, hypotonia, hyperammonemia, hypoglycemia, and failure to thrive.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Organic acidemias

6LXjAA.title: Interstitium
6LXjAA.description: The space between cells where extracellular fluid collects. Takes part in fluid exchange with capillaries and contains fluid that eventually enters the lymphatic system.

pLXLAA.title: Rexinoid
pLXLAA.description: An analog of the retinoid X receptor (RXR), which is involved in several pathways that regulate cell growth and differentiation.

JLXsAA.title: Infundibular stalk
JLXsAA.description: The connection between the median eminence of the hypothalamus and the posterior pituitary. Contains the axons of the posterior pituitary neurons. Damage to the stalk leads to loss of posterior pituitary hormones (oxytocin and ADH). Hyperprolactinemia can also result because lactotrophs in the anterior pituitary no longer receive inhibitory signals from the hypothalamus.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamus and pituitary gland

ILXY_A.title: Bronchopulmonary segment
ILXY_A.description: A segment of lung tissue that is supplied by a segmental bronchus and a segmental branch of the pulmonary artery. Surrounded by a connective tissue septum (intersegmental septum). Contains a branch of the pulmonary vein.

GLXB_A.title: Pulmonary veins
GLXB_A.description: The blood vessels that carry oxygenated blood from the lung to the left atrium.

uLXpzA.title: Cyclooxygenase-2
uLXpzA.description: An enzyme expressed in inflammatory cells and vascular endothelium. Converts arachidonic acid to cyclic endoperoxides, which serve as precursors for thromboxane A2, prostaglandins, and prostacyclin. Inhibited by NSAIDs and selective COX-2 inhibitors (e.g., celecoxib).

ELX8zA.title: Arachidonic acid
ELX8zA.description: A polyunsaturated fatty acid derived from membrane phospholipids. Serves as the precursor for leukotrienes, thromboxane A2, prostaglandins, and prostacyclin.

vLXAzA.title: Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase
vLXAzA.description: An enzyme involved in de novo pyrimidine synthesis that converts dihydroorotate to orotate (orotic acid). Inhibited by leflunomide.

DLX1-A.title: Orotate
DLX1-A.description: An intermediate in the de novo synthesis of pyrimidine.

wLXh-A.title: Dihydroorotate
wLXh-A.description: An intermediate in the de novo synthesis of pyrimidine.

CLXq-A.title: India ink staining
CLXq-A.description: A type of negative stain with carbon that is most commonly used to identify organisms with a polysaccharide capsule (e.g., Cryptococcus neoformans). The capsule is not penetrated by the ink and appears as a halo around the organism against a dark background.

xLXE-A.title: Actin
xLXE-A.description: A cytoskeletal microfilament involved in cellular processes such as muscle contraction, cell motility, and cell division.

BLXz-A.title: Hypoalbuminemia
BLXz-A.description: A condition of decreased serum albumin concentrations. Etiologies include proteinuria and decreased hepatic albumin synthesis. Leads to edema and transudative pleural effusions.

yLXdZ_.title: Tuberculoid leprosy
yLXdZ_.description: A type of leprosy characterized by hypesthetic, hairless, cutaneous granulomas and asymmetric enlargement of peripheral nerves. In contrast to lepromatous leprosy, characterized by a largely Th1-type immune response and low bacterial load.

ALXRZ_.title: Lepromatous leprosy
ALXRZ_.description: A communicable type of leprosy characterized by multiple, diffuse cutaneous lesions and late-developing, symmetrical anesthesia. In contrast to tuberculoid leprosy, characterized by humoral Th2 response and high bacterial load.

zLXrZ_.title: Skene duct cyst
zLXrZ_.description: A retention cyst that results from obstruction, accumulation of fluid, and cystic dilation of the ducts that drain the Skene (paraurethral) glands. Located on the anterior vaginal wall near the opening of the urethra.

-LXDZ_.title: Vaginal polyp
