-LXDZ_.description: A benign mucosal proliferation that contains a core of connective tissue and is covered by squamous epithelium. Arises from the mucosa of the vaginal wall and can protrude from the vaginal introitus.

ZoXZ0_.title: Odd-chain fatty acid
ZoXZ0_.description: A type of fatty acid with an odd number of carbon atoms. β-oxidation breaks down odd-chain fatty acids into acetyl-CoA and propionyl CoA.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

0oXe0_.title: Gingivitis
0oXe0_.description: A reversible form of periodontal disease characterized by redness, inflammation, and bleeding gums. Risk factors include poor oral hygiene, diabetes mellitus, smoking, older age, nutritional deficiencies, and the use of certain medications.

aoXQ0_.title: Glossitis
aoXQ0_.description: An inflammation of the tongue characterized by a smooth surface and redness. Can be a sign of local conditions (e.g., allergic reaction, injury) or systemic conditions (e.g., Sjögren syndrome, vitamin deficiencies).

YoXn0_.title: Ligamentum arteriosum
YoXn0_.description: A remnant of the obliterate ductus arteriosus that connects to the aorta (typically the aortic arch) and the left pulmonary artery.

destinations.label: Prenatal and postnatal physiology →  Fetal circulation

boXH0_.title: Anti-DNase B antibody
boXH0_.description: An antibody used as a marker for recent skin and/or throat infection by group A beta-hemolytic streptococci (GAS). Increased anti-DNase B antibody titers can be used to identify recent GAS skin infection, particularly if ASO titers are falsely negative.

XoX90_.title: Drug efficacy
XoX90_.description: The maximal effect a drug is capable of producing. A partial agonist has lower efficacy than a full agonist.

coXaa_.title: Macroorchidism
coXaa_.description: A condition of abnormally large testicles. Classically associated with fragile X syndrome.

destinations.label: Rare inherited syndromes → Fragile X syndrome

1oX2a_.title: Linagliptin
1oX2a_.description: A DPP-4 inhibitor used for glycemic control in patients with diabetes.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

WoXPa_.title: Amylin analogs
WoXPa_.description: A class of antidiabetic medications that mimic the effects of the pancreatic hormone amylin. Amylin slows gastric empyting, promotes satiety, and decreases postprandial glucagon release.

eoXxa_.title: Xanthopsia
eoXxa_.description: A visual abnormality in which there is a predominance of yellow in vision. Classically associated with digoxin toxicity.

UoXbY_.title: FMR1 gene
UoXbY_.description: The gene responsible for producing FMR1 protein. This protein shuttles mRNA into the cell, which is crucial to neural development. The accumulation of CGG repeats in FMR1 leads to gene silencing and causes fragile X syndrome.

destinations.label: Rare inherited syndromes → Fragile X syndrome

2oXTY_.title: Short gastric arteries
2oXTY_.description: A collection of arteries that arise from the splenic artery and supply the gastric fundus and greater curvature of the stomach.

foXkY_.title: Left gastroepiploic artery
foXkY_.description: A branch of the splenic artery that supplies the greater curvature of the stomach and anastomoses with the right gastroepiploic artery.

media.title: Arterial supply of the gastrointestinal tract

ToX6Y_.title: Right gastroepiploic artery
ToX6Y_.description: A branch of the gastroduodenal artery that supplies the greater curvature of the stomach and anastomoses with the left gastroepiploic artery.

goXFY_.title: Left gastric artery
goXFY_.description: A branch of the celiac artery that supplies the lesser curvature of the stomach and anastomoses with the right gastric artery.

SoXyY_.title: Gastroduodenal artery
SoXyY_.description: A branch of the common hepatic artery that gives rise to the right gastroepiploic artery and the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery. Supplies the pylorus of the stomach, proximal duodenum, and the head of the pancreas.

hoXcb_.title: Common hepatic artery
hoXcb_.description: A branch of the celiac artery that gives rise to the right gastric artery, gastroduodenal artery, and proper hepatic artery.

3oXSb_.title: Superior pancreaticoduodenal artery
3oXSb_.description: A branch of the gastroduodenal artery that supplies the duodenum and pancreas. Further divides into an anterior and posterior portion. Its branches anastomose with the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery.

media.title: Arterial supply of the duodenum, pancreas, and spleen

RoXlb_.title: Right gastric artery
RoXlb_.description: A branch of the proper hepatic artery (or less commonly the common hepatic artery) that supplies the lesser curvature of the stomach.

ioXJb_.title: Posterior gastric artery
ioXJb_.description: A branch of the splenic artery that supplies the posterior gastric wall and fundus of the stomach.

QoXub_.title: Heteroplasmy
QoXub_.description: The heterogeneity of mitochondrial DNA within a cell. Caused by the selective distribution of mitochondria with mutated DNA and can result in variable expression of diseases that follow mitochondrial inheritance.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Other types of inheritance

joX_b_.title: Glycerol 3-phosphate
joX_b_.description: The phosphoric ester of glycerol. An important component of phospholipids. Combines with three fatty acids to form triglycerides.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

PoXWX_.title: Dihydroxyacetone phosphate
PoXWX_.description: An intermediate of glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. Converted to glycerol-3 phosphate during the synthesis of triglycerides.

4oX3X_.title: BCL-2
4oX3X_.description: An antiapoptotic protein that inhibits the intrinsic pathway of apoptosis by maintaining impermeability of the mitochondrial membrane. Translocation t(14,18) can lead to overexpression of Bcl-2, which results in inhibition of apoptosis. Alterations in Bcl-2 are associated with follicular lymphomas and diffuse large B cell lymphoma.

koXmX_.title: Locus heterogeneity
koXmX_.description: The production of identical phenotypes or disorders by mutations in genes located in different chromosomal loci. Examples of such disorders include hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, osteogenesis imperfecta, familial hypercholesterolemia, and retinitis pigmentosa.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

OoXIX_.title: Hyperinsulinism
OoXIX_.description: A condition of elevated blood insulin levels. Hyperinsulinism associated with hyperglycemia is caused by reduced peripheral insulin sensitivity (e.g., from type 2 diabetes mellitus). Hyperinsulinism associated with hypoglycemia is caused by excess endogenous insulin secretion (e.g., from insulinoma, Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome).

loXvX_.title: L-selectin
loXvX_.description: A cell adhesion molecule found on the surface of lymphocytes. Facilitates attachment to endothelial cells.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

NoX-X_.title: 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase
NoX-X_.description: An enzyme that converts cortisone into its active form cortisol, and vice versa, thereby regulating local glucocorticoid activity.

moXVc_.title: Interosseous muscles
moXVc_.description: The intrinsic muscles of the hand that perform finger abduction (dorsal interosseous muscles) and adduction (palmar interosseous muscles). Innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

5oXic_.title: Lymph
5oXic_.description: Interstitial fluid that is collected in lymphatic vessels. It has a high viscosity due to high protein and lipid concentration. Other components of lymph fluid include electrolytes, glucose, white blood cells, and water. Lymph is transported back into circulation through the lymphatic system.

MoXMc_.title: Thoracodorsal nerve
MoXMc_.description: A peripheral nerve of the upper limb that is a branch of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus (nerve roots C6-8). Innervates the latissimus dorsi muscle.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

noX7c_.title: Suprascapular nerve
noX7c_.description: A peripheral nerve of the upper limb that arises from the brachial plexus (nerve roots C4-C6). Innervates the infraspinatus and supraspinatus muscles.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

LoXwc_.title: Acute promyelocytic leukemia
LoXwc_.description: A rare subtype of acute myeloid leukemia in which myeloid cells proliferate but stop maturing when the cell is in the promyelocyte stage. Associated with t(15;17) translocations and responds to therapy with all-trans retinoic acid.

media.title: Auer rods in acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL)

KoXU1_.title: Falciform ligament
KoXU1_.description: A derivative of ventral mesentery that attaches the liver to the anterior abdominal wall. Contains the ligamentum teres hepatis and paraumbilical veins.

6oXj1_.title: Gastrohepatic ligament
6oXj1_.description: A fold of peritoneum that extends from the lesser curvature of the stomach to the liver. Contains the right and left gastric vessels. Separates the greater and lesser sacs on the right. Together with the hepatoduodenal ligament, it forms the lesser omentum.

JoXs1_.title: Nucleus accumbens
JoXs1_.description: A region of the forebrain that contains GABAergic neurons. Involved in the control of the mesolimbic pathway.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

qoXC1_.title: Leiomyosarcoma
qoXC1_.description: A malignant tumor of smooth muscle. Can originate from smooth muscle in various tissues of the body, including the uterus, gastrointestinal tract, and skin.

IoXYW_.title: Scolex
IoXYW_.description: Anterior or “head” segment of a tapeworm with hooks or suckers for attachment.

media.title: Head of a pork tapeworm (Taenia solium)

HoXKW_.title: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase
HoXKW_.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of acetyl-CoA to malonyl-CoA using biotin (vitamin B7) as a cofactor.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

media.title: Absorption, metabolism, and synthesis of fatty acids

soXtW_.title: Propionyl carboxylase
soXtW_.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of propionyl-CoA to methylmalonyl-CoA using biotin (vitamin B7) as a cofactor.

GoXBW_.title: Methylcrotonyl CoA carboxylase
GoXBW_.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA to 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA, an important step in the breakdown of leucine. Uses biotin (vitamin B7) as a cofactor.

toXXd_.title: Pyruvate
toXXd_.description: An alpha-keto acid that serves as an intermediate in several metabolic pathways (e.g., gluconeogenesis, glycolysis).

FoXgd_.title: Succinate dehydrogenase
FoXgd_.description: An enzyme complex in the inner mitochondrial membrane that catalyzes the conversion of succinate to fumarate in the citric acid cycle and transfers electrons from FADH2 to ubiquinone in the electron transport chain.

8oXOd_.title: Biotin deficiency
8oXOd_.description: A rare nutritional disorder associated with excessive consumption of raw egg whites. Clinical features include dermatitis, enteritis, and alopecia.

uoXpd_.title: Glutathione reductase
uoXpd_.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the reduction of glutathione disulfide (GSSG) to the sulfhydryl form of glutathione (GSH) in the presence of NADPH and riboflavin.

EoX8d_.title: Redox reaction
EoX8d_.description: A chemical reaction in which electrons are transferred from one substance to another. Involves both a reduction and an oxidation process.

voXAd_.title: Fatty acyl-CoA synthetase
voXAd_.description: An enzyme involved in fatty acid degradation that attaches a CoA group to a fatty acid prior to transport via the carnitine shuttle.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

DoX1V_.title: Serine
DoX1V_.description: A nonessential, hydrophilic, uncharged amino acid.

woXhV_.title: Fatty acid synthase
woXhV_.description: A multi-enzyme complex that catalyzes fatty acid synthesis using vitamin B5 as a cofactor.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

CoXqV_.title: Transketolase
CoXqV_.description: A thiamine-dependent enzyme that is involved in the non-oxidative pathway of the hexose monophosphate shunt.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Pentose phosphate pathway

xoXEV_.title: Hexose monophosphate shunt
xoXEV_.description: A cytoplasmic metabolic pathway that degrades abundant glucose-6-phosphate, thereby providing NADPH as well as ribose for nucleotide synthesis. Consists of an oxidative and nonoxidative phase.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Pentose phosphate pathway

BoXzV_.title: Methionine synthase
BoXzV_.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of homocysteine into methionine by transferring a methyl group from 5-methyl tetrahydrofolate in the presence of vitamin B12.

yoXde_.title: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase
yoXde_.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA, using vitamin B12 as a cofactor. Involved in the metabolism of odd-chain fatty acids and in the process of nerve myelination.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

AoXRe_.title: Hypogastric nerve
AoXRe_.description: A paired nerve bundle that arises from the T12-L3 spinal levels and runs between the superior and inferior hypogastric plexuses. Accompanies the internal iliac artery on each side. Contain sympathetic fibers (descending from the superior hypogastric plexus) and parasympathetic fibers (ascending from the inferior hypogastric plexus).

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

_oX5e_.title: Mons pubis
_oX5e_.description: The skin and soft tissue overlying the female pubic symphysis.

zoXre_.title: Iliohypogastric nerve
zoXre_.description: A mixed motor and sensory nerve that originates from the lumbar plexus (T12-L1). Innervates caudal parts of the internal oblique and transversus abdominis and carries sensory information from the lateral hip and suprapubic region.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

-oXDe_.title: B-cell acute lymphocytic leukemia
-oXDe_.description: A subtype of acute lymphocytic leukemia that originates from B cells and accounts for ~ 80–85% of cases.

ZKXZU_.title: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve
ZKXZU_.description: A nerve that originates from L2-L3 nerve roots in the lumbar plexus. Courses laterally to supply sensation to the lateral thigh. Compression of the nerve causes meralgia paraesthetica.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Innervation of the thigh
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

aKXQU_.title: Y descent
aKXQU_.description: A component of the jugular venous pulse that correlates with emptying of blood from the right atrium into the right ventricle after opening of the tricuspid valve.  Becomes more prominent in patients with constrictive pericarditis and absent in patients with cardiac tamponade.

YKXnU_.title: Gluteus medius muscle
YKXnU_.description: A gluteal muscle that originates from the outer surface of the ilium (between the iliac crest) and anterior and posterior gluteal lines and inserts onto the greater trochanter. Innervated by the superior gluteal nerve and supplied by the superior gluteal artery. Abducts, internally rotates, and extends the hip joint.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region

media.title: Superficial and deep muscles of the gluteal region

bKXHU_.title: Paradoxical split
bKXHU_.description: An auscultatory finding in which the splitting of the second heart sound (S₂) is audible during expiration but not inspiration. Caused by delayed closure of the aortic valve (e.g., in severe aortic stenosis) that results in A₂ being heard after P₂ during expiration (split reversal). During inspiration, closure of the pulmonary valve is also delayed, so A₂ and P₂ occur simultaneously.

XKX9U_.title: EML4-ALK
XKX9U_.description: A fusion gene that consists of portions of the echinoderm microtubule-associated protein-like 4 (EML4) gene and the anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) gene. Associated with 3-7% of cases of non-small cell lung carcinoma.

cKXa2_.title: Signet cell
cKXa2_.description: A mucin-filled cell with a peripheral nucleus, which gives the appearance of a signet ring. Associated with diffuse type of gastric cancer (signet ring cell carcinoma), Krukenberg tumors, and some forms of lung adenocarcinoma.

1KX22_.title: Dopamine beta-hydroxylase
1KX22_.description: An enzyme present in the adrenal medulla, sympathetic nerves, and noradrenergic and adrenergic neurons of the central nervous system that converts dopamine to noradrenaline. Vitamin C is a cofactor.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla

WKXP2_.title: Neuropeptide Y
WKXP2_.description: A neurotransmitter that has several functions in the central and peripheral nervous systems. Involved in appetite stimulation, regulation of anxiety-related behavior, and neuronal excitability. Primarily stored in the hypothalamus.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Regulation of appetite and satiety

VKXG2_.title: Fat-soluble vitamins
VKXG2_.description: The vitamins A, D, E, and K, which are absorbed via chylomicrons by enterocytes and stored in the body for long periods of time. Associated with a greater risk for toxicity than water-soluble vitamins.

eKXx2_.title: Classical conditioning
eKXx2_.description: A type of learning that leads to an involuntary response. A biologically potent, unconditioned stimulus (e.g., the smell of food) leads to a natural, unconditioned response (e.g., salivation). If the unconditioned stimulus is repeatedly paired with a neutral stimulus (e.g., the sound of a bell), the neutral stimulus can become a conditioned stimulus that leads to the same natural response, which is now a conditioned response (e.g., the sound of a bell leads to salivation).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

UKXbf_.title: Operant conditioning
UKXbf_.description: A behavioristic learning theory that connects a stimulus and a reaction. A key feature is that a specific behavior will be more likely if it gets rewarded and less likely if it gets punished. Desired behavior can thus be stimulated by positive reinforcement (reward) or negative reinforcement (taking away punishment).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

2KXTf_.title: Positive reinforcement
2KXTf_.description: A process by which the addition of a stimulus in response to a behavior increases the behavior (e.g., an employee continues to work overtime because he gets a salary bonus). A feature of operant conditioning.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

fKXkf_.title: Negative reinforcement
fKXkf_.description: A process by which the removal of a stimulus in response to a behavior increases the behavior (e.g., a child who continues to get good grades gets excused from doing chores). A feature of operant conditioning.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

TKX6f_.title: Leptin
TKX6f_.description: A hormone predominantly produced in adipose tissue. It is a key mediator of long-term regulation of food intake and body weight and inhibits hunger.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Regulation of appetite and satiety

SKXyf_.title: Proopiomelanocortin
SKXyf_.description: A precursor polypeptide primarily synthesized in the anterior pituitary gland. During posttranslational modification, it is cleaved into several biologically active polypeptides including ACTH, melanocyte-stimulating hormone, beta-lipotropin, and beta-endorphin.

hKXcT_.title: Internal pudendal artery
hKXcT_.description: A branch of the internal iliac artery that supplies blood to the perineum, genitalia, anal canal, and erectile tissues.

media.title: Pelvis with blood supply of the anal canal

3KXST_.title: Deep artery of the penis
3KXST_.description: A branch of the internal pudendal artery that supplies blood to the deep structures of the penis. It enters the corpus cavernosum and gives off the helicine arteries, which are involved in the process of erection.

RKXlT_.title: SMAD4
RKXlT_.description: A transcription factor and tumor suppressor involved in regulating the transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) family pathway. Mutations in the SMAD4 gene on chromosome 18 are associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, juvenile polyposis syndrome, and cancers of the pancreas and colon."

iKXJT_.title: Percutaneous transfemoral arterial catheterization
iKXJT_.description: A percutaneous procedure during which a catheter is inserted through the femoral artery to achieve access into the arterial system. Typically used during cardiac catheterization, in which the catheter is passed into the coronary vessels and/or chambers of the heart.

QKXuT_.title: Long-chain fatty acids
QKXuT_.description: A fatty acid with a total carbon-chain length between 14-20. The carnitine shuttle is required to transport LCFAs into the mitochondrial matrix, where they serve as substrates for β-oxidation.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

PKXWg_.title: Enterobacter
PKXWg_.description: A genus of enteric, gram-negative bacilli of the family of Enterobacteriaceae. Important cause of health care-associated infections such as CLABSI, bacteremia, and UTI.

4KX3g_.title: Endocarditis
4KX3g_.description: A condition characterized by inflammation of the inner lining of the heart and valves (endocardium). Generally caused by infection (e.g., from microorganisms that spread hematogenously from a distant source). Other causes include rheumatic diseases and nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis.

kKXmg_.title: Mucicarmine stain
kKXmg_.description: A staining method used to identify mucin (e.g., in gastric tumors) and the thick polysaccharide capsule of some organisms (e.g., Cryptococcus).

OKXIg_.title: Free nerve endings
OKXIg_.description: A type of somatosensory receptor located in the deeper epidermal layers of the skin and in the walls of the viscera. They sense pain (nociception) and temperature (thermoreception).

mKXVS_.title: Arrector pili muscle
mKXVS_.description: A muscle that consists of obliquely-directed smooth muscle fibers that attach to the dermal sheath that surrounds hair follicles. Innervated by the sympathetic nervous system. Contraction of these muscles, which occurs as a result of fear or a cold environment, results in goosebumps and causes hair to become upright.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Skin appendage

5KXiS_.title: Pilosebaceous unit
5KXiS_.description: A skin appendage that consists of a sebaceous gland, arrector pili muscle, and hair follicle.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Skin appendage

MKXMS_.title: Apocrine sweat gland
MKXMS_.description: A skin appendage found in the dermis, most prominently in the axilla, perineum, and groin. Stimulated by sex hormones to secrete a protein-rich substance that can be transformed by bacteria into odorous sweat. Not involved in thermoregulation. The cells of apocrine glands secrete substances via budding and pinching of a part of the cytoplasm.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Skin appendage

LKXwS_.title: East African sleeping sickness
LKXwS_.description: An infectious disease endemic to eastern and southeastern Africa caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense, which is transmitted by the bite of the tsetse fly. Infection occurs in two stages, a hemolymphatic stage characterized by intermittent fever, Winterbottom sign, and cutaneous manifestations (e.g., trypanosomal chancre) followed by a meningoencephalitic phase characterized by daytime somnolence, nocturnal insomnia, behavioral changes, and neurologic changes.

oKX0h_.title: West African sleeping sickness
oKX0h_.description: An infectious disease endemic to western and central Africa caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma brucei gambiense, which is transmitted by the bite of the tsetse fly. Infection occurs in two stages, a hemolymphatic stage characterized by intermittent fever, Winterbottom sign, and cutaneous manifestations (e.g., trypanosomal chancre) followed by a meningoencephalitic phase characterized by daytime somnolence, nocturnal insomnia, behavioral changes, and neurological changes up to coma and death if left untreated.

KKXUh_.title: Melarsoprol
KKXUh_.description: An antiparasitic drug used to treat late-stage African trypanosomiasis. Commonly causes severe adverse effects such as myocarditis and encephalopathy.

6KXjh_.title: Nifurtimox
6KXjh_.description: An antiparasitic medication used to treat acute T. cruzi infection (Chagas disease). Not effective in the treatment of chronic Chagas disease. Also used to treat T. brucei infection (African sleeping sickness). Generates reactive oxygen species that damage parasite DNA and proteins.

pKXLh_.title: Eflornithine
pKXLh_.description: A drug used to treat the second stage of West African sleeping sickness. Inhibits ornithine decarboxylase. A topical formulation can be used to treat excessive facial hair growth in women. Adverse effects of systemic use include diarrhea, anemia, and leukopenia. Adverse effects of topical use include erythema, a stinging sensation, and an acneiform eruption.

JKXsh_.title: Suramin
JKXsh_.description: A drug used to treat river blindness and the first stage of African sleeping sickness. Its exact mechanism of action is unclear. Common adverse effects include gastrointestinal upset, malaise, and various skin sensations (e.g., crawling, tingling, tenderness). Not commercially available in the United States.

7KX43_.title: Bacteroides fragilis
7KX43_.description: A rod-shaped, gram-negative, beta-lactamase-producing obligately anaerobe. Normally grows in the colon but can be found in infections throughout the body in patients with bowel trauma.

HKXK3_.title: Facultative anaerobe
HKXK3_.description: Bacterial species that are capable of aerobic respiration but can switch to anaerobic respiration if no oxygen is available.

sKXt3_.title: Postpartum thyroiditis
sKXt3_.description: An autoimmune-mediated destructive thyroiditis that occurs within 12 months postpartum. Typically follows a triphasic pattern of transient thyrotoxicosis, hypothyroidism, and eventual return to a euthyroid state. Postpartum thyroiditis should be distinguished from Graves disease as management differs.

GKXB3_.title: Enteroendocrine cells
GKXB3_.description: A group of specialized cells in the gastric and intestinal mucosa (e.g., K cells, L cells, and I cells), as well as in the pancreas (e.g., alpha, beta, and delta islet cells). Secrete small molecules or peptides into the bloodstream to exert systemic effects.

tKXXR_.title: Paneth cell
tKXXR_.description: A type of specialized cell located in the epithelium at the base of the crypts of Lieberkuhn. Can be identified microscopically by large, intracellular eosinophilic granules that contain molecules that regulate host response and immunity.

FKXgR_.title: Hurthle cell
FKXgR_.description: A large, polygonal epithelial cell with acidophilic cytoplasm, numerous mitochondria, and a hyperchromatic nucleus with prominent nucleoli. Found in the thyroid gland, parathyroid glands, salivary glands, and kidneys. Their presence on thyroid histopathology is nonspecific and can be seen in Hashimoto thyroiditis, Hürthle cell carcinoma, Graves disease, and in previously-irradiated thyroid glands.

uKXpR_.title: Alpha-glucosidase
uKXpR_.description: An enzyme of the brush border of the small intestine that hydrolyzes the terminal α-(1,4)-bond of starch or disaccharides to produce an alpha-glucose molecule. Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors are used as antidiabetic drugs.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

EKX8R_.title: Glucokinase
EKX8R_.description: An insulin-dependent kinase that adds a phosphate group to a six carbon sugar, most notably glucose (to produce glucose-6-phosphate) or fructose (to produce fructose-6-phosphate). Located primarily in the liver and the β-cells of the pancreas. Glucokinase is inhibited by fructose-6-phosphate.

vKXAR_.title: Glucose transporter 2
vKXAR_.description: A transmembrane carrier protein that facilitates an insulin-independent, bidirectional, glucose movement across the cell membrane. It is expressed in β islet cells, and in the liver, kidney, and small intestine.

DKX1i_.title: Glucose transporter 1
DKX1i_.description: A uniporter membrane transport protein that facilitates insulin-independent glucose movement into cells. Expressed in most human cells. Particularly important for transport across that blood-brain barrier.

wKXhi_.title: Glucose transporter 3
wKXhi_.description: A uniporter membrane transport protein that facilitates insulin-independent glucose movement into the cell. It is expressed in all human tissues but functions as a major transporter in the central nervous system and placenta.

9KXNi_.title: Glucose transporter 5
9KXNi_.description: A uniporter membrane transport protein that facilitates insulin-independent fructose movement into the cell. Primarily in the gastrointestinal tract (on the brush border of intestinal cells), spermatocytes, and liver.

CKXqi_.title: Glucose transporter 4
CKXqi_.description: An insulin-dependent glucose transporter that facilitates glucose uptake into the cell. Expressed primarily in adipose tissues and striated muscle.

BKXzi_.title: 24,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol
BKXzi_.description: An inactive intermediate in vitamin D metabolism formed from 25-hydroxycholecalciferol.

yKXdQ_.title: 24-hydroxlyase
yKXdQ_.description: An enzyme involved in vitamin D metabolism. Catalyzes degradation of 1,25-hydroxycholecalciferol and 25-hydroxycholecalciferol into 24-hydroxylated products.

AKXRQ_.title: Auerbach plexus
AKXRQ_.description: A network of ganglia located between the longitudinal and circular muscle layers of the gastrointestinal tract. Extends around the circumference of the gut from the esophagus to the rectum and controls gastrointestinal tract motility.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Enteric nervous system

_KX5Q_.title: Meissner plexus
_KX5Q_.description: A plexus that lies in the submucosa of the intestinal wall. Relaxes the smooth muscle of the gastrointestinal tract to facilitate the passage of food, regulates blood flow, and controls absorption by the epithelium. Nerves of this plexus are derived from parasympathetic fibers of the superior mesenteric plexus, which are derived from neural crest cells.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Enteric nervous system

zKXrQ_.title: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase
zKXrQ_.description: The rate-determining enzyme of gluconeogenesis. Converts fructose-1,6-bisphosphate to fructose-6-phosphate. Stimulated by citrate. Inhibited by AMP and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate.

-KXDQ_.title: Protein phosphatase 1
-KXDQ_.description: An enzyme involved in regulation of glycogen metabolism. Activates glycogen synthase and deactivates phosphorylase kinase, both via dephosphorylation.

media.title: Effects of protein phosphatase 1 in glycogen metabolism

Z6XZj_.title: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate
Z6XZj_.description: A metabolite of both glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. Can be converted to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate as well as fructose-6-phosphate.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Sequence of reactions

06Xej_.title: Fructose-6-phosphate
06Xej_.description: A metabolite of both glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. Can be converted to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate as well as glucose-6-phosphate.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Sequence of reactions

a6XQj_.title: Chondronectin
a6XQj_.description: An adhesion factor in cartilage that establishes a connection between the extracellular matrix and chondrocytes.

Y6Xnj_.title: Uridine diphosphate glucose
Y6Xnj_.description: An activated form of glucose that serves as a substrate for glycogenesis.

b6XHj_.title: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenases
b6XHj_.description: A group of enzymes that catalyze the initial step of fatty acid β-oxidation by introducing a trans double-bond between C2 (α) and C3 (β) of acyl-CoA.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

X6X9j_.title: Incretin
X6X9j_.description: A digestive tract hormone that increases insulin secretion from beta cells of the pancreas, decreases glucagon levels and slows gastric emptying in response to food intake. Two major incretins are glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP).

destinations.label: Diabetes medications → Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (incretin mimetics)

c6XaP_.title: Biguanide
c6XaP_.description: A class of antidiabetic drug that increases peripheral insulin sensitivity, decreases hepatic gluconeogenesis, and decreases intestinal glucose absorption. Metformin is the only available agent of this class

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

16X2P_.title: Ammonia
16X2P_.description: A compound generated through protein digestion in enterocytes. The liver converts ammonia to glutamine, which can be excreted as urea by the kidneys. Advanced liver disease compromises appropriate ammonia clearance and leads to increased serum ammonia concentrations, which can result in hepatic encephalopathy.

W6XPP_.title: I cells
W6XPP_.description: A type of enteroendocrine cell of the small intestine that produces cholecystokinin.

d6XoP_.title: Extinction (psychology)
d6XoP_.description: The loss (unlearning) of a learned behavior due to discontinuation of a reward (in classical conditioning) or reinforcement (in operant conditioning).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

V6XGP_.title: Secretin
V6XGP_.description: A hormone produced by duodenal S cells. Increases pancreatic bicarbonate secretion and bile secretion into the duodenum. Decreases gastric acid secretion.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

e6XxP_.title: S cell (pancreas)
e6XxP_.description: Secretin-producing cells located in the duodenum. Stimulated by acid and fatty acids in the duodenal lumen. Secretin increases pancreatic bicarbonate secretion and decreases gastric acid secretion.

U6Xb4_.title: Hyperpigmentation
U6Xb4_.description: A darkening of the skin due to an overproduction of melanin. Associated with several conditions, including adrenal insufficiency and secondary hypercortisolism.

26XT4_.title: K cells
26XT4_.description: A type of enteroendocrine cell located in the duodenum and jejunum that produces gastric inhibitory peptide. Stimulated by increased intraluminal amino acids, fatty acids, and oral glucose.

T6X64_.title: Hepatocyte nuclear factor
T6X64_.description: A group of transcription factors primarily expressed in the liver that regulate production of several proteins. Defective HNF is associated with the development of maturity onset diabetes of the young (MODY) type III (particularly HNF 1).

g6XF4_.title: Staghorn calculus
g6XF4_.description: Large radiopaque urinary stone that fills the entire renal pelvis and calyces; associated with chronic upper urinary tract infections, urease-producing organisms (most commonly Proteus mirabilis), and alkaline urine.

media.title: Staghorn calculus and left ureteric calculus

S6Xy4_.title: Akimbo test
S6Xy4_.description: A physical examination maneuver used to assess the deltoid muscle. The patient places the hands on the iliac crest, abducted at the coronal plane, and rotates the shoulder internally while flexing the elbow joint and pronating the forearm. Considered positive and indicates injury to the deltoid muscle if the patient experiences pain or weakness with flexing while pronating the forearm.

h6Xck_.title: Hornblower's sign
h6Xck_.description: A physical examination maneuver used to assess the teres minor muscle. The patient abducts the arm at 90º in the scapular plane, flexes the elbow at 90º, and then attempts to externally rotate the forearm against resistance. Considered positive if the patient cannot perform external rotation or experiences pain with motion.

R6Xlk_.title: Streptococcus mutans
R6Xlk_.description: A gram-positive, alpha hemolytic bacteria that belongs to the Viridans group of streptococci. Part of the normal flora of the oropharynx and associated with dental caries. Can cause subacute endocarditis, usually after an oropharyngeal/dental procedure in a patient with previously damaged heart valves.

i6XJk_.title: Fc receptor
i6XJk_.description: A membrane receptor protein found on many cells such as neutrophils, natural killer cells, and macrophages. Recognizes and binds to antibodies that have attached to pathogens and mediates a phagocytic and/or cytotoxic response.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Lymphoid cell line

Q6Xuk_.title: Excyclotorsion
Q6Xuk_.description: An outward, rotational movement of the eye. Enabled by the inferior oblique muscle.

j6X_k_.title: Incyclotorsion
j6X_k_.description: An inward, rotational movement of the eye. Enabled by the superior oblique muscle.

P6XWO_.title: Hypotropia
P6XWO_.description: A position of the eyes in which one eye is deviated downward in comparison to the contralateral eye. The contralateral eye is termed hypertropic in relation to the hypotropic eye. HYPERtropia is the more commonly used term.

destinations.label: Ocular motility disorders and strabismus → Basic terms

46X3O_.title: α-intercalated cell
46X3O_.description: A type of epithelial cell found in the collecting tubule of the nephron. Responsible for secreting protons into the urine through H+ATPase and H+/K+ATPase.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Urine production

k6XmO_.title: Glycogen phosphorylase kinase
k6XmO_.description: A cAMP-dependent serine/threonine-specific protein kinase involved in glycogen metabolism. Phosphorylates and activates glycogen phosphorylase, which stimulates glycogenolysis.

O6XIO_.title: Fatty acid
O6XIO_.description: A carboxylic acid with an unbranched chain of carbon atoms differing in length (from 4–24 carbon atoms). Can be unsaturated (with C=C double bonds) or saturated (without C=C double bonds). Typically found as esters (in triglycerides, phospholipids or cholesterol esters). Degradation by β-oxidation releases energy.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

N6X-O_.title: Interleukin 11
N6X-O_.description: A cytokine produced by bone marrow stromal cells and endothelial cells that stimulates megakaryocyte proliferation and maturation and thereby increases platelet production.

m6XVl_.title: Ganglion
m6XVl_.description:
1. In neuroanatomy, "ganglion" refers to an accumulation of nerve cell bodies outside the CNS.
2. In general surgery, the term refers to a ganglion cyst (synovial cyst).

56Xil_.title: Megakaryopoiesis
56Xil_.description: The proliferation and maturation of megakaryocytes, which give rise to thrombocytes.

n6X7l_.title: Siderosis
n6X7l_.description: The accumulation of iron (in the form of hemosiderin) within tissue (e.g., central nervous system, lungs, liver).

o6X0N_.title: Interleukin-14
o6X0N_.description: A cytokine secreted by T cells and B-lineage lymphoma cells that promotes activation of B cells and inhibition of immunoglobulin secretion.

K6XUN_.title: Huntingtin gene
K6XUN_.description: Gene on chromosome 4p16.3 that encodes the protein huntingtin, which participates in the transport of vesicles, protein trafficking, postsynaptic signaling, regulation of transcription, and apoptosis of neurons. Expanded CAG trinucleotide repeats in the HTT gene are associated with Huntington disease.

66XjN_.title: Tau protein
66XjN_.description: A protein encoded by microtubule-associated protein tau (MAPT) gene on chromosome 17. Essential for neuronal cytoskeleton architecture, microtubule stabilization and assembly, and axonal transport regulation. Mutations in tau protein are associated with frontotemporal dementia and Alzheimer disease.

p6XLN_.title: Progranulin
p6XLN_.description: A precursor of granulin (a protein that regulates cell growth) encoded by the GRN gene on chromosome 17. Mutations of the progranulin gene are associated with frontotemporal dementia.

J6XsN_.title: Inferior hypogastric plexus
J6XsN_.description: An autonomic nerve plexus located on the lateral pelvic wall. Receives sympathetic fibers from the superior hypogastric plexus (via the ipsilateral hypogastric nerve) and sacral splanchnic nerves. Receives parasympathetic fibers from pelvic splanchnic nerves. Supplies autonomic fibers on each side to the nerve plexuses of urogenital organs (e.g., prostatic plexus, uterovaginal plexus, vesical plexus) and the anal canal above the pectinate line.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

q6XCN_.title: Paravertebral ganglia
q6XCN_.description: A collection of sympathetic ganglia that run from the lower cervical region to the sacral level of the spinal cord. Contains cell bodies of postganglionic sympathetic fibers

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system

I6XYm_.title: Ovarian failure
I6XYm_.description: The complete or near complete depletion of ovarian follicles and failure of the ovaries to respond to gonadotropins, which results in hypoestrogenemia and high FSH concentrations. Manifests with symptoms of menopause such as irregular menstrual cycles, amenorrhea, hot flashes, and vaginal dryness.

r6Xfm_.title: Beta-3 receptor
r6Xfm_.description: A G protein-linked adrenergic receptor. Activation increases lipolysis in adipose tissue, increases thermogenesis in skeletal muscle, and causes bladder detrusor muscle relaxation.

76X4m_.title: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
76X4m_.description: A group of ionotropic, cholinergic receptors on neurons and skeletal muscle that are activated by acetylcholine and nicotine. Expressed on neurons in the CNS critical for maintaining memories. In the peripheral nervous system, transmits efferent signals in presynaptic and postsynaptic sympathetic, parasympathetic, and motor neurons.

H6XKm_.title: Prevertebral ganglia
H6XKm_.description: A collection of sympathetic ganglia closely associated with the major abdominal branches of the aorta. Contains the cell bodies of postganglionic sympathetic fibers. Includes the celiac, superior mesenteric, aorticorenal, and inferior mesenteric ganglia.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity
Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system

media.title: Segment of the spinal cord with spinal roots, nerves, and fibers

s6Xtm_.title: Gonadotropin
s6Xtm_.description: A polypeptide hormone secreted by the anterior pituitary gland. The two principal gonadotropins are luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which stimulate gonadal production of a variety of hormones such as estradiol, progesterone, inhibins, and testosterone.

G6XBm_.title: Theca interna
G6XBm_.description: An endocrine cell in the ovary that expresses receptors for luteinizing hormone and secretes androstenedione, which enters granulosa cells and is converted to estrone and estradiol. Provides structure and support to the follicle as it matures.

t6XX5_.title: Granulosa cell
t6XX5_.description: A somatic cell of the sex cord that is closely associated with the developing female oocyte. Converts androstenedione to estradiol by the enzyme aromatase during the follicular phase of the menstrual cycle. After ovulation, granulosa cells turn into granulosa lutein cells that produce progesterone.

destinations.label: The menstrual cycle → Overview of the menstrual cycle

F6Xg5_.title: Unconditioned stimulus
F6Xg5_.description: A stimulus that evokes an unconditioned (unlearned) response, especially in the context of classical conditioning (e.g., the smell of food, which leads to salivation).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

86XO5_.title: Unconditioned response
86XO5_.description: An unlearned response that follows an unconditioned stimulus, especially in the context of classical conditioning (e.g., salivation caused by the smell of food).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

u6Xp5_.title: Neutral stimulus
u6Xp5_.description: A stimulus that does not initially evoke a specific response. If repeatedly paired with an unconditioned stimulus, the neutral stimulus will eventually lead to the same response and is then referred to as a conditioned stimulus (e.g., pairing a ringing bell with the smell of food eventually leads to salivation even without food nearby).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

E6X85_.title: Conditioned stimulus
E6X85_.description: A neutral stimulus that is presented in conjunction with an unconditioned stimulus and then elicits a conditioned response. For example, a bell (neutral stimulus) elicits salivation (conditioned response) because it was previously presented in conjunction with food (unconditioned stimulus). A key feature of classical conditioning.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

v6XA5_.title: Hydrophobia
v6XA5_.description: An irrational fear of swallowing liquids, often associated with painful dysphagia and triggered by pharyngeal spasms. Classically associated with rabies virus infection.

D6X1M_.title: Disinhibition (psychology)
D6X1M_.description: A pattern of socially inappropriate behavior (e.g., offensive language, not respecting personal boundaries) and impulsivity (e.g., reckless spending). Seen in several neurological and psychiatric conditions, including frontotemporal dementia.

w6XhM_.title: Conditioned response
w6XhM_.description: A learned response to a conditioned stimulus in classical conditioning (e.g., salivation in response to a bell that has become associated with food).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

96XNM_.title: Alpha motor neurons
96XNM_.description: Lower motor neurons that are located in the anterior horns of the spinal cord or the cranial nerve nuclei within the brainstem. Axons extend into the periphery and innervate skeletal muscle.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

media.title: Cross section of the spinal cord
Motor neuron columns in the spinal cord and plexus formation

x6XEM_.title: Splanchnic nerves
x6XEM_.description: A pair of visceral nerves that carry afferent and efferent sympathetic and parasympathetic fibers of the autonomic nervous system. Distinguished as cardiopulmonary, thoracic, lumbar, sacral, and pelvic splanchnic nerves. The pelvic splanchnic nerves only carry parasympathetic fibers.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system

B6XzM_.title: Ambroxol
B6XzM_.description: A mucolytic used in the management of respiratory tract disorders that cause accumulation of excessive viscous secretions. Not currently available in the United States.

y6Xdn_.title: Lubiprostone
y6Xdn_.description: A prostaglandin derivative that activates chloride channels on the apical surfaces of enterocytes. Results in increased intestinal fluid secretion and fecal transit.

A6XRn_.title: Lysine
A6XRn_.description: An essential amino acid with hydrophilic properties. Has a positive side chain at physiologic pH.

_6X5n_.title: Proline
_6X5n_.description: A nonessential amino acid with hydrophobic properties.

z6Xrn_.title: Dendrotoxin
z6Xrn_.description: A neurotoxin produced by the black mamba snake. Binds potassium channels on presynaptic neurons and delays repolarization, which increases the release of acetylcholine.

-6XDn_.title: Respiratory burst
-6XDn_.description: The destruction of phagocytosed pathogens via the production of reactive oxygen species (e.g., hydrogen peroxide, hypochlorous acid). Important enzymes include NADPH oxidase and myeloperoxidase. Occurs primarily in neutrophils and monocytes.

0pXeL_.title: Hydroxylation
0pXeL_.description: A chemical reaction that inserts a hydroxyl group (-OH) into a compound.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

apXQL_.title: Tropocollagen
apXQL_.description: An intermediate product of collagen synthesis that consists of a triple helix of procollagen chains. Several tropocollagen molecules create a collagen fibril.

YpXnL_.title: Osteoid
YpXnL_.description: A soft, immature part of the bone matrix that is synthesized by osteoblasts prior to mineralization. Mainly consists of collagen type I. Defective mineralization of osteoid is called osteomalacia.

bpXHL_.title: Guaifenesin
bpXHL_.description: An expectorant that facilitates mucociliary clearance by increasing the effective hydration of the respiratory tract and thereby reducing the viscosity of respiratory mucus.

XpX9L_.title: Pseudoephedrine
XpX9L_.description: An α-adrenergic receptor agonist (α1>α2) that is used as a decongestant. Pseudoephedrine constricts blood vessels in the nose and thereby reduces edema, hyperemia, and congestion. Also some stimulation of β2-adrenergic receptors causing smooth muscle tissue in respiratory bronchioles to dilate.

1pX2o_.title: NMDA receptor
1pX2o_.description: An ionotropic receptor that depolarizes the neuron when activated by glutamate (and glycine less frequently). Critical for controlling synaptic plasticity and memory function. Overactivation can cause excitotoxicity and cell death.

WpXPo_.title: Medullary cough center
WpXPo_.description: A region of the medulla oblongata that controls involuntary coughing. Suppressed by antitussive medications such as dextromethorphan and codeine.

dpXoo_.title: Mature teratoma
dpXoo_.description: A germ cell tumor that is composed of mature, differentiated tissue. Includes dermoid cysts (most common) and struma ovarii.

VpXGo_.title: Celiac ganglion
VpXGo_.description: A part of the sympathetic nervous system located near the origin of the celiac artery from the aorta. Innervates the liver (via hepatic plexus), stomach, gallbladder, bile duct, spleen (via splenic plexus), pancreas, adrenal glands (via suprarenal plexus), and the first part of the small intestine.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity
Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system

epXxo_.title: Superior mesenteric ganglion
epXxo_.description: A part of the sympathetic nervous system derived from the celiac plexus that is located near the origin of the superior mesenteric artery from the aorta. Innervates structures of the midgut (i.e., the distal duodenum, jejunum, ileum, cecum, appendix, ascending colon, and proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon).

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity
Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system

UpXbK_.title: Aorticorenal ganglion
UpXbK_.description: A paired ganglion that corresponds with the renal arteries. Forms a part of the celiac plexus and receives fibers from the posterior vagal trunk, lesser splanchnic nerves, and least splanchnic nerves. Innervates the kidney, proximal ureter, adrenal gland, and ovaries/testes.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system
Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

2pXTK_.title: Inferior mesenteric ganglion
2pXTK_.description: A part of the sympathetic nervous system located near the origin of the inferior mesenteric artery from the aorta. Contains cell bodies of postganglionic sympathetic nerve fibers and innervates structures of the hindgut.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system
Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

fpXkK_.title: Stellate ganglion
fpXkK_.description: A sympathetic ganglion formed by the fusion of the first thoracic and inferior cervical ganglia. Located anterior to the C7 vertebra. Damage can result in Horner syndrome.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system

gpXFK_.title: Stellate ganglion block
gpXFK_.description: A technique in which local anesthetic is injected around the stellate ganglion. Used in the management of several conditions (e.g., chronic regional pain syndrome, cancer-related pain, Raynaud phenomenon).

hpXc6_.title: Glutathione synthetase
hpXc6_.description: An enzyme in the glutathione synthesis pathway that combines gamma-glutamylcysteine with glycine to form glutathione.

3pXS6_.title: Class I antiarrhythmic drug
3pXS6_.description: A group of medications that act to inhibit cardiac arrhythmias. These drugs block fast sodium channels that are responsible for rapid depolarization (phase 0 of cardiac action potentials). Further subdivided into Class IA, IB, and IC drugs.

ipXJ6_.title: Hemiparesis
ipXJ6_.description: A condition of unilateral weakness or paralysis affecting half of the body.

QpXu6_.title: Uniporter
QpXu6_.description: An integral membrane protein that transports molecules in one direction. Functions as an ion channel or a carrier protein.

jpX_6_.title: Facilitated diffusion
jpX_6_.description: A process of passive chemical diffusion across a membrane enabled either by ion channels or carriers for particular molecules. The transport of glucose and fructose into cells via GLUT transporters is an example of facilitated diffusion.

PpXWp_.title: Symporter
PpXWp_.description: A membrane transport protein that moves two different molecules in the same direction across a membrane.

media.title: Overview of the proximal convoluted tubule

4pX3p_.title: Antiporter
4pX3p_.description: A membrane transport protein that moves an ion across a membrane and down its concentration gradient to power the transport of a second substance against its gradient in the opposite direction.

kpXmp_.title: Multidrug resistance protein 1
kpXmp_.description: A protein that pumps out toxins, including chemotherapeutic agents. Classically seen in adrenocortical carcinoma and can decrease responsiveness to chemotherapy.

OpXIp_.title: Phenylethanolamine-N-Methyltransferase
OpXIp_.description: An enzyme that converts norepinephrine to epinephrine. Primarily found in the adrenal medulla.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla

lpXvp_.title: Bile
lpXvp_.description: A yellow-green fluid produced by the liver. Helps to emulsify and digest fat. Consists of water, cholesterol, conjugated bile acids, and the pigment bilirubin. Stored in the gallbladder and released into the duodenum via the bile ducts in response to cholecystokinin.

NpX-p_.title: Chiasma (genetics)
NpX-p_.description: The sites on paired chromosomes at which chromatids cross over and exchange genetic material during prophase of meiosis I.

mpXVJ_.title: Tyrosine
mpXVJ_.description: A nonessential hydrophilic amino acid, synthesized by hydroxylation of phenylalanine. A precursor of catecholamines and thyroid hormones. When incorporated into proteins, it is a target of phosphorylation by kinases.

MpXMJ_.title: Ape hand deformity
MpXMJ_.description: A manifestation of median nerve injury caused by inability to abduct the thumb.

npX7J_.title: Interphalangeal joint
npX7J_.description: A hinge joint located between the proximal, middle, and distal phalanges of the hand and foot. In the hand, they allow flexion and extension of the phalanges. In the foot, they allow plantarflexion and dorsiflexion.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

media.title: Muscles of the dorsum of the foot (dorsal view)
Normal appearance of hands and wrists

LpXwJ_.title: Supraclavicular nerve
LpXwJ_.description: A nerve that arises from the ventral rami of C3 and C4 spinal nerves. Descends in the neck through the posterior triangle and provides sensory supply to the skin over the upper and posterior shoulder, clavicle, and anterior and lateral chest.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

6pXjq_.title: Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm
6pXjq_.description: A sensory nerve that branches from the medial cord of the brachial plexus. Innervates the skin of the medial forearm.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

ppXLq_.title: Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve
ppXLq_.description: The cutaneous division of the musculocutaneous nerve, which exits between the biceps brachii and brachialis muscles in the antecubital fossa. Provides sensation to the lateral aspect of the forearm.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

IpXYI_.title: Cephalic vein
IpXYI_.description: A superficial vein of the upper extremity that originates from the lateral aspect of the dorsal venous arch of the hand and empties into the axillary vein.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Veins

rpXfI_.title: Basilic vein
rpXfI_.description: A superficial vein of the upper extremity that arises from the medial aspect of the dorsal venous arch of the hand. Joins the brachial vein to form the axillary vein.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Veins

7pX4I_.title: Median cubital vein
7pX4I_.description: A superficial vein of the cubital fossa that connects the cephalic and basilic veins. Commonly used as a site of intravenous access.

destinations.label: Upper arm and elbow → Cubital fossa (antecubital fossa)
Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Veins

HpXKI_.title: Median antebrachial vein
HpXKI_.description: A superficial vein of the forearm that originates from the palmar venous network of the hand and terminates in the median cubital vein (most common). It mainly drains the superficial structures of ventral mid-forearm and wrist.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Veins

spXtI_.title: Buck fascia
spXtI_.description: The deep layer of penile fascia that surrounds the corpus cavernosum and corpus spongiosum. Superficial to the tunica albuginea but deep to the Dartos fascia.

GpXBI_.title: Brachial artery
GpXBI_.description: A continuation of the axillary artery that serves as the main arterial supply for the arm, including the coracobrachialis, biceps, and triceps brachialis muscles. Originates at the inferior border of the teres major, passes from the medial aspect of the humerus to the anterior aspect of the arm, and terminates just below the cubital fossa by bifurcating into the radial and ulnar arteries.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries
Upper arm and elbow → Vasculature and lymphatics

tpXXr_.title: Ulnar artery
tpXXr_.description: A branch of the brachial artery that courses medially in the forearm before anastomosing with branches of the radial artery to form the deep palmar arch of the hand.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

FpXgr_.title: Radial artery
FpXgr_.description: A branch of the brachial artery that courses laterally in the forearm before anastomosing with branches of the ulnar artery to form the deep palmar arch of the hand.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

8pXOr_.title: Deep palmar arch
8pXOr_.description: A deep arterial anastomosis formed by the distal radial artery (main) and ulnar artery (deep palmar branch). It anastomoses with the superficial palmar arch via common palmar digital arteries. Its main function is to supply the bones, joints, and deep muscles of the hand with blood.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

upXpr_.title: Superficial palmar arch
upXpr_.description: A superficial arterial anastomosis formed by the distal ulnar artery (main) and radial artery (superficial palmar branch), located just below the palmar aponeurosis.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

EpX8r_.title: Thyrocervical trunk
EpX8r_.description: A short branch of the subclavian artery that supplies the thyroid gland, brachial plexus, and the viscera and muscles of the neck.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

vpXAr_.title: Subclavian artery
vpXAr_.description: A pair of major arteries of the upper thorax that supply the upper extremities as well as structures in the head, neck, and thorax. The left subclavian artery originates from the aorta, whereas the right subclavian artery originates from the brachiocephalic trunk.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

DpX17_.title: Limbic system
DpX17_.description: A collection of brain structures involved in emotion, memory, olfaction, behavior, and autonomic nervous system function. Includes the hippocampus, amygdala, anterior thalamic nuclei, mammillary bodies, and cingulate gyrus.

wpXh7_.title: Porin
wpXh7_.description: Barrel proteins that are present in the outer membrane of certain bacteria. Allow molecules (e.g., antibiotics) to diffuse across the cell membrane.

9pXN7_.title: Histone deacetylase
9pXN7_.description: An enzyme that removes acetyl groups from histone proteins, which exposes positively-charged lysine residues. As a result, negatively-charged DNA binds more tightly to the histone, which prevents transcription.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

CpXq7_.title: Histone methyltransferase
CpXq7_.description: An enzyme that transfers methyl groups to lysine and arginine residues on histone proteins. This exerts epigenetic control of transcription and typically results in suppression of gene transcription.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

xpXE7_.title: Annealing
xpXE7_.description: A step in polymerase chain reaction (PCR) in which single-stranded DNA (and less commonly, RNA) forms hydrogen bonds to a complementary single strand, which forms a double strand.

ApXRH_.title: ATP7B gene
ApXRH_.description: A gene that encodes copper-transporting ATPase 2. Mutations of this gene can result in dysfunctional protein or failure of protein synthesis, which results in Wilson disease.

_pX5H_.title: Leucine
_pX5H_.description: An essential, purely ketogenic amino acid with a branched aliphatic side chain.

zpXrH_.title: Sarcopenia
zpXrH_.description: A reduction in skeletal muscle mass and strength. Causes include cachexia, obesity, and aging.

destinations.label: Aging changes → Bones, muscles, and joints

-pXDH_.title: Promoter
-pXDH_.description: A segment of DNA upstream (toward the 5' end) of a gene that regulates transcription initiation.

ZJXZs_.title: Solar lentigo
ZJXZs_.description: A benign cutaneous lesion that typically manifests as a flat, oval, uniformly hyperpigmented macule. Caused by proliferation of melanocytes in response to chronic sun exposure.

0JXes_.title: Skin tags
0JXes_.description: A benign, small, skin-colored, pedunculated papule on a narrow stalk that most commonly develops in skin creases (e.g., axilla, inframammary fold, inguinal region).

aJXQs_.title: Iodotyrosine deiodinase
aJXQs_.description: An enzyme in the thyroid gland that catalyzes the deiodination of mono- (MIT) and diiodotyrosine (DIT). The recycled iodide is provided back into the T3 and T4 synthesis.

XJX9s_.title: Alveolar ventilation
XJX9s_.description: The volume of gas that reaches the alveoli every minute. Calculated as (tidal volume – physiologic dead space) x respiratory rate.

cJXaG_.title: Vitreous humor
cJXaG_.description: A gel-like substance that fills the eye between the lens and the retina.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Segments and chambers of the eye

media.title: Embryological eye development: 2nd to 9th month of gestation

1JX2G_.title: Bradypnea
1JX2G_.description: A decreased rate of breathing. For adults: < 12/min. For children 1–5 years of age: < 20/min; for children 6-12 months of age: < 25/min; for children less than 6 months of age: < 30/min).

destinations.label: Respiratory failure and arrest → Initial management

WJXPG_.title: Hypoventilation
WJXPG_.description: A respiratory minute volume that does not meet the metabolic needs and causes a respiratory acidosis due to excess accumulation of carbon dioxide.

VJXGG_.title: Retroperitoneum
VJXGG_.description: A potential space that exists between the peritoneal cavity and the posterior abdominal wall. Structures that exist in this space include the adrenal glands, kidneys, ureters, aorta, inferior vena cava, duodenum (except the first segment), and ascending/descending colon.

eJXxG_.title: Filtration fraction
eJXxG_.description: The ratio of glomerular filtration rate to renal plasma flow; often estimated by creatinine clearance divided by PAH clearance. Normally ~ 20%. Increases in response to angiotensin II.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function

2JXTt_.title: Fecal elastase-1
2JXTt_.description: An enzyme produced by the pancreas. Measured to assess pancreatic function, often in the workup of steatorrhea. Levels < 200 mcg/g are abnormal; levels < 100 mcg/g are diagnostic for exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.

fJXkt_.title: Popliteal fossa
fJXkt_.description: The depression of the posterior aspect of the knee joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The popliteal fossa

TJX6t_.title: Poikilothermia
TJX6t_.description: An impaired ability to regulate body temperature. Often used to describe acutely ischemic, cool limbs.

gJXFt_.title: 5-HT1 receptors
gJXFt_.description: A group of G-protein-coupled receptors that bind to serotonin.

SJXyt_.title: Glutamate
SJXyt_.description: The  main excitatory neurotransmitter in the brain, released by almost half of brain synapses. Clinically important for its role in neurotoxicity secondary to neural injury. It is also a nonessential amino acid synthesized in neurons from glutamine. Plays a role in the glucose-alanine cycle.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

hJXcF_.title: Nasolabial fold
hJXcF_.description: The skin creases that course from the lateral edge of the nose to the lateral edge of the corner of the mouth.

3JXSF_.title: Ipsilateral
3JXSF_.description: A descriptor for processes or structures on the same side of the body.

RJXlF_.title: Nerve to stapedius
RJXlF_.description: A branch of the facial nerve that innervates the stapedius muscle. Damage to this nerve results in ipsilateral hyperacusis.

iJXJF_.title: Bulbus cordis
iJXJF_.description: The bulbus cordis is part of the developing heart and links the primitive (embryonic) ventricle to the truncus arteriosus. Together, the primitive ventricle and the bulbus cordis give rise to the left and the right ventricles, the smooth part deriving from the primitive ventricle and the outflow tract deriving from the bulbus cordis.

QJXuF_.title: Hesselbach triangle
QJXuF_.description: A triangular region located on each side of the lower abdominal wall. Bordered medially by the lateral margin of the rectus sheath, laterally by the inferior epigastric vessels, and inferiorly by the inguinal ligament. This triangle helps differentiate direct (inside the triangle) from indirect (outside the triangle) inguinal hernias.

media.title: Borders of the inguinal canal and contents of the spermatic cord

jJX_F_.title: Retroviridae
jJX_F_.description: A family of positive-sense, single-stranded RNA viruses that uses reverse transcriptase to create a DNA intermediate and integrate with the genome of a host cell. This permits the production of proteins necessary for virus replication. Examples include human immunodeficiency virus and human T-lymphotropic virus.

PJXW8_.title: Para-aminohippuric acid
PJXW8_.description: A compound that is almost entirely excreted by the kidneys. Its clearance is used to estimate effective renal plasma flow.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function

4JX38_.title: Idursulfase
4JX38_.description: A recombinant form of the lysosomal enzyme iduronate-2-sulfatase. Used to treat Hunter syndrome.

kJXm8_.title: Arginine
kJXm8_.description: A conditionally essential amino acid with a positive side chain at physiologic pH.

lJXv8_.title: Aspartate
lJXv8_.description: A nonessential amino acid with a negatively-charged side group at physiologic pH.

NJX-8_.title: Sodium phenylbutyrate
NJX-8_.description: A precursor to sodium phenylacetate that is used to treat hyperammonemia by promoting the excretion of nitrogen precursors.

mJXVu_.title: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure
mJXVu_.description: The mean pressure in the pulmonary artery over the course of the cardiac cycle. Can be calculated using direct measures taken during cardiac catheterization or estimated noninvasively on echocardiography. Elevated mPAP (e.g., > 20-25 mm Hg) is indicative of pulmonary hypertension.

LJXwu_.title: Gasping breathing
LJXwu_.description: A form of slow, irregular breathing seen imminently prior to or in the early stages of cardiac arrest. Agonal breaths are thought to be part of a lower brainstem reflex, triggered by extreme hypoxia. Without intervention (e.g., CPR), respiratory efforts will cease entirely (terminal apnea).

KJXUE_.title: Atypical lymphocyte
KJXUE_.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by the presence of reactive T cells with abundant cytoplasm on peripheral blood smear. Typically associated with infectious mononucleosis but can be associated with other infections (e.g., rubella, roseola, acute HIV infection) and drug reactions.

6JXjE_.title: Efavirenz
6JXjE_.description: An antiretroviral non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor that is used for treatment of HIV infection. Adverse effects include hepatotoxicity and rash.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

pJXLE_.title: Elvitegravir
pJXLE_.description: A drug that reversibly inhibits HIV integrase, which prevents the HIV genome from integrating into host DNA. Generally well-tolerated, but adverse effects insomnia, dizziness, and increases in serum creatine kinase.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

JJXsE_.title: Fusion inhibitors
JJXsE_.description: A class of antiretroviral drugs used to treat HIV infection. Inhibits viral fusion to CD4 T cells by binding to envelope glycoprotein 41 (gp41). Enfuvirtide is the only currently approved drug in this class.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

IJXYv_.title: Maraviroc
IJXYv_.description: An antiretroviral drug that blocks the CCR5 receptor on the surface of T cells and monocytes needed for some HIV genotypes to infect cells.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

rJXfv_.title: Dolutegravir
rJXfv_.description: A drug that reversibly inhibits HIV integrase, which prevents the HIV genome from integrating into host DNA. Generally well-tolerated, but adverse effects insomnia, dizziness, and increases in serum creatine kinase.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

HJXKv_.title: Muller maneuver
HJXKv_.description: A maneuver used to evaluate airway collapse (e.g. in the setting of OSA). After forced expiration, the patient attempts inspiration with a closed mouth and nose, which leads to airway collapse that can be detected via hypopharyngoscopy.

sJXtv_.title: Cysteine
sJXtv_.description: A nonessential amino acid synthesized from essential amino acids. Can form covalent disulfide bonds with other cysteine residues in a polypeptide to create cystine.

GJXBv_.title: Heparan sulfate
GJXBv_.description: A glycosaminoglycan found on cell surfaces and in the extracellular matrix. Involved in cell signaling.

tJXXD_.title: Linker histone
tJXXD_.description: A histone that binds to the nucleosome and linker DNA to stabilize a chromatin fiber.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

8JXOD_.title: Hydrocodone
8JXOD_.description: An opioid used primarily in pain management in combination with acetaminophen and/or ibuprofen. Carries a high risk of addiction.

uJXpD_.title: Teratogen
uJXpD_.description: An environmental factor that disturbs the normal development of a developing fetus (e.g., by causing cell death or interfering with cellular differentiation), which can result in malformations and/or birth defects. Classes of teratogens include radiation, maternal infections, chemicals, and drugs.

EJX8D_.title: Ketogenesis
EJX8D_.description: The production of ketone bodies. The key enzyme involved in this process is HMG-CoA synthase.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Ketone body metabolism

DJX1w_.title: Principle of double effect
DJX1w_.description: The prioritization of a drug's positive effects with relatively less concern paid to potential adverse effects. This is a crucial aspect of hospice care, a setting in which several medications (e.g., opioids, benzodiazepines, sedatives) are used more liberally despite the potential for adverse effects (e.g., respiratory depression, dependence).

wJXhw_.title: V2 receptor
wJXhw_.description: A class of vasopressin receptors that are coupled to a Gs-protein. Activation upregulates the insertion of aquaporin-2 channels on the luminal surface of principle cells resulting in increased water permeability and reabsorption in the collecting tubules of the kidney.

9JXNw_.title: Gut-associated lymphatic tissue
9JXNw_.description: A component of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue that consists of immune cells of the gastrointestinal tract, including lymphocytes and antigen-presenting cells. Includes the Peyer patches of the small intestine.

CJXqw_.title: Orexin
CJXqw_.description: A group of neurotransmitters that promote wakefulness and are made by neurons in the lateral hypothalamus. Loss of orexins is associated with REM sleep-related disturbances, including narcolepsy, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and hypnagogic hallucinations.

xJXEw_.title: Urea transporter A1
xJXEw_.description: A urea transporter located whose activity at the apical tubular cell membrane increases in response to activation of the V2 receptor. Facilitates urea reabsorption in the inner medullary collecting duct.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Urine production

BJXzw_.title: Carbaminohemoglobin
BJXzw_.description: A compound of carbon dioxide bound to hemoglobin at the N-terminus of globin.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen and carbon dioxide transport

AJXR9_.title: Common carotid artery
AJXR9_.description: A pair of vessels that are the main arterial supply to the head and neck. The left CCA arises directly from the aortic arch; the right CCA is a branch of the right brachiocephalic trunk. Contained within the carotid sheath and terminate by bifurcating into the external and internal carotid arteries at the upper border of the thyroid cartilage.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

media.title: Branches of the external carotid artery

zJXr9_.title: Basilar artery
zJXr9_.description: An artery formed by the confluence of the two vertebral arteries at the central groove of the pons. Lies in the central pontine groove and bifurcates into the posterior cerebral arteries at the upper pontine border. Its paired lateral branches include the superior cerebellar arteries, pontine arteries, labyrinthine arteries, and anterior inferior cerebellar arteries.

media.title: Course and segments of the vertebral artery

-JXD9_.title: Homogentisic acid
-JXD9_.description: An intermediate of tyrosine degradation. Elevated serum or urine levels are seen in patients with alkaptonuria due to defective homogentisic acid dioxygenase.

ZqXZC_.title: Chloride shift
ZqXZC_.description: The mass movement of chloride ions from the extracellular space to the intracellular space of erythrocytes. CO2 diffuses into the erythrocyte, where it is catalyzed to form carbonic acid, which then dissociates to form H+ and HCO3- ions. Intracellular HCO3- ions are exchanged for extracellular Cl- ions by Band 3 protein to maintain cellular osmolality and increase the intracellular diffusion of CO2.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen and carbon dioxide transport

0qXeC_.title: Bohr effect
0qXeC_.description: A physiologic phenomenon in which increased serum carbon dioxide (increased H+ concentration, decreased pH) results in reduced affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen (right shift of the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve), which facilitates oxygen loading in the lungs and unloading in the peripheral tissues.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen and carbon dioxide transport

YqXnC_.title: Great cerebral vein
YqXnC_.description: A deep cerebral vein formed by the union of the two internal cerebral veins and the basal veins (of Rosenthal). It drains into the straight sinus.

cqXax_.title: 2,4-Dinitrophenol
cqXax_.description: An organic compound used as an off-label weight loss drug. Uncouples oxidative phosphorylation and increases membrane permeability, which leads to decreased proton gradient and ATP production as well as increased oxygen consumption and thermogenesis.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Clinical significance

1qX2x_.title: Adipokines
1qX2x_.description: A group of cytokines secreted by adipose tissue that regulate the inflammatory response. Examples include leptin, adiponectin, and omentin.

WqXPx_.title: ATP synthase
WqXPx_.description: An enzyme in the mitochondrial inner membrane, which is the final enzyme of the electron transport chain. Uses energy from the proton gradient to add a phosphate to ADP to make ATP.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Electron transport chain and ATP synthesis

eqXxx_.title: Hyperosmolarity
eqXxx_.description: A condition in which the blood is more concentrated (e.g., with sodium, glucose, and other substances) than normal. Occurs during diabetic ketoacidosis and hyperglycemic hyperosmolar syndrome.

UqXbB_.title: Homogentisic acid dioxygenase
UqXbB_.description: An enzyme involved in tyrosine metabolism that catalyzes the degradation of homogentisate to 4-maleylacetoacetate. Defect of this enzyme is the underlying cause of alkaptonuria.

2qXTB_.title: Leptomeningeal angioma
2qXTB_.description: A benign vascular tumor involving the leptomeninges (the arachnoid and pia mater). A common finding in patients with Sturge-Weber syndrome.

fqXkB_.title: Diencephalon
fqXkB_.description: A secondary brain vesicle that arises during the 5th week of embryonic development from the prosencephalon. Gives rise to the thalamus, hypothalamus, subthalamic nuclei, pineal gland, optic nerve, retina, and 3rd ventricle.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Embryology of the brain

media.title: Anatomical illustration of the thalamus and hypothalamus

SqXyB_.title: Sodium-calcium exchanger
