SqXyB_.description: A transmembrane antiporter that imports 3 sodium ions down a concentration gradient in exchange for 1 calcium ion against a concentration gradient.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Urine production

hqXcy_.title: Catalase
hqXcy_.description: An enzyme that converts hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen gas. Used to protect cells from reactive oxygen species.

3qXSy_.title: Automaticity of the heart
3qXSy_.description: The ability of cardiac cells to spontaneously depolarize.

iqXJy_.title: Lactase
iqXJy_.description: An enzyme in the small intestine responsible for the breakdown of lactose into glucose and galactose.

QqXuy_.title: 25α-hydroxylase
QqXuy_.description: A hepatic enzyme that converts D3 (cholecalciferol) to 25-hydroxyvitamin D.

jqX_y_.title: Extraocular muscles
jqX_y_.description: A set of seven muscles within the orbit that control the movement of the eyeball and superior eyelid. Includes the levator palpebrae superioris, superior rectus, inferior rectus, medial rectus, lateral rectus, inferior oblique, and superior oblique.

PqXWA_.title: Ovarian hyperthecosis
PqXWA_.description: A rare condition of unknown etiology characterized by nests of luteinized theca cells in the ovarian stroma. Manifests with features of hyperandrogenism and insulin resistance.

4qX3A_.title: Oligoovulation
4qX3A_.description: A condition of infrequent or irregular ovulation (often defined as cycles ≥ 36 days or < 8 cycles per year).

kqXmA_.title: Cell-mediated immunity
kqXmA_.description: A form of adaptive immunity mediated by cytotoxic T cells (not B cells or antibodies). Primarily responsible for protecting the body against intracellular pathogens (e.g., viruses).

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

OqXIA_.title: Watershed area
OqXIA_.description: A tissue bed supplied by distal arteriole branches from more than one arterial source. In the case of severe hypoperfusion, blood supply through these small, distal arterioles may be insufficient to meet metabolic demands, resulting in ischemia.

lqXvA_.title: Superior cerebellar artery
lqXvA_.description: A branch of the basilar artery that supplies the superior surface of the cerebellum, superior and middle cerebellar peduncles, and the midbrain.

NqX-A_.title: Brainstem
NqX-A_.description: The caudal part of the brain, which consists of the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata. Functions include control of visual and auditory reflexes, regulation of autonomic functions (e.g., circulation, respiration, gastrointestinal activity, salivation, lacrimation), and hosting several sensory and motor pathways.

mqXV__.title: Median thyroid anlage
mqXV__.description: An endodermal thickening in the floor of the primordial pharynx that differentiates into the follicular cells of the thyroid gland.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Embryology

MqXM__.title: Parathyroid gland
MqXM__.description: A set of two pairs of endocrine glands that secrete parathyroid hormone. The superior glands are located near the superior pole of the thyroid gland at the junction of cricoid and thyroid cartilages. The inferior glands are located in the area between the inferior poles of the thyroid lobes and the superior mediastinum.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands → Parathyroid glands

KqXUz_.title: Myosin light-chain kinase
KqXUz_.description: An enzyme in myocytes that phosphorylates a serine residue on the regulatory light chain of myosin II. Phosphorylation of myosin allows myosin to form a crossbridge with actin, which results in muscle contraction. This enyzme is activated by a calcium-calmodulin complex.

6qXjz_.title: Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency
6qXjz_.description: A neurodegenerative disorder caused by abnormal mitochondrial metabolism (dysfunction of the citric acid cycle), which results in lactate buildup. Manifests with nonspecific symptoms (e.g., lethargy, poor feeding, tachypnea). Severe dysfunction manifests early in life and is associated with poorer prognosis.

JqXsz_.title: Histiocyte
JqXsz_.description: A macrophage found in tissues (i.e., not the blood). Has large amounts of pink cytoplasm. Can form granulomas with giant cells and lymphocytes.

qqXCz_.title: Th2 cell
qqXCz_.description:
A subset of helper T-cells that promotes the B-cell response and production of antibodies. Secretes IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, 
 IL-10, and IL-13.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

IqXY-_.title: Islet amyloid polypeptide
IqXY-_.description: A polypeptide that is co-secreted with insulin from pancreatic β cells. It inhibits glucagon secretion, delays gastric emptying, and increases satiety. Amylin analogs (e.g., pramlintide) can be used for glycemic control. Accumulation of pro-amylin aggregates in the pancreas is thought to play a role in the pathogenesis of type II diabetes.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Regulation of appetite and satiety

7qX4-_.title: Insulitis
7qX4-_.description: The infiltration of the islets of Langerhans by lymphocytes, which can result in autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells. Seen in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus.

HqXK-_.title: γ-glutamyl carboxylase
HqXK-_.description: An enzyme that activates vitamin K-dependent proteins (i.e., factors II, VII, IX, X, protein C, protein S) by converting their glutamic acid moiety into γ-carboxyglutamic acid.

sqXt-_.title: Hydrolase
sqXt-_.description: An enzyme that cleaves substrates by breaking covalent bonds using water molecules. Hydrolases that play a critical role in the degradation of cellular molecules include lipases, esterases, proteases, and glucosidases.

destinations.label: Enzymes and biocatalysis → Classes of enzymes

GqXB-_.title: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis
GqXB-_.description: A neuroendocrine system that regulates several physiologic processes, including the stress response, metabolism, and the immune system. Involves release of corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) by the hypothalamus, which stimulates the release of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) from the anterior pituitary, which in turn regulates release of glucocorticoids by the adrenal cortex.

tqXXZz.title: Residual confounding
tqXXZz.description: The presence of additional unmeasured factors that confound the relationship between an exposure and an outcome that cannot be controlled for in an analysis.

FqXgZz.title: All-cause mortality
FqXgZz.description: The total number of deaths that occur in a given population, regardless of cause.

uqXpZz.title: Ectopic
uqXpZz.description: A descriptor for an abnormal site or position (e.g., ectopic pregnancy).

EqX8Zz.title: Pharynx
EqX8Zz.description: The mucosa-lined cavity behind the nose and mouth that connects to the esophagus.

vqXAZz.title: Thyroid isthmus
vqXAZz.description: The component of the thyroid that stretches over the trachae and connects the two thyroid lobes.

DqX10z.title: Branchial cleft
DqX10z.description: The external ectodermal grooves between consecutive branchial arches. The first cleft develops into the external auditory meatus. Failure of obliteration can result in a branchial cleft cyst. The 2–4th clefts are obliterated in-utero.

wqXh0z.title: Foramen cecum (tongue)
wqXh0z.description: A small, midline indentation in the posterior aspect of the tongue. The embryologic remnant of the duct from which the thyroid gland developed.

9qXN0z.title: Interviewer bias
9qXN0z.description: A type of information bias in which different interviewing approaches towards exposed and unexposed groups, or cases and controls, prompt different responses between groups and the conclusion that there are systematic differences between groups when there are in fact none.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

CqXq0z.title: Valine
CqXq0z.description: An essential, purely glucogenic amino acid with a branched aliphatic side chain.

xqXE0z.title: Monoamine neurotransmitter
xqXE0z.description: A group of neurotransmitters that have a single amino group connected to an aromatic ring. Examples include dopamine, serotonin, and epinephrine.

BqXz0z.title: Phosphoprotein p24
BqXz0z.description: A capsid protein of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). It is coded for by the group-specific antigen (gag) region of HIV genetic material. Immunoassays that detect p24 protein are used as screening tests for HIV infection.

yqXdaz.title: Glutaminase
yqXdaz.description: An enzyme that hydrolyzes glutamine to glutamate and ammonium (irreversible reaction). Isoenzymes are found in the brain to generate the neurotransmitter glutamate, or in the kidney, where ammonium excretion contributes to maintaining acid-base balance.

destinations.label: Amino acids →  Biochemical reactions of amino acid metabolism

-qXDaz.title: Tryptophan
-qXDaz.description: An essential, aromatic amino acid with hydrophobic properties. Used to synthesize niacin and serotonin.

0IXeYz.title: Survival bias
0IXeYz.description: A type of selection bias that occurs when the disease risk or the effect of an exposure is estimated using only individuals who have survived without experiencing the outcome of interest at the time of measurement. Excluding those who experienced the outcome before the time of measurement can underestimate the true effect of the exposure.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

aIXQYz.title: Inferior vena cava
aIXQYz.description: The main vessel that receives venous drainage from the lower extremities, pelvis, and abdomen and delivers it to the right atrium of the heart.

media.title: Abdominal aorta and inferior vena cava

YIXnYz.title: Renal medulla
YIXnYz.description: The innermost portion of the kidney, which contains the renal pyramids.

XIX9Yz.title: Collecting duct
XIX9Yz.description: The final segment of the nephron, which is involved in electrolyte homeostasis. Major cell types of the collecting duct include alpha cells (for acid secretion), beta cells (for bicarbonate secretion), and principal cells (for water and sodium absorption and potassium secretion).

1IX2bz.title: Gömöri trichrome stain
1IX2bz.description: A type of histological stain used to evaluate muscle tissue (e.g., in cases of mitochondrial myopathy).

WIXPbz.title: Allosteric regulation
WIXPbz.description: A phenomenon in which the binding of a ligand to a protein's allosteric site switches the protein from one conformational state to another and thereby alters the protein's functional activity (V-type allosteric modulation) and/or the affinity of additional ligands for the same protein's active site (K-type allosteric modulation). Follows Hill kinetics. Can also be classified as positive or negative allosteric modulation (based on whether the protein's functional activity and active site binding are increased or decreased) or as heterotropic or homotropic allosteric modulation (based on whether different ligands or the same ligand interact at the allosteric site and active site).

dIXobz.title: Inverse agonist
dIXobz.description: A molecule that binds to the same receptor as the agonist but has a different binding site. Results in the opposite effect of an agonistic response.

UIXbXz.title: Tactile agnosia
UIXbXz.description: Inability to recognize objects by touch using texture, shape, and temperature as cues without visual input. Caused by a lesion in the contralateral parietal lobe (areas 5 and 7).

2IXTXz.title: Interstitial cell of Cajal​​​​​​​
2IXTXz.description: A cell found in the smooth muscle of the gastrointestinal tract. Acts as a pacemaker that creates the bioelectrical slow wave potential, which is the basis for peristalsis. Thought to be the cell of origin of gastrointestinal stromal tumors.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Enteric nervous system

gIXFXz.title: Periarteriolar lymphatic sheath
gIXFXz.description: A region of splenic white matter composed of lymphocytes that encircle splenic arterioles. Consists primarily of CD4+ T-cells. Serves as the site of plasma cell formation.

iIXJcz.title: Presenilin-1
iIXJcz.description: The protein product of the gene PSEN1. Associated with the production of amyloid beta from amyloid precursor protein. Mutations are associated with early-onset Alzheimer dementia.

QIXucz.title: Anal canal
QIXucz.description: The distal portion of the large intestine. Divided by the pectinate line into an upper portion (derived from endoderm, supplied by the superior rectal artery, has visceral innervation) and a lower portion (derived from ectoderm, supplied by the inferior rectal artery, has somatic innervation).

jIX_cz.title: Inosine-5′-monophosphate dehydrogenase
jIX_cz.description: A purine metabolic enzyme that, in the presence of NAD+, converts inosine monophosphate (IMP) to xanthosine monophosphate (XMP), which subsequently gets converted to guanosine monophosphate (GMP). Inhibited by mycophenolate mofetil and ribavirin

PIXW1z.title: Amyloid precursor protein
PIXW1z.description: A precursor protein that, when cleaved, produces beta amyloid. The gene that encodes APP is located on chromosome 21 and is associated with familial cases of Alzheimer dementia.

kIXm1z.title: Amyloid beta
kIXm1z.description: A peptide of roughly 40 amino acids that is derived from amyloid precursor protein. Constitutes the major component of the amyloid plaques seen in patients with Alzheimer disease.

media.title: Amyloid-β plaque formation in Alzheimer disease

OIXI1z.title: Piebaldism
OIXI1z.description: A rare, autosomal dominant disorder characterized by dysfunctional proliferation and migration of melanoblasts, which results in an abnormal distribution of melanocytes that manifests with patchy depigmentation (e.g., white forelock). Caused by mutations in the cell-surface receptor tyrosine kinase gene.

lIXv1z.title: Autologous
lIXv1z.description: A term that usually describes cells or tissue components that are removed from a patient and used for transfusion or transplant back to the same patient.

NIX-1z.title: Inferior epigastric vein
NIX-1z.description: A vein that anastomoses with the superior epigastric vein and drains into the external iliac vein. With the inferior epigastric artery, it forms part of the lateral border of the inguinal triangle.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

mIXVWz.title: Azygos vein
mIXVWz.description: A vein that forms around the T12 vertebral level by the anastomosis of the right subcostal vein and the right ascending lumbar vein. Passes through the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm and courses in front of the vertebral bodies. Drains into the superior vena cava at the level of T4.

5IXiWz.title: Short gastric veins
5IXiWz.description: A group of 4-5 small veins that drain into the splenic vein and form part of the portal system. They drain the fundus and part of the greater curvature of the stomach. These veins can become distended in portal hypertension, causing gastric varices.

media.title: Tributaries of the hepatic portal vein

MIXMWz.title: Mediastinum
MIXMWz.description: The space between the medial surfaces of the lungs that extends longitudinally from the sternum to the diaphragm and anteroposteriorly from the sternum to the vertebrae. Further divided into the superior and inferior mediastinum.

nIX7Wz.title: Anterior mediastinum
nIX7Wz.description: The portion of the inferior mediastinum that occupies the space between the lungs that extends from the sternum to the anterior pericardium of the heart. Contains the thymus, lymph nodes, and fat.

LIXwWz.title: Middle mediastinum
LIXwWz.description: The portion of the inferior mediastinum that occupies the space between the lungs that is enclosed within the fibrous pericardium. Contains the heart, origins of the great vessels, and the bifurcation of the trachea.

oIX0dz.title: Langer lines of skin tension
oIX0dz.description: The topographic lines on the body that correlate with the natural orientation of the reticular fibers of the reticular dermis. Used to guide surgical incisions so as to ensure optimal wound healing.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Structure of the skin

KIXUdz.title: Posterior mediastinum
KIXUdz.description: The portion of the inferior mediastinum that occupies the space between the lungs that extends anteroposteriorily from the heart to the vertebral bodies. Contains the esophagus, the descending thoracic aorta, the azygous and hemiazygous veins, the thoracic duct, and lymph nodes.

6IXjdz.title: Superior mediastinum
6IXjdz.description: The space between the lungs that lies above the pericardium (approximately the level of the sternal angle). Contains the arch of the aorta (and origins of its branches), the superior vena cava (and its tributaries), and portions of the esophagus, trachea, thoracic duct, and the thymus.

pIXLdz.title: Normocytic anemia
pIXLdz.description: A type of anemia that is characterized by red blood cells of normal size (with a mean corpuscular volume of 80–100 fL). Etiologies include hemolytic anemias, acute bleeding, and early anemia of chronic disease.

JIXsdz.title: Globus pallidus
JIXsdz.description: A part of the basal ganglia involved in regulating voluntary movement. Lies medial to the putamen and consists of the internal globus pallidus (GPi) and the external globus pallidus (GPe).

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

IIXYVz.title: Hemiazygous vein
IIXYVz.description: The continuation of the left ascending lumbar vein that enters the thorax through the aortic hiatus. Receives blood from the left hemithorax (posterior intercostal veins and left subcostal vein) and the left lower esophagus. Drains into the azygous vein.

rIXfVz.title: Cori cycle
rIXfVz.description: The metabolic cycle in which pyruvate is reduced to lactate via lactate dehydrogenase in cells undergoing anaerobic glycolysis (e.g., skeletal muscle). Lactate is transported to the liver, where it is converted into glucose. It is then transported back to the muscles for energy production.

HIXKVz.title: Penis
HIXKVz.description: Genitourinary organ present in males that is responsible for the transfer of sperm from the testes and transfer of urine from the bladder.

media.title: Median section of the male pelvis with detail of a testicle

sIXtVz.title: Glans penis
sIXtVz.description: The distal end of the corpus spongiosum in males. Contains the external urethral meatus.

media.title: Median section of the male pelvis with detail of a testicle

GIXBVz.title: Urethral glands
GIXBVz.description: A type of mucus-secreting gland along the wall of the male urethra. The mucus protects the epithelium against urine.

DIX1Uz.title: Seminal vesicles
DIX1Uz.description: A paired set of glandular structures attached to the posterior part of the urinary bladder. Connected to a duct that merges with the vas deferens to create the ejaculatory duct, which then empties into the prostatic urethra. Secretions from the seminal vesicles, ductus deferens, and prostate contribute to the semen (ejaculatory fluid).

destinations.label: Male reproductive organs → Epididymis, ductus deferens, and accessory glands

CIXqUz.title: Testes
CIXqUz.description: A pair of ellipsoid-shaped male reproductive structures that are composed of seminiferous tubules surrounded by a thick capsule (the tunica albuginea). Connected to the abdominal wall via the spermatic cords.

destinations.label: Male reproductive organs → Testes, scrotum, and spermatic cord

xIXEUz.title: Sperm
xIXEUz.description: The mature male gametes (i.e., mature spermatozoa), which consist of a head formed by an acrosome and nucleus and a tail formed by a midpiece (mitochondria and microtubules), principal piece (flagellum), and end piece.

0rXefz.title: Prostate gland
0rXefz.description: An accessory organ of reproduction composed of glandular, fibrous, and smooth muscle tissue. Located within the pelvis, posterior to the pubic symphysis, inferior to the bladder, anterior to the rectum, and superior to the perineal membrane. Secretes various substances that help to liquefy semen after ejaculation.

arXQfz.title: HMG-CoA lyase
arXQfz.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of HMG-CoA to acetyl-CoA and acetoacetate. Essential for the formation of ketone bodies in the liver.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Ketone body metabolism

YrXnfz.title: T tubule
YrXnfz.description: A transverse tubular invagination of the cell membrane (sarcolemma) of striated muscle fibers. Contacts the sarcoplasmic reticulum and facilitates coordinated contraction of striated muscles.

XrX9fz.title: Meninges
XrX9fz.description: A trio of membranes that consists of the dura mater, arachnoid mater, and pia mater. Lines the cranium and spinal canal and acts as an enveloping layer to protect and nourish CNS structures.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

crXaTz.title: Oncogene
crXaTz.description: A previously normal gene (proto-oncogene) that has undergone mutation resulting in a gain of function and now has the potential to cause cancer. Examples include BRAF (melanoma, papillary thyroid cancer), N-myc (neuroblastoma), and BCR-ABL (CML, ALL).

frXkgz.title: Staging (oncology)
frXkgz.description: An assessment of the disease stage of cancer. Factors evaluated include the size and extent of the main tumor, number of nearby lymph nodes involved, and metastasis. Used to evaluate prognosis and guide management.

TrX6gz.title: Colitis
TrX6gz.description: An inflammation of colonic tissue. Etiologies include infection, allergic reaction, ischemia, and inflammatory bowel disease.

grXFgz.title: Dura mater
grXFgz.description: The outermost meningeal layer. Derived from mesoderm. Forms the epidural space.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

media.title: Transverse section of the lumbar spine

SrXygz.title: Arachnoid mater
SrXygz.description: The middle meningeal layer. Derived from neural crest. Forms the outer layer of the subarachnoid space.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

hrXcSz.title: Pia mater
hrXcSz.description: The innermost meningeal layer. Derived from neural crest. Forms the inner layer of the subarachnoid space.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

3rXSSz.title: Falx cerebelli
3rXSSz.description: A small, sickle-shaped fold of the dura mater that partially separates the two cerebellar hemispheres.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

RrXlSz.title: Tentorium cerebelli
RrXlSz.description: A fold of the dura mater in the axial plane that separates the cranial cavity into infratentorial and supratentorial compartments.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

irXJSz.title: Motor homunculus
irXJSz.description: A somatotopic representation of the body in the motor cortex. The body is represented in an upside-down manner, with the toes at the superior end and the face and tongue at the inferior end of the motor cortex. The cortical area for each body part is directly related to the degree of innervation of that part (e.g., the hands have larger areas of cortical representation than the lower extremities).

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

QrXuSz.title: Myosatellite cells
QrXuSz.description: A skeletal muscle cell precursor responsible for the regeneration of muscle and other myosatellite cells in response to injury.

PrXWhz.title: Astrocyte
PrXWhz.description: A star-shaped, glial cell of the central nervous system that supports the epithelial cells of the blood-brain barrier, maintains extracellular osmotic homeostasis, and moderates the healing and scarring process.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

4rX3hz.title: Microglia
4rX3hz.description: The macrophages of the central nervous system, which activate in response to tissue damage. Derived from mesoderm.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

krXmhz.title: Myelin
krXmhz.description: An electrical insulator that increases the conduction velocity of electrical signals transmitted along axons in the nervous system. Formed by oligodendrocytes (central nervous system) and Schwann cells (peripheral nervous system).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

OrXIhz.title: Tanycytes
OrXIhz.description: A type of ependymal glial cell located mainly on the floor of the third and fourth ventricles. They play a role in glucose homeostasis and transport substances between the blood and ventricles. Derived from radial glial cells of the neuroepithelium (neuroectoderm).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

5rXi3z.title: Positive-pressure ventilation
5rXi3z.description: The artificial ventilation of a patient's lungs with external positive pressure during the inspiratory cycle of respiration.

MrXM3z.title: Motilin
MrXM3z.description: A gastrointestinal hormone produced by Mo cells in the small intestine (particularly during the fasting state). Stimulates peristalsis and gallbladder contraction.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

LrXw3z.title: Anal valves
LrXw3z.description: A group of transverse folds that connect the distal end of the anal columns.

KrXURz.title: Lipofuscin
KrXURz.description: A cellular pigment that results from deposition of lipid-containing, lysosomal degradation products in the tissues. Deposition increases with age and results in yellow-brown deposits seen on histopathologic examination.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cellular adaptation

6rXjRz.title: Free radical damage
6rXjRz.description: A cellular injury that occurs due to exposure to free radicals and/or reactive oxygen species. Results in lipid peroxidation of cellular membranes, protein denaturation, breakage of DNA, and cell death.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Free radical injury
DNA replication and repair → Mechanisms of DNA damage

prXLRz.title: Squamous cell carcinoma
prXLRz.description: A malignant epithelial cancer that arises from squamous cells. Common sites of origin include the lung, head and neck, skin, and esophagus.

media.title: Keratin pearls in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC)

JrXsRz.title: Carcinoma in situ
JrXsRz.description: A group of irreversibly dysplastic cells that involve the entire thickness of the epithelium but do not invade the basement membrane. Has a high probability of progression into cancer.

IrXYiz.title: Metastasis
IrXYiz.description: The dissemination of cancer cells from the site of the primary tumor to another part of the body.

rrXfiz.title: Senile amyloidosis
rrXfiz.description: The deposition of transthyretin protein in the tissues (particularly the heart). Can cause cardiomegaly and heart failure due to infiltrative cardiomyopathy.

7rX4iz.title: Aerobic metabolism
7rX4iz.description: A mechanism for the production of ATP that requires oxygen and produces CO2 and water. Involves glycolysis, the TCA cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation via the electron transport chain.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Overview

HrXKiz.title: Anaerobic metabolism
HrXKiz.description: A biochemical pathway for the production of ATP that does not require oxygen. It involves glycolysis and reduction of pyruvate to lactate.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Necrosis
Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Overview

srXtiz.title: Parenchyma
srXtiz.description: The functional part(s) of an organ, as opposed to the organ's structural framework and capsule.

GrXBiz.title: Adrenal capsule
GrXBiz.description: Fibrous outer layer that surrounds the adrenal cortex.

8rXOQz.title: Herpesviridae
8rXOQz.description: A family of enveloped viruses with a linear, double-stranded DNA structure. Includes herpes simplex viruses 1 and 2, varicella zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and human herpesviruses 6, 7, and 8.

urXpQz.title: Neuroendocrine cell
urXpQz.description: A specialized cell that receives neuronal (nervous system) input and releases hormonal (endocrine) output. Typically stains positive for chromogranin and synaptophysin.

media.title: Sympathetic innervation of the adrenal medulla

vrXAQz.title: Denys-Drash syndrome
vrXAQz.description: A rare congenital condition caused by a sporadic point mutation of the WT1 gene on chromosome 11, which leads to a defect in zinc finger transcription factor. Patients present with Wilms tumor, urogenital deformities such as male pseudohermaphroditism, and mesangial renal sclerosis resulting in nephrotic syndrome.

DrX1jz.title: Internal hemorrhoid
DrX1jz.description: A type of hemorrhoid that arises above the pectinate line from the superior hemorrhoidal plexus. Not typically painful.

wrXhjz.title: External hemorrhoid
wrXhjz.description: A type of hemorrhoid that arises below the pectinate line from the inferior hemorrhoidal plexus. Can be painful.

CrXqjz.title: Odontoblast
CrXqjz.description: A cell involved in the formation of dentin in teeth. Originates from neural crest cells.

xrXEjz.title: Ectocervical cancer
xrXEjz.description: A type of cervical cancer that originates from squamous cells of the ectocervix.

media.title: Pap smear: tools, sample collection, and sample preparation

BrXzjz.title: Liposarcoma
BrXzjz.description: A soft tissue sarcoma that arises from precursors of adipocytes. Most commonly develop in the extremities and retroperitoneum.

ArXRPz.title: Myeloblast
ArXRPz.description: An immature white blood cell that can differentiate into a neutrophil, eosinophil, or basophil.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

_rX5Pz.title: Cytopenia
_rX5Pz.description: Decreased number of blood cells. May refer to decreased white blood cells, red blood cells, platelets and/or combination of all three.

zrXrPz.title: c-myc gene
zrXrPz.description: A proto-oncogene that codes for a transcription factor of the MYC family and is often found to be overexpressed in various kinds of tumors (e.g., cervical cancer, colon cancer, Burkitt lymphoma).

-rXDPz.title: CDK4
-rXDPz.description: A serine/threonine kinase activated by cyclin D that phosphorylates the retinoblastoma protein, which leads to the release of E2F. This promotes cell cycle progression from  G1 phase to S phase.

media.title: Cell cycle regulation: cyclins and cyclin-dependent kinases

b7XH4z.title: Mismatch repair gene
b7XH4z.description: A collection of genes that encode proteins that recognize and excise mismatched nucleotides in newly synthesized DNA strands. Essential for the maintenance of genomic stability. Examples include MLH1 and MSH2.

c7Xakz.title: Mild cognitive impairment
c7Xakz.description: A condition of cognitive decline that does not compromise daily functioning. May include impairments in memory and/or in other cognitive domains, such as concentration and attention. Affected individuals are often aware of these deficits. May progress to dementia.

17X2kz.title: Medium spiny neuron
17X2kz.description: A GABAergic neuron that sends inhibitory projections to nuclei of the basal ganglia. Makes up ~95% of the neurons in the striatum.

W7XPkz.title: Receptor tyrosine kinase
W7XPkz.description: A transmembrane receptor generally activated by ligand-induced dimerization and autophosphorylation of cytoplasmic tyrosine residues, which triggers activation of downstream signaling cascades. Involved in cellular proliferation, differentiation, and migration. Gain-of-function mutations or receptor/ligand overexpression can cause cancer.

d7Xokz.title: Epidermal growth factor receptor
d7Xokz.description: A transmembrane glycoprotein with tyrosine kinase activity that binds to different epidermal growth factors. Ligand binding induces dimerization of the receptor and tyrosine autophosphorylation, which leads to activation of various processes, such as cell proliferation, differentiation, adhesion, migration, and inhibition of apoptosis. Mutations in EGFR gene are associated with several epithelial cancers.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

V7XGkz.title: Vasculogenesis
V7XGkz.description: The de novo formation of blood vessels.

e7Xxkz.title: Certolizumab
e7Xxkz.description: A humanized, monoclonal antibody against TNF-α used to treat several inflammatory conditions such as inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

U7XbOz.title: Golimumab
U7XbOz.description: A humanized, monoclonal antibody against TNF-α used to treat several inflammatory conditions such as inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

27XTOz.title: Soma
27XTOz.description: The region of a cell (typically used in reference to a neuron or other brain cell) that contains the nucleus as well as surrounding cytoplasm and other organelles (e.g., Nissl bodies).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

f7XkOz.title: Dendrite
f7XkOz.description: A small projection of neuronal cytoplasm. Typically involved in reception of intercellular signaling.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

T7X6Oz.title: Axon
T7X6Oz.description: The projection from a neuron's cell body along which action potentials travel to send intercellular signals. Ends in a synapse.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

S7XyOz.title: Artery of Adamkiewicz
S7XyOz.description: A thoracic radicular artery (branch of the intercostal vasculature) that supplies the lower two-thirds of the spinal cord (below T8) via the anterior spinal artery. Due to the lack of collateral blood supply to the spinal cord below the level of T8, occlusion of the artery of Adamkiewiz commonly leads to anterior spinal artery syndrome.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy
Incomplete spinal cord syndromes → Anterior cord syndrome

h7Xclz.title: Oncocyte
h7Xclz.description: An eosinophilic epithelial cell characterized by granular cytoplasm, which is due to abundant mitochondria.

Q7Xulz.title: Prostaglandin F2α
Q7Xulz.description: A signaling molecule derived from arachidonic acid that induces uterine and bronchiolar smooth muscle contractions. Used in the termination of intrauterine pregnancies, to induce labor, and for the treatment of glaucoma.

media.title: Arachidonic acid metabolism and interfering drugs

j7X_lz.title: Obligate anaerobe
j7X_lz.description: A microorganism that only grows in the absence of oxygen. Lacks enzymes that protect against oxidative stress (e.g., catalase and superoxide dismutase). Examples include the Bacteroides and Clostridium species, most species of Fusobacterium, and a few species of Actinomyces.

P7XWNz.title: Cerebellar Purkinje cell
P7XWNz.description: A large, cerebellar GABAergic neuron with extensive dendritic projections. Plays a role in controlling movement.

47X3Nz.title: Sonic hedgehog gene
47X3Nz.description: A gene on the long arm of chromosome 7 that codes for a signaling protein involved in CNS, ocular, craniofacial, and limb development. It is responsible for formation of a midline in the ventral forebrain and primitive eye field. In the limb bud, it is expressed primarily at the base in the zone of polarizing activity and is responsible for maintaining anteroposterior limb polarity in the embryo (i.e., radioulnar or mediolateral limb polarity in the fetus). A defect in this gene can cause holoprosencephaly, cyclopia, craniofacial defects (e.g., cleft palate), and limb defects.

destinations.label: Basics of embryology → Molecular biology of embryogenesis

k7XmNz.title: Collagen, type I, alpha
k7XmNz.description: Genes that encodes collagen Type I alpha chain including (COL1A1 and COL1A2). Mutations in these genes are associated with osteogenesis imperfecta, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, and osteoporosis.

O7XINz.title: Mammillary bodies
O7XINz.description: A part of the diencephalon and limbic system located on the inferior part of the brain. Atrophy of these structures is associated with Wernicke encephalopathy.

l7XvNz.title: Larva currens
l7XvNz.description: Raised, pruritic, serpiginous rash that is pathognomonic of Strongyloides stercoralis infection and caused by migration of larvae under the skin.

L7Xwmz.title: Migratory motor complexes
L7Xwmz.description: Distinct peristaltic waves occurring during the interdigestive period that are triggered by the release of motilin and other mechanisms. Promotes the passage of undigested food through the intestine.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Innervation and gut motility

o7X05z.title: Lactotroph
o7X05z.description: An eosinophilic cell in the anterior pituitary that produces prolactin. Stimulated by thyrotropin-releasing hormone and estrogen, and tonically inhibited by dopamine.

K7XU5z.title: Michaelis-Menten plot
K7XU5z.description: A way of modeling Michaelis-Menten enzyme kinetics that relates concentration of substrate to reaction rate.

p7XL5z.title: Aromatic amino acid decarboxylase
p7XL5z.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the decarboxylation of several amino acids to form neurotransmitters (e.g., dopamine, histamine, serotonin) and neuromodulators (e..g, phenethylamine, tyramine, tryptamine). Uses active vitamin B6 as a cofactor. For the treatment of Parkinson disease, decarboxylase inhibitors (e.g., carbidopa) are used to inhibit peripheral conversion of L-DOPA to dopamine outside of the CNS.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla
Amino acids →  Biochemical reactions of amino acid metabolism

q7XC5z.title: Pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A
q7XC5z.description: A rare autosomal dominant condition which is characterized by end-organ resistance to PTH due to a defective G protein alpha subunit. Patients present with hypocalcemia despite elevated PTH synthesis. The phenotype of PHP is Albright hereditary osteodystrophy, which is characterized by short stature, a round face, short fourth and fifth metacarpal bones, and developmental delay.

I7XYMz.title: Meniscus sign
I7XYMz.description: A radiographic finding characterized by a crescent-shaped concavity formed by the accumulation of fluid at the lung bases. Can be seen in patients with a pleural effusion.

77X4Mz.title: Phrenoesophageal ligament
77X4Mz.description: A peritoneal fold that encircles the distal portion of the esophagus and gastroesophageal junction and connects them to the peritoneal surface of the diaphragm. Enables longitudinal motion of the esophagus during respiration and swallowing.

H7XKMz.title: Phrenicocolic ligament
H7XKMz.description: A peritoneal fold that extends from the splenic flexure of the colon to the peritoneal surface of the diaphragm. Supports the spleen.

s7XtMz.title: Ligamentum venosum
s7XtMz.description: The remnant of the fetal ductus venosus. Lies between the caudate lobe and left lobe of the liver (dorsal aspect). Can communicate with the portal vein. Often continues as the round ligament of the liver.

destinations.label: Prenatal and postnatal physiology →  Fetal circulation

G7XBMz.title: Multipotent
G7XBMz.description: The ability of a cell to differentiate into more than one related cell type (e.g., hematopoietic stem cells, which can differentiate into myeloid or lymphoid cells).

t7XXnz.title: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy
t7XXnz.description: An autoimmune inflammatory myopathy characterized by severe proximal muscle weakness, extremely high creatine kinase levels, and evidence of necrosis on biopsy. Most cases are idiopathic but one subtype may be induced by exposure to statins.

E7X8nz.title: Serous inflammation
E7X8nz.description: Inflammation with a thin and watery fluid that lacks fibrinogen and fibrin. Can be seen in viral serositis as well as in skin inflammation (e.g., blisters).

v7XAnz.title: Fibrinous pleuritis
v7XAnz.description: Acute pleuritis characterized by exudative inflammation, which results in fibrin and leukocyte extravasation into the pleural space.

D7X1Lz.title: Tropheryma whipplei
D7X1Lz.description:
An intracellular, gram-positive bacillus that causes Whipple disease. Stains positive on Periodic acid–Schiff
stain.

w7XhLz.title: Competitive antagonist
w7XhLz.description: A molecule that competes with an agonist for the active site of a receptor. Binding results in inhibition of the effect of the agonist in a dose-dependent fashion. The inhibitory effect can be overcome by increasing agonist concentration.

97XNLz.title: Methyl-CpG binding protein 2 gene
97XNLz.description: A gene that encodes methyl-CpG binding protein 2. Mutation (missense, frameshift, nonsense) of this gene is associated with Rett syndrome.

C7XqLz.title: Allosteric activator
C7XqLz.description: In enzyme kinetics, a molecule that reversibly binds to an enzyme at a site other than the active site, inducing a conformational change that increases affinity to the substrate. This lowers the Michaelis-Menten constant. The maximum reaction velocity remains unchanged.

x7XELz.title: Lamellar body
x7XELz.description: A secretory organelle found in type II pneumocytes and keratinocytes of the epidermis. In the lungs, they store, transport, and release surfactant. In the epidermis, they help maintain a lipid-rich permeability barrier. Appear on electron microscopy as granules with parallel stacks of membrane lamellae.

B7XzLz.title: Germinal epithelium
B7XzLz.description: The epithelium of the female and male gonads. Derived from coelomic epithelium, which lines the peritoneum.

-7XDoz.title: Plasmalogens
-7XDoz.description: A class of phospholipids that is most abundant in myelin. The biosynthesis of plasmalogens is initiated by two enzymes located in peroxisomes. Deficiency leads to abnormalities in the myelination of nerve cells.

aHXQKz.title: Agenesis
aHXQKz.description: A failure of organ growth due to the absence of primordial tissue from which the organ is derived.

YHXnKz.title: Aplasia
YHXnKz.description: An embryological abnormality in which an organ is not present although the primordial tissue from which that organ is derived exists (e.g. thymic aplasia)

cHXa6z.title: Malformation
cHXa6z.description: An embryological abnormality caused by interruption of normal development due to an intrinsic disruption (versus deformation due to extrinsic disruption). Typically occurs between weeks 3 and 8 of development. Examples include Arnold-Chiari malformation, anencephaly, holoprosencephaly, and arteriovenous malformation.

dHXo6z.title: Positive punishment
dHXo6z.description: A process by which the addition of a stimulus in response to a behavior decreases the behavior (e.g., a driver stops parking illegally in response to a fine). A feature of operant conditioning.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

VHXG6z.title: Negative punishment
VHXG6z.description: A process by which the removal of a stimulus in response to a behavior decreases the behavior (e.g., a child stops acting out because his parents take away his video games when he behaves poorly). A feature of operant conditioning.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

eHXx6z.title: Pentostatin
eHXx6z.description: A purine analog that inhibits adenosine deaminase and thus prevents the deamination of adenosine to inosine. Most often used to treat hairy cell leukemia.

UHXbpz.title: Mitochondrial respiratory chain
UHXbpz.description: A biochemical mechanism used to produce ATP. Consists of the electron transport chain, which generates an electrochemical proton gradient over the inner mitochondrial membrane, and oxidative phosphorylation, which couples the electron transport chain with ATP synthesis.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Summary

SHXypz.title: Cytochrome c
SHXypz.description: A protein of the mitochondrial electron transport chain. Activates caspases In the intrinsic pathway of apoptosis.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Electron transport chain and ATP synthesis

RHXlJz.title: Thermogenin
RHXlJz.description: A proton channel found in brown adipose tissue that physiologically uncouples electron transport and ATP synthesis to generate heat (instead of ATP).

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Clinical significance

OHXIqz.title: Malignant tumor
OHXIqz.description: A collection of rapidly dividing, abnormal cells that typically have the following characteristics: poorly differentiated, high mitotic rate, locally destructive and invasive, and able to metastasize.

oHX0rz.title: Sesamoid bones
oHX0rz.description: A bone that forms after birth within tendons or a joint capsule (e.g., patella in the knee, pisiform bone in the wrist). Acts as a fulcrum or pulley that increases a force or change its direction.

pHXLrz.title: Bone-specific alkaline phosphatase
pHXLrz.description: A bone-specific glycoprotein found on the surface of osteoblasts. Can be measured to evaluate bone metabolism; increased serum concentrations indicate increased bone turnover.

JHXsrz.title: Subdural space
JHXsrz.description: A potential space located between the arachnoid mater and dura mater. Conditions in which this space can be seen include subdural hemorrhage (due to ruptured bridging veins), empyema, and hygroma.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

qHXCrz.title: Branchial apparatus
qHXCrz.description: An embryological structure composed of five paired arches (composed of mesodermal and neural crest cells) bound externally by an ectodermal cleft and internally by an endodermal pouch. Differentiate into various head and neck structures. Is externally visible below the developing brain of a 4-week old embryo.

FHXgHz.title: Branchial arch
FHXgHz.description: A set of embryonic structures. Forms the mesenchymal core (mesodermal and neural crest cells) of the branchial apparatus. Branchial arches 1,2,3,4, and 6 form several structures (e.g., nerves, arteries, cartilages); the 5th branchial arch makes no significant contributions.

8HXOHz.title: Anaplasia
8HXOHz.description: A loss of morphologic features of cellular maturity (loss of cellular differentiation). Assessed in the grading of neoplasia.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cellular adaptation

uHXpHz.title: Branchial pouch
uHXpHz.description: The internal endodermal pouches between consecutive branchial arches. Branchial pouch derivatives include middle ear epithelium and mastoid air cells (1st pouch); tonsillar epithelium (2nd pouch); inferior parathyroids and thymus (3rd pouch); superior parathyroids (4th pouch).

EHX8Hz.title: Peripheral neuropathy
EHX8Hz.description: A condition of peripheral nerve damage characterized by distal sensory loss, burning sensations, and/or weakness. Etiologies include systemic disease (e.g., diabetes), infections (HIV), traumatic injury, vitamin deficiency, medications (e.g., chemotherapy, antibiotics), ischemia, autoimmune and vasculitic disorders, and excessive alcohol consumption.

vHXAHz.title: Retinopathy
vHXAHz.description: A disease of the retina, which can result in vision impairment. Most commonly caused by retinal vascular disease; often seen in diabetes and hypertension. Can be broadly categorized into proliferative and nonproliferative retinopathy. Loss of vision is typically insidious and, in most patients, occurs 20–30 years after disease onset. Occasionally, acute loss of vision may occur as a result of retinal detachment, vitreous hemorrhage, or macular edema.

DHX1sz.title: Thymus gland
DHX1sz.description: A primary lymphatic organ located in the anterior mediastinum where T lymphocytes are produced and mature. Is most prominent during infancy and childhood, begins to involute at puberty, and becomes atrophic in adulthood.

xHXEsz.title: CD19
xHXEsz.description: A transmembrane glycoprotein found in all cells of B-cell lineage except plasma cells. Used as a marker in the evaluation of chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

BHXzsz.title: First branchial arch
BHXzsz.description: A branchial arch that forms the maxillary process, mandibular process, malleus, incus, and muscles of mastication, the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3), and maxillary artery, and the sphenomandibular ligament, among other structures.

AHXRGz.title: Second branchial arch
AHXRGz.description: A branchial arch that forms the Reichart cartilage (stapes, styloid process, lesser horn of the hyoid), the muscles of facial expression (stapedius, stylohyoid, platysma, posterior belly of the digastric), the facial nerve (CN VII), the stapedial artery, and the stylohyoid ligament.

_HX5Gz.title: Third branchial arch
_HX5Gz.description: A branchial arch that forms the greater horn of the hyoid, stylopharyngeus muscle, glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), common carotid artery, and internal carotid artery.

-HXDGz.title: Fourth-sixth branchial arches
-HXDGz.description: A set of branchial arch derivatives that forms the thyroid cartilage, the cricoid, corniculate, cuneiform, and the arytenoids. The muscular component of the 4th arch differentiates into the pharyngeal constrictors, the cricothyroid, and levator veli palatini. The muscular component of the 6th arch differentiates into all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid. The 4th arch forms the superior laryngeal branch of the vagus nerve (CN X); the 6th arch forms the recurrent laryngeal branch of the vagus nerve. The 4th arch also contributes to the posterior third of the tongue.

0sXetz.title: Fifth branchial arch
0sXetz.description: A branchial arch derivative that regresses in utero and does not contribute to the development of any structures of the head and neck.

csXaFz.title: Hyperuricosuria
csXaFz.description: The increased urinary excretion of uric acid. Quantified as > 800 mg/day in men and > 750 mg/day in women.

WsXPFz.title: lacZ
WsXPFz.description: A gene found on the lac operon that encodes β-galactosidase, an enzyme that cleaves lactose into galactose and glucose.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Regulation of transcription

esXxFz.title: Aminoaciduria
esXxFz.description: The increased urinary excretion of amino acids. Often secondary to an inborn error of metabolism. Examples include cystinuria, phenylketonuria, and maple syrup urine disease.

UsXb8z.title: Cystine
UsXb8z.description: A compound formed when two molecules of cysteine (the sulfur-containing, non-essential amino acid) are bound by a disulfide bond. Functions as an antioxidant and is an important component of skin and hair. Not soluble in acidic urine and thus can form kidney stones. Alkalinization of urine can prevent recurrent cystine nephrolithiasis.

2sXT8z.title: Clonorchis sinensis
2sXT8z.description: A trematode (fluke) that causes clonorchiasis. Endemic to Asia and transmitted by ingestion of undercooked fish. Main complications are cholangitis and cholangiocarcinoma.

media.title: Life cycle of Clonorchis sinensis (Chinese liver fluke)

TsX68z.title: Tsetse fly
TsX68z.description: The vector of African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness).

SsXy8z.title: Nissl body
SsXy8z.description: The rough endoplasmatic reticulum of neurons. Consists of granular bodies in nerve cell bodies and dendrites (not in axons) that synthesize proteins (e.g., neurotransmitter). The granules stain blue with aniline (Nissl) staining. Nerve injury results in degradation of the Nissl bodies (chromatolysis).

hsXcuz.title: Cushing ulcer
hsXcuz.description: A type of stress ulcer that develops in patients with brain injury. Caused by increased vagal stimulation, which increases production of gastric acid.

destinations.label: Peptic ulcer disease → Subtypes and variants

3sXSuz.title: Right marginal artery
3sXSuz.description: A large branch of the right coronary artery that supplies the anterior and diaphragmatic surfaces of the right ventricle.

RsXluz.title: Lipooligosaccharide
RsXluz.description: An endotoxin produced by some gram-negative bacteria, including Neisseria meningitidis and Haemophilus influenzae. Induces TNF-α and IL-1, which leads to septic shock.

QsXuuz.title: Poly-D-glutamate
QsXuuz.description: The polypeptide component of the capsule of Bacillus anthracis, which protects against phagocytosis.

jsX_uz.title: Ovary
jsX_uz.description: The female reproductive organ that produces the ovum. Derived from mesoderm and lined by simple cuboidal cells.

PsXWEz.title: Vagina
PsXWEz.description: The female lower reproductive tract, which extends from the cervix to the vulva. Derived from endoderm and is lined by nonkeratinized, stratified squamous epithelium.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Vagina and vulva

media.title: Female reproductive organs and their neurovascular supply

4sX3Ez.title: Laminin
4sX3Ez.description: A protein that provides fibrous structural stability to the basement membrane. Binds to integrins.

ksXmEz.title: Autocrine signaling
ksXmEz.description: A form of cellular signaling in which a cell produces chemical messengers (e.g. hormones or cytokines) that subsequently act on that same cell via surface receptor binding of the secreted chemical messenger.

OsXIEz.title: Paracrine signaling
OsXIEz.description: A form of cellular signaling in which a cell produces a chemical messenger (e.g. hormones or cytokines) that can then exert effects on local cells in direct contact with the messenger. There is no distant effect (e.g., on other organs or tissues) from the messenger.

lsXvEz.title: Vulva
lsXvEz.description: The outer part of the female lower genitourinary tract, which consists of several structures including the labia minora and majora, the vestibular bulbs, and the Bartholin glands.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Vagina and vulva

NsX-Ez.title: Cervix
NsX-Ez.description: The lower part of the uterus, which consists of the endocervix (lined with single columnar epithelium) and ectocervix (lined with stratified squamous epithelium. The junction between these two layers forms the transformation zone.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Uterus and cervix

msXVvz.title: Corona radiata (neuroanatomy)
msXVvz.description: The white matter tracts that run bilaterally at the level of the lateral ventricles. Distortion of these fibers can be seen in patients with normal pressure hydrocephalus.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

5sXivz.title: Lateral thyroid anlage
5sXivz.description: Paired endodermal cell thickenings derived from the 4th branchial pouch. Located lateral to the median thyroid anlage. Fuse with the median thyroid anlage to form the parafollicular C cells of the thyroid gland.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Embryology

nsX7vz.title: Aortic arches
nsX7vz.description: A set of embryological vascular structures that develop into the arteries of the head and neck.

osX0Dz.title: Prostatic utricle
osX0Dz.description: A small, blind, sac-like, midline pouch located in the prostatic urethra. Flanked by the openings of the ejaculatory duct.

KsXUDz.title: Ejaculatory duct
KsXUDz.description: A paired set of ducts formed by the union of the vas deferens and the duct of the seminal vesicle. During ejaculation, they serve as the conduit by which semen enters the prostatic urethra.

destinations.label: Male reproductive organs → Epididymis, ductus deferens, and accessory glands

6sXjDz.title: Bladder diverticula
6sXjDz.description: Abnormal outpouching of the urinary bladder wall. Can be congenital (secondary to posterior urethral valve or neurogenic bladder) or acquired (secondary to bladder outlet obstruction). Usually consists of mucosa forming a pouch through the muscular bladder wall.

psXLDz.title: Laryngopharynx
psXLDz.description: A continuation of the oropharynx that extends from the superior border of the epiglottis (at the level of the hyoid bone) to the beginning of the esophagus (at the inferior aspect of the cricoid cartilage). Also, functions to keep food out of the larynx.

JsXsDz.title: Dysphonia
JsXsDz.description: The clinical diagnosis of an alteration in the pitch, quality, and/or volume of the voice that impacts communication. Often mistakenly used as a synonym for hoarseness, which is a patient-reported symptom of dysphonia

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Vagus nerve palsy (X)

qsXCDz.title: Spindle cell
qsXCDz.description: An elongated, spindle-shaped cell associated with several cancers, including anaplastic thyroid cancers, meningiomas, and sarcomas.

IsXYwz.title: Heme
IsXYwz.description: An iron-porphyrin complex that serves as a cofactor for several enzymes/proteins, including hemoglobin, myoglobin, cytochromes, and catalases.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

rsXfwz.title: Pleomorphism
rsXfwz.description: A descriptor for variability in size, shape, and staining characteristics of cells and/or their nuclei. A feature of malignant neoplasms. Also refers to the ability of bacteria to alter shape and/or size in response to specific environmental conditions.

7sX4wz.title: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase
7sX4wz.description: A receptor with intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity that is important for the development of the brain and nervous system. Mutation is associated with lung adenocarcinoma, neuroblastoma, and anaplastic large cell lymphoma.

HsXKwz.title: Systolic ejection
HsXKwz.description: The second phase of systole, occurring between the opening of the aortic valve and the onset of peak ventricular pressure.

ssXtwz.title: Isovolumetric relaxation
ssXtwz.description: The first phase of diastole, characterized by a rapid decrease in ventricular wall tension without a change in ventricular volume.

GsXBwz.title: CD52
GsXBwz.description: A surface glycoprotein found on most lymphocytes (T and B cells). It is the target of alemtuzumab.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

tsXX9z.title: Isovolumetric contraction
tsXX9z.description: The first phase of systole, characterized by a rapid increase in ventricular wall tension without a change in ventricular volume.

EsX89z.title: Genitourinary schistosomiasis
EsX89z.description: A form of chronic schistosomiasis characterized by chronic granulomatous inflammation in response to the deposition of Schistosoma eggs in the genitourinary tract. Can cause hematuria, obstructive uropathy, and infertility. Associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder.

vsXA9z.title: Pulmonary schistosomiasis
vsXA9z.description: A form of chronic schistosomiasis characterized by chronic granulomatous inflammation in response to the deposition of Schistosoma eggs in the pulmonary system. Deposition of eggs in the pulmonary arterioles causes granulomatous endarteritis, which can cause pulmonary hypertension. Pulmonary involvement can also develop as a result of portosystemic shunting due to hepatosplenic schistosomiasis.

xsXECz.title: Accessory pancreatic duct
xsXECz.description: A minor pancreatic duct that drains into the major pancreatic duct (30%) or directly into the duodenum (70%) via the minor duodenal papilla.

AsXRxz.title: Pancreas divisum
AsXRxz.description: A congenital malformation caused by failure of the ventral and dorsal pancreatic buds to fuse by the 8th week of embryonic development. Typically asymptomatic but can cause chronic abdominal pain or pancreatitis.

0GXeBz.title: Michaelis-Menten kinetics
0GXeBz.description: A type of kinetics seen with nonallosteric enzyme, receptor, and transporter systems. Follows the equation V₀ = (Vmax.[S])/(Km + [S]) in which V₀ is the initial reaction rate, Vmax is the maximum reaction rate, [S] is the substrate concentration, and Km (the Michaelis-Menton constant) is the substrate concentration at which the initial reaction rate is half of Vmax. Results in a hyperbolic graph when plotting V₀ as a function of [S].

YGXnBz.title: Vmax
YGXnBz.description: The maximum rate at which an enzyme can catalyze a reaction (i.e., when the active sites of the enzyme are saturated with substrate). Directly proportional to enzyme concentration.

bGXHBz.title: Michaelis constant
bGXHBz.description: The substrate concentration at which half of the active sites of an enzyme are bound by substrate; reaction velocity is ½ of Vmax at this concentration. Inversely related to the affinity of an enzyme for its substrate.

XGX9Bz.title: Oophorectomy
XGX9Bz.description: Surgical removal of one or both ovaries.

cGXayz.title: Adenocarcinoma
cGXayz.description: An epithelial cancer that arises from glandular tissue. Common types include adenocarcinomas of the lung, gastrointestinal tract, breast, and prostate.

dGXoyz.title: Cellular differentiation
dGXoyz.description: The process by which cells undergo significant epigenetic and molecular changes to develop into a different, and often more specialized, cell type. Evaluated during tumor grading.

VGXGyz.title: Tumor grade
VGXGyz.description: A histopathologic assessment of neoplastic cells. Cells whose morphology and organization are relatively normal are well-differentiated (low grade); abnormal cells are poorly differentiated or undifferentiated/anaplastic (high grade). Specific criteria for low- and high-grade classifications vary according to type of malignancy.

UGXbAz.title: CA 27-29
UGXbAz.description: A tumor marker whose concentration is elevated in certain breast cancers. Not used as a screening tool; can be used to follow response to therapy. Can also be elevated in cancers of the colon, stomach, kidney, lung, ovary, pancreas, uterus, and liver as well as in certain non-cancerous conditions (e.g., liver cirrhosis, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, pelvic inflammatory disease, endometriosis, systemic lupus erythematosus, pregnancy).

destinations.label: Tumor markers → Common tumor markers in peripheral blood

2GXTAz.title: Troponin C
2GXTAz.description: A calcium-binding protein that facilitates activation of skeletal and cardiac muscle.

media.title: Actin filaments and actin-binding proteins in the contractile apparatus

fGXkAz.title: Crossbridge
fGXkAz.description: The binding of the myosin head to actin at a 90° angle, which occurs after myosin undergoes a conformational change induced by intracellular calcium.

3GXS_z.title: Venous return
3GXS_z.description: The rate at which blood flows back to the heart, which typically equals cardiac output. Increases with fluid expansion and increased sympathetic activity; decreases with blood loss.

RGXl_z.title: Curling ulcer
RGXl_z.description: A type of stress ulcer that develops in patients with severe burns. Caused by decreased plasma volume (hypovolemia), which leads to a decline in gastric blood flow that weakens the mucosal barrier and causes mucosal ischemia.

destinations.label: Peptic ulcer disease → Subtypes and variants

iGXJ_z.title: Gartner duct
iGXJ_z.description: Vestigial remnant of the mesonephric duct in females. May result in a Gartner duct cyst.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Ductal sex differentiation

QGXu_z.title: Central neurocytoma
QGXu_z.description: A very rare, benign, intraventricular central nervous system tumor that grows from the septum pellucidum.

jGX__z.title: Cytokeratin
jGX__z.description: A family of intracytoplasmic intermediate filaments that make up the cellular cytoskeleton. Found predominantly in epithelial cells and thus is used in histochemical staining to identify neoplasms of epithelial origin.

PGXWzz.title: 60S ribosome
PGXWzz.description: The large subunit of the eukaryotic ribosome. It has peptidyltransferase activity and it contains the tRNA binding site. The 60S subunit is inactivated by Shiga-toxin and Shiga-like toxin.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

OGXIzz.title: Pertussis toxin
OGXIzz.description: An AB exotoxin produced by Bordetella pertussis that inhibits host phagocytic activity. The toxin increases adenylate cyclase activity by inactivating the Gi subunit.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

lGXvzz.title: Deep peroneal nerve
lGXvzz.description: A nerve that arises from the common peroneal (fibular) nerve. Innervates the muscles of the anterior compartment of the leg (responsible for ankle and toe dorsiflexion) and the skin of the first digital web space. Injury is usually secondary to anterior compartment compression or ski boot syndrome and can cause foot drop.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Innervation
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

NGX-zz.title: Sural nerve
NGX-zz.description: A purely sensory nerve of the lower extremity formed by branches of the tibial nerve and the common peroneal nerve. Supplies sensation to the lateral distal leg, ankle, and foot. Injury is commonly secondary to trauma and calcaneus fracture.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves
The leg, ankle, and foot → Innervation

media.title: Innervation of the lower extremity (dorsal view)

mGXV-z.title: Squalene epoxidase
mGXV-z.description: A rate-limiting enzyme in sterol biosynthesis that utilizes NADPH and oxygen to produce squalene epoxide. It is also an important enzyme in fungi because it ensures the synthesis of ergosterol, an integral part of the fungal cell membrane

MGXM-z.title: I-cell disease
MGXM-z.description: A lysosomal storage disease in which impaired phosphotransferase leads to defective targeting of lysosomal enzymes. As a result, the enzymes are secreted instead of reaching the lysosomes. Build up of substances that would normally be degraded by lysosomes lead to blindness, hyperplastic gums, coarse facial features, abnormal bone growth, and claw hands.

nGX7-z.title: Superficial peroneal nerve
nGX7-z.description: A nerve of the lower extremity that innervates the lateral compartment of the leg (foot eversion by peroneus longus and peroneus brevis) and the skin that overlies the anteromedial leg and dorsal foot, exclusive of the first web space. A branch of the common peroneal nerve. Injury to this nerve is commonly secondary to entrapment at the lateral ankle or via fibular fracture.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves
The leg, ankle, and foot → Innervation

LGXw-z.title: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma in situ
LGXw-z.description: A subtype of lung adenocarcinoma characterized by a small (≤ 3 cm), localized tumor that exhibits lepidic growth along alveolar structures and is noninvasive. Formerly referred to as bronchioloalveolar carcinoma.

oGX0Z-.title: Bartholin gland cyst and abscess
oGX0Z-.description: A retention cyst (a cyst caused by obstruction of an excretory duct) arising from the ducts of the Bartholin glands. It results from inflammation or trauma that causes obstruction and accumulation of the mucus produced by the glands. It manifests as an unilateral mass located in the posterolateral part of the vaginal introitus. Bartholin gland abscess occurs when an infection develops behind the obstructed duct.

pGXLZ-.title: Atrial reflex
pGXLZ-.description: A physiologic reflex characterized by an increased heart rate in response to atrial distension (increased venous return to the heart). Mediated by stretch receptors in the atria.

qGXCZ-.title: Syncytium
qGXCZ-.description: A multinucleated mass of cytoplasm that is not divided by cellular membranes. Allows rapid conduction of electrical and molecular signals.

rGXf0-.title: Protoporphyrin
rGXf0-.description: The last intermediate of the heme biosynthesis pathway. In the presence of iron, protoporphyrin is converted to heme by ferrochelatase. Lead poisoning can cause inhibition of ferrochelatase, which results in accumulation of protoporphyrin.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

HGXK0-.title: Disopyramide
HGXK0-.description: A class IA antiarrhythmic medication used to treat ventricular arrhythmias. Adverse effects include dry mouth, urinary hesitancy, and constipation.

GGXB0-.title: Mexiletine
GGXB0-.description: A non-selective voltage-gated sodium channel blocker and class IB antiarrhythmic agent.

8GXOa-.title: Ibutilide
8GXOa-.description: A potassium channel blocker and a class III antiarrhythmic agent.

uGXpa-.title: Dofetilide
uGXpa-.description: A sulfonamide class III antiarrhythmic agent and potassium channel blocker used for the treatment and prevention of atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter.

9GXNY-.title: Tricuspid valve
9GXNY-.description: A valve located between the right atrium and right ventricle. Has 3 valve leaflets. Supported by a fibrous annulus,  chordae tendineae, and papillary muscles.

ZtXZX-.title: Papillary muscles
ZtXZX-.description: The muscles of the heart that extend from the ventricular wall and the septum and attach via chordae tendineae to the atrioventricular valves. These muscles contract during systole to prevent prolapse of valve leaflets and regurgitation into the atria when pressure rises during ventricular contraction

media.title: Anatomy of the heart and adjacent large vessels

btXHX-.title: Tyrosine hydroxylase
btXHX-.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of tyrosine to L-DOPA in the presence of tetrahydrobiopterin. Deficiency of this enzyme manifests with progressive early encephalopathy.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla

ctXac-.title: Anopsia
ctXac-.description: A defect of the visual field that causes partial or full blindness.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Scotoma and anopia

1tX2c-.title: Binasal hemianopsia
1tX2c-.description: A loss of the inner half of the visual field of both eyes caused by impingement of the noncrossing fibers of both optic nerves. Etiologies include atherosclerosis and aneurysms of the internal carotid arteries that result in compression of the outer part of the optic chiasma.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Scotoma and anopia

VtXGc-.title: Oral cavity
VtXGc-.description: The most proximal part of the digestive tract, which consists of the oral vestibule and the oral cavity proper. Serves as a conduit for food and a respiratory passage, provides taste sensation, and assists in phonation.

etXxc-.title: Oral vestibule
etXxc-.description: The area of the mouth between the lips, teeth and cheeks.

UtXb1-.title: Oral cavity proper
UtXb1-.description: The major part of the oral cavity. Bounded anteriorly by the teeth, posteriorly by the palatine arches, superiorly by the hard palate, inferiorly by the tongue, and laterally by the cheeks.

2tXT1-.title: Oral fissure
2tXT1-.description: The opening of the oral cavity bounded by the lips. Connects with the oral vestibule.

TtX61-.title: Labial commissure
TtX61-.description: The corner of the mouth opening (i.e., where the upper and lower lips meet at the lateral edges of the mouth).

gtXF1-.title: Vermilion border
gtXF1-.description: The line of demarcation between the highly keratinized squamous epithelium of the face and the less keratinized epithelium of the labial mucosa (i.e., the vermilion).

StXy1-.title: Palate
StXy1-.description: The roof of the mouth, which separates the nasal cavity from the oral cavity. Composed of the anterior hard palate, and the posterior soft palate.

media.title: Neuromusculature of the hard and soft palate

htXcW-.title: Hard palate
htXcW-.description: The anterior, bony portion of the roof of the mouth. Consists of the palatine process of the maxilla and the horizontal plate of palatine bone. Separates the nasal and oral cavities.

media.title: Neuromusculature of the hard and soft palate

3tXSW-.title: Soft palate
3tXSW-.description: The posterior part of the palate. Consists of soft tissue, including the tensor veli palatini, levator veli palatini, palatopharyngeus, palatoglossus, and uvula. Elevation of the soft palate protects the airway during swallowing.

media.title: Neuromusculature of the hard and soft palate

itXJW-.title: Levator veli palatini muscle
itXJW-.description: A paired pharyngeal muscle that elevates and laterally deviates the soft palate when it contracts. Innervated by branches of the vagus nerve.

media.title: Neuromusculature of the hard and soft palate
Muscles of the palate and extrinsic muscles of the tongue

PtXWd-.title: Musculus uvulae
PtXWd-.description: A muscle that originates at the palatine bone and aponeurosis that shortens and elevates the uvula. Innervated by the pharyngeal plexus.

4tX3d-.title: Decubitus position
4tX3d-.description: A descriptor for positioning of the body on a horizontal surface. Generally used with a prefix to specify which part of the body touches the surface (e.g., left lateral decubitus position).

ktXmd-.title: Mylohyoid nerve
ktXmd-.description: A branch of the inferior alveolar nerve (a branch of the mandibular branch of the trigeminal nerve), which innervates the anterior belly of the digastric muscle.

ltXvd-.title: Hydroxymethylbilane
ltXvd-.description: An intermediate of the heme biosynthesis pathway. Converted to uroporphyrinogen III by uroporphyrinogen III synthase.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

NtX-d-.title: Granulation tissue
NtX-d-.description: A type of connective tissue generated by fibroblasts during wound healing. Initially, it is composed of type III collagen, which is then replaced by type I collagen to create a stronger extracellular matrix.

destinations.label: Wound healing → Phases of wound healing

ntX7V-.title: Cell death
ntX7V-.description: A biological process leading to the irreversible cessation of the cell's vital functions. Main types include apoptosis (programmed cell death), necrosis/oncosis, pyroptosis, and autophagy.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Overview of cell death

media.title: Necrosis vs. Apoptosis: Types of Cell Death

LtXwV-.title: Lysosomal storage diseases
LtXwV-.description: A heterogeneous group of diseases that are due to defective lysosomal enzymes. This leads to the accumulation of toxic metabolic products, resulting in a variety of findings depending on the underlying enzyme deficiency. Lysosomal storage diseases comprise sphingolipidoses (Fabry disease, Gaucher disease, Niemann-Pick disease, Tay-Sachs disease, Krabbe disease and metachromatic leukodystrophy) and mucopolysaccharidoses (Hurler and Hunter syndrome)

otX0e-.title: Severe congenital neutropenia
otX0e-.description: A condition of neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count < 200/microliter) that occurs in infants at or around birth due to bone marrow failure of the myeloid lineage. Associated with neutrophil elastase gene, WASP gene, and HAX1 mutations.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital neutrophil and phagocyte disorders

KtXUe-.title: Mesenteric vessels
KtXUe-.description: The vasculature that supplies the gastrointestinal tract. Includes the superior mesenteric artery, inferior mesenteric artery, superior mesenteric vein, and inferior mesenteric vein.

media.title: Tributaries of the hepatic portal vein
Arterial supply of the gastrointestinal tract

6tXje-.title: Basophilic
6tXje-.description: A histopathologic descriptor for a substance with high affinity for basic dyes (e.g., hematoxylin), which results in blue coloration.

ptXLe-.title: Cresyl violet stain
ptXLe-.description: An aniline dye that stains RNA blue. Has high affinity for polyribosomes in the cytoplasm and on the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

JtXse-.title: Memory B cell
JtXse-.description: A type of B cell involved in memory formation as part of the acquired immune response. In response to re-exposure to a previously encountered antigen, memory B cells develop into plasma cells that secrete predominantly IgG and induce a faster and stronger immune response.

qtXCe-.title: Radiolucency
qtXCe-.description: The dark areas on x-ray, fluoroscopy, and CT scans. Represents low-density areas (e.g., air, most gallstones, plastic or wooden foreign bodies), which absorb fewer x-rays than high-density areas, allowing more x-rays to reach the film. This results in a darker appearance as x-rays appear black on radiographic images.

rtXfU-.title: Colonic atresia
rtXfU-.description: A rare congenital anomaly of the colon that either results in stenosis or complete absence of a colonic segment, which leads to obstruction and subsequent abdominal distention. A dilated proximal segment and absence of gas in the rectum may be seen on x-ray.

7tX4U-.title: Meconium plug syndrome
7tX4U-.description: A transient neonatal bowel obstruction caused by thickened meconium in the colon. Symptoms appear within the first days of life and include delayed meconium passage, vomiting, and abdominal distention. Risk factors include prematurity, maternal diabetes, magnesium sulfate use for tocolysis, and underlying conditions such as Hirschsprung disease and cystic fibrosis. Diagnosis typically involves a contrast enema, which may also be therapeutic. Failure to intervene increases the risk of complications such as bowel perforation and ischemia.

HtXKU-.title: Refractive error
HtXKU-.description: A group of conditions in which light rays entering the eye are not focused onto the retina, leading to blurred vision. Comprises myopia (nearsightedness), hyperopia (farsightedness), astigmatism, and presbyopia.

stXtU-.title: K1 capsular polysaccharide
stXtU-.description: A virulence factor found in some strains of Escherichia coli that protects against phagocytosis by impairing opsonization.

GtXBU-.title: Levator palpebrae superioris muscle
GtXBU-.description: A muscle that elevates the upper eyelid and opens the eye. Originates from the roof of the orbit and inserts in the upper eyelid on the superior border of the tarsal plate. Innervated by the oculomotor nerve (CN III).

8tXO2-.title: Congenital neutrophil and phagocyte disorders
8tXO2-.description: A group of congenital immunodeficiency disorders characterized by an impaired ability of phagocytic cells to kill pathogens. Examples include chronic granulomatous disease, leukocyte adhesion deficiency, Chédiak-Higashi syndrome, myeloperoxidase deficiency, and congenital neutropenia.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital neutrophil and phagocyte disorders

vtXA2-.title: Lacrimal duct system
