vtXA2-.description: A collection of structures that supply tear fluid for the surface of the eyeball and the eyelid. Consists of lacrimal gland, tarsal glands, lacrimal sacs, and the nasolacrimal ducts.

xtXEf-.title: Orbit
xtXEf-.description: A bony cavity of the skull that houses the eyeball.

media.title: Nerves of the eye and the orbital cavity
Arteries of eye and orbital cavity

BtXzf-.title: Cellular atypia
BtXzf-.description: A structurally irregular or abnormal cell, usually secondary to chronic irritation or infection. Examples of atypical features include multiple or enlarged nucleoli, bare nuclei, non-uniformity of cell size (anisocytosis), and cytoplasmic vacuoles. Presence of numerous atypical cells may indicate a premalignant state.

ytXdT-.title: Lens
ytXdT-.description: The transparent and flexible biconvex refractory structure of the eye. Involved in accommodation.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Segments and chambers of the eye

AtXRT-.title: Optic disc
AtXRT-.description: A region of the eye located medial to the fovea centralis. Formed by axons of ganglion cells that leave the eye to form the optic nerve. Does not contain photosensitive receptors and thus creates in a blind spot in the visual field.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

_tX5T-.title: Optic cup
_tX5T-.description: A central depression located in the middle of the optic disc.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

ztXrT-.title: Macula
ztXrT-.description: An oval-shaped, yellow spot located on the lateral side of the optic disc near the center of the posterior wall of the retina. Lacks blood vessels. Contains the fovea centralis.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

-tXDT-.title: Canal of Schlemm
-tXDT-.description: A vessel in the eye that conveys aqueous humor from the anterior chamber to the episcleral vessels.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Segments and chambers of the eye

aFXQg-.title: Cornea
aFXQg-.description: The anterior, transparent part of the external layer of the eyeball. Refracts light.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

YFXng-.title: Sclera
YFXng-.description: The posterior, opaque, and fibrous part of the external layer of the eyeball. Protects and stabilizes the eye.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

bFXHg-.title: Iris
bFXHg-.description:
May refer to:
1. A pigmented membrane with a central opening, the pupil, that adjusts its size in response to light
2. An abbreviation for immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

XFX9g-.title: Ciliary body
XFX9g-.description: Part of the uvea. Located behind the iris and composed of the ciliary ring, epithelium with ciliary processes, and ciliary muscle. Functionality includes anchoring the lens, accommodation, and aqueous humor production.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

cFXaS-.title: Choroid
cFXaS-.description: A component of the uvea that is formed by an outer, pigmented layer and an inner, highly vascularized layer. Supplies the retina.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

media.title: Retinal layers and structure of the globe of the eye
Cross section of the posterior part of the eyeball

WFXPS-.title: Retinal cones
WFXPS-.description: The flask-shaped, first-order receptor cells of the retina. They contain three spectrally different types of visual pigments and are involved in color vision. Primarily found within the fovea centralis.

dFXoS-.title: Endocardium
dFXoS-.description: The layer of the heart that forms its inner surface. Consists of three sublayers (endothelium, smooth muscle and connective tissue, and subendocardium).

VFXGS-.title: Myocardium
VFXGS-.description: The striated muscle of the heart, which is layered between the epicardium and endocardium. Supplied by the coronary arteries.

UFXbh-.title: Pericardium
UFXbh-.description: The fibroserous sac that encloses the heart. Layers include the serous pericardium (inner layer), which is further subdivided into a visceral and parietal layer, and the fibrous pericardium (outer layer).

media.title: Pleural and pericardial layers (cross-section of the thorax)

gFXFh-.title: Lacrimal sac
gFXFh-.description: A dilated portion of the nasolacrimal duct that gathers tear fluid.

hFXc3-.title: Conjunctiva
hFXc3-.description: A highly vascularized mucous membrane that lines the inside of the eyelids and sclera. Divided into two distinct layers: palpebral (tarsal) conjunctiva and bulbar conjunctiva. Accessory glands in the conjunctiva produce tear fluid.

3FXS3-.title: Intercalated discs
3FXS3-.description: The cell-cell adhesion structures that connect cardiomyocytes and facilitate the transmission of signals to synchronize cardiomyocyte activity. Composed of three different complexes: fascia adherens, desmosomes, and gap junctions. Found at the Z line of the sarcomere.

RFXl3-.title: Nuclear receptor
RFXl3-.description: A family of ligand-modulated transcription factors that regulate a variety of biological processes, including metabolism, cell proliferation, and development. Their ligands can cross plasma membranes and interact directly with the nuclear receptors, either in the cytosol or within the nucleus. Examples include steroid hormones and small, lipid-soluble molecules such as thyroid hormone.

iFXJ3-.title: Cardiac Purkinje cell
iFXJ3-.description: A cardiac cell that conducts electrical impulses from the proximal bundle branches of the heart to the ventricular myocytes, which results in ventricular contraction.

QFXu3-.title: PKHD1
QFXu3-.description: A gene located on chromosome 6 that codes for fibrocystin. Mutations of this gene are seen in autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease.

jFX_3-.title: Ophthalmic artery
jFX_3-.description: An intracranial branch of the internal carotid artery. Enters the orbit through the optic canal. Supplies blood to the orbital structures (i.e., the eyeball, optic nerve, extraocular muscles, lacrimal gland), as well as the forehead and the nasal cavity.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Vasculature and innervation

media.title: Arteries of eye and orbital cavity

PFXWR-.title: Central artery of the retina
PFXWR-.description: The main branch of the ophthalmic artery, which supplies the retina and parts of the optic nerve. Since it is a terminal artery with no anastomosis, its occlusion causes blindness.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Vasculature and innervation

media.title: Arteries of eye and orbital cavity

4FX3R-.title: Lacrimal artery
4FX3R-.description: A branch of the ophthalmic artery that supplies the lacrimal gland, eyelids and conjunctiva.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Vasculature and innervation

kFXmR-.title: Long posterior ciliary arteries
kFXmR-.description: A pair of arteries found in each eye. Arises from the ophthalmic artery and supplies the iris and ciliary body.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Vasculature and innervation

OFXIR-.title: Short posterior ciliary arteries
OFXIR-.description: A collection of arteries in the eye that arise from the ophthalmic artery, divide into 15-20 branches, and supply the choroid.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Vasculature and innervation

media.title: Valve thrombosis in recurrent endocarditis of the mitral valve

NFX-R-.title: Supraorbital artery
NFX-R-.description: A branch of the ophthalmic artery that supplies part of the orbit, forehead, and scalp. Passes through the supraorbital foramen.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Vasculature and innervation

mFXVi-.title: Frontal artery
mFXVi-.description: A branch of the ophthalmic artery that supplies the medial aspects of the forehead and scalp.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Vasculature and innervation

5FXii-.title: Ophthalmic veins
5FXii-.description: The veins of the eye (the superior and inferior ophthalmic veins) that drain into the cavernous sinus.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Vasculature and innervation

media.title: Valve thrombosis in recurrent endocarditis of the mitral valve

MFXMi-.title: HFE gene
MFXMi-.description: A gene located on chromosome 6 that codes for human hemochromatosis protein, which regulates iron absorption by facilitating the binding of transferrin with its receptor. Mutations in this gene are seen in individuals with hereditary hemochromatosis.

LFXwi-.title: Isoleucine
LFXwi-.description: An essential amino acid with a branched aliphatic side chain. Can metabolize into either ketone bodies or glucose.

oFX0Q-.title: Palpebral fissure
oFX0Q-.description: The opening between the upper and lower eyelid, defined as the elliptical space between the medial and lateral canthi of the open eye.

KFXUQ-.title: Orbital septum
KFXUQ-.description: A piece of connective tissue that forms the anterior boundary of the orbit. Runs from the margin of the eyelids to the periosteum of the orbital margin. Within the eyelid, the orbital septum thickens and forms the tarsal plates.

media.title: Anatomy of the eye and surrounding structures

6FXjQ-.title: Tarsal plates
6FXjQ-.description: The thick, densely packed part of the orbital septum that contains the tarsal glands. Further divided into a superior tarsal plate (superior tarsus) and an inferior tarsal plate (inferior tarsus).

JFXsQ-.title: Inferior fascicle of optic radiation
JFXsQ-.description: The inferior fascicle of the optic radiation, which carries visual information from the lower part of the retina. Arises from the lateral geniculate nucleus and projects to the visual cortex through the temporal lobe. Lesions to this area cause contralateral upper quadrantanopia.

rFXfj-.title: Retinal pigment epithelium
rFXfj-.description: The outermost layer of the retina, which contains melanin granules, provides nutrition to photoreceptors, absorbs light and prevents reflection, aids in the formation of rhodopsin, and stores vitamin A.

media.title: Congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium (CHRPE)

uFXpP-.title: Phagolysosome
uFXpP-.description: Cytoplasmic organelle of phagocytic cells formed by the fusion of phagosome and lysosome.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Phagocytosis and killing

vFXAP-.title: Convergence
vFXAP-.description: The simultaneous inward movement of both eyes to maintain focus on close objects (e.g., eyes crossing when looking at one's own nose). Mediated by the oculomotor nerve via the action of the medial recti muscles.

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Accommodation and convergence

wFXh4-.title: Neurofilaments
wFXh4-.description: An intermediate filament expressed by neurons that plays a role in maintaining cell shape and facilitating axonal transport. Can be used in immunohistochemical staining to identify tumors of neuronal origin.

9FXN4-.title: Tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase
9FXN4-.description: A glycosylated enzyme normally expressed in dendritic cells, macrophages, and osteoclasts. Involved in skeletal development and mineralization, collagen synthesis and degradation, and immune cell development and response. TRAP expression is increased in hairy cell leukemia.

BFXz4-.title: Platelets
BFXz4-.description: A blood cell involved in primary hemostasis. Produced by megakaryocytes. Aggregates and interacts with fibrinogen to form a platelet plug.

yFXdk-.title: Superior fascicle of optic radiation
yFXdk-.description: The superior fascicle of the optic radiation, which carries visual information from the upper part of the retina. Arises from the lateral geniculate nucleus and projects to the visual cortex through the parietal lobe. Lesions to this area cause contralateral lower quadrantanopia.

AFXRk-.title: Lateral plantar nerve
AFXRk-.description: A branch of the tibial nerve that supplies sensation to the lateral aspect of the dorsum of the foot and innervates several deep muscles of the foot.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Innervation

zFXrk-.title: Anti-HCV antibody
zFXrk-.description: An antibody against hepatitis C antigen whose presence indicates past infection with hepatitis C virus. Appears within 2 weeks of infection and persists for life.

-FXDk-.title: Tibial nerve
-FXDk-.description: A branch of the sciatic nerve that provides motor innervation to the muscles of the posterior compartment of the thigh and leg and muscles of the sole of the foot. Supplies sensation to the sole of the foot and medial part of the dorsal leg.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Innervation
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

Z8XZO-.title: Limiting plate
Z8XZO-.description: A ring of hepatocytes that surrounds the connective tissue of hepatic portal triads. Inflammation and necrosis of this region is known as piecemeal necrosis or interface hepatitis.

08XeO-.title: CAMP factor
08XeO-.description: A pore-forming protein produced by group B streptococcus (GBS, or S. agalactiae). Not essential for virulence but can be used to identify GBS, as it enlarges the hemolysis area in cultures formed by S. aureus. This factor should not be confused with cAMP (cyclic adenosine monophosphate). CAMP is an acronym for Christie Atkins and Munch Peterson, the authors of the test.

a8XQO-.title: Light-near dissociation
a8XQO-.description: An attenuated pupillary light reflex with a relatively preserved pupillary near reflex. Seen in conditions that selectively damage the dorsal midbrain regions involved in the light reflex but spare the more ventral fibers involved in the near reflex (e.g., Parinaud syndrome, Argyll-Robertson pupil in neurosyphilis).

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Other pupillary defects

Y8XnO-.title: Hutchinson pupil
Y8XnO-.description: An ophthalmologic finding characterized by a fixed and dilated pupil. Caused by compression of the oculomotor nerve (e.g., from uncal herniation).

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Other pupillary defects
Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Subtypes and variants

X8X9O-.title: Blown pupil
X8X9O-.description: Pupillary dilation (may be accompanied by ptosis) due to saccular aneurysm in the posterior communication artery territory or uncal herniation causing compression of the ipsilateral oculomotor cranial nerve.

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Other pupillary defects

c8Xal-.title: Gardener's pupil
c8Xal-.description: Pupillary dilation (mydriasis) due to ingestion of plant alkaloids, e.g., of Jimson weed (Datura stramonium)

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Other pupillary defects

18X2l-.title: Iris dilator muscle
18X2l-.description: A smooth muscle that dilates the iris. Innervated by sympathetic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion. These fibers reach the eye by traveling with the long and short ciliary nerves.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

d8Xol-.title: Phosphatase
d8Xol-.description: An enzyme that removes phosphate groups from a substrate

destinations.label: Enzymes and biocatalysis → Classes of enzymes

V8XGl-.title: Periampullary tumor
V8XGl-.description: A group of neoplasms that arise from structures near the ampullar of Vater, including the pancreatic head, the distal common bile duct, and the duodenum.

destinations.label: Pancreatic and hepatic surgery → Pancreatic surgery

e8Xxl-.title: Optic tract
e8Xxl-.description: A part of the visual system of the brain and continuation of the optic nerves that carries information from the optic chiasm to ipsilateral lateral geniculate nuclei, pretectal nuclei, and superior colliculi.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Overview of the visual pathways

U8XbN-.title: Visual field
U8XbN-.description: The area in which objects can be seen while focusing the eyes on a central point.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Visual field examination

f8XkN-.title: Polyarthralgia
f8XkN-.description: A condition of joint pain that affects five or more joints simultaneously.

g8XFN-.title: TDP-43
g8XFN-.description: An DNA binding protein located in the nucleus that regulates transcription. Abnormal TDP-43 is associated with some variants of frontotemporal dementia and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

S8XyN-.title: Prion disease
S8XyN-.description: A group of neurodegenerative diseases associated with accumulation of misfolded prion proteins. Includes kuru, Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD), Gerstmann-Sträussler-Scheinker syndrome, and fatal familial insomnia.  Neuropathology shows neuronal loss and gliosis without evidence of inflammation.

h8Xcm-.title: Wright staining
h8Xcm-.description: A histologic stain used to differentiate blood cells on urine and blood samples. Can be combined with Giemsa staining.

media.title: Barr body and aberrant nuclear projection

38XSm-.title: Benznidazole
38XSm-.description: An antiparasitic agent used primarily in the treatment of Trypanosoma cruzi infection (Chagas disease). Functions by generating free radicals that cause DNA damage in the parasite. Adverse effects include dermatitis and peripheral neuropathy.

R8Xlm-.title: Silver stain
R8Xlm-.description: A histologic stain used to identify various bacteria (e.g., Pseudomonas, Legionella, Leptospira, H. pylori, Treponema) and fungi (e.g., Pneumocystis, Cryptococcus, Candida).

i8XJm-.title: JAK-STAT signaling pathway
i8XJm-.description: A signaling pathway comprised of cell-surface receptors, Janus kinases (JAKs), and signal transducer and activator of transcription proteins (STATs). External ligand binding leads to phosphorylation of STATs, which then act as a transcription factor.

Q8Xum-.title: Tyrosine kinase
Q8Xum-.description: A group of > 90 enzymes that regulate cell signaling, growth, proliferation, differentiation, and adhesion by adding high energy phosphate groups to tyrosine residues of proteins. Several tyrosine kinases are proto-oncogenes (e.g., ALK, JAK2, RET).

P8XW5-.title: Hyaluronic acid
P8XW5-.description: A glycosaminoglycan found in the extracellular matrix of connective tissue. Also found in the bacterial capsule of Streptococcus pyogenes.

48X35-.title: Cyclin
48X35-.description: A group of proteins that regulate the cell cycle at different phases via activation of cyclin-dependent protein kinases.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

k8Xm5-.title: Cyclin D
k8Xm5-.description: A protein that regulates the transition from G1 to S phase in the cell cycle via activation of cyclin-dependent protein kinases. Forms a complex with CDK4, which initiates DNA replication by inactivating retinoblastoma protein.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

O8XI5-.title: Hemorrhagic infarct
O8XI5-.description: Infarction in organs with dual blood supply (e.g., lung, intestine, testes, and liver). Commonly due to occlusion of vessels and subsequent extravasation of RBCs into the ischemic tissue.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Ischemia

l8Xv5-.title: Granzyme
l8Xv5-.description: A serine protease secreted by cytotoxic T cells and NK cells to induce apoptosis of malignant cells and virus-infected cells.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Lymphoid cell line

N8X-5-.title: Perforin
N8X-5-.description: A pore-forming protein secreted by cytotoxic T cells and NK cells to induce apoptosis of malignant cells and virus-infected cells.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Lymphoid cell line

m8XVM-.title: Very low density lipoprotein
m8XVM-.description: A lipoprotein secreted by the liver that delivers hepatic triglycerides to peripheral tissue. Contains apolipoproteins E, C-II, and B-100.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

58XiM-.title: Carcinoma
58XiM-.description: A cancer that arises from epithelial cells (e.g., the lining of the respiratory tract, urinary tract, reproductive tracts, and skin). Contrast with sarcomas, which arise from mesenchymal cells

n8X7M-.title: NOD2
n8X7M-.description: An intracellular protein and key part of the NK-kB pathway that possess a leucine rich segment that detects muramyl dipeptide, a bacterial molecular marker. Mutations in NOD2 are implicated in several autoinflammatory diseases such as sarcoidosis and Crohn disease.

L8XwM-.title: β-catenin
L8XwM-.description: An intracellular protein that acts as a transcription factor to influence cellular proliferation. In normal cellular physiology, the Wnt signaling pathway mediates the destruction of this protein via the tumor suppressor protein APC. Failure of this regulatory process is implicated in colorectal cancer.

o8X0n-.title: Wnt signaling pathway
o8X0n-.description: A pathway used to regulate cellular proliferation. Activation of the pathway permits cellular growth and proliferation via beta catenin activity, whereas inactive Wnt signaling permits proteasomal destruction of beta catenin. Dysregulation of this pathway is implicated in colorectal cancer.

K8XUn-.title: Arteriovenous oxygen difference
K8XUn-.description: The difference between arterial oxygen content and venous oxygen content. Used in the Fick principle to calculate cardiac output.

68Xjn-.title: Fick principle
68Xjn-.description: A formula used to calculate cardiac output. Cardiac output (CO) = (rate of oxygen consumption) / (arterial oxygen content − venous oxygen content)

J8Xsn-.title: Pathogen-associated molecular patterns
J8Xsn-.description: A group of molecules that are recognized by receptors of the innate immune system as foreign to the host. PAMPs are typically essential for microorganism survival and thus relatively conserved among a class of microorganisms.

I8XYL-.title: Nodular sclerosing classical Hodgkin lymphoma
I8XYL-.description: The most common subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma. On histology, it is characterized by sclerosis with numerous collagen fibers, a thick capsule, and nodular infiltrates composed of Reed-Sternberg cells. It is primarily localized to the mediastinal and cervical regions. It has a good prognosis.

r8XfL-.title: Mixed-cellularity classical HL
r8XfL-.description: A subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma. Characterized on histology by scattered Reed-Sternberg cells on a diffuse (or slightly nodular) mixed inflammatory background without sclerosis. Primarily localized to the abdominal and splenic regions. It has a good prognosis.

78X4L-.title: Lymphocyte-rich classical HL
78X4L-.description: A rare subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma. Histologically characterized by scattered Reed-Sternberg cells and small lymphocytes in a nodular (or less commonly a diffuse) cellular background. Primarily localized to the cervical and/or axillary regions. It has a good prognosis.

H8XKL-.title: Lymphocyte-depleted classical HL
H8XKL-.description: The rarest and most aggressive subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma. Characterized on histology by numerous Reed-Sternberg cells and/or sparse non-neoplastic lymphocytes. Primarily localized to the region below the diaphragm.

s8XtL-.title: Nodular lymphocyte predominant HL
s8XtL-.description: A rare subtype of Hodgkin lymphoma. Histologically characterized by a nodular pattern and sparse large pleomorphic lymphoid (LP) cells admixed with abundant B lymphocytes in a meshwork of follicular dendritic cells. NLPHL has a favourable prognosis compared with most other subtypes of Hodgkin lymphoma.

G8XBL-.title: Metastatic calcification
G8XBL-.description: A diffuse calcification of normal tissue (especially lung, kidney, and gastric mucosa) caused by chronic hypercalcemia or a high phosphate-calcium solubility product. Calcinosis of collecting ducts may lead to nephrogenic diabetes and renal failure. Associated with conditions that cause hypercalcemia (e.g., hyperparathyroidism, sarcoidosis, multiple myeloma).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cellular inclusions

t8XXo-.title: Dystrophic calcification
t8XXo-.description: A localized calcification in abnormal, damaged tissue in patients with normal serum calcium levels. Often seen in tissues that have been affected by the general "wear and tear" of aging (e.g., calcific aortic stenosis). Associated with fat necrosis (pancreatitis), infarcts, thrombi, congenital CMV, CREST syndrome, and atherosclerotic plaques.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cellular inclusions

v8XAo-.title: Leukocyte extravasation
v8XAo-.description: The process by which leukocytes move from the circulatory system to sites of tissue injury. Occurs primarily at the postcapillary venules.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Acute local inflammation

D8X1K-.title: Leukocyte margination
D8X1K-.description: The first step in leukocyte extravasation, in which leukocytes are distributed peripherally along the endothelial surface. Successful margination requires the dilation of postcapillary venules and Rouleaux formation of leukocytes.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

w8XhK-.title: Confined placental mosaicism
w8XhK-.description: Discrepancy between the chromosomal composition (genotype) of the fetus and the placenta. Characterized by both normal and abnormal cell lines within the placenta. Occurs in about 1-2% of pregnancies.

98XNK-.title: Sialyl-LewisX
98XNK-.description: A cell adhesion molecule that facilitates leukocyte margination and rolling by binding to E-selectin and P-selectin. Deficiencies of this molecule result in leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 2.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

x8XEK-.title: P-selectin
x8XEK-.description: An adhesion molecule found on endothelial cells. Stored and released from Weibel-Palade bodies within the endothelium in response to inflammation. Release is mediated by histamine.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

y8Xd6-.title: CD34
y8Xd6-.description: A transmembrane protein that is expressed by hematopoietic stem cells and progenitor cells in the bone marrow. Used as a marker to identify stem cells (e.g., to enrich for bone marrow transplantation).

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Bone marrow and hematopoiesis

z8Xr6-.title: Lymphocyte function-associated antigen-1
z8Xr6-.description: An integrin that facilitates leukocyte adhesion by binding to ICAM. Consists of CD18 and CD11a. Defects in LFA-1 can result in leukocyte adhesion deficiency (type 1).

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

0uXep-.title: Leukocyte rolling
0uXep-.description: The second step in leukocyte extravasation, which is characterized by a transient, weak interaction of leukocytes with endothelial cells. Mediated by adhesion molecules on endothelial cells (e.g., P-selectin, E-selectin, GlyCAM-1, and CD34) and leukocytes (e.g., Sialyl-LewisX, L-selectin).

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

YuXnp-.title: Hypnozoite
YuXnp-.description: A form of malarial parasites P. ovale or P. vivax that exists outside of erythrocytes. Can remain dormant in the liver after initial infection and are thought to cause malaria relapse.

1uX2J-.title: Equatorial plate
1uX2J-.description: Imaginary line that is midline between the two centrosomes (i.e., point of origin of the mitotic spindle). It occurs during the metaphase of mitosis.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

WuXPJ-.title: Signs of chronic liver disease
WuXPJ-.description: Features include jaundice, scleral icterus, spider angioma, gynecomastia, palmar erythema, ascites, asterixis, and encephalopathy.

VuXGJ-.title: Low density lipoprotein receptor
VuXGJ-.description: A cell surface receptor that mediates endocytosis of LDL molecules. Located on all cells but most concentrated on hepatocytes. Defects or deficiency of the LDL receptor cause familial hypercholesterolemia.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

euXxJ-.title: NREM sleep
euXxJ-.description: A dreamless phase of sleep that consists of three stages (N1, N2, N3) of increasing sleep depth. Characterized by low frequency and high-voltage waves on EEG.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Sleep physiology

fuXkq-.title: Mycoplasma pneumonia
fuXkq-.description: An atypical pneumonia caused by Mycoplasma pneumoniae that manifests with insidious onset, nonproductive cough and low-grade fever. Associated with the formation of cold agglutinins (IgM) and subclinical hemolytic anemia.

guXFq-.title: Cholesterol 7-α hydroxylase
guXFq-.description: A cytochrome p450 enzyme that converts cholesterol to 7-alpha-hydroxycholesterol. This step is the first and rate-limiting step of bile acid synthesis. Deficiency of 7-α hydroxylase is associated with an increased risk of gallstone disease.

SuXyq-.title: Inositol
SuXyq-.description: A carbolic sugar used in the treatment of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) of preterm neonates.

huXcI-.title: Funny current
huXcI-.description: A slow, inward current that occurs at the start of phase 4 of the pacemaker action potential as a result of influx of Na+ and K+ through hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels. Spontaneous depolarization caused by this current is responsible for the automaticity of cardiac pacemaker cells.

media.title: Action potentials of pacemaker cells in the sinus node

3uXSI-.title: Homeostasis
3uXSI-.description: A state of equilibrium maintained by many interdependent, active, physiologic processes.

RuXlI-.title: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channel
RuXlI-.description: An ion channel on the surface of pacemaker cells that opens following membrane repolarization and allows a slows influx of sodium and potassium ions (funny current). Responsible for the spontaneous depolarization of pacemaker cells. Cyclic nucleotides (e.g., cAMP) can bind to it and lower the threshold for its activation.

juX_I-.title: Biot respirations
juX_I-.description: A pathological breathing pattern characterized by irregular breathing followed by regular or irregular periods of apnea. Etiologies include increased intracranial pressure and brain damage (e.g., pontine injuries).

PuXWr-.title: Cyclin-CDK complex
PuXWr-.description: A complex protein that consists of a cyclin and a cyclin-dependent kinase. Phosphorylate other proteins to regulate the progression of the cell cycle. Must be activated and inactivated at specific points of the cell cycle to allow for normal progression of the cell cycle.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

4uX3r-.title: Phosphofructokinase-2
4uX3r-.description: An enzyme that interconverts fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and fructose-6-phosphate. Fructose bisphosphatase-2 is active in the fasting state and creates fructose-6-phosphate for gluconeogenesis. Phosphofructokinase-2 is active in the fed state and increases glycolysis.

media.title: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis regulation by fructose-2,6-bisphosphate

kuXmr-.title: Ketosis
kuXmr-.description: A condition of elevated serum ketone body concentration. Seen in starvation states, diabetes, and as an effect of intentionally ketogenic diets.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Glycogen storage disorders (GSD)

OuXIr-.title: Glucose-6-phosphate
OuXIr-.description: An important intermediate in the production and catabolism of glucose. In catabolic reactions (e.g. glycolysis), this molecule is formed when hexokinase/glucokinase converts glucose to glucose-6-phosphate. In the production of glucose (e.g. gluconeogenesis), glucose-6-phosphate is the final intermediate before glucose-6-phosphatase converts it to glucose for release into the serum.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Sequence of reactions

luXvr-.title: Respiratory rate
luXvr-.description: The number of breaths taken per minute. Normal rate for an adult at rest is 12-20 breaths per minute.

NuX-r-.title: Neuritis
NuX-r-.description: An inflammation of a peripheral nerve. Can lead to pain, numbness, and/or loss of function. Etiologies include viral infection,  rheumatologic, and autoinflammatory diseases.

muXV7-.title: Ophthalmic nerve
muXV7-.description: The ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve. Supplies sensation to the forehead, anterior scalp, upper eyelid, and eyeball. Also contains sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that facilitate pupil dilation and innervate the ciliary body, iris, lacrimal gland, conjunctiva, and cornea.

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Origin and pathways of the cranial nerves

media.title: Trigeminal nerve branches and areas of sensory innervation

5uXi7-.title: Maxillary nerve
5uXi7-.description: The maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve. A purely sensory nerve that exits the skull via the infraorbital foramen and supplies sensation to the lower eyelid, cheek, part of the nasal cavity, lateral nose, upper lip, teeth, and gingiva.

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Origin and pathways of the cranial nerves

media.title: Trigeminal nerve branches and areas of sensory innervation

MuXM7-.title: Neuroendocrine tumor
MuXM7-.description: A well-differentiated tumor derived from neuroendocrine cells. NETs are found throughout the body. They most commonly arise in the lungs and gastrointestinal system and are classified as functioning or nonfunctioning. Examples include insulinoma, glucagonoma, and lung neuroendocrine tumor. Markers include synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and neuron-specific enolase.

nuX77-.title: N-acetylglucosaminyl-1-phosphotransferase
nuX77-.description: Enzyme that phosphorylates mannose residues to form mannose-6-phosphate in glycoproteins in the Golgi apparatus, which marks them for transportation to lysosomes. Impairment causes I-cell disease.

LuXw7-.title: Phosphofructokinase-1
LuXw7-.description: The rate-limiting enzyme in the pathway of glycolysis. Converts fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-biphosphate. Stimulated by insulin, AMP, and fructose 2,6-biphosphate. Inhibited by glucagon, ATP, and citrate.

ouX0H-.title: Autoclave
ouX0H-.description: A device that utilizes pressurized steam to sterilize medical instruments. Generally considered lethal to bacteria, viruses, fungi, and spores.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

KuXUH-.title: Meningoencephalitis
KuXUH-.description: The simultaneous inflammation of the brain parenchyma (encephalitis) and the meniges (meningitis).

6uXjH-.title: Medulla oblongata
6uXjH-.description: A part of the hindbrain situated in the brainstem beneath the pons and anterior to the cerebellum. Involved in the regulation of the autonomic nervous system, including cardiorespiratory function, bulbar reflexes, and vasomotor function.

media.title: Cranial nerve nuclei of the medulla oblongata

IuXYs-.title: Eicosanoids
IuXYs-.description: A family of inflammatory signaling molecules derived from fatty acids, such as arachidonic acid. There are multiple subfamilies of eicosanoids, including prostaglandins, thromboxanes, leukotrienes, lipoxins, resolvins, and eoxins.

ruXfs-.title: Acetoacetate
ruXfs-.description: A ketone body produced by the liver during states of ketogenesis (e.g., fasting states, insulin deficiency). Can be detected in the urine.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Ketone body metabolism

7uX4s-.title: Thiophorase
7uX4s-.description: A mitochondrial enzyme of ketogenolysis. Activates acetoacetate to acetoacetyl-CoA by using succinyl-CoA as a coenzyme. Acetoacetyl-CoA is then converted into two molecules of acetyl-CoA that can be introduced into the citric acid cycle. Lack of this enzyme prevents hepatocytes from metabolizing ketone bodies for energy.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Ketone body metabolism

HuXKs-.title: Intestinal transit time
HuXKs-.description: The time required for food to pass through the gastrointenstinal tract. Assessment of transit time can be used to evaluate chronic constipation, diarrhea, dyspepsia, and malabsorptive disorders.

suXts-.title: Inguinal canal
suXts-.description: A passage along the groin region on the inferior part of the abdominal wall. Bounded superiorly by the internal oblique and tranversus abdominis muscles, anteriorly by the external and internal oblique aponeuroses, inferiorly by the inguinal ligament, and posteriorly by the transversalis fascia and conjoint tendon.

GuXBs-.title: Tunica vaginalis
GuXBs-.description: A pouch of serous membrane that covers the testis. Forms from the processus vaginalis during the descent of the testis from the abdomen into the scrotum.

media.title: Layers of the abdominal wall and male reproductive organs

tuXXG-.title: Van gene
tuXXG-.description: Group of genes that convey resistance to vancomycin in Enterococcus and other species (e.g., S. aureus). Some induce a change in peptidoglycan synthesis, while others encode enzymes. All cause diminished vancomycin affinity.

FuXgG-.title: Spermatic cord
FuXgG-.description: A cord-like structure that runs through the inguinal canal. Contains the vas deferens, tunica vaginalis, testicular and cremasteric arteries and nerves, pampiniform plexus, and lymphatic vessels. Consists of three layers of tissue: the external spermatic fascia (derived from the external oblique), the cremasteric muscle and fascia (derived from the internal oblique), and the internal spermatic fascia (derived from the fascia transversalis).

media.title: Structure and content of the spermatic cord

8uXOG-.title: DNA primer
8uXOG-.description: A short sequence of DNA nucleotides on which DNA polymerase initiates replication. Commonly used in polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

EuX8G-.title: Musculocutaneous nerve injury
EuX8G-.description: A nerve injury caused by trauma and/or compression of cervical roots C5-C7. Manifests with sensory loss over the lateral aspect of the forearm from the elbow to the base of the thumb, loss of elbow flexion (secondary to brachialis and coracobrachialis paralysis), and loss of forearm supination (secondary to biceps brachii paralysis).

destinations.label: Peripheral nerve injuries → Nerve injuries in the upper body

DuX1t-.title: Northern blot
DuX1t-.description: A laboratory method that involves gel electrophoresis and blotting to detect RNA sequences.

9uXNt-.title: Cavernous sinus
9uXNt-.description: A collection of venous sinuses that surround the pituitary gland. Collects blood from the eyes and superficial cortex and drains into the internal jugular vein. The internal carotid artery and the abducens nerve pass through the middle of the cavernous sinus, while the oculomotor, trochlear, ophthalmic, and maxillary nerve are located towards the lateral wall of the sinus.

CuXqt-.title: Basal nucleus
CuXqt-.description: A collection of neurons in the substantia innominata of the basal forebrain. It is the major source of cholinergic innervation of the cerebral cortex. Decreases in acetylcholine synthesis by this area are associated with Alzheimer disease and Huntington disease; increases are associated with Parkinson disease.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

xuXEt-.title: Genioglossus
xuXEt-.description: A fan-shaped muscle that forms the greater portion of the body of the tongue. Protracts and depresses the tongue. Innervated by the hypoglossal nerve (CN  XII).

BuXzt-.title: Hyoglossus muscle
BuXzt-.description: An extrinsic muscle of the tongue that originates from the hyoid bone and inserts into the lateral and inferior aspects of the tongue. Depresses and retracts the tongue.

media.title: Muscles of the palate and extrinsic muscles of the tongue

yuXdF-.title: Styloglossus muscle
yuXdF-.description: A muscle of the tongue that originates from the styloid process. Elevates and retracts the tongue. Innervated by the hypoglossal nerve.

_uX5F-.title: Foliate papillae
_uX5F-.description: A series of structures located on the posterolateral aspects of the tongue that contain lingual taste buds.

-uXDF-.title: Fungiform papillae
-uXDF-.description: A series of structures located on the anterior two-thirds of the tongue that contain lingual taste buds. Primarily innervated by trigeminal fibers.

ZEXZ8-.title: KatG gene
ZEXZ8-.description: A gene expressed by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that encodes a catalase-peroxidase enzyme that normally converts isoniazid into its active metabolite. Mutations in this gene can result in decreased enzyme activity and confer resistance to isoniazid.

0EXe8-.title: Lingual artery
0EXe8-.description: A branch of the external carotid artery that supplies the floor of the oral cavity and tongue. Branches include the sublingual artery, dorsal lingual artery, suprahyoid artery, and deep lingual artery.

media.title: Branches of the external carotid artery

aEXQ8-.title: Lingual vein
aEXQ8-.description: A paired vein that drains the tongue. Enters the internal jugular vein near the hyoid bone.

YEXn8-.title: Raphe nuclei
YEXn8-.description: A group of serotonergic neurons distributed near the midline of the brainstem that projects to various parts of the brain. Facilitates motor, somatosensory, and limbic functions. Dysfunction is associated with several neuropsychiatric and neurological disorders.

bEXH8-.title: Masseter muscle
bEXH8-.description: A muscle of mastication that originates from the zygomatic arch and inserts into the angle of the mandible. Innervated by the mandibular nerve. Elevates and protrudes the mandible.

XEX98-.title: Anterior horn cell
XEX98-.description: Motor neurons present in the anterior grey column (ventral horn) of the spinal cord. Axons of these neurons innervate skeletal muscles in the extremities.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

cEXau-.title: Temporalis muscle
cEXau-.description: A muscle of mastication that originates in the temporal fossa and inserts into the coronoid process and mandibular ramus. Innervated by the mandibular nerve. Elevates and retracts the mandible.

1EX2u-.title: Lateral pterygoid muscle
1EX2u-.description: A muscle of mastication that extends between the infratemporal fossa and the condyle of the mandible. Innervated by the mandibular nerve.

dEXou-.title: Primary palate
dEXou-.description: An anatomical structure that forms the roof of the mouth. Formed through the fusion of the medial nasal prominences in the midline with palatine processes. The palatine processes are horizontal processes of the developing maxilla.

media.title: Development of the face and palate

3EXSv-.title: Extrinsic muscles of the tongue
3EXSv-.description: A group of four muscles of the tongue (i.e., genioglossus, hyoglossus, styloglossus, palatoglossus) that originate outside the tongue. Their main function is to alter the position of the tongue.

media.title: Muscles of the palate and extrinsic muscles of the tongue

kEXmD-.title: Oral phase (swallowing)
kEXmD-.description: The first phase of swallowing. Occurs in the oral cavity. Consists of chewing and breakdown of particulate material and combination with saliva. Terminates with the transfer of the food bolus to the oropharynx, which initiates the pharyngeal phase of swallowing.

OEXID-.title: Pharyngeal phase (swallowing)
OEXID-.description: The second phase of swallowing, in which the vocal folds close, the larynx rises, and the epiglottis covers the larynx to prevent food from entering the airway.

lEXvD-.title: Esophageal phase (swallowing)
lEXvD-.description: The third and final phase of swallowing, in which the esophageal sphincter opens to allow a food bolus to move into the esophagus. Terminates when the lower esophageal sphincter opens to allow the food bolus to enter the stomach.

NEX-D-.title: Intrinsic muscles of the tongue
NEX-D-.description: A group of four muscles of the tongue (i.e., superior longitudinal muscle, inferior longitudinal muscle, transverse muscle, vertical muscle) that are located entirely within the tongue (no external attachments). Their main function is to alter the shape and size of the tongue.

LEXww-.title: Voltage-gated sodium channel
LEXww-.description: A sodium ion channel that responds to cell depolarization and facilitates initiation and propagation of the action potential. Found on neurons, cardiac myocytes, and neuroendocrine cells.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Action potential

oEX09-.title: Use-dependence
oEX09-.description: A phenomenon in which the effects of a drug increase as the heart rate increases.

KEXU9-.title: Voltage-gated calcium channel
KEXU9-.description: A calcium ion channel that responds to cell depolarization and plays a role in several cellular functions, including muscle contraction, hormone release, and cell signaling.

6EXj9-.title: Prolyl hydroxylase
6EXj9-.description: An enzyme that hydroxylates L-proline in procollagen. Vitamin C is a cofactor for this enzyme.

qEXC9-.title: ATP7A gene
qEXC9-.description: A gene located on the X chromosome that codes for a copper-transporting transmembrane protein with ATPase activity. Mutations in this gene can cause Menkes disease.

destinations.label: Connective tissue diseases → Connective tissue disorders

IEXYC-.title: Thymic involution
IEXYC-.description: An age-related regression of the thymus that results in a loss of tissue mass and structure, which leads to a decrease in production of naïve T cells.

rEXfC-.title: Crypt abscess
rEXfC-.description: An infiltration of neutrophils into the lumen of intestinal crypts due to a breakdown of the crypt epithelium. Associated with ulcerative colitis.

7EX4C-.title: Neurofibrillary tangle
7EX4C-.description: A collection of intracellular aggregates composed of hyperphosphorylated tau. Accumulation of neurofibrillary tangles impairs neuronal function and leads to cell death. Associated with Alzheimer disease; the severity of tangle formation correlates with the degree of dementia.

tEXXx-.title: Superior temporal gyrus
tEXXx-.description: The superior portion of the temporal lobe, which is involved in the processing of verbal and nonverbal communication. Contains the Wernicke area. Lesions to the superior temporal gyrus can cause conduction aphasia.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

FEXgx-.title: Prostaglandin G2
FEXgx-.description: A cyclic endoperoxide derived from arachidonic acid. It is the first intermediate in the biosynthesis of prostaglandins. Converted to prostaglandin H2 by cyclooxygenase (COX).

vEXAx-.title: α-Synuclein
vEXAx-.description: A protein from the SNCA gene on chromosome 4, primarily found in terminal axons. Excess aggregation forms intracellular Lewy bodies, which are associated with neurodegeneration in α-synucleinopathies (e.g., Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, and multiple system atrophy).

DEX1B-.title: Basal forebrain
DEX1B-.description: A heterogeneous collection of structures located in the inferior region of the forebrain near the midsagittal plane. Includes the nucleus accumbens, nucleus basalis of Meynert, medial septal nucleus, nucleus of the diagonal band, and substantia innominata.

wEXhB-.title: STK11 gene
wEXhB-.description: A tumor suppressor gene that encodes serine/threonine kinase 11. Mutations of this gene are associated with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and 30% of lung adenocarcinomas.

CEXqB-.title: Accommodation
CEXqB-.description: The adjustment of the eyes to different distances (e.g., near vision versus far vision). Primarily mediated by the lens, which changes convexity to adapt the refractory power, and the ciliary muscles (via the Edinger-Westphal nuclei).

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Accommodation and convergence

xEXEB-.title: Serrated polyps
xEXEB-.description: A type of colonic polyp with a star-shaped or serrated luminal structure on histopathologic examination. Considered to have moderate potential to undergo malignant transformation.

BEXzB-.title: Transillumination
BEXzB-.description: The process of using a bright light applied to the skin over a lesion to assess for transmission of light. Masses that contain translucent fluid (e.g., hydrocele, cystic hygroma) will transilluminate, whereas others (e.g., solid tumor, hernia) will not.

yEXdy-.title: Posterior communicating artery
yEXdy-.description: A pair of arteries at the base of the brain that form part of the circle of Willis. Each posterior communicating artery arises from the internal carotid artery and connects with the posterior cerebral artery of its corresponding side. Aneurysms of the posterior communicating artery can cause CN III palsy.

AEXRy-.title: Demyelination
AEXRy-.description: A process in which myelin sheaths of nerves become damaged, which impairs electrical conduction. Central demyelination occurs within the CNS (e.g., multiple sclerosis); peripheral demyelination affects the PNS (e.g., Guillain-Barré syndrome).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

_EX5y-.title: Adenoma-carcinoma sequence
_EX5y-.description: The progressive accumulation of mutations in oncogenes (e.g., KRAS) and tumor suppressor genes (e.g., APC, TP53) that results in the slow transformation of benign colonic adenomas into carcinomas. APC gene mutation (loss of cellular adhesion and increased cellular proliferation) leads to KRAS gene mutation (unregulated cellular signaling and cellular proliferation), which leads to TP53 and DCC gene mutation (malignant transformation of adenoma to carcinoma).

ZvXZA-.title: Cofactors
ZvXZA-.description: An atom or molecule whose presence is essential for the action of an enzyme (e.g., thiamine pyrophosphate for several dehydrogenases).

avXQA-.title: Active site
avXQA-.description: The enzymatically active site for a specific substrate on an enzyme. Consists of a binding site for the substrate and a catalytic site for the enzymatic reaction.

destinations.label: Enzymes and biocatalysis → General characteristics of enzymes

1vX2_-.title: Isomerases
1vX2_-.description: Enzymes that convert compounds from one isomeric form to another. Examples include triosephosphate isomerase, phosphopentose isomerase, and phosphohexose isomerase.

destinations.label: Enzymes and biocatalysis → Classes of enzymes

dvXo_-.title: Trypsinogen
dvXo_-.description: A pancreatic proenzyme that is secreted into the duodenum, where it is activated into trypsin by the enzyme enteropeptidase found on duodenal mucosal cells.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Digestion and absorption of dietary proteins

VvXG_-.title: PRSS1 gene
VvXG_-.description: A gene that encodes cationic trypsinogen. Mutations in this gene cause hereditary pancreatitis and may play a role in the development of idiopathic pancreatitis.

evXx_-.title: SPINK1 gene
evXx_-.description: A gene that encodes a pancreatic trypsin inhibitor. Mutations of this gene are associated with hereditary pancreatitis.

UvXbz-.title: Hereditary pancreatitis
UvXbz-.description: An autosomal dominant condition caused by a mutation in the PRSS1 gene. Characterized by recurrent attacks of acute pancreatitis that can start during childhood.

2vXTz-.title: Familial pancreatitis
2vXTz-.description: A condition of pancreatitis that occurs in a family at a greater incidence than the general population. May or may not be due to a genetic defect. Contrast with hereditary pancreatitis, which follows an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance.

fvXkz-.title: Lingual nerve
fvXkz-.description: A sensory branch of the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve. Supplies somatic sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

TvX6z-.title: Black pigment gallstones
TvX6z-.description: A radiopaque gallstone composed of calcium bilirubinate. Risk factors for development include hemolysis (e.g., from sickle cell anemia, hereditary spherocytosis) and Crohn disease. Cholecystectomy is curative.

media.title: Pathophysiology for different types of gallstones

gvXFz-.title: Brown pigment gallstones
gvXFz-.description: A radiolucent gallstone composed of calcium salts of unconjugated bilirubin and a small amount of cholesterol. In the US, the main cause is unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia (e.g., Gilbert syndrome) and biliary stasis (e.g., total parenteral nutrition). In Asia, these stones are mainly a complication of biliary tract infection (due to bilirubin deconjugation by bacterial β-glucuronidase). Mainly found in the intrahepatic bile ducts rather than the gallbladder and have a tendency to recur after cholecystectomy.

media.title: Pathophysiology for different types of gallstones

SvXyz-.title: β-glucuronidase
SvXyz-.description: A lysosomal enzyme that deconjugates direct bilirubin. Present in breast milk and can cause neonatal unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Also found in intestinal brush border cells, where it deconjugates direct bilirubin to release indirect bilirubin that is then reabsorbed and recycled. Bacterial β-glucuronidase in the biliary tract is implicated in the pathogenesis of brown pigment gallstones.

hvXc--.title: Syphilitic keratitis
hvXc--.description: A nonulcerative, interstitial keratitis that develops as a late complication of syphilis. More common in patients with congenital syphilis than acquired syphilis. Causes stromal inflammation.

3vXS--.title: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
3vXS--.description: A highly aggressive cancer that arises from the pancreatic epithelium (most commonly the ductal epithelium and rarely the acinar epithelium).

RvXl--.title: Glycogen synthase
RvXl--.description: A key enzyme of glycogenesis. Catalyzes the α-1,4-glucosidic linkage of UDP-glucose with the hydroxyl group at the free end of the glycogen chain. Activated by protein phosphatase and inhibited by protein kinase A.

media.title: Glycogen synthesis: elongation of unbranched chains

ivXJ--.title: HMG-CoA reductase
ivXJ--.description: The rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis that breaks down 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A into mevalonate. Activated by insulin and inhibited by glucagon. Inhibitors of HMG-CoA reductase (i.e., statins) are used to treat hypercholesterolemia.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Cholesterol metabolism

QvXu--.title: Jugular fossa
QvXu--.description: A groove in the inferior part of the base of the skull that contains the bulb of the internal jugular vein.

jvX_--.title: Mandibular nerve
jvX_--.description: The mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve. Has both sensory and motor functions. Exits the trigeminal cave and enters the infratemporal fossa through the foramen ovale. Supplies the muscles of mastication and parasympathetic innervation of the parotid gland.

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Origin and pathways of the cranial nerves

media.title: Trigeminal nerve branches and areas of sensory innervation
Cutaneous innervation of the trigeminal nerve

PvXWZZ0.title: Glycopeptides
PvXWZZ0.description: A class of molecules consisting of peptides with carbohydrates attached to amino acid side chains. Some glycopeptides have antimicrobial properties (e.g., vancomycin, bacitracin).

4vX3ZZ0.title: Epoxides
4vX3ZZ0.description: A class of molecules with a reactive ring. Some epoxides (e.g., fosfomycin) have antimicrobial properties.

kvXmZZ0.title: Lipopeptides
kvXmZZ0.description: A class of molecules characterized by a lipid bound to a peptide. Some lipopeptides have antimicrobial properties (e.g., daptomycin, echinocandins).

OvXIZZ0.title: Glycylcyclines
OvXIZZ0.description: A tetracycline-derivative class of antibiotics that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit. Tigecycline is only agent in this class.

lvXvZZ0.title: Lincosamides
lvXvZZ0.description: A class of antibiotics that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit. Clindamycin is the most widely used lincosamide.

mvXV0Z0.title: Oxazolidinones
mvXV0Z0.description: A class of antibiotics that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit. Examples include linezolid and tedizolid.

5vXi0Z0.title: Nitrofurans
5vXi0Z0.description: A class of antimicrobial drugs that interferes with protein and DNA synthesis and function. Examples include nitrofurantoin and nifurtimox.

MvXM0Z0.title: Neurophysins
MvXM0Z0.description: A group of carrier proteins that transport vasopressin and oxytocin from the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei in the hypothalamus to the posterior pituitary gland for storage and release.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamus and pituitary gland

nvX70Z0.title: Scaphoid tubercle
nvX70Z0.description: A palpable bony prominence on the inferior lateral edge of the scaphoid bone. Scaphoid bone fracture can cause scaphoid tubercle tenderness.

LvXw0Z0.title: Perilunate dislocation
LvXw0Z0.description: A form of carpal injury characterized by lunate dislocation and disruption of the lunocapitate ligament, typically caused by hyperextension (e.g., fall on an outstretched hand). Corresponds to stage II of the Mayfield classification of perilunate ligament injuries. May lead to carpal instability. Imaging shows lunate dislocation and dorsal displacement of the capitate.

ovX0aZ0.title: Spinocerebellar tract
ovX0aZ0.description: An ascending neuronal pathway that transmits proprioceptive information to the ipsilateral cerebellum via the inferior cerebellar peduncle. Further subdivided into anterior and posterior tracts.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

KvXUaZ0.title: Postprandial state
KvXUaZ0.description: A descriptor for the period immediately following eating.

6vXjaZ0.title: Fasting state
6vXjaZ0.description: The complete absence of food intake. In a physiological context, it may also refer to the state after complete resorption and digestion of a meal. Fasting leads to metabolic changes (e.g., increased glycogenolysis) to provide energy for maintaining bodily functions.

pvXLaZ0.title: Lactate
pvXLaZ0.description: An end product of glycolytic glucose metabolism that is interconverted to pyruvate by lactate dehydrogenase. Production increases in states of hypoperfusion and impaired aerobic metabolism.

JvXsaZ0.title: Amphenicols
JvXsaZ0.description: A class of antibiotics that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by reversibly binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit. Chloramphenicol is the most widely used amphenicol.

qvXCaZ0.title: Contralateral
qvXCaZ0.description: A descriptor for processes or structures on opposite sides of the body.

IvXYYZ0.title: Lesser petrosal nerve
IvXYYZ0.description: A parasympathetic branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve that synapses in the otic ganglion and innervates the parotid, buccal and labial glands.

rvXfYZ0.title: Accessory meningeal artery
rvXfYZ0.description: A branch of the maxillary artery or middle meningeal artery. Enters the skull through the foramen ovale and supplies the trigeminal ganglion and parts of the dura mater.

7vX4YZ0.title: Pterygoid plexus
7vX4YZ0.description: A venous plexus associated with the infratemporal fossa that drains into the internal maxillary vein. Communicates with other venous structures such as the superficial facial veins and the cavernous sinus and thus can facilitate the spread of infection.

HvXKYZ0.title: Enteropeptidase
HvXKYZ0.description: An enzyme that activates trypsinogen via proteolytic cleavage at the N-terminal.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Digestion and absorption of dietary proteins

GvXBYZ0.title: Internal jugular vein
GvXBYZ0.description: A paired vein that collects blood from the brain, face, and thyroid gland. Arises from the confluence of the sigmoid and inferior petrosal sinus, exits the skull through the jugular foramen, continues inside the carotid sheath together with the carotid artery and the vagus nerve, and unites with the subclavian vein to form the brachiocephalic vein.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

tvXXbZ0.title: Middle meningeal artery
tvXXbZ0.description: A branch of the maxillary artery that enters the skull through the foramen spinosum and supplies large parts of the dura mater and cranial bone. Injury to this artery can cause an epidural hematoma.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

wvXhXZ0.title: Cholesterol
wvXhXZ0.description: A steroid alcohol that is an essential component of the cell membrane. Serves as a precursor for steroid hormones and bile acids.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Cholesterol metabolism

9vXNXZ0.title: Endocardial cushions
9vXNXZ0.description: A set of two protuberances located on the dorsal and ventral inner surfaces of the primitive heart tube. They fuse to separate the atria from the ventricles. Also involved in the formation of the membranous interventricular septum and parts of the atrioventricular septum.

CvXqXZ0.title: Immunophenotyping
CvXqXZ0.description: A technique that uses antibodies conjugated to fluorescent compounds to analyze the protein expression of specific cell populations.

xvXEXZ0.title: Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase
xvXEXZ0.description: A cytosolic enzyme that catalyzes the irreversible step of oxaloacetate conversion to phosphophenolpyruvate. Participates in gluconeogenesis and requires GTP to function.

BvXzXZ0.title: Nucleus pulposus
BvXzXZ0.description: The gelatinous core of the vertebral disc. Derived from the notochord and allows the disc to withstand compression and torsion. Degeneration of the outer fibrous annulus of the vertebral disc can cause extrusion of the nucleus pulposus and compression of a spinal nerve root.

yvXdcZ0.title: External auditory canal
yvXdcZ0.description: A canal that runs from the external acoustic meatus in the pinna to the tympanic membrane. The walls of the outer third of the canal are formed by the cartilage of the pinna. The inner two-thirds of the canal is formed by petrous part of the temporal bone. The canal transmits sound waves to the tympanic membrane.

AvXRcZ0.title: Endolymphatic duct
AvXRcZ0.description: A duct formed by the union of two ductules from the utricle and saccule. Lies within the vestibular aqueduct of the temporal bone and connects the utricle and saccule with the endolymphatic sac.

_vX5cZ0.title: Cell adhesion molecule
_vX5cZ0.description: A group of cell surface proteins that facilitates binding of one cell to another cell or to the extracellular matrix. Include integrins, selectins, and cadherins.

zvXrcZ0.title: Dorsal scapular nerve
zvXrcZ0.description: A motor nerve that arises from the C5 anterior spinal root. Innervates the rhomboid major, rhomboid minor, and levator scapulae muscles.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

-vXDcZ0.title: Endothelin
-vXDcZ0.description: A peptide that plays a major role in vascular homeostasis by causing vasoconstriction and raising blood pressure. Three isoforms of endothelin (ET) are known: ET-1, ET-2, and ET-3.

ZDXZ1Z0.title: Bosentan
ZDXZ1Z0.description: A competitive antagonist of endothelin-1 at the endothelin receptor that decreases pulmonary vascular resistance. Commonly used for treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension.

destinations.label: Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale → Long-term management

0DXe1Z0.title: Gluteus maximus muscle
0DXe1Z0.description: A gluteal muscle that originates from the sacrum, coccyx, ilium, and sacrotuberous ligament and inserts onto the gluteal tuberosity of the femur and iliotibial band. Innervated by the inferior gluteal nerve and supplied by the superior and inferior gluteal arteries. Externally rotates and extends the hip joint.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region

media.title: Superficial and deep muscles of the gluteal region

aDXQ1Z0.title: Steroidogenic acute regulatory protein
aDXQ1Z0.description: A transport protein that transfers cholesterol from the outer mitochondrial membrane to the inner mitochondrial membrane, which is the rate-limiting step for steroid hormone synthesis.

YDXn1Z0.title: α-oxidation
YDXn1Z0.description: A process that breaks down branched-chain fatty acids (e.g., phytanic acid). Occurs exclusively in peroxisomes. Refsum disease is a disorder of α-oxidation.

XDX91Z0.title: Retinoblastoma gene
XDX91Z0.description: A tumor suppressor gene found on chromosome 13 that encodes retinoblastoma protein. Mutations in the Rb gene are associated with retinoblastoma and osteosarcoma, among other cancers.

cDXaWZ0.title: Sacroiliac joint
cDXaWZ0.description: A synovial joint located between the articular surfaces of the ilium and the sacrum. Stabilized by strong sacroiliac ligaments and transmits weight from the vertebral column to the hip bones. Inflammation of the sacroiliac joints results in sacroiliitis, a typical finding in ankylosing spondylitis.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

1DX2WZ0.title: Pubic symphysis
1DX2WZ0.description: A fibrocartilaginous joint between the right and left pubic rami. Forms a part of the anterior boundary of both the pelvic inlet and the pelvic outlet.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

WDXPWZ0.title: Enzymatic glycosylation
WDXPWZ0.description: A post-translational modification in which a carbohydrate is attached to the side chain of an amino acid by glycosyltransferase enzymes. Occurs in the Golgi apparatus and rough endoplasmic reticulum. Based on the site of the side chain to which the carbohydrate group is added, enzymatic glycosylation is classified as N-linkage (addition to a nitrogen), O-linkage (addition to hydroxyl), or C-linkage (addition to carbon).

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

dDXoWZ0.title: Pelvic diaphragm
dDXoWZ0.description: The innermost layer of the pelvic floor. Consists of the broad levator ani muscle and the coccygeus muscle and is surrounded by the superior and inferior fasciae of the pelvic diaphragm.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

VDXGWZ0.title: Circumduction gait
VDXGWZ0.description: An abnormal gait in which the leg does not flex at the knee and ankle, and with each step is rotated away from the body, then towards it, which forms a semicircle. Typically associated with extensor hypertonia in the lower limb.

eDXxWZ0.title: Uveoscleral pathway
eDXxWZ0.description: The nontrabecular outflow of aqueous humor of the eye. Predominantly involves flow from the anterior chamber into the ciliary muscle, from which it enters the supraciliary and suprachoroidal spaces. Accounts for 5-15% of aqueous outflow.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Segments and chambers of the eye

UDXbdZ0.title: Anterior pelvic tilt
UDXbdZ0.description: A forward tilting of the pelvis with respect to the lower limbs. Caused by weakness of the hip extensors (e.g., inferior gluteal nerve injury) or by spasticity of the hip flexors.

2DXTdZ0.title: Backward lurching gait
2DXTdZ0.description: An abnormal gait in which the trunk tilts backwards during the heel strike phase in the limb with the weak hip extensor (e.g., inferior gluteal nerve injury).

destinations.label: Peripheral nerve injuries → Nerve injuries in the lower body

fDXkdZ0.title: Foot drop
fDXkdZ0.description: A deformity in which the foot remains in the plantarflexed (extended) position. It is caused by weakness of ankle dorsiflexors (due to injury to the L5 nerve root, sciatic nerve, common peroneal nerve, or deep peroneal nerve) or by spasticity of the ankle plantar flexors (equinovarus deformity).

TDX6dZ0.title: Tensor fasciae latae muscle
TDX6dZ0.description: A hip muscle that originates from the anterior superior iliac spine and inserts onto the lateral condyle of the tibia via the iliotibial band. Innervated by the superior gluteal nerve and supplied by the superior gluteal artery and lateral circumflex femoral artery. Flexes, abducts, and internally rotates the thigh. Stabilizes the pelvis when bearing weight on the leg.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region

3DXSVZ0.title: Vasodilation
3DXSVZ0.description: A relaxation of the smooth muscle cells that line blood vessels, which decreases vascular resistance and increases blood flow.

RDXlVZ0.title: Vasoconstriction
RDXlVZ0.description: A constriction of the smooth muscle cells that line blood vessels, which increases vascular resistance and reduces blood flow.

QDXuVZ0.title: Sternocleidomastoid muscle
QDXuVZ0.description: A muscle that originates from the medial portion of the clavicle as well as manubrium sterum and inserts into the mastoid process. It is innervated by the spinal accessory nerve. Unilateral contraction of the sternocleidomastoid turns the head to the opposite side. Bilateral sternocleidomastoid contract causes neck flexion.

jDX_VZ0.title: External occipital protuberance
jDX_VZ0.description: A bony prominence on the external surface of the occipital bone. The upper fibers of the trapezius muscle and the nuchal ligament are attached to this protuberance.

PDXWeZ0.title: Insular cortex
PDXWeZ0.description: A region of the cerebral cortex buried within the Sylvian fissure that is part of the limbic system. Involved in the perception of gustatory stimuli and integration of somatosensory stimuli.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

4DX3eZ0.title: GBS
4DX3eZ0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Group B Streptococcus
2. Guillain-Barre syndrome
3. Glasgow-Blatchford score

kDXmeZ0.title: Sudan stain
kDXmeZ0.description: A type of stain with high affinity for lipids often used to evaluate for steatorrhea (e.g., from malabsorption syndromes).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cellular inclusions

ODXIeZ0.title: Glucose-1-phosphate
ODXIeZ0.description: A glucose molecule with a phosphate group attached to the 1'-carbon that is an intermediate of glycogenolysis, glycogenes, and galactose metabolism.

MDXMUZ0.title: Drug-induced liver injury
MDXMUZ0.description: A form of liver injury that is caused by drugs or herbal medicines. May be hepatocellular (e.g., hepatitis, coagulative necrosis), cholestatic, and/or steatotic.

nDX7UZ0.title: Gel electrophoresis
nDX7UZ0.description: A technique that allows macromolecules (DNA, RNA, and proteins) to be detected and separated. Samples are cleaved enzymatically into smaller pieces, then applied on a gel media that is connected to positive and negative electrodes, enabling further segregation of the sample based on size and electrical charge of molecules.

LDXwUZ0.title: Hypothenar hammer syndrome
LDXwUZ0.description: A rare condition describing ulnar artery aneurysm or thrombosis at Guyon's canal. Commonly manifests with pain over the hypothenar eminence, cold sensitivity, and ulnar nerve paresthesia. Seen in individuals whose occupation requires use of vibrating tools, as well as sports with vibration impact to the hand, including baseball, mountain biking, and golfing. Treatment may be conservative or involve operative management.

oDX02Z0.title: FOXP3
oDX02Z0.description: A transcription factor expressed in regulatory T cells that is required for their proper development and function.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

6DXj2Z0.title: pH scale
6DXj2Z0.description: A logarithmic scale that expresses the acidity or alkalinity of a solution based on the concentration of hydrogen ions  (pH = -log[H⁺]). The neutral value of pH is 7, with lower values being acidic and higher values being basic.

pDXL2Z0.title: N-acetylglutamate
pDXL2Z0.description: A molecule that is synthesized from glutamate and acetyl-CoA by the mitochondrial enzyme N-acetylglutamate synthase. It acts as an allosteric activator of the enzyme carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I, which is involved in the urea cycle.

JDXs2Z0.title: Isoelectric point
JDXs2Z0.description: Th pH at which a molecule carries no net electrical charge (i.e., it is electrically neutral).

qDXC2Z0.title: Interventricular foramina
qDXC2Z0.description: A paired set of structures that drain cerebrospinal fluid between the lateral ventricles and the third ventricle. Stenosis of either foramen can cause obstructive hydrocephalus.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

IDXYfZ0.title: N-acetylglutamate synthase
IDXYfZ0.description: A mitochondrial enzyme that synthesizes N-acetylglutamate (NAG) from glutamate and acetyl CoA. This enzyme is present primarily in the liver and small intestine, and its activity is increased by arginine. A deficiency of this enzyme can cause hyperammonemia because NAG is an allosteric activator of the enzyme carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I, which is involved in the conversion of ammonia to urea.

rDXffZ0.title: Lateral apertures
rDXffZ0.description: A paired set of structures located at the cerebellopontine angle that drain cerebrospinal fluid between the fourth ventricle and the subarachnoid space.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

7DX4fZ0.title: Median aperture
7DX4fZ0.description: A structure that drains cerebrospinal fluid between the fourth ventricle (of the ventricular system) and the cisterna magna (of the subarachnoid space).

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

HDXKfZ0.title: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1 deficiency
HDXKfZ0.description: An autosomal recessive condition caused by a mutation of the CPS1 gene on chromosome 2q, which is responsible for the synthesis of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1, an enzyme in the urea cycle that converts ammonia to carbamoyl phosphate. Patients with this condition develop features of hyperammonemia (e.g., encephalopathy) during the neonatal period.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Urea cycle disorders

sDXtfZ0.title: Arachnoid granulations
sDXtfZ0.description: A group of projections of the arachnoid mater into the dural sinuses. Facilitate the reabsorption of cerebrospinal fluid from the subarachnoid space into the venous system.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

GDXBfZ0.title: Orotic acid
GDXBfZ0.description: A heterocyclic compound that is involved in pyrimidine synthesis. It is synthesized from carbamoyl phosphate and aspartate by the enzyme dihydroorotate dehydrogenase. It is combined with phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate and uracil by the enzyme UMP synthase to form uridine monophosphate. Deficiency of UMP synthase (orotic aciduria) or certain enzymes involved in the urea cycle (e.g., ornithine transcarbamylase) can result in orotic acid accumulation.

tDXXTZ0.title: Ornithine
tDXXTZ0.description: A nonproteinogenic amino acid that is involved in the urea cycle. Synthesized in the cytoplasm from arginine by arginase. Transported into the mitochondria by ornithine translocase and converted to citrulline by ornithine transcarbamylase.

FDXgTZ0.title: Deoxynucleotide triphosphates
FDXgTZ0.description: The building blocks of DNA, which include deoxyadenosine triphosphate (dATP), deoxythymidine triphosphate, (dTTP), deoxycytosine triphosphate (dCTP), and deoxyguanosine triphosphate (dGTP).

destinations.label: Purines and pyrimidines → Synthesis of deoxyribonucleotides

8DXOTZ0.title: Citrulline
8DXOTZ0.description: A nonproteinogenic amino acid formed from ornithine and carbamoyl phosphate via ornithine transcarbamylase in the urea cycle as well as from arginine via nitric oxide synthase. Used as a precursor (with aspartate) for argininosuccinate.

uDXpTZ0.title: Argininosuccinate
uDXpTZ0.description: A nonproteinogenic amino acid that is involved in the urea cycle. Produced from citrulline and aspartate by argininosuccinate synthetase and broken down into arginine and fumaric acid by argininosuccinate lyase.

EDX8TZ0.title: CD55
EDX8TZ0.description: A surface protein found on erythrocytes that inhibits intravascular hemolysis by preventing the assembly of C3 and C5 convertases. Normally attached to erythrocytes via a GPI anchor.

vDXATZ0.title: CD59
vDXATZ0.description: A surface protein found on erythrocytes that inhibits intravascular hemolysis by preventing the production of the membrane attack complex. Normally attached to erythrocytes via a GPI anchor.

DDX1gZ0.title: Ornithine translocase
DDX1gZ0.description: A mitochondrial protein that is involved in the urea cycle. It translocates ornithine from cytoplasm into mitochondria and moves citrulline in the opposite direction (from mitochrondria into cytoplasm).

9DXNgZ0.title: Pyramidal tract
9DXNgZ0.description: A collection of nerve fibers that encompasses the corticobulbar and corticospinal tracts. Consists of upper motor neurons that originate in the cerebral cortex and terminate in either the brainstem (corticobulbar tract) or spinal cord (corticospinal tract).

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

CDXqgZ0.title: Extrapyramidal system
CDXqgZ0.description: A neural network of the motor system that facilitates involuntary reflexes, movement, and coordination. Includes the tectospinal, lateral vestibulospinal, pontine reticulospinal, and rubrospinal tracts. Responsible for many of the primitive reflexes (e.g., Babinski reflex).

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

xDXEgZ0.title: Inferior rectal artery
xDXEgZ0.description: A branch of the internal pudendal artery that supplies the anal canal below the pectinate line.

media.title: Blood supply and lymphatic drainage of the anal canal

BDXzgZ0.title: Inferior rectal nerve
BDXzgZ0.description: A branch of the pudendal nerve that provides sensory innervation to the anal canal below the pectinate line and motor innervation to the external anal sphincter.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

yDXdSZ0.title: Inferior gluteal artery
yDXdSZ0.description: A branch of the internal iliac artery that supplies the gluteal region and thigh.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

ADXRSZ0.title: Piriformis muscle
ADXRSZ0.description: A gluteal muscle that originates from the anterior surface of the sacrum and sacrotuberous ligament and inserts onto the greater trochanter. Innervated by the nerve to the piriformis muscle from the sacral plexus and supplied by the superior and inferior gluteal arteries and the lateral sacral artery. Abducts and laterally rotates the thigh.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region

media.title: Muscles of the hip and gluteal region

_DX5SZ0.title: Quadratus femoris
_DX5SZ0.description: A gluteal muscle that laterally rotates the femur at the hip joint.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region

media.title: Muscles of the hip and gluteal region

zDXrSZ0.title: Median sacral artery
zDXrSZ0.description: A branch of the abdominal aorta that supplies pelvic structures including L4 and L5, the sacrum, and the coccyx.
