destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

-DXDSZ0.title: Deep circumflex iliac artery
-DXDSZ0.description: A branch of the external iliac artery that supplies the iliacus, iliac fossa, and deep abdominal wall of the inguinal region.

ZwXZhZ0.title: Superior rectal artery
ZwXZhZ0.description: A branch of the inferior mesenteric artery that supplies the anal canal above the pectinate line (upper two-thirds of the rectum).

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

media.title: Blood supply and lymphatic drainage of the anal canal

0wXehZ0.title: Superior rectal vein
0wXehZ0.description: A vein that drains the distal colon and rectum and empties into the inferior mesenteric vein.

media.title: Pelvis with blood supply of the anal canal
Blood supply and lymphatic drainage of the anal canal

awXQhZ0.title: Inferior rectal veins
awXQhZ0.description: A pair of veins that drains the anal canal below the pectinate line. Empty into the internal pudendal veins.

YwXnhZ0.title: Ubiquitin
YwXnhZ0.description: A small, regulatory protein added to another protein via ubiquitination. Can mark a protein target for degradation by proteasomes.

destinations.label: Proteins and peptides → Protein degradation and associated diseases

bwXHhZ0.title: Mesenteric adenitis
bwXHhZ0.description: An enlargement and inflammation of the mesenteric lymph nodes that causes abdominal pain that can mimic appendicitis. Etiologies include viral and bacterial gastroenteritis and inflammatory bowel disease.

XwX9hZ0.title: Dehydrogenase
XwX9hZ0.description: An enzyme that catalyzes oxidation-reduction reactions.

destinations.label: Enzymes and biocatalysis → Classes of enzymes

cwXa3Z0.title: Pseudopalisades
cwXa3Z0.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by elongated nuclei stacked in rows that often radiate away from a central area of necrosis. Classically associated with glioblastoma multiforme.

1wX23Z0.title: Auriculotemporal nerve
1wX23Z0.description: A sensory branch of the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve. Has a cutaneous branch that supplies sensory innervation to the skin over the tragus, temple, and tympanic membrane. Also has small articular branches to the temporomandibular joint and a parasympathetic branch to the parotid gland.

destinations.label: Skull → Temporal, infratemporal, and pterygopalatine fossae

media.title: Trigeminal nerve branches and areas of sensory innervation

WwXP3Z0.title: Mean arterial pressure
WwXP3Z0.description: An indicator of hemodynamic stability. Can be calculated as cardiac output (CO) × total peripheral resistance (TPR), or estimated as ⅓ systolic pressure + ⅔ diastolic pressure.

dwXo3Z0.title: Hyporeflexia
dwXo3Z0.description: A condition of diminished deep tendon reflexes. Common causes include lower motor neuron injury (e.g., from Guillain–Barré syndrome), hypothyroidism, drug reactions (e.g., benzodiazepine toxicity), and hypermagnesemia.

VwXG3Z0.title: Carbamoyl phosphate
VwXG3Z0.description: A molecule that transfers its carbamoyl group to ornithine to form citrulline in the first step of the urea cycle. Also involved in pyrimidine synthesis to form orotic acid.

ewXx3Z0.title: Uridine monophosphate
ewXx3Z0.description: A nucleotide used in RNA in place of thymine. Also serves as an intermediate in the pyrimidine synthesis pathway.

UwXbRZ0.title: Uridine monophosphate synthase
UwXbRZ0.description: An enzyme that forms uridine monophosphate from orotic acid and phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate. The enzyme actually performs 2 discrete functions, orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and orotidine 5'-monophosphate decarboxylase, both coded by a single gene. Deficiency of this enzyme causes orotic aciduria.

2wXTRZ0.title: Inosine monophosphate
2wXTRZ0.description: A nucleoside involved in purine synthesis that serves as a precursor for adenosine monophosphate (AMP) and guanosine monophosphate (GMP).

fwXkRZ0.title: Phosphoribosylpyrophosphate
fwXkRZ0.description: A molecule involved in pyrimidine and purine synthesis. Transfers phosphoribose groups for the synthesis of several nucleotide monophosphates (e.g., UMP, GMP, AMP).

TwX6RZ0.title: Apolipoprotein C-III
TwX6RZ0.description: An apolipoprotein found on very low density lipoprotein. Increased levels are associated with hypertriglyceridemia and atherosclerosis.

gwXFRZ0.title: HHS
gwXFRZ0.description:
1. Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state
2. Hypothenar hammer syndrome
3. United States Department of Health and Human Services

SwXyRZ0.title: Antiparietal cell antibodies
SwXyRZ0.description: A type of antibody that targets gastric parietal cells, causing parietal cell destruction, decreased acid production, and chronic gastritis. Associated with pernicious anemia.

hwXciZ0.title: Anti-IF antibodies
hwXciZ0.description: Antibodies that target intrinsic factor and inhibit vitamin B12 binding. Associated with pernicious anemia.

RwXliZ0.title: Vitamin E toxicity
RwXliZ0.description: A rare toxicity of vitamin E that can alter the metabolism of warfarin, which results in an enhanced anticoagulant effect that increases the risk of bleeding.

iwXJiZ0.title: Treacher Collins syndrome
iwXJiZ0.description: An autosomal dominant disorder caused by defective neural crest cell migration into the first and second branchial arches. Typical features include cleft palate, slanting eyes (with the lateral canthi more inferior than the medial canthi), maxillary and mandibular hypoplasia (depressed cheekbones and overbite), and ear deformities with conductive hearing loss.

destinations.label: Rare inherited syndromes → Treacher Collins syndrome

QwXuiZ0.title: Fourth branchial cleft cyst
QwXuiZ0.description: A rare anomaly caused by persistence of the fourth branchial cleft (normally resorbed in utero) as a closed sac. Typically manifests as a left-sided abscess in close proximity to the left lobe of the thyroid gland.

jwX_iZ0.title: Lacunar ligament
jwX_iZ0.description: A triangular ligament that extends from the inguinal ligament superiorly to the pectineal line inferiorly with its apex facing the pubic symphysis. Formed by the reflected portion of the medial end of the external oblique aponeurosis and forms the medial boundary of the femoral canal. This ligament can be cut to widen the femoral canal in the event of a strangulated femoral hernia.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Femoral triangle and fasial compartments of the thigh

4wX3QZ0.title: Phenylalanine
4wX3QZ0.description: An essential amino acid and precursor to tyrosine, it can be metabolized into either ketone bodies or glucose. At high concentrations, such as in phenylketonuria (PKU), phenylalanine can be toxic.

kwXmQZ0.title: Femoral canal
kwXmQZ0.description: The most medial compartment of the femoral sheath. Bounded by the inguinal ligament anteriorly, the pubic ramus and pectineal ligament posteriorly, the lacunar ligament medially, and the femoral vein laterally. Herniation of intra-abdominal contents through this canal causes femoral hernia.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Femoral triangle and fasial compartments of the thigh

OwXIQZ0.title: Inferior epigastric artery
OwXIQZ0.description: A branch of the external iliac artery that anastomoses with the superior epigastric artery. Supplies the rectus abdominis muscle and parts of the deep abdominal wall. Variant anatomy includes divisions into superficial and deep inferior epigastric arteries.

destinations.label: Anterior abdominal wall → Vasculature and innervation

lwXvQZ0.title: Conjoint tendon
lwXvQZ0.description: A tendon formed from the aponeuroses of the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles. Attached medially to the pubic tubercle. Forms the medial portion of the posterior inguinal canal. Weakness of the conjoint tendon results in direct inguinal hernia.

NwX-QZ0.title: GABA transaminase
NwX-QZ0.description: An enzyme involved in the degradation of the neurotransmitter GABA. Inhibited by some anticonvulsant drugs (e.g., vigabatrin, valproic acid).

MwXMjZ0.title: Middle ear
MwXMjZ0.description: An air-filled cavity between the external ear canal and the inner ear. The ossicles (the malleus, the incus, and the stapes) and the facial nerve cross the middle ear space.

nwX7jZ0.title: Inner ear
nwX7jZ0.description: The innermost portion of the ear. Includes structures such as the cochlea (involved in hearing) and the vestibular system (involved in maintaining balance) and is situated within the petrous part of the temporal bone.

LwXwjZ0.title: Rectus sheath
LwXwjZ0.description: A sheath formed by the aponeuroses of the external oblique, internal oblique, and transversus abdominis muscles. The anterior rectus sheath extends along the entire length of the rectus abdominis; the posterior rectus sheath is absent below the arcuate line. The anterior and posterior sheaths fuse at the lateral end of the rectus abdominis to form the linea semilunaris.

6wXjPZ0.title: Ventral hernia
6wXjPZ0.description: The protrusion of intraabdominal contents through the anterior abdominal wall. Includes epigastric, umbilical, and the majority of incisional hernias.

pwXLPZ0.title: Eustachian tube
pwXLPZ0.description: A canal that connects the middle ear cavity to the nasopharynx. It is responsible for equilibrating the middle ear pressure with atmospheric pressure.

qwXCPZ0.title: Transversalis fascia
qwXCPZ0.description: The fascia of the transversus abdominis muscle, which forms the posterior lamina of the rectus sheath and lies anterior to the peritoneum.

media.title: Peritoneum and fascias of the abdomen

IwXY4Z0.title: Aponeurosis
IwXY4Z0.description: A flat, white connective tissue sheath that connects the muscle it originates from to the part it moves. Examples include the palmar aponeurosis, plantar aponeurosis, and aponeuroses of the internal and external oblique muscles.

media.title: Plantar aponeurosis and the medial longitudinal arch of the foot

rwXf4Z0.title: Tympanic cavity
rwXf4Z0.description: An air-filled cavity in the middle ear that contains the ear ossicles and helps conduct sound from the external ear to the inner ear.

7wX44Z0.title: Inguinal ligament
7wX44Z0.description: A fibrous band that extends from the anterior superior iliac spine laterally to the pubic tubercle medially. Formed by the lower free border of the external oblique aponeurosis, which folds upon itself. The internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles originate from its lateral end.

HwXK4Z0.title: Median umbilical ligament
HwXK4Z0.description: A remnant of the obliterated urachus that extends from the apex of the urinary bladder to the umbilicus. Covered by the median umbilical fold, a layer of peritoneum. Used as a landmark during laparoscopic surgical exploration of the abdomen and pelvis.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Embryology

swXt4Z0.title: Mastoid process
swXt4Z0.description: A protuberance of the temporal bone located posterior to the ear. Serves as the attachment point for several muscles (e.g., sternocleidomastoid, posterior belly of the digastric muscle).

GwXB4Z0.title: PTEN gene
GwXB4Z0.description: A tumor suppressor gene that negatively regulates the PI3k/AKT pathway. Mutations in this gene are associated with Cowden syndrome and breast, prostate, and endometrial cancer

twXXkZ0.title: Lateral thoracic artery
twXXkZ0.description: A branch of the axillary artery that supplies blood to the lateral structures of the thorax and the breast.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries
Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage

FwXgkZ0.title: Medial umbilical ligaments
FwXgkZ0.description: A pair of peritoneal folds that lie on the sides of the median umbilical ligament and extend from the pelvis to the umbilicus. Remnants of the umbilical arteries. Used as landmarks during laparoscopic surgical exploration.

destinations.label: Prenatal and postnatal physiology →  Fetal circulation

8wXOkZ0.title: Lateral umbilical ligament
8wXOkZ0.description: A pair of peritoneal fold that contain the inferior epigastric vessels. They lie lateral to the medial umbilical ligaments and extend from the deep inguinal ring to the arcuate line on either side.

uwXpkZ0.title: Small nuclear ribonucleoprotein
uwXpkZ0.description: A complex of small nuclear RNA sequences and proteins. Can combine with other RNA sequences and proteins to form spliceosomes.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Post-transcriptional modification (RNA processing)

EwX8kZ0.title: Supravesical fossae
EwX8kZ0.description: A pair of peritoneal depressions bounded by the central median umbilical ligament and the two medial umbilical ligaments. Herniation of bowel through the peritoneal fold of the supravesical fossae can rarely occur and cause an internal hernia.

vwXAkZ0.title: Heat shock protein
vwXAkZ0.description: A type of chaperone protein with several diverse functions, which include protein folding, assembly of protein complexes, sorting of proteins into proper subcellular compartments, cell-cycle control, and signaling.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Protein folding and misfolding

DwX1OZ0.title: Anterior nucleus (hypothalamus)
DwX1OZ0.description: A hypothalamic nucleus that regulates dissipation of heat via the parasympathetic nervous system. Damage to this region results in hyperthermia.

wwXhOZ0.title: Beta-globin locus
wwXhOZ0.description: A gene cluster that contains genes that encode beta-globin, delta-globin, gamma-globins, and episilon-globin. Expression of these genes is controlled by a single locus control region.

9wXNOZ0.title: Superficial perineal pouch
9wXNOZ0.description: A space in the anterior perineal region (urogenital triangle) that is bounded superiorly by the perineal membrane and inferiorly by the superficial perineal fascia (fascia of Colles). It contains the superficial perineal nerves, branches of the perineal artery, and the ischiocavernosus, bulbospongiosus, and superficial transverse perineal muscles. In females, this space also contains the greater vestibular glands and their ducts, while in males it includes the ducts of the bulbourethral glands.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

CwXqOZ0.title: Clathrin
CwXqOZ0.description: A protein that facilitates the formation of coated vesicles (e.g., from the trans-Golgi network to lysosomes and for receptor-mediated endocytosis)

media.title: Structure and function of the Golgi apparatus

xwXEOZ0.title: Anti-SRP antibody
xwXEOZ0.description: One of the myositis-specific autoantibodies, with activity against the signal recognition particle involved in translocation of proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum. Associated most commonly with a phenotype of immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy. However, it may also be seen in dermatomyositis.

BwXzOZ0.title: Brown adipose tissue
BwXzOZ0.description: A mitochondria-rich type of adipose tissue used to generate heat, particularly in young infants. Found around the kidneys, adrenal glands, pancreas, interscapular area, and neck. The brown color is derived from cytochrome c, which is located in the densely populated mitochondria

ywXdlZ0.title: Rectovesical pouch
ywXdlZ0.description: Anatomic space in the peritoneal cavity between the posterior bladder and anterior rectum. In male individuals, this space is the lowest part of the peritoneal cavity in the upright position. Serves as a potential space for intraperitoneal fluid collection.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic cavity and pelvic spaces

_wX5lZ0.title: Trans-Golgi network
_wX5lZ0.description: A secretory pathway that sorts newly synthesized proteins and endocytosed extracellular materials into different subcellular compartments.

zwXrlZ0.title: Nitric oxide synthase
zwXrlZ0.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the production of nitric oxide from arginine. Plays an important role in modulating smooth muscle tone, especially in the endothelium.

-wXDlZ0.title: Cadherins
-wXDlZ0.description: A family of calcium-dependent glycoproteins that facilitate cell-to-cell adhesion at adherens junctions. Link to the actin cytoskeleton via catenin and vinculin.

Z9XZNZ0.title: Catenin
Z9XZNZ0.description: A protein located on the intracellular side of the cell membrane that connects intracellular actin filaments with transmembrane adhesion proteins (e.g., cadherins).

a9XQNZ0.title: Mitogen-activated protein kinase
a9XQNZ0.description: A family of serine/threonine protein kinases involved in cell signaling processes mediating apoptosis, survival, proliferation, and differentiation. Extracellular stimuli include cytokines, growth factors, and mitogens.

b9XHNZ0.title: Intraperitoneal organs
b9XHNZ0.description: The organs that are completely covered by the visceral peritoneum. Includes the stomach, first part of duodenum, jejunum, ileum, cecum, appendix, transverse colon, sigmoid colon, liver, gallbladder, spleen, and the tail of the pancreas.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Intraperitoneal and extraperitoneal abdominal structures

X9X9NZ0.title: Secondary retroperitoneal organ
X9X9NZ0.description: An organ that is initially located intraperitoneally but becomes retroperitoneal due to the fusion of the organs and their mesenteries to the parietal peritoneal lining (retroperitonealization). Includes the ascending and descending colon, duodenum (second, third and fourth parts), and pancreas.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Intraperitoneal and extraperitoneal abdominal structures

19X2mZ0.title: Hyperuricemia
19X2mZ0.description: An increased serum concentration of uric acid (≥7 mg/dL for men; ≥6.0 mg/dL for women). Etiologies include uric acid overproduction (e.g., increased cell turnover in malignancies, hemolytic anemias) and increased purine consumption (e.g., excessive alcohol or protein). Increases the risk of developing gout and kidney failure.

W9XPmZ0.title: Mood stabilizer
W9XPmZ0.description: A group of drugs used to treat acute episodes of mania and depression and to prevent relapses of manic, hypomanic, or depressive episodes in patients with bipolar disorder and schizoaffective disorder. Examples include lithium and certain anticonvulsants, such as sodium valproate, carbamazepine, and lamotrigine.

e9XxmZ0.title: Axillary lymph node dissection
e9XxmZ0.description: A surgical procedure used in the treatment of breast cancer. Ten or more axillary lymph nodes are removed for histopathologic evaluation of lymph node metastasis.

U9Xb5Z0.title: Precontemplation stage
U9Xb5Z0.description: The first stage in the transtheoretical model of behavioral change, in which an individual does not realize that a specific behavior is problematic.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

29XT5Z0.title: Phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate synthetase
29XT5Z0.description: An enzyme that converts ribose-5-phosphate into phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate (PRPP). PRPP is needed for numerous biosynthesis pathways including de-novo synthesis of purine and pyrimidine nucleotides (e.g., AMP, GMP, UMP).

f9Xk5Z0.title: Homocystine
f9Xk5Z0.description: A disulfide consisting of two molecules of the amino acid homocysteine and the main transport form of homocysteine in the blood (besides albumin-bound homocysteine).

T9X65Z0.title: Adenosine monophosphate
T9X65Z0.description: A nucleotide that consists of a purine nucleoside (adenosine), which has one phosphate group attached to the 5′ carbon. The purine nucleoside adenosine, in turn, consists of a nitrogenous, double-ring purine base (adenine) attached to ribose 1-phosphate.

g9XF5Z0.title: Guanosine monophosphate
g9XF5Z0.description: A nucleotide that consists of a purine nucleoside (guanosine), which has one phosphate group attached to the 5′ carbon. The purine nucleoside guanosine, in turn, consists of a nitrogenous, double-ring purine base (guanine) attached to ribose 1-phosphate.

S9Xy5Z0.title: Leukodystrophies
S9Xy5Z0.description: A group of genetic disorders that affect the white matter of the central nervous system by disrupting the growth and/or maintenance of the myelin sheath.

h9XcMZ0.title: Peripheral nervous system
h9XcMZ0.description: The component of the nervous system (e.g., nerves and ganglia) that does not include the brain and spinal cord.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

39XSMZ0.title: Paracellular transport
39XSMZ0.description: The transport of materials (e.g., ions, sugars, amino acids, peptides) between cells. Restricted by tight junctions.

R9XlMZ0.title: CD25
R9XlMZ0.description: A protein that is expressed on dendritic cells and regulatory T cells. Forms a component of the IL-2 receptor. Targeted by daclizumab to treat relapsing multiple sclerosis.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

i9XJMZ0.title: Utricle
i9XJMZ0.description: An otolith organ that senses motion in the horizontal plane (forward-backward and left-right movement).

media.title: Receptive fields of the vestibular system

Q9XuMZ0.title: Saccule
Q9XuMZ0.description: An otolith organ that senses motion in the sagittal plane (vertical movement).

media.title: Receptive fields of the vestibular system

j9X_MZ0.title: Semicircular canal
j9X_MZ0.description: A component of the labyrinth of the inner ear that senses rotary movement. There are three semicircular canals: posterior, horizontal (lateral), and anterior.

49X3nZ0.title: Cochlear duct
49X3nZ0.description: The endolymph-filled inner ear cavity, which originates at the saccule and ends as a blind pouch. Separated from the vestibular duct by the Reissner membrane and from the tympanic duct by the basilar membrane. Contains the organ of Corti.

k9XmnZ0.title: Tympanic duct
k9XmnZ0.description: The perilymph-filled inner ear cavity that extends from the round window to the helicotrema, after which it continues as the vestibular duct. Separated from the cochlear duct by the basilar membrane. Transduces mechanical impulses from the middle ear and conducts them to the organ of Corti.

O9XInZ0.title: Umbo
O9XInZ0.description: The most depressed portion of the tympanic membrane where the malleus attaches.

l9XvnZ0.title: Cone of light
l9XvnZ0.description: A cone-shaped light reflection of an otoscope light in the anterior, inferior quadrant of the tympanic membrane. Can be absent in several middle ear disorders (e.g., otitis media).

N9X-nZ0.title: Stria vascularis
N9X-nZ0.description: The epithelial lining of the outer cochlear wall, which contains many small blood vessels and capillaries that produce endolymph for the cochlear duct.

m9XVLZ0.title: Parathyroid cells
m9XVLZ0.description: The primary cell type of the parathyroid gland. Responsible for the production and release of parathyroid hormone. Regulate calcium homeostasis in response to stimulation of membrane-bound, calcium-sensing receptors.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands → Parathyroid glands

L9XwLZ0.title: Vanillylmandelic acid
L9XwLZ0.description: A byproduct of epinephrine and norepinephrine degradation. Increased urine concentrations of VMA are associated with neuroendocrine tumors, e.g. neuroblastoma.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla

o9X0oZ0.title: Homovanillic acid
o9X0oZ0.description: A byproduct of dopamine degradation. Increased urine concentrations of HVA are associated with neuroendocrine tumors, e.g., neuroblastoma.

J9XsoZ0.title: Acoustic maculae
J9XsoZ0.description: The sensory neuroepithelium of the utricle and saccule that detects changes in gravity (e.g., head position). Generates electric impulses transmitted by the vestibular nerve and therefore contributes to maintaining posture, orientation, and stability.

u9Xp6Z0.title: Clinoid processes
u9Xp6Z0.description: The parts of the sphenoid bone that surround the sella turcica. Divided into anterior and posterior parts.

D9X1pZ0.title: Otic capsule
D9X1pZ0.description: A mesenchymal cartilaginous shell around the otic vesicle that develops into the bony labyrinth. Can be injured in petrous temporal bone fractures.

w9XhpZ0.title: Skull base
w9XhpZ0.description: The floor of the cranial cavity that separates the brain from other facial structures. Consists of 5 main bones (ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, paired frontal, and paired temporal bones) and is divided into 3 regions (anterior, middle, and posterior cranial fossae).

99XNpZ0.title: Cranial fossa
99XNpZ0.description: The floor of the cranial cavity, which is divided into three distinct depressions: the anterior cranial fossa, middle cranial fossa, and posterior cranial fossa.

C9XqpZ0.title: Basilar skull fracture
C9XqpZ0.description: A skull fracture that involves at least one of the bones that make up the skull base. Manifestations include periorbital ecchymosis with CSF rhinorrhea, CSF otorrhea, mastoid ecchymosis, and otorrhagia.

x9XEpZ0.title: Traumatic chiasmal syndrome
x9XEpZ0.description: A condition caused by tearing of the optic chiasm due to frontal and anterior skull base fracture. Manifests with bitemporal hemianopia and scotomata.

B9XzpZ0.title: Gustducin
B9XzpZ0.description: A G protein-coupled receptor expressed taste receptor cells of the tongue. Involved in sensation for bitter, sweet and umami tastes.

y9XdJZ0.title: First-generation H1 receptor antagonist
y9XdJZ0.description: A reversible histamine-1 receptor inhibitor with significant anticholinergic effects. Used to treat allergies and motion sickness. Also has a sedative effect because it can cross the blood-brain barrier.

A9XRJZ0.title: Second-generation H1 receptor antagonist
A9XRJZ0.description: A reversible inhibitor of histamine-1 receptors that has minimal anticholinergic effects and does not cross the blood-brain barrier. Typically used to treat allergies.

_9X5JZ0.title: Fc region
_9X5JZ0.description: An antibody region that contains the constant region of the heavy chain and determines the antibody isotype. Binds complement (for IgG and IgM). Also binds many immunological cells, such as macrophages, to stimulate phagocytic or cytotoxic activity. Contains the carboxy terminal and has many carbohydrate side chains.

z9XrJZ0.title: Cold abscess
z9XrJZ0.description: A non-inflammed abscess, typically associated with Mycobacterium tuberculosis lymphadenitis. Can also occur with staphylococcal infections in patients with hyper-IgE syndrome.

ZCXZqZ0.title: Fab region
ZCXZqZ0.description: A region on an antibody that contains the variable and hypervariable regions. Recognizes and binds to antigens and thus determines the idiotype.

0CXeqZ0.title: Perivascular pseudorosette
0CXeqZ0.description: A histopathologic finding associated with ependymomas. Characterized by tumor cells that are arranged in a papillary structure around a central blood vessel.

destinations.label: Brain tumors → Primary brain tumors according to age

bCXHqZ0.title: Ultraviolet B
bCXHqZ0.description: A type of ultraviolet light of wavelength 280–320 nm. Can cause sunburn and skin aging. Also used in phototherapy (e.g., for psoriasis, vitiligo).

cCXaIZ0.title: Vitamin D 25-hydroxylase
cCXaIZ0.description: A hepatic enzyme that hydroxylates cholecalciferol to produce calcidiol (25-hydroxyvitamin D).

1CX2IZ0.title: Hepatic osteodystrophy
1CX2IZ0.description: A group of metabolic bone diseases (e.g., osteoporosis and osteomalacia) that can develop in patients with chronic liver disease.

WCXPIZ0.title: Clonorchiasis
WCXPIZ0.description: A parasitic infection caused by the trematode Clonorchis sinensis (liver fluke). Mostly asymptomatic. If symptomatic, it can cause cholangitis, cholelithiasis, and nonspecific symptoms (e.g., abdominal pain, diarrhea, fatigue). Associated with an increased risk of developing cholangiocarcinoma.

media.title: Life cycle of Clonorchis sinensis (Chinese liver fluke)

dCXoIZ0.title: Trichuris dysentery syndrome
dCXoIZ0.description: Chronic bloody diarrhea caused by heavy infection with the intestinal nematode Trichuris trichiura.

VCXGIZ0.title: J-chain
VCXGIZ0.description: A small joining polypeptide component of the antibodies IgA and IgM, which is required for polymer formation at the Fc regions via disulfide bridges.

UCXbrZ0.title: Loa Loa filariasis
UCXbrZ0.description: An infection caused by the nematode Loa loa and spread by Chrysops flies (i.e., deer fly, horse fly). Manifests with transient, localized subcutaneous swellings (Calabar swelling) and eye symptoms caused by migration of the worm across the subconjunctivae.

fCXkrZ0.title: Olfactory bulb
fCXkrZ0.description: A structure located on the inferior side of the cerebral hemispheres that processes information received from olfactory neurons and sends axonal projections to the olfactory cortex.

gCXFrZ0.title: Primary olfactory cortex
gCXFrZ0.description: An area of the cerebral cortex that processes the sensation of smell. Receive direct input from the olfactory bulb.

RCXl7Z0.title: Purine
RCXl7Z0.description: A nitrogenous base with a 2-ring structure. Examples include adenine and guanine. Purines are metabolized in the liver to form uric acid.

media.title: Overview of purine and pyrimidine bases

iCXJ7Z0.title: Dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve
iCXJ7Z0.description: A branch of the ulnar nerve that innervates the medial and dorsal aspects of the 4th and 5th digits. Does not pass through the ulnar canal and is thus spared from ulnar nerve compression at the wrist.

QCXu7Z0.title: Internal anal sphincter
QCXu7Z0.description: A sphincter that functions to close the anal canal and anal opening. Responsible for ~ 85% of the resting pressure of the anal canal. Innervated by the enteric nervous system and is under involuntary control.

jCX_7Z0.title: External anal sphincter
jCX_7Z0.description: A sphincter that enables closure of the anal canal and anal opening. Consists of skeletal muscle and is innervated by the pudendal nerve.

PCXWHZ0.title: HLA-DQ8
PCXWHZ0.description: An HLA subtype associated with 5-10% of cases of celiac disease.

4CX3HZ0.title: HLA-DQ2
4CX3HZ0.description: An HLA subtype associated with 90-95% of cases of celiac disease.

kCXmHZ0.title: H+/K+ ATPase
kCXmHZ0.description: A proton pump that uses the energy from ATP hydrolysis to exchange intracellular H⁺ with extracellular K⁺. Located on parietal cells of the stomach and renal tubular cells.

NCX-HZ0.title: Steroid hormones
NCX-HZ0.description: A group of steroids that function as hormones to modulate several physiologic processes, including the immune response, salt and water balance, development of sexual characteristics, and metabolism. Includes corticosteroids of the adrenal cortex (e.g., aldosterone, cortisol) and sex steroids of the gonads (e.g., testosterone, estrogen).

5CXisZ0.title: Posterior cord of the brachial plexus
5CXisZ0.description: A bundle of nerve fibers formed by the posterior divisions of the upper, middle, and lower trunks of the brachial plexus. Gives rise to the axillary nerve, upper subscapular nerve, thoracodorsal nerve, and lower subscapular nerve. Continues into the axillary cavity as the radial nerve.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

MCXMsZ0.title: Lateral cord of the brachial plexus
MCXMsZ0.description: A bundle of nerve fibers formed by the anterior divisions of the upper and middle trunks of the brachial plexus. Gives rise to the lateral pectoral nerve, musculocutaneous nerve, and lateral root of the median nerve.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

nCX7sZ0.title: Medial cord of the brachial plexus
nCX7sZ0.description: A bundle of nerve fibers that arises from the anterior division of the inferior trunk, which originates from the nerve roots C8-T1 of the brachial plexus. Gives rise to the medial pectoral nerve, medial brachial cutaneous nerve, medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, ulnar nerve, and the medial root of the median nerve.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

LCXwsZ0.title: Total claw hand
LCXwsZ0.description: A condition caused by paralysis of the lumbricals (e.g., due to combined median and ulnar nerve injury or injury to the C8 and T1 nerve roots). Manifests with persistent flexion of the interphalangeal joints and extension of the metacarpophalangeal joints in the hand.

destinations.label: Peripheral nerve injuries → Nerve injuries in the upper body

oCX0GZ0.title: Lower trunk of the brachial plexus
oCX0GZ0.description: A bundle of nerve fibers formed from the anterior rami of the spinal segments C8 and T1. It ends by dividing into an anterior and posterior division and contributes motor and sensory innervation to the ulnar nerve. Injury to the lower trunk of the brachial plexus causes Klumpke palsy.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

KCXUGZ0.title: Upper trunk of the brachial plexus
KCXUGZ0.description: A bundle of nerve fibers formed from the anterior rami of the spinal segments C5 and C6. Gives rise to the suprascapular nerve and the nerve to subclavius, then divides into an anterior and posterior division, from which it contributes to the axillary and musculocutaneous nerves. Injury to the upper trunk of the brachial plexus causes Erb palsy.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

6CXjGZ0.title: Pyrimidine
6CXjGZ0.description: A nitrogenous base with a 1-ring structure. Examples include cytosine, thymine, and uracil.

media.title: Overview of purine and pyrimidine bases

pCXLGZ0.title: Jod-Basedow phenomenon
pCXLGZ0.description: A condition of thyrotoxicosis that develops in iodine-deficient individuals with thyroid abnormalities after administration of iodine (e.g., from contrast, amiodarone, or supplements).

JCXsGZ0.title: Postadrenalectomy syndrome
JCXsGZ0.description: The development of a pituitary tumor following bilateral adrenalectomy for refractory Cushing syndrome. The tumor compresses the optic chiasm, which can cause visual field defects and headaches, and secretes ACTH and melanocyte-stimulating hormone, which results in cutaneous hyperpigmentation.

tCXXFZ0.title: Pancreatic enzymes
tCXXFZ0.description: A group of enzymes produced by the pancreatic acinar cells to aid in digestion. Initially secreted as inactive zymogens. Once present in the small bowel, these zymogens become activated and perform their digestive functions. Examples include trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, pancreatic lipase, amylase, and phospholipase.

FCXgFZ0.title: Malaise
FCXgFZ0.description: A general feeling of discomfort, illness, or uneasiness.

uCXpFZ0.title: Gluteus minimus muscle
uCXpFZ0.description: A hip muscle that originates from the posterior surface of the ilium and inserts onto the greater trochanter of the femur. Innervated by the superior gluteal nerve and supplied by the superior gluteal artery. Abducts and internally rotates the thigh.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region

media.title: Superficial and deep muscles of the gluteal region

ECX8FZ0.title: Thymic medulla
ECX8FZ0.description: The pale central region of the thymus that predominantly consists of thymic epithelial cells and immature T cells. Site of negative selection of self-reactive T cells.

vCXAFZ0.title: Autoimmune regulator
vCXAFZ0.description: A transcription factor encoded by a gene on chromosome 21 that regulates the expression of autoantigens. Facilitates the elimination of self-reactive T cells. Dysfunction of AIRE is associated with chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital T-cell immunodeficiencies

DCX18Z0.title: Tissue-restricted antigen
DCX18Z0.description: An antigen that is expressed in a specific type of tissue or organ. The epithelial cells of the medullary thymus can express all the different tissue-restricted antigens found in the body by a process called promiscuous gene expression.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

wCXh8Z0.title: Thymocyte
wCXh8Z0.description: A T cell progenitor derived from hematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow. Primarily found in the thymic cortex.

9CXN8Z0.title: Lymph node medullary sinus
9CXN8Z0.description: The region of the lymph node medulla that communicates with the efferent lymphatics. Contains macrophages and dendritic cells.

CCXq8Z0.title: Splenic marginal zone
CCXq8Z0.description: A region in the spleen between the red pulp and lymphoid follicle of the white pulp. Contains macrophages, dendritic cells, and B cells, which function as antigen-presenting cells.

xCXE8Z0.title: Splenic follicle
xCXE8Z0.description: A region of the splenic white pulp located between the periarteriolar lymphatic sheath and marginal zone. Predominantly contains B lymphocytes, which multiply and divide there.

BCXz8Z0.title: Thymic cortex
BCXz8Z0.description: The dense peripheral region of the thymus that contains thymocytes and immature T cells. Site of positive selection of T cells.

_CX5uZ0.title: Pulmonary cryptococcosis
_CX5uZ0.description: A pulmonary fungal infection caused by Cryptococcus gattii and Cryptococcus neoformans. Most commonly seen in immunocompromised patients. Clinical presentation is variable and nonspecific (e.g., cough, fever, shortness of breath).

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Opportunistic fungal infections

zCXruZ0.title: Branchial cleft sinus
zCXruZ0.description: A lateral neck sinus caused by incomplete obliteration of the branchial clefts between branchial arches. The most common site of the branchial cleft sinus is the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid (due to incomplete obliteration of the second branchial cleft).

-CXDuZ0.title: First branchial pouch
-CXDuZ0.description: The internal endodermal pouch between the first and second branchial arches. It gives rise to the middle ear cavity, eustachian tube, and mastoid air cells.

ZxXZEZ0.title: First branchial cleft
ZxXZEZ0.description: The ectodermal groove between the first and second branchial arches. Develops into the external auditory canal.

0xXeEZ0.title: Third branchial pouch
0xXeEZ0.description: The endodermal pouch between the third and fourth branchial arches. The ventral portion of the third branchial pouch gives rise to the thymus and the dorsal portion gives rise to the inferior parathyroid glands.

axXQEZ0.title: Fourth branchial pouch
axXQEZ0.description: The endodermal pouch between the fourth and sixth branchial arches. The ventral portion of the fourth branchial pouch gives rise to the ultimobranchial body (which develops into the parafollicular cells of the thyroid gland) and the dorsal portion gives rise to the superior parathyroid glands.

YxXnEZ0.title: Xanthosine monophosphate
YxXnEZ0.description: A purine nucleotide with a xanthine base that serves as an intermediate in purine metabolism (e.g., GMP synthesis).

cxXavZ0.title: Nonstructural protein 5B
cxXavZ0.description: A RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase coded for by the genome of the hepatitis C virus. The drug sofosbuvir targets this enzyme.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

1xX2vZ0.title: RNA-dependent RNA polymerase
1xX2vZ0.description: An enzyme that synthesizes an RNA strand on an RNA template. This enzyme is essential for the replication of RNA viruses. RNA viruses with a positive-sense RNA can use the host cell's protein translation machinery to synthesize RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. RNA viruses with a negative-sense RNA must bring their own RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase into the cell. This enzyme is not required for replication of viruses or cells with a DNA genome.

exXxvZ0.title: Action potential
exXxvZ0.description: A sequence of electrical changes that occurs on an excitable cell membrane (e.g., neurons, myocytes) that results in a rapid rise (depolarization) followed by a fall (repolarization) in the membrane potential. Different cell types generate different action potentials, depending on the types of voltage-gated ion channels in their cell membranes.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Action potential

UxXbDZ0.title: Resting potential
UxXbDZ0.description: The voltage difference across an excitable cell membrane in the resting phase. Normally ranges from -70 mV (in neuronal cells) to -90 mV (in skeletal and cardiac muscle cells). Primarily determined by the equilibrium potential of K+ ions and to a lesser extent by the equilibrium potentials of other ions.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Resting potential

media.title: Action potential and ion flux in myocardial contractile cells

fxXkDZ0.title: Pendrin
fxXkDZ0.description: A membrane protein that functions as a sodium-independent chloride anion exchanger. In the kidneys (distal convoluted tubule, connecting tubule, and cortical collecting duct), it functions as a chloride-bicarbonate and plays an important role in acid-base homeostasis. In the inner ear, it helps maintain appropriate endolymph composition. In the thyroid, it transports iodide into the follicle lumen in exchange for chloride. Biallelic mutation of the pendrin gene causes Pendred syndrome.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Function

TxX6DZ0.title: Hip bones
TxX6DZ0.description: A pair of composite bone structures, each composed of three fused bones: ilium, ischium, and pubis. Part of the pelvic girdle.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

gxXFDZ0.title: Ilium
gxXFDZ0.description: The largest component of the hip bone. Forms the iliac crest and the superior part of the acetabulum.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

SxXyDZ0.title: Ischium
SxXyDZ0.description: The posterior and inferior component of the hip bone. Forms the inferoposterior part of the acetabulum.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

3xXSwZ0.title: Pelvic inlet
3xXSwZ0.description: A plane that separates the abdominal and pelvic cavities. Bounded posteriorly by the sacral promontory, anteriorly by the pubic symphysis, and laterally by the bony rim of the pelvis.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

media.title: Plane of the pelvic inlet: diameter

RxXlwZ0.title: Pelvic outlet
RxXlwZ0.description: The inferior opening of the pelvis. Bounded by the sacrum and coccyx posteriorly, the ischial tuberosities laterally, and the pubic symphysis anteriorly.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

ixXJwZ0.title: Lumbosacral joint
ixXJwZ0.description: An intervertebral joint with two facet joints located between the last lumbar vertebra (L5) and the sacral promontory. Stabilized by iliolumbar ligaments.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

QxXuwZ0.title: Sacrococcygeal joint
QxXuwZ0.description: A cartilaginous joint between the sacrum and coccyx that is stabilized by the sacrococcygeal ligaments.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

jxX_wZ0.title: Deep transverse perineal muscle
jxX_wZ0.description: A muscle that is part of the deep perineal pouch, originating from the inferior rami of the ischium. Acts to stabilize the perineal body and consequently the entire pelvic floor.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

PxXW9Z0.title: External urethral sphincter
PxXW9Z0.description: A group of skeletal muscles that allow voluntary control over urinary-flow inhibition. The male external urethral sphincter surrounds the membranous urethra, while the female external urethral sphincter is comprised of three distinct muscles (urethrovaginal muscle, compressor urethrae, and sphincter urethrae) working in unison.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

4xX39Z0.title: Perineal membrane
4xX39Z0.description: A triangularly-shaped sheet of dense fibrous tissue located inferiorly to the deep transverse perineal muscle. Provides attachment to the muscles of the external genitalia and allows passage of the urethra and vagina.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

lxXv9Z0.title: Superficial perineal layer
lxXv9Z0.description: The outermost layer of the pelvic floor. Consists of the ischiocavernosus muscle, the bulbocavernosus muscle (bulbospongiosus muscle in male individuals), the external anal sphincter, and the superficial transverse perineal muscle.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

mxXVCZ0.title: Transthyretin
mxXVCZ0.description: A transport protein synthesized by the liver that carries thyroxine and the retinol-RBP complex. Decreased serum levels may indicate the presence of malnutrition. Abnormally configured protein fibrils of transthyretin may result in the accumulation of amyloid in various tissues. Conditions that result in the accumulation of transthyretin include wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis, familial amyloid polyneuropathy, and familial amyloid cardiomyopathy.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Function

nxX7CZ0.title: Francisella tularensis
nxX7CZ0.description: A facultative intracellular coccobacillus that causes tularemia. Transmitted by ticks, rabbits, and deer flies.

oxX0xZ0.title: Heme moiety
oxX0xZ0.description: An iron-containing compound found in many proteins (i.e., hemoproteins) such as hemoglobin, myoglobin, and cytochromes.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

pxXLxZ0.title: Middle colic artery
pxXLxZ0.description: A branch of the superior mesenteric artery that divides into right and left branches. The right branch supplies the right portion of the transverse colon and anastomoses with the right colic artery at the hepatic flexure. The left branch supplies the left portion of the transverse colon and anastomoses with the left colic artery at the splenic flexure.

media.title: Arterial blood supply of the colon

JxXsxZ0.title: Southwestern blot
JxXsxZ0.description: A form of gel electrophoresis that is used to detect specific DNA-binding proteins (e.g., transcription factors) using oligonucleotide probes.

qxXCxZ0.title: Thin layer chromatography
qxXCxZ0.description: A laboratory technique that analyzes a mixture by separating it into its components. Can be used to detect specific drugs and/or metabolites.

IxXYBZ0.title: Chondrocalcinosis
IxXYBZ0.description: Calcium deposition in cartilage identified on imaging, typically in calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease (pseudogout). Can also occur secondary to joint injury/surgery or metabolic conditions (e.g., hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, hemochromatosis), as well as in advanced age.

7xX4BZ0.title: Overriding aorta
7xX4BZ0.description: A congenital anomaly associated with tetralogy of Fallot in which the aorta is displaced over the ventricular septal defect (instead of the left ventricle). Causes blood from both ventricles to flow into the aorta.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Tetralogy of Fallot

HxXKBZ0.title: Transtheoretical model
HxXKBZ0.description: A biopsychosocial model that focuses on intentional behavior change of the individual. Stages include precontemplation, contemplation, preparation, action, and maintenance.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

FxXgyZ0.title: Urogenital diaphragm
FxXgyZ0.description: The middle layer of the pelvic floor, which spans between the ischial and pubic rami. Consists of the deep transverse perineal muscle and the urethral sphincter, which are enclosed by the superior and inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

uxXpyZ0.title: Anterior sacroiliac ligament
uxXpyZ0.description: An anterior attachment between the ilium and the sacrum composed of multiple thin strands. Forms a broad band that supports the sacroiliac joint and makes up the anterior-inferior portion of the joint capsule.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

ExX8yZ0.title: Posterior sacroiliac ligament
ExX8yZ0.description: A thick ligament composed of three distinct bands that form a posterior attachment between the ilium and the sacrum. Supports the sacroiliac joint.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

vxXAyZ0.title: Sacrospinous ligament
vxXAyZ0.description: A thin, triangular ligament located between the sacrum and the ischial spine. Supports and immobilizes the sacrum during weight transfer from the vertebral column. Thought to be a fibrous part of the coccygeus muscle.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

media.title: Muscles and ligaments of the pelvis

DxX1AZ0.title: Sacrotuberous ligament
DxX1AZ0.description: A triangular posterior attachment between the sacrum and the ischial tuberosity. Supports and immobilizes the sacrum during weight transfer from the vertebral column.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

9xXNAZ0.title: Greater sciatic foramen
9xXNAZ0.description: A foramen in the posterior part of pelvis that is bounded anterolaterally by the greater sciatic notch of the ilium, posteromedially by the sacrotuberous ligament, inferiorly by the sacrospinous ligament and superiorly by the sacroiliac ligament. Contains the piriformis muscle, internal pudendal vessels, superior and inferior gluteal vessels, superior and inferior gluteal nerves, pudendal nerve, sciatic nerve, posterior femoral cutaneous nerve, the nerve to obturator internus, and the nerve to quadratus femoris.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

CxXqAZ0.title: Lesser sciatic foramen
CxXqAZ0.description: A foramen in the posterior part of pelvis. Bounded superiorly by the sacrospinous ligament and the ischial spine, anteriorly by the ischial tuberosity, and posteriorly by the sacrotuberous ligament. Contains the internal vessels, the pudendal nerve, the tendon of the obturator internus muscle, and the nerve to the obturator internus muscle.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

xxXEAZ0.title: Pararectal fossa
xxXEAZ0.description: The anatomic space formed by folds of peritoneum surrounding the intraperitoneal part of the rectum. Laterally continuous with the rectovesical pouch in male individuals and the rectouterine pouch in female individuals.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic cavity and pelvic spaces

BxXzAZ0.title: Ischiorectal fossa
BxXzAZ0.description: The fat-filled spaces surrounding the anal canal that facilitate expansion of the anal canal during defecation. The lateral walls of the ischiorectal fossae contain the pudendal nerve within each side of the Alcock canal.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic cavity and pelvic spaces

yxXd_Z0.title: Retropubic space
yxXd_Z0.description: An extraperitoneal anatomic space located between the pubic symphysis and the anterior surface of the bladder.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic cavity and pelvic spaces

AxXR_Z0.title: Stool osmotic gap
AxXR_Z0.description: A calculation used to identify if watery diarrhea has an osmotic or secretory etiology. Calculated with the equation: 290 - [2x (stool sodium + stool potassium)], with 290 mOsm representing stool osmolarity. A low stool osmotic gap (< 50) is suggestive of secretory diarrhea; a high gap (> 100) is suggestive of osmotic diarrhea.

_xX5_Z0.title: Almotriptan
_xX5_Z0.description: A 5-HT receptor agonist that vasoconstricts cranial arteries. Used for acute treatment of migraine and cluster headaches. Can cause a transient increase in blood pressure.

zxXr_Z0.title: Pectineal ligament
zxXr_Z0.description: A tendinous band that is an inferolateral extension of the lacunar ligament. Attaches to the superior ramus of the pubic ramus medially and runs along the pectineal line of the ilium.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Femoral triangle and fasial compartments of the thigh

-xXD_Z0.title: Cervical plexus
-xXD_Z0.description: A nerve plexus composed of the anterior rami of the cervical nerve roots, which provides motor and sensory innervation to most neck muscles and the area over the anterior and lateral neck.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

ZBXZzZ0.title: Vasa nervorum
ZBXZzZ0.description: The small, intraneural vessels that supply blood to peripheral nerves. Susceptible to compression injury.

0BXezZ0.title: First-order oculosympathetic neuron
0BXezZ0.description: A neuron that arises from the hypothalamus and synapses at the ciliospinal center of Budge in the intermediolateral gray column of the spinal cord at C8–T2.

YBXnzZ0.title: Estrone
YBXnzZ0.description: An estrogenic hormone secreted by the ovaries, placenta, and adipose tissue. Converted from androstenedione directly by aromatase or from testosterone via estradiol. Less potent than estradiol but more potent than estriol.

1BX2-Z0.title: Third-order oculosympathetic neuron
1BX2-Z0.description: A postganglionic, sympathetic neuron that originates in the superior cervical ganglion and travels through the adventitia of the internal carotid artery and the cavernous sinus in close proximity to the 6th cranial nerve before reaching target tissues.

UBXbZ00.title: Positive cooperativity
UBXbZ00.description: A phenomenon in which the binding of a ligand to a protein with multiple binding sites increases the binding of additional ligands to the same protein. Examples include the binding of oxygen to hemoglobin (which increases the affinity of hemoglobin for additional oxygen molecules) and the binding of fructose-2,6-bisphosphate to phosphofructokinase-1 (which increases the affinity of phosphofructokinase-1 for fructose-6-phosphate).

2BXTZ00.title: Second-order oculosympathetic neuron
2BXTZ00.description: A preganglionic, sympathetic neuron that originates from the ciliospinal center of Budge and Waller and passes through the apex of the lung and stellate ganglion to synapse in the superior cervical ganglion.

TBX6Z00.title: CAD enzyme
TBX6Z00.description: A trifunctional, cytosolic enzyme that facilitates de novo synthesis of pyrimidine nucleotides. Includes glutamine-dependent carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 2 (CPS2), aspartate carbamoyltransferase, and dihydroorotase.

SBXyZ00.title: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 2
SBXyZ00.description: A cytosolic enzyme and the rate-limiting enzyme of de novo pyrimidine synthesis. Uses ATP, glutamine, and CO2 to form carbamoyl phosphate.

jBX_000.title: Nonmegaloblastic anemia
jBX_000.description: A type of macrocytic anemia in which DNA synthesis occurs normally, in contrast to megaloblastic anemia. Peripheral blood smear is characterized by large red blood cells (macrocytes) without hypersegmented neutrophils. Etiologies include liver disorders, alcohol use disorder, hypothyroidism, and myelodysplastic syndrome.

PBXWa00.title: Volumetric macrocyte
PBXWa00.description: A type of macrocyte with increased mean corpuscular volume and normal cell diameter. Contain an increased quantity of hemoglobin. Can be induced by chronic hydroxyurea therapy.

4BX3a00.title: Megaloblast
4BX3a00.description: An abnormal, large, nucleated red blood cell precursor, characteristic of vitamin B₁₂ deficiency and folate deficiency. Either destroyed in the bone marrow or released into the circulation as a macrocyte.

lBXva00.title: Monoclonal antibody
lBXva00.description: A drug that consists of immunoglobulins that bind to a single, specific antigen. Used to treat many different conditions. Examples include alemtuzumab, an anti-CD52 antibody used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia, and abciximab, an anti-glycoprotein IIb/IIIa antibody used to inhibit platelet function.

LBXwY00.title: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma
LBXwY00.description: The most common histologic variant of renal cell carcinoma. Characterized by polygonal cells with clear, glycogen and/or lipid-filled cytoplasm. Typically originates from the proximal convoluted tubule. Most cases are sporadic, but inherited cases can be associated with Von Hippel-Lindau disease.

KBXUb00.title: Thymidylate synthase
KBXUb00.description: An enzyme involved in pyrimidine synthesis. Catalyzes the methylation of dUMP to dTMP, which requires 5,10-methylene-tetrahydrofolate (5,10-methylene-THF) as a cofactor. Targeted by some chemotherapeutic agents, such as 5-fluorouracil (5-FU).

6BXjb00.title: Troisier's sign
6BXjb00.description: The finding of an enlarged, hard left supraclavicular node (Virchow node) as the result of abdominal carcinoma metastasis.

pBXLb00.title: Negative selection of T-cells
pBXLb00.description: A process of T cell selection that takes place in the thymic medulla. Tests if T cells can bind to self-antigens presented on MHC. T cells that do not bind receive a survival signal; dysfunctional T cells undergo apoptosis. Ensures that the thymus does not produce self-reacting T-cells.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

JBXsb00.title: Positive selection of T-cells
JBXsb00.description: A process of T cell selection that takes place in the thymic cortex. Selects for T cells that express T-cell receptors that can bind MHC appropriately (i.e., not too strongly or too weakly).

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

qBXCb00.title: Spectrin
qBXCb00.description: A plasma membrane protein that maintains plasma membrane integrity and stabilizes the cytoskeletal structure. Defective spectrin in erythrocyte membranes is the most common cause of hereditary spherocytosis.

IBXYX00.title: Pterion
IBXYX00.description: A region of the lateral skull where the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones join. One of the weakest parts of the skull. Lies over the anterior division of the middle meningeal artery; fracture that involves the pterion can rupture this vessel and cause an epidural hematoma.

rBXfX00.title: Pineal gland
rBXfX00.description: A gland located along the midline on the dorsal surface of the midbrain. Secretes melatonin and plays a role in the control of circadian rhythm.

7BX4X00.title: Transpulmonary pressure
7BX4X00.description: The difference between the alveolar pressure and the pleural pressure. The transpulmonary pressure helps to keep the lungs expanded. This pressure falls to zero in pneumothorax.

HBXKX00.title: Arginase deficiency
HBXKX00.description: An inherited urea cycle disorder that leads to mild, episodic hyperammonemia. Typically manifests in toddlers and causes spasticity and failure to meet developmental milestones.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Urea cycle disorders

sBXtX00.title: Pelvic floor
sBXtX00.description: A complex fibromuscular structure bounded by the pelvic outlet that maintains the pelvic organs in place. Separates the perineum from the pelvic cavity and is divided into two openings: the urogenital and rectal hiatus. Stabilized by the perineal body (central tendon of the perineum). Plays an integral role in urinary continence and defecation.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

GBXBX00.title: Internal iliac artery
GBXBX00.description: An artery that originates from the common iliac artery at the sacroiliac joint and descends inferiorly into the pelvis, where it divides into an anterior and posterior trunk at the superior border of the greater sciatic foramen. Supplies the pelvic organs and walls, the gluteal region, and the peritoneum.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

media.title: Pelvis with blood supply of the anal canal

tBXXc00.title: Ovarian artery
tBXXc00.description: A paired artery that supplies the ovaries and lateral third of the fallopian tube. Arises from the aorta inferior to the renal arteries (near L2). Forms an anastomosis with the ovarian branch of the uterine artery.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

media.title: Blood supply of the female reproductive organs (dorsal view)

FBXgc00.title: Coccygeus muscle
FBXgc00.description: A muscle running from the ischial spine to the lower sacrum and coccyx. Functions to support and raise the pelvic floor.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

uBXpc00.title: Iliofemoral ligament
uBXpc00.description: A Y-shaped ligament that runs from the anterior inferior iliac spine and the acetabular rim to the intertrochanteric line and the greater trochanter. It is the strongest ligament in the human body and reinforces the fibrous capsule of the hip joint anteriorly. In a standing position, the iliolumbar ligament prevents excessive lateral rotation and hyperextension of the hip.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Hip joint

EBX8c00.title: Ischiofemoral ligament
EBX8c00.description: A ligament of the hip joint that runs from the ischial region of the acetabulum to the neck of the femur. Reinforces the fibrous capsule anteriorly and limits medial rotation and extension of the thigh.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Hip joint

vBXAc00.title: Pubofemoral ligament
vBXAc00.description: A ligament of the hip joint that runs from the pubic part of the acetabular rim and the superior pubic ramus to the femoral neck. Reinforces the fibrous capsule inferiorly and limits abduction and extension of the hip joint.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Hip joint

DBX1100.title: Transverse acetabular ligament
DBX1100.description: A fibrous structure on the lower part of the acetabulum that converts the acetabular notch into a foramen. Allows passage of vessels and nerves into the joint space.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Hip joint

wBXh100.title: Round ligament of the head of femur
wBXh100.description: A ligament of the hip joint that originates within the acetabular fossa and attaches to the fovea capitis femoris. Forms a pathway for the foveolar artery to the head of the femur.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Hip joint

9BXN100.title: Ski boot compression syndrome
9BXN100.description: A condition caused by compression of the extensor tendons and deep peroneal nerve at the anterior ankle by the tongue of a ski boot or other ill-fitting shoes, which results in synovitis and neuritis. Can mimic anterior compartment syndrome.

CBXq100.title: Microembolization
CBXq100.description: The occlusion of an arteriole or terminal part of an artery by a small embolus (e.g. inflamed atherosclerotic plaques). Can cause physical obstruction, vasoconstriction, inflammation, and/or microinfarction.

xBXE100.title: Atherothrombosis
xBXE100.description: The formation of blood clots within an artery as a result of atherosclerosis. Can cause coronary artery disease, stroke, transient ischemic attack, and/or peripheral arterial disease.

BBXz100.title: Cardiac embolism
BBXz100.description: An embolus that arises from an intracardiac origin (e.g., the chambers of the heart, endocardial surfaces). Can cause organ infarction (e.g., stroke, renal infarct, splenic infarct) and acute limb ischemia.

yBXdW00.title: Obturator foramen
yBXdW00.description: An opening formed by the ischium and pubis bones of the pelvis. Conatins the obturator canal, which serves as the passage for the obturator artery, vein, and nerve.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

ABXRW00.title: Pudendal canal
ABXRW00.description: A sheath of fascia located in the inferolateral wall of the ischiorectal fossa that conveys the pudendal nerve and internal pudendal artery and vein.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

_BX5W00.title: Vascular lacuna
_BX5W00.description: The medial space in the upper thigh, inferior the inguinal ligament, through which the femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve, the femoral artery, and the femoral vein pass. Contains the node of Cloquet and other lymph nodes.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

media.title: Contents and borders of the muscular lacuna and vascular lacuna
Boundaries of the muscular lacuna and vascular lacuna

zBXrW00.title: Muscular lacuna
zBXrW00.description: The lateral space in the upper thigh, inferior to the inguinal ligament, through which the iliopsoas muscle, lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh, and femoral nerve pass.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

media.title: Contents and borders of the muscular lacuna and vascular lacuna
Boundaries of the muscular lacuna and vascular lacuna

ZyXZd00.title: Pelvis
ZyXZd00.description: A ring-like structure of the axial skeleton that connects the vertebral column with the lower extremities. Formed by the hip bones (ilium, ischium, pubis), sacrum, and coccyx. Largely immobile, in contrast to the pectoral girdle, and thus provides stability and proper transfer of weight from the vertebral column to the lower extremities in the upright position.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

YyXnd00.title: Pseudohypha
YyXnd00.description: A hypha-like filament formed by a chain of budding yeast cells that have not become detached from each other. Pseudohypha can be distinguished from true septate hyphae by the presence of constrictions at the site of septae.

byXHd00.title: Macroconidium
byXHd00.description: A large asexual fungal spore formed from a vegetative yeast, hyphal cell, or a specialized conidiogenous cell.

XyX9d00.title: 4th ventricle
XyX9d00.description: A CSF-filled, diamond-shaped sac located in the pons or upper medulla. Receives CSF inflow from the aqueduct of Sylvius. CSF flows out through the lateral paired foramen of Luschka, medial foramen of Magendie, and inferiorly into the central canal.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

cyXaV00.title: Microconidium
cyXaV00.description: A small asexual fungal spore formed from a vegetative yeast, hyphal cell, or a specialized conidiogenous cell.

1yX2V00.title: Conidium
1yX2V00.description: An asexual fungal spore formed from a vegetative yeast, hyphal cell, or a specialized conidiogenous cell.

WyXPV00.title: Dimorphic fungus
WyXPV00.description: A fungus that has both a hyphal (mold) form at colder temperatures and a yeast or spherule form at warmer temperatures. Examples include Blastomyces dermatitidis, Candida albicans, Histoplasma capsulatum, Sporothrix schenckii, and Coccidioides immitis.

dyXoV00.title: Actin rockets
dyXoV00.description: A rapid polymerization of actin that facilitates movement of Listeria monocytogenes between host cells without leaving the intracellular space, which allows bacteria to avoid extracellular antibodies.

UyXbe00.title: Emissary veins
UyXbe00.description: A collection of valveless veins that connect the intracranial dural venous sinuses with the extracranial venous system. Since blood may flow in either direction, they contribute to the regulation of intracranial venous pressure. Can also carry extracranial infections into the brain to cause septic thrombi, meningitis and/or brain abscesses.

TyX6e00.title: Dedifferentiation
TyX6e00.description: The regression of a cell from a specialized to an unspecialized form.

gyXFe00.title: Sodium–hydrogen antiporter 3
gyXFe00.description: A transport protein found on the apical surfaces of proximal convoluted tubule cells and intestinal epithelial cells as well as the basolateral surfaces of duodenal and pancreatic cells. Moves sodium into cells in exchange for hydrogen.

3yXSU00.title: Idarucizumab
3yXSU00.description: A monoclonal antibody that is used to reverse the effects of the anticoagulant dabigatran.

jyX_U00.title: Direct thrombin inhibitor
jyX_U00.description: An anticoagulant that directly inhibits thrombin (factor IIa). Examples include bivalirudin, argatroban, and desirudin.

media.title: Mechanism of action: anticoagulants that prevent secondary hemostasis

PyXW200.title: Bivalirudin
PyXW200.description: A parenterally administered and reversible direct thrombin inhibitor that prevents cleavage of fibrinogen to fibrin by thrombin.

4yX3200.title: Streptokinase
4yX3200.description: A protein produced by group A streptococci. It catalyzes the conversion of plasminogen to plasmin, which is responsible for clot breakdown. Streptokinase can be used as a thrombolytic in patients with acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, or ischemic stroke.

kyXm200.title: Phosphodiesterase type 3
kyXm200.description: A phosphodiesterase isoform that is found in vascular smooth muscle, platelets, oocytes, spermatocytes, and adipocytes. It hydrolyzes both cGMP and cAMP.

OyXI200.title: Bacitracin
OyXI200.description: An antibiotic that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by preventing the transfer of peptides into the cell wall. Primarily used in topical formulation. Used in bacterial cultures to differentiate Streptococcus agalactiae (which is resistant to bacitracin) from Streptococcus pyogenes.

lyXv200.title: Novobiocin
lyXv200.description: An antibiotic that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase in gram-positive bacteria and some gram-negative bacteria. Among gram-positive cocci, S. saprophyticus is intrinsically resistant to novobiocin. This property is used in bacterial cultures to differentiate Staphylococcus saprophyticus from other species of Staphylococcus.

NyX-200.title: Pyrrolidonyl arylamidase test
NyX-200.description: A test used to detect pyrrolidonyl arylamidase (pyrrolidonyl aminopeptidase), an enzyme produced by certain bacteria such as Enterococcus spp. and Streptococcus pyogenes.

myXVf00.title: Hippurate test
myXVf00.description: A microbiological test used for presumptive identification of group B streptococci, Gardnerella vaginalis, Listeria monocytogenes, Campylobacter jejuni, and Listeria monocytogenes.

MyXMf00.title: Lamellar bone
MyXMf00.description: A mature bone formed by the remodeling of woven bone into strong, organized sheets of collagen.

nyX7f00.title: Gallbladder dysmotility
nyX7f00.description:
Delayed gallbladder emptying that can be caused by biliary sludging, autonomic neuropathy, obesity and insulin resistance or hypertriglyceridemia. Gallbladder dysmotility usually predisposes to cholesterol gallstone formation.

A condition of delayed gallbladder emptying, which predisposes to cholesterol gallstone formation. Etiologies include biliary sludging, autonomic neuropathy, obesity, insulin resistance, and hypertriglyceridemia

LyXwf00.title: Parathyroidectomy
LyXwf00.description: The surgical removal of one or more parathyroid glands. Typically performed to treat primary hyperparathyroidism.

oyX0T00.title: Intra-alveolar pressure
oyX0T00.description: The air pressure within the alveoli of the lung. During inspiration, the lung volume and the volume of alveoli increase. This decreases the intra-alveolar pressure to a sub-atmospheric value (about -1 cmH2O). At the end of inspiration, the intra-alveolar pressure reaches an atmospheric pressure value again (0 cmH2O).

KyXUT00.title: Familial dysbetalipoproteinemia
KyXUT00.description: An autosomal-recessive, inherited hyperlipoproteinemia caused by a mutation in the ApoE gene, which encodes apolipoprotein E. Results in increased levels of triglyceride-rich lipoprotein remnants in the serum. Usually asymptomatic until symptoms of atherosclerosis develop. Patients can develop xanthomas.

6yXjT00.title: Familial hyperchylomicronemia
6yXjT00.description: An autosomal-recessive condition caused by a deficiency of lipoprotein lipase (type 1A) or apolipoprotein C-II (type 1B). Manifests with elevated serum concentrations of triglycerides, chylomicrons, and VLDL. Not associated with increased risk of atherosclerosis.

pyXLT00.title: Type IV hyperlipoproteinemia
pyXLT00.description: An autosomal-dominant lipid disorder characterized by elevated triglyceride and VLDL levels.

JyXsT00.title: Apolipoprotein C-II
JyXsT00.description: An apolipoprotein that serves as a cofactor for lipoprotein lipase. Found in chylomicrons, VLDL, and HDL.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

qyXCT00.title: Apolipoprotein B-48
qyXCT00.description: An apolipoprotein that mediates the secretion of chylomicron particles that originate from the intestine into the lymphatics.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

IyXYg00.title: Apolipoprotein A-1
IyXYg00.description: A protein that forms a large component of HDL cholesterol. Enables efflux of fat molecules from cells to tissues. Also acts as a cofactor for lecithin cholesterolacyltransferase (LCAT).

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

7yX4g00.title: Mixed hearing loss
7yX4g00.description: A combination of conductive and sensorineural hearing loss.

GyXBg00.title: End artery
GyXBg00.description: An artery that is the only source of oxygenated blood to a particular region (i.e., it does not have effective anastomoses).

tyXXS00.title: Mevalonate
tyXXS00.description: A vital substrate in cholesterol synthesis. HMG-CoA reductase and NADPH are required for the conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate during cholesterol synthesis. Given the fundamental role cholesterol synthesis plays in cell survival, the mevalonate pathway is a major target of many anti-cancer regimens. Most HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors have a similar structure to mevalonate.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Cholesterol metabolism

8yXOS00.title: Embolus
8yXOS00.description: A circulating piece of material in the bloodstream, e.g., a detached blood clot, fat tissue, clumps of bacteria, a foreign object, or an air bubble, which is capable of obstructing or blocking a blood vessel and thus causing infarction.

uyXpS00.title: Type II hyperlipoproteinemia
uyXpS00.description: An autosomal-dominant inherited group of diseases characterized by defects in LDL receptors. Manifests with increased serum concentrations of LDL-C and early development of atherosclerosis.

EyX8S00.title: Familial hypoalphalipoproteinemia
EyX8S00.description: An autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations in the gene that encodes apolipoprotein A-1. Characterized by low levels of HDL cholesterol. Associated with premature coronary heart disease and stroke.

-yXD300.title: Toxic keratoconjunctivitis
-yXD300.description: A noninfectious, nonallergic conjunctivitis that develops in response to irritants in the environment (e.g., air pollution, chemicals) or medications. May result in corneal damage in patients with long-term exposure to an offending agent.

bAXHR00.title: Cholesterol synthesis
bAXHR00.description: A multi-step biochemical pathway in which cholesterol is synthesized from acetyl CoA. Intermediate molecules in their sequential order of production include acetoacetyl CoA, HMG CoA, mevalonate, isopentenyl pyrophosphate, farnesyl pyrophosphate, squalene, and lanosterol. Takes place in the cytosol, peroxisomes, and smooth endoplasmic reticulum of cells, primarily in the liver, intestines, adrenal gland, and reproductive organs. Regulated by sterol regulatory element-binding protein.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Cholesterol metabolism

cAXai00.title: Lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase
cAXai00.description: An enzyme synthesized by the liver that reversibly binds mainly to HDL particles. Catalyzes the esterification of free cholesterol on the surface of HDL, contributing to its maturation.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

1AX2i00.title: Pancreatic lipase
1AX2i00.description: A pancreatic enzyme that facilitates the breakdown of dietary fats. Normal range: 3–43 U/L. Increased serum levels are associated with acute pancreatitis and renal failure. Decreased serum levels are associated with limited exocrine pancreatic function (e.g., from cystic fibrosis, chronic pancreatitis).

WAXPi00.title: Brown recluse spider
WAXPi00.description: A spider that produces a venom that results in an erythematous, vesiculating lesion that can become necrotic. Rarely results in systemic symptoms or life-threatening complications (e.g., angioedema, acute hemolytic anemia).

dAXoi00.title: Hot tub folliculitis
dAXoi00.description: A type of folliculitis that is most commonly caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa and typically develops 8–48 hours after exposure to contaminated water (e.g., swimming, hot tub). The eruption most commonly occurs on the buttocks and trunk, following the distribution of the bathing suit.

destinations.label: Skin and soft tissue infections → Purulent SSTIs

eAXxi00.title: Choreoathetoid movement
eAXxi00.description: A combination of quick, involuntary movements of the hands and feet (chorea) with slower, writhing movements (athetosis). Etiologies include Huntington disease, Sydenham chorea, and drug adverse effects (e.g., tardive dyskinesia).

2AXTQ00.title: Apolipoprotein
2AXTQ00.description: A protein that maintains the structure of lipoproteins, binds and transports lipids, regulates enzyme activity, and directs lipid metabolism.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

fAXkQ00.title: Lipases
fAXkQ00.description: A group of enzymes that catalyze the splitting of triglycerides into glycerol and free fatty acids.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Digestion and absorption of lipids

TAX6Q00.title: Hypomere
TAX6Q00.description: The part of the myotome that gives rise to the muscles of the anterolateral thorax and abdomen.

destinations.label: Embryogenesis → Differentiation of the embryonic disc

gAXFQ00.title: Anechoic
gAXFQ00.description: A descriptor for the complete absence of echoes (reflected sound waves) when a substance is evaluated with ultrasonography. Appears dark on the sonogram. Fluid (e.g., in a cyst) tends to have this property.

hAXcj00.title: Acute cholecystitis
hAXcj00.description: An acute inflammation of the gallbladder that typically manifests with fever, tenderness in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen, and a positive Murphy sign. Typically caused by obstructing cholelithiasis and subsequent bacterial infection.

3AXSj00.title: Chronic cholecystitis
3AXSj00.description: A chronic inflammation of the gallbladder characterized by inflammatory cell infiltration on histopathologic examination. Thought to be caused by mechanical irritation and/or recurrent cholecystitis that leads to fibrosis of the gallbladder. Almost always associated with gallstones.

RAXlj00.title: Chief cell
RAXlj00.description: The cells located at the base of the gastric pits that secrete pepsinogen in response to stimulation by the vagus nerve and local acidic pH.

iAXJj00.title: Pyoverdine
iAXJj00.description: A virulence factor produced by some species of Pseudomonas, including P. aeruginosa. Acts as a siderophore that facilitates bacterial survival in iron-deficient conditions. Contributes to the blue-green color of some Pseudomonas infections.

QAXuj00.title: Paraneoplastic encephalomyelitis
