QAXuj00.description: An inflammatory disorder of the central nervous system that occurs in association with malignancy (most commonly small cell lung cancer). Can involve multiple sites (e.g., brainstem, cerebellum, spinal cord, autonomic nervous system). Specific antibody-associated subtypes include anti-Hu encephalomyelitis, anti-Ma2-associated encephalitis, and anti-CRMP5 encephalomyelitis.

PAXWP00.title: Centrilobular necrosis
PAXWP00.description: A form of hepatocellular necrosis characterized by necrotic hepatocytes that encircle the terminal hepatic venule. Seen after exposure to hepatotoxic agents and in patients with Budd-Chiari syndrome.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

lAXvP00.title: Opacity protein
lAXvP00.description: A virulence factor of pathogenic Neisseria species that facilitates bacterial cell adherence to and invasion of host cells. Also impairs lymphocyte activation.

NAX-P00.title: Pinocytosis
NAX-P00.description: A type of endocytosis in which invaginations of the cellular membrane form intracellular vesicles that are then fused to lysosomes for degradation of vesicular contents. Cells rely on this mechanism for immune surveillance and endocytosis of previously metabolized nutrients (e.g. amino acids from previously catabolized protein).

mAXV400.title: Methionine
mAXV400.description: A glucogenic, essential amino acid. Encoded by the start codon (AUG).

MAXM400.title: Puborectalis muscle
MAXM400.description: A muscle of the pelvic floor that stretches from the body of the pubic bones to the coccyx, forming a sling around the lower rectum. Part of the levator ani muscle group, along with the iliococcygeus and pubococcygeus muscles.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

nAX7400.title: Pubococcygeus muscle
nAX7400.description: A muscle of the pelvic floor that stretches from the body of the pubic bones and the anterior aspect of the tendinous arch, around the urogenital hiatus to the coccyx and anococcygeal ligaments. Part of the levator ani muscle group, along with iliococcygeus and puborectalis. Strengthening this muscle through Kegel exercises combats urinary incontinence.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

LAXw400.title: Iliococcygeus muscle
LAXw400.description: A muscle of the pelvic floor that stretches from the ischial spines and the posterior aspect of the tendinous arch to the coccyx and anococcygeal ligaments. Part of the levator ani muscle group, along with pubococcygeus and puborectalis.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

oAX0k00.title: H1 receptor
oAX0k00.description: A G-protein coupled receptor found in the CNS and peripheral tissues that is stimulated by histamine. Stimulation of H1 in the CNS is responsible for several processes such as neurotransmission, circadian rhythm, and memory. Stimulation of H1 in peripheral tissues is involved in the pathophysiology of allergic reactions (e.g., hives, asthma, allergic rhinitis).

KAXUk00.title: Middle rectal artery
KAXUk00.description: A branch of the anterior division of the internal iliac artery that supplies the distal rectum, proximal anal canal, distal ureters, the prostate gland and seminal vesicles in males, and the vagina in females.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

media.title: Blood supply and lymphatic drainage of the anal canal

pAXLk00.title: Onycholysis
pAXLk00.description: A separation of the nail from the nail bed. Etiologies include infection, trauma, psoriasis, thyroid disease, and medication adverse effects (e.g., from taxane chemotherapy).

JAXsk00.title: Ticlopidine
JAXsk00.description: An irreversible P2Y12 receptor antagonist (ADP receptor blocker) that inhibits platelet aggregation. Used to reduce the risk of thrombotic stroke in patients who are unable to receive other types of antiplatelet therapy. Adverse effects include severe neutropenia, rash, and diarrhea.

qAXCk00.title: Suprapiriform foramen
qAXCk00.description: The superior portion of the greater sciatic foramen, which is divided by the piriformis muscle. Contains the superior gluteal vessels and nerve.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

IAXYO00.title: Infrapiriform foramen
IAXYO00.description: The inferior portion of the greater sciatic foramen, which is divided by the piriformis muscle. Contains the inferior gluteal vessels and nerve, the sciatic nerve, the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve, the pudendal nerve, the nerve to obturator internus, and the nerve to quadratus femoris.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

rAXfO00.title: Motion sickness
rAXfO00.description: A condition that develops in response to real or perceived motion as a result of incongruent vestibular, visual, and/or somatosensory information. Symptoms include nausea, headache, abdominal discomfort, malaise, sweating, and salivation.

7AX4O00.title: Dominant allele
7AX4O00.description: The allele which is phenotypically apparent in heterozygous individuals.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

HAXKO00.title: Superior colliculi
HAXKO00.description: A pair of structures that plays a role in orienting the head and eyes by coordinating sensory (e.g., visual, auditory, somatosensory) information with motor signals. Forms part of the roof of the midbrain.

GAXBO00.title: Lens subluxation
GAXBO00.description: A partial or complete dislocation of the ocular lens from its enclosing capsule. Etiologies include trauma and connective tissue disorders (e.g., Marfan syndrome).

destinations.label: Diseases of the lens → Ectopia lentis

tAXXl00.title: Gargoylism
tAXXl00.description: A term previously used to describe the characteristic dysmorphic features associated with Hurler syndrome, which include frontal bossing, elongated skull, flattened nasal bridge, broad nasal tip, anteverted nostrils, constant nasal discharge, and spaced and protruded eyes.

FAXgl00.title: Metyrapone
FAXgl00.description: A medication that inhibits cortisol synthesis in the adrenal cortex by inhibiting the enzyme 11β-hydroxylase. Used as an adjunct treatment in Cushing disease.

8AXOl00.title: Adult hemoglobin
8AXOl00.description: The predominant form of hemoglobin present in adults. Consists of 2 α-globin and 2 β-globin subunits (α2β2).

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin variants

uAXpl00.title: Recombinant human erythropoietin
uAXpl00.description: An erythropoiesis-stimulating agent used to treat anemia of chronic kidney disease, chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression, and anemia of myelodysplastic syndromes.

EAX8l00.title: Prostacyclin analogs
EAX8l00.description: A group of drugs that cause vasodilation by binding to prostacyclin receptors and increasing intracellular cAMP. cAMP inhibits myosin light chain kinase and results in vascular smooth muscle relaxation. Examples include epoprostenol, iloprost, and treprostinil. Primarily used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension.

vAXAl00.title: Endothelin receptor antagonists
vAXAl00.description: A class of drugs used in the management of pulmonary arterial hypertension (group 1 pulmonary hypertension). They act by binding to and inhibiting endothelin-1 receptors. As the protein endothelin-1 is a potent vasoconstrictor, its receptor antagonism causes vasodilation and reduction in vascular resistance. Examples include bosentan, macitentan, and ambrisentan.

destinations.label: Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale → Long-term management

DAX1N00.title: Caseating granuloma
DAX1N00.description: A granuloma with central necrosis that causes a cheese-like appearance. Associated with tuberculosis.

wAXhN00.title: Covalently closed circular DNA
wAXhN00.description: A form of hepatitis B DNA arranged in a covalently-linked ring. Can be transcribed into viral mRNA by host RNA polymerase. Targeted by interferons.

CAXqN00.title: Cerebellar hemispheres
CAXqN00.description: The two divisions of the cerebellar that lie on the sides of the cerebellar vermis.

Y_Xn500.title: Pontocerebellar fibers
Y_Xn500.description: The second order neurons that carry impulses from the pons to the cerebellum via the middle cerebellar peduncle.

b_XH500.title: Olivocerebellar tract
b_XH500.description: An afferent cerebellar tract that relays excitatory motor input from the cerebral cortex and contributes to motor coordination. Transmits nerve signals via the internal capsule to the inferior olivary nucleus and then via climbing fibers in the contralateral inferior cerebellar peduncle to the contralateral cerebellar hemisphere.

c_XaM00.title: Dorsal spinocerebellar tract
c_XaM00.description: A spinal tract that originates at the posterior thoracic nucleus in the spinal cord and carries proprioceptive information from the upper body (segments C8-L3) to the cerebellum via the inferior cerebellar peduncle. Unlike the ventral spinocerebellar tract, these fibers are uncrossed.

1_X2M00.title: Ventral spinocerebellar tract
1_X2M00.description: A spinal tract that carries proprioceptive information from the lower body (below L2) to the cerebellum. Crosses the midline twice: first on entry into the spinal cord, and again after entering the cerebellum via that superior cerebellar peduncle.

d_XoM00.title: Rubrospinal tract
d_XoM00.description: A tract that originates in the red nucleus and descends into the spinal cord. Involved in the control of muscle tone and action of flexor muscle groups.

e_XxM00.title: Mossy fibers
e_XxM00.description: The axons of afferent neurons from the cerebral cortex, pons, spinal cord, and vestibular nuclei to the cerebellum. Named for the fuzzy appearance of their synaptic junctions with granule cells. Stimulate granule cells, which in turn send excitatory stimuli to the Purkinje cells.

U_Xbn00.title: Climbing fibers
U_Xbn00.description: The neuronal fibers that originate in the inferior olivary nucleus of the medulla and pass through the inferior cerebellar peduncle to enter the cerebellum, where they synapse with the deep cerebellar nuclei and Purkinje cells. Facilitate motor coordination.

2_XTn00.title: Dentate nucleus
2_XTn00.description: The largest and most lateral of the cerebellar nuclei. Has a tooth-like serrated edge and is located within in the white matter of the cerebellar hemispheres. Along with the other cerebellar nuclei, aids in the coordination and planning of motor movements.

h_XcL00.title: Cerebellar cortex
h_XcL00.description: A structure of the cerebellum that contains neuronal cells and consists of 3 distinct layers: the outermost molecular layer, the middle Purkinje layer, and the innermost granular layer.

R_XlL00.title: Anabolic steroid
R_XlL00.description: A group of androgens whose effects include increased muscle mass and virilization, cardiovascular events (e.g., myocardial infarction, stroke), increased libido, and metabolic changes (e.g., hyperlipidemia, glucose intolerance).

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

i_XJL00.title: Frontal bossing
i_XJL00.description: An increased prominence of the forehead. Associated with acromegaly (due to excess growth hormone), chronic anemias (where the medullary cavities of the bone expand due to increased hematopoiesis), achondroplasia, and rickets.

Q_XuL00.title: Erosive gastritis
Q_XuL00.description: An acute, diffuse mucosal injury to the stomach characterized by ulceration of the superficial epithelium. Associated with major stress and/or trauma and a common source of upper GI bleeding in acutely ill patients.

j_X_L00.title: Penetrating ulcer
j_X_L00.description: An extension of a peptic ulcer through the gastric mucosa without perforation or leakage of luminal contents into the peritoneal cavity.

P_XWo00.title: Lymphokines
P_XWo00.description: A group of proteins that mediate the immune response (e.g., chemotaxis of inflammatory mediators, antibody production, sensitization to antigens). Also implicated in the development of type IV hypersensitivity reactions. Produced by T cells.

O_XIo00.title: Posterior intercostal veins
O_XIo00.description: A group of 11 paired veins that drain the posterior intercostal spaces. The veins run with the posterior intercostal artery along the undersurface of the corresponding rib.

media.title: Anatomy of the intercostal neurovascular bundle

l_Xvo00.title: Superior intercostal veins
l_Xvo00.description: A pair of veins that drain the 2nd, 3rd and 4th posterior intercostal veins. The left superior intercostal vein is considered to be part of the azygos venous system.

m_XVK00.title: Ascending aorta
m_XVK00.description: The section of the aorta between the aortic valve and the arch of the aorta.

media.title: Parts of the aorta and its branches

n_X7K00.title: Febuxostat
n_X7K00.description: A xanthine oxidase inhibitor used as second-line treatment for hyperuricemia (e.g., for treatment of chronic gout).

L_XwK00.title: Purine salvage pathway
L_XwK00.description: The mechanism by which purine nucleotides (e.g., adenine, guanine, and hypoxanthine) are recycled and reconverted to nucleotides (e.g., AMP, GMP, and IMP) through phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate (PRPP)-dependent reactions. Key enzymes of this process include adenine phosphoribosyltransferase (APRT) and hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT).

o_X0600.title: Deoxyadenosine trisphosphate
o_X0600.description: A purine nucleoside triphosphate used in DNA synthesis that is lymphotoxic in high concentrations. Accumulates in patients with adenosine deaminase deficiency and results in severe combined immunodeficiency.

destinations.label: Purines and pyrimidines → Synthesis of deoxyribonucleotides

6_Xj600.title: N-acetyltransferase
6_Xj600.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the biotransformation of arylamine compounds (e.g., isoniazid) and hydrazine derivates (e.g., tricyclic antidepressants) via acetylation, i.e. the transfer of acetyl groups from acetyl-CoA. Hepatic N-acetyltransferase is clinically significant because polymorphisms frequently occur that can impair metabolism of certain drugs.

q_XC600.title: Essential fatty acids
q_XC600.description: A group of fatty acids that cannot be synthesized by humans and, therefore, must be obtained through dietary intake. Examples include linoleic acid and eicosapentaenoic acid.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

I_XYp00.title: Linoleic acid
I_XYp00.description: An essential, polyunsaturated omega-6 fatty acid. Consumption is associated with lower serum concentrations of LDL cholesterol and triglycerides and higher serum concentrations of HDL cholesterol.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

7_X4p00.title: Basal cistern
7_X4p00.description: A compartment within the subarachnoid space formed by the separation of the pia mater and arachnoid membrane. Filled with cerebrospinal fluid.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

H_XKp00.title: Extended-spectrum penicillins
H_XKp00.description: A group of semi-synthetic penicillins with a broader antibiotic spectrum of activity compared to naturally-occurring penicillins. Examples include aminopenicillins and antipseudomonal penicillins.

s_Xtp00.title: Platelet-derived growth factor
s_Xtp00.description: A signaling molecule secreted by platelets and macrophages that stimulates angiogenesis, cellular proliferation, differentiation, and migration.

G_XBp00.title: Beau lines
G_XBp00.description: A transverse groove that runs across a fingernail or toenail. Results from temporary arrest of proximal nail matrix proliferation.

t_XXJ00.title: Nuclear atypia
t_XXJ00.description: A histopathologic descriptor for abnormalities of cell nuclei. Can be seen in precancerous and malignant conditions but may be a feature of benign conditions (e.g., reactive change to inflammation).

8_XOJ00.title: Autonomous thyroid nodule
8_XOJ00.description: A localized, nodular, and usually benign lesion of the thyroid gland that can produce thyroid hormone. Hyperfunctioning nodules have increased uptake on radioiodine scans.

u_XpJ00.title: S2 radiculopathy
u_XpJ00.description: An uncommon condition characterized by impingement of the S2 nerve root. Manifestations include decreased sensation of the posterior thigh, lower leg, and perineum. Can also cause incontinence and/or sexual dysfunction.

D_X1q00.title: Pyramidal cell
D_X1q00.description: A type of neuron that is predominantly found in the cerebral cortex, hippocampus, and amygdala. Consist of a pyramidal cell body, one single axon, a dominant apical dendrite, and several smaller basal dendrites. Play important roles in motor signaling and cognition.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Microscopic anatomy

w_Xhq00.title: Gerstmann syndrome
w_Xhq00.description: A constellation of findings seen after strokes that affect the dominant parietal cortex. Findings include dysgraphia (difficulty writing), dyscalculia (difficulty with mathematical calculations), finger agnosia (inability to distinguish various fingers), and an inability to differentiate right from left.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

9_XNq00.title: Neocortex
9_XNq00.description: A six-layered structure that forms the majority of the surface of the cerebral hemispheres. Responsible for high-level processes such as sensory perception, cognition, language skills, and spatial reasoning.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Microscopic anatomy

A_XRI00.title: Structures that pass through the diaphragm
A_XRI00.description: The structures that pierce the diaphragm do so at three openings or hiatuses; the caval hiatus at the level of T8 (which contains the inferior vena cava and the phrenic nerve), the esophageal hiatus at T10 (which contains the esophagus, vagus nerves, and the left gastric vessels), and the aortic hiatus at T12 (which contains the aorta, the azygos vein, and the thoracic duct).

__X5I00.title: Caval hiatus
__X5I00.description: The diaphragmatic aperture at the level of the eighth thoracic vertebra (T8). Conveys the inferior vena cava and the right phrenic nerve.

z_XrI00.title: Esophageal hiatus
z_XrI00.description: The diaphragmatic aperture at the level of the tenth thoracic vertebra (T10). Conveys the esophagus and the vagus nerve. The protrusion of an abdominal structure/organ into the thorax through a lax diaphragmatic esophageal hiatus is referred to as a hiatal hernia.

-_XDI00.title: Aortic hiatus
-_XDI00.description: The diaphragmatic aperture at the level of the twelfth thoracic vertebra (T12). Conveys the aorta, azygos vein, and the thoracic duct.

ZzXZr00.title: Mannose
ZzXZr00.description: A 6-carbon sugar that is often added as a post-translational modification to intracellular proteins. Acts as a marker for export products of the Golgi apparatus to be targeted to lysosomes.

0zXer00.title: Superior vena cava
0zXer00.description: The main vein that receives venous drainage from structures above the diaphragm and delivers it to the right atrium of the heart. Formed by the junction between the left and right brachiocephalic veins. The upper half is located in the superior mediastinum, and the lower half is located in the middle mediastinum.

azXQr00.title: Sphingomyelin
azXQr00.description: A lipid that plays an important role in membrane structure and function, especially in myelinated cells. Accumulates in patients with Niemann-Pick disease.

YzXnr00.title: Cavernous nerves
YzXnr00.description: A group of parasympathetic and sympathetic nerves that originate from the inferior hypogastric plexus. They facilitate penile/clitoral enlargement during sexual stimulation.

bzXHr00.title: Superior vesical artery
bzXHr00.description: A branch of the internal iliac artery that supplies the superior bladder, seminal vesicles, ductus deferens, and portions of the ureter.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Urinary bladder

XzX9r00.title: Adenylation
XzX9r00.description: The covalent attachment of adenosine monophosphate (AMP) to an amino acid side chain. Used to regulate protein activity.

czXa700.title: Muscles of mastication
czXa700.description: A group of muscles (the masseter, temporalis, medial pterygoid, and lateral pterygoid) responsible for movement of the jaw at the temporomandibular joint. Develop from the first branchial arch and are supplied by the mandibular branch of the trigeminal nerve.

1zX2700.title: Vibrio parahaemolyticus
1zX2700.description: A gram-negative rod found in salt and brackish waters that can contaminate seafood and cause gastroenteritis (vibriosis).

WzXP700.title: Superior mesenteric lymph nodes
WzXP700.description: A cluster of lymph nodes that surround the superior mesenteric artery. Receives lymphatic drainage from the distal duodenum, jejunum, ileum, the colon proximal to the splenic flexure, and the inferior mesenteric lymph nodes. Drains into the preaortic lymph nodes.

dzXo700.title: Gonadal mosaicism
dzXo700.description: A phenomenon in which an individual carries a germ cell line that is genetically distinct from the rest of the body. Typically the result of a mutation in sex cells (e.g., eggs or sperm).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

VzXG700.title: Variable expressivity
VzXG700.description: A phenomenon in which phenotypic expression varies among individuals with the same genotype. Conditions that manifest with variable expressivity include neurofibromatosis type 1 and Marfan syndrome.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

ezXx700.title: Dominant negative mutation
ezXx700.description: A gene mutation that results in nonfunctional protein that impairs the function of protein produced by the wild-type allele in heterozygotes (e.g., mutant, nonfunctional p53 that binds to DNA and prevents functional p53 from binding).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

2zXTH00.title: PAH
2zXTH00.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:

1. Pulmonary arterial hypertension
2. Para-aminohippuric acid
3. Phenylalanine hydroxylase (enzyme)
4. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon

fzXkH00.title: REM sleep latency
fzXkH00.description: The period of time between the onset of sleep and the first REM episode. Typically between 90–120 minutes in a healthy person.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Sleep physiology

TzX6H00.title: Gamma-carboxyglutamic acid
TzX6H00.description: An amino acid produced by the reaction of gamma-glutamyl carboxylase with vitamin K. Used in the synthesis of several coagulation factors, including factors VII, IX, X, and XIV, Protein S and Protein C.

gzXFH00.title: Hydroxyproline
gzXFH00.description: A modified amino acid produced by the hydroxylation of proline by prolyl hydroxylase. Contributes to the heat resistance and stability of collagen. Deficiency of vitamin C (scurvy) results in decreased hydroxyproline synthesis.

SzXyH00.title: Cotransmitters
SzXyH00.description: Cotransmitters are known as neuromodulators and are released at the synapses together with neurotransmitters. They do not act directly on the postsynapse but modulate the excitability of the postsynaptic neuron for the neurotransmitter. Most cotransmitters belong to the group of neuropeptides. Examples include nitric oxide, ATP, and neuropeptide Y.

3zXSs00.title: Root cause analysis
3zXSs00.description: A retrospective analysis performed after a medical error has occurred in order to identify active and latent errors to specify who was affected, what happened, where it happened, when it happened, and how it happened. The focus in a root cause analysis is to understand system-level factors that allowed an error to occur, rather than blaming an individual. A root cause analysis is required by the Joint Commission for all sentinel events and never events, and its end product involves recommendations to prevent the error from occurring again.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Analysis of medical error

RzXls00.title: Failure mode and effects analysis
RzXls00.description: A proactive medical error analysis technique used to anticipate potential factors that could go wrong when a new procedure, technique, or protocol is to be implemented in clinical practice. The goal is to identify preventive or corrective measures before a potential medical error occurs (i.e., a prospective medical error analysis).

destinations.label: Patient safety → Analysis of medical error

izXJs00.title: Decoy receptor
izXJs00.description: A receptor that recognizes and binds specific cytokines with high affinity and specificity. However, it is not able to activate the receptor complex and thus acts as an inhibitor by preventing the cytokines from binding to their regular receptors.

QzXus00.title: Testis-determining factor
QzXus00.description: A protein that is encoded by the sex-determining region Y (SRY) gene on the Y chromosome. Promotes the differentiation of the bipotent gonadal primordium into the testis, thus initiating male sex determination.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Gonadal sex differentiation

jzX_s00.title: Hydropic degeneration
jzX_s00.description: The accumulation of water in cells in response to injury. Impaired Na+/K+-ATPase pump function (e.g., due to hypoxia) decreases ATP production, which leads to Na+ accumulation in the cell. Consequently, water follows Na+, which leads to cell swelling.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cell injury

PzXWG00.title: β-thalassemia minor
PzXWG00.description: A mild version of β-thalassemia caused by a defect in a single allele of the β-globin gene (heterozygosity). Typically asymptomatic but can cause mild anemia.

4zX3G00.title: β-thalassemia major
4zX3G00.description: The more severe form of β-thalassemia, which is caused by the inheritance of two defective alleles in the β-globin gene (homozygosity). Manifests with hemolytic anemia that typically requires chronic transfusions.

kzXmG00.title: Thayer-Martin agar
kzXmG00.description: A culture medium that favors the growth of Neisseria species. Contains vancomycin (which inhibits the growth of gram-positive organisms), trimethoprim and colistin (which inhibit the growth of gram-negative organisms), and nystatin (which inhibits the growth of fungi).

OzXIG00.title: Transferrin saturation
OzXIG00.description: A measure of the amount of iron bound to transferrin. A high value (> 45%) indicates iron overload; a low value (< 20%) indicates iron deficiency.

NzX-G00.title: Lobules of the mammary glands
NzX-G00.description: The functional glandular units of the breast that produce milk during lactation. The normal breast has 15-20 lobules.

5zXit00.title: Lactiferous sinuses
5zXit00.description: The expansions of the lactiferous ducts located directly beneath the nipple that act as reservoirs for milk. The lactiferous ducts and sinuses serve as connections between the breast lobule and the nipple.

MzXMt00.title: Exertional hemoglobinuria
MzXMt00.description: A condition characterized by intravascular hemolysis due to mechanical erythrocyte damage from exercises that have a repetitive mechanical impact (e.g., marching).

nzX7t00.title: α-globin
nzX7t00.description: A protein component of fetal and adult hemoglobin.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin synthesis

LzXwt00.title: Hydroxylysine
LzXwt00.description: A modified amino acid produced by the hydroxylation of lysine by lysyl hydroxylase. Contributes to the heat resistance and stability of collagen. Deficiency of vitamin C (scurvy) results in decreased hydroxylysine synthesis.

ozX0F00.title: Hematin
ozX0F00.description: A dark pigment resulting from the oxidation of heme, e.g., by gastric acid.

KzXUF00.title: Hyperemia
KzXUF00.description: An increase in the blood flow to a specific area of the body.

6zXjF00.title: Tazobactam
6zXjF00.description: A β-lactamase inhibitor used in combination with β-lactam antibiotics (particularly piperacillin) to prevent bacteria from inactivating the antibiotic.

destinations.label: Overview of antibiotic therapy → Beta-lactam antibiotics

pzXLF00.title: Hemoglobin crystals
pzXLF00.description: Dense rectangular structures within erythrocytes that are composed of precipitated hemoglobin. Hemoglobin crystals suggest hemoglobin C disease, as hemoglobin C is less soluble than normal hemoglobin.

JzXsF00.title: Fidaxomicin
JzXsF00.description: A bactericidal antibiotic that inhibits RNA polymerase and thus impairs protein synthesis. Used as a first-line therapy for initial episodes of C. difficile infection.

qzXCF00.title: Drug affinity
qzXCF00.description: A measure of how well a drug/molecule binds to a receptor/another molecule. A higher affinity indicates a stronger binding.

IzXY800.title: Affinity maturation
IzXY800.description: A process in which B cells interact with T-helper cells to produce antibodies with higher affinity for specific antigens. Mechanisms leading to increased affinity include somatic hypermutation and clonal selection.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

tzXXu00.title: Amastia
tzXXu00.description: The complete absence of breast tissue as a result of failure of the mammary ridge to develop.

destinations.label: Overview of common breast conditions → Disorders of breast development

8zXOu00.title: Human factors engineering
8zXOu00.description: A discipline that examines the interaction between individuals and their work environment as well as the tools and processes they use for work in order to design systems that are safe and easy to use. In the context of patient safety, the goal of human factors design is to identify risk factors for medical error and design systems that reduce such risks.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medical errors

EzX8u00.title: Active error
EzX8u00.description: An error that occurs at the interface between a human and an aspect of a system. Typically occurs at the frontline of patient care. Active errors are distinctly different from latent errors, which are flaws in an overarching system.

vzXAu00.title: Latent error
vzXAu00.description: A system design issue (e.g., organizational, cultural, and/or physical environment factors) that predisposes the people working in systems to make mistakes. For example, if two medications with very different indications have very similar names, the likelihood of an incorrect medication administration increases. Distinct from active errors such as negligence.

DzX1E00.title: Communication error
DzX1E00.description: An error in communication between the health care personnel and the patient as well as among health care personnel.

wzXhE00.title: Diagnostic error
wzXhE00.description: An error or delay in diagnosis.

9zXNE00.title: Treatment errors
9zXNE00.description: An error resulting from inappropriate medical procedures, incorrect administration of treatment, incorrect drug dosage or method of use, and failure to provide treatment or respond to diagnoses in a timely manner.

CzXqE00.title: Preventive errors
CzXqE00.description: A type of error that results from failure to implement appropriate prophylaxis, failure to provide adequate monitoring and/or follow-up treatment, or failure in equipment and system maintenance.

xzXEE00.title: Adverse reaction
xzXEE00.description: An unintended, unexpected, or undesirable consequence of a correct and justified action

BzXzE00.title: Adverse event
BzXzE00.description: A problem (e.g., injury, disability, prolonged hospital stay, death) caused by medical care rather than underlying disease. Further classified as preventable (if the harm were due to a medical error and could have been avoided completely), ameliorable (if the harm could not have been avoided, but its severity could have been minimized significantly), and nonpreventable (if the harm were not due to medical error and could not have been avoided).

yzXdv00.title: Sentinel event
yzXdv00.description: An unexpected adverse event that results in the death or serious physical or psychological injury of a patient. Examples include wrong-site surgery, retention of a foreign object in a patient after a procedure, and inpatient suicide. Near-miss occurrences of these types of serious adverse events are also considered sentinel events. There is some overlap in the definitions of never events and sentinel events.

AzXRv00.title: Near miss
AzXRv00.description: A medical error that could have resulted in an adverse event but did not do so, either incidentally or due to a timely intervention (e.g., a nurse identifies that a doctor's order is incorrect).

_zX5v00.title: Medical malpractice
_zX5v00.description: The occurrence of negligent conduct on the part of a health care provider or performance of a medical task with unreasonable lack of skill.

destinations.label: Medical professionalism and codes of conduct → Malpractice, misconduct, and physician impairment

zzXrv00.title: Safety culture
zzXrv00.description: A culture that promotes safety awareness, develops and implements measures for the maintenance of a safe work environment, and ensures that individuals can openly express safety concerns. Components of this culture include acknowledgment of the possibility of medical errors by any individual, a blame-free environment, positive reinforcement, and the absence of negative consequences following medical error reporting.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medical errors

-zXDv00.title: Quality improvement
-zXDv00.description: A prospective and retrospective review of existing practices with the aim of identifying areas of improvement and implementing system-based interventions. The focus is on system-based improvements and not on placing blame.

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

Z-XZD00.title: Run chart
Z-XZD00.description: A graphic representation of the impact of an intervention on quality over time to determine if the perceived improvement is random (random trend) or indicates a true improvement (true trend).

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

a-XQD00.title: Shewhart chart
a-XQD00.description: A graphic representation to determine if a perceived improvement in quality over time is statistically significant.

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

Y-XnD00.title: Convenience sample
Y-XnD00.description: A study population that is drawn from a population that is easy to reach. Since the chosen is not chosen at random, this type of study can lead to bias.

1-X2w00.title: Thoracic sympathetic ganglia
1-X2w00.description: A network of 11-12 interconnected ganglia that lie on either side of the thoracic vertebrae. The upper portion gives fibers to the cardiac, pulmonary, aortic, and esophageal plexuses. The lower portion gives fibers to the greater, lesser, and least splanchnic nerves.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system

V-XGw00.title: Cell nucleus
V-XGw00.description: A membrane-bound organelle that contains most of the genetic information of the cell. It is only found in eukaryotic cells. The nucleus controls the cell's activities via gene expression.

e-Xxw00.title: Nucleus
e-Xxw00.description:
1. Cell nucleus: a membrane-bound organelle that contains most of the genetic information of the cell
2. Nucleus (neuroanatomy): an accumulation of nerve cell bodies in the central nervous system

f-Xk900.title: S4
f-Xk900.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Sacral spinal nerve 4
2. The 4th sacral vertebrae
3. The 4th heart sound

T-X6900.title: Endorphins
T-X6900.description: A family of endogenous opioids produced by the CNS and pituitary gland. Involved in the inhibition of pain signals.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

g-XF900.title: Palmitic acid
g-XF900.description: A primary end product of fatty acid synthesis. This 16-carbon fatty acid is the only fatty acid that humans can synthesize de novo.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

h-XcC00.title: Medicare
h-XcC00.description: A US national health insurance program that covers individuals ≥ 65 years of age and patients with end-stage renal failure, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and/or permanent disability. Part A covers hospital care, hospice care, and skilled nursing facility care; Part B covers physician fees, emergency department visits, preventive health care and screening, diagnostics studies, and rehabilitation; Part C allows for enrollment in private insurance plans approved by Medicare; and Part D covers prescription drugs.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payers

3-XSC00.title: Medicaid
3-XSC00.description: A US state- and federally-funded insurance program that covers individuals with a low income.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payers

R-XlC00.title: Emtricitabine
R-XlC00.description: A nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used to treat HIV infection. Interferes with viral RNA-dependent DNA polymerase. Adverse effects include diarrhea, headache, and nausea.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

i-XJC00.title: Didanosine
i-XJC00.description: A nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used to treat HIV infection. Interferes with viral RNA-dependent DNA polymerase. Adverse effects include peripheral neuropathy, rash, and pancreatitis.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

Q-XuC00.title: Stavudine
Q-XuC00.description: A nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used to treat HIV infection. Interferes with viral DNA-dependent DNA polymerase. Adverse effects include peripheral neuropathy, headache, rash, nausea, and hepatotoxicity.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

j-X_C00.title: Diplococcus
j-X_C00.description: A bacterial species that is round in shape and typically found in pairs of cells. Examples include S. pneumoniae, Enterococcus, and Neisseria.

m-XVB00.title: Olfactory bulb mitral cell
m-XVB00.description: A type of specialized neuron found in the olfactory bulb. Helps relay impulses from olfactory epithelium to the cerebral cortex.

5-XiB00.title: Tufted cell
5-XiB00.description: A type of specialized neuron found in the olfactory glomeruli. Receives impulses from the olfactory epithelium and then amplifies and relays these signals to the cerebral cortex.

n-X7B00.title: Olfactory epithelium
n-X7B00.description: The lining of the nasal cavity, which consists of specialized cells that detect smell. Includes olfactory receptor neurons and their cilia, basal cells, and sustentacular cells.

L-XwB00.title: Frontal sinuses
L-XwB00.description: A pair of air-filled cavities in the frontal bone, located superolateral to the nasal ridge. Connect to the middle nasal meatus and vary significantly in size between individuals.

o-X0y00.title: Ethmoidal sinuses
o-X0y00.description: A collection of air-filled cavities located between the orbits and the nasal cavity. Consist of anterior, middle (now considered to be part of the anterior), and posterior portions.

K-XUy00.title: Sphenoid sinuses
K-XUy00.description: A pair of air-filled cavities in the sphenoid bone and the most posterior paranasal sinuses.

6-Xjy00.title: Maxillary sinuses
6-Xjy00.description: A pair of air-filled cavities located in the maxilla. The largest paranasal sinuses. Drain into the nasal cavity via the middle meatus.

p-XLy00.title: Superior meatus
p-XLy00.description: A structure that receives drainage mainly from the posterior ethmoidal air cells. Located between the superior nasal conchae and the middle nasal conchae.

J-Xsy00.title: Middle meatus
J-Xsy00.description: A nasal passage located on the lateral wall of the nasal cavity between the inferior and middle concha. Receives the openings of the frontal and maxillary sinuses as well as the anterior ethmoidal air cells.

q-XCy00.title: Inferior meatus
q-XCy00.description: A nasal passage located on the lateral wall of the nasal cavity below the inferior concha. Receives the opening of the nasolacrimal duct.

I-XYA00.title: Sphenoethmoidal recess
I-XYA00.description: A structure located above the superior nasal conchae that receives drainage from the sphenoid sinuses.

7-X4A00.title: Diphtheria antitoxin
7-X4A00.description: A medication comprised of equine antidiphtheria toxin antibodies. Administered during acute episodes of diphtheria as treatment and to prevent sequelae of the infection. Not routinely used as prophylaxis. Can cause serum sickness.

H-XKA00.title: Medial frontal micturition center
H-XKA00.description: A center in the front of the brain responsible that activates the detrusor reflex when the bladder is full. Damage to this center can lead to urinary incontinence.

s-XtA00.title: Verbal apraxia
s-XtA00.description: A disorder caused by inability to execute motor movements needed to produce speech, which results in halting speech and sound distortions.

G-XBA00.title: Chimerism
G-XBA00.description: The presence of two genetically distinct cell lines that arise from two different zygotes that fused into one single embryo. Compared to mosaicism, where all cell lines have the same zygotic origin, chimerism features cell lines derived from two different zygotes.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

t-XX_00.title: Pampiniform plexus
t-XX_00.description: A network of small veins that runs within the spermatic cord and provides venous drainage to the scrotal structures in males; in females, it drains the ovaries.

media.title: Structure and content of the spermatic cord

F-Xg_00.title: Costal margin
F-Xg_00.description: A boundary of the anterior abdominal wall formed by the cartilages of the 7th-10th ribs and the xiphoid process.

8-XO_00.title: Subcostal plane
8-XO_00.description: An imaginary transverse plane that passes through the 10th costal cartilage anteriorly (i.e., the inferior limit of the costal margins) and the inferior border of the L3 vertebral body posteriorly. Marks the boundary between the hypochondriac and epigastric regions superiorly and the lateral and umbilical regions inferiorly.

E-X8_00.title: Somatic mosaicism
E-X8_00.description: The selective presence of a mutation in individual somatic cells. Caused by a mutation during mitosis after fertilization. Usually affects multiple tissues or organs. McCune-Albright syndrome is caused by somatic mosaicism in G-protein signaling.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

w-Xhz00.title: Splice mutation
w-Xhz00.description: A genetic mutation that occurs between an exon and intron (splice site). The resulting mutation alters mRNA splicing and subsequent processing (e.g., inclusion of introns or exclusion of exons), which results in an altered protein-coding sequence.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

9-XNz00.title: Transpyloric plane
9-XNz00.description: A transverse plane that lies midway between the suprasternal notch and the pubic symphysis. Passes through the 9th costal cartilage. Posteriorly, it lies at the level of the inferior border of the L1 vertebra.

C-Xqz00.title: Transtubercular plane
C-Xqz00.description: A transverse plane that lies midway between the transpyloric plane and the pubic symphysis. Passes through the iliac tubercles and body of the L5 vertebra. Marks the boundary between the umbilical and lateral regions of the anterior abdominal wall superiorly and the pubic and iliac regions inferiorly.

y-Xd-00.title: Mid-clavicular line
y-Xd-00.description: An imaginary vertical line on the anterior abdominal wall that connects the midpoint of the clavicle caudally to the midinguinal point (midpoint between the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubic symphysis) caudally.

media.title: Vertical lines used in topographic anatomy of the thorax

A-XR-00.title: Nuclear factor of activated T-cells
A-XR-00.description: A family of cytosolic transcription factors activated by signaling through the T-cell receptor that promotes T-cell replication and maturation. Dephosphorylation of NFAT by calcineurin allows the transcription factors to enter the nucleus to stimulate gene expression.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

_-X5-00.title: FK506 binding protein
_-X5-00.description: A binding protein that forms a complex with the immunosuppressive agent tacrolimus to inhibit calcineurin, which normally promotes T cell activation. Sirolimus (also called rapamycin) binds to FKBP to inhibit mTOR, which normally promotes T cell proliferation and differentiation.

--XD-00.title: Sacral sympathetic ganglia
--XD-00.description: A network of 4-5 interconnected ganglia that lie anterior to the sacrum. Gives rise to the sacral splanchnic nerve.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Sympathetic nervous system

0ZceZa0.title: Histotoxic hypoxia
0ZceZa0.description: The impairment of mitochondrial ATP production due to a defect in oxygen utilization despite normal blood oxygen saturation and delivery to tissues. Causes include cyanide and hydrogen sulfide toxicity.

aZcQZa0.title: Mid-axillary line
aZcQZa0.description: An imaginary vertical line on the anterolateral abdominal wall that extends cranially from the midpoint between the anterior and posterior axillary folds to the iliac tubercles caudally. Marks the boundary between the anterior and lateral abdominal walls.

media.title: Vertical lines used in topographic anatomy of the thorax

bZcHZa0.title: Electromechanical coupling
bZcHZa0.description: The process by which an electrical signal that reaches the sarcolemma of a myocyte is translated into a muscle contraction.

cZca0a0.title: Rectus abdominis muscle
cZca0a0.description: A paired strap muscle of the anterior abdominal wall. Originates from the pubic crest and pubic symphysis. Inserts onto the xiphoid process and the 5th–7th ribs. Innervated by the anterior rami of the lower thoracic nerves. Flexes the trunk, aids in forced expiration, and helps increase intra-abdominal pressure.

1Zc20a0.title: Pyramidalis muscle
1Zc20a0.description: A small triangular muscle of the anterior abdominal wall that lies in front of the rectus abdominis above the pubic symphysis. Originates from the pubic symphysis and inserts into the linea alba. Lies within the rectus sheath and is innervated by the subcostal nerve. Tenses the linea alba.

WZcP0a0.title: Arcuate line
WZcP0a0.description: The inferior limit of the posterior rectus sheath. Lies approximately ⅓ of the distance between the umbilicus and the pubic symphysis.

dZco0a0.title: Erythroid progenitor cell
dZco0a0.description: A stem cell found in bone marrow that gives rise to erythrocytes.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Red cell line: erythrocytes

VZcG0a0.title: Linea semilunaris
VZcG0a0.description: A curved, vertical line on the anterior abdominal wall at the lateral edge of each rectus abdominis muscle. Herniation of intra-abdominal contents through this line is known as a Spigelian hernia.

UZcbaa0.title: Somatic hypermutation
UZcbaa0.description: A process in which a gene locus undergoes a rate of mutation that is 100,000-1,000,000 times greater than the rate of mutation in the rest of the genome. Typically results in single-base substitutions. Normally occurs only in proliferating B cells to generate antibodies against specific antigens.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

TZc6aa0.title: Internal thoracic artery
TZc6aa0.description: A branch of the first part of the subclavian artery. Lies behind the first 6 costal cartilages, just lateral to the sternal border. Divides into the musculophrenic artery and the superior epigastric artery.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

gZcFaa0.title: Renal cortex
gZcFaa0.description: The outer functional portion of the kidney, located between the capsule and the inner medulla. Extends down into the medulla between the pyramids. Contains glomeruli, proximal convoluted tubules, distal convoluted tubules, and renal vessels.

SZcyaa0.title: Renal pelvis
SZcyaa0.description: The portion of the kidney where the major calyces come together to form the ureteropelvic junction (the connection to the ureter).

hZccYa0.title: Glomerulus
hZccYa0.description: A network of capillaries in the renal corpuscle. Filters blood across capillary walls to the surrounding Bowman capsule. Supported by intraglomerular mesangial cells.

3ZcSYa0.title: Colles fascia
3ZcSYa0.description: A continuation of the deep membranous layer (Scarpa fascia) of the superficial fascia of the abdominal wall. Forms the superficial fascia of the perineum.

RZclYa0.title: Camper fascia
RZclYa0.description: A superficial, fatty layer of the superficial fascia of the abdominal wall.

iZcJYa0.title: Scarpa fascia
iZcJYa0.description: The deep membranous layer of the superficial layer of the abdominal wall. Continues into the perineum as Colles fascia and into the scrotum as the dartos muscle layer. Fuses with the deep fascia of the thigh, below and parallel to the inguinal ligament; thus, helps to contain the spread of extravasated urine in cases of anterior urethral rupture.

QZcuYa0.title: Costal facet
QZcuYa0.description: A portion of a vertebra that articulates with a rib. Further categorized as superior, inferior, and transverse costal facets.

PZcWba0.title: Colonization
PZcWba0.description: The presence of microorganisms in the human body (e.g., skin, conjunctiva, gastrointestinal tract, respiratory tract, urinary tract) with no symptoms or immune response, or on surfaces of indwelling medical devices (e.g., urinary catheters).

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

kZcmba0.title: Sacrum
kZcmba0.description: A fused portion of the spine located inferior to the lumbar spine and superior to the coccyx. Consists of 5 fused vertebrae (S1–S5)

OZcIba0.title: Coccyx
OZcIba0.description: The most inferior portion of the spine. Consists of 3–5 fused vertebrae.

mZcVXa0.title: Articular process
mZcVXa0.description: The flat surfaces at the junction of the vertebral pedicles and laminae (two on the superior aspect, two on the inferior aspect) that articulate with the articular processes of the adjacent vertebrae, forming the zygapophyseal or facet joints.

LZcwXa0.title: Vertebral foramen
LZcwXa0.description: The central space between the vertebral arch and vertebral body. Contains the spinal cord, nerve roots, meninges, and blood vessels. Adjacent vertebral foramina form the continuous vertebral canal extending from the foramen magnum to the sacral hiatus.

oZc0ca0.title: External oblique muscle
oZc0ca0.description: The largest and most superficial of the anterolateral muscles of the abdominal wall. Originates from the lower 8 ribs. Lateral fibers insert into the outer lip of the iliac crest; medial fibers form an aponeurosis that contributes to the anterior layer of the rectus sheath. Functions include lateral flexion of the trunk and maintenance of abdominal tone. Innervated by the lower 5 intercostal nerves and the subcostal nerve.

pZcLca0.title: Substance P
pZcLca0.description: A peptide neurotransmitter and signaling molecule. Enhances transmission of pain. Other effects included inflammation, vasodilation, and stimulation of growth.

JZcsca0.title: Thoracolumbar fascia
JZcsca0.description: The deep fascia of the trunk. The thoracic fascia extends from the spines of the thoracic vertebrae to the angles of the ribs and fuses superiorly with the deep cervical fascia. The lumbar fascia extends from the 12th rib to the iliac crest and sacrum. It encloses the muscles of the back (i.e., erector spinae, quadratus lumborum, and transversus spinalis muscles).

IZcY1a0.title: Commercial health insurance
IZcY1a0.description: A health insurance plan sold by a private company (i.e., not funded by the government). May be sponsored by an employer or school or purchased individually through the ACA health insurance marketplace. Includes health maintenance organizations, point-of-service plans, preferred provider organizations, and exclusive provider organizations. Specific benefits vary across plans.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payers

sZct1a0.title: Internal oblique muscle
sZct1a0.description: An anterolateral muscle of the abdominal wall that lies between the external oblique and the transversus abdominis. Function includes lateral flexion of the trunk. Its aponeurosis contributes to the formation of the rectus sheath.

GZcB1a0.title: Health maintenance organizations
GZcB1a0.description: A type of health insurance plan that consists of a network of physicians and hospitals that provide coverage for its enrollees, with no coverage at out-of-network providers except for emergency services. Specialist care typically requires primary care physician referral.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payers

tZcXWa0.title: Exclusive provider organization
tZcXWa0.description: A type of health insurance plan that consists of a network of physicians and hospitals that provide coverage for its enrollees, with no coverage at out-of-network providers except for emergency services. Patients typically can see an in-network specialist without a referral.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payers

FZcgWa0.title: Preferred provider organization
FZcgWa0.description: A type of health insurance plan that consists of a network of physicians and hospitals that provide coverage for its enrollees. Visits with out-of-network providers are possible but have higher costs than in-network providers. Patients can typically see an in-network specialist without a referral.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payers

8ZcOWa0.title: Point-of-service
8ZcOWa0.description: A type of health insurance plan that consists of a network of physicians and hospitals that provide coverage for its enrollees. Visits at out-of-network providers are possible but have higher costs than in-network providers. Specialist care typically requires primary care physician referral.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payers

uZcpWa0.title: Urobilin
uZcpWa0.description: A compound produced from reabsorbed urobilinogen that is excreted by the kidneys. Contributes to the yellow color of urine.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Metabolism of erythrocytes

EZc8Wa0.title: Transversus abdominis muscle
EZc8Wa0.description: The deepest muscle of the anterolateral abdominal wall. Its fibers are oriented transversely. Functions to maintain abdominal tone and increase intra-abdominal pressure.

vZcAWa0.title: Leukoerythroblastic smear
vZcAWa0.description: The presence of immature and/or abnormal cells (e.g., dacrocytes, nucleated red blood cells, myelocytes, metamyelocytes, and myeloblasts, giant platelets) in the peripheral blood. Associated with conditions in which the bone marrows is replaced by fibrosis, tumor, and/or granulomatous change.

DZc1da0.title: Mantle zone
DZc1da0.description: A region of a lymphoid follicle that surrounds a germinal center. Consists of predominantly unchallenged B-cells.

wZchda0.title: Cervical subluxation
wZchda0.description: A misalignment of cervical vertebrae that can cause nerve root compression, which manifests with paresthesia, paresis, and/or pain. Associated with rheumatoid arthritis.

9ZcNda0.title: Ulnar deviation
9ZcNda0.description: Displacement of fingers toward the side of the ulna.

CZcqda0.title: Complement component 3
CZcqda0.description: A protein of the innate immune system that cleaves into the pro-inflammatory compounds C3a and C3b.

xZcEda0.title: Myalgia
xZcEda0.description: A symptom of muscle discomfort (e.g., aching, soreness, pain).

BZczda0.title: Lens placode
BZczda0.description: An embryonic structure that consists of a thickening of ectoderm. Develops into the lens pit, which develops into the lens.

yZcdVa0.title: Optic grooves
yZcdVa0.description: A group of small grooves that arise from the neural fold bilaterally in the third week of embryonic development. Develop into optic vesicles after closure of the neural tube.

AZcRVa0.title: Choroidal fissure
AZcRVa0.description: A central groove in the optic cup that allows the entrance of the blood vessels that supply the eye. Normally closes in the 7th week of embryonic development. Failure to close leads to coloboma.

_Zc5Va0.title: Zonular fibers
_Zc5Va0.description: A collection of radially arranged fibers that connect the lens to the ciliary body.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Segments and chambers of the eye

zZcrVa0.title: Retina
zZcrVa0.description: The innermost layer of the eye, which is composed of several layers of specialized cells that convert light into neural signals. Contains the optic disc and macula.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

media.title: Retinal layers and structure of the globe of the eye

-ZcDVa0.title: Tarsal glands
-ZcDVa0.description: A component of the lacrimal apparatus located within the tarsal plate with orifices at the rim of the marginal zone of the conjunctiva. They produce a lipid layer that protects against dehydration of the cornea.

Z0cZea0.title: Nasolacrimal duct
Z0cZea0.description: A duct that drains tear fluid from the lacrimal sac into the inferior meatus of the nose.

media.title: Lacrimal apparatus and tear film layers

00ceea0.title: Infraorbital foramen
00ceea0.description: A part of the maxillary bone at the inferior aspect of the orbit that contains infraorbital nerves and vessels.

a0cQea0.title: Supraorbital notch
a0cQea0.description: A part of the frontal bone located at the superior aspect of the orbit that contains supraorbital nerves and vessels.

Y0cnea0.title: Ethmoidal foramina
Y0cnea0.description: A set of openings in the ethmoid bone located lateral to the olfactory groove. Contains ethmoidal nerves and vessels.

X0c9ea0.title: External iliac artery
X0c9ea0.description: A terminal branch of the common iliac artery that originates at the level of the sacroiliac joint. Continues as the common femoral artery below the inguinal ligament and is the main arterial supply of the lower limbs. Branches into the inferior epigastric artery and deep circumflex iliac artery.

media.title: Pelvis with blood supply of the anal canal

c0caUa0.title: Rift Valley fever virus
c0caUa0.description: A helical, single-stranded, negative-sense RNA virus of the Bunyaviridae family. Its reservoir is cattle, sheep, goats, camels. Its vector is mosquitoes. Causes Rift Valley fever.

10c2Ua0.title: Pubic tubercle
10c2Ua0.description: A palpable bony prominence on the superior ramus of the pubic bone, located ~ 2.5 cm lateral to the pubic symphysis. The inguinal ligament and the conjoint tendon are attached to it. The relation of a groin hernia to the pubic tubercle helps distinguish between a femoral hernia (below and lateral to the pubic tubercle) from an inguinal hernia (above and lateral to the pubic tubercle).

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Femoral triangle and fasial compartments of the thigh

W0cPUa0.title: Starry sky pattern
W0cPUa0.description: A histopathologic pattern associated with Burkitt lymphoma. Characterized by tingible body macrophages (that contain phagocytized tumor cells) scattered diffusely within a sheet of uniform neoplastic cells.

V0cGUa0.title: T-arm
V0cGUa0.description: A region located at the 3' end of the tRNA molecule that contains ribothymidine, pseudouridine, and cytidine. Tethers tRNA to the ribosome.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

e0cxUa0.title: Evolocumab
e0cxUa0.description: A PCSK9 inhibitor used for the treatment and prevention of cardiovascular conditions (e.g., myocardial infarction, hyperlipidemia, hypercholesterolemia). Administered subcutaneously. Adverse effects include nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, and influenza.

media.title: Overview of lipid metabolism and lipid-lowering agents

20cT2a0.title: Fixed dilated pupil
20cT2a0.description: A dilated pupil that is unresponsive to light stimulus. Etiologies include drugs (e.g., parasympatholytics, sympathomimetics, cyanide, methanol, barbiturates), cranial nerve III injury (e.g., due to uncal herniation), hypothermia, acute angle-closure glaucoma, and brain death.

destinations.label: Physiology and abnormalities of the pupil → Other pupillary defects

f0ck2a0.title: Lisdexamfetamine
f0ck2a0.description: A prodrug of the stimulant dextroamphetamine, which increases the release of dopamine and norepinephrine in the central nervous system. Used to treat binge eating disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Adverse effects include paresthesia, insomnia, and dry mouth.

T0c62a0.title: Chromosomes
T0c62a0.description: The structures of tightly coiled DNA that are located inside the nucleus of a cell. They carry hereditary information in the form of genes.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

media.title: Homologous chromosomes before and after replication

g0cF2a0.title: Diploid cell
g0cF2a0.description: A somatic cell that contains a complete set of paired chromosomes.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

S0cy2a0.title: Chromatid
S0cy2a0.description: One of the two identical strands of a replicated chromosome. Formed prior to cell division.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

30cSfa0.title: Allelic heterogeneity
30cSfa0.description: A phenomenon in which different mutations of the same allele result in the same disease. Depending on the type of mutation, the respective phenotypic expression can vary from mild to serious. A common cause of variable penetrance and variable expressivity of genetic diseases.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

R0clfa0.title: True diverticulum
R0clfa0.description: An outpouching of a hollow viscus that contains all of the layers of the wall of the viscus (e.g., mucosa, muscular layer, serosa). Meckel diverticulum is an example of a true diverticulum.

i0cJfa0.title: Discounted fee-for-service
i0cJfa0.description: A fixed payment schedule with discounted prices for each individual service, negotiated between health care providers and payers (e.g., health insurance companies).

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payment models

Q0cufa0.title: Promyelocyte
Q0cufa0.description: A granulocytic precursor cell that develops from a myeloblast and evolves into a myelocyte. Usually found in the bone marrow.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

j0c_fa0.title: Safinamide
j0c_fa0.description: A selective inhibitor of monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) used to treat Parkinson disease. Decreases dopamine catabolism in the brain and prolongs the effect of dopamine.

P0cWTa0.title: Myelocyte
P0cWTa0.description: A granulocytic precursor cell that develops from a promyelocyte and evolves into a metamyelocyte. Found on peripheral blood smear of patients with chronic myelogenous leukemia or left shift (e.g., from acute inflammation).

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

media.title: Chronic myeloid leukemia on blood smear

40c3Ta0.title: Metamyelocyte
40c3Ta0.description: A granulocytic precursor cell that develops from a myelocyte and evolves into a band cell. Found on peripheral blood smear of patients with chronic myelogenous leukemia or left shift (e.g., from acute inflammation).

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

k0cmTa0.title: Diffusion (transport)
k0cmTa0.description: The movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration (i.e., down their concentration gradient). Does not require ATP.

O0cITa0.title: Leukocyte alkaline phosphatase
O0cITa0.description: An enzyme found in mature leukocytes. Staining of LAP on peripheral blood smear is used to calculate the LAP score. A high LAP score is associated with an increased number of mature white blood cells (e.g., from leukemoid reaction or myeloproliferative disorders); a low LAP score is associated with an increased number of immature white blood cells (e.g., from CML).

l0cvTa0.title: Active transport
l0cvTa0.description: The movement of molecules across a membrane from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration (i.e., against their concentration gradient). Further subdivided into primary active transport (which uses ATP) and secondary active transport (which uses another type of molecule's electrochemical gradient).

N0c-Ta0.title: Retroperitoneal organ
N0c-Ta0.description: An organ that is covered by parietal peritoneum on the anterior aspect and by adventitia on the posterior aspect. Includes the esophagus, lower rectum, anal canal, kidneys, ureters, adrenal glands, abdominal aorta, and inferior vena cava.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Intraperitoneal and extraperitoneal abdominal structures

m0cVga0.title: Tingible body macrophage
m0cVga0.description: A macrophage that has phagocytosed apoptotic debris. Found in germinal centers of lymphoid organs (e.g., lymph nodes, spleen). Associated with lymphomas and Castleman disease.

M0cMga0.title: Globoside
M0cMga0.description: A glycolipid found in the erythrocyte membrane. Plays important roles in P antigen function, cell communication, and cell adhesion.

n0c7ga0.title: Duffy antigen
n0c7ga0.description: A glycoprotein receptor found on red blood cells. Plasmodium vivax binds to Duffy antigens to invade RBCs and cause malaria. Antibodies against Duffy antigen can cause transfusion reactions and hemolytic disease of the newborn.

L0cwga0.title: Hemoglobin SC disease
L0cwga0.description: A variant of sickle cell disease caused by heterozygosity for hemoglobin S and hemoglobin C. Results in a phenotype more severe than sickle cell trait but not as severe as sickle cell disease (e.g., fewer acute sickling events).

o0c0Sa0.title: Enalaprilat
o0c0Sa0.description: The produg of ACE-inhibitor enalapril that may be used to treat hypertensive crisis, with the onset of action between 15-30 min following IV administration.

K0cUSa0.title: Subglottis
K0cUSa0.description: An anatomical region bounded superiorly by the vocal cords and inferiorly by the trachea.

J0csSa0.title: Global payment
J0csSa0.description: A health care payment model in which a fixed payment is given to a health care organization for the needs of a population of patients during a specified time period (e.g., monthly or yearly)

destinations.label: Health care system → Alternative payment models

q0cCSa0.title: Capitation
q0cCSa0.description: A health care payment model in which physicians receive a specified amount of compensation per patient during each payment period, regardless of the actual amount of health care utilized by the patient.

destinations.label: Health care system → Alternative payment models

I0cYha0.title: Fee-for-service
I0cYha0.description: A payment model in which health care providers are compensated for each individual service provided (e.g., individual laboratory tests, imaging studies, and procedures).

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payment models

G0cBha0.title: Polyclonal proliferation
G0cBha0.description: A normal response to an antigenic stimulus in which many B and T cells proliferate, which allows the immune system to recognize many different antigens and epitopes from a pathogen.

t0cX3a0.title: Fas ligand
t0cX3a0.description: A protein expressed by T lymphocytes that triggers apoptosis when bound to the Fas receptor of a target cell. Mediates the extrinsic pathway of apoptosis.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Apoptosis

F0cg3a0.title: Metalloproteinase
F0cg3a0.description: An enzyme that breaks down components of the extracellular matrix. Also involved in wound healing, remodeling, and scar formation. Includes alveolar elastase as well as collagenases, gelatinases, stromelysins, and matrilysins.

destinations.label: Wound healing → Phases of wound healing

80cO3a0.title: Fibrillin-1 gene
80cO3a0.description: A gene located on chromosome 15 that encodes a component of connective tissue microfibrils. Defects result in the production of abnormal elastin and cause Marfan syndrome.

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Etiology and classification

u0cp3a0.title: Collagenase
u0cp3a0.description: A matrix metalloproteinase involved in several physiologic functions, including immunity, wound healing, and scar formation. Dysregulation of collagenase results in destruction of the extracellular matrix (e.g., in gas gangrene). Injections of collagenase can be used in the treatment of Dupuytren contracture and to promote wound healing.

v0cA3a0.title: Growth hormone receptor antagonist
v0cA3a0.description: A class of drugs used to suppress excess growth hormone production for the treatment of acromegaly. Pegvisomant is the most widely used drug in the class.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

D0c1Ra0.title: Pegvisomant
D0c1Ra0.description: A growth hormone receptor antagonist used to treat acromegaly.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

w0chRa0.title: Neuropil
w0chRa0.description: A structure formed by a dense collection of axonal, dendritic, and glial cell processes.

C0cqRa0.title: Adult T cell leukemia-lymphoma
C0cqRa0.description: A rare but aggressive malignancy deriving from T-cells. It may either manifest as leukemia or lymphoma, with cutaneous lesions, enlarged body organs, and hypercalcemia. CD4-positive and CD25-positive lymphocytes can be identified via flow cytometry. Associated with the HTLV-1 virus.

x0cERa0.title: Acute HIV infection
x0cERa0.description: A syndrome of early HIV infection that consists of nonspecific manifestations, including fever, headache, weight loss, lymphadenopathy, sore throat, maculopapular rash, myalgia, and diarrhea. Most early HIV infections are asymptomatic.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Clinical features

A0cRia0.title: Ligand
A0cRia0.description: A chemical messenger that binds specifically to a receptor. Examples include proteins, steroids, small organic molecules (e.g., nitric oxide), hormones, and neurotransmitters.

_0c5ia0.title: Epithelial sodium channel
_0c5ia0.description: An ion channel responsible for secondary active transport of Na⁺ reabsorption in the collecting duct of the nephron, colon, and sweat glands. Blocked by the potassium-sparing diuretics amiloride and triamterene. Aldosterone increases the number of ENaC channels in the collecting duct.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Urine production

z0cria0.title: Gs protein coupled receptor
z0cria0.description: A transmembrane receptor that increases membrane adenylate cyclase activity when stimulated. Increased adenylate cyclase activity increases cyclic AMP synthesis, which in turn increases protein kinase A activity (cyclic AMP signal transduction pathway). Examples of Gs-coupled receptors include beta-adrenergic, dopamine-1, histamine-2, vasopressin-2, certain anterior pituitary hormones (e.g., FSH, LH, ACTH, MSH, TSH), CRH, hCG, GHRH, PTH, calcitonin, and glucagon. Certain toxins, (e.g., cholera toxin) also stimulate Gs-coupled receptors.

-0cDia0.title: Gi protein coupled receptor
-0cDia0.description: A transmembrane receptor that decreases membrane adenylate cyclase activity when stimulated. Decreased adenylate cyclase activity decreases cyclic AMP synthesis, which in turn decreases protein kinase A activity (cyclic AMP signal transduction pathway). Examples of Gi-coupled receptors include muscarinic 2, alpha-2 adrenergic, and dopamine-2 receptors. Certain toxins, e.g., pertussis toxin, work by inactivating Gi-coupled receptors.

ZacZQa0.title: Gq protein coupled receptor
ZacZQa0.description: A transmembrane receptor that increases membrane phospholipase C activity when stimulated (phosphatidylinositol signal transduction pathway). Phospholipase C increases the synthesis of diacylglycerol, which stimulates protein kinase C activity, and inositol triphosphate, which increases intracytoplasmic calcium concentration. Example of Gq-coupled receptors are histamine-1, alpha-1 adrenergic, vasopressin-1, muscarinic-1, muscarinic-3, GnRH, oxytocin, thyrotropin releasing hormone, angiotensin II, and gastrin receptors.

0aceQa0.title: Ras
0aceQa0.description: A monomeric, membrane-bound GTPase that activates signal transduction pathways such as the MAP kinase cascade, which leads to transcription of target genes for cell growth and proliferation. The ras genes (KRas, NRas, HRas), are proto-oncogenes, meaning mutations in them can cause uninhibited production of the ras protein, which commonly leads to tumor formation.

aacQQa0.title: Signal amplification
aacQQa0.description: Increase in the number of signaling molecules at every step of a signal cascade.

YacnQa0.title: UBE3A
YacnQa0.description: A gene on chromosome 15. Deletions or mutations are associated with Angelman syndrome.

destinations.label: Rare inherited syndromes → Prader-Willi syndrome and Angelman syndrome

bacHQa0.title: Euploidy
bacHQa0.description: A term in genetics indicating that the chromosome number is an exact multiple of a haploid set.

Xac9Qa0.title: Ovotesticular disorder of sexual development
Xac9Qa0.description: A rare disorder characterized by the presence of both ovarian and testicular tissues. Most commonly associated with a 46,XX karyotype or 46,XX/46,XY mosaicism.

destinations.label: Differences (disorders) of sex development → Ovotesticular disorder of sex development

cacaja0.title: Beta-adrenergic agonist
cacaja0.description: A class of drugs that bind to and activate β-receptors in a selective or nonselective manner. Exerts effects on cardiac muscle (increased inotropy and chronotropy), smooth muscle (relaxation or contraction depending on the receptor), and the liver (β2 stimulation of glycogenolysis).

dacoja0.title: Two-point discrimination
dacoja0.description: A test to assess a patient's sensory innervation. The ability to identify two discrete points that are ≤ 5 mm apart suggests intact sensory innervation.

VacGja0.title: Glabrous skin
VacGja0.description: An area of skin that does not contain hair follicles (e.g., over the palms and soles).

eacxja0.title: Cerebellum
eacxja0.description: The part of the hindbrain that lies within the posterior cranial fossa, inferior to the occipital lobes and dorsal to the brainstem. Consists of three lobes (the anterior, posterior, and flocculonodular lobe). Involved in the coordination of movement, proprioception, and balance.

2acTPa0.title: Signal transducer and activator of transcription protein family
2acTPa0.description: A family of transcription factors activated by Janus kinases. STAT proteins regulate several cellular functions, including the activity of cytokines and growth factors, and are involved in the proliferation of myeloid cells.

fackPa0.title: Beta-adrenergic receptor
fackPa0.description: A group of Gs-protein-coupled receptors. β1 receptor stimulation increases heart rate and contractility, renin release from the juxtaglomerular apparatus, and lipolysis. β2 receptor stimulation increases smooth muscle relaxation in blood vessels, bronchioles, and uterus, insulin release from pancreatic beta cells, glycogenolysis and lipolysis, potassium uptake by cells, and aqueous humor production.  β3 receptor stimulation increases lipolysis, thermogenesis, and detrusor relaxation.

Tac6Pa0.title: Phosphatidylinositide 3-kinases
Tac6Pa0.description: A kinase involved in the signal transduction system of many cellular functions (e.g., cell migration, metabolism, proliferation, and regulation of apoptosis).

SacyPa0.title: Protraction
SacyPa0.description: The action of moving a part of the body anteriorly.

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

hacc4a0.title: Retraction
hacc4a0.description: The action of moving a part of the body posteriorly.

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

4ac3ka0.title: Ziehl-Neelsen stain
4ac3ka0.description: An acid-fast stain, which can be used to identify organisms that have high mycolic acid content (e.g., Mycobacteria, Nocardia). Stained structures typically appear red.

5aciOa0.title: Intrinsic pathway (apoptosis)
5aciOa0.description: A type of programmed cell death regulated by Bcl-2 proteins. Initiated by BAX and BAK, which create pores in the mitochondrial membraneŽ that lead to the release of cytochrome C from the inner mitochondrial membrane into the cytoplasmŽ. This activates caspases that facilitate apoptosis.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Apoptosis

MacMOa0.title: Extrinsic pathway (apoptosis)
MacMOa0.description: A type of programmed cell death regulated by cytotoxic T cell activity and ligand receptor interactions (e.g., Fas and FasL, TNF-α). Activation results in caspase activity that facilitates apoptosis.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Apoptosis

LacwOa0.title: GABA-A receptor
LacwOa0.description: An inhibitory, ligand-gated ion channel in the brain. Consists of 5 subunits that surround a central ion channel that is selective for chloride ions. Targeted by benzodiazepines and barbiturates. Activation of the receptor opens the channel and enables chloride ions to flow across the cell membrane, which leads to hyperpolarization of postsynaptic neurons.

oac0la0.title: Superior petrosal sinuses
oac0la0.description: A pair of lateral dural venous sinuses that connect the cavernous sinuses with the transverse sinuses bilaterally. Lie on the petrous temporal bone. Receive venous drainage from the inferior cerebral veins, cerebellar veins, and labyrinthine veins (from the inner ear).

KacUla0.title: Inferior petrosal sinuses
KacUla0.description: A pair of lateral dural venous sinuses that receive venous drainage from the cavernous sinus and drain into the internal jugular vein. As it drains the cavernous sinus, it also receives venous drainage from the pituitary gland and is thus used as the site of venous sampling of ACTH concentration in the workup of Cushing disease.

6acjla0.title: Transverse sinuses
