6acjla0.description: A pair of inferolateral dural venous sinuses that lie on the occipital bone. Receive venous drainage from the confluence of sinuses (e.g., the superior sagittal sinus, straight sinus, and occipital sinus) and drain into the sigmoid sinuses.

pacLla0.title: Dural venous sinuses
pacLla0.description: A collection of valveless venous channels that lie between the two layers of the dura mater. Receive venous drainage from the brain and empty into the internal jugular vein.

Jacsla0.title: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease
Jacsla0.description: A group of aggressive and rapidly progressive complications of solid organ transplantation and allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Manifests with variable, nonspecific symptoms (e.g., fever, weight loss, fatigue, lymphadenopathy). Associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection of B cells. Can regress with reduction of immunosuppression.

qacCla0.title: Inferior olivary nucleus
qacCla0.description: A structure in the medulla oblongata that relays motor and sensory information to the cerebellum to facilitate motor coordination. Input sources include the red nucleus, cortex, spinal cord, superior colliculus, and regulatory cerebellar fibers. Axons that arise from the inferior olives cross in the medulla and ascend as climbing fibers in the contralateral inferior cerebellar peduncle.

7ac4Na0.title: Myositis
7ac4Na0.description: An inflammation of muscle tissue, which typically manifests with fatigue and muscle weakness. Leads to elevated serum creatinine kinase concentration. Etiologies include inflammatory conditions and infections.

HacKNa0.title: Periorbital edema
HacKNa0.description: Swelling of the soft tissues that surround the orbital cavity. Usually secondary to trauma, inflammation, protein deficiency (e.g., nephrotic syndrome), or malignancy.

sactNa0.title: Early term infant
sactNa0.description: A live birth that occurs between 37 0/7 weeks and 38 6/7 weeks of gestation.

uacpma0.title: Plasmacytoid cells
uacpma0.description: Rare immune cells found in blood and lymph tissues that release large amounts of interferon type 1 in response to viral infections. They have also been implicated in exacerbating autoimmune diseases such as SLE.

wach5a0.title: Amastigote
wach5a0.description: A eukaryotic protist cell without visible external cilia or flagella that describes a Hemoflagellate intracellular lifecycle phase of the parasite in its vertebrate host.

destinations.label: General parasitology → Tissue and blood protozoa

9acN5a0.title: Triatomines
9acN5a0.description: A subfamily of insects that contains many species that act as vectors of the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, which causes Chagas disease. Often bites on the face and sheds feces that contain T. cruzi, which then invade the host through the bite wound.

Cacq5a0.title: Type 2 collagen
Cacq5a0.description: The most abundant type of collagen in articular and hyaline cartilage. Also found in the vitreous body and nucleus pulposus.

xacE5a0.title: Trypomastigote
xacE5a0.description: An infective form of the Trypanosoma brucei and Trypanosoma cruzi parasites. Has a characteristic C shape that can be found on peripheral blood smear of infected patients.

destinations.label: General parasitology → Tissue and blood protozoa

YYcnna0.title: Tat protein
YYcnna0.description: A protein produced by HIV that upregulates gene transcription.

XYc9na0.title: Tat gene
XYc9na0.description: A gene that encodes tat protein (transactivator protein), which is involved in viral transcription of HIV.

1Yc2La0.title: Cyclin B
1Yc2La0.description: A component of mitosis promoting factor, a cyclin-CDK complex that regulates the G2 checkpoint of the cell cycle.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

WYcPLa0.title: Quiescent cell
WYcPLa0.description: A cell type that remains mostly in the G0 phase and only enters the G1 phase when stimulated by mitogenic stimuli. Examples include cells in exocrine and endocrine glands, hepatocytes, peripheral blood lymphocytes, renal tubular epithelium, smooth muscle cells, and periosteal cells.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

dYcoLa0.title: Central chromatolysis
dYcoLa0.description: A reaction of a neuronal cell body in response to an axonal injury; it is characterized by swelling of the neuronal body, dispersion of the Nissl bodies, and displacement of the nucleus to the periphery. These changes reflect an increase in the protein synthesis in an effort to restore the integrity of the damaged axon.

destinations.label: Peripheral nerve injuries → Types of nerve damage

VYcGLa0.title: Diphtheroids
VYcGLa0.description: A group of aerobic, pleomorphic, gram-positive bacilli. Closely related to Corynebacterium diphtheriae but stain more uniformly and lack metachromatic granules. Usually are commensals of the skin and mucous membranes but can cause nosocomial infections.

eYcxLa0.title: Reactive astrogliosis
eYcxLa0.description: A collection of nonspecific, reactive changes (e.g., proliferation, hypertrophy) to astrocytes in response to CNS damage.

UYcboa0.title: Permanent cell
UYcboa0.description: A cell type that remains in the G0 phase of the cell cycle. Due to an inability to proliferate, they require stem cells for regeneration or are replaced by fibrous connective tissue when destroyed. Examples include neurons, skeletal and cardiac myocytes, erythrocytes, granulocytes, platelets, and osteocytes.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

2YcToa0.title: Sabouraud agar
2YcToa0.description: A growth medium that contains dextrose and peptones. Used to culture dermatophytes and other fungi.

fYckoa0.title: Penicillinase
fYckoa0.description: A type of beta-lactamase that degrades the beta-lactam ring of penicillin antibiotics. Production by bacteria confers antibacterial resistance.

TYc6oa0.title: Löwenstein-Jensen agar
TYc6oa0.description: A growth medium used to culture Mycobacterium species. Includes components that inhibit the growth of gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria. Evidence of mycobacterial growth can take as long as 8 weeks.

gYcFoa0.title: Cowpox
gYcFoa0.description: A cutaneous infection caused by cowpox virus that typically manifests with tender, ulcerating papulovesicles. Can be associated with localized lymphadenopathy, fever, and flu-like symptoms. Most commonly transmitted by cats and rodents.

SYcyoa0.title: Influenza A virus
SYcyoa0.description: The main causal pathogen of influenza. Compared to other subtypes of influenzavirus, it has a greater propensity for antigenic changes (drift and shift) in its envelope glycoproteins (hemagglutinin and neuraminidase).

hYccKa0.title: Bunyaviridae
hYccKa0.description: A group of negative-sense, ssRNA viruses with 3 segments that have a pseudo-circular structure. In 2017, the family bunyaviridae was taxonomically reclassified into the order bunyavirales. Responsible for causing California encephalitis, Sandfly/Rift Valley fevers, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever and Hantavirus associated infections.

RYclKa0.title: Paramyxovirus
RYclKa0.description: A family of enveloped viruses with a nonsegmented, single-stranded RNA structure. Includes parainfluenza virus, measles virus, and mumps virus.

iYcJKa0.title: Flavivirus
iYcJKa0.description: A family of enveloped viruses with a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA structure. Includes hepatitis C virus, yellow fever virus, dengue fever virus, St. Louis encephalitis virus, West Nile virus, and Zika virus.

jYc_Ka0.title: Hepadnaviridae
jYc_Ka0.description: A group of enveloped viruses with a circular, partially double-stranded DNA structure. Hepatitis B virus is a hepadnavirus.

kYcm6a0.title: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis
kYcm6a0.description: A condition caused by an arenavirus and transmitted by exposure to the urine or feces of rodents. Manifestations include an influenza-like illness, headache, meningismus, and typical findings in cerebrospinal fluid of viral meningitis (e.g., variable cell count with lymphocytic predominance).

NYc-6a0.title: RNA primase
NYc-6a0.description: An enzyme involved in DNA synthesis. RNA primase attaches to the lagging strang of DNA and synthesizes an RNA primer in the 5'→3' direction. DNA polymerase can then attach to this primer and synthesize DNA complementary to the lagging strand.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA replication

mYcVpa0.title: Saprophyte
mYcVpa0.description: An organism that lives on and obtains nutrients from dead organic matter (e.g., fungi).

LYcwpa0.title: Leukotriene D4
LYcwpa0.description: A product of eicosanoid synthesis that functions to contract smooth muscle, which results in bronchoconstriction and vasoconstriction. Receptors for this leukotriene are targeted by anti-asthmatic agents (e.g., montelukast).

KYcUJa0.title: Immunodeficiency with thymoma
KYcUJa0.description: A rare, primary immunodeficiency that occurs in adults. Characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia, low levels of B cells, and benign thymoma.

6YcjJa0.title: Caveolae
6YcjJa0.description: Invaginations in the sarcolemma (cell membrane) of smooth muscle cells that are located close to the sarcoplasmic reticulum. It contains various receptors and ion channels involved in signal transduction.

JYcsJa0.title: Terminal cisterna
JYcsJa0.description: The part of the sarcoplasmic reticulum in muscle cells that encircle myofibrils and lie adjacent to T-tubules. In skeletal muscles, two terminal cisternae and a T-tubule form a triad, while in cardiac muscle, one terminal cisterna and a T-tubule form a diad. The close proximity of T-tubules and terminal cisternae allows for direct transmission of action potentials to the sarcoplasmic reticulum, enabling quick release of Ca2+ for muscle contraction.

qYcCJa0.title: Caldesmon
qYcCJa0.description: A protein that binds actin, myosin, calmodulin, and tropomyosin. Involved in cytoskeletal function (e.g., cell motility) and regulation of smooth muscle contraction.

IYcYqa0.title: Calponin
IYcYqa0.description: A protein found in smooth muscle cells that binds to actin, tropomyosin, and calmodulin. Regulates muscle contraction by blocking myosin-binding sites.

sYctqa0.title: Dihydropyridine receptor
sYctqa0.description: An L-type, voltage-gated calcium channel found in the T-tubules of skeletal muscle. Responds to voltage changes (e.g., from muscle cell depolarization) and facilitates the release of intracellular calcium stored in the sarcoplasmic reticulum, which leads to skeletal muscle contraction.

GYcBqa0.title: Phosphagen system
GYcBqa0.description: A group of high-energy phosphate compounds that allow muscle cells to maintain a reserve of high-energy phosphates in the form of phosphocreatine. Provide immediate but limited energy for muscle tissue during short bursts of rapid movement. Synthesized from arginine and glycine.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Overview

tYcXIa0.title: DNAI1 gene
tYcXIa0.description: A gene on chromosome 9 that encodes an important component of the dynein complex. Mutations in this are associated with primary ciliary dyskinesia.

FYcgIa0.title: Creatine
FYcgIa0.description: An organic acid synthesized in the kidneys and liver. Creatine phosphate is as an important short-term energy source in muscle cells that replenishes ATP stores by donating phosphate groups. Converted to creatinine through removal of phosphate residues and cyclization.

uYcpIa0.title: Notogenesis
uYcpIa0.description: the process in which the notochord arises from midline mesoderm in the 3rd-4th week of embryonic development.

EYc8Ia0.title: Vestibular complex
EYc8Ia0.description: A collection of neurons located in the pons and medulla that form the cranial origin of the vestibular nerve. Receives information from the inner ear and sends efferents to the cerebellum, spinal cord, cranial nerves III, IV, and VI (responsible for extraocular movements), and the thalamus for the coordination of balance.

vYcAIa0.title: Reticular formation
vYcAIa0.description: A network of neurons in the brainstem that plays a vital role in the control of consciousness, arousal, autonomic functions (e.g., respiration. hemodynamics), and motor, sensory, and visceral functions. Damage to the reticular formation can cause coma and death.

DYc1ra0.title: Rev protein
DYc1ra0.description: A regulatory protein of HIV involved in the translocation of unspliced and incompletely spliced mRNAs (that encode structural proteins) from the nucleus to the cytoplasm

wYchra0.title: Rev gene
wYchra0.description: An HIV gene that encodes for rev protein, which regulates translocation of unspliced and incompletely spliced mRNAs.

9YcNra0.title: Env gene
9YcNra0.description: A viral gene that encodes envelope proteins.

CYcqra0.title: Bone marrow
CYcqra0.description: The spongy, soft tissue that fills the hollow spaces within cancellous (spongy) bone. Composed of stromal cells and stem cells. Functions include hematopoiesis, filtration of aging erythrocytes, and storage of immune cells.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Bone marrow and hematopoiesis

xYcEra0.title: Gag gene
xYcEra0.description: The gag gene (group-specific antigen gene) codes for core structural proteins of retroviruses such as human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). In HIV, the gag gene codes for matrix proteins and nucleocapsid proteins (e.g., p24 capsid protein).

BYczra0.title: Internal urethral sphincter
BYczra0.description: A circular smooth muscle that surrounds the neck of the bladder where the urethra begins, preventing the release of urine. Controlled by the sympathetic nervous system.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

yYcd7a0.title: Superficial epigastric artery
yYcd7a0.description: A branch of the femoral artery that arises just below the inguinal ligament and runs superiorly in the superficial fascia of the abdominal wall. Anastomoses with the inferior epigastric artery. Supplies the anterior abdominal wall and skin of the abdomen.

destinations.label: Anterior abdominal wall → Vasculature and innervation

AYcR7a0.title: pol gene
AYcR7a0.description: A genome that encodes the viral enzymes protease, reverse transcriptase, and integrase.

-YcD7a0.title: Rectovesical space
-YcD7a0.description: An anatomic space in the peritoneal cavity located posterior to the lower portion of the bladder and the prostate gland, inferior to the rectovesical pouch. Divided into three regions by the rectoprostatic fascia of Denonvillier.

abcQHa0.title: Carotid sheath
abcQHa0.description: The three layers of the deep cervical fascia that envelop the common carotid artery, the internal carotid artery, the internal jugular vein, and the vagus nerve.

bbcHHa0.title: Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis
bbcHHa0.description: A rare condition in which a benign lipidic neoplasm overgrows within the kidney. It is theorized that infection (usually with E. coli or Proteus) is the causative factor, and an inappropriate host inflammatory response perpetuates the condition. Diagnosis is made with imaging showing a mass and a confirmatory biopsy. Surgery is often curative.

WbcPsa0.title: Caroticotympanic artery
WbcPsa0.description: The first intracranial branch of the internal carotid artery that enters the middle ear cavity and anastomoses with the inferior tympanic artery. Supplies the structures of the middle ear.

dbcosa0.title: Artery of the pterygoid canal
dbcosa0.description: A small artery that lies in the pterygoid canal with the pterygoid nerve. May arise either from the internal carotid artery or the maxillary branch of the external carotid artery. Supplies the eustachian tube.

VbcGsa0.title: Meningohypophyseal trunk
VbcGsa0.description: A branch of the internal carotid artery that is also known as the posterior trunk. Is the arterial supply to the inferior part of the pituitary gland, the tentorium cerebelli, and cranial nerves III, IV, V, and VI.

ebcxsa0.title: Swiss cheese model of error causation
ebcxsa0.description: A model used to understand how errors occur in complex systems. Slices of Swiss cheese are an analogy for the components of these complex systems. Each slice represents a sub-system in which there are vulnerabilities with the potential for an error to occur (the holes in the Swiss cheese). It is only when the holes of all the slices of cheese align that harm occurs.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Analysis of medical error

UbcbGa0.title: Pterygoid canal
UbcbGa0.description: A foramen in the greater wing of the sphenoid bone that transmits the artery and nerve of the pterygoid canal from the middle cranial fossa to the pterygopalatine fossa.

fbckGa0.title: Plan, do, study, act cycle
fbckGa0.description: A model used to improve health care quality. The “Plan” phase consists of defining an area that needs improvement and planning potential interventions to bring about a corrective change. The “Do” phase consists of testing the intervention. The “Study” phase consists of assessing the impact of the intervention on quality of health care. The “Act” phase consists of implementing the new intervention if the previous test showed a positive impact on health care quality or restarting the cycle if the results were negative or had no significant impact.

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

gbcFGa0.title: SMART criteria
gbcFGa0.description: A tool used to assist in the setting of objectives. Goals should be SMART: Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Relevant, and Time-limited.

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

hbccta0.title: Anterior spinal artery
hbccta0.description: An artery formed by the union of the branches of the vertebral artery. Lies in the anterior median fissure of the spinal cord and supplies the parts of the spinal cord that carry the spinal motor tracts.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

3bcSta0.title: Posterior spinal arteries
3bcSta0.description: A pair of arteries that supply the dorsal aspect of the spinal cord that carry the tracts of proprioception and vibration sense. Most commonly arise from the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (and less commonly the vertebral artery).

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

media.title: Arterial supply territories of the spinal cord

Rbclta0.title: Eribulin
Rbclta0.description: A nontaxane microtubule inhibitor that inhibits the growth phase of the microtubule. Arrests the cell cycle at the G2/M phase. Used to treat breast cancer and liposarcoma.

ibcJta0.title: Cell cycle-nonspecific antineoplastic agents
ibcJta0.description: A class of antineoplastic drugs that acts on cells during all phases of the cell cycle (i.e., when cells are traversing the cell cycle and when they are in the G0 phase). Examples include platinum agents (e.g., cisplatin) and alkylating agents (e.g., busulfan).

Qbcuta0.title: Antitumor antibiotics
Qbcuta0.description: A heterogeneous class of antineoplastic drugs interfere with cell division. They are cell-cycle specific antineoplastic agents that act during multiple phases of the cell cycle. Examples include bleomycin, dactinomycin, and doxorubicin.

PbcWFa0.title: Alpha-thalassemia minima
PbcWFa0.description: A type of alpha thalassemia in which there is a defect in 1 of the 4 alleles responsible for coding of the α-globin chains. Patients are asymptomatic and have normal HbA, HbA2, and HbF.

4bc3Fa0.title: Aldesleukin
4bc3Fa0.description: A recombination form of interleukin-2 that stimulates the proliferation and activation of T cells, B cells, NK cells, and thymocytes. Can stimulate lymphokine-activated killer cells and tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. Used to treat metastatic melanoma and metastatic renal cell carcinoma.

kbcmFa0.title: Epoetin alfa
kbcmFa0.description: A recombinant form of erythropoietin used to stimulate the erythroid cell lineage in the setting of chronic kidney disease-induced anemia or drug-induced anemia.

ObcIFa0.title: Sargramostim
ObcIFa0.description: A colony-stimulating factor that stimulates proliferation, differentiation, and activity of neutrophils, eosinophils, monocytes, and macrophages. Used in the management of chemotherapy-induced neutropenia.

lbcvFa0.title: Endocrine signaling
lbcvFa0.description: A form of cellular signalling in which a cell produces a chemical messenger (e.g. hormones or cytokines) that enters the bloodstream and exerts its effects on cells distant from the site of secretion.

Nbc-Fa0.title: Merkel cell carcinoma
Nbc-Fa0.description: A rare, rapidly progressive neuroendocrine neoplasm that typically manifests as a painless, firm, nontender, red-blue nodule on the head or neck. Some cases are associated with Merkel cell polyomavirus infection.

destinations.label: Collection of dermatological disorders → Erythema ab igne

5bci8a0.title: Coagulase-negative staphylococci
5bci8a0.description: A class of staphylococci that lack coagulase, which distinguishes them from Staphylococcus aureus. A major part of normal skin flora but can cause catheter-associated bloodstream infections, endocarditis, infections of orthopedic prostheses, and surgical site infections. S. epidermidis is the most common species.

MbcM8a0.title: Shunt fraction
MbcM8a0.description: An estimate of the amount of venous blood that bypasses oxygenation. Calculated to monitor pulmonary oxygenation in critically ill patients.

nbc78a0.title: Anti-inflammatory cytokines
nbc78a0.description: A group of immunomodulatory proteins that regulate the proinflammatory cytokine response to a trigger (e.g., infection, injury, ischemia). Includes interleukins 4, 5, 10, 11, and 13 as well as TGF-β.

media.title: Effects of T-helper cells in secondary lymphatic organs

Lbcw8a0.title: Osmotic pressure
Lbcw8a0.description: The minimum pressure that must be applied to prevent the flow of a solvent across a semi-permeable membrane. Directly proportional to the concentration of solute particles in the solvent; pure solvent from a lower concentration solute is drawn across a semipermeable membrane into a higher concentration solute. In humans, this is primarily driven by colloid (e.g., albumin).

IbcYEa0.title: Umami
IbcYEa0.description: A type of taste that can be triggered by various amino acids (e.g., glutamate, aspartate). Increases appetite for protein-rich foods.

sbctEa0.title: Anthrax toxin
sbctEa0.description: An exotoxin secreted by B. anthracis. Consists of lethal factor, edema factor, and a protective antigen that facilitates entry into host cells.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

GbcBEa0.title: Lethal factor
GbcBEa0.description: A component of the anthrax toxin that disrupts cell signaling pathways (e.g., mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway), which results in cellular death.

Fbcgva0.title: Löffler medium
Fbcgva0.description: A growth medium used to cultivate Corynebacterium diphteriae.

8bcOva0.title: Cystine-tellurite agar
8bcOva0.description: A medium used to grow Corynebacterium diphteriae. Contains animal tissue, sodium chloride, L-cystine, and sodium thiosulfate. The differentiation between C. diphtheriae and other diphtheroids is based on the capacity of C. diphtheriae to produce brown-black halos around the colonies.

vbcAva0.title: Regan-Lowe charcoal agar
vbcAva0.description: A culture medium that favors the growth of Bordetella species. Contains charcoal, blood, and cephalexin to inhibit other bacterial growth.

wbchDa0.title: Central sulcus
wbchDa0.description: sulcus that separates the frontal and parietal lobes.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

media.title: Lateral view of the cerebral lobes

ybcdwa0.title: Lactose fermenter
ybcdwa0.description: A property of several bacterial species that is detected on selective growth medium (most commonly MacConkey agar). The ability to ferment lactose leads to the production of acidic byproducts that stains the colonies pink. Examples of lactose-fermenting bacteria include E. coli and Klebsiella.

AbcRwa0.title: Pseudohyperkalemia
AbcRwa0.description: A falsely elevated potassium concentration in a laboratory report. Frequently caused by the lysis of erythrocytes either during or after the collection of the blood sample (e.g., due to prolonged use of a tourniquet or delayed analysis of the sample).

ZXcZ9a0.title: Prosencephalon
ZXcZ9a0.description: A primary brain vesicle that gives rise to the telencephalon and diencephalon. Arises from the cranial part of the neural tube during the 4th week of embryonic development.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Embryology of the brain

media.title: Regions of the brain with embryological derivation

0Xce9a0.title: Rhombencephalon
0Xce9a0.description: A primary brain vesicle that gives rise to the metencephalon and myelencephalon. Arises from the cranial part of the neural tube during the 4th week of embryonic development.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Embryology of the brain

media.title: Regions of the brain with embryological derivation

aXcQ9a0.title: Telencephalon
aXcQ9a0.description: A secondary brain vesicle that arises during the 5th week of embryonic development from the prosencephalon. Gives rise to the cerebral hemispheres and parts of the basal ganglia.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Embryology of the brain

media.title: Regions of the brain with embryological derivation
Anatomical illustration of the thalamus and hypothalamus

YXcn9a0.title: Metencephalon
YXcn9a0.description: A secondary brain vesicle that arises during the 5th week of embryonic development from the rhombencephalon. Gives rise to the pons, cerebellum, and cranial part of the 4th ventricle.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Embryology of the brain

media.title: Regions of the brain with embryological derivation

bXcH9a0.title: Myelencephalon
bXcH9a0.description: A secondary brain vesicle that arises during the 5th week of embryonic development from the rhombencephalon. Gives rise to the medulla oblongata and the caudal part of the 4th ventricle.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Embryology of the brain

media.title: Regions of the brain with embryological derivation

2XcTxa0.title: Onchocerca volvulus
2XcTxa0.description: A filarial parasite responsible for onchocerciasis, or 'river blindness.' Transmitted from the black fly (Simulium spp.) to humans, where adult filarial worms develop before microfilariae are released into the circulation.

fXckxa0.title: Onchocerciasis
fXckxa0.description: A parasitic disease also known as river blindness. Caused by Onchocerca volvulus. Larvae are inoculated when the black fly (Simulum spp.) bites. Adult worms develop in the human host before releasing microfilariae into the circulation. Inflammation in response to the microfilariae causes widespread scarring. Ocular involvement may result in blindness. The second most common cause of infection-related blindness, after trachoma.

TXc6xa0.title: Diethylcarbamazine
TXc6xa0.description: An antihelminthic drug used to treat loiasis and lymphatic filariasis (e.g., from Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia malayi, Brugia timori).

3XcSBa0.title: Anterior choroidal artery
3XcSBa0.description: A branch of the internal carotid artery that lies just lateral to the optic tract and ends in the choroidal fissure. It supplies the optic tract, lateral geniculate nuclei, a part of the thalamus and hippocampus, and posterior limb of the internal capsule.

iXcJBa0.title: Schistosoma haematobium
iXcJBa0.description: A parasitic blood fluke endemic to sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East, and the southern Arabian Peninsula. Causes schistosomiasis (mainly genitourinary tract disease) after cercariae from snails penetrate the skin, mature into adults in the liver, and migrate to the vesical venous plexus. Its egg has a terminal spine. Infection is associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder and pulmonary hypertension.

kXcmya0.title: Neoplasia
kXcmya0.description: The process of abnormal, excessive proliferation of tissue. Can be benign or malignant.

qXcC_a0.title: R0
qXcC_a0.description:
A term that can refer to:
1. A resection margin of healthy tissue around a tumor indicating complete removal (both microscopically and macroscopically).
2. Abbreviation of basic reproduction number, an epidemiological value for evaluating infectivity that varies depending on the ability of the virus to be transmitted.

GXcBza0.title: Steatosis
GXcBza0.description: The accumulation of excess fat in cells, usually hepatocytes (i.e., hepatic steatosis). Can also occur in other tissues, including muscle, the kidneys, and the heart.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cellular inclusions

FXcg-a0.title: Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
FXcg-a0.description: The movement of the mitral valve towards the ventricular septum during systole. In cases of septal hypertrophy, this facilitates contact between the mitral valve and the septum, which results in left ventricular outflow obstruction. Commonly seen in patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy.

8XcO-a0.title: Congenital long QT syndrome
8XcO-a0.description: An inherited cardiac condition in which the QT interval (ventricular depolarization and repolarization) is prolonged. Arises from mutations in genes that encode potassium channels within myocytes. Most patients remain asymptomatic until they develop syncope, seizures, and/or life-threatening arrhythmias, including torsades de pointes and ventricular fibrillation.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cell injury

EXc8-a0.title: Polar body
EXc8-a0.description: A cellular byproduct of the meiotic division of an oocyte.

destinations.label: Basics of embryology → Germ cell development (gametogenesis)

DXc1ZY0.title: Field effect
DXc1ZY0.description: An area in which cellular and molecular alterations result in normal cells being replaced with precancerous cells, predisposing to the development of neoplasms in that area.

9XcNZY0.title: Giemsa staining
9XcNZY0.description: A histologic stain used to detect various bacteria (e.g., Rickettsia, Chlamydia, Borrelia) and protozoa (e.g., Trypanosomes, Plasmodia) on blood smear or bone marrow smear.

yXcd0Y0.title: Sterilization (microbiology)
yXcd0Y0.description: A technique used to destroy all microbial life (including spores) on the surface of an object or in a fluid. Examples include steam sterilization (autoclave) and dry air sterilization.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

accQaY0.title: Pasteurization
accQaY0.description: The process of heating food (e.g., milk, fruit juices), usually to 60-70°C, to destroy pathogens and extend product shelf life. Does not destroy heat-resistant spores.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

bccHaY0.title: Hydrogen peroxide
bccHaY0.description: An oxidizing agent and disinfectant that can produce hydroxyl free radicals that damage essential cell components, including lipids, proteins, and DNA.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

cccaYY0.title: Quaternary ammonium compound
cccaYY0.description: An ammonium agent that, at high concentrations, denatures proteins and disrupts cytoplasmic membranes. Can be used as an antiseptic. At lower concentrations, can be used as a preservative in eye drops.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

WccPYY0.title: Isolation precautions
WccPYY0.description: A series of measures taken to prevent the spread of infectious diseases when standard precautions are not sufficient to halt the spread of infection. Includes contact precautions, droplet precautions, and airborne precautions.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Isolation precautions

dccoYY0.title: Droplet precautions
dccoYY0.description: A set of measures implemented for the care of patients with suspected or confirmed infection with pathogens that are spread via droplet transmission (e.g., N. meningitides, B. pertussis, influenza). Includes placing patients in single rooms, use of surgical masks by infected patients during transport; and the use of surgical masks by health care providers when within 3–6 feet of the patient. Always performed in addition to standard precautions.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Isolation precautions

VccGYY0.title: Airborne precautions
VccGYY0.description: A set of measures implemented to reduce the transmission of airborne infections (e.g., tuberculosis, measles, varicella). Includes placing patients in airborne infection isolation rooms, use of surgical masks by infected patients during transport, and the use of N95 respirators by health care providers caring for the patient. Always performed in addition to standard precautions.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Isolation precautions

2ccTbY0.title: Vestibulotoxicity
2ccTbY0.description: A dysfunction of the cochleovestibular system of the inner ear that results in disorders of balance.

fcckbY0.title: Fas/FasL
fcckbY0.description: A molecular complex that triggers the extrinsic pathway of apoptosis by activating caspases. Also involved in negative selection in the thymic medulla.

Tcc6bY0.title: Bax
Tcc6bY0.description: A protein of the bcl-2 family that serves as a proapoptotic regulator of the intrinsic pathway of apoptosis.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Apoptosis

gccFbY0.title: Paraganglioma
gccFbY0.description: A rare neuroendocrine neoplasm arising from neural crest cells, located in autonomic ganglia (extra-adrenal paraganglioma) or the adrenal medulla (pheochromocytoma). May produce catecholamines.

SccybY0.title: Tapentadol
SccybY0.description: An analgesic that binds to μ-opioid receptors and inhibits the reuptake of norepinephrine to inhibit ascending pain pathways. Used to treat neuropathic pain.

jcc_XY0.title: True ribs
jcc_XY0.description: A rib that directly connects to the sternum via costal cartilage. Ribs 1-7 are considered true ribs.

PccWcY0.title: False ribs
PccWcY0.description: A rib that does not directly connect to the sternum. Ribs 8-12 are considered false ribs.

kccmcY0.title: Omphalomesenteric duct cyst
kccmcY0.description: A cyst that forms due to failed obliteration of the omphalomesenteric duct, which can lead to small bowel obstruction if bowel twists around the cyst.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The umbilical cord

OccIcY0.title: Povidone-iodine
OccIcY0.description: A commonly used preoperative antiseptic and oxidizing halogen-releasing agent that works by penetrating the cell in order to disrupt protein and nucleic acid structure as well as nucleic acid synthesis.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

Ncc-cY0.title: Mesolimbic
Ncc-cY0.description: A dopaminergic pathway in the brain that connects the ventral tegmental area of the midbrain and the ventral striatum (nucleus accumbens and olfactory tubercle). Controls the reward system of the brain. Overstimulation of this pathway can cause positive symptoms (e.g., hallucinations). It is the target of antipsychotic drugs in the treatment of schizophrenia.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

mccV1Y0.title: Mesocortical pathway
mccV1Y0.description: A dopaminergic pathway in the brain that travels from the ventral area to the prefrontal cortex. Involved in executive functions. Hypoactivity in this pathway is seen in patients with negative symptoms of psychosis.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

MccM1Y0.title: HLA-DR4
MccM1Y0.description: An allele of class II major histocompatibility complex that is associated with a variety of autoimmune disorders, including rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes mellitus, and Addison disease.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → Immune tolerance and autoimmunity

occ0WY0.title: Basal vein
occ0WY0.description: Paired paramedian deep cerebral veins that drain the temporal lobes and empty into the great cerebral vein of Galen

pccLWY0.title: Sebum
pccLWY0.description: A substance composed of lipids that is secreted by sebaceous glands into the follicular duct of the pilosebaceous unit. Has photoprotective, antimicrobial, antioxidant, lubricant, and hydrophobic properties.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Skin appendage

JccsWY0.title: Superficial thrombophlebitis of the breast
JccsWY0.description: A rare, self-limited condition characterized by thickening, pain, and erythema of the superficial veins of the breast and/or anterior chest wall. Can occur after surgery, radiation therapy, and trauma.

qccCWY0.title: Inferior medial pontine syndrome
qccCWY0.description: A neurologic condition caused by inferior medial pontine infarction, which results from occlusion of the circumferential branches of the basilar artery. Manifestations include ipsilateral lateral rectus palsy, contralateral hemiparesis/hemiplegia, and contralateral loss of fine touch, proprioception, and vibration.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

IccYdY0.title: Weber syndrome
IccYdY0.description: A neurologic condition characterized by a medial midbrain infarction from occlusion of the posterior cerebral artery. Manifestations include ipsilateral oculomotor nerve palsy, contralateral hemiparesis/hemiplegia (superior alternating hemiplegia), and contralateral parkinsonism.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

7cc4dY0.title: Suprascapular nerve entrapment
7cc4dY0.description: An entrapment of the suprascapular nerve within the suprascapular notch caused by ossification of the superior transverse ligament. Causes pain with shoulder movements and atrophy and paresis of the supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles, which results in weakened arm abduction and external rotation.

FccgVY0.title: Glutaraldehyde
FccgVY0.description: A disinfectant whose microbicidal effect is mediated by alkylation of sulfhydryl, hydroxyl, carboxyl, and amino groups of RNA, DNA, and proteins. Also active against spores.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Disinfectants, antiseptics, and sterilization

uccpVY0.title: Medial lemniscus
uccpVY0.description: A white matter column located in the medial aspect of the midbrain, pons, and cranial medulla. Comprised of myelinated axons that arise in the caudal medulla from the contralateral nucleus cuneatus and nucleus gracilis. Synapses with neurons in the ventral posterolateral nucleus of the thalamus. Transmits proprioception, vibration, and fine touch impulses from the trunk and extremities.

Ecc8VY0.title: Lateral lemniscus
Ecc8VY0.description: A fiber tract located in the pons that relays cochlear and olivary input to the inferior colliculus. Part of the auditory pathway.

vccAVY0.title: Spinal lemniscus
vccAVY0.description: A spinal nerve tract composed of afferent fibers that carry sensory information to the thalamus. Forms part of the spinothalamic tract and conveys pain and temperature sensation.

Dcc1eY0.title: Lateral ventricles
Dcc1eY0.description: A set of C-shaped cavities in the cerebral hemispheres of the brain that, along with the third and fourth ventricles, contain cerebrospinal fluid. Drain into the third ventricle via right and left interventricular foramina (foramina of Monro), respectively.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

wccheY0.title: 3rd ventricle
wccheY0.description: A CSF-filled cavity in the diencephalon. Drains into the 4th ventricle via the cerebral aqueduct.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

9ccNeY0.title: Internal arcuate fibers
9ccNeY0.description: The axons of the nucleus gracilis and nucleus cuneatus. After decussation, they are referred to as the medial lemniscus.

BcczeY0.title: Accessory cuneate nucleus
BcczeY0.description: A small brainstem nucleus located laterally to the cuneate nucleus in the medulla oblongata. Receives sensory input from the upper extremity and gives rise to the cuneocerebellar tract. Travels to the cerebellum via the inferior cerebellar peduncle.

AccRUY0.title: Solitary nucleus
AccRUY0.description: A nucleus in the medulla that receives general visceral afferent signals from the glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves and special visceral afferent signals from the facial, glossopharyngeal, and vagus nerves. Mediates the baroreceptor reflex.

_cc5UY0.title: Above the dentate line
_cc5UY0.description: A part of the anal canal derived from endoderm. Supplied by the superior rectal artery (a branch of the inferior mesenteric artery). Drains venous blood into the superior rectal vein. Drains lymph into the internal iliac lymph nodes.

zccrUY0.title: Below the dentate line
zccrUY0.description: A part of the anal canal derived from ectoderm. Supplied by the inferior rectal artery (a branch of the internal pudendal artery) and receives somatic innervation from the inferior rectal branch of the pudendal nerve. Drains venous blood into the inferior rectal vein. Drains lymph into the superficial inguinal lymph nodes.

b1cH2Y0.title: Transversus thoracis muscle
b1cH2Y0.description: A small muscle that lies on the inner surface of the anterior thorax and separates the thoracic cage from the parietal pleura. Acts as an accessory muscle during expiration. Innervated by intercostal nerves.

X1c92Y0.title: Anal sinuses
X1c92Y0.description: A group of recesses located in the anal canal between the anal columns. End in small transverse folds (anal valves).

11c2fY0.title: Femoral vein
11c2fY0.description: A vein in the thigh that is a direct continuation of the popliteal vein in the lower leg. Lies in the adductor canal and forms the medial boundary of the femoral canal. Continues above the inguinal ligament as the external iliac vein.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Vascular supply of the thigh
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

W1cPfY0.title: Emboliform nucleus
W1cPfY0.description: A deep cerebellar nucleus that, together with the globose nucleus, forms the interposed nucleus. Impulses from the emboliform nucleus help control limb movements.

U1cbTY0.title: Deep inguinal ring
U1cbTY0.description: The internal opening of the inguinal canal. Bounded superolaterally by the transversalis fascia and inferomedially by the inferior epigastric vessels.

21cTTY0.title: Glycoprotein 160
21cTTY0.description: An HIV glycoprotein that is cleaved to form envelope glycoproteins gp41 and gp120.

S1cyTY0.title: Foveolar cell
S1cyTY0.description: Mucus-producing cells that line the gastric mucosa.

h1ccgY0.title: Sodium-dependent glucose cotransporter
h1ccgY0.description: A membrane protein that mediates glucose and sodium transport across apical cell membranes in the small intestine and kidneys. Utilizes the energy provided by the sodium gradient across the cell membrane for active glucose transport. SGLT1 is responsible for almost all sodium-dependent glucose uptake in the small intestine; SGLT2 is responsible for almost all sodium-dependent glucose reabsorption in the proximal tubule.

31cSgY0.title: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate
31cSgY0.description: An intermediate metabolite of several biochemical pathways, including glycolysis and gluconeogenesis.

41c3SY0.title: Subclavian vein
41c3SY0.description: A large vein in the supraclavicular fossa that arises as a continuation of the axillary vein. Its tributaries are the external jugular vein and the dorsal scapular vein. Receives lymph on the left side from the thoracic duct and on the right side from the lymphatic duct. Joins the internal jugular vein to form the brachiocephalic vein.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

O1cISY0.title: Sodium-dependent glucose cotransporter 1
O1cISY0.description: A sodium-dependent glucose symporter found in the small intestine responsible for absorption into enterocytes. Also found in the proximal convoluted tubule of the kidney.

m1cVhY0.title: Deep cervical fascia
m1cVhY0.description: A layer of fascia in the neck that consists of an investing layer (which surrounds the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles), the carotid sheaths, a pretracheal layer (which surrounds the esophagus, trachea, and thyroid gland), and a prevertebral layer (which surrounds the deep muscles of the neck, the sympathetic trunk, the brachial plexus, the subclavian artery, and the phrenic nerve).

L1cwhY0.title: Epineurium
L1cwhY0.description: The outer layer of dense connective tissue around a nerve.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

o1c03Y0.title: Perineurium
o1c03Y0.description: A layer of connective tissue around nerve fascicles.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

K1cU3Y0.title: Endoneurium
K1cU3Y0.description: The inner layer of connective tissue around a single nerve fiber

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

p1cL3Y0.title: Aβ fibers
p1cL3Y0.description: A type of large, myelinated nerve fiber that carries the sensations of cutaneous mechanoreceptors.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Classification of nerve fibers

J1cs3Y0.title: Aδ fibers
J1cs3Y0.description: A myelinated nerve fiber that carries the sensations of thermal and mechanical pain. Facilitates the withdrawal response to pain (e.g., rapidly moving the hand when burned).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Classification of nerve fibers

r1cfRY0.title: Excitatory postsynaptic potential
r1cfRY0.description: A depolarizing potential that develops in a postsynaptic membrane as the result of increased influx of cations. The summation of multiple excitatory postsynaptic potentials can cause the postsynaptic neuron to reach the threshold for the generation of an action potential.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

H1cKRY0.title: Electrical synapses
H1cKRY0.description: A type of synapse that transmits signals between neurons joined by a gap junction by the flow of electrical current (i.e., movement of ions). Unlike chemical synapses, which require the transmission of a neurotransmitter across a cleft, electrical synapses transmit the signal directly and without delay.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

s1ctRY0.title: Enkephalins
s1ctRY0.description: A class of endogenous opioid peptides involved in the regulation of nociception. They act as agonists at μ and δ opioid receptors, thereby producing analgesia. Also involved in the regulation of stress.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

G1cBRY0.title: Erythema nodosum leprosum
G1cBRY0.description: An immunological complication of lepromatous leprosy characterized by multiple inflammatory, subcutaneous lesions as well as symptoms such as fever, malaise, joint pain, lymphadenopathy, uveitis, orchitis, and glomerulonephritis.

F1cgiY0.title: Nesiritide
F1cgiY0.description: A recombinant form of B-type (brain) natriuretic peptide that binds to guanylate cyclase receptors and increases intracellular cGMP, which results in smooth muscle relaxation. Previously used to treat acute decompensated heart failure but has not been shown to improve mortality or rates of rehospitalization.

u1cpiY0.title: Ascending loop of Henle
u1cpiY0.description: The segment of the nephron after the descending loop of Henle. It is divided into a thin and a thick limb. Both limbs are impermeable to water; reabsorb Na+, Cl-, and K+; and induce reabsorption of Ca2+ and Mg2+ via the K+ potential. This makes ultrafiltrate less hypertonic as it ascends.

E1c8iY0.title: Renal hilum
E1c8iY0.description: The central, medial, and concave portion of the kidney where the renal pelvis, artery, vein, and accompanying nerves enter.

v1cAiY0.title: Paranephric fat
v1cAiY0.description: The adipose tissue superficial to the renal fascia. Protects the kidneys from trauma.

D1c1QY0.title: Perinephric fat
D1c1QY0.description: The adipose tissue that envelopes the kidneys. Covered by renal fascia.

x1cEQY0.title: Scalene muscles
x1cEQY0.description: A group of three pairs of muscles in the lateral neck, namely the anterior, middle, and posterior scalenes. They play a key role in neck movements and in elevating the first and second ribs during respiration. Also involved in the etiology of various neck and neurological syndromes, such as thoracic outlet syndrome.

0WcePY0.title: Pharyngoconjunctivitis
0WcePY0.description: A highly contagious form of conjunctivitis caused by adenovirus infection. Typically manifests with follicular conjunctivitis, fever, pharyngitis, and regional lymphadenopathy.

aWcQPY0.title: Cisterna magna
aWcQPY0.description: A subarachnoid cavity located between the dorsal medulla oblongata and the cerebellum. Connected to the fourth ventricle by the foramen of Magendie and the foramina of Luschka, all of which drain cerebrospinal fluid into the cistern.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

XWc9PY0.title: Infrahyoid muscles
XWc9PY0.description: A group of four pairs of muscles that are located in the anterior triangle of the neck inferior to the hyoid bone. Include the superficially located omohyoid and sternohyoid muscles and the deeper sternothyroid and thyrohyoid muscles. Innervated by the ansa cervicalis except for the thyrohyoid, which is innervated by the hypoglossal nerve. Primarily depress the hyoid bone, except for the sternothyroid, which depresses the thyroid cartilage.

TWc6kY0.title: Axillary vein
TWc6kY0.description: Main vein of the upper limb. Formed at the outer border of the teres major by the union of the basilic vein and the accompanying veins of the brachial artery. Continues as the subclavian vein at the outer border of the 1st rib. The cephalic and basilic veins are its main tributaries. It lies medial to the axillary artery in the axillary fossa.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage
Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Veins

gWcFkY0.title: Angiotensin II receptor type 1
gWcFkY0.description: A Gq coupled receptor that is activated by the binding of angiotensin II. Found in vascular smooth muscle, the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal gland, and the posterior pituitary. Stimulation increases blood pressure, filtration fraction in the kidney, aldosterone secretion, and vasopressin secretion. Angiotensin receptor blockers bind to this receptor.

SWcykY0.title: Lateral pectoral nerve
SWcykY0.description: A peripheral nerve that arises from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus (nerve roots C5, C6, C7). With the medial pectoral nerve, innervates the pectoralis major.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

hWccOY0.title: Medial pectoral nerve
hWccOY0.description: A peripheral nerve that arises from the medial cord of the brachial plexus (nerve roots C8, T1). Innervates the pectoralis minor and, along with the lateral pectoral nerve, the pectoralis major.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

jWc_OY0.title: Artesunate
jWc_OY0.description: An antimalarial drug used especially for the treatment of severe falciparum malaria. May be given intravenously or orally. Adverse effects include bradycardia, allergic reactions, vertigo, and leukopenia. May precipitate hemolytic anemia in patients with G6PD deficiency.

kWcmlY0.title: Coronoid fossa
kWcmlY0.description: A depression on the ventral aspect of the distal humerus that lies above the trochlea. Receives the coronoid process of the ulna when the forearm is flexed.

OWcIlY0.title: Medial epicondyle
OWcIlY0.description: The most medial bony prominence on the distal shaft of the humerus. Site of insertion of most flexor muscles of the forearm. Can get inflamed with repetitive forearm flexion (i.e., golfer elbow). The ulnar nerve lies in a groove on the posterior aspect of the medial epicondyle.

lWcvlY0.title: Lateral epicondyle
lWcvlY0.description: The most lateral bony prominence on the distal shaft of the humerus. Site of insertion of most extensor muscles of the forearm. Can get inflamed with repetitive forearm extension (i.e., tennis elbow).

NWc-lY0.title: Radial fossa
NWc-lY0.description: A bony depression above the capitulum on the ventral aspect of the distal humerus. Receives the head of the radius when the forearm is flexed.

mWcVNY0.title: Olecranon fossa
mWcVNY0.description: A bony depression on the dorsal aspect of the distal humerus. Receives the olecranon process of the ulna when the forearm is extended. Prevents hyperextension of the elbow joint.

MWcMNY0.title: Coracobrachialis muscle
MWcMNY0.description: A muscle of the flexor (anterior) compartment of the arm. Originates from the coracoid process of the scapula and inserts into the medial aspect of the shaft of the humerus. Innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve. Flexes the arm at the shoulder and is a weak shoulder adductor.

oWc0mY0.title: Segment-indicating muscle
oWc0mY0.description: A skeletal muscle innervated by only one segment of the spinal cord. Testing the tone and reflexes of the muscle helps localize a nerve lesion.

KWcUmY0.title: Genetic transversion
KWcUmY0.description: A type of point mutation in which a purine is replaced by a pyrimidine (e.g., A to C, A to T, G to C, G to T) or vice versa.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

6WcjmY0.title: Genetic transition
6WcjmY0.description: A type of point mutation in which a purine is replaced by a purine (e.g., A to G, G to A) or a pyrimidine is replaced by a pyrimidine (e.g., C to T, T to C).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

pWcLmY0.title: Neurogenic bowel dysfunction
pWcLmY0.description: Impaired colonic and anorectal function due to disruption of the neural pathways that regulate bowel motility, sphincter control, and sensation. Most commonly results from brain, spinal cord, or peripheral nerve lesions and may manifest as constipation, fecal incontinence, or both. The pattern of dysfunction depends on the level and completeness of the neurological injury.

JWcsmY0.title: Urachal cyst
JWcsmY0.description: Persistent cyst-like remnant of the median umbilical ligament (urachus) that is due to partial failure to obliterate. Usually asymptomatic; however, may become secondarily infected.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Embryology

qWcCmY0.title: Vesicourachal diverticulum
qWcCmY0.description: Outpouching of the anterosuperior aspect of the urinary bladder due to a failure of complete closure of the urachus where it connects with the bladder.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Embryology

7Wc45Y0.title: Brodifacoum
7Wc45Y0.description: A 4-hydroxycoumarin vitamin K antagonist that is commonly used in rodent poisoning and pesticides. Longer-acting and more lethal than warfarin.

GWcB5Y0.title: Bicipital aponeurosis
GWcB5Y0.description: A fan-shaped connective tissue sheath that connects the biceps tendon to the ulna. Forms the roof of the cubital fossa and protects underlying neurovascular structures. Thickening of the aponeurosis can cause median nerve compression.

destinations.label: Upper arm and elbow → Cubital fossa (antecubital fossa)

tWcXMY0.title: Cubital fossa
tWcXMY0.description: A triangular depression on the ventral aspect of the elbow joint bound laterally by the brachioradialis, medially by the pronator teres, and superiorly by an imaginary line between the humeral epicondyles. Contains (from lateral to medial) the radial nerve, biceps tendon, brachial artery, and median nerve.

destinations.label: Upper arm and elbow → Cubital fossa (antecubital fossa)

FWcgMY0.title: Synapse
FWcgMY0.description: The junction across which signals or action potentials are transmitted from a presynaptic to a postsynaptic structure (e.g., neurons, muscle).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

8WcOMY0.title: Deep brachial artery
8WcOMY0.description: The first branch of the brachial artery. Supplies the posterior compartment of the arm (i.e., the triceps muscle). Gives rise to the radial collateral artery that is part of the arterial anastomosis of the elbow joint.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries
Upper arm and elbow → Vasculature and lymphatics

vWcAMY0.title: Brachial vein
vWcAMY0.description: A deep vein of the upper limb that forms from the radial and ulnar veins and becomes the axillary vein at the outer border of the teres major.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Veins
Upper arm and elbow → Vasculature and lymphatics

wWchnY0.title: Medial cutaneous nerve of arm
wWchnY0.description: A sensory nerve that arises from the medial cord of the brachial plexus and supplies the skin over the lower 1/3rd of the medial arm.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

adcQoY0.title: Ansa cervicalis
adcQoY0.description: A motor nerve loop that is a part of the cervical nerve plexus. Formed from the C1–C3 spinal roots and lies in the carotid triangle superficial to the internal jugular vein. Innervates three of the four pairs of infrahyoid muscles (omohyoid, sternohyoid, and sternothyroid).

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

bdcHoY0.title: Treatment adherence
bdcHoY0.description: The extent to which an individual follows recommendations from a health care professional. This includes adherence to prescribed medication as well as other medical advice, e.g., on lifestyle changes. Adherence to medication can be assessed objectively by examining pharmacy records, counting pills, or measuring blood levels of the prescribed drug.

fdck6Y0.title: Orbicularis oris muscle
fdck6Y0.description: A multilayered muscle of facial expression that encircles the mouth. Innervated by the buccal branch of the facial nerve. Facilitates the precise movements of the lips during speech and facial expression.

4dc3JY0.title: Anterior cervical triangle
4dc3JY0.description: A region of the neck in the shape of an inverted triangle with the base formed by the lower border of the mandible, the apex by the jugular notch, the medial border formed by the midline of the neck, and the lateral border formed by the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle.

kdcmJY0.title: Venous angle
kdcmJY0.description: The junction at the termination of the internal jugular vein and the subclavian vein on either side of the neck. Receives venous drainage from the head, neck, and upper extremities. It also receives lymphatic drainage via the thoracic duct, which drains into the left venous angle and the right lymphatic duct, which drains into the right venous angle.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

OdcIJY0.title: Radioulnar joints
OdcIJY0.description: A uniaxial pivot joint located proximally and distally between the radius and ulna. Allows the distal end of the radius to move anteriorly and medially over the ulna (i.e., forearm pronation and supination).

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

ldcvJY0.title: Distal radioulnar joint
ldcvJY0.description: A synovial pivot joint between the head of the ulna and the ulnar notch on the distal radius supported by radioulnar ligaments. Along with the proximal radioulnar joint, it is responsible for forearm pronation and supination.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

KdcUIY0.title: Anconeus
KdcUIY0.description: An extensor muscle of the posterior compartment of the forearm that originates from the lateral humeral epicondyle and inserts into the posterior part of the ulna.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

6dcjIY0.title: Vestibular ganglion
6dcjIY0.description: An accumulation of the cell bodies of the first order cells of the afferent vestibular pathway. Lies in the internal acoustic meatus within the petrous temporal bone. The axons of these cells travel in the vestibular part of the vestibulocochlear nerve and terminate in the vestibular nuclei in the brainstem.

IdcYrY0.title: Extensor compartment of the forearm
IdcYrY0.description: A compartment of the posterior forearm that is separated from the flexor compartment by the interosseous membrane, which extends between the radius and ulna. Contains twelve muscles that act as forearm supinators and extensors of the wrist and fingers. Innervated by the radial nerve.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

HdcKrY0.title: Arcuate nucleus (medulla)
HdcKrY0.description: A brainstem nucleus located anterior to the pyramids. Receives input from the corticospinal tract and gives rise to the arcuatocerebellar tract. Responsible for chemoreception and breathing control.

sdctrY0.title: Idiotype
sdctrY0.description: The three-dimensional characteristic of an immunoglobulin variable region that imparts the immunoglobulin specificity for a given antigen.

GdcBrY0.title: Arcuate nucleus (hypothalamus)
GdcBrY0.description: A hypothalamic nucleus located adjacent to the third ventricle. Regulates the secretion of neuroendocrine hormones from the pituitary gland and inhibits lactation. Damage to this area can result in neuroendocrine dysfunction.

Edc87Y0.title: A-alpha fibers
Edc87Y0.description: A type of myelinated, sensory nerve fiber that carries impulses from muscle spindles to alpha motoneurons.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Classification of nerve fibers

vdcA7Y0.title: C fibers
vdcA7Y0.description: An unmyelinated nerve fiber that carries sensation of chemical, thermal, and mechanical pain.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Classification of nerve fibers

Ddc1HY0.title: Chemical synapses
Ddc1HY0.description: A type of synapse (consisting of presynaptic membrane, synaptic cleft, and postsynaptic membrane) in which signals are transferred between neurons via a neurotransmitter (e.g., GABA, glutamate).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

wdchHY0.title: Scaphoid bone
wdchHY0.description: A carpal bone located on the radial side of the proximal row of carpal bones. Located within the anatomical snuffbox. The most commonly fractured carpal bone.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

media.title: Normal x-ray of the carpal bones

9dcNHY0.title: Lunate bone
9dcNHY0.description: A carpal bone that articulates with the radius proximally, capitate and hamate distally, scaphoid laterally, and triquetrum medially. A fracture or dislocation can cause acute carpal tunnel syndrome.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

media.title: Bones of the hand and wrist

CdcqHY0.title: Triquetrum
CdcqHY0.description: A carpal bone that articulates with the radius, the pisiform anteriorly, the hamate distally, and the lunate laterally.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

xdcEHY0.title: Pisiform
xdcEHY0.description: The smallest carpal bone. Located in the tendon of the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle. Functions as a sesamoid bone.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

BdczHY0.title: Trapezoid bone
BdczHY0.description: A carpal bone that serves as the origin of the adductor pollicis. It is the smallest bone of the distal carpal row.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

media.title: Bones of the hand and wrist

ydcdsY0.title: Capitate
ydcdsY0.description: The largest of the carpal bones, located in the center of the wrist, which serves as origin for the oblique head of the adductor pollicis.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

AdcRsY0.title: Sperm granuloma
AdcRsY0.description: A collection of sperm due to leakage from the vas deferens into the surrounding interstitium. Mostly asymptomatic and resorbs over time, but sperm can also elicit an immune response that leads to chronic inflammation and pain. Complication of vasectomy.

_dc5sY0.title: Major duodenal papilla
_dc5sY0.description: The common opening of the major pancreatic duct and common bile duct, located in the second portion of the duodenum.

zdcrsY0.title: Dorsal pancreatic duct
zdcrsY0.description: The duct that drains the dorsal bud of the developing pancreas. Merges with the ventral pancreatic duct to form the main pancreatic duct.

-dcDsY0.title: Minor duodenal papilla
-dcDsY0.description: The opening of the dorsal pancreatic duct into the duodenum

0VceGY0.title: Ventral pancreatic duct
0VceGY0.description: The duct that drains the ventral bud of the developing pancreas. Merges with the dorsal pancreatic duct to form the main pancreatic duct.

YVcnGY0.title: Hepatic diverticulum
YVcnGY0.description: An embryonic outgrowth of endoderm that arises from the foregut and gives rise to the liver parenchyma.

bVcHGY0.title: Median umbilical fold
bVcHGY0.description: A peritoneal fold that covers the median umbilical ligament, which is a remnant of the obliterated urachus that extends from the apex of the urinary bladder to the umbilicus.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Embryology

XVc9GY0.title: Urinary tract
XVc9GY0.description: A system comprising the kidneys, renal pelvis, ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra. Responsible for removing urea and toxins from the body.

cVcatY0.title: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase II deficiency
cVcatY0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder of long-chain fatty acid oxidation caused by a deficiency of the mitochondrial enzyme carnitine palmitoyltransferase II. The lethal neonatal hepatocardiac form and the severe infantile hepatocardiomuscular form manifest with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, liver failure, and cardiomyopathy. The myopathic form is least severe and manifests with myalgia, rhabdomyolysis, myoglobinuria, and renal injury.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism disorders

WVcPtY0.title: Carnitine transporter deficiency
WVcPtY0.description: A congenital condition characterized by a defective plasma-membrane carnitine transporter that leads to renal loss, systemic carnitine deficiency, and impaired fatty acid oxidation of the carnitine transporter. Causes hypoketotic hypoglycemia and muscle weakness.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism disorders

dVcotY0.title: Scapulothoracic joint
dVcotY0.description: The area of articulation between the anterior scapula and the posterior thoracic cage. It is not a true anatomical joint (it does not directly connect skeletal structures with fibrous, cartilaginous, or synovial tissue).

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Joints of the shoulder girdle

VVcGtY0.title: Newborn screening
VVcGtY0.description: A combination of tests performed on newborns via heel prick blood sampling. These tests typically screen for genetic disorders (e.g., cystic fibrosis), endocrine disorders (e.g., congenital hypothyroidism), hemoglobinopathies (e.g., sickle cell disease, thalassemia), and metabolic disorders (e.g., galactosemia, fatty acid oxidation disorders, lysosomal disorders).

eVcxtY0.title: Semispinalis muscles
eVcxtY0.description: A group of back muscles that belong to the transversospinalis group muscles (deep layer of the intrinsic back muscles). Includes the semispinalis capitis, semispinalis cervicis, and the semispinalis thoracis muscles.

UVcbFY0.title: Brachiocephalic vein
UVcbFY0.description: A vein found on both sides of the body, formed by the union of the internal jugular vein and the subclavian vein. Each drains blood from the head, neck, upper limbs, and upper part of the thorax and empties into the superior vena cava.

2VcTFY0.title: Tetrahydrobiopterin deficiency
2VcTFY0.description: A congenital disorder characterized by accumulation of phenylalanine as a result of decreased conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine. Often caused by a deficiency in dihydropteridine reductase, which normally reduces dihydrobiopterin to tetrahydrobiopterin. Clinically indistinguishable from classic phenylketonuria. Differentiation can be made through an oral tetrahydrobiopterin loading test. Unlike classic PKU, this condition requires treatment with BH4 supplementation in addition to dietary phenylalanine restriction and tyrosine supplementation.

fVckFY0.title: Brachiocephalic vein obstruction
fVckFY0.description: A condition caused by thrombosis, stenosis, external compression, or vascular tumor invasion of the brachiocephalic vein. Manifests with unilateral upper extremity swelling, pain, and weakness and unilateral facial and neck swelling.

TVc6FY0.title: Extrinsic muscles of the hand
TVc6FY0.description: A group of muscles that originate outside the hand. Their muscle bellies are located in the forearm, but they insert into structures of the hand. These muscles are the flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris, flexor digitorum superficialis, flexor digitorum profundus, flexor pollicis longus, pronator quadratus, extensor carpi radialis longus, extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum, extensor digiti minimi, extensor carpi ulnaris, abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, and the extensor indicis.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

gVcFFY0.title: Intrinsic muscles of the hand
gVcFFY0.description: A smaller group of muscles located within the hand itself. This group includes the thenar, hypothenar, interossei, and the lumbrical muscles.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

hVcc8Y0.title: Upper subscapular nerve
hVcc8Y0.description: Nerve that arises from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus and supplies the subscapularis.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

3VcS8Y0.title: Lower subscapular nerve
3VcS8Y0.description: Nerve that arises from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus and supplies the subscapularis and teres major.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

QVcu8Y0.title: Infraspinous fossa
QVcu8Y0.description: A concave depression located inferior to the scapular spine on the posterior aspect of the scapula. The infraspinatus muscle, which forms part of the rotator cuff, inserts here.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

jVc_8Y0.title: Infraspinatus muscle
jVc_8Y0.description: A rotator cuff muscle that originates from the infraspinatous fossa on the dorsal surface of the scapula and inserts into the greater tubercle of the humerus. Externally rotates the humerus.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Muscles of the shoulder girdle

NVc-uY0.title: Procerus muscle
NVc-uY0.description: A small, triangular muscle that extends from the lower part of the nasal bone to the lateral nasal cartilages. Pulls the skin between the eyebrows caudal to flare the nostrils. Innervated by the facial nerve.

mVcVEY0.title: Buccinator muscle
mVcVEY0.description: A cheek muscle that lies between the maxilla and mandible. Retracts the angle of the mouth and stiffens the cheek wall to help with chewing. Innervated by the facial nerve.

5VciEY0.title: Mentalis muscle
5VciEY0.description: A small, paired muscle of the chin, that originates from the mentum (tip of the chin) and inserts into the surrounding soft tissue. Innervated by the facial nerve. Elevates the central portion of the lower lip.

nVc7EY0.title: Styloid process of the temporal bone
nVc7EY0.description: A thin, elongated bony process that protrudes anteriorly and inferiorly from the temporal bone. Serves as an attachment for several muscles (e.g., styloglossus, stylohyoid, stylopharyngeus).

LVcwEY0.title: Stylohyoid muscle
LVcwEY0.description: A thin muscle that arises from the styloid process and inserts onto the hyoid bone. Elevates the tongue and retracts and elevates the hyoid bone. Innervated by the facial nerve.

oVc0vY0.title: Stylohyoid ligament
oVc0vY0.description: A thin, fibrous ligament that extends from the tip of the styloid process to the hyoid bone. Partial or complete ossification of the ligament causes Eagle syndrome. Develops from the 2nd branchial arch.

KVcUvY0.title: Digastric muscle
KVcUvY0.description: A muscle with 2 bellies (anterior and posterior). The anterior belly originates from the symphysis menti on the mandible and is innervated by the trigeminal nerve (mylohyoid nerve). The posterior belly originates from the mastoid process and is innervated by the facial nerve. The muscles converge at the intermediate tendon, which is attached to the hyoid bone. Helps to open the jaw.

6VcjvY0.title: Stylopharyngeus muscle
6VcjvY0.description: A pharyngeal muscle that originates from the styloid process, passes between the superior and middle pharyngeal constrictors, and inserts predominantly onto the thyroid cartilage. Elevates the pharynx and larynx. Innervated by the glossopharyngeal nerve.

pVcLvY0.title: Photoallergen
pVcLvY0.description: A substance that, after previous sensitization, causes a delayed hypersensitivity reaction in response to ultraviolet radiation. Manifestations are similar to rash induced by allergic contact dermatitis. Common photoallergens include sunscreens, NSAIDs, and fragrances.

rVcfDY0.title: Non-enveloped virus
rVcfDY0.description: A group of viruses that lack a lipid bilayer covering. Typically more stable in acidic environments and more resistant to dry heat and detergents compared to enveloped viruses. Includes some DNA viruses (e.g., adenovirus, papillomavirus, parvovirus, polyomavirus) and RNA viruses (e.g., calicivirus, picornavirus, reovirus, and hepevirus).

media.title: General structures of different virus particles

7Vc4DY0.title: Costodiaphragmatic recess
7Vc4DY0.description: The space formed by the parietal pleura at the base of the lung between the diaphragm and the ribs. In the nonrecumbent position, this recess is the most dependent site of pleural cavity and is, therefore, the site for accumulation of fluid in the case of a pleural effusion or hemothorax. On a 2D projection (e.g., posteroanterior chest x-ray), this region is visualized as the costophrenic angle.

sVctDY0.title: Enveloped viruses
sVctDY0.description: A group of viruses that have a lipid bilayer covering, which is acquired during virion budding and release from the host cell. Typically less stable in acidic environments and less resistant to dry heat and detergents compared to non-enveloped viruses. Includes some DNA viruses (e.g., herpesvirus, poxvirus, and hepadnavirus) and several RNA viruses (e.g., flavivirus, togavirus, and retrovirus).

GVcBDY0.title: Encapsulated pathogens
GVcBDY0.description: A group of pathogens covered by a capsule that protects them from opsonization and phagocytosis. Examples include some gram-positive bacteria (e.g., Streptococcus), gram-negative bacteria (e.g., Pseudomonas, Neisseria, Salmonella), and yeast (e.g., Cryptococcus).

tVcXwY0.title: Chyle
tVcXwY0.description: A cloudy, milky substance that contains lymphatic fluid, triglycerides, and other lipids. Taken up from the intestine during digestion and conveyed by the thoracic duct to empty into the venous system.

FVcgwY0.title: X descent
FVcgwY0.description: A component of the jugular venous pulse that correlates with inferior displacement of the closed tricuspid valve during atrial relaxation and ventricular contraction. Becomes absent in patients with tricuspid regurgitation and right-sided heart failure.

media.title: Jugular venous pressure waveforms in common cardiac conditions

DVc19Y0.title: Superior epigastric artery
DVc19Y0.description: A branch of the internal thoracic artery that descends along the abdominal wall and anastomoses with branches of the inferior epigastric artery near the umbilicus. Supplies the anterior abdominal wall.

9VcN9Y0.title: Autonomous sensory zone
9VcN9Y0.description: An area of skin that has sensory innervation from a single peripheral nerve (without overlapping sensory innervation from adjacent nerve territories).

BVcz9Y0.title: Epitrochlear lymph nodes
BVcz9Y0.description: A group of superficial lymph nodes located on the medial side of the arm above the medial epicondyle of the humerus. Drains the ulnar side of the forearm and hand into the axillary lymph nodes.

destinations.label: Upper arm and elbow → Cubital fossa (antecubital fossa)

yVcdCY0.title: Aortic isthmus
yVcdCY0.description: The part of the aorta that is located distal to the left subclavian artery. Forms the junction between the aortic arch and descending aorta. Contains the insertion of the cranial end of the ligamentum arteriosum. Is the most common location for aortic coarctation and blunt thoracic aortic injury.

aecQxY0.title: Pulmonary trunk
aecQxY0.description: The blood vessel that originates from the right ventricle of the heart. Divides into the left and right pulmonary arteries and carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs for oxygenation.

feckyY0.title: Pericardial cavity
feckyY0.description: The space between the visceral and parietal layers of the serous pericardium. Contains serous, pericardial fluid. The capacity of the cavity is limited by the stiff, fibrous pericardium. The abnormal accumulation of fluid in the pericardial space (pericardial effusion) increases intrapericardial pressure, potentially causing pericardial tamponade.

gecFyY0.title: Septum primum
gecFyY0.description: A cranially located, embryologic cardiac structure. Extends caudally toward the dorsal endocardial cushion, which narrows the foramen primum.

heccAY0.title: Septum secundum
heccAY0.description: An embryologic cardiac structure that grows caudally toward the dorsal endocardial cushion. The septum primum expands concurrently, which narrows the foramen secundum and leaves the residual foramen ovale.

jec_AY0.title: Pleura
jec_AY0.description: A serous membrane of the lung that reflects on itself, which forms two layers with a potential space in between (pleural cavity). The inner invests the surface of the lungs (visceral pleura) and is insensitive to pain. The outer layer lines the thoracic wall, diaphragm, and mediastinum (parietal pleura) and is sensitive to pain.

PecW_Y0.title: Accessory hemiazygos vein
