PecW_Y0.description: A vein located to the left of the vertebral column that receives venous drainage from the 5th to the 8th intercostal spaces. Terminates by joining either the azygos vein by crossing the vertebral column at the T8 vertebra or by joining the hemiazygos vein.

kecm_Y0.title: Fossa ovalis
kecm_Y0.description: A small, oval-shaped depression in the interatrial septum of the heart. A remnant of the foramen ovale, which usually closes after birth.

MecMzY0.title: Primary active transport
MecMzY0.description: The movement of molecules against their concentration gradient across a selectively permeable membrane. Requires ATP as an energy source.

nec7zY0.title: Secondary active transport
nec7zY0.description: The use of the electrochemical gradient (e.g., generated by primary active transport) of one type of molecule to move another type of molecule against its gradient. Does not directly require ATP. Includes symporters (e.g., the sodium-glucose symporter) and antiporters (e.g., the sodium–hydrogen antiporter).

LecwzY0.title: Receptor-mediated endocytosis
LecwzY0.description: A process in which specific target receptors on the outer cell membrane bind external molecules, which then become packaged in endocytic vesicles. Typically mediated by clathrin proteins.

oec0-Y0.title: Apple peel atresia
oec0-Y0.description: A form of intestinal atresia characterized by a blind proximal end (usually the duodenum) with the distal small bowel wrapped around the superior mesenteric artery in a spiral that resembles an apple peel. Can be an isolated malformation, associated with malrotation, or secondary to in utero vascular accidents.

KecU-Y0.title: Nitrate reductase
KecU-Y0.description: A bacterial enzyme that converts nitrate to nitrite. Produced by Enterobacteriaceae spp. (e.g., E. coli, Proteus, Serratia).

pecL-Y0.title: Leukotrienes
pecL-Y0.description: A group of inflammatory mediators produced by leukocytes that potentiate allergic and asthmatic responses. They are metabolites of arachidonic acid and are produced by the enzyme 5-lipoxygenase.

qecC-Y0.title: Conduction aphasia
qecC-Y0.description: An acquired language disorder characterized by impaired repetition with paraphasia (sounds are substituted or transposed), which patients try to correct. Comprehension is preserved but patients cannot encode phonological information for production. Caused by damage to the arcuate fasciculus of the parietal lobe.

7ec4Zb0.title: Superior gemellus
7ec4Zb0.description: A deep gluteal muscle that originates from the ischial spine and inserts onto the greater trochanter. Innervated by the nerve to the obturator internus muscle and supplied by the lateral sacral artery and the superior and inferior gluteal arteries. Laterally rotates the thigh.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region

sectZb0.title: Dutasteride
sectZb0.description: A testosterone analog that acts as a competitive 5α-reductase inhibitor that prevents the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone. Used to treat benign prostatic hyperplasia and male pattern hair loss.

tecX0b0.title: Obturator internus muscle
tecX0b0.description: A muscle that originates from the ischiopubic ramus and posterior surface of the obturator membrane and inserts into the medial aspect of the greater trochanter. Innervated by the nerve to obturator internus, which is composed of L5, S1, and S2 roots. Abducts and externally rotates the hip joint.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → The gluteal region

media.title: Muscles of the hip and gluteal region

Fecg0b0.title: Rotterdam criteria
Fecg0b0.description: A set of diagnostic criteria for polycystic ovarian syndrome. Diagnosis requires ≥ 2 of the following: oligoovulation and/or anovulation, evidence of hyperandrogenism (e.g., acne, hirsutism, male-pattern hair loss), and polycystic ovaries on ultrasonography.

uecp0b0.title: Iliacus
uecp0b0.description: A large muscle innervated by the femoral nerve that enables flexion of the hip. At its distal end, the muscle joins the psoas to form the iliopsoas.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

wechab0.title: Rectus femoris muscle
wechab0.description: A part of the quadriceps femoris muscle that arises from the anterior inferior iliac spine and inserts into the patellar tendon. Innervated by the femoral nerve. Extends the knee joint and flexes the hip joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

media.title: Muscles of the anterior compartment of the thigh

xecEab0.title: Semimembranosus muscle
xecEab0.description: A muscle in the posterior compartment of the thigh that originates from the ischial tuberosity and inserts onto the superomedial surface of the tibia. Innervated by the tibial branch of the sciatic nerve. Flexes the knee joint and extends the hip joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

media.title: Muscles of the posterior thigh (hamstring muscles)

Beczab0.title: Semitendinosus muscle
Beczab0.description: A muscle in the posterior compartment of the thigh that originates from the ischial tuberosity and inserts via the pes anserinus into the anteromedial surface of the proximal tibia. Innervated by the tibial branch of the sciatic nerve. Flexes the knee joint and extends the hip joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

media.title: Muscles of the posterior thigh (hamstring muscles)

AecRYb0.title: Obturator externus muscle
AecRYb0.description: A muscle of the medial compartment of the thigh that orginates from the anterior surface of the obturator membrane and inserts into the posterior aspect of the greater trochanter. Innervated by the obturator nerve. Adducts and laterally rotates the hip joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

_ec5Yb0.title: Gracilis muscle
_ec5Yb0.description: A muscle of the medial compartment of the thigh that originates from the ischiopubic ramus and inserts into the anteriomedial aspect of the proximal tibia via the pes anserinus. It is innervated by the obturator nerve. It adducts, flexes, and internally rotates the hip joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

zecrYb0.title: Pectineus muscle
zecrYb0.description: A muscle of the medial compartment of the thigh that originates from the superior pubic ramus and inserts into the pectineal line on the femur. Innervated by the femoral nerve and occasionally by the obturator nerve. Adducts, flexes, and externally rotates the hip joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

-ecDYb0.title: Adductor magnus muscle
-ecDYb0.description: A muscle of the medial compartment of the thigh. Consists of an adductor and a hamstring part. The adductor part, which originates from the ischiopubic ramus and inserts into the linea aspera on the femur, is innervated by the obturator nerve. The hamstring part, which originates from the ischial tuberosity and inserts into the adductor tubercle on the femur, is innervated by the sciatic nerve. Both parts adduct the hip joint. In addition, the adductor part flexes the hip joint while the hamstring part extends the hip joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

ZUcZbb0.title: Adductor longus muscle
ZUcZbb0.description: A muscle of the medial compartment of the thigh that originates from the pubic body and inserts into the linea aspera on the femur. Innervated by the obturator nerve. Adducts and flexes the hip joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

0Ucebb0.title: Adductor brevis muscle
0Ucebb0.description: A muscle of the medial compartment of the thigh that originates from the pubic body and inferior pubic ramus, and inserts into the linea aspera on the femur. Innervated by the obturator nerve. Adducts the hip joint.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Muscles of the thigh

aUcQbb0.title: Amino group
aUcQbb0.description: A nitrogen-containing functional group (-NH2) of amines and amino acids. Has basic properties, which means that it can be protonated to NH3+.

YUcnbb0.title: Carboxyl group
YUcnbb0.description: Oxygen-containing functional group of the carbon acids (COOH). Has acidic properties, which means that it can be deprotonated to COO-.

XUc9bb0.title: Femoral triangle
XUc9bb0.description: A triangular intermuscular space in the superomedial aspect of the anterior thigh. Bound by the inguinal ligament, the medial border of the sartorius, and the medial border of the adductor longus. Contains, from lateral to medial, the femoral nerve, femoral artery, femoral vein, femoral canal, and lymphatic vessels.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Femoral triangle and fasial compartments of the thigh

cUcaXb0.title: Femoral ring
cUcaXb0.description: The abdominal opening of the femoral canal. Bounded anteriorly by the inguinal ligament, posteriorly by the pectineal ligament, medially by the lacunar ligament, and laterally by the medial border of the femoral vein.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Femoral triangle and fasial compartments of the thigh

1Uc2Xb0.title: Hemoglobin C
1Uc2Xb0.description: A hemoglobin protein variant caused a point mutation that results in the substitution of a glutamic acid residue for a lysine residue in the beta subunit. Heterozygous carriers (HbAC) are typically asymptomatic; homozygous individuals (HbCC) typically develop mild anemia and jaundice.

WUcPXb0.title: Macroangiopathic hemolytic anemia
WUcPXb0.description: A type of extrinsic hemolytic anemia caused by mechanical destruction of erythrocytes (e.g., from mechanical heart valves, aortic stenosis).

destinations.label: Hemolytic anemia → Mechanical destruction of RBCs

eUcxXb0.title: Femoral artery
eUcxXb0.description: The continuation of the external iliac artery and main artery of the thigh. Begins behind the inguinal ligament at the midinguinal point. Becomes the popliteal artery at the adductor hiatus.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Vascular supply of the thigh
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Arteries

UUcbcb0.title: Profunda femoris artery
UUcbcb0.description: The main branch of the femoral artery. Arises from the posterolateral aspect of the main trunk about 3.5 cm distal to the inguinal ligament. Supplies every muscular compartment of the thigh and the femoral head and neck.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Arteries
Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Vascular supply of the thigh

media.title: Arterial blood supply of the femur

fUckcb0.title: Cerebellopontine angle
fUckcb0.description: An anatomical space in between cerebellum and pons. Contains vessels and cranial nerves. Associated with vestibular schwannomas.

destinations.label: Brain tumors → Primary brain tumors according to age

TUc6cb0.title: His-Purkinje conduction system
TUc6cb0.description: The conduction fibers located in the cardiac subendocardium that conduct electrical impulses from the cardiac pacemakers (i.e., SA node, AV node) to the myocardium.

SUcycb0.title: Posterior cutaneous nerve of thigh
SUcycb0.description: A branch of the sacral plexus that receives fibers from the anterior and posterior divisions of the anterior rami. Innervates the inferior part of the gluteal region, the posterior aspect of the scrotum/labia majora, and the posterior aspect of the thigh and upper calf.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Innervation of the thigh
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves

RUcl1b0.title: Type 1 muscle fibers
RUcl1b0.description: A subtype of skeletal muscle fiber that can contract for long periods of time with little force. Contains abundant mitochondria and myoglobin, which cause it to have a dark red appearance.

iUcJ1b0.title: Type 2 muscle fibers
iUcJ1b0.description: A subtype of skeletal muscle fiber that can contract quickly and powerfully but fatigues very quickly. Contains few mitochondria and myoglobin, which results in a whitish appearance.

QUcu1b0.title: Tetanus toxoid
QUcu1b0.description: A denatured tetanus toxin used in tetanus vaccination. Can be conjugated to polysaccharide antigens to improve the immunogenicity of other vaccines (e.g., Hib vaccine).

jUc_1b0.title: Schistosoma mansoni
jUc_1b0.description: A parasitic blood fluke endemic to sub-Saharan Africa, western South America, and the South Caribbean islands. Causes schistosomiasis (mainly intestinal tract disease) after cercariae from snails penetrate the skin, mature into adults in the liver, and migrate to the mesenteric venules of the colon. Its eggs have a lateral spine.

media.title: Microscopy of two cercariae of Schistosoma mansoni

PUcWWb0.title: Schistosoma japonicum
PUcWWb0.description: A parasitic blood fluke endemic to the Yangtze River Basin in China, the Philippines, and Indonesia. Causes schistosomiasis (mainly intestinal tract diseases) after cercariae from snails penetrate the skin, mature into adults in the liver, and migrate to the mesenteric venules of the small and large intestines.

4Uc3Wb0.title: Polycystin 1
4Uc3Wb0.description: A large transmembrane protein encoded by the PKD1 gene on chromosome 16. Mutations are associated with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. Along with polycystin-2, it is involved in renal tubular cell proliferation, migration, and interactions with other cells.

kUcmWb0.title: Polycystin 2
kUcmWb0.description: A large transmembrane protein encoded by the PKD2 gene on chromosome 4. Mutations are associated with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. Along with polycystin-1, it is involved in renal tubular cell proliferation, migration, and interactions with other cells.

lUcvWb0.title: Merkel disc receptor
lUcvWb0.description: A mechanoreceptor located in the superficial layers of hairy and hairless skin. These receptors are slow-adapting, sense deep static touch, mechanical pressure, and position, and have small receptive fields with well-defined borders. Very sensitive to edges, corners, and shapes.

LUcwdb0.title: Suprapatellar bursa
LUcwdb0.description: A fluid-filled sac located between the anterior surface of the distal femur and the quadriceps tendon. Communicates with the knee joint cavity, which is why distention of this bursa can be a sign of intraarticular knee effusion.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The knee joint

6UcjVb0.title: Popliteal artery
6UcjVb0.description: A continuation of the femoral artery that originates at the adductor hiatus and terminates at the inferior border of the popliteus muscle by dividing into its terminal branches.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Arteries
Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The popliteal fossa

JUcsVb0.title: Ulna
JUcsVb0.description: A long bone of the forearm, located parallel to the radius and found medially when in anatomical position.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

IUcYeb0.title: Enthesis
IUcYeb0.description: The point of insertion of a tendon or ligament to bone.

HUcKeb0.title: Urachal sinus
HUcKeb0.description: A congenital abnormality caused by partial failure of the cranial end of the urachus to obliterate. Results in discharge of cloudy, serous, and/or bloody fluid from the umbilicus.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Embryology

EUc8Ub0.title: Corticotropin-releasing hormone stimulation test
EUc8Ub0.description: A test used to differentiate between pituitary and ectopic sources of excess ACTH in patients with Cushing syndrome. If serum ACTH and cortisol levels increase, Cushing disease is confirmed; minimal or no change in levels suggests an ectopic source. Also used to differentiate between 1°, 2°, and 3° adrenal insufficiency.

vUcAUb0.title: Calcaneal tendon
vUcAUb0.description: The tendon that attaches the converged soleus and gastrocnemius muscles to the calcaneus.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

DUc12b0.title: Pulmonary vascular resistance
DUc12b0.description: The resistance that must be overcome in order to move blood through the pulmonary vasculature. It is calculated using the mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP), pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP), and cardiac output using the following formula: PVR = (mPAP - PAWP)/(cardiac output). It is expressed in Wood units; a value of > 2 Wood units is considered abnormal.

9UcN2b0.title: Ileocecal valve
9UcN2b0.description: A sphincter muscle valve found in the lower right quadrant of the abdomen that separates the small bowel (ileum) and large bowel (cecum). Provides a mechanical barrier to bacterial migration into the small intestine. Regulates the exit of fluid and nutrients into the colon.

CUcq2b0.title: Direct inguinal hernia
CUcq2b0.description: A direct protrusion of intra-abdominal contents through the weakened posterior wall of the inguinal canal, medial to the inferior epigastric artery. Typically develops among older adults as a result of conditions that increase intra-abdominal pressure (e.g., chronic constipation, chronic cough).

xUcE2b0.title: Indirect inguinal hernia
xUcE2b0.description: An abnormal protrusion of intra-abdominal contents through the deep inguinal ring. The hernial sac lies lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels. Large hernias travel through the inguinal canal and protrude out of the superficial inguinal ring. Can be congenital (secondary to a patent processus vaginalis) or acquired.

BUcz2b0.title: Anterior tibial artery
BUcz2b0.description:
A branch of the popliteal artery. Originates at the inferior border of the popliteus muscle within the popliteal fossa,
enters the anterior compartment of the leg through a gap in the upper part of the interosseous membrane, and continues as the dorsalis pedis artery beyond the ankle joint. Supplies the muscles of the anterior compartment of the leg.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Arteries
The leg, ankle, and foot → Vasculature

yUcdfb0.title: Posterior tibial artery
yUcdfb0.description: A terminal branch of the tibioperoneal trunk of the popliteal artery. Originates at the inferior border of the popliteus muscle within the popliteal fossa and terminates just beyond the medial malleolus by dividing into medial and lateral plantar arteries. Supplies the muscles of the posterior compartment of the leg and the plantar aspect of the foot.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Arteries
The leg, ankle, and foot → Vasculature

-UcDfb0.title: Fibular artery
-UcDfb0.description: A terminal branch of the tibioperoneal trunk of the popliteal artery. Originates at the inferior border of the popliteus muscle within the popliteal fossa and terminates at the inferior tibiofibular joint by dividing into lateral calcaneal branches. Supplies the muscles of the lateral compartment of the leg and the deep flexor group of the posterior compartment of the leg.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Arteries
The leg, ankle, and foot → Vasculature

Z2cZTb0.title: Dorsalis pedis artery
Z2cZTb0.description: A continuation of the anterior tibial artery. Originates at the ankle joint in the anterior aspect of the first intermetatarsal space and terminates by anastomosing with the lateral plantar artery to form the plantar arch. Supplies the great toe and medial half of the second toe. Its branches (the tarsal arteries and arcuate artery), supply the muscles of the foot, the medial malleolus, the lateral four toes, and the dorsal aspect of the foot.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Vasculature
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Arteries

02ceTb0.title: Great saphenous vein
02ceTb0.description: The largest vein in the body. A continuation of the medial marginal vein of the foot (medial end of the dorsal venous arch) that runs superficially along the lower limb and terminates into the femoral vein. Drains blood from the anteromedial aspect of the sole, leg, and thigh.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Vasculature
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

a2cQTb0.title: Small saphenous vein
a2cQTb0.description: A superficial vein of the leg that forms as a continuation of the lateral marginal vein of the foot (lateral end of the dorsal venous arch). Drains the posterior and lower leg.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Vasculature
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

b2cHTb0.title: Spinocerebellum
b2cHTb0.description: A portion of the cerebellum that consists of the vermis and the intermediate zones of the cerebellar hemispheres. Receives input from the spinal cord and is involved in the coordination of limb movement and maintenance of muscular tone.

destinations.label: Cerebellum → Functional zones of the cerebellum

X2c9Tb0.title: Vestibulocerebellum
X2c9Tb0.description: A part of the cerebellum that receives input from the vestibular nuclei of cranial nerve VIII, the superior colliculi, and the visual cortex. Involved in ocular movement, gaze stability, and maintaining balance.

destinations.label: Cerebellum → Functional zones of the cerebellum

c2cagb0.title: Saphenofemoral junction
c2cagb0.description: The site at which the great saphenous vein passes through the saphenous opening in the deep fascia of the thigh to meet the femoral vein. Typically located ~ 4 cm inferolaterally to the pubic tubercle.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Vasculature
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

U2cbSb0.title: Superior cerebellar peduncles
U2cbSb0.description: A pair of white matter tracts that are located on either side in the dorsolateral region of the caudal midbrain and connect the midbrain with the cerebellum. They contain the cerebellothalamic and cerebellorubral tracts, which relay motor planning output signals from the cerebellum. They receive blood from the superior cerebellar artery.

media.title: Connections of the superior cerebellar peduncle

f2ckSb0.title: Inferior cerebellar peduncles
f2ckSb0.description: A pair of white matter tracts that are located on either side in the dorsolateral region of the medulla and connect the medulla with the cerebellum. They contain the posterior spinocerebellar, cuneocerebellar, trigeminocerebellar, olivocerebellar, and vestibulocerebellar tracts, which relay proprioceptive signals to the cerebellum, and the cerebellovestibular tract, which relays signals to the vestibular nuclei. They receive blood from the anterior and posterior inferior cerebellar arteries.

media.title: Connections of the inferior cerebellar peduncle

g2cFSb0.title: Alcoholic cerebellar degeneration
g2cFSb0.description: A condition caused by degeneration of Purkinje cells in the cerebellum due to chronic alcohol use. Both ethanol and malnutrition contribute to cerebellar atrophy. Manifests with gait and truncal ataxia. Neuroimaging typically shows degeneration of the cerebellar vermis (anterosuperior vermis). Can occur with other alcohol-related disorders (e.g., Wernicke encephalopathy) or as an isolated disorder.

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Complications of alcohol use

S2cySb0.title: Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate
S2cySb0.description: A carbohydrate metabolite formed by the phosphorylation of fructose-6-phosphate by phosphofructokinase-2. Activates phosphofructokinase-1, which promotes glycolysis. Conversion of fructose-2,6-bisphosphate back to fructose-6-phosphate by fructose bisphosphatase-2 promotes gluconeogenesis.

h2cchb0.title: Adipose triglyceride lipase
h2cchb0.description: A key enzyme that facilitates the release of fatty acids from triacylglycerol stores during intracellular lipolysis. Produces fatty acids for energy production.

32cShb0.title: Haptocorrin
32cShb0.description: A salivary glycoprotein that binds to vitamin B12 and protects it from the acidic environment in the stomach. In the duodenum, the pancreatic enzyme trypsin separates haptocorrin from vitamin B12 so that B12 can bind to intrinsic factor and be absorbed in the ileum.

i2cJhb0.title: Navicular bone
i2cJhb0.description: A boat-shaped bone located medially in the proximal foot. Articulates with the talus posteriorly, the cuboid laterally, and the three cuneiform bones anteriorly.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Bones and joints

media.title: Bones of the foot (dorsal and plantar views)

52ciRb0.title: Metatarsophalangeal joints
52ciRb0.description: The joints between the metatarsal bones and the proximal phalanges of the foot.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Bones and joints

media.title: Bones of the foot (dorsal and plantar views)

n2c7Rb0.title: West Nile meningoencephalitis
n2c7Rb0.description: A condition caused by West Nile virus infection. Typically manifests with signs of viral meningitis (e.g., fever, headache, meningeal signs) and encephalitis (e.g., altered mental status, extrapyramidal symptoms). Other symptoms might include malaise, myalgia, and anorexia. Symptoms typically last for 3-10 days. Associated with a morbilliform rash on the trunk and extremities.

destinations.label: Miscellaneous mosquito-borne diseases → Mosquito-borne Flavivirus diseases

L2cwRb0.title: Plantar fascia
L2cwRb0.description: A thick band of connective tissue that extends from the calcaneal tuberosity to the plantar aspect of the proximal phalanges of the toes. Supports the bony arches of the foot and facilitates foot movements.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Bones and joints

media.title: Plantar aponeurosis and the medial longitudinal arch of the foot

o2c0ib0.title: Capsule staining
o2c0ib0.description: A microbiologic diagnostic technique in which two stains are used - one acidic and one basic - to differentiate bacterial capsular material from the cell wall. This is especially useful to highlight the presence or absence of a capsule for the purpose of identifying encapsulated species such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, Klebsiella pneumoniae, or Haemophilus influenzae.

K2cUib0.title: Neuromuscular end plate
K2cUib0.description: A part of the cell membrane of striated muscle cells that lies in close proximity to the terminal motor neuron axon. Stimulation of nicotinic receptors at this site by acetylcholine results in muscle contraction.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

media.title: Signal transduction at the motor end plate

62cjib0.title: Babesia microti
62cjib0.description: A protozoal parasite that infects red blood cells and causes babesiosis. Typically transmitted via ticks (e.g., Ixodes).

I2cYQb0.title: Muscularis mucosa
I2cYQb0.description: A thin layer of smooth muscle that lies deep to the epithelium and lamina propria and separates the mucosa of the intestine from the submucosa. Considered the deepest mucosal layer.

r2cfQb0.title: Dicrotic notch
r2cfQb0.description: A slight increase in aortic pressure during the early portion of diastole. Corresponds to closure of the aortic valve.

s2ctQb0.title: CD14
s2ctQb0.description: A cell surface marker expressed primarily on macrophages. Recognizes pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) such as lipopolysaccharide.

E2c8jb0.title: Fertility factor
E2c8jb0.description: A bacterial plasmid that enables the transfer of genetic material between bacteria. Can exist freely in the cytoplasm or become integrated into the bacterial genome via recombination.

D2c1Pb0.title: Volumetric flow rate
D2c1Pb0.description: Defined in cardiac physiology as the amount of blood that flows through a valve per unit time.

w2chPb0.title: Sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase
w2chPb0.description: A sarcoplasmic calcium pump and exchanger that removes calcium ions from the cytosol. Facilitates termination of contraction in the plateau phase of the cardiac action potential.

-2cD4b0.title: Adductor canal
-2cD4b0.description: A musculofascial tunnel that extends from the apex of the femoral triangle to the adductor hiatus. Contains the femoral vessels, the saphenous nerve, and the nerve to the vastus medialis.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Femoral triangle and fasial compartments of the thigh

afcQkb0.title: Anthrax toxin protective antigen
afcQkb0.description: A component of anthrax toxin that binds to endothelial receptors and facilitates entry of edema factor and lethal factor into host cells.

bfcHkb0.title: Popliteal vein
bfcHkb0.description: A deep vein of the lower limb formed by the union of the anterior tibial, posterior tibial, and fibular veins at the inferior border of the popliteus. Continues at the adductor hiatus as the femoral vein, which drains the posterior and lower leg.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The popliteal fossa
Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

Xfc9kb0.title: Paraumbilical veins
Xfc9kb0.description: A collection of small veins that run in the round ligament of the liver and form an anastomosis between the portal circulation and caval circulation. Can become enlarged in patients with portal hypertension, which leads to caput medusae.

cfcaOb0.title: Superior epigastric vein
cfcaOb0.description: A superficial vein that runs along the anterior abdominal wall and drains into the internal thoracic vein. Anastomoses with the inferior epigastric vein near the umbilicus.

1fc2Ob0.title: Veins of Retzius
1fc2Ob0.description: A portosystemic shunt between branches of the superior mesenteric vein or inferior mesenteric vein and the branches of the inferior vena cava.

Tfc6lb0.title: Endochondral ossification
Tfc6lb0.description: The process by which bone is formed indirectly from mesenchymal cells via a cartilaginous model. Responsible for the formation of long bones and bones at the base of the skull.

Sfcylb0.title: Sialic acid
Sfcylb0.description: A neuraminic acid derivative found on most cell surfaces. Plays an important role in some viral infections (e.g., influenza virus, which has hemagglutinin that binds to sialic acid residues) and bacterial infections (e.g., S. pneumoniae, which uses sialic acid to facilitate adherence).

3fcSNb0.title: Histidine
3fcSNb0.description: An essential, glucogenic amino acid that is formed into histamine by decarboxylation. Unlike other basic amino acids (arginine, lysine), it has no net charge at body pH. Demands for histidine increase during growth periods.

RfclNb0.title: Efferent arteriole
RfclNb0.description: A blood vessel that carries previously filtered blood away from the glomerulus. These vessels, via coordinated dilation or constriction, play an important role in regulating glomerular filtration rate despite variations in systemic blood pressure.

ifcJNb0.title: Afferent arteriole
ifcJNb0.description: A blood vessel that supplies the glomerulus of the kidney for filtration. Plays an important role in controlling systemic blood pressure.

QfcuNb0.title: Coefficient of filtration
QfcuNb0.description: A measure of the glomerular permeability to fluid. Conceptually, it represents the amount of fluid that can be filtered through a given area of membrane in a given time at a set fluid pressure.

PfcWmb0.title: Iohexol
PfcWmb0.description: A iodinated contrast material. Adverse effects include anaphylaxis, thyrotoxic crisis, seizures, and nephrotoxicity.

OfcImb0.title: Obligate pathogens
OfcImb0.description: A pathogen that does not belong to the physiological flora and must cause a disease in order to be transmitted.

lfcvmb0.title: Bacterial capsule
lfcvmb0.description: An envelope that surrounds some bacterial cells. Usually composed of polysaccharide. B. anthracis has a polypeptide capsule. Acts as a virulence factor that facilitates adherence to host cells and protection against phagocytosis, lysozymes, reactive oxygen species, and complement-mediated lysis.

Nfc-mb0.title: Anaerobic bacteria
Nfc-mb0.description: An organism that does not require oxygen for growth.

5fci5b0.title: Virulence
5fci5b0.description: The severity of a disease caused by a pathogen. Expressed as the number of individuals who become severely ill or die due to an infection over the total number of individuals who have contracted the disease. LD50 is another parameter used to describe virulence.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

nfc75b0.title: Posterior antebrachial cutaneous nerve
nfc75b0.description: A superficial nerve that arises from the radial nerve and supplies sensation to the skin over the posterior part of the forearm.

ofc0Mb0.title: Pyridoxal kinase
ofc0Mb0.description: An enzyme that phosphorylates pyridoxal to pyridoxal phosphate, the active form of vitamin B6.

KfcUMb0.title: Celiac lymph nodes
KfcUMb0.description: A collection of lymph nodes located near the origin of the celiac trunk from the aorta. They receive lymphatic drainage from the stomach, upper duodenum, liver, pancreas, spleen, and superior, and inferior mesenteric lymph nodes. They drain into the preaortic lymph nodes.

6fcjMb0.title: Pre-aortic lymph nodes
6fcjMb0.description: A cluster of lymph nodes that lie anterior to the abdominal aorta. They receive lymphatic drainage from the celiac, superior mesenteric, and inferior mesenteric lymph nodes and drain into the intestinal lymphatic trunk.

pfcLMb0.title: Common iliac lymph nodes
pfcLMb0.description: A cluster of lymph nodes located in the pelvis, adjacent to the common iliac vessels. They receive lymphatic drainage from the middle third of the ureter and the internal and external iliac lymph nodes. They drain into the para-aortic lymph nodes.

JfcsMb0.title: Cysterna chyli
JfcsMb0.description: A lymphatic structure that is formed by the union of the intestinal and left lumbar lymphatic trunks (less commonly, right lumbar lymphatic trunk) and continues as the thoracic duct. Receives lymph from the abdominal viscera, abdominal wall (below level of the umbilicus), and lower limbs.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Lymphatics of the abdominal cavity

qfcCMb0.title: Hypoproliferative anemia
qfcCMb0.description: Normocytic, normochromic anemia characterized by a low reticulocyte count (<2–2.5%). Typically seen in chronic inflammation (due to abnormal sensitivity to iron and erythropoietin), chronic kidney disease (due to insufficient erythropoietin production), early iron deficiency anemia (before the hypochromic, microcytic stage), and myelodysplastic syndromes.

IfcYnb0.title: Gliosis
IfcYnb0.description: A collection of nonspecific, reactive changes (e.g., proliferation, hypertrophy) to glial cells in response to CNS damage.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

rfcfnb0.title: Rexed laminae
rfcfnb0.description: A collection of ten layers of the gray matter of the spinal cord. Each contains distinct cellular structure and function.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

HfcKnb0.title: Familial combined hyperlipidemia
HfcKnb0.description: An autosomal-dominant condition caused by defects in genes that encode apolipoproteins and/or lipoprotein lipase. Manifests with increased serum concentrations of triglycerides, LDL cholesterol, and VLDL cholesterol. Associated with early atherosclerotic complications (cardiovascular disease).

sfctnb0.title: Powder-burn lesion
sfctnb0.description: Black, brown, or bluish nodules or cystic structures seen on the serosal surfaces of the ovaries and peritoneum in cases of endometriosis.

GfcBnb0.title: Total body water
GfcBnb0.description: The total amount of water in the body, which is approximately 60% of body mass. Further subdivided into extracellular fluid (e.g., interstitial fluid and plasma) and intracellular fluid (e.g., in erythrocytes).

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function

ufcpLb0.title: End-diastolic volume
ufcpLb0.description: The volume of blood in the right or left ventricle at the end of filling (diastole), before contraction (systole). Dependent on ventricular distensibility and ventricular filling pressure. Based on the Frank-Starling mechanism, an increase causes in EDV increases cardiac preload by stretching cardiac myocyte sarcomeres, which results in increased myocardial contractility.

Efc8Lb0.title: Metalization
Efc8Lb0.description: The deposition of metal particles into the skin after exposure to a powerful electric current. The current is transmitted to metallic objects (e.g., jewelry), which can become very hot and cause local burns.

destinations.label: Environmental pathology → Electrical and lightning injuries

vfcALb0.title: Phase I block
vfcALb0.description: The principal action of succinylcholine, whereby it acts on nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction and results in prolonged depolarization at the motor end plate. Results in muscle contraction and fasciculation followed by muscle relaxation. Potentiated by cholinesterase inhibitors.

media.title: Mechanism of action: depolarizing muscle relaxants

Dfc1ob0.title: Phase II block
Dfc1ob0.description: A phenomenon associated with large and/or frequent doses of succinylcholine. Despite continued depolarization by succinylcholine, the postsynaptic membrane repolarizes and becomes resistant to depolarization by acetylcholine (desensitized), which leads to prolonged muscle relaxation. Can be reversed with cholinesterase inhibitors.

wfchob0.title: Butyrylcholinesterase
wfchob0.description: An enzyme found in the liver, brain, kidneys, pancreas, and blood that can hydrolyze several choline-based esters (e.g., succinylcholine). Decreased serum levels can result from cirrhosis or organophosphate pesticide exposure (occupational or accidental).

9fcNob0.title: Common acute lymphoblastic leukemia antigen
9fcNob0.description: An integral membrane protein expressed by lymphoid progenitors. Used as a marker in the evaluation of acute lymphocytic leukemia and some other lymphoid malignancies (e.g., Burkitt lymphoma). It also functions as a metalloproteinase.

Cfcqob0.title: Acute myelomonocytic leukemia
Cfcqob0.description: An uncommon form of acute myeloid leukemia characterized by the proliferation of abnormal neutrophil and monocyte precursors (e.g., myeloblasts, monoblasts). Can be detected morphologically or with immunophenotypical markers (e.g., CD14, CD11c, CD64).

xfcEob0.title: HLA-DR
xfcEob0.description: An MHC II cell surface receptor. Various subtypes are associated with specific diseases (e.g., HLA-DR5 with Hashimoto thyroiditis).

Bfczob0.title: Acute megakaryoblastic leukemia
Bfczob0.description: An uncommon form of acute myeloid leukemia characterized by the proliferation of abnormal megakaryoblasts. Can be detected with immunophenotypical markers (e.g., CD41, CD61). Associated with myelofibrosis.

yfcdKb0.title: Tetrahydrofolate polyglutamate
yfcdKb0.description: The biologically active form of folate. Folate monoglutamate (the transport form of folate) is transported into cells and metabolized to folate polyglutamate by folylpolyglutamate synthetase.

AfcRKb0.title: Mixed oxygen venous saturation
AfcRKb0.description: The percentage of oxygen bound to hemoglobin when sampled from the right side of the heart. Accurate measurements, usually made from pulmonary artery catheters, reflect oxygen saturation in blood from the superior and inferior vena cava as well as the coronary sinus. Used as a marker of oxygen consumption in tissues.

destinations.label: Arterial blood gas analysis → Mixed oxygen venous saturation

_fc5Kb0.title: Arterial oxygen saturation
_fc5Kb0.description: The percentage of oxygen-saturated hemoglobin compared to total hemoglobin in arterial blood. Measured by arterial blood gas analysis. Can be estimated on pulse-oximetry.

destinations.label: Arterial blood gas analysis → Arterial blood gas analysis

zfcrKb0.title: Arterial oxygen content
zfcrKb0.description: The amount of oxygen transported by arterial blood. Includes the fraction bound to hemoglobin as well as oxygen dissolved in plasma. Calculated by the equation: CaO₂ (mL/dL) = (1.31 × Hgb × SaO₂ × 0.01) + (0.0225 × PaO₂). Clinically estimated from arterial blood sampling.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen transport and conditions that affect oxygenation

-fcDKb0.title: Methylergometrine
-fcDKb0.description: An ergot alkaloid agent used to manage postpartum hemorrhage secondary to uterine atony. Increases the frequency and amplitude of uterine contractions, which shortens labor and reduces blood loss. Contraindications for use include pre-existing hypertension and preeclampsia.

ZTcZ6b0.title: Counterstain
ZTcZ6b0.description: A histological diagnostic technique in which a primary stain is used to identify certain cells of interest, and a second, contrasting stain (the "counterstain") is used to further highlight cells that do not stain with the first stain. A common example is eosin staining as a counterstain to hematoxylin or safranin dye as a counterstain to crystal violet in Gram staining.

0Tce6b0.title: Excitotoxicity
0Tce6b0.description: A process in which an excess of the excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate overactivates receptors and causes neuronal damage and cell death. Can occur during status epilepticus and traumatic brain injury.

aTcQ6b0.title: AMPA receptor
aTcQ6b0.description: An ionotropic receptor that depolarizes neurons when activated by glutamate (and less frequently, glycine). Critical for controlling synaptic plasticity and memory function. Overactivation can cause excitotoxicity and cell death.

cTcapb0.title: Stromal cell-derived factor 1
cTcapb0.description: A chemokine that binds to CXCR4 and plays an important role in many processes, including the activation of hematopoietic stem cells and cell adhesion molecules.

1Tc2pb0.title: Right shift of the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve
1Tc2pb0.description: A shift of the hemoglobin dissociation curve to the right (due to ↑ temperature, ↑ 2,3-diphosphoglycerate, ↑ pCO₂ and/or ↓ pH), resulting in a decreased affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve

dTcopb0.title: Abduction
dTcopb0.description: An anatomical descriptor for movement away from the body's midline.

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

VTcGpb0.title: Cilastatin
VTcGpb0.description: A drug that inhibits dehydropeptidase, a renal tubular enzyme that metabolizes imipenem. Cilastatin is typically administered with imipenem to increase its duration of action.

eTcxpb0.title: Schuffner granules
eTcxpb0.description: A histopathologic finding of dark, brick-red dots seen within the cytoplasm of erythrocytes infected with Plasmosdium vivax or Plasmodium ovale.

media.title: Tertian malaria: immature trophozoite in Plasmodium vivax infection

UTcbJb0.title: End-systolic volume
UTcbJb0.description: The volume of blood in the ventricles at the end of contraction (systole). Dependent on contractility and afterload. When compared to the end-diastolic volume as a ratio, it yields the ventricular ejection fraction.

fTckJb0.title: Procollagen
fTckJb0.description: A triple-helical intermediate in collagen synthesis that is formed from preprocollagen by the hydroxylation of proline and lysine residues, the subsequent glycosylation of hydroxylysine residues, and finally the formation of disulfide and hydrogen bonds between the preprocollagen chains.

TTc6Jb0.title: Preprocollagen
TTc6Jb0.description: A collagen precursor polypeptide chain that consists of a pro-α chain with repeating Gly-X-Y sequences, where X and Y are typically proline or lysine.

gTcFJb0.title: Melanosome
gTcFJb0.description: An organelle that serves as the site for the synthesis and storage of melanin. Dendritic processes transfer melanosomes to adjacent and distant keratinocytes.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Cells of the skin

STcyJb0.title: Partial albinism
STcyJb0.description: A genetic condition characterized by the partial absence of melanin pigment from melanosomes in the body due to defects in the biosynthesis of melanin.

hTccqb0.title: Total albinism
hTccqb0.description: A genetic condition characterized by the total absence of melanin pigment from melanosomes in the body due to defects in the biosynthesis of melanin.

3TcSqb0.title: Melanoblast
3TcSqb0.description: A melanocyte precursor derived from neural crest cells.

RTclqb0.title: Dihydroxyphenylalanine
RTclqb0.description: An amino acid derived from tyrosine that is the precursor from which catecholamines (i.e., dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine) are synthesized. Refers to both enantiomers (L-DOPA and D-DOPA), of which L-DOPA is biochemically active in humans. L-DOPA is used to treat the symptoms of Parkinson disease by increasing dopamine synthesis.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla

iTcJqb0.title: Hemoglobin Barts
iTcJqb0.description: A form of hemoglobin formed by γ-globin chains that develop when there is a deficiency of alpha globin chains in alpha thalassemias. It is most pronounced when all 4 alleles for alpha globulin are missing, so-called Hb Barts disease, and leads to hydrops fetalis.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin variants

QTcuqb0.title: Epidermotropism
QTcuqb0.description: The abnormal presence of lymphocytes in the epidermis (e.g., in patients with mycosis fungoides and cutaneous T-cell lymphomas).

PTcWIb0.title: Respiratory quotient
PTcWIb0.description: The ratio of carbon dioxide produced to oxygen consumed by the body during the metabolism of various substrates. Values of 0.7 for lipids, 0.8 for proteins, and 1.0 for carbohydrates are typical.

4Tc3Ib0.title: Alveolar gas equation
4Tc3Ib0.description: An equation used to determine the alveolar partial pressure of oxygen (PAO₂): PAO₂ ≈ [FiO₂ × (atmospheric pressure - 47)] - [(PaCO₂)/R], where FiO₂ is the concentration of inhaled oxygen, PaCO₂ is the partial pressure of carbon dioxide in the artery, atmospheric pressure is 760 mm Hg at sea level, and R is the respiratory quotient.

kTcmIb0.title: Internal iliac vein
kTcmIb0.description: A large vein that drains the pelvis and joins the external iliac vein to form the common iliac vein.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

OTcIIb0.title: Internal pudendal veins
OTcIIb0.description: A pair of veins that run along with the internal pudendal artery. Drain the perineum, including the anal canal below the pectinate line, before emptying into the internal iliac veins.

media.title: Pelvis with blood supply of the anal canal

lTcvIb0.title: Superior mesenteric vein
lTcvIb0.description: A vein that drains the structures derived from the midgut (e.g., ascending and transverse colon). Runs with the superior mesenteric artery and joins the splenic vein to form the portal vein.

NTc-Ib0.title: External iliac veins
NTc-Ib0.description: A pair of veins that begin as the continuation of the femoral veins as they cross the inguinal ligament. Each joins an internal iliac vein to form a common iliac vein.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

mTcVrb0.title: Inferior mesenteric vein
mTcVrb0.description: A vein that drains the structures derived from the hindgut (e.g., splenic flexure, sigmoid colon, descending colon, rectum). Typically drains into the splenic vein.

media.title: Tributaries of the hepatic portal vein

5Tcirb0.title: Ventilation-perfusion ratio
5Tcirb0.description: The volumetric ratio of air that reaches the alveoli (ventilation) to alveolar blood supply (perfusion) per minute. Typical value is ~ 0.8. Higher at the apex of the lung (V > Q) because the lung bases are better ventilated and perfused than the apices in an upright position.

MTcMrb0.title: t(14:18)
MTcMrb0.description: A chromosomal abnormality leading to translocation of heavy-chain Ig (from chromosome 14) and BCL-2 (from chromosome 18) that is often seen in follicular lymphoma. The translocation leads to overexpression of the BCL-2 gene, causing pathological resistance to apoptosis.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

nTc7rb0.title: Carbon dioxide transport
nTc7rb0.description: The transport of carbon dioxide in the blood. Occurs in three forms: 1) dissolved CO2 in plasma, 2) CO2 buffered with water and transported as carbonic acid, and 3) protein-bound CO2 (especially to hemoglobin). The majority of CO2 transport (75%) occurs inside erythrocytes.

JTcs7b0.title: Catechol-O-methyltransferase
JTcs7b0.description: An enzyme that degrades catecholamines by adding a methyl group to its structure. Substrates include dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla

qTcC7b0.title: Striae gravidarum
qTcC7b0.description: A scarring of the dermis that manifests during pregnancy as erythematous, violaceous, and/or hypopigmented linear striations on the abdomen. Typically asymptomatic.

ITcYHb0.title: Lepromin skin test
ITcYHb0.description: A test used to classify leprosy. Lepromin (an antigen isolated from heat-killed M. leprae) is injected intradermally, and the skin is assessed 3-4 weeks later for induration. Measures the ability of a patient to mount a T-cell response. Positive in cases of tuberculoid leprosy; negative in cases of lepromatous leprosy. Can be positive in patients with no leprosy exposure or infection.

rTcfHb0.title: α-thalassemia minor
rTcfHb0.description: A hereditary hemoglobinopathy characterized by mutations in both α-globin genes. This results in impaired synthesis of both α-chains of hemoglobin. Affected individuals are typically asymptomatic. Causes microcytosis with or without mild anemia.

7Tc4Hb0.title: Gastric varices
7Tc4Hb0.description: The dilation of gastric submucosal veins, most commonly located in the fundus and cardia that is caused by the formation of portosystemic collaterals in individuals with portal hypertension. Can occur as isolated gastric varices or as gastric extensions of esophageal varices.

HTcKHb0.title: FABER test
HTcKHb0.description: A physical examination procedure performed to evaluate for pathology of the hip or sacroiliac joint. With the patient in the supine position, the leg is Flexed, ABducted, and Externally Rotated (FABER), and the heel is placed on the contralateral knee. Pain in the ipsilateral joints of the pelvis indicates a positive test.

sTctHb0.title: Structural gene
sTctHb0.description: Gene that encodes for any RNA or protein product (including enzyme or structural protein) that does not participate in regulation.

GTcBHb0.title: Platelet adhesion
GTcBHb0.description: The first step in response to vascular endothelial injury, in which platelets adhere to endothelial adhesion molecules (e.g., glycoprotein Ib) to initiate the process of platelet activation.

tTcXsb0.title: Weibel-Palade body
tTcXsb0.description: A storage granule found in endothelial cells. Contains von Willebrand factor and selectins (e.g., P-selectin).

FTcgsb0.title: Glycoprotein Ib
FTcgsb0.description: A glycoprotein that forms part of the receptor for von Willebrand factor on the endothelial lining. Mediates platelet adhesion. Deficiency of GpIb causes Bernard-Soulier syndrome.

8TcOsb0.title: Nonmutually exclusive probability
8TcOsb0.description: The likelihood of two events occurring simultaneously (e.g., the probability that a patient is male and has hypertension).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

uTcpsb0.title: Mutually exclusive probability
uTcpsb0.description: A condition in which the likelihood of two events occurring at the same time is zero (i.e., only one of the outcomes can occur at a time).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

wTchGb0.title: Propionic aciduria
wTchGb0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder caused by a deficiency of propionyl CoA carboxylase, which converts propionyl-CoA to methylmalonyl-CoA. Usually manifests in infancy with vomiting, lethargy, hypotonia, failure to thrive, seizures, anion gap metabolic acidosis, hyperammonemia, ketotic hypoglycemia, and urinary excretion of propionic acid.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Organic acidemias

9TcNGb0.title: Even-chain fatty acid
9TcNGb0.description: A type of fatty acid with an even number of carbon atoms. β-oxidation breaks down odd-chain fatty acids into acetyl-CoA.

CTcqGb0.title: Threonine
CTcqGb0.description: A polar essential amino acid that is both glucogenic and ketogenic.

xTcEGb0.title: Propionyl-CoA
xTcEGb0.description: An intermediary in the metabolism of odd-chain fatty acids, pyrimidines (thymine, uracil), and certain amino acids (isoleucine, valine, threonine, methionine). Converted to succinyl-CoA, which then enters the TCA cycle.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

yTcdtb0.title: Methylmalonyl-CoA
yTcdtb0.description: An intermediary in the metabolism of odd-chain fatty acids, the amino acids isoleucine, valine, methionine, and threonine, and the pyrimidines thymine and uracil. Formed from propionyl-CoA by propionyl-CoA carboxylase and converted by methylmalonyl-CoA mutase to succinyl-CoA, which then enters the TCA cycle.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

ATcRtb0.title: β-hydroxybutyrate
ATcRtb0.description: A ketone body produced by the liver during states of ketogenesis (e.g., fasting states, insulin deficiency). Not typically detected by standard urine ketone tests.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Ketone body metabolism

_Tc5tb0.title: Catechol group
_Tc5tb0.description: An organic carbon structure that contains a carbon ring and 2 hydroxyl groups. Catechol-containing monoamine (catecholamines) include norepinephrine, epinephrine, and dopamine.

zTcrtb0.title: Galactitol
zTcrtb0.description: A sugar alcohol produced by the reduction of galactose. Serum and urine levels are elevated in patients with disorders of galactose metabolism (e.g., galactokinase deficiency, classic galactosemia), which can lead to deposition in the lenses that causes cataracts.

-TcDtb0.title: Endosomal sorting complexes required for transport
-TcDtb0.description: A protein complex involved protein sorting and transport, including viral budding and vesicle formation.

bgcHFb0.title: Postvasectomy pain syndrome
bgcHFb0.description: A condition characterized by chronic, dull, aching pain in the testes in patients who have had a vasectomy. Caused by the accumulation of testicular fluid in the epididymis. Thought to be distinct from typical postprocedural pain.

Xgc9Fb0.title: Barometric pressure
Xgc9Fb0.description: The pressure exerted by the atmosphere at any given point. Decreases with elevation.

cgca8b0.title: Partial pressure
cgca8b0.description: The pressure exerted by a specific gas in a mixture of gases if it were alone at the same temperature and volume.

1gc28b0.title: Physiologically appropriate secondary polycythemia
1gc28b0.description: An increase in total red blood cell mass as a result of an appropriate compensatory response to a prolonged reduction in tissue oxygen saturation (e.g., living at high altitude).

WgcP8b0.title: Orexigenic hormones
WgcP8b0.description: A group of hormones that stimulate appetite. Includes ghrelin, agouti-related protein, and neuropeptide Y.

dgco8b0.title: Radiofemoral delay
dgco8b0.description: A delay in palpation of the femoral arterial pulse when compared to the radial arterial pulse. Can be caused by coarctation of the aorta, vascular obstruction (e.g., atherosclerosis), and aneurysms.

Ugcbub0.title: Capping
Ugcbub0.description: The addition of a cap of 7-methylguanosine to the 5' end of hnRNA to form the five-prime cap. Occurs during transcription. Capping occurs in a 5' → 3' direction, leaving the 5' end open.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Post-transcriptional modification (RNA processing)

Tgc6ub0.title: Catabolite activator protein
Tgc6ub0.description: A protein whose binding to the promoter region of DNA is enabled by cAMP. Promotes the subsequent binding of RNA polymerase.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Regulation of transcription

Sgcyub0.title: Antifibrinolytic
Sgcyub0.description: A group of drugs that impair fibrinolysis, typically by interfering with plasmin formation. Examples include aminocaproic acid and tranexamic acid.

3gcSEb0.title: Pulmonary atresia
3gcSEb0.description: A congenital heart defect characterized by right ventricular outflow obstruction, typically due to failure of pulmonary valve formation. This defect prevents the right heart from pumping blood into the lungs directly. Lung perfusion, therefore, depends on shunt flow from the right side of the heart to the left and from the aorta to the pulmonary arteries.

igcJEb0.title: Cytosine deaminase
igcJEb0.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the reaction between cytosine and water to uracil and ammonia. Fungal cytosine deaminase metabolizes flucytosine to 5-fluorouracil.

jgc_Eb0.title: Karnofsky performance status
jgc_Eb0.description: A clinical tool for measuring a patient's functional capacity. The patient's ability to perform activities of daily living is used to calculate a score between 0 and 100 (0 implies patient death, 100 indicates no limitations to activity). The Karnofsky score can be used prognostically and/or help determine appropriate treatment strategies in cancer therapy.

destinations.label: Overview of palliative medicine → Outcome measurement in palliative medicine

PgcWvb0.title: Carbonic anhydrase II
PgcWvb0.description: A cytosolic isoform of the enzyme carbonic anhydrase, which catalyzes the interconversion of carbon dioxide and water to bicarbonate and protons. A defect in this enzyme is seen in conditions such as osteopetrosis and type 3 renal tubular acidosis.

4gc3vb0.title: Supraglottis
4gc3vb0.description: An anatomical region from the inferior boundary of the hyoid bone to the false vocal cords.

OgcIvb0.title: Delayed sequence intubation
OgcIvb0.description: A method of procedural sedation that allows for adequate preoxygenation prior to endotracheal intubation. Typically involves the administration of sedating agents that do not depress airway reflexes or respiratory drive (e.g. ketamine, dexmedetomidine) and may include attempted visualization of the glottis prior to intubation with paralytics.

destinations.label: Airway management → High-risk conditions for intubation

Ngc-vb0.title: Reactive atypia
Ngc-vb0.description: A collection of benign cellular changes (e.g., enlarged nucleolus or multiple nucleoli, loss of cytoplasmic clearing) without neoplastic change as a result of inflammation and injury.

mgcVDb0.title: Aquaporin-2
mgcVDb0.description: A membrane channel that incorporates into the membranes of the distal convoluted tubules and collecting ducts of the kidney as a result of antidiuretic hormone activity. Conducts water molecules and prevents the passage of ions and other small molecules. Draws water out of the urine and into hyperosmolar kidney tissue, which concentrates the urine.

destinations.label: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion → Pathophysiology

media.title: Effect of ADH on the kidney

ngc7Db0.title: Noninvasive papillary urothelial carcinoma
ngc7Db0.description: A malignant growth in the bladder that forms finger-like projections on its inner surface without invading deeper tissue.

LgcwDb0.title: Foam stability index
LgcwDb0.description: A semi-quantitative test used to assess fetal lung maturity. Amniotic fluid is mixed with ethanol. In the presence of adequate surfactant, foam can form. The index refers to the highest quantity of ethanol that can be added to amniotic fluid with the formation of stable foam.

KgcUwb0.title: Lecithin-sphingomyelin ratio
KgcUwb0.description: A marker of fetal lung maturity that compares the amniotic fluid concentrations of the glycoproteins lecithin and sphingomyelin, which are components of surfactant. A ratio of > 2.4 indicates lung maturity; a ratio < 1.5 is associated with a higher risk of developing fetal respiratory distress syndrome.

Jgcswb0.title: Glutathione reduction
Jgcswb0.description: A reaction that converts oxidized glutathione to its reduced form. This reduced form functions as an antioxidant that prevents the cellular damage caused by reactive oxygen species.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Metabolism of erythrocytes

media.title: Reduction and oxidation reactions of glutathione

qgcCwb0.title: 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate mutase
qgcCwb0.description: An enzyme present only in RBCs and non-erythroid cells of the placenta that converts 1,3-BPG to 2,3-BPG. When 2,3-BPG binds to hemoglobin, it causes a conformational change that results in oxygen release.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Metabolism of erythrocytes

rgcf9b0.title: Osteocalcin
rgcf9b0.description: A hormone secreted by osteoblasts that increases bone mineralization and regulates calcium ion homeostasis. Also stimulates insulin and adiponectin secretion. Often used as a marker for bone formation processes.

7gc49b0.title: Hole zones
7gc49b0.description: Spaces within the certain types of collagen fibrils (e.g., type 1 collagen) that are formed by the staggered arrangement of the collagen triple helices.

HgcK9b0.title: Interferon
HgcK9b0.description: A cell-signaling protein secreted by cells infected by viruses, bacteria, or parasites, as well as by leukocytes and fibroblasts in response to infection or neoplastic proliferation. Interferons have antiviral, antimicrobial, and antiproliferative properties. Part of the innate immune system.

destinations.label: Cytokines and eicosanoids → Interferons and tumor necrosis factor family

sgct9b0.title: Mometasone
sgct9b0.description: A glucocorticoid that is used topically (e.g., for eczema) or as an inhaled steroid (e.g., for asthma).

GgcB9b0.title: Inhaled glucocorticoid
GgcB9b0.description: A glucocorticoid that is dispersed via aerosol and inhaled. Used most commonly in the management of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Adverse effects include oral candidiasis and hoarseness due to vocal cord atrophy.

tgcXCb0.title: Secondar lymphoid organs
tgcXCb0.description: A lymphoid organ in which immune cells interact with extrinsic antigens to generate an antigen-specific response. Secondary lymphoid organs include the spleen for blood-borne antigens, the lymph nodes for antigens in lymphatic fluid, tonsils for inhaled antigens, and the Peyer patches for ingested antigens.

FgcgCb0.title: Primary lymphoid organs
FgcgCb0.description: A lymphoid organ that generates mature lymphocytes from immature progenitor cells. Examples include the bone marrow, which produces immune cells and facilitates B-cell maturation, and the thymus, which facilitates T-cell maturation.

8gcOCb0.title: V(D)J recombination
8gcOCb0.description: A process in which different parts of the variable (V), diversity (D), and joining (J) gene segments are brought together by site-specific recombination to produce immunoglobulin heavy chains or T-cell receptors. V(D)J recombination is an antigen-independent process that is involved in the generation of antibody and T-cell receptor diversity.

ugcpCb0.title: Bordet-Gengou agar
ugcpCb0.description: A culture medium used to isolate Bordetella spp. Contains potato extract, blood, and glycerol.

Egc8Cb0.title: Lung neuroendocrine tumor
Egc8Cb0.description: A rare type of neuroendocrine lung tumor that consists predominantly of neuroendocrine enterochromaffin cells, which stain positive for chromogranin A.

vgcACb0.title: Split hand syndrome
vgcACb0.description: A wasting pattern that frequently occurs as an early sign of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, in which the muscles of the thenar eminence atrophy due to degeneration of the lateral portion of the anterior horn of the spinal cord.

Dgc1xb0.title: Nedocromil sodium
Dgc1xb0.description: A mast cell stabilizer used to treat chronic asthma. Associated with minimal adverse effects, which include throat irritation and cough.

wgchxb0.title: Muscularis propria (gastrointestinal tract)
wgchxb0.description: The muscular layer of the intestinal wall that lies superficial to the submucosa. Consists of an inner circular layer and outer longitudinal layer of smooth muscle. Contains the Auerbach (myenteric) nerve plexus.

Cgcqxb0.title: Lamina propria
Cgcqxb0.description: A layer of connective tissue that lies deep to the epithelium. Contains fibroblasts, immune cells, blood vessels, and other cells and structures that support the overlying epithelium.

xgcExb0.title: Retinoic acid receptor
xgcExb0.description: A nuclear hormone receptor activated by retinoid derivatives such as vitamin A. Together with RXR, these receptors function as paired heterodimers, which are bound to DNA in their inactive form. Upon ligand activation, RAR-RXR initiates transcription and leads to a change in gene expression.

ygcdBb0.title: Mollaret meningitis
ygcdBb0.description: A rare but benign recurrent aseptic meningitis caused by HSV-2. Affected patients have recurrent episodes of meningitis (headache, meningismus) with transient neurological symptoms (in 50% of cases). Most patients have spontaneous remission of symptoms and no long-term neurological sequelae.

destinations.label: Herpes simplex virus infections → Subtypes and variants

AgcRBb0.title: Reverse use-dependence
AgcRBb0.description: A phenomenon in which the effects of a drug decrease as the heart rate increases. Antiarrhythmics that exhibit this phenomenon are more effective at preventing arrhythmias at normal or slower heart rates.

_gc5Bb0.title: Contraction alkalosis
_gc5Bb0.description: An increase in serum pH as a result of intravascular volume loss of fluid with a relatively low bicarbonate concentration (e.g., from hemorrhage, vomiting, diarrhea, diuretic use). Caused by the effects of aldosterone and angiotensin II. Angiotensin II increases Na+/H+ exchange in the proximal tubules to promote renal excretion of H+ ions (and increase bicarbonate reabsorption) to compensate for the loss of Na+. Aldosterone and angiotensin II increase the activity of H+ ATPase pumps in type A intercalated cells located in the collecting ducts which increase H+ excretion and bicarbonate reabsorption.

zgcrBb0.title: Coenzyme Q10
zgcrBb0.description: A coenzyme that plays a role in energy production by muscle cells. Reduction in coenzyme Q10 synthesis may play a role in statin-related muscle injuries.

-gcDBb0.title: Humoral immune response
-gcDBb0.description: The parts of the immune system mediated by proteins and other macromolecules that are secreted into bodily fluids and/or the bloodstream. The humoral immune response of the innate immune system includes acute phase reactants and the complement system. The humoral immune response of the adaptive immune system includes B cells and secreted antibodies.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

ZScZyb0.title: Bronchial epithelium
ZScZyb0.description: A continuous layer of epithelial cells that lines the bronchial tree. Consists of goblet, ciliated, and basal cells. Acts as a barrier to maintain the normal airway interface and activates inflammatory cells in response to inhaled irritants. Facilitates the response to chronic inflammation by means of tissue repair, fibrosis, and squamous metaplasia.

aScQyb0.title: Lateral corticospinal tract
aScQyb0.description: A descending white matter tract composed of myelinated axons of upper motor neurons that originate from the cerebral cortex. The majority (~ 90%) of the fibers within this tract decussate. Terminates on anterior horn cells of the spinal cord. Provides voluntary motor control over contralateral extremity muscles.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

media.title: Overview of the ascending and descending pathways of the spinal cord

YScnyb0.title: Immune dysregulation, polyendocrinopathy, enteropathy, X-linked syndrome
YScnyb0.description: A rare X-linked autoimmune disease that most commonly affects males. Manifests in the first 6 months of life with enteropathy, skin conditions (eczema, erythroderma, psoriasis), type 1 diabetes mellitus, and thyroid disease. It is caused by a mutation in the FOXP3 gene, which is essential for the production and normal function of regulatory T cells.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital T-cell immunodeficiencies

bScHyb0.title: STAT3 gene
bScHyb0.description: A gene that belongs to the signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) gene family. It regulates genes that are involved in many cellular functions, such as cell growth and division, cell movement, and apoptosis. STAT3 mutations are the underlying cause of sporadic and dominant forms of the hyper-IgE syndrome.

XSc9yb0.title: World Health Organization
XSc9yb0.description: A specialized governing body within the United Nations that is responsible for global and regional public health research, implementation, and guidelines.

cScaAb0.title: High value test
cScaAb0.description: A test in which an abnormal or diagnostic result must be greater in value than a set cutoff value for that particular test (e.g., serum lipase concentration for the evaluation of pancreatitis).

1Sc2Ab0.title: Low value test
1Sc2Ab0.description: A test in which an abnormal or diagnostic result must be lower in value than a set cutoff value for that particular test (e.g., serum hemoglobin concentration for the evaluation of anemia).

WScPAb0.title: RNA polymerase I
WScPAb0.description: An eukaryotic enzyme that transcribes rRNA from DNA within the nucleolus.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  RNA polymerases and transcription factors

dScoAb0.title: Pyruvate kinase
dScoAb0.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the final step of glycolysis, in which phosphoenolpyruvate undergoes dephosphorylation to pyruvate, and thereby producing one molecule of ATP.

VScGAb0.title: Prodigiosin
VScGAb0.description: A red pigment produced by Serratia marcescens.

eScxAb0.title: Staphyloxanthin
eScxAb0.description: A pigment produced by some strains of Staphylococcus aureus. It lends the bacterium its characteristic golden color. With its antioxidant effect, staphyloxanthin also acts as a virulence factor, working to neutralize reactive oxygen species.

UScb_b0.title: Interleukin-13
UScb_b0.description: A cytokine that is primarily produced by Th2 CD4 cells. It activates the alternative macrophage activation pathway and acts on B cells to induce isotype switching to IgE

2ScT_b0.title: Interleukin-21
2ScT_b0.description: A cytokine produced by Th2 and Th17 CD4 cells. IL-21 decreases IgE production, promotes the differentiation of natural killer T cells and B cells, and acts as an autocrine signal to induce Th17 differentiation.

fSck_b0.title: Classical macrophage activation
fSck_b0.description: A pathway of macrophage activation in which the macrophages are primed by interferon-gamma, which is secreted from Th1 cells and subsequently activated by microbial products (e.g., bacterial lipopolysaccharides). Classical macrophage activation is a pro-inflammatory mechanism that serves to destroy pathogens, but it can lead to concurrent tissue damage.

TSc6_b0.title: Choristoma
TSc6_b0.description: The presence of normal tissue at a site where this type of tissue is not normally found (e.g., gastric tissue in Meckel diverticulum).

gScF_b0.title: RNA polymerase III
gScF_b0.description: A eukaryotic enzyme that transcribes tRNA from DNA in the nucleolus.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  RNA polymerases and transcription factors

SScy_b0.title: Dermatophytes
SScy_b0.description: A group of fungi that infect keratinized tissue and cause tinea (e.g., tinea pedia). Includes the genera Microsporum, Epidermophyton, and Trichophyton.

hScczb0.title: Microsporum
hScczb0.description: A genus of fungi that infects keratinized tissue and causes dermatophyte infections (e.g., tinea pedis).

iScJzb0.title: Suppurative Inflammation
iScJzb0.description: A descriptor for conditions that cause inflammation and the production of purulent exudate (e.g., cutaneous infections).

QScuzb0.title: Pulmonary hyperinflation
QScuzb0.description: An abnormal increase in the functional residual capacity of the lung and a complication of the increased compliance of the lungs commonly seen in chronic obstructive pulmonary lung disease. Total lung capacity is also increased in these patients and causes flattening of the diaphragm on chest X-ray.

jSc_zb0.title: Leiomyoma
jSc_zb0.description: A type of benign tumor composed of smooth muscle.

4Sc3-b0.title: Anergy
4Sc3-b0.description: A lack of a normal immune response to particular antigens, cytokines, and allergens. Can be due to a lack of costimulatory signals. Anergy testing is a diagnostic procedure used to obtain information on the competence of the cellular immune system (e.g., PPD tuberculin skin test).

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → Immune tolerance and autoimmunity

kScm-b0.title: Diffuse axonal injury
kScm-b0.description: A shearing neuronal trauma secondary to rapid acceleration, deceleration, and/or rotational injuries. Causes microscopy changes in the brain that may not be evident on imaging.

lScv-b0.title: Adenosine diphosphate
lScv-b0.description: A nucleoside diphosphate that can be converted to adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and adenosine monophosphate (AMP) to facilitate energy transfer through dephosphorylation. Also involved in platelet activation.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Electron transport chain and ATP synthesis

NSc--b0.title: Band 3 anion transport protein
NSc--b0.description: A transport protein that exchanges bicarbonate ions for chloride ions. Found on the erythrocyte cell membrane and the basolateral membrane of the distal convoluted tubule.

mScVZX0.title: Carbonic acid
mScVZX0.description: A weak acid formed from CO2 and water. Its formation is catalyzed by carbonic anhydrase. Dissociates rapidly to form H+ and HCO3- ions.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen and carbon dioxide transport

5SciZX0.title: Ferruginous body
5SciZX0.description: A small (< 3 μm), golden-brown, dumbbell-shaped particle that contains iron. Most often seen in the alveolar septum in conditions such as asbestosis.

MScMZX0.title: Vitamin K epoxide reductase complex subunit 1
MScMZX0.description: A subunit of vitamin K epoxide reductase that is the target of warfarin.

LScwZX0.title: Generalized transduction
LScwZX0.description: A process in which bacterial DNA is transferred from one bacterium to another bacterium via a bacteriophage. Occurs when a lytic bacteriophage infects a bacterium and cleaves bacterial DNA. This DNA becomes packaged in the phage capsid. The bacteriophage then infects another bacterium and transfers the DNA.

oSc00X0.title: Intrapulmonary conducting system
oSc00X0.description: The system of connecting bronchi and bronchioles that send air back and forth between the trachea and the respiratory segments of the lung. Begins with the main stem bronchi and ends with the terminal bronchioles.

KScU0X0.title: Formication
KScU0X0.description: A form of paresthesia characterized by a sensation that resembles crawling of insects on or under the skin. Most often a symptom of polyneuropathy accompanied by other sensation disturbances. Can also appear in delusional disorders, substance intoxication or withdrawal, and menopause.

6Scj0X0.title: Enolase
6Scj0X0.description: An enzyme involved in glycolysis that catalyzes the reversible isomerization of 2-phosphoglycerate (2-PG) to phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP).

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Sequence of reactions

pScL0X0.title: Fructose-bisphosphate aldolase
pScL0X0.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate and dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP) via the glycolysis metabolic pathway.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Sequence of reactions

JScs0X0.title: Primary structure
JScs0X0.description: The sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide chain.

7Sc4aX0.title: Transcortical motor aphasia
7Sc4aX0.description: A type of aphasia characterized by a lack of fluency with intact comprehension and repetition.

HScKaX0.title: Arcuate fasciculus
HScKaX0.description: A structure made of white matter that connects the frontal, parietal, and temporal lobes. The arcuate fasciculus is important for language processing in the left hemisphere and visuospatial processing in the right hemisphere. An isolated lesion to this structure will cause impaired speech repetition with preserved fluency and comprehension, also known as conduction aphasia.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

GScBaX0.title: Microsomal monooxygenase
GScBaX0.description: An enzyme system that consists of cytochrome P450 species, NADPH-P450 reductase, and cytochrome b5. Involved in the metabolism of several endogenous and exogenous substrates.

tScXYX0.title: Quadrantanopia
tScXYX0.description: A defect in the visual field that causes a loss of vision in a quarter of the field. Quadrantanopia usually affects both eyes.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Scotoma and anopia

uScpYX0.title: Heterogeneous nuclear RNA
uScpYX0.description: An umbrella term for several types of RNA found in the cell nucleus. Predominantly consists of precursor mRNA.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  RNA: Structure and characteristics

ESc8YX0.title: Charcot-Leyden crystal
ESc8YX0.description: A histopathologic finding in patients with eosinophilic inflammation and/or proliferation (e.g., asthma, parasitic infections).

vScAYX0.title: Dendritic cell
vScAYX0.description: A phagocytic antigen-presenting cell. Expresses MHC class II and Fc receptors. Inhibited by interleukin-10.

DSc1bX0.title: Pen test
DSc1bX0.description: A test to detect weakness in the abductor pollicis brevis muscle: The patient is asked to lay his or her hand flat on a surface, palm facing upwards. The physician holds a pen over the hand and asks the patient to touch it with the thumb. Inability to touch the pen by abducting the thumb indicates median nerve palsy/abductor pollicis brevis weakness.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

wSchbX0.title: Erector spinae
wSchbX0.description: A group of muscle bellies that enable extension of the trunk and assist in truncal rotation. These muscles are innervated by direct branches from the spinal nerves.

9ScNbX0.title: Encephalomalacia
9ScNbX0.description: A softening or loss of brain parenchyma due to tissue injury and resultant liquefactive necrosis (e.g., due to cerebral ischemia, hemorrhage, traumatic brain injury). Can be associated with gliosis. Typically asymptomatic but can precipitate seizures. Visible as volume loss with regional hypoattenuation on CT scan.

CScqbX0.title: Nyctalopia
