CScqbX0.description: The inability to see well in dim light. Can be caused by vitamin A deficiency, which compromises the ability to synthesize photosensitive visual pigments in the retina.

xScEbX0.title: Polycistronic mRNA
xScEbX0.description: An individual mRNA that encodes several distinct proteins that are translated synchronously. Seen in many bacteria and chloroplast mRNAs.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Regulation of transcription

BSczbX0.title: Monocistronic mRNA
BSczbX0.description: This is an mRNA that encodes only one protein. One gene (cistrone) = one protein.  Unique to eukaryotes.

yScdXX0.title: RNA interference
yScdXX0.description: An important pathway of post-transcriptional gene regulation. microRNAs combine with specific ribonucleoproteins to form the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC) which uses the microRNA as a template for binding to the 3' UTR of specific mRNAs. The binding of the RISC to the target mRNA either inhibits translation or induces degradation of the transcript, in both cases preventing expression of the final protein product.

AScRXX0.title: Site-specific recombination
AScRXX0.description: A protein-regulated process in which DNA rearrangements occur at specific DNA sequences that are recognized by recombinase enzymes (e.g., integrases). Can lead to insertions, inversions, and/or deletions of DNA. Examples include V(D)J recombination in lymphocytes and the integration of bacteriophage lambda into E. coli.

_Sc5XX0.title: Mobile genetic element
_Sc5XX0.description: A pair of sequence of nucleotides that can move around within a genome or be transferred from one species to another. Some of these elements are viruses, in which site-specific recombination is used to move their genomes into and out of the chromosomes of their host cell.

zScrXX0.title: Minimum inhibitory concentration
zScrXX0.description: The lowest concentration of an antimicrobial that inhibits the growth of a specific microorganism isolate.

-ScDXX0.title: Quinupristin
-ScDXX0.description: A newer streptogramin bactericidal antibiotic used to treat resistant gram-positive infections. Binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis. Used in conjunction with dalfopristin, which binds to a different site on the 50S subunit.

ZhcZcX0.title: Dalfopristin
ZhcZcX0.description: A newer streptogramin bactericidal antibiotic used to treat resistant gram-positive infections. Binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis. Used in conjunction with quinupristin, which binds to a different site on the 50S subunit.

0hcecX0.title: Quinupristin/dalfopristin
0hcecX0.description: A combination of streptogramin bactericidal antibiotics used to treat resistant gram-positive infections. Use of these two antibiotics in combination exerts a synergistic effect due to stabilized binding and action at two different sites of the 50S ribosomal subunit to inhibit bacterial protein synthesis.

bhcHcX0.title: Ureterovesical junction
bhcHcX0.description: The location where the ureters meet the bladder (anterolateral fornix of vagina near the insertion point at the level of the trigone of the bladder).

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Ureters

Xhc9cX0.title: Perineal body
Xhc9cX0.description: A fibromuscular mass located at the intersection between the urogenital and anal triangles. Acts as the central tendon of the perineum. Essential for the integrity of the pelvic floor. Rupture, particularly during vaginal birth, predisposes individuals to prolapse of the pelvic organs (i.e., rectum, bladder, uterus).

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

chca1X0.title: Bulbospongiosus muscle
chca1X0.description: A muscle that arises from the perineal body. In males, it covers the bulb of the penis, facilitates the expulsion of urine, and plays a role in maintaining erections. In females, it covers the vestibular bulbs and greater vestibular glands.

WhcP1X0.title: β-galactosidase
WhcP1X0.description: An enzyme encoded by the lacZ gene of the lac operon in E. coli. Cleaves lactose into galactose and glucose.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Regulation of transcription

dhco1X0.title: Ceramide trihexoside
dhco1X0.description: A glycolipid found in multiple body tissues. Normally broken down by α-galactosidase. Accumulates in patients with Fabry disease.

VhcG1X0.title: Mitochondrial RNA polymerase
VhcG1X0.description: A eukaryotic enzyme that transcribes mitochondrial RNA from mitochondrial DNA within the cytoplasm.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  RNA polymerases and transcription factors

ehcx1X0.title: Oral polio vaccine
ehcx1X0.description: Live attenuated oral formulation of the polio vaccine. Provides longer lasting immunity when compared to the inactivated vaccine. Three or more spaced doses are recommended, starting at 2 months of age. Associated in rare cases with vaccine-associated polio, which is why it is not used in the United States.

UhcbWX0.title: Acellular pertussis vaccine
UhcbWX0.description: Vaccines that contain the inactivated B. pertussis toxin. Vaccine formulations may differ; other B. pertussis components such as the fimbrial antigen or components of the bacterial filament may be used. Typically administered as part of the DTaP vaccine, starting at 2 months of age.

fhckWX0.title: Anchoring bias
fhckWX0.description: A type of bias in which there is an inappropriate reliance on an initial perception or information hinders later judgment when new information is available (e.g., favoring a diagnosis proposed earlier despite new evidence). May lead to diagnostic errors.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

Thc6WX0.title: Nernst potential
Thc6WX0.description: The diffusion potential (i.e., voltage gradient) that prevents any further movement of an ion down its concentration gradient. Represents the point at which opposing forces generated by the concentration gradient and electrical gradient are counterbalanced. Calculated by the Nernst equation, E = log (Cₒ/Cᵢ) × 60/z, where E is the equilibrium potential of the ion, Cₒ is the extracellular ion concentration, Cᵢ is the intracellular ion concentration, and z is the charge of the ion.

destinations.label: Resting potentials and action potentials → Distribution of charge inside and outside the cell

ghcFWX0.title: High-molecular-weight kininogen
ghcFWX0.description: A circulating plasma protein that participates in the activation of the fibrinolytic system and the complement system and the generation of vasoactive peptides such as bradykinin.

ShcyWX0.title: Transglutaminase
ShcyWX0.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the formation of an isopeptide bond between the gamma-carboxamide moiety on the side group of glutamine and the amino moiety on the side chain of lysine. Transglutaminases play a role in forming extensively cross-linked proteins (e.g., elastin, coagulation by factor XIII).

hhccdX0.title: Desmosine
hhccdX0.description: A pyridinium ring formed by the condensation of four lysine residues. Desmosine forms the crosslink between tropoelastin molecules.

ihcJdX0.title: Curschmann spiral
ihcJdX0.description: A spiral mucus plug in sputum that is formed from shed bronchial epithelium. Seen in individuals with asthma.

QhcudX0.title: Inspiratory:expiratory ratio
QhcudX0.description: The ratio of inspiratory time to expiratory time in the breathing cycle. During normal spontaneous breathing, it is approximately 1:2. It is a parameter typically monitored in patients who are mechanically ventilated and adjusted based on underlying disease (e.g., a ratio of 1:4 for patients with obstructive lung disease).

PhcWVX0.title: Convenience sampling
PhcWVX0.description: A nonprobability sampling technique in which study participants are included in a study based on their convenient accessibility and proximity to the investigator.

khcmVX0.title: Tropoelastin
khcmVX0.description: A small soluble protein that is translated from the ELN gene on chromosome 7q. Tropoelastin molecules aggregate in the extracellular matrix to form a large elastin molecule.

Nhc-VX0.title: Ghon focus
Nhc-VX0.description: A granuloma in the lung that represents the primary site of infection of pulmonary tuberculosis. Usually found in the middle or lower lobes of the lung.

mhcVeX0.title: Enterococcus faecium
mhcVeX0.description: A gram-positive bacterium that is a normal component of the gastrointestinal tract flora. Can cause urinary tract infections, biliary tract infections, and endocarditis (especially after genitourinary or gastrointestinal interventions).

5hcieX0.title: Pseudochylothorax
5hcieX0.description: A chronic, exudative effusion that is enriched with cholesterol and characterized by cholesterol crystal formation. Has a milky appearance, similar to that of a true chylothorax. Common causes include chronic pneumothorax, tuberculous pleurisy, rheumatoid pleurisy, and empyema.

MhcMeX0.title: Epithelioid macrophage
MhcMeX0.description: A differentiated tissue macrophage that can form the wall of a granuloma, resembling an epithelial cell layer. The fusion of several epithelioid macrophages is called a Langhans giant cell.

nhc7eX0.title: Cytolysin
nhc7eX0.description: A virulence factor of E. faecalis. It functions by forming a pore in target cell membranes, leading to cellular lysis. This is believed to be the main mechanism responsible for the hemolytic activity of E. faecalis.

LhcweX0.title: CD40L/CD40 binding
LhcweX0.description: The interaction between the membrane receptor on B lymphocytes (CD40) and the CD40 ligand (CD40L) on Th cells. This activation results in memory B cell formation and is important for class switching.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

ohc0UX0.title: Bone morphogenetic protein receptor type II
ohc0UX0.description: A transmembrane serine/threonine receptor kinase and member of the TGF-β family. It is involved in regulation of cell proliferation and apoptosis.

KhcUUX0.title: Acebutolol
KhcUUX0.description: A lipid-soluble, cardioselective beta blocker (β1 selective) with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity.

6hcjUX0.title: Segmental demyelinating neuropathy
6hcjUX0.description: A type of neuropathy characterized by loss of saltatory conduction. Caused by damage to Schwann cells and breakdown of myelin over a few segments along the length of the internode, while the the axon or neuronal body remain intact. Nerve conduction studies characteristically show prolongation of distal and F wave latencies and a decrease in conduction velocity. Common causes include acute and chronic inflammatory demyelinating neuropathies, metachromatic leukodystrophy, type 1 and type 4A Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, Dejerine-Sotta syndrome, and diphtheritic neuropathy. The defects caused by segmental demyelination are typically reversible once Schwann cells regenerate.

phcLUX0.title: Degenerative axonal neuropathy
phcLUX0.description: A type of neuropathy characterized by degeneration of the distal parts of the axon and secondary demyelination. Nerve conduction studies characteristically show a decreased action potential amplitude. Most cases of acquired neuropathies (e.g., diabetes, amyloidosis, paraneoplastic syndromes, Lyme disease, drugs, toxins, vitamin deficiencies), as well as certain hereditary neuropathies (e.g., type 2 Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, porphyria, giant axonal neuropathy, Friedrich ataxia, ataxia-telangiectasia), are the result of axonal degeneration. The defects caused by axonal degeneration are typically irreversible.

JhcsUX0.title: Gastrin-releasing peptide
JhcsUX0.description: A neuropeptide produced by vagal nerve endings in the stomach. It stimulates G cells to secrete gastrin.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

qhcCUX0.title: Hypovolemia
qhcCUX0.description: A condition in which the volume of extracellular fluid is decreased. Typically caused by loss of both salt and water (e.g., from vomiting, diarrhea, diuretic use). Severe hypovolemia can cause hypotension and shock.

7hc42X0.title: Nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae
7hc42X0.description: The unencapsulated serotypes of Haemophilus influenzae, which commonly cause mucosal infections (e.g., sinusitis, otitis media, conjunctivitis, pneumonia).

HhcK2X0.title: Asteroid body
HhcK2X0.description: A star-shaped, eosinophilic inclusion body in the cytoplasm of epithelioid or giant cells in non-caseating granulomas (e.g., from sarcoidosis, foreign body reactions). Consists of various lipids.

thcXfX0.title: N-methyl-D-aspartate
thcXfX0.description: A synthetic amino acid derivative that binds to a subtype of ionotropic glutamate receptors (NMDA receptors).

FhcgfX0.title: Absolute polycythemia
FhcgfX0.description: An elevated total RBC mass. Can be divided into primary (polycythemia vera) or secondary causes (erythropoietin-dependent). Secondary polycythemia can be further subdivided as physiologically appropriate (e.g., chronic hypoxia) or inappropriate (exogenous erythropoietin production).

8hcOfX0.title: Physiologically inappropriate secondary polycythemia
8hcOfX0.description: A form of secondary (erythropoietin-dependent) absolute polycythemia, caused by an increase of erythropoietin in the absence of a physiological need (normal blood oxygen levels). Renal cell carcinoma is commonly associated with paraneoplastic EPO production.

uhcpfX0.title: Piloerection
uhcpfX0.description: The involuntary erection of hair on the surface of the skin due to contraction of the sympathetically innervated piloerector muscles. Piloerection increases the volume of air between hair and skin and therefore increases thermal insulation. Piloerection primarily occurs following exposure to cold, but it can also occur as a result of fear.

destinations.label: Skin and skin appendage → Skin appendage

Ehc8fX0.title: Glycopyrrolate
Ehc8fX0.description: An anticholinergic that blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors.  Used to treat conditions of excess secretion (e.g., hyperhidrosis, peptic ulcer, drooling)

Dhc1TX0.title: Hypoxic ventilatory drive
Dhc1TX0.description: Hyperventilation that is induced by hypoxemia. Normally, ventilation is predominantly driven by an increase in PaCO₂, which is sensed by central chemoreceptors in the medulla. However, in patients with a PaO₂ less than 70 mm Hg, stimulation of oxygen chemoreceptors in the carotid body can lead to hyperventilation.

whchTX0.title: Cercaria
whchTX0.description: The larval form of a trematode (flat worms).

9hcNTX0.title: Elfin facies
9hcNTX0.description: A set of facial features characterized by broad forehead, wide mouth, full cheeks and lips, and a long, smooth philtrum. Seen in certain genetic diseases, especially in Williams syndrome.

yhcdgX0.title: Pulmonary arteries
yhcdgX0.description: The blood vessels that carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs for oxygenation.

AhcRgX0.title: Descending aorta
AhcRgX0.description: A region of the aorta that is distal to the ligamentum arteriosum. Arises as a continuation of the aortic arch and lies within the posterior mediastinum in the thoracic cavity. Continues inferiorly as the abdominal aorta after passing through the diaphragm at the level of the T12 vertebra. Terminates with the division of the two common iliac arteries at the level of the L4 vertebra.

_hc5gX0.title: Miltefosine
_hc5gX0.description: An antiprotozoal drug used to treat all forms of leishmaniasis and infections caused by free-living amebae (e.g., primary amebic meningoencephalitis). Its mechanism of action is not fully understood but thought to involve interaction with phospholipids and steroids in the parasitic cell membrane, which leads to apoptosis.

zhcrgX0.title: Stibogluconate
zhcrgX0.description: A treatment for all forms of Leishmaniasis. It inhibits the production of purine triphosphate molecules (e.g. ATP), ultimately stalling the metabolism of Leishmania species.

-hcDgX0.title: Inferior thyroid artery
-hcDgX0.description: An artery that runs with the recurrent laryngeal nerve and supplies the posterior portion of the thyroid gland and the superior and inferior parathyroid glands. Usually branches from the thyrocervical trunk but can originate from the subclavian artery.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Gross anatomy

media.title: Blood supply of the thyroid gland

Z3cZSX0.title: Ascending pharyngeal artery
Z3cZSX0.description: A branch of the external carotid artery that supplies the base of the skull and anastomoses with the anterior and posterior cerebral circulations.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

media.title: Branches of the external carotid artery

03ceSX0.title: Segmental bronchi
03ceSX0.description: A passage of the airway that includes generations 2-8 of the respiratory tree. Branches off into smaller sections.

a3cQSX0.title: Delta waves (EEG)
a3cQSX0.description: An EEG waveform seen on polysomnography during the N3 stage of non-REM sleep. Characterized by a low frequency (0.5–4 Hz) and high amplitude.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Sleep physiology

b3cHSX0.title: Atypical absence seizure
b3cHSX0.description: A generalized seizure characterized by transient unresponsiveness. Atypical absence seizures begin more slowly than typical absence seizures, last for a few minutes, are often associated with a loss of postural tone, and have a spike-and-wave complex on EEG with a frequency that is less than 2.5 Hz. Atypical absence seizures are seen in conditions such as Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and Dravet syndrome.

destinations.label: Generalized epilepsy in childhood → Idiopathic generalized epilepsy syndromes

X3c9SX0.title: Spike-wave discharge
X3c9SX0.description: An EEG pattern characterized by a spike followed by a wave. It typically occurs during absence seizures (typical or atypical) and continuously in the background among patients with certain epilepsy syndromes such as Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.

c3cahX0.title: Periodic sharp wave complex
c3cahX0.description: An EEG waveform with a frequency of 1–2 Hz that is seen in the early stages of sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.

13c2hX0.title: Sodium oxybate
13c2hX0.description: A sodium salt of gamma hydroxybutyric acid used to treat narcolepsy.

W3cPhX0.title: Primary gain
W3cPhX0.description: The internal advantages obtained as a result of being ill (e.g., sympathy, attention).

destinations.label: Somatic symptom and related disorders → Factitious disorders

d3cohX0.title: Homatropine
d3cohX0.description: An antimuscarinic medication that is less potent than atropine and that has a shorter duration of action. Homatropine is most commonly used as a cycloplegic and mydriatic before ophthalmologic examination.

V3cGhX0.title: Necrotizing bronchopneumonia
V3cGhX0.description: A severe complication of bacterial pulmonary infection or superinfection that is characterized by inflammation, consolidation, and multiple cystic cavitations within the lung parenchyma. The most common causative organisms are Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Haemophilus influenzae.

U3cb3X0.title: Band neutrophil
U3cb3X0.description: An immature neutrophil that is released into the blood in response to ongoing inflammation. Band neutrophils normally develop into segmented granulocytes over the course of 4–5 days.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

23cT3X0.title: 6-mercaptopurine
23cT3X0.description: An antimetabolite (purine analog) that impairs cell replication. It is mainly used as an immunosuppressant for autoimmune diseases, renal transplantation, and inflammatory bowel disease.

f3ck3X0.title: Muscarinic-3 receptor
f3ck3X0.description: A Gq-coupled muscarinic receptor subtype found in exocrine and endocrine glands, endothelial cells, and certain smooth muscles. Stimulation causes gut peristalsis, increased detrusor contraction, bronchoconstriction, miosis, and vasodilation due to increased production of NO by endothelial cells. Stimulation of M3 receptors can also result in increased secretion of tears, saliva, sweat, gastric acid, and insulin.

T3c63X0.title: Systemic vascular resistance
T3c63X0.description: A measure of the resistance that circulatory blood flow has to overcome to flow throughout the body (excluding the pulmonary vasculature). Can be calculated with the following equation: SVR = (mean arterial pressure - central venous pressure)/cardiac output.

R3clRX0.title: Creola bodies
R3clRX0.description: An aggregate of desquamated epithelial cells often found in the sputum of asthma patients. Signify damage to the respiratory epithelium.

i3cJRX0.title: Thyroglossal fistula
i3cJRX0.description: A rare thyroglossal duct anomaly that forms a fistula between the foramen cecum and the skin of the neck.

Q3cuRX0.title: Cinchonism
Q3cuRX0.description: A group of adverse effects caused by treatment with quinine or its derivatives. Includes nausea, dizziness, headache, tinnitus, and visual changes. Hypoglycemia, flushing, and urticaria may also occur.

P3cWiX0.title: Pancreatic retention cyst
P3cWiX0.description: A rare, non-neoplastic cyst that can form within the pancreas as a result of a chronically occluded pancreatic duct (e.g., due to pancreatic duct calculus or adenocarcinoma) or as a congenital abnormality (e.g., in cases of cystic fibrosis).

43c3iX0.title: Papillary urothelial carcinoma
43c3iX0.description: A carcinoma of the epithelial lining of the urinary tract that grows in thickened, dysplastic, finger-like projections from the inner surface of the bladder.

O3cIiX0.title: Nitrosamine
O3cIiX0.description: A type of nitrate and amine-containing chemical found in manufactured, smoked, and processed foods, pesticides, tobacco products, and cosmetics. Consumption of food high in this chemical compound is associated with increased risk of developing gastric cancer.

l3cviX0.title: Corneal stroma
l3cviX0.description: A thick, fibrous part of the cornea composed of layers of type I collagen.

N3c-iX0.title: Sinus venosus
N3c-iX0.description: An embryological structure that forms parts of the heart. The left horn forms the coronary sinus; the right horn forms part of the right atrium.

n3c7QX0.title: Corneal abrasion
n3c7QX0.description: A defect of the corneal epithelium caused by ocular trauma (e.g., scrape or scratch injuries from foreign bodies). Symptoms include foreign body sensation, eye pain, and eye watering.

media.title: Corneal abrasion due to foreign body under the upper eyelid
Corneal abrasion highlighted by fluorescein staining

L3cwQX0.title: Appendix testis
L3cwQX0.description: A vestigial remnant of the Müllerian duct system and one of the four main testicular appendages. Torsion of this structure is a common cause of acute scrotum (especially in children).

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Ductal sex differentiation

63cjjX0.title: Decorticate posture
63cjjX0.description: A posture characterized by flexion of upper extremities and extension of lower extremities. Can be seen in patients with severe brain injury that occurs proximal to the level of the red nucleus.

p3cLjX0.title: Decerebrate posture
p3cLjX0.description: A posture characterized by extension of bilateral upper and lower extremities. Can be seen in patients with severe brain injury that occurs at or distal to the level of the red nucleus.

q3cCjX0.title: AR gene
q3cCjX0.description: A gene on chromosome Xq responsible for androgen receptor formation. Androgen insensitivity syndrome (AIS) is diagnosed based on a mutation of this gene.

destinations.label: Differences (disorders) of sex development → Androgen insensitivity syndrome

I3cYPX0.title: Pathogenicity
I3cYPX0.description: The ability of a pathogen to cause a disease after infecting the host. Sometimes expressed as the number of individuals who experience the disease over the total number of individuals infected by the pathogen.

r3cfPX0.title: Melioidosis
r3cfPX0.description: An infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei endemic primarily to northern Australia and Southeast Asia. Transmitted via environmental contact with the skin, respiratory tract, and gastrointestinal tract. Can cause local skin disease, pneumonia, and/or bacteremia, though most cases are subclinical.

73c4PX0.title: ACOG
73c4PX0.description: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists

H3cKPX0.title: Bone morphogenetic protein receptor type 2 gene
H3cKPX0.description: A gene located on the long arm of chromosome 2 that encodes bone morphogenetic protein receptor type 2. Defects in this gene are associated with familial pulmonary arterial hypertension.

s3ctPX0.title: MYH7 gene
s3ctPX0.description: A gene on the long arm of chromosome 14 that codes for the beta-myosin heavy chain, which forms a part of type II myosin in skeletal and cardiac muscle cells. A defect in this gene is a common cause of familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

G3cBPX0.title: MYBPC3 gene
G3cBPX0.description: A gene on the short arm of chromosome 11 that codes for cardiac myosin binding protein C, which prevents the breakdown of thick filaments in cardiac sarcomeres. A defect in this gene is a common cause of familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

t3cX4X0.title: TTN gene
t3cX4X0.description: A gene on the long arm of chromosome 2 that codes for titin, a structural and functional component of sarcomeres. A defect in this gene is a common cause of familial dilated cardiomyopathy.

F3cg4X0.title: Polyribosylribitol phosphate
F3cg4X0.description: The main component of the polysaccharide capsule of Haemophilus influenzae. Conjugated to diphtheria toxin, tetanus toxoid, or the meningococcal outer membrane protein to produce the Hib vaccine.

83cO4X0.title: Sodium-potassium-chloride cotransporter
83cO4X0.description: An ion channel that facilitates the secondary active transport of sodium, potassium, and chloride into cells.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Urine production

u3cp4X0.title: Sigmoid-shaped interventricular septum
u3cp4X0.description: An age-related intraventricular septal change in the heart caused by thickening of the subaortic region and an apparent increase in intraventricular septal thickness. This feature is most commonly seen in elderly patients.

E3c84X0.title: Secretory protein
E3c84X0.description: A protein that is destined for secretion into the extracellular space. Examples include digestive enzymes, antibodies, neurotransmitters, and extracellular matrix proteins. Secretory proteins are synthesized in the rough endoplasmic reticulum and moved into the extracellular space via secretory vesicles.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

v3cA4X0.title: Endoplasmic reticulum signal sequence
v3cA4X0.description: A short peptide sequence that is present in the propeptide chain of a secretory protein. It is the first part of the propeptide to be synthesized and is, therefore, located at the N-terminal of the peptide chain. It serves as a binding site for the signal recognition peptide, which facilitates binding of the growing peptide chain with its ribosome to the endoplasmic reticulum.

D3c1kX0.title: Signal recognition particle
D3c1kX0.description: A cytosolic ribonucleoprotein that can bind to the endoplasmic reticulum signal sequence of a growing peptide chain as well the SRP receptor of endoplasmic reticulum. This protein inhibits elongation of the peptide chain when bound to the ER signal sequence. It also facilitates binding of the ribosomal mRNA with its growing peptide chain to the endoplasmic reticulum.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Protein sorting

media.title: Translocation of ribosomes to the endoplasmic reticulum during translation

w3chkX0.title: Platelet and endothelial cell adhesion molecule 1
w3chkX0.description: A vascular antigen expressed by endothelial cells, platelets, and lymphocytes. Commonly used as an immunohistochemical marker of hepatic angiosarcoma.

C3cqkX0.title: Azo dye
C3cqkX0.description: A type of dye commonly used in paints, printing inks, varnishes, carpets, leather products, and foods. Some contain the carcinogenic compound benzidine.

x3cEkX0.title: Nuclear localization signal
x3cEkX0.description: A short peptide sequence that is present in the propeptide chain of a nuclear protein. Serves as a binding site for the importin (karyopherin) molecule, which facilitates entry of the protein into the nucleus via the nuclear pore complex.

B3czkX0.title: MacCallum plaque
B3czkX0.description: A thickening of the posterior part of the left atrium wall above the mitral valve due to chronic inflammation and fibrosis. Associated with rheumatic heart disease.

A3cROX0.title: Superior hypogastric plexus
A3cROX0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers situated retroperitoneally at the aortoiliac junction. Receives sympathetic fibers from the lumbar splanchnic nerves and parasympathetic fibres from the pelvic splanchnic nerves (via the hypogastric nerve). Conveys branches to the inferior mesenteric, ureteric, and gonadal plexuses.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

_3c5OX0.title: Polyphagia
_3c5OX0.description: A symptom of excessive hunger and/or thirst.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Regulation of appetite and satiety

z3crOX0.title: Hot nodule
z3crOX0.description: A circumscribed area of increased radioiodine uptake on a radionuclide scan, which indicates a hyperfunctioning (autonomous) thyroid nodule.

-3cDOX0.title: Exertional dyspnea
-3cDOX0.description: A condition characterized by shortness of breath and difficulty breathing when engaged in light to moderate physical activities. Can be caused by a broad range of cardiac, pulmonary, and inflammatory conditions (e.g., CHF, asthma, COPD, sarcoidosis).

ZRcZlX0.title: Mevalonate pathway
ZRcZlX0.description: A fundamental pathway for cholesterol synthesis. Important cofactors and enzymes include NADPH and HMG-CoA reductase.  This pathway is a target for cholesterol reducing medications and some chemotherapy regimens. It can be summarized as follows: acetyl-CoA → acetoacetyl-CoA → HMG-CoA → mevalonic acid → mevalonate 5-P → mevalonate 5-PP → Isopentenyl-5-PP →→→→ cholesterol

bRcHlX0.title: Encephalopathy
bRcHlX0.description: A diffuse disruption of brain function and/or structure. Etiologies include infection, metabolic disturbances, medication adverse effects, mass effects (e.g., from tumors), and radiation.

VRcGNX0.title: Cancer immunotherapy
VRcGNX0.description: A cancer treatment that stimulates the host's immune system to target malignant cells. Examples of cancer immunotherapy include immune checkpoint inhibitors (e.g., PD-1 inhibitors), CAR T-cell therapy, and vaccine-based therapy.

fRckmX0.title: Vocal cord granuloma
fRckmX0.description: A complication of endotracheal intubation caused by inflammation and ulceration during the intubation process. Can cause vocal hoarseness that manifests ~ 4 weeks after intubation.

destinations.label: Benign laryngeal lesions → Vocal fold granuloma

gRcFmX0.title: Pugilistic attitude
gRcFmX0.description: A description of a body posture associated with burned corpses employed in forensics. The posture is a result of opisthotonus of the flexor muscles (particular the paraspinal muscles) and flexion of the joints of all extremities, which occurs as a result of contraction and stiffening of the muscles exposed to fire. Less commonly known as fencer's attitude.

hRcc5X0.title: Interlobular renal artery
hRcc5X0.description: The small arteries in the kidneys that originate from the arcuate arteries and give off afferent arterioles that ultimately supply the glomeruli.

3RcS5X0.title: Interlobar renal artery
3RcS5X0.description: The first arterial branches from the renal artery. These vessels nourish the renal lobes and give rise to the arcuate arteries as they course towards the cortex.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Renal blood flow

RRcl5X0.title: GTPase
RRcl5X0.description: A superfamily of binding proteins that hydrolyze GTP ("ON" state) to GDP ("OFF" state) and orthophosphate. This "ON"/"OFF" switching controls a variety of biological processes, including Ras proteins, membrane transport, and transmission of mitogenic signals.

media.title: Signal transduction of G protein-coupled receptors

iRcJ5X0.title: GTP cap
iRcJ5X0.description: The binding of GTP to the alpha and beta tubulin subunits of microtubules, which provides stability during microtubule assembly and disassembly (dynamic instability). During assembly, GTP bound to a beta tubulin subunit can be hydrolyzed, allowing for polymerization, while the other GTP molecule bound to the alpha subunit stays bound, maintaining structure and function during polymerization.

QRcu5X0.title: Heat therapy
QRcu5X0.description: A modality of physical therapy used to relieve pain and induce muscle relaxation. Involves the application of heat to joints, muscle, and/or soft tissue (e.g., using hot cloths, ultrasound, heating pads, warm compresses).

kRcmMX0.title: Phosphoenolpyruvate
kRcmMX0.description: A monocarboxylic acid that is an intermediate in both glycolysis and gluconeogenesis. Synthesized from oxaloacetic acid by the enzyme phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase and converted to pyruvate by the enzyme pyruvate kinase. Can also be reversibly synthesized from or converted to 2-phosphoglycerate by the enzyme enolase.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Sequence of reactions

ORcIMX0.title: Phosphoglucose isomerase
ORcIMX0.description: A cytosolic enzyme that reversibly converts glucose-6-phosphate to fructose-6-phosphate.

lRcvMX0.title: External capsule
lRcvMX0.description: A region of white matter between the lentiform nucleus and the claustrum. It contains the cholinergic fibers that connect the basal forebrain to the cerebral cortex.

NRc-MX0.title: Claustrum
NRc-MX0.description: A thin sheet of subcortical gray matter that lies medial to the insular cortex and lateral to the putamen.

nRc7nX0.title: PKA
nRc7nX0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) PKA = protein kinase A: A cAMP-dependent serine/threonine-specific protein kinase that regulates the activity of various enzymes (including glycogen phosphorylase kinase) via phosphorylation.
2) pKa = acid dissociation constant: A measure of acid strength. The lower the pKa of a substance, the more acidic it is and the more easily it gives up protons.

LRcwnX0.title: Honeycombing
LRcwnX0.description: A pathological and radiographic finding of fibrotic lung parenchyma composed of diffuse cysts of varying size. Honeycombing is an important criterion in determining a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern, which is associated with pulmonary fibrosis and highly specific for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

oRc0LX0.title: Traction bronchiectasis
oRc0LX0.description: A type of bronchiectasis characterized by irreversible dilatation of the bronchi and bronchioles in areas of tissue that are scarred from pulmonary fibrosis or other types of abnormal lung parenchyma.

KRcULX0.title: Long-term potentiation
KRcULX0.description: A process by which a synapse is continuously strengthened through repeated depolarization. Plays a critical role in memory and learning. Diminished in patients with Alzheimer disease.

6RcjLX0.title: Mitral annular calcification
6RcjLX0.description: A chronic degenerative condition that affects the annulus (base) of the mitral valve. Can cause mitral stenosis or mitral regurgitation. Risk factors include advanced age, chronic kidney disease, and increased mitral valve stress (e.g., hypertension, aortic stenosis).

IRcYoX0.title: Perivalvular abscess
IRcYoX0.description: A myocardial abscess that involves structures near the cardiac valve. Can cause conductive abnormalities such as third-degree atrioventricular block. Typically caused by infective endocarditis due to suppurative species (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus).

media.title: Prosthetic aortic valve with endocarditis and valve ring abscess

HRcKoX0.title: Manual lymphatic drainage
HRcKoX0.description: A form of massage that is applied in direction of the heart to increase the natural drainage of lymphatic fluid in patients with lymphedema.

tRcXKX0.title: Secondary protein structure
tRcXKX0.description: The protein structure formed as a result of hydrogen bonds between the α-amino group of one amino acid and the oxygen atom of the α-carboxyl group of another amino acid. The two main secondary protein structures are alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets.

FRcgKX0.title: α-amino group
FRcgKX0.description: An amino (NH₂) group that is covalently attached to the alpha carbon of the amino acid. Peptide bonds, as well as hydrogen bonds, are formed between the α-amino group of one amino acid and the α-carboxyl group of another amino acid.

8RcOKX0.title: α-carboxyl group
8RcOKX0.description: A carboxyl (COOH) group that is covalently attached to the alpha carbon of the amino acid. Peptide bonds, as well as hydrogen bonds, are formed between the α-carboxyl group of one amino acid and the α-amino group of another amino acid.

uRcpKX0.title: Hydrophobic interaction
uRcpKX0.description: The tendency of non-polar molecules to aggregate together in a polar solvent so as to minimize the surface area that is in contact with the polar molecules.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

ERc8KX0.title: Disulfide bond
ERc8KX0.description: A covalent bond between two sulfur atoms that forms when the sulfur-containing side chains of two cysteine amino acids are in close proximity. Disulfide bonds play a role in the formation of tertiary and quaternary protein structures (e.g., triple helical structure of collagen), the conversion of cysteine to cystine, and the formation of oxidized glutathione. Drugs that disrupt disulfide bonds in proteins (e.g., N-acetylcysteine) are used as mucolytics.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Protein folding and misfolding

vRcAKX0.title: Tertiary protein structure
vRcAKX0.description: A three-dimensional protein structure formed by the folding of the secondary structure. Tertiary structures are formed by electrostatic side chain interactions and disulfide bonds.

DRc16X0.title: Quaternary protein structure
DRc16X0.description: A three-dimensional protein structure that is formed by the interaction of tertiary structure monomers. Quaternary structures are formed by electrostatic side chain interactions, disulfide bonds, and/or metallic bonds.

wRch6X0.title: Parkin
wRch6X0.description: An E3 ubiquitin ligase that is coded for the PARK2 gene on chromosome 6q. Parkin assists in the ubiquination of dysfunctional mitochondrial proteins and prevents apoptosis. Impaired parkin function has been implicated in autosomal recessive juvenile Parkinson disease and tumorigenesis.

CRcq6X0.title: Gluten
CRcq6X0.description: A group of proteins (e.g., gliadins, glutelins) that is found in certain cereal such as wheat, barley, and rye. Hypersensitivity to gluten is responsible for celiac disease.

xRcE6X0.title: Dorsal nucleus of the vagus
xRcE6X0.description: A motor nucleus of the vagal nerve that is located in the medulla, posterior to the hypoglossal nerve nucleus and anterior to the floor of the fourth ventricle. It gives rise to preganglionic parasympathetic fibers that innervate thoracic and abdominal viscera.

destinations.label: Autonomic nervous system → Parasympathetic nervous system

BRcz6X0.title: Ortner syndrome
BRcz6X0.description: A condition characterized by vocal hoarseness due to compression of the recurrent laryngeal nerve from an underlying cardiovascular disorder (e.g., enlarged left atrium, aortic aneurysm, aberrant subclavian vessel).

yRcdpX0.title: Nuclear chromatin clumping
yRcdpX0.description: A reversible process that occurs following cell injury (e.g., ischemia), in which chromatin condenses and clusters together forming a compact mass.

ARcRpX0.title: Endonuclease
ARcRpX0.description: An enzyme responsible for the cleavage of nucleotides and the release of DNA bases.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

_Rc5pX0.title: Glycerol kinase
_Rc5pX0.description: An enzyme found in the liver that phosphorylates free glycerol, which allows the liver to recycle glycerol that is released during VLDL metabolism. Not found in adipose tissue.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

zRcrpX0.title: Autoimmune cytopenia
zRcrpX0.description: A decrease in blood cell count due to autoimmune antibody destruction. Includes any combination of the following conditions: autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA), autoimmune neutropenia (AIN), and autoimmune thrombocytopenia (ITP).

-RcDpX0.title: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome
-RcDpX0.description: An autosomal dominant disorder in which defective Fas-FasL interaction results in failure of the extrinsic (death receptor) apoptosis pathway. Leads to proliferation of antigen-specific lymphocyte lineages. Clinical manifestations include generalized adenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and autoimmunity (typically Evans syndrome).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Apoptosis

ZicZJX0.title: Lancisi sign
ZicZJX0.description: A physical exam finding in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation. The V wave merges with the C wave, forming a prominent wave on jugular venous examination that can resemble the carotid-pulse wave of aortic regurgitation.

0iceJX0.title: Intermittent asthma
0iceJX0.description: The mildest stage of bronchial asthma characterized by symptoms (or the need to use an inhaler) on ≤ 2 days per week, ≤ 2 nighttime awakenings per month, the ability to perform all routine activities, and normal lung function tests in between the exacerbations.

aicQJX0.title: Persistent asthma
aicQJX0.description: A more severe stage of bronchial asthma characterized by symptoms (or the need to use an inhaler) on > 2 days per week, > 2 nighttime awakenings per month, inability to perform all routine activities as a result of symptoms, or abnormal lung function tests in between the exacerbations. Persistent asthma can be further classified into mild, moderate, and severe forms.

YicnJX0.title: Ranke complex
YicnJX0.description: A lung lesion seen in patients with a history of pulmonary tuberculosis that consists of a calcified granuloma with an associated calcified lymph node. It is a fibrosed and calcified Ghon complex.

WicPqX0.title: Malate dehydrogenase
WicPqX0.description: An enzyme found in mitochondria and the cytosol that catalyzes the reversible conversion of oxaloacetate to malate.

eicxqX0.title: Succinyl-CoA synthetase
eicxqX0.description: A mitochondrial enzyme involved in the Krebs cycle that catalyzes the reversible conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate.

UicbIX0.title: Acyl group
UicbIX0.description: A molecular moiety that consists of a carbon chain attached to a carbon atom that is double-bonded to an oxygen atom (i.e., R-C=O). Coenzyme A and lipoamide are used as acyl carriers in biochemical reactions.

2icTIX0.title: HMG-CoA
2icTIX0.description: A metabolic intermediate that consists of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric acid linked to coenzyme A by a high-energy thioester bond. Synthesized from acetoacetyl-CoA by HMG-CoA synthase. Converted to mevalonate for cholesterol synthesis by HMG-CoA reductase and to acetoacetate for ketogenesis by HMG-CoA lyase.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Ketone body metabolism

fickIX0.title: Malonyl-CoA
fickIX0.description: A metabolic intermediate of the fatty acid synthesis pathway that consists of malonic acid linked to coenzyme A by a high-energy thioester bond. Synthesized from acetyl-CoA by acetyl-CoA carboxylase. Used by malonyl-CoA-acyl carrier protein transacylase.

iicJrX0.title: Red hepatization
iicJrX0.description: An inflammatory stage of lobar pneumonia. Characterized by neutrophils, red blood cells, and fibrin in the alveoli, which results in a liver-like consistency of the affected lung. Precedes gray hepatization.

QicurX0.title: Gray hepatization
QicurX0.description: An inflammatory stage of lobar pneumonia that follows red hepatization. Characterized by the destruction of red blood cells that have infiltrated the alveoli, which results in a fibrinosuppurative exudate that gives the affected lung a gray appearance on gross examination.

jic_rX0.title: Maleylacetoacetic acid
jic_rX0.description: An organic acid formed from homogentisic acid by the enzyme homogentisate oxidase. Converted to fumaric acid by the enzymes maleylacetoacetate isomerase and fumarylacetoacetase.

PicW7X0.title: Lipocortin-1
PicW7X0.description: An anti-inflammatory protein induced by glucocorticoid therapy that inhibits the release of arachidonic acid and thus decreases concentrations of prostaglandins, prostacyclins, and other inflammatory molecules.

4ic37X0.title: Antoni B region
4ic37X0.description: A histopathologic feature of schwannomas. Typically located adjacent to Antoni A regions. In contrast to Antoni A regions, Antoni B regions are less cellular and less tightly packed.

destinations.label: Brain tumors → Primary brain tumors according to age

kicm7X0.title: Edema factor
kicm7X0.description: A component of the anthrax toxin that binds to calcium and calmodulin and gains adenylate cyclase activity, which increases cAMP levels and results in cellular edema. Thought to be responsible for the edematous borders of black eschars that form in patients with cutaneous anthrax.

OicI7X0.title: Traumatic neuroma
OicI7X0.description: A benign tumor that develops in response to nerve injury (e.g., amputations or other types of surgery). They arise from disorganized proliferation of nerve fibers or their myelin sheaths. Manifestations include pain, paresthesia, cold intolerance, and positive Tinel sign at the neuroma site.

destinations.label: Peripheral nerve injuries → Types of nerve damage

Nic-7X0.title: Protein-energy malnutrition
Nic-7X0.description: A group of disorders of malnutrition characterized by muscle atrophy and varying other features depending on the form. Primary forms include marasmus (wasting of muscle mass and loss of body fat), kwashiorkor (edematous malnutrition), and marasmic kwashiorkor (a combination of the two conditions). Secondary PEM results from an underlying condition.

micVHX0.title: Pyloric sphincter
micVHX0.description: A ring of smooth muscle at the distal aspect of the pyloric canal. Controls the movement of gastric contents into the duodenum.

5iciHX0.title: Phase I trial
5iciHX0.description: The phase of a clinical trial that involves administering doses of a new drug to healthy volunteers to determine its safety and preliminary pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic properties.

MicMHX0.title: Phase 0 trial
MicMHX0.description: The phase of a clinical trial in which subtherapeutic doses of a new drug are tested among a small group of healthy volunteers to determine preliminary pharmacokinetic and/or pharmacodynamic properties of the drug.

nic7HX0.title: Phase II trial
nic7HX0.description: The phase of a clinical trial in which a small number of individuals with the disease of interest take the drug to determine its efficacy, effective dosing, and adverse effects.

LicwHX0.title: Phase III trial
LicwHX0.description: The phase of a clinical trial involving a large-scale, randomized study to compare the experimental drug with a placebo or the current "gold standard" of treatment.

oic0sX0.title: Phase IV trial
oic0sX0.description: A postapproval/postmarketing stage in drug development in which the effects of long-term use of the drug are assessed. Can result in the withdrawal of the drug from the market.

6icjsX0.title: Peristalsis
6icjsX0.description: A concerted contraction and relaxation of smooth muscle that propagates a substance along the length of a lumen. One example is gut peristalsis, in which the muscularis externa of the bowel contracts and relaxes to propel chyme distally through the intestine.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Innervation and gut motility

ricfGX0.title: Interval appendectomy
ricfGX0.description: The surgical removal of the appendix after complete resolution of an initial episode of inflammation. Typically performed ~ 6 weeks after resolution of complicated appendicitis (i.e., appendicular abscess, appendicular mass) that was managed conservatively.

7ic4GX0.title: Retroperitoneal lymph node dissection
7ic4GX0.description: The surgical removal of retroperitoneal lymph nodes. Typically performed as part of the staging workup and/or management of metastatic urological malignancies (e.g., testicular cancer).

HicKGX0.title: Scrotal orchiectomy
HicKGX0.description: The removal of a testis through a scrotal incision. Typically performed for benign conditions (e.g., testicular necrosis, gender reassignment surgery). Contraindicated if there is suspicion for testicular malignancy.

sictGX0.title: Phase V trial
sictGX0.description: Post-marketing surveillance of a new drug that compares the real-life effectiveness to the efficacy found in research studies.

GicBGX0.title: Anterior-posterior diameter
GicBGX0.description: The distance between the anterior and posterior chest wall. Increased in conditions such as emphysema (due to air trapping), resulting in the appearance of a barrel chest.

FicgtX0.title: Chilaiditi sign
FicgtX0.description: A radiolucency below the diaphragm caused by the presence of a bowel loop in this region. It is typically caused by a volvulus. This sign can be mistaken for a pneumoperitoneum.

8icOtX0.title: CysLT1
8icOtX0.description: A leukotriene receptor. Blocked by montelukast/zafirlukast in maintenance treatment of asthma and allergic rhinitis.

uicptX0.title: Forced expiratory volume
uicptX0.description: The maximum volume of air that can be forcefully expired after maximal inspiration. The volume expired after 1 second (FEV1) is most commonly assessed; the volume expired in 6 seconds is sometimes used to approximate forced vital capacity (FVC).

Eic8tX0.title: Coronary perfusion pressure
Eic8tX0.description: The driving pressure that forces blood into the coronary arteries during diastole. Calculated as the difference in pressure between the aorta and left ventricle during diastole.

vicAtX0.title: Macrophage elastase
vicAtX0.description: An enzyme produced by macrophages that plays a role in the degradation of elastin in the lungs. Abnormal activity is associated with the development of emphysema. Degraded by tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases (TIMPs).

Dic1FX0.title: Glial scar
Dic1FX0.description: A reactive process that involves the activation and hypertrophy of astrocytes, which leads to the formation of a thick, gliotic scar.

9icNFX0.title: Hypoproteinemia
9icNFX0.description: A low serum concentration of protein. Etiologies include deficiencies, malabsorption, protein-losing enteropathies, proteinuria (e.g., nephrotic syndrome), liver failure, and sepsis.

CicqFX0.title: Blood protein
CicqFX0.description: The proteins in the serum, which include albumin (60%), clotting factors, globulins, transferrin, haptoglobin, and lipoproteins. With the exception of globulins, all serum proteins are produced in the liver and are reduced in liver failure. "Plasma proteins" refer to serum proteins without the clotting factors.

destinations.label: Protein analysis → Basics of protein analysis

xicEFX0.title: Ischemic hepatitis
xicEFX0.description: An acute, diffuse hepatocellular injury caused by hepatic hypoperfusion (e.g., cardiopulmonary failure, sepsis). Can be asymptomatic or manifest with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and anorexia. Characterized by transient severe elevations of serum aminotransferase and increased levels of LDH.

0QceuX0.title: Clumping factor A
0QceuX0.description: A virulence factor of S. aureus that binds to fibrinogen, promoting platelet activation, aggregation, and blood clumping.

destinations.label: Staphylococcal diseases → Resistance and virulence of staphylococci

YQcnuX0.title: Serotonergic drug
YQcnuX0.description: A group of drugs that increase serotonin activity in the central and peripheral nervous systems by inhibiting serotonin reuptake (e.g., SSRIs, tricyclic antidepressants) or metabolism (e.g., MAOIs, St. John's wort); increasing serotonin synthesis and release (e.g., amphetamines); or activating serotonin receptors (e.g., triptans).

bQcHuX0.title: Probe-to-bone test
bQcHuX0.description: A clinical test to evaluate for osteomyelitis related to chronic ulcers. A sterile blunt probe is inserted into the ulcer. Direct contact of the probe to bone indicates a possibility of underlying osteomyelitis.

XQc9uX0.title: Parotitis
XQc9uX0.description: An inflammation of the parotid gland. Most commonly caused by viral infections (e.g., mumps, Epstein-Barr virus infection, influenza). Manifestations include local pain and erythema, earache, and progressive swelling of the neck and jaw area.

cQcaEX0.title: Pericardial window
cQcaEX0.description: A surgical procedure in which a portion of the pericardium is removed in order to drain excess fluid from the pericardial space, usually into the pleural cavity. Prevents reaccumulation of fluid in the pericardial space.

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Treatment

1Qc2EX0.title: Haemophilus influenzae serotype b
1Qc2EX0.description: An encapsulated strain of Haemophilus influenzae that can cause severe infections (e.g., meningitis, epiglottitis). The incidence of these infections has decreased with routine vaccination against type b capsular polysaccharide.

WQcPEX0.title: 11-deoxycorticosterone
WQcPEX0.description: A compound formed from progesterone by 21-hydroxylase. Converted to corticosterone by 11β-hydroxylase. Has some mineralocorticoid activity.

dQcoEX0.title: Allergen
dQcoEX0.description: An antigen that elicits an IgE-mediated, type I hypersensitivity response in individuals with an allergy to the substance containing the particular antigen.

destinations.label: Hypersensitivity reactions → Type I hypersensitivity reaction

VQcGEX0.title: Epinephrine autoinjector
VQcGEX0.description: A portable medical device that delivers a prespecified amount of IM epinephrine. Used in the pre-hospital emergency treatment of anaphylaxis. Should be administered into the anterolateral thigh and can be given over clothing. The adult autoinjector contains 0.3 mg and while the pediatric one contains 0.15 mg. Some formulations come preloaded with 2 doses.

UQcbvX0.title: Nebulized
UQcbvX0.description: Referring to the administration of a drug in the form of a mist or spray inhaled into the lungs.

2QcTvX0.title: Cytoreductive therapy
2QcTvX0.description: A form of therapy aimed at reducing the volume of a tumor or collection of cells. Can be performed via surgery, radiation, or medication. Used in the treatment of many malignancies and systemic mastocytosis. Intent can be curative or palliative.

fQckvX0.title: Degranulation
fQckvX0.description: The release of preformed immunomodulatory or cytotoxic substances from secretory vesicles within cells, such as granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils) or mast cells.

SQcyvX0.title: Black hairy tongue
SQcyvX0.description: A condition characterized by elongated filiform papillae of the tongue, which results in yellow-brown discoloration. Associated with smoking, antibiotic therapy, dehydration, and gastrostomy tube use.

hQccDX0.title: Redistribution (pharmacology)
hQccDX0.description: The transfer of an administered drug between different body compartments. The concept is important for understanding the action of lipophilic substances (e.g., inhalational anesthetics). Distribution of lipophilic substances to fatty tissue causes early termination of the drug's action. If the agent is administered over a longer period of time or repeatedly, it builds up in adipose tissue, causing a prolonged drug action and delayed elimination.

3QcSDX0.title: Episclera
3QcSDX0.description: The outermost layer of the sclera, which is the posterior, opaque, and fibrous part of the external layer of the eyeball. Provides vascular supply to the sclera and helps protect and stabilize the eye.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Layers of the eye

RQclDX0.title: Common pathway (hemostasis)
RQclDX0.description: The part of the coagulation cascade at which the intrinsic pathway and extrinsic pathway meet and factor X is activated. Consists of factors X, V, II, and I (fibrinogen).

iQcJDX0.title: Hyperesthesia
iQcJDX0.description: A pathologically increased sensitivity to tactile stimuli that results in an increased sensation of pain.

jQc_DX0.title: Intra-aortic balloon pump
jQc_DX0.description: A circulatory assist device placed in the descending aorta to increase myocardial perfusion. Consists of a double-lumen catheter with an attached balloon close to the tip. Hemodynamic monitoring is used to time inflation and deflation of the balloon. Inflation during diastole leads to increased blood flow into the coronary arteries, while deflation during systole reduces afterload. Typically used as a bridge therapy in conditions with acutely reduced cardiac output (e.g., cardiogenic shock and refractory heart failure).

PQcWwX0.title: Preproinsulin
PQcWwX0.description: The first of two insulin precursors produced following insulin gene transcription and translation. Contains a terminal signal sequence that is cleaved in the rough endoplasmic reticulum to produce proinsulin.

4Qc3wX0.title: Proinsulin
4Qc3wX0.description: The second of two insulin precursors produced following insulin gene transcription and translation, and following cleavage of a signal sequence from preproinsulin in the rough endoplasmic reticulum. Undergoes protein folding and disulfide bridge formation before being packed in secretory granules, together with proteases, for exocytosis. The proteases cleave proinsulin to form mature insulin and C-peptide.

kQcmwX0.title: Transaldolase
kQcmwX0.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of sedoheptulose-7-phosphate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate to erythrose-4-phosphate and fructose-6-phosphate in the nonoxidative (reversible) reaction of the pentose phosphate pathway.

OQcIwX0.title: Serine protein kinase
OQcIwX0.description: An enzyme that phosphorylates the amino acid serine at its hydroxy group.

lQcvwX0.title: Inferior leads
lQcvwX0.description: The ECG leads II, III, and aVF. ST elevation and/or dynamic T wave inversion in these leads corresponds to infarction of the myocardium supplied by the right coronary artery.

NQc-wX0.title: Hofmann elimination
NQc-wX0.description: A process in which a compound spontaneously degrades in the plasma and tissue. Atracurium undergoes Hofmann elimination to laudanosine.

mQcV9X0.title: Lithium-induced hyperparathyroidism
mQcV9X0.description: An adverse effect of lithium therapy caused by the elevation of the calcium-sensing setpoint of the parathyroid glands and induction of parathyroid hormone production.

5Qci9X0.title: Renal outer medullary potassium channel
5Qci9X0.description: An ATP-dependent channel involved in renal potassium homeostasis. In cells of the thick ascending limb, potassium movement through ROMK channels into the lumen creates a gradient that drives passive magnesium and calcium reabsorption through paracellular channels. In principal cells of the cortical collecting duct, potassium is secreted into the lumen through apical ROMK channels and is not reabsorbed.

media.title: Transporters in the distal tubule, pars recta

MQcM9X0.title: Brimonidine
MQcM9X0.description: A selective α2 adrenergic agonist. The ophthalmic formulation decreases the production of aqueous humor and is used to treat open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension. The topical formulation is thought to induce vasoconstriction and is used to treat rosacea-associated erythema.

nQc79X0.title: Lymphangitic carcinomatosis
nQc79X0.description: The presence of cancerous cells in the lymphatics of the pulmonary system (e.g., from lung cancer or metastasis from a different site). Commonly affects the interstitium and results in thickening of bronchovascular bundles and interstitial septae.

LQcw9X0.title: Pulmonary tumor embolism
LQcw9X0.description: The presence of cancerous cells in the pulmonary blood vessels (e.g., from lung cancer or tumor emboli from a different site). Can cause pulmonary hypertension and right-sided heart failure.

oQc0CX0.title: Relative hypotension
oQc0CX0.description: A blood pressure (BP) that is defined by a greater than 20% decrease in the patient’s mean arterial pressure (MAP). This BP may be within the normal range of BPs for the population. However, it may indicate hypoperfusion of important organs because it is acutely lower than the patient’s normal BP.

6QcjCX0.title: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
6QcjCX0.description: A type of brain injury caused by hypoxia and ischemia, typically occurring around birth. Causes include perinatal asphyxia and placental and umbilical cord complications. May result in neurological disabilities, e.g., cerebral palsy, epilepsy, intellectual disability, and hearing and/or visual impairment.

destinations.label: Perinatal asphyxia and hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy → Definitions

pQcLCX0.title: Effective circulating volume
pQcLCX0.description: The portion of extracellular fluid in the arterial system that effectively perfuses tissue.

JQcsCX0.title: Advanced glycation end-products
JQcsCX0.description: A heterogeneous group of compounds formed by reactions between reducing sugars and amino groups. Formation is associated with hyperglycemia (e.g., due to uncontrolled diabetes mellitus) and microvascular disease (e.g., diabetic nephropathy and retinopathy).

qQcCCX0.title: C wave
qQcCCX0.description: The second peak of the jugular venous pulse, which correlates with contraction of the right ventricle and bulging of the tricuspid valve into the right atrium.

IQcYxX0.title: V wave
IQcYxX0.description: A component of the jugular venous pulse that correlates with increased right atrial pressure due to filling against the closed tricuspid valve. Becomes more prominent in patients with tricuspid insufficiency and right heart failure.

rQcfxX0.title: Bone morphogenetic proteins
rQcfxX0.description: A group of growth factors that induce the formation of bone and cartilage both during embryologic development and postnatally. Also involved in ectopic calcification (e.g., of blood vessels).

destinations.label: Cytokines and eicosanoids → Transforming growth factor family

7Qc4xX0.title: Prevotella
7Qc4xX0.description: A genus of anaerobic, gram-negative rods that can cause upper airway infections, aspiration pneumonia, dental infections, and female genital tract infections.

sQctxX0.title: A wave
sQctxX0.description: The first peak of the jugular venous pulse, which correlates with atrial contraction. Becomes absent in patients with atrial fibrillation.

GQcBxX0.title: Matrix γ-carboxyglutamic acid protein
GQcBxX0.description: An antagonist of bone morphogenic proteins that inhibits ectopic calcification (e.g., of blood vessels).

tQcXBX0.title: Acinetobacter baumannii
tQcXBX0.description: A gram-negative, aerobic bacillus that can cause opportunistic, hospital-acquired, multidrug-resistant infections. Often found as a colonizer of the skin, oropharynx, and respiratory tract.

FQcgBX0.title: Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4
FQcgBX0.description: A protein receptor involved in the regulation of T cell activation. Its expression is upregulated by T cell receptor activation and pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g., IL-12, IFN-γ). Anti-CTLA-4 antibodies (e.g., ipilimumab) are immune checkpoint inhibitors used in anticancer therapy.

8QcOBX0.title: Programmed cell death 1
8QcOBX0.description: A transmembrane protein found on T cells, B cells, and NK cells. Functions as a checkpoint inhibitor; binding to PD-1 ligand leads to inhibition of apoptosis. Also promotes the conversion of effector T cells to Treg cells. Targeted by immunotherapies such as pembrolizumab and nivolumab.

uQcpBX0.title: Glutamine phosphoribosylpyrophosphate amidotransferase
uQcpBX0.description: The rate-limiting enzyme of de novo purine synthesis that is involved in the conversion of phosphoribosylpyrophosphate (PRPP) into AMP, IMP, and GMP. Its activity is negatively regulated by these products and inhibited by 6-mercaptopurine.

EQc8BX0.title: Monro-Kellie principle
EQc8BX0.description: A physiologic principle that states that the sum of the volumes of blood, cerebrospinal fluid, and brain within the cranium are constant and remain in a dynamic relationship within the cranial vault. Thus, an increase in one must be compensated by a decrease in the other(s).

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Pathophysiology

vQcABX0.title: Monofilament test
vQcABX0.description: A screening test for peripheral neuropathy (especially due to diabetes). A nylon monofilament is probed onto the foot with enough pressure (∼ 10 g) to bend the monofilament. Several points over both feet are tested, including the dorsal aspect of the 1st web space, the plantar aspect of the toes, and the heads of the metatarsals. Inability to sense pressure indicates loss of sensation of the foot and is a sign of peripheral neuropathy.

DQc1yX0.title: USMLE® Step 2
DQc1yX0.description: A component of the second part of the United States Medical Licensing Examination. It is a 9-hour, computer-based test that consists of ~ 318 multiple-choice questions that are separated into 8 blocks of ~ 40 questions each. Content tested includes principles of clinical science needed to provide patient care (e.g., clinical evaluation and management).

destinations.label: The United States Medical Licensing Examination® (USMLE) → Step 2 CK description

wQchyX0.title: Choroid plexus xanthogranuloma
wQchyX0.description: Generally asymptomatic and incidential tumors of the choroid plexus.  These tumors are rich in cholesterol, mononuclear cells, and hemosiderin blood products. Xanthogranulomas are generally not large enough to be symptomatic. However, they can be fatal when they rupture, in which case they manifest as intraventricular hemorrhage.

9QcNyX0.title: Common bile duct
9QcNyX0.description: A part of the extrahepatic portion of the biliary tree and part of the portal triad that is formed by the union of the common hepatic duct and cystic duct. Travels in the free edge of the lesser omentum in the hepatoduodenal ligament, posterior to the duodenum and the pancreas, and connects with the main pancreatic duct to drain into the ampulla of Vater.

CQcqyX0.title: Total contact cast
CQcqyX0.description: A specialized fiberglass or plaster cast used to offload pressure points of the foot for the management of neuropathic foot ulcers. The cast is customized to fit the contours of the foot in order to distribute body weight equally, which decreases the pressure over areas of the foot that typically bear weight (e.g., heel, metatarsal heads, lateral sole, toes) to expedite ulcer healing.

xQcEyX0.title: 18-hydroxycorticosterone
xQcEyX0.description: A derivative of corticosterone formed during mineralocorticoid production. Converted by aldosterone synthase to aldosterone.

BQczyX0.title: Sclerosing mediastinitis
BQczyX0.description: A condition caused by excessive fibrosis and scarring in the mediastinum, typically secondary to chronic infection (i.e., histoplasmosis, pulmonary tuberculosis) or due to idiopathic causes. Can present similarly to superior vena cava syndrome.

yQcdAX0.title: Mural thrombus
yQcdAX0.description: A blood clot that develops along the endocardium, usually within the left atrium or left ventricle. Etiologies include conditions that cause wall motion abnormalities (e.g., atrial fibrillation, complications of myocardial infarction). Can embolize and cause stroke, renal infarction, and other thromboembolic phenomena.

media.title: Aortic abdominal aneurysm with mural thrombus

cjcazX0.title: Cyclopia
cjcazX0.description: A feature of severe holoprosencephaly in which there is a single, midline orbit and eye. The nose is typically absent or merely a tubular remnant (proboscis).

1jc2zX0.title: Rostral neuropore
1jc2zX0.description: The most rostral (anterior) portion of the embryonic neural tube. Develops into the head and brain. Errors in development of the rostral neuropore can cause anencephaly.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Embryology of the spinal cord

WjcPzX0.title: Mitotic figure
WjcPzX0.description: A histopathologic finding of a nucleus undergoing mitosis, in which chromosome threads can be visualized. A high number of mitotic figures indicates rapidly dividing cells and may indicate that a sample comes from malignant tissue.

media.title: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung

djcozX0.title: Cystoisospora
djcozX0.description: A genus of protozoa that can cause self-limited, watery diarrhea in immunocompetent patients and chronic diarrhea in immunocompromised patients (e.g., due to AIDS). Transmitted by ingestion of oocysts. Can be detected by acid-fast staining and fluorescence techniques. Not readily detected by routine stool ova and parasite examination.

VjcGzX0.title: Kinyoun stain
VjcGzX0.description: A modified version of the Ziehl-Neelsen stain that is used to identify acid-fast species.

ejcxzX0.title: Benserazide
ejcxzX0.description: A decarboxylase inhibitor that is given in combination with levodopa (co-beneldopa) to prevent its decarboxylation to dopamine peripherally, thereby increasing availability in the brain and preventing side-effects of increased peripheral dopamine levels (nausea, vomiting, orthostatic hypotension). Benserazide is not available in the US.

2jcT-X0.title: 72-hour fasting plasma glucose test
2jcT-X0.description: A diagnostic test used to assess for endogenous hyperinsulinism (e.g., suspected insulinoma). The test involves serial laboratory measurements (e.g., insulin, glucose, and C-peptide levels) during and after a medically supervised fast that lasts up to 72 hours. If hypoglycemia develops and insulin levels remain high, the test is positive and fasting is concluded.

fjck-X0.title: Natural increase
fjck-X0.description: The number of births exceeding the number of deaths in a population in a given time period.

gjcF-X0.title: Ribosomal protein S12
gjcF-X0.description: A protein involved in facilitating interactions between tRNA and ribosomal subunits. Mutations in this protein are can confer resistance to streptomycin.

Sjcy-X0.title: SOX10
Sjcy-X0.description: A transcription factor encoded by the SOX10 gene that is involved in the development and differentiation of neural crest cells (e.g., for the formation of the enteric nervous system and melanocytes).

hjccZc0.title: Nestin
hjccZc0.description: An intermediate filament protein expressed primarily in nerve cells. Involved in the radial growth of axons.

QjcuZc0.title: Probiotic therapy
QjcuZc0.description: The use of live microorganisms with potentially beneficial properties to influence host microbiological flora (e.g., oral formulations to influence gut microflora). Effectiveness is unclear.

jjc_Zc0.title: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate
jjc_Zc0.description: A weak androgen produced by the adrenal gland that can be interconverted to dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) by sulfotransferases in the adrenal gland, liver, and intestines. Used as a marker for adrenal androgen secretion (e.g., due to adrenal tumors or functional adrenal hyperandrogenism from polycystic ovary syndrome).

PjcW0c0.title: Granuloma annulare
PjcW0c0.description: A benign, palpable, ring-shaped, skin-colored to violaceous nodule of unclear etiology that most commonly manifests on the extremities (especially the dorsal hands and feet). Typically manifests with localized lesions but can become generalized.

destinations.label: Collection of dermatological disorders → Cutaneous granulomas

4jc30c0.title: Pulmonary consolidation
4jc30c0.description: The replacement of air within alveoli with a different substance (e.g., pus, blood, neoplastic cells). Appears as a poorly demarcated radiopaque area in the lung fields on imaging. Often results in impaired gas exchange. Most commonly caused by pneumonia, but also seen in pulmonary edema, bronchoalveolar carcinoma, and other pulmonary conditions.

kjcm0c0.title: DNA viruses
kjcm0c0.description: A group of viruses that have genetic material composed of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). Includes herpesviruses, poxviruses, hepadnaviruses, adenoviruses, papillomaviruses, polyomaviruses, and parvoviruses.

media.title: General structures of different virus particles

OjcI0c0.title: RNA viruses
OjcI0c0.description: A group of viruses that have genetic material composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA). Includes reoviruses, picornaviruses, hepeviruses, caliciviruses, togaviruses, retroviruses, coronaviruses, orthomyxoviruses, paramyxoviruses, rhabdoviruses, filoviruses, arenaviruses, bunyaviruses, and deltaviruses.

ljcv0c0.title: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia
ljcv0c0.description: A type of schizophrenia defined by persistent positive symptoms (e.g., delusions, hallucinations, and/or disorganized speech) despite trials of ≥ 6 weeks of 2 different antipsychotics at their maximum doses.

Njc-0c0.title: Physician Health Program
Njc-0c0.description: A supervising body that manages clinicians with conditions that potentially impair work (e.g., substance use disorders). Typically not directly involved in treatment but is involved in guiding a clinician's colleagues, directing a clinician to treatment, mediating discussions between the clinician and medical boards, and evaluating readiness to safely return to work.

destinations.label: Medical professionalism and codes of conduct → Malpractice, misconduct, and physician impairment

mjcVac0.title: Patient-controlled analgesia
mjcVac0.description: A type of pain control delivered intravenously by an infusion pump in response to a patient's request (e.g., by pressing a button). Used to manage severe, acute pain that is expected to be limited in duration.

MjcMac0.title: Negative-sense RNA
MjcMac0.description: A type of viral RNA that must be transcribed by RNA-dependent RNA polymerase into positive-sense RNA before it can be translated into proteins.

njc7ac0.title: Positive-sense RNA
njc7ac0.description: A type of viral RNA that, unlike negative-sense RNA, can be readily translated into proteins. Does not require RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.

Ljcwac0.title: Splenic flexure
Ljcwac0.description: The segment of the colon that marks the transition from the transverse colon to the descending colon. Perfused by the peripheries of the vascular territories of the superior mesenteric artery and the inferior mesenteric artery; it is a watershed region.

ojc0Yc0.title: Afterpains
ojc0Yc0.description: A postpartum condition characterized by pain caused by intermittent uterine contractions. Most commonly occur during nursing due to the effect of oxytocin. Typically resolves within one week after delivery.

KjcUYc0.title: Galactocele
KjcUYc0.description: A soft, cystic collection that forms in the breast after obstruction of a milk duct. Typically diagnosed via visualization of a fat-fluid level on mammography, visualization of a complex mass on ultrasonography, and/or aspiration of milky contents.

6jcjYc0.title: Schmorl nodes
6jcjYc0.description: Protrusion of the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral disc into the adjacent vertebral endplate. Common incidental finding on x-ray in asymptomatic patients. Can also occur in association with Scheuermann disease, Wilson disease, sickle cell anemia, and spinal stenosis. Important to differentiate from osteomyelitis and malignancy.

media.title: Scheuermann kyphosis of the lumbar spine

pjcLYc0.title: Serotonin release assay
pjcLYc0.description: A laboratory test used to diagnose heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. The test is positive if radioactively-labeled donor platelets react with the patient's serum, which confirms the presence of an anti-platelet factor 4 antibody.

JjcsYc0.title: Sporothrix schenckii
JjcsYc0.description: A dimorphic, cigar-shaped yeast with branching hyphae and clusters of conidia. Commonly found in soil. Introduction of spores into the skin causes sporotrichosis.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Other fungal infections

qjcCYc0.title: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
qjcCYc0.description: An obstruction to the flow of blood out of the left ventricle, which leads to increased afterload and, in some cases, hypertrophy, dilatation, and ventricular failure. Causes of fixed LVOT obstruction include bicuspid aortic valve and coarctation of the aorta. Causes of dynamic (variable) LVOT obstruction include hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy

IjcYbc0.title: Arabinosyltransferase
IjcYbc0.description: A transferase enzyme that catalyzes the production of arabinoglycan, a constituent of the cell wall of Mycobacteria. Arabinosyltransferase is the target of the antimycobacterial drug ethambutol.

7jc4bc0.title: Adduction
7jc4bc0.description: An anatomical descriptor for movement toward the body's midline.

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

HjcKbc0.title: Retroversion
HjcKbc0.description: An anatomical descriptor for posterior tilting of a body part (e.g., the uterus).

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

sjctbc0.title: Supination
sjctbc0.description: The action of rotating the forearm outward or the sole of the foot inward.

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

GjcBbc0.title: Pronation
GjcBbc0.description: The action of rotating the forearm inward or the sole of the foot outward.

destinations.label: Anatomical terms → Anatomical terms of motion

tjcXXc0.title: Mechanical thrombectomy
tjcXXc0.description: An endovascular procedure in which a stent and stent retriever is used to physically remove a thrombus from the circulation. Used to remove proximal large artery occlusion in the anterior cerebral circulation.

FjcgXc0.title: Circinate balanitis
FjcgXc0.description: A type of balanitis characterized by small, shallow, nontender ulcers on the glans penis. Typically associated with reactive arthritis.

destinations.label: Disorders of the glans penis and foreskin → Balanitis and balanoposthitis

8jcOXc0.title: End-diastolic pressure-volume relationship
8jcOXc0.description: A measure of left ventricular compliance; the slope of the EDPVR (the bottom line of the pressure-volume loop) is the inverse of the ventricular compliance.

ujcpXc0.title: Sine wave pattern
ujcpXc0.description: An ECG finding characterized by absent P waves and wide QRS complexes that merge with the T waves. Can be seen in patients with severe hyperkalemia.

Ejc8Xc0.title: Immunoblast
Ejc8Xc0.description: An activated lymphocyte that later undergoes clonal proliferation. Appears on peripheral blood smear as an enlarged lymphocyte with a deeply basophilic, wide rim of cytoplasm.

wjchcc0.title: Convulsion
