wjchcc0.description: An episode of excessive muscle contraction. Etiologies include generalized convulsive status epilepticus and tonic-clonic seizures.

9jcNcc0.title: Qualitative data
9jcNcc0.description: A variable that is expressed in categorical terms (e.g., eye color, sex, race).

Cjcqcc0.title: Quantitative data
Cjcqcc0.description: A variable that can be measured in numerical terms (e.g., age, weight, temperature).

xjcEcc0.title: Never event
xjcEcc0.description: A serious adverse event that is clearly identifiable, causes serious injury or death, and is considered preventable to the extent that it should never occur. Examples include wrong-site surgery, wrong-patient surgery, post-procedure retention of a foreign object in a patient, ABO mismatch, and inpatient suicide. There is some overlap in the definitions of never events and sentinel events.

Bjczcc0.title: Forcing function
Bjczcc0.description: A design element that prevents an action from being performed by the user or does not allow one action to be completed before another, separate action is performed. For example, if an electronic medical record requires the user to enter a password and a reason for accessing confidential psychiatric records, the user must make an active choice to view those records and cannot inadvertently view sensitive data.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medical errors

AjcR1c0.title: Streptococcus sanguinis
AjcR1c0.description: A gram-positive, catalase-negative, alpha-hemolytic coccus that is a part of the Viridans streptococci group of bacteria. Associated with dental plaques and can cause subacute bacterial endocarditis.

_jc51c0.title: Radial glial cell
_jc51c0.description: Embryonic glial cells that play an important role in the production and migration of neurons during brain development. Primarily located in the periventricular zones.

zjcr1c0.title: Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act
zjcr1c0.description: An act passed by US Congress in 1986 that requires emergency departments in hospitals that receive Medicare funding to evaluate any patient presenting for care, and to stabilize individuals with emergency medical conditions (including labor), regardless of the patient's ability to pay for the treatment provided.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care access

-jcD1c0.title: Skew deviation
-jcD1c0.description: A vertical misalignment of the eyes caused by a supranuclear lesion of cranial nerves III, IV, and VI in which one eye is rotated downward and inward while the other eye is rotated upward and outward. Typically associated with other signs of posterior fossa dysfunction (e.g., hemisensory loss and hemiparesis).

ZPcZWc0.title: Synthetic cathinone
ZPcZWc0.description: A synthetic analog of a naturally-occurring amphetamine. Intoxication typically causes manifestations of sympathetic stimulation (e.g., hyperthermia, tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis, mydriasis) and neuropsychiatric symptoms (e.g., agitation, hallucinations, paranoia). Not typically detectable on routine urine toxicology screening.

0PceWc0.title: Non-enzymatic fat necrosis
0PceWc0.description: A form of necrosis seen in fat deposits (e.g., the breast) following blunt trauma or surgery.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Necrosis

YPcnWc0.title: Staging of chronic kidney disease
YPcnWc0.description: A staging system used to classify the degree of decline in renal function for patients with chronic kidney disease. Classification is based on the cause, eGFR category (G1-G5), and albuminuria category (A1-A3).

dPcodc0.title: Corona phlebectatica
dPcodc0.description: A circular collection of small veins that can develop around the lateral or medial aspect of the ankle. Associated with underlying venous disease.

media.title: Telangiectasias, reticular veins, and corona phlebectatica

VPcGdc0.title: Turbulent blood flow
VPcGdc0.description: A disordered blood flow that most commonly occurs at arterial branch points and through stenotic vessels and valves. Creates sound waves that can be auscultated as murmurs or bruits.

ePcxdc0.title: Choroid plexitis
ePcxdc0.description: An inflammation of the choroid plexus typically seen in association with an infectious process (e.g. encephalitis, meningitis, and/or ventriculitis caused by Nocardia or Cryptococcus). Identified on CT or MRI as bilateral enlargement of the choroid plexus or lateral ventricle choroid plexus asymmetry.

UPcbVc0.title: Colloid cyst (brain)
UPcbVc0.description: A developmental malformation that typically occurs in the anterior third ventricle and can lead to hydrocephalus by blocking the foramen of Monro. Usually consists of an inner layer of mucin-producing or ciliated cells that produce a gelatinous material (colloid) enclosed in a fibrous outer layer. Typically asymptomatic but can cause intermittent headache and sudden, spontaneous falls.

2PcTVc0.title: Scaphoid abdomen
2PcTVc0.description: An abdomen that has a sunken, concave anterior abdominal wall. Can be seen in newborns with diaphragmatic hernia.

fPckVc0.title: Prophage
fPckVc0.description: The genetic material that a bacteriophage inserts into an infected bacterium, which can be integrated into the infected bacterium's chromosome or remain as a separate plasmid.

TPc6Vc0.title: Monoclonal proliferation
TPc6Vc0.description: The production of a single cell type from one ancestral cell. In contrast to polyclonal proliferation, monoclonal proliferation is typically pathologic (e.g., excessive proliferation of a single plasma cell that results in multiple myeloma).

SPcyVc0.title: Time to echo
SPcyVc0.description: The time between the delivery of external radio frequency energy and measurement of emitted radio frequency energy on magnetic resonance imaging.

hPccec0.title: Repetition time
hPccec0.description: The amount of time between radio frequency pulses delivered to a slice on magnetic resonance imaging.

3PcSec0.title: Bacterial competence
3PcSec0.description: The ability of some bacteria to undergo transformation (i.e., the transfer and expression of new genes from environmental bacterial DNA). Can be intrinsic (i.e., natural competence) or induced by laboratory conditions (i.e., artificial or induced competence).

RPclec0.title: Far-eastern blot
RPclec0.description: A laboratory method of transferring lipids onto a thin polyvinylidene fluoride membrane. Used in the investigation of membrane-bound enzyme reactions and the structural analysis of lipids.

iPcJec0.title: c-KIT mutation
iPcJec0.description: A mutation of the c-KIT cytokine receptor. Activating mutations are associated with tumorigenesis (e.g., of gastrointestinal stromal tumors). Inactivating mutations are associated with piebaldism.

QPcuec0.title: Cycloplegia
QPcuec0.description: A loss of lens accommodation due to paralysis of the ciliary muscle. Often induced by ophthalmic drugs (e.g., muscarinic antagonists).

jPc_ec0.title: L cell
jPc_ec0.description: An enteroendocrine cell of the gastrointestinal mucosa that secretes glucagon-like peptide-1 in response to food intake. Mediates long-term satiety.

PPcWUc0.title: Arabinogalactan
PPcWUc0.description: A polysaccharide formed by the two monosaccharides arabinose and galactose. Part of the mycobacterial cell wall.

4Pc3Uc0.title: Rest pain
4Pc3Uc0.description: A symptom of severe peripheral artery disease characterized by constant pain, most commonly around the distal metatarsals. Typically worsens with elevation and improves with dependency (e.g., hanging feet over the edge of a bed or standing).

kPcmUc0.title: NMDA receptor antagonist
kPcmUc0.description: A class of drugs that inhibit the action of the NMDA receptor. Results in a wide variety of effects with applications in sedation and analgesia. Examples include ketamine, amantadine, dextromethorphan, and phencyclidine (PCP).

media.title: Mechanism of action: drugs used in Parkinson disease

OPcIUc0.title: Alpha-2 receptor agonist
OPcIUc0.description: A group of drugs that activate α2 receptors in presynaptic sympathetic neurons of the central nervous system, which leads to a decrease in sympathetic tone that causes vasodilation and lowers blood pressure. Adverse effects include orthostatic hypotension, sedation, and bradycardia. Agents include clonidine and methyldopa.

lPcvUc0.title: Effector T cells
lPcvUc0.description: A group of T cells that respond to a stimulus by migrating to a site of infection and producing cytotoxins. Includes T helper cells, killer T cells, and regulatory T cells.

NPc-Uc0.title: Piriform sinus
NPc-Uc0.description: A set of depressions in the hypopharynx located posterolaterally to both sides of the laryngeal opening. Food particles can become trapped in these spaces. Squamous cell carcinoma of the hypopharynx most commonly develops in this region.

mPcV2c0.title: Lipodystrophy
mPcV2c0.description: A condition characterized by a lack of adipose tissue (i.e., lipoatrophy). Can be congenital (e.g., due to inherited metabolic syndromes) or acquired (e.g., drug-induced lipodystrophy at the site of injection of insulin).

MPcM2c0.title: Alpha-2 receptor antagonist
MPcM2c0.description: A class of drugs that blocks presynaptic α2 receptors, which results in increased release of norepinephrine and serotonin. There are few drugs of this class that are used clinically; mirtazapine is an α2 receptor antagonist used to treat depression.

nPc72c0.title: Interleukin-28
nPc72c0.description: A cytokine secreted by dendritic cells after viral or bacterial activation that mainly targets epithelial cells and hepatocytes.

LPcw2c0.title: State medical board
LPcw2c0.description: A supervisory entity that governs physician and physician assistant licensure and the practice of medicine by these licensees in a state. Can initiate disciplinary actions in case of violation of a medical licensing provision.

6Pcjfc0.title: Child protective services
6Pcjfc0.description: A government agency that is responsible for protecting children who are abused and/or neglected. In the United States, child protective services are typically organized at the individual state level.

destinations.label: Ethics of communicating medical information → Reporting

pPcLfc0.title: Fluorescein staining
pPcLfc0.description: A type of staining used to identify corneal abrasions and foreign bodies in the eye during ophthalmologic evaluation. Fluorescein stains the basement membrane, which is exposed following damage to the cornea. Areas stained by fluorescein fluoresce upon slit lamp, ophthalmoscopic, and Wood lamp examination.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Slit lamp biomicroscopy examination

media.title: Corneal abrasion highlighted by fluorescein staining

JPcsfc0.title: Scald
JPcsfc0.description: A thermal injury sustained from contact with hot fluids (e.g., boiling water, steam). The most common burn injury among children.

media.title: Second-degree scalding injury (2b; deep partial-thickness burn) after initial debridement

qPcCfc0.title: Dartos fascia
qPcCfc0.description: A thin layer of connective tissue deep to the skin of the scrotum. Contains the dartos muscle.

IPcYTc0.title: Dartos muscle
IPcYTc0.description: A thin layer of smooth muscle within the tunica dartos in the scrotum. Contraction causes wrinkling of the scrotal skin, which decreases heat loss.

rPcfTc0.title: External spermatic fascia
rPcfTc0.description: A thin membrane derived from the aponeurosis of the external oblique muscle. Covers the surface of the spermatic cord and testes.

media.title: Structure and content of the spermatic cord

7Pc4Tc0.title: P/D1 cell
7Pc4Tc0.description: A specialized enteroendocrine cell that secretes ghrelin. Most abundant in the gastric fundus.

HPcKTc0.title: 5-HT2A receptor
HPcKTc0.description: A serotonin receptor targeted by second-generation antipsychotics (e.g., risperidone, quetiapine, ziprasidone).

sPctTc0.title: Cremasteric fascia
sPctTc0.description: A layer of fascia surrounding the testes. Derived from the aponeurosis of the abdominal internal oblique muscle. Contains the cremasteric muscle.

media.title: Layers of the abdominal wall and male reproductive organs

GPcBTc0.title: Cremaster muscle
GPcBTc0.description: A thin layer of striated and smooth muscle that covers the testes and the spermatic cord. Originates from the internal oblique muscle and inserts into the tunica vaginalis. Raises and lowers the testes to regulate scrotal temperature.

tPcXgc0.title: Internal spermatic fascia
tPcXgc0.description: A thin membrane derived from the abdominal transversalis fascia. Covers the surface of the spermatic cord and testes.

FPcggc0.title: Fibrin degradation products
FPcggc0.description: A group of compounds created when plasmin cleaves crosslinked fibrin. Multiple FDPs are generated by this process because fibrin is cleaved at multiple sites. D-dimer is an FDP used clinically to assess for recent intravascular coagulation and/or fibrinolysis.

8PcOgc0.title: Saddle pulmonary embolism
8PcOgc0.description: A blood clot (e.g., from deep vein thrombosis) that lodges at the bifurcation of the pulmonary trunk as it splits into the right and left pulmonary arteries. Can obstruct blood flow through the pulmonary arteries and lead to right heart strain, hemodynamic instability, and/or death.

uPcpgc0.title: Apolipoprotein B
uPcpgc0.description: An apolipoprotein found in several lipoproteins, including chylomicrons, LDL, and VLDL. Further subdivided into apolipoprotein B-48 and B-100.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

EPc8gc0.title: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein
EPc8gc0.description: A protein involved in the production of several beta-lipoproteins, including chylomicrons, LDL, and VLDL. Mutations in the gene that encodes this protein can cause hereditary abetalipoproteinemia.

DPc1Sc0.title: Cecum
DPc1Sc0.description: The most proximal portion of the large intestine (located proximal to the ascending colon). Located in the right iliac fossa. Includes the vermiform appendix.

wPchSc0.title: Colon
wPchSc0.description: The portion of the gastrointestinal tract between the cecum and the rectum. It is the largest portion of the large intestine. Consists of ascending, transverse, descending, and sigmoid parts.

9PcNSc0.title: Rectum
9PcNSc0.description: A portion of the large intestine located posterior to the bladder. Becomes the anal canal at the level of the coccyx.

CPcqSc0.title: Ascending colon
CPcqSc0.description: The most proximal portion of the colon, which courses from the right iliac fossa to the inferior aspect of the liver. Retroperitoneal.

xPcESc0.title: Transverse colon
xPcESc0.description: The portion of the colon between the ascending and descending parts. Courses from the inferior aspect of the liver to the inferior aspect of the spleen. Intraperitoneal.

BPczSc0.title: Descending colon
BPczSc0.description: The portion of the colon between the transverse and sigmoid parts. Courses from the inferior aspect of the spleen to the left iliac fossa. Retroperitoneal.

yPcdhc0.title: Sigmoid colon
yPcdhc0.description: The most distal portion of the colon, which courses from the left iliac fossa to the rectum. Intraperitoneal.

APcRhc0.title: Anorectal junction
APcRhc0.description: An angle between the anal canal and the lower part of the rectum at the level of the pelvic floor.

_Pc5hc0.title: Taenia coli
_Pc5hc0.description: Three longitudinal smooth muscle bands located in the muscularis propia of the cecum and colon.

zPcrhc0.title: Haustra
zPcrhc0.description: Saccular outpouchings of the colonic wall that give the colon its characteristic segmental appearance. Haustra are identifiable on a plain abdominal x-ray. The sigmoid colon is devoid of haustra.

-PcDhc0.title: Apple core lesion
-PcDhc0.description: A lesion caused by constriction of a lumen with proximal dilation, which results in the characteristic appearance of an apple core. Can be caused by colorectal carcinoma and esophageal carcinoma.

04ce3c0.title: Ischiocavernosus muscle
04ce3c0.description: A pair of superficial pelvic wall muscles that facilitate the movement of blood from the crura into the body of the penis or clitoris. Innervated by the pudendal nerve.

a4cQ3c0.title: Ribose-5-phosphate
a4cQ3c0.description: A product of the non-oxidative branch of the pentose phosphate pathway and an intermediate of the oxidative branch. Serves as a precursor to many other biomolecules (e.g., nucleotides, DNA, RNA, ATP).

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Pentose phosphate pathway

Y4cn3c0.title: Sleep spindle
Y4cn3c0.description: A short burst of EEG waves with a frequency of 12–14 Hz that occurs during stage N2 of nonrapid eye movement sleep.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Sleep physiology

b4cH3c0.title: K-complex
b4cH3c0.description: A high amplitude, diphasic (negative waveform followed by positive waveform), frontocentral slow wave seen on EEG during stage N2 of nonrapid eye movement sleep.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Sleep physiology

X4c93c0.title: Per diem payment
X4c93c0.description: A health care payment model in which a health care organization is compensated a fixed amount per patient per day for a specific care service provided, regardless of the actual costs involved for providing services for any particular patient.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payment models

c4caRc0.title: Lead pipe sign
c4caRc0.description: A finding seen on contrast barium enema of patients with ulcerative colitis. Characterized by the complete loss of haustral markings in the colon due to chronic inflammation, which results in a smooth, cylindrical appearance of the affected colon.

14c2Rc0.title: Griffiths point
14c2Rc0.description: A watershed area near the splenic flexure (approximately ⅔ of the way along transverse colon) where a branch from the ascending left colic artery forms a small anastomosis with the marginal artery of the colon. Connects terminal branches of the superior mesenteric artery and inferior mesenteric artery. Susceptible to ischemic colitis.

W4cPRc0.title: Sudeck point
W4cPRc0.description: A watershed area of the rectosigmoid junction where a branch from the inferior mesenteric artery forms a small anastomosis with a branch of the superior rectal artery. Susceptible to ischemic colitis.

d4coRc0.title: AMBOSS
d4coRc0.description: A platform used by medical professionals worldwide to learn, practice, and teach. Includes comprehensive, personalized Qbanks and a Library developed by over 100 clinicians and technology experts. Combines trusted, high-quality medical content with meaningful, cutting-edge technology. The AMBOSS mission is to empower all medical professionals to provide the best possible care.

V4cGRc0.title: Internal hemorrhoidal plexus of veins
V4cGRc0.description: A plexus of veins located in the submucosa of the anal canal, proximal to the pectinate line. Drains into the portal system of veins. Internal hemorrhoids form from dilated veins of this plexus.

e4cxRc0.title: External hemorrhoidal plexus of veins
e4cxRc0.description: A plexus of veins located in the submucosa of the anal canal, distal to the pectinate line. Drains into the systemic (caval) system of veins. External hemorrhoids form from dilated veins of this plexus.

U4cbic0.title: Graded challenge test
U4cbic0.description: The administration of a drug in a controlled clinical setting to rule out a drug hypersensitivity reaction (DHR). The patient is exposed to increasing amounts of the drug until a full dose has been administered, then observed to determine whether a DHR occurs. Does not distinguish between allergic and nonallergic reactions.

24cTic0.title: Population pyramid
24cTic0.description: A graphical representation of age and sex distribution of a population.

destinations.label: Population health → Elements describing population health

T4c6ic0.title: Soft tissue
T4c6ic0.description: A type of tissue that is nonossified and noncalcified. Surrounds, connects and supports hard tissue (e.g., bone) and internal organs. Includes muscle, tendons, ligaments, fascia, synovial membranes, skin, adipose tissue, and both blood and lymphatic vessels.

g4cFic0.title: Acute calculous cholecystitis
g4cFic0.description: An acute inflammation of the gallbladder due to gallstone obstruction of the cystic duct. Most common type of cholecystitis.

S4cyic0.title: Cinacalcet
S4cyic0.description: A drug that increases the sensitivity of the calcium-sensing receptor on parathyroid glands. Results in lower serum concentrations of parathyroid hormone, calcium, and phosphorus. Used to treat hypercalcemia (e.g., due to hyperparathyroidism, parathyroid carcinoma).

i4cJQc0.title: Unconscious proprioception
i4cJQc0.description: The unconscious perception of relative position and movement of the body. Coordinated by the cerebellum and the spinocerebellar tract.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

k4cmjc0.title: Parinaud syndrome
k4cmjc0.description: A group of ophthalmologic findings associated with pretectal lesions. Includes vertical gaze abnormalities, nystagmus, impaired convergence, upper eyelid retraction, ptosis, and pupillary abnormalities.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

N4c-jc0.title: Hepatic capsule
N4c-jc0.description: The two adherent layers that cover the liver. Consists of an outer serous layer derived from peritoneum, which covers the entire liver (except the bare area), and a fibrous inner layer (the Glisson capsule) that covers the entire liver (including the bare area).

m4cVPc0.title: Lines of Zahn
m4cVPc0.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by alternating pink layers (which consist of platelets and fibrin) and red layers (which consist of erythrocytes). Found in thrombi that are formed at sites of high blood flow (e.g., arterial thrombi that form antemortem).

54ciPc0.title: Stellate cell (cerebellum)
54ciPc0.description: A star-shaped neuron with multiple arborizations that forms part of the molecular (outermost) later of the cerebellar cortex.

M4cMPc0.title: Intestinal taeniasis
M4cMPc0.description: A condition caused by the ingestion of Taenia larva in undercooked or raw meat. T. solium is associated with pork; T. saginata is associated with beef. Typically asymptomatic but can cause gastrointestinal symptoms such as abdominal pain, anorexia, weight loss, nausea, vomiting, and obstruction.

media.title: Head of a pork tapeworm (Taenia solium)

n4c7Pc0.title: Hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis
n4c7Pc0.description: An endocrine axis that regulates the production of sex hormones. Includes the hypothalamus (which produces gonadotopin-releasing hormone), the anterior pituitary gland (which produces luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone), and the gonads (which produce estrogen and testosterone).

L4cwPc0.title: Osteomalacia
L4cwPc0.description: A condition characterized by impaired osteoid mineralization and disrupted microarchitecture at the growth plate. Can be caused by vitamin D deficiency (most common), proximal tubular acidosis, and hypophosphatemia. Manifestations include bone pain, pathologic fractures, and myopathy.

o4c04c0.title: Rickets
o4c04c0.description: A pediatric condition characterized by impaired mineralization and disrupted microarchitecture at the growth plate. Can be caused by vitamin D deficiency (most common), proximal tubular acidosis, hypophosphatemia, and low oral calcium intake. Manifestations include bone deformities (e.g., genu varum, costochondral abnormalities) and impaired growth.

media.title: Rickets secondary to vitamin D deficiency fact sheet

K4cU4c0.title: Growth hormone receptor deficiency
K4cU4c0.description: An autosomal recessive condition caused by a defect of growth hormone receptors. Manifestations include short stature, microcephaly, saddle nose, and metabolic abnormalities (e.g., hyperlipidemia, episodic hypoglycemia).

destinations.label: Short stature → Genetic causes of short stature

64cj4c0.title: Bispecific antibody
64cj4c0.description: An antibody that can interact with two specific molecules. Can be used to bring T cells (e.g., by binding to CD3, a T-cell surface molecule) and tumor cells (by binding to tumor antigens) together to induce an immune response to the tumor.

p4cL4c0.title: Catumaxomab
p4cL4c0.description: A monoclonal antibody that binds to CD3 (a T-cell surface molecule) and epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM, a tumor cell surface marker). Has an Fc region that can bind to macrophages, natural killer cells, and dendritic cells. Used to treat malignancy-related ascites.

J4cs4c0.title: Cytotoxic drug-antibody complex
J4cs4c0.description: A type of anticancer therapy that consists of a cytotoxic drug linked to an antibody to a tumor cell antigen. The antibody domain allows the drug to target tumor cells with higher specificity than conventional chemotherapy. Examples include brentuximab vedotin and trastuzumab emtansine.

q4cC4c0.title: Bispecific T-cell engager
q4cC4c0.description: A bispecific, monoclonal antibody that is used to recruit T cells (via binding to CD3) to cancer cells (via binding to a tumor antigen).

I4cYkc0.title: Single-chain variable fragment
I4cYkc0.description: A fusion protein that consists of the heavy and light chain variable regions (VH and VL) of an antibody, which are connected by a peptide linker.

r4cfkc0.title: Superior tarsal muscle
r4cfkc0.description: A smooth muscle that originates in the levator palpebrae superioris and inserts in the superior tarsal plate of the eyelid. Its primary function is to raise the eyelid and the levator palpebrae superioris. Innervated by branches of the sympathetic chain from the superior cervical ganglion. Can be denervated in Horner syndrome, which results in ptosis.

s4ctkc0.title: Tripod position
s4ctkc0.description: A position adopted by patients with respiratory distress in which they lean forward while sitting, with their hands on their knees. Optimizes the use of accessory muscles of respiration.

G4cBkc0.title: Rete testis
G4cBkc0.description: A network of collecting tubules located in the hilum of the testis. Receives spermatozoa from the seminiferous tubules and gives rise to the efferent ductules, which eventually connect with the epididymis.

t4cXOc0.title: Scrotum
t4cXOc0.description: Distal sac-like end of the spermatic cord that is continuous with the anterior abdominal wall and contains the testes.

84cOOc0.title: Lingula (lung)
84cOOc0.description: A projection of the upper lobe of the left lung that consists of two bronchopulmonary segments: the superior lingular segment and the inferior lingular segment.

E4c8Oc0.title: Duodenojejunal flexure
E4c8Oc0.description: A junction between the jejunum and the 4th part of duodenum. Located on the left side of the L2 vertebra.

v4cAOc0.title: Duodenum
v4cAOc0.description: The first and widest part of the small intestine. Except for its first part, the duodenum is a retroperitoneal organ.

D4c1lc0.title: Jejunum
D4c1lc0.description: The second part of the small intestine. Intraperitoneal.

w4chlc0.title: Ileum
w4chlc0.description: The last and narrowest part of the small intestine. Intraperitoneal.

94cNlc0.title: Lordosis
94cNlc0.description: A ventral convexity of the spine. The lumbar and cervical regions of the spine are physiologically lordotic. Increased lordosis (hyperlordosis) in the lumbar spine occurs to compensate for hyperkyphosis in the thoracic spine or fixed flexion deformity of the hips, in patients with developmental dysplasia of the hip, achondroplasia, and obesity.

C4cqlc0.title: Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery
C4cqlc0.description: A branch of the superior mesenteric artery that supplies the head of the pancreas and parts of the duodenum. Anastomoses with branches of the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery.

media.title: Arterial supply of the duodenum, pancreas, and spleen

B4czlc0.title: Pepsinogen
B4czlc0.description: A prohormone produced by gastric chief cells in response to vagal stimulation and stomach acid. Converted to pepsin by stomach acid.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

A4cRNc0.title: Non-24 hour sleep-wake disorder
A4cRNc0.description: A circadian rhythm disorder in which patients are not able to align with the environmental 24-hour rhythm. More common in people who are blind.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders

-4cDNc0.title: Gastric inhibitory polypeptide
-4cDNc0.description: A hormone produced by the K cells of the duodenum and jejunum. Increases pancreatic insulin secretion and decreases gastric acid secretion.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal tract → Secretory and regulatory products of the gastrointestinal tract

ZkcZmc0.title: Multidetector computed tomography
ZkcZmc0.description: A computed tomography imaging technique that has higher spatial resolution than conventional computed tomography due to its use of multiple detectors.

0kcemc0.title: Corneal dystrophy
0kcemc0.description: A group of inherited noninflammatory disorders that cause the accumulation of various substances in the cornea and result in morphological changes. Symptoms include progressive visual impairment and symptoms of recurrent corneal erosion (e.g., foreign body sensation, eye pain, tearing, and blurry vision).

destinations.label: Corneal disorders → Corneal degeneration, dystrophy, and deposits

akcQmc0.title: Mo cells
akcQmc0.description: A type of enteroendocrine cell of the small intestine that secretes motilin.

bkcHmc0.title: Plicae circulares
bkcHmc0.description: A collection of transverse folds of the mucosa and submucosa of the small intestine that increase absorptive surface area. Most prominent in the jejunum.

Xkc9mc0.title: Intestinal villi
Xkc9mc0.description: A collection of finger-like projections of gasrointestinal mucosa. Each contains smaller projections called microvilli and has an arteriole, venule, and lymphatic channel at its core. Lined by simple columnar epithelium and specialized cells of the small intestine.

1kc25c0.title: Suspensory muscle of duodenum
1kc25c0.description: A fold of peritoneum that attaches the duodenojejunal flexure to the retroperitoneum. Can be used as a landmark to distinguish between the upper and lower gastrointestinal tracts.

WkcP5c0.title: Pars interarticularis
WkcP5c0.description: The region of a vertebra between the superior and inferior articular processes at the junction of the pedicle and lamina. Fracture or defect of the pars interarticularis results in spondylolysis. Bilateral fractures can allow the vertebra cranial to the fractures to slip forward and result in spondylolisthesis.

UkcbMc0.title: Donabedian model
UkcbMc0.description: A method of evaluating healthcare quality. Comprises the domains of structural measures, process measures, outcome measures, and balancing measures.

2kcTMc0.title: Process measures
2kcTMc0.description: A domain of measurement in the Donabedian model to assess the quality of health care. Comprises an evaluation of the actions performed in a health care system as it was planned. Includes diagnostics, treatment, and preventive care (e.g., percentage of individuals receiving immunizations or cancer screening).

fkckMc0.title: Outcome measures
fkckMc0.description: A domain of measurement in the Donabedian model. Measures the final impact of healthcare services or interventions on patient health status (e.g., maternal mortality rates, rates of surgical complications).

Tkc6Mc0.title: Balancing measures
Tkc6Mc0.description: A domain of measurement in the Donabedian model to assess the quality of health care. They evaluate unintended consequences of change in one system of health care on other systems/outcomes (e.g., hypoglycemia rates after an initiative to reduce the HbA1c, readmission rates after an initiative to reduce hospital length of stay).

hkccnc0.title: Defensin
hkccnc0.description: An antimicrobial peptide secreted by Paneth cells of the small intestine as part of the innate immune response.

3kcSnc0.title: Caudal neuropore
3kcSnc0.description: The most caudal (posterior) portion of the embryonic neural tube. Develops into portions of the spinal cord. Errors in development of the rostral neuropore can cause spina bifida.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Embryology of the spinal cord

Rkclnc0.title: Blinatumomab
Rkclnc0.description: A bispecific T-cell engager that targets CD3 (to recruit T cells) and CD19 (a B cell surface molecule). Results in proliferation of T cells and an immune response against CD19-positive cells. Used to treat refractory acute lymphoid leukemia.

Qkcunc0.title: Corneal degeneration
Qkcunc0.description: A gradual deterioration of corneal tissue. Etiologies include normal aging, band keratopathy due to hypercalcemia, and trauma. Can affect the ability of the eye to focus.

destinations.label: Corneal disorders → Corneal degeneration, dystrophy, and deposits

kkcmLc0.title: Biphasic anaphylactic reaction
kkcmLc0.description: A type of anaphylactic reaction characterized by the recurrence of symptoms within 6-24 hours after initially successful treatment and without re-exposure to an antigen.

lkcvLc0.title: Popcorn cell
lkcvLc0.description: A variant of a Reed-Sternberg cell characterized by polylobulated nuclei that resemble popcorn. Associated with nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma.

mkcVoc0.title: Endocervix
mkcVoc0.description: The mucosal surface of the cervical canal (supravaginal cervix). Lined with simple columnar epithelium.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Uterus and cervix

5kcioc0.title: Ectocervix
5kcioc0.description: The mucosal surface of the vaginal cervix. Lined with nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Uterus and cervix

Lkcwoc0.title: Omentum
Lkcwoc0.description: A part of the visceral peritoneum that extends from the stomach and proximal duodenum to other abdominal organs (e.g., stomach, liver). Further divided into the greater omentum and lesser omentum.

okc0Kc0.title: Peritoneal ligaments
okc0Kc0.description: A collection of folds of visceral peritoneum between certain gastrointestinal organs or between a gastrointestinal organ and the abdominal wall. Examples include the gastrosplenic, gastrocolic, and hepatoduodenal ligaments.

6kcjKc0.title: Gastrophrenic ligament
6kcjKc0.description: A fold of visceral peritoneum that extends between the stomach and the diaphragm. Contains the left inferior phrenic artery. Anchors the stomach to the diaphragm.

pkcLKc0.title: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy
pkcLKc0.description: A condition in which anterior degeneration of the spinal canal (e.g., due to osteophytes of the cervical vertebrae) results in compression of the cervical spinal cord. It is the most common cause of cervical myelopathy.

JkcsKc0.title: Peritoneal spaces
JkcsKc0.description: A group of potential spaces between adjacent organs or between an organ and the abdominal wall in which intraperitoneal fluid can accumulate. Examples include the hepatorenal space and the pelvic spaces such as the rectouterine space.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

qkcCKc0.title: Right hepatic artery
qkcCKc0.description: A branch of the proper hepatic artery that supplies the caudate lobe (segment I) and the right portion (segments V-VIII) of the liver. Often gives rise to the cystic artery.

IkcY6c0.title: Left hepatic artery
IkcY6c0.description: A branch of the proper hepatic artery that supplies the caudate lobe (segment I) and the left portion (segments II-IV) of the liver. Often gives rise to the middle hepatic artery.

rkcf6c0.title: Peritoneal cavity
rkcf6c0.description: The potential space between parietal and visceral peritoneum. Includes the greater sac and the lesser sac.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

7kc46c0.title: Visceral peritoneum
7kc46c0.description: A component of peritoneum that forms the serosal surface of the intraperitoneal organs, mesentery, omentum, and peritoneal ligaments. Receives visceral innervation and is pain insensitive.

media.title: Peritoneum and fascias of the abdomen

HkcK6c0.title: Parietal peritoneum
HkcK6c0.description: A component of peritoneum that lines the abdominopelvic cavity. Receives somatic innervation and is pain sensitive.

media.title: Peritoneum and fascias of the abdomen

skct6c0.title: Lipemia retinalis
skct6c0.description: An ophthalmologic finding characterized by pale pink discoloration of the retinal vessels and/or fundus due to light scattering from increased concentrations of chylomicrons. Does not affect vision.

GkcB6c0.title: Familial dyslipidemias
GkcB6c0.description: A group of heritable conditions that cause increased serum lipoprotein levels as a result of abnormalities in proteins involved in lipid metabolism. Examples include familial hyperchylomicronemia, familial hypercholesterolemia, and familial dysbetalipoproteinemia.

Fkcgpc0.title: Layers of the alimentary canal
Fkcgpc0.description: The alimentary canal consists of four layers: the mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria, and the serosa (for intraperitoneal organs) or adventitia (for retroperitoneal organs).

8kcOpc0.title: Q wave
8kcOpc0.description: An ECG finding that represents the beginning of ventricular depolarization. Normal Q waves are narrow (< 0.04 s). Pathologic Q waves are abnormally wide (≥ 0.04 s) and/or abnormally deep (≥ 0.2 mV or > 25% of the R wave amplitude) and can develop due to myocardial injury.

ukcppc0.title: Primitive gut tube
ukcppc0.description: A derivative of the endodermal lining of the yolk sac that develops into the gastrointestinal tract. Regions include the the foregut, midgut, and hindgut.

vkcApc0.title: Descemet membrane
vkcApc0.description: The basement membrane of the corneal endothelium. Located between the stromal tissue of the cornea and the corneal endothelium.

Dkc1Jc0.title: La belle indifférence
Dkc1Jc0.description: A lack of concern about the nature or implications of symptoms of illness. It is classically associated with conversion disorder but is not specific to this condition; it may also be present in neurological conditions (e.g., Parkinson disease, stroke, epilepsy).

destinations.label: Somatic symptom and related disorders → Functional neurological symptom disorder

wkchJc0.title: Valvulitis
wkchJc0.description: An inflammation of the endocardium that involves a heart valve. Can cause regurgitation murmurs. Associated with rheumatic fever.

xkcEJc0.title: Elbow anastomosis
xkcEJc0.description: Anastomosis of several upper extremity arteries (brachial, deep brachial, ulnar, and radial) around the elbow joint that functions to nourish the articular and periarticular tissues of the elbow.

destinations.label: Upper arm and elbow → Elbow joint

BkczJc0.title: Intercostobrachial nerve
BkczJc0.description: The lateral cutaneous branch of the second intercostal nerve. This nerve originates in the thorax but traverses the axilla to innervate the skin in the medial, proximal arm. This nerve can be damaged in axillary lymph node dissections.

_kc5qc0.title: Trendelenburg position
_kc5qc0.description: A position in which the patient is supine with the head tilted down such that the legs are above the level of the heart. Uses of this position include certain abdominal surgeries (for better access to pelvic structures), internal jugular vein catheterization (to increase vein prominence), and prevention of obstructive shock from large venous air emboli.

zkcrqc0.title: Protein F
zkcrqc0.description: A fibronectin‑binding protein that mediates the adherence of S. pyogenes to epithelial cells.

-kcDqc0.title: Grief
-kcDqc0.description: The cognitive, behavioral, and emotional response to the loss or death of someone close. Grief constitutes a normal reaction to loss. It has a variable duration but typically lasts 6–12 months. Treatment is usually not required.

destinations.label: Grief and end-of-life counseling → Bereavement and grief

0OceIc0.title: Intraperitoneal
0OceIc0.description: A descriptor for being situated within the peritoneum. Can be used to describe organs that are lined by visceral peritoneum (e.g., stomach, spleen, liver) and route of delivery of medications (e.g., intraperitoneal antibiotics to treat peritonitis).

YOcnIc0.title: Primary bone healing
YOcnIc0.description: A type of bone healing that occurs when the broken ends of the bone are < 1 mm apart. Involves formation of lamellar bone directly in the fracture gap (gap healing).

destinations.label: Bone tissue → Bone remodeling and healing

bOcHIc0.title: Secondary bone healing
bOcHIc0.description: A type of bone healing that occurs when the broken ends of a bone are > 1 mm apart. Involves initial bridging of the fracture by connective tissue or cartilage (fibrocartilage callus), conversion to woven bone (bony callus) by endochondral ossification, and remodeling into resilient lamellar bone.

destinations.label: Bone tissue → Bone remodeling and healing

XOc9Ic0.title: Nuchal rigidity
XOc9Ic0.description: An inability to flex the neck due to rigidity of the neck muscles. Can be elicited with either passive or active flexion. Associated with meningitis.

cOcarc0.title: Cryptococcus
cOcarc0.description: A genus of fungi that can cause meningoencephalitis and pneumonia, particularly in patients who are immunocompromised. Species include C. neoformans and C. gattii.

1Oc2rc0.title: Latex agglutination test
1Oc2rc0.description: A test used to evaluate for an antibody immune response to a specific antigen. Latex beads coated with antigen agglutinate in the presence of antigen-specific antibody.

WOcPrc0.title: Tachyzoite
WOcPrc0.description: A cellular stage of Toxoplasma gondii that actively replicates and can spread throughout the body in the blood stream. Converts to a bradyzoite at a later stage.

dOcorc0.title: Leukocidin
dOcorc0.description: A virulence factor of certain bacteria (e.g., S. aureus). Creates pores in cell membranes, which results in necrotic mucocutaneous lesions.

VOcGrc0.title: Dextran
VOcGrc0.description:
1. A synthetic colloid of glucose polymers most commonly used as a volume expander in hypovolemia, which also has antithrombotic properties.
2. A virulence factor produced by S. sanguinis. Facilitates binding to fibrin-platelet aggregates on damaged heart valves.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

eOcxrc0.title: Anterior humeral circumflex artery
eOcxrc0.description: A branch of the third part of the axillary artery that supplies the glenohumeral joint and the surrounding muscles. It circles anteriorly around the surgical neck of the humerus and ends in an anastomosis with the posterior humeral circumflex artery lateral to the humerus.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage
Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

UOcb7c0.title: Magical thinking
UOcb7c0.description: The invention of causal relationships between behaviors and events that is inconsistent with an individual's cultural norms (e.g., believing that thoughts are able to control reality).

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Common developmental behaviors

2OcT7c0.title: Posterior humeral circumflex artery
2OcT7c0.description: A branch of the third part of the axillary artery that supplies the glenohumeral joint and the surrounding muscles. It passes through the quadrangular space of the axilla, circles posteriorly around the surgical neck of the humerus, and ends in an anastomosis with the anterior humeral circumflex artery lateral to the humerus.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries
Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage

fOck7c0.title: Valbenazine
fOck7c0.description: A drug used to treat tardive dyskinesia. Its mechanism of action is unclear but thought to involve reversible inhibition of vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2), which results in depletion of catecholamines.

TOc67c0.title: Neonatal meningitis-causing Escherichia coli
TOc67c0.description: A serotype of E. coli that causes meningitis in neonates. Produces the virulence factor K1 capsular polysaccharide, which protects the bacterium from phagocytosis.

SOcy7c0.title: Healthcare-associated pneumonia
SOcy7c0.description: A type of pneumonia that is acquired in health care facilities, including nursing homes, hemodialysis centers, and outpatient clinics. Formerly considered synonymous with hospital-acquired pneumonia.

hOccHc0.title: Dependent position
hOccHc0.description: A body position that facilitates gravity-dependent redistribution of nutrients or fluids (e.g., a supine position that results in improved oxygen and blood flow delivery to the posterior segments of the lung, or prolonged standing that results in lower limb edema formation). Can be used in the clinical setting for the diagnosis or management of different conditions (e.g., passive leg elevation in shock can increase venous blood return to the heart).

iOcJHc0.title: Rickettsia typhi
iOcJHc0.description: A small, gram-negative, obligate intracellular coccobacillus that causes endemic typhus. Transmitted via flea bites.

jOc_Hc0.title: Mycobacterium marinum
jOc_Hc0.description: A nonmotile, aerobic, gram-positive, acid-fast bacillus with a rich lipid cell wall. Causes aquarium granuloma.

POcWsc0.title: Fish tank granuloma
POcWsc0.description: A dermal granulomatous infection of the hands caused by Mycobacterium marinum. Associated with exposure to aquatic environments and/or marine animals.

OOcIsc0.title: Borrelia recurrentis
OOcIsc0.description: A spirochete that causes louse-borne relapsing fever. Its vector is Pediculus humanus corporis (body louse).

lOcvsc0.title: Descent of gonads
lOcvsc0.description: A caudal change in the anatomic position of male and female gonads during the antenatal development of the reproductive system.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Descent of gonads

mOcVGc0.title: Ocular clonus
mOcVGc0.description: A physical examination finding characterized by slow, continuous, horizontal eye movements. Associated with serotonin syndrome.

LOcwGc0.title: Megalomania
LOcwGc0.description: A delusion in which a person believes they possess extreme greatness or omnipotence.

oOc0tc0.title: Hallucinogen persisting perception disorder
oOc0tc0.description: The spontaneous recurrence of acute hallucinogen intoxication due to reabsorption of the intoxicating substance from bodily stores (e.g., fat). Manifestations include visual hallucinations, depressive symptoms, and panic. Can occur episodically or continuously and develop weeks after the initial intoxication.

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Hallucinogen-related disorders

KOcUtc0.title: Anakinra
KOcUtc0.description: An interleukin-1 (IL-1) receptor antagonist used as an immunosuppressive agent to treat conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis and neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease (NOMID).

6Ocjtc0.title: Epidemic typhus
6Ocjtc0.description: An infectious disease caused by Rickettsia prowazekii and transmitted via the body louse. Manifestations include fever, severe headache, malaise, myalgia, abdominal pain, nausea, and a maculopapular or petechial rash 4-5 days after fever onset.

JOcstc0.title: Epithalamus
JOcstc0.description: The most caudal part of the diencephalon, located above the thalamus. Consists of the habenular nuclei, habenular commissure, stria medullaris, and pineal gland. Involve in control of the sleep-wake cycle and stress response.

qOcCtc0.title: Subthalamus
qOcCtc0.description: A part of the diencephalon, located inferior to the thalamus. Contains the subthalamic nucleus, which is involved in the basal ganglia indirect pathway.

IOcYFc0.title: Ribulose-5-phosphate
IOcYFc0.description: An end product of the oxidative (irreversible) phase of the pentose phosphate pathway.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Pentose phosphate pathway

rOcfFc0.title: 6-phosphogluconolactone
rOcfFc0.description: An intermediate in the oxidative (irreversible) phase of the pentose phosphate pathway. Conversion of glucose-6-phosphate to 6-phosphogluconolactone is catalyzed by glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase.

destinations.label: Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis → Pentose phosphate pathway

7Oc4Fc0.title: Weil-Felix test
7Oc4Fc0.description: A diagnostic test for rickettsial infections, whereby suspensions of Proteus antigens (OX 19, OX 2, or OX K) are mixed with a patient's serum. Agglutination occurs in the serum of patients acutely infected with Rickettsia.

sOctFc0.title: Corpora arenacea
sOctFc0.description: A collection of calcified inclusions found in the pineal gland and choroid plexuses. Can be seen on neuroimaging and used as radiologic landmarks.

GOcBFc0.title: Mesothelium
GOcBFc0.description: The squamous epithelium that lines the surface of body structures derived from mesoderm (e.g., the peritoneal, pleural, and pericardial cavities).

tOcX8c0.title: Antinociceptive system
tOcX8c0.description: A complex of nervous system structures involved in the inhibition of pain transmission pathways.

FOcg8c0.title: Mucosa (gastrointestinal tract)
FOcg8c0.description: The innermost layer of the gastrointestinal tract. Consists of an epithelial lining with glandular tissue, the lamina propria, and the muscularis mucosa.

8OcO8c0.title: Serosa (gastrointestinal tract)
8OcO8c0.description: The outermost layer of the portions of the gastrointestinal tract that are contained within the abdominal cavity (e.g., small intestine, transverse colon). Consists of connective tissue that contains blood vessels, lymphatics, and fat. Covered by a simple squamous epithelium (mesothelium). Continuous with the mesenteries and the peritoneum.

media.title: Histological layers of the gastrointestinal tract

uOcp8c0.title: Adventitia (gastrointestinal tract)
uOcp8c0.description: The outermost layer of the portions of the gastrointestinal tract that are not contained within the abdominal cavity (e.g., esophagus, ascending colon, descending colon). Consists of connective tissue that contains blood vessels, lymphatics, and fat. Compared to the serosa, the adventitia is thicker and is not covered by mesothelium.

media.title: Histological layers of the gastrointestinal tract

EOc88c0.title: Epithelium of the gastrointestinal tract
EOc88c0.description: The innermost layer of the mucosal layer of the gastrointestinal tract. Consists of a protective layer of simple columnar cells.

vOcA8c0.title: Submucosa (gastrointestinal tract)
vOcA8c0.description: A layer of connective tissue that contains blood vessels, lymphatics, nerves, and glands that supports the overlying mucosa. Contains the Meissner plexus, provides parasympathetic innervation to glands, and is responsible for the secretomotor activity of the gastrointestinal tract.

wOchuc0.title: Endemic typhus
wOchuc0.description: An exanthematous typhus fever caused by Rickettsia typhi, which is transmitted by rat or cat fleas. Manifestations include fever, severe headache, malaise, myalgia, abdominal pain, nausea, and a maculopapular or petechial rash 7 days after fever onset.

BOczuc0.title: Subphrenic space
BOczuc0.description: A potential space between the liver and inferior surface of the diaphragm in the supracolic compartment of the greater sac. Divided into right and left portions by the falciform ligament.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

yOcdEc0.title: Paracolic gutters
yOcdEc0.description: The spaces between the abdominal wall and the colon.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

_Oc5Ec0.title: Recommended dietary allowance
_Oc5Ec0.description: The average daily intake that is sufficient to meet the nutrient requirements of over 97% of the healthy population.

Xlc9vc0.title: Mycobacterium scrofulaceum
Xlc9vc0.description: An acid-fast bacillus can cervical lymphadenitis in children (scrofula).

clcaDc0.title: Sacral plexus
clcaDc0.description: A group of nerves that originate from the anterior rami of L4 to S4 . Carries motor and sensory innervation to the lower limb and pelvis. Branches include the nerve to piriformis, the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve, and the pudendal nerve.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves
Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Innervation of the thigh

1lc2Dc0.title: Lumbar plexus
1lc2Dc0.description: A group of nerves that originate from the ventral rami of T12 to L5. Carries motor and sensory innervation to the lower limb and pelvis. Branches include the iliohypogastric nerve, femoral nerve, and obturator nerve.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves
Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Innervation of the thigh

WlcPDc0.title: Lipogenesis
WlcPDc0.description: The process by which acetyl-CoA and fatty acids are combined to form triglycerides.

dlcoDc0.title: Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase
dlcoDc0.description: An enzyme involved in folate metabolism that reduces N5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate to methyltetrahydrofolate. Mutations in the MTHFR gene can result in increased serum concentrations of homocysteine and homocystinuria.

VlcGDc0.title: Adenosine deaminase deficiency
VlcGDc0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder characterized by the impaired metabolism of deoxyadenosine during DNA breakdown. Deoxyadenosine accumulation results in lymphocyte toxicity and severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Purine salvage deficiencies

glcFwc0.title: Diffuse-type gastric cancer
glcFwc0.description: A type of gastric cancer that, in contrast to intestinal-type gastric cancer, is poorly differentiated and more likely to invade the gastric wall and metastasize. Can result in thickening of the stomach wall (linitis plastica). Histopathologic examination shows scattered signet-ring cells without gland formation. Associated with several factors, including, smoking, alcohol consumption, H. pylori infection, and diets that are high in nitrates and salt. Can be caused by a hereditary syndrome (hereditary diffuse gastric cancer).

Slcywc0.title: Intestinal-type gastric cancer
Slcywc0.description: A type of gastric cancer that, in contrast to diffuse-type gastric cancer, is more well-differentiated and less aggressive. Associated with several factors, including, smoking, alcohol consumption, H. pylori infection, and diets that are high in nitrates and salt.

hlcc9c0.title: Anarthria
hlcc9c0.description: A severe form of dysarthria characterized by the inability to articulate words (speechlessness) due to impaired neuromuscular control of the muscles used for speech. Language and cognition are usually preserved.

Rlcl9c0.title: Trifluoperazine
Rlcl9c0.description: A first-generation antipsychotic primarily used to treat schizophrenia. Adverse effects include blurred vision, extrapyramidal symptoms, and muscular weakness.

4lc3Cc0.title: Paliperidone
4lc3Cc0.description: An atypical antipsychotic drug used primarily to treat schizophrenia. Adverse effects include weight gain, extrapyramidal syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, and orthostatic hypotension.

klcmCc0.title: Unexpandable lung
klcmCc0.description: A condition in which the lung is unable to re-expand after fluid removal (e.g., thoracentesis) due to the presence of fibrotic lung tissue.

OlcICc0.title: Short bowel syndrome
OlcICc0.description: A syndrome of malnutrition caused by significant surgical resection of the small intestine. Results in the inability to absorb the necessary macronutrients, water, and electrolytes needed to maintain homeostasis despite adequate nutritional intake.

Nlc-Cc0.title: Polyploidy
Nlc-Cc0.description: A state in which cells have more than two paired sets of chromosomes.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

5lcixc0.title: Proximal deep inguinal lymph node
5lcixc0.description: A proximal deep inguinal lymph node that is located inferior to the inguinal ligament. Historically, the node was used as an indicator of pelvic metastasis in melanoma of the lower extremities, but evidence suggests that it has little predictive value.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

MlcMxc0.title: Amine precursor uptake and decarboxylation cells
MlcMxc0.description: A group of endocrine cells that secrete peptide hormones (e.g., secretin, cholecystokinin). These cells take up amine precursors (e.g., 5-hydroxytryptophan) and decarboxylate them to form amines. Mutation of these cells can lead to neuroendocrine tumors.

nlc7xc0.title: Left renal vein compression
nlc7xc0.description: A condition characterized by compression of the left renal vein between the aorta and proximal superior mesenteric artery. Manifestations include hematuria and left flank plain.

olc0Bc0.title: Familial amyloid polyneuropathy
olc0Bc0.description: An autosomal dominant form of hereditary amyloidosis caused by mutated transthyretin protein (ATTR). Typically affects the peripheral and autonomic nerves.

KlcUBc0.title: Coffee bean sign
KlcUBc0.description: A radiographic finding of sigmoid volvulus characterized by the appearance of a dilated loop of twisted bowel that resembled a coffee bean or kidney bean.

destinations.label: Sigmoid volvulus and cecal volvulus → Diagnosis

IlcYyc0.title: Woltman sign
IlcYyc0.description: A delayed relaxation of the deep tendon reflexes commonly seen in patients with hypothyroidism. Also associated with advanced age, pregnancy, and diabetes mellitus.

rlcfyc0.title: Howship-Romberg sign
rlcfyc0.description: A clinical finding of pain and paresthesia over the inner aspect of the thigh caused by compression of the obturator nerve.

destinations.label: Peripheral nerve injuries → Nerve injuries in the lower body

7lc4yc0.title: Sternal dehiscence
7lc4yc0.description: A potentially life-threatening postoperative complication of median sternotomy characterized by separation of the edges of the sternum. Can lead to wound infection (i.e., mediastinitis) and hemorrhage from puncture of surrounding organs and vessels.

HlcKyc0.title: Multidrug resistance-associated protein 2
HlcKyc0.description: A transporter that moves nonbile acid organic anions (e.g., conjugated bilirubin) from hepatocytes into bile canaliculi. Defects in this transporter can cause Dubin-Johnson syndrome.

FlcgAc0.title: Chronic meningitis
FlcgAc0.description: A type of meningitis that lasts for ≥ 4 weeks. Typically manifests with subacute-onset fever, headache, and vomiting. Etiologies include inflammatory conditions, infections, and malignancies.

ulcpAc0.title: CCR7
ulcpAc0.description: A chemokine receptor that is involved in T cell and B cell activation, dendtric cell differentiation, and memory T cell migration to secondary lymphoid tissue.

vlcAAc0.title: Nymph
vlcAAc0.description: An immature form of some arthropods, including ticks and lice, that undergoes multiple developmental stages to reach the adult state. Nymphs typically resemble the adult form but are smaller in size.

Dlc1_c0.title: Nit
Dlc1_c0.description: The egg of a louse. Laid by adult female lice on the base of human hair shafts, where they typically remain firmly attached and hatch after 8-9 days.

xlcE_c0.title: Burkholderia
xlcE_c0.description: A genus of gram-negative bacilli that includes B. cepacia (which causes pneumonia in patients with cystic fibrosis) and B. pseudomallei (which causes melioidosis).

Blcz_c0.title: Hypogammaglobulinemia
Blcz_c0.description: A decrease in the serum concentration of immunoglobulins. Etiologies include nephrotic syndrome, drug-induced reactions, acquired humoral immunodeficiencies, and congenital immunodeficiencies.

ylcdzc0.title: Woodruff plexus
ylcdzc0.description: A collection of arteries located in the posterior portion of the inferior nasal meatus. Thought to be a site of bleeding for posterior epistaxis.

AlcRzc0.title: Bronchioloalveolar carcinoma
AlcRzc0.description: An obsolete term for well-differentiated, noninvasive adenocarcinomas that grow along the alveolar septa. Adenocarcinomas of the lung are now described on a spectrum of lepidic growth and include adenocarcinoma in situ, minimally-invasive adenocarcinoma, invasive lepidic-predominant adenocarcinoma, and invasive, mucinous-predominant adenocarcinoma.

_lc5zc0.title: TIMI score
_lc5zc0.description: A risk score for patients with unstable angina or NSTEMI that functions as a prognostic tool to calculate a patient's risk of death and ischemic events. Can also be used to guide the therapeutic regimen.

zlcrzc0.title: Jugular vein suppurative thrombophlebitis
zlcrzc0.description: A severe, potentially fatal condition usually resulting from oropharyngeal infections. Characterized by infection of the carotid sheath vessels and bacteremia. Manifestations include fever, respiratory distress, neck pain, and throat pain. Most commonly caused by oropharyngeal flora (e.g., Fusobacterium necrophorum).

-lcDzc0.title: Saddle anesthesia
-lcDzc0.description: A condition of anesthesia or paresthesia that involves the S2-S5 dermatomes, which affects the area around the anus, genitalia, and inner thighs. Typically occurs in association with cauda equina syndrome.

YNcn-c0.title: Andexanet alfa
YNcn-c0.description: A modified, inactive form of human factor Xa that binds to factor Xa inhibitors, such as rivaroxaban and apixaban, to reverse their anticoagulant effects (e.g., in patients who have life-threatening or uncontrolled bleeding). Also inhibits tissue factor pathway inhibitor to increase thrombin generation.

cNcaZ10.title: Auramine-rhodamine stain
cNcaZ10.description: A method of bacterial staining used to visualize acid-fast bacilli (e.g., Mycobacteria). Binds to mycolic acid present in the cell wall, which results in reddish-yellow fluorescence.

1Nc2Z10.title: Wild-type allele
1Nc2Z10.description: An allele that encodes the most common phenotype in a given population.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

WNcPZ10.title: Candida skin test
WNcPZ10.description: A diagnostic test in which Candida albicans antigen is injected intradermally to the arm. The injection site is examined 48 hours later. Induration ≥5 mm in diameter is considered a positive reaction and indicates prior exposure to antigen and an intact immune response mediated by T cells.

VNcGZ10.title: Ku70 protein
VNcGZ10.description: A eukaryotic protein that, with Ku80, forms the Ku heterodimer to crop broken DNA strands in preparation for nonhomologous end joining.

eNcxZ10.title: Ku80 protein
eNcxZ10.description: A eukaryotic protein that, with Ku70, forms the Ku heterodimer to crop broken DNA strands in preparation for nonhomologous end joining.

UNcb010.title: Vitamin C toxicity
UNcb010.description: A syndrome caused by excess vitamin C (ascorbic acid). Manifestations include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, bloating, fatigue, and nephrolithiasis (due to increased formation of calcium oxalate). Also increases the risk of developing iron toxicity in vulnerable patients (e.g., patients who receive frequent transfusions).

2NcT010.title: Corneal limbus
2NcT010.description: The border between the cornea and the sclera of the eye.

fNck010.title: Perilimbal
fNck010.description: An anatomical descriptor for the region near the border between the cornea and the sclera of the eye.

TNc6010.title: Diloxanide
TNc6010.description: An antiprotozoal drug that is used to eradicate intestinal cysts from Entamoeba histolytica infection. Not currently approved for use in the United States.

gNcF010.title: Edaravone
gNcF010.description: A free radical scavenger that has been shown to slow functional decline in some patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

3NcSa10.title: Riboflavin deficiency
3NcSa10.description: A deficiency of riboflavin (vitamin B2). Vitamin B2 is a precursor for flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD), which serves as a redox cofactor for various enzymes, including glutathione reductase. Manifestations of riboflavin deficiency include cheilitis, glossitis, stomatitis, and anemia. Can occur due to starvation or malabsorptive syndromes.

iNcJa10.title: Pyridoxine deficiency
iNcJa10.description: A nutritional deficiency characterized by cheilitis, glossitis, stomatitis, sideroblastic anemia, and neurologic manifestations (e.g., seizures, peripheral neuropathy).

PNcWY10.title: Persistent truncus arteriosus
PNcWY10.description: A congenital heart defect caused by failed separation of the aorta and pulmonary artery during development. Characterized by a single trunk that receives output from both ventricles. Results in cyanosis, respiratory distress, and heart failure within the first few weeks of life.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Persistent truncus arteriosus

lNcvY10.title: Sodium sulfacetamide
lNcvY10.description: An antimicrobial agent that inhibits bacterial folic acid synthesis. Used to treat ocular infections, cutaneous infections, and rosacea.

NNc-Y10.title: Azelaic acid
NNc-Y10.description: A drug used to treat acne vulgaris and rosacea. Its mechanism of action is unclear but may include antimicrobial properties and inhibition of microcomedo formation.

mNcVb10.title: Oxymetazoline
mNcVb10.description: A selective α1 adrenergic agonist and α2 adrenergic receptor partial agonist. Induces vasoconstriction and is used to treat eye redness, epistaxis, nasal congestion, and rosacea-associated erythema.

5Ncib10.title: Spindle apparatus
5Ncib10.description: A structure composed of multiple cytoskeletal proteins that forms perpendicular to the axis of cell division to condense chromosomes and facilitate chromosomal separation during mitotic or meiotic cell division.

KNcUX10.title: Ovarian vein
KNcUX10.description: A vein that drains one of the ovaries. The right ovarian vein empties into the inferior vena cava. The left ovarian vein empties into the left renal vein.

rNcfc10.title: Zona pellucida
rNcfc10.description: A specialized extracellular matrix produced by oocyte and follicle granulosa cells. Surrounds the oocyte and facilitates the acrosomal reaction and fusion of oocyte and spermatocyte.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Oogenesis and folliculogenesis

GNcBc10.title: Labia majora
GNcBc10.description: The folds of skin that surround and cover the vaginal ostium and the labia minora.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Vagina and vulva

8NcO110.title: Labia minora
8NcO110.description: The folds of hairless skin that surround the vaginal vestibule.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Vagina and vulva

9NcNW10.title: Circumvallate papillae
9NcNW10.description: A series of structures located on the posterior aspect of the tongue that contain lingual taste buds.

_Nc5d10.title: Hyperploid
_Nc5d10.description: A descriptor for having greater than the normal number of chromosomes in a cell.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

zNcrd10.title: Hypoploidy
zNcrd10.description: A descriptor for having fewer than the normal number of chromosomes in a cell.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

-NcDd10.title: Mycetoma
-NcDd10.description: A chronic infection of the skin and soft tissue that typically affects the lower extremities. Most cases occur in tropical and subtropical areas. Often caused by fungal species, including Madurella mycetomatis and Trematosphaeria grisea or bacteria of the order actinomycetes.

ZmcZV10.title: Tocilizumab
ZmcZV10.description: A monoclonal antibody IL-6 receptor antagonist. Reduces cytokine and acute phase reactant production. Used in the treatment of giant cell arteritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and rheumatoid arthritis. Approved for emergency use in conjunction with corticosteroids for the management of hospitalized patients with severe COVID-19.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

YmcnV10.title: Lymphangioma
YmcnV10.description: A malformation of the lymphatic system composed of endothelium-lined cysts that contain lymphatic fluid. Most commonly manifests as a cluster of clear and/or hemorrhagic vesicles on the skin.

bmcHV10.title: Affinity chromatography
bmcHV10.description: A laboratory method that is used to separate specific substances from a mixture using molecules that have high specificity for a given target. Examples of ligands and target molecules that can be used in this technique include antigens and antibodies, enzymes and substrates, and proteins and nucleic acids.

Xmc9V10.title: Liquid chromatography
Xmc9V10.description: A laboratory method that is used to separate a mixture into individual components. The mixture is dissolved in a liquid (the mobile phase) and filtered through a solid structure (the stationary phase).

cmcae10.title: Motor impersistence
cmcae10.description: The inability to sustain certain postures or positions, such as eye closure, mouth opening, and tongue protrusion. Associated with diffuse cerebral disease and right-hemisphere lesions. Its underlying pathomechanism is unclear but may be related to disorders of directed attention.

WmcPe10.title: T-cell acute lymphocytic leukemia
WmcPe10.description: A subtype of acute lymphocytic leukemia that originates from T cells and accounts for ~ 15–20% of cases. Further subdivided into early (pro-T) ALL, intermediate-T ALL, and mature T-cell ALL.

VmcGe10.title: Vitamin E deficiency
VmcGe10.description: A rare vitamin deficiency that can manifest with progressive spinocerebellar degeneration and peripheral neuropathy, sometimes accompanied by hemolytic anemia and retinitis pigmentosa. Etiologies include severe malnutrition and malabsorption syndromes (e.g. short bowel, cholestatic liver disease, cystic fibrosis).

UmcbU10.title: Vitamin B3 toxicity
UmcbU10.description: A syndrome caused by excess vitamin B3 (niacin). Characterized by facial flushing (caused by prostaglandin release), hyperuricemia, and hyperglycemia.

2mcTU10.title: Granulomatous inflammation
2mcTU10.description: A distinct type of chronic inflammation that is characterized by the formation of granulomas in the affected tissue, which wall off a stimulus (e.g., pathogen, foreign body) without completely degrading or eradicating it. Granulomatous diseases include certain bacterial infections (e.g., Mycobacteria, Bartonella, Listeria), fungal infections (e.g., histoplasmosis), and autoinflammatory diseases (e.g. Crohn disease, sarcoidosis).

gmcFU10.title: Internal laryngeal nerve
gmcFU10.description: The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve, which supplies sensory innervation of the larynx up to the vocal folds, the epiglottis, and the base of the tongue.

SmcyU10.title: Transudative effusion
SmcyU10.description: A collection of fluid that is low in proteins and cells that has permeated into the pleural space. Causes include increased capillary hydrostatic pressure and/or decreased capillary oncotic pressure (e.g., due to lack of albumin).  Defined by Light's criteria; the fluid is characterized by a low protein count and specific gravity and normal glucose levels.

hmcc210.title: Exudative pleural effusions
hmcc210.description: A collection of fluid that is high in proteins and cells that has permeated into the pleural space due to increased vascular permeability. Analysis of the fluid reveals a cellular (cloudy) fluid with high protein and low glucose concentration. Pleural exudate is most likely to occur secondary to a bacterial infection, lymphatic obstruction, or malignancy.

jmc_210.title: Vilazodone
jmc_210.description: A selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor and 5-HT1A receptor partial agonist. Used to treat major depressive disorder in adults. Adverse effects include diarrhea, nausea and vomiting, and insomnia

PmcWf10.title: Vortioxetine
PmcWf10.description: A serotonin modulator and stimulator used to treat major depressive disorder. Adverse effects include nausea, constipation, and vomiting.

OmcIf10.title: Amoxapine
OmcIf10.description: A tricyclic antidepressant with additional antipsychotic properties. Used primarily in the treatment of depression with prominent anxiety, agitation, and/or psychotic features. Adverse effects include drowsiness, dry mouth, and constipation.

lmcvf10.title: Tricyclic antidepressant overdose
lmcvf10.description: Features include anticholinergic effects (e.g., flushed and dry skin, thirst, hyperthermia, mydriasis), cardiotoxic effects due to inhibition of cardiac fast sodium channels (e.g., prolonged QTc, ventricular arrhythmias), and neurotoxicity due to GABA-A inhibition (e.g, convulsions, coma).

destinations.label: Psychiatric drug poisoning → Tricyclic antidepressant overdose

media.title: ECG abnormalities in tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) toxicity

5mciT10.title: Small bowel obstruction
5mciT10.description: An interruption in the normal passage of contents of the small bowel due to a structural barrier. Most commonly caused by adhesions (e.g., from prior abdominal surgery) and incarcerated hernias. Manifestations include colicky abdominal pain, constipation, abdominal distention, and early-onset vomiting.

MmcMT10.title: Large bowel obstruction
MmcMT10.description: An interruption in the normal passage of contents of the large bowel due to a structural barrier. Most commonly caused by malignant tumors (e.g., colorectal carcinoma). Manifestations include colicky abdominal pain, constipation, abdominal distention, and late-onset vomiting.

nmc7T10.title: Nelfinavir
nmc7T10.description: A protease inhibitor used as part of an antiretroviral regimen for the treatment of HIV. Inhibits the cleavage of viral Gag-Pol polyprotein precursors. Common adverse effects include insulin resistance, hyperglycemia, diarrhea, and lipodystrophy.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

LmcwT10.title: Lopinavir
LmcwT10.description: A protease inhibitor used as part of an antiretroviral regimen for the treatment of HIV. Inhibits the cleavage of viral Gag-Pol polyprotein precursors. Typically used in combination with ritonavir, which inhibits the breakdown of lopinavir. Common adverse effects include gastrointestinal distress, headaches, muscle pain, and fatigue.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

omc0g10.title: CCR5 receptor antagonist
omc0g10.description: A drug that blocks the CCR5 coreceptor on the surface of CD4+ cells, which prevents interaction with viral gp120 and thus inhibits viral entry into cells. Maraviroc is an agent in this class.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

tmcXh10.title: Endothelium-derived relaxing factor
tmcXh10.description: A substance produced and released by the endothelium that mediates relaxation of smooth muscle via the activation of guanylate cyclase. Also inhibits platelet activity. Nitric oxide is a type of EDRF.

Emc8h10.title: Superficial thrombophlebitis
Emc8h10.description: A condition of inflammation and thrombosis of a superficial vein. Manifestations include pain, tenderness, induration, and erythema overlying a superficial vein, often with a palpable cord.

wmch310.title: Neoadjuvant therapy
wmch310.description: A first-step therapy that is provided before the main treatment. For example, chemotherapy that is administered before surgery to shrink the tumor.

destinations.label: Principles of cancer care → Overview of cancer care

xmcE310.title: Interventricular foramen (heart)
xmcE310.description: An opening between the two ventricles of the heart that arises temporarily during cardiac morphogenesis.

_mc5R10.title: Cold urticaria
_mc5R10.description: A subtype of physical urticaria characterized by the formation of hives and/or angioedema within minutes after exposure to cold temperatures. Typically idiopathic but can be associated with infection or hematologic disorders.

destinations.label: Hypothermia and frostbite → Nonfreezing cold injuries

05cei10.title: Chapman reflex point
05cei10.description: An osteopathic term that refers to nerve gangliform contractions located deep to the skin and subcutaneous tissue that can be felt as small, discrete, and smooth palpable nodules ~ 2 mm in diameter. Pain at any of these neurolymphatic points corresponds to specific visceral dysfunctions throughout the body. Although these points are typically diagnostic, they may also be used as a therapeutic modality.

a5cQi10.title: Mepolizumab
a5cQi10.description: A humanized monoclonal antibody against IL-5 used for the management of severe eosinophilic asthma. Common adverse effects include injection reactions, headache, and back pain.

25cTj10.title: Neonatal lupus syndrome
25cTj10.description: A congenital immune condition caused by the placental transfer of maternal anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies.  Manifestations include cardiac findings (e.g., heart block), cutaneous findings (e.g., photosensitivity, periorbital rash), hepatic abnormalities (e.g., hepatosplenomegaly, cholestasis), and hematologic abnormalities (e.g., anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia).

destinations.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus → Special patient groups

f5ckj10.title: Invariant chain
f5ckj10.description: A polypeptide involved in the formation of the peptide-binding groove of MHC class II molecules. Also involved in subsequent export of MHC class II molecules from the endoplasmic reticulum.

T5c6j10.title: Aconitase
T5c6j10.description: A mitochondrial enzyme involved in the Krebs cycle that catalyzes the stereo-specific isomerization of citrate to isocitrate.

g5cFj10.title: Fumarase
g5cFj10.description: A mitochondrial enzyme involved in the Krebs cycle that catalyzes the reversible hydration and dehydration of fumarate to malate.

R5clP10.title: J wave
R5clP10.description: A positive waveform seen on ECG at the junction between the end of the QRS complex and the beginning of the ST segment. Etiologies include hypothermia, hypercalcemia, and Brugada syndrome.

j5c_P10.title: Leukapheresis
j5c_P10.description: A process in which white blood cells are separated from the rest of the blood. Can be used to isolate and store white blood cells for autologous transplantation after chemotherapy. Also used in the management of leukostasis and hyperleukocytosis to reduce the leukocyte count (e.g., in the setting of acute myeloid leukemia).

P5cW410.title: Midgut volvulus
P5cW410.description: A life-threatening condition most commonly seen in neonates and infants in which the small intestine twists around the superior mesenteric artery, often due to intestinal malrotation. Midgut volvulus can result in intestinal obstruction and compromised blood flow, which can lead to bowel ischemia and necrosis if left untreated.

destinations.label: Intestinal malrotation, midgut volvulus, and gastric volvulus → Midgut volvulus

O5cI410.title: Nocturnal penile tumescence
