O5cI410.description: A test used to differentiate psychogenic from organic erectile dysfunction. An apparatus detects if a man achieves an erection while sleeping. If an erection is detected, this suggests that the etiology of the man's erectile dysfunction is psychogenic rather than organic.

destinations.label: Male reproductive organs → Male sexual response

m5cVk10.title: Epididymis
m5cVk10.description: An elongated, cordlike structure on the posterior surface of the testis. Connects the testis with the ductus (vas) deferens. The coiled portion of the epididymis facilitates storage, transport, and maturation of spermatozoa.

destinations.label: Male reproductive organs → Epididymis, ductus deferens, and accessory glands

55cik10.title: Obstructed hernia
55cik10.description: A type of hernia in which the lumen of the intestine within the hernial sac has become completely obstructed.

M5cMk10.title: Ehrlichia
M5cMk10.description: A genus of intracellular, gram-negative bacteria that causes ehrlichiosis. Typically transmitted via ticks (e.g., Amblyomma americanum).

media.title: Ehrlichia canis morulae in a monocyte

n5c7k10.title: Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis
n5c7k10.description: A rare condition characterized by inflammation and thrombosis of the pelvic veins. Most often occurs in the postpartum period (within 1 week after delivery). Most commonly affects the right ovarian vein. Risk factors include Cesarean deliveries, infections, and abortion. Manifestations include fever, abdominal pain, and tenderness on the affected side; a palpable cord may be present.

L5cwk10.title: Merozoite
L5cwk10.description: The motile and infective stage of a sporozoan parasite. Capable of initiating a new life cycle of development.

o5c0O10.title: Anaplasma
o5c0O10.description: A genus of intracellular, gram-negative bacteria that causes anaplasmosis. Typically transmitted via ticks (e.g., Ixodes scapularis, Ixodes pacificus).

K5cUO10.title: Seated flexion test
K5cUO10.description: An osteopathic screening test used to assess for sacroiliac joint dysfunction. With the patient sitting upright, the physician places a thumb on each of the posterior superior iliac spines and the patient then slowly bends forward. The test is negative if the thumbs move symmetrically in a superior direction and positive if one thumb moves more superiorly than the other, indicating a sacroiliac joint dysfunction on that side.

destinations.label: Pelvic and sacral osteopathy → Diagnostic tests

65cjO10.title: Standing flexion test
65cjO10.description: An osteopathic screening test that assesses for sacroiliac joint dysfunction. The patient stands erect with their feet shoulder-width apart. The physician places a thumb on each of the posterior superior iliac spines. The patient bends forward without flexing their knees. The test is negative if the thumbs move symmetrically in a superior direction. The test is positive if one thumb moves more superiorly than the other, indicating a sacroiliac joint dysfunction on that side.

destinations.label: Pelvic and sacral osteopathy → Diagnostic tests

p5cLO10.title: Sphinx test
p5cLO10.description: An osteopathic procedure that helps distinguish physiologic from nonphysiologic dysfunctions of the sacrum.

destinations.label: Pelvic and sacral osteopathy → Diagnostic tests

J5csO10.title: Ober test
J5csO10.description: A physical examination procedure that helps evaluate for iliotibial band and/or tensor fascia lata tightness.

destinations.label: Pelvic and sacral osteopathy → Special tests

I5cYl10.title: Wallenberg test
I5cYl10.description: A physical examination procedure used to evaluate for vertebrobasilar insufficiency.

r5cfl10.title: Cisapride
r5cfl10.description: A drug used to treat various gastrointestinal conditions, including gastroparesis, constipation, dyspepsia, and nocturnal symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux disease. Increases acetylcholine release at the myenteric plexus.

H5cKl10.title: ASIS compression test
H5cKl10.description: An osteopathic screening test to assess for sacroiliac joint dysfunctions. With the patient lying supine on the examination table, the physician applies anterior-to-posterior pressure to each anterior superior iliac spine while stabilizing the other, causing compression of the sacroiliac joint. The test is positive on the side that demonstrates resistance to compression, indicating an ipsilateral sacroiliac joint dysfunction.

destinations.label: Pelvic and sacral osteopathy → Diagnostic tests

s5ctl10.title: Spring test
s5ctl10.description: An osteopathic test used to differentiate between forward (flexion) and backward (extension) dysfunctions of the sacrum.

destinations.label: Pelvic and sacral osteopathy → Diagnostic tests

cMcan10.title: Still technique
cMcan10.description: A passive myofascial release technique that combines direct and indirect approaches and involves the application of an axial force while engaging the restrictive barrier. First, the dysfunctional region is brought to a neutral position by placing the patient in the direction of ease. Next, the physician applies an axial force (e.g., compression) and gently moves the region to engage the restrictive barrier.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Myofascial release techniques

1Mc2n10.title: Suboccipital soft tissue release technique
1Mc2n10.description: A soft tissue manipulation technique used to reduce tension in the fascia and musculature of the cervical spine, particularly in the suboccipital space.

eMcxn10.title: Streptococcal toxic shock-like syndrome
eMcxn10.description: A systemic inflammatory reaction caused by superantigens (streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxins) produced by Streptococcus pyogenes. Invasive Group A streptococcal infection (e.g., necrotizing fasciitis) is the most common risk factor for streptococcal TSS. Manifestations include fever, myalgia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, altered mental status, features of shock, and rarely, a desquamating rash.

kMcmK10.title: Watson test
kMcmK10.description: A clinical test used to assess for scapholunate ligament instability.

lMcvK10.title: Ballottement test
lMcvK10.description: A physical examination maneuver used to detect knee joint effusion. Considered positive if a free-floating patella is palpated when it is tapped while the knee joint is extended or flexed.

NMc-K10.title: Bulge sign
NMc-K10.description: A physical examination maneuver that assesses for excessive fluid in the suprapatellar pouch.

mMcV610.title: Kleiger test
mMcV610.description: A physical examination maneuver that evaluates for distal tibiofibular syndesmosis (i.e., high ankle sprain). Reproduction of pain in the area of the ankle syndesmosis with external rotation of the foot suggests a high ankle sprain.

5Mci610.title: Talar tilt test
5Mci610.description: An orthopedic examination maneuver where inversion and eversion stress is applied to assess for a sprain or rupture to the calcaneofibular ligament, anterior talofibular ligament, and deltoid ligament.

MMcM610.title: Squeeze test
MMcM610.description: A physical examination maneuver that assesses for tibiofibular syndesmosis (i.e., high ankle sprain)

nMc7610.title: Pneumaturia
nMc7610.description: The passage of air in the urine. Causes include colovesical fistulas and emphysematous urinary tract infections.

KMcUp10.title: Fecaluria
KMcUp10.description: The passage of fecal contents in the urine. Caused by fistula formation between the gastrointestinal and urinary tracts (e.g., due to Crohn disease, diverticulitis, or malignancy).

IMcYJ10.title: Leg length discrepancy
IMcYJ10.description: A difference in the lengths of the legs. Further classified as anatomical leg length discrepancy, in which there is a difference in leg bone lengths (e.g., due to congenital or acquired bone abnormalities), and functional leg length discrepancy, in which the leg bones are the same length but muscular abnormalities (e.g., due to contractures, compensation, muscular imbalances) result in the appearance of different leg lengths.

sMctJ10.title: First trimester
sMctJ10.description: The part of pregnancy between 0 and 13 weeks of gestation.

GMcBJ10.title: Second trimester
GMcBJ10.description: The part of pregnancy from 14 weeks through 27 weeks of gestation.

tMcXq10.title: Third trimester
tMcXq10.description: The part of pregnancy from 28 weeks through 40 weeks of gestation.

uMcpq10.title: Embryoblast
uMcpq10.description: The inner cell mass of the cleaving embryo (morula). Gives rise to the embryo proper and extraembryonic membranes.

EMc8q10.title: Organogenesis
EMc8q10.description: The process of organ formation from the germ layers during embryonic development. Occurs after gastrulation.

vMcAq10.title: Fetogenesis
vMcAq10.description: The process by which the fetus develops after the first eight weeks after fertilization (i.e., after the embryonic period). During this period, the organ systems continue to mature, and the fetus continues to grow.

DMc1I10.title: Linea nigra
DMc1I10.description: A darkening of the midline skin of the abdomen that can occur during pregnancy. Can extend from the xiphoid process to the pubic symphysis. Typically regresses postpartum. Thought to be caused by placental production of melanocyte-stimulating hormone.

destinations.label: Pregnancy → Clinical signs of early pregnancy

media.title: Linea nigra and polymorphic eruption of pregnancy

wMchI10.title: Hyperdiploid
wMchI10.description: A descriptor for having greater than the normal diploid number of chromosomes in a cell.

9McNI10.title: Inhalation rib dysfunction
9McNI10.description: A type of somatic dysfunction in which one or several ribs are held in inhalation, i.e., the ribs move cephalad during inspiration, but caudad motion is restricted during exhalation.

destinations.label: Thoracic spine and rib osteopathy → Rib dysfunctions

CMcqI10.title: Exhalation rib dysfunction
CMcqI10.description: A type of somatic dysfunction in which one or several ribs are held in exhalation, i.e., the ribs move caudad during exhalation, but cephalad motion is restricted during inhalation.

destinations.label: Thoracic spine and rib osteopathy → Rib dysfunctions

BMczI10.title: Urine osmolar gap
BMczI10.description: The difference between measured urine osmolality and calculated urine osmolality, where calculated urine osmolality  =  (2 × [Na + K]) + [BUN]/2.8 + [glucose]/18. Used to estimate urine NH4+ concentration in metabolic acidosis. Decreased UOG can be caused by impaired renal excretion (e.g., due to renal tubular acidosis); increased UOG can be seen as part of the appropriate renal response to acidemia

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

_Mc5r10.title: Uterine cycle
_Mc5r10.description: A part of the menstrual cycle that involves changes that occur in the uterine lining (i.e., the endometrium). Consists of three phases: menstruation (in which the functional layer of the endometrium sloughs off in the absence of pregnancy), a proliferative phase (in which endometrial cells and glands proliferate), and a secretory phase (in which the functional layer of the endometrium prepares for potential oocyte implantation).

-McDr10.title: Ovarian cycle
-McDr10.description: A part of the menstrual cycle that involves changes that occur in the ovaries. Consists of a follicular phase (in which FSH stimulates the development of ovarian follicles) and a luteal phase (in which an oocyte is released, and the corpus luteum develops).

ZncZ710.title: Ring-enhancing lesion
ZncZ710.description: A radiologic descriptor for a lesion that has a peripheral rim of increased radiodensity (due to concentration of an enhancing contrast dye)

VncGH10.title: Cortico-basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical loop
VncGH10.description: A neuronal circuit between the cortices of the brain, the basal ganglia, and the thalamus. Coordinates movement of skeletal muscle via a direct pathway and an indirect pathway.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

encxH10.title: Neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus
encxH10.description: The presence of neurological and psychiatric symptoms in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus that cannot be attributed to another condition. Possible manifestations include aseptic meningitis, headache, and mononeuropathies.

destinations.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus → Specific clinical manifestations

gncFs10.title: Ombitasvir
gncFs10.description: A non-nucleoside NS5A polymerase inhibitor used to treat chronic hepatitis C infection (genotypes 1a, 1b, and 4) in combination with paritaprevir and ritonavir. This treatment regimen can also include ribavirin and/or dasabuvir. Adverse effects include headache, fatigue, nausea, pruritus, skin reactions, insomnia, asthenia, hyperbilirubinemia, and hepatotoxicity.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

Sncys10.title: Dasabuvir
Sncys10.description: A non-nucleoside inhibitor of NS5B (non-structural protein 5B) used as an antiviral drug to treat chronic hepatitis C infection (genotype 1) in combination with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir, with or without ribavirin. Adverse effects include fatigue, insomnia, pruritus, asthenia, and nausea.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

hnccG10.title: Grazoprevir
hnccG10.description: A protease inhibitor used to treat chronic hepatitis C infection (genotype 1 or 4). Administered in combination with elbasvir, either with or without ribavirin. Adverse effects include fatigue, headache, anorexia, and nausea.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

incJG10.title: Solar elastosis
incJG10.description: An age-related cutaneous change characterized by the development of diffusely thickened and wrinkled skin, sometimes with yellow discoloration. Caused by the accumulation of damaged collagen and elastic tissue as a result of chronic sun exposure (photoaging).

4nc3t10.title: Augmentation of labor
4nc3t10.description: The process of stimulating uterine contractions (e.g., with oxytocin infusion) to result in delivery for patients with prolonged labor or inadequate contractions.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormal stages of labor

kncmt10.title: Marginal zone lymphoma
kncmt10.description: A subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that arises from postgerminal center marginal zone B cells. Stains positive for pan B-cell markers (e.g., CD19, CD20). A subtype is MALT lymphoma, which is associated with chronic H.pylori infection.

Nnc-t10.title: Alternating hemiplegia
Nnc-t10.description: A rare neurologic disorder of infancy. Manifestations include recurrent episodes of paralysis that affect different parts of the body, choreiform movements, and developmental delay. Typically caused by mutations in genes that regulate the activity of the Na+/K+ ATPase.

mncVF10.title: Greater petrosal nerve
mncVF10.description: A nerve that arises from the geniculate ganglion and contains preganglionic parasympathetic fibers. Also transmits taste sensation from the soft palate. Courses through the foramen lacerum of the temporal bone in the middle cranial fossa.

5nciF10.title: Myelitis
5nciF10.description: A condition of inflammation of the spinal cord. Etiologies include infection (e.g., poliomyelitis, osteomyelitis), and autoimmune conditions (e.g., transverse myelitis, acute disseminated encephalomyelitis).

media.title: Lytic lesion in long bone from subacute osteomyelitis

MncMF10.title: Galbreath technique
MncMF10.description: A lymphatic drainage technique, first described by Dr. William Otis Galbreath in 1929, that involves manipulation of the mandible. Often used to treat patients with eustachian tube dysfunction.

onc0810.title: Spencer technique
onc0810.description: An osteopathic articulatory technique of the glenohumeral joint that aims to improve shoulder range of motion. The Spencer technique consists of 7 steps that begin with the patient lying in the lateral recumbent position with the affected shoulder up. With the clavicle and scapula stabilized, the dysfunctional shoulder is taken through the following sequence: extension, flexion, circumduction with compression, circumduction with traction, abduction and adduction with external rotation, internal rotation, and traction.

6ncj810.title: Aortic valve sclerosis
6ncj810.description: An irregular thickening of the aortic leaflets seen in older adults. Caused by lipid accumulation, inflammation, and calcification. Can cause a systolic ejection murmur on auscultation. Severe sclerosis can result in aortic valve stenosis.

pncL810.title: Zink pattern
pncL810.description: An osteopathic postural model describing the alternating pattern of preferred directions of fascial rotation at four transitional areas of the spine: the occipitoatlantal junction rotated left, the cervicothoracic junction rotated right, the thoracolumbar junction rotated left, and the lumbosacral junction rotated right. Observed in approx. 80% of individuals without an underlying condition.

qncC810.title: Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy
qncC810.description: A procedure used to insert a gastric feeding tube. An endoscope is used to facilitate and guide the insertion of the tube through a small incision in the abdominal wall.

HncKu10.title: Conceptional age
HncKu10.description: The fetal age counted from the moment of conception. Can be directly determined in pregnancies that result from assisted reproductive technologies. In unassisted pregnancies, it is assumed to be 2 weeks younger than the gestational age.

snctu10.title: Ivacaftor
snctu10.description: A CFTR modulator used to treat patients who are homozygous for the F508del mutation in the CFTR gene. Improves chloride transport by increasing the likelihood that the chloride channel of CFTR protein is open. Used in combination with lumacaftor.

GncBu10.title: Tezacaftor
GncBu10.description: A CFTR modulator used to treat patients who are homozygous for the F508del mutation in the CFTR gene. Increases normal intracellular processing and trafficking of functional CFTR protein to the cell surface. Used in combination with ivacaftor.

tncXE10.title: Lumacaftor
tncXE10.description: A CFTR modulator used to treat patients who are homozygous for the F508del mutation in the CFTR gene. Improves the conformational stability of the defective protein, which leads to increased intracellular processing and trafficking of functional protein to the cell surface. Used in combination with ivacaftor.

FncgE10.title: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator
FncgE10.description: A new class of drugs used to treat cystic fibrosis by modulating the expression of defective CFTR protein. Different modulators can improve the production, intracellular processing, and function of defective protein.

8ncOE10.title: Antibody isotype
8ncOE10.description: The class of antibody produced by B cells; there are 5 isotypes (IgA, IgM, IgD, IgG, IgE) that are encoded in the constant domain of the immunoglobulin gene and determined by the Fc region of the heavy chains. Class switching occurs during B cell maturation.

media.title: General structure of immunoglobulins exemplified by IgG

uncpE10.title: Heavy chain
uncpE10.description: The large subunit of antibodies that forms the Fc fragment and, together with the light chain, the Fab fragment. There are five types of heavy chains: γ, δ, α, μ, and ε that determine the isotypes of immunoglobulins: IgG, IgD, IgA, IgM, and IgE respectively.

media.title: General structure of immunoglobulins exemplified by IgG

Enc8E10.title: Anti-phospholipase A2 receptor antibodies
Enc8E10.description: A group of autoantibodies produced by patients with idiopathic (primary) membranous nephropathy.

Dnc1v10.title: Muscle energy
Dnc1v10.description: An osteopathic technique to treat joint restrictions, hypertonicity, and muscle weakness by using voluntary muscle contraction in a controlled position against an equal counterforce. Postisometric relaxation and reciprocal inhibition are the most commonly used muscle energy techniques.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Muscle energy techniques

9ncNv10.title: Articulatory technique
9ncNv10.description: A direct, passive osteopathic manipulative technique that uses either gentle rhythmic motions or concentric repetitive movements to increase the range of motion of a restricted joint. Indicated in children and adolescents, older individuals, and postoperative patients. Examples include rib raising and Spencer technique.

Cncqv10.title: Myofascial technique
Cncqv10.description: A nonspecific group of osteopathic techniques used in musculoskeletal manual medicine directed at musculature and fascia.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Myofascial release techniques

xncEv10.title: High-velocity low-amplitude
xncEv10.description: An osteopathic manipulative treatment that involves the brief application of a rapid force over a short distance to move a joint past its restrictive barrier.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → High-velocity low-amplitude technique

Bnczv10.title: Counterstrain
Bnczv10.description: A passive, indirect osteopathic technique to treat tender points. The patient is placed in a pain-free position (position of ease), which is held for 90 seconds to shorten the muscle, restore its normal length, and alleviate the tension and strain of the affected structures.

yncdD10.title: Costoclavicular syndrome test
yncdD10.description: A physical examination maneuver used to assess for thoracic outlet syndrome.

_nc5D10.title: Vault hold
_nc5D10.description: An osteopathic diagnostic method used in the field of cranial osteopathy to evaluate the sphenobasilar synchondrosis.

-ncDD10.title: Reciprocal tension membrane
-ncDD10.description: An osteopathic term that describes the dural attachment between the cranium and S2 of the vertebral column.

ZLcZw10.title: Compression of the fourth ventricle (CV4)
ZLcZw10.description: A craniosacral technique in which the practitioner applies gentle superomedial traction to the fourth ventricle, intensifying the pressure during exhalation.

0Lcew10.title: Sacral rocking
0Lcew10.description: An osteopathic manipulative technique that applies a gentle rocking motion to the sacrum in tandem with the respiratory cycle to relax the muscles of the lumbosacral junction. This technique augments the flexion and extension phases of the sacrum and is indicated in patients with tight lumbosacral paraspinal muscles, dysmenorrhea, pelvic congestion syndrome, or sacroiliac dysfunctions.

XLc9w10.title: Occipital condyle decompression
XLc9w10.description: A craniosacral technique used to balance the reciprocal tension membrane at the hypoglossal canal to improve the function of the hypoglossal nerve (cranial nerve XII). Performed with the patient in the supine position. The physician holds the patient's head in their palms, with the index and middle fingers contacting the condylar processes on both sides. Gentle cephalad and lateral traction is then applied at the base of the occiput.

dLco910.title: Radiation colitis
dLco910.description: An adverse effect of radiation therapy to the abdomen and/or pelvis. Manifestations include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain within weeks after receiving radiotherapy. Chronic effects include malabsorption and stricture formation.

VLcG910.title: Fulminant colitis
VLcG910.description: A condition of severe bowel inflammation that typically causes > 10 stools per day, lower gastrointestinal bleeding, abdominal pain, and abdominal distension. Etiologies include inflammatory bowel disease (e.g., ulcerative colitis, Crohn disease) and infection (e.g., caused by C. difficile).

eLcx910.title: Rebound tenderness
eLcx910.description: A physical examination finding characterized by an abrupt increase in pain when an examiner suddenly releases compression of the abdominal wall. Caused by irritation of the receptors in parietal peritoneum.

SLcyC10.title: CD4+/CD8+ ratio
SLcyC10.description: The proportion of CD4+ T-helper cells to cytotoxic CD8+ T cells. Normally between 1-4. Abnormalities in the CD4+/CD8+ ratio reflect immune system dysfunction (e.g., increased ratio in patients with sarcoidosis, decreased ratio in patients with HIV infection).

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Lymphoid cell line

RLclx10.title: Alvarado score
RLclx10.description: A score used to predict the likelihood of acute appendicitis based on clinical features and laboratory parameters.

iLcJx10.title: Lead pipe rigidity
iLcJx10.description: A physical examination finding of smooth, uniform tonic resistance in response to passive movement. Seen in some patients with Parkinson disease. Also associated with neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

QLcux10.title: Tertiary adrenal insufficiency
QLcux10.description: A state of decreased adrenal production of glucocorticoids and adrenal androgens as a result of decreased production of CRH in the hypothalamus. The most common cause is a sudden discontinuation of glucocorticoids after prolonged glucocorticoid therapy.

LLcwy10.title: Voxilaprevir
LLcwy10.description: A protease inhibitor used to chronic hepatitis C infection (all genotypes). Administered in combination with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir. Adverse effects include headache, fatigue, diarrhea, and nausea.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

oLc0A10.title: Glecaprevir
oLc0A10.description: A protease inhibitor used to chronic hepatitis C infection (all genotypes). Administered in combination with pibrentasvir. Adverse effects include headache, fatigue, nausea, diarrhea, and weakness.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

KLcUA10.title: Paritaprevir
KLcUA10.description: A protease inhibitor used to treat chronic hepatitis C infection (genotype 1 or 4). Administered in combination with ombitasvir and ritonavir and used in a regimen that includes ribavirin and/or dasabuvir. Adverse effects include headache, fatigue, nausea, pruritus, skin reactions, insomnia, asthenia, hyperbilirubinemia, and hepatotoxicity.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

6LcjA10.title: Daclatasvir
6LcjA10.description: A drug used to chronic hepatitis C infection (genotype 1, 3, or 4) by binding to the N-terminus within domain 1 of nonstructural protein 5A (NS5A) and inhibiting viral RNA replication and virion assembly. Administered in combination with sofosbuvir or ribavirin/interferon. Adverse effects include headache, fatigue, nausea, and bradycardia.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

pLcLA10.title: Elbasvir
pLcLA10.description: A nonnucleoside NS5A polymerase inhibitor used to treat chronic hepatitis C infection (genotype 1 and 4) in combination with grazoprevir. Adverse effects include headache, fatigue, anorexia, nausea, and hepatotoxicity.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

JLcsA10.title: Pibrentasvir
JLcsA10.description: A nonnucleoside NS5A polymerase inhibitor used in combination with glecaprevir to treat hepatitis C infection.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

rLcf_10.title: Progressive inhibition of neuromusculoskeletal structures
rLcf_10.description: A myofascial release technique that involves the gradual application of inhibitory pressure to the most tender point (primary point) and the insertion site of the affected muscle (end point). Primarily used to manage pain, improve range of motion, and enhance circulation.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Myofascial release techniques

7Lc4_10.title: Type 1 somatic dysfunction
7Lc4_10.description: An osteopathic term used to describe a group curve of 3 or more vertebrae in the thoracic and lumbar spine that follows the first law of Fryette, which states when the spine is neutral, side bending and rotation occur to opposite sides.

HLcK_10.title: Type 2 somatic dysfunction
HLcK_10.description: An osteopathic term used to describe an individual dysfunctional vertebral segment in the thoracic and lumbar spine that follows the second law of Fryette, which states when the spine is flexed or extended, side bending and rotation occur to the same side.

sLct_10.title: Citrullination
sLct_10.description: The posttranslational conversion of the amino acid arginine into citrulline, which is relatively more hydrophobic. Carried out by peptidylarginine deiminases.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Post-translational modification

GLcB_10.title: Metyrapone stimulation test
GLcB_10.description: A test in which metyrapone (which blocks the conversion of 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol) is used to induce a decrease in serum cortisol concentration. The normal physiologic response to a decreased serum cortisol concentration is an increase in ACTH secretion. This test can be used to detect pituitary dysfunction that results in impaired ACTH secretion.

tLcXz10.title: Vitamin B1 deficiency
tLcXz10.description: A deficiency of vitamin B₁ (thiamine), which leads to impaired glucose breakdown and damage to highly aerobic tissues. Most commonly seen in patients with alcohol use disorder. Can manifest as beriberi, Wernicke encephalopathy, or Korsakoff syndrome.

vLcAz10.title: Inflammatory appendicular mass
vLcAz10.description: An inflammatory mass composed of an inflamed appendix and its adjacent inflamed viscera. May be palpable as a tender mass in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen.

CLcq-10.title: Hilum of the lung
CLcq-10.description: A central area on the medial surface of the lung. Contains the main bronchi, pulmonary and bronchial arteries and veins, pulmonary nervous plexus, and lymphatic vessels, which are all enveloped by a pleural sleeve.

yLcdZW0.title: Adductor hiatus
yLcdZW0.description: An opening at the junction of the middle and lower ⅓ of the adductor magnus muscle. The femoral vessels pass through the adductor hiatus and continue into the popliteal fossa as popliteal vessels.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Femoral triangle and fasial compartments of the thigh

aocQ0W0.title: Washout period
aocQ0W0.description: A period of time during which a patient receives no treatment (e.g., medication) before starting a new therapy. E.g., used in clinical trials to help ensure that observed effects are due to the new therapy.

Xoc90W0.title: Facet joints
Xoc90W0.description: The synovial joints formed between the superior and inferior articular processes of consecutive vertebrae. As these joints are in close proximity to the spinal foramina, facet joint hypertrophy (e.g., due to arthritis) can lead to spinal stenosis.

WocPaW0.title: Pleural fluid analysis
WocPaW0.description: The analysis of fluid that accumulates within the pleural cavity. Components include gross appearance, total protein, cell counts, bacterial cultures, and concentrations of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), glucose, and adenosine deaminase. The Light criteria can be used to classify a pleural effusion as exudative based on analysis of pleural fluid protein and LDH.

2ocTYW0.title: Fluorodeoxyglucose
2ocTYW0.description: A glucose analog used in positron emission tomography scans. Uptake of FDG by tissues indicates metabolism of glucose. Thus, FDG-avid lesions are metabolically active, while FDG-nonavid lesions are not.

Toc6YW0.title: Key rib
Toc6YW0.description: An osteopathic term used to describe the major restrictor in group rib dysfunctions. In inhalation dysfunctions, the key rib is the lowest rib, restricting the full range of motion of the ribs above during exhalation. In exhalation dysfunctions, the key rib is the uppermost rib, restricting the full range of motion of the ribs below during inhalation.

destinations.label: Thoracic spine and rib osteopathy → Rib dysfunctions

SocyYW0.title: Myofascial trigger point
SocyYW0.description: An osteopathic term for firm, discrete, palpable, hypersensitive nodules in skeletal muscles that are spontaneously painful or tender. Typically have a referred pain pattern, often with a predictable distribution. Can be treated with various musculoskeletal manipulative techniques.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Myofascial trigger point

iocJbW0.title: Somatic dysfunction
iocJbW0.description: A state of impaired or altered function of somatic system components, including skeletal, arthrodial, and myofascial structures, and related vascular, lymphatic, and neural elements. Caused e.g., by trauma, emotional stress, infection or viscerosomatic reflexes. Diagnosed via the TART criteria.

4oc3XW0.title: Perforator veins
4oc3XW0.description: The lower limb veins that connect the superficial venous system with the deep venous system by piercing through the deep fascia. Contain valves that ensure unidirectional flow of blood from the superficial to the deep system. Valvular incompetence of perforator veins can result in varicose veins and chronic venous insufficiency.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

kocmXW0.title: Lumbosacral plexus
kocmXW0.description: A network of nerves composed of the lumbar plexus, which is formed by the subcostal nerve (T12) and first four lumbar nerves (L1–L4), and the sacral plexus, which is formed by the last two lumbar nerves (L4–L5) and the first four sacral nerves (S1–S4).

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Nerves
Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → Innervation of the thigh

6ocj1W0.title: Scapular anastomosis
6ocj1W0.description: An anastomosis between the branches of the subclavian artery and the axillary artery that forms a circulatory system around the scapula. Provides collateral circulation to the arm in case of occlusion or injury to one of the contributing vessels.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage
Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

Jocs1W0.title: Hypergammaglobulinemia
Jocs1W0.description: An increase in the serum concentration of immunoglobulins (most commonly IgM). Etiologies include chronic infection, autoimmune disorders, and malignancies.

qocC1W0.title: Hypochlorous acid
qocC1W0.description: A reactive oxygen species produced by neutrophils through activation of the NADPH oxidase complex during the oxidative burst.

IocYWW0.title: Autonomic dysreflexia
IocYWW0.description: A cardiovascular complication of spinal cord injury above the level of T6. Characterized by a loss of autonomic responses that control heart rate and vascular tone, which results in hypertension, headache, and diaphoresis. Patients can develop bradycardia or tachycardia.

7oc4WW0.title: Hydrolysis
7oc4WW0.description: A chemical reaction that involves the breakdown of a compound by reacting with water. Typically catalyzed by an enzyme (e.g., hydrolysis of carbohydrates by enzymes such as lactase, galactase, and amylase).

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

soctWW0.title: Perimolysis
soctWW0.description: The erosion of enamel on the inner (lingual) surfaces of anterior maxillary teeth due to chronic regurgitation of acidic gastric contents. Associated with self-induced vomiting (e.g., in bulimia nervosa) that has occurred for at least 6 months.

GocBWW0.title: Brenner tumor
GocBWW0.description: An ovarian tumor with histologic resemblance to transitional cell urothelium. Typically benign and asymptomatic. Can sometimes cause abdominal pain and/or vaginal bleeding.

destinations.label: Overview of ovarian tumors →  Epithelial ovarian tumors

8ocOdW0.title: Vena comitans
8ocOdW0.description: A vein that accompanies a peripheral artery. Typically paired (i.e., venae comitantes).

uocpdW0.title: Radial vein
uocpdW0.description: A paired vein in the lateral forearm that extends from the hand to the cubital fossa. Terminates by anastomosing with the ulnar vein and forming the brachial vein at the elbow. Drains the hand, the lateral forearm, and the elbow joint.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Veins
Upper arm and elbow → Vasculature and lymphatics

Eoc8dW0.title: Ulnar vein
Eoc8dW0.description: A pair of deep veins of the forearm that originate from the deep venous palmar arch and terminate in the deep compartment of the forearm (in the cubital fossa). Drains from the deep palmar arch into the brachial veins.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Veins
Upper arm and elbow → Vasculature and lymphatics

Doc1VW0.title: Reynolds number
Doc1VW0.description: A ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces. Laminar flow occurs at low Reynolds numbers because viscous forces dominate; turbulent flow occurs at high Reynolds numbers because inertial forces dominate.

wochVW0.title: Subclavian nerve
wochVW0.description: A motor nerve that arises from the C5-C6 anterior spinal roots. Innervates the subclavius muscle.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

9ocNVW0.title: Fleischner sign
9ocNVW0.description: A radiologic finding characterized by a prominent central pulmonary artery. Etiologies include pulmonary hypertension and distention due to a massive pulmonary embolism.

CocqVW0.title: Scalene triangle
CocqVW0.description: A region formed by the clavicle and the anterior and middle scalene muscles. Contains the subclavian artery and the three trunks of the brachial plexus. Compression of structures within the triangle results in thoracic outlet syndrome.

xocEVW0.title: Fovea capitis
xocEVW0.description: A depression on the head of the femur in which the ligamentum teres femoris inserts.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The femur

BoczVW0.title: Reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction
BoczVW0.description: A laboratory technique in which a sample of mRNA is converted to complementary DNA (cDNA) by reverse transcriptase. The cDNA is then amplified by the standard PCR procedure to detect and quantify the amount of mRNA. Abbreviation RT-PCR not to be confused with real-time PCR (qPCR).

AocReW0.title: Hutchinson sign of the nail
AocReW0.description: A dermatologic finding of periungual pigmentation at the proximal and/or lateral nail fold. Associated with subungual melanoma but can be seen in some benign conditions (e.g., nail lentigines).

-ocDeW0.title: Clinically significant involuntary weight loss
-ocDeW0.description: A loss of > 5% of usual body weight within 6–12 months. Excludes deliberate weight loss (e.g., due to exercise, changes in diet, and/or the use of medications such as thyroxine).

destinations.label: Unexpected weight changes → Unexpected weight loss

ZKcZUW0.title: Dorello canal
ZKcZUW0.description: An osseous canal located at the petrous ridge of the temporal bone. Encloses the inferior petrous sinus and abducens nerve.

0KceUW0.title: Short-acting beta agonist
0KceUW0.description: A class of bronchodilating medications with a short duration of action (< 6 hours). These medications also have a quick onset of action (1-5 minutes). Used to treat acute exacerbations of asthma and COPD. Usually administered via a nebulizer or metered-dose inhaler.

aKcQUW0.title: MDI
aKcQUW0.description: A device used for the delivery of inhaled respiratory medications, such as albuterol. The device consists of a pressurized canister that propels the medication into the lungs when inhaled.

YKcnUW0.title: Noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation
YKcnUW0.description: A type of ventilatory support that does not require an invasive artificial airway (i.e., no endotracheal intubation). Typically applied to a patient's upper airway via a mask or mouthpiece. Commonly used for the treatment of asthma and COPD exacerbations.

bKcHUW0.title: Direct oral anticoagulant
bKcHUW0.description: An oral anticoagulant that directly binds to clotting factors (e.g., thrombin, factor Xa). Examples include dabigatran, rivaroxaban, and apixaban.

cKca2W0.title: Ileus
cKca2W0.description: An inability of intestinal contents to pass through the intestinal tract (e.g., due to obstruction or dysfunction of peristalsis). Further subdivided into mechanical and functional ileus.

1Kc22W0.title: Median claw
1Kc22W0.description: A pathologic hand posture that occurs in patients with distal median nerve injury (e.g., in carpal tunnel syndrome). When asked to extend the fingers of the affected hand, the patient can only extend the ring finger and the little finger. Typically accompanied by sensory deficits over the first three digits and the radial side of the ring finger.

dKco2W0.title: Erythrocyte transketolase
dKco2W0.description: An enzyme whose activity decreases if there is a deficiency of thiamine (vitamin B1). Can be assessed in the evaluation of Wernicke encephalopathy.

eKcx2W0.title: Rome IV diagnostic criteria for functional constipation in adults
eKcx2W0.description: A set of criteria used to evaluate for a diagnosis of functional constipation. To meet criteria, patients must have ≥ 2 of the following for ≥3 months: straining, lumpy or hard stools, sensation of incomplete evacuation, sensation of anorectal obstruction, need for manual maneuvers to aid defecation, < 3 spontaneous bowel movements per week.

2KcTfW0.title: Magnesium hydroxide
2KcTfW0.description: A medication used as an antacid or as a laxative (via osmotic retention of fluid).

gKcFfW0.title: Permissive hypotension
gKcFfW0.description: The maintenance of systolic blood pressure between 70–90 mm Hg to maintain adequate perfusion without exacerbating hemorrhage (e.g., in patients with hemorrhagic shock due to a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm). Can be achieved with careful administration of vasodilatory drugs (e.g., nitrates) and/or fluids.

SKcyfW0.title: Pulsus bisferiens
SKcyfW0.description: The presence of two pulsations per cardiac cycle. The first pulsation is typically rapid and short, which is then followed by a slower, broader pulse.

3KcSTW0.title: Bulk-forming laxatives
3KcSTW0.description: A type of laxative that increases the bulk and water content of stool, facilitating its passage through the intestines.

iKcJTW0.title: Salpingectomy
iKcJTW0.description: The partial or complete resection of a fallopian tube. Indications include ruptured ectopic pregnancy, hydrosalpinx, and malignancy. Can be performed via a laparoscopic or open approach.

QKcuTW0.title: Salpingostomy
QKcuTW0.description: The creation of an opening in the fallopian tube to remove tubal contents (e.g., in the management of tubal ectopic pregnancy, hydrosalpinx). The opening is sutured shut at the end of the procedure. Can be performed laparoscopically or through an open approach.

4Kc3gW0.title: Narcotic bowel syndrome
4Kc3gW0.description: A condition of moderate to severe abdominal pain that can develop in patients who receive > 100 mg/day of morphine (or its equivalent). The pain is typically chronic (> 3 months) and does not respond to additional opioid therapy.

kKcmgW0.title: Nasal potential difference test
kKcmgW0.description: A physiologic test of CFTR dysfunction that is sometimes used during the diagnosis of cystic fibrosis (CF). It indirectly assesses Cl- movement by measuring the potential difference across the nasal epithelium in response to nasal infusion of standardized solutions. It is typically performed if other diagnostic tests for CF, e.g., sweat test and genetic testing, are inconclusive.

mKcVSW0.title: Charcot neuropathic osteoarthropathy
mKcVSW0.description: A progressive degeneration of a bone and/or joint caused by repetitive trauma, abnormal vascular flow, and inflammation. Typically precipitated by conditions that result in decreased sensation (e.g., peripheral neuropathies caused by diabetes, tabes dorsalis, spinal cord injury). Manifestations include erythema, edema, warmth, and the formation of pressure ulcers near the affected area.

MKcMSW0.title: Bacterial adhesin
MKcMSW0.description: A virulence factor found on the surface of some bacteria that facilitate adhesion to cells. Facilitates colonization and infection of the host. Adhesins are usually pili or fimbria on gram-negative bacteria and proteins or polysaccharides on gram-positive bacteria.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanism of bacterial infection and disease

LKcwSW0.title: Methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus
LKcwSW0.description: A strain of Staphylococcus aureus that is susceptible to certain beta-lactam antibiotics (e.g., nafcillin, oxacillin), in contrast to methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).

oKc0hW0.title: Linkage disequilibrium
oKc0hW0.description: The property of particular alleles at two linked loci to be expressed more or less often than would be expected in the general population. Can occur in settings where allelic loci are within close proximity to each other on a chromosome, therefore decreasing the probability of DNA recombination.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

pKcLhW0.title: Basic metabolic panel
pKcLhW0.description: A laboratory test that includes the serum concentrations of several compounds, including sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate, urea nitrogen, creatinine, and glucose. Sometimes also contains the serum calcium concentration.

JKcshW0.title: Projectile vomiting
JKcshW0.description: An episode of vomiting associated with excessive force. Can be preceded by nausea. Etiologies include gastroenteritis and conditions that cause increased intracranial pressure.

rKcf3W0.title: Hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis
rKcf3W0.description: A part of the neuroendocrine system that regulates the production of thyroid hormones. Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH), which is produced by the hypothalamus, stimulates the pituitary gland to produce thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), which, in turn, stimulates the thyroid gland to produce T3 and T4. T3 and T4 suppress the production of TRH and TSH from the hypothalamus and pituitary gland.

sKct3W0.title: Marasmic kwashiorkor
sKct3W0.description: A condition of severe malnutrition characterized by features of both marasmus (e.g., low weight-for-height and reduced mid-upper arm circumference) and kwashiorkor (e.g., peripheral pitting edema).

vKcARW0.title: Mental status examination
vKcARW0.description:
An assessment of mental status. Assess:
- Patient appearance (e.g., dress, hygiene), alertness, speech (e.g., tone, volume, rate, rhythm), and behavior
- Mood and affect (e.g., flat, appropriate), including congruency
- Thought process (e.g., linear, tangential) and thought content
- Memory, simple calculating, judgment, and higher cortical functioning (e.g., response to a scenario, interpretation of a common phrase). 
Common assessments include the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA).

DKc1iW0.title: Cerebellar signs
DKc1iW0.description: A collection of signs associated with cerebellar dysfunction. Can be remembered with the mnemonic DASHING: Dysdiadochokinesis and Dysmetria, Ataxia, Slurred speech, Hypotonia, Intention tremor, Nystagmus, Gait disturbances.

wKchiW0.title: Hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy
wKchiW0.description: A group of hereditary peripheral neuropathies characterized by a loss of both large myelinated and unmyelinated fibers. Examples include hereditary sensory radicular neuropathy and familial dysautonomia.

BKcziW0.title: Clinical signs of significant dehydration
BKcziW0.description: A collection of symptoms that includes tachycardia, postural or orthostatic hypotension, reduced skin turgor (skin tenting), dry mucous membranes, collapsed neck veins in the supine position, and decreased urine output.

yKcdQW0.title: ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis
yKcdQW0.description: A type of glomerulonephritis with minimal or no immune complex or complement deposits seen on histopathologic examination (e.g., immunofluorescence, electron microscopy) of glomerular tissue. Immunofluorescence microscopy shows cytoplasmic or perinuclear ANCA antibody staining. Examples include granulomatosis with polyangiitis and microscopic polyangiitis.

AKcRQW0.title: Saddle nose deformity
AKcRQW0.description: A depression of the nasal dorsum. Most commonly caused by trauma. Can also be caused by pathologic destruction of bone and cartilage (e.g., due to relapsing polychondritis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis, congenital syphilis, malignancy).

Z6cZjW0.title: Fluid compartment
Z6cZjW0.description: A section of the body in which fluid is distributed. The two main compartments are intracellular (which contains approximately ⅔ of total fluid volume) and extracellular (contains approximately ⅓ of total fluid volume).

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function

06cejW0.title: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting
06cejW0.description: An adverse effect of many different types of chemotherapy. Further subdivided into acute (occurring 1-2 hours after administration of chemotherapy), delayed (occurring > 24 hours after administration of chemotherapy), and anticipatory (occurring prior to treatment as a conditioned response to previous nausea and vomiting).

destinations.label: Complications of cancer therapy → Gastrointestinal complications

a6cQjW0.title: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
a6cQjW0.description: A term to describe the histopathological findings of small-vessel vasculitides (e.g., cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis, IgA vasculitis). Findings include neutrophil-predominant perivascular inflammatory infiltrate with fibrinoid destruction of the vascular walls. This term is often used incorrectly as a synonym for cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis.

X6c9jW0.title: Dolasetron
X6c9jW0.description: A 5-HT3 receptor antagonist used to prevent nausea and vomiting due to chemotherapy or surgery. Adverse effects include headache, fatigue, and bradycardia.

W6cPPW0.title: Countercurrent multiplication
W6cPPW0.description: A countercurrent mechanism system is a mechanism that expends energy to create a concentration gradient. In the nephron, it refers to the active reabsorption of NaCl from the ascending limb of the loop of Henle into the interstial space. This makes the interstitium hypertonic and creates a concentration gradient that allows the water to passively move from the tubular fluid in the descending limb into the interstitial space.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Physiology of the tubular system

V6cGPW0.title: Phagosome
V6cGPW0.description: A vesicle that forms from the cytoplasmic membrane of a phagocyte in order to engulf a particle.

e6cxPW0.title: Histidinemia
e6cxPW0.description: An autosomal recessive condition characterized by increased serum concentrations of histidine due to deficiency of histidase. Patients with this condition are typically asymptomatic.

U6cb4W0.title: P6 acupressure wristband
U6cb4W0.description: A device that applies pressure to the P6 acupressure point on the anterior wrist, which is located between the palmaris longus and flexor carpi radialis tendons. May have some benefits for the treatment of nausea and vomiting associated with motion sickness and pregnancy.

26cT4W0.title: Plasma membrane Ca2+ ATPase
26cT4W0.description: A plasma membrane transport protein that regulates intracellular calcium concentrations by pumping calcium ions from the cytosol into the extracellular space.

f6ck4W0.title: General paresis
f6ck4W0.description: A form of neurosyphilis that causes severe, progressive dementia and cerebral atrophy. Early manifestations include personality changes and deficits of memory and judgment. Can cause neurologic symptoms, including dysarthria, hypotonia, and tremors.

T6c64W0.title: Immunoreactive trypsinogen
T6c64W0.description: A proenzyme of trypsin that accumulates in the blood of newborns with cystic fibrosis. Serum concentrations can be assessed as part of newborn screening for this condition.

g6cF4W0.title: Superoxide dismutase
g6cF4W0.description: An enzyme that scavenges oxygen radicals and converts them into hydrogen peroxide. Defects in this enzyme are associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

S6cy4W0.title: Rothmund–Thomson syndrome
S6cy4W0.description: A syndrome characterized by short stature, sparse hair, poikiloderma, skeletal abnormalities, and cataracts. Associated with an increased risk of osteosarcoma.

h6cckW0.title: Netherton syndrome
h6cckW0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in SPINK5, a gene that encodes a serine protease kinase. Manifestations are variable and include scaly erythroderma, eczematous patches, hair abnormalities (e.g., trichorrhexis invaginata, in which individual strands of hair have thick and thin areas).

36cSkW0.title: Functional outlet disorder
36cSkW0.description: A subtype of primary constipation in which there is difficulty evacuating stool once it reaches the rectum. Can manifest with prolonged straining, rectal discomfort, and difficulty passing even soft stools. May be caused by inadequate rectal propulsive forces, increased resistance to evacuation (e.g., inappropriate contraction of pelvic floor muscles), or other factors (e.g., structural blockage by a rectocele).

R6clkW0.title: Balloon expulsion test
R6clkW0.description: A latex balloon attached to a catheter is inserted into the patient's rectum and 50 mL of fluid is injected into the balloon. The patient is given privacy and asked to expel the balloon into a toilet. Inability to expel the balloon within 60 seconds suggests a diagnosis of pelvic dyssynergia.

i6cJkW0.title: Primary constipation
i6cJkW0.description: Constipation with no identifiable organic (anatomic, metabolic, or biochemical) etiology. Most commonly caused by inadequate fluid intake, fiber intake, and/or physical activity as well as slow/delayed colon transit times and pelvic floor dysfunction. Of note, there is some controversy over the use of the term "functional constipation" as a synonym of primary constipation; it is included in the Rome IV classification of constipation but the American Gastroenterological Association no longer recommends its use.

Q6cukW0.title: Secondary constipation
Q6cukW0.description: A subtype of constipation caused by a specific etiology (e.g., mechanical, drug-related, endocrine, neurologic). Examples include constipation due to malignant obstruction, opiate adverse effects, and diabetic neuropathy.

j6c_kW0.title: Ceramide
j6c_kW0.description: A lipid molecule consisting of sphingosine and one fatty acid.

46c3OW0.title: Mild hypothermia
46c3OW0.description: A stage of hypothermia in which the core body temperature is 32–35°C (89.6–95°F). Manifestations include tachycardia, tachypnea, confusion, amnesia, dysarthria, impaired judgment, and ataxia.

k6cmOW0.title: Moderate hypothermia
k6cmOW0.description: A stage of hypothermia in which the core body temperature is 28–32°C (82.4–89.6°F). Manifestations include CNS depression, hypoventilation, hyporeflexia, bradycardia, and arrhythmias

O6cIOW0.title: Prucalopride
O6cIOW0.description: A 5-HT4 receptor agonist that has enterokinetic properties. Results in stimulation of the peristaltic reflex, increased intestinal secretions, and increased gastrointestinal motility. Used in the management of chronic constipation refractory to osmotic and secretory laxatives. Contraindicated in patients with inflammatory bowel disease and megacolon.

l6cvOW0.title: Hutchinson sign of the nose
l6cvOW0.description: A vesicular rash on the nasal alae due to herpes zoster ophthalmicus. Indicates involvement of the nasociliary nerve, a branch of the ophthalmic nerve (V₁).

N6c-OW0.title: Linaclotide
N6c-OW0.description: A peptide agonist of guanylate cyclase that increases intestinal secretion of bicarbonate and chloride and improves fecal transit. Used to treat chronic constipation refractory to treatment with osmotic and stimulant laxatives. Also used to treat irritable bowel syndrome with constipation.

m6cVlW0.title: Plecanatide
m6cVlW0.description: A peptide agonist of guanylate cyclase that increases intestinal secretion of bicarbonate and chloride and improves fecal transit. Used to treat chronic constipation refractory to treatment with osmotic and stimulant laxatives. Also used to treat irritable bowel syndrome with constipation.

56cilW0.title: Pseudo-Pelger-Huet abnormality
56cilW0.description: A peripheral blood smear finding of granulocytes that have reduced segmentation (e.g., neutrophils with bilobed nuclei). Causes include myelodysplastic syndrome, myeloid leukemias, antineoplastic medications, and immunosuppressants.

n6c7lW0.title: Syndrome of apparent mineralocorticoid excess
n6c7lW0.description: A rare autosomal recessive condition caused by a deficiency of renal isoenzyme 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2. This enzyme is responsible for converting cortisol to cortisone in the kidneys. Deficiency results in increased binding of cortisol to mineralocorticoid receptors. Manifestations include failure to thrive, early-onset severe hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and a low serum aldosterone concentration.

destinations.label: Renal tubular disorders → Syndrome of apparent mineralocorticoid excess

L6cwlW0.title: Palpation thyroiditis
L6cwlW0.description: A condition of hyperthyroidism due to thyroid gland manipulation during parathyroid surgery. Typically self-limited and resolves within weeks to months.

o6c0NW0.title: Lung transplantation
o6c0NW0.description: The transplantation of a lung from a deceased donor. Indicated in patients with end-stage lung disease who are predicted to survive < 2 years under medical and/or surgical management. Complications include pneumonia, graft rejection, airway anastomotic complications, and infection as a result of immunosuppressive therapy.

K6cUNW0.title: Lymphocele
K6cUNW0.description: A collection of lymphatic fluid within the body that is not contained by an epithelial lining. Can develop in the retroperitoneum as a complication of pelvic surgical procedures.

66cjNW0.title: Generalized lymphadenopathy
66cjNW0.description: Lymph node enlargement in two or more noncontiguous lymph node regions. Typically caused by underlying systemic disease (e.g., autoimmune disease, malignancy).

76c4mW0.title: Toxic alcohol poisoning
76c4mW0.description: Poisoning by a group of alcohols that are either directly toxic or have toxic metabolites. Often associated with a high osmolar gap and/or an anion gap metabolic acidosis. Examples of toxic alcohols include ethylene glycol, methanol, isopropyl alcohol, diethylene glycol, and propylene glycol.

F6cg5W0.title: Opioid-induced constipation
F6cg5W0.description: An adverse effect of opioid therapy caused by reduced peristalsis. Manifestations typically develop when initiating or increasing opioid therapy and include straining, < 3 bowel movements per week, and formation of hard stool.

86cO5W0.title: Rome IV diagnostic criteria for opioid-induced constipation
86cO5W0.description: A condition of new or worsening functional constipation in the setting of starting, changing, or increasing the dose of opioid therapy. To meet criteria for opioid-induced constipation, patients must have ≥ 2 of the following: straining, lumpy or hard stools, sensation of incomplete evacuation, sensation of anorectal obstruction, need for manual maneuvers to aid defecation, < 3 spontaneous bowel movements per week; AND loose stools are rarely present without the use of laxatives

v6cA5W0.title: Gene therapy
v6cA5W0.description: The genetic modification of cells (e.g., repairing a defective gene) to treat or cure disease.

D6c1MW0.title: Annular ligaments of trachea
D6c1MW0.description: The horizontal fibrous bands that join adjacent rings of tracheal cartilage together.

96cNMW0.title: Amyloid nephropathy
96cNMW0.description: A condition characterized by amyloid deposition in the kidneys. Manifestations vary but include progressive chronic kidney disease, proteinuria, renal tubular acidosis, and polyuria.

x6cEMW0.title: Ascitic fluid analysis
x6cEMW0.description: The analysis of ascitic fluid to determine the underlying cause and identify infection (e.g., spontaneous bacterial peritonitis or secondary peritonitis). Components include gross appearance, total protein, the serum-ascites albumin gradient, cell counts, bacterial cultures, PCR, and concentrations of lactate dehydrogenase, glucose, amylase, and adenosine deaminase.

B6czMW0.title: High serum-ascites albumin gradient ascites
B6czMW0.description: A condition of ascites in which the serum-ascites albumin gradient is ≥ 1.1 g/dL. Etiologies include cirrhosis, alcohol-related liver disease, right heart failure, and portal vein thrombosis.

y6cdnW0.title: Low serum-ascites albumin gradient ascites
y6cdnW0.description: A condition of ascites in which the serum-ascites albumin gradient is < 1.1 g/dL. Etiologies include hypoalbuminemia (e.g., du to nephrotic syndrome), malignancy, infection (e.g., tuberculosis), and pancreatitis.

A6cRnW0.title: Multiplex polymerase chain reaction
A6cRnW0.description: A type of polymerase chain reaction that analyzes multiple different DNA sequences at the same time by using multiple primers. Can be used to evaluate genetic conditions for specific underlying DNA mutations, various infections (e.g., influenza-like illness, meningitis), and hematologic malignancies.

z6crnW0.title: Acute mesenteric artery embolism
z6crnW0.description: A condition of acute mesenteric ischemia due to embolic occlusion of the mesenteric artery. Atrial fibrillation is the most common risk factor. Typically manifests with sudden-onset abdominal pain. Management includes revascularization with resection of gangrenous bowel, if present, with subsequent lifelong anticoagulation.

-6cDnW0.title: Acute mesenteric artery thrombosis
-6cDnW0.description: A type of acute mesenteric ischemia caused by thrombotic occlusion of the mesenteric artery. Typically manifests with subacute-onset abdominal pain. Management includes revascularization and resection of gangrenous bowel, if present, with subsequent lifelong anticoagulation.

ZpcZLW0.title: Mesenteric venous thrombosis
ZpcZLW0.description: A type of mesenteric ischemia caused by thrombotic occlusion of the mesenteric vein(s). Risk factors include thrombophilia and coagulopathies. Typically manifests with subacute-onset abdominal pain. Management includes immediate anticoagulation and endovascular revascularization if anticoagulation does not result in clinical improvement. Lifelong anticoagulation is recommended in patients with underlying thrombophilia or coagulopathy.

0pceLW0.title: Nonobstructive mesenteric ischemia
0pceLW0.description: A type of acute mesenteric ischemia caused by hypoperfusion of the bowel without physical obstruction, e.g., due to cardiac or septic shock. Manifestations include abdominal pain, distention, and a positive fecal occult blood test. Management includes catheter-directed infusion of vasodilators (e.g., prostaglandin E1, papaverine) into the mesenteric arteries.

apcQLW0.title: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales
apcQLW0.description: A group of gram-negative bacteria, including Klebsiella and Escherichia coli, that can produce enzymes capable of inactivating antibiotics of the carbapenem class (e.g., meropenem).

YpcnLW0.title: Peripherally acting μ-opioid receptor antagonist
YpcnLW0.description: A drug that antagonizes μ-opioid receptors outside of the central nervous system (e.g., in the gastrointestinal tract). Used to treat opioid-induced constipation. Examples include methylnaltrexone, naloxegol, alvimopan, and naldemedine.

bpcHLW0.title: Intestinal secretagogues
bpcHLW0.description: A group of drugs that improve colonic transit time by increasing intestinal secretion of water, bicarbonate, and chloride. Examples include linaclotide, plecanatide, and lubiprostone. Used in the management of chronic constipation refractory to osmotic and/or stimulant laxatives.

Xpc9LW0.title: Slow transit constipation
Xpc9LW0.description: A subtype of primary constipation (i.e., constipation with no identifiable secondary cause) characterized by slow colonic transit time on a motility study (normal mean colonic transit time is 30–40 hours, with an upper limit of 70 hours).

1pc2oW0.title: Spiramycin
1pc2oW0.description: An antimicrobial medication that can be used to treat some gram-positive, gram-negative, and parasitic organisms (e.g., Toxoplasma). Not approved for routine use in the United States. Has an unknown mechanism of action.

dpcooW0.title: Constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome
dpcooW0.description: A variant of irritable bowel syndrome characterized by recurrent abdominal pain or discomfort that is associated with constipation rather than diarrhea (< 25% of bowel movements are loose stools in patients with IBS-C).

VpcGoW0.title: Hepatitis
VpcGoW0.description: A condition of liver inflammation. Etiologies include infection (e.g., by hepatitis B virus), chronic alcohol use, drug toxicity, and fatty liver disease. Typically causes increased transaminase concentrations.

epcxoW0.title: Osteodystrophy
epcxoW0.description: A condition of abnormal bone growth and/or morphology (e.g., due to renal disease or mineral deficiency).

UpcbKW0.title: Periostitis
UpcbKW0.description: An inflammation of the periosteum (the layer of connective tissue surrounding bone). Manifestations include swelling, tenderness, and stiffness near the affected bone.

2pcTKW0.title: Rhagades
2pcTKW0.description: A dermatologic finding of perioral fissures, cracks, and/or scars, particularly near the corners of the mouth and nose. Associated with congenital syphilis.

fpckKW0.title: Salt and pepper retinopathy
fpckKW0.description: An ophthalmologic finding of abnormal retinal pigmentation. Associated with congenital rubella syndrome and some mitochondrial diseases.

destinations.label: Congenital TORCH infections → Congenital rubella infection

Tpc6KW0.title: Engraftment
Tpc6KW0.description: The structural integration of tissue into the host. Different clinical criteria for engraftment exist for different tissues (e.g., stem cells, solid organs). For example, successful engraftment following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is defined by an absolute neutrophil count of 1,000/µl or three consecutive days with a count greater than 500/µl.

Rpcl6W0.title: Tryptophan hydroxylase
Rpcl6W0.description: An enzyme that hydroxylates tryptophan to produce 5-hydroxytryptophan. This reaction is the rate-limiting step of serotonin synthesis. Requires tetrahydrobiopterin as a cofactor.

ipcJ6W0.title: SAM
ipcJ6W0.description:
An abbreviation that can stand for:

1. Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve: the movement of the MV towards the ventricular septum during systole. If septal hypertrophy, this facilitates contact between the MV and the septum, which results in LV outflow obstruction. Associated with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy.

2. S-adenosyl methyonine: an important cofactor (methyl donor) for the synthesis of epinephrine and the 7-methylguanine cap on eukaryotic mRNA. Synthesized from methionine. After donating a methyl group, it is converted to S-adenosylhomocysteine, which is remethylated back to methionine in the presence of vitamin B12 and N-methyl-THF.

jpc_6W0.title: Talcosis
jpc_6W0.description: A form of pneumoconiosis caused by occupational and/or domestic exposure to talc, a silicate mineral used in numerous industries (e.g., food, drug, cosmetic, and ceramic production). Typically manifests with centrilobular and subpleural nodules with sparing of the lung bases.

PpcWpW0.title: Long-acting beta agonist
PpcWpW0.description: A class of bronchodilating medications with a long duration of action (≥ 12 hours). Onset of action is variable (quick for formoterol, longer for salmeterol). Used for long-term control of symptoms of asthma and COPD. Usually administered via a nebulizer or metered-dosed inhaler.

4pc3pW0.title: Gastroesophageal junction
4pc3pW0.description: The juncture of the distal esophagus and the proximal stomach (i.e., the cardia). Endoscopically it is identifiable as the Z line and the site at which the gastric mucosal folds terminate. Histologically, the GEJ is defines as the squamocolumnar junction between the esophageal squamous mucosa and the gastric columnar mucosa.

kpcmpW0.title: Water brash
kpcmpW0.description: A symptom of excessive salivation triggered by refluxing of stomach acid associated with symptomatic gastroesophageal reflux disease.

OpcIpW0.title: Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome
OpcIpW0.description: An inflammatory disorder in individuals with HIV infection characterized by worsening of an infectious condition caused by the initiation of antiretroviral therapy. Thought to be caused by returning immune function that results in inflammatory reactions at sites of infection.

Npc-pW0.title: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy
Npc-pW0.description: A condition of cumulative neuropsychologic symptoms (e.g., cognitive impairment, personality changes, depression, suicidality) attributed to repeated traumatic brain injuries (e.g., from sports-related concussions, military traumas).

mpcVJW0.title: Asthma maintenance therapy
mpcVJW0.description: A group of medications used for maintenance therapy of asthma. Commonly used classes include inhaled corticosteroids with or without inhaled long-acting beta agonists, long-acting muscarinic antagonists, leukotriene receptor antagonists, and asthma biologics, e.g., anti-IgE antibodies, anti-IL-5 antibodies

LpcwJW0.title: Impressionistic speech
LpcwJW0.description: A descriptor for speech content that is lacking in detail and emphasizes emotional content (e.g., "it's incredible, the best, just so amazing!"). A characteristic of histrionic personality disorder.

opc0qW0.title: Gastric emptying scintigraphy
opc0qW0.description: A study used to assess for delayed gastric emptying. Typically involves ingestion of a solid meal that contains a radioactive tracer, followed by sequential imaging studies to assess the rate of gastric emptying. Normal gastric emptying time is usually 4 hours.

KpcUqW0.title: Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome
KpcUqW0.description: Recurrent episodes of vomiting attributed to chronic cannabis use. The Rome IV criteria for diagnosing this condition are the same as for cyclic vomiting syndrome (≥ 3 distinct episodes of vomiting in the past year, each lasting < 1 week, with ≥ 2 episodes in the past six months), with the additional requirements of prolonged cannabis use and the resolution of vomiting symptoms with cessation of use.

ppcLqW0.title: ATP synthase inhibitor
ppcLqW0.description: A compound that blocks ATP synthesis by stopping the electron transfer via an increased proton gradient. Examples include oligomycin and N,N'-Dicyclohexylcarbodiimide.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Clinical significance

media.title: Mechanism of action: respiratory chain inhibitors

JpcsqW0.title: High-power field
JpcsqW0.description: The area visible under the microscope when using high-power magnification. Most commonly refers to a magnification of 400 times compared to normal vision.

qpcCqW0.title: Oval fat body
qpcCqW0.description: A finding on urine microscopy characterized by the presence of lipid droplets within sloughed-off tubular cells of the kidneys. These lipid droplets have a Maltese cross appearance under polarized light. Associated with nephrotic syndrome.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

IpcYIW0.title: Avoidance coping
IpcYIW0.description: A strategy of minimizing, denying, and/or avoiding stressors. Often results in additional stress (e.g., due to the progressive worsening of stressors that are not addressed).

rpcfIW0.title: Trimethobenzamide
rpcfIW0.description: A benzamide antiemetic drug that inhibits the medullary chemoreceptor trigger zone.

7pc4IW0.title: Calciphylaxis
7pc4IW0.description: A rare, systemic condition caused by reduced blood flow in arterioles due to progressive calcification and fibrosis. Most commonly occurs in patients with end-stage renal disease and manifests with painful, necrotic skin lesions.

HpcKIW0.title: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome
HpcKIW0.description: A neurological condition that typically manifests with altered mental status, seizures, headache, and visual disturbances. Causes include severe hypertension, certain autoimmune diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus), and medications such as immunosuppressants or antineoplastic agents. Characterized by radiological findings of vasogenic edema in subcortical white matter, especially in the posterior cerebral hemispheres. Most patients achieve complete clinical and radiological recovery with early recognition and treatment.

spctIW0.title: Asthma reliever
spctIW0.description: A group of medications with a quick onset of action used for relief of acute asthma exacerbations. Includes short-acting beta agonists and inhaled corticosteroid-formoterol.

tpcXrW0.title: Thyrotoxicosis
tpcXrW0.description: A clinical syndrome caused by increased serum concentrations of circulating thyroid hormones (e.g., due to Graves disease, thyroiditis, exogenous thyroid hormone toxicity). Manifests with weight loss, arrhythmia, tachycardia, muscle weakness, tremor, hyperreflexia, anxiety, and irritability.

8pcOrW0.title: Colorectal stricture
8pcOrW0.description: An abnormal narrowing of the colon or rectum that can obstruct the passage of stool contents. Causes include anastomotic strictures (e.g., following surgery for colorectal cancer), inflammatory bowel disease, malignancy, infections, and radiation therapy. Manifests with bowel obstruction, constipation, diarrhea, and/or tenesmus. Treatment options may include endoscopic balloon dilation and reselction/stricturoplasty.

Epc8rW0.title: Polycarbophil
Epc8rW0.description: A drug used to restore normal moisture levels and bulk to contents of the intestinal tract. Used to treat diarrhea and constipation.

vpcArW0.title: Facilitated positional release
vpcArW0.description: An indirect, passive myofascial release technique in which the spine is placed in a neutral position and a facilitating force (e.g., compression) is applied while moving the dysfunctional region into its direction of ease. The position is held for 3-5 seconds and then relaxed. Used to improve joint function and reduce tissue tension in superficial musculature and deep intervertebral muscles.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Myofascial release techniques

Dpc17W0.title: Colon transit time
Dpc17W0.description: The time required for bowel contents to pass through the colon. Mean colon transit time is 30–40 hours. Can be assessed via serial barium x-rays, capsule endoscopy, or scintigraphy to evaluate patients with idiopathic constipation, diarrhea, and/or malabsorptive disorders.

wpch7W0.title: Ustekinumab
wpch7W0.description: An immune-modulating monoclonal antibody that interferes with the activity of IL-12 and IL-23, which are responsible for natural killer cell activation and CD4+ T-cell differentiation and activation. Used to treat Crohn disease, plaque psoriasis, and psoriatic arthritis.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

9pcN7W0.title: Piriformis syndrome
9pcN7W0.description: A condition caused by entrapment of the sciatic nerve by the piriformis muscle. Manifestations include pain, tingling, and numbness in the buttock and distribution of the sciatic nerve.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Clinical significance

xpcE7W0.title: Lateral femoral circumflex artery
xpcE7W0.description: An artery that arises from the profunda femoris artery (lateral side) and courses down anterior and in the middle of the branches of the femoral nerve. Along with the medial femoral circumflex artery, it supplies the head and neck of the femur. Damage or trauma to this artery can result in avascular necrosis of the femoral head.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Hip joint

Bpcz7W0.title: Pitolisant
Bpcz7W0.description: A histamine H3 receptor antagonist/inverse agonist used to treat excessive daytime sleepiness and reduce cataplexy attacks in patients with narcolepsy.

ypcdHW0.title: Solriamfetol
ypcdHW0.description: A selective dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor used to treat excessive daytime sleepiness (e.g., from narcolepsy or sleep apnea).

-pcDHW0.title: Nimodipine
-pcDHW0.description: A short-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker with a half-life of < 2 hours. Commonly used to prevent secondary vasospasm after subarachnoid hemorrhage.

gJcFtW0.title: Chyluria
gJcFtW0.description: The presence of chyle in the urine, resulting in a cloudy appearance. Most commonly associated with lymphatic filariasis as a result of communication between the lymphatic system and the urinary tract. Other (rare) causes include partial nephrectomy.

3JcSFW0.title: Red flag
3JcSFW0.description: A sign or symptom that potentially indicates a serious pathology or risk of poor outcomes. For example, clinically significant weight loss in a patient with recurrent epigastric pain could indicate malignancy of the upper gastrointestinal tract; acute urinary retention or (overflow) incontinence in a patient with lower back pain could indicate spinal cord compression.

iJcJFW0.title: Eszopiclone
iJcJFW0.description: A nonbenzodiazepine sedative-hypnotic drug that acts as a GABA-A receptor agonist. Used to treat sleep disorders. It is the (S)-enantiomer of zopiclone.

mJcVuW0.title: Low T3 low T4 syndrome
mJcVuW0.description: A subtype of euthyroid sick syndrome characterized by a normal serum TSH concentration and decreased serum free T3 and free T4 concentrations. Typically asymptomatic.

5JciuW0.title: Imiquimod
5JciuW0.description: An immune modifier that is a Toll-like receptor 7 agonist that stimulates an immune response against tumor cells, causing apoptosis. Used topically to treat many dermatologic conditions, including actinic keratoses, superficial basal cell carcinomas, herpes simplex infections, and anogenital warts. Adverse effects include burning pain at application site, dermal rash, pruritus.

LJcwuW0.title: Typical angina
LJcwuW0.description: A condition of cardiac chest pain secondary to myocardial ischemia that meets all of the following characteristics: (1) substernal chest pain of typical quality and duration (e.g., transient retrosternal pain), (2) provoked by exertion or emotional stress, and (3) relieved by rest and/or nitroglycerin.

oJc0EW0.title: Atypical angina
oJc0EW0.description: A type of chest pain that meets 2 out of 3 of the following characteristics of typical angina: (1) substernal chest pain of typical quality and duration (e.g., transient retrosternal pain), (2) provoked by exertion or emotional stress, and (3) relieved by rest and/or nitroglycerin.

KJcUEW0.title: Nonanginal chest pain
KJcUEW0.description: A type of chest pain that meets ≤ 1 of the following criteria: (1) substernal chest pain of typical quality and duration (e.g., transient retrosternal pain), (2) provoked by exertion or emotional stress, and (3) relieved by rest and/or nitroglycerin.

6JcjEW0.title: Cosyntropin
