6JcjEW0.description: An exogenous adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) used in the ACTH stimulation test to confirm adrenal gland dysfunction. Adverse effects include bradycardia or tachycardia, HTN, peripheral edema, and minor irritation at the injection site.

IJcYvW0.title: Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol, revised
IJcYvW0.description: A tool used to assess and guide the management of the patients who are undergoing alcohol withdrawal. Ten features are used for scoring: nausea and vomiting, tremor, paroxysmal sweats, anxiety, agitation, tactile disturbances, auditory disturbances, visual disturbances, headache, orientation. The CIWA-Ar is a revised and reduced version of the CIWA, which included 15 features.

media.title: Clinical institute withdrawal assessment for alcohol (CIWA-Ar)

7Jc4vW0.title: Loeys-Dietz syndrome
7Jc4vW0.description: A connective tissue disorder characterized by marfanoid habitus and increased risk of ascending aortic aneurysms and aortic dissection. Can be distinguished from Marfan syndrome be by the following distinct features: hypertelorism, bifid uvula, cleft palate, easy bruising and keloids, arterial tortuosity (winding course of arteries).

destinations.label: Connective tissue diseases → Inherited connective tissue diseases

HJcKvW0.title: Epidermal growth factor
HJcKvW0.description: A protein that interacts with the tyrosine kinase epidermal growth factor receptor to regulate cell division and differentiation. Excess EGF can result in unregulated cell proliferation.

destinations.label: Basics of embryology → Molecular biology of embryogenesis

sJctvW0.title: Immunofixation
sJctvW0.description: A laboratory technique that uses specific antigens to detect the presence of specific antibodies in the serum or urine. Used in the evaluation of multiple myeloma, Waldenström macroglobulinemia, and other disorders that result in abnormal antibody production.

GJcBvW0.title: Metabolic encephalopathy
GJcBvW0.description: A condition of altered mental status and cerebral dysfunction that is not attributable to an primary underlying brain disease. Examples include encephalopathies induced by electrolyte abnormalities (e.g., hyponatremia, hypocalcemia), hypoglycemia, and hepatic dysfunction.

tJcXDW0.title: Mood disorder questionnaire
tJcXDW0.description: A survey used to assess and monitor for symptoms of bipolar disorder and other mood disorders. Consists of 13 items that are scored either "yes" or "no." Items include having more energy than usual and being more talkative or speaking more quickly than usual.

FJcgDW0.title: Patient Health Questionnaire-9
FJcgDW0.description: A survey used to assess and monitor for symptoms of major depressive disorder. Consists of 9 items that are scored from a scale of 0 (not at all) to 3 (nearly every day).

8JcODW0.title: Thyroid aplasia
8JcODW0.description: A disorder of embryologic development characterized by complete absence of thyroid tissue. Causes congenital hypothyroidism.

uJcpDW0.title: Thyroid dysplasia
uJcpDW0.description: A disorder of embryologic development characterized by abnormal development and/or location of thyroid tissue. Can cause congenital hypothyroidism.

vJcADW0.title: Fractional tissue oxygenation extraction
vJcADW0.description: The ratio of oxygen removed from the blood by tissues during capillary exchange (i.e., amount of oxygen consumed by tissue divided by amount of oxygen delivered to that tissue). Inversely proportional to mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO₂).

DJc1wW0.title: Crush syndrome
DJc1wW0.description: The systemic manifestations that develop from crush injury due to the release of intracellular substances (e.g., myoglobin, potassium) from destroyed muscle cells. Manifestations include compartment syndrome, acute kidney injury, and shock.

wJchwW0.title: Crush injury
wJchwW0.description: A traumatic injury to skeletal muscle caused by a prolonged crushing force (e.g., after being trapped under a collapsed structure). Can result in traumatic muscle breakdown and rhabdomyolysis.

CJcqwW0.title: Rhabdomyolysis
CJcqwW0.description: The breakdown of skeletal muscle tissue caused by either traumatic injury (e.g., crush injury) or nontraumatic injury (e.g., seizures, ischemia). Muscle cell components (e.g., myoglobulin, potassium, phosphate) are released into the blood, which can result in electrolyte imbalances, fluid shifts, and myoglobinuria. Can lead to acute kidney injury.

xJcEwW0.title: Electron transport chain inhibitors
xJcEwW0.description: A group of compounds that block ATP synthesis by reducing the proton gradient in mitochondria, which disrupts oxidative phosphorylation. Examples include rotenone (which inhibits complex I), antimycin (which inhibits complex III), and cyanide, carbon monoxide, and azides (which inhibit complex IV).

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Clinical significance

media.title: Mechanism of action: respiratory chain inhibitors

BJczwW0.title: Respiratory chain inhibitors
BJczwW0.description: A group of compounds that inhibit the function of the electron transport chain (i.e., oxidative phosphorylation) or ATP synthase. Examples include rotenone, antimycin, cyanide, carbon monoxide, azides, and oligomycin.

destinations.label: Electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation → Clinical significance

media.title: Mechanism of action: respiratory chain inhibitors

_Jc59W0.title: Nephronophthisis
_Jc59W0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder characterized by an impaired ability to concentrate the urine as a result of dysfunctional cilia, basal bodies, and/or centrosomes. Typically progresses to end-stage renal disease by 20 years of age.

zJcr9W0.title: Rickettsia conorii
zJcr9W0.description: A gram-negative, obligate intracellular bacterial species typically transmitted by ticks. Can cause several diseases, including Mediterranean spotted fever.

-JcD9W0.title: Enteropathic arthritis
-JcD9W0.description: A seronegative spondyloarthropathy that develops in association with inflammatory bowel disease. Typically affects joints of the lower extremities but can involve the spine.

ZqcZCW0.title: Macrophage activation syndrome
ZqcZCW0.description: A type of potentially life-threatening hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis that occurs secondary to rheumatologic conditions (e.g., adult-onset Still disease, Kawasaki disease). Systemic hyperinflammation manifests with persistent fever, splenomegaly, rash, and/or altered mental status. Laboratory findings include cytopenias, coagulopathy, elevated ferritin level, abnormal liver chemistries, and hypertriglyceridemia.

0qceCW0.title: Occult gastrointestinal bleeding
0qceCW0.description: Gastrointestinal bleeding that is not visible. Can be diagnosed by fecal occult blood test.

destinations.label: Gastrointestinal bleeding → Low risk GI bleeding

aqcQCW0.title: Overt gastrointestinal bleeding
aqcQCW0.description: Gastrointestinal bleeding that is visible in the form of hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia. Severe bleeding may be accompanied by other symptoms, e.g., hypotension, tachycardia.

YqcnCW0.title: Ocular sarcoidosis
YqcnCW0.description: A complication of sarcoidosis that can involve the several parts of the eye, including orbit, anterior and posterior segments of the eye, conjunctivae, lacrimal glands, and extraocular muscles. Can cause many symptoms, including dry eye, blurry vision, photophobia, eye redness, and pain.

bqcHCW0.title: Neurosarcoidosis
bqcHCW0.description: A complication of sarcoidosis characterized by neurologic findings, including cranial mononeuropathies (e..g, CN VII dysfunction), neuroendocrine dysfunction (e.g., diabetes insipidus, hypopituitarism), encephalopathy, peripheral neuropathy, and myopathy.

Xqc9CW0.title: Urine osmolality
Xqc9CW0.description: A measure of urine concentration defined as the amount of osmotically-active particles dissolved per kilogram of urine. An increased urine osmolality indicates concentrated urine (e.g., due to dehydration). A decreased urine osmolality indicates dilute urine (e.g., due to diabetes insipidus).

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

cqcaxW0.title: Urine culture
cqcaxW0.description: A test to detect bacteria in the urine by applying a urine sample to a culture plate, which provides nutrients for bacteria to grow. Can be used to determine bacterial species and patterns of antibiotic resistance.

VqcGxW0.title: Cannot intubate-cannot ventilate
VqcGxW0.description: The inability to intubate the trachea in addition to the inability to ventilate or oxygenate with bag-mask ventilation or a supraglottic airway device.

eqcxxW0.title: Cricothyroid ligament
eqcxxW0.description: A fibroelastic membrane consisting of three parts: a thickened median part and right and left lateral parts. It connects the cricoid cartilage to the thyroid cartilage. The upper edges of the lateral part of the conus elasticus form the vocal ligaments. It is the location of incision for cricothyrotomy.

media.title: Ultrasound identification of the cricothyroid membrane

2qcTBW0.title: Telescoping fingers
2qcTBW0.description: A deformity of the hand caused by bone resorption and/or osteolysis and soft tissue collapse in the fingers. Results in shortening of the fingers and loose skin. It is a characteristic feature of arthritis mutilans.

fqckBW0.title: Ventilator weaning
fqckBW0.description: The process of easing a patient off of mechanical ventilatory support. Includes decreasing support (e.g., pressure support) and the fraction of inspired oxygen.

Tqc6BW0.title: Myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome
Tqc6BW0.description: A multisystem condition characterized by severe fatigue that is not improved by rest, postexertional malaise, and unrefreshing sleep. The exact cause is unknown, but possible factors include genetic predisposition, infections, and immune abnormalities.

gqcFBW0.title: Arthritis mutilans
gqcFBW0.description: A rare severe and destructive form of arthritis that causes bone resorption and/or osteolysis, with subsequent collapse of the soft tissue of the affected area (e.g., hands, feet). Etiologies include psoriatic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and less commonly, gout.

SqcyBW0.title: Sedative-hypnotic drugs
SqcyBW0.description: A class of drugs that inhibit the CNS function and are able to reduce anxiety and/or induce sleep. An increase in dose increases the degree of CNS inhibition, ranging from sedation to coma. Drugs in this class include benzodiazepines and Z-drugs, barbiturates, and melatonin agonists.

3qcSyW0.title: Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome
3qcSyW0.description: A systemic inflammatory reaction caused by superantigens (TSST-1 and staphylococcal enterotoxins) produced by Staphylococcus aureus. Classically associated with prolonged tampon placement and postsurgical wounds. Manifestations include fever, a desquamating rash, myalgia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, altered mental status, features of shock, and thrombocytopenia.

RqclyW0.title: Lissencephaly
RqclyW0.description: A congenital malformation characterized by the underdevelopment of gyri and sulci in the brain due to a failure of neuronal cell migration. Associated defects include microcephaly, ventriculomegaly, and craniofacial abnormalities.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Embryology of the brain

iqcJyW0.title: Prehepatic jaundice
iqcJyW0.description: A type of jaundice caused by the accumulation of unconjugated bilirubin, which is due to either increased hemoglobin breakdown or impaired hepatic uptake.

QqcuyW0.title: Extrahepatic jaundice
QqcuyW0.description: A type of jaundice caused by the accumulation of bilirubin due to extrahepatic biliary duct obstruction. Etiologies include choledocolithiasis and pancreatic cancer.

jqc_yW0.title: Serum osmolality
jqc_yW0.description: The concentration of different solute particles (osmoles) in the serum, expressed in mOsm/kg. Sometimes used synonymously with serum osmolarity. Serum osmolality can be measured using an osmometer (normal range is 275-295 mOsm/kg) or estimated by calculating the serum osmolarity (in mOsm/L): 2 × (serum sodium concentration in mEq/L) + (serum glucose concentration in mg/dL)/18 + (serum urea concentration in mg/dL)/2.8.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function

PqcWAW0.title: Brain fog
PqcWAW0.description: A collection of cognitive disturbances caused by multiple conditions (e.g., fibromyalgia, anxiety disorders, chronic fatigue syndrome). Manifestations include anterograde amnesia, retrograde amnesia, and difficulty concentrating.

4qc3AW0.title: Widespread pain index
4qc3AW0.description: A screening tool used to assess pain symptoms (e.g., for the evaluation of fibromyalgia). Patients indicate whether they have pain or tenderness in 19 different regions of the body, including the shoulder girdles, extremities, jaw, chest, shoulder, and neck, and back. Score range is 0-19 (1 point per region).

kqcmAW0.title: Aarskog-Scott syndrome
kqcmAW0.description: A hereditary disorder with manifestations that include characteristic facial features (e.g., hypertelorism, a small nose, a long philtrum, a widow's peak hairline), short stature in childhood, and hand abnormalities (e.g., brachydactyly, syndactyly, single palmar crease).

OqcIAW0.title: Cohen syndrome
OqcIAW0.description: A hereditary disorder with manifestations that include hypotonia, microcephaly, developmental delay, characteristic facial features (e.g., a low hairline, arched eyelids, thick eyelashes and eyebrows, and a high palate), and vision problems (e.g., myopia, strabismus, decreased visual acuity).

lqcvAW0.title: C-terminal telopeptide
lqcvAW0.description: A degradation production of type I collagen that is used as a marker of bone turnover. Increased serum concentrations of C-terminal telopeptide indicate increased bone turnover (e.g., in patients with osteoporosis). Can be monitored to assess response to antiresorptive therapies (e.g., bisphosphonates).

5qci_W0.title: Lower respiratory tract infection
5qci_W0.description: An infection involving the lower respiratory tract (i.e., the bronchi, bronchioles, and/or lung parenchyma). Examples include pneumonia, bronchitis, and bronchiolitis.

MqcM_W0.title: hrHPV genotyping
MqcM_W0.description: A study that detects high-risk human papillomavirus types (e.g., genotyping via polymerase chain reaction). Used in cervical cancer screening and anal cancer screening.

KqcUzW0.title: Pituitary microadenoma
KqcUzW0.description: A benign tumor of the pituitary gland with a diameter < 10 mm.

6qcjzW0.title: Pituitary macroadenoma
6qcjzW0.description: A benign tumor of the pituitary gland with a diameter ≥ 10 mm.

pqcLzW0.title: Macroprolactinoma
pqcLzW0.description: A benign, prolactin-producing tumor with a diameter ≥ 10 mm. Often causes mass effect (e.g., headache, bitemporal hemianopsia, diplopia) and effects of hyperprolactinemia.

JqcszW0.title: Preconception counseling
JqcszW0.description: A form of medical counseling provided to a woman who is planning to conceive. Aimed at reducing adverse health effects for the woman and her (future) child by educating her about healthy lifestyle choices and addressing modifiable risk factors.

qqcCzW0.title: Nivolumab
qqcCzW0.description: An immune checkpoint inhibitor and monoclonal antibody that is used, alone or with ipilimumab, for the treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer with deficient mismatch repair, renal cell carcinoma, melanoma, and other cancers.

IqcY-W0.title: Pembrolizumab
IqcY-W0.description: An immune checkpoint inhibitor and monoclonal antibody against programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) that is used in the treatment of unresectable and/or metastatic solid tumors with genetic anomalies such as mismatch repair deficiency and microsatellite instability. Results in an antitumor T-cell response.

rqcf-W0.title: Ipilimumab
rqcf-W0.description: A monoclonal antibody that is used in combination with nivolumab for the treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer with deficient mismatch repair or high microsatellite instability. It is also used to treat melanoma and renal cell carcinoma. It activates the immune system by targeting CTLA-4 which downregulates T-cell activation pathways.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

7qc4-W0.title: Noninsulinoma pancreatogenous hypoglycemia
7qc4-W0.description: A rare type of recurrent hypoglycemia caused by pancreatic lesions that is characterized by diffuse islet involvement (nesidioblastosis), islet hypertrophy, hyperplasia, and enlarged and hyperchromatic β-cell nuclei.

HqcK-W0.title: Nonislet cell tumor hypoglycemia
HqcK-W0.description: A paraneoplastic syndrome associated with nonislet cell tumors and characterized by episodic hypoglycemia. Most commonly seen with tumors of mesenchymal or epithelial origin. Most often caused by overproduction of insulin-like growth factor 2. Can also be caused by replacement of hepatic tissue by tumor and production of autoantibodies against insulin or its receptor.

GqcB-W0.title: Intraembryonic coelom
GqcB-W0.description: A cavity formed during embryogenesis as a result of ventral outgrowth of the lateral margins of the germinal disc and convergence of the ectoderm and overlying lateral plate mesoderm.

8qcOZd0.title: Corrected serum sodium concentration for hyperglycemia
8qcOZd0.description: A formula used to calculate the actual serum sodium concentration in patients with hyperglycemia (which causes dilutional hyponatremia due to movement of water from the intracellular to the extracellular space). The Katz formula is: corrected sodium concentration = measured sodium concentration + 0.016 × (serum glucose concentration - 100). The Hillier formula is: corrected sodium concentration = measured sodium concentration + 0.024 × (serum glucose concentration - 100).

uqcpZd0.title: Jump sign (myofascial pain syndrome)
uqcpZd0.description: A physical examination finding characterized by an involuntary, sudden jerk or wince in response to stimulation of a tender area or trigger point.

Eqc8Zd0.title: Hungry bone syndrome
Eqc8Zd0.description: A complication of parathyroidectomy characterized by severe hypocalcemia despite a normal or increased serum concentration of parathyroid hormone. In addition to hypocalcemia, patients can also develop hypophosphatemia, hypomagnesemia, and hyperkalemia.

vqcAZd0.title: Glomerular hematuria
vqcAZd0.description: Red blood cells in the urine resulting from damage to the glomeruli (e.g., glomerulonephritis). Typically manifests with urine of normal appearance that shows dysmorphic red blood cells (e.g., acanthocytes) and red blood cell casts on urinalysis.

Dqc10d0.title: Nonglomerular hematuria
Dqc10d0.description: Red blood cells in the urine resulting from urothelial damage (e.g., nephrolithiasis, malignancy, cystitis, trauma), or tubulointerstitial damage (e.g., renal papillary necrosis, or interstitial nephritis). Typically manifests with red or pink urine and sometimes with clots. Red blood cells appear normal on urinalysis.

wqch0d0.title: Safe triangle
wqch0d0.description: An area of the chest formed anteriorly by the lateral border of pectoralis major, laterally by the lateral border of latissimus dorsi, inferiorly by the line of the 5th intercostal space, and superiorly by the base of the axilla. Used as a site for chest tube insertion to minimize the risk of damage to vessels and muscle tissue.

destinations.label: Chest tube placement → Landmarks and positioning

Cqcq0d0.title: Aortic area
Cqcq0d0.description: An area at the right 2nd intercostal space, along the parasternal line, at which aortic valve murmurs are best auscultated.

media.title: Anatomical locations and auscultatory sites for heart valves

xqcE0d0.title: Pulmonic area
xqcE0d0.description: An area at the left 2nd intercostal space, along the parasternal line, at which pulmonary valve murmurs are best auscultated.

media.title: Auscultatory sites of the heart valves

Bqcz0d0.title: Tricuspid area
Bqcz0d0.description: An area at the left 4th intercostal space, along the parasternal line, at which tricuspid valve murmurs are best auscultated.

media.title: Anatomical locations and auscultatory sites for heart valves

yqcdad0.title: Mitral area
yqcdad0.description: An area at the left 5th intercostal space in the midclavicular line (over the cardiac apex), at which mitral valve murmurs are best auscultated.

media.title: Anatomical locations and auscultatory sites for heart valves

AqcRad0.title: Patient Health Questionnaire-2
AqcRad0.description: A survey used to assess the presence of depressed mood and loss of interest or pleasure in routine activities over the last two weeks. It contains only the first two questions from the Patient Health Questionnaire-9.

_qc5ad0.title: Beck Depression Inventory
_qc5ad0.description: A 21-question, multiple-choice, self-reported inventory used to measure the severity of depression. Items assessed include mood, guilt, interest in activities, and sleep.

-qcDad0.title: Transvestic disorder
-qcDad0.description: A paraphilic disorder characterized by persistent and intense sexual arousal derived from fantasies, urges, and/or behaviors related to dressing in clothes typically associated with the opposite sex. In contrast to transvestism, these features must cause clinically significant distress and/or impairment.

destinations.label: Sexual dysfunction and paraphilic disorders → Paraphilic disorders

ZIcZYd0.title: Sexual aversion disorder
ZIcZYd0.description: A disorder previously identified in the DSM-4 (and no longer listed in the DSM-5); previously defined as a persistent aversion to genital sexual contact with a sexual partner that results in clinically significant distress and/or impairment.

0IceYd0.title: Blumer shelf
0IceYd0.description: A mass in the rectouterine pouch that develops as a result of peritoneal spread of gastric cancer.

aIcQYd0.title: Fetishistic disorder
aIcQYd0.description: A persistent and intense sexual arousal and fixation related to nonliving objects (e.g., shoes) or nongenital parts of the body (e.g., feet, hair). Does not include sexual arousal limited to sex toys and/or clothing used for cross-dressing (e.g., as part of transvestic disorder). Must cause clinically significant distress and/or impairment.

destinations.label: Sexual dysfunction and paraphilic disorders → Paraphilic disorders

YIcnYd0.title: Widow spiders
YIcnYd0.description: A genus of venomous spiders whose bite results in latrodectism. Most species within this genus have a shiny black body with red markings.

bIcHYd0.title: Gender nonconformity
bIcHYd0.description: The behavior of gender expression that does not match the typical social norms of an individual's stereotypical gender role. In contrast to gender dysphoria, these behaviors do not cause clinically significant distress and/or impairment.

XIc9Yd0.title: Suicide attempt
XIc9Yd0.description: A self-directed, injurious behavior carried out with an intent to end one's own life that does not result in a fatal outcome.

WIcPbd0.title: Ammonium chloride
WIcPbd0.description: A drug used in the treatment of hypochloremia and/or metabolic alkalosis. Increases free hydrogen ion concentrations. Also used as an expectorant because it stimulates the production of respiratory tract fluid.

dIcobd0.title: Weighted vaginal cone
dIcobd0.description: A device used as part of pelvic floor muscle training for stress urinary incontinence. Can be inserted into the vagina and held in place by contracting the pelvic floor.

eIcxbd0.title: C3 nephritic factor
eIcxbd0.description: An autoantibody against C3 convertase, an enzyme used in the alternative pathway of complement activation. Patients with C3 nephritic factor typically develop membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis during childhood.

UIcbXd0.title: Reverse Barton fracture
UIcbXd0.description: An intra-articular fracture of the distal radius with associated volar displacement.

fIckXd0.title: Thyroid lobectomy
fIckXd0.description: The surgical removal of one thyroid lobe. In contrast to a hemithyroidectomy, this procedure leaves the isthmus intact.

TIc6Xd0.title: Excessive drinking
TIc6Xd0.description: A pattern of alcohol use defined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Its criteria include binge drinking, heavy drinking, any alcohol use in pregnant women or individuals under 21 years of age.

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Classifications of alcohol use

gIcFXd0.title: Binge drinking
gIcFXd0.description: A pattern of alcohol use defined by the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism as capable of raising a person’s blood alcohol concentration to ≥ 0.08%. On average, it requires the consumption of ≥ 4 standard drinks in women and ≥ 5 standard drinks in men across a 2-hour period.

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Classifications of alcohol use

SIcyXd0.title: Standard alcoholic drink
SIcyXd0.description: An alcoholic drink that contains 14.0 grams (0.6 ounces) of pure alcohol. Common standard drinks include 12 fluid ounces of 5% alcohol beer, 5 fluid ounces of 12% alcohol wine, and 1.5 fluid ounces of 40% alcohol (80 proof) liquor.

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Classifications of alcohol use

3IcScd0.title: Marginal artery of Drummond
3IcScd0.description: An anastomotic network between the terminal branches of the superior mesenteric artery and inferior mesenteric artery. Extends from the ileocecal junction to the rectosigmoid junction. Provides collateral blood supply to the colon in the event of an occlusion.

RIclcd0.title: Cisgender
RIclcd0.description: A gender identity characterized by the correspondence between an individual's gender identity and their sex assigned at birth.

QIcucd0.title: Transsexual
QIcucd0.description: The historical term for “transgender” or “intersex.” Generally considered stigmatizing today. Sometimes used in literature when referring to transgender individuals who are undergoing or have undergone gender transitioning.

PIcW1d0.title: E-cigarette or vaping product use associated lung injury
PIcW1d0.description: A spectrum of lung injuries associated with e-cigarette use and vaping. Can be self-limited or progress to life-threatening acute respiratory failure. Manifestations include dyspnea, cough, and chest pain. The exact pathophysiology has not yet been identified.

4Ic31d0.title: Teratogenic drugs
4Ic31d0.description: A group of drugs that can cause harm to the developing fetus (e.g., defects in organogenesis, growth retardation, functional deficits). Examples include tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, ACE inhibitors, and warfarin.

OIcI1d0.title: Hepatitis A vaccine
OIcI1d0.description: A vaccine against hepatitis A virus. Available as a single-antigen inactivated hepatitis A vaccine or as a combination inactivated vaccine against hepatitis A and hepatitis B. Recommended as a routine vaccination for children 12-23 months of age and as a catch-up vaccination for individuals 2 years of age or older.

NIc-1d0.title: Meningococcal B vaccine
NIc-1d0.description: An inactivated, monovalent, recombinant protein vaccine against Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B. Recommended for individuals > 10 years of age who are at increased risk for meningococcal infections (e.g., patients with asplenia or complement deficiencies).

mIcVWd0.title: Measles, mumps, rubella vaccine
mIcVWd0.description: A live attenuated vaccine that protects against measles, mumps, and rubella. It is part of the immunization schedule of children in the United States and is given in 2 doses: one between 12-15 months of age and the second between 4-6 years of age.

MIcMWd0.title: Yellow fever vaccine
MIcMWd0.description: A live attenuated vaccine that is recommended for primary prophylaxis against yellow fever in individuals ≥ 9 months of age and traveling to endemic regions (e.g., South America, Africa).

nIc7Wd0.title: Rabies vaccine
nIc7Wd0.description: An inactivated vaccine against the rabies virus. Used for preexposure prophylaxis in individuals at high risk of rabies (e.g., veterinarians, travelers to endemic areas) and for postexposure prophylaxis following suspected or confirmed rabies exposure.

oIc0dd0.title: Decarboxylating malate dehydrogenase
oIc0dd0.description: An enzyme that converts malate and NAD+ into pyruvate and NADPH.

KIcUdd0.title: Vulval vestibule
KIcUdd0.description: A part of the vulva into which the urethra, vagina, Bartholin glands, and Skene ducts open.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Vagina and vulva

pIcLdd0.title: Calabar swelling
pIcLdd0.description: A localized and transient subcutaneous swelling seen in patients with loiasis. Common locations include the face and extremities. May be preceded by localized pain and/or itch. Thought to be caused by a hypersensitivity reaction to microfilariae.

JIcsdd0.title: Skin snip biopsy
JIcsdd0.description: A punch biopsy of the skin to detect and quantify Onchocerca volvulus microfilariae. The tissue is incubated in normal saline for 24 hours to facilitate the release of the microfilariae (larvae), which are then detected by microscopic examination.

qIcCdd0.title: CHD
qIcCdd0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Coronary heart disease
2. Congenital heart defect
3. Common hepatic duct

IIcYVd0.title: Mazzotti test
IIcYVd0.description: A test used to evaluate for onchocerciasis. Diethylcarbamazine, which inhibits nematode neuromuscular transmission, is administered. A positive result is characterized by the development of symptoms (e.g., pruritus, ocular symptoms, and constitutional symptoms) as a result of the inflammatory response to dying microfilariae.

HIcKVd0.title: Enzyme-linked immunoelectrotransfer blot
HIcKVd0.description: A technique that uses sodium dodecyl sulfate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to study antigen–antibody pairs. Used for the diagnosis of neurocysticercosis.

sIctVd0.title: Loa loa
sIctVd0.description: A filarial nematode transmitted by the bite of a deer fly, horsefly or mango fly. Causes loiasis when larvae mature into adult worms in subcutaneous tissue and produce microfilariae, which are then released into the circulation.

GIcBVd0.title: Osteoporosis risk factors
GIcBVd0.description: The risk factors for osteoporosis include postmenopausal state, advanced age, chronic use of corticosteroids and proton pump inhibitors, endocrine disease (e.g., hypercortisolism, hypogonadism, hyperthyroidism, hyperparathyroidism), chronic kidney disease, immobilization, and lifestyle factors such as alcohol abuse, smoking, and malnutrition/low BMI.

tIcXed0.title: Follicular cysts of the ovary
tIcXed0.description: A type of benign and functional ovarian cyst that develops when a Graafian follicle continues to grow rather than rupture and release an egg (i.e., it fails to ovulate). It is the most common cause of an ovarian mass in young women of reproductive age and associated with hyperestrogenism and endometrial hyperplasia.

FIcged0.title: Hollenhorst plaque
FIcged0.description: A retinal lesion caused by cholesterol crystal embolization, most commonly from the carotid artery. Appears as a bright yellow, refractile lesion on ophthalmoscopy. Patients may be asymptomatic or present with ocular symptoms, e.g., amaurosis fugax.

destinations.label: Diseases of the retina → Other retinal disorders

media.title: Hollenhorst plaque causing branch retinal artery occlusion (BRAO)

8IcOed0.title: Radicular pain
8IcOed0.description: A condition of pain that follows a dermatomal distribution of a nerve due to an inflamed and/or compressed nerve root.

uIcped0.title: Ixazomib
uIcped0.description: A proteasome inhibitor that arrests cell growth at the G2-M phase and causes apoptosis. Often used in the treatment of multiple myeloma. Adverse effects include peripheral neuropathy, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, and herpes zoster reactivation.

EIc8ed0.title: Legionella urinary antigen test
EIc8ed0.description: A rapid urinary test used to diagnose Legionella pneumophila pneumonia. Very sensitive (70-100%) and specific (95-100%) for L. pneumophila serogroup 1, but does not detect other serotypes.

vIcAed0.title: S. pneumoniae urinary antigen test
vIcAed0.description: A rapid urinary test used to diagnose S. pneumoniae infection. Sensitivity has been reported to be around 50–80% and specificity >90%.

DIc1Ud0.title: Pattern recognition receptor
DIc1Ud0.description: A receptor that is specific for molecular components of foreign microorganisms. PRRs may be secreted into the circulation or function as transmembrane or intracellular receptors. Examples include Toll-like receptors and NOD-like receptors.

wIchUd0.title: Major histocompatibility complex
wIchUd0.description: A group of transmembrane proteins encoded by HLA genes that present antigen fragments to T cells and bind T-cell receptors. Can be further subdivided into MHC I and MHC II.

xIcEUd0.title: T cell-dependent activation of B cells
xIcEUd0.description: A process by which T helper cells activate B cells. Antigen-presenting cells bind, process, and present peptide antigens via MHC class II receptors to activate T helper cells. Activated Th2 cells release cytokines to facilitate immunoglobulin class switching and differentiation of primed B cells into plasma cells that produce IgA, IgE, or IgG.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

BIczUd0.title: T cell-independent activation of B cells
BIczUd0.description: A rapid and nonspecific B cell response to nonpeptide antigens that does not require T helper cells. Polysaccharide, lipid, and lipopolysaccharide antigens activate B cells and induce IgM production (without class switch recombination). Responses are generally short-lived; does not produce memory B cells.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → B cells (B lymphocytes)

yIcd2d0.title: Colon transit studies
yIcd2d0.description: A collection of studies used to evaluate colonic motility (i.e., the duration of time required for gastrointestinal contents to pass through the colon). Examples include colon transit scintigraphy, wireless motility capsule tests, and the use of radio-opaque markers.

media.title: Colon transit test with radiopaque markers

AIcR2d0.title: Colon transit scintigraphy
AIcR2d0.description: A nuclear medicine test to assess for delayed colonic transit. The patient is given a meal containing radioisotopes (99m-technetium or 111-indium). A gamma camera is used to detect and follow the leading edge of the radioisotope, which is the distal-most part of the bowel where the radio-isotope is detected.

_Ic52d0.title: Wireless motility capsule test
_Ic52d0.description: A test used to assess gastric emptying time, small bowel transit time, and colon transit time. A wireless capsule with sensors for temperature, pH, and pressure is ingested; the time elapsed until expulsion of the capsule is noted. pH sensors detect the differences in pH levels in the various bowel segments.

zIcr2d0.title: Asparagine
zIcr2d0.description: A non-essential, glucogenic amino acid. Can be synthesized by asparagine synthetase from aspartate with the transfer of an amino group from glutamine. Can be deaminated to form aspartate and then oxaloacetate.

-IcD2d0.title: Glutamine
-IcD2d0.description: A non-essential, glucogenic amino acid. Can be formed by glutamine synthetase by the attachment of free ammonia to glutamate (i.e., the glutamine cycle).

ZrcZfd0.title: Steroid stress dosing
ZrcZfd0.description: An increased glucocorticoid dosage that is required perioperatively and in cases of severe infection/critical illness to meet increased demands during times of high stress and to prevent adrenal crisis.

0rcefd0.title: Pedigree analysis
0rcefd0.description: A genetic depiction of a family history, with special emphasis on particular phenotypic traits and their inheritance.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Pedigree analysis

Yrcnfd0.title: Chromosomal mosaicism
Yrcnfd0.description: A phenomenon in which cell populations with different karyotypes (i.e., different chromosomal content) are present in the same individual.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

brcHfd0.title: Imidazotetrazines
brcHfd0.description: Imidazotetrazines are the class of DNA-alkylating agents. Temozolomide is the only drug in this class approved for the treatment of glioblastoma multiforme.

Xrc9fd0.title: Nitrosourea
Xrc9fd0.description: A class of chemotherapeutic agents that alkylates DNA. Examples include carmustine and lomustine. Can cause pulmonary toxicity.

crcaTd0.title: Carmustine
crcaTd0.description: An alkylating chemotherapeutic agent of the nitrosourea class typically used in the treatment of brain cancers, multiple myeloma, and lymphomas. Common adverse effects include neurotoxicity and pulmonary toxicity.

1rc2Td0.title: Lomustine
1rc2Td0.description: An alkylating chemotherapeutic agent from nitrosourea class typically used in the treatment of brain cancers and Hodgkin lymphoma. Common adverse effects include myelosuppression, neurotoxicity, and pulmonary toxicity.

media.title: Wrong base pairing due to alkylation

WrcPTd0.title: Alkyl sulfonate
WrcPTd0.description: A class of chemotherapeutic agents derived from alkane sulfonic acids that act through alkylation of DNA. Busulfan belongs to this class of drugs.

drcoTd0.title: Hydrazines
drcoTd0.description: A class of chemotherapeutic agents derived from hydrazine that functions by alkylation of DNA. Procarbazine is a member of this class.

VrcGTd0.title: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor
VrcGTd0.description: An ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor characterized by androgen-producing testicular structures. Primarily affects women 30-40 years of age and manifests with virilization and an abdominal mass.

destinations.label: Overview of ovarian tumors →  Sex cord-stromal tumors of the ovary

ercxTd0.title: Pelvic exenteration
ercxTd0.description: A radical procedure that involves an en bloc resection of the uterus, ovaries, fallopian tubes, and vagina in women and the prostate and seminal vesicles in men; along with a portion of the rectosigmoid, lower urinary tract (bladder, portion of the urethra), and pelvic lymph nodes. Followed by urinary and bowel diversions or anastomoses. Performed with curative or palliative intent for locally advanced pelvic cancers (e.g., cervical cancer, prostate cancer, rectal cancer). Associated with high (∼ 10%) mortality.

2rcTgd0.title: Metolazone
2rcTgd0.description: A thiazide-like diuretic that inhibits sodium reabsorption in the distal tubules of the nephron, which results in increased excretion of water and sodium. Can cause hypokalemia, hypercalcemia, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis, and hypomagnesemia.

Trc6gd0.title: Apathy
Trc6gd0.description: A lack of emotion or concern, especially with regards to matters that are normally considered important.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Appearance and behavior

ircJSd0.title: Pseudovaginal perineoscrotal hypospadias
ircJSd0.description: A type of 5-alpha reductase deficiency characterized by the presence of hypospadias, micropenis, and an incompletely closed urogenital opening that resembles a vagina in karyotypically normal males (46, XY).

QrcuSd0.title: SSI
QrcuSd0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Sliding scale insulin
2. Surgical site infection

jrc_Sd0.title: Mucosal neuroma
jrc_Sd0.description: A peripheral nerve tumor of mucosal tissue that most commonly develops on the lips and/or tongue. Associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia 2B.

PrcWhd0.title: COPD assessment test
PrcWhd0.description: A questionnaire used to quantify health status impairment in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Patients rate the following symptoms on a scale from 0 (best) to 5 (worst): cough, phlegm production, chest tightness, breathlessness walking uphill, limitation of daily activities at home, limitation of activities outside the home, quality of sleep, and level of energy.

4rc3hd0.title: Modified Medical Research Council dyspnea scale
4rc3hd0.description: An assessment tool used to evaluate the extent of a patient's functional disability caused by dyspnea (e.g., secondary to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Its scale ranges from 0 (dyspnea only with strenuous exercise) to 4 (too dyspneic to leave the house or breathless when dressing).

krcmhd0.title: Hepatitis D virus infection
krcmhd0.description: A liver infection caused by hepatitis D virus and spread via sexual, parenteral, and perinatal contact. Only develops in patients who are infected with hepatitis B virus; hepatitis D virus uses the HBsAg coat of hepatitis B to propagate. Can cause acute or chronic infection.

destinations.label: Overview of viral hepatitides → Hepatitis D

OrcIhd0.title: Blood pH
OrcIhd0.description: The degree of acidity or alkalinity of the blood. Typical blood pH is between 7.35-7.45. Acidemia is defined as pH < 7.35; alkalemia is defined as pH > 7.45.

lrcvhd0.title: Acute CINV
lrcvhd0.description: The occurrence of nausea and/or vomiting within 24 hours of the initiation of chemotherapy. 5-HT3 receptor antagonists (e.g., ondansetron) are the preferred antiemetic treatment because peripheral serotonin pathways are primarily responsible for acute CINV.

destinations.label: Complications of cancer therapy → Gastrointestinal complications

Nrc-hd0.title: Delayed CINV
Nrc-hd0.description: The onset of nausea and/or vomiting 24 to 120 hours after chemotherapy. Neurokinin receptor antagonists (e.g., aprepitant) are the preferred antiemetic treatment because delayed CINV is primarily initiated in a central pathway containing the substance P neurotransmitter.

destinations.label: Complications of cancer therapy → Gastrointestinal complications

mrcV3d0.title: Anticipatory CINV
mrcV3d0.description: The occurrence of nausea and/or vomiting prior to chemotherapy as a conditioned response following nausea or vomiting with previous chemotherapy. Preventive measures include providing patients with information about the condition, an appropriate antiemetic regimen, and anxiolytic agents (e.g., lorazepam).

destinations.label: Complications of cancer therapy → Gastrointestinal complications

5rci3d0.title: Breakthrough CINV
5rci3d0.description: The onset of nausea and/or vomiting within five days of receiving chemotherapy despite the use of standard antiemetic prophylaxis.

destinations.label: Complications of cancer therapy → Gastrointestinal complications

MrcM3d0.title: Refractory CINV
MrcM3d0.description: The onset of nausea and/or vomiting in patients with a history of CINV that did not respond to prophylactic and rescue antiemetic therapy during previous chemotherapy.

destinations.label: Complications of cancer therapy → Gastrointestinal complications

Lrcw3d0.title: Hypotonic hyponatremia
Lrcw3d0.description: Hyponatremia with a low serum osmolality (< 280 mOsm). Often referred to as "true hyponatremia." Can be further classified into hypovolemic, euvolemic, or hypervolemic hypotonic hyponatremia based on the patient's volume status.

orc0Rd0.title: Isotonic hyponatremia
orc0Rd0.description: Hyponatremia with a normal serum osmolality (280–295 mOsm). Causes include post-TURP syndrome and laboratory artifact (i.e., pseudohypotremia).

KrcURd0.title: Hypertonic hyponatremia
KrcURd0.description: Hyponatremia with a high serum osmolality (> 295 mOsm). Osmotically active solutes in the plasma (e.g., hyperglycemia) lead to fluid shifts from the intracellular space into the extracellular space, resulting in dilutional hyponatremia.

6rcjRd0.title: Pancytosis
6rcjRd0.description: A concurrent increase in all three blood cell lines (i.e., polycythemia, leukocytosis, and thrombocytosis)

IrcYid0.title: Exercise-induced hematuria
IrcYid0.description: A condition of self-limited gross or microscopic hematuria that occurs following strenuous exercise.

7rc4id0.title: Irritant contact dermatitis
7rc4id0.description: A form of contact dermatitis caused by direct cytotoxic insult to the skin and a subsequent inflammatory response. May be triggered by chemical, mechanical, and/or physical irritants (e.g., detergents, acids and alkalis, metals). Typically manifests acutely (i.e., within seconds to hours after exposure to an irritant) with pain, stinging, pruritus, erythematous skin with vesicles, and edema. Can progress to chronic irritant contact dermatitis, with scaling, lichenification, hyperkeratosis, and fissuring.

destinations.label: Occupational skin diseases → Irritant contact dermatitis

HrcKid0.title: Exanthematous drug eruption
HrcKid0.description: A type IV hypersensitivity reaction that most commonly develops 5-14 days after receiving an offending drug (most commonly antibiotics). Typically manifests with erythematous macules and papules on the trunk and proximal extremities that resolve after discontinuation of the offending drug. Associated symptoms include pruritus and low-grade fever.

destinations.label: Hypersensitivity reactions → Type IV hypersensitivity reaction

GrcBid0.title: Growth stunting
GrcBid0.description: A growth rate below the corresponding growth velocity for age and sex that results from chronic malnutrition. Defined as z score below 2 standard deviations in height-for-age charts; weight may be proportional for height.

trcXQd0.title: Cannabinoid receptor
trcXQd0.description: A G-protein coupled receptor and part of the endocannabinoid system. Endocannabinoids and exogenous cannabinoids (e.g., tetrahydrocannabinol, dronabinol, nabinol) bind to and stimulate these receptors. CB1 receptors are mainly located in the central and peripheral nervous system. CB2 receptors are mainly located in the gastrointestinal tract, inflammatory cells, and platelets.

FrcgQd0.title: Sodium-chloride cotransporter
FrcgQd0.description: A protein on the apical surface of the distal convoluted tubule that reabsorbs sodium and chloride ions. Encoded by the SLC12A3 gene on chromosome 16q. Inhibited by thiazide diuretics. A loss of function of this protein causes Gitelman syndrome.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Urine production

8rcOQd0.title: Segmented RNA virus
8rcOQd0.description: An RNA virus with a segmented genome (e.g., influenza virus, rotavirus). This property facilitates the exchange of genome segments between different virus strains during coinfection of a single host cell (i.e., viral reassortment).

vrcAQd0.title: Ovarian cystadenocarcinoma
vrcAQd0.description: A malignant ovarian tumor of epithelial origin. Can be serous (most common ovarian malignant neoplasm) or mucinous. Typically manifests with an adnexal mass that causes abdominal distension, pain, and urinary symptoms. Has psammoma bodies on histopathologic examination.

destinations.label: Overview of ovarian tumors →  Epithelial ovarian tumors

Drc1jd0.title: Triple screen test
Drc1jd0.description: A prenatal screening test performed at 15–22 weeks' gestation that includes the measurement of β-HCG, alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), and estriol in maternal serum. Decreased levels of free estriol and AFP suggest numerical abnormalities of the fetal chromosomes. β-HCG is also elevated in trisomy 21 and decreased in trisomy 18. In cases with an increased risk (based on maternal age, lab results, and ultrasound), amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling are recommended for chromosome analysis.

wrchjd0.title: Neck dissection
wrchjd0.description: The therapeutic or prophylactic removal of the cervical lymph nodes with or without adjacent neurovascular and muscular tissue for the management of head and neck malignancies, e.g., thyroid cancer and oropharyngeal cancer. The extent of dissection depends on the type, location, and stage of the cancer.

Crcqjd0.title: Leukocyte adhesion
Crcqjd0.description: The third step in leukocyte extravasation, which is characterized by the firm binding of leukocytes to the endothelium prior to migration out of the blood vessel. Mediated by adhesion molecules on endothelial cells and leukocytes.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

xrcEjd0.title: Nephrotome
xrcEjd0.description: A division of the mesoderm and part of the pronephros. With the nephric tubules, it carries out temporary excretory function. Some of the urogenital system is derived from it.

Brczjd0.title: Thyroid function test
Brczjd0.description: Blood tests used to determine the function of the thyroid. They include: thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), thyroxine (T4), and triiodthyronine (T3).

ArcRPd0.title: Choleretic
ArcRPd0.description: A substance that stimulates the production of bile by the liver (e.g., ursodeoxycholic acid).

_rc5Pd0.title: Cholagogue
_rc5Pd0.description: A substance that promotes an increased flow of bile from the gallbladder into the duodenum (e.g., cholecystokinin).

Y7cn4d0.title: Nonallergic rhinitis with eosinophilia syndrome
Y7cn4d0.description: The most common type of inflammatory nonallergic rhinitis. Characterized by nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, hyposmia, and the presence of eosinophils in the nasal mucosa. Usually develops in middle-aged individuals.

b7cH4d0.title: Rhinoscleroma
b7cH4d0.description: A chronic granulomatous disease of the upper respiratory tract that is caused by Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis. Endemic to Asia, Africa, and South America. Manifestations include nasal obstruction, rhinorrhea, and nasal deformity. Can progress to tracheal wall thickening and luminal narrowing.

X7c94d0.title: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax
X7c94d0.description: A subtype of spontaneous pneumothorax defined by the absence of underlying lung disease

17c2kd0.title: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus
17c2kd0.description: A specific presentation of lupus. Includes a wide range of dermatologic manifestations that may or may not be associated with systemic disease.

destinations.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus → Specific clinical manifestations

W7cPkd0.title: Magnetic resonance arthrography
W7cPkd0.description: An imaging technique for joints that uses gadolinium contrast to distend the joint, highlight articular structures, and reveal soft tissue defects.

d7cokd0.title: Cardiolipin
d7cokd0.description: A component of the inner mitochondrial membrane that stabilizes the enzymes of oxidative phosphorylation.

V7cGkd0.title: Uncomplicated diverticulitis
V7cGkd0.description: A condition of acute, localized colonic diverticular inflammation without associated complications (e.g., perforation, abscess, obstruction). Typically manifests with acute-onset, lower left quadrant pain.

e7cxkd0.title: Recombination-activating genes
e7cxkd0.description: A set of genes that encode RAG proteins 1 and 2, which together form V(D)J recombinase, an enzyme required for V(D)J recombination in T cells and B cells. Autosomal recessive RAG1 and RAG2 loss-of-function mutations are a rare cause of severe combined immunodeficiency.

U7cbOd0.title: Presenilin-2
U7cbOd0.description: The protein product of the gene PSEN2. Mutations in the gene are associated with early-onset Alzheimer dementia.

27cTOd0.title: Infratentorial
27cTOd0.description: A descriptor for a position located inferiorly to the cerebellum tentorium (the dura mater that covers the cerebellum and supports the occipital lobes).

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

T7c6Od0.title: Fried egg cell
T7c6Od0.description: A cell with a clear cytoplasm and round nucleus. Conditions that have a fried egg appearance on histopathologic analysis of tissue include hairy cell leukemia, seminoma, and oligodendroglioma.

i7cJld0.title: Ketonemia
i7cJld0.description: The presence of ketone bodies (e.g., acetoacetic acid, beta-hydroxybutyric acid, acetone) in the serum.

Q7culd0.title: Occupational rhinitis
Q7culd0.description: A type of rhinitis caused by exposure to workplace substances, such as detergents, grain dust, wood dust, and chemicals. Can be mediated by allergic or nonallergic reactions to proteins in airborne substances. Commonly associated with occupational asthma.

j7c_ld0.title: Nonallergic rhinitis
j7c_ld0.description: A type of rhinitis that can be acute or chronic and can persist throughout the year. Symptoms are similar to allergic rhinitis (e.g., nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, postnasal drip) but nonallergic rhinitis is not mediated by an immune response. Typically affects adults.

P7cWNd0.title: Hormonal rhinitis
P7cWNd0.description: A type of nonallergic rhinitis that is typically associated with hormonal changes. Etiologies include pregnancy, menstruation, puberty, oral contraceptive use, and hypothyroidism. Hormonal rhinitis in pregnancy usually begins during the second month and stops after delivery.

l7cvNd0.title: Gender
l7cvNd0.description: A social construct referring to the norms (e.g., attitudes, behaviors) associated with an individual's sex. Often described in binary terms (e.g., man, woman).

N7c-Nd0.title: Meyer sign
N7c-Nd0.description: A nonspecific and insensitive clinical sign for deep vein thrombosis. Considered positive when compression of the calf elicits pain.

m7cVmd0.title: Hormone response element
m7cVmd0.description: A specific DNA sequence that is able to bind complementary hormone-receptor complexes. Binding initiates the transcription of downstream genes. Examples include thyroid hormone response element and estrogen hormone response element.

n7c7md0.title: Acamprosate
n7c7md0.description: A drug used to help maintain abstinence from alcohol. Decreases glutamate activity within the CNS.

destinations.label: Alcohol use disorder → Initiation of pharmacotherapy

L7cwmd0.title: Alcoholics Anonymous
L7cwmd0.description: A support group whose members are committed to stopping alcohol use and maintaining sobriety. One of its tenets is a twelve-step program, which includes admitting a lack of control over one's addiction, reflection with the help of an experienced sponsor, and helping others who have similar addictions.

I7cYMd0.title: Patient note
I7cYMd0.description: The written documentation of a patient's medical care and the reasoning behind it. Notes may be written by any member of the medical team and may include admission notes (H&P), daily progress notes, transfer notes, and discharge summaries.

destinations.label: Daily life of the intern → Medical notes

77c4Md0.title: TIMI coronary grade flow
77c4Md0.description:
A grading system used to evaluate the effectiveness of lysis therapy in patients with myocardial infarction. The procedure involves measuring coronary perfusion via angiogram 90 minutes after administration of lysis. 
Grade 0: no perfusion
Grade 1: penetration of contrast without perfusion
Grade 2: partial perfusion
Grade 3: normal perfusion

H7cKMd0.title: Cannon A waves
H7cKMd0.description: A physical examination finding seen in AV dissociation (e.g., in third-degree heart block) that is caused by the atria and ventricles contracting simultaneously, which leads to blood being pushed against a closed tricuspid valve. The result is a retrograde pressure wave throughout the venous system that may appear as pulsations in the jugular vein.

87cOnd0.title: Gastrointestinal perforation
87cOnd0.description: A full-thickness injury of the wall of the gastrointestinal tract that results in leakage of enteric contents. Causes include direct trauma (e.g., penetrating injury) and ischemia (e.g., due to bowel obstruction).

v7cAnd0.title: Osmosis
v7cAnd0.description: The process by which a solvent (e.g., water) moves through a semipermeable membrane from an area of less concentrated solution to an area of more concentrated solution.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function

C7cqLd0.title: Nulligrad
C7cqLd0.description: A woman who has never been pregnant.

-7cDod0.title: Dilute Russell viper venom time
-7cDod0.description: A test used to screen for phospholipid-dependent coagulation (e.g., as part of testing for lupus anticoagulants). Russell viper venom usually induces the formation of blood clots. However, in the presence of lupus anticoagulants, which bind to the venom, this effect is suppressed, so clotting time is prolonged.

ZHcZKd0.title: Squamous metaplasia of lactiferous ducts
ZHcZKd0.description: A histopathologic finding associated with subareolar abscesses. Characterized by transformation of the cuboidal epithelium of the lactiferous ducts into keratinizing squamous epithelium. Associated with smoking and more common among postmenopausal women.

0HceKd0.title: Posterior fat pad sign
0HceKd0.description: A radiographic sign characterized by the presence of a lucent crescent in the olecranon fossa. Can be seen on a lateral view of the elbow joint in which the joint is flexed at ~ 90°. Represents an elbow joint effusion (e.g., in the setting of a supracondylar fracture or radial head fracture). The joint effusion lifts fatty tissue off the bone, resulting in the crescent shape.

media.title: Anterior and posterior fat pad signs in supracondylar humerus fracture

bHcHKd0.title: Emergency exploratory laparotomy
bHcHKd0.description: An urgent surgical procedure in which the abdominal cave is opened, typically with a midline incision, and abdominal organs in all 4 quadrants are evaluated for pathologies (e.g., ischemia, perforation, abdominal bleeding). Indications include blunt or penetrating abdominal trauma or acute abdomen with signs of perforation, peritonitis, or hemodynamic instability.

eHcx6d0.title: Cherry-red skin
eHcx6d0.description: A rare finding in patients with carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning. Caused by the formation of carboxyhemoglobin. Because of its low prevalence (~ 1%) and high subjectivity, it is not considered a useful diagnostic tool. Can be useful as a postmortem sign for lethal CO poisoning.

RHclJd0.title: Clostridium perfringens alpha toxin
RHclJd0.description: A bacterial virulence factor produced by Clostridium perfringens. Acts as a phospholipase to degrade cell membranes and tissue. Its effects result in gas gangrene and the development of a double zone of hemolysis seen on blood agar cultures.

iHcJJd0.title: Staphylococcus aureus alpha toxin
iHcJJd0.description: A bacterial virulence factor produced by Staphylococcus aureus. Causes apoptosis through the formation of pores in the cell membrane.

PHcWqd0.title: Basic airway maneuvers
PHcWqd0.description: Interventions that may be performed to treat airway compromise in patients without anticipated complications. Strategies rely on specific positioning (head-tilt/chin lift, jaw-thrust), oxygenation (high-flow oxygen by nasal cannula, face mask, or non-rebreather), and/or ventilation (bag-mask ventilation with or without PEEP valve) strategies. Adjunct interventions include the establishment of nasopharyngeal airway (NPA) or oropharyngeal airway (OPA).

4Hc3qd0.title: Video laryngoscopy
4Hc3qd0.description: A type of laryngoscopy that uses a rigid blade with a fiberoptic camera on the distal end, facilitating real-time visualization of the airway during endotracheal intubation.

kHcmqd0.title: Gum-elastic bougie
kHcmqd0.description: A long, semirigid, plastic introducer that is narrower than an endotracheal tube lumen. Used to facilitate passage through narrow vocal cords. Its tip is bent slightly to allow blind entry into a hidden anterior larynx, and the material allows tactile feedback to sense contact with tracheal rings.

media.title: Eschmann endotracheal tube introducer (gum elastic bougie)

OHcIqd0.title: Awake fiberoptic intubation
OHcIqd0.description: An endotracheal intubation technique that does not require paralysis and involves minimal sedation. Local anesthetic is used to minimize airway sensation and reflexes. A flexible fiberoptic laryngoscope is used to visualize the glottis and guide a preloaded endotracheal tube over it into the trachea.

lHcvqd0.title: Herbert pits
lHcvqd0.description: A pathognomonic finding of trachoma characterized by visible, shallow pits in the cornea.

MHcMId0.title: Endomyocardial biopsy
MHcMId0.description: A procedure that involves cardiac catheterization to obtain heart muscle tissue. Can be used to evaluate allograft transplant rejection, myocarditis, and infiltrative cardiac diseases. Complications include perforation and arrhythmias.

nHc7Id0.title: Otorrhea
nHc7Id0.description: A drainage of liquid from the ear. Etiologies include conditions that affect the external ear canal and conditions that affect the middle ear with associated perforation of the tympanic membrane.

LHcwId0.title: Gallium scan
LHcwId0.description: A nuclear medicine scan that uses gallium-67, which has affinity for acute phase reactants such as lactoferrin and transferrin, to identify areas of inflammation (e.g., from osteomyelitis). Can be used in patients for whom MRI is contraindicated (e.g., due to metal implants).

oHc0rd0.title: Aural toilet
oHc0rd0.description: A process of cleaning the external auditory canal to remove cerumen, discharge, debris, and/or foreign objects. Methods include suction, dry mopping the outer entrance to the external ear canal, and, if the TM is intact, gentle otic lavage. Often indicated in the management of otitis externa and chronic suppurative otitis media.

KHcUrd0.title: Myringotomy
KHcUrd0.description: A procedure in which an incision is made in the tympanic membrane to drain purulence from severe acute otitis media. Can be used to facilitate placement of a tube (i.e., tympanostomy) to allow continued drainage (e.g., to treat recurrent acute otitis media).

pHcLrd0.title: Nasal nitric oxide test
pHcLrd0.description: A screening test for primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD). The amount of nitric oxide in a nasal exhalation is measured. Low levels are associated with PCD and merit further diagnostic evaluation for this condition.

JHcsrd0.title: Rapid antigen detection test
JHcsrd0.description: A rapid diagnostic test used to detect an antigen in a variety of samples: e.g., blood, mucous, urine, or feces. It uses immunochemical methods that are based on the principle of antigen-antibody binding. Examples include the rapid strep antigen detection test, malaria rapid diagnostic test, immunofluorescence assays for influenza A and B, and enzyme immunoassays for detection of Giardia lamblia in stool samples.

qHcCrd0.title: Granulomatous gastritis
qHcCrd0.description: A subtype of gastritis characterized by the presence of multiple granulomas in the gastric mucosa. Etiologies include tuberculosis, syphilis, Crohn disease, and sarcoidosis.

rHcf7d0.title: Hepatitis B immune globulin
rHcf7d0.description: A preparation of IgG against hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). Administered as part of post-exposure prophylaxis for hepatitis B virus.

7Hc47d0.title: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for hepatitis B
7Hc47d0.description: A set of measures that can be taken after exposure to hepatits B virus. Depending on immunization status, affected individuals either receive active immunization in form of hepatitis B vaccination, passive immunization in form of hepatitis B immune globulin, or both. Postexposure prophylaxis is most effective when administred within a 24-hour window.

HHcK7d0.title: Celiac disease serology
HHcK7d0.description: A group of serologic studies used to evaluate celiac disease. Detection of IgA antitissue transglutaminase antibody (tTG) is the gold standard. Further diagnostic antibodies include IgG deamidated gliadin peptide and antiendomysial (EMA) IgA antibodies.

GHcB7d0.title: Capillary refill time
GHcB7d0.description: The time it takes for blood to return to distal capillaries after blanching (normally < 2 seconds). Assessed by applying pressure to the distal finger until it is white, releasing the pressure, and then observing for the return of normal color. Capillary refill time can be used to quickly assess peripheral perfusion and the adequacy of fluid resuscitation.

tHcXHd0.title: Pulmonary hamartoma
tHcXHd0.description: A benign neoplasm of malformed lung tissue that consists of muscle, fat, bone, and cartilage. Typically asymptomatic and often found incidentally.

uHcpHd0.title: Atopic march
uHcpHd0.description: A clinical phenomenon in which patients with atopic dermatitis subsequently develop allergic rhinitis and/or asthma (i.e., the atopic triad). Occurs in ~ 80% of patients with atopic dermatitis.

EHc8Hd0.title: Pronucleus
EHc8Hd0.description: A cell nucleus (of either the egg or sperm) that has a haploid set of chromosomes. The female and male pronuclei fuse to form the zygote nucleus.

vHcAHd0.title: Closed reduction and internal fixation
vHcAHd0.description: A procedure to repair fractures and/or dislocation with physical manipulation (e.g., via traction) followed by percutaneous fixation with mechanical devices (e.g., Kirschner wires).

destinations.label: Trauma and orthopedic surgery → Internal fixation

DHc1sd0.title: Microthrombocytopenia
DHc1sd0.description: A condition of decreased platelet count with small platelet size. Associated with Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome and X-linked thrombocytopenia, both of which are caused by WAS gene mutations.

wHchsd0.title: Acute diarrhea
wHchsd0.description: A condition of frequent defecation (≥ 3 times per day) that lasts ≤ 14 days.

9HcNsd0.title: Persistent diarrhea
9HcNsd0.description: A condition of frequent defecation (≥ 3 times per day) that lasts > 14 days and < 30 days.

CHcqsd0.title: Chronic diarrhea
CHcqsd0.description: A condition of frequent defecation (≥ 3 times per day) that lasts > 30 days.

xHcEsd0.title: Antidiarrheal agent
xHcEsd0.description: A group of drugs that reduce peristalsis, lengthen colonic transit time, and/or decrease fecal volume. Examples include loperamide and diphenoxylate-atropine.

yHcdGd0.title: Closed fracture
yHcdGd0.description: A fracture that does not come into contact with the outside environment.

AHcRGd0.title: Unstable fracture
AHcRGd0.description: A type of fracture in which fractured bone fragments are significantly displaced, misaligned, or shifted from their normal anatomical position.

_Hc5Gd0.title: Stable fracture
_Hc5Gd0.description: A type of fracture in which fractured fragments remain in their normal anatomical alignment and do not move or shift significantly.

zHcrGd0.title: Retinal rods
zHcrGd0.description: The slender, cylindrical, first-order receptor cells of the retina. Contain rhodopsin and are achromatic. Mainly found around the fovea centralis.

ZscZtd0.title: Subareolar abscess
ZscZtd0.description: A complication of periductal mastitis characterized by the development of an abscess as a result of lactiferous duct damage and rupture. Associated with squamous metaplasia of the lactiferous ducts.

0scetd0.title: Bartholin gland cyst
0scetd0.description: A retention cyst (a cyst caused by obstruction of an excretory duct) arising from the ducts of the Bartholin glands. It results from inflammation or trauma that causes obstruction and accumulation of the mucus produced by the glands. It manifests as an unilateral mass located in the posterolateral part of the vaginal introitus. Bartholin gland abscess occurs when an infection develops behind the obstructed duct.

destinations.label: Bartholin gland cyst and abscess → Bartholin gland cyst

ascQtd0.title: Bartholin gland abscess
ascQtd0.description: An acute infection of a Bartholin gland or Bartholin gland cyst, most commonly due to E. coli. Symptoms include unilateral pain and swelling of the vulva and dyspareunia.

destinations.label: Bartholin gland cyst and abscess → Bartholin gland abscess

bscHtd0.title: Histidine decarboxylase
bscHtd0.description: An enzyme that converts histidine to histamine. Found in histamine-producing cells, such as mast cells, basophils, enterochromaffin-like cells, and histaminergic neurons. Use pyridoxine (vitamin B6) as a cofactor.

Xsc9td0.title: MRA
Xsc9td0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Magnetic resonance angiography
2. Magnetic resonance arthrography
3. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist

WscPFd0.title: Drug-induced lichen planus
WscPFd0.description: A dermatologic condition that manifests with lesions that are grossly similar to those seen in patients with lichen planus. Common triggers include beta blockers, ACE inhibitors, and penicillamine.

escxFd0.title: Telotristat
escxFd0.description: An inhibitor of tryptophan hydroxylase (the rate-limiting enzyme in serotonin synthesis). Used to treat carcinoid syndrome diarrhea that does not respond to somatostatin analogues.

2scT8d0.title: Neonatal resuscitation
2scT8d0.description: A structured sequence of management steps performed to maximize the chance of survival for neonates with respiratory failure, apnea, bradycardia, and/or cardiac arrest following birth. Emphasizes immediate newborn care, positive pressure ventilation, chest compressions, and resuscitation medications adapted to neonatal physiology.

fsck8d0.title: Prostatic venous plexus
fsck8d0.description: A network of veins around the prostate gland. Receives blood from the deep dorsal vein of the penis and drains into the vesical and internal iliac veins.

Tsc68d0.title: Vi capsule
Tsc68d0.description: A capsule that surrounds Salmonella typhi bacteria. Serves as a virulence factor by inhibiting complement activation and phagocytosis by the host. The vaccine against S. typhi contains Vi capsular polysaccharide.

Qscuud0.title: Shield chest
Qscuud0.description: A broad chest. Can be seen in patients with Turner syndrome.

destinations.label: Differences (disorders) of sex development → Turner syndrome

jsc_ud0.title: Pyosalpinx
jsc_ud0.description: The accumulation of pus in the fallopian tubes. Caused by fallopian tube infection and inflammation (salpingitis) in pelvic inflammatory disease that has resulted in tubal adhesions and obstruction.

PscWEd0.title: Intercostal artery
PscWEd0.description: An artery that lies within the costal groove below each rib. There are nine pairs of anterior intercostal arteries and eleven pairs of posterior intercostal arteries. On each side, the first six anterior intercostal arteries arise from the ipsilateral internal thoracic artery and the remaining three from the musculophrenic artery. The first two posterior intercostal arteries arise from the ipsilateral subclavian artery, and the remaining nine arise from the descending thoracic aorta.

4sc3Ed0.title: Lateral axillary lymph nodes
4sc3Ed0.description: A group of lymph nodes found in the axillary space posteromedial to the axillary artery. Its lymphatic afferents receive lymph from the entire upper limb. Its efferents drain into the central and apical axillary lymph nodes as well as the inferior deep cervical lymph nodes.

OscIEd0.title: Vertebral venous plexus
OscIEd0.description: A network of valveless veins that run longitudinally along the entire vertebral column. Consists of an external plexus surrounding the external aspect of vertebrae and an internal plexus between the dura mater and vertebral bodies. The internal and external plexuses communicate freely with each other and the intervertebral veins, spinal cord veins, basilar plexus, deep cervical veins, azygos-hemiazygos system, and lumbar veins.

lscvEd0.title: Intercostal vein
lscvEd0.description: A vein that lies within the costal groove below each rib. There are nine pairs of intercostal veins anteriorly and eleven pairs of intercostal veins posteriorly. Anteriorly, the intercostal veins drain into the ipsilateral internal thoracic vein or its tributary, the musculophrenic vein. Posteriorly, the intercostal veins drain either directly or indirectly into the azygos vein on the right, and into the hemiazygos or accessory hemiazygos on the left.

media.title: Anatomy of the intercostal neurovascular bundle

Nsc-Ed0.title: FAP
Nsc-Ed0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Familial adenomatous polyposis
2. Familial amyloid polyneuropathy

mscVvd0.title: Loss-of-function mutation
mscVvd0.description: A mutation in a gene that results in decreased or absent function of that gene (i.e., partial or complete inactivation).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

5scivd0.title: Medullary hypertonicity
5scivd0.description: An osmotic gradient that results from the medullary interstitium being hypertonic with respect to the tubular fluid.

MscMvd0.title: KCNQ1 gene
MscMvd0.description: A gene that encodes potassium channels in the heart, inner ear, stomach, and colon. Loss-of-function mutations in this gene can cause congenital long QT syndrome.

nsc7vd0.title: KCNE1 gene
nsc7vd0.description: A gene located on chromosome 11p that encodes potassium channels in the heart and inner ear. Loss-of-function mutations of this gene can cause congenital long QT syndrome.

Lscwvd0.title: Thyroid agenesis
Lscwvd0.description: The complete absence of the thyroid gland due to a failure of medial and lateral anlagen formation during embryogenesis. A common cause of congenital hypothyroidism in developed countries.

IscYwd0.title: Basal-bolus insulin regimen
IscYwd0.description: An insulin regimen that combines once or twice daily long-acting insulin (e.g., glargine, detemir) or NPH insulin with scheduled and correctional rapid-acting insulin (e.g., aspart) at mealtimes. Results in better glucose control and lower incidence of nocturnal hypoglycemia than sliding-scale insulin regimens.

rscfwd0.title: Sliding-scale insulin regimen
rscfwd0.description: An insulin regimen that uses a specified dose of rapid-acting or regular insulin to treat a given level of hyperglycemia. Often administered independent of food intake, prior insulin administration, or insulin sensitivity.

ssctwd0.title: Point-of-care test
ssctwd0.description: A test or diagnostic measure that can be provided without further transport of a sample (e.g., blood) or the patient to the laboratory or another facility.

uscp9d0.title: Hepatic acinus
uscp9d0.description: A functional unit of the liver supplied by a terminal branch of the hepatic artery. Hepatocytes closer to the arterioles receive blood that is more oxygen-rich (and highest in potential toxin concentration).

Esc89d0.title: Cyclophilin
Esc89d0.description: A protein that can catalyze cis-to-trans isomerization of peptide bonds at proline residues to facilitate protein folding. Found abundantly throughout human cells. Cyclosporine A binds to cyclophilin to form a complex that can inhibit calcineurin.

xscECd0.title: Plasma aldosterone concentration
xscECd0.description: The concentration of aldosterone in the serum. The ratio of plasma aldosterone concentration (PAC) to plasma renin activity (PRA) is used to evaluate for primary aldosteronism.

BsczCd0.title: Plasma renin activity
BsczCd0.description: A measure of the activity of renin in the serum, given in ng/mL/hour. A PRA < 1 ng/mL/hour is considered low. The ratio of plasma aldosterone concentration (PAC) to plasma renin activity (PRA) is used to evaluate for primary aldosteronism.

yscdxd0.title: Burkholderia pseudomallei
yscdxd0.description: A facultative intracellular, gram-negative bacterium that is predominantly found in soil and water. Transmitted via percutaneous inoculation as well as inhalation, aspiration, or ingestion of contaminated sources. Causes melioidosis.

AscRxd0.title: Japanese encephalitis virus
AscRxd0.description: An flavivirus transmitted via the Culex tritaeniorhynchus mosquito. Causes Japanese encephalitis. Endemic to temperate and tropical areas of Asia. Major hosts include pigs and birds.

_sc5xd0.title: Localized Lymphadenopathy
_sc5xd0.description: An enlargement of lymph nodes in a single lymph node region (e.g., axillary lymphadenopathy).

ZGcZBd0.title: PAC
ZGcZBd0.description:
An abbreviation for either:
- Plasma aldosterone concentration
- Premature atrial contraction

YGcnBd0.title: Full-thickness biopsy
YGcnBd0.description: A procedure used to obtain a sample that contains all layers of a target tissue. Used for histopathologic examination to distinguish between normal and abnormal tissue segments. Most commonly used for gastrointestinal sampling (e.g., for Hirshprung disease) and cutaneous biopsies (e.g., for melanoma).

bGcHBd0.title: Exophytic
bGcHBd0.description: A descriptor for a structure that is growing outward (e.g., a tumor growing outward from the surface epithelium).

XGc9Bd0.title: Hemorrhagic shock
XGc9Bd0.description: A type of hypovolemic shock characterized by severe fluid loss from bleeding. Etiologies include trauma, postpartum hemorrhage, and gastrointestinal bleeding.

WGcPyd0.title: Cytoprotective agents
WGcPyd0.description: A class of drugs that prevent damage to the gastric mucosa without inhibiting gastric acid production. Used in the treatment of peptic ulcer disease and gastritis. Prostaglandin E1 analogue (misoprostol) and sucralfate are the commonly used drugs from this class.

dGcoyd0.title: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma
dGcoyd0.description: A subtype of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors. PPAR-γ serve as transcription factors that increase insulin sensitivity by upregulating the transcription of adiponectin and GLUT4 glucose transporters in adipose and muscle cells. Thiazolidinediones, a class of antidiabetic medications, are PPAR-γ agonists. A fusion product of PPAR-γ with PAX8 can result in oncogenic transformation.

media.title: Mechanism of action: oral diabetes medications

VGcGyd0.title: Acid suppression medications
VGcGyd0.description: A class of drugs that protect the gastric mucosa by inhibiting acid production. Used in the treatment of peptic ulcer disease and gastritis. Examples include proton pump inhibitors and H2 antagonists.

eGcxyd0.title: Nonrebreather mask
eGcxyd0.description: An oxygen delivery system that consists of a face mask with flap valves and an attached reservoir connected to high-flow oxygen at 10-15 L/min. Used when FiO₂ > 40% is desired and patients are spontaneously breathing.

destinations.label: Oxygen therapy → Basic oxygen delivery systems

2GcTAd0.title: Immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis
2GcTAd0.description: A type of glomerulonephritis associated with deposition of immune complexes on glomerular tissue seen on histopathologic examination (e.g., immunofluorescence, electron microscopy). Examples include IgA nephropathy, lupus nephritis, and poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.

fGckAd0.title: Blood typing
fGckAd0.description: A laboratory test used to determine an individual's ABO blood type and RhD status.

TGc6Ad0.title: Familial isolated pituitary adenoma syndrome
TGc6Ad0.description: A rare, familial, autosomal dominant syndrome caused by mutations in the AIP gene. Manifests with pituitary adenomas without other associated abnormalities. It is the most common familial cause of acromegaly/gigantism.

SGcyAd0.title: Hemangioma
SGcyAd0.description: A vascular tumor that is typically benign. There are several types of hemangiomas, including congenital hemangiomas, infantile hemangiomas, and hepatic hemangiomas.

destinations.label: Benign skin tumors → Vascular skin tumors

hGcc_d0.title: Arterial thromboembolism
