hGcc_d0.description: An occlusion of a peripheral artery by a blood clot fragment (thromboembolus) that has dislodged from a clot (thrombus) formed at a different site. Arterial thromboembolism is a common cause of stroke, acute limb ischemia, and acute mesenteric ischemia.

3GcS_d0.title: Procoagulant
3GcS_d0.description: A substance that promotes blood coagulation. Includes factors V, VII, VIII, IX, and X

RGcl_d0.title: Magnetic resonance venography
RGcl_d0.description: A modality of magnetic resonance imaging used to examine the veins. An intravenous contrast medium is often used to enhance image quality. Typical applications include diagnosis of venous thrombosis, especially if assessment using ultrasound is inconclusive or not possible (e.g., cerebral vein thrombosis).

QGcu_d0.title: Anterior scalenectomy
QGcu_d0.description: A surgical procedure in which the anterior scalene muscle is resected. Used to treat thoracic outlet syndrome.

jGc__d0.title: Hepatic lobule
jGc__d0.description: A hexagon-shaped lobule of the liver that consists of a central vein surrounded by portal triads at the vertices. The anatomical unit of the liver.

PGcWzd0.title: Portal lobule
PGcWzd0.description: A triangular-shaped lobule of the liver with central veins at the vertices and the portal triad at the center. Serves as the bile-synthetic functional unit of the liver. Bile flows from the periphery to the intrahepatic bile ductules in the portal triad.

4Gc3zd0.title: Frontal release sign
4Gc3zd0.description: The re-emergence of primitive reflexes in adults as a result of frontal lobe damage.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

kGcmzd0.title: Plantar reflex
kGcmzd0.description: A spinal reflex elicited by stroking the plantar aspect of the foot in a "J" pattern. Using a firm object, pressure is applied to the heel, up the lateral side of the sole to the base of the small toe, then medially across the ball of the foot. Children <1-2 years of age will exhibit the extensor plantar reflex (i.e., extension of the hallux and fanning of the toes). After 1-2 years of age, the flexor plantar reflex (i.e., flexion and adduction of the toes) will be seen, unless there is an upper motor lesion of the corticospinal tract, in which case pressure will elicit the pathological extensor plantar reflex (Babinski sign).

OGcIzd0.title: Photoscreening
OGcIzd0.description: A pediatric vision test used to detect errors of refraction and screen for amblyogenic risk factors. Can also be used as an alternative for visual acuity testing in preverbal and/or noncooperative children.

NGc-zd0.title: Red reflex
NGc-zd0.description: The reflection of light in the ocular fundus, which is normally red in color. Can be assessed using an ophthalmoscope or retinoscope. Alterations in the red reflex (e.g., absence, asymmetry) are abnormal and merit evaluation to determine the underlying cause (e.g., cataracts, retinoblastoma).

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Fundoscopic exam

mGcV-d0.title: HAS-BLED score
mGcV-d0.description: A score used to estimate the bleeding risk in patients with atrial fibrillation who are starting or continuing anticoagulation therapy. Risk factors include uncontrolled hypertension, renal disease, liver disease, stroke history, labile INR, age > 65 years, alcohol use, prior major bleeding, and use of other medications that can predispose to bleeding (e.g., NSAIDs, aspirin).

media.title: HAS-BLED score: Bleeding risk in atrial fibrillation

MGcM-d0.title: 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3 deficiency
MGcM-d0.description: A rare autosomal recessive disorder of sexual development in karyotypically normal males (46,XY) characterized by a decreased production of 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3, which is responsible for the conversion of androstenedione to testosterone. Low testosterone levels during fetal development results in undervirilization of male external genitalia and underdevelopment of the internal genitalia (male pseudohermaphroditism).

destinations.label: Differences (disorders) of sex development → 17β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3 deficiency​

nGc7-d0.title: Persistent Mullerian duct syndrome
nGc7-d0.description: A rare disorder of sex development in karyotypically normal males (46, XY) that is characterized by the persistence of the Müllerian duct derived structures (uterus, cervix, fallopian tubes, upper ⅔ of vagina) due to insensitivity to or insufficient production of the Mullerian inhibiting factor.

destinations.label: Differences (disorders) of sex development → Persistent Mullerian duct syndrome

LGcw-d0.title: Hypoestrogenism
LGcw-d0.description: Lower estrogen levels in female individuals than expected values for age. Causes include menopause, ovarian insufficiency (primary or acquired), and dysfunction or suppression of the hypothalamus. Signs include breast atrophy, vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary atrophy (i.e., dry, pale atrophic vaginal mucosa with or without introitus stenosis), decreased libido, thin dry skin, and decreased bone mineral density. Signs of no prior estrogen exposure include an absence of breast development and a prepubertal appearance of the vaginal mucosa (i.e., red and thin).

oGc0ZV0.title: Bare area of the liver
oGc0ZV0.description: A triangle-shaped area on the surface of the liver that does not have a peritoneal covering.

6GcjZV0.title: Cough suppressant
6GcjZV0.description: A drug used for symptomatic treatment of cough. Mechanisms of action include suppression of the central cough receptor in the brain and inhibition of stretch receptors in the lungs and pleura. Examples include benzonatate, codeine, and dextromethorphan.

pGcLZV0.title: HLA-B8
pGcLZV0.description: An allele of class I major histocompatibility complex that is associated with several autoimmune disorders, including Addison disease, myasthenia gravis, and Graves disease.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → Immune tolerance and autoimmunity

JGcsZV0.title: HLA-A3
JGcsZV0.description: An allele of class I major histocompatibility complex that is associated with hereditary hemochromatosis.

qGcCZV0.title: Procoagulant-anticoagulant balance
qGcCZV0.description: The physiologic balance between pathways that promote blood coagulation and pathways that inhibit blood coagulation.  Procoagulants include factors V, VII, VIII, IX, and X. Anticoagulants include antithrombin III, protein C, and protein S.

rGcf0V0.title: Hepatitis A pre-exposure prophylaxis
rGcf0V0.description: A set of preventive measures that can be taken to potentially avoid hepatitis A virus infection. Includes general measures (e.g., hand-washing, food and water hygiene) and active immunization against hepatitis A virus. Vaccination is recommended for all children > 12 months of age and certain unimmunized high-risk groups (e.g., men who have sex with men, individuals with chronic liver disease).

7Gc40V0.title: Hepatitis A post-exposure prophylaxis
7Gc40V0.description: A set of measures that can be taken after exposure to hepatitis A virus. Indicated for all previously unvaccinated individuals and should be administred within 2 weeks of exposure. Depending on age and comorbidities, affected individuals should receive either active or passive immunization.

HGcK0V0.title: Disproportionate dwarfism
HGcK0V0.description: A category of dwarfism characterized by ≥ 1 body parts being relatively small, while the others might be of average size and/or relatively larger in size  (e.g., average-sized torso with short extremities). Seen in achondroplasia.

sGct0V0.title: Proportionate dwarfism
sGct0V0.description: A category of dwarfism in which all body parts are small to the same extent but maintain the same proportion (relative size to one another) as a body of average stature.

GGcB0V0.title: Hedgehog protein family
GGcB0V0.description: A family of growth factors essential for signaling pathways during embryonic and postnatal development. Examples include Sonic hedgehog, Desert hedgehog, and Indian hedgehog.

tGcXaV0.title: Wnt-7 gene
tGcXaV0.description: A gene that encodes for a growth factor essential for embryonic development. Regulates cellular growth and proliferation at the distal end of each developing limb as well as in dorsal-ventral patterning during the development of various structures (e.g., limbs, urogenital tract). Mutations in the gene have been implicated in the oncogenesis of colorectal cancer.

FGcgaV0.title: Fibroblast growth factor protein family
FGcgaV0.description: A growth factor family with mitogenic activity. Involved in various processes, including embryonic development of the limbs, cell growth, and tissue repair.

8GcOaV0.title: Transforming growth factor family
8GcOaV0.description: A growth factor family that is involved in multiple processes, such as cell growth, embryonic development (bone, cartilage, skeletal muscle), and regulation of the immune system. Dysregulation of TGF genes is implicated in the pathogenesis of several autoimmune diseases and various types of cancers.

destinations.label: Cytokines and eicosanoids → Transforming growth factor family

uGcpaV0.title: Gout
uGcpaV0.description: A common inflammatory arthropathy characterized by painful and swollen joints caused by precipitation of uric acid crystals.

CGcqYV0.title: Cleidocranial dysplasia
CGcqYV0.description:
An autosomal dominant condition characterized by delayed closure of the cranial sutures, craniofacial dysmorphism (e.g., frontal bossing, prominent chin, maxillary hypoplasia), dental abnormalities, and hypoplastic clavicles. 
Caused by a mutation in a transcription factor involved in osteoblast development.

xGcEYV0.title: Lower urinary tract atrophy
xGcEYV0.description: A variety of changes to the urethra and bladder resulting from low estrogen levels. Includes urethral shortening, thinning of the mucosa, and muscle weakness leading to decreased contractility and compliance of the bladder and urethra. Patients may experience dysuria, urinary incontinence, and frequent UTIs. Commonly a manifestation of genitourinary syndrome of menopause.

BGczYV0.title: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
BGczYV0.description: A common abdominal surgery that uses a laparoscopic approach to remove the gallbladder. Indications include symptomatic cholelithiasis, acalculous cholecystitis, and porcelain gallbladder.

yGcdbV0.title: Gallbladder drainage
yGcdbV0.description: A procedure used to decompress the gallbladder by draining bile either percutaneously (e.g., via percutaneous cholecystectomy) or endoscopically (e.g., via endoscopic transpapillary or transmural drainage). Used in the management of high-risk acute cholecystitis and cholangitis.

AGcRbV0.title: MPTP
AGcRbV0.description: A prodrug of MPP+, a neurotoxic substance that selectively causes damage to dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and induces parkinsonism. A major impurity of the production of the synthetic opioid desmethylprodine (MPPP). MPTP is used to induce parkinsonism in animal models.

_Gc5bV0.title: Structural heart disease
_Gc5bV0.description: A category of heart conditions defined by the American Heart Association. Encompasses ischemic, valvular, and congenital heart disease, as well as all types of cardiomyopathy.

zGcrbV0.title: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy
zGcrbV0.description: An emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis that is performed within 72 hours of the onset of symptoms or within the same hospital admission.

-GcDbV0.title: Delayed laparoscopic cholecystectomy
-GcDbV0.description: An elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy that is typically performed ~ 6 weeks after the resolution of an acute biliary disease (e.g. acute cholecystitis, acute cholangitis).

ZtcZXV0.title: Pulmonary embolism severity index score
ZtcZXV0.description: A prognostic risk stratification tool used to categorize patients with acute pulmonary embolism into five groups (I-V) according to morbidity and mortality. Uses 11 variables to calculate risk, including age, sex, and history of cancer. Can help to decide whether inpatient treatment is warranted.

0tceXV0.title: Simplified pulmonary embolism severity index score
0tceXV0.description: A prognostic risk stratification tool (based on the PESI score) used to categorize patients with acute pulmonary embolism into low-risk, moderate-risk, and high-risk groups regarding morbidity and mortality. Uses only 7 out of the original 11 variables to calculate the risk. Can aid in deciding for or against inpatient treatment.

Xtc9XV0.title: 46, XX ovarian dysgenesis
Xtc9XV0.description: A disorder of sexual development in karyotypically normal females (46, XX) characterized by the presence of streak ovaries due to impaired ovarian development during embryogenesis. Patients with this condition develop primary amenorrhea and infertility, despite having female internal genital organs (uterus and vagina).

destinations.label: Differences (disorders) of sex development → 46,XX gonadal dysgenesis

ctcacV0.title: Epsilon wave
ctcacV0.description: A small upward ECG waveform that can be seen at the end of the QRS complex in leads V1–4 in patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC). Highly specific for this condition.

WtcPcV0.title: Rome IV criteria for functional chest pain
WtcPcV0.description: A set of criteria used to diagnose functional chest pain. Includes retrosternal noncardiac chest pain or discomfort, no esophageal symptoms (e.g., heartburn, dysphagia), and no evidence for GERD, eosinophilic esophagitis, or any other major esophageal motor disorder. Criteria must be met for the last 3 months before diagnosis with symptom onset at least 6 months before diagnosis.

2tcT1V0.title: Unstable atrial fibrillation
2tcT1V0.description: A state of hemodynamic instability (i.e., life-threatening or refractory hypotension, myocardial ischemia, pulmonary edema, or cardiogenic shock) due to uncontrolled atrial fibrillation.

ftck1V0.title: Stable atrial fibrillation
ftck1V0.description: The presence of atrial fibrillation without signs of hemodynamic instability.

gtcF1V0.title: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
gtcF1V0.description: A subtype of atrial fibrillation in which the arrhythmia resolves within 7 days of onset either following treatment or spontaneously. The frequency of recurring episodes may vary.

Stcy1V0.title: Persistent atrial fibrillation
Stcy1V0.description: The presence of atrial fibrillation for > 7 days.

htccWV0.title: Permanent atrial fibrillation
htccWV0.description: A subtype of atrial fibrillation for which therapeutic attempts are no longer made to convert to or maintain sinus rhythm, unless the patient and treating physician agree to do so.

3tcSWV0.title: Log-kill hypothesis
3tcSWV0.description: A hypothesis that posits that a given dose of anticancer therapy will kill a specific fraction of cancerous cells, regardless of the initial size of the tumor.

RtclWV0.title: Growth fraction
RtclWV0.description: The percentage of cancerous cells in a sample that are actively proliferating (as opposed to remaining in the G0 phase).

itcJWV0.title: Cell cycle-specific antineoplastic agents
itcJWV0.description: A type of anticancer agent that acts only on cells during a specific phase of the cell cycle. Due to this specificity, these agents only target proliferating cells. Examples of drugs with cell cycle specificity include bleomycin (which arrests the cell cycle at G₂ phase) and taxanes (which act on microtubules during M phase).

QtcuWV0.title: Delusion of grandeur
QtcuWV0.description: A false belief, despite evidence to the contrary and/or a lack of supporting evidence, involving a sense of personal greatness or superiority (e.g., an individual believes that they are on a messianic mission). Delusions of grandeur may occur in psychotic disorders (e.g., bipolar disorder, schizophrenia). Pervasive delusions of grandeur are characteristic of narcissistic personality disorder.

jtc_WV0.title: Disorder of thought content
jtc_WV0.description: A disturbance in the content of one's thoughts or ideas. Examples include poverty of thought, suicidal or homicidal ideations, obsessions, compulsions, phobias, and delusions.

PtcWdV0.title: Delusion of control
PtcWdV0.description: A fixed, false belief that an external force is controlling one's thoughts or behavior. Specific examples include the delusion that one's thoughts can be heard by others (thought broadcasting) and the delusion that other's thoughts are being inserted into one's head (thought insertion).

4tc3dV0.title: Persecutory delusion
4tc3dV0.description: A false belief involving suspicion or mistrust (e.g., an individual believes they are being targeted, harassed, or persecuted), despite evidence to the contrary and/or a lack of supporting evidence.

ktcmdV0.title: Delusion of guilt
ktcmdV0.description: A fixed, false belief that one is responsible for something bad.

OtcIdV0.title: Erotomanic delusion
OtcIdV0.description: A fixed, false belief that someone is in love with the individual affected by the delusion.

ltcvdV0.title: Somatic delusion
ltcvdV0.description: A fixed, false belief that one has a certain illness.

Ntc-dV0.title: Mood congruence
Ntc-dV0.description: A consistency between a person's mood (i.e., their emotional state) and their situational context (e.g., their state of health, degree of stressors).

mtcVVV0.title: Disturbance of perception
mtcVVV0.description: A disturbance in sensory perception. Examples include hallucinations, illusions, and dissociation (derealization, depersonalization).

5tciVV0.title: Disorganized thinking
5tciVV0.description: A disturbance in the logical connection between thoughts or the flow of thoughts. Examples include circumstantiality, tangentiality, loose associations (derailment), flight of ideas, neologism, word salads, clang associations, and thought blocking.

MtcMVV0.title: Erythropoietic protoporphyria
MtcMVV0.description: A dermatologic condition characterized by a tender, nonblistering, photosensitive rash that typically manifests during childhood. Caused by dysfunction of ferrochelatase, an enzyme in the heme synthetic pathway.

ntc7VV0.title: Wide-complex tachycardia
ntc7VV0.description: A category of tachyarrhythmias (i.e., pulse >100 bpm) characterized by a wide QRS complex (> 120 ms; or 3 small squares on the ECG). Includes monomorphic ventricular tachycardia, polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (e.g., torsades de pointes), supraventricular tachycardia with variable conduction (e.g., with bundle branch blocks or accessory pathways), pacemaker-associated tachycardia, and tachyarrhythmias caused by drugs or metabolic conditions that widen the QRS interval.

6tcjeV0.title: Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency
6tcjeV0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder caused by deficiency or absence of argininosuccinate synthetase due to mutation of the ASS1 gene. Causes neurologic symptoms in the first days of life due to hyperammonemia. Also results in an increased serum citrulline concentration.

ptcLeV0.title: Argininosuccinate lyase deficiency
ptcLeV0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder that causes increased serum concentrations of ammonia, citrulline, and argininosuccinic acid.

JtcseV0.title: Epothilone
JtcseV0.description: A metabolite produced by Sorangium cellulosum. Inhibits mitosis by stabilizing polymerized microtubules. Analogs of epothilone (e.g., ixabepilone) are used as antineoplastic drugs.

qtcCeV0.title: Ixabepilone
qtcCeV0.description: An epitholone B analog that arrests the cell cycle at the G2/M phase by stabilizing microtubule polymers. Used to treat breast cancer.

rtcfUV0.title: Macrothrombocytopenia
rtcfUV0.description: A condition of abnormally giant platelets and thrombocytopenia. Associated with Bernard-Soulier syndrome, immune thrombocytopenia, von Willebrand disease type 2B, and Chédiak–Higashi syndrome (pancytopenia).

7tc4UV0.title: Volume depletion
7tc4UV0.description: A deficit in extracellular fluid volume, which occurs due to a loss of total body sodium. Distinct from dehydration, which refers to a loss of total body water. Manifestations of volume depletion include delayed capillary refill (≥ 3 sec), hypotension, tachycardia, decreased skin turgor, dry oral mucosa, sunken eyes, and decreased urine output.

HtcKUV0.title: Asbestos
HtcKUV0.description: Fibrous silicate minerals used in construction, fireproofing, and insulation. Exposure to asbestos can cause nonmalignant diseases (e.g., asbestosis) and cancers (e.g., lung cancer, mesothelioma).

GtcBUV0.title: Peak inspiratory flow rate
GtcBUV0.description: The maximum airflow rate attained during inspiration. In spontaneously breathing patients, it is proportional to the inspiratory effort, which increases in response to higher respiratory demand (e.g., due to exercise, pulmonary disease, acidosis) and decreases with respiratory muscle weakness (e.g., due to fatigue, neuromuscular disease, sedation).

ttcX2V0.title: Dihydrobiopterin reductase
ttcX2V0.description: An NADPH-dependent enzyme that converts dihydrobiopterin to tetrahydrobiopterin, which is a cofactor for nitric oxide synthase and the enzymes that hydroxylate phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan. A deficiency of dihydrobiopterin reductase causes malignant phenylketonuria.

Ftcg2V0.title: Two-person bag-mask-ventilation technique
Ftcg2V0.description: A technique of bag-mask ventilation in which one person uses both hands to achieve mask seal and open the airway while a second person delivers breaths. Ideal for emergency settings and difficult ventilation scenarios (e.g., in patients with severe obesity).

utcp2V0.title: Classic phenylketonuria
utcp2V0.description: A congenital deficit of phenylalanine hydroxylase that results in accumulation of phenylalanine in the central nervous system. Causes psychomotor retardation, seizures, a musty odor, and pale skin/hair (from lack of melanin production).

Etc82V0.title: Atresia
Etc82V0.description: An absence or abnormal opening of a structure that is usually patent (e.g., duodenal atresia, in which a portion of the duodenal lumen is closed).

vtcA2V0.title: Nasal septum
vtcA2V0.description: A cartilaginous structure that separates the right and left nasal cavities. Supplied by several arteries including the sphenopalatine artery and the anterior and posterior ethmoidal arteries. Innervated by the anterior ethmoidal nerve, the nasal branches of the greater palatine nerve, and the nasopalatine nerve.

Dtc1fV0.title: UDP-galactose 4-epimerase deficiency
Dtc1fV0.description: A rare, autosomal recessive defect that results in a deficiency of UDP-galactose-4-epimerase. Manifests in the early neonatal period with jaundice, vomiting, hepatosplenomegaly, cataracts, and failure to thrive.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of carbohydrate metabolism → Galactosemia

wtchfV0.title: Branched-chain fatty acid
wtchfV0.description: A saturated fatty acid that has ≥ 1 methyl groups that branch off of the main carbon chain.

9tcNfV0.title: Desloratadine
9tcNfV0.description: An antihistaminic drug and active metabolite of loratadine used to treat allergic rhinitis and urticaria.

CtcqfV0.title: Levocetirizine
CtcqfV0.description: An antihistaminic drug and enantiomer of cetirizine used to treat allergic rhinitis and urticaria.

xtcEfV0.title: Seldinger technique
xtcEfV0.description: A technique used to safely gain access to a body lumen or cavity (e.g., vessel, trachea, chest wall) through a small opening. A narrow, semi-rigid introducer (e.g. needle, trocar, or guide-wire) is used to enter the opening, followed by sliding a wider flexible tube (e.g. vascular catheter, endotracheal tube, chest drain) over the introducer, facilitating its entry into the lumen or cavity. The rigid introducer is then removed.

BtczfV0.title: Epiploic appendage
BtczfV0.description: A small, physiologic, fat-filled outpouching of the peritoneum found on the surface of the colon (primarily transverse and sigmoid colon). Ischemic infarction of an appendage (e.g., due to torsion) can lead to epiploic appendagitis.

ytcdTV0.title: Epiploic appendagitis
ytcdTV0.description: A condition of ischemic infarction of an epiploic appendage (e.g., due to torsion or spontaneous thrombosis of an associated vein). The most common manifestation is lower abdominal pain. Other manifestations include early satiety, nausea and vomiting, and diarrhea.

AtcRTV0.title: Ristocetin
AtcRTV0.description: An antibiotic used for platelet aggregation tests. Activates von Willebrand factor to bind glycoprotein Ib, thereby inducing platelet aggregation. Failure of aggregation occurs in conditions such as von Willebrand disease and Bernard-Soulier syndrome.

_tc5TV0.title: Radiocapitellar line
_tc5TV0.description: An anatomic line that can be drawn through the center of the neck of the radius to pass through the center of the capitellum of the humerus on a lateral x-ray of the elbow joint. The line does not intersect the capitellum if an elbow dislocation is present.

-tcDTV0.title: Acute abdominal series
-tcDTV0.description: A series of radiographs of the abdomen and chest used to detect pneumoperitoneum and/or bowel obstruction in patients with acute abdominal pain. Consists of two abdominal x-rays (in supine position and upright position) and a chest x-ray (in upright position).

ZFcZgV0.title: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy
ZFcZgV0.description: A condition of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) that results as a complication of sepsis due to pathogen- and inflammation-triggered activation of the coagulation cascade.

0FcegV0.title: Mild traumatic brain injury
0FcegV0.description: A trauma-induced disruption of brain function associated with a GCS ≥ 13-15 at least 30 minutes post-injury and ≥ 1 of the following: altered mental state at the time of the injury, loss of consciousness < 30 minutes, posttraumatic amnesia < 24 hours, or minor neurological abnormalities not requiring surgical intervention. Sometimes used interchangeably with the term concussion.

media.title: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) fact sheet

aFcQgV0.title: Paragonimus
aFcQgV0.description: A genus of parasitic trematodes (lung flukes) that infect lung tissue. Typically transmitted by ingesting eggs that contaminate undercooked crustacean meat. Paragonimus westermani is endemic to southeast Asia; Paragonimus kellicotti is endemic to North America.

WFcPSV0.title: Cerebrovascular fibromuscular dysplasia
WFcPSV0.description: A condition of fibromuscular dysplasia that involves the carotid and/or vertebral arteries. Manifestations include nonspecific symptoms (e.g., headache, pulsatile tinnitus, neck pain, dizziness), symptoms of brain ischemia (e.g., amaurosis fugax, Horner syndrome, transient ischemic attack, stroke), and cervical bruit.

dFcoSV0.title: High-altitude pulmonary edema
dFcoSV0.description: A noncardiogenic pulmonary edema that occurs within 2–4 days of ascent to high altitude. Manifestations include dry cough, dyspnea, wheezing, and cyanosis. It is the most common cause of death following rapid ascent to high altitude.

VFcGSV0.title: High-altitude cerebral edema
VFcGSV0.description: A severe manifestation of acute mountain illness after ascent to high altitude characterized by encephalopathy. Primarily manifests with altered mental status and ataxia. Concurrent symptoms of high-altitude pulmonary edema such as cough and dyspnea may also be present.

eFcxSV0.title: Spinal infections
eFcxSV0.description: Includes vertebral osteomyelitis, diskitis, spondylodiskitis, and spinal epidural abscess.

UFcbhV0.title: Postconcussion syndrome
UFcbhV0.description: A collection of symptoms that can persist beyond three months after traumatic brain injury. Manifestations include headaches, dizziness, fatigue, sleep disturbance, irritability, impaired memory, and impaired concentration.

2FcThV0.title: Ageusia
2FcThV0.description: A complete loss of taste sensation. Etiologies include damage to the lingual and/or glossopharyngeal nerves (e.g., due to neuritis, radiation, or compression by a cerebellopontine mass), hypothyroidism, or an adverse reaction to medications (e.g., antibiotics, antihypertensives, tricyclic antidepressants).

TFc6hV0.title: Pegloticase
TFc6hV0.description: A recombinant form of uricase. Converts uric acid to allantoin to decrease serum uric acid concentrations. Used to treat chronic gout.

gFcFhV0.title: Modified Valsalva maneuver
gFcFhV0.description: A modification of the standard Valsalva maneuver used to cardiovert supraventricular tachycardias. The patient is asked to sit up in a semirecumbent position and blow into a 10 mL syringe for 15 seconds (this achieves a strain of 40 mm Hg). At the end of the exhalation, the patient is laid supine and the patient's legs are passively elevated to 45° for 15 seconds. The patient is then returned to the semirecumbent position for 45 seconds, and the cardiac rhythm is reassessed.

hFcc3V0.title: Acetowhitening
hFcc3V0.description: Whitening of mucosal epithelium seen after application of 5% acetic acid for 3-5 minutes. Used to improve visualization of mucosal lesions associated with human papillomavirus infection (e.g., anogenital warts, cervical lesions).

RFcl3V0.title: Testicular infarction
RFcl3V0.description: A condition of ischemic damage to the testicle. Caused by compression of the testicular vasculature (e.g., from torsion, incarcerated hernia, epididymo-orchitis).

iFcJ3V0.title: Cervical collar
iFcJ3V0.description: A rigid orthotic device used to stabilize and restrict motion of the cervical spine postoperatively or in cases of known or suspected injury in order to protect the spinal cord from damage.

QFcu3V0.title: Cervical spine immobilization
QFcu3V0.description: A set of measures taken to restrict motion of the cervical spine postoperatively or in cases of known or suspected spinal injury in order to protect the spinal cord from damage. Includes the use of rigid cervical collars, long spinal board immobilization, in-line manual stabilization, and log-roll maneuvers.

PFcWRV0.title: Nontaxane microtubule inhibitor
PFcWRV0.description: A group of chemotherapeutic agents that inhibits microtubule stability by blocking mitotic spindles without affecting depolymerization and thereby stops the process of cell division. Agent includes eribulin. Commonly used in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer and unresectable liposarcoma. Adverse effects include myelosuppression, peripheral neuropathy, and QT prolongation.

4Fc3RV0.title: Sweet syndrome
4Fc3RV0.description: An inflammatory skin condition that manifests with sudden-onset fever and painful skin lesions (erythematous papules, plaques, and nodules). Associated with infections (e.g., upper respiratory, gastrointestinal), malignancy (e.g., acute myeloid leukemia), inflammatory bowel disease, pregnancy, and certain medications (e.g., granulocyte-colony stimulating factor).

kFcmRV0.title: Procedural sedation and analgesia
kFcmRV0.description: The administration of sedatives and/or analgesics to ease anxiety and pain while maintaining cardiorespiratory function during diagnostic or therapeutic procedures outside of the operating room.

OFcIRV0.title: MRI contraindications
OFcIRV0.description: Factors that may interfere with the magnetic field required for MR imaging and that can prohibit its safe use. These contraindications include medical devices (e.g., pacemakers, ICDs, insulin pumps, prostheses, stents, vascular access ports, joint replacements), cosmetic applications (tattoos, body piercings, or permanent make up), and claustrophobia. Further contraindications, e.g., pregnancy, breastfeeding, and renal disease, may apply if contrast is to be used.

lFcvRV0.title: Antalgic gait
lFcvRV0.description: A limp caused by the effort to avoid pain while walking. Characterized by a shortened stance phase and increased swing phase of the affected leg. Can be caused by any condition that causes pain in the lower extremity when under strain (e.g., arthritis, trauma, infection).

MFcMiV0.title: Sex pilus
MFcMiV0.description: An appendage encoded for by F factor that attaches two bacterial cells together. The subsequent retraction of the sex pili facilitates the formation of a conjugal (mating) bridge through which the transfer of plasmid DNA between two bacteria can occur in the process known as bacterial conjugation.

LFcwiV0.title: Lytic bacteriophage
LFcwiV0.description: A virus that makes use of the bacterial cellular machinery to manufacture phage components and multiply rapidly. Lysis of the host bacterium occurs to release new phage particles.

pFcLQV0.title: Continuous cardiac telemetry
pFcLQV0.description: The use of a telemetry device with ECG leads for continuous measurement of heart rate and rhythm. Used for monitoring critically ill inpatients and, in the outpatient setting, for the diagnosis of paroxysmal arrhythmias (Holter monitoring). Most inpatient cardiac telemetry devices can also measure respiratory rate (using the respiration-induced changes in heart rhythm) and blood pressure (using a cuff that autoinflates and deflates at preset intervals and electrical transducers that utilize the oscillatory blood pressure monitoring technique).

qFcCQV0.title: Synaptobrevin
qFcCQV0.description: A membrane protein involved in the formation of SNARE complexes, which mediate vesicle fusion.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

IFcYjV0.title: Horizontal gene transfer
IFcYjV0.description: The movement of genetic material from one bacterium to another via three main mechanisms: transformation, transduction, and conjugation.

HFcKjV0.title: R factor (bacteriology)
HFcKjV0.description: A set of genes necessary for the transfer of extrachromosomal DNA that encodes for antibiotic resistance between bacteria.

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanisms of drug resistance

sFctjV0.title: R plasmid
sFctjV0.description: An extrachromosomal segment of DNA that encodes for resistance to antibiotics. Consists of the R factor (genes necessary for the transfer of the R plasmid between bacteria) and R determinant (genes that confer antibiotic resistance).

destinations.label: General bacteriology → Mechanisms of drug resistance

GFcBjV0.title: Paragonimus westermani
GFcBjV0.description: A trematode (fluke) found most commonly in Asian countries (particularly China, Korea, Japan, the Philippines, Taiwan, and India). Transmitted via ingestion of undercooked shellfish. Ingested organisms cause paragonimiasis when they encyst in the duodenum and penetrate through the abdominal wall and diaphragm into the lung.

media.title: Life cycle of Paragonimus westermani (lung fluke)

tFcXPV0.title: Contraindications to adenosine
tFcXPV0.description: A set of contraindications that includes pre-existing second-degree AV block, complete heart block, sick sinus syndrome in the absence of a pacemaker, concurrent verapamil or digoxin therapy, reactive airway disease, and Wolff-Parkinson White syndrome with either atrial fibrillation or antidromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia.

FFcgPV0.title: Antidromic conduction
FFcgPV0.description: The conduction of a nerve impulse in the opposite direction of its normal direction of conduction. For example, in antidromic atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia, the cardiac nerve impulse travels in the normal (orthodromic) direction through the accessory pathway and then back via the antidromic conduction through the atrioventricular node, which results in a wide QRS complex on ECG.

8FcOPV0.title: Orthodromic conduction
8FcOPV0.description: The conduction of a nerve impulse in its normal (anterograde) direction (e.g., orthodromic atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia in which the nerve impulse travels via orthodromic conduction through the atrioventricular node before returning via antidromic conduction through the accessory pathway, seen as a narrow QRS complex on ECG).

uFcpPV0.title: Physiologic sinus tachycardia
uFcpPV0.description: An increased heart rate ≥100 beats per minute, mediated by the sinoatrial node, due to a physiologic release of catecholamines in response to triggers such as exercise, fear, anxiety, pain, fever, and hemodynamic compromise. Although the underlying cause should be treated, the tachycardia itself should not be treated, as it is an appropriate compensatory mechanism.

EFc8PV0.title: Inappropriate sinus tachycardia
EFc8PV0.description: A syndrome characterized by an inexplicable increase in the heart rate to >100 bpm at rest or with minimal physical activity. Typically accompanied by symptoms such as palpitations, dizziness, and dyspnea. Underlying causes (e.g., medications, illness, anxiety, or structural heart disease) should be ruled out.

vFcAPV0.title: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis
vFcAPV0.description: A group of small vessel vasculitides that are associated with the formation of autoantibodies against cytoplasmic components of neutrophils, such as proteinase-3 and myeloperoxidase. Includes granulomatosis with polyangiitis, eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, microscopic polyangiitis, and single-organ vasculitis.

28cTNV0.title: Uncomplicated appendicitis
28cTNV0.description: An acutely inflamed appendix with no evidence of complications, such as gangrene, perforation, peritonitis, abscess, or an associated inflammatory mass.

f8ckNV0.title: Complicated appendicitis
f8ckNV0.description: An acutely inflamed appendix complicated by perforation, peritonitis, abscess, and/or an associated inflammatory mass.

S8cyNV0.title: Aortic dissection detection risk score
S8cyNV0.description: A score used to stratify patients into low, moderate and high risk for acute aortic dissection. Patients are scored on one of three domains: predisposing conditions (e.g., Marfan syndrome), features of pain (e.g., sudden pain) and physical findings (e.g., pulse asymmetry).

38cSmV0.title: Contraindications to beta blockers
38cSmV0.description: The absolute contraindications to beta blockers include asthma, atrioventricular block, cardiogenic shock, symptomatic bradycardia, and known allergy. Relative contraindications include bradycardia, hypotension, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (lung function should be monitored).

j8c_mV0.title: Pleural cap
j8c_mV0.description: A curved density at the apex of the lung seen on chest x-ray. Common in older adults and can be a result of pleural scarring (e.g., idiopathic, infectious, radiation-induced), malignancy (apical lung cancer or lymphoma), an abscess in the neck or mediastinum, or a hemothorax (seen on supine view) due to trauma or aortic dissection.

P8cW5V0.title: Extracorporeal life support
P8cW5V0.description: An advanced life support method in which a cardiopulmonary bypass system circulates the patient's blood through artificial gas exchange membranes. Venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) only provides respiratory support (e.g., in acute respiratory distress syndrome), while venoarterial ECMO (VA-ECMO) provides full cardiorespiratory support (e.g., in cardiogenic shock).

destinations.label: Care of the critically ill patient → Resuscitation and stabilization

48c35V0.title: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome
48c35V0.description: A rare, autosomal dominant syndrome that causes premature aging. Additional manifestations include failure to thrive, progressive atherosclerosis, atrophic skin changes, and alopecia. Characteristic facial manifestations include circumoral cyanosis, a thin nose, micrognathia, and retrognathia.

k8cm5V0.title: Lamin
k8cm5V0.description: An intermediate filament found on the inner nuclear membrane of the cell. Serves as a binding site for various proteins involved in the regulation of transcription.

O8cI5V0.title: Nesprin
O8cI5V0.description: A protein found predominantly in the outer nuclear membrane of the cell. Facilitates connections to the cytoskeleton.

l8cv5V0.title: Pthirus pubis
l8cv5V0.description: A blood-sucking louse that causes pediculosis pubis when the female louse lays eggs at the base of hairs, which then hatch after 6-8 days. Spread primarily via sexual contact.

destinations.label: Lice infestation → Pediculosis pubis (pubic lice infestation)

N8c-5V0.title: Sarcoptes scabiei
N8c-5V0.description: A mite that causes scabies when female mites burrow into the epidermis, destroy keratinocytes, and lay eggs. Transmitted via skin-to-skin contact.

m8cVMV0.title: Pediculus humanus
m8cVMV0.description: A species of sucking louse that infects humans. Includes two subspecies: Pediculus humanus humanus (Pediculosis humanus corporis, the body louse), which causes pediculosis corporis, and Pediculus humanus capitis (the head louse), which causes pediculosis capitis.

media.title: Developmental stages of the body louse

58ciMV0.title: Streptozocin
58ciMV0.description: A cell cycle-nonspecific antineoplastic agent that inhibits DNA synthesis by alkylating and cross-linking DNA. Used to treat various cancers, including neuroendocrine tumors and adrenocortical carcinoma.

J8csnV0.title: Flutter wave
J8csnV0.description: A high-frequency wave with a regular morphology that represents atrial activity on ECG of patients with atrial flutter. Gives the baseline of the ECG a characteristic sawtooth appearance.

q8cCnV0.title: Focal atrial tachycardia
q8cCnV0.description: A narrow-complex regular elevated heart rate (>100/min) that arises from a focal point in the atria (not the sinoatrial node). On ECG, there are discrete P waves.

I8cYLV0.title: Supraventricular re-entrant tachycardia
I8cYLV0.description: An elevated heart rate of >100/min that occurs due to a re-entrant pathway above the level of the bundle of His. Subtypes include atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia (AVNRT), atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia (AVRT), and sinoatrial node re-entrant tachycardia (SANRT).

H8cKLV0.title: Pleural sliding
H8cKLV0.description: Back-and-forth sliding of a hyperechogenic band between the ribs normally seen on thoracic ultrasound. Represents differing movement of the parietal and visceral pleura during respiration. Typically absent in conditions in which the visceral and parietal pleura are separated (e.g., pneumothorax, pleural effusion), pulmonary fibrosis, and ARDS.

s8ctLV0.title: Centrilobular zone
s8ctLV0.description: The functional zone of the hepatic acinus. Contains centrilobular hepatocytes and surrounds the central vein. The zone most sensitive to ischemia (due to poor oxygenation) and metabolic toxins (due to high density of cytochrome P450 enzymes).

G8cBLV0.title: Intermediate zone (liver)
G8cBLV0.description: The functional zone of the hepatic acinus. Contains midzonal hepatocytes and is the zone most susceptible to hepatocellular necroptosis due to yellow fever.

t8cXoV0.title: Periportal zone
t8cXoV0.description: The functional zone of the hepatic acinus that surrounds the portal triad. Contains periportal hepatocytes and is the zone most susceptible to viral hepatitis and toxic substance ingestion.

media.title: Periportal zone and portal triad of liver

F8cgoV0.title: Comet-tail artifact
F8cgoV0.description: An ultrasonographic finding characterized by echogenic vertical lines originating from the lung pleura. These reverberation artifacts are also called B-lines and are caused by the high disparity between the acoustic impedance of water and air. They move in synchrony with breathing and indicate contact of the parietal and visceral pleura. Therefore, they are not present in pneumothorax. Can be seen in patients with interstitial edema.

88cOoV0.title: Seashore sign
88cOoV0.description: A normal ultrasound finding in M-mode in which "waves" (horizontal lines representing the stationary parietal pleura) are seen proximal to the "shore" (a granular pattern representing the moving visceral pleura).

media.title: Illustration of seashore sign on lung ultrasound

u8cpoV0.title: Stratosphere sign
u8cpoV0.description: An abnormal ultrasound finding in M-mode in which horizontal lines ("stratosphere" or "barcode") are seen through the entire field and the normal granular pattern caused by moving visceral pleura is absent. Typically seen in pneumothorax.

v8cAoV0.title: Hyperorality
v8cAoV0.description: A type of impulsive behavior characterized by behaviors that include excessive chewing, sucking, lip-smacking, and examination of objects with the mouth. Associated with neurologic disorders such as Kluver-Bucy syndrome and frontotemporal dementia.

destinations.label: Rare neurological diseases → Kluver Bucy syndrome

98cNKV0.title: Central poststroke pain
98cNKV0.description: A type of central neuropathic pain that occurs with lesions caused by a stroke. Characterized by pain and dysesthesia affecting the ipsilateral face and contralateral body and most commonly occurs following damage to the spinothalamic tract. Called thalamic pain syndrome when following a thalamic stroke.

x8cEKV0.title: Signs of increased work of breathing
x8cEKV0.description: A constellation of clinical signs that indicate an increased effort to maintain oxygenation and ventilation due to an underlying respiratory pathology (e.g., asthma). Signs of increased work of breathing include accessory muscle use (e.g., sternocleidomastoid and scalene muscles), tripod positioning, nasal flaring, retractions (intercostal, subcostal, and suprasternal), grunting, pursed lips, and paradoxical breathing.

destinations.label: Respiratory failure and arrest → Clinical features

B8czKV0.title: A-lines
B8czKV0.description:
A term that can refer to:
1) Arterial line
2) Physiological reverberation artifacts of the pleura on pulmonary ultrasound. The distance between each repeating A-line is the same as the distance from the skin surface to the parietal pleura. A-lines are often erased by B-lines. In the absence of B-lines (e.g., in pneumothorax), A-lines are more easily detectable.

y8cd6V0.title: Contraindications to succinylcholine
y8cd6V0.description: A set of contraindications to the use of succinylcholine, which includes: 1) hyperkalemia, 2) renal failure without regular dialysis or wide QRS on ECG; 3) severe burns or muscle trauma (e.g., crush injury, rhabdomyolysis), 4) conditions that cause denervation (e.g., stroke, spinal cord injury), 5) late intraabdominal sepsis, and 6) neuromuscular disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis, muscular dystrophy).

A8cR6V0.title: Apex-to-cupola distance
A8cR6V0.description: The interpleural distance between the visceral pleura at the tip of the lung (apex) and the parietal side at the thoracic wall (cupola). Can be measured in a chest x-ray to evaluate the size of a pneumothorax. Another measurement used to gauge the size of a pneumothorax in chest x-rays is the interpleural distance at the level of the lung hilus.

_8c56V0.title: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor poisoning
_8c56V0.description: A toxicity most commonly caused by exposure to organophosphate or carbamate agents. Manifests as cholinergic excess with muscarinic effects (e.g., bradycardia, miosis, lacrimation, salivation, bronchorrhea, bronchospasm, urination, emesis, diarrhea), nicotinic effects (e.g., flaccid paralysis, respiratory arrest), and CNS effects (e.g., seizure, coma).

z8cr6V0.title: Muscarinic-1 receptor
z8cr6V0.description: A Gq-coupled muscarinic receptor subtype found in exocrine glands (e.g., parietal cells) and the central nervous system, where it mediates cognitive functions.

-8cD6V0.title: Pulmonary component of the second heart sound
-8cD6V0.description: A component of the second heart sound that is caused by the closure of the pulmonary valve. Best heard at the second left intercostal space near the parasternal region (pulmonary area). Normally, it is heard after the component of the second heart sound caused by aortic valve closure (A2) and is softer than A2.

media.title: Anatomical locations and auscultatory sites for heart valves

ZucZpV0.title: Aortic component of the second heart sound
ZucZpV0.description: A component of the second heart sound that is caused by the closure of the aortic valve. Best heard at the second right intercostal space near the parasternal region (aortic area). Normally, it precedes the component of the second heart sound caused by pulmonary valve closure (P2) and is louder than P2.

aucQpV0.title: Ventriculomegaly
aucQpV0.description: An enlargement of the cerebral ventricles seen on neuroimaging. Seen in conditions such as hydrocephalus and cerebral atrophy.

Xuc9pV0.title: Programmed death-ligand 1
Xuc9pV0.description: A transmembrane protein found on the surface of tumor cells. Binds to the programmed cell death 1 ligand on T cells and causes T-cell dysfunction, thereby decreasing the immune response against the tumor. Antibodies against this protein (e.g., durvalumab, avelumab, atezolizumab) are used as anticancer therapies.

cucaJV0.title: Darbepoetin-alpha
cucaJV0.description: A long-acting form of recombinant erythropoietin. Used to stimulate the erythroid cell lineage in the setting of chronic kidney disease-induced anemia or drug-induced anemia.

OucIrV0.title: Functional chest pain
OucIrV0.description: A condition characterized by recurrent chest pain or discomfort without a discernable cause, possibly due to esophageal hypersensitivity. Diagnosis is based on the Rome IV diagnostic criteria. Management includes psychotherapy and central neuromodulators (e.g., SSRIs).

lucvrV0.title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging
lucvrV0.description: A form of MRI optimized to image cardiac structure, function, and perfusion. Used to assess various cardiac conditions, including cardiomyopathy, valvular heart disease, coronary artery disease, and congenital heart defects.

Nuc-rV0.title: Phytanic acid
Nuc-rV0.description: A branched-chain fatty acid that can only be metabolized by alpha-oxidation in the peroxisome. Refsum disease, in which alpha-oxidation is impaired, results in the accumulation of phytanic acid.

mucV7V0.title: SBP
mucV7V0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Systolic blood pressure
2. Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis

nuc77V0.title: Postural drainage
nuc77V0.description: A technique in which the body is positioned to align the trachea inferiorly to a fluid-overloaded area of the lung to facilitate the removal of fluids by expectoration.

Lucw7V0.title: Point-of-care ultrasound
Lucw7V0.description: Portable ultrasound used for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. Commonly used in emergency and critical care medicine for initial assessment and ongoing monitoring.

ouc0HV0.title: CPP
ouc0HV0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Cerebral perfusion pressure
2. Coronary perfusion pressure
3. Central precocious puberty
4. Calcium pyrophosphate

KucUHV0.title: End-organ dysfunction
KucUHV0.description: The damage sustained by organ systems as a result of systemic pathological states, particularly those of the circulatory system (e.g., chronic hypertension, hypertensive crisis, shock), which impair the perfusion of the brain, heart, kidneys, and other organs (e.g., eyes in hypertensive crises).

6ucjHV0.title: Clinical features of peritonitis
6ucjHV0.description: A constellation of clinical findings that suggest irritation of the peritoneal lining of the abdomen. Symptoms are usually nonspecific (e.g., abdominal pain, distention, fever), while physical examination findings typically include rebound tenderness, rigidity, and guarding.

pucLHV0.title: Permissive hypertension
pucLHV0.description: A treatment strategy in which hypertension is tolerated in order to prevent hypoperfusion. E.g., in patients with acute ischemic stroke, systolic blood pressure up to 220 mm Hg may be accepted to facilitate cerebral blood flow.

destinations.label: Ischemic stroke → Initial evaluation and acute stabilization

qucCHV0.title: Atrioventricular nodal blocking agent
qucCHV0.description: A drug that slows conduction through the atrioventricular node. Often used to treat supraventricular tachycardias. Examples include adenosine, beta blockers, nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, and digoxin.

7uc4sV0.title: Safe apnea time
7uc4sV0.description: The period during intubation in which patients can safely go without spontaneous breathing. Begins after anesthetic induction or paralysis and lasts until the SpO2 reaches 88–90%. Allows for a buffer before organ dysfunction (e.g. hypoxic brain injury, cardiac dysrhythmia) and death can occur (typically at SpO2 < 70-75%). Rescue ventilation is recommended if patients are not successfully intubated within this time.

HucKsV0.title: Apneic oxygenation
HucKsV0.description: A technique used during intubation to extend safe apnea time by applying high-flow (15 L/min) oxygen by nasal cannula to apneic patients, which increases FiO2 delivery to the alveoli and allows oxygen to enter the bloodstream by diffusion alone without requiring lung expansion or breaths.

suctsV0.title: Malakoplakia
suctsV0.description: A condition of chronic granulomatous inflammation associated with Rhodococcus equi infections. Most commonly involves the genitourinary tract. Characterized by the presence of histiocytes that contain Michaelis-Gutmann bodies (iron and calcium inclusion bodies).

GucBsV0.title: Michaelis-Gutmann body
GucBsV0.description: A round, lamellar, basophilic inclusion body seen in the cytoplasm of histiocytes in patients with malakoplakia. Contains calcium and iron.

tucXGV0.title: Glycosylation-dependent cell adhesion molecule-1
tucXGV0.description: A cell adhesion molecule found on the surface of endothelial cells. Facilitates attachment to leukocytes.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Chemotaxis and leukocyte extravasation

FucgGV0.title: Stromelysin
FucgGV0.description: A type of matrix metalloproteinase that is produced by fibroblasts and proliferating keratinocytes. Breaks down certain types of collagen (e.g., type III) and gelatin. Involved in the remodeling phase of wound healing.

vucAGV0.title: Tube duodenostomy
vucAGV0.description: The surgical creation of a duodenocutaneous fistula for the management of large duodenal perforations (i.e., > 3 cm) that cannot be primarily closed.

Duc1tV0.title: Intensive care unit
Duc1tV0.description: A unit that provides the highest level of care available in a hospital.

yucdFV0.title: Fibrillatory waves
yucdFV0.description: A type of waveform seen on ECG in patients with atrial fibrillation, in which normal P waves and the normal isoelectric baseline are not discernible. Characterized by low amplitude, high frequency, and irregular morphology. Represents atrial activity.

_uc5FV0.title: Normocapnia
_uc5FV0.description: The presence of a physiologic pCO₂ level in arterial blood (i.e., 33-45 mm Hg).

YEcn8V0.title: Long-acting muscarinic antagonist
YEcn8V0.description: A class of muscarinic antagonists that have a long duration of action (typically ≥ 12 hours). Used for maintenance therapy for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Examples include tiotropium, aclidinium, umeclidinium, and glycopyrrolate.

bEcH8V0.title: Short-acting muscarinic antagonist
bEcH8V0.description: A class of muscarinic antagonists with an onset of action of 10-15 minutes and a short duration of action (4-6 hours). Used to treat acute exacerbations of asthma and COPD. Examples include ipratropium and oxitropium.

XEc98V0.title: Neurogenic pulmonary edema
XEc98V0.description: An acute onset pulmonary edema thought to be caused by a catecholamine surge. Occurs following a significant CNS event, including a spinal cord or head injury, stroke, CNS infection, or status epilepticus.

cEcauV0.title: Rumination syndrome
cEcauV0.description: A disorder characterized by regurgitation of recently ingested food soon after eating. The regurgitation is usually effortless and not preceded by retching. Classified as a functional gastroduodenal disorder and an eating disorder.

2EcTEV0.title: Myelin figure
2EcTEV0.description: A histopathologic marker of cellular injury characterized by aggregates of damaged cell membranes (peroxidized lipids) that resemble myelin sheaths.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cell injury

fEckEV0.title: Pneumonia severity index for CAP
fEckEV0.description: A score used to assess the mortality risk in patients with community-acquired pneumonia. Can be used to evaluate the need for inpatient treatment. Criteria include patient age, comorbidities, and laboratory findings.

TEc6EV0.title: Uncomplicated nausea and vomiting of pregnancy
TEc6EV0.description: A symptom of pregnancy that manifests with nausea and vomiting, usually between 4 and 16 weeks of gestation.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Common discomforts during pregnancy

REclvV0.title: Emergence reaction
REclvV0.description: A spectrum of symptoms seen during emergence from anesthesia or procedural sedation before becoming fully conscious. Includes confusion, agitation, irritability, combativeness, nightmares, and hallucinations. Can occur after administration of inhalational anesthetic agents, anticholinergic drugs, benzodiazepines, and ketamine.

destinations.label: Procedural sedation and analgesia → Recovery and discharge

iEcJvV0.title: Balint syndrome
iEcJvV0.description: A rare neurologic condition characterized by simultanagnosia, optic ataxia, and ocular apraxia. Caused by lesions of the posterior parietal lobe.

QEcuvV0.title: Simultanagnosia
QEcuvV0.description: A neurologic deficit characterized by an inability to integrate the elements of a visual scene despite having sufficient acuity to resolve individual elements.

jEc_vV0.title: Optic ataxia
jEc_vV0.description: A neurologic deficit characterized by difficulty reaching objects in the peripheral visual field (e.g., reaching beyond or lateral to an object).

PEcWDV0.title: Ocular apraxia
PEcWDV0.description: A neurologic deficit characterized by an inability to direct gaze accurately to new targets.

kEcmDV0.title: SUN protein
kEcmDV0.description: A protein found predominantly in the inner nuclear membrane of the cell. Facilitates connections to the cytoskeleton.

OEcIDV0.title: Mixed acid-base disorder
OEcIDV0.description: The simultaneous presence of ≥ 2 primary acid-base disorders (e.g., respiratory alkalosis and metabolic acidosis in salicylate intoxication). Often manifests with a near-normal arterial pH in the presence of substantial changes in both HCO₃ and pCO₂ and lesser- or greater-than-expected compensatory responses.

lEcvDV0.title: Red flags for hypertensive crisis
lEcvDV0.description: A group of symptoms that may indicate acute end-organ damage in a patient with hypertension. The presence of any of these symptoms should prompt further diagnostics. Red flags include acute dyspnea, chest pain, altered mental status, and focal neurological symptoms.

KEcU9V0.title: Asphyxiant gas
KEcU9V0.description: A gas that causes systemic and/or tissue hypoxia. Simple asphyxiants are inert gases (e.g., carbon dioxide, methane, nitrogen, helium) that can lead to arterial hypoxemia, suffocation, unconsciousness, and death in high concentrations by displacing oxygen from the atmosphere, especially in enclosed spaces. Chemical asphyxiants (e.g., carbon monoxide, phosphine, nitric oxide) interfere with oxygen transport and/or oxidative metabolism, leading to tissue hypoxia, metabolic acidosis, and cardiovascular collapse.

pEcL9V0.title: Fibrothorax
pEcL9V0.description: A restrictive lung disease characterized by extensive pleural fibrosis causing respiratory insufficiency. Etiologies include iatrogenic injury (e.g., pleurodesis), infection (e.g., empyema, tuberculosis), inflammatory disorders (e.g., collagen vascular disease), and environmental exposures (e.g., asbestos).

JEcs9V0.title: Aclidinium
JEcs9V0.description: A reversible, competitive inhibitor of M3 muscarinic receptors in bronchial smooth muscle that causes bronchodilation. Used to treat acute exacerbations of asthma and COPD.

qEcC9V0.title: Pulmonary hygiene
qEcC9V0.description: A collection of methods to clear pulmonary and airway secretions in patients with impaired endogenous clearance (e.g., aspiration or inadequate cough), with the goal of maintaining upper and lower airway patency and preventing aspiration. Includes oral hygiene measures, tracheal suctioning, administration of mucus-controlling agents, bronchoscopy, kinetic therapy, and chest physiotherapy.

HEcKCV0.title: Primary psoas abscess
HEcKCV0.description: A psoas abscess secondary to hematogenous or lymphatic spread of a pathogen from a distant and often occult primary focus.

sEctCV0.title: Secondary psoas abscess
sEctCV0.description: A psoas abscess secondary to the continuous spread of a pathogen from an adjacent infectious focus, e.g., vertebral osteomyelitis or acute appendicitis.

tEcXxV0.title: Whole-body CT
tEcXxV0.description: A type of imaging that is primarily used to assess injuries in polytrauma patients. In polytrauma patients, the whole body CT sequence typically consists of a noncontrast CT of the head and spine, a thoracic and upper abdominal CT with angiography, and abdominal and pelvic CT in the portal venous phase.

FEcgxV0.title: Auto-PEEP
FEcgxV0.description: A descriptor in mechanical ventilation that describes the use of positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) generated by the patient (not the ventilator). Occurs due to incomplete expiration (i.e., air trapping) at the end of a breath cycle due to outflow obstruction (e.g., due to asthma or COPD). Increases the risk of breath-stacking and dynamic hyperinflation.

8EcOxV0.title: Dynamic hyperinflation
8EcOxV0.description: A phenomenon that can occur in patients who are mechanically ventilated with high auto-PEEP. Characterized by the initiation of a new breath before complete expiration occurs (i.e., breath-stacking), which leads to progressively increased airway and intrathoracic pressures with each cycle. Results in increased work of breathing, dyspnea, ineffective ventilation, barotrauma, impaired hemodynamics, ventilator dyssynchrony, and unreliable monitoring.

uEcpxV0.title: Foreign body reaction
uEcpxV0.description: A condition caused by the inflammatory response to an exogenous substance (e.g., retained suture, debris introduced by trauma). Can manifest with localized pain and swelling and increase the risk of developing infection.

EEc8xV0.title: Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation
EEc8xV0.description: An analgesic therapy used to modify pain perception by administering continuous electrical impulses via electrodes on the skin.

destinations.label: Principles of pain management → Subtypes and variants

vEcAxV0.title: PLC
vEcAxV0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Phospholipase C
2. Posterolateral corner of the knee
3. Pityriasis lichenoides chronica

ZvcZAV0.title: RR interval
ZvcZAV0.description: The interval of time between two successive R waves on an ECG. A sinus rhythm has a constant or regular RR interval, which is typically 0.6–1 second. Arrhythmias have variable RR intervals, which can be regularly irregular (i.e., the RR variation follows a regular pattern, as in second-degree heart block) or irregularly irregular (i.e., variable RR interval with no pattern, as in atrial fibrillation).

0vceAV0.title: Cyclin A
0vceAV0.description: A protein that regulates cell cycle transition by binding to cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) 1 and 2. The transcription of cyclin A begins at the G1 restriction point and peaks in the middle of the S phase. The cyclin A-CDK2 complex allows the transition from the G1 to the S phase, and the cyclin A-CDK1 complex allows the transition from the S to the G2 phase.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

avcQAV0.title: Cyclin E
avcQAV0.description: A protein that regulates the transition from the G1 to the S phase of the cell cycle by binding to cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) and activating it.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

YvcnAV0.title: Cyclin C
YvcnAV0.description: A protein that regulates cell cycle transition by binding to cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) 3 and 8. The cyclin C-CDK3 complex allows the transition from the G0 to the G1 phase, and the cyclin C-CDK8 complex regulates gene transcription by phosphorylating transcription factors and RNA polymerase II.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle regulation

bvcHAV0.title: Janus kinase 3 protein
bvcHAV0.description: A protein involved in function of the immune system. A part of the JAK/STAT signaling pathway. Regulates growth of B cells, T cells, and natural killer cells.

Xvc9AV0.title: Strawberry gingivitis
Xvc9AV0.description: A characteristic feature of granulomatosis with polyangiitis characterized by painful, erythematous, gingival inflammation with petechiae that results in the appearance of the surface of a strawberry.

cvca_V0.title: Mesometrium
cvca_V0.description: The largest part of the broad ligament of the uterus. Covers the uterus and extends laterally, connecting it to the pelvic wall.

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Ligaments of the female pelvis

media.title: Supporting ligaments of the uterus (dorsal view)

1vc2_V0.title: Push-dose vasopressors
1vc2_V0.description: A group of vasopressor medications administered as an immediate temporizing measure in patients with critically low blood pressure to prevent hemodynamic collapse. Agents with short onset and half-life (e.g., phenylephrine) are given as an intravenous bolus while waiting for fluid and vasopressor infusions to be prepared or during procedures associated with transient hypotension.

WvcP_V0.title: Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale
WvcP_V0.description: A standardized and validated clinical tool to assess sedation and agitation in critically ill patient. Ranges from unarousable (-5) to combative (+4).  Used as a target to titrate sedative medications in critical care settings.

dvco_V0.title: Aprosodia
dvco_V0.description: An inability to convey or interpret variations in the tone of voice. Caused by lesions in the Wernicke area of the nondominant hemisphere. Patients with aprosodia usually have robotic speech.

VvcG_V0.title: Globus sensation
VvcG_V0.description: A sensation of a lump or foreign body in the throat. Can be persistent or intermittent. Typically improves with repeated swallowing. Most commonly associated with gastroesophageal reflux disease and anxiety.

evcx_V0.title: Esophageal trachealization
evcx_V0.description: An endoscopic finding of multiple rings in the esophagus, which results in a furrowed or corrugated appearance similar to the trachea. The most common underlying cause is eosinophilic esophagitis.

UvcbzV0.title: Sphygmomanometry
UvcbzV0.description: The measurement of blood pressure using a sphygmomanometer, a device that consists of an inflatable cuff and a manometer.

2vcTzV0.title: Patient-ventilator dyssynchrony
2vcTzV0.description: A phenomenon that can occur in mechanically ventilated patients, characterized by a mismatch in breathing phase and/or airflow between patient and equipment. Complications include discomfort, hypoxia, barotrauma, and prolonged need for mechanical ventilation.

fvckzV0.title: Lean process improvement
fvckzV0.description: Quality improvement methodology that focuses on eliminating unnecessary steps in delivering patient care. Aims to optimize workflows, reduce waste, and improve the overall quality of care.

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

Tvc6zV0.title: Dupilumab
Tvc6zV0.description: A monoclonal antibody against the interleukin-4 receptor that results in decreased release of cytokines, chemokines, nitric oxide, and IgE. Used to treat asthma and atopic dermatitis.

gvcFzV0.title: PIP
gvcFzV0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Proximal interphalangeal
2. Peak inspiratory pressure

hvcc-V0.title: Ideal body weight
hvcc-V0.description: The theoretical ideal weight of a patient, estimated based on their height using the following formulas: For men, IBW = [50 kg + 2.3 × (height in inches - 60)] and for women, IBW = [45.5 kg + 2.3 × (height in inches - 60)]. Initially derived to represent a target or desirable body weight to calculate nutritional intake. Also used to guide drug dosing and targets for endotracheal tube depth and tidal volumes in mechanically ventilated patients.

3vcS-V0.title: Arterial line
3vcS-V0.description: An intravascular catheter inserted into the lumen of an artery (e.g., the radial artery) in critical care and operative settings for the purposes of continuous invasive blood pressure monitoring and access for frequent arterial blood sampling.

Rvcl-V0.title: Traumatic pneumothorax
Rvcl-V0.description: A type of pneumothorax that results from a blunt or penetrating trauma to the chest wall. Contrast with spontaneous pneumothorax.

ivcJ-V0.title: Alarm fatigue
ivcJ-V0.description: A phenomenon of clinician desensitization to alarms (e.g., from electronic record and ordering systems, monitors, ventilators) due to an excessive proportion of false, nuisance, and inopportune alarms. Associated with adverse outcomes in patient safety.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

Qvcu-V0.title: Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia
Qvcu-V0.description: A category of ventricular tachyarrhythmias characterized by a wide QRS complex (>120 ms; or 3 small squares on the ECG), in which all the QRS complexes appear similar in axis, amplitude, and duration from beat to beat, as they arise from a singular focus. The rhythm is regular and the heart rate is typically 120–300/min.

destinations.label: Management of tachycardia → Stable wide-complex tachycardia

media.title: Comparison of monomorphic and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT), including torsades de pointes

jvc_-V0.title: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
jvc_-V0.description: A category of ventricular tachyarrhythmias characterized by a wide QRS complex (>120 ms; or 3 small squares on the ECG), in which the QRS complexes vary in axis, amplitude, and duration from beat to beat, as they may arise from multiple foci. The rhythm may be regular or irregular and the rate is highly variable. Includes torsades de pointes, as well as VT arising from ARVC, Brugada syndrome, or digoxin toxicity.

destinations.label: Management of tachycardia → Stable wide-complex tachycardia

media.title: Comparison of monomorphic and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT), including torsades de pointes

PvcWZe0.title: Esophageal hypermotility disorders
PvcWZe0.description: A group of conditions characterized by increased and often unsynchronized esophageal peristalsis. Typically manifests with central chest pain and dysphagia. Includes diffuse esophageal spasm and hypercontractile esophagus.

4vc3Ze0.title: Tropical pulmonary eosinophilia
4vc3Ze0.description: A rare complication of filariasis caused by a hypersensitivity reaction to microfilariae. Characteristic findings including eosinophilia, wheezing, and fever.

kvcmZe0.title: Nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium
kvcmZe0.description: A type of squamous epithelium that is not protected by layers of dead, keratin-containing cells. Sites with this type of epithelium include the linings of the corneas, esophagus, anal cavity, vagina, and certain parts of oral cavity (e.g., soft palate, ventral surface of the tongue, floor of the mouth, buccal mucosa).

OvcIZe0.title: Microfilaria
OvcIZe0.description: The blood circulating stage of filariasis-causing roundworms. Microfilariae are released into circulation by adult roundworms and can be picked up by vector organisms during blood meals. In the vector organisms, microfilariae develop into larval worms, which can infect a host organism on the next blood meal. Can be detected on peripheral blood smear.

Nvc-Ze0.title: Electrical storm
Nvc-Ze0.description: A syndrome of electrical instability in the heart, defined by ≥ 3 episodes of sustained ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, or appropriate shocks delivered by an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator within a 24-hour period. This condition can be life-threatening and occurs most often in patients with myocardial infarction, structural heart disease, and inherited cardiac arrhythmias.

mvcV0e0.title: Ventilator-induced lung injury
mvcV0e0.description: A syndrome that can occur in mechanically ventilated patients. Caused by a combination of excess pressure (barotrauma), excess volume (volutrauma), repetitive alveolar opening and closing (atelectrauma), release of inflammatory mediators from the lung (biotrauma), and oxygen toxicity.

ovc0ae0.title: Acute gastritis
ovc0ae0.description: A condition of acute inflammation caused by gastric mucosal injury. Characterized by neutrophilic infiltration on histopathologic analysis.

qvcCae0.title: Instrumental dead space
qvcCae0.description: The part of the circuit in patients who are mechanically ventilated that conducts air but does not participate in gas exchange and lies outside of the patient's airway. Includes the endotracheal tube, connectors, ventilator tubing, and inner compartments of the respirator.

IvcYYe0.title: Peak inspiratory pressure
IvcYYe0.description: The maximum air pressure measured during inspiration in patients who are mechanically ventilated. Reflects airway resistance and lung compliance. Values > 35–40 cm H₂O are considered elevated. Correlates with a higher risk of ventilator-induced lung injury in pressure-controlled ventilation modes.

rvcfYe0.title: Plateau pressure
rvcfYe0.description: The maximum air pressure in patients who are mechanically ventilated, measured during a pause at the end of inspiration when airflow has ceased and pressure has equilibrated through the elastic lung tissue. Reflects lung compliance and alveolar pressure. Values > 30 cm H₂O are considered elevated. Correlates with a higher risk of ventilator-induced lung injury in volume-controlled ventilation modes.

uvcpbe0.title: Cardiac implantable electronic device interrogation
uvcpbe0.description: The evaluation, monitoring, and analysis of the data, operation, and settings of devices such as pacemakers and AICDs to identify any malfunction and guide their reprogramming if necessary.

yvcdce0.title: Hertoghe sign
yvcdce0.description: A dermatologic finding characterized by thinning of the lateral portion of the eyebrows. Associated with atopic dermatitis.

AvcRce0.title: Relapsing polychondritis
AvcRce0.description: A rare inflammatory disease with an autoimmune component, characterized by chondritis (e.g., auricular, nasal, and/or laryngotracheobronchial) with or without systemic connective tissue involvement (e.g., arthropathy, episcleritis, and/or valvular heart disease). Laryngotracheobronchial chondritis may be life-threatening, requiring urgent tracheotomy.

_vc5ce0.title: CMT
_vc5ce0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
2. Cervical motion tenderness
3. Congenital muscular torticollis

aDcQ1e0.title: Red flags for headache
aDcQ1e0.description: A characteristic in a patient with headache that suggests a potentially dangerous underlying cause requiring urgent investigation. This may include certain patient characteristics (e.g., anticoagulation use), headache features (e.g., thunderclap onset), or accompanying symptoms (e.g., change in mental state).

VDcGWe0.title: Glucagon tolerance test
VDcGWe0.description: A test used to assess an individual's physiological response to glucagon. Often used at the conclusion of a 72-hour fasting plasma glucose test for the workup of hypoglycemia. Historically used in the workup for growth hormone deficiency.

UDcbde0.title: Familial amyloid cardiomyopathy
UDcbde0.description: An autosomal dominant form of hereditary amyloidosis caused by mutated transthyretin protein (ATTR). Typically affects the ventricular endomyocardium and causes restrictive cardiomyopathy and arrhythmias.

2DcTde0.title: Myeloid cell lineage
2DcTde0.description: The group of cells that arise from the common myeloid progenitor cells. Includes erythrocytes, thrombocytes, granulocytes, and monocytes.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

fDckde0.title: Transient lower esophageal sphincter relaxation
fDckde0.description: A relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter that occurs independently of the act of swallowing. It is a physiological reflex most likely mediated by the vagus nerve in response to gastric distension. An increase in the frequency of TLESRs can lead to gastroesophageal reflux disease.

TDc6de0.title: Oophoropexy
TDc6de0.description: A surgical procedure to prevent the recurrence of ovarian torsion. The utero-ovarian ligaments are plicated or the ovary is fixed to either the posterior abdominal or pelvic sidewall. This procedure is not routinely recommended because its effects on fertility are yet to be established.

SDcyde0.title: Expiratory positive airway pressure
SDcyde0.description: The pressure provided to the patient by a mechanical ventilator that is present throughout the breathing cycle and measurable at end-expiration. Used to describe parameters for BiPAP and pressure-support ventilation modes. Equivalent to CPAP if no additional inspiratory support is provided. Often used interchangeably with the term PEEP.

hDccVe0.title: Inspiratory positive airway pressure
hDccVe0.description: The pressure provided to the patient by a mechanical ventilator that is present during the inspiratory phase. Represents the sum of the expiratory positive airway pressure (EPAP) and any additional inspiratory pressure support. Used to describe parameters for BiPAP and pressure-support ventilation modes.

media.title: Airway pressure in spontaneous breathing and mechanical ventilation

PDcWee0.title: Ventilation strategies
PDcWee0.description: The selection of the most appropriate mode of ventilation and ventilation parameters for the underlying pulmonary pathophysiology. Examples include continuous positive airway pressure for cardiogenic pulmonary edema and mechanical ventilation with low tidal volume and high positive end-expiratory pressure for ARDS.

kDcmee0.title: PDA
kDcmee0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Patent ductus arteriosus
2. Posterior descending coronary artery

destinations.label: Acyanotic congenital heart defects → Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)

media.title: Cardiac hemodynamics in patent ductus arteriosus

ODcIee0.title: Bite block
ODcIee0.description: A rigid intraoral device used in intubated patients to protect the teeth of the patient and any flexible intraoral tubing (e.g., an endotracheal tube) from damage or obstruction from biting and/or jaw clenching.

lDcvee0.title: Oxygen toxicity
lDcvee0.description: A constellation of adverse effects of prolonged exposure to high concentrations of supplemental oxygen therapy (e.g., from high-flow nasal cannula therapy). Free-radical formation causes cellular damage and dysfunction, triggering apoptosis and inflammatory cascades that primarily affect the respiratory and central nervous systems.

NDc-ee0.title: Hyperoxemia
NDc-ee0.description: An excessive supply of oxygen to tissue (i.e., arterial oxygen partial pressure > 120 mm Hg). Can lead to oxygen toxicity.

mDcVUe0.title: Normoxemia
mDcVUe0.description: A degree of arterial oxygenation within normal limits (i.e., arterial oxygen partial pressure of 80–120 mm Hg).

5DciUe0.title: Collins method
