5DciUe0.description: A mathematical formula used to calculate the size of a pneumothorax using a chest x-ray taken in PA view with the patient in the erect posture. The interpleural distance is measured in cm at the apex (A), the upper half (B), and the lower half (C) of the collapsed lung. The size of a pneumothorax (Y) = 4.2 + [4.7 x (A + B + C)]. This method cannot be used with supine CXR, in children, and in hydropneumothoraces.

media.title: Collins method for calculation of pneumothorax size

MDcMUe0.title: Aromatic amino acid
MDcMUe0.description: An amino acid that contains an aromatic ring. Examples include tryptophane, phenylalanine, and tyrosine.

nDc7Ue0.title: Desmoplastic melanoma
nDc7Ue0.description: A rare type of melanoma that most commonly develops on sun-damaged skin of elderly, light-skinned individuals. Typically manifests as a pigmented or skin-colored macule, papule, or nodule that is often symptomatic (e.g., painful or tingling) due to perineural invasion. Characterized histopathologically by scant spindle cells and minimal cellular atypia.

LDcwUe0.title: Esophagogastric junction outflow obstruction
LDcwUe0.description: A rare condition characterized by incomplete lower esophageal sphincter relaxation that may be associated with weak peristalsis, resulting in stasis of esophageal contents in a third of those affected. Typically manifests with dysphagia, retrosternal chest pain, and heartburn. Diagnosed on esophageal manometry. May resolve spontaneously. Botox injections may be useful in those with persistent symptoms.

oDc02e0.title: Medial pterygoid muscle
oDc02e0.description: A muscle of mastication that originates from the sphenoid bone and palatine bone and inserts into the medial surface of the mandibular angle. Innervated by the medial pterygoid nerve, a branch of the mandibular nerve. Bilateral contraction of these muscles elevates the mandible. Unilateral contraction deviates the mandible to the contralateral side.

6Dcj2e0.title: Indwelling pleural catheter
6Dcj2e0.description: A small tube that is tunneled through the skin and inserted into the pleural cavity. Primarily used for frequent drainage of reaccumulating pleural fluid (e.g., malignant effusions) because it can remain in situ for months.

pDcL2e0.title: X-linked hereditary sideroblastic anemia
pDcL2e0.description: The most common type of congenital sideroblastic anemia. Caused by mutations in the heme synthesis enzyme delta-aminolevulinic acid synthase. Manifestations include microcytic anemia, basophilic stippling on peripheral blood smear, and ringed sideroblasts on bone marrow aspirate.

JDcs2e0.title: Trichuriasis
JDcs2e0.description: A tropical gastrointestinal parasitosis caused by the whipworm Trichuris trichiura. The infection, which is acquired by ingesting the eggs of this whipworm, is often asymptomatic. Heavy infestations can cause abdominal pain, bloody or mucoid diarrhea, anemia, and, in the pediatric age group, rectal prolapse.

qDcC2e0.title: Bacterial secretion systems
qDcC2e0.description: A collection of protein complexes found on bacterial cell membranes that mediate the release of substances (e.g., virulence factors) into the surrounding environment. Different secretion systems can be distinguished based on structure, function, and specificity (e.g., type III secretion system).

IDcYfe0.title: Cathelicidins
IDcYfe0.description: A family of antimicrobial peptides most commonly found in neutrophils, macrophages, and epithelial cells. Part of the innate immune system. One cathelicidin is LL-37, which can neutralize bacterial lipopolysaccharide.

rDcffe0.title: Morphine milligram equivalent
rDcffe0.description: A tool that uses oral morphine as a reference point to compare the analgesic effect of different opioids. Does not account for incomplete cross-tolerance or pharmacokinetic differences.

7Dc4fe0.title: OME
7Dc4fe0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Otitis media with effusion
2. Oral morphine equivalent

HDcKfe0.title: Incomplete cross-tolerance
HDcKfe0.description: A pharmacologic phenomenon characterized by the development of tolerance to the effects of one drug (through chronic use) that leads to partial tolerance to the effect of another drug. Often occurs with drugs that work by the same pharmacologic mechanism (e.g., act on the same receptor). For example, a patient who chronically uses oxycodone can develop tolerance to its effects as well as tolerance to other opioids.

sDctfe0.title: Entry inhibitor
sDctfe0.description: A class of antiretroviral drugs used to treat HIV infection by targeting the process of HIV entry into the cell. There are three main classes of entry inhibitors: attachment inhibitors (e.g., maraviroc), coreceptor binding inhibitors, and fusion inhibitors (e.g., enfuvirtide).

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

FDcgTe0.title: Deltopectoral groove
FDcgTe0.description: A depression located between the deltoid muscle and pectoralis major. Contains the cephalic vein.

uDcpTe0.title: Quadratus lumborum muscle
uDcpTe0.description: A paired muscle of the posterior abdominal wall. Originates from the iliac crest and inserts into the 12th rib and the transverse processes of L1-L4. Unilateral contraction causes lateral flexion of the lumbar spine; bilateral contraction causes extension of the lumbar spine and supports forced expiration.

EDc8Te0.title: Ibalizumab
EDc8Te0.description: A monoclonal antibody that binds to CD4+ cell receptors to block HIV-1 virus from infecting the cell. Does not result in immunosuppression.

vDcATe0.title: Enteroclysis
vDcATe0.description: A radiologic imaging test of the small bowel in which contrast medium (usually barium) is administered via an enteric tube into the beginning of the small bowel. Movement of contrast through the intestine is monitored either via x-ray, CT, or MRI. Can be used to evaluate for mucosal injury (e.g., ulcers), tumors, and signs of inflammation.

media.title: Small bowel stricture in Crohn disease

9DcNge0.title: Activated prothrombin complex concentrate
9DcNge0.description: A plasma derivative used to aid clotting in bleeding disorders. Composed of activated factor VII as well as nonactivated factors II, IX, and X. Activated PCC is licensed for control of bleeding in hemophilia but has been used off-label for anticoagulant reversal.

CDcqge0.title: Middle rectal veins
CDcqge0.description: A pair of veins that drains the anal canal inferior to the pectinate line. Empty into the internal pudendal veins.

xDcEge0.title: Spinal cord injury
xDcEge0.description: An insult to the spinal cord secondary to trauma (most common), disease, or degeneration. Manifestations include sensory and/or motor disturbances below the level of injury.

BDczge0.title: Abdominal radiograph
BDczge0.description: An abdominal radiographic study that assesses the urinary, renal and gastrointestinal system. Often used to evaluate patients with acute abdominal pain and to confirm correct positioning of indwelling devices in the abdomen (e.g., stents, feeding tubes).

yDcdSe0.title: Nasoenteric tube
yDcdSe0.description: A narrow-bore, flexible tube used for short-term enteral feeding. Placed either in the stomach or the second or third portion of the duodenum.

ADcRSe0.title: Computerized physician order entry
ADcRSe0.description: The electronic placing of instructions (e.g., medication orders). Associated with fewer medical errors compared to verbal and written orders.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medication errors

-DcDSe0.title: Closed-loop communication
-DcDSe0.description: A communication method for reducing communication errors, in which the receiver of information repeats that information back to the sender, upon which the sender confirms that the information has been received as intended.

0wcehe0.title: Morbidity and mortality review
0wcehe0.description: A meeting within a hospital in which a department reviews complications and/or deaths that have occurred within its department to review potential systems error and improve professional education and patient care.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Analysis of medical error
Clerkship guide → Attending meetings and conferences

awcQhe0.title: Fishbone diagram
awcQhe0.description: A quality control technique used to break down and visualize the most significant factors that may have contributed to an error or problem.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Analysis of medical error

Ywcnhe0.title: Availability heuristic
Ywcnhe0.description:
A cognitive bias in which judgments are made based on the availability of information in an individual's memory. 
Events that are perceived as significant or that are more easily recalled are considered more representative of the truth than events that are perceived as less significant or that are less easily recalled. Can lead to diagnostic errors (e.g., when a physician makes a premature diagnosis due to having seen several patients with a similar clinical presentation).

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

bwcHhe0.title: Framing bias
bwcHhe0.description: A cognitive bias characterized by the tendency to be influenced by how information is presented (e.g., the order of symptoms and/or emphasis placed on specific findings). Can influence decision-making by patients and lead to diagnostic errors among health care providers.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

Xwc9he0.title: Visceral bias
Xwc9he0.description: A cognitive bias in which clinical decisions are influenced by positive or negative feelings towards the patient (e.g., not believing symptoms described by a patient with substance use disorder). Can lead to underdiagnosis or overdiagnosis and/or treatment.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

cwca3e0.title: POEMS syndrome
cwca3e0.description: A rare plasma cell disorder that causes chronic overproduction of proinflammatory cytokines. Manifestations include polyneuropathy (P), organomegaly (O), endocrinopathy (E), increased production of monoclonal plasma proteins (M), and skin changes (S).

1wc23e0.title: Emergency surgical airway
1wc23e0.description: The creation of a patent airway in the anterior neck to facilitate emergency oxygenation. Used in "can't intubate, can't ventilate" situations after all other maneuvers have failed. Examples include a needle cricothyrotomy or a surgical cricothyrotomy.

dwco3e0.title: Flavoxate
dwco3e0.description: An antispasmotic agent that inhibits phosphodiesterase and results in the relaxation of smooth muscle. Used to treat bladder spasticity.

VwcG3e0.title: Overflow diarrhea
VwcG3e0.description: A condition in which partial bowel obstruction blocks the passage of solid stool, while still allowing liquid stool to pass.

ewcx3e0.title: Pain out of proportion to physical examination
ewcx3e0.description: A type of severe pain experienced by an individual that is inconsistent with the physical examination (e.g., little or no findings that could explain the severity). Can be caused by conditions that compromise blood flow (e.g., compartment syndrome, mesenteric ischemia) or necrotizing infections.

UwcbRe0.title: Bezoar
UwcbRe0.description: A gastrointestinal foreign body formed by accumulated ingested material (e.g., food and plant material, hair, drugs). Can cause gastrointestinal obstruction. Risk factors include gastric dysmotility (e.g., from organic or drug-induced causes) and gastric outlet obstruction.

2wcTRe0.title: Turnaround time
2wcTRe0.description: The time between a diagnostic test being ordered and the result becoming available for interpretation. Can be used to help determine which test should be ordered and track the efficiency of processes in clinical laboratories and diagnostic imaging departments.

fwckRe0.title: Small bowel follow-through
fwckRe0.description: A fluoroscopic technique that involves the ingestion of an oral contrast (e.g., barium or a water-soluble agent) followed by dynamic x-ray imaging of the small intestine. Used to assess bowel diameter, peristalsis, and patency. Can diagnose obstructions or lesions of the bowel lumen.

Twc6Re0.title: Water-soluble contrast challenge
Twc6Re0.description: A test involving the ingestion of water-soluble contrast material, followed by abdominal x-ray 8 and 24 hours later. Used to diagnose bowel obstruction, assess the success of nonoperative management, and as an adjunctive treatment in partial or low-grade small bowel obstruction.

gwcFRe0.title: Air-fluid level
gwcFRe0.description: A radiologically visible interface between a collection of fluid and the air above within a hollow structure (e.g., a segment of bowel or a cavitary lung lesion). Can appear as a flat line or a crescent depending on the viscosity of the fluid. Visible on erect and decubitus radiographs and axial CT scans. Causes include bowel obstruction and several types of lung lesion.

SwcyRe0.title: Multiplanar reconstruction
SwcyRe0.description: The process of converting diagnostic imaging data from one view (e.g., axial) to another (e.g., coronal or sagittal). Usually used in multi-detector CT scanning and aids in the generation of three-dimensional reconstructions.

3wcSie0.title: Enteric tube
3wcSie0.description: A term encompassing several tubes that can be inserted into the stomach and/or intestines from various points of entry for the purpose of suction, feeding, and/or administration of medication. Includes orogastric and nasogastric tubes, oroenteric and nasoenteric tubes, and gastrostomy and jejunostomy tubes.

Rwclie0.title: Cecopexy
Rwclie0.description: A laparoscopic or open surgical procedure that involves fixation of the cecum to the abdominal wall. Can be used in the management of cecal volvulus.

Qwcuie0.title: Drug clearance
Qwcuie0.description: A measure of the rate of drug elimination. Defined as the plasma volume that is completely cleared of a substance in a given period of time.

jwc_ie0.title: Renal clearance
jwc_ie0.description: The plasma volume that is completely cleared of a substance in a given period of time. Renal clearance is calculated by the following formula: Clearance of X (mL/min) = (urine concentration of X (mg/mL) × (urine flow rate (mL/min)) / Plasma concentration of X (mg/mL).

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function

OwcIQe0.title: Percutaneous bowel decompression
OwcIQe0.description: A palliative procedure used to treat malignant bowel obstruction when surgery is not indicated (e.g., metastatic cancer that causes multi-level obstruction). Involves extraction of intestinal fluid and air from the bowel by needle puncture through the abdominal wall under ultrasound guidance, followed by placement of a drainage tube.

lwcvQe0.title: Endoscopic decompression, detorsion, and reduction
lwcvQe0.description: An emergency endoscopic procedure used to treat uncomplicated sigmoid volvulus that aims to relieve intraluminal pressure and rotate twisted bowel segments, restoring their vascular integrity. Often accompanied by placement of a temporary colon decompression tube.

destinations.label: Sigmoid volvulus and cecal volvulus → Treatment

Nwc-Qe0.title: Endoscopic bowel decompression
Nwc-Qe0.description: An endoscopic procedure used to treat bowel obstruction in patients for whom surgery is not indicated (e.g., malignant multilevel obstruction). Involves decompression of intraluminal contents and placement of a transanal drainage tube.

mwcVje0.title: Onchocercoma
mwcVje0.description: A subcutaneous nodule containing adult worms of Onchocerca volvulus in patients with onchocerciasis. Typically located over bony prominences.

5wcije0.title: Mitochondrial toxicity
5wcije0.description: A disruption of mitochondrial function most commonly caused by HIV treatment with nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors. NRTIs inhibit the enzyme responsible for the replication of mitochondrial DNA. Symptoms include myopathy, peripheral neuropathy, lipodystrophy, and hepatic steatosis with lactic acidosis.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

MwcMje0.title: Dihydrofolate reductase inhibitors
MwcMje0.description: A class of drugs used as antibacterial (e.g., trimethoprim), antiprotozoal (e.g., pyrimethamine), and anticancer (e.g., methotrexate) agents.

nwc7je0.title: Atazanavir
nwc7je0.description: A protease inhibitor used as part of an antiretroviral regimen for the treatment of HIV infection. Inhibits cleavage of Gag-Pol polyprotein precursors, which results in the formation of noninfectious viral particles. Adverse effects include nephrolithiasis, kidney injury, and hyperbilirubinemia.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

KwcUPe0.title: COVID-19
KwcUPe0.description: A respiratory infection caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Can be asymptomatic or manifest with fever, dry cough, shortness of breath, anorexia, fatigue, and/or myalgia. Less common symptoms include headache, runny nose, and diarrhea. Can progress to severe pneumonia leading to acute respiratory distress syndrome.

6wcjPe0.title: Digenic inheritance
6wcjPe0.description: A mode of inheritance characterized by two genetic loci whose allelic contributions determine the resulting phenotype. Examples include certain hereditary causes of deafness, certain hereditary forms of nephrotic syndrome, and autosomal recessive early-onset familial forms of Parkinson disease.

pwcLPe0.title: IgG4-related disease
pwcLPe0.description: A progressive immune-mediated fibroinflammatory condition characterized by sclerotic masses and organ dysfunction. The most common manifestations include type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis, retroperitoneal fibrosis, sialadenitis and dacryoadenitis, Riedel thyroiditis, and tubulointerstitial nephritis.

IwcY4e0.title: Diagnostic thoracentesis
IwcY4e0.description: A procedure used to obtain a sample of pleural fluid for analysis in order to determine the cause of the pleural effusion. Performed by inserting a needle into the pleural cavity.

rwcf4e0.title: Therapeutic thoracentesis
rwcf4e0.description: A procedure used to drain pleural fluid (pleural effusion) to relieve symptoms (e.g., dyspnea). Performed by inserting a needle into the pleural cavity.

7wc44e0.title: Dysentery
7wc44e0.description: A condition of intestinal infection and inflammation that results in mucoid-bloody diarrhea with an inflammatory exudate composed of polymorphonuclear leukocytes. Causative pathogens include Shigella (bacillary dysentery) and Entamoeba histolytica (amebic dysentery).

GwcB4e0.title: Limb ataxia
GwcB4e0.description: The inability to perform coordinated movements with the upper and/or lower extremities, which can manifest with dysmetria. Positive finger-to-nose test indicates ataxia of the upper limbs and positive heel-knee-shin test indicates ataxia of the lower limbs. Most commonly results from lesions of the cerebellar hemispheres.

twcXke0.title: Signs of unstable bradycardia
twcXke0.description: A group of signs and symptoms caused by hypoperfusion that occur if severe bradycardia leads to insufficient cardiac output. Features include chest pain, pulmonary edema, respiratory distress, shock, altered mental status, low oxygen saturation, hypotension, and poor capillary refill.

8wcOke0.title: Amebic dysentery
8wcOke0.description: An infectious disease caused by the anaerobic protozoan Entamoeba histolytica. Manifests with bloody diarrhea and painful defecation. Diagnosis is confirmed based on visualization of cysts and/or trophozoites in stool.

9wcNOe0.title: Dizziness
9wcNOe0.description: An umbrella term commonly used by patients to describe a variety of sensations, including vertigo, presyncope, imbalance, and confusion. In the specialist context of vestibular disorders, dizziness can be defined more specifically as a nonvertiginous disturbance in spatial orientation.

CwcqOe0.title: Sialoendoscopy
CwcqOe0.description: A minimally invasive procedure in which a flexible endoscope is inserted into the salivary duct to evaluate and treat salivary gland disorders.

xwcEOe0.title: Wormian bones
xwcEOe0.description: Small, irregular accessory bones that develop within cranial sutures, typically on the lambdoid suture. Often incidental but sometimes associated with conditions such as osteogenesis imperfecta, rickets, progeria, and Down syndrome.

BwczOe0.title: Incident reporting system
BwczOe0.description: A system for voluntary reporting of medical errors to improve patient safety.

ywcdle0.title: Isavuconazole
ywcdle0.description: A triazole antifungal that works by inhibiting the synthesis of ergosterol, a component of the fungal cell membrane. Used in the treatment of severe aspergillosis and mucormycosis.

AwcRle0.title: Cevimeline
AwcRle0.description: A cholinergic agonist that binds to and activates muscarinic receptors, which leads to increased exocrine gland (e.g., salivary, sweat) secretions and increased gastrointestinal and urinary tract muscle tone. Used to relieve dry mouth associated with Sjögren syndrome.

_wc5le0.title: Systems error
_wc5le0.description: A medical error that results from a series of actions and/or factors in treatment or diagnosis, including flaws in technical design, organizational design, decision-making, and failure to recognize and mitigate hazards and risks in the health care setting.

zwcrle0.title: Myoedema
zwcrle0.description: A localized painless muscle contraction induced by light muscle percussion or pressure that manifests with palpable muscle swelling. This finding is highly specific of hypothyroid myopathy.

-wcDle0.title: Vermilion
-wcDle0.description: The labial mucosa (i.e., the colored portion of the upper and lower lips).

Z9cZNe0.title: Epidural space
Z9cZNe0.description: A potential space between bones of the cranium/spine and the dura mater.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Meninges, falces, and spaces

09ceNe0.title: Protected health information
09ceNe0.description: The information related to an individual's health status and stored by health care providers in order to identify and treat the individual. Includes patient demographics, medical history, laboratory results, and procedural results. Protected under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

a9cQNe0.title: Ground-glass opacity
a9cQNe0.description: A chest x-ray and CT finding that refers to areas of increased density (e.g., partially occupied air spaces, thickening of the interstitium, partial atelectasis) with preserved visibility of bronchial structures and blood vessels. This finding is nonspecific and can be seen in acute respiratory distress syndrome, viral pneumonia, and malignancy.

media.title: Ground glass opacification in Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia

Y9cnNe0.title: β-carotene
Y9cnNe0.description: A vitamin A precursor and orange pigment found in yellow and leafy vegetables and fruits. Functions include antioxidant properties, the ability to stimulate the adaptive immune system, and the ability to induce tumor cell apoptosis.

b9cHNe0.title: Omega-3 fatty acid
b9cHNe0.description: An unsaturated fatty acid found mainly in fish and plant oils. Includes eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), and α-linolenic acid (ALA). Important for fetal development. May prevent cardiovascular disease.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

X9c9Ne0.title: Degarelix
X9c9Ne0.description: A gonadotropin-releasing hormone antagonist used in the treatment of advanced prostate cancer. Adverse effects include injection site reactions and hot flashes.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

c9came0.title: Carotenemia
c9came0.description: An increased serum concentration of carotenes (e.g., from consumption of carrots, sweet potatoes, kale, oranges). Can manifest with yellowish skin discoloration.

19c2me0.title: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2
19c2me0.description: A novel coronavirus that causes COVID-19, the pandemic disease that primarily causes respiratory illness, including severe pneumonia. Transmitted person-to-person via respiratory droplets. Identified as the causative pathogen of a cluster of cases of pneumonia first detected in Wuhan, China.

d9come0.title: SCA
d9come0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Superior cerebellar artery
2. Spinocerebellar artery
3. Spinocerebellar ataxia
4. Sickle cell anemia

V9cGme0.title: Warthin-Finkeldey cell
V9cGme0.description: A multinucleated giant cell formed from the fusion of lymphocytes. Found within hyperplastic lymph nodes during the early stages of measles and in HIV infection. Typically composed of 8-15 fused nuclei with no cytoplasm.

e9cxme0.title: Red flags for dyspepsia
e9cxme0.description: A collection of features that includes age > 60 years, family history of gastrointestinal malignancy, unintentional weight loss, anorexia, dysphagia, odynophagia, persistent vomiting, and signs of gastrointestinal bleeding (e.g., unexplained iron deficiency anemia, melena).

U9cb5e0.title: Ectopic pinealoma
U9cb5e0.description: An extremely rare tumor that originates in brain tissue outside the pineal gland and appears histologically similar to parenchymal pinealomas. Most commonly located in the chiasmal-sellar region and can mimic pituitary adenoma both clinically (e.g., with visual disturbances, headaches, hypopituitarism) and on imaging (i.e., a sellar mass). More commonly develops in children.

f9ck5e0.title: Lung recruitment maneuvers
f9ck5e0.description: A series of interventions performed in mechanically ventilated patients to enhance and homogenize gas exchange in nonaerated portions of the lungs. Increased transpulmonary pressure is transiently applied using a variety of strategies to open up and maintain the patency of collapsed alveoli.

g9cF5e0.title: Electronic fetal heart rate monitoring
g9cF5e0.description: The measurement of fetal heartbeat (including baseline heart rate, accelerations, and decelerations) and uterine contractions (including frequency, intensity, and duration) with a cardiotocograph.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

h9ccMe0.title: High frequency oscillatory ventilation
h9ccMe0.description: A ventilation strategy used as a rescue maneuver in acute respiratory failure (e.g., ARDS). Uses small tidal volumes (smaller than dead space ventilation volumes) at high rates (hence "oscillatory") combined with a constant level of airway pressure. It is thought to decreases the risk of volutrauma (e.g., VILI).

R9clMe0.title: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
R9clMe0.description: The most common type of autoimmune pituitary inflammation (primary hypophysitis). Often occurs in late pregnancy or the postpartum period. Characterized by early lymphocytic infiltration and pituitary enlargement followed by progressive pituitary destruction, atrophy, and fibrosis. Can affect the anterior pituitary gland (i.e., lymphocytic adenohypophysis, which causes adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, hypogonadism), the posterior pituitary gland (i.e., lymphocytic infundibuloneurohypophysitis, which causes diabetes insipidus), or both (i.e., lymphocytic panhypophysitis).

i9cJMe0.title: TBI
i9cJMe0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Traumatic brain injury
2. Tracheobronchial injury
3. Total body irradiation

Q9cuMe0.title: Malperfusion syndrome
Q9cuMe0.description: A complication of aortic dissection where blood flow to major vascular beds is interrupted, resulting in ischemia and end-organ damage. Malperfusion syndrome may affect the gut, kidneys, upper or lower limbs, as well as coronary, spinal, or cerebral circulation.

49c3ne0.title: Imidazole derivatives
49c3ne0.description: A group of antifungal agents with a broad spectrum of activity. They inhibit fungal cytochrome P450, which decreases fungal synthesis of ergosterol from lanosterol, resulting in cell death. Typically used to treat topical infections (e.g., dermatophyte infections, vulvovaginal candidiasis). Examples include clotrimazole, miconazole, and ketoconazole.

O9cIne0.title: Vascular organ of lamina terminalis
O9cIne0.description: A brain area located within the lamina terminalis at the ventral end of the third ventricle. Contains osmoreceptors. Lacks a blood-brain interface. It is one of the circumventricular organs.

m9cVLe0.title: B pattern
m9cVLe0.description: A term used in lung ultrasound to denote the presence of ≥ 3 B lines within one intercostal space. A B pattern suggests an interstitial parenchymal pathology such as pulmonary edema, ARDS, or pneumonia.

59ciLe0.title: B lines
59ciLe0.description: An artifact that appears on lung ultrasound as hyperechoic vertical lines perpendicular to the pleural line that move with respiration, do not fade with depth, obscure pulmonary A-lines, and resemble the beam of a flashlight. Three or more lines indicate increased tissue density (e.g., due to pulmonary edema or atelectasis) and correlate with Kerley B lines on chest x-ray.

media.title: Illustration of B-lines on lung ultrasound

n9c7Le0.title: Minimum necessary standard
n9c7Le0.description: A standard policy for the disclosure of private health information set by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). Disclosure must be limited to the minimum amount necessary to satisfy function (e.g., patient care) or request (e.g., by health insurance).

destinations.label: Ethics of communicating medical information → Confidentiality

L9cwLe0.title: Renal cortical necrosis
L9cwLe0.description: A rare kidney disease caused by sudden-onset, ischemic necrosis of the renal cortex in the kidneys (e.g., due to disseminated intravascular coagulation, obstetric complications, or septic shock). Characterized by vasospasms and microvascular injury with vascular thrombosis.

destinations.label: Acute kidney injury → Subtypes and variants

o9c0oe0.title: Advanced maternal age
o9c0oe0.description: A descriptor for age ≥ 35 years of a pregnant individual at the estimated date of delivery. Associated with an increased risk of pregnancy-related complications such as preterm birth, stillbirth, birth defects (e.g., chromosomal abnormalities), fetal growth restriction, placental abruption, and preeclampsia.

K9cUoe0.title: Encapsulated bacteria
K9cUoe0.description: A group of bacteria that have an outer polysaccharide capsule, which serves as a virulence factor that prevents phagocytosis by host immune cells. Examples include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Neisseria meningitidis, Escherichia coli, Salmonella, Klebsiella, and Group B streptococcus.

69cjoe0.title: Pylephlebitis
69cjoe0.description: A condition of suppurative thrombosis of the portal vein due to an infectious cause (e.g., diverticulitis, appendicitis). Manifestations include fever, abdominal pain (often in the right upper quadrant), nausea, and vomiting.

p9cLoe0.title: Fundal height
p9cLoe0.description: The length from the top of the uterus to the top of the pubic symphysis. From 20 weeks' gestation, fundal height (in cm) roughly approximates the week of gestation. Used to screen for fetal growth abnormalities from 24 weeks' gestation and to roughly estimate gestational age in an emergency.

J9csoe0.title: Branched-chain organic acidemias
J9csoe0.description: A group of autosomal recessive hereditary disorders caused by defects in enzymes required for the breakdown of the products of branched-chain amino acid metabolism. Examples include methylmalonic acidemia, propionic acidemia, and isovaleric acidemia. Typically manifest in infancy with vomiting, lethargy, seizures, hypotonia, failure to thrive, anion gap metabolic acidosis, ketotic hypoglycemia, hyperammonemia and urinary excretion of organic acids.

q9cCoe0.title: Splay
q9cCoe0.description: The difference between the concentration at which a substance can be maximally reabsorbed by the kidney (before excretion begins) and the concentration at which filtration of the substance into the urine begins. Glucose processing by the kidney demonstrates splay. Because nephrons have different tubular maximums for glucose reabsorption, some excrete glucose before others. This results in a smooth transition of the resorption curve to a plateau state as transporters become fully saturated.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Measurement of renal function

I9cYKe0.title: Trial of labor after cesarean
I9cYKe0.description: A planned or attempted childbirth in a mother who has had a prior cesarean delivery. Results in vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) if successful or a repeat cesarean delivery if unsuccessful. Associated with increased risk of rupture of the cesarean scar on the uterus. Contraindicated in patients with a history of > 2 prior low-transverse cesarean deliveries and classic cesarean delivery.

r9cfKe0.title: Anti-PD-1 antibodies
r9cfKe0.description: A group of monoclonal antibodies that serve as immune checkpoint inhibitors. Block the interaction between PD-1 (on T-cells) and PD-L1/2 (on antigen-presenting or tumor cells). Used as part of anticancer immunotherapy. Examples include nivolumab and pembrolizumab.

79c4Ke0.title: Atezolizumab
79c4Ke0.description: An immune checkpoint inhibitor and monoclonal antibody against programmed death-ligand 1 and 2 (PD-L1/2). Used for the treatment of advanced urothelial cancer, lung cancer, and triple-negative breast cancer.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

H9cKKe0.title: Durvalumab
H9cKKe0.description: An immune checkpoint inhibitor and monoclonal antibody against programmed death-ligand 1 and 2 (PD-L1/2). Used for the treatment of advanced urothelial cancer and non-small cell lung cancer.

s9ctKe0.title: Avelumab
s9ctKe0.description: An immune checkpoint inhibitor and monoclonal antibody against programmed death-ligand 1 and 2 (PD-L1/2). Used for the treatment of Merkel cell carcninoma, urothelial cancer, and advanced renal cell carcinoma (first line in combination with axitinib).

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

G9cBKe0.title: GAD
G9cBKe0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Generalized anxiety disorder
2. Glutamic acid decarboxylase

t9cX6e0.title: RPF
t9cX6e0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Renal plasma flow
2. Retroperitoneal fibrosis

F9cg6e0.title: Immune checkpoint
F9cg6e0.description: A mechanism to suppress or modulate T-cell function through expression and interaction of ligands such as PD-1 and CTLA-4. Often enhanced by tumors and in chronic infections. Immune checkpoint inhibitors can be used as anticancer therapies.

89cO6e0.title: PTA
89cO6e0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Percutaneous transluminal angioplasty
2. Peritonsillar abscess
3. Pure tone audiometry

u9cp6e0.title: OCD
u9cp6e0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Obsessive-compulsive disorder
2. Osteochondritis dissecans

v9cA6e0.title: Central vein of the liver
v9cA6e0.description: A vein at the center of the hepatic lobules that collects blood from the liver sinusoids and returns it to the circulation via the hepatic veins, which leave the liver and empty into the vena cava.

D9c1pe0.title: Orthotopic
D9c1pe0.description: A descriptor for something that occurs in the normal location within the body (e.g., orthotopic liver transplantation).

B9czpe0.title: Gonadotroph
B9czpe0.description: A basophilic cell in the anterior pituitary that produces gonadotropins (i.e., follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone). Stimulated by pulsatile gonadotropin-releasing hormone secretion and inhibited by prolactin and gonadocorticoids.

y9cdJe0.title: Arterial embolism
y9cdJe0.description: The occlusion of a peripheral artery by a mass traveling through the bloodstream (embolus). Emboli are most commonly blood clot fragments (thromboemboli) but can also be formed from gas bubbles (air emboli), fat globules (fat emboli), cholesterol crystals (atheroemboli), infectious particles (septic emboli), or foreign bodies (e.g., talc emboli). Can cause stroke, acute limb ischemia, and acute mesenteric ischemia.

_9c5Je0.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
_9c5Je0.description: The excessive accumulation of fat in hepatocytes in the absence of an alternative cause (e.g., heavy alcohol use, drug-induced liver injury) in an individual with at least one cardiometabolic risk factor (e.g., hypertension, hyperlipidemia, impaired glucose tolerance). Previously referred to as nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.

z9crJe0.title: End-stage liver disease
z9crJe0.description: A condition characterized by nonreversible chronic liver failure, most commonly as a result of decompensated cirrhosis.

-9cDJe0.title: Corrected serum calcium concentration
-9cDJe0.description: A calcium concentration that has been corrected to account for the serum albumin concentration. Used to identify if patients who are suspected of having hypo- or hypercalcemia actually have a normal serum calcium concentration as a result of high or low serum albumin concentrations, respectively. Corrected Ca2+ (in mg/dL) = measured total Ca2+ (in mg/dL) + [0.8 x (4.0 - albumin concentration in g/dL)].

ZCcZqe0.title: Risk-reducing mastectomy
ZCcZqe0.description: A mastectomy that is performed in patients with hereditary predispostion to breast cancer (e.g., BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations) in order to decrease the chance of developing breast cancer.

0Cceqe0.title: HIV-1/2 combination immunoassay
0Cceqe0.description: A fourth-generation, enzyme-linked immunoassay that detects antibodies against HIV-1 and HIV-2 serotypes as well as the presence of p24 capsid antigen in serum. Cannot differentiate between HIV-1 and HIV-2 infection. Since 2014, this test has been recommended as the first-line screening test to detect HIV infection.

YCcnqe0.title: Cerebral blood flow
YCcnqe0.description: The volume of blood (in mL) supplied to brain tissue (in units of 100 g) per minute. Directly proportional to cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) and inversely proportional to cerebrovascular resistance (CVR). Maintained relatively constant across a wide range of systemic blood pressure through cerebral autoregulation.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Pathophysiology
Cerebrovascular system → Cerebral blood flow regulation

bCcHqe0.title: Cerebral autoregulation
bCcHqe0.description: The process by which cerebral blood flow (CBF) is maintained constant across a wide range of mean arterial pressures (MAPs), typically between 50–150 mm Hg. Increases in MAP trigger precapillary vascular constriction within seconds; decreases in MAP cause vasodilation. Outside of this range, CBF becomes directly proportional to MAP. Autoregulation can be disrupted by brain injury and its limits are affected by drugs, sympathetic nerve activity, and chronic hypertension.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Pathophysiology

XCc9qe0.title: Secondary brain injury
XCc9qe0.description: The neuronal damage that occurs after an initial insult (e.g., trauma, stroke, hemorrhage) to previously unaffected brain tissue. Mediated by excitotoxic and inflammatory cascades, oxidative stress, secondary ischemia and hypoperfusion, reperfusion injury, and edema. Exacerbated by disturbances in glucose, oxygen delivery, carbon dioxide, temperature regulation, intracranial pressure, hemostasis, and cerebral metabolic demand.

destinations.label: Secondary brain injury and neuroprotective measures → Definitions

cCcaIe0.title: Rectoanal inhibitory reflex
cCcaIe0.description: A process characterized by involuntary relaxation of the internal anal sphincter in response to rectal distension, which facilitates the passage of rectal contents through to the anal canal. Facilitates a determination of whether contents in the rectum are gaseous, solid, or liquid. Also facilitates flatulence without simultaneous passage of feces.

1Cc2Ie0.title: Disconnection hyperprolactinemia
1Cc2Ie0.description: A condition of hyperprolactinemia caused by infundibular stalk damage, which interrupts the inhibitory effect of hypothalamic dopamine on pituitary lactotrophs. Causes include tumors with suprasellar extension and pituitary stalk dissection due to trauma or surgery.

WCcPIe0.title: Jealousy
WCcPIe0.description: A thought process characterized by anxiety or concern over one's possessions and/or relationships. Pathologic jealousy, which results in significant dysfunction that impairs daily life, includes obsessional jealousy and delusional disorder, jealous type.

dCcoIe0.title: Mixed delusion
dCcoIe0.description: A combination of two or more delusions that occur at the same time. Typically, one delusion does not predominate over the other.

VCcGIe0.title: Unspecified delusion
VCcGIe0.description: A fixed, false belief that does not fit the criteria for other types of delusions (e.g., persecutory, jealousy, erotomanic, grandiose, somatic).

eCcxIe0.title: Major adverse cardiac event
eCcxIe0.description: A commonly used umbrella term for endpoints in cardiological studies (e.g., validation of risk-scores or the evaluation of side effects in therapy regimens). There is no established definition of which events are included, but common examples include myocardial infarction, unscheduled PCI, stroke, and death.

UCcbre0.title: Blunt cerebrovascular injury
UCcbre0.description: A group of nonpenetrating injuries (e.g. stretching, impingement) to major head and neck blood vessels (e.g. carotid and vertebral arteries) that can cause stroke through disruption of the intima, formation of wall hematomas or thrombi, and/or occlusion of the vascular lumen.

2CcTre0.title: Endotracheal tube
2CcTre0.description: A tube placed into the trachea through the mouth (orotracheal) or nose (nasotracheal) to maintain a patent airway. Used perioperatively for anesthetized patients and has various indications in emergency medicine, including acute respiratory failure, poor oxygenation or ventilation, and risk of airway compromise.

fCckre0.title: Neurocritical care unit
fCckre0.description: A critical or intensive care unit that provides specialized care for patients with life-threatening neurological and neurosurgical disorders (e.g., intracranial hemorrhage and stroke, traumatic and hypoxic brain injury, neuromuscular disorders). Focuses on specific treatments of these conditions and the management of mechanical ventilation, intracranial pressure, and other issues specific to this population.

gCcFre0.title: Pneumocephalus
gCcFre0.description: The presence of air within the intracranial cavity due to disruption of the dura mater. Etiologies include trauma and intracranial surgery. Manifestations include headache, vomiting, seizures, irritability, and dizziness.

SCcyre0.title: Type and screen
SCcyre0.description: A test that identifies a patient's blood type (i.e., ABO and RhD type) and the presence of antibodies. Does not identify a specific unit of blood for transfusion.

hCcc7e0.title: Compatibility testing
hCcc7e0.description: A pretransfusion test that evaluates whether a specified unit of red blood cells is compatible with a specified recipient's blood type and antibody screen. May include electronic or serologic crossmatching.

3CcS7e0.title: Hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma
3CcS7e0.description: A rare subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by a proliferation of T cells that infiltrate the spleen, liver, and bone marrow. Most commonly develops in young and middle-aged men. Manifestations include B symptoms, hepatosplenomegaly, and thrombocytopenia.

RCcl7e0.title: ICS
RCcl7e0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Intercostal space
2. Internal carotid stenosis
3. Inhaled corticosteroid

iCcJ7e0.title: GRACE score
iCcJ7e0.description: A risk score that is used to estimate mortality in patients with ACS. Can help to guide management (e.g., timing of reperfusion therapy in NSTEMI). It is based on data from the large Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE).

QCcu7e0.title: HEART score
QCcu7e0.description: A tool to evaluate the risk of major adverse cardiac events in patients presenting at the emergency department with chest pain. The name is an acronym of the scores' components: history, ECG, age, risk factors, and troponin level.

PCcWHe0.title: Panlobular emphysema
PCcWHe0.description: A morphologic subtype of emphysema characterized by destruction of the entire acinus of the lung. Associated with alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency and frequently found in the lower lobes.

destinations.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease → Subtypes and variants

4Cc3He0.title: Centrilobular emphysema
4Cc3He0.description: A morphologic subtype of emphysema characterized by centrally located inflammation within the acini of the lung. Associated with smoking and frequently found in the upper lobes.

destinations.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease → Subtypes and variants

OCcIHe0.title: Neoangiogenesis
OCcIHe0.description: A formation of new blood vessels in neoplastic tissue. Increases the blood supply to the growing neoplasm.

lCcvHe0.title: Warburg effect
lCcvHe0.description: The mechanism by which malignant cells shift their cellular metabolism from glycolysis and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation under aerobic conditions to glycolysis and preferential lactate production, regardless of the oxygen supply. Even though lactate generation is less efficient in terms of ATP production, the mechanism is thought to promote growth, survival, and proliferation of cancer cells.

NCc-He0.title: Hypothalamospinal tract
NCc-He0.description: A tract that carries first order sympathetic neurons originating in the hypothalamus to the intermediolateral cell column of the spinal cord at the level of C8-T2 (cilospinal center of Budge). Damage to this tract results in ipsilateral Horner syndrome.

5Ccise0.title: Retinal hemorrhage
5Ccise0.description: A bleeding of the vessels in the retina. Can be seen on fundoscopy in the setting of several conditions, including head and neck trauma, sepsis, coagulopathy, hypertension, intoxication (e.g., CO poisoning), eye infections (e.g., CMV retinitis), and chronic disease (e.g., diabetes mellitus).

destinations.label: Diseases of the retina → Vascular diseases of the retina

media.title: Retinal findings in shaken baby syndrome

MCcMse0.title: Anti-PD-L1 antibody
MCcMse0.description: A group of monoclonal antibodies that serve as immune checkpoint inhibitors. They block the interaction of PD-L1/2 (on antigen-presenting, epithelial, immune, and tumor cells) with PD-1 (on T cells). Used as part of anticancer immunotherapy. Examples include atezolizumab, durvalumab, and avelumab.

nCc7se0.title: Uncomplicated pyelonephritis
nCc7se0.description: A type of pyelonephritis caused by a typical uropathogen, such as E. coli, in an immunocompetent patient with normal genitourinary anatomy and normal renal function.

LCcwse0.title: Complicated pyelonephritis
LCcwse0.description: A type of pyelonephritis that occurs in patients at high risk of developing complications such as sepsis or renal abscess. Risk factors include age > 60 years, a history of nephrolithiasis, immunodeficiency, sepsis, renal disease or history of renal surgery, and an inadequate response to oral empiric therapy.

oCc0Ge0.title: Open spina bifida
oCc0Ge0.description: A congenital defect of vertebral arch fusion in which the defect is not covered by skin. Typically caused by an underlying neural tube defect. Examples of conditions associated with open spina bifida are meningomyelocele and myeloschisis.

KCcUGe0.title: Conjunctival suffusion
KCcUGe0.description: An ophthalmologic finding characterized by bilateral diffuse reddening of the conjunctivae. In patients with suspected infectious illness, it is relatively specific for leptospirosis.

pCcLGe0.title: Chronic migraine
pCcLGe0.description: A migraine disorder characterized by a ≥ 3-month history of headaches ≥ 15 days/month, with ≥ 8 days/month in which the headache has migraine characteristics or is relieved by migraine-specific medication (e.g., triptans, ergotamine).

JCcsGe0.title: Tension pneumocephalus
JCcsGe0.description: A type of pneumocephalus in which intracranial air causes mass effect and increased intracranial pressure. Can cause deteriorating mental status and signs of brain herniation. Can be life-threatening if the air is not emergently evacuated.

qCcCGe0.title: Hypercontractile esophagus
qCcCGe0.description: An esophageal hypermobility disorder characterized by hypertensive propagative esophageal contractions in which at least 20% of swallows have a distal contractile integral > 8,000 mm Hg/sec/cm.

rCcfte0.title: Brainstem syndromes
rCcfte0.description: A group of neurologic syndromes caused by brainstem lesions (e.g., due to ischemia, neoplasms, demyelination, or infections). Manifestations include ipsilateral cranial nerve lesions (e.g., ipsilateral oculomotor nerve palsy) and contralateral long tract sign (e.g., contralateral hemiparesis).

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

HCcKte0.title: Fecal-oral transmission
HCcKte0.description: The spread of pathogens from the stool of an infection person to the mouth of another (e.g., via a contaminated food supply or inadequate handwashing prior to food preparation).

sCctte0.title: Pulmonary embolism rule-out criteria
sCctte0.description: A scoring system used to rule out pulmonary embolism in patients with a low pretest probability of PE based on Wells criteria or revised Geneva score.

destinations.label: Pulmonary embolism → Pretest probability of pulmonary embolism

ECc8Fe0.title: Sickle cell beta thalassemia
ECc8Fe0.description: A compound heterozygous hemoglobinopathy that occurs when an individual inherits one beta-thalassemia allele (β0 or β+) and one hemoglobin S allele (HbS), which both affect the beta-globin gene. HbSβ0 thalassemia causes severe sickle cell anemia, whereas HbSβ+ thalassemia causes mild-to-moderate sickle cell disease.

vCcAFe0.title: Anisopoikilocytosis
vCcAFe0.description: A histopathologic finding in which red blood cells appear of both varying size (anisocytosis) and varying shape (poikilocytosis).

wCch8e0.title: Biogenic amines
wCch8e0.description: A group of nitrogenous compounds that are synthesized by the decarboxylation of amino acids. Examples include neurotransmitters (e.g., dopamine, serotonin), histamine, and neuromodulators (e.g., phenethylamine, tyramine, tryptamine).

9CcN8e0.title: Phospholamban
9CcN8e0.description: A protein expressed in cardiomyocytes that decreases the affinity of sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium-ATPase for calcium. This inhibition leads to the decreased availability of calcium within cardiomyocytes and decreased cardiac contractility.

destinations.label: Cardiac physiology → Regulation of cardiac activity

CCcq8e0.title: Ewart sign
CCcq8e0.description: A clinical finding of dullness at the base of the left lung, with increased vocal fremitus and bronchial breathing. Secondary to compression of the lung parenchyma by a large pericardial effusion.

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Clinical features

xCcE8e0.title: Spinal trigeminal nucleus
xCcE8e0.description: A sensory nucleus of the trigeminal nerve that is located in the lateral pons and lateral medulla. Receives pain, temperature, and crude touch sensory impulses from the ipsilateral face and transmits impulses to the ventral posteromedial nucleus of the thalamus.

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Origin and pathways of the cranial nerves

BCcz8e0.title: Labial dysarthria
BCcz8e0.description: A type of dysarthria caused by weakness of the lips and perioral muscles, typically as a result of facial nerve palsy. Results in an inability to articulate labial phonemes such as "P" and "B".

yCcdue0.title: Chylopericardium
yCcdue0.description: A collection of chylous fluid within the pericardial space. Typically the result of injury to the thoracic duct from surgery or trauma. Can also be congenital.

ACcRue0.title: Optic radiation
ACcRue0.description: A collection of axons that course from the lateral geniculate body in the thalamus to the primary visual cortex in the occipital lobe. The inferior fascicle of the optic radiation (Meyer loop) is located in the temporal lobe and relays visual information from the lower part of the retina. The superior fascicle of the optic radiations is located in the parietal lobe and relays visual information from the upper part of the retina.

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Origin and pathways of the cranial nerves

_Cc5ue0.title: Stress echocardiography
_Cc5ue0.description: An ultrasound examination of the heart performed during or immediately after exercise or pharmacologically-induced stress. Most commonly used for the detection and monitoring of coronary artery disease. Typical findings of ischemia include regional wall motion abnormalities and changes in global left ventricular function.

zCcrue0.title: Abortifacient
zCcrue0.description: A substance or drug that is used to induce an abortion. Examples include mifepristone and methotrexate.

-CcDue0.title: Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome
-CcDue0.description: An umbrella term for the entities NSTEMI and unstable angina (UA).

0xceEe0.title: Endoleak
0xceEe0.description: A common complication of endovascular aneurysm repair. Blood continues to flow outside the new lumen and into the aneurysm sac despite the placement of an endoluminal graft. Some endoleaks resolve spontaneously; others require reintervention to avoid continued aneurysm expansion and the risk of rupture.

bxcHEe0.title: High-resolution esophageal manometry
bxcHEe0.description: A diagnostic tool that offers a detailed assessment of the amplitude, length, and duration of the esophageal peristaltic waves and is the gold standard for diagnosing esophageal motility disorders. An esophageal catheter with several pressure sensors (up to 36 in total) is placed and the patient is asked to swallow small volumes of water several times. The resulting data allows the distal contractile integral (product of the amplitude, duration, and length of the wave) and distal latency (the time between initiation and deceleration of peristalsis) to be calculated.

cxcave0.title: Muscles of facial expression
cxcave0.description: A group of muscles of the face that facilitate facial expression (e.g., creasing the forehead, raising the eyebrows, closing the eyelids, pursing the lips, puffing out the cheeks). Innervated by cranial nerve VII. The lower motor neuron supplying the superior muscles of facial expression receives bilateral upper motor neuron input; the lower motor neuron supplying the inferior muscles of facial expression is innervated by the contralateral upper motor neuron.

1xc2ve0.title: Three prime untranslated region
1xc2ve0.description: A section of messenger RNA following the stop codon that contains elements that regulate gene expression. Contains bindings sites for regulatory proteins and microRNAs.

WxcPve0.title: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma
WxcPve0.description: A carcinoma of the salivary gland that arises from malignant transformation or a primary or recurrent benign pleomorphic adenoma.

dxcove0.title: Pulse glucocorticoid therapy
dxcove0.description: The administration of high doses of intravenous glucocorticoids (e.g., 500 to 1,000 mg/day) over a short duration (e.g., 3 days). Can be used to treat several inflammatory conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis, interstitial pneumonia, DRESS syndrome, and acute allograft rejection. Associated with a greater risk of adverse effects (e.g., immunosuppression).

VxcGve0.title: Sialadenitis
VxcGve0.description: An acute inflammation of the salivary glands. Subtypes are acute suppurative sialadenitis, caused by bacterial infection (e.g., Staphylococcus aureus), and nonsuppurative sialadenitis, caused by viral infection (e.g., mumps) and/or chronic conditions.

destinations.label: Diseases of the salivary glands → Sialadenitis

excxve0.title: Granulomatous sialadenitis
excxve0.description: A type of chronic sialadenitis characterized by granulomatous inflammation. Etiologies include autoimmune disease (e.g., sarcoidosis), vasculitis (e.g., ANCA-associated vasculitides), a response to foreign bodies (including tumors), and xanthogranulomatous sialadenitis.

2xcTDe0.title: Covered entity
2xcTDe0.description: According to 45 CFR 164.103, a covered entity is a health plan, a health care clearinghouse, or a health care provider who transmits any health information in electronic form in connection with a transaction covered by this subchapter. Covered entities have a responsibility to protect the privacy of health information in accordance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

fxckDe0.title: Tier 1 select agent
fxckDe0.description: A group of biological agents that are potential threats for misuse as biological weapons. Examples include Ebola virus, Bacillus anthracis, and Yersinia pestis.

Txc6De0.title: Dihydrofolate acid
Txc6De0.description: A folic acid derivative that is reduced by dihydrofolic acid reductase to form tetrahydrofolic acid, which can be used for nucleotide synthesis.

gxcFDe0.title: D-Ala-D-Ala
gxcFDe0.description: A dipeptide component of bacterial peptidoglycan, a cell wall component. It is the target of various antibiotics (e.g.,  penicillins, cephalosporins).

3xcSwe0.title: Anorexia
3xcSwe0.description: A loss of appetite. Etiologies include psychiatric disorders (e.g., anorexia nervosa), chronic disease (e.g., chronic kidney disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), and chronic infections (e.g., tuberculosis).

ixcJwe0.title: Sacubitril
ixcJwe0.description: A prodrug whose active metabolite inhibits neprilysin, an enzyme that normally breaks down peptides. As a result, the concentration of natriuretic peptides (e.g., atrial natriuretic peptide, brain natriuretic peptide) increases. Used in combination with valsartan to treat chronic heart failure.

Qxcuwe0.title: Medial tibial stress syndrome
Qxcuwe0.description: An overuse injury of the lower leg that is common in runners and military recruits. Clinical features include diffuse pain over the posteromedial aspect of the middle and distal tibia that is often accompanied by tenderness of the surrounding muscles. In the early stages of the syndrome, pain begins with the onset of activity and slowly resolves during the course of exercise. In later stages, pain persists even after the activity has ended.

destinations.label: Sports injuries → Medial tibial stress syndrome

jxc_we0.title: Nucleotidase
jxc_we0.description: An enzyme that hydrolyzes a nucleotide into a nucleoside and phosphate.

PxcW9e0.title: Adenosine A1 receptor
PxcW9e0.description: A Gi-coupled adenosine receptor that is found in the brain, spinal cord, testes, heart, bronchi, and autonomic nerve terminals.

4xc39e0.title: Adenosine A2A receptor
4xc39e0.description: A Gs-coupled adenosine receptor that is found in the heart, blood vessels, lungs, spleen, platelets and certain areas of the central nervous system (e.g., striatum, nucleus accumbens, olfactory tubercle).

kxcm9e0.title: American Medical Association
kxcm9e0.description: An association of physicians and medical students in the United States that provides several guidelines, including the Physician Specialty Codes, the Code of Medical Ethics, and the Current Procedural Terminology coding system.

OxcI9e0.title: Nizatidine
OxcI9e0.description: A drug that competes with histamine for H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells, which results in decreased gastric acid secretion and gastric volume. Used to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease.

lxcv9e0.title: Remdesivir
lxcv9e0.description: A nucleotide analog that inhibits RNA synthesis. Has been shown to have in vitro activity against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Its clinical efficacy is not well understood.

destinations.label: COVID-19 (coronavirus disease 2019) → Management of hospitalized patients

Nxc-9e0.title: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
Nxc-9e0.description: An aggressive type of T-cell lymphoma that most commonly manifests with painless adenopathy and B symptoms. Further subvided into ALK-positive and ALK-negative subtypes.

5xciCe0.title: Dravet syndrome
5xciCe0.description: A rare epilepsy syndrome characterized by recurrent seizures that typically develop before 1 year of age, resulting in poor neurodevelopment. Seizures can be prolonged and cause status epilepticus. Most commonly caused by mutations in the voltage-gated sodium channel alpha-1 gene.

MxcMCe0.title: AMA
MxcMCe0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Antimitochondrial antibodies
2. Antimicrosomal antibody
3. American Medical Association
4. Against medical advice

nxc7Ce0.title: Air-bone gap
nxc7Ce0.description: A finding on pure tone audiometry in which the auditory threshold for air conduction is greater than the auditory threshold for bone conduction. Indicates that there is a conductive element contributing to a patient's hearing loss.

LxcwCe0.title: Die-punch fracture
LxcwCe0.description: An impacted, intra-articular fracture of the lunate fossa of the distal radius. Most commonly caused by an axial loading force applied against the distal radius.

oxc0xe0.title: Conscientious objection
oxc0xe0.description: The refusal to perform a certain elective treatment or procedure out of moral and/or religious personal conflict.

destinations.label: Medical professionalism and codes of conduct → Conflicts of interest

KxcUxe0.title: Unemancipated minor
KxcUxe0.description: An underaged person (i.e., < 18 years) who is legally subject to the authority, supervision, and decision of a parent or guardian.

pxcLxe0.title: Emphysematous pyelonephritis
pxcLxe0.description: A rare, life-threatening form of pyelonephritis characterized by gas formation within or around the kidney. Most commonly seen in patients with poorly controlled diabetes (90%) or immunodeficiency. Typically caused by E.coli. Treatment includes IV antibiotics, percutaneous drainage, and, in some cases, nephrectomy.

Jxcsxe0.title: Hereditary progressive arthro-ophthalmodystrophy
Jxcsxe0.description: A group of inherited connective tissue disorders whose manifestations include a distinctive facial appearance (flattened face due to underdeveloped cheekbones and nasal bridge), severe myopia, hearing loss, and joint abnormalities (hypermobility that progresses to joint pain and stiffness).

IxcYBe0.title: Stanford type A aortic dissection
IxcYBe0.description: An aortic dissection that involves the ascending aorta, regardless of the site of the original intimal tear.

rxcfBe0.title: Stanford type B aortic dissection
rxcfBe0.description: An aortic dissection that originates distal to the left subclavian artery and does not involve the ascending aorta.

sxctBe0.title: Cyclobenzaprine
sxctBe0.description: A centrally-acting drug that relaxes skeletal muscle. Used to treat muscle spasms.

GxcBBe0.title: Muscarine
GxcBBe0.description: A toxin found in many mushrooms. It is structurally similar to acetylcholine. Manifestations of toxicity include bradycardia, sweating, salivation, tearing, bronchospasm, and incontinence. Does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier.

Fxcgye0.title: Frontal gait disorder
Fxcgye0.description: A gait disorder seen in patients with bilateral frontal lobe lesions. Characterized by poor balance (frontal disequilibrium), an inability to initiate the process of walking and hesitations on turns (ignition apraxia), and shuffling as if the feet are glued to the ground (magnetic gait).

8xcOye0.title: Fidelity (ethical principle)
8xcOye0.description: A medical principle defined as the obligation to faithfully perform health care services (e.g., to provide care in a manner that avoids impairment due to personal or financial interests).

uxcpye0.title: Psychomotor agitation
uxcpye0.description: A state of restlessness accompanied by purposeless movements (e.g. tapping fingers, pacing). Etiologies include alcohol withdrawal, bipolar disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, major depressive disorder, and post-traumatic stress disorder.

Exc8ye0.title: Cardinal symptoms of acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Exc8ye0.description: Worsening of dyspnea, increased frequency and severity of cough, and increased volume and/or purulence of sputum.

destinations.label: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease → Clinical features

vxcAye0.title: Disorientation
vxcAye0.description: A mental state characterized by an altered awareness of time, place, and/or person.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

Dxc1Ae0.title: High-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy
Dxc1Ae0.description: A type of oxygen delivery system that provides heated and humidified oxygen through a specialized nasal cannula at rates of up to 60 L/min. Used in the treatment of acute respiratory failure. Advantages include delivery of 100% FiO₂ with variable PEEP, reductions in respiratory effort, and improved gas exchange.

destinations.label: Oxygen therapy → Advanced oxygen delivery systems

9xcNAe0.title: In-frame mutation
9xcNAe0.description: A mutation of a gene with the insertion or deletion of a number of nucleotides that is divisible by three. These types of mutations tend to be less severe than frameshift mutations, as the missing (or added) codons often lead to partially functional peptides.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

CxcqAe0.title: ACS
CxcqAe0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Acute coronary syndrome
2. Acute compartment syndrome
3. Acute chest syndrome
4. Anterior cord syndrome
5. Abdominal compartment syndrome
6. American Cancer Society

xxcEAe0.title: Polypharmacy
xxcEAe0.description: The regular and concurrent use of multiple medications (usually defined as ≥ 5 medications).

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Management of existing medications

BxczAe0.title: Prescribing cascade
BxczAe0.description: A cycle that arises when symptoms resulting from an adverse reaction to a medication are treated with a new medication. An example is the prescription of a proton pump inhibitor to reduce gastrointestinal adverse effects caused by NSAID use.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medication errors

yxcd_e0.title: Perforant pathway
yxcd_e0.description: A primarily glutamatergic pathway that connects the dentate gyrus, the CA3 and CA1 regions, and the subiculum of the hippocampus with the entorhinal cortex. It is a pathway for long-term potentiation.

AxcR_e0.title: Glutamate-gated ion-channel
AxcR_e0.description: An ion channel that is activated by the binding of glutamate. Examples include NMDA, AMPA, and kainate receptors.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

_xc5_e0.title: Fragility fracture
_xc5_e0.description: A type of pathological fracture in which disorders of bone metabolism lead to an increased vulnerability to fractures. Typically affects the vertebrae, hip, or wrist. Common causes include osteoporosis, Paget disease of bone, osteomalacia, and osteopetrosis.

zxcr_e0.title: Vertebral compression fracture
zxcr_e0.description: The most common type of vertebral fracture. Etiologies include trauma and pathological fracture in the setting of underlying conditions (e.g., osteoporosis, malignancy). Often asymptomatic but can cause acute back pain and point tenderness.

ZBcZze0.title: Personal protective equipment
ZBcZze0.description: The equipment worn for protection against and prevention of the further transmission of microbiological, chemical, and/or radiological hazards. Examples include gloves, gowns, masks, face shields, and respirators (e.g., N95 respirators and portable air-purifying respirators).

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Personal protective equipment (PPE)

0Bceze0.title: Intellectual disability
0Bceze0.description: A condition characterized by impaired intellectual functioning (e.g., learning, problem-solving, abstract thinking) and adaptive functioning (e.g., at school or work, in social situations) with onset during the developmental period.

aBcQze0.title: Intelligence quotient
aBcQze0.description: A score derived from a set of tests that assess the performance of an individual in different cognitive domains, such as abstract reasoning, arithmetic, and language comprehension. The tests are standardized and reflect the performance of an individual compared to the general population level.

bBcHze0.title: Chordee
bBcHze0.description: A congenital abnormality characterized by an abnormal ventral curvature of the penis. Usually associated with a ventral urethral meatus (hypospadias).

destinations.label: Abnormalities of the male urethra and webbed penis → Hypospadias

XBc9ze0.title: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome
XBc9ze0.description: A variant of irritable bowel syndrome characterized by recurrent abdominal pain or discomfort that is associated with diarrhea rather than constipation.

cBca-e0.title: Hemozoin
cBca-e0.description: A waste product formed by blood-feeding parasites (e.g., Plasmodium, Schistosoma) during the digestion of hemoglobin into free heme. Formed by the polymerization of heme.

media.title: Macrogametocytes of different types of Plasmodium

1Bc2-e0.title: Chemotherapy-induced diarrhea
1Bc2-e0.description: A type of diarrhea that occurs following the administration of antineoplastic drugs. Typically caused by damage to the intestinal mucosa. Common agents that cause this condition include irinotecan, 5-fluorouracil, and cetuximab.

destinations.label: Complications of cancer therapy → Gastrointestinal complications

WBcP-e0.title: Salpingo-oophorectomy
WBcP-e0.description: A surgical procedure to remove the ovary and fallopian tube on one or both sides.

dBco-e0.title: Grossly disorganized behavior
dBco-e0.description: A range of behaviors during goal-directed activities that lead to difficulty with performing activities of daily living. Manifestations may include catatonia and/or socially inappropriate emotional responses (e.g., inappropriate smiling or laughing, infantile behavior).

VBcG-e0.title: Deidentified health information
VBcG-e0.description: An edited medical record in which any details that could allow the patient to be identified have been removed. The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) restricts the use of protected health information but not the use of deidentified health information.

eBcx-e0.title: Oxygen-induced hypercapnia
eBcx-e0.description: A state of hypercapnic respiratory failure (PaCO₂ > 45 mm Hg or a rise > 5 mm Hg in patients with chronically elevated PaCO₂) precipitated by the use of supplemental oxygen in at-risk patients, e.g., patients with COPD.

fBckZU0.title: Ventricular assist device
fBckZU0.description: A mechanical device implanted into the heart to support or replace the function of one or both of the ventricles in patients with end-stage heart failure. Used for the left ventricle (LVAD), right ventricle (RVAD), or both (BiVAD), and implanted via open surgery or percutaneously (e.g., impella). May be placed temporarily (to aid myocardial recovery or in patients awaiting heart transplants) or permanently (in patients not eligible for a transplant).

TBc6ZU0.title: Type I high affinity IgE receptor
TBc6ZU0.description: A receptor that is expressed in tetrameric form on mast cells and basophils and in trimeric form on Langerhans cells, dendritic cells, and monocytes. Antigen binding results in receptor cross-linking and cell activation (e.g., release of histamine and cytokines).

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

gBcFZU0.title: Lymphangiography
gBcFZU0.description: A diagnostic procedure used to detect lymphatic leakage. Involves the injection of contrast medium into the lymphatic channels followed by imaging. Can also be therapeutic if a sclerosing contrast agent is used.

SBcyZU0.title: Delusional parasitosis
SBcyZU0.description: A delusional disorder in which a patient develops a false belief that he or she is infested with parasites (e.g., helminths, worms, mites). Often includes the tactile hallucination of formication.

hBcc0U0.title: EGFR
hBcc0U0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Estimated glomerular filtration rate
2. Epidermal growth factor receptor

3BcS0U0.title: Liothyronine
3BcS0U0.description: A synthetic form of the thyroid hormone triiodothyronine (T₃). Used mostly in the treatment of myxedema coma.

RBcl0U0.title: Medication review
RBcl0U0.description: A structured examination of a patient's medications. Performed as part of comprehensive medical history and reviewed periodically (e.g., during transition of care such as, admission, transfer, discharge; to compare new medication orders with past medication orders). Performed to identify medications as causative agents for certain conditions and to avoid medication errors such as duplication, omission, dosing errors, and drug interactions.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medication errors

iBcJ0U0.title: Drug interaction checker
iBcJ0U0.description: A software used to identify pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic drug interactions to minimize the risk of adverse drug events (e.g., adverse effects, therapeutic failure).

QBcu0U0.title: Pyruvate decarboxylation
QBcu0U0.description: The conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA by the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. This reaction links glycolysis to the citric acid cycle.

jBc_0U0.title: Fluctuance
jBc_0U0.description: A physical examination finding in which the application of pressure to one pole of a lesion transmits the pressure to every other point on the surface of the swelling. Can be seen in abscesses due to the accumulation of pus.

PBcWaU0.title: Nonbinary
PBcWaU0.description: A descriptor for individuals who do not identify with either of the binary gender categories (i.e., women or men).

4Bc3aU0.title: Gender-neutral language
4Bc3aU0.description: A style of language that avoids attribution of individuals to binary gender categories (i.e., women and men). Includes using gender-neutral pronouns and terms that do not identify gender (e.g., chairperson instead of chairwoman).

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Affirmative care

kBcmaU0.title: Person under investigation
kBcmaU0.description: An individual with clinical features of and/or risk factors for a disease that merit diagnostic testing for it.

OBcIaU0.title: Personal protective equipment for COVID-19
OBcIaU0.description: The equipment recommended for health care personnel working with COVID-19 cases and PUIs. Includes an isolation gown, gloves, eye protection (e.g., goggles, disposable full-face shield), and N95 respirator or face mask.

media.title: Putting on SARS-CoV-2 personal protective equipment (PPE)

NBc-aU0.title: Appreciation in medical decision-making
NBc-aU0.description: The ability of a patient to determine how facts are relevant to their personal situation.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

mBcVYU0.title: Reasoning in medical decision-making
mBcVYU0.description: The ability of a patient to use information provided by a physician to make decisions regarding their care.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

MBcMYU0.title: Reflecting (communication skill)
MBcMYU0.description: A communication skill characterized by paraphrasing a patient's thoughts and feelings to demonstrate listening and check for understanding.

LBcwYU0.title: Iodoquinol
LBcwYU0.description: An antiprotozoal drug that is used to eradicate intestinal cysts of Entamoeba histolytica. As a luminal agent, it is not absorbed and, therefore, does not have a systemic effect. Not currently approved for use in the United States.

6BcjbU0.title: Paucicellular
6BcjbU0.description: A descriptor for a sparse number and/or distribution of cells.

pBcLbU0.title: Minor disorders of esophageal peristalsis
pBcLbU0.description: A group of esophageal disorders that, in contrast to the major motility disorders, typically remain asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic and usually resolve spontaneously. Includes ineffective esophageal motility and fragmented peristalsis.

qBcCbU0.title: Mood disorders
qBcCbU0.description: A group of psychiatric disorders characterized by emotional disturbances and the inability to control them. Associated with impaired social and occupational functioning. Includes depressive disorders (e.g., major depressive, cyclothymic disorder, dysthymic disorder) and bipolar disorders.

IBcYXU0.title: Ottawa COPD risk scale
IBcYXU0.description: A validated clinical score used to risk-stratify patients with acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and predict short-term outcomes (e.g., mortality, critical care unit admission, intubation and mechanical ventilation). Parameters include examination findings (e.g., heart rate, O2 saturation), history (e.g., history of intubation), and diagnostic test results (e.g., ECG findings, serum CO2 concentration).

destinations.label: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease → Disposition

rBcfXU0.title: Gonadal artery
rBcfXU0.description: A paired artery that arises from the aorta inferior to the renal arteries (near L2). In male individuals, the gonadal artery is the testicular artery, which supplies the testes. In female individuals, the gonadal artery is the ovarian artery, which supplies the ovaries.

media.title: Abdominal aorta and inferior vena cava
Parts of the aorta and its branches

7Bc4XU0.title: Trauma center
7Bc4XU0.description: A health facility that provides specialized care to patients with serious traumatic injuries. Different levels (I–V) designated by the American College of Surgeons classify centers according to the breadth and level of advanced care they provide, the availability of specialists, and the degree of their community and academic involvement.

HBcKXU0.title: AMPLE history
HBcKXU0.description: A mnemonic used primarily in trauma, emergency, and first-responder settings to recall the following essential elements of rapid focused history taking: Allergies, Medications, Past medical history and pregnancy status, Last meal, and Events leading up to the current illness/injury. A variant mnemonic SAMPLE includes Signs/Symptoms as the first component.

destinations.label: Management of trauma patients → Secondary survey

FBcgcU0.title: Batson venous plexus
FBcgcU0.description: A network of valveless veins connecting the deep pelvic veins and thoracic veins to the internal vertebral venous plexus. Thought to facilitate the hematogenous spread of malignancy cancer and infections to the spine.

8BcOcU0.title: Accessory pathway
8BcOcU0.description: An abnormal electrical connection between the atrium and ventricle that is usually congenital. The direction of electrical impulse conduction may be anterograde (toward the ventricles), retrograde (toward the atria), or both.
