May lead to AVRT as a result of a reentry circuit with the AV node or other preexcited tachyarrhythmias where abnormal atrial impulses are conducted through the pathway (e.g., preexcited atrial fibrillation).

uBcpcU0.title: Testicular artery
uBcpcU0.description: A paired artery that supplies the testes. Arises from the aorta inferior to the renal arteries (near L2). Enters the scrotum via the deep inguinal ring of the inguinal canal.

vBcAcU0.title: Testicular vein
vBcAcU0.description: A paired vein that drains the testes in male individuals. Receives blood from the pampiniform plexus on both sides of the body. On the right, the testicular vein drains into the inferior vena cava. On the left, it drains into the left renal vein.

media.title: Abdominal aorta and inferior vena cava

wBch1U0.title: Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score
wBch1U0.description: A score used in the early phase of an ischemic stroke to evaluate the extent of the infarction in the MCA territory on noncontrast head CT. A normal head CT has a baseline score of 10, and points are subtracted for ischemic changes, with the lowest possible score being 0. Can be used to inform some treatment decisions and assess prognosis.

9BcN1U0.title: Modified Rankin scale
9BcN1U0.description: A scale used to quantify the degree of disability and dependence in daily activities before and after cerebral stroke. The scale ranges from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (death).

CBcq1U0.title: Ragged-red fiber appearance
CBcq1U0.description: A muscle biopsy finding in patients with mitochondrial myopathies (e.g., MELAS syndrome, MERRF syndrome). Caused by the proliferation of nonfunctional mitochondria, which appear as subsarcolemmal red deposits when stained with modified Gomori trichrome.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Mitochondrial myopathies

ABcRWU0.title: Peroral endoscopic myotomy
ABcRWU0.description: An endoscopy-guided myotomy of the inner circular muscle layer of the lower esophageal sphincter. Used to treat achalasia. May be considered in other esophageal motility disorders (e.g., diffuse esophageal spasm), which may require extending the myotomy incision into the esophageal body.

_Bc5WU0.title: Pneumatic dilation
_Bc5WU0.description: An endoscopic procedure in which a low-compliance balloon is used to dilate narrowed segments of the esophagus. Can be used to treat achalasia, esophageal strictures, and motility disorders with esophagogastric junction obstruction.

-BcDWU0.title: Signs of unstable tachycardia
-BcDWU0.description: Features of unstable tachycardia that warrant immediate management (e.g., cardioversion, defibrillation, CPR). These include an acutely altered mental state or loss of consciousness, ischemic chest pain, hypotension, shock or signs of hypoperfusion, and signs of acute heart failure (pulmonary edema, respiratory distress).

destinations.label: Management of tachycardia → Unstable tachycardia with pulse

dycoVU0.title: Primary amebic meningoencephalitis
dycoVU0.description: A fulminant and usually fatal form of meningoencephalitis caused by infection with Naegleria fowleri, an ameba found in warm freshwater that can enter the central nervous system via the cribriform plate. Manifestations include fever, headache, photophobia, nausea, seizures, and altered mental status.

VycGVU0.title: CT pulmonary angiography
VycGVU0.description: An IV contrast-enhanced CT scan used to visualize the pulmonary arterial tree in order to identify or rule out pulmonary embolism.

UycbeU0.title: Resuscitative thoracotomy
UycbeU0.description: A procedure performed to obtain urgent and/or emergent access to the thoracic cavity to perform temporizing lifesaving measures (e.g., relieving cardiac tamponade, achieving hemostasis of cardiac or vascular injuries, performing open cardiac massage and/or aortic cross-clamping, controlling air embolism). Typically immediately followed by definitive surgical management.

destinations.label: Management of trauma patients → Primary survey

2ycTeU0.title: Expectant management
2ycTeU0.description: A management strategy that involves serial clinical monitoring (i.e., intermittent screening for symptoms of disease).

fyckeU0.title: Informed refusal
fyckeU0.description: A refusal by a patient to receive recommended medical management after adequate discussion of the risks, benefits, and alternatives.

Tyc6eU0.title: Civil commitment
Tyc6eU0.description: An intervention that restricts the autonomy of an individual with a mental health disorder and compels the individual to receive treatment in an inpatient setting (involuntary admission) or an outpatient one (community treatment orders).

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Involuntary commitment

gycFeU0.title: Health literacy
gycFeU0.description: The ability to independently acquire, process, comprehend, and use health information to make informed health care decisions.

destinations.label: Health care system → Social aspects of health care

SycyeU0.title: Basic reproduction number
SycyeU0.description: An epidemiological value that evaluates the ability of a virus to be transmitted. A base value, R0=0, indicates that there is no transmission. A value of 1 indicates that, on average, an infected individual passes the virus on to one other individual. A value of 2 indicates that, on average, each infected person passes the virus on to two others. Efforts to prevent the spread of infection (e.g., social distancing, quarantine) aim to decrease the value.

media.title: Modeling the spread of COVID-19 based on R0

hyccUU0.title: Secondary sclerosing cholangitis
hyccUU0.description: A chronic cholestatic biliary disease characterized by biliary strictures resulting from an identifiable cause (e.g., malignancy, surgery, chronic pancreatitis). Can lead to secondary biliary cirrhosis.

3ycSUU0.title: Intracerebral steal phenomenon
3ycSUU0.description: A paradoxical decrease in blood flow to the injured parts of the brain secondary to hypercapnia-induced cerebral vasodilation. Blood vessels in the injured parts of the brain are maximally dilated, while vasodilation in the unaffected brain tissue redistributes blood and worsens the ischemia in the affected area.

RyclUU0.title: Narrow-complex tachycardia
RyclUU0.description: A category of tachyarrhythmias (i.e., pulse > 100 bpm) with a normal, narrow QRS complex (< 120ms). Includes tachycardias with regular patterns (e.g. sinus tachycardia, AVRT, AVNRT, focal atrial tachycardia, atrial flutter with fixed conduction) and irregular patterns (e.g. atrial fibrillation with rapid response, atrial flutter with variable conduction and multifocal atrial tachycardia). The origin is usually supraventricular.

iycJUU0.title: Sinus tachycardia
iycJUU0.description: A heart rate ≥ 100 beats per minute that originates from the sinus node.

destinations.label: Management of tachycardia → Stable, regular narrow-complex tachycardia

media.title: Sinus tachycardia with a left bundle-branch block

QycuUU0.title: Red blood cell indices
QycuUU0.description: A set of calculated red blood cell (RBC) parameters used to determine the cause of anemia. Includes average RBC size (mean corpuscular volume), average amount of hemoglobin per RBC (mean corpuscular hemoglobin), average concentration of hemoglobin per RBC (mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration), and average variation in the size of RBCs (RBC distribution width). Reported as part of the complete blood count.

jyc_UU0.title: Kubler-Ross model
jyc_UU0.description: A model that details five stages that an individual experiences in grief: denial, anger, bargaining, depression, and acceptance. Individuals may experience some or all of these stages and not always in the order presented above.

destinations.label: Grief and end-of-life counseling → Bereavement and grief

PycW2U0.title: Institutional review board
PycW2U0.description: A group of people at a research institution who are responsible for safeguarding the rights and welfare of people who participate as subjects in research. They can approve, deny, and request changes in the study design of research investigations.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Research ethics

mycVfU0.title: Waardenburg syndrome
mycVfU0.description: An autosomal dominant pigmentation disorder characterized by patchy depigmentation of the skin and hair, heterochromia iridum, a broad nasal root, and in some cases, congenital deafness, cleft lip and palate, and neural tube defects.

destinations.label: Collection of dermatological disorders → Waardenburg syndrome

5ycifU0.title: Normothermia
5ycifU0.description: A state in which the body is at normal temperature, generally considered to be 36-37.9°C.

MycMfU0.title: SVT with aberrancy
MycMfU0.description: A group of tachyarrhythmias (i.e., heart rate > 100/min) that originate in the atria or AV node and are characterized by a wide QRS complex (> 120 ms) due to conduction abnormalities (e.g., bundle branch blocks, accessory pathways). Depending on the origin, the rhythm is regular or irregular.

nyc7fU0.title: Ancillary brain death tests
nyc7fU0.description: A series of tests that are used to confirm brain death when examination of brain stem reflexes and/or the apnea test cannot be performed. Includes tests for blood flow (e.g., CT or MR brain angiography, transcranial doppler, radionuclide brain scan) and tests for electrical activity (e.g., electroencephalography).

LycwfU0.title: Hypermetabolism
LycwfU0.description: A state of increased energy expenditure at rest. Can develop in the setting of severe illness and/or injury.

oyc0TU0.title: Ganglionic blocker
oyc0TU0.description: A drug that decreases autonomic activity by inhibiting neurotransmission (nicotinic receptor activation) within autonomic ganglia. Examples include trimethaphan and hexamethonium.

KycUTU0.title: Trimetaphan camsilate
KycUTU0.description: A nicotinic antagonist and ganglionic blocker that can be used to induce hypotension during surgery (e.g., to reduce bleeding).

6ycjTU0.title: Mecamylamine
6ycjTU0.description: A nicotinic antagonist and ganglionic blocker that can be used to treat hypertension. It has largely been replaced by other therapeutic agents.

pycLTU0.title: Hexamethonium
pycLTU0.description: A nicotinic antagonist and ganglionic blocker that can be used to treat hypertension. It has largely been replaced by other therapeutic agents.

JycsTU0.title: Fasciola hepatica
JycsTU0.description: A trematode parasite primarily found in ruminant mammals (the definitive hosts). Snails serve as the intermediate hosts. Ingestion results in migration of the organism through the intestinal wall into the biliary ducts, which causes fascioliasis.

qycCTU0.title: Reticulocytosis
qycCTU0.description: The presence of a significant number of reticulocytes (a type of immature red blood cell) in the peripheral blood. Several criteria for reticulocytosis exist, including a fraction >2% and an absolute reticulocyte count >75,000/mcL. Formulas also exist to account for the degree of anemia (e.g., corrected absolute reticulocyte count).

IycYgU0.title: Fascioliasis
IycYgU0.description: A parasitic infection caused by Fasciola hepatica or Fasciola gigantica (liver flukes). Early manifestations include fever, right upper quadrant pain, hepatomegaly, and eosinophilia. Can progress to a chronic biliary phase, with manifestations that include abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and common bile duct obstruction.

rycfgU0.title: Lacosamide
rycfgU0.description: An antiepileptic medication that stabilizes hyperexcitable neuronal membranes and inhibits neuronal activity by enhancing slow inactivation of sodium channels.

7yc4gU0.title: Emancipated minor
7yc4gU0.description: An underaged person who is not legally subject to the authority, supervision, and decisions of a parent or guardian. Depending on the state, this may apply to minors >13 years of age who live independently or are self-sufficient, are married or parents, serve in the military, or have been declared by a court as emancipated.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

HycKgU0.title: Complementary and alternative medicine
HycKgU0.description: A term for products and practices that are not a part of standard medical care. Examples include dietary and herbal supplements, chiropractic medicine, homeopathy, and traditional medicine practices (e.g., acupuncture).

tycXSU0.title: Typhoid fever
tycXSU0.description: A systemic illness caused by Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi. Manifestations include fever, chills, abdominal pain, rose spots on the trunk and abdomen, and hepatosplenomegaly.

FycgSU0.title: Paratyphoid fever
FycgSU0.description: A systemic illness caused by Salmonella enterica serotypes Paratyphi A, B, and C. Manifestations include fever, chills, abdominal pain, rose spots on the trunk and abdomen, and hepatosplenomegaly.

8ycOSU0.title: Enteric fever
8ycOSU0.description: A term that refers to both typhoid and paratyphoid fever (although it is sometimes used synonymously with typhoid fever only). Caused by Salmonella enterica serotypes Typhi and Paratyphi. Manifestations include fever, abdominal pain, and rose spots on the trunk and abdomen.

uycpSU0.title: Ineffective esophageal motility
uycpSU0.description: A minor esophageal motility disorder characterized by acontractile breaks > 5 cm within normally occurring peristalsis in > 50% of swallows on high-resolution manometry.

Eyc8SU0.title: Fragmented peristalsis
Eyc8SU0.description: A minor esophageal motility disorder characterized by failed/weak peristalsis in > 50% of swallows on high-resolution esophageal manometry.

vycASU0.title: Oncologic emergencies
vycASU0.description: A group of complications of malignancy and/or the treatment of malignancy. Can be further classified based on whether the complication is metabolic (e.g., tumor lysis syndrome, hypercalcemia of malignancy), hematologic (e.g., hyperviscosity syndrome), structural (e.g., superior vena cava syndrome), or treatment-related (e.g., febrile neutropenia) in etiology.

Dyc1hU0.title: Perimetrium
Dyc1hU0.description: The peritoneal serosa that forms the outer layer of the uterus and covers the uterine body. The anterior cervix and lateral uterine body are covered by adventitia (not by peritoneum).

destinations.label: Female reproductive organs → Uterus and cervix

9ycNhU0.title: Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor
9ycNhU0.description: A class of drug that inhibits Bruton tyrosine kinase, blocking the B-cell receptor signaling cascade. This inhibits the survival and proliferation of both malignant and normal B cells. These drugs are used in the treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia, lymphoma, Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, and graft-versus-host disease. Example agents include ibrutinib and acalabrutinib.

CycqhU0.title: Buccopharyngeal fascia
CycqhU0.description: A layer of fascia that spans between the carotid sheaths, posterior to the esophagus and the lateral lobes of the thyroid gland.

xycEhU0.title: Cricotracheal ligament
xycEhU0.description: A ligament that connects the cricoid ligament with the first tracheal ring.

yycd3U0.title: Foreskin
yycd3U0.description: The retractable skin that covers the glans penis.

_yc53U0.title: Thyrohyoid membrane
_yc53U0.description: A fibroelastic membrane that connects the hyoid bone to the thyroid cartilage. Has thickenings medially and laterally (the median and lateral thyrohyoid ligaments). Penetrated by the internal laryngeal nerve and superior laryngeal artery.

-ycD3U0.title: Ibrutinib
-ycD3U0.description: An irreversible inhibitor of Bruton tyrosine kinase that causes decreased proliferation of malignant B cells. Used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma, mantle cell lymphoma, marginal zone lymphoma, Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, and chronic graft-versus-host disease.

ZAcZRU0.title: Acalabrutinib
ZAcZRU0.description: An irreversible inhibitor of Bruton tyrosine kinase that causes decreased proliferation of malignant B cells. Used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia, small lymphocytic lymphoma, and mantle cell lymphoma.

0AceRU0.title: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus
0AceRU0.description: A coronavirus that causes MERS, a respiratory illness that leads to severe pneumonia with high mortality rates ~10%). Transmitted person-to-person via respiratory droplets or through contaminated surfaces. First identified in China in 2002 with rapid spread to other countries resulting in a pandemic. Brought under control in 2003 by implementing intensified screening measures and isolating patients with suspected SARS-CoV infection.

aAcQRU0.title: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus
aAcQRU0.description: A coronavirus that causes MERS, a respiratory illness that leads to severe pneumonia with high mortality rates ~34%). Transmitted mainly animal-to-person (especially from infected camels). Person-to-person transmission is less common with the exception of close contacts (e.g., family members, health care workers). First identified in the Arabian Peninsula in 2012; all cases outside the Middle East can be related to travelers from that region.

YAcnRU0.title: Temporary cardiac pacing
YAcnRU0.description: The use of extrinsic electrical stimulation to restore a normal heart rate in hemodynamic compromise due to bradyarrhythmia or tachyarrhythmia. Temporary cardiac pacing may be transcutaneous (via pads on the chest wall) or transvenous (via an electrode threaded into the right atrium/ventricle).

destinations.label: Management of bradycardia → Temporary cardiac pacing

bAcHRU0.title: Catheter-directed thrombolysis
bAcHRU0.description: The infusion of fibrinolytic agents directly into the thrombus through a fluoroscopically positioned catheter. Uses lower doses of fibrinolytic drugs than systemic thrombolysis.

XAc9RU0.title: Eunatremia
XAc9RU0.description: A normal concentration of sodium in the blood (i.e., 136–145 mEq/L).

cAcaiU0.title: Fastidious microorganism
cAcaiU0.description: A group of organisms with complex or stringent nutritional requirements. They are difficult to culture and only grow with specific nutritional supplementation and precise environmental control.

1Ac2iU0.title: High-risk sexual behavior
1Ac2iU0.description: A sexual behavior that is associated with an increased risk of acquiring sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and/or resulting in unplanned pregnancies. Examples include unprotected sexual activity, early sexual activity (< 18 years of age), anal sex, mouth-to-genital contact, engaging with multiple sexual partners, and having a high-risk sexual partner (e.g., someone with multiple sexual partners or STIs).

WAcPiU0.title: Cross-species transmission
WAcPiU0.description: The spread of a virus from one host species to a new host species, which is then able to infect and spread the virus throughout its own population, which creates a new host population.

dAcoiU0.title: Anti-Hu antibody
dAcoiU0.description: An antibody against the Hu protein, which is an RNA-binding protein in the nuclei of neurons. Associated with paraneoplastic neurological syndromes caused by small cell lung cancer (e.g., pure sensory neuropathy, encephalomyelitis, cerebellar degeneration).

UAcbQU0.title: 14-3-3 protein
UAcbQU0.description: A family of proteins that are ubiquitously expressed in the brain and involved in neural signaling, development, and neuroprotection. Increased concentrations of 14-3-3 in cerebrospinal fluid are associated with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.

2AcTQU0.title: Antineuronal antibodies
2AcTQU0.description: A group of antibodies whose presence in the serum and/or cerebrospinal fluid is associated with paraneoplastic neurologic disease (e.g., paraneoplastic encephalitis, paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration). Examples include anti-Hu antibodies, anti-Yo antibodies, and anti-Tr antibodies.

fAckQU0.title: Pulmonary embolism response team
fAckQU0.description: A multidisciplinary team of specialists that can evaluate and provide recommendations for the management of patients with pulmonary embolism. Team members can include hematologists, cardiologists, cardiac or vascular surgeons, radiologists, and emergency or critical care specialists.

TAc6QU0.title: Irregularly irregular pulse
TAc6QU0.description: A pulse in which the interval between individual pulse waves varies with no consistent pattern. Can be seen in patients with atrial fibrillation, multifocal atrial tachycardia, and wandering atrial pacemaker.

gAcFQU0.title: Irregularly irregular RR interval
gAcFQU0.description: An ECG pattern in which the time interval between two successive QRS complexes varies inconsistently. Can be seen in patients with atrial fibrillation, multifocal atrial tachycardia, and wandering atrial pacemaker.

SAcyQU0.title: Ulcer
SAcyQU0.description: A morphologic descriptor used to describe several types of lesions. In dermatology, it refers to a loss of the epidermis, including the basement membrane, with exposure of the underlying dermis (partial thickness), subcutis (full thickness), or muscle, bone, or tendon. In gastroenterology, it refers to a lesion that extends beyond the mucosa (disrupts the muscularis mucosae) to involve the submucosa and beyond.

media.title: Types of edges in ulcers and their most common causes

3AcSjU0.title: 46,XX testicular disorder of sex development
3AcSjU0.description: A rare disorder of sexual development caused by translocation of the SRY gene onto an X or other chromosome during spermatogenesis in individuals with 46,XX karyotype. Patients with this condition typically have male external genitalia, small or undescended testes, short stature, and infertility. They do not develop Müllerian duct structures.

destinations.label: Differences (disorders) of sex development → 46,XX testicular disorder of sex development

iAcJjU0.title: Acrosome
iAcJjU0.description: An organelle located at the anterior part of the head of spermatozoa. Develops from the Golgi apparatus during spermatogenesis. Contains enzymes, including acid phosphatase, neuraminidase, and hyaluronidase, which serve to dissolve the zona pellucida that surrounds the membrane of an oocyte.

destinations.label: Male reproductive organs →  Spermatogenesis and spermiogenesis

jAc_jU0.title: Pericardial decompression syndrome
jAc_jU0.description: A rare but life-threatening complication of pericardial fluid drainage. It occurs within 48 hours and is characterized by the sudden onset of acute heart failure symptoms (including pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock). The etiology is unknown but appears to be associated with the rapid drainage of large-volume effusions; to reduce the risk, gradual drainage over several days is recommended and close monitoring should be considered.

kAcmPU0.title: Piroxicam
kAcmPU0.description: A reversible nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug that inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 and 2. Typically used for the management of pain caused by osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis.

OAcIPU0.title: High-risk headache
OAcIPU0.description: A headache with clinical features that might indicate a serious or life-threatening condition. These features include, e.g., any red flags, features of secondary headaches, Horner syndrome, and fever.

lAcvPU0.title: Nonvalvular Afib
lAcvPU0.description: A term previously used to categorize atrial fibrillation occurring in patients with either no valvulopathy or any valvulopathy except moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis or a mechanical heart valve (these exceptions significantly increase the risk of thromboembolism).

MAcM4U0.title: Low FODMAP diet
MAcM4U0.description: A diet that is low in fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols. Used in the management of irritable bowel syndrome because high-FODMAP foods are associated with exacerbation of symptoms and gut inflammation.

nAc74U0.title: Cerebriform
nAc74U0.description: Resembling the structure of the brain (e.g., highly-grooved).

LAcw4U0.title: Extracorporeal photopheresis
LAcw4U0.description: A procedure that involves removal of blood from a patient, isolation of white blood cells, and UVA radiation of these cells before returning blood to the patient. Can be used to treat cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

oAc0kU0.title: Colostomy
oAc0kU0.description: A surgical procedure that creates an opening for the colon through the abdominal wall. Usually performed when a portion of the rectum or colon is surgically removed because of disease (e.g., colon cancer, rectal cancer, Crohn disease). Colostomy can also refer to the opening itself.

IAcYOU0.title: Opportunistic fungal infection
IAcYOU0.description: An infection caused by fungi that are typically present but nonpathogenic in immunocompetent individuals, e.g., Candida albicans. Most opportunistic fungal infections occur in individuals who are immunocompromised.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Opportunistic fungal infections

rAcfOU0.title: Handover
rAcfOU0.description: The exchange of information between health care providers when passing on responsibility for the care of patients  (e.g., at the end of a shift).

destinations.label: Daily life of the intern → Signouts

HAcKOU0.title: Read-back
HAcKOU0.description: A procedure performed during information transmission in which the receiver repeats key information back to the transmitter. Performed to prevent misinterpretation during verbal communication.

sActOU0.title: Authority gradient
sActOU0.description: The steepness of hierarchies in a team. Includes formally established and perceived hierarchies. This term often refers to how the distribution of power in a group affects communication and decision-making.

GAcBOU0.title: Teamwork training
GAcBOU0.description: A program in which members of a health care team with different training, roles, and responsibilities are trained to act together to promote the best interests of patients.

tAcXlU0.title: Low birth weight
tAcXlU0.description: A birth weight of < 2,500 g regardless of the gestational age.

FAcglU0.title: Very low birth weight
FAcglU0.description: A birth weight between 1,000 g and 1,499 g (regardless of the gestational age).

8AcOlU0.title: Extremely low birth weight
8AcOlU0.description: A birth weight <1,000 g (regardless of the gestational age).

EAc8lU0.title: Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease
EAc8lU0.description: A rare genetic condition that causes primary immunodeficiency. Affected individuals have defects in IFN-γ mediated immunity. This increases susceptibility to infection with weakly virulent mycobacteria (e.g., environmental mycobacteria, BCG vaccine).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital T-cell immunodeficiencies

vAcAlU0.title: Amphoric breath sounds
vAcAlU0.description: A harsh, hollow breath sound with high-pitched overtones heard on lung auscultation. It is produced by air passing through a large, superficial cavity that communicates with the bronchial system (e.g., a cyst or abscess) and cannot be heard if there is fluid or a fungal ball within the cavity.

DAc1NU0.title: Triangulated relationship
DAc1NU0.description: A phenomenon that describes when two individuals are in conflict and each individual tries to align with a third individual for support or seeks mediation from the third individual.

AAcRmU0.title: Torus tubarius
AAcRmU0.description: A mucosal prominence in the lateral aspect of the nasopharynx that protects the opening of the eustachian tube. Formed by the cartilaginous portion of the medial end of the eustachian tube.

_Ac5mU0.title: Semilunar hiatus
_Ac5mU0.description: A semicircular opening on the lateral aspect of the middle nasal meatus. Part of the ostiomeatal complex. Receives drainage from the frontal sinus (via the frontonasal duct), the maxillary sinus, and the anterior ethmoidal air cells.

zAcrmU0.title: Vegan diet
zAcrmU0.description: A plant-based diet that excludes all animal products (e.g., meat, seafood, dairy, eggs, honey). A fruitarian diet is a vegan diet that includes raw fruits but no vegetables or grains; some fruitarians eat also seeds and nuts.

destinations.label: Principles of nutrition → Vegetarian and vegan diet

Z_cZ5U0.title: Adverse drug reaction
Z_cZ5U0.description: An unintended negative effect caused by a drug that was administered appropriately (i.e., at a normal dose). Can be predictable (i.e., due to the known pharmacological effect of the drug) or unpredictable (e.g., due to an allergy).

0_ce5U0.title: Hindsight bias
0_ce5U0.description: A term used in safety analysis that refers to the tendency to judge the events that preceded a negative outcome as obvious errors based on that known outcome. Can also refer to a person's tendency to overestimate his or her ability to have predicted an outcome.

e_cxMU0.title: Glial cytoplasmic inclusion
e_cxMU0.description: A histopathologic finding of cytoplasmic inclusion bodies (which commonly contain alpha-synuclein) in glial cells. A pathologic hallmark of multiple system atrophy.

U_cbnU0.title: Cutaneous nocardiosis
U_cbnU0.description: An infection of the skin caused by Nocardia species, either through direct inoculation or dissemination from another site of infection. Manifestations include skin ulcerations, cellulitis, nodules, subcutaneous abscesses, and pyoderma. Spreading of the infection can result in lymphocutaneous nocardiosis (with regional lymphadenopathy and lymphadenitis) or subcutaneous mycetoma.

f_cknU0.title: Ligament of head of femur
f_cknU0.description: A ligament of the hip that connects the fovea capitis femoris with the acetabular notch. The foveolar artery passes through it. While the thigh is flexed, the ligament of the head of the femur tenses with lower extremity abduction and rotation and relaxes with lower extremity adduction.

destinations.label: Thigh, knee, and popliteal fossa → The femur

T_c6nU0.title: Foveolar artery
T_c6nU0.description: A branch of the obturator artery that supplies the head of the femur, passing through the ligament of the head of the femur. Its disruption can result in avascular necrosis of the hip.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Hip joint

g_cFnU0.title: Factitious hypercalcemia
g_cFnU0.description: An increase in total serum calcium levels caused by increased protein levels (e.g., hyperalbuminemia in dehydrated patients, paraproteinemia in patients with multiple myeloma). The concentration of non-protein bound calcium (ionized, physiologically active calcium) remains normal and the patient is, therefore, asymptomatic.

3_cSLU0.title: Volume-control ventilation
3_cSLU0.description: A mandatory mode of mechanical ventilation in which the tidal volume is the primary controlled ventilatory parameter and inspiratory pressure is variable.

R_clLU0.title: Pressure-control ventilation
R_clLU0.description: A mandatory mode of mechanical ventilation in which the inspiratory pressure limit is the primary controlled ventilatory parameter and tidal volume is variable.

i_cJLU0.title: Pressure-regulated volume-control
i_cJLU0.description: A mandatory mode of mechanical ventilation that is a hybrid of VCV and PCV. The inspiratory pressure limit and the desired target tidal volume is set by the clinician. The ventilator uses adaptive targeting to keep adjusting the inspiratory pressure with each breath based on the measured tidal volume.

Q_cuLU0.title: Pressure-support ventilation
Q_cuLU0.description: A spontaneous mode of mechanical ventilation in which the patient is primarily responsible for the initiation, rate, and volume of breaths. The ventilator provides IPAP and EPAP to support the patient's respiratory efforts.

j_c_LU0.title: Inspiratory flow rate
j_c_LU0.description: The airflow rate attained during inspiration. Reflects inspiratory effort in spontaneously breathing patients. Can be a set parameter in mechanically-ventilated patients to control the airflow delivered to the lungs during the inspiratory phase (e.g., 60 L/minute).

4_c3oU0.title: Palatine process
4_c3oU0.description: A part of the maxilla that forms large portions of the nasal floor and hard palate.

destinations.label: Skull → Temporal, infratemporal, and pterygopalatine fossae

k_cmoU0.title: Lacrimal punctum
k_cmoU0.description: An opening near the medial eyelid that collects tears produced by the associated lacrimal gland.

l_cvoU0.title: Superior nasal conchae
l_cvoU0.description: A pair of structures in the nose that arise from the posterior surface of the labyrinth of ethmoid. They connect to the lateral nasal wall via the superior meatus.

N_c-oU0.title: Middle nasal conchae
N_c-oU0.description: A pair of structures in the nose that consist of the medial surfaces of the labyrinth of ethmoid. They connect to the lateral nasal wall via the middle meatus.

5_ciKU0.title: Frontonasal duct
5_ciKU0.description: A duct that drains the frontal sinuses to the semilunar hiatus.

M_cMKU0.title: Pharyngeal recess
M_cMKU0.description: A well-demarcated groove in the lateral aspect of the nasopharynx, located behind the torus tubarius.

n_c7KU0.title: Adverse drug event
n_c7KU0.description: An injury that occurs in the course of the use of a drug. Includes adverse drug reactions (which occur at normal doses), medication errors, intentional overdoses, therapeutic failures, and adverse drug withdrawal events (harm caused by dose reduction and/or drug discontinuation).

L_cwKU0.title: Full-body plethysmography
L_cwKU0.description: A type of pulmonary function test that measures volumes that cannot be measured via spirometry (e.g., functional residual capacity, residual volume). Performed with the patient placed in a sealed container and breathing into a mouthpiece. Mainly used to diagnose obstructive and restrictive lung diseases.

media.title: Chalk Talk: Pulmonary function testing - Body plethysmography

6_cj6U0.title: Wheal
6_cj6U0.description: A well-circumscribed, pruritic, and erythematous plaque with a round, oval, or serpiginous shape. It is characteristic of urticaria.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Primary skin lesions

r_cfpU0.title: Bleomycin-induced lung injury
r_cfpU0.description: A collection of clinical syndromes affecting the lungs that are caused by bleomycin or a synergistic combination of the drug with high-flow oxygen. Manifestations include pulmonary fibrosis, bronchiolitis obliterans, acute pneumonitis, and ARDS.

7_c4pU0.title: Pressure support
7_c4pU0.description: A parameter used in spontaneous modes of mechanical ventilation consisting of added airway pressure during the inspiratory phase that supports the patient's work of breathing. In many clinical settings, the term pressure support is used synonymously with pressure-support ventilation, despite technically being a component of it.

H_cKpU0.title: Trigger sensitivity (mechanical ventilation)
H_cKpU0.description: A pre-set negative pressure or airflow threshold used to identify respiratory effort and trigger breath delivery in patients who are mechanically ventilated. Higher sensitivity allows patients to trigger breaths more easily but may also lead to inappropriate breath delivery (e.g., in response to other body movements).

s_ctpU0.title: Out-of-network provider
s_ctpU0.description: A group of providers, specialists, and hospitals who do not participate in an insurer’s provider network. Thus, the provider has not accepted the insurer's negotiated price, which often results in higher out-of-pocket costs for the patient.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

G_cBpU0.title: Bile salt
G_cBpU0.description: A bile acid that has been conjugated with glycine or taurine, which results in water solubility.

t_cXJU0.title: Vallecula sign
t_cXJU0.description: Narrowing or complete loss of the normal pre-epiglottic air shadow (which represents the vallecula) on a lateral x-ray of the neck. This sign is typically seen in acute epiglottitis.

8_cOJU0.title: 3,4-Dihydroxyphenylacetic acid
8_cOJU0.description: A neuronal metabolite formed by the breakdown of dopamine by monoamine oxidase.

destinations.label: Adrenal gland → Hormones of the adrenal medulla

D_c1qU0.title: Pleuritic chest pain
D_c1qU0.description: A symptom characterized by acute, sharp retrosternal pain that is typically aggravated by coughing, swallowing, and deep inspiration. Common causes include pleuritis, pulmonary embolism, pericarditis, myocardial infarction, and pneumothorax.

9_cNqU0.title: Tubocurarine
9_cNqU0.description: A long-acting, nondepolarizing skeletal muscle relaxant that competitively antagonizes acetylcholine at the motor junction, preventing depolarization and causing paralysis. Has a slow onset of action. Causes significant histamine release. Adverse effects include hypotonia and bronchospasm.

C_cqqU0.title: Burnout syndrome
C_cqqU0.description: A reaction to chronic stress that results in a sense of detachment, emotional exhaustion, and a decreased sense of accomplishment/productivity. Types of burnout include work burnout, caregiver burnout, and physician burnout.

x_cEqU0.title: ARDSnet protocol for FiO2/PEEP titration
x_cEqU0.description: A protocol developed for ARDS to guide the tandem titration of PEEP and FiO2 in the context of lung-protective ventilation.

A_cRIU0.title: Pulmonary oxygen toxicity
A_cRIU0.description: A manifestation of oxygen toxicity in the lungs that occurs following prolonged hyperoxemia, e.g., in hyperbaric oxygenation. Characterized by pulmonary edema, hemorrhage, and parenchymal damage. Symptoms include substernal pain, cough, and dyspnea. May become irreversible if exposure to high FiO₂ continues.

__c5IU0.title: Absorption atelectasis
__c5IU0.description: A form of alveolar collapse that occurs when the absorption of gas from an alveolus exceeds the amount of gas entering it. Absorption atelectasis occurs when highly concentrated oxygen displaces all the nitrogen (which usually holds alveoli open) and is rapidly absorbed, or when the air in alveoli distal to a bronchial obstruction is gradually reabsorbed.

z_crIU0.title: Type II myocardial infarction
z_crIU0.description: Acute myocardial injury caused by oxygen supply/demand mismatch. Underlying causes include coronary vasospasm, coronary artery dissection, microvascular dysfunction, emboli, anemia, and arrhythmias.

-_cDIU0.title: Severe otitis externa
-_cDIU0.description: A condition of inflammation of the external auditory canal that is persistent, associated with otitis media, or is associated with local or systemic spread. Can cause fever, intense pain, severe edema, regional lymphadenopathy, and periauricular erythema.

0zcerU0.title: Blastoconidium
0zcerU0.description: A fungal spore produced by budding. Examples of fungi that produce blastoconidia include Trichosporon spp. and Paracoccidioides spp.

azcQrU0.title: Castleman disease
azcQrU0.description: A group of rare lymphoproliferative disorders that can involve a single region of lymph nodes (unicentric) or multiple regions of lymph nodes (multicentric). Typically asymptomatic but can cause fevers, night sweats, and fatigue. Many cases are associated with HHV-8 infection.

YzcnrU0.title: Hemobilia
YzcnrU0.description: A condition of bleeding from the biliary tree. Manifestations include abdominal pain, melena, and acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Most commonly caused by procedural interventions (e.g., liver biopsy, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography).

bzcHrU0.title: Indapamide
bzcHrU0.description: A long-acting, thiazide-like diuretic that acts on the proximal segment of the distal tubule of the nephron. Commonly used to treat hypertension and edema due to congestive heart failure.

Xzc9rU0.title: Nevus simplex
Xzc9rU0.description: A common skin lesion of infancy that typically appears as an ill-defined, pink, blanchable macule or patch. Common locations include the glabella (angel kiss) and the occiput (stork bite). Formed by superficial capillaries in the upper dermis. Typically resolves across months to years.

1zc27U0.title: Paramedian pontine reticular formation
1zc27U0.description: A premotor structure in the brainstem responsible for the generation of eye and head movements, including horizontal saccades. A lesion at the paramedian pontine reticular formation results in a horizontal gaze palsy.

WzcP7U0.title: Duret hemorrhage
WzcP7U0.description: A hemorrhage of the midbrain caused by progressive brain herniation, which results in compression of the brainstem and subsequent damage to its vascular supply. Usually fatal.

dzco7U0.title: Palbociclib
dzco7U0.description: A cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitor that suppresses DNA replication and decreases tumor cell proliferation. Used in conjunction with endocrine therapy to treat breast cancer.

VzcG7U0.title: Curare
VzcG7U0.description: A long-acting neuromuscular blocking agent that competes with acetylcholine for nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. Historically used as a skeletal muscle relaxant (paralytic) in general anesthesia. It has since been replaced by synthetic derivatives that are safer to use.

ezcx7U0.title: Epistasis
ezcx7U0.description: A phenomenon in which the expression of one gene is influenced by the expression of another gene. For example, the gene responsible for albinism (lack of pigment) is not part of the gene responsible for skin color. Therefore, if the albinism gene is expressed, the individual will be pale-skinned, regardless of what skin color would have otherwise been expressed phenotypically.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

hzccsU0.title: Histone deacetylation
hzccsU0.description: A mechanism of gene regulation that involves the removal of an acetyl group from the lysine residues of histone proteins by histone deacetylases. This leads to more tightly coiled DNA and decreased transcription.

destinations.label: Nucleotides, DNA, and RNA →  DNA structure and the human genome

kzcmGU0.title: Pediatric appendicitis score
kzcmGU0.description: A score used to predict the likelihood of acute appendicitis based on clinical features and laboratory parameters in children.

OzcIGU0.title: Endocannabinoids
OzcIGU0.description: A group of endogenous arachidonic acid derivatives that can bind to cannabinoid receptors. They neuromodulate the central and peripheral nervous systems and are involved in the regulation of appetite and energy homeostasis.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Regulation of appetite and satiety

lzcvGU0.title: Cardiac catheterization laboratory
lzcvGU0.description: A location in the hospital where diagnostic and/or interventional coronary angiography is performed for cardiovascular diseases.

Nzc-GU0.title: Concertina effect
Nzc-GU0.description: A cyclical preexcitation pattern seen on ECG (e.g., in patients with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome) composed of periods of progressive shortening of the PR interval with an associated widening of the QRS complex. This pattern is suggestive of a long refractory period in the accessory pathway.

mzcVtU0.title: Van der Waals force
mzcVtU0.description: A relatively weak, noncovalent attraction between molecules or atoms. Attraction is distance-dependent and diminishes quickly when the distance between molecules increases.

5zcitU0.title: Cholesteryl ester transfer protein
5zcitU0.description: A cytoplasmatic protein that promotes the transport of cholesteryl esters and triglycerides between lipoproteins of different types.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

MzcMtU0.title: PCSK9
MzcMtU0.description: A protease primarily located on the plasma membrane of hepatocytes. Mediates the internalization of LDL receptors.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Lipid transport

nzc7tU0.title: Jamaican vomiting sickness
nzc7tU0.description: A condition that results from the ingestion of hypoglycin A and hypoglycin B, which are toxins found in fruits of the ackee tree that inhibit fatty acid oxidation. Manifestations include acute-onset vomiting and hypoglycemia, which can result in dehydration, shock, seizures, coma, and death.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

LzcwtU0.title: Wolff-Parkinson-White pattern
LzcwtU0.description: A condition in which patients present with the classic WPW preexcitation pattern but no documented arrhythmia or symptoms. This term is occasionally used to refer to the preexcitation pattern itself. Not to be confused with WPW syndrome, which consists of the characteristic preexcitation pattern and either symptoms or arrhythmias.

KzcUFU0.title: Short-lasting unilateral neuralgiform headache attacks with cranial autonomic symptoms
KzcUFU0.description: A condition of trigeminal autonomic cephalgia characterized by frequent episodes (> 20/day) of unilateral, stabbing pain that typically last from 2 seconds to 10 minutes. Usually accompanied by autonomic symptoms (e.g., nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, conjunctival injection, eyelid edema). Unlike trigeminal neuralgia, SUNA can be triggered without a refractory period.

6zcjFU0.title: Sandifer syndrome
6zcjFU0.description: A manifestation of gastroesophageal reflux disease in infants and children characterized by dystonic neck posturing (acquired torticollis) and opisthotonic arching of the spine associated with eating.

destinations.label: Gastroesophageal reflux in children → Clinical features

IzcY8U0.title: End-tidal CO₂
IzcY8U0.description: The partial pressure of carbon dioxide (in mm Hg) present in the air at the end of expiration. Commonly measured during mechanical ventilation and procedural sedation (i.e., through capnometry and capnography). Transducers that detect CO₂ may be applied externally to patients or built into ventilators.

rzcf8U0.title: Triggered activity
rzcf8U0.description: The repetitive activation of cardiac myocytes resulting from afterdepolarizations. It is an underlying mechanism of certain types of tachyarrhythmia (e.g., focal atrial tachycardia).

7zc48U0.title: Afterdepolarization
7zc48U0.description: Depolarization of the membrane of a cardiac myocyte that occurs prematurely, either during the repolarization phase of the action potential (early afterdepolarization) or after (late afterdepolarization). Can trigger the depolarization of new cells. Commonly occurs due to electrolyte channel imbalance.

HzcK8U0.title: Delayed afterdepolarization
HzcK8U0.description: An afterdepolarization that occurs after full repolarization (i.e., in phase 4 of the cardiac action potential cycle) and can cause arrhythmias. Typically occur in states of high intracellular calcium, e.g., digitalis toxicity, hyperkalemia, hypercalcemia, and catecholamine overload.

szct8U0.title: Early afterdepolarization
szct8U0.description: An afterdepolarization that occurs before full repolarization (i.e., in phase 2 or phase 3 of the cardiac action potential). Can cause arrhythmias in patients with heart failure and prolonged QT syndromes.

GzcB8U0.title: Per-protocol analysis
GzcB8U0.description: A method of statistical analysis in which treatment and control groups are compared using data from only the patients who finished the treatment that they were originally assigned to receive. This method helps to estimate the effect of the treatment itself, but it is prone to bias, as the original randomization is no longer preserved.

tzcXuU0.title: Noninferiority trial
tzcXuU0.description: A trial that intends to show that a new treatment's effect is not inferior by greater than a specified amount compared to the effect of an established treatment.

FzcguU0.title: Influenza season
FzcguU0.description: An annually-recurring period of time characterized by peak influenza activity (i.e., when influenza virus infections are most prevalent). It is approximately October to April in the northern hemisphere and May to October in the southern hemisphere.

uzcpuU0.title: Pericardiac fat pad sign
uzcpuU0.description: A radiographic finding of pericardial effusion. The effusion collects between the epicardiac fat and the anterior mediastinal fat, resulting in a > 2-mm stripe of soft tissue anterior to the heart that is visible on lateral chest x-ray.

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Diagnosis

Ezc8uU0.title: Posterior inferior bulge sign
Ezc8uU0.description: A radiologic finding of pericardial effusion. As an effusion begins to form, it collects first along the posterior surface of the heart and in the posterior-inferior pericardiac recess. This effusion is visible on lateral chest x-ray and thoracic CT as a bulge in the cardiac silhouette.

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Diagnosis

Dzc1EU0.title: Peri-arrest arrhythmia
Dzc1EU0.description: Any arrhythmia causing hemodynamic compromise, which, if untreated, can result in cardiac arrest. Typically grouped into three categories: bradycardias, narrow complex tachycardias, and broad complex tachycardias.

9zcNEU0.title: Limiting reagent
9zcNEU0.description: A chemical substance that, when depleted, causes a stop to a chemical reaction. Determines the amount of product that can be formed in a given chemical reaction.

xzcEEU0.title: Granulocytosis
xzcEEU0.description: The presence of an increased number of granulocytes (i.e., neutrophils, basophils, eosinophils).

yzcdvU0.title: Homing
yzcdvU0.description: The movement of a cell toward a specific type of tissue, usually in response to the presence of specific chemokines, receptors, and/or antigens.

AzcRvU0.title: Infundibular septum
AzcRvU0.description: A portion of the ventricular septum. Defects in the infundibular septum account for ~ ⅓ of all ventricular septal defects. These defects result in loss of support of the right and/or left aortic valve cusp, which results in progressive aortic regurgitation.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Tetralogy of Fallot

_zc5vU0.title: Hypocalvaria
_zc5vU0.description: A condition of incomplete formation of the skull bones. It is a birth defect associated with maternal ACE inhibitor use.

zzcrvU0.title: Partogram
zzcrvU0.description: A graphical representation of a patient's cervical dilation over time. Facilitates comparison with the normal progress of labor achieved by 95% of nulliparous women who have singleton term pregnancies, spontaneous onset of labor, vaginal delivery, and normal neonatal outcomes.

-zcDvU0.title: Pancrelipase
-zcDvU0.description: A drug that contains a combination of lipase, amylase, and protease that have been harvested from porcine pancreatic glands. Aids in the breakdown of fats, starch, and protein in the duodenum. Used to treat pancreatic insufficiency (e.g., due to cystic fibrosis).

Z-cZDU0.title: Buprenorphine/naloxone
Z-cZDU0.description: An oral drug that combines a partial opioid agonist (buprenorphine) and an opioid antagonist (naloxone). Used to treat opioid use disorder. The opioid antagonist is not readily absorbed when taken orally. However, if the drug is misused (e.g., injected or inhaled), the antagonist negates the therapeutic effects of the partial agonist.

0-ceDU0.title: Cytokine storm
0-ceDU0.description: An acute, systemic inflammatory response caused by an excess release of cytokines and subsequent overactivation of the immune system (e.g., T lymphocytes, macrophages, endothelial cells). Can be triggered by systemic infections and drugs (e.g., oxaliplatin and lenalidomide).

a-cQDU0.title: Posterolateral tract
a-cQDU0.description: A spinal cord tract located at the tips of the dorsal horns. Contains axons that carry sensory information (e.g., pressure, crude touch). The axons ascend or descend in this tract before entering the gray matter of the dorsal horn, where they synapse to second-order neurons that project to the contralateral side of the spinal cord and ultimately form the spinothalamic tract.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

media.title: Cross section of the spinal cord
Ascending sensory tracts of the spinal cord

Y-cnDU0.title: Diabetic lumbosacral plexopathy
Y-cnDU0.description: A form of lumbosacral plexus injury caused by diabetes mellitus. Microvasculitis causes damage to the plexus formed by the spinal roots T12-S4, which results in a variety of symptoms, including pain in the lower back and legs and progressive weakness of the proximal legs.

b-cHDU0.title: Inflammasome
b-cHDU0.description: A cytosolic multiprotein oligomer of the innate immune system that promotes the initiation of inflammatory responses and induction of pyroptosis. Detects pathogenic microorganisms, crystals (e.g., uric acid crystals), and sterile stressors and triggers the activation of the highly proinflammatory cytokines IL-1b and IL-18.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Acute local inflammation

X-c9DU0.title: Bare lymphocyte syndrome
X-c9DU0.description: A congenital immunodeficiency disorder characterized by deficiencies in major histocompatibility complex I or II, which are usually expressed on lymphocytes. Typically results in recurrent respiratory, gastrointestinal, and urinary tracts.

1-c2wU0.title: Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity
1-c2wU0.description: An immune response in which immune cells bind to and lyse target cells that have specific antibodies attached to their surface antigens. Most commonly mediated by NK cells that interact with IgG and subsequently release cytotoxic substances to kill the target cell. Eosinophils can also mediate ADCC by interacting with IgE-coated helminths.

d-cowU0.title: Starvation
d-cowU0.description: A state of severe deficiency of caloric energy intake that is below the level necessary to maintain normal bodily functions. Prolonged starvation leads to depletion of vital proteins, organ failure, and death.

V-cGwU0.title: White lung
V-cGwU0.description:
A term that can refer to:
1. A radiographic finding of extensive consolidation and/or atelectasis of the lung.
2. Asbestosis of the lung.

U-cb9U0.title: First part of the duodenum
U-cb9U0.description: The proximal segment of the duodenum. Lies intraperitoneally between the pylorus and the superior duodenal flexure at the level of the L1 vertebra. It is posterior to the gallbladder and quadrate lobe and anterior to the bile duct, gastroduodenal artery, portal vein, inferior vena cava, and pancreatic head. Its superior surface is attached to the lesser omentum. Its inferior surface is attached to the greater omentum.

2-cT9U0.title: Venturi mask
2-cT9U0.description: An oxygen delivery system consisting of a face mask attached to an air-entrainment valve that has holes to draw in room air and dilute the oxygen at a predictable rate. The FiO₂ delivered depends on the size of these holes and the oxygen flow rate. Six color-coded valves are available that deliver fixed FiO₂ increments ranging from 24% to 60%.

destinations.label: Oxygen therapy → Basic oxygen delivery systems

f-ck9U0.title: Second part of the duodenum
f-ck9U0.description: The descending part of the duodenum. It lies at the level of L1-L3 vertebrae, posterior to the transverse colon and anterior to the right kidney. Curves around the head of the pancreas. Contains the ampulla of Vater, the sphincter of Oddi, the minor duodenal papilla, and the major duodenal papilla.

T-c69U0.title: Third part of the duodenum
T-c69U0.description: The inferior portion of the duodenum. Courses horizontally to the left, anterior to the abdominal aorta and the inferior vena cava and posterior to the superior mesenteric vessels.

S-cy9U0.title: Acute compartment syndrome
S-cy9U0.description: A surgical emergency in which increased pressure within a muscle compartment leads to impaired tissue perfusion. Most commonly affects the lower legs but can also occur in other parts of the upper and lower limbs and the abdomen. Presents with rapidly progressive pain and paresthesia, and without treatment, eventually motor deficits, absent pulses, pallor, and poikilothermia. Diagnosis is confirmed via measurement of compartment pressures.

h-ccCU0.title: Chronic exertional compartment syndrome
h-ccCU0.description: Recurrent pain and/or neurological symptoms in an extremity due to exertion. Exertion increases pressure in a noncompliant fascial compartment, leading to transiently reduced tissue perfusion.

R-clCU0.title: Low-dose computed tomography scan
R-clCU0.description: An imaging technique that combines multiple x-ray images, often taken in a helical pattern around the patient, to create cross-sectional pictures of a structure. Delivers less radiation compared to conventional CT scan techniques. Most often used to scan the chest as part of lung cancer screening.

i-cJCU0.title: GNAS gene
i-cJCU0.description: A gene that encodes the alpha subunit of G proteins. Mutations in the GNAS gene are associated with McCune-Albright syndrome, primary macronodular adrenal hyperplasia, and progressive osseous heteroplasia.

Q-cuCU0.title: Pseudoacromegaly
Q-cuCU0.description: A syndrome characterized by severe insulin resistance and accelerated linear growth (due to hyperinsulinemia and subsequent activation of IGF-1 receptors).

4-c3xU0.title: Equipment for difficult airway management
4-c3xU0.description: Specialized equipment that is readily available for difficult airway management. Includes various oral and nasopharyngeal airways, forceps, bag valve mask devices, stylets, tube exchangers, direct and video laryngoscopes, flexible bronchoscopes, supraglottic devices, endotracheal tubes, and surgical airway sets. Often available as a portable storage unit.

k-cmxU0.title: Compressive myelopathy
k-cmxU0.description: A spinal cord injury caused by compression (e.g., from disc herniation, osteophytes, or tumors). Typically results in sensory loss and upper motor neuron signs (e.g., spastic paralysis, hyperreflexia) below the level of compression and lower motor neuron signs (e.g., flaccid paralysis, hyporeflexia) at the level of the lesion.

N-c-xU0.title: Leukotriene A₄
N-c-xU0.description: The first product created from 5-hydroperoxyeicosatetraenoic acid (5-HPETE) in the 5-lipoxygenase pathway. Derivatives include leukotriene C₄, D₄, and E₄.

m-cVBU0.title: Palmitoleic acid
m-cVBU0.description: An omega-7 monounsaturated fatty acid that is synthesized from palmitic acid. Dietary sources include breast milk, animal fats, vegetable oils, and marine oils. It is a common constituent of human adipose tissue and reaches high concentrations in the liver.

5-ciBU0.title: Postrenal acute kidney injury
5-ciBU0.description: A type of acute kidney injury caused by obstruction of the urinary tract (e.g., due to stones, benign prostatic hyperplasia, malignancy, congenital anomalies). The BUN:Cr ratio and the fractional excretion of sodium (FENa) vary.

L-cwBU0.title: Spacer
L-cwBU0.description: A large, empty plastic device used to facilitate the inhalation of asthma medicine. Collects the medicine released by metered-dose inhalers (MDIs), thus facilitating more time for controlled inhalation. Spacers can reduce the risk of developing oral candidiasis from inhaled glucocorticoid therapy.

K-cUyU0.title: Automatic static perimetry
K-cUyU0.description: A systematic testing modality that uses a computer program to measure visual field function. Generates different patterns (maps) of visual sensitivity that correspond to different diseases of the eye.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Visual field examination

6-cjyU0.title: Humidified oxygen
6-cjyU0.description: The addition of water vapor to supplemental oxygen in order to improve patient comfort.

destinations.label: Oxygen therapy → General principles of oxygen delivery

p-cLyU0.title: Nasal cannula
p-cLyU0.description: A common method of oxygen delivery consisting of a tube connected to an oxygen source that branches out into two small hollow plastic prongs that are placed in the nostrils. Can deliver FiO₂ of 20–40% at flow rates of 1–6 L/minute.

destinations.label: Oxygen therapy → Basic oxygen delivery systems

J-csyU0.title: Simple oxygen face mask
J-csyU0.description: An oxygen delivery system consisting of a face mask connected to an oxygen source. The mask has exit valves to prevent rebreathing expired air but does not have an external reservoir bag (in contrast to a nonrebreather mask). Delivers FiO₂ of 30–60% at flow rates of 5-10 L/minute.

destinations.label: Oxygen therapy → Basic oxygen delivery systems

q-cCyU0.title: Transtracheal oxygen therapy
q-cCyU0.description: A method of delivering long-term oxygen therapy that is an alternative to nasal cannula. A narrow catheter attached to oxygen tubing is percutaneously inserted directly into the trachea, bypassing the upper airways.

destinations.label: Oxygen therapy → Advanced oxygen delivery systems

I-cYAU0.title: Ergot toxicity
I-cYAU0.description: An intoxication that causes convulsive (e.g., fasciculations, paresthesias, and seizures) and/or gangrenous symptoms (e.g., peripheral necrosis). Historically, it occurred from consumption of ergot alkaloids produced by fungi (e.g., contaminated rye). Nowadays, it is only rarely seen due to overdosing or pharmacological interactions with ergot-based drugs (e.g., ergotamine).

7-c4AU0.title: Ultrasound biomicroscopy
7-c4AU0.description: A noninvasive, high-resolution ultrasonographic technique used to visualize structures in the anterior segment of the eye.

s-ctAU0.title: Goldmann applanation tonometry
s-ctAU0.description: The measurement of intraocular pressure with a nonportable applanation tonometer. A probe is placed directly over the anesthetized cornea and the force required to indent the cornea is measured. Goldmann applanation tonometry is the gold standard for measuring intraocular pressure. It is operator dependent, requires specialist training, can only be performed in a seated position, and is less accurate in corneal scarring.

t-cX_U0.title: Target oxygen saturation range
t-cX_U0.description: A recommended oxygen saturation range (as detected by pulse oximetry) for a patient receiving supplemental oxygen therapy. The range depends on the condition being treated and whether the patient has any risk factors for complications from oxygen therapy.

u-cp_U0.title: Electrophysiological study
u-cp_U0.description: An invasive cardiac-specific electrophysiological test used as part of the evaluation and management of arrhythmias. Under fluoroscopy, multielectrode catheters are placed in multiple locations in the heart and electrical stimulation is used to stimulate and diagnose arrhythmias. Radiofrequency or cryogenic ablation of arrhythmogenic foci can be performed at the same time.

v-cA_U0.title: PALM-COEIN system
v-cA_U0.description: A classification system for causes of abnormal uterine bleeding. Categorized by structural (PALM: Polyps, Adenomyosis, Leiomyomas, Malignancy and hyperplasia) and nonstructural (COEIN: Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, and Not otherwise classified) causes.

C-cqzU0.title: Phlegmon
C-cqzU0.description: A localized inflammatory mass of the soft tissue, usually secondary to a bacterial infection. May develop into an abscess.

x-cEzU0.title: Fecalith
x-cEzU0.description: A hardened mass of feces that forms as a result of chronic constipation. In some cases, it can be felt as a palpable abdominal mass. Can result in fecal impaction.

B-czzU0.title: Appendiceal fecalith
B-czzU0.description: A concretion of feces that develops in the appendix. Can obstruct the appendiceal lumen, which increases the risk of developing acute appendicitis (especially perforated appendicitis). May be visible on x-ray or CT scan as a well-defined hyperdensity.

y-cd-U0.title: Cefotetan
y-cd-U0.description: A second-generation cephalosporin that can be used to treat bone and joint infections, gynecologic infections, lower respiratory tract infections, skin infections, and urinary tract infections.

A-cR-U0.title: SCD
A-cR-U0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Sickle cell disease
2. Sudden cardiac death
3. Subacute combined degeneration

_-c5-U0.title: Handheld applanation tonometry
_-c5-U0.description: A portable handheld device used to measure intraocular pressure. A probe is placed directly over the anesthetized cornea and the force required to indent the cornea is measured.

--cD-U0.title: Logorrhea
--cD-U0.description: An explosive, excessive, incoherent, and uncontrollable talkativeness that is associated with certain psychiatric conditions (e.g., mania).

ZZ1ZZ20.title: Functional ovarian cyst
ZZ1ZZ20.description: An ovarian cyst that develops due to disruption in the development of follicles or the corpus luteum. The most common types are follicular cysts, corpus luteum cysts, and theca lutein cysts.

0Z1eZ20.title: Nonfunctional ovarian cysts
0Z1eZ20.description: A group of ovarian cysts that do not produce hormones. Includes chocolate cysts (endometriomas), dermoid cysts (cystic teratomas), cystadenoma (serous or mucinous), and some malignant cysts (ovarian cancers).

YZ1nZ20.title: One-Minute Telegram 1-2020-1/3
YZ1nZ20.description:
Remdesivir, a nucleotide analog that inhibits viral RNA polymerases, has been proven to be effective against SARS-CoV-2 in vitro and its relative safety has already been demonstrated in a phase 3 trial in patients with Ebola.
Gilead Sciences, the producer of remdesivir, has published data on an international group of 53 patients hospitalized with COVID-19, who were selected based on undisclosed criteria. [...]

bZ1HZ20.title: One-Minute Telegram 1-2020-2/3
bZ1HZ20.description: Evidence that the loss of smell and taste may precede respiratory symptoms in COVID-19 was found early in the course of the pandemic. An observational case series from Wuhan, China, has now investigated the presence of further neurological symptoms in hospitalized patients. [...]

XZ19Z20.title: One-Minute Telegram 1-2020-3/3
XZ19Z20.description: The CDC has been tracing e-cigarette, or vaping, product use-associated lung injury (EVALI) since August 2019. It is strongly linked to vitamin E acetate, an additive sometimes found in vape cartridges, and can cause acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). [...]

dZ1o020.title: Nihilistic delusion
dZ1o020.description: A fixed, false belief that one is dead or does not exist, that one's body is breaking down, or that the world around them does not exist.

VZ1G020.title: Ovarian serous cystadenoma
VZ1G020.description: The most common type of benign ovarian epithelial neoplasm. Thought to derive from fallopian tube epithelium. Typically appears as a unilateral, enlarged, and unilocular cystic mass of the ovary on ultrasonography. Characterized by psammoma bodies on histopathologic examination.

destinations.label: Overview of ovarian tumors →  Epithelial ovarian tumors

eZ1x020.title: Zolmitriptan
eZ1x020.description: A triptan primarily used for the treatment of acute migraines. Adverse effects include jaw tightness, warm/cold sensation, and heaviness sensation.

UZ1ba20.title: Omental cake
UZ1ba20.description: A radiologic finding of omental thickening. Most commonly results from infiltration of the omental fat by intraperitoneal metastases (e.g., from gastrointestinal or ovarian cancers).

2Z1Ta20.title: Ovarian mucinous cystadenoma
2Z1Ta20.description: The second most common type of benign ovarian epithelial neoplasm. Characterized by thick and gelatinous mucin secretion. Typically appears as a unilateral, enlarged, and multilocular cystic mass of the ovary on ultrasonography.

destinations.label: Overview of ovarian tumors →  Epithelial ovarian tumors

fZ1ka20.title: Writer's dystonia
fZ1ka20.description: A type of focal dystonia that affects hands. Typically manifests when performing specific tasks that require fine hand movements (e.g., writing, playing an instrument).

TZ16a20.title: Pemphigus
TZ16a20.description: A group of life-threatening autoimmune blistering diseases characterized by acantholysis and the development of autoantibodies against desmosomes that affect the skin and, sometimes, the mucosa. Types of pemphigus include pemphigus vulgaris and pemphigus foliaceus.

gZ1Fa20.title: Empty delta sign
gZ1Fa20.description: A radiological finding in contrast-enhanced CT/MRI that resembles the Greek letter delta (Δ). Consists of a central hypodensity (representing the thrombus) with a triangular outline of contrast enhancement. May be seen in cerebral venous thrombosis of the superior sagittal sinus.

SZ1ya20.title: Focus-assessed transthoracic echocardiography
SZ1ya20.description: A truncated transthoracic echo protocol used in critically ill patients to provide a rapid assessment of cardiac function and guide diagnosis. Typically performed at the patient's bedside by noncardiologists.

3Z1SY20.title: Mechanic's hands
3Z1SY20.description: A dermatologic finding characterized by hyperkeratotic skin with horizontal fissures on the palmar and/or lateral parts of the fingers. Associated with dermatomyositis and polymyositis.

nZ17X20.title: Visual acuity
nZ17X20.description: A measurement of clarity or sharpness of central vision at various distances. Can be measured using a Snellen chart (using letters, numbers, tumbling Es, or picture tests). Normal visual acuity is expressed as 20/20 vision, which indicates that the individual can see clearly at 20 feet what should normally be seen at that distance. 20/40 vision indicates that the individual must be 20 feet away to see what a person with normal vision can see at 40 feet.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Visual acuity

LZ1wX20.title: Obsession
LZ1wX20.description: A repetitive, persistent, intrusive, and unpleasurable thought or urge (e.g., that food is contaminated, that one must carry out acts of violence). Obsessions often cause distress and anxiety. Often related to a compulsion (i.e., a ritualistic, repetitive behavior) that may relieve or suppress the obsession.

oZ10c20.title: Compulsion
oZ10c20.description: A repetitive, ritualistic behavior (e.g., touching, washing) or mental act (e.g., counting, repeating a word silently) that one feels is necessary to perform. Often in response to an obsession (i.e., a repetitive, persistent thought), such as fear of contamination or discomfort with disorganization.

KZ1Uc20.title: Primary mitral regurgitation
KZ1Uc20.description: A subtype of mitral valve insufficiency caused by structural dysfunction of the valve apparatus itself (i.e., not due to a secondary cause such as heart failure).

6Z1jc20.title: Secondary mitral regurgitation
6Z1jc20.description: A subtype of mitral valve insufficiency caused by dysfunction of the left ventricle (i.e., the valve apparatus is normal).

JZ1sc20.title: Voxel
JZ1sc20.description: A discrete element of a 3D image mapped on a regular grid. It is a basic unit of CT image calculation. A voxel is the cube equivalent to a pixel in a 2D image, the term being a contraction of “VOLume ELement” analogous to the contraction of “PICture ELement” in “pixel.”

rZ1f120.title: Religious delusion
rZ1f120.description: A fixed, false belief with religious reference. Affected individuals may believe they are a god or receive divine messages.

7Z14120.title: Delusion of poverty
7Z14120.description: A fixed, false belief that one is financially incapacitated or that poverty is inevitable.

HZ1K120.title: Pericardiotomy
HZ1K120.description: A procedure performed to drain fluid from the pericardial sac. Commonly used in the management of cardiac tamponade.

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Treatment

vZ1AW20.title: Dorsal slit
vZ1AW20.description: A procedure in which an incision is made in the foreskin of the dorsal aspect of the penis. Can be used to relieve strangulation of the glans penis (e.g., by a paraphimosis) or to visualize the urethral meatus in patients who have a phimosis.

destinations.label: Disorders of the glans penis and foreskin → Paraphimosis

9Z1Nd20.title: Bizarre delusion
9Z1Nd20.description: A fixed, false belief of a phenomenon that could never happen in real life because it is physically or logically implausible (e.g., that one's organs were removed without leaving any scars).

CZ1qd20.title: Rizatriptan
CZ1qd20.description: A triptan used for the treatment of acute migraines. Adverse effects include fatigue, somnolence, and dizziness.

001ee20.title: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
001ee20.description: A type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma characterized by malignant T-cell infiltration of the skin. Includes mycosis fungoides and Sezary syndrome.

a01Qe20.title: Dysphasia
a01Qe20.description: A decreased ability to comprehend and/or formulate language due to damage to specific brain regions.

Y01ne20.title: Palpation of the axillary lymph nodes
Y01ne20.description: A part of the physical examination in which the examiner supports the patient's relaxed arm and palpates into the axillary region, pressing their fingers against the chest wall behind the pectoralis muscle and sliding downward.

media.title: Palpable lymph nodes of the axillary region

b01He20.title: Unsealed source radiotherapy
b01He20.description: A form of radiation therapy that involves the administration of radiopharmaceuticals that accumulate in target tissues.

X019e20.title: Sealed source radiotherapy
X019e20.description: A form of radiation therapy in which radioactive material is implanted either beside or within the target tissue. Involves targeted high-dose radiation delivery to the tumor, resulting in fewer adverse effects on surrounding healthy tissue compared to external radiation therapy.

c01aU20.title: Radiation-induced lung injury
c01aU20.description: An injury to the lungs caused by exposure to ionizing radiation. Causes inflammation (radiation pneumonitis) in the early stage and permanent changes (radiation-induced pulmonary fibrosis) in the late stage.

1012U20.title: Posterior acoustic shadowing
1012U20.description: A form of ultrasonographic imaging artifact characterized by a lack of echoic signal behind structures that strongly absorb and/or reflect ultrasonic waves (e.g., bone, metal, gallstones).

W01PU20.title: Iridocorneal angle
W01PU20.description: An angular recess located between the cornea and the anterior surface of the iris. Contains the trabecular meshwork through which aqueous humor drains from the anterior chamber of the eye into the scleral venous sinus. Occlusion of this angle is the underlying cause of angle-closure glaucoma.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Segments and chambers of the eye

V01GU20.title: Hartmann pouch of the gallbladder
V01GU20.description: A dilation that may be seen on the ventral aspect of the gallbladder, proximal to the gallbladder neck. Gallstones can become trapped in this pouch. Previously thought to be a pathologic finding but now thought to be an anatomic variant.

e01xU20.title: Glaucomatous optic neuropathy
e01xU20.description: Damage to the optic disc, optic nerve, and retinal nerve fiber layer and the subsequent visual impairment due to chronically elevated intraocular pressures of open-angle or angle-closure glaucoma. A characteristic finding is optic disc cupping on fundus examination.

U01b220.title: PSA
U01b220.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Prostate-specific antigen
2. Procedural sedation and analgesia

201T220.title: Radiopharmaceutical
201T220.description: A drug that contains radioisotopes that are used for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Examples include compounds that contain Tc99m-pertechnetate (which is taken up by the thyroid and used for imaging) and radium-223 (which is taken up by the bone and used to treat metastatic cancer in the bone).

f01k220.title: Popliteal artery entrapment syndrome
f01k220.description: A rare condition caused by an accessory or aberrant insertion of the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle, which compresses the popliteal artery against the medial condyle of the femur during muscle contraction. Manifests with claudication pain.

g01F220.title: CO-oximetry
g01F220.description: A laboratory study that measures the percentages of different hemoglobin concentrations in blood samples using spectrophotometry. Most commonly used to measure carboxyhemoglobin but can also be used to differentiate oxygenated hemoglobin, deoxygenated hemoglobin, methemoglobin, and sometimes sulfhemoglobin. Testing is indicated if there is a saturation gap (i.e., discrepancy) between SpO₂ and PaO₂ measurements. CO-oximetry performed on blood samples is more reliable than noninvasive pulse CO-oximetry.

h01cf20.title: Ultrafiltration
h01cf20.description: The use of a semi-permeable membrane to remove isosmotic fluid. In hemodialysis, ultrafiltration is combined with filtration and the removal of toxic substances. In congestive heart failure, ultrafiltration can be used alone to remove excessive fluid.

301Sf20.title: Head impulse, nystagmus, test of skew
301Sf20.description: A three-step physical examination technique used to clinically differentiate between peripheral and central causes of acute vestibular syndrome. Consists of a head impulse test, evaluation of nystagmus, and a test of skew. Peripheral causes have a positive head impulse test, unidirectional horizontal nystagmus, and a negative test of skew. A central cause is suspected if any of the following are present: vertical, torsional, or direction-changing nystagmus, a negative head impulse test, or a positive skew deviation test.

R01lf20.title: Caloric test
R01lf20.description: A physical examination maneuver used to evaluate vestibular function. Either warm or cold water is infused into the external ear canal to create a temperature change in the endolymph, which causes it to shift. Cold water infusion triggers contralateral horizontal nystagmus; warm water triggers ipsilateral horizontal nystagmus. Unilaterally decreased or absent response indicates ipsilateral vestibular hypofunction.

i01Jf20.title: Sunitinib
i01Jf20.description: An inhibitor of multiple receptor tyrosine kinases that is used to treat gastrointestinal stromal tumors, advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, and renal cell carcinoma.

Q01uf20.title: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy
Q01uf20.description: A rare, autosomal dominant disorder characterized by muscle weakness and wasting that primarily affects the face, shoulder blades, and upper arms. Symptoms typically are slowly progressive and arise before 20 years of age.

P01WT20.title: Partial hospitalization program
P01WT20.description: A program used in the treatment of psychiatric conditions and substance use disorders. Participating individuals reside at home but visit the treatment facility for day programs that include therapy and skill-building groups. The goals of a PHP are to reduce hospitilizations and provide participants with a stable daily structure.

4013T20.title: Reflective listening
4013T20.description: A communication strategy that involves listening to and understanding what another person is saying (both verbally and through body language) and then reflecting upon what was heard and responding actively.

k01mT20.title: Drug potentiation
k01mT20.description: A pharmacologic phenomenon in which the effect of a drug is increased in the presence of another drug that itself has no therapeutic effect. For example, the administration of carbidopa (a decarboxylase inhibitor) in combination with levodopa prevents peripheral decarboxylation of levodopa and, therefore increases its availability.
