destinations.label: Fundamentals of pharmacology → Drug interactions and the cytochrome P450 system

O01IT20.title: Synergistic drug interaction
O01IT20.description: A pharmacologic phenomenon in which the resultant effect of two administered drugs is greater than the sum of their individual effects. Examples of two drugs that have synergistic interaction are aspirin and clopidogrel for dual antiplatelet therapy.

destinations.label: Fundamentals of pharmacology → Drug interactions and the cytochrome P450 system

l01vT20.title: Antagonistic drug interaction
l01vT20.description: A pharmacologic phenomenon in which the resultant effect of two administered drugs is less than the sum of their individual effects. Examples of two drugs that have antagonistic interaction are ethanol and methanol; ethanol has a higher affinity for alcohol dehydrogenase and, therefore, competitively inhibits the formation of toxic metabolites in patients with methanol toxicity.

destinations.label: Fundamentals of pharmacology → Drug interactions and the cytochrome P450 system

N01-T20.title: Additive drug interaction
N01-T20.description: A pharmacologic phenomenon in which the resultant effect of two administered drugs is equal to the sum of their individual effects (neither synergistic nor antagonistic). Examples of two drugs that have additive interaction for analgesia include aspirin and acetaminophen.

destinations.label: Fundamentals of pharmacology → Drug interactions and the cytochrome P450 system

m01Vg20.title: Permissive drug interaction
m01Vg20.description: A pharmacologic phenomenon in which the presence of one substance is required for another substance to exert its full effect. For example, cortisol increases the sensitivity of adrenoceptors to catecholamines.

destinations.label: Fundamentals of pharmacology → Drug interactions and the cytochrome P450 system

501ig20.title: Monogenic disorder
501ig20.description: A condition caused by a single gene defect, which may be inherited or occur sporadically. Examples of monogenic disorders include sickle cell anemia, cystic fibrosis, and Huntington disease.

n017g20.title: Palilalia
n017g20.description: A speech disorder characterized by the involuntary repetition of words or phrases with increasing rapidity. Diseases associated with palilalia include schizophrenia, Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, and Tourette syndrome.

p01LS20.title: Review of systems
p01LS20.description: A part of history taking during which a patient is asked questions about symptoms related to different organ systems that are relevant to the presenting complaint. The objective of the review of systems is to reveal any associated symptoms and/or conditions that might affect the patient's diagnosis and management. The current Medicare documentation guidelines define 14 systems for review: Constitutional; Eyes; Ears, Nose, Mouth, Throat; Cardiovascular; Respiratory; Gastrointestinal; Genitourinary; Musculoskeletal; Integumentary (skin and/or breast); Neurological; Psychiatric; Endocrine; Hematologic/Lymphatic; and Allergic/Immunologic.

J01sS20.title: ROS
J01sS20.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Reactive oxygen species
2. Review of systems

q01CS20.title: Gas solubility coefficient
q01CS20.description: A measure of the solubility of a gas in a liquid. Defined as the ratio of the amount of gas dissolved in a liquid to the partial pressure of the gas at equilibrium. Changes with temperature.

7014h20.title: Anterior corticospinal tract
7014h20.description: A descending white matter tract composed of myelinated axons of upper motor neurons that originate from the cerebral cortex. Formed at the level of the caudal medulla primarily by nondecussating corticospinal tract fibers. Descends into the spinal cord before crossing over at the anterior spinal commissure to terminate on anterior horn cells. Provides voluntary motor control over contralateral axial (i.e., trunk) muscles.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

H01Kh20.title: Corticobulbar tract
H01Kh20.description: A descending white matter tract composed of myelinated axons of upper motor neurons that originate from the cerebral cortex. Terminates on motor nuclei of cranial nerves. Provides voluntary motor control of muscles of the face and neck.

media.title: Cross section of the spinal cord

s01th20.title: Thalamocortical tract
s01th20.description: An ascending white matter tract composed of the myelinated axons of third-order neurons that originate from the thalamus. Terminates on different regions of the cortex. Transmits somatosensory information from the thalamus to the cortex.

G01Bh20.title: Chromhidrosis
G01Bh20.description: A rare condition characterized by the production of colored sweat. Caused by the secretion of lipofuscin granules by the sweat glands, which can result in black, brown, blue, green, or yellow coloration.

x01ER20.title: Test of skew
x01ER20.description: A bedside examination to clinically distinguish between peripheral and central causes of vertigo and acute vestibular syndrome. The patient is asked to fixate on a point, and the eyes are alternately occluded. The presence of skew deviation (vertical ocular misalignment) is indicative of a central cause (e.g., cerebellar stroke).

B01zR20.title: IVF
B01zR20.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. In vitro fertilization
2. Intravenous fluids

y01di20.title: Pediatric Intensive Care Unit
y01di20.description: An intensive care unit that provides specialized care for pediatric patients with life-threatening medical and/or surgical conditions.

A01Ri20.title: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit
A01Ri20.description: An intensive care unit that provides specialized care for newborns with life-threatening medical and/or surgical conditions.

z01ri20.title: Needlestick injury
z01ri20.description: An injury caused by accidental puncture of the skin with a needle.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Health care personnel exposures

-01Di20.title: Sharps injury
-01Di20.description: An umbrella term for injuries caused by accidental penetration of the skin by any sharp object (e.g., scalpel, wires, pins, glass shards).

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Health care personnel exposures

Za1ZQ20.title: History of present illness
Za1ZQ20.description: A detailed description of a patient's chief complaint and progression of the symptoms from the initial onset or from the previous encounter.

destinations.label: Medical history → History of present illness

0a1eQ20.title: Past medical history
0a1eQ20.description: A patient's health status prior to their current presentation. Includes previous major illnesses, surgeries, hospitalization, medications, and allergies.

aa1QQ20.title: International Society of Thrombosis and Haemostasis DIC score
aa1QQ20.description: A score that assesses different laboratory parameters (platelet count, D-dimer, prothrombin time, fibrinogen) to grade the severity of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Designed for use only in patients with an underlying disorder associated with DIC (e.g., sepsis, malignancy, trauma).

media.title: ISTH score for disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)

Ua1bP20.title: Sickle cell chronic lung disease
Ua1bP20.description: A complication of sickle cell anemia that manifests with interstitial abnormalities on chest x-ray, impaired pulmonary function (i.e., restrictive or obstructive lung disease, hypoxemia, and abnormal diffusion capacity), and, in severe cases, pulmonary hypertension.

3a1S420.title: Sexual history
3a1S420.description: Includes details on current and past sexual partners, sexual practices, contraception use, history of sexually transmitted infection, relationship status, and other factors affecting health, such as intimate partner violence.

destinations.label: OB/GYN: history and physical examination → Gynecologic and obstetric history

la1vk20.title: Thrombomodulin
la1vk20.description: An integral membrane protein on endothelial cells involved in hemostasis. Thrombomodulin binds thrombin, thereby reducing thrombin's activation of procoagulant clotting factors and enhancing its activation of the anticoagulant protein C.

Na1-k20.title: Patient-physician discordance
Na1-k20.description: A difference between the patient and physician's understanding of health-related information (e.g., patient's symptoms, disease prognosis, drug regimen). Can lead to negative heath care outcomes.

ma1VO20.title: Visual medication schedule
ma1VO20.description: A communication tool that uses digitized color pictures (e.g., images of tablets, syringes) to instruct patients on their medication schedule. Used to improve understanding of the medication regimen and medical adherence in patients with low literacy levels.

5a1iO20.title: NAD
5a1iO20.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to: 
1. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide 
2. No acute/apparent distress
3. No abnormality detected; Nothing abnormal detected/discovered

Ma1MO20.title: Intermittent pneumatic compression devices
Ma1MO20.description: A type of wearable medical device used to prevent deep venous thromboses. Exerts compressive pressure to facilitate venous return.

na17O20.title: POD
na17O20.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Postoperative day
2. Pouch of Douglas

Ja1sl20.title: Superior recess of the lesser sac
Ja1sl20.description: A recess in the right side of the cranial part of the omental bursa (lesser sac). Bounded by the caudate lobe of the liver, coronary ligament, diaphragm, and gastrohepatic ligament.

qa1Cl20.title: Inferior recess of the lesser sac
qa1Cl20.description: A recess in the caudal part of the omental bursa (lesser sac). Bounded by the gastrocolic ligament, posterior surface of the stomach, transverse colon, transverse mesocolon, and anterior surface of the pancreas.

Ia1YN20.title: Maze procedure
Ia1YN20.description: A surgical procedure that is performed to ablate atrial fibrillation and restore sinus rhythm. A series of incisions are made in the atrial endocardium to block rogue action potentials. The procedure can be performed surgically (COX III procedure) or via a catheter (COX IV procedure).

ra1fN20.title: GTPAL
ra1fN20.description: An abbreviation used to describe components of parity. Includes Gravidity (i.e., number of pregnancies), Term births (i.e., number of pregnancies carried to ≥ 37 weeks), Preterm births (i.e., number of births between 20-37 weeks of gestation), Abortions/Miscarriages, and Living children.

destinations.label: Obstetrics and gynecology clerkship → Clinical tasks

7a14N20.title: Integumentary system
7a14N20.description: An organ system that consists of the skin, hair, nails, and associated glands.

Ha1KN20.title: Cobicistat
Ha1KN20.description: A CYP3A4 inhibitor used for pharmacokinetic enhancement of antiretroviral therapy for HIV infection. Decreases the breakdown of certain antiretroviral, including darunavir and atazanavir.

destinations.label: Fundamentals of pharmacology → Drug interactions and the cytochrome P450 system

sa1tN20.title: Protection quantity
sa1tN20.description: The maximum amount of ionizing radiation to the whole body or part of the body that has been determined to not cause acute damage and/or long-term health effects.

Ga1BN20.title: Dosimetry
Ga1BN20.description: The measurement of doses of radiation (e.g., the amounts of ionizing radiation absorbed by tissue). Typically expressed in units of gray (Gy).

ta1Xm20.title: Irradiation
ta1Xm20.description: A process by which the body is exposed to high-energy radiation (e.g., x-rays, gamma rays, neutrons, protons). Controlled doses of radiation can be used to treat cancer.

Fa1gm20.title: Plateau iris configuration
Fa1gm20.description: An anatomical variant of the iris in which it is abnormally inserted in a more anterior position onto the ciliary body and lies on a horizontal plane (compared to its normal slightly convex plane). This configuration crowds the trabecular meshwork and obstructs aqueous humor outflow, resulting in angle-closure glaucoma. It is the most common cause of angle-closure glaucoma in individuals < 50 years of age.

ua1pm20.title: Threshold dose
ua1pm20.description: A dose of radiation below which there is no effect on the target tissue's response.

va1Am20.title: Masked hypertension
va1Am20.description: A subtype of hypertension in which blood pressure readings are normal when measured in a clinical setting but are consistently elevated when measured outside of a clinical setting.

xa1E520.title: Pulsed wave Doppler
xa1E520.description: An ultrasonographic technique that measures the velocity of blood flow. Often used to measure velocity from the left ventricular outflow tract in order to assess cardiac function.

Ba1z520.title: Continuous wave Doppler
Ba1z520.description: An ultrasonographic technique that simultaneously transmits and receives sound waves from distinct sources. Allows for high-velocity flow to be measured but is not able to localize where velocity flow originates (i.e., spatial distribution of the reflecting structures is not possible).

media.title: Continuous wave (CW) Doppler in aortic valvular stenosis

Aa1RM20.title: Abdominal aortic plexus
Aa1RM20.description: A sympathetic nerve plexus that is located on the anterior surface of the abdominal aorta between the origins of the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries. Derived from the fibers of the celiac ganglia and lumbar sympathetic trunk. Gives rises to parts of the inferior mesenteric nerve plexus and superior hypogastric nerve plexus.

_a15M20.title: S-adenosyl methionine synthase
_a15M20.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of methionine and ATP to S-adenosylmethionine. Deficiency of this enzyme causes hypermethioninemia.

destinations.label: Amino acids →  Catabolism of the carbon skeleton of amino acids

za1rM20.title: Dorsal nerve of the penis
za1rM20.description: A branch of the pudendal nerve that lies on the dorsal surface of the penis lateral to the dorsal artery of the penis. Provides somatosensory innervation to the skin and glans of the penis.

ZY1Zn20.title: Post-ERCP pancreatitis
ZY1Zn20.description: Acute pancreatic inflammation triggered by ERCP.

bY1Hn20.title: Cerebrospinal fluid erythrocytosis
bY1Hn20.description: The presence of erythrocytes in cerebrospinal fluid, which can be caused by traumatic lumbar puncture, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and, rarely, hemorrhagic encephalitis (e.g., HSV encephalitis, primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, acute hemorrhagic encephalomyelitis)

XY19n20.title: Hypoglycorrhachia
XY19n20.description: A decreased concentration of glucose in cerebrospinal fluid (i.e., < 40 mg/dL or a cerebrospinal fluid:serum glucose ratio < 0.6). Etiologies include bacterial, fungal, and amebic meningitis/encephalitis and certain CNS malignancies (e.g., carcinomatous meningitis).

1Y12L20.title: Bradford Hill criteria
1Y12L20.description: A set of nine criteria that help to establish causality in epidemiological studies. The list includes strength, dose-response relationship, temporality, reproducibility, specificity, plausibility, coherence, experiment, and analogy.

WY1PL20.title: Kerandel sign
WY1PL20.description: A delayed but increased pain response that is disproportionate to an applied stimulus (i.e., hyperesthetic) in a bony prominence or soft tissue. Associated with the neurologic phase of African trypanosomiasis. Caused by damage to the dorsal root ganglia.

dY1oL20.title: Iridotrabecular contact
dY1oL20.description: Contact between the anterior surface of the iris and the trabecular meshwork or other structures within the iridocorneal angle.

VY1GL20.title: RIETE
VY1GL20.description: A scoring system used to predict the risk of bleeding within the first 3 months of anticoagulation in patients with venous thromboembolism. Parameters include recent major bleeding (2 points); abnormal renal function or anemia (1.5 points each); age > 75 years (1 point); evidence of PE (1 point); and cancer (1 point). The risk of bleeding is classified as low (score 0), intermediate (score 1-4), or high (score > 4).

eY1xL20.title: Borborygmus
eY1xL20.description: A gurgling or rumbling sound of the abdomen that is caused by the movement of gas through the bowels.

UY1bo20.title: Emicizumab
UY1bo20.description: A humanized monoclonal antibody used to treat hemophilia A. It bridges activated factor IX and factor X and, therefore, restores the function of factor VIII, which is deficient in patients with hemophilia.

2Y1To20.title: Anterolisthesis
2Y1To20.description: A condition in which a vertebral body slips anteriorly to an adjacent, inferior vertebral body.

fY1ko20.title: Mecasermin
fY1ko20.description: A recombinant insulin-like growth factor (IGF-1) that is used to treat patients with primary severe IGF-1 deficiency who manifest with growth failure.

TY16o20.title: Tagged white blood cell scan
TY16o20.description: A nuclear medicine study that involves tagging a patient's white blood cells with a radioactive isotope and reinjecting them intravenously. Can be used to localize regions of inflammation (e.g., due to prosthetic joint infections, osteomyelitis, vascular graft infections).

gY1Fo20.title: Darrow-Yannet diagram
gY1Fo20.description: A diagram used to illustrate extracellular volume, intracellular volume, and osmolality and identify how these parameters change as a result of different clinical conditions (e.g., adrenal insufficiency, SIADH).

SY1yo20.title: Plugged milk duct
SY1yo20.description: An obstruction of the mammary duct by milk stasis, which can result in distention of mammary tissue and the formation of a tender, nonerythematous palpable lump without associated systemic symptoms (e.g., fever, myalgia, or chills).

hY1cK20.title: Moderator band
hY1cK20.description: A muscular structure located in the right ventricle that extends from the base of the anterior papillary muscle to the ventricular septum. Acts as part of the electrical conduction pathway.

3Y1SK20.title: Neurofeedback
3Y1SK20.description: A type of psychotherapy that uses a computer-based program to assess brain activity patterns, then subsequently uses sound and visual signals to assist in retraining brain activity. Used to treat many conditions, such as migraines, bladder dysfunction, and posttraumatic stress disorder.

RY1lK20.title: PFAPA syndrome
RY1lK20.description: A childhood syndrome characterized by recurrent febrile episodes associated with aphthous stomatitis, pharyngitis, and adenitis. These episodes typically last for 3-6 days at regular intervals of 2-8 weeks. Typically self-limited.

iY1JK20.title: Cystitis glandularis
iY1JK20.description: A benign proliferative disorder of the bladder characterized by proliferation of mucus-secreting glands in the epithelium of the bladder.

jY1_K20.title: Stria terminalis
jY1_K20.description: A fascicle of nerve fibers that run along the lateral wall of the thalamus. Connects the amygdala to the hypothalamus. Involved in emotional and behavioral responses.

PY1W620.title: Urostomy
PY1W620.description: A surgical procedure in which an opening in the abdominal wall is made for urine to empty via a conduit or pouch created from a bowel segment. Generally performed when the bladder is not functioning or has to be removed (e.g., due to spinal cord injury, bladder cancer, or spina bifida).

lY1v620.title: 5-methyltetrahydrofolate
lY1v620.description: A methylated derivate of tetrahydrofolic acid. Formed from 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate by methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase. Used as a methyl donor by the enzyme methionine transferase to generate methionine from homocysteine.

NY1-620.title: 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate
NY1-620.description: A derivative of tetrahydrofolic acid, in which a methylene bridge (-CH₂-) is present between the N5 and N10 nitrogen atoms. Generated from tetrahydrofolate and serine by serine hydroxymethyltransferase. Converted to dihydrofolate when used as a cofactor for the conversion of dUMP to dTMP by thymidylate synthase. Converted to 5-methyltetrahydrofolate by methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase.

mY1Vp20.title: Postburn hypermetabolism
mY1Vp20.description: A metabolic phenomenon that can be seen in patients with moderate to severe burn injuries. Characterized by an initial hypometabolic phase that occurs within 48 hours after injury and a subsequent hypermetabolic state with insulin resistance that develops 5-7 days after injury and can last up to ~ 3 years.

MY1Mp20.title: One-Minute Telegram 2-2020-1/3
MY1Mp20.description: In the wake of COVID-19, many hospitals have braced themselves for the tough ethical choices arising when demand exceeds the resources available. In March 2020, the Association of Bioethics Program Directors (ABPD) conducted a voluntary survey among its 91 members in 79 US and Canadian academic medical centers to assess the selection criteria and scoring systems in place to triage patients needing ventilation. [...]

nY17p20.title: One-Minute Telegram 2-2020-2/3
nY17p20.description: Current guidelines recommend pausing metformin for 1–2 days before major surgery because of the risk of lactic acidosis. But what do we know about the benefits of its long-term use before major surgery? [...]

LY1wp20.title: One-Minute Telegram 2-2020-3/3
LY1wp20.description: Many hospitals are struggling with insufficient space and resources to treat patients with COVID-19. Early identification of patients that will progress to critical illness would enable a more adequate and efficient distribution of medical resources. [...]

6Y1jJ20.title: SOAP note
6Y1jJ20.description: An acronym for "Subjective data, Objective data, Assessment, Plan," which is an organizational format used for medical documentation (e.g., for daily inpatient progress notes) and presentations.

destinations.label: Daily life of the intern → Daily progress notes

pY1LJ20.title: WNT4 gene
pY1LJ20.description: A gene that influences the sex determination cascade of embryonic development. Considered essential for the development of female internal genitalia (e.g., ovarian differentiation). Mutations in this gene are associated with the development of streak gonads and Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome.

destinations.label: Development of the reproductive system → Gonadal sex differentiation

GY1Bq20.title: Vocal apparatus
GY1Bq20.description: The collection of structures that are involved in the formation of speech. Includes the respiratory organs that produce the necessary stream of air (e.g., lungs, bronchi, and trachea) for speech, mobile speech structures (e.g., larynx, pharynx, tongue, lips), and fixed speech structures (e.g., teeth, nasal cavity).

tY1XI20.title: Anterior communicating artery
tY1XI20.description: An artery that supplies the anterior columns of the fornix, cingulate gyrus, hypothalamus, lamina terminalis, optic chiasm, and para-olfactory area. Its branches include the median artery of the corpus callosum and subcallosal artery.

FY1gI20.title: Thought process
FY1gI20.description: The way an individual organizes and connects ideas and associations. Normally, thought process is logical and coherent and thus easy to follow for other people. Disturbances will lead to incoherent, illogical, or even incomprehensible thought process.

8Y1OI20.title: Thought content
8Y1OI20.description: What an individual is thinking about, i.e, main themes and beliefs. Disturbances of thought content include delusions, obsessions and compulsions, phobias, anxieties, and suicidal or homicidal ideation.

uY1pI20.title: Pseudothrombocytopenia
uY1pI20.description: A spuriously low platelet count seen in laboratory studies that occurs due to platelet clumping in vitro. Automatic counters mistake platelet clumps for individual platelets or white blood cells. Clumping can occur secondary to sampling- (e.g., technique, anticoagulant used in collection tubes) or disease-related factors (e.g., antibodies to EDTA anticoagulant, viral infections, malignancy).

EY18I20.title: Fund of knowledge
EY18I20.description: The amount of information that an individual has stored in their memory about current events, history, places, people, and things. Fund of knowledge increases with education and decreases in a number of conditions (e.g., dementia).

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

vY1AI20.title: Hepatocyte canalicular membrane
vY1AI20.description: The membrane of hepatocytes that faces the bile canaliculi. Has microvilli and transporters for the active secretion of substances such as bile salts, conjugated bilirubin, phospholipids, and certain drugs.

DY11r20.title: Wisconsin Card Sorting Test
DY11r20.description: A neuropsychologic test that is used to assess cognitive executive function. The examiner presents stimulus cards with three different criteria: color, symbol, and number. The patient is instructed to match cards they draw from a deck to those stimulus cards according to an underlying rule that they must deduce based on being told if their match was correct or incorrect. After 10 cards, the rule changes.

wY1hr20.title: Isomers
wY1hr20.description: A set of molecules that have the same chemical formula (i.e., number of each type of atom) but distinct chemical structures (i.e., molecular arrangement of atoms). Further subdivided into structural isomers (which have different connectivity of atoms) and spatial isomers (which have the same connectivity but different three-dimensional orientation).

9Y1Nr20.title: Z-lumirubin
9Y1Nr20.description: A water-soluble structural isomer of unconjugated bilirubin (4Z,15Z-bilirubin). Formed by an irreversible photoisomerization reaction. Can be excreted in bile and urine without being conjugated

CY1qr20.title: 4Z,15E-bilirubin
CY1qr20.description: A water-soluble spatial isomer of unconjugated bilirubin. Formed by a reversible photoisomerization reaction. Can be excreted in bile without being conjugated.

yY1d720.title: Noncardiogenic pulmonary edema
yY1d720.description: A form of pulmonary edema caused by increased permeability of the pulmonary capillaries. Fluid is characteristically rich in protein. Causes include pneumonia, blood transfusion-related acute lung injury, and preeclampsia.

media.title: Noncardiogenic edema and acute lung injury

AY1R720.title: Alexander's law
AY1R720.description: Increased intensity of nystagmus when the gaze is directed toward its fast component and decrease when the gaze is directed in the opposite direction. Typically seen in acute unilateral vestibular lesions.

_Y15720.title: Mesorectum
_Y15720.description: The adipose tissue and connective tissue that surrounds the rectum. Contains vasculature and lymph nodes.

Zb1ZH20.title: Topical corticosteroids (TCS)
Zb1ZH20.description: An anti-inflammatory agent frequently used in the management of dermatological conditions such as atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, and vitiligo. Potencies range from low (e.g., hydrocortisone 1-2.5%) to medium (e.g., triamcinolone 0.1%), high (e.g., fluocinonide 0.05%), and ultra high (e.g., clobetasol 0.05%). Forms include lotions, ointments, creams, and gels.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Overview of treatment

0b1eH20.title: Standard operating procedure
0b1eH20.description: A detailed, written, step-by-step set of instructions that organizations (e.g., hospitals) compile to facilitate and standardize the execution of certain tasks and procedures.

Yb1nH20.title: Scrubbing in
Yb1nH20.description: Refers to the thorough decontamination of hands and forearms with an antimicrobial solution to reduce the risk of surgical site infections. This routine is executed by involved medical personal (e.g., surgeons, nurses, surgical technologists) before every operative procedure. It is usually followed by donning a sterile gown and gloves.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Pre-surgical infection prevention measures

bb1HH20.title: Effect size
bb1HH20.description: A quantitative measure of the strength of association between two correlated variables. Examples include correlation coefficients, mean differences (e.g., t-test and ANOVA), odds ratio, relative risk, and absolute risk reduction. Large effect sizes can be measured with small sample sizes, lend the study a high degree of statistical power, and support causality.

Xb19H20.title: Clinical clerkship
Xb19H20.description: A mandatory clinical course of US medical schools; includes internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, neurology, psychiatry, usually family medicine, and sometimes ambulatory care. Classically they occur in 3rd year, although some curriculums also have clerkships in 2nd or 4th year. During a clerkship, students are part of a medical team with assigned patients and learn clinical skills under supervision of physicians.

cb1as20.title: Pre-rounding
cb1as20.description: The process of gathering information (e.g., interval events, subjective information, laboratory results, imaging results) on hospitalized patients before formal rounding. Typically includes a targeted interval history and directed physical examination.

Wb1Ps20.title: Lethargy
Wb1Ps20.description: A state of impaired consciousness and drowsiness from which the patient can be awoken if exposed to moderate external stimuli. Less severe than stupor and coma.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

db1os20.title: Obtundation
db1os20.description: A state of impaired consciousness characterized by low response to external stimuli, a decreased interest in the surrounding environment, increased sleepiness, and drowsiness between the sleeping episodes.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

eb1xs20.title: Flash pulmonary edema
eb1xs20.description: A type of sudden-onset cardiogenic pulmonary edema triggered by an acute physiological stressor (e.g., ischemia, drugs, acute valvular dysfunction, tachyarrhythmia). Most commonly occurs in patients with hypertension and in such cases is considered a type of hypertensive emergency. The resulting sympathetic activation increases afterload and preload, thereby creating a vicious cycle of worsening forward flow and pulmonary edema.

Ub1bG20.title: Ashman phenomenon
Ub1bG20.description: The appearance of a wide QRS complex on an ECG due to a physiologic, aberrantly conducted supraventricular beat in a patient with otherwise narrow QRS complexes. Seen in supraventricular tachyarrhythmias, especially atrial fibrillation. While Ashman phenomenon has a similar morphological appearance to a premature ventricular complex, the mechanism is different.

hb1ct20.title: Mood incongruence
hb1ct20.description: An inconsistency between a person's mood (i.e., their emotional state) and their situational context (e.g., their state of health, degree of stressors).

3b1St20.title: Titer
3b1St20.description: A measure of concentration that represents the lowest dilution of a substance that can be detected by a specific assay. Typically expressed in a ratio (e.g., 1:320, which indicates that a substance is still detectable when the original sample is diluted by a factor of 320).

lb1vF20.title: SNS
lb1vF20.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Sympathetic nervous system
2. Somatic nervous system
3. Specialized nutrition support

Nb1-F20.title: Leukonychia
Nb1-F20.description: A whitish discoloration of the nail, which can be caused by pathology of the nail plate (true leukonychia), pathology of the nail bed (apparent leukonychia), or exogenous substances on the nail plate (pseudoleukonychia).

mb1V820.title: Paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity
mb1V820.description: A complication of acute brain injury characterized by recurrent episodes of excessive sympathetic activity (e.g., fever, tachycardia, hypertension, tachypnea).

destinations.label: Traumatic brain injury → Paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity (PSH)

5b1i820.title: Rapid shallow breathing index
5b1i820.description: An index of the ratio of respiratory frequency to tidal volume (f/VT). Commonly used as an indicator for when to wean ventilation settings. A RSBI of ≥ 105 breaths/min/L has a high predictive value for weaning failure.

ob10u20.title: Pregnancy of unknown location
ob10u20.description: A positive pregnancy test in an individual without sonographic evidence of an intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy. Causes include early viable intrauterine pregnancy, nonvisualized ectopic pregnancy, and pregnancy loss.

Kb1Uu20.title: Hymenolepis nana
Kb1Uu20.description: A tapeworm contracted by ingestion of contaminated food or water. It is the most common cause of human tapeworm infection. Ingestion of eggs and/or cysticercoids can cause hymenolepiasis.

Jb1su20.title: Uncomplicated ectopic pregnancy
Jb1su20.description: An ectopic pregnancy without any features of complicated ectopic pregnancy (e.g., severe bleeding, tubal rupture).

qb1Cu20.title: Complicated ectopic pregnancy
qb1Cu20.description: An ectopic pregnancy associated with severe bleeding (e.g., hemoperitoneum, vaginal bleeding), rupture (e.g., tubal rupture), and/or hemodynamic compromise.

7b14E20.title: Malathion
7b14E20.description: An irreversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that is commonly used as an insecticide. In low doses, it can be used to treat scabies, head lice, and body lice.

Hb1KE20.title: American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status classification system
Hb1KE20.description:
A classification system used to assess patient fitness before undergoing an interventional procedure. 
ASA I: normal health. ASA II: well-controlled mild-moderate systemic illness. ASA III: severe disease that is not incapacitating. ASA IV: severe, incapacitating disease that is a constant threat to life. ASA V: moribund patient; not expected to survive without intervention. ASA VI: organ donor with irreversible loss of brain function.

sb1tE20.title: Benzocaine
sb1tE20.description: A short-acting ester used as a local anesthetic agent. Reversibly blocks sodium channels of nerve fibers, thereby inhibiting the conduction of nerve impulses.

Eb18v20.title: Hymenolepiasis
Eb18v20.description: An infection caused by Hymenolepis nana (dwarf tapeworm). Most infections are asymptomatic; heavy tapeworm burden can result in anorexia, abdominal pain, and diarrhea.

vb1Av20.title: Primary heart field
vb1Av20.description: An embryonic structure of mesodermal origin that gives rise to the left and right atria and the left ventricle.

Db11D20.title: Secondary heart field
Db11D20.description: An embryonic structure of mesodermal origin that gives rise to the right ventricle and outflow tract.

wb1hD20.title: Rectus sheath hematoma
wb1hD20.description: An accumulation of blood within the rectus sheath that most commonly arises from the disruption of a branch of the inferior epigastric artery. Manifestations include acute onset abdominal pain with a palpable abdominal mass.

9b1ND20.title: Lisfranc fracture
9b1ND20.description: A tarsometatarsal fracture that can involve damage to the cartilage of the midfoot joints. Typically manifests with tenderness at the dorsal aspect of the midfoot and bruising at either surface of the midfoot.

destinations.label: General principles of fractures → Overview of common fractures

Cb1qD20.title: Pulse-temperature dissociation
Cb1qD20.description: The presence of both fever and bradycardia. Can be caused by many infectious diseases, including yellow fever, typhoid fever, dengue fever, ebola virus disease, brucellosis, tularemia, and Legionella infection.

xb1ED20.title: Gangrenous cholecystitis
xb1ED20.description: A complication of acute cholecystitis characterized by ischemic necrosis of the gallbladder. It is the most common complication of acute cholecystitis.

Bb1zD20.title: Gallbladder perforation
Bb1zD20.description: A complication of acute cholecystitis characterized by full-thickness injury of the gallbladder wall, which can result in leakage of gallbladder contents into the abdominal cavity.

yb1dw20.title: Orificial tuberculosis
yb1dw20.description: A rare form of mucocutaneous tuberculosis that occurs in patients with advanced tuberculosis of the lung, gastrointestinal tract, and/or genitourinary tract. Caused by infiltration of Myobacterium tuberculosis into the skin or mucosa from excretions (e.g., sputum, feces, urine). Manifests in the oral and/or anogenital region as a red-yellow nodule that breaks down to a punched out ulcer.

Ab1Rw20.title: Miliary cutaneous tuberculosis
Ab1Rw20.description: A form of cutaneous tuberculosis that develops acutely in patients who are immunocompromised as a result of hematogenous spread of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to the skin. Manifests with numerous red, umbilicated papules. Lesions typically heal after a few weeks with residual hypopigmentation and/or scarring.

_b15w20.title: Metastatic tuberculous abscess
_b15w20.description: A form of tuberculosis that can develop in patients who are immunocompromised as a result of hematogenous spread of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to the subcutaneous tissue. Typically manifests as one or more non-tender, subcutaneous nodules that then ulcerate and/or drain to the overlying skin via sinus tracts.

zb1rw20.title: Emergency medical condition
zb1rw20.description: A medical condition that manifests with acute, life-threatening symptoms and/or high risk of impairment of an organ or body part.

-b1Dw20.title: Cholecystoenteric fistula
-b1Dw20.description: An abnormal communication between the lumen of the gallbladder (cholecystoenteric) or common bile duct (choledochoenteric) and the lumen of the bowel (usually stomach or duodenum) that can lead to large gallstones entering the bowel, resulting in gallstone ileus.

0X1e920.title: Room air entrainment
0X1e920.description: The admixture of room air with delivered oxygen during oxygen therapy. This process is due to a negative pressure gradient generated by either the patient's inspiratory force or the delivery device itself (e.g., Venturi systems). The result is the delivery of a lower FiO₂ than that of the oxygen source.

destinations.label: Oxygen therapy → General principles of oxygen delivery

YX1n920.title: Iliopsoas muscle
YX1n920.description: A posterior abdominal wall muscle that originates from the fusion of iliacus and psoas major muscles and inserts onto the lesser trochanter. Innervated by the femoral nerve and supplied by the iliolumbar artery and medial femoral circumflex artery. Flexes the hip and trunk and externally rotates the hip.

bX1H920.title: Nebulizer
bX1H920.description: A device that aerosolizes a liquid medication (or a solution) into a fine spray or mist for inhalation into the lungs.

destinations.label: Oxygen therapy → Basic oxygen delivery systems

media.title: Nebulizer mask attached to air compressor

cX1aC20.title: EPS
cX1aC20.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Electrophysiology study
2. Extrapyramidal syndrome
3. Extracellular polymeric substance
4. Encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis

1X12C20.title: PRN
1X12C20.description: An abbreviation for the latin phrase "pro re nata," which means "as needed." Used to describe parameters for taking medications (e.g., PRN for pain).

WX1PC20.title: Biliary stricture
WX1PC20.description: A narrowing of the bile duct that can obstruct bile flow. Etiologies include malignancy, postsurgical change, and chronic inflammation (e.g., from chronic pancreatitis or primary sclerosing cholangitis).

dX1oC20.title: Cold-induced diuresis
dX1oC20.description: A phenomenon characterized by diuresis in the early phase of hypothermia. Caused by fluid shifts to the core (as a result of peripheral vasoconstriction), which are sensed by central volume receptors and result in decreased serum antidiuretic hormone concentrations.

eX1xC20.title: Pseudomosaicism
eX1xC20.description: A finding of an abnormal cell line in one cell culture flask from amniocentesis. Can be caused by sporadic chromosome mutation.

UX1bx20.title: Paraproteinemic neuropathy
UX1bx20.description: A group of neuropathies characterized by the presence of excess homogeneous immunoglobulins produced by the abnormal clonal proliferation of B lymphocytes or plasma cells. Manifestations include paresthesias, gait ataxia, and dysesthesia.

2X1Tx20.title: Prune belly syndrome
2X1Tx20.description: A rare congenital syndrome characterized by partial absence of the abdominal wall muscles (which results in a prune-like or wrinkled appearance), bilateral cryptorchidism, and urinary tract malformations (e.g., obstruction at the bladder neck). As a result, bladder distension occurs with an increased risk of hydronephrosis and renal failure. Other complications include underdevelopment of the lungs.

gX1Fx20.title: Electrodesiccation
gX1Fx20.description: A dermatologic procedure that uses heat to remove benign lesions (e.g., seborrheic keratosis and sebaceous hyperplasia) on the skin.

hX1cB20.title: Insular ribbon sign
hX1cB20.description: A loss of definition of the gray-white interface along the lateral margins of the insula seen on CT imaging. It is an early indicator of ischemic stroke along the middle cerebral artery. This part of the insula is supplied by the insular segment of the middle cerebral artery and is susceptible to ischemia due to a lack of collateral supply.

RX1lB20.title: Enterolithotomy
RX1lB20.description: The surgical removal of a gallstone from the bowel (i.e., enterotomy and stone removal) in patients with gallstone ileus. Can be performed via open surgery or laparoscopically.

iX1JB20.title: Cozen test
iX1JB20.description: A test for the diagnosis of lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow). The examiner holds the patient's hand with the thumb placed over the lateral epicondyle. The patient makes a fist, pronates the forearm, deviates radially, and extends the fist against the examiner's resistance. Pain over the lateral epicondyle indicates a positive test.

destinations.label: Orthopedic examination → Arm and hand examination

QX1uB20.title: Rounding
QX1uB20.description: During rounds, clinicians present information about patients to the whole team (i.e., attending, residents, nurses, students, etc.), which allows for discussions with all who are involved in the patients' care. Additionally, rounding offers a great learning opportunity as participants observe colleagues' presentations, see different approaches to patient interactions and management, and discuss questions with the attending.

4X13y20.title: Pseudoglandular period of lung development
4X13y20.description: The second stage of lung development, in which bronchioles and terminal bronchioles are formed from the endodermal tubules during gestational weeks 5-17. Lung capillaries and type II pneumocytes develop in this period. Errors in this stage can lead to the formation of bronchogenic cysts.

kX1my20.title: Canalicular period of lung development
kX1my20.description: The third stage of lung development, in which respiratory bronchioles and primitive alveoli are formed during gestational weeks 16-25. Surfactant production also begins during this stage (gestational weeks 20-22). Errors in this stage can lead to pulmonary hypoplasia or respiratory distress syndrome.

OX1Iy20.title: Saccular period of lung development
OX1Iy20.description: The fourth stage of lung development, in which alveolar ducts and thin-walled alveoli separated by primary septa are formed from gestational week 26 until birth.

mX1VA20.title: Secondary septa of alveoli
mX1VA20.description: The septa between definitive alveoli. Arise from the walls of terminal sacs as protrusions during the alveolar stage of lung development (36 weeks of gestational age to several years after birth).

LX1wA20.title: Cell-free fetal DNA
LX1wA20.description: A type of DNA of fetal origin (derived from syncytiotrophoblasts) that circulates in maternal blood. Circulating amounts of cffDNA can be compared to concentrations of cell-free maternal DNA to screen for genetic disorders. Serum concentrations of cffDNA decrease rapidly following delivery.

6X1j_20.title: Clinical decision support system
6X1j_20.description: A computer-based system designed to analyze data within electronic health records to assist health care professionals in clinical decision-making tasks (e.g., by reporting drug-drug interactions).

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medical errors

pX1L_20.title: RRR
pX1L_20.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Regular rate and rhythm
2. Relative risk reduction

vX1A-20.title: Closed glove method
vX1A-20.description: A method of donning sterile surgical gloves with the hands completely covered by the surgical gown.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Pre-surgical infection prevention measures

DX11Zf0.title: Open glove method
DX11Zf0.description: A method of donning sterile surgical gloves in which the individual's hands are not covered by the surgical gown, but instead extend beyond the gown cuffs.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Pre-surgical infection prevention measures

wX1hZf0.title: T-tube drain
wX1hZf0.description: A T-shaped drain used to provide external biliary drainage (e.g., to treat bile duct injury), decompress the biliary tree (e.g., to treat acute cholangitis), and rarely, to extract common bile duct stones. The short arms of the T-tube are placed within the common bile duct; the long arm is brought out percutaneously through the abdominal wall.

9X1NZf0.title: Noradrenergic pheochromocytoma
9X1NZf0.description: A pheochromocytoma with decreased expression of the enzyme phenylethanolamine-N-methyltransferase, which converts epinephrine to norepinephrine. Characteristic of extramedullary pheochromocytomas and pheochromocytomas that occur in association with von Hippel-Lindau disease. Less symptomatic than adrenergic pheochromocytomas.

CX1qZf0.title: Cerebral peduncles
CX1qZf0.description: A pair of structures that arise at the lateral ventral aspect of the pons and are separated by the interpeduncular cistern. They connect the brainstem to the thalami and contain the major white matter tracts (e.g., corticobulbar tract, corticospinal tract).

AX1R0f0.title: L&D
AX1R0f0.description: An abbreviation for "Labor & Delivery" (i.e., obstetric care units in North American hospitals).

_X150f0.title: Contraception
_X150f0.description: A method intended to prevent pregnancy. Examples include hormonal contraception (e.g., oral contraceptives, vaginal rings) and nonhormonal contraception (e.g., abstinence, copper intrauterine devices).

zX1r0f0.title: Zygote intrafallopian transfer
zX1r0f0.description: An assisted reproductive technology in which the fertilized embryo is transferred laparoscopically into the fallopian tube.

-X1D0f0.title: Tubal ligation
-X1D0f0.description: A surgical procedure in which both fallopian tubes are permanently blocked or severed to prevent pregnancy.

Zc1Zaf0.title: Nuchal cord
Zc1Zaf0.description: An obstetric complication of childbirth in which the umbilical cord becomes wrapped 360 degrees around the fetal neck. Can result in severe obstruction of blood flow in the fetal umbilical vein with consequent cardiorespiratory distress and neurological impairment.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Umbilical cord complications

0c1eaf0.title: Aedes aegypti
0c1eaf0.description: A vector of transmission of several viruses, including the yellow fever virus, dengue virus, chikungunya virus, and Zika virus. Commonly found in tropical regions of Africa, and subtropical regions in the Middle East, Southeast Asia, southeastern United States, Northern Australia, and Pacific and Indian islands.

ac1Qaf0.title: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis type 2
ac1Qaf0.description: A rare form of membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis characterized by the presence of electron-dense deposits in the glomerular basement membrane. Caused by anomalous regulation of the alternative complement pathway.

Yc1naf0.title: Comprehensive metabolic panel
Yc1naf0.description: A laboratory test that typically measures several components of the serum, including the concentrations of sodium, potassium, bicarbonate, chloride, creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, glucose, calcium, total protein, albumin, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin.

bc1Haf0.title: Primary septa of alveoli
bc1Haf0.description: The septa between terminal sacs. Formed when terminal sacs arise from the alveolar ducts during the saccular period of lung development (26 weeks of gestational age to birth).

cc1aYf0.title: Neuroprotective measures
cc1aYf0.description: A set of measures to prevent and/or minimize secondary brain injury in the immediate management of patients who have sustained a traumatic brain injury or stroke. Includes maintenance of normoxia, normocapnia, normotension, normothermia (or, in some cases controlled hypothermia), and euglycemia.

destinations.label: Secondary brain injury and neuroprotective measures → Definitions

1c12Yf0.title: Median effective dose
1c12Yf0.description: The dose of a drug required to produce 50% of the maximum possible response. The same drug may have different ED50 values based on the indication (e.g., aspirin has different ED50 values for headache and for coronary artery disease).

Wc1PYf0.title: Peripheral sensitization
Wc1PYf0.description: A state of increased neuronal sensitivity and/or reduced neuronal threshold of peripheral nociceptive neurons that occurs in response to injury, inflammation, and/or repetitive stimulation. Results in abnormal pain perception (e.g., hyperalgesia, allodynia) and usually ceases once the tissue injury or inflammation heals.

dc1oYf0.title: Central sensitization
dc1oYf0.description: A state of increased neuronal excitability and/or reduced inhibition in the central nervous system and recruitment of nonnociceptive fibers (e.g., Aβ fibers) into the nociceptive pathway due to injury, inflammation, and/or repetitive stimulation. Results in abnormal pain perception (e.g., hyperalgesia, allodynia) and continues even after the initial injury has healed.

Tc16bf0.title: Child sexual abuse
Tc16bf0.description: The involvement of a child in sexual activity with an adult or other child that involves any of the following: a lack of proper understanding and inability to provide informed consent, a lack of developmental readiness and/or inability to provide consent, or the involvement is illegal or socially unacceptable.

gc1Fbf0.title: Small blue round cell tumor
gc1Fbf0.description: A histopathologic descriptor for a tumor that has clusters of uniform, undifferentiated small cells that stain blue as a result of scant cytoplasm and relatively large nuclei. Examples of SBRCTs include certain non-Hodgkin lymphomas (e.g., anaplastic large cell lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma), small cell lung carcinoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, and primitive neuroectodermal tumors (e.g., neuroblastoma, medulloblastoma).

Sc1ybf0.title: RUNX1 gene
Sc1ybf0.description: A gene on the long arm of chromosome 21 that encodes for runt-related transcription factor 1 (Runt1 protein), which forms a part of a protein complex that activates genes involved in hematopoiesis.

hc1cXf0.title: Histone deacetylase inhibitors
hc1cXf0.description: A class of drugs that inhibits the enzyme histone deacetylase, which normally decreases gene transcription by deacetylating histones and tightening DNA coils. Examples include belinostat, panobinostat, romidepsin, and valproic acid.

3c1SXf0.title: Fasting insulin concentration
3c1SXf0.description: A marker used to identify peripheral insulin resistance. A fasting insulin concentration > 109 pmol/L indicates insulin resistance. This cutoff has a low sensitivity for detecting insulin resistance.

Rc1lXf0.title: Serum amyloid associated protein
Rc1lXf0.description: An acute phase reactant that is involved in cholesterol transport to the liver for bile excretion and modulates multiple immune responses. Can accumulate in tissues of patients with chronic inflammatory conditions (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease) and lead to reactive amyloidosis.

ic1JXf0.title: Double minutes
ic1JXf0.description: The fragments of chromosomal DNA that become rearranged as extrachromosomal circular DNA. Formed as a result of gene amplification, or chromothripsis (chromosomal shattering) and subsequent repair by nonhomologous end joining or microhomology-mediated break repair. Cancer cells frequently contain double minutes of oncogenes.

Qc1uXf0.title: Panitumumab
Qc1uXf0.description: A monoclonal antibody against the epidermal growth factor receptor. Used to treat colorectal cancer. Adverse effects include gastrointestinal upset, acneiform rash, ulcerative keratitis, and hypomagnesemia.

jc1_Xf0.title: Fetal presentation
jc1_Xf0.description: The part of the fetus that overlies the maternal pelvic inlet, i.e., the head (cephalic or vertex presentation) or buttocks/feet (breech presentation).

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Orientation in utero

Pc1Wcf0.title: Gene amplification
Pc1Wcf0.description: An increase in the number of copies of a gene sequence without a proportional increase in the number of copies of other gene sequences. Occurs in-vivo in cancer cells and during embryonic development (e.g., by extrareplication and recombination, breakage-fusion-bridge cycles). Leads to the formation of double minutes or homogeneous staining regions. Occurs in-vitro during a polymerase chain reaction.

4c13cf0.title: Fetal position
4c13cf0.description: An obstetric term that refers to the relationship and orientation of the presenting fetal part to the maternal pelvis (e.g., fetus facing the maternal symphysis pubis or sacrum; fetal occiput pointing left or right).

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Orientation in utero

kc1mcf0.title: Autoimmune lymphocytic oophoritis
kc1mcf0.description: An autoimmune-mediated disease characterized by inflammation and atrophy of the ovaries, which can result in primary ovarian insufficiency. Manifestations include irregular menses, dysmenorrhea, abdominal distension, and nausea. Associated with other autoimmune diseases (e.g., polyendocrine syndromes, diabetes mellitus).

Oc1Icf0.title: KIFB1 gene
Oc1Icf0.description: A tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 1p that encodes kinesin family member 1B, which is involved in intracellular transport and cellular apoptosis. Mutations in this gene are associated with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, neuroblastoma, and nonsyndromic paraganglioma.

mc1V1f0.title: Secondary ovarian insufficiency
mc1V1f0.description: Impaired ovarian function due to inadequate gonadotropic stimulation of the ovaries by the hypothalamus and/or pituitary glands, i.e., hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Causes include isolated GnRH deficiency, functional hypothalamic amenorrhea, and brain injury, infection, infiltration, or infarction.

Mc1M1f0.title: Oophoritis
Mc1M1f0.description: A condition of inflammation of one or both ovaries, generally caused by bacteria or autoimmune diseases. Typically associated with salpingitis and/or pelvic inflammatory disease. Clinical manifestations include vaginal discharge, pelvic pain, and fever.

nc171f0.title: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis
nc171f0.description: A rare disorder characterized by periodic attacks of muscle paralysis and hypokalemia in patients with hyperthyroidism and a concomitant susceptibility gene mutation in sarcolemmal ion channels (most commonly a loss of function mutation in KCNJ18 gene, which codes for an inward rectifying potassium channel). Seen primarily in patients of Asian descent.

Lc1w1f0.title: Postcholecystectomy diarrhea
Lc1w1f0.description: An uncommon complication of cholecystectomy that results in chronic diarrhea, likely due to excess bile acids in the colon and/or bile acid malabsorption (i.e., cholerrheic diarrhea).

Jc1sWf0.title: "Pimping"
Jc1sWf0.description: Despite the term's derogatory connotation, it is still commonly used to describe the experience of a senior physician (e.g., attending) questioning a junior (e.g., student), typically in rapid succession and sometimes in a Socratic manner. It allows personalized teaching from a senior physician but is sometimes considered bullying if done in a toxic manner. Unlike popular belief likely started from the article "The Art of Pimping" by FL Brancati in 1989, the word did not originate from "pump question" as a translation of the German word "Pümpfrage." AMBOSS does not condone the term's continual usage.

destinations.label: Clerkship guide → Clinical evaluation: how to impress your preceptors

qc1CWf0.title: Soluble fibrin
qc1CWf0.description: A product of fibrinogen degradation. Thrombin cleaves fibrinogen into fibrin monomers that normally quickly form a clot. Small amounts of these monomers may circulate as soluble fibrin. Levels are often elevated in diseases involving thrombosis (e.g., disseminated intravascular coagulation).

Ic1Ydf0.title: Thrombin-antithrombin complex
Ic1Ydf0.description: A complex formed during inactivation of thrombin by antithrombin. It positively correlates with the level of activated thrombin and can, therefore, be used as a laboratory marker for hypercoagulability.

rc1fdf0.title: Plasmin-α2-plasmin inhibitor complex
rc1fdf0.description: A complex formed during inhibition of plasmin by α2-plasmin inhibitor (formerly called antiplasmin). Formation of fibrin leads to the generation of plasmin and increased complex formation. PPIC can be used as a laboratory marker for fibrinolytic activity.

Hc1Kdf0.title: Patient presentation
Hc1Kdf0.description: A term for the formalized description of a patient case as communicated by one member of the medical team to another. The exact format is typically standardized by the team member's role. A physician's patient presentation should include the patient's presenting symptoms, examination findings, diagnostic findings, probable diagnosis, and plan of care (e.g., the SOAP format).

destinations.label: Daily life of the intern → Rounds

Dc11ef0.title: Shelf exam
Dc11ef0.description: A series of examinations created by the National Board of Medical Examiners. Each examination focuses on a specific clinical subject (e.g., Pediatrics, Psychiatry, Surgery). These examinations are frequently used by medical schools to assess students at the end of a clinical rotation.

destinations.label: Clerkship guide → Exams: what to expect

9c1Nef0.title: Child neglect
9c1Nef0.description: The failure to meet a child's basic physical, emotional, medical, or educational needs.

xc1Eef0.title: Civatte body
xc1Eef0.description: A round, eosinophilic, structure formed by the apoptosis of keratinocytes in the stratum basale of the epidermis. Associated with lichen planus and discoid lupus erythematous.

Bc1zef0.title: Erythroleukoplakia
Bc1zef0.description: A type of nonhomogeneous oral leukoplakia characterized by white plaques with red speckles. Has a higher risk of malignant transformation than homogeneous leukoplakia.

Ac1RUf0.title: Oral proliferative verrucous leukoplakia
Ac1RUf0.description: A rare, nonhomogeneous form of leukoplakia that has a warty appearance and a high rate of malignant transformation into squamous cell carcinoma.

_c15Uf0.title: Homogeneous oral leukoplakia
_c15Uf0.description: The most common form of oral leukoplakia. Characterized by homogeneous white plaques with well-defined margins. Has a lower risk of malignant transformation than nonhomogeneous forms of leukoplakia.

zc1rUf0.title: Nonhomogeneous oral leukoplakia
zc1rUf0.description: A form of oral leukoplakia characterized by lesions that are nonhomogeneous in appearance and/or texture. Examples include erythroleukoplakia and oral proliferative verrucous leukoplakia. Associated with a higher risk of malignant transformation than homogeneous forms of leukoplakia.

c11aff0.title: Family-centered rounding
c11aff0.description: A type of rounding at the bedside that allows for real-time dialogue between the health care team, the patient, and their caregivers. Typically used in the pediatric inpatient setting.

V11Gff0.title: Overt umbilical cord prolapse
V11Gff0.description: A condition in which a part of the umbilical cord lies between the antecedent part of the fetus (mostly head) and the pelvic wall, causing rupture of membranes and acute, life-threatening hypoxia for the fetus.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Umbilical cord complications

f11kTf0.title: Criteria for imaging prior to LP in suspected meningitis
f11kTf0.description: Clinical features that suggest head imaging may be warranted prior to lumbar puncture to reduce procedural complication risk. These include focal neurological deficits, altered mental status, immunocompromise, papilledema, history of CNS disease, and recent new-onset seizures.

T116Tf0.title: Spinal cord reflexes
T116Tf0.description: A type of reflex in which the integrating center of the reflex arc lies within the spinal cord. Examples include the biceps reflex, the knee reflex, and the ankle reflex. The reflex arc of spinal reflexes does not involve the brain or brainstem. However, upper motor neurons may modify the intensity of the reflex response.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord reflexes

g11FTf0.title: C-Fos gene
g11FTf0.description: A proto-oncogene that encodes leucine zipper proteins that are involved in DNA binding and dimerization to form transcription factor complex AP-1. Its retroviral oncogene homolog is v-fos.

S11yTf0.title: HEADSS assessment
S11yTf0.description: An acronym for the elements of a comprehensive social history for adolescents. It stands for: home, education and employment, eating, activities, drugs, sexuality, suicidal ideation and depression, and safety.

destinations.label: Pediatrics: history and physical examination → Social history

h11cgf0.title: Luteal-placental shift
h11cgf0.description: The time period around weeks 6-7 of gestation, in which the function of the corpus luteum declines and the production of progesterone gradually shifts from the corpus luteum to the placenta.

Q11ugf0.title: Molecular cloning
Q11ugf0.description: A technique that produces recombinant DNA molecules within host organisms (e.g., bacteria). Involves the isolation of a specific DNA sequence and the subsequent production of complementary DNA via reverse transcriptase, which is then inserted into a bacterial plasmid that produces copies of the target DNA.

j11_gf0.title: Cre-Lox recombination
j11_gf0.description: A site-specific recombinase technology that facilitates the manipulation of target genes (e.g.,  deletions, insertions) at specific developmental points. Can be used to study the effect of gene expression alteration.

P11WSf0.title: Solute diuresis
P11WSf0.description: An increase in urine output as a result of an increase in the urinary excretion of solutes, such as glucose, urea, electrolytes (e.g., sodium, chloride, bicarbonate), organic acids (e.g., ketoacids, amino acids), and exogenous substances (e.g., mannitol, glycerol). Can be caused by a failure of solute reabsorption from the proximal convoluted tubule or the loop of Henle and exogenous solute overload.

N11-Sf0.title: AVPR2 gene
N11-Sf0.description: A gene on the long arm of the X chromosome that encodes the vasopressin-2 receptor. A mutation in this gene is responsible for most cases of hereditary nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

611j3f0.title: NPH
611j3f0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Normal pressure hydrocephalus
2. Neutral Protamine Hagedorn (NPH) insulin

q11C3f0.title: Sterile technique
q11C3f0.description: A set of practices and procedures that establish and maintain sterility in a given area. Includes only touching sterile objects with sterile materials, keeping items above waist level, and avoiding puncturing or tearing sterile barriers.

destinations.label: Surgery clerkship → Working in the OR

s11tRf0.title: Cardioplegia
s11tRf0.description: An intentional and temporary myocardial arrest induced by often cold and hypokalemic cardioplegia solutions during cardiac surgery. The goals are to protect the myocardium by minimizing myocardial metabolism and to provide a motionless and bloodless operative site.

G11BRf0.title: Deep hypothermic circulatory arrest
G11BRf0.description: A perioperative technique used in surgeries involving blood vessels that supply the brain (e.g., aneurysm repair of the aortic arch, surgery of head and neck vessels). The goal is to minimize cerebral metabolism by reducing the patient's body temperature so that the blood supply can be temporarily interrupted.

t11Xif0.title: Catheter angiography
t11Xif0.description: An imaging modality that combines catheter insertion, local contrast dye application, and radiography to visualize and investigate blood vessels such as coronary, cerebral, and abdominal arteries. In addition to imaging, therapeutic procedures can be performed via the catheter (e.g., revascularization, stent implantation, or chemoembolization).

u11pif0.title: Hill kinetics
u11pif0.description: A type of kinetics seen with allosteric enzyme, receptor, and transporter systems. Follows the equation V₀ = (Vmax.[S]ⁿ)/(K' + [S]ⁿ) in which V₀ is the initial reaction rate, Vmax is the maximum reaction rate, [S] is the substrate concentration, K' is the substrate concentration at which the initial reaction rate is half of Vmax, and n is the Hill coefficient (which indicates the degree of allosteric cooperativity) with n > 0 and n ≠ 1. Results in a sigmoid graph when plotting V₀ as a function of [S].

v11Aif0.title: Allosteric site
v11Aif0.description: The sites on proteins (e.g., enzymes, receptors) at which molecules bind and regulate their activity via conformational changes in protein structure (allosteric modulation).

D111Qf0.title: X-intercept
D111Qf0.description: The value of the x-axis coordinate at which a line, curve, or surface intercepts the x-axis.

w11hQf0.title: Y-intercept
w11hQf0.description: The value of the y-axis coordinate at which a line, curve, or surface intercepts the y-axis.

C11qQf0.title: Negative cooperativity
C11qQf0.description: A phenomenon in which the binding of a ligand to a protein with multiple binding sites decreases the binding of additional ligands to the same protein. Examples include the binding of glutamine to cytidine triphosphate (which prevents the affinity of cytidine triphosphate for additional glutamine) and the binding of 2,3-diphosphoglycerate to hemoglobin (which decreases the affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen molecules).

y11djf0.title: Irreversible inhibitor
y11djf0.description: A molecule that binds to and permanently inhibits the activity of an enzyme or receptor. New enzymes or receptors must be synthesized to replace the disabled ones. Can be competitive (if the inhibitor binds to the active site) or noncompetitive (if it does not bind to the active site). With respect to enzyme kinetics, irreversible inhibition decreases the maximum reaction rate (Vmax) by decreasing the amount of functioning enzyme but does not decrease the Michaelis-Menten constant (Km).

aW1QPf0.title: K-type allosteric modulator
aW1QPf0.description: An allosteric modulator that primarily alters the affinity of the active site of an enzyme or receptor for its substrate or ligand. With respect to enzyme kinetics, these allosteric modulators do not significantly alter the maximum reaction rate (Vmax) but significantly increase or decrease K', the substrate concentration at which the reaction rate is half of Vmax. Most allosteric enzymes belong to the this group.

YW1nPf0.title: Hypnagogic hallucination
YW1nPf0.description: A type of sleep hallucination in which vivid, often frightening visual or auditory hallucinations occur as the patient falls asleep. (Remember: HypnaGOgic → GO to sleep)

bW1HPf0.title: Hypnopompic hallucination
bW1HPf0.description: A type of sleep hallucination in which vivid, often frightening visual or auditory, dream-like hallucinations occur as the patient wakes up. Less common than hypnagogic hallucinations.

hW1cOf0.title: Executive function
hW1cOf0.description: A set of cognitive functions for executing new and complex tasks. Examples include planning, decision-making, working memory, responding to feedback, impulse inhibition, and flexibility.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

4W13lf0.title: Circumstantial thought process
4W13lf0.description: Nonlinear thought expressed in speech as long-winded explanations and with multiple deviations from the central topic before a central idea is finally expressed.

kW1mlf0.title: Tangential thought process
kW1mlf0.description: Nonlinear thought expressed in speech as a gradual deviation from a focused idea or question (e.g., a person gets off topic and does not appropriately answer a question).

mW1VNf0.title: Epithelial–mesenchymal transition
mW1VNf0.description: A process in which a subset of epithelial cells transforms into mesenchymal cells during embryogenesis. The epithelial cells lose their polarity and intercellular adhesions and gain mesenchymal cell proteins, which facilitates travel to other sites of the developing organism. Cells can then go through a reverse process (mesenchymal-epithelial transition).

MW1MNf0.title: Complement activation-related pseudoallergy
MW1MNf0.description: A type of pseudoallergic reaction with symptoms of a type I hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., rash, angioedema). Not IgE-mediated; caused by complement-mediated mast cell degranulation.

nW17Nf0.title: Sinus arrest
nW17Nf0.description: Temporary absence of sinoatrial node depolarization on ECG (absent P waves).

media.title: Sinus bradycardia with sinus pause and junctional escape rhythm

LW1wNf0.title: Transverse myelitis
LW1wNf0.description: A subtype of myelitis (inflammation of the spinal cord) characterized by rapid paralysis and sensory changes below the level of the affected segment. Sometimes associated with a band-like sensation across the trunk. Causes include infections (e.g., herpes zoster) and autoimmune disorders (e.g., multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica).

oW10mf0.title: Mechanical CPR device
oW10mf0.description: A mechanical device designed to provide chest compressions. Types include load-distributing bands (a backboard and a band that goes across the chest) and piston devices (a backboard and a rigid frame with a piston that compresses the chest).

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)

KW1Umf0.title: Central canal
KW1Umf0.description: A cerebrospinal fluid-containing canal that originates in the caudal part of the medulla oblongata as a continuation of the fourth ventricle and runs along the entire length of the spinal cord within the gray commissure. Terminates caudally as the terminal ventricle in the conus medullaris. Formed within the neural tube during primary neurulation.

IW1Y5f0.title: X-ray tube
IW1Y5f0.description: A vacuum tube that converts electrical energy into x-rays and heat by accelerating electrons from the cathode to a high velocity via a high-voltage field, so that they collide with neutrons of the anode and emit a beam of x-rays.

7W145f0.title: Extracorporeal CPR
7W145f0.description: The use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in cardiac arrest patients refractory to standard ACLS.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Extracorporeal life support (ECLS)

HW1K5f0.title: Trinucleotide repeat expansion disease
HW1K5f0.description: An inherited disease that is caused by a repetition of DNA base triplets. Examples include fragile X syndrome, Huntington disease, myotonic dystrophy, and Friedreich ataxia. Disease severity correlates with the number of trinucleotide repetitions and often shows genetic anticipation.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

sW1t5f0.title: Mesencephalon
sW1t5f0.description:
A term than can refer to: 
1. The part of the brainstem called the midbrain
2. The primary and secondary brain vesicles that form during embryonic development and ultimately give rise to the midbrain

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Embryology of the brain

media.title: Anatomical illustration of the thalamus and hypothalamus

GW1B5f0.title: Secondary brain vesicle
GW1B5f0.description: A vesicle that arises from a primary brain vesicle during the 5th week of embryonic development. The secondary brain vesicles are the telencephalon, diencephalon, mesencephalon, metencephalon, and myelencephalon.

EW18Mf0.title: Intercostal nerves
EW18Mf0.description: A collection of somatic nerves that arise from the ventral rami of the T1-T11 spinal nerves. Located in the costal groove along the inferior margin of the superior rib. They innervate the thoracic wall, pleura, and peritoneum. Vulnerable to injury when the intercostal space is perforated.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Gross anatomy

media.title: Anatomy of the intercostal neurovascular bundle

vW1AMf0.title: Disseminated herpes zoster
vW1AMf0.description: A subset of herpes zoster characterized by > 20 extradermatomal vesicles, a rash affecting three or more dermatomes, and/or visceral organ involvement. Typically only affects immunocompromised individuals.

DW11nf0.title: Status myoclonus
DW11nf0.description: A state of nearly continuous myoclonus that lasts > 30 minutes. Most commonly occurs in patients who have experienced a hypoxic brain injury following cardiac arrest.

destinations.label: Rare neurological diseases → Myoclonic status epilepticus

wW1hnf0.title: Oxygen delivery
wW1hnf0.description: The rate at which oxygen is transported from the lungs to the peripheral circulation. Calculated with the following formula: DO₂ (mL/min) = cardiac output x arterial oxygen content. Normal value is ~ 1,000 mL O₂/min.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Oxygen transport and conditions that affect oxygenation

9W1Nnf0.title: Carbon dioxide production rate
9W1Nnf0.description: The amount of carbon dioxide produced and exhaled by the body or a specific organ per minute.

BW1znf0.title: Visual agnosia
BW1znf0.description: An inability to recognize visually presented objects despite otherwise normal vision. Caused by a lesion in the visual association cortex in the occipital lobe or ventral visual stream in the temporal lobe.

yW1dLf0.title: Auditory agnosia
yW1dLf0.description: An inability to recognize sounds despite preserved hearing ability. Caused by lesions of the auditory ventral stream (anterior superior temporal gyrus).

AW1RLf0.title: Visuospatial agnosia
AW1RLf0.description: An inability to localize and orient oneself and/or identify relationships between objects in the environment. Often associated with damage to the right posterior parietal area of the brain.

_W15Lf0.title: Spinoolivary tract
_W15Lf0.description: An ascending sensory pathway that transmits unconscious proprioceptive information from the spinal cord to the cerebellum via a relay in the inferior olivary nuclei.

destinations.label: Spinal cord tracts and reflexes → Spinal cord tracts

zW1rLf0.title: Autotopagnosia
zW1rLf0.description: An inability of an individual to localize parts of their body. Caused by damage to the left posterior parietal area of the cortex.

-W1DLf0.title: Praxis
-W1DLf0.description: An ability of an individual to enact a skill or perform a particular voluntary movement to achieve a goal.

Zd1Zof0.title: Reticulospinal tract
Zd1Zof0.description: A descending extrapyramidal tract that consists of medial subpathways (originating from the pontine reticular formation) and lateral subpathways (originating from the medullary pontine formation). Involved in the facilitation of voluntary and reflex responses, muscle tone, and posture.

0d1eof0.title: Vestibulospinal tract
0d1eof0.description: An extrapyramidal descending tract that consists of motor neurons divided into medial and lateral subpathways. The lateral vestibulospinal tract controls muscle tone in leg extensors, which help maintain upright posture. The medial vestibulospinal tract innervates neck musculature and facilitates muscle tone and head movements.

ad1Qof0.title: Tectospinal tract
ad1Qof0.description: A descending extrapyramidal tract that originates in the superior colliculus of the midbrain. The presumed function involves the mediation of reflex posturing of the head in response to auditory or visual stimuli.

Yd1nof0.title: Rigors
Yd1nof0.description: A symptom of vigorous shivering, often accompanied by diaphoresis and a subjective feeling of cold. Associated with fevers.

bd1Hof0.title: National Board of Medical Examiners®
bd1Hof0.description: A nonprofit organization that creates examinations intended to assess clinical knowledge and patient management skills of health professionals. These examinations include the USMLE Step 1, Step 2 CK, Step 2 CS, and Step 3 examinations.

Xd19of0.title: COMATs
Xd19of0.description: A series of examinations created by the National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners. Each examination consists of 125 items on a specific subject (e.g., Pediatrics, Psychiatry, Surgery).

Wd1PKf0.title: One-Minute Telegram 4-2020-1/3
Wd1PKf0.description: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) has been at the center of attention since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has recently revoked emergency use authorization for both chloroquine and HCQ because the potential side effects outweigh the benefits. [...]

dd1oKf0.title: One-Minute Telegram 4-2020-2/3
dd1oKf0.description: The topic of gun ownership has long polarized public opinion in the US. Firearm violence, including mass shootings and suicide, has been described as a public health crisis that requires immediate attention nationwide, yet resistance to stronger regulation of firearm ownership remains high. [...]

Vd1GKf0.title: One-Minute Telegram 4-2020-3/3
Vd1GKf0.description: Tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the greatest killers worldwide, and its eradication by 2030 is one of the targets set by the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Previous research in children and adults has shown that a 4-month rifampin regimen is equally effective in treating latent TB and has higher completion rates than the usual 9-month isoniazid regimen, but it has not become established due to the high cost per rifampin pill. [...]

ed1xKf0.title: Glioneuronal hamartoma
ed1xKf0.description: A nodule that can be found in the brain of patients with tuberous sclerosis. Consists of enlarged, disorganized, and atypical neuronal and glial tissue. Thought to form from abnormal neuronal migration. Can calcify with age and become hard or sclerotic.

Ud1b6f0.title: Blastema
Ud1b6f0.description: A mass of undifferentiated, pluripotent cells.

Td166f0.title: Rubro-olivary tract
Td166f0.description: A fiber tract that conveys motor information from the red nucleus in the midbrain to the ipsilateral inferior olivary nuclei in the medulla via the central tegmental tract. Forms a part of the dentato-rubro-olivary pathway and is involved in the coordination of motor movement.

Sd1y6f0.title: False positive rate
Sd1y6f0.description: The proportion of people without a condition who test positive. It is equal to 1 - specificity (true negative rate). A test with a high false positive rate has low specificity.
