id1Jpf0.title: Semont repositioning maneuver
id1Jpf0.description: A therapeutic maneuver for posterior semicircular canal BPPV.

Qd1upf0.title: Ectopia cordis
Qd1upf0.description: A congenital condition in which the heart is partially or completely placed out of the chest cavity as a result of impaired fusion of the chest wall.

jd1_pf0.title: Side-lying maneuver
jd1_pf0.description: A provocative test used to diagnose posterior semicircular canal BPPV. Can be used as an alternative to the Dix-Hallpike maneuver.

Pd1WJf0.title: Supine roll test
Pd1WJf0.description: A provoking maneuver used to diagnose lateral (horizontal) semicircular canal BPPV.

4d13Jf0.title: Upbeat nystagmus
4d13Jf0.description: A variant of vertical nystagmus in which the eyes beat toward the forehead. Manifests with a torsional nystagmus component in most patients with posterior canal BPPV on performing the Dix-Hallpike maneuver.

kd1mJf0.title: Lambert sign
kd1mJf0.description: A physical examination finding in which a patient's hand grip strength gradually increases over several seconds of strength testing. Indicates improved muscle strength with repetitive use and can be seen in patients with Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome.

Od1IJf0.title: Torsional nystagmus
Od1IJf0.description: Rotary oscillations of the eye along its anteroposterior axis. In benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, torsional nystagmus is seen as the beating of the upper pole of the eyes toward the dependent ear on moving the head from side to side (with the patient in a supine position). A horizontal or vertical nystagmus component is also typically present in torsional nystagmus due to an inner ear pathology.

ld1vJf0.title: Barbecue rotation
ld1vJf0.description: A therapeutic maneuver for patients with lateral (horizontal) semicircular canal BPPV after eliciting geotropic nystagmus on a provoking maneuver.

Nd1-Jf0.title: Gufoni maneuver
Nd1-Jf0.description: A therapeutic maneuver for patients with lateral (horizontal) semicircular canal BPPV showing geotropic or apogeotropic nystagmus elicted by provoking maneuver.

md1Vqf0.title: Forced prolonged positioning
md1Vqf0.description: A therapeutic maneuver for patients with lateral (horizontal) semicircular canal BPPV with geotropic or apogeotropic nystagmus elicited on provoking maneuver.

5d1iqf0.title: Erosio interdigitalis blastomycetica
5d1iqf0.description: A subtype of candidal intertrigo that develops in the web spaces of the digits. Risk factors for development include frequent wet work and hyperhidrosis.

Kd1UIf0.title: Radiation boost
Kd1UIf0.description: Supplemental irradiation of the tumor bed that is applied after initial radiotherapy, with the aim of destroying residual tumor cells and local tumor recurrence.

6d1jIf0.title: Neoadjuvant radiotherapy
6d1jIf0.description: Radiotherapy applied before the main treatment, typically preoperatively, with the goal of reducing tumor size to help facilitate resection and increase the chances of a curative operation.

pd1LIf0.title: Head-shaking maneuver
pd1LIf0.description: A therapeutic maneuver for patients with lateral (horizontal) semicircular canal BPPV with apogeotropic nystagmus elicited by provoking maneuver.

Jd1sIf0.title: Intraoperative radiotherapy
Jd1sIf0.description: Radiotherapy that delivers a high dose of radiation to a targeted area during surgery. Compared to conventional external beam radiotherapy, the procedure's precision minimizes radiation exposure to surrounding tissue and also reduces the chance of tumor cell repopulation since there is no delay between surgery and radiotherapy.

qd1CIf0.title: Adjuvant radiotherapy
qd1CIf0.description: Radiotherapy applied after surgery, with the goal of destroying any malignant cells still present after surgery.

Id1Yrf0.title: Inferior lumbar triangle
Id1Yrf0.description: A triangular region located on each side of the lower lumbar region. Bounded inferiorly by the iliac crest, medially by the latissimus dorsi muscle, and laterally by the external oblique muscle. This triangle can be the point of protrusion of inferior lumbar hernias (petit hernias).

rd1frf0.title: Superior lumbar triangle
rd1frf0.description: A triangular region located on each side of the upper lumbar region. Bounded superiorly by the 12th rib, medially by the erector spinae muscle, and laterally by the internal oblique muscle. This triangle can be the point of protrusion of superior lumbar hernias (Grynfeltt hernias).

Gd1Brf0.title: Chemoradiotherapy
Gd1Brf0.description: A combination of chemotherapy and radiotherapy to treat cancer.

Ed187f0.title: Superior suprarenal artery
Ed187f0.description: An artery that branches off the inferior phrenic artery. Supplies the adrenal gland.

vd1A7f0.title: Inferior phrenic arteries
vd1A7f0.description: A pair of arteries that branch off of the abdominal aorta at the level of the T12 vertebra. Each directly supplies the ipsilateral half of the diaphragm and the inferior portion of the esophagus and gives rise to a superior suprarenal artery, which supplies the ipsilateral adrenal gland.

Dd11Hf0.title: Middle suprarenal arteries
Dd11Hf0.description: A pair of arteries that branch off of the abdominal aorta at the level of the L2 vertebra between the inferior phrenic arteries and the renal arteries, superior to the origin of the superior mesenteric artery. They supply the adrenal glands.

wd1hHf0.title: Inferior suprarenal artery
wd1hHf0.description: An artery that arises from the renal artery. Supplies the adrenal gland.

9d1NHf0.title: Nitrogen balance
9d1NHf0.description: The difference between protein intake and protein loss as represented by the nitrogen found in amino acids. Used to determine dietary protein requirements. Stress-induced hormones (e.g., catecholamines, cortisol) lead to proteolysis and decreased nitrogen balance. Increased protein intake and anabolic states lead to increased nitrogen balance.

Cd1qHf0.title: Renal arteries
Cd1qHf0.description: A pair of arteries that arise from the abdominal aorta at the level of the inferior border of the L1 vertebra. Each directly supplies the ipsilateral kidney and gives rise to an inferior suprarenal artery, which supplies the adrenal gland.

0V1eGf0.title: Reichert cartilage
0V1eGf0.description: A cartilaginous structure in the dorsal part of the second pharyngeal arch. Gives rise to the stapes, lesser cornu of the hyoid bone, styloid process of the temporal bone, and stylohyoid ligament.

aV1QGf0.title: Apogeotropic nystagmus
aV1QGf0.description: A variant of horizontal nystagmus in which the eyes beat toward the ceiling (or the nondependent ear) when the head is turned from side to side with the patient in supine position. Can be elicited using the supine roll maneuver in patients with lateral semicircular canal BPPV; and, in association with a downbeat component, in patients with cerebellar or brainstem lesions.

media.title: Animation: Apogeotropic horizontal nystagmus in lateral canal BPPV

YV1nGf0.title: Geotropic nystagmus
YV1nGf0.description: A variant of horizontal nystagmus in which the eyes beat toward the ground (or the dependent ear) when the head is turned from side to side with the patient in supine position. In patients with lateral semicircular canal BPPV, this type of nystagmus can be elicited using the supine-roll maneuver.

media.title: Animation: Geotropic horizontal nystagmus in lateral canal BPPV

2V1TFf0.title: United States Medical Licensing Examination®
2V1TFf0.description: A three-part examination for medical licensure in the United States organized by the National Board of Medical Examiners and the Federation of State Medical Boards. Includes Step 1, Step 2 CK, and Step 3.

destinations.label: The United States Medical Licensing Examination® (USMLE)

hV1c8f0.title: Bacterascites
hV1c8f0.description: A positive ascitic fluid bacterial culture in the presence of ascitic fluid neutrophil count < 250 cells/mm³ that is not associated with a surgically treatable intraabdominal source of infection. Bacterascites may represent transient bacterial colonization of ascitic fluid or early spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.

3V1S8f0.title: Hypertrophic olivary degeneration
3V1S8f0.description: A rare degenerative disease that develops as a result of focal injury to the dentato-rubro-olivary tract, which connects the cerebellum and brainstem for motor coordination. Classically manifests with palatal myoclonus and results in hypertrophic degeneration of the inferior olive.

RV1l8f0.title: Gallstone
RV1l8f0.description: A stone created from precipitated bile components in the gallbladder. Can result in gallstone disease (e.g., cholelithiasis). There are three main types of gallstones: cholesterol stones (~ 80%), black pigment stones (~ 10%), and mixed (brown pigment) stones (~ 10%).

media.title: Pathophysiology for different types of gallstones

iV1J8f0.title: Singular canal
iV1J8f0.description: An osseous canal located within the petrous temporal bone. The posterior ampullary nerve (singular nerve) traverses through it.

QV1u8f0.title: Posterior ampullary nerve
QV1u8f0.description: A branch of the vestibular nerve that transmits afferent innervation from the posterior semicircular canal. Selective transection of this nerve is used to treat refractory cases of benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.

jV1_8f0.title: Canalith repositioning maneuvers
jV1_8f0.description: A set of specific sequential maneuvers performed to mobilize otoconia out of the semicircular canal and back into the vestibule. Used to treat benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Examples include the Epley maneuver and the Semont repositioning maneuver.

PV1Wuf0.title: Neuromuscular blockers
PV1Wuf0.description: A type of muscle relaxant drug that blocks transmission at the neuromuscular junction, leading to temporary paralysis of downstream skeletal muscle. Commonly used in anesthesia, airway management, and mechanical ventilation. Subcategorized into depolarizing and nondepolarizing subtypes.

4V13uf0.title: Head-tilt/chin-lift
4V13uf0.description: A basic airway positioning maneuver performed to maintain patency and airflow in patients with potential airway compromise. Consists of tilting the head of the patient posteriorly and lifting the chin (and attached soft tissues) anteriorly to align the oral, pharyngeal, and laryngeal axes.

destinations.label: Airway management → Initial airway opening maneuvers

kV1muf0.title: Pertinent positive
kV1muf0.description: A disease-specific clinical finding (e.g., symptom or risk factor) that is present and used to aid in establishing a diagnosis (e.g., presence of tachycardia may raise suspicion for a diagnosis of pulmonary embolism).

OV1Iuf0.title: Pertinent negative
OV1Iuf0.description: A clinical finding (e.g., symptom or risk factor) that may be related to a patient's chief complaint but is absent. Can be used to aid in establishing a diagnosis (e.g., lack of cough in a patient with tonsillar exudates may raise suspicion for streptococcal pharyngitis; lack of fever in a patient with headache may lower suspicion for meningitis).

lV1vuf0.title: USMLE® Step 1
lV1vuf0.description: The first part of the United States Medical Licensing Examination. An 8-hour, computer-based test that consists of approximately 280 multiple choice questions. which are separated into 7 blocks of approximately 40 questions each. Content tested includes principles and mechanisms that underlie health, disease, and therapies. On January 26, 2022, test results were changed from a numeric score to a pass/fail system.

destinations.label: The United States Medical Licensing Examination® (USMLE) → Step 1 description

NV1-uf0.title: Step 2 Clinical Skills
NV1-uf0.description: A former component of the second part of the United States Medical Licensing Examination. Consisted of 12 standardized patient encounters that each lasted for up to 15 minutes. Examinees were expected to obtain a history, perform a physical examination (when appropriate), and formulate an assessment and plan. Following each patient encounter, 10 minutes were designated to complete a patient note. Was permanently suspended in January 2021.

mV1VEf0.title: Rhodopsin
mV1VEf0.description: A visual pigment and G protein-coupled receptor that is found in retinal rods. Contains the vitamin A derivative 11-cis-retinal. Activated by light (phototransduction).

MV1MEf0.title: Vestibular function tests
MV1MEf0.description: A set of tests used to identify nystagmus in response to vestibular stimulation. Used to assess the integrity and function of the vestibular apparatus of the inner ear. Includes caloric testing, rotational chair testing, electronystagmography, and vestibular-evoked myogenic potentials.

oV10vf0.title: Podiatry
oV10vf0.description: A medical speciality that evaluates and treats conditions that affect the lower extremities (i.e., the feet, ankles, and related structures).

KV1Uvf0.title: Yacovino maneuver
KV1Uvf0.description: A therapeutic maneuver for anterior semicircular canal BPPV.

6V1jvf0.title: Male circumcision
6V1jvf0.description: A procedure in which the prepuce (foreskin) of the penis is surgically removed for medical, cultural, or religious reasons.

pV1Lvf0.title: PEG
pV1Lvf0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Polyethylene glycol
2. Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy

JV1svf0.title: Placenta accreta spectrum
JV1svf0.description: A condition that encompasses the types of abnormally adherent placenta. It includes placenta accreta, increta, and percreta. Typically results in delayed separation and/or placental retention as well as postpartum hemorrhage.

qV1Cvf0.title: Dental caries
qV1Cvf0.description: The progressive destruction of dental tissue following damage to the enamel by acid produced by bacteria in dental plaque. Manifestations include tooth pain and bad breath.

rV1fDf0.title: Cawthorne-Cooksey exercises
rV1fDf0.description: A series of exercises of the eye, head, and body used in the management of peripheral vertigo or balance disorders. These exercises provoke vestibular symptoms; repeated exercise can fatigue the vestibular response and result in habituation by the central nervous system.

7V14Df0.title: T-piece
7V14Df0.description: A tracheal oxygen delivery system shaped like the letter T that allows for oxygen to be delivered via one arm and exhaled air to exit from the other.

destinations.label: Oxygen therapy → Advanced oxygen delivery systems

HV1KDf0.title: Langhans giant cell
HV1KDf0.description: A type of multinucleated giant cell that forms from the fusion of epithelioid macrophages. Associated with granulomatous diseases such as tuberculosis and sarcoidosis.

sV1tDf0.title: Graphesthesia
sV1tDf0.description: The ability to identify numbers and letters drawn on the palm of the hand.

GV1BDf0.title: Baresthesia
GV1BDf0.description: The ability to evaluate and discriminate between the weights of different objects by holding and/or lifting them.

tV1Xwf0.title: National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale
tV1Xwf0.description: A tool used to evaluate the severity of a stroke in the acute setting. Includes an assessment of level of consciousness, orientation to month and age, ability to follow commands, horizontal extraocular movements, visual fields, presence of facial palsy, motor drift and ataxia of the extremities, sensation, language, dysarthria, and attention.

8V1Owf0.title: Auscultation
8V1Owf0.description: A physical examination technique that involves listening to internal sounds of the body (e.g., heart, lung, and bowel sounds), typically using a stethoscope.

uV1pwf0.title: Cerebral atrophy
uV1pwf0.description: A loss of cerebral tissue (e.g., neurons and neuronal connections). Can be generalized or focal. Associated with several conditions, including stroke, traumatic brain injury, and Alzheimer disease. Manifestations include dementia, seizures, and aphasia.

EV18wf0.title: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
EV18wf0.description: A condition characterized by orthostatic headache, low cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) pressure, and diffuse meningeal enhancement on MRI. Can be caused by CSF leakage from the spinal cord.

vV1Awf0.title: Otolith organs
vV1Awf0.description: A pair of structures (the saccule and utricle) in the inner ear that contain otoliths. They facilitate the perception of linear acceleration (in the horizontal and vertical planes).

DV119f0.title: Pure tone audiometry
DV119f0.description: A procedure in which a patient signals if various frequencies are audible via headphones (air conduction) and a bone oscillator placed on the mastoid bones (bone conduction). Used to generate audiograms.

wV1h9f0.title: Word recognition score
wV1h9f0.description: A score generated by testing the ability of a patient to correctly repeat single-syllable words given at a particular sound intensity level. Typically decreases with increased sensorineural hearing loss.

9V1N9f0.title: Hypopigmentation
9V1N9f0.description: A lightening of the skin due to decreased presence of melanin. Associated with several conditions, including endocrine disorders and dermatologic disorders (e.g., pityriasis alba, postinflammatory change from atopic dermatitis).

CV1q9f0.title: Horizontal nystagmus
CV1q9f0.description: A type of nystagmus characterized by constant drift of the eyes toward the intact hemisphere with a fast phase toward the side of the lesion. Typically low in amplitude. Etiologies include benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (when the horizontal semicircular canal is affected) and unilateral disease of the cerebellar hemispheres.

xV1E9f0.title: Vertical nystagmus
xV1E9f0.description: A type of jerk nystagmus characterized by upbeating or downbeating movements of the eyes. Etiologies include benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (when the anterior or posterior semicircular canal is affected) and lesions of the posterior fossa.

yV1dCf0.title: Contraversive nystagmus
yV1dCf0.description: A subtype of apogeotropic nystagmus in which the beating direction is the opposite as that of spontaneous horizontal nystagmus while supine.

AV1RCf0.title: Ampullary cupula
AV1RCf0.description: A structure of the vestibular system located at the end of each semicircular duct. A collection of innervated hair cells (ampullary crest) is located at its base. The cupula moves across the ampullary crest due to the movement of endolymphatic fluid.

_V15Cf0.title: Colectomy
_V15Cf0.description: The surgical resection of all or part of the large bowel. Used to treat malignancy (e.g., colon cancer) and several diseases (e.g., volvulus, Crohn disease).

zV1rCf0.title: Brandt-Daroff exercises
zV1rCf0.description: A series of exercises of the head and body used used in the management of peripheral vertigo or balance disorders. These exercises use rapid lateral movements to promote repositioning of inner ear debris toward the utricular cavity.

-V1DCf0.title: Ephedra sinica
-V1DCf0.description: An herb that naturally contains ephedrine and pseudoephedrine, which stimulate the central nervous system. At low doses, the herb acts as a decongestant and can be used to promote urination and treat asthma, bronchitis, and cough. High doses can increase the risk of heart attack and stroke. It is currently banned by the FDA.

Ze1Zxf0.title: Mucous membrane
Ze1Zxf0.description: A membrane that lines several parts of the body, including portions of the gastrointestinal, respiratory, and genitourinary tracts. Consists of epithelium and connective tissue and can sometimes include a muscle layer.

0e1exf0.title: Submucosa
0e1exf0.description: A layer of tissue found beneath the mucosa in several parts of the body, including portions of the gastrointestinal, respiratory, and genitourinary tracts. Contains connective tissue, vasculature, lymphatic vessels, and nerves.

ae1Qxf0.title: Wellens syndrome
ae1Qxf0.description: A syndrome characterized by unstable angina and deeply inverted or biphasic T waves in leads V₂-V₃ in the absence of significant ST-segment elevation. Caused by severe proximal stenosis of the left anterior descending artery.

media.title: Left anterior descending coronary artery disease

Ye1nxf0.title: Visual phototransduction
Ye1nxf0.description: The process by which rhodopsin, a visual pigment molecule in the photoreceptor cells of the retina, absorbs photons and convert light energy to an electrical cellular response.

be1Hxf0.title: Genome-wide association study
be1Hxf0.description: A genetic study that analyzes the genomes of multiple people to identify genetic variations (e.g., single-nucleotide polymorphisms) associated with a specific disease.

Xe19xf0.title: Urinary fistula
Xe19xf0.description: An abnormal connection between any part of the urinary tract (e.g., kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra) and adjacent organs or body cavities (e.g., reproductive organs, gastrointestinal tract).

ce1aBf0.title: Aqueductal stenosis
ce1aBf0.description: A type of obstructive hydrocephalus that can occur between the third and fourth ventricles. Most commonly congenital. Manifestations include headaches, seizures, and intellectual disability.

We1PBf0.title: Mentzer index
We1PBf0.description: A ratio of the mean corpuscular volume to red blood cell count. Used as a screening tool for thalassemia.  A ratio < 13 suggests thalassemia; a ratio > 13 suggests iron deficiency anemia.

Ve1GBf0.title: Microsporidia
Ve1GBf0.description: An order of intracellular, spore-forming fungi that cause oppportunistic ocular, pulmonary, intestinal, and musculoskeletal infections. Genuses within this order include Enterocytozooan, Nosema, Trachipleistophora, Pleistophora, Vittaforma, and Microsporidum.

2e1Tyf0.title: Pruritus gravidarum
2e1Tyf0.description: A dermatologic condition of pregnancy (typically the late second trimester to the early third trimester) that manifests with intermittent pruritus in the abdomen area that can spread to involve the trunk, palms, and soles. Caused by an increase in bile acids within the skin.

fe1kyf0.title: Anti-Lewis antibodies
fe1kyf0.description: A group of antibodies directed against the Lewis blood group antigens. These antibodies are rare causes of transfusion reactions.

Te16yf0.title: Lewis antigen system
Te16yf0.description: A human blood group system that consists of antigens encoded by the FUT2 and FUT3 genes. These antigens are passively adsorbed onto erythrocytes.

ge1Fyf0.title: Venetoclax
ge1Fyf0.description: A targeted anticancer drug that inhibits the antiapoptotic protein BCL-2. Used to treat acute myeloid leukemia, chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma, mantle cell lymphoma, and multiple myeloma.

Se1yyf0.title: Range of motion
Se1yyf0.description: A maximum angle through which a joint can move when a certain action is performed (e.g., flexion). Assessed with active, passive, or assisted movements. Measured in degrees.

he1cAf0.title: Sarin
he1cAf0.description: An irreversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used as a chemical warfare agent. Causes classic symptoms of organophosphate poisoning, including increased salivation, diarrhea, bronchospasm, lacrimation, tremor, and paralysis.

3e1SAf0.title: Mustard gas
3e1SAf0.description: A chemical weapon that causes blisters and burns, conjunctivitis, temporary blindness, dyspnea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Severe toxicity can cause bone marrow suppression (aplastic anemia, pancytopenia) but is not usually fatal.

Re1lAf0.title: Electrocochleography
Re1lAf0.description: A test that measures the summating potential generated by cochlear hair cells and of the cochlear nerve action potential in response to acoustic stimulation. These findings can aid in the differential diagnosis of vertigo.

Qe1uAf0.title: Vestibular suppressants
Qe1uAf0.description: Drugs used to decrease the effects of vestibular dysfunction, such as vertigo, nystagmus, and nausea. Classes of drugs used for vestibular suppression include antihistamines, benzodiazepines, and centrally-acting anticholinergics.

je1_Af0.title: Input/output monitoring
je1_Af0.description: A method of monitoring a patient's fluid status. All inputs (oral, intravenous, subcutaneous) and fluid losses (through urination, vomiting, and diarrhea) are documented and the difference between these is calculated, giving either a positive balance (more fluid has been taken in than lost) or a negative balance (more fluid has been lost than taken in).

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Monitoring and evaluation

4e13_f0.title: Talaromyces marneffei
4e13_f0.description: A dimorphic fungus that can cause talaromycosis (formerly penicilliosis) in immunosuppressed individuals. Endemic to Southeast Asia.

ke1m_f0.title: Talaromycosis
ke1m_f0.description: An opportunistic fungal infection caused by Talaromyces marneffei. Endemic to Southeast Asia. Manifestations include fever, weight loss, lymphadenopathy, skin lesions, respiratory symptoms, and gastrointestinal symptoms.

le1v_f0.title: Heterodisomy
le1v_f0.description: An error in meiosis I that results in two different homologous chromosomes from one parent passed to offspring (uniparental disomy).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

me1Vzf0.title: Mitotic phase
me1Vzf0.description: The last phase of the eukaryotic cell cycle, which includes mitosis and cytokinesis. It is the shortest phase of the cell cycle.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

5e1izf0.title: Cytokinesis
5e1izf0.description: The division of a cell's cytoplasm after mitosis into two new daughter cells. Part of the M phase of the cell cycle.

destinations.label: The cell cycle → Cell cycle phases

Ke1U-f0.title: X-ray changes suggestive of FBA
Ke1U-f0.description: Early findings include focal hyperlucency, reduced pulmonary markings in the affected lung, and, in severe cases, flattening of the ipsilateral hemidiaphragm and mediastinal shift to the unaffected side. Atelectasis is a sign of complete airway obstruction. Late findings include focal consolidation, ipsilateral pleural effusion, and ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.

6e1j-f0.title: Hereditary paraganglioma-pheochromocytoma syndrome
6e1j-f0.description: An autosomal dominant condition characterized by early-onset development of multiple, recurrent extra-adrenal paragangliomas and pheochromocytomas.

pe1L-f0.title: Head injury
pe1L-f0.description: A trauma to the head that may be associated with soft tissue injury, skull fractures, and/or traumatic brain injury.

Je1s-f0.title: Closed head injury
Je1s-f0.description: A head injury in which the dura mater remains intact. Typically results from blunt force trauma to the head. It is the most common type of head injury.

qe1C-f0.title: Open head injury
qe1C-f0.description: A head injury in which the dura mater is breached, which exposes cranial contents to the environment. Typically results from penetrating trauma to the head (e.g., gunshot injury, blunt force injury that causes skull fracture).

Ie1YZT0.title: Hyperdynamic circulation
Ie1YZT0.description: A condition in which cardiac output (circulatory volume) is increased above the normal limits at rest (i.e., > 8 L/min). Manifestations include tachycardia and an increased pulse pressure. Etiologies include hypervolemia, liver failure, pregnancy, sepsis, and thyrotoxicosis.

re1fZT0.title: Ochronotic osteoarthropathy
re1fZT0.description: A manifestation of alkaptonuria characterized by joint pain and degeneration that results from the deposition of homogentisic acid within hyaline articular cartilage (e.g., in intervertebral discs). Can result severe ankylosis.

He1KZT0.title: Primary brain injury
He1KZT0.description: A brain injury that occurs as an immediate consequence at the time of the trauma. Can be focal (e.g., intracranial hemorrhage, contusion) or diffuse (e.g., diffuse axonal injury, cerebral edema).

se1tZT0.title: Labyrinthectomy
se1tZT0.description: The surgical destruction of the labyrinth of the inner ear. Used to treat intractable vertigo due to vestibular dysfunction, such as refractory Ménière disease. Ipsilateral hearing and vestibular function are completely lost as a consequence of this procedure. There, it is typically only performed in patients with unilateral disease.

Ge1BZT0.title: Vestibular neurectomy
Ge1BZT0.description: Surgical transection of the vestibular nerve. Hearing is preserved as the cochlear nerve is left intact. Used to treat intractable vertigo due to vestibular dysfunction (i.e., refractory Ménière disease).

te1X0T0.title: Coup-contrecoup injury
te1X0T0.description: A type of traumatic head injury in which an injury occurs at the site of the impact (coup injury) as well as the site directly opposite to the impact (contrecoup injury) due to linear transmission of force within the enclosed cranium.  More common in high-impact head injuries. The frontal and temporal lobes are most commonly affected.

xe1EaT0.title: PTPN22 gene
xe1EaT0.description: A gene located on chromosome 1 that encodes lymphoid protein tyrosine phosphatase (Lyp), a protein expressed in immune cells. Mutations in this gene have been associated with various autoimmune diseases, including type 1 diabetes mellitus, systemic lupus erythematosus, Graves disease, and rheumatoid arthritis.

ye1dYT0.title: Hephaestin
ye1dYT0.description: A homolog of ceruloplasmin that is involved in iron export from enterocytes.

Ae1RYT0.title: Visual release hallucinations
Ae1RYT0.description: A condition characterized by visual hallucinations that occur in association with loss of visual acuity. The associated visual deficit can be caused by ocular conditions or injury to the optic nerve, optic chiasm, and/or brain.

_e15YT0.title: Ottawa ankle and foot rules
_e15YT0.description: A set of criteria used to guide whether patients should receive radiographic imaging after a traumatic ankle or midfoot injury. Radiographs are indicated if there is an inability to bear weight immediately after the injury and upon evaluation. In addition, for traumatic ankle pain, radiographs are indicated if there is point tenderness at the lateral malleolus or medial malleolus; for traumatic midfoot pain, radiographs are indicated if there is point tenderness at the base of the fifth metatarsal or the navicular.

ze1rYT0.title: B-type inclusion
ze1rYT0.description: An intracytoplasmic inclusion body found on histopathologic examination of host epithelial cells infected by poxviruses (e.g., smallpox virus and vaccinia virus). Involved in viral replication.

-e1DYT0.title: Ataxia-telangiectasia-like-disorder type 2
-e1DYT0.description: An autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder caused by defects in DNA excision repair. Characterized by developmental delay, ataxia, sensorineural hearing loss, short stature, cutaneous and ocular telangiectasia, and photosensitivity.

ZU1ZbT0.title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 1
ZU1ZbT0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder characterized by cerebellar ataxia, oculomotor apraxia, cerebellar atrophy, and severe axonal sensorimotor neuropathy.

0U1ebT0.title: Ataxia with oculomotor apraxia type 2
0U1ebT0.description: An autosomal recessive condition characterized by progressive cerebellar ataxia, oculomotor apraxia, distal amyotrophy, sensory and motor axonal neuropathy, and increased serum alpha-fetoprotein concentration.

aU1QbT0.title: RIDDLE syndrome
aU1QbT0.description: An autosomal recessive immunodeficiency disorder characterized by hypersensitivity to ionizing radiation, immunodeficiency, facial dysmorphism, and learning difficulties. Additional manifestations include ataxia, conjunctival telangiectasia, and increased serum concentrations of AFP.

YU1nbT0.title: Oncosis
YU1nbT0.description: Cellular swelling and resulting damage that occurs from ischemia and leads to cell death/necrosis with karyolysis. Sometimes used synonymously with necrosis (oncotic necrosis).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Necrosis

bU1HbT0.title: Meniere triad
bU1HbT0.description: A symptomatic triad of peripheral vertigo, tinnitus, and sensorineural hearing loss. Characteristic of Ménière disease.

XU19bT0.title: Signs of poor peripheral perfusion
XU19bT0.description: A constellation of features seen in tissue hypoperfusion and/or peripheral vasoconstriction (e.g., due to shock). Signs include cold or clammy skin (especially in the extremities); color changes, such as pallor, mottling, and peripheral cyanosis; and delayed capillary refill (> 2 seconds).

cU1aXT0.title: Lermoyez syndrome
cU1aXT0.description: A variant of Ménière disease in which hearing improves during or immediately after acute attacks of vertigo. In contrast, patients with Ménière disease develop or have worsening sensorineural hearing loss during acute attacks of vertigo.

WU1PXT0.title: Hemiataxia
WU1PXT0.description: A lack of coordination of voluntary movements in one half of the body.

dU1oXT0.title: Social determinants of health
dU1oXT0.description: The political, cultural, and socioeconomic conditions in which individuals are born and live and that have an impact on health, e.g., education, the natural environment, nutrition, wealth distribution, gender, race, and/or access to health care. Recognizing and addressing the inequities arising from disparities between these determinants can improve the health of the most vulnerable and susceptible individuals.

destinations.label: Health care system → Social aspects of health care

VU1GXT0.title: Transneuronal degeneration
VU1GXT0.description: The death of a neuron as a result of loss of input from and/or disruption of output to another neuron.

eU1xXT0.title: Anterograde transneuronal degeneration
eU1xXT0.description: The death of a postsynpatic neuron as a result of a loss of input from its corresponding presynaptic neuron.

UU1bcT0.title: Preolivary sulcus
UU1bcT0.description: A groove that runs in a craniocaudal direction on the ventromedial surface of the medulla oblongata between the pyramid and the inferior olivary nucleus. The hypoglossal nerve emerges from the cranial portion of this sulcus.

2U1TcT0.title: Postolivary sulcus
2U1TcT0.description: A groove that runs in a craniocaudal direction on the ventrolateral surface of the medulla oblongata. Formed by the lateral eminence of the inferior olivary nucleus. The rootlets of the glossopharyngeal nerve, vagus nerve, and accessory nerve emerge from this sulcus from a cranial to caudal direction

fU1kcT0.title: Antivenom
fU1kcT0.description: An agent used to neutralize venoms and treat toxic envenomations (e.g., snake bites). Typically consists of a mixture of immune globulins derived from the serum of animals immunized against a particular venom.

TU16cT0.title: Gnathostomiasis
TU16cT0.description: A food-borne zoonotic disease caused by the migration of Gnathostoma third-stage larvae in human tissue. Endemic to Asia, South America, and Central America. Transmitted primarily via ingestion of raw or undercooked intermediate hosts (e.g., frogs, birds, freshwater fish). Manifestations include eosinophilia and intermittent, migratory subcutaneous swelling.

gU1FcT0.title: Gray (unit)
gU1FcT0.description: The international system unit of radiation dosage. Expressed as the amount of energy absorbed per mass of tissue (e.g., joule/kilogram).

hU1c1T0.title: Symptoms of bradycardia
hU1c1T0.description: A group of symptoms that can develop when the heart rate is too slow to maintain sufficient cardiac output, leading to reduced organ perfusion. Symptoms are nonspecific and include fatigue and exercise intolerance, symptoms of cerebral hypoperfusion (presyncope, syncope, dizziness), symptoms of cardiovascular hypoperfusion (dyspnea on exertion, angina), and symptoms of renal hypoperfusion (oliguria).

3U1S1T0.title: Pan cultures
3U1S1T0.description: The collection of microbiological culture samples from multiple potential sources in search of an organism responsible for a patient's infection. Usually includes at least two blood cultures, a urine culture, and a sputum culture, although more samples may be included based on clinical judgment.

RU1l1T0.title: Otosyphilis
RU1l1T0.description: A manifestation of syphilis infection affecting the cochleovestibular system that can result in permanent hearing loss. Can occur at any stage of infection, with or without additional neurologic involvement (i.e., neurosyphilis or ocular syphilis). Common symptoms include tinnitus, vertigo, and sensorineural hearing loss (unilateral or bilateral).

iU1J1T0.title: Thermoregulation
iU1J1T0.description: The process by which the body maintains a consistent core body temperature despite variations in environmental temperature. Facilitated by changes in metabolic activity and sweating.

QU1u1T0.title: Type Ia sensory fiber
QU1u1T0.description: A type of afferent sensory neuron that innervates muscle spindles and responds to changes in muscle length and the velocity of muscle length changes.

jU1_1T0.title: Type Ib sensory fiber
jU1_1T0.description: A type of afferent sensory nerve fiber that innervates the Golgi tendon organs and responds to changes in muscle tension.

PU1WWT0.title: Type II sensory fiber
PU1WWT0.description: A type of afferent sensory neuron that innervates muscle spindles and responds only to changes in muscle length.

4U13WT0.title: Fexinidazole
4U13WT0.description: An oral antiparasitic medication used as monotherapy to treat both stages I and II of T. cruzi gambiense infection. Its mechanism of action is not fully understood but may involve activation by nitroreductase and subsequent generation of reactive oxygen species that damage parasite DNA.

kU1mWT0.title: LAD
kU1mWT0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to: 
1. Left anterior descending artery
2. Left axis deviation
3. Leukocyte adhesion deficiency
4. Lymphadenopathy

OU1IWT0.title: Central venous oxygen saturation
OU1IWT0.description: The venous oxygen saturation sampled from the tip of a central venous catheter near the right side of the heart, which reflects blood mostly from the superior vena cava (SVC) and less from the inferior vena cava (IVC). Used as a surrogate marker of oxygen delivery and consumption in tissues, and can estimate cardiac output. Not to be confused with mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO₂), which is sampled more distally and reflects a mixture of blood from the SVC, IVC, and the coronary sinus.

lU1vWT0.title: Indole test
lU1vWT0.description: A biochemical identification test that is used to identify if an organism can convert tryptophan into indole. Can be used to differentiate between different members of the Enterobacteriaceae family. E. coli is indole-positive; Klebsiella and Enterobacter are indole-negative.

5U1idT0.title: Macronutrient
5U1idT0.description: Chemical substances consumed in large amounts that provide bodily energy, among other purposes. There are three main classes: carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.

MU1MdT0.title: Focal neurological deficit
MU1MdT0.description: A clinical symptom or sign that indicates injury to a specific anatomical region of the nervous system (e.g., nerve, spinal cord, brain). Examples include hemiplegia, lateralized facial weakness, focal sensory deficits, and dysfunction of speech, vision, and hearing.

nU17dT0.title: CRC
nU17dT0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Colorectal carcinoma
2. Corrected reticulocyte count

LU1wdT0.title: Blastocystis
LU1wdT0.description: A genus of anaerobic protozoa that may be a commensal organism or a true pathogen that causes gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g., diarrhea, nausea, cramping). Can be seen on light microscopy of stool specimens.

oU10VT0.title: Fracture Risk Assessment Tool
oU10VT0.description: A clinical tool used to estimate the 10-year probability of developing a major osteoporotic fracture (e.g., hip, spine, shoulder, forearm) in patients aged between 40 and 90 years of age who are not undergoing treatment for osteoporosis.

KU1UVT0.title: Suppurative granuloma
KU1UVT0.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by an irregularly-shaped (e.g., stellate) granuloma with central abscess and/or microabscess formation. It is a characteristic of several infectious conditions, including cat scratch disease, lymphogranuloma venereum, and tularemia. Not typically seen in patients with sarcoidosis.

6U1jVT0.title: Dicoumarol
6U1jVT0.description: A naturally-occurring anticoagulant that competitively inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase, which results in the depletion of active vitamin K in the blood. Prevents the formation of prothrombin and, therefore, inhibits blood clotting.

pU1LVT0.title: Exotoxin A
pU1LVT0.description:
A term that can refer to:
1) Pseudomonas exotoxin A
2) Streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxin A
3) Clostridioides difficile exotoxin A

7U14eT0.title: Lucid interval
7U14eT0.description: A temporary period of relatively normal neurologic, cognitive, and/or behavioral function in a patient with an underlying neurologic or psychiatric condition. In patients with a traumatic brain injury (e.g., epidural hematoma), a lucid interval may precede the onset or worsening of neurologic dysfunction. In patients with a psychiatric condition (e.g., dementia), a lucid interval reflects a temporary return of normal or near-normal cognition or behavior.

GU1BeT0.title: Primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
GU1BeT0.description: A rare hereditary disorder characterized by symmetrical hyperostosis of long bones, digital clubbing, skin thickening, and hyperhidrosis. Most commonly caused by an autosomal recessive mutation in the 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase (HPGD) gene, which is involved in the breakdown of prostaglandin E2 in the lungs.

FU1gUT0.title: Endolymphatic sac tumor
FU1gUT0.description: A rare neuroectodermal tumor that arises from the dorsal aspect of the petrous part of the temporal bone. Typical manifestations include hearing loss, tinnitus, and vertigo. Most often associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease.

8U1OUT0.title: Schwannomatosis
8U1OUT0.description: A rare genetic disorder characterized by the presence of multiple schwannomas (nerve sheath tumors) without the involvement of the vestibular nerve. Typically associated with pain, paraesthesia, and weakness.

DU112T0.title: Succenturiate placenta
DU112T0.description: A variation of placental morphology characterized by one or more accessory lobes that develop separate from the main placental body. Risk factors include advanced maternal age and in vitro fertilization. Can increase the risk of retained placental tissue and placenta previa.

wU1h2T0.title: Nixtamalization
wU1h2T0.description: A process in which grain is soaked and cooked in an alkaline solution. When corn is nixtamalized, niacytin, which is nutritionally unavailable because it is bound to hemicellulose, becomes absorbable by the gastrointestinal tract. Nixtamalization can also decrease aflatoxin toxin contamination.

9U1N2T0.title: Coproantigen
9U1N2T0.description: An antigen found in feces. Tests to detect various coproantigens can be performed to diagnose infectious and/or intestinal conditions (e.g., amoebiasis, bacterial gastroenteritis, viral gastroenteritis).

CU1q2T0.title: Kynurenine pathway
CU1q2T0.description: A metabolic pathway in which niacin (vitamin B₃) is synthesized from tryptophan. Occurs primarily in the liver. Uses vitamin B₂ (riboflavin) and vitamin B₆ (pyridoxine) as cofactors. Deficiencies of enzymes involved in this pathway are a rare cause of pellagra. Increased production of metabolites from this pathway (e.g., kynurenic acid, quinolinic acid) is implicated in the pathogenesis of some inflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.

xU1E2T0.title: Leptomeninges
xU1E2T0.description: The inner two layers of the meninges (i.e., arachnoid mater and pia mater). Can be a site of metastasis in patients with cancer.

BU1z2T0.title: Limbic encephalitis
BU1z2T0.description: An autoimmune inflammation of the limbic system. Most commonly caused by immune reactions to an underlying malignancy but can also be caused by infections and systemic autoimmune conditions. Manifestations include memory impairment, seizures, confusion, and psychiatric symptoms (e.g., depression, hallucinations).

AU1RfT0.title: Bone turnover
AU1RfT0.description: A physiologic process in which osseous tissue is resorbed and reformed over time for bone remodeling and calcium and phosphate homeostasis. A high bone turnover rate (e.g., due to Paget disease, hyperparathyroidism, or thyrotoxicosis) results in weak woven bone.

zU1rfT0.title: Waiter's tip posture
zU1rfT0.description: A pathologic posture characterized by the arm held in adduction and internal rotation with an extended forearm and a flexed wrist. It is the typical posture caused by Erb palsy (due to muscle weakness in the C5 and C6 myotomes).

destinations.label: Peripheral nerve injuries → Nerve injuries in the upper body

media.title: Waiter's tip deformity in Erb palsy

-U1DfT0.title: Brain window
-U1DfT0.description: The computed tomography parameters that are used to optimally visualize tissue with density similar to brain tissue. A typical brain window is a width of 80 Hounsfield units and a length of 40 Hounsfield units. Can be used to evaluate for brain parenchymal lesions (e.g., atrophy, intracranial bleed, tumor). Has limited ability to delineate skeletal abnormalities.

Z21ZTT0.title: Bone window
Z21ZTT0.description: The computed tomography parameters used to optimally visualize tissue with a density similar to that of bone. A typical bone window (for temporal bone) is a width of 2800 Hounsfield units and a length of 600 Hounsfield units. Can be used to evaluate for subtle fractures that may be missed on conventional radiography. Visualization of soft tissue structures is limited.

a21QTT0.title: Charlson comorbidity index
a21QTT0.description: A scoring system used to estimate 10-year survival in an individual with multiple medical comorbidities. Each comorbidity is given a score from 1‑6 based on type and severity. The patient's age is also taken into account.

Y21nTT0.title: Effacement of basal cisterns
Y21nTT0.description: A radiologic finding characterized by obliteration of the basal cisterns due to mass effect (e.g., due to cerebral edema, large intracranial hematoma, uncal herniation).

X219TT0.title: Typical AVNRT
X219TT0.description: A subtype of AVNRT where anterograde conduction occurs across the slow-conducting pathway and retrograde conduction occurs in the fast pathway.

c21agT0.title: Doege-Potter syndrome
c21agT0.description: A paraneoplastic syndrome associated with solitary fibrous tumors that is characterized by episodic hypoglycemia. Typically caused by overproduction of insulin-like growth factor-2.

1212gT0.title: Talc granulomatosis
1212gT0.description: A condition caused by intravenous use of medications intended for oral use, which often contain talc. Manifestations include pulmonary fibrosis, lung micronodules, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and emphysema.

W21PgT0.title: Paroxysmal tachycardia
W21PgT0.description: A type of tachyarrhythmia with an abrupt onset or offset. May recur suddenly, often without a clear inciting trigger.

d21ogT0.title: Aberrant conduction
d21ogT0.description: The conduction of a supraventricular myocardial impulse outside of the normal His-Purkinje system, typically resulting in a wide QRS complex on ECG. Can be caused by underlying bundle branch blocks, conduction delays, and, according to some definitions, accessory pathways.

V21GgT0.title: Cerebral contusion
V21GgT0.description: A focal, traumatic brain injury that can vary in severity from a bruise and edema to hemorrhage and necrosis.

e21xgT0.title: Chloroquine
e21xgT0.description: An antimalarial drug whose mechanism of action is not fully understood but is thought to involve interference of parasite lysosome function. Also used as an antirheumatoid drug because it decreases the immune response against autoantigenic peptides. Has been investigated as an antiviral drug for COVID-19 based on mechanisms that are not fully understood.

U21bST0.title: Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine
U21bST0.description: Drugs derived from 4-aminoquinoline. Both are used as antimalarial blood schizonticides. Hydroxychloroquine is also frequently used as an antirheumatic or to treat lupus flares. Retinal toxicity is a serious adverse effect associated with their use.

221TST0.title: Hydroxychloroquine
221TST0.description: An antimalarial drug with a mechanism of action that is not fully understood but is thought to involve interference of parasite lysosome function. Widely used in the treatment of autoimmune diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus and rheumatoid arthritis) because it decreases complement-dependent antigen-antibody reactions. Has been investigated as an antiviral drug for COVID-19 based on immunomodulatory mechanisms that are not fully understood.

T216ST0.title: Atypical AVNRT
T216ST0.description: A subtype of AVNRT where anterograde conduction occurs across the fast-conducting pathway and retrograde conduction occurs in the slow-conducting pathway.

h21chT0.title: Crude rate
h21chT0.description: A measure of frequency calculated by dividing the total number of cases in a specific time period by the total number of people in the population. Does not account for specific population characteristics.

321ShT0.title: Specific rates
321ShT0.description: A measure of frequency that accounts for a specific characteristic of a subgroup within the population (e.g., sex-specific, age-specific).

R21lhT0.title: Standardized rates
R21lhT0.description: A type of crude rate that has been adjusted to consider specific population characteristics to facilitate comparison between groups. Often used to report death rates.

i21JhT0.title: Reverse causality
i21JhT0.description: The presence of an association between cause and effect that is different than common presumption. Can also describe an association with a two-way causal relationship. For example, exposure to pollution can increase the risk of developing asthma; chronic medical conditions can impact socioeconomic status and increase the risk of exposure to pollution.

P21W3T0.title: Temporality
P21W3T0.description: A criterion used to help establish causality in epidemiologic studies. Characterized by the observation of an effect after a given cause (e.g., surgical site infection that develops occurs after incision of the skin).

k21m3T0.title: Reproducibility
k21m3T0.description: A criterion used to help establish causality in epidemiologic studies. The evidence for a causal relationship increases when similar findings are observed in different studies held in different places with different sample sizes.

O21I3T0.title: Biologic plausibility
O21I3T0.description: A criterion used to help establish causality in epidemiologic studies. Describes the presence of well-established biological theories that can explain the relationship between a proposed exposure and outcome.

l21v3T0.title: Coherence (epidemiology)
l21v3T0.description: A criterion used to help establish causality in epidemiologic studies. Describes the concordance between new evidence that supports a proposed relationship and previously established evidence. A proposed relationship between an exposure and an outcome should not contradiction prior established knowledge about the exposure and/or outcome.

N21-3T0.title: Experimental evidence
N21-3T0.description: A criterion used to help establish causality in epidemiologic studies. Describes the data drawn from experimental manipulation (e.g., changes in disease prevalence after the initiation of an intervention).

m21VRT0.title: Analogy (epidemiology)
m21VRT0.description: A criterion used to help establish causality in epidemiologic studies. Describes a situation in which there is strong evidence of a causal relationship beteween an exposure and an outcome, and this evidence is used to support a causal relationship between another similar exposure and/or another similar outcome.

521iRT0.title: CBD
521iRT0.description:
An abbreviation that may refer to: 
1. Common bile duct
2. Cannabidiol
3. Corticobasal degeneration

M21MRT0.title: Accelerated atrioventricular junctional rhythm
M21MRT0.description: A slower form of junctional tachycardia with heart rates of ~ 60-100 beats/min. Classically associated with digoxin toxicity.

L21wRT0.title: Paroxysmal junctional tachycardia
L21wRT0.description: A subtype of junctional tachycardia characterized by a sudden-onset rapid tachyarrhythmia (heart rate > 100 beats/minute). May be seen in patients with myocardial ischemia or transiently during slow pathway ablation in AVNRT. Most commonly seen in infants after cardiac surgery or with congenital heart disease (junctional ectopic tachycardia).

J21siT0.title: Conjunctivitis-otitis syndrome
J21siT0.description: A condition characterized by concurrent purulent conjunctivitis and acute otitis media. Most commonly associated with Haemophilus influenzae infection (approx. 80% of cases).

7214QT0.title: Reduviidae
7214QT0.description: An insect family that contains the Triatominae subfamily, which is a vector of Chagas disease.

s21tQT0.title: Urine protein/creatinine ratio
s21tQT0.description: The ratio of total protein to total creatinine in the urine. The ratio obtained from a single urinary sample (i.e., a spot urine) can be used to estimate 24-hour protein excretion (e.g., a spot ratio of 3000 mg/g can be used to estimate proteinuria of approx. 3.5 g/24 hours).

G21BQT0.title: Acid-fast stain
G21BQT0.description: A staining technique that can be used to identify organisms that have high mycolic acid content (e.g., Mycobacteria, Nocardia). Stained organisms are considered acid-fast. Examples of acid-fast stains include the Ziehl-Neelsen stain and the auramine-rhodamine stain.

t21XjT0.title: CT angiographic spot sign
t21XjT0.description: A computed tomography finding characterized by a localized area of contrast enhancement within an acute intracerebral hemorrhage that is not visible on precontrast imaging. Indicates active bleeding and potential hematoma expansion.

media.title: Spot sign in active intracerebral hemorrhage

F21gjT0.title: DBP
F21gjT0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Diastolic blood pressure
2. Vitamin D-binding protein
3. D site of albumin promoter (albumin D-box) binding protein

821OjT0.title: Late term infant
821OjT0.description: A child delivered between 41 0/7 weeks and 41 6/7 weeks of gestation.

v21AjT0.title: Severe traumatic brain injury
v21AjT0.description: A traumatic brain injury associated with a Glasgow coma scale score of ≤ 8 points. It is often an indication for endotracheal intubation.

D211PT0.title: Moderate traumatic brain injury
D211PT0.description: A traumatic brain injury associated with a Glasgow coma scale score between 9–12 points.

w21hPT0.title: Retinaldehyde
w21hPT0.description: A form of vitamin A that is a component of rhodopsin in the human eye. Involved in the signaling cascade that converts light photons into electrical impulses in the retina, which facilitates the perception of visual stimuli by the human brain.

921NPT0.title: Health care-associated infection
921NPT0.description: An infection acquired after receiving health care in any setting (including a hospital, long-term care facility, nursing home, ambulatory care clinic, or home care) or after a surgical procedure or placement of an indwelling device. More likely to be caused by multidrug-resistant organisms than community-acquired infections.

C21qPT0.title: Neurogenic fever
C21qPT0.description: A fever of noninfectious etiology in a patient with an acute neurologic condition (e.g., stroke, traumatic brain injury). Thought to be caused by injury to the hypothalamic temperature regulatory center.

destinations.label: Secondary brain injury and neuroprotective measures → Neurogenic fever and targeted temperature management

x21EPT0.title: Symptomatic cholelithiasis
x21EPT0.description: A condition of gallstone disease associated with symptoms (e.g., dyspepsia, flatulence, abdominal pain, fever) and/or complications attributed to gallstone disease (e.g., cholecystitis, cholangitis, choledocholithiasis, biliary pancreatitis).

B21zPT0.title: 3-minute walk test
B21zPT0.description: A clinical decision support tool used to assess patients with acute exacerbations of COPD in the emergency department and to determine who can be safely discharged home.

destinations.label: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease → Disposition

y21d4T0.title: RP interval
y21d4T0.description: The interval between the QRS complex and the following P wave on an ECG. Used in the classification of certain subtypes of tachyarrhythmias.

A21R4T0.title: Acute CNS insult
A21R4T0.description: A term used to depict an acute injury to the brain and/or spinal cord. Examples include hemorrhagic stroke, ischemic stroke, traumatic brain injury, and traumatic spinal cord injury.

_2154T0.title: Targeted temperature management
_2154T0.description: The controlled maintenance of a target body temperature, which is used to prevent or minimize secondary brain injury in patients with cardiac arrest or acute CNS insults.

destinations.label: Secondary brain injury and neuroprotective measures → Neurogenic fever and targeted temperature management

af1QkT0.title: Euglycemia
af1QkT0.description: A state in which the serum has a normal glucose concentration (e.g., 70-110 mg/dL when fasting; 140-199 mg/dL after a two-hour plasma glucose value during a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test).

bf1HkT0.title: Somatoparaphrenia
bf1HkT0.description: A delusion characterized by the belief that one's limb (most commonly the left arm) does not belong to one's body. Often associated with somatosensory disturbances and unilateral spatial neglect.

Xf19kT0.title: Asomatognosia
Xf19kT0.description: A sensation that parts of the body are missing. May be associated with with damage to the right premotor cortex.

1f12OT0.title: Poland syndrome
1f12OT0.description: A condition characterized by unilateral aplasia or hypoplasia of the pectoralis muscles and breast with associated finger abnormalities (e.g., brachysyndactyly). Most commonly develops on the right side.

destinations.label: Overview of common breast conditions → Disorders of breast development

Wf1POT0.title: Uterine incarceration
Wf1POT0.description: A rare complication of pregnancy characterized by trapping of the uterus between the sacral promontory and the pubic symphysis. Risk factors include persistent retroflexion of the uterus, uterine adhesions, and fibroids. Most commonly results in abdominal, suprapubic, or back pain and urinary symptoms (e.g., dysuria, frequency) around 14-16 weeks' gestation.

df1oOT0.title: Connective tissue growth factor
df1oOT0.description: A cystein-rich extracellular protein that regulates angiogenesis and intercellular signaling for proliferation, differentiation, and cell adhesion. Also promotes fibrosis during wound healing.

Vf1GOT0.title: Tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases
Vf1GOT0.description: A group of enzymes that inhibit metalloproteinases, which results in decreased breakdown of extracellular matrix.

2f1TlT0.title: Primary teeth
2f1TlT0.description: The first set of teeth, which develops between the sixth week in utero through late adolescence. Consists of 20 teeth in total: a central incisor, lateral incisor, canine, first molar, and secondary molar in each quadrant of the mouth.

ff1klT0.title: Permanent teeth
ff1klT0.description: The second set of teeth, which typically develops starting around 6 years of age as the primary teeth begin to shed. Consists of 6 maxillary molars, 6 mandibular molars, 4 maxillary premolars, 4 mandibular premolars, 2 maxillary canines, 2 mandibular canines, 4 maxillary incisors, and 4 mandibular incisors.

Tf16lT0.title: Intracranial hemorrhage
Tf16lT0.description: A condition of bleeding within the skull. Etiologies include traumatic brain injury and nontraumatic causes (e.g., hemorrhagic stroke, ruptured aneurysm, hypertensive vasculopathy). Manifestations include headache, vomiting, and altered mental status.

gf1FlT0.title: Core ischemic zone
gf1FlT0.description: An area of potentially irreversible brain tissue injury characterized by neuronal and glial necrosis from severe ischemia due to stroke.

Sf1ylT0.title: Ischemic penumbra
Sf1ylT0.description: An area of potentially reversible brain tissue injury caused by hypoperfusion due to stroke. Tissue in the penumbra can recover after an ischemic event due to collateral artery supply and/or reperfusion therapy (e.g., thrombolysis, thrombectomy).

3f1SNT0.title: Pale infarct
3f1SNT0.description: The development of tissue death as a result of inadequate perfusion. Commonly caused by arterial occlusion and predominantly affects solid organs with single blood supply (e.g., heart, kidney, spleen). Characterized by the absence of hemorrhage and red blood cell accumulation (in contrast to hemorrhagic infarct).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Ischemia

Rf1lNT0.title: Bcl-2 homologous antagonist/killer protein
Rf1lNT0.description: A protein of the bcl-2 family that serves as a proapoptotic regulator of the intrinsic pathway of apoptosis. Dysregulation of Bak protein is suspected to play a role in carcinogenesis.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Apoptosis

if1JNT0.title: Bcl-2-associated death promoter
if1JNT0.description: A protein of the bcl-2 family that serves as a proapoptotic regulator of the intrinsic pathway of apoptosis. Inhibits antiapoptotic proteins such as bcl-2 and bcl-xL, thereby facilitating the activation of the Bax/Bad complex and promoting apoptosis.

Qf1uNT0.title: B-cell lymphoma-extra large protein
Qf1uNT0.description: An antiapoptotic protein that belongs to the Bcl-2 family of proteins. Inhibits the intrinsic pathway of apoptosis by maintaining the integrity of the mitochondrial membrane, which prevents the release of cytochrome c and inhibits the initiation of apoptosis.

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Apoptosis

jf1_NT0.title: Pyroptosis
jf1_NT0.description: A highly inflammatory form of apoptosis triggered by a cytosolic multiprotein oligomere called the inflammasome (also known as pyroptosome). Promotes the elimination of various pathogens through a signaling cascade that results in the maturation, activation, and release of proinflammatory cytokines and pore-forming proteins.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Acute local inflammation

Pf1WmT0.title: Bleeding type disseminated intravascular coagulation
Pf1WmT0.description: A type of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) characterized by a predominance of mild to moderate bleeding (e.g., petechiae, hematuria, oozing from IV sites) due to enhanced fibrinolysis. Associated with underlying leukemia, obstetric disease, and aortic aneurysms.

4f13mT0.title: Organ failure type disseminated intravascular coagulation
4f13mT0.description: A type of disseminated intravascular coagulation characterized by a predominance of organ dysfunction (e.g., liver dysfunction, pancreatitis) due to hypercoagulability, thrombosis, and suppression of fibrinolysis. Associated with underlying infections and sepsis.

kf1mmT0.title: Massive bleeding type disseminated intravascular coagulation
kf1mmT0.description: An overt type of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) characterized by severe, often life-threatening bleeding due to hyperfibrinolysis and consumption of platelets and coagulation factors through widespread microvascular thrombosis. Associated with obstetrical diseases and surgical complications.

Of1ImT0.title: Nonsymptomatic type disseminated intravascular coagulation
Of1ImT0.description: A latent type of disseminated intravascular coagulation characterized by little to no clinical symptoms, with laboratory abnormalities consistent with low-grade hyperfibrinolysis and/or hypercoagulability.

of10MT0.title: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy
of10MT0.description: A hereditary cardiomyopathy characterized by asymmetric left ventricular hypertrophy that leads to left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. Hypertrophy typically affects the septum and results in dynamic LVOT obstruction that varies with preload, afterload, and left ventricular inotropy. Can be asymptomatic or cause symptoms of myocardial ischemia, heart failure, syncope, and arrhythmias.

6f1jMT0.title: Fascia adherens
6f1jMT0.description: A ribbon-like structure found in the transversal sections of intercalated discs. Involved in the mechanical coupling of cardiomyocytes. Defects in the fascia adherens are implicated in the pathogenesis of cardiomyopathies and arrhythmias.

If1YnT0.title: Osimertinib
If1YnT0.description: A molecular targeted therapy that is an irreversible epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI). Used as a first-line treatment for metastatic, EGFR-positive, non-small cell lung cancer.

sf1tnT0.title: Fluid intelligence
sf1tnT0.description: The ability to reason, problem solve, and think abstractly in novel situations (without specific prior experience and/or knowledge).

Gf1BnT0.title: Crystallized intelligence
Gf1BnT0.description: The ability to remember and use previously acquired knowledge and experience.

Ff1gLT0.title: Palatopharyngeus
Ff1gLT0.description: A pharyngeal muscle that originates from the palatine aponeurosis and the hard palate and inserts into the posterior border of the thyroid cartilage. Innervated by the pharyngeal plexus. Elevates the pharynx and larynx during swallowing.

8f1OLT0.title: Erythema multiforme major
8f1OLT0.description: Erythema multiforme with moderate to severe mucosal involvement and extensive cutaneous lesions (e.g., typical target lesions) affecting < 10% of total body surface area. Systemic symptoms (e.g., fever, weakness, malaise) may be present.

uf1pLT0.title: Sublingual caruncle
uf1pLT0.description: A pair of papillae, each of which is located lateral to the lingual frenulum on the sublingual surface of the tongue and medial to the sublingual glands. It is the site where the submandibular and sublingual glands empty into the oral cavity.

Ef18LT0.title: Perfusion
Ef18LT0.description: The delivery of fluid to an organ or tissue. Typically refers to the delivery of blood but can also describe the delivery of lymph. Can be measured as the volume of fluid delivered to a specific mass of tissue over a specific period of time (e.g., mL/min/g).

Df11oT0.title: Peribronchial cuffing
Df11oT0.description: A radiological finding caused by inflammation, fluid, and mucus around the bronchi. It is described as haziness around bronchi that can be seen end-on (donut sign). This finding can be seen in many pulmonary conditions (e.g., asthma, cystic fibrosis, and bronchitis).

wf1hoT0.title: Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy
wf1hoT0.description: A benign, self-limited, pruritic, inflammatory condition that most commonly affects primiparous women in the third trimester of pregnancy or immediately postpartum. Clinical features include extremely pruritic, erythematous papules within abdominal striae. The lesions can spread to the chest, back, and extremities, and coalesce into urticarial plaques, sparing the face, palms, and soles.

destinations.label: Maternal complications during pregnancy → Pregnancy dermatoses

9f1NoT0.title: Moyamoya disease
9f1NoT0.description: A rare cerebrovascular disorder characterized by progressive stenosis and occlusion in the terminal part of the internal carotid arteries with the compensatory formation of tiny vessels. Manifestations include transient ischemic attacks, strokes, hemorrhage, and seizures.

xf1EoT0.title: Hyperleukocytosis
xf1EoT0.description: A leukocyte count > 100,000/mm³. Seen in patients with underlying leukemia (e.g., acute myelocytic leukemia, acute lymphocytic leukemia) and myeloproliferative disorders.

yf1dKT0.title: Chronification
yf1dKT0.description: The transition of acute, transient symptoms into chronic, more persistent ones.

Af1RKT0.title: Coinfection
Af1RKT0.description: The concurrent infection of a host by two or more separate pathogens. A coinfection can aggravate disease severity and/or duration (e.g., coinfection of hepatocytes with hepatitis B and hepatitis D virus).

_f15KT0.title: Superinfection
_f15KT0.description: A second infection that is superimposed on a previous one. Often caused by a different pathogen that is resistant to antimicrobials used to treat the previous infection.

zf1rKT0.title: Middlebrook medium
zf1rKT0.description: A growth medium that can be used to cultivate mycobacterial species (e.g., Mycobacterium tuberculosis).

-f1DKT0.title: Constructional apraxia
-f1DKT0.description: The inability to draw or assemble objects that consist of different parts. Can occur due to the damage to different areas of the brain, including those in the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes, in either hemisphere.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Appearance and behavior

ZT1Z6T0.title: Apraxia of lid opening
ZT1Z6T0.description: The inability to voluntarily open the eyes in the absence of levator palpebrae muscle palsy. Etiologies include neurodegenerative disorders (e.g., multiple system atrophy) and focal lesions that involve the medial frontal lobe or basal ganglia.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Appearance and behavior

0T1e6T0.title: Carrier (infectious disease)
0T1e6T0.description: An organism that hosts and transmits a pathogen that causes an infectious disease. The harboring organism itself is usually immune to the pathogen and/or is asymptomatic.

aT1Q6T0.title: Seroconversion
aT1Q6T0.description: The process during which an organism develops detectable antibodies against a specific pathogen.

YT1n6T0.title: WPW with atrial fibrillation
YT1n6T0.description: The presence of atrial fibrillation in patients with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. As impulses may be conducted through the bundle of Kent (in addition to the AV node), the heart rate is very high (frequently > 200/minute) and the ECG shows polymorphic, wide QRS complexes.

media.title: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome after conversion from atrial fibrillation (2/2)

cT1apT0.title: Hepatitis B preexposure prophylaxis
cT1apT0.description: A set of preventive measures that can be taken to prevent hepatitis B virus infection. Includes general lifestyle measures (e.g., practicing safe sex, not sharing drug needles), screening of blood products, and active hepatitis B immunization. Vaccination is recommended for all individuals.

1T12pT0.title: Sebaceous carcinoma
1T12pT0.description: A malignant tumor of the sebaceous glands. Rare; most commonly develops on the head (especially the eyelids) or neck as a nontender, round nodule. Commonly associated with Muir-Torre syndrome.

WT1PpT0.title: Modified Ashworth scale
WT1PpT0.description: A scale for assessing muscle tone. The grade ranges from 0 to 4, with 0 indicating no resistance to passive movements and 4 indicating flexor or extensor posture that cannot be overcome with passive movement. The modified scale contains an additional grade, 1+, which describes slight increase in muscle tone (a catch followed by minimal resistance through the remainder of the range of motion).

eT1xpT0.title: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia
eT1xpT0.description: A pediatric myeloproliferative disorder characterized by activating mutations of the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway that result in the presence of abnormal myelomonocytic cells in the peripheral blood and bone marrow. Can also infiltrate other tissues, resulting in hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy.

UT1bJT0.title: Psilocybin
UT1bJT0.description: An alkaloid compound found in Psilocybe mushrooms. Ingestion can result in euphoria, hallucinogenic effects, tachycardia, and mydriasis.

2T1TJT0.title: Colpocleisis
2T1TJT0.description: A surgical procedure in which the vagina is closed off or narrowed to provide more support for pelvic organs. Used to treat pelvic organ prolapse.

TT16JT0.title: Paratonia
TT16JT0.description: A form of hypertonia characterized by involuntary variable resistance during passive movement. The degree of resistance can depend on the speed of movement and/or the amount of force applied. Etiologies include anxiety, dementia, and lesions and degenerative disorders of the frontal lobe.

gT1FJT0.title: Oppositional paratonia
gT1FJT0.description: A form of paratonia in which a patient involuntarily resists passive movement during the assessment of tone.

ST1yJT0.title: Facilitatory paratonia
ST1yJT0.description: A form of paratonia in which a patient involuntarily assists passive movement during the assessment of tone.

hT1cqT0.title: Early goal-directed therapy
hT1cqT0.description: A therapeutic strategy to guide hemodynamic support of patients with sepsis, which includes monitoring the following resuscitation targets: mean arterial pressure (MAP), central venous pressure (CVP), and central venous oxygen saturation (ScvO₂).

3T1SqT0.title: Reinforcement maneuver
3T1SqT0.description: A physical examination technique used to reinforce stretch reflexes (e.g., knee and ankle reflexes). The patient clenches the teeth, interlocks the hands, and pulls the clenched hands to the sides. Typically results in more pronounced stretch reflexes.

RT1lqT0.title: Preexcitation pattern
RT1lqT0.description: A pattern on a resting ECG that suggests the presence of ventricular preexcitation through an accessory atrioventricular pathway (e.g., the bundle of Kent in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome). Can include a short PR interval, a wide QRS complex, and/or a slurred QRS upstroke (delta wave). The pattern can occur intermittently and is typically masked during preexcited tachyarrhythmias due to the rapid heart rate (often > 200/min).

iT1JqT0.title: Preexcitation syndrome
iT1JqT0.description: The clinical constellation of accessory pathway-related ventricular preexcitation and associated tachyarrhythmia (e.g., atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia, atrial flutter, atrial fibrillation). Resting ECG typically shows a preexcitation pattern, although this is often masked during preexcited tachycardia, which can show a heart rate > 200/min and a wide QRS complex.

lT1vIT0.title: Exemestane
lT1vIT0.description: An aromatase inhibitor that decreases estrogen production by inhibiting the conversion of androgens to estrogens. Used to treat postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

nT17rT0.title: Population attributable risk
nT17rT0.description: A measure of risk used to determine the proportion of incidence of a disease in the total population that is attributed to the exposure. Calculated as the difference beteween the incidence rate of the entire study population and the incidence rate in the unexposed group.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Estimates of population impact

oT107T0.title: Accordion sign
oT107T0.description: A radiologic finding that can be seen in contrast-enhanced imaging of edematous and inflamed large bowel. Characterized by alternating areas of low attenuation (from edematous haustra) and high attenuation (due to contrast material trapped between the thickened haustral folds). Can be seen in patients with pseudomembranous colitis due to C. difficile infeciton.

6T1j7T0.title: Electrophysiological examination
6T1j7T0.description: A procedure that assesses the function of nerve and muscle fibers and/or cells. Typically involves measurement and amplification of neuromuscular action potentials using a system of microelectrodes. Can have both diagnostic and therapeutic applications. Examples include electrophysiological studies, electromyography, and nerve conduction studies.

pT1L7T0.title: Antidromic AVRT
pT1L7T0.description: A type of atrioventricular reciprocating tachycardia where conduction of the reentry circuit is antegrade through the accessory pathway and retrograde through the AV node. The result is a wide QRS complex tachyarrhythmia, which may be indistinguishable from other regular wide-complex tachycardias on ECG appearance alone.

JT1s7T0.title: 5α-reductase
JT1s7T0.description: An enzyme that converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone. It is found in several tissues, including the testes, ovaries, and skin.

qT1C7T0.title: Antagonist
qT1C7T0.description: A molecule that binds to a receptor and prevent its activation.

IT1YHT0.title: Acidophil cell
IT1YHT0.description: A cell type of the anterior pituitary that stains well with acidic dyes (e.g., eosin). Includes somatotrophs (which secrete growth hormone) and lactotrophs (which secrete prolactin).

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamus and pituitary gland

7T14HT0.title: Basophilic cell
7T14HT0.description: A cell type of the anterior pituitary that stains well with basic dyes (e.g., haematoxylin). Includes corticotrophs (which secrete ACTH), thyrotrophs (which secrete TSH), and gonadotrophs (which secrete FSH and LH).

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamus and pituitary gland

sT1tHT0.title: Adolescent
sT1tHT0.description: A developmental period between middle childhood and adulthood. The precise age range varies depending on the source and extends from 10 to 24 years of age. This period is characterized by cognitive, physical, and psychosocial development.

GT1BHT0.title: Acute hepatitis B virus infection
GT1BHT0.description: A disease that occurs ≤ 6 months after an individual was exposed to HBV. In most cases, affected individuals develop subclinical hepatitis. Can be asymptomatic or cause nonspecific symptoms (e.g., fatigue, arthralgias, myalgias, fever), right upper quadrant pain, jaundice, hepatomegaly, and fulminant hepatitis.

tT1XsT0.title: Chronic hepatitis B virus infection
tT1XsT0.description: A hepatitis B virus Infection that lasts ≥ 6 months due to incomplete viral clearance. Most commonly affects infants and young children who were infected perinatally. Manifestations include liver failure, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma.

FT1gsT0.title: Men who have sex with men
FT1gsT0.description: A term used to describe male individuals who engage in sexual activity with other male individuals.

uT1psT0.title: Saccade
uT1psT0.description: A conjugate eye movement that shifts the point of fixation toward an object of interest.

ET18sT0.title: Tuberculoma
ET18sT0.description: A granuloma that forms from tubercles (scattered tuberculous foci), typically due to disseminated tuberculous disease. Most commonly develops in the brain but can form in the spinal cord.

vT1AsT0.title: Relaxed circular DNA
vT1AsT0.description: A special DNA structure associated with the hepatitis B viral capsid. Thought to be converted into covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) by host cell DNA repair mechanisms. Plays a role in the chronification of HBV infection.

DT11GT0.title: Urokinase
DT11GT0.description: An enzyme that promotes fibrinolytic pathways by catalyzing the conversion of plasminogen to plasmin. Found in plasma, urine, and other types of tissues. Can be used as a thrombolytic to treat patients with acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, or ischemic stroke.

wT1hGT0.title: Methyltestosterone
wT1hGT0.description: A methylated derivative of testosterone used to treat hypogonadism and delayed puberty and to promote anabolism after events associated with significant catabolism (e.g., burns, surgery, trauma).
