destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

9T1NGT0.title: Oxandrolone
9T1NGT0.description: A synthetic testosterone derivative used to promote anabolism after events associated with significant catabolism (e.g., burns, surgery, trauma).

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

CT1qGT0.title: Fluoxymesterone
CT1qGT0.description: A synthetic androgen used for replacement therapy in testosterone-deficient states and for treatment of metastatic breast cancer in postmenopausal women.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

xT1EGT0.title: Copper intrauterine device
xT1EGT0.description: A T-shaped copper device placed into uterus for contraception. Produces local inflammation that prevents implantation of an embryo. Can be used for emergency contraception if inserted within 120 hours of unprotected intercourse.

BT1zGT0.title: Anti-p40 antibody
BT1zGT0.description: An antibody against a p63 isoform, which is expressed in squamous cells. Can be used as an immunohistochemical marker to identify squamous cell carcinoma of the lung.

yT1dtT0.title: Tromner sign
yT1dtT0.description: A physical examination finding elicited by tapping the terminal phalanx of a relaxed finger (usually the middle finger) on the palmar side while holding the hand level with the proximal phalanges. A pathologic response is flexion of the terminal phalanx of the tapped finger and thumb or when flexion is asymmetrical when comparing the hands. Indicates an upper motor neuron lesion above the fifth or sixth cervical segment of the spinal cord.

AT1RtT0.title: Hoffmann sign
AT1RtT0.description: A physical examination finding elicited by flicking the nail of the patient's middle finger downward while loosely holding the remainder of hand, allowing the fingernail to move upward reflexively. A pathologic response is a quick flexion and adduction of the thumb and/or index finger of the same hand.

_T15tT0.title: Oppenheim sign
_T15tT0.description: An upper motor neuron sign characterized by extension of the hallux and fanning of the other toes upon scratching along the crest of the tibia.

zT1rtT0.title: Schaeffer sign
zT1rtT0.description: An upper motor neuron sign characterized by toe extension and fanning of the toes upon compression of the Achilles tendon.

-T1DtT0.title: Reference interval
-T1DtT0.description: A range of values from the lower limit of normal to the upper limit of normal (as typically observed in 95% of the healthy population).

Zg1ZFT0.title: Soleal line
Zg1ZFT0.description: An oblique line on the posterior surface of the proximal tibia that is the origin of the soleus muscle.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Muscles

0g1eFT0.title: Allergic shiner
0g1eFT0.description: The presence of edema and hyperpigmentation of the lower eyelid as a result of venous congestion. Associated with allergic rhinitis and conjunctivitis.

ag1QFT0.title: Fluorescent antibody stain
ag1QFT0.description: The use of fluorescent dyes in combination with immunoglobulin binding to identify specific biomolecules in a tissue sample. Includes direct immunofluorescence (in which immunoglobulin is conjugated with a fluorescent dye and added to tissue) and indirect immunofluorescence (in which immunoglobulin is added to tissue and antibody-antigen complexes are then labeled with a fluorescent antibody).

Yg1nFT0.title: Factor VII deficiency
Yg1nFT0.description: An autosomal recessive bleeding disorder caused by mutation of the F7 gene, which leads to deficiency and/or dysfunction of coagulation factor VII. Clinical manifestations are highly variable and range from asymptomatic disease to life-threatening bleeding after minor trauma. Associated with a normal aPTT and a prolonged PT.

cg1a8T0.title: Hemoglobin Zurich
cg1a8T0.description: An inherited disorder characterized by the presence of an abnormal form of hemoglobin in which the distal histidine in the beta globin chain is replaced by arginine, which increases the ligand binding space around iron. Results in increased binding to carbon monoxide; the carboxyhemoglobn concentration is often more than 3% in affected individuals.

1g128T0.title: Mestranol
1g128T0.description: A synthetic estrogen derivative previously used in hormonal contraceptives. It has largely been replaced by ethinyl estradiol.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

Wg1P8T0.title: Ethinyl estradiol
Wg1P8T0.description: A synthetic estrogen used in combination with progestins for hormonal contraception and menopausal hormone therapy. Ethinyl estradiol-based contraceptives are available as pills, patches, and vaginal rings.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

dg1o8T0.title: Etonogestrel
dg1o8T0.description: A long-acting progestin used for contraception, either alone as a subdermal implant or in combination with estrogens as a vaginal ring.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

Vg1G8T0.title: Norethindrone
Vg1G8T0.description: A progestin derivative used for hormonal contraception either in combination with estrogens (as combined oral contraceptives) or alone (as progestin-only pills).

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

eg1x8T0.title: Phymatous changes
eg1x8T0.description: Cutaneous findings in rosacea of skin thickening, enlarged pores, and nodule formation due to underlying inflammation and overactive sebaceous glands. Lesions may or may not be actively inflamed. Often includes an enlarged, bulbous nose (rhinophyma). Previously classified as a subtype of rosacea.

Ug1buT0.title: Carbogen
Ug1buT0.description: A mixture of 5% CO₂ and 95% O₂ used in the treatment of central retinal artery occlusion.

fg1kuT0.title: Tinea barbae
fg1kuT0.description: A dermatophyte infection that affects bearded areas of the skin. Typically manifests with erythematous papules, patches, and pustules, and crusting around the hair (kerion-like plaques).

Tg16uT0.title: Tinea faciei
Tg16uT0.description: A dermatophyte infection that affects the facial skin. Typically manifests with small, erythematous, scaly papules, plaques, and pustules.

gg1FuT0.title: Acquired von Willebrand disease
gg1FuT0.description: A deficiency of von Willebrand factor (vWF) that is secondary to underlying conditions, such as lymphoproliferative and myeloproliferative diseases (e.g., multiple myeloma, monoclonal gammopathies, lymphoma, essential thrombocythemia), autoimmune diseases (e.g., SLE), or cardiovascular defects. Typically results in a bleeding diathesis.

Sg1yuT0.title: Community-acquired infection
Sg1yuT0.description: An infection that is acquired in the general population and not within a health care setting (as opposed to a health care-associated infection). CAI requires that infectious symptoms develop prior to or within 48 hours of presentation to a hospital and more than 30 days after receiving health care in any setting.

3g1SET0.title: Pneumatic otoscopy
3g1SET0.description: A physical examination technique that uses a pneumatic bulb attached to an otoscope to test tympanic membrane mobility. Normally, the tympanic membrane moves easily upon exerted pressure. Impaired mobility may indicate effusion or a nonintact TM.

Rg1lET0.title: Antitoxin active antibiotics
Rg1lET0.description: A group of antibiotics that inhibit the synthesis of certain bacterial toxins. This inhibition can also modulate the host's immune response, which is thought to be beneficial in conditions like toxic shock syndrome. Examples include lincosamides and oxazolidinones.

ig1JET0.title: Comedone
ig1JET0.description: A skin-colored papule that forms when pilosebaceous ducts become blocked with keratinaceous debris and sebum (e.g., due to acne vulgaris). Subtypes include closed comedones (whiteheads) and open comedones (blackheads).

jg1_ET0.title: Enzymatic fat necrosis
jg1_ET0.description: A death of adipose tissue due to release of lipases and amylases from the pancreatic cells (e.g., due to pancreatitis).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Necrosis

Pg1WvT0.title: Tall man lettering
Pg1WvT0.description: A technique used to prevent medication errors by differentiating look alike drugs by capitalizing the dissimilar letters (e.g., buPROPion vs. busPIRone)

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medication errors

kg1mvT0.title: Diffusion
kg1mvT0.description: The spontaneous movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration (e.g., oxygen across the alveolocapillary membrane down the concentration gradient).

lg1vvT0.title: Alpha granule
lg1vvT0.description: A secretory granule found in the cytoplasm of platelets and megakaryocytes. Contains a large variety of proteins, including von Willebrand factor, plasma proteins, coagulation factors, and protease inhibitors, which are released upon platelet activation.

Ng1-vT0.title: Enophthalmos
Ng1-vT0.description: A posterior displacement of the eye within the orbit. Can be caused by orbital floor fracture with subsequent prolapse of tissue toward the maxillary sinus.

mg1VDT0.title: Infraorbital nerve
mg1VDT0.description: A branch of the maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve that gives off the posterior superior alveolar nerve, middle superior alveolar nerve, and anterior superior alveolar nerve. Can be injured by an orbital blowout fracture.

5g1iDT0.title: Acidiophilic
5g1iDT0.description: A histopathologic descriptor for a substance with high affinity for acidic dyes (e.g., eosin), which results in red coloration.

Mg1MDT0.title: Bile acid diarrhea
Mg1MDT0.description: A condition characterized by increased colonic secretion and motility secondary to an increased concentration of bile acid within the colon. Causes of increased colonic bile acid concentration include biliary-enteric fistula, postcholecystectomy, and decreased bile acid reabsorption in the ileum (e.g., due to ileal resection).

ng17DT0.title: Facultative intracellular bacteria
ng17DT0.description: A group of bacteria that typically replicate within host cells but can also replicate in the external environment. Includes Salmonella spp., Francisella spp, Yersinia spp., Legionella pneumophila, and Listeria monocytogenes.

Lg1wDT0.title: vanA gene
Lg1wDT0.description: The most common bacterial gene that confers resistance to vancomycin. Encodes a ligase that catalyzes the binding of D-alanine to D-lactate, which leads to the formation of D-alanyl-D-lactate.

destinations.label: Multidrug-resistant organism infections → Common gram-positive bacteria

og10wT0.title: Platelet activation
og10wT0.description: A component of platelet plug formation in primary hemostasis that follows platelet adhesion. Involves platelet shape change and secreation of mediators that further increase platelet activation and aggregation. Platelet activators include collagen, ADP, and thrombin.

Kg1UwT0.title: Plasminogen
Kg1UwT0.description: The inactivate precursor of plasmin. Activated by tissue plasminogen activator (tPA), urokinase, and many fibrinolytic drugs via proteolytic cleavage.

6g1jwT0.title: Charge-coupled device camera
6g1jwT0.description: A camera that contains a light-sensitive silicon chip that is able to convert photons into digital signals. Produces images that are sensitive to high-energy radiation, heat, and light. Used in Western blot imaging.

Jg1swT0.title: Secondary survey
Jg1swT0.description: An assessment of critically ill or injured patients if they are considered stable after a primary survey. Includes a focused history, more thorough physical examination than the primary survey, and select diagnostic studies (e.g., imaging). Can detect commonly missed injuries (e.g., aortic, rectal, and ureteral injuries).

destinations.label: Management of trauma patients → Secondary survey

qg1CwT0.title: Supraglottic airway device
qg1CwT0.description: A group of devices placed via the oropharynx to facilitate ventilation from above the glottis. Can be inserted by providers who are not trained in advanced airway skills or can be used by trained providers for rescue ventilation (e.g., if facemask ventilation is not possible). Includes laryngeal mask airways and laryngeal tube airways.

Ig1Y9T0.title: Bridging necrosis
Ig1Y9T0.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by necrotic tissue that links vascular structures. Can be seen in patients with fulminant hepatitis, in which hepatocyte necrosis can link blood vessels in the liver (i.e., portal bridging necrosis).

rg1f9T0.title: Blast injury
rg1f9T0.description: A complex type of trauma caused by exposure to an explosion. Can result in injuries due to high pressure (e.g., tympanic membrane rupture, blast lung), blunt and penetrating force (e.g., fractures, flying debris), and explosive products (e.g., toxic fumes, burns).

7g149T0.title: Aortic valve area
7g149T0.description: The opening area of the aortic valve measured during systole. An important factor in the evaluation of severity of aortic valve stenosis. An AVA between 3.0-4.0 cm² is considered normal, while an AVA < 1.0 cm² constitutes severe stenosis.

Hg1K9T0.title: Myeloschisis
Hg1K9T0.description: A severe form of open spinal dysraphism caused by the complete failure of portions of the neural tube to fuse, which results in the development of bare, exposed neural tissue without coverage of meninges, bones, or skin. Affected individuals have varying degrees of spinal cord dysfunction symptoms. Associated with elevated AFP in prenatal screening.

tg1XCT0.title: Testolactone
tg1XCT0.description: An aromatase inhibitor that prevents the conversion of androstenedione to estrone and testosterone to estrogen. Can be used to treat estrogen-promoted breast cancer in postmenopausal women and to slow the progression of precocious pseudopuberty in children.

Fg1gCT0.title: Antianginal drugs
Fg1gCT0.description: A class of drugs that help relieve angina (chest pain caused by myocardial ischemia). Includes nitrates, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, and ranolazine.

8g1OCT0.title: Active management of the third stage of labor
8g1OCT0.description: An approach to the management of the third stage of labor aimed to prevent postpartum hemorrhage. Includes administration of uterotonic medications, controlled umbilical cord traction, and massage of the uterine fundus after delivery of the placenta.

ug1pCT0.title: Depressed skull fracture
ug1pCT0.description: A skull fracture in which the skull depresses inward toward the brain parenchyma. Typically occurs secondary to a high-energy blunt force injury to the skull. The parietal and frontoparietal regions are the most common sites of depressed skull fractures.

Eg18CT0.title: Skull fracture
Eg18CT0.description: A fracture of the skull (e.g., due to trauma). Can be further subdivided by anatomical region, degree of displacement (e.g., undisplaced or depressed (5-10 mm), and number of fracture fragments (e.g., comminuted fracture).

media.title: Anterior and posterior fat pad signs in supracondylar fracture
Cranial vault fracture with epidural hematoma

vg1ACT0.title: Neuroimaging
vg1ACT0.description: The use of radiologic techniques (e.g., computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, positron emission tomography) to view structures of the nervous system (e.g., brain, spinal cord). Further subdivided into structural imaging (i.e., visualization of gross structures) and functional imaging (i.e., visualization of changes in blood flow related to nervous system activity).

Cg1qxT0.title: Liver synthetic function tests
Cg1qxT0.description: A group of laboratory tests that measure hepatocellular synthetic function. Most commonly includes albumin, bilirubin, and prothrombin time. Extrahepatic factors may influence test results.

xg1ExT0.title: Intra-axial lesion
xg1ExT0.description: A lesion within the parenchyma of the brain or spinal cord. Examples include an intraparenchymal bleed (e.g., intracerebral hemorrhage), cerebral tumors (e.g., glioblastoma, astrocytoma), spinal cord tumors (e.g., spinal ependymoma), and parenchymal infection of the central nervous system (e.g., brain abscess).

Bg1zxT0.title: Extra-axial lesion
Bg1zxT0.description: A central nervous system lesion that lies outside the parenchyma of the brain and spinal cord but within the cranium or vertebral column. Examples include meningeal bleeds (e.g., extradural hemorrhage, subdural hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage), meningeal tumors (e.g., meningioma, arachnoid cyst), extramedullary spinal tumors (e.g., schwannoma, glioma, meningioma), and meningeal infections (e.g., meningitis).

yg1dBT0.title: PAR
yg1dBT0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Population attributable risk
2. Pseudoautosomal region

Ag1RBT0.title: Elderly-onset rheumatoid arthritis
Ag1RBT0.description: A subtype of rheumatoid arthritis that manifests in individuals ≥ 60 years of age. Characterized by acute-onset arthritis, primarily of the large joints. Systemic manifestations (e.g., fever, myalgia, weight loss) are common. Affects both sexes equally.

_g15BT0.title: Palindromic rheumatism
_g15BT0.description: An autoinflammatory and autoimmune disorder characterized by relapsing episodes of joint pain, swelling, and stiffness that typically last 12–72 hours. Asymptomatic between episodes. Progresses to rheumatoid arthritis in > 60% of affected individuals. Progression to other autoimmune conditions (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjogren syndrome) may also occur.

zg1rBT0.title: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate
zg1rBT0.description: A nucleotide analog reverse-transcriptase inhibitor (NtRTI) used to treat chronic hepatitis B virus infection and HIV infection. Typically combined with other antiretroviral medications. Adverse effects include lactic acidosis, nephrotoxicity, and hepatotoxicity.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

-g1DBT0.title: TDF
-g1DBT0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Testis-determining factor
2. Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate

ZS1ZyT0.title: Tenofovir alafenamide
ZS1ZyT0.description: A nucleotide analog reverse-transcriptase inhibitor (NtRTI) used to treat chronic hepatitis B virus infection and HIV infection. It is a prodrug of tenofovir that is absorbed more quickly than tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF). Typically combined with other antiretroviral medications. Has less risk of nephrotoxicity and bone toxicity than TDF.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

0S1eyT0.title: Acid steatocrit
0S1eyT0.description: A laboratory test that assesses that fat content of a stool sample. Calculated by taking the volume of the fatty layer in a centrifuged sample and dividing it by the volume of the liquid-free solid fecal layer.

bS1HyT0.title: Precordial catch syndrome
bS1HyT0.description: An idiopathic pediatric condition that causes episodic, sharp chest pain that most commonly occurs during rest or with mild activity and worsens with inspiration.

cS1aAT0.title: Herniography
cS1aAT0.description: A fluoroscopic imaging technique for evaluating the inguinal and pelvic regions for hernias. Iodinated contrast is injected into the peritoneal cavity and enters the inguinal fossae while the patient performs Valsalva maneuvers in multiple positions to disperse the contrast material. Hernias are visualized as a radiopaque sac.

WS1PAT0.title: Sports hernia
WS1PAT0.description: A condition of chronic groin pain, assumed to be secondary to injury or weakness of the posterior wall of the inguinal canal. An actual hernia may or may not be present. This condition is typically seen in athletes.

eS1xAT0.title: Herniorrhaphy
eS1xAT0.description: A type of hernia repair in which sutures are used to close the abdominal wall defect without the use of a mesh. Most commonly used in small hernias and contaminated surgical fields. Herniorrhaphy is associated with a higher rate of hernia recurrence but a lower risk of infection than mesh repair (i.e., hernioplasty).

US1b_T0.title: Inguinodynia
US1b_T0.description: Chronic or recurrent pain in the groin. Common causes include inguinal hernia, nerve entrapment (e.g., following mesh repair of inguinal hernia due to scar tissue), and musculoskeletal pain.

2S1T_T0.title: Reduction en masse
2S1T_T0.description: A rare complication that occurs after manual reduction of an inguinal hernia (more commonly with indirect inguinal hernias), where a loop of bowel remains incarcerated and then becomes strangulated. Although the hernia may no longer be palpable on exam, the patient develops abdominal pain.

TS16_T0.title: Hypervigilance
TS16_T0.description: A state of heightened or exaggerated sensitivity and response to environmental stimuli. Can be seen in various anxiety disorders, including posttraumatic stress disorder

gS1F_T0.title: CD56
gS1F_T0.description: A neural cell adhesion molecule found on natural killer cells. Cells with intermediate levels of CD56 are responsible NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. Cells with high levels of CD56 produce cytokines but do not significantly mediate cytotoxicity.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Lymphoid cell line

SS1y_T0.title: Emprosthotonus
SS1y_T0.description: A spastic contraction of the abdominal muscles that results in anterior arching of the trunk.

hS1czT0.title: Orthotonus
hS1czT0.description: A spastic contracture characterized by rigid straightness of the body.

RS1lzT0.title: Plexopathy
RS1lzT0.description: A nerve disorder or injury that affects the brachial or lumbosacral plexus. Typically causes pain and motor or sensory deficits.

iS1JzT0.title: Pegylated interferon alfa
iS1JzT0.description: A recombinant interferon alpha with antiviral and antineoplastic properties that is conjugated with polyethylene glycol (PEG). Pegylation increases molecule size and leads to slower absorption, longer half-life, and decreased clearance rate to increase the duration of biologic activity. Used to treat chronic hepatitis C infection.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against hepatitis B and C

QS1uzT0.title: Medical expulsive therapy
QS1uzT0.description: A treatment for ureteral stones that uses various medications (e.g., alpha-blockers) to relax smooth muscle and facilitate stone passage.

jS1_zT0.title: Sinusoidal capillarization
jS1_zT0.description: A process in which liver sinusoidal endothelial cells lose their fenestrations and acquire a vascular phenotype. This transformation contributes to the development of fibrosis in patients with chronic liver disease, which compromises hepatocyte function and leads to liver failure.

4S13-T0.title: Clinical features of thyrotoxicosis
4S13-T0.description: Features include palpitations, weight loss, heat intolerance, anxiety, menstrual irregularities, myopathy, tremor, and lid lag. Additional features in children include rapid growth, emotional lability, behavioral issues, and poor school performance.

kS1m-T0.title: Clinical features of bleeding disorders
kS1m-T0.description: Signs and symptoms that are consistent with an underlying bleeding disorder. This constellation can include easy bruising, petechiae and/or purpura, bleeding gums, epistaxis, heavy menstrual bleeding, and prolonged or excessive bleeding after surgery.

destinations.label: Hemostasis and bleeding disorders → Clinical features

OS1I-T0.title: Factor XI
OS1I-T0.description: A coagulation factor that is involved in the intrinsic pathway of secondary hemostasis. After its activation by factor XII or thrombin, factor XIa activates factor IX. Congenital factor XI deficiency (hemophilia C) is rare and can lead to a mild to moderate bleeding disorder.

lS1v-T0.title: Confluence of sinuses
lS1v-T0.description: The union of three dural venous sinuses: the superior sagittal sinus, the straight sinus, and the occipital sinus. Drains into left and right transverse sinuses.

NS1--T0.title: H⁺/K⁺ antiporter
NS1--T0.description: A cotransporter that exchanges hydrogen ions and potassium ions. Involved in the regulation of intracellular pH of and potassium homeostasis.

mS1VZg0.title: MET
mS1VZg0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Metabolic equivalent of task
2. Medical expulsive therapy

5S1iZg0.title: Urine drug screening
5S1iZg0.description: A laboratory test that evaluates the urine for the presence of common drugs and/or illicit substances (e.g., amphetamines, cannabinoids, cocaine, opiates, phencyclidine). Can be performed using enzyme multiplied immunoassay or gas chromatography-mass spectrometry technique.

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Management of substance use disorder

MS1MZg0.title: Hereditary congenital lymphedema
MS1MZg0.description: An autosomal dominant condition that results in the development of lymphedema in the lower extremities in early infancy. Most commonly caused by a missense mutation in the VEGFR-3 gene.

nS17Zg0.title: Transforming growth factor-α
nS17Zg0.description: A growth factor involved in cell migration, proliferation, and differentiation through binding to the epidermal growth factor receptor.

LS1wZg0.title: Seabather eruption
LS1wZg0.description: A pruritic, papular dermatitis caused by hypersensitivity to jellyfish or sea anemone larvae trapped in skin areas under a bathing suit. Common on the United States Atlantic coast (e.g., Florida, Massachusetts), Bermuda, and the Caribbean.

oS100g0.title: Nematocyst
oS100g0.description: A venom-containing capsule found within the tentacles of some jellyfish. Discharges venom with mechanical pressure. Can be identified on skin scrapings of patients who have sustained a jellyfish sting.

KS1U0g0.title: Thrombus
KS1U0g0.description: A blood clot formed as the final product of hemostasis. Consists of red blood cells, platelets, and fibrin strands.

6S1j0g0.title: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis type I
6S1j0g0.description: The most common form of membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis. Characterized by subendothelial immune complex deposits that trigger the activation of the classical complement pathway, which results in a cascade that can cause cell injury, mesangial proliferation, and matrix expansion.

pS1L0g0.title: Gerota fascia
pS1L0g0.description: A dense, elastic layer of connective tissue that surrounds the kidney, adrenal gland, and perirenal fat. Divides the retroperitoneal space into perirenal, anterior, and posterior pararenal spaces.

rS1fag0.title: Lumbosacral transitional vertebrae
rS1fag0.description: A variety of congenital spinal abnormalities in which the transverse processes of L5 are fused to the transverse process of S1 (sacralization; more common) or vice-versa (lumbarization; less common). Frequently asymptomatic but may be associated with an increased risk of degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis.

7S14ag0.title: Carotid ultrasonography
7S14ag0.description: A noninvasive ultrasonographic technique used to evaluate the carotid and/or vertebral arteries. Referred to as a carotid duplex ultrasound when Doppler assessment of blood flow direction and velocity is added.

HS1Kag0.title: Transcranial Doppler
HS1Kag0.description: A noninvasive sonographic imaging method used in patients with suspected cerebrovascular disease that measures the rate and direction of blood flow inside intracranial vessels (e.g., the middle cerebral artery).

8S1OYg0.title: European League Against Rheumatism
8S1OYg0.description: A European organization that supports patients with rheumatic diseases, health professionals, and the scientific rheumatology societies. Its stated mission is to reduce the burden of rheumatic diseases on the individual and society and to improve the treatment, prevention, and rehabilitation of rheumatic diseases.

uS1pYg0.title: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
uS1pYg0.description: The most common type of retinal detachment. Caused by retinal tears that fill with retinal fluid due to vitreous degeneration, which leads to centripetal retinal detachment. Risk factors include older age, myopia, previous intraocular surgery, trauma, and posterior vitreous detachment.

media.title: Scleral buckling surgery in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment

DS11bg0.title: Familial hypokalemic periodic paralysis
DS11bg0.description: A rare genetic disorder characterized by sudden attacks of weakness and paralysis associated with hypokalemia. Attacks may be triggered by strenuous exercise, eating carbohydrate-rich food, or infusions of insulin and dextrose.

wS1hbg0.title: Hypokalemic periodic paralysis
wS1hbg0.description: An autosomal dominant disorder with incomplete penetrance characterized by episodes of rapid-onset muscle weakness, paralysis, and hypokalemia. Is the most common form of periodic paralysis and is typically caused by mutations in the CACNA1S calcium channel gene (type 1 hypokalemic periodic paralysis) or SCN4A sodium channel gene (type 2 hypokalemic periodic paralysis).

9S1Nbg0.title: Acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
9S1Nbg0.description: An acute presentation of cutaneous lupus erythematosus typically characterized by a photosensitive malar or maculopapular rash. Frequently associated with active systemic lupus erythematosus.

destinations.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus → Specific clinical manifestations

xS1Ebg0.title: Axonopathy
xS1Ebg0.description: The structural or functional defect of an axon or its terminal either as a cause or result of neurogenerative conditions.

BS1zbg0.title: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
BS1zbg0.description: A group of conditions caused by atherosclerosis. Examples include cardiovascular disease (e.g., ischemic heart disease), cerebrovascular disease (e.g., stroke), peripheral artery disease (e.g., claudication), and aortic aneurysm.

_S15Xg0.title: Lupus band test
_S15Xg0.description: A direct immunofluorescence technique that can be used to identify a continuous band of immunoreactants (e.g., IgG and complement) along the dermal-epidermal junction. This finding is associated with lupus erythematosus.

zS1rXg0.title: Mean aortic pressure gradient
zS1rXg0.description: The difference in pressure between the left ventricle and the ascending aorta during systole. An important factor in the evaluation of the severity of aortic valve stenosis. Pressures normally equilibrate relatively rapidly when the valve opens. Valvular stenosis limits the increase in aortic pressure, while increasing the LV pressure, leading to a higher gradient. A transaortic gradient of < 10 mmHg is considered normal, while a gradient of ≥ 40 mmHg constitutes severe stenosis.

media.title: Continuous wave (CW) Doppler in aortic valvular stenosis

-S1DXg0.title: Transaortic velocity
-S1DXg0.description: The maximum velocity of blood flow measured across the aortic valve during systole. Used in the evaluation of the severity of aortic valve stenosis and inversely related to the aortic valve area. A transaortic velocity < 2.0 m/second is considered normal, while a velocity ≥ 4.0m/second constitutes severe stenosis.

media.title: Continuous wave (CW) Doppler in aortic valvular stenosis

Zh1Zcg0.title: Signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on x-ray
Zh1Zcg0.description: Typical features of left ventricular hypertrophy on chest x-ray include a rounded heart apex and left cardiac border, as well as narrowing of retrocardiac space in the lateral view. In later stages the left ventricle may also dilate, leading to enlargement of the left ventricle.

0h1ecg0.title: Temporal dispersion
0h1ecg0.description: A phenomenon seen in nerve conduction studies in which different types of nerve fibers (e.g., A, B, and C fibers) cause differences in signal scattering and latency between the stimulating and recording electrode due to different degrees of myelination. Can also be a pathologic sign of demyelinating neuropathies (e.g., acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy).

ah1Qcg0.title: Next-generation sequencing
ah1Qcg0.description: A large-scale molecular analysis technique used to investigate whole genomes, entire exomes, or small numbers of targeted genes. Simultaneously analyzes millions of DNA base pairs in parallel and compares the results to the reference human genome.

Yh1ncg0.title: Psychogenic nonepileptic seizure
Yh1ncg0.description: An episode of involuntary movement, sensation, or behavior that is similar in appearance to an epileptic seizure; however, the underlying cause is psychiatric distress rather than abnormal brain activity. Associated with conversion disorder, anxiety, and psychoses.

bh1Hcg0.title: Atypical adenomatous hyperplasia
bh1Hcg0.description: A pulmonary lesion ≤ 5 mm in size caused by atypical pneumocyte or club cell growth along alveolar walls without cytologic features of carcinoma.

Xh19cg0.title: Minimally-invasive pulmonary adenocarcinoma
Xh19cg0.description: A subtype of lung adenocarcinoma that exhibits a lepidic growth pattern with ≤ 5 mm of invasion. Lesions are typically ≤ 3 cm in size.

ch1a1g0.title: Motor unit action potential
ch1a1g0.description: A compound electric potential produced by skeletal myocytes of a motor unit during voluntary activity or during stimulation by an electrode or alpha motor neuron. Its shape on electromyography can be biphasic, triphasic, or occasionally, polyphasic.

Wh1P1g0.title: Polyphasic motor unit potential
Wh1P1g0.description: A signal pattern seen on electromyography. Increased readings of short-duration, low-amplitude polyphasic potentials can indicate a pathologic process, such as a myopathy (e.g., polymyositis) or neuromuscular junction disorder (e.g., myasthenia gravis).

dh1o1g0.title: Transient elastography
dh1o1g0.description: An ultrasonographic technique in which liver stiffness is measured. Used as a diagnostic tool for the early diagnosis of liver fibrosis and progression to liver cirrhosis.

Vh1G1g0.title: Lateralizing symptom
Vh1G1g0.description: A symptom or physical examination finding that indicates which side of the body (i.e., left or right) is the most likely location of a lesion (e.g., ischemia, bleeding, inflammation, seizure focus). Most commonly used to describe neurological findings (e.g., right hemiparesis caused by a left hemispheric stroke), but can also refer to other symptoms (e.g., right-sided headache caused by GCA affecting the right temporal artery)

eh1x1g0.title: RT-PCR cycle threshold
eh1x1g0.description: The number of cycles required by reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to amplify a sample to a detectable level.

Uh1bWg0.title: Occult inguinal hernia
Uh1bWg0.description: An inguinal hernia that is not identifiable on physical examination. May manifest with inguinodynia or vague inguinal discomfort.

2h1TWg0.title: 2019 EULAR/ACR classification criteria for SLE
2h1TWg0.description: A set of criteria used to assist physicians in making a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Includes positive antinuclear antibody and various clinical findings (constitutional, hematologic, neuropsychiatric, mucocutaneous, serosal, musculoskeletal, and renal) and immunologic findings (i.e., the presence of antiphospholipid antibodies, complement proteins, and/or SLE-specific antibodies).

gh1FWg0.title: Ristocetin cofactor assay
gh1FWg0.description: A diagnostic test that measures the ability of von Willebrand factor (vWF) to agglutinate platelets. Ristocetin is an antibiotic that activates vWF to bind glycoprotein Ib, thereby inducing platelet aggregation. Failure of platelet aggregation after adding ristocetin can be seen in patients with von Willebrand disease and Bernard-Soulier syndrome.

Sh1yWg0.title: Cruveilhier‑von‑Baumgarten syndrome
Sh1yWg0.description: A rare condition in which a patent umbilical vein forms an anastomosis between the left branch of the portal vein and the veins of the anterior abdominal wall. Results in a portal systemic bypass circuit that leads to portal hypertension and a cirrhotic liver.

hh1cdg0.title: Ipsiversive torsional nystagmus
hh1cdg0.description: A type of torsional nystagmus where the upper pole of the eye beats toward the affected side. Can be seen in anterior and posterior canal BPPV, as well as medial longitudinal fasciculus lesions.

3h1Sdg0.title: Hypothalamic-melanocortin system
3h1Sdg0.description: A part of the neuroendocrine system that regulates appetite, energy homeostasis, and skin pigmentation. Includes neurons that express neuropeptide Y, agouti gene-related peptide, and/or pro-opiomelanocortin.

Rh1ldg0.title: Goserelin
Rh1ldg0.description: A gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor agonist that can either be used to stimulate (via pulsatile administration) or suppress (via continuous administration, which downregulates GnRH receptors) LH and FSH secretion. Commonly used continuously to treat hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, precocious puberty, menorrhagia, and endometriosis. Used in pulsatile fashion to increase fertility.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

ih1Jdg0.title: Inguinal hernia reduction
ih1Jdg0.description: A procedure in which the clinician manually returns the contents of an incarcerated inguinal hernia through the fascial defect. This procedure is contraindicated in patients with signs of strangulation of hernial contents.

Qh1udg0.title: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy
Qh1udg0.description: A condition that can develop in patients with liver cirrhosis characterized by normal cardiac output and contractility at rest and a dysfunctional cardiac response (e.g., inotropic incompetence, QT-interval prologation) to stress.

Ph1WVg0.title: Euvolemic hyponatremia
Ph1WVg0.description: A subtype of hypotonic hyponatremia that is not associated with clinical signs of hypovolemia (e.g., dehydration, orthostatic hypotension) or hypervolemia (e.g., edema, ascites, jugular venous distension). Associated with increased total body water and normal total body sodium. Etiologies include syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion, primary polydipsia, adrenal insufficiency, and hypothyroidism.

4h13Vg0.title: Hypervolemic hyponatremia
4h13Vg0.description: A subtype of hypotonic hyponatremia associated with signs of fluid overload (e.g., edema, ascites, jugular venous distension), increased total body sodium, and increased total body water. Can be caused by conditions that result in decreased effective circulating volume (e.g., congestive heart failure, cirrhosis).

kh1mVg0.title: Bowel preparation
kh1mVg0.description: The use of a clear liquid diet and/or medication (e.g., polyethylene glycol) to induce diarrhea and purge the bowel of fecal matter. Bowel preparation is performed up to 24 hours prior to colorectal surgery or procedures such as colonoscopy to allow the mucosa to be visualized more easily and to reduce the risk of surgical complications.

Oh1IVg0.title: Hepatopulmonary syndrome
Oh1IVg0.description: A pulmonary complication of chronic liver disease and/or portal hypertension characterized by severe hypoxemia due to dilation of the intrapulmonary vasculature.

mh1Veg0.title: Peptide YY
mh1Veg0.description: A hormone secreted by L cells of the small and large intestine in response to protein-rich chyme. Suppresses appetite and slows gastric emptying.

5h1ieg0.title: Adenylate kinase deficiency
5h1ieg0.description: A rare hereditary enzymopathy characterized by a deficiency of adenylate kinase, which normally catalyzes the interconversion of ATP, ADP, and AMP. Manifests with moderate-to-severe hemolytic anemia.

Mh1Meg0.title: Hexokinase deficiency
Mh1Meg0.description: A rare, autosomal recessive enzymopathy caused by mutations in the HK1 gene, which encodes hexokinase-1 (an enzyme involved in the phosphorylation of glucose and other six-carbon monosaccharides). Manifests with moderate-to-severe hemolytic anemia.

nh17eg0.title: Cannabinoid receptor agonist
nh17eg0.description: A class of drug that acts on the cannabinoid receptors (CB1, CB2). Used as an appetite stimulant and to treat chemotherapy-induced nausea.

Lh1weg0.title: Canadian CT head rule
Lh1weg0.description: A clinical decision rule used to determine the need for neuroimaging in patients with mild traumatic brain injury.

ph1LUg0.title: Pregnenolone
ph1LUg0.description: An endogenous steroid precursor of many steroid hormones. Also functions as a negative allosteric modulator of the CB1 receptor.

Jh1sUg0.title: Cardiac CT
Jh1sUg0.description: A radiological study that uses multidetector CT techniques to assess cardiac structure and function (e.g., chamber and valve anatomy, coronary artery calcium). CT angiography of the coronary arteries can also be added and is sometimes used as a noninvasive alternative to cardiac catheterization.

Ih1Y2g0.title: Jacobsen syndrome
Ih1Y2g0.description: A rare genetic condition caused by the deletion of the long arm of chromosome 11. Clinical features include pre- and postnatal growth restriction, facial dysmorphism (e.g., hypertelorism, coloboma, skull deformities), and hematologic disturbances (e.g., platelet dysfunction, thrombocytopenia, pancytopenia).

7h142g0.title: Platypnea
7h142g0.description: A symptom of shortness of breath that worsens when standing or sitting and improves when lying supine.

Hh1K2g0.title: Orthodeoxia
Hh1K2g0.description: A decrease in arterial blood oxygen saturation when moving from a lying position to an upright position.

sh1t2g0.title: Contrast echocardiography
sh1t2g0.description: An ultrasound examination of the heart that uses intravenous contrast agents to enhance visualization of cardiac structures and blood flow. Contrast agents contain gas-filled microbubbles that produce strong echos. Used in the diagnosis of various cardiovascular conditions including intracardiac shunts, thrombi, and pseudoaneurysms.

Gh1B2g0.title: Lung perfusion scintigraphy
Gh1B2g0.description: A diagnostic imaging tool that records the distribution of pulmonary arterial blood flow. It is used to evaluate cardiovascular and pulmonary disorders (e.g., pulmonary thromboembolism, hepatopulmonary syndrome, pulmonary artery stenosis).

media.title: Lung perfusion scintigraphy in hepatopulmonary syndrome

th1Xfg0.title: Complex skin abscess
th1Xfg0.description: A type of skin abscess that requires specialized treatment because of its location (e.g., perianal, perirectal), the pathogens involved (e.g., resistant pathogens), or patient characteristics (e.g., immunodeficiency). Management of these abscesses usually involves soft tissue imaging and a surgical procedure.

destinations.label: Skin and soft tissue infections → Purulent SSTIs

8h1Ofg0.title: Percutaneous transhepatic thrombolysis
8h1Ofg0.description: A procedure used to dissolve blood clots in the portal vein via direct infusion of fibrinolytic agents into the thrombus. The transhepatic approach is carried out by introducing a catheter through the portal vein under ultrasonographic guidance.

uh1pfg0.title: Antithrombotic agents
uh1pfg0.description: A group of drugs used to prevent clot formation and clot growth. Includes anticoagulants (e.g., Vitamin K antagonists, heparin, direct oral anticoagulants) and antiplatelet drugs (e.g., aspirin, clopidogrel, glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors)

Eh18fg0.title: Peritoneal fold
Eh18fg0.description: A structure that connects intra-abdominal organs to each other or to the abdominal wall. Examples include the omentum, mesentery, and peritoneal ligaments.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

vh1Afg0.title: Superior duodenal fold
vh1Afg0.description: A fold of peritoneum that surrounds the superior duodenal recess and overlies the inferior mesenteric vein. Has a free lower edge. Used as a reference point in abdominal surgery to mark the fourth part of the duodenum and beginning of the jejunum.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

Dh11Tg0.title: Inferior duodenal fold
Dh11Tg0.description: A fold of peritoneum that surrounds the inferior duodenal recess near the fourth part of the duodenum. Has a free upper edge.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

wh1hTg0.title: Gastropancreatic fold
wh1hTg0.description: A fold of peritoneum that runs between the lesser curvature of the stomach and the neck of the pancreas. Divides the lesser sac into the superior and inferior recesses. The upper part of the fold overlies the left gastric artery. The lower part overlies the common hepatic artery.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Peritoneal cavity and spaces

9h1NTg0.title: Chromophobe cell
9h1NTg0.description: A cell type of the anterior pituitary that stains poorly with acidic and basic dyes. Does not secrete any hormones. May represent undifferentiated stem cells with potential for hormone production or degranulated acidophils/basophils that have lost their secretory function.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamus and pituitary gland

Ch1qTg0.title: Agouti-related peptide
Ch1qTg0.description: A neuropeptide involved in appetite stimulation. Produced by the agouti-related peptide/neuropeptide Y coexpressing neurons of the arcuate nucleus in the hypothalamus.

Bh1zTg0.title: Laminar blood flow
Bh1zTg0.description: A type of blood flow in which blood moves smoothly (i.e., in parallel with the blood vessel wall).

yh1dgg0.title: Aniridia
yh1dgg0.description: The partial or complete absence of the iris. Can be an isolated finding, develop with other ocular abnormalities, or be seen as part of a syndrome (e.g., WAGR syndrome, Gillespie syndrome)

Ah1Rgg0.title: Somatostatin analogues
Ah1Rgg0.description: A group of drugs that are used to treat acromegaly, carcinoid syndrome, and esophageal variceal bleeding. Examples include octreotide and lanreotide.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

zh1rgg0.title: Abnormal posturing
zh1rgg0.description: The maintenance of a particular body position for an extensive period of time. Can occur involuntarily as a result of muscle hypertonia (e.g., flexor or extensor posturing from stroke) and acute dystonia or voluntarily in conditions such as catalepsy.

-h1Dgg0.title: Malignant catatonia
-h1Dgg0.description: A life-threatening, rapidly progressive form of catatonia characterized by fever, diaphoresis, autonomic instability, delirium, and rigidity.

031eSg0.title: MNS blood group system
031eSg0.description: A group of rare red blood cell antigens that includes M, N, S, s, and U antigens.

a31QSg0.title: Kell blood group system
a31QSg0.description: A rare group of red blood cell antigens that includes Jka (JK1), Jkb (JK2), and JK3 antigens. Its components are also expressed in the epithelium of descending vasa recta, where they function as urea transporters.

Y31nSg0.title: Kidd blood group system
Y31nSg0.description: A group of rare red blood cell antigens that includes K (K1), k (K2), Kp(a), Kp(b), Js(a), and Js(b) antigens. Responsible for ~ 10% of cases of severe hemolytic disease of the newborn.

b31HSg0.title: Risk factor
b31HSg0.description: A variable or attribute that increases the probability of developing a disease or injury. For example, obesity is a risk factor for coronary artery disease. May be further classified as a modifiable risk factor (e.g., smoking, physical inactivity, excessive alcohol intake) or a nonmodifiable risk factor (e.g., age, genetics).

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Measures of association

X319Sg0.title: Glycated albumin
X319Sg0.description: A form of albumin that has been modified by glucose. Its serum concentration is used as a measure of average blood glucose concentration from the previous 2–4 weeks, particularly in individuals with hemoglobinopathy and/or renal disorders.

c31ahg0.title: Glycated protein
c31ahg0.description: A protein that has been modified by glucose via glycation of amino groups. Its serum concentration is used as a measure of average blood glucose concentration.

1312hg0.title: Glomerulonephritis
1312hg0.description: Glomerular inflammation (i.e., proliferation of glomerular cells and leukocyte infiltration). May be acute or chronic. Can be primary (i.e., due to a pathological process isolated within the glomerulus) or secondary (i.e., due to a systemic condition). Conditions causing glomerulonephritis typically manifest with nephritic syndrome, but isolated nephrotic syndrome or nephritic-nephrotic syndrome may be present.

V31Ghg0.title: Accountable care organization
V31Ghg0.description: A network of health care providers (e.g., physicians, other clinicians, hospitals) that enroll voluntarily to provide coordinated care to a group of individuals. They contract with different payers (e.g., Medicare, private health insurance companies), who provide financial incentives for working together to provide high-quality care at lower cost (e.g., using alternative payment models).

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care delivery models

e31xhg0.title: Tabletop test
e31xhg0.description: A test used to diagnose hand contractures in patients with Dupuytren contracture or limited joint mobility syndrome. Evaluates the ability to flatten the palms against the surface of a table, which can be impaired by flexion contractures of the metacarpophalangeal joints.

331SRg0.title: Distal intestinal obstruction syndrome
331SRg0.description: A common gastrointestinal complication of cystic fibrosis characterized by small intestine obstruction due to pancreatic insufficiency, thickened stool, poor motility, and fecal stasis in the distal ileum and right colon. Manifestations include abdominal distention, pain, flatulence, and a palpable cecal mass.

i31JRg0.title: Community-associated MRSA infection
i31JRg0.description: An infection with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus that is not associated with recent contact with the health care system.

Q31uRg0.title: Health care-associated MRSA infection
Q31uRg0.description: An infection with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus associated with recent contact with the health care system (e.g., hospitalization, surgery, dialysis, residence in a long-term care facility).

j31_Rg0.title: Round ligament varicosity
j31_Rg0.description: A rare condition during pregnancy in which the pelvic veins draining the round ligament and inguinal canal are dilated. Presents as a tender, palpable mass in the groin area that may be indistinguishable from inguinal hernia on physical exam.

P31Wig0.title: Avulsion fracture
P31Wig0.description: A type of fracture that occurs from bone shearing at the insertion point of a tendon or ligament, caused by a sudden and intense muscle contraction or by trauma.

destinations.label: General principles of fractures → Subtypes and variants

4313ig0.title: Aortic bifurcation
4313ig0.description: The point at which the abdominal aorta bifurcates into the right and left common iliac arteries. Usually located at the level of L4 vertebra, near the level of the umbilicus.

k31mig0.title: Lumbar arteries
k31mig0.description: A series of paired arteries (usually four pairs) that arise from the abdominal aorta at the levels of L1-L4. They supply the lumbar segments of the spinal cord and the posterior abdominal wall.

O31Iig0.title: p57 protein
O31Iig0.description: A cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor protein encoded on chromosome 11 that acts as a negative regulator on the cell cycle. Produced by a paternally imprinted but maternally expressed gene. Immunohistochemical staining for p57 can be used to diagnose a partial hydatidiform mole.

l31vig0.title: Fecal calprotectin concentration
l31vig0.description: The measure of calprotectin concentration in the stool, which can be used as a noninvasive screening test for inflammatory bowel disease. Calprotectin is released by neutrophils after migration to a site of acute inflammation; concentration positively correlates with the severity of inflammation.

N31-ig0.title: Loop recorder
N31-ig0.description: A device used in the evaluation of arrhythmia or syncope that records the patient's heart rhythm up to an hour prior to the arrhythmic event as well as during the event. Can be triggered automatically or by the patient. External or event loop recorders are worn externally for short periods of time (4-6 weeks). Implantable loop recorders can be used for up to 36 months (e.g., for patients with more infrequent episodes).

m31VQg0.title: Event recorder
m31VQg0.description: A device used in the evaluation of arrhythmias or syncope to record the patient's heart rhythm during symptomatic episodes. Some devices are triggered to record data either by the patient or automatically by the arrhythmia; others have a short memory and can also store information for up to an hour prior to being triggered (loop event recorders).

531iQg0.title: Ileocolonoscopy
531iQg0.description: The endoscopic examination of the rectum, colon, and terminal ileum. Directly visualizes the intestinal mucosa and facilitates tissue biopsy. Has high sensitivity for the diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease.

M31MQg0.title: Dorsal pancreatic artery
M31MQg0.description: A branch of the splenic artery that supplies the pancreas and anastomoses with the pancreaticoduodenal and the transverse (or inferior) pancreatic arteries.

n317Qg0.title: Pericentral fibrosis
n317Qg0.description: The deposition of connective tissue around the central vein (centrilobular region). Etiologies include alcoholic liver disease, adult nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, chronic graft rejection, and conditions that cause necrosis of centrilobular hepatocytes (e.g., drug-induced hepatic injury)

L31wQg0.title: Inferior pancreatic artery
L31wQg0.description: A continuation of the left branch of the dorsal pancreatic artery that supplies the body and tail of the pancreas.

o310jg0.title: Greater pancreatic artery
o310jg0.description: A branch of the splenic artery that supplies the pancreas and anastomoses with the branches of the transverse (or inferior) pancreatic artery.

K31Ujg0.title: Bridging fibrosis
K31Ujg0.description: The deposition of connective tissue within the hepatic lobule, typically between the central vein and portal triad (porto-central bridging fibrosis). Can result in the formation of pseudolobules. Indicates advanced liver fibrosis.

631jjg0.title: Fibrosing cholestatic hepatitis
631jjg0.description: A rare, fulminant form of liver disease that occurs in patients with untreated hepatitis B or hepatitis C viral infections who are receiving immunosuppressive therapy (e.g., following organ transplantation). Characterized by periportal or pericellular fibrosis, hepatocyte ballooning, and severe cholestasis with bile duct injury.

p31Ljg0.title: Periportal fibrosis
p31Ljg0.description: The deposition of connective tissue around the portal triad (periportal region). Etiologies include hepatotropic virus infections and pediatric nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.

J31sjg0.title: Pericellular fibrosis
J31sjg0.description: The deposition of connective tissue around hepatocytes in the vicinity of the hepatic sinusoids, which results in a chicken wire or lattice appearance on histopathologica examination. Etiologies include alcoholic liver disease, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, and vitamin A toxicity.

q31Cjg0.title: Sustained virologic response
q31Cjg0.description: The absence of hepatitis C virus RNA after 12 weeks of therapy with direct-acting antivirals. A patient in this state is considered to be cured of hepatitis C virus infection.

I31YPg0.title: Creeping fat
I31YPg0.description: A hyperplastic growth of adipose tissue that results in the accumulation of mesenteric fat around the circumference of the intestine. The degree of hyperplasia correlates with the severity of transmural inflammation. Pathognomonic for Crohn disease.

t31X4g0.title: Jejunal arteries
t31X4g0.description: A collection of arteries that arise from the superior mesenteric artery and supply the jejunum.

F31g4g0.title: Ileal arteries
F31g4g0.description: A collection of arteries that arise from the superior mesenteric artery and supply the ileum.

831O4g0.title: Ileocolic artery
831O4g0.description: A branch of the superior mesenteric artery that supplies the terminal ileum, cecum, appendix, and part of the ascending colon. Divides into the ileal artery, appendicular artery, anterior and posterior cecal arteries, and ascending colic artery.

u31p4g0.title: Cecal artery
u31p4g0.description: A branch of the ileocolic artery that supplies the cecum and the ileocecal valve. Further subdivided into an anterior and a posterior portion.

E3184g0.title: Appendicular artery
E3184g0.description: A branch of the ileocolic artery (or, less commonly, the ileal or posterior cecal artery) that supplies the appendix.

D311kg0.title: Right colic artery
D311kg0.description: A branch of the superior mesenteric artery that supplies the ascending colon. Divides into ascending (superior) and descending (inferior) branches, which anastomose with the middle colic and ileocolic arteries, respectively.

w31hkg0.title: Left colic artery
w31hkg0.description: A branch of the inferior mesenteric artery that supplies the distal third of the transverse colon and the descending colon. Divides into ascending and descending branches, which anastomose with the middle colic and sigmoid arteries, respectively.

931Nkg0.title: Sigmoid arteries
931Nkg0.description: A collection of arteries that originate from the inferior mesenteric artery and supply the sigmoid colon.

C31qkg0.title: SCN
C31qkg0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Severe congenital neutropenia
2. Suprachiasmatic nucleus

x31Ekg0.title: Subcostal nerves
x31Ekg0.description: A pair of sensorimotor nerves that originate from the ventral rami of the twelfth thoracic nerve. Provides motor supply to the muscles of the lower anterior abdominal wall and sensory supply to skin over the hip and peripheral part of the diaphragm.

B31zkg0.title: Elexacaftor
B31zkg0.description: A CFTR modulator that increases normal intracellular processing and trafficking of functional CFTR protein to the cell surface. Used in combination with ivacaftor and tezacaftor to treat cystic fibrosis.

y31dOg0.title: Primigravidity
y31dOg0.description: The state of being pregnant for the first time.

A31ROg0.title: Multigravidity
A31ROg0.description: The state of having been pregnant more than once.

_315Og0.title: Transmural
_315Og0.description: A descriptor for involvement of all layers of a structure (e.g., transmural inflammation in Crohn disease that involves the entire thickness of the bowel wall).

z31rOg0.title: Acquired thrombophilia
z31rOg0.description: A group of acquired conditions in which an individual is predisposed to thrombosis or thromboembolism. Includes antiphospholipid syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, nephrotic syndrome, malignancy, oral contraceptive pills/hormone replacement therapy, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, pregnancy, advanced age, smoking, obesity, surgery, immobilization, and trauma.

0R1elg0.title: Conjugation (conception)
0R1elg0.description: A stage after fertilization during which the sperm and ovum fuse to form the zygote.

aR1Qlg0.title: Standardized incidence ratio
aR1Qlg0.description: A ratio of the incidence rate of a disease from a study cohort with that of the general population. A SIR of 1 indicates similar incidence.

YR1nlg0.title: Periviable birth
YR1nlg0.description: A live birth that occurs between 20 0/7 weeks and 25 6/7 weeks of gestation.

bR1Hlg0.title: Blalock–Thomas–Taussig shunt
bR1Hlg0.description: A palliative surgical procedure used to increase pulmonary blood flow in patients with ductal-dependent cyanotic congenital heart defects (e.g., tetralogy of Fallot) by creating a communication between the subclavian artery and pulmonary artery. This procedure is only performed to defer the elective surgery for complete repair.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Tetralogy of Fallot

cR1aNg0.title: Lateral inguinal fossa
cR1aNg0.description: A depression located lateral to the lateral umbilical fold in the anterior abdominal wall. Overlies the deep inguinal ring. It is a common site for indirect inguinal hernia.

1R12Ng0.title: Arterial switch procedure
1R12Ng0.description: A surgical procedure to correct transposition of the great vessels in patients who do not have a significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. Involves transection of the aorta and pulmonary artery and translocation to opposite ventricles.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Transposition of the great vessels (TGV)

WR1PNg0.title: Rastelli procedure
WR1PNg0.description: A surgical procedure to correct transposition of the great vessels in patients who have a large ventricular septal defect (VSD) and a significant left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. Involves tunneling the LVOT through the VSD and placing a valved conduit between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Transposition of the great vessels (TGV)

dR1oNg0.title: Superior duodenal recess
dR1oNg0.description: A peritoneal space near the superior left portion of the fourth part of the duodenum. It is bounded anteriorly by the superior duodenal fold.

VR1GNg0.title: Inferior duodenal recess
VR1GNg0.description: A peritoneal space near the left portion of the fourth part of the duodenum, inferior to the duodenojejunal flexure. It is bounded anteriorly by the inferior duodenal fold.

fR1kmg0.title: ABCD2 score
fR1kmg0.description: A clinical tool used to assess the risk of stroke after a suspected transient ischemic attack. Components include age, blood pressure, symptoms (e.g., unilateral weaknes), duration of symptoms, and history of diabetes mellitus.

TR16mg0.title: Step-up therapy
TR16mg0.description: Sequential treatment strategy that employs drugs of gradually increasing toxicity/effectiveness until treatment proves effective. Especially used in the treatment of chronic conditions, such as IBD and asthma.

gR1Fmg0.title: Top-down therapy
gR1Fmg0.description: Sequential treatment strategy that begins with high potency and, typically, more toxic medications to induce remission of disease and then switching to less potent but, typically, less toxic medications to maintain remission.

SR1ymg0.title: Induction therapy
SR1ymg0.description: The first series of measures taken to treat a disease, with the goal of inducing remission. Especially used in the context of treating cancer (e.g., induction chemotherapy for leukemia) and chronic diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease.

hR1c5g0.title: Steroid-sparing agent
hR1c5g0.description: A nonsteroidal immunosuppressive therapy typically used to reduce the dose and/or duration of steroid therapy needed to achieve a therapeutic effect. Examples include azathioprine, methotrexate, and TNF-α inhibitors.

3R1S5g0.title: Amnioreduction
3R1S5g0.description: A procedure used to used to reduce amniotic fluid volume. Used to relieve symptoms of maternal dyspnea and/or discomfort in severe polyhydramnios and improve uteroplacental perfusion in twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome.

RR1l5g0.title: CTN
RR1l5g0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Cardiac troponin
2. Classical trigeminal neuralgia

iR1J5g0.title: Subscapular fossa
iR1J5g0.description: A concave depression located on the costal surface of the body of the scapula. The subscapularis muscle attaches here.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

QR1u5g0.title: Nephrotic-range proteinuria
QR1u5g0.description: Urine protein excretion of ≥ 3.5 g/24 hours, or ≥ 3000 mg/g protein/creatinine ratio in a spot urine sample.

jR1_5g0.title: Hospital-onset MRSA infection
jR1_5g0.description: An infection caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus associated with a positive culture from a normally-sterile site that is obtained > 48 hours after hospital admission.

PR1WMg0.title: Hemosuccus pancreaticus
PR1WMg0.description: A condition of hemorrhage (often life-threatening) from the pancreatic duct that can be caused by pseudocyst or tumor erosion into a vessel (most commonly a splenic artery pseudoaneurysm).

4R13Mg0.title: Cameron lesion
4R13Mg0.description: An erosion or ulcer that develops in the sac of a hiatal hernia. Can cause acute or chronic upper gastrointestinal bleeding.

kR1mMg0.title: Crystal violet
kR1mMg0.description: A dye with antimicrobial properties that is used in Gram staining. Gram-positive organisms retain the dye because of a thick layer of peptidoglycan in their cell walls. Also used to mark skin (e.g., in preparation for surgery).

lR1vMg0.title: Radioactive iodine uptake measurement
lR1vMg0.description: A thyroid function test that quantifies iodine absorption by the thyroid. Radioactive iodine is administered orally. Several hours to days later, a thyroid probe or gamma camera is used to determine the percentage of administered radioactive iodine taken up by the thyroid gland. Often combined with thyroid scintigraphy.

NR1-Mg0.title: Munchies
NR1-Mg0.description: A state of increased appetite and enhanced appreciation of food due to the activation of the endogenous endocannabinoid system. Commonly associated with cannabis (marijuana) use.

mR1Vng0.title: Postterm infant
mR1Vng0.description: An infant whose delivery occurred after 42 weeks (≥ 42 0/7) of gestation.

5R1ing0.title: Hyperpyrexia
5R1ing0.description: A medical emergency characterized by a fever exceeding 41.5°C (106.7°F) that is caused by an abnormally high hypothalamic set point. Associated symptoms include diaphoresis, impaired consciousness, and seizures. Underlying causes include CNS infections and hemorrhages.

MR1Mng0.title: Red blood cell count
MR1Mng0.description: A test that measures the concentration of red blood cells. The normal range for men is 4.3-5.9 million cells per microliter (mcL); for women who are not pregnant, it is 3.5-5.5 million cells/mcL; for children, it is 3.5-5.0 million cells/mcL. Reported as part of the complete blood count.

nR17ng0.title: Toll-like receptor 2
nR17ng0.description: A member of the toll-like receptor family and vital part of the innate immune system that interacts with several ligands, including lipoteichoic acid. This interaction stimulates the production of TNF-α and promotes the inflammatory response.

oR10Lg0.title: Extracellular polymeric substances
oR10Lg0.description: A heterogeneous group of polymers, including various polysaccharides, enzymes, and lipids, that are synthesized by microorganisms to create biofilms.

KR1ULg0.title: Staphylococcal enterotoxin B
KR1ULg0.description: A heat-stable enterotoxin produced by Staphylococcus aureus that can cause food poisoning. Can also act as a superantigen and cause toxic shock syndrome.

6R1jLg0.title: Staphylococcal enterotoxin A
6R1jLg0.description: A heat-stable enterotoxin produced by Staphylococcus aureus. It is the most frequent cause of staphylococcal food poisoning. Can also act as a superantigen and cause toxic shock syndrome.

JR1sLg0.title: SEA
JR1sLg0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Spinal epidural abscess
2. Staphylococcal enterotoxin A

qR1CLg0.title: Coronary ligament
qR1CLg0.description: A peritoneal reflection between the inferior surface of diaphragm and the superior and posterior surfaces of the right lobe of the liver. Divided into anterior (upper) and posterior (lower) layers. Surrounds the bare area of the liver.

rR1fog0.title: Second impact syndrome
rR1fog0.description: A potentially fatal condition thought to occur due to the rapid development of cerebral edema resulting from a second head injury in a patient who has not fully recovered from a recent traumatic brain injury (TBI), e.g., athletes who prematurely return to competitive sport after mild TBI.

7R14og0.title: Potato extract
7R14og0.description: A mixture of potato proteins used for cultivation in microbiology to promote the growth of various bacteria, yeasts, and fungi.

HR1Kog0.title: Mueller-Hinton agar
HR1Kog0.description: A growth medium used in microbiology for antibiotic susceptibility testing and to cultivate Neisseria and Moraxella species. For susceptibility testing of Streptococcus species, 5% sheep blood and NAD are typically added to the composition.

sR1tog0.title: Perirenal space
sR1tog0.description: A pair of retroperitoneal spaces that are enclosed within the anterior and posterior layers of the perirenal fascia. Each contains perirenal fat and envelops a kidney, adrenal gland, and associated vessels and collecting systems.

GR1Bog0.title: Anterior pararenal spaces
GR1Bog0.description: A pair of retroperitoneal spaces contained between the posterior parietal peritoneum and the anterior layer of the perirenal fascia. The right anterior pararenal space contains the second part of the duodenum and ascending colon with its mesentery. The left anterior pararenal space contains the fourth part of the duodenum and descending colon with its mesentery.

tR1XKg0.title: Posterior pararenal spaces
tR1XKg0.description: A pair of retroperitoneal spaces contained between the posterior layer of the perirenal fascia and the transversalis fascia. Contains fat.

FR1gKg0.title: Congenital Chagas disease
FR1gKg0.description: A congenital infectious disease caused by maternal-fetal transmission of the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi. Often asymptomatic but can manifest with prematurity, low APGAR score, low birth weight, hepatosplenomegaly, hematologic abnormalities (e.g., anemia, thrombocytopenia), and menigitis. Can progress to chronic Chagas disease if left untreated.

8R1OKg0.title: Egg on a string
8R1OKg0.description: A chest x-ray finding characterized by an enlarged cardiac silhouette (giving the appearance of an egg) and a narrowed superior mediastinum (giving the appearance of a string) due to stress-induced thymic atrophy. Associated with transposition of the great vessels.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Transposition of the great vessels (TGV)

uR1pKg0.title: Allergic salute
uR1pKg0.description: A habit of wiping the nose with a transverse or upward movement of the hand. Associated with allergic rhinitis.

ER18Kg0.title: Albumin-to-creatinine ratio
ER18Kg0.description: The ratio of urine albumin concentration to urine creatinine concentration. An ACR < 30 mg/g is considered normal to mildly increased; an ACR 30-300 mg/g for more than 3 months indicates likely chronic kidney disease. An ACR > 300 mg/g is severely increased.

vR1AKg0.title: Nitrogen wastes
vR1AKg0.description: A group of compounds (ammonia, urea, uric acid, and creatinine) that are produced during protein metabolism and eliminated from the body to remove excess nitrogen.

9R1N6g0.title: Truss
9R1N6g0.description: A belt with a pad used to externally compress a hernia after complete reduction. Can be used as supportive care of an uncomplicated inguinal hernia in a patient who refuses or cannot undergo surgery.

CR1q6g0.title: Back blows
CR1q6g0.description: A first-aid maneuver used along with chest compressions in the emergency stabilization of responsive patients with complete airway obstruction due to foreign body aspiration, with the goal of dislodging the aspirated object.

media.title: Back blows and chest thrusts in infants

xR1E6g0.title: Thirst center
xR1E6g0.description: A region of the hypothalamus that regulates the sensation of thirst. Consists of the organum vasculosum of the lamina terminalis, subfornical organ, and median preoptic nucleus. Activated by increased serum osmolality and angiotensin II.

BR1z6g0.title: Clinical swallow evaluation
BR1z6g0.description: A clinical assessment of the anatomy, function, and reflexes of the mouth, tongue, and mandible involving a trial of food and liquid. Informs decisions on dietary modification and further testing for oropharyngeal dysphagia (e.g., modified barium swallow).

-R1Dpg0.title: Right ventricular atrialization
-R1Dpg0.description: An anatomic abnormality caused by downward positioning of the tricuspid valve during cardiac development, which results in the right ventricle functionally becoming part of the right atrium. Associated with Ebstein anomaly.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Ebstein anomaly

0i1eJg0.title: Adynamic bone disease
0i1eJg0.description: A type of mineral and bone disorder characterized by low bone turnover, decreased collagen synthesis, and decreased minzeralization of bone collagen. Associated with chronic kidney disease.

bi1HJg0.title: TMV system
bi1HJg0.description: A classification system for bone pathologies associated with chronic kidney disease. Its components are bone turnover (T), bone mineralization (M), and bone volume (V).

Xi19Jg0.title: CGA classification
Xi19Jg0.description: A classification system used for the staging of chronic kidney disease. Its components include cause, glomerular filtration rate, and degree of albuminuria. Higher stages are associated with poorer prognosis.

ci1aqg0.title: Mosaic trisomy 21
ci1aqg0.description: A genetic cause of Down syndrome in which postzygotic nondisjunction during mitosis leads to the formation of two cell lines (one with a free trisomy karyotype and one with a normal karyotype). This results in varying phenotypic expression, ranging from the classic clinical presentation of trisomy 21 to a near-normal phenotype.

1i12qg0.title: Inferior phrenic veins
1i12qg0.description: A pair of tributaries of the inferior vena cava that drain the inferior surface of the diaphragm. The left inferior phrenic vein typically empties into the left renal vein or the left suprarenal vein.

Wi1Pqg0.title: Tubular basement membrane
Wi1Pqg0.description: The structural component of a nephron, which provides stability to tubular epithelial cells and restricts the passage of macromolecules between the tubule and interstitium.

di1oqg0.title: Lumbar veins
di1oqg0.description: A series of paired venous tributaries (usually four pairs) of the inferior vena cava that drain the posterior, lateral, and anterior abdominal wall. The first and second pairs of lumbar veins can also empty into the ascending lumbar or azygos veins.

Vi1Gqg0.title: Benign nephrosclerosis
Vi1Gqg0.description: A complication of chronic hypertension characterized by sclerosis of afferent renal arterioles and small caliber arteries. The associated vascular changes only moderately reduce the glomerular filtration rate. Can result in focal ischemic atrophy.

ei1xqg0.title: Ascending lumbar veins
ei1xqg0.description: A pair of veins that interconnect ipsilateral lumbar veins and drain the lumbar vertebral column. They join the subcostal veins to form the azygos vein on the right and hemiazygos vein on the left.

Ui1bIg0.title: Renal veins
Ui1bIg0.description: A pair of veins that drain the kidneys and empty into the inferior vena cava. The left renal vein receives the left suprarenal, left gonadal, and left inferior phrenic veins.

2i1TIg0.title: Suprarenal veins
2i1TIg0.description: A pair of veins that drain the adrenal glands. The right suprarenal vein empties into the inferior vena cava.  The left suprarenal vein empties into the left renal vein.

Ti16Ig0.title: Hepatic veins
Ti16Ig0.description: A group of veins that drain the liver and empty into the inferior vena cava. Includes the left hepatic, right hepatic, middle hepatic, and minor hepatic veins (which usually number between 1-5).

gi1FIg0.title: Balanced Robertsonian translocation
gi1FIg0.description: A chromosomal abnormality that involves the fusion of the long arms of two acrocentric chromosomes at the centromere. The short arms of the two chromosomes involved are lost.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

hi1crg0.title: Drug-induced skin reaction
hi1crg0.description: Damage to the skin and/or mucous membranes caused by an adverse reaction to a drug. Can be immunologic (e.g., hypersensitivity reactions) or nonimmunologic (pharmatoxicologic). Common clinical manifestations include fixed drug eruptions, erythema multiforme, urticaria, bullous drug eruptions, lichenoid drug eruptions, photosensitivity reactions, DRESS, and Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

3i1Srg0.title: Hernioplasty
3i1Srg0.description: A form of hernia repair in which mesh is used to close or reinforce the closure of an abdominal wall defect. Hernioplasty is associated with a higher risk of surgical site infection but a lower rate of hernia recurrence than simple suture repair (i.e., herniorrhaphy).

ji1_rg0.title: Left gastric vein
ji1_rg0.description: A vein that drains the fundus and upper body of the stomach and typically empties into the portal vein. Can form a part of the portocaval anastomosis as it receives venous drainage from the esophageal veins (caval system).

Pi1W7g0.title: Right gastric vein
Pi1W7g0.description: A vein that drains the stomach and empties into the portal vein or one of its branches.

4i137g0.title: Cystic veins
4i137g0.description: A group of veins that drain the neck of the gallbladder and the cystic duct and empty into the portal vein or one of its branches.

ki1m7g0.title: Superior pancreaticoduodenal veins
ki1m7g0.description: A pair of veins that drain the duodenum and pancreas. The anterior branch empties into the right gastroepiploic vein or the confluence of right gastroepiploic and right colic veins. The posterior branch empties into the portal vein

Oi1I7g0.title: Pancreatic veins
Oi1I7g0.description: A group of small veins that drain the body and tail of the pancreas and empty into the splenic vein.

li1v7g0.title: Left gastroepiploic vein
li1v7g0.description: A vein that drains the body of the stomach and the greater omentum. It courses through the gastrosplenic ligament and empties into the splenic vein.

Ni1-7g0.title: Posterior gastric veins
Ni1-7g0.description: A group of veins that drain the middle part of the posterior surface of the stomach and empty into the splenic vein. They may become prominent in patients with portal hypertension.

5i1iHg0.title: Left colic vein
5i1iHg0.description: A vein that drains the distal third of the transverse colon and the descending colon and empties into the inferior mesenteric vein.

Mi1MHg0.title: Sigmoid vein
Mi1MHg0.description: A vein that drains the sigmoid colon and empties into the inferior mesenteric vein.

ni17Hg0.title: Right gastroepiploic vein
ni17Hg0.description: A vein that drains the greater omentum, distal body of the stomach, and antrum of the stomach. Empties into the superior mesenteric vein.

Li1wHg0.title: Heterotaxy
Li1wHg0.description: An abnormality characterized by incorrect left-right axis arrangement of the thoracic and abdominal organs. Associated with asplenia, polysplenia, duplication of right-sided organs (e.g., two right lungs or two right atria), and cardiac abnormalities (e.g., transposition of the great arteries).

oi10sg0.title: Inferior pancreaticoduodenal veins
oi10sg0.description: A set of veins (anterior and posterior) that drain the head of the pancreas and duodenum. They empty into the superior mesenteric vein.

Ki1Usg0.title: Jejunal veins
Ki1Usg0.description: A group of veins that drain the jejunum and empty into the superior mesenteric veins.

6i1jsg0.title: Ileal veins
6i1jsg0.description: A group of veins that drain the ileum and empty into the superior mesenteric vein.

pi1Lsg0.title: Ileocolic vein
