pi1Lsg0.description: A vein that drains the terminal ileum, appendix, cecum, and part of the ascending colon. Empties into the superior mesenteric vein.

Ji1ssg0.title: Cecal vein
Ji1ssg0.description: A set of veins (anterior and posterior) that drain the cecum and empty into the ileocolic vein (a tributary of superior mesenteric vein).

qi1Csg0.title: Appendicular vein
qi1Csg0.description: A vein that drains the appendix and empties into the ileocolic vein (a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein).

Ii1YGg0.title: Right colic vein
Ii1YGg0.description: A vein formed by a group of tributaries that drain the ascending colon. Typically empties into the superior mesenteric vein.

ri1fGg0.title: Middle colic vein
ri1fGg0.description: A vein formed by a group of tributaries that drain the transverse colon. Typically empties into the superior mesenteric vein.

7i14Gg0.title: Cavocaval anastomosis
7i14Gg0.description: A valveless anastomotic network that connects the superior vena cava and inferior vena cava. Provides an alternative route for venous drainage in the event of superior or inferior vena cava occlusion. Includes the azygos-hemiazygos veins, vertebral venous plexus, and superficial body wall veins.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Important anastomoses and collateral circulation

Hi1KGg0.title: Common iliac veins
Hi1KGg0.description: A pair of veins (right and left) formed by the union of the external and internal iliac veins. They join to form the inferior vena cava at the level of L5.

si1tGg0.title: Internal thoracic veins
si1tGg0.description: A pair of veins that arise from the superior epigastric veins, run alongside the internal thoracic arteries, and empty into the brachiocephalic veins. They drain blood from the chest wall and breasts.

Gi1BGg0.title: Superficial epigastric vein
Gi1BGg0.description: A vein that drains the lower part of the anterior abdominal wall and empties into the great saphenous vein. It anastomoses with the thoracoepigastric vein (a part of superior vena cava system).

ti1Xtg0.title: 5'-nucleotidase
ti1Xtg0.description: An enzyme that hydrolyzes a nucleotide into a nucleoside and phosphate. Increased serum concentrations of 5'-NP are associated with hepatobiliary diseases and more specific than increased serum alkaline phosphatase concentrations.

Fi1gtg0.title: Acceleration-deceleration injury
Fi1gtg0.description: An injury caused by an abrupt halt of motion. Examples include coup-contrecoup injury (in which the brain hits the inner surface of the skull), subdural hemorrhage (due to shearing of bridging veins), and cervical spine injuries.

8i1Otg0.title: Tiopronin
8i1Otg0.description: A drug that interacts with cystine to form tiopronin-cystine disulfide, which is more water-soluble than cystine alone. Used to prevent the formation of cystine stones.

ui1ptg0.title: Superficial inguinal ring
ui1ptg0.description: A triangle-shaped opening of the inguinal canal located at the medial aspect of the external oblique aponeurosis.

Ei18tg0.title: Type I ovarian tumors
Ei18tg0.description: A type of low-grade ovarian neoplasm that typically develops as a large, unilateral, cystic lesion. Includes endometrioid, clear cell, and seromucinous carcinomas, low-grade serous carcinomas, mucinous carcinomas, and malignant Brenner tumors.

destinations.label: Overview of ovarian tumors →  Epithelial ovarian tumors

vi1Atg0.title: Type II ovarian tumors
vi1Atg0.description: A type of high-grade, aggressive ovarian neoplasm that typically involves both ovaries. Includes high-grade serous carcinomas, carcinosarcomas, and undifferentiated carcinomas.

destinations.label: Overview of ovarian tumors →  Epithelial ovarian tumors

Di11Fg0.title: Triangular ligaments of the liver
Di11Fg0.description: A pair of peritoneal ligaments that connect a lobe of the liver (right and left) with the inferior surface of the diaphragm. Each is formed by the fusion of coronary ligaments.

9i1NFg0.title: Thoracoepigastric vein
9i1NFg0.description: A vein that connects the superficial epigastric vein with the lateral thoracic vein. Forms a part of the cavocaval anastomosis. Can become dilated if there is occlusion of the superior or inferior vena cava.

Ci1qFg0.title: Lateral thoracic veins
Ci1qFg0.description: A pair of veins that drain the lateral thoracic wall and upper lateral abdominal wall and empty into the axillary vein. Communicates with the superficial epigastric vein via the thoracoepigastric vein.

-i1D8g0.title: Spermarche
-i1D8g0.description: The initiation of sperm development, which is triggered primarily by the effects of follicle-stimulating hormone on the testes. Associated with the development of secondary sexual characteristics.

aQ1Qug0.title: Sequential integrated test
aQ1Qug0.description: A prenatal screening test that combines measurements from the first trimester combined test and second trimester quadruple test.

YQ1nug0.title: Uremic frost
YQ1nug0.description: A rare dermatologic manifestation of uremia characterized by crystalline, white-yellow deposits on the skin that appear after sweat that has a high concentration of urea evaporates.

bQ1Hug0.title: Acetylcholinesterase
bQ1Hug0.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the breakdown of acetylcholine into choline and acetic acid. Found in the neuromuscular junction, at neuronal synapses, and on red blood cell membranes.

XQ19ug0.title: Hyperbilirubinemia
XQ19ug0.description: An increased serum concentration of bilirubin, which can be further characterized by the amount of unconjugated (indirect) and conjugated (direct) bilirubin. Etiologies include cholestasis, hemolysis, and hepatocellular injury. Can result in jaudice. Normal serum total bilirubin concentration is typically 0.1-1.0 mg/dL; normal serum direct bilirubin concentration is typically 0.0-0.3 mg/dL.

cQ1aEg0.title: Vesicular monoamine transporter-2
cQ1aEg0.description: A monoamine transporter protein that packages various neurotransmitters (epinephrine, norepinephrine, serotonin, histamine, and especially dopamine) in vesicles for exocytotic release. Drugs that inhibit VMAT-2 include reserpine and tetrabenazine.

1Q12Eg0.title: Glucuronic acid
1Q12Eg0.description: A carboxylic acid and metabolite of glucose that serves as a conjugating agent (for glucuronidation) to create more hydrophilic metabolites.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Metabolism of erythrocytes

WQ1PEg0.title: Greater splanchnic nerves
WQ1PEg0.description: A pair of preganglionic sympathetic nerve fibers that arise from the T5-T9 thoracic sympathetic ganglia, synapse at the celiac plexus and chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla, and carry visceral sympathetic fibers and sensory fibers.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

dQ1oEg0.title: Lesser splanchnic nerves
dQ1oEg0.description: A pair of preganglionic sympathetic nerve fibers that typically arise from T10-T11 thoracic sympathetic ganglia (can arise from T9-T10). They synapse at the celiac ganglion and aorticorenal ganglion and carry visceral sympathetic fibers and sensory fibers.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

VQ1GEg0.title: Least splanchnic nerves
VQ1GEg0.description: A pair of preganglionic sympathetic nerve fibers that arise from the T11 and/or T12 thoracic sympathetic ganglia.  They synapse at the celiac ganglion, aorticorenal ganglion, and renal plexus and carry visceral sympathetic and sensory fibers.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

eQ1xEg0.title: Lumbar splanchnic nerves
eQ1xEg0.description: A group of paired nerves (usually 2-4 pairs) that contain preganglionic sympathetic and visceral sensory fibers. They arise from the lumbar sympathetic trunk and synapse at the celiac, renal, and inferior mesenteric plexuses.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

UQ1bvg0.title: Sacral splanchnic nerves
UQ1bvg0.description: A pair of nerves that arise from the first two sacral sympathetic ganglia, contain preganglionic sympathetic and visceral sensory fibers, and synapse at the inferior hypogastric plexus.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

2Q1Tvg0.title: Anterior cranial fossa
2Q1Tvg0.description: The floor of the cranial vault, which contains the frontal lobes of the brain. Its anterior border is formed by the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone, the orbital plate of the frontal bone, and the lesser wings and body of the sphenoid bone. Its posterior border is formed by the lesser wings of the sphenoid bone.

fQ1kvg0.title: Middle cranial fossa
fQ1kvg0.description: A depression in the skull base that contains the temporal lobes of the brain. Its anterior wall is formed by the posterior margins of the lesser wings of the sphenoid bone, the anterior clinoid processes, and the anterior margin of the chiasmatic groove. Its posterior wall is formed by the anterior surface of the petrous temporal bones and the dorsum sellae.

TQ16vg0.title: Posterior cranial fossa
TQ16vg0.description: The posterior portion of the skull base, which contains the brainstem and cerebellum. Its anterior wall is formed by the posterior surface of the petrous temporal bone. Its posterior wall is formed by the occipital bone.

gQ1Fvg0.title: Acrocephalosyndactyly type I
gQ1Fvg0.description: An autosomal dominant condition caused by mutations in the FGFR2 gene on chromosome 10. Manifestations include bicoronal synostosis (which results in a flattened, recessed forehead), maxillary hypoplasia (which resulted in a flattened midface), protruding and widely-separated orbits, strabismus, and syndactyly (typically with bone and soft tissue fusion of the 2nd-5th digits).

SQ1yvg0.title: Pars membranacea septi
SQ1yvg0.description: A fibrous part of the heart that forms part of the interventricular septum. The atrioventricular bundle courses from the right atrium to the ventricles at its posterior surface.

hQ1cDg0.title: Local anesthetic systemic toxicity
hQ1cDg0.description: An adverse effect of local anesthetic injection caused by systemic absorption (typically because of proximity to highly vascular sites or accidental intravascular injection). Manifestations include central nervous system toxicity (e.g., tinnitus, perioral numbness, dysgeusia, agitation, seizures) and cardiovascular toxicity (e.g., bradyarrhythmias, hypotension, cardiac arrest).

3Q1SDg0.title: Travoprost
3Q1SDg0.description: A prostaglandin F2α analog used to treat open-angle glaucoma. Can cause permanent hyperpigmentation of the iris and reversible hyperpigmentation of periorbital tissue.

RQ1lDg0.title: Gonadectomy
RQ1lDg0.description: The surgical removal of a gonad (i.e., testis or ovary). Used to treat gonadal tumors (including prophylactic treatment for individuals with disorders of sex development).

iQ1JDg0.title: Eunuchoidal proportions
iQ1JDg0.description: A tall, slim body habitus with long extremities. Characterized by an upper body to lower body ratio of < 1 and arm span exceeding height by ≥ 6 cm. Can occur in male prepubertal hypogonadism.

QQ1uDg0.title: Object permanence
QQ1uDg0.description: The ability to understand that objects remain present even if they can no longer be seen. Typically develops between 6 and 9 months of age.

jQ1_Dg0.title: Schedule II drugs
jQ1_Dg0.description: A group of drugs that have been identified by the United States Drug Enforcement Administration to have high potential for abuse. Examples include methadone, hydromorphone, meperidine, oxycodone, fentanyl, cocaine,  and methamphetamine.

PQ1Wwg0.title: Isosexual precocious puberty
PQ1Wwg0.description: Early development of secondary sexual characteristics that match an individual's biological sex. Can occur in both central precocious puberty and peripheral precocious puberty.

4Q13wg0.title: Heterosexual precocious puberty
4Q13wg0.description: Early development of secondary sexual characteristics that are discordant with the individual's biological sex (e.g., breast development in boys or facial hair in girls). Causes include McCune-Albright syndrome, Leydig cell tumors, and congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

kQ1mwg0.title: Figure of 3 sign
kQ1mwg0.description: A radiographic finding characterized by a 3-shaped outline formed by dilatation of the aortic arch and left subclavian artery, indentation due to coarctation of the aorta, and dilatation of the descending aorta.

destinations.label: Acyanotic congenital heart defects → Coarctation of the aorta

OQ1Iwg0.title: Celiac plexus
OQ1Iwg0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic fibers that correspond with portions of the celiac trunk, superior mesenteric arteries, and renal arteries. Includes the celiac, superior mesenteric, and aorticorenal ganglia. Receives sympathetic input from the greater and lesser splanchnic nerves and parasympathetic input from the posterior vagal trunk.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

lQ1vwg0.title: Phrenic plexus
lQ1vwg0.description: A nerve plexus that arises from the celiac plexus and innervates the diaphragm and adrenal glands.

NQ1-wg0.title: Superior mesenteric plexus
NQ1-wg0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that correspond with the superior mesenteric artery. Derived from the celiac plexus. Innervates the midgut, liver, and pancreas.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

mQ1V9g0.title: Benign precocious thelarche
mQ1V9g0.description: A premature development of the breast without other associated secondary sexual characteristics. Can be unilateral or bilateral.

5Q1i9g0.title: Benign precocious menarche
5Q1i9g0.description: A premature development of uterine bleeding (can range from an isolated event to regular monthly bleeding) without other associated secondary sexual characteristics.

MQ1M9g0.title: Precocious pubarche
MQ1M9g0.description: The development of pubic hair before 8 years of age in girls and 9 years of age in boys.

nQ179g0.title: Short stature homeobox gene
nQ179g0.description: A gene located on the X and Y chromosomes that is involved in bone growth and development. SHOX gene deficiency is responsible for the development of short stature in several different genetic disorders, including Turner syndrome.

LQ1w9g0.title: Intermesenteric plexus
LQ1w9g0.description: A part of the autonomic plexus that corresponds with the abdominal aorta and lies between the origins of the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries. Connects the celiac plexus with the inferior mesenteric plexus and gives rise to the testicular/ovarian, renal, and ureteric plexuses.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

oQ10Cg0.title: Inferior mesenteric plexus
oQ10Cg0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that correspond with the inferior mesenteric artery and innervates the structures of the hindgut.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

KQ1UCg0.title: Flexor retinaculum of the foot
KQ1UCg0.description: A thick oblique band of fascia that extends from the medial malleolus to the medial aspect of the calcaneus. Forms the roof of the tarsal tunnel. Tendons of the deep posterior compartment, the posterior tibial vessels, and the tibial nerve pass under it.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Bones and joints

6Q1jCg0.title: Flexor retinaculum of the hand
6Q1jCg0.description: A thick strip of connective tissue at the wrist that spans from the pisiform and hook of hamate medially to the trapezium and scaphoid laterally. The flexor retinaculum forms the roof of the carpal tunnel binding down the flexor tendons of the digits and the median nerve, and also forms the floor of the Guyon canal.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Muscles and fascia

media.title: Cross-section of wrist showing the carpal tunnel and Guyon canal

pQ1LCg0.title: Tarsal tunnel
pQ1LCg0.description: A narrow passage posterior to the medial malleolus that is formed by the calcaneus and the flexor retinaculum of the foot. Contains the tendons of the posterior tibialis, flexor digitorum longus, and flexor hallucis longus muscles, the posterior tibial artery and vein, and the tibial nerve.

destinations.label: The leg, ankle, and foot → Bones and joints

media.title: Tarsal tunnel (malleolar canal) with flexor retinaculum of the foot

JQ1sCg0.title: Medication error
JQ1sCg0.description: A medical error in which a patient is prescribed the incorrect drug or the correct drug at an incorrect dose, frequency, or formulation. Can occur at the stages of ordering, transcribing, dispensing, and administering a drug.

qQ1CCg0.title: Renal failure
qQ1CCg0.description: A loss of renal function that can occur suddenly (acute kidney failure) or gradually (chronic kidney failure). Typically leads to increased serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen concentrations.

IQ1Yxg0.title: Penetrating brain injury
IQ1Yxg0.description: An injury to the head caused by an object that penetrates the skull and/or dura mater. High-velocity projectile injury (e.g., gunshot injury) causes significant tissue injury and is associated with a worse prognosis compared to low-velocity or nonprojectile injury (e.g., stab injury)

rQ1fxg0.title: Blunt head injury
rQ1fxg0.description: An injury caused by blunt force trauma to the head (e.g., falls, motor vehicle accidents). It is the most common cause of traumatic head injury.

7Q14xg0.title: White rami communicantes
7Q14xg0.description: A collection of structures that connect the preganglionic sympathetic nerve fibers of the spinal cord to the sympathetic trunk. Found in association with the T1-L2 spinal segments (thoracolumbar sympathetic outflow). The majority of the fibers are myelinated.

HQ1Kxg0.title: Flooding
HQ1Kxg0.description: A technique used in behavioral therapy to treat phobic disorders. The patient is exposed directly to a real, anxiety-provoking stimulus until the feeling of fear is replaced by a sense of calm and control.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Behavioral therapy

sQ1txg0.title: Fritsch maneuver
sQ1txg0.description: A technique used in obstetrics to aid the expulsion of the placenta after childbirth. One hand grasps the labia majora and presses it firmly into the vulva. Simultaneously, the second hand is positioned at the posterior side of the uterus and is pushed distally against the other hand. The placenta is then manually removed.

GQ1Bxg0.title: Anterior vagal trunk
GQ1Bxg0.description: A nerve formed by fibers of the left vagus nerve within the esophageal plexus. Innervates the intra-abdominal esophagus and stomach. Gives off a hepatic branch that supplies the liver and gallbladder.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

tQ1XBg0.title: Posterior vagal trunk
tQ1XBg0.description: A nerve formed by fibers of the right vagus nerve within the esophageal plexus. It innervates the intra-abdominal esophagus and stomach. Gives off branches to the celiac plexus.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

FQ1gBg0.title: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome
FQ1gBg0.description: A group of rare, inherited inflammatory disorders characterized by recurrent inflammatory attacks that involve multiple systems in the absence of infection or autoimmune disease. Includes three conditions: familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome, Muckle-Wells syndrome, and neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease.

uQ1pBg0.title: Heart defects with increased risk of infective endocarditis
uQ1pBg0.description: Heart defects that increase the risk of adverse outcomes in patients with infective endocarditis; includes a history of IE, prosthetic cardiac valves, prosthetic material used for cardiac valve repair, unrepaired cyanotic congenital heart disease, repaired congenital heart disease with residual defects, repaired congenital heart defects during the first 6 months after the procedure, and history of cardiac transplant with cardiac valvulopathy.

EQ18Bg0.title: Patients at high risk for infective endocarditis
EQ18Bg0.description: A group of patients who have an increased risk for adverse outcomes of infective endocarditis. These patients should receive antibiotic prophylaxis when they undergo procedures with a high risk for bacteremia. Includes patients who have: history of IE, prosthetic cardiac valves, prosthetic material used for cardiac valve repair, unrepaired cyanotic congenital heart disease, repaired congenital heart disease with residual defects, repaired congenital heart defects during the first 6 months after the procedure, or history of cardiac transplant with cardiac valvulopathy.

vQ1ABg0.title: Dental procedures with high risk of bacteremia
vQ1ABg0.description: Procedures that increase the risk of bacteremia in patients with infective endocarditis include: tooth extractions, dental abscess drainage, and procedures that involve gingival manipulation or oral mucosa perforation (including routine dental cleaning).

DQ11yg0.title: Secukinumab
DQ11yg0.description: A monoclonal antibody against IL-17A used to treat psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis.

wQ1hyg0.title: Ixekizumab
wQ1hyg0.description: A monoclonal antibody against IL-17A used to treat plaque psoriasis.

9Q1Nyg0.title: Caudate lobe
9Q1Nyg0.description: A segment of the liver located on its posterior aspect. Bounded inferiorly by the porta hepatis, on the left by the fissure for ligamentum venosum, and on the right by the inferior vena cava. Supplied by the hepatic artery and portal vein and drains directly into the inferior vena cava.

CQ1qyg0.title: Median arcuate ligament
CQ1qyg0.description: A ligamentous arch that connects the medial ends of the right and left diaphragmatic crura at the level of the T12 vertebra. Forms the anterior boundary of the aortic hiatus.

xQ1Eyg0.title: Celiac artery compression syndrome
xQ1Eyg0.description: A condition caused by compression of the celiac artery by the median arcuate ligament of the diaphragm. Manifestations include postprandial epigastric abdominal pain, weight loss, and an abdominal bruit.

BQ1zyg0.title: Splenic artery aneurysm
BQ1zyg0.description: A condition characterized by vessel wall dilatation of the splenic artery. Can be asymptomatic or associated with abdominal/flank pain, hematemesis, and/or hematochezia.

yQ1dAg0.title: Carl Jung's theory
yQ1dAg0.description: A collection of concepts of analytic psychology developed by Carl Jung. Includes the collective unconscious and the Jungian archetypes.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

AQ1RAg0.title: Jungian archetypes
AQ1RAg0.description: A component of Carl Jung's psychoanalytical theory that refers to parts of the collective unconscious that represent universal patterns, symbols, and images. They have universal meaning across cultures and include, for example, the persona, the self, and the shadow.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

_Q15Ag0.title: Acute vestibular syndrome
_Q15Ag0.description: A combination of new-onset vertigo, spontaneous nystagmus, nausea, vomiting, and gait instability that persists continuously for ≥ 1 day (the duration can only be determined retrospectively). Caused by unilateral impairment of the vestibular system. Vestibular neuritis is the most common peripheral etiology. Strokes of the brainstem or cerebellum are important central causes.

-Q1DAg0.title: Congenital contractural arachnodactyly
-Q1DAg0.description: An autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder caused by a mutation of the fibrillin-2 gene. Clinical features include Marfanoid habitus, joint contractures, and aortic root dilation.

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Differential diagnoses

0j1e_g0.title: Activin
0j1e_g0.description: A cytokine that belongs to the transforming growth factor-β protein family. Stimulates the release of follicle-stimulating hormone and promotes the development of various tissues (e.g., neural, cardiac, renal) during embryogenesis.

destinations.label: Cytokines and eicosanoids → Transforming growth factor family

aj1Q_g0.title: Allergic nasal crease
aj1Q_g0.description: A physical examination finding characterized by a transverse hyperpigmented or hypopigmented line at the junction of the lower third and middle third of the nasal bridge, which is the natural crease formed when the nose is pushed upwards by the allergic salute. Associated with allergic rhinitis.

Yj1n_g0.title: Ovarian germ cell tumor
Yj1n_g0.description: A type of ovarian tumor that is derived from the primordial germ cells of the ovary (e.g., oocytes). Can be benign or malignant. Subtypes of OGCTs include mature and immature teratomas, dysgerminomas, yolk sac tumors, embryonal carcinomas, and nongestational choriocarcinomas.

destinations.label: Overview of ovarian tumors →  Ovarian germ cell tumors

bj1H_g0.title: Axial skeleton
bj1H_g0.description: A part of the skeletal system that consists of the vertebral column, ribs, sternum, and bones of the head.

Xj19_g0.title: Appendicular skeleton
Xj19_g0.description: A part of the skeletal system that consists of the bones of the upper and lower limbs, scapula, clavicle, and hip bones.

cj1azg0.title: Superior transverse scapular ligament
cj1azg0.description: A ligament that traverses the suprascapular notch and attaches at the base of the coracoid process of the scapula. Converts the notch into a foramen through which the suprascapular nerve passes. Ossification of the ligament can lead to suprascapular nerve entrapment at the suprascapular notch.

1j12zg0.title: Supraglenoid tubercle
1j12zg0.description: A tubercle located above the glenoid fossa on the superolateral border of the scapula. The glenohumeral ligament of the shoulder joint attaches here.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Bones of the shoulder girdle

Wj1Pzg0.title: Cranial sutures
Wj1Pzg0.description: The fibrous joints that connect the bones of the skull. They facilitate expansion of the skull while the brain grows in size and then close and fuse. Examples include the coronal suture, sagittal suture, and lambdoid suture.

dj1ozg0.title: SVR
dj1ozg0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Systemic vascular resistance
2. Sustained virologic response

Vj1Gzg0.title: Language disorder
Vj1Gzg0.description: A communication disorder characterized by a delayed and/or impaired ability to comprehend and/or produce language (i.e., spoken, written, signed). Individuals classically have limited sentence structure, vocabulary, and speaking skills.

ej1xzg0.title: Superior thoracic artery
ej1xzg0.description: A branch of the first part of the axillary artery that runs anteromedially along the superior border of the pectoralis minor before it passes between it and the pectoralis major to reach the thoracic wall. Typical anastomoses with the intercostal arteries and the internal thoracic artery. Supplies the first and second intercostal, the superior part of the serratus anterior, the pectoral, and the subclavius muscles, as well as the skin of the thoracic wall.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries
Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage

Uj1b-g0.title: Thoracoacromial artery
Uj1b-g0.description: A short artery that branches off of the second part of the axillary artery and courses posteriorly to the pectoralis minor muscle before it pierces the clavipectoral fascia, and further divides into four branches: pectoral, deltoid, acromial, and clavicular.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage
Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

2j1T-g0.title: Subscapular artery
2j1T-g0.description: A branch of the third part of the axillary artery. It descends along the lateral border of the subscapularis on the posterior axillary wall before it divides into the thoracodorsal artery and the circumflex scapular artery. Supplies muscles in the shoulder region and forms part of the scapular anastomosis.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries
Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage

fj1k-g0.title: Dorsal scapular artery
fj1k-g0.description: An artery that branches from the subclavian artery or the thyrocervical trunk, supplies the levator scapulae and rhomboid muscles, and contributes to the arterial anastomosis around the scapula.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage
Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

Tj16-g0.title: Suprascapular artery
Tj16-g0.description: A branch of the thyrocervical trunk that contributes to the scapular anastomosis and supplies the rotator cuff, supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage
Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

gj1F-g0.title: Circumflex scapular artery
gj1F-g0.description: A branch of the subscapular artery that forms part of the scapular anastomosis. It passes through the triangular space of the axilla to reach the infraspinous fossa and supplies the deltoid, teres minor and triceps brachii muscles, the glenohumeral joint, and the adjacent skin.

destinations.label: Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage
Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

Sj1y-g0.title: Triangular space
Sj1y-g0.description: A triangular anatomical space that contains the circumflex scapular artery and vein. Bounded superiorly by the teres minor, inferiorly by the teres major, and laterally by the long head of the triceps.

media.title: Visual mnemonic: Axillary spaces and their borders

hj1cZS0.title: Anesthetic
hj1cZS0.description: A drug that produces temporary loss of sensation and/or awareness. Includes general anesthetics, which cause reversible loss of consciousness, and local anesthetics, which cause reversible loss of sensation in a specific, localized part of the body.

3j1SZS0.title: CAPS
3j1SZS0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome
2. Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome

Rj1lZS0.title: OGCT
Rj1lZS0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Oral glucose challenge test
2. Ovarian germ cell tumor

Qj1uZS0.title: Depressive disorders
Qj1uZS0.description: A group of conditions characterized by empty, sad, and/or irritable mood that result in decreased functionality. Differences between these disorders pertain to etiology and chronicity. Includes disruptive mood dysregulation disorder, major depressive disorder, persistent depressive disorder, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, substance/medication-induced depressive disorder, and depressive disorder due to another medical condition.

Pj1W0S0.title: Guided questioning
Pj1W0S0.description: A method used in cognitive therapy to create awareness for suppressed emotions and thoughts. The therapist asks a series of graded questions to eventually guide a patient's thought process and behavior toward therapeutic goals. This method aims to help patients develop new perspectives through active engagement and critical thinking.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Cognitive therapy

4j130S0.title: Journaling (psychiatry)
4j130S0.description: A technique used in psychotherapy, most commonly as a part of cognitive behavioral therapy. Involves writing prompts and exercises that guide the patient through reflective, introspective writing to express thoughts, feelings, and experiences. This technique aims to assist patients in gaining insight into emotions and thoughts.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Cognitive therapy

Oj1I0S0.title: ARF
Oj1I0S0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Acute renal failure
2. Acute respiratory failure
3. Acute rheumatic fever

mj1VaS0.title: CT scan without contrast
mj1VaS0.description: A computerized tomography scan in which no radiocontrast agent is used. Commonly used to evaluate head and spinal trauma, stroke, interstitial lung disease, and urolithiasis. Often used for patients at risk for contrast-induced nephropathy.

5j1iaS0.title: Phlebolith
5j1iaS0.description: A calcified blood clots within a vein. Most commonly develop in the pelvis, where they can mimic ureteric calculi on radiographic studies.

Mj1MaS0.title: Platelet-derived growth factor receptor α gene
Mj1MaS0.description: A gene that encodes platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFRA) protein. Mutations in this gene are associated with gastrointestinal stromal tumors and chronic eosinophilic leukemia.

nj17aS0.title: 24-hour urine profile
nj17aS0.description: A collection of urine over a 24-hour period. Used to measure total daily urine output and daily excretion of substances in urine, including creatinine, electroytes (e.g., sodium, calcium, oxalate), and hormones (e.g., cortisol).

pj1LYS0.title: Cognitive restructuring
pj1LYS0.description: A psychotherapeutic method that aims to assist patients in changing dysfunctional cognitive structures. First, automatic thoughts (e.g., dysfunctional/negative views of the self, future, and/or world) are identified. Then, the therapist uses guided questioning to rationally dispute and challenge the patient's cognitive distortions to help find a healthy rebuttal to irrational and/or maladaptive thoughts. Mainly used in cognitive behavioral therapy.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Cognitive therapy

rj1fbS0.title: Mindfulness
rj1fbS0.description: A practice that aims to bring one's full attention to the present moment without applying judgment in order to become less reactive to unpleasant internal phenomena. Teaching mindfulness has been integrated into various psychotherapeutic interventions and is a key component of dialectical behavioral therapy.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Dialectical behavioral therapy

7j14bS0.title: Emotional regulation
7j14bS0.description: The practice of actively and rationally choosing an emotional reaction to a stimulus. This practice involves reducing emotional vulnerability and altering a natural behavioral response (i.e., the individual makes an active choice between acting with or against a specific emotion). Emotion-regulation skills are taught within some types of psychotherapy (e.g., dialectical-behavioral therapy, schema therapy).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Dialectical behavioral therapy

Hj1KbS0.title: Distress tolerance
Hj1KbS0.description: An individual's capacity to withstand emotional distress. The development of this ability can be supported by teaching acceptance and willingness in challenging situations instead of acting on maladaptive urges. Learning and practicing distress tolerance is a module of dialectical behavioral therapy.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Dialectical behavioral therapy

sj1tbS0.title: Interpersonal effectiveness
sj1tbS0.description: An individual's ability to act effectively in the context of relationships, self-respect, and objectives. The aim of interpersonal effectiveness as a module of dialectical behavioral therapy is to assist patients in anticipating consequences of interpersonal situations, learning how to build and maintain functional relationships, and end destructive ones.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Dialectical behavioral therapy

tj1XXS0.title: Unconscious (psychiatry)
tj1XXS0.description: A mental system that is part of the topographic Freudian model. The unconscious system operates via primary process thinking (i.e., primitive, pleasure-seeking urges) and includes repressed thoughts. The unconscious system is normally inaccessible to conscious awareness because of negative consequences (e.g. shame, pain, embarrassement) but can be apparent in individuals who have psychosis and in children.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

Fj1gXS0.title: Preconscious (psychiatry)
Fj1gXS0.description: A mental system that is part of the topographic Freudian model. The preconscious system contains memories and/or thoughts of which one is not presently aware. After being consciously retrieved, these memories and/or thoughts are easily brought into awareness.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

8j1OXS0.title: Conscious (psychiatry)
8j1OXS0.description: A mental system that is part of the topographic Freudian model. The conscious system operates via secondary process thinking (e.g., logical, organized, mature, tolerant) and includes all ongoing thoughts of which one is currently aware.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

uj1pXS0.title: Burr hole craniotomy
uj1pXS0.description: A minimally-invasive neurosurgical procedure in which a hole 5–30 mm in diameter is drilled through the skull using a bone drill (trephine) to evacuate an epidural and/or subdural collection (e.g., hematoma, empyema). Can be used as a temporizing procedure in patients with impending brain herniation or to drain chronic collections.

vj1AXS0.title: Twist drill craniostomy
vj1AXS0.description: A minimally-invasive percutaneous neurosurgical procedure used in the management of chronic subdural hematoma. Consists of drilling a hole < 5 mm in diameter through the skull to evacuate the hematoma. Can be performed at the bedside.

Dj11cS0.title: Id (psychiatry)
Dj11cS0.description: A component of the structural Freudian model. The id is part of the unconscious mind and includes instinctive impulses and drives (e.g., aggression, sexual urges). It operates via primary process thinking and mainly seeks gratification, regardless of possible consequences and constraints.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

wj1hcS0.title: Super-ego (psychiatry)
wj1hcS0.description: A component of the structural Freudian model. The super-ego represents one's ideals and internalized cultural norms. It is responsible for rational and reality-oriented thought and suppresses the urges of the id.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

9j1NcS0.title: Ego (psychiatry)
9j1NcS0.description: A component of the structural Freudian model. The ego mediates between the id, super-ego, and external environment. It ensures effective functioning and delays the id's need for immediate gratification. This is achieved, for example, by using defense mechanisms to restrict unwanted impulses. In Carl Jung's psychoanalytical theory, the ego represents the current awareness of all emotions, thoughts, and memories.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

Cj1qcS0.title: Corpora amylacea
Cj1qcS0.description: A type of small, laminated structure composed of sulfated glycosaminoglycans. Found in several tissues, including the prostate, brain, and lung.

xj1EcS0.title: Allergic transfusion reaction
xj1EcS0.description: An allergic, nonanaphylactic reaction that is characterized by urticaria that develop during, towards the end, or shortly after transfusion of blood products. Caused by the presence of preformed recipient antibodies against plasma components in donor blood.

Bj1zcS0.title: Anaphylactic transfusion reaction
Bj1zcS0.description: An anaphylactic reaction that occurs within a few seconds to minutes after receiving blood products. Commonly occurs in individuals with IgA deficiency who receive blood products that contain IgA antibodies.

Aj1R1S0.title: Personal unconscious (psychiatry)
Aj1R1S0.description: A component of Carl Jung's analytical psychology that refers to anything within an individual's mind that is not presently conscious (e.g., repressed or forgotten memories). Some of these contents may be recalled to consciousness.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

_j151S0.title: Retrocalcaneal bursitis
_j151S0.description: An inflammation of the synovial bursa between the anteroinferior calcaneal tendon and posterosuperior calcaneus. Manifests with heel pain. Associated with calcaneal tendinitis and Haglund deformity.

zj1r1S0.title: Collective unconscious (psychiatry)
zj1r1S0.description: A concept of Carl Jung's analytical psychology that refers to structures of the unconscious mind that are shared among human beings. It is based on latent memories from the ancestral and evolutionary past that form characteristics of the human species and include the Jungian archetypes.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

-j1D1S0.title: Persona (psychiatry)
-j1D1S0.description: A component of Carl Jung's analytical psychology that refers to the public presentation of one's self, adapted to social norms and expectations. It conceals the true self and forms a compromise between the individual and society.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

ZP1ZWS0.title: Anima/animus (psychiatry)
ZP1ZWS0.description: A component of Carl Jung's analytical psychology that refers to the countersexual, unconscious aspects of the human psyche. In male individuals, the anima represents the feminine unconscious side; in female individuals, the animus represents the masculine unconscious side.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

0P1eWS0.title: Shadow (psychiatry)
0P1eWS0.description: A component of Carl Jung's analytical psychology that represents unconscious, repressed aspects of the personality. It is the source of instinctive, irrational impulses that are often considered negative.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

aP1QWS0.title: Self (psychiatry)
aP1QWS0.description: A component of Carl Jung's analytical psychology that represents the human psyche as a whole. It is an overarching concept that unifies male and female as well as conscious and unconscious. According to Jung, the self is superordinated to the conscious ego and the most complete expression of individuality.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

YP1nWS0.title: Theory of schema therapy
YP1nWS0.description: A theory based on the notion that people acquire certain basic schemas (i.e., mental structures) that help interpret and organize information and thereby establish certain behavioral patterns throughout the course of their lives. These schemas, in part, set the conditions for meeting psychological needs and, therefore, also influence behavior. This concept forms the basis of schema therapy.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Psychoanalytic theory

XP19WS0.title: Fusiform aneurysm
XP19WS0.description: A spindle-shaped arterial aneurysm that involves the entire wall of a vessel. Caused by atherosclerosis. Most commonly affects vertebrobasilar vessels.

cP1adS0.title: Acute subdural hematoma
cP1adS0.description: A subdural hematoma that becomes symptomatic immediately after or within 3 days of the inciting event. Typically progresses rapidly and often requires surgical evacuation of the clot.

1P12dS0.title: Subacute subdural hematoma
1P12dS0.description: A subdural hematoma that becomes symptomatic 4–20 days after the inciting event.

WP1PdS0.title: Chronic subdural hematoma
WP1PdS0.description: A subdural hematoma that becomes symptomatic ≥ 3 weeks after the inciting event. Typically enclosed in a vascular neomembrane.

2P1TVS0.title: Traumatic aneurysm
2P1TVS0.description: A rare type of aneurysm caused by damage to the vessel intima due to shearing forces from trauma.

fP1kVS0.title: Reverse differential cyanosis
fP1kVS0.description: A condition in which the lower body appears pink and the upper body appears cyanotic. Can occur in children with transposition of the great vessels if there is concomitant left ventricle outflow tract obstruction (e.g., coarctation of the aorta, aortic stenosis), which causes oxygenated blood from the pulmonary arteries to enter the descending aorta via a patent ductus arteriosus. Results in decreased preductal and increased postductal oxygen saturations.

media.title: Intracardiac shunt in the transposition of the great vessels

TP16VS0.title: Anal verge
TP16VS0.description: The transitional area where the anal canal meets the exterior skin (perianal skin).

hP1ceS0.title: Progressive primary tuberculosis
hP1ceS0.description: A severe form of primary tuberculosis that can occur in individuals with impaired cellular immunity (e.g., due to HIV infection) and/or an immature immune system (e.g., young children). Can be associated with necrosis and cavitation of lungs.

3P1SeS0.title: Hyperlactatemia
3P1SeS0.description: A serum lactate concentration of > 2 mmol/L. Etiologies include tissue hypoperfusion (e.g., in severe heart or lung disease, shock), liver disease (which leads to reduced lactate clearance), and metformin use. Can lead to lactic acidosis.

RP1leS0.title: Acceptance and commitment therapy
RP1leS0.description: A psychotherapeutic method that encourages patients to embrace their psychological state while simultaneously encouraging commitment to change. Can be used to treat anxiety-related disorders (e.g., obsessive-compulsive disorder) and psychosis.

iP1JeS0.title: Acceptance-based depression and psychosis therapy
iP1JeS0.description: A psychotherapeutic method that combines elements of behavioral activation with acceptance and commitment therapy. Used in combination with pharmacotherapy as maintenance treatment for patients with major depressive disorder with psychotic features.

QP1ueS0.title: Angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor
QP1ueS0.description: A combination of a neprilysin inhibitor (sacubitril) and an angiotensin receptor blocker (valsartan) used to treat heart failure. Should not be used in combination with ACE inhibitors because of an associated elevated risk of angioedema.

kP1mUS0.title: Axilla
kP1mUS0.description: A pyramid-shaped area at the junction of the arm and thorax, inferior to the shoulder joint, that is bounded by four walls, an apex (the axillary inlet), and a base. The axillary artery, axillary vein, brachial plexus, and lymphatic vessels pass through here between the trunk and the upper limb. Also contains the axillary lymph node groups, fat, and connective tissue.

OP1IUS0.title: Pelvic kidney
OP1IUS0.description: A failure of embryologic kidney development in which the kidney does not migrate and remains in the pelvis. Typically asymptomatic but can cause pelvic pain, nephrolithiasis, and ureteral obstruction.

lP1vUS0.title: Retroperitoneal sarcoma
lP1vUS0.description: A rare malignant connective tissue tumor in the retroperitoneal space. Often manifests at an advanced stage with nonspecific abdominal symptoms (e.g., pain, distention, and changes in bowel habits). The most common subtypes are liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma.

NP1-US0.title: Omentectomy
NP1-US0.description: The surgical resection of the omentum. Often performed for cytoreduction and debulking of epithelial ovarian tumors or metastatic spread of other cancers.

mP1V2S0.title: Clavipectoral fascia
mP1V2S0.description: A layer of deep fascia beneath the clavicular head of the pectoralis major muscle. Extends inferiorly from the clavicle and surrounds the subclavius and pectoralis minor muscles. The section between the subclavius and pectoralis minor is called the costocoracoid membrane. The section between the first rib and the coracoid process of the scapula thickens to form the costocoracoid ligament. Inferiorly, it forms the suspensory ligament of the axilla, to which the axillary fascia attaches.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries
Shoulder and axilla → Vascular supply and lymphatic drainage

5P1i2S0.title: Droplet nuclei
5P1i2S0.description: A particle < 5 µm in diameter that arises from dried residual portions of larger respiratory droplets. Produced during coughing, sneezing, and speaking. They remain suspended in air and can travel long distances. Responsible for airborne transmission of tuberculosis, measles, varicella, and other airborne diseases.

MP1M2S0.title: Ammonium chloride acidification test
MP1M2S0.description: A gold standard test used to diagnose incomplete distal renal tubular acidosis. An oral dose of ammonium chloride is administered, which is followed by serial measurements of serum bicarbonate concentration and urine pH over 6 hours. In patients with incomplete distal renal tubular acidosis, the urine pH fails to drop below 5.3.

destinations.label: Renal tubular disorders →  Distal renal tubular acidosis (type 1)

KP1UfS0.title: Right-sided heart failure
KP1UfS0.description: Heart failure due to structural or functional impairment of the right heart circulatory system that results in impaired delivery of blood flow to the pulmonary circulation and/or elevated venous pressures.

6P1jfS0.title: Deltoid ligament
6P1jfS0.description: A triangular band that stabilizes the medial ankle. Consists of the anterior tibiotalar ligament, tibiocalcaneal ligament, posterior tibiotalar ligament, and tibionavicular ligament.

pP1LfS0.title: Cardiothoracic ratio
pP1LfS0.description: A ratio calculated by dividing the cardiac diameter by the thoracic diameter on the same horizontal level in a posteroanterior view chest x-ray. A normal ratio ranges between 0.42-0.5. An increased ratio can indicate cardiomegaly but can also be caused by pericardial effusion.

JP1sfS0.title: Middle trunk of the brachial plexus
JP1sfS0.description: A bundle of nerve fibers formed from the anterior rami of spinal segment C7. It ends by dividing into an anterior and posterior division. Contributes to the musculocutaneous, radial, median, and lateral pectoral nerves.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Nerves

qP1CfS0.title: patients at risk of transfusion-associated graft versus host disease
qP1CfS0.description: A group of patients that includes the following: bone marrow transplant recipients, patients with primary or secondary cellular immunodeficiency, patients who receive blood products from first- or second-degree relatives, patients treated with alemtuzumab or purine analogs, and patients with Hodgkin lymphoma.

IP1YTS0.title: Nothnagel syndrome
IP1YTS0.description: A neurologic syndrome caused by damage to the quadrigeminal plate and superior cerebellar peduncles of the midbrain. Manifests with ipsilateral or bilateral oculomotor nerve palsy and ipsilateral cerebellar ataxia.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

rP1fTS0.title: Claude syndrome
rP1fTS0.description: A neurologic syndrome caused by damage to the dorsomedial aspect of the midbrain. Manifests with ipsilateral oculomotor nerve palsy and contralateral cerebellar hemiataxia.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

7P14TS0.title: Left-sided heart failure
7P14TS0.description: Heart failure due to structural or functional impairment of the left heart circulatory system that results in tissue hypoperfusion and/or increased pulmonary capillary pressure. Common underlying causes include arterial hypertension, coronary artery disease, and aortic stenosis.

HP1KTS0.title: Atonic bladder
HP1KTS0.description: A bladder that does not adequately contract due to underactivity of the detrusor muscle. Results in impaired ability to spontaneously urinate.

sP1tTS0.title: Hyperchloremia
sP1tTS0.description: A serum chloride concentration > 105 mEq/L. Commonly associated with normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. Other causes include dehydration, sodium balance disorders (e.g., due to excessive saline infusion), and adverse effects of drugs (e.g., carbonic anhydrase inhibitors).

GP1BTS0.title: Hypochloremia
GP1BTS0.description: A serum chloride concentration < 95 mEq/L. Common causes include heavy vomiting and diuretics, which both lead to metabolic alkalosis. Can also occur as part of compensatory mechanisms for chronic respiratory acidosis.

FP1ggS0.title: Developmental regression
FP1ggS0.description: The loss of a previously-achieved developmental milestone. Can occur in one or multiple domains of development (e.g., motor, language, social skills). Etiologies include hospitalization (temporary regression), child abuse, autism spectrum disorder, hereditary neurologic disorders (e.g., Rett syndrome, spinal muscular atrophy, mitochondrial encephalopathies, certain inborn errors of metabolism), acquired neurologic insults (e.g., meningitis, hydrocephalus), and hereditary myopathies.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Overview of abnormal development

8P1OgS0.title: Behavioral activation
8P1OgS0.description: A psychotherapeutic approach that focuses on facilitating change by raising patients' awareness of behavioral patterns that influence their mood. Treatment is aimed at encouraging activities that have a positive influence on their mood and reducing behavioral patterns that lead to avoidance and self-isolation. Used to treat patients with major depressive disorder and/or anxiety.

uP1pgS0.title: Sensorimotor stroke
uP1pgS0.description: A type of lacunar syndrome that results from small vessel occlusion that affects the thalamus and posterior limb of the internal capsule. Manifestations include contralateral hemiplegia and sensory loss in the face, arm, and leg.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

EP18gS0.title: Reticulocyte
EP18gS0.description: An immature red blood cell that develops in the bone marrow during erythropoiesis. Circulates in the blood for 1-2 days before developing into a mature red blood cell. Can increase in the blood due to increased erythropoiesis (e.g., secondary to hemolysis or hemorrhage).

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Red cell line: erythrocytes

vP1AgS0.title: Ataxic hemiparesis
vP1AgS0.description: A type of lacunar syndrome that results from small vessel occlusion that affects the posterior limb of the internal capsule. Can also involve the thalamus, cerebral peduncle, and/or pons. Manifestations include ipsilateral ataxia and hemiparesis. The cause of ipsilateral manifestations is not fully understood but may involve disruption of the cerebello-thalamo-cortical pathways.

destinations.label: Overview of stroke → Stroke symptoms by affected region

_P15hS0.title: Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor
_P15hS0.description: An antineoplastic agent that targets poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase 1/2, which are critical proteins in the base excision repair pathway for single-strand DNA breaks. Used to treat ovarian, breast, and prostate cancers. Examples include olaparib, rucaparib, and niraparib.

zP1rhS0.title: Olaparib
zP1rhS0.description: A first-generation oral poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor used as maintenance therapy for ovarian cancer associated with BRCA1/2 mutations.

-P1DhS0.title: Niraparib
-P1DhS0.description: An oral poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor used to treat epithelial ovarian cancer. Selectively inhibits PARP1 and PARP2.

Z41Z3S0.title: Veliparib
Z41Z3S0.description: An oral poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor used in combination with chemotherapy for the treatment of epithelial ovarian cancer.

041e3S0.title: Venography
041e3S0.description: A radiologic technique that uses intravenously injected contrast dye in combination with an imaging modality (e.g., CT, MRI, fluoroscopy) to evaluate blood flow through the veins. Can be used to diagnose deep vein thrombosis, identify suitable veins for arterial bypass grafting, and assess venous malformations.

a41Q3S0.title: Valsartan-sacubitril
a41Q3S0.description: A neprilysin inhibitor/angiotensin receptor combination drug used to treat chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Reduces all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, hospitalization for heart failure compared to enalapril (an ACE inhibitor).

Y41n3S0.title: Protein kinase inhibitors
Y41n3S0.description: A class of drugs that inhibits protein kinases, which are involved in multiple cell functions (e.g., growth, division). Commonly used as targeted therapy in cancer treatment. Includes tyrosine kinase inhibitors, serine/threonine kinase inhibitors, and MEK inhibitors.

b41H3S0.title: V600E mutated-BRAF oncogene inhibitors
b41H3S0.description: A group of protein kinase inhibitors that selectively target BRAF oncogenes that have a V600E mutation. Used to treat metastatic melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and thyroid cancer. Examples include vemurafenib and dabrafenib.

X4193S0.title: BCR-ABL and c-KIT tyrosine kinase inhibitors
X4193S0.description: A group of drugs that inhibit BCR-ABL and c-KIT tyrosine kinases. Used to treat diseases that are associated with hyperactivity of these proteins (e.g., chronic myeloid leukemia, gastrointestinal stromal tumor). Examples include imatinib, dasatinib, and nilotinib. A common adverse effect is fluid retention.

c41aRS0.title: MEK inhibitors
c41aRS0.description: A group of enzyme inhibitors (e.g., trametinib, cobimetinib) that target the mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase enzymes MEK1 and/or MEK2. Used to treat malignant melanoma and nonsmall cell lung cancer.

1412RS0.title: Trametinib
1412RS0.description: A MEK inhibitor used to treat malignant melanoma (in combination with dabrafenib), nonsmall cell lung cancer, and other cancers associated with dysregulation of the MAP kinase signaling pathway.

W41PRS0.title: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia
W41PRS0.description: The physiologic variation of the heart rate during respiration. Characterized by an increase in heart rate during inspiration and a decrease during expiration. More evident in young adults.

destinations.label: ECG → Determination of heart rate and rhythm

media.title: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia and right bundle branch block
Sinus arrhythmia and prominent U waves

d41oRS0.title: Reactive nitrogen intermediates
d41oRS0.description: A family of antimicrobial molecules derived from nitric oxide (which is produced by inducible nitric oxide synthase). They are highly reactive due to presence of unpaired electrons. Produced within macrophages to facilitate killing of microorganisms.

V41GRS0.title: Lipoarabinomannan
V41GRS0.description: A surface lipoglycan and virulence factor associated with Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Causes release of TNF-α and scavenges reactive oxygen species. Its mannosylated form is involved in regulating the innate immune response.

e41xRS0.title: Segmented neutrophil
e41xRS0.description: A mature neutrophil granulocyte. Develops from immature precursors (band neutrophils) over the course of 4-5 days.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

U41biS0.title: Neprilysin inhibitor
U41biS0.description: A drug that inhibits neprilysin (a metalloproteinase), which results in increased serum concentrations of natriuretic peptides, which induce vasodilation and natriuresis. Sacubitril is a neprilysin inhibitor that acts through an active metabolite (LBQ657).

241TiS0.title: Double mastectomy
241TiS0.description: The surgical removal of both breasts. Can be performed prophylactically to reduce the risk of developing breast cancer (e.g., in female individuals with BRCA gene mutations) or as part of breast cancer treatment.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Surgical resection of tumor and breast reconstruction

f41kiS0.title: Skin-sparing mastectomy
f41kiS0.description: The surgical removal of the breast tissue, nipple, and areola while leaving the majority of skin intact. Facilitates simultaneous reconstruction via implants or tissue.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Surgical resection of tumor and breast reconstruction

T416iS0.title: Nipple-sparing mastectomy
T416iS0.description: The surgical removal of breast tissue with sparing of the skin and nipple. Facilitates simultaneous reconstruction via implants or tissue.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Surgical resection of tumor and breast reconstruction

h41cQS0.title: Sacral micturition center
h41cQS0.description: A structure located in the intermediolateral gray matter of the S2-S4 portion of the spinal cord that contains nerves that form the micturition reflex arc. Consists of afferent parasympathetic nerves that transmit information about bladder fullness and efferent parasympathetic nerves that mediate bladder contraction.

341SQS0.title: Tasimelteon
341SQS0.description: A melatonin receptor agonist used to treat non-24-hour sleep-wake disorder.

R41lQS0.title: Dyssomnia
R41lQS0.description: A group of primary sleep disorders characterized by difficulty falling and/or staying asleep, which can result in hypersomnia (excessive daytime sleepiness). Includes insomnia disorder, obstructive sleep apnea, and narcolepsy.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Classification of sleep disorders

Q41uQS0.title: Erosive osteoarthritis
Q41uQS0.description: A subtype of hand osteoarthritis typically seen in older (postmenopausal) women. Characterized by the sudden onset of pain, swelling, and erythema of the interphalangeal joints, significant functional impairment, and the presence of erosions on imaging.

j41_QS0.title: Hypoandrogenism
j41_QS0.description: A deficiency of androgens, e.g., dehydroepiandrosterone, dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, and androstenedione. Symptoms of androgen deficiency include low libido, fatigue, depressive symptoms, infertility, and erectile dysfunction.

P41WjS0.title: Pyomyositis
P41WjS0.description: A bacterial infection affecting skeletal muscle that is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes. Symptoms typically include fever, pain, and swelling of the affected area (usually the lower extremities).

4413jS0.title: Myiasis
4413jS0.description: A parasitic infection caused by dipterous fly larvae feeding on affected tissue. Seen worldwide but most commonly in tropical and subtropical areas. The greatest risk factor is uncovered wounds. Treatment consists of removal of the larvae.

k41mjS0.title: C9orf72 gene
k41mjS0.description: A gene that encodes C9orf72 protein, which is involved in endosomal trafficking, regulation of autophagy, and promotion of axonal growth. Mutations in the gene are associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, often in combination with frontotemporal dementia.

O41IjS0.title: FUS gene
O41IjS0.description: A gene that encodes FUS protein, which is involved in DNA transcription and repair. Mutations in the FUS gene are associated with soft tissue sarcoma, frontotemporal dementia, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

N41-jS0.title: Anterior epistaxis
N41-jS0.description: A type of epistaxis that is caused by bleeding in the anteroinferior region of the nasal septum (Kiesselbach plexus), which results in bleeding from the nostrils. It is the most common type of epistaxis. Most common in children < 10 years of age.

m41VPS0.title: Posterior epistaxis
m41VPS0.description: A type of epistaxis that is caused by bleeding in the posteroinferior region of the lateral nasal cavity (Woodruff plexus). Most common in older individuals (> 50 years of age).

n417PS0.title: Rhinosporidiosis
n417PS0.description: A granulomatous fungal infection caused by Rhinosporidium seeberi that manifests with a polypoidal soft tissue mass, most commonly in the anterior part of the nasal cavity.

L41wPS0.title: Endoglin
L41wPS0.description: A type-I transmembrane glycoprotein expressed on endothelial cells. Acts as a coreceptor for ligands of the TGF-β superfamily. Plays a key role in angiogenesis.

641j4S0.title: Hypnic jerk
641j4S0.description: A spontaneous myoclonic contraction that occurs at the onset of the NREM phase of sleep (N1 stage). Commonly associated with a sensation of twitching or falling.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Sleep physiology

p41L4S0.title: Neutrophil left shift
p41L4S0.description: An increase in the number of immature neutrophils (banded neutrophils, metamyelocytes). Commonly occurs as a reaction to infection and/or inflammation because polymorphonuclear leukocytes are released into the circulation before they are fully mature in order to meet the increased demand.

J41s4S0.title: Little area
J41s4S0.description: An area of the anteroinferior nasal septum where the Kiesselbach plexus is located. Rupture of the vessels in this area is the most common cause of epistaxis.

q41C4S0.title: Rapid eye movement sleep-related parasomnias
q41C4S0.description: A group of sleep disorders characterized by a dissociation between rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and the awake state. Includes REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), nightmare disorder, and recurrent isolated sleep paralysis.

destinations.label: Sleep and sleep disorders → Classification of sleep disorders

I41YkS0.title: Trendelenburg gait
I41YkS0.description:
A gait abnormality characterized by leaning of the trunk toward one side of the body during the stance phase of gait due to weakness of the ipsilateral abductor muscles. Etiologies include Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease and
developmental dysplasia of the hip.

7414kS0.title: FEUrea
7414kS0.description: The percentage of glomerular filtered urea (Ur) that is excreted in the urine in relation to filtered creatinine (Cr). FEUrea (%) = (serum Cr × urine Ur)/(serum Ur × urine Cr) × 100. Uses include differentiation of prerenal and extrinsic causes in acute kidney injury and identification of the mechanism of hyponatremia in patients taking diuretics.

G41BkS0.title: Microsporidiosis
G41BkS0.description: A fungal infection caused by species within the order Microsporidia (e.g., Enterocytozooan, Nosema, Trachipleistophora). Typically causes opportunistic infection and can affect the ocular, pulmonary, intestinal, and musculoskeletal systems.

F41gOS0.title: Diagnostic overshadowing
F41gOS0.description: A diagnostic error that consists of misattributing physical symptoms to mental illness. Can lead to underdiagnosis of comorbidities in patients with psychiatric illness.

u41pOS0.title: Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy
u41pOS0.description: A prophylactic surgery that involves the removal of both fallopian tubes and ovaries to reduce the risk of developing epithelial ovarian cancer. Only used in patients at high risk for ovarian cancer (e.g., BRCA1/2 carriers, patients with Lynch syndrome).

v41AOS0.title: Intracardiac electrography
v41AOS0.description: The measurement of electrical activity of the heart measured by electrode catheters placed within the heart by cardiac catheterization. Used in the assessment of arrhythmias.

D411lS0.title: Automated external defibrillator
D411lS0.description: A portable electronic defibrillator designed for use by untrained lay rescuers for the treatment of cardiac arrest. Once pads are attached, it can independently assess rhythm, determine if a shock is required, and deliver a shock.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Basic life support (BLS)

w41hlS0.title: EMS
w41hlS0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Emergency medical services
2. Electrical muscle stimulation

B41zlS0.title: Contraindications for lumbar puncture
B41zlS0.description: Relative contraindications for lumbar puncture include signs of increased intracranial pressure, bleeding disorders (e.g., coagulation disorders, platelet disorders, anticoagulation therapy), and local infections (e.g., epidural abscess).

y41dNS0.title: Fluid attenuated inversion recovery
y41dNS0.description: A type of MRI sequence that involves eliminating the signal from fluids (e.g., cerebrospinal fluid). Most commonly used in MRI of the head to detect subtle abnormalities of the brain. Indications include suspected meningitis, multiple sclerosis, stroke, and hemorrhage.

A41RNS0.title: Opening pressure
A41RNS0.description: The pressure of cerebrospinal fluid detected at the start of lumbar puncture (normally 5-20 cm H₂O if the patient is lying down; values may be significantly higher if sitting). Causes of elevated opening pressure include CNS infection, hemorrhage, and hydrocephalus.

z41rNS0.title: Contraindications to anticoagulation
z41rNS0.description: Contraindications to anticoagulation depend on the indication but typically include significant active bleeding, severe anemia of unknown etiology, platelets < 50,000/mm³, and recent high-risk bleeding events (e.g., intracerebral hemorrhage).

-41DNS0.title: Obstructive sleep-disordered breathing
-41DNS0.description: A condition characterized by obstructive abnormalities in breathing pattern or of oxygenation or ventilation during sleep. These include snoring, mouth breathing, and breathing pauses. Obstructive sleep-disordered breathing comprises a spectrum that increases in severity from primary snoring to obstructive sleep apnea.

0k1emS0.title: Somatopleuric coelomic epithelium
0k1emS0.description: A mesodermal structure formed after the splitting of the lateral plate mesoderm by the intraembryonic coelom. It lies close to the ectoderm and forms the parietal layer of the pericardial, pleural, and peritoneal cavities.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Embryology of the peritoneum

ak1QmS0.title: Splanchnopleuric coelomic epithelium
ak1QmS0.description: A mesodermal structure formed after the splitting of the lateral plate mesoderm by the intraembryonic coelom. It lies close to the endoderm and forms the visceral layer of the pericardial, pleural, and peritoneal cavities.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Embryology of the peritoneum

Yk1nmS0.title: Pericardioperitoneal canals
Yk1nmS0.description: A pair of structures that arise from the lateral limbs of the intraembryonic coelom. They connect the developing thoracic and abdominal cavities.

bk1HmS0.title: Septum transversum
bk1HmS0.description: A mesodermal structure that lies between the developing heart and abdominal cavity. Gives rise to the central tendon of the diaphragm, connective tissue for the liver, and ventral mesentery.

Xk19mS0.title: Pneumatoenteric recesses
Xk19mS0.description: A pair of recesses that develop within the paraesophageal mesenchyme and extend between the lung bud and the foregut. The recess on the right side persists to form a part of the lesser sac.

ck1a5S0.title: Hepatoenteric recess
ck1a5S0.description: A downward extension of the right pneumatoenteric recess. Gives rise to a part of the lesser sac.

1k125S0.title: Mesogastrium
1k125S0.description: A type of mesentery that connects the stomach to the anterior and posterior abdominal wall. Further divided into a dorsal portion, which connects the greater curvature of the stomach to the posterior abdominal wall and gives rise to the greater omentum and splenorenal ligament, and a ventral portion, which connects the lesser curvature of the stomach to the anterior abdominal wall and gives rise to the lesser omentum and falciform ligament.

Wk1P5S0.title: Myeloid sarcoma
Wk1P5S0.description: A tumor that consists of myeloid blasts and is located at a site other than the bone marrow.

dk1o5S0.title: Active cancer
dk1o5S0.description: A term typically used to refer to histopathologically-confirmed cases of cancer (except for basal cell carcinomas and squamous cell carcinomas of the skin) that have been diagnosed and/or treated within the past 6 months. Also includes recurrent and metastatic cancer.

Uk1bMS0.title: Nalbuphine
Uk1bMS0.description: An opioid analgesic used to treat moderate to severe pain. It is an agonist at the κ-receptor and a mixed agonist/antagonist at μ-receptor. Can be administered intravenously, intramuscularly, or subcutaneously. Does not cause euphoria or respiratory depression.

2k1TMS0.title: Dynorphins
2k1TMS0.description: A group of endogenous opioid peptides that act as agonists primarily at the κ opioid receptor. Thought to be involved in the pathophysiology of several psychiatric conditions, including mood disorders and substance use disorders.

fk1kMS0.title: Heroin
fk1kMS0.description: An opioid drug most commonly used as a recreational drug, though it has been used as an analgesic medication outside of the United States. Can be taken orally or as a suppository, injected, smoked, or insufflated. Effects include euphoria, sedation, nausea, vomiting, respiratory depression, and hypotonia.

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Opioid-related disorders

Tk16MS0.title: Effective arterial blood volume
Tk16MS0.description: The proportion of total blood volume that is present within the arterial circulation. Low effective arterial blood volume (e.g., due to reduced cardiac output, vasodilation, or hemorrhage) stimulates the baroreceptor-mediated release of vasopressin and activates the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, leading to vasoconstriction and increased retention of sodium and water by the kidneys.

Sk1yMS0.title: OTC
Sk1yMS0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Over-the-counter
2. Oxytetracycline (a tetracycline antibiotic)
3. Ornithine transcarbamylase

3k1SnS0.title: 0.45% NaCl
3k1SnS0.description: A hypotonic crystalloid fluid containing sodium and chloride, each with a concentration of 77 mEq/L (77 mmol/L). Often expressed as a fraction of normal saline (0.9% NaCl).

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

Rk1lnS0.title: 0.22% NaCl
Rk1lnS0.description: A hypotonic crystalloid fluid containing sodium and chloride, each with a concentration of 39 mEq/L (39 mmol/L). Often expressed as a fraction of normal saline (0.9% NaCl).

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

ik1JnS0.title: Ceiling effect
ik1JnS0.description: A pharmacologic phenomenon in which the therapeutic limit of a drug is reached. Thereafter, an increase in dose does not increase the functional response but does increase the adverse effects.

Qk1unS0.title: Clinical features of deep vein thrombosis
Qk1unS0.description: Features include unilateral swelling, tightness, heaviness, warmth, erythema, dull pain in the affected limb, and, possibly, fever.

jk1_nS0.title: β-melanocyte-stimulating hormone
jk1_nS0.description: An endogenous peptide hormone that is cleaved from proopiomelanocortin. Involved in hypothalamic control of human body weight.

Pk1WLS0.title: Potentiometry
Pk1WLS0.description: A laboratory method to measure the concentration of a solute in plasma. Performed by measuring the electrical potential generated by the solute when the solute selective membrane is immersed in plasma. Types of potentiometry include indirect potentiometry (dilution of the sample) and direct potentiometry (without dilution).

4k13LS0.title: Receptor affinity
4k13LS0.description: The degree to which a ligand binds to a target receptor. Ligands with low affinity can be displaced from a target receptor by ligands with higher affinity for the same receptor.

kk1mLS0.title: Pil1
kk1mLS0.description: A virulence factor expressed on the surface of S. gallolyticus that binds to collagen, interferes with biofilm formation, and facilitates initial attachment and colonization of heart valves.

Ok1ILS0.title: Indications for prophylaxis against infective endocarditis
Ok1ILS0.description: A set of indications for preprocedural prophylaxis against infective endocarditis. Includes history of infective endocarditis, presence of prosthetic cardiac valves or prosthetic material used for cardiac valve repair, unrepaired cyanotic congenital heart disease, repaired congenital heart disease with residual defects, repaired congenital heart defects during the first 6 months after the procedure, and history of cardiac transplant with cardiac valvulopathy. Applies to the following procedures: dental procedures that involve manipulation of gingival tissue or the periapical region of the teeth, procedures involving perforation, incision, or biopsy of the oral or respiratory tract mucosa, and surgical procedures for management of infected skin and soft tissue.

lk1vLS0.title: Fibrocystin
lk1vLS0.description: A membrane-spanning protein involved in the maintenance of primary cilia of the renal collecting duct and biliary epithelial cells. Mutations in the gene that encodes this protein are associated with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease.

nk17oS0.title: PPN
nk17oS0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Partial parenteral nutrition (also known as peripheral parenteral nutrition)
2. Paraproteinemic neuropathy

Lk1woS0.title: NAM
Lk1woS0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. N-acetylmuramic acid
2. Negative allosteric modulation
3. Necrotizing autoimmune myopathy

qk1CKS0.title: Breakthrough cancer pain
qk1CKS0.description: A sudden increase in pain in patients who have cancer. Can occur spontaneously (without obvious precipitating factor), incidentally (with identifiable cause, such as certain movements), or as a result of pain medication wearing off.

rk1f6S0.title: Proximal DVT
rk1f6S0.description: A venous thrombosis involving one or more of the proximal veins of the lower limbs (i.e., the popliteal, femoral, common femoral, profunda femoris, and iliac veins) and/or the inferior vena cava.

Gk1B6S0.title: Recurrent venous thromboembolism
Gk1B6S0.description: Venous thromboembolism that recurs after the completion of the first 2 weeks of antithrombotic therapy

Ek18pS0.title: Dextrose solutions
Ek18pS0.description: Hypotonic crystalloid solutions containing dextrose in water at different concentrations: e.g., 5% dextrose in water (D5W) contains 5 g/dL dextrose; 10% dextrose in water (D10W) contains 10 g/dL dextrose; 50% dextrose in water (D50W) contains 50 g/dL dextrose.

Dk11JS0.title: Hypervolemia
Dk11JS0.description: A condition in which the volume of extracellular fluid is increased due to an excess of total body sodium (i.e., salt) and water. Clinical features include peripheral edema, abdominal ascites, weight gain, and dyspnea.

wk1hJS0.title: Hypertonic saline
wk1hJS0.description: A hypertonic crystalloid solution used for the treatment of hyponatremia and cerebral edema. Various concentrations are available, e.g., 3% NaCl, which comprises 513 mEq/L (513 mmol/L) of both sodium and chloride, and 5% NaCl, which comprises 856 mEq/L (856 mmol/L) of both sodium and chloride. Highly concentrated formulations (e.g., 23.4%) are also used.

Ck1qJS0.title: Euvolemia
Ck1qJS0.description: The presence of normal amounts of water and blood volume in the body. Typically used in the context of a volume assessment (e.g., in the evaluation of sodium disorders, and renal failure) as a contrast to hypovolemia and hypervolemia.

_k15qS0.title: Mature minor
_k15qS0.description: An unemancipated minor who is deemed to have the capacity to make medical decisions (e.g., accept or refuse treatments) without knowledge and/or agreement from their parents. The definition of a mature minor varies in each state and is dictated by individual statutes or judicial decisions.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

zk1rqS0.title: Mature minor doctrine
