zk1rqS0.description: A law that allows mature minors (i.e., unemancipated minors deemed mature enough to make medical decisions) to proceed with medical treatment if the minor is an older adolescent, can understand the ramifications of their decisions, and the benefits of making the decision outweighs the risks. The exact implementation of the law varies from state to state.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

-k1DqS0.title: Deep vein
-k1DqS0.description: A collection of veins that lie deep to the deep fascia and function primarily to return the blood in the systemic circulation to the heart. Deep veins of the upper limb include the brachial, axillary, and subclavian veins. Deep veins of the lower limb include the femoral, tibial, and popliteal veins. The internal jugular vein is the deep vein of the neck.

ZO1ZIS0.title: Superficial vein
ZO1ZIS0.description: A collection of veins that lie within the subcutaneous tissue, superficial to the deep fascia. Primarily involved in thermoregulation via vasodilation and vasoconstriction. Also serve as collateral venous drainage if the deep veins are blocked. Includes superficial veins of the upper limb (cephalic and basilic veins) lower limb (small and great saphenous veins), and neck (external jugular and anterior jugular veins).

aO1QIS0.title: Acquired cystic kidney disease
aO1QIS0.description: A condition characterized by the formation of multiple, small cysts in the kidneys in patients who are undergoing renal replacement therapy. Typically asymptomatic but associated with the development of renal cell carcinoma.

YO1nIS0.title: Melanogenesis
YO1nIS0.description: The process by which melanocytes produce the skin pigment melanin in melanosomes. Two different pigments can be synthesized: eumelanin (brown to black color) and pheomelanin (yellow to red color). The ratio of these pigments influences the color of skin, hair, and eyes.

XO19IS0.title: Methylnaltrexone
XO19IS0.description: A peripherally acting μ-opioid receptor antagonist. It is a quaternary ammonium derivative of naltrexone with limited ability to penetrate the blood-brain barrier. Can reverse the adverse effects of opioid treatment (e.g., constipation, pruritus) without diminishing pain relief or precipitating withdrawal.

cO1arS0.title: Naloxegol
cO1arS0.description: A peripherally acting μ-opioid receptor antagonist. It is a pegylated conjugate of naloxone with limited ability to penetrate the blood-brain barrier. Antagonizes μ-opioid receptors in the gastrointestinal tract. Used to treat patients with opioid-induced bowel dysfunction. Does not provide analgesia or induce withdrawal.

1O12rS0.title: Alvimopan
1O12rS0.description: A peripherally acting μ-opioid receptor antagonist with limited blood-brain barrier penetration. Used to treat postoperative ileus. Does not provide analgesia or induce withdrawal.

VO1GrS0.title: Naldemedine
VO1GrS0.description: A peripherally acting opioid receptor antagonist. It is a structurally modified amide derivative of naloxone that is unable to cross the blood-brain barrier. Antagonizes peripheral μ-, κ-, and δ-opioid receptors. Used to treat opioid-induced constipation.

eO1xrS0.title: Diphenoxylate
eO1xrS0.description: A centrally acting opioid used to treat diarrhea that prolongs intestinal transit time by slowing contractions. Only available as a combination drug with atropine to prevent abuse.

2O1T7S0.title: Suicidal behavior
2O1T7S0.description: Any thoughts of or attempts to end one's own life.

TO167S0.title: Type I secretion system
TO167S0.description: A group of structurally and functionally related protein complexes in the cell envelope of Gram-negative bacteria that facilitate the secretion of virulence factors (e.g., proteases, lipases).

gO1F7S0.title: Type IV secretion system
gO1F7S0.description: A group of structurally and functionally related protein complexes in the cell envelope of Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria that facilitate conjugation, transportation of proteins, and transformation of DNA to target cells.

SO1y7S0.title: Outer membrane protein A
SO1y7S0.description: A part of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria that serves as a key virulence factor for evasion of host defense mechanisms, biofilm formation, antibiotic resistance, and immunomodulation.

3O1SHS0.title: Coagulase positive Staphylococcus
3O1SHS0.description: A class of staphylococci that produces coagulase. It is a major part of the natural skin flora but can cause skin and soft tissue infections, endocarditis, osteomyelitis, and toxin-mediated diseases. The most common type is Staphylococcus aureus.

OO1IsS0.title: Terminal villi
OO1IsS0.description: A developmental stage of chorionic villi in the placenta (4th month of gestation). Characterized by a reduced number of cytotrophoblast cells (Langhans cells) on their inner layer. They float freely in the intervillous space and facilitate fetomaternal gas and nutrient exchange.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

lO1vsS0.title: T-wave flattening
lO1vsS0.description: An ECG finding characterized by a reduction in amplitude of the T wave. Can be caused by myocardial ischemia, hypokalemia, hypothyroidism, and hypoglycemia.

NO1-sS0.title: Features of overt GI bleeding
NO1-sS0.description: A collection of features of overt hemorrhage from an upper or lower gastrointestinal source. Include hematemesis, melena, and hematochezia.

mO1VGS0.title: Biphasic T wave
mO1VGS0.description: A T wave on ECG that consists of an upward and downward deflection. The direction of the initial deflection is variable. Etiologies of a biphasic T wave with an initial positive deflection include acute myocardial ischemia and Wellens syndrome. Hypokalemia can result in a biphasic T wave with an initial negative deflection.

5O1iGS0.title: Cytolethal-distending toxin
5O1iGS0.description: A heat-labile toxin produced by several bacterial species, including H. ducreyi, E. coli, Shigella spp., and Campylobacter spp.. Impairs epithelial cell and lymphocyte function and induces the inflammasome.

MO1MGS0.title: Villous trees
MO1MGS0.description: A collection of structures that originate from the chorionic plate and branch into the intervillous space. They facilitate fetomaternal gas and nutrient exchange in the placenta. Consists of stem villi, intermediate villi, terminal villi, and anchoring villi.

destinations.label: The placenta, umbilical cord, and amniotic sac → The placenta

KO1UtS0.title: Lipid panel
KO1UtS0.description: A group of laboratory tests used to diagnose and follow-up patients with dyslipidemia, and for the evaluation of cardiovascular risk. Generally includes triglycerides, total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and non-HDL levels.

6O1jtS0.title: Basic airway adjuncts
6O1jtS0.description: Devices used to enhance the success of basic airway maneuvers, e.g., oropharyngeal airway, nasopharyngeal airway

7O14FS0.title: Tarasoff decision
7O14FS0.description: A California Supreme Court case (Tarasoff v. Regents of the University of California) that established the physician duty to warn. Based on the Tarasoff decision, if a patient discloses a plan to harm another person, the physician is obligated to break doctor-patient confidentiality and inform the police to warn the potential victim.

destinations.label: Ethics of communicating medical information → Confidentiality

HO1KFS0.title: Gardnerella
HO1KFS0.description: A genus of gram variable, facultative anaerobic, pleomorphic bacteria that can cause bacterial vaginosis. Gardnerella vaginalis is the only species within this genus.

tO1X8S0.title: Acute heart failure
tO1X8S0.description: The rapid onset of new or worsening signs and symptoms of heart failure. May occur in patients with no previous diagnosis (de novo heart failure) or patients with preexisting heart failure (acutely decompensated heart failure).

DO11uS0.title: Monoamine-depleting agents
DO11uS0.description: A group of drugs that cause reversible inhibition of vesicular monoamine transporter-2 (VMAT-2), which results in impaired packaging of monoamines (especially dopamine) into vesicles and decreased dopamine release. Used to treat chorea associated with Huntington disease, tardive dyskinesia, and Tourette syndrome.

wO1huS0.title: Clinical features of infective endocarditis
wO1huS0.description: Features include constitutional symptoms (e.g., fevers, chills, tachycardia, weight loss), cough, pleuritic chest pain, new heart murmur or arrhythmia, and extracardiac manifestations (e.g., cutaneous changes, renal injury).

9O1NuS0.title: Gonadal vein
9O1NuS0.description: A pair of veins that drain the testis (in male individuals) or ovaries (in female individuals). The right gonadal vein empties into the inferior vena cava. The left gonadal vein empties into the left renal vein.

CO1quS0.title: Left suprarenal vein
CO1quS0.description: A vein that drains the left adrenal gland and empties into the left renal vein.

xO1EuS0.title: Right suprarenal vein
xO1EuS0.description: A vein that drains the right adrenal gland and empties into the inferior vena cava.

BO1zuS0.title: Damage-associated molecular patterns
BO1zuS0.description: A heterogeneous group of host molecules that can trigger a noninfectious inflammatory response when detected by pattern recognition receptors (PRRs). They are released from injured tissue or dying cells. Examples include heat shock proteins, fibrinogen, defensins, and mtDNA.

yO1dES0.title: Nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like receptors
yO1dES0.description: A family of intracellular pattern-recognition receptors that can recognize both pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). Thought to be involved in innate immune system signaling (e.g., activation of MAPKs and the NF-κB pathway).

_O15ES0.title: Clinical features of pulmonary embolism
_O15ES0.description: Includes acute onset of dyspnea, tachycardia, tachypnea, pleuritic chest pain, cough, hemoptysis, and associated features of DVT.  Patients with massive PE may have syncope or presyncope, jugular venous distention, Kussmaul sign, obstructive shock, and/or circulatory collapse.

media.title: Pulmonary embolism: pathophysiologic response of the lung

zO1rES0.title: Prepyloric vein
zO1rES0.description: A vein that runs anteriorly to the pylorus and empties into the right gastric vein. Used as a marker to identify the pylorus of the stomach during surgery.

-O1DES0.title: Pallor
-O1DES0.description: A morphologic descriptor for paleness of the skin and/or mucous membranes.

Zl1ZvS0.title: Floating elbow fracture
Zl1ZvS0.description: A concomitant humerus (supracondylar) fracture and forearm (radius and/or ulna) fracture in the same limb.

0l1evS0.title: Direct cerebral venography
0l1evS0.description: An invasive radiological examination of the cerebral venous system. A microcatheter is used to inject contrast directly into the dural sinus or cerebral veins. Has been largely replaced by CT and MRI studies but can be  combined with endovascular treatment (e.g., local thrombolysis) to diagnose and treat cerebral venous thrombosis.

al1QvS0.title: Septic cerebral venous thrombosis
al1QvS0.description: A subtype of cerebral venous thrombosis with an infectious etiology. Most commonly results from direct spread of infection from adjacent structures such as the face, ears, or nose.

Yl1nvS0.title: Insensible water losses
Yl1nvS0.description: The volume of body fluids lost daily from the respiratory system, skin, and stool; can increase during illness, e.g., with fever, diarrhea. These losses are not easily measured and are typically estimated.

bl1HvS0.title: Features of autoimmune hemolytic anemia
bl1HvS0.description: A collection of findings that includes ↓ hemoglobin, ↑ reticulocytes, ↑ bilirubin, ↑ LDH, a positive Coombs test, and the presence of spherocytes on a peripheral blood smear.

Xl19vS0.title: Inferior vena cava thrombosis
Xl19vS0.description: A thrombus in the inferior vena cava, which can manifest with back or flank pain, hematuria, oliguria/anuria, leg pain, leg swelling, and/or dilated leg veins. Risk factors include renal cell carcinoma, abdominal trauma, and large abdominal masses that cause extrinsic compression of the vein.

cl1aDS0.title: Mechanical circulatory support
cl1aDS0.description: A mechanical device that provides support for patients with circulatory failure. Temporary devices include intra-aortic balloon pump, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and extracorporeal ventricular assist devices. Long-term support can be provided by intracorporeal ventricular assist devices or an artificial heart.

1l12DS0.title: MCS
1l12DS0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Microscopy (or microbial), culture, and sensitivity
2. Mechanical circulatory support

Wl1PDS0.title: Lymphoscintigraphy
Wl1PDS0.description: A nuclear medicine imaging technique used to image the lymphatic system. Can be used to localize areas of obstruction in patients with lymphedema and to identify lymph node metastases from malignancies.

dl1oDS0.title: Electrical impedance plethysmography
dl1oDS0.description: A noninvasive test to evaluate for deep venous thrombosis. Assesses blood flow by measuring changes in vessel volume associated with small changes in electrical impedance. Its use has largely been replaced by compression Doppler ultrasonography.

el1xDS0.title: Human herpes virus
el1xDS0.description: A member of a large family of DNA viruses (Herpesviridae). Includes herpes simplex viruses 1 and 2, varicella zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, human herpes viruses 6 and 7, and Kaposi sarcoma-associated virus.

Ul1bwS0.title: IL-17 inhibitors
Ul1bwS0.description: A group of monoclonal antibodies used to treat chronic inflammatory diseases, such as psoriasis and ankylosing spondylitis. Examples include secukinumab, ixekizumab, brodalumab.

2l1TwS0.title: IL-23 inhibitors
2l1TwS0.description: A group of monoclonal antibodies used to treat autoimmune inflammatory disorders, such as psoriasis, Crohn disease, and ulcerative colitis. Examples include guselkumab, tildrakizumab, risankizumab, and ustekinumab (which also inhibits IL-12).

fl1kwS0.title: Marsh classification
fl1kwS0.description: The (modified) Marsh classification is used in the histopathologic diagnosis of celiac disease. Findings are rated on a scale of 0 (no changes; celiac disease unlikely) to IIIc (significant changes; celiac disease likely) according to the presence and severity of three pathognomonic changes: villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, and intraepithelial lymphocytic infiltration.

gl1FwS0.title: 12:21 chromosomal translocation
gl1FwS0.description: The most common chromosomal translocation in childhood B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Observed in ~ 25% cases of pediatric B-cell ALL. The 12;21 translocation results in the ETV6-RUNX1 fusion gene, which encodes a chimeric transcription factor affecting hematopoietic cell proliferation and differentiation. Associated with a favorable prognosis.

hl1c9S0.title: Functional dyspepsia
hl1c9S0.description: A functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by upper GI symptoms (e.g., epigastric pain, bloating, etc.) that may vary in severity. It is a diagnosis of exclusion and is usually diagnosed when no organic cause for the symptoms can be identified. Its pathophysiology is not entirely understood.

3l1S9S0.title: Functional heartburn
3l1S9S0.description: A condition characterized by symptoms of reflux that cannot be attributed to esophageal acid exposure or pathologic findings during the diagnostic workup (e.g., during esophagogastroduodenoscopy or esophageal pH monitoring). It is a diagnosis of exclusion.

Rl1l9S0.title: Lateral ECG leads
Rl1l9S0.description: The ECG leads I, aVL, V5, and V6. ST elevation or dynamic T wave inversion in these leads corresponds to infarction of the myocardium supplied by the left circumflex artery, the diagonal branch of the left anterior descending artery (LAD), or the distal LAD.

Ql1u9S0.title: DGP
Ql1u9S0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Deamidated gliadin peptide 
2. Diabetic gastroparesis

jl1_9S0.title: Xerotrachea and xerobronchitis
jl1_9S0.description: A drying of the mucous membranes of the trachea, bronchi, and bronchioles. Can cause a nonproductive cough. Etiologies include Sjögren syndrome and artificial airways that bypass the nasal passages (e.g., tracheostomy).

4l13CS0.title: Primary Sjögren syndrome
4l13CS0.description: A case of Sjögren syndrome that is not caused by an underlying rheumatologic disease. Typically associated with the HLA-DR52 and HLA-DRB1 haplotypes. Parotid swelling and antibodies against the Ro/SS-A and La/SS-B antigens are more common in primary than secondary Sjögren syndrome.

kl1mCS0.title: Secondary Sjögren syndrome
kl1mCS0.description: The occurrence of Sjogren syndrome concomitantly with another autoimmune disease (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, primary biliary cirrhosis).

Ol1ICS0.title: Onasemnogene abeparvovec
Ol1ICS0.description: A recombinant, virus vector-based gene therapy used to treat spinal muscular atrophy. It delivers a normal copy of the SMN1 gene, which encodes human survival motor neuron (SMN) protein, to the neurons of the anterior horns of the spinal cord

5l1ixS0.title: Sézary cell
5l1ixS0.description: An atypical lymphocyte with characteristic grooved nuclei seen on peripheral blood smear or bone marrow biopsy in patients with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome).

Ml1MxS0.title: Deep vein thrombosis of the upper extremity
Ml1MxS0.description: A type of deep vein thrombosis that most commonly affects the subclavian and axillary veins. Manifestations include pain, pitting edema, and dilation of the superficial veins in the affected upper limb. Risk factors include indwelling central venous catheters in the neck or upper extremity, prothrombotic states (e.g., malignancy), and immobilization. Less common than deep vein thrombosis in the lower extremities.

destinations.label: Deep vein thrombosis → Subtypes and variants

nl17xS0.title: Early-diastolic blood flow reversal
nl17xS0.description: A finding on pulse-wave Doppler study characterized by transient reversal of blood flow during early diastole. It is part of the normal triphasic arterial flow response in peripheral arteries.

Ll1wxS0.title: Urinary stress test
Ll1wxS0.description: A test for stress incontinence. While supine or standing, the patient performs the Valsalva maneuver or coughs. Leakage of urine during increased abdominal pressure confirms the diagnosis.

ol10BS0.title: Core ethical principles
ol10BS0.description: The four basic principles of bioethics and medical practice: autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, and justice.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Medical ethics

pl1LBS0.title: Advance health care directive
pl1LBS0.description: A legal document used to guide what health care decisions should be made if an individual loses decision-making capacity. Directs treatment decisions and establishes potential surrogate decision-makers. Completed when an individual retains decisional capacity. Examples include a Medical Power of Attorney (Health Care Proxy), Living Will, and Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) order.

destinations.label: Capacity, competence, and consent → Decision-making capacity

rl1fyS0.title: Stomatitis
rl1fyS0.description: An inflammation of the mucous membranes of the mouth and lips.

Hl1KyS0.title: CDT
Hl1KyS0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Carbohydrate-deficient transferrin
2. Cytolethal-distending toxin

sl1tyS0.title: Tagged red blood cell scintigraphy
sl1tyS0.description: A nuclear medicine technique that involves radiolabeling of red blood cells with technetium-99m and subsequent imaging. Can be used to localize areas of active bleeding (e.g., to evaluate lower gastrointestinal bleeding). Can detect bleeds as slow as 0.1‑0.5 mL/min (more sensitive than angiography and CT angiography).

Gl1ByS0.title: Lumbar lymphatic trunks
Gl1ByS0.description: A paired set of structures that receive lymphatic drainage from the para-aortic lymph nodes and drain into the cisterna chyli.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Lymphatics of the abdominal cavity

tl1XAS0.title: Intestinal lymphatic trunk
tl1XAS0.description: A structure that drains the preaortic lymph nodes and empties into the cisterna chyli.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Lymphatics of the abdominal cavity

Fl1gAS0.title: Abdominal prevertebral plexus
Fl1gAS0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers seen in relation to the abdominal aorta and its branches. Innervates the abdominal and pelvic viscera.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Nerves of the abdominal cavity

media.title: Abdominal prevertebral plexus and sympathetic trunk

vl1AAS0.title: Tonsillectomy
vl1AAS0.description: A surgical procedure in which tonsils are removed. Tonsillectomy can be either total or subtotal.

9l1N_S0.title: Hepatic plexus
9l1N_S0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that arise from the celiac and superior mesenteric plexuses. Innervates the stomach, liver, gallbladder, proximal duodenum, and pancreas.

Bl1z_S0.title: Splenic plexus
Bl1z_S0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that arise from the celiac plexus. Innervates the spleen.

yl1dzS0.title: Renal plexus
yl1dzS0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that arise from the celiac ganglion, celiac plexus, aorticorenal ganglion, aortic plexus, lowest thoracic splanchnic nerve, and first lumbar splanchnic nerve. Innervates the kidney and gives branches to the ureteric, ovarian, and testicular plexuses.

Al1RzS0.title: Ureteric plexus
Al1RzS0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that innervate the ureter. The upper portion arises from fibers of the renal and aortic plexuses, the middle portion from the hypogastric nerve and superior hypogastric plexus, and the lower portion from the hypogastric nerve and inferior hypogastric plexus.

_l15zS0.title: Ovarian plexus
_l15zS0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that arise from the renal, aortic, superior, and inferior hypogastric plexuses. Innervates the ovaries.

zl1rzS0.title: Testicular plexus
zl1rzS0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that arise from the renal, aortic, and inferior hypogastric plexuses. Innervates the testes.

-l1DzS0.title: Myelopoiesis
-l1DzS0.description: The process by which myeloid white blood cells (granulocytes, monocytes, mast cells) develop from myeloid precursor cells in the bone marrow.

destinations.label: Basics of hematology → Myeloid cell line

ZN1Z-S0.title: Uterovaginal plexus
ZN1Z-S0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that arise from the inferior hypogastric plexus. Innervates the fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, and upper vagina.

0N1e-S0.title: Real-time quaking-induced conversion
0N1e-S0.description: A diagnostic tool for sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Involves the mixing of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) with recombinant prion protein (rPrP) and thioflavin T. If CSF contains misfolded prion protein (PrPSc), it will induce conformation changes in rPrP. These rPrP fibrils bind to thioflavin T, which will fluoresce.

aN1Q-S0.title: Prostatic plexus
aN1Q-S0.description: A collection of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerve fibers that arise from the inferior hypogastric plexus. Innervates the prostate, prostatic urethra, internal urethral sphincter, corpora cavernosa (via cavernous nerves), seminal vesicles, vas deferens, and ejaculatory duct.

YN1n-S0.title: A priori
YN1n-S0.description: A Latin phrase that means "from earlier." Used to refer to knowledge that is available before making an empiric observation. In research and Bayesian analysis, it refers to knowledge that is available about one or more probability distributions before an experiment or test is conducted (e.g., pretest probabilities).

bN1H-S0.title: Post hoc
bN1H-S0.description: A Latin phrase that means "after this." Used to refer to knowledge that is available after making an empiric observation. In the context of research, it often refers to statistical analysis that is conducted at the end of the study.

XN19-S0.title: Lumbar sympathetic trunk
XN19-S0.description: A network of four interconnected ganglia lying on either side of the lumbar vertebrae. Gives rise to the lumbar splanchnic nerves. It is continuous with the thoracic sympathetic ganglia superiorly and sacral sympathetic ganglia inferiorly.

cN1aZh0.title: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
cN1aZh0.description: A type of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation that supports both respiratory and hemodynamic function. Blood is removed from the venous system via a cannula in a large vein and returned after oxygenation via a cannula in a large artery. Used for cardiogenic shock and for support following cardiac surgery. May also be used in acute respiratory failure.

1N12Zh0.title: Venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
1N12Zh0.description: A type of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation that supports respiratory function only and is used in hemodynamically stable patients. A large venous cannula (or two) is placed and blood is removed from the venous system and returned after oxygenation. Indicated as a rescue treatment for patients with acute respiratory failure awaiting improvement or as a permanent solution for the underlying disease process (e.g., as a bridge to lung transplantation).

WN1PZh0.title: Whole bowel irrigation
WN1PZh0.description: A method of gastrointestinal decontamination consisting of enteral administration of large volumes of an osmotically balanced solution (typically 2 L/hour in adults). Used in the treatment of toxic ingestion of extended-release medications, drug packets, or toxic metals to wash out the gastrointestinal tract and prevent absorption.

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Decontamination

eN1xZh0.title: Vasodilatory shock
eN1xZh0.description: A type of shock caused by uncontrolled vasodilation and hyporeactivity of vascular smooth muscle to endogenous vasoconstrictors. Seen in conditions including sepsis, anaphylaxis, and calcium channel blocker overdose.

UN1b0h0.title: CRT
UN1b0h0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Cardiac resynchronization therapy (device)
2. Capillary refill time
3. Cognitive remediation therapy

fN1k0h0.title: Fatal familial insomnia
fN1k0h0.description: A rare, fatal, transmissible spongiform encephalopathy characterized by progressively worsening insomnia that leads to mental and physical deterioration. Caused by mutations of the prion protein gene that lead to formation and accumulation of misfolded prion protein in the brain.

TN160h0.title: Prion protein gene
TN160h0.description: The gene that encodes major prion protein (PrP). Mutations in this gene are associated with several cognitive and neurodegenerative disorders, including Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, Gerstmann-Sträussler-Scheinker syndrome, and fatal familial insomnia.

hN1cah0.title: Betaine
hN1cah0.description: An endogenous choline metabolite used to treat homocystinuria and prevent nephrolithiasis. It acts as a methyl group donor in the remethylation of homocysteine to methionine and acidifies the urine, which can reduce the formation of struvite and calcium phosphate stones.

iN1Jah0.title: Bethesda system (thyroid)
iN1Jah0.description: A cytopathologic classification system used to categorize thyroid fine-needle aspiration cytology findings into 6 variants based on malignant potential. The categories include: I, nondiagnostic; II, benign; III, atypia or follicular lesion of undetermined significance; IV, follicular neoplasm; V, suspicious for malignancy; and VI, malignant.

QN1uah0.title: Aortoenteric fistula
QN1uah0.description: An abnormal connection between the aorta or aortoiliac tree and the gastrointestinal tract (most commonly the duodenum). Can occur as a surgical complication or due to chronic compression of an abdominal aortic aneurysm with the gastrointestinal tract. Typically manifests with profound life-threatening gastrointestinal hemorrhage.

jN1_ah0.title: Anterior ciliary arteries
jN1_ah0.description: A collection of arteries in the eye that arise from the muscular branches of the ophthalmic artery and supply the iris.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Vasculature and innervation

media.title: Valve thrombosis in recurrent endocarditis of the mitral valve

PN1WYh0.title: Central vein of the retina
PN1WYh0.description: A short vein found in each eye that travels in the optic nerve and drains into either the superior ophthalmic vein or into the cavernous sinus directly. Drains blood from the capillaries of the retina.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Vasculature and innervation

media.title: Valve thrombosis in recurrent endocarditis of the mitral valve

4N13Yh0.title: Disease burden
4N13Yh0.description: A measure used in epidemiology to estimate the impact of a health problem on a given population, using indicators such as mortality, morbidity, and financial cost. This impact can be quantified using cost-effectiveness analyses by calculating the associated disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and/or quality-adjusted life years (QALYs)

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

kN1mYh0.title: Ischemic priapism
kN1mYh0.description: A type of priapism caused by inadequate venous outflow from the corpus cavernosum. Common causes include medications (e.g., sildenafil, alprostadil, trazodone) and hematological conditions (e.g., sickle cell disease). Manifests with a persistent, painful, fully rigid erection and is a urologic emergency.

ON1IYh0.title: Angular vein
ON1IYh0.description: The uppermost segment of the facial vein. Drains the anterior region of the scalp. Forms an anastomosis from the superficial facial veins to the intracranial veins. Facial infections can spread via the angular vein to the cavernous sinus and cause life-threatening thrombosis.

media.title: Valve thrombosis in recurrent endocarditis of the mitral valve

lN1vYh0.title: Quality-adjusted life year
lN1vYh0.description: A measure of quantity of life lived that is corrected for loss of quality of life caused by diseases and disabilities. A year of life in perfect health is given a QALY of 1.

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

NN1-Yh0.title: Disability-adjusted life years
NN1-Yh0.description: A combined measure of years of life lost and years lived with disability. One DALY is equivalent to one lost year of life at full health. DALYs are used to assess the total burden of disease within a population.

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

5N1ibh0.title: Thrombopoiesis
5N1ibh0.description: The production of platelets in the bone marrow. Involves thrombopoietin-regulated differentiation and maturation of megakaryocytes.

MN1Mbh0.title: Primary immune thrombocytopenia
MN1Mbh0.description: An idiopathic autoimmune hematologic disorder characterized by isolated thrombocytopenia. It is a diagnosis of exclusion.

nN17bh0.title: Secondary immune thrombocytopenia
nN17bh0.description: An autoimmune hematologic disorder causing isolated thrombocytopenia. Can be secondary to conditions (e.g., SLE or HIV) or secondary to medication use (e.g., quinine). Distinguished from primary ITP, which is idiopathic.

LN1wbh0.title: Bullous subconjunctival hemorrhage
LN1wbh0.description: A subconjunctival hemorrhage with elevation of the hemorrhagic area due to blood pooling in the subconjunctival space. Suggestive of intraocular injury (e.g., scleral laceration) and requires further diagnostic workup (e.g., slit lamp examination, CT scan).

oN10Xh0.title: Baseline characteristics
oN10Xh0.description: The demographic, clinical, and other objective data collected for each participant at the beginning of a study.

pN1LXh0.title: Meckel scan
pN1LXh0.description: A noninvasive nuclear imaging technique that uses technetium-99m pertechnetate to evaluate for a Meckel diverticulum.

qN1CXh0.title: Amsel criteria
qN1CXh0.description: A set of criteria used to diagnose bacterial vaginosis. Includes the presence of clue cells, positive whiff test, vaginal pH > 4.5, and presence of thin, homogeneous, gray-white or yellow vaginal discharge. Diagnosis is confirmed if three out of four criteria are met.

HN1Kch0.title: Radioactive iodine uptake
HN1Kch0.description: The absorption of radioactive iodine either due to toxic or iatrogenic exposure (e.g., thyroid scintigraphy or radioiodine therapy).

GN1Bch0.title: Radioactive iodine
GN1Bch0.description: A radioactive isotope of iodine that is used for diagnostic and/or therapeutic purposes. Iodine-123 is used in radioactive iodine uptake testing. Iodine-131 is used in radioiodine therapy. Exposure to iodine-131 and other radioactive iodine isotopes can also occur following radiation exposure (e.g., nuclear disaster)

8N1O1h0.title: Hour-1 bundle
8N1O1h0.description: A group of five critical elements that should be performed within 60 minutes of recognizing septic shock or a high probability of sepsis. The elements are: measure lactate level, draw blood cultures before starting antibiotics, begin administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics, rapid infusion of large volumes of IV fluids if hypotension or hyperlactatemia are present, and vasopressor administration to keep MAP ≥ 65 mm Hg.

vN1A1h0.title: Vasopressin
vN1A1h0.description:
1. Vasopressin (hormone): a posterior pituitary hormone, also known as arginine vasopressin (AVP), that regulates osmotic balance, sodium homeostasis, and blood pressure.
2. Vasopressin (medication): a synthetic AVP analogue used to treat vasodilatory shock, esophageal variceal hemorrhage, and arginine vasopressin deficiency.

DN11Wh0.title: Primary hrHPV testing
DN11Wh0.description: A screening strategy for cervical cancer based on FDA-approved DNA testing for high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV DNA testing). Abnormal results should be followed by reflex cervical cytology testing.

9N1NWh0.title: Hyperadrenergic symptoms
9N1NWh0.description: A constellation of symptoms including tachycardia, hypertension, anxiety, tremor, sweating, and weight loss resulting from increased sympathetic activity or enhanced response to normal sympathetic activity.

CN1qWh0.title: Antigen
CN1qWh0.description: A substance that triggers an immunologic response and reacts with antigen-specific antibodies or B-cell antigen receptors.

xN1EWh0.title: Needle manometry
xN1EWh0.description: The direct measurement of intracompartmental pressure using a needle (e.g., a simple 18-gauge needle) attached to a pressure sensor. Used in the evaluation of acute compartment syndrome.

BN1zWh0.title: Visual pigment
BN1zWh0.description: A G protein-coupled receptor that consists of opsin bound to the vitamin A derivative 11-cis-retinal. Absorbs light as the first step in visual perception. The spectral sensitivity of opsin varies, which results in four distinct visual pigments (one in retinal rods, three in retinal cones).

_N15dh0.title: Peroneal tendonitis
_N15dh0.description: An overuse injury that affects the tendons of the peroneus longus and peroneus brevis muscles and manifests with acute or chronic pain over the lateral aspect of the lower extremity. Common in runners.

Zm1ZVh0.title: Para-aortic bodies
Zm1ZVh0.description: A collection of chromaffin cells derived from the neural crest that is found in relation to the abdominal prevertebral plexus. It is the main site of catecholamine secretion during the fetal period and regresses in size after 3 years of age. Forms one of the sites for extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma (paraganglioma).

0m1eVh0.title: Double PCL sign
0m1eVh0.description: A radiologic sign seen on sagittal MRI of the knee in patients with displaced bucket handle meniscal tears. The tear flips toward the joint and mimics the appearance of the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL).

am1QVh0.title: MIS
am1QVh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Multisystem inflammatory syndrome
2. Müllerian-inhibiting substance
3. Melanoma in situ

Ym1nVh0.title: MIF
Ym1nVh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Macrophage migration inhibitory factor
2. Melanocyte-inhibiting factor
3. Müllerian-inhibiting factor

bm1HVh0.title: PVR
bm1HVh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Pulmonary vascular resistance
2. Peripheral vascular resistance
3. Postvoid residual volume

cm1aeh0.title: Leukotrichia
cm1aeh0.description: A localized depigmentation of hair due to loss of melanocytes in the hair bulb. Seen in approx. 50% of individuals with vitiligo.

1m12eh0.title: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
1m12eh0.description: A benign skin condition characterized by diffuse, hypopigmented macules 1-10 mm in size. Most commonly develops in sun-exposed areas.

Wm1Peh0.title: Costomediastinal recess
Wm1Peh0.description: A potential space in the pleural cavity between the mediastinal pleura and the costal pleura. Along with the costodiaphragmatic recess, it facilitates lung expansion during forced inspiration.

fm1kUh0.title: Vision
fm1kUh0.description: The afferent structures that receive, transmit, and process visual information. Includes retinal structures (photoreceptor cells, bipolar cells, ganglion cells), the optic nerves (CN II), optic chiasms, optic tracts, lateral geniculate nuclei, and optic radiations. Terminates in the primary visual cortex.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Overview of the visual pathways

Tm16Uh0.title: Pupil
Tm16Uh0.description: The opening in the center of the iris through which light enters the eye. Pupillary size is variable and mediated by autonomic fibers. Increased brightness causes pupillary constriction (miosis); increased darkness causes pupillary dilation (mydriasis).

Rm1l2h0.title: Mitotane
Rm1l2h0.description: A drug that directly inhibits the synthetic function of the adrenal cortex. Used to treat adrenal tumors in patients who cannot undergo resection. Contraindicated in pregnancy due to its teratogenic effects.

Qm1u2h0.title: Cernilton
Qm1u2h0.description: A rye‐grass pollen extract with anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative properties that has been used to treat benign prostate hyperplasia, prostate-related pain, and chronic prostate inflammation.

Pm1Wfh0.title: Blood-borne pathogen
Pm1Wfh0.description: A pathogen that is carried in the bloodstream and spread through contact with blood or other bodily fluids. Examples include HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C.

4m13fh0.title: Left gonadal vein
4m13fh0.description: A vein drains the testis or ovary on the left side. Empties into the left renal vein.

km1mfh0.title: Right gonadal vein
km1mfh0.description: A vein that drains the testis or ovary on the right side. Empties into the inferior vena cava.

Nm1-fh0.title: HPV/Pap cotesting
Nm1-fh0.description: A cervical cancer screening strategy in which both cervical cytology (Pap smear) and HPV DNA testing are performed.

mm1VTh0.title: Chronic gout therapy
mm1VTh0.description: A general term for medications that lower serum uric acid by reducing its production or increasing its excretion. Used primarily in the treatment of chronic gout. Includes xanthine oxidase inhibitors and uricosurics.

nm17Th0.title: Vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1
nm17Th0.description: An autosomal recessive condition characterized by early-onset rickets, muscle weakness, failure to thrive, hypotonia, and pathologic fractures. Caused by a mutation in the CYP27B1 gene, which impairs 1α-hydroxylase synthesis (type 1A VDDR), or a CYP2R1 gene defect, which impairs 25-hydroxylase synthesis (type 1B VDDR). These mutations prevent the conversion of inactive vitamin D to the active form (1,25‑dihydroxyvitamin D₃, calcitriol).

destinations.label: Osteomalacia and rickets → Subtypes and variants

Lm1wTh0.title: Vitamin D-dependent rickets type 2
Lm1wTh0.description: An autosomal recessive condition characterized by early-onset rickets, failure to thrive, and alopecia. Caused by a mutation in the vitamin D receptor gene, which leads to end-organ resistance to vitamin D.

destinations.label: Osteomalacia and rickets → Subtypes and variants

7m14Sh0.title: Positive acute phase reactant
7m14Sh0.description: A molecule whose serum concentration increases in the setting of acute inflammation. Includes C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, ferritin, hepcidin, and haptoglobin.

Hm1KSh0.title: Nonconvulsive status epilepticus
Hm1KSh0.description: A type of status epilepticus that manifests with altered mental state in the absence of convulsions. Typically seen in the critically ill. Causes include electrolyte abnormalities, hypoxic brain injury, stroke, brain tumors, acute hormonal alterations, and medication with epileptogenic potential. Diagnosis requires a high index of suspicion. Electroencephalography can show focal or generalized cortical seizure activity.

sm1tSh0.title: Trabecular outflow
sm1tSh0.description: The primary pathway of drainage for the aqueous humor of the eye. Involves flow from the anterior chamber into the trabecular meshwork, from where it enters the canal of Schlemm and subsequently the episcleral vessels. Accounts for 85-95% of aqueous outflow.

destinations.label: Eye and orbit →  Segments and chambers of the eye

Gm1BSh0.title: Lactiferous duct fistula
Gm1BSh0.description: A complication of periductal mastitis characterized by a fistula between the lactiferous duct and the surface of the breast, typically in the areola or periareolar region. Typically manifests with purulent nipple discharge; in women who are lactating, it can manifest with galactorrhea (milk fistula). Can result in abscess formation.

8m1Ohh0.title: Midstream urine sample
8m1Ohh0.description: A method of obtaining a urine sample that involves the collection of urine partway through urination (i.e., excluding the initial stream and the terminal portion of urination). Decreases the risk of contamination with bacteria from the hands and genitalia.

um1phh0.title: Saturated solution of potassium iodine
um1phh0.description: A compound administered to decrease the release of thyroid hormones and the uptake of iodine by the thyroid gland. Used for pretreatment before thyroid surgery, adjunctive therapy in thyroid storm, and prophylaxis to decrease radioactive iodine uptake after nuclear accident or overdose in patients undergoing radioactive iodine ablation. Contains 1 g of potassium iodide per mL.

Em18hh0.title: Frozen section
Em18hh0.description: A laboratory technique in which a freshly biopsied specimen is rapidly cooled and sectioned using a cryostat to facilitate rapid microscopic examination. Typically used during surgical resection of malignant or potentially malignant tumors in which the frozen section report could influence the extent of resection (e.g., evaluation of resected margins for tumor spread, differentiating a follicular adenoma from a follicular carcinoma).

vm1Ahh0.title: Rilonacept
vm1Ahh0.description: A fusion protein that acts as an IL-1 decoy by binding to IL-1β and preventing it from interacting with the IL-1 receptor. Used to treat cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes.

wm1h3h0.title: Lower extremity venous ultrasound
wm1h3h0.description: An ultrasound of the veins in the lower extremities (e.g., iliac, femoral, popliteal, distal calf veins), that comprises compression ultrasound techniques and/or duplex scanning. Used primarily in the diagnostic evaluation of deep vein thrombosis. Can also evaluate superficial thrombophlebitis.

9m1N3h0.title: TAO
9m1N3h0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Thromboangiitis obliterans
2. Thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy

xm1E3h0.title: Vasopressin (medication)
xm1E3h0.description: Synthetic analogues of arginine vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone). Agents include vasopressin, desmopressin, and terlipressin. Used to treat conditions such as vasodilatory shock, esophageal variceal hemorrhage, hepatorenal syndrome, arginine vasopressin deficiency, hemophilia, von Willebrand disease, and nocturnal enuresis.

destinations.label: General endocrinology → Hypothalamic and pituitary drugs

Bm1z3h0.title: Left heart catheterization
Bm1z3h0.description: A procedure used in the diagnosis and treatment of cardiac conditions. A catheter is passed into the left side of the heart to evaluate ventricular and valvular function, aortic root anatomy, and to perform a coronary angiogram. Sometimes erroneously used as a synonym for coronary angiography, a more limited procedure that does not assess ventricular or valvular anatomy or function.

zm1rRh0.title: Reset osmostat syndrome
zm1rRh0.description: A cause of euvolemic hypotonic hyponatremia in which the set point of osmolality that triggers the release of ADH is decreased, but changes in the osmolality continue to elicit an adequate response. Associated with neurologic conditions (e.g., epilepsy, paraplegia), malignancy, malnutrition, and pregnancy.

Z51Zih0.title: MARCH algorithm
Z51Zih0.description: An approach to trauma care on the battlefield. Performed in order: Massive hemorrhage (assess and control sources of life-threatening bleeding), Airway (check if airway is patent), Respiration (assess for chest wounds and tension pneumothorax, measure pulse oximetry), Circulation (assess for other sources of bleeding and hemorrhagic shock), Hypothermia prevention (minimize cold exposure)/Head injury.

a51Qih0.title: Fractional excretion of uric acid
a51Qih0.description: The percentage of glomerular filtered uric acid excreted in the urine. Used to help determine volume status in patients with hypotonic hyponatremia; FEUA < 12% suggests low effective arterial volume and ≥ 12% suggests euvolemia (e.g., in SIADH).

Y51nih0.title: Pediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric disorders associated with streptococcal infections
Y51nih0.description: An immune-mediated neuropsychiatric disorder that is preceeded by a GAS infection and characterized by the sudden onset or worsening of obsessive-compulsive disorder and/or tic disorder.

X519ih0.title: Sterile pyuria
X519ih0.description: The presence of significant leukocyturia that is not accompanied by evidence of bacteria in the urine on standard microscopy or urine culture. Common noninfectious causes include contamination of the urine sample (e.g., by vaginal leukocytes), glomerular or tubulointerstitial disease, and inflammation of or trauma to the lower urinary tract (e.g., due to uroliths, urinary catheterization). Certain infections (e.g., gonorrhea, chlamydia, herpes genitalis, trichomoniasis, urogenital tuberculosis, schistosomiasis) can also cause sterile pyuria.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → History and physical examination

c51aQh0.title: Calcium sensing receptors
c51aQh0.description: The G-protein coupled receptors found on parathyroid and renal tubular cells that regulate calcium homeostasis. Encoded by the CASR gene on chromosome 3. Binding of calcium activates the receptors and subsequently decreases parathyroid hormone secretion and renal calcium reabsorption. Inactivating mutations of the receptor cause familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia and neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism. Activating mutations cause autosomal dominant hypocalcemia. Calcimimetics (e.g., cinacalcet) are positive allosteric modulators of these receptors.

1512Qh0.title: Teprotumumab
1512Qh0.description: A monoclonal antibody that inhibits the insulin like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF-1R). Used in the treatment of Graves orbitopathy.

d51oQh0.title: Z band
d51oQh0.description: A line that separates one sarcomere from another. Acts as an anchoring point for actin filaments through anchoring proteins such as α-actinin. Connected to the M line through the titin protein.

U51bjh0.title: Harlequin color change
U51bjh0.description: A transient, self-limited vascular phenomenon in neonates characterized by episodic, sharply-demarcated plethora on one half of the body. Typically begins between the 3rd and 5th days of life. The exact cause is unknown but thought to be related to vasomotor instability from an immature hypothalamus.

251Tjh0.title: Staphylococcal pustulosis
251Tjh0.description: A staphylococcal skin infection that most commonly develops in neonates and infants. Manifests with pustules on an erythematous base, typically in moist areas susceptible to skin trauma (e.g., the diaper region, axillary fossa, and nape of the neck). Can be localized or diffuse and associated with systemic symptoms (e.g., fever).

f51kjh0.title: AR
f51kjh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Aortic regurgitation
2. Autosomal recessive
3. Attributable risk
4. Absolute risk

T516jh0.title: AI
T516jh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Aortic insufficiency
2. Adrenal insufficiency
3. Aromatase inhibitor
4. Artificial intelligence

g51Fjh0.title: AS
g51Fjh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Aortic stenosis
2. Ankylosing spondylitis

S51yjh0.title: PS
S51yjh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Pulmonary stenosis
2. Pyloric stenosis
3. Parasympathetic
4. Performance status

h51cPh0.title: Internal pneumatic stabilization
h51cPh0.description: A nonsurgical treatment for severe flail chest that typically involves long-term mechanical ventilation.

R51lPh0.title: TEC
R51lPh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Transient erythroblastopenia of childhood
2. Tactical evacuation care
3. Toxic erythema of chemotherapy

i51JPh0.title: cABCDE approach
i51JPh0.description: A modified version of the ABCDE approach for primary evaluation in advanced trauma life support. Includes assessment of critical hemorrhage (the "C") before the assessment of airway, breathing, circulation, disability, and exposure.

Q51uPh0.title: Ravulizumab
Q51uPh0.description: A recombinant monoclonal antibody that inhibits the immune system by binding to and deactivating complement C5 (the terminal part of the complement cascade). Used to treat paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome. Increases the risk of infection with encapsulated bacteria (e.g., Neisseria spp.).

j51_Ph0.title: Parachute reflex
j51_Ph0.description: A developmental reflex that appears around 6 months of age and persists throughout life. Elicited with the sensation of falling. To test for this reflex, the child is held in upright position with the back to the examiner and suddenly rotated forward with the body facing down. In response, the child's arms extend toward the ground in a protective motion to brace the fall.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Primitive reflexes

P51W4h0.title: Fetal pole
P51W4h0.description: A thickening of the margin of the yolk sac. Indicates the presence of an embryo within the gestational sac. Visible on transvaginal ultrasonography typically at 7 weeks of gestation but can be seen as early as 6 weeks or as late as 9 weeks of gestational age.

45134h0.title: Double decidual sac sign
45134h0.description: An ultrasonographic finding in the early stage of intrauterine pregnancy (fetal weeks 2–9). Characterized by two echogenic rings around the gestational sac resulting from the two layers of the decidua (capsularis and parietalis). It is a specific but not a sensitive sign for identifying a true gestational sac.

media.title: First trimester ultrasound, double sac sign

k51m4h0.title: Intradecidual sign
k51m4h0.description: An ultrasonographic finding in the early stage of intrauterine pregnancy. Characterized by an echogenic area (resulting from the thickened decidua at the site of implantation) on one side of an echogenic line (resulting from the endometrial stripe of the collapsed uterine cavity). It is a specific but not a sensitive sign for identifying a true gestational sac.

O51I4h0.title: Pseudogestational sac
O51I4h0.description: A finding on transvaginal ultrasonography caused by a pocket of fluid in the uterine cavity. Can be mistaken for a true gestational sac of intrauterine pregnancy. Typically present centrally within the uterine cavity, has irregular borders, is filled with debris, and does not cause certain signs associated with a true gestational sac (e.g., double decidual sign, intradecidual sign), although the absence of these signs does not define a pseudogesational sac.

l51v4h0.title: POC
l51v4h0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Point-of-care
2. Products of conception
3. Primary olfactory cortex

551ikh0.title: AVS
551ikh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Adrenal venous sampling
2. Aortic valve stenosis
3. Acute vestibular syndrome

M51Mkh0.title: Meningococcal vaccines
M51Mkh0.description: A set of vaccines that confer immunity against Neisseria meningitidis. Consists of the meningococcal conjugate (MenACWY vaccine), the meningococcal B vaccine, and the pentavalent meningococcal vaccine (MenABCWY vaccine).

J51sOh0.title: Stria medullaris
J51sOh0.description: A part of the epithalamus that consists of afferent fibers from the anterior perforated substance, thalamus, and hypothalamus that project to the habenular nuclei. Located caudal to the facial colliculus, runs transversely across the ventricular floor, and passes into the median sulcus.

I51Ylh0.title: Selective arterial embolization
I51Ylh0.description: A therapeutic procedure in which certain materials (e.g., coils, ethanol, polyvinylalcohol, microspheres, gelatin sponge, cyanoacrylate, sodium tetradecyl sulfate) are introduced into a blood vessel via a vascular catheter in order to stop or prevent hemorrhage, to decrease the size of vascular structures (e.g., tumors), or to decrease blood flow in vascular malformations (e.g., arteriovenous fistulas, hemangiomas).

r51flh0.title: Telemedicine
r51flh0.description: The practice of providing remote clinical care for patients using information and communication technologies. May include telephone encounters, video conferencing, and secure patient portals.

7514lh0.title: Nonischemic priapism
7514lh0.description: A type of priapism often caused by a fistula between the cavernosal artery and corpus cavernosum (e.g., due to blunt or penetrating trauma to the pelvic, perineal, and/or genital region). Manifests with a persistent or recurrent, painless, partially rigid erection and is not a urologic emergency.

H51Klh0.title: Complete penetrance
H51Klh0.description: The phenotypical expression of a trait in all carriers of a specific gene (i.e., if an individual has a genetic mutation it will always manifest as the disease). Diseases that are completely penetrant have a penetrance value of one.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

s51tlh0.title: Incomplete penetrance
s51tlh0.description: A type of genetic penetrance in which phenotypical expression of a particular gene or genomic region is not observed in all individuals.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

G51Blh0.title: Distal penile shunting
G51Blh0.description: A surgical procedure in which a fistula is created between the corpora cavernosa and glans penis. Performed by inserting a large biopsy needle percutaneously through the glans (Winter technique), cutting through the glans (Ebbehoj technique), or excising the distal tip of the corpus cavernosum (Al-Ghorab technique). Used to treat low-flow priapism that is refractory to medical management.

w51hmh0.title: Effective half-life
w51hmh0.description: The time it takes for a drug's plasma concentration to reach 50% of its initial value during the most clinically important phase of its kinetics. For drugs with atypical kinetics (e.g., those with a high volume of distribution), the effective half-life may be shorter than the terminal elimination half-life but more predictive of the drug's duration of effect and accumulation.

B51zmh0.title: Tactical Combat Casualty Care
B51zmh0.description: A set of trauma care guidelines used during combat. The aim is to reduce preventable deaths in military personnel during tactical missions.

destinations.label: Military medicine → Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC)

A51R5h0.title: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
A51R5h0.description: A term used in the Bethesda system to describe an overall normal cervical cytology (Pap smear). To report NILM, the cytological specimen must be adequate for evaluation, and the cells should have no changes suggestive of atypia or dysplasia. Reporting of reactive changes, endometrial cells, or organisms may be included.

-51D5h0.title: Left ventricular strain pattern
-51D5h0.description: An ECG pattern of ST depression and T-wave inversion in the left precordial leads seen in a patient at rest. Suggestive of left ventricular hypertrophy.

aM1QMh0.title: Transferrin receptor
aM1QMh0.description: A transmembrane glycoprotein that is expressed by the TFR1 and TFR2 genes. Mediates endocytosis of the transferrin-iron complex. Present on the surface of most cells (especially immature erythroid precursors and hepatocytes). Its expression is increased in states of iron deficiency and increased erythropoiesis and decreased in states of iron overload and decreased erythropoiesis.

XM19Mh0.title: AVN
XM19Mh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Atrioventricular node
2. Avascular necrosis

cM1anh0.title: Klein line
cM1anh0.description: A straight line drawn along the superior border of the femoral neck that normally passes through the femoral head on hip x-ray. In slipped capital femoral epiphysis, the Klein line does not intersect the femoral head or there is marked asymmetry between the affected and unaffected sides.

1M12nh0.title: Pudendal nerve injury
1M12nh0.description: An injury to the pudendal nerve, which can result in paresthesia or decreased sensation in the perineal region, pelvic pain, urinary and/or fecal incontinence, and sexual dysfunction. Etiologies include pelvic surgery, trauma, childbirth, and repetitive movements, such as frequent cycling.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Complications of delivery

WM1Pnh0.title: C5 inhibitor
WM1Pnh0.description: A monoclonal antibody against the complement protein C5, which results in inhibition of the proinflammatory and cytolytic effects of the terminal complement cascade. Used to treat paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria. Examples include eculizumab and ravulizumab.

dM1onh0.title: Isodisomy
dM1onh0.description: A mechanism of uniparental disomy that occurs when there is a nondisjunction error in meiosis II, which results in the inheritance of two identical homologous chromosomes from one parent. Can also occur if postzygotic chromosomal duplication leads to duplication of one chromosome of one pair and there is subsequent loss of the other.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

VM1Gnh0.title: Reversal reaction
VM1Gnh0.description: An immunological complication of leprosy characterized by an inflammatory exacerbation of preexisting subcutaneous lesions and development of severe neuritis.

eM1xnh0.title: Lucio phenomenon
eM1xnh0.description: A rare complication of leprosy characterized by irregular, sharply demarcated, superficial ulcerative lesions, that mainly affects the limbs. Unlike other leprosy reactions, Lucio phenomenon is not typically associated with neuritis or systemic manifestations.

UM1bLh0.title: Leprosy reaction
UM1bLh0.description: A group of immunologic complications of leprosy that usually occur after the initiation of anti-leprosy treatment.  Includes type 1 reactions (reversal reactions), type 2 reactions (erythema nodosum leprosum), and Lucio phenomenon.

2M1TLh0.title: Anti-VGCC antibodies
2M1TLh0.description: A group of autoantibodies directed against voltage-gated calcium channels in the presynaptic terminal of the neuromuscular junction. The resulting decreased calcium ion influx leads to impaired presynaptic vesicle fusion and decreased release of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine.

fM1kLh0.title: Amifampridine
fM1kLh0.description: A drug used as first-line treatment for Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome. Prolongs the action potential by blocking presynaptic potassium channels, thereby increasing presynaptic calcium concentrations.

gM1FLh0.title: Hemoglobin H
gM1FLh0.description: A form of hemoglobin predominantly seen in α-thalassemia intermedia (HbH disease) and occasionally in some minor forms. A mutation in the α chain results in an unstable β-chain tetramer, which aggregates inside the erythrocytes forming HbH bodies or inclusions that can be detected on peripheral blood smears.

destinations.label: Erythrocyte morphology and hemoglobin → Hemoglobin variants

SM1yLh0.title: Hot tub lung
SM1yLh0.description: A type of hypersensitivity pneumonitis caused by Mycobacterium avum complex.

hM1coh0.title: Shared risk factors for PUD, GERD and gastritis
hM1coh0.description: A collection of risk factors that includes long-term use of NSAIDs, glucocorticoids, tobacco, caffeine, and alcohol as well as H. pylori infection (for PUD and gastritis).

RM1loh0.title: Neonatal pain assessment
RM1loh0.description: A tool used to characterized pain in neonates. Scoring systems use physiologic parameters (e.g., vital signs, skin color), behavioral changes (e.g., consolability, facial expressions, muscle tone), and contextual factors (e.g., age) to evaluate pain. Examples include the Premature Infant Pain Profile (PIPP), Neonatal Infant Pain Scale (NIPS), Neonatal Pain Agitation Sedation Scale (N-PASS), and the Crying, Requires oxygen saturation, Increased vital signs, Expression, Sleeplessness (CRIES) score.

QM1uoh0.title: Clofazimine
QM1uoh0.description: An antimycobacterial agent used in the treatment of lepromatous leprosy. Most common side effects include skin discoloration, abdominal pain, and diarrhea.

jM1_oh0.title: Madarosis
jM1_oh0.description: An acquired or congenital loss of eyebrows or eyelashes.

PM1WKh0.title: Rose Bengal test
PM1WKh0.description: A rapid agglutination assay used to diagnose brucellosis. Rose Bengal-stained Brucella antigen is added to the patient's serum sample. Visible clumping indicates a positive result.

4M13Kh0.title: Hemoglobin E
4M13Kh0.description: A structural hemoglobin variant produced by a point mutation in the β chain and commonly seen in Asian individuals. Homozygous individuals have a phenotype similar to β-thalassemia minor, while carriers can have only mild microcytosis. Variable phenotypes occur in heterozygous individuals with another thalassemia mutation (e.g., HbE/β-thalassemia).

kM1mKh0.title: Thyroid cancer tumor markers
kM1mKh0.description: A group of substances secreted by thyroid follicular and parafollicular cells. Includes thyroglobulin in differentiated thyroid cancer (i.e., follicular and papillary cancer), and calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen in medullary cancer. Primarily used as an aid in determining the prognosis (elevated levels after thyroidectomy/RAIA indicate recurrence or poor response to therapy). Also used as supportive evidence in the diagnosis of medullary thyroid cancer.

OM1IKh0.title: Sonographic signs of thyroid malignancy
OM1IKh0.description: A set of features that includes reduced echogenicity, microcalcifications, irregular or infiltrative margins, and taller-than-wide shape.

lM1vKh0.title: Neonatal encephalopathy
lM1vKh0.description: A clinically defined syndrome of CNS dysfunction in the early newborn period that can result from various underlying pathologies. Characterized by an altered level of consciousness, seizures, difficulty initiating/maintaining respiration, decreased muscle tone and reflexes. The most common subtype is hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.

destinations.label: Perinatal asphyxia and hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy → Definitions

mM1V6h0.title: Anteroseptal leads
mM1V6h0.description: The ECG leads V1-V4. ST elevation and/or dynamic T wave inversion in these leads corresponds to infarction of the myocardium supplied by the left anterior descending artery.

5M1i6h0.title: Primary inoculation tuberculosis
5M1i6h0.description: A form of cutaneous tuberculosis in individuals with no prior immunity to tuberculosis. Occurs after the inoculation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from an exogenous source via injured skin or mucosa. Manifests as a nodule that ulcerates to form a firm and nontender ulcer with accompanying lymph node enlargement.

MM1M6h0.title: Diascopy
MM1M6h0.description: A test to assess blanchability of skin. Used to distinguish between vascular (blanchable) and nonvascular or hemorrhagic skin lesions (nonblanchable). Performed by applying pressure onto the skin using the finger or a glass slide and observing for color change.

nM176h0.title: Stress ulcer prophylaxis
nM176h0.description: The prescription of acid suppression medications (e.g., PPIs or H2 blockers) to prevent gastrointestinal hemorrhage (e.g., due to the formation of stress ulcers) in critically ill patients with moderate to high GI bleeding risk.

destinations.label: Peptic ulcer disease → Subtypes and variants

LM1w6h0.title: Tuberculosis miliaris cutis disseminata
LM1w6h0.description: A fulminant form of cutaneous tuberculosis caused by hematogenous dissemination from the primary focus of infection (e.g., lung, meninges) in individuals with impaired immunity (e.g., as a result of measles, scarlet fever, or HIV infection). Manifests as papules and crusted vesicles over the trunk, buttocks, thighs, and genitalia.

JM1sph0.title: Galeazzi test
JM1sph0.description: A pediatric physical examination maneuver used to assess the hips and legs. The child is placed in the supine position with their hips flexed to 90 degrees and their feet flat on the examination table. Unequal height of the knees (positive Galeazzi test) suggests a dislocated hip or leg length discrepancy.

destinations.label: Developmental dysplasia of the hip → Clinical features

qM1Cph0.title: Cystoplasty
qM1Cph0.description: A surgical procedure for bladder enlargement using a detubularized segment of ileum, cecum, or sigmoid colon. Used to treat bladder fibrosis, urinary incontinence, and detrusor overactivity.

IM1YJh0.title: Pericardial tuberculosis
IM1YJh0.description: A form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis that affects the pericardium and can result in pericardial effusion, constrictive pericarditis, or effusive-constrictive pericarditis.

rM1fJh0.title: Ultrashort-segment Hirschsprung disease
rM1fJh0.description: A variant of Hirschsprung disease characterized by a very short segment of aganglionosis, usually limited to the distal rectum. Patients often present in later infancy or childhood with chronic constipation and failure to thrive. May be treated conservatively with diet, stool softeners, and laxatives.

7M14Jh0.title: Hirschsprung-associated enterocolitis
7M14Jh0.description: An inflammatory complication of Hirschsprung disease with variable symptoms and severity. Classic features include fever, abdominal distention, and diarrhea. Management involves bowel decompression and antibiotics. Severe enterocolitis can lead to toxic megacolon or sepsis.

HM1KJh0.title: Cardiac pacemaker cells
HM1KJh0.description: A group of cardiac cells that can spontaneously (i.e., without input from the nervous system) generate action potentials. These action potentials are converted to electrical impulses and ultimately result in myocardial contraction. Pacemaker cells are found in the sinoatrial node, atrioventricular node, bundle of His, and Purkinje fibers. In a normal adult heart, the sinoatrial node is the pacemaker and generates impulses at the rate of ~ 60–100/min.

GM1BJh0.title: Tuberculous lymphadenitis
GM1BJh0.description: A form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis that causes granulomatous inflammation and caseous necrosis of lymph nodes. Manifests as discrete or matted, nontender lymphadenopathy, with or without discharging sinus tracts. Most commonly involves the cervical and supraclavicular lymph node groups.

8M1Oqh0.title: Givosiran
8M1Oqh0.description: A small interfering RNA agent (active against hepatic ALAS1) used to reduce the frequency of attacks in patients with acute hepatic porphyria and administered subcutaneously.

uM1pqh0.title: Chronic hyponatremia
uM1pqh0.description: Hyponatremia with an onset ≥ 48 hours or of unknown duration

wM1hIh0.title: Saquinavir
wM1hIh0.description: An HIV-1 protease inhibitor used in the treatment of HIV infection. Because it has a poor bioavailability if administered alone, it must be coadministered with ritonavir, which increases its absorption into the bloodstream.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

9M1NIh0.title: Fosamprenavir
9M1NIh0.description: A prodrug of the HIV protease inhibitor amprenavir. Used as a part of combined antiretroviral therapy to treat HIV infection. Its use is associated with an increased risk of hypercholesterolemia and myocardial infarction.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

xM1EIh0.title: Expedited treatment
xM1EIh0.description: An approach to disease management whereby therapeutic interventions are started before diagnostic confirmation. Examples include expedited partner therapy for sexually transmitted infections and expedited treatment for cervical cancer without histopathologic confirmation.

BM1zIh0.title: Severely symptomatic hyponatremia
BM1zIh0.description: Hyponatremia accompanied by signs and symptoms of central nervous system dysfunction, e.g., altered mental status, focal neurological deficits, seizures, or coma.

AM1Rrh0.title: Type 1 cryoglobulinemia
AM1Rrh0.description: The presence of monoclonal immunoglobulins (most commonly IgM; rarely IgG or IgA) in the serum. May be asymptomatic but can manifest as a hyperviscosity syndrome or, less frequently, as cryoglobulinemic vasculitis. An underlying lymphoproliferative disorder (e.g., Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, multiple myeloma) should always be ruled out.

_M15rh0.title: Autoimmune encephalitis
_M15rh0.description: A group of CNS disorders characterized by immune-mediated inflammation of the brain parenchyma. Clinical features can vary widely depending on the etiology but generally resemble those of infectious encephalitis (e.g., neuropsychiatric manifestations, dyskinesias, dystonia, seizures, and other focal neurological symptoms). Diagnosis is typically based on the exclusion of infectious causes and identification of autoantibodies against intracellular or extracellular neuronal components.

Zn1Z7h0.title: High-risk factors for osmotic demyelination syndrome
Zn1Z7h0.description: Risk factors for developing osmotic demyelination syndrome following the correction of hyponatremia. Factors include alcohol use disorder, malnutrition, liver disease, hypokalemia, and initial sodium concentrations ≤ 105 mEq/L.

an1Q7h0.title: GOLD group A
an1Q7h0.description: A COPD classification based on no exacerbations in the past year (or one exacerbation not leading to a hospital admission) and either an mMRC dyspnea score of ≤ 1 or a CAT score of 0-9.

Yn1n7h0.title: Monokines
Yn1n7h0.description: A group of cytokines secreted by monocytes and macrophages.

cn1aHh0.title: Balanced IV fluid solutions
cn1aHh0.description: Parenteral fluids that do not significantly alter the homeostasis of the extracellular compartment, e.g., lactated Ringer's solution. There are two main categories: solutions with low chloride content (< 110 mEq/L) and solutions with minimal effect on the acid-base equilibrium (electrical neutrality).

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

1n12Hh0.title: Keshan disease
1n12Hh0.description: A cardiomyopathy associated with selenium deficiency. Endemic in certain areas of China. Most commonly affects children and women of childbearing age.

Wn1PHh0.title: Pulmonary congestion
Wn1PHh0.description: A state in which the pulmonary vessels are exposed to increased capillary pressures due to left-sided heart failure, resulting in vessel dilation. Sometimes used synonymously with pulmonary edema, although they are distinct entities and pulmonary edema may result from processes other than pulmonary congestion.

dn1oHh0.title: Osmolarity
dn1oHh0.description: The number of solute particles (or osmoles) per unit volume of solvent (mOsm/L). Distinct from osmolality (mOsm/kg) but used interchangeably in clinical practice, as 1 L and 1 kg of biological solutions are often equivalent. Used to describe the measured osmotic pressure of therapeutic fluids, as well as calculated estimates of the serum osmotic pressure.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

Vn1GHh0.title: Tonicity
Vn1GHh0.description: The capability of a fluid (e.g., an IV solution) to make water move in or out of a cell via an osmotic gradient. Related to but distinct from osmolarity, as it reflects the osmotic effect of particles that cannot freely penetrate cell membranes (i.e., the effective osmotic pressure gradient).

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

en1xHh0.title: 10% dextrose in water
en1xHh0.description: A crystalloid solution that contains 10 g/dL (555 mmol/L) of dextrose (a glucose isomer). Despite having a hyperosmolar composition, D10W acts as a hypotonic solution in the body due to the rapid intracellular uptake of glucose.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

Un1bsh0.title: 5% dextrose in 0.9% NaCl
Un1bsh0.description: A crystalloid solution that contains 252 mmol/L (50 g/L) of dextrose (a glucose isomer) and sodium and chloride, each with a concentration of 154 mEq/L (154 mmol/L). Despite having a hyperosmolar composition (560 mOsm/L), D5NS acts as an isotonic solution in the body because, as a result of the rapid intracellular uptake of glucose, the tonicity is only determined by the NaCl concentration.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

2n1Tsh0.title: 5% dextrose in 0.45% NaCl
2n1Tsh0.description: A crystalloid solution that contains 252 mmol/L (50 g/L) of dextrose (a glucose isomer) and sodium and chloride, each with a concentration of 77 mEq/L (77 mmol/L). Despite having a hyperosmolar composition (406 mOsm/L), D5½NS acts as a hypotonic solution in the body because, as a result of the rapid intracellular uptake of glucose, the tonicity is only determined by the NaCl concentration.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

Tn16sh0.title: Uncomplicated inguinal hernia
Tn16sh0.description: An inguinal hernia with no features of incarceration, strangulation, or bowel obstruction.

gn1Fsh0.title: Complicated inguinal hernia
gn1Fsh0.description: Complications of inguinal hernias, such as incarceration, bowel obstruction, and/or strangulation.

Sn1ysh0.title: Cardiac dyssynchrony
Sn1ysh0.description: A loss of coordination of contraction and relaxation between different heart chambers or areas of myocardium. Can occur between the atria and ventricles, the two ventricles, or within a ventricle. Can result in atrial stretch, reduced ventricular filling, and reduced cardiac output.

3n1SGh0.title: Carnett sign
3n1SGh0.description: An abdominal examination finding in which the intensity of abdominal pain increases or remains unchanged during maneuvers that tense the abdominal muscles (e.g., lifting the head and shoulders off the examination table when lying in a supine position, active straight leg raise). Indicates that the abdominal wall is the source of pain.

Rn1lGh0.title: Fothergill sign
Rn1lGh0.description: An abdominal examination finding that suggests the presence of a rectus sheath hematoma. Characterized by an abdominal mass that does not cross the midline. During maneuvers that tense the abdominal muscles (e.g., lifting the head and shoulders off the examination table when lying in a supine position, active straight leg raise), the location of the mass does not change and its prominence on palpation remains unchanged or increases.

in1JGh0.title: Rasmussen aneurysm
in1JGh0.description: An inflammatory pseudoaneurysm of a branch of the pulmonary artery lying adjacent to a tuberculous cavity. A rare complication of pulmonary tuberculosis that manifests with hemoptysis.

jn1_Gh0.title: High-performance liquid chromatography
jn1_Gh0.description: A form of column chromatography used to separate and identify the different components of a sample. Applications in clinical practice include detection of drug metabolites, detailed hemoglobin analyses (hemoglobin variants, glycated hemoglobin), and detection of amino acids in blood and urine samples (e.g., for the diagnosis of inborn errors of metabolism).

Pn1Wth0.title: Chalk stick fracture
Pn1Wth0.description: A traumatic fracture of an ankylosed spine (e.g., due to ankylosing spondylitis). Can occur after minimal trauma due to altered spinal biomechanics.

media.title: Cervical chalk stick fracture in ankylosing spondylitis
Cervical chalk stick fracture in ankylosing spondylitis

4n13th0.title: H. pylori test-and-treat strategy
4n13th0.description: A management strategy for H. pylori infection in patients with dyspepsia without risk factors for gastric malignancy. Consists of noninvasive testing and, if results are positive, treatment with antibiotics and acid suppression medications. This strategy reduces the need for endoscopy and the prolonged use of antisecretory medications.

kn1mth0.title: Garden spade deformity
kn1mth0.description: A physical examination finding associated with Smith fractures, in which volar displacement of the distal radius results in the forearm and hand having the appearance of a garden spade.

On1Ith0.title: Dinner fork deformity
On1Ith0.description: A physical examination finding associated with Colles fractures, in which dorsal angulation and displacement of the distal radius results in the forearm and hand having the shape of a fork.

ln1vth0.title: Sick day rules
ln1vth0.description: A set of rules that can be taught to patients with certain chronic conditions to prevent complications during intercurrent illnesses. Examples include steroid dose increase for patients who are steroid-dependent to prevent adrenal crises during times of increased physiological stress and rules about temporarily omitting drugs associated with acute kidney injury (e.g., ACE inhibitors) during illnesses that cause dehydration (e.g., vomiting, diarrhea, fevers).

Nn1-th0.title: Synchronous tumor
Nn1-th0.description: A malignancy that is detected simultaneously or within ≤ 6 months after the detection of another malignancy.

mn1VFh0.title: Metachronous tumor
mn1VFh0.description: A malignancy that is detected > 6 months after the detection of another malignancy.

Kn1U8h0.title: Sipuleucel-T
Kn1U8h0.description: A cell-based vaccine used to treat castration-resistant (hormone-refractory) prostate cancer. Contains a recombinant protein made of granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) and prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP).
