It is thought to induce an immune response against PAP-expressing tumor cells.

6n1j8h0.title: Familial atypical multiple mole melanoma syndrome
6n1j8h0.description: An autosomal dominant condition characterized by numerous (> 50) melanocytic nevi, including multiple atypical nevi, and a family history of melanoma. Individuals with this condition have an increased risk of developing melanoma, pancreatic cancer, and other malignancies.

pn1L8h0.title: Osteoglophonic dysplasia
pn1L8h0.description: An extremely rare, autosomal dominant skeletal dysplasia characterized by craniofacial abnormalities, unerupted teeth, and dwarfism. Caused by mutations in the FGFR1 gene.

Jn1s8h0.title: Caplacizumab
Jn1s8h0.description: A humanized monoclonal antibody used to treat acquired or immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Prevents microvascular thrombosis by inhibiting the interaction between von Willebrand factor and platelets.

qn1C8h0.title: Pemberton sign
qn1C8h0.description: A physical examination finding to assess for venous congestion in patients with goiter. The sign is positive if bilateral elevation of the arms for more than one minute elicits facial plethora. Caused by obstruction of the external jugular and subclavian veins at the level of the thoracic inlet by the clavicles and enlarged thyroid gland.

In1Yuh0.title: L-glutamine
In1Yuh0.description: A pharmaceutical-grade oral preparation of L-glutamine used to treat sickle cell disease. Thought to protect against oxidative stress in red blood cells, which reduces sickling.

rn1fuh0.title: Tylosis
rn1fuh0.description: An autosomal-dominant condition characterized by oral leukoplakia and thickened, yellowish skin on the soles of the feet and hands. Caused by a mutation in the RHBDF2 gene. Increases the risk of esophageal cancer.

Hn1Kuh0.title: GOLD group B
Hn1Kuh0.description: A COPD classification based on no exacerbations in the past year (or one exacerbation not leading to a hospital admission) and either an mMRC dyspnea score of ≥ 2 or a CAT score of ≥ 10.

tn1XEh0.title: Hemihyperplasia
tn1XEh0.description: A condition characterized by enlargement of one side of the body. It may be idiopathic or occur as part of overgrowth syndromes such as Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, neurofibromatosis type 1, and proteus syndrome.

Fn1gEh0.title: Negative mood
Fn1gEh0.description: A persistent inability to feel positive emotions (e.g., happiness, satisfaction, love). Used as a diagnostic criterion (e.g., for acute stress disorder) by the DSM-V.

8n1OEh0.title: Symptomatic anemia
8n1OEh0.description: A collection of clinical features that occur if there is insufficient circulating hemoglobin to meet the body's oxygen demand. Findings may include pallor, fatigue, lightheadedness, exertional dyspnea, palpitations, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, and tachypnea.

En18Eh0.title: Pseudohypoaldosteronism
En18Eh0.description: A disorder of mineralocorticoid activity that causes hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis in patients with normal renal function. Depending on the type, can be associated with abnormalities in volume status, serum sodium concentration, and serum chloride concentration.

Dn11vh0.title: Cold nodule
Dn11vh0.description: A circumscribed area of reduced radioiodine uptake on a radionuclide scan, which indicates a thyroid nodule with reduced or no physiologic secretory function.

Cn1qvh0.title: Internal jugular vein thrombosis
Cn1qvh0.description: A rare condition characterized by obstruction of the internal jugular vein by a clot. Causes include hypercoagulable states, Lemierre syndrome, intravenous drug use, internal jugular vein cannulation, and malignancy (e.g., lung cancer, thyroid cancer).

zn1rDh0.title: Capreomycin
zn1rDh0.description: An aminoglycoside used to treat drug-resistant tuberculosis. Adverse effects include nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, vestibulotoxicity, and neuromuscular blockade.

-n1DDh0.title: Kanamycin
-n1DDh0.description: An aminoglycoside used to treat drug-resistant tuberculosis. Adverse effects include nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, vestibulotoxicity, and neuromuscular blockade.

ZL1Zwh0.title: Ethionamide
ZL1Zwh0.description: An antibiotic that is chemically related to isoniazid and blocks the synthesis of mycolic acid. Used to treat drug-resistant tuberculosis. Adverse effects include hepatotoxicity, peripheral neuropathy, and gastric irritation.

0L1ewh0.title: Cycloserine
0L1ewh0.description: An antibiotic that inhibits cell wall synthesis in Mycobacterium tuberculosis as well as gram-positive and gram-negative organisms. Used as a second-line agent in drug-resistant tuberculosis. Adverse effects include peripheral neuropathy, depression, and psychosis.

aL1Qwh0.title: Para-aminosalicylic acid
aL1Qwh0.description: A drug that inhibits folate synthesis and is used in drug-resistant tuberculosis. Adverse effects include a hypersensitivity reaction that manifests with the combination of fever, arthralgia, skin rash, hepatosplenomegaly, and lymphadenopathy.

YL1nwh0.title: Rifapentine
YL1nwh0.description: An antibiotic that is closely structurally related to rifampin and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis. Used to treat Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium avium complex infections. Adverse effects include hepatotoxicity.

WL1P9h0.title: POC glucose
WL1P9h0.description: A rapid assessment of glucose levels obtained using a glucose meter. A POC glucose test can be performed at the bedside (or at home by ambulatory patients).

hL1cxh0.title: Thumb grind test
hL1cxh0.description: A test used to assess the integrity of the carpometacarpal joint of the thumb. It is performed by applying axial compression along the plane of the metacarpal bone and rotating the thumb metacarpal base. Pain or crepitus indicates a positive grind test, suggesting carpometacarpal osteoarthritis. However, a negative grind test does not exclude osteoarthritis.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Clinical significance

PL1WBh0.title: Thumb lever test
PL1WBh0.description: A test used to assess the integrity of the carpometacarpal joint of the thumb. It is performed by grasping the first metacarpal just distal to the base and moving it back and forth in the lateral and medial directions. Pain or crepitus indicates a positive lever test, suggesting carpometacarpal osteoarthritis.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Clinical significance

NL1-Bh0.title: HSP
NL1-Bh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Henoch-Schönlein purpura
2. Heat shock protein
3. Hereditary spastic paraplegia

5L1iyh0.title: Hereditary papillary renal cell carcinoma
5L1iyh0.description: An autosomal dominant condition with high penetrance. Results from activating mutations of the MET proto-oncogene, which is located on the long arm of chromosome 7. Usually associated with type 1 papillary renal cell carcinoma.

ML1Myh0.title: Heartburn
ML1Myh0.description: A burning retrosternal discomfort, commonly after meals, worsened by bending or lying down. It is the typical symptom in GERD, along with regurgitation.

nL17yh0.title: T follicular helper cell
nL17yh0.description: A type of CD4+ T-helper cell that is found in lymphoid follicles. Promotes B-cell activation and antibody production.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → T cells (T lymphocytes)

oL10Ah0.title: Sleep-disordered breathing
oL10Ah0.description: A range of disorders related to respiratory issues that occur during sleep. These include primary snoring, fragmented sleep, obstructive sleep apnea, central sleep apnea, sleep-related hypoventilation disorders, and sleep-related hypoxemia disorders.

KL1UAh0.title: Auto-adjusting positive airway pressure
KL1UAh0.description: A form of noninvasive ventilation that is programmed to adjust in real-time to only deliver the lowest possible positive airway pressure. Can be used in the initial titration of positive airway pressure and the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea.

6L1jAh0.title: APAP
6L1jAh0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:

1. Acetaminophen
2. Auto-adjusting positive pressure ventilation

pL1LAh0.title: Adaptive servo-ventilation
pL1LAh0.description: A device that delivers positive airway pressure and is programmed to continuously measure airflow or minute ventilation and to adjust pressures accordingly. Can be used in the treatment of central sleep apnea. Contraindicated in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction.

JL1sAh0.title: Paired branches of the abdominal aorta
JL1sAh0.description: The branches of the abdominal aorta that supply the abdominal wall, kidneys, adrenal glands, and gonads. Includes the inferior phrenic, middle suprarenal, renal, gonadal, and lumbar arteries.

qL1CAh0.title: Indirect fluorescent antibody test
qL1CAh0.description: A semiquantitative, rapid test to detect specific antibodies or antigens present in a patient's serum.

IL1Y_h0.title: Acute radiation syndrome
IL1Y_h0.description: An acute condition caused by irradiation of a significant portion of the body with an external, high dose of penetrating radiation in a short period of time. Clinical features include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, myelosuppression, and pneumonitis.

rL1f_h0.title: Chronic radiation injury
rL1f_h0.description: A chronic illness caused by tissue damage that results from multiple doses of radiation over an extended period of time. Manifestations include fibrosis, impaired wound healing, and malignancy (leukemias, solid tumors).

7L14_h0.title: Isotonic bicarbonate
7L14_h0.description: A crystalloid solution that is prepared by adding 150 mL of 8.4% sodium bicarbonate (i.e., three 50-mL ampules) to 850 mL of D5W or sterile water (a total of 1000 mL). Acts as an isotonic solution in the body, even when prepared with D5W, since the effective osmotic pressure gradient is determined by the concentrations of Na and HCO₃ (~150 mEq/L each) that remain after the rapid intracellular uptake of glucose.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

HL1K_h0.title: Fluid creep
HL1K_h0.description: A term used to describe the accumulation of IV fluids that are given in excess of patient requirements, typically from overlooked sources outside of calculated maintenance fluid prescriptions, e.g., fluids used to dilute medication infusions, preserve catheter patency, or replenish electrolytes.

sL1t_h0.title: 50% dextrose in water
sL1t_h0.description: A crystalloid solution that contains 50 g/dL (2780 mmol/L) of dextrose (a glucose isomer). Usually available as a 50-mL vial containing 25 g of dextrose, or a 25-mL vial containing 12.5 g of dextrose. Used primarily to treat symptomatic hypoglycemia and as an adjunctive treatment for hyperkalemia (e.g., combined with IV insulin).

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

GL1B_h0.title: Risk factors for fluid overload
GL1B_h0.description: A set of factors that increase a patient's risk of developing fluid overload in response to IV infusions. Includes medical conditions, e.g., heart failure, kidney disease, and cirrhosis, and factors related to infusions, e.g., the use of large volumes of fluid, hypotonic solutions, and rapid infusion rates.

tL1Xzh0.title: IV fluid challenge
tL1Xzh0.description: The administration of a small amount of IV crystalloid solution to assess fluid responsiveness (i.e., improvement in organ perfusion and hemodynamic parameters). E.g., 100–200 mL over 5–10 minutes or 250–500 mL over 15–20 minutes, with subsequent clinical and/or diagnostic reevaluation.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Monitoring and evaluation

8L1Ozh0.title: Hemodynamic monitoring parameters
8L1Ozh0.description: A collection of clinical and diagnostic parameters used to evaluate a patient's circulatory status and response to treatments, e.g., IV fluids or vasopressors. Composed of parameters of macrocirculation (e.g., heart rate, MAP, cardiac output, CVP) and microcirculation (e.g., capillary refill time, serum lactate, ScvO₂).

uL1pzh0.title: Distal motor latency
uL1pzh0.description: The time between stimulation of a nerve and subsequent muscular contraction.

EL18zh0.title: Drug-resistant tuberculosis
EL18zh0.description: A form of tuberculosis infection caused by mycobacteria that are resistant to antitubercular drugs. Types include rifampin-resistant tuberculosis, monoresistant tuberculosis, multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis.

zL1rZ30.title: Intravaginal testicular torsion
zL1rZ30.description: A type of testicular torsion in which the spermatic cord is twisted within the tunica vaginalis. Commonly associated with bell-clapper deformity.

-L1DZ30.title: Hematospermia
-L1DZ30.description: The presence of blood in semen. Common causes include prostate infection, iatrogenic trauma as a result of transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy, and seminal vesicle cysts.

Zo1Z030.title: Bell-clapper deformity
Zo1Z030.description: A congenital malformation in which the tunica vaginalis attaches high on the spermatic cord. Characterized by increased testicular mobility and associated with intravaginal testicular torsion.

0o1e030.title: Extravaginal testicular torsion
0o1e030.description: A type of testicular torsion in which there is a concomitant twisting of the testicle, spermatic cord, and tunica vaginalis. The most common type of testicular torsion in neonates.

ao1Q030.title: Mesorchium
ao1Q030.description: A fold of tissue that connects the epididymis and testes and originates from the primordial mesentery.

Yo1n030.title: Sling and swathe
Yo1n030.description: A bandage or orthotic device that supports a semiflexed elbow (sling) while limiting shoulder rotation and keeping the shoulder immobilized in adduction and internal rotation (swathe).

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

bo1H030.title: Bronze baby syndrome
bo1H030.description: A rare complication of phototherapy in children with elevated direct bilirubin (> 2mg/dL). Thought to be caused by an abnormal integumental accumulation of bronze-colored pigments that are photoisomers of bilirubin. Manifests with a reversible grayish-brown discoloration of the skin, urine, and serum and usually resolves within weeks after the end of phototherapy.

Xo19030.title: Sustained ventricular tachycardia
Xo19030.description: An arrhythmia originating in the ventricles characterized by tachycardia (> 100/minute) with broad QRS complexes (> 120 ms) on ECG and lasting longer than 30 seconds or terminated with treatment in hemodynamically unstable patients.

co1aa30.title: Inherited arrhythmia syndromes
co1aa30.description: A group of genetic syndromes caused by mutations in genes that encode cardiac ion channels resulting in a  predisposition for arrhythmias. May manifest with syncope or sudden cardiac death. Examples include Brugada syndrome and congenital long QT syndrome.

Wo1Pa30.title: Deflazacort
Wo1Pa30.description: A glucocorticoid agent with immunosuppressive and antiinflammatory properties used to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Slows down progression of muscle-related complications of the disease such as muscle weakness, respiratory insufficiency, and cardiac failure.

Vo1Ga30.title: Ulnar styloid
Vo1Ga30.description: A bony eminence located at the distal ulna, projecting posteriorly and medially. Grants flexibility to the hand and wrist.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

eo1xa30.title: Dorsal tubercle of the radius
eo1xa30.description: A bony prominence of the distal radius that serves as a pulley for the extensor pollicis longus tendon.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Bones and joints

Uo1bY30.title: Capture beat
Uo1bY30.description: A phenomenon seen on ECG during ventricular tachycardia in which a sinus node impulse travels through the AV node and triggers a normal ventricular depolarization. Capture beats appear as a normal sinus rhythm interrupting the wide QRS complex pattern of ventricular tachycardia.

2o1TY30.title: Fusion complex
2o1TY30.description: An ECG finding in which a supraventricular impulse and ectopic ventricular depolarization coincide at the ventricle, resulting in a complex with elements of both a regular QRS complex and a premature ventricular complex. Most commonly seen in ventricular tachycardia.

go1FY30.title: End-gaze nystagmus
go1FY30.description: A physiological horizontal jerk nystagmus caused by maintenance of extreme eye position. In contrast, gaze-evoked nystagmus is caused by maintenance of eccentric eye positions

So1yY30.title: Deescalation techniques
So1yY30.description: Verbal and nonverbal techniques used to help manage patient agitation. These include giving the patient space, open body language, calm verbal interaction with active listening, identifying the patient's emotions and expectations, and establishing clear and concise communication (e.g., repeating key concepts to the patient).

destinations.label: Approach to the agitated or violent patient → Deescalation

3o1Sb30.title: Risk factors for peptic ulcer disease
3o1Sb30.description: Factors include H. pylori infection, chronic NSAID use, smoking, and heavy alcohol use.

Ro1lb30.title: EVD
Ro1lb30.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. External ventricular drain
2. Ebola virus disease

io1Jb30.title: External ventricular drain
io1Jb30.description: A device that facilitates external drainage of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and/or blood from the ventricles of the brain and invasive intracranial pressure monitoring. Typically inserted as an emergency neurosurgical procedure to treat life-threatening intracranial hypertension associated with CSF outflow obstruction. Can also be used to deliver medication.

Qo1ub30.title: Digit span backward
Qo1ub30.description: A neurocognitive test to assess attention and working memory. The examiner presents a set of digits at distinct, regular intervals (e.g., 3-5-1). The patient is asked to repeat these digits in the reverse order (i.e., 1-5-3). The number of digits is then increased. A normal result is correct recitation of ≥ 4 digits. Causes for a pathological test result include delirium, focal left frontal damage, aphasia, and dementia.

jo1_b30.title: Distal radioulnar joint instability
jo1_b30.description: A condition caused by dislocation or subluxation of the distal radioulnar joint. Typically due to fractures to the distal radius or ulnar styloid process. Radiographic signs include shortening of the radius > 5 mm and widening of the joint space. May occur after initial injury or develop during healing. Usually requires surgical repair.

Po1WX30.title: Risk factors for tuberculosis
Po1WX30.description: A set of demographic and environmental factors that increase a patient's likelihood of contracting tuberculosis. These include immunosuppression (e.g., caused by HIV, malnutrition, diabetes, immunosuppressive medications), alcohol use, tobacco use, and close proximity to people with active tuberculosis (e.g., institutional living, working in health care, and having resided in a country with high prevalence).

lo1vX30.title: Lightning injury
lo1vX30.description: A type of electrical injury caused by lightning and characterized by cutaneous manifestations (e.g., burns, Lichtenberg figure, and metalization) and cardiac manifestations (e.g., ventricular fibrillation and asystole). Can result in complex regional pain syndrome.

destinations.label: Environmental pathology → Electrical and lightning injuries

mo1Vc30.title: DNA recombination
mo1Vc30.description: The exchange of genetic material between two DNA strands, which produces a new sequence of nucleotides. Occurs at least once for each aligned chromosome pair during meiosis. Responsible for genetic diversity and genome integrity.

5o1ic30.title: Mutant allele
5o1ic30.description: A form of an allele that does not code for the most common phenotype in a population.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Fundamental concepts of genetics

Mo1Mc30.title: Regulatory RNA
Mo1Mc30.description: A conserved group of RNA molecules that are responsible for epigenetic gene regulation and modification of chromatin structure. Typically are noncoding RNA molecules that do not produce translated protein products. Regulation occurs via multiple methods including RNA interference pathways, protein modification, and alteration of chromatin structural proteins (e.g., histones).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Epigenetic regulation of gene expression

no17c30.title: Striae
no17c30.description:
1. Striae (dermatology): a linear scarring of the dermis that becomes progressively hypopigmented and atrophic
2. Stria vascularis: the epithelial lining of the outer cochlear wall
3. Stria terminalis: a fascicle of nerve fibers that run along the lateral wall of the thalamus
4. Stria medullaris: a part of the epithalamus
5. Acoustic striae: a part of the auditory pathway located in the trapezoid body of the pons

Lo1wc30.title: Acoustic striae
Lo1wc30.description: A part of the auditory pathway located in the trapezoid body of the pons.

Ko1U130.title: SAE
Ko1U130.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Selective arterial embolization
2. Serious adverse event

so1tW30.title: Excitation-contraction coupling
so1tW30.description: A process in which an initiating stimulus (e.g., action potential, chemical stimulus) triggers an increase in intracellular Ca²⁺ and subsequent myofilament shortening, resulting in muscular contraction. Striated muscles (cardiac and skeletal) are stimulated by an electrical signal in the form of an action potential. Smooth muscle can be stimulated by electrical and chemical stimuli.

Go1BW30.title: Glycogen
Go1BW30.description: A complex polymer that consists of multiple chains of glucose molecules. Acts as a storage form of glucose and is present in all types of cells, with the exception of erythrocytes. Mainly stored in the liver and skeletal muscle. Converted back to glucose via glycogenolysis.

Fo1gd30.title: Hyperthyroidism in pregnancy
Fo1gd30.description: Increased thyroid gland function during pregnancy. Typically caused by Graves disease or hCG-mediated hyperthyroidism.

destinations.label: Graves disease → Graves disease in pregnancy

uo1pd30.title: Myofibril
uo1pd30.description: A contractile thread that is arranged in parallel columns in muscle cells. Composed of myofilaments (actin and myosin) and regulatory proteins and are facilitate muscle contraction.

Eo18d30.title: Acute viral tonsillopharyngitis
Eo18d30.description: A viral infection of the pharynx and/or pharyngeal tonsils, e.g., caused by adenovirus, coronavirus, or influenza virus.

destinations.label: Acute tonsillitis and pharyngitis → Clinical features

vo1Ad30.title: Acute bacterial tonsillopharyngitis
vo1Ad30.description: A bacterial infection of the pharynx and/or pharyngeal tonsils, e.g., caused by group A streptococci, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, or Corynebacterium diphtheriae.

destinations.label: Acute tonsillitis and pharyngitis → Clinical features

Do11V30.title: Scarlatiniform rash
Do11V30.description: A diffuse erythematous or fine maculopapular rash that first appears on the torso and spreads to the extremities. Characteristically spares the palms, soles, and perioral area. Typically associated with Streptococcus pyogenes infection but may also be seen in other infections, e.g., mycoplasma and viral hepatitis.

Co1qV30.title: Rate control for atrial fibrillation
Co1qV30.description: A mainstay of treatment of atrial fibrillation to normalize the ventricular heart rate. Drugs used for rate control include beta-blockers (e.g., esmolol, propranolol, metoprolol) and nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (e.g., diltiazem, verapamil).

xo1EV30.title: Rhythm control for atrial fibrillation
xo1EV30.description: A treatment strategy for atrial tachyarrhythmias (usually atrial fibrillation) to restore sinus rhythm and prevent atrial remodeling. Includes elective synchronized cardioversion and the use of antiarrhythmics such as flecainide, propafenone, ibutilide, dofetilide, or amiodarone.

zo1re30.title: Rapid assessment by cardiac echo
zo1re30.description: A bedside echocardiographic evaluation for patients in circulatory shock that facilitates differentiation between the different types of shock, i.e., hypovolemic shock, cardiogenic shock, obstructive shock, distributive shock.

0K1eU30.title: Low QRS voltage
0K1eU30.description: An ECG finding defined by a QRS amplitude < 5 mm in all limb leads or < 10 mm in all chest leads due to attenuation of the electrical signal. Etiologies include obesity, pericardial effusion, mediastinal processes, lung disease, and myocardial infiltration or degeneration (e.g., amyloidosis, scleroderma, myxedema, previous large myocardial infarction).

XK19U30.title: Neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia
XK19U30.description: A rare condition in newborns characterized by maternal-fetal platelet incompatibility resulting in fetal thrombocytopenia. Caused by the formation of maternal IgG antibodies against fetal platelets (most commonly targeting platelet antigen 1a), which cross the placenta. Can present with petechiae and ecchymoses within a few hours after birth; severe cases can result in spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage.

destinations.label: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn → Differential diagnoses

cK1a230.title: Subdural hygroma
cK1a230.description: A collection of CSF in the subdural space. Can occur due to a tear in the arachnoid membrane following a head injury. Appearance on neuroimaging can resemble chronic subdural hemorrhage.

VK1G230.title: Massive blood transfusion
VK1G230.description: The complete replacement of a patient's blood volume  (∼ 10 units of blood) within 24 hours, or at least 50% of the blood volume in any 3-hour period (∼ 5 units of blood). Definitions vary across the literature.

UK1bf30.title: Immediate hemodynamic support
UK1bf30.description: The use of fluids, vasopressors, inotropes, and/or adjunctive therapies (e.g., corticosteroids) in the acute management of shock to support cardiovascular circulation and improve organ and tissue perfusion.

gK1Ff30.title: Nonimmune hydrops fetalis
gK1Ff30.description: A subgroup of hemolytic diseases of the fetus and newborn characterized by the development of fetal hydrops that is not caused by red cell alloimmunization. Etiologies include severe fetal anemia, congenital infections or heart defects, and chromosomal aberrations. Account for approximately 90% of hydrops fetalis cases.

destinations.label: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn → Subtypes and variants

SK1yf30.title: Fluid responsiveness
SK1yf30.description: A term describing the ability of fluid therapy to measurably increase cardiac output (e.g., by 10–15 %) for a given patient. Can be assessed using preload-increasing maneuvers (e.g., IV fluid challenge, passive leg raise test) or other specialized diagnostic tests.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Monitoring and evaluation

hK1cT30.title: Passive leg raise test
hK1cT30.description: A test used to predict a patient's response to IV fluid therapy (and risk of fluid overload). Both legs are raised to 45° for ~ 1 minute, which increases venous return (preload) by ~ 150–300 mL. Cardiac output and vital signs are assessed for a positive response (e.g., increase in stroke volume by ≥ 10%). Differs from a fluid challenge in that no exogenous fluid administration is required (i.e., it is a self-volume challenge) and it is easily reversible.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Monitoring and evaluation

3K1ST30.title: Postpartum urinary retention
3K1ST30.description: A postpartum complication characterized by urinary retention due to injury to the pudendal nerve during birth. Manifestations include small void volumes, urinary frequency, and bladder discomfort.

RK1lT30.title: Colovesical fistula
RK1lT30.description: A fistula between the colon and the bladder. Common causes include diverticulitis, colon cancer, and Crohn disease.

iK1JT30.title: Bosniak classification
iK1JT30.description: A system used to classify renal cysts based on their complexity on a CT scan and estimate the likelihood of malignancy. Ranges from Bosniak I (simple cyst with thin, well-defined walls and homogeneous simple fluid) to Bosniak IV (cystic mass with ≥ 1 contrast-enhancing nodule).

media.title: Bosniak classification of cystic renal masses

QK1uT30.title: 8.4% sodium bicarbonate
QK1uT30.description: A concentrated solution containing 8.4 g/dL (1 mEq/mL) of sodium bicarbonate in water. Typically available as a 50-mL ampule, which can be given intravenously as a bolus or used to create isotonic bicarbonate solutions for infusion.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Types of parenteral fluids

jK1_T30.title: Lambda sign
jK1_T30.description: An ultrasonographic finding seen in dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy. The junction of the chorion and the placenta appears triangular and resemble the Greek symbol λ (lambda).

media.title: Lambda sign (twin peak sign) in twin pregnancy

PK1Wg30.title: Dominant R wave
PK1Wg30.description: A tall R wave in lead V1 on an ECG. Can be a normal finding in children and young adults. Pathological causes include right ventricular hypertrophy, right bundle branch block, posterior myocardial infarction, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

4K13g30.title: Cation-exchange medications
4K13g30.description: A group of drugs used to treat hyperkalemia that release sodium or calcium ions, which are exchanged for potassium in the gut, resulting in enhanced enteral potassium elimination. Consists of two classes: resins (e.g. sodium polystyrene sulfonate) and polymers (e.g., patiromer).

NK1-g30.title: Acute group A streptococcal tonsillopharyngitis
NK1-g30.description: An infection of the pharynx and/or pharyngeal tonsils caused by group A streptococci (GAS). GAS infection requires antibiotic treatment to prevent complications such as peritonsillar abscess, rheumatic fever, and poststreptococcal reactive arthritis or glomerulonephritis.

oK10h30.title: Sodium channel blockers
oK10h30.description: A group of drugs that inhibit voltage-gated sodium channels. Includes class I antiarrhythmics (e.g., procainamide), local anesthetic agents (e.g., lidocaine), specific antiepileptics (e.g., phenytoin, carbamazepine, lamotrigine), tricyclic antidepressants, and cocaine. Manifestations of sodium channel blocker toxicity include ECG changes (wide QRS complex, QT prolongation, right axis deviation), cardiac dysrhythmias, and seizures.

KK1Uh30.title: Splenectomy
KK1Uh30.description: A surgical procedure (laparoscopic or open) consisting of partial or total removal of the spleen. Indications include spleen rupture, significant splenomegaly or hypersplenism, and certain hematologic disorders and malignancies.

sK1t330.title: Pseudohyponatremia
sK1t330.description: Isotonic hyponatremia caused by laboratory artifact; occurs with very high amounts of protein or lipids in the plasma.

CK1qi30.title: Fear conditioning
CK1qi30.description: A model of behavioral learning in which conditioning of neutral stimuli with fear in a traumatic situation (e.g., a car accident) leads to anxiety as a neurobiological response to the neutral stimulus (e.g., cars) alone.

xK1Ei30.title: Type 1 myocardial infarction
xK1Ei30.description: Myocardial infarction caused by atherosclerotic plaque disruption or acute coronary thrombosis.

zK1rQ30.title: Cervical lymphadenitis
zK1rQ30.description: Tender, enlarged cervical lymph nodes. Typically results from an infectious or inflammatory process and resolves with treatment of the underlying condition.

Z61Zj30.title: Necrotizing pneumonia
Z61Zj30.description: A rapidly progressive, severe type of community-acquired pneumonia that usually manifests with sepsis and leads to pulmonary cavitation and gangrene. Most commonly caused by S. aureus (in adults) and P. aeruginosa (in children).

b61Hj30.title: Preload dependence
b61Hj30.description: A physiologic state in which cardiac output is determined primarily by the preload; i.e., changes in end-diastolic volume of the right and/or left ventricle directly affect changes in stroke volume. A drop in preload (e.g., from hypovolemia or diuresis) can precipitate circulatory shock in preload-dependent conditions (e.g., types of right ventricular failure, severe pulmonary hypertension, cardiac tamponade, severe aortic valve stenosis).

X619j30.title: MAS
X619j30.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Macrophage activation syndrome
2. Meconium aspiration syndrome

c61aP30.title: TTM
c61aP30.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Targeted temperature management
2. Trichotillomania

1612P30.title: HPS
1612P30.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Hepatopulmonary syndrome
2. Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis

W61PP30.title: PEM
W61PP30.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Protein-energy malnutrition
2. Paraneoplastic encephalomyelitis

m61Vl30.title: Modified Sgarbossa criteria for suspected STEMI
m61Vl30.description: A tool for identifying a STEMI in patients with known left bundle branch block or ventricular pacing. Diagnostic findings include: concordant ST elevation ≥ 1 mm in at least one lead with a positive QRS; concordant ST depression ≥ 1 mm in at least one lead from leads V1–V3; and proportionally excessive discordant ST elevation (ST elevation ≥ 25% of the depth of the S wave, i.e., ST/S ratio ≤ -0.25) in at least one lead with ST elevation ≥ 1 mm.

destinations.label: Acute coronary syndrome → ECG changes in STEMI

media.title: Modified Sgarbossa criteria for MI in LBBB

K61UN30.title: Myocardial injury
K61UN30.description: Any damage to myocardial tissue that leads cardiac troponin (cTn) levels to rise above the 99th percentile of the upper reference limit.

r61fm30.title: Radiologically isolated syndrome
r61fm30.description: The presence of demyelinating lesions characteristic of multiple sclerosis (MS) in an asymptomatic individual. Not considered an MS phenotype but may progress to MS.

7614m30.title: Dalfampridine
7614m30.description: A potassium channel blocker used to improve walking in individuals with multiple sclerosis.

G61Bm30.title: ECG findings in hyperkalemia
G61Bm30.description: A set of findings that include tall peaked T waves (mild hyperkalemia); QRS prolongation and P-wave flattening (moderate hyperkalemia);  absent P wave, intraventricular conduction block, and abnormal QRS morphology (severe hyperkalemia).

t61X530.title: Iliolumbar ligament
t61X530.description: A strong anterior attachment between the transverse process of L5 and the ilium. Supports the lumbosacral joint.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

E618530.title: Hereditary hemochromatosis
E618530.description: An autosomal recessive disorder characterized by excess iron deposition. Most commonly caused by a mutation in the HFE gene but may also be caused by mutations in other genes (e.g., hepcidin, transferrin receptor 2, ferroportin 1). Features of advanced disease include hepatomegaly, cirrhosis, bronzed skin, diabetes mellitus, arthralgia, and cardiomyopathy.

v61A530.title: Secondary hypoparathyroidism
v61A530.description: The suppression of parathyroid hormone secretion from the parathyroid glands as a result of hypercalcemia (e.g., due to hypervitaminosis D, osteolytic metastases, humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy) or severe hypomagnesemia.

w61hM30.title: Vitamin D-dependent rickets
w61hM30.description: A group of autosomal recessive conditions that are caused by impaired conversion of vitamin D precursors to active metabolites (type 1A and 1B VDDR) or inactivation of the vitamin D receptor (type 2 VDDR). Results in severe rickets during infancy.

C61qM30.title: Acetic acid
C61qM30.description: An acid with an antiseptic effect commonly used in the treatment of otitis externa.

x61EM30.title: Hymenoptera sting
x61EM30.description: A sting from insects of the Hymenoptera order (e.g., bees, wasps, hornets, yellow jackets, fire ants), which releases venom and causes transient, localized pain, erythema, and swelling. Severe stings can result in anaphylaxis.

B61zM30.title: Ocular ischemic syndrome
B61zM30.description: A condition caused by chronic ocular hypoperfusion associated with severe carotid artery stenosis. Symptoms include gradual, abrupt, or transient visual loss and ocular pain. Can result in anterior segment manifestations (e.g., conjunctival/episcleral injection, corneal edema, rubeosis iridis, neovascular glaucoma) and/or posterior segment manifestations (e.g., retinal hemorrhages, narrowed retinal arteries, microaneurysms).

A61Rn30.title: Anococcygeal ligament
A61Rn30.description: A fibrous raphe formed mainly by fibers of the levator ani muscles uniting in the midline. Attached to the coccyx and located posterior to the anus.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

_615n30.title: Ca/Cr clearance ratio
_615n30.description: An index of renal calcium excretion used in the evaluation of abnormal calcium metabolism. Determined by measuring the concentrations of calcium (Ca) and creatinine (Cr) in the serum and in a 24-hour urine collection sample. Calculated with the following formula: [urine Ca X serum Cr]/[urine Cr X serum Ca].

z61rn30.title: Urogenital hiatus
z61rn30.description: An opening in the pelvic floor in female individuals, through which the urethra and vagina pass. Located anterior to the anus and formed by a gap between the two levator ani.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

Yp1nL30.title: Polarized light microscopy
Yp1nL30.description: A microscopy technique that uses polarized light to visualize specific structures (e.g., green amyloid fibrils on Congo red stain, bright and polychromatic hair shafts in patients with Chédiak–Higashi syndrome). Typically used to visualize birefringent structures, which have a refractive index that depends on light polarization.

Xp19L30.title: Informed consent for research purposes
Xp19L30.description: The process of communication between a potential participant of a study and the investigators, which serves to provide understandable and sufficient information about the study so that the potential participant can make an informed, voluntary decision about whether to enroll. An informed consent form must be signed if the participant agrees to enroll in the study.

1p12o30.title: Monocytopenia
1p12o30.description: A decrease in the number of circulating monocytes to less than 3% of the total amount of leukocytes. Can occur in aplastic anemia and certain malignancies (e.g., hairy cell leukemia).

Wp1Po30.title: Leishmania
Wp1Po30.description: A genus of protozoans that are transmitted by the bite of phlebotomine sandflies and cause leishmaniasis. Grouped into Old World species (e.g., L. major, L. tropica, L. aethiopica), which are found in Africa and Asia, and New World species (L. mexicana, L.  venezuelensis, L. amazonensis), which are found in Central and South America. Old World species only cause cutaneous or visceral disease while some New World species can cause mucosal disease in addition to cutaneous or visceral disease.

destinations.label: General parasitology → Tissue and blood protozoa

Vp1Go30.title: Rhino-orbito-cerebral mucormycosis
Vp1Go30.description: A severe form of mucormycosis caused by inhalation of Mucor or Rhizopus spores, which cause a rapidly progressive, necrotizing infection of the paranasal sinuses and nasal cavity. Can spread to the orbit and cranial cavity. Typically seen in patients who have uncontrolled diabetes mellitus or are immunocompromised.

ep1xo30.title: Cutaneous mucormycosis
ep1xo30.description: A localized form of mucormycosis that is caused by the entry of Mucor or Rhizopus spores through a break in the skin (e.g., due to trauma, injections, burns, or surgery). Typically causes a localized cellulitis.

Up1bK30.title: Phlebotominae
Up1bK30.description: A sandfly whose bite can transmit the protozoan disease leishmaniasis and certain arboviral diseases (e.g., Rift valley fever, pappataci fever).

Tp16K30.title: Extramedullary hematopoietic pseudotumor
Tp16K30.description: An area of hematopoietic tissue that expands outside the bone marrow and through the bone cortex (causing bone deformities) or that embolizes and lodges in other organs (commonly the liver, spleen, mediastinum). May cause mass effect symptoms as it increases in size.

Rp1l630.title: Acetabular labrum
Rp1l630.description: A ring of fibrous cartilage located along the rim of the acetabulum. Provides an articular surface for the femoral head.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Hip joint

Pp1Wp30.title: Genetic counseling
Pp1Wp30.description: The education and support provided to patients with suspected or confirmed genetic diseases and carriers thereof. Includes a detailed family history, risk-based genetic testing, and perinatal counseling.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Genetic counseling

4p13p30.title: Clear-cell carcinoma of the cervix
4p13p30.description: A rare subtype of adenocarcinoma of the cervix, frequently associated with exposure to diethylstilbestrol (DES). Represents 4% of all cervical carcinomas.

kp1mp30.title: Crash cart
kp1mp30.description: A portable cart that contains equipment and medications used for the bedside resuscitation of patients who are critically ill or in cardiorespiratory arrest. Typically contains equipment for airway management and IV or IO access, a cardioverter-defibrillator, and medications for cardiac arrest, anaphylaxis, hypoglycemia, and opiate overdose.

Op1Ip30.title: Complicated lower urinary tract symptoms
Op1Ip30.description: A group of symptoms and factors that, when present, should raise suspicion for a complicated cause of urinary tract symptoms. For suspected prostate cancer, these include abnormal findings on digital rectal examination, an elevated prostate-specific antigen level, and hematuria. For suspected chronic urinary retention, these include recurrent urinary tract infections, a palpable bladder, and underlying risk factors for bladder disorder (e.g., neurologic disorder, urethral stricture).

lp1vp30.title: Frequency volume chart
lp1vp30.description: The real-time documentation by the patient of volume and time of each void. Used as an objective measure of lower urinary tract function.

Np1-p30.title: FVC
Np1-p30.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Forced vital capacity
2. Frequency volume chart

mp1VJ30.title: Voiding diary
mp1VJ30.description: A patient-maintained method of documenting fluid intake, urinary volume, frequency, and symptoms associated with urination. Records include the time of day of each micturition, any interference with sleep patterns, episodes of urinary incontinence, lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), and pain with voiding and/or bladder filling. Used to assess symptom severity and response to treatment in patients with LUTS, including urinary incontinence, benign prostatic hypertrophy, and interstitial cystitis.

5p1iJ30.title: Neonatal bacterial pneumonia
5p1iJ30.description: Pneumonia that occurs within the first 28 days of life. Symptoms include respiratory abnormalities (e.g., tachypnea, hypoxia, increased work of breathing) and other nonspecific symptoms (e.g., lethargy, poor feeding, jaundice).

destinations.label: Neonatal bacterial infections → Neonatal bacterial pneumonia

Mp1MJ30.title: Early-onset group B Streptococcal infection
Mp1MJ30.description: An infection with Streptococcus agalactiae (e.g., neonatal sepsis, neonatal meningitis, neonatal pneumonia) that occurs within the first 6 days of life. Typically acquired vertically from the birthing parent.

destinations.label: Prevention of neonatal Group B streptococcal infections → Overview

np17J30.title: Late-onset group B Streptococcus infection
np17J30.description: An infection with Streptococcus agalactiae (e.g., sepsis, meningitis, urinary tract infection, pneumonia) that occurs between 7 and 89 days of life. Typically acquired horizontally from nosocomial or community environments.

destinations.label: Prevention of neonatal Group B streptococcal infections → Overview

Lp1wJ30.title: Cardiac siderosis
Lp1wJ30.description: The process of accumulation of iron in cardiac tissue. Can lead to chamber remodeling and subsequent dilated or restrictive cardiomyopathy. Occurs in individuals with iron overload, e.g., due to hereditary hemochromatosis or repeated blood transfusions.

op10q30.title: Rectal hiatus
op10q30.description: A centrally positioned opening in the pelvic floor through which the rectum passes.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

Kp1Uq30.title: Perineum
Kp1Uq30.description: A diamond-shaped region located between the thighs. Comprises the area between the anus and external genitalia. Located inferior to the muscles of the pelvic floor and thereby separated from the pelvic cavity.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

6p1jq30.title: Perineal region
6p1jq30.description: An anatomical region inferior to the pelvic diaphragm, bounded by the pubic symphysis anteriorly, the coccyx posteriorly, and the ischial tuberosities laterally.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

pp1Lq30.title: Hemoglobin E disease
pp1Lq30.description: A condition caused by homozygosity of the hemoglobin E allele. Patients can be asymptomatic or present with features resembling β-thalassemia minor (i.e., mild microcytic anemia).

Jp1sq30.title: Superficial transverse perineal muscle
Jp1sq30.description: A slim transverse muscle located posterior to the deep transverse perineal muscle. Stabilizes the perineal body.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

qp1Cq30.title: Deep perineal pouch
qp1Cq30.description:
Anatomical space between the superior and inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm (perineal membrane).
Contains the deep transverse perineal muscle, urethral sphincter, and part of the urethra and vagina.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

Ip1YI30.title: Urogenital triangle
Ip1YI30.description: The anterior part of the perineal region, divided from the anal triangle by an imaginary line between the ischial tuberosities. Contains the deep and superficial perineal pouch as well as the perineal membrane.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

rp1fI30.title: Anal triangle
rp1fI30.description: The posterior part of the perineal region, divided from the urogenital triangle by an imaginary line between the ischial tuberosities. Contains the anal canal, the external anal sphincter muscle, and the ischiorectal fossae.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic floor and perineal region

7p14I30.title: Clinical features of hypothyroidism
7p14I30.description: A constellation of clinical features related to low circulating levels of thyroid hormone. Symptoms include fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, constipation, abnormal menstrual cycle, and decreased cognitive function. Signs include bradycardia, pretibial or periorbital edema, goiter, delayed relaxation of the deep tendon reflexes, and dry skin.

Hp1KI30.title: Cre recombinase
Hp1KI30.description: An enzyme that catalyzes site-specific recombination between loxP DNA sequences. Used in molecular biology to knock out or introduce different genes to cells.

sp1tI30.title: LoxP sequence
sp1tI30.description: A sequence of DNA that contains a site for Cre recombinase binding. Occurs naturally only in the P1 bacteriophage infecting E. coli, but can be introduced to other cells to construct a system for manipulation with Cre recombinase, which is collectively known as a Cre-LoxP system.

Gp1BI30.title: Prenatal gonorrhea screening
Gp1BI30.description: A screening test for gonorrhea infection in asymptomatic pregnant women using a nucleic acid amplification test of a vaginal swab. Recommended during the first trimester for all women < 25 years of age. Recommended during the first and third trimester for women with any of the following risk factors: living in a high-prevalence area, past or present history of sexually transmitted disease, new or multiple sexual partners, inconsistent condom use when not in a mutually monogamous relationship, and history of exchanging sex for drugs or money.

8p1Or30.title: Neonatal bacterial sepsis
8p1Or30.description: An infection with a positive bacterial blood or CSF culture that occurs within 28 days of life. Clinical features are often subtle and nonspecific (e.g., vital sign instability, lethargy, cyanosis, jaundice).

destinations.label: Neonatal bacterial infections → Neonatal bacterial sepsis

up1pr30.title: ACA
up1pr30.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Anticentromere antibody
2. Anticardiolipin antibody
3. Anterior communicating artery
4. Anterior cerebral artery

Ep18r30.title: Arcuate line (ilium)
Ep18r30.description: An anatomic landmark on the internal surface of the ilium, located inferior to the iliac fossa. Forms the lateral border of the pelvic inlet.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

vp1Ar30.title: Pectineal line (pubis)
vp1Ar30.description: A ridge on the superior ramus of the pubic bone; forms the anterior border of the pelvic inlet.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

Dp11730.title: Anterior superior iliac spine
Dp11730.description: An anatomical landmark located on the the most anterior part of the iliac crest where it forms a prominence. Aids in the identification of the McBurney and Lanz points as well as the inguinal ligament.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

Cp1q730.title: Superior pubic ligament
Cp1q730.description: A strong attachment between the two pubic tubercles. Provides stability for the pubic symphysis.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

xp1E730.title: Inferior pubic ligament
xp1E730.description: An inferior attachment between the pubic bones. Provides stability for the pubic symphysis and forms the anterior border of the pelvic outlet.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

yp1dH30.title: Obturator membrane
yp1dH30.description: A thin fibrous membrane that spans the obturator foramen. Perforated by the obturator canal, through which the obturator vessels and nerve pass.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

Ap1RH30.title: Critical illness-related corticosteroid insufficiency
Ap1RH30.description: A decrease in glucocorticoid levels in critically ill patients caused by an impaired HPA axis stress response. Features include refractory hypotension, fever, neurological and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, and metabolic abnormalities (e.g., hyponatremia, hypoglycemia, hyperkalemia, acidosis). Necrosis or hemorrhage of the hypothalamus, pituitary, or adrenal glands may also be present.

_p15H30.title: Obturator canal
_p15H30.description: A passageway within the obturator membrane that contains the obturator artery, vein, and nerve.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Joints, ligaments, and foramina of the pelvis

zp1rH30.title: Interstitial line sign
zp1rH30.description: A finding on transvaginal ultrasound characterized by an echogenic line that extends from the gestational sac into the upper uterus. It is the most specific finding for interstitial ectopic pregnancy.

-p1DH30.title: Rectouterine pouch
-p1DH30.description: Anatomic space in the peritoneal cavity between the posterior uterus and anterior rectum. In female individuals, this space is the lowest part of the peritoneal cavity in the upright position. Serves as a potential space for intraperitoneal fluid collection (e.g., ascites, blood, pus, malignant cells).

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Pelvic cavity and pelvic spaces

ZJ1Zs30.title: Endomysium
ZJ1Zs30.description: The layer of connective tissue surrounding individual muscle fibers.

0J1es30.title: Perimysium
0J1es30.description: The layer of connective tissue surrounding muscle fascicles, which are made up of muscle fibers. Perimysium is present in skeletal and smooth muscles, but not in cardiac muscles.

YJ1ns30.title: Ischial spine
YJ1ns30.description: A triangular, pointed eminence on the posterior surface of the ischium. Provides attachment to multiple muscles (e.g., levator ani, coccygeus, gemellus superior).

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

bJ1Hs30.title: Ischial tuberosity
bJ1Hs30.description: A large prominence on the posterior surface of the ramus of the ischium. Forms the lateral boundary of the pelvic outlet and provides attachment to multiple muscles (e.g., adductor magnus, semimembranosus, biceps femoris).

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Bony pelvis

cJ1aG30.title: Cranial giant cell arteritis
cJ1aG30.description: Giant cell arteritis predominantly affecting the common carotid artery and its branches, most commonly the temporal artery. Manifests with predominantly cranial symptoms, such as temporal headache, jaw claudication, and vision disturbances.

1J12G30.title: Large-vessel giant cell arteritis
1J12G30.description: A subtype of giant cell arteritis (GCA) involving the main branch of the aorta and/or its primary branches. Manifestations include chest pain, abdominal pain, and limb claudication. Classic cranial symptoms may be absent or less predominant than in cranial GCA.

WJ1PG30.title: Rule of threes
WJ1PG30.description:
A term that can refer to:
1. Rule of threes (osteopathic medicine)
2. Rule of threes (mathematics)

destinations.label: Thoracic spine and rib osteopathy → Anatomy

2J1Tt30.title: Catarrhal stage of pertussis
2J1Tt30.description: The first clinical stage of pertussis. Characterized by coryza and a mild cough. Fever, if present, is usually low-grade. Typically lasts 1–2 weeks but can be briefer in young infants. It is the most infective stage of pertussis. Followed by the paroxysmal stage.

fJ1kt30.title: Paroxysmal stage of pertussis
fJ1kt30.description: The second clinical stage of pertussis. Characterized by the absence of fever and the onset of coughing spells that progressively increase in severity. The spells are often interspersed with high-pitched, whooping inspirations (gasping for air) and followed by vomiting and diaphoresis. Complications of pertussis such as pneumonia, apnea, failure to thrive, rib fractures, rectal prolapse, and subconjunctival or subdural hemorrhage typically occur during this stage. Occurs following the catarrhal stage, typically lasts 2–8 weeks, and is followed by the convalescent stage.

TJ16t30.title: Prenatal screening for Group B streptococcus
TJ16t30.description: A screening test used to detect vaginal-rectal colonization with group B Streptococcus (GBS). Screening guides targeted antibiotic prophylaxis to prevent vertical transmission of GBS infection to neonates. Routinely performed on pregnant women from 36+0 to 37+6 weeks' gestation.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Group B streptococcus screening

SJ1yt30.title: Inferior vesical artery
SJ1yt30.description: A branch of the anterior trunk of the internal iliac artery that supplies the fundus of the bladder and the lower part of the ureter. In male individuals, it also supplies the prostate gland, seminal vesicles, and ductus deferens.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

hJ1cF30.title: Vaginal artery
hJ1cF30.description: A branch of the anterior trunk of the internal iliac artery that usually replaces the inferior vesical artery in female individuals. Supplies the anterior and posterior wall of the vagina.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

3J1SF30.title: Non-striated muscle
3J1SF30.description: Muscle that lacks the banding patterns of striated muscle under a microscope. This is due to contractile fibers not being arranged in sarcomeres. Smooth muscle is nonstriated muscle.

RJ1lF30.title: Iliolumbar artery
RJ1lF30.description: A branch of the internal iliac artery that gives off an iliac and a lumbar branch. The iliac branch supplies the ilium and the iliacus muscle, and the lumbar branch supplies the quadratus lumborum and the psoas muscle.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

iJ1JF30.title: Confusion assessment method
iJ1JF30.description: A clinical assessment tool used to diagnose delirium that evaluates four features related to the patient's mental status. Delirium is diagnosed when feature 1 (acute onset or fluctuation), 2 (inattention), and either 3 (disorganized thinking) or 4 (altered consciousness) are present.

QJ1uF30.title: Lateral sacral arteries
QJ1uF30.description: The branches from the internal iliac artery that supply the skin posterior to the sacrum.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

jJ1_F30.title: Superior gluteal artery
jJ1_F30.description: A large branch of the internal iliac artery that supplies the muscles and skin of the gluteal region.

destinations.label: Pelvis and hip joint → Vessels, nerves, and lymphatics of the pelvis

PJ1W830.title: Clinical features of hepatic encephalopathy
PJ1W830.description: A constellation of nonspecific, reversible neurological signs and symptoms resulting from complex metabolic alterations in patients with acute or chronic liver disease. Commonly includes altered level of consciousness (ranging from mild confusion to coma), changes in the sleep-wake cycle, memory loss, personality changes, asterixis, and muscle rigidity.

lJ1v830.title: Risk factors for bloodborne diseases
lJ1v830.description: Factors that increase the risk of contracting bloodborne diseases (e.g., HIV, or hepatitis B and C virus) include occupational exposure (e.g., health care workers), unsafe injections or transfusions, drug use, and high-risk sexual behaviors (e.g., commercial sex work, anal sex, unprotected sex with individuals from high-risk groups or geographical areas).

NJ1-830.title: Tea and toast syndrome
NJ1-830.description: A type of malnutrition caused by a diet that is poor in protein and salt, combined with adequate or excessive fluid intake; as a consequence, hypotonic hyponatremia can develop. Commonly seen in elderly patients who cannot or do not wish to prepare and eat a proper meal.

mJ1Vu30.title: Risk factors for aspiration
mJ1Vu30.description: A constellation of patient risk factors that reduce airway protection reflexes and increase the probability of inhaling foreign material (e.g., gastric contents). These include altered mental status (e.g., sedation, intoxications), conditions affecting the central nervous system (e.g., stroke, dementia, Parkinson disease), and gastrointestinal diseases (e.g., tracheoesophageal fistulas).

nJ17u30.title: Barmah Forest virus
nJ17u30.description: An alphavirus of the Togaviridae family that is transmitted via the bite of an infected Culex annulirostis or Aedes vigilax mosquito. Found in Australia and Papua New Guinea. Barmah forest virus disease manifests with fever, headache, fatigue, joint pain and swelling, and skin rashes.

LJ1wu30.title: Cognitive stimulation therapy
LJ1wu30.description: A therapeutic program, usually involving small groups of patients, that aims to improve cognitive abilities (e.g., memory) in patients with cognitive impairment (e.g., delirium or dementia). Therapy is usually administered by trained personnel and includes activities such as word searches and board games.

KJ1UE30.title: Acute physiology and chronic health evaluation II
KJ1UE30.description: A scoring system used to assess the severity of organ dysfunction and the risk of mortality. Commonly used in critically ill patients. The score considers age; temperature; mean arterial pressure; heart rate; respiratory rate; oxygenation; arterial pH; serum bicarbonate, sodium, potassium, and creatinine levels; presence of acute kidney injury; hematocrit levels; white blood cell count; and the patient's Glasgow coma scale score.

destinations.label: Care of the critically ill patient → Predictive scoring systems

6J1jE30.title: Behavioral pain scale
6J1jE30.description: A scale used to identify pain in critically ill patients on mechanical ventilation. Three items are evaluated and awarded points: facial expression, movement of the upper limbs, and mechanical ventilation compliance. A score ≥ 5 is considered to reflect an unacceptable level of pain and requires appropriate analgesia.

destinations.label: Acute pain management → Special patient groups

pJ1LE30.title: Critical care pain observation tool
pJ1LE30.description: A scale used to identify pain in critically ill patients. Four items are evaluated and awarded points: facial expressions, body movements, ventilator compliance in intubated patients or vocalization in nonintubated patients, and muscle tension. A score ≥ 3 indicates significant pain.

destinations.label: Acute pain management → Special patient groups

JJ1sE30.title: Gluten challenge
JJ1sE30.description: The supervised reintroduction of gluten-rich foods for 2-8 weeks in individuals with suspected celiac disease who have been consuming a gluten-free diet. If diagnostic studies are performed in patients who have not recently consumed gluten, they may have false-negative results. When gluten is regularly consumed for even a short period, it typically results in characteristic mucosal changes in the small bowel and the production of antibodies.

qJ1CE30.title: Spontaneous awakening trial
qJ1CE30.description: A trial of stopping all sedating medications (without compromising analgesia) and restarting them at lower doses. In critically ill patients, daily interruption of narcotics and sedation has been associated with improved outcomes, including a shorter period of mechanical ventilation and in the ICU.

HJ1Kv30.title: Recombinant activated factor VII
HJ1Kv30.description: An activated recombinant clotting factor used to treat hemorrhage in patients with hemophilia A, hemophilia B, acquired hemophilia, factor VII deficiency, and Glanzmann thrombasthenia.

sJ1tv30.title: T-sign
sJ1tv30.description: An ultrasonographic finding seen in monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies. The absence of a chorion between the layers of intertwin membrane results in the appearance of the letter T.

media.title: T-sign in monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy

GJ1Bv30.title: Epimysium
GJ1Bv30.description: The dense, fibrous sheath of tissue that surrounds a muscle.

tJ1XD30.title: Lomitapide
tJ1XD30.description: A microsomal triglyceride transfer protein inhibitor used to treat abetalipoproteinemia in combination with other lipid-lowering agents. Decreases blood levels of VLDL, LDL, and chylomicrons.

FJ1gD30.title: Plaque reduction neutralization test
FJ1gD30.description: A quantitative study that measures specific neutralizing antibody titers. The patient's serum is mixed with a particular virus and analyzed to determine the number of plaque-forming units created. Used for suspected flavivirus infections (e.g., dengue fever, Zika virus infection) to confirm the diagnosis and rule out cross-reactivity.

8J1OD30.title: Confusion assessment method intensive care unit
8J1OD30.description: A variation of the confusion assessment method (CAM) that is modified for use in critically ill patients. For patients unable to communicate verbally, yes/no questions are asked which can be answered with a hand squeeze to assess for disordered thinking. For sedated patients, the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale can be used to assess consciousness and fluctuations in mental state.

destinations.label: Care of the critically ill patient → Supportive care

media.title: Confusion assessment method intensive care unit (CAM-ICU)

uJ1pD30.title: CAM
uJ1pD30.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Confusion assessment method
2. Complementary and alternative medicine
3. Cell adhesion molecule

EJ18D30.title: Powassan virus
EJ18D30.description: A tick-borne orthoflavivirus endemic to North America. Infections typically occur in the spring to early fall and manifest with febrile illness that can progress to a neuroinvasive disease (meningitis, encephalitis).

vJ1AD30.title: IgM antibody capture enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
vJ1AD30.description: A diagnostic test used for qualitative detection of viral IgM antibodies. IgM antibodies are captured on a plate using anti-IgM antibodies followed by the addition of specific viral antigens. Used for detection of viral diseases like Dengue fever and West Nile fever.

DJ11w30.title: Inebilizumab
DJ11w30.description: A humanized monoclonal antibody against CD19 used to prevent attacks in aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder. Common side effects include arthralgias and increased susceptibility to infections.

wJ1hw30.title: Satralizumab
wJ1hw30.description: A humanized monoclonal antibody against IL-6 receptor used to prevent attacks in aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.

9J1Nw30.title: Staccato cough
9J1Nw30.description: A subtype of cough characterized by short, repetitive coughs with deep inspirations in between. Can be caused by chlamydial pneumonia. The whooping cough of pertussis can mimic a staccato cough.

CJ1qw30.title: Afebrile pneumonia syndrome
CJ1qw30.description: A syndrome of pneumonia without fever in the late neonatal period or during early infancy. Typically caused by Chlamydia trachomatis, Ureaplasma urealyticum, or cytomegalovirus. Less commonly caused by respiratory syncytial virus and certain parainfluenza virus serotypes.

xJ1Ew30.title: Pneumococcal conjunctivitis
xJ1Ew30.description: An acute bacterial conjunctivitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae (most commonly nonencapsulated strains). Keratitis usually does not occur (unless corneal trauma is present) because S. pneumoniae cannot penetrate the intact corneal epithelium.

yJ1d930.title: Prenatal screening for Chlamydia trachomatis
yJ1d930.description: A screening test for Chlamydia trachomatis infection in asymptomatic pregnant women using a nucleic acid amplification test of a vaginal swab. Recommended during the first and third trimesters for women < 25 years of age who are not in mutually monogamous relationships or who have a sexual partner with a sexually transmitted disease.

-J1D930.title: Carbon dioxide narcosis
-J1D930.description: A severe manifestation of hypercapnia characterized by a depressed level of consciousness. Can develop in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

aq1QC30.title: Mild hypercalcemia
aq1QC30.description: A total serum calcium concentration of 10.6–11.9 mg/dL (2.63–2.99 mmol/L) or ionized (free) calcium concentration of 5.26–7.9 mg/dL (1.32–1.99 mmol/L).

Yq1nC30.title: Moderate hypercalcemia
Yq1nC30.description: A total serum calcium concentration of 12–14 mg/dL (3–3.5 mmol/L) or ionized (free) calcium concentration of 8–10 mg/dL (2–2.5 mmol/L).

1q12x30.title: Sundowning
1q12x30.description: An increase in neuropsychiatric symptoms (e.g., anxiety, confusion, agitation) in the evening or at night, possibly due to alterations in the circadian rhythm. Typically seen in patients with previous cognitive impairment (e.g., dementia, Parkinson disease, delirium).

dq1ox30.title: Urine protein dipstick test
dq1ox30.description: A rapid, semiquantitative test that detects proteins (typically albumin) in the urine using colorimetry. Based on the color change of the protein-readout segment of the dipstick, one of the following interpretations is made: negative, trace, 1+, 2+, 3+, and 4+, which correspond roughly to urine protein concentrations of < 0.1 g/L, 0.15 g/L, 0.3 g/L, 1 g/L, 3 g/L, and > 10 g/L, respectively. Assuming an average daily urine output of 1 L, readings of 3+ and 4+ are considered surrogates for nephrotic range proteinuria (> 3.5 g/day).

Vq1Gx30.title: Eosinophil cast
Vq1Gx30.description: A finding on urine microscopy typically associated with allergic interstitial nephritis. Caused by amalgamations of plasma proteins and eosinophils in renal tubules.

Uq1bB30.title: ACL
Uq1bB30.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Anterior cruciate ligament
2. Anticardiolipin antibody

2q1TB30.title: Theca externa
2q1TB30.description: The outer layer of the theca folliculi. Consists of fibroblast-like cells and smooth muscle cells embedded in collagen matrix. Unlike the theca interna, the theca externa does not produce hormones.

Tq16B30.title: Post‑exposure prophylaxis for Lyme disease
Tq16B30.description: A single dose of oral doxycycline if a tick bite (Ixodes spp) is suspected and the following criteria are met: tick attachment for ≥ 36 hours, prophylaxis can be started within 72 hours of the tick bite, and the tick bite occurred in a highly endemic area.

gq1FB30.title: Pay-for-performance
gq1FB30.description: A payment model in which compensation depends on health care providers meeting certain metrics for the quality and efficiency of care provided.

destinations.label: Health care system → Alternative payment models

hq1cy30.title: Xanthine oxidase inhibitors
hq1cy30.description: A class of drugs that decrease uric acid production by inhibiting xanthine oxidase, an enzyme involved in purine metabolism. Typically used in the management of gout and hyperuricemia. Examples include allopurinol and febuxostat.

Pq1WA30.title: Autoimmune hepatitis-primary sclerosing cholangitis overlap syndrome
Pq1WA30.description: An autoimmune liver disease characterized by clinical, serological, and cholangiographic features of both autoimmune hepatitis and primary sclerosing cholangitis.

kq1mA30.title: IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis
kq1mA30.description: A manifestation of IgG4-related disease that has features similar to primary sclerosing cholangitis (e.g., cholestasis, strictures in intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts). Typically accompanied by IgG4-related pancreatitis.

mq1V_30.title: Orthodromic AVRT
mq1V_30.description: A type of atrioventricular reciprocating tachycardia where conduction of the reentry circuit is antegrade through the AV node and retrograde through the accessory pathway. The resulting tachyarrhythmia has narrow QRS complex, as ventricular depolarization happens rapidly through the His-Purkinje system. It is often indistinguishable from AVNRT on ECG appearance alone.

nq17_30.title: Clean-contaminated wound
nq17_30.description: A type of surgical wound that involves entry into the respiratory, gastrointestinal, or genitourinary tract without breaking sterile technique (e.g., encountering contents of the gastrointestinal tract).

oq10z30.title: Teach back method
oq10z30.description: A technique to verify patients' understanding of the health information they have been given. Patients demonstrate their understanding of information by teaching it back to the clinician.

pq1Lz30.title: Immune tolerance
pq1Lz30.description: The unresponsiveness of an organism’s immune system to antigens in an effort to prevent harmful over-reactivity. There are two types of mechanisms of immune tolerance: central (e.g., negative selection of T cells) and peripheral (e.g., suppression of lymphocyte activation).

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → Immune tolerance and autoimmunity

Gq1B-30.title: Stork test
Gq1B-30.description: A procedure that is part of Greenman's modified 10-step screening examination that is used to assess the movement of the sacroiliac joint. With the patient standing, the physician places one thumb over the posterior superior iliac spine and the other thumb over the midline of the sacrum at the same level. The physician asks the patient to flex their hip. A negative test is indicated by the thumb over the posterior superior iliac spine moving inferior (in relation to the thumb over the sacrum). A positive test is indicated by the thumb over the posterior superior iliac spine moving superior (in relation to the thumb over the sacrum). A positive test indicates sacroiliac joint restriction in correlation to the standing flexion test.

tq1XZR0.title: Signs of wound infection
tq1XZR0.description: Features of acute wound infection include erythema, swelling, and increased pain, all of which may be accompanied by purulent drainage. Infected chronic wounds may manifest similarly and/or with friable granulation tissue and a strong, unpleasant odor.

Fq1gZR0.title: Regularly irregular rhythm
Fq1gZR0.description: A clinical or ECG finding of an irregular heart rhythm in which the irregularity is consistent, e.g., every third beat is dropped. Can be seen in conditions such as second-degree AV blocks.

8q1OZR0.title: Braden scale
8q1OZR0.description: A scale used to assess a patient's risk of developing a pressure ulcer. The following six domains are evaluated on scales of 1 to 4 and 1 to 3: activity level, mobility, sensory perception, nutrition, exposure to moisture, and exposure to friction. Lower total scores indicate a higher risk.

uq1pZR0.title: Norton scale
uq1pZR0.description: A scale used to assess a patient's risk of developing a pressure ulcer. The following five domains are evaluated on a scale of 1 to 4: physical condition, mental condition, mobility, activity, and continence. Lower total scores indicate a higher risk.

Eq18ZR0.title: Symptoms of heart failure
Eq18ZR0.description: A group of symptoms that typically occur as a result of impaired cardiac function. The most common symptoms are fatigue and dyspnea, which can progress to orthopnea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. May be associated with features of fluid overload (e.g., peripheral edema or productive cough).

Dq110R0.title: Wound closure strips
Dq110R0.description: Adhesive strips used for noninvasive wound closure. May be applied to uncomplicated clean wounds instead of sutures when wound edges can be approximated without tension, or as an additive measure to further secure sutured wounds.

9q1N0R0.title: Hair apposition technique
9q1N0R0.description: A noninvasive technique used to close scalp lacerations. Strands of hair are grasped from both sides of the wound and interlocked over the wound in a twist, which is secured with a drop of tissue adhesive.

destinations.label: Soft tissue injuries of the head and neck → Scalp lacerations

xq1E0R0.title: Junctional escape rhythm
xq1E0R0.description: A type of escape rhythm generated by ectopic pacemaker cells in the AV node. Can be seen when atrial impulses are not transmitted through the AV node, e.g., in third-degree AV block. P waves are completely dissociated from the QRS complexes or may even be absent, depending on the etiology. The QRS complexes are typically narrow and occur at a rate of 40-60/minute.

destinations.label: Atrioventricular block → Third-degree AV block (complete heart block)

Bq1z0R0.title: Ventricular escape rhythm
Bq1z0R0.description: A type of escape rhythm generated by ectopic pacemaker cells in the ventricles (typically the bundle of His). Can be seen when atrial impulses are not transmitted through the AV node, e.g., in third-degree AV block. P waves are completely dissociated from the QRS complexes or may even be absent, depending on the etiology. The QRS complexes are typically wide and occur at a rate of 20-40/minute.

destinations.label: Atrioventricular block → Third-degree AV block (complete heart block)

yq1daR0.title: Risk factors for urinary tract obstruction
yq1daR0.description: A set of conditions that indicate an increased risk for developing an obstruction along the urinary tract. Conditions include prostate enlargement, urinary stones, pelvic or abdominal surgery or trauma, pelvic or abdominal tumors, retroperitoneal disease, bladder dysfunction, pelvic floor disorders, and neurological disease or injury.

Aq1RaR0.title: Diabetic dermopathy
Aq1RaR0.description: A common cutaneous finding of diabetes mellitus characterized by asymptomatic, erythematous papules that progress to atrophic, hyperpigmented macules and patches. Most commonly develops on pretibial skin.

zq1raR0.title: Pure androgen-secreting adrenal tumor
zq1raR0.description: A type of adrenal tumor that only produces androgens, which results in features of virilization in female individuals. They are usually malignant tumors and are rare in comparison to most functional adrenocortical tumors, which produce both androgens and corticosteroids.

0I1eYR0.title: Kidney Disease Improving Global outcomes (KDIGO) criteria for staging of AKI
0I1eYR0.description: A commonly used classification system for acute kidney injury (AKI) that was introduced with the 2012 KDIGO guidelines. AKI is classified as stage 1-3 based on changes in serum creatinine and urine output.

aI1QYR0.title: Acute mountain sickness
aI1QYR0.description: A condition that occurs after rapid ascent to high altitude (usually above 2000–2500 m) as a result of inadequate acclimatization to lower levels of atmospheric oxygen. Usually, initial manifestations are nonspecific, e.g., headache, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, weakness, and/or dyspnea, but it can also progress to potentially lethal high-altitude cerebral or pulmonary edema.

bI1HYR0.title: 11-deoxycortisol
bI1HYR0.description: A compound formed from 17-hydroxyprogesterone by 21-hydroxylase. Converted to cortisol by 11β-hydroxylase.

XI19YR0.title: Jeanne sign
XI19YR0.description: A hyperextension of the MCP joint of the thumb during a key pinch movement due to loss of function of the adductor pollicis muscle and predominance of the extensor pollicis longus and the abductor pollicis brevis. Can be caused by ulnar nerve lesions.

1I12bR0.title: Right ventricular outflow tract obstruction
1I12bR0.description: A cardiac defect characterized by the inability of blood to pass out of the right ventricle through the pulmonary valve. Causes include pulmonic valve stenosis, defects in the infundibulum, and defects in the pulmonary artery.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Tetralogy of Fallot

VI1GbR0.title: Dengue with warning signs
VI1GbR0.description: Warning signs include abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, hemorrhagic manifestations (e.g., petechiae, epistaxis, gingival bleeding), extravascular fluid accumulation (e.g., pleural effusion, ascites), lethargy, restlessness, liver enlargement > 2 cm below the costal margin, and increased hematocrit with decreased platelets (measured on > 2 consecutive blood tests). Typically manifests during the late febrile stage and suggests progression to severe dengue.

eI1xbR0.title: Graham patch
eI1xbR0.description: A surgical repair method used for small, perforated duodenal ulcers. Well-vascularized omentum is used to plug the perforation and is stitched into place. Can be performed laparoscopically or via an open surgical technique.

UI1bXR0.title: Hemostatic methods
UI1bXR0.description: A set of techniques to stop bleeding. Primary measures include applying pressure, packing deeper wounds, and interrupting the blood flow with a tourniquet.
