Further measures include pharmacological hemostasis with antifibrinolytics or locally applied hemostatic agents (e.g., epinephrine or fibrin), surgical hemostasis with thermal coagulation or ligation (e.g., with sutures or clips), and interventional methods such as angiographic embolization.

destinations.label: Management of trauma patients → Primary survey

TI16XR0.title: Acute peripheral vestibulopathy
TI16XR0.description: A term used to encompass peripheral causes of acute vestibular syndrome (i.e., vestibular neuritis and labyrinthitis).

gI1FXR0.title: Cepacia syndrome
gI1FXR0.description: A severe, necrotizing pneumonia caused by Burkholderia cepacia. Commonly progresses to sepsis and respiratory failure. More common in patients with cystic fibrosis and following lung transplantation.

SI1yXR0.title: Ofatumumab
SI1yXR0.description: A fully human antibody against CD20 used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia and relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.

3I1ScR0.title: Lateral dorsal thalamic nucleus
3I1ScR0.description: The most anterior nucleus of the lateral nuclear group of the thalamus. Receives afferent fibers from the pretectum as well as the superior colliculus and projects to the limbic system, especially the cingulate gyrus. Involved in spatial learning and memory.

iI1JcR0.title: Antiprogestins
iI1JcR0.description: A competitive inhibitor of progesterone receptors that causes inhibition or delay of ovulation, suppression of endometrial maturation, and pregnancy termination. Examples include mifepristone and ulipristal acetate.

destinations.label: Female sex hormones → Reproductive system drugs

jI1_cR0.title: Pendular nystagmus
jI1_cR0.description: A type of nystagmus defined by sinusoidal oscillating movements of one or both eyes. It is often asymmetrical, dissociated between the eyes, and can occur in any direction (circular, vertical, horizontal, or any other wave movement). It is always considered pathologic and related to multiple sclerosis, encephalitis, stroke, or brainstem drug toxicity.

PI1W1R0.title: Window period of hepatitis B infection
PI1W1R0.description: A period in the course of hepatitis B infection during which neither HBsAg nor anti-HBs antibodies can be detected. There are two such window periods. The first one, which is similar to the classic window period of any infection, occurs between exposure to the hepatitis B virus and the appearance of HbsAg in serum. The second one occurs at the time of seroconversion from HBsAg to anti-HBs antibodies and is caused by the equivalence zone phenomenon, in which relatively equal amounts of HBsAg and anti-HBs antibodies in serum prevent the detection of both HBsAg and anti-HBs antibodies. Testing for anti-HBc antibodies can help detect cases that would be missed during the second window period.

media.title: Serology time course of acute and resolved hepatitis B infection

4I131R0.title: Siponimod
4I131R0.description: A modulator of sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor used to treat clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting  multiple sclerosis, and secondary-progressive multiple sclerosis. Side effects include hypertension, transient bradycardia, and dose-dependent lymphopenia.

kI1m1R0.title: Ozanimod
kI1m1R0.description: A selective modulator of sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor used for management of clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, and secondary-progressive multiple sclerosis. Side effects include headache, hypertension, transaminase increase, and bradycardia. Contraindicated in individuals with a history of recent myocardial infarction, heart failure, unstable angina, or AV block.

OI1I1R0.title: Peripheral vestibular system
OI1I1R0.description: The portion of the vestibular system that consists of the inner ear (utricle, saccule, and semicircular canals) and pathways to the brainstem (vestibulocochlear nerve). Plays an important role in maintaining balance, posture, spatial orientation, and coordinating head and eye movements (i.e., the vestibuloocular reflex).

lI1v1R0.title: Central vestibular system
lI1v1R0.description: The portion of the vestibular system that consists of the vestibular nuclei and structures in the cerebellum and brainstem. Plays an important role in maintaining balance, posture, spatial orientation, and coordinating head and eye movements (i.e., the vestibulo-ocular reflex).

NI1-1R0.title: Unidirectional nystagmus
NI1-1R0.description: A subtype of nystagmus characterized by beating of the eyes in only one direction (e.g., right-beating nystagmus that does not convert to left-beating nystagmus on gaze testing to the left). Can be caused by peripheral vestibular disorders (e.g., acute vestibular neuritis). In contrast, direction-changing nystagmus can be caused by a stroke.

MI1MWR0.title: Complex fracture
MI1MWR0.description: A fracture in which the bone is broken into many pieces and/or the surrounding tissue is damaged (e.g., due to displacement of bone fragments).

nI17WR0.title: MSH
nI17WR0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Melanocyte-stimulating hormone
2) MutS homolog 1 or MutS homolog 2

LI1wWR0.title: Nailfold capillary microscopy
LI1wWR0.description: A noninvasive evaluation of the nailfold vessels using an instrument (e.g., dermatoscope, ophthalmoscope) and a drop of oil to enhance transparency. Can be used to distinguish primary Raynaud phenomenon from nailbed changes seen in systemic sclerosis spectrum disorders.

oI10dR0.title: PVC
oI10dR0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Premature ventricular complex
2) Polyvinyl chloride

JI1sdR0.title: Isoelectric focusing
JI1sdR0.description: An electrophoretic technique that separates proteins based on their net charge. Commonly used to identify abnormal hemoglobin chains (e.g., for the diagnosis of sickle cell disease).

II1YVR0.title: Lateral posterior thalamic nucleus
II1YVR0.description: A thalamic nucleus that is part of the posterior subgroup of the lateral thalamic nuclei. Receives input from the superior colliculus and projects to the superior parietal lobe. Contributes to vision and regulation of visual attention.

HI1KVR0.title: Ventral anterior thalamic nucleus
HI1KVR0.description: A thalamic nucleus that is part of the ventral subgroup of the lateral thalamic nuclei. Consists of a principal part and a magnocellular part. Receives input from the basal ganglia and projects to the premotor cortex. Responsible for modulating and coordinating movement.

sI1tVR0.title: Ventral lateral thalamic nucleus
sI1tVR0.description: A thalamic nucleus that is part of the ventral subgroup of the lateral thalamic nuclei. Receives input from the basal ganglia and cerebellum and projects to the primary motor cortex. Responsible for modulating and coordinating movement.

GI1BVR0.title: Scottie dog with a collar sign
GI1BVR0.description: A radiologic sign specific for spondylolysis. The normal appearance of the lumbar spine in an oblique projection at 45° is referred to as the Scottie dog sign. In patients with spondylolysis, the fracture line has the additional appearance of a dog's collar.

FI1geR0.title: Ventral posterior thalamic nucleus
FI1geR0.description: A somatosensory thalamic nucleus that is part of the ventral subgroup of the lateral thalamic nuclei. Can be subdivided into the ventral posterolateral thalamic nucleus and the ventral posteromedial thalamic nucleus.

8I1OeR0.title: Ventral posterolateral thalamic nucleus
8I1OeR0.description:
A subdivision of the ventral posterior thalamic nucleus. Receives somatosensory input from the spinothalamic tract
and the medial lemniscus. Projects to the somatosensory cortex. Involved in proprioception and the perception of vibration, pain, pressure, touch, and temperature.

uI1peR0.title: Hemoglobinemia
uI1peR0.description: The presence of free hemoglobin in the plasma. Occurs as a result of severe intravascular hemolysis if haptoglobin and hemopexin, the hemoglobin-binding proteins, become saturated.

EI18eR0.title: Ventral posteromedial thalamic nucleus
EI18eR0.description: A subdivision of the ventral posterior thalamic nucleus. Receives somatosensory input from the trigeminal and gustatory pathways. Projects to the somatosensory cortex. Responsible for the perception of taste and facial sensation.

DI11UR0.title: Posterior thalamo-subthalamic paramedian arteries
DI11UR0.description: A group of arteries that arise from the P1 segment of the posterior cerebral artery. Supply ventral, intralaminar, and medial nuclear groups of the thalamus. Infarction is associated with impaired learning, memory loss, visual disturbance, and confabulation.

wI1hUR0.title: Thalamogeniculate arteries
wI1hUR0.description: The branches of the posterior cerebral artery that supply the ventral nuclear group of the thalamus and medial geniculate thalamic nucleus. Infarction is associated with impairment of movement, contralateral hemisensory loss, and thalamic pain syndrome.

9I1NUR0.title: Posterior choroidal arteries
9I1NUR0.description: A group of arteries arising from the P2 segment of the posterior cerebral artery. Supply the intralaminar nuclei, the pulvinar, and the medial and lateral geniculate nuclei. Infarction is associated with contralateral hemisensory loss and thalamic pain syndrome.

CI1qUR0.title: Anterior thalamosubthalamic paramedian arteries
CI1qUR0.description: A group of arteries that arise from the posterior communicating artery and supply the anterior, ventral, and intralaminar nuclear groups of the thalamus. Infarction of these arteries is associated with facial asymmetry, memory loss, hemiparesis, apraxia, and hemispatial neglect.

BI1zUR0.title: Synkinetic ptosis
BI1zUR0.description: A type of congenital ptosis caused by a defective connection between the motor fibers of the oculomotor and trigeminal nerves. Clinical features include permanent ptosis and transient eyelid retraction with laughter or mastication.

yI1d2R0.title: Concussion
yI1d2R0.description: A term used to describe a heterogeneous subset of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) with complex underlying pathophysiology, variable clinical features and recovery time, and without an alternate explanation (e.g., intoxication, comorbidity, other injuries) or abnormalities on standard neuroimaging. Sometimes used interchangeably with mTBI, however, mTBI is the preferred term as its definition is more precise.

media.title: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) fact sheet

_I152R0.title: Trichiasis
_I152R0.description: An abnormal inward growth of eyelashes toward the eye. Can cause conjunctival hyperemia, epiphora, and photophobia. Common complications include corneal abrasions and ulcers due to irritation.

zI1r2R0.title: Blepharophimosis syndrome
zI1r2R0.description: A rare autosomal dominant condition characterized by congenital blepharophimosis, ptosis, epicanthus inversus, and telecanthus.

ar1QfR0.title: Homologous recombination repair
ar1QfR0.description: A mechanism of double-stranded DNA repair in which damaged strands are repaired using complementary strands from intact homologous DNA as a template. No DNA is lost in this type of repair. Defective in breast and ovarian cancers with BRCA1 mutation and in Fanconi anemia.

destinations.label: DNA replication and repair → DNA repair mechanisms

Yr1nfR0.title: Dorsomedial hypothalamic nucleus
Yr1nfR0.description: A hypothalamic nucleus within the tuberal nuclear group. Involved in the regulation of appetite and thirst, circadian activity and the cardiovascular response to stress. Damage to this area can result in hypophagia and hypodipsia.

br1HfR0.title: Myokymia
br1HfR0.description: A rapid, spontaneous, constant, fascicular contraction of the orbicularis oculi muscle that does not lead to eyelid closure. Usually unilateral and involves either the lower or upper eyelid.

Xr19fR0.title: Exophthalmometry
Xr19fR0.description: An ophthalmologic exam that uses an ophthalmometer, which measures the position of the eye within the orbit. Typically used as a diagnostic tool for conditions such as proptosis and exophthalmos.

Wr1PTR0.title: ATLS
Wr1PTR0.description: A framework developed by the American College of Surgeons (ACS) for the structured management of trauma patients. Consists of the primary survey (i.e., ABCDE approach), secondary survey (e.g., head-to-toe injury assessment, complete history, additional diagnostics), and tertiary survey (e.g., delayed re-examination for missed injuries).

Vr1GTR0.title: Maintenance therapy
Vr1GTR0.description: A type of therapy that is provided indefinitely in order to maintain disease remission and/or prevent disease progression. Used as a part of the management of certain chronic diseases, including certain infections, malignancies, and psychiatric conditions. Typically initiated in concurrence with or after the treatment of the acute disease flare.

er1xTR0.title: Lung volume reduction surgery
er1xTR0.description: A surgical procedure in which parts of the lung are resected to mitigate the effects of pulmonary hyperinflation (e.g., respiratory muscle fatigue, airway obstruction). Performed in patients with severe emphysema who primarily have upper lobe involvement and low exercise capacity even after pulmonary rehabilitation.

gr1FgR0.title: Habenula
gr1FgR0.description: A stalk-like component of the epithalamus that connects the pineal gland to the thalamus. Consists of the habenular nuclei and is involved in nociception, mood, the sleep-wake cycle, and reproductive behavior. Alterations to this area are associated with mood disorders.

Sr1ygR0.title: Habenular commissure
Sr1ygR0.description: A fiber bundle that connects the habenular nuclei of both sides. Calcification is common.

hr1cSR0.title: Hirano body
hr1cSR0.description: An intracellular, rod-shaped, eosinophilic aggregate of actin and actin-associated proteins. Can be found on histopathologic examination of neurons in association with neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer disease and Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease.

Rr1lSR0.title: Adrenal hemorrhage
Rr1lSR0.description: A condition characterized by bleeding into one or both adrenal glands potentially causing acute adrenal insufficiency and crisis. Can be traumatic (e.g., due to blunt or penetrating trauma) or nontraumatic (e.g., due to meningococcemia, HIT, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, or anticoagulation).

jr1_SR0.title: Venous limb gangrene
jr1_SR0.description: The development of ischemic necrosis of a distal extremity despite palpable or doppler pulses, occurring as a complication of deep vein thrombosis. Often associated with the use of warfarin in patients with acquired hypercoagulability (e.g., in malignancy, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, antiphospholipid syndrome).

4r13hR0.title: Peliosis hepatis
4r13hR0.description: A rare vascular condition characterized by multiple blood-filled cysts and vascular sinuses in the liver. Caused by infection, neoplasms, toxins, or certain medications (e.g., anabolic steroids). May be asymptomatic or manifest with abdominal pain, fever, weight loss, jaundice, and hepatomegaly. In rare cases, cysts may rupture, causing intraperitoneal hemorrhage. Known as bacillary peliosis when caused by Bartonella spp. infection, which predominantly affects immunocompromised individuals.

Or1IhR0.title: Pulseless ventricular tachycardia
Or1IhR0.description: A form of ventricular tachycardia where there is insufficient cardiac output to generate a palpable pulse. Typically results from a combination of insufficient filling time during diastole combined with ineffective ventricular contractions.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Advanced cardiac life support (ACLS)

Nr1-hR0.title: Cerebral fornix
Nr1-hR0.description: A C-shaped bundle of nerve fibers that forms the major output tract of the hippocampus. Part of the limbic system and the Papez circuit.

mr1V3R0.title: Cingulum
mr1V3R0.description: A white matter tract of the brain that connects the cingulate gyrus to the entorhinal cortex. Part of the limbic system and the Papez circuit.

5r1i3R0.title: TPO
5r1i3R0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Thrombopoietin
2) Thyroid peroxidase

Mr1M3R0.title: Mixed nystagmus
Mr1M3R0.description: A pattern of different types of jerk nystagmus. Most commonly it has a peripheral cause and is caused by a unilateral lesion in the vestibular organ. A mixed horizontal-torsional nystagmus is most commonly caused by unilateral damage of the semicircular canals (e.g., vestibular neuritis, labyrinthitis). A mixed vertical-torsional nystagmus is most commonly caused by hyperfunction of the otolith organs (e.g., benign paroxysmal positional vertigo). In both cases a left-right imbalance emerges. The nystagmus always directs to the more activated side.

nr173R0.title: Hs and Ts
nr173R0.description:
A mnemonic used to help remember the reversible causes of cardiac arrest, which are divided into two groups: 
- Hs: hypoxia, hypovolemia, hydrogen ions (acidosis), hypo/hyperkalemia, hypothermia
- Ts: toxins, thrombosis (coronary and pulmonary), tamponade, tension pneumothorax

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Reversible causes of cardiac arrest

or10RR0.title: Arachnoid cyst
or10RR0.description: A common, benign, and usually asymptomatic cystic lesion of the arachnoid membrane. Contains cerebrospinal fluid.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Ventricular system

Kr1URR0.title: PH
Kr1URR0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Potential hydrogen (pH scale for acidity and alkalinity)
2. Pulmonary hypertension
3. Portal hypertension

6r1jRR0.title: WHO group 3 pulmonary hypertension
6r1jRR0.description: A subtype of pulmonary hypertension (PH) defined as PH caused by the effects of chronic hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction and subsequent vascular remodeling. Specific etiologies include chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, interstitial lung disease, and obstructive sleep apnea.

destinations.label: Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale → Etiology

Jr1sRR0.title: Perimortem cesarean delivery
Jr1sRR0.description: A cesarean delivery performed in cardiac arrest, with the aim of optimizing the survival chances of both the fetus and the mother (e.g., by relieving maternal aortocaval compression).

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Special patient groups

Ir1YiR0.title: Apple jelly nodules
Ir1YiR0.description: Yellowish-orange nodules seen on diascopy in lupus vulgaris and cutaneous sarcoidosis.

rr1fiR0.title: Heparin-containing products
rr1fiR0.description: A collection of medications and medical devices that contain heparin or heparin derivatives. These include unfractionated heparin and low molecular weight heparins, but also other products that may contain smaller amounts of heparin such as flushes (for intravenous lines and locks), heparin-bonded catheters, parenteral nutrition preparations, and prothrombin complex concentrates.

7r14iR0.title: Nonheparin anticoagulant
7r14iR0.description: A number of anticoagulant medications that may be considered for use in patients in whom heparin-containing products are contraindicated (e.g., due to heparin-induced thrombocytopenia) or not tolerated (e.g., due to allergy). These include oral anticoagulants (e.g., DOACs, VKAs) and nonheparin parenteral anticoagulants (e.g., argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux).

Hr1KiR0.title: 4Ts score
Hr1KiR0.description: A score used to estimate the pretest probability of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia based on the degree and timing of the thrombocytopenia, the likelihood of an alternative diagnosis, and the presence of thrombosis or other complications. A low score can rule the condition out. However, treatment should be initiated immediately in patients with an intermediate or high-risk score, without waiting for further confirmatory tests.

sr1tiR0.title: HITT
sr1tiR0.description: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) complicated by thrombosis and/or thromboembolism. Venous and/or arterial thrombosis occurs in up to half of patients with HIT.

Gr1BiR0.title: Floppy eyelid syndrome
Gr1BiR0.description: A bilateral eyelid malposition disorder characterized by eyelid laxity, eye pruritus, keratopathy, ptosis, and chronic noninfectious papillary conjunctivitis. Commonly associated with obesity, sleep apnea, and keratoconus.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Upper eyelid eversion

tr1XQR0.title: Adrenal vein thrombosis
tr1XQR0.description: The thrombotic obstruction of a main adrenal vein and/or related structures (e.g., capsular veins). Often complicated by adrenal hemorrhage and insufficiency. Rarely occurs but has been observed in severe infection (e.g., pneumonia) and acquired hypercoagulability (e.g., due to malignancy, DIC, HIT).

8r1OQR0.title: Lewy neurite
8r1OQR0.description: An abnormal neurite that contains filamentous inclusions similar to those found in Lewy bodies.

ur1pQR0.title: Droxidopa
ur1pQR0.description: A synthetic amino acid that is converted to norepinephrine by dopadecarboxylase. Used to treat neurogenic orthostatic hypotension and parkinsonism.

Er18QR0.title: Labyrinthine artery
Er18QR0.description: An artery of variable origin that most often arises from the anterior inferior cerebellar artery. Travels with the vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII) and supplies the inner ear.

vr1AQR0.title: Pontine arteries
vr1AQR0.description: Paired arterial branches of the basilar artery that supply the pons. Of variable quantity (3–5).

wr1hjR0.title: Bundled payment
wr1hjR0.description: A health care payment model in which a health care organization is compensated a fixed amount for all services provided for a clinically-defined episode of care. The compensation is then distributed among all health care providers involved in the care of the patient for that specific episode.

destinations.label: Health care system → Alternative payment models

9r1NjR0.title: Jerk nystagmus
9r1NjR0.description: A type of nystagmus that results in a periodic rhythmic ocular oscillation of the eyes characterized by a slow movement toward a defined direction followed by a fast, corrective movement backward. The name of the nystagmus is determined by the direction of movement in the fast phase (i.e., left-beating, right-beating, downbeat, upbeat).

Cr1qjR0.title: Peripheral nystagmus
Cr1qjR0.description: A jerk nystagmus with its origin in the labyrinth (i.e., semicircular canals and otolith organs). Caused by an abnormal vestibular tone between vestibular nerves and the labyrinth. Can be either physiological (e.g., optokinetic nystagmus) or pathological (e.g., vestibular neuritis). Typically shows a mixed nystagmus pattern with horizontal and torsional movement.

Ar1RPR0.title: Central nystagmus
Ar1RPR0.description: Nystagmus that has its origin in the central system. Can be physiologic or pathological; motion can be jerk or pendular. Pathological lesions are typically located in the brain stem or the cerebellum (e.g., stroke). Can also derive from metabolic disease (e.g., Wernicke encephalopathy) and intoxications (e.g., Phenytoin).

zr1rPR0.title: Trisomy rescue
zr1rPR0.description: A chromosomal aberration in which a cell initially contains three copies of a chromosome from nondisjunction, then loses one of those chromosomes. If both of the remaining chromosomes are from the same parent, this results in uniparental disomy.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Types of mutations

071e4R0.title: Left ventricular thrombus
071e4R0.description: A blood clot in the left ventricle. Usually occurs as a complication of anterior myocardial infarction or dilated cardiomyopathy. May cause systemic thromboembolic phenomena (e.g., thromboembolic stroke, acute mesenteric ischemia).

a71Q4R0.title: Wearable cardioverter-defibrillator
a71Q4R0.description: An external device that is worn under clothing and provides continuous arrhythmia monitoring and automatic defibrillation for potentially fatal ventricular tachyarrhythmia. May be used as a bridge until an implantable cardiac defibrillator (ICD) is placed or can be used long-term in patients not eligible for an ICD.

Y71n4R0.title: Long-acting reversible contraceptives
Y71n4R0.description: A device that provides reversible, long-term contraception for 3-12 years. Includes intrauterine devices and progestin implants.

W71PkR0.title: Spontaneous nystagmus
W71PkR0.description: A pathological nystagmus that arises without external provocation. Can derive from central lesions (e.g., stroke, medication intoxication, metabolic disease) or peripheral lesions (e.g., vestibular neuritis, migraine, benign paroxysmal positional vertigo).

d71okR0.title: Clinical features of traumatic brain injury
d71okR0.description: The clinical manifestations of intracranial trauma. Features include loss of consciousness, headache, amnesia, focal neurological deficits, and signs of increased intracranial pressure (e.g., Cushing triad, cerebral herniation syndromes).

e71xkR0.title: Monosodium urate monohydrate crystals
e71xkR0.description: A crystallized form of uric acid that can develop in individuals with hyperuricemia. In gout, these crystals deposit in joints and soft tissues and cause inflammation, known as crystal-induced arthritis or arthropathy. Monosodium urate crystals on synovial fluid analysis are diagnostic of gout. Visible uric acid crystals in newborn diapers may indicate inadequate fluid intake.

U71bOR0.title: Pituitary incidentaloma
U71bOR0.description: A pituitary tumor that is discovered incidentally when imaging the area for an unrelated reason.

271TOR0.title: Incidentaloma
271TOR0.description: A lesion or tumor detected on an imaging study that was ordered for an unrelated reason.

g71FOR0.title: Non-AIDS-defining cancer
g71FOR0.description: A group of cancers that are more likely to occur in individuals with an HIV infection. These cancers include Hodgkin lymphoma, lung cancer, and infection-related cancers such as anal cancer, oropharyngeal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Does not include Kaposi sarcoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, or invasive cervical cancer, which are considered AIDS-defining cancers.

S71yOR0.title: Photoprotective measures
S71yOR0.description: A set of measures to prevent and/or minimize skin damage from ultraviolet solar radiation. Includes regular use of sunscreen with a minimum SPF of 15-30, avoiding the sun (remaining indoors or in the shade), and wearing protective clothing (e.g., long sleeves, wide-brimmed hats, clothing with SPF ratings, and sunglasses that filter UV light).

h71clR0.title: Risdiplam
h71clR0.description: An mRNA splicing modulator used to treat spinal muscular atrophy. Improves the efficiency of SMN2 gene transcription, which leads to increased systemic SMN protein production.

i71JlR0.title: Goldman risk index
i71JlR0.description: A tool used to assess the risk of cardiac complications prior to noncardiac surgery. Contains 9 independent risk factors, including age > 70 years, jugular venous distention or preoperative third heart sound, arrhythmia other than sinus or premature atrial contractions, and myocardial infarction within the last 6 months. Largely replaced by the revised cardiac risk index.

P71WNR0.title: Medical negligence
P71WNR0.description: The failure to perform an action with the skill, care, and knowledge expected of a health care provider under reasonable circumstances.

k71mNR0.title: Isolated HIT
k71mNR0.description: Acute heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) in the absence of thrombosis.

m71VmR0.title: Gaze-evoked nystagmus
m71VmR0.description: A pathological horizontal jerk nystagmus caused by maintenance of eccentric eye position. In contrast, end-gaze nystagmus is caused by maintenance of extreme eye position.

M71MmR0.title: Caloric nystagmus
M71MmR0.description: A type of horizontal jerk nystagmus caused by infusing cold or warm water into the external ear canal. This is called "Caloric testing" and is used to evaluate vestibular function. The temperature change in the endolymph creates an activity gradient between the vestibular systems. The nystagmus directs towards the more activated vestibular organ. With ice-cold water, brainsteam death can be tested in comatose patients.

n717mR0.title: TSH suppression therapy
n717mR0.description: Administration of L-thyroxine at a dose sufficient to suppress serum TSH to subnormal levels with the aim to minimize the risk of thyroid cancer recurrence or growth. Part of the adjuvant treatment of well-differentiated thyroid cancer after surgery and radioactive iodine ablation.

L71wmR0.title: Cardiac Myosin Binding Protein C
L71wmR0.description: An accessory protein in striated muscle cells, found in the A bands of sarcomeres. Mutations in this gene are associated with familial autosomal dominant hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy.

o7105R0.title: AIDS-defining cancers
o7105R0.description: A group of cancers that confirm a diagnosis of AIDS when diagnosed in a patient with HIV infection. Includes Kaposi sarcoma, invasive cervical cancer, and primary CNS lymphoma.

K71U5R0.title: Systemic fungal infection
K71U5R0.description: A fungal infection involving internal organs, most commonly the lungs. Systemic fungal infections may be caused by opportunistic organisms in immunocompromised individuals or endemic infections in both immunocompetent and immunocompromised individuals.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Systemic fungal infections

p71L5R0.title: Risk factors for hemorrhagic stroke
p71L5R0.description:
A group of patient factors that increase the likelihood of hemorrhagic stroke. The most common, modifiable risk factors include arterial hypertension, high alcohol intake, and smoking.
Nonmodifiable risk factors include male sex, advanced age, and neurovascular abnormalities, e.g. arteriovenous malformations, aneurysms, and cerebral amyloid angiopathy.

r71fMR0.title: Herd immunity
r71fMR0.description: A type of indirect protection from an infectious disease that occurs when a sufficient amount of the population becomes immune to the disease, which results in protection of nonimmune individuals due to low incidence. Thresholds for herd immunity depend on the infectiousness of the pathogen (e.g., 75% immunity for mumps, 95% for measles).

s71tMR0.title: Galactomannan enzyme immunoassay
s71tMR0.description: A test that identifies a carbohydrate found in the cell wall of Aspergillus spp. A positive result identifies the presence of Aspergillus spp. in the test sample and supports a clinical diagnosis of aspergillosis, but a definitive diagnosis requires histopathologic evidence of invasion or a positive culture.

t71XnR0.title: Overlap myopathy
t71XnR0.description: Any inflammatory myopathy that occurs in association with features of another autoimmune connective tissue disease (e.g., lupus or rheumatoid arthritis).

871OnR0.title: Juvenile idiopathic inflammatory myopathy
871OnR0.description: An inflammatory myopathy (e.g., dermatomyositis, polymyositis, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy) manifesting in an individual under 18 years of age. Characteristic findings are generally similar to those in the adult forms of each myopathy (including classic proximal skeletal muscle weakness), but there are some differences, such as the type of autoantibodies present.

u71pnR0.title: Poikiloderma
u71pnR0.description: Skin changes characterized by a combination of hyperpigmented or hypopigmented macules, telangiectasia, and epidermal atrophy. May be congenital or acquired and can be seen in various disorders, including mycosis fungoides and connective tissue disorders such as dermatomyositis.

D711LR0.title: Iron-rich foods
D711LR0.description: Includes red meat, legumes, dark green leafy vegetables, and iron-fortified foods (including fortified formula for infants).

w71hLR0.title: Ganzoni formula
w71hLR0.description:
A formula used to calculate the total iron deficit in patients with iron deficiency anemia.

Total iron deficit in mg = subject weight in kg x (target hemoglobin in g/dL - current hemoglobin in g/dL) x 2.4 + iron stores in mg (A value of 500 mg is used for iron stores for adults and children weighing > 35 kg and 15 mg/kg for children under 35 kg.)

C71qLR0.title: Muscle dysmorphia
C71qLR0.description: A form of body dysmorphic disorder characterized by a preoccupation with one's body not being muscular, large, or lean enough. Affected individuals typically have an average or muscular physical appearance. Occurs almost exclusively in men.

B71zLR0.title: CT colonography
B71zLR0.description: A computed tomography of the abdomen with oral contrast and rectal insufflation of air, allowing for noninvasive visualization of the colon, e.g., for detection of mucosal irregularities such as polyps and colorectal cancer. Bowel preparation with a laxative is generally necessary, and IV contrast may be used.

y71doR0.title: Enteral stenting
y71doR0.description: An endoscopic technique in which a stent is placed to restore and preserve passage through a segment of the gastrointestinal tract. Commonly used for obstructive processes (e.g., malignancies or strictures) of the esophagus, duodenum, or colon.

z71roR0.title: Ki-67 index
z71roR0.description: The fraction of cells positive for the Ki-67 antigen. Ki-67 is only expressed in cells actively undergoing proliferation and is therefore used as a marker of cellular proliferation and as a surrogate for clinical course in certain cancers (e.g., breast and prostate cancer, neuroendocrine tumors).

ZH1ZKR0.title: Adjuvant chemotherapy
ZH1ZKR0.description: Chemotherapy that follows the primary treatment of malignant tumors (most often surgery) with the goal of destroying any remaining malignant cells and preventing recurrence.

aH1QKR0.title: Clinical features of thrombocytopenia
aH1QKR0.description: A collection of symptoms and signs seen in patients with a low platelet count. Common symptoms include easy bruising, prolonged bleeding after a minor injury, and mucosal bleeding (e.g., bleeding gums).  Common signs include petechiae and purpura. Rarely, patients may present with spontaneous life-threatening bleeding (e.g., hemorrhagic stroke).

XH19KR0.title: Cardiopulmonary bypass
XH19KR0.description: An extracorporeal circulation method used to replace the heart and lungs by pumping venous blood through an artificial gas-exchange membrane and returning it to the arterial circulation. Most commonly used during cardiac surgery, as it allows the heart to be stopped in order to provide a bloodless and stable surgical field.

1H126R0.title: Acute encephalopathy
1H126R0.description: A diffuse pathological process in the brain with no associated structural lesion that develops acutely (< 4 weeks), and can manifest as coma, stupor, or delirium. Acute encephalopathy commonly results from a metabolic or toxic insult.

WH1P6R0.title: Seizure precautions
WH1P6R0.description: A set of measures used to decrease a patient's risk of recurring seizures (e.g., avoiding sleep deprivation, alcohol, certain medications) and to protect against potential adverse events such as injury secondary to seizure activity (e.g., avoiding unsupervised activities, showering rather than bathing, complying with driving restrictions). In-hospital precautions include padded side rails, positioning the bed at the lowest level, and having oral suction and oxygen available at the bedside and a call light within reach.

dH1o6R0.title: Fecal immunochemical test
dH1o6R0.description: A test that uses hemoglobin antibodies to detect occult blood in a stool sample. As a screening tool for colorectal cancer, it has a higher sensitivity than classic guaiac-based occult blood tests. Positive tests are followed up with colonoscopy.

UH1bpR0.title: Push enteroscopy
UH1bpR0.description: An endoscopic technique that allows for visualization of the jejunum (~50-100 cm beyond the angle of Treitz), performed periorally using a dedicated enteroscope (or a pediatric colonoscope) with an overtube mechanism.

2H1TpR0.title: Internal hordeolum
2H1TpR0.description: A warm, erythematous, tender swelling of the posterior eyelid (palpebral conjunctiva) caused by acute suppurative inflammation of the meibomian glands (tarsal sebaceous glands with orifices at the conjunctival rim).

fH1kpR0.title: Anti-nuclear matrix protein-2 antibody
fH1kpR0.description: A myositis-specific autoantibody with activity against nuclear matrix protein-2. Associated with a phenotype of dermatomyositis that confers an increased risk of cancer.

TH16pR0.title: Anti–transcriptional intermediary factor 1-γ antibody
TH16pR0.description: A myositis-specific autoantibody with activity against the transcriptional intermediary factor 1-γ. Associated with a phenotype of dermatomyositis characterized by more mild muscle involvement and an increased risk of cancer.

SH1ypR0.title: Calcitonin gene-related peptide
SH1ypR0.description: A peptide neurotransmitter and signaling molecule that is a potent vasodilator. Transmits nociception, acts as an appetite suppressant, and enhances gastric acid secretion. Its chronotropic function within the cardiovascular system increases the heart rate.

hH1cJR0.title: Anti-small ubiquitin-like modifier-1 activating enzyme antibody
hH1cJR0.description: A myositis-specific autoantibody with activity against the small ubiquitin-like modifier activating enzyme. Can be associated with dermatomyositis.

3H1SJR0.title: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 antibody
3H1SJR0.description: A myositis-specific autoantibody with activity against melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5. Associated with a phenotype of dermatomyositis characterized by minimal muscle involvement, significant skin involvement, and possibly rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease.

RH1lJR0.title: Anti-threonyl-tRNA synthetase antibody
RH1lJR0.description: A myositis-specific autoantibody with activity against threonyl-tRNA synthetase. Associated with a phenotype of antisynthetase syndrome characterized by more severe interstitial lung disease.

iH1JJR0.title: Anti-alanyl-tRNA synthetase antibody
iH1JJR0.description: A myositis-specific autoantibody with activity against alanyl-tRNA synthetase. Associated with a phenotype of antisynthetase syndrome characterized by more severe interstitial lung disease and less severe muscle involvement.

QH1uJR0.title: Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase antibody
QH1uJR0.description: A myositis-specific autoantibody with activity against the 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase enzyme. Associated with a phenotype of immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy that most commonly occurs following statin use.

PH1WqR0.title: Acute invasive fungal rhinosinusitis
PH1WqR0.description: An inflammation of the paranasal sinuses and adjacent nasal cavity caused by a fungal pathogen that occurs primarily in immunocompromised patients. Possible signs include nasal eschar, bony erosion, vascular invasion (e.g., of the carotid arteries, cavernous sinus), and spread to intracerebral regions. Aspergillus and Mucor are the most commonly identified pathogens. Symptoms typically progress within hours to days. The mortality rate is high.

4H13qR0.title: Cortical spreading depression
4H13qR0.description: An electrophysiologic phenomenon characterized by a wave of depolarization in the cerebral cortex in which the excitation of cortical neurons is followed by the suppression of spontaneous neuronal activity. During cortical spreading depression, proinflammatory molecules are upregulated, which may activate meningeal nociceptors. Associated with ischemic cerebral events and migraine aura.

OH1IqR0.title: Neurogenic inflammation
OH1IqR0.description: A pathologic process in which peripheral nociceptor neurons release potent, vasoactive, proinflammatory neuropeptides (e.g., substance P, calcitonin gene-related peptide, or neurokinin A) that lead to a cascade of events, including plasma protein extravasation, vasodilation, and degranulation of mast cells, which results in inflammation of the target tissue.

lH1vqR0.title: Controlled ileal release budesonide
lH1vqR0.description: A formulation of the synthetic steroid budesonide that is released in environments with a pH ≥5.5. This facilitates drug delivery distal to the proximal small bowel. Used to treat Crohn disease that involves sites of inflammation in the ileum and/or ascending colon.

LH1wIR0.title: Nonexertional heatstroke
LH1wIR0.description: A severe heat-related illness typically caused by passive exposure to high ambient temperatures and characterized by significantly elevated core body temperature (typically defined as > 40°C) and significant CNS dysfunction, e.g., altered mental status.

oH10rR0.title: Exertional heatstroke
oH10rR0.description: A type of heatstroke that is primarily caused by strenuous physical activity. High ambient temperatures are often a contributing factor. Characterized by hyperthermia > 40°C and central nervous system dysfunction (e.g., altered mental status). Most commonly affects young, otherwise healthy individuals.

pH1LrR0.title: Acute aortic occlusion
pH1LrR0.description: A severe, life-threatening vascular event, most commonly caused by aortic thrombosis or embolism. Symptoms vary depending on the location of the occlusion and may include findings of lower limb, mesenteric, and/or renal ischemia.

qH1CrR0.title: Accessory muscles of respiration
qH1CrR0.description: A group of muscles that are recruited when the respiratory demand is increased, either physiologically (e.g., exercise) or in disease (e.g., asthma, COPD). The main accessory inspiratory muscles are the sternocleidomastoid, scalenes, intercostals, pectoralis major, and trapezius. The main accessory expiratory muscles are the rectus abdominis, the obliques, and the transversus abdominis.

IH1Y7R0.title: Contaminated wound
IH1Y7R0.description: A wound that contains foreign and/or potentially contaminated material. Foreign materials include solid bodies (e.g., bullets, retained suture). Potentially contaminated materials include saliva (including human/animal bites), urine, feces, and other bodily fluids.

rH1f7R0.title: Globus pallidus internus
rH1f7R0.description: The medial segment of the pallidum. Inhibits the thalamus via GABA release, thereby decreasing motor activity.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

7H147R0.title: Globus pallidus externus
7H147R0.description: The lateral segment of the pallidum. Inhibits the subthalamic nucleus, thereby causing motor activity to increase.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Basal ganglia

HH1K7R0.title: PHACE syndrome
HH1K7R0.description: A rare syndrome of unknown etiology characterized by: Posterior fossa anomalies, Hemangiomas, Arterial anomalies, Cardiac anomalies, and Eye anomalies.

tH1XHR0.title: Monostotic
tH1XHR0.description: A descriptor for involvement of a single bone.

FH1gHR0.title: Polyostotic
FH1gHR0.description: A descriptor for involvement of more than one bone.

8H1OHR0.title: Mazabraud syndrome
8H1OHR0.description: A rare syndrome characterized by polyostotic fibrous dysplasia and multiple Intramuscular myxomas. Associated with mutations of the GNAS1 gene.

uH1pHR0.title: Irritable myopathic process
uH1pHR0.description: A set of findings on electromyography (EMG) that are characteristic of myopathy and can help distinguish between myopathic and neuropathic processes. These include myopathic motor unit action potentials (polyphasic and of short duration and low amplitude), an increase in spontaneous activity (e.g., fibrillations, positive sharp waves), and early recruitment.

DH11sR0.title: Signs of respiratory distress
DH11sR0.description: Signs include tachypnea, use of accessory muscles of respiration, nasal flaring, grunting, cyanosis, and an inability to lie flat. Caused by increased work of breathing to meet oxygen demands.

destinations.label: Respiratory failure and arrest → Clinical features

wH1hsR0.title: Rat-bite fever
wH1hsR0.description: A systemic illness caused by Streptobacillus moniliformis and transmitted by infected rats or mice. Manifestations include fever, rigors, and polyarthralgia. Can cause severe organ damage (e.g., hepatosplenomegaly, interstitial pneumonia, endocarditis).

9H1NsR0.title: Respiratory failure
9H1NsR0.description: A condition that develops either acutely or chronically when the respiratory system is unable to adequately oxygenate the body (defined as a PaO₂ of < 60 mmHg/8 kPa) and/or eliminate carbon dioxide (defined as a PaCO₂ of > 50 mmHg/6.5 kPa). Can occur in respiratory tract disorders or conditions that alter the biomechanics or regulation of respiration (e.g., myopathies, loss of central respiratory drive).

CH1qsR0.title: Signs of complete airway obstruction
CH1qsR0.description: Signs include sudden inability to speak or cry out, absent breath sounds, use of accessory muscles of respiration, and paroxysmal chest and abdominal movements. Cyanosis and loss of consciousness may occur secondary to profound hypoxia.

xH1EsR0.title: Clinical features of partial airway obstruction
xH1EsR0.description: Symptoms depend on the location of the obstruction and may include coughing, hoarseness, and/or dyspnea. Examination findings may include dysphonia, stridor, monophonic wheeze, and/or hyperresonance.

BH1zsR0.title: Clinical features of chronic foreign body airway obstruction
BH1zsR0.description: In addition to the clinical features seen in partial airway obstruction (e.g., wheeze, dyspnea, and cough), signs of superadded infection may be seen, such as fever and purulent sputum.

yH1dGR0.title: Allocortex
yH1dGR0.description: A three-layered part of the cerebral cortex that consists of the hippocampus and the olfactory cortex.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Microscopic anatomy

AH1RGR0.title: Stellate cells (brain)
AH1RGR0.description: A star-shaped interneuron of the cerebral cortex. Their axons do not leave the cerebral cortex.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Microscopic anatomy

_H15GR0.title: Flexible bronchoscopy
_H15GR0.description: The use of a thin, narrow, flexible bronchoscope to examine the upper and lower airways. Used in the diagnosis of lung conditions such as infections and tumors. By passing tools along the bronchoscope, it can also be used to treat foreign body aspiration, remove masses, and manage airway stenosis.

zH1rGR0.title: Muddy brown casts
zH1rGR0.description: A type of granular cast that can be seen on urinalysis of patients with acute tubular necrosis. Formed by spilled cellular contents of infarcted tubular epithelial cells.

destinations.label: Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract → Urinalysis

media.title: Urine casts in acute tubular necrosis

-H1DGR0.title: Rigid bronchoscopy
-H1DGR0.description: The use of a large, hollow inflexible bronchoscope to examine the upper and lower airways. Can be used for diagnostic purposes, when large tissue samples are required, but is predominantly used for therapeutic purposes, such as removal of foreign bodies, airway stenting, and debulking masses.

Zs1ZtR0.title: E chart
Zs1ZtR0.description: An ophthalmological chart used to evaluate visual acuity. Typically displays several rows of the letter “E” in different sizes and rotations. The patient, from a predetermined distance from the chart (in the US typically 20 feet or 6 meters), covers one eye and consecutively reads the rows of letters out loud beginning with the smallest row they can read. The patient is asked to point or state in which direction the "legs" of the E are pointing: up, down, left or right.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Visual acuity

0s1etR0.title: Suspected upper airway foreign body
0s1etR0.description: Suspect an upper airway foreign body if there is a history of potential aspiration in combination with stridor, hoarse voice or cry, or drooling.

as1QtR0.title: Suspected lower airway foreign body
as1QtR0.description: A history of potential aspiration in combination with cough, monophonic wheeze, and/or unilateral or focally reduced breath sounds should raise suspicion of lower airway foreign body aspiration.

bs1HtR0.title: Pyramids (brainstem)
bs1HtR0.description: Paired white matter structures that contain the motor fibers of the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts. Form the base of the medulla and relay motor signals.

cs1aFR0.title: Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine
cs1aFR0.description: A messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) vaccine against COVID-19. Results in host expression of a full-length spike protein, which elicits an immune response.

1s12FR0.title: Moderna COVID-19 vaccine
1s12FR0.description: A messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) vaccine against COVID-19. Results in host expression of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, which elicits an immune response.

Ts168R0.title: Vedolizumab
Ts168R0.description: An immune-modulating monoclonal antibody that binds to the α4β7 integrin, blocking its interaction with mucosal addressin cell adhesion molecule-1 (MAdCAM-1), which results in inhibition of T-cell migration across the endothelium. Used to treat Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

Ss1y8R0.title: Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices
Ss1y8R0.description: A committee of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention that provides guidance on the use of vaccines.

is1JuR0.title: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy
is1JuR0.description: A nontraumatic death that occurs in a person with epilepsy with or without evidence of a seizure and no other underlying condition that could explain it. This diagnosis requires demonstrating the absence of alternative causes on autopsy.

Qs1uuR0.title: Hemispherotomy
Qs1uuR0.description: The surgical disconnection of the cortex of one hemisphere from the subcortical structures in the same hemisphere and from the other hemisphere without removal of the affected hemisphere. Used to treat individuals with pharmacoresistant epilepsy in which the epileptogenic focus is limited to one hemisphere.

js1_uR0.title: Spinal disc herniation
js1_uR0.description: A form of degenerative disk disease characterized by complete herniation of the nucleus pulposus through a tear in the annulus fibrosus.

Ps1WER0.title: Passive elastic recoil of the lungs
Ps1WER0.description: The passive process by which the lungs expel air. About ⅓ of the elastic recoil of the lungs is due to the elastic fibers of the lungs; ⅔ is due to the surface tension of the alveoli.

4s13ER0.title: Barrier contraception
4s13ER0.description: A type of contraceptive that prevents sperm from entering the uterus. Includes condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps, sponges, and spermacides.

ks1mER0.title: Harlequin sign
ks1mER0.description: A physical examination finding characterized by flushing and hyperhidrosis of one side of the face due to excessive ipsilateral sympathetic activation (e.g., in the setting of contralateral Horner syndrome).

Os1IER0.title: Cricopharyngeal myotomy
Os1IER0.description: A surgical procedure in which the cricopharyngeal muscle (the main component of the upper esophageal sphincter) is incised to relieve an esophageal obstruction. Used to treat oropharyngeal dysphagia due to primary cricopharyngeal dysfunction and symptomatic Zenker diverticulum.

ls1vER0.title: Anti-histidyl-tRNA synthetase antibody
ls1vER0.description: A myositis-specific autoantibody with activity against histidyl-tRNA synthetase. Associated with the classic phenotype of antisynthetase syndrome.

Ns1-ER0.title: Anti-Mi-2 antibodies
Ns1-ER0.description: A myositis-specific autoantibody with activity against the Mi2 nuclear helicase protein. Associated with the classic phenotype of dermatomyositis.

ms1VvR0.title: Trichloroacetic acid
ms1VvR0.description: A protein denaturant and keratolytic agent used to treat warts and as a component of chemical peels.

5s1ivR0.title: Podophyllin
5s1ivR0.description: A plant-derived antimitotic agent that results in localized tissue necrosis. Used as a topical treatment for warts.

Ms1MvR0.title: Hydrocolloid dressing
Ms1MvR0.description: An occlusive or semiocclusive dressing that combines gel-forming agents (e.g., carboxymethylcellulose) in an adhesive matrix. It swells to form a gel on contact with moisture or exudate, maintaining a moist wound environment, which supports autolytic debridement.

ns17vR0.title: Radioimmunotherapy
ns17vR0.description: A type of cancer therapy that combines radiation therapy and immune therapy. Engineered monoclonal antibodies that are specific for tumor antigens are bound to radioactive nucleotides, which results in higher doses of radiation reaching the target cancer cells and less off-target effects. Predominantly used to treat non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

os10DR0.title: TCA
os10DR0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Tricyclic antidepressant
2. Trichloroacetic acid

Js1sDR0.title: Anterior rhinoscopy
Js1sDR0.description: A technique in which an otoscope or a nasal speculum is used with an external light source to visualize the anterior to middle parts of the nasal cavity.

qs1CDR0.title: Thiopurines
qs1CDR0.description: A group of purine antimetabolites with immunosuppressive effects. Used to treat several conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, and systemic lupus erythematosus. Examples include azathioprine and mercaptopurine.

Hs1KwR0.title: Magill forceps
Hs1KwR0.description: A pair of angled forceps that is used to guide the placement or passage of endotracheal tubes, nasogastric tubes, or tracheal/esophageal suctions. Also used to retrieve a foreign body that is lodged in the upper airway under direct vision.

Gs1BwR0.title: Needle cricothyroidotomy
Gs1BwR0.description: An emergency airway procedure in which a large-bore intravenous cannula is placed through the cricothyroid membrane into the trachea to oxygenate the patient. Performed in "cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate" scenarios. Used as a temporizing measure until a definitive airway can be placed as it does not allow for effective exhalation.

ts1X9R0.title: Scalpel cricothyroidotomy
ts1X9R0.description: An emergency surgical airway procedure in which the cricothyroid membrane is incised and either an endotracheal tube or a tracheostomy tube placed into the trachea. Performed in "cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate" scenarios to provide a definitive airway through which the patient can be ventilated.

Fs1g9R0.title: Chest thrusts
Fs1g9R0.description: A basic first-aid maneuver designed to dislodge an upper airway foreign body in infants by increasing intrathoracic pressure. Place the child in a supine position, tilt the head back, and apply pressure swiftly and firmly to the lower third of the sternum (similar location as CPR). Repeat up to 5 times at the rate of 1 compression per second.

media.title: Back blows and chest thrusts in infants

Ds11CR0.title: Live birth
Ds11CR0.description: The birth of an infant with postnatal presence of vital signs (e.g., respiration, pulse, umbilical cord pulse).

ws1hCR0.title: Term pregnancy
ws1hCR0.description: A birth that occurs between 37 and 42 weeks of gestation. Subdivided into early term (37 to 38 6/7 weeks), full term (39 to 40 6/7 weeks), and late term (40 to 41 6/7 weeks) deliveries.

xs1ECR0.title: Lanreotide
xs1ECR0.description: A somatostatin analog used to treat acromegaly, carcinoid syndrome, and neuroendocrine tumors.

aG1QBR0.title: Two thumb-encircling hands technique
aG1QBR0.description: The recommended technique for chest compressions in neonates and infants if two health care providers are present. Both hands encircle the chest, with the fingers spread around the thorax. The thumbs are placed on top of each other over the lower third of the breastbone and compress the sternum. Results in more effective compressions and higher coronary artery perfusion than the two-finger technique.

YG1nBR0.title: Salt-and-pepper skull
YG1nBR0.description: A radiologic finding in which the calvarium appears mottled or speckled on imaging, resembling coarse grains of salt and pepper. Most commonly associated with hyperparathyroidism, especially secondary to chronic renal disease. Reflects abnormal bone turnover with patchy demineralization and resorption of trabecular bone. Indicates advanced metabolic bone involvement.

WG1PyR0.title: Serine protease inhibitor
WG1PyR0.description: A group of proteins that antagonize the activity of various serine proteases. Includes protease-nexin-1 (which inhibits thrombin), α2-antiplasmin (which inhibits plasmin), and α1-antitrypsin (which inhibits trypsin).

dG1oyR0.title: IPV
dG1oyR0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Intrapulmonary percussive ventilator
2. Intimate partner violence
3. Inactivated poliovirus vaccine

2G1TAR0.title: Mutualism
2G1TAR0.description: A relationship between a symbiont and its host that benefits both parties.

TG16AR0.title: Two-finger technique
TG16AR0.description: The recommended technique for chest compressions in neonates and infants if only one health care provider is present. The chest is compressed using two fingers placed on the lower half of the sternum, just below the intermammary line. Allows for faster alternations between compressions and delivering breaths for the single health care provider.

hG1c_R0.title: Tick neurotoxin
hG1c_R0.description: A neurotoxin that impairs motor nerve transmission, which results in muscle weakness and paralysis. Tick neurotoxin mechanisms are not fully understood. May involve inhibition of sodium flux across axonal membranes in Dermacentor species and inhibition of acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction in Ixodes species.

3G1S_R0.title: Extraperitoneal organ
3G1S_R0.description: An organ that lies outside the peritoneal cavity, with one aspect covered by the peritoneum.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Intraperitoneal and extraperitoneal abdominal structures

RG1l_R0.title: Subperitoneal organ
RG1l_R0.description: An extraperitoneal organ that lies below the peritoneal cavity.

destinations.label: Abdominal cavity → Intraperitoneal and extraperitoneal abdominal structures

QG1u_R0.title: Bowel program
QG1u_R0.description: A management strategy for constipation and fecal incontinence caused by neurogenic bowel dysfunction (e.g., secondary to a spinal cord injury or stroke). Involves regularly scheduled bowel evacuation with the help of suppositories, enemas, and/or manual stimulation.

jG1__R0.title: Alternating pressure mattress
jG1__R0.description: A type of mattress composed of several air-filled cells that are sequentially inflated and deflated automatically. Provides intermittent pressure relief across the body. Used in the prevention and management of decubitus ulcers.

PG1WzR0.title: Obligate parasite
PG1WzR0.description: A parasite that cannot survive outside its host. Examples include viruses, certain bacteria (e.g., Rickketsia and Chlamysia), protozoa (e.g., Plasmodium), and helminths (e.g, roundworms).

OG1IzR0.title: Metachronous
OG1IzR0.description: A process that occurs at different times. In oncology, metachronous cancers are typically defined as developing > 6 months after the first primary cancer develops.

nG17-R0.title: Facultative parasite
nG17-R0.description: A parasite that does not rely on a host for completion of its life cycle.

6G1jZi0.title: Anterior cecal artery
6G1jZi0.description: A branch of the ileocolic artery that, with the posterior cecal artery, supplies the cecum and terminal ileum.

pG1LZi0.title: Posterior cecal artery
pG1LZi0.description: A branch of the ileocolic artery that, with the anterior cecal artery, supplies the cecum and terminal ileum.

JG1sZi0.title: Type III metacarpal base fracture
JG1sZi0.description: An extraarticular fracture at the base of the first metacarpal bone. Usually a transverse fracture, or less commonly an oblique fracture.

7G140i0.title: HIV protease inhibitors
7G140i0.description: A class of antiretroviral drugs used to treat HIV infection. They inhibit viral protease, preventing maturation of new viruses. Examples include indinavir, ritonavir, nelfinavir, and lopinavir. Adverse effects include hyperglycemia, nephrolithiasis and crystal-induced nephropathy, and lipodystrophy.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

media.title: HIV replication and mechanism of action of antiretroviral drugs

HG1K0i0.title: Open wound
HG1K0i0.description: A wound in which the continuity of the overlying skin is broken, exposing the underlying tissue. Examples include abrasions, lacerations, open fractures, and penetrating injuries (e.g., stab wounds, gunshot injury).

sG1t0i0.title: Closed wound
sG1t0i0.description: A wound in which the overlying skin is intact but the underlying tissue is damaged. This type of injury is typically caused by blunt trauma. Examples include hematomas, contusions, closed fracture, and crush injuries.

tG1Xai0.title: Normocytosis
tG1Xai0.description: A descriptor for cells (usually erythrocytes) of normal size. Normocytic erythrocytes may be seen in healthy patients, patients with anemia of chronic disease, and those with hemolytic anemia.

FG1gai0.title: Antihuman globulin
FG1gai0.description: An animal-derived antibody that targets human antibodies and/or complement.

8G1Oai0.title: Infective stage
8G1Oai0.description: A stage in a parasite's life cycle during which it can invade a host.

uG1pai0.title: Diagnostic stage
uG1pai0.description: A stage in a parasite's life cycle during which it emerges from the host and can be detected with clinical and/or laboratory methods.

vG1Aai0.title: Definitive airway
vG1Aai0.description: A type of advanced airway device placed in the trachea with a cuff that is inflated below the vocal cords, secured in place, and connected to assisted ventilation. Definitive airways may consist of orotracheal tubes, nasotracheal tubes, tracheostomies, or cricothyroidotomies.

xG1EYi0.title: Isthmic spondylolisthesis
xG1EYi0.description: A condition in which a vertebral body slips forward in relation to the subjacent vertebra as a result of an abnormality in the pars interarticularis. Typically occurs at L5-S1 and is the most common form of spondylolisthesis in individuals < 18 years of age.

BG1zYi0.title: Do-not-intubate order
BG1zYi0.description: An advanced directive for patient care that precludes intubation. Can accompany or be separate from a do-not-resuscitate order (DNR). Individual patient wishes should be carefully considered: E.g., a patient with a DNI without a DNR should still receive chest compressions and bag-mask-ventilation in the event of cardiac arrest, but not intubation.

destinations.label: Goals of care → Limitation of life-sustaining treatment

yG1dbi0.title: Direct laryngoscopy
yG1dbi0.description: A procedure in which a lighted laryngoscope is inserted via the mouth and oropharynx to enable direct line of sight of the larynx. Often performed during endotracheal intubation but may also be used for laryngeal biopsy.

zG1rbi0.title: Degenerative spondylolisthesis
zG1rbi0.description: A condition in which a vertebral body slips forward in relation to the subjacent vertebra due to degenerative changes, without an associated disruption or defect in the vertebral ring. Typically occurs at L4-L5 and is the most common form of spondylolisthesis in adults > 50 years of age.

-G1Dbi0.title: Diverticulotomy
-G1Dbi0.description: A procedure that involves endoscopic or, less commonly, open surgical division of the septum that separates a diverticulum from the physiological esophageal lumen. Commonly performed for Zenker diverticulum.

Zt1ZXi0.title: Diverticulectomy
Zt1ZXi0.description: The surgical resection of a diverticulum. Commonly performed for Zenker, Meckel, and bladder diverticula.

0t1eXi0.title: Diverticulopexy
0t1eXi0.description: A procedure that involves the suspension of an upper esophageal (Zenker) diverticulum onto the hypopharyngeal wall to prevent the entry of food particles and secretions and ensure drainage.

at1QXi0.title: Paradoxical dysphagia
at1QXi0.description: A form of dysphagia characterized by difficulty swallowing liquids, while solids are easily swallowed. Common in patients with achalasia.

Xt19Xi0.title: Diaphragm with spermicide
Xt19Xi0.description: A female contraceptive method in which a barrier with a substance (e.g., foam, gel, cream) that inhibits sperm motility is inserted over the cervix prior to sexual intercourse.

Vt1Gci0.title: Superior ulnar collateral artery
Vt1Gci0.description: A branch of the brachial artery. Accompanies the ulnar nerve and contributes to elbow anastomosis.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

et1xci0.title: Inferior ulnar collateral artery
et1xci0.description: A branch of the brachial artery. Contributes to elbow anastomosis.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

Ut1b1i0.title: Middle ulnar collateral artery
Ut1b1i0.description: A branch of the brachial artery that arises between the superior and inferior ulnar collateral arteries. Ensures collateral circulation to the skin by branching off perforator arteries.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

2t1T1i0.title: Palmar carpal arch
2t1T1i0.description: An anastomosis between the palmar carpal branch of the radial artery and the palmar carpal branch of the ulnar artery.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

ft1k1i0.title: Dorsal carpal arch
ft1k1i0.description: An anastomosis between the dorsal carpal branch of the radial artery and the dorsal carpal branch of the ulnar artery.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

Tt161i0.title: Alternating electric field therapy
Tt161i0.description: An anticancer therapy that consists of a noninvasive, wearable device that delivers tumor-treating fields (low-intensity, alternating electrical fields) to tumor cells. Approved for the treatment of recurrent supratentorial glioblastoma.

St1y1i0.title: Patient counseling
St1y1i0.description: The process of providing information, advice, and assistance to patients to improve their health, treatment adherence, and quality of life.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

Qt1uWi0.title: Selective pregnancy reduction
Qt1uWi0.description: The termination of the fetus with health anomalies in a multiple pregnancy. Typically performed in the second trimester (i.e., after the anomaly scan).

lt1vdi0.title: Drug-induced long QT syndrome
lt1vdi0.description: A prolongation of the corrected QT interval caused by certain drugs, primarily those that inhibit potassium efflux during the rapid repolarization phase. Causative agents include class Ia and III antiarrhythmics, antibiotics (macrolides, fluoroquinolones), antipsychotics, antihistamines, and antidepressants.

Nt1-di0.title: PCP
Nt1-di0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Pneumocystis pneumonia
2. Phencyclidine
3. Primary care physician

Mt1MVi0.title: Acquired LQTS
Mt1MVi0.description: An acquired cardiac condition in which the QT interval is prolonged. Most commonly caused by drugs (e.g., antiarrhythmics, macrolides) and electrolyte imbalances. Typically asymptomatic, but may lead to torsade de pointes, which can progress to ventricular fibrillation and sudden cardiac death.

nt17Vi0.title: 5 As model of behavior change
nt17Vi0.description: An evidence-based behavioral intervention strategy that aims to help individuals with intentional changes to behavior. Composed of the following steps: assessing the patient's behavior, knowledge, and motivation; advising the patient on health risks and the benefits of change; collaboratively agreeing on appropriate treatment goals; assisting the patient to develop coping and support strategies; arranging plans for follow-up support.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

ot10ei0.title: Hemoglobin C trait
ot10ei0.description: A condition in which individuals are heterozygous carriers of the hemoglobin C mutation in the beta globin gene. They also have one normal copy of hemoglobin A, producing hemoblogin AC (HbAC). Patients with hemoglobin C trait are typically asymptomatic because of the functioning copy of hemoglobin A.

pt1Lei0.title: Narrow QRS complex
pt1Lei0.description: Typically a QRS complex duration of < 120 ms (or fewer than three small squares on the ECG). Indicates normal ventricular depolarization. Physiological (i.e., sinus rhythm), but also seen in any supraventricular ectopic or arrhythmogenic focus/foci.

Jt1sei0.title: Wide QRS complex
Jt1sei0.description: Typically a QRS complex duration of > 120 ms (or more than three small squares on the ECG). Indicates prolonged ventricular depolarization and may be seen in ventricular rhythms (e.g., ventricular tachycardia or premature ventricular beats) or in supraventricular rhythms with aberrant conduction (e.g., complete bundle branch block).

It1YUi0.title: Leptospira kirschneri
It1YUi0.description: A pathogenic species of Leptospira that can cause leptospirosis. It is a spiral-shaped, motile, aerobic spirochete. Best visualized with dark field microscopy, silver stain, or fluorescent microscopy because it does not stain well on Gram stain.

Ht1KUi0.title: Urease-producing bacteria
Ht1KUi0.description: A group of organisms that can produce urease capable of converting urea to ammonia and carbon dioxide, causing an increase in pH. Organisms include Proteus, Cryptococcus, H pylori, Ureaplasma, Nocardia, Klebsiella, S epidermidis, and S saprophyticus.

st1tUi0.title: Type IV metacarpal base fracture
st1tUi0.description: An extraarticular, pediatric physeal fracture at the base of the first metacarpal bone. Most commonly a type II Salter-Harris fracture.

Ft1g2i0.title: Global developmental delay
Ft1g2i0.description: A provisional diagnosis for children < 5 years of age who have not met key developmental milestones across multiple areas of cognitive abilities but who are too young to be formally assessed.

Dt11fi0.title: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Dt11fi0.description: A rare inherited arrhythmia syndrome characterized by polymorphic ventricular tachycardia triggered by adrenergic stimulation. Manifests as physical/emotional stress-induced syncope or sudden cardiac death in an otherwise healthy young adult or child. Associated with high mortality rates in untreated patients.

wt1hfi0.title: Alcohol withdrawal seizures
wt1hfi0.description: The occurrence of seizures in a patient experiencing alcohol withdrawal syndrome; usually brief, generalized, tonic-clonic seizures occurring 8–48 hours after cessation of heavy alcohol consumption.

9t1Nfi0.title: Kaliuresis
9t1Nfi0.description: The excretion of any amount of potassium in the urine. However, it is commonly used to describe excessive potassium in the urine. Kaliuresis may be present in conditions such as Bartter syndrome, Gitelman syndrome, and acute leukemia, and in patients who use thiazide or loop diuretics.

yt1dTi0.title: Nonfocal neurologic deficit
yt1dTi0.description: A neurologic symptom or sign that does not correlate with a specific anatomic region of the nervous system (e.g., nerve, spinal cord, brain). Examples include unconsciousness, confusion, amnesia, unsteadiness, dizziness, cardiac or vegetative signs, and bilateral weakness.

At1RTi0.title: Cold agglutinin syndrome
At1RTi0.description: A rare form of cold agglutinin hemolytic anemia in which cold-sensitive autoantibody-mediated hemolysis occurs secondary to another condition (e.g., infection, lymphoma). Cold antibodies in cold agglutinin syndrome can be either IgG or IgM and are usually polyclonal when secondary to infection and monoclonal when secondary to a lymphoproliferative disorder.

destinations.label: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia → Cold agglutinin hemolytic anemia

zt1rTi0.title: CAS
zt1rTi0.description:
An abbreviation that may refer to:
1. Carotid artery stenosis
2. Cold agglutinin syndrome

-t1DTi0.title: Bendamustine
-t1DTi0.description: An alkylating chemotherapeutic agent; its exact mechanism of action is unknown. Common indications include chronic lymphocytic leukemia and indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Common adverse effects include fever, nausea, vomiting, and myelosuppression.

ZF1Zgi0.title: RA
ZF1Zgi0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Rheumatoid arthritis
2. Right atrium

YF1ngi0.title: Ice pack test
YF1ngi0.description: A test used in patients with ptosis to evaluate for myasthenia gravis. An ice pack is placed on the closed eyelids for 2-5 minutes. The test is considered positive if the ptosis resolves; cooling improves neuromuscular transmission and reduces symptoms of myasthenia gravis.

cF1aSi0.title: Gastropathy
cF1aSi0.description: Injury of the gastric mucosa, usually involving a disruption in the protective mucous barrier. Gastropathy is accompanied by little to no inflammation, which distinguishes it from gastritis.

1F12Si0.title: Paradoxical chest movement
1F12Si0.description: A physical examination finding characterized by movement of the chest wall inward during inspiration and outward during expiration. Common causes include flail chest, diaphragm paralysis, and respiratory distress.

dF1oSi0.title: Mononuclear cell
dF1oSi0.description: A type of blood cell with a single nucleus, e.g., a lymphocyte or monocyte.

VF1GSi0.title: Ventilator bundle
VF1GSi0.description: A set of 4 standardized practices in order to prevent ventilator-associated infection consisting of: 1) Elevation of head of the bed to 30–45° 2) Daily assessment of extubation readiness 3) Daily interruption of sedation (sedation vacation) 4) Peptic ulcer and deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Prevention of common health care-associated infections

eF1xSi0.title: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy
eF1xSi0.description: A novel oncological therapy using T cells obtained from the patient that are genetically engineered to target tumor antigens. Predominantly reserved for the treatment of chemotherapy-resistant hematologic malignancies, e.g., acute lymphoblastic leukemia and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

UF1bhi0.title: Crisis resource management
UF1bhi0.description: A set of strategies and tools to improve team management and patient outcomes in emergency situations, with a focus on effective leadership, communication, and situational awareness.

2F1Thi0.title: Signs of hypoxia
2F1Thi0.description: A group of symptoms and signs that typically occur as a result of hypoxia. These may include altered mental status, respiratory distress, cyanosis, and tachycardia.

destinations.label: Respiratory failure and arrest → Clinical features

SF1yhi0.title: Systemic immunomodulatory medication
SF1yhi0.description: A drug that regulates or normalizes the function of the immune system. Examples include glucocorticoids, cytotoxic agents and antimetabolites, and monoclonal antibodies. Used in the management of organ transplants and infectious, autoimmune, and inflammatory diseases.

hF1c3i0.title: POLICE principle
hF1c3i0.description: A strategy to minimize inflammation and encourage healing of closed wounds, such as contusions and sprains: (P) protection, (OL) optimal loading, (I) ice, (C) compression, and (E) elevation. It is a modification of the RICE principle, which recommended resting (R) the injured part.

destinations.label: Sports injuries → Initial management of sports injuries

QF1u3i0.title: LTA
QF1u3i0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Laryngeal tube airway
2. Laser thermal ablation
3. Lipoteichoic acid

jF1_3i0.title: Colorimetric capnometer
jF1_3i0.description: A device used to help confirm correct endotracheal tube placement via detection of CO₂. If the tube is correctly situated in the trachea, exhaled CO₂ passes over pH-sensitive paper within the device, causing the color to change from purple to yellow.

kF1mRi0.title: Health insurance premium
kF1mRi0.description: A payment made to the health insurance provider, typically monthly, to maintain coverage. Amount usually depends on the policy type and individual factors. The health plan's deductible, copayments, and coinsurance are paid separately.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

lF1vRi0.title: Out-of-pocket expenses
lF1vRi0.description: Health care costs that are paid by an individual rather than by their insurance plan. Includes deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

NF1-Ri0.title: Out-of-pocket maximum
NF1-Ri0.description: An annual limit on the amount of money that an individual has to pay for covered health care services in a year (not including premiums). After this amount is reached, all covered health services are paid in full by the health plan for the rest of that plan year.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

mF1Vii0.title: Deductible
mF1Vii0.description: A predetermined amount paid out of pocket by the patient before the insurance company begins to pay for health expenses. After the deductible is paid, the individual usually only pays for copayment or coinsurance for covered services.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

5F1iii0.title: Copayment
5F1iii0.description: A fixed amount, defined in the insurance policy, paid by the patient to a health service provider at the time of the service (e.g., doctor's appointment, filling a prescription)

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

MF1Mii0.title: Coinsurance
MF1Mii0.description: A predetermined percentage of health care expenses for which an individual is responsible after meeting the deductible. The insurance company pays the remainder of the expenses.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

nF17ii0.title: Critical access hospital
nF17ii0.description: A designation assigned to small hospitals in rural areas by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services in order to ensure and improve access to health care services.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care access

LF1wii0.title: Affordable Care Act
LF1wii0.description: A comprehensive health care reform law passed by the US Congress in 2010 aiming to ensure and expand affordable health care for all Americans by making health insurance affordable, expanding Medicare eligibility, and supporting health care delivery models that lower health care costs.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care access

oF10Qi0.title: Patient-centered medical home
oF10Qi0.description: A team-based health care delivery model coordinated through a patient's primary care physician. Core components include health care accessibility and continuity of care, comprehensive care coordinated across multiple providers and care settings, patient-centered care, and emphasis on high-quality care and patient safety (e.g., through quality improvement initiatives and population health management).
