destinations.label: Health care system → Health care delivery models

pF1LQi0.title: Anki
pF1LQi0.description:
A highly customizable flashcard program with effective spaced repetition. The AMBOSS add-on for Anki integrates pop-up explanations, images, and direct links to high-yield AMBOSS content into all your Anki cards, regardless of the deck you use. It also lets you seamlessly connect your question practice with Anki - allowing you to launch Qbank sessions directly from Anki targeting selected cards or tags and to instantly find relevant AnKing flashcards from Qbank questions and sessions.

Visit:
- apps.ankiweb.net to install Anki
- amboss.com/us/anki to install the AMBOSS add-on

JF1sQi0.title: Noncomprehensive deductible
JF1sQi0.description: A type of deductible that applies to specific areas of coverage or medical expenses in a health insurance policy.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

qF1CQi0.title: Comprehensive deductible
qF1CQi0.description: A type of deductible that applies to and includes all the areas of coverage of the health insurance plan.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

IF1Yji0.title: Individual deductible
IF1Yji0.description: A deductible that each individual in the plan pays before the health insurance plan starts to pay for medical expenses.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

rF1fji0.title: Family deductible
rF1fji0.description: A type of deductible that applies to two or more individuals in a health insurance plan.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

7F14ji0.title: Embedded deductible
7F14ji0.description: Two deductible amounts within one insurance plan (individual and family), in which each member contributes the same amount towards meeting the deductible. Once a member of the plan meets the deductible, this individual becomes eligible for copayment and coinsurance.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

HF1Kji0.title: True family deductible
HF1Kji0.description: A type of deductible in which members can meet the deductible by pooling expenses. The deductible can be met by all members or just one member of the family and there is no limit to the amount payed by each member towards meeting the family deductible. Once the amount is met, the entire family is eligible for copayment and coinsurance.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

GF1Bji0.title: Progestin intrauterine device
GF1Bji0.description: A progestin-releasing (e.g., levonorgestrel-releasing) contraceptive device that is placed into the uterus. Local progesterone causes thickening of cervical mucus and decidualization of the endometrium, both of which prevent implantation of an embryo.

tF1XPi0.title: Self-pay
tF1XPi0.description: An individual who pays out of pocket for a health care service rather than using insurance (e.g., Medicare, Medicaid, or private health insurance). Includes individuals who are uninsured and individuals who have health insurance but do not use it for a particular service.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care payers

FF1gPi0.title: Medullary breast cancer
FF1gPi0.description: A rare subtype of invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast that is often associated with the BRCA1 mutation. Appears as a well-circumscribed, soft tumor with smooth borders, and as such often resembles a benign tumor.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Types of breast cancer

8F1OPi0.title: Jet ventilation
8F1OPi0.description: A type of ventilation in which oxygen is delivered at high pressure to the trachea. It is often used to provide oxygenation during rigid bronchoscopy or after the placement of a needle cricothyrotomy. Exhalation is passive and may be insufficient, leading to gas trapping.

EF18Pi0.title: AVPU scale
EF18Pi0.description: A scale used to rapidly assess a patient's level of consciousness and mental status: (A) fully alert and responsive, (V) opens eyes and responds appropriately to verbal stimulation, (P) responds to painful stimuli either by moving or, e.g., groaning or crying out, and (U) unresponsive.

destinations.label: Altered mental status and coma → Coma scores

vF1APi0.title: PEARLS model
vF1APi0.description: An acronym composed of six communication goals to help caregivers promote patient-centered care: Partnership, Empathy, Apology/Acknowledgment, Respect, Legitimization, and Support.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

CF1q4i0.title: Inhaled nitric oxide
CF1q4i0.description: A gas used to treat some cardiopulmonary conditions, such as pulmonary hypertension. Inhaled nitric oxide is a potent vasodilator that improves oxygenation and reduces right-to-left shunting.

_F15ki0.title: Atypical femoral fracture
_F15ki0.description: A transverse or short oblique noncomminuted fracture of the subtrochanteric region of the femur or femoral shaft, occurring after no or minimal trauma. Associated with long-term bisphosphonate use in patients with osteoporosis.

zF1rki0.title: Bone turnover marker
zF1rki0.description: A biomarker of bone metabolism that can be measured in the serum or urine. Includes markers of bone formation (e.g, carboxy-terminal propeptide of type I collagen) and bone resorption (e.g., C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen) and can be used to monitor adherence and response to osteoporosis treatment.

Z81ZOi0.title: Sugammadex
Z81ZOi0.description: A selective relaxant binding agent that reduces the availability of neuromuscular-blocking agents. Can be used to reverse neuromuscular blockade caused by rocuronium or vecuronium.

081eOi0.title: Contraindications for iodinated radiocontrast
081eOi0.description: Relative contraindications for iodinated contrast medium include a history of previous anaphylactic reactions, acute kidney injury or severe chronic kidney disease, and hyperthyroidism. In high-risk patients, premedication can be used to lower the risk of anaphylaxis or thyrotoxicosis.

a81QOi0.title: Arthroscopic hip debridement
a81QOi0.description: A minimally invasive surgical procedure in which the hip joint is visualized using an endoscope and damaged tissue is removed. Can be used to treat acetabular labrum tears and femoroacetabular impingement.

Y81nOi0.title: T stage
Y81nOi0.description: The component of the TNM system of staging malignant tumors that is based on local tumor growth and invasiveness, ranging from stage T0 to T4. Tx refers to a T stage that cannot be assessed.

b81HOi0.title: N stage
b81HOi0.description: The component of the TNM system of staging malignant tumors that is based on extent of regional lymph node involvement, ranging from stage N0 to N3. Nx indicates that the extent of nodal involvement cannot be assessed.

X819Oi0.title: M stage
X819Oi0.description: The component of the TNM system of staging malignant tumors that is based on the absence (M0) or presence (M1) of distant metastasis. Additional qualifiers (e.g., a-c) may be added to the stage to describe the extent and/or location of metastases.

1812li0.title: Benign essential blepharospasm
1812li0.description: A type of focal dystonia that results in involuntary contractions of the orbicularis oculi muscle and other periocular muscles, leading to increased bilateral eyelid closure.

V81Gli0.title: Nutrient artery of the humerus
V81Gli0.description: An artery that supplies the medullary cavity of the humerus. Originates from the brachial artery, at the middle of the arm, and enters the humerus posterior to the deltoid tuberosity.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the upper limbs → Arteries

T816Ni0.title: Idiopathic progressive cardiac conduction disease
T816Ni0.description: A form of idiopathic fibrosis affecting the His-Purkinje conduction system, leading to bundle branch block and, later, complete AV block.

g81FNi0.title: MCP extension test
g81FNi0.description: A test used to assess the integrity of the carpometacarpal joint of the thumb. Performed by placing one finger on the interphalangeal joint and applying resistance against extension while the patient tries to extend the thumb. Pain or crepitus indicates a positive test, suggesting carpometacarpal osteoarthritis.

destinations.label: Forearm, wrist, and hand → Clinical significance

R81lmi0.title: Altered mental status
R81lmi0.description: An acute change in alertness and/or cognition. Symptoms and signs include changes in thought pattern, memory, perception, behavior, and/or level of consciousness. Potential underlying causes include primary CNS processes (e.g., trauma, infection), general medical conditions (e.g., endocrine or metabolic disorders), substance-related causes, and/or psychiatric illness. Depending on the level of impairment, mental status may be assessed using brief tests of cognition (e.g., abbreviated mental test) or a mental status examination; the Glasgow coma scale or full outline of unresponsiveness score may be used in patients with a depressed level of consciousness.

destinations.label: Altered mental status and coma → Summary

i81Jmi0.title: Incidence risk
i81Jmi0.description: The number of new cases of disease divided by the population at risk at the start of the observation period. The incidence risk is a proportion and takes values from 0% - 100%.

Q81umi0.title: Elimination diet
Q81umi0.description: A time-limited and systematic approach to the exclusion and gradual reintroduction of foods and food groups (e.g., dairy, soy, eggs, gluten, nuts) from a person's diet. May be used to identify foods that trigger gastrointestinal symptoms in conditions such as eosinophilic gastritis and irritable bowel syndrome.

48135i0.title: Swallowed aerosolized steroids
48135i0.description: An off-label treatment for eosinophilic GI disease in which aerosolized steroids originally intended for inhalation are swallowed. These steroids can have a local antiinflammatory effect in the upper GI tract.

O81I5i0.title: Anterior tibial vein
O81I5i0.description: A deep vein of the leg. Arises from the venae comitantes of the dorsalis pedis artery and accompanies the anterior tibial artery. Drains the anterior aspect of the leg and foot.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

l81v5i0.title: Posterior tibial vein
l81v5i0.description: A deep vein of the leg. Arises from the medial and lateral plantar veins and accompanies the posterior tibial artery. Drains the posterior aspect of the leg and foot.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

N81-5i0.title: Fibular veins
N81-5i0.description: Deep veins of the leg. Arise from the medial and lateral plantar veins and accompany the fibular artery. Drain the lateral aspect of the leg.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

581iMi0.title: Dorsal venous arch of the foot
581iMi0.description: A superficial vein that lies on the dorsal aspect of the heads of the lateral four metatarsal bones. Continues as the medial and lateral marginal veins. The dorsal digital veins unite to form dorsal metatarsal veins, which drain into the dorsal venous arch.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

M81MMi0.title: Plantar venous arch of the foot
M81MMi0.description: A deep vein that lies on the plantar aspect of the lateral four metatarsal bones. Continues as the medial and lateral plantar veins. The plantar digital veins unite to form metatarsal veins that drain into the deep plantar venous arch.

destinations.label: Neurovasculature of the lower limbs → Veins

n817Mi0.title: Exercise-associated hyponatremia
n817Mi0.description: A condition of potentially life-threatening hyponatremia that can occur following intense physical exercise. Usually affects athletes participating in endurance events. Caused by increased fluid intake, persistent secretion of ADH, and sodium loss via diaphoresis. Clinical manifestations can be nonspecific and include dizziness, bloating, headache, nausea, and vomiting.

o810ni0.title: MR elastography
o810ni0.description: An MRI technique that measures liver stiffness and determines the degree of fibrosis using shear waves generated by a device placed on the patient’s right upper quadrant.

K81Uni0.title: Strain elastography
K81Uni0.description: An ultrasonographic technique that measures liver stiffness and determines the degree of fibrosis. Strain is applied to the liver tissue by actively pressing the transducer toward the liver or by holding the transducer in place against the movements caused by cardiovascular pulsation and breathing.

681jni0.title: Adult-onset asthma
681jni0.description: An uncommon phenotype of asthma in which patients present with symptoms for the first time in adulthood. Typically nonallergic in etiology. Involves a poor response to standard treatment. Exposure to allergens at work (i.e., occupational asthma) should be excluded.

q81Cni0.title: Mean pressure gradient
q81Cni0.description: The average instantaneous difference in pressure (i.e., the pressure gradient) across a blood vessel or valve. Can be measured invasively using a vascular catheter or estimated by measuring the peak velocity of blood flow across a valve/stenotic vascular segment on Doppler. Pressure gradients are increased across stenotic vessels or valves; the degree of increase corresponds to the severity of stenosis.

I81YLi0.title: Hepatic venous pressure gradient measurement
I81YLi0.description: An invasive technique used to calculate the difference between free and wedge pressures in the hepatic vein. HVPG > 5 mm Hg represents portal hypertension. HVPG ≥ 10 mm Hg indicates clinically significant portal hypertension and can predict decompensation and symptom development.

r81fLi0.title: METAVIR​ scoring system
r81fLi0.description: A scoring system for the histological grading and staging of chronic hepatitis in liver biopsy samples. Grading scores range from A1 (minimal chronic hepatitis) to A3 (severe chronic hepatitis); staging scores range from F0 (no fibrosis) to F4 (cirrhosis or advanced liver scarring).

7814Li0.title: IASL scoring system
7814Li0.description: A scoring system for the histological grading and staging of chronic hepatitis in liver biopsy samples. Grading scores range from minimal to severe chronic hepatitis; staging scores range from mild fibrosis to cirrhosis.

G81BLi0.title: Code status
G81BLi0.description:
A term used to describe a patient’s expressed preferences regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation and endotracheal intubation. There are three possible codes: “full code” (make every effort to resuscitate), “DNR" (do not resuscitate), and “DNI" (do not intubate). The term is unlikely to be familiar to a layperson; therefore it should not be used in discussion with patients or their family members.

A patient's code status should be confirmed verbally with the patient or their appropriate surrogate at each hospital admission (regardless of the previous status) and documented.

destinations.label: Goals of care → Limitation of life-sustaining treatment

E818oi0.title: Prediabetes
E818oi0.description: Elevated glucose and/or hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels that do not meet the criteria for type 2 diabetes mellitus, i.e., fasting plasma glucose 100–125 mg/dL (5.6–6.9 mmol/L), 2-hour glucose value after oral glucose tolerance test 140–199 mg/dL (7.8–11.0 mmol/L), or HbA1c 5.7–6.4%. Individuals with prediabetes are at high risk of developing diabetes mellitus.

v81Aoi0.title: Overweight
v81Aoi0.description: A metabolic-nutritional condition characterized by the accumulation of excess body fat. In adults, defined as a body mass index (BMI) of 25–29.9 kg/m² or, in adults of Asian descent, 23–24.9 or 23–27.4 kg/m². In children, defined as a BMI in the 85th–94th percentile for age and sex.

D811Ki0.title: Multitarget stool DNA test
D811Ki0.description: A stool-based assay that detects certain mutations typical for early colorectal carcinoma (e.g., mutations of the KRAS gene) or colonic polyps. Multitargeted stool DNA testing can be combined with fecal immunochemical testing (FIT DNA test) to increase specificity. Used primarily as a screening tool for colorectal carcinoma. Positive tests are followed up with colonoscopy.

C81qKi0.title: Femoral facial syndrome
C81qKi0.description: A condition associated with maternal diabetes and severe oligohydramnios. Characterized by femoral hypoplasia/agenesis and malformations of the face (e.g., cleft palate, micrognathia).

x81EKi0.title: Bone mineral density
x81EKi0.description: A measurement of calcium and other minerals in an area of bone. Used to evaluate for osteoporosis, evaluate response to osteoporosis treatment, and assess fracture risk. Often obtained using dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA).

B81zKi0.title: Major osteoporotic fracture
B81zKi0.description: A fracture of the vertebrae, hip, distal forearm, or proximal humerus in a patient with osteoporosis. These are typically fragility fractures that follow little to no trauma.

y81d6i0.title: Individually identifiable health information
y81d6i0.description: The information related to an individual's health that could potentially be used to identify that individual. Includes common identifiers (e.g., name, address, date of birth) and payment information. Protected from inappropriate use and disclosure by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

destinations.label: Ethics of communicating medical information → Confidentiality

A81R6i0.title: Left ventricular end-diastolic pressure
A81R6i0.description: The pressure in the left ventricle of the heart at the end of diastole. Can be measured with left heart catheterization. Used as a surrogate marker for preload in cardiac physiology. Related but not identical to pulmonary capillary wedge pressure.

Yu1npi0.title: Femoral neck axis
Yu1npi0.description: A line that equally divides the femoral neck through the center of the femoral head.

bu1Hpi0.title: Vertebral fracture assessment
bu1Hpi0.description: An imaging technique that uses dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) to assess for the presence of vertebral fractures in the thoracic and lumbar spine.

Xu19pi0.title: Sensate focus exercises
Xu19pi0.description: A series of exercises that focus on sensual experiences using touch without the goal of orgasm. It is couple-oriented and can be used to treat female orgasmic disorder and performance anxiety in men.

cu1aJi0.title: Occult fracture
cu1aJi0.description: A fracture that is not visible on conventional radiography such as x-ray. If clinical suspicion is high, advanced imaging (e.g., CT or MRI) can be used for further evaluation.

destinations.label: General principles of fractures → Subtypes and variants

1u12Ji0.title: Osteonecrosis of the jaw
1u12Ji0.description: An area of exposed maxillofacial bone(s) for at least 8 weeks. Can occur secondary to radiation, infection, or steroid or bisphosphonate use.

media.title: Advanced medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw

Wu1PJi0.title: Clinical features of anaphylaxis
Wu1PJi0.description: A collection of rapid-onset symptoms suggestive of anaphylaxis. Can involve the skin and mucous membranes (e.g., hives, flushing, angioedema), respiratory tract (e.g., stridor, wheezing), gastrointestinal tract (e.g., vomiting, diarrhea), and the cardiovascular system (e.g., tachycardia, hypotension, signs of end-organ hypoperfusion).

du1oJi0.title: Clinical features of sepsis
du1oJi0.description: A collection of signs and symptoms suggestive of sepsis, which includes: fever, tachycardia, and signs of organ dysfunction. Features of an underlying infection can also be present. Patients with septic shock also have hypotension.

2u1Tqi0.title: Life-threatening asthma exacerbation
2u1Tqi0.description: A subset of severe asthma exacerbation that manifests with drowsiness, confusion, silent chest, and/or signs of respiratory failure (e.g., PaCO₂ ≥ 45 mmHg and/or PaO₂ < 60 mmHg).

fu1kqi0.title: Venous blood gas
fu1kqi0.description: A laboratory test of venous blood that measures pH, pCO₂, pO₂, and HCO₃ concentration. Used to estimate acid-base status. pO₂ in a VBG cannot accurately assess systemic oxygenation.

Tu16qi0.title: Advanced airway device
Tu16qi0.description: A device that allows for the securing of a patient's airway using invasive means. Includes supraglottic airway devices, endotracheal tubes (i.e., intubation), and surgical airway devices.

Su1yqi0.title: Laryngospasm
Su1yqi0.description: A prolonged and involuntary closure of the vocal cords. May lead to life-threatening airway obstruction. Triggers include light anesthesia, aspiration, hypocalcemia, and/or injury to the superior laryngeal nerve.

Ru1lIi0.title: Physician impairment
Ru1lIi0.description: The inability of a clinician to provide an adequate level of medical care due to a mental health disorder, substance use disorder, or physical condition that limits the use of motor, cognitive, and/or perceptive skills.

destinations.label: Medical professionalism and codes of conduct → Malpractice, misconduct, and physician impairment

Qu1uIi0.title: Psychotropic drug
Qu1uIi0.description: A group of drugs used to treat various neuropsychiatric conditions. Includes antidepressants, anxiolytics, antipsychotics, stimulants, and mood stabilizers.

ju1_Ii0.title: Pediatric end-stage liver disease score
ju1_Ii0.description: A scoring system used for pediatric patients < 12 years of age with liver disease to prioritize those in need of a transplant. The score is calculated based on albumin, bilirubin, and INR values, as well as growth failure and the child's age (< 1 year or > 1 year of age).

media.title: PELD Score - Age Younger Than 12 years

Pu1Wri0.title: MAT
Pu1Wri0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Multifocal atrial tachycardia
2. Microscopic agglutination test
3. Medication-assisted treatment

4u13ri0.title: Microscopic agglutination test
4u13ri0.description: An antibody detection test used to diagnose leptospirosis. Patient serum is incubated with Leptospira serovars, and titers are obtained for serovars that react with patient serum.

ku1mri0.title: Gestational thrombocytopenia
ku1mri0.description: A benign and self-limited thrombocytopenia commonly observed during pregnancy. Platelet count is typically > 100,000/mm³.

Ou1Iri0.title: Dilutional anemia
Ou1Iri0.description: A type of anemia caused by an increase in plasma volume. Commonly observed among athletes with increased fluid intake and pregnant women.

Nu1-ri0.title: Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment
Nu1-ri0.description: A form containing medical orders to guide end-of-life medical care for an individual with a limited life expectancy or disabling condition. Signed by an individual who has decision-making capacity or by their surrogate decision-maker.

mu1V7i0.title: Chondrolysis
mu1V7i0.description: A rapid degeneration of articular cartilage. Can be idiopathic or arise as a complication of slipped capital femoral epiphysis and septic arthritis.

nu177i0.title: Emergency transfusion
nu177i0.description: The use of blood components in patients who require an urgent transfusion before pretransfusion testing results are available. Type-specific blood products are used when the recipient's ABO blood type is known. Universal donor blood components (e.g., uncrossmatched blood type O RBCs or uncrossmatched blood type AB plasma) are used in patients whose blood type is unknown.

Lu1w7i0.title: Electronic crossmatch
Lu1w7i0.description: A method of crossmatching used prior to a blood transfusion to confirm compatibility between donor RBCs and the recipient's serum or plasma through the automated issuing of ABO and Rh type-specific donor RBC units. Used in recipients with a negative antibody screen and no prior history of antibodies against non-ABO RBC antigens; may be used as an alternative to immediate-spin crossmatch.

ou10Hi0.title: Serologic crossmatch by direct agglutination
ou10Hi0.description: A method of crossmatching used prior to a blood transfusion to confirm compatibility between donor RBCs and the recipient's serum or plasma. Performed by mixing donor RBCs with the recipient's serum or plasma. Detection of agglutination or hemolysis indicates ABO incompatibility.

Ku1UHi0.title: Serologic crossmatch by indirect Coombs test
Ku1UHi0.description: A method of crossmatching used prior to a blood transfusion in recipients with a positive antibody screen or prior history of antibodies against non-ABO RBC antigens. Confirms compatibility between selected antigen-negative donor RBCs and the recipient's serum or plasma. Based on the alloantibodies identified during current and previous antibody screens, RBC units that are negative for the corresponding antigens are mixed with the recipient's serum or plasma and Coombs reagent; agglutination or hemolysis indicates incompatibility.

pu1LHi0.title: RBC antibody screen
pu1LHi0.description: A laboratory test used to screen for the presence of antibodies against non-ABO RBC antigens in the serum or plasma of a potential transfusion recipient. Performed as part of "type and screen" during routine pretransfusion testing.

Hu1Ksi0.title: Rickettsial infection
Hu1Ksi0.description: An infectious bacterial disease caused by species of Rickettsia, a genus of obligate intracellular gram-negative bacilli transmitted by arthropod vectors. Clinical features can vary by species. Common manifestations include acute febrile illness associated with cutaneous lesions (e.g., rash and/or eschar).

destinations.label: Tick-borne diseases → Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF)

wu1hti0.title: Stark law
wu1hti0.description: A federal law that prohibits physicians from self-referrals (i.e., referring patients to entities with which the physician or one of their immediate family members has a financial relationship).

destinations.label: Medical professionalism and codes of conduct → Referral of patients

9u1Nti0.title: Hypercapnic central sleep apnea
9u1Nti0.description: A form of central sleep apnea (CSA) characterized by elevated daytime CO2 levels (hypercapnia) due to hypoventilation. Sleep onset leads to worsening hypoventilation and hypercapnia, causing nighttime arousals. Conditions associated with hypercapnic CSA include neuromuscular diseases and chest wall diseases.

Cu1qti0.title: Nonhypercapnic central sleep apnea
Cu1qti0.description: A form of central sleep apnea (CSA) characterized by normal or low daytime CO2 levels (eucapnia or hypocapnia). PCO2 at the onset of sleep is below the apnea threshold, leading to a cycle of apnea, arousal, and compensatory hyperventilation. Examples include Cheyne-Stokes breathing in heart failure, high-altitude periodic breathing, and primary CSA.

xu1Eti0.title: Sexual assault
xu1Eti0.description: The nonconsensual involvement of an individual in any sexual activity through the use of force, the threat of force, coercion, abuse of authority, or due to the victim's inability to give consent (e.g., unconscious, incapacitated, intellectually disabled).

media.title: Bruise on the right cheek and infraorbital area

yu1dFi0.title: NS1 antigen test
yu1dFi0.description: A test to detect the nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) of the dengue virus. NS1 can be detected directly after the onset of clinical symptoms before IgM antibodies develop. A positive test confirms the diagnosis; a negative test does not rule out dengue infection. Not recommended after day 7 of symptomatic infection due to low sensitivity.

Au1RFi0.title: Alloantibody
Au1RFi0.description: An antibody produced against a foreign antigen following antigen exposure (e.g., through blood transfusion, pregnancy, or transplant).

_u15Fi0.title: Exercise-associated hyponatremic encephalopathy
_u15Fi0.description: A complication of exercise-associated hyponatremia that can manifest with symptoms of cerebral edema (e.g., agitation, confusion, seizures).

zu1rFi0.title: Dengue nonstructural protein 1
zu1rFi0.description: A viral protein crucial for replication of dengue virus and thought to be involved in dengue-induced vascular leakage. Secreted into the host bloodstream during infection. It is an early marker of infection.

-u1DFi0.title: Rape
-u1DFi0.description: A type of sexual violence that involves sexual intercourse or any form of vaginal, anal, or oral sexual penetration committed by a perpetrator without the consent of the victim.

0E1e8i0.title: Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia
0E1e8i0.description: A congenital bone growth disorder that results in short stature or dwarfism. Clinical features include skeletal and joint malformations involving the spine, hips, and knees, and abnormalities affecting the eyes and ears.

aE1Q8i0.title: Camptodactyly arthropathy coxa vara pericarditis syndrome
aE1Q8i0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder characterized by camptodactyly, arthropathy, and hip joint deformities, resulting in shortened limbs and, in some cases, coxa vara and pericardial or pleural effusion. Caused by a mutation in the PRG4 gene.

YE1n8i0.title: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia
YE1n8i0.description: A group of autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive disorders involving the epiphysis of long bones. Clinical features include a painful, waddling gait and short stature. Diagnosis is based on family history, radiological features, and genetic testing.

XE198i0.title: Proximal femoral focal deficiency
XE198i0.description: A congenital deformity of the proximal femur characterized by shortening of both legs and a short, flexed, abducted, and externally rotated thigh. The cause is unknown. Diagnosis is based on physical examination and imaging.

cE1aui0.title: Fibular deficiency
cE1aui0.description: A congenital absence of the fibula of unknown cause. Clinical features include short legs, equinovalgus foot deformity, a fibrous band instead of the fibula, and, in some cases, the absence of one or two toes.

1E12ui0.title: Congenital short femur
1E12ui0.description: A congenital abnormality of the femur that occurs during the prenatal period, leading to incomplete or abnormal development. Clinical features may vary but typically include a shortened femur and an externally rotated, flexed, abducted hip.

eE1xui0.title: Omenn syndrome
eE1xui0.description: An autosomal recessive form of severe combined immunodeficiency disease most commonly caused by mutations in the RAG genes or IL-7 receptor alpha gene. Symptoms usually develop shortly after birth and include features of autoimmunity (e.g., erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly) and immunodeficiency (e.g., recurrent infections).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital mixed immunodeficiencies

UE1bEi0.title: Rhythm strip
UE1bEi0.description: A prolonged recording (typically 10 seconds) from a single ECG lead (most commonly lead II), used to analyze a patient's cardiac rhythm.

2E1TEi0.title: Genetic analysis
2E1TEi0.description: A procedure to detect changes in genetic material, including DNA sequences, RNA sequences, gene expression, and chromosome structure. Can be used to diagnose genetic disorders and predict the probability of certain conditions.

fE1kEi0.title: NAFLD score
fE1kEi0.description: A noninvasive scoring system used to estimate the presence of advanced liver fibrosis in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (previously known as NAFLD). Parameters include age, BMI, AST, ALT, platelet, and albumin levels; and the presence of impaired fasting glucose or diabetes.

gE1FEi0.title: Bilateral choanal atresia
gE1FEi0.description: A congenital disorder characterized by complete or partial obstruction of both posterior nares. Complete obstruction manifests soon after birth with respiratory distress that worsens with feeding and improves with crying. Partial obstruction of both nares causes noisy breathing (stertor).

SE1yEi0.title: Gastric bypass surgery
SE1yEi0.description: A type of surgical procedure that can be used for weight loss, as part of reconstruction following gastrectomy, and to create a hepaticojejunostomy to treat bile duct obstruction.

3E1Svi0.title: Acne fulminans
3E1Svi0.description: A rare, severe form of acne that is characterized by painful ulcerative skin lesions and systemic inflammatory symptoms (e.g., fever, myalgia, arthritis). Can be caused by isotretinoin therapy.

RE1lvi0.title: Purpura fulminans
RE1lvi0.description: A condition characterized by purpura that rapidly progress to bullae and infarction-related skin necrosis, with a high mortality rate. It may occur secondary to infections (most commonly Meningococcus and Streptococcus) and conditions that cause DIC. It may also be the first indication of a protein C or protein S deficiency.

iE1Jvi0.title: Hepatic artery thrombosis
iE1Jvi0.description: A thrombotic obstruction of the hepatic artery that typically occurs as a complication of liver transplantation. May lead to hepatocellular necrosis, biliary injury, hepatic abscess, and graft failure.

lE1vDi0.title: Symptoms of cerebral edema
lE1vDi0.description: The clinical manifestations of brain tissue edema. Localized edema typically results in focal neurological deficits whereas generalized edema can include headaches, nausea and vomiting, altered mental state, and, in severe cases, seizures and coma. Cerebral edema can additionally cause raised ICP, which can have overlapping symptoms.

nE17wi0.title: Remnant gastric cancer
nE17wi0.description: A cancer that arises at the gastric remnant after partial gastrectomy. Develops as a result of chronic irritation due to biliary or pancreatic secretions.

JE1s9i0.title: Signs of oversedation
JE1s9i0.description: Manifestations of an excessive administration of sedative-hypnotic drugs that can lead to brain injury, aspiration, cardiac failure, and death if unrecognized or untreated. Findings include obtundation and respiratory depression, e.g., bradypnea, signs of increased work of breathing, hypoxemia, hypercapnia.

qE1C9i0.title: Radiation proctitis
qE1C9i0.description: An adverse effect of radiation therapy to the rectal mucosa. Further subdivided into acute radiation proctitis (i.e., radiation damage that causes symptoms within weeks after radiation therapy) and chronic radiation proctopathy (i.e., epithelial atrophy and fibrosis that develop months after radiation therapy).

IE1YCi0.title: Gram-positive diplococcus
IE1YCi0.description: A bacterial species that is round in shape, typically found in pairs of cells, and appears blue/purple on Gram stain. Examples include S. pneumoniae and Enterococcus.

7E14Ci0.title: SPE
7E14Ci0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Serum protein electrophoresis
2. Streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxin

HE1KCi0.title: Streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxins
HE1KCi0.description: A superantigen exotoxin produced by Streptococcus pyogenes. It bridges MHC class II molecules on antigen-presenting cells and T-cell receptors on T cells outside of the normal binding sites. Results in a large release of IL-1, IL-2, IFN-γ, and TNF-α, which can lead to various diseases, including toxic shock syndrome.

uE1pxi0.title: Premature adrenarche
uE1pxi0.description: A benign pubertal variant characterized by premature development of pubic and axillary hair, acne, and/or adult-type body odor due to early activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis without other associated secondary sexual characteristics. Associated with increased serum androgen concentrations. Bone age can be normal or advanced for chronological age.

9E1NBi0.title: Idiopathic premature pubarche
9E1NBi0.description: A benign pubertal variant characterized by the development of pubic hair without evidence of premature adrenarche (e.g., advanced bone age or increased serum androgen concentrations) before the age of 8 years in girls and 9 years in boys. May be related to increased sensitivity of the pilosebaceous unit to age-appropriate androgen concentrations.

yE1dyi0.title: Herpes simplex virus
yE1dyi0.description: The virus that causes herpes. The two subtypes of herpes simplex virus are herpes simplex virus 1, which predominantly causes oral infections, and herpes simplex virus 2, which predominantly causes genital infections.

AE1Ryi0.title: Sigmoid volvulus
AE1Ryi0.description: A twisting of the sigmoid colon around its mesentery resulting in closed-loop bowel obstruction and increased risk of intestinal ischemia and perforation. Can spontaneously detort in some cases. Risk factors include chronic constipation and colonic dysmotility.

destinations.label: Sigmoid volvulus and cecal volvulus → Clinical features

_E15yi0.title: Cecal volvulus
_E15yi0.description: A twisting of the cecum around its mesentery resulting in acute bowel obstruction and increased risk of intestinal ischemia and perforation. Risk factors include prior abdominal surgery, exertion, and pelvic masses.

destinations.label: Sigmoid volvulus and cecal volvulus → Clinical features

media.title: Bird beak sign in cecal volvulus

zE1ryi0.title: Aural polyp
zE1ryi0.description: A benign polypoid proliferation of the middle or external ear. Common causes include cholesteatoma, chronic otitis media, and chronic inflammatory processes. Manifestations include otorrhea, hearing loss, otalgia, and a sensation of a mass in the ear.

-E1Dyi0.title: Granulomatous amebic encephalitis
-E1Dyi0.description: A rare central nervous system infection caused by free-living Amoeba species (e.g., Acanthamoeba spp., Balamuthia mandrillaris, Sappinia pedata). Primarily affects individuals who are immunocompromised. Characterized by progressively worsening neurologic function, manifesting as decreased consciousness, focal neurologic signs, seizures, and coma. Nearly always fatal.

destinations.label: General parasitology → Protozoa that cause ocular and neurological disease

0v1eAi0.title: Drug-induced hemolytic anemia
0v1eAi0.description: An intravascular or extravascular form of hemolytic anemia that is caused by exposure to a specific drug. Can be immune mediated or occur as a result of oxidant injury in patients with G6PD deficiency. Commonly implicated drugs include beta-lactam antibiotics (e.g., penicillins, cephalosporins), trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, NSAIDs (e.g., diclofenac, aspirin), dapsone, and primaquine.

av1QAi0.title: Drug fever
av1QAi0.description: A febrile response that coincides with the administration of a drug and resolves after withdrawal of the offending agent. Can be associated with rash (e.g., morbilliform drug eruption). Mechanisms include hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anticonvulsants, penicillin), altered thermoregulation (e.g., thyroxine, anticholinergics), pyrogens in parenteral drug preparations, and idiosyncratic reactions (e.g., malignant hyperthermia).

destinations.label: Fever → Differential diagnoses by risk factors

Yv1nAi0.title: MAC
Yv1nAi0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Mycobacterium avium complex
2. Minimum alveolar concentration
3. Membrane attack complex
4. Monitored anesthesia care

bv1HAi0.title: Waddling gait
bv1HAi0.description: An abnormal gait pattern caused by weakness of the pelvic girdle muscles (especially the gluteus medius muscle) due to myopathy. Gluteal weakness results in hip drop when the affected leg swings (Trendelenburg sign).

Xv19Ai0.title: Expedited partner therapy
Xv19Ai0.description: The treatment of sexual partners of patients who have been diagnosed with sexually transmitted infections (e.g., chlamydia, gonorrhea) by giving prescriptions to the index patients.

destinations.label: Sexually transmitted infections → Management of sexual partners

Vv1G_i0.title: Vocal cord dysfunction
Vv1G_i0.description: A condition characterized by episodic, paradoxical vocal cord adduction during inspiration, which can result in sudden dyspnea. The etiology is not fully understood; it is associated with laryngeal hyperresponsiveness (e.g., due to inhaled irritants, GERD, or chronic postnasal drip) and psychiatric conditions (e.g., anxiety, depression). Diagnosed with laryngoscopic examination of vocal cord movement during an acute episode.

Tv16zi0.title: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide
Tv16zi0.description: The concentration of nitric oxide in exhaled air. Elevation suggests airway inflammation (e.g., allergic/eosinophilic asthma, atopy, eosinophilic bronchitis). Higher FeNO levels indicate more inflammation, which can support a diagnosis of asthma in patients with typical symptoms.

gv1Fzi0.title: Real-time polymerase chain reaction
gv1Fzi0.description: A PCR technique that utilizes fluorescence (e.g., intercalating dyes or DNA probes) for monitoring amplification of targeted DNA during the PCR via computer software. Q-PCR is not to be confused with RT-PCR (reverse transcriptase PCR), although quantitative reverse transcription PCR (RT-qPCR) is a method. Semiquantitative real-time PCR is also possible.

hv1c-i0.title: Quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction
hv1c-i0.description: A combined RT-PCR and qPCR technique in which a sample of mRNA is converted to complementary DNA (cDNA) by reverse transcriptase. The cDNA is then amplified by real-time PCR to detect and quantify the amount of RNA.

3v1S-i0.title: Airway clearance techniques
3v1S-i0.description: A variety of techniques to clear pulmonary secretions in patients with chronic pulmonary diseases (e.g., cystic fibrosis, bronchiectasis, COPD). Techniques range from coughing and breathing exercises and postural drainage and percussion to positive expiratory pressure therapy.

Rv1l-i0.title: Corticosteroid-binding globulin
Rv1l-i0.description: A protein that binds to and transports glucocorticoids and progesterone. Primarily synthesized in the liver and released in the bloodstream. Measuring the concentration of CBG helps to determine the proportion of glucocorticoid that is unbound and, therefore, biologically active.

iv1J-i0.title: Airborne infection isolation room
iv1J-i0.description: A room with negative pressure used to isolate patients with suspected or confirmed airborne infections (e.g., tuberculosis, measles, varicella, COVID-19). These rooms limit the spread of infection by facilitating frequent air changes (6–12 air cycles/hour) and preventing contaminated air from escaping the room.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Isolation precautions

Qv1u-i0.title: Respirator
Qv1u-i0.description: A type of personal protective equipment that covers the nose and mouth and protects the wearer against airborne particles (e.g., bacteria, viruses, dust), fumes, and vapors. Types include air-purifying respirators (e.g., N95 respirators) and air-supplying respirators.

jv1_-i0.title: N95 respirator
jv1_-i0.description: A type of disposable respiratory personal protective equipment that fits tightly over the nose and mouth and filters at least 95% of airborne particles. Used to protect individuals against infections (e.g., tuberculosis, COVID-19, influenza) in the health care setting and against hazardous material in other industries (e..g, mining, construction).

Pv1WZQ0.title: Respiratory hygiene
Pv1WZQ0.description: A collection of methods to control the transmission of respiratory infections (e.g., influenza, COVID-19). Includes covering the nose and mouth (e.g., masking), maintaining a distance of 3-6 feet, disposal of tissue after use, and washing of hands after coming into contact with respiratory secretions.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Health care hygiene

4v13ZQ0.title: Surgical face mask
4v13ZQ0.description: A type of disposable respiratory personal protective equipment that loosely fits over the nose and mouth. Provides protection from large-sized droplets and splashes (e.g., of bodily fluids or other hazardous fluids). Does not provide protection from inhaling droplet nuclei (size < 5 µm).

mv1V0Q0.title: Fomite
mv1V0Q0.description: An object that can be contaminated after coming in contact with bodily secretions (e.g., saliva, nasal secretions) and transmit infections to a new host.

5v1i0Q0.title: Vaginal adenosis
5v1i0Q0.description: A condition characterized by the presence of glandular columnar epithelium within the upper two-thirds of the vaginal wall. Common causes include exposure to diethylstilbestrol in utero and exposure to other progestogens and nonsteroidal estrogens. In women who have been exposed to diethylstilbestrol in utero it is associated with a high risk of vaginal clear cell adenocarcinoma.

destinations.label: Vulvar and vaginal cancer → Vaginal cancer

Mv1M0Q0.title: Dyskeratosis
Mv1M0Q0.description: A histopathologic finding characterized by premature keratinization of the stratum granulosum.

nv170Q0.title: Coronary artery calcium score
nv170Q0.description: A score used to predict cardiovascular disease risk by measuring the amount of calcification in the coronary arteries seen on a cardiac CT scan. Examples include visual scores or semi-automated scores such as the Agatston score, which correlates with the 10-year risk of developing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

Lv1w0Q0.title: DICES GAPS
Lv1w0Q0.description: A mnemonic to remember the features of major depressive disorder. "D" or "I" must be present for diagnosis. Consists of: Depressed mood (can present as irritability in children), Interest loss (anhedonia), Concentration (poor concentration or difficulty making decisions), Energy (low energy or fatigue), Sleep (insomnia or hypersomnia), Guilt (low self-esteem), Appetite (decreased appetite or overeating), Psychomotor agitation or retardation, and Suicidal ideation.

ov10aQ0.title: Bladder scanner
ov10aQ0.description: A device that uses automated ultrasound technology to measure the volume of the bladder. It is often performed at the bedside to quantify postvoid residual volume.

qv1CaQ0.title: Simple extrafascial hysterectomy
qv1CaQ0.description: Surgical removal of the uterus and cervix. Depending on the indication for surgery and the age of the patient, one or both of the ovaries and fallopian tubes may also be removed. Common indications include cervical cancer, endometrial cancer, and menorrhagia.

destinations.label: Invasive cervical cancer → Surgical interventions for cervical cancer

Iv1YYQ0.title: Modified radical hysterectomy
Iv1YYQ0.description: En bloc removal of the uterus, cervix, upper 1/4th of the vagina, and the parametrium. Typically performed in conjunction with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy for early-stage cervical cancer .

destinations.label: Invasive cervical cancer → Surgical interventions for cervical cancer

rv1fYQ0.title: Radical hysterectomy
rv1fYQ0.description: En bloc removal of the uterus, cervix, upper one-third to upper half of the vagina, the parametrium, and, if needed, resection of involved aspects of the adjacent organs. Typically performed in conjunction with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy for early-stage cervical cancer.

destinations.label: Invasive cervical cancer → Surgical interventions for cervical cancer

Hv1KYQ0.title: Mucoactive agents
Hv1KYQ0.description: A group of medications that improve mucus clearance in the lungs, including mucolytics, mucokinetics, expectorants, and mucoregulators. Frequently used to treat chronic pulmonary conditions, such as bronchiectasis and COPD.

tv1XbQ0.title: Anginal equivalent
tv1XbQ0.description: A symptom of ischemia (other than chest pain) that is associated with exertion or stress, or relieved by short-acting nitrates or rest. Symptoms include pain in the jaw or arm, dyspnea, fatigue, epigastric pain, and nausea.

8v1ObQ0.title: Phytobezoar
8v1ObQ0.description: A foreign body composed of partially digested plant material that most commonly forms in the stomach due to the impairment of the grinding mechanism of the stomach.

uv1pbQ0.title: Sputum analysis
uv1pbQ0.description: A group of tests used to evaluate respiratory mucus for evidence of infection or abnormal cells. Typically includes cell count, smear microscopy (e.g., Gram stain, acid-fast stain), culture, and cytology. Can be used to diagnose or screen for several respiratory tract conditions.

Ev18bQ0.title: Safe injection practices
Ev18bQ0.description: A set of practices that are used to prevent transmission of infection by sharps injury. Includes hand hygiene, use of gloves, use of aseptic techniques, use of single-use, disposable syringes, use of single-dose vials, and proper disposal of sharp wastes.

vv1AbQ0.title: Standard precautions
vv1AbQ0.description: A set of measures used for all patient care. Includes hand hygiene, safe injection practices, respiratory hygiene, and the use of appropriate personal protective equipment (e.g., gloves, gown, surgical mask, eye protection) if there is a risk of exposure to body fluids or other potentially infectious material.

Dv11XQ0.title: Hemolytic transfusion reaction
Dv11XQ0.description: An immune-mediated adverse reaction to blood transfusion. Further subdivided into acute and delayed reactions. Acute reactions typically occur < 24 hours after transfusion and are caused by ABO incompatibility or the immune response to major blood group antigens. Delayed reactions typically occur days to weeks after transfusion and are caused by the immune response to minor blood group antigens or D (Rh) antigens

wv1hXQ0.title: Muscle-specific tyrosine kinase antibody
wv1hXQ0.description: An autoantibody against muscle-specific kinase, a transmembrane protein in the neuromuscular junction. Binding of anti-MuSK antibodies leads to a reduction in the formation of the acetylcholine receptor and results in impaired muscle contraction. This antibody can be present in patients with myasthenia gravis.

9v1NXQ0.title: Guselkumab
9v1NXQ0.description: A monoclonal antibody that binds to IL-23, which prevents interaction with the IL-23 receptor and inhibits the release of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Used in the treatment of plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and ulcerative colitis.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

Cv1qXQ0.title: Unsaturated fatty acid
Cv1qXQ0.description: A fatty acid that contains one or more double bounds. Most of the unsaturated fatty acids are also essental for humans, i.e. cannot be produced in the body and should be obtained from nutritional sources.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

xv1EXQ0.title: Monounsaturated fatty acid
xv1EXQ0.description: A fatty acid that contains one double bond. Examples include palmitoleic and oleic acid.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

Bv1zXQ0.title: Polyunsaturated fatty acid
Bv1zXQ0.description: A fatty acid that contains more than one double bonds. Examples include omega-6 (e.g., linoleic) and omega-3 (e.g., alpha-linolenic) acid.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

yv1dcQ0.title: Omega-6 fatty acid
yv1dcQ0.description: A polyunsaturated fatty acid mainly found in seeds and seed oils. Examples include linoleic and arachidonic acid. Serves as a precursor for the production of leukotrienes and prostaglandins.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

Av1RcQ0.title: Alectinib
Av1RcQ0.description: An antineoplastic drug that belongs to the second generation of ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Used as a second-line treatment in advanced-stage, ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after prior treatment with crizotinib and/or after development of CNS metastases.

_v15cQ0.title: Afatinib
_v15cQ0.description: An antineoplastic drug that belongs to the class of EGFR inhibitors. Irreversibly inhibits the activity of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Used to treat advanced-stage, EGFR-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

zv1rcQ0.title: Janus kinase inhibitors
zv1rcQ0.description: A group of small molecule drugs that block the activity of one or more of the JAK proteins (JAK1, JAK2, JAK3, and TYK2). JAKs are involved in immune responses, inflammatory reactions, and hematopoiesis. Indications for JAK inhibitors include inflammatory diseases (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis) and myeloproliferative disorders (e.g., polycythemia vera). Examples include tofacitinib, baricitinib, and ruxolitinib.

-v1DcQ0.title: Encorafenib
-v1DcQ0.description: A small molecule inhibitor used in the treatment of malignant melanoma and other cancers with a V600E mutation of the BRAF gene. Often coadministered with MEK inhibitors.

ZD1Z1Q0.title: ALA
ZD1Z1Q0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Alpha-aminolevulinic acid
2. Alpha-linolenic acid
3. Alpha-lipoic acid

0D1e1Q0.title: Alpha-linolenic acid
0D1e1Q0.description: An omega-3 fatty acid found in dietary plant sources, such as nuts, seeds, and vegetable oils.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

YD1n1Q0.title: Coronary computed tomography angiography
YD1n1Q0.description: A noninvasive method used to assess the amount of plaque in the coronary arteries involving a CT scan with IV contrast. Scoring systems are frequently used to report the degree of plaque or stenosis.

bD1H1Q0.title: Regadenoson
bD1H1Q0.description: A selective A2A receptor agonist that acts as a coronary vasodilator. It may be used during a pharmacological stress test.

1D12WQ0.title: Histrelin acetate
1D12WQ0.description: A GnRH agonist in the form of a subcutaneous implant that is used in the treatment of advanced prostate cancer, central precocious puberty, and off-label for puberty suppression in transgender children and young adults.

UD1bdQ0.title: Gender-affirming surgery
UD1bdQ0.description: A set of surgical procedures to align a transgender person's body with their gender identity. Can include genital surgery (e.g., construction of a vagina or phallus), gonadectomy, hysterectomy, chest surgery (mastectomy or breast augmentation), and other procedures (e.g., facial feminization or masculinization, voice surgery).

destinations.label: Principles of transgender health care → Gender-affirming surgery

2D1TdQ0.title: Gender-affirming hormone therapy
2D1TdQ0.description: Hormone therapy (testosterone or a combination of estrogen and antiandrogen) used to align a person's physical appearance with their gender identity.

destinations.label: Principles of transgender health care → Hormone therapy

fD1kdQ0.title: Microgravity
fD1kdQ0.description: A state in which the body is subject to miniscule gravitational force. The effects of a microgravity environment can be experienced by humans during free falls, parabolic flights, and spaceflight. Although often referred to as "zero gravity," gravitational forces are never actually zero.

gD1FdQ0.title: Hypogravity
gD1FdQ0.description: A gravitational force that is lower than the gravitational force on the surface of the earth (1 G) but still significant (e.g., the gravitational force experienced on the surface of the moon, 0.17 G).

SD1ydQ0.title: Crew medical restraint system
SD1ydQ0.description: A system used in microgravity environments for securing the patient and, if necessary, the care provider as well. Has an attached work station with equipment for providing medical care.

hD1cVQ0.title: Gender-affirming care
hD1cVQ0.description: A set of interventions to align a person's body with their gender identity. Includes gender-affirming hormone therapy, gender-affirming surgery, voice modification, and other measures such as hair removal or chest binding. Gender-affirming care also refers to ensuring respectful and appropriate health care for individuals of all gender identities.

destinations.label: Principles of transgender health care → Definitions

3D1SVQ0.title: Chain of survival
3D1SVQ0.description: A series of actions that decrease the mortality associated with a life-threatening event when each action in the series is executed properly and in the correct order. Examples include the chains of survival for management of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and stroke.

PD1WeQ0.title: Gender expression
PD1WeQ0.description: The external representation of gender through behavior. Gender expression typically reflects gender identity.

4D13eQ0.title: Chromosomal sex
4D13eQ0.description: The designation of sex based on karyotype (e.g., XX for female, XY for male).

kD1meQ0.title: Phenotypical sex
kD1meQ0.description: The physical manifestations of sex comprising the genital organs and secondary sexual characteristics as determined by an individual’s chromosomal and hormonal constitution.

OD1IeQ0.title: Sex assigned at birth
OD1IeQ0.description: The sex (i.e., male or female) assigned to an individual at birth. Generally done by a physician, midwife, nurse, and/or lay person on inspection of the infant’s genitals and/or determination of chromosomes.

lD1veQ0.title: Cismale
lD1veQ0.description: A male individual who identifies as male (gender identity matches sex assigned at birth).

ND1-eQ0.title: Cisfemale
ND1-eQ0.description: A female individual who identifies as female (gender identity matches sex assigned at birth).

mD1VUQ0.title: Gender transition
mD1VUQ0.description: The process of recognizing and expressing a gender identity that is not in alignment with one's assigned gender. Includes social changes (e.g., changing legal name) and medical treatment (e.g., gender-affirming hormone therapy).

5D1iUQ0.title: Gender affirmation
5D1iUQ0.description: The process of undergoing the social, legal, and/or physical changes necessary to complete gender transition. May involve gender-affirming hormone therapy and/or surgery.

MD1MUQ0.title: Third gender
MD1MUQ0.description: The identity of a gender besides male and female as defined by oneself and/or society (e.g., Hijras in the Indian subcontinent, Khanith in Oman, and two-spirit identities in the United States).

nD17UQ0.title: Genderfluid
nD17UQ0.description: A gender identity that is in flux between genders.

oD102Q0.title: Cryopreservation
oD102Q0.description: A process that preserves cells or tissues by cooling them to very low temperatures. Can be used for fertility preservation (cryopreservation of oocytes, embryos, sperm, or testicular tissue), in research (e.g., cryopreservation of stem cells), and other areas.

KD1U2Q0.title: Puberty suppression therapy
KD1U2Q0.description: Treatment to delay puberty, which may be used in precocious puberty or in transgender adolescents to delay the development of secondary sex characteristics. Gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists are the most commonly used puberty inhibitors.

destinations.label: Principles of transgender health care → Hormone therapy

6D1j2Q0.title: Improvement science
6D1j2Q0.description: A multidisciplinary applied science based on researching and determining which improvement strategies work in health care systems and policies in order to ensure quality, safety, and value.

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

pD1L2Q0.title: Public health
pD1L2Q0.description: A branch of health care that focuses on the promotion of health and the prevention of diseases in a specific country or population through public and individual measures.

JD1s2Q0.title: Homosexuality
JD1s2Q0.description: An attraction to individuals of the same sex. May also be defined as attraction to the same gender independent of sex assigned at birth (e.g., a transgender man who is attracted to men may identify as gay).

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual orientation

qD1C2Q0.title: Heterosexuality
qD1C2Q0.description: An attraction to individuals of the opposite sex. May also be defined as attraction to the opposite gender independent of sex assigned at birth (e.g., a transgender man who is attracted to women may identify as heterosexual).

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual orientation

ID1YfQ0.title: Bisexuality
ID1YfQ0.description: An attraction to individuals of the same as well as the opposite sex and/or gender, often in varying and/or fluctuating degrees.

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual orientation

rD1ffQ0.title: Pansexuality
rD1ffQ0.description: A sexual and/or emotional attraction to people independent of sex, gender, or sexual orientation.

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual orientation

7D14fQ0.title: Global health
7D14fQ0.description: A branch of health care that focuses on the treatment and prevention of diseases on a transnational level. Priorities include improving human health and achieving health equity.

HD1KfQ0.title: Polysexuality
HD1KfQ0.description: An attraction to individuals of many but not all genders or sexual orientations

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual orientation

sD1tfQ0.title: Asexuality
sD1tfQ0.description: The absence of sexual attraction to other people. Asexuality does not imply an inability to emotionally or romantically connect with other people.

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual orientation

GD1BfQ0.title: Air pollution
GD1BfQ0.description: The presence or release of noxious substances into the air, which is mainly caused by fuel combustion in industrial facilities and motorized vehicles. Pollutants include carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, atmospheric particulate matter, and nitrogen dioxide. Associated with respiratory diseases (e.g. asthma, COPD), cardiovascular disease, and certain types of cancer.

tD1XTQ0.title: Noise pollution
tD1XTQ0.description: A form of pollution caused by unwanted environmental sounds (e.g., from railways and aircraft). Associated with adverse health effects, such as sleep disturbance and stress.

FD1gTQ0.title: Greenhouse gases
FD1gTQ0.description: A collection of atmospheric gases (e.g., carbon dioxide and methane) that absorb and subsequently emit thermal infrared radiation, increasing the temperature of the Earth's surface. The effect of heat being trapped in the Earth's atmosphere is termed the "greenhouse effect".

8D1OTQ0.title: Gender neutral
8D1OTQ0.description: A gender identity that does not align with the notion of having a gender.

uD1pTQ0.title: Bigender
uD1pTQ0.description: A gender identity that comprises both male and female gender.

ED18TQ0.title: Genderqueer
ED18TQ0.description: A gender identity that is not aligned with the traditional understanding of gender as a binary construct.

vD1ATQ0.title: Vector-borne diseases
vD1ATQ0.description: A group of infectious diseases that are transmitted via arthropod vectors, such as ticks and mosquitoes.

DD11gQ0.title: Pollution
DD11gQ0.description: The introduction of harmful substances (solids, liquids, gases) into the environment that can affect water, air, and/or soil quality and result in harm to living organisms.

wD1hgQ0.title: Ground-based medical support
wD1hgQ0.description: The provision of instructions for medical care to the crew of an aircraft or low earth orbit mission via a telecommunication link.

destinations.label: Fitness to fly and inflight medical events → Inflight medical events

9D1NgQ0.title: Low earth orbit mission
9D1NgQ0.description: A space mission that is confined to an orbital height < 2000 km above the surface of the earth.

CD1qgQ0.title: Automated chest compression device
CD1qgQ0.description: A battery-operated or pneumatic device that is used to provide chest compressions. Can provide consistently high-quality chest compressions without interruptions and enable cardiopulmonary resuscitation to be performed with fewer care providers and in tighter quarters or extreme environments (e.g., spaceflight).

xD1EgQ0.title: Chest compressions
xD1EgQ0.description: A key cardiopulmonary resuscitation technique used to minimize irreversible myocardial and neurological damage in patients with cardiac arrest. Involves sequential anteroposterior compressions applied to the thorax at an adequate rate (i.e., 100–120 per minute) and depth (i.e., 4 cm in infants, 5–6 cm in all other age groups) with minimal interruptions and full chest recoil in between compressions. Can be manual or automated.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)

BD1zgQ0.title: Climate change
BD1zgQ0.description: A sustained change in global climate systems mostly due to anthropogenic alterations to the composition of the atmosphere and land use, but also due to natural internal processes (e.g., volcanic eruptions) and external influences. Components of the climate system include weather patterns, the water cycle, the land surface, ice, and living components of the Earth.

media.title: Climate change: increases in average temparature and temperature variability

yD1dSQ0.title: LGBT+ culture
yD1dSQ0.description:
An umbrella term for the culture shared by lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer individuals
Communities affiliated with LGBT+ culture may or may not define themselves based on gender or sexual activities.

AD1RSQ0.title: Incel
AD1RSQ0.description: An online subculture based on the shared inability to find a sexual partner despite the desire for sexual partnership. Incel culture is highly controversial due to its misogynistic tendencies.

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual activities

_D15SQ0.title: Negative inotropes
_D15SQ0.description: Drugs that decrease the force of myocardial contraction. Includes beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, class 1A antiarrhythmics (e.g., procainamide), and class 1C antiarrhythmics (e.g., flecainide, propafenone).

1w123Q0.title: The Ottawa SAH clinical decision rule
1w123Q0.description: A validated set of clinical criteria used to rule out subarachnoid hemorrhage among selected patients presenting to the emergency department with acute severe nontraumatic headache.

media.title: Ottawa SAH rule for headache evaluation

dw1o3Q0.title: Patient dumping
dw1o3Q0.description: A practice in which hospitals/health care facilities or emergency departments fail to screen or treat and/or transfer patients due to lack of insurance or inability to pay for care (e.g., homeless and indigent patients).

Vw1G3Q0.title: Indigent patient
Vw1G3Q0.description: An individual who has exhausted federal social health care programs (e.g., Medicare,Medicaid), whose income is at or below the federal poverty line, and/or is not able to pay for health care.

ew1x3Q0.title: Congestive hepatopathy
ew1x3Q0.description: A condition that is characterized by increased pressure and impaired drainage in the hepatic veins, resulting in hypoxia and cell death of the hepatic parenchyma and, over time, leading to cirrhosis. The progression to cirrhosis as a result of right-sided heart failure is referred to as cardiac cirrhosis, which is sometimes erroneously used as a synonym for congestive hepatopathy.

media.title: Dilated inferior vena cava and hepatic veins in congestive hepatopathy

2w1TRQ0.title: Cerebral angiography
2w1TRQ0.description: A procedure used to detect and treat structural abnormalities in the blood vessels of the head, neck, and brain. Under fluoroscopy, a catheter is advanced into the common carotid artery via the femoral or brachial artery, and iodinated contrast is used to visualize the cerebrovascular system. Diagnostic findings include aneurysms, stenosis, thrombosis, atherosclerosis, and arteriovenous malformations or fistulas. Therapeutic uses include coil embolization, stenting, thrombolysis, and thrombectomy.

gw1FRQ0.title: Patient identification error
gw1FRQ0.description: An error that is the result of misidentification of a patient. Examples include administration of medications to the wrong patient, hemolytic transfusion reaction from major blood group incompatibility, and wrong patient surgery.

Sw1yRQ0.title: Device errors
Sw1yRQ0.description: A type of medical error. Further subdivided into user-associated device errors (e.g., incorrect use of equipment due to improper training or the use of unergonomic equipment) and device-associated device errors (e.g., the use of outdated or malfunctioning equipment).

hw1ciQ0.title: Monitoring errors
hw1ciQ0.description: A type of medical error associated with monitoring equipment (e.g., faulty telemetry) or medication monitoring (e.g., inadequate assessment of drug trough levels).

3w1SiQ0.title: Documentation errors
3w1SiQ0.description: A type of error associated with documentation of patient information (e.g., entering information in the wrong chart, using wrong abbreviations, improper documentation of allergies).

Rw1liQ0.title: Procedural errors
Rw1liQ0.description: A type of error associated with medical procedures (e.g., wrong-site surgery, transfusion of wrong blood product). Often due to failure to follow a protocol.

iw1JiQ0.title: Transition of care errors
iw1JiQ0.description: A type of medical error that can occur during patient transfer, handoff, or discharge. Examples include loss of vital information during handoff and discharge of a patient without booking necessary follow-up appointments. Measures of prevention include standardization of handoffs and discharge protocols.

Qw1uiQ0.title: Airborne transmission
Qw1uiQ0.description: The transmission of infection via the inhalation of pathogen-containing aerosolized droplet nuclei (< 5 µm in size), which can remain suspended in the air for prolonged periods of time. Is the most contagious form of infection transmission. Infections that can spread by airborne transmission include varicella, measles, disseminated herpes zoster, and tuberculosis. Certain activities (e.g., aerosol-generating health care procedures) can facilitate airborne transmission of infections that are not typically spread by airborne transmission.

jw1_iQ0.title: Posterior cervical lymphadenopathy
jw1_iQ0.description: A swelling of one or lymph nodes located in the posterior cervical lymph node chain (suboccipital lymph nodes, postauricular lymph nodes). Etiologies include malignancy, infection, inflammation in the scalp, neck, and/or upper thoracic region, and infections (e.g., rubella, roseola).

kw1mQQ0.title: Technetium-99m
kw1mQQ0.description: A radioactive tracer that can be used to visualize various structures in the body via a gamma camera. Studies that use this technique include bone scintigraphy, myocardial perfusion imaging, cholescintigraphy, and the Meckel scan.

Ow1IQQ0.title: Droplet transmission
Ow1IQQ0.description: The transmission of infection via the inhalation of pathogen-containing respiratory droplets that are > 5 µm in size and settle down within approx. 6 feet from the patient. Infections that can spread by droplet transmission include pertussis, pharyngeal diphtheria, rubella, mumps, parvovirus B19 infection, and adenovirus infection.

Nw1-QQ0.title: Cephalocaudal
Nw1-QQ0.description: A term that is used to describe the progression of an event or the orientation of a structure in the head-to-toe direction.

mw1VjQ0.title: Physician Quality Reporting System
mw1VjQ0.description: A reporting program created by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) and in use until superseded by the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) in 2017. PQRS gave health care professionals the opportunity to assess the quality of care they provided in order to ensure that patients received timely and appropriate care.

destinations.label: Health care system → Alternative payment models

Lw1wjQ0.title: Contact transmission
Lw1wjQ0.description: The transmission of infection via physical contact with an infected person (direct contact transmission) or with a fomite (indirect contact transmission). It is the most common form of infection transmission. Infections that can spread by contact transmission include rubella, mumps, certain skin infections (e.g., varicella, herpes, scabies), certain enteric infections (e.g., C. difficile, rotavirus), and certain viral pulmonary infections (e.g., parainfluenza).

pw1LPQ0.title: Urine immunoassay
pw1LPQ0.description: An antibody-based, enzymatic, qualitative test to detect certain drugs and metabolites in urine (e.g., tricyclic antidepressants except for clomipramine, illicit drugs).

Jw1sPQ0.title: Contagious period
Jw1sPQ0.description: The time interval in which an infected host can transmit the infection to a susceptible host.

rw1f4Q0.title: Wet wrap therapy
rw1f4Q0.description: An adjuvant therapy for chronic pruritic skin conditions (e.g., moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, psoriasis) in which a topical treatment (e.g., emollients, topical corticosteroids) is applied to the affected area directly (or into a moistened bandage), followed by a dry outer bandage.

7w144Q0.title: Noncommunicating hydrocele
7w144Q0.description: A collection of scrotal fluid that has no connection to the peritoneal cavity. May be idiopathic or secondary to an underlying pathology (e.g., trauma, tumor, torsion, infection).

Hw1K4Q0.title: CNS stimulants
Hw1K4Q0.description: A group of substances that increase the activity of the CNS. Typically result in increased alertness and energy, elevated mood, and enhanced sympathetic tone (e.g., elevated heart rate, blood pressure, breathing rate). Examples include caffeine, cocaine, amphetamines, and methamphetamines.

sw1t4Q0.title: CNS depressants
sw1t4Q0.description: A group of substances that depress the activity of the CNS and reduce sympathetic tone (i.e., decreased heart rate, blood pressure, and respiratory rate). CNS depressants include sedative-hypnotic drugs, e.g., barbiturates, benzodiazepines, Z-drugs, and GHB. Other substances, e.g., alcohol, opioids, antidepressants, antipsychotics, gabapentinoids, and certain antihistamines, have variable or dose-dependent CNS depressant effects.

Gw1B4Q0.title: Ulceroglandular tularemia
Gw1B4Q0.description: The most common form of tularemia (zoonotic infection caused by Francisella tularensis), which manifests with an ulcer and tender regional lymphadenopathy.

Fw1gkQ0.title: Lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis
Fw1gkQ0.description: The most common form of sporotrichosis (infection with Sporothrix schenckii), which involves ulcerous skin lesions, ascending lymphangitis, and associated nodules without systemic involvement. Usually affects immunocompetent individuals.

zw1rlQ0.title: Trauma-informed communication
zw1rlQ0.description: An approach to patient communication that acknowledges the impact that past traumatic events (e.g., sexual assault, natural disaster) may have on an individual. Aims to avoid triggering or exacerbating trauma symptoms during medical evaluation (e.g., history taking, physical examination).

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Trauma-informed communication

Z91ZNQ0.title: Counseling on weight management
Z91ZNQ0.description: A set of strategies for supporting patients interested in losing weight. Includes setting realistic goals, encouraging patients to monitor what they eat, engaging in stimulus control (e.g., buying fewer calorie-rich foods), encouraging regular weighing, providing nutritional education, encouraging patients to increase physical activity, and enhancing social support by including family members or friends.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Counseling on nutrition and regular exercise

c91amQ0.title: Flexible endoscopy
c91amQ0.description: A minimally invasive procedure performed by inserting a flexible, camera-equipped tube into a hollow organ (e.g., the gastrointestinal tract, upper airways). Can be used for inspection and/or treatment in many conditions, e.g., gastroesophageal reflux disease, peptic ulcers, colonic polyps, and foreign body aspiration.

1912mQ0.title: Rigid endoscopy
1912mQ0.description: A minimally invasive procedure performed by inserting a rigid, camera-equipped tube into a hollow organ, joint spaces, or body cavity. Can be used to biopsy abdominal organs, explore the thoracic cavity, or facilitate surgery (e.g., arthroscopic surgery).

W91PmQ0.title: Pigment network
W91PmQ0.description: A grid-like network of pigment visible on dermoscopy. Formed by melanocytes and melanin in basal keratinocytes.

d91omQ0.title: Dyspraxia
d91omQ0.description: A condition that reduces a person's ability to perform coordinated, purposeful, and/or learned movements when asked (e.g., combing one's hair, putting on shoes and socks), even though the request is understood. The complete loss of this ability is called apraxia.

V91GmQ0.title: Epimastigote
V91GmQ0.description: A morphologic stage of Hemoflagellate protozoa that occurs in an invertebrate host (vector). Morphologically resembles a trypomastigote but is smaller.

destinations.label: General parasitology → Tissue and blood protozoa

e91xmQ0.title: Promastigote
e91xmQ0.description: A morphologic stage of Hemoflagellate protozoa that occurs in an invertebrate host (vector). Morphologically resembles an epimastigote but does not have an undulating membrane.

destinations.label: General parasitology → Tissue and blood protozoa

Q91uMQ0.title: Behavioral emergency response team
Q91uMQ0.description: A multidisciplinary rapid response team that can be deployed anywhere in the hospital to provide immediate intervention in behavioral crises. Usually includes a psychiatry-trained clinician and security personnel as well as members from other relevant services (e.g., social worker or pastoral support). Although conventions vary, the call for this team is often "code white."

destinations.label: Approach to the agitated or violent patient → Management

j91_MQ0.title: Behavioral Activity Rating Scale
j91_MQ0.description:
A validated scoring tool used to evaluate a patient's level of agitation. 
Levels of agitation are categorized as follows:
1 = Unrousable or very difficult to arouse
2 = Asleep but rousable with normal verbal or physical stimulus
3 = Visibly sedate with lethargic or drowsy appearance
4 = Alert with a normal level of activity (verbal and physical)
5 = Noticeably increased activity; responds to verbal deescalation
6 = Significantly increased activity without the need for restraints
7 = Violent behavior that requires restraints

P91WnQ0.title: Medications for the treatment of agitation
P91WnQ0.description: A group of medications used to reduce anxiety and agitation, including agents from several drug classes such as benzodiazepines, antipsychotics, and dissociative anesthetics. These medications are also referred to as sedatives or tranquilizers.

destinations.label: Approach to the agitated or violent patient → Pharmacotherapy

k91mnQ0.title: Physical restraints
k91mnQ0.description: A set of methods, materials, devices, or equipment that impair or limit free movement of a patient's extremities, body, or head.

destinations.label: Approach to the agitated or violent patient → Physical restraints

N91-nQ0.title: Pelvic girdle pain
N91-nQ0.description: A condition characterized by pain of the sacroiliac joints and the symphysis pubis. Occurs commonly during pregnancy due to pressure from the uterus, increased lumbar lordosis, and relaxation of the pelvic ligaments due to hormonal changes.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Common discomforts during pregnancy

591iLQ0.title: Unintentional injury
591iLQ0.description: A broad term that encompasses injuries that are not caused on purpose or with the intent of causing harm to oneself or others.

p91LoQ0.title: Plasma derivative
p91LoQ0.description: A blood product that contains high concentrations of plasma proteins obtained from plasma from multiple donors (pooled plasma).
