Commonly used plasma derivatives include human albumin, coagulation factors (including PCC and aPCC), and immunoglobulins (e.g., tetanus immunoglobulin, anti-D Rhesus immunoglobulin).

r91fKQ0.title: Hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy
r91fKQ0.description: A treatment modality for peritoneal carcinomatosis. After cytoreductive surgery, during which all visible metastases are resected, the peritoneal cavity is irrigated intraoperatively with a warm chemotherapeutic agent, with the goal of destroying malignant cells while avoiding the systemic toxicity of chemotherapy.

destinations.label: Colorectal cancer → Treatment of colon cancer

7914KQ0.title: ASCVD risk-enhancing factors
7914KQ0.description: Parameters that can be used to upwardly revise the risk assessment for patients with borderline or intermediate ASCVD risk. Examples include premature ASCVD in a first-degree relative, chronic inflammatory conditions (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, HIV/AIDS), and metabolic syndrome. The presence of these factors may influence the decision to initiate or intensify statin treatment.

s91tKQ0.title: Significant coronary artery stenosis
s91tKQ0.description: Commonly defined as ≥ 50% narrowing of the left main coronary artery or ≥ 70% narrowing of other coronary arteries.

F91g6Q0.title: Supravital staining
F91g6Q0.description: A staining method that uses nontoxic dye solutions (e.g., crystal violet), which facilitates histologic examination of living cells.

891O6Q0.title: Wilkins score
891O6Q0.description: A score used to determine whether a patient with mitral valve stenosis is a candidate for percutaneous transmitral valve balloon commissurotomy (PMBC). Four parameters (leaflet thickening, leaflet mobility, leaflet calcification, and subvalvular anatomy) are evaluated using echocardiography and each is scored from 0 to 4. A total score of less than 8 indicates a favorable prognosis with PMBC.

media.title: Wilkins morphology score for mitral valve stenosis

w91hpQ0.title: Acute CPP crystal arthritis
w91hpQ0.description: The acute form of calcium pyrophosphate crystal deposition disease. Manifests similarly to an acute gout flare, with sporadic episodes of monoarticular synovitis affecting large joints. Unlike gout, it can last for months and may be associated with systemic symptoms.

destinations.label: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease → Clinical features

x91EpQ0.title: Fetal heart rate variability
x91EpQ0.description: The physiologic variation of the time interval between heartbeats. Represented on cardiotocography by the oscillation of the fetal heart rate (FHR) around its baseline. Determined by measuring the amplitude between the highest and lowest turning point of the FHR curve. Decreased or increased variability (< 6 bpm or > 25 bpm) may indicate fetal distress.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

media.title: Cardiotocogram (CTG) showing different types of FHR baseline variability

y91dJQ0.title: Delayed cerebral ischemia
y91dJQ0.description: A complication of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) defined as a worsening neurological status that cannot be attributed to other causes (e.g., hypoxemia or seizures). While it is associated with cerebral vasospasm, the exact pathophysiology is not known. Typically occurs 3 days to 2 weeks after SAH.

A91RJQ0.title: Reassuring fetal heart rate tracing
A91RJQ0.description: A fetal heart tracing that shows a good beat to beat variability (> 5 beats/minute), > 2 accelerations within a 20 minute period, and no evidence of fetal distress (e.g., fetal bradycardia, fetal tachycardia, late or variable decelerations, sinusoidal pattern). A reassuring tracing indicates fetal well-being.

_915JQ0.title: Bruce protocol
_915JQ0.description: The most common protocol used during treadmill cardiac exercise stress testing. It consists of seven 3-minute stages of increasing speed and incline.

-91DJQ0.title: Staphylococcal enterotoxin
-91DJQ0.description: A type of heat-stable superantigen produced by certain strains of Staphylococcus aureus that can cause food poisoning and toxic shock syndrome.

ZC1ZqQ0.title: Abacavir-related hypersensitivity syndrome
ZC1ZqQ0.description: A severe adverse effect of abacavir therapy that can develop in HLA-B*57:01-positive individuals. Manifestations include fever, maculopapular rash, constitutional symptoms (e.g., malaise headache), gastrointestinal symptoms, and pulmonary symptoms.

destinations.label: Human immunodeficiency virus infection → Antiretroviral therapy

0C1eqQ0.title: Safety data sheet
0C1eqQ0.description: A document summarizing the characteristics of a hazardous chemical substance and guidance for its handling, storage, and transport. Should be obtained by health workers for any patient with a known or suspected exposure. The US Occupational Safety and Health Administration mandates that a safety data sheet is provided by substance manufacturers and posted by employers in workplaces where the substance is used.

aC1QqQ0.title: Penetrating neck trauma
aC1QqQ0.description: A stab or gunshot injury to the neck.

bC1HqQ0.title: Round ligament pain
bC1HqQ0.description: A common pregnancy-associated condition characterized by sharp pain in the lower abdomen and groin area (most often right-sided) during the second and third trimester. Caused by stretching of the round ligament of the uterus as the uterus expands.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Common discomforts during pregnancy

cC1aIQ0.title: Metabolic equivalents of task
cC1aIQ0.description: Metabolic Equivalent of Task (MET) is a measure of energy expenditure for a particular physical activity. 1 MET = 3.5 mL O₂/kg/min; higher METs indicate greater activity intensity.

destinations.label: Coronary artery disease → Cardiac stress testing

hC1c7Q0.title: Sigmoid colectomy
hC1c7Q0.description: Removal of the sigmoid colon. Performed for malignant (e.g., colon cancer) as well as benign (e.g., sigmoid volvulus with bowel gangrene, diverticular disease) conditions primarily affecting the sigmoid colon.

4C13HQ0.title: Pulsed dye laser
4C13HQ0.description: A type of laser that produces pulses of visible light at a wavelength of 585 or 595 nm. Used to treat vascular skin conditions (e.g., port wine stains, telangiectasis, cherry angiomas) and nonvascular skin conditions (e.g., warts, angiofibromas).

OC1IHQ0.title: Baloxavir marboxil
OC1IHQ0.description: An antiviral drug used in the prophylaxis and treatment of influenza A and B. The drug inhibits the endonuclease activity of the viral RNA polymerase, thereby preventing viral replication.

destinations.label: Antiviral agents → Antivirals against influenza viruses

5C1isQ0.title: Acute procedural anxiety
5C1isQ0.description: A condition of fear related to health care procedures (e.g., medical, surgical, dental), which manifests with symptoms of anxiety and can take the form of a panic attack.

MC1MsQ0.title: X-ray features of right ventricular dilation
MC1MsQ0.description: A collection of features seen on chest x-ray in patients with right ventricular enlargement. Findings on the PA view include rounding of the mid-left heart border (secondary to the rotation of the heart) and a widening of the space between the left main bronchus and left heart border. On the lateral view, the retrosternal clear space is decreased and the heart border is displaced posteriorly toward the spine.

nC17sQ0.title: Respiratory event index
nC17sQ0.description: The number of apneas plus hypopneas with desaturation of ≥ 4%, usually measured by home sleep apnea testing.

LC1wsQ0.title: Portal cavernoma
LC1wsQ0.description: A cluster of portosystemic or portoportal collateral blood vessels that usually form in response to portal vein thrombosis to substitute blood flow. These vessels can cause bile duct compression and strictures, leading to portal cavernoma cholangiopathy.

pC1LGQ0.title: Pes planus
pC1LGQ0.description: A type of foot deformity characterized by the absence or reduction of the medial longitudinal arch while standing. May be a normal physiological variant in children, acquired in adults, or congenital.

7C14tQ0.title: Shine-Dalgarno sequence
7C14tQ0.description: A ribosomal binding site contained in prokaryotic mRNA. Enables the initiation of protein synthesis by aligning the start codon and ribosome.​​​​​​​ Generally located ∼ 8 bases upstream of the start codon.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

sC1ttQ0.title: Dermatophagoides farinae
sC1ttQ0.description: A mite species whose waste products (e.g., scales, feces, secretions) can cause allergic reactions.

GC1BtQ0.title: Lockout period
GC1BtQ0.description: The duration for which a forcing function prevents an event from happening. For example, in patient-controlled analgesia systems, no analgesics are administered to the patient for a predetermined duration after the last dose (typically 6–15 minutes) regardless of the number of times a new dose is requested (e.g., by pressing a button).

uC1pFQ0.title: N-acetylglutamate synthase deficiency
uC1pFQ0.description: A rare congenital disorder caused by partial or complete loss of N-acetylglutamate synthetase. Characterized by symptoms of hyperammonemia (e.g., nausea, vomiting, delayed growth).

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Urea cycle disorders

wC1h8Q0.title: Demodex spp.
wC1h8Q0.description: A mite species that colonizes human sebaceous glands and hair follicles (mainly on the forehead, nose, and eyelids) and feed on epithelial cells. Clinically significant species include Demodex folliculorum (primarily affects hair follicles) and Demodex brevis (primarily affects sebaceous glands).

9C1N8Q0.title: Demodicosis
9C1N8Q0.description: A condition caused by infestation with mites of the Demodex genus. Characterized by a rosacea-like eruption (erythematous papules and pustules) and commonly affects the cheeks and eyelids.

CC1q8Q0.title: Latrotoxin
CC1q8Q0.description: A venom produced by spiders of the genus Latrodectus (black widow spiders). Functions as a neurotoxin that causes pore formation in the neuronal membranes of axonal terminals, which results in massive release of neurotransmitters (acetylcholine, norepinephrine).

xC1E8Q0.title: Black widow spider envenomation
xC1E8Q0.description: A condition caused by envenomation by widow spiders (genus Latrodectus). Manifestations include localized pain and erythema at the bite site, muscle aches and/or rigidity, and in severe cases, systemic symptoms (e.g., tachypnea, diaphoresis, nausea).

BC1z8Q0.title: Subfebrile
BC1z8Q0.description: Slightly elevated body temperature that is not yet considered a fever; generally 37.5–38°C (or 99.5–100.4°F).

yC1duQ0.title: Calcaneal stress fracture
yC1duQ0.description: A bone fracture of the calcaneus caused by repetitive stress (e.g., overload, increase in physical activity). Manifestations include heel pain, swelling, and tenderness to palpation, particularly with compression of the posterior sides of the heel (positive calcaneal squeeze test).

AC1RuQ0.title: PF4 heparin immunoassay
AC1RuQ0.description: A group of quantitative serological tests that detect antibodies against heparin/platelet factor 4 (PF4) complexes in serum. Used in the workup of suspected heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. As these tests also detect clinically insignificant anti-heparin/PF4 antibodies in heparin-exposed patients (i.e., antibodies that do not activate platelets), a positive immunoassay typically requires confirmation with a functional platelet activation assay.

_C15uQ0.title: Functional platelet activation assay
_C15uQ0.description: A confirmatory test for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) performed if the initial immunoassay is positive. Measures clinically significant anti-heparin/PF4 antibodies (i.e., antibodies that cause platelet activation and thrombosis) in a patient's serum, as clinically insignificant antibodies may be present in heparin-exposed patients without HIT. It is not widely available and usually take several days until results are available.

zC1ruQ0.title: Heel pad syndrome
zC1ruQ0.description: A condition characterized by damage to the fatty and fibrous tissue in the heel due to acute trauma or repetitive overload. Typically results in deep, mid-heel pain that increases with activity and when walking on hard surfaces and tenderness in the mid-portion of the heel.

destinations.label: Collection of orthopedic conditions → Heel pad syndrome

-C1DuQ0.title: Calcaneal squeeze test
-C1DuQ0.description: A test performed by compressing the medial and lateral aspects of the heel between the thumb and index finger. Pain elicited by this maneuver distinguishes calcaneal stress fracture from the other causes of heel pain (e.g., plantar fascitis, tarsal tunnel syndrome, heel pad syndrome).

bx1HEQ0.title: Intralesional injection
bx1HEQ0.description: The direct delivery of medication into dermatologic lesions via percutaneous injection. Commonly injected drugs include corticosteroids and chemotherapeutic agents (e.g., bleomycin, fluorouracil, methotrexate).

Xx19EQ0.title: Guideline-directed medical therapy
Xx19EQ0.description: The stepwise use of evidence-based clinical evaluation, diagnostic studies, medication, and procedures to manage heart failure.

1x12vQ0.title: Prediction of alcohol withdrawal severity scale
1x12vQ0.description: A score used in patients hospitalized for alcohol withdrawal to predict the risk of developing complications (e.g., alcohol withdrawal seizures, alcohol withdrawal psychotic disorder, alcohol withdrawal delirium). Includes historical information (e.g., prior alcohol withdrawal syndrome), clinical manifestations (e.g., autonomic hyperactivity), and blood alcohol concentration.

destinations.label: Alcohol withdrawal → Risk and severity-based management

ex1xvQ0.title: SBS
ex1xvQ0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Shaken baby syndrome
2. Short bowel syndrome
3. Sphenobasilar synchondrosis

Ux1bDQ0.title: Malleus
Ux1bDQ0.description: The most lateral ossicle of the middle ear. Located between the tympanic membrane and the incus. Consists of a head, neck, manubrium, and anterior and lateral processes.

2x1TDQ0.title: Stapes
2x1TDQ0.description: The most medial and smallest ossicle of the middle ear. Consists of a head, neck, crura, and base (which articulates with the oval window).

fx1kDQ0.title: Incus
fx1kDQ0.description: The middle of the three ossicles of the middle ear. Articulates anteromedially with the malleus and inferomedially with the stapes. Consists of a body, long crus, short crus, and lenticular process.

Tx16DQ0.title: Accessory ossicle
Tx16DQ0.description: A secondary ossification center seen in association with adjacent bones. Usually congenital but can develop secondary to trauma or degenerative disease. Can be seen in the shoulder, elbow, spine, wrist, hip, knee, and feet.

gx1FDQ0.title: 2013 ACC/AHA pooled cohort equations
gx1FDQ0.description: Equations used to predict the occurrence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in patients with no history of ASCVD, based on the presence of traditional ASCVD risk factors. The reported ASCVD risk percentage can help guide patient counseling and therapeutic decisions (e.g., antiplatelet therapy, cholesterol and blood pressure management).

media.title: ASCVD risk calculator (2013 ACC/AHA pooled cohort equations)

Sx1yDQ0.title: Traditional ASCVD risk factors
Sx1yDQ0.description: A set of factors used to estimate an individual's 10-year and lifetime risk of ASCVD. Includes demographics (i.e., age, race, ethnicity, sex), patient history (i.e., smoking status, diabetes mellitus, antihypertensive use), and clinical information (i.e., systolic blood pressure, total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol).

3x1SwQ0.title: Survival to discharge
3x1SwQ0.description: An admitted patient's likelihood of surviving to be discharged from hospital. Typically used for patients who have had a cardiac arrest and is often contrasted with immediate survival (the likelihood of obtaining a return of spontaneous circulation). Survival to discharge includes patients discharged to other long-term care facilities such as rehabilitation centers or extended care facilities.

ix1JwQ0.title: Neutropenic enterocolitis
ix1JwQ0.description: A form of necrotizing inflammation typically involving the cecum that occurs in individuals with neutropenia. Manifestations include fever, abdominal pain, watery or bloody diarrhea, vomiting, and, on CT scan, bowel wall thickening and mesenteric stranding.

Qx1uwQ0.title: Uncrossmatched blood transfusion
Qx1uwQ0.description: The provision of red blood cell units for emergency transfusion without performing pretransfusion crossmatching. Usually performed in life-threatening situations when the benefits of transfusion outweigh the risks of potential transfusion reactions.

kx1m9Q0.title: RDI
kx1m9Q0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:

1. Respiratory disturbance index
2. Recommended daily intake
3. Recommended dietary intake

Ox1I9Q0.title: Allied health
Ox1I9Q0.description: A group of health care professionals that does not include licensed nurses or physicians. May include audiologists, therapists (speech and language pathologists, occupational therapists, physical therapists, respiratory therapists), nutritionists, dietitians, and other health professionals depending on the country and jurisdiction.

Nx1-9Q0.title: Infestation
Nx1-9Q0.description: A parasitic disease caused by the attack of a large number of ectoparasites. Sometimes also used to describe severe helminthic disease.

6x1jxQ0.title: Cutaneous angiosarcoma
6x1jxQ0.description: A rare, vascular, malignant tumor of soft tissue that most commonly develops on the head, neck, or breasts. Associated with radiation therapy and chronic lymphedema.

px1LxQ0.title: Angiosarcoma
px1LxQ0.description: A rare malignant tumor arising from vascular or lymphatic endothelium. Common subtypes include cutaneous angiosarcoma, breast angiosarcoma, and hepatic angiosarcoma.

Jx1sxQ0.title: BAL
Jx1sxQ0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Bronchoalveolar lavage
2. British anti-Lewisite
3. Blood alcohol level

Ix1YBQ0.title: Transport host
Ix1YBQ0.description: A host that mechanically transports a parasite from one host to another. The parasite does not need it for passing any stage of its development.

rx1fBQ0.title: BPD
rx1fBQ0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Bronchopulmonary dysplasia
2. Borderline personality disorder
3. Bipolar disorder
4. Biparietal diameter

7x14BQ0.title: Transvaginal apical suspension
7x14BQ0.description: A suspension technique used in patients with pelvic organ prolapse in which the vaginal vault is surgically attached to the surrounding structures (e.g., sacrospinous, uterosacral ligaments) to prevent recurrent prolapse. Can also be combined with hysterectomy.

Hx1KBQ0.title: Colporrhaphy
Hx1KBQ0.description: A minimally invasive surgical procedure used to treat pelvic organ prolapse (most commonly cystocele or rectocele). The anterior or posterior vaginal walls are sutured to the adjacent tissue to provide better structural support for the bladder or rectum, respectively.

sx1tBQ0.title: Engraftment syndrome
sx1tBQ0.description: A clinical syndrome that is characterized by fever, rash, diarrhea and/or, in more severe cases, organ dysfunction. Thought to be mediated by the rapid release of proinflammatory cytokines, products of neutrophil degranulation, and oxidative metabolism within the first 3–4 days of engraftment.

Gx1BBQ0.title: Rasmussen encephalitis
Gx1BBQ0.description: A chronic inflammatory brain condition of unknown origin that affects one hemisphere. Pathological features include an initial lymphocytic infiltration and acute inflammation that progresses to parenchymal atrophy. Clinically characterized by treatment-refractory focal epileptic seizures, of which epilepsia partialis continua (a long-lasting focal status epilepticus) is one of the most common types. Treated with methylprednisolone pulse therapy and intravenous immunoglobulin; hemispherectomy is used in refractory cases.

tx1XyQ0.title: Clinical features of cystic fibrosis
tx1XyQ0.description: The signs and symptoms that may be present in patients with cystic fibrosis. Infants may present with meconium ileus, failure to thrive, prolonged jaundice, and salt wasting. Older patients may present with respiratory symptoms (e.g., recurrent infections, nasal polyps), gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g., steatorrhea, recurrent pancreatitis), and/or infertility (e.g., azoospermia, congenital absence of vas deferens in males).

Fx1gyQ0.title: Sleep arousal
Fx1gyQ0.description: A term used to describe the transition from a deep sleep stage to a lighter sleep stage, or a sleep state to a wake state (awakening). Arousal in the context of sleep studies is usually defined using EEG and EMG criteria, such as the return to alpha or theta waves for a certain period of time, which is often associated with increased EMG tone.

Ex18yQ0.title: Hypoglossal nerve stimulation
Ex18yQ0.description: A procedure for treating obstructive sleep apnea that involves implantation of a pacing device that modulates the genioglossus muscle and thereby reduces airway collapsibility.

vx1AyQ0.title: High-intensity statin therapy
vx1AyQ0.description: A statin dosage that is expected to reduce LDL by ≥ 50%. Examples include 20–40 mg of rosuvastatin or 40–80 mg atorvastatin daily.

wx1hAQ0.title: Palatal implant
wx1hAQ0.description: A type of malleable rod that is implanted into the soft palate, which causes local fibrosis and leads to stiffening of the soft palate. This is thought to be beneficial in preventing the collapse of the upper airways during sleep and can be a treatment option in obstructive sleep apnea or snoring.

9x1NAQ0.title: Acute hyperventilation syndrome
9x1NAQ0.description: The acute onset of dyspnea, tachypnea, and agitation. Can progress to chest pain, syncope, paresthesias, and tetany secondary to respiratory alkalosis, causing hypocalcemia and hypophosphatemia. Often triggered by emotionally stressful events.

Cx1qAQ0.title: STOP-BANG questionnaire
Cx1qAQ0.description: A questionnaire used to screen patients with suspected obstructive sleep apnea based on risk factors and clinical features. Each item present receives 1 point, with a higher score indicating an increased risk of OSA. The name of the questionnaire is a mnemonic to remember the items: S – Snoring loudly, T – feeling Tired or fatigued, O – Observed apneas during sleep, P – high blood Pressure, B – BMI > 35, A – Age > 50 years, N – Neck circumference > 40 cm, G – male Gender.

media.title: STOP-BANG Score for Obstructive Sleep Apnea

Bx1zAQ0.title: Positive myoclonus
Bx1zAQ0.description: An involuntary muscle twitch caused by a contraction of muscle fibers. Seen in metabolic encephalopathies, epilepsy, and traumatic brain injury.

yx1d_Q0.title: Negative myoclonus
yx1d_Q0.description: A brief loss of muscle activity during tonic contraction. Seen in metabolic encephalopathies (e.g., hepatic encephalopathy) and epilepsy.

Ax1R_Q0.title: Log roll maneuver
Ax1R_Q0.description: A maneuver used to reposition patients between the supine and lateral decubitus positions while maintaining spinal immobilization. Helpful for posterior body examination, preventing aspiration during emesis, and for transfers (e.g., off stretchers). Requires synchronized movement of multiple trained health providers, with at least one provider maintaining in-line stabilization of the head and neck, while others secure the limbs and support the patient's weight.

media.title: Log roll maneuver with spinal motion restrictions

_x15_Q0.title: Sympathomimetic toxidrome
_x15_Q0.description: A term used to refer to signs and symptoms resulting from the toxic effects of sympathomimetic agents (e.g., pseudoephedrine, amphetamines, caffeine, cocaine, theophylline). These include tachycardia, hypertension, mydriasis, agitation, confusion, sweating, psychosis, and seizures.

destinations.label: Stimulant intoxication and withdrawal → Stimulant intoxication

zx1r_Q0.title: Reflex seizure
zx1r_Q0.description: A seizure that is consistently provoked by a certain factor (e.g., flashing lights, hyperventilation).

-x1D_Q0.title: Sleep study
-x1D_Q0.description:
A test that examines physiologic variables during sleep to diagnose sleep-related conditions, e.g., sleep-related breathing disorders or nocturnal seizures. The number and type of variables assessed depend on the type of test. 
Examples include in-laboratory polysomnography and out-of-center sleep testing for obstructive sleep apnea.

ZB1ZzQ0.title: Patient-clinician relationship
ZB1ZzQ0.description: A relationship that is entered into by mutual consent between a patient (or surrogate) and a clinician. In this relationship, the clinician has a fiduciary responsibility to the patient. The relationship can be terminated by the clinician only after giving advanced notification to the patient (or surrogate) and by facilitating transfer of care but can be terminated by the patient (or surrogate) at any time. Limited patient-clinician relationships, which last only for a certain duration, can be established without the patient's (or surrogate's) consent in certain circumstances (e.g., in emergencies, care for prisoners under court order).

destinations.label: Challenging clinical and ethical scenarios → Patient-clinician relationships
Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

0B1ezQ0.title: Open-ended question
0B1ezQ0.description: A question that cannot be answered with a one-word response, such as "yes" or "no". They are used in communication when a descriptive answer is required and/or to encourage discussion.

YB1nzQ0.title: Sleep-related hypoxemia disorder
YB1nzQ0.description: A group of sleep-related breathing disorders characterized by hypoxemia during sleep (SpO2 ≤ 88% for > 5 minutes) without a concomitant rise in PaCO2.

bB1HzQ0.title: Intestinal current measurement
bB1HzQ0.description: A highly specialized physiologic test of CFTR dysfunction that is rarely used during the diagnosis of cystic fibrosis (CF). It indirectly assesses Cl- movement by measuring the potential difference across biopsied rectal tissue in response to immersion in standardized solutions. It is typically performed if other diagnostic tests for CF, e.g., sweat test and genetic testing, are inconclusive.

1B12-Q0.title: Tracheobronchial secretions
1B12-Q0.description: A substance produced by the tracheobronchial mucous glands. Consists of 99% water and 1% protein, lipid, carbohydrate, and inorganic material. Tracheobronchial secretions play a role in the immune defense and in water and heat exchange of the respiratory tract. Production is increased during infections or irritation.

WB1P-Q0.title: Medium-intensity statin therapy
WB1P-Q0.description: A statin dosage that is expected to reduce LDL by 30–49%. Examples include 5–10 mg of rosuvastatin or 10–20 mg atorvastatin daily.

dB1o-Q0.title: Low-dose aspirin therapy
dB1o-Q0.description: A daily aspirin dose of 75–100 mg. Used for primary and secondary prevention (e.g., of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, recurrent pregnancy loss due to preeclampsia).

UB1bZj0.title: Photoepilation
UB1bZj0.description: The use of laser or intense pulsed light therapy to remove hair via selective photothermolysis.

fB1kZj0.title: Cystic fibrosis-related diabetes
fB1kZj0.description: A condition often seen in patients with cystic fibrosis (CF) and concomitant pancreatic insufficiency. Progressive pancreatic fibrosis leads to the destruction of insulin-producing islet cells of the endocrine pancreas and insulin deficiency, which results in diabetes mellitus.

TB16Zj0.title: Cystic fibrosis-related liver disease
TB16Zj0.description: A multifactorial condition affecting hepatic function that is often seen in patients with cystic fibrosis (CF) and concomitant pancreatic insufficiency. The combination of cholestasis, steatosis, and hepatic congestion leads to progressive biliary fibrosis and cirrhosis. CFLD is associated with a poor prognosis and decreased life expectancy in patients with CF.

gB1FZj0.title: Dornase alfa
gB1FZj0.description: A recombinant form of DNase that breaks down extracellular DNA in sputum, thereby reducing its viscosity and increasing mucociliary clearance; used in cystic fibrosis.

SB1yZj0.title: Laryngeal amyloidosis
SB1yZj0.description: A localized form of amyloidosis that only involves the larynx. Manifestations include hoarseness, globus sensation, hemoptysis, stridor, and dyspnea. Laryngoscopy typically shows a firm, orange-yellow to gray epithelial nodule on a vocal cord.

kB1maj0.title: Coronary artery spasm
kB1maj0.description: Sudden vasoconstriction in one of the coronary arteries, which causes complete or near-complete narrowing of the vessel, reducing the blood supply to the heart.

destinations.label: Chronic coronary disease → Ischemia with nonobstructive coronary arteries (INOCA)

lB1vaj0.title: Unprovoked seizures
lB1vaj0.description: Seizures that are not triggered by an acute event (e.g., stroke, trauma, acute intoxication) or occur beyond a specified time after the event.

mB1VYj0.title: Resource stewardship
mB1VYj0.description: The concept of managing the distribution of limited health care resources in order to avoid unnecessary tests and treatments. Strategies include allocating resources to those who need them the most and identifying interventions that result in harm and/or waste.

5B1iYj0.title: Dose dumping
5B1iYj0.description: A phenomenon in which toxicity is observed due to a rapid release of the entire dose or a significant fraction of a drug into the systemic circulation in a short period of time. Can occur when modified-release medications are crushed, which results in the release of the full dose within a tablet or capsule.

nB17Yj0.title: Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System
nB17Yj0.description: A standardized method of reporting the results of coronary CT angiography. It reports the degree of plaque or stenosis on a scale from 0 (no plaque or stenosis) to 5 (100% occlusion).

LB1wYj0.title: Three-vessel coronary artery disease
LB1wYj0.description: A form of coronary artery disease involving stenosis of all three major coronary arteries, i.e., the left anterior descending artery, the left circumflex artery, and the right coronary artery.

oB10bj0.title: Stable coronary artery disease
oB10bj0.description: A nonacute form of ischemic heart disease that causes reversible myocardial ischemia. Often used synonymously with “chronic coronary disease."

pB1Lbj0.title: Professional misconduct
pB1Lbj0.description: A willfully unethical behavior or action by a health care provider. Examples include bullying, physician self-referral, sexual harassment of colleagues or patients, and billing fraud.

destinations.label: Medical professionalism and codes of conduct → Malpractice, misconduct, and physician impairment

DB111j0.title: Chiasmal syndrome
DB111j0.description: Triad of bitemporal visual field defects, unilateral or bilateral reduction in visual acuity, and optic atrophy.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Damage in the region of the optic chiasm

9B1N1j0.title: Closed-loop bowel obstruction
9B1N1j0.description: A type of mechanical bowel obstruction in which the proximal and distal ends of the obstructed loop are closed (e.g., volvulus, obstructed inguinal hernia, obstructing colon cancer with a competent ileocecal valve). Closed-loop bowel obstruction can rapidly lead to ischemia and perforation and typically necessitates surgical intervention.

xB1E1j0.title: Preventable adverse event
xB1E1j0.description: Any adverse event that could have been prevented by observing common rules of safety and error prevention.

BB1z1j0.title: Stroke mimic
BB1z1j0.description: A group of conditions that can cause neurological deficits similar to those of acute ischemic stroke. Stroke mimics include brain tumors, postictal states, migraines, and sepsis. Toxic or metabolic causes (e.g., hypoglycemia) can also mimic stroke.

yB1dWj0.title: Huff coughing
yB1dWj0.description: An airway clearance technique used in certain medical conditions, e.g., bronchiectasis, cystic fibrosis, COPD, that helps to mobilize mucus. It is a type of controlled coughing that combines deep breathing, forceful exhalations, and diaphragmatic breathing.

AB1RWj0.title: Airway protective reflexes
AB1RWj0.description: A group of mechanisms that prevent aspiration into the lower respiratory tract. Examples include the gag reflex, cough reflex, coordinated deglutition reflexes, and glottic closure reflexes. Impairment of these mechanisms can occur due to damage to these reflex pathways or impaired consciousness.

_B15Wj0.title: Spontaneous ventilatory mode
_B15Wj0.description: A setting of the mechanical ventilator in which each breath is initiated by the patient and ventilatory support is synchronized with the patient's own respiratory efforts. Benefits of this setting include low risk of barotrauma, prevention of respiratory muscle atrophy, and decreased need for sedation or paralysis.

zB1rWj0.title: Endotracheal tube cuff
zB1rWj0.description: An inflatable balloon at the end of the endotracheal tube. When inflated, it forms an airway seal within the trachea.

-B1DWj0.title: Ventilator circuit
-B1DWj0.description: The collection of tubing that connects a patient's airway device (e.g., endotracheal tube, tracheostomy tube) to a ventilator and the devices that are connected to this tubing (e.g., heaters, humidifiers, nebulizers, inhalers, filters, suction catheters).

Zy1Zdj0.title: Sedation assessment tool
Zy1Zdj0.description: A tool that is used to assess and titrate the depth of sedation for patients who are mechanically ventilated. Examples include the Richmond agitation-sedation scale and Riker sedation-agitation scale for adults and the COMFORT scale for children.

0y1edj0.title: X-ray findings of left atrial enlargement
0y1edj0.description: A series of features seen on PA or AP chest x-ray that suggest left atrial enlargement. These features include a double right heart border (double density sign), an extra bump on the left cardiac border below the left bronchus from enlargement of the left atrial appendage (third mogul sign), a widened carinal angle (> 90°), and a raised left mainstem bronchus.

ay1Qdj0.title: Interprofessional team
ay1Qdj0.description: A team of individuals with different professional backgrounds or specialities (e.g., a nurse, a physical therapist, and a physician; a surgeon, an anesthesiologist, and a radiologist) who collaborate toward a common goal.

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Teamwork and mutual support

cy1aVj0.title: Spinal precautions
cy1aVj0.description: A set of measures and devices to minimize movement of the spine in order to reduce the risk of causing or worsening spinal cord injury. Used in patients with suspected or known spinal cord injury as well as those at risk, e.g., patients with known or suspected unstable spinal fractures. Measures include cervical immobilization with a collar and blocks, use of a backboard or vacuum mattress, and keeping patients immobilized when moving them (logrolling).

Vy1GVj0.title: SBAR tool
Vy1GVj0.description: A communication tool to assist transfers of patient care between health providers (e.g., handoff, consults) that summarizes the following: Situation (reasons for discussing the patient), Background (relevant patient history), Assessment (evaluation of health status), and Recommendations (for further management). A variant of this tool (ISBAR) systematically includes Identification (of the provider and the patient) in addition to the SBAR components.

Ry1lUj0.title: Ask-tell-ask
Ry1lUj0.description: A communication strategy that is considered a key element of patient-centered communication. It involves asking an open-ended question to establish the patient's current baseline knowledge or particular concern (ask), providing relevant information in response (tell), and checking in again to see if the information was clearly understood (ask). May be used in repeated cycles throughout a conversation with a patient.

ly1v2j0.title: Errors in dispensation
ly1v2j0.description: A medication error associated with drug dispensation that is often caused by errors related to medications with similar names and/or appearances. Examples include dispensing an incorrect medication or dosage and miscalculating a dose.

Gy1Bgj0.title: Variation management
Gy1Bgj0.description: An area of improvement science that emphasizes the optimization and understanding of processes and systems in order to improve health care quality. Typically addresses teams, leadership positions, processes within the system, and overall culture.

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

uy1pSj0.title: High reliability organizations
uy1pSj0.description: Organizations that consistently experience fewer accidents or harmful events than anticipated and managed to avoid serious accidents or catastrophes despite operating in complex, high-risk environments.

yy1d3j0.title: Merit-based Incentive Payment System
yy1d3j0.description: A performance-based incentive program implemented by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) in 2017 that offers payments to eligible health care providers for high-quality and cost-effective care; aimed at improving overall health care quality, reducing costs, and increasing the use of appropriate health care information.

destinations.label: Health care system → Alternative payment models

Ay1R3j0.title: Axial spondyloarthritis
Ay1R3j0.description: A form of chronic inflammatory arthritis that affects the axial skeleton. Affected individuals are commonly positive for HLA-B27 and may also have extraarticular manifestations such as anterior uveitis, inflammatory bowel disease, and entheses. Axial spondyloarthritis can be divided into radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (also known as ankylosing spondylitis) and nonradiographic axial spondyloarthritis.

_y153j0.title: Value-based Payment Modifier program
_y153j0.description: A pay-for-performance program that provides payment adjustments to clinicians and independent practitioners based on the quality and cost-effectiveness of care delivered.

zy1r3j0.title: Nonradiographic axial spondyloarthritis
zy1r3j0.description: A subtype of axial spondyloarthritis. Patients experience symptoms of inflammatory back pain and sacroiliitis, but no pathological changes are visible on plain radiographs. Sacroiliitis is typically seen on MRI. Up to 30% of affected individuals progress to radiographic axial spondyloarthritis within 10 years of diagnosis.

-y1D3j0.title: Medicare Electronic Health Record Incentive Program
-y1D3j0.description: An incentive program that provides payments for eligible health care providers who use electronic health records (EHR) technology in ways that can positively impact patient care.

destinations.label: Health care system → Alternative payment models

XA19Rj0.title: Sensitive physical examination
XA19Rj0.description: A clinical evaluation (e.g., inspection, palpation, and/or use of instruments) that involves or exposes body parts considered sensitive by the patient. These body parts are typically the breasts, genitals, and anorectal region, but can also include near-sensitive body parts (e.g., groin, buttocks) or exposure of undergarments. The presence of a chaperone is recommended and should be offered to patients prior to the examination.

eA1xij0.title: Clinician burnout
eA1xij0.description: A type of burnout syndrome that occurs in health care providers. Symptoms of emotional exhaustion, detachment, and reduced job satisfaction and/or productivity can manifest in health care providers as cynicism, viewing patients as objects or medical conditions, difficulty focusing and taking longer to complete tasks, and/or persistent exhaustion despite appropriate periods of rest.

destinations.label: Life outside of the hospital → Mental health considerations

UA1bQj0.title: Caregiver burnout
UA1bQj0.description: A type of burnout syndrome in long-term informal caregivers (e.g., family members or friends) that is caused by stress from the demands of caretaking. Signs of caregiver burnout include emotional and/or physical exhaustion, difficulty concentrating, and anger towards or emotional detachment from the person in their care.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling →  Counseling on caregiver burnout

2A1TQj0.title: Six Sigma
2A1TQj0.description: A data-driven quality-control methodology for reducing variation and defect rates while improving cycle times utilizing statistical analyses. "Six sigma" stands for the aim of producing errors/defects/variations at a rate of less than 3.4 per million events/units/cycles ("sigma" stands for "standard deviation," and 3.4:1,000,000 is the mean for a six-standard-deviation event.

fA1kQj0.title: Chart rounds
fA1kQj0.description: A type of rounding in which the medical team first discusses the patient's status and care plans in an office space before going to bedside to communicate directly with the patient.

TA16Qj0.title: Modified traditional rounds
TA16Qj0.description: A type of rounding in which the medical team discusses a patient's status and care plans outside the patient's room (e.g., in the hallway) before approaching the bedside to communicate directly with them.

NA1-Pj0.title: Common cause variation
NA1-Pj0.description: A term that refers to the expected random variation in the performance metrics of a process or system, for which many factors are simultaneously responsible. Data points attributable to common cause variation fall within the upper and lower control limits of a control chart.

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

mA1V4j0.title: Special cause variation
mA1V4j0.description: A term that refers to unexpected variations in a process. Typically, there is a specific attributable reason, referred to as the assignable cause. On a control chart, data points attributable to special cause variation fall outside the upper or lower control limits or create specific patterns (e.g., trends, mixtures, stratification, shifts, over-control).

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

LA1w4j0.title: Time out
LA1w4j0.description: A pause before initiation of a medical procedure in which all team members confirm the identity of the patient and the nature and site of the procedure.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medical errors

pA1Lkj0.title: CUS statement
pA1Lkj0.description: A stepwise model for reporting safety concerns in a manner that does not challenge another individual’s authority. Includes stating that one is concerned (C), escalating to state that one is uncomfortable (U) if their concern was not heard, and then escalating to state that there is a relevant safety issue (S) if necessary.

7A14Oj0.title: Situational awareness
7A14Oj0.description: An individual's perception of their environment, understanding of its implications, and anticipation of its future. A high level of situational awareness among a team improves patient safety and reduces medical errors.

sA1tOj0.title: Mandatory ventilation mode
sA1tOj0.description: A setting of the mechanical ventilator in which the level of ventilatory support is preset by the health care provider independent of the patient's respiratory effort. Helpful for patients whose respiratory drive and/or musculature are impaired. May require sedation to prevent patient-ventilator dyssynchrony.

GA1BOj0.title: Refractory ascites
GA1BOj0.description: Ascites that does not respond to treatment or recurs after therapeutic paracentesis despite dietary sodium restriction and high-dose diuretic therapy.

uA1plj0.title: Bedside rounding
uA1plj0.description: A type of rounding in which all discussions about the patient's status and care plans occur at the bedside. Includes patient-centered rounding, family-centered rounding, and traditional rounding.

EA18lj0.title: Skin tenting
EA18lj0.description: In severe volume depletion, a sign in which skin remains in a "tented" position after pinching to evaluate skin turgor. In fractures, a sign in which fracture fragments cause the skin to protrude outward.

vA1Alj0.title: Skin turgor
vA1Alj0.description: A clinical marker of extracellular volume status. Assessed by measuring skin elasticity after pinching. In healthy patients, the skin returns to a normal position almost immediately. Turgor is reduced if the skin remains "tented" for longer. This finding often correlates with interstitial fluid loss, however, it less reliable in people with reduced or defective elastin (e.g., older adults, patients with Marfan syndrome).

DA11Nj0.title: Subcutaneous fluid therapy
DA11Nj0.description: A form of parenteral fluid therapy administration in which fluids are infused subcutaneously (typically into the upper back between the scapula, abdomen, thigh, or arm) and then slowly absorb into the intravascular compartment. Provides a therapeutic alternative in mild to moderate fluid loss if patients cannot tolerate oral fluids and IV access is unsuitable or unavailable.

destinations.label: Dehydration and hypovolemia → Initial fluid therapy for dehydration and hypovolemia

wA1hNj0.title: Drug-resistant epilepsy
wA1hNj0.description: Epilepsy in which at least two antiseizure medications, given in adequate dosages either as monotherapy or combination therapy, have failed to prevent seizures.

CA1qNj0.title: High-resolution computed tomography
CA1qNj0.description: A noncontrast CT imaging technique that produces high-resolution images. Most commonly used to assess diseases affecting lung parenchyma and airways (e.g., interstitial lung disease, bronchiectasis).

-A1Dmj0.title: Resolved epilepsy
-A1Dmj0.description: Absence of seizures in an individual with epilepsy who either has an age-dependent syndrome (e.g., childhood absence epilepsy) and is now past the applicable age or is seizure-free for at least 10 years without receiving antiseizure medications for at least the last 5 years.

Y_1n5j0.title: CAD
Y_1n5j0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Coronary artery disease
2. Cold agglutinin disease
3. Carotid artery dissection

X_195j0.title: Interictal
X_195j0.description: Term used to characterize events, clinical signs, and EEG features that take place between seizures.

R_1lLj0.title: Tiebreaker test
R_1lLj0.description: An additional test that is performed when there is a discordance between the results of two previously performed tests. An example of a tiebreaker test in a serial testing strategy is to perform an HIV nucleic acid amplification test if a patient has a positive HIV-1/2 combination immunoassay and a subsequently negative or indeterminate HIV-1/HIV-2 antibody differentiation assay.

i_1JLj0.title: Serial testing strategy
i_1JLj0.description: A testing algorithm in which the combination of positive results from serially performed unique tests is required to diagnose a disease or perform subsequent management. Increases the positive predictive value of the testing algorithm and efficiency of resource utilization. Usually, the initial test has higher sensitivity, and the subsequent test(s) have higher specificity. An example is the use of a nontreponemal test followed by a treponemal test for the diagnosis of syphilis.

Q_1uLj0.title: Parallel testing strategy
Q_1uLj0.description: A testing algorithm in which one positive result from simultaneously performed unique tests is sufficient to diagnose a disease or perform subsequent management. Increases the negative predictive value of the testing algorithm, decreases the efficiency of resource utilization, and increases the risk of unnecessary follow-up tests. Often used in the early phase of diagnostic workup or for clinically urgent situations.

j_1_Lj0.title: HIV-1/HIV-2 antibody differentiation immunoassay
j_1_Lj0.description: A supplemental test in the serial testing algorithm for the diagnosis of HIV infection. Performed if the patient has has a positive HIV-1/2 combination immunoassay. Can distinguish between infections by HIV-1 and HIV-2.

P_1Woj0.title: Laboratory error
P_1Woj0.description: A medical error that occurs at any stage from the ordering of the test to the reporting and interpretation of the test result. An important cause of diagnostic errors. Can be classified into preanalytical phase errors (e.g., misplaced order, ordering the inappropriate test, improper specimen collection, storage, or transport, incorrect patient-specimen identification), analytical phase errors (e.g., equipment malfunction, reagent contamination, calibration drift), and postanalytical phase errors (e.g., transcribing error, prolonged turnaround time).

4_13oj0.title: Agitation
4_13oj0.description: A state of heightened arousal that can manifest in a variety of ways, from subtle psychomotor agitation to aggressive and/or violent behavior. May be caused by a psychiatric disorder, substance use, or occur as a result of a general medical condition, e.g., hypoglycemia or traumatic brain injury.

destinations.label: Approach to the agitated or violent patient → Definitions

k_1moj0.title: Continuous renal replacement therapy
k_1moj0.description: A form of extracorporeal renal replacement therapy that provides a slower solute clearance and ultrafiltration over a longer period of time than intermittent hemodialysis. Often used for critically ill patients who meet criteria for hemodialysis (e.g., intractable fluid overload) but cannot tolerate other treatment modalities due to hemodynamic instability. May also be initiated for patients with persistent or worsening acute kidney injury in the absence of other hemodialysis criteria.

destinations.label: Renal replacement therapy → Hemodialysis and hemofiltration

O_1Ioj0.title: Distributive injustice
O_1Ioj0.description: A type of social injustice that is the result of inequitable distribution of resources. In health care settings, this type of injustice can result in disparities in health care outcomes.

destinations.label: Health care system → Social aspects of health care

N_1-oj0.title: Defibrotide
N_1-oj0.description: A medication used to treat hepatic venoocclusive disease after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Consists of a mixture of single-stranded oligonucleotides, which bind to the endothelium of small vessels and have local antiinflammatory, antiischemic, and antithrombotic effects (e.g., by stimulating fibrinolysis and reducing thrombin generation).

5_1iKj0.title: IPASS
5_1iKj0.description: A comprehensive handoff program that trains clinicians to exchange patient information concisely. The initials stand for illness severity, patient summary, action list, situational awareness and contingency plans, and synthesis by the receiver.

destinations.label: Daily life of the intern → Signouts

n_17Kj0.title: Metrics (quality improvement)
n_17Kj0.description: A quantitative standard used to evaluate performance quality and monitor improvement. Examples in health care include the percentage of patients in a clinic with a hemoglobin A1C under 8% (as a metric for diabetes care) and the number of hours a patient waits in the emergency room on average (as a metric for system efficiency).

J_1s6j0.title: Erythrocytapheresis
J_1s6j0.description: A process in which RBCs are separated from whole blood. Can be used to isolate RBCs for blood donations or therapeutically, such as in the management of sickle cell crisis, severe malaria, and hemolytic disease of the newborn (e.g., via exchange transfusion).

q_1C6j0.title: Vocal fold cyst
q_1C6j0.description: Benign, sac-like structure in the lamina propria of the vocal cords caused by obstruction of laryngeal mucus-secreting glands. Typically, located unilaterally and of yellow-whitish color. Vocal fold cysts primarily occur in children.

destinations.label: Benign laryngeal lesions → Vocal fold cyst

I_1Ypj0.title: Apheresis
I_1Ypj0.description: An extracorporeal procedure in which a patient's blood is passed through a machine that separates a particular component and returns the remaining components to the patient. Types include plasmapheresis, erythrocytapheresis, plateletpheresis, and leukapheresis

7_14pj0.title: Reviewable sentinel event
7_14pj0.description: A sentinel event that is subject to review by the Joint Commission. Includes any medical error that results in death or permanent disability as well as any of the following: abduction, rape, or homicide of a patient, health care provider, or visitor at the health care organization, inpatient suicide or suicide within 72 hours of discharge, perinatal death of the mother or a normal birth weight neonate without a congenital disorder, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia > 30 mg/dL, hemolytic transfusion reaction from major blood group incompatibility, invasive procedures or radiotherapy on the wrong site or wrong patient, foreign body retention, and prolonged fluoroscopy.

H_1Kpj0.title: Nonreviewable sentinel event
H_1Kpj0.description: A sentinel event that is not subject to review by the Joint Commission. Examples include death or permanent disability after discharge against medical advice, hemolytic transfusion reactions from minor blood group incompatibility, unsuccessful suicide attempts that result in permanent disability, medication errors that do not result in death or permanent disability, and near-miss sentinel events.

s_1tpj0.title: Nonmenstrual TSS
s_1tpj0.description: A form of staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome (a systemic inflammatory reaction) that is associated with surgical procedures, e.g., postsurgical wound packing or postpartum or postabortion infections. It is caused by a strain of Staphylococcus aureus that produces superantigenic exotoxins, e.g., TSST-1, staphylococcal enterotoxins.

G_1Bpj0.title: Menstrual TSS
G_1Bpj0.description: A form of staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome (a systemic inflammatory reaction) that is associated with menstruation, e.g., high-absorbency tampon use or prolonged placement of tampons, menstrual cups, or vaginal sponges. It is caused by a strain of vaginal Staphylococcus aureus that produces the superantigenic exotoxin TSST-1.

t_1XJj0.title: Skill-based error
t_1XJj0.description: A type of active error in which the health care provider is not cognizant of the act of commission (a slip) or omission (a lapse). Typically occurs when a health care provider is engaged in skills-based performance or schematic behavior (e.g., performing a very familiar task with a low level of attention). Distinct from mistakes and violations, in which the provider is cognizant of the action or decision that leads to the active error.

u_1pJj0.title: Pachyderma
u_1pJj0.description: Abnormal thickening and wrinkling of the skin. Associated with some cancers, pachydermoperiostosis, acromegaly, elephantiasis, and podoconiosis. Laryngeal pachyderma is characterized by rough, thickened mucosa and potential swelling, and is associated with GERD or chronic bacterial infection. Malignant transformation into laryngeal cancer is possible.

destinations.label: Benign laryngeal lesions → Precancerous lesions of the larynx

v_1AJj0.title: Apparent death
v_1AJj0.description: The reduction of vital function to a minimum, which results in the appearance of death without signs of certain death.

w_1hqj0.title: Intermediary life
w_1hqj0.description: The period of time between irreversible cardiopulmonary death and biological death.

9_1Nqj0.title: Biological death
9_1Nqj0.description: A permanent and irreversible cellular injury with complete cessation of metabolic cell function. Tissue that has undergone biological death is unsuitable for transplantation.

C_1qqj0.title: Legal death
C_1qqj0.description: The recognition of a person's death under the law. Legal death includes medically determined death as well as the presumption under the law that a person is dead after a prolonged and unexplained absence with no signs of life (declaration of death in absentia).

A_1RIj0.title: Uniform determination of death act
A_1RIj0.description: Legal provisions regarding death vary from state to state. However, all states have adopted the “Uniform determination of death act” (1981), which specifies that the determination of death must be made in accordance with accepted medical standards and depends on: irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions (cardiopulmonary death) or irreversible cessation of all functions of the entire brain, including the brainstem (brain death).

Zz1Zrj0.title: Endoprosthesis
Zz1Zrj0.description: An artificial device placed inside the body to replace damaged or missing body parts, or for structural support. Commonly used in bone and joint replacements and as stents (e.g., gastrointestinal, vascular).

media.title: Knee joint with a cemented endoprosthesis (AP view)
Endoluminal aortic prosthesis following a Stanford type B dissection

0z1erj0.title: Factitious fever
0z1erj0.description: The manipulation of a patient's temperature measurement, either by the patient themselves or a surrogate. The temperature elevation may be false (e.g., due to heating the thermometer) or real (e.g., due to injecting bacteria). Often reported as a feature of Munchausen syndrome or Munchausen syndrome by proxy.

az1Qrj0.title: Adnexal detorsion
az1Qrj0.description: A minimally invasive surgical procedure, most often performed in combination with diagnostic laparoscopy, to reverse ovarian torsion in premenopausal patients. The procedure involves untwisting the torsed adnexal structure with the goal of preserving the affected ovary.

Yz1nrj0.title: Heuristic
Yz1nrj0.description: A mental shortcut or a simplified decision-making strategy that decreases the cognitive workload. Used to draw conclusions or solve problems quickly and efficiently when the amount of information input is insufficient or excessive. Can result in cognitive biases.

bz1Hrj0.title: Zoledronic acid
bz1Hrj0.description: A bisphosphonate that inhibits osteoclastic activity, resulting in decreased bone resorption, and, therefore, decreased skeletal calcium release. Used to treat bone metastases, hypercalcemia associated with malignancy, and osteoporosis.

Xz19rj0.title: Bypassing agents
Xz19rj0.description: Blood concentrates or medications used to treat patients with inhibitors to coagulation factors. These agents "bypass" the inhibited factor by acting on factors further down the hemostasis pathway. Examples include recombinant VIIa, prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC), and the monoclonal antibody emicizumab.

cz1a7j0.title: Design validation
cz1a7j0.description: An error prevention strategy in human factors engineering. Includes evaluating whether or not a device meets user requirements regarding its intended purpose and assessing usability by testing the devices under actual and/or simulated conditions (usability testing).

1z127j0.title: Platelet function analysis
1z127j0.description: A laboratory study that assesses platelet adhesion and/or aggregation and is often used to evaluate the effect of medication on platelet function. Multiple assays are available and their use is rapidly increasing, as they provide a point-of-care evaluation of primary hemostasis. PFA has replaced bleeding time as the initial test for assessing platelet function at most institutions.

Wz1P7j0.title: Safety Assurance Factors for Electronic health record Resilience guide
Wz1P7j0.description: An evidence-based checklist created by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality to help health care providers use electronic health records safely. Specific areas of interest include correct patient identification and follow-up of test results.

dz1o7j0.title: Float staff
dz1o7j0.description: A group of staff members that is on standby to be deployed when sufficient workload capacity is not available (e.g., during peak working hours, during periods of employee absence).

2z1THj0.title: Brainstem areflexia
2z1THj0.description: The absence of all reflexes that have their relays at the level of the brainstem. These reflexes include the pupillary reflex, corneal reflex, vestibuloocular reflexes, jaw jerk, gag reflex, cough reflex, and in the case of neonates and young infants, the rooting reflex and sucking reflex.

fz1kHj0.title: Plethoric inferior vena cava
fz1kHj0.description: An ultrasound finding seen in cardiac tamponade and right ventricular failure. In healthy individuals, inspiration reduces intrathoracic pressure, increasing venous return and causing the IVC to collapse. In cardiac tamponade or right ventricular failure, venous return does not decrease, and the IVC remains >50% of its normal diameter during inspiration.

Sz1yHj0.title: Finger thoracostomy
Sz1yHj0.description: A procedure performed as an alternative to needle decompression in tension pneumothorax that is thought to more effectively decompress the lungs. An incision is made in the fifth intercostal space along the mid- or anterior axillary line and a finger is inserted into the pleural cavity. Commonly used in traumatic chest injuries, including traumatic cardiac arrest.

hz1csj0.title: Open cardiac massage
hz1csj0.description: A resuscitative procedure for patients in cardiac arrest that is performed through a thoracotomy incision. One hand is placed under the heart, the other above, and the heart is then gently compressed from the apex upward at a rate of 100/minute. Performed in patients in cardiac arrest during or shortly after cardiac surgery, or in traumatic cardiac arrest when a thoracotomy has been performed.

iz1Jsj0.title: Electrocerebral silence
iz1Jsj0.description: A finding on electroencephalography defined by the absence of electrical activity with an amplitude > 2 microvolts when the recording is performed with scalp electrodes that are at least 10 cm apart and have interelectrode impedances between 100 and 10,000 Ohms. Occurs with severe hypothermia, supratherapeutic doses of general anesthesia, and brain death

Pz1WGj0.title: Nonspinal causes of acute back pain
Pz1WGj0.description: Referred pain to the back from a nonspinal etiology (i.e., outside the spinal cord, vertebral column, and back muscles). Urgent causes include vascular emergencies (aortic dissection, AAA), infections (psoas abscess, pneumonia, cholecystitis), and acute pancreatitis. Other causes include abdominopelvic malignancy, referred joint pain, stable rib fractures, nephrolithiasis, and renal infarction.

kz1mGj0.title: Death certificate
kz1mGj0.description: A legal document issued by a medical practitioner certifying a person's death. Includes the date, time, and cause of death. Physicians are usually authorized to sign death certificates when the manner of death is natural. For violent or suspicious deaths, the authority lies with a coroner or medical examiner.

Nz1-Gj0.title: Death note
Nz1-Gj0.description: A note entered in the medical record by the physician who pronounces the patient's death. Should contain the time at which the physician was informed about the probable death of the patient, duration and findings of the death pronouncement examination, time of death, probable cause of death, whether the local death investigation office was notified, and a whether a next-of-kin was present and when present, their requests regarding clinical autopsy, organ donation, or a body bequest.

5z1itj0.title: Gastric volvulus
5z1itj0.description: A twisting of the stomach along its axis, typically beyond 180°, which results in variable degrees of gastric outlet obstruction and increased risk of intestinal ischemia and perforation. Risk factors include age > 50 years, diaphragmatic abnormalities (e.g., hiatal hernia, paraesophageal hernia), gastric ligament abnormalities, and phrenic nerve paralysis.

destinations.label: Intestinal malrotation, midgut volvulus, and gastric volvulus → Gastric volvulus

oz10Fj0.title: Goniometer
oz10Fj0.description: A device used to measure the angle of the range of motion for a joint.

Kz1UFj0.title: Inclinometer
Kz1UFj0.description: A device for measuring range of motion. Consists of a circle filled with fluid and an arrow placed inside it, a scale marked from 0° to 359°, and a base. To measure range of motion, the base is aligned with the moving segment of the joint.

wz1hEj0.title: Clinical death
wz1hEj0.description: A term that generally refers to the cessation of respiration and circulation and may be reversible.

xz1EEj0.title: Degloving
xz1EEj0.description: The complete detachment of areas of skin and soft tissue from underlying structures (e.g., muscle or bone). Can be due to forceful separation caused by high-energy trauma, or seen as a postmortem change as part of the natural decomposition process.

Az1Rvj0.title: Relational injustice
Az1Rvj0.description: A type of social injustice that is the result of prejudice against certain individuals or groups of individuals. In health care settings, this type of injustice can result in disparities in health care access, treatment, and outcomes.

destinations.label: Health care system → Social aspects of health care

_z15vj0.title: Knee bulge sign
_z15vj0.description: A test to assess for knee joint effusion. The examiner applies pressure above the patella to push fluid from the suprapatellar pouch to the knee joint cavity, and then applies pressure behind the lateral margin of patella. The emergence of a bulge on the medial aspect of the knee indicates knee joint effusion.

0-1eDj0.title: Spiritual care and counseling
0-1eDj0.description: An intervention that focuses on the individual's spiritual, cultural, and/or religious needs and aims to relieve stress and improve overall quality of life. Spiritual care is provided by trained specialists (e.g., chaplains, counselors, psychologists).

destinations.label: Grief and end-of-life counseling → End-of-life counseling

U-1b9j0.title: Infectious rashes in childhood
U-1b9j0.description: Rashes that most commonly occur in children and are caused by infection with a pathogen (e.g., virus, bacteria, fungus, parasite).

f-1k9j0.title: Prolonged postoperative ileus
f-1k9j0.description: A condition of impaired bowel motility  that persists for > 72 hours following surgery without a mechanical obstruction.

T-169j0.title: Cardiac arrest
T-169j0.description: The sudden cessation of cardiac function, resulting in loss of circulation. Cardiac arrest is fatal unless resuscitative measures (e.g., CPR, defibrillation of shockable rhythms) are immediately administered.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Summary

g-1F9j0.title: Cardiac imaging
g-1F9j0.description: Diagnostic modalities used to evaluate cardiac structure, function, and pathophysiology. Examples include echocardiography, cardiac CT, cardiac MRI, and myocardial perfusion imaging.

S-1y9j0.title: Clinical features of airway obstruction
S-1y9j0.description: Signs and symptoms that suggest impending or total loss of airway patency. These include features of partial airway obstruction (e.g., stridor, hypoxia, signs of increased work of breathing) and complete airway obstruction (inability to speak, paradoxical chest/abdomen movement) as well as features of conditions associated with an anticipated loss of airway protection (e.g., reduced level of consciousness, inability to swallow secretions).

destinations.label: Airway management → Clinical features of airway compromise

h-1cCj0.title: Directive counseling
h-1cCj0.description: A counseling approach in which the clinician takes an active part in the decision-making process by providing advice, guidance, and recommendations based on their expert clinical judgment.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

3-1SCj0.title: Fetal malpresentation
3-1SCj0.description: A fetal position in which the fetus is in a noncephalic presentation (e.g., breech presentation) with a part of the body other than the head overlying the maternal pelvic inlet.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormalities in fetal orientation

R-1lCj0.title: Simple bowel obstruction
R-1lCj0.description: Bowel obstruction with no evidence of complications (i.e., no features of bowel ischemia, bowel perforation, or red flags for complicated bowel obstruction)

4-13xj0.title: LEMON assessment
4-13xj0.description: A mnemonic used to assess an airway and predict difficult intubation conditions. The steps are: (L) Look for features associated with a difficult airway (e.g., facial trauma, large incisors, or a beard); (E) Evaluate mouth opening and larynx position; (M) assess oral accessibility using the Mallampati score; (O) assess for Obesity and conditions concerning for airway Obstruction; (N) evaluate Neck mobility.

O-1Ixj0.title: Wet gangrene
O-1Ixj0.description: A subtype of gangrenous necrosis caused by superinfection. Characterized by coagulative and liquefactive necrosis on histopathologic examination.

l-1vxj0.title: Dry gangrene
l-1vxj0.description: A subtype of gangrenous necrosis caused by ischemia. Characterized by coagulative necrosis on histopathologic examination.

N-1-xj0.title: Oropharyngeal airway
N-1-xj0.description: An airway adjunct used to help maintain airway patency and facilitate ventilation of an unconscious patient. Consists of a curved plastic tube that is placed in the patient's mouth, with the tip lying in the oropharynx to prevent the tongue from occluding the airways.

m-1VBj0.title: Adult Protective Services
m-1VBj0.description: An agency that protects older (> 65 years of age) and disabled adults (18-64 years of age) from abuse, neglect, and financial exploitation. They receive and investigate complaints and provide social, medical, and legal assistance. In the US, physicians are legally and ethically obligated to report suspected older adult abuse or neglect to Adult Protective Services.

5-1iBj0.title: Long-Term Care Ombudsman program
5-1iBj0.description: An agency that assists residents of long-term care facilities (e.g., nursing homes) and protects them from abuse, neglect, and financial exploitation. They receive and investigate complaints and provide social, medical, and legal assistance. In the US, physicians are legally and ethically obligated to report suspected abuse that occurred in an institution to Long-Term Care Ombudsman programs.

n-17Bj0.title: Health care assistance program
n-17Bj0.description: A financial aid program that helps allocate health care resources to individuals who have limited incomes. Examples include Medicaid, Medicare, and county-specific financial aid programs.

L-1wBj0.title: Acute motor axonal neuropathy
L-1wBj0.description: A variant of Guillain-Barre syndrome that manifests with acute paralysis and loss of reflexes without sensory loss. Typically occurs after an infection with Campylobacter jejuni and may be associated with antibodies directed toward GM1 ganglioside-like epitopes.

6-1jyj0.title: APS
6-1jyj0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Adult Protective Services
2. Antiphospholipid syndrome
3. Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome

p-1Lyj0.title: Uninterpretable ECG
p-1Lyj0.description: An ECG that cannot be accurately assessed because of abnormalities at baseline. Examples of abnormalities include complete left bundle branch block, LV hypertrophy, resting ST-segment abnormality (≥ 0.1 mV), preexcitation syndromes, digoxin use, electrolyte abnormalities, and ventricular pacing.

J-1syj0.title: Precision medicine
J-1syj0.description: The individualization of medical treatment based on the patient's specific genetic or molecular markers. Examples include cancer treatments (e.g., treatments for HER-2 positive breast cancer) and CFTR modulators in cystic fibrosis.

q-1Cyj0.title: Patient decision aid
q-1Cyj0.description: A tool that is used to facilitate shared decision-making by helping patients better understand the various treatment options for a particular condition as well as the risks and benefits of each treatment.

I-1YAj0.title: PAD
I-1YAj0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Peripheral artery disease
2. Physician-assisted death

r-1fAj0.title: Mill test
r-1fAj0.description: A test for lateral epicondylitis. The examiner fully extends the examinee's elbow, flexes their wrist, and pronates the forearm while palpating the lateral epicondyle. The emergence of pain in the area of the lateral epicondyle indicates lateral epicondylitis.

destinations.label: Orthopedic examination → Arm and hand examination

7-14Aj0.title: HIV-associated arthritis
7-14Aj0.description: A type of arthritis involving the large joints in individuals with HIV. Typically lasts < 6 weeks, causes no radiological changes, and is self-limited. A diagnosis of exclusion; should be considered in HIV-positive patients with negative HLA-B27, no other features of rheumatological conditions, and no evidence of a preceding infectious trigger.

destinations.label: HIV-associated conditions → Rheumatological and musculoskeletal complications

H-1KAj0.title: Painful articular syndrome
H-1KAj0.description: An acute arthralgia that occurs in HIV patients and manifests as acute severe pain (typically in one large joint) lasting 2-24 hours.

destinations.label: HIV-associated conditions → Rheumatological and musculoskeletal complications

s-1tAj0.title: Diffuse infiltrative lymphocytosis syndrome
s-1tAj0.description: An HIV-associated condition that manifests with salivary gland swelling and symptoms of chronic sicca syndrome

destinations.label: HIV-associated conditions → Rheumatological and musculoskeletal complications

u-1p_j0.title: Undifferentiated shock
u-1p_j0.description: A term for shock (i.e., tissue hypoxia with end-organ damage) with an underlying cause that has not yet been identified.

D-11zj0.title: Nasogastric tube
D-11zj0.description: A flexible tube that is passed through the nostrils and into the stomach. Uses include gastric decompression (e.g., in bowel obstruction) and the administration of medication or nutritional support (e.g., in dysphagia).

w-1hzj0.title: Naproxen test
w-1hzj0.description: A test used to determine the etiology of fever of unknown origin (FUO). Naproxen is administered every 12 hours for three days. Resolution of the fever during the naproxen trial is associated with a malignant etiology.

C-1qzj0.title: Maudsley test
C-1qzj0.description: A test for lateral epicondylitis. The patient sits with their hands lying on a table, elbow extended, and forearm pronated. The patient is then asked to lift middle finger, while the examiner pushes it down to the table. Pain in the area of lateral epicondyle is considered a positive sign.

destinations.label: Orthopedic examination → Arm and hand examination

x-1Ezj0.title: Latent autoimmune diabetes in adults
x-1Ezj0.description: A slowly progressing form of autoimmune diabetes that shares genetic features of both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Patients have circulating autoantibodies directed against pancreatic beta-cell antigens (e.g., ICA, GAD65). They typically do not require insulin at diagnosis but progress to insulin dependence after several months to years.

_-15-j0.title: Control limits
_-15-j0.description: The values of a quality metric that are +3 (upper control limit) and -3 (lower control limit) standard deviations away from the mean. A data point that falls outside these values is an indicator of a signal (special cause affecting the quality metric).

z-1r-j0.title: Quality metric
z-1r-j0.description: An indicator used to assess and compare the quality of systems and to track improvements in the system's quality over time. Includes structural measures, process measures, outcome measures, and balancing measures.

--1D-j0.title: Pareto principle
--1D-j0.description: A statistical principle that influences an effect with multiple causes. A major part of the effect is determined by a minority of the causes. The exact proportions vary depending on the scenario, but in most cases, approximately 80% of the effect is determined by approximately 20% of the causes. Used for targeted interventions that yield the maximum benefit for a given amount of effort as well as for prioritization of interventions.

ZZWZZP0.title: Failure mode
ZZWZZP0.description: A specific way in which a step of a process or a part of a system can fail. In failure modes and effects analysis, failure modes are identified prospectively by inductive reasoning.

0ZWeZP0.title: Cyclic neutropenia
0ZWeZP0.description: A rare hematologic disease characterized by recurrent fever and low neutrophil levels. Other symptoms include headache, stomatitis, and recurrent infections. Can be inherited or acquired. Management includes granulocyte colony-stimulating factor and the treatment of any associated infections.

aZWQZP0.title: Nasopharyngeal airway
aZWQZP0.description: An airway adjunct used to help maintain airway patency and facilitate ventilation. Consists of a flexible plastic tube inserted via a nostril to lie with the tip in the nasopharynx. Can be used alone or in conjunction with another nasopharyngeal airway (NPA) and/or an oropharyngeal airway (OPA).

XZW9ZP0.title: Difficult airway
XZW9ZP0.description: An upper airway with anatomical or physiological features that increase the difficulty of bag-mask ventilation and/or endotracheal intubation. Underlying risk factors can be congenital or acquired.

1ZW20P0.title: Gastric lavage
1ZW20P0.description: A method of gastrointestinal decontamination consisting of enteral administration of warm saline or water via a large-bore orogastric tube, and subsequent aspiration of the fluid, in order to remove and prevent absorption of pills or pill fragments. Used in the treatment of certain toxic ingestions (extended-release or enteric-coated medications, drug packets, or toxic metals) in very rare situations.

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Decontamination

eZWx0P0.title: Single-dose activated charcoal
eZWx0P0.description: An adsorbent agent used to treat some types of enteral poisoning by gastrointestinal decontamination. Involves the enteral administration of one dosage of activated charcoal, typically given in a ratio of 10 grams charcoal to 1 gram toxin. Most effective for single toxic ingestions occurring ≤ 1 hour prior to presentation. Can be considered for single ingestion of slowly metabolizing toxins > 1 hour from presentation.

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Decontamination

UZWbaP0.title: Multidose activated charcoal
UZWbaP0.description: An adsorbent agent used to treat some types of enteral poisoning by enhanced elimination. Involves the enteral administration of repeated dosages of activated charcoal. May be used for potentially fatal ingestions of carbamazepine, theophylline, quinine, phenobarbital, or dapsone.

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Enhanced elimination

2ZWTaP0.title: NSAID-induced ulcer
2ZWTaP0.description: A gastric or duodenal ulcer caused by NSAID therapy, which inhibits cyclooxygenases and disrupts the production of protective gastric mucosal prostaglandins, thereby predisposing to mucosal injury.

destinations.label: Peptic ulcer disease → Subtypes and variants

SZWyaP0.title: Advanced airway management
