SZWyaP0.description: A series of procedures to secure the airway that are performed by specially-trained providers in order to provide adequate ventilation. These include the placement of supraglottic airways, intubation, and the creation of surgical airways.

hZWcYP0.title: Clean intermittent catheterization
hZWcYP0.description: The insertion and removal of a urinary catheter in regular intervals (4–6 times a day) in order to empty the bladder of patients with urinary retention and/or neurogenic bladder dysfunction. Associated with fewer catheter-associated urinary tract infections compared to indwelling transurethral catheters.

3ZWSYP0.title: Bladder irrigation
3ZWSYP0.description: Irrigation of the bladder with intermittent boluses or a continuous flow of sterile solution through an indwelling urinary catheter. Indications include preventing or removing blood clots during hematuria, removing mucus or stones, and delivering medications for infections or interstitial cystitis.

iZWJYP0.title: Retropubic prostatectomy
iZWJYP0.description: A surgical technique used to remove some or all of the prostatic tissue. It uses an open surgical transcapsular retropubic approach and the tissue is enucleated using the index finger through the anterior prostatic capsule.

QZWuYP0.title: Congenital hyperinsulinism
QZWuYP0.description: A cause of recurrent hypoglycemia in infancy. Results in decreased serum beta-hydroxybutyrate and free fatty acid concentrations with detectable serum insulin or C-peptide. Can be caused by single-gene defects or be seen in association with congenital syndromes (e.g., Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome).

jZW_YP0.title: Molimina symptoms
jZW_YP0.description: A collection of symptoms associated with normal reproductive hormonal cycling. Includes cramping, breast tenderness, and changes in appetite and mood in the premenstrual phase and thin cervical mucus secretions in the middle of the menstrual cycle.

PZWWbP0.title: Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome
PZWWbP0.description: A congenital syndrome caused by partial deletion of the short arm of chromosome 4. Manifestations include growth restriction, microcephaly, heart defects, and intellectual disability.

4ZW3bP0.title: Abdominoplasty
4ZW3bP0.description: A surgical procedure that includes removal of skin and fat as well as plication of the rectus muscle. Used to reduce the laxity of the abdominal wall, which can occur after multiple pregnancies or significant weight loss.

kZWmbP0.title: Gustilo-Anderson open fracture grading system
kZWmbP0.description: A grading system for open fractures. Components include wound size, degree of contamination, presence of comminution and/or periosteal stripping, presence of vascular injury, and extent of soft tissue coverage.

OZWIbP0.title: Rancho Los Amigos Scale
OZWIbP0.description: A scale used to grade cognitive and behavioral function during the recovery period after brain injury. Ranges from level I (total assistance required, no response to external stimuli) to level X (purposeful and appropriate behavior, relatively independent and uses compensatory strategies).

lZWvbP0.title: Gonadoblastoma
lZWvbP0.description: An ovarian malignancy that consists of germ cells and sex cord stroma. Individuals with Turner syndrome and 45,X/46,XY mosaicism) are at increased risk for this malignancy.

NZW-bP0.title: Ceftolozane/tazobactam
NZW-bP0.description: An antibiotic drug that combines ceftozolane, a 5th generation cephalosporin, with tazobactam, a β-lactamase inhibitor. Often used to treat multidrug-resistant infections caused by P. aeruginosa or ESBL-producing organisms.

mZWVXP0.title: Primary prevention of ASCVD
mZWVXP0.description: A series of interventions to reduce the risk of developing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Involves lifestyle modifications (e.g., smoking cessation) and management of comorbid conditions such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes mellitus. Pharmacotherapy may include statins and/or antiplatelet agents.

5ZWiXP0.title: Management of ASCVD
5ZWiXP0.description: A series of interventions designed to reduce the risk of further cardiovascular events in patients with history of a clinical ASCVD (e.g., coronary artery disease, stroke, peripheral artery disease). Interventions include antiplatelet therapy, lifestyle modifications (e.g., healthy diet, exercise, smoking cessation), cholesterol management, and management of comorbid conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and overweight and obesity.

nZW7XP0.title: Diisopropyl fluorophosphate
nZW7XP0.description: An irreversible cholinesterase inhibitor used as a topical miotic agent in ophthalmology. Can be used to treat accommodative esotropia and glaucoma.

LZWwXP0.title: Papillary hidradenoma
LZWwXP0.description: A benign cutaneous adnexal tumor that most commonly develops on the vulvar region as a solitary, skin-colored nodule.

oZW0cP0.title: Frasier syndrome
oZW0cP0.description: A rare congenital condition caused by mutations in the WT1 gene, which encodes a protein involved in renal and gonadal development. Affected individuals with an XY karyotype typically have normal-appearing female external genitalia and streak gonads and are at increased risk for developing gonadoblastoma.

KZWUcP0.title: Cefiderocol
KZWUcP0.description: A siderophore cephalosporin whose side chain forms complexes with iron. As a result, it can use bacterial iron transport systems to cross the outer membrane of bacteria. Thereafter, the cephalosporin component binds to penicillin-binding proteins to inhibit peptidoglycan synthesis. Often used to treat multidrug-resistant infections caused by P. aeruginosa or ESBL-producing organisms.

6ZWjcP0.title: Pores of Kohn
6ZWjcP0.description: The small connections between pulmonary alveoli that provide a collateral pathway for airflow (separate from the pulmonary tree). Typically begin to form around 3-4 years of age. The immaturity of pores of Kohn in young children may contribute to the increased incidence of round pneumonia in this age group.

pZWLcP0.title: Fulvestrant
pZWLcP0.description: An estrogen receptor antagonist used to treat hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. It blocks estrogen receptor dimerization and DNA binding, reduces nuclear uptake of the receptor, and increases estrogen receptor degradation.

qZWCcP0.title: Low health literacy
qZWCcP0.description: The inability to access or navigate the health care system, or to acquire, comprehend, and use health information to make informed health care decisions. Primarily attributable to the complexity of health care information and health care systems. Patients of all ages, ethnicities, languages, cultures, incomes, and educational levels can be affected by health illiteracy.

IZWY1P0.title: Features of pulmonary arterial hypertension
IZWY1P0.description: A collection of clinical findings in pulmonary arterial hypertension. They include dyspnea, chest pain, fatigue, cyanosis, and signs and symptoms of right heart failure and the underlying etiology.

destinations.label: Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale → Clinical features

7ZW41P0.title: Occupational lung disease
7ZW41P0.description: A respiratory disorder caused by occupational exposures. Examples include pneumoconioses (e.g., asbestosis, silicosis, byssinosis), which are types of interstitial lung disease, work-related asthma, work-related COPD, cancer (e.g., due to exposure to asbestos, radiation), and hypersensitivity pneumonitis.

HZWK1P0.title: Clinical features of portal hypertension
HZWK1P0.description: Features include signs and symptoms of the underlying disease (e.g., stigmata of chronic liver disease), signs of increased blood flow via portosystemic anastomoses (caput medusae, anorectal, esophageal, and gastric varices), splenomegaly, and ascites.

sZWt1P0.title: Centrocyte
sZWt1P0.description: A follicle center cell with elongated or cleaved nuclei (resulting in an angulated appearance of the nuclear membranes) and very little cytoplasm. It is the predominant cell type of follicular lymphoma.

FZWgWP0.title: Gastrointestinal decontamination
FZWgWP0.description: Therapeutic interventions to remove a toxin from the gastrointestinal (GI) tract by reducing its absorption and/or facilitating clearance. Techniques involve either binding in the GI tract (e.g., single-dose activated charcoal) or removal from the GI tract (e.g., whole bowel irrigation or gastric lavage).

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Decontamination

8ZWOWP0.title: Pleuromutilin
8ZWOWP0.description: A class of antibiotics that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the peptidyl transferase center of the 50S ribosomal subunit, which impairs proper positioning of tRNA. Examples include lefamulin and retapamulin.

EZW8WP0.title: Thanatophoric dysplasia
EZW8WP0.description: The most common type of lethal skeletal dysplasia. Caused by mutations in the fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) gene. Manifestations include micromelia, macrocrania, thickened skin folds, and temporal lobe dysplasia.

vZWAWP0.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure
vZWAWP0.description: A condition characterized by acute decompensated chronic liver disease in combination with additional organ failure (e.g., kidney, brain, coagulation). Short-term mortality is high.

DZW1dP0.title: Pre-ART era
DZW1dP0.description: The period of time before antiretroviral therapy was available for treatment of HIV and AIDS.

wZWhdP0.title: ART era
wZWhdP0.description: The period of time after antiretroviral therapy for HIV and AIDS became widely available and used.

9ZWNdP0.title: Transurethral resection of the prostate syndrome
9ZWNdP0.description: A rare complication of transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) caused by the absorption of irrigants used during the procedure. Characterized by dilutional hyponatremia and a constellation of neurological and pulmonary symptoms (e.g., restlessness, headaches, seizures, tachypnea, hypoxia, respiratory distress).

CZWqdP0.title: Joint Commission
CZWqdP0.description: A United States nonprofit organization that evaluates and accredits health care organizations and promotes initiatives to improve patient safety.

xZWEdP0.title: Faciocutaneoskeletal syndrome
xZWEdP0.description: An autosomal dominant congenital syndrome caused by mutations in the HRAS gene, which results in growth delay, short stature, developmental delay, macrocephaly, coarse facial features, loose skin, cardiomyopathy, and papillomata (benign, wart-like growths).

BZWzdP0.title: Progressive pigmentary purpura
BZWzdP0.description: A pigmented purpuric dermatosis that typically manifests with asymptomatic, discrete, nonblanchable, purpuric macules and patches on the lower extremities.

yZWdVP0.title: Enhanced elimination (toxicology)
yZWdVP0.description: Therapeutic interventions to remove toxins from blood and/or tissues. Techniques include multidose-activated charcoal administration, urine alkalinization, and extracorporeal therapy (e.g., dialysis).

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Enhanced elimination

-ZWDVP0.title: Toxidrome
-ZWDVP0.description: A collection of signs and symptoms commonly associated with a substance or class of substances that has reached toxic levels in the body.

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Initial management

a0WQeP0.title: Bamlanivimab
a0WQeP0.description: A neutralizing monoclonal antibody that binds to an epitope of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor-binding domain, thereby blocking the entry of SARS-CoV-2 into host cells.

Y0WneP0.title: Etesevimab
Y0WneP0.description: A neutralizing monoclonal antibody that binds to an epitope of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor-binding domain, thereby blocking the entry of SARS-CoV-2 into host cells.

b0WHeP0.title: Casirivimab
b0WHeP0.description: A neutralizing monoclonal antibody that binds to an epitope of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor-binding domain, thereby blocking the entry of SARS-CoV-2 into host cells.

X0W9eP0.title: Imdevimab
X0W9eP0.description: A neutralizing monoclonal antibody that binds to an epitope of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor-binding domain, thereby blocking the entry of SARS-CoV-2 into host cells.

10W2UP0.title: Action hierarchy of human factors engineering
10W2UP0.description: A tool that categorizes actions that aim to prevent medical errors into stronger, intermediate, and weaker actions, depending on their reliance on human effort to be performed correctly. Examples of  "stronger actions" include simplifying processes and standardizing equipment. Examples of "weaker actions" include audible warnings and double checking of processes.

W0WPUP0.title: Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act
W0WPUP0.description: A collection of laws and regulations developed in 2009 by the U.S. Congress to encourage the implementation of electronic health records and improve privacy and security of health information.

d0WoUP0.title: Note bloat
d0WoUP0.description: The creation of lengthy electronic health record notes containing redundant, clinically irrelevant, and/or outdated information. Can lead to difficulties in identifying key aspects of patient care and negatively affect patient safety. Often a result of copying and pasting.

V0WGUP0.title: Fragmentation of health care
V0WGUP0.description: A lack of integration and coordination between the services of health care providers and/or organizations. Common causes include reimbursement models that disincentivize care coordination, prioritization of individual over shared accountability, siloization of a patient's health information, overutilization of specialist services, and window-shopping for services by patients. Can result in gaps in the transition of care, unnecessary repetition of medical interventions, and lower quality and higher costs of care.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care fragmentation

e0WxUP0.title: Care coordination
e0WxUP0.description: The deliberate organization of patient care activities and exchange of information among providers involved in a patient's care. Improves effectiveness, safety, and efficiency of health care services.

U0Wb2P0.title: Multiparametric MRI
U0Wb2P0.description: A type of magnetic resonance imaging that produces a high-definition, three-dimensional image of the target organ. Its primary clinical use is in MRI-guided biopsy and staging of prostate cancer, though other uses are currently being explored.

20WT2P0.title: Grade group
20WT2P0.description: A histological classification of prostate cancer that is based on the Gleason score. Grade groups are more accurate prognostic indicators than the Gleason score. Used in the risk stratification of patients with localized prostate cancer to tailor management.

f0Wk2P0.title: Protracted bacterial bronchitis
f0Wk2P0.description: A bacterial infection of the bronchi, most often by H. influenzae, S. pneumoniae, or M. catarrhalis, that causes productive cough and is especially common in children. Clinical diagnostic criteria include daily cough for > 4 weeks, resolution within 2–4 weeks of antibiotic therapy, and an absence of alternate diagnoses.

T0W62P0.title: Quantitative ultrasonography
T0W62P0.description: An ultrasonographic technique used to assess osteoporotic fracture risk. Measures the transmission of sound waves through limb bones and reflectance of sound waves off of bony surfaces.

g0WF2P0.title: CTC
g0WF2P0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Computed tomography colonography
2. Circulating tumor cell

R0WlfP0.title: Risk factors for ischemic stroke
R0WlfP0.description: A collection of patient factors that increase the risk of ischemic stroke. Traditionally classified as either nonmodifiable (e.g., age ≥ 65 years, male sex, genetic factors, minority groups) or modifiable risk factors (e.g., hypertension, hyperlipidemia, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, alcohol and/or tobacco use).

i0WJfP0.title: Sensory extinction
i0WJfP0.description: A neurological symptom that that can occur in patients with unilateral brain damage. If both sides are stimulated, a patient with extinction will not perceive the stimulus on the affected side. If the sides are stimulated individually, both stimuli can be perceived. Common causes include ischemic stroke.

Q0WufP0.title: Protective isolation for immunosuppressed patients
Q0WufP0.description: A set of measures implemented to reduce the risk of infections among immunosuppressed patients in the hospital. Includes dust minimization strategies, prohibition of organic material near the patient, isolation of the patient in well-sealed rooms with laminar airflow, the use of HEPA air filters and frequent air changes, positive ambient air pressure, and the use of N95 masks by immunosuppressed patients when they leave their protective environment.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Isolation precautions

j0W_fP0.title: Antibiotic lock therapy
j0W_fP0.description: A practice use for prophylaxis and/or treatment that involves instilling an antibiotic into the lumen(s) of a central venous catheter and allowing it to dwell inside the line for 4-24 hours. Can be given for catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSI) in conjunction with systemic IV antibiotics to attempt to salvage the intravenous line. Other indications include infection prophylaxis for certain patient populations: e.g., short-term hemodialysis via tunneled catheters, long-term central venous catheterization in immunosuppressed patients, and history of recurrent CRBSIs.

P0WWTP0.title: Thin-wall introducer needle
P0WWTP0.description: A wide-gauge needle used to percutaneously puncture an artery or vein, allowing passage of a guide wire. Thin-wall introducer needles have thin walls to minimize the size of the resultant vessel hole.

40W3TP0.title: Real-time feedback loop
40W3TP0.description: A communication loop in which feedback is provided immediately after an action is performed. A very effective strategy to increase compliance and situational awareness.

k0WmTP0.title: Electronic hand hygiene monitoring
k0WmTP0.description: A hand hygiene station that consists of an electronic hand hygiene dispenser coupled with monitoring tools (e.g., radiofrequency sensors worn by health care providers, video monitoring). Used to monitor compliance to hand hygiene and provide real-time feedback to health care providers.

l0WvTP0.title: Champions-led rounding
l0WvTP0.description: A process in which individuals advocate for and support the implementation of a particular quality improvement measure via regular patient rounds and communicating with health care providers. Examples include rounding processes led by hand hygiene champions, champions in central line care, and antibiotic stewardship champions.

N0W-TP0.title: Antibiotic stewardship
N0W-TP0.description: A coordinated effort to evaluate and improve the prescribing of antibiotics by implementing measures that encourage the proper selection and use of antibiotic regimens to reduce antibiotic resistance and adverse effects. Elements may include monitoring appropriate antibiotic choice and dosage, providing educational resources, and antibiotic audits.

m0WVgP0.title: Office for Human Research Protection
m0WVgP0.description: A part of the United States Department of Health and Human Services whose mission is to protect the rights, welfare, and wellbeing of human subjects involved in research. Provides regulatory oversight and recommendations on ethical and regulatory issues in research.

50WigP0.title: Vulnerable population
50WigP0.description: A population that has insufficient ability to protect or advocate for their own interests (e.g., due to a lack of resources, education, and/or ability). Examples of vulnerable populations include non-English speakers, children, and individuals without capacity.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Research ethics

M0WMgP0.title: Strychnine
M0WMgP0.description: A plant alkaloid that can be found in herbal medications, rodenticides, and as an adulterant in illicit drugs. Toxicity results in mydriasis, hyperreflexia and clonus, stiffness of facial and neck muscles, and characteristic tonic-clonic seizures with preserved alertness throughout and after the seizure.

n0W7gP0.title: Cystoisospora belli
n0W7gP0.description: A gastrointestinal protozoan that can cause nonbloody diarrhea, particularly in patients who are immunocompromised. Transmitted via ingestion of sporulated oocysts.

L0WwgP0.title: Eteplirsen
L0WwgP0.description: A drug that binds to exon 51 of dystrophin premessenger RNA. As a result, this exon is excluded from mRNA processing, resulting in the production of truncated dystrophin protein. Used to increase the production of partially functional dystrophin in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

o0W0SP0.title: Universal decolonization protocol
o0W0SP0.description: A set of measures that are recommended for patients in intensive care units. Includes twice daily application of intranasal mupirocin for the first 5 days of hospital stay and daily chlorhexidine baths (instead of soap and water). It is the most effective strategy to prevent nosocomial methicillin-resistant S. aureus infections.

K0WUSP0.title: AIN
K0WUSP0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Anal intraepithelial neoplasia
2. Acute interstitial nephritis
3. Anterior interosseous nerve

60WjSP0.title: AIS
60WjSP0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Androgen insensitivity syndrome
2. Adenocarcinoma in situ
3. Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis

70W4hP0.title: Nondirective counseling
70W4hP0.description: A counseling approach in which the clinician takes a neutral part in the decision-making process by assisting the patient in making decisions in accordance with the patient's own views and beliefs.

H0WKhP0.title: Body donation
H0WKhP0.description: The donation of a deceased patient's body for medical education or research.

s0WthP0.title: Documentation of death
s0WthP0.description: The health care information generated after the death of a patient. Includes the death note, death summary, and death certificate.

G0WBhP0.title: Coroner
G0WBhP0.description: An elected government official tasked with running investigations to determine the cause, time, and manner of deaths that occurred under unexpected, violent, and/or suspicious circumstances or in the absence of a physician. Coroners declare death, issue death certificates, initiate inquests, and request medicolegal autopsies. They are not required to have medical training. Qualifications, functions, and authority vary by state.

t0WX3P0.title: Medical examiner
t0WX3P0.description: A medically trained government official tasked with running investigations to determine the cause, time, and manner of deaths that occurred under unexpected, violent, and/or suspicious circumstances or in the absence of a physician. Unlike coroners, medical examiners are board-certified specialists (usually pathologists) who are trained to perform autopsies. Qualifications, functions, and authority vary by state.

F0Wg3P0.title: Death investigation office
F0Wg3P0.description: An appointed or elected government official that leads investigations to determine the cause of deaths that occurred under unexpected, violent, and/or suspicious circumstances. They also declare death, issue death certificates, initiate inquests, and request autopsies. Depending on the state, these investigators can either be medical examiners or coroners.

80WO3P0.title: Horizontal gaze palsy
80WO3P0.description: The inability to move both eyes in a single horizontal direction. Most commonly caused by injury to the pons (horizontal gaze center, 6th cranial nerve nucleus) due to stroke. More common than vertical gaze palsy.

u0Wp3P0.title: One-and-a-half syndrome
u0Wp3P0.description: A syndrome characterized by the combination of a horizontal gaze palsy with internuclear ophthalmoplegia on horizontal gaze in the opposite direction. Can be caused by injury to the paramedian pontine reticular formation.

E0W83P0.title: Dissociated nystagmus
E0W83P0.description: A type of nystagmus that is worse in one eye and lacks rhythmic concordance between the two eyes. Can be caused by internuclear ophthalmoplegia.

v0WA3P0.title: Saccadic pursuit
v0WA3P0.description: The impairment of normal smooth pursuit with compensatory catch-up saccades.

w0WhRP0.title: Ventriculostomy
w0WhRP0.description: A neurosurgical procedure involving the creation of an opening into the ventricles of the brain through which devices for cerebrospinal fluid drainage and/or monitoring can be inserted (e.g., external ventricular drains, ventriculoperitoneal shunts). Commonly used in the management of obstructive hydrocephalus and intracranial hypertension.

90WNRP0.title: Nonasthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis
90WNRP0.description: A respiratory condition characterized by eosinophilic inflammation of the bronchi. Symptoms include cough, wheezing, and dyspnea, and sputum eosinophilia is a characteristic finding. Usually has a good response to corticosteroids. Unlike in asthma and COPD, there is no obstruction or airway hyperresponsiveness in nonasthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis.

YaWnQP0.title: APC
YaWnQP0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Activated protein C
2. Adenomatous polyposis coli
3. Antigen-presenting cell
4. Argon plasma coagulation
5. Atrial premature contraction
6. Anaphase-promoting complex

baWHQP0.title: Positive occipital sharp transients of sleep
baWHQP0.description: Physiological EEG pattern consisting of sharp, occipital, positive waves (may be isolated or grouped together with a frequency of 4–5 Hz). Indicates tired state or stage 2 of NREM sleep.

caWajP0.title: Slow activity
caWajP0.description: A nonspecific, pathologic EEG pattern consisting of a background (baseline) frequency of < 8 Hz in an awake adult. Indicates disturbed brain function.

1aW2jP0.title: Paroxysmal discharge
1aW2jP0.description: A general term used to describe any EEG pattern of electrical activity that begins suddenly and stands out from the background electrical activity of the brain (e.g., spikes, sharp waves, etc.). Considered an epileptiform discharge.

daWojP0.title: Vertex waves
daWojP0.description: A physiological EEG pattern consisting of rapidly-rising, triphasic, positive, low-amplitude waveforms. Mostly bilateral and symmetric. Best seen at the vertex and occurs primarily in stage 1 of REM sleep.

VaWGjP0.title: Sharp wave
VaWGjP0.description: A pathological EEG pattern consisting of a rapidly rising wave between 70 and 200 ms. Considered an interictal epileptiform discharge and indicates epilepsy.

eaWxjP0.title: Spike (EEG)
eaWxjP0.description: A pathological EEG pattern consisting of a steeply sloped peak < 70 ms. Considered an interictal epileptiform discharge and indicates epilepsy.

UaWbPP0.title: Cervical leiomyoma
UaWbPP0.description: A leiomyoma located in the cervix (not the body of the uterus). Can be seen as an enlargement of the cervix on speculum examination.

media.title: Overview of uterine leiomyoma types and location

2aWTPP0.title: Polyspike
2aWTPP0.description: A pathological EEG pattern of waves and many spikes in rapid succession. Referred to as a polyspike wave complex if followed by slow waves.

SaWyPP0.title: Brainstem auditory evoked potential
SaWyPP0.description: The electrical response of the brain, as measured by electroencephalography, in response to auditory stimuli.

haWc4P0.title: Somatosensory evoked potential
haWc4P0.description: The electrical response of the brain, as measured by electroencephalography, in response to electrical stimulation of superficial nerves (e.g., tibial nerve).

3aWS4P0.title: Door-to-balloon time
3aWS4P0.description: A performance metric for the management of acute coronary syndrome. Refers to the time elapsed between arrival to the hospital and inflation of the balloon during percutaneous coronary intervention. Should ideally be < 90 minutes and not exceed 120 minutes.

iaWJ4P0.title: Cranial nerve reflexes
iaWJ4P0.description: A group of reflexes triggered by stimulation of the cranial nerves. Includes the pupillary reflex, corneal reflex, conjunctival reflex, lacrimation reflex, jaw jerk reflex, gag reflex, and cough reflex.

jaW_4P0.title: Finger-to-finger test
jaW_4P0.description: A test of coordination that evaluates for limb (appendicular) ataxia. Patients are tasked with alternating between touching their nose and the examiner's finger as quickly as possible. The examiner can move their finger to accentuate deficits. Cerebellar lesions typically manifest with ipsilateral dysmetria and/or intention tremor.

4aW3kP0.title: Neurophysiological diagnostics
4aW3kP0.description: A group of tests that assess nerve, muscle, and/or brain function. Includes electroencephalography, nerve conduction studies, and electromyography.

maWVOP0.title: Average risk of CRC
maWVOP0.description: Individuals with no prior history of colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, or adenomatous polyps and no family history of hereditary colon cancer syndromes (e.g., HNPCC, familial adenomatous polyposis) are considered to be at average risk of developing colorectal cancer.

5aWiOP0.title: Workload capacity
5aWiOP0.description: A concept in human factors engineering. Defined as the amount of cognitive processing power that is available to perform a task. Represented schematically as the difference between total cognitive capacity and mental workload (cognitive load). Calculated based on response times to target detection tasks using a systems factorial approach or linear ballistic accumulator approach.

MaWMOP0.title: CD4 count
MaWMOP0.description: A laboratory test that determines the proportion of CD-4 T lymphocytes in serum, expressed as a number of cells per volume unit (cells/cubic mm). Primarily used to assess and monitor the degree of immunosuppression and response to antiretroviral therapy in patients with HIV. Normal values lie in the range of 500-1400, while a CD4 count of < 200 suggests advanced HIV.

naW7OP0.title: Induced abortion
naW7OP0.description: The use of interventions (e.g., medications, procedures) to end a pregnancy.

paWLlP0.title: HFE
paWLlP0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Human factors engineering
2. High FE2+ gene or protein (hemochromatosis gene or protein)

qaWClP0.title: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder
qaWClP0.description: A spectrum of neurological disorders, ranging from mild impairment to dementia, seen in patients who are HIV-positive.

IaWYNP0.title: Opioid-induced neurotoxicity
IaWYNP0.description: A syndrome characterized by acute delirium, myoclonus, hallucinations, and hyperalgesia in individuals with a history of chronic morphine, hydromorphone, or hydrocodone use. It is believed to result from the accumulation of active metabolites of these opioids over time.

7aW4NP0.title: Mortuary
7aW4NP0.description: A place where dead bodies are stored and prepared for burial, or cremation. Mortuaries are usually private businesses that allow friends and family to visit the deceased and hold funeral ceremonies.

taWXmP0.title: Usability testing
taWXmP0.description: A technique used to evaluate a product's ability to meet its intended purpose by testing it in real conditions with users who can give input on its accessibility and function (e.g., providing novel laparoscopic surgery devices for use during nonsimulated procedures).

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medical errors

FaWgmP0.title: Sexual health forensic examination
FaWgmP0.description: An examination performed by trained specialists after a sexual assault. Involves a thorough assessment for signs of trauma, documentation using standardized forms, and collection of evidence in a timely fashion to prevent loss of evidence (e.g., due to changing clothes, showering, or urinating).

8aWOmP0.title: Sexual assault nurse examiner
8aWOmP0.description: A nurse who has received specialized training in the forensic and medical examination of individuals who have been sexually assaulted.

uaWpmP0.title: Sexual assault forensic evaluation kit
uaWpmP0.description: A kit that contains instructions, documents, and evidence collection equipment for the forensic evaluation of individuals who have have been subjected to sexual assault. Evidence collection equipment includes bags for the individual's clothing, a comb to collect hair and fiber samples, and materials for fluid collection.

EaW8mP0.title: Mental workload
EaW8mP0.description: A concept in human factors engineering defined as the amount of cognitive processing power that is required to perform the task(s) that one is engaged in. Depends on the number of tasks, their complexity, and the familiarity/level of experience with the given task(s). Measures such as the time-to-completion, error rate for time-constrained tasks, task-invoked pupillary responses are often used as surrogate measures for cognitive workload.

vaWAmP0.title: Paget cell
vaWAmP0.description: A malignant intraepithelial cell with abundant pale cytoplasm and large nuclei. In Paget disease of the breast, Paget cells are typically found as single cells or groups of cells in the epidermis of the nipple.

DaW15P0.title: Thrombophilia testing
DaW15P0.description: A collection of laboratory and genetic studies used to evaluate for a predisposition to intravascular thrombosis. Can include an antiphospholipid antibody panel; activity assays for protein C, protein S, antithrombin; and genetic tests for conditions like factor V Leiden disease or prothrombin gene mutations.

waWh5P0.title: Occult breast cancer
waWh5P0.description: A rare type of breast cancer characterized by the presence of metastatic disease (e.g., axillary metastases) without an identifiable primary breast tumor after full diagnostic workup.

CaWq5P0.title: Reducing subsequent stroke risk
CaWq5P0.description: A set of preventive measures that should be initiated in patients after an ischemic stroke to reduce subsequent stroke risk. Measures include antiplatelet therapy, blood pressure management, and blood glucose management.

destinations.label: Ischemic stroke → Reducing subsequent stroke risk

BaWz5P0.title: Rh blood group, D antigen
BaWz5P0.description: The most common Rh antigen. Pregnant individuals who are RhD-negative and exposed to RhD-positive red blood cells can develop anti-D antibodies.

yaWdMP0.title: High alert medication
yaWdMP0.description: A medication that bears a high risk of causing serious patient harm (e.g., due to a narrow therapeutic range or potential for severe adverse effects).

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medication errors

AaWRMP0.title: Morgue
AaWRMP0.description: A hospital room or building in which the bodies of deceased individuals are kept pending autopsy, identification, or transport.

_aW5MP0.title: Cold agglutinin hemolytic anemia
_aW5MP0.description: A group of autoimmune disorders characterized by hemolysis that is caused by the binding of cold-sensitive autoantibodies to red blood cells. Includes cold agglutinin disease, a primary (idiopathic) disorder, and cold agglutinin syndrome, which occurs secondary to another clinical condition (e.g., infection, lymphoma). In these disorders, hemolysis is often triggered by low body temperature and/or cold ambient temperatures.

destinations.label: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia → Cold agglutinin hemolytic anemia

zaWrMP0.title: RHD
zaWrMP0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Rheumatic heart disease
2. Rh(D) antigen
3. Rh disease

-aWDMP0.title: Board order
-aWDMP0.description: A disciplinary action that is initiated by a state medical licensing board against a licensee. Can range from additional education (remediation) to monetary fines and the suspension or revocation of the medical license. May be disclosed to the public at the discretion of the state medical licensing board.

aYWQnP0.title: Wrong dose medication error
aYWQnP0.description: A medication error that involves the prescription, preparation, dispensation, and/or administration of the wrong quantity of a medication.

YYWnnP0.title: Wrong route medication error
YYWnnP0.description: A medication error involving the administration of medication via a different route than intended (e.g., intravenous administration of an intramuscular drug). These errors can result in potentially life-threatening complications.

XYW9nP0.title: Hospital emergency code
XYW9nP0.description: A term that quickly and unambiguously describes different types of on-site medical emergencies that require immediate action. Although codes are not universally standardized in the US, most hospitals use similar codes (e.g. code blue for adult medical emergency or cardiac arrest).

WYWPLP0.title: Timed Up and Go test
WYWPLP0.description: A test used to assess mobility and fall risk in the elderly. The patient is asked to get up from a chair, walk a distance of 3 meters, turn around, walk back, and sit down again. The time from getting up to reseating is recorded and compared with the mean time of the respective age group.

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Screening for geriatric syndromes

dYWoLP0.title: State medical licensing provisions
dYWoLP0.description: A set of laws that authorize the state medical boards to establish and govern the licensure process for physicians and physician assistants as well as the practice of medicine by these licensees in their state.

VYWGLP0.title: Hektoen enteric agar
VYWGLP0.description: A culture medium that contains proteose peptone, various sugars (e.g., lactose, sucrose, salicin), sodium thiosulfate, and iron (III) ammonium citrate. Used to identify and differentiate between Shigella (which grows as green colonies) and Salmonella (which grows as black colonies).

fYWkoP0.title: Endometrial ablation
fYWkoP0.description: The surgical destruction of the uterine lining. Used to treat heavy menstrual bleeding in patients who do not wish to preserve fertility.

gYWFoP0.title: Self-referral
gYWFoP0.description:
A term that can refer to: 
1.  The act of a patient who initiates a referral to a specialist on their own (i.e., without a primary care physician’s referral). 
2. The practice of referring a patient to a facility or another provider with which the referring physician or their family members have financial relationships. Prohibited by the Stark law.

SYWyoP0.title: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services
SYWyoP0.description: A federal agency that is a part of the Department of Health and Human Services and administers government insurance services, such as Medicare, Medicaid, and the Children's Health insurance program. Previously called the Health Care Financing Administration.

hYWcKP0.title: Modified radical vulvectomy
hYWcKP0.description: A surgical procedure in which parts of the vulva and sometimes the inguinofemoral lymph nodes are removed. Less invasive compared to radical vulvectomy. It is the preferred treatment option in patients with invasive vulvar carcinoma.

3YWSKP0.title: Billing fraud
3YWSKP0.description: The intentional billing for reimbursement of services that have not been rendered, have been rendered inadequately, and/or have been performed unnecessarily.

RYWlKP0.title: Incompetence
RYWlKP0.description:
A term that can refer to: 
1. The inability of an individual or organization to perform a task at an expected performance level as a result of a deficiency in knowledge and/or skill 
2. The inability of a structure to function as expected (e.g., cervical incompetence, venous incompetence, valvular incompetence)
3. A legal term that describes the inability to make decisions regarding one's health care

oYW0JP0.title: Breast architectural distortion
oYW0JP0.description: A radiologic sign characterized by a tethered/indented appearance of the normal breast parenchyma due to an invisible mass. Visible with breast ultrasonography, MRI, and mammography. This finding can be independent or associated with other structural abnormalities. Etiologies include radial scars, fat necrosis, sclerosing adenosis, and breast cancer.

KYWUJP0.title: Adrenal suppression
KYWUJP0.description: A decrease in endogenous glucocorticoid production following the administration of glucocorticoids. Adrenal suppression can occur after as little as 2 weeks of oral, parenteral, or inhaled corticosteroid therapy. It can lead to an adrenal crisis in the presence of physiologic stress like infections, in the perioperative period, or if prolonged glucocorticoid therapy is discontinued suddenly.

destinations.label: Glucocorticoids → Preventing complications of glucocorticoid therapy

6YWjJP0.title: Rescue medication
6YWjJP0.description: An emergency drug that provides immediate and potentially life-saving relief from acute symptoms. Examples include lorazepam for epileptic seizures and albuterol for asthma exacerbation.

pYWLJP0.title: Seronegative rheumatoid arthritis
pYWLJP0.description: A term to identify patients with rheumatoid arthritis who have normal rheumatoid factor and anticitrullinated peptide antibodies. In general, these patients have a better prognosis and fewer extraarticular manifestations than those with positive antibodies. Alternative diagnoses should always be considered (e.g., psoriatic arthritis, lupus arthritis, gout).

qYWCJP0.title: Ultrasonography-based cervical insufficiency
qYWCJP0.description: The inability of the uterine cervix to retain a pregnancy in the second trimester, which can lead to abortion and premature birth. Ultrasonography-based cervical insufficiency is diagnosed in women with a history of one preterm birth with mild symptoms (e.g., pelvic pressure, premenstrual-like cramping) and a cervix length < 25 mm seen on transvaginal ultrasonography.

IYWYqP0.title: Therapeutic hypothermia
IYWYqP0.description: A treatment in which the core body temperature is lowered (e.g., using chilled intravenous fluids) to ≤ 35°C to decrease the metabolic rate and improve recovery following ischemic conditions that affect highly oxygen-dependent tissue (e.g., brain, heart). Indications include neonatal hypoxic encephalopathy. Recommended temperature varies by indication.

destinations.label: Secondary brain injury and neuroprotective measures → Neurogenic fever and targeted temperature management

rYWfqP0.title: Boyle's law
rYWfqP0.description: A physical law that states that when the pressure exerted upon a gas is multiplied by the volume of the gas, a constant number is achieved (PV = c). If the pressure (P) increases, the volume of the gas (V) must decrease.

7YW4qP0.title: Mild ascites
7YW4qP0.description: Ascites only detectable by ultrasound. Also referred to as grade 1 ascites.

HYWKqP0.title: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation
HYWKqP0.description: A rare, congenital birth defect of the lower respiratory tract characterized by abnormal development of the tracheobronchial tree resulting in cystic and adenomatous masses in the trachea and lung. Previously known as congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation (CCAM).

FYWgIP0.title: Physical examination-based cervical insufficiency
FYWgIP0.description: The inability of the uterine cervix to retain a pregnancy in the second trimester, which can lead to abortion and premature birth. Examination-based cervical insufficiency is diagnosed in women with cervical dilatation on digital or speculum inspection. If the dilation is ≥ 2 cm, amniocentesis is performed to check for intraamniotic infection.

vYWAIP0.title: Two-stage exchange arthroplasty
vYWAIP0.description: A two-stage surgical procedure used to treat prosthetic joint infections. The initial stage involves the debridement and complete removal of prosthetic material and, in many cases, the placement of an antimicrobial-impregnated cement spacer into the dead space. The second stage involves implantation of new prothesis weeks to months after the initial procedure.

DYW1rP0.title: Tunneled central venous catheter
DYW1rP0.description: A central venous line in which several centimeters of the catheter follow a subcutaneous course, forming a tunnel between the entry point to the skin (usually the pectoral area) and the venous puncture site (usually the internal jugular vein). Typically used for long-term fluid and medication administration or hemodialysis due to a lower risk of infection and higher durability than nontunneled catheters.

destinations.label: Vascular access → Long-term central venous access

media.title: Central venous catheters for renal replacement therapy

wYWhrP0.title: Neonatal anesthetic toxicity
wYWhrP0.description: A rare complication that can occur in a neonate after a pudendal block was administered to the mother during labor. Symptoms include apnea, cyanosis, hypotonia, seizures, mydriasis, seizures, bradycardia, and a prolonged QT interval.

9YWNrP0.title: Role incompatibility
9YWNrP0.description: A type of conflict that may be intrapersonal (i.e., caused by incompatible demands placed upon one person due to different roles they hold) or interpersonal (caused by incompatible goals between individuals).

BYWzrP0.title: Post-Q fever fatigue syndrome
BYWzrP0.description: A common sequelae of acute Q fever. Clinical features include fatigue, headache, night sweats, arthralgia, myalgia, fasciculations, blurred vision, and painful lymphadenopathy.

destinations.label: Q fever → Acute Q fever vs. chronic Q fever

yYWd7P0.title: Clinical peer review activity
yYWd7P0.description: A process in which health care providers from a specific professional competency evaluate the performance of one or more of their own peers. Includes activities of morbidity and mortality reviews and quality assurance committees. In order to increase participation in and the effectiveness of these activities, the Health Care Quality Improvement Act protects the information generated by such activities, when performed in good faith, from legal discovery.

ZbWZHP0.title: Synovitis
ZbWZHP0.description: Inflammation of the synovial membrane that lines the joint capsule. Most commonly manifests with arthralgia, erythema, warmth, tenderness to palpation, and swelling. Typically occurs in rheumatoid arthritis and other types of inflammatory arthritis.

0bWeHP0.title: General anesthesia
0bWeHP0.description: A state of pharmacologically induced unconsciousness, characterized by a lack of response even to painful stimuli. Typically accompanied by loss of protective reflexes, airway patency, and spontaneous respiration. General anesthesia may also lead to impaired cardiovascular function.

YbWnHP0.title: Somatropin
YbWnHP0.description: A recombinant polypeptide identical to human growth hormone. Used to treat growth failure (e.g., due to growth hormone deficiency, idiopathic short stature, or Turner syndrome).

bbWHHP0.title: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children
bbWHHP0.description: A syndrome seen in children with COVID-19 that manifests with features of severe inflammation and multiorgan failure. Should be suspected in individuals < 21 years of age who test positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection and present with fever, laboratory evidence of inflammation, severe illness requiring hospitalization, and multisystem (> 2) organ involvement in the absence of another plausible diagnosis.

1bW2sP0.title: Tidal irrigation
1bW2sP0.description: The repeated distension and irrigation of a body cavity with sterile fluid. Most commonly performed in joint cavities to evacuate infectious and purulent material in septic arthritis or provide symptomatic relief.

VbWGsP0.title: Scrub typhus
VbWGsP0.description: An infectious disease caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi that is transmitted through the bites by larval mites (chiggers). Manifestations include fever, headache, myalgia, and rash.

ebWxsP0.title: Brill-Zinsser disease
ebWxsP0.description: Recrudescence of a latent infection of epidemic louse-borne typhus, which can manifest months to years after the initial infection. Symptoms are usually milder than the original infection.

UbWbGP0.title: Chiggers
UbWbGP0.description: A colloquial term for Trombiculidae and Leeuwenhoekiidae mites in their larval stage. Chigger bites can cause focal dermatitis, and bites from the genus Leptotrombidium can transmit the bacteria that cause scrub typhus.

2bWTGP0.title: Appreciative Inquiry
2bWTGP0.description: An approach to engaging people in creating positive change and a shared vision for the future. Focused on identifying and further developing already-existing strengths rather than concentrating on deficits. Practically implemented by using the 4-D cycle (Discovery, Dream, Design, Destiny). AI is also used at an individual level as part of the collaborative conflict managing strategy (i.e., asking simple, positive questions to better understand the other party's position) and as a method of patient counseling (e.g., to encourage health behavior change).

PbWWFP0.title: Jones fracture
PbWWFP0.description: A fracture of the fifth metatarsal bone of the foot at the base of the shaft. It is the most common type of midfoot fracture.

destinations.label: General principles of fractures → Overview of common fractures

4bW3FP0.title: Hepatoportoenterostomy
4bW3FP0.description: A surgery that removes damaged and blocked bile ducts and replaces the structures with a segment of the small intestine. Often used as a bridge towards liver transplant. It is the treatment of choice for neonates with biliary atresia.

destinations.label: Congenital visceral malformations → Biliary tract malformations

ObWIFP0.title: Pimavanserin
ObWIFP0.description: An atypical antipsychotic that acts as a selective serotonin 5-HT2A receptor inverse agonist. Used to treat hallucinations and delusions associated with Parkinson disease psychosis.

NbW-FP0.title: Fetal fibronectin test
NbW-FP0.description: A test used to measure the level of fibronectin, a protein that attaches the fetal amniotic sac to the uterus. An increased fetal fibronectin (fFN) concentration in cervicovaginal fluid may indicate an increased risk of preterm birth. Often used in conjunction with cervical length measurement.

mbWV8P0.title: Cystoisosporiasis
mbWV8P0.description: An infection caused by Cystoisospora (formerly known as Isospora). Manifests with watery, nonbloody diarrhea, which can be debilitating for immunocompromised individuals. In individuals with HIV, cystoisosporiasis is an AIDS-defining condition.

5bWi8P0.title: Time of death
5bWi8P0.description: The time at which the final examination of the deceased is concluded and confirms death.

MbWM8P0.title: Tick bite prevention
MbWM8P0.description: Measures to prevent tick bites. Includes avoiding grassy or brushy areas where ticks may be found, wearing protective clothing (e.g., pants; long-sleeve shirts, tucked in), using tick repellent, and checking clothing and body for ticks after being outdoors.

nbW78P0.title: Suicide safety plan
nbW78P0.description: A document that outlines a plan of support for individuals who are at risk of suicide. Typically structured in several steps, including recognizing warning signs, using coping strategies, and contacting professionals. Individuals who agree to use a safety plan may still be at risk of suicide.

obW0uP0.title: Situational awareness test
obW0uP0.description: A test that uses subjective and objective measures to determine the level of situational awareness (SA) of an individual or team. Product-oriented SA tests, such as the real-time probe test and the task interruption test (Situation Awareness Global Assessment Technique), make direct SA measurements. Process-oriented tests, such as physiologic indices (e.g., eye tracking) and trained observer ratings, infer SA levels based on indirect measures.

KbWUuP0.title: Change impact analysis
KbWUuP0.description: An analysis technique in which the links between aspects of a system (traces) are identified, and the impact of a change in one aspect of a system on others (dependencies) is assessed.

6bWjuP0.title: Onset-to-door time
6bWjuP0.description: A performance metric for the management of acute ischemic conditions (e.g., acute coronary syndrome, stroke). Refers to the time elapsed between the onset of ischemic symptoms and arrival at the hospital. An increase in this time correlates with a worse prognosis.

JbWsuP0.title: Default surrogate decision-maker
JbWsuP0.description: An individual who is designated based on a legally established hierarchy to make health care decisions for a patient who lacks capacity and has no advance directives. Generally, this hierarchy prioritizes spouses, then adult children, parents, siblings, and close friends. In some states, third parties (e.g., ethics committees) may be appointed if no other surrogate is available.

qbWCuP0.title: Singleton pregnancy
qbWCuP0.description: A pregnancy that results in the development and birth of a single fetus.

IbWYEP0.title: Amniotic fluid tests for fetal lung maturity
IbWYEP0.description: A group of tests that assess components of surfactant and surfactant production, thereby providing a surrogate parameter for fetal lung maturity. Used in high-risk patients where the gestational age is unknown and the risk of fetal lung immaturity is high. Tests include lamellar body count, measurement of phosphatidylglycerol, the lecithin/sphingomyelin ratio, the foam stability index, and the surfactant/albumin ratio.

EbW8vP0.title: Doppler velocimetry of the umbilical artery
EbW8vP0.description: An ultrasonographic study used to assess for placental insufficiency in pregnant individuals with fetal growth restriction. Reduced or reversed end-diastolic flow indicates placental insufficiency.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Antepartum fetal surveillance testing

wbWhDP0.title: Simplified Disease Activity Index
wbWhDP0.description: A validated disease activity scoring system recommended by the ACR for patients with rheumatoid arthritis. It is used to classify the disease into one of four categories: low, moderate, or severe disease activity, or remission, taking into account the patient and evaluator global assessments, CRP levels, and the results of a 28-joint physical examination.

media.title: Simplified Disease Activity Index for RA (SDAI)

9bWNDP0.title: Clinical Disease Activity Index
9bWNDP0.description: A validated disease activity scoring system recommended by the ACR for patients with rheumatoid arthritis. It is used to classify the disease into one of four categories: low, moderate, or severe disease activity, or remission, taking into account the patient and evaluator global assessments and the results of a 28-joint physical examination.

media.title: Clinical Disease Activity Index for RA (CDAI)

CbWqDP0.title: Disease Activity Score with 28-joint count
CbWqDP0.description: A validated scoring system recommended by the ACR for patients with rheumatoid arthritis. It is used to classify the disease into one of four categories: low, moderate, or severe disease activity, or remission, taking into account the patient global assessment, CRP or ESR levels, and the results of a 28-joint physical examination.

xbWEDP0.title: Wooden chest syndrome
xbWEDP0.description: An uncommon adverse event induced by opioids during which decreased chest wall compliance and abdominal muscle rigidity leads to impaired ventilation (spontaneous or assisted). Typically associated with high doses of fentanyl but can occur with other opioids.

BbWzDP0.title: Alfentanil
BbWzDP0.description: A short-acting analgesic that is a less potent derivate of fentanyl. Commonly used during procedural sedation because of its almost immediate onset of action.

AbWRwP0.title: Ketofol
AbWRwP0.description: A term used to describe the combination of ketamine and propofol in various ratios (e.g., 1:1 or 1:2). Commonly used for procedural sedation and analgesia.

_bW5wP0.title: Nescient error
_bW5wP0.description: A type of active error that is committed as a result of a knowledge deficit, which can cause an individual to intentionally and in good faith perform an action (or choose not to perform one) based on their existing fund of knowledge and expect a different outcome than the one that would most likely occur. Can be prevented by personnel training (e.g., continued medical education seminars).

zbWrwP0.title: Henry's law
zbWrwP0.description: A physical law that determines the solubility of an ideal gas in a liquid. For an ideal gas at a constant temperature, the concentration of the gas dissolved in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas at the gas-liquid interface. Represented mathematically as C = k x P, in which C is the concentration of dissolved gas, k is the Henry law constant for the gas-liquid system at a particular temperature, and P is the partial pressure of the gas.

-bWDwP0.title: Workaround
-bWDwP0.description: A temporary or quick solution that bypasses a flaw in a system or a limitation in a process but does not address the underlying problem(s). Their use in health care systems is pervasive but can negatively impact patient safety in the long term. Can be completely eliminated only by a forcing function, but excessive use of forcing functions in a system or process that is highly reliant on workarounds can cause the entire system or process to fail.

UXWbxP0.title: Cold agglutinin
UXWbxP0.description: A type of autoantibody against a red blood cell antigen that activates at a temperature < 37°C and causes red blood cell agglutination and hemolysis.

destinations.label: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia → Cold agglutinin hemolytic anemia

2XWTxP0.title: Uniform Anatomical Gifts Act
2XWTxP0.description: A US law that regulates the use of bodies and anatomic parts for organ donation, research, and training.

3XWSBP0.title: Progesterone supplementation
3XWSBP0.description: A medication used to treat amenorrhea, infertility, and premenstrual syndrome. May also help to prevent preterm labor by enhancing the natural progesterone pathways responsible for pregnancy maintenance. Can be given intramuscularly, orally, or vaginally.

QXWuBP0.title: Contemplation stage
QXWuBP0.description: The second stage in the transtheoretical model of behavioral change, in which an individual is aware of a problematic behavior but unwilling to change it.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

PXWWyP0.title: Preparation stage
PXWWyP0.description: The third stage in the transtheoretical model of behavioral change, in which an individual is preparing to make a behavioral change.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

4XW3yP0.title: Action stage
4XW3yP0.description: The fourth stage in the transtheoretical model of behavioral change, in which an individual demonstrates a change in behavior.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

kXWmyP0.title: Maintenance stage
kXWmyP0.description: The fifth stage in the transtheoretical model of behavioral change, in which an individual upholds behavioral changes and integrates them into the lifestyle. This stage may be permanent or individuals may relapse.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

OXWIyP0.title: Relapse stage
OXWIyP0.description: An optional stage in the transtheoretical model of behavioral change, in which an individual's achieved behavioral changes are reversed. Ideally, a new cycle of behavioral change is started subsequently, and individuals are able to learn from each relapse.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → General concepts of patient counseling

nXW7AP0.title: Epilepsy
nXW7AP0.description:
A chronic neurologic disorder characterized by a predisposition to seizures as defined by one of the following:
- Two or more unprovoked or reflex seizures separated by more than 24 hours
- One unprovoked or reflex seizure in an individual with a high risk of subsequent seizures (e.g., after traumatic brain injury, stroke, CNS infections)
- Diagnosis of an epilepsy syndrome: a group of epileptic disorders characterized by a set of features typically occurring together.

LXWwAP0.title: Reflex epilepsy
LXWwAP0.description: A subtype of epilepsy characterized by recurrent reflex seizures (i.e., seizures that are consistently provoked by a certain factor, such as flashing lights.

IXWYzP0.title: Mouth care
IXWYzP0.description: A multidisciplinary care plan that addresses oral symptoms (dry mouth, pain, dysphagia, and difficulty speaking) frequently found in patients who are frail, intubated, or receiving end-of-life care. Treatment may include facilitated routine care, frequent lip and mouth moistening, artificial saliva, analgesics, and antifungal therapy.

sXWtzP0.title: Fluoropyrimidine
sXWtzP0.description: A class of pyrimidine analog antimetabolite with antineoplastic and immunosuppressive effects. Fluoropyrimidines inhibit thymidylate synthase, which decreases the formation of thymine-containing deoxyribonucleotides. Agents include 5-fluorouracil, capecitabine, and tegafur.

GXWBzP0.title: Monitored anesthesia care
GXWBzP0.description: The administration of sedatives and analgesia by an individual (typically an anesthesiologist) who is exclusively responsible for sedating and monitoring the patient. Intubation is usually not required.

tXWX-P0.title: Carotid sinus hypersensitivity
tXWX-P0.description: An exaggerated parasympathetic response to carotid sinus stimulation (e.g., tight collar, carotid sinus massage) characterized by a cardiac pause of ≥ 3 seconds and/or a drop in systolic blood pressure ≥ 50 mm Hg. Clinically, it can manifest with episodes of lightheadedness, presyncope, syncope, or sudden falls.

8XWO-P0.title: Neonatal myasthenia gravis
8XWO-P0.description: A self-limited condition caused by the transplacental transfer of acetylcholine receptor antibodies. Clinical features include hypotonia, poor sucking, and respiratory distress. Symptoms are transient and terminate once maternal antibodies are cleared. Management is based on the severity of the condition and can include acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, plasmapheresis, or IV IgG.

EXW8-P0.title: Active phase of labor
EXW8-P0.description: The second phase of the first stage of labor, in which the dilation of the cervix proceeds more quickly. At a dilation of ≥ 6 cm, the majority of women are in active labor, and the rate of dilation is approximately 1.2–1.5 cm per hour.

vXWA-P0.title: Lung point
vXWA-P0.description: Visible lung sliding (healthy lung) adjacent to an area without visible lung sliding (pneumothorax) on ultrasound. Pathognomonic for pneumothorax but may be absent in large pneumothorax.

CXWqZ40.title: Conjunctival reflex
CXWqZ40.description: A cranial reflex elicited by irritation of the conjunctiva. Normal response is eye closure due to contraction of the orbicularis oculi muscle.

xXWEZ40.title: Lacrimation reflex
xXWEZ40.description: A cranial reflex elicited by irritation of the conjunctiva or cornea. Normal response is tearing.

_XW5040.title: Nociplastic pain
_XW5040.description: A type of pain that arises from altered nociception despite there being no clear evidence of underlying tissue damage.

zXWr040.title: Pulmonary artery systolic pressure
zXWr040.description: The pressure in the pulmonary artery during systole. Can be estimated noninvasively based on echocardiographic findings or measured directly during cardiac catheterization. PASP elevation is suggestive of pulmonary hypertension.

ZcWZa40.title: Invasive fetal heart rate monitoring
ZcWZa40.description: An invasive form of intrapartum electronic fetal heart rate monitoring in which an electrode is placed on the fetal scalp through the cervical canal. Can only be used after rupture of membranes has occurred.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

0cWea40.title: Ovarian cancer
0cWea40.description: A malignancy of the ovary that typically affects women > 55 years of age. It is the second most common gynecologic malignancy in the US after endometrial cancer.

2cWTb40.title: Red flags for back pain
2cWTb40.description: Includes severe or progressive neurological symptoms, risk factors for infection (e.g., immunosuppression, fever, intravenous drug use, glucocorticoid use, recent infection), recent trauma (e.g., injury or medical procedures), use of anticoagulants, risk factors for malignancy (e.g., unexplained weight loss, a history of cancer, age > 50 years), and findings of vascular pathology (e.g., abnormal vital signs, new murmur, pulsatile abdominal mass, unequal pulses or blood pressure).

destinations.label: Back pain → Red flags for back pain

gcWFb40.title: Intrauterine pressure catheter
gcWFb40.description: A device placed transvaginally in the uterine cavity during labor to assess the frequency, duration, and strength of uterine contractions. Typically used in situations in which external assessment of uterine contractions is challenging (e.g., moving patients, obese patients). Can also facilitate amnioinfusion.

ScWyb40.title: Compromise (conflict management strategy)
ScWyb40.description: A conflict management strategy aimed at finding a practical solution that partially satisfies both parties (lose-lose solution).

hcWcX40.title: Avoidance (conflict management strategy)
hcWcX40.description: A conflict management strategy in which one party ignores or withdraws from the conflict.

3cWSX40.title: Accommodation (conflict management strategy)
3cWSX40.description: A conflict management strategy in which one party acquiesces to the other instead of prioritizing their own interests.

RcWlX40.title: Competition (conflict management strategy)
RcWlX40.description: A conflict management strategy in which one party insists on pursuing their own interest despite the other one's resistance. While this approach may lead to a quick solution, it may damage the relationship with the other conflict party.

icWJX40.title: Collaboration (conflict management strategy)
icWJX40.description: A conflict management strategy in which both parties work together to find a mutually satisfying solution to a disagreement (win-win solution). This approach usually requires significant effort but helps to maintain a good relationship between the conflict parties and often leads to innovative solutions.

QcWuX40.title: Residual limb pain
QcWuX40.description: A condition characterized by pain proximal to the level of an amputation, which distinguishes it from phantom limb pain. Common causes include neuromas, soft tissue damage, infections, and vascular insufficiency.

jcW_X40.title: Overhead expenditure
jcW_X40.description: An expense incurred to support income-generating services while not directly generating income.

PcWWc40.title: Terminal agitation
PcWWc40.description: A syndrome occurring near the end of life that includes symptoms of cognitive decline, restlessness, altered affect, and/or hallucinations; it may be part of an unrecognized acute delirium. This is often distressing to both the patient and the family and needs to be addressed as part of comprehensive palliative care.

destinations.label: Overview of palliative medicine → Management of imminently dying patients

4cW3c40.title: Placental alpha microglobulin-1
4cW3c40.description: A protein that is released from decidual cells and found in high concentrations in amniotic fluid. Measurement of PAMG-1 in vaginal fluid can be used to support a diagnosis of premature rupture of membranes.

5cWi140.title: Lower urinary tract
5cWi140.description: The portion of the urinary tract that consists of the urethra and bladder with the addition of the prostate in male individuals. Its function is the storage and voluntary elimination of urine.

McWM140.title: Stable vertebral injury
McWM140.description: A vertebral fracture, dislocation, or ligamentous injury that does not impair the structural integrity of the spine. Spinal column elements remain resistant to displacement without the risk of further neurological damage or progressive deformity.

ncW7140.title: Unstable vertebral injury
ncW7140.description: A vertebral fracture, dislocation, or ligamentous injury that impairs the structural integrity of the spine and poses a risk of further neurological damage and/or progressive deformity.

LcWw140.title: Vulvovaginectomy
LcWw140.description: A surgical procedure in which some parts of the vulva and vagina are removed. Can be used to treat stage I vaginal cancer.

ocW0W40.title: Wide local excision
ocW0W40.description: A surgical procedure in which a skin lesion confined to the dermis or epidermis is removed along with a margin of healthy tissue surrounding the lesion.

HcWKd40.title: Contraindications for metformin
HcWKd40.description: Includes severely impaired renal function (eGFR < 30 mL/minute/1.73 m2), acute or chronic metabolic acidosis (including diabetic ketoacidosis), and hypersensitivity to metformin or any of its components.

scWtd40.title: Acute transfusion reaction
scWtd40.description: An immune or nonimmune-mediated adverse reaction that occurs during or within 24 hours of the transfusion of blood products.

GcWBd40.title: Delayed transfusion reaction
GcWBd40.description: An immune or nonimmune-mediated adverse reaction that occurs more than 24 hours after the transfusion of blood products. Can occur weeks to months after the transfusion.

tcWXV40.title: Large joints
tcWXV40.description: An operational definition frequently used in rheumatology when referring to the shoulder, elbow, hip, knee, and ankle joints.

FcWgV40.title: Small joints
FcWgV40.description: An operational definition frequently used in rheumatology when referring to the distal joints of the wrist, the metacarpophalangeal joints, metatarsophalangeal joints, and proximal interphalangeal joints of the hand and foot.

ucWpV40.title: Evaluator global assessment
ucWpV40.description: A tool for evaluators (e.g., a nurse or physician) to assess the disease severity of patients with conditions such as heart failure or rheumatoid arthritis. The evaluator assesses the patient’s current disease activity using a visual analog scale from 0 to 10, with 0 representing “not active” and 10 representing “extremely active”.

EcW8V40.title: Patient global assessment
EcW8V40.description: A tool to assess how conditions such as heart failure or rheumatoid arthritis impact patients' everyday lives. Patients' responses are measured on a visual analog scale from 0 to 10, with 0 representing minimal impact and 10 representing a large impact.

vcWAV40.title: Minimal sedation
vcWAV40.description: The administration of a sedative to induce a state of relaxation while maintaining normal responsiveness.

9cWNe40.title: Lung isolation
9cWNe40.description: The physical separation of one lung from the other in order to initiate and maintain one-lung ventilation. May be performed to facilitate intrathoracic surgery or to separate healthy lung tissue still capable of participating in gas exchange from lung tissue that is bleeding, infected, or compromised by a bronchopleural fistula. Lung isolation is performed with selective endobronchial intubation, a double-lumen endotracheal tube, or a bronchial blocker.

CcWqe40.title: Bronchial artery embolization
CcWqe40.description: A procedure in which coils or embolic material are inserted under fluoroscopic guidance into the bronchial arteries supplying distal blood vessels that are either actively bleeding or at risk of bleeding. Occlusion of the bronchial arteries usually leads to rapid resolution of hemoptysis.

destinations.label: Hemoptysis → Massive hemoptysis and life-threatening hemoptysis

BcWze40.title: CDAI
BcWze40.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Clinical Disease Activity Index (for rheumatoid arthritis)
2. Crohn Disease Activity Index

ycWdU40.title: Major bleeding
ycWdU40.description: A clinically significant hemorrhage, possibly life-threatening. Major bleeding is objectively defined as symptomatic bleeding in a critical area (e.g., intracranial) or as bleeding in any area that leads to a decrease in hemoglobin ≥ 2 g/dL, transfusion of ≥ 2 units of pRBCs, or death.

-cWDU40.title: Monoarthritis
-cWDU40.description: An inflammation of a singular joint. Manifestations include joint pain, swelling, warmth, erythema, and limited range of motion. Common etiologies include trauma, infection, and crystal deposition disease. Polyarthritic disorders may initially manifest with monoarthritis.

Z1WZ240.title: Arthritis
Z1WZ240.description: An inflammation of one or more joints. Manifestations include joint pain, swelling, warmth, erythema, and limited range of motion.

Y1Wn240.title: Knee-chest position
Y1Wn240.description: A position in which the individual is kneeling with the chest on the floor and the head turned to one side such that the knees and the hips form an "A." Used during labor to widen the pelvic space and diminish pressure on the symphysis. Also applied during intrauterine resuscitation measures to increase fetal oxygenation.

b1WH240.title: Formal ultrasound
b1WH240.description: An ultrasound performed by a radiologist or sonographer that typically takes place within the radiology department. A point of care ultrasound, by contrast, is generally performed at the bedside by a clinician (e.g., trained in critical care or emergency medicine).

11W2f40.title: Abdominal wall defects
11W2f40.description: A condition in which the abdominal wall is compromised in such a way that may lead to the protrusion of underlying organs. Congenital causes include omphalocele, gastroschisis, and umbilical hernia.

destinations.label: Congenital visceral malformations → Abdominal wall defects

e1Wxf40.title: Xpert® MTB/RIF assay
e1Wxf40.description: A highly specific assay that uses nucleic acid amplification to rapidly detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis genetic material and identifies mutations causing rifampin resistance. It is one of the most common molecular tests for the diagnosis of tuberculosis, but other assays with similar characteristics may be available depending on location.

U1WbT40.title: Loss of fetal station
U1WbT40.description: The repositioning of a fetal presenting part from its previous station back towards the abdomen. It is a characteristic feature of uterine rupture.

21WTT40.title: Lateral flow urine lipoarabinomannan assay
21WTT40.description: A nonsputum-based diagnostic test used to detect mycobacterial antigens in urine. Mainly used for HIV patients with severe disease and/or those with a CD4 count < 100 cells/mm³ for a rapid point-of-care diagnosis.

41W3S40.title: Classic symptoms of hyperglycemia
41W3S40.description: A condition of elevated blood glucose levels. Classically causes polyuria, polydipsia, and polyphagia.

O1WIS40.title: Obesity-related comorbidities
O1WIS40.description: A group of conditions frequently seen in patients with obesity, including type 2 diabetes mellitus, arterial hypertension, asthma, osteoarthritis, depression, and gastroesophageal reflux disease.

l1WvS40.title: Budesonide enema
l1WvS40.description: A rectal formulation of the synthetic steroid budesonide. Used to treat diarrhea and rectal bleeding in patients with inflammatory bowel disease that involves sites of inflammation in the rectum, sigmoid colon, and/or ascending colon.

51Wih40.title: Hypocontractile uterine dysfunction
51Wih40.description: A type of uterine dysfunction characterized by a decrease in frequency (< 3 contractions/10 minutes), duration (< 50 seconds), and/or intensity (< 200 Montevideo units within 10 minutes) of uterine contractions during the first stage of labor.

M1WMh40.title: Crenation
M1WMh40.description: The process of osmotic water diffusion out of a red blood cell, which changes the shape of its surface to a notched, spiky appearance.

61Wj340.title: Obstetric anal sphincter injuries
61Wj340.description: A third- or fourth-degree laceration that occurs during childbirth. These lacerations involve the anal sphincter and, in severe cases, the anal mucosa. Short-term complications include hemorrhage and infection. Long-term complications include urinary and/or fecal incontinence, chronic perineal pain, and dyspareunia.

J1Ws340.title: Spinal manipulation and mobilization
J1Ws340.description: A form of manual therapy for low back pain that is typically performed by physical therapists, osteopaths, and chiropractors to decrease pain and increase the range of joint motion and muscle relaxation. Spinal manipulation uses high-velocity low-amplitude manual thrusts to the spine at or just beyond the physiological range of motion, while spinal mobilization uses low-velocity small/large-amplitude passive movements within the physiological range of motion.

q1WC340.title: Complex ovarian cyst
q1WC340.description: An ovarian cyst with solid components, multiple fluid-filled areas, septations, thick walls, and/or hemorrhage. Compared to simple ovarian cysts, they are associated with a higher risk of malignancy and, therefore, require follow-up with serial ultrasonography or surgical exploration.

I1WYR40.title: Simple ovarian cyst
I1WYR40.description: A unilocular ovarian cyst that is filled with fluid, has no solid components, and has smooth thin walls. Ultrasound appearance is anechoic with acoustic enhancement. Associated with a low risk for malignancy.

r1WfR40.title: Acute back pain
r1WfR40.description: Acute onset of back pain lasting less than 4–6 weeks and most commonly due to nonspecific musculoskeletal pain. Less common causes include conditions of the spinal column (e.g., spinal cord compression, bone metastases, vertebral fractures) and referred pain from thoracic, abdominal, pelvic, retroperitoneal, or cardiovascular conditions. Acute back pain associated with new or rapidly progressive neurological abnormalities requires urgent intervention to prevent permanent neurological damage.

media.title: Degenerative disk disease with disk extrusion

H1WKR40.title: Single cover test
H1WKR40.description: A test used to detect manifest strabismus (heterotropia). One eye is covered for a few seconds and the uncovered eye is observed for a shift in fixation. Fixation shift in the uncovered eye indicates misalignment of that eye.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Cover tests

s1WtR40.title: Countries with a high burden of tuberculosis
s1WtR40.description: The 20 countries in the world estimated by the WHO to have the highest absolute number of TB cases (in alphabetical order) are Angola, Bangladesh, Brazil, China, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Kenya, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines, Russia, South Africa, Thailand, Tanzania, and Vietnam.

F1Wgi40.title: Cover tests
F1Wgi40.description: A type of ophthalmological examination used to detect the presence or degree of eye deviation in individuals with suspected eye misalignment. The examinee's eye is covered for a few seconds, and refixation movements are observed after the eye is uncovered.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Cover tests

81WOi40.title: Fundoscopy
81WOi40.description: A component of the eye examination in which an ophthalmoscope is used to visualize structures of the optical fundus, e.g., the retina, optic cup, optic disc, retinal vessels, macula, and fovea. Can be performed using direct ophthalmoscopy or indirect ophthalmoscopy.
