destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Fundoscopic exam

w1WhQ40.title: Nonspecific back pain
w1WhQ40.description: Back pain that cannot be attributed to a specific cause after a full evaluation. Patient history and physical examination reveal atraumatic back pain, normal neurological findings, and no red flag features for back pain.

91WNQ40.title: Radical vulvectomy
91WNQ40.description: A surgical procedure in which the entire vulva (i.e., clitoris, labia majora and minora, vulvar vestibule, vaginal introitus) and the inguinofemoral lymph nodes are removed. Usually performed in cases of vulvar dysplasia or malignancy.

C1WqQ40.title: Booster phenomenon
C1WqQ40.description: A tuberculin skin test (TST) finding that may be seen in individuals who are undergoing repeated TB testing (e.g., health care workers) if the initial TB infection was many years ago. The initial TST can give a falsely negative result due to waning immunity and is followed by a positive TST due to the initial test having stimulated or "boosted" immunity. Caution should be taken not to misinterpret booster phenomenon as an infection having occurred between the two tests.

B1WzQ40.title: Alternate cover test
B1WzQ40.description: A bedside examination to assess for latent strabismus. The patient is asked to fixate on a point, and the eyes are alternately occluded. A refixation movement of the occluded eye upon being uncovered indicates misalignment.

y1Wdj40.title: Calcium pyrophosphate crystals
y1Wdj40.description: A rhomboid-shaped, positively birefringent crystal that can be found in the synovial fluid of patients with calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease (pseudogout). These crystals form and deposit in articular cartilage and cause joint inflammation and cartilage destruction.

z1Wrj40.title: Migratory arthritis
z1Wrj40.description: A pattern of arthritis involving the rapid onset of synovitis in > 1 joint that resolves, followed by synovitis (usually asymmetrical) in other joints. Occurs in multiple conditions (e.g., acute rheumatic fever, early Lyme arthritis, reactive arthritis, disseminated gonococcal infection).

-1WDj40.title: Intermittent arthritis
-1WDj40.description: A pattern of arthritis characterized by recurring episodes (flares) of synovitis in > 1 joint. Occurs in gout and acute calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease.

WWWP440.title: Viral vector vaccine
WWWP440.description: A vaccine that uses a modified nonpathogenic virus to induce an immune response in the host. Examples include the rVSV-ZEBOV Ebola vaccine and the Janssen (Johnson & Johnson) COVID-19 vaccine.

media.title: Mechanism of action of viral vector-based COVID-19 vaccines

eWWx440.title: Interpersonal role incompatibility
eWWx440.description: A type of conflict that occurs when assigned goals and responsibilities of one person are incompatible with those of others (e.g., at a workplace).

UWWbk40.title: Intrapersonal role incompatibility
UWWbk40.description: A type of conflict that occurs when there are incompatible demands placed upon an individual due to different roles they hold (e.g., work/family conflict).

2WWTk40.title: Free androgen index
2WWTk40.description: The ratio of total testosterone to sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG). It is used to estimate the amount of physiologically active testosterone.

fWWkk40.title: Radiation-associated vascular ectasia
fWWkk40.description: The most common type of chronic radiation injury to the rectal mucosa. Characterized by friable mucosal telangiectasias. Manifests with rectal bleeding and subsequent iron deficiency anemia months to years following radiation therapy to the pelvic area.

TWW6k40.title: Chronic radiation proctopathy
TWW6k40.description: A type of chronic radiation injury to the rectal mucosa characterized by epithelial atrophy and fibrosis. Manifests with rectal pain, fecal urgency, and constipation.

gWWFk40.title: Acute radiation proctitis
gWWFk40.description: An inflammation of the rectum caused by acute radiation damage to the mucosa. Most commonly seen within 6 weeks after pelvic radiation therapy. Symptoms include pelvic and rectal pain, nonbloody diarrhea, mucous rectal discharge, tenesmus, and fecal urgency.

iWWJO40.title: Sodium butyrate
iWWJO40.description: The sodium salt of butyrate, a short-chain fatty acid that is produced in the intestines by bacterial fermentation. This salt has antiinflammatory properties and is used in enemas to treat inflammatory bowel disease and acute radiation proctitis.

jWW_O40.title: Alcohol-based hand rub
jWW_O40.description: A foam or gel disinfectant preparation that contains 60–95% alcohol and is used for hand hygiene. Quicker to use and more effective than washing with soap and water against most organisms with the exception of bacterial spores (e.g., Clostridium difficile spores), certain protozoal oocysts (e.g., Cryptosporidium parvum), and certain nonenveloped viruses (e.g., norovirus).

PWWWl40.title: Clinical diagnosis
PWWWl40.description: The identification of a disease or condition based on the patient's medical history and examination findings. Laboratory, imaging, and histology studies may confirm an uncertain clinical diagnosis.

oWW0m40.title: Sputum culture conversion
oWW0m40.description: Two consecutive negative sputum cultures collected 15 to 30 days apart in an individual with previously positive cultures for tuberculosis. Sputum culture conversion indicates a good response to antituberculosis treatment. The time to culture conversion is used as a tool to predict the efficacy of the therapeutic regimen being used, which is especially relevant for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.

KWWUm40.title: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis
KWWUm40.description: A Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolate that is resistant to at least isoniazid, rifampin, and possibly additional drugs.

6WWjm40.title: Extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis
6WWjm40.description: A subset of multidrug-resistant TB with additional resistance to fluoroquinolones and second-line IV agents, e.g., amikacin, kanamycin, capreomycin.

JWWsm40.title: Decision matrix
JWWsm40.description: A decision-making tool that evaluates and compares a set of options against various criteria. Can be used for shared decision making or motivational interviewing during patient counseling and for targeted interventions or prioritization of resources to yield the maximum benefit for a given amount of effort.

qWWCm40.title: Closed-ended question
qWWCm40.description: A question that can be answered only by selecting between a limited number of options (e.g., yes or no, options on a list of choices, rating on a scale). Used for clarifications after open-ended questions, objective assessment of a subjective feature (e.g., pain scales), seeking permission (e.g., to provide information, to perform an examination), or confronting patients (e.g., for inappropriate behavior, malingering). Can shut down or obstruct a discussion if used inappropriately.

IWWY540.title: Baricitinib
IWWY540.description: An oral JAK (Janus kinase) inhibitor that is used in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. It inhibits tyrosine kinase, thereby inhibiting cytokine signal transmission, immune system activation, and inflammation.

destinations.label: COVID-19 (coronavirus disease 2019) → Management of hospitalized patients

rWWf540.title: Targeted therapy
rWWf540.description: A cancer therapy directed at a specific molecular target. The goal is to attack cancer cells effectively while reducing the impact on healthy cells. Targeted therapies are usually small molecules or antibodies.

7WW4540.title: Broad-spectrum antibiotic
7WW4540.description: An antibiotic that is active against a wide range of bacteria. Often used for empiric antibiotic therapy. Examples include vancomycin, fluoroquinolones, and third-generation cephalosporins.

tWWXM40.title: Word catheter
tWWXM40.description: An inflatable balloon catheter used to promote drainage and healing of a Bartholin gland cyst or Bartholin gland abscess.

8WWOM40.title: Moderate sedation
8WWOM40.description: A drug-induced state of reduced consciousness in which purposeful reactions to verbal commands and cardiorespiratory function are maintained.

uWWpM40.title: Deep sedation
uWWpM40.description: A drug-induced state of reduced consciousness in which patients only purposefully react to repeated or painful stimuli. Cardiovascular function is usually intact but supportive interventions may be required to maintain a patent airway and adequate respiration.

vWWAM40.title: Storage LUTS
vWWAM40.description: Symptoms of bladder irritation predominantly caused by an overactive bladder, including urinary frequency and urgency, nocturia, and urge incontinence.

DWW1n40.title: Voiding LUTS
DWW1n40.description: Symptoms of bladder outlet obstruction, including urinary hesitancy, straining to urinate, poor urinary stream, prolonged terminal dribbling, and sensation of incomplete voiding. Associated with certain urinary conditions (e.g., benign prostatic hyperplasia, prostate cancer, urethral stricture) and neurological conditions (e.g., multiple sclerosis, spinal cord compression).

_WW5L40.title: Aseptic injection technique
_WW5L40.description: A method to prevent microbial contamination when handling, preparing, and storing injection supplies (e.g., medications, syringes, needles, IV tubing). Aseptic injection technique includes preparing medications in a clean area, wiping the vial stopper with alcohol prior to penetration, using only sterile syringes and needles to enter a medication vial, and cleaning the skin with alcohol prior to percutaneous penetration.

zWWrL40.title: Aerosol-generating procedure
zWWrL40.description: A procedure that generates suspended aerosolized particles, increasing the risk of infection transmission to health care personnel. Examples include intubation, noninvasive positive pressure ventilation, tracheotomy, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, bronchoscopy, and sputum induction.

-WWDL40.title: Laparoscopic ovarian drilling
-WWDL40.description: A laparoscopic procedure in which ovarian tissue is reduced with a laser beam or surgical needle to decrease its volume and androgen production. This hormonal shift can induce FSH secretion and improve ovarian function in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome. Typically a second-line treatment option for ovulation induction.

ZdWZo40.title: I-PASS method
ZdWZo40.description: A comprehensive handoff program that trains clinicians to exchange patient information concisely. The initials stand for illness severity, patient summary, action list, situational awareness and contingency plans, and synthesis by the receiver.

YdWno40.title: Velopharyngeal insufficiency
YdWno40.description: A structural disorder that causes the inability to form a seal between the nasopharynx and oropharynx. Characterized by hypernasal speech, which may impair intelligibility.

destinations.label: Cleft lip and cleft palate → Clinical features

XdW9o40.title: Early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma
XdW9o40.description: A solitary hepatocellular carcinoma > 2 cm in size or up to three small (≤ 3 cm) tumors confined to the liver, with no evidence of portal hypertension or macrovascular invasion in patients with preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A or B) and good performance status.

cdWaK40.title: Intermediate-stage hepatocellular carcinoma
cdWaK40.description: The presence of > 3 HCC tumors, or 2-3 tumors if any tumor exceeds 3 cm in size, with no sign of macrovascular invasion and no extrahepatic metastases in patients with preserved hepatic function (Child-Pugh A or B) and good performance status.

1dW2K40.title: Advanced-stage hepatocellular carcinoma
1dW2K40.description: The presence of macrovascular invasion, lymphatic metastasis, and/or extrahepatic metastatic spread in ambulatory patients with hepatocellular carcinoma who have preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A or B).

WdWPK40.title: CAP
WdWPK40.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Community-acquired pneumonia
2. Catabolite activator protein

ddWoK40.title: BMD
ddWoK40.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Bone mineral density
2. Becker muscular dystrophy

VdWGK40.title: Lymphocytic interstitial pneumonitis
VdWGK40.description: An interstitial lung disease seen in autoimmune and lymphoproliferative disorders as well as in HIV infection. Patients present with cough and dyspnea. Imaging findings are characterized by bilateral infiltration of the lungs, appearing as reticular and ground glass opacities primarily in the lower lobes.

destinations.label: Interstitial lung diseases → Classification of idiopathic interstitial pneumonias

edWxK40.title: Health care clearinghouse
edWxK40.description: An organization that receives nonstandard health information from other entities (e.g., health care providers) and transforms them into standard data elements and formats that can be forwarded to and processed by payors (e.g., insurance companies). Examples of medical clearinghouses include billing services, repricing companies, and community health management information systems.

UdWb640.title: Health care provider
UdWb640.description: A person or health care facility that is licensed, certified, and/or legally authorized to provide health care services within the scope of their practice. Examples include doctors, hospitals, psychologists, dentists, chiropractors, nursing homes, and pharmacies.

2dWT640.title: Normotension
2dWT640.description: A systolic blood pressure of 90-139 mm Hg and diastolic blood pressure of 60-89 mm Hg.

fdWk640.title: HIPAA Security Rule
fdWk640.description: The Security Standards for the Protection of Electronic Protected Health Information (Security Rule) identify administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for the protection of electronically stored personal health information (e-PHI). Covered entities must ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of e-PHI and implement reasonable safeguards to protect this information from anticipated threats, uses, and disclosures.

TdW6640.title: HIPAA Privacy Rule
TdW6640.description: The HIPAA Privacy Rule provides national regulations for the protection of personal health information (PHI), establishes limits to the use and disclosure of said information, and grants patients certain rights regarding their PHI (e.g., the right to obtain copies of their health records).

gdWF640.title: Physical safeguard
gdWF640.description: The physical measures and policies that aim to prevent unauthorized access to personal health information (PHI) and secure buildings and electronic equipment. Examples of physical safeguards include facility access controls, workstation security, and media controls. Covered entities are obligated by the HIPAA Security Rule to implement physical safeguard standards for the protection of electronically stored PHI.

SdWy640.title: Technical safeguard
SdWy640.description: The technical measures and policies that aim to prevent unauthorized access of personal health information (PHI) and protect their integrity and availability. Examples of technical measures include the use of password protection, user identification with access logs, and secure networks. Covered entities are obligated by the HIPAA Security Rule to implement technical safeguard standards for the protection of PHI.

RdWlp40.title: Postpartum dyspareunia
RdWlp40.description: Dyspareunia that commonly occurs within 6 months after giving birth. Can be related to multiple factors, including vaginal dryness due to breastfeeding, perineal trauma during delivery, postpartum depression, and/or relationship changes.

idWJp40.title: Home blood pressure monitoring
idWJp40.description: The self-measurement of blood pressure by a patient at periodic intervals outside of a clinical setting. May be used to confirm the diagnosis of hypertension and monitor antihypertensive treatment.

QdWup40.title: Antispasmodics
QdWup40.description: A group of drugs that decrease the tone and motility of smooth muscle cells. There are two types of antispasmodics: antimuscarinics (e.g., butylscopolamine) and smooth muscle relaxants (e.g., mebeverine). Uses include the treatment of cramping or colicky pain (e.g., biliary, intestinal), irritable bowel syndrome, and overactive bladder incontinence.

4dW3J40.title: Body surface decontamination
4dW3J40.description: A set of procedures for removing residual contaminants from a patient's skin and mucous membranes to prevent further patient and health care provider exposure. Includes removal of clothing, eye and wound irrigation, and washing of skin with soap and water. Should be performed in cases of known or suspected exposure to chemical, biological, radiologic, or nuclear hazards.

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Decontamination

OdWIJ40.title: Revascularization
OdWIJ40.description: The restoration or augmentation of blood flow in a previously ischemic organ or body part (e.g., due to embolism or thrombotic occlusion). Can be performed surgically (bypass surgery, endarterectomy, or surgical embolectomy) or through other interventions (e.g., percutaneous transluminal angioplasty or stenting, pharmacologic or mechanical thrombectomy/embolectomy).

ldWvJ40.title: Lymph node dissection
ldWvJ40.description: A surgical procedure that removes either some of the lymph nodes (regional lymphadenectomy) or most/all of the lymph nodes certain area (radical lymphadenectomy). Used to evaluate for tumor metastasis.

NdW-J40.title: Three-dimensional rendering
NdW-J40.description: A computer reconstruction that is able to process two-dimensional medical images (e.g., obtained by CT or MRI) into three-dimensional renderings. Provides an enhanced visualization of structures (e.g., bones, organs, vessels).

mdWVq40.title: Elective salpingo-oophorectomy
mdWVq40.description: The bilateral removal of the ovaries and Fallopian tubes. Can be performed in combination with hysterectomy for benign uterine disease to reduce the risk of ovarian cancer and breast cancer. Due to potential long-term health risks, it is usually not recommended for women < 51 years of age.

5dWiq40.title: EPO
5dWiq40.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Erythropoietin
2. Exclusive provider organization

LdWwq40.title: Aggregatibacter aphrophilus
LdWwq40.description: A gram-negative bacillus of the HACEK group that can cause infective endocarditis. Formerly named Haemophilus aphrophilus.

KdWUI40.title: Vaginoplasty
KdWUI40.description: A surgical procedure that constructs, reconstructs, or tightens the vagina. Commonly used in transgender medicine and in the treatment of congenital vaginal abnormalities and complications after childbirth (e.g., pelvic organ prolapse). When additional tissue is required, it may come from skin grafts, bowel segments, or in transgender patients, inverted penile or scrotal skin.

6dWjI40.title: Polytetrafluoroethylene graft
6dWjI40.description: A synthetic polymer vascular graft that is used as a conduit to replace or repair blood vessels (e.g., for arterial bypass surgery, endarterectomy, or fistula construction for dialysis).

JdWsI40.title: Window prophylaxis
JdWsI40.description: The provision of treatment for latent tuberculosis infection to children < 5 years of age who have been in contact with an individual with tuberculosis. Children may not have a cellular immune response to tuberculosis (and have negative tuberculosis testing) but still be at risk for progression to active tuberculosis.

IdWYr40.title: Androgen deprivation therapy
IdWYr40.description: The therapy of choice for advanced and metastatic prostate cancer. Decreases prostate cancer growth by decreasing serum testosterone concentrations. Can be achieved with surgical castration (bilateral orchiectomy) or medical castration (e.g., with GnRH agonists or antagonists such as leuprolide, which can be combined with antiandrogen drugs).

rdWfr40.title: Postexposure prophylaxis
rdWfr40.description: An intervention administered after exposure to an infectious pathogen to reduce the risk of developing a disease. Interventions include immunizations, antibiotics, antivirals, and immunoglobulins. Postexposure prophylaxis is available for various exposures, including HIV, bacterial meningitis, tuberculosis, hepatitis B, tetanus, rabies, and anthrax.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Prevention of community spread

7dW4r40.title: Viremia
7dW4r40.description: The presence of viruses in the blood. Can be harmless and transient or the result of serious infection.

HdWKr40.title: Latent infection
HdWKr40.description: An asymptomatic infection that is able to persist in a dormant or inactive state in the body and reactivate under certain conditions. Examples include HSV infection, VZV infection, and tuberculosis.

GdWBr40.title: Cyclical mastalgia
GdWBr40.description: A type of benign breast pain that occurs at regular intervals during the menstrual cycle due to the effects of hormones on breast tissue.

CdWqH40.title: Functional pes planus
CdWqH40.description: A physiologic type of flat feet characterized by preserved joint functionality and typically asymptomatic course. In most cases does not require any treatment.

BdWzH40.title: Atypical leg pain
BdWzH40.description: A type of leg pain caused by ischemia (e.g., due to peripheral artery disease) that is distinct from the cramping pain of claudication. Includes leg pain that sometimes begins at rest and worsens with exertion (i.e., leg pain on exertion and rest) and nonlimiting pain with exertion (i.e., leg pain/carry on).

_dW5s40.title: Cyclic progestin therapy
_dW5s40.description: The administration of progestin for either 10-12 days (short course) or 3-4 weeks per month (long course). Used to treat abnormal uterine bleeding, endometrial hyperplasia, and pain associated with endometriosis. Results in withdrawal bleeding after completion of the course.

0VWeG40.title: Intramuscular immunoglobulin therapy
0VWeG40.description: The intramuscular administration of immunoglobulin, generally to confer short-term protection against certain infections. Use case examples include postexposure prophylaxis for measles, mumps, and rubella, preexposure prophylaxis for hepatitis A, and preexposure prophylaxis for varicella zoster, particularly in immunocompromised children or pregnant women.

aVWQG40.title: Small-volume thoracocentesis
aVWQG40.description: The aspiration of a small volume of pleural fluid (typically 30–60 mL) for the diagnosis of the underlying cause of a new, asymptomatic pleural effusion.

YVWnG40.title: Large-volume thoracocentesis
YVWnG40.description: The aspiration of a large volume of pleural fluid (at least 400–500 mL). Performed for symptomatic relief from a pleural effusion as well as for the diagnosis of its underlying cause.

XVW9G40.title: Sonographic Murphy sign
XVW9G40.description: Acute pain in the right upper quadrant elicited on compression of the gallbladder fundus with the ultrasound transducer during sonography. Similar to the Murphy sign elicited on deep palpation of the right upper quadrant. A strong indicator of acute cholecystitis.

cVWat40.title: Ultra-high potency topical steroid
cVWat40.description: The strongest class of topical corticosteroids (class 1). Used to decrease cutaneous inflammation (e.g., in atopic dermatitis and seborrheic dermatitis) and/or suppress a dysregulated cutaneous immune response (e.g., in psoriasis, alopecia areata, and vitiligo). Often used for skin lesions that are lichenified and/or affect areas with thicker skin (e.g., on the palms and soles). Includes clobetasol propionate 0.05%, fluocinonide 0.1% cream, and halobetasol propionate 0.05%.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Overview of treatment

1VW2t40.title: Extracorporeal shock wave therapy
1VW2t40.description: A noninvasive therapy modality that promotes tissue healing by using repeated shock waves to induce microtrauma to a lesion (e.g., tendinopathy, fibrous plaques).

2VWTF40.title: Anticipatory lactation counseling
2VWTF40.description: The provision of counseling to new mothers prior to hospital discharge regarding optimal breastfeeding techniques (e.g., proper positioning and latch) and how to prevent and manage common issues (e.g., nipple injury).

TVW6F40.title: Infectious esophagitis
TVW6F40.description: Inflammation of the esophageal mucosa secondary to a local infection. The most common causative pathogens include Candida spp., herpes simplex virus, and Cytomegalovirus. Infectious esophagitis typically occurs in immunosuppressed individuals.

gVWFF40.title: Noble test
gVWFF40.description: A provocation test for iliotibial band syndrome. The patient lies on the unaffected side and flexes the affected knee to 90°. The examiner exerts constant pressure on the lateral femoral epicondyle while extending the knee. If pain is elicited, the test is positive.

SVWyF40.title: Oral immunotherapy
SVWyF40.description: The ingestion of increasing doses of a food allergen in a controlled setting to desensitize the immune system.

hVWc840.title: Anaphylaxis emergency action plan
hVWc840.description: A medical document that contains a list of all foods to which a patient is allergic, examples of allergic symptoms, and personalized instructions for medical treatment (e.g., use of an epinephrine autoinjector) in the case of allergic reaction.

3VWS840.title: Cross-contact
3VWS840.description: The accidental transfer of an allergen-containing food to another food that might then cause an allergic reaction.

iVWJ840.title: pH buffer
iVWJ840.description: A combination of a weak acid and its conjugate base (e.g., H₂CO₃ and HCO₃⁻) or a weak base and its conjugate acid. Resists a change in the pH of the system. Important extracellular buffers include the bicarbonate buffer system, inorganic phosphate buffer system, and plasma proteins (e.g., albumin). Important intracellular buffers include organic phosphates (e.g., 2,3-diphosphoglycerate) and hemoglobin.

kVWmu40.title: Desquamative interstitial pneumonia
kVWmu40.description: A rare type of idiopathic interstitial pneumonia that most commonly affects individuals 40-50 years of age with a history of smoking. Clinical features include gradual dyspnea and nonproductive cough. Imaging studies show ground-glass opacities without peripheral reticular opacities.

destinations.label: Interstitial lung diseases → Classification of idiopathic interstitial pneumonias

lVWvu40.title: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
lVWvu40.description: A type of idiopathic interstitial pneumonia that most commonly occurs in nonsmokers 50-60 years of age. Also associated with connective tissue diseases (e.g., systemic sclerosis), HIV infection, and hypersensitivity pneumonitis. Clinical features include progressive dyspnea and cough over weeks to months. Imaging studies show ground-glass and reticular opacities predominantly in the lower pulmonary zones.

destinations.label: Interstitial lung diseases → Classification of idiopathic interstitial pneumonias

qVWCv40.title: Rehydration solution for malnourished children
qVWCv40.description: An oral rehydration solution specifically formulated for treating dehydration in children with severe malnutrition. Contains less sodium and more potassium than standard oral rehydration solution.

destinations.label: Dehydration and hypovolemia → Initial fluid therapy for dehydration and hypovolemia

rVWfD40.title: Founder effect
rVWfD40.description: The reduction in genetic variation resulting from the establishment of a new population by a small subset of a larger population.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Population genetics

7VW4D40.title: Mutation-selection balance
7VW4D40.description: An equilibrium in a population between the occurrence of deleterious alleles resulting from mutation and the elimination of deleterious alleles resulting from selection.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Population genetics

uVWpw40.title: Continued fluid needs
uVWpw40.description: The fluid therapy requirements of patients that remain after acute stabilization with fluid resuscitation. Examples include replacement of remaining fluid deficits, replacement of ongoing fluid losses (e.g., through the skin or gastrointestinal tract), correction of free water deficit, maintenance fluids, and fluids required to treat associated metabolic disturbances.

destinations.label: Intravenous fluid therapy → Continued fluid needs
Dehydration and hypovolemia → Continued fluid needs

wVWh940.title: Structure-activity relationship
wVWh940.description: The relationship between a molecule's chemical structure and its biological activity.

9VWN940.title: Full agonist
9VWN940.description: A molecule that binds to a receptor and activates the receptor with the highest response it can elicit.

1eW2B40.title: Chronic airway obstruction
1eW2B40.description: A term that encompasses obstructive chronic bronchitis, emphysema, and small airway disease.

VeWGB40.title: Intramuscular epinephrine
VeWGB40.description: The intramuscular administration of epinephrine to treat anaphylaxis (e.g., with an epinephrine autoinjector). Should be administered into the anterolateral thigh (vastus lateralis muscle). Achieves a faster and higher plasma concentration when compared to subcutaneous application.

TeW6y40.title: Teething
TeW6y40.description: The process by which an infant's first teeth emerge through the gums. Occurs usually between 6 and 10 months of age. Symptoms include such as drooling, irritability, disrupted sleep, and/or swelling/inflammation of the gums.

SeWyy40.title: Intrauterine insemination
SeWyy40.description: An infertility treatment in which washed and concentrated sperm are introduced directly into the uterine cavity at the time of ovulation.

jeW_A40.title: Language development
jeW_A40.description: The process of forming communication skills through either spoken or signed language. Consists of both understanding and processing language (i.e., receptive language ) and formulating and conveying language to others (i.e., expressive language ability).

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Developmental milestones

PeWW_40.title: Cognitive development
PeWW_40.description: The development of reasoning and problem-solving skills in a child.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Developmental milestones

keWm_40.title: Anticipatory guidance
keWm_40.description: A form of proactive counseling on physical, emotional, psychological, and/or developmental changes that can be expected to occur in an individual.

7eW4Zk0.title: Open mesenteric bypass surgery
7eW4Zk0.description: A surgical procedure for the treatment of mesenteric ischemia in which a vascular graft (either an autologous vein or a polytetrafluoroethylene graft) is inserted between the aorta or iliac artery and the obstructed artery, distal to the occlusion, to reestablish perfusion. During the procedure, the bowel is inspected for severe ischemia and perforation.

seWtZk0.title: Transporters associated with antigen processing
seWtZk0.description: A protein complex that transports endogenous peptide fragments into the rough endoplasmic reticulum for eventual loading onto MHC I molecules.

8eWO0k0.title: Peripheral tolerance
8eWO0k0.description: A type of immunological tolerance that occurs in the immune periphery, following the egression of T and B cells from their primary lymphoid organs, and ensures deletion of or induction of anergy in self-antigens (i.e., T and B cells that are reactive to self) that escape into the periphery.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → Immune tolerance and autoimmunity

ueWp0k0.title: Central tolerance
ueWp0k0.description: A type of immunological tolerance that occurs at an early stage of lymphoid cell development and ensures the detection of self-antigens, i.e., T and B cells that are reactive to self.

destinations.label: Adaptive immune system → Immune tolerance and autoimmunity

xeWEak0.title: Tympanoplasty
xeWEak0.description: A surgical procedure to repair a nonhealing defect in the tympanic membrane either with or without placement of a graft to prevent infection and restore hearing ability. The most common indication is perforation of the tympanic membrane due to chronic otitis media.

BeWzak0.title: Oral fluid challenge
BeWzak0.description: The oral administration of a small amount of fluid to assess a patient's ability to tolerate oral fluid intake.

AeWRYk0.title: Amiodarone-induced pulmonary toxicity
AeWRYk0.description: A group of pulmonary conditions that can develop as an adverse effect of amiodarone therapy. Includes pulmonary fibrosis and chronic interstitial pneumonitis.

_eW5Yk0.title: Tobacco intoxication
_eW5Yk0.description: A clinical syndrome that can develop following the use of excessive amount of tobacco or nicotine. Manifestations include restlessness, anxiety, insomnia, increased gastrointestinal motility, tachycardia, and hypertension.

destinations.label: Tobacco product use and smoking cessation → Clinical features

-eWDYk0.title: Cocaine intoxication
-eWDYk0.description: The manifestations of acute cocaine use, which include: euphoria, arousal, increased vigilance, impaired judgment, alertness, grandiosity, anxiety, irritability, mood swings, psychotic symptoms (e.g., paranoia, hallucinations), sweating, tachycardia, hypertension, chest pain/angina, and mydriasis.

aUWQbk0.title: Auricular hematoma
aUWQbk0.description: The formation of a hematoma in the external ear after blunt trauma to the side of the head. Commonly seen in persons who take part in contact sports, such as boxing. If left untreated, it can lead to cauliflower ear formation.

YUWnbk0.title: Cauliflower ear
YUWnbk0.description: A deformity of the ear that typically develops after blunt trauma and auricular hematoma formation. An auricular hematoma disrupts the blood supply to the auricular cartilage, resulting in cartilage necrosis and fibrocartilage formation. Classically seen in individuals who take part in contact sports, such as boxing, wrestling, and rugby.

cUWaXk0.title: Dysproteinemia
cUWaXk0.description: A condition characterized by an overproduction of monoclonal immunoglobulins or immunoglobulin molecule subunits.

1UW2Xk0.title: Hypofibrinogenemia
1UW2Xk0.description: A disorder characterized by low or undetectable plasma fibrinogen levels. Can be acquired (e.g., due to hemodilution or consumption of clotting factors) or congenital (e.g., afibrinogenemia, type I fibrinogen deficiency).

VUWGXk0.title: Sleeve gastrectomy
VUWGXk0.description: A weight loss surgical procedure in which a large part of the greater curvature of the stomach is removed (~ 80%), leaving only a narrow tube-shaped remainder (“sleeve”).

eUWxXk0.title: Laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding
eUWxXk0.description: A weight loss surgical procedure in which an inflatable silicon band is placed close to the top of the stomach, creating a small pouch that reduces the stomach's reservoir capacity.

gUWFck0.title: Gelatinous pseudocyst
gUWFck0.description: A cystlike lesion caused by dilation of perivascular spaces due to mucous and gelatinous material produced by the fungus Cryptococcus neoformans. Most commonly seen in the basal ganglia and has a soap bubble appearance on MRI.

iUWJ1k0.title: Gorlin sign
iUWJ1k0.description: The ability to touch the tip of the nose or chin with the tongue. Commonly seen in patients with Ehler-Danlos syndrome.

OUWIWk0.title: Neural tube derivatives
OUWIWk0.description: Structures that develop from neural tube. Comprise central nervous system (including glial cells except microglia) and retina.

lUWvWk0.title: Neural crest derivatives
lUWvWk0.description: Structures that develop from neural crest. Include the adrenal medulla, pigment cells, Schwann cells, meninges (pia and arachnoid mater), pharyngeal arch cartilage, odontoblast, aorticopulmonary septum, endocardial cushions, and cranial bones.

5UWidk0.title: Causes of splenomegaly
5UWidk0.description: A group of conditions that cause splenic enlargement. Includes conditions that increase splenic activity (e.g., hemolysis, polycythemia, infections, autoimmune diseases, extramedullary hematopoiesis), portal hypertension, hematological malignancies, and other infiltrative diseases.

MUWMdk0.title: Modified Marshall scoring system for organ dysfunction
MUWMdk0.description: A score used to determine whether a patient has organ failure of the respiratory, cardiovascular, or renal system. Each system is scored on a scale from 0 to 4, with a score of 2 or more indicating organ failure.

nUW7dk0.title: Cranial nerve nuclei
nUW7dk0.description: A collection of neuronal bodies in the brainstem associated with one or more cranial nerves. Cranial nerve fibers comprises the axons of the neurons located within the cranial nerve nuclei.

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Origin and pathways of the cranial nerves

LUWwdk0.title: Glomerular filtration
LUWwdk0.description: A process in which plasma is filtrated through the pores of the kidney glomeruli.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Urine production

media.title: Effects of NSAIDs and ACEIs on renal filtration

IUWYek0.title: Grounded theory
IUWYek0.description: A qualitative research methodology that involves inductively developing hypotheses from systemically collected and analyzed data (e.g., observations or interviews), which can then be generalized to a larger population to explain social phenomena.

rUWfek0.title: Ethnography
rUWfek0.description: A qualitative research methodology that involves the study and recording of cultural and/or social practices through fieldwork in the setting of the culture or society of interest.

7UW4ek0.title: Phenomenology
7UW4ek0.description: A qualitative research methodology aimed at gaining a deeper understanding of the subjective view of a person who has experienced a phenomenon of interest. Data is typically obtained by interview-based methods.

HUWKek0.title: Action research
HUWKek0.description: A qualitative research methodology that involves embedding the researcher in a setting of interest (e.g., a specific school) and the researcher collaborating with individuals who are part of that setting (e.g., the teachers of that school) to identify and resolve issues specific to that setting through practice and for the purpose of improving practices (e.g., the use of tablet computers in that school).

sUWtek0.title: Qualitative research
sUWtek0.description: A research approach that analyzes nonnumerical data, which is typically obtained by observation or recording of speech. The collected data is explored for patterns, from which theories or hypotheses can be inductively developed. As opposed to quantitative research, qualitative research does not run statistical analysis of the collected data or test hypotheses.

GUWBek0.title: Quantitative research
GUWBek0.description: A research approach in which numerical data is statistically analyzed in order to identify patterns and/or test hypotheses. Can be observational or experimental.

tUWXUk0.title: High-risk HPV
tUWXUk0.description: A group of HPV types that are associated with an increased risk of cervical, anogenital, oral, and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas. High-risk HPV types include HPV 16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68. HPV 16 and 18 are responsible for most HPV-related cancers.

destinations.label: Human papillomavirus infection → Overview of HPV-associated diseases

8UWOUk0.title: Axonal transport
8UWOUk0.description: The movement of different substances and organelles to and from the neuronal cell body along an axon. It involves cytoskeletal microtubules and the motor proteins dynein and kinesin, which facilitate the movement of substances to and from the cell body, respectively.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Nerve tissue

CUWq2k0.title: Gastric adenocarcinoma
CUWq2k0.description: The most common histological type of gastric cancer (95% of cases). Arises from glandular cells and can be further classified into intestinal, diffuse, and intermediate type gastric carcinoma.

Z2WZTk0.title: Fetal scalp blood sampling
Z2WZTk0.description: An intrapartum procedure to test pH and lactate in fetal capillary blood. The fetal scalp is incised transvaginally, and a specimen of blood is collected for analysis.

X2W9Tk0.title: Toxicodendron
X2W9Tk0.description: A genus of flowering plants that produce urushiol, which can cause severe allergic contact dermatitis. Prevalent in North America and some parts of Asia.

c2Wagk0.title: Dermatomycosis
c2Wagk0.description: A mycotic infection of tissue with high keratin content (e.g., skin, nails, hair) caused mainly by dermatophytes (e.g., Trichophyton), which require keratin for growth. Can also be caused by Malassezia. Includes tinea pedis, tinea capitis, and pityriasis versicolor.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Superficial fungal infections

12W2gk0.title: Modified CT severity index for acute pancreatitis
12W2gk0.description: A radiological scoring system used to rate the severity of acute pancreatitis. CT findings are graded on a scale from 0 to 10 based on the degree of pancreatic inflammation, the extent of necrosis, and the presence of extrapancreatic complications. Disease is categorized as mild (0–2 points), moderate (4–6 points), or severe (8-10 points).

destinations.label: Acute pancreatitis → Severity grading and prognostic scores

W2WPgk0.title: CT severity index for acute pancreatitis
W2WPgk0.description: A radiological scoring system used to rate the severity of acute pancreatitis. CT findings are graded on a scale from 0 to 10 based on the degree of pancreatic inflammation and extent of necrosis. Disease is categorized as mild (0–3 points), moderate (4–6 points), or severe (7–10 points).

destinations.label: Acute pancreatitis → Severity grading and prognostic scores

media.title: CT severity index for acute pancreatitis

V2WGgk0.title: Revised Atlanta grades of severity
V2WGgk0.description: A set of criteria for defining the severity of acute pancreatitis. Considered mild if there is no organ failure and no complications, moderately severe if there is transient (< 48 hours) organ failure, and severe if there is persistent (> 48 hours) single or multiple organ failure.

destinations.label: Acute pancreatitis → Severity grading and prognostic scores

e2Wxgk0.title: BALI score
e2Wxgk0.description: A score used to evaluate the severity of acute pancreatitis using four variables: (B) BUN ≥ 25 mg/dL, (A) age ≥ 65 years, (L) LDH ≥ 300 U/L, and (I) IL-6 ≥ 300 pg/mL. Each criterion is worth one point; a score of three points is associated with a mortality rate of ≥ 25% and four points with a mortality rate of ≥ 50%.

22WTSk0.title: Drug-induced pancreatitis
22WTSk0.description: A type of pancreatitis triggered by drug exposure. Commonly implicated drugs include steroids, azathioprine, sulfonamides, loop and thiazide diuretics, protease inhibitors, nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, and anticonvulsants (e.g., valproic acid). These drugs should be stopped if pancreatitis is suspected.

f2WkSk0.title: Statistical heterogeneity
f2WkSk0.description: A phenomenon in which the observed effects of an intervention are more different from one another than can be attributed to random error or chance alone. For instance, individual trials that are part of a larger systemic review may demonstrate different outcomes (some showing benefit while others show harm), despite every attempt being made to standardize these trials.

g2WFSk0.title: Primary stabbing headache
g2WFSk0.description: A short, extremely intense type of headache characterized by single or multiple stab-like pain episodes that typically last only seconds. Can be idiopathic or secondary to an underlying condition. Commonly seen in individuals who have migraines.

k2Wm3k0.title: Intravascular hemolytic anemia
k2Wm3k0.description: A form of hemolysis in which erythrocytes are lysed within blood vessels, usually due to mechanical damage or complement fixation. Laboratory findings include decreased haptoglobin, presence of schistocytes, and urine hemosiderin/hemoglobin.

O2WI3k0.title: Under-5 mortality
O2WI3k0.description: The probability of a child born in a specific year or period dying by the age of five per 1000 live births.

l2Wv3k0.title: Life expectancy
l2Wv3k0.description: The average number of years a person can expect to live calculated on the basis of current death rates depending on demographic factors such as year of birth, sex, and geographic region. Life expectancy at birth is the average number of years a newborn can expect to live based on current sex-specific death rates for a specific region and/or social group.

N2W-3k0.title: Health-adjusted life expectancy
N2W-3k0.description: The average number of years a person can expect to live in full health, taking into account the years a person is expected to live in poor health due to disease or injury.

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

m2WVRk0.title: Years of potential life lost
m2WVRk0.description: A measure of premature mortality that estimates the years of potential life lost due to premature deaths. Calculated by the sum of life years lost annually by persons below the age of life expectancy of the population who suffered early deaths. Places greater emphasis to deaths at a younger age compared to deaths at an older age. Can be used to measure the overall health of an area.

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

52WiRk0.title: Standardized mortality ratio
52WiRk0.description: The ratio between the observed number of deaths in a study population and the expected number of deaths in a standard population. A ratio greater than 1.0 is interpreted as excess deaths in the study population.

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

M2WMRk0.title: Health promotion
M2WMRk0.description: Efforts that empower individuals to improve their health. These may occur on an individual or population level.

n2W7Rk0.title: Cluster analysis
n2W7Rk0.description: A technique of statistical classification that involves organizing data points or objects into groups (clusters) based on similarity to each other and dissimilarity to those in other clusters.

L2WwRk0.title: Entrainment test
L2WwRk0.description: A clinical test used to diagnose functional tremor. The patient is asked to perform voluntary movement (e.g. tapping) with an unaffected limb with a given rhythm that is different from the frequency of the tremor. Considered positive if the tremor of the affected limb aligns with the frequency of the voluntary movement, if the voluntary movement causes a change in frequency or a disruption of pattern in the affected limb, or if the patient is unable to perform the voluntary movement in the unaffected limb.

K2WUik0.title: Actinic purpura
K2WUik0.description: A benign cutaneous lesion that typically manifests as recurrent, irregularly-shaped, dark purple macules on extensor surfaces. Caused by chronic sun exposure, which results in dermal atrophy that results in susceptibility to bruising with minor trauma.

p2WLik0.title: Coccidioides posadasii
p2WLik0.description: A dimorphic pathogenic fungus with a natural habitat in semiarid soil. Endemic to South America, parts of Mexico, and the southwestern United States. Inhalation of its barrel-shaped spores can cause coccidioidomycosis. Seen on microscopy as spherules containing endospores.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

s2WtQk0.title: Gulf War syndrome
s2WtQk0.description: A chronic, multisystem condition seen in veterans of the 1991 Gulf War. Manifestations include chronic fatigue, diarrhea, memory impairment, muscle and joint pain, and malignancy. Has been linked to exposure to chemical warfare agents, pyridostigmine bromide, and other chemicals (e.g., pesticides, uranium).

destinations.label: Military medicine → Combat- and deployment-associated conditions

t2WXjk0.title: Agent Orange
t2WXjk0.description: An herbicide used by the US military during the Vietnam War to defoliate jungle and destroy food crops. Exposure to Agent Orange is associated different types of cancer (e.g., leukemia, bladder cancer), Parkinson disease, and ischemic heart disease. Children of exposed mothers have an increased risk for birth defects (e.g., spina bifida).

F2Wgjk0.title: Elution studies
F2Wgjk0.description: A laboratory procedure in which antibodies attached to red blood cells are dissociated and rendered available for specific antibody identification. May be used in the workup of hemolytic transfusion reactions, hemolytic disease of the newborn, and autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

82WOjk0.title: Green tobacco sickness
82WOjk0.description: A form of nicotine poisoning that predominantly affects tobacco harvesters. Caused by transdermal absorption of nicotine from wet tobacco plants. Symptoms include dizziness, headache, nausea, vomiting, and blood pressure fluctuations.

v2WAjk0.title: Nitrogen narcosis
v2WAjk0.description: A syndrome caused by increased nitrogen levels from breathing compressed air while diving at depth. Manifestations include altered mental status (e.g., euphoria, confusion, hostility) and loss of fine motor control skills. Severity of symptoms increases with diving depth, ultimately leading to unconsciousness and, subsequently, death.

D2W1Pk0.title: Community surveys
D2W1Pk0.description: A type of observational, analytic study that consists of a set of survey questions sent out to a pre-selected target audience to understand more about that particular community.

w2WhPk0.title: Thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome
w2WhPk0.description: An extremely rare adverse event that can develop after receiving a COVID-19 viral vector vaccine. Reports describe arterial and/or venous thrombosis within 6 weeks of immunization associated with thrombocytopenia and PF4 antibodies. Evidence for treatment is limited, but suggestions include IV immunoglobulins and nonheparin-based anticoagulation.

92WNPk0.title: Placebo-controlled clinical trial
92WNPk0.description: A type of experimental study design that involves two or more randomized groups. One group receives active treatment, and the other(s) receive a placebo. Used to account for the placebo effect (an effect produced by the placebo drug that cannot be attributed to the properties of the placebo itself).

C2WqPk0.title: Equivalence trial
C2WqPk0.description: A trial designed to show that two or more interventions differ by no more than an acceptable degree as defined by a prespecified margin of inferiority and superiority.

x2WEPk0.title: Publication bias
x2WEPk0.description: A bias that occurs when the findings of a study affect the likelihood of its publication, causing an imbalance toward the publication of positive results.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

B2WzPk0.title: Forest plot
B2WzPk0.description: A graph that combines the estimated results from multiple studies addressing the same question and visualizes each study's effect size, confidence interval, and calculated overall effect.

A2WR4k0.title: Risk of bias
A2WR4k0.description: The probablility that a study will give misleading results.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

_2W54k0.title: Dialysis arthropathy
_2W54k0.description: An osteoarticular syndrome seen in patients on renal replacement therapy and caused by the deposition of β-2 microglobulin amyloid in bones and joints. Characterized by a destructive arthropathy affecting large and small joints, bone erosions and cysts, and subsequent pathological fractures.

z2Wr4k0.title: Anamnestic response
z2Wr4k0.description: The rapid reappearance of antibodies and cellular immune activity following exposure to a previously encountered antigen. Reexposure to the antigen activates memory B cells and memory T cells, leading to a faster and more efficient humoral and cellular response compared to the primary exposure.

-2WD4k0.title: Gender bias
-2WD4k0.description: A type of cognitive bias that occurs as a result of false assumptions about an individual's real or perceived gender.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

ZfWZkk0.title: Information bias (psychology)
ZfWZkk0.description: A type of cognitive bias in which a decision-maker collects more information than necessary because of a false belief that more evidence (e.g., in support of a diagnosis) is necessarily better. Can lead to overtesting.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

0fWekk0.title: Confirmation bias (psychology)
0fWekk0.description: A type of cognitive bias in which a decision-maker tends to favor evidence that supports preconceived notions, ignoring other results.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

afWQkk0.title: Omission bias
afWQkk0.description: A type of cognitive bias in which inaction is preferred over action regardless of the facts. Results from obligation to nonmaleficence. More common than commission bias.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

YfWnkk0.title: Commission bias
YfWnkk0.description: A type of cognitive bias in which action is preferred over inaction regardless of the facts. Results from obligation to beneficence.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

bfWHkk0.title: Ascertainment bias (psychology)
bfWHkk0.description: A type of cognitive bias that occurs as a result of preset assumptions that lead to a difference in treatment. Examples include gender bias and stereotyping bias.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

XfW9kk0.title: Hop test
XfW9kk0.description: A set of clinical tests that are used in the diagnosis of some painful traumatic conditions (e.g., stress fractures or syndesmotic ankle injury) and evaluation of functional performance of the lower extremity. The patient is asked to repeatedly hop on the affected leg. In some variants, hop distance is measured. Considered positive if it elicits worsening of pain, reduced hopping distance, and/or inability to perform the test.

WfWPOk0.title: Allocation concealment
WfWPOk0.description: The process in a randomized trial of preventing investigators from gaining foreknowledge of which groups participants are assigned to using techniques such as centralized randomization schemes, pharmacy-controlled randomization, and sequentially numbered containers. Used to prevent selection bias.

dfWoOk0.title: Regression to mean
dfWoOk0.description: A statistical phenomenon that occurs when extreme measurements (e.g., unusually high or high measurements) are followed by measurements closer to the mean, potentially letting natural variation appear as real change.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Measures of central tendency and outliers

VfWGOk0.title: Posttest probability
VfWGOk0.description: The probability that a patient with signs and/or symptoms of a disease will have that disease after diagnostic testing. Taking into account factors such as test sensitivity and specificity, disease prevalence, and patient history, posttest probability helps guide decisions regarding the reliability of the diagnosis.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

media.title: Effect of prevalence on post-test probabilities

efWxOk0.title: Hypothesis-generating testing
efWxOk0.description: A method of research based on the investigation of data for patterns and relationships permitting the development of a hypothesis that can then be validated in a subsequent study.

UfWblk0.title: Hypothesis-driven testing
UfWblk0.description: A method of research based on the development of a specific, measurable, and falsifiable hypothesis that is then validated using data collected through observation and/or experimentation.

2fWTlk0.title: Clinical features of hemolytic anemia
2fWTlk0.description: A collection of clinical manifestations of hemolytic anemia; can include features of hemolysis (e.g., jaundice, back or flank pain, dark urine) and features of anemia (e.g., pallor, fatigue, exertional dyspnea).

TfW6lk0.title: Cytochrome b5 reductase
TfW6lk0.description: A NADH-dependent enzyme that converts ferricytochrome from a Fe⁺³ to a Fe⁺² form. Deficiency of this enzyme causes methemoglobinemia.

gfWFlk0.title: Skin hyperextensibility
gfWFlk0.description: A physical examination finding of skin that is stretchable beyond normal. A common finding in certain connective tissue disorders, such as Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome.

SfWylk0.title: Joint hypermobility
SfWylk0.description: A physical examination finding of joints that are flexible beyond the normal range. Can occur as a benign condition or as a result of hereditary connective tissue disorders (e.g., Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, Marfan syndrome). Can cause joint pain, joint instability, subluxation, and dislocation.

QfWuNk0.title: CRM
QfWuNk0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Canalith repositioning maneuvers
2. Crisis resource management

PfWWmk0.title: Aggregate bias (psychology)
PfWWmk0.description: A type of cognitive bias in which a decision-maker believes that aggregated data (e.g., from larger studies) does not apply to the individual case.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

NfW-mk0.title: Efficacy
NfW-mk0.description: The degree to which an intervention produces the desired outcome under ideal conditions. In pharmacology, the term refers to the degree to which a drug will produce the desired effect.

mfWV5k0.title: Effectiveness
mfWV5k0.description: The degree to which an intervention produces the desired outcome under real-world conditions or, more generally, the extent to which an intervention achieves its desired purpose.

5fWi5k0.title: End point
5fWi5k0.description: In clinical trials, an objectively measureable event or outcome typically defined in the trial objectives used to determine whether the intervention studied was beneficial. Examples include survival, improvements in life quality, and symptom relief.

MfWM5k0.title: Clinical outcome
MfWM5k0.description: A measurable change in health, function, or quality of life resulting from an intervention.

nfW75k0.title: Surrogate endpoint
nfW75k0.description: A type of clinical endpoint that is used if an actual endpoint (primary endpoint) is unavailable for measure to determine whether a specific intervention was beneficial. Examples include reduced tumor size and decreased biomarker levels.

LfWw5k0.title: Basic calcium phosphate crystal deposition diseases
LfWw5k0.description: A type of crystalline arthropathy in which basic calcium phosphate (BCP) crystals are deposited in joints, resulting in BCP-associated arthritis (including Milwaukee shoulder syndrome), or in periarticular structures, causing calcific tendinitis. Typically seen in women and tends to affect large joints, especially the shoulder.

destinations.label: Basic calcium phosphate crystal deposition diseases

ofW0Mk0.title: Nonviral hepatitis
ofW0Mk0.description: Liver inflammation from causes other than virus infection. Types of nonviral hepatitis include alcoholic hepatitis, toxic hepatitis, and autoimmune hepatitis. Hepatitis can lead to cirrhosis, liver failure, and death.

KfWUMk0.title: Undifferentiated inflammatory arthritis
KfWUMk0.description: A diagnosis of exclusion for patients with symptoms of inflammatory arthritis that are not attributable to trauma or acute inflammatory events; often a transitional state preceding a definitive diagnosis.

6fWjMk0.title: Oral health program
6fWjMk0.description: A series of public health interventions (e.g., fluoride services, tooth brushing programs) that aim to reduce oral disease (e.g., tooth decay, gum disease, oral cancer) and improve oral health.

JfWsMk0.title: Intervention analysis
JfWsMk0.description: A method of statistical analysis that measures the extent to which a change occurred in a system (time series data) after a known intervention (e.g., medical treatment) was introduced.

GfWBnk0.title: Alcohol-induced cardiomyopathy
GfWBnk0.description: A type of dilated cardiomyopathy caused by chronic heavy alcohol consumption. Manifests with signs and symptoms of chronic heart failure. Alcohol cessation may result in recovery of cardiac function.

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Complications of alcohol use

wfWhok0.title: Gabapentinoids
wfWhok0.description: A class of drugs derived from the inhibitory neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA). Originally developed as antiepileptics, they are now commonly used to treat neuropathic pain. Examples include gabapentin and pregabalin.

CfWqok0.title: Massive hemoptysis
CfWqok0.description: The rapid or voluminous loss of blood from the lower respiratory tract. There is no universally accepted definition for massive hemoptysis and described blood loss parameters vary widely, i.e., can range from > 100 mL/24 hours to > 1000 mL/24 hours.

destinations.label: Hemoptysis → Massive hemoptysis and life-threatening hemoptysis

xfWEok0.title: Refractory shock
xfWEok0.description: Potentially lethal manifestation of cardiovascular failure characterized by inadequate hemodynamic response to high doses of antihypotensive agents (e.g., dobutamine, epinephrine). Symptoms include hypotension, decreased tissue perfusion, and organ failure.

BfWzok0.title: Bisphenol A
BfWzok0.description: Organic synthetic compound that serves as a precursor in the production of polycarbonate plastics and epoxy resins. BPA is suspected to have estrogen-mimicking properties, potentially acting as an endocrine disruptor.

_fW5Kk0.title: Fasciitis
_fW5Kk0.description: Inflammation of fascia, i.e., the thin connective tissue that surrounds and stabilizes structures such as muscles, blood vessels, and organs. Common clinically relevant subtypes are plantar fasciitis, necrotizing fasciitis, and eosinophilic fasciitis.

zfWrKk0.title: Pure sensory neuropathy
zfWrKk0.description: A subtype of neuropathy characterized by sensory symptoms (i.e., paresthesia, numbness, pain) without motor symptoms. Etiologies include malignancy (paraneoplastic pure sensory neuropathy), medication adverse effects (e.g., due to cisplatin), and nutritional deficiencies.

ZTWZ6k0.title: Vitamin toxicity
ZTWZ6k0.description: A syndrome caused by excessive levels of one or more vitamins. Most likely to occur with fat-soluble vitamins (e.g., vitamin A or D), which, unlike water-soluble vitamins, accumulate in the body over time. Most commonly caused by oversupplementation or other forms of excessive intake. Symptoms depend on the specific vitamin and may include visual, dermatological, and behavioral changes as well as gastrointestinal upset.

aTWQ6k0.title: Subphrenic abscess
aTWQ6k0.description: An accumulation of pus located directly under the diaphragm. Most commonly a complication of surgery (e.g., splenectomy). Manifests with fever, pain over the 8th-11th ribs on the affected side, cough, and increased respiratory rate. Complications include sepsis and, ultimately, death.

bTWH6k0.title: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
bTWH6k0.description: A syndrome characterized by the progressive accumulation of surfactant protein in the alveoli. Can be caused by autoimmunity or genetic mutations or occur secondary to certain conditions (e.g., HIV) or exposure to toxic substances (e.g., chemotherapeutic agents). Symptoms most commonly include dyspnea, cough, and fatigue but can vary depending on the cause.

destinations.label: Rare inherited syndromes → Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP)

XTW96k0.title: Ureterovaginal fistula
XTW96k0.description: An abnormal connection between the vagina and the distal ureter. Etiologies include laceration during surgical procedures, prolonged/obstructed labor, cancer, and radiation therapy. Typically manifests with continuous urine incontinence.

cTWapk0.title: Selective renal venography
cTWapk0.description: A diagnostic imaging study during which contrast dye is intravenously injected into the renal vein. Used to detect disruption of venous blood flow (e.g. due to renal vein thrombosis) and visualize the anatomy of the renal veins.

fTWkJk0.title: Limb length discrepancy
fTWkJk0.description: A difference in the lengths of the arms (i.e., arm length discrepancy) or legs (i.e., leg length discrepancy). Can be idiopathic, congenital, or acquired.

STWyJk0.title: Direct vision internal urethrotomy
STWyJk0.description: An endoscopic procedure used for the management of urethral strictures (e.g., simple bulbar strictures) during which a cystoscope is inserted into the urethra and scar tissue is incised.

QTWuqk0.title: First-line antihypertensive medications
QTWuqk0.description: A group of drugs recommended as initial treatment for most patients with hypertension. Consists of thiazide diuretics, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs), and calcium channel blockers. Chosen based on patient characteristics and comorbidities.

kTWmIk0.title: Methotrexate-induced pulmonary toxicity
kTWmIk0.description: An adverse effect of both low- and high-dose methotrexate therapy. Can manifest with various pulmonary conditions, including fibrosis, pneumonitis, and pneumonia. Symptoms usually develop within a year after the beginning of treatment, can occur in an acute or chronic pattern.

lTWvIk0.title: Breastfeeding complications
lTWvIk0.description: Includes inadequate breast milk production, breast engorgement, nipple injury, puerperal mastitis, mammary candidiasis, galactocele, excessive weight loss in breastfed infants, and jaundice (e.g., breastfeeding jaundice, breast milk jaundice).

destinations.label: Infant nutrition and breastfeeding → Breastfeeding complications

NTW-Ik0.title: Pulmonary fibrosis
NTW-Ik0.description: A restrictive lung condition characterized by scarring of lung tissue, which results in reduced lung compliance. Manifestations include progressive dyspnea, persistent dry cough, fatigue, and inspiratory crackles on auscultation. Can be idiopathic or secondary to medications, interstitial lung disease, or infection.

oTW07k0.title: Urethral injury
oTW07k0.description: A traumatic injury that can manifest with blood at the urethral meatus, pain, and/or inability to pass urine. Urethral integrity is often evaluated with retrograde urethrogram.

KTWU7k0.title: Act of omission
KTWU7k0.description: A medical ethics term that refers to failure to perform a task (e.g., care for a patient).

6TWj7k0.title: Fight bite
6TWj7k0.description: A bite injury that occurs when a person punches another individual in the mouth with a closed fist. Can result in minor lacerations. Injury to the metacarpophalangeal joint capsule and/or extensor tendon sheath can result in deep anaerobic infection.

pTWL7k0.title: PCI
pTWL7k0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Percutaneous coronary intervention
2. Prophylactic cranial irradiation
3. Peritoneal cancer index

JTWs7k0.title: Brodalumab
JTWs7k0.description: A human monoclonal antibody used to treat psoriasis. Binds to the interleukin-17 receptor, thereby preventing its activation. Common adverse effects include arthralgia, fatigue, and headache.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

qTWC7k0.title: Plerixafor
qTWC7k0.description: A hematopoetic stem cell mobilizer used in combination with G-CSF to mobilize stem cells and allow their collection from peripheral blood for autologous stem cell transplantation. Indicated in patients with multiple myeloma and non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Adverse effects include gastrointestinal upset, headache, dizziness, and arthralgia.

ITWYHk0.title: Cabozantinib
ITWYHk0.description: A targeted anticancer therapy that blocks the activity of VEGFR, MET, RET, and several other receptor tyrosine kinases. Used to treat advanced renal cell carcinoma and sorafenib-refractory hepatocellular carcinoma. Adverse effects include gastrointestinal upset and hand-foot skin reaction.

HTWKHk0.title: Respiratory bronchiolitis-interstitial lung disease
HTWKHk0.description: A rare type of interstitial lung disease that most commonly develops in heavy smokers 30-50 years of age. Manifestations include progressive dyspnea and cough. Imaging studies show ground-glass and reticular opacities, predominantly in the lower pulmonary zones.

destinations.label: Interstitial lung diseases → Classification of idiopathic interstitial pneumonias

tTWXsk0.title: Idiopathic pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis
tTWXsk0.description: A rare type of interstitial lung disease that most commonly affects individuals between 50-60 years of age. Manifestations include progressive dyspnea, dry cough, and recurrent infections. Imaging findings are characterized by pleural and subpleural thickening of the upper pulmonary lobes.

destinations.label: Interstitial lung diseases → Classification of idiopathic interstitial pneumonias

uTWpsk0.title: Septic bursitis
uTWpsk0.description: An infection of a synovial bursa (e.g., prepatellar, olecranon, trochanteric). Manifestations include acute joint pain, redness, tenderness, limited mobility, and systemic signs of infection (e.g., fever, elevated inflammatory markers).

ETW8sk0.title: Pinguecula
ETW8sk0.description: A small, yellowish, raised plaque on the conjunctiva composed of protein, fat, or calcium. Most commonly located on the medial conjunctiva but can also be located on the lateral conjunctiva.

vTWAsk0.title: Organic dust toxic syndrome
vTWAsk0.description: A type of pneumoconiosis caused by organic dust contaminated with mycotoxins (e.g., from moldy hay, stored grain, silage). Manifestations include fever and flu-like symptoms that typically develop 4–12 hours after exposure to contaminated organic dust.

destinations.label: Interstitial lung diseases → Overview of pneumoconioses

wTWhGk0.title: Severe hypertriglyceridemia
wTWhGk0.description: A serum triglyceride concentration > 500 mg/dL in adults (> 1000mg/dL in children). Etiologies include hyperlipoproteinemia types I and IV. Associated with an increased risk for pancreatitis and coronary artery disease.

9TWNGk0.title: Acute triglyceride-induced pancreatitis
9TWNGk0.description: An episode of acute pancreatitis that is precipitated by high serum triglyceride levels (usually > 1000 mg/dL). Pathogenesis involves toxic fatty acids that are released from triglycerides via breakdown by pancreatic lipase. Associated with primary (e.g., type IV or familial hyperlipidemia) as well as secondary (e.g., due to medications) forms of hypertriglyceridemia.

ATWRtk0.title: Staphyloma
ATWRtk0.description: An abnormal protrusion of the uvea through the sclera, which has undergone thinning. This outpouching gives the thinned sclera an almost black appearance because of the darker uvea.

_TW5tk0.title: Phonophobia
_TW5tk0.description: An increased sensitivity to sounds. Associated with migraine headaches.

zTWrtk0.title: Idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis
zTWrtk0.description: A rare disease characterized by episodic diffuse alveolar hemorrhage. Hemosiderin from repeated episodes of bleeding accumulates over time, causing permanent fibrosis. The etiology is unclear but may be autoimmune-related.

XgW9Fk0.title: Pathogen
XgW9Fk0.description: An organism known to cause disease in humans and, if identified on diagnostics, that is always considered an infection.

cgWa8k0.title: Upper respiratory tract
cgWa8k0.description: The section of the airway between the nares and the epiglottis, encompassing the nasopharynx, oropharynx, and hypopharynx. Some definitions also include the larynx.

1gW28k0.title: Lower respiratory tract
1gW28k0.description: The section of the airway below the epiglottis, encompassing the trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli. Definitions vary for the starting point of the lower airway, with some including the larynx as part of the upper airway.

WgWP8k0.title: Primary bloodstream infection
WgWP8k0.description: A laboratory-confirmed infection of the bloodstream that is not the result of an infection elsewhere (e.g., intravascular catheter-related infection, including central line-associated infection)

UgWbuk0.title: Intrauterine pregnancy
UgWbuk0.description: A pregnancy that occurs within the uterus, as opposed to an extrauterine (ectopic) pregnancy.

2gWTuk0.title: Inflammatory back pain
2gWTuk0.description: A type of nontraumatic back pain caused by conditions such as ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis. Most commonly affects the lumbar spine and is characteristically insidious in onset, worse at night or at rest, and relieved by activity. Usually affects individuals < 40 years of age.

fgWkuk0.title: HIV viral load testing
fgWkuk0.description: A test to determine the number of copies of HIV RNA in a serum sample. Used in patients with confirmed HIV to monitor response to treatment and for certain treatment decisions (e.g., management of HIV infection during pregnancy).

SgWyuk0.title: Qualitative polymerase chain reaction
SgWyuk0.description: A type of polymerase chain reaction that only detects the presence or absence of a specific gene product.

hgWcEk0.title: Suppurative thrombophlebitis
hgWcEk0.description: Thrombosis of a vein related to an infection, most commonly intravascular catheter-related infection, local spread of an infection, or infection linked to IV drug use. Diagnosed based on positive blood cultures and confirmation of a thrombus (e.g., visualization on CT, on US, or upon removal of an indwelling catheter). Complications may include septic emboli and persistent bacteremia or fungemia.

PgWWvk0.title: Isocyanate-induced asthma
PgWWvk0.description: A type of non-IgE-mediated allergic asthma caused by inhalation of isocyanates. Asthma clinical features may be accompanied by alveolitis, eczema, and/or urticaria.

MgWMDk0.title: Technetium-99
MgWMDk0.description: A radionucleotide isotope that can be administered orally or intravenously during radioimaging to enhance certain tissues (e.g., brain, thyroid, bone). Technetium emits gamma rays, which can be detected by a gamma camera for imaging with PET scans. Adverse effects include hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., fever, rash, angioedema, anaphylaxis).

ngW7Dk0.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing
ngW7Dk0.description: A diagnostic study used for the global assessment of exercise capacity. Combines repeated measurements of lung function (e.g., spirometry, respiratory rate), cardiovascular function (e.g., ECG, blood pressure), and gas exchange (e.g., oxygen uptake, carbon dioxide output) during increasingly strenuous exercise. Indications include unexplained dyspnea, suspected exercise-induced bronchospasm, and exercise intolerance. Also used to evaluate exercise capacity and response to treatment in patients with cardiovascular and/or respiratory diseases, and for preoperative evaluation prior to lung and/or cardiac surgery.

LgWwDk0.title: AIP
LgWwDk0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Acute interstitial pneumonia
2. Acute intermittent porphyria
3. Autoimmune pancreatitis

ogW0wk0.title: Cannabis use disorder
ogW0wk0.description: A disorder characterized by severe functional impairment within a 1-year period of cannabis use. Features include the use of cannabis in larger amounts or over a longer period than intended, continued cannabis use despite social or interpersonal problems that are directly caused or exacerbated by its use, a significant increase in the amount of cannabis needed to achieve intoxication, and withdrawal symptoms.

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Cannabis-related disorders

KgWUwk0.title: Consolidation therapy
KgWUwk0.description: The second phase of a chemotherapy regimen. Consolidation therapy aims to maintain remission by destroying any remaining tumor cells after induction therapy.

DgW1xk0.title: Neurovascular imaging
DgW1xk0.description: A set of imaging techniques used to visualize extra- and intracranial blood vessels that supply the central nervous system. Can be noninvasive (e.g., duplex sonography of the carotid arteries, magnetic resonance angiography) or invasive (e.g., conventional angiography).

wgWhxk0.title: Cross-tapering
wgWhxk0.description: A pharmacological technique in which the dose of one medication is gradually decreased and eventually discontinued while the dose of a new medication is simultaneously increased. Can prevent drug interactions, discontinuation syndromes, and worsening of symptoms.

ygWdBk0.title: Cyclizine
ygWdBk0.description: A first-generation antihistamine used to treat symptoms associated with motion sickness (e.g., nausea, vomiting, vertigo) and postoperative nausea and vomiting. Common adverse effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.

AgWRBk0.title: Alosetron
AgWRBk0.description: A selective 5-HT₃ antagonist used to treat diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome. Thought to slow gastrointestinal passage. Common adverse effects include constipation, abdominal discomfort and pain, and nausea. Associated with rare cases of life-threatening ischemic colitis.

_gW5Bk0.title: N-Nitrosodimethylamine
_gW5Bk0.description: A highly hepatotoxic compound and group 2A carcinogen found in low concentrations in certain foods (e.g., cured meat, fish) and drinks (e.g., beer). Has also been found as a contaminant in pharmaceuticals (e.g., valsartan, nizatidine, ranitidine).

zgWrBk0.title: Butterfly vertebrae
zgWrBk0.description: A rare defect of the vertebral bodies that results from lack of fusion of the two lateral chondrification centers during embryogenesis. Has the appearance of butterfly wings on x-ray. Associated with some congenital conditions (e.g., Alagille syndrome, Jarcho-Levin syndrome).

ZSWZyk0.title: Heterotopic pregnancy
ZSWZyk0.description: A rare condition characterized by multiple gestations in which one is intrauterine and another ectopic. Occurs more frequently in patients undergoing infertility treatments (e.g., in vitro fertilization).

0SWeyk0.title: Squaric acid dibutyl ester
0SWeyk0.description: A contact allergen used as a topical immunotherapy to treat alopecia areata. Has an immunomodulatory effect on the hair follicles.

aSWQyk0.title: Diphenylcyclopropenone
aSWQyk0.description: A contact allergen used as a topical immunotherapy to treat alopecia areata. Has an immunomodulatory effect on the hair follicles.

YSWnyk0.title: Treatment-resistant depression
YSWnyk0.description: A condition in which symptoms of major depressive disorder persist despite good adherence to two or more trials of established antidepressant therapy at appropriate doses.

bSWHyk0.title: Diagnostic criteria for premature ejaculation
bSWHyk0.description: A set of diagnostic criteria established by the DSM-V, which include: (A) ejaculation that occurs within ∼ 1 minute of penetration and before the patient wishes to ejaculate; (B) occurrence during ≥ 75% of all sexual encounters and presence for ≥ 6 months; (C) clinically significant distress in the individual; (D) not due to another mental disorder, severe relationship distress, substance abuse, and/or an organic disorder.

cSWaAk0.title: Racemic mixture
