cSWaAk0.description: A mixture of both enantiomers (i.e., levorotatory and dextrorotatory forms) of a molecule in equal proportions.

2SWT_k0.title: Pathologic phimosis
2SWT_k0.description: The inability to retract the foreskin (prepuce) due to distal scarring. Preputial scarring and fibrosis can result from trauma, infection, and inflammation.

destinations.label: Disorders of the glans penis and foreskin → Phimosis

fSWk_k0.title: Physiologic phimosis
fSWk_k0.description: The inability to retract the foreskin in the absence of preputial scarring, fibrosis, infection, trauma, or inflammation. Phimosis is physiologic in most school-age boys and has a high likelihood of spontaneous resolution with increasing age.

destinations.label: Disorders of the glans penis and foreskin → Phimosis

SSWy_k0.title: Testicular workup for ischemia and suspected torsion score
SSWy_k0.description: A scoring system that is used to determine the likelihood of testicular torsion. Measures include the following: Hard testis (2 points); Swelling (2 points); Nausea/vomiting (1 point); Absent cremasteric reflex (1 point); High riding testis (1 point). Scores ≤ 2 indicate low risk, scores of 3 or 4 indicate medium risk and warrant ultrasonography, and scores > 5 indicate high risk, for which patients should proceed to surgical exploration of the scrotum.

media.title: Testicular Workup for Ischemia and Suspected Torsion (TWIST) score

3SWSzk0.title: Purulent pericarditis
3SWSzk0.description: A type of infectious pericarditis characterized by pus in the pericardial sac, which can result in pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade. Can develop after thoracic surgery or cardiac injury. The most common causative organisms are Staphylococcus and Streptococcus.

RSWlzk0.title: Intrapericardial fibrinolysis
RSWlzk0.description: A procedure used to treat persistent purulent pericarditis and constrictive pericarditis. Involves irrigation of the pericardium with streptokinase, urokinase, or tissue plasminogen activator. Surgical drainage may be required if there is extensive loculation.

iSWJzk0.title: Preputioplasty
iSWJzk0.description: A procedure in which a narrow, nonretractile foreskin is widened surgically to achieve a foreskin that can retract or retract more comfortably. Indicated in phimosis and recurrent balanoposthitis.

jSW_zk0.title: Barrier ointment
jSW_zk0.description: A topical medication that forms a physical barrier between the skin and potential irritants. Used to help maintain the skin's physical barrier and treat minor skin irritations (e.g., irritant contact dermatitis).

PSWW-k0.title: Masson body
PSWW-k0.description: A type of granulation tissue bud composed of foamy macrophages, mononuclear cells, and fibrous tissue. Considered a characteristic histologic feature of ​​​​​​​cryptogenic organizing pneumonia. Can also be found in diffuse alveolar damage.

destinations.label: Interstitial lung diseases → Classification of idiopathic interstitial pneumonias

4SW3-k0.title: One-stage exchange arthroplasty
4SW3-k0.description: A surgical procedure used to treat prosthetic joint infections. The prothesis is removed, infectious material debrided, and a new prothesis implanted in a single procedure.

OSWI-k0.title: Urinary extravasation
OSWI-k0.description: The collection of urine in tissues and cavities surrounding the urinary tract, which can develop due to trauma to the kidneys, ureters, or urethra. Complications include sepsis and urinomas.

lSWv-k0.title: SSS
lSWv-k0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Sick sinus syndrome
2. Symptom severity scale

mSWVZO0.title: Cultural syndrome
mSWVZO0.description: A varied set of psychiatric and/or somatic conditions that occur exclusively in a specific culture or society and are generally recognized as medical conditions in the respective communities. Common examples include Ataque de nervios, Dhat syndrome, and Khyâl cap.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Culture in the health care setting

nSW7ZO0.title: Ataque de nervios
nSW7ZO0.description: A cultural syndrome associated with individuals of Latino and/or Caribbean descent. Most commonly begins immediately after a stressful event related to the family, such as the death of a loved one or a conflict with a spouse. Common symptoms are intense screaming, crying, and shaking, physical and/or verbal aggression, and episodes of fainting and psychogenic nonepileptic seizures.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Culture in the health care setting

LSWwZO0.title: Dhat syndrome
LSWwZO0.description: A cultural syndrome associated with male individuals of South Asian descent, in which somatic symptoms (e.g., fatigue, anxiety, impotence) are attributed to loss of semen (considered an essential bodily fluid in Hindu culture), despite no underlying physiologic dysfunction.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Culture in the health care setting

oSW00O0.title: Taijin kyofusho
oSW00O0.description: A cultural syndrome associated with Japanese culture. Typically characterized by the avoidance of interpersonal situations due to a belief that one's actions, appearance, and/or physical characteristics (e.g., shape of face, body odor) are offensive to others. This belief may also lead to symptoms similar to those seen in a panic attack (e.g., palpitations, dyspnea).

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Culture in the health care setting

qSWC0O0.title: Khyal cap
qSWC0O0.description: A cultural concept of distress associated with individuals of Cambodian descent. Symptoms of a panic attack (e.g., palpitations), tinnitus, and neck soreness are attributed to a windlike substance that may have infected the body. Often meets the criteria of panic attack.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Culture in the health care setting

ISWYaO0.title: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
ISWYaO0.description: A subtype of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) caused by a pathogenic mutation in the COL3A1 gene, which leads to defective type III procollagen. Complications include spontaneous arterial aneurysms, dissections, and organ rupture. Joint hypermobility and skin hyperextensibility are absent or less prominent than in other EDS subtypes.

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Etiology and classification

rSWfaO0.title: Classical Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
rSWfaO0.description: A subtype of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) caused by a pathogenic mutation in the COL5A1 or COL5A2 gene, which leads to defective type V collagen. Characterized by large and small joint hypermobility, skin hyperextensibility, and widened atrophic scars. The skin typically has a velvety or doughy appearance. Cardiovascular features (e.g., heart valve defects, aneurysms, dissections) are less common than in other EDS subtypes.

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Etiology and classification

7SW4aO0.title: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
7SW4aO0.description: The most common type of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS); the pathogenic gene variant is unknown. Predominantly characterized by joint instability (e.g., shoulder and patella dislocations). Other clinical features include small- and large-joint hypermobility, joint pain, scoliosis, and premature osteoarthritis. Skin hyperextensibility is less severe than in classic EDS.

destinations.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and Marfan syndrome → Etiology and classification

HSWKaO0.title: Spermatic cord block
HSWKaO0.description: A nerve block procedure that aims to anesthetize scrotal contents. May be performed using anatomical landmarks or under ultrasound guidance. Applications include pain management and anesthesia for surgery or painful noninvasive procedures (e.g., manual testicular detorsion).

sSWtaO0.title: Retropharyngeal space
sSWtaO0.description: An area that runs from the base of the skull to the mediastinum and is bound by the carotid sheath laterally, the prevertebral muscles posteriorly, and the esophagus anteriorly. This space is clinically significant because it is susceptible to deep neck infections (e.g., retropharyngeal abscesses).

FSWgYO0.title: Crotalinae
FSWgYO0.description: A subfamily of venomous vipers found widely across Europe, Asia, and the Americas. Includes rattlesnakes, water moccasins, cottonmouths, and copperheads. Venom effects vary across species but include neurotoxic, hemotoxic, cytotoxic, myotoxic, and proinflammatory effects.

uSWpYO0.title: Double dye test
uSWpYO0.description: A test used to evaluate for a vesicovaginal fistula. The bladder is instilled with methylene blue, which dyes the urine blue. The test is considered positive if a tampon inserted into the vagina stains blue, indicating a communication tract between the bladder and vagina.

ESW8YO0.title: Gold standard test
ESW8YO0.description: The best method available for determining the presence or absence of a disease. Used as the standard to which other tests are compared.

vSWAYO0.title: Lipschutz ulcer
vSWAYO0.description: A rare condition characterized by the sudden onset of painful, large ( > 1 cm), symmetric vulvar ulcerations (kissing ulcers). May be preceded by an influenza- or EBV-like prodrome. Most common among nonsexually active adolescent girls or young women.

DSW1bO0.title: Acute aortic syndrome
DSW1bO0.description: A group of conditions affecting the aorta that have a similar clinical presentation and that may be impossible to differentiate between until surgery. Includes aortic dissection, intramural hematoma, penetrating aortic ulcer, and thoracic aortic rupture.

9SWNbO0.title: Relugolix
9SWNbO0.description: A nonpeptide gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist that competitively binds to pituitary GnRH receptors. Decreases LH and FSH secretion, which results in decreased serum testosterone concentrations. Used to treat hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.

CSWqbO0.title: Invasive blood pressure monitoring
CSWqbO0.description: An advanced method of recording blood pressure via an intraarterial cannula. Typically used for critically ill patients as it allows for the continuous monitoring of blood pressure and can more accurately record blood pressure at lower levels than blood pressure cuffs.

ySWdXO0.title: Periodontal ligament
ySWdXO0.description: A collagenous ligament that connects the root of the tooth to the alveolar bone.

ASWRXO0.title: Hank's Balanced Salt Solution
ASWRXO0.description: An isotonic buffer solution used to maintain osmolality and pH to preserve cell integrity in vitro. Contains glucose and several inorganic salts, including sodium bicarbonate and magnesium sulfate.

bhWHcO0.title: Bunina body
bhWHcO0.description: A small, round or oval, eosinophilic intraneuronal inclusion that appears bright pink on H&E staining. Found in remaining lower motor neurons in individuals with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Thought to be a specific hallmark of ALS.

XhW9cO0.title: Ammonia intoxication
XhW9cO0.description: A condition caused by exposure to ammonia, such as from environmental exposure. Clinical features include rhinorrhea, scratchy throat, chest tightness, cough, dyspnea, and eye irritation.

chWa1O0.title: Hereditary cancer syndrome
chWa1O0.description: A group of genetic disorders characterized by an increased susceptibility to specific types of cancer. Some of the most common hereditary cancer syndromes include hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome, Lynch syndrome, Li–Fraumeni syndrome, Cowden syndrome, and Peutz–Jeghers syndrome.

1hW21O0.title: Chlorine
1hW21O0.description: A green-yellow, water-soluble gas. Sources of exposure include household products (e.g., cleaning mixtures, pool disinfectant) and various industries (e.g., papermaking, textiles, paint). Dissolution in water leads to the formation of hypochlorous and hydrochloric acid and free oxygen radicals.

WhWP1O0.title: Nitrogen oxides
WhWP1O0.description: A group of gaseous oxides that contain nitrogen. Includes NO, a colorless and odorless gas, and NO₂, a reddish-brown gas with a pungent odor. The main sources of exposure in urban areas are motor vehicle exhausts and indoor gas stoves. Also generated from the decomposition of silage. Exposure can cause irritation of mucous membranes (e.g., cough, dyspnea, chest pain), pulmonary symptoms (e.g., chemical pneumonitis, bronchiolitis obliterans), acute respiratory distress syndrome, sepsis, and acute heart failure.

dhWo1O0.title: 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzodioxin
dhWo1O0.description: A type of polychlorinated dibenzodioxin that is most commonly formed during combustion or as a side product of chemical synthesis. Best known as a contaminant in the herbicide Agent Orange, which was used during the Vietnam War. Classified as a carcinogen and is associated with birth defects.

2hWTWO0.title: Parasitism
2hWTWO0.description: A relationship between a symbiont (parasite) and its host in which the symbiont benefits from the relationship and the host is harmed.

fhWkWO0.title: Chlorinated hydrocarbon
fhWkWO0.description: A group of compounds that contain chlorine, carbon, and hydrogen. Can be found in several pesticides (e.g., DDT, lindane), industrial chemicals (e.g., PCB), and chlorine waste products (e.g., furans, dioxins). Compounds from this group generally persist in the environment and can cause endocrine system toxicity and cancer.

ThW6WO0.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
ThW6WO0.description: A class of organic substances characterized by the presence of at least two fused aromatic rings. Found in natural sources (e.g., coal, bitumen) but also form during combustion (e.g., of wood, garbage, tobacco, fossil fuels). Some substances have been classified as possible or probable human carcinogens.

ghWFWO0.title: Dental avulsion
ghWFWO0.description: A dental injury in which a tooth is completely displaced from its socket.

ShWyWO0.title: CHC
ShWyWO0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Combined estrogen-progestin hormonal contraception
2. Chlorinated hydrocarbon

hhWcdO0.title: Dental subluxation
hhWcdO0.description: The disruption of the periodontal ligament with subsequent instability of the tooth within the dental socket. In dental subluxation, the tooth is mobile but remains in the correct anatomical position, while in dental luxation, the tooth is displaced into a nonanatomical position.

ihWJdO0.title: Secondary iron overload
ihWJdO0.description: An acquired condition characterized by excess iron deposition. Causes include iron-loading anemias (e.g., beta-thalassemia major), frequent transfusion, chronic liver disease (e.g., heavy alcohol use, hepatitis C, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease), and porphyria cutanea tarda. Manifestations are similar to those of primary iron overload (e.g., skin hyperpigmentation, arthropathies, cirrhosis).

jhW_dO0.title: Milwaukee shoulder syndrome
jhW_dO0.description: A rare crystalline arthropathy caused by the deposition of basic calcium phosphate crystals in or around the shoulder joint. It causes significant destruction of the joint, noninflammatory joint effusion, and rotator cuff deficits. May affect joints other than the shoulder in a significant proportion of patients.

destinations.label: Basic calcium phosphate crystal deposition diseases → Milwaukee shoulder syndrome

OhWIVO0.title: Leptospira interrogans
OhWIVO0.description: A pathogenic species of Leptospira that can cause leptospirosis. It is a spiral-shaped, motile, aerobic spirochete. Best visualized with dark field microscopy, silver stain, or fluorescent microscopy because it does not stain well on Gram stain.

lhWvVO0.title: Cultural formulation interview
lhWvVO0.description: A set of questions asked during a mental health examination to assess the effect of the patient's culture on their perception of psychiatric symptoms. This process promotes therapeutic planning, enhances the patient's engagement during the examination, and helps bridge cultural differences between the physician and the patient that may hinder the management of the patient's condition.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Culture in the health care setting

NhW-VO0.title: Acoustic impedance
NhW-VO0.description: The degree of tissue resistance to ultrasound beam penetration. Acoustic impedance is related to the tissue density and the velocity of the ultrasound beam as it passes through the tissue. Air has low acoustic impedance (i.e., allows ultrasound beams to pass through easily) whereas solid organs or fluid-filled areas have higher acoustic impedance.

mhWVeO0.title: Acoustic window
mhWVeO0.description: Areas of the body that transmit ultrasound waves with good ultrasound conductivity. Examples include the liver (acoustic window to the gallbladder) and the filled bladder (acoustic window to the pelvis).

5hWieO0.title: Shiga toxin-associated hemolytic uremic syndrome
5hWieO0.description: The most common form of hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS). Predominantly occurs in children and manifests with the HUS triad (microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury). Caused by bacteria that produce Shiga toxin and are typically transmitted via contaminated foods: most commonly Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) and, rarely, Shigella dysenteriae. A diarrheal illness usually occurs 5–14 days before HUS.

MhWMeO0.title: Non-Shiga toxin-associated HUS
MhWMeO0.description: Hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) that is not caused by Shiga toxin-producing bacteria. Includes complement-mediated HUS (caused by complement pathway dysregulation) and secondary HUS (e.g., due to non-Shiga toxin infections, autoimmune diseases, or cytotoxic drugs).

nhW7eO0.title: Intraocular lens
nhW7eO0.description: An artificial lens that is implanted into the lens chamber after the removal of a cataract.

LhWweO0.title: Patient cohorts
LhWweO0.description: The practice of grouping patients with the same or similar medical condition. Used in research studies to compare treatments and in hospitals to reduce the spread of infection by placing patients with the same infection or colonization together in a room or on a floor.

ohW0UO0.title: HARK screening tool
ohW0UO0.description: A screening instrument for intimate partner violence. Questions ask whether the individual has been (H)umiliated or emotionally abused by; (A)fraid of; (R)aped or forced to have any kind of sexual activity by; or (K)icked, hit, slapped or physically hurt by a partner during the last year.

KhWUUO0.title: STaT questions
KhWUUO0.description: A screening instrument for intimate partner violence. Comprised of the following questions: "Have you ever been in a relationship where your partner has pushed or slapped you?" (S), "Have you ever been in a relationship where your partner threatened you with violence?" (T), and "Have you ever been in a relationship where your partner has thrown, broken or punched things?" (T)

6hWjUO0.title: Pneumopericardium
6hWjUO0.description: The presence of air within the pericardium. Can result from infection with gas-producing organisms or the formation of a fistula between the respiratory tract or upper gastrointestinal tract and the pericardium. A fistula may be caused by trauma (including procedures such as pericardiocentesis), neoplasm, or may be idiopathic.

phWLUO0.title: HITS score
phWLUO0.description: A screening instrument for intimate partner violence. Questions ask how often an individual has been (H)urt physically, (I)nsulted or talked down to, (T)hreatened with physical harm, and (S)creamed or cursed at by a partner.

JhWsUO0.title: Phosgene
JhWsUO0.description: A colorless gas that can be found in household products (e.g., paint removers, dry-cleaning fluids) and in industry settings (e.g., plastic production, pesticides). Intoxication can lead to irritation of the mucous membranes (e.g., lacrimation, cough) and the respiratory system (e.g., pulmonary edema, cyanosis, dyspnea). Exposure to very high concentrations can cause immediate death.

uhWpfO0.title: Primary hyperoxaluria
uhWpfO0.description: A group of genetic disorders that impair the metabolism of glyoxylate and oxalate, resulting in an accumulation of oxalate in the kidneys and other tissues. Primary hyperoxaluria typically manifests with recurrent urolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis. If the disease progresses to renal failure, systemic oxalosis occurs and oxalate deposits may develop in the bones, myocardium, soft tissues, retinas, and peripheral nervous system.

DhW1TO0.title: Pirfenidone
DhW1TO0.description: An antifibrotic agent that inhibits TGF-β stimulated collagen synthesis, decreases extracellular matrix accumulation, and blocks PDGF effects in vitro. Used to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

whWhTO0.title: Nintedanib
whWhTO0.description: An intracellular inhibitor of tyrosine kinases that target fibrogenic growth factors (e.g., vascular endothelial growth factor receptor, fibroblast growth factor receptor, and platelet-derived growth factor receptor). Used to treat idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

9hWNTO0.title: Yusho disease
9hWNTO0.description: A condition caused by the accidental mass poisoning by polychlorinated biphenyl-contaminated rice bran oil in 1968 in northern Kyushi, Japan, which affected ~ 14,000 people. Manifested with acneiform eruptions, hyperpigmentation of skin, nails, conjunctivae, and gingiva, a decreased immune response, and menstrual irregularities. "Yusho" translates to "oil symptoms."

ChWqTO0.title: Fetal dysmaturity
ChWqTO0.description: A condition in postterm pregnancy that causes fetal weight loss, subcutaneous wasting, dry skin due to decreased vernix, absence of lanugo, increased scalp hair, and long fingernails. It is thought to be due to placental insufficiency and oligohydramnios. Complications include polycythemia, hypoglycemia, perinatal asphyxia, meconium aspiration, persistent pulmonary hypertension, and neurodevelopmental abnormalities.

xhWETO0.title: Polychlorinated dibenzofurans
xhWETO0.description: A group of polyhalogenated organic compounds derived from dibenzofurans. Mostly found as byproducts in the manufacture of other chemicals (e.g., PCBs, pesticides) or as a result of combustion processes (e.g., burning of waste). Short-term exposure causes chloracne. Classified as probable human carcinogens.

BhWzTO0.title: Persistent organic pollutants
BhWzTO0.description: A group of organic chemical compounds that persist and accumulate in the environment, food, and fatty tissue, thereby posing a risk to human, wildlife, and environmental health. Includes pesticides (e.g., DDT), industrial chemicals (e.g., polychlorinated biphenyls), and unintentionally produced byproducts (e.g., polychlorinated dibenzodioxins).

AhWRgO0.title: Congeners (chemistry)
AhWRgO0.description: A group of chemical substances that are related to each other by origin, structure, and/or function.

_hW5gO0.title: IARC classification
_hW5gO0.description: A system developed by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) to classify substances based on their carcinogenicity to humans. Consists of 4 groups: group 1 (carcinogenic to humans), group 2A (probably carcinogenic to humans), group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans), and group 3 (not classifiable as to its carcinogenicity to humans).

zhWrgO0.title: Laryngeal chemoreflex
zhWrgO0.description: A complex behavioral response that can be triggered by acidic stimuli (e.g., regurgitation of gastric contents into the pharynx) or organic stimuli (e.g., carbohydrates), resulting in variable degrees of apnea, respiratory inhibition, bradycardia, desaturation, and cardiovascular collapse.

-hWDgO0.title: Naphthalene
-hWDgO0.description: A polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon used in the industrial production of phthalic anhydride and moth balls. Acute exposure (e.g., ingestion, inhalation) can cause neurotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, and hemolytic anemia. Chronic exposure has been linked to cataracts and retinal damage.

Z3WZSO0.title: Late-term pregnancy
Z3WZSO0.description: A pregnancy between 41 0/7 weeks and 41 6/7 weeks of gestation.

a3WQSO0.title: Irritant balanoposthitis
a3WQSO0.description: A mild inflammation of the penis and prepuce due to irritation of the skin. Can be caused by excessive cleaning with soap. Often occurs in patients with atopic dermatitis.

destinations.label: Disorders of the glans penis and foreskin → Balanitis and balanoposthitis

Y3WnSO0.title: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw
Y3WnSO0.description: A complication of osteoclast inhibitor therapy (e.g., bisphosphonates, RANKL inhibitors) and antiangiogenic drugs (e.g., VEGF inhibitors, tyrosine kinase inhibitors) that is characterized by exposure and necrosis of the jaw bone with associated pain, erythema, and swelling.

b3WHSO0.title: Perianal streptococcal dermatitis
b3WHSO0.description: An infection of the perianal skin by group A streptococci. Manifestations include a perianal, pruritic rash, rectal pain, and blood-streaked stools. Most common in children between 6 months and 10 years of age.

destinations.label: Skin and soft tissue infections → Nonpurulent SSTIs

X3W9SO0.title: Ramelteon
X3W9SO0.description: A melatonin receptor agonist used to treat insomnia characterized by difficulty with sleep onset. Adverse effects include dizziness, fatigue, and nausea.

c3WahO0.title: Revised Atlanta classification
c3WahO0.description: A set of definitions and criteria for the diagnosis, severity grading, morphological features, and complications of acute pancreatitis. This classification is a 2012 revision of the original Atlanta classification that was devised in 1992.

13W2hO0.title: Linear array transducer
13W2hO0.description: A type of ultrasound transducer in which the piezoelectric crystals have a linear arrangement, generating a rectangular image. Typically emits ultrasound beams at a high frequency, which leads to a high-resolution image at the expense of limited depth penetration. Uses include imaging of superficial structures such as breast tissue and peripheral vessels.

W3WPhO0.title: Curvilinear array transducer
W3WPhO0.description: A type of ultrasound transducer in which the piezoelectric crystals have a convex arrangement, generating a cone-shaped image. Emits ultrasound beams at a low frequency, which permits visualization of deeper tissues but at the expense of low resolution. Uses include transabdominal, pelvic, and thoracic ultrasound.

d3WohO0.title: Phased array transducer
d3WohO0.description: A type of ultrasound transducer in which the piezoelectric crystals are arranged densely within a small area. Generates a cone-shaped or sector image with a very narrow near field. Has a small footprint, making it the preferred transducer for areas with narrow acoustic windows such as intercostal spaces (e.g., for transthoracic echocardiography). This transducer also allows for continuous wave Doppler application.

V3WGhO0.title: Endocavitary probe
V3WGhO0.description: A type of ultrasound transducer used to visualize structures through natural orifices. The piezoelectric crystals are arranged in the shape of a narrow cylindrical head, which emits ultrasound beams at a high frequency and generates a high-resolution image but with limited depth penetration. Uses include endorectal, transvaginal, and perioral ultrasound.

e3WxhO0.title: PDL
e3WxhO0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Pulsed dye laser
2. Periodontal ligament

U3Wb3O0.title: IOL
U3Wb3O0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Induction of labor
2. Intraocular lens

23WT3O0.title: Retentive encopresis
23WT3O0.description: A type of encopresis associated with underlying constipation or fecal impaction with consequent overflow fecal incontinence. Can be behavioral (e.g., constipation that develops after suppressing the urge to defecate) or due to organic disease (e.g., Hirschsprung disease, spinal cord injuries, cerebral palsy, other disorders that affect the pelvic floor and external anal sphincter).

f3Wk3O0.title: Nonretentive encopresis
f3Wk3O0.description: A type of encopresis that is not associated with constipation or fecal overflow incontinence. Usually has no organic cause and is more commonly associated with a history of behavioral or psychologic problems (e.g., anxiety, depression, ADHD, conduct disorder).

h3WcRO0.title: Olfactory reference syndrome
h3WcRO0.description: A condition in which individuals mistakenly believe that their body odor is foul and offensive to others. This may lead to extreme distress during social interactions and/or complete avoidance of interpersonal situations.

33WSRO0.title: Sialography
33WSRO0.description: The imaging of the salivary glands. Includes conventional sialography, which involves injection of contrast to one of the salivary ducts and examining it fluoroscopically or via computed tomography, and magnetic resonance sialography, which is noninvasive and typically does not require contrast.

R3WlRO0.title: Chemical restraint
R3WlRO0.description: A medication that is used to impair or limit free movement of a patient's extremities, body, or head. Examples include benzodiazepines and antipsychotics.

i3WJRO0.title: Four-point restraint
i3WJRO0.description: A type of physical restraint system in which the ankles and wrists are bound to a bed frame with soft leather braces.

Q3WuRO0.title: Idiopathic neonatal hepatitis
Q3WuRO0.description: A neonatal condition with unclear etiology characterized by intralobular inflammation of the liver and multinucleated giant cell formation. Causes obstructive jaundice.

j3W_RO0.title: Delayed passage of meconium
j3W_RO0.description: An inability in newborns to pass meconium within 48 hours of birth. Common causes include perinatal administration of certain drugs (e.g., magnesium sulfate, opiates) to the mother, functional ileus (e.g., due to prematurity, sepsis, respiratory distress, electrolyte abnormalities, congenital hypothyroidism), Hirschsprung disease, meconium ileus (typically due to cystic fibrosis), and intestinal obstruction (e.g., volvulus, anal atresia).

P3WWiO0.title: Female orgasmic disorder
P3WWiO0.description: A psychiatric diagnosis characterized by a marked delay in, infrequency of, or absence of orgasm or markedly reduced intensity of orgasmic sensations that persist for ≥ 6 months and result in clinically significant distress.

destinations.label: Sexual dysfunction and paraphilic disorders → Sexual dysfunction

m3WVQO0.title: Miliaria rubra
m3WVQO0.description: A transient exanthem characterized by erythematous, nonfollicularly-based papules, often with a background of erythema. Most commonly distributed on the head, neck, and upper trunk. Can occur in the diaper region due to localized humidity and heat. Caused by blockage of eccrine sweat ducts within the epidermis.

53WiQO0.title: Transthyretin stabilizer
53WiQO0.description: A medication used in the treatment of cardiac amyloidosis. Counteracts the pathologic dissociation of the protein transthyretin into monomers that misassemble into amyloid fibrils. Examples include tafamidis and diflunisal.

M3WMQO0.title: Top of the basilar syndrome
M3WMQO0.description: The thromboembolic occlusion of the anterior part of the basilar artery, which leads to ischemia and infarction of the midbrain, thalami, temporal lobes, and/or occipital lobes. Clinical manifestations include impairment of mental status, behavior, memory, vision, and oculomotor and pupillary function. Sensory and motor deficits are typically absent.

n3W7QO0.title: Destination therapy
n3W7QO0.description: An intervention intended to permanently treat a condition. Most often refers to the use of a mechanical circulatory support device (e.g., left ventricular assist device) to permanently treat advanced heart failure. Distinct from bridging therapy, in which the device is used temporarily until transplant.

L3WwQO0.title: Brain biopsy
L3WwQO0.description: A procedure performed in patients with neurological disorders or brain masses in the case of diagnostic uncertainty. A small sample of material is removed with a needle (typically stereotactically, under image guidance) or during surgery (open biopsy) and sent for analysis. Because the procedure carries a number of risks (including infection and neurological damage), alternative methods of confirming the diagnosis are preferred.

o3W0jO0.title: Glossolalia
o3W0jO0.description: A type of rhythmic speech consisting of pseudowords. Considered a culturally-embedded religious activity. A clear connection with psychopathology has not been established.

K3WUjO0.title: Radiopaque marker study
K3WUjO0.description: A study conducted to assess colonic motility (e.g., to evaluate patients with chronic constipation or diarrhea). The patient swallows a series of radiopaque beads, and serial x-rays are obtained until all markers have been expelled.

63WjjO0.title: Fat stranding
63WjjO0.description: An imaging finding of an abnormally increased attenuation of intraabdominal, retroperitoneal, or subcutaneous fat. Can indicate the presence of inflammation.

p3WLjO0.title: Prolonged neonatal jaundice
p3WLjO0.description: A condition of neonatal jaundice that lasts > 14 days after birth. Most affected neonates have benign unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Neonates with conjugated hyperbilirubinemia should be evaluated for cholestatic liver disease (e.g., biliary atresia, lipid storage diseases, choledochal cyst).

I3WYPO0.title: Graded compression ultrasonography
I3WYPO0.description: An ultrasonographic technique in which the transducer is used to gradually compress the abdominal wall, which displaces the bowel to better visualize intraabdominal structures. Can be used to diagnose appendicitis in children and pregnant individuals.

83WO4O0.title: Speech sound disorder
83WO4O0.description: A communication disorder characterized by difficulty producing speech sounds correctly due to insufficient phonological knowledge or an inability to create the sounds.

v3WA4O0.title: Glasgow-Imrie score
v3WA4O0.description: A scoring system used to predict the severity of acute pancreatitis 48 hours after admission. Along with age, seven laboratory parameters are evaluated: WBC, blood glucose, BUN, PaO₂, serum calcium, serum albumin, and AST or ALT.

_3W5OO0.title: Hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy
_3W5OO0.description: A procedure used to treat advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. Involves the placement of a catheter into the hepatic artery and subsequent infusion of cytotoxic chemotherapy. Thought to maximize local drug concentrations by bypassing the hepatic first pass effect. Also decreases systemic adverse effects.

z3WrOO0.title: MUDPILES
z3WrOO0.description: An mnemonic for causes of high anion gap acidosis: Methanol intoxication, Uremia, Diabetic ketoacidosis, Paraldehyde, Isoniazid or Iron overdose, Inborn error of metabolism, Lactic acidosis, Ethylene glycol intoxication, Salicylate intoxication.

-3WDOO0.title: FUSEDCARS
-3WDOO0.description: A mnemonic for causes of normal anion gap acidosis: Fistula (biliary, pancreatic), Ureterogastric conduit, Saline administration, Endocrine (Addison disease, hyper-PTH), Diarrhea, Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor, Ammonium chloride, Renal tubular acidosis, Spironolactone.

ZRWZlO0.title: Phlyctenular conjunctivitis
ZRWZlO0.description: A nodular lesion that forms at the cornea and/or conjunctiva and is caused by a hypersensitivity reaction to microbial antigens, primarily staphylococci, Mycobacteria tuberculosis, and chlamydia, although other agents, viruses, and fungi have also been implicated.

0RWelO0.title: Intermittent renal replacement therapy
0RWelO0.description: A form of extracorporeal renal replacement therapy in which hemodialysis and/or hemofiltration is provided intermittently in sessions typically lasting 3-5 hours. It enables faster solute clearance and ultrafiltration compared with continuous renal replacement therapy.

destinations.label: Renal replacement therapy → Hemodialysis and hemofiltration

aRWQlO0.title: Perioperative bridging therapy
aRWQlO0.description: A method of reducing the risk of both periprocedural thromboembolism and bleeding in patients taking a vitamin K antagonist (VKA) such as warfarin. The VKA is discontinued a few days before an elective procedure and, when the international normalized ratio (INR) is in the subtherapeutic range, a shorter-acting parenteral anticoagulant such as low molecular weight heparin or unfractionated heparin is administered. After the procedure, the VKA is reinitiated, and the parenteral agent is continued until the INR returns to the therapeutic range.

destinations.label: Periprocedural management of oral anticoagulant therapy → Periprocedural management of VKAs

cRWaNO0.title: Nonsuicidal self-injury
cRWaNO0.description: The intentional infliction of harm or pain on oneself (e.g., cutting, burning, excessive scratching, hitting) without suicidal intent. Occasionally associated with certain psychiatric disorders (e.g., borderline personality disorder).

1RW2NO0.title: Tree-in-bud sign
1RW2NO0.description: A finding in thin-section chest CT in which areas of centrilobular nodules are connected to a branching linear structure. Produced by caseation within or around bronchioles and smaller segments of the airway. Typically seen in tuberculosis but can also occur in other bacterial, viral, or fungal infections (e.g., Haemophilus influenzae, Aspergillus) and in cystic fibrosis.

WRWPNO0.title: Hair plexus
WRWPNO0.description: A type of mechanoreceptor that consists of nerve endings wrapped around the base of a hair bulb. Involved in sensing rapid hair movement and skin deflection.

dRWoNO0.title: Endosteal scalloping
dRWoNO0.description: A radiographic pattern of focal bone resorption of the inner cortex layer (i.e., the endosteum) caused by slow-growing benign or malignant medullary lesions (e.g., enchondroma, osteomyelitis, chondrosarcoma, multiple myeloma).

VRWGNO0.title: Osteosclerosis
VRWGNO0.description: An abnormal hardening of bone tissue caused by increased bone formation and/or decreased bone resorption. Causes increased fragility of the affected bones despite elevated bone density. Etiologies include congenital (e.g., osteopetrosis), inflammatory (e.g., osteomyelitis), toxic (e.g., bisphosphonate intoxication), endocrine (e.g., hyperparathyroidism), and neoplastic (e.g., multiple myeloma, osteosarcoma) disorders.

SRWymO0.title: Apnea of prematurity
SRWymO0.description: A developmental disorder characterized by episodes of apnea that last > 20 seconds or shorter episodes that are accompanied by hypoxemia and/or bradycardia in premature infants. Caused by immature respiratory control.

destinations.label: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome → Differential diagnoses

3RWS5O0.title: Anterior axillary line
3RWS5O0.description: An imaginary vertical line on the anterolateral abdominal wall that runs through the highest point of the anterior axillary fold, which is formed by the pectoralis major muscle.

RRWl5O0.title: Hyperechogenicity
RRWl5O0.description: The ability of tissue to reflect more sound waves compared to other tissue, which results in increased brightness on ultrasonography. Tissues with relatively high echogenicity include bone and fascia.

iRWJ5O0.title: Hypoechogenicity
iRWJ5O0.description: The ability of tissue to reflect fewer sound waves compared to other tissue, which results in decreased brightness on ultrasonography. Tissues with relatively low echogenicity include lung, fat, and liver.

QRWu5O0.title: Surface epithelium
QRWu5O0.description: A specialized layer of tissue formed by closely aggregated cells that line the outer surface of organs, blood vessels, the skin, and the inner surface of body cavities. Divided into squamous, cuboidal, and columnar types.

4RW3MO0.title: 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzofuran
4RW3MO0.description: A type of polychlorinated dibenzofuran that is most commonly formed during combustion or as a side product of chemical synthesis. Classified as a carcinogen and is associated with birth defects.

mRWVnO0.title: Metabolic complications of AKI
mRWVnO0.description: The metabolic disturbances that may result from acute kidney dysfunction. They include hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, hypermagnesemia, and metabolic acidosis.

5RWinO0.title: Oral phosphate binders
5RWinO0.description: A collection of medications that bind to dietary phosphate and prevent its absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. Used to treat hyperphosphatemia in patients with impaired renal phosphate excretion (e.g., in acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease). Agents include sevelamer, calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, magnesium hydroxide, and lanthanum.

KRWULO0.title: Folliculin
KRWULO0.description: A protein encoded by the tumor suppressor gene FLCN. Mutations in FLCN can cause Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome.

pRWLLO0.title: Eosinophilic folliculitis
pRWLLO0.description: A pruritic rash characterized by coalescing papules or pustules. Typically seen in patients with advanced HIV or AIDS. May be misdiagnosed as acne or bacterial folliculitis. However, the rash can occur in areas not commonly affected by acne (e.g., retroauricular region) and cultures from pustules are typically sterile. Usually disappears with antiretroviral therapy.

media.title: Eosinophilic folliculitis in a child with HIV infection

JRWsLO0.title: Substantia innominata
JRWsLO0.description: An area of the brain located in the posterior part of the anterior perforated substance of the basal forebrain. Consists of gray and white matter and contains the basal nucleus of Meynert. Degeneration of cholinergic neurons in the basal nucleus plays a role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer disease.

qRWCLO0.title: CKD-EPI equation
qRWCLO0.description: An equation used to estimate the glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in patients with chronic kidney disease based on the patient's serum creatinine and/or cystatin C levels, age, and gender. It is considered to be more accurate than the MDRD equation in patients with normal or mildly decreased renal function (i.e., eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m2).

IRWYoO0.title: MDRD equation
IRWYoO0.description: An equation used to estimate the glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in patients with chronic kidney disease based on the patient's age, gender, and serum creatinine level. Useful in patients with an eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 but tends to underestimate the true GFR in patients with normal or mildly decreased renal function.

rRWfoO0.title: Kinetic eGFR
rRWfoO0.description: An equation used to estimate the glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in the setting of rapidly changing renal function. It is based on the patient's prior creatinine level at steady-state and the change in serum creatinine level within a specific time interval. Useful in patients with acute kidney injury for whom conventional eGFR equations, which assume that creatinine is in a steady-state (e.g., CKD-EPI), are not appropriate.

7RW4oO0.title: Paraplegia
7RW4oO0.description: A partial or complete paralysis of the lower extremities caused by injury to the spinal cord.

tRWXKO0.title: Primary effusion lymphoma
tRWXKO0.description: A rare subtype of non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma most commonly seen in HIV-positive patients coinfected with human herpesvirus-8. Typically manifests with large effusions in the peritoneal, pleural, or pericardial spaces.

vRWAKO0.title: Cerebellar ataxia
vRWAKO0.description: A type of ataxia caused by injury to the cerebellum. Manifestations vary based on the underlying cause and severity of cerebellar injury but include gait ataxia, truncal ataxia, limb ataxia, tremor, dysdiadochokinesia, dysarthria, and oculomotor dysfunction (including nystagmus).

wRWh6O0.title: STOP SV strategy
wRWh6O0.description: A program developed by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to prevent sexual violence, mitigate its effects, address its social determinants, and facilitate access to services for individuals who have experienced violence.

9RWN6O0.title: Collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
9RWN6O0.description: A heterogeneous group of disorders characterized histologically by segmental collapse and sclerosis of the glomerular tuft. Manifests as nephrotic syndrome and rapid loss of renal function. Typically seen in patients with HIV (HIV-associated nephropathy), especially those of African descent, but can also occur in individuals who do not have HIV.

CRWq6O0.title: Capillary leakage
CRWq6O0.description: An increased leakage of fluid from the intravascular space into the interstitial space. Etiologies include increased hydrostatic pressure (e.g., in heart failure), decreased capillary oncotic pressure (e.g., albumin loss in renal failure or decreased albumin production in liver failure), and increased capillary permeability (e.g., in sepsis).

BRWz6O0.title: Woman Abuse Screening Tool
BRWz6O0.description:
An eight-question screening tool used to screen for intimate partner violence.
1) Has your partner ever abused you sexually?
2) Has your partner ever abused you emotionally?
3) Has your partner ever abused you physically?
4) Do you ever feel frightened by what your partner says or does?
5) Do arguments ever result in hitting, kicking, or pushing?
6) Do arguments ever result in you feeling down or bad about yourself? Often, sometimes, never?
7) Do you and your partner work out arguments with great difficulty, some difficulty, or no difficulty?
8) In general, how would you describe your relationship? A lot of tension, some tension, no tension?

_RW5pO0.title: Microtia
_RW5pO0.description: A congenital deformity of the ear characterized by underdevelopment of the pinna and hearing impairment. Varies in severity and can occur as an isolated birth defect or as part of a syndrome (e.g., Treacher Collins syndrome, Goldenhar syndrome).

ZiWZJO0.title: Anotia
ZiWZJO0.description: A congenital ear deformity characterized by complete absence of the pinna and hearing impairment. Can occur as an isolated birth defect or as part of a syndrome (e.g., Treacher Collins syndrome, Goldenhar syndrome).

0iWeJO0.title: Benign fasciculation syndrome
0iWeJO0.description: A chronic condition characterized by profuse fasciculations without muscle weakness, atrophy, or other neurologic abnormalities. The pathophysiology of this condition is not fully understood; stress, anxiety, and caffeine consumption have been identified as exacerbating factors.

destinations.label: Rare neurological diseases → Cramp fasciculation syndrome

aiWQJO0.title: Abdominal obesity
aiWQJO0.description: A condition characterized by excessive deposition of abdominal fat (subcutaneous and intra-abdominal) that is independent of BMI and results in a large waist circumference, defined as ≥ 88 cm in women and ≥ 102 cm in men (or ≥ 80 cm in women and ≥ 90 cm in men of Asian descent). Intra-abdominal fat has distinct metabolic activity compared to subcutaneous fat, and abdominal obesity is associated with an increased risk of diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

YiWnJO0.title: Nerve conduction velocity
YiWnJO0.description: A parameter measured during motor nerve conduction studies. Decreased nerve conduction velocity indicates nerve demyelination and/or nerve compression (e.g., median nerve compressed within flexor retinaculum in carpal tunnel syndrome; demyelination of peripheral nerves in Guillain-Barre syndrome).

diWoqO0.title: Varicella-zoster retinitis
diWoqO0.description: A group of disorders characterized by rapidly progressive necrosis of the retina caused by herpes zoster infection. Can manifest as acute retinal necrosis (ARN) or progressive outer retinal necrosis (PORN). Associated with a poor prognosis for vision preservation, especially in the case of PORN.

ViWGqO0.title: Presbyphagia
ViWGqO0.description: The characteristic changes and mild decline in swallowing function seen in older adults. Is typically asymptomatic. Dysphagia in an older patient should not be assumed to be presbyphagia.

TiW6IO0.title: Natriuretic peptide
TiW6IO0.description: A peptide hormone released from myocytes in response to increased stretch (e.g., due to fluid overload). Ventricular or brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) is released from ventricular myocytes, while atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) is released by atrial myocytes. Leads to systemic vasodilation and increased diuresis.

SiWyIO0.title: Bulbar muscles
SiWyIO0.description: The muscles of the throat and mouth responsible for swallowing and speech.

hiWcrO0.title: Congenital heart disease
hiWcrO0.description: An inborn structural defect of the heart and/or great vessels. Depending on the anomaly, shunting can occur. Right-to-left shunting results in deoxygenated blood bypassing the lungs and entering the systemic circulation, which results in cyanosis. Examples include transposition of the great vessels and tetralogy of Fallot. Acyanotic congenital heart defects with left-to-right shunting include ventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect, and patent ductus arteriosus.

3iWSrO0.title: SCOFF questionnaire
3iWSrO0.description: A screening tool for eating disorders that consists of five close-ended questions. A score of ≥ 2 indicates that anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa is likely. May be less effective at identifying other eating disorders

RiWlrO0.title: Hemorrhagic transformation of ischemic stroke
RiWlrO0.description: A complication of ischemic stroke characterized by the development of hemorrhage in the same region as previous ischemia within 1-2 days of the ischemic event. Typically associated with the use of thrombolytic therapy.

QiWurO0.title: Afferent pathway
QiWurO0.description: A neural pathway that consists of sensory fibers that transmit impulses from sensory receptors to the central nervous system.

jiW_rO0.title: Efferent pathway
jiW_rO0.description: A neural pathway that conducts neural impulses from the central nervous system to their peripheral target region.

PiWW7O0.title: Sensory level
PiWW7O0.description: The most caudal dermatome with intact sensation for both light touch and pinprick.

4iW37O0.title: Immunoglobulin G index
4iW37O0.description: The ratio of cerebrospinal to serum immunoglobulin G concentrations divided by the ratio of cerebrospinal to serum albumin concentrations (i.e., (CSF IgG/serum IgG)/(CSF albumin/serum albumin)). Used to assess intrathecal production of immunoglobulins. A raised IgG index can be caused by multiple sclerosis or transverse myelitis.

miWVHO0.title: Walled-off necrosis
miWVHO0.description: An enclosed collection of pancreatic and/or peripancreatic necrotic tissue that usually develops from an acute necrotic collection and matures over at least 4 weeks after the onset of necrotizing pancreatitis. It is distinct from pancreatic abscess, which is a collection of purulent material without significant necrotic tissue.

niW7HO0.title: Bedside index of severity of acute pancreatitis
niW7HO0.description: A score to determine the severity of acute pancreatitis based on five criteria: BUN > 8.9 mmol/L, altered mental status, presence of systemic inflammatory response syndrome, age > 60 years, and pleural effusion on chest x-ray. A score of ≥ 2 indicates severe pancreatitis.

destinations.label: Acute pancreatitis → Severity grading and prognostic scores

media.title: Bedside index of severity of acute pancreatitis (BISAP score)

oiW0sO0.title: Citrate toxicity
oiW0sO0.description: A disorder that occurs when citrate levels become elevated, most commonly following massive blood transfusion. Citrate is added to blood products and acts as a preservative and anticoagulant. Citrate toxicity can cause profound hypocalcemia, metabolic alkalosis, and other electrolyte abnormalities.

6iWjsO0.title: High efficiency particulate air filter
6iWjsO0.description: A filtration system that eliminates particles of a particular size (e.g., dust, bacteria, viruses) from the air by conducting it through an arrangement of fiber mats. Can be used in infection prevention (e.g., in airborne infection isolation rooms and powered air-purifying respirators).

piWLsO0.title: Silo filler's disease
piWLsO0.description: An occupational disease caused by the inhalation of silo gas (NO₂ and CO₂). Immediate symptoms (e.g., cough, nausea) may be followed by a symptom-free period (3–30 hours) before the onset of chemical pneumonitis. Prevention involves personal protective equipment and proper workplace controls.

JiWssO0.title: Powered air-purifying respirator
JiWssO0.description: A respirator connected to a power source (e.g., a battery). It removes specific components (e.g., gases, bacteria, viruses) from the air by actively conducting it through a set of filters. Usually part of a system that covers the whole head, providing eye protection as well.

HiWKGO0.title: Overtransfusion
HiWKGO0.description: The excessive transfusion of packed red blood cells, which may lead to an increased risk of morbidity and mortality.  The exact hemoglobin threshold for overtransfusion varies between studies but is typically stated as more than 11-12 g/dL 24 hours after the last transfusion was given.

siWtGO0.title: MTP
siWtGO0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Metatarsophalangeal
2. Massive transfusion protocol
3. Microsomal transfer protein

GiWBGO0.title: Massive transfusion protocol
GiWBGO0.description: An established protocol designed to safely and swiftly replace blood loss in massive hemorrhage. Typically involves the coordinated release, delivery, and transfusion of a fixed ratio of blood products in order to minimize complications from massive transfusion.

tiWXtO0.title: Massive hemorrhage
tiWXtO0.description: A potentially life-threatening volume of blood loss. Various definitions exist, including the loss of more than 1 blood volume within 24 hours, loss of 50% of the total blood volume within 3-4 hours, bleeding rate of more than 150 mL/minute, and bleeding that leads to significant hypotension (SBP < 90 mmHg) and tachycardia (HR > 110/minute).

FiWgtO0.title: Central nervous system depression
FiWgtO0.description: A state of inhibited and/or suppressed brain activity. Manifestations include decreased respiratory rate and heart rate and a lower level of consciousness. Drugs that cause CNS depression include ethanol, opioids, and benzodiazepines.

8iWOtO0.title: Renally cleared medications
8iWOtO0.description: Medications with active forms or metabolites that are eliminated primarily by the kidneys through excretion and/or metabolism (e.g., metformin, digoxin). May accumulate in patients with acute or chronic kidney dysfunction and therefore often require renal dose adjustment.

uiWptO0.title: Hepatotoxicity
uiWptO0.description: The ability of a substance to damage the liver. Hepatotoxic drugs include acetaminophen, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, terbinafine, nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, and statins.

viWAtO0.title: Alternatives to blood transfusion
viWAtO0.description: A variety of treatments used to prevent and treat blood loss and anemia with the aim of avoiding blood transfusion. Includes the use of erythropoiesis-stimulating agents; supplementation of B12, folate, and/or iron (including iron transfusions); reducing blood loss through the use of antifibrinolytics; and minimizing iatrogenic blood loss through proactive hemostasis and surgical techniques.

DiW1FO0.title: Chimney sweeps' carcinoma
DiW1FO0.description: A cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the scrotum caused by exposure to soot. First described in British chimney sweeps in the 18th century.

CiWqFO0.title: Digital breast tomosynthesis
CiWqFO0.description: A radiographic technique that uses mammography images obtained at different angles to reconstruct an image of the breast. Used in screening and diagnostics for breast cancer.

BiWzFO0.title: Hyposomnia
BiWzFO0.description: A decrease in sleep time as a result of a difficulty in initiating and/or maintaining sleep. Causes include poor sleep hygiene and environmental disturbances (e.g., noise), pain, stimulant medications, life stressors and certain psychiatric illnesses (e.g., major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder), certain sleep disorders (e.g., insomnia disorder, delayed sleep phase disorder), and diseases affecting the brain (e.g., tumors, metabolic encephalopathies).

_iW58O0.title: Inoculation
_iW58O0.description: The introduction of immunologically active material (e.g., microorganisms, antigens, antibodies) into an organism.

-iWD8O0.title: Long exercise test
-iWD8O0.description: A provocative electrodiagnostic test in which the compound motor action potential is measured at baseline, during 5 minutes of sustained exercise, and over a 30-45 minute period after exercise. Used in the evaluation of certain skeletal muscle channelopathies, such as periodic paralyses and paramyotonia congenita.

ZQWZuO0.title: Compound muscle action potential
ZQWZuO0.description: The sum of muscle action potentials of synchronously activated muscle fibers during motor nerve conduction studies. Can be used to evaluate for axonal damage.

0QWeuO0.title: Andersen-Tawil syndrome
0QWeuO0.description: A rare, autosomal dominant disorder characterized by the clinical triad of periodic paralysis, cardiac abnormalities (e.g., arrhythmias), and dysmorphic features (e.g., hypertelorism, syndactyly, clinodactyly of the 5th finger, micrognathia, broad forehead, malar hypoplasia, cleft palate). Caused by mutations in a potassium channel encoded by the KCNJ2 gene.

YQWnuO0.title: Hyperreninemia
YQWnuO0.description: A state of elevated serum renin concentration. Can be triggered by decreased renal perfusion, hyponatremia, and increased sympathetic tone. Leads to activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and subsequent increase in blood pressure and extracellular fluid volume and decrease in serum potassium concentration. Etiologies of hyperreninemia include dehydration, hemorrhage, diabetic nephropathy, Bartter syndrome, and Gitelman syndrome.

XQW9uO0.title: Albuminuria
XQW9uO0.description: The excretion of albumin in the urine. Occurs in conditions in which the permeability of the glomerular filtration barrier is increased (e.g., diabetic nephropathy, nephrotic syndrome). Further classified as microalbuminuria (30–300 mg/day) or macroalbuminuria (>300 mg/day).

cQWaEO0.title: Glomerulosclerosis
cQWaEO0.description: A scarring of the renal glomeruli with deposition of extracellular matrix, which leads to impaired glomerular filtration and proteinuria. Can occur in a segmental pattern (e.g., in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis) or nodular pattern (e.g., in diabetic nephropathy).

1QW2EO0.title: Erythropoietin-stimulating agent
1QW2EO0.description: Recombinant human erythropoietin drug formulations that are used to treat anemia of chronic kidney disease, chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression, and anemia in myelodysplastic syndromes. Stimulate the production of erythrocytes in the bone marrow.

dQWoEO0.title: Rehabilitation
dQWoEO0.description: The restoration, maintenance, or improvement of former capacity, function, or condition. Medical professionals are often involved in either medical or social rehabilitation. Medical rehabilitation deals with the rehabilitation of physical and/or psychological function impaired by a medical condition. Social rehabilitation concerns social standing, privileges, and/or participation in response to circumstances with negative social and/or economic effects on the individual.

VQWGEO0.title: Medical rehabilitation
VQWGEO0.description: The restoration, maintenance, or improvement of physical and/or psychological function impaired by a medical condition.

eQWxEO0.title: Social rehabilitation
eQWxEO0.description: The restoration, maintenance, or improvement of social standing, privileges, and/or participation in response to circumstances with negative social and/or economic effects on the individual.

UQWbvO0.title: Anal pruritus
UQWbvO0.description: An itching of the anal region that can vary in severity from mildly irritating to extremely uncomfortable. Can be idiopathic or caused by infection (e.g., Candida, pinworm), local irritation (e.g., fecal leakage), inflammatory disorders (e.g., psoriasis, eczema), systemic diseases (e.g., uremia), or neoplasms (e.g., Paget disease).

TQW6vO0.title: Deliriogenic medications
TQW6vO0.description: A group of medications that can promote the development or worsen the symptoms of delirium. Includes benzodiazepines, anticholinergic drugs, and opioids.

gQWFvO0.title: Toddler
gQWFvO0.description: A child between the ages of 1 and 3 years.

QQWuDO0.title: Preschool-age child
QQWuDO0.description: A child in the age range to attend preschool. In the US, this is typically between 3 and 5 years of age.

jQW_DO0.title: School-age child
jQW_DO0.description: A child between the ages of 6 and 12 years.

PQWWwO0.title: Uremic bleeding syndrome
PQWWwO0.description: A condition seen in advanced renal failure in which patients present with prolonged or spontaneous bleeding in different organs, e.g., the skin, urinary or gastrointestinal tract. Diagnosis is clinical but bleeding time is typically prolonged. Treatment usually involves a combination of desmopressin, cryoprecipitate, erythropoietin, conjugated estrogens, and/or dialysis.

kQWmwO0.title: Transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease
kQWmwO0.description: A rare complication of blood transfusions that most commonly occurs in immunosuppressed patients. Lymphocytes in the transfused blood attack host tissues, causing symptoms such as fever, rash, and gastrointestinal upset. Laboratory studies show pancytopenia and deranged liver chemistries. The condition is almost universally fatal.

OQWIwO0.title: Mill wheel sign
OQWIwO0.description: A churning sound on auscultation of the precordial region throughout the cardiac cycle. Caused by the presence of air within the chambers of the heart (e.g., due to venous air embolism).

lQWvwO0.title: Air lock
lQWvwO0.description: An obstruction of the right ventricular outflow tract by a large air bubble can occur due to venous air embolism. Can lead to decreased pulmonary arterial and systemic arterial pressure and increased central venous pressure, ultimately resulting in circulatory collapse.

5QWi9O0.title: Reactive follicular hyperplasia
5QWi9O0.description: An increased size and quantity of lymphoid follicles in lymph nodes due to activation of B cells by inflammatory and/or immunologic triggers, such as infections and autoimmune diseases.

8QWOBO0.title: Chloride-responsive metabolic alkalosis
8QWOBO0.description: A type of metabolic alkalosis manifesting with low urinary chloride concentration (≤ 25 mEq/L) that can be corrected by the administration of a chloride-containing solution (e.g., normal saline). Associated with volume and chloride depletion. Etiologies include vomiting, excessive nasogastric suction, and cystic fibrosis.

uQWpBO0.title: Tofacitinib
uQWpBO0.description: A Janus kinase inhibitor used in the treatment of autoimmune diseases (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, ulcerative colitis). Adverse effects include upper respiratory tract infections, nasopharyngitis, and elevated cholesterol levels

destinations.label: COVID-19 (coronavirus disease 2019) → Management of hospitalized patients

EQW8BO0.title: Toe-brachial index
EQW8BO0.description: A sensitive, noninvasive test for peripheral artery disease in the lower extremity. The systolic blood pressure of the first toe is divided by the systolic blood pressure of the brachial artery. A ratio of ≤ 0.70 is commonly used as a threshold to indicate the presence of peripheral arterial disease.

xQWEyO0.title: Emergency medicine
xQWEyO0.description: A primary care specialty that focuses on treating patients with urgent and emergent health care needs.

yQWdAO0.title: Anti-GQ1b antibody
yQWdAO0.description: An autoantibody against the ganglioside antigen GQ1b. May be detected in patients with Miller-Fisher syndrome and Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis, which are variants of Guillain-Barré syndrome.

AQWRAO0.title: Anti-GT1a antibody
AQWRAO0.description: An autoantibody against the ganglioside antigen GT1a. Classically seen in patients with the pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant of Guillain–Barre syndrome. Can also be found in patients with Miller-Fisher Syndrome and Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis.

_QW5AO0.title: Ganglioside
_QW5AO0.description: A molecule derived from a ceramide with an oligosaccharide chain and one or more sialic acids linked to the chain. While they are ubiquitous throughout the body, they are particularly abundant in the central and peripheral nervous systems, where they play an important role in the development and regeneration of neuronal cells. Associated with various pathologies, as targets of autoimmunity (e.g., multiple sclerosis, Guillain–Barre syndrome), disturbed ganglioside metabolism (e.g., infantile epilepsy, Huntington disease), and ganglioside accumulation (e.g., Tay-Sachs disease).

zQWrAO0.title: Orbital abscess
zQWrAO0.description: A complication of orbital cellulitis that typically manifests with a more severe presentation (e.g., worse pain, greater degree of proptosis) compared to uncomplicated orbital cellulitis. Typically diagnosed with CT scan, which may show a ring-enhancing lesion and/or an air-fluid level in the extraconal space.

-QWDAO0.title: Postobstructive pneumonia
-QWDAO0.description: A pulmonary infection occurring distal to an obstruction of the airway. Obstruction of the airway causes stasis of pulmonary secretions and lung atelectasis, promoting bacterial colonization and subsequent infection. This can be seen in various conditions, e.g., advanced lung cancer, aspirated foreign body.

0jWe_O0.title: Induced sputum
0jWe_O0.description: A method of collecting a respiratory sputum sample while minimizing nasal and oral secretions. Performed by inhaling nebulized saline (isotonic or hypertonic) followed by coughing and expectorating a respiratory sputum sample for analysis.

YjWn_O0.title: Putting on PPE (donning)
YjWn_O0.description: The act of putting on personal protective equipment (PPE) prior to an activity to reduce infection risk to both providers and patients. The type of PPE used varies based on the level of precautions required. Steps may include hand hygiene, gowning, and putting on a mask, respirator, goggles, face shield, and/or gloves.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Personal protective equipment (PPE)

XjW9_O0.title: Features of severe untreated congenital hypothyroidism
XjW9_O0.description: A syndrome caused by severe, untreated congenital hypothyroidism. Manifestations include skeletal deformities (e.g., short stature, delayed fontanelle closure) and permanent intellectual disability.

1jW2zO0.title: Chronic neutrophilic leukemia
1jW2zO0.description: An extremely rare myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by leukocytosis with significant left shift (≥ 80% of WBCs are segmented neutrophils and band forms) and mutations in the CSF3R gene.

WjWPzO0.title: Endobronchial ultrasound
WjWPzO0.description: A diagnostic procedure that utilizes an ultrasound transducer placed using bronchoscopy to visualize peribronchial and mediastinal structures. Typically used to guide needle aspiration of lymph nodes and masses for lung cancer staging, and to facilitate the diagnosis of other pulmonary conditions (e.g., sarcoidosis, tuberculosis).

UjWb-O0.title: Gallstone disease
UjWb-O0.description: The presence of stones in the gallbladder which cause symptoms (e.g., biliary colic, nausea). Further subdivided into uncomplicated disease (biliary colic without gallstone-related complications) and complicated disease (e.g., acute cholecystitis, gallstone ileus).

TjW6-O0.title: Intrinsic resistance
TjW6-O0.description: A naturally occurring phenomenon that describes the innate ability of a bacterial species to resist certain antibiotics (e.g., Enterococcus spp. have intrinsic resistance to penicillinase-resistant penicillins, such as oxacillin and cephalosporins).

hjWcZl0.title: Echogenicity
hjWcZl0.description: The ability of tissue to reflect sound waves. Tissues with relatively high echogenicity appear brighter on ultrasonography.

3jWSZl0.title: Durant maneuver
3jWSZl0.description: A maneuver in which the patient is placed in the left lateral decubitus position if there is concern for venous air embolism. Allows the air to be trapped in the right ventricular apex and, therefore, prevents the obstruction of the pulmonary outflow tract.

QjWuZl0.title: Osler triad
QjWuZl0.description: A clinical triad caused by S. pneumonia, which consists of meningitis, pneumonia, and endocarditis. Often associated with heavy drinking, smoking, cocaine use, and splenectomy.

jjW_Zl0.title: Composite measure
jjW_Zl0.description: A quality measure used in the assessment of health care facilities that aggregates structural, process, and outcome measures into a single score to provide a more comprehensive view.

PjWW0l0.title: Umbilical cord entanglement
PjWW0l0.description: The intrauterine wrapping of the umbilical cord around one or more fetal body parts or the intertwining of the two umbilical cords in monochorionic monoamniotic twin pregnancy. Increases the risk for prolonged labor, umbilical cord compression, and mortality.

4jW30l0.title: Intertwin amniotic fluid discordance
4jW30l0.description: A difference in amniotic fluid volume of the two amniotic sacs in a diamniotic twin pregnancy. Causes include twin-twin transfusion syndrome, preterm premature rupture of membranes of one of the amniotic sacs, and oligohydramnios or polyhydramnios in one of the amniotic sacs due to a congenital anomaly in one of the twins.

kjWm0l0.title: Spontaneous fetomaternal hemorrhage
kjWm0l0.description: A bleed that introduces fetal erythrocytes into the maternal circulation without evidence of preceding trauma or abruption. Can be hemodynamically insignificant or massive, which increases the risk for fetal morbidity and mortality. Manifestations are highly variable but include decreased fetal movement, fetal anemia, and hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.

ljWv0l0.title: Dental dam
ljWv0l0.description: A sheet of latex or polyurethane that is used during oral sex as a barrier between the mouth and vagina or anus to protect against sexually transmitted infections.

njW7al0.title: Growth spurt
njW7al0.description: The increase in a child's rate of linear growth that generally peaks at 13–14 years of age (boys) or 11–12 years of age (girls). Lasts ~ 2 years.

LjWwal0.title: HPP
LjWwal0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Hypophosphatasia
2. Hypokalemic periodic paralysis (preferred terms: hypoPP, hypoKPP, or HOKPP)
3. Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis (preferred terms: hyperPP, hyperKPP, or HKPP)

ojW0Yl0.title: Variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
ojW0Yl0.description: A rare variant of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease that is thought to result from bovine-to-human transmission of prions. Manifests with progressive neuropsychiatric symptoms (e.g., personality changes, myoclonus) and has a slightly more protracted course than standard CJD.

rjWfbl0.title: Precipitous labor
rjWfbl0.description: A type of labor that lasts < 3 hours after the commencement of regular contractions. May be caused by low resistance of the birth canal and strong or painless uterine contractions. Risk factors include multiparty, placental abruption, and severe intrauterine growth restriction.

HjWKbl0.title: Symptoms of splenomegaly
HjWKbl0.description: A group of clinical symptoms and findings related to an enlarged spleen. Patients may report left upper quadrant pain, early satiety, and bloating. Clinical findings may include portal hypertension, splenic infarcts, and evidence of splenic sequestration (e.g., cytopenias, refractory anemia).

FjWgXl0.title: Orthophoria
FjWgXl0.description: The alignment of the eyes with balanced binocular fixation of the eyes (i.e., when viewing an object, the lines of vision converge at the object).

8jWOXl0.title: MSIS diagnostic criteria for prosthetic hip and/or knee infections
8jWOXl0.description: A set of criteria used alongside clinical features to establish a diagnosis in a patient with suspected prosthetic joint infection of the hip and/or knee.

ujWpXl0.title: Liquefaction
ujWpXl0.description: The transformation of a solid material into a liquid (e.g., due to cell lysis in liquefactive necrosis).

EjW8Xl0.title: Splenic infarction
EjW8Xl0.description: An ischemic injury to the spleen that results in tissue necrosis. Typically caused by obstruction of the splenic artery (e.g., due to a hypercoagulable state, thromboembolism, or septic embolism). Manifestations include left shoulder and left upper quadrant pain, splenomegaly, nausea, vomiting, and fever. Complications include hemorrhage, atraumatic rupture, abscess, pseudocyst, and aneurysm.

DjW1cl0.title: Multiple comparisons test
DjW1cl0.description: A statistical method used in situations in which several hypotheses are tested simultaneously with one data set (e.g., the data of a trial is tested for different outcomes). Adjusts the results for multiple comparisons to mitigate the high risk of one or more false positive results.

xjWEcl0.title: Legacy effect
xjWEcl0.description: A phenomenon in which an intervention carried out early in the course of a chronic disease has benefits even after cessation of the intervention. For example, lipid-lowering therapy results in decreased cardiac events even decades after therapy is stopped.

-jWD1l0.title: Cross-sectional imaging
-jWD1l0.description: An umbrella term for imaging modalities that allow for visualization of cross-sectional slices of the body. This term can be used broadly to refer to CT, MRI, PET, or SPECT.

ZPWZWl0.title: Thrombohemorrhagic event
ZPWZWl0.description: A clotting and/or bleeding complication such as stroke, vascular thrombosis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, or life-threatening bleeding. May occur in patients with solid tumors and hematologic neoplasms due to a combination of multiple factors (e.g., coagulation abnormalities, inflammatory cytokines, side effects of chemotherapy, surgical procedures, infections).

YPWnWl0.title: Parenteral nutrition-associated cholestasis
YPWnWl0.description: A hepatic complication of prolonged parental nutrition (> 2 weeks) leading to intrahepatic cholestasis. Usually seen in neonates, esp. preterm infants. Clinical features include elevated serum direct bilirubin (≥ 2.0 mg/dL) and mildly elevated AST, ALT, and GGTP.

destinations.label: Specialized nutrition support → Intestinal failure-associated liver disease

bPWHWl0.title: Intestinal failure-associated liver disease
bPWHWl0.description: A liver disease caused by medical and surgical management strategies used for intestinal failure (e.g., chronic parental nutrition).

destinations.label: Specialized nutrition support → Intestinal failure-associated liver disease

VPWGdl0.title: Acute uterine inversion
VPWGdl0.description: The collapse of the uterine fundus into the endometrial cavity, occurring immediately after or within 24 hours of delivery.

ePWxdl0.title: Chronic uterine inversion
ePWxdl0.description: A collapse of the uterine fundus into the endometrial cavity that gas gone unnoticed or uncorrected, usually seen weeks or months after delivery.

UPWbVl0.title: Driver diagram
UPWbVl0.description: A visual chart of ≥ 3 levels that displays a team's aim and its contributors (i.e., drivers). The first level is reserved for the aim that is connected to the direct contributors (i.e., primary drivers) to achieving the aim. Primary drivers are connected to the secondary drivers or specific change ideas. This chart allows a team to systematically discuss all the aspects of a project and organize potential changes.

fPWkVl0.title: Pelvic floor dysfunction
fPWkVl0.description: Laxity or tension of the pelvic floor muscles and/or connective tissue. Causes include muscle or nerve damage (e.g., from surgery or trauma), increased intra-abdominal pressure, and genetic conditions. Can manifest with urinary or bowel symptoms (e.g., urinary incontinence, constipation), pelvic organ prolapse, sexual dysfunction, a feeling of pressure (e.g., pelvic, rectal), and/or pelvic pain.

TPW6Vl0.title: Short cervical length
TPW6Vl0.description: A cervical length of < 25 mm that is measured via transvaginal ultrasound either at or before 24 weeks' gestation.

destinations.label: Maternal complications during pregnancy → Cervical insufficiency

SPWyVl0.title: Hereditary thrombocytosis
SPWyVl0.description: A rare inherited disorder caused by mutations in the thrombopoietin gene or thrombopoietin receptor gene. Affected individuals typically have elevated platelets but are otherwise asymptomatic; occasionally, thrombotic or hemorrhagic events occur.

PPWWUl0.title: Secondary bloodstream infection
PPWWUl0.description: A laboratory-confirmed bloodstream infection that is secondary to an infection at another site. Confirmed by identifying the same pathogen(s) on cultures from blood and the suspected primary source of infection.

4PW3Ul0.title: Puerperal sepsis
4PW3Ul0.description: Maternal sepsis that develops between birth and 6 weeks postpartum. Common infection source sites include the genital tract (e.g., endometritis), urinary tract (e.g., acute pyelonephritis), and skin and soft tissue (e.g., surgical site infection).

kPWmUl0.title: Shift rule
kPWmUl0.description: The first rule used to interpret the data on a run chart. A shift represents ≥ 6 sequential points either all above or below the median (e.g., ≥ 6 consecutive months with admission rates higher than the median).

lPWvUl0.title: Trend rule
lPWvUl0.description: The second rule used to interpret the data on a run chart. A trend represents ≥ 5 rising or falling sequential points in which repeating values are ignored (e.g., ≥ 5 sequential months of falling admission rates with each month's rate lower than the previous).

mPWV2l0.title: Astronomical point
mPWV2l0.description: A point on a run chart that is unusually high or low. Although every data set has a highest and lowest point, these are only considered astronomical points when there is an obvious discrepancy with the surrounding values.

MPWM2l0.title: Renal infarction
MPWM2l0.description: The acute loss of blood supply to the renal parenchyma, which results in necrosis and loss of kidney function.

nPW72l0.title: Continuous-monitoring blood culture system
nPW72l0.description: A blood culture incubator. Blood culture bottles are placed in the incubator and their CO2 content is monitored. A significant and/or sustained rise in CO2 indicates a positive blood culture.

LPWw2l0.title: Addition rule
LPWw2l0.description: A statistical rule that states that a probability of either of two events is equal to the sum of probabilities of each event minus the probability of them occurring simultaneously.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

rPWfTl0.title: Inducible bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue
rPWfTl0.description: A type of lymphoid tissue found within the lungs, usually along bronchi or perivascular spaces. Responsible for generating an adaptive immune response to antigens encountered in the upper and lower respiratory tracts following inflammation or infection. It is thought to be associated with COPD, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, asthma, and rheumatoid lung disease.

sPWtTl0.title: Uranium mining
