sPWtTl0.description: The extraction of uranium ore from a source in the ground using different mining techniques (e.g., open-pit mining, underground mining). Natural radioactive decay of uranium ore emits radon gas, which causes lung cancer.

GPWBTl0.title: Oxygen saturation on pulse oximetry
GPWBTl0.description: The percentage of oxygen-saturated hemoglobin as measured by a pulse oximetry device, which measures the differences in light absorption properties of oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin. Often used as a surrogate for the true percentage of oxygen-saturated hemoglobin as measured during arterial blood gas analysis (SaO₂) but may not correspond to SaO₂ in patients with abnormal hemoglobin forms (e.g., carboxyhemoglobin, methemoglobin, sulfhemoglobin) or poor peripheral circulation (e.g., in shock, hypothermia).

tPWXgl0.title: Angiostrongylus cantonensis
tPWXgl0.description: A parasitic roundworm predominantly found in Southeast Asia and the tropical Pacific islands. Transmitted between rats and mollusks (e.g., snails, slugs). Ingestion of contaminated foods can cause eosinophilic meningitis.

FPWggl0.title: Baylisascaris procyonis
FPWggl0.description: A roundworm found in the majority of raccoons in North America. Transmitted through the fecal-oral route via the ingestion of eggs in soil or larvae in infected tissue. Migration of larvae through the tissue of the host (e.g., lungs, brain, heart) causes a variety of syndromes, including severe neurologic disease (eosinophilic meningoencephalitis).

uPWpgl0.title: Familial lipoprotein lipase deficiency
uPWpgl0.description: An autosomal recessive disease caused by a deficiency of lipoprotein lipase. Manifestations include abdominal pain (which may or may not be caused by chronic pancreatitis), hepatosplenomegaly, and cutaneous xanthomas. Not associated with atherosclerosis.

destinations.label: Rare inherited syndromes → Familial lipoprotein lipase deficiency

EPW8gl0.title: Alipogene tiparvovec
EPW8gl0.description: A gene therapy medication that was used to treat lipoprotein lipase (LPL) deficiency. Intramuscular injection of a viral vector transports a gain-of-function variant of the LPL gene into muscle cells, which leads to synthesis of active LPL and subsequent transient reduction of triglyceride plasma levels. Was never approved in the US and marketing authorization was not renewed after expiration in Europe due to high costs and low demand.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Gene therapy

vPWAgl0.title: Psychogenic pseudosyncope
vPWAgl0.description: A syncope mimic that is not associated with a decrease in cerebral perfusion or true loss of consciousness. Caused by psychological factors (e.g., conversion disorder).

wPWhSl0.title: Perniosis
wPWhSl0.description: A condition characterized by the inflammation of small blood vessels triggered by an abnormal reaction to cold and humid conditions. Manifests with bluish-red skin discoloration on fingers, toes, legs, and in the face. May be accompanied by pain, itching, burning, swelling, and, in severe cases, bullae.

destinations.label: Hypothermia and frostbite → Nonfreezing cold injuries

BPWzSl0.title: Uncomplicated CRBSI
BPWzSl0.description: Clinical resolution of symptoms and negative blood cultures within 72 hours of appropriate antibiotic therapy in a patient without any of the features of complicated CRBSI.

yPWdhl0.title: Complicated CRBSI
yPWdhl0.description: Persistent fever and/or positive blood cultures despite 72 hours of appropriate treatment, development of complications (e.g., infective endocarditis, suppurative thrombophlebitis), or presence of risk factors for severe disease, such as active malignancy, immunosuppression, or an intravascular device.

APWRhl0.title: Photosensitive melanopsin-containing retinal ganglion cell
APWRhl0.description: A cell found in the retinal ganglion that projects via the retinohypothalamic tract to the suprachiasmatic nucleus of the hypothalamus. Involved in regulation of circadian rhythm and the pupillary light reflex.

-PWDhl0.title: Intravascular catheter-related bloodstream infections
-PWDhl0.description: A nosocomial primary bloodstream infection that is diagnosed based on it occurring > 48 hours after placement of an intravascular line and within 48 hours of removal PLUS confirmation that the catheter is the source of the infection (e.g., positive quantitative blood cultures from the catheter lumen and peripheral venipuncture, no other source of infection, resolution of symptoms on catheter removal).

Z4WZ3l0.title: PE
Z4WZ3l0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Pulmonary embolism
2. Physical examination
3. Pulmonary edema

a4WQ3l0.title: Clinical features of pneumonia
a4WQ3l0.description: Features include malaise, fever, productive cough, dyspnea, tachypnea, and pleuritic chest pain. Atypical pneumonia may also manifest with extrapulmonary features (e.g., headache, sore throat).

b4WH3l0.title: Multiple comparisons problem
b4WH3l0.description: A phenomenon in statistics in which the rate of type 1 error increases when multiple comparisons are performed. The error rate can be adjusted for the number of comparisons using various methods (e.g., Bonferroni correction, pairwise comparisons).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

X4W93l0.title: Bonferroni correction
X4W93l0.description: A method for controlling for the type 1 error (i.e., spurious positive results) in multiple comparisons (e.g., in ANOVA), in which the α-value is divided by the number of tests performed.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

e4WxRl0.title: Adrenal incidentaloma
e4WxRl0.description: An adrenal mass that is detected on imaging performed for reasons other than evaluation for a suspected adrenal condition. Adrenal incidentalomas are clinically unapparent.

T4W6il0.title: Underimmunization
T4W6il0.description: A suboptimal level of immunization. Applies to individuals who have either not received or received an incomplete series of recommended vaccines for which they are eligible. Can also apply to communities with a high proportion of underimmunized individuals.

g4WFil0.title: Self-limited
g4WFil0.description: A term used to describe a medical problem (e.g., infection, illness, symptom) that resolves regardless of treatment or intervention.

S4Wyil0.title: Cl−/HCO3− exchanger
S4Wyil0.description: A family of plasma membrane proteins that exchange chloride ions and bicarbonate ions. Includes band 3, pendrin, and the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR).

h4WcQl0.title: Pendred syndrome
h4WcQl0.description: An autosomal recessive condition caused by mutations that result in reduced activity of the pendrin exchanger. Manifestations include sensorineural hearing loss, hypothyroidism with goiter, and hypovolemia and metabolic alkalosis in response to thiazide diuretics.

34WSQl0.title: Anti-GM1 antibody
34WSQl0.description: An autoantibody directed against the ganglioside GM1. May be detected in patients with Guillain–Barré syndrome and multifocal motor neuropathy.

R4WlQl0.title: Pelvic cellulitis
R4WlQl0.description: An acute or chronic inflammation of the parametrium that is considered to be a form of pelvic inflammatory disease.

destinations.label: Pelvic inflammatory disease → Subtypes and variants

i4WJQl0.title: McDonald cerclage
i4WJQl0.description: A surgical procedure performed to prevent preterm birth in women with cervical insufficiency that involves placing a suture in the cervix, typically using a transvaginal approach, to reinforce cervical closure. Usually removed between 36 and 37 weeks' gestation or at the onset of preterm labor.

destinations.label: Maternal complications during pregnancy → Cervical insufficiency

Q4WuQl0.title: Shirodkar cerclage
Q4WuQl0.description: A surgical procedure during which a suture is placed in the cervical submucosal tissue to treat cervical insufficiency. Usually removed between 36 and 37 weeks' gestation or at the onset of preterm labor. Can be left in place if cesarean delivery is planned.

destinations.label: Maternal complications during pregnancy → Cervical insufficiency

j4W_Ql0.title: Functional asplenia
j4W_Ql0.description: A condition in which phagocytic activity of the spleen is lost while splenic tissue is preserved. Can develop as a complication of sickle cell disease as a result of repeated infarction secondary to vasoocclusion from sickle cell buildup.

k4Wmjl0.title: Population (genetics)
k4Wmjl0.description: A group of individuals or organisms that interbreed and live at the same territory at the same time.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Population genetics

O4WIjl0.title: Gene pool
O4WIjl0.description: A total of genes present in a population.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Population genetics

l4Wvjl0.title: Genetic variation
l4Wvjl0.description: A difference in genomes between organisms of the same species.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Population genetics

N4W-jl0.title: PAS
N4W-jl0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Periodic acid-Schiff
2. Pediatric appendicitis score

m4WVPl0.title: Chest tube
m4WVPl0.description: A clear tube that can be inserted into the pleural space to evacuate fluid (e.g., due to pleural effusion, hemothorax, empyema) or air (pneumothorax).

54WiPl0.title: Apolipoprotein C-II deficiency
54WiPl0.description: An autosomal recessive disease caused by a deficiency of lipoprotein lipase. Typically results in abdominal pain due to recurrent pancreatitis. Hepatosplenomegaly and cutaneous xanthomas may be seen. Not associated with atherosclerosis.

M4WMPl0.title: Retinal dysplasia
M4WMPl0.description: The abnormal development of retinal tissue, which can be caused by genetic syndromes (e.g., trisomy 13, trisomy 18) or intrauterine infection (e.g., cytomegalovirus infection, toxoplasmosis). Characterized by rosettes of dysplastic retinal cells on histopathologic examination.

n4W7Pl0.title: Retinal astrocytic hamartoma
n4W7Pl0.description: A slow-growing, whitish tumor that can form near the optic nerve and cause leukocoria. Associated with tuberous sclerosis complex and neurofibromatosis type 1. Can appear similar to an early retinoblastoma.

L4WwPl0.title: Myelinated retinal nerve fiber
L4WwPl0.description: A common and benign ophthalmologic finding characterized by white, striated patches on the surface of the retina that typically have frayed or feathered borders. Can result in an enlarged blind spot, scotomas, myopia, and/or ambylopia.

J4Ws4l0.title: Methotrexate-related leukoencephalopathy
J4Ws4l0.description: A type of toxic encephalopathy associated with the high-dose intravenous or intrathecal administration of methotrexate. Symptoms include headache, seizures, confusion, and neurologic deficits. The acute form manifests shortly after initiation of treatment and is usually transient. The chronic form has a slower onset, and neurologic symptoms are often permanent.

74W4kl0.title: Splenic abscess
74W4kl0.description: An enclosed collection of pus within the spleen that is usually caused by hematogenous spread of bacteria (e.g., Streptococci, Staphylococci) from a septic source (e.g., endocarditis). Risk factors include intravenous drug use, immunosuppression, infectious conditions, and trauma to the spleen.

H4WKkl0.title: Carpal tunnel syndrome in pregnancy
H4WKkl0.description: The most common peripheral neuropathy diagnosed during pregnancy and caused by compression of the median nerve by the transverse carpal ligament. Etiologies include ​hormone-mediated weight gain and edema of the wrist.

destinations.label: Carpal tunnel syndrome → Special patient groups

s4Wtkl0.title: Drug-induced myopathy
s4Wtkl0.description: An adverse reaction to medical or recreational drugs (e.g., corticosteroids, statins, cocaine) that manifests with muscle weakness, myalgia, creatine kinase elevation, and/or myoglobinuria in the absense of any muscle disease.

G4WBkl0.title: Zidovudine-induced myopathy
G4WBkl0.description: An adverse effect of zidovudine therapy characterized mialgia and weakness that improves after discontinuing drug therapy.

t4WXOl0.title: Cocaine-induced myopathy
t4WXOl0.description: An adverse effect of cocaine use characterized by proximal muscle weakness, predominantly of the lower extremities and other symptoms such as delirium, chest pain, fever, hypotension.

F4WgOl0.title: Anti-soluble liver antigen antibodies
F4WgOl0.description: An autoantibody that is diagnostic of type 1 autoimmune hepatitis and is prognostic for severe disease.

84WOOl0.title: Reactive airway disease
84WOOl0.description: An unspecific label used to describe patients with a syndrome that is characterized by symptoms similar to asthma (e.g., wheezing, coughing, sputum production). Most commonly used in pediatrics. Not to be confused with reactive airways dysfunction syndrome (RADS).

E4W8Ol0.title: Hormone-sensitive prostate cancer
E4W8Ol0.description: The clinical scenario in which a patient with advanced prostate cancer has either never received treatment with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) or continues to exhibit sensitivity to ADT.

w4Whll0.title: Ampullary cancer
w4Whll0.description: A rare type of gastrointestinal cancer that forms in the ampulla of Vater. Manifestations include jaundice (most common), abdominal and/or back pain, gastrointestinal upset, and nonspecific symptoms of malignancy (e.g., fatigue, weight loss). Most ampullary cancers are adenocarcinomas; neuroendocrine and mixed subtypes have also been reported.

94WNll0.title: Adenocarcinoma of the ampulla of Vater
94WNll0.description: The most common type of ampullary cancer. Either originates from intestinal epithelium that covers the ampulla (intestinal type), from epithelium of the distal bile and pancreatic duct (pancreatobiliary type), or contains both types. Pancreatobiliary adenocarcinomas are associated with worse prognosis.

C4Wqll0.title: Atherectomy
C4Wqll0.description: A percutaneous revascularization procedure that excises atherosclerotic plaque from the arterial wall in an attempt to improve blood flow. Unlike balloon angioplasty, this technique removes arterial plaque rather than compressing it into the arterial wall.

y4WdNl0.title: Retinal emboli
y4WdNl0.description: Emboli that occlude the retinal artery or its branches. Typically caused by carotid atherosclerosis or valvular heart disease. On fundoscopy, cholesterol emboli (Hollenhorst plaques) are bright yellow and refractile, platelet-fibrin emboli are dull gray, and calcific emboli are large, white intravascular bodies. Often asymptomatic but can cause amaurosis fugax or retinal artery occlusion leading to partial or complete loss of vision.

destinations.label: Diseases of the retina → Other retinal disorders

A4WRNl0.title: Postinfectious irritable bowel syndrome
A4WRNl0.description: A functional bowel disorder that presents with nonspecific symptoms (e.g., diffuse pain, bloating, diarrhea, constipation) after a gastrointestinal infection. Occurs in the absence of a specific organic pathology and is more common after a bacterial infection than a viral or parasitic infection. Presumed pathophysiological mechanisms include persistent low-level intestinal inflammation, trapping of air, and altered motility.

z4WrNl0.title: Corneal ulcer
z4WrNl0.description: A corneal epithelial defect involving the underlying stroma, typically a complication of keratitis. Etiology includes infection (most commonly bacterial, but may also be viral, fungal, or parasitic) and autoimmune diseases. Corneal ulcer is considered an ophthalmological emergency.

-4WDNl0.title: Hypertrichosis lanuginosa acquisita
-4WDNl0.description: A paraneoplastic phenomenon characterized by development of fine hair (lanugo hair), most commonly around the head and neck. Associated with cancers of the colon, breast, lung, and kidney.

ZkWZml0.title: Severe gastroenteritis
ZkWZml0.description: A classification of gastroenteritis that typically includes bloody stools, severe diarrhea or vomiting, significant abdominal pain, prolonged symptoms (> 1 week), high fever, signs of dehydration, features of sepsis, and/or end-organ damage.

0kWeml0.title: Intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy
0kWeml0.description: An intravitreal, antiangiogenic therapy used to inhibit vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) to treat various ocular diseases (e.g., wet age-related macular degeneration, macular edema, diabetic retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion). Agents used include bevacizumab, ranibizumab, and aflibercept.

YkWnml0.title: Motility-related dysphagia
YkWnml0.description: Dysphagia caused by a neurological or muscular disorder. Characterized by dysphagia predominantly with liquids or liquids and solid food. Examples include esophageal motility disorders, progressive muscular dystrophy, and stroke.

bkWHml0.title: Structural dysphagia
bkWHml0.description: Dysphagia due to a mechanical or anatomical obstruction to the passage of food from the oropharynx to the stomach. Typically manifests as dysphagia predominantly with solid food but can progress to dysphagia with liquids. The obstruction may be intramural (e.g., esophageal stricture, esophageal malignancy), intraluminal (e.g., food bolus impaction), or extrinsic (e.g., thyromegaly or hilar lymphadenopathy).

XkW9ml0.title: Urine cytology
XkW9ml0.description: A pathology study that evaluates the urine for malignant cells. Mainly used for surveillance in patients with known urothelial carcinoma, but can be used to help diagnose patients with a high pretest probability of urinary tract cancer (e.g., those with gross hematuria).

ckWa5l0.title: Vasoplegia
ckWa5l0.description: A state of systemic vasodilation and decreased systemic vascular resistance due to impaired vascular reactivity, which can result in life-threatening hypotension.

1kW25l0.title: Stab wound
1kW25l0.description: An injury sustained from penetration of tissue by a sharp object, which can result in hemodynamic instability due to hemorrhage. If a foreign body (e.g., a knife) is in place in the wound, it may be tamponading hemorrhage and should only be removed in a controlled setting where the patient can receive immediate surgical intervention.

WkWP5l0.title: Dog bite
WkWP5l0.description: A bite injury from a dog, which can result in minor or major injury and carries a risk of infectious complication (e.g., abscess, bacteremia, necrotizing soft tissue infection). Notable pathogens include Streptococcus, Staphylococcus, Pasteurella, Haemophilus, and Capnocytophaga.

dkWo5l0.title: Cat bites
dkWo5l0.description: A bite injury from a cat, which generally carries a higher risk of infection and complication (e.g., bacteremia, necrotizing soft tissue infection) compared to other bite wounds because of deep penetrating injury.

VkWG5l0.title: Bowel and bladder dysfunction
VkWG5l0.description: The cooccurence of lower urinary tract symptoms (e.g., dysuria, urgency, frequency, enuresis, incontinence, retention) and bowel symptoms (e.g., encopresis, constipation) due to the close relationship of the urinary tract, anus, and rectum.

2kWTMl0.title: Sterile abscess
2kWTMl0.description: A collection of pus within the dermis or subcutaneous tissue that is not caused by infection. Can form as a complication of subcutaneous/intramuscular injection when the injected substance (e.g., glucocorticoids, synthol, oils) is not absorbed and causes persistent irritation or as a result of ongoing inflammation in a previously septic abscess after the causative pathogen has been cleared.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Acute local inflammation

fkWkMl0.title: Septic abscess
fkWkMl0.description: A collection of pus within the dermis or subcutaneous tissue that results from infection.

destinations.label: Local inflammatory responses → Acute local inflammation

TkW6Ml0.title: Serum free light chain assay
TkW6Ml0.description: The measurement of serum concentrations of free kappa and lambda immunoglobulin light chains. Used in the evaluation of  plasma cell dyscrasias (e.g., multiple myeloma, monoglonal gammopathy of unknown significance).

SkWyMl0.title: Urine protein electrophoresis
SkWyMl0.description: A test that measures the amount of protein (e.g., albumin, globulins) in urine. Usually, urine is collected over 24 hours to provide insight into compositional changes throughout the day. Electrical current is then used to separate the serum proteins based on their charge, size, and shape. Used to diagnose multiple myeloma, monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance, and other plasma cell dyscrasias.

hkWcnl0.title: Renal laceration
hkWcnl0.description: A tear in kidney tissue. May lead to urinary extravasation and/or bleeding into the abdominal cavity, depending on the depth and location of the tear.

3kWSnl0.title: Ureteral avulsion
3kWSnl0.description: Traumatic shearing of the ureter that results in ureteral discontinuity. Often iatrogenic, e.g., due to the use of instruments too large for the ureter or attempted removal of insufficiently fragmented stones.

RkWlnl0.title: Ureteral laceration
RkWlnl0.description: Injury to the ureter that results in a partial opening, which ranges from pinpoint defects to large openings. Usually treated with ureter stenting.

ikWJnl0.title: Idiopathic hirsutism
ikWJnl0.description: A subtype of hirsutism associated with normal ovulation and menstruation, gonadotropins, and serum testosterone and DHEA-S concentrations. May be caused by dysfunctional peripheral androgen activity.

kkWmLl0.title: Diagnostic criteria for Kawasaki disease
kkWmLl0.description: The clinical diagnosis of Kawasaki disease requires fever lasting ≥ 5 days in combination with ≥ 4 specific symptoms: erythema and edema and/or desquamation of the distal extremities, polymorphous rash (originating on the trunk), painless bilateral conjunctivitis without exudate, oropharyngeal mucositis (strawberry tongue, cracked and red lips), and cervical lymphadenopathy (usually unilateral).

NkW-Ll0.title: Premorbidity
NkW-Ll0.description: An individual's condition or state of function prior to the onset of a disorder or pathology.

mkWVol0.title: Baseline electrocardiogram
mkWVol0.description: An electrocardiogram that is recorded prior to the onset and/or after the termination of a disorder and most commonly used for comparison during an acute illness. Findings on baseline ECG may be normal, variant, or abnormal depending on the patient's demographics and preexisting conditions.

nkW7ol0.title: Cardiac defibrillator
nkW7ol0.description: A device used in emergency settings to cardiovert and/or defibrillate the heart (e.g., to manage tachycardia and/or cardiac arrest). Standard cardioverter defibrillators designed for in-hospital and ambulance use can also function as cardiac monitors. Subtypes of defibrillators include automated external defibrillators (AEDs), designed for public use, and automated implantable cardioverter defibrillators (AICDs), designed for implantation within the chest.

LkWwol0.title: CVA
LkWwol0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Cerebrovascular accident
2. Costovertebral angle
3. Cough-variant asthma
4. Central venous access

KkWUKl0.title: AAV
KkWUKl0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Antibody-associated vasculitis
2. Adaptive assisted ventilation
3. Adenocarcinoma of the ampulla of Vater

6kWjKl0.title: Monoclonal spike
6kWjKl0.description: A finding on serum or urine electrophoresis characterized by a peak in the gamma-globulin zone. Caused by the overproduction of monoclonal immunoglobulins (paraproteins), typically due to plasma cell dyscrasias (e.g., multiple myeloma, Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance).

pkWLKl0.title: Monoclonal protein
pkWLKl0.description: A monoclonal immunoglobulin (paraprotein) that is produced in plasma cell dyscrasias (e.g., multiple myeloma, Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance). Detected on serum or urine electrophoresis as a spike in the gamma-globulin zone (monoclonal spike, M spike).

JkWsKl0.title: DES
JkWsKl0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Diethylstilbestrol
2. Distal or diffuse esophageal spasm
3. Dysfunctional elimination syndrome
4. Dialysis disequilibrium syndrome

qkWCKl0.title: Intravenous drug use
qkWCKl0.description: The intravenous injection of recreational drugs (e.g., heroin), which results in rapid and high drug bioavailability. Complications of substerile injection technique include abscesses, endocarditis, and osteomyelitis.

rkWf6l0.title: Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 2
rkWf6l0.description: An inherited syndrome with manifestations that include adrenal insufficiency, autoimmune thyroiditis, type 1 diabetes mellitus, primary hypogonadism, and hypopituitarism. Unlike autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1, it is not associated with hypoparathyroidism. Multiple modes of inheritance (e.g., autosomal recessive, autosomal dominant) have been reported.

tkWXpl0.title: Transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily V member 1
tkWXpl0.description: A cation channel encoded by a gene on chromosome 17p. Found primarily in nociceptors of the peripheral nervous system. Activated by noxiously high temperature and capsaicin, which lead to a sensation of burning pain. Can be sensitized by certain inflammatory mediators (e.g., bradykinin) and desensitized by prolonged exposure to capsaicin.

8kWOpl0.title: Piezo-type mechanosensitive ion channel component 2
8kWOpl0.description: A cation channel encoded by a gene on chromosome 11p. Found primarily in mechanoreceptors (e.g., Merkel discs, Golgi tendon organs, muscle spindles, bladder wall mechanoreceptors, pulmonary stretch receptors). Activated by mechanical stimuli. Plays a central role in light touch sensation, proprioception, and stretch sensation in visceral organs. Loss of function of this protein is a cause of type 5 distal arthrogryposis.

ukWppl0.title: Food bolus impaction
ukWppl0.description: Acute dysphagia caused by total or near-total obstruction of the esophageal lumen by a food bolus, typically a piece of meat. Requires prompt removal of the obstructing bolus and evaluation for a possible underlying esophageal disorder.

CkWqJl0.title: Congenital hypopituitarism
CkWqJl0.description: A condition caused by mutations in genes that encode transcription factors involved in anterior pituitary development. Can result in deficiencies of multiple pituitary hormones due to abnormalities in somatotrophs, thyrotrophs, lactotrophs, corticotrophs, and/or gonadotrophs.

xkWEJl0.title: Neonatal diabetes mellitus
xkWEJl0.description: A condition characterized by persistent hyperglycemia in the neonatal period. Typically caused by a monogenic defect (most commonly in KCNJ11 or ABCC8, which affects the activity of the pancreatic beta-cell K-ATP channel). There are many causes of hyperglycemia in the neonatal period; neonatal diabetes mellitus is usually suspected when insulin-dependent hyperglycemia persists for > 1 week.

BkWzJl0.title: Neonatal hypocalcemia
BkWzJl0.description: Low serum calcium or ionized calcium in a newborn. Defined as serum calcium < 7 mg/dL or serum ionized calcium < 4 mg/dL in the first 72 hours after birth. Can be caused by several conditions including prematurity, maternal diabetes, fetal growth restriction, and hypoparathyroidism. May be asymptomatic or manifest with jitteriness, muscle jerking, apnea, feeding intolerance, or seizures.

AkWRql0.title: Step down unit
AkWRql0.description: A hospital unit (or several assigned beds within a unit) that provides a higher level of care than a general ward (e.g., close monitoring or intensive supportive therapy) but a lower level of care than an intensive care unit.

destinations.label: Care of the critically ill patient → Definitions

zkWrql0.title: Balance (ability)
zkWrql0.description: The ability to maintain one's center of mass over one's base of support. Involves the vestibular system, the visual system, proprioception, the musculoskeletal system, and the central nervous system.

UOWb7l0.title: Sickle cell test
UOWb7l0.description: A test in which the presence of sickled cells is assessed on a blood smear under anaerobic conditions or by reduction with sodium hydrosulfite (sickle solubility test). This test only detects if sickling hemoglobin is present and does not reliably distinguish between between sickle cell trait, sickle cell anemia, and compound sickle cell disease with other variant hemoglobins.

2OWT7l0.title: Central cyanosis
2OWT7l0.description: A bluish discoloration of the skin of the trunk and mucous membranes. Almost always caused by severe hypoxemia and occurs when desaturated hemoglobin concentration is above 3–5 g/dL, which typically occurs at blood oxygen saturation below 80–85% in patients with normal hemoglobin concentration. Rare causes include methemoglobinemia and sulfhemoglobinemia.

ROWlHl0.title: Hospital-acquired conditions
ROWlHl0.description: A condition that a patient develops while hospitalized (i.e., that was not present on admission), and which often represents a preventable adverse event. Examples include hospital-acquired infections, adverse drug events, pressure ulcers, venous thromboembolisms, falls, and obstetric adverse events.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of hospital-acquired conditions

iOWJHl0.title: Lund-Browder chart
iOWJHl0.description: A set of charts that take into account the different proportions of children and adults (children have proportionally up to 20% larger heads and up to 13% smaller legs) to more precisely estimate the burn surface area involved.

QOWuHl0.title: Complement receptors
QOWuHl0.description: A type of membrane-bound receptor responsible for binding effector protein fragments produced in response to antigen-antibody complexes or damage-associated molecules.

jOW_Hl0.title: Follicular dendritic cells
jOW_Hl0.description: A specialized type of antigen-presenting dendritic cell that are found in lymphoid follicles. Their main function is to present native antigens to potential memory cells.

POWWsl0.title: High-order explosives
POWWsl0.description: A group of chemicals with a high rate of reaction. Detonation produces a large volume of initial pressure and a supersonic overpressurization shock wave. Exposure to an explosion of high-order explosives causes blast injuries. Examples include nitroglycerin, Semtex, C-4, and TNT.

OOWIsl0.title: Blast lung injury
OOWIsl0.description: Pulmonary barotrauma caused by the overpressure wave (blast wave) created by an explosion. May involve parenchymal hemorrhage, pulmonary edema, pneumothorax, arterial air embolism, and/or delayed inflammatory changes.

5OWiGl0.title: Blast-induced ocular trauma
5OWiGl0.description: Primary blast injury of the eye. May involve rupture of the globe, retinitis, and/or orbital fractures caused solely by forces transmitted from the overpressure wave (blast wave) of an explosion.

MOWMGl0.title: Blast-induced abdominal injury
MOWMGl0.description: Intraabdominal injury caused by the overpressure wave (blast wave) created by an explosion. Injuries may include gastrointestinal perforation, gastrointestinal bleeding, and/or intraabdominal hemorrhage due to solid organ damage.

nOW7Gl0.title: KCNE2/KCNQ1 channel
nOW7Gl0.description: A heteromer of the KCNQ1 channel (potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily KQT member 1) and ancillary protein KCNE2 (potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily E member 2). Unlike the KCNQ1 monomer, which is a voltage-gated K⁺ channel, the KCNQ1/KCNE2 heteromer is not voltage-gated and is a constitutionally open K⁺ channel. Found on the luminal surface of parietal cells of the stomach, where they serve to replenish the gastric lumen's potassium concentration, which is decreased as a result of transport of K⁺ into the parietal cell by the H⁺/K⁺ ATPase antiporter.

LOWwGl0.title: Patient-prosthesis mismatch
LOWwGl0.description: A phenomenon caused by the implantation of a prosthetic valve with a functional area that is too small for the cardiac demands of the patient. Leads to left ventricle hypertrophy and is associated with increased mortality.

HOWKFl0.title: Pre-XDR tuberculosis
HOWKFl0.description: A subset of multidrug-resistant TB isolates with additional resistance to either fluoroquinolones or second-line IV agents (e.g., amikacin, kanamycin, capreomycin) but not both.

sOWtFl0.title: Clinical features of acute liver failure
sOWtFl0.description: Features include jaundice, altered mental status, abdominal pain, abdominal distention (ascites), nausea/vomiting, hepatosplenomegaly, fatigue, and fever.

tOWX8l0.title: Direct cholangioscopy
tOWX8l0.description: A diagnostic and therapeutic procedure that uses a very slim endoscope to visualize the biliary tree. It is inserted through the mouth, advanced to the duodenum, and guided into the bile duct for observation of the biliary mucosa and lumen.

FOWg8l0.title: Viral hepatitis panel
FOWg8l0.description: Commonly includes hepatitis A IgM, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis B core IgM, and hepatitis C antibody with reflex to hepatitis C RNA testing.

DOW1ul0.title: Cardiac implantable electronic device
DOW1ul0.description: An umbrella term for all implanted devices that deliver electrical impulses to the heart. Cardiac implantable electronic devices include pacemakers, cardioverter defibrillators, and cardiac resynchronization therapy devices.

wOWhul0.title: Inactivated complement factor 3b
wOWhul0.description: A fragment part of the complement system formed by the first cleavage of C3b. Acts as an opsonin.

COWqul0.title: Neutropenic FUO
COWqul0.description: A temperature > 38.3°C recorded on multiple occasions in a patient with neutrophil count of < 500/mm3 with no clear etiology despite appropriate diagnostics (including least 2 days of culture incubation).

xOWEul0.title: HIV-associated FUO
xOWEul0.description: A temperature of > 38.3°C recorded on multiple occasions in a patient with HIV that lasts for > 4 weeks (or > 3 days if hospitalized), with no clear etiology despite appropriate diagnostics (including at least 2 days of culture incubation).

BOWzul0.title: Nosocomial FUO
BOWzul0.description: A temperature of > 38.3°C recorded on multiple occasions that lasts for > 3 days in a hospitalized patient who was afebrile on admission, with no clear etiology despite appropriate diagnostics (including  at least 2 days of culture intubation).

yOWdEl0.title: Mini-Cog
yOWdEl0.description: A simple and highly sensitive screening tool used to assess for early dementia in older adults. The test includes two components, clock drawing and three-item recall, and takes two to four minutes to administer.

AOWREl0.title: Melanonychia
AOWREl0.description: A brown or black discoloration of the nail plate that most commonly occurs due to melanocyte activation (e.g., due to trauma, infection, inflammation) or melanocyte proliferation (which can be benign or malignant). Subtypes include longitudinal melanonychia, diffuse melanonychia, and transverse melanonychia.

_OW5El0.title: Therapeutic paracentesis
_OW5El0.description: The removal of a large volume of fluid from the peritoneum to relieve symptoms caused by ascites.

alWQvl0.title: Autoinflammatory disorders
alWQvl0.description: A group of disorders caused by dysregulation of the innate immune system. Manifestations include episodic fever, unexplained serositis, uveitis, rash, and/or lymphadenopathy in the absence of autoreactive T-cells or elevated autoantibody titers. Disorders may be hereditary (e.g., periodic fever syndromes) or acquired (e.g., Crohn disease, adult-onset Still disease).

clWaDl0.title: Arterial air embolism
clWaDl0.description: The presence of gas bubbles in the arterial circulation. Most commonly seen as a manifestation of decompression illness or as an iatrogenic injury. Embolization can occur in any organ, but mortality is highest with coronary or cerebral vasculature involvement.

elWxDl0.title: Facial synkinesis
elWxDl0.description: The involuntary movement of facial muscles that occurs with voluntary movement of another facial muscle group (e.g., facial spasms while closing the eyes).

UlWbwl0.title: Laceration
UlWbwl0.description: A deep cut or tear in the skin and/or underlying tissue, typically caused by blunt or shearing forces. Lacerations are often characterized by irregular and jagged edges.

flWkwl0.title: Tension neck syndrome
flWkwl0.description: A syndrome characterized by pain, soreness and/or discomfort in the neck and shoulder muscles. Caused by suboptimal posture and prolonged periods of static positioning, most commonly in the workplace. Risk factors include unergonomic equipment and accommodations, sedentary work with lack of motion, and weak musculature.

TlW6wl0.title: Vibration syndrome
TlW6wl0.description: A condition associated with prolonged exposure to hand-transmitted vibration (e.g., occupational use of vibrating power tools). Manifestations include neurological symptoms (e.g., paresthesia, tingling, sensory loss), decreased grip strength due to hand muscle necrosis, and peripheral vasospasm. Complications include osteoporosis and joint damage.

glWFwl0.title: Clay-shoveler fracture
glWFwl0.description: An avulsion fracture of a spinous process of the lower cervical or upper thoracic vertebrae (most commonly C6/C7). First described among clay shovelers who sustained this injury when lifting their shovels; clay would stick to the shovel and result in sudden forces on the neck and back. Can also be caused by direct trauma to the spinous process (e.g., in a motor vehicle crash).

destinations.label: Cervical spine injuries → Lower cervical spine injuries

3lWS9l0.title: Free PSA:total PSA ratio
3lWS9l0.description: The percentage of free prostate specific antigen (PSA) compared to total PSA. Used to assess the risk of prostate cancer in patients with moderately elevated total PSA levels (i.e., 4.0–10.0 ng/mL). As free PSA levels are low in prostate cancer, a low free PSA:total PSA ratio (< 10–20%) suggests a higher probability of prostate cancer.

RlWl9l0.title: Prostate specific antigen density
RlWl9l0.description: A prostate specific antigen (PSA) parameter calculated by dividing total PSA levels by prostate volume. Can be used to determine the benefit of performing a prostate biopsy in individuals with moderately elevated total PSA levels. A low PSA density (< 0.8 ng/mL/cc) suggests that clinically significant cancer is unlikely and a biopsy can be avoided.

QlWu9l0.title: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve
QlWu9l0.description: A metric used to evaluate the ability of a screening or diagnostic test to correctly predict the probability of a binary outcome (e.g., disease vs. no disease). A receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve with an area under the curve (AUC) close to 1.0 indicates that the test has high combined sensitivity and specificity, while a ROC with an AUC closer to 0.5 indicates that the test has poor discriminative ability.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

4lW3Cl0.title: Urine:serum electrolyte ratio
4lW3Cl0.description: A ratio used to evaluate the effect of urine composition on the level of serum sodium in hyponatremia; urine:serum electrolyte ratio = (urine sodium + urine potassium)/(serum sodium). A result of ≤ 0.5 indicates electrolyte-free urine (i.e., urine composition is contributing to increasing serum sodium), a result of ~ 1 indicates that urine composition is having no effect on serum sodium, and a result of > 1 indicates electrolyte-rich urine (i.e., urine composition is contributing to lowering serum sodium). Values between 0.6 and 1 are inconclusive.

OlWICl0.title: Hypobaric hypoxia
OlWICl0.description: A type of hypoxia caused by inspiration of a low partial pressure of oxygen. Typically occurs at high altitudes.

NlW-Cl0.title: Pancreaticobiliary reflux
NlW-Cl0.description: The reflux of pancreatic juice into the biliary tract (e.g., due to defects of the pancreaticobiliary junction or acquired insufficiency of the sphincter of Oddi).

mlWVxl0.title: Nonepileptic seizure
mlWVxl0.description: A seizure or seizure-like activity that occurs in the absence of abnormal brain wave activity (e.g., on EEG). May be physiological (secondary to arrhythmia or syncope) or psychological (known as psychogenic nonepileptic seizures).

nlW7xl0.title: Nociceptors
nlW7xl0.description: A heterogeneous group of receptors located in free nerve endings of the skin and, in lesser numbers, the muscles, joints, and viscera. Responsible for pain sensation.

LlWwxl0.title: Thermoception
LlWwxl0.description: The sense of temperature differences inferred from heat flux.

JlWsBl0.title: CACNA1S gene
JlWsBl0.description: A gene on chromosome 1q that encodes the alpha 1S subunit of a sarcolemmal, dihydropyridine-sensitive, L-type, voltage-gated calcium channel. Autosomal dominant mutations of this gene are responsible for type 1 hypokalemic periodic paralysis and susceptibility to certain types of malignant hyperthermia and thyrotoxic periodic paralysis.

qlWCBl0.title: SCN4A gene
qlWCBl0.description: A gene on chromosome 17q that encodes the alpha subunit of a sarcolemmal, type IV, voltage-gated sodium channel. Diseases caused by autosomal dominant mutations of this gene include hyperkalemic periodic paralysis, type 2 hypokalemic periodic paralysis, and potassium-aggravated myotonia. An autosomal recessive mutation of this gene is responsible for a rare type of congenital myasthenic syndrome.

7lW4yl0.title: Androgen synthesis inhibitors
7lW4yl0.description: A group of drugs that inhibit androgen synthesis. Used in the management of androgen-dependent conditions (e.g., benign prostatic hypertrophy, prostate cancer, precocious puberty). Examples include abiraterone and enzalutamide.

FlWgAl0.title: Draining sinus
FlWgAl0.description: A newly formed channel that results from bacterial infection (e.g., with nontuberculous mycobacteria). Leads from the focus of an infection (e.g., dental infection) to the skin surface. Usually drains purulent discharge.

ulWpAl0.title: Intercondylar notch of the femur
ulWpAl0.description: A recession between the medial and lateral epicondyles of the femur. The anterior cruciate ligament attaches to the roof and wall of the notch.

ElW8Al0.title: Hereditary unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia
ElW8Al0.description: A collection of genetic conditions (e.g., Gilbert syndrome, Crigler-Najjar syndrome) that arise from mutations in the UGT1A1 gene and result in elevated levels of unconjugated bilirubin.

DlW1_l0.title: Mannose-binding lectin
DlW1_l0.description: A serum protein that is involved in the activation of the complement system. Genetically influenced variations of serum concentrations of this protein, together with other environmental and genetic factors, may play a role in increased susceptibility to infections and autoimmune, cardiovascular, and metabolic conditions.

9lWN_l0.title: Aspirin challenge test
9lWN_l0.description: A diagnostic test for aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD) caused by NSAID intolerance. The test is diagnostic of AERD if oral/nasal inhalation or IV administration of aspirin reproduces symptoms.

ClWq_l0.title: Knee dislocation
ClWq_l0.description: A dislocation of the tibia and femur across the knee joint. The tibia can be dislocated anteriorly, posteriorly, medially, laterally, or rotationally. Complications include damage to the popliteal artery and common peroneal nerve.

destinations.label: Knee ligament injuries → Tibiofemoral joint dislocation

ylWdzl0.title: MRI thermal burn injury
ylWdzl0.description: A thermal injury sustained from magnetic resonance imaging. Risk factors include the presence of conductive/metallic objects (e.g., pulse oximeter, ECG leads), clothing with metallic microfibers (e.g., sportswear), tattoos containing metal pigments (e.g., mercury, iron), and contact with the scanner walls.

-lWDzl0.title: Vacuole
-lWDzl0.description: A cell organelle that stores substances such as lipids, proteins, pigments, and minerals (storage vacuoles) or fuses with lysosomes to lyse substances (lytic vacuoles).

YNWn-l0.title: Natural selection
YNWn-l0.description: A process through which individuals having traits that are beneficial for survival are more likely to reproduce and pass these traits to offspring.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Population genetics

bNWH-l0.title: Testosterone flare
bNWH-l0.description: A rapid and transient increase in testosterone seen in patients starting GnRH agonists for prostate cancer. Occurs secondary to a rise in luteinizing hormone. Can cause an acute worsening of symptoms such as bone pain and urinary retention. May be prevented by a short course (< 4 weeks) of first-generation antiandrogens such as flutamide or bicalutamide.

dNWoZN0.title: Gleason grade
dNWoZN0.description: Histological patterns of prostate cancer. Depending on the degree of tumor cell differentiation and extent of stromal invasion, the tumor is graded from Gleason grade 1 (well-differentiated) to Gleason grade 5 (poorly differentiated).

VNWGZN0.title: Intracellular accumulation
VNWGZN0.description: An abnormal increase in intracellular storage of either natural cellular constituents (e.g., lipids, water, proteins) or other substances (e.g., carbon, infectious agents).

destinations.label: Cellular changes and adaptive responses → Cellular inclusions

UNWb0N0.title: Genetic bottleneck
UNWb0N0.description: A decrease in genetic variability caused by a dramatic decrease of a size of a population due to external events (e.g., disasters, diseases, wars). Can lead to increased risk of accumulation of recessive alleles and genetic drift.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Population genetics

2NWT0N0.title: Genitourinary melanoma
2NWT0N0.description: A rare subtype of melanoma that more commonly affects female individuals. Prognosis is generally poor. Comprises ~ 45% of all mucosal melanomas.

fNWk0N0.title: Genetic drift
fNWk0N0.description: A random fluctuation in allele frequency within a population. Has a larger effect in smaller populaitons.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Population genetics

iNWJaN0.title: Metastatic studding
iNWJaN0.description: A descriptor for the formation of tumor nodules along a tissue surface (most commonly on the peritoneum, as in peritoneal carcinomatosis).

PNWWYN0.title: Drug-seeking behavior
PNWWYN0.description: A term used to describe potentially manipulative and/or demanding behaviors aimed at obtaining prescription medication, typically for recreational use but potentially also for illicit sale. For example, individuals may specifically request medication by name, mention having a high physical tolerance, or claim to have lost prescriptions.

4NW3YN0.title: Patient health questionnaire-15
4NW3YN0.description: A questionnaire used to evaluate the severity of somatic symptoms and screen for patients at risk for somatization. Consists of 15 items that are scored on a scale from 0 ("not bothered at all") to 2 ("bothered a lot"). The total score is then used to determine if symptom severity is low, medium, or high.

destinations.label: Somatic symptom and related disorders → Diagnostic approach and general management

lNWvYN0.title: Hypoplasminogenemia
lNWvYN0.description: An inherited condition characterized by abnormally low serum concentrations of plasminogen, which results in the accumulation of fibrin. Manifests with the formation of inflamed, woody growths on mucous membranes (especially the conjunctiva). Less commonly affects the gastrointestinal tract, lungs, and the central nervous system.

mNWVbN0.title: Telemetry
mNWVbN0.description: The recording and transmission of an instrument's measurements. The uses of telemetry in medicine include continuous and/or realtime monitoring of vital signs, heart rhythm, and brain electrical activity.

5NWibN0.title: Deleterious allele
5NWibN0.description: An allele, presence of which decreases the fitness of an individual.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Population genetics

MNWMbN0.title: Heterozygous advantage
MNWMbN0.description: A phenomenon in which heterozygosity in a certain gene leads to increased fitness compared to either dominant or recessive homozygosity.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Population genetics

LNWwbN0.title: Shave biopsy
LNWwbN0.description: A method of skin biopsy. A superficial shave biopsy is an incisional biopsy in which a thin, flat tissue specimen is removed by a scalpel or razor; used for superficial lesions. A deep shave (saucerization) biopsy is an excisional biopsy in which a curved blade is used to fully excise a skin lesion by scooping out tissue to the level of the deep reticular dermis; used for suspicious skin lesions to rule out malignancy.

KNWUXN0.title: Bladder training
KNWUXN0.description: A form of behavioral therapy used in the treatment of urinary incontinence and interstitial cystitis. Scheduled voiding regimens and patient education are used to suppress urinary urgency and, for patients with incontinence, to increase the leak-free interval.

6NWjXN0.title: Micturition
6NWjXN0.description: The action of urinating, which facilitates the excretion of waste products filtered from the kidneys.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Urinary bladder

pNWLXN0.title: Pontine micturition center
pNWLXN0.description: A collection of neuronal cell bodies located in the pons. Responsible for the coordination of micturition via the regulation of parasympathetic innervation of the detrusor muscle and somatic innervation of the external urethral sphincter.

destinations.label: Overview of the urinary tract → Urinary bladder

qNWCXN0.title: Passive fecal incontinence
qNWCXN0.description: The involuntary passage of feces without awareness.

INWYcN0.title: Fecal incontinence
INWYcN0.description: The involuntary passage of solid or liquid feces over a period of ≥ 3 months. Causes include anal disorders (e.g., anal sphincter weakness or injury), rectal disorders (e.g., pelvic floor dysfunction), and neurological disorders (e.g., spinal cord injury). Initial management consists of supportive care, dietary fiber supplementation, and antidiarrheals if necessary.

7NW4cN0.title: Pseudocowpox
7NW4cN0.description: A self-limited parapoxvirus infection of the skin that typically manifests with tender red-blue papules, vesicles, or nodules on the hands or arms. Typically transmitted by contact with dairy cows. Complications include lymphangitis and secondary bacterial infection.

HNWKcN0.title: PBR
HNWKcN0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Peptide-binding region
2. Pancreaticobiliary reflux
3. Parabrachial region

ENW81N0.title: Prostate cancer antigen 3 gene
ENW81N0.description: An RNA gene expressed frequently in malignant prostate tissue. Increased PCA3 expression in a urine sample taken after digital rectal examination suggests a high probability of prostate cancer and indicates the need for prostate biopsy in individuals with moderately elevated prostate-specific antigen levels or a repeat biopsy after an initial negative biopsy.

vNWA1N0.title: Giant cell myocarditis
vNWA1N0.description: A rare type of autoimmune myocarditis most likely caused by T lymphocyte-mediated inflammation. Manifestations include symptoms of acute heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, and heart block. Typically has a fulminant or fatal course.

CNWqWN0.title: Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis
CNWqWN0.description: An autoimmune disorder that manifests with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and encephalopathy. Considered a variant of Guillain-Barré syndrome. Antibodies against GQ1b ganglioside, a component of the myelin in the oculomotor nerve, are frequently present.

ANWRdN0.title: Anal sphincter electromyography
ANWRdN0.description: A diagnostic procedure that measures muscle activity in response to neural stimulation to detect dysfunction at the level of the neuromuscular junction, the muscle, and the corresponding nerve. The procedure involves inserting a small sponge electrode into the anal canal and recording sphincter muscle electrical activity.

zNWrdN0.title: Severe cutaneous acute reaction
zNWrdN0.description: A group of four very rare drug induced skin eruptions that are associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Comprises drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), and acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP).

-NWDdN0.title: Coping mechanisms
-NWDdN0.description: The behavioral and mental strategies that can be consciously mobilized by an individual to aid in handling external stressors (e.g., stress, illness). Can be further divided into reactive coping (i.e. strategies that are activated following a stressor) and proactive coping (i.e. anticipatory strategies activated to prevent future stressors).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Coping strategies

ZmWZVN0.title: Low and very low risk prostate cancer
ZmWZVN0.description: Localized prostate cancer with pretreatment prostate-specific antigen levels < 10 ng/mL, a favorable grade group, and low tumor burden in biopsy cores

0mWeVN0.title: Intermediate or high-risk prostate cancer
0mWeVN0.description: Localized prostate cancer with pretreatment prostate-specific antigen levels > 10 ng/mL (> 20 ng/mL indicates high risk) and an unfavorable grade group

amWQVN0.title: Localized prostate cancer
amWQVN0.description: Tumor confined to the prostate (T1–T2) or tumor with extracapsular extension (T3a) without evidence of extension into the seminal vesicles, lymph node involvement, or metastasis (i.e., N0, M0)

bmWHVN0.title: Locally advanced prostate cancer
bmWHVN0.description: There is no standardized definition for this commonly used term but it is typically used to refer to prostate cancer with extension into the seminal vesicles (T3b), adjacent periprostatic tissue (T4), or regional lymph node involvement (N1) in the absence of distant metastases (M0).

XmW9VN0.title: Metastatic prostate cancer
XmW9VN0.description: Prostate cancer with evidence of spread to lymph nodes outside the true pelvis, or nonnodal regions such as bone (most common site, especially the vertebrae), lungs, liver, and adrenal glands

cmWaeN0.title: Fowler position
cmWaeN0.description: A patient position in which patient is seated at an angle between 60 and 90 degrees.

WmWPeN0.title: Undifferentiated connective tissue disease
WmWPeN0.description: A term used to describe a clinical entity that manifests with laboratory evidence (e.g., positive ANAs, other autoantibodies) and clinical evidence of autoimmunity (e.g., arthralgia, Raynaud phenomenon, photosensitivity) for ≥ 3 years without fulfilling the criteria for any specific connective tissue disease. Approximately 25% of patients progress to an identifiable systemic autoimmune disease within 1–3 years.

VmWGeN0.title: Semi-Fowler position
VmWGeN0.description: A patient position in which patient is seated at an angle between 30 and 45 degrees.

SmWyUN0.title: Integrated delivery system
SmWyUN0.description: An organized network that contractually requires health care providers in the network to coordinate care across settings for a particular patient population and is accountable as a whole for both economic and clinical outcomes of their services.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care delivery models

RmWl2N0.title: Severe hypocalcemia
RmWl2N0.description: A total serum calcium level ≤ 7.5 mg/dL (< 1.9 mmol/L) or ionized (free) calcium level < 3.6 mg/dL (< 0.9 mmol/L).

qmWCgN0.title: Transfusion-associated sepsis
qmWCgN0.description: The development of sepsis as a result of bacterial contamination of transfused blood products (e.g., due to contaminated donor blood or environmental contamination of blood product). Associated pathogens include Bacillus, Streptococcus, Staphylococcus, Clostridium, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Proteus, and Pseudomonas species.

rmWfSN0.title: S1
rmWfSN0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. The first heart sound
2. The first sacral vertebra or nerve root

7mW4SN0.title: Iron chelation
7mW4SN0.description: A pharmacotherapy used to treat acute iron intoxication and hemochromatosis. Also used to prevent complications from iron overload that can occur in patients receiving chronic blood transfusions. Chelating agents (e.g., deferoxamine, deferiprone, deferasirox) bind excess iron ions and enhance iron excretion (e.g., in urine and/or feces), thereby preventing iron accumulation in vital organs.

smWtSN0.title: S2
smWtSN0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. The second heart sound
2. The second sacral vertebra or nerve root

GmWBSN0.title: Salpingopharyngeus muscle
GmWBSN0.description:
A pharyngeal muscle that originates from the pharyngeal end of the pharyngotympanic tube and passes down­ward within the salpingopharyngeal fold, blending with the palatopharyn­geus muscle in the pharyngeal wall.
Elevates the pharynx and assists the tensor veli palatini to open the pharyngotym­panic tube when swallowing. Innervated by the pharyngeal plexus.

tmWXhN0.title: Superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle
tmWXhN0.description: A pharyngeal muscle that originates from the pterygomandibular ligament, medial pterygoid plate, pterygoid hamulus, and mandible. Inserts into the median pharyngeal raphe. Closes the soft palate during swallowing and constricts the upper part of the pharynx to allow downward propulsion of a food bolus. Innervated by the pharyngeal plexus.

FmWghN0.title: Middle pharyngeal constrictor muscle
FmWghN0.description: A pharyngeal muscle that originates from the stylohyoid ligament and the horns of the hyoid bone and inserts into the pharyngeal raphe. Constricts the middle part of the pharynx to allow downward propulsion of a food bolus. Innervated by the pharyngeal plexus.

8mWOhN0.title: Inferior pharyngeal constrictor muscle
8mWOhN0.description: A pharyngeal muscle that consists of two parts: the thyropharyngeus muscle, which originates from the lamina of the thyroid cartilage, and the cricopharyngeus muscle, which originates in the cricoid cartilage of the larynx and inserts into the pharyngeal raphe. Constricts the lower part of the pharynx to allow downward propulsion of a food bolus and prevent the passage of food into the trachea. Also prevents pharyngeal reflux into the esophagus. Innervated by the pharyngeal plexus.

EmW8hN0.title: Team-based care
EmW8hN0.description: The delivery of health services by the coordinated efforts of at least two health care providers.

DmW13N0.title: Multidisciplinary care
DmW13N0.description: The delivery of health services by the coordinated efforts of health care providers trained in different disciplines (e.g., specialities).

CmWq3N0.title: Anti-TNF-α antibodies
CmWq3N0.description: An antibody that binds to tumor necrosis factor alpha, interfering with its ability to bind to its receptor. Results in decreased cytokine-driven inflammation. Used to treat many inflammatory conditions, including psoratic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and hidradenitis suppurativa. Examples include adalimumab, infliximab, and certolizumab.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

xmWE3N0.title: Papulopustular
xmWE3N0.description: A dermatologic descriptor for a rash that consists of both papules (small, palpable skin lesions < 1 cm in size) and pustules (small, pus-containing blisters < 1 cm in size).

AmWRRN0.title: Sickle cell hemoglobin D disease
AmWRRN0.description: A rare compound heterozygous hemoglobinopathy that occurs in individuals with one hemoglobin S allele and one hemoglobin D allele, both of which affect the beta-globin gene. The HbD variant determines how severe the disease is. One variant, Hb-Punjab/Los Angeles, causes a sickle cell disease presentation.

zmWrRN0.title: Symptomatic carotid stenosis
zmWrRN0.description: The presence of symptoms attributable to carotid artery stenosis within the past 6 months. Common symptoms caused by ischemia of the carotid artery territory include transient ischemic attack, contralateral weakness and/or sensory deficits, and ipsilateral transient blindness.

-mWDRN0.title: Asymptomatic carotid stenosis
-mWDRN0.description: An atherosclerotic narrowing of the carotid artery in individuals who have not experienced a transient ischemic attack or symptoms attributable to ischemia of the carotid artery territory within the past 6 months.

b5WHiN0.title: Low-intensity statin therapy
b5WHiN0.description: A statin dosage that is expected to reduce LDL by < 30%. Examples include 10 mg of simvastatin or 20 mg lovastatin daily.

15W2QN0.title: Renal vascular injury
15W2QN0.description: An injury to the renal vein or artery leading to active bleeding, thrombosis, and/or devascularization.

V5WGQN0.title: Voretigene neparvovec
V5WGQN0.description: A gene therapy agent that delivers to cells a normal copy of the RPE65 gene, the product of which is responsible for conversion of retinoids during phototransduction in the retina. Is approved for the treatment of retinal dystrophies associated with mutations in RPE65 gene (e.g., Leber congenital amaurosis).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Gene therapy

e5WxQN0.title: Breast hypertrophy
e5WxQN0.description: A condition characterized by the proliferation of breast connective tissue, glandular hypertrophy, and/or excess fatty tissue, which results in abnormal breast enlargement. Underlying causes include aromatase excess syndrome, hyperprolactinemia, and increased sensitivity to estrogen and progesterone.

U5WbjN0.title: Tisagenlecleucel
U5WbjN0.description: A chimeric antibody receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy used to treat relapsing or refractory acute lymphoblastic leukemia in individuals up to 25 years. Represents a lentiviral vector that is administered to autologous T-cells to induce production of anti-CD19 T-cell receptors; the reprogrammed T-cells attack B-cells, including blast cells. A frequent adverse effect is cytokine release syndrome.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Gene therapy

S5WyjN0.title: C3 convertase
S5WyjN0.description: A serine protease and component of the complement pathway that cleaves C3 into C3a and C3b.

35WSPN0.title: Unexpected weight gain
35WSPN0.description: An unintentional increase in body weight without an increase in calorie intake or a decrease in physical activity. Causes can be environmental (e.g., lack of sleep, stress), hormonal (e.g., hypothyroidism, Cushing syndrome), or inherited (e.g., Prader-Willi syndrome).

destinations.label: Unexpected weight changes → Unexpected weight gain

i5WJPN0.title: Transarterial embolization
i5WJPN0.description: A minimally invasive procedure in which an endovascular catheter is fluoroscopy-guided into the artery supplying a tumor, vascular abnormality, or bleeding site. Injection of synthetic material through the catheter interrupts blood flow within the artery. Transarterial embolization may be used to stop active bleeding, prevent vascular rupture, or reduce tumor size.

j5W_PN0.title: Carotid revascularization
j5W_PN0.description: An intervention performed to restore patency of a stenosed extracranial carotid artery, with the goal of reducing the risk of stroke in the carotid artery territory. Performed by carotid endarterectomy, carotid artery stenting, or, less commonly, carotid artery bypass grafting.

45W34N0.title: Clinically significant carotid stenosis
45W34N0.description: Narrowing of the carotid artery by ≥ 50%.

k5Wm4N0.title: Moderate carotid stenosis
k5Wm4N0.description: Narrowing of the carotid artery by 50%–69%.

O5WI4N0.title: Severe carotid stenosis
O5WI4N0.description: Narrowing of the carotid artery by 70%–99%.

l5Wv4N0.title: Chromosomal microarray
l5Wv4N0.description: A microchip-based genetic diagnostic method that detects copy number variations (i.e., small deletions or duplications).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Genetic testing

N5W-4N0.title: Split renal function
N5W-4N0.description: The measurement of the relative contribution of each kidney to total renal function. Usually estimated using renal scintigraphy with labeled radionuclides.

n5W7kN0.title: Single-gene sequencing
n5W7kN0.description: A determination of the sequence of a single gene. Commonly used techniques include Sanger sequencing and next generation sequencing.

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Genetic testing

L5WwkN0.title: Cannonball metastases
L5WwkN0.description: A term used to describe the radiologic appearance of multiple, large, round, well-defined pulmonary metastases. They are usually associated with widely metastatic malignancy.

J5WsON0.title: Thermal ablation
J5WsON0.description: The use of very high temperature (radiofrequency ablation, microwave ablation) or very low temperature (cryoablation) to damage or destroy areas of pathological tissue. Can be used in various conditions; targets include tumors, areas of the brain (for the treatment of seizures), and parts of the heart (to treat arrhythmias).

I5WYlN0.title: Tracheal rupture
I5WYlN0.description: The partial or complete puncture or laceration of the trachea or the main bronchi as the result of trauma.

75W4lN0.title: Tetracycline
75W4lN0.description: An antibiotic in the tetracycline class used to treat various infections (e.g., actinomycosis, listeriosis, gram-negative infections).

H5WKlN0.title: PAP
H5WKlN0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
2. Positive airway pressure
3. Pulmonary artery pressure

G5WBlN0.title: Belimumab
G5WBlN0.description: A human recombinant monoclonal antibody that targets the B lymphocyte stimulator, indirectly decreasing B-cell survival and the production of autoantibodies. Approved for the treatment of systemic lupus erythematosus.

F5WgNN0.title: Comitant strabismus
F5WgNN0.description: A type of strabismus in which the deviation of the eyes (i.e., the angle between the visual axes of both the eyes) varies with the directions of gaze. Characteristically seen in paralytic strabismus (e.g., due to ophthalmoplegia) and restrictive strabismus.

E5W8NN0.title: Full-thickness rectal prolapse
E5W8NN0.description: The protrusion of all layers of the rectum through the anus, which results in a mass of concentric mucosal folds.

v5WANN0.title: Partial rectal prolapse
v5WANN0.description: The protrusion of rectal mucosa through the anus, which results in a mass of radial mucosal folds.

D5W1mN0.title: Rectopexy
D5W1mN0.description: A surgical procedure for rectal prolapse in which rectal tissue is affixed to the sacral promontory with sutures or mesh.

w5WhmN0.title: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita
w5WhmN0.description: The presence of multiple congenital joint contractures. Most commonly affects the joints of the arms and legs but can also involve the jaw and the spine. Associated with connective tissue disorders and muscle disorders (e.g., muscular dystrophies and congenital myopathies).

95WNmN0.title: Lateral hamstring reflex
95WNmN0.description: A lower limb deep tendon reflex mediated by S1. The reflex is positive if knee flexion occurs upon tapping the biceps femoris tendon, which is located at the posterolateral aspect of the knee. In patients with an absent Achilles reflex, assessing the lateral hamstring reflex helps differentiate between peripheral neuropathy (preserved lateral hamstring reflex) and radiculopathy (absent lateral hamstring reflex).

C5WqmN0.title: Facial diplegia
C5WqmN0.description: A rare condition characterized by damage to both facial nerves, which results in symptoms of bilateral facial muscle weakness (e.g., inability to frown and close the eyelids completely, mouth drooping).

y5Wd5N0.title: Arnold's nerve
y5Wd5N0.description: The auricular branch of the vagus nerve, which innervates the tragus and the external acoustic meatus. Stimulation of the nerve can elicit a cough (Arnold’s nerve ear-cough reflex).

A5WR5N0.title: Arnold’s nerve ear-cough reflex
A5WR5N0.description: A reflex elicited by mechanical stimulation of the external auditory meatus, which activates Arnold's nerve and results in a cough.

YMWnMN0.title: Capillary electrophoresis
YMWnMN0.description: A method of separating molecules based on their electrophoretic mobility; commonly used to detect abnormal hemoglobin variants. A blood sample is added to an alkaline buffer solution in a capillary tube and then exposed to electrical charges. The charged hemoglobin fractions separate into discrete zones based on their electrophoretic mobility at a specific pH.

dMWonN0.title: ECG findings of ischemia
dMWonN0.description: A collection of static or dynamic electrocardiographic features that are consistent with past or ongoing myocardial ischemia. Examples include ST elevation, ST depressions, pathologic Q waves, T wave changes, and new intraventricular conduction abnormalities.

eMWxnN0.title: Diskectomy
eMWxnN0.description: A surgical procedure to remove the herniated portion of the intervertebral disk. Used in the management of degenerative disk diseases that cause symptomatic compression of the spinal cord or nerve roots. Can be performed with an open approach (laminectomy with diskectomy), minimally invasive surgery (hemilaminectomy with microdiskectomy), or under fluoroscopic guidance (percutaneous diskectomy).

UMWbLN0.title: Sickle cell hemoglobin E disease
UMWbLN0.description: A rare compound heterozygous hemoglobinopathy that occurs in individuals with one hemoglobin S allele and one hemoglobin E allele, which both affect the beta-globin gene. In most cases the hemoglobinopathy causes a mild form of sickle cell disease, but occasionally severe manifestations occur (e.g., stroke, vasoocclusive crisis, acute chest syndrome).

2MWTLN0.title: Electroporation
2MWTLN0.description: Usage of a high-voltage electrical field for DNA delivery into cells. Electrical field change permeability of the cell membrane allowing for passage of the substances with large molecular weight (such as nucleic acids).

destinations.label: Basics of human genetics → Gene therapy

fMWkLN0.title: Vocal fold retention cyst
fMWkLN0.description: A benign, sac-like structure that can form in the lamina propria of the vocal cords. Develops as a result of obstruction of laryngeal mucus-secreting glands due to inflammation from high vocal stress.

gMWFLN0.title: Vocal fold epidermoid cyst
gMWFLN0.description: A benign, sac-like structure that can form in the lamina propria of the vocal cords. Develops as a result of obstruction of laryngeal mucus-secreting glands due to a congenital anomaly or vocal trauma.

SMWyLN0.title: Papulovesicular
SMWyLN0.description: A dermatologic descriptor for a rash that consists of both papules (small, palpable skin lesions < 1 cm in size) and vesicles (small, fluid-filled blisters < 1 cm in size).

iMWJoN0.title: Acute sickle cell hepatic crisis
iMWJoN0.description: The mildest form of sickle cell hepatopathy caused by hepatic ischemic during a vasoocclusive crisis. Occurs in ∼ 10% of patients.  Symptoms include fever, acute onset RUQ pain, jaundice, and tender hepatomegaly. Laboratory studies typically show transaminitis and conjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Management is mainly supportive (for the vasoocclusive episode). Can progress to severe sickle cell hepatopathy.

QMWuoN0.title: Sickle cell hepatopathy
QMWuoN0.description: An acute hepatobiliary complication of sickle cell disease. Liver dysfunction (e.g., elevated liver enzymes) and hyperbilirubinemia occurs secondary to intrahepatic sickling during a sickle cell vasoocclusive crisis. Symptoms can progress from mild ischemia (i.e., hepatic crisis) to acute hepatic sequestration, and rarely to life-threatening cholestasis (i.e., acute intrahepatic cholestasis).

jMW_oN0.title: Acute hepatic sequestration
jMW_oN0.description: A form of sickle cell hepatopathy that results from ischemia and subsequent sequestration of blood in the liver during a vasoocclusive crisis. Symptoms include acute RUQ pain, hepatomegaly, and anemia. Laboratory studies typically show normal transaminase levels, predominantly conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, and elevated alkaline phosphate. Treatment involves simple or exchange transfusion.

PMWWKN0.title: Acute intrahepatic cholestasis
PMWWKN0.description: A life-threatening form of sickle cell hepatopathy. Symptoms include acute fever and RUQ pain and can progress rapidly to symptoms of acute liver failure. Laboratory evaluation may find transaminitis, mixed hyperbilirubinemia, elevated alkaline phosphate, and coagulopathy. Treatment involves exchange transfusion and supportive management of liver failure and/or coagulopathy.

4MW3KN0.title: Paresis
4MW3KN0.description: A partial loss of voluntary motor control. Manifests with weakness and/or limited range of movement.

kMWmKN0.title: Vasoreactivity testing
kMWmKN0.description: A test performed during right heart catheterization to determine if a patient with pulmonary arterial hypertension will respond favorably to calcium channel blocker (CCB) therapy. Mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) is measured after administration of a vasodilator (e.g., inhaled nitric oxide); if there is a ≥ 10 mm Hg reduction in mPAP and the absolute mPAP is ≤ 40 mm Hg with an increased or unchanged cardiac output, the patient is considered potentially responsive to CCB therapy.

destinations.label: Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale → Long-term management

OMWIKN0.title: Risk factors for MRSA infection
OMWIKN0.description: A group of factors that are associated with an increased risk of infection with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Includes colonization with MRSA, previous use of antibiotics, invasive devices (e.g., indwelling catheters), skin trauma, and sharing of unsterile equipment (e.g., needles for injection drug use).

lMWvKN0.title: Tracheal carcinoma
lMWvKN0.description: A malignant tumor of the trachea that occurs most commonly in men aged between 60 and 70 years. Risk factors include smoking and exposure to inhaled hydrocarbons.

destinations.label: Head and neck carcinomas → Tracheal carcinoma

NMW-KN0.title: Acoustic radiation force impulse
NMW-KN0.description: An ultrasonographic technique used to quantify liver stiffness. It is integrated into conventional ultrasound systems, thereby allowing simultaneous visualization of liver morphology. Used as a diagnostic tool for the early diagnosis of liver fibrosis and progression to liver cirrhosis.

mMWV6N0.title: Anal sphincter complex
mMWV6N0.description: An anatomical region that consists of the internal anal sphincter, external anal sphincter, and puborectalis muscle.

5MWi6N0.title: Upper limit of normal
5MWi6N0.description: A value at the upper extreme of the reference range (e.g., 95th percentile) of the target population.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Measures of dispersion

MMWM6N0.title: ECG findings in hypocalcemia
MMWM6N0.description: The classic ECG finding in hypocalcemia is a prolonged QT interval as a result of lengthening of the ST segment. A QTc > 500 ms increases the risk of developing life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias.

LMWw6N0.title: Habit reversal therapy
LMWw6N0.description: A therapy used to treat habitual behavioral problems, such as trichotillomania, tics, skin picking, or nail biting. Includes learning to acknowledge the targeted habit and its antecedent signs (awareness training) and performance of a voluntary movement that prevents completion of the targeted habit (competing-response training), such as clenching the fists for a set period of time to prevent skin picking.

6MWjpN0.title: Simple transfusion
6MWjpN0.description: The most common type of packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion, in which pRBCs are administered to a patient without removing any of their blood. Doing so increases the patient's total number of RBCs and dilutes their original RBCs. By contrast, an exchange transfusion involves administering pRBCs while simultaneously removing an equal  volume of the patient's blood, thereby replacing (rather than diluting) their RBCs.

JMWspN0.title: Lip carcinoma
JMWspN0.description: A malignant tumor of the skin of the lips, usually arising from squamous cells. The main risk factors are tobacco use, alcohol use, and chronic ultraviolet radiation exposure. Can manidest as an exophytic or infiltrative lesion or a nonhealing ulcer.

destinations.label: Head and neck carcinomas → Lip carcinoma

IMWYJN0.title: Actigraphy
IMWYJN0.description: A watch-like device attached to a patient's wrist to record movements during sleep and estimate sleep-wake patterns. May be used to evaluate for sleep disorders but reliability is limited if the patient remains still for long periods of time while awake at night.

rMWfJN0.title: Salter-Harris type 3 fracture
rMWfJN0.description: A transverse fracture of the physis and epiphysis that may extend to the joint and affect the articular surface.

media.title: Fracture of the medial malleolus and of the epiphyseal plate

7MW4JN0.title: Salter-Harris type 1 fracture
7MW4JN0.description: A physeal fracture that passes through the growth plate without involving bone, separating the epiphysis from the metaphysis. If the fracture is undisplaced, it is often undetectable on x-ray.

HMWKJN0.title: Salter-Harris type 2 fracture
HMWKJN0.description: A transverse fracture of the metaphysis and physis, which often involves separation of a triangular section of the metaphysis. It is the most common type of Salter-Harris fracture.

sMWtJN0.title: Salter-Harris type 4 fracture
sMWtJN0.description: A fracture through the metaphysis, physis, and epiphysis that enters the joint.

GMWBJN0.title: Salter-Harris type 5 fracture
GMWBJN0.description: A fracture characterized by impaction and disruption of the physics, Occurs due to a crush or compression injury. These fractures are often not seen on x-ray and commonly lead to limb-length discrepancies, angular deformities and/or growth disruption in children.

tMWXqN0.title: Sigma receptor
tMWXqN0.description: A cell surface receptor that is agonized by several drugs, including cocaine, PCP, methamphetamine, and dextromethorphan. Its endogenous ligands are not fully understood. Further subdivided into sigma-1 and sigma-2 subtypes.

FMWgqN0.title: Contraindications to NSAIDs
FMWgqN0.description: A group of risk factors that preclude the use of NSAIDs. These contraindications include previous NSAID hypersensitivity reaction, pregnancy, increased risk of bleeding (e.g., taking anticoagulant medications, perioperative bleeding risk), kidney injury (e.g., due to dehydration, kidney disease), peptic ulcer disease (e.g., prior/active peptic ulcer disease, GI bleeding, GI perforation), and cardiovascular disease (e.g., recent and/or active myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary artery bypass graft).

8MWOqN0.title: Intranasal synechia
8MWOqN0.description: A complication of nasal surgery characterized by the formation of scar tissue between two opposing mucosal surfaces in the nasal cavity (e.g., between the turbinates and the lateral nasal wall).

9MWNIN0.title: Monomorphic fungi
