9MWNIN0.description: A type of fungus that exists exclusively as either yeast or mold.

BMWzIN0.title: Fungal fragmentation
BMWzIN0.description: A type of asexual fungal reproduction mechanism that occurs when a portion of the mycelium splits from the body of the fungus and the resulting fragment is capable of continuing replicating.

AMWRrN0.title: Budding
AMWRrN0.description: A type of asexual fungal reproduction mechanism that occurs when an outgrowth, bud, or appendage develops on the surface of the cell or the hypha, with its cytoplasm being continuous with that of the parent cell. The nucleus of the parent cell divides, and one daughter nucleus migrates into the bud. This fragment eventually detaches after the nucleus divides via mitosis from the parent cell and is capable of replicating using the same process. Yeasts (e.g., Candida spp.) mainly reproduce using this mechanism.

_MW5rN0.title: Asexual spore production
_MW5rN0.description: A type of asexual fungal reproduction mechanism that occurs when a haploid cell is produced via mitosis and released from the parent body (e.g., hypha, sporogenous cell). Spores may be released externally or within a special reproductive structure, where they grow independently.

ZnWZ7N0.title: Homothallism
ZnWZ7N0.description: The possession of resources to reproduce sexually in a single fungus (i.e., the thallus contains both male and female sex organs, thus enabling self-fertilization). Seen in fungi such as Aspergillus nidulans and  P. jirovecii.

0nWe7N0.title: Heterothallism
0nWe7N0.description: The division of sexes between fungi of a single (self-sterile) species. This mechanism of reproduction occurs between two separate mycelia.

bnWH7N0.title: Osteosynthetic procedures
bnWH7N0.description: A type of procedure that involves the fixation (stabilization and immobilization) of bone fractures using mechanical devices (e.g., screws, plates, nails, and wires). Internal fixation involves the placement of mechanical devices within the body; external fixation involves external hardware.

destinations.label: Trauma and orthopedic surgery → Osteosynthetic procedures

cnWaHN0.title: Red flags in diarrhea
cnWaHN0.description: Patients with red flags usually require a detailed diagnostic workup and close supervision during management. Red flags in acute diarrhea include systemic symptoms (e.g., fever), dehydration, bloody stools, immunocompromise, and recent antibiotic use. Red flags in chronic diarrhea include unintended weight loss, hypoalbuminemia, onset in individuals > 50 years of age, and a family history of GI malignancies.

1nW2HN0.title: Sickle cell diseases
1nW2HN0.description: A group of inherited syndromes characterized by the presence of hemoglobin S, an abnormal hemoglobin that is poorly soluble and polymerizes when deoxygenated, which results in sickle-shaped erythrocytes. These syndromes manifest with vasoocclusive phenomena and hemolytic anemia.

media.title: Sickle cell disease with drepanocytes and target cells

WnWPHN0.title: Tongue carcinoma
WnWPHN0.description: A type of head and neck malignancy that arises from squamous cells of the anterior tongue (squamous cell cancer of the oral tongue) or posterior tongue (squamous cell cancer of the base of the tongue). Manifestations include pain, nonhealing ulcers, dysphagia, and dysarthria. Risk factors include exposure to carcinogens (e.g., alcohol, tobacco, human papillomavirus).

fnWksN0.title: Aerophony
fnWksN0.description: The hearing of one's own breathing. Can be caused by patulous eustachian tube.

TnW6sN0.title: Anomalous pancreaticobiliary junction
TnW6sN0.description: An anomaly of the biliary tree caused by the fusion of the pancreatic duct and the common bile duct before passage through the duodenal wall, which results in the creation of a long common channel. Frequently found in individuals with biliary cysts, as the common channel allows pancreatic secretions to reflux into the biliary tree with subsequent inflammation and cystic degeneration.

gnWFsN0.title: Under-five mortality rate
gnWFsN0.description: The rate of death of children < 5 years of age per specific time period. Calculated as the number of deaths of children < 5 years divided by the total number of live births × 1,000.

destinations.label: Population health → Measures of disease frequency

hnWcGN0.title: Expansive pyramid
hnWcGN0.description: A graphical representation of demographics in a population in which the birth rate is higher than the death rate. For example, a population with a high birth rate and low life expectancy.

destinations.label: Population health → Elements describing population health

3nWSGN0.title: Stationary pyramid
3nWSGN0.description: A graphical representation of a population in which the age distribution remains relatively constant over time. For example, a population with a low or stable birth rate, low or stable mortality rate, and high or stable life expectancy.

destinations.label: Population health → Elements describing population health

RnWlGN0.title: Constrictive pyramid
RnWlGN0.description: A visualization of a population in which death rate is higher than the birth rate. For example, a population with a low birth rate and high life expectancy.

destinations.label: Population health → Elements describing population health

QnWuGN0.title: Pronator drift
QnWuGN0.description: An examination finding of asymmetric pronation and drifting movement of the arms when the patient stands with outstretched arms and closed eyes. Cerebellar lesions typically cause pronation and upward drift; upper motor neuron lesions typically cause pronation and downward drift.

jnW_GN0.title: MEP
jnW_GN0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Motor evoked potential
2. Motor end plate
3. Maximal expiratory pressure

4nW3tN0.title: Vaccination hesitancy
4nW3tN0.description: A state of feeling ambivalent about or resistant to receiving vaccinations. Resulting behaviors may include delay of vaccination, cautious acceptance of vaccinations, refusal of selected vaccinations, and/or refusal of all vaccinations.

OnWItN0.title: Medication-assisted treatment
OnWItN0.description: An approach to the treatment of opioid use disorder or alcohol use disorder that combines counseling with pharmacological and behavioral therapy, tailored to each patient's needs. Improves outcomes (e.g., maintenance of sobriety, reduced overdose deaths) over either form of therapy alone.

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Management of substance use disorder

lnWvtN0.title: Anoscopy
lnWvtN0.description: A procedure in which an anoscope is inserted into the anus to visualize the anus and rectum. Anoscopy is typically used to evaluate for hemorrhoids or causes of perianal pain.

NnW-tN0.title: Jackknife position
NnW-tN0.description: A position in which the patient lies on their abdomen with hips (and if needed, knees) flexed such that the perineal region is easily visualized. Often used for procedures involving the anus and rectum.

5nWiFN0.title: Lateral decubitus position
5nWiFN0.description: A position in which the patient lies on their side. Used for examinations, such as digital rectal examination, and surgeries involving the thorax or hip.

nnW7FN0.title: Vocal abuse
nnW7FN0.description: A strain on the vocal cords caused by excessive talking, shouting, and/or coughing. Can result in polyps, granulomas, and edema and change the sound of the voice.

LnWwFN0.title: Modifiable risk factor
LnWwFN0.description: A behavior (e.g., nutrition, tobacco use, physical activity), environmental factor (e.g., UV exposure, occupational hazards), or clinical condition (e.g., obesity, hypertension, dyslipidemia) that can be altered through lifestyle changes, medical treatments, or preventive strategies to reduce the risk of disease or adverse health outcomes.

onW08N0.title: Nonmodifiable risk factor
onW08N0.description: A personal attribute or behavior that increases the risk of a disease and cannot be changed. Examples include age, genetics, and family history.

KnWU8N0.title: Risk factors for poor adherence
KnWU8N0.description: An attribute or variable that decreases the likelihood of a patient adhering to recommended treatment. Examples include excessive medical costs, lack of support, inconvenience of medical treatment, and insufficient patient understanding.

pnWL8N0.title: ​​​​​Superiority trial
pnWL8N0.description: A clinical trial that aims to prove that a study treatment or intervention is better than an existing treatment or placebo.

znWrDN0.title: Pseudo right bundle branch block
znWrDN0.description: An ECG pattern that resembles the findings of a right bundle branch block (rSr′ pattern) but is caused by a different etiology, such as an accessory electric pathway or an inherited arrhythmia (e.g., Brugada syndrome). May be partial (i.e., present only in some precordial leads).

0LWewN0.title: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
0LWewN0.description: A type of pancreatic neoplasm derived from cells found within the islets of Langerhans. Includes insulinomas, gastrinomas, glucagonomas, somatostatinomas, and VIPomas.

dLWo9N0.title: Hoover sign
dLWo9N0.description:
1. Neurology: A sign used to differentiate between organic and functional paresis. With the patient lying in the supine position, the examiner places their hand under the affected heel and asks the patient to lift their unaffected leg against resistance. In functional paresis, downward pressure is felt on the hand under the affected heel.
2. Pulmonology: A sign observed in patients with severe airway obstruction (e.g., COPD, asthma) characterized by retraction of the lower intercostal spaces during inspiration.

VLWG9N0.title: Hip abductor sign
VLWG9N0.description: A sign used to differentiate between organic and functional paresis. While lying in the supine position, the patient is asked to abduct the unaffected leg against resistance. In functional paresis, the affected leg remains in its original position. In organic paresis, the affected leg moves in a hyperadducting direction, overpowered by the resistance exerted by the examiner.

eLWx9N0.title: Finger abduction test
eLWx9N0.description: A test used to differentiate between organic and functional paresis. With their forearms resting on a surface and both wrists extended, the patent is asked to perform abduction finger movements in their unaffected hand against resistance for 2 minutes. In patients with functional paralysis, simultaneous involuntary muscle contractions are evoked in the affected hand.

gLWFCN0.title: Signet-ring sign
gLWFCN0.description: A radiographic finding in bronchiectasis and scapholunate dissociation. In bronchiectasis, the cross-sectional bronchial diameter exceeds that of the adjacent pulmonary artery branch (diameters are typically equal in healthy individuals). In scapholunate dissociation, the scaphoid tubercle cortex appears as a ring-like shadow due to rotary subluxation of the scaphoid.

RLWlxN0.title: Individuals at high risk of HIV infection
RLWlxN0.description: Factors include men who have sex with men, multiple or anonymous sexual partners, a sexual partner with HIV or another STI, unprotected vaginal or anal sex, having other STIs, requesting testing for STIs, exchanging sex for drugs or money, history of or current IV drug use, living or receiving medical care in a setting with high HIV prevalence (e.g., correctional facilities, STI clinics), and transgender youth.

4LW3BN0.title: Clinical features of peripheral arterial disease
4LW3BN0.description: Features include intermittent claudication, rest pain, trophic skin changes, poor wound healing, cool peripheries, and diminished or absent peripheral pulses.

NLW-BN0.title: BDSM
NLW-BN0.description: An umbrella term for a variety of practices and roleplay involving bondage and discipline (BD), dominance and submission (DS), and/or sadism and masochism (SM).

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual activities

mLWVyN0.title: Indirect pulp cap
mLWVyN0.description: A method of preserving a tooth that has decay, trauma, or other damage. The decayed dentin of the tooth is removed, the open dentin is covered with a sealant, and the tooth is sealed with a filling.

LLWwyN0.title: HIV-1 and HIV-2 antibody differentiation immunoassay
LLWwyN0.description: An enzyme-linked immunoassay that is used to confirm a positive HIV-1/2 combination immunoassay and to distinguish between HIV-1 and HIV-2 infection.

KLWUAN0.title: Periapical abscess
KLWUAN0.description: The most common type of dental abscess. Characterized by infection of the dental pulp leading to the collection of pus at the apex of the dental root.

6LWjAN0.title: Periodontal abscess
6LWjAN0.description: The second most common type of dental abscess. Characterized by an infection located deep in the periodontal pocket. The most common causes are periodontitis and food impaction.

pLWLAN0.title: Malocclusion
pLWLAN0.description: Any deviation of ideal tooth positioning or improper alignment of the upper and lower dental arches. Usually asymptomatic. Can be treated with orthodontic measures (e.g., braces).

JLWsAN0.title: Ear foreign body
JLWsAN0.description: The presence of a foreign body (e.g., a small toy, insect) in the external auditory canal, most commonly impacted at the bony-cartilaginous junction. Can cause otalgia, ear fullness, hearing loss, and otorrhea.

media.title: Examination and surface anatomy of the tympanic membrane

qLWCAN0.title: Interim analysis
qLWCAN0.description: An analysis of data in clinical trials that takes place before all data has been collected. The performance of interim analyses should be specified in the study protocol. If an interim analysis shows an intervention to be particularly beneficial, futile, or harmful, the trial may be stopped early.

ILWY_N0.title: Food and Drug Administration
ILWY_N0.description: A US federal agency whose mission is to ensure the safety, efficacy, and security of medications, biological products, and medical devices. It also monitors the food supply, cosmetics, tobacco products, and products that emit radiation.

rLWf_N0.title: Investigational new drug
rLWf_N0.description: A substance with therapeutic potential that has been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for testing in human subjects.

sLWt_N0.title: Nasal vestibule
sLWt_N0.description: The most anterior part of the nasal cavity. It is lined with hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and sweat glands. Hairs within the nasal vestibule help filter small particles.

GLWB_N0.title: Intranasal packing
GLWB_N0.description: A commonly used technique for the management of refractory epistaxis. Involves the placement of nasal packing devices into the nasal cavity, which exert local pressure and allow clot formation.

tLWXzN0.title: Warm ischemia time
tLWXzN0.description: The time that passes from withdrawal of life support in an organ donor to the initiation of cold organ preservation.

FLWgzN0.title: Cold ischemia time
FLWgzN0.description: The time that passes from the initiation of cold organ preservation to the warming of the organ within the recipient following the restoration of blood perfusion.

8LWOzN0.title: Precapillary pulmonary hypertension
8LWOzN0.description: A subtype of pulmonary hypertension caused by remodeling of the pulmonary vasculature that leads to increased vascular resistance. Characterized on right heart catheterization by a mean pulmonary arterial pressure > 20 mm Hg with pulmonary arterial wedge pressure ≤ 15 mm Hg, and pulmonary vascular resistance ≥ 3 Wood units.

destinations.label: Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale → Definitions

uLWpzN0.title: Postcapillary pulmonary hypertension
uLWpzN0.description: A subtype of pulmonary hypertension caused by increased pulmonary venous pressure (typically secondary to left-sided heart failure). Characterized on right heart catheterization as mean pulmonary arterial pressure > 20 mm Hg with pulmonary arterial wedge pressure > 15 mm Hg and pulmonary vascular resistance < 3 Wood units.

destinations.label: Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale → Definitions

ELW8zN0.title: Abdominal paradox
ELW8zN0.description: The paradoxical inward movement of the abdomen during inspiration. Occurs due to diaphragmatic fatigue or paralysis and the inability of the diaphragm to maintain outward expansion while intercostal muscles are contracting during inspiration. Etiologies include neuropathic, myopathic, inflammatory, and metabolic disorders, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, mechanical ventilation, and trauma.

BLWz-N0.title: Red blood cell mass
BLWz-N0.description: The total quantity of erythrocytes found in the circulation. Can be directly measured by radionuclide dilution. Polycythemia vera can cause an increase in RBC mass; anemia can cause a decrease in RBC mass.

yLWdZm0.title: Drug scheduling
yLWdZm0.description: A legal classification of drugs and substances depending on their potential for physical and psychological abuse and medical use. Regulated by the Controlled Substances Act. Ranges from Class I drugs (not used medically, high potential for abuse) to Class V drugs (low potential for abuse).

aoWQ0m0.title: Subungual melanoma
aoWQ0m0.description: A rare subtype of acral lentiginous melanoma that develops within the nail unit (usually from the nail matrix). Typically manifests as a longitudinal black or brown band. Can result in periungual pigmentation of the proximal or lateral nail folds (Hutchinson sign). More common in patients with darker skin types.

UoWbYm0.title: Orthostatic syncope
UoWbYm0.description: A type of syncope or presyncope that is mediated by orthostasis, a drop in blood pressure (orthostatic hypotension) and/or rise in heart rate (orthostatic tachycardia) that occur in response to postural changes (e.g., from supine to standing).

2oWTYm0.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor
2oWTYm0.description: A medication that inhibits the action of regulatory proteins, known as checkpoint proteins, on the immune response. Checkpoint inhibitors are used in the treatment of cancers which produce checkpoint proteins that reduce a patient's intrinsic antineoplastic T-cell activity.

destinations.label: Immunosuppressants → Biological agents used in immunotherapy

foWkYm0.title: Collier sign
foWkYm0.description: The development of unilateral or bilateral lid retraction due to a midbrain lesion of the superior colliculi and the medial longitudinal fasciculus. Characteristically occurs in Parinaud syndrome.

ToW6Ym0.title: Bloodstream infection
ToW6Ym0.description: The presence of viable pathogen(s) in the bloodstream, identified by a positive blood culture result. Can be categorized into primary and secondary bloodstream infections.

goWFYm0.title: Dural tail sign
goWFYm0.description: An MRI finding characterized by thickening and enhancement of the dura mater. Most commonly seen in association with meningiomas. The dura mater typically tapers away from the tumor, resulting in a tail-like appearance.

SoWyYm0.title: Opioid rotation
SoWyYm0.description: A pharmacologic management approach for patients with poorly controlled pain. One opioid is exchanged with another one at an equianalgesic dose. Goals include improved analgesia (due to reduced tolerance) and fewer adverse effects.

hoWcbm0.title: Endovascular infection
hoWcbm0.description: An infection that involves either the arterial or venous vasculature; can affect native vessels or implanted devices. Examples include infective endocarditis, mycotic aneurysms, and vascular graft infections.

3oWSbm0.title: Vesicant agent
3oWSbm0.description: A drug that can result in tissue damage, blister formation, and frank necrosis when inadvertently infused into the tissue surrounding a vein. Examples include vasopressors and certain groups of chemotherapeutic agents.

destinations.label: Vascular access → Infiltration and extravasation injuries

RoWlbm0.title: Cancer-related fatigue
RoWlbm0.description: A subjective, distressing sense of mental, physical, or emotional exhaustion related to cancer and the associated treatment. The fatigue is persistent, disproportionate to physical activity, and decreases the patient's quality of life.

destinations.label: Principles of cancer care → Cancer-related complications

QoWubm0.title: Genetic cancer syndromes
QoWubm0.description: A group of inherited syndromes that increase the risk of developing cancer at an early age. Mutations typically affect regulating factors of the cell cycle or impair DNA repair. Approximately 5% of malignancies are a result of inherited mutations.

joW_bm0.title: Secretin-enhanced MRCP
joW_bm0.description: A noninvasive test of pancreatic function and structure that utilizes IV secretin to stimulate and evaluate pancreatic exocrine function and visualizes the entire pancreatic duct. Can be performed in conjunction with a standard MRCP. Features of chronic pancreatitis on s-MRCP include an irregular dilated main pancreatic duct and dilated side branches.

loWvXm0.title: Posterior rhinoscopy
loWvXm0.description: A procedure in which a posterior rhinoscopy mirror is inserted into the patient's mouth, behind the soft palate, to examine the posterior nasal cavity and nasopharynx. It is rarely used now, as nasal endoscopy is better tolerated and more sensitive in detecting nasal pathology.

NoW-Xm0.title: Alcohol
NoW-Xm0.description: A chemical compound that contains one or more hydroxyl groups (−OH) bound to a carbon atom. Often used to refer to ethyl alcohol (ethanol).

moWVcm0.title: Ventricular compliance
moWVcm0.description: The change in volume of the left ventricle per unit change in pressure. Compliance of the ventricular wall decreases as the ventricular wall is stretched. Ventricular hypertrophy and restrictive cardiomyopathy result in decreased compliance. Dilated cardiomyopathy results in increased compliance.

5oWicm0.title: Chest wall compliance
5oWicm0.description: The change in volume of the chest wall per unit change in transmural pressure (i.e., the relative pressure between atmospheric pressure and intrapleural space pressure). Children have lower chest wall compliance than adults. In older adulthood, chest wall compliance decreases.

MoWMcm0.title: Renal osteodystrophy
MoWMcm0.description: An alteration of bone morphology in patients with underlying chronic kidney disease. Can predispose to bone fragility and fracture. Diagnosed via bone biopsy.

KoWU1m0.title: Anxiety disorder due to another medical condition
KoWU1m0.description: An anxiety disorder that develops as a direct physiological consequence of another medical condition. Examples include panic attacks from arrhythmias, hyperthyroidism, and pheochromocytoma. Often associated with onset after 45 years of age and the presence of atypical symptoms that are related to the underlying medical condition, such as vertigo, incontinence, amnesia, and loss of consciousness.

6oWj1m0.title: Secondary psychosis
6oWj1m0.description: A distorted perception of reality characterized by delusions, hallucinations, and/or disorganized behavior that is caused by an underlying medical disorder (e.g., brain tumor, electrolyte abnormality) or is substance-induced.

roWfWm0.title: Pulmonary arteriovenous fistula
roWfWm0.description: An abnormal communications between pulmonary arteries and veins

7oW4Wm0.title: Sleep deprivation
7oW4Wm0.description: A state of inadequate quantity and/or quality of sleep. Can be due to external factors (e.g., irregular sleep schedule, jet lag, shift work) or sleeping disorders (e.g., insomnia, sleep apnea, hypersomnolence disorders, narcolepsy).

FoWgdm0.title: NCC
FoWgdm0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Neural crest cell
2. Na-Cl cotransporter

CoWqVm0.title: Embolotherapy
CoWqVm0.description: A procedure that involves inserting synthetic material (e.g., a balloon, coils) via an angiographic catheter into a blood vessel. Used to control hemorrhage and manage highly vascular neoplasms, aneurysms, and arteriovenous malformations.

yoWdem0.title: Flow-volume loop
yoWdem0.description: A graphical representation of spirometry findings in which the airflow rates during forced respiratory maneuvers are plotted on the y-axis against lung volume on the x-axis. Specific patterns of flow-volume loops are characteristic of certain respiratory pathologies.

zoWrem0.title: Paraphilia
zoWrem0.description: An abnormally intense and persistent sexual interest, which can manifest as urges, fantasies, and/or behaviors. In contrast to paraphilic disorders, paraphilias do not cause significant distress and/or functional impairment.

aKWQUm0.title: Anal sphincter tone
aKWQUm0.description: The degree of contraction of the anal sphincter muscles, which are normally contracted to maintain fecal continence. Tone is assessed during a digital rectal examination while the patient is relaxed and while they are squeezing. A weak anal sphincter may indicate an underlying neurological disorder, while sphincter hypertonia may indicate an anal fissure or pelvic floor dyssynergia.

1KW22m0.title: Perforated tympanic membrane
1KW22m0.description: A breach in the membrane between the middle ear and ear canal. Can occur secondary to infection, barotrauma (e.g., from scuba diving, blast injuries), or mechanical trauma from foreign objects (e.g., cotton swabs). Clinical features include pain, hearing loss, tinnitus, and otorrhea.

VKWG2m0.title: Milan criteria
VKWG2m0.description: A set of criteria used by many transplantation societies to determine if patients with hepatocellular carcinoma are eligible for liver transplantation. Patients are considered eligible if they have either one tumor measuring ≥ 2 cm and ≤ 5 cm or 2-3 tumors measuring ≥ 1 cm and ≤ 3 cm and no extrahepatic metastasis or vascular invasion.

eKWx2m0.title: Necrotizing pancreatitis
eKWx2m0.description: The necrosis of pancreatic parenchyma and peripancreatic tissue. Occurs as a complication of acute pancreatitis in 5–10% of patients and usually evolves over several days.

UKWbfm0.title: Perimesencephalic SAH
UKWbfm0.description: A nonaneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. CTA shows a specific pattern of hemorrhage, with blood in the basal cisterns anterior to the midbrain or pons without intraparenchymal or intraventricular extension. Typically considered benign and has a good prognosis.

2KWTfm0.title: Overactive bladder
2KWTfm0.description: A condition characterized by urinary urgency (often in combination with nocturia and urinary frequency) that is not attributable to urinary infection or other pathology. May occur with or without urinary incontinence.

destinations.label: Overactive bladder and urgency urinary incontinence → Definitions

fKWkfm0.title: Enteroatmospheric fistula
fKWkfm0.description: A subtype of enterocutaneous fistula involving an abnormal communication between the lumen of the intestine and the external atmosphere. Manifests with leakage of intestinal contents through the open abdomen. Most commonly arises as a complication of abdominal surgery.

hKWcTm0.title: Spasmus nutans
hKWcTm0.description: A condition characterized by ocular oscillations, head nodding, and torticollis. Most commonly develops between 6 and 12 months of age.

RKWlTm0.title: Sorafenib
RKWlTm0.description: A multikinase inhibitor that is used as a molecular targeted therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma, renal cell carcinoma, and thyroid carcinomas.

iKWJTm0.title: Lenvatinib
iKWJTm0.description: A multikinase inhibitor that is used as a molecular targeted therapy in hepatocellular, endometrial, renal, and thyroid carcinomas.

jKW_Tm0.title: Demographic transition
jKW_Tm0.description: The changes that occur in a population that goes from having high birth rates and high death rates to having low birth rates and low death rates.

destinations.label: Population health → Elements describing population health

PKWWgm0.title: HFS
PKWWgm0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Hemifacial spasm
2. Hand foot syndrome

4KW3gm0.title: ARR
4KW3gm0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Absolute risk reduction
2. Aldosterone-to-renin ratio

kKWmgm0.title: Dorsocervical fat pad
kKWmgm0.description: A hump on the upper central back that forms due to the accumulation of fat. Etiologies include chronic exposure to excess glucocorticoid (e.g., due to Cushing syndrome) and HIV-associated lipodystrophy.

OKWIgm0.title: Postmenopausal bleeding
OKWIgm0.description: In individuals not taking hormone replacement therapy (HRT): any uterine bleeding that occurs ≥ 12 months after the onset of permanent amenorrhea due to age-related loss of ovarian follicular function. In individuals taking HRT: any bleeding other than expected withdrawal bleeding from cyclic HRT.

destinations.label: Vaginal bleeding → Vaginal bleeding in nonpregnant adults

lKWvgm0.title: ECG changes in elevated intracranial pressure
lKWvgm0.description: A pattern of ECG abnormalities seen in patients with acutely elevated intracranial pressure. Features include ST segment changes, flattened or inverted T waves, prominent U waves, and prolongation of the QTc interval. Most commonly described in association with traumatic brain injury and/or subarachnoid hemorrhage.

media.title: ECG changes in raised intracranial pressure

NKW-gm0.title: Uremic encephalopathy
NKW-gm0.description: A deterioration in mental status and cognitive function caused by severe acute or chronic kidney injury. The exact etiology is unknown, but theories include that it may be a result of reduced urinary clearance of metabolic products with subsequent accumulation of neurotoxic metabolites.

mKWVSm0.title: Psychogenic unresponsiveness
mKWVSm0.description: An unresponsive state caused by an underlying psychiatric disorder. Often associated with mood and psychotic disorders. May manifest with features of stupor, coma, catatonia, dissociation, and/or psychogenic nonepileptic seizures.

destinations.label: Altered mental status and coma → Mimics

oKW0hm0.title: Products of conception
oKW0hm0.description: The tissue derived from a fertilized egg (e.g., fetus, placenta). Most commonly used to refer to tissue that remains in the body after a pregnancy loss.

KKWUhm0.title: Full Outline of UnResponsiveness
KKWUhm0.description: A standardized scale used to assess level of consciousness and neurological status. Particularly useful for intubated patients, as level of consciousness can be assessed without testing verbal responses.

destinations.label: Altered mental status and coma → Coma scores

6KWjhm0.title: Anhydrous ammonia
6KWjhm0.description: A substance used in manufacturing, refrigeration, and as fertilizer in agriculture. Due to its anhydrous chemical properties, contact (e.g., from inhalation, cutaneous exposure, or ingestion) can cause tissue dehydration and caustic burns.

JKWshm0.title: Nasal turbinates
JKWshm0.description: The bony structures inside the nose that help filter, heat, and humidify inhaled air. Most individuals have three pairs of turbinates (the superior, middle, and inferior turbinates).

qKWChm0.title: Goals of care
qKWChm0.description: The aim of medical care for an individual patient based on the patient's values, priorities, and preferences in a given clinical context. Typically determined through a shared decision-making process that includes the health care provider and the patient or their health care proxy. Used to guide decisions regarding the overall care plan, including the use or avoidance of specific medical interventions.

rKWf3m0.title: Surgically implantable catheter
rKWf3m0.description: A surgically implanted central venous catheter composed of a catheter terminating in the central circulation and a subcutaneous reservoir, which is usually placed over the pectoralis muscle several centimeters caudal to the clavicle. The catheter is accessed by passing a needle through the intact skin into the reservoir and is used for long-term delivery of medications (e.g., antibiotics or chemotherapy). It may remain in place for years if there are no complications.

destinations.label: Vascular access → Long-term central venous access

HKWK3m0.title: Ambulatory blood pressure measurement
HKWK3m0.description: The periodic measurement of blood pressure via a portable sphygmomanometer while a patient carries out routine daily activities. Typically obtained across a 24-hour period. Used to diagnose hypertension, especially if white coat hypertension or masked hypertension is suspected.

GKWB3m0.title: Small molecule inhibitor
GKWB3m0.description: An engineered molecule that reduces tumor growth by targeting the activity of specific protein receptor pathway sequences in cancer cells. Many protein kinase inhibitors have been approved for use in cancer treatment, e.g., tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as imatinib.

tKWXRm0.title: Immunotoxin
tKWXRm0.description: A protein moiety that contains both a toxin and a specific growth factor or antibody that binds to target cells. This mechanism allows for precision drug delivery of cytotoxic agents to cancer cells, thereby sparing healthy cells.

FKWgRm0.title: Common cold
FKWgRm0.description: A nonspecific, acute, self-limited viral infection of the upper respiratory tract, frequently manifesting with rhinorrhea, nasal obstruction, sneezing, and coughing. Most commonly caused by rhinovirus infection.

8KWORm0.title: Bronchiolectasis
8KWORm0.description: A radiologic description for dilation of the bronchioles. Thick-walled bronchioles can appear as a tree-in-bud pattern or nodular pattern on CT scan; traction bronchiolectasis appears as cystic airspaces associated with fibrosis.

EKW8Rm0.title: Risk factors for adrenal crisis
EKW8Rm0.description: For patients on long-term glucocorticoid therapy, factors include sudden cessation of treatment and intercurrent physiological stress (e.g., illness, surgery). For patients not on glucocorticoid therapy, factors include pituitary apoplexy and bilateral adrenal hemorrhage or infarction.

DKW1im0.title: Intersex
DKW1im0.description: The congenital presence of chromosomal and/or phenotypical patterns that do not fit binary notions of male or female sex and/or gender identity, generally, due to a disorder of sex development.

wKWhim0.title: International classification of headache disorders, 3rd edition
wKWhim0.description: The International Headache Society classification for all headache-related disorders. Used to aid diagnosis and guide management.

9KWNim0.title: Nonverbal pain scale
9KWNim0.description: A pain scale for patients unable to communicate (i.e., secondary to cognitive disorders or intubation). The score includes observations of patient behavior (e.g., grimacing, agitation, guarding) and patient vital signs (e.g., tachycardia, tachypnea, hypertension).

xKWEim0.title: Hepatorenal syndrome-acute kidney injury
xKWEim0.description: A type of acute kidney injury in patients with decompensated cirrhosis. Defined by an acute increase in serum creatinine in the presence of cirrhosis with ascites. Other causes and contributing factors (e.g., diuretic use, shock, structural kidney injury) must be excluded or reversed in order to make the diagnosis. Formerly called type 1 HRS.

yKWdQm0.title: Hepatorenal syndrome-nonacute kidney injury
yKWdQm0.description: A nonacute renal impairment in patients with cirrhosis. Can be further divided into hepatorenal syndrome-acute kidney disease (impairment present for < 3 months) and hepatorenal syndrome-chronic kidney disease (impairment present for ≥ 3 months). Other causes and contributing factors (e.g., diuretic use, shock, structural kidney injury) must be excluded or reversed in order to make the diagnosis. Formerly named type 2 HRS.

-KWDQm0.title: VOC
-KWDQm0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Volatile organic compound
2. Vaso-occlusive crisis

06Wejm0.title: Coloenteric fistula
06Wejm0.description: An abnormal communication between the colon and the small bowel.

a6WQjm0.title: Gastrocolic fistula
a6WQjm0.description: An abnormal communication between the stomach and the colon.

d6WoPm0.title: Transmasculine
d6WoPm0.description: A male-leaning or diverse gender identity in an individual assigned as female sex at birth.

V6WGPm0.title: Transfeminine
V6WGPm0.description: A female-leaning or diverse gender identity in an individual assigned as male sex at birth.

U6Wb4m0.title: Cross-dressing
U6Wb4m0.description: The practice of wearing clothes traditionally associated with another sex. The terms “transvestism” and “transvestite” may be considered stigmatizing due to historical discrimination and pathologization of this practice.

destinations.label: Sexuality and sexual medicine → Sexual activities

Q6Wukm0.title: Occlusal splint
Q6Wukm0.description: A custom-made dental device designed to reduce damage to the teeth and surrounding structures caused by jaw clenching and/or teeth grinding. Frequently used by individuals with temporomandibular joint dysfunction.

P6WWOm0.title: Canalplasty
P6WWOm0.description: A surgical procedure that aims to reconstruct and/or widen a narrowed external auditory canal (e.g., in patients with external auditory canal atresia).

k6WmOm0.title: Advance care planning
k6WmOm0.description: A process in which an individual clarifies and communicates their preferences for managing future health care. The aim is to align preferences for interventions (e.g., CPR, ventilator use, artificial nutrition) with personal and cultural values. Preferences are often documented in an advance directive, a physician orders for life-sustaining treatment form, and/or through designation of a medical power of attorney.

O6WIOm0.title: Disease outbreak
O6WIOm0.description: The sudden occurrence of more cases of a disease than expected in a given area, population, and/or season.

l6WvOm0.title: Hyposmolality
l6WvOm0.description: A state of osmolality below the normal physiologic range (e.g., < 275 mOsm/kg for serum).

N6W-Om0.title: Disease clustering
N6W-Om0.description: An unusual aggregation, real or perceived, of cases of a disease that are grouped together in time and space.

L6Wwlm0.title: Symptoms of tachycardia
L6Wwlm0.description: A collection of symptoms that may be present in patients with an elevated heart rate. Typically occur secondary to ischemia or hypoperfusion and include palpitations, chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, lightheadedness, and syncope.

K6WUNm0.title: Anoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
K6WUNm0.description: Global brain injury caused by complete cessation of blood flow (anoxia) during cardiac arrest. It is the most common cause of death in patients surviving cardiac arrest.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Complications

66WjNm0.title: Anoxia
66WjNm0.description: A complete lack of oxygen delivery to tissues in the setting of complete cessation of blood flow during cardiac arrest.

J6WsNm0.title: Provoked venous thromboembolism
J6WsNm0.description: A venous thromboembolic event (e.g., deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism) that has occurred in the presence of an inciting factor such as trauma, surgery, or cancer.

q6WCNm0.title: Unprovoked venous thromboembolism
q6WCNm0.description: A venous thromboembolic event (e.g., deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism) that has occurred in the absence of an inciting factor such as trauma, surgery, or cancer.

I6WYmm0.title: Phantom limb sensation
I6WYmm0.description: The sensation that an amputated or lost limb is still intact, often involving pain (phantom limb pain).

r6Wfmm0.title: Hip osteotomy
r6Wfmm0.description: A surgical procedure to improve hip joint coverage that involves cutting the femur and/or pelvis and repositioning the acetabulum and/or femur. Used to treat hip dysplasia and Legg-Calve-Perthes disease.

76W4mm0.title: Clinical index of stable febrile neutropenia
76W4mm0.description: A prognostic score for stable patients with solid tumors and neutropenic fever. The score incorporates performance status (ability to perform daily activities), COPD diagnosis, chronic cardiovascular disease, mucositis, stress-induced hyperglycemia, and monocyte count. Scores range from 0-8, with a score of 0 suggesting low risk of complications, 1-2 suggesting intermediate risk, and ≥ 3 suggesting high risk.

s6Wtmm0.title: First dose hypotension
s6Wtmm0.description: A sudden, severe, and symptomatic decrease in blood pressure caused by the first administration, increase in dose, or reinitiation of an antihypertensive drug. Manifestations include dizziness, lightheadedness, and syncope. This effect is especially common if two antihypertensive medications are given at the same time.

t6WX5m0.title: Oxcarbazepine
t6WX5m0.description: An anticonvulsant agent that is structurally similar to carbamazepine. Thought to block voltage-sensitive sodium channels, which decreases the propagation of synaptic impulses. Used to treat seizure disorders, bipolar disorders, and neuropathic pain.

F6Wg5m0.title: Chronotropic incompetence
F6Wg5m0.description: The heart rate is unable to increase sufficiently in response to increased activity or demand. Typically defined as reaching < 80% of the expected age-predicted maximal heart rate.

86WO5m0.title: Ambrisentan
86WO5m0.description: A drug that blocks endothelin receptors (ETA and ETB) on vascular endothelium and smooth muscle. Used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension.

D6W1Mm0.title: Event monitor
D6W1Mm0.description: A form of ambulatory ECG monitoring used to assess for suspected symptomatic arrhythmias that are not detected on a 12-lead ECG. The monitor is worn for 2-4 weeks, during which time the patient can press a button to initiate and transmit an ECG recording if they experience symptoms.

w6WhMm0.title: Mobile cardiovascular telemetry
w6WhMm0.description: A form of ambulatory ECG monitoring used to assess for suspected arrhythmias that are not identified on a 12-lead ECG or Holter monitor. The monitor is worn for 2-4 weeks, during which time data is transmitted daily for analysis as well as if an arrhythmia is detected or the patient indicates they are experiencing symptoms.

x6WEMm0.title: Adipsic arginine vasopressin deficiency
x6WEMm0.description: A rare condition characterized by defects in water balance homeostatic mechanisms (e.g., loss of thirst and arginine vasopressin secretion). Can be caused by rupture of aneurysms of the anterior communicating artery in the circle of Willis, and mass effect from tumors.

y6Wdnm0.title: Mediterranean diet
y6Wdnm0.description: A diet high in vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, and sources of unsaturated fats (e.g., olive oil, nuts and fish). Typically includes a low intake of meat and dairy. The Mediterranean diet has been shown to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease and overall mortality and is thought to be associated with healthier aging.

_6W5nm0.title: Atlantodental interval
_6W5nm0.description: The distance between the anterior arch of the atlas and the dens axis. Can be evaluated using x-ray or CT of the cervical spine. Pathological increase to > 3 mm in adults and > 5 mm in children suggests atlantoaxial instability (e.g., due to trauma or rheumatoid arthritis).

ZpWZLm0.title: Osmoregulation
ZpWZLm0.description: The maintenance of constant osmotic pressure in a cell relative to the extracellular space through the movement of a solvent (e.g., water) through the cell's semipermeable membrane.

apWQLm0.title: Health belief model
apWQLm0.description: A health behavior change framework used to understand and predict how individuals engage in health-related behaviors. Based on the idea that a person’s perceptions of susceptibility to a health issue, the severity of that issue, the benefits of taking action, and the barriers to doing so influence their likelihood of taking health-related actions, especially in seeking care or adopting preventive measures.

YpWnLm0.title: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status
YpWnLm0.description: A scale from 0 to 5 used to describe a patient's functional ability. Patients who are fully active are given a score of 0, those unable to complete any self-care are given a score of 4, and deceased individuals are given a score of 5.

bpWHLm0.title: Martin-Gruber anastomosis
bpWHLm0.description: A nerve communication between the median and ulnar nerves in the forearm, which can result in atypical motor and sensory innervation of the hand.

XpW9Lm0.title: Adenolipoma
XpW9Lm0.description: A variant of lipoma characterized by mature adipose tissue with interspersed eccrine glands and ducts.

cpWaom0.title: Keutel syndrome
cpWaom0.description: An autosomal recessive condition characterized by calcification of cartilage, pulmonary stenosis, and brachytelephalangism. Caused by mutations in the MGP gene, which encodes a matrix protein.

1pW2om0.title: Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome
1pW2om0.description: An autosomal recessive condition characterized by severe insulin resistance as a result of a mutation in the INSR gene, which encodes an insulin receptor. Additional features include coarse facial features, dental abnormalities, hirsutism, and acanthosis nigricans.

WpWPom0.title: Nirmatrelvir
WpWPom0.description: An orally-administered medication that inhibits the activity of the SARS-CoV-2-3CL protease, which is required by the SARS-CoV-2 virus for replication. Coadministration with the protease inhibitor ritonavir slows the metabolism of nirmatrelvir, which results in an increased duration of action.

dpWoom0.title: Molnupiravir
dpWoom0.description: An orally-administered nucleoside analog that increases the frequency of viral RNA mutations, which impairs viral replication. Used to treat mild-to-moderate coronavirus disease.

VpWGom0.title: Aceruloplasminemia
VpWGom0.description: An autosomal recessive condition characterized by the accumulation of iron in tissues as a result of a mutation in the gene that encodes ceruloplasmin, which is involved in iron transport. Clinical features include anemia, liver failure, neurologic symptoms (e.g, ataxia, dementia), and retinal degeneration.

epWxom0.title: Donohue syndrome
epWxom0.description: An autosomal recessive condition characterized by severe insulin resistance as a result of a mutation in the INSR gene, which encodes an insulin receptor. Associated with distinctive facial features, including large and low-set ears, a flat nasal bridge, thick lips, macrostomia, and hypertelorism.

UpWbKm0.title: Nesidioblastosis
UpWbKm0.description: A term used to describe histologic neoformation of islets of Langerhans from pancreatic duct epithelium. This term is sometimes used to describe persistent hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia of infancy.

2pWTKm0.title: Shoshin beriberi
2pWTKm0.description: A type of beriberi (thiamine or vitamin B₁ deficiency) characterized by rapidly progressive heart failure and distributive shock.

fpWkKm0.title: Jaccoud arthropathy
fpWkKm0.description: A collection of joint deformities associated with systemic lupus erythematosus. Includes thumb subluxation, ulnar deviation, and boutonniere deformities, and swan neck deformities.

gpWFKm0.title: Johanson-Blizzard syndrome
gpWFKm0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the UBR1 gene. Characterized by growth failure, exocrine pancreatic dysfunction, intellectual disability, sensorineural hearing loss. Also associated with hypothyroidism and dental abnormalities.

hpWc6m0.title: Drospirenone
hpWc6m0.description: A contraceptive medication that suppresses ovulation. Also has antimineralocorticoid and antiandrogenic activity.

3pWS6m0.title: Sociocusis
3pWS6m0.description: A type of hearing loss caused by nonoccupational noise exposure.

RpWl6m0.title: Empyema necessitans
RpWl6m0.description: A complication of empyema characterized by rupture of the empyema through the chest wall (out of the pleural space and into surrounding soft tissues).

ipWJ6m0.title: Immunodiffusion
ipWJ6m0.description: A laboratory technique in which reactants (e.g., antibodies, antigens) are distributed in wells within a gel. The precipitation of immune complexes in the gel is used to detect if specific antibodies and/or antigens are present.

QpWu6m0.title: FOXO3 gene
QpWu6m0.description: A gene that encodes the transcription factor forkhead box O-3 (FoxO3). Specific alleles of this gene are associated with longevity, likely related to the regulation of metabolism, oxidative stress, the cell cycle, and immunity.

jpW_6m0.title: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis
jpW_6m0.description: A rare condition characterized by the proliferation of smooth muscle-like cells in the lungs, kidneys, and/or lymphatic tissue. Manifestations include dyspnea, pneumothorax, pleural effusion, and the development of angiomyolipomas in the kidneys. Subtypes include sporadic LAM and LAM associated with tuberous sclerosis.

PpWWpm0.title: Rhodococcus
PpWWpm0.description: A genus of gram-positive organisms commonly found in the gastrointestinal tracts of herbivores and in the environment. Species include R. equi (which can cause cause pulmonary infections, particularly in individuals who are immunosuppressed), R. rhodochrous, R. fascians, and R. erythropolis.

4pW3pm0.title: Saccharin test
4pW3pm0.description: A test used to evaluate mucociliary clearance. A saccharin tablet is placed on the medial face of the inferior turbinate, and the patient is asked to swallow repeatedly until they can perceive a sweet taste. Normal nasal mucociliary clearance transit time is typically < 20 minutes.

kpWmpm0.title: Septum pellucidum
kpWmpm0.description: A membrane located between the cerebral hemispheres that connects with the corpus callosum. Congenital absence of the septum pellucidum is associated with development delay, seizures, and abnormal development of the pituitary gland and/or optic disc (septo-optic dysplasia).

OpWIpm0.title: Niikawa–Kuroki syndrome
OpWIpm0.description: A disorder caused by mutations in the KMT2D and KDMA6 genes. Manifestations include developmental delay, intellectual disability, facial dysmorphism, and dental and skeletal abnormalities.

lpWvpm0.title: Cogan syndrome
lpWvpm0.description: An autoimmune vasculitis that typically manifests with vestibuloauditory dysfunction and interstitial keratitis. Often associated with systemic vasculitis (e.g., aortitis).

NpW-pm0.title: Avoidant restrictive food intake disorder
NpW-pm0.description: An eating disorder characterized by avoidance or restriction of food (e.g., due to sensory qualities of food, lack of interest) and at least one negative consequence (significant weight loss, malnutrition, dependence on nutrition support, and/or impaired psychosocial function). Features of ARFID cannot be explained by body image disturbance, cultural practice, or food shortage.

mpWVJm0.title: Lonapegsomatropin
mpWVJm0.description: A sustained-release formulation of recombinant polypeptide identical to human growth hormone. Used to treat growth failure (e.g., due to growth hormone deficiency, idiopathic short stature, or Turner syndrome).

5pWiJm0.title: Etoricoxib
5pWiJm0.description: A COX-2 inhibitor used as an analgesic. Not commercially available in the United States.

MpWMJm0.title: Zopiclone
MpWMJm0.description: A nonbenzodiazepine sedative-hypnotic drug that acts as a GABA-A receptor agonist. Used to treat sleep disorders. Consists of a racemic mixture of two stereoisomers; the (S)-enantiomer (eszopiclone) is bioactive. Zopiclone is not commercially available in the United States.

npW7Jm0.title: Hydrocolpos
npW7Jm0.description: A distention of the vaginal cavity caused by the presence of fluid. Most commonly caused by an imperforate hymen.

LpWwJm0.title: Mucocolpos
LpWwJm0.description: A distention of the vaginal cavity caused by the presence of mucus. Fetal mucocolpos can occur due to the effect of material estrogen on fetal cervical glands.

opW0qm0.title: Pyocolpos
opW0qm0.description: A distention of the vaginal cavity caused by the presence of purulent fluid.

KpWUqm0.title: Pheniramine
KpWUqm0.description: An ophthalmic medication that blocks the release of histamine from mast cells in the conjunctival epithelium. Used to treat ocular itching and redness (i.e., due to allergic conjunctivitis).

6pWjqm0.title: Soda lime
6pWjqm0.description: A highly alkaline substance used as a carbon dioxide absorbent in a circle breathing system.

ppWLqm0.title: Kisspeptin
ppWLqm0.description: A protein secreted by the hypothalamus that is involved in the regulation of gonadotropin-releasing hormone secretion (e.g., at the initiation of puberty). Loss-of-function mutations in the gene the encodes kisspeptin can result in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

JpWsqm0.title: Menadione
JpWsqm0.description: A synthetic, water-soluble form of vitamin K that can cause hemolytic anemia and kernicterus in infants. This formulation of vitamin K is not currently used to treat individuals in the United States.

qpWCqm0.title: Dracunculiasis
qpWCqm0.description: An infection caused by ingestion of Dracunculus medinensis larvae. The larvae penetrate the gastrointestinal tract, mature and migrate to subcutaneous tissue, and emerge through the skin. Manifestations include fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and pruritic skin papules that can become painful as the parasite emerges.

media.title: Life cycle of Dracunculus medinensis (Guinea worm)

IpWYIm0.title: Dracunculus medinensis
IpWYIm0.description: A nematode (roundworm) whose larvae can infect small crustaceans. Ingestion of contaminated water or animals that have ingested these crustaceans can result in larval penetration of the gastrointestinal system, which causes dracunculiasis.

media.title: Life cycle of Dracunculus medinensis (Guinea worm)

rpWfIm0.title: Ankyloglossia
rpWfIm0.description: A condition characterized by limited tongue mobility due to an abnormally short frenulum. Can result in difficult lifting or protruding the tongue. Complications include difficulty with breastfeeding and speech articulation.

7pW4Im0.title: Ponticelli regimen
7pW4Im0.description: A treatment regimen for membranous nephropathy that consists of 6 months of steroid therapy (methylprednisolone and prednisone) and chlorambucil therapy. A modified version replaces chlorambucil with cyclophosphamide.

HpWKIm0.title: Bilastine
HpWKIm0.description: A selective peripheral H₁ receptor antagonist. Because it does not cross the blood-brain barrier, it is nonsedating. Not available in the United States.

spWtIm0.title: Xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis
spWtIm0.description: A rare gallbladder disease characterized by destructive inflammation and the accumulation of fibrous tissue and lipid-laden macrophages. Manifestations include acute-onset right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.

GpWBIm0.title: Abatacept
GpWBIm0.description: A drug that binds to CD40 and CD86 on antigen-presenting cells, which blocks interaction with CD28 and inhibits T-cell activation. Used to treat rheumatoid arthritis, polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and psoriatic arthritis.

tpWXrm0.title: Transarterial radioembolization
tpWXrm0.description: A procedure used for the treatment of liver tumors. Involves the catheter-directed transarterial injection of radioactive spheres into the tumor-feeding artery, leading to selective irradiation of the tumor-bearing liver segment or lobe.

FpWgrm0.title: External patch recorder
FpWgrm0.description: A form of ambulatory continuous ECG monitoring used to assess for arrhythmias and confirm the correlation between patient-reported symptoms and the arrhythmia. Uses a patch to provide up to 14 days of 1-lead ECG recording with a trigger that allows patients to report symptoms. Used as an alternative to a Holter monitor.

8pWOrm0.title: Osteochondrosis
8pWOrm0.description: A group of disorders characterized by abnormal enchondral ossification (e.g., due to injury or overuse of the growth plate and ossification centers). Commonly affected locations include the femoral head, the capitulum of the humerus, and the apophysis of the calcaneus.

DpW17m0.title: Metabotropic receptors
DpW17m0.description: A type of ion channel that increases ion flux in response to ligand binding through signal transduction mechanisms involving second messengers, such as G proteins.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

wpWh7m0.title: Voltage-gated ion channels
wpWh7m0.description: Transmembrane ion channels that are activated by changes in the electrical membrane potential and allow the passage of ions when open. Voltage-gated ion channels are generally specific to one of the major physiological ions (K⁺, Na⁺, Ca²⁺, Cl⁻)

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

9pWN7m0.title: Mechanically-gated ion channels
9pWN7m0.description: A type of transmembrane ion channel that is activated by changes in the structure of the membrane and allows the passage of ions when open. Mechanically-gated ion channels are generally specific to one of the major physiological ions (K⁺, Na⁺, Ca²⁺, Cl⁻).

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

CpWq7m0.title: Neurotrophic factor
CpWq7m0.description: A substance that enhances neuronal survival and differentiation. Examples include neurotrophins, neuropoietic cytokines, interleukins, and tissue growth factors.

BpWz7m0.title: Complement component 2 deficiency
BpWz7m0.description: An inherited genetic condition characterized by decreased production or complete absence of C2 protein. Associated with an increased risk of developing systemic lupus erythematosus and increased susceptibility to bacterial infections, especially with encapsulated pathogens (e.g., Pneumococcus).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital complement deficiencies

ypWdHm0.title: Synaptic transmission
ypWdHm0.description: The process of communication between two neurons, involving the release of a neurotransmitter by the presynaptic neuron and the neurotransmitter binding to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

ApWRHm0.title: Fast neurotransmission
ApWRHm0.description: Direct activation of a ligand-gated ion channel by a neurotransmitter.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

zpWrHm0.title: Neurotransmitter receptors
zpWrHm0.description: A membrane-bound receptor protein that is activated by a neurotransmitter. Found on presynaptic and postsynaptic neuronal membranes.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Neurotransmitters

0JWesm0.title: Nasal septal ulceration
0JWesm0.description: Ulceration through the mucosa, submucosa, and perichondrial layers of the nasal septum, resulting in exposure of the nasal cartilage.

destinations.label: Miscellaneous ear, nose, and throat disorders → Nasal septal ulceration and perforation

aJWQsm0.title: Synaptic plasticity
aJWQsm0.description: The ability of synaptic transmission to change in strength and/or efficacy over time as the nervous system adapts to new information. Plays a central role in early development of neural circuitry, learning, and memory.

YJWnsm0.title: Neurotransmitter diffusion
YJWnsm0.description: A dispersal of a neurotransmitter out of the synaptic cleft.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

bJWHsm0.title: Neurotransmitter enzymatic degradation
bJWHsm0.description: A termination process done by enzymes in the synaptic cleft (e.g., acetylcholinesterase) yielding an inactive substance.

destinations.label: Nerve tissue, synapses, and neurotransmitters → Synapses

dJWoGm0.title: Hydrometrocolpos
dJWoGm0.description: A distention of the vaginal and uterine cavities caused by the presence of fluid. Most commonly caused by an imperforate hymen.

VJWGGm0.title: Indirect ophthalmoscopy
VJWGGm0.description: An ophthalmological examination in which the examiner uses a light source attached to their head and a handheld lens to examine the fundus of the eye. Provides an inverted and magnified image with a wider field of view than that provided by a direct ophthalmoscope.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Fundoscopic exam

eJWxGm0.title: Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy
eJWxGm0.description: A form of muscular dystrophy that manifests with contractures, humeroperoneal muscle weakness, and cardiac conditions (e.g., arrhythmias). Its inheritance pattern is variable. Onset is typically in the first or second decade of life.

UJWbtm0.title: Poncet disease
UJWbtm0.description: A form of reactive arthritis involving multiple large and small joints that can affect patients with active tuberculosis.

2JWTtm0.title: Pegcetacoplan
2JWTtm0.description: A drug that binds to complement protein C3 and regulates its cleavage into downstream effectors of complement activation. Used to treat paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria.

fJWktm0.title: Lasmiditan
fJWktm0.description: A highly selective 5-HT1F receptor agonist that is thought to decrease stimulation of the trigeminal system. Used to treat acute migraine headaches. Common adverse effects include dizziness, fatigue, paresthesia, and sedation.

TJW6tm0.title: Risankizumab
TJW6tm0.description: A monoclonal antibody that binds to IL-23, which prevents interaction with the IL-23 receptor and inhibits the release of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Used in the treatment of plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and inflammatory bowel disease.

gJWFtm0.title: Ilizarov apparatus
gJWFtm0.description: An orthopedic device that consists of metal rings, rods, and tensioned wires arranged circumferentially around a limb bone to lengthen or reshape the bone.

SJWytm0.title: Rutherford classification
SJWytm0.description: A classification system for peripheral artery disease. Grades the severity of acute limb ischemia on a spectrum from viable tissue to permanent tissue loss. Grades chronic limb ischemia on a spectrum from asymptomatic disease to permanent tissue loss.

hJWcFm0.title: Ollier disease
hJWcFm0.description: A rare syndrome characterized by the development of multiple enchondromas, typically in a unilateral distribution. Caused by mutations in the genes that encode isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH1, IDH2).

3JWSFm0.title: Maffucci syndrome
3JWSFm0.description: A rare syndrome characterized by the development of multiple enchondromas, deep venous malformations on the hands and feet, lymphatic malformations, spindle cell hemangiomas, and chondrosarcoma. Caused by mutations in the genes that encode isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH1, IDH2).

RJWlFm0.title: Bicytopenia
RJWlFm0.description: A decreased number of two types of blood cells (i.e., erythrocytes, leukocytes, platelets). Causes include megaloblastic anemia, immune thrombocytopenic purpura, and alcoholic liver disease.

iJWJFm0.title: Mefenamic acid
iJWJFm0.description: A reversible inhibitor of cyclooxygenase-1 and 2 that decreases the formation of prostaglandin precursors. Used as an analgesic (e.g., due to primary dysmenorrhea).

jJW_Fm0.title: Goal-directed IV fluid therapy
jJW_Fm0.description: Titration of intravenous fluid therapy to specific targets of perfusion, such as heart rate, mean arterial pressure, central venous pressure, urine output, BUN, and hematocrit. Used to help ensure adequate organ perfusion (e.g., in conditions associated with third-space fluid loss) while avoiding fluid overload and its complications (e.g., pulmonary edema, abdominal compartment syndrome).

lJWv8m0.title: Atypical syncope
lJWv8m0.description: A subtype of vasovagal syncope characterized by recurrent syncopal episodes without an identifiable underlying cause or trigger (e.g., emotional stress, painful stimuli, physical exertion).

NJW-8m0.title: Occupational therapy
NJW-8m0.description: A rehabilitative service that assists individuals with regaining or improving physical abilities that have been impaired by disease, injury, and/or disability, particularly within the person-environment interface. Examples of abilities that can be rehabilitated with occupational therapy include activities of daily living (e.g., bathing, dressing), functional mobility, and home maintenance.

mJWVum0.title: Pfannenstiel incision
mJWVum0.description: A type of incision technique used for Cesarean delivery. Involves a transverse, slightly curved incision of the lower anterior abdomen and noncontractile uterine fundus. Ideally, the incision should be placed 2–3 cm above the symphysis pubis.

5JWium0.title: Joel-Cohen incision
5JWium0.description: A type of incision technique used for Cesarean delivery. Involves a straight incision that is placed ~ 3 cm below the anterior superior iliac spine line.

MJWMum0.title: Sotrovimab
MJWMum0.description: A recombinant IgG1k monoclonal antibody that binds to the spike protein receptor-binding domain of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Prevents the spike protein-mediated binding and entry into human cells.

nJW7um0.title: Triglyceride synthesis
nJW7um0.description: The esterification of glycerol and three fatty acids into triglyceride, which occurs mainly in the liver and adipose tissue. Its rate-determining enzyme is glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase. Synthesized triglycerides are either stored in adipose tissue or transported to muscle for energy utilization.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Fatty acid metabolism

IJWYvm0.title: Atropine challenge test
IJWYvm0.description: A diagnostic test involving measuring the response to atropine administration. Used to support the diagnosis of cholinergic poisoning or differentiate between functional and intrinsic causes of bradyarrhythmias.

rJWfvm0.title: Sinus pause
rJWfvm0.description: An ECG finding in which the sinoatrial node depolarizes more than 3 seconds after the preceding atrial depolarization.

7JW4vm0.title: Wiggers diagram
7JW4vm0.description: A diagram that shows the relationships between left ventricular pressure, left ventricular volume, left atrial pressure, and aortic pressure during systole and diastole.

HJWKvm0.title: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
HJWKvm0.description: A group of conditions characterized by reversible cerebral arterial dilation and narrowing, which typically results in sudden, severe thunderclap headaches. Can also cause seizures and focal neurologic deficits. Neuroimaging typically shows smooth, tapered vessels with focally dilated segments.

sJWtvm0.title: Godet sign
sJWtvm0.description: A sign of soft tissue edema characterized by the persistence of indentation in the skin after application of pressure.

GJWBvm0.title: Sinus tarsi syndrome
GJWBvm0.description: A condition characterized by inflammation of the sinus tarsi, which can cause pain, swelling, and erythema. Caused by lateral ankle stress (e.g., from excessive pronation, which compresses soft tissues in the sinus tarsi).

tJWXDm0.title: Methocarbamol
tJWXDm0.description: A central nervous system depressant that causes skeletal muscle relaxation. Used to treat muscle spasm.

FJWgDm0.title: Belatacept
FJWgDm0.description: A drug that binds to CD80 and CD86 on antigen-presenting cells and blocks interaction with CD28, thereby inhibiting T-cell costimulation. Used for organ transplant (kidney, lung) rejection prophylaxis.

8JWODm0.title: Flexner-Wintersteiner rosette
8JWODm0.description: A histopathologic finding of retinoblastoma characterized by tumor cells that surround a central lumen composed of cytoplasmic extensions of the surrounding cells.

uJWpDm0.title: Stereopsis
uJWpDm0.description: The ability to perceive depth from visual stimuli received by both eyes (i.e., binocular vision).

vJWADm0.title: Sapovirus
vJWADm0.description: A virus of the Caliciviridae family that causes gastroenteritis. Transmission occurs via the fecal‑oral route. Clinically indistinguishable from norovirus infection.

DJW1wm0.title: Coitarche
DJW1wm0.description: The age at first sexual intercourse.

wJWhwm0.title: Fostamatinib
wJWhwm0.description: A spleen tyrosine kinase inhibitor that inhibits signal transduction of Fc-activating receptors and B-cell receptors, thereby reducing antibody-mediated destruction of platelets in individuals with immune thrombocytopenia.

9JWNwm0.title: Hailey-Hailey disease
9JWNwm0.description: An autosomal dominant condition caused by a mutation in the ATP2C1 gene, which encodes an ATPase involved in calcium signaling. Typically manifests with flaccid vesicles and bullae in intertriginous areas. These lesions rupture and leave erosions. Associated with pruritus and pain.

CJWqwm0.title: Vorapaxar
CJWqwm0.description: An antagonist of protease-activated receptor-1, which is found on platelets. Inhibits platelet aggregation and is used to reduce thrombotic cardiovascular events (e.g., myocardial infarction, stroke) in individuals who have a history of myocardial infarction and/or peripheral arterial disease.

xJWEwm0.title: CEAP classification of chronic venous disorders
xJWEwm0.description: A standardized system used to classify features of chronic venous disorders. The categories are: Clinical (e.g., manifestations of venous disease), Etiological (e.g., congenital, primary, secondary), Anatomical (e.g., superficial, perforating, deep veins), and Pathophysiological (e.g., due to reflux, obstruction).

BJWzwm0.title: CHEK2 gene
BJWzwm0.description: A tumor suppressor gene whose normal function involves regulation of the cell cycle. Mutations in the CHEK2 gene are associated with breast cancer, colorectal cancer, and thyroid cancer, among others.

yJWd9m0.title: Ergometrine
yJWd9m0.description: A uterine smooth muscle stimulant that results in sustained contractions. Used to shorten the third stage of labor. Not commercially available in the United States.

AJWR9m0.title: Abemaciclib
AJWR9m0.description: A cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitor that suppresses DNA replication and decreases tumor cell proliferation. Used in conjunction with endocrine therapy to treat breast cancer.

_JW59m0.title: Elamipretide
_JW59m0.description: A drug that binds to cardiolipin (a component of mitochondria) and protects it from oxidative damage. This drug was evaluated as a treatment for mitochondrial myopathy but failed to show clinically and statistically significant benefit.

zJWr9m0.title: Ibrexafungerp
zJWr9m0.description: A triterpenoid antifungal used to treat vulvovaginal candidiasis. Inhibits glucan synthase, which prevents the formation of 1,3-beta-D-glucan, a component of the fungal cell wall.

-JWD9m0.title: Ribociclib
-JWD9m0.description: A cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitor that suppresses DNA replication and decreases tumor cell proliferation. Used in conjunction with endocrine therapy to treat breast cancer.

ZqWZCm0.title: Pantoprazole
ZqWZCm0.description: A drug that irreversibly inhibits H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells, which leads to an increase in stomach pH and suppression of gastric acid secretion. Used to treat conditions caused by excessive gastroesophageal acidity (e.g., dyspepsia, gastroesophageal reflux disease).

0qWeCm0.title: Omeprazole
0qWeCm0.description: A drug that irreversibly inhibits H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells, which leads to an increase in stomach pH and suppression of gastric acid secretion. Used to treat conditions caused by excessive gastroesophageal acidity (e.g., dyspepsia, gastroesophageal reflux disease).

aqWQCm0.title: Daratumumab
aqWQCm0.description: A monoclonal anti-CD38 antibody used to treat multiple myeloma, usually as part of a drug regimen (e.g., in combination with bortezomib, lenalidomide, carfilzomib, or pomalidomide). Adverse effects include upper respiratory infection, neutropenia, and infusion-related reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis).

YqWnCm0.title: Aprotinin
YqWnCm0.description: A protein preparation isolated from bovine lung that inhibits proteases, including plasmin and kallikrein. As a result, it inhibits fibrinolysis and thrombin generation. Not available for commercial use in the United States due to an increased risk of mortality.

bqWHCm0.title: Yohimbe
bqWHCm0.description: A plant used in herbal medicine as a treatment for erectile dysfunction. Its bark contains the alkaloid yohimbine, which blocks presynaptic alpha-2-adrenergic receptors. Evidence of its efficacy is limited.

XqW9Cm0.title: Ginseng
XqW9Cm0.description: A plant used in herbal medicine with proposed properties that include glucose management, immune system enhancement, and antiinflammatory effects. Evidence of its efficacy is limited. Includes American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius) and Asian or Korean ginseng (Panax ginseng).

cqWaxm0.title: Menotropin
cqWaxm0.description: A preparation of follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone purified from the urine of postmenopausal women. Used to stimulate ovarian follicular growth and maturation (e.g., in individuals with primary ovarian failure). Also used to stimulate spermatogenesis.

1qW2xm0.title: Recombinant human follicle-stimulating hormone
1qW2xm0.description: A formulation of follicle-stimulating hormone derived from recombinant DNA. Used to stimulate the development of multiple follicles (e.g., for assisted reproduction), induce ovulation, and induce spermatogenesis.

WqWPxm0.title: Wunderlich syndrome
WqWPxm0.description: A rare condition characterized by spontaneous, acute-onset renal hemorrhage into the subcapsular and perirenal spaces. Classic manifestations are the Lenk triad: acute flank pain, the presence of a flank mass, and hypovolemic shock. Etiologies include neoplasms (e.g., angiomyolipoma) and vascular disorders (e.g., polyarteritis nodosa, renal artery aneurysms).

dqWoxm0.title: Acquired dysfibrinogenemia
dqWoxm0.description: An acquired coagulopathy characterized by dysfunctional fibrinogen, which results in easy bleeding. Etiologies include liver disease (e.g., hepatitis, cirrhosis), immune disorders, and multiple myeloma.

VqWGxm0.title: Myelomatous meningitis
VqWGxm0.description: A rare complication of multiple myeloma characterized by the infiltration of tumor cells in the meninges. Manifestations include cranial nerve deficits, encephalopathy, radiculopathy, cauda equina syndrome.

eqWxxm0.title: Polymicrogyria
eqWxxm0.description: A developmental abnormality in which the brain has multiple small gyri, which results in excessive folding and a thickened cortex. Can result in developmental delay, seizures, and other neurologic abnormalities.

UqWbBm0.title: Isochromosome
UqWbBm0.description: A structural chromosomal abnormality in which there are two copies of the same arm of a chromosome (e.g., deletion of the short arm with replacement with a copy of the long arm). Isochromosome Xq can cause Turner syndrome.

2qWTBm0.title: Sodium metabisulfite test
2qWTBm0.description: A diagnostic test for sickle cell disorders in which sodium metabisulfite, a deoxygenating agent, is added to a sample of blood. The sample is then assessed for sickling. This test has largely been replaced by the use of high performance liquid chromatography.

fqWkBm0.title: Allotype (immunology)
fqWkBm0.description: A structural variation within the polypeptide chain of an immunoglobulin. Allotypes can exist within a specific immunoglobulin isotype (e.g., polymorphisms within the IgG isotype). Allotype differences can potentiate immunogenicity.

TqW6Bm0.title: Pellegrini–Stieda syndrome
TqW6Bm0.description: A condition characterized by focal medial knee pain as a result of chronic injury and/or insufficiency of the medial collateral ligament of the knee. Typically manifests with crescent-shaped calcifications near the medial femoral condyle (Pellegrini-Stieda lesions).

gqWFBm0.title: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
gqWFBm0.description: An aggressive, malignant brainstem tumor that most commonly develops in young children (median age 5-9 years). Can cause hydrocephalus, cranial nerve palsies, ataxia, and/or brain hemorrhage.

SqWyBm0.title: Haploinsufficiency
SqWyBm0.description: A state in which a diploid organism has only a single copy of a particular allele, which is insufficient to produce its specified phenotype. Can result from a loss-of-function mutation.

hqWcym0.title: Retrograde ejaculation
hqWcym0.description: A condition in which semen enters the bladder (via retrograde flow) instead of exiting through the urethral meatus. Can occur as a result of injury to the bladder neck sphincter or due to failure of bladder neck closure during ejaculation (e.g., in patients with peripheral neuropathy due to diabetes mellitus). Can result in infertility.

RqWlym0.title: Ontario Family History Assessment Tool
RqWlym0.description: A standardized questionnaire used to evaluate patients with a personal or family history of BRCA mutation-associated cancer (e.g., breast cancer, ovarian cancer). Helps guide the decision of whether a patient needs referral for genetic counseling.

PqWWAm0.title: Terminal-stage hepatocellular carcinoma
PqWWAm0.description: The presence of advanced liver cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C) or a severely reduced performance status (ECOG 3-4) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma, regardless of tumor burden or the presence of metastases.

4qW3Am0.title: Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein
4qW3Am0.description: A globulin normally produced by fetal endodermal tissues with unclear function (possibly similar to albumin). Physiologically enters maternal circulation and can be used for prenatal testing; increased MSAFP is associated with fetal anomalities (e.g., neural tube defects, abdominal wall defects).

kqWmAm0.title: Geriatric Depression Scale-15
kqWmAm0.description: A self-reported questionnaire with a yes/no format that measures depression in older adults. Comprises 15 items, 10 of which indicate depression if the answer is yes, the other 5 of which indicate depression if the answer is no. The questionnaire takes approximately 5 to 7 minutes to complete and is thus manageable for people with limited energy or cognitive issues.

destinations.label: Major depressive disorder → Special patient groups

OqWIAm0.title: Complement component 1q deficiency
OqWIAm0.description: An inherited condition characterized by absent or abnormal C1q protein. Manifestations include recurrent skin lesions, cataracts, hair loss, and increased susceptibility to infections. Strongly associated with systemic lupus erythematosus and renal disease (especially mesangial proliferative glomerulonephritis).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital complement deficiencies

lqWvAm0.title: Complement component 1r deficiency
lqWvAm0.description: A rare inherited condition characterized by a decreased serum C1r protein concentration. This deficiency results in the inability to form the C1 complex, disrupting the classical pathway cascade and increasing the risk of developing recurrent infections. Strongly associated with systemic lupus erythematosus.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital complement deficiencies

NqW-Am0.title: Complement component 1s deficiency
NqW-Am0.description: A rare inherited condition characterized by a decreased serum C1s protein concentration. This deficiency results in the inability to form the C1 complex, disrupting the classical pathway cascade and increasing the risk of developing recurrent infections. Strongly associated with systemic lupus erythematosus.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital complement deficiencies

mqWV_m0.title: Pomalidomide
