mqWV_m0.description: An immunomodulatory drug that induces cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, enhances T cell and NK cell cytotoxicity, and inhibits the production of proinflammatory cytokines. Used to treat multiple myeloma.

5qWi_m0.title: Complement component 4 deficiency
5qWi_m0.description: An inherited condition characterized by decreased production or complete absence of C4 protein due a mutation in either the C4A or C4B gene. This deficiency results in the inability to activate the classical complement cascade, increasing the risk of developing recurrent infections. Strongly associated with systemic lupus erythematosus.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital complement deficiencies

MqWM_m0.title: Mannose-binding lectin deficiency
MqWM_m0.description: An inherited condition characterized by low levels of mannose-binding lectin. Thought to increase susceptibility to infections, particularly in individuals with weaker immune systems (e.g., infants, individuals who are immunosuppressed).

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital complement deficiencies

nqW7_m0.title: Friable cervix
nqW7_m0.description: A physical examination finding of a cervix that bleeds easily even with mild contact. Typically seen on vaginal speculum examination in patients with cervicitis and/or pelvic inflammatory disease.

LqWw_m0.title: Hemicholinium-3
LqWw_m0.description: A drug that blocks the presynaptic reuptake of choline, which results in decreased acetylcholine synthesis. Used as a research tool (e.g., in animal and in vitro studies).

oqW0zm0.title: Voxelotor
oqW0zm0.description: A drug that reversibly binds to hemoglobin and stabilizes its oxygenated state, which inhibits hemoglobin S polymerization in individuals with sickle cell disease.

KqWUzm0.title: Kirby-Bauer test
KqWUzm0.description: A laboratory technique used to identify antibiotic susceptibility. Culture media are inoculated with a specific organism. Discs that contain a specific concentration of antibiotic are placed on the media, and the extent of the resulting zone of inhibition is used to determine antibiotic susceptibility.

6qWjzm0.title: Urethrorrhagia
6qWjzm0.description: A condition of bleeding from the urethra, which typically manifests with the passage of blood from the urethral meatus at the end of urination.

pqWLzm0.title: Timothy syndrome
pqWLzm0.description: A congenital syndrome characterized by a prolonged QT interval (which increases the risk of developing cardiac arrhythmias), cardiac muscle hypertrophy, syndactyly, dysmorphic facial features, and development delay. Caused by a mutation in the CACNA1C gene, which encodes calcium channels on several types of cells.

JqWszm0.title: Trichobezoar
JqWszm0.description: A gastrointestinal foreign body composed of accumulated ingested hair. Can cause gastrointestinal obstruction.

qqWCzm0.title: Ameloblastoma
qqWCzm0.description: A tumor of odontogenic epithelium that most commonly develops in the lower jaw. Can be locally invasive and destructive to tissue around the jaw, sinuses, and orbits.

IqWY-m0.title: Bullectomy
IqWY-m0.description: The surgical removal of nonfunctional air sacs in the lung (bullae or blebs). Typically performed to increase the amount of space available for lung expansion (e.g., in patients with emphysema).

rqWf-m0.title: Bipartite patella
rqWf-m0.description: A patellar defect characterized by failure of fusion of an accessory ossification center. Usually asymptomatic but can result in anterior knee pain, especially after trauma or overuse.

7qW4-m0.title: Pellegrini-Stieda lesion
7qW4-m0.description: A radiologic finding of ossifications at sites of prior trauma near the medial collateral ligament of the knee. Often crescent-shaped. Most patients with these lesions are asymptomatic, but some can develop medial knee pain (Pellegrini-Stieda syndrome).

HqWK-m0.title: Hyperprosexia
HqWK-m0.description: A fixation of one's attention on a specific idea or stimulus. Typically results in the exclusion of other stimuli. Can be seen in compulsive disorders.

sqWt-m0.title: Hypoprosexia
sqWt-m0.description: A lack of ability to hold one's attention.

GqWB-m0.title: Dolichostenomelia
GqWB-m0.description: The presence of abnormally long limbs (relative to the length of the trunk). Can be seen in individuals with Marfan syndrome.

tqWXZ50.title: Denticulate ligament
tqWXZ50.description: A ligamentous extension of the pia mater that stabilizes the spinal cord within the vertebral canal by anchoring it to the dura mater.

FqWgZ50.title: Hofbauer cell
FqWgZ50.description: A fetally-derived macrophage found in placental villi. Thought to play a role in placental morphogenesis (e.g., angiogenesis) and homeostasis (e.g., vasoregulation).

8qWOZ50.title: Joubert syndrome
8qWOZ50.description: An autosomal recessive condition characterized by underdevelopment of the cerebellar vermis. Manifestations include gross motor milestone delay, ataxia, hyperpnea, and low muscle tone.

uqWpZ50.title: Calsequestrin
uqWpZ50.description: A calcium-binding protein that serves as a calcium buffer and reservoir within the sarcoplasmic reticulum of cardiac myocytes, where it binds to the ryanodine receptor. Mutations in the calsequestrin 2 gene (CASQ2 gene) can cause catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.

EqW8Z50.title: Prekallikrein
EqW8Z50.description: A precursor molecule that forms kallikrein, a serine protease, when cleaved by activated Factor XII.

vqWAZ50.title: Prekallikrein deficiency
vqWAZ50.description: A rare inherited condition characterized by decreased or absent production of prekallikrein, which is the precursor of kallikrein, a serine protease. Associated with a prolonged partial thromboplastin time and normal prothrombin and thrombin times. Not associated with clinical bleeding.

DqW1050.title: Kinetoplast
DqW1050.description: A mitochondrial DNA-constaining organelle found in many flagellated protists, including Leishmania and Trypanosoma species. Appearas as a rod-shaped structure perpendicular to the amastigote nucleus on peripheral blood smear.

wqWh050.title: Psoas syndrome
wqWh050.description: Dysfunction or injury of the iliopsoas muscle caused by overuse, trauma, or prolonged hip flexion that manifests with lower back pain that may radiate down the leg or to the groin. The Thomas test for testing iliopsoas hypertonicity will be positive.

9qWN050.title: Mansonella
9qWN050.description: A filarial nematode genus whose primary vectors are midges (genus Culicoides) and black flies. Species within this genus that cause human infection (mansonellosis) include M. ozzardi (endemic to Central and South America), M. perstans (endemic to Africa), and M. streptocerca (endemic to Africa).

CqWq050.title: Mansonellosis
CqWq050.description: A filarial disease caused by Mansonella species. Most infections are asymptomatic. Symptomatic manifestations include fever, headache, rash, pericarditis, pleuritis, and arthralgia. Symptoms are related to migration of the adult worms.

xqWE050.title: Dercum disease
xqWE050.description: A rare connective tissue disease characterized by the development of painful lipomas. These lipomas can develop in subcutaneous tissue or in deeper tissue (e.g., in close proximity to muscle or bone).

BqWz050.title: Pseudoesotropia
BqWz050.description: A type of pseudostrabismus characterized by the appearance of eye crossing (i.e., strabismus) as a result of a wide nasal bridge and/or large epicanthal folds. Most commonly occurs in infants and young children. More prominent with lateral gaze.

yqWda50.title: Mucopolysaccharidosis type III
yqWda50.description: A autosomal recessive condition characterized by mutations in the genes that encode enzymes that process heparan sulfate. Manifestations include developmental delay (usually apparent by 2-5 years of age), behavioral disturbances (e.g., hyperactivity, irritability), hirsutism, hearing loss, and visual impairment.

AqWRa50.title: Irukandji syndrome
AqWRa50.description: A condition caused by envenomation from certain box jellyfish species. Manifestations include tachycardia, diaphoresis, severe and generalized pain, hypertension, and vomiting. Can result in potentially life-threatening cardiac complications.

_qW5a50.title: Dohle body
_qW5a50.description: A blue cytoplasmic inclusion formed by remnants of rough endoplasmic reticulum that can be seen in neutrophils on peripheral blood smear. Associated with infectious and inflammatory disease.

zqWra50.title: Holoenzyme
zqWra50.description: The active form of an enzyme (e.g., the combination of an apoenzyme and its required bound cofactor).

-qWDa50.title: Epidermodysplasia verruciformis
-qWDa50.description: A rare, autosomal recessive skin disorder characterized by selective immunodeficiency that results in infection by human papillomaviruses. Manifests with multiple verrucous (wart-like) skin lesions in infancy or early childhood. Results in early development of actinic keratoses and cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas.

ZIWZY50.title: Azaspiracid poisoning
ZIWZY50.description: A condition caused by the consumption of a marine algal toxin (azaspiracid) that can accumulate in shellfish species. Causes self-limited gastrointestinal illness (e.g., nausea, vomiting, diarrhea).

0IWeY50.title: Phelan-McDermid syndrome
0IWeY50.description: A rare inherited syndrome characterized by hypotonia, developmental delay, and an impaired ability to feel pain and sweat. Caused by a mutation or delete of the SHANK3 gene on chromosome 22.

aIWQY50.title: Nemaline myopathy
aIWQY50.description: A rare inherited muscle disorder characterized by muscle weakness and threadlike structures (nemaline bodies) on muscle biopsy. Manifestations are variable, ranging from profound generalized weakness in infancy to mild focal weakness in adulthood.

YIWnY50.title: Terminal web
YIWnY50.description: A filamentous area found on the apical surface of microvilli-containing epithelial cells. Contraction of the terminal web spreads out microvilli to aid in absorption.

bIWHY50.title: Asymmetric septal hypertrophy
bIWHY50.description: A cardiac finding characterized echocardiographically by an interventricular septum to left ventricular free wall thickness ratio ≥ 1.3. Most commonly seen in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

XIW9Y50.title: Lutembacher syndrome
XIW9Y50.description: A rare type of heart disease characterized by an atrial septal defect in combination with mitral stenosis. These findings can be congenital or acquired.

cIWab50.title: Umeclidinium
cIWab50.description: A reversible inhibitor of muscarinic M3 receptors that acts on bronchial smooth muscle, resulting in bronchodilation.

1IW2b50.title: Riociguat
1IW2b50.description: A drug that directly stimulates soluble guanylate cyclase and stabilizes its binding to nitric oxide. Results in increased formation of cGMP and vasodilation. Used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension.

WIWPb50.title: Lipoid proteinosis
WIWPb50.description: A rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by the deposition of collagenous material in the skin and soft tissues. Caused by a mutation in the ECM1 gene. Manifestations include waxy papules on the face, hyperkeratotic plaques at sites of trauma, and ankyloglossia.

dIWob50.title: Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma
dIWob50.description: A rare, slow-growing type of astrocytoma characterized histologically by pleomorphic cells, reticulin deposition, and eosinophilic granular bodies. Most commonly forms in the temporal lobe.

VIWGb50.title: Somniloquy
VIWGb50.description: A parasomnia characterized by speaking while in a state of sleep.

eIWxb50.title: Kingella kingae
eIWxb50.description: A Gram-negative colonizer of the oropharynx that can cause bloodstream, joint, and bone infections, most commonly in children.

UIWbX50.title: Hydranencephaly
UIWbX50.description: A congenital condition characterized by the absence of the cerebral hemispheres and the presence of cerebrospinal fluid within the cranial cavity.

2IWTX50.title: Fesoterodine
2IWTX50.description: A prodrug of 5-hydroxymethyl tolterodine, which acts as a competitive antagonist of muscarinic receptors. Used to treat overactive bladder in adults, including urgency urinary incontinence, and neurogenic detrusor overactivity in children.

destinations.label: Overactive bladder and urgency urinary incontinence → Treatment

fIWkX50.title: X-linked lymphoproliferative disease
fIWkX50.description: A rare immunodeficiency disorder characterized by immune dysregulation after Epstein-Barr virus infection. Manifestations include fulminant infectious mononucleosis (often complicated by hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis), dysgammaglobulinemia, and lymphoma.

gIWFX50.title: Primary psychosis
gIWFX50.description: A distorted perception of reality characterized by delusions, hallucinations, and/or disorganized behavior that is caused by an underlying psychiatric disorder, e.g., schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder.

3IWSc50.title: Trabecular bone score
3IWSc50.description: An indirect measure of bone architecture derived from dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) images of the lumbar spine. A high trabecular bone score is associated with a low risk of fracture, while a low score reflects a higher fracture risk.

RIWlc50.title: Systems approach
RIWlc50.description: A patient safety approach in health care that aims to identify sources of medical errors and introduce measures to prevent these errors in a system (e.g., a hospital, a single department) rather than at the level of the individual.

iIWJc50.title: Monkeypox virus
iIWJc50.description: A double-stranded DNA virus of the orthopoxvirus genus that belongs to the family of Poxviridae. Endemic in Central and Western Africa. Transmission can occur via contact of contaminated material with broken skin or mucus membranes and inhalation. Infection causes monkeypox, a smallpox-like illness.

QIWuc50.title: Mpox
QIWuc50.description: A rare, smallpox-like condition caused by monkeypox virus infection. Manifestations include flu-like symptoms, lymphadenopathy, and a painful, blistering rash that usually appears within 1 to 3 days after the onset of fever.

OIWI150.title: Choledochoduodenal fistula
OIWI150.description: An abnormal connection between the common bile duct and the duodenum.

mIWVW50.title: Apoenzyme
mIWVW50.description: A type of enzyme that requires a cofactor but is not bound by one. Binding of the required cofactor results in the formation of the active enzyme (holoenzyme).

LIWwW50.title: Reducible hernia
LIWwW50.description: A type of hernia in which the contents of the hernial sac can return back through the abdominal wall defect into the peritoneal cavity, either spontaneously or with the application of gentle external pressure.

JIWsd50.title: Double-lumen endotracheal tube
JIWsd50.description: An endotracheal tube with two lumens that allow for isolation and independent ventilation of the right and left lungs. Double-lumen endotracheal tubes may be used to isolate a functioning lung from blood or secretions produced by lung disease or to provide differential ventilation if lungs are asymmetrically affected.

IIWYV50.title: Ethyl glucuronide
IIWYV50.description: A metabolite of alcohol that is used as a biomarker of alcohol consumption. Present for ≤ 5 days following the consumption of alcohol in urine samples, and for approx. 3 months in hair samples. False positive results are possible in patients with urinary tract infections and/or exposure to mouthwash, hand sanitizer, yeast, or overripe fruits (all of which may contain low levels of alcohol).

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Confirmation of alcohol use

rIWfV50.title: American Sign Language
rIWfV50.description: A natural language that uses hand movements and facial expressions. Used in deaf and hearing impaired communities in the majority of the United States and English-speaking Canada.

7IW4V50.title: Speechreading
7IW4V50.description: The observation and interpretation of nonauditory clues (e.g., lip movements, hand gestures, facial expressions) to understand what a speaker is saying.

HIWKV50.title: Waist circumference
HIWKV50.description: A clinical measurement used to estimate abdominal (visceral) fat. Following exhalation, the waist is measured at the level of the top of the iliac crest. A circumference ≥ 102 cm in men and ≥ 88 cm in women (adults of Asian descent: ≥ 90 cm and ≥ 80 cm, respectively) is consistent with abdominal obesity. Higher waist circumferences are associated with an increased risk for cardiometabolic disease, irrespective of BMI.

destinations.label: Principles of nutrition → Diagnostic tools for assessing healthy weight and body mass

GIWBV50.title: Moderately severe acute pancreatitis
GIWBV50.description: A subtype of pancreatitis (Atlanta grade) characterized by acute pancreatitis with the presence of transient organ failure (< 48 hours) and/or local or systemic complications.

destinations.label: Acute pancreatitis → Severity grading and prognostic scores

tIWXe50.title: Mild acute pancreatitis
tIWXe50.description: A subtype of pancreatitis (Atlanta grade) characterized by acute pancreatitis without organ failure, local complications, or systemic complications.

destinations.label: Acute pancreatitis → Severity grading and prognostic scores

8IWOe50.title: Screening, brief intervention, and referral to treatment
8IWOe50.description: A screening tool used for the early identification of individuals at risk for, or experiencing, substance use or mental health disorders. Following screening, a brief intervention to increase patient awareness is carried out followed by referral onward for specialist treatment if necessary.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Counseling on substance use disorders

wIWhU50.title: BAE
wIWhU50.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Bronchial artery embolization
2. Barium enema
3. Biatrial enlargement

yIWd250.title: Suprapubic aspiration
yIWd250.description: A procedure for obtaining a sterile urine sample by percutaneously inserting a needle through the abdominal wall and into the bladder.

AIWR250.title: Madelung deformity
AIWR250.description: A condition characterized by abnormal growth of the radius, which leads to bowing of the radial shaft and misalignment where the radius and ulna meet the bones of the wrist. Manifestations include wrist pain and impaired wrist range of motion.

_IW5250.title: ALDH2 gene
_IW5250.description: A gene that encodes the mitochondrial isoform of aldehyde dehydrogenase, an enzyme that breaks down acetaldehyde (e.g., in the metabolism of alcohol).

zIWr250.title: ALDH2 deficiency
zIWr250.description: A genetic deficiency in which acetaldehyde is insufficiently metabolized. Can lead to flushing, urticaria, and/or respiratory symptoms after consuming alcohol.

ZrWZf50.title: Aldehyde dehydrogenase
ZrWZf50.description: An enzyme that breaks down acetaldehyde (e.g., in the metabolism of alcohol). Exists in two isoforms: a catalytically inactive cytosolic isozyme and a catalytically active mitochondrial isozyme.

0rWef50.title: Phosphorus
0rWef50.description: An essential element found in the structure of organic material (e.g., DNA, RNA, cell membranes, bones) and critical for the production and storage of energy (e.g., adenosine triphosphate).

arWQf50.title: Sodium
arWQf50.description: The most abundant extracellular mineral. Involved in cellular electrolyte balance, fluid balance, cellular membrane transport, muscle contraction, and neuronal firing.

YrWnf50.title: Calcium
YrWnf50.description: An essential element. As an electrolyte (Ca⁺²), it is involved in signaling pathways, neuromuscular function, and muscle contraction. Calcium apatite forms a significant portion of bone mineral.

brWHf50.title: Potassium
brWHf50.description: The most abundant intracellular mineral. Involved in cellular electrolyte balance, fluid balance, cellular membrane transport, and pH balance.

1rW2T50.title: Hum test
1rW2T50.description: A test used as an alternative to the Weber test to differentiate between conductive hearing loss and sensorineural hearing loss. The patient is asked to hum; if the hum is heard louder in one ear, the patient is likely to have conductive hearing loss in that ear.

WrWPT50.title: Wood unit
WrWPT50.description: A simplified measurement of vascular resistance with units in mm Hg/liter per minute.

erWxT50.title: Surveillance (public health)
erWxT50.description: The collection, analysis, and interpretation of health-related data required for the planning and evaluation of public health interventions.

UrWbg50.title: Fibrosis-4 score
UrWbg50.description: A score used to estimate the risk of advanced liver fibrosis in patients with MASLD or chronic hepatitis B or C. Parameters include age, ALT, AST, and platelet count.

media.title: FIB-4 for Noninvasive Diagnosis of Hepatic Fibrosis

2rWTg50.title: Racecadotril
2rWTg50.description: An antidiarrheal agent that reduces hypersecretion of electrolytes and water into the intestinal lumen by inhibiting the degradation of endogenous opioids (enkephalins). Used in the treatment of acute diarrhea.

frWkg50.title: Whole School, Whole Community, Whole Child
frWkg50.description: A student-centered framework developed by the CDC for addressing health in schools.

grWFg50.title: Health advocacy
grWFg50.description: The promotion of public health through collaboration with community stakeholders and engagement with policymakers

SrWyg50.title: Avulsion injury
SrWyg50.description: The traumatic shearing of tissues from their anatomic attachments. Avulsion injuries of the skin and subcutaneous fat range from the detachment of small skin flaps to the complete degloving of an extremity, while those involving tendons range from tendon tears to complete ruptures with or without avulsion fractures of fragments of bone attached to tendinous insertion sites.

hrWcS50.title: Harm reduction strategies
hrWcS50.description: A set of strategies and policies to reduce the health risks resulting from activities such as substance use or sex work. Examples include needle exchange programs and safe sex counseling and materials.

QrWuS50.title: Darier disease
QrWuS50.description: An autosomal dominant condition caused by a mutation in the ATP2A2 gene, which encodes SERCA2 (a calcium-ATPase pump). Typically manifests in the second decade of life with hyperkeratotic papules on the chest, which can be pruritic or painful. Associated with palmoplantar pits, red and white nails (candy cane nails), and cobblestoning of the oral mucosa.

PrWWh50.title: Lenk triad
PrWWh50.description: A collection of manifestations associated with Wunderlich syndrome. Consists of acute flank pain, the presence of a flank mass, and hypovolemic shock.

4rW3h50.title: Oligometastatic disease
4rW3h50.description: An intermediate state between localized and disseminated malignant disease. In some cases, oligometastatic disease may be treated with curative intent; this involves radical local treatment of the primary tumor and the metastatic lesions.

krWmh50.title: Hypoperfusion
krWmh50.description: A reduction in blood flow to an organ, resulting in impaired function, e.g., reduced cognition with cerebral hypoperfusion. Hypoperfusion is commonly caused by hypotension but may also be present with normal systemic blood pressure.

OrWIh50.title: Elephantiasis
OrWIh50.description: A condition of severe lymphedema (most commonly of the arms or legs). Etiologies include congenital lymphedema and lymphedema secondary to infection (e.g., filariasis), surgery, and trauma. Can result in chronic cutaneous changes (i.e., elephantiasis nostras verrucosa).

lrWvh50.title: C-D-xylose breath test
lrWvh50.description: A breath test used for the diagnosis of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth and/or carbohydrate malabsorption.  Bacteria in the gut metabolize ingested C14-labeled D-xylose into C14-labeled CO₂, which is exhaled by the patient and measured. Elevated levels of C14-labeled CO₂ indicate SIBO or carbohydrate malabsorption.

nrW7350.title: Perchlorate
nrW7350.description: An inorganic anion that inhibits the activity of the sodium-iodide symporter of the basolateral membrane of thyroid cells, thereby decreasing the active transport of iodine. Previously used to treat hyperthyroidism but is no longer commercially available in the United States. Use is associated with a high risk of developing aplastic anemia and nephrotic syndrome.

LrWw350.title: Ask Suicide-Screening Questions suicide risk screening tool
LrWw350.description: A screening tool used to identify individuals at risk of suicide. Includes four questions on recent wishes to be dead, thoughts about being better off dead, thoughts about suicide, and past suicide attempts. Patients reporting any of these should be asked about current thoughts of suicide.

KrWUR50.title: Dentalgia
KrWUR50.description: A symptom of dental pain (e.g., from tooth decay or injury).

6rWjR50.title: Doorknob statement
6rWjR50.description: A comment or concern expressed by a patient at the end of a visit (e.g., when the physician is about to place their hand on the doorknob to leave the examination room), which is often of high relevance or urgency. Can be avoided by soliciting all items on the patient's agenda at the beginning of the interview.

prWLR50.title: Leading question
prWLR50.description: A question that directs the respondent to a specific, predetermined answer (e.g., "you've never missed a dose of your medication, right?"). Can lead to inaccurate responses and should be avoided.

GrWBi50.title: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
GrWBi50.description: A malignancy that arises from the squamous cells of the mucosal epithelium in the nasal cavity, paranasal sinuses, oral cavity, pharynx, larynx, or trachea. Clinical features depend on the site and etiology of the primary tumor.

9rWNj50.title: Expanded access
9rWNj50.description: An FDA program that grants use of an investigational drug or medical device for the treatment of a serious condition for which there is no comparable or satisfactory alternative treatment available.

CrWqj50.title: Complement component deficiencies
CrWqj50.description: A group of rare inherited conditions characterized by absent or abnormal complement component proteins, which increases the risk of recurrent bacterial infections and autoimmune conditions.

destinations.label: Congenital immunodeficiency disorders → Congenital complement deficiencies

Z7WZ450.title: West Haven criteria
Z7WZ450.description: A system used to determine the severity of hepatic encephalopathy based on clinical findings (e.g., altered mental status, asterixis, disorientation). Hepatic encephalopathy can be classified as minimal hepatic encephalopathy or assigned a grade from I to IV.

a7WQ450.title: Gastric rugae
a7WQ450.description: The ridges of the gastric wall formed by the mucosa and submucosa. Contraction of the muscles in the wall results in folding and coiling. Relaxation facilitates distention of the stomach (e.g., to accommodate food boluses). Various conditions can affect the morphology of the gastric rugae; gastritis can cause thickening of the rugae, and Menetrier disease can result in tortuosities and a cobblestone or cerebriform appearance in the gastric fundus and body.

b7WH450.title: Elephantiasis nostras verrucosa
b7WH450.description: A complication of chronic lymphedema characterized by sclerotic thickening of the skin, which results in hyperkeratotic and verrucous papules and plaques with a cobblestone appearance.

X7W9450.title: Closed comedone
X7W9450.description: A comedone with no apparent follicular opening or surrounding erythema. Contains sebum and unoxidized keratinaceous debris.

c7Wak50.title: Open comedone
c7Wak50.description: A comedone with a dilated follicular opening and a core of dark, dry, oxidized keratinaceous debris.

W7WPk50.title: Testicular sperm extraction
W7WPk50.description: A procedure in which an incision is made in the testis, the seminiferous tubule is examined for sperm, and sperm is collected (e.g., for intracytoplasmic sperm injection). Commonly performed in patients with nonobstructive azoospermia (i.e., sperm present in the testis but not in the ejaculate).

S7WyO50.title: Milkmaid grip
S7WyO50.description: A physical examination finding characterized by the inability to maintain muscle contraction in the hands. The patient is asked to grip the examiner's fingers. Intermittent loss of contraction results in alternating squeeze and release of grip ("milking"). Can be seen in Sydenham chorea.

37WSl50.title: Visual field testing
37WSl50.description: A part of the eye examination that evaluates both central and peripheral vision to identify potential visual deficits. Can be conducted using various techniques (both with and without instrumentation), such as confrontation visual field testing and automated perimetry.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Visual field examination

R7Wll50.title: Katz index of independence in activities of daily living
R7Wll50.description: A tool used to assess independence in performing six standard activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring, continence, and eating). One point is given for each activity patients are able to perform independently. Classification of function ranges from full (score of 6) to severely impaired (score ≤ 2).

Q7Wul50.title: Visual Function-14
Q7Wul50.description: An 18-item questionnaire used to assess the degree of functional impairment experienced by patients with cataracts and other eye disorders. Patients are asked to report, on a scale from 0 (unable to do) to 4 (no difficulties performing activity), how much difficulty they have with activities such as reading, watching TV, and driving. Scores are added together to calculate the severity of the patient's impairment and suitability for interventions such as surgery.

j7W_l50.title: Lawton instrumental activities of daily living scale
j7W_l50.description: A tool used to assess independence in performing eight standard instrumental activities of daily living (grocery shopping, managing transportation, using the telephone, preparing meals, housekeeping, managing finances, doing laundry, managing medication). One point is given for each activity patients are able to perform relatively independently. Scores range from 8 (high function, independent) to 0 (low function, dependent).

P7WWN50.title: Frailty
P7WWN50.description: A geriatric syndrome that encompasses variable impairments in multiple domains (e.g., mobility, strength, cognition, nutrition, and physical activity) and that increases the risk for morbidity and mortality. Frailty can be evaluated using various clinical tools, such as the Canadian Study of Health and Aging Clinical Frailty Scale.

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Screening for geriatric syndromes

k7WmN50.title: Glare testing
k7WmN50.description: An assessment of visual acuity performed in bright light. Patients with cataracts experience light scattering that worsens visual acuity compared to when acuity is assessed without bright light.

l7WvN50.title: Tracheal injury
l7WvN50.description: A potentially life-threatening injury to the tracheobronchial tree. Common causes include medical procedures, caustic inhalation, and blunt or penetrating trauma.

57Wim50.title: Adrenal hyperplasia
57Wim50.description: The idiopathic enlargement of adrenal gland tissue with associated hormone overproduction. Most commonly occurs bilaterally and manifests with increased serum concentrations of adrenal hormones. Can result in hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome) and hypercortisolism (Cushing syndrome).

L7Wwm50.title: Acute kidney injury stage 1
L7Wwm50.description: A sudden increase in serum creatinine by ≥ 0.3 mg/dL (26.5 mcmol/L) or 1.5–1.9 times baseline OR a decrease in urine output to < 0.5 mL/kg/hour for 6-12 hours.

o7W0550.title: Acute kidney injury stage 2
o7W0550.description: A sudden increase in serum creatinine by 2.0–2.9 times baseline OR a decrease in urine output to < 0.5 mL/kg/hour for ≥ 12 hours.

K7WU550.title: Acute kidney injury stage 3
K7WU550.description: An increase in serum creatinine to ≥ 4 mg/dL (354 mcmol/L) or by ≥ 3 times baseline, OR anuria for ≥ 12 hours, OR a decrease in urine output to < 0.3 mL/kg/hour for ≥ 24 hours, OR any acute kidney injury requiring renal replacement therapy. In patients < 18 years of age, AKI stage 3 is defined a decrease in eGFR to < 35 mL/min/1.73 m².

67Wj550.title: Pes anserine bursitis
67Wj550.description: Inflammation of the anserine bursa. May manifest with tenderness and/or swelling over the pes anserinus insertion.

destinations.label: Collection of orthopedic conditions → Pes anserinus pain syndrome

p7WL550.title: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction
p7WL550.description: A group of rare but potentially life-threatening type IV hypersensitivity reactions that includes acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP), drug reaction with eosinophilia with systemic symptoms (DRESS), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN).

destinations.label: Drug hypersensitivity reactions → Subtypes and variants

s7WtM50.title: Infectious gastroenteritis
s7WtM50.description: Inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract due to an infectious agent (viruses; less commonly, bacteria, parasites, fungi). The typical presentation includes acute diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain.

F7Wgn50.title: Cochlear symptoms
F7Wgn50.description: The auditory (rather than vestibular) manifestations of vestibulocochlear nerve dysfunction. Symptoms include sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus.

87WOn50.title: Metastasectomy
87WOn50.description: The surgical removal of one or more metastases.

E7W8n50.title: Palmar hyperlinearity
E7W8n50.description: The presence of multiple creases and lines on the palms and soles. Associated with atopic dermatitis and ichthyosis.

w7WhL50.title: Sleep inertia
w7WhL50.description: A physiologic transition state between sleeping and waking that is characterized by drowsiness, disorientation, a desire to return to sleep, and impaired cognitive, motor, and sensory performance. Can last from minutes to several hours.

97WNL50.title: Abscess incision and drainage
97WNL50.description: A procedure used to treat skin and soft tissue abscesses in which an incision is made into the overlying tissue to facilitate pus drainage.

A7WRo50.title: Automated translation software
A7WRo50.description: A software program that automatically translates text or speech from one language to another. May be used in a medical context for interpretation and communication of medical information but often requires editing to verify correctness and precision.

_7W5o50.title: Lower limit of normal
_7W5o50.description: A cutoff at the lower extreme of the reference range (5th percentile) of the target population.

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Measures of dispersion

z7Wro50.title: Deprescribing
z7Wro50.description: The process of systematically identifying and discontinuing inappropriate medications (e.g., those no longer needed, or for which actual or potential harms outweigh benefits), taking into account the patient's preferences, values, and therapy goals.

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Management of existing medications

0HWeK50.title: Energy expenditure
0HWeK50.description: The amount of energy the body requires to maintain essential metabolic processes including circulation and respiration and to provide energy during physical activity.

cHWa650.title: Defense Health Agency
cHWa650.description: A combat support agency that was established in 2013 to provide integrated and efficient health services to the military. Services include developing health information technology systems, providing pharmacy and medical logistics, performing medical research, and operating TRICARE health benefits.

destinations.label: Military medicine → Health care in the military

2HWTp50.title: Complicated parapneumonic effusion
2HWTp50.description: A type of pleural effusion that is complicated by infection. Typically arises from pneumonia, lung abscesses, or bronchiectasis. Analysis of pleural fluid typically shows a pH < 7.2, increased LDH concentration, and glucose concentration < 60 mg/dL.

gHWFp50.title: Tubal infertility
gHWFp50.description: A type of infertility that results from an inability of the ovum to pass through the fallopian tube, commonly due to tubal obstruction and/or impaired ciliary movement. Frequent causes of tubal infertility include scarring and/or adhesions within the fallopian tubes from ascending STI (i.e., pelvic inflammatory disease), ectopic pregnancy, endometriosis, and/or surgical adhesions.

hHWcJ50.title: Chloride-resistant metabolic alkalosis
hHWcJ50.description: A type of metabolic alkalosis manifesting with high urinary chloride concentration (> 40 mEq/L) that cannot be corrected by the administration of a chloride-containing solution (e.g., normal saline). Associated with inappropriate renal excretion of sodium chloride. Etiologies include hyperaldosteronism, Cushing syndrome, Liddle syndrome, and severe hypokalemia.

iHWJJ50.title: Resting metabolic rate
iHWJJ50.description: ​​​​​​​The amount of energy required to maintain basic life-sustaining function at rest in a temperate environment during digestive activity. Typically measured during the day after 12 hours without exercise.

4HW3q50.title: Mini Nutritional Assessment
4HW3q50.description: A screening tool for malnutrition in older adults. The short form (MNA-SF) includes six self-reported responses to questions on food intake, weight loss, mobility, psychological stress or acute disease, dementia or depression, and BMI. A score ≥ 12 excludes malnutrition and/or malnutrition risk. If a score ≤ 11 is obtained, the long form of the MNA (MNA-LF) should be completed.

kHWmq50.title: Risk factors for sexually transmitted infections
kHWmq50.description: In sexually active individuals, risk factors include: < 25 years of age, inconsistent condom use outside of a mutually monogamous relationship, history of STI, new or multiple sexual partners, a partner with an STI or other sexual partners, men who have sex with men, history of incarceration, exchanging sex for drugs or money, and IV drug use. Local health departments may identify additional risk factors depending on local prevalence patterns.

NHW-q50.title: Maddrey discriminant function
NHW-q50.description: A formula used to predict outcomes in patients with alcoholic hepatitis. Patients with a score of ≥ 32 are considered to have severe alcoholic hepatitis, with a 1-month mortality rate of 20-50%; these patients may benefit from corticosteroid therapy. The MELD score has replaced the Maddrey discriminant function as the preferred index to assess severity and predict outcomes in alcohol-associated hepatitis.

media.title: Maddrey discriminant function for alcoholic hepatitis

mHWVI50.title: Lille model for alcohol-associated hepatitis
mHWVI50.description: A formula to determine response to corticosteroid therapy in patients with alcoholic hepatitis. A Lille score of ≥ 0.45 predicts nonresponse to steroid therapy.

5HWiI50.title: Geriatric syndromes
5HWiI50.description: A group of complex health conditions in older adults that may result from multiple risk factors and organ system impairments, and that make individuals vulnerable to additional physical stressors or insults. Frailty is one of the primary geriatric syndromes; examples of others include cognitive impairment, malnutrition, and falls.

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Screening for geriatric syndromes

nHW7I50.title: Calf muscle pump
nHW7I50.description: The physiological pressure gradient in the lower extremities created by the contraction of the calf muscles. Promotes the return of venous blood to the heart. Can become impaired when veins are incompetent or obstructed, leading to venous hypertension.

LHWwI50.title: Multiphase imaging
LHWwI50.description: A term used to describe imaging obtained at various time points after the administration of contrast material (i.e., during the precontrast, arterial, portal venous, and delayed phases).

pHWLr50.title: Well-woman exam
pHWLr50.description: An annual health care visit that focuses on gynecology. Typically involves taking a comprehensive history and, if indicated, screening (e.g., for cervical cancer, STIs), a breast and pelvic examination, immunizations, and counseling.

IHWY750.title: TRICARE
IHWY750.description: A health care program for active-duty service members of the US army, National Guard and Reserve members, retirees and their family members. Designed to provide integrated health care through military treatment facilities and civilian managed care support contractors to eligible Americans in the US and abroad

destinations.label: Military medicine → Health care in the military

rHWf750.title: Military Health System
rHWf750.description: A federal health care program run by the United States Department of Defense. Targeted with ensuring that all active duty and reserve component personnel of the US army stays healthy and operational.

destinations.label: Military medicine → Health care in the military

7HW4750.title: Reticulocytopenia
7HW4750.description: A decreased number of reticulocytes in the peripheral blood (typically < 0.5% of all red blood cells). Etiologies include primary bone marrow disorders (e.g., aplastic anemia, myelodysplastic disorders), malignant bone marrow infiltration (e.g., leukemia), viral infections (e.g., parvovirus B19), nutritional deficiencies (e.g., iron, vitamin B12, folate, or copper), chronic kidney disease, and medication adverse effects.

sHWt750.title: Superficial temporal artery
sHWt750.description: A terminal branch of the external carotid artery. Arises in the parotid gland and courses over the zygomatic arch. Giant cell arteritis commonly affects this artery.

destinations.label: Head and neck region → Vasculature and innervation

8HWOH50.title: Ulcerative colitis endoscopic index of severity
8HWOH50.description: An 8-point scale used to determine the severity of ulcerative colitis that considers vascular pattern (0-2 points); bleeding (0-3 points); and erosions and/or ulcers (0-3 points) seen on endoscopy.

EHW8H50.title: Acute severe ulcerative colitis
EHW8H50.description: The acute onset of moderate-to-severe or fulminant ulcerative colitis as defined by the presence of six or more bowel movements per day in addition to at least one systemic sign of toxicity (e.g., tachycardia, fever, hemoglobin < 10.5 g/dL, ESR > 30 mm/hour).

destinations.label: Ulcerative colitis → Acute severe ulcerative colitis

_HW5G50.title: Mesenteric artery occlusive disease
_HW5G50.description: The obstruction of blood flow in one or more of the three major mesenteric arteries (celiac artery, superior mesenteric artery, and/or inferior mesenteric artery). It is most commonly caused by atherosclerotic plaque.

-HWDG50.title: Sitophobia
-HWDG50.description: The fear of eating related to unpleasant postprandial symptoms. Causes include Crohn disease, chronic mesenteric ischemia, and chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.

ZsWZt50.title: VHA
ZsWZt50.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Veterans Health Administration
2. Viscoelastic hemostatic assay

csWaF50.title: Quantitative computed tomography
csWaF50.description: An imaging technique that uses CT technology to assess bone mineral density. Performed on the spine, hip, tibia, or radius.

WsWPF50.title: Chronic nausea and vomiting syndrome
WsWPF50.description: A functional gastrointestinal disorder that includes episodes of nausea and vomiting without an underlying organic or structural disease. Diagnosis is made using the Rome IV criteria: Nausea and/or vomiting are present at least once a week, and self-induced vomiting, eating disorders, regurgitation, and rumination have been excluded.

dsWoF50.title: Keratolytics
dsWoF50.description: An agent used for the treatment of hyperkeratosis (abnormal thickening of the skin), a manifestation of psoriasis and other dermatologic conditions. Common agents include salicylic acid, urea, and alpha hydroxy acids (e.g., glycolic acid, lactic acid).

gsWF850.title: Primary narcolepsy
gsWF850.description: A type of narcolepsy that develops in the absence of injury to the hypothalamus (i.e., secondary narcolepsy). The exact etiology is unknown.

SsWy850.title: Secondary narcolepsy
SsWy850.description: A type of narcolepsy that occurs as a result of damage to the hypothalamus, e.g., due to a stroke, a tumor, head trauma, or, less commonly, a genetic cause such as Niemann-Pick disease type C or Prader-Willi syndrome.

hsWcu50.title: Pedunculated polyp
hsWcu50.description: A polyp attached to the mucosal layer by a stalk.

3sWSu50.title: Sessile polyp
3sWSu50.description: A broad-based polyp that is attached directly to the mucosal layer; does not have a stalk.

4sW3E50.title: Vegetarian diet
4sW3E50.description: A plant-based diet that may include dairy products but not meat or, typically, seafood. A lacto-ovo vegetarian diet inlcudes eggs, whereas a lacto-vegetarian diet includes only dairy products. A pescetarian-vegetarian diet also includes seafood.

destinations.label: Principles of nutrition → Vegetarian and vegan diet

OsWIE50.title: Collection of a nasopharyngeal sample
OsWIE50.description: A procedure in which a synthetic fiber swab is inserted through the nostril and advanced parallel to the palate until contacting the posterior nasopharynx (approximately as deep as the distance between the nostril and ear). Once resistance is felt, the swab is rotated to absorb secretions from the posterior nasopharynx and then slowly removed.

media.title: Nasopharyngeal (NP) and oropharyngeal (OP) swab equipment and technique for SARS-CoV-2

NsW-E50.title: Autoimmune thyroid disease
NsW-E50.description: A term used to describe diseases that cause immune-mediated inflammation and/or dysfunction of the thyroid gland (may result in hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism). Examples include Hashimoto thyroiditis, Graves disease, and certain types of subacute thyroiditis (e.g., postpartum thyroiditis).

msWVv50.title: Snare polypectomy
msWVv50.description: A method of endoscopic removal of polyps that have low malignancy potential. The polyp is encircled by a thin wire snare, leaving a margin of surrounding healthy tissue. The snare is then retracted, which causes the snare to tighten and cut through the encircled tissue. Can be performed with electrocautery (i.e., hot snare) or without (i.e., cold snare).

5sWiv50.title: Adenomatous polyposis syndromes
5sWiv50.description: A subtype of hereditary polyposis syndromes. Characterized by numerous adenomatous polyps and an increased risk of colon cancer and other intestinal and extraintestinal tumors. Comprises classic familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), FAP subtypes (e.g., Gardner syndrome, Turcot syndrome, attenuated FAP), and MUTYH-associated polyposis.

MsWMv50.title: Hamartomatous polyposis syndromes
MsWMv50.description: A subtype of hereditary polyposis syndrome. Characterized by hamartomatous polyps. Includes Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome (PJS), Juvenile polyposis syndrome (JPS), and PTEN-Hamartoma Tumor syndromes (PHTS).

nsW7v50.title: Classic familial adenomatous polyposis
nsW7v50.description: An autosomal dominant adenomatous polyposis syndrome caused by a mutation in the APC tumor suppressor gene. Characterized by the presence of hundreds of adenomatous colorectal polyps that have a high potential for malignant transformation.

7sW4w50.title: GOLD groups
7sW4w50.description: A classification system used by the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) to stratify the severity of COPD symptoms and guide treatment. Distinct from GOLD grades 1-4, which stratify the severity of airflow limitation.

ssWtw50.title: MacEwen sign
ssWtw50.description: A sign of late hydrocephalus. Percussion of the skull near the junction of the frontal, temporal, and parietal bones evokes an unusually resonant sound. Caused by separation of cranial sutures due to increased intracranial pressure

GsWBw50.title: Alpha-2-delta calcium channel ligands
GsWBw50.description: A class of medications that bind to the alpha-2-delta-1 subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels in the brain. These medications are the first-line medical therapy for restless legs syndrome. Agents include gabapentin, gabapentin enacarbil, and pregabalin.

8sWO950.title: Left ventricular end-systolic dimension
8sWO950.description: The diameter of the left ventricle of the heart at the end of systole, commonly measured as a one-dimensional distance on an echocardiogram. Used as a marker of left ventricular function in the assessment of mitral and aortic regurgitation.

usWp950.title: Paratenic host
usWp950.description: A type of intermediate host that is not required for the continuation of the parasitic life cycle but can maintain it. For example, parasitic larvae may be ingested by a paratenic host and grow while remaining at the same stage of development before further transmission.

EsW8950.title: Cortical deafness
EsW8950.description: A condition caused by bilateral damage to the primary auditory cortex. Characterized by an inability to hear both pure tones and complex sounds. Reflex responses that depend on the subcortical structures (e.g., startle reflex) are preserved.

destinations.label: The cerebral cortex, meninges, basal ganglia, and ventricular system → Cerebral cortex

DsW1C50.title: Phthalic anhydride
DsW1C50.description: An organic compound used in the large-scale production of plasticizers (e.g., in vinyl chloride). Short-term exposure through skin contact and/or inhalation can cause irritation. Chronic exposure can result in bronchitis, asthma, and other respiratory conditions.

wsWhC50.title: Trichophyton verrucosum
wsWhC50.description: A slow-growing, spore-forming dermatophyte that commonly causes ringworm in cattle. Can be transmitted to humans via contact with infected animals or contaminated equipment.

9sWNC50.title: mRNA vaccine
9sWNC50.description: A type of vaccine that delivers messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) to host cells, which then produce and express an antigen that then elicits an immune response. Examples include the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines.

media.title: Mechanism of action of mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccines

xsWEC50.title: Self-stimulatory behavior
xsWEC50.description: The repetition of non-goal-directed movements to stimulate the senses, including self-injurious behavior such as banging the head. It can be a manifestation of catatonia or of neurodevelopmental disorders (e.g., autism spectrum disorder).

ysWdx50.title: PTEN hamartoma tumor syndromes
ysWdx50.description: A group of autosomal dominant hamartomatous polyposis syndromes caused by germline mutations in the PTEN tumor suppressor gene. Associated with presence of hamartomas throughout the body (e.g., colon, breast, thyroid, endometrium) and an increased risk of cancer in the affected areas. Examples include Cowden syndrome (most common), Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndrome, and Proteus syndrome.

AsWRx50.title: Characteristic liver chemistries in alcohol-associated hepatitis
AsWRx50.description: The liver chemistries performed to support a clinical diagnosis of alcoholic hepatitis include AST (> 50 IU/L); AST:ALT ratio (> 1.5); both AST and ALT (< 400 IU/L); and serum total bilirubin (> 3 mg/dL).

_sW5x50.title: High-fiber diet
_sW5x50.description: A diet comprising at least 20-30 g of fiber per day. A high fiber diet may be recommended for the management of various gastroenterological conditions (e.g., constipation, hemorrhoids, irritable bowel syndrome) and can reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease and diabetes. Foods that are high in fiber include vegetables (e.g., broccoli, peas), fruits (e.g. berries, apples), legumes (e.g., lentils, black beans), and grains (e.g. oatmeal, whole grain bread).

zsWrx50.title: Suppressive antibiotic therapy
zsWrx50.description: The long-term use of antibiotics to suppress, rather than eradicate, an infection. Typically used for complicated infections (e.g., osteomyelitis) in patients unsuitable for aggressive treatments (e.g., surgical resection) because of comorbidities or complications at the infection site.

ZGWZB50.title: Constitutional neutropenia
ZGWZB50.description: A condition characterized by a decreased absolute neutrophil count (< 1500/mcL) in the absence of secondary causes and without an increased risk of infection. Mainly occurs in individuals of African, Middle Eastern, and West Indian descent.

YGWnB50.title: Micronutrients
YGWnB50.description: Chemical elements or substances required by the body in very small amounts for normal growth, development, and function of living organisms. Micronutrients comprise vitamins and minerals (including trace elements).

cGWay50.title: Alcoholic liver disease/nonalcoholic fatty liver disease index
cGWay50.description: A validated score that utilizes mean corpuscular volume, AST:ALT ratio, BMI, and gender to help differentiate alcoholic liver disease (ALD) from nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). An ANI > 0 is suggestive of ALD and an ANI < 0 suggests NAFLD.

1GW2y50.title: CAB approach
1GW2y50.description: An approach to the initial management of suspected cardiac arrest: Chest compressions, Airway, and Breathing. This sequence minimizes the time to initiation of chest compressions.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)

WGWPy50.title: Tract curettage
WGWPy50.description: A surgical procedure in which granulation tissue is removed from a sinus or fistula with a probe. Used in the treatment of pilonidal disease and hidradenitis suppurativa.

eGWxy50.title: Exogenous osteomyelitis
eGWxy50.description: A type of osteomyelitis caused by a local infection with direct penetration of the bone. Commonly associated with trauma, surgical implants, foreign bodies, peripheral arterial disease, and/or diabetes. More common in adults.

UGWbA50.title: Hematogenous osteomyelitis
UGWbA50.description: A type of osteomyelitis caused by dissemination of a pathogen in the bloodstream (most commonly S. aureus) that infiltrates the bone. Hematogenous osteomyelitis is more common in children.

iGWJ_50.title: Journal club
iGWJ_50.description: A gathering of individuals to discuss recent literature relevant to a particular discipline (e.g., medicine). Often involves the critical appraisal of one or more research studies.

QGWu_50.title: Person-first language
QGWu_50.description: Language that foregrounds the individual, e.g., "an individual with cirrhosis" rather than "a cirrhotic patient." Person-first language aims to reduce the potential for stigma and bias by distinguishing individuals from their medical condition and/or circumstances.

jGW__50.title: First morning urine
jGW__50.description: A sample of urine that is collected from the first urination after awakening in the morning. Patients should be instructed to void before sleeping and remain recumbent until the sample is obtained in the morning.

PGWWz50.title: Drug test
PGWWz50.description: A test to detect the presence of drugs and drug metabolites in a biological sample (e.g., urine, blood/serum, saliva, or hair). The choice of modality depends on whether the test is for screening or confirmation.

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Management of substance use disorder

4GW3z50.title: Phlebotonic supplement
4GW3z50.description: A natural plant extract or similar synthetic compound used in the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency. May increase venous tone and decrease capillary permeability symptoms, thereby relieving symptoms (e.g., pain, sensation of heaviness, edema), although evidence of long-term effects is lacking. Examples include disodium flavodate, grape seed extract, and horse chestnut seed extract.

OGWIz50.title: Odontogenic
OGWIz50.description: An adjective used to describe processes or conditions related to teeth.

NGW-z50.title: Acrocyanosis
NGW-z50.description: A vasospastic condition that causes blue discoloration of the peripheral extremities (most commonly the hands) due to decreased oxyhemoglobin, typically in response to cold temperatures. Discoloration is usually transient but often persists during the winter months. It may be primary (idiopathic) or secondary (caused by another condition). Acrocyanosis is also sometimes erroneously used as a synonym for peripheral cyanosis, which is a broader term used to describe blue discoloration of the extremities and may have multiple etiologies.

6GWjZM0.title: Zoster vaccination
6GWjZM0.description: The use of vaccination to prevent varicella zoster virus reactivation (i.e., shingles). Options include a recombinant vaccine and a live-attenuated varicella-zoster virus vaccine (unavailable in the United States).

pGWLZM0.title: Renal and bladder ultrasound
pGWLZM0.description: A noninvasive imaging study that uses high-frequency sound waves to examine and document the number, size, shape, and location of kidneys, ureters, and bladder as well as vascular, congenital, and other abnormalities.

JGWsZM0.title: Damage control surgery
JGWsZM0.description: A staged approach to managing patients with traumatic or nontraumatic injuries who require immediate surgical intervention, but need further resuscitation prior to definitive surgical treatment. The initial phase of damage control surgery is aimed at controlling bleeding, contamination, and necrosis. After postoperative patient stabilization, definitive surgical repair can be carried out.

IGWY0M0.title: MR urography
IGWY0M0.description: An imaging study that uses MRI with contrast to assess the entire urinary tract system (e.g., kidney, ureters, bladder).

7GW40M0.title: Temporary abdominal closure
7GW40M0.description: A surgical technique in which the abdominal fascia is not immediately reapproximated after laparotomy. Indications include prevention of abdominal compartment syndrome, the need to reassess the abdominal contents with second-look surgery, and/or primary inability to close the abdomen.

HGWK0M0.title: Second-look surgery
HGWK0M0.description: A surgical procedure performed at a predetermined time after an initial procedure to assess the effectiveness of previous treatment and the need for further surgical intervention. Most commonly performed within 48 hours of emergency abdominal surgery to evaluate tissue perfusion and bleeding control.

tGWXaM0.title: Universal protocol
tGWXaM0.description: A three-step process developed by the Joint Commission to prevent wrong-site, wrong-procedure, and wrong-person surgery. Includes preprocedural verification of the patient's identity, surgical site, and surgical procedure, surgical site marking, and a time out.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medical errors

8GWOaM0.title: Metabolic liver disease
8GWOaM0.description: A group of diseases that can result in liver damage (e.g., cirrhosis, liver cancer). Caused by pathologic accumulation of misfolded proteins or metals as a result of disrupted metabolic pathways. Examples include hereditary hemochromatosis, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, Wilson disease, and glycogen storage diseases.

uGWpaM0.title: Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System
uGWpaM0.description: A system that uses standardized terminology and set criteria to classify liver lesions on imaging in patients at risk for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Diagnostic categories range from LR-1 (definitely benign) to LR-5 (definitely HCC), with the additional categories LR-M (likely malignant but unclear if HCC) and LR-TIV (tumor in vein).

CGWqYM0.title: Therapeutic phlebotomy
CGWqYM0.description: The removal of blood from the body to treat an underlying disorder or complication. Used as first-line treatment for serum iron removal in patients with hereditary hemochromatosis. It is also used to remove red blood cells in patients with polycythemia vera, porphyria cutanea tarda, and sickle cell disease.

ZtWZXM0.title: Crazy-paving pattern
ZtWZXM0.description: A nonspecific chest CT finding characterized by interlobular septal thickening and/or intralobular septal thickening superimposed on ground-glass opacity resembling crazy paving. Crazy-paving pattern is a nonspecific finding that may be seen in various conditions, including infection, acute respiratory distress syndrome, pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, and neoplasms.

0tWeXM0.title: Ablative therapy
0tWeXM0.description: The destruction of abnormal tissue using heat, extreme cold, chemicals, or lasers. Ablation is commonly used in the management of arrhythmias, cancer, skin growths, and chronic pain.

YtWnXM0.title: Radiofrequency rhizotomy
YtWnXM0.description: A minimally-invasive procedure that selectively destroys nerves with heat generated with radiofrequency waves, preventing the transduction of pain signals. Can be used to treat pain associated with degenerative facet joints in the spine and trigeminal neuralgia.

XtW9XM0.title: Functional status assessment
XtW9XM0.description: The evaluation of an individual's ability to perform tasks of daily living (i.e., basic, instrumental, and advanced activities of daily living) in order to determine their care needs.

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Functional status assessment

ctWacM0.title: Home hazard assessment and modification
ctWacM0.description: A fall prevention strategy that evaluates potential hazards in the home environment and provides appropriate modification (e.g., ensuring floors, hallways, and stairs are well-lit and clear of wires and clutter; rugs are removed or taped to the floor; bathtub has a non-slip mat; grab bars or rails are installed in the bathroom or on stairs).

1tW2cM0.title: Warm agglutinin
1tW2cM0.description: A type of autoantibody (typically IgG) against a red blood cell antigen that activates at a temperature ≥ 37°C and causes red blood cell agglutination and hemolysis.

WtWPcM0.title: Yuzpe regimen
WtWPcM0.description: A dosing regimen of combined oral contraceptive pills (i.e., pills that contain both estrogen and a progestin) that can be used as an emergency contraception method. Less effective than other emergency contraception methods. Adverse effects include nausea and vomiting.

UtWb1M0.title: Microcytic hypochromic anemia
UtWb1M0.description: A type of anemia characterized by smaller than normal red blood cells (mean corpuscular volume < 80 fL) with a lower than normal hemoglobin concentration (mean corpuscular hemoglobin < 27 pg/cell).

2tWT1M0.title: Percutaneous ethanol injection
2tWT1M0.description: A type of ablative therapy in which ethanol is injected to destroy tissue. Used to treat malignancies, in particular thyroid cancer and primary and secondary liver tumors, and manage chronic pain via neurolysis.

ftWk1M0.title: Volvulus
ftWk1M0.description: A twisting of an intraperitoneal loop of intestines around its mesentery, which causes strangulation of the blood supply and mechanical bowel obstruction.

destinations.label: Intestinal malrotation, midgut volvulus, and gastric volvulus → Midgut volvulus
Sigmoid volvulus and cecal volvulus → Summary
Intestinal malrotation, midgut volvulus, and gastric volvulus → Gastric volvulus

3tWSWM0.title: Nonsurgical biopsy
3tWSWM0.description: A method of obtaining tissue for histopathological examination that does not involve an open incision or other surgical technique. Examples include needle aspiration and core needle biopsy guided by imaging or endoscopy.

RtWlWM0.title: Myeloma defining event
RtWlWM0.description: A collection of clinical features of end-organ damage and biomarkers of malignancy that, when considered in combination with clonal proliferation of plasma cells, define multiple myeloma.

jtW_WM0.title: Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer staging system
jtW_WM0.description: A staging system used to guide management and estimate prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma. Staging is based on tumor burden, severity of liver dysfunction, and the patient's performance status. Scores range from 0 (very early disease) to D (end-stage disease).

4tW3dM0.title: Peritoneal cancer index
4tW3dM0.description: A scoring system for peritoneal carcinomatosis that quantitatively assesses the distribution and size of cancer implants within 13 regions of the abdomen and pelvis. Used for prognostication and guidance of management.

ktWmdM0.title: Very early hepatocellular carcinoma
ktWmdM0.description: A single small (≤ 2 cm) hepatocellular carcinoma tumor that is confined to the liver, with no evidence of portal hypertension or macrovascular invasion in patients with preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A or B) and good performance status.

OtWIdM0.title: Acne keloidalis nuchae
OtWIdM0.description: A chronic, inflammatory folliculitis characterized by pruritic papules, hypertrophic scarring, and scarring alopecia on the occipital scalp. Most commonly seen in individuals with darker skin types.

destinations.label: Dermatological conditions in skin of color → Acne keloidalis nuchae

ltWvdM0.title: Dermatosis papulosa nigra
ltWvdM0.description: A common, benign skin condition characterized by brown papules on the malar and temple areas of the face, neck, and upper trunk. Most commonly seen in individuals with darker skin types.

destinations.label: Dermatological conditions in skin of color → Dermatosis papulosa nigra

NtW-dM0.title: Mycobacterium microti
NtW-dM0.description: A mycobacterial species of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex that can cause tuberculosis in animals (especially wild rodents). It is a rare cause of infections in humans. Manifestations include anorexia and malaise.

mtWVVM0.title: Postinflammatory hyperpigmentation
mtWVVM0.description: An acquired hyperpigmentation disorder that results from injury (e.g., skin abrasion), inflammation (e.g., atopic dermatitis), or procedures (e.g., cryotherapy, radiation). Manifests as pigmented macules or patches with irregular borders and can persist if the underlying cause is not treated. Typically affects individuals with dark skin.

5tWiVM0.title: Prognathism
5tWiVM0.description: The protrusion of either the mandible (mandibular prognathism) or the maxilla (maxillary prognathism). Usually leads to misalignment of the top and lower teeth.

MtWMVM0.title: Factor X deficiency
MtWMVM0.description: A rare coagulopathy that can be inherited or acquired (e.g., in the setting of vitamin K deficiency or liver failure). Can result in epistaxis, menorrhagia, haemarthrosis, intracranial hemorrhage, and gastrointestinal bleeding.

otW0eM0.title: Acute osteomyelitis
otW0eM0.description: An infection of the bone that has lasted <2 weeks at the time of treatment initiation.

KtWUeM0.title: Subacute osteomyelitis
KtWUeM0.description: An infection of the bone that has lasted 2-6 weeks at the time treatment is initiated. Some sources place the range at 2-12 weeks.

6tWjeM0.title: Chronic osteomyelitis
6tWjeM0.description: An infection of the bone that has lasted ≥ 6 weeks when treatment is initiated. Some sources place the cutoff point at ≥ 12 weeks.

qtWCeM0.title: Renal colic
qtWCeM0.description: A condition characterized by severe unilateral flank pain that often radiates to the groin. Caused by ureteral obstruction, most commonly from nephrolithiasis, and may be associated with nausea and vomiting.

rtWfUM0.title: Physeal arrest
rtWfUM0.description: A growth disturbance of immature bone at the physeal growth plate. Caused by the premature closure of the growth plate.

7tW4UM0.title: PML-RARA fusion gene
7tW4UM0.description: A fusion gene formed by a balanced translocation of the RARA (retinoic acid receptor alpha) gene located on chromosome 17 and the PML (promyelocytic leukemia) gene on chromosome 15. Involved in the pathogenesis of acute promyelocytic leukemia.

HtWKUM0.title: Amniotomy
HtWKUM0.description: A procedure in which the amniotic sac is ruptured in order to release amniotic fluid.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Normal spontaneous labor

stWtUM0.title: Delayed cord clamping
stWtUM0.description: The delayed clamping of the umbilical cord for at least 30-60 seconds after birth. Increases hemoglobin levels in term infants and improves neonatal outcomes in preterm infants (e.g., by decreasing the need for blood transfusions and lowering the risk for hemorrhage and necrotizing enterocolitis).

ttWX2M0.title: Cervical dilation
ttWX2M0.description: The opening of the cervix. Occurs during labor as a result of uterine contractions. The cervix can also be opened with the use of mechanical dilators (e.g., to facilitate curettage or hysteroscopy).

FtWg2M0.title: Toddler fracture
FtWg2M0.description: A type of nondisplaced fracture of the distal tibial shaft, which usually occurs following an acute trauma (e.g., falling, tripping). Most commonly seen in children between 9 months and 3 years of age. Manifestations include the inability to bear weight, localized tenderness, and irritability.

destinations.label: Tibial and fibular fractures → Subtypes and variants

8tWO2M0.title: Serralysin
8tWO2M0.description: A protease enzyme produced by Serratia marcescens. Modulates the host inflammatory responses (e.g., by activating various transcription factors and inactivating antimicrobial peptides).

utWp2M0.title: Bland urine sediment
utWp2M0.description: A finding of urine sediment with no, or only a few, cells and/or casts. Bland urine sediment is seen in healthy patients but may also be seen in patients with certain types of kidney disease (e.g., prerenal AKI, certain types of acute interstitial nephritis).

EtW82M0.title: Lithotripsy
EtW82M0.description: A procedure for breaking down a stone (e.g., kidney stone or gallstone) into smaller pieces that commonly involves shock waves or lasers.

DtW1fM0.title: Bacterial tracheitis
DtW1fM0.description: A life-threatening bacterial infection of the trachea associated with tracheal exudates and pseudomembranes that obstruct the airway. Manifestations include stridor and respiratory distress. Can affect patients with artificial or native airways; among affected individuals with native airways, most commonly occurs in children under 6 years of age. May be confused with viral croup, but patients are often more ill-appearing and do not respond to conventional croup treatment(s).

wtWhfM0.title: Sarilumab
wtWhfM0.description: A monoclonal antibody against the IL-6 receptor, which leads to a reduction in cytokine and acute-phase reactant production. Used in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. Approved for emergency use in conjunction with corticosteroids for the management of hospitalized patients with severe COVID-19.

9tWNfM0.title: Ventricular septal rupture
9tWNfM0.description: A life-threatening complication of myocardial infarction that most commonly occurs 3–5 days after infarct. Usually associated with left anterior descending (LAD) artery infarction because the septal arteries arise from the LAD. Clinical manifestations include a new holosystolic murmur and acute-onset right heart failure that can progress to cardiogenic shock.

-tWDTM0.title: Percutaneous rhizotomy
-tWDTM0.description: A minimally-invasive procedure that selectively destroys nerves. A needle is inserted at the site of the target nerve, which facilitates radiofrequency rhizotomy (which results in heat injury), mechanical balloon compression (which results in compression injury), or chemical rhizolysis (which uses glycerol to disrupt nerve function). Can be used to treat pain associated with degenerative facet joints in the spine and trigeminal neuralgia.

ZFWZgM0.title: Post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis
ZFWZgM0.description: A form of secondary myelofibrosis seen in advanced polycythemia vera as a result of progressive fibrosis of the bone marrow. Previously referred to as spent phase polycythemia vera.

aFWQgM0.title: Gastrointestinal bleeding prophylaxis
aFWQgM0.description: The prescription of acid suppression medications (e.g., PPIs, H2 blockers) to help prevent peptic ulcer formation and gastrointestinal hemorrhage in patients at increased risk of peptic ulcer disease (e.g., those who use NSAIDs or oral corticosteroids, critically ill patients).

YFWngM0.title: Postinflammatory hypopigmentation
YFWngM0.description: A lightening in skin pigmentation following an injury or inflammatory dermatosis of the skin. Typically self-limited.

UFWbhM0.title: Oxygen saturation gap
UFWbhM0.description: The difference between peripheral oxygen saturation detected by pulse oximeter and calculated arterial oxygen saturation based on blood gas analysis. A difference > 5% is clinically significant and may indicate carbon monoxide poisoning, methemoglobinemia, sulfhemoglobinemia, or a hemoglobin disorder with abnormal oxygen affinity.

2FWThM0.title: Oxygen affinity test
2FWThM0.description: A blood gas analysis measurement for calculating p50, the partial pressure of dissolved oxygen (PO₂) at which 50% of hemoglobin is saturated with oxygen. Decreased p50 indicates a left shift in the oxygen saturation curve and increased hemoglobin affinity for oxygen. Increased p50 indicates a right-shifted oxygen saturation curve and decreased hemoglobin affinity for oxygen.

fFWkhM0.title: Primary familial and congenital polycythemia
fFWkhM0.description: An autosomal-dominant genetic disorder that results in isolated polycythemia. Erythropoietin receptor mutations cause autonomous RBC production in the bone marrow irrespective of the erythropoietin level, which is typically low as a result of negative feedback.

TFW6hM0.title: Primary polycythemia
TFW6hM0.description: An excess of circulating red blood cells resulting from congenital (e.g., primary familial and congenital polycythemia) or acquired (e.g., polycythemia vera) bone marrow defects.

gFWFhM0.title: Dagger sign
gFWFhM0.description: A radiographic sign of ankylosing spondylitis characterized by a radiodense line running through the center of vertebral bodies on spine x-ray. Caused by ossification of the spinal ligaments.

hFWc3M0.title: Fulminant myocarditis
hFWc3M0.description: A severe manifestation of myocarditis characterized by hemodynamic instability and/or electrical instability (e.g., ventricular arrhythmia, high-grade atrioventricular block).

iFWJ3M0.title: Compensatory pause
iFWJ3M0.description: A pause that compensates for the prematurity of a preceding extrasystolic beat. Results in an interval between the preextrasystolic and postextrasystolic beats that is exactly twice as long as the P-P interval of normal heart activity.

QFWu3M0.title: Tinea incognito
QFWu3M0.description: A dermatophyte infection with an atypical clinical presentation (e.g., decreased scale and erythema, poor demarcation) caused by prior use of corticosteroids or immunomodulatory drugs.

PFWWRM0.title: Indeterminate mass
PFWWRM0.description: A mass that cannot be confirmed to be benign or malignant based on radiologic features on initial imaging. Typically requires additional imaging and/or pathological evaluation of tissue to make a definitive diagnosis.

kFWmRM0.title: Clinical manifestations of connective tissue disorders
kFWmRM0.description: A highly heterogenous set of signs and symptoms that can manifest in all organs. Common clinical features include constitutional symptoms (e.g., fatigue, malaise, fever), arthralgia, mayalgia, rashes, skin ulceration, Raynaud phenomenon, dry eyes and mouth, and shortness of breath.

destinations.label: Connective tissue diseases → Clinical manifestations of connective tissue disorders

OFWIRM0.title: Central pulse
OFWIRM0.description: The pulse palpated from an artery close to the heart (e.g., femoral or carotid pulse). In an emergency, palpating a central pulse increases the likelihood of detecting a pulse in a patient with hypotension.

mFWViM0.title: Complementary DNA
mFWViM0.description: DNA that has been synthesized from mRNA by the enzyme reverse transcriptase. Typically used in polymerase chain reaction procedures to detect and quantify the amount of mRNA in a sample.

nFW7iM0.title: Respiratory drive
nFW7iM0.description: The intensity of respiratory muscle stimulation by the respiratory centers located in the central nervous system. Respiratory muscles generate mechanical output, which determines the breathing effort, i.e., the frequency and depth of spontaneous inspiration.

KFWUQM0.title: Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome
KFWUQM0.description: A rare but severe presentation of antiphospholipid syndrome. Characterized by multiorgan small vessel thrombosis and failure occurring simultaneously or within 1 week. Treatment is not standardized but usually consists of anticoagulation, immunosuppressive therapy, and management of any precipitating factors.

6FWjQM0.title: Erythrocyte adenosine deaminase
6FWjQM0.description: An enzyme that deaminates adenosine to inosine and 2′-deoxyadenosine to 2′-deoxyinosine. Involved in purine metabolism. Increased activity of this enzyme in erythrocytes is seen in individuals with Diamond-Blackfan anemia.

qFWCQM0.title: Compensated cirrhosis
qFWCQM0.description: The asymptomatic stage of cirrhosis in which complications of portal hypertension (e.g., overt ascites, variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy) are absent. Evidence of portal hypertension (e.g., gastroesophageal varices) may be present.

rFWfjM0.title: Diabetic gastroparesis
rFWfjM0.description: A complication of diabetes mellitus characterized by delayed gastric emptying due to nonmechanical obstruction. Typically manifests with postprandial fullness, nausea, vomiting, and bloating.

7FW4jM0.title: Postconceptional age
7FW4jM0.description: The age of a newborn, calculated as the sum of gestational age and number of weeks since birth.

HFWKjM0.title: Brief resolved unexplained event
HFWKjM0.description: A sudden, brief, resolved episode without apparent cause in infants < 1 year of age that includes ≥ 1 of the following: cyanosis; pallor; absent, decreased, or irregular breathing; hypertonia; hypotonia; and altered level of responsiveness. This term is recommended by the American Academy of Pediatrics in place of "apparent life-threatening event (ALTE)."

sFWtjM0.title: Smoking cessation
sFWtjM0.description: The process of discontinuing smoking. The use of support strategies such as behavioral counseling, nicotine replacement therapy, and medication to reduce cravings (e.g., bupropion) increases the likelihood of success, especially when used in combination.

destinations.label: Tobacco product use and smoking cessation → Management

tFWXPM0.title: Bile esculin agar
tFWXPM0.description: A growth medium containing bile, esculin, and ferric citrate. Used to isolate S. gallolyticus and Enterococcus species. Bacterial hydrolization of esculin causes a blackening of the medium and dark colonies.

FFWgPM0.title: Thiosulfate citrate bile salts sucrose agar
FFWgPM0.description: A growth medium containing sodium thiosulfate, sodium citrate, sodium chloride, saccharose, proteose peptone and other nutrients. Used to isolate Vibrio and Enterococcus species, which appear as round, smooth, glistening, and slightly flattened yellow colonies.

uFWpPM0.title: Broselow tape
