uFWpPM0.description: A tape measure used in pediatric emergencies to provide rapid recommendations on medication dosages, equipment sizing, and defibrillator shock dosages based on the patient's height. The tape is color-coded, with each color corresponding to a drawer in the pediatric code cart that contains appropriately sized equipment. The Broselow tape is designed for children up to ~ 12 years of age and ~ 36 kg (80 lbs).

EFW8PM0.title: FOLFIRINOX
EFW8PM0.description: A chemotherapy regimen used to treat pancreatic cancer. Consists of leucovorin calcium (folinic acid; FOL), 5-fluorouracil (F), irinotecan (IRIN), and oxaliplatin (OX).

vFWAPM0.title: Nab-paclitaxel
vFWAPM0.description: An anti-cancer drug that consists of paclitaxel bound to nanoparticle albumin, which facilitates its delivery to tumor cells. Used to treat metastatic breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and pancreatic cancer.

wFWh4M0.title: Arrhythmia symptoms
wFWh4M0.description: A collection of features that may be seen in individuals experiencing an abnormal heart rate or rhythm. Includes generalized fatigue or weakness, dizziness, syncope, palpitations, an irregular pulse, and, in tachyarrhythmias, the sensation of a racing heart.

xFWE4M0.title: Straight urinary catheter
xFWE4M0.description: A transurethral catheter that is removed after drainage of the bladder, unlike a Foley catheter, which remains in place. Used to obtain a sterile urine sample or intermittently drain the bladder.

BFWz4M0.title: Benzonatate
BFWz4M0.description: A local anesthetic that suppresses cough via anesthesia of respiratory stretch receptors. Overdose can result in visual disturbances, tremors, and seizures.

yFWdkM0.title: Reticular vein
yFWdkM0.description: A small, dilated, subdermal vein, blue to green in color, with a diameter ≥ 1 mm and < 3 mm. Can develop in the lower extremities due to venous insufficiency. Corresponds to CEAP class C1 venous disease.

media.title: Telangiectasias, reticular veins, and corona phlebectatica

AFWRkM0.title: Adrenocorticotropic hormone gel
AFWRkM0.description: A gel preparation of a melanocortin peptide with direct antiinflammatory and immunomodulating actions. ACTH stimulates the adrenal cortex to increase cortisol production. Can be used in the treatment of several inflammatory conditions (e.g., multiple sclerosis, lupus, infantile spasms).

zFWrkM0.title: Premature closure bias
zFWrkM0.description: A cognitive bias in which a clinician prematurely accepts a diagnosis without verifying it and/or considering alternative causes. Can lead to misdiagnosis and delayed diagnosis.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

-FWDkM0.title: Overconfidence bias
-FWDkM0.description: A cognitive bias in which an individual assumes their skills and knowledge to be greater than they are in objective reality. Can result in false clinical decision-making, misdiagnosis, and patient harm.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

Z8WZOM0.title: Zebra retreat bias
Z8WZOM0.description: A cognitive bias in which a clinician is reluctant to consider a diagnosis because of its rarity, despite the existence of evidence that supports the diagnosis.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

08WeOM0.title: Canavan disease
08WeOM0.description: A genetic neurologic condition characterized by progressive degeneration of the white matter. Caused by deficiency of the enzyme aspartoacylase. Manifests during infancy with macrocephaly, lack of head control, and hypotonia.

a8WQOM0.title: Conjunction fallacy
a8WQOM0.description: The false assumption that the probability of a joint event (e.g., multiple clinical findings) is greater than the probability of any of the events occurring individually.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

U8WbNM0.title: Ambulatory venous pressure
U8WbNM0.description: An invasive test used to assess the severity of chronic venous insufficiency. A needle is inserted into the dorsal foot vein and attached to a pressure transducer; pressure measurements are taken before and after the patient performs an exercise, such as toe raises. Rarely used due to its invasive nature and the availability of other diagnostic tests.

28WTNM0.title: Radical nephroureterectomy
28WTNM0.description: A surgical procedure involving the removal of the kidney, renal pelvis, ureter, and the part of the bladder around the ureteral orifice (bladder cuff removal).

f8WkNM0.title: Venous clinical severity score
f8WkNM0.description: A scoring system used to assess the severity of chronic venous disease over time, with treatment. The following ten clinical factors are each scored from 0 (none) to 3 (severe): pain; varicose veins; venous edema; skin pigmentation; inflammation; induration; number, duration, and size of active ulcers; use of compression therapy. The individual scores are summed to obtain a total score.

T8W6NM0.title: CEAP class C0
T8W6NM0.description: The clinical class of CEAP in which there are no visible or palpable signs of chronic venous disease in the lower extremities.

g8WFNM0.title: CEAP class C1
g8WFNM0.description: The clinical class of CEAP in which telangiectasias and/or reticular veins are present in the lower extremities.

S8WyNM0.title: CEAP class C2
S8WyNM0.description: The clinical class of CEAP in which varicose veins are present in the lower extremities.

h8WcmM0.title: CEAP class C3
h8WcmM0.description: The clinical class of CEAP in which venous edema is present in the lower extremities.

38WSmM0.title: CEAP class C4
38WSmM0.description: The clinical class of CEAP in which changes in the skin or subcutaneous tissue of the lower extremities are present. Such changes may include pigmentation, stasis dermatitis, lipodermatosclerosis, atrophie blanche, and corona phlebectatica.

R8WlmM0.title: CEAP class C5
R8WlmM0.description: The clinical class of CEAP in which healed venous ulcers are present in the lower extremities.

i8WJmM0.title: CEAP class C6
i8WJmM0.description: The clinical class of CEAP in which active venous ulcers are present in the lower extremities.

Q8WumM0.title: Enteric oxalosis
Q8WumM0.description: An increase in intestinal absorption of oxalate due to conditions that lead to fat malabsorption. Results in increased oxalate excretion in urine. Often associated with Crohn disease and/or short bowel syndrome resulting from surgical resection.

k8Wm5M0.title: ASPA gene
k8Wm5M0.description: A gene located on chromosome 17 that encodes the enzyme aspartoacylase. Aspartoacylase is responsible for the metabolism of N-acetylaspartic acid (NAA) in the brain. Mutation of this gene is associated with Canavan disease.

O8WI5M0.title: Nonneoplastic-physiologic hypercortisolism
O8WI5M0.description: A type of endogenous hypercortisolism that can occur with many common conditions, e.g., uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, heavy alcohol use, major depressive disorder, obesity, and physical stress, and in pregnant patients. In contrast to endogenous Cushing syndrome, the cause of hypercortisolism is nonneoplastic.

m8WVMM0.title: Dental fluorosis
m8WVMM0.description: A condition caused by excessive consumption of fluoride or excessive use of fluoride toothpaste. Dental fluorosis is characterized by porous, mottling, and opaque white staining of the enamel and only occurs in children ≤ 6 years old.

58WiMM0.title: Skeletal fluorosis
58WiMM0.description: A condition caused by excessive consumption of fluoride, typically due to very high levels in drinking water. Skeletal fluorosis manifests with joint pain and stiffness and with bone and joint deformities.

M8WMMM0.title: Popeye sign
M8WMMM0.description: Distal displacement of the biceps belly on contraction, following a proximal biceps tendon tear. Named after the cartoon character Popeye, known for his bulging biceps upon eating spinach.

destinations.label: Biceps tendinopathy and biceps tendon rupture → Clinical features

L8WwMM0.title: Bridging therapy
L8WwMM0.description: A temporary strategy used to stabilize patients until a long-term treatment becomes available (e.g., the use of mechanical circulatory devices in patients awaiting heart transplant) or until a concomitantly administered long-term treatment reaches therapeutic levels (e.g., the use of low molecular weight heparin in patients starting warfarin therapy).

68WjnM0.title: Unna boot
68WjnM0.description: An inelastic compression bandage that is impregnated with zinc oxide. Can decrease edema, inflammation, and pruritus, and promote wound healing. Used on the lower extremities to treat post-operative wounds or advanced chronic venous disease (e.g., stasis dermatitis or venous ulcers). Must be changed weekly.

q8WCnM0.title: Pelvic examination
q8WCnM0.description: A physical examination of female genitalia and reproductive organs. Typically involves a visual examination of the external genitalia, bimanual palpation of the uterus and adnexa, and a speculum examination to visualize the vagina and cervix.

destinations.label: OB/GYN: history and physical examination → Gynecologic examination

78W4LM0.title: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
78W4LM0.description: A rare condition that typically manifests in the third decade of life with eye pain, uveitis, vertigo, nausea, headaches, and vitiligo. Thought to be caused by a dysregulated immune response to human leukocyte antigen.

destinations.label: Diseases of the uvea → Rare conditions

H8WKLM0.title: Sunset-glow fundus
H8WKLM0.description: A funduscopic finding in individuals with Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease. Characterized by an inflamed choroid with orange-red discoloration due to depigmentation.

destinations.label: Diseases of the uvea → Rare conditions

G8WBLM0.title: RIPE TB regimen
G8WBLM0.description: A first-line drug regimen used to treat active tuberculosis consisting of rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.

t8WXoM0.title: Australian bat lyssavirus
t8WXoM0.description: A virus of the Lyssavirus genus that is endemic to Australia. Can be transmitted to humans via bat bite, scratch, and direct contact with saliva. Manifestations are similar to rabies, including headache, paralysis, delirium, and, ultimately, death.

98WNKM0.title: Australian bat lyssavirus infection
98WNKM0.description: An infection with the Australian bat lyssavirus, which causes a syndrome indistinguishable from rabies. Transmission occurs via infected bats (e.g., bite, scratch, contact with saliva).

C8WqKM0.title: Lingual thyroid
C8WqKM0.description: A rare, abnormal mass of ectopic thyroid tissue at the base of tongue. Caused by a failure of the thyroid gland to descend to its normal position during embryogenesis.

destinations.label: Thyroid gland and parathyroid glands →  Embryology

x8WEKM0.title: Lupus miliaris disseminatus faciei
x8WEKM0.description: A rare inflammatory granulomatous dermatosis characterized by the development of multiple red-brown papules on the face (particularly the central face, lower eyelids, forehead, and nasolabial folds). Spontaneous resolution of lesions often occurs within 1–3 years but can leave scarring.

A8WR6M0.title: Hendra virus
A8WR6M0.description: A virus of the Paramyxoviridae family that belongs to the Henipavirus genus. Its natural reservoir is the flying fox, which transmits the virus via bodily fluids to horses. Human contact with an infected horse can result in severe respiratory, flu-like disease that can progress to encephalitis.

_8W56M0.title: Henipavirus
_8W56M0.description: A genus of linear, nonsegmented, negative-strand RNA viruses that belongs to the Paramyxoviridae family. Its natural reservoir is bats. Examples include Hendra virus, Nipah virus, and Kumasi virus.

z8Wr6M0.title: Hendra virus disease
z8Wr6M0.description: An extremely rare disease (< 10 cases have been reported) caused by infection with Hendra virus. Transmitted via contact with bodily fluids of infected horses, therefore, individuals with exposure to horses (e.g., veterinarians, equestrians) are at increased risk. After 9-16 days, infected individuals develop a severe, flu-like respiratory disease that can progress to encephalitis. Mortality is high (∼ 60%). No specific treatment available. A postexposure prophylaxis with neutralizing antibodies is currently under development.

ZuWZpM0.title: Metamizole
ZuWZpM0.description: A drug that is thought to inhibit central cyclooxygenases and activate endogenous pain-modulating systems, which leads to analgesic, antipyretic, and spasmolytic effects. Adverse effects include hypotonia, allergic reactions, and, in very rare cases, agranulocytosis. Not commercially available in the United States.

auWQpM0.title: Palmoplantar pustulosis
auWQpM0.description: A chronic inflammatory skin condition that manifests with sterile vesicles and pustules on the palms and soles. Often accompanied by pruritus or pain and can result in painful fissuring. Most common in individuals between 40 and 60 years of age.

buWHpM0.title: Buruli ulcer
buWHpM0.description: A necrotizing infection caused by Mycobacterium ulcerans. Often transmitted by skin contact with contaminated water. Typically begins as a painless nodule that slowly ulcerates with undermined edges. Can progress to involve deeper tissue (e.g., tendon, bone).

1uW2JM0.title: Gyromitra mushroom
1uW2JM0.description: A poisonous mushroom species found in Europe and North America that contains the toxin gyromitrin. Poisoning following ingestion typically manifests with vomiting and gastrointestinal discomfort and may lead to liver failure, renal failure, and signs of central nervous system toxicity (e.g., seizures).

WuWPJM0.title: Chemoprophylaxis
WuWPJM0.description: The administration of a medication to prevent disease. Examples include the use of antibiotics to prevent infections in individuals who are immunocompromised, the use of anticoagulants to prevent deep venous thrombosis, and the use of statins to prevent cardiovascular disease.

VuWGJM0.title: Gastrectomy
VuWGJM0.description: The surgical removal of all or part of the stomach. Typically performed as part of the treatment for gastric cancer.

euWxJM0.title: Subtotal gastrectomy
euWxJM0.description: The surgical removal of a portion of the stomach. Indications include gastric neoplasms and severe gastric ulcer disease.

huWcIM0.title: Diaphragmatic hernia
huWcIM0.description: The protrusion of intraabdominal contents through a congenital or acquired defect in the diaphragm, into the chest cavity.

media.title: Posttraumatic diaphragmatic hernia simulating diaphragm elevation

kuWmrM0.title: CDC STEADI algorithm for falls
kuWmrM0.description: A strategy used to reduce the risk of falls in community-dwelling older adults. Includes a screen for risk of falls, a comprehensive assessment of recent falls and modifiable risk factors, and tailored interventions for fall prevention.

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Screening for geriatric syndromes

OuWIrM0.title: Breakthrough seizure
OuWIrM0.description: The occurrence of a seizure in a patient with epilepsy following a period of sustained remission on antiepileptic drug therapy. Common causes include missed medication doses, new drug interactions, and triggers such as alcohol consumption, recreational drug use, sleep deprivation, and intercurrent illness.

muWV7M0.title: Gastrocolic reflex
muWV7M0.description: The neural activation of colonic peristalsis that occurs when stomach cells are stretched following a meal.

5uWi7M0.title: Normal transit constipation
5uWi7M0.description: A subtype of primary constipation (i.e., constipation with no identifiable secondary cause) in which the patient reports symptoms of constipation (e.g., bloating, hard stools, difficulty evacuating stools), but colonic transit time is normal on a motility study.

MuWM7M0.title: Canadian Study of Health and Aging clinical frailty scale
MuWM7M0.description: A scale used to classify the fitness or frailty level of older adults. Based on a clinical assessment of mobility, balance, and the person's ability to perform basic and instrumental activities of daily living. Scores range from 1 (very fit) to 9 (terminally ill), with frailty ranging from a score of 4 (living with very mild frailty) to 8 (living with very severe frailty).

ouW0HM0.title: Memory Impairment Screen
ouW0HM0.description: A four-item screen of cognitive impairment that tests delayed recall and takes approximately four minutes to complete.

KuWUHM0.title: Six-item screener
KuWUHM0.description: A brief cognitive screening tool that assesses orientation and delayed recall. Can be administered face-to-face or over the telephone.

JuWsHM0.title: Adenoidectomy
JuWsHM0.description: The surgical excision of the adenoids. Used to treat chronic or recurrent otitis media, otitis media with effusion (glue ear), reccurent sinusitis, and severe nasal obstruction (e.g., obstructive sleep apnea).

quWCHM0.title: Biliary obstruction
quWCHM0.description: A blockage in the ducts that transport bile from the liver to the small intestine. Can cause biliary colic, nausea, vomiting, and jaundice. The most frequent cause is gallstones; other common causes include malignancy and cysts.

ruWfsM0.title: Pocket infection
ruWfsM0.description: A localized infection of the subcutaneous space in which a surgically implanted device (e.g., pacemaker) is located.

7uW4sM0.title: Fracture fixation device
7uW4sM0.description: A type of orthopedic hardware used to immobilize broken bones. Composed of intramedullary nails, external fixation pins, plates, and screws.

suWtsM0.title: Recurrent acute otitis media
suWtsM0.description: The occurrence of ≥ 3 episodes of acute otitis media within 6 months or ≥ 4 episodes of acute otitis media within 12 months.

GuWBsM0.title: Cortical cataract
GuWBsM0.description: A type of cataract that originates in the outer layer of the lens and grows toward the center, forming a wedge-shaped opacity.

tuWXGM0.title: Nuclear cataract
tuWXGM0.description: A type of cataract that affects the center of the lens. May appear as an opacification or yellow-brown discoloration of the lens area.

FuWgGM0.title: Subcapsular cataract
FuWgGM0.description: A type of cataract that occurs within the lens capsule. Can manifest behind the posterior or anterior lens capsule. Posterior subcapsular cataracts are often rapidly progressive and are more common than anterior subcapsular cataracts.

8uWOGM0.title: Immature cataract
8uWOGM0.description: An early stage of cataract progression. Opacities can be seen but the red reflex is still present, and it is possible to visualize the retina.

uuWpGM0.title: Mature cataract
uuWpGM0.description: An advanced stage of cataract progression characterized by complete clouding of the lens and white or yellow-brown discoloration. The red reflex is absent and visual acuity is generally reduced.

EuW8GM0.title: Hypermature cataract
EuW8GM0.description: The end stage of cataract progression. Characterized by complete white clouding of the lens due to liquification of the cortex. The nucleus often sinks in the cortex and appears brown.

vuWAGM0.title: Clinical features of bowel obstruction
vuWAGM0.description: Symptoms of bowel obstruction include abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation, and abdominal distention. Physical findings include tympany on abdominal percussion, high-pitched bowel sounds, and an empty rectal vault.

DuW1tM0.title: Infant dyschezia
DuW1tM0.description: A benign condition in which healthy infants aged < 9 months strain and/or cry for at least 10 minutes before defecation. Stools are typically soft or liquid and of normal frequency. Caused by an inability to coordinate abdominal contractions with pelvic floor relaxation and typically resolves within a few weeks.

wuWhtM0.title: Congenital cataract
wuWhtM0.description: A clouding of the lens present at birth. Etiologies include infections, genetic mutations, and metabolic disorders.

AuWRFM0.title: Antireflux surgery
AuWRFM0.description: A group of procedures used to treat reflux symptoms (e.g., in patients with symptoms refractory to medical therapy). Includes endoscopic procedures (e.g., radiofrequency treatment, transoral incisionless fundoplication) and surgical procedures (e.g., magnetic sphincter augmentation, laparoscopic Hill gastropexy, laparoscopic fundoplication).

_uW5FM0.title: Nevus of Ota
_uW5FM0.description: A pigmentary disorder characterized by coalescing blue-gray macules in the distribution of the ophthalmic and/or maxillary branches of the trigeminal nerve. Typically unilateral and frequently involves the eye (e.g., sclera, conjunctiva, uvea). Can rarely undergo malignant transformation (e.g., uveal melanoma). More common in individuals with darker skin pigmentation.

zuWrFM0.title: Nevus of Ito
zuWrFM0.description: A pigmentary disorder characterized by coalescing blue-gray macules in the distribution of the posterior supraclavicular and/or lateral cutaneous brachial nerves. Can be seen in association with a nevus of Ota. Very rarely associated with malignant transformation. More common in individuals with darker skin pigmentation.

-uWDFM0.title: Nevus of Hori
-uWDFM0.description: An acquired pigmentary disorder characterized by the development of coalescing blue-gray macules, typically in the bilateral zygomatic areas. Most common among adult women of Chinese and Japanese descent. In contrast to a nevus of Ota, it does not involve the eye.

ZEWZ8M0.title: High-risk chromosomal abnormalities in multiple myeloma
ZEWZ8M0.description: Cytogenetic abnormalities that confer a poor prognosis in multiple myeloma. Include the following: t(4;14), t(14;16), t(14;20), deletion 17p, gain 1q, p53 mutation.

0EWe8M0.title: Actinic prurigo
0EWe8M0.description: A chronic dermatologic condition characterized by the development of pruritic papulonodules and plaques induced by exposure to ultraviolet radiation. Associated with conjunctivitis and cheilitis. More prevalent in individuals of Native American and Mestizo ancestry.

aEWQ8M0.title: Heparin resistance
aEWQ8M0.description: A state in which therapeutic doses of unfractionated heparin do not achieve the desired effect on the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) and activated coagulation time (ACT). Most commonly caused by antithrombin III deficiency.

YEWn8M0.title: Smoldering multiple myeloma
YEWn8M0.description: An asymptomatic clonal plasma cell dyscrasia. Differentiated from monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) by a significantly higher risk of progression to multiple myeloma. Management is usually expectant unless at least two out of three high-risk features are present (serum monoclonal protein > 2 g/dL, serum-free light chain ratio > 20, or bone marrow plasma cells > 20%).

bEWH8M0.title: Arteriovenous graft
bEWH8M0.description: A surgical connection for renal replacement therapies (e.g., hemodialysis, hemofiltration), in which a synthetic tube is used to connect an artery and a vein. Compared to an AV fistula, an AV graft can be used sooner because it does not require a period of maturation; it also carries a higher risk of thrombosis and infection.

destinations.label: Renal replacement therapy → Hemodialysis and hemofiltration

XEW98M0.title: Conditioning regimen
XEW98M0.description: A series of treatments that prepare a patient for stem cell transplantation. Help eliminate residual cancer cells and prevent rejection of transplanted cells. Regimens may include chemotherapy, systemic immunomodulatory drugs, and whole-body radiation therapy.

cEWauM0.title: Bifid uvula
cEWauM0.description: A split or forked uvula, typically containing less muscule tissue than a normal uvula. A bifid uvula may be a sign of a submucosal cleft of the palate.

destinations.label: Cleft lip and cleft palate → Clinical features

dEWouM0.title: Pulmonary rehabilitation
dEWouM0.description: A supervised program for individuals with chronic lung disease (e.g., COPD, interstitial lung disease, cystic fibrosis) that combines health education, exercise training, nutrition counseling, and behavioral health interventions to help patients achieve and maintain their optimal level of function and independence.

VEWGuM0.title: Muscle enzymes
VEWGuM0.description: A group of enzymes found in high levels in skeletal muscle cells. Includes creatinine phosphokinase, aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, lactate dehydrogenase, and aldolase. Increased levels of muscle enzymes in the serum can result from any injury to skeletal muscle cells.

eEWxuM0.title: Examination of extraocular muscles
eEWxuM0.description: A part of the ophthalmologic examination that tests movements of the eye. Instruct the patient to follow your finger while keeping the head immobile. Stand in front of the patient and trace a letter "H" in the air, then move your finger towards the patient's nose to test for accommodation. Absent or reduced eye movement in any direction can indicate a cranial nerve deficit.

destinations.label: Examination of the eye → Examination of extraocular muscles

UEWbEM0.title: Dialysate
UEWbEM0.description: A solution containing water, electrolytes, and salts. Used during dialysis (e.g., hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis) to create a difference in concentration gradients with the blood or peritoneal fluid, thereby promoting diffusion of solutes across a semipermeable membrane.

TEW6EM0.title: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine 15
TEW6EM0.description: A conjugate vaccine that protects against 15 subtypes of S. pneumoniae. The minimum age for the first dose is 6 weeks old.

SEWyEM0.title: Posterior malleolus
SEWyEM0.description: The posterior segment of the distal end of the tibia.

hEWcvM0.title: Bimalleolar fracture
hEWcvM0.description: A fracture of the lateral and medial malleoli. Usually caused by injury due to supination or external rotation. Manifestations include pain, swelling, bruising, deformity, and inability to bear weight. Most commonly occurs in older women, young males, and individuals over 60 years of age.

iEWJvM0.title: Calot triangle
iEWJvM0.description: An anatomical space formed by the common hepatic duct, the cystic duct, and the cystic artery. Often confused with the hepatobiliary triangle.

4EW3DM0.title: Metastatic infection
4EW3DM0.description: A secondary focus of infection in an anatomically distant site from the primary site of infection. Examples include pulmonary or brain abscesses resulting from hematogenous seeding of bacteria from an infected heart valve.

kEWmDM0.title: Mycobacterium ulcerans
kEWmDM0.description: An acid-fast, gram-positive bacillus that can cause chronic, necrotizing ulcers (i.e., Buruli ulcer).

nEW7wM0.title: Endoscopic submucosal dissection
nEW7wM0.description: The endoscopic resection of GI tract epithelial lesions that have not invaded the muscular layer. This technique can allow for curative therapy of early-stage cancer of the esophagus, stomach, colon, or rectum without surgery or chemotherapy.

LEWwwM0.title: Ramucirumab
LEWwwM0.description: A recombinant monoclonal antibody that binds to the vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) and inhibits the VEGF–VEGFR2 pathway. Used in the treatment of advanced gastric cancer, metastatic colon cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and select hepatocellular carcinomas.

oEW09M0.title: Peritoneovenous shunt
oEW09M0.description: A conduit with a one-way valve that connects the peritoneal cavity and the systemic venous system. Used in the treatment of refractory ascites to allow continuous drainage of peritoneal fluid into the venous system, typically through a subcutaneous catheter that drains into the internal jugular or subclavian vein.

6EWj9M0.title: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine 20
6EWj9M0.description: An inactivated conjugate vaccine that protects against 20 subtypes of S. pneumoniae. The minimum age for the first dose is 6 weeks old.

pEWL9M0.title: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine
pEWL9M0.description: A vaccine that consists of pneumococcal capsular polysaccharide antigens that are conjugated with a protein that is nearly identical to diphtheria toxin. Linkage to the toxin faciltates the recognition and processing of the polysaccharide antigen by the immune system. Several formulations with varying numbers of capsular types are available, including PCV15, PCV20, and PCV 21.

qEWC9M0.title: Buprenorphine waiver
qEWC9M0.description: A waiver issued by the US federal government that allows a practitioner to administer, dispense, and prescribe buprenorphine for medication-assisted treatment of opioid use disorder in outpatient settings. Also referred to as an "x-waiver."

7EW4CM0.title: Serial abdominal examination
7EW4CM0.description: The reexamination of a patient's abdomen at regular intervals (e.g., every 4 hours) after an initial (baseline) abdominal examination. Commonly performed in patients with acute abdominal pain or trauma to determine if the patient's condition is stable or deteriorating.

sEWtCM0.title: Equipoise
sEWtCM0.description: A situation in which the benefits and risks of two or more medical interventions are thought to be generally equivalent. This principle underlies the ethical basis for the randomization of patients to different treatment arms in a clinical trial.

GEWBCM0.title: Hawkins sign
GEWBCM0.description: A radiographic sign that is characterized by subchondral radiolucency of the talar dome and indicates sufficient vascularity of the talus and a low risk of avascular necrosis. If present, the Hawkins sign is usually seen on x-rays 6-8 weeks after injury.

EEW8xM0.title: Mortise view
EEW8xM0.description: An anteroposterior x-ray view obtained by positioning the ankle with 15°–20° of internal rotation. It is used to better visualize the distal tibia, distal fibula, talus, and proximal fifth metatarsal.

vEWAxM0.title: Canale view
vEWAxM0.description: An x-ray projection obtained by placing the ankle in full plantar flexion, pronating the foot 15°, and positioning the x-ray beam at a 75° angle. It is used to better visualize the talar neck.

wEWhBM0.title: Clinical features of pyelonephritis
wEWhBM0.description: A group of signs and symptoms that suggest infection involving the upper urinary tract (e.g., kidneys). Includes flank pain, costovertebral angle tenderness, and features of systemic infection (e.g., fever, chills, nausea, weakness). Lower urinary tract symptoms (e.g., dysuria, urgency, frequency) may also be present.

9EWNBM0.title: Malunion
9EWNBM0.description: A fractured bone that heals in an abnormal or suboptimal position. Clinical features include limb-length discrepancies, rotated or bent appearance, and impaired limb function. Treatment usually requires osteotomy.

zEWryM0.title: Urinalysis findings of UTI
zEWryM0.description: Findings include pyuria (i.e., positive leukocyte esterase or microscopy with ≥ 5 WBCs/HPF) and bacteriuria (i.e., positive urinary nitrates or microscopic visualization of bacteria).

-EWDyM0.title: Vocal cord paralysis
-EWDyM0.description: Impaired mobility of one or both of the vocal cords due to dysfunction of the recurrent laryngeal nerve or vagus nerve. Causes include infection, neoplasm, and iatrogenic injury (e.g., thyroid surgery). Unilateral injury (more common) can be asymptomatic, or it can cause voice change, difficulty swallowing, and/or shortness of breath. Bilateral injury typically causes airway compromise and requires surgical intervention.

destinations.label: Cranial nerve palsies → Vagus nerve palsy (X)

0vWeAM0.title: Unhealthy drug use
0vWeAM0.description: The use of illegal drugs or the nonmedical use of prescription medications, such as using another person's prescription or taking medications in greater amounts or for longer than prescribed.

avWQAM0.title: Risk factors for MDRO infection
avWQAM0.description: Features associated with a greater risk of colonization or infection by an organism resistant to ≥ 1 antimicrobial agent. Examples include prolonged hospitalization, prior antibiotic use, indwelling medical devices, and prior infection, colonization, or exposure to a multidrug-resistant organism.

bvWHAM0.title: Hospital withdrawal management
bvWHAM0.description: An inpatient withdrawal treatment program for individuals who require 24-hour monitoring, active medical management, and access to addiction services. Indicated for patients who are unstable, have severe withdrawal, and/or have coingestions or comorbidities that necessitate hospitalization (e.g., polysubstance overdose attempt, sepsis).

destinations.label: Substance-related and addictive disorders → Management of substance use disorder

XvW9AM0.title: ​​​​​​​Residential withdrawal management
XvW9AM0.description: An inpatient withdrawal treatment program with 24-hour nursing support. Typically reserved for individuals with severe withdrawal who are unlikely to complete outpatient withdrawal treatment and require daily access to a physician. Colloquially referred to as "detox" programs.

1vW2_M0.title: Outpatient withdrawal management
1vW2_M0.description: A withdrawal program with low patient oversight in which primary care physicians prescribe medications for outpatient use. Usually reserved for stable patients with a secure home environment and high general functioning who need daily or less than daily support.

2vWTzM0.title: Skin of color
2vWTzM0.description: Skin with higher pigmentation than that traditionally associated with Northern European heritage. Certain dermatological conditions (e.g., pseudofolliculitis barbae, keloids) are seen more commonly in individuals with skin of color.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Skin of color

3vWS-M0.title: li blood group system
3vWS-M0.description: A blood group system based on the I antigen, which is found in the cell membrane of red blood cells in all adults, and the i antigen, which is found only in red blood cells of the developing fetus and newborn infants.

RvWl-M0.title: Antidepressant-induced mania
RvWl-M0.description: A manic or hypomanic episode precipitated by antidepressant use in a person with undiagnosed bipolar disorder.

ivWJ-M0.title: Hepatic infarction
ivWJ-M0.description: A rare, ischemic injury of the liver that is usually caused by obstruction of the intrahepatic branch of the hepatic artery (e.g., from iatrogenic ligation of the hepatic artery during cholecystectomy, thrombus, or embolus). May be asymptomatic or manifest with fever, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and back or right shoulder pain.

QvWu-M0.title: Prism glasses
QvWu-M0.description: Glasses with a prismatic correction that improves diplopia by redirecting light to the correct place on the retina. The prism may be permanently ground into the lens, or it can be applied temporarily (e.g., as a vinyl sticker placed on top of the glasses lens, also known as a Fresnel prism).

jvW_-M0.title: Blunt cardiac injury
jvW_-M0.description: An injury to the heart resulting from blunt force trauma. Includes cardiac contusion, arrythmias, myocardial rupture, pericardial injury, septal and valvular injury, and coronary artery injury.

4vW3Zn0.title: Waddell triad
4vW3Zn0.description: A clinical triad commonly seen in children who sustain direct blunt force trauma from the impact of a motor vehicle. Consists of contralateral head injury, ipsilateral femoral shaft fracture, and ipsilateral intrathoracic or intraabdominal injury.

OvWIZn0.title: Handlebar injury
OvWIZn0.description: An abdominal injury caused by directly striking the handlebar of a bicycle or scooter. Includes hepatic lacerations and injury to the pancreas, spleen, mesentery, and/or hollow organs (e.g., bowel).

lvWvZn0.title: Hypertrophic neuropathy
lvWvZn0.description: A histopathological finding in demyelinating types of polyneuropathies in which cells are layered on top of each other, resembling onion bulbs. Occurs as a result of repeated demyelination and remyelination.

NvW-Zn0.title: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
NvW-Zn0.description: A gestational trophoblastic disease with malignant behavior. Includes invasive moles, postmolar gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, gestational choriocarcinoma, placental site trophoblastic tumors, and epitheliod trophoblastic tumors.

destinations.label: Gestational trophoblastic disease → Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia

5vWi0n0.title: Fasciocutaneous flap
5vWi0n0.description: A type of soft tissue reconstruction used to repair large defects. Composed of skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia, and an associated vessel that typically arises in fascial planes in between muscles. In contrast to skin grafts, fasciocutaneous flaps have their own blood supply and do not depend on adequate vascularization of the recipient site.

MvWM0n0.title: Renal hematoma
MvWM0n0.description: A collection of blood within the renal parenchyma due to parenchymal or renal vessel injury. Common causes include blunt force abdominal trauma and penetrating trauma. Clinical features include flank tenderness, ecchymosis, and hematuria.

nvW70n0.title: Liver elastography
nvW70n0.description: An imaging technique that measures liver stiffness to determine the degree of fibrosis. Elastography is performed using ultrasound (i.e., transient elastography) or magnetic resonance imaging.

KvWUan0.title: Diversion colitis
KvWUan0.description: An inflammatory condition that only occurs in defunctioned intestinal segments (e.g., following colostomy, colovaginoplasty, or ileostomy). The pathogenesis is unclear; may result from bacterial overgrowth, nutrient deficiency, ischemia, and disruption of the mucin layer. The remaining GI tract is unaffected.

6vWjan0.title: Neovagina
6vWjan0.description: A surgically created vagina that is most commonly formed from inverted penile or scrotal skin, skin grafts, and/or ileum or sigmoid bowel segments. Created for transgender patients or patients with a congenitally absent vagina (e.g., Mullerian agenesis).

JvWsan0.title: Persistent allergic rhinitis
JvWsan0.description: Symptoms of allergic rhinitis (i.e., nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, itchy nose, sneezing) last for > 4 days/week for > 4 weeks/year.

qvWCan0.title: Seasonal allergic rhinitis
qvWCan0.description: A type of allergic rhinitis characterized by symptoms (i.e., nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, itchy nose, sneezing) that occur on exposure to allergens that occur during particular seasons (e.g., hay fever, which is caused by exposure to pollen)

IvWYYn0.title: Moderate to severe allergic rhinitis
IvWYYn0.description: Symptoms of allergic rhinitis (i.e., nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, itchy nose, sneezing) interfere with the quality of life (e.g., they lead to exacerbations of coexisting asthma, decreased sleep, impaired school performance, inability to carry out daily activities)

7vW4Yn0.title: Episodic allergic rhinitis
7vW4Yn0.description: A type of allergic rhinitis characterized by symptoms (i.e., nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, itchy nose, sneezing) that occur on exposure to allergens that are not normally a part of the individual's environment (e.g., a visit to a farm)

HvWKYn0.title: Perennial allergic rhinitis
HvWKYn0.description: A type of allergic rhinitis characterized by symptoms (i.e., nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, itchy nose, sneezing) that occur on exposure to allergens that are normally a part of the patient's environment (e.g., allergic rhinitis caused by house dust, animal dander from a pet, or dust mites)

svWtYn0.title: Intermittent allergic rhinitis
svWtYn0.description: Symptoms of allergic rhinitis (i.e., nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, itchy nose, sneezing) last for < 4 days/week or < 4 weeks/year.

GvWBYn0.title: Mild allergic rhinitis
GvWBYn0.description: Symptoms of allergic rhinitis (i.e., nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, itchy nose, sneezing) do not interfere with the quality of life.

tvWXbn0.title: Recombinant zoster vaccine
tvWXbn0.description: A recombinant vaccine that provides immunity against varicella-zoster virus (HHV-3), the pathogen responsible for chickenpox and shingles. Recommended for individuals ≥ 50 years and individuals ≥ 19 years of age who have a history of immunosuppression, regardless of any history of shingles.

8vWObn0.title: Clinical Opioid Withdrawal Scale
8vWObn0.description: A validated tool that can be used to assess and classify the severity of opioid withdrawal. Commonly used to objectively verify opioid withdrawal symptoms prior to initiating opioid withdrawal treatment with buprenorphine.

uvWpbn0.title: PAIR procedure
uvWpbn0.description: A minimally invasive procedure used to treat hydatid liver cysts. Consists of ultrasound- or CT-guided percutaneous puncture (P) of the cyst, aspiration (A) of its contents, injection (I) of a scolicidal agent (e.g., hypertonic saline, ethanol), and reaspiration (R) after ≥ 15 minutes. This procedure is repeated until the reaspirated contents are clear. The cyst is then filled with isotonic sodium chloride solution.

EvW8bn0.title: Scolicidal agent
EvW8bn0.description: A group of agents used to treat hydatid cysts (e.g., during the PAIR procedure). Includes formalin, hydrogen peroxide, hypertonic saline, chlorhexidine, absolute alcohol, and cetrimide.

vvWAbn0.title: Sclerosing mesenteritis
vvWAbn0.description: An idiopathic autoimmune condition that is characterized by inflammation, fat necrosis, and fibrosis of the bowel mesentery and is often diagnosed incidentally based on CT scan findings. Often asymptomatic, but symptoms may include abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, constipation, nausea, vomiting, and/or weight loss.

DvW1Xn0.title: Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma
DvW1Xn0.description: A rare type of fibrosarcoma characterized histopathologically by alternating collagenous and myxoid components with spindle cells arranged in whorling patterns. Clinically manifests as a painless, slow-growing mass, usually located in the proximal extremities and/or trunk.

wvWhXn0.title: CTNNB1 gene
wvWhXn0.description: The gene that encodes the protein beta-catenin, which is involved in cell signaling as a part of the Wnt signaling pathway. Mutations in CTNNB1 lead to the accumulation of beta-catenin and the formation of desmoid tumors.

AvWRcn0.title: Impaired hypoglycemia awareness
AvWRcn0.description: A complication of diabetes (especially type 1) in which typical symptoms of hypoglycemia do not develop. It is common in individuals with recurrent hypoglycemic episodes and increases the risk of severe hypoglycemia.

_vW5cn0.title: Proctocolitis
_vW5cn0.description: Inflammation of the rectum that extends beyond the rectosigmoid junction into the colon. May occur secondary to infection with enteric or sexually transmitted pathogens, as part of inflammatory bowel disease, or secondary to radiation or ischemia. Characteristic features include diarrhea, anorectal pain, abdominal cramping, anal discharge, and tenesmus.

-vWDcn0.title: Serotype
-vWDcn0.description: A subgroup within a species of microorganisms that share a specific surface antigen. Different serotypes can produce different clinical presentations and illness severities. Examples of pathogens with multiple serotypes include Salmonella (> 2,500 known serotypes) and Chlamydia trachomatis (19 serotypes).

XDW91n0.title: Progressive outer retinal necrosis
XDW91n0.description: A condition characterized by rapidly progressive necrosis of the retina in individuals who are immunocompromised (e.g., due to AIDS). Manifestations include blurred vision, visual loss, and eye pain due to necrosis of the outer retina and/or posterior pole. Can progress to retinal detachment. Unlike acute retinal necrosis, PORN is associated with limited intraocular inflammation. Most commonly caused by varicella-zoster virus.

cDWaWn0.title: LP
cDWaWn0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Lumbar puncture
2. Lichen planus

1DW2Wn0.title: Tuskegee syphilis study
1DW2Wn0.description: An infamous study to investigate the outcomes of untreated syphilis, conducted between 1932 and 1972 by the US Public Health Service and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention at the Tuskegee Institute in Alabama. The study followed a group of 399 low-income African American men who had syphilis but who were not informed of their diagnosis and were denied penicillin therapy, even after it become the standard treatment in 1947. By the time the study ended in scandal, 128 of the men had died from syphilis or its complications, 40 of the participants' wives had been infected, and 19 children were born with congenital syphilis.

dDWoWn0.title: Acute retinal necrosis
dDWoWn0.description: A condition characterized by rapidly progressive necrosis of the retina, which typically manifests with blurred vision, visual loss, and eye pain due to iridocyclitis, vitritis, necrotizing retinitis, and/or occlusive retinal vasculitis. Can progress to retinal detachment. Unlike progressive outer retinal necrosis (PORN), ARN is associated with significant intraocular inflammation. Most commonly caused by varicella-zoster virus.

eDWxWn0.title: Social skills training
eDWxWn0.description: A type of behavioral training for patients who have difficulty with everyday activities (e.g., social interaction, independent living, personal care) due to psychiatric or developmental conditions. Examples include breaking down complex social interactions (e.g., conversations) into simple steps and interpreting information in a context-appropriate manner (e.g., evaluating potential responses to a given stimulus).

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Social skills training

UDWbdn0.title: Assertive community treatment
UDWbdn0.description: An integrated treatment approach for patients with severe psychiatric conditions (e.g., schizophrenia, bipolar disorder) who are at ongoing risk of hospitalization, incarceration, and/or unstable housing. The goal is to provide resources and support outside of health care institutions (e.g., home, public parks, and shelters) to promote recovery and stable community living.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care access

2DWTdn0.title: Digital pressure test
2DWTdn0.description: A test used to diagnose the presence of an abscess in paronychia. Light pressure is applied to the volar aspect of the affected fingertip. Identification of a well-demarcated area of blanching after application of pressure indicates abscess.

fDWkdn0.title: Six Ps of cutaneous lichen planus
fDWkdn0.description: The 6 Ps of lichen planus summarize the main clinical features of lichen planus: purple, polygonal, planar, pruritic, papules, and plaques. Sometimes referred to as 5 Ps of lichen planus (with purple papules counted as one feature).

TDW6dn0.title: Passive rewarming
TDW6dn0.description: A treatment for hypothermia that uses insulating materials (e.g., blankets) to promote heat retention to increase core body temperature without the application of external heat.

gDWFdn0.title: Active rewarming
gDWFdn0.description: A treatment for hypothermia that uses an external heat source to increase core body temperature. Active rewarming can be external (e.g., using heating pads or warm humidified air) or internal (e.g., using thoracic or peritoneal lavage with warm fluids or hemodialysis).

SDWydn0.title: Immersion injury
SDWydn0.description: A nonfreezing cold injury that occurs if the feet are exposed to wet and cold environments for long periods of time; can result in chronic pain. Immersion injury commonly affects individuals experiencing homelessness and military personnel.

destinations.label: Hypothermia and frostbite → Nonfreezing cold injuries

media.title: Nonfreezing cold injury (immersion foot, trench foot)

kDWmen0.title: Food insecurity
kDWmen0.description: A lack of access to a sufficient amount of nutritious food. Food insecurity is considered a social determinant of health and is affected by other socioeconomic, geographic, and cultural factors (e.g., impaired access to culturally appropriate food, lack of transportation).

ODWIen0.title: FRAIL scale
ODWIen0.description: A tool used to assess frailty in older adults, based on five elements that form the acronym FRAIL: fatigue, resistance (difficulty walking up stairs), ambulation (difficulty walking a few hundred yards), illnesses (presence of ≥ 5), and loss of weight (≥ 5% of body weight in the past 12 months). Each element is worth one point, with a score of 1-2 indicating prefrailty, and 3-5 indicating frailty.

lDWven0.title: Hypomethylating agents
lDWven0.description: A group of antineoplastic nucleoside metabolic inhibitors used to treat hematologic disorders that are characterized by immature myeloid cell lines (e.g., myelodysplastic syndromes, AML, chronic myelomonocytic leukemia). They work by inhibiting DNA methylation, which alters epigenetic gene expression and allows myeloid cell lines to differentiate and mature. Examples include azacytidine and decitabine. Myelosuppression is the most common adverse effect.

mDWVUn0.title: Second cancer
mDWVUn0.description: The development of a type of cancer that is unrelated to a patient's current or previous cancer diagnosis, but that may share the underlying etiology (e.g., tobacco smoking, familial cancer syndromes). Second cancers may also occur as an adverse effect of the primary cancer treatment; radiotherapy or certain types of chemotherapy (e.g., alkylating agents) have been implicated.

LDWwUn0.title: Palliative chemotherapy
LDWwUn0.description: A regimen of chemotherapeutic agents used to reduce local symptoms and prolong survival. Palliative chemotherapy is not expected to be curative.

destinations.label: Principles of cancer care → Overview of cancer care

oDW02n0.title: Curative chemotherapy
oDW02n0.description: An aggressive regimen of one or more chemotherapeutic agents used with the intention of achieving complete remission.

destinations.label: Principles of cancer care → Overview of cancer care

KDWU2n0.title: Response evaluation criteria in solid tumors
KDWU2n0.description: A standardized set of rules to objectively determine whether a solid tumor is responding to therapy. Target lesions are measured before and after treatment, typically with CT or MRI. Change in size is used to classify the tumor as completely responsive (disappearance of the lesion), partially responsive (≥ 30% decrease in lesion size), stable (no significant change in lesion size), or progressive (≥ 20% increase in lesion size).

6DWj2n0.title: Narrow band imaging
6DWj2n0.description: An endoscopic technique in which narrowed-spectrum blue light is used to enhance the vascular and mucosal characteristics of areas of interest. Can help guide biopsies and predict which areas are likely to be dysplastic.

media.title: Flat polyp on ileocecal valve (narrow band imaging)

pDWL2n0.title: Chromoendoscopy
pDWL2n0.description: An endoscopic technique in which a dye is applied to the mucosal surface to enhance mucosal irregularities and guide targeted biopsies.

JDWs2n0.title: Advanced cancer
JDWs2n0.description: A cancer that is at a late stage (typically stage IV), includes distant metastasis, and/or is life-limiting (i.e., an estimated 6-24 months of remaining life).

qDWC2n0.title: Differential reinforcement
qDWC2n0.description: A type of behavioral therapy that aims to increase desirable behaviors by reinforcing them (e.g., by giving a reward) while minimizing undesirable behaviors by withholding reinforcement (e.g., by ignoring inappropriate behavior).

sDWtfn0.title: Uncomplicated diarrhea
sDWtfn0.description: An increase of up to 6 bowel movements per day from baseline without fever, blood in the stool, moderate to severe cramping, significant dehydration, or an impaired ability to perform basic activities of daily living.

GDWBfn0.title: Complicated diarrhea
GDWBfn0.description: An increase of ≥ 7 bowel movements per day or any diarrhea accompanied by fever, dehydration, bleeding, severe cramping, or the inability to perform basic activities of daily living.

tDWXTn0.title: Malignant colorectal polyp
tDWXTn0.description: A colorectal polyp with evidence of neoplastic infiltration through the submucosa that does not extend through the muscularis mucosa. Constitutes the earliest stage of colorectal cancer (pT1 in the TNM classification).

FDWgTn0.title: Cognitive remediation therapy
FDWgTn0.description: A type of therapy to improve cognitive function and quality of life in patients with cognitive deficits due to schizophrenia. Therapy involves increasingly complex tasks related to attention, memory, language, and executive functioning. Often combined with individual or group therapies aimed at improving social functioning.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Cognitive remediation therapy

8DWOTn0.title: Favorable subgroup of cancer of unknown primary
8DWOTn0.description: A cancer of unknown primary origin with characteristics suggesting a likely response to a specific anticancer treatment regimen. Examples include neuroendocrine tumors, cancers with a single metastatic deposit, squamous cell cancers affecting nonsupraclavicular lymph nodes, cancers with colorectal immune or molecular markers, cancers in male patients with bone metastases and elevated PSA, and cancers in female patients with either isolated axillary lymph node involvement or serous peritoneal adenocarcinomatosis.

uDWpTn0.title: Unfavorable subgroup of cancer of unknown primary
uDWpTn0.description: A cancer of unknown primary (CUP) that has none of the features of a favorable CUP and thus has a more negative prognosis.

DDW1gn0.title: Compressive spinal emergencies
DDW1gn0.description: Compression of the spinal cord, conus medullaris, or the cauda equina which, if not treated emergently, can cause permanent neurological damage. Causes include disk herniation, spinal epidural abscess or hematoma, spinal metastases, or trauma.

wDWhgn0.title: Egg protein-containing vaccines
wDWhgn0.description: A vaccine that contains small quantities of egg protein. Examples include vaccines for yellow fever, influenza, measles, and mumps. With the exception of a history of anaphylaxis, egg allergies are generally only considered precautions, not contraindications, for administering most egg protein-containing vaccines.

9DWNgn0.title: SFLC involved:uninvolved ratio
9DWNgn0.description: A metric of the relative levels of free kappa and lambda immunoglobulin light chains measured in the serum. Reflects the excess production of the elevated light chain (involved light chain) compared to the normal light chain (uninvolved light chain). Used for the diagnosis and risk stratification of plasma cell dyscrasias (e.g., multiple myeloma).

CDWqgn0.title: Tendinosis
CDWqgn0.description: A non-inflammatory degeneration of tendon fibers caused by repetitive strain on tendons at their point of origin or insertion in a bone. Typically caused by overload or overuse injury.

xDWEgn0.title: Clinical criteria of brain death
xDWEgn0.description: A set of criteria for diagnosing brain death. There must be an irreversible loss of brain function attributable to a specific cause (e.g., clinical or radiologic evidence of acute, severe damage to the CNS) in the absence of factors that may impede proper clinical judgment (e.g., electrolyte imbalances, locked-in syndrome, abnormal core temperature, abnormal systolic blood pressure, intoxication or the effects of CNS-depressing drugs/neuromuscular blockade).

ADWRSn0.title: Triple flexion reflex
ADWRSn0.description: A reflex characterized by flexion of the hip and knee and dorsiflexion of the foot in response to noxious stimuli of the foot. It is a sign of upper neuron impairment that typically appears 1-3 days after injury.

ZwWZhn0.title: Cutaneous granuloma
ZwWZhn0.description: A nodular collection of macrophages, epithelioid histiocytes, and admixed multinucleate giant cells that forms as a result of chronic inflammation. This structure can form when the immune system is unable to completely eliminate a foreign substance. The resultant granulomatous inflammation attempts to wall off the foreign substance. Subdivided into infectious and noninfectious types.

0wWehn0.title: Rapidly progressive dementia
0wWehn0.description: A rare subset of dementias that develop and progress over a course of weeks to months. Causes include autoimmune disease, impaired blood flow, infection, medication toxicity, prion disease, toxic substances, vitamin deficiencies, malignancy, and recurrent seizures.

XwW9hn0.title: Perceptual-motor function
XwW9hn0.description: A neurocognitive domain that involves the interaction between sensory perception and motor function. Includes visual perception, visuoconstructional ability, perceptual-motor coordination, and motor planning.

cwWa3n0.title: Social cognition
cwWa3n0.description: A neurocognitive domain that involves the interpretation of social information, including insight into one's own and others' social behavior.

WwWP3n0.title: Patterns suspicious for nonaccidental injuries in children
WwWP3n0.description: Include bruises with unusual patterns (e.g., linear), in unusual locations (e.g., back or ears), and/or in unusual age groups (infants < 4 months of age); bite marks; immersion burns; fractures of long bones or vertebrae or fractures in nonambulatory children; and severe head injuries.

VwWG3n0.title: Demand valve oxygen
VwWG3n0.description: An oxygen delivery system consisting of a face mask with side vents that allow for exhalation. High-flow oxygen with 100% FiO₂ is delivered intermittently when the patient inhales. Demand valve oxygen is used for the treatment of cluster headaches (also allowing for hyperventilation during treatment) and is a first-aid device for several diving-related disorders.

2wWTRn0.title: Bone morphogenetic protein receptor type 1A
2wWTRn0.description: A gene that encodes for a transmembrane kinase receptor protein. Mutations in this gene are associated with juvenile polyposis syndrome.

SwWyRn0.title: Mistake (patient safety)
SwWyRn0.description: A type of failure in patient care in which an intentional action taken to treat a patient is incorrect (based on a standard of care). Can be rule-based (a decision to do the incorrect action) or knowledge-based (not knowing which action is correct). An example is misinterpretation of a treatment algorithm resulting in giving an incorrect treatment.

RwWlin0.title: Aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase deficiency
RwWlin0.description: A rare genetic condition characterized by decreased activity of L-amino acid decarboxylase enzymes, which leads to impaired synthesis of neurotransmitters (e.g., dopamine, serotonin). Symptoms manifest early in life and include muscle weakness, oculogyric crisis, failure to thrive, and disruptions of the autonomous nervous system.

iwWJin0.title: CT contraindications
iwWJin0.description: There are no absolute contraindications for CT scan. The procedure should be strictly limited in certain patient groups (e.g., children, pregnant individuals) because of the relatively high radiation dose. Contraindications for iodinated IV contrast (if required) should also be considered.

PwWWQn0.title: Monosodium glutamate
PwWWQn0.description: The sodium salt of glutamic acid. Natural sources with high MSG content include animal products (e.g., cheese, meat, fish) and certain vegetables (e.g., tomatoes, shiitake mushrooms). Also used as a flavor enhancer in prepared foods. Although adverse reactions have been reported anecdotally, these effects have not been confirmed in studies. The FDA considers foods with added MSG to be safe.

4wW3Qn0.title: B vitamins
4wW3Qn0.description: A group of essential water-soluble vitamins, including vitamin B1 (thiamine), B2 (riboflavin), B3 (niacin or nicotinic acid), B5 (pantothenic acid), B6 (pyridoxine), B7 (biotin), B9 (folic acid), and B12 (cobalamin).

kwWmQn0.title: Serratia marcescens
kwWmQn0.description: A catalase-positive, gram-negative bacillus in the family Enterobacteriaceae.

OwWIQn0.title: Pulpitis
OwWIQn0.description: An inflammation of the dental pulp usually due to a bacterial (e.g., Streptococcus mutans) infection. Clinical features include pain and increased sensitivity to cold and heat. Can result in tooth death.

mwWVjn0.title: Nasal suction
mwWVjn0.description: A method of removing mucus from the nasal passages. Devices include bulb syringes and catheters attached to negative pressure.

5wWijn0.title: Full code
5wWijn0.description: An order (e.g., via an advanced directive or physician order for life-sustaining treatment form) by which a patient requests all forms of life-sustaining measures, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation and intubation.

nwW7jn0.title: Renal abscess
nwW7jn0.description: A localized infection of the renal parenchyma that develops either as a complication of acute pyelonephritis or from the hematogenous spread of infection from another location in the body. Clinical presentation is similar to pyelonephritis (e.g., fever, flank pain, costovertebral angle tenderness). Treatment depends on the size of the abscess: antibiotics and drainage for abscesses > 5 cm; antibiotics and possible drainage for abscesses 3-5 cm; antibiotics alone for abscesses < 3 cm.

LwWwjn0.title: Biceps squeeze test
LwWwjn0.description: A test used to assess the integrity of the distal biceps tendon. With the patient's elbow between 60 and 80 degrees of flexion and the forearm in pronation, the clinician squeezes the belly of the biceps. Considered positive (indicating distal biceps tendon rupture) if there is no resulting supination of the patient's forearm or wrist.

destinations.label: Biceps tendinopathy and biceps tendon rupture → Diagnosis

owW0Pn0.title: Anaclitic depression
owW0Pn0.description: A type of depression associated with interpersonal dependency and characterized by feelings of helplessness and weakness as well as fears of abandonment. Associated with past experiences of abandonment and loss. Initially described in children who have been separated from their caregivers.

rwWf4n0.title: Food protein-induced allergic proctocolitis of infancy
rwWf4n0.description: A common type of delayed inflammatory non-IgE mediated food allergy in young infants. Caused by non-IgE mediated inflammation of the distal colon in response to food proteins (e.g., soy protein and cow's milk). Symptoms usually manifest within the first several weeks of life and often include rectal bleeding and/or diarrhea. Usually resolves spontaneously by one year of age.

HwWK4n0.title: Unhealthy alcohol use
HwWK4n0.description: A level of alcohol consumption associated with potential or actual harm. Encompasses alcohol use disorder, binge drinking, heavy drinking, and any alcohol use in individuals for whom abstinence is advised (e.g., pregnant individuals).

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Classifications of alcohol use

swWt4n0.title: Nasopharyngeal aspiration
swWt4n0.description: A method for removing mucous from the nasal and pharyngeal passages. A small-caliber suction catheter is inserted into the nares and advanced into the pharynx, and suction is applied while retracting the catheter. Used to relieve upper airway mucous obstruction and/or to collect nasopharyngeal specimens. Adverse effects may include bradycardia and bronchospasm.

twWXkn0.title: Sleep bruxism
twWXkn0.description: Involuntary and repetitive teeth grinding and/or jaw clenching during sleep.

FwWgkn0.title: Awake bruxism
FwWgkn0.description: Involuntary and repetitive teeth grinding and/or jaw clenching during wakefulness.

8wWOkn0.title: Dental attrition
8wWOkn0.description: The loss of tooth structure on the morsal surface due to teeth grinding.

uwWpkn0.title: Dental abfraction
uwWpkn0.description: The loss of tooth structure due to noncarious lesions from biomechanical overload (e.g., teeth grinding).

DwW1On0.title: Late gadolinium enhancement
DwW1On0.description: A cardiac MRI distribution pattern seen 10-20 minutes after IV administration of gadolinium-based contrast agents as a result of differences in volume, uptake, and/or washout within the extracellular space of myocardial tissue. Late gadolinium enhancement is seen in areas of myocardial injury, e.g., necrosis, edema, scar tissue, focal areas of fibrosis.

wwWhOn0.title: Infectious encephalitis
wwWhOn0.description: An inflammation of the brain parenchyma caused by viruses (most common), bacteria, fungi, or parasites. Infectious encephalitis can be sporadic (e.g., herpes simplex encephalitis) or endemic (e.g., Japanese encephalitis virus). Clinical features include altered mental status, focal neurological deficits, seizures, and signs of inflammation (e.g., fever, rash).

9wWNOn0.title: Encephalomyelitis
9wWNOn0.description: A concurrent inflammation of the brain (encephalitis) and spinal cord (myelitis). Types include paraneoplastic, infectious (e.g., due to West Nile virus), and postinfectious (e.g., acute disseminated encephalomyelitis) encephalomyelitis. Clinical features are suggestive of both brain tissue (e.g., altered mental status) as well as spinal cord inflammation (e.g., flaccid paralysis).

CwWqOn0.title: Sepsis screening tool
CwWqOn0.description: A decision support tool that utilizes clinical parameters to help identify sepsis before frank clinical deterioration occurs. Measured parameters vary but commonly include blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, and mental status. Examples of sepsis screening tools include the Modified Early Warning Score, National Early Warning Score, and SIRS criteria.

xwWEOn0.title: Cerebellitis
xwWEOn0.description: An inflammation of the cerebellum. Most commonly caused by infections (e.g., acute postviral cerebellitis) but can also be caused by immune reactions to an underlying malignancy (e.g., paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration).  Manifestations include ataxia, vertigo, nystagmus, and dysmetria.

BwWzOn0.title: Paraneoplastic encephalitis
BwWzOn0.description: Inflammation of the central nervous system (CNS) caused by an immune-mediated response to a systemic malignancy. Typically associated with autoantibodies against intracellular neuronal antigens. Symptoms may vary by affected CNS region. Can be the first manifestation of a previously undiagnosed malignancy.

AwWRln0.title: Nicotine withdrawal
AwWRln0.description: A withdrawal syndrome caused by decreased nicotine levels in the blood. Typically occurs when an individual with nicotine dependence abruptly stops smoking. Symptoms include cravings, irritability, impaired concentration, restlessness, and weight gain.

_wW5ln0.title: Brainstem encephalitis
_wW5ln0.description: An inflammation of the brainstem and adjacent regions, caused by infectious, autoimmune, or paraneoplastic conditions. Manifestations include bulbar palsy, dysautonomia, and sensorineural hearing loss.

-wWDln0.title: Uncomplicated malaria
-wWDln0.description: A class of malaria without the severe organ dysfunction characteristic of severe malaria.

a9WQNn0.title: Shepherd fracture
a9WQNn0.description: A fracture involving the posterolateral tubercle of the talus due to forced hyperplantar flexion and inversion.

Y9WnNn0.title: Cedell fracture
Y9WnNn0.description: A fracture involving the posteromedial tubercle of the talus due to forced dorsiflexion and pronation.

b9WHNn0.title: Crystallopathy
b9WHNn0.description: A range of medical disorders caused by the deposition of crystals or crystal-like particulate matter (e.g., misfolded proteins or airborne microparticles) that results in a host immune response and tissue injury. Common disease manifestations include renal colic, biliary colic, acute kidney injury, interstitial lung disease, and inflammatory arthritis.

X9W9Nn0.title: Sinotubular junction
X9W9Nn0.description: The junction between the aortic root and the ascending aorta. Formed by the aortic valve commissures and the distal parts of the aortic sinuses. It is a common location for supravalvular aortic stenosis.

19W2mn0.title: Type 0 spinal muscular atrophy
19W2mn0.description: A very rare, severe type of spinal muscular atrophy with disease onset already during pregnancy, when mothers may observe decreased or absent fetal movement. Symptoms at birth include severe muscle weakness, hypotonia, and respiratory insufficiency. Patients typically fail to meet motor milestones. Death usually occurs due to respiratory failure during the first 6 months of life.

N9W-nn0.title: Periodontitis
N9W-nn0.description: A condition characterized by gingival inflammation and loss of supportive connective tissues (e.g., the periodontal ligament, alveolar bone). Clinical features include gingival bleeding and tooth mobility.

m9WVLn0.title: β-globin
m9WVLn0.description: A protein component of the main adult hemoglobin HbA (α2,β2). Encoded on the HBB gene on chromosome 11.

59WiLn0.title: Dental plaque
59WiLn0.description: A bacterial film that forms on the surface of teeth. Accumulation of dental plaque is responsible for most periodontal diseases (e.g., caries, gingivitis, periodontitis).

M9WMLn0.title: Dental calculus
M9WMLn0.description: A type of hardened dental plaque that forms and accumulates in the setting of inadequate teeth flossing and cleaning. Clinical findings include teeth staining, malodorous breath, receding gums, and chronic gingivitis.

n9W7Ln0.title: γ-globin
n9W7Ln0.description: A protein component of fetal hemoglobin HbF (α2,γ2). Encoded on the HBG1 and HBG2 genes on chromosome 11.

o9W0on0.title: Recombinant cytokines
o9W0on0.description: Recombinant cytokines are drug analogs of natural cytokines and colony-stimulating factors to stimulate specific cells in order to enhance the immense system. Recombinant cytokines include recombinant erythropoietin, recombinant interferons, and recombinant interleukins.

K9WUon0.title: Eltrombopag
K9WUon0.description: A thrombopoietin agonist that increases platelet production by stimulating megakaryocytes in the bone marrow. Used in the treatment of ITP and in certain thrombocytopenias of other origins.

v9WA6n0.title: Prechemotherapy screening
v9WA6n0.description: A collection of tests performed prior to beginning chemotherapy in order to predict and thus mitigate the adverse effects of treatment. Key goals of prechemotherapy screening include establishing baseline organ function, identifying comorbidities, and estimating physiologic reserve. Typical studies in preoperative screening are CBC, CMP, ECG, echocardiogram, and frailty testing.

destinations.label: Principles of cancer care → Preparation for cancer treatment

C9Wqpn0.title: Oprelvekin
C9Wqpn0.description: A recombinant form of interleukin-11 that stimulates platelet production and hepatic synthesis of acute phase proteins (e.g., fibrinogen). Indications include thrombocytopenia following myelosuppressive chemotherapy.

aCWQqn0.title: Risk factors for HCV infection
aCWQqn0.description: Factors include injection drug use, coinfection with HBV or HIV, MSM, history of incarceration, born between 1945 and 1965, child born to a birthing parent positive for HCV, and history of blood transfusion prior to 1992.

YCWnqn0.title: Tympanic plexus
YCWnqn0.description: A nerve plexus located in the middle ear, formed by branches of the tympanic nerve and carotid plexus responsible for supplying sensory innervation to the middle ear and eustachian tube mucosal tissues.

bCWHqn0.title: Kunjin virus
bCWHqn0.description: A subtype of the West Nile virus that is transmitted via the bite of an infected Aedes, Anopheles, or Culex mosquito. Infection manifests with fever, headache, myalgias, rash, and, rarely, encephalitis.

destinations.label: Miscellaneous mosquito-borne diseases → Mosquito-borne Flavivirus diseases

XCW9qn0.title: Reed-Sternberg-like cells
XCW9qn0.description: A type of cell that has similar morphology and immunophenotype to the Reed-Sternberg cells seen in Hodgkin lymphoma. Found in some types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, these cells are distinguished from true Reed-Sternberg cells based on their immunophenotype and cellular environment.

dCWoIn0.title: Snowboarder fracture
dCWoIn0.description: A fracture of the lateral process of talus most commonly seen in snowboarding injuries from landing after an aerial maneuver or jump. Forced ankle joint dorsiflexion and inversion cause the talus to become locked in place by the surrounding bones. Consequent axial loading results in fracture of the lateral process.

fCWkrn0.title: Anti-SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibodies
fCWkrn0.description: Monoclonal antibodies that target the spike protein of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Uses include preexposure prophylaxis (e.g., of immunosuppressed individuals or those with contraindications to COVID-19 vaccines) and treatment of high-risk patients with COVID-19. Examples of regimens include bebtelovimab, sotrovimab, bamlanivimab plus etesevimab, casirivimab plus imdevimab, and tixagevimab plus cilgavimab.

SCWyrn0.title: Asymptomatic COVID-19
SCWyrn0.description: Individuals with a positive virological test for COVID-19 but no symptoms attributable to the infection.

hCWc7n0.title: Mild COVID-19
hCWc7n0.description: Individuals with symptomatic COVID-19 in the absence of dyspnea, hypoxemia, or pneumonia

3CWS7n0.title: Moderate COVID-19
3CWS7n0.description: Individuals with confirmed COVID-19 and evidence of lower respiratory tract involvement (including imaging findings of lung parenchymal involvement, and) but no hypoxemia (i.e., SpO2 ≥ 94% on room air at sea level)

RCWl7n0.title: Severe COVID-19
RCWl7n0.description: Individuals with pneumonia, hypoxemia with SpO2 < 94%, and/or lung infiltrates > 50% due to COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2 infection).

iCWJ7n0.title: Critical COVID-19
iCWJ7n0.description: Individuals with respiratory failure, septic shock, and/or multiple organ dysfunction syndrome due to COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2 infection).

PCWWHn0.title: Modifiable risk factors for cardiovascular disease
PCWWHn0.description: Modifiable risk factors include smoking, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and hypertension.

mCWVsn0.title: Recombinant interferon alpha
mCWVsn0.description: A recombinant form of interferon alpha used to treat chronic viral infections (e.g., HBV, HCV, HHV8, HPV) and neoplastic conditions (e.g., myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms). Its antiviral action is due to inhibition of viral protein synthesis, breakdown of viral RNA, and increased expression of MHC class I molecules. Its antineoplastic action is due to inhibition of hematopoietic progenitor cells (e.g., megakaryocytes) in addition to increased production and presentation of tumor antigens to the immune system.

5CWisn0.title: Recombinant interferon gamma
5CWisn0.description: A recombinant form of interferon gamma used to treat chronic granulomatous diseases (e.g., leprosy, leishmaniasis, toxoplasmosis). Results in activation of macrophages and NK cells. Has both antimicrobial and antiviral activity.

oCW0Gn0.title: Recombinant interleukin-12
oCW0Gn0.description: A recombinant form of interleukin-12 given after chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy to support the immunsystem.

pCWLGn0.title: Generalized anxiety disorder 7-item scale
pCWLGn0.description: A survey used to screen for anxiety, assess the severity of symptoms, and monitor symptoms over time. Consists of seven items scored from a scale of 0 (not at all) to 3 (nearly every day). Item scores are added to calculate the total score, which can range from 0-4 (mild anxiety) up to 15-21 (severe anxiety).

JCWsGn0.title: Afterdrop
JCWsGn0.description: The phenomenon of continued cooling of a patient's core body temperature during the initial stages of rewarming. Afterdrop occurs when cold, acidemic blood flows from the peripheral to the core circulation, resulting in a temperature and pH drop. May cause fatal cardiac dysrhythmias.

tCWXFn0.title: Alcohol-associated hepatitis
tCWXFn0.description: A clinical syndrome characterized by inflammatory liver disease resulting from long-term heavy alcohol consumption. If alcohol-associated hepatitis develops acutely, patients may present with jaundice, nausea, low-grade fever, leukocytosis, tender hepatomegaly, transaminitis, and hyperbilirubinemia. A chronic course can lead to irreversible alcohol-associated cirrhosis.

wCWh8n0.title: Sterility (physiology)
wCWh8n0.description: A permanent state of infertility (i.e., inability to conceive a child).

9CWN8n0.title: Reproductive life plan
9CWN8n0.description: The establishment of goals related to conceiving or preventing pregnancy in alignment with an individual's values and priorities.

destinations.label: Family planning → Approach to family planning

zCWrun0.title: Induction chemotherapy
zCWrun0.description: A high-dose regimen of chemotherapy utilized to drastically reduce the tumor cell count.

destinations.label: Principles of cancer care → Overview of cancer care

-CWDun0.title: Consolidation chemotherapy
-CWDun0.description: A regimen of chemotherapy given after induction chemotherapy to eradicate any remaining cancer cells.

destinations.label: Principles of cancer care → Overview of cancer care

ZxWZEn0.title: Maintenance chemotherapy
ZxWZEn0.description: A regimen of low dose-chemotherapy used to maintain cancer remission.

destinations.label: Principles of cancer care → Overview of cancer care

dxWovn0.title: Ospemifene
dxWovn0.description: A selective estrogen receptor modulator used to alleviate symptoms such as vaginal dryness and dyspareunia associated with genitourinary syndrome of menopause.

exWxvn0.title: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss
exWxvn0.description:
A sudden, usually unilateral and idiopathic loss of hearing over a period of 3 days. Treatment includes systemic 
 and intratympanic corticosteroid administration.

UxWbDn0.title: Severe anemia
UxWbDn0.description: A hemoglobin level below approximately 7-8 g/dL. The threshold for severe anemia is based on the age and sex of the patient. Patients typically have symptoms of anemia (e.g., fatigue, palpitations, breathlessness) and/or hemodynamic compromise.

2xWTDn0.title: Moderate anemia
2xWTDn0.description: A hemoglobin level between approximately 7 and 10.9 g/dL. The threshold for defining moderate anemia is based on the age and sex of the patient. Patients may or may not have symptoms of anemia (e.g., fatigue, palpitations, breathlessness).

fxWkDn0.title: Mild anemia
fxWkDn0.description: A hemoglobin level below the normal range based on age and sex, but above 10-11 g/dL (definitions vary among experts). Patients are frequently asymptomatic but may experience symptoms of anemia (e.g., breathlessness, fatigue, palpitations).

gxWFDn0.title: Murray Valley encephalitis virus
gxWFDn0.description: A mosquito-borne flavivirus, of the family Flaviviridae, that most commonly occurs in Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Indonesia. Most of the cases are subclinical. Infection manifests with fever, myalgias, headaches, nausea and/or vomiting, and, rarely, encephalitis.

hxWcwn0.title: Mild frostbite
hxWcwn0.description: A freezing injury to the superficial layers of the skin. Clinical features include edema, numbness, and clear blisters. It is associated with minimal or no tissue loss.

3xWSwn0.title: Severe frostbite
3xWSwn0.description: A freezing injury that extends beyond the subcutaneous tissue, involving muscle, tendons, and bone. Clinical features include hemorrhagic vesicles and demarcation of necrotic tissue. It is associated with significant tissue loss.

RxWlwn0.title: Tracheoinnominate fistula
