RxWlwn0.description: A fistula between the innominate artery and the trachea that results in life threatening hemoptysis. Most commonly caused by a tracheostomy tube eroding into the innominate artery.

PxWW9n0.title: Rome IV criteria for cyclical vomiting syndrome
PxWW9n0.description: A set of clinical criteria used to diagnose cyclical vomiting syndrome. Considers the duration, frequency, and pattern of episodes, along with symptom-free intervals. Diagnostic thresholds differ between adults and children.

OxWI9n0.title: Postexertional malaise
OxWI9n0.description: The worsening of symptoms (e.g., fatigue, muscle aches, flu-like symptoms) after even minor physical, mental, or social activity. Occurs in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and postacute COVID-19 syndrome. Symptoms typically worsen 12-48 hours after exertion. Duration ranges from a few days to several months.

destinations.label: Myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome → Clinical features

5xWiCn0.title: Cryoablation
5xWiCn0.description: A treatment that uses liquid nitrogen to expose abnormal tissue (e.g., tumors) to very low temperatures and destroy malignant or premalignant cells. Often used to treat skin lesions.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Overview of treatment

nxW7Cn0.title: Cluster period
nxW7Cn0.description: A duration of typically several weeks or months during which cluster headache attacks occur on a regular basis and at least once every other day.

KxWUxn0.title: Abrasion
KxWUxn0.description: A superficial skin injury caused by rubbing, scraping, and/or irritation.

6xWjxn0.title: Trichogram
6xWjxn0.description: A procedure in which hairs are plucked from the scalp and examined under a microscope to evaluate the hair shaft and tip.

qxWCxn0.title: Chronic venous insufficiency
qxWCxn0.description: A term used to describe the edema, characteristic skin changes (hyperpigmentation, stasis dermatitis), and ulcers secondary to chronic venous hypertension. Varicose veins may or may not be present.

IxWYBn0.title: Neonatal fever
IxWYBn0.description: A body temperature of ≥ 38°C (100.4°F) in a neonate (≤ 28 days of age).

destinations.label: Fever in infants ≤ 60 days of age → Summary

rxWfBn0.title: Targeted phototherapy
rxWfBn0.description: A type of phototherapy (most commonly UVB) used to treat skin conditions, including psoriasis, vitiligo, and atopic dermatitis. In contrast to traditional phototherapy, high-intensity radiation is delivered only to affected skin areas via laser and nonlaser technologies, reducing the adverse effects and required treatment duration and frequency.

FxWgyn0.title: Nonmass enhancement
FxWgyn0.description: An area of enhancement on MRI that lacks a defined volume, shape, or outline of a mass. Typically used in the description of breast imaging; seen in both benign and malignant lesions.

_xW5_n0.title: Encephalitic rabies
_xW5_n0.description: An inflammation of the brain parenchyma caused by rabies, a neurotropic RNA virus of the family Rhabdoviridae. It is the most common clinical manifestation of CNS rabies infection. Symptoms include fever, hydrophobia, agitation, dysautonomia, and seizures.

YBWnzn0.title: Telogen gravidarum
YBWnzn0.description: A type of telogen effluvium seen in postpartum individuals due to a drop in circulating placental estrogen levels. Results in diffuse, nonscarring hair loss.

bBWHzn0.title: Critical care transition program
bBWHzn0.description: A structured process in which members of a critical care team continue to regularly evaluate patients following discharge from an ICU. This process is thought to reduce adverse events when patients with complex medical issues have a reduction in their level of care.

cBWa-n0.title: Unintended pregnancy
cBWa-n0.description: A pregnancy that occurs in an individual who does not desire pregnancy at that time or at all.

1BW2-n0.title: Family planning
1BW2-n0.description: The management of reproduction by individuals and couples to prevent pregnancy, optimize pregnancy spacing, determine the number of children conceived, and/or address infertility with the use of family planning services.

WBWP-n0.title: Foreign body granuloma
WBWP-n0.description: A reaction of noncaseating granulomatous inflammation in response to foreign material in cutaneous or subcutaneous tissues. Can be due to endogenous (e.g., hair fragments) or exogenous (e.g., cosmetic fillers) materials.

destinations.label: Collection of dermatological disorders → Cutaneous granulomas

dBWo-n0.title: Periodontal examination
dBWo-n0.description: The physical examination of the gingiva, teeth, and bite.

VBWG-n0.title: Infertility services
VBWG-n0.description: An evaluation for couples who have not conceived after 1 year of unprotected vaginal intercourse if the woman is < 35 years of age, or 6 months if  ≥ 35 years of age. Also includes counseling for individuals and couples who are infertile, sterile, or not physically able to conceive, e.g., same-sex couples, individuals with reproductive organ disorders (e.g., Mullerian agenesis).

eBWx-n0.title: Breast scintigraphy
eBWx-n0.description: A nuclear medicine imaging method that was previously used as an adjuvant method to mammography in patients with indeterminate mammograms, for follow-up in patients with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, and for postsurgical cancer screening. Breast scintigraphy has largely been replaced by MRI.

2BWTZL0.title: LOC
2BWTZL0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Loss of consciousness
2. Level of consciousness

hBWc0L0.title: Anti-Yo antibody
hBWc0L0.description: An onconeural autoantibody directed against Purkinje cells of the cerebellum associated with paraneoplastic neurological syndromes (e.g., cerebellar encephalomyelitis) and autoimmune diseases.

3BWS0L0.title: Anti-amphiphysin antibody
3BWS0L0.description: An onconeural autoantibody directed against the protein amphiphysin, a compound of synaptic vesicles. Its formation is most commonly associated with paraneoplastic stiff-person syndrome and breast cancer.

RBWl0L0.title: Anti-Ri antibody
RBWl0L0.description: An onconeural autoantibody directed against a group of RNA-binding proteins in CNS nerve cell nuclei associated with paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (e.g., opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome) and autoimmune diseases.

iBWJ0L0.title: Trichoscopy
iBWJ0L0.description: An examination of the hair and scalp using a dermatoscope. Can be used to visualize hair shafts, hair follicle openings, perifollicular epidermis, and blood vessels of the scalp.

QBWu0L0.title: Anti-Tr antibody
QBWu0L0.description: An antibody targeted against delta/notch-like epidermal growth factor-related receptor (DNER) of Purkinje cells associated with paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration syndrome and Hodgkin lymphoma.

jBW_0L0.title: PLASMIC score
jBW_0L0.description: A clinical risk assessment tool used to predict the likelihood of severe ADAMTS13 deficiency in patients with suspected thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Components of the scoring system include platelet count, indicators of hemolysis (i.e., indirect bilirubin, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin), active malignancy, history of transplantation, and MCV, INR, and creatinine levels.

NBW-aL0.title: Pigmented purpuric dermatosis
NBW-aL0.description: A group of skin disorders of unknown etiology that involve inflammation of the superficial capillaries in the skin. Manifests as purpura and petechiae on the lower extremities, which can coalesce into red, brown, or yellow pigmented patches. May also manifest with pruritus.

mBWVYL0.title: Exercise-induced vasculitis
mBWVYL0.description: A benign, self-limited, cutaneous, small vessel vasculitis that can develop following physical activity, especially in hot weather. Appears as an erythematous rash or purpura on the lower limbs and may be associated with pruritus, burning, and lower limb edema.

5BWiYL0.title: False negative rate
5BWiYL0.description: The proportion of people with a condition who test negative. It is equal to 1 - sensitivity (true positive rate). A test with a high false negative rate has low sensitivity.

oBW0bL0.title: Clinical features of chronic venous disease
oBW0bL0.description: Features include lower extremity edema (may be unilateral) that spares the toes and feet and worsens with standing and heat, pain, pruritis, numbness, and/or tingling. Skin changes include stasis dermatitis, hemosiderin staining, and telangiectasias.

qBWCbL0.title: BI-RADS
qBWCbL0.description: A standardized method for reporting the results of breast imaging (mammogram, ultrasound, MRI). Results are reported as one of seven categories from 0 to 6. Category 0 indicates that further imaging is needed; category 1: negative result; category 2: benign finding; category 3: probably benign finding; category 4: suspicious/abnormal finding; category 5: high likelihood of malignancy (≥ 95%); and category 6: confirmed malignancy (via biopsy).

GBWBXL0.title: Anti-NMDA receptor antibody
GBWBXL0.description: An autoantibody against the GluN1 subunit of the N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor in neurons. Associated with anti-NMDAR encephalitis syndrome and ovarian teratoma in young women.

tBWXcL0.title: Anti-LGI1 antibody
tBWXcL0.description: An autoantibody directed against leucine-rich glioma inactivated-1 protein of neurons. It is typically associated with faciobrachial dystonic episodes and limbic encephalitis syndrome.

8BWOcL0.title: Anti-CASPR2 antibody
8BWOcL0.description: An autoantibody against contactin-associated protein-like 2 (Caspr2), a cell adhesion molecule present in both CNS and PNS axons. It disrupts the clustering of voltage-gated potassium channels (VGKC) and is associated with autoimmune encephalitis, peripheral nerve hyperexcitability, and thymomas.

uBWpcL0.title: Anti-AMPA receptor antibody
uBWpcL0.description: A rare type of autoantibodies against alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor, a postsynaptic transmembrane glutamate receptor. Associated with anti-AMPA antibody encephalitis, which may manifest as limbic encephalitis syndrome.

CBWq1L0.title: Fertility preservation
CBWq1L0.description: The process of storing oocytes, sperm, embryos, or reproductive tissue in order to conceive at a later date. May be performed prior to treatment that may affect fertility (such as chemotherapy or surgery, including gender-affirming surgery) or for individuals who want to delay conception until they are older, when fertility may have declined.

xBWE1L0.title: VGKC-complex antibodies
xBWE1L0.description: Autoantibodies against potassium-channel-associated proteins, most commonly LGI1 and CASPR2. Associated with various neurologic conditions, such as limbic encephalitis syndrome, neuromyotonia, and idiopathic epilepsy.

_BW5WL0.title: Chronic inducible urticaria
_BW5WL0.description: A subgroup of chronic urticaria in which symptoms are induced by an identified external trigger. Subtypes include physical urticarias (e.g., cold/heat urticaria, solar urticaria, vibratory angioedema, delayed pressure urticaria) and nonphysical urticarias (e.g., cholinergic urticaria, contact urticaria, aquagenic urticaria).

-BWDWL0.title: Neuroprognostication
-BWDWL0.description: The interpretation of multimodal diagnostic studies to predict the likelihood of neurological recovery following return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) after cardiac arrest. Usually conducted no earlier than 72 hours after ROSC or 72 hours after normothermia if targeted temperature management is used. Includes studies such as pupillary reflex, EEG, and neuroimaging.

ZyWZdL0.title: Listeria encephalitis
ZyWZdL0.description: An inflammation of the brain parenchyma (most commonly of the brainstem) caused by bacteria of the genus Listeria. In most cases, the course of the disease is biphasic, beginning with a prodromal phase with malaise, fever, headache, and nausea/vomiting, followed by various focal neurological deficits (mostly brainstem symptoms) and/ or impaired consciousness.

0yWedL0.title: Murray Valley encephalitis
0yWedL0.description: An inflammation of the brain parenchyma caused by the Murray Valley encephalitis virus. Infection manifests with a prodromal stage with myalgias, fever, headache, nausea, and vomiting followed by neurological symptoms, such as altered mental status, meningismus, seizures, and in severe cases, coma.

destinations.label: Miscellaneous mosquito-borne diseases → Mosquito-borne Flavivirus diseases

ayWQdL0.title: Enteroviral encephalitis
ayWQdL0.description: Inflammation of the brain caused by enteroviruses, RNA viruses of the family Picornaviridae. Most commonly affects children, young adults, and immunocompromised individuals, particularly those with B-cell depletion or B-cell disorders. Symptoms include fever, headache, diarrhea, rashes, and neurological deficits.

YyWndL0.title: Dependent edema
YyWndL0.description: The accumulation of fluid in the interstitial space in areas of the body influenced by gravity, e.g., the lower limbs in ambulatory patients and the sacral area in patients who are not ambulatory.

TyW6eL0.title: HLA allosensitization
TyW6eL0.description: The formation of circulating antibodies against human leukocyte antigens (HLAs). Typically occurs following exposure to proteins from another individual during blood transfusions, pregnancy, or previous organ transplantation. Can reduce the pool of potentially compatible organ donors and increase the risk of transplant rejection.

SyWyeL0.title: Vascular access steal syndrome
SyWyeL0.description: A complication of hemodialysis and/or hemofiltration in which excessive blood flow into the AV fistula or AV graft causes blood to be diverted away from perfusing the distal limb. Can lead to painful ischemia in the fingers and hand.

destinations.label: Renal replacement therapy → Hemodialysis and hemofiltration

hyWcUL0.title: Prolonged intermittent renal replacement therapy
hyWcUL0.description: A type of renal replacement therapy (RRT) that is provided intermittently over 6-18 hours. Aims to combine the advantages of continuous RRT (slow and efficient solute clearance, minimizing blood pressure changes) with the advantages of intermittent RRT (patients have periods off dialysis, allowing for other activities and procedures).

destinations.label: Renal replacement therapy → Hemodialysis and hemofiltration

3yWSUL0.title: Chronic hypertension in pregnancy
3yWSUL0.description: A form of hypertension that is defined as having sustained systolic blood pressure ≥140 mm Hg and/or diastolic blood pressure > 90 mm Hg before 20 weeks' gestation. Also includes individuals who take antihypertensive medications before pregnancy.

destinations.label: Hypertensive pregnancy disorders → Chronic hypertension in pregnancy

4yW32L0.title: Tumor board
4yW32L0.description: A group of physicians and providers from different specialties (e.g., medical and radiation oncology, surgery, radiology, pathology, palliative medicine) who work together to determine the best diagnostic and treatment approach for individuals with cancer.

kyWm2L0.title: Vasogenic cerebral edema
kyWm2L0.description: A type of brain edema resulting from an accumulation of extracellular fluid due to disruption of the blood brain barrier.

NyW-2L0.title: Burow solution
NyW-2L0.description: A solution of aluminum acetate used to treat inflamed skin conditions (typically using wet compresses) and chronic ear infections.

5yWifL0.title: Complete cleft lip
5yWifL0.description: A cleft on the upper lip that extends into the nostrils. Can be unilateral or bilateral. Commonly associated with cleft palate.

MyWMfL0.title: Incomplete cleft lip
MyWMfL0.description: A cleft on the upper lip that does not extend into the nostril. Can be unilateral or bilateral.

6yWjTL0.title: Intramedullary
6yWjTL0.description:
A term used to describe something located within the:
1. Medulla oblongata
2. Parenchyma of the spinal cord (e.g., intramedullary spinal tumor)
3. Bone marrow space (e.g., intramedullary implant)

JyWsTL0.title: Traube sign
JyWsTL0.description: Pistol shot-like sounds over the femoral artery heard on auscultation in patients with chronic aortic regurgitation.

qyWCTL0.title: Acute renal replacement therapy
qyWCTL0.description: The short-term use of renal replacement therapy for acute conditions (e.g., acute kidney injury, poisoning, acute decompensated heart failure). Most often utilizes hemodialysis and/or hemofiltration.

IyWYgL0.title: Chronic renal replacement therapy
IyWYgL0.description: The long-term use of renal replacement therapy for end-stage renal disease. Modalities include dialysis (peritoneal dialysis or hemodialysis) performed at home or in an outpatient center, and kidney transplantation.

GyWBgL0.title: Gastrointestinal motility disorders
GyWBgL0.description: A group of disorders in which abnormal muscle or nerve function results in spasms or akinesis in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Can manifest as nonspecific GI symptoms (e.g., dysphagia, early satiety, constipation) that vary depending on the underlying cause (e.g., chronic colonic pseudoobstruction, achalasia).

8yWOSL0.title: Ear wick
8yWOSL0.description: A small piece of compressed sponge or ribbon gauze that is inserted into the external auditory canal to improve the delivery of antiseptic or antimicrobial ear drops if the canal is narrowed, e.g., because of swelling.

uyWpSL0.title: Vasa recta (intestines)
uyWpSL0.description: The straight arteries that arise from the arterial arcades of the branches of a mesenteric artery and enter the bowel wall.

EyW8SL0.title: Vasa recta (kidneys)
EyW8SL0.description: An arteriolar-capillary bed that nourishes the nephron segments of the renal medulla.

destinations.label: Physiology of the kidney → Renal blood flow

DyW1hL0.title: Acute on chronic kidney disease
DyW1hL0.description: The acute worsening of renal function in a patient with preexisting chronic kidney disease. The risk of progression to renal failure is high. If treated promptly, patients with acute on chronic kidney disease may return to baseline renal function.

wyWhhL0.title: Whole blood sodium
wyWhhL0.description: A measurement of sodium concentration in a whole blood sample using the direct ion-selective electrode method (direct potentiometry). Preferred in patients with severe hyperlipidemia or hyperproteinemia in whom the indirect potentiometry method utilized by most serum chemistry analyzers may produce spuriously low sodium concentration results.

9yWNhL0.title: Equine-derived antitoxin
9yWNhL0.description: Equine-derived antitoxins are immunoglobulins that are derived from the blood of horses that have been immunized with a specific bacterial toxin/toxoid (e.g., botulinum toxin).

CyWqhL0.title: Trospium chloride
CyWqhL0.description: A muscarinic antagonist used to treat overactive bladder, including urgency urinary incontinence.

destinations.label: Overactive bladder and urgency urinary incontinence → Treatment

xyWEhL0.title: Endemic fungal infection
xyWEhL0.description: An infection caused by fungi that are only found in specific geographical regions, e.g., coccidioidomycosis in the arid regions of the Southwestern United States. Endemic fungal infections are usually the result of inhaling fungal spores and can occur in both immunocompromised and immunocompetent patients.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Endemic fungal infections

ByWzhL0.title: Speech therapy
ByWzhL0.description: A type of therapy used for language disorders (e.g., aphasia), voice disorders (e.g., dysphonia), speech disorders (e.g., stutter), cognitive-communication disorders, and swallowing disorders (e.g., dysphagia).

yyWd3L0.title: Obvious signs of irreversible death
yyWd3L0.description: Features of a cause and/or stage of death that is obviously irreversible. Includes late postmortem changes (e.g., decomposition) and injuries incompatible with life (e.g., decapitation, truncal transection). Used to guide in-hospital and out-of-hospital protocols about death pronouncement, attempting resuscitation, and/or termination of resuscitation efforts.

_yW53L0.title: Complex attention
_yW53L0.description: A neurocognitive domain that involves the ability to focus and sustain thoughts on a specific task or topic. Includes sustained attention, divided attention, selective attention, and processing speed.

zyWr3L0.title: Learning and memory
zyWr3L0.description: A neurocognitive domain that involves the process of recalling and retaining information. Includes free recall, cued recall, recognition memory, semantic and autobiographical long-term memory, and implicit learning.

XAW9RL0.title: Sterility (microbiology)
XAW9RL0.description: A state of being free of pathogenic organisms (i.e., exclusion of live microbes or death of any present microbes).

cAWaiL0.title: Dietary nitrate
cAWaiL0.description: A chemical compound that contains NO₃⁻ and is found in various food items (e.g., foods preserved by curing or smoking).

1AW2iL0.title: Lorcaserin
1AW2iL0.description: A selective serotonin agonist that binds to receptors in the hypothalamus to reduce appetite. Previously used to aid with weight loss in patients who are obese. Not commercially available in the United States (withdrawn in 2020 due to clinical trial data showing an increased risk of malignancy).

fAWkQL0.title: Hemodiafiltration
fAWkQL0.description: A hybrid renal replacement therapy modality that combines the principles of dialysis (e.g., diffusion) and hemofiltration (e.g., convection and ultrafiltration) to remove a wide range of solutes (i.e., low, medium, and large molecules) from the blood.

destinations.label: Renal replacement therapy → Hemodialysis and hemofiltration

hAWcjL0.title: Fidelity (psychotherapy)
hAWcjL0.description: A stage of psychosocial development according to a model proposed by Erik Erikson. In this stage, adolescents advance through a psychosocial crisis related to identity and role confusion.

3AWSjL0.title: Competence (psychotherapy)
3AWSjL0.description: A stage of psychosocial development according to a model proposed by Erik Erikson. In this stage, children (7–10 years of age) advance through a psychosocial crisis related to industry and inferiority.

PAWWPL0.title: Cerebrospinal fluid flow study
PAWWPL0.description: An imaging modality in which radioisotopes are injected into the CSF to evaluate the anatomy of CSF compartments and CSF flow dynamics.

4AW3PL0.title: Atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration
4AW3PL0.description: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the earth's atmosphere, measured in parts per million (ppm).

kAWmPL0.title: Radiative forcing
kAWmPL0.description: The energy flux per unit area in the atmosphere, measured in W/m². Positive radiative forcing indicates that the Earth receives more energy from the sun than it radiates out into space; negative radiative forcing indicates that the Earth radiates more energy out into space than it receives from the sun.

sAWtOL0.title: Fiber-type grouping
sAWtOL0.description: A characteristic finding of a neurogenic disorder in denervated muscle fibers that have undergone reinnervation from collateral sprouting via adjacent surviving motor neurons.

tAWXlL0.title: Prostration
tAWXlL0.description: A state of extreme physical and/or mental weakness.

FAWglL0.title: Aquagenic pruritus
FAWglL0.description: A sensation of intense itching without associated skin changes that occurs immediately upon contact with hot or cold water and can last for an hour or more. Causes include chronic urticaria, myelodysplastic disorders (e.g., polycythemia vera), and hypereosinophilic syndrome.

DAW1NL0.title: AMI
DAW1NL0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Acute myocardial infarction
2. Acute mesenteric ischemia

wAWhNL0.title: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa
wAWhNL0.description: A type of epidermolysis bullosa in which the blister cleavage plane is within the lamina lucida of the basement membrane zone. Subtypes include JEB-generalized severe (which is associated with a high risk of mortality in the first few years of life), JEB-generalized intermediate (which has more favorable prognosis), and JEB-pyloric atresia.

9AWNNL0.title: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
9AWNNL0.description: A type of epidermolysis bullosa in which the blister cleavage plane is below the lamina lucida of the basement membrane zone. Two major subtypes are dominant dystrophic EB and recessive dystrophic EB, which is typically more severe than the dominant subtype and can cause fusion and deformation of digits.

CAWqNL0.title: Kindler epidermolysis bullosa
CAWqNL0.description: A type of epidermolysis bullosa characterized by photosensitivity, poikiloderma, and skin fragility with formation of acral blisters. Blister cleavage planes develop in multiple skin layers.

xAWENL0.title: Acute urticaria
xAWENL0.description: A form of urticaria (with or without angioedema) that lasts ≤ 6 weeks.

BAWzNL0.title: Chronic urticaria
BAWzNL0.description: A form of urticaria (with or without angioedema) characterized by recurrent symptoms that occur on most days of the week for > 6 weeks.

AAWRmL0.title: Splanchnic vein thrombosis
AAWRmL0.description: The formation of a blood clot within the splanchnic venous system. Includes portal vein thrombosis (most common), splenic vein thrombosis, mesenteric vein thrombosis, and hepatic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari syndrome). Risk factors include liver cirrhosis, myeloproliferative disorders, and congenital hypercoagulable diseases (e.g., protein C deficiency, Factor V Leiden mutation).

-AWDmL0.title: Civil surgeon
-AWDmL0.description: A physician employed by the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to carry out domestic medical screenings. Civil surgeons must have at least 4 years of professional experience following residency and an unrestricted license to practice medicine in the state in which the examinations take place.

Z_WZ5L0.title: Crossed straight leg raise test
Z_WZ5L0.description: An assessment for lumbosacral radiculopathy. With the patient in the supine position, the examiner lifts the extended leg that is contralateral to the suspected lesion. The test is considered positive if the patient experiences pain radiating to the motor and sensory area of the affected nerve root in the leg ipsilateral to the lesion. Highly specific, but not sensitive, for lumbar nerve root lesions.

0_We5L0.title: Reverse straight leg raise test
0_We5L0.description: An assessment for lumbosacral radiculopathy. With the patient in the prone position, the examiner flexes the knee of the affected leg 90-140º and extends the hip by lifting up the leg. The test is considered positive if the patient experiences pain in the ipsilateral leg radiating to the motor and sensory area of the affected nerve root.

a_WQ5L0.title: Biodiversity intactness index
a_WQ5L0.description: An estimation of the variety and number of species in a given area, which is used as an indicator of ecologic change as a result of human influences.

c_WaML0.title: Periductal mastitis
c_WaML0.description: A type of nonpuerperal mastitis characterized by inflammation of nondilated subareolar ducts of the breast. Typically seen in reproductive-age women (median age at presentation: ∼32 years). Smoking is a major risk factor.

f_WknL0.title: High risk of colorectal cancer
f_WknL0.description: An individual with increased risk of colorectal cancer (e.g., due to inflammatory bowel disease, familial cancer syndromes, hereditary polyposis, personal or family history history of colorectal carcinoma). Such individuals require additional cancer screening.

3_WSLL0.title: Posterior leads
3_WSLL0.description: The ECG leads V7–V9. ST elevations in these leads correspond to myocardial infarction of the posterior wall. Obtained by placing ECG leads over the posterior chest wall.

media.title: Right-sided and posterior (extended left) ECG lead placement

R_WlLL0.title: Postpolypectomy coagulation syndrome
R_WlLL0.description: A condition that may occur following endoscopic polyp removal with electrocautery. A transmural burn triggers an inflammatory response that manifests with fever, localized abdominal pain, elevated CRP, and an elevated white blood cell count. Typically resolves with supportive management.

j_W_LL0.title: USMLE® Content Outline
j_W_LL0.description: An outline released by the Federation of State Medical Boards of the United States, Inc. (FSMB) and National Board of Medical Examiners (NBME) that organizes the content of the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) examinations. Domains within the outline include General Principles of Foundational Science, Behavioral Health,  Biostatistics, and organ systems.

P_WWoL0.title: Iron-loading anemia
P_WWoL0.description: A group of disorders characterized by ineffective erythropoiesis, suppression of hepcidin synthesis, and excess iron absorption. May be inherited (e.g., beta thalassemia, congenital sideroblastic anemias) or acquired (e.g., myelodysplastic syndromes).

O_WIoL0.title: Right-sided leads
O_WIoL0.description: The ECG leads V3R–V6R. ST elevations in these leads correspond to myocardial infarction of the right ventricle. Obtained by mirroring the placement of V3–V6 on the right side of the chest. Some sources define the right-sided leads as V1R-V6R, but leads V3R–V6R are typically sufficient to assess for right-sided myocardial infarction.

media.title: Right-sided and posterior (extended left) ECG lead placement

N_W-oL0.title: Herpes gladiatorum
N_W-oL0.description: A cutaneous herpes simplex virus infection acquired from nonsexual physical contact (e.g., wrestling). Common sites of involvement include the torso and extremities.

destinations.label: Herpes simplex virus infections → Cutaneous herpes

n_W7KL0.title: Dilation and evacuation
n_W7KL0.description: The dilation of the cervix and evacuation of the uterus with forceps and vacuum aspiration. Used for abortion after 13 weeks' gestation or for removal of products of conception after fetal demise. Referred to as intact dilation and evacuation when the fetus is removed in one piece.

L_WwKL0.title: Periodontal disease
L_WwKL0.description: A group of inflammatory conditions that affect the supporting tissues of the teeth, including the gingiva, periodontal ligament, and/or alveolar bone.

6_Wj6L0.title: Ever smoker
6_Wj6L0.description: A person who has smoked at least 100 cigarettes during their lifetime. Defined by the US Preventive Services Task Force.

r_WfpL0.title: Cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis
r_WfpL0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder of bile acid metabolism. Clinical features include chronic diarrhea resistant to treatment and cataracts that develop during infancy. If untreated, progresses to cholestatic liver disease, cognitive impairment, spasticity, epilepsy, and tendinous xanthomas formation.

7_W4pL0.title: NGLY1 deficiency
7_W4pL0.description: An autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the NGLY1 gene, which usually encodes N-glycanase, an enzyme involved in protein deglycosylation. Clinical features include hyperkinetic movement disorder, developmental delay, convulsive disorders, and failure to thrive.

H_WKpL0.title: Severe chronic neutropenia
H_WKpL0.description: A rare condition characterized by severe neutropenia (i.e., < 500 cells/mm³) that persists or recurs repeatedly over weeks or months. Results in increased susceptibility to infection.

G_WBpL0.title: Granulomatous drug reaction
G_WBpL0.description: A rare hypersensitivity reaction with granuloma formation in response to self or foreign antigens. Reactions may be limited to the skin or cause systemic effects. Symptoms can take months to years to manifest after drug exposure and often resemble malignancy or other granulomatous diseases.

u_WpJL0.title: Carpal bone mobilization therapy
u_WpJL0.description: A technique in which the bones of the wrist are manipulated with the aim of improving range of motion. The examiner manually glides the bones of the wrist in different directions. May be used in the treatment of carpal tunnel syndrome.

E_W8JL0.title: Therapeutic ultrasound
E_W8JL0.description: A technique in which the energy generated by ultrasound is used in the treatment of medical conditions. Mechanisms involve the application of heat or mechanical stress. Examples of uses for therapeutic ultrasound include physical therapy of joints and extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy.

x_WEqL0.title: Hand symptom diagram
x_WEqL0.description: A picture on which a patient specifies the location and pattern of upper extremity symptoms (e.g., paresthesias). Can be used to help diagnose carpal tunnel syndrome.

y_WdIL0.title: Bile acid synthesis disorders
y_WdIL0.description: A group of autosomal recessive metabolic disorders caused by mutations in genes responsible for bile acid synthesis. Onset is usually during infancy. Clinical features include failure to thrive, jaundice, steatorrhea, hepatomegaly, and growth delay.

UzWbHL0.title: Acanthamoeba
UzWbHL0.description: An ameba that can cause opportunistic infections, including acanthamoeba keratitis and granulomatous amebic encephalitis. Found in soil and water and can be transmitted through inhalation of cysts or direct skin contact.

destinations.label: General parasitology → Protozoa that cause ocular and neurological disease

2zWTHL0.title: Cerebral embolism
2zWTHL0.description: An arterial blockage in the brain caused by debris that formed elsewhere (e.g., cardiac thrombus, septic embolus from endocarditis). Resulting symptoms depend on the brain region affected.

fzWkHL0.title: Periorbital ecchymosis
fzWkHL0.description: A collection of blood beneath the skin around the eye. Can develop as a result of basilar skull fracture or anterior or middle fossa facial trauma.

gzWFHL0.title: Nitric oxide synthase inhibitor
gzWFHL0.description: A compound that inhibits the synthesis of nitric oxide from L-arginine. Endogenous NOS inhibitors include ADMA and L-NMMA. Nitric oxide overproduction is thought to mediate vasodilation in sepsis; however, the clinical use of NOS inhibitors is not yet well understood.

SzWyHL0.title: Never smoker
SzWyHL0.description: A person who has never smoked or who has smoked fewer than 100 cigarettes in their lifetime. Defined by the US National Center for Health Statistics.

hzWcsL0.title: Former smoker
hzWcsL0.description: A person who has smoked at least 100 cigarettes in their lifetime and has since quit smoking. Defined by the US National Center for Health Statistics.

3zWSsL0.title: Every day smoker
3zWSsL0.description: A person who has smoked at least 100 cigarettes in their lifetime and currently smokes every day. Defined by the US National Center for Health Statistics.

RzWlsL0.title: Current smoker
RzWlsL0.description: A person who has smoked at least 100 cigarettes during their lifetime and currently smokes. Defined by the US National Center for Health Statistics.

QzWusL0.title: Periapical lesion
QzWusL0.description: An inflammatory process of the apex of a tooth root caused by bacterial infection of the dental pulp. Includes granulomas, radicular cysts, and abscesses.

4zW3GL0.title: Early infantile epileptic encephalopathy
4zW3GL0.description: A genetic disorder characterized by tonic spasms in infancy associated with a burst-suppression pattern on electroencephalography. Additional features include developmental delay and motor deficits. Typically associated with structural brain abnormalities (e.g., hemimegalencephaly, porencephaly.

kzWmGL0.title: Cemento-osseous dysplasia
kzWmGL0.description: A condition characterized by the replacement of normal bone in the jaw with connective tissue matrix and abnormal bone. Most commonly develops in the periapical area of teeth.

OzWIGL0.title: Postcoital bleeding
OzWIGL0.description: Spotting or bleeding during or after sexual activity that is unrelated to menstruation.

destinations.label: Vaginal bleeding → Vaginal bleeding in nonpregnant adults

lzWvGL0.title: Mucocutaneous candidiasis
lzWvGL0.description: A fungal infection of the skin or mucus membranes caused by a species of Candida, most commonly Candida albicans. Commonly manifests on the skin as a well-demarcated erythematous patch with confluent papules and pustules or on the mucosa as one or more white plaques.

ozW0FL0.title: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex
ozW0FL0.description: A type of epidermolysis bullosa in which the blister cleavage plane is intraepidermal. It is the most common form of EB.  Bullae typically heal without scarring. Subtypes include EBS-localized (previously termed Weber-Cockayne), EBS-generalized intermediate (previously termed Koeber), and EBS-generalized severe (previously termed Dowling-Meara).

KzWUFL0.title: Major depression inventory
KzWUFL0.description: A screening tool used to assess and stratify the severity of symptoms of depression. The patient is asked to reflect on the last week and rank the frequency of symptoms in 10 domains from none of the time (0) to all the time (5 points). Scores of 21-25 suggest mild depression, 26-30 moderate depression, and ≥ 31 severe depression.

6zWjFL0.title: van Gogh syndrome
6zWjFL0.description: A psychiatric condition consisting of repetitive self-mutilation, typically in conjunction with psychosis. This entity is not listed in the DSM-V and does not have well-established criteria.

IzWY8L0.title: Capgras syndrome
IzWY8L0.description: A fixed, false belief that a familiar person has been replaced by an identical duplicate.

HzWK8L0.title: Paracentesis-induced circulatory dysfunction
HzWK8L0.description: A complication of large volume paracentesis that can occur hours to days after the procedure. Related to a reduction in effective blood volume, which can result in renal impairment, hyponatremia, encephalopathy, and/or death.

szWt8L0.title: Posterior myocardial infarction
szWt8L0.description: A myocardial infarction caused by interruption of blood flow to the posterior wall. Findings include ST depressions in ECG leads V1-V3 that are confirmed by ST elevations in the posterior ECG leads (V7-V9). Isolated posterior myocardial infarctions are uncommon and typically manifest as extensions of inferior or lateral infarctions.

media.title: Right-sided and posterior (extended left) ECG lead placement

GzWB8L0.title: de Winter T wave
GzWB8L0.description: An ECG pattern associated with anterior myocardial ischemia. Caused by acute obstruction of the proximal left anterior descending coronary artery. Characterized by precordial J-point depression combined with tall, symmetrical T waves.

tzWXuL0.title: Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale
tzWXuL0.description: A risk assessment tool used to assess thoughts, intentions, plans, and actions relating to suicide. Patients who report an intent or plan for suicide in the last month and/or an action toward suicide in the last three months are considered at high risk and require immediate psychiatric evaluation.

8zWOuL0.title: Bright-light therapy
8zWOuL0.description: A treatment for mood disorders that utilizes daily exposure to blue-white light (typically 10,000 lux for 30 minutes each morning for up to 6 weeks). Recommended as first-line treatment for seasonal affective disorder.

wzWhEL0.title: Problem-solving therapy
wzWhEL0.description: A form of psychotherapy used for mental health conditions such as depression and anxiety. Patients are guided through a structured process of identifying a problem, considering possible solutions, implementing a solution, and assessing its outcome(s).

BzWzEL0.title: Medication preloading
BzWzEL0.description: The administration of a medication prior to another intervention (e.g., to increase the efficacy of the intervention or reduce its adverse effects).

yzWdvL0.title: High-intensity focused ultrasound
yzWdvL0.description: A noninvasive procedure that uses high intensity ultrasound waves to induce tissue necrosis. Can be used in the treatment of various tumors (e.g., liver, kidney, bone, prostate, uterine fibroids).

-zWDvL0.title: Low pretest probability of pulmonary embolism
-zWDvL0.description: A low probability of having a pulmonary embolism based on patient history and clinical features. Typically defined as a modified Wells score for PE ≤ 4, a Wells score for PE < 2, or a revised Geneva score < 4.

destinations.label: Pulmonary embolism → Pretest probability of pulmonary embolism

Z-WZDL0.title: High pretest probability of pulmonary embolism
Z-WZDL0.description: A high probability of having a pulmonary embolism based on patient history and clinical features. Typically defined as a modified Wells score for PE > 4, a Wells score for PE ≥ 7, or a revised Geneva score >10.

destinations.label: Pulmonary embolism → Pretest probability of pulmonary embolism

0-WeDL0.title: Intermediate pretest probability of pulmonary embolism
0-WeDL0.description: An intermediate probability of having a pulmonary embolism based on patient history and clinical features. Typically defined as a Wells score for PE of 2-6 or a revised Geneva score of 4-10.

destinations.label: Pulmonary embolism → Pretest probability of pulmonary embolism

a-WQDL0.title: Female genital mutilation
a-WQDL0.description: The partial or total removal of the external female genitalia performed for traditional reasons in parts of Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, typically before the individual is 15 years of age. The term "female circumcision" is no longer used due to the implication of it being a procedure comparable to male circumcision. FGM is a harmful tradition with no clinical benefit that can have detrimental effects on an individual's physical, mental, and sexual health. For this reason, it is considered a violation of human rights today.

Y-WnDL0.title: Barmah Forest virus disease
Y-WnDL0.description: A mosquito-borne viral disease caused by the Barmah forest virus.  Barmah forest virus disease manifests with fever, headache, fatigue, joint pain and swelling, and skin rashes.

destinations.label: Miscellaneous mosquito-borne diseases → Mosquito-borne Togavirus diseases

b-WHDL0.title: Noninvasive prenatal testing
b-WHDL0.description: A group of tests that can be used to evaluate for trisomy 21, 18, and 13, and other select sex chromosome aneuploidies. Though term typically refers to cell-free fetal DNA testing, there are other serum screening tests (e.g., first-trimester combined test) that are also noninvasive.

d-WowL0.title: Range of motion exercises
d-WowL0.description: A type of physical therapy that involves repetitive movement of a specific joint to preserve or improve joint mobility. Range of motion exercises can be passive, assisted, or active.

V-WGwL0.title: Magnetic resonance neurography
V-WGwL0.description: A type of magnetic resonance imaging used to evaluate peripheral nerves (e.g., in patients with peripheral neuropathy).

g-WF9L0.title: Clinical features of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
g-WF9L0.description: A collection of signs and symptoms suggestive of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in patients with ascites. Features may be subtle and include diffuse abdominal pain, fever, worsening ascites, jaundice, and new-onset or worsening encephalopathy. Asymptomatic presentations are also possible.

S-Wy9L0.title: Paraneoplastic panel
S-Wy9L0.description: A group of laboratory tests for autoantibodies to proteins in the nervous system. Used to evaluate for paraneoplastic syndromes. Includes antineuronal nuclear antibody 1, antiglial nuclear antibodies, and antibodies against P/Q voltage-gated calcium channels.

i-WJCL0.title: Retapamulin
i-WJCL0.description: A topical antibiotic that impairs bacterial protein synthesis by binding to protein L3 on the ribosomal 50S subunit, preventing peptidyl transfer. Used to treat impetigo caused by methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes.

4-W3xL0.title: 5 As of access to health care
4-W3xL0.description: A set of factors that influence an individual's ability to enter into or use a health care system. Established by Penchansky and Thomas in 1981, the specific dimensions are availability, (physical) accessibility, accommodation, affordability, and acceptability. Used to assess existing health care systems and develop new models for accessible health care.

N-W-xL0.title: Poor neonatal adaptation
N-W-xL0.description: A syndrome that includes jitteriness, poor feeding, respiratory distress, and hypoglycemia in neonates who have had in utero exposure to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. Often resolves with no long-term consequences.

m-WVBL0.title: Mixed hyperbilirubinemia
m-WVBL0.description: The presence of increased concentrations of unconjugated (indirect) and conjugated (direct) bilirubin in the serum. Etiologies include cirrhosis and hepatitis.

5-WiBL0.title: Spontaneous gas gangrene
5-WiBL0.description: A life-threatening necrotizing soft tissue infection caused by Clostridium septicum. Usually occurs in patients with malignancy (e.g., colon carcinoma), diabetes, or immunosuppression. C. speticum spreads hematogenously from an initital lesion in the GI tract to the muscle tissue. Clinical features include excruciating muscle pain, edema with subsequent skin discoloration (red-purple to black) and gas production. Crepitus, as well as a feathering pattern of gas in soft tissue imaging, are generally present. Treatment includes surgical debridement in combination with antibiotic therapy.

L-WwBL0.title: Primary graft failure
L-WwBL0.description: A complication of the early postoperative period after organ transplantation in which there is inadequate function of the transplanted organ leading to organ death and/or retransplantation.

o-W0yL0.title: Primary graft dysfunction
o-W0yL0.description: A complication of organ transplantation that is characterized by organ-specific measures of impaired function. Lung PGD involves diffuse pulmonary opacities on imaging and hypoxemia within 72 hours after graft implantation. Cardiac PGD involves ventricular dysfunction within 24 hours after graft implantation.

6-WjyL0.title: Drug-induced neutropenia
6-WjyL0.description: The destruction of neutrophils by drug-dependent antibodies against neutrophil membrane glycoproteins, leading to an absolute neutrophil count of < 1500/mm³ (neutropenia) or < 500/mm³ (agranulocytosis). Can predispose to severe infections (e.g., sepsis). Common causative agents include antibiotics, carbamazepine, clozapine, levamisole, and antithyroid drugs.

J-WsyL0.title: Gametocytes
J-WsyL0.description: A type of trophizite within the malaria parasite life cycle that transformed into male or female precursors instead of asexual schizonts. The malaria life cycle begins when the Anopheles mosquito ingests gametocytes.

7-W4AL0.title: Work of breathing
7-W4AL0.description: The energy used to overcome elastic recoil and airway resistance by the respiratory muscles for respiration. Determined by elastic recoil and airway resistance and expressed (in joules) as the product of pressure and volume (W = P × V).

H-WKAL0.title: Anti-Kell antibody
H-WKAL0.description: An antibody (usually IgG) against Kell blood group antigens that can result in the destruction of both mature red blood cells and their precursors. Can cause hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn and transfusion reactions.

G-WBAL0.title: Immune privilege
G-WBAL0.description: The ability of certain tissues or organs (e.g., cornea, central nervous system, placenta, testis) to tolerate the introduction of allografts without eliciting an inflammatory immune response. Placement of allografts in an immune-privileged site does not lead to graft rejection.

t-WX_L0.title: The 4 R's of trauma-informed care
t-WX_L0.description: The SAMHSA’s traumainformed approach for medical staff or organizations. The ultimate goal of this approach is to avoid retraumatization. The four Rs are Realization, Recognize, Respond, Resist retraumatization.

destinations.label: Patient communication and counseling → Trauma-informed communication

A-WR-L0.title: Process map
A-WR-L0.description: The visualization of processes using tools such as flowcharts to establish, analyze, and improve processes. Outlines each step within a process, identifies task owners and relationships, and provides details regarding expected timelines.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Analysis of medical error

0ZdeZo0.title: Cold stimulation test (cold urticaria)
0ZdeZo0.description: A diagnostic test for cold urticaria in which a cold object is applied to the skin and then removed. The appearance of a palpable wheal with pruritus after the skin rewarms indicates a positive test. If there is no reaction or only erythema or pruritus, the test is negative.

aZdQZo0.title: Ice cube test
aZdQZo0.description: A cold stimulation test used to evaluate for cold urticaria. A bag with an ice cube and a small amount of water is placed against the skin for 5 minutes. Response is evaluated 10 minutes after removing the bag. If a palpable pruritic or burning wheal appears, the test is positive.

YZdnZo0.title: TempTest 4.0
YZdnZo0.description: A device used for evaluating cold urticaria by identifying the temperature threshold at which symptoms occur.

fZdkao0.title: Nonmotile cilia
fZdkao0.description: The hair-like projections found on the apical surface of epithelial cells. Composed of nine doublet microtubules without a central microtubule pair (9 + 0 axoneme). Involved in signal sensation and transduction and the regulation of cellular differentiation and division.

SZdyao0.title: Admission criteria for patients with dehydration and hypovolemia
SZdyao0.description: A set of criteria used to assess the need for inpatient treatment for dehydration or hypovolemia. Criteria include severe, prolonged, or excessive fluid loss, inability to tolerate oral fluids, significant derangements of electrolytes, high-risk patients (extremes of age, underlying health conditions), or barriers to follow-up.

RZdlYo0.title: aVR ST-segment elevation
RZdlYo0.description: An ECG finding concerning for obstructive disease of the left main coronary artery and/or proximal left anterior descending artery. Especially concerning when accompanied by multilead ST depressions, which most commonly occur in leads I, II, aVL, and V4-V6.

PZdWbo0.title: As-treated analysis
PZdWbo0.description: A statistical analysis method in which participants are evaluated based on the treatment they ultimately received, regardless of the initial treatment assigned by randomization. This method is a variant of per-protocol analysis and is mainly used to assess adverse effects of treatment.

OZdIbo0.title: Mild to moderate gastroenteritis
OZdIbo0.description: A classification of infectious diarrhea in which symptoms do not disrupt daily life or functioning. Patients present with nausea, diarrhea, and/or vomiting but are able to maintain normal hydration. Other features (e.g., abdominal pain), if present, are not significant and physical examination is typically normal.

KZdUco0.title: Immunoglobulin light chain restriction
KZdUco0.description: The disproportionate decrease in the cell surface expression of either kappa or lambda immunoglobulin light chains, resulting in an abnormal kappa:lambda ratio. This finding is associated with B-cell lymphomas such as chronic lymphocytic leukemia, hairy cell leukemia, and mantle cell lymphoma and is indicative of B-cell monoclonality.

6Zdjco0.title: Risk factors for syphilis infection
6Zdjco0.description: Factors include men who have sex with men, adolescents, infants born to a birthing parent with syphilis, HIV infection, history of sexually transmitted infection, multiple sexual partners, unprotected sex, substance use disorders, and history of incarceration.

JZdsco0.title: Hanks balanced salt solution
JZdsco0.description: An isotonic salt solution that is physiologically balanced to preserve or promote the growth of many cell types. It is the preferred medium for maintaining the viability of an avulsed tooth.

IZdY1o0.title: Pericoronitis
IZdY1o0.description: The inflammation and/or infection of the periodontal tissue surrounding an emerging tooth.  Most commonly occurs with the eruption of the mandibular third molar.

rZdf1o0.title: Respiratory support
rZdf1o0.description: The use of intervention(s) to assist breathing, oxygenation, and/or ventilation. Includes repositioning, airway clearance, oxygen therapy, noninvasive ventilation, and intubation with mechanical ventilation.

vZdAWo0.title: Interpersonal therapy for adolescents
vZdAWo0.description: A time-limited (12 to 16 weeks) treatment approach that aims to improve understanding of problematic interpersonal relationships (e.g., with parents or peers) and/or life situations and thereby help control a patient's moods and patterns of behavior. Used in adolescents aged 12-18 years with major depressive disorder.

CZdqdo0.title: Immunosenescence
CZdqdo0.description: An age-associated phenomenon characterized by decreased function of the immune system as a result of multiple factors (e.g., decreased naive T cells, decreased response to antigens). Results in increased susceptibility to infection, decreased response to vaccination, and increased risk of inflammatory diseases.

xZdEdo0.title: Deep suction
xZdEdo0.description:
A term that can refer to:
1. Deep nasopharyngeal suction
2. Deep endotracheal suction (of endotracheal tubes or tracheostomies)

e0dxUo0.title: Endotracheal suction
e0dxUo0.description: A method for removing mucous and lower respiratory secretions from an endotracheal or tracheostomy tube. A small-caliber suction catheter is inserted into the artificial airway (superficial suction) and may be continued until resistance is met at the level of the tracheal carina (deep suction). Negative pressure is applied as the catheter is withdrawn.

U0db2o0.title: Kaplan-Meier curve
U0db2o0.description: A graphical representation of data derived from Kaplan-Meier analysis. The x-axis represents time and the y-axis represents the estimated probability of survival. Allows for an estimation of the probability that the subject will survive up to a point in time.

f0dk2o0.title: Zoster vaccine live
f0dk2o0.description: A live-attenuated vaccine that provides immunity against varicella-zoster virus (HHV-3), the pathogen responsible for chickenpox and shingles. Is less effective than the recombinant zoster vaccine. No longer commercially available in the United States.

g0dF2o0.title: Survivor guilt
g0dF2o0.description: A psychological condition characterized by persistent feelings of guilt associated with surviving a life-threatening situation (e.g., cancer, motor vehicle collision, natural disaster). Can stem from distress over a sense of self worth, distress about the belief that one could have done more for others, and/or distress over the deaths of others.

R0dlfo0.title: Red flags in urinary incontinence
R0dlfo0.description: Conditions that suggest underlying pathology in urinary incontinence and require referral to a specialist for further investigation. These include pain, hematuria or proteinuria, recurrent urinary tract infections, symptoms of obstruction, pelvic organ prolapse, suspected fistula, elevated postvoid residual volume, and incontinence after radiation or surgery.

50digo0.title: Capillary blood gas
50digo0.description: A laboratory test that quickly assesses the level of oxygen, carbon dioxide, bicarbonate, and pH in blood collected from the capillary system (usually from the heel, fingertip, or earlobe). Capillary blood values are usually similar to arterial blood values.

M0dMgo0.title: Vertebral facet dislocation
M0dMgo0.description: An anterior displacement of one vertebral body over another. Typically caused by excess flexion (e.g., due to a motor vehicle collision). Further classified as unilateral or bilateral.

destinations.label: Cervical spine injuries → Lower cervical spine injuries

o0d0So0.title: Exercise-induced urticaria
o0d0So0.description: A type of physical (inducible) urticaria that is triggered by physical activity. Can be a result of elevated core body temperature or an early symptom of exercise-induced anaphylaxis.

K0dUSo0.title: Right-to-left cardiac shunt
K0dUSo0.description: A phenomenon in which blood from the right side of the heart flows to the left side due to a cardiac defect. Causes deoxygenated blood to enter the systemic circulation, which leads to cyanosis. Associated cardiac defects include transposition of the great vessels, tricuspid atresia, and tetralogy of Fallot.

destinations.label: Cyanotic congenital heart defects → Overview of cyanotic congenital heart defects

q0dCSo0.title: Femoral arteriovenous fistula
q0dCSo0.description: An abnormal connection between the femoral artery and vein. Most commonly caused by percutaneous access to these vessels for cardiovascular procedures.

70d4ho0.title: Denervation
70d4ho0.description: The loss of efferent innervation of a target tissue (i.e., a muscle, another nerve, or a gland) due to degeneration of the responsible nerve.

t0dX3o0.title: Patient Health Questionnaire-9 modified for adolescents
t0dX3o0.description: A survey used to assess for and monitor symptoms of major depressive disorder in adolescents. Based on the PHQ-9 used for adults but modified to include irritability in the assessment of mood and weight loss in the assessment of appetite.

v0dA3o0.title: Anthropometric measurements
v0dA3o0.description: A set of measurements of the body. Used to evaluate an individual's overall health, nutritional status, and risk for disease. Example measurements include height, weight, BMI, and waist circumference.

90dNRo0.title: Peripheral venous access
90dNRo0.description: A catheter terminating in a peripheral vein that can be used for intravenous fluid therapy, medication administration, and/or blood sampling.

x0dERo0.title: Urethral insert
x0dERo0.description: A device that is inserted into the urethra to prevent involuntary leakage of urine. May be inserted by the patient whenever incontinence is expected, e.g., prior to physical activity, and removed for micturition.

B0dzRo0.title: External catheter
B0dzRo0.description: An external urine collection device used in the management of incontinence. For individuals with male genitalia, a sheath is fitted over the penis (similar to a condom) with a tube at the distal end that connects to a drainage bag. For patients with female genitalia, a sheath or silicone cap is placed over the urethra and connected to a diversion bag or a collection device attached to suction.

-0dDio0.title: AED
-0dDio0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Automated external defibrillator
2. Antiepileptic drug

ZadZQo0.title: Evidence of VZV immunity
ZadZQo0.description: A set of criteria used to determine the need for vaccination or postexposure prophylaxis against varicella-zoster virus. Based on serum antibody titers or record of past infection or vaccination.

aadQQo0.title: Acute bacterial conjunctivitis
aadQQo0.description: A type of infectious conjunctivitis most commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumonia and Haemophilus influenza in children and Staphylococcus aureus in adults, and characterized by thick mucopurulent discharge. Symptoms commonly last for 7-10 days but may last for up to 4 weeks.

YadnQo0.title: Chronic bacterial conjunctivitis
YadnQo0.description: A type of infectious conjunctivitis commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus, Moraxella lacunata, or enteric bacteria in which symptoms (e.g., red eye, purulent discharge, and pain) typically last for more than 4 weeks.

badHQo0.title: Transient causes of urinary incontinence
badHQo0.description: A group of reversible conditions that can cause acute urinary incontinence. Often remembered using the mnemonic DIAPPERS: Delirium, Infection of the urinary tract, Atrophic vaginitis, Pharmaceuticals, Psychiatric conditions, Excessive urine output, Reduced mobility, and Stool impaction.

cadajo0.title: Ectopic atrial bradycardia
cadajo0.description: An ectopic atrial rhythm with a rate of < 50 bpm generated by an atrial pacemaker other than the sinoatrial node.

3adS4o0.title: Peripartum hemorrhage
3adS4o0.description: A term used to refer to either antepartum hemorrhage (i.e., the occurrence of vaginal bleeding after the 20th week of gestation) or postpartum hemorrhage (i.e., blood loss ≥ 1000 mL or bleeding associated with signs or symptoms of hypovolemia within 24 hours of delivery).

Radl4o0.title: Cold stimulation test (Raynaud phenomenon)
Radl4o0.description: A test used to diagnose and assess treatment for Raynaud phenomenon. The hands are submerged in cold water to trigger symptoms and then removed. The time needed for the fingers to return to normal body temperature is recorded. Normal rewarming time is < 10 minutes.

ladvko0.title: Less urgent hyperkalemia
ladvko0.description: A serum potassium concentration of < 6.0 mEq/L in patients who do not have clinical features of hyperkalemia (e.g., muscle weakness, paresthesia, hyporeflexia) or ECG changes characteristic of hyperkalemia (e.g., tall, peaked T waves).

Nad-ko0.title: Uremic platelet dysfunction
Nad-ko0.description: An acquired impairment of platelet function seen in patients with advanced renal insufficiency. Results in prolonged bleeding time and an increased bleeding tendency.

nad7Oo0.title: Clinical microsystems
nad7Oo0.description: A core functional unit (e.g., neonatal ICU, emergency department) that exists within a larger organization (e.g., hospital) and provides care for a set population at a specific location. Clinical microsystems involve the interaction of various roles (e.g., patients, health care professionals, support staff), processes (e.g., information sharing), and environmental factors (e.g., work environment, facility architecture, and equipment).

destinations.label: Quality improvement → Continuous quality improvement in health care

7ad4No0.title: Canadian TIA score
7ad4No0.description: A clinical tool used to assess the seven-day risk of stroke after a transient ischemic attack. A score is derived from patient history, physical examination, and bedside and blood test findings.

HadKNo0.title: Drug hypersensitivity reaction
HadKNo0.description: An unpredictable adverse drug reaction caused by an immunologically-mediated or inflammatory response to a medication and/or its inactive ingredients. Can be immediate (typically mast cell mediated, e.g., anaphylaxis, angioedemia, urticaria) or nonimmediate (typically T-cell mediated, e.g., fixed drug eruptions, DRESS, Stevens Johnson syndrome).

media.title: Facial edema in drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)

Fadgmo0.title: Red flags in eating disorders
Fadgmo0.description: A collection of clinical features and laboratory parameters suggestive of a severe eating disorder that may require inpatient management. Includes very low BMI (< 15 kg/m2), rapid weight loss, unstable vital signs, metabolic abnormalities, abnormal ECG, and acute refusal to eat or uncontrolled bingeing and/or purging.

8adOmo0.title: Percent median BMI
8adOmo0.description: A method used to compare an individual's BMI to a reference population. Calculated by dividing the individual's BMI by the median (50th percentile) BMI for their age and sex and multiplying by 100.

Dad15o0.title: Active urine sediment
Dad15o0.description: A finding of urine sediment with cells, casts, or crystals. Can be useful in the diagnosis of kidney disease, e.g., acute tubular necrosis, nephritic syndrome, nephrotic syndrome, crystalline nephropathy.

xadE5o0.title: Postoperative pulmonary edema
xadE5o0.description: The acute postsurgical development of pulmonary edema. Etiology may be cardiogenic (e.g., due to myocardial infarction or arrhythmia) or noncardiogenic (e.g., severe central nervous system trauma, acute lung injury, negative pressure pulmonary edema, or anaphylaxis).

AadRMo0.title: Primary osteoarthritis
AadRMo0.description: A chronic degenerative disease involving joint tissues (e.g., cartilage). The cause is unknown, but it is more commonly seen in older adults than in younger adults. Typically affects the knees, hands, and hips. Symptoms include pain and stiffness, which may progress to functional impairment.

_ad5Mo0.title: Secondary osteoarthritis
_ad5Mo0.description: A degenerative disease involving joint tissues (e.g., cartilage) caused by an underlying medical condition (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis) or trauma. Symptoms include pain and stiffness, which may progress to functional impairment.

-adDMo0.title: Treponemal tests
-adDMo0.description: Tests that detect antibodies against treponemal antigens. Treponemal tests include Treponema pallidum particle agglutination (TPPA) and the fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption test (FTA-ABS).

ZYdZno0.title: Serofast status
ZYdZno0.description: The persistence of a nontreponemal serological response (≥ fourfold decline in titers) in a patient who has received treatment for syphilis.

YYdnno0.title: Functional incontinence
YYdnno0.description: A type of incontinence in which the patient has normal bladder and/or bowel function but cannot access and/or use the toilet in time as a result of physical or cognitive impairment.

cYdaLo0.title: APRI score
cYdaLo0.description: A score used to confirm the presence of cirrhosis in patients with chronic HBV, chronic HCV, MASLD, AIH, or PBC. Laboratory parameters used in the score include AST and platelet count.

1Yd2Lo0.title: Clinical features of malignant otitis externa
1Yd2Lo0.description: Features include symptoms of acute otitis externa (e.g., red and swollen external auditory canal, otorrhea, conductive hearing loss), severe and persistent ear and/or jaw pain, fever, headache, facial nerve palsy, periauricular erythema and edema, and granulation tissue at the cartilage-bone junction of the external auditory canal on otoscopy.

VYdGLo0.title: Opioid use disorder
VYdGLo0.description: A chronic disease characterized by a persistent pattern of maladaptive behaviors related to the use of opioids, including use despite adverse consequences and a preoccupation with obtaining opioids.

eYdxLo0.title: PCV
eYdxLo0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Pressure-control ventilation
2. Polycythemia vera
3. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine

UYdboo0.title: Inappropriate weight compensatory behaviors
UYdboo0.description: An action performed to control body weight, e.g., following a binge eating episode. May include self-induced vomiting, misuse of laxatives or other medications, food restriction, and excessive exercise.

2YdToo0.title: Family-based therapy
2YdToo0.description: A type of psychotherapy used in the management of adolescents with eating disorders. Consists of three phases: phase one focuses on weight restoration, with the caregiver responsible for the adolescent's eating; in phase 2, the adolescent becomes responsible for their own eating; and phase 3 focuses on the psychosocial issues related to the eating disorder.

fYdkoo0.title: Binge eating episode
fYdkoo0.description: An episode during which an individual consumes an excessive amount of food within a certain period of time (usually ≤ 2 hours) and experiences a loss of control while eating (e.g., inability to stop eating despite being full; inability to control what they are eating). Recurrent episodes are characteristic of certain eating disorders, e.g., bulimia nervosa and binge eating disorder.

gYdFoo0.title: Chronic otitis externa
gYdFoo0.description: An inflammation of the external auditory canal lasting from at least 6 weeks to 3 months.

SYdyoo0.title: Acute otitis externa
SYdyoo0.description: An inflammation of the external auditory canal lasting < 6 weeks.

hYdcKo0.title: Supportive therapy for conjunctivitis
hYdcKo0.description: A set of measures for the relief of ocular symptoms associated with conjunctivitis. Examples include refrigerated artificial tears, cleaning discharge from the eye, compresses (warm or cold), and discontinuation of contact lens use.

3YdSKo0.title: Red flags in conjunctivitis
3YdSKo0.description: A collection of symptoms in patients with conjunctivitis that suggest a concerning underlying etiology. Includes significant eye pain, vision changes, corneal involvement, symptoms suggestive of neisserial conjunctivitis or herpes simplex conjunctivitis, or risk factors that predispose patients to serious infections, e.g., contact lens use, immunodeficiency, or a history of recurrent conjunctivitis.

destinations.label: Overview of conjunctivitis → Red flags in conjunctivitis

QYduKo0.title: Rescue breathing
QYduKo0.description: A method of providing additional ventilatory support to patients with apnea or bradypnea (e.g., due to opioid toxicity, general anesthesia, cardiac arrest). Commonly performed using bag-mask ventilation or mouth-to-mouth.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)

jYd_Ko0.title: Urogenital ridge
jYd_Ko0.description: An embryologic structure that derives from the intermediate mesoderm and gives rise to the urogenital organs.

PYdW6o0.title: Hemopericardium
PYdW6o0.description: The accumulation of blood in the pericardial space between the parietal and visceral pericardium. Clinically similar to other types of pericardial effusion and can lead to cardiac tamponade.

destinations.label: Pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade → Etiology

4Yd36o0.title: Performance status
4Yd36o0.description: A type of score that assesses an individual's independent functional ability. Factors assessed include the level of assistance required for normal activities and the presence of symptoms. Typically used to predict a patient's ability to tolerate anticancer therapy.

lYdv6o0.title: Pubic symphysis diastasis
lYdv6o0.description: A rare complication of the peripartum period in which there is a widening of the pubic symphysis beyond the physiologic width (i.e., > 10 mm).

NYd-6o0.title: Destot sign
NYd-6o0.description: A physical examination finding of a hematoma superior to the inguinal ligament. Suggests pelvic ligament injury  (e.g., due to pubic symphysis diastasis, pelvic fracture).

5Ydipo0.title: Relative energy deficiency in sport
5Ydipo0.description: A syndrome in athletes that is characterized by impaired physiological function in multiple systems due to inadequate energy intake relative to energy expenditure. Includes the components traditionally referred to as the female athlete triad (relative calorie deficit, menstrual dysfunction, and decreased bone density) as well as impairments in cardiovascular health, immunity, GI function, and neurocognitive function.

nYd7po0.title: Self-efficacy
nYd7po0.description: The perception a person has of their ability to complete a particular task or achieve desired results. Self-efficacy may be assessed to estimate a patient's ability to actively participate in the management of their medical condition(s).

oYd0Jo0.title: Sex hormone profile
oYd0Jo0.description: A group of laboratory tests that measure the levels of sex hormones in the blood. The panel typically includes testosterone, estradiol, luteinizing hormone (LH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), and sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG).

6YdjJo0.title: Infiltration anesthesia
6YdjJo0.description: The loss of sensation in a localized superficial area via injection of a local anesthetic agent into subcutaneous or submucosal tissue.

qYdCJo0.title: Eutectic mixture of local anesthetics
qYdCJo0.description: A topical anesthetic cream containing 2.5% lidocaine and 2.5% prilocaine.

IYdYqo0.title: Lidocaine/epinephrine/tetracaine
IYdYqo0.description: A topical anesthetic agent containing lidocaine, epinephrine, and tetracaine that is available in various formulations.

rYdfqo0.title: Chemoimmunotherapy
rYdfqo0.description: A type of cancer therapy that combines one or more chemotherapy agents with immunotherapy agents. This combination often has a synergistic effect, leading to improved treatment outcomes. For example, the combination of the chemotherapy agents fludarabine and cyclophosphamide with the immunotherapy agent rituximab is a common treatment regimen in chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

7Yd4qo0.title: Topical anesthesia
7Yd4qo0.description: The loss of sensation to skin or mucosa by direct application of a local anesthetic agent (e.g., in the form of a gel, ointment, spray, or patch).

tYdXIo0.title: Micromelia
tYdXIo0.description: A growth defect characterized by abnormally small limbs. Associated with skeletal dysplasias (e.g., osteogenesis imperfecta).

uYdpIo0.title: Sacral sparing
uYdpIo0.description: The preservation of deep anal pressure sensation, voluntary anal contraction, and light touch and pinprick sensation in sacral spinal cord segments (S4-S5) and below.

vYdAIo0.title: HIPAA Permitted Uses and Disclosures
vYdAIo0.description: The standard policy for disclosure of protected health information (PHI). Disclosure of PHI is permitted to patients themselves; to health care workers involved in the patient's care; for treatment, payment, and health care operations purposes; for national priority purposes; for research and public health purposes (limited data set); and when disclosure cannot be reasonably prevented (e.g., if the patient is incapacitated).

DYd1ro0.title: Risk factors for MOE
DYd1ro0.description: Includes age > 60 years, diabetes mellitus, and immunosuppression.

xYdEro0.title: Serologic evidence of immunity
xYdEro0.description: The presence of serum antibody titers that are expected to offer protection against a particular disease. Antibodies may be present due to prior infection or vaccination. Examples include Hepatitis B surface antibody titers and varicella antibody IgG.

0bdeHo0.title: Secnidazole
0bdeHo0.description: An antiprotozoal and antibacterial nitroimidazole derivative used to treat bacterial vaginosis. Thought to interfere with DNA synthesis.

YbdnHo0.title: Puerperal hematoma
YbdnHo0.description: An accumulation of blood in the vulva, vagina, or retroperitoneum, most commonly resulting from iatrogenic injury (e.g., cervical laceration, episiotomy) during childbirth. Clinical findings include postpartum bleeding, severe pain in the perineum, and a palpable vaginal mass. Severe bleeding can lead to hypovolemic shock, which can be life-threatening.

Xbd9Ho0.title: Punctal occlusion
Xbd9Ho0.description: A therapy to reduce dry eye symptoms by occluding the upper and/or lower puncta to delay the clearance of natural tears. May be temporary (e.g., silicone or collagen plugs) or permanent (e.g., thermal or laser cautery).

cbdaso0.title: Ankyloblepharon
cbdaso0.description: A complete or partial fusion of the ciliary edges of the upper and lower eyelid. May be congenital or acquired (e.g., secondary to trauma or cicatrizing conjunctivitis).

1bd2so0.title: Psoas muscle hematoma
1bd2so0.description: A hematoma located in the retrofascial space within the psoas muscle. Etiologies include trauma, surgery, anticoagulant use, and coagulation disorders.

dbdoso0.title: Allergen testing
dbdoso0.description: Studies done to identify the causative allergen in patients with allergic symptoms and/or conditions (e.g., pruritus, rash, sneezing, nasal congestion). Modalities include skin tests and immunoassays.

VbdGso0.title: Red flags for rhinosinusitis
VbdGso0.description: A set of features suggestive of complications of rhinosinusitis. Includes high/prolonged fever, severe headache, altered mental status, focal neurologic deficits, ophthalmic complications, facial edema, and failure to improve after treatment.

ebdxso0.title: Spontaneous retroperitoneal hematoma
ebdxso0.description: Bleeding into the retroperitoneal space without preceding trauma or iatrogenic intervention.

UbdbGo0.title: Microdeletion syndrome
UbdbGo0.description: A group of syndromes characterized by chromosomal deletions that cannot be detected by light microscopy (typically < 5 megabases). Examples include DiGeorge syndrome, Prader-Willi syndrome, Angelman syndrome, and neurofibromatosis type I and II.

2bdTGo0.title: X-linked disease
2bdTGo0.description: A condition that is inherited on the X chromosome. Historically, this term has been subdivided into dominant and recessive forms of inheritance, although this distinction is somewhat unclear because of the phenomenon of uneven X-inactivation in female individuals.

fbdkGo0.title: Sterile field
fbdkGo0.description: An area that is kept free of microbial contamination prior to an invasive procedure. May include surfaces, instruments, and personnel. A sterile field is usually achieved by disinfecting surfaces; using antiseptic skin preparation; and using sterile barriers such as drapes, personal protective equipment, and sterile covers for equipment.

gbdFGo0.title: Vascular dilator
gbdFGo0.description: A device used in percutaneous procedures to mechanically widen the tissue tract, allowing for the insertion of larger devices (e.g., sheaths, catheters).

SbdyGo0.title: Sterile ultrasound probe cover
SbdyGo0.description: A sterile cover for an ultrasound probe that helps prevent infection during ultrasound-guided invasive procedures (e.g., central line placement, biopsies). Ultrasound gel is placed in a sterile plastic sheath. This portion of the sheath is applied directly to the surface of the probe and held in place with rubber bands or adhesive strips. The remainder of the sheath is extended to cover the transducer and cord with a sterile barrier.

3bdSto0.title: Pseudopemphigoid
3bdSto0.description: A nonprogressive cicatricial conjunctivitis that clinically mimics ocular cicatricial pemphigoid but develops in response to certain topical medications, particularly glaucoma treatment.

Qbduto0.title: Usual interstitial pneumonia
Qbduto0.description: A type of interstitial lung disease characterized by distinct radiologic and histopathologic findings that are highly specific for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). On a CT scan, a honeycomb appearance of the lung parenchyma with subpleural and basal predominance is sufficient to diagnose IPF. If imaging is inconclusive, histopathologic features of UIP (e.g., dense subpleural fibrosis) increase diagnostic accuracy.

jbd_to0.title: Skin preparation
jbd_to0.description: The process of disinfecting intact skin using antiseptic (e.g., alcohol-, chlorhexidine-, iodine-based) solutions to decrease skin bacterial load and prevent surgical and procedural site infections.

PbdWFo0.title: Simple interrupted suture
PbdWFo0.description: A suture technique in which each stitch is placed and tied separately under minimal or no tension. Failure of one knot does not affect the suture line. Commonly used to close small wounds that are well-approximated (e.g., punch biopsy site, lacerations).

4bd3Fo0.title: Sterile dressing
4bd3Fo0.description: A wound dressing applied in a sterile field. Reduces the risk of infection by preventing wound contamination and absorbing wound exudate. Commonly applied at surgical and procedural sites (e.g., central line insertion site).

kbdmFo0.title: Occlusive dressing
kbdmFo0.description: A dressing with an impermeable barrier against air and moisture. Dressings may be impregnated with occlusive agents (e.g., petrolatum gauze) or medications (e.g., topical steroids). Commonly used for wound care (e.g., around chest tube insertion sites) and as part of the treatment for certain dermatological conditions (e.g., atopic dermatitis and lichen simplex chronicus).

ObdIFo0.title: Tecovirimat
