ObdIFo0.description: An antiviral drug that inhibits the VP37 envelope wrapping protein in orthopoxviruses. Tecovirimat is approved by the FDA for the treatment of smallpox. It may also be used for the treatment of monkeypox.

Nbd-Fo0.title: Brincidofovir
Nbd-Fo0.description: An Orthopoxvirus nucleotide analog that inhibits viral DNA polymerase. Brincidofovir is a prodrug that is intracellularly converted to cidofovir, and it is FDA-approved for the treatment of smallpox.

mbdV8o0.title: Brown bag medication review
mbdV8o0.description: A type of medication reconciliation intended to reduce polypharmacy and medication errors. The patient brings all medications to the clinic and reviews with a clinician why, when, and how they take each one. Results are then compared to the medication list on the patient's records and disparities between the two are corrected.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of medication errors

MbdM8o0.title: Fetal heart rate tracing
MbdM8o0.description: A method of monitoring fetal status during pregnancy and labor that traces a fetus's baseline heart rate, baseline heart rate variability, and heart rate accelerations or decelerations.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

nbd78o0.title: Category I FHR tracing
nbd78o0.description: A normal fetal heart rate pattern that is not associated with fetal hypoxic acidemia and, therefore, does not require any treatment.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

Lbdw8o0.title: Category III FHR tracing
Lbdw8o0.description: An abnormal fetal heart rate pattern associated with an increased risk of fetal hypoxic acidemia. Management includes resuscitative measures and scalp stimulation. If neither results in FHR acceleration, expedited delivery is indicated.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Intrapartum fetal monitoring

Jbdsuo0.title: Ring vaccination
Jbdsuo0.description: A targeted infection mitigation strategy in which the primary and secondary close contacts of a confirmed case are vaccinated, limiting the spread of a contagion. Ring vaccination was key to the elimination of smallpox in the 1970s.

IbdYEo0.title: CRS
IbdYEo0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Chronic rhinosinusitis
2) Cytokine release syndrome
3) Congenital rubella syndrome

rbdfEo0.title: Vasopressinase
rbdfEo0.description: A placental aminopeptidase that degrades antidiuretic hormone (ADH). Increased production of vasopressinase in the third trimester of pregnancy results in decreased serum ADH concentrations. Excessive increase in production can result in transient diabetes insipidus of pregnancy.

destinations.label: Arginine vasopressin disorders → Special patient groups

GbdBEo0.title: Multivariate model
GbdBEo0.description: A statistical method that calculates the individual contributions of multiple risk factors (also called independent variables) to an outcome (also called the dependent variable). Different types of multivariable analysis (e.g., multiple linear regression, multiple logistic regression) can be used to analyze different outcomes.

tbdXvo0.title: Vaginal pH
tbdXvo0.description: The degree of acidity or alkalinity of vaginal fluid. A normal vaginal fluid pH is between 4 and 4.5.

destinations.label: Diagnostic procedures in gynecology → Genital swabs

vbdAvo0.title: Blood flashback
vbdAvo0.description: The initial flow of blood into the needle hub upon successful entry into a blood vessel.

Dbd1Do0.title: Milk fistula
Dbd1Do0.description: An abnormal connection between the breast tissue and a lactiferous duct. May occur as a rare complication following breast procedures (e.g. surgery or biopsy) in women who are lactating.

9bdNDo0.title: Postembolization syndrome
9bdNDo0.description: A common complication of transarterial embolization characterized by fever, pain, nausea, and vomiting within 72 hours after embolization in the absence of infection. Believed to be caused by inflammatory response to necrotic tissue. The condition is typically self-limited.

CbdqDo0.title: Compassion fatigue
CbdqDo0.description: Profound physical and/or mental exhaustion due to burnout and/or secondary traumatic stress from the long-term care of patients. Manifestations include lack of empathy, indifference to others, emotional withdrawal, and irritability. May lead to negative coping behaviors (e.g., excessive alcohol use) or psychiatric illness (e.g., anxiety, depression).

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

-bdDwo0.title: Chlamydial neonatal conjunctivitis
-bdDwo0.description: A form of infectious conjunctivitis seen in newborns and caused by perinatal transmission of C. trachomatis. Typically manifests 1-3 weeks after delivery with eyelid swelling and ocular discharge. Frequently accompanied by chlamydial infection of the nasopharynx, genitals, or lungs.

ZXdZ9o0.title: Gestational AVP disorder
ZXdZ9o0.description: A complication of pregnancy characterized by an impaired ability of the kidneys to effectively concentrate urine due to increased activity and/or circulating levels of vasopressinase and subsequent disruption of arginine vasopressin (AVP) hormone balance. Typically resolves with delivery.

destinations.label: Arginine vasopressin disorders → Special patient groups

aXdQ9o0.title: Coccydynia
aXdQ9o0.description: Pain at the coccyx. Typically occurs due to direct external trauma or injury during childbirth. Manifests with pain and tenderness of the coccyx, esp. when sitting or leaning back. Management includes protection (e.g., Donut or wedge cushions), analgesics, and local heat or ice. Resolves spontaneously in the majority of patients.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Complications of delivery

YXdn9o0.title: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease
YXdn9o0.description: A subtype of interstitial lung disease that may occur in patients with connective tissue diseases such as systemic sclerosis or rheumatoid arthritis.

bXdH9o0.title: Acute calcaneal fracture
bXdH9o0.description: A fracture of the calcaneus that results from either a high-energy impact to healthy bone (e.g., fall or motor vehicle accident) or a low-energy impact to osteoporotic or diseased bone.

cXdaCo0.title: Reiter syndrome
cXdaCo0.description: The term "Reiter syndrome" was historically used for the condition now known as reactive arthritis. This term is not used within AMBOSS. Hans Reiter was a German microbiologist and convicted Nazi war criminal who performed medical experiments on concentration camp prisoners.

WXdPCo0.title: High-sensitivity troponin
WXdPCo0.description: A high-sensitivity myocardial troponin assay that is able to detect significantly lower levels of troponin compared to traditional assays, allowing for early detection of myocardial infarction. Given its high sensitivity, it may be falsely positive in healthy individuals.

dXdoCo0.title: Reduction mammaplasty
dXdoCo0.description: The surgical removal of breast tissue to reduce breast volume and improve symptoms typically due to breast hypertrophy.

VXdGCo0.title: Clara cell
VXdGCo0.description: The term "Clara cell" was historically used for the cell type now known as a club cell. This term is not used within AMBOSS. Max Clara was a German anatomist and member of the Nazi Party who conducted research on the bodies of concentration camp prisoners.

eXdxCo0.title: Hallervorden–Spatz disease
eXdxCo0.description: The term "Hallervorden–Spatz disease" was historically used for the condition now known as neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation 1 (pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration). This term is not used within AMBOSS. Julius Hallervorden, a German neuroscientist, and Hugo Spatz, a German neuropathologist, were members of the Nazi Party who conducted experiments on the brains of individuals murdered by the Nazi regime.

UXdbxo0.title: Wegener granulomatosis
UXdbxo0.description: The term "Wegener granulomatosis" was historically used for the condition now known as granulomatosis with polyangiitis. This term is not used within AMBOSS. Friedrich Wegener was a German pathologist and member of a paramilitary wing of the Nazi Party who was complicit in experiments on individuals murdered by the Nazi regime.

2XdTxo0.title: Aseptic neonatal conjunctivitis
2XdTxo0.description: A now rare inflammation of the conjunctiva in newborns. Usually results from silver nitrate exposure, which was historically used after birth to prevent infectious conjunctivitis. Typically mild and self-limited.

fXdkxo0.title: IV extravasation
fXdkxo0.description: The leakage or unintentional administration of a vesicant solution into the tissue surrounding a vascular access device (e.g, peripheral IV catheter or IO needle).

destinations.label: Vascular access → Infiltration and extravasation injuries

TXd6xo0.title: IV infiltration
TXd6xo0.description: The leakage or unintentional administration of a nonvesicant solution or medication into the tissue surrounding a vascular access device (e.g., peripheral IV catheter or IO needle).

destinations.label: Vascular access → Infiltration and extravasation injuries

SXdyxo0.title: Planned repeat cesarean birth
SXdyxo0.description: A planned cesarean delivery in a patient who has had a prior cesarean delivery.

hXdcBo0.title: Vaginal birth after cesarean
hXdcBo0.description: A vaginal delivery in a patient who has had a prior cesarean delivery.

iXdJBo0.title: Plantar fascia rupture
iXdJBo0.description: A traumatic tear of the plantar fascia characterized by acute pain in the arch of the foot. Usually occurs during or following dynamic activities (e.g., intense exercise). Primarily affects individuals with pes planus.

jXd_Bo0.title: Allergic vulvovaginitis
jXd_Bo0.description: An inflammation of vulvar and/or vaginal tissue as a result of allergic contact dermatitis (e.g., to laundry or cleaning detergents, textile fibers, sanitary napkins).

PXdWyo0.title: Mechanical vulvovaginitis
PXdWyo0.description: An inflammation of vulvar and/or vaginal tissue as a result of mechanical forces (e.g., rubbing due to chronic pruritus, friction from tight clothes, retained foreign body). More common in individuals with estrogen deficiency and lichen sclerosus.

NXd-yo0.title: Skilled nursing facility
NXd-yo0.description: A facility (usually a designated unit within a nursing home) that provides short-term, post-acute care (skilled nursing and/or subacute rehabilitation services) to adults following hospital discharge.

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Care settings for older adults

MXdMAo0.title: Low segment transverse incision
MXdMAo0.description: A type of incision for cesarean delivery in which the lower anterior abdomen and noncontractile uterine fundus are transversely incised. Types include Pfannenstiel incision and Joel-Cohen incision.

LXdwAo0.title: Classical cesarean incision
LXdwAo0.description: A type of incision for cesarean delivery that involves vertical incision of the anterior abdomen and contractile uterine fundus.

6Xdj_o0.title: Barthel index
6Xdj_o0.description: A tool used to assess the following activities of daily living: bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring, continence, eating, grooming, mobility, and climbing stairs. The maximum score of 20 indicates full function; lower scores indicate increasing functional impairment.

pXdL_o0.title: Catagen phase
pXdL_o0.description: The phase of the hair growth cycle in which the hair detaches from the blood supply and active hair growth ends.

JXds_o0.title: Dermatoscope
JXds_o0.description: An instrument that utilizes light and magnification to examine the skin. A dermatoscope can be used for dermoscopy to evaluate skin lesions or for trichoscopy to evaluate hair and scalp.

qXdC_o0.title: Advanced activities of daily living
qXdC_o0.description: A group of nonessential daily activities that require a high level of cognitive functioning, such as working, traveling, volunteering, using electronic devices, or engaging in hobbies.

destinations.label: Introduction to geriatrics → Functional status assessment

IXdYzo0.title: Late-life function and disability instrument
IXdYzo0.description: A tool used to evaluate disability and function in older adults. The 16-item disability component evaluates the frequency and capability of participation in social and personal life tasks such as traveling, visiting others, and managing personal health and finances. The 32-item function component evaluates the ability to perform specific actions, such as washing dishes and climbing stairs.

rXdfzo0.title: Temporal triangular alopecia
rXdfzo0.description: A type of circumscribed, nonscarring hair loss that mainly affects the frontotemporal scalp. Onset is typically before adolescence.

7Xd4zo0.title: ECF
7Xd4zo0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Extracellular fluid
2. Enterocutaneous fistula

GXdBzo0.title: Unblinding
GXdBzo0.description: The intentional revelation to investigators and/or research subjects about how participants are allocated into groups (e.g., treatment group, control group) in blinded clinical trials. Specific circumstances, such as a subject's pregnancy or adverse events that affect safety, may require unblinding. Investigators may also decide to unblind a study after the completion of the trial.

tXdX-o0.title: Multimorbidity
tXdX-o0.description: The coexistence of two or more chronic diseases in an individual.

zXdr0K0.title: Trichorrhexis nodosa
zXdr0K0.description: A hair shaft deformity characterized by the development of weak points in the shaft due to physical or chemical trauma or genetic predisposition. Leads to increased hair breakage.

-XdD0K0.title: Pili torti
-XdD0K0.description: A congenital form of alopecia in which the hair shaft is flattened and has multiple twists, resulting in fragile hair that breaks easily.

ZcdZaK0.title: Monilethrix
ZcdZaK0.description: A rare, predominantly autosomal dominant disorder resulting in dry and brittle hair that breaks easily. Hairs have a characteristic beaded appearance on trichoscopy.

bcdHaK0.title: Binge eating prevention strategies
bcdHaK0.description: A set of strategies, often implemented in consultation with a registered dietitian, to help reduce cravings and the urge to binge eat. Includes maintaining a structured eating schedule, avoiding food restriction, increasing food variety, and ensuring adequate nutrition.

Xcd9aK0.title: BCL-2 inhibitor
Xcd9aK0.description: A class of drug that inhibits BCL-2, a group of proteins that regulate apoptosis in B cells. These proteins are sometimes overexpressed in malignant cells, leading to abnormal survival and proliferation. Venetoclax is the first approved drug in this class and is used in the treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and acute myeloid leukemia.

1cd2YK0.title: Chemical cautery
1cd2YK0.description: A procedure that uses chemicals (e.g., silver nitrate) to destroy tissue. Commonly used to ablate skin lesions and seal superficial blood vessels causing epistaxis.

WcdPYK0.title: Silver nitrate stick
WcdPYK0.description: An applicator stick coated in a cauterizing agent (silver nitrate) that destroys tissue. Commonly used to ablate skin lesions and seal superficial blood vessels causing epistaxis.

hcdcXK0.title: Attention (cognition)
hcdcXK0.description: The ability of an individual to focus and sustain their thoughts on a specific task/topic. Can be assessed by asking the patient to spell a word backward or count in twos.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

3cdSXK0.title: Memory (cognition)
3cdSXK0.description: The process of recalling information. Classified according to the length of time a particular piece of information can be recalled into sensory, short-term, and long-term memory.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Sensorium and cognition

RcdlXK0.title: Mood (psychiatry)
RcdlXK0.description: A subjective emotional state identified by an individual. Can be congruent or incongruent with affect.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Mood and affect

icdJXK0.title: Speech (psychiatry)
icdJXK0.description: Speech is the spontaneous production of the spoken language (i.e., the act of speaking) and is characterized by  rate, volume, quantity, articulation and fluency, and speech latency.

QcduXK0.title: Insight (psychiatry)
QcduXK0.description: Insight is an individual's awareness and understanding of their current medical problem, and it can be assessed based on the patient's recognition that they have a current medical condition, compliance with treatment, and ability to relabel unusual mental events as pathological.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Insight and judgment

jcd_XK0.title: Judgment (psychiatry)
jcd_XK0.description: The ability of an individual to make considerate decisions when performing a task based on their understanding of the current circumstances and their problem-solving abilities.

destinations.label: Mental status examination → Insight and judgment

4cd3cK0.title: Flick sign
4cd3cK0.description: A commonly reported symptom in patients with carpal tunnel syndrome. When symptoms are severe, e.g., at night, patients shake the hand to relieve symptoms.

Ncd-cK0.title: Nasal tampon
Ncd-cK0.description: An absorbent nasal packing used to treat epistaxis. It expands to fill the nasal cavity, applying pressure to the bleeding vessel.

mcdV1K0.title: Nasal balloon catheter
mcdV1K0.description: A catheter that is inserted into the nasal cavity during epistaxis. Once inserted, attached balloons are inflated to apply pressure to the bleeding vessel. A single-balloon catheter is used for anterior epistaxis; posterior epistaxis requires a two-balloon catheter.

JcdsWK0.title: Subinvolution of placental implantation site
JcdsWK0.description: A condition in which the uterus remains abnormally large following delivery because of the persistence of dilated uteroplacental vessels. It is the second most common cause of secondary postpartum hemorrhage and clinical features include abnormal, severe uterine bleeding (most commonly during the second week postpartum), fever, lower abdominal pain, and signs of hypovolemia.

destinations.label: Postpartum hemorrhage → Subinvolution of placental implantation site

IcdYdK0.title: Sport-related concussion
IcdYdK0.description: A direct physical impact to the head, neck, or body that occurs during a sports-related or exercise-related activity, and that transmits an impulsive force to the brain, resulting in a traumatic brain injury.

destinations.label: Mild traumatic brain injury → Sports-related concussion

ycddUK0.title: Agitated saline
ycddUK0.description: A mixture of air and saline used as a contrast agent during echocardiography to confirm catheter position during a procedure (e.g., pericardiocentesis) or to identify a patent foramen ovale. Commonly performed by rapidly mixing the contents of an air-filled (0.5–1 mL) and a saline-filled (8–9 mL) syringe back and forth several times using a three-way stopcock with the catheter port closed prior to injection.

zcdrUK0.title: Primary PCI
zcdrUK0.description: A treatment for myocardial infarction involving emergency percutaneous coronary intervention without the administration of fibrinolytic therapy.

destinations.label: Acute coronary syndrome → Management of STEMI

a1dQ2K0.title: Choreic hand
a1dQ2K0.description: A physical examination finding characterized by intermittent wrist flexion with extension of the digits. Can be present in patients with Sydenham chorea.

Y1dn2K0.title: Entrapment neuropathies
Y1dn2K0.description: A group of peripheral neuropathies caused by pressure on and/or irritation to a nerve as it passes through an anatomical narrowing. Includes carpal tunnel syndrome, radiculopathy, cubital tunnel syndrome, and tarsal tunnel syndrome.

b1dH2K0.title: Vaccine-associated chickenpox rash
b1dH2K0.description: A mild varicella infection caused by immunization with the live-attenuated varicella vaccine. Characterized by skin lesions that manifest 5-42 days (median 21 days) following immunization and are few in number (< 50 total) compared to regular chickenpox. Typically, the lesions are maculopapular and frequently occur at the immunization injection site.

c1dafK0.title: Vaso-occlusive event
c1dafK0.description: An acute presentation of sickle cell disease that is typically triggered by any event associated with reduced oxygen tension (e.g., hypoxia, infection, dehydration) in which sickled erythrocytes cause vascular occlusion and subsequent tissue infarction; virtually any organ can be affected with corresponding symptoms (e.g., severe bone pain, acute chest pain, stroke). Dactylitis (acute swelling and pain in hands and feet) is common.

11d2fK0.title: Screening to Brief Intervention
11d2fK0.description: A screening tool for substance use in adolescents developed by the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA). Categorizes the risk for substance use disorder into three distinct levels: no reported use, lower risk, and higher risk based on the self-reported frequency of use (never, once or twice, monthly, weekly or more).

W1dPfK0.title: Brief Screener for Tobacco, Alcohol, and other Drugs
W1dPfK0.description: A screening tool for substance use in adolescents developed by the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA). Categorizes the risk for substance use disorder into three distinct levels: no reported use, lower risk, and higher risk based on the self-reported frequency of use measured in days/year.

31dSgK0.title: Acute anemia in sickle cell disease
31dSgK0.description: A drop in hemoglobin levels ≥ 2.0 g/dL from baseline, or a hemoglobin value < 6 g/dL (if baseline is unknown). Possible etiologies include aplastic crisis, splenic sequestration, acute hepatic sequestration, acute chest syndrome, delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction, and sepsis. Acute blood loss (not necessarily linked to sickle cell disease) should also be considered.

R1dlgK0.title: Yaws
R1dlgK0.description: An infectious disease caused by Treponema pallidum pertenue that is transmitted by direct, typically nonsexual, contact. The condition manifests initially with a single papilloma that ulcerates and heals without scarring (stage 1). Without treatment, similar lesions will start to develop on the face, legs, arms, and/or the anogenital region within several weeks to months (stage 2). Finally, often following a dormant period of several years, the infection spreads to the cartilage and bone, causing destructive osteitis with potentially severe disfigurement of the face, fingers, toes, and legs that may resemble leprosy (stage 3). Treatment consists of azithromycin or benzathine penicillin.

41d3SK0.title: Silent cerebral infarct
41d3SK0.description: A cerebral infarct, identified on neuroimaging, that did not manifest with overt symptoms of stroke at the time of the incident. Subtle, nonspecific symptoms may have been present but are often overlooked. Affected individuals have an increased risk of future stroke and vascular dementia.

O1dISK0.title: Antiestrogen therapy
O1dISK0.description: A medication that suppresses the production of estrogen or its effects on cells. It is often used to treat estrogen-driven disease processes (e.g., breast cancer). Examples include selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) and aromatase inhibitors.

o1d03K0.title: Intraabdominal hypertension
o1d03K0.description: A sustained or recurrent elevation of intraabdominal pressure to ≥ 12 mm Hg

p1dL3K0.title: Indications to consult orthopedics for fractures
p1dL3K0.description: The characteristics of a fracture that may indicate the need for urgent orthopedic intervention. Includes skin tenting, open fractures, potentially operable long bone fractures, comminuted fractures, displaced intra-articular fractures, fracture-dislocations, unstable pelvic fractures, and signs of neurovascular compromise or compartment syndrome.

q1dC3K0.title: Opioid-induced respiratory depression
q1dC3K0.description: The presence of bradypnea or apnea, reduced tidal volume, and hypoxemia related to opioid use. The mechanism is multifactorial and includes reduced cortical arousal, reduced ventilatory reflexes to hypoxia and hypercapnia, sleep-disordered breathing, and rigidity of the respiratory skeletal muscles. Can progress to respiratory failure and arrest.

71d4RK0.title: Partial knee replacement
71d4RK0.description: Replacement of one (unicompartmental knee replacement) or two (bicompartmental knee replacement) compartments of the knee joint with a prosthesis. Commonly performed in patients with osteoarthritis of one or two compartments of the knee joint and persistent pain and functional impairment despite conservative management.

t1dXiK0.title: Primed IV tubing
t1dXiK0.description: An intravenous (IV) extension tube or full IV administration set that has been flushed with normal saline or a similar fluid to remove all air prior to its connection to a venous access device.

w1dhQK0.title: Acupuncture
w1dhQK0.description: A component of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in which very fine needles are placed superficially under the skin in specific locations. Used to treat a variety of ailments.

91dNQK0.title: Acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis
91dNQK0.description: An acute necrotizing bacterial infection of the gingiva characterized by gingival inflammation, white plaques, ulcerations, bleeding, and fetid breath.

x1dEQK0.title: Clinical features of cirrhosis
x1dEQK0.description: Features include jaundice, scleral icterus, spider angioma, gynecomastia, palmar erythema, ascites, asterixis, and encephalopathy.

B1dzQK0.title: Vulvar hematoma
B1dzQK0.description: An accumulation of blood in the vulvar soft tissue.

y1ddjK0.title: Vaginal hematoma
y1ddjK0.description: An accumulation of blood in the vaginal soft tissue.

ZWdZPK0.title: Exercise stress imaging
ZWdZPK0.description: A diagnostic study used to test coronary perfusion and inducible myocardial ischemia. Graded exercise is used to induce an oxygen demand-supply mismatch. Echocardiogram, myocardial perfusion scan (e.g., SPECT, PET), or cardiac MRI is then obtained to evaluate for ischemia

destinations.label: Coronary artery disease → Cardiac stress testing
Cardiac stress testing → Exercise stress testing

0WdePK0.title: Three-way stopcock
0WdePK0.description: A valve used to control the flow of liquid or gas between three ports. The three-way stopcock can only turn 180° and therefore only two of the three ports can be open at the same time. Commonly used during procedures such as thoracentesis, paracentesis, and pericardiocentesis.

aWdQPK0.title: Water seal
aWdQPK0.description: A drainage tube submerged in a water chamber, acting as a one-way valve. Allows for the drainage of air and fluid from the patient while preventing reverse flow. Commonly used after chest tube placement.

YWdnPK0.title: Pigtail catheter
YWdnPK0.description: A catheter with a looped distal end containing multiple holes. Allows for air and fluid drainage and is commonly used to treat pneumothorax, pericardial effusion, and urinary tract obstruction.

iWdJOK0.title: Chest drainage system
iWdJOK0.description: A system that connects to a chest tube to drain air or fluid from the pleural space or mediastinum, acting as a one-way valve. Traditionally comprised of three chambers: the first collects drained fluid, the second functions as a water seal, and the third allows for the option of controlled suction.

QWduOK0.title: Blunt dissection
QWduOK0.description: A surgical technique in which tissue planes are separated without cutting. Commonly performed using fingers, clamps, or blunt-edged scissors. When performed with clamps or scissors, the instrument's closed tip is advanced gently and then spread open to separate tissue planes.

KWdUmK0.title: Absorbable suture
KWdUmK0.description: A type of suture that dissolves as the wound heals. Commonly used for rapidly healing tissues, since the suture strength is lost within days to weeks. Examples of absorbable sutures include plain gut, chromic gut, Vicryl, and Monocryl.

JWdsmK0.title: Classic triad of meningitis
JWdsmK0.description: A group of findings that often manifest in patients with meningitis. Includes fever, meningismus, and altered mental state.

7Wd45K0.title: Rim sign
7Wd45K0.description: A radiologic sign characterized by widening of the glenohumeral joint > 6 mm. Can be seen on the anteroposterior view of a shoulder x-ray. Associated with posterior shoulder dislocation.

HWdK5K0.title: Trough line sign
HWdK5K0.description: A radiologic sign characterized by vertical density in the medial humeral head, which is caused by compression fracture. Can be seen on the anteroposterior view of a shoulder x-ray. Associated with posterior shoulder dislocation.

sWdt5K0.title: CRAFFT
sWdt5K0.description: A validated screening tool to evaluate for problematic substance use in adolescents. It consists of 6 questions that ask about riding in a Car with someone who was using substances, using substances to Relax or while Alone, Forgetting what happened while using substances, being told by Family or friends to cut down on substance use, and getting into Trouble while using substances. An answer of "yes" to 2 or more questions suggests a serious problem with substance use. CRAFFT+N also asks about nicotine use.

media.title: Car, Relax, Alone, Forget, Friends, Trouble (CRAFFT) Calculator

tWdXMK0.title: Risk factors for abdominal aortic aneurysm
tWdXMK0.description: Include smoking (most important risk factor), advanced age, atherosclerosis (ASCVD), hypercholesterolemia,  arterial hypertension, positive family history, male sex, and trauma.

FWdgMK0.title: Orphan drug
FWdgMK0.description: A designation by the US Food and Drug Administration for a drug or vaccine that could potentially be used to diagnose, prevent, or treat a rare disease (defined as affecting < 200,000 people in the US). Such a designation provides pharmaceutical companies financial incentives to further develop the drug or vaccine and establish its safety and efficacy in clinical trials.

uWdpMK0.title: Early-onset schizophrenia
uWdpMK0.description: A subtype of schizophrenia with onset between 13 and 18 years of age. More commonly manifests with premorbid deficits (e.g., social withdrawal, cognitive decline) compared to adult-onset schizophrenia. Hallucinations (mainly auditory) occur more commonly than delusions. The course and functional impairment are more severe than in adult-onset schizophrenia.

9WdNnK0.title: Immunochromatography
9WdNnK0.description: A point-of-care diagnostic study that can rapidly identify the presence of a particular substance or molecule (e.g., an antigen) by detecting its binding to an antibody. Testing is performed in a liquid sample that moves along a membrane. Examples include pregnancy tests, COVID-19 tests, and rapid HIV tests.

yWddLK0.title: Pseudogynecomastia
yWddLK0.description: The proliferation of fatty (not glandular) tissue in the subareolar region in male individuals. Most commonly seen in overweight or obese individuals. Resolves spontaneously with weight loss.

_Wd5LK0.title: Diagnostic paracentesis
_Wd5LK0.description: The aspiration of a small volume of fluid from the peritoneum to aid in the diagnosis and management of ascites and other intraabdominal conditions.

zWdrLK0.title: Chaplain
zWdrLK0.description: A certified member of the clergy who tends to spiritual needs in a nonreligious institution (e.g., hospitals, nursing facilities, schools).

-WdDLK0.title: Joint attention
-WdDLK0.description: The purposefully shared focus of two individuals on an object. The focus can be coordinated by one individual alerting another to a specific object (e.g., pointing to it, eye gazing).

addQoK0.title: Valvuloplasty
addQoK0.description: A procedure performed in patients with valvular stenosis to separate fused or calcified valve leaflets. The approach may be surgical (e.g., open commissurotomy) or via transcatheter (e.g., percutaneous balloon valvuloplasty).

YddnoK0.title: Pathological gynecomastia
YddnoK0.description: Gynecomastia that occurs due to a pathological disruption in the estrogen/testosterone ratio. Can occur at any age. Causes include medications, chronic conditions (e.g., liver cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease), and estrogen-secreting tumors of the testes.

bddHoK0.title: Physiological gynecomastia
bddHoK0.description: Gynecomastia caused by a physiological change in the estrogen/testosterone ratio. Can occur in neonates (due to transplacental transfer of maternal estrogens), during puberty (due to relative estradiol excess until testosterone secretion reaches adult levels), and in individuals > 50 years of age (due to waning testosterone levels).

Xdd9oK0.title: Curtain sign
Xdd9oK0.description: A physical examination finding in which manual elevation of the more ptotic eyelid (in patients with asymmetric ptosis) causes increased ptosis of the contralateral eyelid.

cddaKK0.title: Posterior long arm splint
cddaKK0.description: An upper extremity splint used to immobilize the elbow and forearm. Extends along the posterior aspect of the arm from the midarm to the midpalmar region, with the arm held in 90° flexion at the elbow and the wrist in a neutral position. Indicated for proximal forearm fractures, distal humerus fractures, and certain elbow ligament injuries.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

eddxKK0.title: Comorbid mental health conditions
eddxKK0.description: The presence of mental health disorders (e.g., depression, anxiety) in patients with somatic disease (e.g., diabetes, COPD) or the coexistence of two or more mental health disorders. Coexisting conditions have additive negative effects on each other that lead to increased disease burden. Synergistic treatment can improve symptoms of both diseases.

Uddb6K0.title: Scoliometer
Uddb6K0.description: An instrument used during scoliosis screening to measure the angle of trunk rotation (ATR). While the patient is in forward flexion during the Adam forward bend test, the device is placed across the patient's spine with the notch overlying the spinous process at the level of the spinal curvature apex. A bubble indicates the degree of lateral tilt (i.e., ATR). An ATR ≥ 5° or ≥ 7° suggests scoliosis and is an indication for confirmatory spinal x-rays.

iddJpK0.title: Clinical gestalt
iddJpK0.description: An unstructured overall clinical impression based on pattern recognition of combinations of clinical variables. Often used by experienced clinicians to guide heuristic decision-making (e.g., determining pretest probability, making clinical diagnoses). Is susceptible to cognitive bias. Can be supplemented by clinical decision tools.

QddupK0.title: Neurovascular examination
QddupK0.description: A set of physical examination maneuvers performed to evaluate for injury to neurological and/or vascular structures. Includes testing for sensation, motor function, intact pulses, and capillary refill. Often used to monitor function before and after treatment for limb injury. Abnormal findings should prompt urgent specialist consult.

jdd_pK0.title: PTSD with dissociative symptoms
jdd_pK0.description: A subtype of PTSD in which individuals meet the diagnostic criteria for PTSD and concomitantly experience symptoms of either derealization or depersonalization.

destinations.label: Acute and posttraumatic stress disorders → Subtypes and variants

PddWJK0.title: PTSD with delayed expression
PddWJK0.description: A subtype of PTSD in which individuals first meet the full diagnostic criteria for PTSD ≥ 6 months after the associated traumatic event(s).

destinations.label: Acute and posttraumatic stress disorders → Subtypes and variants

4dd3JK0.title: Derealization
4dd3JK0.description: A sense of unreality with detachment from one's environment.

kddmJK0.title: Depersonalization
kddmJK0.description: A sense of unreality with detachment from oneself (e.g., body perception, feelings, thoughts, and/or actions).

OddIJK0.title: Breakthrough varicella infection
OddIJK0.description: A wild-type VZV infection that occurs in individuals who have received ≥ 1 dose of the chickenpox vaccine ≥ 42 days prior to symptom onset.

lddvJK0.title: Acquired hydrocephalus
lddvJK0.description: An abnormal enlargement of the cerebral ventricles resulting from excess cerebrospinal fluid accumulation. Can occur at any age after birth due to brain injury or disease.

Ndd-JK0.title: Recreational drug
Ndd-JK0.description: A psychoactive substance with a stimulant, depressant, or hallucinogenic effect on the central nervous system used for nonmedical, recreational purposes.

mddVqK0.title: Physiologic anemia of infancy
mddVqK0.description: Physiologic decrease in red blood cell production caused by a reduction in erythropoietin production and shorter lifespan of erythrocytes. Anemia typically appears at 8-12 weeks of age in term infants and at 4-8 weeks of age in preterm infants and gradually resolves by 2 years of age.

destinations.label: Overview of neonatal conditions → Physiologic anemia of infancy

5ddiqK0.title: SSHADESS
5ddiqK0.description: An acronym for the elements of a psychosocial history for adolescents. It stands for: strengths, school, home, activities, drugs and substance use, emotions and eating, sexuality, and safety. It is similar to the HEADSS assessment, but emphasizes a strengths-based approach, e.g., asking what they enjoy doing and what they are most proud of.

odd0IK0.title: Serious adverse event (clinical trial)
odd0IK0.description: An adverse event during a clinical trial that is life-threatening, causes or prolongs hospitalization, or results in significant morbidity, congenital anomalies, or death.

KddUIK0.title: Unexpected adverse event (clinical trial)
KddUIK0.description: An adverse event during a clinical trial whose nature, severity, or frequency is unknown at the start of the trial (e.g., not described in protocol-related documentation of the intervention or product labeling by the manufacturer) or unexpected given the participant's underlying diseases or risk factors. Can also occur after market approval during phase 4 trials.

6ddjIK0.title: Imaginary companion
6ddjIK0.description: A fictitious human, animal, or object that a child or adolescent creates in their mind and which they engage with as if they were real and had a personality. Considered a part of normal child development and pretend play.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Common developmental behaviors

pddLIK0.title: Duroziez sign
pddLIK0.description: A physical examination finding in which a to-and-fro bruit is heard over the femoral artery when slight pressure is applied with a stethoscope. Associated with aortic regurgitation.

JddsIK0.title: Picky eating
JddsIK0.description: A behavior pattern that includes the refusal to eat certain foods, unwillingness to try new foods, eating a limited amount of food, and/or having strong preferences for certain foods. Typically does not require further evaluation if no red flag signs or symptoms are present (e.g., failure to thrive).

qddCIK0.title: Data monitoring committee
qddCIK0.description: An independent panel of experts who periodically review the conduct and data of ongoing trials to ensure participant safety and scientific merit. Required for nearly all phase 3 trials and for phase 1 and 2 trials that are multicenter, blinded, or involve a high-risk intervention.

IddYrK0.title: Stopping rules
IddYrK0.description: A set of statistical criteria established before the start of a clinical trial to determine when the intervention should be stopped because of safety concerns, futility, or early evidence of clear benefit.

rddfrK0.title: Risk factors for opioid overdose
rddfrK0.description: Includes the prescription of high-dose or high-potency opioids or opioids with a long half-life, concurrent use of sedatives or hypnotics, comorbid mental health conditions, current or history of substance use disorder (including opioid use disorder), recent cessation of medication for opioid use disorder, obtaining prescriptions from multiple providers, recent release from incarceration, comorbidities (such as COPD, sleep-related breathing disorders, renal insufficiency, hepatic insufficiency), and age ≥ 65 years.

7dd4rK0.title: Precipitated opioid withdrawal
7dd4rK0.description: The acute onset of opioid withdrawal syndrome triggered by opioid antagonists (e.g., naloxone) or partial agonists (e.g., buprenorphine).

uddp7K0.title: UAE
uddp7K0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Unexpected adverse event
2. Uterine artery embolization

Edd87K0.title: Null value
Edd87K0.description: A number that corresponds to the null hypothesis (i.e., that no association between the exposure and the outcome exists). The null value is 1 for ratios (e.g., relative risk, odds ratio) and 0 for differences (e.g., attributable risk, absolute risk reduction).

destinations.label: Statistical analysis of data → Hypothesis testing and probability

AddRsK0.title: Reflex cervical cytology
AddRsK0.description: A screening strategy for cervical cancer in which cervical cytology (Pap smear) is performed on all individuals with an abnormal primary HPV screening result (regardless of the HPV genotype detected). Reflex cytology testing should ideally be performed on the same laboratory specimen as the primary HPV test.

zddrsK0.title: Signs of impending respiratory failure
zddrsK0.description: Signs include increased work of breathing (e.g., tachypnea, grunting, nasal flaring, retractions), respiratory fatigue, pallor/flushing, altered mental status, cyanosis, bradycardia, and hypoxemia.

-ddDsK0.title: Vasomotor symptoms
-ddDsK0.description: A brief, episodic sensation of heat that most commonly occurs during perimenopause and menopause but can also occur in male hypogonadism. Vasomotor symptoms often affect the face and upper chest and are frequently associated with sweating, anxiety, palpitations, and, if they occur at night, sleep disturbance. In perimenopause and menopause, it is likely caused by thermoregulatory dysfunction and peripheral vasodilation due to hypoestrogenic effects on the hypothalamus.

aVdQGK0.title: Hering's law of equal innervation
aVdQGK0.description: The principle that the muscles of both eyes receive equal motor innervation. In patients with unilateral or asymmetric ptosis (e.g., due to myasthenia gravis), innervation to both eyelids increases, causing the less affected eyelid to retract and appear nonptotic. Manual elevation of the eyelid with more severe ptosis eliminates the compensatory mechanism, thereby revealing ptosis of the less affected eyelid.

YVdnGK0.title: Perinatal generalized anxiety disorder
YVdnGK0.description: A subtype of generalized anxiety disorder that can develop from pregnancy through 1 year postpartum. Manifests with disproportionate, overwhelming fears about fetal and parental well-being that cause functional impairment (e.g., inability to work).

bVdHGK0.title: Red flag features for neonatal HSV
bVdHGK0.description: A set of maternal and neonatal features associated with an increased risk of HSV infection in infants < 60 days of age. Maternal features include maternal genital herpetic lesions and/or fever 48 hours before and after delivery. Neonatal features include cutaneous vesicles, mucous membrane ulcers, seizure, hypothermia, and abnormal laboratory findings (i.e., CSF pleocytosis without organisms on gram stain, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, DIC, and/or elevated alanine aminotransferase).

XVd9GK0.title: HSV testing in infants < 60 days
XVd9GK0.description: A set of diagnostic tests used to detect herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection in infants < 60 days of age. Consists of serum alanine aminotransferase along with viral culture and HSV PCR of samples from serum, CSF, and surface swabs of the mouth, nasopharynx, conjunctivae, anus, and vesicles.

destinations.label: Congenital TORCH infections → Congenital herpes simplex virus infection

cVdatK0.title: Postpolypectomy bleeding
cVdatK0.description: A type of lower gastrointestinal bleeding that occurs up to 30 days after a polypectomy procedure and requires urgent medical evaluation. Additional interventions may be required to achieve hemostasis, e.g. repeat endoscopy, angiography, or surgery.

eVdxtK0.title: Vaginal wet mount preparation
eVdxtK0.description: A diagnostic test for vaginal infections (e.g., bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis, vulvovaginal candidiasis). A sample of vaginal discharge is transferred to a slide and mixed with normal saline or potassium hydroxide and then examined under a microscope.

destinations.label: Diagnostic procedures in gynecology → Genital swabs

UVdbFK0.title: Westley croup score
UVdbFK0.description: A scoring system used to determine the severity of croup. Assesses five domains: level of consciousness, air entry, presence of cyanosis, stridor, and retractions. Patients are scored from mild disease (≤ 2) to impending respiratory failure (≥ 12).

2VdTFK0.title: Virus-induced wheeze
2VdTFK0.description: A condition seen in young children (< 6 years) in which a viral infection precipitates wheezing episodes. The pathophysiology is unclear, but the effect of edema on airway resistance is thought to be more pronounced when the child's airways are smaller. The majority of episodes resolve with age. Affected children have an increased risk of developing asthma.

TVd6FK0.title: Subglottic stenosis
TVd6FK0.description: A narrowing of the airway at the subglottic level. Can manifest with stridor, respiratory distress, cyanotic episodes, and recurrent infections. Can be either congenital or acquired (most commonly due to scarring in the larynx).

gVdFFK0.title: Subglottic hemangioma
gVdFFK0.description: A congenital condition in which a vascular mass develops in the subglottic space (typically below the vocal cords). May have rapid and significant growth and can obstruct the airway.

RVdl8K0.title: Prescription drug monitoring program
RVdl8K0.description: An electronic database that records prescriptions for controlled substances (e.g., opioids, benzodiazepines, amphetamines). Some states require clinicians to review the PDMP report prior to every controlled substance prescription in order to identify aberrant behavior (e.g., use of multiple pharmacies and/or prescribers) and high-risk prescription combinations and to monitor public health interventions.

iVdJ8K0.title: Hickam's dictum
iVdJ8K0.description: A principle that states that a patient can have multiple conditions simultaneously. A corollary to Occam's razor. Consideration of this principle can help to prevent premature closure bias.

QVdu8K0.title: Occam razor
QVdu8K0.description: A principle that states that a single explanation for a phenomenon (e.g., one underlying illness causing several manifestations) is more likely to be true than multiple explanations (e.g., multiple simultaneous illnesses resulting in presenting symptoms). Often used as a heuristic but can lead to premature closure bias.

PVdWuK0.title: Chronic cough
PVdWuK0.description: In adults: the presence of cough > 8 weeks. In children < 14 years of age: daily cough present for > 4 weeks.

4Vd3uK0.title: Acute cough
4Vd3uK0.description: In adults: presence of cough < 3 weeks. In children: presence of cough < 2 weeks.

kVdmuK0.title: Subacute cough
kVdmuK0.description: In adults: presence of cough for 3–8 weeks. In children: presence of cough for 2–4 weeks.

lVdvuK0.title: Hyperphosphatemic familial tumoral calcinosis
lVdvuK0.description: A recessive genetic condition associated with deficiency of or resistance to intact FGF23 and characterized by hyperphosphatemia, with increased 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D levels, decreased PTH, increased gastrointestinal calcium absorption, and localized bony proliferations. Most commonly caused by mutations in FGF23 or related genes (e.g., GALNT3, KL).

mVdVEK0.title: Mainstem intubation
mVdVEK0.description: The placement of the distal end of an endotracheal tube into either the right or left main bronchus. This may occur inadvertently during intubation or be a therapeutic component in the management of unilateral lung pathology.  Bronchial intubation may result in hypoxia, asymmetric breath sounds, and high peak pressures.

5VdiEK0.title: Controlled substance agreement
5VdiEK0.description: A written agreement between the patient and their medical provider used to mitigate the risks associated with the prescription of controlled substances that are accepted for medical use (e.g., opiates, stimulants). Provides information on the risks of treatment and sets clear expectations for the patient and their medical provider, such as limits on prescriptions, consent for random drug testing, and reasons for dismissal from treatment.

nVd7EK0.title: Cold knife conization
nVd7EK0.description: A method to perform cervical conization in which a scalpel is used to remove a cone-shaped portion of cervical tissue. Typically requires general or regional anesthesia. Used for diagnosis and/or treatment of cervical cancer.

destinations.label: Invasive cervical cancer → Surgical interventions for cervical cancer

LVdwEK0.title: Lipid emulsion therapy
LVdwEK0.description: The IV administration of lipids to treat local anesthetic systemic toxicity. Acts as a lipid sink that allows the offending drug to be removed from tissue and redistributed into the lipid phase of the plasma. Also used in the treatment of refractory toxicity from other fat-soluble medications, e.g., tricyclic antidepressants, antiarrhythmic agents, organic phosphorus compounds, calcium channel blockers, and beta blockers.

oVd0vK0.title: Clinical features of urinary tract infection
oVd0vK0.description: Features include dysuria, increased urinary frequency, urinary urgency, hematuria, and suprapubic tenderness. In upper UTI, symptoms also include fever, flank pain, costovertebral angle tenderness, nausea, vomiting, and malaise.

6VdjvK0.title: Family cluster
6VdjvK0.description: The occurrence of a disease in at least two family members at the same time.

qVdCvK0.title: Electrical capture
qVdCvK0.description: The successful conduction of current from a pacemaker to the heart, which results in a QRS complex. Confirmed by ECG findings of a pacer spike immediately followed by a wide QRS complex.

destinations.label: Management of bradycardia → Temporary cardiac pacing
Cardiac implantable electronic devices → Permanent pacemakers

IVdYDK0.title: Mechanical capture
IVdYDK0.description: The cardiac contraction that occurs secondary to conduction of current from a pacemaker. Confirmed by palpating pulses, pulse oximetry, or direct visualization of ventricular contraction on POCUS.

destinations.label: Management of bradycardia → Temporary cardiac pacing
Cardiac implantable electronic devices → Permanent pacemakers

GVdBDK0.title: Return precautions
GVdBDK0.description: A set of verbal and/or written instructions given to the caregiver or patient outlining signs and/or symptoms that indicate the patient needs urgent medical attention.

FVdgwK0.title: Large esophageal varices
FVdgwK0.description: Esophageal varices that are ≥ 5 mm. Large esophageal varices are a risk factor for esophageal hemorrhage.

uVdpwK0.title: Stimulated urinary void
uVdpwK0.description: A method used to obtain clean-catch urine samples for non-toilet-trained children. The genital area is cleaned and then a cold saline-soaked gauze is rubbed in a circular motion over the suprapubic area to stimulate voiding. The urine is collected midstream in a sterile cup.

media.title: Voiding stimulation technique for clean-catch urine in infants

EVd8wK0.title: Rectal tube
EVd8wK0.description: A tube that is inserted 10-15 cm into the rectum and held in place with an inflated balloon. Fecal matter is redirected into an external collection bag. Indications include medication administration, colonic decompression, and prevention of patient soiling with refractory diarrhea.

aedQxK0.title: Red flags for human trafficking
aedQxK0.description: A set of features potentially indicating that a patient is a victim of human trafficking. Signs include being accompanied by an individual who speaks for them and declines to leave (may be an older woman), delayed presentation of medical problems, injuries or illnesses that do not fit with the stated history, signs of sexual or physical abuse, history that appears to be scripted, stated age being older than the patient appears, frequent relocation, lack of documentation, and tattoos possibly denoting ownership (e.g., names) that the patient may be reluctant to talk about.

bedHxK0.title: Red wale mark
bedHxK0.description: Longitudinal red streaks on the surface of a varix that look like red corduroy wales. The presence of red wale marks indicates recent or impending bleeding and is a high-risk feature in esophageal varices.

cedaBK0.title: Pacemaker spike
cedaBK0.description: A narrow upward deflection seen on ECG, caused by an electrical impulse from a pacemaker.

destinations.label: Cardiac implantable electronic devices → Permanent pacemakers
Management of bradycardia → Temporary cardiac pacing

1ed2BK0.title: Lower UTI
1ed2BK0.description: An infection of the bladder (cystitis) with or without associated urethral infection (urethritis). Manifestations include irritative lower urinary tract symptoms (e.g., increased urinary frequency, urinary urgency, dysuria), gross hematuria, and suprapubic tenderness.

WedPBK0.title: Upper UTI
WedPBK0.description: An infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) and/or ureter. Manifestations include fever, costovertebral tenderness, flank pain, nausea, and vomiting.

dedoBK0.title: Chronic opioid therapy
dedoBK0.description: The use of daily or almost-daily opioid therapy for ≥ 90 days. Often used for the treatment of chronic pain and pain at the end of life (e.g., in hospice care).

VedGBK0.title: Urine chromatography
VedGBK0.description: A type of urinary test that uses chromatographic techniques (i.e., separating a sample into its components), typically in combination with mass spectrometry, to identify the presence of certain drugs and/or metabolites.

gedFyK0.title: Atypical pediatric UTI
gedFyK0.description: A collection of clinical features seen in children with a UTI suggestive of underlying pathology or complicated infection. These include UTI in neonates, severe symptoms (e.g., sepsis, raised creatinine), poor urine flow, caustive pathogen other than E. coli, persistent symptoms despite 48–72 hours of antibiotics, complications (e.g., renal abscess), urinary tract abnormalities, and abdominal or bladder mass.

destinations.label: Urinary tract infections in children and adolescents → Subtypes and variants

hedcAK0.title: Malaria parasitemia
hedcAK0.description: The concentration of malaria parasites detected on thin blood smear microscopy of an individual with malaria. Can be expressed as the percentage of RBCs that contain Plasmodium species or as the number of parasites per microliter of blood. Used to classify infection severity and monitor response to treatment.

RedlAK0.title: Attentional capture
RedlAK0.description: A phenomenon in which one's attention is drawn unintentionally to another target as a result of a change in stimulus (e.g., a physician examining a patient immediately shifts their attention once a pager beeps).

ned7zK0.title: ROM
ned7zK0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Range of motion
2. Rupture of membranes

KedU-K0.title: Fetal malposition
KedU-K0.description: A position in which the fetus is in the cephalic presentation but not oriented anteriorly in the pelvis (i.e., occiput posterior position or occiput transverse position).

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormalities in fetal orientation

6edj-K0.title: Puerperal mastitis
6edj-K0.description: Mastitis associated with lactation. Occurs in up to 10% of lactating individuals. Staphylococcus aureus is the most common causative pathogen of infectious puerperal mastitis.

GedBZ60.title: Bowel resection
GedBZ60.description: A surgical procedure to remove part of the small intestine, large intestine, or both. Used to treat malignancy (e.g., bowel cancer) and several diseases (e.g., volvulus, Crohn disease).

uedp060.title: Postpartum retroperitoneal hematoma
uedp060.description: Bleeding into the retroperitoneal space in the peripartum period. Often caused by vascular injury (e.g., uterine artery rupture or laceration). May manifest with symptoms of hemodynamic instability. Management includes close observation, stabilization, and angiographic or surgical hemorrhage control if indicated.

destinations.label: Normal labor and delivery → Complications of delivery

Eed8060.title: Figure-of-eight suture
Eed8060.description: A suture technique used to stop bleeding from small vessels or to provide additional strength in high-tension areas. Associated with increased scarring and thus avoided on the face and other areas of cosmetic concern.

Ded1a60.title: Barriers to follow-up
Ded1a60.description: A series of factors that may impact an individual's ability to attend scheduled appointments or seek timely emergency care. Includes both practical barriers (e.g., lack of insurance, limited or no access to a telephone or vehicle, language barriers, cognitive impairment, living in remote areas, difficulty getting time off work) and sociocultural barriers (e.g., previous negative experiences, concerns over discrimination, low health literacy).

wedha60.title: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea
wedha60.description: A type of diarrhea that occurs during or shortly after antibiotic use, most likely due to altered intestinal flora. C. difficile infection is a severe form of antibiotic-associated diarrhea.

_ed5Y60.title: Finger-tip unit
_ed5Y60.description: The quantity of topical medication (e.g., cream, gel, ointment) that stretches from the distal skin crease to the tip of the index finger when dispensed from a nozzle with a 5 mm diameter. In adults, an FTU corresponds to ~ 0.5 g of agent and covers an area of skin equivalent to two handprints.

1Ud2X60.title: Principal investigator
1Ud2X60.description: The person responsible for the preparation, conduct, and administration of a research grant, contract, and legal compliance of a sponsored research project.

WUdPX60.title: Maximum recommended local anesthetic dose
WUdPX60.description: The maximum recommended local anesthetic dose is based on the specific agent; the patient's weight, age, and comorbidities; and whether epinephrine is added to the solution. This dose should be reduced in patients at increased risk for local anesthetic systemic toxicity.

eUdxX60.title: Keratinocyte carcinoma
eUdxX60.description: A term typically used to refer to cutaneous carcinomas of keratinocyte origin (i.e., basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma).

UUdbc60.title: Common Rule
UUdbc60.description: A policy that applies to all biomedical and behavioral research involving human subjects that is conducted or supported by a federal department or agency.

3UdS160.title: Cranial vault
3UdS160.description: The roof of the cranial cavity, which, together with the skull base, encases the brain. Consists of the paired frontal bones, the paired parietal bones, the squamous portions of the temporal bones, and the interparietal part of the occipital bone.

RUdl160.title: Hypomania checklist
RUdl160.description: A self-report instrument that is used to identify hypomanic symptoms, most commonly in patients with depressive symptoms, to screen for bipolar disorder. Consists of 32 items that are scored either “yes” or “no." A score > 13 is considered a positive result. Reported overall sensitivity is 80% with a specificity of 65% in populations with mood disorders.

iUdJ160.title: Orbital compartment syndrome
iUdJ160.description: A vision-threatening emergency caused by an acute and sustained increase in intraorbital pressure that leads to impaired perfusion and ischemia of the optic nerve and retina. Manifests with reduced visual acuity, eye pain, periorbital swelling, and/or proptosis. Most commonly caused by a traumatic retrobulbar hematoma.

QUdu160.title: Lateral canthotomy and cantholysis
QUdu160.description: An emergency surgical procedure to treat orbital compartment syndrome. Involves a horizontal incision from the lateral canthus to the rim of the orbit followed by exposure of the lateral canthal tendon and cantholysis.

destinations.label: Orbital disorders → Lateral canthotomy and cantholysis

jUd_160.title: Inferior cantholysis
jUd_160.description: An incision of the lateral canthal tendon (typically following lateral canthotomy). Used for orbital decompression in patients with orbital compartment syndrome.

PUdWW60.title: CSF detection studies
PUdWW60.description: A group of studies used to detect cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in nasal and/or ear discharge. Studies include applying a drop of the discharge to gauze or tissue paper to assess for the halo sign (a rapidly expanding ring of clear fluid surrounding blood) and sample analysis to assess for the presence of β2-transferrin (gold standard).

kUdmW60.title: X-ray findings in pneumonia
kUdmW60.description: Include findings of lobar pneumonia (e.g., consolidation in one or more pulmonary lobes with overlying air bronchograms), bronchopneumonia (e.g., scattered areas of poorly defined patchy infiltrates with overlying air bronchograms), atypical/interstitial pneumonia (e.g., diffuse reticular opacities with minimal or no consolidation), and/or parapneumonic effusion.

NUd-W60.title: Posttraumatic stress disorder
NUd-W60.description: A psychiatric disorder triggered by a personally experienced or witnessed traumatic event. Symptoms persist for more than 1 month and include intrusive thoughts, avoidance of reminders of traumatic events, negative cognition or mood (e.g., depression), and altered reactivity and arousal (e.g., irritability, sleep disturbances).

destinations.label: Acute and posttraumatic stress disorders → Summary

mUdVd60.title: Sensitization (immunology)
mUdVd60.description: The initial asymptomatic immune response to an antigen, in which antigen presenting cells capture and present allergens to immune cells, thereby generating allergen-specific immunoglobulins.

nUd7d60.title: Hepatic enzyme-inducing AEDs
nUd7d60.description: Antiseizure drugs that induce liver enzymes (e.g., cytochrome P450), including carbamazepine, felbamate oxcarbazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone, and rufinamide. Effects include quicker metabolism of reproductive steroids, which can decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives if taken simultaneously.

LUdwd60.title: Major congenital malformations
LUdwd60.description: A structural or functional defect in a developing fetus that affects life expectancy or has a significant medical, social, or cosmetic impact. Examples include neural tube defects, congenital heart defects, orofacial clefts, and hypospadias.

oUd0V60.title: Urinary bladder pressure measurement
oUd0V60.description: An indirect method of assessing abdominal cavity pressure by measuring the pressure within the urinary bladder. Used for the diagnosis of intaabdominal hypertension and abdominal compartment syndrome.

KUdUV60.title: Reverse Trendelenberg position
KUdUV60.description: A position in which the patient lies supine, with the bed or operating table tilted up so that the head is above the level of the heart. Commonly used to improve surgical exposure during upper abdominal surgery and reduce bleeding during head and neck procedures. May also be used to improve respiratory parameters in mechanically ventilated patients.

pUdLV60.title: Transient hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
pUdLV60.description: An often asymptomatic and reversible cardiological condition in infants of mothers with diabetes characterized by thickening of ventricular walls and the intraventricular septum and reduced ventricular size. Caused by excessive exposure to maternal glucose and insulin. Results in left ventricular outflow obstruction and systolic or diastolic dysfunction

destinations.label: Diabetes mellitus in pregnancy → Fetal and neonatal complications of diabetes mellitus in pregnancy

JUdsV60.title: Outpatient civil commitment
JUdsV60.description: A legal intervention that restricts the autonomy of an individual with a mental health disorder and compels the individual to receive treatment in an outpatient setting.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Involuntary commitment

qUdCV60.title: Inpatient civil commitment
qUdCV60.description: An intervention that restricts the autonomy of an individual with a mental health disorder and compels the individual to receive treatment in an inpatient setting. Criteria for involuntary admission vary by state but commonly include danger to self, danger to others, and grave disability due to underlying psychiatric illness. In most cases, involuntary admission cannot last for more than 72 hours without a court order.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Involuntary commitment

HUdKe60.title: Local anesthesia
HUdKe60.description: A procedure involving the application or injection of local anesthetic agents into tissue to achieve reversible numbing of pain conduction by blocking nerve endings at and around the site of administration. Used primarily to decrease the pain associated with minor procedures. Can consist of topical anesthesia or infiltration anesthesia.

sUdte60.title: Regional anesthesia
sUdte60.description: The reversible numbing of pain conduction through the injection of local anesthetic agents around nerves in the peripheral or central nervous system, which blocks pain in the corresponding innervated tissue. Regional anesthesia can be divided into peripheral nerve blocks, neuraxial anesthesia (i.e., spinal anesthesia, epidural anesthesia), and intravenous regional anesthesia.

GUdBe60.title: Esophagram
GUdBe60.description: A diagnostic test in which serial x-rays of the chest are taken while a patient swallows contrast (e.g., barium or gastrografin). Used in the diagnosis of conditions affecting the pharynx or esophagus (e.g., dysphagia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, achalasia, perforation).

FUdgU60.title: Localizing signs
FUdgU60.description: A set of physical exam findings that assist in identifying the location of an abnormal condition or lesion. Examples include deviation on tongue protrusion (suggests an ipsilateral hypoglossal nerve palsy) or tenderness and a pause in inspiration on palpation of the right upper quadrant (Murphy sign) in patients with cholecystitis.

EUd8U60.title: Risk factors for systemic fungal infection
EUd8U60.description: Conditions or treatments that impair immunity and increase susceptibility to fungal infection, e.g., HIV, diabetes mellitus, immunosuppressant medication, and indwelling catheters.

destinations.label: Overview of fungal infections → Management of systemic fungal infections

02deT60.title: Social admission
02deT60.description: A hospital admission where the patient does not typically require specialized inpatient management (e.g., IV medications) but instead is either being provided with outpatient care while residing in a hospital or is temporarily being provided with a safe environment until an appropriate discharge plan can be made. Indications include concern for patient safety, poor adherence to outpatient treatment, and imminent facility transfer (e.g., to a nursing home).

a2dQT60.title: Risk factors for invasive meningococcal disease
a2dQT60.description: Complement deficiencies, use of complement inhibitors, HIV infection, functional or anatomical asplenia, community outbreaks, planned travel to countries with high rates of meningococcal disease, living in residential housing (e.g., college dormitory, military barracks), and working in high-risk settings (e.g., laboratories that work with Neisseria meningitidis)

Y2dnT60.title: Postobstructive pulmonary edema
Y2dnT60.description: The sudden onset of severe, noncardiogenic pulmonary edema following relief of a severe airway obstruction. Caused by the transudation of fluid from the pulmonary capillaries into the alveoli due to forceful negative inspiratory pressure against a closed airway. Causes of airway obstruction include upper airway infections, upper airway edema, and laryngospasm following extubation of the trachea.

12d2g60.title: Nutrition Risk in the Critically Ill score
12d2g60.description: A score used to determine the need for specialized nutrition support. Points are based on age, number of comorbidities, number of days in hospital prior to ICU admission, interleukin-6 level, APACHE II score, and the SOFA score on admission. A patient with a NUTRIC score ≥ 6 is considered to be at high nutritional risk.

W2dPg60.title: Nutrition Risk Screening 2002 score
W2dPg60.description: A score used to determine the need for specialized nutrition support. Points are based on nutritional status (BMI, weight loss in the last three months, decreased oral intake in the last week), and severity of current illness. A patient with an NRS-2002 score ≥ 5 is considered to be at high nutritional risk.

f2dkS60.title: Risk factors for severe Haemophilus influenzae type b disease
f2dkS60.description: Conditions include functional or anatomical asplenia (including sickle cell disease), HIV infection, immunoglobulin deficiency, early component complement deficiencies, early component complement inhibitor use, and malignant neoplasms requiring immunosuppressive therapy (i.e., hematopoietic stem cell transplant, chemotherapy, or radiation therapy).

T2d6S60.title: Risk factors for invasive pneumococcal disease
T2d6S60.description: Factors include chronic heart disease, chronic lung disease, chronic renal disease (CKD or nephrotic syndrome), chronic liver disease, diabetes mellitus, CSF leak, cochlear implant, functional or anatomical asplenia (including sickle cell disease), immunosuppression from disease (including HIV) or treatment, excessive alcohol use, and smoking.

32dSh60.title: Immediate drug hypersensitivity reactions
32dSh60.description: An immunologically mediated drug hypersensitivity reaction that typically manifests within 1 hour after exposure to the culprit drug.

R2dlh60.title: Nonimmediate DHRs
R2dlh60.description: An immunologically mediated drug hypersensitivity reaction that typically manifests > 1 hour after exposure to the culprit drug.

j2d_h60.title: Binet staging system
j2d_h60.description: A staging system for chronic lymphocytic leukemia that stratifies patients into three risk groups. Stage A (low risk) involves < 3 lymphoid sites. Stage B (intermediate risk) involves ≥ 3 lymphoid sites. Stage C (high risk) involves anemia (Hb < 10 g/dL) and/or thrombocytopenia (platelets < 100,000/mm³).

42d3360.title: Heel drop exercise
42d3360.description: A strengthening exercise used to treat conditions such as plantar fasciitis and Achilles tendinitis. The individual stands with the forefeet on a step or block and raises both heels together (standing on the ball of the foot); the heel of the affected (painful) foot is then lowered just below horizontal. The exercise is repeated multiple times (up to 180/day).

k2dm360.title: Continuous glucose monitor
k2dm360.description: A subcutaneous device that continuously monitors glucose levels throughout the day to help patients with diabetes mellitus titrate insulin therapy.

O2dI360.title: Dry needling
O2dI360.description: A technique in which fine needles are inserted into the patient's skin to target nociceptive trigger point pain. Needles are placed either superficially in the subcutaneous tissue or deeper into the myofascial tissue. Although dry needling appears similar to acupuncture, the underlying theory and placement of the needles are based on Western biomedical science rather than traditional Chinese medicine.

52diR60.title: Novavax COVID-19 vaccine
52diR60.description: An inactivated monovalent vaccine containing a recombinant SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.

M2dMR60.title: Risk factors for HAV infection
M2dMR60.description: A collection of variables and attributes that increase an individual's risk of contracting hepatitis A. Factors include chronic liver disease, HIV infection, men who have sex with men, intravenous drug use, homelessness, travel to endemic areas, close contact with international travelers from endemic areas, and working in high-risk settings (e.g., laboratories that work with hepatitis A and health care facilities for high-risk individuals).

L2dwR60.title: Membrane sweeping
L2dwR60.description: An obstetric procedure used to induce normal spontaneous delivery. The amniotic membranes are manually separated from the lower uterus wall during a pelvic examination, leading to cervical ripening and uterine contractions. Risks include discomfort or pain from the procedure, vaginal bleeding, and irregular contractions.

o2d0i60.title: Coefficient of variation
o2d0i60.description: A statistical relative measure of dispersion that is calculated by dividing the standard deviation by the mean. Used to compare variations of multiple data sets.

K2dUi60.title: Risk factors for NSAID-induced GI toxicity
K2dUi60.description: Factors that increase the likelihood of peptic ulcer disease and its complications. These include age > 60 years, H. pylori infection, comorbidities, prior peptic ulcer disease, dyspepsia, use of high doses of NSAIDs or higher-risk NSAIDs (sulindac, piroxicam, and ketorolac), and concurrent use of antithrombotics, corticosteroids, aspirin, or SSRIs.

destinations.label: Peptic ulcer disease → Subtypes and variants

p2dLi60.title: Acute-on-chronic limb ischemia
p2dLi60.description: An acute arterial occlusion caused by atherosclerotic plaque rupture in a patient with known peripheral arterial disease. Patients with acute-on-chronic limb ischemia typically have a longer period of time in which the affected limb is salvageable compared to patients with acute limb ischemia because of prior recruitment of collateral blood vessels.

J2dsi60.title: Physical counterpressure measures
J2dsi60.description: Maneuvers that enhance venous blood return to the heart and can help prevent symptomatic orthostatic hypotension and syncope. These include squatting, sitting, leg crossing, bending forward, and/or muscle pumping or tensing.

I2dYQ60.title: Acyl-CoA
I2dYQ60.description: A biochemical substance that consists of coenzyme A combined with any fatty acid. Acyl-CoA is the product of fatty acid activation, which is facilitated by the enzyme acyl-CoA synthetase.

destinations.label: Lipids and their metabolism → Digestion and absorption of lipids

r2dfQ60.title: Fundic gland polyp
r2dfQ60.description: A type of gastric polyp located in the body or fundus of the stomach. Can arise sporadically or in association with familial adenomatous polyposis or chronic proton pump inhibitor therapy. Usually asymptomatic. Appears on endoscopy as a sessile mass without a stalk.

H2dKQ60.title: Insulin sensitivity
H2dKQ60.description: The responsiveness of the cells to insulin (e.g., glucose uptake from the bloodstream in response to insulin).

s2dtQ60.title: Receptor sensitivity
s2dtQ60.description: The responsiveness of a receptor to a ligand. Changes in receptor sensitivity can result in a different response to the same concentration of a ligand.

G2dBQ60.title: Antibiotic sensitivity
G2dBQ60.description: The susceptibility of a bacterial pathogen to antibiotics. Antibiotic sensitivity testing allows the sensitivity of a pathogen to specific antibiotics to be reported as susceptible, intermediate, or resistant.

u2dpj60.title: Cholera vaccine
u2dpj60.description: An oral vaccine designed to prevent infection from cholera. An attenuated live vaccine is licensed in the USA; attenuated and inactivated versions are available internationally. Protection is transient (lasting up to 3 years); therefore, its use is limited to outbreaks, humanitarian crises with a high-risk of cholera transmission, and travelers to areas with active cholera transmission.

v2dAj60.title: Satellite pharmacy
v2dAj60.description: A separate pharmaceutical work area in or outside a hospital that belongs to and is dependent on a centrally licensed hospital pharmacy.

92dNP60.title: Circulating nurse
92dNP60.description: A registered nurse who works outside the sterile field of the operating room. Responsibilities including preparing the patient and the operating room prior to surgery, monitoring and repositioning the patient, and supporting other team members during surgery (e.g., providing additional instruments, handling specimens).

B2dzP60.title: Clinical dehydration scale for acute gastroenteritis in children ≤ 5 years of age
B2dzP60.description: A score used to assess the severity of dehydration in young children (up to 5 years of age) with acute gastroenteritis. Children are scored from 0-2 in four areas (general appearance, presence of tears, sunken eyes, and dry mucous membrane) with a score of zero indicating no dehydration; a score of ≥ 5 indicates moderate to severe dehydration.

_2d5460.title: Scrub nurse
_2d5460.description: A registered nurse who assists the surgeon in the sterile field during surgery. Responsibilities include preparing the operating room, sterilizing instruments, preparing the surgical site prior to surgery, and passing instruments to the surgeon during surgery.

z2dr460.title: Surgical hand rub
z2dr460.description: A hand hygine method using disinfectants containing alcohol and phenol mixtures. Used as an alternative to scrubbing with a sponge.

destinations.label: Infection prevention and control → Pre-surgical infection prevention measures

media.title: Surgical hand disinfection using an alcohol-based rub

ZfdZk60.title: Voluntary tube opening maneuver
ZfdZk60.description: A maneuver that can be performed while diving to open the eustachian tube and prevent middle ear barotrauma.  The maneuver consists of placing the tip of the tongue behind the front teeth, closing the glottis, and swallowing air while keeping the soft palate neutral.

0fdek60.title: Multi-dose container
0fdek60.description: A container of liquid parenteral medication that is intended for more than one use. Multi-dose vials contain an antimicrobial preservative (e.g., benzyl alcohol).

afdQk60.title: Single-dose container
afdQk60.description: A container of liquid parenteral medication that is intended for single use in a single patient. Single-dose vials do not contain an antimicrobial preservative.

bfdHk60.title: Sheath introducer
bfdHk60.description: A wide-bore single-lumen catheter that is placed in a central vein for rapid and/or high-volume fluid administration or as a conduit for a pulmonary artery catheter or pacing leads. Proprietary names include Cordis and MAC.

Xfd9k60.title: Prior authorization
Xfd9k60.description: A process in which health care providers must obtain advance approval from a patient's health insurance company before providing a nonemergency service (e.g., diagnostic test, treatment, prescription) in order for the service to qualify for reimbursement.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

WfdPO60.title: Internal jugular line
