WfdPO60.description: A central venous line that enters the internal jugular vein in the neck and terminates in the superior vena cava, just above the junction of the superior vena cava and the right atrium.

dfdoO60.title: Femoral line
dfdoO60.description: A central venous line that enters the femoral vein in the groin and terminates in the inferior vena cava or the iliac vein.

VfdGO60.title: Subclavian line
VfdGO60.description: A central venous line that enters the skin below the clavicle and terminates in the superior vena cava, just above the junction of the superior vena cava and the right atrium.

efdxO60.title: Triple-lumen central venous catheter
efdxO60.description: A central venous line that has three independent channels. Can be used for the simultaneous administration of multiple medications or solutions at different rates. Allows for concurrent measurement of central venous pressure if necessary.

Ufdbl60.title: Reverse Hill-Sachs defect
Ufdbl60.description: A depression fracture of the anteromedial portion of the humeral head. Associated with posterior shoulder dislocation. An untreated reverse Hill-Sachs defect can result in osteonecrosis of the humeral head.

2fdTl60.title: Reverse Bankart lesion
2fdTl60.description: A detachment of the posteroinferior labrum of the humeral head with avulsion of the posterior capsular periosteum.  Results in laxity of the inferior glenohumeral ligament that can lead to posterior shoulder dislocation.

gfdFl60.title: Childhood wasting
gfdFl60.description: Low body weight as a result of acute malnutrition, rapid weight loss, or insufficient weight gain in infants and children. Defined as z score below 2 standard deviations in BMI-for-age charts or weight-for-length charts. Associated with significant morbidity and mortality.

jfd_N60.title: Simple breast cyst
jfd_N60.description: A benign breast lesion that is most commonly seen in premenopausal women. Characteristic features on ultrasound include a well-circumscribed, anechoic breast mass with thin walls and posterior acoustic enhancement. Simple breast cysts typically resolve spontaneously.

PfdWm60.title: Complicated breast cyst
PfdWm60.description: A type of breast cyst that has most features of a simple breast cyst (e.g., well-circumscribed mass, no septations, no mural thickening) on ultrasound but unlike a simple cyst, may have debris (internal echoes). It is associated with a low (< 2%) risk of malignancy.

4fd3m60.title: Complex breast cyst
4fd3m60.description: A breast cyst with internal septations, thick walls, asymmetric mural thickening, and/or solid and cystic components. Complex breast cysts are associated with an increased risk of concomitant malignancy and should be biopsied.

mfdV560.title: Pre-claim review
mfdV560.description: A process used by health insurance plans (e.g., Medicare) that requires health care providers to request provisional affirmation of coverage prior to submitting a final claim for payment.

ofd0M60.title: Pyloroplasty
ofd0M60.description: A procedure used to widen the gastric outlet and thereby improve gastric emptying. May be performed in the treatment of gastroparesis or peptic ulcer disease.

KfdUM60.title: Gastrojejunostomy
KfdUM60.description: A procedure to create an anastomosis between the stomach and jejunum. May be performed in patients with gastric outlet obstruction (e.g., due to malignancy), gastroparesis, or as part of weight loss surgery.

IfdYn60.title: Secondary lactase deficiency
IfdYn60.description: Acquired lactase deficiency resulting from damage to lactase-containing epithelial cells due to gastrointestinal disease (e.g., infectious gastroenteritis, inflammatory bowel disease). Onset of clinical features of lactose intolerance coincides with the onset of gastrointestinal pathology. Most commonly occurs in infants, although individuals of any age can be affected. Generally resolves after treatment of the underlying condition.

ufdpL60.title: Sprain
ufdpL60.description: A traumatic stretch or tear of a ligament.

Efd8L60.title: Casting
Efd8L60.description: The application of a circumferential plaster or fiberglass wrap to provide external immobilization to an injured extremity.

Dfd1o60.title: Ulnar gutter splint
Dfd1o60.description: A splint used to immobilize the 4th and 5th digits of the hand. Extends from the finger pads to the proximal forearm along the ulnar aspect of the hand and arm, with the wrist dorsiflexed at 20°, the MCP joint flexed 50°–90°, and the IP joints in extension. Indications include phalangeal and metacarpal fractures of the 4th and 5th digit (including boxer's fractures) and soft tissue injuries of the same area.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

wfdho60.title: Radial gutter splint
wfdho60.description: A type of splint used to immobilize the 2nd and 3rd digits of the hand. Extends from the finger pads to the proximal forearm along the radial aspect of the hand and arm, with the wrist dorsiflexed at 20°, the MCP joint flexed 50°–90°, and the IP joints in extension. Indications include phalangeal and metacarpal fractures of the 2nd and 3rd digit and soft tissue injuries of the same area.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

Cfdqo60.title: Traumatic optic neuropathy
Cfdqo60.description: Vision loss due to injury of the optic nerve from a penetrating or blunt force head trauma. Severity of injury varies from contusion to avulsion of the nerve.

destinations.label: Disorders of the visual pathway → Traumatic optic neuropathy (TON)

Bfdzo60.title: Amobarbital
Bfdzo60.description: A barbiturate primarily used as a sedative-hypnotic agent for the short-term treatment of insomnia. Not FDA-approved.

AfdRK60.title: OEIS syndrome
AfdRK60.description: A syndrome that consists of the following birth defects: omphalocele (O), exstrophy of the bladder and portions of bowel (E), imperforate anus (I), and spinal dysraphism (S).

zfdrK60.title: Weight bearing as tolerated
zfdrK60.description: An instruction for a patient to self-titrate the proportion of body weight placed on an affected limb according to comfort, up to full body weight.

-fdDK60.title: Non-weight-bearing
-fdDK60.description: A restriction on placing any weight on an injured or recently operated limb in order to facilitate healing.

ZTdZ660.title: Weight bearing status
ZTdZ660.description: The proportion of body weight placed on a limb during ambulation. Weight-bearing restrictions are prescribed when a limb has been injured or recently operated on to facilitate healing.

0Tde660.title: Fracture reduction
0Tde660.description: The restoration of normal alignment and position of bone fragments following a fracture. Typically performed with manipulation that reverses the mechanism of injury and frees distal bone fragments from impingements that keep them out of anatomical alignment.

aTdQ660.title: Immobilization
aTdQ660.description: The prevention of movement of bone fragments or joints using splints, casts, braces, or traction. Used to treat fractures, soft tissue injuries, and some inflammatory diseases.

WTdPp60.title: Narrative inquiry
WTdPp60.description: A qualitative research methodology that involves the study of narratives as the basic unit of describing and recording human experience.

dTdop60.title: Guidewire embolism
dTdop60.description: The complete or partial loss of a guidewire into the pulmonary circulation of a patient that occurs as a complication of central venous line insertion. Typically requires retrieval by an interventional radiologist.

destinations.label: Central venous access → Pitfalls and troubleshooting

VTdGp60.title: Thyroid acropachy
VTdGp60.description: A rare dermatological finding in patients with Graves disease that typically manifests as digital clubbing. Other manifestations include swelling of the hands and feet and periosteal bone formation over time.

eTdxp60.title: Dorsal splint
eTdxp60.description: A splint used to immobilize the dorsum of the hand and distal forearm. Placed with the MCP joints flexed at 60–90 degrees, the PIP and DIP joints fully extended, and the wrist extended at 15–20 degrees. Covers from the tip of the fingers on the dorsal aspect of the hand to the midforearm. Indications include injury to the distal forearm, wrist and/or hand (e.g., metacarpal fractures).

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

UTdbJ60.title: Volar splint
UTdbJ60.description: A type of splint that typically extends along the volar forearm from the high mid-palm of the hand to the mid-forearm. Indications include phalangeal and/or metacarpal fractures of the 2nd–5th digits, and soft tissue injuries of the same area. Placed with the MCP joints flexed at 60–90 degrees and the wrist extended at 20 degrees.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

2TdTJ60.title: Intrinsic plus position
2TdTJ60.description: The position of the hand used for immobilization with a splint or cast. The wrist is dorsiflexed at 20°, the MCP joints are flexed between 60° and 90°, and the fingers are fully extended or in slight flexion (10°). Often described as the position of the hand when holding a soda can.

STdyJ60.title: Phenomenological hermeneutics
STdyJ60.description: The investigation of phenomena and the associated experience through the interpretation of sources (e.g., interviews) within the subjective, cultural, and historical context of the phenomenon and its experience.

jTd_q60.title: Gastrostomy tube
jTd_q60.description: A type of feeding tube inserted endoscopically, surgically, or fluoroscopically through a small incision in the abdominal wall directly into the stomach. Used for long-term enteral nutrition (e.g., in patients with dysphagia after a stroke). When inserted endoscopically, the inserted feeding tube is commonly referred to as a percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) tube.

lTdvI60.title: Low-risk AV block
lTdvI60.description: A collection of atrioventricular blocks (AVBs) that are unlikely to progress to complete heart block and/or sudden cardiac death. Examples include first-degree AVB, second-degree AVB of the Mobitz I subtype, and 2:1 AVB thought to be at the AV nodal level.

destinations.label: Atrioventricular block → Management of AV blocks

NTd-I60.title: High-risk AV block
NTd-I60.description: A collection of atrioventricular blocks (AVBs) that carry a high risk to progress to complete heart block and/or sudden cardiac death. Examples include second degree AVB of the Mobitz II type, 2:1 AV block due to infranodal block, high-grade AV block, and third-degree AV block.

destinations.label: Atrioventricular block → Management of AV blocks

MTdMr60.title: Blunt thoracic aortic injury
MTdMr60.description: An injury of the aorta, most commonly at the aortic isthmus, distal to the exit of the left subclavian artery. Typically caused by rapid deceleration during blunt chest trauma. Clinical findings are initially unspecific (e.g., chest pain, dyspnea, dysphagia) and severity ranges from intimal lesions to aortic rupture.

media.title: Widened mediastinum secondary to traumatic thoracic aortic injury

nTd7r60.title: Aortic pseudocoarctation
nTd7r60.description: An elongation of the supra-aortic isthmus with kinking and low-grade narrowing of the descending aorta, without a pressure gradient across the lesion. Associated with congenital heart anomalies (e.g., bicuspid aortic valve) but can also be caused by blunt trauma to the chest. Clinical findings include upper extremity hypertension with lower extremity hypotension. May mimic true aortic coarctation.

LTdwr60.title: Benign asbestos pleural effusion
LTdwr60.description: An asbestos-related lung disease characterized by exudative effusion. Usually unilateral and results in no or nonspecific symptoms (e.g., dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, fever). Develops 10–20 years after asbestos exposure. Biopsy is required to exclude malignancy (e.g., mesothelioma) and tuberculosis.

6Tdj760.title: Calcimimetics
6Tdj760.description: A class of drug that mimics the binding of calcium to the calcium-sensing receptor in parathyroid chief cells, thereby decreasing PTH secretion. Used in the treatment of hyperparathyroidism if parathyroidectomy is contraindicated. Examples include cinacalcet and etelcalcetide.

pTdL760.title: Spectacular shrinking deficit
pTdL760.description: A rapid clinical improvement after symptom onset in patients with embolic stroke. Caused by distal migration of the embolus, leading to recanalization of the affected vessel.

JTds760.title: Postoperative endophthalmitis
JTds760.description: An inflammation of the anterior and posterior eye segments following intraocular surgery (e.g., cataract surgery). Usually occurs within 6 weeks of surgery. Symptoms include pain and decreased visual acuity. Clinical examination reveals conjunctival hyperemia and chemosis, hypopyon, corneal edema, and infection.

rTdfH60.title: Tourniquet
rTdfH60.description: A device used to apply circumferential pressure to a limb in order to constrict blood flow. Commonly used to stop hemorrhage from traumatic injuries or to minimize blood loss and improve visualization during surgery.

sTdtH60.title: Neonatal hypomagnesemia
sTdtH60.description: Low serum magnesium levels in a newborn. Defined as serum magnesium < 1.6 mg/dL. Potential causes include prematurity, maternal diabetes, fetal growth restriction, hypoparathyroidism, and inadequate intake of magnesium. May be asymptomatic or manifest with jitteriness, apnea, feeding intolerance, and seizures.

GTdBH60.title: Risk factors for dental caries
GTdBH60.description: A set of factors that increase an individual's risk of developing dental caries. These include family members with cavities, consumption of sugary food and drinks, special health care needs, and wearing orthodontic braces or appliances.

8TdOs60.title: Risk factors for pediatric dyslipidemia
8TdOs60.description: A set of factors that increase the risk of dyslipidemia during childhood. Includes pediatric medical conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, obesity, chronic kidney disease, heart transplant, coronary aneurysms, inflammatory diseases, and HIV; and exposure to smoking. Also includes a parent with dyslipidemia or a first or second-degree relative with a history of coronary events (e.g., MI, angina, stroke, cardiovascular interventions) at a young age (i.e., < 55 years if ♂ or < 65 years if ♀).

destinations.label: Lipid disorders in children → Risk factors

uTdps60.title: Risk factors for pediatric iron deficiency anemia
uTdps60.description: Risk factors include low socioeconomic status, prematurity or low birth weight, exposure to lead, breastfeeding beyond 4 months of age without supplemental iron, inadequate dietary intake of iron (e.g., due to restrictive diet, feeding problems, excessive milk intake), poor growth, chronic blood loss (e.g., menorrhagia, gastrointestinal bleeding), and gastrointestinal malabsorption (e.g., celiac disease, inflammatory bowel disease).

destinations.label: Iron deficiency anemia → Iron deficiency anemia in children and adolescents

vTdAs60.title: Screening questions for sudden cardiac death in children
vTdAs60.description: A risk assessment used to identify children at risk of sudden cardiac death. Includes four questions: any prior loss of consciousness (e.g., syncope or seizure) without warning, any exercise-related chest pain or shortness of breath, any relatives who unexpectedly died at < 50 years old, and any relatives with genetic heart conditions (→HCM, HOCM, ACM, LQTS, short QT, BrS, CPVT) diagnosed at < 50 years of age.

wTdhG60.title: Uterotonic agents
wTdhG60.description: A group of drugs that increase muscle tone in the uterus. Commonly used to treat postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony and for induction of labor. Examples include oxytocin, methylergonovine, and prostaglandins such as misoprostol.

9TdNG60.title: Jejunostomy
9TdNG60.description: A procedure used to create a percutaneous opening through the abdominal wall into the lumen of the jejunum, bypassing the proximal small bowel and stomach. Can be used in the management of bowel perforation or intestinal obstruction (i.e., venting jejunostomy) and for the delivery of enteral nutrition.

CTdqG60.title: Gatrostomy
CTdqG60.description: A procedure used to create a percutaneous opening through the abdominal wall directly into the stomach. Can be used for intestinal decompression in the management of intestinal obstruction or ileus (i.e., venting gastrostomy) and for the delivery of enteral nutrition.

_Td5t60.title: Uterine dehiscence
_Td5t60.description: A separation of uterine musculature with uterine serosa remaining intact.

zTdrt60.title: Neuraxial anesthesia
zTdrt60.description: A type of regional anesthesia involving the administration of local anesthetic agents into the subarachnoid or epidural space to achieve reversible numbing of pain conduction. Subdivided into spinal anesthesia and epidural anesthesia.

-TdDt60.title: Postviral syndrome
-TdDt60.description: The persistence of physical, neurological, and/or psychological symptoms for weeks to months after the resolution of an acute viral infection. Manifestations include fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, mood disturbances (e.g., depressed mood), headaches, and sleep disturbances.

ZgdZF60.title: Bacterial conjunctivitis
ZgdZF60.description: A type of conjunctivitis caused by bacterial infection. Includes hyperacute bacterial conjunctivitis (neisserial conjunctivitis), acute bacterial conjunctivitis, and chlamydial conjunctivitis. Bacterial conjunctivitis can be an ocular emergency and, if left untreated, can cause blindness.

0gdeF60.title: Viral conjunctivitis
0gdeF60.description: A form of infectious conjunctivitis that is typically caused by adenovirus or herpes simplex virus. Viral conjunctivitis is the most common overall cause of conjunctivitis.

agdQF60.title: Noninfectious conjunctivitis
agdQF60.description: A type of conjunctivitis caused by mechanical irritation or systemic conditions. Includes allergic conjunctivitis, keratoconjunctivitis sicca, ocular cicatricial pemphigoid, and toxic keratoconjunctivitis.

YgdnF60.title: Polyuria-polydipsia syndrome
YgdnF60.description: A condition characterized by hypotonic polyuria. Caused by arginine vasopressin deficiency (central diabetes insipidus), arginine vasopressin resistance (nephrogenic diabetes insipidus), or primary polydipsia. Differential diagnoses include other causes of polyuria and polydipsia, e.g., uncontrolled diabetes mellitus.

Ugdbu60.title: Autoimmune hepatitis-primary biliary cholangitis overlap syndrome
Ugdbu60.description: An autoimmune liver disease characterized by clinical, serological, and histopathological features of both autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cholangitis.

fgdku60.title: Null hypothesis significance testing
fgdku60.description: A method of statistical inference that tests experimental data against the null hypothesis (i.e., the assumption that there is no association between two measured variables).

Tgd6u60.title: Type 1 autoimmune hepatitis
Tgd6u60.description: A type of autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) characterized by the presence of antinuclear (ANA), anti-smooth muscle antibodies (ASMA), and anti-soluble liver antigen/liver pancreas antibodies (anti-SLA). It makes up 80% of AIH cases and is most common in adults.

ggdFu60.title: Type 2 autoimmune hepatitis
ggdFu60.description: A type of autoimmune hepatitis characterized by the presence of anti-liver-kidney microsomal-1 antibodies (anti-LKM-1) and anti-liver cytosol antibodies-1 (ALC-1). It is less common than type 1 AIH and occurs primarily in children.

RgdlE60.title: Prevention of infectious conjunctivitis
RgdlE60.description: A collection of measures to prevent infectious conjunctivitis and its transmission. Examples include regular hand washing, avoiding touching the eyes, and good contact lens hygiene. For infected individuals, patients should isolate, avoid sharing items (e.g., towels), and routinely disinfect hands and surfaces.

PgdWv60.title: Eluxadoline
PgdWv60.description: A mu opioid receptor agonist, delta opioid receptor antagonist, and kappa opioid receptor agonist. Used to treat abdominal pain and diarrhea caused by irritable bowel syndrome. Its use is associated with acute pancreatitis.

4gd3v60.title: Tenapanor
4gd3v60.description: A sodium/hydrogen exchanger 3 inhibitor that reduces sodium absorption in the small intestine and colon. As a result, intestinal lumen water secretion and intestinal transit time increase, leading to softened stool consistency. Used to treat constipation caused by irritable bowel syndrome.

kgdmv60.title: Tegaserod
kgdmv60.description: A partial neuronal 5-HT4 receptor agonist that stimulates the peristaltic reflex and increases intestinal secretion. Used to treat irritable bowel syndrome. Not commercially available in the US.

lgdvv60.title: Gluten-related disorders
lgdvv60.description: A spectrum of disorders that are related to the consumption of gluten. Includes celiac disease, dermatitis herpetiformis, gluten ataxia, nonceliac gluten sensitivity, and wheat allergy.

Ngd-v60.title: Interpersonal rejection sensitivity
Ngd-v60.description: A pathological tendency to perceive benign social cues as evidence of rejection. This tendency is a feature of major depressive disorder with atypical features.

mgdVD60.title: exposure and response prevention
mgdVD60.description: A type of cognitive behavioral therapy in which the patient is guided through repeated and prolonged exposures to situations that provoke anxiety and/or obsessive thoughts and is encouraged to avoid compulsive behaviors. Used to treat obsessive-compulsive disorder.

destinations.label: Psychotherapy and defense mechanisms → Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)

5gdiD60.title: ERP
5gdiD60.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Effective refractory period
2) Exposure and Response Prevention

8gdOC60.title: Indications for pacemaker implantation
8gdOC60.description: A collection of cardiac arrhythmias for which permanent pacemaker implantation is the definitive treatment. Examples include high-risk atrioventricular blocks (e.g., third-degree AV block, Mobitz type II AV block, high-grade AV block), and symptomatic bradycardia secondary to sinus node dysfunction, infranodal AV block, or atrial fibrillation.

destinations.label: Cardiac implantable electronic devices → Permanent pacemakers

vgdAC60.title: Sinus bradycardia
vgdAC60.description: A sinus rhythm (i.e., visible P waves preceding each QRS complex and a regular PR interval) with a rate < 60/min.

media.title: Sinus bradycardia with sinus pause and junctional escape rhythm

ygddB60.title: Ocular surface disease
ygddB60.description: A condition caused by disorders of the corneal or conjunctival epithelium. Symptoms include foreign body sensation, irritation, and itching. Causes of the underlying epithelial disorders are manifold and include infectious (e.g., keratitis), autoimmune (e.g., ocular mucous membrane pemphigoid), and noninfectious (e.g., dry eye disease) diseases. A diagnosis of ocular surface disease is suggested if there is increased uptake of an ocular surface dye stain.

_gd5B60.title: Descending transtentorial herniation
_gd5B60.description: A downward displacement of brain tissue through the tentorial notch due to increased intracranial pressure in the supratentorial space, usually caused by a mass lesion. Further subdivided into lateral herniation and central herniation.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Subtypes and variants

zgdrB60.title: Delusional disorder, jealous type
zgdrB60.description: A delusional disordered characterized by a fixed false belief that one's partner is unfaithful or that one may lose a valued relationship due to the threat of a rival. The delusion is often based on incorrect inferences (e.g., that a missed phone call must be due to infidelity). Must cause significant dysfunction that impairs daily life.

-gdDB60.title: Obsessional jealousy
-gdDB60.description: A subtype of obsessive-compulsive disorder characterized by nondelusional persistent thoughts that one's partner is unfaithful or that one may lose a valued relationship due to the threat of a rival. Typically results in repetitive behaviors in response to concerns about infidelity. Must cause significant dysfunction that impairs daily life.

ZSdZy60.title: Ciguatoxin
ZSdZy60.description: A toxin formed by Gambierdiscus dinoflagellates. Ingestion of large, predatory reef fish (e.g., grouper, barracuda) that have accumulated this toxin in their tissues can result in ciguatera fish poisoning.

0Sdey60.title: CTX
0Sdey60.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Ceftriaxone
2) Ciguatoxin

aSdQy60.title: Correction principle
aSdQy60.description: A provision of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), which states that individuals should be provided with a timely means to dispute the accuracy or integrity of their individually identifiable health information, and to have erroneous information corrected or to have a dispute documented if their requests are denied.

destinations.label: Ethics of communicating medical information → Confidentiality

dSdoA60.title: Contact lens hygiene
dSdoA60.description: Measures for individuals who use contact lenses to reduce the risk of ocular infections such as conjunctivitis, keratitis, and anterior uveitis. Includes washing hands before handling the lenses, cleaning lenses in disinfecting solution, avoiding getting water on lenses, not wearing lenses while sleeping, and replacing contact lenses and storage cases at the recommended intervals.

eSdxA60.title: Parenteral nutrition-associated liver disease
eSdxA60.description: An outdated term for liver disease caused by medical and surgical management strategies used for intestinal failure (e.g., chronic parenteral nutrition). The updated term is "intestinal failure-associated liver disease (IFALD)".

5SdiZp0.title: CSF leak precautions
5SdiZp0.description: Measures to prevent or reduce CSF leaks in patients with dural tears (e.g., due to craniofacial trauma). Precautions include bed rest with head of bed elevation and avoidance of straining and Valsalva maneuver (e.g., use of stool softeners to prevent straining with defecation).

pSdL0p0.title: Lethal triad of trauma
pSdL0p0.description: A combination of hypothermia, acidosis, and coagulopathy seen in patients with severe traumatic injuries. The three conditions exacerbate each other, resulting in death if not corrected.

8SdOYp0.title: Residual sedation
8SdOYp0.description: An adverse effect of sedative-hypnotic drugs in which sedative effects (e.g., drowsiness) persist beyond the intended time span.

DSd1bp0.title: Paradoxical reaction
DSd1bp0.description: An atypical response to medication characterized by symptoms opposite to the expected effects. Most frequently seen with medications like benzodiazepines, barbiturates, inhalational anesthetics, and antihistamines.

wSdhbp0.title: Staged ascent
wSdhbp0.description: The gradual ascent to higher altitude, including regular stops and overnight stays at intermittent altitudes to allow for acclimatization. Reduces the incidence and severity of high-altitude illnesses such as acute mountain sickness.

BSdzbp0.title: Eucapnic voluntary hyperpnea
BSdzbp0.description: A bronchial provocation test that may be used to diagnose exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB), though it is not available in many settings. The patient hyperventilates a dry, cold gas mixture containing 5% CO2 for 6 minutes, with spirometry performed before and after the test. A decrease in FEV1 of 10% or more is consistent with EIB.

ASdRXp0.title: Conducted electrical weapon
ASdRXp0.description: A weapon that delivers a high voltage but low amperage electrical charge, causing temporary neuromuscular incapacitation.

destinations.label: Environmental pathology → Electrical and lightning injuries

_Sd5Xp0.title: Buddy taping
_Sd5Xp0.description: A technique used to treat an injured finger or toe. The injured digit is securely taped to an adjacent uninjured one to provide support and alignment and for immobilization. Indications include sprains, nondisplaced stable fractures of the proximal or middle phalanx, and proximal interphalangeal dislocations.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Lower extremities
Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

ZhdZcp0.title: Respiratory airway secretory cell
ZhdZcp0.description: A progenitor cell for type II pneumocytes found in the respiratory bronchioles. Normal differentiation and maturation of these cells can be disrupted as a result of chronic exposure to cigarette smoke.

media.title: Cells and structures of lungs and airways

0hdecp0.title: Postobstructive diuresis
0hdecp0.description: A polyuric state resulting from the rapid renal elimination of accumulated water and electrolytes after relief of urinary tract obstruction, typically bladder outlet obstruction or bilateral ureteral obstruction. Pathological postobstructive diuresis may lead to dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, hypovolemia, and hypovolemic shock.

ahdQcp0.title: Diabetes mellitus in pregnancy
ahdQcp0.description: Consists of gestational diabetes mellitus (impaired glucose tolerance that develops during pregnancy) and pregestational diabetes mellitus (diabetes mellitus that is present before conception).

Yhdncp0.title: Corneal endotheliitis
Yhdncp0.description: An inflammation of the corneal endothelium that manifests with edema, cellular deposits (keratic precipitate), and anterior chamber inflammation. Causes are multifactorial and include infections, adverse drug reactions, and surgical procedures. Associated with visual changes, pain, and photophobia.

bhdHcp0.title: Trabeculitis
bhdHcp0.description: A condition in which inflammation and resultant edema in the trabecular meshwork causes obstruction and dysfunction, leading to raised intraocular pressure. Typically caused by viral infections and associated with uveitis.

Xhd9cp0.title: Prescription drug diversion
Xhd9cp0.description: The transfer of a pharmaceutical substance from its lawful intended use to an unlawful use or distribution channel. Commonly diverted drugs include opioids, benzodiazepines, and amphetamines.

chda1p0.title: Matricectomy
chda1p0.description: A procedure in which part or all of the nail matrix is removed via chemicals (e.g., phenol), surgery, cryotherapy, or laser. Can be used to treat ingrown toenails, thickened nails, and congenital nail dystrophies.

1hd21p0.title: Decompression illness
1hd21p0.description: A disorder caused by the formation of inert gas bubbles in the blood or tissue after a rapid reduction in environmental pressure (e.g., caused by a rapid ascent from a dive or in an aircraft). Includes decompression sickness and arterial gas embolism.

dhdo1p0.title: Paradoxical reaction to benzodiazepines
dhdo1p0.description: A dose-dependent reaction to benzodiazepines that is opposite to the expected effect. Most frequently occurs in older adults, with symptoms including talkativeness, restlessness, anxiety, irritability, and aggression. Treatment involves cessation of the causative drug.

ghdFWp0.title: Blast wave
ghdFWp0.description: A pressure wave created by the supersonic expansion of gas following the detonation of a high-order explosive. May cause occult internal organ damage.

Qhdudp0.title: Dive table
Qhdudp0.description: A numerical table used by divers to determine safe dive times and depths and provide guidance for ascent rate and minimum surface intervals between dives. Helps to reduce the risk of complications such as decompression illness and barotrauma. Dive tables have been largely replaced by wearable dive computers.

OhdIVp0.title: Diving history
OhdIVp0.description: The acquisition of information required to accurately evaluate and manage diving-related complications. Includes timing of symptom onset, details of the dive (e.g., depth, dive time, ascent rates, decompression stops, inspired gas mixture), and the patient's medical history (e.g., asthma, patent foramen ovale).

Nhd-Vp0.title: Epithelioid trophoblastic tumor
Nhd-Vp0.description: A type of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia characterized histologically by nests, cords, and/or sheets of intermediate trophoblastic cells with eosinophilic to clear cytoplasm. Most commonly arises in the lower uterine segment or cervix.

mhdVep0.title: Lifitegrast
mhdVep0.description: A lymphocyte function-associated antigen-1 antagonist used to treat dry eye syndrome.

5hdiep0.title: Apical compartment prolapse
5hdiep0.description: The herniation of the uterus and cervix, cervix alone, or vaginal vault into the lower vagina, hymen, or beyond the vaginal introitus. Commonly after pelvic surgery (e.g., hysterectomy). Often associated with enterocele.

6hdjUp0.title: Home health care
6hdjUp0.description: A medical service (e.g., medication, physical therapy) provided by professional health care personnel (e.g., nurses, social workers, physical therapists) in the patient's home. Typically coordinated by a home health agency.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health care access

IhdY2p0.title: T hysterotomy
IhdY2p0.description: A surgical procedure that involves making a low uterine segment transverse incision with a vertical extension. Used to remove uterine contents (e.g., during a cesarean delivery).

rhdf2p0.title: Lipohemarthrosis
rhdf2p0.description: The presence of fat and blood in a joint, resulting from bone marrow leakage into the joint space (e.g., after trauma or surgery). Lipohemarthrosis in the context of trauma suggests an underlying fracture.

shdt2p0.title: Pulmonary barotrauma
shdt2p0.description: A lung injury caused by a pressure gradient between the ambient environment, the airway, the alveoli and/or the surrounding tissue. Can be caused by mechanical ventilation, rapid ascent while diving or flying, or explosions. Manifestations include pneumothorax, pulmonary hemorrhage, air embolism, and inflammatory changes.

Fhdgfp0.title: hCG-mediated hyperthyroidism
Fhdgfp0.description: A type of hyperthyroidism resulting from increased levels of hCG. hCG binds to TSH receptors and stimulates the thyroid. Causes include gestational transient thyrotoxicosis with or without hyperemesis gravidarum, multiple gestation, and gestational trophoblastic disease.

destinations.label: Graves disease → Graves disease in pregnancy

whdhTp0.title: Keratoconjunctivitis
whdhTp0.description: An inflammation of both the conjunctiva and the cornea. May have an infectious or noninfectious etiology.

xhdETp0.title: Directly observed therapy
xhdETp0.description: The use of a trained individual to watch a patient receive their medication (e.g., swallowing oral medications, receiving an IM injection). Observation may occur in person or remotely. Often used in the treatment of tuberculosis and certain STIs.

_hd5gp0.title: Clinical features of ectopic pregnancy
_hd5gp0.description: Features include lower abdominal pain and guarding, vaginal bleeding, and signs of early pregnancy, typically manifesting 6–8 weeks after the last menstrual period. Physical findings include cervical motion and adnexal tenderness, a palpable adnexal mass, and hemorrhagic shock in tubal rupture.

Z3dZSp0.title: Gonococcal conjunctivitis
Z3dZSp0.description: A conjunctivitis caused by Neisseria gonorrhea. This is most common in newborns and sexually active young adults. The infection manifests with rapid onset hyperemia and significant purulent drainage in both eyes, fever, and preauricular lymphadenopathy. Because this infection can threaten vision, prompt treatment with intravenous antibiotics (ceftriaxone or ciprofloxacin) is important.

b3dHSp0.title: Patellar subluxation
b3dHSp0.description: Partial displacement of the patella from the femoral trochlear groove.

V3dGhp0.title: Asthma action plan
V3dGhp0.description: An individualized, written plan of action that should be provided to all patients with asthma, detailing what symptoms signal worsening asthma, how to adjust medications in response, and when to seek medical care.

U3db3p0.title: Sexual assault response team
U3db3p0.description: A multidisciplinary group that coordinates medical care, psychological and social support, and forensic evidence collection for individuals who have been sexually assaulted. Team members include nurses or physicians trained as sexual assault forensic examiners, law enforcement officers, patient advocates, prosecutors, and forensic laboratory personnel.

f3dk3p0.title: Drug-facilitated sexual assault
f3dk3p0.description: A sexual attack facilitated by the intentional or unintentional use of an intoxicating substance that rendered the affected individual incapacitated or unconscious, impairing their ability to resist and recall details of the assault. Red flags include a period of unconsciousness, amnesia, and/or confusion at the time of the suspected assault.

i3dJRp0.title: Trauma team
i3dJRp0.description: A multidisciplinary team for trauma care comprised of emergency medicine, intensive care, surgery, and nursing specialties. Members typically include a team leader, airway manager, assessment physician, proceduralist, trauma nurse, trauma technician, respiratory therapist, radiographer, and scribe.

Q3duRp0.title: Traumatic amputation
Q3duRp0.description: The immediate loss of a limb or appendage resulting from injury to an extremity.

P3dWip0.title: Countries with medium-to-high HBV prevalence
P3dWip0.description: Countries with ≥ 2% HBV prevalence. Includes all of the countries in Asia, the Pacific Islands, and most of the countries in Africa.

43d3ip0.title: Countries with high HBV prevalence
43d3ip0.description: Countries with ≥ 8% HBV prevalence. Includes all of the countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, the Pacific Islands, and East and Southeast Asia, excluding Japan.

O3dIip0.title: Cytology-alone screening
O3dIip0.description: A screening strategy for cervical cancer based on evaluation of cervical cytology (i.e., Pap smear without HPV genotyping). Abnormal results are generally followed by a reflex HPV test.

m3dVQp0.title: Sexual assault forensic examiner
m3dVQp0.description: A health care professional who has received specialized training in the medical and forensic examination of individuals who have been sexually assaulted.

M3dMQp0.title: Three-density pattern
M3dMQp0.description: A mixed obstructive and infiltrative process seen on high-resolution lung CT scan. Characterized by a combination of three sharply demarcated attenuations: normal lung, ground-glass opacities (i.e., high attenuation), and lucent lung (i.e., decreased attenuation and vascularity). Highly specific for fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis and helps differentiate it from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

L3dwQp0.title: Congenital athymia
L3dwQp0.description: The absence of the thymus gland at birth, which results in T-cell deficiency and high susceptibility to infection (severe combined immunodeficiency). Can be seen in individuals with 22q11.2 deletion (DiGeorge syndrome).

o3d0jp0.title: Bruckner test
o3d0jp0.description: The evaluation of the red reflex in both eyes simultaneously. Can be used to assess ocular alignment, corneal abnormalities, and refractive errors.

K3dUjp0.title: Olecranon bursa
K3dUjp0.description: A synovial fluid-filled sac located between the skin and the olecranon process on the extensor surface of the elbow. Reduces friction with movement of the elbow joint.

63djjp0.title: Human trafficking
63djjp0.description: The recruitment, harboring, transportation, or provision of a person for the purpose of labor and/or sexual exploitation through the use of force, fraud, or coercion.

A3dROp0.title: Neurological assessment
A3dROp0.description: A serial bedside assessment of level of consciousness based on the Glasgow coma scale, pupillary response, and motor and sensory functions. Used to detect impending neurological deterioration and facilitate timely intervention.

_3d5Op0.title: Chance fracture
_3d5Op0.description: An unstable spine fracture caused by excessive spinal flexion (e.g., during a motor vehicle collision). Typically occurs at the thoracolumbar junction. The fracture extends horizontally through the vertebral body, spinous process, and pedicles.

YRdnlp0.title: Rapid Appraisal for Trafficking
YRdnlp0.description:
A 4-item screening tool used to help identify individuals who may be victims of human trafficking. An affirmative answer to any of these questions warrants further investigation:
1) Have you ever worked or done things in a place that made you feel scared or unsafe?
2) Have you ever been tricked or forced into doing work you did not want to do?
3) Have you ever been afraid to leave or quit a work situation due to fears of violence or threats of harm to yourself or your family?
4) Have you ever received anything in exchange for sex (e.g., a place to stay, gifts, food)?

cRdaNp0.title: Fracture blister
cRdaNp0.description: A type of blister that occurs over a fracture or dislocation site. Typically manifests hours to days after an injury. Can be clear or hemorrhagic. Most common in areas with bony prominences (e.g., elbow, foot and ankle).

WRdPNp0.title: Spinal needle
WRdPNp0.description: A needle and stylet designed to facilitate dural puncture and access to deep tissues or body cavities. Commonly available in standardized lengths between 1.5 and 5 inches and diameters between 19 and 30 G.

media.title: Lumbar puncture (1/2): materials, patient positioning, and puncture site

mRdVnp0.title: RRT
mRdVnp0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Renal replacement therapy
2. Rapid response team
3. Registered respiratory therapist

nRd7np0.title: Clinical features of acute compartment syndrome
nRd7np0.description: A set of signs and symptoms that raise suspicion for compartment syndrome. The characteristic feature is deep, burning, diffuse pain out of proportion to physical signs and injury mechanism. Other features include pallor, reduced pulses, paresthesias, sensory deficits, and/or muscle weakness.

qRdCLp0.title: Susto
qRdCLp0.description: A cultural syndrome primarily associated with Latin American cultures in which somatic symptoms (e.g., pain, stomachache, headache) and psychological symptoms (e.g., sadness, lack of motivation, sleep troubles) are attributed to a stressful life event that causes the soul to leave the body.

8RdOKp0.title: IVC
8RdOKp0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Inferior vena cava
2. Inspiratory vital capacity

uRdpKp0.title: CDI
uRdpKp0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Central diabetes insipidus
2. Clostridioides difficile infection

vRdAKp0.title: Carry-over effect
vRdAKp0.description: A situation that arises during a crossover trial when the residual effect of the first intervention persists into the second. The washout period is supposed to reduce this effect.

DRd16p0.title: Recruitment bias
DRd16p0.description: A type of bias that can occur in cluster-randomized trials if individuals are recruited into a study or selected for inclusion after an intervention has already been allocated to a specific cluster. Can affect allocation concealment and lead to unblinding.

zRdrpp0.title: Pulmonary sarcoidosis
zRdrpp0.description: An inflammatory disease of the lungs and intrathoracic lymph nodes that is characterized by cough, dyspnea, chest tightness, and bilateral hilar adenopathy on chest imaging.

-RdDpp0.title: Cardiac sarcoidosis
-RdDpp0.description: A rare inflammatory disease of the heart characterized by granuloma formation, which can lead to conduction abnormalities and arrhythmias, congestive heart failure, syncope, and sudden death.

ZidZJp0.title: Mediastinoscopy
ZidZJp0.description: A surgical procedure that allows exploration and biopsy of lymph nodes or other tissue (e.g., tumors) in the mediastinum. Used for diagnosing thoracic diseases (e.g., sarcoidosis, lymphoma) and lung cancer staging.

0ideJp0.title: Epidural catheter
0ideJp0.description: A fine plastic tube (catheter) that is percutaneously inserted into the epidural space. Indications include epidural anesthesia (e.g., during labor, perioperatively) and analgesia (e.g., chronic pain management).

cidaqp0.title: Twiddler syndrome
cidaqp0.description: An uncommon complication of cardiac implantable electronic devices caused by the accidental or deliberate manipulation of the pulse generator, resulting in lead coiling and retraction. May result in failure to detect abnormal rhythms, failure to achieve mechanical capture, or stimulation of noncardiac structures (e.g., the diaphragm, pectoral muscle).

1id2qp0.title: Vaginal hormone therapy
1id2qp0.description: A hormonal medication (e.g., estrogen, dehydroepiandrosterone) that is administered vaginally and typically prescribed for hypoestrogenic urogenital atrophy (e.g., vulvovaginitis during menopause or lactation).

WidPqp0.title: PGD
WidPqp0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Preimplantation genetic diagnosis
2. Primary graft dysfunction

didoqp0.title: Intracranial hypotension
didoqp0.description: A condition in which there is decreased fluid pressure within the brain cavity. Caused by the leakage of cerebrospinal fluid (e.g., due to a dural defect, spinal trauma, lumbar puncture leak). Manifestations include severe headache (especially when upright), nausea, vomiting, and visual changes.

VidGqp0.title: Fall on out-stretched hand
VidGqp0.description: The most common cause of distal radius fractures. Can also cause damage to ligamentous structures of the hand and wrist, carpal fractures, and clavicular fractures.

UidbIp0.title: Synthase
UidbIp0.description: A type of enzyme that catalyzes a reaction that links two molecules (e.g., ATP synthase, which catalyzes the formation of ATP). This term was previously used synonymously with the term “synthetase,” which now more specifically refers to synthases that use energy produced by the hydrolysis of a nucleoside triphosphate (e.g., ATP).

Tid6Ip0.title: DNA ligase
Tid6Ip0.description: An enzyme that catalyzes the formation of a phosphodiester bond between adjacent nucleotides within a double-stranded DNA molecule. Used in the repair of single-stranded breaks and in DNA replication to join Okazaki fragments.

Ridlrp0.title: Food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome
Ridlrp0.description: A non-IgE-mediated food allergy primarily seen in infants. Caused by non-IgE-mediated inflammation of the entire gastrointestinal tract in response to food proteins (e.g., cow's milk, soy protein). Symptoms typically include vomiting, diarrhea, weight loss, and failure to thrive.

iidJrp0.title: CST
iidJrp0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Contraction stress test
2. Cardiac stress test

Qidurp0.title: High risk stress fracture
Qidurp0.description: A stress fracture in a location associated with a high rate of fracture progression, nonunion, or delayed healing.  These sites include the superolateral femoral neck, patella, anterior tibia, medial malleolus, talus, navicular, and the proximal 5th metatarsal shaft.

jid_rp0.title: Rectal bleeding
jid_rp0.description: Lower gastrointestinal bleeding that originates in the rectum. Overt rectal bleeding typically manifests with hematochezia. Common causes include anal fissures, hemorrhoids, and constipation.

4id37p0.title: Pulse generator
4id37p0.description: A thin metal case that is a part of a cardiac implantable electronic device. Contains a power source to produce electrical impulses and a programmable computer.

destinations.label: Cardiac implantable electronic devices → Technical background

lidv7p0.title: Pulmonary bleb
lidv7p0.description: A small (< 1 cm), thin-walled space containing air that results from subpleural alveolar rupture. Usually located on the lung apices. The vast majority are asymptomatic, but ruptured blebs are thought to cause spontaneous pneumothoraces.

LidwHp0.title: Gastrojejunostomy tube
LidwHp0.description: A type of feeding tube inserted endoscopically, surgically, or fluoroscopically through a small incision in the abdominal wall into the stomach, with an additional tube threaded into the jejunum. Used for long-term enteral nutrition into the small intestine and simultaneous venting or decompression of the stomach (e.g., in malignant gastric outlet obstruction, severe gastroparesis).

Fidgtp0.title: US Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use
Fidgtp0.description: A set of criteria that can be used to determine the safest method of contraception for individuals with specific medical conditions or relevant history (e.g., advanced age, history of smoking). Eligibility criteria are assigned to categories ranging from 1 to 4; e.g., category 1 indicates no limitations on the use of a specific contraceptive method; conversely, category 4 represents an absolute contraindication in the setting of certain conditions/factors.

destinations.label: Contraception → U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria (USMEC) for contraceptive use

8idOtp0.title: Tongue type fracture
8idOtp0.description: A type of calcaneal fracture in which the posterior tuberosity is avulsed upward by the Achilles tendon. Skin and soft tissue can be compressed by this displaced fragment, potentially leading to skin necrosis and conversion of a closed fracture to an open fracture.

Eid8tp0.title: Bohler angle
Eid8tp0.description: A radiographic measurement used to identify subtle fractures of the calcaneus. The Bohler angle is the angle formed by a line from the posterior tuberosity of the calcaneus to the apex of the posterior facet, and a line from the apex of the posterior facet to the apex of the anterior process. The normal range for this angle is 20-40°. An angle under 20° is suggestive of a compression fracture.

vidAtp0.title: Dental malocclusion
vidAtp0.description: The misalignment between the teeth of the upper and lower jaws when biting. Often further classified as overbite, underbite, crossbite, and overcrowding.

widhFp0.title: X-ray findings of COPD
widhFp0.description: Findings include signs of pulmonary hyperinflation (e.g., increased anteroposterior diameter, flattened diaphragm, horizontal ribs, widened intercostal spaces, hyperlucency of lung tissue, and an elongated cardiac silhouette) and signs of bullous emphysema (e.g., parenchymal bullae or pulmonary blebs).

CidqFp0.title: Blast wind
CidqFp0.description: A forced flow of superheated air following an explosion. May cause physical displacement of people, objects, and/or debris.

BidzFp0.title: Primary blast injury
BidzFp0.description: An injury caused solely by forces transmitted from the overpressure wave (blast wave) created by an explosion.

XQd9up0.title: Endogenous hyperinsulinism
XQd9up0.description: A condition in which there is an oversecretion of insulin (e.g., resulting from an insulinoma). Characterized by inappropriately high serum levels relative to blood sugar levels, which manifests as hypoglycemic symptoms.

dQdoEp0.title: Lead lines
dQdoEp0.description: An x-ray finding present in children exposed to lead. Pathological deposition of calcium leads to dense metaphyseal bands. The term is sometimes incorrectly used to describe the Burton line (a thin purple-blue line on the gums), which is a classic sign of chronic lead exposure.

UQdbvp0.title: Designated record set
UQdbvp0.description: According to 45 CFR 160.501, a designated record set is a group of records maintained by or for a covered entity that is: (i) The medical records and billing records about individuals maintained by or for a covered health care provider; (ii) The enrollment, payment, claims adjudication, and case or medical management record systems maintained by or for a health plan; or (iii) Used, in whole or in part, by or for the covered entity to make decisions about individuals.

2QdTvp0.title: Pes anserinus
2QdTvp0.description: A common tendon for the sartorius, gracilis, and semitendinosus muscles that inserts at the anteromedial aspect of the proximal tibia.

media.title: Ligaments and retinacula of the patella

fQdkvp0.title: Danger assessment-5
fQdkvp0.description: A set of five questions used to assess the risk of death or severe injury from intimate partner violence: Has the physical violence increased in frequency or severity over the last year? Has your partner ever hurt you or threatened you with a weapon? Do you believe your partner is capable of killing you? Does your partner ever choke you? Is your partner violently or constantly jealous of you? An affirmative response to two or more of the questions indicates an increased risk.

lQdvwp0.title: Autoinflation device
lQdvwp0.description: A patient-controlled device that opens the eustachian tube by raising pressure in the nose, which improves drainage of fluid from the middle ear.

mQdV9p0.title: Mondor sign
mQdV9p0.description: A central plantar ecchymosis and/or hematoma. A specific sign of a compression fracture of the calcaneus.

GQdBxp0.title: Shoulder pad sign
GQdBxp0.description: A clinical finding secondary to amyloid infiltration of the tendons and capsule of the shoulder that is seen in systemic AL amyloidosis (primary amyloidosis). Infiltration and swelling cause a prominent appearance of the bilateral anterior deltoid area, and limit movement.

tQdXBp0.title: Enhanced cognitive behavioral therapy
tQdXBp0.description: A psychotherapy method that employs the behavioral modification and cognitive restructuring techniques of cognitive behavioral therapy in a sequential, manual-based format. Used in the management of all types of eating disorders and involves addressing factors that maintain the eating disorder, e.g., low self-esteem and perfectionism.

FQdgBp0.title: Core decompression
FQdgBp0.description: A surgical treatment for the early stages of avascular necrosis. A core segment of the bone is removed to decrease intraosseous pressure and stimulate angiogenesis. Typically used for osteonecrosis of the femoral head, humeral head, or lunate bone.

destinations.label: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head → Treatment

EQd8Bp0.title: Deconditioning
EQd8Bp0.description: The physical changes that develop after an extended period of inactivity, including decreased muscle strength and mass, and shortness of breath and tachycardia with physical activity. Severity may range from mildly decreased exercise tolerance to difficulty performing daily activities.

vQdABp0.title: Exercise rhinolaryngoscopy
vQdABp0.description: A procedure in which a flexible laryngoscope is inserted through the nose and secured, allowing visualization of the larynx while the patient exercises. Used to diagnose conditions such as exercise-induced laryngeal dysfunction.

wQdhyp0.title: Tafamidis
wQdhyp0.description: A non-NSAID derivative of benzoxazole that binds to transthyretin in the bloodstream and prevents it from misfolding into the amyloid fibril form. Also referred to as a transthyretin stabilizer due to its mechanism of action. Used in the treatment of transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR).

BQdzyp0.title: Vision rehabilitation
BQdzyp0.description: A program to support individuals with vision loss. Program goals include optimizing reading capability, providing emotional support, and training patients in the use of assistive devices so that activities of daily living can be performed safely.

_Qd5Ap0.title: Immersion pulmonary edema
_Qd5Ap0.description: A type of pulmonary edema that is precipitated by immersion in water (e.g., diving or swimming) and is characterized by the rapid onset of dyspnea, cough, and/or hemoptysis. It is thought to be due to blood redistribution from the legs and abdomen to the lungs.

0jde_p0.title: Humanitarian use device
0jde_p0.description: A medical device intended to treat conditions affecting 8,000 or fewer individuals in the USA a year. Because of the difficulty of running trials able to recruit enough participants with these conditions, the threshold for efficacy required for approval by the FDA is much lower, with the standard set as a probable benefit to health, which outweighs the risk of harm.

ajdQ_p0.title: Sodium phenylbutyrate/taurursodiol
ajdQ_p0.description: A combination medication composed of sodium phenylbutyrate/taurursodiol. Previously used to treat amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. No longer commercially available in the US.

Xjd9_p0.title: Drug holiday
Xjd9_p0.description: Temporary discontinuation of pharmacological therapy under medical supervision. Used to reduce side effects and prevent tolerance from developing.

djdozp0.title: Central neuromodulators
djdozp0.description: A group of drugs used to treat conditions with gut-brain dysregulation (i.e., functional gastrointestinal disorders). Central neuromodulators alter the concentration or activity of neurotransmitters like serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine. Examples include selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, tricyclic antidepressants, and atypical antipsychotics.

VjdGzp0.title: Parasite
VjdGzp0.description: A symbiotic organism that lives on or in a larger organism (host) in order to feed, develop, and/or multiply, causing harm to the host in the process.

fjdk-p0.title: Intraretinal hemorrhage
fjdk-p0.description: The extravasation of blood between the layers of the retina (inner and outer plexiform layers). As a result of intraretinal compression, the hemorrhages form dot or blot-like shapes.

destinations.label: Diseases of the retina → Vascular diseases of the retina

gjdF-p0.title: Venous beading
gjdF-p0.description: A nonspecific sign of retinal ischemia seen on fundoscopy. Irregular dilation and constriction of the venules in the retina leads to a string of beads appearance.

jjd_ZJ0.title: Finger splint
jjd_ZJ0.description: An upper extremity splint used to immobilize the interphalangeal joints of the fingers. Can be placed on the dorsal and/or volar aspects of the finger and encompass the joints proximal and distal to the injury. Indicated for fractures, dislocations, and tendinous injuries of the fingers.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

PjdW0J0.title: Thumb spica
PjdW0J0.description: A type of splint or cast used to immobilize the thumb and wrist while allowing the other fingers freedom of motion. Extends from the distal phalanx of the thumb to the proximal third of the forearm along the radial aspect with the wrist dorsiflexed at 20° and the thumb abducted. Indicated for soft tissue injuries and/or fractures of the thumb and wrist (e.g., scaphoid fractures).

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

4jd30J0.title: Sugar tong forearm splint
4jd30J0.description: An upper extremity splint used to immobilize the wrist and prevent supination and pronation of the forearm. Extends along the dorsal and volar aspects of the forearm in a U-shape that encircles the elbow, which is flexed at 90°, and ends just proximal to the MCP joints on both sides. Indications include wrist and/or forearm fractures.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

kjdm0J0.title: Coaptation splint
kjdm0J0.description: An upper extremity splint used to immobilize the humerus while allowing forearm pronation and supination. Extends along the lateral and medial upper arm in a U-shape from the axilla back to the top of the shoulder, encircling the elbow, which is flexed at 90°. Indicated for humeral shaft fractures.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

OjdI0J0.title: Posterior ankle splint
OjdI0J0.description: A lower extremity splint used to immobilize the ankle and foot, preventing flexion and extension. Extends from the plantar surface of the metatarsal heads along the posterior leg to the level of the fibular head, with the ankle in 90° flexion. Indicated for severe ankle sprains, isolated malleolar fractures, and foot fractures.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Lower extremities

ljdv0J0.title: Anterior-posterior ankle splint
ljdv0J0.description: A lower-extremity splint used to immobilize the ankle and foot. Consists of a posterior ankle splint plus an anterior slab extending from the dorsum of the foot at the MTP joints to the level of the fibular head, with the ankle in 90° flexion. Provides additional immobilization for severe ankle injuries.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Lower extremities

Njd-0J0.title: Stirrup splint
Njd-0J0.description: A lower-extremity splint used to immobilize the ankle and foot, preventing eversion and inversion. Extends from the lateral mid-calf, encircling the heel, to the medial mid-calf, with the ankle flexed at 90°. Indications include ankle sprains and isolated, nondisplaced malleolar fractures. Can be combined with posterior ankle splints to add stability to unstable ankle fractures.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Lower extremities

mjdVaJ0.title: Walking boot
mjdVaJ0.description: A prefabricated removable medical boot designed for weight-bearing while limiting movement at the ankle joint. Used primarily in the treatment of stable uncomplicated ankle fractures and soft tissue injuries of the ankle and foot.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Lower extremities

MjdMaJ0.title: PRP
MjdMaJ0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Platelet rich plasma
2) Panretinal photocoagulation

njd7aJ0.title: Brief FiGHTS score
njd7aJ0.description: A validated screening tool to estimate the risk of firearm carriage in adolescents. One point is given for each of the following: being in a physical Fight in the past year; Gender (men); needing medical care for being Hurt in a physical fight in the past year; being Threatened or injured with a weapon on school property in the past year; and ever smoking ≥ 1 cigarette daily for ≥ 30 days. A score of ≥ 2 indicates an increased risk for carrying a firearm.

pjdLYJ0.title: Buried bumper syndrome
pjdLYJ0.description: A condition in which the internal bumper of the gastrostomy tube erodes into the gastric wall, becoming lodged between the gastric and abdominal walls. Often caused by excessive external traction on the internal bumper.

JjdsYJ0.title: Large volume paracentesis
JjdsYJ0.description: The removal of > 5 L of fluid from peritoneum during one procedure.

FjdgXJ0.title: Clinical features of hypervolemia
FjdgXJ0.description: A collection of signs suggestive of volume overload. Includes weight gain, jugular venous distension, peripheral edema, and crackles on pulmonary auscultation (suggestive of pulmonary edema).

Ejd8XJ0.title: CKD stage 1
Ejd8XJ0.description: The presence of kidney damage and a normal or elevated eGFR (i.e., eGFR > 90 mL/min/1.73 m2).

vjdAXJ0.title: CKD stage 3
vjdAXJ0.description: The presence of kidney damage and a decreased eGFR that is divided into two subcategories: G3a (i.e., eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m2) and G3b (i.e., eGFR 30-44 mL/min/1.73 m2).

Djd1cJ0.title: CKD stage 2
Djd1cJ0.description: The presence of kidney damage and a mildly decreased eGFR (i.e.,: eGFR 60-89 mL/min/1.73 m2).

wjdhcJ0.title: CKD stage 5
wjdhcJ0.description: The presence of kidney failure with a severely decreased eGFR (i.e., eGFR < 15 mL/min/1.73 m2).

9jdNcJ0.title: CKD stage 4
9jdNcJ0.description: The presence of kidney damage and a severely decreased eGFR (i.e., eGFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73 m2).

xjdEcJ0.title: Skeletal traction
xjdEcJ0.description: The application of a pulling force to part of the body to align bones or joints (e.g., to reduce fractures or dislocations), or to stretch muscles and reduce spasms (e.g., cervical muscle traction).

yjdd1J0.title: CoA
yjdd1J0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Coarctation of the aorta
2) Coenzyme A

AjdR1J0.title: Chlorine intoxication
AjdR1J0.description: A condition caused by exposure to chlorine, which is found in several household cleaning products (e.g., laundry detergent, pool disinfectant) and is used in various industries (e.g., papermaking, textiles, paint). Exposure can lead to irritation of the mucous membranes (e.g., lacrimation, throat irritation), the respiratory system (e.g., dyspnea, cyanosis, cough), and the autonomic nervous system (e.g., tachycardia, nausea, vomiting).

aPdQWJ0.title: Blast-induced otologic injury
aPdQWJ0.description: An ear injury caused by the overpressure wave (blast wave) created by an explosion. Tympanic membrane rupture is the most common injury. Symptoms include hearing loss, ear pain, tinnitus, and vertigo.

XPd9WJ0.title: Developmental delay
XPd9WJ0.description: A delay in the age at which children are expected to reach developmental milestones

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Overview of abnormal development

cPdadJ0.title: Endotenon
cPdadJ0.description: A thin layer of connective tissue that surrounds individual tendon fascicles of a tendon.

1Pd2dJ0.title: Epitenon
1Pd2dJ0.description: A layer of loose connective tissue that surrounds the tendon fascicles and endotenon of a tendon.

WPdPdJ0.title: Paratenon
WPdPdJ0.description: A loose connective tissue septa that radiates from the epitenon and carries nerves and blood vessels between the tendon fascicles of a tendon.

dPdodJ0.title: Arachidonic acid-prostaglandin pathway
dPdodJ0.description: A metabolic pathway in which arachidonic acid is converted by cyclooxygenases into a precursor (prostaglandin H₂) for the biosynthesis of other prostaglandins, leukotrienes, and thromboxanes.

VPdGdJ0.title: Neuropathic ulcer
VPdGdJ0.description: An open wound on the foot or toes caused by a loss of peripheral sensation leading to repetitive trauma and tissue damage. Causes include diabetes, other causes of peripheral neuropathy, and foot deformities.

media.title: Features of arterial, venous, and neuropathic ulcers

UPdbVJ0.title: Acute hemorrhagic erosive gastropathy
UPdbVJ0.description: A direct injury of the gastric mucosa that can be caused by alcohol, caffeine, certain drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aspirin) or supplements (e.g., iron, potassium), corrosive substances (e.g., acids, disinfectants), or ischemic injury (e.g., due to hypovolemia, sepsis, or severe burns). Affected individuals typically develop symptoms of gastritis, nausea/vomiting, and upper gastrointestinal tract bleeding (e.g., hematemesis).

fPdkVJ0.title: Hemivertebra
fPdkVJ0.description: A vertebral anomaly characterized by a lack of formation of one half of a vertebral body. Associated with OEIS syndrome, VACTERL syndrome, and diabetes mellitus in pregnancy.

hPdceJ0.title: Stranger anxiety
hPdceJ0.description: A normal developmental stage in which an infant or young child is fearful of unknown individuals. Manifests with crying and/or clinging to a known caregiver when around strangers. Typically lasts from 6 months to 2 years of age.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Common developmental behaviors

3PdSeJ0.title: Developmental separation anxiety
3PdSeJ0.description: A normal developmental stage in which an infant or young child is afraid to be separated from their caregiver. Manifests with crying and/or clinging if the caregiver tries to leave and often continued crying after the caregiver has left. Typically peaks between 9-18 months and resolves by 3 years of age.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Common developmental behaviors

RPdleJ0.title: Tissue adhesive
RPdleJ0.description: An adhesive that can be used to repair small, superficial wounds in which the wound edges can be approximated without tension, or in addition to other wound closure techniques.

QPdueJ0.title: Double-J stent
QPdueJ0.description: A thin hollow tube with two looped ends containing multiple holes. Allows for the drainage of fluid and is commonly placed in the ureter for urinary drainage in urolithiasis. The loops on both ends prevent stent migration.

mPdV2J0.title: Purging
mPdV2J0.description: A type of inappropriate weight compensatory behavior in which an individual deliberately expels food and/or fluids from their body. May include self-induced vomiting and/or misuse of medications (i.e., laxatives, diuretics). Can occur in multiple types of eating disorders.

oPd0fJ0.title: Chronic wound
oPd0fJ0.description: Wounds that do not begin to heal (e.g., ≥ 50% reduction in wound surface area within 4 weeks) or that do not completely heal within the expected time frame (typically 12 weeks) despite appropriate care.

pPdLfJ0.title: Occult hip fracture
pPdLfJ0.description: A hip fracture not detected on hip x-ray. Clinical features consistent with a hip fracture (e.g., new inability to ambulate, pain with range of motion of the hip, tenderness) may be present.

qPdCfJ0.title: Catch-up growth
qPdCfJ0.description: A period of rapid growth that is seen in children recovering from growth faltering, allowing them to attain an acceptable weight-for-length and/or BMI-for-age z score. This period is facilitated by rapid weight gain (which is often 2-3 times the average rate of weight gain per age).

sPdtTJ0.title: Penile intraepithelial neoplasia
sPdtTJ0.description: A precancerous penile lesion caused by dysplasia of squamous cells, marked with varying degrees of atypia. The epithelial basement membrane is intact and the lesion is, therefore, not invasive (but has invasive potential). Risk factors include HPV infection, lichen planus, balanitis, and immunosuppression.

GPdBTJ0.title: Perianal intraepithelial neoplasia
GPdBTJ0.description: A precancerous perianal lesion caused by dysplasia of squamous cells, marked with varying degrees of atypia. The epithelial basement membrane is intact and the lesion is, therefore, not invasive (but has invasive potential). Risk factors include HPV infection, lichen planus, balanitis, and immunosuppression.

tPdXgJ0.title: Anal intraepithelial neoplasia
tPdXgJ0.description: A premalignant squamous lesion of the anal mucosa, most often caused by persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, particularly HPV 16. Its high-grade form, high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (corresponds to AIN grades II–III), is the direct precursor to anal cancer and is especially prevalent in groups at high risk, such as people living with HIV.

uPdpgJ0.title: Nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists
uPdpgJ0.description: A subgroup of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) with a lower risk of hyperkalemia and hormonal side effects than steroidal MRAs. Used to treat cardiorenal disease (i.e., in type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease). Examples include finerenone and esaxerenone.

CPdqSJ0.title: Phototoxic agent
CPdqSJ0.description: A drug or plant compound that causes a photosensitivity reaction after exposure to ultraviolet radiation. Previous sensitization to the agent is not necessary. Examples include systemic drugs (e.g., tetracycline), topical drugs (e.g., hydrocortisone), sunscreen (e.g., those containing cinnamates), or plants (e.g., celery, lime).

_Pd5hJ0.title: Enhanced recovery after surgery
_Pd5hJ0.description: A multimodal perioperative care pathway that improves recovery and reduces the risk of serious adverse effects after major surgery. Key elements of the pathway include optimal pain management, early mobility, and minimal interruption in enteral intake.

Z4dZ3J0.title: Men who have sex with women
Z4dZ3J0.description: A term used to describe men who engage in sexual activity with women only.

04de3J0.title: Care plan
04de3J0.description: A summary of a patient's medical conditions, goals of care, and any agreed-upon treatment protocols. Typically created, maintained, and documented by the treating team through shared decision-making and tailored to individual patient needs and preferences.

a4dQ3J0.title: Phototest
a4dQ3J0.description: A collection of studies that assess the reaction of the skin when exposed to UV radiation. Methods include minimal erythema dose testing, provocation phototesting, and photopatch testing. Indications include primary photodermatoses, solar urticaria, and allergic contact dermatitis.

Y4dn3J0.title: March fracture
Y4dn3J0.description: A stress fracture of the metatarsals, most commonly at the second metatarsal neck. Commonly seen in athletes and new military recruits.

b4dH3J0.title: Low-risk stress fractures
b4dH3J0.description: A stress fracture in a location associated with a lower risk of healing complications (e.g., fracture progression, nonunion, delayed healing). These sites include the 1st–4th metatarsal shafts, fibula, lateral malleolus, medial femoral neck, calcaneus, cuneiform, and cuboid.

W4dPRJ0.title: Antegrade pyelography
W4dPRJ0.description: An imaging test (x-ray) that uses contrast injected into the renal pelvis to visualize filling defects in the upper urinary tract due to obstruction (e.g., due to a stricture, stone, or tumor).

V4dGRJ0.title: Photoprovocation test
V4dGRJ0.description: A test that aims to reproduce photodermatoses by repeatedly exposing a patient to fixed doses of UV radiation for a period of at least 3 days.

f4dkiJ0.title: Periprosthetic fracture
f4dkiJ0.description: A fracture associated with an orthopedic implant used for joint arthroplasty or fracture fixation. The most common fracture sites are the hip and knee.

destinations.label: General principles of fractures → Subtypes and variants

h4dcQJ0.title: Field block
h4dcQJ0.description: The infiltration of local anesthetic in a circumferential border around a surgical field. Results in anesthesia of the surgical field without disrupting the anatomy.

j4d_QJ0.title: Harris axial view
j4d_QJ0.description: An x-ray view of the foot that provides good visualization of the talocalcaneal joint. The sole of the foot is held perpendicular to the long axis of the leg and the x-ray beam is directed at the sole of the foot at a 45° angle.

M4dMPJ0.title: Diabetic macular edema
M4dMPJ0.description: A form of diabetic retinopathy characterized by macular edema and/or hard exudates. Diabetic maculopathy is the most common cause of vision loss in diabetic patients.

destinations.label: Diabetic retinopathy → Overview of diabetic retinopathy

H4dKkJ0.title: Bulky compression dressing
H4dKkJ0.description: A type of lower extremity dressing that is used for postoperative control of edema or for injuries to the lower extremity. Consists of several layers of fluffy batting wrapped around the affected area followed by an elastic bandage.

F4dgOJ0.title: Conjunctival limbal autograft
F4dgOJ0.description: A tissue transplantation procedure in which limbal and conjunctival tissue is resected from one part of the eye and placed in another part of the same eye or the other eye of the same person. Indications include chronic inflammation, chemical or thermal trauma, pterygium, and ocular surface squamous neoplasia.

84dOOJ0.title: Bare sclera excision
84dOOJ0.description: A surgical technique used in pterygium surgery in which the pterygium and affected conjunctiva are resected and the sclera is left exposed to reepithelialize. Associated with a high risk of pterygium recurrence.

1kd25J0.title: Central herniation
1kd25J0.description: Downward displacement of the diencephalon, midbrain, and pons through the tentorial notch. A subtype of descending transtentorial herniation. Clinical manifestations include brain stem dysfunction, oculomotor nerve palsy, and Duret hemorrhages.

destinations.label: Elevated intracranial pressure and brain herniation → Subtypes and variants

dkdo5J0.title: Persistent hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia
dkdo5J0.description: A condition characterized by dysregulated insulin secretion, which results in persistent hypoglycemia. Symptoms typically manifest within 72 hours after birth.

ekdx5J0.title: Uncus
ekdx5J0.description: A hook-shaped limbic structure located in the anterior part of the parahippocampal gyrus, which is a part of the medial temporal lobe of the brain. Functions of the uncus include olfaction, emotion, and memory.

UkdbMJ0.title: Pericallosal artery
UkdbMJ0.description: A distal continuation of the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) that goes over the superior aspect of the corpus callosum in the pericallosal cistern. Supplies the corpus callosum and the medial aspect of the cerebral hemispheres.

2kdTMJ0.title: Food protein-induced enteropathy
2kdTMJ0.description: A non-IgE-mediated food allergy primarily seen in infants. Caused by non-IgE-mediated inflammation of the small bowel in response to food proteins (e.g., milk protein). Symptoms typically include malabsorption, intermittent vomiting, prolonged diarrhea, and failure to thrive. Treatment involves the removal of offending protein from the infant's diet.

SkdyMJ0.title: Viloxazine
SkdyMJ0.description: A selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor primarily used in the management of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Adverse effects include somnolence, decreased appetite, and fatigue.

ikdJnJ0.title: Ocular syphilis
ikdJnJ0.description: An ocular complication of syphilis infection that can occur at any stage of disease, potentially leading to permanent vision loss. The most common manifestation is panuveitis; conjunctivitis, keratitis, and retinal vasculitis may also be present.

5kdioJ0.title: Breakthrough pain
5kdioJ0.description: A sudden increase in pain occurring spontaneously or as a result of an event (e.g., mobilizing) despite a baseline of adequately controlled chronic pain.

qkdCKJ0.title: Z-track technique
qkdCKJ0.description: A technique to minimize fluid leakage following paracentesis or intramuscular drug administration. The skin is pulled ~ 2 cm prior to needle insertion and released only after needle entry into the peritoneum (during paracentesis) or completion of the intramuscular injection. The skin returns to its original position, sealing the site of needle insertion, which prevents fluid from leaking out of the peritoneal cavity or muscle.

7kd46J0.title: Parallel group
7kd46J0.description: An experimental study design in which participants remain within their assigned groups for the entire duration of the study.

GkdB6J0.title: Hemorrhagic ascites
GkdB6J0.description: The presence of ascitic fluid in the peritoneal cavity with an RBC count > 50,000 mm³. Etiologies include peritoneal carcinomatosis and iatrogenic causes (e.g., trauma following paracentesis or biopsy in patients with cirrhosis).

xkdEJJ0.title: Suboptimally dated gestational age
xkdEJJ0.description: A gestational age that was not confirmed or adjusted using ultrasound before 22 0/7 weeks of gestation.

BkdzJJ0.title: Cervical ripening
BkdzJJ0.description: A process of cervical softening, dilatation, and thinning in preparation for labor and delivery. This occurs either naturally via hormonal changes or is expedited with pharmacologic or mechanical stimulation. The Bishop score is used to assess cervical ripeness.

_kd5qJ0.title: Risk factors for opioid-related harm
_kd5qJ0.description: Factors that increase the risk of adverse effects of opioids include age over 65 years, pregnancy, hepatic or renal impairment, a history of substance misuse, previous overdose, comorbid mental health conditions, sleep-disordered breathing, and polypharmacy (increases the risk of drug-drug interactions).

destinations.label: Opioids → Risk factors for opioid-related harm

-kdDqJ0.title: Retained antrum syndrome
