-kdDqJ0.description: A rare cause of hypergastrinemia. Occurs because of incomplete excision of the gastric antrum during gastrectomy.

aOdQIJ0.title: Risk factors for pediatric hearing loss
aOdQIJ0.description: A set of factors associated with early pediatric hearing loss. Includes congenital TORCH infections, congenital malformations of the skull and ear (e.g., microtia), hospitalization > 5 days in a neonatal intensive care unit, prolonged use of ototoxic medications (e.g., chemotherapy, aminoglycosides), meningitis or encephalitis, head trauma, recurrent otitis media, and a family history of childhood hearing loss.

bOdHIJ0.title: CDC longitudinal growth charts for the 5th to 95th percentile
bOdHIJ0.description: A chart that shows the percentile curves for age-dependent physical growth, either by stature and body weight or by body mass index. Used for individuals between 2 and 20 years of age.

media.title: Body mass index-for-age percentiles (female individuals 2–20 years; 5ᵗʰ–95ᵗʰ percentiles)
Stature- and weight-for-age percentiles (female individuals 2–20 years; 5ᵗʰ–95ᵗʰ percentiles)
Stature- and weight-for-age percentiles (male individuals 2–20 years; 5ᵗʰ–95ᵗʰ percentiles)
Body mass index-for-age percentiles (male individuals 2–20 years; 5ᵗʰ–95ᵗʰ percentiles)

WOdPrJ0.title: Functional hypoparathyroidism
WOdPrJ0.description: Reversible parathyroid dysfunction caused by either hypermagnesemia, which can suppress PTH synthesis, or hypomagnesemia, which can increase PTH resistance.

TOd67J0.title: Protodeclarative pointing
TOd67J0.description: The act of pointing at an object or activity to draw the attention of another person. Typically present by 18 months of age. The absence of protodeclarative pointing after 18 months of age is a red flag for autism spectrum disorder.

SOdy7J0.title: Signs of vascular injury
SOdy7J0.description: Clinical features suggesting injury to an artery or vein. Typically includes one or more of the following: weakened distal pulses, palpable thrill, pulsatile hemorrhage, expanding hematoma, and distal pain, pallor, paresthesia, poikilothermia, or paralysis.

lOdvsJ0.title: Delayed emergence
lOdvsJ0.description: Inability to regain full consciousness 30-60 minutes after general anesthesia. Typically caused by the residual effect of one more perioperative agents (e.g., opioids, benzodiazepines, propofol, muscle relaxants) due to factors, such as dosing errors, drug interactions, hypothermia, underlying conditions (e.g., liver or kidney dysfunction), or metabolic alterations (e.g., hypoglycemia, electrolyte imbalances).

destinations.label: Procedural sedation and analgesia → Recovery and discharge

NOd-sJ0.title: Early pregnancy loss
NOd-sJ0.description: An intrauterine pregnancy of < 13 weeks' gestation that is not viable, as evidenced by ultrasonography showing a lack of fetal cardiac activity or an empty gestational sac.

mOdVGJ0.title: Size-date discrepancy
mOdVGJ0.description: A discrepancy between the gestational age as estimated by measurement of embryonic, fetal, or uterine size and the gestational age as estimated based on the last menstrual period.

rOdfFJ0.title: Indications for HIV PrEP
rOdfFJ0.description: A collection of factors that place individuals at a sufficiently elevated risk of HIV that preexposure prophylaxis is recommended. Includes individuals who inject drugs and demonstrate high-risk behaviors (e.g., needle sharing, HIV-positive injection partner), and those who have been sexually active in the past 6 months (vaginal or anal sex) with an HIV-positive partner, had unprotected sex with a partner of unknown HIV status, or been diagnosed with a bacterial STI in the past 6 months.

7Od4FJ0.title: Newborn hearing screen
7Od4FJ0.description: A screening procedure to detect congenital hearing loss in newborns. Tests include otoacoustic emissions (OAE) or automated auditory brainstem response (AABR). Newborns who fail the newborn hearing screen must have a full audiology evaluation by 3 months of age.

HOdKFJ0.title: Indications for HIV PEP
HOdKFJ0.description: A collection of circumstances involving a high-risk exposure to the HIV virus. Includes injury from HIV-contaminated instruments (e.g., needlestick injury), unprotected sex with an individual with HIV, and exposure of an open wound or mucus membrane to HIV-contaminated bodily fluids.

GOdBFJ0.title: Undersensing
GOdBFJ0.description: The failure of a pacemaker device to sense cardiac depolarizations, leading to the delivery of inappropriate impulses by the pulse generator.

tOdX8J0.title: Oversensing
tOdX8J0.description: The sensing of inappropriate stimuli by a cardiac implantable electronic device leading to an undesirable response. In permanent pacemakers, expected pulse generation can be inhibited. In implantable cardioverter defibrillators, shocks may be delivered unnecessarily.

FOdg8J0.title: Failure to capture
FOdg8J0.description: The inability of a pacemaker device to achieve mechanical capture.

uOdp8J0.title: Long arm anterior-posterior splint
uOdp8J0.description: An upper extremity splint used to immobilize both the elbow and wrist joints. Involves placing one plaster or fiberglass slab along the posterior (dorsal) aspect of the arm, extending from the midarm to the midpalmar region, plus another anterior (volar) slab to further stabilize the forearm. The elbow is flexed at 90° and the wrist is in a neutral position. Indicated for unstable forearm injuries (e.g. combined radius and ulna fractures).

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

BOdzuJ0.title: Patient Health Questionnaire for Adolescents
BOdzuJ0.description: A long questionnaire used to identify potential psychiatric disorders in adolescents, including major depressive disorder, dysthymia, generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, and substance misuse or dependence. In primary care settings, parts of this tool may be used to screen for a particular diagnosis of concern; the screen for major depressive disorder is commonly used.

dldoDJ0.title: Ballard score
dldoDJ0.description: A physical examination that is performed on newborns shortly after delivery to estimate gestational age. Using the New Ballard Score, six physical characteristics and six neuromuscular findings are assigned a score from -1 to 5. After adding the scores, the final value may range from -10 to 50; -10 corresponds to a gestational age of 20 weeks, whereas 50 corresponds to a gestational age of 44 weeks.

fldkwJ0.title: Left uterine displacement
fldkwJ0.description: The manual displacement of a gravid uterus in the left lateral direction to relieve aortocaval compression. Used in the management of hypotension and/or cardiac arrest in pregnancy.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Special patient groups

jld_9J0.title: Shunt series
jld_9J0.description: A series of plain radiographs of the course of a cerebral shunt, including views of the skull, neck, chest, and abdomen. Used to evaluate the integrity of a cerebral shunt in patients with suspected malfunction.

nld7xJ0.title: Dichotomized Constans score
nld7xJ0.description: Tool for the assessment of pretest probability for upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT). One point is given for each of the following: venous material (e.g., central venous catheter, pacemaker lead), unilateral edema, and localized pain. One point is subtracted if another diagnosis is at least equally plausible. A score ≤ 1: UEDVT unlikely; a score ≥ 2: UEDVT likely.

destinations.label: Deep vein thrombosis → Subtypes and variants

LldwxJ0.title: Midline catheter
LldwxJ0.description: A venous access device that is inserted in the upper extremity and terminates in the axillary vein. A midline catheter is typically about 20 cm in length.

destinations.label: Vascular access → Overview of vascular access

old0BJ0.title: Secondary upper extremity vein thrombosis
old0BJ0.description: A deep vein thrombosis of the upper extremity due to an indwelling device in the vein (e.g., central venous catheter) or a hypercoagulable state (e.g., malignancy).

destinations.label: Deep vein thrombosis → Subtypes and variants

GldByJ0.title: Mammary candidiasis
GldByJ0.description: A fungal infection of the breast that is typically caused by Candida albicans and commonly associated with breastfeeding.

tldXAJ0.title: Breastfeeding dyad
tldXAJ0.description: An intimate physical, psychological, and emotional bond between the breastfeeding parent and child.

vldAAJ0.title: Pediatric vision risk assessment
vldAAJ0.description: A set of factors that increase a child's risk of vision impairment and/or loss. Includes an abnormal eye examination, prior abnormal visual acuity testing, a 1st-degree relative with eye disorders and/or early use of glasses, and an abnormal ocular history from caregiver or child (e.g., reported unusual appearance of the eye(s), difficulty seeing near or far, crossing or asymmetric movement of the eyes, or an injury to the eye).

Dld1_J0.title: MCHAT
Dld1_J0.description: An autism screening tool validated for use in children between 16 and 30 months of age that assesses comprehension, communication, social skills, and behavior. Children who screen positive require further evaluation for autism spectrum disorder.

wldh_J0.title: Mucosal melanoma
wldh_J0.description: A rare type of melanoma that originates from melanocytes in mucosal membranes, most commonly in the head and neck and the anorectal and female genital regions.

eNdxZq0.title: Transitional neonatal hypoglycemia
eNdxZq0.description: A normal physiological drop in a newborn's plasma glucose levels by up to 30 mg/dL within the first 2 hours of life, to a median concentration of approximately 55 mg/dL. Plasma glucose typically increases to a normal level of 80–85 mg/dL within 72 hours of birth.

destinations.label: Overview of neonatal conditions → Neonatal hypoglycemia

TNd60q0.title: Wet-to-dry dressing
TNd60q0.description: A wet dressing (e.g., saline-moistened gauze) that is directly placed on a wound, covered with dry gauze, and left to dry. Wound drainage and dead tissue are removed along with the dried dressing (i.e., mechanical debridement).

SNdy0q0.title: Hyperglycemia tests
SNdy0q0.description: A group of tests used to screen for and/or diagnose diabetes mellitus. Considered diagnostic if ≥ 2 results are abnormal in an asymptomatic patient or a random blood glucose level is abnormal in a patient with symptoms of hyperglycemia. Abnormal results include random blood glucose level ≥ 200 mg/dL, blood glucose level ≥ 200 mg/dL 2 hours after oral glucose tolerance testing, fasting blood glucose level ≥ 126 mg/dL, and hemoglobin A1c ≥ 6.5%.

hNdcaq0.title: Symptoms of pulmonary congestion
hNdcaq0.description: A collection of symptoms that result from the accumulation of fluid in the lungs (e.g., due to left-sided heart failure). Includes dyspnea (including paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea), orthopnea, and symptoms of cardiac asthma (e.g., wheezing, coughing). Bilateral crackles may be present on auscultation.

RNdlaq0.title: Proximal upper extremity deep vein thrombosis
RNdlaq0.description: Thrombosis of the axillary or subclavian vein.

destinations.label: Deep vein thrombosis → Subtypes and variants

iNdJaq0.title: Distal upper extremity deep vein thrombosis
iNdJaq0.description: Thrombosis of the brachial, radial, ulnar, or interosseus veins. Often asymptomatic. Treatment is usually only required in symptomatic patients.

destinations.label: Deep vein thrombosis → Subtypes and variants

QNduaq0.title: Eustachian tube dysfunction
QNduaq0.description: An impairment of the opening and closing of the eustachian tube (ET) that may result in a buildup of fluid in the middle ear and impaired hearing. Types of ET dysfunction include obstructive ET dysfunction, in which the ET does not open properly, and patulous ET dysfunction, in which the ET remains open. Symptoms may include hearing loss, ear pressure or fullness, and/or ear pain.

jNd_aq0.title: High ankle sprain
jNd_aq0.description: A sprain of the syndesmotic ligaments that connect the tibia and fibula in the lower leg. Usually caused by excessive external rotation of the foot and leg.

PNdWYq0.title: Cuboid syndrome
PNdWYq0.description: A type of foot sprain that involves a minor disruption or subluxation of the calcaneocuboid ligament near the midtarsal joint. Typically manifests as lateral foot pain after an inversion injury of the foot and ankle.

MNdMbq0.title: Persistent neonatal hypoglycemia
MNdMbq0.description: Low plasma glucose levels (< 50 mg/dL) in a newborn that persist beyond the first 48 hours of life. Usually associated with congenital conditions, such as Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, congenital hypopituitarism, and congenital hyperinsulinism. Screening should occur between 48-72 hours of life to exclude transitional neonatal hypoglycemia.

destinations.label: Overview of neonatal conditions → Neonatal hypoglycemia

nNd7bq0.title: Veress needle
nNd7bq0.description: A sharp needle with an inserted blunt stylet. Used to access the peritoneal cavity and create pneumoperitoneum during laparoscopic surgery.

LNdwbq0.title: Relative rest
LNdwbq0.description: The modification of daily activity and exercises during rehabilitation in order to minimize aggravation of the injured area while avoiding deconditioning and disuse atrophy.

qNdCXq0.title: Risk factors for developmental disorders in children with otitis media with effusion
qNdCXq0.description: A collection of factors that increase a child's risk for adverse developmental outcomes after developing otitis media with effusion. Includes conditions affecting eustachian tube position and drainage (Down syndrome, craniofacial abnormalities, cleft palate) as well as developmental, social, or behavioral disorders (e.g., autism spectrum disorder and neurodevelopmental disorders).

destinations.label: Otitis media with effusion → Clinical features

INdYcq0.title: Distal tibiofibular syndesmosis
INdYcq0.description: A fibrous joint where the tibia and fibula are connected by the distal anterior tibiofibular ligament, distal posterior tibiofibular ligament, transverse ligament, and interosseous ligament.

sNdtcq0.title: Peritoneal fluid analysis
sNdtcq0.description: The analysis of fluid that accumulates within the peritoneal cavity. Components include gross appearance, total protein, the serum-ascites albumin gradient, cell counts, bacterial cultures, PCR, and concentrations of lactate dehydrogenase, glucose, amylase, and adenosine deaminase.

FNdg1q0.title: Red flags for pediatric fever
FNdg1q0.description: Clinical features in febrile children that are consistent with life-threatening illness. Includes an ill appearance, signs of sepsis, signs of respiratory distress, petechial rash or signs of meningitis, and seizures (excluding simple febrile seizures).

8NdO1q0.title: Risk factors for hypertrophic scars and keloids
8NdO1q0.description: Factors that increase an individual's risk of developing hypertrophic scars and keloids. Examples include surgical incisions, deep partial-thickness burns, and lacerations.

destinations.label: Hypertrophic scars and keloids → Risk factors

BNdzWq0.title: Individuals at risk for poliovirus
BNdzWq0.description: Includes individuals living or visiting endemic regions, laboratory workers working with specimens that may contain polioviruses, close contacts of individuals who may be infected with the poliovirus, and unvaccinated or undervaccinated adults whose children will be receiving oral poliovirus vaccine.

yNdddq0.title: Evidence of immunity to mumps, measles, rubella
yNdddq0.description: A set of criteria used to determine the need for vaccination against measles, mumps, and/or rubella. The following are considered evidence of immunity: being born before 1957; evidence of MMR or MMRV vaccination (for measles and mumps: appropriate doses based on age and risk level; for rubella: at least one dose at ≥ 12 months of age); or laboratory evidence of immunity (i.e., antibody titers) or prior infection (e.g., PCR).

cmdaeq0.title: Klebsiella aerogenes
cmdaeq0.description: A gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic rod that belongs to the family of Enterobacteriaceae. Part of the intestinal flora.

dmdoeq0.title: Triangular fibrocartilage complex sprain
dmdoeq0.description: An injury of the triangular fibrocartilage complex, which connects the radius, ulna, lunate, and triquetrum and provides stability to the wrist. Usually caused by forced ulnar deviance. Clinical features include pain along the ulnar side of the wrist, decreased range of motion, and reduced grip strength.

VmdGeq0.title: Lunate fracture
VmdGeq0.description: An uncommon carpal fracture, most commonly caused by a fall onto an outstretched hand. Frequently accompanied by dislocation and/or other carpal fractures. Orthopedic consultation is recommended.

emdxeq0.title: Dorsal intercalated segment instability
emdxeq0.description: A form of scapholunate instability characterized by abnormal extension of the lunate. Common causes include fall on an outstretched hand, congenital ligament laxity, and repetitive stress (e.g., walking with crutch support). Clinical features include pain with wrist extension, weakness, and tenderness over the scapholunate joint. Lateral x-ray typically shows an abnormal scapholunate angle.

UmdbUq0.title: Volar intercalated segment instability
UmdbUq0.description: A form of wrist instability characterized by abnormal volar rotation of the lunate. Typically occurs as a complication of lunotriquetral ligament injury that causes disruption of the radiocarpal (particularly ulnocarpal) ligaments. Clinical features include nonspecific wrist pain and a clunking sensation with ulnar deviation of the wrist.

gmdFUq0.title: Diuretic misuse
gmdFUq0.description: The improper use of diuretics (e.g., for weight loss). May be seen in individuals with bulimia nervosa and anorexia nervosa as a purging behavior. Can result in dehydration, orthostatic hypotension, and electrolyte abnormalities (e.g., hyponatremia, hypokalemia).

3mdS2q0.title: Elbow fracture
3mdS2q0.description: A fracture of one or more bones that comprise the elbow joint. Can include distal humerus fractures, radial head fractures, coronoid process fractures, and olecranon fractures.

PmdWfq0.title: Combination vaccines
PmdWfq0.description: A vaccine that contains more than one antigen to protect against multiple diseases with a single injection. Includes the DTaP vaccine, DTaP-HepB-IPV vaccine, DTaP-IPV-Hib vaccine, MMR vaccine, MMRV vaccine, DTaP-IPV vaccine, and Tdap vaccine.

kmdmfq0.title: Catch-up vaccination schedule
kmdmfq0.description: A vaccination schedule used for children and adolescents who are > 1 month behind the recommended age-appropriate vaccination schedule. For partially vaccinated individuals, catching up with the next dose in the immunization series is recommended; do not restart the series.

media.title: ACIP catch-up immunization schedule: children and adolescents ≤ 18 years of age

OmdIfq0.title: Vaccine Information Statement
OmdIfq0.description: An information sheet produced by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) that discusses the benefits and risks for a particular vaccine. In the United States, it is federally required to provide Vaccine Information Statements for every vaccine an individual will receive.

lmdvfq0.title: Z-plasty
lmdvfq0.description: A surgical technique used to increase the length of a scar, especially a contracted scar, to reduce tension, camouflage the scar, or change the direction of the scar to better align with skin lines. This is accomplished by creating two triangular flaps in a Z shape, which are then transposed to create a new scar direction.

Nmd-fq0.title: Surgical taping
Nmd-fq0.description: The use of paper tape across a wound or incision that has been closed with sutures to reduce tension and prevent abnormal scar formation.

mmdVTq0.title: Short-term central venous access
mmdVTq0.description: A venous access device inserted directly into a central vein without tunneling or port implant. Typically intended to remain in place ≤ 14 days.

5mdiTq0.title: Long term central venous access
5mdiTq0.description: A venous access device that terminates in a large central vein and has a proximal end that is surgically implanted or tunneled under several centimeters of skin to reduce the chance of infection. May remain in place for months to years after insertion.

destinations.label: Vascular access → Long-term central venous access

nmd7Tq0.title: Risk factors for life-threatening pediatric infection
nmd7Tq0.description: Factors that increase the risk of life-threatening infection in febrile children. Includes age ≤ 60 days, immunocompromised state, current or recent hospitalization, underimmunization, and the presence of an indwelling device (e.g., VP shunt, central line, indwelling urinary catheter).

pmdLgq0.title: Prosody
pmdLgq0.description: The patterns of intonation, rhythm, stress, and pitch in speech.

qmdCgq0.title: Central vein
qmdCgq0.description: A vein located near the heart that has a wide lumen and fast-flowing blood. Examples include the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, subclavian veins, common iliac veins, and the external iliac veins.

7md4Sq0.title: Muscle hematoma
7md4Sq0.description: A collection of extravasated blood within a muscle group. May result from a traumatic injury or occur spontaneously.

HmdKSq0.title: GOLD group E
HmdKSq0.description: A COPD classification based on ≥ 2 exacerbations in the past year (or ≥ 1 leading to a hospital admission). Group E replaced groups C and D in the 2023 update to the GOLD classification.

smdtSq0.title: Commotio cordis
smdtSq0.description: Ventricular fibrillation and sudden cardiac death caused by a relatively mild nonpenetrating blunt force trauma to the precordial area, most commonly due to a hard, spherical object (e.g., a baseball). Not to be confused with cardiac contusion, which involves structural injury of the heart.

GmdBSq0.title: Appetite stimulant
GmdBSq0.description: Medications used to stimulate appetite in conditions causing anorexia or cachexia (e.g., HIV, malignancy). FDA-approved appetite stimulants include megestrol acetate, oxandrolone, and dronabinol.

tmdXhq0.title: Fracture-dislocation
tmdXhq0.description: An injury that includes both a bone fracture and dislocation of one or more nearby joints. Usually caused by sudden impact. Can be accompanied by severe ligamentous injury and/or intraarticular entrapment of bone fragments. Operative intervention is often required.

8mdOhq0.title: Elbow fat pad sign
8mdOhq0.description: A radiographic lucency on a lateral elbow x-ray caused by fat that has been displaced by a joint effusion. Can manifest anterior (anterior fat pad sign) and/or posterior (posterior fat pad sign) to the distal humerus. May be the only sign of an occult elbow fracture.

media.title: Anterior and posterior fat pad signs in supracondylar humerus fracture

umdphq0.title: Elastic compression bandage
umdphq0.description: A long stretchable cloth wrapped around a sprain or strain to reduce swelling.

xmdE3q0.title: Obstructive azoospermia
xmdE3q0.description: Absence of spermatozoa in semen despite normal spermatogenesis due to structural or functional abnormalities along the sperm transport system. Possible causes include infection (e.g., gonorrhea), iatrogeny (e.g., vasectomy), congenital (e.g., absent vas deferens in patients with cystic fibrosis), or genetic conditions (e.g., decreased sperm motility in primary ciliary dyskinesia).

15d2Qq0.title: Exercise-associated postural hypotension
15d2Qq0.description: The inability to stand or walk without assistance (i.e., collapse) after vigorous exertion. Most commonly occurs in athletes after sudden cessation of intense physical exercise. Caused by high cardiac demand during exercise followed by decreased venous return to the heart upon stopping. Typically manifests with dizziness and weakness in the absence of altered consciousness. Diagnosis is made by exclusion of other causes of exercise-induced weakness (e.g., heat stroke).

V5dGQq0.title: Sternotomy
V5dGQq0.description: Surgical division of the sternum performed to obtain access to thoracic organs and vessels.

35dSPq0.title: Ottawa knee rules
35dSPq0.description: A validated tool to help determine when x-rays are indicated for emergency department patients with knee injuries.

destinations.label: Knee ligament injuries → Acute internal knee derangement

R5dlPq0.title: Risk factors for cerumen removal complications
R5dlPq0.description: Includes anatomical abnormalities of the ear canal, perforated tympanic membrane, and increased risk of bleeding or infection.

Q5duPq0.title: Posterolateral corner
Q5duPq0.description: An area in the posterolateral aspect of the knee where several important tendons and ligaments meet. Stabilized by the fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon, and popliteofibular ligament. Often damaged in association with lateral collateral and cruciate ligament injuries.

m5dVkq0.title: Cerumen removal methods
m5dVkq0.description: The clinical techniques used to remove impacted cerumen from the external ear canal. Includes cerumenolytic agents, ear canal irrigation, and/or manual removal.

55dikq0.title: Risk factors for cerumen impaction
55dikq0.description: A set of patient characteristics that increase the risk of cerumen impaction. Factors include anatomical abnormalities of the ear (e.g., ear canal stenosis), use of foreign objects in the ear canal (e.g., hearing aids, cotton swabs, earbud headphones), dermatological conditions affecting the ear canal, and populations with increased susceptibility (i.e., young children, individuals with cognitive impairment, and older adults).

destinations.label: Cerumen impaction → Risk factors for cerumen impaction

K5dUOq0.title: Tuft fracture
K5dUOq0.description: An extraarticular fracture of the distal phalanx.

65djOq0.title: Subungual hematoma
65djOq0.description: A collection of blood under the nail plate, usually secondary to a crush injury and/or nail bed laceration.

I5dYlq0.title: Posterior long-leg splint
I5dYlq0.description: A lower-extremity splint used to immobilize the knee and leg. Extends along the posterior leg from the gluteal cleft to the malleoli, with the knee slightly flexed. Indicated for acute knee injuries (e.g., ACL injury, patellar tendon rupture, patellar fracture or dislocation) and other tibial and fibular injuries. Can be extended to the metatarsals, with the ankle in 90° flexion, if ankle immobilization is also required.

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Lower extremities

75d4lq0.title: Sugar tong splint
75d4lq0.description: A long U-shaped splint used to immobilize part of an extremity, e.g., forearm sugar tong splint, humerus sugar tong splint, ankle sugar tong splint

destinations.label: Conservative treatment of fractures → Lower extremities
Conservative treatment of fractures → Upper extremities

u5dpNq0.title: Total body surface area
u5dpNq0.description: The total area of skin involved in an injury (e.g., burn) or disease (e.g., psoriasis). Calculated using tools such as the Lund-Browder chart and the rule of nines to assess the severity of the condition.

cMdanq0.title: Risk factors specific to keloids
cMdanq0.description: Factors that increase an individual's risk of developing a keloid scar. Examples include genetic predisposition, minor trauma, and delayed wound healing.

destinations.label: Hypertrophic scars and keloids → Risk factors

dMdonq0.title: Theophylline poisoning
dMdonq0.description: Condition caused by the accumulation of theophylline in the body. Clinical presentation can vary and may include cardiac (tachycardia and arrhythmia), neurological (headache, tremor, agitation, seizures), and gastrointestinal (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) symptoms.

VMdGnq0.title: Coude catheter
VMdGnq0.description: A thin, flexible urinary catheter with a semirigid curved tip. May be used if there is difficulty inserting a flexible straight tip catheter (e.g., because of an enlarged prostate). Used for both intermittent and continuous drainage.

eMdxnq0.title: Three-way Foley catheter
eMdxnq0.description: A Foley catheter with three channels, allowing for bladder irrigation. Most commonly used if frequent or continuous bladder irrigation is anticipated (e.g., in patients with gross hematuria with urinary blood clot retention).

UMdbLq0.title: Gross motor development
UMdbLq0.description: The development of movements (e.g., sitting up, walking) that require the use of large muscle groups.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Developmental milestones

2MdTLq0.title: Fine motor development
2MdTLq0.description: The development of precise movements (e.g., picking up a small object) that require the use of small muscles.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Developmental milestones

fMdkLq0.title: Receptive language
fMdkLq0.description: The ability to understand and process language.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Developmental milestones
Child development and milestones → Developmental milestones

gMdFLq0.title: Developmental surveillance
gMdFLq0.description: A process performed by a clinician to identify any problems with a child's development. At every clinical encounter, the clinician should elicit any parent concerns, review the child's developmental history, observe the child, and inquire about possible risk factors and protective elements for developmental delay.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Overview of abnormal development

SMdyLq0.title: Developmental screening
SMdyLq0.description: The use of validated clinical tools to monitor a child's development in the domains of speech, cognitive/social and motor skills. Utilized during the 9-, 18-, and 30-month well-child visits and whenever there are concerns of abnormal development.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Overview of abnormal development

hMdcoq0.title: Developmental deviation
hMdcoq0.description: A phenomenon in which developmental milestones within a given domain are not achieved in the expected order (e.g., the infant can use a spoon before developing pincer grasp).

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Overview of abnormal development

3MdSoq0.title: Developmental dissociation
3MdSoq0.description: Significant developmental delay in one domain but not in other domains (e.g., able to ride a bike but cannot speak in full sentences).

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Overview of abnormal development

PMdWKq0.title: Neurovascular injury
PMdWKq0.description:
A term that can refer to an injury involving either of the following:
1. Peripheral nerves and/or blood vessels (usually arteries)
2. The vascular supply of the central nervous system
Neurovascular injuries can occur as a result of medical illness, trauma, or iatrogenically, and can be disabling and/or threatening to life and limb.

lMdvKq0.title: Osteopathic manipulative treatment
lMdvKq0.description: A set of techniques used by osteopathic physicians to alleviate pain and restore function. Techniques include soft tissue manipulation, myofascial release, and adjustments.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Osteopathic manipulative treatment

NMd-Kq0.title: Exercise therapy for chronic pain
NMd-Kq0.description: A prescribed exercise plan used to improve chronic pain. May be performed independently at home or under supervision (either one-on-one or in a group setting). Example exercises include muscle-strengthening exercises, stretching, and aerobic exercise.

mMdV6q0.title: Interventional pain management
mMdV6q0.description: The use of minimally invasive techniques by specialized clinicians to provide chronic pain relief. Techniques include placement of drugs (e.g., steroids, opioids) into targeted areas (i.e., joint space, epidural space, nerve plexus), neurostimulator placement, and nerve ablation.

destinations.label: Principles of pain management → Nonpharmacological analgesia

5Mdi6q0.title: Intraarticular injection
5Mdi6q0.description: The injection of an agent (e.g., glucocorticoids, hyaluronic acid, local anesthetic) into a joint space for a therapeutic purpose. Common indications include osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and rotator cuff disease.

LMdw6q0.title: Isolated developmental delay
LMdw6q0.description: A delay in the normal developmental progression within a single developmental domain (i.e., motor development, language development, social development, emotional development), as compared to global developmental delay, where multiple domains are affected.

destinations.label: Child development and milestones → Overview of abnormal development

oMd0pq0.title: Ear canal irrigation
oMd0pq0.description: The process of flushing the external ear canal with water or saline with or without a bacteriostatic agent (e.g., hydrogen peroxide) to remove impacted cerumen, ear canal debris, and/or foreign bodies. Often performed with a bulb syringe, a syringe with or without a flexible catheter, or an automated pulse irrigator machine.

qMdCpq0.title: Comprehensive behavioral intervention for tics
qMdCpq0.description: A behavioral intervention for tics that includes habit reversal training to identify premonitory urges and train patients to suppress tics; functional assessment and intervention to identify and change environmental situations that worsen tics; and relaxation training to decrease anxiety.

7Md4Jq0.title: Contraindications to live vaccines
7Md4Jq0.description: Live attenuated vaccines (e.g., MMR, varicella, rotavirus, live attenuated influenza vaccine) should not be administered to individuals who are pregnant, severely immunocompromised (e.g., patients with hematologic or solid malignancies; HIV infection with CD4 cell count < 200 and CD4 percentage of ≤15%; or those on long-term immunosuppressive therapy), or have recently received immunoglobulin-containing blood products (e.g., IVIG, whole blood).

GMdBJq0.title: Anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity
GMdBJq0.description: An adverse effect of anthracycline (e.g., doxorubicin, idarubicin) accumulation leading to cardiomyocyte death with subsequent left ventricular dysfunction and, in severe cases, congestive heart failure.

8MdOqq0.title: Full knee x-ray series
8MdOqq0.description: A set of radiographs commonly used to evaluate the knee for injury. Includes anteroposterior (AP) and lateral views, inferior-superior axial views of the patella (i.e., skyline or sunrise view), and views of the intercondylar notch.

wMdhIq0.title: Tetanus, diphtheria vaccine
wMdhIq0.description: An inactivated vaccine that contains the tetanus toxoid and reduced diphtheria toxoid. Either Td or Tdap is used in individuals ≥ 7 years of age for catch-up immunizations, boosters every 10 years, and postexposure tetanus prophylaxis.

9MdNIq0.title: HIV-associated distal symmetric polyneuropathy
9MdNIq0.description: Axonal peripheral neuropathy in individuals with HIV that cannot be attributed to a cause other than HIV infection.  Symptoms include pain, numbness, and weakness in the extremities, typically starting in the feet and hands (stocking glove distribution) and spreading upwards, decreased pinprick and vibration sensation in distal lower extremities, and decreased or absent ankle jerk reflex. Caused by direct neurotoxicity of HIV virus or cART medications.

BMdzIq0.title: Opioid exit strategy
BMdzIq0.description: A plan that is developed by the prescribing clinician, in collaboration with the patient, before the initiation of opioids. Outlines the steps for treatment discontinuation or transitioning to medication-assisted treatment if the risks of opioid therapy exceed the benefits.

0nde7q0.title: Photosensitivity with HIV infection
0nde7q0.description: A collection of photosensitive disorders seen in patients with HIV infection. Includes immune-mediated conditions, e.g., chronic actinic dermatitis, actinic lichenoid leukomelanoderma of HIV, and porphyria cutanea tarda, and drug-induced phototoxic and photoallergic reactions.

andQ7q0.title: Juvenile spring eruption
andQ7q0.description: A variant of polymorphous light eruption that affects the ears of children. Papules, plaques, and vesicles form on the ears after exposure to sunlight. More common in children with short hair.

dndoHq0.title: Immunization schedule by medical indication
dndoHq0.description: Immunization recommendations for individuals at increased risk of infection (e.g., due to immunocompromised status, end-stage renal disease, chronic conditions).

media.title: ACIP immunization schedule by medical indication: children and adolescents ≤ 18 years of age
ACIP immunization schedule by medical or other indications: adults ≥ 19 years of age

VndGHq0.title: Mastoidectomy
VndGHq0.description: A surgical procedure in which diseased mastoid air cells are excised. Indications include cholesteatoma, mastoiditis, and chronic suppurative otitis media with complications.

hndcGq0.title: Dry ear precautions
hndcGq0.description: A set of precautions to prevent water from entering the ear canal during water activities (e.g., swimming, showering). Indications include recurrent otitis externa and a perforated tympanic membrane. Includes using water-tight ear plugs that occlude but do not enter the ear canal and, if the tympanic membrane is intact, acidifying ear drops after water activities.

PndWtq0.title: Maximal inspiratory pressure
PndWtq0.description: Measure (in cmH₂O) to evaluate inspiratory muscle function (e.g., diaphragm, external intercostal muscles). Determined by having the patient inhale with as much force as possible against a closed mouthpiece. Values below -80 cmH₂O in men and below -70 cmH₂O in women rule out significant inspiratory muscle weakness.

destinations.label: Pulmonary function testing → Respiratory muscle function testing

4nd3tq0.title: Maximal expiratory pressure
4nd3tq0.description: Measure (in cmH₂O) to evaluate global expiratory muscle function (e.g., abdominal muscles, internal intercostal muscles). Determined by having the patient exhale with as much force as possible against a closed mouthpiece. Values above 130 cmH₂O in men and above 100 cmH₂O in women rule out significant expiratory muscle weakness.

destinations.label: Pulmonary function testing → Respiratory muscle function testing

kndmtq0.title: Challenge-dechallenge-rechallenge test
kndmtq0.description: A test used to assess whether symptoms are the result of an adverse effect to an agent. If following cessation of exposure (dechallenge) the symptoms cease and appear again after reexposure to an agent (rechallenge), the test is positive and the symptoms are concluded to be secondary to the agent. Used in clinical trials to identify adverse effects and in dermatology to diagnose photodermatoses.

OndItq0.title: Clostridium septicum
OndItq0.description: A gram-positive, anaerobic, spore-forming bacillus found in the gastrointestinal tract and in soil. Can cause life-threatening gas gangrene and is associated with colon cancer.

IndYuq0.title: Capsaicin
IndYuq0.description: A colorless irritant phenolic amide that is readily absorbed by the skin and used topically to relieve pain (e.g., in postherpetic neuralgia, diabetic neuropathy, complex regional pain syndrome). Contact with mucous membranes causes a burning sensation. Naturally found in chili peppers.

7nd4uq0.title: Measles, mumps, rubella, varicella vaccine
7nd4uq0.description: A live attenuated vaccine that protects against measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella. It can be used as part of routine childhood immunization at 12 months and 4 years of age, although there is an increased risk of postvaccination seizure in children < 24 months of age.

sndtuq0.title: Small nonenveloped virus
sndtuq0.description: A nonenveloped virus that is < 50 nm in size. Has a tough protein capsid that makes it extremely resistant to most disinfectants. Viruses of the families Picornaviridae, Caliciviridae, Astroviridae, Parvoviridae, and Polyomaviridae are small nonenveloped viruses.

GndBuq0.title: Large nonenveloped virus
GndBuq0.description: A nonenveloped virus that is ≥ 50 nm in size. Less resistant than small nonenveloped viruses but more resistant than enveloped viruses to disinfectants. Viruses of the families Reoviridae, Adenoviridae, and Papillomaviridae are large nonenveloped viruses.

tndXEq0.title: Pars flaccida
tndXEq0.description: The flaccid part of the tympanic membrane. It is triangular-shaped and located above the malleolar folds.

media.title: Examination and surface anatomy of the tympanic membrane

FndgEq0.title: Pars tensa
FndgEq0.description: The stiff part of the tympanic membrane (TM). The pars tensa comprises the majority of the TM, is located inferiorly to the malleolar folds, and, in healthy individuals, should be mobile during pneumatic otoscopy.

media.title: Examination and surface anatomy of the tympanic membrane

8ndOEq0.title: Stocking-glove distribution
8ndOEq0.description: A characteristic pattern of sensory symptoms in the hands and feet that includes numbness, pain, and a burning or prickling sensation. Commonly seen in conditions associated with peripheral polyneuropathy, e.g., diabetes mellitus and Guillain-Barré syndrome.

undpEq0.title: Mineral-based sunscreen
undpEq0.description: A type of sunscreen that contains inorganic UV filters (e.g., zinc oxide, titanium dioxide) that scatter or reflect UV radiation and visible light, depending on the formulation.

End8Eq0.title: Chemical sunscreen
End8Eq0.description: A type of sunscreen that contains organic UV filters that absorb UV radiation.

vndAEq0.title: Risk factors for acute otitis media
vndAEq0.description: A set of individual and environmental characteristics that increase the risk of developing acute otitis media. Factors include daycare attendance, exposure to tobacco smoke, pacifier use, family history of acute otitis media, male sex, and craniofacial abnormalities.

AndRDq0.title: Risk factors for measles, mumps, and/or rubella
AndRDq0.description: Factors that increase the risk of contracting or transmitting measles, mumps, and/or rubella include living in a crowded dormitory (e.g., college students), working in a health care facility, international travel, HIV infection, and household or close contact with immunocompromised individuals.

zndrDq0.title: Age-related sicca syndrome
zndrDq0.description: A condition characterized by xerophthalmia and xerostomia in older patients without evidence of Sjogren syndrome. Results from decreased tear and saliva production due to age-related acinar atrophy with fat replacement, interstitial fibrosis, and ductal dilation.

-ndDDq0.title: R-value for liver injury
-ndDDq0.description: A value used to determine the pattern of injury in drug-induced liver injury. Calculated as (ALT/ULN ALT)/(ALP/ULN ALP). A value of > 5 is consistent with a hepatocellular injury pattern, 2-5 mixed injury pattern, and < 2 cholestatic injury pattern.

aLdQwq0.title: Xylazine
aLdQwq0.description: An alpha-2 agonist veterinary sedative that is used as an adulterant in illicit opioids, e.g., fentanyl and heroin.

XLd9wq0.title: Anterior drawer test of the ankle
XLd9wq0.description: The application of anterior force to the posterior aspect of the talus while the tibia is held fixed.  Anterior movement of the foot suggests rupture of the anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL).

1Ld29q0.title: Short leg cast
1Ld29q0.description: A circumferential cast of the lower extremity that immobilizes the ankle and foot and extends from the fibular head to the distal metatarsals. Indicated for fractures and/or severe sprains of the foot and ankle.

WLdP9q0.title: Manual in-line cervical stabilization
WLdP9q0.description: A cervical spine immobilization technique that involves placing the hands on either side of the patient's head while gripping the skull base to keep it in a neutral position. Typically used if a cervical collar is unavailable or the collar needs to be removed to allow unimpeded access to the neck, e.g., during examination or airway management.

2LdTCq0.title: Nonintact tympanic membrane
2LdTCq0.description: A loss of integrity of the tympanic membrane. Causes include tympanic membrane perforation, the presence of tympanostomy tubes, or a history of intratympanic injections, ear surgery, or barotrauma.

hLdcxq0.title: Hard signs of extremity vascular injury
hLdcxq0.description: Overt signs of arterial injury which necessitates urgent evaluation and intervention to prevent limb loss or exsanguination. Includes active hemorrhage, absent distal pulses, expanding hematoma, new bruit, and/or signs of distal ischemia (e.g., pallor, paraesthesias, pain).

3LdSxq0.title: Hemodynamic instability
3LdSxq0.description: A state of rapidly deteriorating and/or fluctuating hemodynamic parameters (e.g., heart rate, blood pressure). Can be a manifestation of circulatory shock, cardiac arrhythmia, heart failure, and/or hypertensive crises.

nLd7yq0.title: Tympanostomy tube otorrhea
nLd7yq0.description: A condition in which discharge enters the external auditory canal from the middle ear canal through a patent tympanostomy tube. Causes include acute otitis media (most common), postoperative discharge following placement for otitis media with effusion, and chronic suppurative otitis media.

oLd0Aq0.title: Post hoc analysis
oLd0Aq0.description: A statistical analysis that is conducted at the end of a research study. Consider only suitable for generating, not testing hypothesis. Disadvantages include lower statistical power and an increased the risk of false positive and false negative findings.

7Ld4_q0.title: Superficial partial thickness burn
7Ld4_q0.description: A second-degree or partial thickness burn that involves the epidermis and upper layers of the dermis (papillary dermis). These burns are painful, erythematous, blanchable, and have a slow capillary refill. Healing occurs in 1-3 weeks and does not leave a scar.

HLdK_q0.title: Deep partial thickness burn
HLdK_q0.description: A second-degree or partial thickness burn that involves the deeper layers of the dermis (papillary and reticular dermis). These burns are less painful, nonblanchable, and appear as mottled skin with red and/or white patches. Healing occurs in ≥ 3 weeks and leaves a scar.

GLdB_q0.title: Proctalgia fugax
GLdB_q0.description: A functional disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of sudden, severe anorectal pain unrelated to defecation. The pain is intermittent and self-limited, with pain-free intervals between episodes.

FLdgzq0.title: Periungual
FLdgzq0.description: The area around a fingernail or toenail.

uLdpzq0.title: Disability benefits
uLdpzq0.description: Funds from public and/or private sources that are paid to individuals with illnesses or disabilities. Federal disability benefits include the Social Security Disability Insurance and Supplemental Security Income. Eligibility criteria include the presence of disability (i.e., the inability to pursue a substantial gainful activity due to a physical or mental condition that is expected to result in death or has lasted or is expected to last at least one year) and meeting work requirements.

ELd8zq0.title: Occupational asthma
ELd8zq0.description: Asthma induced by specific workplace allergens and/or irritants. Symptoms typically improve when the individual is not in the workplace.

ALdRZI0.title: Differential misclassification bias
ALdRZI0.description: A misclassification bias in which the frequency of classification errors differs between the groups under comparison. Skews the odds ratio either toward or away from the null value.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

_Ld5ZI0.title: Implicit bias
_Ld5ZI0.description: Unconscious attitudes and/or perceptions toward specific social groups (e.g., based on age, weight, race, or gender). Implicit bias can negatively impact patient care and perpetuate disparities in treatment.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Risk factors for medical errors

zLdrZI0.title: High-risk conditions for cervical cancer
zLdrZI0.description: Immunocompromise, exposure to DES in-utero, and a current or past history of a high-grade precancerous cervical lesion are considered high-risk conditions for invasive cervical cancer. Screening modalities and intervals should be individualized for these groups of individuals.

destinations.label: Cervical cancer screening → Overview of screening recommendations

1od2aI0.title: MSE
1od2aI0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Mental status examination
2. Myoclonic status epilepticus

WodPaI0.title: Low-risk BCC subtypes
WodPaI0.description: The most common basal cell carcinoma (BCC) subtypes. They have an indolent clinical course and a low risk of recurrence after excision. Examples include nodular BCC and superficial BCC.

destinations.label: Basal cell carcinoma → Subtypes and variants

dodoaI0.title: High-risk BCC subtypes
dodoaI0.description: Subtypes of basal cell carcinoma (BCC) that are likely to have an aggressive course and are associated with a high risk of recurrence after excision. They account for < 20% of all BCCs. Examples include micronodular BCC, infiltrative BCC, morpheaform BCC, basosquamous (metatypical) BCC, and sclerosing BCC.

destinations.label: Basal cell carcinoma → Subtypes and variants

5odicI0.title: Anatomical risk factors for patellar dislocation
5odicI0.description: A set of anatomical abnormalities that increase the risk of patellar dislocation. They include, for example: trochlear or patellar dysplasia (abnormal growth or development of the femoral trochlea or patella), patella alta (a "high-riding" patella), patellar tilt, and ligament hyperlaxity or joint hypermobility.

ood01I0.title: Fitzpatrick classification of skin types
ood01I0.description: A controversial skin type classification system based on skin color and the potential for skin to tan or burn after UV exposure. Skin types range from type I (lightest skin tone) to type VI (darkest skin tone), and classification is based on subjective self-reported sensitivity to UV radiation. It was initially developed for psoriasis to guide phototherapy dosage for light skin tones and was later adapted to guide recommendations for photoprotective measures and predict the risk of sunburn and skin cancer. However, the risk of skin cancer is underestimated in individuals with darker skin tones (type IV-VI).

Jods1I0.title: Recombinant vaccine
Jods1I0.description: A type of vaccine that combines a segment of pathogen DNA with the DNA of another organism (e.g., a yeast or mammalian cell) or virus in order to produce large amounts of the pathogen antigen (e.g., a protein, replicated DNA). May be inactivated (most common) or live. Examples of inactivated recombinant protein vaccines include the hepatitis B vaccine, human papillomavirus vaccine, recombinant influenza vaccine, recombinant shingles vaccine, and the meningococcal B vaccine.

HodKWI0.title: Penrose drain
HodKWI0.description: A flexible flat rubber tube, usually made of latex. Primarily used as a passive surgical drain or a small tourniquet.

xodEVI0.title: Clinical features of open fractures
xodEVI0.description: Nearby soft tissue injuries, visible bone fragments in an open wound, and/or greasy or oily blood loss.

destinations.label: General principles of fractures → Subtypes and variants

yoddeI0.title: Principle of proportionality
yoddeI0.description: A bioethical principle stating that an intervention's potential benefits should be proportionately greater than its potential harm or burden.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Medical ethics

AodReI0.title: Complications of prolonged immobilization
AodReI0.description: Complications of prolonged immobilization (e.g., due to long-term use of casts or splints or critical illness) include venous thromboembolism, pneumonia, decubitus ulcers, muscle atrophy, and cardiovascular deconditioning.

eKdx2I0.title: Postoperative respiratory failure
eKdx2I0.description: Definitions of postoperative respiratory failure vary depending on the source. Definitions include: > 1 day of postoperative ventilation, PaO₂ < 60 mm Hg on room air, or pulse oximetry < 90% with the need for supplemental oxygen.

3KdSTI0.title: Fentanyl test strips
3KdSTI0.description: A harm reduction tool to assess for the presence of fentanyl and fentanyl analogues in recreational drugs (e.g., pressed pills).

PKdWgI0.title: Femoral trochlear groove
PKdWgI0.description: A concave groove on the anterior surface of the distal femur, over which the patella glides during knee flexion and extension.

4Kd3gI0.title: Q angle
4Kd3gI0.description: An acute angle formed by the quadriceps femoris muscle and patellar tendon intersection. An increased Q angle indicates greater lateral force exerted on the patella by the quadriceps, and can be associated with various knee disorders, including patellar dislocation and patellofemoral pain syndrome.

kKdmgI0.title: Lateral patellar apprehension test
kKdmgI0.description: A clinical test to assess for lateral patellar instability. With the knee relaxed in 30 degrees of flexion, lateral force is applied to the medial patella; or, in a variant called the moving patellar apprehension test, the knee is fully extended, lateral force is applied to the patella, and the knee is then flexed. In a positive test, the maneuver produces discomfort or apprehension (either expressed by the patient or evidenced by contraction of the quadriceps).

OKdIgI0.title: Osteochondral fracture
OKdIgI0.description: A type of fracture on the articular surface of a joint, which affects both the cartilage and the underlying subchondral bone. The bony fragment may be small and thin and can be missed on radiograph. Most frequently occurs in the patella following an acute patellar dislocation.

NKd-gI0.title: Patellar instability
NKd-gI0.description: A general term used to refer to either patellar dislocation, or to patellar subluxation (partial patellar dislocation).

mKdVSI0.title: Indications to test for immunity to measles, mumps, and rubella
mKdVSI0.description: Immunity should be assessed in the following at-risk groups to determine the need for MMR vaccination: pregnant individuals as part of routine prenatal care; immunosuppressed individuals; undervaccinated individuals who have been exposed to measles, mumps, and/or rubella; those with suspected prior infection that was not confirmed with laboratory testing; and individuals with inadequate or unknown vaccination status who are at increased risk of acquiring or transmitting measles, mumps, and/or rubella.

pKdLhI0.title: Secondary research
pKdLhI0.description: The collation and analysis of existing data. Examples include narrative reviews, systematic reviews, and metaanalyses.

JKdshI0.title: Primary research
JKdshI0.description: The collection of original data directly from the source for a specific research purpose. Examples include surveys, interviews, observational studies, and experimental studies.

qKdChI0.title: Clinical features of strangulation
qKdChI0.description: Features include bruising around the neck, ligature marks, subconjunctival hemorrhage, facial petechiae, dysphagia, and voice changes.

media.title: Petechiae of the conjunctiva after violent asphyxiation

EKd8RI0.title: Frog-leg position
EKd8RI0.description: A supine position in which the patient abducts and externally rotates the hips, resembling the appearance of a frog's legs at rest.

DKd1iI0.title: Single-arm trial
DKd1iI0.description: A study design in which a single group of participants receives an intervention and is then followed over time to observe its effects.

AKdRQI0.title: WHO definition of anemia
AKdRQI0.description: The hemoglobin levels at which the World Health Organization defines anemia in otherwise healthy individuals, based on sex and age. Adult males: Hb < 13 g/dL; nonpregnant women: Hb < 12 g/dL; pregnant women: Hb < 11 g/dL; adolescents 12-14 years: Hb < 12 g/dL; children 5-11 years: Hb < 11.5 g/dL; children 6-59 months: Hb < 11 g/dL.

-KdDQI0.title: Finger cascade sign
-KdDQI0.description: A physical examination technique used to assess for rotational deformity of the fingers. The patient is asked to make a loose fist with the wrist in supination. A finger cascade sign is normal if all fingers come together symmetrically over the hypothenar muscle and scaphoid. A finger cascade sign is abnormal if the fingers overlap or have varying angles of convergence; this suggests a metacarpal and/or phalangeal fracture.

Y6dnjI0.title: Nondifferential misclassification bias
Y6dnjI0.description: A misclassification bias in which the frequency of classification errors is similar in the groups under comparison. If the misclassified variable is dichotomous, the odds ratio is skewed towards the null value. If the misclassified variable is not dichotomous (i.e., more than two exposure or health outcome categories), the odds ratio can either be skewed towards or away from the null value.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

b6dHjI0.title: Misclassification bias
b6dHjI0.description: An error in which research subjects are classified into the wrong exposure or outcome groups, thereby distorting the observed association.

destinations.label: Epidemiology → Random errors, bias, and confounding

X6d9jI0.title: Refined carbohydrates
X6d9jI0.description: A type of carbohydrate that contains a maximum of two saccharide units, including monosaccharides (e.g., glucose, fructose, galactose) and disaccharides (e.g., sucrose, lactose). High intake is associated with several ASCVD risk factors, e.g., hypertriglyceridemia and diabetes mellitus.

16d2PI0.title: Vulnerable adult
16d2PI0.description: An individual 18 years of age or older who is unable to meet their needs and/or protect themselves from harm or exploitation without assistance. Physical or mental illness or disability, drug use, and older age can contribute to impairment or insufficiency of the individual's faculties.

U6db4I0.title: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis
U6db4I0.description: A study of the predictors of progression from asymptomatic to clinical ASCVD in a multiethnic population that includes Black, White, Hispanic, and Asian (predominantly Chinese) Americans.

26dT4I0.title: Hepatitis B postvaccination serology testing
26dT4I0.description: The measurement of anti-HBs titers after completion of the HepB vaccine series in individuals at risk for HBV infection. Used as a proxy for immunity to HBV infection.

f6dk4I0.title: Contraceptive failure rate
f6dk4I0.description: The percentage of individuals who become pregnant within 12 months of initiating a contraceptive method. Typical use includes individuals who use the method incorrectly or inconsistently, whereas perfect use includes only individuals who follow the method correctly and consistently.

T6d64I0.title: Cerebrovascular disease
T6d64I0.description: A group of conditions related to disordered blood flow to the brain due to ischemia or bleeding. Cerebrovascular diseases include stroke, carotid artery stenosis, aneurysms, and vascular malformations.

O6dIOI0.title: Moderately elevated transaminases
O6dIOI0.description: A laboratory finding of ALT and/or AST levels 5–15x the upper limit of normal.

56dilI0.title: Therapeutic misconception
56dilI0.description: A phenomenon in which study participants do not fully understand the difference between ordinary care and research, e.g., participants may believe that they are receiving individualized treatment rather than being treated according to a protocol.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Research ethics

M6dMlI0.title: Therapeutic misestimation
M6dMlI0.description: A phenomenon in which an individual misjudges the risk or benefit of participating in research.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Research ethics

n6d7lI0.title: Combined hormonal contraception
n6d7lI0.description: A medication that includes both estrogen and progestin to prevent pregnancy. Available as a pill, patch, or vaginal ring. CHCs can also be used to treat some hormone-mediated conditions (e.g., PCOS, menopause, acne, endometriosis).

66djNI0.title: Handoff-related errors
66djNI0.description: Handoff-related errors are those that occur during the transfer of care of a patient, which may occur at a provider's change of shift or when a patient is transferring to a new care setting.

destinations.label: Patient safety → Prevention of communication errors

q6dCNI0.title: Severely elevated transaminases
q6dCNI0.description: A laboratory finding of ALT and/or AST levels > 15x the upper limit of normal.

I6dYmI0.title: Massively elevated transaminases
I6dYmI0.description: A laboratory finding of ALT and/or AST levels > 10,000 U/L.

G6dBmI0.title: Medical chaperone
G6dBmI0.description: An authorized health care provider who acts as an impartial observer during an encounter between a patient and another health care provider. Often used to reduce patient apprehension during sensitive examinations, e.g., gynecologic or urological examinations.

F6dg5I0.title: Complications of stress fractures
F6dg5I0.description: Complications include delayed healing, progression to a complete fracture, avascular necrosis, and nonunion.

86dO5I0.title: Clinical features of stress fractures
86dO5I0.description: Features include pain that worsens with activity and resolves with rest, focal bone tenderness, and soft tissue swelling.

v6dA5I0.title: Progressive muscle relaxation
v6dA5I0.description: A relaxation technique involving tensing and then relaxing different muscle groups in a systematic manner.

-6dDnI0.title: Canadian C-Spine Rule
-6dDnI0.description: A clinical decision rule used to evaluate the need for cervical spine imaging following blunt cervical trauma. Criteria for forgoing imaging include the absence of high-risk features (i.e., age ≥65, high impact mechanism, and/or paraesthesias in the extremities), the presence of low-risk features allowing safe clinical evaluation, and the patient's ability to actively rotate the neck by 45 degrees to the left and right.

ZpdZLI0.title: Pain neuroscience education
ZpdZLI0.description: An educational technique that involves teaching patients about the neurophysiological, neurobiological, psychological, and social components of pain. Aims to help patients reconceptualize how they perceive pain to decrease fear of movement, reduce pain and catastrophizing, and improve function.

apdQLI0.title: Red flags for sexual assault
apdQLI0.description: Red flags include genital, anal, or oral injuries; lower abdominal or genital pain; symptoms of sexually transmitted infections; and clinical features of strangulation or physical abuse.

Tpd6KI0.title: Critical congenital heart diseases
Tpd6KI0.description: A group of structural cardiac conditions that affect neonates and can cause serious complications. Includes hypoplastic left heart syndrome, tetralogy of Fallot, coarctation of the aorta, pulmonary or tricuspid atresia, and transposition of the great vessels. Typically screened for at birth using pulse oximetry and requires surgery in the first year of life.

Qpdu6I0.title: Envenomation
Qpdu6I0.description: The exposure to a toxic substance secreted by a venomous animal, typically via a bite or sting.

4pd3pI0.title: Penicillin-binding protein 3
4pd3pI0.description: A type of penicillin-binding protein. Functions as a component of the divisome in certain bacteria and is the binding site of monobactam antibiotics (e.g., aztreonam).

lpdvpI0.title: Clinical features of menopause
lpdvpI0.description: Symptoms include menstrual abnormalities, vasomotor symptoms (e.g., hot flashes, night sweats), vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract atrophy (which can cause, e.g., vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and UTIs), neuropsychiatric symptoms (e.g., irritability, depression), and other symptoms (e.g., hair thinning, decreased libido).

npd7JI0.title: Supplemental nutrition assistance program
npd7JI0.description: A federally funded supplemental nutrition assistance program in the United States (formerly known as food stamps). The program provides financial assistance for purchasing food to individuals with low or no income.

LpdwJI0.title: Special supplemental nutrition program for women, infants, and children
LpdwJI0.description: A federally funded supplemental nutrition program for women, infants, and children in the US. It provides nutrition education, supplemental food, and breastfeeding support to low or no income families with pregnant or postpartum individuals and/or children < 5 years of age.

KpdUqI0.title: Maternal, infant, and early child home visiting program
KpdUqI0.description: A federally funded program in the United States that provides resources to promote maternal and child health through visits to homes of pregnant individuals, infants, and children who are < 5 years of age and at increased risk for negative outcomes.

IpdYII0.title: Induced menopause
IpdYII0.description: The permanent loss of ovarian function as a result of medical interventions.

rpdfII0.title: Vulvovaginal atrophy
rpdfII0.description: Changes in the vulva and vagina resulting from low estrogen levels. Includes loss of subcutaneous fat, thinning of the vaginal mucosa, elevated vaginal pH, and prolapse. Commonly a manifestation of genitourinary syndrome of menopause but may occur in low-estrogen states with other causes, e.g., lactation or use of medications such as selective estrogen receptor modulators.

GpdBII0.title: Gestational sac
GpdBII0.description: A fluid-filled cavity that forms in early pregnancy. In a viable intrauterine pregnancy, it is located within the uterus and contains the yolk sac or embryo/fetus.

tpdXrI0.title: Fetal biometric parameters
tpdXrI0.description: Antenatal ultrasound measurements of biparietal diameter, head circumference, abdominal circumference, and femur length. Can be used to assess fetal growth and estimate gestational age.

media.title: Fetal biometry: biparietal diameter and head circumference

updprI0.title: Adverse effects of opioids
updprI0.description: Adverse effects include nausea, vomiting, constipation, urinary retention, and at higher doses, respiratory depression and CNS depression. Long-term use is associated with tolerance, dependency, and opioid-induced hyperalgesia.

Epd8rI0.title: Modified biophysical profile
Epd8rI0.description: A noninvasive evaluation of fetal wellbeing consisting of nonstress testing and amniotic fluid measurement. A normal modified biophysical profile is indicated by a reactive nonstress test and either an amniotic fluid index ≥ 5 cm or a single vertical deep pocket of amniotic fluid > 2 cm.

destinations.label: Prenatal care → Antepartum fetal surveillance testing
Principles of pain management → Classification of pain
Principles of pain management → Classification of pain
Principles of pain management → Classification of pain

9pdN7I0.title: Opioid-induced hyperalgesia
9pdN7I0.description: An increased perception of pain as a result of nociceptive sensitization from acute or chronic opioid use.

Cpdq7I0.title: Pain sensitization
Cpdq7I0.description: An enhanced responsiveness of the nociceptive pathway to stimuli that manifests as abnormal pain perception (e.g., hyperalgesia and allodynia). The pathophysiology is not completely understood but is thought to involve peripheral and central sensitization. Pain sensitization plays a major role in the generation and maintenance of chronic and neuropathic pain.

Bpdz7I0.title: Bioidentical hormones
Bpdz7I0.description: Any exogenous hormone designed to mimic hormones produced by the body. The use of this term is not recommended because it includes both FDA-approved hormone therapy and compounded hormones, which are not FDA-approved, are unregulated, and have no evidence of superior efficacy to FDA-approved options.

_pd5HI0.title: Early menopause
_pd5HI0.description: The occurrence of physiological menopause between 40 and 45 years of age with no other identified cause.

aJdQsI0.title: Inactivated influenza vaccine
aJdQsI0.description: A vaccine that contains inactivated influenza virus that is administered intramuscularly. Can be either egg-based or cell culture-based. The minimum age for immunization is 6 months. For patients with a severe egg allergy (i.e., anaphylaxis), either use a cell culture-based vaccine or administer an egg-based vaccine in a monitored clinical setting.

YJdnsI0.title: Live-attenuated influenza vaccine
YJdnsI0.description: A vaccine that contains live-attenuated influenza virus that is administered intranasally. The attenuated virus is temperature-sensitive and can replicate in the nose but not in the lungs. Approved for individuals 2-49 years of age.  Avoid in individuals with contraindications to live vaccines and in young children with known asthma or recent wheezing (i.e., wheezing in the preceding 12 months). Since it is egg-based, individuals with a severe egg allergy (i.e., anaphylaxis) should receive the vaccine in a monitored clinical setting.

bJdHsI0.title: Recombinant influenza vaccine
bJdHsI0.description: A synthetic influenza vaccine that contains the influenza hemagglutinin (HA) antigen made with recombinant technology. The vaccine does not contain the influenza virus or use eggs for production (egg-free). Approved in individuals ≥ 18 years of age and preferred in individuals ≥ 65 years of age.

eJdxGI0.title: Umbilical cord blood banking
eJdxGI0.description: A technique used to store blood collected from a newborn's umbilical cord for use at a later time. The stem cells contained in cord blood can be used in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Cord blood can be stored in a public bank to be used by the community at large or in a private bank to be used at the discretion of its owner.

2JdTtI0.title: Spontaneous cerebellar hemorrhage
2JdTtI0.description: A type of intracerebral hemorrhage, most commonly caused by poorly controlled hypertension, that usually manifests with occipital headache, neck stiffness, nystagmus, and gait ataxia. Diagnosed via CT of the head without contrast. Emergency surgical decompression is the first-line management. Complications include brain herniation, severe brainstem injury, and/or respiratory failure.

TJd6tI0.title: Postictal lactic acidosis
TJd6tI0.description: A type of transient anion gap metabolic acidosis that can follow a seizure and is characterized by increased lactic acid and reduced serum bicarbonate. Lactic acidosis results from excess muscle exertion in the setting of inadequate oxygen delivery. Usually resolves spontaneously 60–90 minutes after seizure activity stops.

gJdFtI0.title: First-degree relatives
gJdFtI0.description: Relatives with no other family members in the bloodline between them. First-degree relatives share 50% of their genetic information. Includes parents, full siblings, and offspring.

SJdytI0.title: Second-degree relatives
SJdytI0.description: Relatives with one family member in the bloodline between them. Second-degree relatives share 25% of their genetic information. Includes grandparents, aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews, grandchildren, and half-siblings.

hJdcFI0.title: Third-degree relatives
hJdcFI0.description: Relatives with two other family members in the bloodline between them. Third-degree relatives share 12.5% of their genetic information. Includes great-grandparents, great-aunts, great-uncles, great-nieces, great-nephews, great-grandchildren, first cousins, half-aunts, and half-uncles.

iJdJFI0.title: T-ACE
iJdJFI0.description:
A validated screening tool that can be used in pregnancy to identify risky alcohol use, includes: 
- T: Tolerance (How many drinks does it take to make you feel high?)
- A: Annoyance (Have people annoyed you by criticizing your drinking?)
- C: Cut down (Have you felt you ought to cut down on your drinking?)
- E: Eye Opener (Have you had a drink first thing in the morning to relieve a hangover?)

PJdW8I0.title: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale
PJdW8I0.description: A validated screening tool for identifying depression in pregnant and postpartum individuals. The survey contains 10 questions, each with 4 possible answer choices that are scored from 0-3 points.

4Jd38I0.title: PMP
4Jd38I0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Pseudomyxoma peritonei
2. Previous menstrual period
3. Prescription monitoring program
4. Pain management program

MJdMuI0.title: Internal mammary lymph nodes
MJdMuI0.description: A group of lymph nodes that drain lymph from the anterior chest wall, anterior diaphragm, and medial breasts. They are arranged as a parasternal, longitudinally-linked chain and are most commonly located in the second or third intercostal spaces on each side.

nJd7uI0.title: Transverse cervical artery
nJd7uI0.description: An artery that arises from the thyrocervical trunk and passes through the posterior triangle of the neck before continuing to the anterior border of the levator scapulae muscle. Further divides into a superficial and a deep branch. Supplies the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid muscles.

oJd0EI0.title: Ascending cervical artery
oJd0EI0.description: An artery that arises from the thyrocervical trunk. Supplies the musculature of the neck as well as the posterior segments of the cervical vertebrae.

qJdCEI0.title: Neuromodulation techniques
qJdCEI0.description: The use of electrical stimulation and/or medication to activate or inhibit action potentials. Used in conditions such as epilepsy, chronic pain, and Parkinson disease.

uJdpDI0.title: Salvage therapy
uJdpDI0.description: A type of treatment that is administered if standard therapy is not effective (e.g., in cancer or HIV treatment).

vJdADI0.title: Cannabidiol
vJdADI0.description: The main nonpsychoactive cannabinoid found in the cannabis plant. Modulates the adverse effects of THC (e.g., anxiety, agitation) when coingested.

AJdR9I0.title: Radiographic features of stress fractures
AJdR9I0.description: Features include a radiolucent fracture line, increased cortical density, and endosteal thickening and/or sclerosis.

_Jd59I0.title: Skin appendage tumor
_Jd59I0.description: A rare type of skin tumor that displays differentiation toward at least one epidermal adnexal line (i.e., follicular, sebaceous, eccrine, and/or apocrine).

dqdoxI0.title: FDP
dqdoxI0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Flexor digitorum profundus
2. Fibrin degradation product

VqdGxI0.title: Behavioral contraception methods
VqdGxI0.description: Behavioral contraception includes coitus interruptus, fertility awareness-based methods, and lactational amenorrhea. These methods are user-dependent and therefore associated with high error rates compared to other forms of contraception.

fqdkBI0.title: Progestin-only contraception
fqdkBI0.description: A form of contraception in which the effects of progesterone (endometrial atrophy, thickening of cervical mucus) prevent pregnancy, although some forms also suppress ovulation. Includes the progestin-only pill, progestin subdermal implant, hormonal IUD, injectable progestin, and emergency contraception (e.g., morning-after pill). May also be used for heavy menstrual bleeding and dysmenorrhea.

Tqd6BI0.title: Steroid flare
Tqd6BI0.description: An inflammatory reaction secondary to injection of a crystal-containing steroid preparation, usually into a joint space. Often manifests as redness and swelling 12-24 hours after the injection.

hqdcyI0.title: Sport Concussion Assessment Tool-6
hqdcyI0.description: An assessment tool for individuals 13 years and older with a suspected concussion. Includes assessment of concussion symptoms and neurological and cognitive function. It is ideally used within 72 hours of the inciting event, but may be used up to 7 days later. For children 8-12 years of age, a child version (i.e., the Child SCAT-6) is used.

RqdlyI0.title: Sport Concussion Office Assessment Tool-6
RqdlyI0.description: An assessment tool for individuals 13 years and older with a suspected concussion. Includes assessment of concussion symptoms and neurological and cognitive function. It is used > 72 hours and up to a month after the inciting event. For children 8-12 years of age, a child version (i.e., the Child SCOAT-6) is used.

kqdmAI0.title: Recombinant LH
kqdmAI0.description: A subcutaneously injected drug used for follicle stimulation in women with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with profound LH deficiency who are infertile and wish to conceive. Adverse effects include ovarian enlargement and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.

OqdIAI0.title: Gonococcal proctitis
OqdIAI0.description: A sexually transmitted infection of the rectum caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, usually contracted through receptive anal intercourse. Symptoms include purulent discharge, anorectal bleeding and pain, rectal mucosa inflammation, and, less commonly, rectal abscess.

oqd0zI0.title: Maternal-fetal medicine
oqd0zI0.description: A subspecialty of obstetrics that is focused on the management of pregnancies in which there is a high risk of maternal and/or fetal complications.

pqdLzI0.title: Saline arthrography
pqdLzI0.description: Performed to assess for penetration of the joint capsule in the setting of a periarticular wound/injury. Used for larger joints (e.g., knee, shoulder). Involves the injection of an appropriate amount of saline into the joint and monitoring for leakage of saline from the wound, which implies joint space violation.

rqdf-I0.title: Last menstrual period
rqdf-I0.description: The date corresponding to the first day of bleeding during an individual's most recent menstrual cycle. It can be used to estimate a pregnant individual's estimated due date, which is assumed to be 280 days after the date of the last menstrual period.

sqdt-I0.title: Blood gas analysis
sqdt-I0.description: The analysis of respiratory and metabolic parameters measured in an arterial, capillary, venous, or mixed blood gas sample, e.g., pH, PCO₂, PO₂, HCO₃. Typically used to diagnose acid-base disorders.

destinations.label: Arterial blood gas analysis → Arterial blood gas analysis

uqdpZr0.title: Aberrant drug-related behaviors
uqdpZr0.description: Behaviors which may suggest abuse, misuse, or diversion of opioids. They may include: obtaining medication from nonmedical sources, requesting prescriptions early, frequently reporting loss of prescriptions, missing or canceling appointments at which no opioid refill is anticipated, obtaining prescriptions from multiple providers, and presenting to the emergency department for medications.

destinations.label: Chronic noncancer pain management → Opioid management

xqdE0r0.title: Y chromosome microdeletion
xqdE0r0.description: Family of genetic conditions that affect the long arm of the Y-chromosome and can cause male infertility, e.g., due to azoospermia or severe oligozoospermia. YCMDs are the second most commonly identified genetic cause of male infertility.

Bqdz0r0.title: Idiopathic dysspermatogenesis
Bqdz0r0.description: Any isolated abnormality in sperm count, motility, and/or morphology without an identifiable cause.

AqdRar0.title: Brief intervention for alcohol cessation
