AqdRar0.description: A 5-15 minute consultation aimed at educating patients about the adverse effects of alcohol use. Includes recommending a reduction in alcohol consumption and gauging patients' motivation to do so.

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Management of unhealthy alcohol use

0IdeYr0.title: Fusobacterium necrophorum
0IdeYr0.description: An anaerobic, non-spore-forming, pleomorphic gram-negative rod that exists as a commensal bacterium of the oral cavity, gastrointestinal system, and female genital tract. Can cause postanginal sepsis with suppurative thrombophlebitis of the jugular vein (Lemierre syndrome) and mastoiditis.

YIdnYr0.title: Fibropolycystic liver disease
YIdnYr0.description: An umbrella term for all conditions of the liver and biliary tract caused by abnormal embryologic development of the ductal plates. Clinical features may include portal hypertension, cholangitis, and gastrointestinal bleeding, although individuals may also be asymptomatic. Conditions can usually be differentiated via characteristic CT and/or MRI findings.

WIdPbr0.title: Corneal spud
WIdPbr0.description: A spud designed specifically to remove ocular foreign bodies.

dIdobr0.title: Corneal burr
dIdobr0.description: A dull burr designed specifically to brush off foreign bodies and rust rings from the cornea.

SIdyXr0.title: Thumb sign
SIdyXr0.description: An enlarged epiglottis (supraglottic narrowing), which has an appearance similar to a thumb on a lateral neck x-ray

PIdW1r0.title: Evidence of immunity to HBV
PIdW1r0.description: A set of criteria used to determine the need for vaccination against hepatitis B. Consists of evidence of a complete hepatitis B vaccine series and/or serologic evidence of immunity (i.e., anti-HBs levels ≥10 mIU/mL). The latter is required to confirm immunity in health care workers and pregnant individuals.

lIdv1r0.title: Amoxicillin/clavulanate
lIdv1r0.description: An antibiotic that is a combination of an aminopenicillin (amoxicillin) and a β-lactamase inhibitor (clavulanate). It has a broad spectrum of action against gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria. Commonly used to treat community-acquired pneumonia and acute bacterial rhinosinusitis.

NId-1r0.title: Ampicillin/sulbactam
NId-1r0.description: An antibiotic that is a combination of an aminopenicillin (ampicillin) and a β-lactamase inhibitor (sulbactam). Covers gram-positive, gram-negative, and anaerobic bacteria. Commonly used to treat skin and intraabdominal infections.

mIdVWr0.title: Piperacillin/tazobactam
mIdVWr0.description: An antibiotic that is a combination of an ureidopenicillin (piperacillin) and a β-lactamase inhibitor (tazobactam). Covers gram-positive bacteria, gram-negative bacteria, and anaerobes. Commonly used to treat intraabdominal infections and hospital-acquired pneumonia.

5IdiWr0.title: Ceftolozane
5IdiWr0.description: A fifth-generation cephalosporin that is effective against gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria. Often given in combination with tazobactam, a β-lactamase inhibitor.

MIdMWr0.title: Elliptical excision
MIdMWr0.description: A procedure in which an entire skin lesion or portion of a lesion is removed with a scalpel in a fusiform (spindle) shape at a length-to-width ratio of 3:1. If the entire lesion is removed with appropriate margins of healthy tissue on either side, this method may be used to obtain diagnostic samples from pigmented skin lesions to rule out melanoma.

LIdwWr0.title: Melanoma microsatellitosis
LIdwWr0.description: One or more distinct groups of melanoma cells that are near the primary melanoma lesion (e.g., adjacent to or below it) but separated from it by any amount of normal tissue.

oId0dr0.title: Surgical margin
oId0dr0.description: The area of tissue that is removed around a tumor specimen. Positive surgical margins contain cancerous cells, negative margins do not.

qIdCdr0.title: Cross-body adduction
qIdCdr0.description: A physical examination maneuver in which the patient elevates their arm to 90° and actively adducts it across their body. Pain elicited by this maneuver suggests acromioclavicular joint pathology.

DId1Ur0.title: Contraindications for induction of labor
DId1Ur0.description: Contraindications to induction of labor include vasa previa, complete placenta previa, transverse fetal lie, umbilical cord prolapse, active maternal genital herpes, and a previous classical cesarean section.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Induction of labor

yIdd2r0.title: Triangle of Koch
yIdd2r0.description: Small anatomical region within the atrioventricular septum superior to the coronary sinus. The AV node is located at its apex.

drdoTr0.title: Apathetic hyperthyroidism
drdoTr0.description: A manifestation of hyperthyroidism in older adults in which the predominant symptoms include depression, apathy, lethargy, and weight loss.

irdJSr0.title: Triheptanoin
irdJSr0.description: A medium-chain triglyceride used as an alternative energy source in the treatment of long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders.

jrd_Sr0.title: HADHA gene
jrd_Sr0.description: A gene encoding the alpha subunit of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein, which catalyzes the last three steps of mitochondrial beta-oxidation of long-chain fatty acids. HADHA mutations lead to trifunctional protein deficiency or LCHAD deficiency.

PrdWhr0.title: Long-chain hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase
PrdWhr0.description: An enzyme of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein complex responsible for the breakdown of long-chain fatty acids in the fatty acid β-oxidation pathway.

JrdsRr0.title: High-dose euglycemic insulin therapy
JrdsRr0.description: The simultaneous administration of high-dose insulin and glucose. Harnesses the inotropic effect of insulin while preventing hypoglycemia. Used in the treatment of beta blocker poisoning and calcium channel blocker poisoning.

destinations.label: Cardiovascular drug poisoning → Antidotes and dosages

trdXQr0.title: Bradycardia workup
trdXQr0.description: A collection of diagnostic tests used to evaluate bradycardia. Depending on the suspected diagnosis, these may include ECG, BMP, troponin, thyroid function tests, and calcium and magnesium levels. Additional testing is guided by the history and results of initial tests and may include CXR, echocardiogram, Holter monitoring, brain natriuretic peptide, and drug levels (e.g., digoxin).

FrdgQr0.title: Respiratory syncytial virus vaccine
FrdgQr0.description: A bivalent vaccine based on the prefusion form of the RSV fusion (F) protein. A one-time dose is recommended for active immunization of adults ≥ 60 years of age and for pregnant individuals between 32 and 36 weeks' gestation for passive immunization of the infant.

-rdDPr0.title: Digitalis effect
-rdDPr0.description: A set of characteristic ECG findings associated with digoxin use but not necessarily digoxin toxicity. Findings include shortened QT intervals, scooped or sagging appearing ST segments, shortened PR intervals, and/or flat and inverted T waves.

Z7dZ4r0.title: Hoarseness
Z7dZ4r0.description: A self-reported symptom of perceived change(s) in one's voice, e.g., raspy, strained, or weak. Often mistakenly used as a synonym for dysphonia, which is a medical diagnosis that may manifest with hoarseness.

07de4r0.title: Blood alcohol concentration
07de4r0.description: The concentration of alcohol in the blood, which is measured in mg/dL or converted to a percentage. The alcohol concentration depends on the amount of alcohol consumed, genetics, and/or medical history (e.g., bariatric surgery).

Y7dn4r0.title: Flocked swab
Y7dn4r0.description: A swab that contains multiple nylon fibers arranged perpendicularly to the plastic applicator stick. These nylon fibers increase the surface area of the swab and allow for easier release of the specimen into the collection medium. Studies have demonstrated increased sensitivity compared to cotton-tipped or rayon swabs.

c7dakr0.title: Hepatocellular injury pattern
c7dakr0.description: A pattern of liver chemistry abnormalities characterized by disproportionate elevation of alanine transaminase (ALT) and aspartate transaminase (AST) compared to alkaline phosphatase (ALP).

17d2kr0.title: Cholestatic injury pattern
17d2kr0.description: A pattern of liver chemistry abnormalities characterized by disproportionate elevation of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) compared to alanine transaminase (ALT) and aspartate transaminase (AST).

W7dPkr0.title: Nonsevere penicillin reaction
W7dPkr0.description: Any symptom following exposure to penicillin that indicates a low risk for anaphylaxis with repeated exposure. Includes nonsevere allergic symptoms (mild urticaria, mild immediate rashes, and delayed nonurticarial maculopapular or morbilliform rash), nonallergic adverse effects (e.g., injection site irritation, diarrhea, headache), and a family history of penicillin allergy without personal exposure or reaction. Allergy testing is recommended to confirm the penicillin allergy. If testing confirms an allergy, affected individuals can typically receive cephalosporins safely.

d7dokr0.title: Severe penicillin reaction
d7dokr0.description: The development of life-threatening or serious adverse effects following exposure to penicillin. Includes immediate type 1 hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis, hypotension, bronchospasm, angioedema, urticaria) within 1-2 hours, serious cutaneous adverse reactions (e.g., drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and hematological or organ involvement (e.g., serum sickness, acute interstitial nephritis, hemolytic anemia). Affected individuals should avoid all β-lactam antibiotics. If no alternative options exist, desensitization is required prior to β-lactam administration.

V7dGkr0.title: Dermabrasion
V7dGkr0.description: A dermatologic procedure in which a rotating brush removes the superficial layers of skin to improve the appearance of wrinkles and scars, typically on the face.

S7dyOr0.title: Suturing
S7dyOr0.description: A procedure used to approximate wound edges to promote healing and minimize scarring. Performed using a specialized needle and suture (thread).

h7dclr0.title: Tissue stapling
h7dclr0.description: A procedure in which a device inserts staples to approximate wound edges. Suitable for low-tension wounds with straight edges. Commonly used to close surgical wounds as an alternative to suturing and in situations in which speed is essential (e.g., brisk bleeding from the scalp).

j7d_lr0.title: Composite International Diagnostic Interview Bipolar Screen
j7d_lr0.description: A brief screening tool for bipolar disorder. The first two questions ask about euphoria and irritability. If patients have experienced either of these symptoms, a third question is asked about impulsive and/or disinhibited behavior. If this initial screening is positive, an additional 9 questions are asked about symptoms.

O7dINr0.title: National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) quick screen
O7dINr0.description: A 4-item screening tool used to assess for substance use. Asks about the frequency of past-year use (from never to daily) of tobacco, recreational drugs, prescription drugs for recreational purposes, and excessive alcohol (≥ 4 drinks a day).

m7dVmr0.title: 4Ps
m7dVmr0.description: A screening questionnaire for substance use. The 4Ps correspond to a personal history of unhealthy substance use in the past, or substance use by a partner, parents, or peers. A modified version for prenatal use, the 4Ps Plus, involves an additional question about recent cigarette, alcohol, or recreational drug use during pregnancy.

57dimr0.title: Invasive prenatal diagnostic testing
57dimr0.description: An examination in which fetal or placental cells are obtained via penetration of the uterine wall (i.e., via chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis) to perform definitive genetic or chromosomal diagnosis.

J7ds5r0.title: Bimanual synkinesis
J7ds5r0.description: A phenomenon in which the voluntary movement of one hand is involuntarily mirrored in the other hand. Common finding in Kallmann syndrome.

q7dC5r0.title: Biopsychosocial model
q7dC5r0.description: A model of medical care that considers the interconnected impact on an individual’s health of biological factors (e.g., age, genetics, medical conditions), social factors (e.g., race, ethnicity, culture, education), and psychological factors (e.g., stress, trauma, mood) by incorporating multiple disciplines and treatment modalities.

H7dKMr0.title: Pain, enjoyment of life and general activity scale
H7dKMr0.description: A validated scale used to evaluate patients with chronic pain. Patients are asked to rate their pain and its impact on enjoyment of life and general activity. Each element is scored from 0 (no pain/does not interfere) to 10 (worst possible pain/completely interferes) and the results are averaged. A ≥ 30% reduction in the average score is considered an adequate response.

t7dXnr0.title: Child life specialist
t7dXnr0.description: A health provider specialized in supporting children receiving medical care, e.g., preparing them for hospital-based procedures that can cause pain and anxiety, facilitating activities to stimulate development, and assisting family members.

F7dgnr0.title: Circulatory hypoxia
F7dgnr0.description: Inadequate supply of oxygen to tissues despite normal arterial oxygen content. Caused by circulatory system disruptions, such as shock (e.g., severe hemorrhage, cardiac failure) and localized hypoperfusion (e.g., thromboembolic vascular occlusion, compartment syndrome).

u7dpnr0.title: Clinical features of stimulant withdrawal
u7dpnr0.description: Dysphoria, psychomotor slowing, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and/or drug craving associated with the sudden cessation of stimulants after prolonged use.

destinations.label: Stimulant intoxication and withdrawal → Stimulant withdrawal

A7dRor0.title: Tetanus-prone wounds
A7dRor0.description: An injury in which there is substantial risk of a tetanus infection developing. Includes dirty wounds (e.g., contaminated with dirt, feces, soil, and/or saliva), deep injuries (e.g., avulsion injuries, crush injuries, puncture wounds), and thermal injuries (e.g., burns, frostbite).

ZHdZKr0.title: Opioid tolerance
ZHdZKr0.description: A physiological state in which patients with chronic opioid use require increasingly larger amounts to achieve the desired effect and/or experience increasingly diminished effects with use of the same amount. More specifically defined by the FDA as use for at least one week of any of the following opioid doses (or an equianalgesic dosage of another opioid): oral morphine 60 mg/per day, oral oxycodone 30 mg/day, oral hydromorphone 8 mg/day, oral oxymorphone 25 mg/day, or transdermal fentanyl 25 mcg/hour.

0HdeKr0.title: Puncture wound
0HdeKr0.description: An injury sustained from penetration of the skin by a sharp, pointed object (e.g., metal nail, needle, animal teeth, piece of wood). The wound is often small with minimal bleeding, but puncture wounds are associated with an increased risk of infection, as dirt and bacteria penetrate into deep tissues.

dHdo6r0.title: NT
dHdo6r0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Nuchal translucency
2) Nasotracheal

eHdx6r0.title: Benefits and risks of opioid therapy
eHdx6r0.description: Benefit is a possible minor reduction in pain. Risks include the various adverse effects of opioids (including the development of opioid use disorder), worsening of pain due to opioid-induced hyperalgesia, and potential impact on employment opportunities (e.g., in safety-critical jobs).

destinations.label: Chronic noncancer pain management → Opioid management

2HdTpr0.title: Quickening
2HdTpr0.description: The first perception of fetal movement by the mother. Usually felt between 16 to 20 weeks' gestation, with patients who have been pregnant previously noticing the movements sooner than patients who are pregnant for the first time.

SHdypr0.title: Orogastric tube
SHdypr0.description: A flexible tube that is passed through the mouth into the stomach.  Uses include gastric decompression (e.g., in bowel obstruction or intubated patients) and gastric lavage (e.g., in poisoned patients).

hHdcJr0.title: Levin tube
hHdcJr0.description: A type of nasogastric tube with a single lumen and multiple holes at the distal end.  Not suitable for continuous suction because of the risk of gastric injury.

3HdSJr0.title: Salem sump tube
3HdSJr0.description: A type of nasogastric tube with two lumens.  The second lumen vents to air and prevents excessive vacuum, protecting the gastric mucosa.  Suitable for continuous suction and longer-term drainage.

RHdlJr0.title: Gram-negative folliculitis
RHdlJr0.description: A localized inflammation of the hair follicle and sebaceous glands that is primarily caused by gram-negative bacteria (e.g., Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Serratia marcescens, Klebsiella spp., Proteus mirabilis). Characterized by perioral and perinasal pustules, papules, and nodules. Typically occurs after long periods of systemic or topical antibiotic use (e.g., systemic tetracycline for acne vulgaris or rosacea).

QHduJr0.title: Recalcitrant acne
QHduJr0.description: A severe form of inflammatory acne vulgaris that does not respond to standard treatment.

4Hd3qr0.title: Bolster dressing
4Hd3qr0.description: A compression dressing used to manage or prevent auricular hematomas. The affected area is padded (e.g., with dental rolls and/or occlusive gauze) and the dressing is secured with nonabsorbable sutures.

qHdCrr0.title: Fever phobia
qHdCrr0.description: The unfounded belief that fever is harmful and, if left untreated, will lead to severe complications (e.g., seizures, brain damage, and/or death).

rHdf7r0.title: Mirror laryngoscopy
rHdf7r0.description: A procedure in which a mirror is used to visualize the larynx down to the level of the vocal cords. Can be performed in office with or without topical anesthetic.

7Hd47r0.title: Anal advancement flap
7Hd47r0.description: Surgical procedure in which damaged anal tissue (i.e., due to fissure or fistula) is excised and healthy tissue is transferred onto the fissure or fistula base.

AHdRGr0.title: Immersion syndrome
AHdRGr0.description: A series of autonomic and respiratory changes caused by sudden immersion in cold water. Typically begins with an involuntary gasp, marked tachypnea, and peripheral vasoconstriction and then progresses to muscle fatigue, hypothermia, and cardiac arrhythmia if immersion continues.

_Hd5Gr0.title: Shallow water blackout
_Hd5Gr0.description: A loss of consciousness while diving that is due to hypoxia caused by intentional hyperventilation, which blunts the respiratory drive. May lead to drowning.

zHdrGr0.title: Mildly elevated transaminases
zHdrGr0.description: A laboratory finding of ALT and/or AST levels 2–5x the upper limit of normal.

-HdDGr0.title: Borderline elevated transaminases
-HdDGr0.description: A laboratory finding of ALT and/or AST levels < 2x the upper limit of normal.

Ysdntr0.title: Laryngopharyngeal reflux
Ysdntr0.description: The retrograde flow of stomach contents into the upper respiratory tract (e.g., pharynx, larynx) leading to irritation of the epithelial lining.

Xsd9tr0.title: Hidradenitis suppurativa-associated comorbidities
Xsd9tr0.description: Includes metabolic syndrome and its components (obesity, diabetes mellitus type 2, hypertension, dyslipidemia), polycystic ovarian syndrome, inflammatory bowel disease, and inflammatory arthropathies.

esdxFr0.title: Clinical features of meningitis
esdxFr0.description: Features commonly include fever, altered mental status, and meningismus (headache, neck stiffness, and photophobia). Other features may include nausea, vomiting, and seizures.

KsdUDr0.title: Postvaccination fever
KsdUDr0.description: A fever that develops within 24 hours after receiving a vaccination. Part of the normal immune response, the fever is usually self-limited (within 48 hours) and can be treated with antipyretics to ease discomfort.

psdLDr0.title: Reflex urine culture
psdLDr0.description: A method for ordering urine cultures in which the culture is only performed if pyuria is detected on urinalysis. Reduces the number of false positive culture results (e.g., due to asymptomatic bacteriuria or contaminated samples) and health care spending by reducing the number of urine cultures sent.

qsdCDr0.title: Nirsevimab
qsdCDr0.description: A monoclonal antibody against respiratory syncytial virus fusion (RSV F) protein that provides passive immunity against RSV infection for ∼ 5 months. Used for RSV prophylaxis in all infants < 8 months of age and in children < 24 months of age with specific indications for RSV prophylaxis.

tsdX9r0.title: RSV season
tsdX9r0.description: The months in which the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) circulates in the community. In the United States, RSV season is typically from October through March. Areas with tropical climates (e.g., Florida, Hawaii, Guam, Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, US Pacific Islands) and Alaska may have unpredictable and longer RSV seasons.

Fsdg9r0.title: Specific indications for RSV prophylaxis in the second year of life
Fsdg9r0.description: Chronic lung disease of prematurity requiring intervention in the 6 months prior to RSV season, severely immunocompromised state, cystic fibrosis associated with severe lung disease or poor weight gain, and children of American Indian and/or Alaska Native descent.

usdp9r0.title: Common features of upper respiratory tract infection
usdp9r0.description: Features include nasal congestion, sore throat, fever, rhinorrhea, and cough. Fever should resolve within 2–3 days and other symptoms typically resolve within 14 days.

destinations.label: Upper respiratory tract infection → Clinical evaluation

BsdzCr0.title: RSV prophylaxis
BsdzCr0.description: Passive immunization with RSV monoclonal antibodies. Indicated in infants < 8 months of age if a maternal RSV vaccine was not administered during pregnancy at least 14 days before birth. Additional RSV prophylaxis is indicated in children 8-24 months of age with risk factors for severe RSV infection.

XGd9Br0.title: Secondary lymphoid follicle
XGd9Br0.description: A structure of the lymph node cortex that consists of a dense mantle zone surrounding a pale germinal center in which B cell proliferation, differentiation, and immunoglobulin class switching occur.

cGdayr0.title: Primary lymphoid follicle
cGdayr0.description: A structure of the lymph node cortex that consists of dense aggregates of naive B lymphocytes. Following B-cell activation by antigen presentation, primary lymphoid follicles transform into secondary lymphoid follicles, which contain germinal centers and are the site of B cell proliferation, differentiation, and immunoglobulin class switching.

dGdoyr0.title: Meningitis PCR panel
dGdoyr0.description: A PCR panel that tests CSF for 14 pathogens known to cause meningitis and/or encephalitis. Includes six bacterial pathogens (E. coli, H. influenzae, L. monocytogenes, N. meningitidis, Group B streptococcus, S. pneumoniae), six viral pathogens (Cytomegalovirus, Enterovirus, Herpes simplex virus 1/2, Human herpes virus 6, Human parechovirus, Varicella zoster virus), and one fungal pathogen (C. neoformans/gattii). As turnaround times are faster compared to CSF cultures, results can expedite tailoring or discontinuing of antibiotics.

eGdxyr0.title: Body packing
eGdxyr0.description: The intentional or coerced ingestion of large quantities of a controlled substance in packaging that prevents absorption, typically as part of a smuggling operation.

destinations.label: Approach to the poisoned patient → Internally concealed controlled substances

gGdFAr0.title: Indications for additional RSV prophylaxis
gGdFAr0.description: Infants: premature birth at < 29 weeks' gestational age, chronic lung disease of prematurity, and hemodynamically significant congenital heart disease; should be considered for conditions that impair mucous clearance (e.g., SMA). Children 12-24 months of age: chronic lung disease of prematurity requiring intervention in the 6 months prior to RSV season, severely immunocompromised state, cystic fibrosis associated with severe lung disease or poor weight gain, and American Indian and/or Alaska Native descent.

HGdK070.title: Adenocarcinoma in situ of the cervix
HGdK070.description: A premalignant precursor to adenocarcinoma of the cervix

media.title: Adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS) of the cervix

GGdB070.title: iPLEDGE
GGdB070.description: A mandatory FDA program designed to reduce the risk of fetal exposure to isotretinoin. Patients, clinicians, and pharmacists must be enrolled in the program in order to receive, prescribe, or dispense the drug. Prescriptions are limited to 30 days of medication at a time and patients must agree not to donate blood during treatment or for 30 days afterwards. Patients who can become pregnant must agree to use two forms of contraception and undergo monthly pregnancy tests throughout treatment and for one month after.

FGdga70.title: Fluorescein dye disappearance test
FGdga70.description: A noninvasive test to assess the patency of a lacrimal duct. The test is considered abnormal if fluorescein dye is cleared asymmetrically within 5 minutes of being placed in both eyes, i.e., pooling of fluorescein in only one eye suggests lacrimal duct obstruction.

EGd8a70.title: Distracting injury
EGd8a70.description: An injury that diverts attention away from another injury, e.g., pain from a hip fracture that distracts a patient from pain from a cervical fracture or an injury that appears alarming and distracts the health care provider from other injuries. Often seen in polytrauma. May mask the severity of other injuries and lead to missed injuries and delays in care.

wGdhY70.title: Red flags of hoarseness
wGdhY70.description: Clinical features in individuals with hoarseness and/or dysphonia that suggest a serious underlying health condition: signs of respiratory distress, recent laryngeal trauma (e.g., endotracheal intubation or surgery of the head or neck), history of neck radiation, neck mass, history of tobacco use disorder, neurological symptoms (e.g., dysarthria), dysphagia, and unintentional weight loss. The presence of one or more red flags requires further evaluation.

CGdqY70.title: Fetal retinoid syndrome
CGdqY70.description: A range of birth defects resulting from in utero exposure to retinoids (e.g., systemic isotretinoin), which are teratogens. Includes craniofacial abnormalities (e.g., cleft palate, microtia, microphthalmia), central nervous system defects (e.g., hydrocephalus, microcephaly, intellectual disability), congenital heart disease, and effects on other organs (e.g., kidneys, thymus, parathyroid gland).

xGdEY70.title: Cycloplegic agent
xGdEY70.description: A topical ophthalmic drug that temporarily paralyzes the ciliary and pupillary sphincter muscles and prevents contraction of the pupillary dilator muscle. Used to dilate the pupils for diagnostic and surgical procedures, and to prevent the formation of synechiae in anterior uveitis.

ctdac70.title: Clinical features of pulmonary edema
ctdac70.description: Progressive dyspnea and tachypnea, signs of hypoxia (e.g., cyanosis, tachycardia), and cough, possibly with pink frothy sputum or expectoration. Physical examination findings include increased fremitus, dullness to percussion, and, in cardiogenic edema, S3 gallop, murmur, elevated JVP, and peripheral edema.

2tdT170.title: Costimulation receptor
2tdT170.description: A class of receptors that modulate an immune cell's response to initial signals (e.g., antigen presentation) and thus facilitate its activation.

ftdk170.title: Ethanol saliva testing
ftdk170.description: A rapid measurement of alcohol in saliva obtained with a point of care saliva test strip. Results estimate the corresponding blood alcohol concentration. May be used by law enforcement to evaluate for alcohol intoxication. Recent smoking can affect results.

Ttd6170.title: Breath ethanol analysis
Ttd6170.description: A rapid measurement of alcohol in breath samples obtained by blowing into a device. Results are the estimated corresponding blood alcohol concentration. May be used by law enforcement to evaluate for alcohol intoxication. Factors that affect results include noncooperation, drinking water ≤ 5 minutes prior to testing, and breathing technique (e.g., hyperventilation).

gtdF170.title: Fatty acid ethyl esters
gtdF170.description: Nonoxidative ethanol metabolites often detectable in blood, hair, and meconium after the ingestion of ethanol. Can be used as a confirmatory test for ethanol within 24 hours of ingestion, but may be detectable for up to 8 days.

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Confirmation of alcohol use

Stdy170.title: Parametrium
Stdy170.description: Fibrofatty connective tissue that surrounds the uterus and the supravaginal portion of the cervix. Is composed of the round ligament, broad ligament, cardinal ligament, and uterosacral ligaments. The uterine pedicle, lymphatics, nerves, and the ureter pass through the parametrium.

OtdId70.title: Atypical rib
OtdId70.description: A rib that deviates from the standard anatomical characteristics and functionality of a typical rib. Ribs 1, 2, 11, and 12 are considered atypical. Some sources also consider rib 10 to be atypical.

ltdvd70.title: Typical rib
ltdvd70.description: A rib that has a standard anatomical structure, including a head, neck, angle, shaft, and tubercle, which articulates with the corresponding vertebra. Ribs 3-10 are considered typical ribs; however, some sources consider rib 10 to be atypical.

ptdLe70.title: Clascoterone
ptdLe70.description: A topical antiandrogen used in the treatment of acne vulgaris. Adverse effects include erythema, pruritus, and scaling.

Dtd1f70.title: Myocardial hibernation
Dtd1f70.description: Myocardial dysfunction in chronic ischemic heart disease. May be reversible if blood flow is restored (e.g., via percutaneous coronary intervention) or oxygen demand is reduced.

xtdEf70.title: Synthetic cannabinoids
xtdEf70.description: A class of synthesized cannabinoid receptor-binding substances that mimic the effect of THC and are used recreationally. Street names include K2 and Spice.

ZFdZg70.title: Cardiac rehabilitation
ZFdZg70.description: A supervised program for individuals with heart failure that combines health education, exercise training, nutrition counseling, and behavioral health interventions to help patients achieve and maintain their optimal level of functioning and independence.

0Fdeg70.title: Secondary restless legs syndrome
0Fdeg70.description: Restless legs syndrome that results from certain conditions (e.g., iron deficiency, end-stage renal disease) or drugs (e.g., dopamine antagonists).

YFdng70.title: Heart failure with improved ejection fraction
YFdng70.description: Previous heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, with a follow-up ejection fraction measurement > 40%.

bFdHg70.title: Heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction
bFdHg70.description: Heart failure with an LVEF of 41–49% and evidence of increased LV filling pressures, e.g., increased natriuretic peptides and hemodynamic measurements.

3FdS370.title: Clonal hematopoiesis
3FdS370.description: A type of premalignant hematological condition in which a population of cells develops from a single mutated hematopoietic stem cell. Examples include clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential and clonal cytopenia of undetermined significance. May progress to myeloid neoplasms such as myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia.

RFdl370.title: Advanced heart failure
RFdl370.description: Severe symptoms of heart failure that persist despite optimal management; require repeated hospitalizations and/or treatment with IV diuretics, inotropes, or vasoactive medications; and in which patients have a severely reduced exercise capacity (e.g., 6-minute walk test distance < 300 m, peak VO₂ < 14 mL/kg/minute).

iFdJ370.title: Vertical mattress suture
iFdJ370.description: A two-stitch suturing technique combining deep and superficial loops. The first stitch is deep and wide and the second stitch is superficial and near the wound edge. Both stitches are perpendicular to the wound. Used to close a deep or gaping wound, especially in areas that are under high tension, such as joints. Can evert the wound edge and reduces the need for layered closure.

QFdu370.title: Horizontal mattress suture
QFdu370.description: A square-shaped stitch with two stitches visible on the surface of the skin, parallel to the wound, and two stitches under the skin, perpendicular to the wound. Used to close a deep or gaping wound in areas that are under high tension (e.g., joints) or if eversion of the wound edge is challenging (e.g., in stellate wounds). Can also be used to achieve hemostasis.

jFd_370.title: Deep dermal suture
jFd_370.description: The placement of interrupted absorbable stitches in the dermal layer to eliminate dead space prior to superficial closure. The stitch starts and ends in the base of the wound so that the knot can be buried. Used to close deep wounds in areas under high tension or with cosmetic significance.

PFdWR70.title: Running subcuticular suture
PFdWR70.description: A continuous, superficial stitch that loops from one side of the wound to the other across the dermal plane. Commonly used for cosmetic closures, especially in areas where minimal scarring is desired.

4Fd3R70.title: Simple running suture
4Fd3R70.description: A continuous stitch that crosses the wound diagonally. Used for rapid closure of long wounds and for simultaneous approximation of the epidermis and dermis.

kFdmR70.title: Translation (osteopathy)
kFdmR70.description: Linear movement along a horizontal, coronal, or sagittal axis. Translation between joint surfaces is commonly referred to as glide. In the cervical spine, horizontal translation of the vertebrae corresponds with sidebending in the opposite direction (e.g., translation of C5 to the right leads to sidebending of C5 to the left).

oFd0Q70.title: Lyme serology
oFd0Q70.description: A testing protocol for the indirect detection of Borrelia burgdorferi. First, an immunoassay detecting IgM and IgG antibodies (tier 1) is performed. If positive, an IgG and/or IgM immunoblot (tier 2) is performed to confirm the diagnosis of Lyme disease.

6FdjQ70.title: Clinical features of pneumothorax
6FdjQ70.description: Includes acute pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, reduced or absent breath sounds, hyperresonance on percussion, and subcutaneous emphysema on palpation. In individuals with tension pneumothorax, clinical features also include distended neck veins, hypotension, and pulsus paradoxus.

JFdsQ70.title: Combined orbital fracture
JFdsQ70.description: A fracture that involves an orbital wall and the orbital rim.

qFdCQ70.title: Oculocardiac reflex
qFdCQ70.description: A marked decrease in heart rate triggered by pressure on the ocular globe and/or traction of the extraocular muscles. Often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and syncope. Junctional rhythm or asystole may occur in extreme cases. Most commonly associated with facial trauma and ocular surgery.

zFdrk70.title: Gestational transient thyrotoxicosis
zFdrk70.description: A type of hCG-mediated hyperthyroidism that is self-limited, resolving in the first half of pregnancy. May be associated with hyperemesis gravidarum. Symptoms of thyrotoxicosis are often subclinical.

a8dQO70.title: Reproductive coercion
a8dQO70.description: A form of intimate partner violence in which an individual attempts to control their partner's reproductive choices. Includes sabotage of birth control methods, coercion into unprotected sex, forcing the continuation of an unwanted pregnancy or the termination of a wanted pregnancy, and injuring a pregnant partner with the intention of causing a miscarriage.

Y8dnO70.title: Drug-induced cognitive impairment
Y8dnO70.description: An altered mental state (e.g., confusion, agitation, hallucinations, decreased psychomotor activity) due to a reversible adverse effect of medication. Older adults, especially those with dementia or multiple medical problems requiring a complex drug regimen, and individuals with substance use disorders are at highest risk. Most commonly caused by anticholinergics, sedatives, diuretics, and antihistamines.

c8dal70.title: Calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonists
c8dal70.description: A class of medication that selectively inhibits the effects of calcitonin gene-related peptide, a neuropeptide involved in pain modulation. Used for acute treatment and prevention of migraines.

V8dGl70.title: E/e′ ratio
V8dGl70.description: An echocardiographic measure of left ventricular filling pressure that can be used to assess diastolic function.

T8d6N70.title: Levonorgestrel (emergency contraceptive)
T8d6N70.description: A high dose of progestin that is taken as an oral pill to prevent pregnancy after unprotected or inadequately protected sexual intercourse.

h8dcm70.title: Ubrogepant
h8dcm70.description: A calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist used for acute treatment of migraines in adults. Common adverse effects include nausea, dry mouth, and somnolence.

38dSm70.title: Rimegepant
38dSm70.description: A calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist used for acute treatment of migraines and prevention of episodic migraine in adults. Common adverse effects include nausea, abdominal pain, and dyspepsia.

R8dlm70.title: 5-HT1F receptor agonists
R8dlm70.description: A class of drugs that selectively target and activate the 5-HT1F receptor. Used for acute treatment of migraines. They do not cause vasoconstriction, making them an alternative for patients with contraindications to vasoconstrictive agents.

N8d-570.title: HPV-based testing
N8d-570.description: A cervical cancer screening strategy that includes either primary HPV DNA testing alone or cotesting (i.e., a Pap smear in combination with HPV DNA testing). HPV-based testing is more accurate at cervical cancer risk estimation than cytology-alone screening.

58diM70.title: HepB vaccine nonresponder
58diM70.description: An individual whose anti-HBs level remains below 10 IU/mL despite receiving two complete series of HepB vaccine and is therefore susceptible to infection. Anti-HBs level should be measured 1-2 months after completion of the second vaccine series.

r8dfL70.title: Choosing Wisely campaign
r8dfL70.description: A campaign by the American Board of Internal Medicine Foundation targeting health care providers and patients that promotes evidence-based health care to reduce the overuse of medical interventions. Includes recommendations on unnecessary testing and treatment from various specialty societies.

s8dtL70.title: Pseudomeningocele
s8dtL70.description: A collection of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in the soft tissues of the back caused by a tear in the dura mater. Most commonly due to trauma or spinal surgery.

t8dXo70.title: Rumack-Matthew nomogram
t8dXo70.description: A graph used in the treatment of acute acetaminophen (APAP) toxicity to determine if the threshold for N-acetylcysteine (NAC) administration has been reached. The patient's serum APAP level is plotted against the time since ingestion. Treatment with NAC is indicated if the plotted point falls above the treatment line.

F8dgo70.title: Quick start approach
F8dgo70.description: A strategy for initiating a new contraceptive immediately after the prescription has been given rather than waiting for the next menstrual cycle. Backup contraception may be required depending on when the contraceptive is initiated during the menstrual cycle.

x8dEK70.title: Stercoral ulcer
x8dEK70.description: An ulcer of the distal colon or rectum caused by fecal impaction. Most commonly affects bedridden patients with long-term constipation.

B8dzK70.title: American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) impairment scale
B8dzK70.description: A standardized grading system to assess and categorize the extent and severity of spinal cord injuries. The scale has 5 grades (A-E) based on preserved sensory and motor function below the spinal cord lesion. Grade A indicates a complete spinal cord injury while grade E indicates normal sensory and muscle function. Should be assessed after the acute phase in which spinal shock occurs (typically 4-12 weeks).

y8dd670.title: Sternal fracture
y8dd670.description: A fracture of the sternum that typically occurs as a result of blunt chest trauma. Clinical features include chest pain and tenderness, difficulty breathing, and bruising over the sternal area. Treatment involves pain control and, in severe cases, surgical stabilization.

_8d5670.title: Hip dislocation
_8d5670.description: Displacement of the femur head from the acetabular socket. Often occurs following high-energy trauma or after total hip replacement surgery and manifests with hip pain radiating to the knee. The direction of the dislocation can be anterior or posterior.

Xud9p70.title: Age-related emphysema
Xud9p70.description: The decline in lung function associated with normal aging. Caused by reduced lung elasticity and respiratory muscle strength and increased chest wall stiffness. Results in airspace enlargement and reduced ventilatory control.

destinations.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease → Subtypes and variants

WudPJ70.title: Clinical features of respiratory failure
WudPJ70.description: Signs and symptoms indicating failure of adequate gas exchange. Features include those associated with hypoxemia (e.g., mental status changes, cyanosis, bradycardia), hypercapnia (e.g., hypopnea, somnolence, headache, asterixis), increased work of breathing (e.g., tachypnea, nasal flaring, grunting, intercostal or subcostal skin retractions), and respiratory muscle fatigue.

destinations.label: Respiratory failure and arrest → Clinical features

dudoJ70.title: Clinical features of ARDS
dudoJ70.description: Includes rapid onset of dyspnea, tachypnea, tachycardia, cyanosis, diffuse crackles, and, less commonly, fever, cough, and chest pain.

destinations.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome → Clinical features

VudGJ70.title: CXR findings in atelectasis
VudGJ70.description: The direct findings of lobar collapse include displacement of fissures and homogeneous lobar opacification. Indirect signs include ipsilateral elevation of diaphragm, mediastinal shift towards the affected side, and contralateral hyperlucency and hyperinflation.

2udTq70.title: Toxic alcohol
2udTq70.description: A type of alcohol that can cause organ damage and/or death if ingested, most often due to the accumulation of toxic metabolites. Toxic alcohols include ethylene glycol, methanol, isopropyl alcohol, diethylene glycol, and propylene glycol.

fudkq70.title: Meningococcal disease
fudkq70.description: Any infection caused by the pathogen Neisseria meningitidis. Includes meningitis and meningococcal septicemia.

Tud6q70.title: Clinical features of atelectasis
Tud6q70.description: Include acute dyspnea, chest pain, tachypnea, tachycardia, and/or cyanosis. Physical examination findings on the affected side include dullness to percussion, diminished breath sounds, decreased fremitus, and/or tracheal deviation towards the affected lung.

mudV770.title: CIS
mudV770.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Carcinoma in situ
2. Clinically isolated syndrome

5udi770.title: Bacterial meningitis score
5udi770.description: A score used to guide management in well-appearing children > 28 days old with CSF pleocytosis. Scoring criteria include CSF analysis (i.e., elevated ANC, elevated protein, positive gram stain), elevated peripheral ANC, and seizure. If all of these factors are negative, a child is very low risk for bacterial meningitis.

Ludw770.title: Chest x-ray of pleural effusion
Ludw770.description: Findings depend on x-ray view, patient positioning, and size of effusion. Small effusions may only be apparent on lateral decubitus as a thin radiopaque area (i.e., a layer of fluid) or on upright PA/AP view as blunting of the costophrenic angle. Larger effusions appear on a PA/AP view as a homogeneous radiopaque area with a meniscus-shaped margin (meniscus sign); they can cause complete opacification of the affected lung and mediastinal shift/tracheal deviation away from the affected lung.

oud0H70.title: Thoracic ultrasound in pleural effusion
oud0H70.description: Findings include a hypoechoic or anechoic fluid collection in the lower margins of the pleural cavity (costodiaphragmatic recess).

qudCH70.title: Alpha-gal syndrome
qudCH70.description: An IgE-mediated allergic reaction to the oligosaccharide galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose found on the cells of nonprimate mammals (e.g., cows, pigs, lambs). Sensitization is believed to occur after a parasitic infection or the bite of a tick (in the US, the Lone star tick). Clinical features include anaphylaxis, urticaria, and/or GI symptoms (e.g., nausea, abdominal pain) after ingestion of mammalian-derived products.

rudfs70.title: Therapeutic lumbar puncture
rudfs70.description: The use of lumbar puncture to either deliver intrathecal medications or to remove CSF (in order to reduce intracranial pressure).

7ud4s70.title: Isometric contraction
7ud4s70.description: A muscle contraction in which the muscle does not change in length.

HudKs70.title: Reciprocal inhibition
HudKs70.description: A direct or indirect muscle energy technique in which the antagonist muscles are contracted, causing reflexive relaxation of the agonist muscles.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Muscle energy techniques

tudXG70.title: PPS
tudXG70.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Postpolio syndrome
2. Psychogenic pseudosyncope
3. Postpericardiotomy syndrome
4. Palliative performance scale

8udOG70.title: Systolic dysfunction
8udOG70.description: Reduced ventricular contractility resulting in ventricular enlargement and reduced ejection fraction.

uudpG70.title: Diastolic dysfunction
uudpG70.description: Reduced ventricular compliance characterized by elevated filling pressures, abnormal relaxation, and increased ventricular stiffness.

Eud8G70.title: Rib raising
Eud8G70.description: An articulatory technique that mobilizes the ribs and intercostal muscles to increase chest wall motion, decrease sympathetic activity, and improve lymphatic return. The physician applies pressure and lifts the rib angles potentially aiding in the alleviation of musculoskeletal pain and improving thoracic and costal function (e.g., in patients with pneumonia).

vudAG70.title: Pentavalent meningococcal vaccine
vudAG70.description: A combined vaccine that provides protection against meningococcal serogroups A, B, C, W, and Y.

Cudqt70.title: Rapid-onset opioids
Cudqt70.description: Opioids with a swift onset (within 5–15 minutes) and a short duration of action (usually < 60 minutes). Used for procedural analgesia, general anesthesia, and management of breakthrough cancer pain.

aEdQ870.title: Nephrostomy tube
aEdQ870.description: A percutaneous catheter inserted through the lower back into the kidney to drain urine directly from the renal pelvis. Typically used to treat upper urinary tract obstruction by enabling temporary or long-term urine drainage.

destinations.label: Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology → Urinary drainage procedures

YEdn870.title: Hemostat
YEdn870.description: A surgical instrument used to clamp blood vessels or grasp tissue.

VEdGu70.title: Maverick point
VEdGu70.description: A tender point that does not follow the general rules of counterstrain and does not resolve when the muscle is shortened (e.g., AC7, PC1, PC3 midline cervical tender points).

iEdJv70.title: Risk factors for severe RSV infection in adults
iEdJv70.description: Diabetes mellitus; immunocompromised state; chronic pulmonary, cardiac, renal, hepatic, neurological, and hematologic disorders; older age; medical frailty; and residence in a long-term care facility.

destinations.label: Respiratory syncytial virus infection → Risk factors

QEduv70.title: Carrying angle
QEduv70.description: The angle between the axis of the humerus and the axis of the forearm in full extension and supination. Normally, the carrying angle is approximately 10–15° away from the body. An increased carrying angle is known as cubitus valgus and a decreased carrying angle is known as cubitus varus.

oEd0970.title: Alcohol-associated coagulopathy
oEd0970.description: A group of disorders that can affect blood clotting in individuals with heavy alcohol use. Includes thrombocytopenia, thrombocytopathy, and prolonged prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time (due to a decrease in clotting factors).

IEdYC70.title: Small bowel bleeding
IEdYC70.description: GI bleeding from a source between the ligament of Treitz and the ileocecal valve. Accounts for 5-10% of all GI bleeds.

rEdfC70.title: Thoracoabdominal diaphragm release
rEdfC70.description: A lymphatic technique to improve thoracoabdominal diaphragm excursion, respiration, and lymphatic return (e.g., in respiratory infections). Contraindications include rib fractures, GERD, and malignancies of the lymphatic system.

7Ed4C70.title: Foodborne illness
7Ed4C70.description: An illness or disease caused by the consumption of contaminated food or drink. Contaminants can be infectious (e.g., bacteria, viruses, parasites) or noninfectious (e.g., bacterial toxins, mushroom toxins, heavy metals, allergens, food additives). Foodborne illness often manifests as gastroenteritis with diarrhea and vomiting, but can also present with neurological symptoms (as seen in botulism and ciguatera fish poisoning).

destinations.label: Food poisoning → Overview of foodborne diseases

GEdBC70.title: Conductive cooling
GEdBC70.description: The direct transfer of heat from the body to another material, typically water. The most effective method for reducing body temperature in heat-related illness.

tEdXx70.title: Evaporative cooling
tEdXx70.description: The transfer of heat from the body to surrounding air and water molecules, often enhanced by air movement, e.g., wind or a fan. A method for reducing body temperature in heat-related illnesses or fever.

yEddy70.title: Hedgehog pathway inhibitors
yEddy70.description: A class of anticancer drugs that target the Hedgehog signaling pathway, which plays a key role in controlling cellular growth and proliferation. Vismodegib and sonidegib are used to treat metastatic or locally advanced basal cell carcinoma. Research is ongoing for their use in the management of other types of cancers.

zEdry70.title: Stage 0 melanoma
zEdry70.description: Melanoma that is confined to the epidermis with no regional (e.g., nodal) spread and no distant metastasis.

-EdDy70.title: Stage I melanoma
-EdDy70.description: Melanoma characterized by local invasion with a Breslow depth ≤ 1 mm (stage IA) or > 1 mm and ≤ 2 mm without ulceration (stage IB), but no regional spread or distant metastasis.

ZvdZA70.title: Stage II melanoma
ZvdZA70.description: Melanoma characterized by a higher degree of local invasion than stage I melanoma, but no regional (e.g., nodal) spread or distant metastasis. Subclassified as stage IIA if Breslow depth is > 1 mm and ≤ 2 mm with ulceration, or > 2 mm and ≤ 4 mm without ulceration; stage IIB if Breslow depth is > 2 mm and ≤ 4 mm with ulceration, or > 4 mm without ulceration; and stage IIC if Breslow depth is > 4 mm with ulceration.

0vdeA70.title: Stage III melanoma
0vdeA70.description: Melanoma characterized by local invasion with any level of Breslow depth and regional (e.g., nodal) spread, but no distant metastasis.

avdQA70.title: Stage IV melanoma
avdQA70.description: Melanoma characterized by local invasion with any level of Breslow depth, possible regional (e.g., nodal) spread, and distant metastasis.

Xvd9A70.title: Passive cooling
Xvd9A70.description: A cooling method that involves separating a patient from external heat sources and/or barriers to heat dissipation (e.g., clothing or equipment).

cvda_70.title: Active cooling
cvda_70.description: A cooling method that involves the application of a medium to facilitate heat transfer from the patient's body. Techniques include immersion (e.g., ice water bath), evaporative and convective cooling (e.g., mist and fan), cooled IV fluids, ice packs, cooling blankets, and internal body cavity lavage with cooled fluids.

ivdJ-70.title: Cutaneous melanoma
ivdJ-70.description: Melanoma that originates from epidermal melanocytes. Much more common than noncutaneous melanoma, which originates from mucosal and uveal melanocytes.

4vd3ZH0.title: Hyperpigmentation disorders
4vd3ZH0.description: A group of benign skin conditions that result from an increase in melanin in the epidermis and/or dermis. May occur as an isolated event due to UV exposure or result from a genetic or medical condition. Hyperpigmented lesions include ephelides (freckles), solar lentigo, café au lait macules, melasma, and postinflammatory hyperpigmentation.

OvdIZH0.title: Clinically significant portal hypertension
OvdIZH0.description: A degree of portal hypertension (hepatic venous pressure gradient ≥ 10 mm Hg) that is associated with an increased rate of decompensated liver disease, such as overt ascites, variceal hemorrhage, and overt hepatic encephalopathy.

ovd0aH0.title: Medicare Health Risk Assessment
ovd0aH0.description: A patient questionnaire administered during a Medicare Annual Wellness Visit to assess general health and risk factors for negative health outcomes. Includes an assessment of demographics, psychological health, substance use behaviors, lifestyle habits, functional ability (e.g., activities of daily living, instrumental activities of daily living), and an overall self-assessment of health.

destinations.label: Adult health maintenance → Overview of health maintenance visits

JvdsaH0.title: Mixed agonist-antagonist opioids
JvdsaH0.description: A class of opioids that provides analgesia through a mix of agonist and antagonist activity at the specific opioid receptor types. Examples include buprenorphine and butorphanol. These drugs have a lower risk of respiratory depression and abuse than pure opioid agonists.

qvdCaH0.title: Light to moderate alcohol use
qvdCaH0.description: A level of drinking that has a low risk of alcohol-related complications. Defined by the US dietary guidelines as ≤ 1 standard drink a day for women and ≤ 2 standard drinks a day for men.

destinations.label: Overview of alcohol use → Classifications of alcohol use

IvdYYH0.title: Initial Preventive Physical Examination
IvdYYH0.description: A one-time office visit focused on promoting disease prevention and early disease detection that is performed within the first 12 months of Medicare Part B enrollment. The visit includes a medical and social history review, a general health assessment (including evaluation of functional ability), and the provision of a plan for future screening and health optimization.

destinations.label: Adult health maintenance → Overview of health maintenance visits

rvdfYH0.title: Annual Wellness Visit
rvdfYH0.description: An annual office visit focused on promoting disease prevention and early disease detection for Medicare beneficiaries. The Initial Annual Wellness Visit occurs ≥ 12 months after Medicare Part B enrollment and Subsequent Annual Wellness Visits occur annually thereafter. The visit includes a medical and social history review, a general health assessment (including evaluation of functional ability and cognitive assessment), and the provision of a plan for future screening and health optimization.

destinations.label: Adult health maintenance → Overview of health maintenance visits

7vd4YH0.title: Chest X-ray findings in noncardiogenic pulmonary edema
7vd4YH0.description: Findings include peripheral, patchy ground-glass opacities, peripheral air bronchograms, and pulmonary consolidations.

GvdBYH0.title: Scapular manipulation technique
GvdBYH0.description: A reduction technique for anterior shoulder dislocations in which the glenoid fossa is repositioned by rotating the scapula medially, while gentle traction is applied to the affected arm.

tvdXbH0.title: Traction-countertraction
tvdXbH0.description: A reduction technique that involves applying traction to the patient's affected limb while an assistant applies countertraction. Used for anterior shoulder dislocations and hip dislocations.

Evd8bH0.title: Crossed extensor reflex
Evd8bH0.description: A muscle energy technique used if direct manipulation of the extremities is not possible (e.g., due to fractures or burns). Based on the principle that contracting a flexor muscle in the unaffected limb can induce relaxation in the flexor muscle and contraction of the extensor muscle in the affected limb (e.g., contracting the left biceps results in relaxation of the right biceps and contraction of the right triceps).

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Muscle energy techniques

_vd5cH0.title: TART
_vd5cH0.description: Osteopathic diagnostic criteria for somatic dysfunctions: Tissue texture changes, Asymmetry, Restriction, and Tenderness. Findings can be used to distinguish between acute and chronic dysfunctions.

QDduVH0.title: Acetabular fracture
QDduVH0.description: A fracture of one or more bones that form the acetabulum, the hip joint socket. Often associated with high-energy injury mechanisms, e.g., motor vehicle collisions or falls from heights.

IDdYfH0.title: Patellofemoral joint view
IDdYfH0.description: An x-ray projection of the patellofemoral joint with the knee in flexion. Used to assess for patella fracture, dislocation and subluxation, and patellofemoral joint disease.

GDdBfH0.title: Autoimmune arthritis
GDdBfH0.description: Causes include rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic vasculitis, Behcet disease, mixed connective tissue disease, and sarcoidosis.

tDdXTH0.title: Risk factors for compressive spinal emergency
tDdXTH0.description: Includes degenerative disk disease, intervertebral disk prolapse or protrusion, vertebral metastases, trauma, spondylolysis, spondylolisthesis, risk factors for epidural abscess, and risk factors for spinal epidermal hematoma.

FDdgTH0.title: Ossicle
FDdgTH0.description: A term used to describe various small bones, including those in the middle ear (auditory ossicles) and normal anatomical variants (accessory ossicles). Accessory ossicles may be congenital or caused by trauma or degeneration and are found in several areas of the body.

9DdNgH0.title: Risk factors for spinal infections
9DdNgH0.description: Risk factors include advanced age, immunocompromise (e.g., steroid use, HIV infection), intravenous drug use, recent bacteremia, recent spinal surgery, intravascular devices, malnutrition, and chronic medical conditions (e.g., diabetes mellitus, renal failure, heart disease, liver cirrhosis, and malignancy).

xDdEgH0.title: Celiac ganglion release
xDdEgH0.description: A visceral manipulation technique to reduce hypersympathetic activity in the celiac ganglion at T5–T9. Used to treat dysfunctions of the upper gastrointestinal tract.

awdQhH0.title: Risk factors for retroperitoneal hematoma
awdQhH0.description: Include trauma, invasive procedures (e.g., percutaneous coronary intervention), anticoagulant use, and renal tumors

YwdnhH0.title: Clinical features of retroperitoneal hematoma
YwdnhH0.description: May be asymptomatic or manifest with pain in the flanks, back, abdomen, and/or legs in addition to symptoms of the underlying condition. Significant bleeding may cause hemodynamic instability.

Xwd9hH0.title: Risk factors for disc herniation
Xwd9hH0.description: Include smoking, obesity, genetic predisposition, prolonged sitting, a sedentary lifestyle, and repetitive heavy lifting, especially with improper lifting technique.

1wd23H0.title: Risk factors for spondylolisthesis
1wd23H0.description: Include congenital malformation of the lumbosacral joints L5-S1, activities with repeated stress on the lower back (e.g., gymnastics, swimming, football, weight lifting), spondylolysis, and degenerative disc disease (in older adults), trauma, and local or systemic pathology (e.g., tumors, Paget's disease, osteogenesis imperfecta, tuberculosis).

VwdG3H0.title: Lichen simplex nuchae
VwdG3H0.description: A form of lichen simplex chronicus that results from habitually rubbing and/or scratching the back of the neck in response to stress. Characterized by a well-defined scaly plaque with crusting and/or erosions, which can extend to the posterior scalp and lead to secondary infection.

ewdx3H0.title: Risk factors for inflammatory arthropathies
ewdx3H0.description: Include genetic predispositions (e.g., HLA-B27 positivity, family history of related conditions), infections (e.g., certain preceding gastrointestinal or genitourinary infections), and autoimmune diseases (e.g., psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease).

fwdkRH0.title: Paraspinal inhibition
fwdkRH0.description: An osteopathic manipulative technique in which paraspinal pressure is applied at L1-L2 to reduce sympathetic tone. Used to increase gastrointestinal motility, especially in ileus.

RwdliH0.title: Belonephobia
RwdliH0.description: A persistent and intense fear of needles. Like other phobias, first-line treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy.

mwdVjH0.title: Single alcohol screening question
mwdVjH0.description: A screening question used to assess for unhealthy alcohol use. Patients are asked how many times they have had ≥ 5 drinks (for men aged ≤ 65 years) or ≥ 4 drinks (for women; for men aged > 65 years) in a single day in the past 12 months. An answer of one or more times a day is considered a positive screening should prompt a more comprehensive assessment with a tool such as AUDIT.

nwd7jH0.title: Risk factors for skin cancer
nwd7jH0.description: Factors include light skin, excessive UV exposure (e.g., sunburn, tanning bed use), immunocompromise, and history of skin cancer.

LwdwjH0.title: Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription medications, and other Substance use Tool
LwdwjH0.description: A screening tool to assess for the use of tobacco, alcohol, prescription drugs for nonmedical purposes, and illicit drugs. An initial 4-item tool (TAPS-1) screens for the use of each substance over the past 12 months. Individuals who report using any substances are asked further questions about their use over the past 3 months (TAPS-2) to determine the frequency of use and risk level.

pwdLPH0.title: Congestive heart failure
pwdLPH0.description: Heart failure with signs and/or symptoms of fluid overload, e.g., peripheral edema and jugular venous distention. Often used to refer to all types of heart failure but is no longer the preferred terminology.

JwdsPH0.title: Rubin I maneuver
JwdsPH0.description: An obstetric maneuver used in the management of shoulder dystocia. Involves applying external suprapubic pressure to the posterior part of the impacted shoulder while using the McRoberts maneuver, in which the maternal hips are abducted, externally rotated, and hyperflexed.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Shoulder dystocia

qwdCPH0.title: Rubin II maneuver
qwdCPH0.description: An obstetric maneuver used in the management of shoulder dystocia. Involves manual rotation of the fetal shoulder girdle by applying pressure to the posterior part of the anterior shoulder.

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Shoulder dystocia

8wdOkH0.title: Neuroborreliosis
8wdOkH0.description: A manifestation of disseminated Lyme disease that can affect the peripheral and/or central nervous system. Can include Bell palsy, meningitis, polyneuropathy, and/or encephalomyelitis. Occurs within the first months of infection (early neuroborreliosis) or months to years later (late neuroborreliosis).

wwdhOH0.title: Vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
wwdhOH0.description: Isolates of Staphylococcus aureus that have acquired resistance to the antibiotic vancomycin. Classified as "intermediate" (VISA) or "resistant" (VRSA) depending on the degree of resistance.

xwdEOH0.title: Causes of aortic dissection
xwdEOH0.description: Include hypertension (most common risk factor), trauma (deceleration injury, valve surgery), vasculitis with aortic involvement, cocaine and amphetamine use, 3rd trimester pregnancy, atherosclerosis, connective tissue disease, and congenital aortic abnormalities (e.g., bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation of the aorta).

09deNH0.title: Benign paroxysmal torticollis of infancy
09deNH0.description: A condition characterized by recurrent episodes of alternating head tilt and/or neck rotation. Manifests in infants < 5 months of age and typically resolves by 3 years of age. Of unknown cause but associated with a family history of migraines and with aura-type symptoms (e.g., nausea, vomiting, irritability, and ataxia).

a9dQNH0.title: Transverse ligament of atlas
a9dQNH0.description: Important stabilizing ligament in the upper cervical spine that secures the odontoid process of the axis (C2) to the anterior arch of the atlas (C1). Integrity is crucial to prevent atlanto-axial subluxation. May be weakened in conditions such as Down syndrome and rheumatoid arthritis.

b9dHNH0.title: Alar ligaments
b9dHNH0.description: A paired ligament that extends from the sides of the dens (odontoid process) of C2 (axis) to the medial sides of the occipital condyles. It stabilizes the atlanto-axial joint, restricting excessive axial rotation, sidebending to the contralateral side, and flexion.

V9dGmH0.title: Isotonic contraction
V9dGmH0.description: A muscle contraction in which the muscle's length changes while its strength remains constant.Common in everyday activities. Involves two forms: concentric (muscle shortens) and eccentric (muscle lengthens).

e9dxmH0.title: Isolytic contraction
e9dxmH0.description: A muscle contraction in which the muscle contracts against resistance while the muscle is forced to lengthen. Used in physical therapy to improve muscle strength and flexibility.

U9db5H0.title: Iliolumbar ligament syndrome
U9db5H0.description: A condition caused by inflammation or tearing of the iliolumbar ligament. Clinical features include recurring low back pain, a tender point at the posterior iliac crest, and a positive FABER test.

T9d65H0.title: Concentric contraction
T9d65H0.description: A muscle contraction in which the muscle shortens while generating force. Commonly occurs during activities that involve moving a load toward the body's center of gravity, such as lifting an object or performing a bicep curl.

S9dy5H0.title: Eccentric contraction
S9dy5H0.description: A muscle contraction in which the muscle lengthens due to an external force. Commonly involved in controlled lowering of weight and deceleration movements. Plays a crucial role in muscle strength, coordination, and injury prevention, particularly in sports and rehabilitation.

h9dcMH0.title: Fryette Laws
h9dcMH0.description: Fryette laws describe the principles of physiological motion of the spine and its segments and are used to diagnose dysfunctions. The first law states that side bending and rotation of vertebral segments occur in opposite directions in the neutral spine. The second law states that side bending and rotation occur in the same direction when the spine is flexed or extended. The third law applies to the entire spine and states that the movement of any vertebral segment in a plane of motion alters its movement in other planes.

39dSMH0.title: Fryette first law of spinal motion
39dSMH0.description: The first law states that when the thoracic and lumbar spine is in a neutral position (i.e., neither flexed nor extended), sidebending precedes rotation, and they occur to opposite sides, e.g., T6 neutral, sidebent left, rotated right (T6 NSLRR). The first law typically applies to a group of more than 2 vertebrae of the thoracic and lumbar spine.

R9dlMH0.title: Fryette second law of spinal motion
R9dlMH0.description: The second law states that when the thoracic and lumbar spine is in a nonneutral position (i.e., flexed or extended), rotation precedes sidebending, and they occur to the same side, e.g., T6 flexed, sidebent right, rotated right (T6 FSRRR). The second law typically applies to a single segment of the thoracic and lumbar spine.

i9dJMH0.title: Fryette third law of spinal motion
i9dJMH0.description: The third law applies to the entire spine (cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine) and states that the movement of any vertebral segment of the spine in a plane of motion alters its movement in other planes (e.g., dysfunction in one plane reduces motion in the other planes).

Q9duMH0.title: Balanced ligamentous tension
Q9duMH0.description: An indirect, passive myofascial release technique that involves positioning the affected ligaments in a state of equal tension in all planes of motion using very light touch (approx. 1-3 lbs). Used to treat somatic dysfunctions and enhance musculoskeletal flexibility.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Myofascial release techniques

49d3nH0.title: Oculocephalogyric reflex
49d3nH0.description: A muscle energy technique that utilizes extraocular muscle contraction to reflexively affect the muscles of the neck and trunk. The patient turns their head toward (reciprocal inhibition effect) or away from the restriction (postisometric effect) while the physician applies gentle force. Used to treat severe, acute cervical and upper thoracic conditions.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Muscle energy techniques

l9dvnH0.title: Behavioral interventions for smoking cessation
l9dvnH0.description: Includes advice to quit, counseling, state tobacco quitlines, text messaging interventions, and individualized self-help materials.

destinations.label: Tobacco product use and smoking cessation → Behavioral interventions for smoking cessation

N9d-nH0.title: Facilitation (osteopathy)
N9d-nH0.description: A state of partial excitation in a pool of spinal neurons (due to recurrent stimulation or irritation) leading to a lower threshold for firing. Persistent hyperexcitation can lead to hypertonicity of the associated structures. Often seen in somatic dysfunctions.

destinations.label: General osteopathic principles → Spinal facilitation and autonomic nervous system

m9dVLH0.title: Cervicothoracic junction
m9dVLH0.description: The area where the cervical spine meets the thoracic spine. This junction, comprising the C7 and T1 vertebrae, is a transitional area that experiences unique biomechanical stresses and is susceptible to pathologies such as degenerative changes and fractures.

59diLH0.title: Occipitoatlantal junction
59diLH0.description: The region at the craniocervical junction where the occipital bone of the skull articulates with the first cervical vertebra. Critical in providing support and enabling a range of head movements, including flexion, extension, and lateral bending. Dysfunction or injury in this area can cause neurological and vascular complications.

M9dMLH0.title: Lumbosacral junction
M9dMLH0.description: The region where the lumbar spine meets the sacral spine, comprising the L5 vertebra, sacrum, intervertebral disc, and supporting ligaments and muscles. Common site for biomechanical stress, leading to conditions such as spondylolisthesis and degenerative disc disease.

69djoH0.title: Hip drop test (osteopathy)
69djoH0.description: An osteopathic examination test that evaluates compensation of the lumbar spine with unleveling of the iliac crest.

t9dX6H0.title: Iliac artery aneurysm
t9dX6H0.description: Dilatation of the iliac artery that involves all three arterial layers. May be asymptomatic or result in acute limb ischemia. Often associated with other aneurysms, especially abdominal aortic aneurysms.

F9dg6H0.title: Femoral artery aneurysm
F9dg6H0.description: Dilatation of the femoral artery involving all three arterial layers. Usually due to degenerative changes associated with atherosclerosis.

destinations.label: Aneurysm → Femoral artery aneurysm and pseudoaneurysm

4Cd3HH0.title: Open book pelvic fracture
4Cd3HH0.description: A mechanically unstable fracture of the pelvic ring with disruption of the pubic symphysis. Causes pelvic bones to separate and resemble an open book. Often associated with severe accompanying abdominal and perineal injuries.

OCdIHH0.title: Upper extremity lymphatic pump
OCdIHH0.description: An osteopathic technique that aims to improve the drainage of lymphatic fluid in the upper and lower extremities by applying a rhythmic milking motion (e.g., effleurage) to the extremity, starting distally and moving proximally.

lCdvHH0.title: Pectoral traction
lCdvHH0.description: An osteopathic manipulative technique that improves thoracic range of motion and lymphatic return by applying traction to the pectoralis minor. Indicated in patients with lymphatic congestion of the upper extremity or patients with reactive airway disease (e.g., asthma). Contraindicated in patients with surgical wounds in or around the pectoral area.

5CdisH0.title: Cochlear hydrops
5CdisH0.description: A condition characterized by excess fluid in the cochlea. It is most commonly associated with Ménière disease, and can cause symptoms such as vertigo, tinnitus, and sensorineural hearing loss.

JCdsGH0.title: Epidermal nevus syndrome
JCdsGH0.description: A group of genetic disorders characterized by the presence of epidermal nevi and extracutaneous symptoms (e.g., ocular, cardiovascular, endocrine, neurologic, and skeletal). An abnormal neural crest causes disorders that appear along Blaschko lines. Examples include Schimmelpenning syndrome, CHILD syndrome, and Nevus comedonicus syndrome.

qCdCGH0.title: Hepatitis E virus infection
qCdCGH0.description: A liver infection caused by hepatitis E virus and spread via fecal-oral, parenteral, and perinatal contact. In the majority of cases, the disease is self-limited.

destinations.label: Overview of viral hepatitides → Hepatitis E

ICdYtH0.title: Inflammatory linear verrucous epidermal nevus
ICdYtH0.description: A rare type of epidermal nevus that manifests at birth or during childhood and has an unknown genetic cause. Characterized by a linear inflammatory plaque along Blaschko lines that most commonly manifests on the extremities. Inflammation is chronic and intermittent.

destinations.label: Nevus → Inflammatory linear verrucous epidermal nevus

sCdttH0.title: Nicotine replacement therapy
sCdttH0.description: A nicotine receptor agonist used for smoking cessation treatment that reduces nicotine withdrawal symptoms. Available in long-acting (i.e., patches) and short-acting forms (i.e., lozenges, gum, inhaler, or nasal spray), which can be used in combination.

destinations.label: Tobacco product use and smoking cessation → Pharmacological treatment

GCdBtH0.title: First-line smoking cessation medications
GCdBtH0.description: Consists of varenicline, bupropion, and nicotine replacement therapy (patch, gum, lozenge, inhaler, and nasal spray).

destinations.label: Tobacco product use and smoking cessation → Pharmacological treatment

tCdXFH0.title: Eustachian tube dysfunction questionnaire
tCdXFH0.description: A seven-item symptom-based questionnaire used to assess for eustachian tube dysfunction (ETD). Patients score each symptom from 1 (no problem) to 7 (severe problems). Scores of ≥14.5 suggest ETD.

FCdgFH0.title: Extended eustachian tube score
FCdgFH0.description: A scoring system for obstructive eustachian tube dysfunction (ETD) that combines subjective measures (patient-reported symptoms) and objective measures (e.g., tympanometry, tubomanometry).

bxdHEH0.title: Serial hemoglobin and hematocrit
bxdHEH0.description: The repeated evaluation of hemoglobin and hematocrit values. Typically assessed in trauma patients or patients with known bleeding sources (e.g., GI bleeding). Decreasing levels suggest ongoing hemorrhage.

WxdPvH0.title: Zoon balanitis
WxdPvH0.description: A benign inflammatory condition that presents as an erythematous patch on the penile glans. Commonly found in older, uncircumcised adults.

destinations.label: Disorders of the glans penis and foreskin → Balanitis and balanoposthitis

VxdGvH0.title: AO Spine classification systems
VxdGvH0.description: A comprehensive framework for classifying spine injuries based on fracture morphology, neurological status, and clinical modifiers. Consists of systems for upper cervical injuries, subaxial cervical injuries, and thoracolumbar injuries.

UxdbDH0.title: Clinical decision rules
UxdbDH0.description: A validated set of criteria that predicts the presence or absence of a clinical condition based on medical history, physical examination, and/or initial diagnostics. Used to guide decisions on additional diagnostic testing and/or management.

fxdkDH0.title: Extension teardrop fracture
fxdkDH0.description: An avulsion fracture of the anteroinferior corner of the vertebral body. Typically caused by forced extension of the neck. Unstable in extension because of anterior longitudinal ligament disruption.

destinations.label: Cervical spine injuries → Upper cervical spine injuries

gxdFDH0.title: Swimmer's view
gxdFDH0.description: A modified lateral view of the cervical spine obtained by overhead abduction of the arm closest to the detector. Used to improve visualization of the C7-T1 junction on plain radiography.

SxdyDH0.title: Vertebral augmentation
SxdyDH0.description: The percutaneous injection of bone cement into a fractured vertebra, with or without using a balloon to reexpand the vertebra. Used in the treatment of compression fractures.

3xdSwH0.title: Vaccine adjuvant
3xdSwH0.description: A component of vaccines that enhances immune response. Examples include aluminum in DTaP and cytosine phosphoguanine (synthetic DNA) in hep B.

RxdlwH0.title: Vaccine preservative
RxdlwH0.description: A component of vaccines that prevents microbial growth. Examples include thimerosal, which is added to multidose influenza vaccines, and phenol, which is added to Pneumovax23.

QxduwH0.title: Posthitis
QxduwH0.description: An inflammation of the foreskin. Typically presents with pruritus, erythema, pain, and edema. Etiologies include infections, inflammatory disorders, irritant and allergic reactions, and precancerous lesions.

destinations.label: Disorders of the glans penis and foreskin → Balanitis and balanoposthitis

kxdm9H0.title: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome
kxdm9H0.description: A systemic health disorder that involves complex interactions between metabolic risk factors (e.g., obesity, diabetes), kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease and leads to multiorgan dysfunction and poor cardiovascular outcomes. Ranges from stage 0 (no risk factors) to stage 4 (clinical cardiovascular disease, e.g., heart failure, stroke, and peripheral artery disease).

OxdI9H0.title: Life's Essential 8
OxdI9H0.description: A framework designed by the American Heart Association to promote and quantify cardiovascular health by focusing on eight key areas: nutrition, physical activity, avoidance of nicotine, sleep, healthy weight, blood lipids, blood glucose, and blood pressure.

mxdVCH0.title: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm
mxdVCH0.description: A descending thoracic aortic aneurysm that extends into the abdominal aorta.
