Typically due to degenerative changes in the aortic wall, which are often exacerbated by hypertension or atherosclerosis. Classified as Crawford Extent I to V based on the extent of aortic involvement. May lead to life-threatening complications such as rupture or dissection.

MxdMCH0.title: Lentigo simplex
MxdMCH0.description: A hyperpigmented (tan, brown, or black), 0.5-2 cm round or oval-shaped macule that manifests during childhood. Unlike freckles and solar lentigo, pigment changes are unrelated to sun exposure. The presence of multiple macules may suggest a lentiginosis syndrome (e.g., Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, LEOPARD syndrome, Cowden syndrome).

LxdwCH0.title: Peaked pupil
LxdwCH0.description: An eccentric or irregularly shaped pupil, often resembling a comma or tadpole. Can result from an iris tear and/or prolapse into the anterior chamber. Seen in open globe injuries, traumatic iridodialysis, and as a complication of ocular surgery.

oxd0xH0.title: Zoster sine herpete
oxd0xH0.description: An atypical form of herpes zoster in which reactivation of the virus occurs without the characteristic rash. Can cause symptoms affecting the peripheral nervous system (leading to radicular pain) or central nervous system (resulting in encephalitis or stroke).

KxdUxH0.title: Lumbosacral plexitis
KxdUxH0.description: A rare idiopathic condition distinguished by acute, severe leg pain and muscle wasting and weakness in associated muscles.

6xdjxH0.title: Chemonucleolysis
6xdjxH0.description: A minimally invasive procedure in which an enzyme is injected into the center of a herniated intervertebral disc, thereby lysing the disc nucleus. Used to treat severe pain related to intervertebral disc herniation.

pxdLxH0.title: POP
pxdLxH0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Progestin-only pills
2. Pelvic organ prolapse

JxdsxH0.title: POPs
JxdsxH0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Progestin-only pills
2. Persistent organic pollutants

qxdCxH0.title: Reasonable exclusion of pregnancy
qxdCxH0.description: A set of CDC criteria that suggests pregnancy is unlikely prior to initiating contraceptives. Includes females with no clinical features of pregnancy and any of the following situations: ≤ 7 days after the start of menses, abstinent or consistently using effective contraception since the start of their last menses, ≤ 7 days of a spontaneous or induced abortion, ≤ 4 weeks postpartum, OR ≤ 6 weeks postpartum and primarily breastfeeding and still amenorrhoeic.

Dxd1AH0.title: Sebaceous hyperplasia
Dxd1AH0.description: A common benign condition of the sebaceous glands that affects adults. Manifests with one or more soft, shiny, yellow or skin-colored papules with central umbilication, typically on the face.

xxdEAH0.title: Radiation fibrosis syndrome
xxdEAH0.description: A type of progressive fibrotic tissue sclerosis caused by radiation therapy. Symptoms may include peripheral neuropathy, chronic pain, myopathy, weakness, brittle bones, dyspnea, hypoxia, and/or signs of cardiac dysfunction.

BxdzAH0.title: Radiation pulmonary fibrosis
BxdzAH0.description: The progressive fibrosis of pulmonary tissue following radiation therapy of the thoracic region. Characterized by the delayed onset of symptoms such as cough, dyspnea, and/or respiratory insufficiency.

yxdd_H0.title: Radiation pneumonitis
yxdd_H0.description: Acute or subacute lung tissue inflammation caused by therapeutic radiation targeting the thoracic region, e.g., radiotherapy for breast cancer, lung cancer, or mediastinal lymphoma.

AxdR_H0.title: Risk factors for pyelonephritis
AxdR_H0.description: Includes women (shorter urethras), pregnancy, urinary tract obstruction, foreign bodies (e.g., indwelling urinary catheters, urologic instrumentation), anatomical abnormalities (e.g., benign prostatic hyperplasia, vesicoureteral reflux, nephrolithiasis, ureteral strictures), cystitis, immunosuppression, and renal transplant.

zxdr_H0.title: Risk factors for nephrolithiasis
zxdr_H0.description: Include a low fluid intake, dehydration, dietary factors (e.g., ketogenic diets, high-sodium low-calcium diets), certain medications (e.g., loop diuretics, antiepiletics), certain GI surgeries (e.g., colectomy and ileostomy), prolonged immobilization, and a personal or family history of nephrolithiasis.

aBdQzH0.title: Preserved ratio impaired spirometry
aBdQzH0.description: A term describing individuals with postbronchodilator FEV1:FVC ratio ≥ 0.70 but an FEV1 < 80% of the predicted value.

bBdHzH0.title: Incisional biopsy
bBdHzH0.description: A procedure in which a portion of a lesion or mass is surgically removed for analysis by a pathologist. Methods include a superficial shave biopsy, partial punch biopsy, and partial fusiform (elliptical) biopsy.

XBd9zH0.title: Chylomicronemia syndrome
XBd9zH0.description: A syndrome caused by severely elevated triglyceride levels (> 1500 mg/dL) that is characterized by abdominal pain, acute pancreatitis, eruptive xanthomas, and lipemia retinalis.

2BdTZs0.title: External rotation technique
2BdTZs0.description: An anterior shoulder dislocation reduction method in which the patient is positioned supine and the affected arm is externally rotated to 90 degrees while held in full adduction with the elbow flexed.

fBdkZs0.title: Spaso technique
fBdkZs0.description: An anterior shoulder dislocation reduction technique in which the patient is positioned supine and traction is applied to the affected arm while raising the arm toward the ceiling. The arm is then externally rotated. Reduction generally occurs after a few minutes.

TBd6Zs0.title: Cunningham technique
TBd6Zs0.description: An anterior shoulder dislocation reduction technique in which the patient is seated upright with the affected arm adducted and the elbow flexed to 90 degrees. Downward traction is applied to the arm, and the shoulder and arm are massaged until reduction occurs.

gBdFZs0.title: FARES technique
gBdFZs0.description: An anterior shoulder dislocation reduction method in which the patient is positioned supine with the elbow fully extended. The forearm and hand are grasped and longitudinal traction is applied to the arm. The forearm is then vertically oscillated while the arm is abducted. Reduction generally occurs at around 120 degrees of abduction.

SBdyZs0.title: Hennepin technique
SBdyZs0.description: An anterior shoulder dislocation reduction method in which the patient is seated or supine and the affected arm is adducted with the elbow flexed to 90 degrees. The arm is then slowly externally rotated until it reaches 90 degrees of external rotation or reduction occurs. If unsuccessful, the arm is slowly abducted until reduction occurs.

RBdl0s0.title: very low fat diet
RBdl0s0.description: A diet comprised of < 5% total fat.

iBdJ0s0.title: Judet views
iBdJ0s0.description: Oblique internal and external radiographic views of the pelvis used to assess for acetabular fractures.

PBdWas0.title: Concha bullosa
PBdWas0.description: A common anatomical variant in which air pockets (pneumatization) are present in the nasal turbinates (conchae). Although frequently asymptomatic, concha bullosa can cause turbinate enlargement and symptoms of nasal obstruction. The middle turbinates are most commonly affected.

4Bd3as0.title: Hospital consumer assessment of healthcare providers and systems
4Bd3as0.description: A system used for standardized measurement and reporting of patients' perception of their hospital experience in the United States. The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) mandates reporting of HCAHPS scores as a part of the Hospital Value-Based Program that determines payments to hospitals for delivered healthcare.

OBdIas0.title: Service recovery
OBdIas0.description: A process of identifying and addressing actual or perceived deficiencies in the care of an individual patient. Downstream goals include restoring patient satisfaction and either addressing or avoiding formal patient complaints.

lBdvas0.title: Postpartum risk factors for VTE
lBdvas0.description: A set of criteria, which, in the postpartum period (42 days after delivery), place patients at additional risk of VTE. Include patient factors (age ≥35 years, BMI ≥30 kg/m2, history of preeclampsia, previous VTE, thrombophilia, peripartum cardiomyopathy, or current smoker), factors associated with delivery (e.g., cesarean delivery, transfusion at delivery, and postpartum hemorrhage), and immobility.

MBdMYs0.title: Subpreputial space
MBdMYs0.description: The space between the prepuce (foreskin) and the glans penis.

nBd7Ys0.title: Balanitis xerotica obliterans
nBd7Ys0.description: A chronic inflammatory dermatosis of the glans penis and foreskin characterized by pruritic, white plaques with epidermal atrophy and scarring. Associated with an increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma.

destinations.label: Disorders of the glans penis and foreskin → Balanitis and balanoposthitis

pBdLbs0.title: Risk factors for spinal infection
pBdLbs0.description: Risk factors include advanced age, immunocompromise (e.g., steroid use, HIV infection), intravenous drug use, recent bacteremia, recent spinal surgery, intravascular devices, malnutrition, and chronic medical conditions (e.g., diabetes mellitus, renal failure, heart disease, liver cirrhosis, and malignancy).

qBdCbs0.title: Electronic health record
qBdCbs0.description: A digital record of a patient's health information that can be accessed by multiple health care providers and institutions. Contains information from all clinicians who are treating the patient.

IBdYXs0.title: Electronic medical record
IBdYXs0.description: A digital record of a patient's health information maintained in one location or by one provider. Unlike an electronic health record, the information can not be readily shared with other providers.

sBdtXs0.title: Risk factors for degenerative disk disease
sBdtXs0.description: Include increased age, tobacco smoking, obesity, sedentary lifestyle, diabetes mellitus, concomitant hip and knee osteoarthritis

GBdBXs0.title: Spray and Stretch
GBdBXs0.description: A technique used to treat myofascial trigger points. The affected muscle is passively stretched while a topical cooling agent is sprayed locally. When applied, the sprays most commonly used (dichlorodifluoromethane-trichloromonofluoromethane and ethyl chloride) lower the temperature of the area, which is thought to temporarily block the stretch reflex mediating the muscle spasm, allowing the muscle to be stretched passively with reduced pain.

FBdgcs0.title: Nerve agents
FBdgcs0.description: A weaponized class of organophosphorus compounds that inhibit acetylcholinesterase. Potential effects include increased salivation and lacrimation, diarrhea, bronchospasm, tremor, seizures, and paralysis.

8BdOcs0.title: Carbamate
8BdOcs0.description: A chemical compound that reversibly inhibits cholinesterases. Used in insecticides and as medicinal agents, e.g., physostigmine, pyridostigmine, and neostigmine.

wBdh1s0.title: Kozak sequence
wBdh1s0.description: A specific sequence of nucleotides in the mRNA that is recognised by the ribosome during translation initiation. Directs the preinitiation complex and small ribosomal subunit to the translation initiation site (start codon). Mutations can lead to decreased protein production.

destinations.label: Translation and protein synthesis → Translation process

yBddWs0.title: Level C personal protective equipment
yBddWs0.description: The clothing and/or equipment recommended for providers caring for patients with possible chemical or radioactive contamination. Includes air-purifying respirators, nitrile or butyl rubber gloves, chemical-resistant clothing, and eye protection.

-BdDWs0.title: Obstructive ETD
-BdDWs0.description: A condition characterized by a chronically closed eustachian tube secondary to obstruction or ineffective dilation. Causes include inflammatory edema (e.g., from allergic rhinitis, gastroesophageal reflux, and infections) and anatomic conditions (e.g., craniofacial abnormalities, adenoid hypertrophy, immature eustachian tube, tumors).

bydHds0.title: Test efficiency
bydHds0.description: The percentage of times that the test gives the correct answer compared to the total number of tests.

destinations.label: Interpreting medical evidence → Evaluation of screening or diagnostic tests

Xyd9ds0.title: Post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis
Xyd9ds0.description: A late complication of treated visceral leishmaniasis characterized by dermal hypopigmented nodules, papules, and/or macules that typically start on the face and spread to the torso and extremities.

cydaVs0.title: Trauma-focused psychotherapy
cydaVs0.description: A form of psychotherapy that uses emotional, cognitive, and/or behavioral techniques to enable the processing of a traumatic event. Techniques include cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure therapy, and eye movement desensitization and reprocessing.

1yd2Vs0.title: Cognitive processing therapy
1yd2Vs0.description: A type of structured, time-limited cognitive behavioral therapy used to teach patients with PTSD how to address and change unhelpful beliefs related to a traumatic event.

eydxVs0.title: Congenital lactase deficiency
eydxVs0.description: A very rare, potentially life-threatening autosomal recessive condition that results in dysfunctional intestinal lactase. Manifests in the first few days of life with severe diarrhea after the introduction of lactose-containing milk (breastmilk or formula).

RydlUs0.title: Absolute contraindication
RydlUs0.description: A patient characteristic or condition in which the risk (e.g., severe complications, death) of a particular treatment or intervention outweighs any potential benefit.

iydJUs0.title: Backup contraception
iydJUs0.description: The use of a barrier form of contraception (e.g., condoms) when the primary form of contraception is not fully effective. Recommended situations include immediately after starting or during unscheduled breaks in hormonal contraception, and if intercurrent illness or medication decreases contraceptive efficacy.

5ydifs0.title: Sulfhemoglobinemia
5ydifs0.description: The presence of sulfhemoglobin in the blood, caused by irreversible binding of a sulfur atom to hemoglobin molecules. As sulfhemoglobin is incapable of carrying oxygen, patients present with cyanosis, headache, and weakness. Causes include exposure to sulfa-containing medications (e.g., phenazopyridine, metoclopramide, sumatriptan) or industrial chemicals (e.g., hydrogen sulfide).

xydEhs0.title: Medical overuse
xydEhs0.description: The use of medical testing and/or interventions in situations in which they are unnecessary, excessive, or pose a greater risk than benefit to the individual. Includes overdiagnosis and overtreatment.

_yd53s0.title: Expressed breastmilk
_yd53s0.description: Breastmilk that is removed from the breast either by hand or with a breast pump. Expressed breastmilk can be stored for later use.

zydr3s0.title: Nonenzyme-inducing AEDs
zydr3s0.description: Antiseizure drugs that do not induce liver enzymes (e.g., cytochrome P450) and thereby do not alter the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Examples include gabapentin, pregabalin, valproate, clobazam, clonazepam, and ethosuximide.

-ydD3s0.title: Ciliary flush
-ydD3s0.description: A ring of dilated conjunctival and episcleral blood vessels surrounding the cornea.

ZAdZRs0.title: Corneal blood staining
ZAdZRs0.description: Opacification of the cornea due to the deposition of hemoglobin and breakdown products of hemoglobin in the corneal stroma. May persist for months to years.

0AdeRs0.title: Traumatic iritis
0AdeRs0.description: A noninfectious inflammation of the anterior uveal tract that occurs after ocular trauma and is limited to the iris.

destinations.label: Traumatic eye injuries → Closed globe contusion

bAdHRs0.title: Radionuclide ventriculography
bAdHRs0.description: A method of measuring ventricular volumes and left ventricular ejection fraction using radioactively tagged red blood cells. Commonly used for baseline and serial assessments of ventricular function in patients receiving cardiotoxic chemotherapy.

2AdTQs0.title: Selective dorsal rhizotomy
2AdTQs0.description: A neurosurgical procedure to relieve spasticity and improve mobility in the lower extremities of children with spastic cerebral palsy. Involves selecting and severing certain afferent neuromotor sensory rootlets, thereby diminishing [afferent] excitatory signaling and reducing spasticity in the affected muscle groups.

hAdcjs0.title: Red flags for orbital cellulitis
hAdcjs0.description: Features that raise suspicion for orbital cellulitis in patients with periorbital swelling and redness. Includes proptosis, chemosis, decreased visual acuity, ophthalmoplegia, and signs of optic neuropathy.

iAdJjs0.title: Traumatic iridocyclitis
iAdJjs0.description: A noninfectious inflammation of the anterior uveal tract that occurs after ocular trauma and involves both the iris and ciliary body.

destinations.label: Traumatic eye injuries → Closed globe contusion

jAd_js0.title: Specific back pain
jAd_js0.description: Back pain attributable to a pathophysiological condition, e.g., trauma, deformity, disease, injury, or infection.

PAdWPs0.title: Mechanical back pain
PAdWPs0.description: A form of specific back pain due to disorders of the spine, intervertebral discs, or surrounding soft tissue. Examples include intervertebral disc disease, vertebral fractures, spondylolisthesis, and muscle strain.

kAdmPs0.title: Chronic back pain
kAdmPs0.description: Persistent or recurring back pain lasting > 12 weeks.

mAdV4s0.title: Risk factors for psoas abscess
mAdV4s0.description: Include immunocompromised state (e.g., HIV infection, chronic corticosteroid use, diabetes mellitus), intravenous drug use, trauma

5Adi4s0.title: Risk factors for acute pancreatitis
5Adi4s0.description: The most common factors are gallstones and alcohol use. Other risk factors include severe hypertriglyceridemia, hypercalcemia, certain medications (e.g., steroids, azathioprine), post-ERCP, viral infections, and cystic fibrosis.

LAdw4s0.title: Etiologic field cancerization
LAdw4s0.description: A collection of factors (e.g., lifestyle, environmental, microbial, genetic) and their interactions that affect tissues and potentially predispose individuals to the development of disease, e.g., interactions between the immune system, microbiome, and diet that influence the development of ulcerative colitis and colorectal cancer.

JAdsks0.title: Milking the umbilical cord
JAdsks0.description: A method of transfusing blood from the placenta to the newborn by gently compressing the uncut umbilical cord between two fingers and sliding the fingers toward the newborn multiple times before applying the umbilical clamp. Enhances neonatal blood volume and hemoglobin levels.

rAdfOs0.title: Radiant warmer
rAdfOs0.description: A warming device placed above an open newborn bed to maintain the newborn's body temperature at 36.5°C. Can be controlled manually, but automated regulation using a skin temperature monitor is preferred.

FAdgls0.title: T-piece resuscitator
FAdgls0.description: A gas-powered device used to deliver air and/or oxygen to a newborn through a mask or advanced airway during resuscitation. Peak inspiratory pressure is fixed; tidal volume varies based on mask seal and respiratory compliance. Inspiration is controlled by intermittently occluding an expiratory orifice in the device.

CAdqNs0.title: Gonococcal arthritis
CAdqNs0.description: A common manifestation of disseminated gonococcal infection that involves inflammation in one or more joints. Comprises purulent gonococcal arthritis and arthritis-dermatitis syndrome.

xAdENs0.title: Focused cardiac ultrasound
xAdENs0.description: A point-of-care cardiac ultrasound examination performed as an adjunct to physical examination for specific indications (e.g., chest pain, trauma, dyspnea, hypotension, cardiac arrest, syncope). Assessment goals include ventricular size and function, volume status, pericardial disease, and gross cardiac abnormalities.

0_de5s0.title: Leptotrombidium spp.
0_de5s0.description: A genus of mites that can cause scrub typhus. Belongs to the family Trombiculidae, which are commonly referred to as chiggers.

a_dQ5s0.title: Orientia tsutsugamushi
a_dQ5s0.description: An obligate, gram-negative, intracellular aerobe that causes scrub typhus. Transmitted by the bite of an infected trombiculid mite larvae (chiggers) from the genus Leptotrombidium.

U_dbns0.title: Open dislocation
U_dbns0.description: A dislocation injury in which the joint capsule and overlying skin are disrupted, exposing the synovial space to the external environment. Associated with an increased risk of septic arthritis.

f_dkns0.title: Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta
f_dkns0.description: A minimally invasive, temporary endovascular occlusion of the aorta performed to prevent exsanguination. Typically reserved as a bridge to definitive treatment for patients with severe hemorrhage and/or multisystem trauma, e.g., pelvic fracture with hemodynamic instability.

T_d6ns0.title: Semaglutide
T_d6ns0.description: A glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist used in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

destinations.label: Diabetes medications → Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (incretin mimetics)

3_dSLs0.title: Boss-Holzach-Matter technique
3_dSLs0.description: A self-administered reduction method for anterior shoulder dislocation. In a semi-recumbent position, the patient flexes the knee ipsilateral to the dislocation to 90° and fully extends the contralateral leg. The patient then interlocks their fingers around the flexed knee with both arms in full extension and leans posteriorly while shrugging the shoulder anteriorly and hyperextending the neck.

j_d_Ls0.title: PREVENT equations
j_d_Ls0.description: Equations used to predict the risk of composite CVD and subtypes (ASCVD and HF). The risk estimate can help guide primary prevention decisions, including lifestyle modifications and pharmacotherapy.

P_dWos0.title: Pelvic stability assessment
P_dWos0.description: A physical examination maneuver to assess the stability of the pelvic ring. With the patient in a supine position, gentle downward compression is applied to the anterior superior iliac spines and lateral compression to the iliac crests. Any gross movement or laxity suggests pelvic fracture or pubic symphysis diastasis.

k_dmos0.title: Clinical features of genitourinary trauma
k_dmos0.description: Includes gross hematuria, abdominal tenderness, high-riding prostate on digital rectal examination, and externally visible signs such as blood at the urethral meatus, and hematomas, lacerations, or wounds in the perineal area. Specific features vary by injury.

O_dIos0.title: Atrial cardiopathy
O_dIos0.description: Any structural or functional atrial changes with the potential to produce disease manifestations. Associated with atrial fibrillation and related thromboembolism.

M_dMKs0.title: Chronotherapy
M_dMKs0.description: A behavioral modification technique used in the treatment of sleep disorders (e.g., delayed sleep phase disorder) if first-line treatment is unsuccessful. The patient's bedtime is gradually and systematically delayed until desired sleep and wake times are achieved.

L_dwKs0.title: Orbital compartment pressure
L_dwKs0.description: The pressure within the orbit, the bony cavity that encloses the globe and accessory organs of the eye. Intraocular pressure is used as a surrogate measure of orbital compartment pressure, but they are not synonymous.

r_dfps0.title: McKenzie therapy
r_dfps0.description: A set of exercises that uses a progressive sequence of movements (e.g., lying prone, prone on elbows, prone on extended hands, standing lumbar extension) to improve low back pain.

D_d1qs0.title: First-void urine
D_d1qs0.description: A method of urine collection in which the patient does not cleanse the genitourinary area before collecting the initial 30 mL from their urine stream. Used in the diagnosis of certain STIs (e.g., chlamydia, gonorrhea).

__d5Is0.title: Type-specific HSV serology
__d5Is0.description: An assay that detects antibodies against herpes simplex virus-specific glycoproteins and differentiates between HSV-1 and HSV-2

Xzd9rs0.title: Intermediate syndrome
Xzd9rs0.description: The onset of muscle weakness 1–4 days after cholinergic poisoning from organophosphate exposure. May result in respiratory failure.

czda7s0.title: Testicular rupture
czda7s0.description: Disruption of the tunica albuginea surrounding the testis, with subsequent exposure of the seminiferous tubules. Typically caused by blunt scrotal trauma.

Rzdlss0.title: Infant hunger cues
Rzdlss0.description: Cues for breastmilk or formula milk include bringing hands to the face, rooting for the nipple or breast, smacking lips, sucking on the hands, and reaching for the breast or bottle. Cues for complementary feeding include excitement when food is seen or presented (e.g., smiling, opening the mouth, reaching for food, and moving the head forward). Crying is a late sign of hunger.

izdJss0.title: Signs of infant satiety
izdJss0.description: Signs related to satiety with breastmilk or formula include a decrease in sucking, extension of the limbs, relaxing the fingers, pushing or arching away, and turning away from the breast or bottle. Signs related to satiety of complementary foods include being easily distracted, turning the head away or pushing food away, closing the mouth when food is presented, playing with food, and throwing food on the floor.

Qzduss0.title: Cytomegalovirus hepatitis
Qzduss0.description: A cytomegalovirus infection of the liver that mostly affects immunocompromised individuals. Common symptoms are prolonged malaise and fever. Findings include mild transaminitis, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, and normal or elevated bilirubin.

Nzd-Gs0.title: Clinical features of nephrotic syndrome
Nzd-Gs0.description: Features include massive proteinuria (sometimes resulting in frothy urine), periorbital and/or peripheral edema (in severe cases, anasarca), hypoalbuminemia, and hyperlipidemia.

5zdits0.title: Turbinoplasty
5zdits0.description: A surgical procedure to reduce the size of the nasal turbinates. Involves the destruction or shrinkage of overlying mucosal tissue (e.g., with electrocautery or laser ablation) or the removal of submucosal tissue.

MzdMts0.title: Turbinectomy
MzdMts0.description: A surgical procedure to reduce the size of the nasal turbinates. Involves the removal of some or all of the turbinate bone. Some techniques also remove the overlying mucosa and submucosal tissue.

6zdjFs0.title: Anterior spinal column
6zdjFs0.description: The portion of the vertebral column composed of the anterior vertebral body, anterior annulus fibrosus, and anterior longitudinal ligament.

media.title: Denis' three-column classification of spinal instability in thoracolumbar injuries

pzdLFs0.title: Middle spinal column
pzdLFs0.description: The portion of the vertebral column composed of the posterior longitudinal ligament, posterior annulus fibrosus, and posterior wall of the vertebral body.

media.title: Denis' three-column classification of spinal instability in thoracolumbar injuries

IzdY8s0.title: Posterior spinal column
IzdY8s0.description: The portion of the vertebral column composed of the posterior arch and the posterior ligamentous complex (ligamentum flavum, interspinous ligament, and supraspinous ligament).

media.title: Denis' three-column classification of spinal instability in thoracolumbar injuries

7zd48s0.title: Cells and flare
7zd48s0.description: An eye examination finding that is consistent with inflammation in the anterior chamber. Cells may resemble dust particles floating in a light beam, while flare refers to a general haziness caused by the scattering of light by extravasated proteins. Conditions that cause cells and flare include uveitis and iritis.

vzdAus0.title: Infant nutrition and breastfeeding
vzdAus0.description: The dietary needs and feeding practices required during the first 12 months of life. Nutrition options are breastfeeding and/or iron-fortified infant formula, with the introduction of complementary foods around 6 months of age.

media.title: Stimulation of milk production and ejection

Dzd1Es0.title: Percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy
Dzd1Es0.description: A procedure to remove intravascular blood clots using a mechanical device deployed through a percutaneously placed catheter. Minimally invasive and typically guided by imaging modalities such as fluoroscopy or ultrasound.

wzdhEs0.title: Percutaneous thromboaspiration
wzdhEs0.description: A minimally invasive procedure to remove intravascular blood clots using transcatheter suction or aspiration. Typically guided by fluoroscopy and may be an adjunct to catheter-directed thrombolysis.

CzdqEs0.title: Handheld Doppler device
CzdqEs0.description: A portable device used to evaluate intravascular blood flow with an audible signal. Commonly used to assess perfusion of extremities and other tissue beds.

AzdRvs0.title: Infectious tenosynovitis
AzdRvs0.description: A closed infection within a tendon sheath that most commonly affects the joints of the hands. Causes include contiguous spread from adjacent structures, direct infection from puncture wounds, and hematogenous spread.

_zd5vs0.title: Kanavel signs
_zd5vs0.description: The four characteristic signs used for the diagnosis of pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis. These consist of fusiform swelling, pain with passive straightening, tenderness to palpation along the tendon sheath, and preference for a flexed position in the affected finger. The presence of one or more signs suggests pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis.

j-d_Cs0.title: Secondhand smoke
j-d_Cs0.description: Involuntary or passive inhalation of smoke from burning tobacco products (e.g., from someone smoking a cigarette in the same room). Exposure to secondhand smoke is associated with similar health consequences as tobacco product use.

k-dmxs0.title: Central neuropathic pain
k-dmxs0.description: Chronic pain arising directly from a lesion to the central nervous system. Most commonly due to stroke, spinal cord injury, or multiple sclerosis. The hallmark of CNP is spinothalamic tract dysfunction in the region of the body affected by the neurological insult.

l-dvxs0.title: Red desaturation test
l-dvxs0.description: A bedside test in which the patient views a red-colored object while covering each eye in turn, and is asked to compare the relative color intensity in each eye. A positive test (reduced intensity in one eye) suggests a monocular optic neuropathy (e.g., optic neuritis).

F-dg_s0.title: Pneumatic retinopexy
F-dg_s0.description: A treatment for retinal detachment in which an expansile gas is injected into the eye to tamponade the affected area. Commonly used gases include sulfur hexafluoride, hexafluoroethane, and perfluoropropane.

8-dO_s0.title: Scleral buckling
8-dO_s0.description: A surgical procedure used to repair a retinal detachment, in which the sclera is indented using a buckle (a silicone band or sponge) to allow apposition of the detached layers.

u-dp_s0.title: Cryoretinopexy
u-dp_s0.description: A treatment for retinal detachment in which freezing temperatures are used to induce an adhesive scar in order to stabilize the retina and prevent further detachment.

v-dA_s0.title: Qp:Qs ratio
v-dA_s0.description: A ratio of the total pulmonary blood flow (Qp) to the total systemic blood flow (Qs). It is calculated to assess and quantify the volume of a shunt. A normal value is 1:1. A Qp:Qs ratio > 1:1 indicates a net left-to-right shunt and a Qp:Qs ratio < 1:1 indicates a net right-to-left shunt. The Qp:Qs ratio may be 1:1 if two (bidirectional) shunts of equal magnitude are present.

_-d5-s0.title: Geiger counter
_-d5-s0.description: A device used to detect the presence of ionizing radiation.

z-dr-s0.title: Radiation dosimeter
z-dr-s0.description: A small instrument that measures an individual's accumulated dose of ionizing radiation over time. Typically worn as a badge.

ZZVZZG0.title: Primary lactase deficiency
ZZVZZG0.description: The most common cause of lactose intolerance. Lactase activity starts to decrease during childhood and further declines with age; the rate is influenced by genetic factors. Onset of clinical features of lactose intolerance is variable but typically starts during adolescence and progresses with age, but can occur from 3 years of age.

cZVa0G0.title: USMEC category 1
cZVa0G0.description: Conditions that are not a contraindication for the selected method of contraception according to the USMEC, a set of criteria used to determine the safest method of contraception for individuals with specific medical conditions or relevant history.

destinations.label: Contraception → U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria (USMEC) for contraceptive use

1ZV20G0.title: USMEC category 2
1ZV20G0.description: Conditions for which the benefits of the selected method of contraception are thought to outweigh the risks according to the USMEC, a set of criteria used to determine the safest method of contraception for individuals with specific medical conditions or relevant history.

destinations.label: Contraception → U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria (USMEC) for contraceptive use

WZVP0G0.title: USMEC category 3
WZVP0G0.description: Conditions in which the risks of the selected method of contraception are thought to outweigh the benefits according to the USMEC, a set of criteria used to determine the safest method of contraception for individuals with specific medical conditions or relevant history.

destinations.label: Contraception → U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria (USMEC) for contraceptive use

dZVo0G0.title: USMEC category 4
dZVo0G0.description: Conditions that are absolute contraindications for the selected method of contraception according to the USMEC, a set of criteria used to determine the safest method of contraception for individuals with specific medical conditions or relevant history.

destinations.label: Contraception → U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria (USMEC) for contraceptive use

UZVbaG0.title: Lipedema
UZVbaG0.description: A loose connective tissue disease characterized by the excessive accumulation of nodular and fibrotic fat, primarily in the limbs, hips, and buttocks. Occurs almost exclusively in women. Typical manifestations include symmetrical swelling, pain, and tenderness in the affected areas.

5ZViXG0.title: Mycoplasma genitalium infection
5ZViXG0.description: A sexually transmitted infection that is frequently asymptomatic but may cause urethritis or cervicitis.

MZVMXG0.title: Dicentric chromosome assay
MZVMXG0.description: A test for estimating radiation exposure based on the frequency of chromosomal aberrations found in cultured lymphocytes, i.e., chromosomes with two centromeres.

LZVwXG0.title: D-sign
LZVwXG0.description: An echocardiographic finding in which the left ventricular septal wall flattens into a D-shape, typically due to right ventricular volume overload. It is seen in the parasternal short axis view and is a sign of right ventricular strain, e.g., in pulmonary embolism.

KZVUcG0.title: Flexion-distraction injury
KZVUcG0.description: An unstable thoracolumbar vertebral injury of the middle spinal column and posterior spinal column. Includes disruption of posterior bony structures (Chance fracture) and/or ligamentous structures. Most common in individuals who sustain rapid deceleration in a motor vehicle crash while restrained by a lap belt.

6ZVjcG0.title: Pseudo-PEA
6ZVjcG0.description: The absence of a detectable pulse despite organized electrical cardiac activity and evidence of cardiac output (based on, e.g., ETCO₂, arterial wave form, echocardiographic findings). Causes include hypovolemia, PE, tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade, and decreased cardiac contractility.

destinations.label: Cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary resuscitation → Advanced cardiac life support (ACLS)

IZVY1G0.title: Pleural line
IZVY1G0.description: A hyperechoic line extending between the ribs distal to the intercostal muscles caused by reflection of ultrasound waves off of the lung parietal pleura. It is a normal finding of the visceral and parietal pleural interface on thoracic ultrasound.

7ZV41G0.title: Pulmonary A-lines
7ZV41G0.description: A series of hyperechoic lines parallel to and at equal intervals below the pleural line seen on lung ultrasound. It is a normal finding caused by reverberation of aerated lung tissue.

sZVt1G0.title: Quad sign
sZVt1G0.description: An abnormal finding on lung ultrasound in which a four-sided area is seen, bordered laterally by rib shadows, anteriorly by the parietal pleura, and posteriorly by the visceral pleura. On M-mode, a sinusoid pattern is seen as the distance between the parietal and visceral pleura varies with respiration. Indicates pleural effusion.

GZVB1G0.title: Shred sign
GZVB1G0.description: An abnormal finding on lung ultrasound in which a ragged or irregular hyperechoic line separates well-aerated lung from consolidated lung. Tissue distal to the line may appear dense, similar to hepatic tissue.

tZVXWG0.title: Peripheral edema
tZVXWG0.description: The accumulation of excess fluid in tissues perfused by the peripheral vascular system, particularly in the feet and legs.

DZV1dG0.title: CRI
DZV1dG0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Congenital rubella infection
2. Cranial rhythmic impulse

wZVhdG0.title: Antibiotic resistance testing
wZVhdG0.description: Laboratory tests used to determine the susceptibility of bacteria to specific antibiotics.

CZVqdG0.title: HIV drug-resistance testing
CZVqdG0.description: A laboratory assay used to assess for mutations in the HIV genome that confer resistance to antiretroviral drugs. Can be done via genotypic assay that looks for treatment-resistant genetic mutations (preferred) or phenotypic assay, which assesses HIV response to ART drugs.

xZVEdG0.title: Nongonococcal urethritis
xZVEdG0.description: Inflammation of the urethra caused by an organism other than Neisseria gonorrhoeae, most commonly Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, or Trichomonas vaginalis. Less common causative organisms include herpes simplex virus, adenovirus, and Haemophilus influenza.

AZVRVG0.title: Infectious uveitis
AZVRVG0.description: An inflammation of the uvea caused by an immune response to infection with a pathogen (e.g., virus or bacteria).

_ZV5VG0.title: Noninfectious uveitis
_ZV5VG0.description: An inflammation of the uvea caused by an inappropriate immune response. Associated with systemic autoimmune and inflammatory conditions (e.g., Behcet disease, ankylosing spondylitis, and sarcoidosis).

a0VQeG0.title: Red flags for torticollis
a0VQeG0.description: Signs and symptoms that may indicate a life-threatening cause of torticollis. Examples include signs of infection (e.g., fever, odynophagia, dysphagia, tender neck mass, vertebral point tenderness), acute or progressing focal neurologic deficits, ataxia, signs of increased ICP, visual changes (e.g., diplopia), preceding trauma, severe neck pain, and conditions associated with atlantoaxial ligamentous laxity (e.g., trisomy 21, achondroplasia, osteogenesis imperfecta).

Y0VneG0.title: Cantholysis
Y0VneG0.description: An incision of the lateral canthal tendon made to decompress the orbit. Used to treat orbital compartment syndrome.

destinations.label: Orbital disorders → Lateral canthotomy and cantholysis

d0VoUG0.title: Generalized Anxiety Disorder-2 scale
d0VoUG0.description: A survey used to screen for generalized anxiety disorder. It contains only the first two questions from the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 scale.

20VT2G0.title: Skin lightening therapy
20VT2G0.description: A treatment used for hyperpigmentation disorders (e.g., melasma) or hypopigmentation disorders (e.g., vitiligo). Includes topical pharmacotherapy (e.g., azelaic acid, ascorbic acid, niacinamide), systemic pharmacotherapy (e.g., oral tranexamic acid), and procedural therapy (e.g., chemical peels, laser therapy).

destinations.label: Hyperpigmentation disorders → Management of hyperpigmentation disorders

f0Vk2G0.title: Radiation-induced heart disease
f0Vk2G0.description: An injury to the heart caused by exposure to ionizing radiation. May result in accelerated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, cardiomyopathy, valvular heart disease, conduction abnormalities, and pericardial disease.

T0V62G0.title: Highly water-soluble irritants
T0V62G0.description: A group of irritant chemical agents that cause immediate symptoms (e.g., burning sensation, tearing, rhinorrhea) upon contact with mucous membranes.

g0VF2G0.title: Poorly water-soluble irritants
g0VF2G0.description: A group of irritant chemical agents that cause symptoms of delayed-onset lung injury (e.g., dyspnea, wheezing, chest tightness) within hours to days after exposure.

30VSfG0.title: Spinal cord injury without radiographic abnormality
30VSfG0.description: Spinal cord injury without evidence of vertebral fracture or dislocation on x-ray or CT.  Most commonly seen in pediatric patients.

destinations.label: Spinal cord injuries → Spinal cord injury without radiographic abnormality (SCIWORA)

L0VwgG0.title: Radiation dermatitis
L0VwgG0.description: An injury to the skin caused by exposure to ionizing radiation. May be acute (developing within 90 days of radiotherapy) or chronic (developing months to years after radiotherapy). Mild features include erythema, pigment changes, desquamation, and fibrosis. Severe features include skin ulceration and necrosis.

o0V0SG0.title: Simple asphyxiant
o0V0SG0.description: A gas that displaces oxygen from inhaled air, causing hypoxemia. Examples include carbon dioxide, methane, nitrogen, and helium.

K0VUSG0.title: Chemical asphyxiant
K0VUSG0.description: A gas that causes tissue hypoxia by disrupting oxygen transport and/or oxidative metabolism. Examples include carbon monoxide, phosphine, and nitric oxide.

I0VYhG0.title: Callus
I0VYhG0.description: A skin lesion with diffuse, evenly distributed hypertrophy caused by repetitive mechanical pressure or irritation.

t0VX3G0.title: Chemical pneumonitis
t0VX3G0.description: The inflammation and/or irritation of lung tissue caused by inhalation of a toxic or irritating substance. Symptoms include dyspnea, cough, and chest tightness.

E0V83G0.title: Vertebral fracture-dislocation
E0V83G0.description: An unstable vertebral fracture with ligament disruption and displacement of the vertebra and/or vertebral fragments.

v0VA3G0.title: Lateral canthotomy
v0VA3G0.description: An incision of the lateral canthus that exposes the lateral canthal tendon. Usually performed with cantholysis to treat orbital compartment syndrome.

destinations.label: Orbital disorders → Lateral canthotomy and cantholysis

w0VhRG0.title: Posterior tension band
w0VhRG0.description: The group of osseous and ligamentous structures that stabilize the spine by limiting flexion. Consists of the posterior longitudinal ligament, supraspinous ligaments, interspinous ligaments, articular facet capsules, and ligamenta flava.

B0VzRG0.title: Principal clinical features of Kawasaki disease
B0VzRG0.description: The typical features of Kawasaki disease seen alongside fever. Features include oropharyngeal mucositis (e.g., cracked lips, strawberry tongue), bilateral conjunctivitis, polymorphous rash, palmar and plantar erythema and/or desquamation, and cervical lymphadenopathy.

y0VdiG0.title: Anterior vertebral line
y0VdiG0.description: A line seen on lateral x-ray that represents the anterior margins of contiguous vertebral bodies. If the line is not smooth (e.g., has an abrupt step-off), misalignment due to a bony or ligamentous injury may be present.

A0VRiG0.title: Posterior vertebral line
A0VRiG0.description: A line seen on lateral x-ray that represents the posterior margins of contiguous vertebral bodies. If the line is not smooth (e.g., has an abrupt step-off), misalignment due to a bony or ligamentous injury may be present.

_0V5iG0.title: Spinolaminar line
_0V5iG0.description: A line seen on lateral x-ray that represents the anterior margins of contiguous spinous processes and defines the posterior margin of the spinal canal. If the line is not smooth (e.g., has an abrupt step-off), misalignment due to a bony or ligamentous injury may be present.

ZaVZQG0.title: Basion dens interval
ZaVZQG0.description: The distance between the basion (midpoint of the anterior margin of the foramen magnum) and the tip of the dens (odontoid process). An interval ≥ 12 mm on lateral x-ray suggests atlanto-occipital dislocation.

0aVeQG0.title: Basion axial interval
0aVeQG0.description: The horizontal distance between the basion (midpoint of the anterior margin of the foramen magnum) and a line extending from the posterior margin of the axis. An interval ≥12 mm on lateral x-ray suggests atlanto-occipital dislocation.

aaVQQG0.title: Powers ratio
aaVQQG0.description: The distance from the tip of the basion (midpoint of the anterior margin of the foramen magnum) to the posterior arch of the atlas divided by the distance from the opisthion (the midpoint of the posterior margin of the foramen magnum) to the anterior arch of the atlas. A ratio ≥ 1 on lateral x-ray suggests anterior atlanto-occipital dislocation.

baVHQG0.title: Congenital muscular torticollis
baVHQG0.description: The most common type of congenital torticollis. Thought to result from intrauterine malpositioning, sternocleidomastoid muscle injury, or abnormal development of a sternocleidomastoid muscle. Manifests with ipsilateral lateral head tilt and contralateral chin rotation.

daVojG0.title: Halo vest
daVojG0.description: A brace used to immobilize the cervical spine. A metal ring circles the head and is attached to the skull with pins. Vertical fixation rods secure the metal ring to a rigid plastic vest worn on the torso. May be used as definitive treatment for cervical fractures or for pre- or postoperative immobilization.

faVkPG0.title: Ozenoxacin
faVkPG0.description: A topical quinolone antibiotic used to treat impetigo.

TaV6PG0.title: Fusidic acid
TaV6PG0.description: A topical antibiotic used to treat skin infections such as impetigo.

SaVyPG0.title: Tummy time
SaVyPG0.description: The prone positioning of an awake, supervised infant for appropriate muscle development. Initiated for 3-5 minutes, 2-3 times per day for neonates and gradually increased to 30 minutes per day by 2 months of age. Neonates are placed on an adult's chest or lap, while older infants with better head control are placed on a firm, flat surface that is free of suffocation risks.

iaVJ4G0.title: Respiratory muscle weakness
iaVJ4G0.description: A lack of strength in muscles used for breathing (e.g., diaphragm, intercostal muscles, abdominal and neck muscles). May manifest with dyspnea, inability to cough, and/or abnormal use of accessory muscles. Causes include neuromuscular disorders, e.g., Guillain-Barré syndrome or motor neuron disease. Can be diagnosed clinically and/or using pulmonary function testing.

QaVu4G0.title: Vaccine antigens
QaVu4G0.description: Antigens used in vaccines to induce a protective immune response against future exposure to those antigens. May be derived directly from a pathogen or synthesized to resemble a pathogen. Examples include live-attenuated pathogens, whole killed organisms, toxoids, and viral vectors.

PaVWkG0.title: Neuromuscular weakness
PaVWkG0.description: An impairment in motor function attributable to abnormalities in the structure or function of muscles, neurons, and/or the neuromuscular junction.

kaVmkG0.title: Paralysis
kaVmkG0.description: Severe or complete loss of muscular strength caused by abnormalities in the central nervous system, peripheral nervous system, neuromuscular junction, or myocytes.

OaVIkG0.title: Grisel syndrome
OaVIkG0.description: Nontraumatic atlantoaxial subluxation following infection and inflammation of adjacent tissues. Manifests as nonmuscular torticollis and typically affects children.

NaV-kG0.title: Bicarbonaturia
NaV-kG0.description: Increased bicarbonate in urine. Typically due to impaired renal bicarbonate reabsorption. Causes include proximal renal tubular acidosis, carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, high serum alkali load (e.g., due to alkalization therapy), and physiological compensation for respiratory alkalosis.

taVXmG0.title: Ramp position
taVXmG0.description: A supine position with padding under the patient's head and shoulders to align the external auditory meatus and sternum horizontally. Used to improve visualization of the larynx during airway management in patients with obesity.

EaV8mG0.title: Folliculitis barbae
EaV8mG0.description: An infection of the hair follicles, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Most commonly occurs in areas where the hair is shaved (e.g., face, axilla, groin) and causes papulopustular lesions. Deep-seated infections are called sycosis barbae and can cause alopecia and scarring.

9aVN5G0.title: Osteolytic lesions
9aVN5G0.description: An area of bone in which normal bone tissue has been replaced by soft tissue, fat, or fluid. Lesions typically appear radiolucent on radiographs and hypodense on CT scans. Etiologies include neoplasms (e.g., osteolytic metastases) and metabolic conditions (e.g., intraosseous lipoma, fibrous dysplasia).

CaVq5G0.title: PERRLA
CaVq5G0.description: An acronym for “pupils equal, round, and reactive to light and accommodation,” describing normal pupillomotor function. PERRL refers to pupil function, excluding the accommodative response.

BaVz5G0.title: Asbestos-related diseases
BaVz5G0.description: A group of conditions caused by exposure to asbestos fibers. Primarily affect the lungs and respiratory system and often emerge years or decades after initial exposure. Encompasses both nonmalignant diseases such as asbestosis and malignant diseases such as lung cancer and mesothelioma.

XYV9nG0.title: Nonchlamydial nongonococcal urethritis
XYV9nG0.description: Urethritis caused by pathogens other than Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae or by a noninfectious etiology, such as chemical irritation.

1YV2LG0.title: Cicatricial alopecia
1YV2LG0.description: A type of hair loss in which hair follicles are destroyed and replaced with scar tissue. May be primary, with an underlying disease process causing destruction of the follicle, or secondary, following injury (e.g., burn or severe infection).

WYVPLG0.title: Patellofemoral maltracking
WYVPLG0.description: A physical examination finding indicating patellar instability and improper dynamic alignment between the patella and the trochlea. Abnormal tracking manifests as lateral deviation of the patella out of the trochlear groove with full extension of the knee, resulting in the J-sign. Patellofemoral maltracking is associated with patellofemoral pain syndrome.

dYVoLG0.title: Iontophoresis
dYVoLG0.description: A noninvasive method in which ionized substances such as medications are administered transdermally using a mild electric current. Increases absorption of drugs into local tissues. Typically used in physical therapy to treat inflammatory conditions and in dermatology for hyperhidrosis.

eYVxLG0.title: Lung markings
eYVxLG0.description: The appearance of pulmonary blood vessels on radiological images. Typically most prominent in the hila and lower lung zones, becoming progressively less visible toward the periphery of the middle and upper lung zones, including the apex.

2YVToG0.title: Non-HDL cholesterol
2YVToG0.description: An umbrella term encompassing various lipoproteins (e.g., low-density lipoprotein, triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, lipoprotein A) and excluding high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C). Considered a marker of atherogenic dyslipidemia, making it a good predictor of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Calculated by subtracting HDL-C from total cholesterol.

kYVm6G0.title: Mediastinal widening
kYVm6G0.description: Abnormal enlargement of the mediastinum seen on imaging studies such as chest x-rays and CT scans. Caused by various conditions, e.g., aortic aneurysm, thymoma, lymphadenopathy, and traumatic injuries. The degree of widening may vary depending on factors such as the patient's age and size.

media.title: Widened mediastinum secondary to traumatic thoracic aortic injury

lYVv6G0.title: Gaiter region
lYVv6G0.description: The lower part of the leg between the midcalf and ankle, which is the area typically protected by gaiter boots. A typical location for venous ulcers.

NYV-6G0.title: Nine-point Beighton score
NYV-6G0.description: A nine-point scoring system used to identify generalized joint hypermobility. Joints of the fingers, elbows, knee, and lumbar spine are assessed. There is no consensus, but a score ≥ 5 is often considered positive.

5YVipG0.title: Durable medical equipment
5YVipG0.description: Equipment that an individual uses repeatedly over time for medical indications. Examples include wheelchairs, hospital beds, home oxygen equipment, blood glucose meters, and some single-use items used with this equipment (e.g., lancets and test strips for checking blood glucose).

MYVMpG0.title: Teleoroentgenogram
MYVMpG0.description: A diagnostic imaging modality used in the evaluation of leg length discrepancy. A single-exposure full-length (hip to ankle) anteroposterior x-ray is taken of both lower extremities while the patient is standing.

nYV7pG0.title: Scanogram
nYV7pG0.description: A diagnostic imaging modality used for the evaluation of leg length discrepancy. While the patient lies supine next to a ruler, three x-rays (of the hip, knee, and ankle) are taken of both legs. It does not image the entire leg.

JYVsJG0.title: Utilization management
JYVsJG0.description: A review of the appropriateness of a provided health care service that considers factors such as cost-effectiveness and quality of care. The review may occur before the service is provided (i.e., prior authorization), during the course of treatment, or after the service is provided.

destinations.label: Health care system → Health insurance basics

qYVCJG0.title: Red flags of foreign body ingestion
qYVCJG0.description: Signs and symptoms of foreign body ingestion that suggest possible life-threatening complications. Signs include drooling, dysphagia, cyanosis, hematemesis, chest pain, and any sign of respiratory distress.

IYVYqG0.title: Mumps orchitis
IYVYqG0.description: Inflammation, swelling, and tenderness of one or both testes caused by the viral infection mumps, most commonly in unvaccinated postpubertal men and boys. Typically develops ≤ 7 days after parotitis.

7YV4qG0.title: Retinal artery occlusion
7YV4qG0.description: Partial or complete obstruction of the central retinal artery or its branches resulting in retinal ischemia. Most commonly caused by thromboemoblism. Manifests with sudden, painless loss of vision. Infarction caused by retinal artery occlusion is a form of ischemic stroke.

destinations.label: Retinal vessel occlusion → Retinal artery occlusion

sYVtqG0.title: Population health management
sYVtqG0.description: Efforts to provide high-quality, cost-conscious health care with the goal of improving the overall health of a group of individuals. Examples include chronic disease management based on population health data and initiatives to address social determinants of health.

GYVBqG0.title: Normal weight
GYVBqG0.description: Adults with a body mass index (BMI) of 18.5–24.9 kg/m² are considered to have a healthy weight. A different BMI range (18.5–22.9 kg/m²) has been proposed for individuals of Asian descent. Normal weight in children is defined as a BMI between the 5th and 85th percentile.

8YVOIG0.title: Muscle fatigue
8YVOIG0.description: The physical inability to continue a movement after several repetitions. Can be physiological, e.g., due to excessive physical exertion, or pathological, e.g., due to neuromuscular disorders such as myasthenia gravis.

vYVAIG0.title: Allergic fungal rhinosinusitis
vYVAIG0.description: A noninvasive fungal form of chronic rhinosinusitis in which fungus colonizing the sinuses triggers an immunologic reaction. Symptoms include thick, peanut butter-like mucin, nasal polyps, hyposmia or anosmia, and facial pressure, fullness, and/or pain.

CYVqrG0.title: Torsional profile
CYVqrG0.description: A rotational profile of the lower extremities used to identify pathological conditions that cause angular or rotational deformities. Includes measurements of the foot progression angle, thigh-foot angle, and external and internal hip rotation

xYVErG0.title: Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema
xYVErG0.description: A syndrome characterized by the coexistence of pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema. Respiratory symptoms such as exertional dyspnea and chronic cough progress over time. There is no specific treatment. Primarily affects smokers and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality.

WbVPsG0.title: FS pattern
WbVPsG0.description: A high-performance liquid chromatography or isoelectric focusing finding that is consistent with sickle cell disease. The presence of hemoglobin types F (HbF) and S (HbS) are reported in decreasing order of concentration.

RbVltG0.title: Tinidazole
RbVltG0.description: A nitroimidazole antimicrobial used in trichomoniasis, giardiasis, amebiasis, and bacterial vaginosis.

jbV_tG0.title: Acute liver injury
jbV_tG0.description: Acute hepatic necrosis that results in elevated transaminases (with or without hyperbilirubinemia) and impaired liver function (i.e., coagulopathy) in patients with no encephalopathy and no chronic liver disease. Can progress to acute liver failure or be fully reversible.

kbVmFG0.title: Brexanolone
kbVmFG0.description: An intravenous drug that is chemically identical to the neurosteroid allopregnanolone and positively modulates GABA-A receptors in the brain. Used to treat postpartum depression. Adverse effects include sedation, dry mouth, loss of consciousness, and flushing.

ObVIFG0.title: Zuranolone
ObVIFG0.description: An oral drug that is chemically identical to the neurosteroid allopregnanolone and positively modulates GABA-A receptors in the brain. Used to treat postpartum depression. Adverse effects include somnolence, dizziness, fatigue, diarrhea, nasopharyngitis, and urinary tract infections.

obV0uG0.title: Sialagogue
obV0uG0.description: A substance that stimulates salivation, such as chewing gum or sour candies. Often used in patients with salivary gland disorders (e.g., sialolithiasis, sialadenitis, and salivary stasis) or xerostomia.

AbVRwG0.title: Letermovir
AbVRwG0.description: An antiviral therapy approved for the prevention of cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection in individuals who received a hemopoietic stem cell transplant or kidney transplant from a CMV-positive donor.

_bV5wG0.title: GD
_bV5wG0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Gestational diabetes
2) Graves disease
3) Gender dysphoria

ZXVZ9G0.title: High-risk conditions for breast cancer
ZXVZ9G0.description: Factors associated with a significantly increased risk of breast cancer. These include a personal history of breast cancer, confirmed or suspected genetic predisposition for breast cancer (e.g., personal or family history of BRCA-related cancers or familial cancer syndromes), and a history of radiation to the chest at a young age.

0XVe9G0.title: Functional leg length discrepancy
0XVe9G0.description: An apparent difference in the lengths of the legs due to muscle abnormalities. Causes include neurological conditions, muscle imbalances (e.g., weakness and/or tightness of the pelvic muscles), contractures, and compensation for non-leg abnormalities (e.g., scoliosis). The leg bones are the same length.

aXVQ9G0.title: Anatomical leg length discrepancy
aXVQ9G0.description: A difference in the lengths of the leg bones. May be idiopathic, congenital (e.g., due to skeletal dysplasia or hemimelia), or acquired (e.g., due to infection or fracture).

YXVn9G0.title: Ultrasound conductivity
YXVn9G0.description: The ability of a medium to conduct ultrasound waves.

bXVH9G0.title: Angle of insonation
bXVH9G0.description: The angle between the ultrasound beam emitted by a transducer and the area of interest.

XXV99G0.title: Acute stress reaction
XXV99G0.description: A response that follows a traumatic event. Symptoms include sadness, fatigue, confusion, decreased concentration and/or memory, hyperarousal, and dissociation. Typically resolves rapidly with reassurance and supportive care.

TXV6xG0.title: Severity-of-illness score for toxic epidermal necrolysis
TXV6xG0.description: A scoring system used to predict the mortality rate for patients with toxic epidermal necrolysis. Incorporates clinical and laboratory risk factors: age ≥ 40 years, malignancy, tachycardia ≥ 120 bpm, glucose > 252 mg/dL, initial percentage of epidermal detachment > 10%, BUN > 28 mg/dL, and bicarbonate < 20 mmol/L.

5XViAG0.title: Tazarotene
5XViAG0.description: A topical retinoid used in the management of acne, psoriasis, and sun-damaged skin

MXVMAG0.title: Euthyroidism
MXVMAG0.description: A state of normal thyroid function and/or normal thyroid hormone levels. Seen in individuals without thyroid disease or patients with adequately treated thyroid disease.

nXV7AG0.title: Resmetirom
nXV7AG0.description: A thyroid hormone receptor beta–selective agonist for the treatment of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis with liver fibrosis.

LXVwAG0.title: Urea (topical)
LXVwAG0.description: A keratolytic agent used in the management of hyperkeratotic conditions such as keratosis pilaris, corns and calluses, keratoderma, and psoriasis

oXV0_G0.title: Infectious respiratory particle
oXV0_G0.description: A pathogen that is expired from an infected person (via, e.g., breathing, talking, coughing, sneezing) and carried through the air.

IXVYzG0.title: Breast self-awareness
IXVYzG0.description: Familiarity with the normal appearance and texture of one's breasts. Counseling individuals to alert health care providers if there is any concerning change in the breast (e.g., lump, nipple discharge, localized pain, skin changes like dimpling or puckering) may help in the early identification of breast cancer.

ccVaYt0.title: Relative value units
ccVaYt0.description: A measure determining the relative value of a medical service compared to all other medical services based on resource utilization (e.g., provider work, operating expenses, liability). Used as a factor in calculating clinician reimbursement.

WcVPYt0.title: Emergency department fast track
WcVPYt0.description: An emergency department pathway in which patients with relatively benign conditions are rapidly evaluated, treated, and discharged, often in a separate, high-throughput area. Conditions appropriate for fast track include URIs, UTIs, and minor traumatic injuries.

destinations.label: Emergency department administration → Patient flow and throughput

dcVoYt0.title: Emergency department observation unit
dcVoYt0.description: A hospital unit for emergency department patients who require an additional 6–24 hours of medical care to determine their disposition.

destinations.label: Emergency department administration → Patient flow and throughput

VcVGYt0.title: Tauopathy
VcVGYt0.description: A class of neurodegenerative diseases characterized by the abnormal accumulation of misfolded tau protein in the brain. Examples include Alzheimer disease, frontotemporal dementia, chronic traumatic encephalopathy, progressive supranuclear palsy, and corticobasal degeneration.

ecVxYt0.title: Screening mammography
ecVxYt0.description: Mammography performed in asymptomatic individuals for early identification and management of breast cancer. Typically limited to bilateral craniocaudal and mediolateral oblique views of the breast. Additional views or digital breast tomosynthesis may be performed to improve visualization of breast tissue if necessary.

UcVbbt0.title: Diagnostic mammography
UcVbbt0.description: Mammography performed to evaluate concerning breast symptoms (e.g., breast mass, focal pain, nipple discharge) or to further evaluate abnormalities detected on screening mammography or breast MRI. In addition to craniocaudal and mediolateral views, supplemental views (e.g., spot compression with magnification) with or without digital breast tomosynthesis may be performed to improve visualization of breast abnormalities.

2cVTbt0.title: Risk factors for peripartum depression
2cVTbt0.description: Risk factors include personal or family history of depression, unplanned or undesired pregnancy, medical complications during pregnancy, lack of social support, financial stress, and history of intimate partner violence.

destinations.label: Major depressive disorder → Depression in the peripartum period

OcVIct0.title: ACD
OcVIct0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1) Anemia of chronic disease
2) Allergic contact dermatitis

mcVV1t0.title: Ocular torticollis
mcVV1t0.description: An abnormal head position that compensates for visual disturbances caused by a condition involving the eyes (e.g., nystagmus, strabismus). May be congenital or acquired.

pcVLWt0.title: Primary Care PTSD Screen for DSM-5
pcVLWt0.description: A questionnaire used in the primary care setting to screen for PTSD. Consists of an initial screening question on exposure to trauma and 5 questions about symptoms. Scores range from 0 to 5, with higher scores (4–5 in men, 3–5 in women) suggesting PTSD.

media.title: Primary Care PTSD Screen for DSM-5 (PC-PTSD-5)

JcVsWt0.title: PTSD Checklist for DSM-5
JcVsWt0.description: A self-report checklist to assess for the presence and severity of PTSD symptoms. Contains 20 items and is based on the DSM-5 diagnostic criteria.

qcVCWt0.title: Triclabendazole
qcVCWt0.description: An antihelminthic benzimidazole derivative used to treat fascioliasis.

IcVYdt0.title: Cancer survivor
IcVYdt0.description: Anyone diagnosed with cancer, from the time of diagnosis throughout their lives. Some definitions also include family members, friends, and caregivers who support an individual with a cancer diagnosis.

destinations.label: Principles of cancer care → Cancer survivorship

scVtdt0.title: Tirbanibulin
scVtdt0.description: A topical microtubule inhibitor used to treat actinic keratosis.

GcVBdt0.title: Annular skin lesion
GcVBdt0.description: A circular or serpiginous macule or skin patch with an erythematous periphery and central clearing. Most commonly a tinea infection.

8cVOVt0.title: Postextubation laryngeal edema
8cVOVt0.description: A complication of endotracheal intubation in which a patient develops swelling in the larynx after extubation. May result in stridor, respiratory distress, and/or respiratory failure. Managed with corticosteroids and/or reintubation.

EcV8Vt0.title: Diaphragm pacing
EcV8Vt0.description: External electrical stimulation of the phrenic nerve or diaphragm to induce diaphragmatic contraction. Used to wean patients from mechanical ventilation and restore efficient breathing in patients with high spinal cord injuries or central hypoventilation syndromes. Uses intrathoracic or intraperitoneal electrodes and an externally worn stimulator box.

wcVhet0.title: Stertor
wcVhet0.description: A low-pitched flapping or snoring sound that results from soft tissue or secretions obstructing the nose, mouth, nasopharynx, and/or oropharynx.

c1Vaft0.title: Posterior tibial tendon dysfunction
c1Vaft0.description: A condition in which inflammation or a tear of the posterior tibial tendon leads to collapse of the medial foot arch. Most common cause of acquired pes planus in adults.

W1VPft0.title: Cyclopentolate
W1VPft0.description: An antimuscarinic agent that is used as a topical mydriatric (e.g., for fundoscopy) and cycloplegic (e.g., for uveitis)

d1Voft0.title: Rigid pes planus
d1Voft0.description: A form of pes planus in which the medial arch remains flattened, regardless of foot positioning (i.e., with or without weight-bearing). May be congenital or acquired.

U1VbTt0.title: Gluteal cleft
U1VbTt0.description: The anatomical groove between the buttocks. Extends from the lower sacrum to the posterior border of the perineum.

21VTTt0.title: Diopter
21VTTt0.description: The unit of lens power used to measure refractive errors of the eye and the focusing strength of corrective lenses. A number farther from zero indicates a more severe refractive error.

h1Vcgt0.title: Refractory media
h1Vcgt0.description: The cornea, lens, aqueous humor, and vitreous humor. These components refract light toward the posterior retina, and defects lead to refractive errors (e.g., myopia, hyperopia).

P1VWSt0.title: Orthokeratology
P1VWSt0.description: The use of rigid gas-permeable contact lenses worn only while sleeping to temporarily reshape the cornea and improve vision. Used in the treatment of myopia.

41V3St0.title: Standard of care
41V3St0.description: A legal term that refers to the extent of care a prudent, reasonable person would perform in a given set of circumstances. In medical contexts, it generally refers to the proper treatment for a specific disease, as established by medical experts and widely practiced by other health care professionals.

O1VISt0.title: Photorefractive keratectomy
O1VISt0.description: Laser removal of the corneal surface. Indicated for the correction of myopia, hyperopia, and astigmatism.

l1VvSt0.title: Small incision lenticule extraction
l1VvSt0.description: Laser removal of a small disc of corneal tissue (a lenticule) through an incision adjacent to the cornea. Indicated for the correction of myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism, and presbyopia.

N1V-St0.title: Corneal ectasia
N1V-St0.description: Thinning and bulging of the cornea. Causes worsening of vision.

m1VVht0.title: Gross negligence
m1VVht0.description: A legal term that refers to reckless, willful, and/or wanton behavior that shows disregard for the safety of others.

G1VBRt0.title: Diffuse pleural thickening
G1VBRt0.description: The abnormal thickening of the pleura, often due to chronic inflammation or effusions. Causes include asbestos exposure and infection. Results in no or nonspecific symptoms such as chest pain.

F1Vgit0.title: Headache associated with refractive errors
F1Vgit0.description: A type of chronic headache that is aggravated by performing visual tasks at distances at which vision is impaired. Alleviated upon task cessation. Usually worse in the second half of the day.

81VOit0.title: Keratorefractive surgery
81VOit0.description: Surgical procedures in which the cornea is reshaped to correct myopia, hyperopia, and/or astigmatism. Includes laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK), photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), and small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE).

v1VAit0.title: Tumor, Node, Metastasis classification
v1VAit0.description: A tumor staging system developed by the American Joint Committee on Cancer. Evaluates the size and extent of the main tumor (T), number of nearby lymph nodes involved (N), and metastasis (M). Used to determine prognosis and guide management.

91VNQt0.title: Developmental lactase deficiency
91VNQt0.description: Transient lactase deficiency that occurs in premature infants. The immature gastrointestinal tract does not produce sufficient levels of lactase until at least 34 weeks of development.

YWVnPt0.title: ERBB2-targeted therapy
YWVnPt0.description: Systemic therapy for ERBB2+ breast cancer. Includes ERBB2-antibodies (e.g., trastuzumab, pertuzumab) and tyrosine-kinase inhibitors (e.g., lapatinib, neratinib).

WWVP4t0.title: Lactase deficiency
WWVP4t0.description: Insufficient levels of lactase in the small intestine, preventing the digestion of large quantities of dietary lactose, leading to lactose malabsorption. Caused by a genetic variant resulting in decreased lactase production or by disruption of the epithelium of the small intestine, resulting in loss of lactase. Can be asymptomatic or cause symptoms of lactose intolerance.

dWVo4t0.title: Lactose malabsorption
dWVo4t0.description:
The inability to digest lactose in the small intestine, leading to passage of lactose into the large intestine.
Can be asymptomatic or cause symptoms of lactose intolerance.

gWVFkt0.title: Rodenticide
gWVFkt0.description: A type of pesticide used to kill rodents (e.g., rats, mice). Active ingredients vary broadly. Examples include strychnine, superwarfarins (e.g., brodifacoum), arsenic, cholecalciferol, and metal phosphides.

hWVcOt0.title: FAST stroke score
hWVcOt0.description: An acronym to help with out-of-hospital identification of stroke: If the patient has any Facial droop, Arm weakness or numbness, or Speech problems, it is Time to call an ambulance. The BE FAST and FASTER modifications include balance and eyesight problems, while FAST PLUS includes severity of limb weakness.

3WVSOt0.title: Platypnea-orthodeoxia syndrome
3WVSOt0.description: A rare syndrome characterized by dyspnea and cyanosis in the upright position due to a right-to-left shunt, e.g., in patent foramen ovale and atrial septal defect.

NWV-lt0.title: Functional scoliosis
NWV-lt0.description: An apparent mild curvature of the spine due to factors such as leg length discrepancy or poor posture rather than a structural abnormality of the spine.

5WViNt0.title: Functional assessment staging tool
5WViNt0.description: A diagnostic tool used to assess the progression of dementia by evaluating a patient's functional abilities across seven stages, ranging from normal functioning to severe cognitive decline.

MWVMNt0.title: Antipseudomonal antibiotic
MWVMNt0.description: An antibiotic used to treat infections caused by P. aeruginosa. Examples include antipseudomonal penicillins (e.g., piperacillin/tazobactam), carbapenems (e.g., meropenem), and cefipime.

nWV7Nt0.title: Pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis
nWV7Nt0.description: An infection of the flexor tendon sheath of a finger. Most commonly caused by puncture wounds. Manifests with the Kanavel signs (fusiform swelling, tenderness to palpation, holding the finger in a flexed position at rest, and pain with passive extension.

JWVsmt0.title: LATCH score
JWVsmt0.description: A validated scoring system to assess the infant's latch during breastfeeding. The name is an acronym of the scores' components: Latch, Audible swallowing, Type of nipple, Comfort, and Hold. Intervention is recommended for scores less than 7.

_WV5Lt0.title: BCS
_WV5Lt0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Breast-conserving surgery
2. Budd-Chiari syndrome

-WVDLt0.title: Talazoparib
-WVDLt0.description: A PARP inhibitor used in the management of certain patients with breast cancer (e.g., patients with BRCA mutations) and metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

ZdVZot0.title: Pertuzumab
ZdVZot0.description: A monoclonal antibody that is a human epidermal growth factor receptor type 2 (ERBB2/HER2) antagonist. Used in the management of ERBB2+ breast cancer.

0dVeot0.title: Ado-trastuzumab emtansine
0dVeot0.description: A conjugate antineoplastic agent composed of an anti-ErbB2 antibody (trastuzumab) and a microtubule inhibitor (emtansine). Used in the management of ERBB2+ breast cancer.

bdVHot0.title: Lapatinib
bdVHot0.description: A tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in the management of ERBB2+ breast cancer.

WdVPKt0.title: Credible interval
WdVPKt0.description: A range of values within which a parameter is likely to lie based on the observed data and Bayesian analysis. Typically specified at a certain confidence level (e.g., 95% or 90%). Unlike frequentist confidence intervals, which reflect sampling variability, Bayesian credible intervals reflect the uncertainty in parameter estimation using the posterior distribution, which combines prior assumptions with current data.

ddVoKt0.title: Posterior probability
ddVoKt0.description: The revised probability of an event occurring after incorporating new information. Determined by updating the prior probability through the application of Bayes' theorem.

VdVGKt0.title: Oral iron
VdVGKt0.description: An orally administered form of iron (i.e., ferrous sulfate, ferrous gluconate, or ferrous fumarate) used for the prevention and treatment of iron-deficiency anemia. Adverse effects include constipation and other gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g., nausea, diarrhea, heartburn).

TdV66t0.title: Acute pilonidal abscess
TdV66t0.description: An acute infection of a pilonidal cyst

3dVSpt0.title: Excessive weight loss in breastfed infants

RdVlpt0.title: GRADE systematic approach
RdVlpt0.description: The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach is used to evaluate the certainty of evidence in systematic reviews.

idVJpt0.title: Friability
idVJpt0.description: The quality of easily crumbling or breaking up into smaller pieces, e.g., tissue that bleeds easily upon slight abrasion or manipulation. Commonly assessed in mucosal tissues such as the gastrointestinal tract or cervix to evaluate inflammation or malignancy.

QdVupt0.title: Post-injection delirium/sedation syndrome
QdVupt0.description: A rare adverse drug event that occurs in < 1% of patients treated with olanzapine long-acting injection. Characterized by excessive sedation and/or delirium that are consistent with the symptoms of oral olanzapine overdose.

jdV_pt0.title: Pre- and post-feed weight
jdV_pt0.description: The difference in infant weight measured before and after feeding under identical conditions. The difference between the pre- and post-feed weight in grams is equal to the amount of milk consumed in mL.

PdVWJt0.title: Pilonidal cyst
PdVWJt0.description: A cyst that forms near the upper gluteal cleft often due to accumulation of hair and skin debris. Can lead to infection, abscess formation, and eventual formation of a sinus tract.

LdVwqt0.title: Topical bexarotene
LdVwqt0.description: A synthetic retinoid analogue gel used to treat cutaneous T-cell lymphomas, e.g., mycosis fungoides.

odV0It0.title: Total body irradiation
odV0It0.description: A form of radiation therapy administered to the whole body. Often used as part of a conditioning regimen for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation to eradicate residual malignant cells, prevent graft rejection, and support the establishment of the new hematopoietic system.

KdVUIt0.title: Systemic bexarotene
KdVUIt0.description: An oral synthetic retinoid analogue used to treat cutaneous T-cell lymphomas, e.g., mycosis fungoides.

6dVjIt0.title: Vorinostat
6dVjIt0.description: An oral histone deacetylase inhibitor used to treat cutaneous T-cell lymphomas, e.g., mycosis fungoides.

JdVsIt0.title: Brentuximab vedotin
JdVsIt0.description: An antibody-drug conjugate that delivers monomethyl auristatin E (a cytotoxic microtubule inhibitor) to CD30+ cells. Administered intravenously and used to treat Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas.

qdVCIt0.title: Exclusive breast milk
qdVCIt0.description: The use of breast milk (i.e., from breastfeeding, self-expressed breast milk, and donor breast milk) as the only form of infant nutrition. Encouraged for all infants less than 6 months of age.

IdVYrt0.title: Hypoallergenic formula
IdVYrt0.description: An infant formula that does not cause an allergic reaction in ≥ 90% of infants with a confirmed cow's milk protein allergy. Includes extensively hydrolyzed infant formulas and amino acid infant formulas.
