sdVtrt0.title: Posthospital syndrome
sdVtrt0.description: A transient state in discharged patients characterized by an increased risk for adverse health events unrelated to the initial diagnosis. Caused by physiologic stressors commonly encountered during hospitalization, such as sleep deprivation, poor nutrition, poor pain control, and deconditioning. Increases the risk of readmission after discharge.

FdVg7t0.title: Graded motor imagery
FdVg7t0.description: A program used in the management of complex regional pain syndrome. The premotor and primary motor cortex are activated across three phases: 1. discriminating between left and right limbs (using pictures); 2. motor imagery (imagining limb movements); 3. mirror therapy (observing reflected limb movements in a mirror).

udVp7t0.title: Sarecycline
udVp7t0.description: A narrow-spectrum tetracycline antibiotic used to treat moderate to severe acne.

wdVhHt0.title: Adapalene
wdVhHt0.description: A topical retinoid used to treat acne vulgaris.

ydVdst0.title: Noninfectious meningitis
ydVdst0.description: An inflammation of the meninges, with negative CSF Gram stain and culture. Often used interchangeably with aseptic meningitis but technically a subform of aseptic meningitis with a noninfectious cause (e.g., medications, malignancy)

AdVRst0.title: Drug-induced meningitis
AdVRst0.description: A noninfectious inflammation of the protective membranes surrounding the brain and the spinal cord that is caused by an adverse reaction to certain medications (e.g., NSAIDs, sulfa drugs).

aVVQGt0.title: Burn center
aVVQGt0.description: A hospital-based facility providing specialized multidisciplinary care for patients with burns. Typically provides both acute care and long-term rehabilitation services.

YVVnGt0.title: Biosynthetic dressing
YVVnGt0.description: A dressing that mimics the dermal and epidermal structures, allowing reepithelialization of the wound while preventing mechanical trauma and bacterial infection.

bVVHGt0.title: Target trial emulation study
bVVHGt0.description: A study that mimics the design and conditions (eligibility criteria, treatment assignment, follow-up procedures, and outcome assessment) of a hypothetical randomized controlled trial (target trial) using observational data. Allows researchers to approximate the causal effects of interventions or exposures in situations in which conducting a randomized controlled trial is impractical or unethical.

XVV9Gt0.title: Clinical features of ascites
XVV9Gt0.description: Features include signs of progressive abdominal distention (e.g., early satiety, weight gain, dyspnea), flank dullness, and shifting dullness.

VVVGtt0.title: Exagamglogene autotemcel
VVVGtt0.description: A gene therapy used in patients with sickle cell disease and recurrent vasoocclusive crises to increase production of fetal hemoglobin and prevent polymerization of hemoglobin S.

eVVxtt0.title: Lovotibeglogene autotemcel
eVVxtt0.description: A gene therapy used in patients with sickle cell disease and recurrent vasoocclusive crises. Edits stem cells to produce a novel form of hemoglobin A, similar in structure to normal adult hemoglobin A.

3VVS8t0.title: Anorgasmia
3VVS8t0.description: Persistent delay of, difficulty achieving, or absence of orgasm, despite otherwise adequate sexual stimulation. May result in distress. Causes include medical or psychiatric conditions (e.g., anxiety) and certain medications (e.g., SSRIs).

4VV3ut0.title: Radiation recall dermatitis
4VV3ut0.description: Acute dermatitis in an area previously treated with radiotherapy, triggered by subsequent medication use (especially chemotherapy agents). Most commonly occurs within 2 months of radiotherapy.

kVVmut0.title: Ovarian transposition
kVVmut0.description: A surgical procedure in which one or both ovaries are separated from the uterus and moved to the paracolic gutter above the iliac crests. Performed before pelvic radiotherapy in individuals who want to preserve fertility.

OVVIut0.title: Sphincter of Oddi manometry
OVVIut0.description: A diagnostic test used in the evaluation of suspected sphincter of Oddi dysfunction. The pressure of the biliary and/or pancreatic ducts is measured with a catheter during ERCP. Pressure ≥ 40 mm Hg in either duct is consistent with sphincter of Oddi dysfunction.

lVVvut0.title: Bull neck appearance
lVVvut0.description: A term used to describe severe cervical lymphadenopathy and soft tissue swelling caused by respiratory diphtheria. Can lead to airway obstruction.

NVV-ut0.title: Luliconazole
NVV-ut0.description: A topical azole antifungal used to treat dermatophyte infections such as tinea pedis, tinea cruris, and tinea corporis.

mVVVEt0.title: Naftifine
mVVVEt0.description: A topical allylamine antifungal used to treat dermatophyte infections such as tinea pedis, tinea cruris, and tinea corporis.

5VViEt0.title: Two feet-one hand syndrome
5VViEt0.description: A dermatophyte infection involving both feet (tinea pedis) and a single (usually the dominant) hand (tinea manuum). Thought to result from autoinoculation as patients scratch an affected area on one foot, spreading it to the hand, and later to the second foot.

MVVMEt0.title: Functional biliary sphincter dysfunction
MVVMEt0.description: Biliary pain that is associated with either elevated liver chemistries or a dilated bile duct and occurs in the absence of structural abnormalities. Thought to be due to dysfunctional motility.

destinations.label: Sphincter of Oddi dysfunction → Suspected biliary sphincter dysfunction

nVV7Et0.title: Functional pancreatic sphincter dysfunction
nVV7Et0.description: Recurrent confirmed episodes of pancreatitis that are associated with abnormal manometry and occur in the absence of structural abnormalities. Thought to be due to dysfunctional motility.

destinations.label: Sphincter of Oddi dysfunction → Suspected pancreatic sphincter dysfunction

rVVfDt0.title: Decontamination measures for lice infestation
rVVfDt0.description: Measures taken to eradicate lice from bedding, clothing, and towels. Involves machine washing items at ≥ 54°C for > 5 minutes. Items that cannot be laundered may be either sealed in a plastic bag for 2 weeks or dry-cleaned.

8VVOwt0.title: Clinical informatics
8VVOwt0.description: A field of practice in which information and communication systems are utilized to improve patient care. Applications include implementing clinical decision support tools, refining clinical processes, and establishing and optimizing electronic health records.

uVVpwt0.title: Left without being seen
uVVpwt0.description: The action of patients who register and/or are triaged in the emergency department but depart before being evaluated by a clinician. Left without being seen rates are often used as a quality indicator for emergency health care delivery.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Liability and litigation

DVV19t0.title: Majocchi granuloma
DVV19t0.description: A rare granulomatous reaction to fungal infection of a hair follicle. May develop after tinea corporis is treated with topical corticosteroids.

wVVh9t0.title: Left without treatment
wVVh9t0.description: The action of patients who register and/or are triaged in the emergency department but depart before receiving treatment. Includes leaving without being seen and seeing a clinician but leaving before treatment.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Liability and litigation

9VVN9t0.title: Discharged against medical advice
9VVN9t0.description: The action of patients who depart before the treating clinician recommends discharge.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Liability and litigation

CVVq9t0.title: Left before treatment complete
CVVq9t0.description: The action of patients who register and/or are triaged in the emergency department but depart before discharge by a clinician. Includes leaving without being seen, leaving without treatment, leaving against medical advice, and eloping.

destinations.label: Principles of medical law and ethics → Liability and litigation

ceVaBt0.title: Aseptic meningitis
ceVaBt0.description: An inflammation of the meninges, with negative CSF Gram stain and culture. Causes can be viral (e.g., enterovirus) or noninfectious (e.g., medication, malignancy). In contrast to bacterial meningitis, the onset may be less acute and altered mental status is not a typical finding.

WeVPBt0.title: Buboes
WeVPBt0.description: Enlarged, tender, and inflamed inguinal and/or axillary lymph nodes. Commonly associated with lymphogranuloma venereum and other infectious diseases (e.g., syphilis, chancroid, and plague).

VeVGBt0.title: Fluocinonide
VeVGBt0.description: A topical corticosteroid used to treat dermatologic conditions that manifest with inflammation and pruritus (e.g., dermatitis and psoriasis).

jeV_At0.title: PET-CT scan
jeV_At0.description: An imaging technique that combines a PET scan and a CT scan, often using both a tracer (e.g., FGD) and contrast. This type of scan is commonly used for cancer diagnosis, staging, and follow-up, as well as before invasive procedures (e.g., biopsies, surgery), as it can provide accurate measurements of neoplastic lesions.

4eV3_t0.title: Nitrogen dioxide poisoning
4eV3_t0.description: A condition caused by exposure to nitrogen dioxide (a reddish-brown gas with a pungent odor), classically in the setting of working in a silo. Reaction of nitrogen dioxide with water (e.g., from the mucous membranes) forms nitric acid, which causes irritation and burning of the mucous membranes. Manifestations of poisoning include respiratory symptoms (e.g., cough, dyspnea), conjunctival symptoms (e.g., eye tearing), and pulmonary symptoms (e.g., chemical pneumonitis).

leVv_t0.title: Febrile status epilepticus
leVv_t0.description: A febrile seizure that lasts more than 30 minutes or a series of febrile seizures lasting more than 30 minutes in total without full recovery of consciousness between seizures. May be generalized or focal.

5eVizt0.title: Monoclonal immunoglobulin glomerulonephritis
5eVizt0.description: A type of glomerulonephritis in which monoclonal immunoglobulins lead to renal damage through a variety of mechanisms, including complement activation and deposition in the glomeruli, renal tubules, or blood vessels. Can manifest in various conditions (e.g., monoclonal immunoglobulin deposition disease, proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits) depending on the mechanism.

neV7zt0.title: Small bowel aspirate
neV7zt0.description: A endoscopic procedure used to sample fluid from the small bowel. Gold standard test for small intestinal bacterial overgrowth.

LeVwzt0.title: Fructose malabsorption
LeVwzt0.description: The inability to absorb fructose in the small intestine, leading to passage of fructose into the large intestine. Bacterial fermentation of fructose and an influx of water into the colon due to increased oncotic pressure can cause abdominal pain, bloating, and diarrhea. May be primary (e.g., hereditary fructose intolerance) or occur secondary to another condition or medication.

oeV0-t0.title: Fluocinolone
oeV0-t0.description: A synthetic corticosteroid administered topically for the treatment of dermatologic conditions that manifest with inflammation and pruritus (e.g., seborrheic dermatitis, psoriasis). Also used as an intravitreal injection in patients with diabetic macular edema.

KeVU-t0.title: Desonide
KeVU-t0.description: A low-potency topical corticosteroid used to treat dermatologic conditions that manifest with inflammation and pruritus (e.g., atopic dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis).

peVL-t0.title: Fertile window
peVL-t0.description: A 6-day window encompassing the 5 days prior to ovulation and the day of ovulation itself, during which an individual is most likely to become pregnant if intercourse occurs.

JeVs-t0.title: Berdazimer gel
JeVs-t0.description: A nitric oxide-releasing agent used to treat molluscum contagiosum in individuals ≥ 1 year of age.

DeV1aF0.title: HPV-related cancers
DeV1aF0.description: Cancers associated with persistent infection with high-risk (oncogenic) types of human papillomavirus (HPV). Includes cervical cancer, other anogenital cancers (e.g., anal cancer, vulvar cancer, penile cancer), and oropharyngeal cancer. HPV vaccination protects against HPV-related cancers.

destinations.label: Human papillomavirus infection → Overview of HPV-associated diseases

weVhaF0.title: Periorificial dermatitis
weVhaF0.description: An inflammatory skin condition characterized by papules and pustules around orifices. Most commonly affects the skin around the mouth (perioral dermatitis) but may affect the skin around the eyes (periorbital dermatitis) or genitals.

9eVNaF0.title: Granulomatous periorificial dermatitis
9eVNaF0.description: A skin condition that manifests with flesh-colored or yellow-brown papules around the mouth, eyes, and nose. Most common in children of color.

xeVEaF0.title: Rolling stone sign
xeVEaF0.description: An ultrasound finding characterized by echogenic foci in the gallbladder that move on repositioning the patient. Differentiates a gallstone from a gallbladder polyp.

ZUVZbF0.title: Laryngectomy
ZUVZbF0.description: Surgical removal of the larynx, most often used to treat laryngeal cancer. May be total or partial (e.g., supraglottic, supracricoid) depending on procedure indication and/or extent of cancer spread. Patients who undergo partial laryngectomy may retain speech and swallowing function. Total laryngectomy affects both speech and swallowing.

0UVebF0.title: Clinical features of tonsillopharyngitis
0UVebF0.description: Features include sudden onset of fever, sore throat, and painful swallowing. Findings may include tender, swollen cervical lymph nodes and tonsillar exudates.

destinations.label: Acute tonsillitis and pharyngitis → Clinical features

aUVQbF0.title: Clinical features of septic arthritis
aUVQbF0.description: Features include acute onset of fever, joint pain, and restricted range of motion. Joints are swollen, red, warm, and painful. Usually monoarticular.

YUVnbF0.title: Dextrose 5% LR
YUVnbF0.description: Lactated Ringer's solution that also contains 50 mg/mL of glucose. Used to prevent hypoglycemia in susceptible patients, e.g., injured or dehydrated infants and children.

1UV2XF0.title: Pregnancy options counseling
1UV2XF0.description: The provision of unbiased, nonjudgmental information and support, as well as necessary referrals, to pregnant individuals regarding their options, which include parenting, adoption, or induced abortion. Usually relevant in the context of unintended pregnancies.

mUVVdF0.title: Cantharidin
mUVVdF0.description: An FDA-approved topical agent used to treat molluscum contagiosum in individuals ≥ 2 years of age.

MUVMdF0.title: Dural puncture epidural anesthesia
MUVMdF0.description: A form of neuraxial anesthesia in which a local anesthetic is injected into the epidural space after the puncture of the dura, allowing a small amount of anesthetic to move into the subarachnoid space. Allows for a more rapid onset of analgesia than epidural anesthesia alone and avoids the risk of fetal bradycardia associated with combined spinal-epidural anesthesia. Most commonly used during labor.

LUVwdF0.title: Paracervical block
LUVwdF0.description: The injection of a local anesthetic into the vaginal fornices (lateral to the cervix) to provide analgesia for the cervix and uterus. Most commonly used for pain management during labor or placement of an IUD.

qUVCVF0.title: Intestinal methanogen overgrowth
qUVCVF0.description: A condition characterized by a pathological overgrowth of methane-producing archaea in the gastrointestinal tract. Clinical features include constipation (most common symptom) and other symptoms seen in small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, e.g., flatulence and abdominal pain.

IUVYeF0.title: Archaea
IUVYeF0.description: A type of single-celled prokaryotic organism, distinct from bacteria due to, e.g., cell wall characteristics. Found in the human gastrointestinal system and often associated with the ability to inhabit extreme environments. Excess archaea causes intestinal methanogen overgrowth.

7UV4eF0.title: Sclerokeratitis
7UV4eF0.description: Inflammation of the sclera (scleritis) and cornea (keratitis).

tUVXUF0.title: Sulfacetamide sodium/sulfur
tUVXUF0.description: A combination medication composed of an antibacterial agent (sulfacetamide sodium) and a keratolytic (sulfur). Used to treat acne, seborrheic dermatitis, and rosacea.

FUVgUF0.title: Intestinal failure
FUVgUF0.description: A severe decrease in intestinal function that prevents adequate absorption of macronutrients and/or water and electrolytes, necessitating intravenous supplementation. May be classified as acute, prolonged, or chronic. Common causes include short bowel syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease.

vUVAUF0.title: Filiform wart
vUVAUF0.description: A hyperkeratotic lesion that affects the face and/or neck and is caused by HPV infection. Usually composed of a narrow base with a single or multiple finger-like projections.

yUVdfF0.title: Syringoma
yUVdfF0.description: A benign tumor of the sweat gland. Syringomas frequently occur in clusters and are most commonly seen on the eyelids but also affect other parts of the face and body.

_UV5fF0.title: Autoinoculation
_UV5fF0.description: The transmission of microorganisms from one part of the body to another. Common in infections that spread via direct contact (e.g., cutaneous warts, molluscum contagiosum).

zUVrfF0.title: Tangenital excision
zUVrfF0.description: The removal of abnormal tissue, layer by layer, until healthy tissue is reached. Most commonly used in burns.

Z2VZTF0.title: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion
Z2VZTF0.description: A condition characterized by excess cortisol secretion (ACTH-independent) without overt clinical features of Cushing syndrome. It is the most common type of functional adrenal incidentaloma. Patients have an increased risk of cardiometabolic disorders.

12V2gF0.title: Pyrethrins with piperonyl butoxide
12V2gF0.description: A topical combination medication that consists of pyrethrins (organic compounds that are neurotoxic to lice) and piperonyl butoxide, which enhances their pediculicidal activity. Used to treat lice infestation.

W2VPgF0.title: Spinosad
W2VPgF0.description: A topical pediculicidal and ovicidal agent that is neurotoxic to lice. Used to treat lice infestation.

e2VxgF0.title: Prevention of lice transmission and reinfection
e2VxgF0.description: Includes measures to eradicate lice from bedding, clothing, and towels (e.g., machine washing items at ≥ 54°C (≥ 130°F), sealing items in a plastic bag for 2 weeks, or dry-cleaning), examining and treating close contacts, and cleaning hairbrushes and accessories (for head lice infestation).

22VTSF0.title: Features highly suggestive of ocular rosacea
22VTSF0.description: Features strongly suggestive of ocular rosacea include conjunctival hyperemia and telangiectasias at lid margins. Slit-lamp examination findings include corneal spade-shaped infiltrates and scleritis or sclerokeratitis.

T2V6SF0.title: Carbohydrate malabsorption
T2V6SF0.description: The inability to efficiently absorb nutritional carbohydrates (e.g., lactose, fructose, sorbitol) in the small intestine, either due to primary (e.g., lactase deficiency) or secondary causes (e.g., SIBO, Crohn disease).

32VShF0.title: Molluscum dermatitis
32VShF0.description: A pruritic eczematous reaction that manifests around molluscum contagiosum lesions. Commonly occurs in patients with atopic dermatitis.

j2V_hF0.title: C3 glomerulopathy
j2V_hF0.description: A rare kidney disease resulting from dysregulation of the alternative complement pathway, leading to deposition of complement factors in the glomeruli. May be acquired or hereditary and is often triggered by infections or autoimmune disorders. Results in glomerulonephritis. Examples include C3 glomerulonephritis and dense deposit disease.

42V33F0.title: Lymphoproliferative disorders
42V33F0.description: A group of disorders characterized by an abnormal proliferation of lymphocytic stem cells that manifest as monoclonal lymphocytosis, lymphadenopathy, and bone marrow infiltration. Examples include B-cell neoplasms, T-cell neoplasms, NK-cell neoplasms, and Hodgkin lymphoma.

k2Vm3F0.title: FIP1L1-PDGFRA
k2Vm3F0.description: A fusion gene caused by a deletion on chromosome 4q12. Results in a constitutively active tyrosine kinase, causing primary eosinophilia.

l2Vv3F0.title: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition Text Revision
l2Vv3F0.description: The revised text of the fifth iteration of a system that provides nomenclature for and classifies psychiatric disorders, published by the American Psychiatric Association.

M2VMRF0.title: Oropouche virus disease
M2VMRF0.description: A midge- and mosquito-borne tropical disease that causes chills, myalgias, arthralgias, abrupt-onset fever, and severe headache. Onset of symptoms occurs within 3-10 days of being bitten. Treatment is supportive and patients usually make a full recovery within one week.

72V4QF0.title: Ground truth
72V4QF0.description: A term used in statistics and machine learning to refer to accurate and verified data obtained through gold standard observation methods that is assumed to be true. Used as a reference point for training and validating machine learning models.

A2VR4F0.title: Potentially sensitizing antepartum events
A2VR4F0.description: Any event during pregnancy during which RhD-negative maternal blood might be exposed to RhD-positive fetal blood. Includes threatened or confirmed pregnancy loss (e.g., spontaneous miscarriage, threatened miscarriage, intrauterine fetal demise), termination of pregnancy, ectopic pregnancy, evacuation of molar pregnancy, invasive prenatal procedures (e.g., chorionic villus sampling, amniocentesis, cordocentesis), antepartum hemorrhage, external cephalic version, and abdominal trauma.

destinations.label: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn → Pathophysiology

_2V54F0.title: Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended
_2V54F0.description: A tool used to assess a patient's global outcome after a traumatic brain injury.  Scores are determined using an ordinal scale ranging from 1 (death) to 8 (full return to normal life). The tool incorporates a patient interview to provide a more nuanced assessment of moderate and good neurological outcomes than the original Glasgow Outcome Scale.

WfVPOF0.title: Secondary tinnitus
WfVPOF0.description: Tinnitus resulting from an identifiable underlying condition. Examples of underlying conditions include infectious, traumatic, and degenerative disorders of the ear; neurological or vascular diseases; and exposure to ototoxic substances.

dfVoOF0.title: Primary tinnitus
dfVoOF0.description: Tinnitus with no discernible underlying cause (i.e., idiopathic). May be associated with sensorineural hearing loss.

VfVGOF0.title: Bothersome tinnitus
VfVGOF0.description: Tinnitus that negatively impacts functioning and quality of life, e.g., it affects sleep, mental health, and/or cognition. Considered persistent if present for at least 6 months.

efVxOF0.title: Nonbothersome tinnitus
efVxOF0.description: Tinnitus that is noticeable but does not negatively impact functioning or quality of life.

UfVblF0.title: Recent-onset tinnitus
UfVblF0.description: Tinnitus that has been present for less than 6 months.

hfVcNF0.title: Reactive leukocytosis
hfVcNF0.description: An elevation in WBC (usually 11,000–30,000/mm³) resulting from stress (e.g., due to surgery, burns, vigorous exercise), medications (e.g., corticosteroids, lithium), or rebound after severe anemia (e.g., following hemorrhage).

jfV_NF0.title: Hospital formulary
jfV_NF0.description: A database of medications that are approved for use in a hospital or healthcare system. Includes information on dosing, administration, and safety monitoring to enable safe and cost-effective use.

kfVmmF0.title: Hydroureteronephrosis
kfVmmF0.description: Dilatation and distension of the renal collecting system and ureter due to distal obstruction.

NfV-mF0.title: Red flags in tinnitus
NfV-mF0.description: Clinical features that suggest a potentially concerning underlying cause of tinnitus. These include unilateral tinnitus, pulsatile tinnitus, sudden or unilateral hearing loss, and focal neurological deficits.

tfVXLF0.title: Chronic blood loss
tfVXLF0.description: A ≥ 2 g/dL decrease in hemoglobin over a 6-month period in the absence of overt signs of bleeding.

ufVpLF0.title: Stapedial myoclonus
ufVpLF0.description: A type of middle ear myoclonus that involves the repeated contraction of the stapedius muscle. Causes an intermittent rhythmic tinnitus that is often described as thumping, tapping, ticking, or clicking.

vfVALF0.title: Vonoprazan
vfVALF0.description: A potassium-competitive acid blocker used in the treatment of erosive esophagitis, GERD, and H. pylori infection. For H. pylori infection, it is used as part of combination therapy.

9fVNoF0.title: Absolute eosinophil count
9fVNoF0.description: The number of eosinophils per cubic millimeter of blood, calculated by multiplying the total white blood cell count by the percentage of eosinophils. Normal values range from 0/mm³ to 500/mm³.

CfVqoF0.title: Platelet-derived growth factor receptor beta gene
CfVqoF0.description: A gene that encodes platelet-derived growth factor receptor beta (PDGFRB) protein. Mutations in this gene are associated with conditions including chronic eosinophilic leukemia and primary familial brain calcification.

BfVzoF0.title: CTD
BfVzoF0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Connective tissue disease
2. Carboxy-terminal domain

zfVrKF0.title: Odontoid view
zfVrKF0.description: A modified anteroposterior view of the C₂ vertebra obtained with the patient's mouth open. Used to improve visualization of the odontoid process and atlantoaxial joint space on plain radiography of the cervical spine.

ZTVZ6F0.title: Anoderm
ZTVZ6F0.description: Nonkeratinized squamous epithelial tissue that lines the distal portion of the anal canal from the dentate line to the anal verge. Unlike typical skin, anoderm lacks hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and melanocytes.

bTVH6F0.title: Cerebral performance category
bTVH6F0.description: A five-point scale used to assess neurological function after cardiac arrest. A score of 1 represents good function, with only minor deficits. Scores of 2 and 3 are used for conscious patients with significant disabilities; patients with a score of 2 are usually independent and patients with a score of 3 are more severely affected and are dependent on care. Patients with a score of 4 are unconscious, and patients with a score of 5 meet criteria for brain death.

cTVapF0.title: 6-minute walk test
cTVapF0.description: A test used to assess functional exercise capacity. Patients walk as far as they can on level ground for 6 minutes; normal values in healthy individuals range from 400 m to 700 m. Commonly used in patients with cardiac and respiratory disease.

WTVPpF0.title: Walking Impairment Questionnaire
WTVPpF0.description: A questionnaire that assesses self-reported walking difficulty in patients with peripheral arterial disease. Comprises four subscales: pain severity, distance, speed, and stairs. The original version is administered in-person by an interviewer, while the modified version can be self-administered or administered by an interviewer over the phone.

3TVSqF0.title: Supervised injection facility
3TVSqF0.description: A facility where individuals can inject preobtained drugs using sterile equipment under medical supervision to reduce the risk of overdose and acquiring infectious diseases.

RTVlqF0.title: Syringe services program
RTVlqF0.description: A harm reduction program that provides various services to people who inject drugs, including provision of sterile injection equipment, disposal of used equipment, counseling, vaccinations, infectious disease testing, and referrals for substance use disorder treatment.

QTVuqF0.title: Metabolic and alcohol-associated liver disease
QTVuqF0.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in individuals with harmful alcohol consumption. The presence of both metabolic and alcohol-related factors can accelerate the progression of liver disease compared to either condition alone, highlighting the need to address alcohol consumption in addition to metabolic factors (such as weight management and insulin resistance).

PTVWIF0.title: Destructive thyroiditis
PTVWIF0.description: A group of conditions characterized by inflammatory damage to thyroid follicles, causing a transient phase of thyrotoxicosis due to release of preformed thyroid hormone, followed by temporary or permanent hypothyroidism. Includes subacute granulomatous thyroiditis, subacute lymphocytic thyroiditis (including postpartum thyroiditis and drug-induced thyroiditis), acute suppurative thyroiditis, palpation thyroiditis, radiation thyroiditis, and Hashimoto thyroiditis.

4TV3IF0.title: Vascular ectasia
4TV3IF0.description: Abnormal dilation of the blood vessels.

lTVvIF0.title: Gender identity
lTVvIF0.description: An individual’s sense of being male, female, or another gender. May or may not correspond with their assigned gender, sex, and/or gender expression.

NTV-IF0.title: Weight-bearing
NTV-IF0.description: Supporting body weight on a limb when standing or during ambulation. Ability to bear weight may be restricted by an illness or injury or for therapeutic reasons.

MTVMrF0.title: Tibial plateau fracture
MTVMrF0.description: A break in the superior surface of the tibia, which articulates with the femoral condyles. Often intra-articular. Typically caused by high-energy force (e.g., motor vehicle collisions). Associated with neurovascular injury, including to the common peroneal nerve, popliteal artery, and anterior tibial artery.

LTVwrF0.title: Fat-fluid level
LTVwrF0.description: A sign of lipohemarthrosis on radiographic joint imaging in which fat is seen floating on synovial fluid within the joint capsule. Often a result of traumatic injury.

HTVKHF0.title: Chronic liver disease
HTVKHF0.description: A spectrum of liver diseases (e.g., hepatitis C, Wilson disease) that persist for ≥ 28 weeks (approx. 6 months). Characterized by progressive liver fibrosis and/or steatosis and deterioration of liver function.

sTVtHF0.title: Deepest vertical pocket (DVP)
sTVtHF0.description: An ultrasound measurement of amniotic fluid in the deepest single pocket of fluid with a width of at least 1 cm. Values between 2-7 cm are normal, < 2 cm indicates oligohydramnios, and ≥ 8 cm indicates polyhydramnios.

GTVBHF0.title: Hepatic fibrosis
GTVBHF0.description: The reversible proliferation of fibroblasts and accumulation of excessive extracellular matrix components (e.g., crosslinked type 1 collagen) in liver parenchyma in response to hepatic injury.

8TVOsF0.title: Sexual risk factors for mpox
8TVOsF0.description: Risk factors and high-risk sexual behaviors include being gay, bisexual, MSM, transgender, or nonbinary with any of the following in the preceding 6 months: newly diagnosed STI, > 1 sex partner, sex at a commercial sex venue, sex at a large public event or with a new partner in a region with mpox outbreak. Also at risk are sexual partners of individuals with any of these risk factors, and travelers to an outbreak area who anticipate engaging in any of the above high-risk sexual behaviors.

uTVpsF0.title: Height-adjusted total kidney volume
uTVpsF0.description: An estimation of total kidney volume, calculated based on kidney length, width, and depth on imaging studies (e.g., MRI, CT) and patient height. Used to assess for risk of rapid progression in ADPKD.

ATVRtF0.title: Sudden unexpected infant death
ATVRtF0.description: An umbrella term for any sudden, unexpected death of a child < 1 year of age. Cause of death may be unexplained (e.g., SIDS) or explained (e.g., trauma, poisoning, metabolic disorder).

_TV5tF0.title: Sudden unexplained death in children
_TV5tF0.description: The sudden, unexpected death of a child ≥ 1 year of age in which the cause of death remains unexplained after a complete postmortem examination.

zTVrtF0.title: Chronic spontaneous urticaria
zTVrtF0.description: A subtype of chronic urticaria in which symptoms appear without an identified external trigger. Stress, infections, and NSAIDs can worsen symptoms in some patients.

-TVDtF0.title: Physical urticaria provocation tests
-TVDtF0.description: A provocation test performed in a controlled clinical setting to confirm the diagnosis of physical urticaria. The test is positive if urticaria is induced after cutaneous exposure to a physical stimuli (e.g., ice cube in a plastic bag, weighted rods, hot bath).

2gVTuF0.title: YEARS algorithm
2gVTuF0.description: A diagnostic score used to assess the risk of pulmonary embolism (PE) in pregnant patients. Variables include clinical signs of deep vein thrombosis, hemoptysis, and whether PE is the most likely diagnosis.

SgVyuF0.title: PVS
SgVyuF0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Persistent vegetative state
2. Plummer-Vinson-Syndrome

RgVlEF0.title: 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria
RgVlEF0.description: A set of diagnostic criteria used to determine the diagnostic likelihood of infective endocarditis. Replaces the modified Duke criteria, which have lower sensitivity, e.g., for culture-negative infective endocarditis and atypical cases.

PgVWvF0.title: Direct intrahepatic portosystemic shunt
PgVWvF0.description: Ultrasound-guided implantation of a stent between the portal vein and the inferior vena cava to decrease portal venous pressure in patients with portal hypertension. Used when TIPS is unsuitable due to hepatic vein obstruction, e.g., in Budd-Chiari syndrome.

FgVgCF0.title: Vesicoamniotic shunting
FgVgCF0.description: A surgery to relieve a lower urinary tract obstruction in a fetus. A catheter is placed, under ultrasound guidance, from the distal end of the fetal bladder into the amniotic cavity.

8gVOCF0.title: Amniopatch
8gVOCF0.description: The infusion of platelets and cryoprecipitate into the amniotic cavity to repair a premature amniotic membrane rupture.

vgVACF0.title: Stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial
vgVACF0.description: A study design in which clusters (such as clinics, hospitals, or groups of patients) are randomly assigned to transition from usual care (control) to an intervention at staggered intervals, allowing each cluster to serve as its own control. Useful if withholding an intervention is considered unethical or if the intervention has a complex rollout.

DgV1xF0.title: Femoral intercondylar distance
DgV1xF0.description: The distance between the medial femoral condyles (knees) while the medial malleoli (ankles) are touching. Measured clinically or radiographically in the standing or supine position. Used to assess genu varum; measurements > 2 standard deviations above average for age or > 6 cm are considered pathologic.

wgVhxF0.title: Intermalleolar distance
wgVhxF0.description: The distance between the medial malleoli (ankles) while the medial femoral condyles (knees) are touching. Measured clinically or radiographically in the standing or supine position. Used to assess genu valgum; measurements > 2 standard deviations above average for age or > 8 cm are considered pathologic.

9gVNxF0.title: Tibiofemoral angle
9gVNxF0.description: The angle formed between the long axes of the femur and the tibia. Measured clinically with a goniometer or radiographically to assess for angular deformities of the knee (i.e., genu varus, genu valgum).

aSVQyF0.title: Sinecatechins
aSVQyF0.description: A topical drug derived from green tea leaves that is used to treat external anogenital warts in immunocompetent individuals. Its specific mechanism of action is unknown.

YSVnyF0.title: Stable slipped capital femoral epiphysis
YSVnyF0.description: A type of slipped capital femoral epiphysis in which the patient is able to ambulate with or without crutches.

destinations.label: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis → Clinical features

bSVHyF0.title: Unstable slipped capital femoral epiphysis
bSVHyF0.description: A type of slipped capital femoral epiphysis in which the patient is unable to ambulate, even with crutches.

destinations.label: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis → Clinical features

hSVczF0.title: Matles test
hSVczF0.description: A test to diagnose Achilles tendon rupture. The patient lies in prone position with the knees flexed to 90°. In Achilles tendon rupture, increased dorsiflexion will be visible in the affected ankle compared to the unaffected ankle.

PSVW-F0.title: Sibling violence
PSVW-F0.description: A type of domestic violence in which a child engages in physical, psychological, or sexual violence against a sibling. The perpetrator is often but not always an older sibling. The most common but least reported type of domestic violence.

kSVm-F0.title: Erythema multiforme minor
kSVm-F0.description: Erythema multiforme with cutaneous target lesions and minimal or no mucosal involvement.

NSV--F0.title: Rowell syndrome
NSV--F0.description: A rare condition characterized by erythema multiforme-like lesions, lupus erythematosus, and distinct immunologic markers, including speckled antinuclear antibody pattern, anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB antibodies, and/or rheumatoid factor.

nSV7Z80.title: Parinaud oculoglandular syndrome
nSV7Z80.description: An infectious eye condition, most commonly caused by Bartonella henselae (i.e., cat scratch disease). Manifests with unilateral follicular conjunctivitis and tender ipsilateral preauricular lymphadenopathy. Not to be confused with Parinaud syndrome.

LSVwZ80.title: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
LSVwZ80.description: A US governmental agency responsible for ensuring safe and healthy working conditions. Creates and enforces workplace safety standards and provides training, outreach, education, and assistance to employers and employees.

6SVj080.title: Deep infiltrating endometriosis
6SVj080.description: Endometriosis that infiltrates structures below the peritoneum, e.g., vaginal wall, rectouterine pouch, bowel, bladder, or ureters. Symptoms include pain with defecation, deep dyspareunia, and dysuria.

HSVKa80.title: Daily Record of Severity of Problems
HSVKa80.description: A validated measurement tool for tracking the severity of somatic and affective symptoms. May be used in the diagnosis of premenstrual dysphoric disorder. Affective and somatic symptoms are recorded daily to compare fluctuations throughout the menstrual cycle.

sSVta80.title: Nonsegmental vitiligo
sSVta80.description: The most common type of vitiligo, which is characterized by a typically bilateral and symmetric distribution, a chronic course with unpredictable periods of disease progression, and a lack of hair follicle involvement in the early phase. Depigmentation typically increases over time. Subtypes include acrofacial (mainly affecting the hands and face), generalized (widely distributed), and universal (involving most or all of the body).

GSVBa80.title: Segmental vitiligo
GSVBa80.description: A type of vitiligo characterized by a typically unilateral distribution and an initial phase of rapid spread which includes early hair follicle involvement and can last for up to 2 years. Following the initial phase, depigmented lesions usually remain stable.

FSVgY80.title: Lidocaine mouthwash
FSVgY80.description: A topical anesthetic used to prevent the gag reflex or to relieve pain in the oral or pharyngeal mucosa. Typically swished then spit out, but may be swallowed. Adverse effects include CNS and cardiovascular depression, e.g., bradycardia.

8SVOY80.title: Chondritis
8SVOY80.description: An inflammation of cartilage due to trauma (e.g., ear piercings), infection, or systemic inflammatory disease (e.g., relapsing polychondritis).

uSVpY80.title: Foreskin hygiene
uSVpY80.description: Care and cleaning of an uncircumcised penis. Includes gentle retraction of the foreskin (never forced) during urination, and rinsing under the foreskin with warm water (no soap) when bathing. After retraction, the foreskin should always be returned to its normal position, covering the glans penis.

ESV8Y80.title: Breast implant
ESV8Y80.description: A prosthetic device that consists of a silicone shell filled with silicone gel or saline. Used in breast reconstruction (e.g., after mastectomy, trauma) or for breast augmentation.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Surgical resection of tumor and breast reconstruction

DSV1b80.title: Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma
DSV1b80.description: A rare and distinct form of T-cell lymphoma that arises in the pericapsular scar tissue adjacent to breast implants, particularly textured implants. Typically manifests 7-10 years after surgery with seroma, breast pain, and/or a palpable mass. Diagnostics include imaging, aspirated fluid cytology, immunohistochemistry (CD30+), and biopsy. Management involves complete removal of the breast implant; radiotherapy and chemotherapy may be required for advanced disease.

wSVhb80.title: Breast implant-associated squamous cell carcinoma
wSVhb80.description: A rare and aggressive squamous cell carcinoma that arises in the pericapsular scar tissue adjacent to breast implants. Manifests several years after surgery with breast pain, seroma, palpable breast mass, and/or capsular contracture.

ySVdX80.title: Advanced chronic liver disease
ySVdX80.description: Suspected cirrhosis in the absence of biopsy, based on liver elastography and platelet count.

ASVRX80.title: Breast implant illness
ASVRX80.description: A poorly understood condition characterized by nonspecific systemic symptoms (e.g., fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, myalgia, arthralgia, depression, gastrointestinal issues) reported by some individuals after undergoing breast implant surgery. Symptoms may be reported weeks or years after surgery. Management focuses on a patient-centered approach, supportive care, and consideration of implant removal.

YhVnc80.title: Ovulation bleeding
YhVnc80.description: An episode of light bleeding or blood-stained discharge during the midpoint of the menstrual cycle (when ovulation occurs). May be accompanied by pain (Mittelschmerz).

bhVHc80.title: Vulvar cotton swab test
bhVHc80.description: A test used to distinguish between generalized and localized vulvodynia. A cotton swab is pressed first against the thighs, then against the labia majora and interlabial sulci, and then against the vulvar vestibule in a systematic clockwise manner, at the 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 o'clock positions. With each touch of the swab, the patient is asked to rate the level of pain.

XhV9c80.title: Arthropathy
XhV9c80.description: A general term for joint disease, including autoimmune joint inflammation (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis), degeneration (e.g., osteoarthritis), and infection (e.g., septic arthritis) and other joint disorders (e.g., due to trauma).

1hV2180.title: Polyarthritis
1hV2180.description: Swelling and/or pain that affects ≥ 5 joints. Causes include rheumatoid arthritis, hand osteoarthritis, and systemic lupus erythematosus.

WhVP180.title: Oligoarthritis
WhVP180.description: Swelling and/or pain that affects ≤ 4 joints. Causes include seronegative spondyloarthropathies, reactive arthritis, and gout.

ehVx180.title: Continuous bladder irrigation
ehVx180.description: The continuous infusion and drainage of sterile fluid into the bladder, typically used to manage gross hematuria. Procedure duration ranges from hours to days depending on clinical need.

UhVbW80.title: Avapritinib
UhVbW80.description: A tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets mutated forms of KIT and PDGFRA. It shows high selectivity with minimal effects on other kinases. FDA approved for the treatment of adults with advanced systemic mastocytosis or gastrointestinal stromal tumors.

2hVTW80.title: Erectile disorder
2hVTW80.description: A psychiatric diagnosis that is made if erectile dysfunction (characterized by difficulty developing and/or maintaining an erection, or reduced rigidity) persists for > 6 months, is not caused by substance use, medications, or another medical or mental condition, and causes clinically significant distress.

destinations.label: Sexual dysfunction and paraphilic disorders → Sexual dysfunction

ThV6W80.title: Alprostadil
ThV6W80.description: A synthetic form of prostaglandin E1 that induces vascular smooth muscle relaxation, leading to vasodilation. Used to treat erectile dysfunction or maintain a patent ductus arteriosus.

ghVFW80.title: Canakinumab
ghVFW80.description: A monoclonal antibody that targets IL-1β. Used to treat conditions such as familial Mediterranean fever and Still disease.

ShVyW80.title: HUS triad
ShVyW80.description: The characteristic features of hemolytic uremic syndrome. Comprises microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury.

hhVcd80.title: Emapalumab
hhVcd80.description: A monoclonal antibody that targets IFN-γ. Used to treat hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.

3hVSd80.title: Orthosis
3hVSd80.description: An external device to assist or restrict movement of the limbs and/or spine.

9hVNT80.title: Breast reconstruction
9hVNT80.description: A procedure to alter the appearance of breasts (e.g., after mastectomy or lumpectomy). Options include reshaping of the breast using existing breast tissue (if available), or the replacement of removed breast tissue with a prosthetic implant or tissue from other parts of the patient's body.

destinations.label: Breast cancer → Surgical resection of tumor and breast reconstruction

ChVqT80.title: Ovulation prediction test
ChVqT80.description: A point-of-care test available over the counter that measures luteinizing hormone (LH) in the urine. An LH surge 1-2 days before anticipated ovulation indicates pending ovulation.

BhVzT80.title: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine 21
BhVzT80.description: An inactivated conjugate vaccine that protects against 21 subtypes of S. pneumoniae. The minimum age for the first dose is 18 years.

yhVdg80.title: Insect bite prevention
yhVdg80.description: Measures to prevent insect bites and the spread of vector-borne diseases. Includes using insect repellent, wearing long sleeves and pants, treating clothing and gear with insecticide, installing insect screens, and using bed nets.

a3VQS80.title: Multifetal reduction
a3VQS80.description: Reduction of the number of fetuses in a multiple gestation pregnancy (usually triplet or above). Performed to improve pregnancy outcomes for the birthing parent and remaining fetus or fetuses. Typically performed in the first trimester.

13V2h80.title: Superficial dyspareunia
13V2h80.description: A type of dyspareunia characterized by pain on vaginal entry.

W3VPh80.title: Deep dyspareunia
W3VPh80.description: A type of dyspareunia characterized by pain (e.g., pelvic pain) with deep penetration or thrusting.

d3Voh80.title: Theca cells
d3Voh80.description: Cells that surround the granulosa cells in the ovarian follicles. The theca interna contains cells for androstenedione synthesis, while the theca externa functions as a layer of connective tissue.

V3VGh80.title: Potassium-competitive acid blockers
V3VGh80.description: A group of drugs that decrease stomach acid production by competitively inhibiting H+/K+ ATPase. Examples include vonoprazan, soraprazan, and revaprazan.

e3Vxh80.title: Tirzepatide
e3Vxh80.description: A dual glucose-dependent GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus, overweight, and obesity. Effects include improved glycemic control and appetite suppression.

U3Vb380.title: Potentially allergenic foods
U3Vb380.description: The nine most common food allergens are peanuts (most common allergen), soybeans, tree nuts, cow's milk, chicken eggs, fish, shellfish, wheat, and sesame.

R3VlR80.title: Food intolerance
R3VlR80.description: An adverse reaction to food without an immunologic cause. Includes lactose intolerance and fructose intolerance. Symptoms include abdominal discomfort.

i3VJR80.title: Gamete donation
i3VJR80.description: A form of assisted reproductive technology using donor oocytes or sperm. Indications include previous failed assisted reproduction with significant sperm abnormalities or diminished ovarian reserve, non-heterosexual partnerships, and significant genetic defects.

j3V_R80.title: Red flags in nipple discharge
j3V_R80.description: Any of the following features in a patient with nipple discharge should raise suspicion for an underlying malignancy: unilateral, uniductal, persistent, spontaneous nipple discharge that is clear, bloody, or serosanguineous; breast mass; and risk factors for breast cancer.

53ViQ80.title: IND
53ViQ80.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to: 
1. Investigational New Drug
2. Intestinal neuronal dysplasia

63Vjj80.title: Neonatal uterine bleeding
63Vjj80.description: A benign, self-limited vaginal bleeding that occurs in up to 5% of female neonates. Caused by withdrawal of maternal estrogen after birth. Typically occurs within 2 weeks after birth and requires no treatment.

73V4P80.title: Mesenchyme
73V4P80.description: The embryonic tissue that gives rise to most connective tissue (e.g., muscles, nerves, bone, and cartilage).

v3VA480.title: Pediatric advanced life support
v3VA480.description: A structured approach to the evaluation and care of critically ill infants and children. Includes guidance on respiratory distress, cardiac arrest, shock, arrhythmias, and postresuscitation care.

D3V1k80.title: Flow-inflating bag
D3V1k80.description: A bag that only inflates when compressed gas is flowing into the bag and the outflow is restricted. Used to provide positive pressure ventilation or continuous positive airway pressure

w3Vhk80.title: Pudendal neuralgia
w3Vhk80.description: A neuropathy involving the pudendal nerve. Typically manifests with unilateral burning vulvar pain and paresthesias and pain that worsens when sitting. Additional features may include dyspareunia, urinary frequency, and urinary urgency.

93VNk80.title: Self-inflating bag
93VNk80.description: A semirigid bag that reinflates automatically, without the need for pressured gas. Used to provide positive-pressure ventilation through a mask or advanced airway device.

ZRVZl80.title: Suction event
ZRVZl80.description: Obstruction of the left ventricular assist device (LVAD) inflow cannula by the left ventricular wall due to reduced left ventricular filling and increased negative pressure. May manifest with hypotension due to low LVAD flow and arrhythmias due to myocardial irritation.

aRVQl80.title: VAD coordinator
aRVQl80.description: A specialized healthcare professional (often a nurse) who manages and supports patients with ventricular assist devices before and after implantation, trains patients and healthcare staff on device use and troubleshooting, and coordinates care with a multidisciplinary team to ensure optimal outcomes.

XRV9l80.title: Fertility threatening
XRV9l80.description: Any condition, treatment, or situation that may temporarily or permanently impair an individual's ability to contribute to conception or achieve a successful pregnancy. Includes medical conditions (e.g., cancer, severe endometriosis, testicular injury), surgical interventions (e.g., oophorectomy, orchiectomy), and treatments (e.g., chemotherapy, radiation) that directly or indirectly affect reproductive organs or function in male or female individuals.

VRVGN80.title: Severity of polyhydramnios
VRVGN80.description: The classification of polyhydramnios based on deepest vertical pocket (DVP) or amniotic fluid index (AFI) measurement on obstetric ultrasound. May be mild (AFI 24–29.9 cm or DVP 8–11 cm), moderate (AFI 30–35 cm or DVP 12–15 cm), or severe (AFI > 35 cm or DVP ≥ 16 cm). The likelihood of an underlying fetal abnormality increases with disease severity.

LRVwn80.title: Anatidophobia
LRVwn80.description: A fictional phobia in which an individual has an irrational fear that somewhere, somehow, a duck or goose is watching them.

media.title: The duck who is watching you

8RVOK80.title: FADIR test
8RVOK80.description: A physical examination maneuver to evaluate for impingement of the hip joint. With the patient in the supine position, the examiner Flexes the hip to 90 degrees, then ADducts and Internally Rotates the hip (FADIR). The test is positive if there is pain in the anterior hip or groin.

vRVAK80.title: Male hypogonadism
vRVAK80.description: A condition caused by reduced function of the testes, leading to decreased testosterone production. Caused by disorders or abnormalities affecting the testes (primary male hypogonadism) or disorders of the hypothalamus and/or pituitary gland (secondary male hypogonadism).

DRV1680.title: Complicated vulvovaginal candidiasis
DRV1680.description: A vaginal candidal infection with ≥ 1 of the following: ≥ 3 episodes of vulvovaginal candidiasis within 1 year, severe symptoms, causative organism other than C. albicans, known immune deficiency or diabetes mellitus.

zRVrp80.title: NSAID hypersensitivity
zRVrp80.description: A range of adverse reactions triggered by NSAIDs. May be pseudoallergic (e.g., aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease) or immunologic allergic (e.g., single NSAID-induced urticaria/angioedema or anaphylaxis).

ZiVZJ80.title: Postpill amenorrhea
ZiVZJ80.description: Amenorrhea for 2–3 months after stopping oral contraceptives. Due to temporary disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis.

aiVQJ80.title: High-tone pelvic floor dysfunction
aiVQJ80.description: A condition characterized by tight pelvic floor muscles that are unable to relax. Can affect urination and bowel movements and can cause pelvic pain and sexual dysfunction.

hiVcr80.title: Eosinophilic lung diseases
hiVcr80.description: An umbrella term for pulmonary conditions with pulmonary and/or peripheral eosinophilia, including eosinophilic pneumonia, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

3iVSr80.title: Eosinophilic pneumonia
3iVSr80.description: A type of eosinophilic lung disease characterized by significant infiltration of eosinophils in the alveoli and pulmonary interstitium. Peripheral eosinophilia may be present. Includes acute idiopathic eosinophilic pneumonia and chronic idiopathic eosinophilic pneumonia.

RiVlr80.title: Acute idiopathic eosinophilic pneumonia
RiVlr80.description: A form of eosinophilic pneumonia characterized by sudden onset and rapid progression of an acute febrile illness, typically in previously healthy individuals. Symptoms include a nonproductive cough and dyspnea. May lead to hypoxemic respiratory failure.

destinations.label: Eosinophilic lung diseases → Acute idiopathic eosinophilic pneumonia

iiVJr80.title: Chronic eosinophilic pneumonia
iiVJr80.description: A form of eosinophilic pneumonia characterized by subacute respiratory symptoms, often in middle-aged individuals with a history of asthma or atopy. Symptoms include cough, dyspnea, and low-grade fever.

destinations.label: Eosinophilic lung diseases → Chronic eosinophilic pneumonia

QiVur80.title: Multidisciplinary sarcoma team
QiVur80.description: A group of health care professionals that provides care for patients with bone and/or soft tissue sarcomas. Includes a radiologist, sarcoma specialist surgeon, pathologist, and oncologist.

OiVI780.title: Apparent life-threatening event
OiVI780.description: An episode of apnea, color or muscle tone change, choking, and/or gagging that is frightening to the observer. This is a historical term that is no longer recommended by the American Academy of Pediatrics.

5iViH80.title: Uterine sliding sign
5iViH80.description: A transvaginal ultrasound test that uses gentle pressure to assess for deep infiltrating endometriosis affecting the rectum and/or sigmoid colon. In a healthy individual, the anterior rectum and sigmoid colon glides freely over the cervix and upper vagina. If the rectosigmoid pouch has been obliterated by endometrial lesions, the tissue does not slide freely and bowel involvement is likely.

niV7H80.title: Vibegron
niV7H80.description: A selective beta-3 agonist used in the treatment of overactive bladder, including urgency urinary incontinence. Stimulates beta-3 adrenergic receptors of the detrusor smooth muscle, relaxing the muscle and increasing bladder capacity for urine.

destinations.label: Overactive bladder and urgency urinary incontinence → Treatment

GiVBG80.title: Anal sphincteroplasty
GiVBG80.description: The surgical reconstruction of the external and/or internal anal sphincters. Common indications are obstetric injury, traumatic injury, or injury during surgical procedures.

viVAt80.title: Corporal blood gas analysis
viVAt80.description: A laboratory test of blood obtained from the corpus cavernosum. Measures pH and the partial pressures of oxygen (pO₂) and carbon dioxide (pCO₂). Used to differentiate ischemic priapism from nonischemic priapism.

wiVhF80.title: Early-onset fetal growth restriction
wiVhF80.description: The onset of fetal growth restriction before 32 weeks' gestation. Compared to late-onset fetal growth restriction, early-onset fetal growth restriction is more likely to be severe, progressive, and associated with fetal genetic abnormalities and/or preeclampsia.

9iVNF80.title: Late-onset fetal growth restriction
9iVNF80.description: The onset of fetal growth restriction at or after 32 weeks' gestation. Restriction is usually milder than in early-onset fetal growth restriction.

cQVaE80.title: Ovarian reserve
cQVaE80.description: The number of oocytes in an individual's ovaries. Indicates reproductive potential. Diminished reserves are often detected by suboptimal response to ovarian stimulation.

2QVTv80.title: Carcinoid crisis
2QVTv80.description: A potentially life-threatening efflux of vasoactive substances (predominantly serotonin) from a neuroendocrine tumor, typically triggered by perioperative tumor manipulation and/or general anesthesia. Characterized by severe and/or refractory symptoms of carcinoid syndrome, labile blood pressure, and multi-organ failure.

TQV6v80.title: AML-defining genetic abnormalities
TQV6v80.description: Somatic mutations, fusions, or rearrangements involving PML::RARA, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11, DEK::NUP214, RBM15::MRTFA, KMT2A, MECOM, NUP98, and NPM1. The presence of any of these genetic abnormalities allows for the diagnosis of AML regardless of the blast count on bone marrow aspiration.

gQVFv80.title: PML::RARA
gQVFv80.description: A fusion gene formed by a balanced translocation of the RARA (retinoic acid receptor alpha) gene located on chromosome 17 and the PML (promyelocytic leukemia) gene on chromosome 15. Involved in the pathogenesis of acute promyelocytic leukemia.

SQVyv80.title: MYC
SQVyv80.description: A family of proto-oncogenes that encode transcription factors regulating cell proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis. All MYC proto-oncogenes are structurally similar but have distinct roles and associations with different types of cancers (e.g., L-MYC in lung cancer, N-MYC in neuroblastoma).

PQVWw80.title: Duplication cyst
PQVWw80.description: A rare congenital cystic abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract.

4QV3w80.title: Schwannoma
4QV3w80.description: A rare, benign tumor that arises from the Schwann cells around cranial or peripheral nerves.

mQVV980.title: Terrible triad of the elbow
mQVV980.description: An elbow injury characterized by a combination of radial head fracture, coronoid process fracture, and medial collateral ligament disruption. Causes significant joint instability and typically requires surgery.

5QVi980.title: Single-digit transvaginal examination
5QVi980.description: A test typically used in the evaluation of women with dyspareunia. A single lubricated finger is inserted into the vaginal introitus, and slowly rotated 360° clockwise while assessing for uncontrolled contractions of the pelvic floor muscles and tenderness of the urethra and/or base of bladder.

pQVLC80.title: Dextroscoliosis
pQVLC80.description: A type of scoliosis characterized by a right-sided convex curvature. Typically occurs in the thoracic spine.

JQVsC80.title: Levoscoliosis
JQVsC80.description: A type of scoliosis characterized by a left-sided convex curvature. Typically occurs in the lumbar spine.

IQVYx80.title: Disruptive behaviors in childhood
IQVYx80.description: Emotional dysregulation, aggression, and other behaviors that occur in disruptive and mood disorders that are diagnosed in childhood (e.g., conduct disorder, oppositional defiant disorder).

HQVKx80.title: Medullary thyroid cancer
HQVKx80.description: A poorly differentiated malignant neoplasm of the parafollicular C cells of the thyroid gland that often arises sporadically but may sometimes be associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN2).

sQVtx80.title: CVS
sQVtx80.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to: 
1. Chorionic villus sampling
2. Cyclical vomiting syndrome

9QVNy80.title: Proliferative phase
9QVNy80.description:
A term used to describe
1. a phase of wound healing.
2. a phase of the menstrual cycle.

xQVEy80.title: Premenstrual affective symptoms
xQVEy80.description: The mood-related changes that occur in PMS and PMDD. May include the following: mood swings or emotional lability; irritability, anger, or increased conflicts; depressed mood; anxiety, tension, and/or feeling on edge.

BQVzy80.title: Premenstrual somatic symptoms
BQVzy80.description: The physical changes that occur in PMS and PMDD. May include the following: joint pain, muscle pain, breast tenderness, or fluid retention (e.g., bloating, weight gain, swelling of the extremities); overeating or food cravings; decreased interest in usual activities; difficulty concentrating; lethargy or lack of energy; hypersomnia or insomnia; feeling overwhelmed or out of control.

-QVDA80.title: Novel influenza A virus
-QVDA80.description: Antigenically and genetically new viruses that primarily originate in birds or pigs. Rarely, they can infect humans with the potential to cause a pandemic.

TjV6-80.title: Hysteropexy
TjV6-80.description: A surgical procedure used in the treatment of uterine prolapse. The cervix is attached to a supporting ligament or structure using sutures or mesh in order to suspend the uterus. Can be performed vaginally, abdominally, or laparoscopically.

OjVI0u0.title: Primary male hypogonadism
OjVI0u0.description: Hypogonadism due to disorders or abnormalities affecting the testes. Characterized by elevated gonadotropin (LH and FSH) levels. Causes include testicular radiation, chemotherapy, testicular trauma, and Klinefelter syndrome.

ljVv0u0.title: Secondary male hypogonadism
ljVv0u0.description: Hypogonadism due to disorders of the hypothalamus and/or pituitary gland (e.g., tumors, infiltrative diseases, head trauma, congenital conditions such as Kallmann syndrome). Characterized by gonadotropin deficiency (due to decreased secretion of GnRH or LH/FSH).

NjV-0u0.title: Organic male hypogonadism
NjV-0u0.description: Hypogonadism due to often irreversible hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis pathology. May be primary (hypergonadotropic) or secondary (hypogonadotropic). Causes include orchitis (e.g., due to mumps virus infection), chemotherapy, Klinefelter syndrome, and damage to the pituitary gland (e.g., due to tumors or infiltrative diseases).

mjVVau0.title: Functional male hypogonadism
mjVVau0.description: Hypogonadism due to often reversible suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis. May be primary (hypergonadotropic) or secondary (hypogonadotropic). Causes include obesity, medications, excessive exercise, and critical systemic illness.

5jViau0.title: Mixed male hypogonadism
5jViau0.description: Hypogonadism resulting from both disorders of the testes (primary) and the hypothalamus and/or pituitary gland (secondary). Causes include heavy alcohol use, chronic diseases (e.g., chronic kidney disease), and congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

MjVMau0.title: Clinical features of male hypogonadism
MjVMau0.description: Features in prepubertal onset include microphallus, eunuchoidal proportions, and cryptorchidism. Features in postpubertal onset include loss of morning erections, low energy, and hot flashes.

njV7au0.title: ETV6-RUNX1
njV7au0.description: A fusion gene resulting from translocation (12;21), which is the most common translocation in childhood B-ALL. Encodes a chimeric transcription factor affecting hematopoietic cell proliferation and differentiation. Associated with a favorable prognosis.

KjVUYu0.title: Therapeutic drug monitoring
KjVUYu0.description: Measuring and monitoring drug levels in the blood to ensure optimization of drug regimens and maintenance of appropriate levels of medication.

qjVCYu0.title: Microphallus
qjVCYu0.description: A penis with a stretched penile length less than 2.5 standard deviation scores below average for the individual's age and ethnicity.

GjVBbu0.title: Scapholunate dissociation
GjVBbu0.description: A form of carpal injury characterized by disruption of the scapholunate and radioscaphocapitate ligaments, typically caused by hyperextension (e.g., fall on an outstretched hand). Corresponds to stage I of the Mayfield classification of perilunate ligament injuries. May lead to carpal instability. Imaging shows widening of the scapholunate joint.

tjVXXu0.title: Extreme delta brush
tjVXXu0.description: A unique electroencephalography (EEG) pattern in patients with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis. Resembles EEG waveforms seen in premature infants.

vjVAXu0.title: Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification system
vjVAXu0.description: A method used to describe the degree and location of pelvic organ prolapse. While the patient is maximally straining, measurements are taken from the hymen to 9 defined points on the vagina, perineal body, and external urethral meatus. The total length of the vagina is also measured at rest.

VPVGdu0.title: Tinea unguium
VPVGdu0.description: A dermatophyte infection of the nail and is the most common cause of onychomycosis. Clinicial features include nail thickening, discoloration, and separation from the nail bed.

media.title: Tinea unguium (onychomycosis) of both big toe nails

ePVxdu0.title: Tolnaftate
ePVxdu0.description: A thiocarbamate antifungal that is used topically in the treatment of dermatophyte infections (e.g., tinea corporis, tinea cruris, tinea pedis).

jPV_eu0.title: Ludington sign
jPV_eu0.description: A visible difference in muscle contour when the patient places both arms behind the head and contracts the biceps. In the affected arm, the muscle belly of the biceps moves distally upon contraction. Indicates proximal biceps tendon rupture.

PPVWUu0.title: Tenotomy
PPVWUu0.description: The surgical release or cutting of a tendon to treat conditions involving tendon tightness, contracture, or dysfunction (e.g., biceps tendinopathy, torticollis).

4PV3Uu0.title: Tenodesis
4PV3Uu0.description: The surgical reattachment of a tendon, either at its original anatomical position or at an alternative bony or soft-tissue site. Commonly used to treat conditions such as biceps tendon rupture and rotator cuff tears.

kPVmUu0.title: Pelvic floor physical therapy
kPVmUu0.description: Techniques to strengthen, relax, and/or improve coordination of the pelvic floor muscles in patients with pelvic floor dysfunction. Includes Kegel exercises, manual therapy (usually performed by a physical therapist), electrical stimulation, biofeedback, and weighted vaginal cones.

lPVvUu0.title: PEEP valve
lPVvUu0.description: An attachment on a self-inflating resuscitation bag that maintains positive end-expiratory pressure by restricting flow during exhalation.

mPVV2u0.title: Diverting ostomy
mPVV2u0.description: A surgical procedure in which a stoma is created in the abdominal wall to reroute stool or urine from a diseased or compromised portion of the bowel or urinary tract into an external bag. Used to relieve pressure, promote healing, and restore function in obstruction or impairment. Includes colostomy (diverting stool from the colon), ileostomy (diverting stool from the ileum), and ileal conduit (diverting urine using a portion of the ileum). Used in the management of conditions such as bowel obstruction, inflammatory bowel disease, and urinary tract dysfunction. Can be temporary or permanent depending on the underlying medical cause.

IPVYTu0.title: Mitotic rate
IPVYTu0.description: A measure of cell division based on mitotic activity. May be measured as a percentage of cells entering mitosis per hour (mitotic rate), as the ratio of cells undergoing mitosis in a given population, e.g., per 1000 cells (mitotic index), or as the number of mitoses in a given area, e.g., per mm² (mitotic count).

rPVfTu0.title: Ovarian carcinoid
rPVfTu0.description: A type of neuroendocrine tumor of the female genital tract. Ovarian carcinoid is rare and generally low-grade. It includes four histological subtypes: insular, trabecular, strumal, and mucinous.

GPVBTu0.title: Risk factors for DDH
GPVBTu0.description: Risk factors that require screening imaging include a positive family history (e.g., in a first-degree relative), breech presentation, a history of tight swaddling of the lower extremities, and a history of prior instability that has resolved.

destinations.label: Developmental dysplasia of the hip → Etiology

tPVXgu0.title: 5-Hydroxytryptophan
tPVXgu0.description: An amino acid precursor of serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine).

FPVggu0.title: Acrosclerosis
FPVggu0.description: The fibrotic thickening and tightening of the skin on the face, distal upper extremities (up to the elbows), and/or distal lower extremities (up to the knees). Results in a waxy appearance, limited range of motion, and deformity of the involved structures. Occurs in systemic sclerosis and mixed connective tissue disease.

8PVOgu0.title: SpO2/FiO2 ratio
8PVOgu0.description: The ratio of peripheral oxygen saturation on pulse oximetry (SpO2) to the fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2). Commonly used as a clinical indicator for hypoxemia and correlates with the PaO2/FiO2 ratio. A value of approx. 500 is considered normal.

EPV8gu0.title: Acquired tracheoesophageal fistula
EPV8gu0.description: An abnormal connection between the trachea and esophagus caused by another condition (e.g., malignancy, trauma). Typically manifests with dysphagia, dyspnea, and/or recurrent lung infections.

BPVzSu0.title: Soft tissue sarcoma
BPVzSu0.description: A rare malignant tumor of connective tissue (e.g., fat and muscle) that most commonly manifests as a palpable mass in the extremities but can develop in any body site. The most common histological subtypes are liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma.

yPVdhu0.title: Chorionicity
yPVdhu0.description: The type of placentation in multifetal gestations. In multichorionic pregnancies (e.g., dichorionic in twin pregnancies, trichorionic in triplet pregnancies), each fetus has an individual placenta; in monochorionic pregnancies, all fetuses share one placenta. Does not reflect zygosity (e.g., monozygotic twins may be monochorionic or dichorionic).

APVRhu0.title: Zygosity
APVRhu0.description: The genetic classification of embryos in a multifetal gestation. A single fertilized ovum (monozygotic) results in genetically identical siblings; multiple fertilized ova (dizygotic, trizygotic, etc.) result in genetically distinct siblings.

d4VoRu0.title: Cerebellar tremor
d4VoRu0.description: Tremor associated with cerebellar lesions (e.g., cerebellar trauma, cerebellar tumors, cerebellitis). Often manifests as intention tremor but can also manifest as postural and/or kinetic tremor.

U4Vbiu0.title: Slipping rib syndrome
U4Vbiu0.description: Nontraumatic chest wall pain due to hypermobility of one or more of ribs 8–10 with subluxation and intercostal nerve irritation.

24VTiu0.title: One-step oral glucose tolerance test
24VTiu0.description: A screening test for diabetes. Blood glucose is measured after fasting and 2 hours after the consumption of 75 g of glucose. If assessing for gestational diabetes, blood glucose is also measured 1 hour after the consumption of glucose.

T4V6iu0.title: Home glucose monitoring
T4V6iu0.description: A method of recording blood glucose levels performed by the patient. Options include fingerstick glucose testing at set intervals (e.g., first thing in the morning, before and after meals) and continuous blood glucose monitoring via a subcutaneous device.

Q4VuQu0.title: Drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol
Q4VuQu0.description: A combined oral contraceptive containing ethinyl estradiol and drospirenone. It is the only combined oral contraceptive approved for the management of premenstrual dysphoric disorder symptoms in menstruating individuals who desire contraception.

54ViPu0.title: Penile block
54ViPu0.description: A form of regional anesthesia of the penis that uses a local anesthetic agent without epinephrine. A dorsal block involves anesthetic infiltration in two positions at the dorsal base of the penis. A ring block involves anesthetic infiltration circumferentially around the base of the penis.

I4VYku0.title: Amnionicity
I4VYku0.description: The number of amniotic sacs in multifetal gestations. In monoamniotic pregnancies, all fetuses share one amniotic sac. In multiamniotic pregnancies, each fetus has a separate amniotic sac

94VNlu0.title: Suzetrigine
94VNlu0.description: A sodium channel blocker used to treat moderate to severe acute pain in adults.

y4VdNu0.title: Abduction relief sign
y4VdNu0.description: A clinical sign of cervical radiculopathy in which abduction of the ipsilateral arm, such as placing it on the head, improves the symptom.

-4VDNu0.title: Recurrent ischemic (stuttering) priapism
-4VDNu0.description: A subtype of ischemic priapism characterized by repeated painful erections interspersed with periods of detumescence. Most commonly occurs in individuals with sickle cell disease.

akVQmu0.title: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
akVQmu0.description: Spontaneous separation in a coronary artery wall due to intramural hemorrhage that is not associated with atherosclerosis, trauma, or medical intervention (e.g., PCI). Can cause acute myocardial infarction, especially in younger women, due to compression of the artery lumen by the intramural hematoma or a dissection flap (i.e., a section of tunica intima that tears away from the tunica media).

destinations.label: Myocardial infarction → Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD)

bkVHmu0.title: Endometrial intraepithelial carcinoma
bkVHmu0.description: Precursor for papillary serous uterine cancer. Should not be confused with endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia, which is a precursor for endometrial cancer.

QkVunu0.title: Portal venous gas
QkVunu0.description: A radiological finding that indicates intravascular gas within the hepatic portal venous system. Associated with increased severity and mortality in bowel ischemia.

LkVwou0.title: Steroidogenic antibodies
LkVwou0.description: A group of antibodies directed against the steroidogenic enzymes cholesterol desmolase, 17α-hydroxylase, and 21β-hydroxylase, which are involved in steroid biosynthesis. Seen in individuals with autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency, autoimmune polyglandular disease, and autoimmune premature ovarian failure associated with primary adrenal insufficiency.

JkVsKu0.title: Endometrial sampling
JkVsKu0.description: A diagnostic procedure in which endometrial tissue is obtained for histopathologic evaluation. May be performed using endometrial biopsy or dilation and curettage, with or without hysteroscopic guidance. The technique used depends on clinical indications, patient factors, operator expertise, and the need for targeted vs. blind tissue collection.

qkVCKu0.title: Long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation
qkVCKu0.description: The presence of atrial fibrillation for > 1 year.

8kVOpu0.title: Terminal ileum
8kVOpu0.description: The most distal portion of the small intestine, which is the absorption site for vitamin B12 and bile acids. Separated from the large intestine via the ileocecal valve and characterized by the presence of Peyer patches. Commonly affected in Crohn disease.

ukVppu0.title: Ileocecal resection
ukVppu0.description: Surgical removal of the terminal ileum, cecum, and possibly the appendix. Indicated for Crohn disease complicated by strictures, fistulas, and/or abscesses. May lead to malabsorption of bile acids and vitamin B12, increasing the risk of diarrhea and complications due to deficiency.

EkV8pu0.title: Surrogacy
EkV8pu0.description: A form of family-building in which an individual becomes pregnant with, carries, and delivers a child for someone else who will parent the child. In gestational surrogacy, pregnancy is achieved through assisted reproductive technology, and the surrogate is genetically unrelated to the child. In traditional surrogacy, pregnancy is achieved using the surrogate's oocytes, with or without assisted reproductive technology, and the surrogate is genetically related to the child.

vkVApu0.title: Osteoradionecrosis
vkVApu0.description: Bone damage caused by ionizing radiation that can develop months to years after exposure. Most commonly occurs in the jaw after radiotherapy for head and neck cancer. Diagnosed by visible bone on oral examination or lytic lesions on imaging.

wkVhJu0.title: Sacral neuromodulation
wkVhJu0.description: A minimally invasive therapy in which a neurostimulator is implanted near the sacrum to deliver electrical impulses to the sacral nerves. Used to manage lower urinary tract and bowel dysfunction, including incontinence.

9kVNJu0.title: Posterior tibial nerve stimulation
9kVNJu0.description: A treatment for overactive bladder in which retrograde electrical activation of the posterior tibial nerve modulates the sacral nerve plexus, influencing the neural pathways that innervate the lower urinary tract. Stimulation can be percutaneous, transcutaneous, or via an implantable device.

AkVRqu0.title: 2012 EULAR/ACR classification criteria for polymyalgia rheumatica
AkVRqu0.description: Classification criteria intended for use as a research tool to identify patients with polymyalgia rheumatica.

media.title: 2012 EULAR/ACR classification criteria for polymyalgia rheumatica

ZOVZIu0.title: Ischemia with nonobstructive coronary arteries
ZOVZIu0.description: A type of chronic coronary disease characterized by myocardial ischemia without the obstruction of coronary arteries. Includes vasospastic angina and microvascular angina.

WOVPru0.title: Incontinence products
WOVPru0.description: Products used to increase comfort and reduce dermatological complications for patients with urinary and fecal incontinence. Includes pads or diapers, barrier creams, and external catheters.

SOVy7u0.title: Tracheoesophageal fistula
SOVy7u0.description: An abnormal connection between the trachea and esophagus. May be congenital or acquired (e.g., caused by malignancy or trauma.

iOVJHu0.title: Onychomadesis
iOVJHu0.description: Spontaneous separation of the nail plate from the proximal nail bed due to temporary arrest in nail growth. May lead to complete or partial shedding of the nail. Often triggered by systemic illnesses, trauma, or drug reactions.

jOV_Hu0.title: Stroke center
