jOV_Hu0.description: A health facility that provides specialized care to patients with stroke. Four levels designated by The Joint Commission classify centers according to the breadth and level of advanced care they provide, the availability of specialists, and the degree of their community and academic involvement.

4OV3su0.title: Pentosan polysulfate
4OV3su0.description: A heparin analog used in the treatment of interstitial cystitis.

mOVVGu0.title: Parvovirus B19 infections
mOVVGu0.description: A variety of clinical presentations caused by infection with parvovirus B19. Most commonly manifests as erythema infectiosum but may also cause arthritis, papular-purpuric gloves-and-socks syndrome, severe anemia, or transient aplastic crisis.

oOV0tu0.title: Coronary artery dissection
oOV0tu0.description: Separation in a coronary artery wall due to intramural hemorrhage. Can cause myocardial infarction due to compression of the artery lumen. Most commonly occurs spontaneously, but can also be traumatic (e.g., from blunt chest trauma) or iatrogenic (e.g., as a complication of PCI).

KOVUtu0.title: Inspiratory stridor
KOVUtu0.description: A pathological high-pitched breath sound produced by inspiration. Typically caused by partial obstruction of the extrathoracic airway, most commonly at or above the glottis.

media.title: Barking cough, inspiratory stridor und chest retractions in viral croup | External video

6OVjtu0.title: Tokophobia
6OVjtu0.description: An extreme fear or phobia of pregnancy and/or childbirth. May result in avoidance of pregnancy or preference for elective cesarean delivery.

pOVLtu0.title: Expiratory stridor
pOVLtu0.description: A pathological high-pitched breath sound produced by expiration. Typically caused by partial obstruction of the intrathoracic airway (e.g., trachea or bronchus).

JOVstu0.title: Gastrointestinal PCR panel
JOVstu0.description: A polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay that detects nucleic acids of specific bacteria, viruses, and toxins in stool samples. Used to identify Campylobacter, Shigella, Salmonella, Escherichia coli, Norovirus, Rotavirus, and other common gastrointestinal infections. Results should be interpreted with caution, as a positive result may indicate an asymptomatic or recently resolved infection.

rOVfFu0.title: Ovarian tumor marker
rOVfFu0.description: Substances secreted by cells in the ovaries that can help in the diagnosis and monitoring of ovarian tumors, although they are nonspecific. Markers include CA 125 for epithelial tumors (human epididymis protein 4 or HE4 may be used with CA 125 for better specificity); AFP, β-hCG, and LDH for germ cell tumors; and inhibin for granulosa cell tumors.

7OV4Fu0.title: Adnexal mass
7OV4Fu0.description: An abnormal growth or lesion in the ovary, fallopian tube, or surrounding tissues. Causes can be benign (e.g., functional ovarian cyst, endometrioma) or malignant (e.g., primary ovarian cancer).

DOV1uu0.title: Distal airway
DOV1uu0.description: The section of the airway encompassing the eighth-generation bronchioles through to the alveoli. Noncartilaginous and typically has an internal diameter of < 2 mm in adults.

wOVhuu0.title: Central airway
wOVhuu0.description: The proximal portion of the lower airway, typically encompassing the trachea and mainstem bronchi.

9OVNuu0.title: Laryngeal fracture
9OVNuu0.description: A fracture of the thyroid cartilage and/or the cricoid cartilage. Typically caused by blunt neck trauma. Symptoms include neck pain, hoarseness, dysphagia, and dyspnea. Can lead to rapidly progressing airway obstruction.

ZlVZvu0.title: Suspected complement-mediated HUS
ZlVZvu0.description: HUS that occurs in individuals with any of the following: atypical age for Shiga toxin-associated HUS (i.e., < 6 months or > 5 years), Shiga toxin-negative diarrhea, no diarrhea, recurrent HUS, insidious onset, and/or family history of HUS.

clVaDu0.title: Low-tone pelvic floor dysfunction
clVaDu0.description: A condition characterized by weak pelvic floor muscles. Can cause urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse.

RlVl9u0.title: Rapid response team
RlVl9u0.description: A multidisciplinary group of health care professionals who provide immediate assistance when an acutely ill patient is experiencing rapid clinical deterioration.

QlVu9u0.title: Mayfield classification
QlVu9u0.description: A classification system used to describe the sequence of carpal ligament injuries in perilunate dislocation leading to perilunate instability, from scapholunate dissociation (stage I) to lunate dislocation (stage IV).

jlV_9u0.title: Midcarpal dislocation
jlV_9u0.description: A form of carpal injury characterized by disruption of the lunocapitate, lunotriquetral, and scaphotriquetral ligaments. Typically caused by hyperextension (e.g., fall on an outstretched hand). Corresponds to stage III of the Mayfield classification of perilunate ligament injuries. May lead to carpal instability. Imaging shows widening of the scapholunate joint.

KlVUBu0.title: Neuroendocrine neoplasm
KlVUBu0.description: A tumor derived from neuroendocrine cells. Classified as neuroendocrine tumors (e.g., insulinoma), neuroendocrine carcinomas (e.g., small cell lung cancer), or paragangliomas (e.g., pheochromocytoma).

JlVsBu0.title: PAPA
JlVsBu0.description: An autosomal dominant autoinflammatory syndrome that manifests with pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne, rarely simultaneously. Onset is often in early childhood.

qlVCBu0.title: PASH
qlVCBu0.description: An autoinflammatory syndrome that manifests with pyoderma gangrenosum, acne, and suppurative hidradenitis. Onset is typically in puberty.

GlVByu0.title: Rectal irrigation
GlVByu0.description: The introduction of saline into the rectum via a rectal tube or catheter to facilitate bowel emptying. Primarily used for managing fecal retention, neurogenic bowel dysfunction, or chronic constipation. May also be indicated in conditions such as Hirschsprung disease, spinal cord injury, or severe functional constipation.

ulVpAu0.title: Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale
ulVpAu0.description: A validated scoring system for the screening and diagnosis of catatonia.

ElV8Au0.title: Mannerism (psychiatry)
ElV8Au0.description: An odd imitation of normal actions (e.g., theatrical speech and/or posturing). May be a symptom of catatonia.

ylVdzu0.title: Eczema coxsakium
ylVdzu0.description: An atypical manifestation of hand, foot, and mouth disease that is characterized by accentuated eruptions in areas of active or inactive atopic dermatitis (eczema).

destinations.label: Coxsackievirus infections → Hand, foot, and mouth disease and herpangina

-lVDzu0.title: Botulism antitoxin
-lVDzu0.description: An equine-derived antitoxin that contains antibodies to all seven types of botulinum neurotoxins. Stops progression of paralysis by neutralizing free toxin in the blood serum. Cannot reverse existing paralysis as it does not neutralize toxins already bound to the synaptic receptor. Used to treat noninfant botulism.

YNVn-u0.title: Overweight and obesity
YNVn-u0.description: Conditions of excess total body fat, typically diagnosed based on BMI and/or waist circumference. Associated with an increased risk of developing weight-related complications.

bNVH-u0.title: Stereotypy
bNVH-u0.description: The persistent repetition of sounds, words, movements, or gestures. Often a feature of autism spectrum disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, or schizophrenia.

fNVk0E0.title: Acrodynia
fNVk0E0.description: A rare syndrome caused by chronic mercury poisoning that manifests with erythema, edema, and hyperkeratosis of the palms, soles, and face. Other clinical features include hyperhidrosis, tachycardia, irritability, tremors, and paresthesias.

TNV60E0.title: EBV nuclear antigen antibodies
TNV60E0.description: Antibodies against Epstein Barr virus (EBV) nuclear antigen. Detectable ≥ 6 weeks after symptom onset and may persist for life.

PNVWYE0.title: Multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa
PNVWYE0.description: Pseudomonas aeruginosa that is resistant to ≥ 1 antibiotic in ≥ 3 generally susceptible antibiotic classes (i.e., fluoroquinolones, penicillins, cephalosporins, aminoglycosides, and carbapenems).

destinations.label: Multidrug-resistant organism infections → Common gram-negative bacteria

NNV-YE0.title: Inferior rectus entrapment
NNV-YE0.description: Entrapment of the inferior rectus muscle, which controls downward eye movement, within a fracture of the orbital floor. Typically caused by an orbital blowout fracture. Can lead to restricted eye movement, diplopia, and pain, especially on attempted upward gaze.

MNVMbE0.title: Candidal intertrigo
MNVMbE0.description: Superficial inflammatory dermatitis occurring in skin folds due to the overgrowth of Candida species, typically Candida albicans.

sNVtcE0.title: Ovulatory dysfunction
sNVtcE0.description: Abnormalities ranging from occasional menstrual cycle irregularities to chronic anovulation. Causes include hypothalamic or anterior pituitary dysfunction, primary ovarian insufficiency, and hyperandrogenism (e.g., in polycystic ovary syndrome). Can lead to amenorrhea and infertility.

DNV1WE0.title: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia
DNV1WE0.description: A subtype of frontotemporal dementia (FTD) that initially manifests with personality and behavioral changes (e.g., disinhibition and apathy). It is the most common subtype of FTD.

wNVhWE0.title: Primary progressive aphasia
wNVhWE0.description: A subtype of frontotemporal dementia that initially manifests with speech and language impairments. Further subclassified as nonfluent variant primary progressive aphasia (PPA) or semantic variant PPA based on characteristic symptoms.

zNVrdE0.title: Boric acid
zNVrdE0.description: A weak topical anti-infective agent. Used topically as a skin protectant (e.g., for relief of discomfort of chapped skin, diaper rash, or sunburn) and for the treatment of fungal infections.

-NVDdE0.title: Pivmecillinam hydrochloride
-NVDdE0.description: A penicillin class antibacterial. Used to treat uncomplicated urinary tract infections caused by susceptible isolates of Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis, and Staphylococcus saprophyticus.

ZmVZVE0.title: AmpC β-lactamase
ZmVZVE0.description: A subtype of beta-lactamase that hydrolyzes β-lactam antibiotics, including cephamycins (e.g., cefoxitin and cefotetan). Encoded by the AmpC gene and produced at baseline levels by numerous bacteria, including Enterobacteriaceae.

destinations.label: Multidrug-resistant organism infections → Common gram-negative bacteria

2mVTUE0.title: Pelvic rest
2mVTUE0.description: Abstention from activities that can strain the pelvic tissues. May be indicated in pregnant individuals to prevent inducing uterine contractions and in individuals recovering from pelvic surgery. Includes sexual intercourse, vaginal douching, tampon use, heavy lifting, and strenuous lower-body exercise.

gmVFUE0.title: Correction insulin therapy
gmVFUE0.description: Rapid-acting or regular insulin that is administered before meals (based on the premeal blood glucose level) or every 4–6 hours (in patients who are not eating). Used alone or in combination with scheduled insulin therapy.

hmVc2E0.title: Adjuvanted influenza vaccine
hmVc2E0.description: A standard-dose, inactivated influenza vaccine that contains a nonaluminum adjuvant called MF59 to trigger a stronger immune response than the nonadjuvanted inactivated influenza vaccine. Approved for individuals aged ≥ 65 years but may be considered (off-label) for individuals aged 18–64 years who have received a solid organ transplant and are on immunosuppressive medications.

3mVS2E0.title: High-dose influenza vaccine
3mVS2E0.description: An inactivated influenza vaccine that contains four times the amount of antigen as standard dose influenza vaccines. Approved for individuals aged ≥ 65 years but may be considered (off-label) for individuals aged 18–64 years who have received a solid organ transplant and are on immunosuppressive medications.

kmVmfE0.title: Gastric decompression
kmVmfE0.description: Placement of a nasogastric or orogastric tube to remove gastric contents, relieve visceral distention, and/or reduce the risk of vomiting and pulmonary aspiration. Indications include bowel obstruction, ileus, and some risk factors for surgical or critically ill patients.

7mV4SE0.title: Functional vision disorder
7mV4SE0.description: A manifestation of functional neurological symptom disorder in which patients experience visual disturbances (e.g., blindness) despite objective evidence of normal visual function.

destinations.label: Somatic symptom and related disorders → Functional neurological symptom disorder

smVtSE0.title: Class 1 obesity
smVtSE0.description: An obesity category defined by BMI 30–34.9 kg/m² in adults and 100–119% of the 95th percentile for age and sex in children. A lower range (25–29.9 or 27.5–29.9 kg/m²) is recommended for adults of Asian descent.

GmVBSE0.title: Class 2 obesity
GmVBSE0.description: An obesity category defined by BMI 35–39.9 kg/m² in adults and 120–139% of the 95th percentile for age and sex in children. A range of 30–34.9 kg/m² is recommended for adults of Asian descent.

tmVXhE0.title: Indications for weight-loss medications
tmVXhE0.description: Adults: BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²; BMI ≥ 27 kg/m² with at least one weight-related complication. Children ≥ 12 years of age: BMI ≥ 95th percentile for age and sex.

FmVghE0.title: Indications for bariatric surgery
FmVghE0.description: Obesity class 1 with T2DM and/or with lack of improvement following nonsurgical interventions; obesity class 2; obesity class 3

8mVOhE0.title: Naltrexone/bupropion extended-release
8mVOhE0.description: A combination of naltrexone (an opioid antagonist) and bupropion (a weak dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor) used to treat adults with obesity or with overweight and weight-related health problems. Mechanisms of action include appetite suppression (through its effects on the hypothalamus) and reduced food cravings (through its effects on the dopamine reward pathway).

umVphE0.title: Diethylpropion
umVphE0.description: A sympathomimetic amine used to induce weight loss by suppressing appetite.

c5VaQE0.title: Indications for systemic antibiotics for otitis externa
c5VaQE0.description: Includes an inability to administer topical therapy for otitis externa, e.g., due to external auditory canal (EAC) edema; risk factors for malignant otitis externa (MOE); infection extending beyond the EAC (e.g., cellulitis, MOE); concurrent acute otitis media; and previous radiotherapy of the ear.

V5VGQE0.title: CAD consortium model (extended)
V5VGQE0.description: A score used to estimate the pretest probability for obstructive coronary artery disease in patients with chest pain. Based on sex, age, symptoms, hospital setting, risk factors (diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and smoking), and CAC score (if available).

media.title: Pretest probability of CAD (extended consortium model)

e5VxQE0.title: Klisic test
e5VxQE0.description: A physical examination technique used to evaluate for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), particularly bilateral DDH. The examiner places their index finger on the ASIS and their middle finger on the greater trochanter; an imaginary line connecting these two points is then extended across the abdomen. The line should bisect or pass superior to the umbilicus. In individuals with DDH, the line passes inferior to the umbilicus.

U5VbjE0.title: AMBOSS GPT
U5VbjE0.description:
Get accurate, up-to-date medical information and a quick reference to AMBOSS articles directly in ChatGPT.


How to activate AMBOSS GPT

1. Go to go.amboss.com/gpt

2. Click the “AMBOSS Medical Knowledge” menu at the top and select “Keep in sidebar,” so it's always easily accessible

3. Ask AMBOSS GPT a question

4. Authorize with your email address and start using it


AMBOSS GPT is available to everyone with no additional charge. For the best experience, we recommend using the same email address you use for your AMBOSS account.

25VTjE0.title: AMBOSS browser extension
25VTjE0.description:
The AMBOSS browser extension provides pop-up definitions for medical terms on any website you visit, including rich multimedia content. You can also access the AMBOSS library for further reading or jump into related AMBOSS Qbank sessions, directly from your current page. The extension is primarily developed for Chrome, but it also runs on other Chromium-based browsers like Microsoft Edge, Opera, and Brave. Visit:
- google.com/chrome to install Google Chrome
- go.amboss.com/chrome to install the AMBOSS browser extension

f5VkjE0.title: Pavlik harness disease
f5VkjE0.description: Erosion of the posterior surface of the acetabulum. Can occur due to prolonged use of a Pavlik harness for the treatment of developmental dysplasia of the hip in infants.

35VSPE0.title: Prurigo nodularis
35VSPE0.description: A chronic skin condition caused by neuronal sensitization to itch and repeated scratching. Manifests as intensely pruritic papules, plaques, and/or nodules, usually on extensor surfaces of the arms and legs. Often a complication of atopic dermatitis, chronic pruritus, or systemic disease (e.g., diabetes, HIV).

k5Vm4E0.title: Infant hip physical examination
k5Vm4E0.description: Physical examination techniques performed at routine well-child visits through 6–9 months of age to assess for clinical features of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). Includes visual inspection, DDH instability maneuvers, hip range of motion, and the Galeazzi test.

destinations.label: Developmental dysplasia of the hip → Screening

N5V-4E0.title: Interstitial cystitis symptom index
N5V-4E0.description: A validated scale for interstitial cystitis that assesses the presence and frequency of the four characteristic symptoms: bladder pain, urinary urgency and frequency, and nocturia.

55VikE0.title: Fulguration
55VikE0.description: The use of an electric current to destroy abnormal tissue.

n5V7kE0.title: Physiological leg misalignment
n5V7kE0.description: A natural and temporary condition observed in children during their developmental stages, characterized by angular misalignment of the legs. Initially, most children are born with a varus alignment, which typically persists until around 2 years of age. Following this period, leg alignment transitions to a neutral position before shifting to a valgus alignment between the ages of 3 and 6. By the age of 7, leg alignment generally stabilizes to a neutral or mildly valgus position.

destinations.label: Angular deformities of the lower extremities → Overview

o5V0OE0.title: Scapholunate ligament
o5V0OE0.description: The ligament that connects the scaphoid and lunate bones. Essential to maintaining the stability and coordination of carpal motion between these two bones during wrist movement. Disruption of the ligament often causes scapholunate dissociation, which is the most common cause of carpal instability and can progress to degenerative arthritis if untreated.

K5VUOE0.title: Feature highly suggestive of DDH
K5VUOE0.description: Abnormal physical examination findings that indicate a likely diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). Comprises hip instability (i.e., frankly dislocated hip, positive instability maneuvers for DDH), limited or asymmetric hip abduction after 4 weeks of age, and leg-length discrepancy (e.g., positive Galeazzi sign).

destinations.label: Developmental dysplasia of the hip → Diagnosis

q5VCOE0.title: Manual therapy
q5VCOE0.description: A type of therapy involving the application of externally generated force to body tissues with therapeutic intent. Provided by physical therapists, occupational therapists, or massage therapists. Includes techniques such as joint and soft tissue mobilization and massage. Used to reduce pain, improve mobility, and/or regain functionality in musculoskeletal conditions, including pelvic floor dysfunction.

I5VYlE0.title: Botulism immune globulin
I5VYlE0.description: A human-derived antitoxin that contains antibodies to botulinum neurotoxin type A and B. Stops progression of paralysis by neutralizing free toxin in the blood serum. Cannot reverse existing paralysis as it does not neutralize toxins already bound to the synaptic receptor. Used to treat infant botulism.

r5VflE0.title: Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment
r5VflE0.description: A program for individuals with overweight or obesity. Led by a trained behavioral interventionist. Involves behavioral strategies (e.g., goal-setting, self-monitoring, problem-solving) to support lifestyle modifications (e.g., diet and exercise changes). Face-to-face sessions are preferred, including ≥ 26 instructive hours over 3–12 months for children (along with family-based counseling) and ≥ 14 sessions over 6 months for adults.

t5VXNE0.title: Cardiovascular health integrated lifestyle diet
t5VXNE0.description: A diet recommended for children with cardiovascular risk factors (e.g., overweight, obesity, lipid disorders, family history of early-onset cardiovascular disease). Emphasizes balanced nutrition with age-appropriate limits on total fat, saturated fat, trans fat, and added sugars. Promotes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and low-fat dairy.

E5V8NE0.title: Esomeprazole
E5V8NE0.description: A proton pump inhibitor that irreversibly inhibits H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells, resulting in an increase in stomach pH and suppression of gastric acid secretion. Used to treat conditions caused by excessive gastroesophageal acidity (e.g., dyspepsia, gastroesophageal reflux disease).

v5VANE0.title: Lansoprazole
v5VANE0.description: A proton pump inhibitor that irreversibly inhibits H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells, resulting in an increase in stomach pH and suppression of gastric acid secretion. Used to treat conditions caused by excessive gastroesophageal acidity (e.g., dyspepsia, gastroesophageal reflux disease).

w5VhmE0.title: Dilute bleach bath
w5VhmE0.description: A therapeutic bath for individuals with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. Used to treat a secondary bacterial skin infection or as an adjuvant therapy to decrease disease severity. Performed twice-weekly for 10 minutes with a lukewarm solution of 0.005% sodium hypochlorite (e.g., ½ cup of 6% liquid bleach added to 40 gallons of water).

95VNmE0.title: Candida auris
95VNmE0.description: A species of fungus that grows as an invasive yeast. Can colonize the skin and contaminate medical equipment. Risk factors for invasive infections (e.g., fungemia) include advanced age, indwelling medical devices, and chronic conditions (e.g., diabetes mellitus, cancer). Approximately 90% of strains are resistant to fluconazole and often cause outbreaks in health care facilities.

XMV9ME0.title: I/T ratio
XMV9ME0.description: The ratio of immature neutrophils (e.g., bands) relative to the total number of neutrophils (mature and immature). Commonly used to evaluate for infections, particularly in neonates. An I/T ratio ≥ 0.2 is a sensitive marker for sepsis.

VMVGnE0.title: Borchardt triad
VMVGnE0.description: Severe epigastric pain and distention, retching without vomiting, and an inability to pass a nasogastric tube. Characteristic of acute gastric volvulus.

destinations.label: Intestinal malrotation, midgut volvulus, and gastric volvulus → Gastric volvulus

SMVyLE0.title: Pathergy
SMVyLE0.description: A nonspecific, exaggerated skin reaction to minor trauma. May be observed in patients with Behcet disease, Sweet syndrome, and pyoderma gangrenosum. Typically manifests as an erythematous papule or pustule in Behcet disease and as one or more painful ulcers in pyoderma gangrenosum.

pMVLpE0.title: Medically assisted reproduction
pMVLpE0.description: Interventions and procedures used to treat infertility and facilitate reproduction. Includes ovulation induction, ovarian stimulation, intrauterine and intravaginal insemination, and assisted reproductive technology.

JMVspE0.title: BODE index
JMVspE0.description: A tool used to predict mortality in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Incorporates body mass index, degree of airflow obstruction, severity of dyspnea, and exercise capacity. Higher scores indicate a higher risk of death.

8MVOqE0.title: Ovulation induction
8MVOqE0.description: The use of medications to stimulate development of a single dominant follicle in patients with anovulation. Methods include oral medications (e.g., letrozole or clomiphene citrate), pulsatile GnRH, and exogenous gonadotropins.

uMVpqE0.title: PR-segment depression
uMVpqE0.description: A depression of the PR segment below the isoelectric line. Most commonly seen in acute pericarditis, typically with diffuse concave-upward ST-segment elevation.

gnVFsE0.title: Eugonadotropic eugonadism
gnVFsE0.description: The state of having normal FSH, LH, and estrogen levels. Distinguishes ovulatory dysfunction with normal hormone levels from ovulatory dysfunction with abnormal hormone levels (i.e., hypergonadotropic hypogonadism or hypogonadotropic hypogonadism). Most commonly discussed in the context of polycystic ovary syndrome.

knVmtE0.title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction
knVmtE0.description: An abnormality in the structure and/or function of the coronary microvasculature leading to reduced myocardial perfusion and myocardial ischemia. May occur without obstructive epicardial coronary artery disease. Coronary microvascular dysfunction is the underlying cause of microvascular angina.

OnVItE0.title: Microvascular angina
OnVItE0.description: A type of angina (i.e., symptoms of cardiac ischemia) that is caused by coronary microvascular dysfunction and occurs without obstructive epicardial coronary artery disease.

destinations.label: Chronic coronary disease → Ischemia with nonobstructive coronary arteries (INOCA)

5nViFE0.title: Skin nodules
5nViFE0.description: An elevated cutaneous and/or subcutaneous cystic or solid lesion > 1 cm in diameter.

nnV7FE0.title: Contraindications to hormone replacement therapy
nnV7FE0.description: Includes unexplained vaginal bleeding, estrogen-sensitive cancers, chronic liver disease, history of thromboembolic events, thrombophilia, and known coronary artery disease.

pnVL8E0.title: Ensifentrine
pnVL8E0.description: A phosphodiesterase 3 and phosphodiesterase 4 inhibitor that is indicated for maintenance treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in adults.

ZLVZwE0.title: Nonfluent variant primary progressive aphasia
ZLVZwE0.description: A variant of primary progressive aphasia characterized by effortful speech, agrammatism, phonological errors, and impaired comprehension of complex sentences.

0LVewE0.title: Semantic variant primary progressive aphasia
0LVewE0.description: A variant of primary progressive aphasia characterized by prominent word-finding difficulties (i.e., anomic aphasia) and impaired word comprehension.

mLVVyE0.title: Cytisinicline
mLVVyE0.description: A partial α4β2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor used in the management of smoking cessation, including e-cigarette dependence.

LLVwyE0.title: Benign paroxysmal vertigo
LLVwyE0.description: A condition characterized by ≥ 5 brief episodes of vertigo in children with or at an increased risk of migraine. Manifests with vomiting, pallor, fearfulness, nystagmus, and/or ataxia. Neurological examination is normal between episodes. Not to be confused with benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.

qLVCAE0.title: Intimal flap
qLVCAE0.description: A portion of the intima of a blood vessel that has detached from the vessel wall. Occurs in, e.g., aortic and carotid dissection, in which it separates the true from the false lumen and is visible on imaging.

sLVt_E0.title: Quinolones
sLVt_E0.description: A class of bactericidal antibiotics primarily used to treat urinary and GI tract infections as well as pneumonia. Effective against a broad spectrum of pathogens, including streptococci and gram-negative organisms. Contraindications include age < 18 years and pregnancy. Adverse affects include QT prolongation and tendinitis.

xLVE-E0.title: Broden view
xLVE-E0.description: An x-ray projection obtained by flexing the knee and internally rotating the ankle 30–45° with the patient supine. Used to assess for lateral process fractures of the talus.

0oVe0v0.title: Body surface area-based dosing
0oVe0v0.description: A method of dosing medications based on the patient's estimated body surface area using height and weight rather than weight alone.

YoVn0v0.title: Lixisenatide
YoVn0v0.description: A glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist used in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

destinations.label: Diabetes medications → Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (incretin mimetics)

XoV90v0.title: Tyrosinemia type 1
XoV90v0.description: A rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by deficiency of fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase, leading to accumulation of toxic tyrosine metabolites. Typically presents in infancy with progressive liver disease, renal tubular dysfunction, and risk of hepatocellular carcinoma.

destinations.label: Inborn errors of metabolism → Tyrosinemia type 1

WoVPav0.title: Methicillin
WoVPav0.description: A semisynthetic penicillinase-resistant penicillin, which is no longer available in the USA due to high rates of adverse effects (e.g., interstitial nephritis).

goVFYv0.title: Clinical features of acute urinary tract obstruction
goVFYv0.description: Features of acute upper urinary tract obstruction (UTO) include flank pain, hematuria, oliguria, nausea, and vomiting. Features of acute lower UTO include urinary retention, suprapubic pain, and palpable bladder.

SoVyYv0.title: Clinical features of chronic urinary tract obstruction
SoVyYv0.description: Chronic upper urinary tract obstruction may be asymptomatic. Clinical features of chronic lower urinary tract obstruction include urinary frequency, urgency, hesitancy, and straining.

PoVWXv0.title: Maximum heart rate
PoVWXv0.description: The highest estimated number of heartbeats per minute an individual can achieve during maximum physical exertion. Typically calculated as 220 − age. Can be used to express exercise intensity.

4oV3Xv0.title: Physiological oliguria
4oV3Xv0.description: A transient reduction in urinary output. May occur in, e.g., fasting, extreme physical exertion, or the postoperative period. Does not reflect underlying renal pathology or increase the risk of subsequent renal impairment.

KoVU1v0.title: Psychological maltreatment of children
KoVU1v0.description: Actions and behaviors from parents or caregivers that adversely impact a child’s cognitive, social, emotional, and physical development. Can be expressed verbally or nonverbally (through active or passive means)

6oVj1v0.title: Medical child abuse
6oVj1v0.description: A form of child maltreatment in which a caregiver fabricates and/or induces symptoms in a child, resulting in unwarranted and potentially harmful medical care.

JoVs1v0.title: Posttraumatic epilepsy
JoVs1v0.description: A chronic condition characterized by recurrent, unprovoked seizures that occur at least 1 week after a traumatic brain injury. (Seizures that occur within 1 week of the trauma are considered to be provoked by the injury.)

toVXdv0.title: Child sex trafficking
toVXdv0.description: A form of human trafficking involving any role in a child's participation in sexual activity for commercial purposes (e.g., recruitment, harboring, transporting).

FoVgdv0.title: Red flags for medical child abuse
FoVgdv0.description: Red flags include clinical findings that are unusual and only occur in the presence of a single caregiver; inconsistent or incongruent medical history; persistent demands for invasive tests or treatments from a caregiver, with no reassurance from normal test results; and a history of unusual illnesses or deaths in the family.

8oVOdv0.title: Clinical features of child sexual abuse
8oVOdv0.description: Features include behavior or sexual insights that are age-inappropriate; injuries in the genital, anal, and oral areas; recurrent urinary tract infections; signs and symptoms of STIs; and pregnancy. Physical examination may be normal.

uoVpdv0.title: Red flags for child maltreatment
uoVpdv0.description: Red flags include inconsistent or implausible history of an illness or injury, delays in seeking medical treatment, injuries concerning for nonaccidental trauma, and red flags for child sexual abuse.

EoV8dv0.title: Risk factors for child maltreatment
EoV8dv0.description: Caregiver factors include being a lone caregiver, intimate partner violence, substance use and/or mental health disorders, financial hardship, and a personal history of maltreatment as a child. Child factors include developmental or physical disability, behavioral disorders, and prematurity or chronic health problems.

voVAdv0.title: Clinical features of child neglect
voVAdv0.description: Features include inadequate, inappropriate, or soiled clothing; malnutrition or growth faltering; poor dentition; poor personal hygiene; and abnormal social, emotional, and/or language development.

woVhVv0.title: Kidney failure risk equation
woVhVv0.description: An equation used to estimate the 2-year and 5-year risk of progression to kidney failure requiring dialysis or transplantation in patients with chronic kidney disease stages G3a–G5. Based on urine albumin levels, sex, age, and estimated glomerular filtration rate.

_oV5ev0.title: Myocardial bridging
_oV5ev0.description: A congenital coronary anomaly involving at least partial encasement of a coronary artery (most often the left anterior descending artery) within the myocardium, which can lead to compression of the artery during systole. Patients are often asymptomatic but sometimes present with angina.

aKVQUv0.title: Postinfectious glomerulonephritis
aKVQUv0.description: An acute inflammation of the glomeruli after an infection (e.g., bacterial, viral, fungal). Streptococcus species were previously the predominant cause, but Staphylococcus species and gram-negative bacteria are now increasingly implicated.

dKVo2v0.title: Pediatric ulcerative colitis activity index
dKVo2v0.description: A scoring system for determining the symptoms (e.g., abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, stool consistency, and frequency) and activity of ulcerative colitis in children. Used to guide treatment and monitor response to therapy.

eKVx2v0.title: Viral myositis
eKVx2v0.description: Myalgia and weakness in skeletal muscle concurrent with or following a viral infection (predominantly influenza A or B). Most commonly occurs in children. Symptoms are usually self-limited and resolve with conservative management.

2KVTfv0.title: Performance-enhancing drug
2KVTfv0.description: A substance used to improve athletic performance or appearance by altering strength, muscle mass, endurance, speed, and/or recovery. Includes anabolic steroids, stimulants, erythropoietin, growth hormone, and beta-2 agonists. Many of these substances are banned in competitive sports.

4KV3gv0.title: Travel medicine
4KV3gv0.description: A discipline of medicine focused on the prevention and management of health risks associated with travel, especially infectious diseases.

NKV-gv0.title: Nutritional Risk Screening 2002
NKV-gv0.description: A screening tool for malnutrition risk in hospitalized patients. Combines markers of nutrition (e.g., recent weight loss, BMI, reduced food intake), current disease severity, and patient age.

pKVLhv0.title: Hypermobility spectrum disorder
pKVLhv0.description: Conditions characterized by symptomatic joint hypermobility that do not fulfill the criteria for any form of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS), including hypermobile EDS.

JKVshv0.title: Juvenile primary fibromyalgia syndrome
JKVshv0.description: A condition characterized by chronic, diffuse, and severe musculoskeletal pain in children and adolescents. Etiology is multifactorial. Clinical diagnosis based on defined criteria, including absence of an underlying condition, tender points on examination, and normal laboratory study results.

IKVY3v0.title: Kocher criteria for septic arthritis
IKVY3v0.description: A set of four criteria (fever, inability to bear weight, ESR ≥ 40 mm/h, and serum WBC > 12,000/mm³) used to differentiate septic arthritis and transient synovitis in children. The more criteria that are met, the higher the probability of septic arthritis.

7KV43v0.title: Horizontal transmission
7KV43v0.description: The spread of pathogens between individuals through direct or indirect contact with infectious material (e.g., blood, respiratory droplets), excluding transmission from parent to child through the placenta or breast milk.

tKVXRv0.title: Risk factors for early-onset sepsis
tKVXRv0.description: Factors associated with an increased risk of neonatal infection with group B Streptococcus (GBS) between birth and 6 days of life. Factors include maternal GBS colonization, maternal intrapartum temperature ≥ 38.0 °C (100.4 °F), intra-amniotic infection, prolonged rupture of membranes lasting ≥ 18 hours, previous newborn affected by GBS, and preterm and/or very low birth weight neonate.

destinations.label: Prevention of neonatal Group B streptococcal infections → Overview

DKV1iv0.title: Neonatal early-onset bacterial sepsis
DKV1iv0.description: An infection with a positive bacterial blood or CSF culture in a neonate that occurs within 72 hours of life.

destinations.label: Neonatal bacterial infections → Neonatal bacterial sepsis

wKVhiv0.title: Neonatal late-onset bacterial sepsis
wKVhiv0.description: An infection with a positive bacterial blood or CSF culture in a neonate that occurs between 3 and 28 days of life.

destinations.label: Neonatal bacterial infections → Neonatal bacterial sepsis

X6V9jv0.title: Drug-induced arthritis
X6V9jv0.description: A condition characterized by joint swelling, warmth, erythema, and/or pain attributed to medical or recreational drugs (e.g., quinolones, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors, aromatase inhibitors) after exclusion of other causes.

16V2Pv0.title: Additive arthritis
16V2Pv0.description: A pattern of arthritis characterized by the onset of synovitis in > 1 joint followed by the gradual onset of synovitis in other joints without resolution. Occurs in several conditions (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, psoriatic arthritis).

S6Vy4v0.title: Type 1 Wolfram syndrome
S6Vy4v0.description: A rare inherited autosomal recessive condition caused by loss of function of the WFS1 gene or a missense mutation in the ZCD2 gene. Manifests with symptoms of central diabetes insipidus, diabetes mellitus, and/or progressive vision loss from optic nerve damage.

h6Vckv0.title: Adipsia
h6Vckv0.description: A lack of thirst and reduced oral intake of liquids. Commonly caused by hypothalamic lesions resulting in an impaired thirst mechanism.

i6VJkv0.title: Postinfectious inflammatory arthritis
i6VJkv0.description: A type of inflammatory arthritis that can occur after the resolution of an extra-articular viral, bacterial, fungal, or parasitic infection. Manifestations vary and depend on the causative pathogen; symptoms range from mild arthralgia to severe, chronic pain.

m6VVlv0.title: Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome
m6VVlv0.description: A rare X-linked overgrowth syndrome caused by mutations in the GPC3 gene. Features of overgrowth may appear in utero and/or after birth and include macrosomia, coarse facial features (e.g., broad nose, wide mouth), and organomegaly. Other common features include structural brain anomalies with variable intellectual disability, congenital musculoskeletal findings, heart defects, hernias, and supernumerary nipples. Increases the risk for certain neoplasms (e.g., Wilms tumor, hepatoblastoma).

H6VKmv0.title: Hypothalamic hamartoma
H6VKmv0.description: A rare, benign lesion located in or near the hypothalamus. May manifest with seizures, precocious puberty, behavioral changes, and/or cognitive impairment.

86VO5v0.title: Canada Health Act
86VO5v0.description: A federal legislation that establishes the criteria and conditions provinces and territories must fulfill to receive federal health care funding. Aims to ensure access to medically necessary hospital and physician services for all eligible residents of Canada without financial or other barriers. Based on five principles: public administration, comprehensiveness, universality, portability, and accessibility.

u6Vp5v0.title: Inuit
u6Vp5v0.description: An Indigenous people inhabiting the Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland, and Alaska, traditionally relying on subsistence-based diets rich in marine mammals and fish. They possess distinct languages (e.g., Inuktitut), cultural practices, and health profiles shaped by environmental, nutritional, and sociopolitical factors.

E6V85v0.title: Acculturative stress
E6V85v0.description: Psychological and physiological strain resulting from the challenges of adapting to a new culture. Often experienced by immigrants, refugees, or minorities navigating cultural differences, discrimination, language barriers, and identity conflict. May contribute to anxiety, depression, and somatic symptoms.

v6VA5v0.title: Status First Nations
v6VA5v0.description: Individuals recognized under Canada’s Indian Act as registered members of a First Nation. Entitled to specific legal rights and benefits (e.g., tax exemptions, access to certain health services, education funding). Status is distinct from non-status First Nations, Métis, and Inuit identities.

D6V1Mv0.title: Portability (Canada Health Act)
D6V1Mv0.description: A principle of the Canada Health Act that ensures continued health coverage for insured residents when they move between provinces or travel within Canada. Provinces and territories must cover necessary hospital and physician services for their eligible residents during travel.

w6VhMv0.title: Indigenous Services Canada
w6VhMv0.description: A federal department tasked with delivering and supporting health, education, infrastructure, and social services for First Nations, Inuit, and Métis communities. Aims to enhance well-being and promote self-determination.

96VNMv0.title: Canadian Medical Protective Association
96VNMv0.description: A mutual, not-for-profit organization supporting Canadian physicians with legal, liability, and risk management services, while promoting safe care and compensating patients harmed by fault/negligence.

C6VqMv0.title: Canadian Medical Association
C6VqMv0.description: A national association representing physicians in Canada, with voluntary membership. Advocates for the medical profession, supports physician wellness, and promotes improvements in health policy and patient care.

x6VEMv0.title: Canadian Medical Association Code of Ethics and Professionalism
x6VEMv0.description: A guiding document that outlines the ethical principles, values, and professional responsibilities of physicians in Canada. Emphasizes key principles (e.g., patient welfare, respect for patient autonomy, integrity, compassion, and justice), alongside a commitment to lifelong learning, continuous professional development, and collaboration with other healthcare professionals.

B6VzMv0.title: Aid to capacity evaluation
B6VzMv0.description: A structured clinical tool used to assess a patient’s ability to make informed medical decisions. Evaluates understanding, appreciation of consequences, reasoning, and ability to communicate a choice. Commonly used for capacity assessments in hospital and outpatient settings in Canada.

A6VRnv0.title: Convention refugee
A6VRnv0.description: A person who meets the United Nations definition of a refugee, having a well-founded fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality, political opinion, or membership in a particular social group. Granted protection under international law.

z6Vrnv0.title: Consolidated block funding
z6Vrnv0.description: A funding mechanism that allocates a large sum to a recipient with broad discretion over its use within a specific area (e.g., health, housing, or community development). Contrasts with categorical grants, which are restricted to narrowly defined purposes. Aims to enhance local flexibility while aligning with broader federal objectives.

-6VDnv0.title: Complex care coordination
-6VDnv0.description: A collaborative approach to managing the needs of patients with multiple chronic conditions, disabilities, or social vulnerabilities. Involves interdisciplinary teams, personalized care plans, and communication across services to improve outcomes and reduce fragmentation.

0pVeLv0.title: Anhydramnios
0pVeLv0.description: A condition characterized by the complete absence of amniotic fluid in the amniotic sac. Causes include fetal renal tract anomalies, rupture of membranes, and placental insufficiency. Associated with poor perinatal outcomes.

apVQLv0.title: Tri-Council Policy Statement
apVQLv0.description: A Canadian guideline that outlines ethical standards for research involving humans. Developed jointly by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR), the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC), and the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC). Based on three core principles: respect for persons, concern for welfare, and justice.

YpVnLv0.title: Personal Health Information Protection Act
YpVnLv0.description: One example of a federal legislation that governs the collection, use, and disclosure of personal health information by health information custodians. Aims to protect patient privacy while facilitating appropriate information sharing for care, planning, and research.

bpVHLv0.title: Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act
bpVHLv0.description: A Federal Canadian law that governs the collection, use, and disclosure of personal information by private sector organizations during commercial activities. Protects individual privacy rights while accommodating legitimate business requirements.

XpV9Lv0.title: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario
XpV9Lv0.description: The regulatory authority for physicians in Ontario that oversees licensing, establishes practice standards, and addresses complaints. Promotes public safety by enforcing ethical conduct, ensuring ongoing competence, and fostering quality in medical services.

cpVaov0.title: Perinatal palliative care
cpVaov0.description: A specialized care approach that supports families when a fetus or newborn is diagnosed with a life-limiting condition. Focuses on comfort, dignity, and quality of life through interdisciplinary care, advanced planning, and emotional support before, during, and after birth.

1pV2ov0.title: Métis
1pV2ov0.description: One of the three constitutionally recognized Indigenous peoples in Canada, alongside First Nations and Inuit. Descendants of First Nations and European ancestry, with distinct culture, language (Michif), and history.

WpVPov0.title: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada
WpVPov0.description: The national professional association of obstetricians, gynaecologists, and women's health care providers in Canada. Develops clinical practice guidelines, promotes education, research, and advocacy to advance reproductive and maternal–fetal health.

dpVoov0.title: Canadian Institute for Health Information
dpVoov0.description: An independent, not-for-profit organization that provides comparable and actionable data to improve health care in Canada. It collects and analyzes information on health system performance, spending, and outcomes across provinces and territories. CIHI's reports, interactive tools, and standards support evidence-based decision‑making by governments, healthcare providers, and researchers.

VpVGov0.title: Public Health Agency of Canada
VpVGov0.description: A federal agency responsible for promoting and protecting public health in Canada. Oversees disease prevention and control, health surveillance, emergency preparedness, and health promotion. Plays a key role in responding to public health threats, including infectious disease outbreaks and pandemics.

epVxov0.title: Epigenetic programming
epVxov0.description: A process by which gene expression is regulated without altering the DNA sequence, typically through mechanisms such as DNA methylation, histone modification, and non-coding RNAs. Occurs during development and in response to environmental factors, influencing cell differentiation and phenotype.

UpVbKv0.title: Interim Federal Health Program
UpVbKv0.description: A Canadian government program administered by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) that provides temporary, limited health care coverage to protected persons, refugee claimants, and certain others who are not eligible for provincial or territorial health insurance. Coverage includes basic, supplemental, and prescription drug benefits for specified groups.

2pVTKv0.title: Housing First
2pVTKv0.description: An evidence-based approach to addressing homelessness that prioritizes providing immediate, permanent housing to individuals experiencing homelessness without preconditions such as employment, sobriety, or treatment compliance. It emphasizes client choice, harm reduction, and the provision of voluntary support services to promote housing stability and well-being.

fpVkKv0.title: Ontario Coroners Act
fpVkKv0.description: A provincial law in Ontario that establishes the framework for investigating deaths that are sudden, unexpected, unexplained, or occur under specific circumstances, known as reportable deaths (e.g., violence, accident, suicide). Outlines the powers and duties of coroners, procedures for inquests, and requirements for reporting such deaths to authorities.

TpV6Kv0.title: Non-Insured Health Benefits program
TpV6Kv0.description: A federal program administered by Indigenous Services Canada that provides eligible First Nations and Inuit with coverage for medically necessary health-related goods and services not covered by provincial or territorial health plans. Benefits include prescription drugs, dental care, vision care, medical supplies and equipment, mental health counselling, and medical transportation.

SpVyKv0.title: CH2OPD2
SpVyKv0.description: A clinical mnemonic used to systematically identify environmental and occupational exposures in a patient’s history. Stands for Community, Home, Hobbies, Occupation, Personal habits, Diet, and Drugs, guiding clinicians to consider potential sources of toxic or hazardous exposures.

hpVc6v0.title: Free community tax clinics
hpVc6v0.description: A community-based service, often coordinated by the Canada Revenue Agency (through the Community Volunteer Income Tax Program), that offers free assistance with income tax preparation and filing for eligible individuals with simple tax situations. Staffed by trained volunteers, these clinics help clients claim benefits and refunds they may be entitled to.

3pVS6v0.title: Medical Officer of Health
3pVS6v0.description: A physician appointed by a public health authority who leads and advises a team of public health professionals, overseeing disease prevention, health promotion, and emergency response at the community or regional level.

RpVl6v0.title: Cree
RpVl6v0.description: The largest Indigenous group in Canada that predominantly resides in the areas spanning from Alberta to Quebec. Acknowledged as having First Nations status under the Indian Act. Comprised of cultural subgroups that speak distinct dialects. Known for a rich oral tradition and cultural heritage.

ipVJ6v0.title: Market Basket Measure
ipVJ6v0.description: A Canadian poverty metric that estimates the income needed for a family of four to purchase a "basket" of goods and services (including food, clothing, shelter, transportation, and other essentials) necessary for a basic standard of living. Households with income below this threshold are considered to be living in poverty.

QpVu6v0.title: Canada Revenue Agency
QpVu6v0.description: A federal agency of the Government of Canada responsible for administering tax laws and benefit programs, collecting taxes, and ensuring compliance for individuals and businesses.

jpV_6v0.title: Guaranteed Income Supplement
jpV_6v0.description: A non-taxable financial benefit from the Government of Canada for seniors who receive Old Age Security and have limited income, offering extra support to reduce poverty among older adults.

PpVWpv0.title: Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion
PpVWpv0.description: A 1986 World Health Organization framework developed at the First International Conference on Health Promotion in Ottawa. Defines health promotion as enabling people to increase control over and improve their health. Identifies five action areas and emphasizes the importance of peace, shelter, education, food, income, a stable ecosystem, social justice, and equity as prerequisites for health.

4pV3pv0.title: Canada Child Benefit
4pV3pv0.description: A non-taxable monthly payment from the Government of Canada designed to assist families with the expenses of caring for children under 18 years. The amount families receive is based on factors such as their annual household income and number of children.

kpVmpv0.title: Ontario Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services
kpVmpv0.description: A provincial government ministry in Ontario that manages support services for families, children, youth, and individuals needing social or developmental assistance. Its work spans areas such as child welfare, income support, disability services, advancing women's interests, and programs for community wellbeing.

OpVIpv0.title: EarlyON Child and Family Centres
OpVIpv0.description: Community-based centres in Ontario offering free programs and resources for families and caregivers with children from birth to age six. Provide opportunities for early learning and development, parent and caregiver support, and connections to community services.

lpVvpv0.title: Ontario Health Protection and Promotion Act
lpVvpv0.description: A provincial statute in Ontario that provides the legal basis for the organization and delivery of public health programs and services. Defines the roles, powers, and duties of local boards of health and the Chief Medical Officer of Health in protecting and promoting community health and disease prevention.

NpV-pv0.title: Federal Health Claims Processing Service
NpV-pv0.description: A centralized electronic system used by the Government of Canada to process and adjudicate health benefit claims for clients of federal plans such as Veterans Affairs Canada, Non-Insured Health Benefits, and the Interim Federal Health Program, supporting provider payments and benefit administration.

mpVVJv0.title: Canadian Codes of Ethics
mpVVJv0.description: Guiding documents developed by national professional organizations to outline ethical standards and responsibilities in various fields (e.g., Canadian Code of Ethics for Psychologists, Canadian Medical Association Code of Ethics and Professionalism). Emphasize principles such as respect, integrity, accountability, and commitment to client or patient well-being. Serve to support ethical decision-making and professional conduct.

5pViJv0.title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission’s Calls to Action
5pViJv0.description: A collection of 94 recommendations issued in 2015 aimed at promoting reconciliation between Indigenous and non-Indigenous peoples in Canada. Divided into two main categories: "Legacy" and "Reconciliation." They focus on systemic injustices in areas such as child welfare, education, health, and justice, urging governments, institutions, and residents to acknowledge and address the legacy of residential schools and other harmful policies, with a focus on healing and fostering reconciliation.

npV7Jv0.title: Canada's Medical Assistance in Dying Law
npV7Jv0.description: A 2016 Canadian law that legalized medical assistance in dying (MAID) for adults with a grievous and irremediable medical condition. It includes eligibility criteria and provides guidance towards the provision of MAID in accordance with the Criminal Code.

LpVwJv0.title: Provincial privacy legislation
LpVwJv0.description: Legal frameworks established by provinces and territories in Canada to oversee the management of individuals’ personal data by local institutions, health systems, and private-sector organizations. These laws define privacy protections, access rights, and responsibilities for safeguarding information within each province.

6pVjqv0.title: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease activity score
6pVjqv0.description: An 8-point scoring system that is based on histology and used to stratify metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis. Three domains are taken into account (steatosis grade, lobular inflammation, and liver cell injury), with a total score of 0-2 indicating mild disease activity, 4-5 indicating moderate disease activity, and 6 or more indicating marked disease activity.

ppVLqv0.title: Constitutional advancement of growth
ppVLqv0.description: A growth pattern in which a child grows rapidly until 2-4 years of age, then grows steadily until puberty, which is usually precocious. Adult height is often normal.

qpVCqv0.title: FTD-motor neuron disease
qpVCqv0.description: A neurodegenerative disorder characterized by clinical features of both motor neuron disease (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) and frontotemporal dementia. Often associated with abnormal aggregation of TDP-43 protein in the brain and spinal cord.

HpVKIv0.title: Biparametric MRI
HpVKIv0.description: A type of high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging that uses T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted sequences, but without dynamic contrast enhancement (compared to multiparametric MRI, which uses all three). Primary clinical use is for the detection, localization, and risk stratification of prostate cancer, particularly if contrast administration is contraindicated or unnecessary.

FpVgrv0.title: Atogepant
FpVgrv0.description: A calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist used for migraine prevention.

8pVOrv0.title: Erenumab
8pVOrv0.description: A calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist used for migraine prevention.

upVprv0.title: Fremanezumab
upVprv0.description: A calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist used for migraine prevention.

vpVArv0.title: Enhancement fee
vpVArv0.description: An out-of-pocket charge for non-insured services or upgrades that go beyond medically necessary care.

DpV17v0.title: Infanticide
DpV17v0.description: The act of causing the death of a newly-born child, typically by a parent.

wpVh7v0.title: Defervescence
wpVh7v0.description: The return to normal body temperature following a fever.

BpVz7v0.title: Menstrual migraine
BpVz7v0.description: Migraines that occur only during menstruation or are more common during menstruation. Can occur with or without aura. Classified as pure menstrual migraines (occur only in the 2 days before and/or after the start of menstruation) or menstrually related migraines (attacks are more common during menstruation but are also present at other times).

YJVnsv0.title: High-consequence infectious diseases
YJVnsv0.description: Infectious diseases that are contagious, can cause widespread severe illness, and pose a high risk to public health. Examples include viruses that cause hemorrhagic fever (e.g., Ebola virus) and respiratory disease (e.g., avian flu).

4JV38v0.title: Presymptomatic type 1 diabetes
4JV38v0.description: An early stage of type 1 diabetes in which ≥ 2 pancreatic islet autoantibodies are present, but the individual has not yet developed hyperglycemia or symptoms of diabetes.

OJVI8v0.title: Antihypertensive medication
OJVI8v0.description: A class of drugs used to lower elevated blood pressure and reduce the risk of cardiovascular events. Includes diuretics, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs), calcium channel blockers, and beta blockers. Selection depends on patient characteristics and comorbidities.

7JV4vv0.title: Growth velocity
7JV4vv0.description: The rate at which a child's length and/or height changes over time. Requires at least 2 measurements over 3 to 6 months. Typical values are based on age and gender.

sJVtvv0.title: Ghent criteria
sJVtvv0.description: A set of criteria used to diagnose Marfan syndrome. Elements include aortic root dilatation, ectopia lentis, FBN1 gene mutation, family history of Marfan syndrome, and systemic clinical features (e.g., musculoskeletal abnormalities, pneumothorax).

0qVeCv0.title: Chronic mastoiditis
0qVeCv0.description: An infection of the mastoid air cells lasting > 1 month. Usually a complication of chronic otitis media. Symptoms are milder and develop more slowly than in acute mastoiditis.

VqVGxv0.title: Lupus cerebritis
VqVGxv0.description: A form of central nervous system involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus that is characterized by brain dysfunction due to inflammation, thrombosis, or autoantibody-mediated injury.

LqVw_v0.title: CVD
LqVw_v0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Cardiovascular disease
2. Chronic venous disease

JqVszv0.title: Time in therapeutic range
JqVszv0.description: The percentage of time over a given monitoring period during which a patient’s INR remains within the pre‑specified therapeutic window. Calculated by linearly interpolating between successive INR measurements (Rosendaal method). A value ≥  65% correlates with a low risk of thromboembolic and bleeding events for a patient on warfarin therapy.

IqVY-v0.title: Garrod nodules
IqVY-v0.description: Subcutaneous fibrofatty thickenings over the dorsal aspects of finger joints, primarily the proximal interphalangeal joints. May be associated with other fibromatoses such as Dupuytren contracture and Peyronie disease.

rqVf-v0.title: Nutrient-stimulated hormone-based medications
rqVf-v0.description: Medications that mimic the effects of hormones that are naturally released in response to nutrient intake and cause increased satiety, slowed gastric emptying, and stimulation of insulin secretion. Examples include GLP-1 receptor agonists (e.g., liraglutide, semaglutide), dual GIP/GLP-1 agonists (e.g., tirzepatide), and amylin analogs (e.g., pramlintide, cagrilintide). Used for diabetes management and/or weight loss.

HqVK-v0.title: Chief Public Health Officer
HqVK-v0.description: The highest-ranking public health official in Canada, acting as the federal government’s primary public health advisor. Responsibilities include offering evidence-based advice to the Minister of Health, leading national public health initiatives, coordinating responses to public health emergencies, and communicating health information to Canadians.

sqVt-v0.title: Canadian Task Force on Preventive Health Care
sqVt-v0.description: An independent panel of experts in primary care, prevention, and evidence-based medicine in Canada. Develops clinical practice guidelines for preventive health care, including screening and counseling recommendations, to improve the health of Canadians. Supported by the Public Health Agency of Canada.

GqVB-v0.title: Sentinel surveillance
GqVB-v0.description: A surveillance system that uses selected, representative reporting sites or institutions (sentinel sites) to systematically collect high-quality data on specific diseases or health events. Used to monitor trends, detect outbreaks, and inform public health interventions when comprehensive surveillance is not feasible.

tqVXZD0.title: Health surveillance
tqVXZD0.description: The systematic and ongoing process of collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and sharing health data to monitor population health, identify trends or outbreaks, and guide public health actions and policies. Helps in recognizing risks, allocating resources, and evaluating interventions.

FqVgZD0.title: Canadian Survey on Disability
FqVgZD0.description: A national survey conducted periodically by Statistics Canada. Gathers detailed information on the type and severity of disabilities, their impacts on daily activities, employment, and social participation among Canadians aged 15 years and older living in private households. The data is used to inform disability-related policy, programs, and research across Canada, excluding individuals in institutional settings.

8qVOZD0.title: WHO International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health
8qVOZD0.description: A framework developed by the World Health Organization for describing and measuring health and disability at both individual and population levels. Incorporates components such as body functions and structures, activities and participation, and contextual factors (environmental and personal), offering a standardized language and conceptual basis for understanding health and disability. It complements the ICD by emphasizing functioning rather than diagnosis.

uqVpZD0.title: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health
uqVpZD0.description: An academic health sciences center located in Toronto, Canada, affiliated with the University of Toronto. Focuses on mental health, substance use, and addiction, providing clinical care, research, education, and advocacy. CAMH is a prominent national resource for mental health and addiction services, public education, and policy development.

EqV8ZD0.title: Panel physician
EqV8ZD0.description: A doctor authorized by immigration authorities to perform medical examinations for individuals applying to immigrate or seek refugee status. Evaluate overall health, screen for communicable diseases, and submit medical reports to immigration agencies. While they provide medical findings, they do not make final decisions regarding immigration or admissibility.

9qVN0D0.title: Child and Family Services
9qVN0D0.description: A term used in Canada to describe government or community-based programs that aim to ensure the safety, well-being, and healthy development of children while supporting families in need. Managed at the provincial and territorial levels. Services include child protection, family support, foster care, adoption, and the prevention of child abuse and neglect.

xqVE0D0.title: The Committee to Advise on Tropical Medicine and Travel
xqVE0D0.description: An expert advisory group convened by the Public Health Agency of Canada to provide guidance on tropical medicine, travel-related illnesses, and the prevention of infectious diseases in travelers. Develops evidence-based recommendations for health professionals, policymakers, and the public on travel and tropical health issues.

BqVz0D0.title: Aboriginal Diabetes Initiative
BqVz0D0.description: A national program in Canada aimed at improving the health of First Nations, Inuit, and Métis people by reducing the prevalence and impact of type 2 diabetes. Emphasizes diabetes prevention, health promotion, screening, and management through culturally appropriate resources and community-driven initiatives.

yqVdaD0.title: Institute for Safe Medication Practices Canada
yqVdaD0.description: An independent, non-profit organization in Canada dedicated to preventing medication errors and promoting safe medication practices nationwide. Offers expert analysis, education, and evidence-based recommendations to healthcare professionals, organizations, and policymakers.

AqVRaD0.title: Canada's Food Guide
AqVRaD0.description: A Canadian nutrition resource created by Health Canada that offers guidance for healthy eating and supporting wellness. Provides science-based advice on food choices, portion sizes, and eating habits, emphasizing the importance of vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and protein foods, and encouraging mindful eating and respect for cultural food traditions.

_qV5aD0.title: Bill C-9
_qV5aD0.description: A Canadian federal bill that amends the Judges Act to reform the process for addressing allegations of misconduct against federally appointed judges. Introduces a more efficient, transparent, and structured system for investigating judicial conduct, replacing the previous framework managed by the Canadian Judicial Council.

zqVraD0.title: GST/HST credit
zqVraD0.description: A non-taxable quarterly benefit provided by the Canadian government to help individuals and families with low or moderate incomes offset the cost of the goods and services tax (GST) and harmonized sales tax (HST). The credit amount is based on household income, marital status, and number of children. Eligible individuals are automatically considered when they file their annual income tax return.

ZIVZYD0.title: Declaration of Helsinki
ZIVZYD0.description: An international ethical guideline developed by the World Medical Association that outlines principles for conducting medical research involving human participants. Addresses key areas, including informed consent, risk-benefit assessment, and the protection of participant rights and welfare.

0IVeYD0.title: Belmont Report
0IVeYD0.description: A foundational document in research ethics developed in the United States and published in 1979. Outlines key ethical principles for conducting research involving human subjects: respect for persons, beneficence, and justice. These principles guide the ethical conduct of research through requirements such as obtaining informed consent, carefully assessing risks and benefits, and ensuring the fair selection of research participants.

aIVQYD0.title: Council for International Organizations of Medical Sciences
aIVQYD0.description: An international organization that works in collaboration with the World Health Organization to promote high ethical standards in human biomedical research. Creates globally recognized guidelines that address research ethics, informed consent, product development and safety, and the protection of research participants.

YIVnYD0.title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission
YIVnYD0.description: A commission in Canada established under the Indian Residential Schools Settlement Agreement to investigate and document the history and long-lasting effects of residential schools and their impact on Indigenous peoples. It collected survivor testimonies, raised public awareness, and issued recommendations called Calls to Action. Its goal was to address past harms and promote reconciliation between Indigenous and non-Indigenous Canadians.

bIVHYD0.title: Consent and Capacity Board
bIVHYD0.description: An independent tribunal in Ontario, Canada, that handles issues related to consent to treatment, decision-making capacity, involuntary psychiatric admissions, and substitute decision-making. Holds hearings under the Health Care Consent Act, the Mental Health Act, and related laws to safeguard the rights and autonomy of individuals with mental health or capacity issues.

cIVabD0.title: Bill C-7
cIVabD0.description: A Canadian federal law bill that amended the Criminal Code to expand access to Medical Assistance in Dying (MAiD). It removed the requirement that a person's natural death be reasonably foreseeable, thereby broadening eligibility. It introduced new safeguards for individuals whose death is not imminent, such as a 90-day assessment period and expert consultation. Temporarily excluded eligibility for individuals seeking MAiD solely on the basis of a mental illness until March 2024.

1IV2bD0.title: Provincial housestaff organizations
1IV2bD0.description: Provincial organizations that represent housestaff (resident physicians) during their postgraduate medical training. Advocate for members on topics like compensation, working conditions, call schedules, and resident wellness. Negotiate collective agreements with provincial health authorities, hospitals, and medical schools to ensure fair treatment and safe training environments. Examples include PARO (Professional Association of Residents of Ontario) and Resident Doctors of BC, among others nationwide.

WIVPbD0.title: Borderline intellectual functioning
WIVPbD0.description: A poorly defined condition characterized by intellectual limitations that impair daily functioning but do not meet the criteria for an intellectual disability.

dIVobD0.title: Residential school syndrome
dIVobD0.description: A term that describes a pattern of psychological and emotional challenges faced by some Indigenous survivors of Canada’s residential school system. It may include symptoms such as depression, anxiety, posttraumatic stress, substance misuse, and a significant loss of cultural identity and family connections. These effects are linked to traumatic experiences of abuse, loss, and systemic disconnection from language, community, and culture within residential schools. Not officially classified as a psychiatric diagnosis.

eIVxbD0.title: The Canadian Association for the Study of Liver Disease
eIVxbD0.description: A national professional organization dedicated to advancing research, education, and clinical practice in hepatology. Brings together clinicians, researchers, and trainees from across Canada to promote liver health, develop clinical guidelines, support knowledge sharing, and advocate for improved prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of liver diseases.

UIVbXD0.title: Association of Medical Microbiology and Infectious Disease Canada
UIVbXD0.description: A national professional organization dedicated to the prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and control of infectious diseases and medical microbiology. Brings together clinicians, laboratory specialists, researchers, and educators to advance research, develop clinical guidelines and best practices, provide continuing education, and advocate for effective infectious disease management and microbiology in Canada.

fIVkXD0.title: Blended payment model
fIVkXD0.description: A physician compensation framework that combines multiple payment methods, such as fee-for-service, salary, and capitation, into a single, integrated approach. Aims to balance financial incentives, promote high-quality, patient-centered care, and support flexible, team-based practice arrangements. Increasingly adopted in Canadian primary care settings to address the limitations of traditional single-method payment systems.

TIV6XD0.title: National Advisory Committee on Immunization
TIV6XD0.description: A Canadian expert advisory body that provides independent, evidence-based recommendations on human vaccines. Operating under the Public Health Agency of Canada, NACI advises public health officials on immunization schedules, vaccine safety and effectiveness, and immunization policies. Its work helps promote consistent, informed, and effective vaccination practices nationwide, protecting public health.

gIVFXD0.title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society
gIVFXD0.description: A national professional organization committed to improving cardiovascular health in Canada through research, education, clinical guidelines, and advocacy. Brings together cardiologists, researchers, and other healthcare professionals to promote excellence in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Develops national clinical practice guidelines and provides ongoing professional education.

3IVScD0.title: Bladder agenesis
3IVScD0.description: A rare congenital condition characterized by the complete absence of the urinary bladder. This condition occurs during fetal development when the bladder fails to form properly.

media.title: Congenital anomalies of the kidneys and urinary tract (CAKUT)

QIVucD0.title: Hoffmann syndrome
QIVucD0.description: A rare form of hypothyroid myopathy in adults with untreated hypothyroidism. Characterized by muscle hypertrophy and weakness, impaired muscle relaxation, and painful muscle spasms.

jIV_cD0.title: Kocher-Debre-Semelaigne syndrome
jIV_cD0.description: A rare form of myopathy in pediatric patients with untreated hypothyroidism. Characterized by muscle pseudohypertrophy and proximal muscle weakness.

PIVW1D0.title: Left ventricular assist device
PIVW1D0.description: A mechanical device that supports the function of the left ventricle in patients with end-stage heart failure. The term most commonly refers to intracorporeal LVADs, which provide continuous blood flow through a surgically implanted pump connected to an external controller and power source.

destinations.label: Mechanical circulatory support → Left ventricular assist devices

lIVv1D0.title: Isoechoic
lIVv1D0.description: The state of two structures reflecting the same amount of sound waves as each other, which results in both structures having the same brightness on ultrasonography.

nIV7WD0.title: Finnish Diabetes Risk Score
nIV7WD0.description: A validated questionnaire developed in Finland to estimate an individual's 10-year risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Includes 8 questions related to age, BMI, waist circumference, physical activity, daily intake of fruits and vegetables, antihypertensive medication use, history of high blood glucose, and family history of diabetes. Widely used across Europe and served as the basis for similar tools adapted to other countries, such as CANRISK in Canada.

LIVwWD0.title: Canadian Diabetes Risk Questionnaire
LIVwWD0.description: A validated risk assessment tool used to estimate an individual’s 10-year risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Incorporates factors such as age, sex, BMI, waist circumference, physical activity, daily consumption of fruits and vegetables, personal and family history of high blood glucose or diabetes, as well as demographic and clinical variables relevant to the Canadian population (e.g., ethnicity, education level).

qIVCdD0.title: CHADS-65 algorithm
qIVCdD0.description: A simplified algorithm used in Canada to guide long-term antithrombotic therapy in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. Oral anticoagulation is indicated if the patient's age is ≥ 65 years or CHADS₂ score is ≥ 1. For patients < 65 years with a CHADS₂ score of 0, low-dose aspirin is indicated if arterial vascular disease (e.g., coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease) is present; otherwise, no antithrombotic therapy is required.

7IV4VD0.title: LEA symbols test
7IV4VD0.description: A validated pediatric vision screening tool that uses easily recognizable symbols (circle, square, house, and apple) of standardized size and spacing to assess visual acuity. Especially useful for young children and individuals with communication or developmental challenges. Provides accurate and reliable visual assessment when letter-based eye charts are not suitable.

sIVtVD0.title: Early intervention program
sIVtVD0.description: A government-funded program under part C of the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act for families with children ≤ 3 years of age who have a disability (e.g., hearing loss, visual impairment, autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability). Provides family-centered services including physical, occupational, speech therapy, and specialized interventions.

uIVpeD0.title: Developmental coordination disorder
uIVpeD0.description: A neurodevelopmental disorder with onset in early childhood characterized by an inability to acquire and execute motor skills. Manifests as clumsiness and inaccuracy of movement, and impairs activities of daily living.

zIVr2D0.title: Plant-based diet
zIVr2D0.description: A type of diet that emphasizes higher intake of foods derived from plants (e.g., vegetables, fruits, legumes, nuts) and lower intake of foods derived from animals (e.g., meat, eggs). Examples include the Mediterranean diet, vegetarian diets, and vegan diets.

hrVcSD0.title: Wound management plan
