hrVcSD0.description: A personalized care strategy developed by a multidisciplinary team to ensure optimal care of patients with chronic wounds. Typically includes details on wound assessments, healing progression, comorbidities, treatment goals, interventions, and follow-up.

3rVSSD0.title: Quadriplegia
3rVSSD0.description: A partial or complete paralysis of the upper and lower extremities caused by injury to the spinal cord.

nrV73D0.title: Cohen's effect size
nrV73D0.description: A standardized measure of the magnitude of difference between two group means. Calculated by dividing the difference in means by the pooled standard deviation and expressed in units of standard deviation. Used to compare studies and measurement scales, and to help assess the practical or clinical relevance of findings beyond statistical significance. Conventionally, a Cohen's effect size of ~ 0.2 is considered small, ~ 0.5 medium, and ≥ 0.8 large.

orV0RD0.title: organ procurement organization
orV0RD0.description: Organ Procurement Organizations are federally designated, not‑for‑profit entities in the United States responsible for the identification, evaluation, recovery, and transportation of organs for transplantation. Each OPO serves a specific geographic region, working closely with hospitals, donor families, and transplant centers.

qrVCRD0.title: Junctional ectopic tachycardia
qrVCRD0.description: A subtype of junctional tachycardia typically seen in infants, characterized by rapid tachyarrhythmia (heart rate >  200 beats/minute) from an ectopic focus in the AV node or the proximal bundle of His. May be congenital or occur within 72 hours of cardiac surgery.

rrVfiD0.title: Macrodactyly
rrVfiD0.description: A rare nonhereditary congenital condition characterized by abnormal overgrowth of the bones and soft tissues of one or more fingers and/or toes. May progress over time.

7rV4iD0.title: Hemimegalencephaly
7rV4iD0.description: A rare congenital brain malformation characterized by abnormal enlargement of one cerebral hemisphere. May be isolated or associated with neurocutaneous syndromes. Typically manifests with severe seizures, developmental delay, and neurological deficits such as contralateral hemiparesis.

Z7VZ4D0.title: Ischemic heart disease
Z7VZ4D0.description: An umbrella term encompassing all chronic and acute forms of myocardial ischemia, including stable coronary artery disease, microvascular angina, and myocardial infarction.

07Ve4D0.title: Chronic coronary disease
07Ve4D0.description: Chronic myocardial ischemia due to atherosclerosis, endothelial dysfunction, and/or microvascular disease. Includes all stable manifestations of ischemic heart disease, including coronary artery disease, microvascular angina, and vasospastic angina.

a7VQ4D0.title: Coronary artery revascularization
a7VQ4D0.description: A procedure used to restore cardiac blood flow and reduce myocardial ischemia. Can be surgical (coronary artery bypass grafting) or endovascular (percutaneous coronary intervention).

b7VH4D0.title: Drive-reduction theory
b7VH4D0.description: A psychological theory proposing that an unmet biological need creates a state of tension, motivating actions to reduce the tension and restore homeostasis.

c7VakD0.title: Schachter-Singer two-factor theory
c7VakD0.description: A psychological theory developed by Stanley Schachter and Jerome E. Singer, which states that an emotional experience is the result of two steps: the perception of nonspecific physiological arousal in response to a stimulus (e.g., palpitations) followed by the cognitive appraisal that determines the emotion (e.g., fear).

17V2kD0.title: Incentive theory
17V2kD0.description: A psychological theory proposing that motivation is primarily driven by environmental factors and their interaction with internal needs. According to this theory, behavior is motivated by a desire for positive incentives (rewards) and avoidance of negative ones (punishments).

W7VPkD0.title: Cognitive dissonance
W7VPkD0.description: A state of psychological tension experienced by an individual when their actions conflict with their beliefs or values. Discomfort motivates a drive to reduce tension by either changing behavior to align with beliefs or altering beliefs to justify behavior.

n7V7mD0.title: CHADS₂ score
n7V7mD0.description: A score on a 0–6 scale introduced in 2001 to assess thromboembolic and stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation. Also an acronym for risk factors: Congestive heart failure, Hypertension, Age ≥ 75 years, Diabetes mellitus (1 point each), and prior Stroke or TIA (2 points). Largely superseded by CHA₂DS₂-VASc score, which is better at identifying truly low-risk patients, but still used in some treatment algorithms (e.g., CHADS-65) because of its simplicity.

67Vj5D0.title: Nitisinone
67Vj5D0.description: A 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase inhibitor used as an adjunct to dietary restrictions for the treatment of hereditary tyrosinemia type 1 and for the reduction of urine homogentisic acid in adults with alkaptonuria. Prevents the formation of toxic metabolites that damage the liver and kidneys. Has replaced liver transplantation as first-line treatment for hereditary tyrosinemia type 1. Requires concomitant restriction of dietary tyrosine and phenylalanine.

I7VYMD0.title: Encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis
I7VYMD0.description: A rare fibroinflammatory disorder characterized by progressive fibrosclerosis of the peritoneum that encases the small bowel. Typically a late complication of long-term peritoneal dialysis, but may be idiopathic or secondary (e.g., to tuberculosis). Clinical features include abdominal pain, nausea, anorexia, weight loss, and recurrent subacute or acute bowel obstruction.

r7VfMD0.title: Pseudocapsule
r7VfMD0.description: A layer of tissue that surrounds a lesion (e.g., a tumor) but is not a true capsule formed by the lesion itself.

87VOnD0.title: Contact dermatitis
87VOnD0.description: An inflammatory skin condition that is caused by direct exposure to external substances. Contact dermatitis encompasses two conditions: allergic contact dermatitis and irritant contact dermatitis.

E7V8nD0.title: Phentermine/topiramate extended release
E7V8nD0.description: A combination of phentermine (a sympathomimetic amine that suppresses appetite) and topiramate (an antiepileptic drug that suppresses appetite and enhances satiety) used to treat individuals > 12 years with obesity and adults with overweight and weight-related health problems.

A7VRoD0.title: Mavacamten
A7VRoD0.description: A cardiac myosin inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adults with symptomatic NYHA class II–III obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

dHVo6D0.title: Electric charge
dHVo6D0.description: A fundamental property of matter. Causes matter to experience a force in an electromagnetic field. Comes in two types, positive and negative. Measured in coulombs. Conserved in closed systems. Examples include electrons (negative charge) and protons (positive charge). Integral to electric forces and fields.

VHVG6D0.title: Coulomb's law
VHVG6D0.description: A fundamental principle of electromagnetism, quantitatively describing the force. Governs the electrostatic interaction between charged particles. States that the force magnitude between two point charges is directly proportional to the product of their charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation distance.

eHVx6D0.title: Electric field
eHVx6D0.description: A vector field around charged particles, described by the force a charge experiences per unit charge. Measured in newtons per coulomb (N/C) or volts per meter (V/m). Essential in electromagnetism, with applications in designing capacitors and analyzing electrostatic interactions.

UHVbpD0.title: Electric potential energy
UHVbpD0.description: Energy stored in charged particles due to their position relative to other charges. Resulting from Coulombic interactions. Changes as charges move in an electric field. Integral to circuits and capacitors. Similar to gravitational potential energy in mechanics. Quantified in joules.

2HVTpD0.title: Electric potential
2HVTpD0.description: Electric potential, the work done per unit charge against an electric field. Measured in volts. Represents electric potential energy per unit charge. Scalar quantity. Determines the energy level at a point in an electric field. Important in circuit analysis and electrostatics.

fHVkpD0.title: Capacitor
fHVkpD0.description: An electrical component, capable of storing and releasing electrical energy. Composed of two conductive plates separated by an insulating material known as a dielectric. Utilized in electronic circuits for energy storage, filtering, and voltage regulation. Exhibits capacitance, measured in farads.

THV6pD0.title: Electric current
THV6pD0.description: The flow of electric charge, typically measured in amperes. Commonly carried by moving electrons in a conductor, such as a wire. Essential in powering electronic devices and circuits. Can be direct (DC) or alternating (AC), affecting directionality and applications.

SHVypD0.title: Risk factors for atopic dermatitis
SHVypD0.description: Includes personal and/or family history of atopy (e.g., atopic triad, food allergies, urticaria), genetic mutations (e.g., in the filaggrin gene), and environmental factors (e.g., living in an urban setting, low UV-light exposure, small family size).

hHVcJD0.title: Triggers for atopic dermatitis
hHVcJD0.description: Includes environmental allergens (e.g., dust mites, animal dander, pollen), environmental conditions (e.g., heat, dry or humid climate), air pollutants (e.g., particulate matter, nitrogen oxide, carbon monoxide), stress, and mechanical and chemical irritants (e.g., wool clothing, detergents).

3HVSJD0.title: Voltage
3HVSJD0.description: An electric potential difference, measured in volts. Drives the flow of electric current in a circuit. A measure of work required to move a charge between two points. Typically generated by sources like batteries or generators. Determines the energy per unit charge available in an electrical system.

iHVJJD0.title: Electrical resistance
iHVJJD0.description: Opposition to the flow of electric current in a conductor. Measured in ohms (Ω). Resulting from collisions between electrons and atoms in a material. Greater in materials with fewer free electrons, like insulators. Influenced by factors such as temperature, material composition, and cross-sectional area.

QHVuJD0.title: Resistivity
QHVuJD0.description: An intrinsic property of a material that quantifies how strongly it resists the flow of electric current.

jHV_JD0.title: Electrical conductance
jHV_JD0.description: A measure of how well a specific component or circuit conducts electric current through a specific object or component; it is the reciprocal of resistance.

PHVWqD0.title: Metallic conduction
PHVWqD0.description: Electric current flow through metal or conductive material. Involves movement of free electrons. Occurs without decomposition of the material. Efficiency affected by temperature and impurities. Crucial in electrical circuits, wiring, and electronic devices.

4HV3qD0.title: Electrolytic conduction
4HV3qD0.description: The movement of ions through a liquid medium, typically an electrolyte. Driven by an applied electric field, resulting in electrical current flow. Common in electrochemical cells, batteries, and electrolysis processes. Involves ionic species transport rather than electron flow.

kHVmqD0.title: Electrical work
kHVmqD0.description: The energy required to move a charge across a potential difference (voltage) or the energy released when a charge moves along a potential difference. Measured in joules in SI units.

OHVIqD0.title: Electrical power
OHVIqD0.description: The rate of doing work, transferring energy, or converting energy. Defined as work done per unit time. Measured in watts (W) in the International System of Units (SI). Commonly assessed in electrical circuits, mechanical systems, and thermal processes.

lHVvqD0.title: Electromotive force
lHVvqD0.description: The voltage generated by a source of electrical energy, such as a battery or generator. Drives the flow of electric current in a circuit. Measured in volts (V). Not a force despite its name. Can result from chemical, mechanical, or physical processes, like in electrochemical cells or thermoelectric devices.

NHV-qD0.title: Alternating current
NHV-qD0.description: An electric current, periodically reversing direction. Characterized by its frequency and amplitude. Commonly used in power transmission because of efficient voltage transformation. Found in household and industry electrical networks. Typically described by sinusoidal waveforms.

mHVVID0.title: RMS voltage
mHVVID0.description: The root mean square voltage, the effective value of alternating current voltage. Calculated as the square root of the average of the squares of instantaneous values over a cycle. Represents equivalent DC voltage providing the same power to a resistive load. Common in electrical engineering to describe AC systems.

5HViID0.title: Capacitors in series
5HViID0.description: A configuration of capacitors, arranged in a single path for current flow. Results in reduced total capacitance. Total capacitance calculated using the reciprocal sum formula. Charge on each capacitor equal. Voltage across capacitors adds to total voltage. Commonly used in electrical circuits to achieve specific capacitance values.

MHVMID0.title: Lorentz force
MHVMID0.description: The force exerted on a charged particle moving in an electromagnetic field is calculated using the equation F = q(E + v × B). Where q is charge, E is electric field, v is velocity, and B is magnetic field.

nHV7ID0.title: Voltmeter
nHV7ID0.description: Instrument for measuring electric potential difference between two points in an electric circuit. Typically characterized by high internal resistance. Used to prevent significant alteration of current flow in the circuit being measured. Often used in conjunction with other instruments for comprehensive electrical analysis.

LHVwID0.title: Magnetic force
LHVwID0.description: A force exerted on a charged particle moving in a magnetic field. Its magnitude determined by the charge, velocity, and magnetic field strength. Direction given by the right-hand rule. Does not perform work on particles. Influences charged particles in electromagnetic devices and applications.

oHV0rD0.title: Loop rule
oHV0rD0.description: A fundamental principle in electrical circuits. Known as Kirchhoff's voltage law. States that the sum of the electromotive forces and potential differences in any closed loop equals zero. Essential for analyzing complex circuits. Used in conjunction with Kirchhoff's current law (KCL).

KHVUrD0.title: Junction rule
KHVUrD0.description: A principle of electrical circuits. States that at any junction in a circuit, the sum of currents entering equals the sum of currents leaving. Also known as the conservation of charge. Essential for analyzing complex circuits. Typically applied in conjunction with the loop rule.

6HVjrD0.title: Ohm's law
6HVjrD0.description: A fundamental principle in physics, relating voltage, current, and resistance. Expressed as V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance. Governs the behavior of electrical circuits. Essential for calculating electrical parameters and designing circuits.

pHVLrD0.title: Ohm
pHVLrD0.description: The unit of electrical resistance, symbolized by Ω. Defined as the resistance when a potential difference of one volt yields a current of one ampere. Named after Georg Simon Ohm. Used in analyses of circuits, measuring how resistors and other components impede electrical flow.

JHVsrD0.title: Point charge
JHVsrD0.description: An idealized model of a charged object, typically treated as having negligible size. Characterized by a specific electric charge value. Generates an electric field that radially diminishes with distance. Fundamental in electrostatics calculations, such as Coulomb's law applications and electric field mappings.

qHVCrD0.title: Watt
qHVCrD0.description: A derived unit of power in the International System of Units (SI). Represents the rate of energy transfer equivalent to one joule per second. Commonly used to quantify electrical power output, such as in light bulbs and appliances. Named after engineer James Watt.

IHVY7D0.title: Joule
IHVY7D0.description: Unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI). Defined as the energy transferred when a force of one newton displaces an object by one meter. Equivalent to one kilogram meter squared per second squared (kg·m²/s²). Commonly used to express energy, work, or heat in physics and engineering contexts.

rHVf7D0.title: Coulomb's constant
rHVf7D0.description: A proportionality constant in electrostatics equations is approximately equal to 8.9875 × 10^9 N m²/C². It is essential in Coulomb's law, relating the electric force between two point charges to their magnitudes and the distance separating them.

FHVgHD0.title: Essential features of atopic dermatitis
FHVgHD0.description: Includes chronic and/or relapsing course of eczematous lesions with typical appearance (e.g., erythematous patches and/or plaques), age-specific distribution patterns (e.g., face, scalp, and extensor surfaces in infants and flexure surfaces in older individuals), and intense pruritus.

EHV8HD0.title: Important features of atopic dermatitis
EHV8HD0.description: Includes typical age of onset < 12 months, personal and/or family history of atopy, and xerosis. Comorbidities and/or complications of atopic dermatitis may also be present.

9HVNsD0.title: Bempedoic acid
9HVNsD0.description: An adenosine triphosphate-citrate lyase inhibitor used to reduce LDL cholesterol levels in individuals with cardiovascular disease or at increased risk of ASCVD.

xHVEsD0.title: Topical calcineurin inhibitors
xHVEsD0.description: A class of nonsteroidal topical immunomodulators used to reduce cutaneous inflammation (e.g., in atopic dermatitis) by inhibiting calcineurin, thereby blocking T-cell activation and subsequent production of proinflammatory cytokines. Includes tacrolimus and pimecrolimus.

destinations.label: Atopic dermatitis → Common topical pharmacological treatments

ksVmED0.title: Weight-bearing exercise
ksVmED0.description: A type of physical activity that stimulates bone formation and increases strength. Generally involves mechanical loading from ground impact or resistance (e.g., brisk walking, running, jumping jacks, resistance training). May also contribute to aerobic fitness.

msVVvD0.title: Vertebral morphometry
msVVvD0.description: The quantitative assessment of vertebral body shape and height. Typically used to identify and classify vertebral fractures on imaging.

LsVwvD0.title: TCS
LsVwvD0.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Topical corticosteroids
2. Tethered cord syndrome

IsVYwD0.title: Stress myocardial perfusion imaging
IsVYwD0.description: A type of nuclear imaging used to evaluate myocardial function and blood flow during or immediately after induced stress. Most commonly used for the evaluation of coronary artery disease. Techniques include single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) and positron emission tomography (PET).

HsVKwD0.title: Stress cardiovascular magnetic resonance
HsVKwD0.description: A radiological examination of the heart used to evaluate myocardial function and blood flow during or immediately after induced stress. Most commonly used for the evaluation of coronary artery disease.

bGVHBD0.title: Hepatic insulin resistance
bGVHBD0.description: The decreased ability of insulin to suppress endogenous hepatic glucose production (i.e., gluconeogenesis, glycogenolysis).

1GV2yD0.title: Nocturnal polyuria
1GV2yD0.description: Nighttime urine production that exceeds bladder capacity, causing enuresis or nocturia. In children, production is ≥ 130% of their expected bladder capacity. In adults, production is more than 20–33% of their daily urine volume.

WGVPyD0.title: Regurgitation
WGVPyD0.description: The passive movement of gastric contents into the pharynx and/or mouth.

3GVS_D0.title: Fecal urgency
3GVS_D0.description: The sudden, insuppressible need to defecate.

RGVl_D0.title: Mirikizumab
RGVl_D0.description: A monoclonal antibody that binds to IL-23, which prevents interaction with the IL-23 receptor and inhibits the release of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Used in the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease.

iGVJ_D0.title: Upadacitinib
iGVJ_D0.description: A JAK inhibitor that is used to treat inflammatory arthritides (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis), atopic dermatitis, and inflammatory bowel disease.

kGVmzD0.title: Topical PDE4 inhibitors
kGVmzD0.description: A class of nonsteroidal topical immunomodulators used to treat inflammatory cutaneous conditions (e.g., atopic dermatitis, plaque psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis) by inhibiting phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) in cutaneous immune cells, thereby increasing intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate and reducing proinflammatory cytokine release. Includes crisaborole and roflumilast.

destinations.label: Atopic dermatitis → Common topical pharmacological treatments

lGVvzD0.title: High-potency topical steroid
lGVvzD0.description: A group of high-potency topical corticosteroids (TCS) used to decrease cutaneous inflammation (e.g., in atopic dermatitis and seborrheic dermatitis) and/or suppress a dysregulated cutaneous immune response (e.g., in psoriasis, alopecia areata, and vitiligo). Consists of TCS class 2 and includes fluocinonide 0.05% and betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% ointment.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Overview of treatment

NGV-zD0.title: Mid-potency topical steroid
NGV-zD0.description: A group of topical corticosteroids (TCS) used to decrease cutaneous inflammation (e.g., in atopic dermatitis and seborrheic dermatitis) and/or suppress a dysregulated cutaneous immune response (e.g., in psoriasis, alopecia areata, and vitiligo). Comprises TCS classes 3–4 and includes hydrocortisone butyrate 0.1%, triamcinolone acetonide 0.1–0.5%, and betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% cream.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Overview of treatment

mGVV-D0.title: Low-potency topical steroid
mGVV-D0.description: A group of topical corticosteroids (TCS) used to decrease cutaneous inflammation in skin conditions (e.g., atopic dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis) that are mild, chronic, and/or affect sensitive areas (e.g., face, genitals). Comprises TCS classes 5–7 and includes hydrocortisone 1–2.5% and desonide 0.05%.

destinations.label: Principles of dermatology → Overview of treatment

MGVM-D0.title: Vidian neurectomy
MGVM-D0.description: A surgical procedure involving transection of the vidian nerve (in the pterygoid canal). Reduces symptoms of chronic rhinitis or refractory vasomotor rhinitis by decreasing parasympathetic innervation to the nasal mucosa. Adverse effects include nasal dryness, palatal and/or upper lip numbness, and dry eye.

5Pfi2ma.title: Levine technique
5Pfi2ma.description: A wound swabbing technique that involves first cleaning and superficially debriding the wound to remove surface contaminants, then rotating a sterile swab over a 1 cm² area of viable tissue with sufficient pressure to extract fluid. This technique has a higher sensitivity and specificity than other wound swabbing techniques.

nPf72ma.title: Clinical features of peripheral neuropathy
nPf72ma.description: Features include sensory loss, neuropathic pain, and/or weakness in the distribution of affected peripheral nerves. They manifest in a focal pattern in mononeuropathies (e.g., isolated nerve involvement) and in a symmetrical, distal, stocking-glove pattern in polyneuropathies. Reflexes are often reduced or absent; chronic peripheral neuropathy can result in muscle atrophy or sensory ataxia.

6Pfjfma.title: Operon model
6Pfjfma.description: A prokaryotic gene regulation system where multiple related genes are transcribed together as a single mRNA molecule, controlled by shared regulatory sequences. A key example is the lactose (lac) operon in E. coli, which coordinates the expression of enzymes for lactose metabolism based on substrate availability. This model is essential for understanding bacterial gene regulation, antibiotic mechanisms, and microbial adaptation to host environments.

destinations.label: Gene expression and transcription →  Regulation of transcription

IPfYTma.title: Studies for weight-related complications
IPfYTma.description: Laboratory studies used to assess for weight-related health problems in individuals with overweight or obesity. Includes CBC, liver chemistries, fasting blood glucose, hemoglobin A1C, fasting lipid profile, and TSH.

EPf8gma.title: Lead hazard screen
EPf8gma.description: A limited evaluation involving selective paint testing and dust sampling to assess for lead hazards. If lead hazards are identified, a full risk assessment should be conducted.

vPfAgma.title: Pythagorean theorem
vPfAgma.description: A theorem stating that in a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse's length (c) is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides' lengths (a and b): c² = a² + b².

CPfqSma.title: Rule of threes (osteopathic medicine)
CPfqSma.description: A method used to identify the position of the thoracic transverse processes relative to the respective spinous processes. The rule separates the thoracic vertebrae into four groups of three vertebrae, each group with a different relationship between the spinous and transverse processes.

destinations.label: Thoracic spine and rib osteopathy → Anatomy

xPfESma.title: Enzymatic debridement
xPfESma.description: A selective chemical process in which exogenous proteolytic enzymes (e.g. collagenases, bromelain, papain) are topically applied to a wound to breakdown devitalized tissue while sparing viable tissue.

yPfdhma.title: Riedel lobe
yPfdhma.description: An anatomical variant of the liver characterized by a tongue-like downward projection of the right hepatic lobe, which may mimic hepatomegaly or a right-sided abdominal mass.

APfRhma.title: Biological debridement
APfRhma.description: The use of sterile larvae or maggots to selectively consume necrotic tissue and biofilm while sparing healthy surrounding tissue. Used in the management of chronic wounds.

_Pf5hma.title: Mechanical debridement
_Pf5hma.description: The physical removal of devitalized tissue using mechanical force, such as wet-to-dry dressings, irrigation, or scrubbing. It is a nonselective form of debridement and may remove some viable tissue along with necrotic material; it is often painful.

zPfrhma.title: Surgical debridement
zPfrhma.description: A form of nonselective debridement in which devitalized, necrotic, infected, or contaminated tissue is excised using an instrument such as a scalpel or scissors.

-PfDhma.title: Alginate dressing
-PfDhma.description: A highly absorbent wound dressing made from seaweed-derived calcium or sodium alginate fibers. Forms a hydrophilic gel on contact with exudate and facilitates autolytic debridement.

Z4fZ3ma.title: Foam dressing
Z4fZ3ma.description: A multilayered wound covering that absorbs exudate while maintaining a moist environment. Also provides cushioning and pressure relief (e.g., over bony prominences).

04fe3ma.title: Polymeric membrane dressing
04fe3ma.description: A flexible polymer-based surface dressing that incorporates surfactants, moisturizers, and superabsorbent components in a semipermeable membrane.

a4fQ3ma.title: Hydrogel dressing
a4fQ3ma.description: A water-rich polymer matrix available as sheets, gels, or impregnated gauze. Provides moisture to dry wounds and facilitates autolytic debridement.

b4fH3ma.title: Hedges' g
b4fH3ma.description: A standardized measure of the magnitude of difference between two group means. Calculated by dividing the difference in means by the pooled and weighted standard deviation and expressed in units of standard deviation. Used to compare studies and measurement scales and to help assess the practical or clinical relevance of findings beyond statistical significance. Conventionally, an effect size of ~ 0.2 is considered small, ~ 0.5 medium, and ≥ 0.8 large.

X4f93ma.title: EPA-certified
X4f93ma.description: A designation from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) indicating compliance with federal environmental or safety standards.

e4fxRma.title: Clinical chorioamnionitis
e4fxRma.description: A clinical syndrome comprising maternal fever and signs of maternal and/or fetal inflammation (e.g., maternal or fetal tachycardia, malodorous amniotic fluid and/or vaginal discharge). Caused by intra-amniotic infection or, less commonly, sterile intra-amniotic inflammation.

U4fbima.title: Sterile intra-amniotic inflammation
U4fbima.description: Inflammation of the amniotic cavity without evidence of infection. Manifests as clinical chorioamnionitis. Inflammatory molecules released by stressed or damaged cells are thought to play a role.

P4fWjma.title: Seton
P4fWjma.description: A surgical thread that is placed through a fistula tract and left in position for several weeks. Aids the healing of fistulas by providing continuous drainage while preventing premature closure of the external opening. Commonly used in the management of anal fistulas.

64fj4ma.title: Toe walking
64fj4ma.description: A gait pattern in which an individual walks on the toes or forefoot without a heel strike. A variation of normal gait in toddlers. Causes beyond 2–3 years of age include neurological, musculoskeletal, and developmental disorders.

J4fs4ma.title: Pediatric gait
J4fs4ma.description: Toddler gait (12–16 months of age) is characterized by a wide base, short and rapid steps, and uncoordinated arm motion. A flat-footed or toe-walking pattern is normal at this age. By ∼ 3 years of age, gait becomes more stable, with equal strides and coordinated arm swing. By ∼ 7 years of age, gait resembles that of an adult, with well-coordinated movements, a heel-toe pattern, and longer strides.

q4fC4ma.title: Neoplastic fever
q4fC4ma.description: A paraneoplastic fever caused by cytokine release by tumors or tumor-activated cells rather than infection. Often unresponsive to acetaminophen but frequently resolves with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (e.g., naproxen).

I4fYkma.title: Tafenoquine
I4fYkma.description: An 8-aminoquinoline drug used for malaria prophylaxis. Adverse effects include hemolysis in individuals with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency.

r4ffkma.title: Balantidiasis
r4ffkma.description: Balantidiasis is a zoonotic parasitic infection caused by the protozoan Balantioides coli.

74f4kma.title: Catch-down growth
74f4kma.description: A period of slow growth preceded by rapid early growth in an infant, which shifts their growth percentiles down toward their genetically determined curve. Usually occurs in large-for-gestational-age or overfed infants and is a normal process.

H4fKkma.title: Features suggestive of Lyme arthritis
H4fKkma.description: Features include large joint monoarthritis (especially knee) with large effusion and mildly elevated inflammatory markers in ambulatory, afebrile children. Residence in or recent travel to an endemic region and/or history of tick bite or Lyme disease support the diagnosis.

t4fXOma.title: Small intestinal fungal overgrowth
t4fXOma.description: A type of dysbiosis characterized by an excessive growth of fungi in the small intestine, which can lead to bloating, flatulence, and abdominal pain.

u4fpOma.title: Indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract
u4fpOma.description: A rare and benign proliferation of NK cells in the gastrointestinal tract. Patients may be asymptomatic or present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g., abdominal pain, diarrhea).

-4fDNma.title: Evanescent rash
-4fDNma.description: A transient rash that appears and disappears, typically within 24 hours. Often seen in conditions such as urticaria or during febrile episodes of adult-onset Still disease.

fkfkMma.title: Ionic compound
fkfkMma.description: Typically consist of a metal and a non-metal, where the metal donates electrons to form positive ions (cations) and the non-metal accepts those electrons to form negative ions (anions). Examples include: NaCl (sodium chloride), Li₂O (lithium oxide), and MgO (magnesium oxide).

Tkf6Mma.title: FOLFOXIRI
Tkf6Mma.description: A chemotherapy regimen comprising leucovorin calcium (folinic acid; FOL), fluorouracil (F), oxaliplatin (OX), and irinotecan (IRI) that is used to treat advanced or metastatic bowel cancer. Common adverse effects include sensory neuropathy, pancytopenia, fatigue, and nausea.

gkfFMma.title: Small bowel adenocarcinoma
gkfFMma.description: A rare malignancy of the small intestine that most commonly occurs in the duodenum. Clinical manifestations are nonspecific; symptoms include intermittent crampy abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, gastrointestinal bleeding, and weight loss. Diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation. Management varies based on stage and molecular features.

SkfyMma.title: Locus of control
SkfyMma.description: The extent to which an individual believes that they have control over their own life. Individuals with a high internal locus of control tend to believe that outcomes are mainly the result of their own actions (e.g., problem solving, persistence), while those with high external locus of control perceive external factors (e.g., luck, institutional structures) as the primary influence on outcomes.

hkfcnma.title: Sleep apnea
hkfcnma.description: Recurrent episodes of breathing cessation during sleep. Caused by upper-airway collapse (obstructive type) or, less commonly, by loss of central respiratory drive (central type). Results in intermittent hypoxemia, sleep fragmentation, and increased cardiovascular and metabolic risk.

3kfSnma.title: Gamblers Anonymous
3kfSnma.description: A twelve-step program for individuals seeking or maintaining abstinence from gambling. Components include regular meetings and working with sponsors to promote personal growth.

Rkflnma.title: Hepatolithiasis
Rkflnma.description: The formation of biliary stones within the intrahepatic bile ducts.

OkfILma.title: Diabetes distress
OkfILma.description: A state of emotional distress arising from the ongoing demands of living with and managing diabetes. Includes worries about self-care, complications, stigma, costs, and social support. Symptoms may overlap with depression but are specific to diabetes-related challenges and may improve with better self-management and/or support. Unaddressed diabetes distress is associated with poorer glycemic control, reduced adherence, and increased risk for diabetes complications.

mkfVoma.title: Modified Schwartz formula
mkfVoma.description: An equation for estimating glomerular filtration rate in children using height and serum creatinine.

5kfioma.title: Full age spectrum formula
5kfioma.description: An equation for estimating glomerular filtration rate in all age groups using normalized serum creatinine.

okf0Kma.title: Post-COVID-19 Functional Status scale
okf0Kma.description: A scale used to evaluate persistent daily functional limitations after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Ranges from grade 0 (no functional limitations) to grade 4 (severe limitations requiring assistance for basic activities). Used to guide follow-up and rehabilitation.

IkfY6ma.title: Fontan procedure
IkfY6ma.description: A palliative surgical procedure for functionally univentricular heart defects, typically performed in stages. The goal is to separate pulmonary and systemic circulations so that the single ventricle supplies the systemic circulation, while pulmonary blood flow occurs passively from the systemic veins.

rkff6ma.title: Autoimmune liver disease overlap syndromes
rkff6ma.description: Conditions that manifest with features of more than one autoimmune liver disease, most commonly autoimmune hepatitis with primary biliary cholangitis or primary sclerosing cholangitis.

7kf46ma.title: Intestinal insufficiency
7kf46ma.description: A condition in which the gut cannot absorb sufficient macronutrients and/or water and electrolytes, but intravenous supplementation is not required to maintain health and/or growth. Intestinal insufficiency is on a spectrum with intestinal failure.

skft6ma.title: Yerkes-Dodson law
skft6ma.description: A psychological principle stating that performance increases with mental or physiological arousal but declines due to stress or anxiety when arousal is too high. The relationship forms an inverted U-shaped curve, indicating that moderate arousal yields the highest performance.

tkfXpma.title: Cannon-Bard theory
tkfXpma.description: A psychological theory developed by Walter B. Cannon and Philip Bard, which states that a stimulus simultaneously and independently triggers both a physiological response and the subjective experience of an emotion. When a stimulus is perceived, the thalamus sends signals to the cerebral cortex, producing the conscious emotion, and to the hypothalamus and autonomic nervous system, generating the bodily response.

Fkfgpma.title: Primary drives
Fkfgpma.description: Instinctual and evolutionarily determined motivations that serve to preserve the individual or the species. Divided into homeostatic (e.g., hunger, the need for sleep) and nonhomestatic drives (e.g., sexuality, curiosity).

8kfOpma.title: Secondary drive
8kfOpma.description: Motivations that are learned throughout life and shaped by the interaction between sociocultural factors and primary drives. Examples include the desire for power, possession, and social recognition.

ukfppma.title: Motivational conflict
ukfppma.description: A psychological theory developed by Kurt Lewin to describe a situation in which an individual experiences two competing motives of similar intensity, complicating decision-making. Can be motivated either by the desire for a stimulus (appetence) or the avoidance of a stimulus (aversion). Common types include approach–approach, avoidance–avoidance, and approach–avoidance conflicts.

Ekf8pma.title: Intestinal lymphangiectasia
Ekf8pma.description: A rare disorder characterized by dilatation of intestinal lymphatic vessels, with leakage of lymph into the gut lumen, which can lead to protein-losing enteropathy. May be primary (also known as Waldmann disease) or secondary to conditions that obstruct or damage intestinal lymphatic drainage.

vkfApma.title: Autoimmune hepatitis-cholestatic syndrome
vkfApma.description: An autoimmune liver disease characterized by autoimmune hepatitis with cholestatic liver injury that does not meet the diagnostic criteria for primary biliary cholangitis or primary sclerosing cholangitis.

Dkf1Jma.title: Cholangitis lenta
Dkf1Jma.description: A histologic pattern of cholestasis that most often manifests in patients with sepsis and/or following transplant. Characterized by dilated, bile-filled ductules with minimal ductal inflammation. Typically reflects severe or ongoing infection and is associated with poor clinical outcomes.

wkfhJma.title: Microvascular complications of diabetes
wkfhJma.description: Nephropathy, retinopathy, and peripheral and autonomic neuropathy caused by prolonged injury to small blood vessels as a result of chronic hyperglycemia. Risk increases with disease duration and poor glycemic control.

fOfk7ma.title: Clinical features of adrenal crisis
fOfk7ma.description: Features include fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, back pain, severe fatigue and/or weakness, postural dizziness, syncope, hypotension and shock (which can manifest as delayed capillary refill and/or tachycardia in young children), confusion, impaired consciousness, and coma.

hOfcHma.title: SCORing atopic dermatitis index
hOfcHma.description: A clinical tool used to assess the severity of atopic dermatitis. Incorporates the extent of body‐surface area involved, intensity of features (i.e., erythema, edema, papules, oozing, crusting, excoriation, lichenification, and dryness), and self-reported symptoms of pruritus and sleep loss. Scores range from 0 to 103 and are categorized into mild (< 25), moderate (25–50), and severe (> 50).

QOfuHma.title: Win ratio method
QOfuHma.description: A statistical method to compare outcomes in study groups in a hierarchical manner (e.g., ranked by clinical importance). For each matched treatment–control pair, the most important outcome (usually survival) is evaluated first. If the patient in the treatment group has a better outcome than the patient in the control group, the treatment group "wins"; if the patient in the control group has a better outcome, the control group "wins"; and if the outcome is the same, it is considered a tie, and the next outcome in the hierarchy is evaluated. The win ratio is calculated by dividing the total number of wins in the treatment group by the number of wins in the control group; a value greater than 1 indicates that treatment performed better than the control, while a value less than 1 favors the control.

jOf_Hma.title: Targeted antimicrobial therapy
jOf_Hma.description: Antimicrobial agents used to target the pathogens identified on diagnostic studies.

kOfmsma.title: Z-technique for wound culture
kOfmsma.description: A wound swabbing technique that involves first cleaning the wound, then rotating a swab over an area of viable tissue in the wound bed (without touching the edges) in a zigzag (“Z”) motion.

nOf7Gma.title: Prolonged first stage of labor
nOf7Gma.description: Slow progression of cervical dilation during the first stage of labor. Encompasses either a prolonged latent phase (> 20 hours in individuals without prior births or > 14 hours in those with prior births) or a prolonged active phase (< 1 cm per 2 hours after ≥ 6 cm dilation).

destinations.label: Abnormal labor and delivery → Abnormal stages of labor

LOfwGma.title: Intrapartum
LOfwGma.description: The time period during childbirth from the onset of contractions to the delivery of the placenta.

oOf0tma.title: Periampullary diverticulum
oOf0tma.description: An outpouching of the duodenal wall involving the ampulla of Vater or located within 2–3 cm of the ampulla. Accounts for ~ 75% of all duodenal diverticula.

KOfUtma.title: Bacillary peliosis
KOfUtma.description: Peliosis hepatis associated with Bartonella henselae infection. Most commonly affects immunocompromised individuals (e.g., with HIV infection). Often seen in combination with bacillary angiomatosis.

IOfYFma.title: Pseudosacculation
IOfYFma.description: The sacculated appearance of an otherwise normal bowel wall, most often seen in Crohn disease. Due to chronic inflammation that leads to asymmetric fibrosis and shortening along the mesenteric border, causing the antimesenteric wall to bulge outward. Pseudosacculations contain all three layers of bowel wall but, unlike true diverticula, they do not extend beyond the normal bowel contour.

vOfA8ma.title: Appendiceal neuroendocrine tumor
vOfA8ma.description: A type of nonepithelial neoplasm of the appendix, most often identified incidentally after routine appendectomy.

BOfzuma.title: Benign esophageal neoplasms
BOfzuma.description: Uncommon lesions that arise from the esophageal wall. Predominant types include esophageal leiomyomas, gastrointestinal stromal tumors, squamous papillomas, and inflammatory or fibrovascular polyps. Diagnosis typically requires endoscopic evaluation and tissue biopsy.

yOfdEma.title: Esophageal leiomyoma
yOfdEma.description: A slow-growing, rare mesenchymal tumor that arises from the smooth muscle cells of the muscularis mucosae or muscularis propria (more common) layer of the esophageal wall. Among the benign esophageal tumors, leiomyoma is the most common.

AOfREma.title: Esophageal squamous papilloma
AOfREma.description: A rare, benign epithelial lesion of the esophagus that appears as a solitary, exophytic, wart‑like growth with a whitish‑pink surface and sharply defined margins. Typically found in the middle and distal thirds of the esophagus.

_Of5Ema.title: Esophageal squamous papillomatosis
_Of5Ema.description: Extensive esophageal involvement of squamous papilloma lesions, which are exophytic, wart-like growths with a whitish-pink appearance. Typically, multiple clustered lesions.

zOfrEma.title: Esophageal fibrovascular polyp
zOfrEma.description: A benign intraluminal esophageal tumor composed of fibrous and adipose tissue, usually attached by a vascular stalk. Progressive enlargement can lead to airway compromise or asphyxiation.

ZlfZvma.title: Lemmel syndrome
ZlfZvma.description: A rare complication of a periampullary duodenal diverticulum characterized by extrinsic compression of the distal common bile (and sometimes pancreatic) duct by the diverticulum. Manifests with obstructive jaundice.

0lfevma.title: Benign pneumoperitoneum
0lfevma.description: The presence of free intraperitoneal gas without perforation or peritonitis. Patients are usually asymptomatic and managed conservatively.

WlfPDma.title: Anal stenosis
WlfPDma.description: A narrowing of the anal canal that occurs when the normal anoderm is replaced by fibrotic scar tissue, resulting in an abnormally tight and inflexible anal canal. Most commonly seen after surgical hemorrhoidectomy, but may also develop in patients with chronic anal inflammation, such as those with Crohn disease.

flfkwma.title: Appendiceal cancer
flfkwma.description: A rare malignancy of the appendix that is most commonly discovered incidentally on cross-sectional imaging or after routine appendectomy. Histological subtypes include appendiceal neuroendocrine tumors, mucinous adenocarcinoma, colonic-type adenocarcinoma, and the more aggressive goblet cell and signet ring adenocarcinomas.

Tlf6wma.title: Small bowel diverticular disease
Tlf6wma.description: An umbrella term that encompasses small bowel diverticulosis and small bowel diverticulitis. In small bowel diverticulosis, diverticula form through the small bowel wall. Patients are usually asymptomatic but may present with chronic, nonspecific symptoms (e.g., abdominal pain, fever, diarrhea) and/or gastrointestinal bleeding. Small bowel diverticulitis is the inflammation of one or more diverticula in the small bowel and is a complication of small bowel diverticulosis.

glfFwma.title: Small bowel diverticulosis
glfFwma.description: The presence of one or more pseudodiverticula or true diverticula in the small bowel wall. Often asymptomatic but may manifest with nonspecific symptoms (e.g., abdominal pain, dyspepsia) and/or gastrointestinal bleeding. Complications include small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, small bowel diverticulitis, and gastrointestinal bleeding.

Slfywma.title: Molecular assay
Slfywma.description: A laboratory test that examines molecules (e.g., DNA, RNA, or proteins) in a biological specimen to detect disease-related changes such as mutations, pathogen genetic material, or biomarkers. Used to support diagnosis, prognosis, or treatment decisions.

hlfc9ma.title: Small bowel diverticulitis
hlfc9ma.description: The inflammation of one or more small bowel diverticula. A complication of small bowel diverticulosis, caused by stasis of contents in the diverticulum, resulting in venous outflow obstruction and infection. Features are nonspecific and may resemble those of other causes of an acute abdomen (e.g., appendicitis). Can lead to complications such as bowel perforation, intra-abdominal abscess formation, and bowel obstruction.

3lfS9ma.title: Appendiceal colonic-type adenocarcinoma
3lfS9ma.description: A subtype of appendiceal neoplasm characterized by infiltrative growth and histologic features that resemble colorectal adenocarcinoma.

Rlfl9ma.title: Goblet cell adenocarcinoma
Rlfl9ma.description: A rare type of cancer that originates in the appendix, characterized by a mix of neuroendocrine and epithelial cells.

ilfJ9ma.title: Appendiceal mucinous adenocarcinoma
ilfJ9ma.description: A subtype of appendiceal adenocarcinoma characterized by infiltrative growth of invasive glands with > 50% of the lesion composed of extracellular mucin.

Qlfu9ma.title: Appendiceal signet-ring adenocarcinoma
Qlfu9ma.description: An aggressive neoplasm in which > 50% of the tumor is composed of signet ring cells.

4lf3Cma.title: Gallium-68 DOTATATE
4lf3Cma.description: A PET radiotracer that is used for evaluating well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors and other somatostatin-expressing conditions (e.g., meningioma, sarcoidosis).

IlfYyma.title: Thyroid dysgenesis
IlfYyma.description: A developmental defect of the thyroid gland resulting in hypoplasia, dysplasia, ectopy, or aplasia. Typically leads to congenital hypothyroidism.

7lf4yma.title: Primary congenital hypothyroidism
7lf4yma.description: A form of congenital hypothyroidism caused by defects in the thyroid gland or thyroid hormone synthesis. Results in insufficient hormone production despite normal hypothalamic–pituitary stimulation.

8lfOAma.title: Brief Eating Disorder in Athletes Questionnaire
8lfOAma.description: A 9-item questionnaire used to identify eating disorders in female elite athletes. Includes questions on body dissatisfaction, drive for thinness, dieting behaviors, and perfectionism.

ulfpAma.title: β-hydroxy β-methylbutyrate
ulfpAma.description: A metabolite of the essential amino acid leucine that facilitates muscle protein synthesis and reduces muscle catabolism. Used as a dietary supplement to increase muscle mass.

Clfq_ma.title: ASA
Clfq_ma.description:
An abbreviation that can refer to:
1. Acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin)
2. Anterior spinal artery
3. American Society of Anesthesiologists

-lfDzma.title: Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule
-lfDzma.description: A regulatory framework by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration that requires prescription drug labeling to include structured information on medication use in pregnancy, lactation, and individuals of reproductive potential. It replaced the pregnancy risk letter categories (A/B/C/D/X) in 2015.

UNfb05a.title: Permanent congenital hypothyroidism
UNfb05a.description: A thyroid hormone deficiency that is present at birth and persists throughout life. Caused by either primary gland defects (e.g., dysgenesis, dyshormonogenesis) or central hypothalamic or pituitary impairment.

nNf7b5a.title: Cyanohydrin
nNf7b5a.description: An organic compound containing both a hydroxyl (-OH) and nitrile (-CN) group attached to the same carbon atom. Formed by addition of hydrogen cyanide to aldehydes or ketones; serves as a versatile intermediate in pharmaceutical synthesis. Some cyanohydrins (e.g., acetone cyanohydrin) are extremely toxic, readily decomposing to release hydrogen cyanide. α-Ketoglutarate cyanohydrin is an endogenous metabolite formed during cyanide detoxification. Mandelonitrile occurs naturally in fruit pits.

LNfwb5a.title: Caroli syndrome
LNfwb5a.description: A condition characterized by features of both Caroli disease (abnormal widening of intrahepatic bile ducts) and congenital hepatic fibrosis.

xNfEW5a.title: Clinical features of acute cholangitis
xNfEW5a.description: Features include fever, right upper quadrant pain, and/or jaundice (Charcot cholangitis triad). In severe cases, Reynolds pentad adds altered mental status and hypotension to the triad. May rapidly progress to septic shock.

Xmf9V5a.title: Clean technique
Xmf9V5a.description: A set of practices used in wound care and minor procedures that aims to limit infection risk when full sterile precautions are not required. Includes standard precautions such as hand hygiene, using clean nonsterile gloves and disposable or appropriately disinfected instruments, and cleaning and disinfecting surfaces to reduce microbial burden.
